caption: Shear stress-strain curves for 3D-printed Ti6Al4V thoracic fusion cages, highlighting the influence of different reinforced scaffold volume ratios on mechanical behavior.
summary: Shear stress-strain curves are presented for 3D-printed Ti6Al4V thoracic fusion cages. These plots demonstrate the mechanical performance of samples with and without reinforced scaffolds. The results indicate that the inclusion of scaffolds enhances the shear strength of the fusion cages, although it slightly affects the overall shear ductility.

caption: Carbon and nitrogen K-edge EELS spectra of ABS polymer subjected to increasing electron doses of 5, 53, 190, and 312 e/Å², with an inset showing the constant Cπ*/Cσ* intensity ratio versus accumulated dose.
summary: The carbon and nitrogen K-edge EELS spectra for ABS show a significant reduction in both pre-peak and main peak intensities as the electron dose increases from 5 to 312 e/Å². The inset confirms that the Cπ*/Cσ* ratio remains constant, indicating that the spectral features decrease following the same trend.

caption: Frequency distribution histogram of GND values for the LPBF specimen, indicating a value of 1.1 × 10^14 m^-2.
summary: This histogram quantifies the GND value distribution for the LPBF specimen. The data reveals a high dislocation density, with a characteristic GND value of 1.1 × 10^14 m^-2. This high value reflects the significant residual stresses and dislocation formation inherent to the LPBF manufacturing process for this superalloy.

caption: Nyquist plots derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests were performed to analyze the interfacial properties of the material. Panel (c) presents the resulting Nyquist plots, which visualize the impedance behavior and provide the necessary data to model the electrochemical interface and understand the underlying corrosion mechanisms occurring at the surface.

caption: Critical temperature landscape for the α-phase in the Fe–Cr–Ni system, illustrating the localized singularities and cusps that complicate numerical analysis.
summary: Representing the α-phase critical temperatures in the Fe–Cr–Ni system, this plot demonstrates the occurrence of numerical singularities and cusps. These features are identified as significant challenges in the computational modeling of the system, reflecting the complex thermodynamic interactions that define the phase boundaries and stability regions for this specific phase.

caption: Comparison of compressive force–displacement results for four lattice structures with varying beam diameters (D), evaluating FE full-geometry simulation (SIM), homogenized model (HOM), and experimental (EXP) data.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of compressive force–displacement behavior across four lattice structures with varying beam diameters. It evaluates the accuracy of FE full-geometry simulations and homogenized model predictions against experimental measurements. The results demonstrate strong agreement in reaction forces and nodal displacements, confirming the validity of the computational models.

caption: Shear modulus mismatch parameter |δGi| as a function of Mo content, illustrating the relative influence of constituent elements.
summary: This plot illustrates the shear modulus mismatch |δGi| relative to Mo content. The model predicts that the contributions to shear modulus mismatch from Mo and Zr are several times greater than those from Hf, Ta, Ti, and Nb, emphasizing the significant role of these specific elements in modulating elastic properties.

caption: Depth-dependent OPD profiles averaged over a 150 µm lateral ROI, showing the evolution of the OPD gradient relative to the surface over time.
summary: The OPD changes at various depths are averaged over a 150 µm lateral region of interest. This plot tracks the depth gradient of the OPD relative to the surface over time, providing a quantitative measure of the optical variations occurring within the powder bed as the droplet interacts with the material.

caption: Atomic structure of the LowIndex-2 interface, illustrating an incoherent interface where the majority of fcc Al atoms (red) lack matching counterparts in the Al3Ni lattice.
summary: The LowIndex-2 interface displays an incoherent atomic structure, evidenced by the lack of registry between the fcc Al atoms and the Al3Ni phase. Unlike the Pearlite-1 orientation, most Al atoms do not find matching counterparts, which is characteristic of incoherent interfaces with higher atomic mismatch.

caption: Creep and recovery response curves showing the effect of the nonlinearity parameter (b) on the predicted mechanical behavior.
summary: This panel displays the impact of the nonlinearity parameter (b) on the creep and recovery response. By comparing different values of (b) to the black reference line calibrated for untreated PLA at 8 MPa and 27 °C, the plot clarifies how this parameter introduces nonlinear effects into the Burgers model.

caption: Electronic band structure and density of states for the Ti2AlW O-phase compound.
summary: Displayed are the band structure and density of states for the Ti2AlW O-phase compound. The electronic structure features a small indirect band gap, which is a common trait among the studied Ti2AlM compounds. This data supports the comparative analysis of stability and elastic properties across the series.

caption: Precision-recall distribution for damage detection using the RAN-3D algorithm, aggregated from 81 independent runs across 500 damaged models with varying parameter combinations.
summary: This plot illustrates the precision-recall performance of the RAN-3D algorithm in detecting damage. By evaluating 81 distinct runs encompassing 500 damaged models with diverse parameter combinations, the distribution demonstrates the algorithm's general applicability for damage detection without targeting specific damage types, providing a comprehensive assessment of its predictive reliability.

caption: Continuous-cooling transformation (CCT) diagram depicting phase evolution as a function of cooling conditions.
summary: The CCT diagram provides a comprehensive overview of phase transformation kinetics during continuous cooling. It serves as a predictive tool for determining the resulting microstructure based on specific cooling paths. By mapping the SSPT temperature against cooling rates, this diagram helps distinguish between diffusional and diffusionless transformation pathways in the material.

caption: Stacked bar plot displaying the feature importance for Model III, designed to classify deposit types originating from S-type magmas.
summary: Model III uses a stacked bar plot to display the importance of geochemical features for classifying deposit types derived from S-type magmas. This visualization helps identify which elements are most critical for the model's decision-making process when analyzing deposits associated with this specific magma source.

caption: Simulated columnar grain morphology for the 2nd layer at the middle position of the curved component.
summary: Representing the middle position of the 2nd layer, this simulation shows the predicted columnar grain structure. The computational model provides insight into the solidification behavior at this specific location, highlighting the grain growth patterns formed during the deposition process within the 3-hour simulation timeframe.

caption: Extrusion force versus time curves for Gel40_Hidro formulation using various nozzle types (M-25G, M-27G, M-30G, and P-25G), where stars indicate the onset of the constant force zone.
summary: Force-time curves for the Gel40_Hidro formulation demonstrate extrusion behavior across different nozzle diameters. The data, measured after 10 minutes of cartridge holding, highlights the transition to a constant force zone, marked by stars, which represents the firmness and steady extrusion required for consistent printing performance during the clogging analysis.

caption: Representative immunofluorescence images of RAW 264.7 cells on the scaffold, highlighting the expression of iNOS (green) and CD206 (red) to assess macrophage polarization.
summary: Immunofluorescence assay results indicate that the number of CD206+ M2-type macrophages increased in the piezoelectric group compared to controls. This panel visualizes the spatial distribution of iNOS and CD206 markers, confirming the immunomodulatory influence of the piezoelectric scaffold on macrophage phenotype polarization at a 50 μm scale.

caption: Tukey simultaneous 95% confidence intervals illustrating pairwise differences in mean grain aspect ratio across four distinct scanning strategies (ST1-ST4).
summary: This plot displays Tukey simultaneous 95% confidence intervals for mean grain aspect ratio differences between scanning strategies. Analysis reveals that ST1 and ST2 exhibit similar mean aspect ratio behaviors, whereas ST3 and ST4 are grouped together, demonstrating significantly higher aspect ratio values compared to the first two strategies.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of the 3D-printed Emerald Green filter, featuring a broad transmission maximum centered between 520 and 530 nm, with low-transmission regions in the blue (440–460 nm) and red (660–680 nm) ranges.
summary: Emerald Green filters demonstrate a broad transmission maximum centered between 520 and 530 nm. The spectral data further indicates two specific low-transmission regions: one in the blue range around 440–460 nm and another in the red range near 660–680 nm, defining the filter's green-selective optical characteristics.

caption: CV curves of 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 half cells measured at varying sweep rates.
summary: The lithium storage performance of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode was evaluated by measuring cyclic voltammetry at various scan rates ranging from 0.1 to 1 mVs-1. These curves illustrate the electrochemical response of the half-cell system under different kinetic conditions, providing insight into the rate-dependent storage mechanisms.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of residual uncured monomers leached from 3D printed Clear V4 (blue) and Biomed Clear (red) resins into DPBS solution, showing characteristic absorption peaks near 225 nm.
summary: This UV-Vis spectroscopic analysis characterizes the residual uncured monomers released from 3D printed Clear V4 and Biomed Clear resins into a DPBS solution. Both resins exhibit strong absorbance between 200 nm and 300 nm, with a distinct maximum absorption peak observed at approximately 225 nm for the tested samples.

caption: Phosphorus concentration levels in H13 ESR ingots, demonstrating a decrease from 201.6 ppm to 193.5 ppm with magnetic field implementation.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the reduction of phosphorus concentration in H13 ESR ingots, which decreases from 201.6 ppm to 193.5 ppm when using an axial static magnetic field. This reduction highlights the improved efficiency of impurity removal and overall chemical homogeneity achieved through the magnetic controlled electroslag remelting process.

caption: Crack tip opening displacement (CTOD) values calculated from the test curves for as-built and heat-treated specimens.
summary: Crack tip opening displacement (CTOD) values are presented for both as-built and heat-treated conditions. The data shows that evaluated orientations exhibit similar behavior regarding crack tip displacement under load, indicating a relatively anisotropic response in terms of maximum force at crack opening across the different processing conditions and printing orientations.

caption: Visible light transmittance curves (390–700 nm) and corresponding photographs of PAP materials, demonstrating the effect of varying PVA content on optical clarity.
summary: Increasing the PVA content in the PAP hydrogel precursor leads to higher crystallinity, which results in a gradual decrease in transmittance within the visible light region of 390–700 nm. Despite this reduction, the materials maintain a relatively high level of optical transparency as shown in the inset photographs.

caption: Pole figures for {100}, {110}, and {111} crystal plane families in the Alloy2 longitudinal section.
summary: Pole figures for the {100}, {110}, and {111} crystal plane families confirm the crystallographic texture of the Alloy2 sample. By comparing the intensities of these families in the X-Z plane, the {100} texture component is identified as the strongest, which aligns perfectly with the observations from the IPF map.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for pure PLA samples measured across various UV-C degradation time intervals.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for pure PLA samples measured across various UV-C degradation time intervals. These measurements were obtained from cross-sections of test pieces to evaluate the thermal response of the polymer before and after UV-C irradiation, providing a baseline for comparison with the GF-reinforced composite materials.

caption: Azimuthal intensity plot of the {311} lattice plane during the uniaxial to biaxial strain path change.
summary: This panel shows the {311} lattice plane intensity as a function of azimuthal angle from 0° to 90° throughout the discontinuous strain path change. It serves to characterize the texture development and grain orientation shifts occurring within the material as it transitions between uniaxial and biaxial loading stages.

caption: High-speed imaging still frame of the 6th track deposition using FeCrAl wire.
summary: This high-speed imaging frame shows the 6th track of FeCrAl wire deposition, filmed from a specific camera angle. The image provides real-time visual data on the melt pool behavior and track formation, assisting in the analysis of deposition stability and the identification of process-related defects.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of BMSCs cultured on various 3D-printed scaffolds after 1 day, illustrating cell distribution and viability.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of BMSCs cultured on various 3D-printed scaffolds after 1 day illustrate cell distribution and viability. The results show that all scaffold groups support abundant adherent cells with no evident dead cells, confirming that the 3D-printed structures are biocompatible and support BMSC growth after 1 day.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectra of F100 to F0 membranes arranged vertically, highlighting characteristic functional groups such as the HEMA-derived –OH group (green dotted line) and the polyurethane-derived –NH group (red dotted line).
summary: ATR-FTIR analysis was performed on all membranes to verify successful copolymerization. The spectra for F100 through F0 are displayed, with specific colored markers identifying key functional groups. The green dotted line denotes the HEMA –OH group, while the red dotted line indicates the polyurethane –NH group, confirming the chemical composition.

caption: Thermal distribution (θ) of the PGW fluid in scenario-5 as predicted by the artificial backpropagation network, illustrating the influence of the heat source variable on the thermal field characteristics.
summary: This panel displays the thermal distribution (θ) of the PGW fluid for scenario-5, as determined by an artificial backpropagation network. It specifically highlights how variations in the heat source variable directly impact the resulting thermal field characteristics, providing a visual representation of the network's predictive output for this specific scenario.

caption: Summary of calculated mechanical parameters for the Z-sinusoid beam, covering neutral axis location, tension and compression centroids, cross-sectional stress profiles, and S-11 tensile stress distribution along the underside.
summary: The Z-sinusoid beam test case provides tabulated FE simulation results for neutral axis positioning, tension and compression centroids, and stress profiles at crest and trough sections. These metrics quantify the S-11 tensile stress distribution along the underside of the beam, facilitating a direct comparison of mechanical performance across different beam geometries.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) versus test time curve for the middle region of the component measured at a normal load of 10 N and a sliding speed of 50 mm/s.
summary: This panel illustrates a representative COF versus test time curve for the middle region of the component. The test was performed at a normal load of 10 N and an increased sliding speed of 50 mm/s, allowing for a comparison of tribological performance under different velocity conditions.

caption: Storage and loss modulus curves for PLA-PBAT-Lotader measured at 185 °C, displaying no crossover between G′ and G″ at low frequencies.
summary: PLA-PBAT-Lotader modulus curves measured at 185 °C over a frequency range of 0.02–625 rad/s are presented. Unlike the Joncryl-modified sample, this blend shows no intersection between the storage and loss moduli at low frequencies, indicating different rheological behavior under the specified test conditions.

caption: Main effect plot demonstrating the correlation between feed rate and tool wear progression.
summary: This panel displays the main effect of feed rate on tool wear. The results indicate that tool wear increases substantially as the feed rate grows. This observation confirms that higher feed rates contribute significantly to the accelerated degradation of the tool during the specified machining conditions.

caption: Trajectory tracking performance of a UAV following a predefined path, comparing the reference path (blue) against the measured flight path before (orange) and after (green) the deployment of an offset-free model predictive control (MPC) estimator.
summary: This plot evaluates the offset-free MPC scheme by tracking a predefined path shown in blue. The trajectory measured before the estimator is deployed is marked in orange, while the path after deployment is marked in green, demonstrating the effectiveness of the estimator in improving the UAV's path-following accuracy during flight.

caption: High-speed camera capture of fracture initiation and propagation in a one-time recycled thermoplastic matrix composite (TMC) during a three-point bending test.
summary: This high-speed photograph documents the failure progression of a one-time recycled TMC during a three-point bending test. Key structural damage features include an interlaminar fracture at the interface of the bottom 0° rod layer, a crack propagating through a 90° rod, and sliding of the bottom-most 0° rod layer.

caption: Nyquist plot displaying the complex impedance behavior of PEO-coated series B samples.
summary: Displaying the imaginary versus real impedance components, this Nyquist plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance of PEO-coated series B samples. This diagram serves as a key representative result for the series, illustrating the interfacial properties and charge transfer resistance associated with the PEO coating under the tested conditions.

caption: Tan delta curves of PLA/hemp hurd composites showing the evolution of the damping peak as the number of recycling steps increases.
summary: As seen in this panel, the tan δ peak increased as the number of recycling steps increased. This plot provides a clear visualization of the damping behavior of the PLA/hemp hurd composites, indicating that the recycling process significantly influences the viscoelastic properties of the composite material.

caption: Spin-wave spectrum displaying the ten lowest-frequency modes for cobalt dots embedded within a permalloy matrix, plotted along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone.
summary: This panel illustrates the spin-wave spectrum for cobalt inclusions in a permalloy matrix. The plot tracks the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone. Line colors represent the in-cobalt concentration factor, providing a visual representation of the magnetic excitation characteristics within this specific composite material configuration.

caption: Experimental assembly showing the substrate, torch holder, vice, and K-type thermocouple positioning.
summary: This image illustrates the physical arrangement of the welding components, including the substrate secured in a vice and the torch holder mounted on the linear axis system. A K-type thermocouple is positioned to measure thermal values, with the resulting readings transmitted directly to the Temperature Records Module for analysis.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops measured along the hard axis (90°) for segments C1–C12, demonstrating an inverse trend in curve ordering compared to the easy axis measurements.
summary: Hysteresis curves measured along the hard axis (90°) for the continuously printed specimen illustrate the loss of magnetic anisotropy. The opposite ordering of curves compared to the easy axis indicates that as print height increases, the magnetic properties shift, reflecting the progressive degradation of the material's directional magnetic alignment.

caption: Electrochemical current-time (I-T) data and CH4 conversion efficiency measured over a 30-hour SOFC test period under a constant 0.6 V bias.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical performance and catalytic activity of the SOFC anode during a 30-hour stability test. By applying a 0.6 V bias, the I-T data and simultaneous GC-HID exhaust analysis demonstrate the conversion efficiency of CH4 fuel, providing a comprehensive view of the cell's operational stability over time.

caption: Atomic force microscopy surface topography of the uncoated S1 sample.
summary: Atomic force microscopy surface topography of the uncoated S1 sample. This image provides critical insight into the surface roughness profile of the S1 specimen. The AFM technique is utilized here to characterize the surface morphology, which serves as a foundational measurement for evaluating the material's subsequent hydrophilic or hydrophobic surface nature.

caption: Local average misorientation (LAM) map of the HIPed sample, highlighting the distribution of internal strain and deformation.
summary: The local average misorientation map displays the spatial distribution of internal strain within the HIPed FGH4113A superalloy. By mapping these misorientation values, the figure characterizes the microstructural state and deformation characteristics of the material following the hot isostatic pressing process, providing insight into the local lattice distortion.

caption: Neutron transmittance of fabricated alloys as a function of thickness under 1 KeV incident neutron energy.
summary: Neutron transmittance data for the fabricated alloys is shown for an incident energy of 1 KeV. Similar to the 1 eV condition, the shielding performance differences between the alloys are reduced, indicating that the specific advantages of certain elements like Gd are less pronounced at higher incident neutron energy levels.

caption: Binary Ni-Nb phase diagram representing the equilibrium phases and solidification behavior of the nickel-niobium system.
summary: The Ni-Nb binary phase diagram represents the equilibrium phases and solidification behavior of the nickel-niobium system. Niobium demonstrates little effect on the solidification temperature range of the IN625 superalloy, which indicates that it does not appreciably modify the solidification zone or influence the final grain morphology of the material.

caption: Raman spectra acquired from five distinct groups of TCP/BO/GO scaffolds, each coated with a different concentration of GO to characterize chemical composition.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was performed on five groups of TCP/BO/GO scaffolds, which were coated with different concentrations of GO. The resulting spectra allow for the characterization of the chemical composition and structural integrity of the scaffolds, confirming the presence and influence of the GO coating across the different experimental groups.

caption: Rotated view of the pure IN 939 specimen along the x-axis by 90 degrees, revealing that the planar cracks transition into line-like features.
summary: Rotating the 3D micro-CT scan of the pure IN 939 specimen by 90 degrees along the x-axis reveals the orientation of internal defects. The previously identified planar cracks now appear as line-like features, as highlighted by black arrows, alongside large pores marked by red arrows within the specimen structure.

caption: Nyquist plot displaying the electrochemical impedance behavior of L-PBF-produced NiTi alloy S2 immersed in pH 7 Hank's solution, highlighting the presence of diffusion impedance in the low-frequency region.
summary: The Nyquist plot for the S2 NiTi alloy specimen demonstrates its electrochemical impedance response over 24, 48, and 72 hours of immersion. The detection of diffusion impedance in the low-frequency region indicates the dissolution of the passive film, providing insight into the degradation behavior of the alloy in Hank's solution.

caption: Unrolled 2D synchrotron HEXRD pattern at 25°C showing diffuse scattering of the βo reflections in the initial state.
summary: This panel displays the initial state of the material at room temperature using unrolled 2D synchrotron HEXRD patterns. The diffraction data reveals diffuse scattering associated with the βo reflections, providing a baseline for the subsequent in-situ heating experiment as the sample undergoes structural evolution during thermal treatment.

caption: Time to reach 1% creep strain for CMSX-4 loaded along the 〈001〉 direction, plotted across various constant stress and temperature conditions.
summary: This panel presents creep performance data for CMSX-4 under constant stress and temperature loading along the 〈001〉 direction. The data quantifies the time required to reach 1% creep strain, providing essential insights into the material's strain softening effects and long-term deformation behavior during steady-state high-temperature engine operation.

caption: 3D surface topography of an SLM-fabricated part processed under optimal conditions (LP 3, SS 1, HD 1).
summary: This 3D surface topography reconstruction illustrates the surface morphology of an SLM-fabricated part produced under optimal processing conditions, specifically defined as LP 3, SS 1, and HD 1. The visualization provides a detailed view of the surface state achieved when the laser parameters are optimized for the manufacturing process.

caption: Magnetization curves comparing as-cast (black squares) and hot-rolled, extruded (red squares) equiatomic NiTi alloy samples under a static magnetic field.
summary: Magnetization curves for equiatomic NiTi alloy are presented to evaluate the impact of thermo-mechanical processing on magnetic properties. The plot compares as-cast and hot-rolled, extruded samples, demonstrating that both conditions exhibit nearly identical paramagnetic behavior, indicating that the thermo-mechanical treatment does not significantly alter the material's magnetic response.

caption: EDS analysis of the LHM-BD fracture surface showing the presence of Al, RE, and Zr elements.
summary: EDS analysis of the fracture surface in panel (d) reveals that the aggregated phase primarily contains Al, RE, and Zr elements. This compositional data suggests the possible presence of Al2RE and Al2Zr phases, which are critical for understanding the microstructural constituents influencing the fracture mechanism of the LHM.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for the pH = 7 classification model, demonstrating that three distinct features contribute with relatively similar magnitudes to the model output.
summary: The beeswarm plot for the pH = 7 class displays the distribution of SHAP values for the model. Unlike the pH = 4.5 class where a single feature dominates, this visualization shows that three different features have close effects on the model's classification performance for this specific pH level.

caption: Specific yield stress plotted against temperature for the Cast_33 superalloy and the selected reference superalloys.
summary: Specific yield stress values are depicted as a function of temperature for the Cast_33 superalloy and the reference superalloys previously described. This comparison highlights the performance of the Cast_33 alloy relative to other Co-Ni-based, Co-based, and commercial superalloys when normalized by density, providing insight into the material's strength-to-weight efficiency at elevated temperatures.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of sample D5 processed under low E0* showing the β-phase matrix and martensitic α” laths.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging of sample D5, processed under low E0*, reveals the microstructural arrangement of the β-phase matrix and martensitic α” laths. This imaging technique provides high-contrast visualization of the phase distribution within the material's microstructure.

caption: SR-PXD refinement for Mn0.65Ni0.65Fe0.7Si0.95Al0.05 (y=0.35) at 310 K, with indexed reflections for the TiNiSi, Ni2In, and MgZn2 phases.
summary: Rietveld refinement of SR-PXD data for Mn0.65Ni0.65Fe0.7Si0.95Al0.05 (y=0.35) at 310 K during heating is shown. The plot includes experimental data, calculated intensities, and difference plots. The pattern is indexed with tick marks for the TiNiSi orthorhombic, Ni2In hexagonal, and MgZn2 hexagonal phases, confirming the structural state of the material at 310 K.

caption: Computer-aided design model of the AM-PXCM unit cell, highlighting the <111> crystallographic direction of the FCC lattice as the axis of bistability.
summary: This CAD model illustrates the AM-PXCM unit cell architecture. It specifically identifies the <111> direction of the underlying FCC structure as the primary axis for bistable behavior. The design serves as the foundational geometry for the metamaterial, enabling the specific mechanical transformations described in the study.

caption: Optical micrograph of Ti-5 wt% Cu processed via LPBF at a volumetric energy density (VED) of 77.55 J/mm³.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the Ti-5 wt% Cu microstructure at a VED of 77.55 J/mm³. The image demonstrates the microstructural changes occurring at higher energy inputs, which are governed by the geometry of the melt pool and the specific thermal conditions established during the LPBF manufacturing process.

caption: Bode plot displaying the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for the S1 NiTi alloy immersed in pH 3 Hank's solution.
summary: The Bode plot for the S1 NiTi alloy provides a frequency-dependent analysis of the electrochemical impedance in a pH 3 Hank's solution. These results, when analyzed alongside the Nyquist plots and the equivalent electrical circuit, characterize the electrochemical interface and passive film stability of the L-PBF-produced material.

caption: Tribo-data map illustrating the friction force distribution, where positive values indicate movement from left to right.
summary: This heatmap displays the spatial distribution of friction forces generated during the test. As noted in the reference, friction force values are positive when the counter body moves from left to right, allowing for a detailed analysis of the directional friction behavior across the contact surface of the sample.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the 0.5 mm thick LB-PBF SS316L thin-walled sample, highlighting the XZ plane microstructure after HT2 treatment.
summary: The 0.5 mm thick sample's microstructure is visualized through this inverse pole figure map following HT2 heat treatment. The image demonstrates the extent of recrystallization and abnormal grain growth induced by the 1150 °C thermal cycle, confirming the microstructural changes observed in the LB-PBF SS316L thin-walled samples.

caption: Distribution of filament contact line spreading speed under various flowabilities.
summary: Spatial distribution of spreading speeds for four different bio-inks is visualized in this panel. The contact line speed between the filament and the substrate is captured to quantify the spreading motion, providing a comparative analysis of how different ink flowabilities influence the dynamic spreading behavior during the printing process.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern corresponding to the α/α′ phase in the 700 °C-annealed specimen.
summary: Shown is the selected area diffraction pattern for the α/α′ phase in the 700 °C-annealed specimen. Similar to the 650 °C condition, the diffraction spots reveal that the lattice parameters of the α′ phase exhibit a slight increase, yet they remain close to the lattice parameters of the as-received specimen.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectrum obtained from point 2# within the Fe-Al-Si intermetallic phase.
summary: Point 2# represents a specific location within the Fe-Al-Si intermetallic phase. The EDS spectrum confirms the presence of Fe, Al, and Si elements. Comparing this result with points 3# and 4# reveals a trend of increasing Fe and Si content alongside decreasing Al content within the identified intermetallic phases.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the imaginary versus real impedance components for as-deposited and 600 °C-annealed coatings in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: The Nyquist plot displays the electrochemical impedance response of as-deposited and 600 °C-annealed coatings in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Annealing leads to an increase in the diameter of the capacitive loop, indicating improved corrosion resistance for the heat-treated coating compared to the as-deposited sample.

caption: High-magnification scanning transmission electron microscopy image of Fe-rich phases in the Al–4Fe cellular structure, indicating the path used for EDS line scanning.
summary: High-magnification STEM imaging focuses on the cellular structure above the melt pool boundary in Al–4Fe. Iron is detected exclusively at the cell boundaries with concentrations reaching approximately 25 wt% (≈13.9 at%). The indicated line scan path facilitates precise compositional analysis of these specific Fe-rich intermetallic phases.

caption: Electron beam trajectory simulation at an acceleration voltage of 35 kV, with beam, upper coil, and lower coil currents maintained at 1, 0.9, and 0.3 A, respectively.
summary: This panel shows the simulated electron beam trajectory at 35 kV acceleration voltage. As noted in the reference, changing the acceleration voltage while keeping coil and beam currents constant causes a shift in the beam focusing point, confirming that the trajectory is dependent on the acceleration voltage settings.

caption: Current efficiency curves plotted as a function of time for three distinct alloy compositions.
summary: This plot illustrates the current efficiency test results for three different alloys. The graph displays the performance stability of these materials over time, providing a comparative analysis of their electrochemical efficiency. These curves serve as a primary metric for evaluating the electrochemical behavior and suitability of the tested alloy samples.

caption: Schematic representation of the experimental configuration utilized for the study.
summary: This panel provides a comprehensive overview of the experimental setup employed in the research. It serves as a visual guide to the configuration and arrangement of the apparatus, ensuring clarity regarding the methodology and the physical environment in which the experimental procedures were conducted throughout the investigation.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of Ni-based superalloy 600 in 0.1 mol/L H2SO4 solution, illustrating the electrochemical response across various temperatures.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for Ni-based superalloy 600 in 0.1 mol/L H2SO4 solution demonstrate the electrochemical behavior at different temperatures. These results, when correlated with observed corrosion pit coarsening and intergranular corrosion, confirm that increasing temperatures exacerbate the corrosion process, significantly impacting the material's electrochemical stability and degradation resistance.

caption: Surface morphology of an AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.845.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image shows the surface morphology of an AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.845. The surface morphology is similar to that of bulk AlInN. This structure is noted for having GaN layers twice as thick as those in samples exhibiting shorter wavelength emissions.

caption: Blue light profile at 450 nm wavelength captured by a CMOS camera, demonstrating a checkerboard pattern across a 16.01 mm by 9.01 mm area with a 0.77 magnification factor.
summary: This panel displays the 450 nm blue wavelength light profile projected onto the focal plane. Captured via CMOS camera, the checkerboard pattern covers an area of 16.01 mm by 9.01 mm. The optical setup achieves a magnification factor of approximately 0.77, ensuring precise spatial distribution of the blue light intensity.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing virgin and recycled ABS/CF composites, illustrating weight percentage as a function of temperature.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for virgin and recycled ABS/CF composites demonstrate that both materials maintain thermal stability up to approximately 400 °C with minimal weight loss. Thermal degradation initiates just above this threshold for both samples. An inset provides a magnified view of the residual weight region, highlighting slight differences in final weight.

caption: Representative immunofluorescence images and topographical fluorescence intensity maps of Collagen X expression, demonstrating peak intensity in the CSK@P/H100 group.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging and topographical maps were utilized to assess Collagen X, a primary marker for the calcified cartilage layer. The findings show that the CSK@P/H100 group exhibits the strongest expression of Collagen X, with significant statistical differences observed when compared to the other three scaffold groups after two months.

caption: Geometric parametrisation of the HCP lattice, highlighting the spatial relationship between the two triangular grids shifted in the y-direction and spaced by c/2 along the z-axis.
summary: The HCP lattice parametrisation is defined by two triangular grids shifted in the y-direction and separated by a distance of c/2 along the z-axis. This geometric arrangement allows for a straightforward design, as it identifies the specific twinning plane that intersects at least one node in all A and B layers.

caption: Pole figures of the CaF2-tailored Ti–6Al–4V alloy at 2 mm from the fracture site, capturing intermediate deformation.
summary: Documenting the {0001} and {10-10} pole figures for the CaF2-tailored Ti–6Al–4V alloy at 2 mm from the fracture, this panel shows the intermediate state of texture evolution. It serves as a reference point for the material's structural response as it approaches the final stages of tensile deformation.

caption: Measured thermal desorption data and Gaussian fit curve for a heating rate of 1200 °C/h.
summary: The thermal desorption spectrum at a 1200 °C/h heating rate is shown with its Gaussian fit. This data is critical for quantifying hydrogen release from trap sites. By integrating the peak area versus time, the amount of hydrogen trapped at specific sites, including misfit dislocations, can be accurately determined.

caption: Statistical distribution of grain sizes across various temperatures and strain rates, represented by box plots showing mean values, 25th/75th percentiles, medians, and 10th/90th percentile whiskers.
summary: This box plot summarizes grain size distributions across all tested temperatures and strain rates. Statistical markers indicate the mean, median, and percentile ranges for each condition. Analysis reveals that mean grain size generally increases as the strain rate decreases, highlighting the sensitivity of microstructural evolution to the applied deformation parameters.

caption: Maximum twist angle plotted against fatigue life for as-built specimens.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the maximum twist angle and fatigue life for as-built specimens. It serves as a baseline for evaluating the mechanical performance of the material under cyclic loading conditions, providing a clear visualization of how the twist angle correlates with the overall fatigue life of the as-built structure.

caption: Plateau stress comparison between graded structures and their uniform counterparts, demonstrating a slight performance enhancement in graded designs.
summary: This bar chart compares the plateau stress values of graded structures against uniform counterparts. The findings reveal that the graded architectures exhibit slightly higher plateau stresses, indicating that the grading strategy effectively improves the energy absorption and stress-bearing characteristics of the lattices during the plateau phase of deformation.

caption: Inverse pole figure mapping of the Alloy 625 microstructure at the center region.
summary: This inverse pole figure mapping displays the microstructure of Alloy 625 at the center region. It serves as a baseline for comparing grain size variations across the radial direction of the specimen, demonstrating the initial grain structure before observing the reduction trends found toward the edge of the material.

caption: Localized HRTEM pattern of the interface, providing detailed atomic-scale structural information of the phases formed during the bonding process.
summary: Localized HRTEM imaging is employed to investigate the interface structure, as the distribution of La and O differs significantly from other regions. This analysis provides atomic-scale insights into the phases around the triangular interface, complementing the broader HAADF-STEM observations of the 200 nm thick Cr–O bonding layer.

caption: Merged fluorescence microscopy image of HGF cells exposed to samples for 24 hours, combining green and red channels to visualize total cell distribution.
summary: Merged fluorescence microscopy images at 10x magnification confirm the presence and distribution of HGF cells under direct contact conditions with the tested samples. This visualization integrates both green and red fluorescence channels to provide a comprehensive view of the cell population and their spatial arrangement relative to the material surfaces.

caption: XPS depth profile of all elements in the LPBF 350/700 sample, accompanied by an inset schematic illustrating the oxide/metallic layer structure and calculated thicknesses.
summary: The XPS depth profile for all elements in the LPBF 350/700 sample demonstrates the formation of an oxide film containing Fe and Mn oxides at the surface and inner regions. The included schematic provides a visual representation of the oxide/metallic layer structure, detailing the calculated thicknesses of these initial layers.

caption: SAED pattern of the interface between phases, where concentric circles indicate overlapped diffraction spots from the Cr-rich phase and the B2/G phases.
summary: The SAED pattern of the interface reveals concentric circles representing overlapped diffraction spots from two distinct phases. Analysis confirms that the Cr-rich phase maintains a Cube-on-Cube orientation relationship with the B2 and G phases, suggesting that one phase acts as a nucleation site for the others during casting.

caption: Tensile stress-strain curves for HT-SB, HT-SB-EP, and HPHT-SB-EP specimens belonging to the 1st series.
summary: The 1st series tensile stress-strain curves illustrate the mechanical response of HT-SB, HT-SB-EP, and HPHT-SB-EP specimens. These plots provide a comparative visualization of the material behavior under tensile loading, serving as a primary indicator of the mechanical properties achieved through the different processing conditions described in the study.

caption: XRD patterns of 316L/IN718 FGM regions 1, 2, and 3 in the as-deposited (AD) condition.
summary: This panel displays the XRD patterns for 316L/IN718 functionally graded materials across three distinct compositional regions in the as-deposited state. Region 1 contains 70–100% IN718, region 2 contains 40–70% IN718, and region 3 contains 0–30% IN718, providing a baseline for structural analysis of the as-fabricated samples.

caption: Chronoamperometric stability test of the Cu8Ni2 (-) || Cu1Ni9 (+) couple performed at a constant cell voltage of 0.23 V.
summary: The Cu8Ni2 || Cu1Ni9 hybrid electrosynthesis system demonstrates excellent stability during a 100-hour chronoamperometric test at 0.23 V. The system maintains a stable current density approaching 150 mA cm-2, proving its durability and superior performance compared to conventional commercial Pt/C electrodes in this specific electrochemical application.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the 880 °C stabilized sample, showing the varied morphologies of intergranular precipitates.
summary: Dark-field TEM analysis of the sample stabilized at 880 °C reveals a diverse range of precipitate morphologies, including granular, rod-shaped, and needle-shaped structures. This imaging confirms the microstructural findings observed in the SEM analysis, providing further evidence of the precipitate characteristics present after this specific high-temperature stabilization treatment.

caption: 16O− distribution map at the crack tip corresponding to a ΔK of approximately 40 MPa√m, showing limited oxygen detection.
summary: The map indicates that 18O− is not detected at the crack tip for the 40 MPa√m condition, with only limited 16O− discerned. This lack of enrichment suggests that at higher crack propagation rates, there is insufficient time for evident oxidation to occur, causing the oxidation effect to diminish significantly.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves representing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the additively manufactured Zn-Mg alloy builds.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves representing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the additively manufactured Zn-Mg alloy builds. These curves provide insight into the corrosion resistance of the printed alloys, serving as a key electrochemical characterization method to evaluate the surface degradation kinetics of the materials in the tested environment.

caption: Raman spectrum of the monolayer MoS2 film, featuring E2g and A1g vibrational modes with a frequency separation of 20.5 cm-1, alongside LO(M) and ZO(M) peaks indicating polycrystallinity.
summary: Raman spectroscopy of the MoS2 film, using a 532 nm laser, confirms the monolayer thickness through the characteristic E2g and A1g vibrational modes with a frequency difference of 20.5 cm-1. Additional LO(M) and ZO(M) peaks are observed, which are attributed to the polycrystalline nature of the synthesized film.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) evolution over time for specimens subjected to 1200-grit size grinding.
summary: This panel illustrates the OCP measurement for specimens prepared via 1200-grit grinding. After a one-hour stabilization period, the curve achieves a steady state, indicating stable electrochemical equilibrium. Consistent with the 1 μm polished samples, the L-PBF specimens exhibit higher OCP values than conventional materials, confirming the impact of surface roughness on electrochemical stability.

caption: B–H hysteresis curves illustrating the magnetic performance of 3D printed bonded magnets.
summary: The B–H hysteresis curves demonstrate the magnetic performance of 3D printed bonded magnets. These curves reveal that the reduction in demagnetising effects within the printed structure contributes to enhanced magnetic properties, specifically resulting in higher remanence (Br) and coercivity (Hci) values compared to conventional counterparts.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curve for geopolymer samples after 3 days of aging, comparing different moduli.
summary: This GCD plot shows the charge-discharge behavior of geopolymer samples after a 3-day aging period. The triangular waveform indicates the material's capacitive nature. The comparison across different moduli highlights how the aging duration and chemical composition influence the electrochemical response and voltage stability of the supercapacitor electrode material.

caption: Debris cloud formation following a 3 km/s impact on an Al 6061-T6 bumper at 20 μs.
summary: This photograph captures the debris cloud generated by a 3 km/s impact on an Al 6061-T6 bumper at 20 μs post-impact. The image illustrates the fragmentation behavior of the aluminum alloy under high-velocity conditions, providing a baseline for comparing the structural response of different bumper materials in this experimental series.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectrum 65 acquired from a dark block-shaped region, confirming a significant chromium enrichment associated with chromium borides.
summary: Spectrum 65 is taken from a dark, block-shaped region within the Colmonoy-5 alloy microstructure. The analysis shows a large concentration of chromium, which is characteristic of the chromium boride phases formed during the sintering process. This confirms the chemical composition of the dark features observed in the micrograph.

caption: XRD pattern of triple-layer Ni-based/2D material nanocomposite coating featuring anomalous diffraction peaks at 37.8° and 43.7°.
summary: The XRD pattern for the triple-layer coating shows results generally consistent with the double-layer configuration but introduces unique features. Specifically, anomalous diffraction peaks emerge at approximately 37.8° and 43.7°, which are absent in single-layer or double-layer samples, suggesting distinct structural or phase changes induced by the triple-layer architecture.

caption: Schematic representation illustrating the extraction strategy for tensile specimens from the bulk material.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the specific sampling locations used for extracting tensile specimens from the material. According to the study, this figure serves as a guide for the specimen preparation process, ensuring consistent extraction methods for the tensile testing performed on the SCM440, S material, and D material samples.

caption: EBSD orientation map of the Inconel-625/CuNiSiCr interface region showing a bimodal grain size distribution.
summary: The EBSD orientation map reveals the grain structure at the transition zone between Inconel-625 and CuNiSiCr alloys. A bimodal grain size distribution is observed, characterized by coarse grains exceeding 100 μm coexisting with extremely fine crystals smaller than 5 μm, which are predominantly located on the Cu-rich side of the interface.

caption: Calculated dissolution temperatures of precipitated phases in the alloy using JMatPro software.
summary: This panel displays the calculated dissolution temperatures of various precipitated phases within the alloy, derived using JMatPro software. The data illustrates the thermal stability of different carbide phases, specifically showing that M6C and M23C6 carbide contents decrease toward zero as temperature increases, while MC carbides maintain high thermal stability.

caption: LIME significance values for spectrogram elements across six representative porous and non-porous surfels, highlighting the contribution of specific frequency bands.
summary: This plot displays LIME significance values for spectrogram elements across six representative porous and non-porous surfels. Analysis reveals that elements within the 11.64–13.97 kHz frequency band, corresponding to indices 30–36, exhibit positive significance between 0.01 and 0.03 for porous surfels, demonstrating the model's ability to identify discriminative spectral features.

caption: Experimental configuration showing the Zwick Roel Z100 machine utilized for performing uni-axial tensile tests at a constant speed of 5 mm/min.
summary: The tensile testing setup is displayed, featuring the Zwick Roel Z100 machine used to conduct uni-axial tensile tests. Specimens were loaded into this apparatus and tested at a crosshead speed of 5 mm/min until fracture occurred. This configuration enabled the systematic testing of three samples per material for averaged results.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from 11 distinct points across the joint, showing consistent deformation behavior with a notable deviation at point 5.
summary: Load-depth curves for 11 points across the joint reveal generally similar deformation shapes and tendencies. Point 5 exhibits a relatively low deformation ratio, which highlights the strengthening effect of the bonding interface. These curves demonstrate the mechanical response of the joint material under localized nanoindentation loading conditions.

caption: Cyclic stability of CO2 adsorption capacity for geopolymer specimens over multiple adsorption-desorption cycles at 20 °C.
summary: Performance of geopolymer specimens during repeated adsorption-desorption cycles at 20 °C is depicted here. Similar to the 0 °C results, the CO2 adsorption capacity shows a slight decline with an increasing number of cycles, confirming the consistent trend of minor capacity loss during the cyclic operation of these materials.

caption: Measured mechanical properties of 55 normal and 10 deformed hexagonal lattice parts plotted as a function of CAD design parameters L, T, and S, showing the distribution of experimental data.
summary: This plot summarizes the mechanical properties measured in both X and Y directions for a dataset of 55 normal and 10 deformed hexagonal lattice parts. It correlates these properties with CAD design parameters, revealing discrepancies between analytical predictions and actual measured values, such as the observed k LE of 1,422.8 kPa.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of 25 randomly generated Al0.3Ga0.7As/GaAs resonant tunneling diodes (RTDs) featuring interface roughness (IR) compared against a smooth reference device.
summary: This plot displays the I-V characteristics of 25 randomly generated RTDs with interface roughness (gray dashed lines), an average performance curve (red dotted line), and a smooth control device (black solid line). The data demonstrates that interface roughness significantly reduces current and shifts the resonant peak bias to higher values.

caption: Surface-to-skeleton distance visualization, showing domain surfaces in blue and skeleton segments in red, used to compute mean distance metrics.
summary: This panel visualizes the domain surfaces in blue and the skeleton segments in red to facilitate the calculation of the mean distance from the surface to the nearest skeleton segment. This quantitative measurement is essential for characterizing the internal geometric relationship between the precipitate surface and its central skeleton.

caption: Critical configuration demonstrating the pinning of the trailing dislocation due to an attractive interaction caused by a negative lattice misfit of -0.5%.
summary: Under a negative 0.5% lattice misfit, the interaction becomes attractive. This configuration highlights the pinning of the trailing dislocation on the exit side. This attractive stress becomes the dominant factor in determining the critical configuration, significantly influencing the bypass stress compared to the repulsive or baseline conditions.

caption: Electronic dispersion of Rb-doped SnSbBiTe4 along the Γ-M direction, accompanied by an energy distribution curve at Γ showing the topological surface state relative to the Rashba band.
summary: Following Rb deposition, ARPES measurements along the Γ-M direction show the emergence of a Dirac surface state. An energy distribution curve extracted at Γ confirms the position of this topological surface state relative to the prominent Rashba spin-split surface band, consistent with the observed electronic structure changes.

caption: Ranking of MEP, TS, and RS control parameters for the FX response.
summary: This panel displays the ranking of MEP, TS, and RS control parameters specifically for the FX response. Derived from the second stage of optimization using a Full Factorial design, the plot illustrates the relative importance of these parameters in influencing the FX output within the experimental optimization framework.

caption: Impedance stability of HPTH60 i-wi material monitored over 100 cycles of 100% mechanical extension.
summary: This panel demonstrates the impedance stability of the HPTH60 material during 100 cycles of 100% extension. The results confirm that the impedance values remain stable throughout the cyclic mechanical testing, indicating robust electrical performance and durability of the i-wi material under repeated strain conditions.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of a TEM lamella extracted from the single-crystal region at Z = 7 mm, revealing the γ′-phase separated by γ-channels.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the microstructure of the as-deposited sample extracted from the bulk single-crystal region at Z = 7 mm. The micrograph clearly resolves the γ′-phase separated by γ-channels, providing a high-contrast visualization of the internal phase distribution within the single-crystal material structure.

caption: Orientation distribution function (ODF) section of 316L stainless steel, illustrating the specific crystallographic texture characteristics.
summary: The ODF section for 316L stainless steel reveals distinct texture characteristics compared to the MA316L variant. These orientation distributions are essential for understanding the material's crystallographic state, as the orientation distribution function provides a comprehensive view of the texture components present within the cross-sectional section of the sample.

caption: Normalized Raman spectra focusing on the 1550–1800 cm⁻¹ region, highlighting the C=C and C=O bond peaks for all treatment conditions.
summary: Focusing on the 1550–1800 cm⁻¹ range, this panel presents normalized Raman spectra to better resolve differences in the degree of conversion. By isolating the C=C and C=O bond peaks, the plot facilitates a detailed band profile analysis, which is essential for accurately estimating the degree of conversion across the various treated samples.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) strain measurements illustrating the localized deformation patterns within the MBLM Zone B.
summary: Structural deformation within the MBLM Zone B is analyzed using DIC strain measurements. Images captured by the VIC-2D system were processed to map the strain distribution, providing a detailed visualization of the material's mechanical response and deformation patterns during the compression testing process.

caption: Live/dead staining results at 7 days post-encapsulation, confirming cell viability on both the PLA scaffold surfaces and within the hydrogel matrices prior to the initiation of experimental vibration protocols.
summary: Live/dead staining performed at 7 days post-encapsulation demonstrates that cells remain viable on both the PLA surfaces and within the hydrogel components. This assessment confirms the health of the cell populations before the start of the experimental vibration protocols, ensuring a baseline for subsequent analysis.

caption: Evolution of the α-AlFeMnSi (022) reference peak during heating at a rate of 0.03 K s⁻¹.
summary: Shown here is the synchrotron diffraction signal for the α-AlFeMnSi (022) reference peak during a heating experiment at 0.03 K s⁻¹. The signal quality is impacted by noise, which increases noticeably as the count intensity decreases, reflecting the challenges of tracking low-intensity peaks during rapid thermal cycling experiments.

caption: Coulombic efficiency and cyclic stability performance of the supercapacitor devices, demonstrating long-term operational reliability.
summary: Cyclic stability of the supercapacitor devices is illustrated to assess long-term performance. This parameter is critical for evaluating the durability and operational reliability of the 3D-TPU/WS2/CB composite electrodes over repeated charge-discharge cycles, providing essential data on the efficiency and degradation characteristics of the energy storage system under practical usage conditions.

caption: Single point load cell (PW4M model) positioned beneath the spreading platform to enable in situ measurement of powder layer density with an accuracy of ± 10 mg.
summary: The PW4M single point load cell, supplied by HBK and customized by Fine-Spect, is shown integrated under the spreading platform. This component allows for the in situ calculation of powder layer density, supporting mass measurements up to 3 kg with a precision of ± 10 mg.

caption: Detailed view of the RF applicator assembly, which includes two parallel copper plate electrodes and four threaded Teflon rods for adjusting electrode spacing, containing a sample box with doped and undoped powder sections.
summary: This photograph illustrates the RF applicator configuration, which consists of two parallel copper plate electrodes and four threaded Teflon rods used to precisely adjust the spacing between them. A sample box is positioned within the applicator, containing distinct dark grey and white sections representing doped and undoped powders, respectively.

caption: Transmittance spectra of 0.1 wt% A-CNC/CTFA resin samples subjected to varying ultrasonication durations.
summary: Transmittance spectra of 0.1 wt% A-CNC/CTFA resin samples are presented for various sonication times. The data demonstrates that increasing the ultrasonication duration enhances the transparency of the composite resin ink, which serves as a direct indicator of improved A-CNC dispersion within the resin matrix.

caption: Temperature-dependent resistivity curves for bare Nb (blue) and TI-patterned (red) bridge segments, illustrating the superconducting transition behavior.
summary: This plot displays the temperature dependence of resistivity for bare Nb and TI-patterned bridge segments. The data reveals a sharp superconducting transition in both regions, with the patterned segment exhibiting a slight reduction in the transition temperature by approximately 0.05 K compared to the bare Nb segment.

caption: Processing window for WE43 alloy showing regions of varying energy input.
summary: This processing window for WE43 alloy illustrates the relationship between energy input and process parameters. The map highlights terminal sections representing distinct regions of low and high energy input. These parameters are critical for controlling the cooling rates, which ultimately influence the refined microstructure observed in the SLM-processed WE43 samples.

caption: Cycling performance of Sn–Ni alloy films over 100 cycles, illustrating the capacity retention characteristics of the material.
summary: Cycling performances of the Sn–Ni films are summarized over 100 cycles. The data indicates that the Ni3Sn4 phase exhibits limited activity for sodium, which is consistent with the charge–discharge test results. This plot highlights the long-term stability and capacity retention of the Sn–Ni alloy films during electrochemical cycling.

caption: IPF//ND reconstructed β grains map for the 180 A Ti/TiCp composite coating, showing the presence of coarse primary β grains that indicate chain-like TiC does not effectively nucleate primary β-Ti.
summary: Reconstructed β grains map for the 180 A condition reveals the presence of coarse primary β grains. The lack of grain refinement suggests that the chain-like TiC particles do not serve as effective nucleation sites for primary β-Ti, as grain growth typically proceeds perpendicular to the molten pool boundary.

caption: Determined values of notch root diameter and corresponding mass loss after ECP for all specimen sets.
summary: This chart presents the notch root diameter and the associated mass loss resulting from the electrochemical polishing process. It quantifies the material removal and dimensional changes occurring in the notched area for all specimen sets, providing insight into the efficiency and impact of the ECP treatment.

caption: Deformation progression of a thick hinge structure with a thickness of 2 mm, shown across various global strain levels.
summary: The deformation of a 2 mm thick hinge structure is documented at increasing global strain increments. Similar to the thinner variant, this structure exhibits strong auxetic behavior and negative Poisson's ratios. Visual evidence confirms that densification occurs at approximately 0.35 global strain, consistent with the observed mechanical response of the system.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the Nimolloy-202-H alloy tip, illustrating the spatial distribution of elements.
summary: This panel presents an atom probe tomography reconstruction of the Nimolloy-202-H alloy tip. The analysis provides a three-dimensional visualization of the material's microstructure, serving as the basis for further quantitative evaluation of the elemental distribution within the analyzed specimen, as detailed in the accompanying proximity histogram analysis.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of 3D printed (AM) FPEA-ProGly samples, illustrating the spectral changes observed before and after the click chemistry reaction with MMC.
summary: The UV-Vis spectra of 3D printed FPEA-ProGly samples are displayed, demonstrating a reaction behavior comparable to the film counterparts. These results indicate that the click chemistry process with MMC successfully modifies the 3D printed material, as evidenced by the spectral shifts observed before and after the UV-initiated reaction.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of FPEA-ProGly film samples, comparing the material state before and after the click chemistry reaction with MMC in the presence of UV light.
summary: Presented here are the UV-Vis spectra for FPEA-ProGly films, highlighting the spectral evolution resulting from the click reaction with MMC. The comparison between the pre- and post-reaction states demonstrates the effectiveness of the photo-initiated click chemistry process on the FPEA-ProGly polymer film samples.

caption: Perfect lattice configuration of the W-DED Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy interface under medium heat input conditions.
summary: This panel displays the initial perfect lattice structure of the W-DED Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy interface as predicted by molecular dynamics simulations. It serves as the baseline reference for the atomic configuration evolution observed under medium heat input conditions, representing the pristine state before the introduction of radiation-induced damage.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the experimentally corrected numerical scheme designed to estimate elastic and thermal strains.
summary: This flowchart outlines the comprehensive numerical methodology employed to calculate elastic and thermal strains. By integrating experimental data into the numerical framework, the scheme provides a robust approach for strain estimation. The diagram serves as a central reference for the overall computational process described in the study's methodology.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis confirming the equiatomic chemical composition of the hot rolled FeCoCrNiMn HEA.
summary: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the hot rolled sample confirms an equiatomic composition of Co 20.69, Cr 20.48, Fe 20.42, Ni 19.45, and Mn 18.96 at%. These results verify that the alloy maintains its intended equiatomic FeCoCrNiMn HEA stoichiometry after the hot rolling process.

caption: Room temperature X-ray diffraction pattern of as-quenched Ni 0.895 Cr 0.105 MnGe 1.05 ribbon flakes, exhibiting enhanced intensity for (002) and (004) peaks due to texture along the (00l) direction.
summary: The XRD pattern for as-quenched ribbon flakes of Ni 0.895 Cr 0.105 MnGe 1.05 shows a distinct relative increase in the intensity of (002) and (004) peaks. This observation confirms a preferred crystallographic texture along the (00l) direction, which is consistent with structural features observed in corresponding SEM images.

caption: Compressive strength of the grid (GRI) pattern as a function of porosity, modeled using the Ryshkewitch equation.
summary: This panel displays the compressive strength of the grid pattern plotted against porosity. The data follows the Ryshkewitch relationship defined by the equation σ = 1033.e −0.083.P, with a high correlation coefficient of R2 = 0.977, demonstrating the predictable mechanical behavior of the grid structure across varying porosity levels.

caption: STEM ADF image of the Stripes strategy sample, showing the distribution of dislocation density zones and entanglement regions.
summary: STEM ADF imaging of the Stripes strategy provides a representative view of the dislocation structures. High-resolution TEM analysis at various magnifications confirms that scan strategies lead to distinct dislocation arrangements. These findings are essential for correlating the fabrication method with the observed dislocation density and subsequent material performance characteristics.

caption: RLC–T heating response for steel S3, illustrating a broadened austenitizing transition that lacks a unique T A value compared to other steels.
summary: Steel S3 displays a complex thermal response during heating, characterized by a broadened austenitizing transition in the RLC–T curve. Unlike the other steels in the study, this material does not exhibit a unique T A value, indicating a more gradual phase transformation process during the austenitization stage.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves comparing LARed and LAR-LSPed tensile specimens, demonstrating high process stability and repeatability through overlapping curves within each group.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for LARed and LAR-LSPed specimens are presented to evaluate tensile performance. The curves within each group show high consistency, confirming the stability and repeatability of the LAR and LSP processing methods. These results serve as the foundation for assessing the mechanical improvements achieved by the LSP treatment.

caption: Intensity map representing plastic deformation events associated with the 50/50 composition ratio region under 372.5 MPa stress.
summary: Plastic deformation event intensities are visualized in this map for the 50/50 composition ratio region. By highlighting the spatial distribution of these events at 372.5 MPa, the panel provides insight into the localized plastic activity occurring within the FGM gauge length during the applied mechanical stress test.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile for specimen 2, highlighting differences between BD (red) and SD (black) states.
summary: Specimen 2 is characterized by its neutron diffraction peak profile, which displays the structural response under BD (red) and SD (black) conditions. This initial profile serves as a baseline for evaluating the specimen's crystalline properties, contributing to the comparative analysis of the four different specimens examined in the study.

caption: Microstructural EPMA point analysis of B4C CoCrFeMnNi, distinguishing between cell boundary and cell interior characteristics.
summary: Focusing on the B4C CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy composite, this EPMA point analysis characterizes the cell boundary (Point C) and cell interior (Point D). These findings support the investigation into the partial elemental decomposition of B4C nanoparticles, illustrating how these elements are distributed within the composite microstructure following the DED process.

caption: Comparison of mean percentage error (%) and mean error (N) across various tested temperatures, visualized through solid-colored and dashed-line box plots respectively.
summary: This panel displays the mean percentage error and mean error values across tested temperatures using solid-colored and dashed-line box plots. These visualizations demonstrate the error metrics, with t-statistic values confirming no significant deviations at 200 °C and elevated temperatures, supporting the overall finding of consistent performance across the tested thermal range.

caption: Ti-Ni binary phase diagram utilized to analyze the thermodynamic stability and formation of intermetallic compounds such as NiTi and Ti2Ni during the welding process.
summary: Panel (b) displays the Ti-Ni binary phase diagram, which acts as a theoretical framework for understanding the reaction equations and formation enthalpies of NiTi and Ti2Ni intermetallics. This diagram is critical for interpreting the microstructural evolution observed at the fusion zone interfaces during the resistance spot welding process.

caption: Thermal expansion coefficient (TEC) curves for alloys 1.6H and 1.6L measured between 100 °C and 900 °C.
summary: This panel displays the TEC curves for alloys 1.6H and 1.6L across a temperature range of 100 °C to 900 °C. For these alloys, which lack a γ′ phase, the data indicates that the TEC value decreases slightly as the Al/Ti ratio is reduced.

caption: Integrated synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern of the as-deposited NiTiCu sample obtained after full azimuthal integration.
summary: This panel displays the synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern for the as-deposited NiTiCu sample. The data represents the diffractogram generated after performing a full integration along the azimuthal angle, providing a comprehensive overview of the structural diffraction characteristics of the material in its as-deposited state.

caption: Mechanical load–displacement behavior observed during indentation of the anodic film on AA7075-T6 tempered aluminum alloy.
summary: This panel shows the raw load-displacement data for the anodic film formed on AA7075-T6 tempered aluminum. The curve characterizes the indentation response of the film, documenting the force applied relative to the penetration depth, which is critical for evaluating the mechanical performance of the T6-tempered material.

caption: Entropy change -ΔSm as a function of temperature for the x = 0.5 alloy, illustrating the magnetic response across the structural phase transition under varying magnetic field strengths.
summary: Representing the x = 0.5 alloy, this graph shows the temperature dependence of -ΔSm near the structural phase transition. Derived from Eq. (1) for fields up to 7 T, the results characterize the magnetic entropy changes, which are critical for evaluating the material's relative cooling power in this specific composition.

caption: Compositional path calibration for Ti60-Ti2AlNb dual alloys, illustrating transition zone widths of 12 mm (solid line) and 4 mm (dashed line) within the Ti-Al-Nb ternary system at 700 °C.
summary: This panel displays the compositional distribution paths for Ti60-Ti2AlNb dual alloys calculated via Thermo-Calc at 700 °C. It compares two distinct transition zone widths, 12 mm and 4 mm, represented by solid and dashed lines respectively, to calibrate the phase equilibrium relations within the ternary Ti-Al-Nb system.

caption: Two-dimensional micro-CT cross-section of a gyroid structure with 81.7% porosity, illustrating internal pore connectivity and trapped residual powder.
summary: This 2D micro-CT image displays the internal architecture of a gyroid structure with 81.7% porosity. Similar to the optical micrograph, this visualization confirms that residual powder is trapped within the interconnected pores during fabrication, contributing to structural heterogeneity within the printed material.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the joint interface prepared under a bonding pressure of 10 MPa.
summary: This histogram details the grain size distribution for the joint interface processed at 10 MPa. The data highlights the impact of increased bonding pressure on grain size, supporting the broader EBSD analysis which shows that microstructure and interfacial properties are highly sensitive to these processing parameters.

caption: Comparison of simulated and measured reflection coefficient values for the 2.4 GHz antenna design.
summary: This plot displays the reflection coefficient for a 2.4 GHz antenna design, comparing simulated data against actual measurements. The results demonstrate good agreement between the simulated and measured performance, validating the design approach for the antenna configuration as described in the study's performance evaluation for the 2.4 GHz frequency band.

caption: Experimental setup for quasi-static compression testing of the ISS using a CMT-5105GL testing machine at room temperature with a 12 mm displacement.
summary: This panel displays the experimental configuration for the quasi-static compression test of the ISS. Conducted at room temperature using a CMT-5105GL testing machine, the setup involves a controlled compression displacement of 12 mm to evaluate the mechanical response of the specimen under quasi-static loading conditions.

caption: Comparison of final average CoF values for 0°, 45°, and 90° samples, showing calculated values of 0.66, 0.91, and 0.68, respectively.
summary: Final average coefficient of friction values are compared across the three sample orientations. While initial frictional responses varied significantly, the final CoF values for all samples converged to nearly identical levels, with calculated averages of 0.66 for 0°, 0.91 for 45°, and 0.68 for 90° samples.

caption: Maximum tool flank wear (VB max) progression curves for CM and UAM conditions.
summary: Maximum tool flank wear (VB max) is plotted against cutting duration for both CM and UAM methods. The data shows a trend similar to the average VB measurements, confirming that ultrasonic vibration serves as an effective mechanism to retard the progression of tool wear throughout the cutting operation.

caption: Elemental distribution map of aluminum within the DAZ region.
summary: Elemental distribution map of aluminum within the DAZ region. This map displays the spatial variation of aluminum, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of the elemental makeup of the DAZ. The results are consistent with the broader elemental mapping analysis conducted on the specimen using STEM-based techniques.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves illustrating the discriminative performance of the default split learning model across various classification thresholds.
summary: The ROC-AUC curves demonstrate the discriminative ability of the default split learning model, providing an evaluation independent of a fixed decision threshold. By capturing probability rankings across all thresholds, these curves indicate strong class separability, confirming that high AUC values reflect robust model performance even when class overlap exists.

caption: Normalized Co K-edge XANES spectra for all samples, illustrating the electronic state of cobalt.
summary: Normalized Co K-edge XANES spectra are displayed for all samples. The spectrum of Ni1Co3@NC closely matches that of Co foil, suggesting that cobalt is present in a metallic state. This finding aligns with results from XRD and XPS analyses, supporting the metallic character of the cobalt species.

caption: Hysteresis loops comparing raw and reacted SmCo magnets, demonstrating that the magnetic properties remain largely unchanged after the corrosion process.
summary: This panel displays the M-H hysteresis loops for raw and reacted SmCo magnets.
