caption: Statistical R-squared values derived from fitting various mathematical models to the drug release kinetics of the thermosensitive printlets.
summary: Statistical analysis of the drug release kinetics from the prepared thermosensitive printlets was conducted using various mathematical models. This table presents the R-squared values obtained from these fittings, providing a quantitative assessment of how well the experimental release data aligns with established kinetic release models.

caption: Collection of printed NdFeB permanent magnets demonstrating diverse 3D geometries, including circular, variable-diameter, pyramidal, and twisted toroidal structures.
summary: This photograph showcases the versatility of the printing process by displaying NdFeB permanent magnets with diverse shapes, such as circular, variable-diameter, pyramidal, and twisted toroidal structures. This development offers improved magnetic-field control solutions for various high-tech applications, demonstrating the potential for creating complex, functional magnetic components through additive manufacturing.

caption: Terahertz imaging of the sample bottom surface illustrating the signal response from the lower interface.
summary: This panel displays a terahertz image of the sample's bottom surface. By focusing on the lower interface, the imaging technique reveals structural details and signal variations across the bottom side of the specimen, facilitating a comprehensive assessment of the sample's internal and external integrity through THz wave interaction.

caption: Improved hardness uniformity observed in the columnar zone of H13 ESR ingots processed at 500 A with an axial static magnetic field.
summary: Enhanced hardness uniformity in the columnar zone of H13 ESR ingots is achieved at 500 A with an axial static magnetic field. This improvement is linked to the refinement of dendrites and carbides, as well as the increased efficiency of inclusion removal during the magnetic controlled electroslag remelting process.

caption: Intrinsic stacking fault energy (Γsf) of the metastable FCC phase in binary CoCrFeNi-W as a function of W concentration, calculated using the TTNI8 database and validated against experimental data from literature.
summary: The intrinsic stacking fault energy of the metastable FCC phase in CoCrFeNi-W alloys is plotted against W concentration. Calculated using the TTNI8 database, these simulation results are compared with experimental data to characterize the influence of tungsten alloying on the stacking fault energy of the FCC matrix.

caption: Product of flow stress increment and hardening rate (σ - σ0.2)θ plotted as a function of the flow stress increment (σ - σ0.2).
summary: The relationship between the rate of dislocation storage and the dislocation density throughout the entire strain hardening stage is represented in this plot. By analyzing the product of the flow stress increment and the hardening rate, the underlying dislocation storage kinetics can be derived for the GBEed samples under different TMP conditions.

caption: Intermediate deformation stage at 600 K demonstrating GB migration and grain shape evolution.
summary: Under the influence of shear stress at 600 K, this snapshot reveals active grain boundary migration. This process leads to observable changes in the size and morphology of the nanocrystalline grains, illustrating how thermal energy facilitates structural reconfiguration and plastic flow in the Ni–Al superalloy during the tensile test.

caption: Design of the additive manufacturing pre-form sample.
summary: The design of the additive manufacturing pre-form sample is presented here. This schematic details the geometry and structural configuration of the pre-form component, which acts as the starting material for the subsequent forging process, highlighting the integration of additive manufacturing within the overall hybrid production workflow.

caption: Comparison of residual stress profiles along the build direction between numerical simulation results and experimental neutron diffraction measurements.
summary: This panel displays a comparative analysis of residual stress profiles along the build direction. The data contrasts numerical simulation predictions with experimental neutron diffraction measurements. The axial stress profiles exhibit a characteristic balance, featuring compressive stresses of approximately -200 MPa near the center and tensile stresses reaching 500 MPa at the edges.

caption: Ti-Al alloy system phase diagram identifying solid-state transformation temperatures Tα and Te.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the Ti-Al system delineates the solid-state transformation temperatures, specifically Tα for the α→α+γ transition and Te for the α or (α+γ)→α2+γ transition. These equilibrium temperatures are critical for understanding the phase evolution and microstructural stability of the Ti4822 alloy during thermal processing.

caption: Comparison of stored energy values for S, C, B, and Cube crystallographic components in S-0 and S-40 samples as determined by neutron diffraction analysis.
summary: Neutron diffraction measurements reveal the stored energy levels for S, C, B, and Cube components in deformed S-0 and S-40 samples. Analysis indicates that the stored energy for the S and C orientations increases with sulfur addition, demonstrating that sulfur content significantly influences the stored energy characteristics of these specific crystallographic components.

caption: Surface trace visualization of grain 6 extracted from the material microstructure.
summary: This panel displays the surface trace of grain 6, which is part of a broader analysis investigating grain orientation changes and phase transformation under a loading force of 252 N. The trace provides a localized view of the grain's structural response during the mechanical loading process.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of TiO2 films synthesized through a multilayer deposition process.
summary: FTIR spectra for TiO2 films deposited via a multilayer process are shown. This spectroscopic analysis provides information on the chemical bonding and molecular vibrations within the multilayered coatings, serving as a characterization tool to evaluate the structural integrity and chemical composition of the films across the different layers.

caption: TGA thermograms of printed materials showing weight loss and derivative weight loss curves over the 50–500°C temperature range.
summary: TGA thermograms for the printed materials are presented over a 50–500°C range, displaying both weight loss and derivative weight loss curves. Analysis of the temperature range for volatile products indicates a mass loss of 0.8–1% for the three samples between 50 and 190°C, consistent with low mass compounds.

caption: In situ SANS scattering curves for sample VB92, previously fatigue-cycled at 900 °C, during a thermal cycle of RT-700-800-900 °C-RT.
summary: Sample VB92, previously cycled at 900 °C, is analyzed via in situ SANS during a thermal cycle up to 900 °C. Similar to the undeformed sample, the scattering data indicates the formation of 30–40 Å large precipitates at 700 °C, highlighting the temperature-dependent structural changes in the superalloy.

caption: Irradiance profile of the diffracted field along the horizontal x-direction for a PDOE illuminated by a plane wave linearly polarized at ±45°. Green and red symbols denote the polarization states for input diagonal (D) and antidiagonal (A) polarizations, respectively, showing distinct states across the diffraction pattern.
summary: The irradiance profile displays the diffracted field along the horizontal axis for input diagonal and antidiagonal polarizations. Green and red symbols indicate specific polarization states across the pattern. At certain locations, these states coincide as linear, while at others, they manifest as orthogonal circular states, reflecting the underlying diffracted field behavior.

caption: Comparison of current-voltage (I-V) characteristics between the ballistic transport regime (orange dashed line with diagonal cross markers) and the regime incorporating acoustic electron-phonon scattering (black line with plus markers).
summary: This plot illustrates the impact of acoustic electron-phonon scattering on electronic transport. By comparing the ballistic regime with the scattering-inclusive model, it is evident that the inclusion of electron-phonon interactions significantly reduces the overall current and shifts the resonant peak bias V r to a lower bias value.

caption: Fracture strain comparison between WAAM ER70S-6 steel and conventional mild steels plotted in the Lode parameter (θ¯) versus equivalent fracture strain (ε‾f) plane.
summary: This panel displays the fracture loci of WAAM ER70S-6 steel plates in the Lode parameter versus equivalent fracture strain plane. It provides a comparative analysis against conventional mild steels, incorporating fracture test data to evaluate the material's ductility and failure characteristics under varying stress states as defined by the Lode parameter.

caption: High-energy X-ray diffraction (HEXRD) patterns comparing the as-built state at room temperature with annealed conditions at room temperature, 900°C, and 1100°C for LPBF-processed cylinders preheated at 650°C.
summary: HEXRD spectra reveal the phase evolution of LPBF-processed cylinders. The persistence and intensity increase of peaks after annealing confirm the stability and growth of M2Zr and M23Zr6 phases. Furthermore, the preservation of these peaks during in-situ high-temperature acquisitions demonstrates the high thermal stability of the constituent phases within the alloy.

caption: Stress nephogram of the vertically printed sample during the first loading cycle under OP conditions.
summary: This panel displays the stress distribution nephogram for a vertically printed sample subjected to the first loading cycle under OP conditions. The visualization provides a spatial representation of stress concentrations, serving as the baseline for evaluating mechanical performance and material response during initial deformation stages in the fatigue testing sequence.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance behavior of samples immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution for 24 hours.
summary: This Bode plot represents the frequency-dependent impedance response of samples after 24 hours of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The inclusion of a constant phase element (CPE) in the analysis is essential to model the non-ideal capacitive behavior and ensure an optimal fit for the experimental data.

caption: Fatigue S-N data for single-crystal DD6 alloy tested at 1000 °C and 1100 °C, illustrating the dependence of failure modes on temperature and stress levels.
summary: Single-crystal DD6 alloy specimens tested at 1000 °C predominantly exhibit Stage I cracking, with one exception showing Mode I cracking. Conversely, all specimens tested at 1100 °C are characterized by Mode I cracking. The plot demonstrates how temperature influences the dominant failure mechanism in this single-crystal superalloy.

caption: Backscattered electron image and corresponding EDS elemental map showing the interface between Cu0 and Cu25 regions where solidification cracking initiates in the IN625-CuCrZr FGAM sample.
summary: This panel displays the initiation of a solidification crack at the interface of the Cu0 and Cu25 regions in an IN625-CuCrZr sample. The BSE image combined with EDS elemental mapping highlights the specific location where the crack originates within the first melt pool of the Cu25 region.

caption: Specific impact strength comparison of sandwich infill versus single infill samples.
summary: Specific impact strength is evaluated here to determine the strength-to-weight ratio, a critical parameter for lightweight structural design. By comparing sandwich infill and single infill samples, this plot highlights the efficiency of the material distribution, emphasizing the importance of balancing structural integrity with reduced mass in engineering applications.

caption: Quantitative cracking susceptibility map of the Fe-Cu-Ni system using Easton's model, showing composition paths for 10L and Ctrl_10L specimens.
summary: Quantitative estimation of cracking susceptibility is performed using Easton's model for the Fe-Cu-Ni system. The composition paths for specimens 10L and Ctrl_10L are plotted, demonstrating that the use of a Ni buffer or low dilution ratios effectively maintains the alloy composition within low-cracking susceptible regions of the ternary space.

caption: Tabulated average grain size values corresponding to the fitted ellipse major diameter measurements shown in the distribution plots.
summary: This table provides the quantitative average grain size data derived from the fitted ellipse major diameter measurements. These values correspond directly to the grain size distributions presented in panel (a), serving as a summary of the microstructural characteristic lengths for the analyzed Hastelloy X sets.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver calculation of elemental segregation profiles for Ta, Cr, Mo, and Hf, demonstrating enrichment in inter-dendritic regions where the solid fraction f_s approaches 1.0.
summary: This panel presents Scheil-Gulliver calculations for Ta, Cr, Mo, and Hf, which segregate toward the inter-dendritic boundaries, corresponding to a solid fraction (f_s) of 1.0. This partitioning behavior is directly linked to the formation of MC carbides in the inter-dendritic regions of the René N5 alloy microstructure.

caption: Nyquist plot comparing EIS curves of samples before and after nitriding treatment, highlighting a semicircular capacitive resistance arc in the high-frequency region.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for samples before and after nitriding. A semicircular capacitive resistance arc is observed in the high-frequency region, which indicates a single and dominant electrochemical mechanism associated with charge transfer occurring at the electrode–electrolyte interface during the testing process.

caption: STEM-LAADF image of the same lamella region, emphasizing grain contrast within the coating and substrate interface.
summary: Utilizing low angle annular dark field imaging, this STEM panel provides complementary grain contrast to the HAADF image. It focuses on the same lamella location, allowing for the visualization of microstructural features and grain boundaries at the interface between the Ti0.45Al0.55N coating and the Ti-5553 alloy substrate.

caption: Native circular dichroism (CD) spectra of CXCL9, HSA-CXCL9(74–103), and HSA recorded between 190 and 250 nm to estimate secondary structure fractions.
summary: Circular dichroism spectra reveal the secondary structure composition of the proteins. The fusion protein HSA-CXCL9(74–103) exhibits a compact folding status characterized by an α-helical signature similar to that of HSA. The low RMSD values confirm the high fidelity of the fusion protein's structural alignment with the native components.

caption: Tubular branching patterns of EPCs observed within GelMA hydrogels of varying concentrations, highlighting the 6% and 8% formulations as having enhanced branching.
summary: Tubular branching of EPCs is visualized across different GelMA hydrogel concentrations. The 6% and 8% GelMA hydrogels exhibited significantly higher tubular branching compared to the other groups, indicating that these specific concentrations are more conducive to the formation of vascular-like structures by the endothelial progenitor cells.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the Al-Sc system showing the thermodynamic stability regions for Al3Sc precipitation.
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram illustrates the thermodynamic stability regions for Al3Sc precipitation within the Al-Sc system. Derived from Scheil module simulations using the TTAL7 database in Thermal-Cal software, the diagram provides the foundational phase formation analysis necessary for understanding the solidification behavior of the 2024Sc alloy.

caption: Raman spectrum of Si-doped BCP treated at 1100 °C, focusing on the 3500-3650 cm⁻¹ range.
summary: Raman spectral analysis of Si-doped BCP samples treated at 1100 °C, specifically within the 3500–3650 cm⁻¹ range, reveals characteristic peaks linked to hydroxyl groups. These results demonstrate the persistence or modification of hydroxyl-related vibrational modes in the material structure following the 1100 °C sintering process compared to lower temperature treatments.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of the 1190SA sample surface following a 120-hour corrosion exposure.
summary: This EDS mapping illustrates the elemental distribution on the 1190SA sample surface after 120 hours of corrosion. Analysis reveals that the resulting cluster phase is enriched in oxygen, nickel, and trace amounts of aluminum, sulfur, and cobalt, while the spinel phase contains oxygen, aluminum, cobalt, tungsten, and minor quantities of sodium, molybdenum, and carbon.

caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 40% hemp content mix, illustrating the uncertainty range for this specific mix design.
summary: This panel presents the probability distribution for the 40% hemp content mix derived from a Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. The plot visualizes the range of potential global warming impacts for this specific mix design, contributing to the overall assessment of how varying hemp content influences environmental performance metrics.

caption: Radar chart displaying the relative frequency of occurrence for key research terms, providing a quantitative overview of the thematic prevalence in the study.
summary: This radar chart quantifies the relative frequency of occurrence for key research terms identified in the study. By mapping these frequencies, the visualization offers a clear overview of the thematic prevalence, allowing for a comparative assessment of the importance of various keywords within the informatics analysis of the alloy research.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the HT2 specimen cross-sectional fracture surface at 1.2% strain amplitude, demonstrating extensive alpha phase fragmentation.
summary: At a 1.2% strain amplitude, this inverse pole figure map captures the fracture surface of the HT2 specimen. It shows significant alpha phase refinement and fragmentation. The absence of coherent crystallographic orientation patterns within these deflected regions supports the finding that mechanical property gradients are the primary factor governing crack deflection behavior.

caption: Minimum creep rates for PBF-LB/M processed single crystals evaluated using octahedral slip systems across three tensile loading orientations.
summary: This visualization presents the predicted minimum creep rates for PBF-LB/M processed single crystals, focusing on octahedral slip systems. The results are plotted for three tensile loading directions, [001], [011], and [111], based on the material parameter sets provided in Table 3 to characterize the mechanical response of the specimens.

caption: Orientation image map of austenite captured at the same location as panel a, displaying the crystallographic orientations prior to the clustering process.
summary: Representing the austenite phase before clustering, this orientation image map corresponds to the same region as the phase map in panel a. The visualization confirms that the crystallographic orientations of the retained austenite regions remain stable and are not altered during the parent grain reconstruction process using the variant graph approach.

caption: Stress versus Larson-Miller parameter plot comparing standard and modified PBF-LB Ni230 samples against wrought Haynes 230 and previously reported PBF-LB Haynes 230 data.
summary: This plot evaluates the creep performance of standard and modified PBF-LB Ni230 by plotting stress against the Larson-Miller parameter. It benchmarks these results against wrought Haynes 230 sheet and plate data, as well as literature values for PBF-LB Haynes 230, to assess material performance across varying temperatures and stress conditions.

caption: Electrochemical impedance Nyquist plot for SLM 316L stainless steel samples processed at a laser scanning speed of 1000 mm/s following 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution.
summary: Representing the electrochemical impedance of SLM 316L stainless steel, this Nyquist plot corresponds to a laser scanning speed of 1000 mm/s. The measurement was taken after 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution, characterizing the electrochemical interface and corrosion behavior of the sample under these specific fabrication and environmental conditions.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the bottom region of the slow deposition along the <011> Al zone axis, showing the microstructural state of the material at the base of the slow deposition process.
summary: The bottom region of the slow deposition is examined using bright-field STEM along the <011> Al zone axis. This image provides a visual record of the precipitate distribution and morphology at the base of the slow deposition, completing the characterization of the centerline microstructure for this specific processing condition.

caption: Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model performance evaluation showing predicted versus actual values.
summary: Multi-Layer Perceptron model performance is depicted via a parity plot, comparing predicted outputs to actual experimental values. This analysis is included among the various methods tested to determine the most suitable machine learning approach, providing insight into the neural network's ability to capture complex relationships in the data.

caption: Voltage-time profiles for V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) at varying current densities from 80 to 160 mA cm -2.
summary: The voltage-time profiles for the V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) electrolyte exhibit stable performance across various current densities. The observed minor increases in overpotential at higher current densities indicate robust electrochemical kinetics, confirming the material's suitability for high-power vanadium redox flow battery applications.

caption: Evolution of austenite and martensite phase fractions as a function of applied magnetic field at 230 K, showing a complete reverse martensitic transformation during field increase to 6.5 T and a forward transformation upon field reduction to 0 T, with a magnetic hysteresis of approximately 0.2 T.
summary: This plot illustrates the phase fraction variation of austenite and martensite at 230 K under a cycling magnetic field up to 6.5 T. It highlights a complete reverse martensitic transformation during field increase and a forward transformation during decrease, characterized by a 0.2 T magnetic hysteresis and defined transformation field thresholds.

caption: EML curve characterizing the magnetic behavior of the Ni80Fe20 thin film sample at an AC frequency of 12 kHz.
summary: Representing the magnetic response at 12 kHz, this EML curve for the 59 nm Ni80Fe20 thin film illustrates the magneto-inductance effect. Consistent with other frequencies, the data was collected with 2 Oe magnetic field increments, contributing to the overall observation of the material's room-temperature magnetic properties.

caption: Stress-strain response of the soft Agilus material obtained from tensile testing.
summary: Tensile test results for the soft Agilus material are displayed as stress-strain data. Eight tests were performed to compile the mechanical properties of the material. These findings, alongside the Vero data, form the basis for the subsequent comparative analysis of Young's modulus for both pure and polluted material samples.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of Alloy 718 base material, showing the grain structure and crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The EBSD inverse pole figure map of Alloy 718 depicts the grain structure of the base material. Comparison with G27 reveals that the grain size of Alloy 718 is coarser, being approximately twice as large as that of G27, which is a key factor in evaluating their relative liquation cracking susceptibility.

caption: Mean squared error (MSE) progression over training epochs for scenario 2 of the PEOF-SNF artificial neural network model.
summary: Scenario 2 illustrates the MSE progression across training epochs for the PEOF-SNF model. The epoch-related data confirms the effectiveness of the ANN technique in studying periodic electroosmotic flow dynamics across a stretched surface, as reflected in the small MSE measurements obtained during the model training phase.

caption: Surface deviation map of a vertically printed surgical guide manufactured via CLIP, illustrating dimensional divergence from the CAD model.
summary: This panel presents the surface deviation analysis for a vertically printed surgical guide produced using CLIP. The heatmap visualizes the dimensional accuracy of the guide after steam sterilization, highlighting areas of positive and negative divergence relative to the CAD file to assess manufacturing precision in the vertical orientation.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the heat-treated alloy matrix showing the absence of visible second-phase particles.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging of the heat-treated alloy matrix reveals a clean microstructure. Examination of this region confirms that no second-phase particles are observable at this magnification level, indicating a uniform distribution or lack of coarse precipitates within the Al matrix under the specified heat treatment conditions.

caption: Projection of the input matrix X onto the first and second principal components, with data points colored by their corresponding target values.
summary: The input matrix X is projected onto the two-component space defined by the PLSR model. By coloring the projected data points according to their target values, this visualization reveals the distribution and clustering of the dataset within the reduced-dimensional space, highlighting the relationship between input features and the target variable.

caption: Design variations of Diamond and Gyroid porous structures featuring uniform, positive, and negative gradient porosities at an average relative density of 40%.
summary: Six distinct porous structures, including Diamond and Gyroid architectures, were generated using Matlab software. These designs incorporate uniform porosity (40% UG), positive gradient porosity (30%–50% PG), and negative gradient porosity (50%–40% NG). All models maintain an average relative density of 40%, facilitating a comparative study of structural gradient effects.

caption: Detailed breakdown of the pseudocapacitive contribution within the CV profile at a scan rate of 1 mVs-1.
summary: The CV profile at a scan rate of 1 mVs-1 is analyzed to show the specific pseudocapacitive contribution. This detailed visualization separates the capacitive current from the total current, providing insight into the fast kinetics and surface-controlled storage processes occurring within the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode at higher rates.

caption: Voltage variation curve of a-Si thin-film during the initial charge and discharge process.
summary: The voltage variation curve for the a-Si thin-film is presented during the initial charge and discharge cycle. This material exhibits an average impedance of 8.3 Ω, which is attributed to the poor electronic conductivity of silicon, highlighting the electrochemical performance limitations of pure a-Si thin-film electrodes during cycling.

caption: Inverse fast Fourier transform pattern reconstructed from the selected red points in the FFT pattern of panel e, highlighting specific lattice features.
summary: The IFFT pattern, reconstructed from the red points identified in the FFT analysis, provides a filtered visualization of the lattice structure at the low-angle grain boundary. This technique allows for the isolation and detailed examination of specific crystallographic features or defects present at the interface of the FCC-Fe grains.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation map of Ni-modified DSS 1.4462, oriented parallel to the build direction.
summary: This inverse pole figure map shows the crystallographic orientation of the Ni-modified DSS 1.4462 specimen relative to the build direction. The map provides spatial information on grain orientations, which, when combined with phase data, helps characterize the texture development and microstructural evolution resulting from the specific Ni-modification and heat treatment process.

caption: Simulated porous structure generated using 20 seeds at a fixed porosity of 80%.
summary: This panel displays a simulated porous structure characterized by 20 seeds while maintaining a constant porosity of 80%. The visualization illustrates the spatial distribution and morphology resulting from this specific seed count, serving as one of four comparative structures plotted to analyze the effect of seed density on architecture.

caption: Comparative elemental composition analysis of passive films formed on wrought and SLM-processed specimens, including those subjected to surface peening (SP), after exposure to a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the elemental composition of passive films developed on wrought and SLM-manufactured materials, both with and without surface peening treatments. The data, derived from exposure to a 3.5 wt% NaCl environment, provides a quantitative comparison of film constituents to evaluate the influence of processing methods on corrosion resistance.

caption: Voltage-time response curves recorded during the plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) process under current-controlled conditions.
summary: Voltage-time responses for the developed PEO coatings are presented in current-controlled mode. This plot illustrates the variation in voltage over time throughout the PEO process, providing essential data on the electrochemical behavior and growth kinetics of the coatings as they are formed under controlled electrical parameters.

caption: Architectural overview of the Regressional and Conditional Generative Neural Network (RCGAN) designed for inverse cubic lattice structure design, illustrating the integrated roles of the generator, regressor, and discriminator components.
summary: The RCGAN framework facilitates inverse design of cubic lattice structures through a three-part architecture. A generator synthesizes structures from noise and target properties, a regressor predicts properties and extracts features from these structures, and a discriminator verifies authenticity by evaluating the extracted features and property data against real structural benchmarks.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of a single SiC@C/SiC nanowire illustrating the multilayered internal structure.
summary: This TEM image provides a detailed view of the SiC@C/SiC nanowire. The multilayer structure of the nanowire is clearly evident, demonstrating that the interface between the SiC and carbon components is well-bonded, which is essential for the structural stability of the overall Bouligand nanowire network.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of van der Waals forces and morphological changes during the 100 ps molecular dynamics adsorption process.
summary: Monitoring the adsorption progression over 100 ps reveals the dynamic evolution of morphology and van der Waals forces. The simulation results demonstrate a clear correlation where increasing van der Waals forces directly correspond to the strengthening of bonds between the particles, providing insight into the adsorption mechanism of the system.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of the as-fabricated sample, revealing the local lattice strain and dislocation density distribution within the austenite and martensite phases.
summary: This kernel average misorientation map characterizes the local lattice strain and dislocation density in the as-fabricated sample. Composed of austenite and lath-shaped martensite, the material exhibits specific misorientation patterns. This EBSD analysis serves as a baseline for understanding the internal strain state of the alloy before heat treatment.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the as-built sample microstructure, highlighting dislocation features alongside a 2D Ti contour map that delineates the interdendritic region.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction visualizes the cellular microstructure of an as-built sample. It highlights the presence of dislocations and utilizes a 2D titanium contour map to clearly identify the interdendritic regions, providing a detailed spatial understanding of the material's internal structural features and chemical distribution.

caption: Logarithmic plot of I(q, t) × q^4 versus q^2, highlighting the negative deviation from Porod’s law caused by the depletion of high-angle scattering in the diffuse interface case.
summary: This plot utilizes a logarithmic scale to characterize the negative deviation from Porod’s law observed in the diffuse interface model. By plotting I(q, t) × q^4 against q^2, the graph clearly demonstrates that the presence of a diffuse interface leads to a depletion of scattering intensity at high angles.

caption: Three-dimensional representation of coating adhesion strength as a function of process parameters during LPCS.
summary: This 3D graph illustrates the relationship between LPCS process parameters and coating adhesion strength. The visualization highlights how varying input conditions influence the mechanical performance of the coating, providing a comprehensive view of the parameter space affecting the adhesion strength of the Ni + Al2O3 coating system.

caption: UV-Vis transmission spectra of the immersion solution at pH 10, comparing room temperature and 37 °C conditions, indicating insignificant changes.
summary: The transmission spectra for the buffer solution at an alkaline pH of 10 exhibit insignificant changes over time at both room temperature and 37 °C. These results confirm the stability of the Au NPs within the 3D printed nanocomposite hydrogel across the tested environmental conditions.

caption: 1 nm-thick cross-section of the ReL 1300 model at room temperature, highlighting the atomic environment distribution within the 12.4 nm simulation cell.
summary: The ReL 1300 model is depicted here as a 1 nm-thick cross-section at room temperature. The visualization uses a color-coded scheme to identify distinct local atomic environments of carbon atoms, offering insight into the structural characteristics of the model within its 12.4 nm horizontal and vertical cell dimensions.

caption: Magnified view of the low-Zr content region of the Zr–Mg phase diagram, highlighting the limited solubility of Zr in Mg.
summary: Focusing on the low-Zr content region, this zoomed-in phase diagram illustrates the restricted solubility of Zr in Mg. Consistent with the Mg–Zr system characteristics, the solubility is less than 0.002 at.% in liquid Mg at experimental temperatures and less than 0.005 at.% in solid Mg near the peritectic temperature.

caption: Reduced magnetization curve of a permalloy film measured at an orientation approximately 1.5° from the hard axis, highlighting distinct hysteresis branch crossings in both ascending and descending field directions.
summary: This plot displays the reduced magnetization of a permalloy film under an applied field near the hard axis. The presence of hysteresis branch crossings is clearly visible. Numeric integration confirms that the normal hysteresis loss in the lenticular region exceeds the crossed regions, ensuring consistency with energy conservation principles.

caption: Direct DFT approach illustrating the computational cell setup used to study impurity effects on APB energy in the γ’ phase.
summary: This panel presents a direct DFT approach for investigating how impurities influence APB energy within the γ’ phase. The schematic illustrates the specific computational cell configuration used in these calculations, providing a foundational atomistic representation for evaluating energy changes associated with impurity incorporation in the lattice structure.

caption: Tabulated characterization data for Al2O3 specimens sintered at varying temperatures, detailing key material properties including porosity, grain size, hardness, and fracture toughness.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive characterization of Al2O3 materials sintered at different temperatures. It lists essential physical and mechanical properties, specifically porosity, grain size, hardness, and fracture toughness, serving as a foundational dataset for evaluating the influence of sintering temperature on the final material performance and structural integrity.

caption: Ceramic single crown in its green state immediately following the printing process.
summary: This panel shows the ceramic single crown after the printing process is complete. The part is in its green state, representing the fragile, un-sintered form of the dental restoration as it appears directly after being removed from the DLP manufacturing equipment.

caption: Rate capability performance of the rGO aerogel, plotted as specific capacitance versus increasing current density.
summary: The rate capability of the 3D rGO aerogel is demonstrated by plotting specific capacitance against increasing current density. This plot provides a clear visualization of how the material's charge storage capacity changes as the discharge rate is raised, serving as a key metric for evaluating its electrochemical performance.

caption: Color map visualization of droplet features v and ra relative to waveform parameters u and t for the last 500 samples.
summary: Depicting the last 500 samples, this heatmap shows the relationship between droplet features v and ra and waveform parameters u and t. Similar to the first 500 samples, the droplet features exhibit high consistency for given waveform parameters, indicating that the process behavior stabilizes over the duration of the experiment.

caption: Cross-sectional 3D digital model of the wave type flow path honeycomb filter.
summary: Displaying the internal cross-section of the wave type flow path, this 3D digital model highlights the intricate channel design of the honeycomb filter. This structural representation is critical for evaluating the wave geometry, which is fabricated through the binder jetting process to achieve the desired filtration performance and mechanical strength.

caption: Linear extrapolation plot for the 3C1N alloy used to determine threshold stress.
summary: The 3C1N alloy data is presented here using linear extrapolation to derive the threshold stress. Utilizing a stress exponent of n = 5, the plot demonstrates a strong correlation coefficient, allowing for the precise determination of the threshold stress value from the x-intercept of the stress-dependent data.

caption: Representative grain morphologies observed in the material under various thermal exposure conditions.
summary: These optical micrographs display the grain morphologies of the material following different thermal exposure conditions. The images provide a visual representation of the microstructural state, supporting the quantitative findings that grain size and boundary characteristics remain stable across the tested thermal regimes, showing no significant morphological changes due to exposure.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves for Ni-Cu@C/HC modified separator cells recorded at scanning rates ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 mV s-1.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for the Ni-Cu@C/HC modified separator cell are shown for scanning rates between 0.1 and 0.4 mV s-1. This composite separator leverages both physical transport and chemical conversion mechanisms to optimize electrochemical performance, as evidenced by the specific current response observed during the cyclic voltammetry testing process.

caption: Spin-polarized total and partial densities of states (DOS) for Ir2NiSn calculated at equilibrium lattice constants using the mBJ-GGA-PBE approximation, with the Fermi level aligned at zero energy.
summary: This plot displays the spin-polarized total and partial densities of states for the Ir2NiSn alloy. Calculated using the mBJ-GGA-PBE approximation at equilibrium lattice constants, the data illustrates the electronic structure with the Fermi level set to zero energy, providing a detailed view of the material's electronic properties.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectra comparing raw materials (GG, CNFs) and lyophilized 3D printed GC scaffolds (GC21, GC31, GC41) to identify characteristic polysaccharide absorption bands and chemical interactions.
summary: ATR-FTIR spectrometry was employed to investigate the chemical interactions occurring between GG and CNFs within the composite formulations. The resulting spectra revealed that all samples exhibited characteristic absorption bands of polysaccharide-based materials, confirming the chemical composition of the raw materials and the lyophilized 3D printed structures.

caption: Elastic modulus measurements compared across different irradiation states for 316L steel specimens subjected to 1066 °C and 1150 °C heat treatments.
summary: Elastic modulus values are compared for 316L steel samples heat-treated at 1066 °C and 1150 °C under varying irradiation conditions. The data indicates that unirradiated samples exhibit a lower elastic modulus compared to their irradiated counterparts, highlighting the influence of irradiation on the mechanical stiffness of the processed 316L steel materials.

caption: Stress-strain response of HD1 to HD5 scaffold structures during uniaxial compression.
summary: Uniaxial compression testing of HD1 through HD5 scaffold structures yielded these stress-strain curves. The data illustrates the mechanical response of the HD series, providing essential insights into the compressive strength and deformation profiles of these specific scaffold architectures under controlled experimental conditions.

caption: Fracture toughness testing configuration for the rolled material, indicating crack extension paths in the LT and TL orientations.
summary: This diagram shows the fracture toughness testing setup for rolled material. Tests were conducted with crack extension perpendicular to the rolling direction, denoted as LT, and in the rolling direction, denoted as TL. Here, L represents the longitudinal or rolling direction, while T represents the transverse direction of the material.

caption: Synchrotron-XRD diffractograms of nitrided specimens annealed for 180 minutes at temperatures ranging from 600 °C to 750 °C, illustrating the phase population stability.
summary: Synchrotron-XRD analysis of specimens annealed for 180 minutes at temperatures between 600 °C and 750 °C reveals minimal variation in the population of nitrides and carbides. The diffractograms confirm that no peaks attributable to Cr(N,C) are present, indicating consistent phase evolution across this specific range of annealing temperatures.

caption: X-ray computed tomography reconstructions of as-built 2024 aluminum alloys with varying Zr concentrations, highlighting cracks in black and isolated pores in blue.
summary: X-ray computed tomography reconstructions reveal the internal defect structure of as-built 2024 alloys with different Zr contents. Cracks are visualized in black, while isolated pores are highlighted in blue. Notably, experimental evidence demonstrates that cracks can be completely eliminated in these alloys when Zr additions exceed 1.98 percent.

caption: Dark-field TEM image focusing on the external NiO particles formed on the sample surface after the static corrosion treatment.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging provides a targeted view of the external NiO particles formed on the sample surface following 600 hours of static corrosion at 565 °C. This visualization technique isolates the NiO phase, allowing for the structural identification and morphological assessment of the particles located at the outermost corrosion layer.

caption: Experimental setup featuring an FL3000 fiber laser integrated with a KUKA industrial robot for the production of single coating lines.
summary: This photograph displays the experimental configuration used for material processing, specifically highlighting the integration of an FL3000 fiber laser with a KUKA industrial robot. This setup is designed to facilitate the precise production of single coating lines as part of the broader study on material deposition techniques.

caption: Resistivity ρ of Ni75Co25 alloy plotted against magnetic field H at 3 K, comparing TMR and PMR configurations.
summary: At 3 K, the Ni75Co25 alloy exhibits distinct resistivity responses under TMR and PMR configurations across a magnetic field range of -10 to 140 kOe. The saturation field for TMR is approximately 3 kOe, while the PMR configuration requires a significantly higher field to reach saturation.

caption: Tomographical reconstruction of an LPBF-fabricated microscopic pillar produced at 90 W, 50 µm hatch spacing, and 250 µs exposure time.
summary: This tomographical reconstruction displays an LPBF-fabricated microscopic pillar. The analysis reveals the surface morphology, specifically highlighting the lower surface roughness caused by attached powder particles. The µCT results confirm the successful fabrication of a defect-free pillar, validating the sequential identification of optimum processing conditions for the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Contour plot of the average rate of curvature change at T p - H p level (1,0), representing the response surface at a high printing temperature and neutral layer height.
summary: Panel (f) displays the contour plot for the T p - H p level (1,0). This visualization characterizes the response surface at a high printing temperature and neutral layer height, providing a comparative view of how these specific parameter settings influence the average rate of curvature change in the printed samples.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) response of four distinct samples, highlighting the ST sample's superior capacitance arc diameter and Zre/Zim values.
summary: The Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of four samples. The ST sample exhibits the largest capacitance arc diameter and Zre/Zim values, indicating distinct electrochemical properties compared to the other samples tested. This plot serves as a primary indicator of the impedance characteristics and passivation film behavior of the materials.

caption: Site-projected density of states for Cr, O, and Mg species in the MgO bridge-angled configuration, showing bulk Cr (left) and surface-adsorbed Cr (right).
summary: In the MgO bridge-angled configuration, the Cr-O interaction observed in the bulk-to-surface transition persists but is noticeably weakened compared to the O bridge case. The Mg atom exhibits only partial interaction with the surface species, indicating that the presence of Mg modulates the electronic coupling between Cr and O.

caption: Ternary Ni-Cr-Al phase diagram at 1200 °C, calculated via CALPHAD, highlighting the Ni-rich corner with specific alloy compositions marked by symbols and two-phase regions indicated by grey shading.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the Ni-rich corner of the Ni-Cr-Al system at 1200 °C, as determined by CALPHAD modeling. The plot identifies the specific nominal compositions of experimental alloys using distinct symbols and highlights two-phase regions in grey, providing the thermodynamic basis for the selected material compositions.

caption: Differential susceptibility versus magnetic field for NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with HNiPy at different temperatures.
summary: Differential susceptibility is plotted against the magnetic field for NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with HNiPy at various temperatures. This visualization allows for a detailed examination of the magnetic susceptibility peaks, which are sensitive to changes in the AFM layer thickness and the overall magnetic configuration of the NiFe/IrMn/NiFe multilayer stack.

caption: Top view of the printed disc sample showing the hexagonal geometry approximation.
summary: This top-view photograph of the printed disc reveals the actual geometry compared to the target design. The printed shape approximates a regular hexagon, indicated by green dashed lines, with a circumscribed blue circle of approximately 35.3 mm diameter. The image demonstrates that the printer's resolution is limited by voxel size.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of the splat/substrate interface within the epitaxial crystallization region, featuring an inset EDX profile for Mo and Ti.
summary: This bright-field STEM image captures the splat/substrate interface within the epitaxial crystallization region. An inset EDX profile for Mo and Ti reveals a diffusion zone approximately 200 nm wide between the two materials. This evidence confirms the presence of strong metallurgical bonding at the interface between the splat and substrate.

caption: Tabulated electrochemical parameters for the Mg–Er–Ni alloys, highlighting the slight decrease in corrosion potential (Ecorr) and the significant increase in corrosion current density (Icorr) as Ni content rises.
summary: This table summarizes the electrochemical parameters for the three Mg–Er–Ni alloys. Analysis of the data reveals that the corrosion potential (Ecorr) decreases slightly with increasing Ni content, while the corrosion current density (Icorr) increases significantly, particularly for the EME3N alloy, indicating higher susceptibility to corrosion with greater Ni additions.

caption: Measured reversible actuation strain of rectangular LCE samples plotted against different printing parameters, evaluated through repeated heating and cooling cycles.
summary: This plot quantifies the reversible actuation strain of single-layer LCE rectangular samples. By subjecting the printed sheets to controlled heating and cooling cycles, the data demonstrates the influence of specific printing parameters on the material's actuation performance, providing a clear measurement of the resulting strain achieved under these varying conditions.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness values for γ and γ' phases measured at positions CT1, CT2, CT3, and CT4 within a 6Ta8Co–10Ta16Co diffusion couple after 1000h of aging at 1100 °C.
summary: This plot displays nanoindentation hardness results for γ and γ' phases across four distinct positions in a diffusion couple aged at 1100 °C for 1000h. The data reveals that γ phase hardness peaks at position CT2, while γ' hardness consistently increases from CT1 to CT4, correlating with higher Co and Ta concentrations.

caption: Representative TUNEL staining images of the cornea, where yellow arrows indicate apoptotic cells, illustrating the reduction of cell death following cL treatment.
summary: TUNEL staining images visualize apoptotic cells in the cornea, marked by yellow arrows. The results show that the SCOP and SCOP+nL groups exhibit a higher density of TUNEL-positive cells compared to the control and SCOP+cL groups, confirming that cL treatment effectively reduces corneal cell apoptosis in DED mice.

caption: Nyquist plot for the S1-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion in the electrolyte.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the S1-6D specimen following a 6-day immersion period. The plot serves as part of a broader evaluation of the corrosion resistance of SLMed TC4 alloys, providing essential impedance characteristics for assessing material degradation over medium-term exposure.

caption: Axisymmetric finite element model illustrating the single shot peening (SP) process and the methodology for calculating resulting dimple diameters.
summary: This axisymmetric finite element model utilizes four-node CAX4R elements for analysis, complemented by CINAX4 infinite elements at the lateral and bottom boundaries. This configuration effectively eliminates specimen size effects and prevents elastic wave reflections, providing a robust framework for simulating the single shot peening process and accurately determining dimple diameters.

caption: Visual appearance of freshly prepared and dry 3D printed dressings containing 0, 0.1, 0.5, and 1 wt% NiCu nanoparticles.
summary: Photographic documentation displays the physical appearance of 3D printed dressings in both fresh and dry conditions. The samples are categorized by NiCu nanoparticle content, ranging from 0 to 1 wt%. As indicated in Fig. 3, these images illustrate the macroscopic state of the dressings used for the hydrophilicity analysis.

caption: Fe K-edge XANES spectrum of E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 with linear combination fitting.
summary: Linear combination fitting applied to the Fe K-edge XANES spectrum of the E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 catalyst allows for the determination of iron oxidation states. This fitting procedure clarifies the chemical environment of iron, complementing the Ni K-edge data to provide a comprehensive view of the catalyst's composition.

caption: SAED pattern inset within the TEM image of Al24.6Co24.6Cr24.6Fe24.6Zr1.5 after 40 hours of milling, revealing the diffraction characteristics.
summary: This panel shows the SAED pattern for the Zr-containing alloy after 40 hours of milling. The diffraction data is used to analyze the crystalline structure and phase stability of the Al24.6Co24.6Cr24.6Fe24.6Zr1.5 system, providing necessary evidence to evaluate the nanostructure and potential hardening sources within the alloy coatings.

caption: Root mean square error (RMSE) indicator values tracked across 79 iterations for the four evaluated multi-objective optimization strategies.
summary: The RMSE indicator values are shown across 79 iterations, reflecting the optimization performance of four different methods. The data indicates that the GP surrogate model provides more accurate modeling of relative density and surface roughness than the SOP model, with the methods ranked by performance as MOGP+EHI, MOGP+NSGA-II, GP+NSGA-II, and SOP+NSGA-II.

caption: Longitudinal cross-section of an extruded strand at a feed rate of 0.5 mm/s, showing a stable extrusion process indicated by the green frame.
summary: This longitudinal micro-CT section displays a strand extruded at 0.5 mm/s. The green frame denotes stable extrusion conditions. At this lowest investigated feed rate, the configuration v0.5–T260–p30 closely matches the process-optimized target structure, demonstrating consistent and stable material deposition across all tested nozzle temperatures and gas pressures.

caption: W-shaped microhardness distribution curve observed in the transition zone of FGM 2, characterized by a distinct minimum hardness value in zone I.
summary: FGM 2 exhibits a W-shaped microhardness curve across its transition zone. The minimum hardness value occurs in zone I, which is dominated by large-sized alpha lamellar structures. This reduction in hardness is attributed to the easier migration of dislocations within alpha-colonies sharing the same lamellar orientation.

caption: Bode phase plot diagram showing the frequency response of the samples, characterized by a linear slope of approximately −1 in the intermediate frequency range.
summary: Bode phase plots for the CP-Ti and Ti–5Ag samples reveal a linear slope of approximately −1 within the intermediate frequency range. This spectral feature is indicative of a monolayer film structure, confirming the electrochemical behavior observed in the Nyquist plots and supporting the analysis of the passivation layer's integrity.

caption: Anodic polarization curves of TNZT alloy in PBS solution at 37 °C, highlighting two replicate measurements and the specific potentials of 400 mV and 1500 mV selected for subsequent tribocorrosion testing.
summary: This figure displays the anodic polarization behavior of TNZT alloy immersed in a PBS solution at a physiological temperature of 37 °C. Two experimental curves are presented to demonstrate reproducibility. Arrows indicate the specific potentials of 400 mV and 1500 mV, which were chosen for further investigation in tribocorrosion experiments.

caption: Phase distribution profile generated using the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm.
summary: This panel displays the phase distribution profile obtained through the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. The visualization represents the optimized phase state, serving as a foundational component of the computational analysis. This result demonstrates the effectiveness of the optimization approach in determining the phase characteristics within the modeled system.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of hASCs encapsulated in GCs, GC-BG, and GC-BGMAs at days 1, 3, and 7, showing live cells stained with Calcein AM (green) and dead cells with PI (red).
summary: Live/dead assays demonstrate that human adipose-derived stem cells encapsulated within GCs, GC-BG, and GC-BGMAs remain viable and proliferate over a seven-day period. The fluorescence microscopy images confirm the absence of cytotoxicity across all tested scaffold compositions, indicating that the materials support healthy cell growth and maintenance throughout the observation timeframe.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of pure HPC, showing the baseline optical response.
summary: This reflectance spectrum characterizes the optical properties of pure HPC. It provides the baseline data for comparing the reflected wavelengths of HPCA samples, which show progressively more prominent reflectance and a redshift in the wavelength range as the degree of substitution increases.

caption: Polar plot of the SLM-formed Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy, revealing a strong texture intensity with a maximum value of 5.
summary: This polar plot illustrates the crystallographic texture of the SLM-formed Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy. The data reveals a strong texture intensity, reaching a maximum value of 5. This result confirms the presence of a preferred orientation in the growth of the columnar structures observed in the alloy during solidification.

caption: Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram illustrating the probability distribution of individual rays on a simulated sensor field at a 200 mm coaxial distance from the process zone, using a 450 nm wavelength across four distinct analyzed points.
summary: This Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram displays the probability distribution of ray scattering on a simulated sensor field at a 200 mm distance from the process zone. Utilizing a 450 nm wavelength, the plot reveals directional scattering dependencies related to the feed direction, incorporating all determined dome and process parameters.

caption: Thermo-Calc pseudo-binary phase diagram for the CoCrFeNi-Mn system, illustrating phase stability versus Mn mole fraction, with a red vertical line marking the temperature path for Mn0.3CoCrFeNi.
summary: The CoCrFeNi-Mn phase diagram shows that the FCC phase field remains largely unchanged within the 0 to 0.1 mole fraction range of Mn. For Mn0.3CoCrFeNi, the diagram reveals a wider solid-phase FCC region spanning approximately 700 to 1400 °C, confirming Mn's role in stabilizing the FCC structure.

caption: Transient temperature gradients (G) at the solidus isotherm plotted against time starting from 0.25 ms, comparing radial (Gr) and depth-direction (Gd) gradients during single-spot solidification.
summary: This plot illustrates the transient temperature gradients at the solidus isotherm following beam termination. The simulation reveals that the temperature gradient is significantly higher in the depth-direction compared to the radial direction. These results, derived from a single-spot solidification model, highlight the directional dependence of thermal dissipation during the cooling process.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the CuCrZr–316L interfacial region showing heavily twinned Cu-rich particles with a broad size distribution within the BCC-Fe matrix.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the interfacial region of the CuCrZr–316L composite. The microstructure features heavily twinned Cu-rich particles characterized by a broad size distribution. These particles are embedded within BCC-Fe grains, indicating that Fe/Cu phase decomposition occurs during both melt and solid-state cooling processes within the material.

caption: Lowest vertical position of the hammer, marking the end of the observed movement sequence.
summary: The hammer is shown at its lowest vertical position in this final frame of the sequence. The red cross highlights the bottom surface at this terminal point, completing the visual documentation of the hammer's movement from the upper starting position to the lowest point of travel.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of the 3D rGO aerogel electrode system, exhibiting characteristic isosceles triangle shapes at various current densities.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for the 3D rGO aerogel electrode system are shown, displaying characteristic isosceles triangle shapes. These profiles, which correspond to the cyclic voltammetry data, demonstrate the capacitive characteristics of the assembled electrode system and confirm its performance across various applied current densities during charge and discharge cycles.

caption: Comprehensive overview of the complete experimental setup incorporating the DBD reactor system.
summary: This panel displays the full experimental system configuration, which integrates the cylindrical DBD reactor shown in panel (a). The diagram outlines the arrangement of the experimental apparatus, demonstrating how the reactor is positioned within the broader system developed to conduct the reaction described in the research.

caption: Force versus displacement curves for PU-infilled third-order MFC (M3) specimens, illustrating the mesh sensitivity analysis used to determine an optimal mesh size of 0.185 mm.
summary: This panel displays the force-displacement response for PU-infilled third-order MFC (M3) specimens during a mesh sensitivity analysis. By evaluating these numerical results, a mesh size of 0.185 mm was selected to effectively balance computational efficiency with the required accuracy for the numerical model of the structure.

caption: Stress-free reference lattice profiles of the {311} plane along the height of the inter-pass rolled wall specimen.
summary: This panel presents the stress-free reference lattice profiles for the {311} plane in the inter-pass rolled wall. The observed inconsistencies in these profiles underscore the significant difficulties encountered when determining a reliable d0 reference for neutron diffraction analysis in materials characterized by coarse grains and strong crystallographic textures.

caption: Bright field TEM image showing TCP phase precipitates in a Re-containing sample pre-strained under [001] tension after creep testing at 1100 °C.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging reveals the formation of TCP phase precipitates within the Re-containing sample following pre-straining under [001] tension and subsequent creep testing at 1100 °C. These observations confirm that pre-strained samples consistently develop P-type TCP precipitates, contrasting with the TCP-free state of untreated samples under identical conditions.

caption: Sheet-based TPMS unit cells demonstrating structural variations defined by level constants c and thicknesses t.
summary: This panel displays sheet-P, sheet-G, and sheet-D based TPMS unit cells. These structures are generated using varying level constants and thicknesses to illustrate the structural diversity possible within the scaffold design. These geometric parameters are fundamental for controlling the porosity and mechanical properties of the resulting bone scaffolding system.

caption: Extraction of the finished compression-molded and joined part from the AMCM system.
summary: Final removal of the compression-molded and joined part marks the completion of the AMCM foundry process. This step demonstrates the successful integration of robot-assisted additive manufacturing and compression molding, resulting in a finished component produced through the automated workflow managed by the system's integrated software architecture.

caption: Relative Corrosion Current (RCC) behavior of HNPT (Ni-P/TiO2 composite) samples measured at 150 °C, highlighting the impact of TiO2 incorporation on degradation.
summary: The RCC behavior of HNPT composite samples is shown for tests performed at 150 °C. This plot illustrates the corrosion degradation kinetics of the Ni-P/TiO2 composite under static conditions. By comparing this to the HNP data, the influence of TiO2 reinforcement on the electrochemical stability of the alloy is effectively demonstrated.

caption: Time-dependent UV-Visible absorption spectra monitoring the stability and formation kinetics of SL-NiNPs.
summary: Time-dependent UV-Visible absorption spectra monitoring the stability and formation kinetics of SL-NiNPs. By tracking the spectral changes over time in DMSO, this analysis provides insight into the evolution and stability of the SL-NiNPs, serving as a key analytical technique to validate the formation process of the nickel-based nanoparticles.

caption: Energy subband configuration of the 10-ML quantum well system under a 0-V reverse bias voltage, illustrating the relative alignment of electron and hole states.
summary: This diagram displays the subband configuration of a 10-ML quantum well at 0-V reverse bias. It serves as a reference for identifying the Γ21-h11 transition and the P1 PL branch, which is characterized as a -1 order Stark-ladder transition, highlighting the electronic state alignment within the quantum-confined structure.

caption: Tauc plot of PVA-assisted SnO2 nanoparticles, resulting in an optical bandgap of 3.76 eV.
summary: PVA-assisted SnO2 nanoparticles are characterized using a Tauc plot of (αhν)2 versus hν. The graphical data indicates an optical bandgap of 3.76 eV. This measurement highlights the specific modification of the electronic properties of SnO2 nanoparticles when synthesized in the presence of the PVA surfactant.

caption: Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) spectrum of hydrogenated polystyrene (PS) processed with a Ni-Mo catalyst, illustrating the chemical composition and reactivity of carbonyl compounds.
summary: This GC–MS spectrum provides analytical evidence of the reactivity of carbonyl compounds within hydrogenated polystyrene samples treated with a Ni-Mo catalyst. The data confirms the successful hydrogenation process, demonstrating the utility of GC–MS measurements in characterizing the chemical transformation and structural changes of the polymer under these specific catalytic conditions.

caption: Van't Hoff plot showing the linear relationship between median plateau pressure and inverse temperature for La2.5Y0.5MgNi14.
summary: Van't Hoff plot for La2.5Y0.5MgNi14 illustrates the linear correlation between the median plateau pressure and the inverse temperature. This fit is derived from the hydrogen absorption data, providing essential thermodynamic insights into the stability and hydrogen interaction characteristics of the yttrium-substituted alloy under the tested temperature range of 293-353 K.

caption: Log-log plot comparing the relative yield strength (σ*/σy,s) versus relative density (ρ*/ρs) for the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy against literature data for AlSi10Mg, Ti-6Al-4V, and IN718 fabricated via additive manufacturing.
summary: This log-log plot illustrates the relative yield strength of the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy as a function of relative density, utilizing the Gibson-Ashby model. The performance is benchmarked against solid and HSL structures of AlSi10Mg, Ti-6Al-4V, and IN718 alloys, providing a comparative assessment of mechanical efficiency within the additive manufacturing framework.

caption: 13C MAS NMR spectra comparing g-C3N4, 0.05 HA-CN, and 0.05 HAPA-CN to analyze carbon environments.
summary: The 13C MAS NMR spectra provide a comparative analysis of the carbon environments within g-C3N4, 0.05 HA-CN, and 0.05 HAPA-CN samples. These spectra allow for the investigation of structural changes and chemical bonding environments resulting from the modification of the graphitic carbon nitride framework with hydroxyacetic and phytic acids.

caption: Room-temperature tensile stress-strain curves for SLM-fabricated HEA samples processed with varying volumetric energy densities (VEDs).
summary: This panel displays the room-temperature tensile stress-strain behavior of HEA samples produced via selective laser melting (SLM) using different process parameters. The curves illustrate how varying the volumetric energy density (VED) influences the mechanical response, providing a baseline for evaluating the material's performance under standard tensile testing conditions.

caption: FESEM micrograph showing the front view of the shear failure surface for Ti16.6-HEA after small punch testing at 400 °C.
summary: This FESEM micrograph displays the front view of the shear failure surface for the Ti16.6-HEA alloy following small punch testing at 400 °C. The visual evidence characterizes the fracture surface features, contributing to the understanding of how titanium content influences failure mechanisms at this elevated temperature.

caption: Raman spectra of carbon materials synthesized using various catalysts, highlighting the structural quality of the resulting carbon nanotubes.
summary: Raman analysis of carbon materials synthesized over different catalysts reveals variations in graphitization and defect density. Specifically, the use of Ni-Fe/γ-Al2O3 results in a minimum ID/IG ratio of 0.43 and a maximum IG'/IG ratio of 0.65, indicating that these carbon nanotubes possess fewer structural defects and higher graphitic characteristics compared to other catalysts.

caption: Sequential model structure for the manufacturing process (MP) as implemented within the OpenLCA software environment.
summary: This schematic illustrates the sequential model structure for the manufacturing process (MP) within the OpenLCA software. It serves as a representative layout for the modeled manufacturing routes, providing a clear visual framework for understanding how these processes are structured and organized for life cycle assessment analysis in the software.

caption: Summary table presenting the fragment velocity, impact point location, and peak pressure values recorded across five valid experimental tests.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive summary of the experimental data collected from five valid tests. It specifically details the fragment velocity, the precise impact point location, and the corresponding peak pressure observed during each trial, serving as a consolidated reference for evaluating the mechanical performance and impact dynamics of the tested specimens.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus actual simulated En values, with the dotted line representing the ideal prediction case and individual dots representing test dataset samples.
summary: The prediction performance of the trained model for En is visualized through a parity plot comparing predicted values to actual simulated values. Each dot represents an individual sample from the test dataset, while the dotted line serves as a reference for the ideal case where predicted and actual values are equal.

caption: Pressure-time response profile recorded during the mechanical testing of the foam pad specimen.
summary: This panel displays the pressure-time curve for the foam pad, representing one of five valid tests conducted to evaluate performance. The data, captured by the acquisition system, illustrates the mechanical response of the foam material under the specified testing conditions, providing a baseline for comparing its pressure distribution characteristics.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CSLM) images showing the spatial organization of epithelial cells (E-cad+, red) and fibroblasts (Vim+, cyan) within a scaffold pore after a 2-week co-culture, highlighting the formation of acini-like structures.
summary: Following a 2-week co-culture period, CSLM imaging reveals the spatial distribution of epithelial cells and fibroblasts within the scaffold pores. The epithelial cells successfully developed into acini-like structures, confirming that the hybrid 3D model effectively supports epithelial morphogenesis into prototypical mammary acini within the engineered environment.

caption: Selective area electron diffraction pattern of the interdendritic zone, revealing the presence of coarsened γ" precipitates.
summary: This selective area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern characterizes the interdendritic zone of the material. The diffraction analysis confirms the presence of coarsened γ" precipitates within this region. Bright-field micrographs, when correlated with this diffraction data, provide clear identification of the metastable γ" phase structure within the microstructure.

caption: Microstructure of the Cu–Al–Mn alloy in the as-hot-rolled condition at a thickness of 2.3 mm, revealing a distinct two-phase morphology.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the Cu–Al–Mn alloy microstructure following hot rolling to a 2.3 mm thickness. The material exhibits a characteristic two-phase structure, which persists despite the initial preheating at 900 °C. This heterogeneous phase distribution serves as the baseline state prior to the subsequent betatization treatment.

caption: Bode phase angle plots for as-built GZ112K alloys, displaying phase shift characteristics across the frequency spectrum for various heat treatment conditions.
summary: Bode phase angle plots for the as-built GZ112K alloy display the phase shift characteristics across the frequency spectrum. These plots, combined with impedance data, facilitate the analysis of electrochemical performance and corrosion resistance, providing insight into the material's response to heat treatments as part of the broader EIS testing results.

caption: Vickers hardness of AFSD-deposited Ti-6Al-4V compared across tool traverse speeds of 254 mm/min, 504 mm/min, and 169 mm/min.
summary: Vickers microhardness results for AFSD Ti-6Al-4V builds are analyzed here in relation to tool traverse speed. The box plot compares specimens B3 (254 mm/min), B8 (504 mm/min), and B9 (169 mm/min), providing a clear visualization of how varying the traverse speed affects the hardness distribution across the nine experimental builds.

caption: Scanning transmission electron microscopy image showing the morphology and embedding of a ZrB2 particle within the Al–Fe matrix.
summary: This STEM image illustrates the structural integration of a ZrB2 particle within the Al–Fe matrix. The analysis, conducted to investigate interfacial stability, provides a clear view of the particle's morphology and its surrounding environment, serving as the primary context for subsequent high-resolution and elemental mapping investigations of the interface.

caption: Creep strain evolution at 593 °C, comparing predictions with and without dynamic recrystallisation.
summary: This panel displays the creep strain evolution at 593 °C. It compares model predictions with and without dynamic recrystallisation. The calculated secondary creep rate is higher when dynamic recrystallisation is considered, as indicated by the solid lines compared to the dashed lines representing the condition without recrystallisation.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of dopamine (DA) recorded at a scanning rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ on the CNT-Pt composite sensor.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms illustrate the electrochemical response of the CNT-Pt composite sensor when detecting dopamine at a scanning rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ within a potential range of -0.2 to 0.4 V. The data indicates the sensor's capability to detect dopamine across a concentration range of 0.15625–5 mM.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy image of TR146 epithelial cells cultured on the upper surface of the PET membrane after 3 days of microfluidic flow.
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy reveals the morphology of TR146 epithelial cells cultured on the upper surface of a PET membrane within the microfluidic device. After 3 days of flow, the cells are visualized in situ, demonstrating successful attachment and growth on the membrane surface as part of the oral mucosa equivalent.

caption: Response surface plot illustrating the duration above melting temperature at a fixed scanning speed of 800 mm/s.
summary: This response surface plot visualizes the time spent above the melting temperature during processing, specifically at a constant scanning speed of 800 mm/s. By fixing this parameter while varying others, the plot provides a clear representation of how thermal conditions evolve within the material during the manufacturing process.

caption: Predicted 3D deposition geometry for Experiment 1 using the Random Forest (RF) model as the geometry-characterization function.
summary: This panel illustrates the predicted 3D deposition geometry for Experiment 1. The visualization utilizes a Random Forest model as the primary geometry-characterization function to estimate the structural outcome of the deposition process, providing a baseline for comparing how different training dataset sizes influence the accuracy of the predicted 3D geometry.

caption: Raman spectral profiles of pure PP and PP/B4C nanocompounds with filler loadings ranging from 2 to 10 wt percent.
summary: This panel displays the Raman spectral profiles for pure PP and PP/B4C mixtures with varying filler loadings of 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 wt percent. These spectra illustrate the baseline vibrational characteristics of the nanocompounds compared to the pure PP reference material across the specified concentration range.

caption: Internal porosity distribution within the bulk powder sample as visualized through CT scanning.
summary: This panel displays the internal porosity distribution within the bulk powder sample, as captured through CT scanning. The qualitative data derived from the scan provides a clear visualization of the void spaces present within the powder bulk, highlighting the structural characteristics of the material at a specific location.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing solute clusters within a 10 × 20 × 20 nm³ volume at a depth of 600 nm under three-energies ion irradiation.
summary: Captured at a depth of 600 nm under three-energies irradiation, this reconstruction reveals the spatial arrangement of solute clusters. At an irradiation dose of 1.39 dpa, the observed cluster density and diameter reflect the influence of the multi-energy ion beam on the microstructural evolution of the irradiated material.

caption: Re-stabilized electric arc forming a plasma column of constant volume following the material transfer event.
summary: Final stabilization of the electric arc occurs after the material transfer event, re-establishing a plasma column with a constant size and volume. This phase signifies the return to nominal deposition conditions, ensuring the continuity of the WA-DED process before the next cycle of material transfer begins.

caption: Impedance variation graph corresponding to the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film during the charge and discharge process.
summary: This impedance variation graph depicts the electrochemical response of the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film.
