The measured average impedance of 6.1 Ω confirms that alloying silicon with germanium successfully optimizes the electron conduction path and ion migration environment, resulting in a reduced charge transfer resistance compared to pure a-Si thin-films.

caption: Overview of the experimental testing system utilized for mechanical evaluation.
summary: The experimental testing system is shown in this photograph, providing a comprehensive view of the apparatus used for the study. This setup serves as the primary platform for conducting the mechanical experiments described in the research, ensuring consistent testing conditions for the various hinge specimens evaluated throughout the investigation.

caption: Direct Energy Deposition (DED) system utilized for sample fabrication, sourced from NanJing HUIRUI Photoelectric Technology.
summary: This panel displays the Direct Energy Deposition (DED) equipment used for the additive manufacturing of the nickel-based superalloy samples. The system, manufactured by NanJing HUIRUI Photoelectric Technology, serves as the primary experimental setup for the preparation of all samples discussed in the study.

caption: Magnified temperature history for Position C, covering the 0–600 s coating duration.
summary: Providing an enlarged view of the thermal data for Position C, this plot captures the temperature transition during the initial 600 s of the coating process. It serves to clarify the specific thermal behavior and temperature evolution at this gear surface location during the early stages of the experiment.

caption: Tan δ curves of damping TPU composites, representing the energy dissipation capacity as a function of temperature for varying prepolymer curing coefficients.
summary: Tan δ curves derived from DMA measurements quantify the damping properties of TPU composites with different prepolymer curing coefficients. These curves highlight the energy dissipation characteristics of the materials, serving as a key indicator of their damping performance and viscoelastic behavior under the tested experimental conditions.

caption: K-Nearest Neighbor model performance on the test dataset.
summary: K-Nearest Neighbor model results illustrate the predictive accuracy of the algorithm on the test dataset. As part of the comparative evaluation of machine learning models, this plot provides insight into how the K-Nearest Neighbor approach performs relative to the other tested algorithms in the study's overall evaluation framework.

caption: Confocal maximum intensity projection images of bioprinted hASCs on day 1 and 7, showing live cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Confocal maximum intensity projection images visualize the viability of bioprinted hASCs on day 1 and 7, with live cells stained green and dead cells red. High cell viability exceeding 98% with minimal dead cells was observed in both printed structure types, confirming the cytocompatibility of the bioprinted composite.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the logarithm of normalized threshold stress as a function of inverse absolute temperature (1000/T) for unreinforced 7775-Al, 10 vol% 13 μm-SiCp-AMC, and 1 vol% 50 nm-SiCp-AMC samples.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature sensitivity of threshold stress for various aluminum matrix composites. By calculating the slopes of these linear relationships, activation energy values (Qo) are determined as 34.4, 26.9, and 24.0 kJ/mol for the unreinforced 7775-Al, 10 vol% 13 μm-SiCp-AMC, and 1 vol% 50 nm-SiCp-AMC samples, respectively.

caption: Low-field AC magnetic susceptibility temperature dependence for the bidirectional melting strategy (BMS) sample, evaluated with scan vector rotations of 0°, 45°, and 90°. Inset data specifies the T M, T A, and T C values, with green double arrows marking the transformation hysteresis width.
summary: The BMS sample's magnetic susceptibility is plotted against temperature for different scan vector rotations. The inset details the transformation temperatures and hysteresis width. Observations indicate that the Δ T hys remains almost constant, which implies that the BMS sample maintains a uniform level of chemical homogeneity throughout the material.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Al-Si system, illustrating the solidification behavior and primary alpha-Al phase formation.
summary: The Al-Si binary phase diagram illustrates the solidification behavior of the Al-12Si alloy. It shows that the primary alpha-Al phase forms at approximately 580 °C. This phase exhibits negligible solubility for Si, which explains the formation of the eutectic Si-rich particles observed in the TEM and EDS analysis.

caption: Modified CreatBot F430 3D printer setup, featuring a bypassed extruder motor, disabled filament sensor, and customized G-code for executing specific raster paths.
summary: The photograph displays the modified CreatBot F430 3D printer hardware. Key modifications include the bypass of the extruder motor and the disabling of the filament sensor. These hardware changes, combined with modified G-code, allow the system to print customized raster paths required for the ATP graded tape process.

caption: Illustration of the three potential Burgers vectors for partial dislocations on the {111} γ plane during the martensitic transformation process.
summary: Each {111} γ plane supports three distinct potential Burgers vectors. Due to the threefold rotational symmetry around the 〈111〉 axis in the FCC structure, any slip action yields the same sequence alteration above the slip plane, ensuring a consistent ε-martensite orientation relationship with the γ matrix during the transformation.

caption: SHAP summary plot ranking the influence of various features on the radius error, identifying the setting radius as the most significant factor.
summary: The SHAP summary plot evaluates feature importance for the Model_for_CNTyarn. It demonstrates that the setting radius has the highest influence on the radius error. This visualization provides a clear ranking of feature contributions, highlighting which parameters are most critical for predicting the printing accuracy of the CNT yarn.

caption: Heat map visualization of the compaction distribution H(r,z) within a cylindrical powder-bed volume measuring 60 mm in diameter and 36 mm in height.
summary: This heat map illustrates the spatial distribution of compaction H(r,z) within a cylindrical powder-bed volume. Based on a mean surface curvature of 36.95 mm for the compacted bulk powder, the visualization provides a quantitative representation of how compaction zones develop during an assisted L-PBF build process.

caption: Isothermal section at the two ternary eutectic reaction temperatures, showing L1 → γ + P + NiMo and L2 → γ + P + σ.
summary: This diagram illustrates the phase relationships at the two ternary eutectic reaction temperatures within the Ni-Cr-Mo system. It highlights the distinct reaction pathways L1 → γ + P + NiMo and L2 → γ + P + σ, which govern the formation of specific three-phase coexisting regions at these thermal conditions.

caption: Parity plot comparing measured rupture times against those predicted by the Wilshire model for stress levels below the proportional limit.
summary: This parity plot displays measured versus predicted rupture times for stress levels below the proportional limit using the Wilshire model. The data reveals a clear grain size effect on rupture time, where excluding the smaller grain size heat would result in a slope significantly closer to the ideal value of 1.00.

caption: Schematic representation of the 45° rotation angle scanning strategy applied between adjacent layers during the additive manufacturing process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the 45° rotation angle scanning strategy used for the M2052 alloy. It represents one of four specific rotation angles between adjacent layers designed to investigate the influence of scanning strategies on the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties of the printed alloy samples.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image displaying large, single-phase yttrium oxide particles within the Y-HX sample matrix.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy reveals the morphology of oxide particles in the Y-HX sample. These particles are characterized as single yttrium oxide phases with relatively larger dimensions compared to those observed in the modified Y-La-HX alloy, providing a baseline for understanding the effect of lanthanum addition on oxide dispersion.

caption: Front-side transmittance spectra of MJT specimens, showing that the spectral shifting behavior is influenced by the digital material composition.
summary: This panel shows the front-side transmittance spectra for MJT specimens. Similar to the absorbance data, the transmittance shifting behavior is dependent on the digital material. This confirms that the optical transmission properties of the tilted surface specimens are significantly affected by the specific digital material used in the study.

caption: Distribution of 20,000 virtual alloy samples generated by the DCVAE model.
summary: This panel presents the resulting distribution of 20,000 virtual alloy sample data points generated by the DCVAE model. The visualization showcases the synthetic sample distribution, providing insight into the generative capability of the DCVAE in replicating the characteristics of the original alloy dataset within the reduced PCA space.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of E. coli bacteria stained with a live/dead kit on composite scaffold systems, with a scale bar of 50 μm.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of E. coli bacteria stained with a live/dead kit on composite scaffold systems, with a scale bar of 50 μm. By utilizing a live/dead bacterial staining kit and fluorescence microscopy, we were able to detect the number of dead and live bacteria on the scaffold surfaces.

caption: Measured transmission spectra for the purple optical filter, contrasting the commercial version with the printed filter derived from an optimized mixture of 0.5 drops Navy Blue, 3.5 drops Orchid, 3.0 drops Ruby, and 4.5 drops Violet.
summary: Panel b presents the purple optical filter, showing the measured transmission spectra for both commercial and printed versions. The printed filter utilizes a specific ink mixture of Navy Blue, Orchid, Ruby, and Violet, demonstrating the effectiveness of the inverse RF model in achieving target optical properties through precise colorant blending.

caption: Visual assessment of the extrudability for the UF + MC_1 mixture.
summary: This photograph illustrates the extrudability test results for the UF + MC_1 mixture. The specimen exhibits a continuous and smooth extrusion profile without any signs of structural failure, such as breaks or surface defects. These observations confirm that the mixture maintains integrity throughout the extrusion process.

caption: Moment resistance and anticipated bending moment diagram for Specimen ER110-3PB-10% derived using nominal design yield strength and geometric parameters.
summary: This panel displays the moment resistance diagram for Specimen ER110-3PB-10% calculated using design-based yield strength and geometric properties. It provides a baseline comparison for the anticipated bending moment behavior, illustrating the structural response under the specified three-point bending test conditions as defined by nominal engineering design standards.

caption: Comparison of hardness versus elastic modulus for aged NiTi-N2 alloy relative to various biomedical metals, including Fe-Cr-Ni, Ti-Nb-Zr-Ta, Ti-6Al-4V, DED NiTi, and Ti-Fe-Ta, with a dashed line indicating the hardness-to-modulus ratio.
summary: This plot compares the mechanical properties of aged NiTi-N2 against established biomedical alloys like Fe-Cr-Ni, Ti-Nb-Zr-Ta, Ti-6Al-4V, DED NiTi, and Ti-Fe-Ta. By plotting hardness against elastic modulus, the figure highlights the performance of the NiTi-N2 material, with the dashed line providing a reference for the hardness-to-modulus ratio across these diverse metallic systems.

caption: Void density evolution as a function of shear strain for irradiated samples, comparing MD simulation results (solid line) with the void collapse model (dashed line).
summary: This panel illustrates the evolution of void density as a function of shear strain for irradiated samples. It compares MD simulation results, represented by a solid line, against the void collapse model, shown as a dashed line. The data highlights the mechanism of void collapse during plastic deformation in irradiated materials.

caption: In-situ photograph capturing the 3D printing process of a ZrO2 sample using a filament-based deposition method.
summary: The photograph captures the active printing of a ZrO2 sample. The fabrication process is performed using a white zirconia filament at a temperature of 180 °C, a printing speed of 15 mm/s, a nozzle size of 0.4 mm, and a slicing layer height of 0.2 mm.

caption: Relative density variation for hot isostatic pressed specimens processed at 150 W laser power as a function of E L and E V.
summary: Hot isostatic pressed specimens processed at 150 W laser power show density variations dependent on E L and E V. Although the final density is generally higher for 300 W specimens, the hot isostatic pressing process effectively modifies the density characteristics compared to the as-built state for these specific laser parameters.

caption: Phase map corresponding to the AFSD-deposited layers, where green indicates ferrite and red indicates austenite.
summary: The phase map of the AFSD-deposited Fe-Cr-Ni alloy displays the spatial distribution of ferrite (green) and austenite (red) phases. The presence of these phases is linked to the transformation of metastable austenite to ferrite during plastic deformation, which contributes to the enhanced mechanical strength observed in the AFSD-processed material.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PGA synthesized from GAMes with TSA catalysis at 190 °C for 1 day.
summary: This MALDI-TOF mass spectrum displays the molecular weight distribution of poly(glycolic acid) (PGA) synthesized from GAMes monomers catalyzed by TSA at 190 °C over a 24-hour period. The data, corresponding to entry 1A in Table 4, characterizes the polymer chain distribution resulting from these specific thermal polymerization conditions.

caption: Nyquist diagram displaying the electrochemical impedance response of Alloy 690 after 15 hours of immersion in a pH 9.0 borate buffer solution at corrosion potential, showing the onset of a capacitive loop.
summary: The Nyquist diagram illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of Alloy 690 after 15 hours of immersion in a borate buffer solution at pH 9.0. The plot reveals the beginning of a capacitive loop, characterizing the initial corrosion potential response of the alloy under these specific ambient temperature conditions.

caption: Initial-range true stress-strain curves showing the elastic region for AMS heat-treated CMT-WAAM and wrought IN718.
summary: Detailing the elastic region, this panel provides an initial-range view of the true stress-strain curves for AMS heat-treated IN718. The plot allows for a precise examination of the elastic-plastic transition and early deformation characteristics of both the CMT-WAAM and wrought material variants under these specific heat treatment conditions.

caption: Quasi-normal distribution table used for sorting participant perspectives.
summary: This table presents a quasi-normal distribution framework utilized during the research study. Participants were instructed to organize their perspectives regarding a specific set of stimuli or statements by arranging them within this structured table, facilitating a systematic approach to qualitative data collection and the categorization of subjective viewpoints.

caption: Profile of the nano-indentation depth versus lateral distance for the LPBF vertical (X–Z) IN718 variant.
summary: The indentation profile for the LPBF vertical (X-Z) IN718 variant demonstrates a sharper gradient and a reduced amount of pile-up compared to the wrought material. This profile confirms that the LPBF processing route results in distinct surface deformation behavior under nanoindentation testing compared to the wrought alloy variant.

caption: TEM micrograph of 3DGPC3 showing the structural arrangement of the composite at a specific magnification.
summary: This TEM image displays the structural arrangement of 3DGPC3. The presence of the GO lamellar structure is shown to enhance cohesion between pastes, which helps to make the print structure more complete. This observation is consistent with the role of GO content in improving the overall composite integrity.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph obtained using the (1-1-3) reflection of (Ti,Mo)C to highlight carbide distribution.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph utilizes the (1-1-3) reflection of (Ti,Mo)C to selectively image the carbide phase within the US-150W sample. By isolating this specific reflection, the distribution and spatial arrangement of the (Ti,Mo)C carbides are clearly visualized, confirming their presence and morphology within the material's microstructure.

caption: Emission spectra of TPU/SAOED composites with varying SAOED concentrations under 365 nm excitation.
summary: This plot displays the emission spectra of TPU/SAOED composite prints, illustrating how varying amounts of SAOED filler influence the photoluminescence behavior. The measurements were conducted under a constant 365 nm excitation wavelength to characterize the optical response of the composites as the concentration of the SAOED additive is systematically adjusted.

caption: Low-field zoomed-in plot of magnetoresistance as a function of magnetic field at a characteristic temperature of 100 K.
summary: This panel shows the magnetoresistance as a function of the magnetic field at 100 K. By zooming in on the low-field region, the plot reveals the specific electronic response and MR characteristics of the material at this elevated temperature, complementing the data obtained at other characteristic temperatures.

caption: Box-and-whisker plot illustrating the distribution and mean yield stress values for specimens subjected to processing condition 1.
summary: This box-and-whisker plot displays the statistical spread and mean yield stress for materials processed under condition 1. The data indicates that yield typically occurs prior to the first scan, confirming that continuous and interrupted testing methods remain comparable for evaluating the mechanical performance of these specific processing conditions.

caption: Experimental configuration showing the physical thermocouple installation on the substrate during the deposition process conducted at Northeastern University.
summary: The photograph displays the practical experimental setup used for in-situ temperature measurement during deposition. By capturing the physical placement of thermocouples on the substrate, this image documents the methodology for acquiring the far-field temperature data necessary to validate and calibrate the predictive FE models for the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Hardness of the Cu-matrix and its contribution to the Cu–9Ni–6Sn-xAl alloy system.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness of the Cu-matrix and its calculated contribution to the overall mechanical hardness of Cu–9Ni–6Sn-xAl alloys. The data reflects the influence of the matrix phase on the alloy's hardness, providing a breakdown of the mechanical properties within the complex multi-component system.

caption: Vickers microhardness values measured for NiTi rotary files subjected to heat treatments at 460, 480, and 500 °C for a duration of 120 min.
summary: Vickers microhardness values are presented for NiTi rotary files following heat treatment at temperatures of 460, 480, and 500 °C for 120 min. These hardness measurements serve as a key mechanical indicator, which is correlated with the fatigue performance of the heat-treated samples as described in the study.

caption: Ground truth image representing the original high-resolution reference data used for evaluating the performance of various coding methods.
summary: This panel displays the ground truth image, which serves as the baseline for high-resolution imaging simulations. It provides the original reference data necessary to evaluate the accuracy and effectiveness of different 1D coding methods and sampling ratios applied in the subsequent simulation results presented in the study.

caption: XRD diffractograms of substrate material after liquid and vapor phase corrosion tests at 250 °C.
summary: Substrate XRD results are shown for liquid and vapor phase corrosion tests at 250 °C. The analysis indicates that the iron present in the material leads to the formation of iron sulfides as the primary corrosion products, consistent with the observed behavior of other iron-containing samples in this study.

caption: Log-log plot of stress versus strain rate for the thin-hinge structure at various axial compressive strains, including base material data for comparison.
summary: This plot displays the stress-strain rate relationship for thin-hinge structures at different compressive strains. The fitted line slopes represent rate sensitivity exponents. Quantitative analysis reveals that the thin-hinge structure exhibits a higher degree of apparent rate-hardening compared to the base photocurable polymer, indicating superior strain rate sensitivity in this configuration.

caption: 3D LSCM micrograph of the Ni-22Cr-14W-2Mo alloy with 0.026% La content after oxidation at 1000 °C for 500 h.
summary: Representing the surface state of the Ni-22Cr-14W-2Mo alloy with 0.026% La, this 3D LSCM micrograph illustrates the morphological changes induced by lanthanum addition after 500 hours at 1000 °C. The visualization allows for an assessment of how this specific lanthanum concentration influences the surface microstructure and oxide development during high-temperature oxidation.

caption: Pole figure illustrating the texture of reconstructed parent β grains for the LPBF example T3.
summary: The pole figure presents the crystallographic texture of reconstructed parent β grains for the LPBF example T3. This panel completes the comparative set of textures, enabling a detailed evaluation of how different LPBF processing parameters affect the orientation of parent grains within the material's microstructure.

caption: EDS point analysis corresponding to the Al–10Ni alloy microstructures.
summary: This panel presents the EDS point analysis conducted on the Al–10Ni alloy samples. The data provides essential compositional information that supports the microstructural observations, confirming the elemental distribution and phase identification necessary to understand the impact of Sm modification on the alloy's solidification behavior and overall structural integrity.

caption: Ternary composition plot illustrating the distribution of desirable phase fractions for bcc Nb (blue) and silicide phases (green), with the overlapping region of interest highlighted.
summary: This ternary composition plot identifies specific regions containing desirable phase fractions of bcc Nb and silicide phases. By mapping these phase distributions, the researchers established a compositional basis for assessing material properties, which facilitated the identification of finer regions for subsequent high-throughput characterization experiments within the studied alloy system.

caption: Hardness versus displacement (H-h) curves for NC Ni-Fe alloy obtained from CLR tests at four different loading rates, with an inset showing an enlarged view of the rectangular region.
summary: Panel (d) illustrates the hardness versus displacement (H-h) curves for the NC Ni-Fe alloy during CLR tests at four different loading rates. The included inset offers an enlarged view of the curves in the outlined rectangular area, enabling precise observation of the alloy's mechanical response during the CLR indentation process.

caption: Element segregation coefficient k plotted against radial position for the bottom section of a φ508mm GH4151 alloy ingot.
summary: This line graph displays the element segregation coefficient k as a function of radial position for the bottom section of a φ508mm GH4151 alloy ingot. By comparing these values with the head section, the plot highlights the spatial distribution of alloying elements and the extent of segregation occurring at the ingot base.

caption: Radar chart comparing the performance metrics of the XGBoost model against alternative machine learning models.
summary: This radar chart evaluates the performance of the XGBoost model relative to other machine learning approaches. The visualization highlights the model's ability to maintain low error metrics and high performance values, confirming its effectiveness in modeling complex nonlinear relationships while successfully avoiding overfitting during the predictive analysis process.

caption: Specific wear rate measurements for as-built and heat-treated specimens.
summary: Specific wear rate data is presented for both as-built and heat-treated conditions. Consistent with the volume loss trends, the as-built samples demonstrate superior wear resistance, while the heat-treated samples consistently display higher specific wear rates across the range of normal loads tested in this study.

caption: Size distribution profile of the Co-Ni/rGO material calculated using the BET model.
summary: The size distribution of the Co-Ni/rGO material is displayed based on the BET model analysis. This histogram provides a quantitative representation of the particle or pore size distribution, which is derived from the nitrogen adsorption data to characterize the physical dimensions of the synthesized Co-Ni/rGO composite.

caption: Room temperature Ni-Fe-Cr ternary phase diagram used to identify the phase composition of the diffusion affected zone based on principal element concentrations.
summary: This room temperature Ni-Fe-Cr ternary phase diagram serves as a reference for interpreting the chemical composition of the joint. Based on the measured concentrations of the principal elements, the diffusion affected zone is identified as being primarily composed of the γ phase, consistent with established phase equilibrium data.

caption: Compressive stress-strain characteristics of the 3Re alloy recorded at different testing temperatures.
summary: Compressive stress-strain characteristics of the 3Re alloy are recorded at different testing temperatures. The alloy demonstrates a clear yielding point followed by a sustained increase in stress, driven by plastic deformation and stress hardening. This trend indicates that higher external stress is required to maintain balance during the compression test.

caption: Compositional profile for the Cu-0.06Ag/Cu-7.28Ni-2.05Ag diffusion couple annealed at 1223K for 96h, comparing experimental measurements with NI and MK simulation results.
summary: Depicting the Cu-0.06Ag/Cu-7.28Ni-2.05Ag diffusion couple after 96 hours of annealing at 1223K, this panel compares experimental data with simulated concentration profiles. The plot highlights the agreement between the NI and MK atomic mobility methods and the measured experimental values, confirming the reliability of the simulation approach for this system.

caption: Tan delta (δ) versus temperature plots for PLA, TCNF/PLA, and ChNF/PLA specimens aged for 3 weeks at room temperature.
summary: Tan delta versus temperature curves are presented for specimens aged for 3 weeks at room temperature. These results are compared against non-aged samples to assess the impact of ageing on the viscoelastic damping properties of the pure PLA and the nanofiber-reinforced composites after a short-term exposure.

caption: Experimental relief strain data for the P9 NiTi sample, showing the variation of x- and y-direction strains relative to the depth from the bottom surface.
summary: This panel shows the relief strain distribution for the P9 sample, detailing the εxx and εyy values at different depths from the bottom surface. The data, derived from the FIB-DIC method, characterizes the residual elastic strain profile induced in the nanocrystalline NiTi material by the P9 laser shock peening treatment.

caption: Time-temperature transformation diagram for A625 illustrating the δ phase formation kinetics for ICS and CDS samples, with dashed lines indicating agreement with literature values from Stoudt et al. and Floreen et al.
summary: This TTT diagram displays the δ phase formation kinetics for A625 under ICS and CDS deposition strategies. The plotted temperature and time ranges for layers 9–15 in the CDS strategy align closely with established literature values for L-PBF and weld metal, confirming the validity of the observed phase transformation behavior.

caption: Representative Nyquist plots for MoldJet 316L samples at top, middle, and bottom build heights, showing single semicircles fitted with curves.
summary: Nyquist plots for MoldJet 316L samples immersed in PBS at open circuit potential exhibit single semicircles across all build heights. These spectra indicate the presence of a stable, protective surface layer on the material, demonstrating electrochemical consistency regardless of the specific build region evaluated during the impedance spectroscopy analysis.

caption: Optical photograph of an etched SB-CoNi-10+ single crystal bar prior to homogenization, displayed against a 1 cm grid background.
summary: This optical photograph displays an etched SB-CoNi-10+ single crystal bar before homogenization. The image is presented against a 1 cm grid background to provide scale. The macro-etching process confirms the successful casting of the bar, demonstrating the absence of freckle chains or significant stray grains throughout the specimen.

caption: Logarithmic current density versus reciprocal charge plot for low VED and low VED_HT samples, demonstrating the high-field repassivation model.
summary: Low VED and low VED_HT samples are analyzed using log(i) versus reciprocal charge (Q-1) coordinates. This plot facilitates the estimation of the characteristic parameter cBV, derived from the high-field repassivation model. The model relates the potential drop in the oxide film to activation energy parameters for ion migration during oxidation.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the transverse (X–Y) plane for the HT1 90° C263 variant, illustrating the texture characteristics.
summary: Representing the HT1 90° variant, this inverse pole figure map shows the grain orientation distribution. Similar to the 0° counterpart, this variant maintains a texture that results in lower misorientation between neighboring grains, which is less effective at inhibiting crack propagation during testing than the eradicated texture found in HT2 variants.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and corresponding elemental distribution map of the bonding interface, revealing a 200 nm thick layer predominantly composed of Cr–O phase.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image and elemental distribution map characterize the bonding interface, which possesses a thickness of approximately 200 nm. The analysis confirms the region is predominantly comprised of a Cr–O phase, while also identifying the presence of W–Si phases within the interface zone of the joint fabricated at 5 MPa.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the Al0.7 alloy following tensile deformation.
summary: Captured after tensile deformation, this bright-field TEM image displays the microstructural state of the Al0.7 alloy. The visualization allows for the examination of dislocation behavior and structural changes at this higher aluminum concentration, providing critical data for understanding the influence of composition on the alloy's overall mechanical deformation characteristics.

caption: Projection view showing the spatial distribution of pores within the x–y plane for the two specimens under investigation along the build direction.
summary: Spatial distributions of pores in the x–y plane for the two specimens are visualized in this projection view. The image highlights the arrangement of pores along the build direction, offering a clear perspective on how porosity is distributed spatially within the cross-section of the studied samples.

caption: Gastric bioaccessible (BAc) nickel leaching data for metallic Ni and various Ni alloys, plotted as a function of surface area, with linear regression models for Ni metal powders and combined Ni metal/alloy powders, including a magnified inset of the origin.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the gastric bioaccessibility of nickel from metallic Ni and various alloys, highlighting a strong correlation between surface area and BAc. The data confirm the relative inertness of austenitic stainless steels and superalloys, while providing regression equations that quantify leaching behavior across different nickel-based materials.

caption: UV-VIS transmittance curves comparing different samples, illustrating the optical transparency and structural purity of the superlattice materials.
summary: UV-VIS transmission measurements provide confirmation of the optical transparency and structural purity of the investigated samples. These transmittance curves complement the structural data, demonstrating that the graded superlattice materials maintain high optical quality, which is essential for their performance in the studied applications.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry profile of EAN containing 0.5 M NiCl₂ recorded at 50 mV·s⁻¹ on a glassy carbon electrode, starting from the open circuit potential.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry measurements for EAN with 0.5 M NiCl₂ were performed starting from the open circuit potential, scanning first in the cathodic direction followed by the anodic direction. This profile characterizes the electrochemical behavior of the nickel-doped electrolyte system at a scan rate of 50 mV·s⁻¹.

caption: Loop component extracted from the unit cell network.
summary: Depicting the final section of the unit cell, this panel highlights the loop component. This specific structural feature completes the three-part decomposition of the unit cell network, enabling a comprehensive validation of the method by examining the loop's contribution to the overall geometry of the validated structure.

caption: Block diagram illustrating the proportional control procedure for print head height adjustment during additive manufacturing.
summary: This block diagram outlines the proportional control procedure used to manage print head height during the manufacturing process. The control logic adjusts the z-coordinate to maintain a specific stand-off distance relative to the underlying part profile, ensuring consistent layer deposition based on the calculated height parameters and feedback loops.

caption: HRTEM micrograph showing the atomic-scale structure of the in-situ formed nanoscale oxides within the HEA-5wt% WC sample.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging provides a detailed view of the atomic structure of the nanoscale oxides formed in the HEA-5wt% WC sample. This visualization confirms the presence and morphology of these oxides, which are critical for understanding the microstructural evolution and the impact of WC particles on the HEA matrix.

caption: Comparison of predicted bead widths w ̂ k against measured widths w k for the third deposition run, presented as a time series with a sampling interval of 0.01 s.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the performance of the selected model by comparing predicted bead widths to measured values from the third deposition run. The dataset, comprising approximately 20,000 points, is visualized as a time series with a sampling interval of 0.01 s, demonstrating the model's predictive accuracy on validation data.

caption: EDS elemental map of Titanium (Ti) distribution within the bcc matrix of the HPT-processed sample AB, demonstrating chemical homogeneity.
summary: The EDS elemental map for Titanium reveals the distribution of this element within the bcc matrix of the HPT-processed sample AB. Consistent with the reference, the map confirms a reasonable degree of chemical homogeneity across the deformed microstructure, indicating that the alloying elements are well-distributed following the severe plastic deformation process.

caption: Phase map of the HT800/3 condition, showing the distribution of γ austenite and α' martensite phases.
summary: The phase map for the HT800/3 condition illustrates the spatial arrangement of γ austenite (blue) and α' martensite (red). This visualization helps characterize the phase composition of the material following the HT800/3 heat treatment and mechanical testing, complementing the SEM observations of the χ phase.

caption: Lithiation-phase apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions for 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes, derived from Eq. (1).

(1), these results allow for the evaluation of ion insertion behavior, highlighting the performance differences between the two distinct electrode fabrication methods during the lithiation process.

caption: Bulk porosity of modified quartz sand B plotted against theoretical surface area coverage or layer thickness.
summary: This graph displays the bulk porosity of modified quartz sand B as a function of theoretical surface area coverage or layer thickness. Consistent with the observed trend for sand A, the porosity of the nano-TiO2-modified sand B increases steadily with higher surface area coverage values across the tested range.

caption: Small Angle X-Ray Scattering (SAXS) profiles comparing NoBPH and BPH specimens, demonstrating an increased volume fraction of secondary precipitates while primary precipitates remain stable.
summary: SAXS measurements reveal distinct differences in the precipitate populations between NoBPH and BPH specimens. The data indicates that while primary precipitates remain unchanged, the BPH specimen exhibits an increased volume fraction of secondary precipitates, providing insight into the microstructural evolution resulting from the specific processing conditions applied to the material.

caption: Total density of states for pure Cu calculated using a 6 × 6 × 6 k-point mesh.
summary: The total density of states for pure copper is shown here, derived from a 6 × 6 × 6 k-point mesh calculation. This higher-density mesh refinement allows for an assessment of convergence in the electronic density of states compared to the 4 × 4 × 4 mesh result.

caption: LRO evolution profile for Ni3(Al,Ti) subjected to a single cascade, highlighting the kinetic reordering process.
summary: Depicted here is the LRO evolution for the Ni3(Al,Ti) system under single cascade conditions. The green dashed line indicates the time required to reach equilibrium between irradiation-induced disordering and kinetic reordering at 100 K. The shaded area reflects the standard error calculated from six independent simulations, showing a striking concordance with (Ni,Co)3(Al,Ti).

caption: Tensile strength versus ductility scatter plot for the high productivity theme, displaying specimen performance relative to ASTM F3001 standards, with color-coded distance from the gas outlet and specific identification of HIP 1050C specimens failing to meet strength criteria.
summary: This plot evaluates tensile strength and ductility for the high productivity theme, using color to denote distance from the gas outlet. While most specimens meet the ASTM F3001 standard, two HIP 1050C specimens located at the rear of the build plate, represented by dark blue diamonds, fail to meet the required strength criteria.

caption: Quantification of dead cell proportions on modified Ti- and Zr-surfaces, represented as the ratio of red to green fluorescence intensity, analyzed via ImageJ with statistical significance determined by the Friedman test.
summary: Quantification of dead cell proportions on modified Ti- and Zr-surfaces, represented as the ratio of red to green fluorescence intensity, analyzed via ImageJ with statistical significance determined by the Friedman test. Live/dead staining after 72 h revealed an overall effect across surfaces, though post-hoc comparisons did not identify significant pairwise differences.

caption: Comprehensive flowchart illustrating the fatigue strength assessment methodology for additive manufactured AISI 316L specimens.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic approach for evaluating the fatigue strength of additive manufactured AISI 316L samples. The process integrates experimental fatigue testing data with machine learning techniques to provide a robust assessment framework, ensuring a structured workflow for analyzing the mechanical performance of the printed metallic components.

caption: Temperature dependence of the derivative of magnetization (dM/dT) used to identify Curie temperatures (Tc) for HTHed Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond samples.
summary: Derivative curves of magnetization with respect to temperature (dM/dT) are plotted to precisely determine Curie temperatures. The analysis reveals distinct Tc values of 267 K, 240 K, 250 K, and 239 K for the HTHed Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond samples, respectively, highlighting the influence of geometry on magnetic transition properties.

caption: Comparison of fracture toughness versus hardness for carbon-free cermets containing 7.0 wt% boron, alloyed with nickel and chromium.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical performance of sintered carbon-free cermets, specifically those containing 7.0 wt% boron and alloyed with nickel and chromium. It compares fracture toughness against hardness values to evaluate the material properties, highlighting the relationship between these two critical mechanical parameters for the investigated alloy compositions.

caption: Deconvoluted Thermal Desorption Spectroscopy (TDS) spectrum for the thick sample, recorded at a heating rate of 1000 K/h.
summary: The deconvoluted TDS spectrum displays the hydrogen desorption behavior for the thick sample at a heating rate of 1000 K/h. Because the sample was not saturated, the deconvoluted peaks are primarily attributed to hydrogen diffusion and desorption processes occurring at the sample surface rather than bulk trapping sites.

caption: Gibbs free energy change curves as a function of formation temperature for various oxides, including TiO and Al2O3, derived from thermochemical data.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermodynamic stability of various oxides, specifically TiO and Al2O3, by showing their Gibbs free energy change curves relative to temperature. The data indicates that the direct formation of the TiO phase is thermodynamically unfavorable at sintering temperatures below 1057 °C, consistent with established thermochemical findings.

caption: Al2O3 TPMS structure model representing a periodic minimal surface architecture.
summary: The Al2O3 TPMS structure model illustrates the application of periodic minimal surface design principles to alumina ceramics. This structural configuration is part of a broader class of lattice architectures fabricated via VPP technology, highlighting the versatility of additive manufacturing in producing complex, high-strength ceramic components with controlled porosity.

caption: Core-loss EELS spectra of the Cr L2,3-edges acquired from points 1 to 7, illustrating the electronic state of chromium near the cell boundary.
summary: Core-loss EELS spectra for the Cr L2 and L3 edges were acquired from seven distinct points across the lamellar boundary. These spectra provide detailed information regarding the electronic state of chromium near the cell boundary, allowing for a localized assessment of chemical variations across the interface of the material layers.

caption: Isothermal TTT diagram of X37CrMoV5-1 tool steel specifically derived for the PBF-LB/M processing condition.
summary: This panel presents an isothermal TTT diagram for X37CrMoV5-1 tool steel, specifically tailored to represent the PBF-LB/M processing condition. Derived from experimental findings, this diagram illustrates the transformation kinetics and phase stability boundaries characteristic of the material when subjected to laser powder bed fusion processing routes.

caption: Failure probability plot for 42S-20P samples calculated from Weibull statistics with a 95% confidence interval.
summary: Failure probability for the 42S-20P samples is illustrated within a 95% confidence interval based on Weibull statistics. This analysis allows for the assessment of the material's mechanical reliability, showing the distribution of failure probability that corresponds to the lower characteristic strength observed in this specific suspension group.

caption: Elastic modulus values extracted at 1 Hz for GelMA control, GelMA with BG, and GelMA with BGMA cryogels.
summary: The elastic modulus at 1 Hz provides a quantitative comparison of the stiffness for the different cryogel formulations. This mechanical parameter highlights the impact of incorporating bioactive glass and its surface modification on the structural integrity and mechanical performance of the GelMA-based cryogel scaffolds.

caption: First nearest neighbor pair distribution function for Fe0.25Ni0.75 in 16- and 32-atom SQS cells following full structural relaxation.
summary: This panel displays the first nearest neighbor pair distribution function for the Fe0.25Ni0.75 composition. The data is derived from 16- and 32-atom SQS models after the structure has undergone full relaxation, providing insight into the local atomic environment and structural stability of this specific alloy configuration.

caption: Experimental Co–Al phase diagram contrasted with a calculated diagram derived using only configurational entropic contributions.
summary: Shown here is the experimental Co–Al phase diagram plotted against a calculated model that considers only configurational entropy. The absence of specific phases like Al3Co4 and Al3Co is noted, and the transition from hcp to fcc Co is not detected because the Gibbs free energy of fcc Co remains higher.

caption: Direct aged specimen stress–time and strain–time curves with corresponding axial (εxx) and lateral (εyy) strain fields during quasi-static compression.
summary: Direct aged specimens undergo quasi-static compression, characterized by stress–time and strain–time curves. DIC strain maps reveal the evolution of axial and lateral strain fields. Similar to other conditions, the deformation sequence begins with an elastic stage showing minimal gradients, while the shear component remains low throughout the entire loading path.

caption: Mechanical compression response of 85% porous carboHIPE lattices pyrolyzed at 800 °C, illustrating the stress-strain performance across four replicate specimens.
summary: Mechanical compression testing results for 85% porous carboHIPE lattices pyrolyzed at 800 °C are presented here. The plot includes stress-strain curves for four replicate samples, all of which were tested to failure. These curves demonstrate the mechanical characteristics and structural integrity of the 85% porosity samples under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Final curved strut geometry with the desired thickness integrated into the completed DCC unit cell.
summary: The final output shows the curved strut rendered with the specified thickness, successfully integrated into the DCC unit cell. This panel demonstrates the culmination of the geometric modeling process, resulting in a fully defined unit cell structure suitable for further analysis or additive manufacturing applications.

caption: Pearson correlation coefficient matrix illustrating the linear relationships between various input features and the target tensile strength (TS) value.
summary: This Pearson correlation coefficient matrix provides a quantitative analysis of the linear correlations between individual features and the target tensile strength (TS). By visualizing these relationships, the matrix identifies which features exhibit the strongest linear associations with tensile strength, facilitating a deeper understanding of the underlying data dependencies for predictive modeling.

caption: Schoen-gyroid (G) TPMS structure illustrating its specific internal connectivity and surface curvature.
summary: The Schoen-gyroid (G) is one of the five primary Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) structures. It is characterized by its unique internal connectivity, surface curvature, and overall topological arrangement, distinguishing it from other TPMS geometries and traditional cubic lattice designs.

caption: Comprehensive experimental methodology flowchart illustrating the systematic process for parameter optimization using the TOPSIS decision-making framework.
summary: This flowchart outlines the complete experimental methodology employed in the study. The process integrates a set of process parameters evaluated through the TOPSIS technique, which prioritizes optimal conditions based on specific mechanical performance metrics, including tensile strength, elastic modulus, flexural strength, flexural modulus, and fracture strain requirements.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H IEA steel evaluated using 1/3-size PCCVN specimens in the L-T orientation.
summary: Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H IEA steel are shown for 1/3-size PCCVN specimens in the L-T orientation. These findings, part of a broader summary of the material's irradiation behavior, were derived from tests conducted at target temperatures of 300 °C and 500 °C to evaluate structural integrity.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles for 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 composite electrodes (256 μm thickness) tested at 0.1C within a 1.0–2.5 V voltage window.
summary: The 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 composite electrode exhibits an initial discharge capacity of 215.47 mAh g-1 at 0.1C. These galvanostatic charge-discharge curves, recorded within a 1.0–2.5 V voltage range, demonstrate the electrochemical performance of the thick 3D-printed architecture compared to conventional ink-cast counterparts under identical testing conditions.

caption: 3D normalized Young’s modulus surface profile for the RNFS:2:0 mono-RNL architecture.
summary: This panel displays the 3D normalized Young’s modulus surface profile for the RNFS:2:0 mono-RNL architecture. The visualization illustrates the anisotropic elastic behavior of the lattice, providing a spatial representation of the modulus distribution as part of the parametric investigation into mono-RNL classification based on anisotropic mechanical response.

caption: Magnetization versus magnetic field plot for the as-rolled sample with the field applied parallel to the rolling direction, featuring an inset highlighting the hysteresis behavior.
summary: The as-rolled sample exhibits magnetization versus field behavior with a ferromagnetic component. The inset reveals a hysteresis loop characterized by a coercivity of 100 Oe, a remnant magnetization of 1.6 kA/m, and a saturation magnetization of 12.6 kA/m, measured at 4.2 K.

caption: Fluctuations in the coefficient of friction observed over the number of cycles for both as-built and heat-treated AlSi10Mg samples at 15 Hz.
summary: At a fretting frequency of 15 Hz, the coefficient of friction for both as-built and heat-treated AlSi10Mg samples exhibits noticeable fluctuations over the number of cycles. This plot captures the dynamic frictional response of the material under these specific high-frequency testing conditions throughout the duration of the experiment.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan performed across an inclusion identified in panel (b), demonstrating an increased concentration of magnesium within the particle.
summary: EDS line scan analysis of the inclusion shown in panel (b) confirms its chemical identity. The spectroscopic data indicates a significant enrichment of magnesium within the inclusion, distinguishing it from the surrounding matrix and providing evidence of the specific elemental composition of these spherical particles found at the fracture surface.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of P3HT-PSL showing characteristic resonance peaks.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of P3HT-PSL reveals that P3HT peaks dominate the signal, appearing significantly stronger than the anticipated PPI-SL peaks. This intensity disparity is attributed to space interactions occurring within the structure. The peak assignments align well with the established PPI-SL structural framework described in literature.

caption: Comparison of relative elongation at fracture and relative reduction of area for wrought and SLM-processed alloy 718, illustrating their comparable susceptibility to hydrogen embrittlement.
summary: This panel compares the relative elongation at fracture and relative reduction of area for wrought and SLM-processed alloy 718. The data demonstrates that both manufacturing methods exhibit a comparable susceptibility to hydrogen embrittlement, indicating that the additive manufacturing process does not significantly alter this specific mechanical performance metric compared to conventional wrought material.

caption: LSCM image of SLM pure tungsten deposit B13 processed at 972 J/mm3, showing the crack distribution relative to the grain structure.
summary: Panel b provides a detailed view of the SLM pure tungsten deposit B13. The image captures the spatial distribution of cracks relative to the grain boundaries. This structural analysis helps explain the mechanical performance of the sample, specifically its high coefficient of friction attributed to the presence of these defects.

caption: Creep behavior of the SLMed IN718 alloy evaluated at a 30 N load, showing the variation in creep resistance relative to the distance from the worn subsurface.
summary: Creep analysis reveals that the creep resistance of the SLMed IN718 alloy is significantly enhanced near the worn subsurface compared to the bulk region. These measurements were conducted following contact sliding at a high load of 30 N, highlighting the improved mechanical stability of the material's surface layer.

caption: Contour plot showing the simultaneous variation of slot length, slot width, and substrate thickness on FSS performance.
summary: Simultaneous three-parameter variation is presented to evaluate complex interactions. The data confirms that although interaction effects exist among slot width, slot length, and substrate thickness, these interactions do not override the dominant role of the slot length in determining the resonance characteristics of the proposed FSS design.

caption: Absorbance spectra of mixed powders within the A92618-C10200 system, illustrating the spectral response across varying levels of contamination.
summary: This figure displays the medium absorbance spectra for the A92618-C10200 material system. The data represents the spectral characteristics of mixed powders evaluated at different amounts of contamination. These results provide a comparative overview of how varying contamination levels influence the optical absorbance properties of the analyzed powder system.

caption: Spectral normal emissivity of 316 stainless steel measured at room temperature using a reflective technique, comparing the pristine state to the condition after 1000 hours of exposure to 750 °C FLiBe.
summary: This plot displays the spectral normal emissivity of 316 stainless steel before and after 1000 hours of exposure to 750 °C FLiBe. Measurements were performed at room temperature using a reflective technique. The data reveals a significant increase in emissivity following FLiBe exposure, despite the relatively small surface roughness changes.

caption: Thickness variation of various Ni-based/2D material nanocomposite coatings, illustrating the impact of deposition efficiency on growth.
summary: This bar chart displays the measured thickness of various Ni-based/2D material nanocomposite coatings. The data reveals that when the bonding strength between BN and MoS2 or WS2 is weak, deposition efficiency decreases, causing the coating thickness to remain lower than expected compared to other nanocomposite formulations.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectra of various oxime esters measured in acetonitrile solvent.
summary: This figure displays the UV–visible absorption spectra for a series of oxime esters in acetonitrile. These spectral profiles are critical for determining light absorption characteristics, such as the maximum absorption wavelength of 355 nm for O-12, and for correlating molar extinction coefficients with polymerization rates under different light sources.

caption: Representative X-ray image of Ti-6Al-4V laser melting, highlighting the melt pool in red and defining keyhole depth (d1) and front wall angle (θ) relative to the 77 μm laser spot size.
summary: This X-ray image illustrates the laser melting process of Ti-6Al-4V plates, specifically identifying the melt pool geometry. Key parameters such as the keyhole depth and the front keyhole wall angle are measured directly from these images to characterize the morphology of the keyhole during the laser processing.

caption: Solidification rate at the solid/liquid interface plotted against the height from the melt pool bottom, evaluated using CtFD simulation.
summary: Solidification rate (R) values are shown as a function of height from the bottom of the melt pool. The simulation data demonstrates that R is at its minimum near the fusion line and increases steadily as the interface progresses toward the center of the melt region.

caption: Schematic representation of the B2 crystal structure for the NiTiCo alloy system.
summary: This panel presents a schematic model of the B2 crystal structure specifically for the NiTiCo alloy. It serves as a comparative representation to the binary NiTi system, illustrating the structural configuration of the ternary alloy within the B2 framework, consistent with the ordered CsCl-type lattice arrangement.

caption: Flow-stress curves comparing base materials, derived from NaMo predictions, against the weld material, obtained via inverse modelling of experimental uniaxial tension test data.
summary: Panel (a) displays flow-stress curves for base and weld materials. Base material curves are generated using NaMo predictions based on chemical compositions and through-process histories. The weld material curve, represented by a grey line, is determined through inverse modelling of experimental uniaxial tension test data, highlighting distinct work-hardening characteristics.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing pure PLA matrix with composites reinforced by 5 wt% untreated and chemically treated enset and sisal fibers.
summary: This figure presents the FTIR spectra analysis of pure PLA and various fiber-reinforced composites. The plot compares the chemical signatures of PLA reinforced with 5 wt% of either untreated or chemically treated enset and sisal fibers, providing insight into the chemical interactions between the polymer matrix and the natural reinforcements.

caption: Sequential deformation images captured during uniaxial loading of the hydrogel specimens.
summary: Sequential deformation images illustrate the physical response of the hydrogel specimens during uniaxial loading. These photographs provide a visual record of the material's behavior under stress, complementing the quantitative mechanical data obtained from the three-point bending tests performed on the independently prepared specimens to ensure consistent and accurate experimental results.

caption: Overlapped atomic configuration of the CN15 layer and the (111) γ' layer, demonstrating the semicoherent interface of the TCP/γ' structure.
summary: This panel shows the overlapped atomic configuration of the CN15 layer and the (111) γ' layer, illustrating the semicoherent interface of the TCP/γ' structure. This specific configuration was selected for misfit strain estimation due to its superior symmetry and atomic distance matching compared to other potential layers.

caption: Full-range XRD patterns comparing Invar 36 powders with AB-10, HT1, and HT2 samples.
summary: This panel displays the full-range XRD patterns for Invar 36 powders alongside the AB-10, HT1, and HT2 samples. These diffraction data provide a comprehensive overview of the crystalline phases present across the different processing conditions, serving as the primary dataset for subsequent structural analysis and crystal plane spacing calculations.

caption: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) image highlighting the lattice structure of the NiTi fiber.
summary: The IFFT image provides a filtered representation of the NiTi fiber lattice structure. By isolating specific frequency components from the FFT, this visualization clarifies the atomic arrangement and structural integrity of the NiTi fiber phase within the analyzed interface region.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of Ni50Ti45Ta5 alloy revealing the typical triangular martensitic morphology.
summary: This bright-field TEM image presents the typical triangular martensitic morphology observed in the Ni50Ti45Ta5 alloy. The sample was prepared using the same VIM method as the other alloys, followed by homogenization, forging, hot drawing, and vacuum annealing, confirming the martensitic structure within the NiTiTa alloy system.

caption: Electrical resistivity evolution of as-fabricated ABD-900AM superalloy during the first heating and cooling cycle from super-solvus 1 temperature.
summary: The electrical resistivity of as-fabricated ABD-900AM is monitored during the first thermal cycle from super-solvus 1 temperature. This zero-load measurement interprets the gamma-prime reaction, as the gamma and gamma-prime phases exhibit distinct resistivity values. A drastic, continuous increase in resistivity is observed starting at 450 °C, indicating the phase reaction.

caption: Contrast-enhanced fluorescence image of the 3D-printed letters under 365 nm LED excitation, revealing strong emission from the cured TMPTA product.
summary: This contrast-enhanced fluorescence image captures the 3D-printed letters under 365 nm LED excitation. The product exhibits strong fluorescence, confirming the successful incorporation and activation of the initiator system within the cured TMPTA matrix. This visual evidence highlights the effective photocuring quality and the optical properties of the printed material.

caption: Force-displacement curves illustrating the compression deformation behavior of HHBS structures across five distinct pinch angles.
summary: This plot displays the force-displacement curves during the compression deformation of HHBS structures with five different pinch angles. These curves characterize the mechanical response, specifically highlighting the platform stage, which represents the main stabilizing energy absorption phase. The data derived from these curves are essential for calculating key performance metrics like EA, SEA, and PCF.

caption: Elongation versus tensile strength comparison of magnesium alloys against conventional metallic implants, biodegradable polymers, and human bone.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the mechanical performance space of magnesium alloys relative to other common metallic implants, human bone, and biodegradable polymers. By mapping elongation against tensile strength, the graph highlights the positioning of various magnesium alloy processing routes, providing a comparative overview of their suitability for biomedical implant applications.

caption: Bode phase angle plots for LPBF specimens, where phase angles approach 75° across a wide frequency range.
summary: Bode phase angle plots demonstrate that all LPBF specimens exhibit similar frequency-dependent impedance modulus behavior. The phase angles consistently approach 75° across a broad frequency range, which suggests the presence of capacitive behavior associated with the formation of protective surface films on the LPBF DSS 2205 and reinforced composites.

caption: Frequency distribution of pore diameters within the S30 configuration, accompanied by an inset showing the spherical morphology of the internal pores.
summary: The histogram presents the frequency distribution of pore diameters observed in the S30 configuration. The included inset highlights the morphology of the porosity, which is predominantly spherical with varied diameters, providing a detailed view of the internal pore characteristics for this specific supported overhang configuration.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry thermograms comparing raw MB, TPU, and PEDOT:PSS against their respective film composites, demonstrating thermal stability up to 80 °C.
summary: DSC thermograms for raw materials and their composite films are presented. Analysis confirms that the starting materials, including PEDOT:PSS, TPU, and MB, remain thermally stable up to 80 °C. No significant thermal events are observed in the PEDOT:PSS and MB samples until reaching 120 °C, indicating structural integrity during processing.

caption: Static magnetic hysteresis loops comparing Co-MG, PS-grafted Co-MG, and commercial materials including Mn–Zn ferrite and permalloy 1J85.
summary: Static magnetic hysteresis loops are presented for Co-MG, PS-grafted Co-MG, and commercial materials like Mn–Zn ferrite and permalloy 1J85. These loops characterize the magnetic response of the materials, with specific parameters derived from the starting and maximum values of the magnetization hysteresis loop derivatives to evaluate their magnetic performance.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to the negative control medium.
summary: Human Gingival Fibroblasts cultured for 72 hours in a negative control medium are visualized using fluorescence microscopy. The Live/Dead staining highlights the population of live (green) and dead (red) cells, serving as a long-term control to compare against the viability results observed with various material extracts.

caption: Violin plot showing the distribution of Lack of Fusion (LoF) porosity across threshold bins for PBF-EB-printed parts.
summary: This violin plot depicts the distribution of LoF porosity in PBF-EB-printed parts across various threshold bins. As indicated by the reference, there is a strong increase in the LoF porosity level as the classification transitions from Excellent to Failed, highlighting a clear correlation between threshold bins and defect severity.

caption: Close-up view of the as-printed AVM-shape component, showing the part still attached to the base plate via support material.
summary: A detailed view of the AVM-shape resin print is presented, captured immediately after the printing process. The component remains connected to the printing base plate through the support material, which is subsequently removed using tweezers to isolate the printed design from the printing surface.

caption: Parity plot showing the relationship between experimental and RF-predicted cycles to failure for long carbon fiber composites, utilizing strain as the input measure for the baseline dataset.
summary: Strain-based predictions for the baseline dataset are depicted in this parity plot. By excluding new data production, this visualization provides a baseline for assessing the model's predictive performance on unseen long carbon fiber composite samples, allowing for a direct comparison with the enhanced dataset outcomes.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology and cross-sectional wear track profile of the as-deposited AZ91 alloy specimen.
summary: This panel displays the 3D morphology and two-dimensional cross-sectional contour of the wear track for the as-deposited AZ91 alloy. The visualization provides a baseline for comparing the wear behavior of the base alloy against the TiC-reinforced composite samples under identical tribological testing conditions.

caption: Posterior-anterior radiograph of the INNOTERE 3D scaffold wedge at 1 month post-owHTO, illustrating the initial stage of osteointegration.
summary: This posterior-anterior radiograph displays the INNOTERE 3D scaffold wedge one month after an opening-wedge high tibial osteotomy (owHTO). The image serves as the baseline for monitoring the progression of osteointegration and scaffold resorption within the surgical site during the early postoperative healing phase.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the natural logarithm of relaxation time (ln τ) versus the inverse temperature (1000/T) for the recycled vitrimer.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between the natural logarithm of the relaxation time and the inverse temperature. By plotting the relaxation time values obtained at different temperatures, the activation energy of the recycled material can be calculated, providing critical insight into the temperature-dependent kinetics of the vitrimer's relaxation process.

caption: Representative stress–strain curve of TSICs illustrating fracture morphologies at distinct failure points along the loading path.
summary: This stress–strain curve displays the mechanical response of TSICs, highlighting specific fracture morphologies at various failure points. The data demonstrates how the design of shear and tensile layer thicknesses allows for the tuning of mechanical properties, with fracture events clearly mapped to the stress-strain behavior of the composite material.

caption: Rate capability performance comparison for PPy/3D-IDCμE devices using different gel electrolytes, showing capacitance retention across varying current densities.
summary: The rate capability investigation demonstrates the performance of PPy/3D-IDCμE devices with different gel electrolytes. The 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H2SO4, 15 wt% PVA in 1M H2SO4, and 1 wt% agarose in 3M LiCl electrolytes retain 62%, 54%, and 42% of their initial capacitance, respectively, when current density increases tenfold.

caption: Parity plot comparing the actual measured values of AOR for α-RHG against the predicted responses generated by the streamlined multiple regression model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the fitting relationship between the actual measured values and the predicted responses for the AOR of α-RHG. The data points exhibit a clear linear relationship, indicating that the streamlined multiple regression model achieves a high level of agreement between the response surface and the true values.

caption: Polar figures derived from EBSD data, indicating the absence of strong crystallographic texture in the as-cast microstructure.
summary: Polar figures generated from EBSD data confirm that the as-cast microstructure of the Ni–Mo–Cr-Gd alloy lacks a strong crystallographic texture. This analysis complements the IPF mapping, ensuring a thorough understanding of the orientation distribution and the isotropic nature of the grains in the as-cast state.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the binary classification accuracy of the CNN model for identifying stringing defects.
summary: The confusion matrix for stringing defects displays the classification results of the CNN model. It serves as a diagnostic tool to assess the model's predictive accuracy, showing how effectively the algorithm differentiates between the presence and absence of stringing defects within the analyzed dataset of manufacturing components.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of rBMSCs stained for live and dead cells within osteochondral scaffolds after 1 and 7 days of culture.
summary: Live and dead staining reveals the viability of rBMSCs seeded in osteochondral scaffolds after 1 and 7 days. Observations indicate that after 1 day, most cells in the subchondral zone attached to the strut surface, while nearly all cells in the cartilage zone hydrogel bricks remained alive and formed spontaneous microspheres.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image focusing on a local region of the 2 wt% TC4 specimen, revealing MgZn2 precipitates located along grain boundaries.
summary: Focusing on a local region of the 2 wt% TC4 specimen, this HAADF-STEM image provides high-contrast visualization of the microstructure. Analysis reveals that MgZn2 precipitation phases are specifically located along the grain boundaries, confirming the distribution of these secondary phases within the alloy matrix.

caption: Response of the material under creep conditions at 1038 ∘ C for the full range of tested stress levels.
summary: This panel shows the creep curves at 1038 ∘ C for all tested stress levels. The results confirm the effectiveness of the linearization method for θ parameters in the logarithmic scale. This approach provides a robust fit for the creep data, ensuring consistency across the tested temperature and stress plane.

caption: Specific capacitance values calculated from galvanostatic charge-discharge data for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors with 5 OTU layers, evaluated across a range of liquid electrolytes.
summary: Specific capacitance values, calculated from galvanostatic charge-discharge data, are presented for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors with 5 OTU layers tested in various liquid electrolytes. These results quantify the performance variations observed with different electrolytes, enabling a clear determination of the optimal electrolyte for achieving high specific capacitance in the micro-supercapacitor system.

caption: Larson-Miller Parameter (L.M.P) plot comparing the stress rupture resistance of heat-treated (HT) LW 4280 against various LPBF-fabricated (ABD-900AM, CM 247LC) and cast (IN 738LC, Rene 80) Ni-superalloys.
summary: This Larson-Miller Parameter plot evaluates the stress rupture resistance of HT LW 4280 across diverse load and temperature conditions. Closed symbols represent LPBF-fabricated specimens, while open symbols denote cast samples. The data reveals that LW 4280 exhibits inferior stress rupture properties compared to cast IN 738LC and Rene 80 alloys.

caption: Pressure distribution contours along the mid-plane of the bipolar plates for nickel foam and serpentine flow-field designs.
summary: Pressure distribution contours along the mid-plane of the bipolar plates are shown to evaluate the impact of structural and flow-field modifications on pressure drop. While the porous nickel foam structure influences flow, the reduction in parasitic losses is relatively small and considered negligible in the overall performance comparison.

caption: Linearized plot representing non-isothermal kinetic parameters derived from the empirical temperature dependency of crystallization half-time.
summary: This plot illustrates the linearization of non-isothermal kinetic parameters, specifically capturing the temperature dependency of the crystallization half-time. By empirically modeling these parameters, the figure provides a framework to adapt kinetic data for non-isothermal conditions, facilitating a more accurate representation of crystallization behavior across varying temperature profiles in the material.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curve of W + TiC/Ni-based composite coatings tested in a 3.5 wt%/L NaCl + 0.002 mol/L Na2S2O3 solution.
summary: The potentiodynamic polarization curve displays the electrochemical response of W + TiC/Ni-based composite coatings in a corrosive environment containing 3.5 wt%/L NaCl and 0.002 mol/L Na2S2O3. By analyzing this curve, researchers can determine the self-corrosion potential and current to evaluate the coating's tendency to corrode and its overall corrosion resistance.

caption: Parity plot depicting the correlation between experimental and predicted DE for System-2, assessed using different n values.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive performance for System-2 across varying n values. Significant fluctuations in predicted DE are observed at 300 °C and 2.5 MPa, indicating that the n parameter plays a critical role in the accuracy of the DE predictions for this particular material system.

caption: Validation of experimental mechanical properties by comparing bulk tensile test data with DIC-derived measurements.
summary: Validation of the mechanical properties is performed by comparing data obtained from bulk tensile tests with those derived from DIC analysis. This panel serves to confirm the consistency and reliability of the experimental mechanical characterization of the WDED-manufactured cp-Ti components across the different testing methodologies employed.

caption: Current output profile of the fuel cell operating at a constant voltage of 0.8 V and 40 °C, showing an initial sharp decrease followed by a stable current plateau of 18.3 mA.
summary: Operating the fuel cell at 40 °C and a constant voltage of 0.8 V results in a characteristic current response. The produced current exhibits a sharp initial decline before stabilizing at a constant value of 18.3 mA, which corresponds to a power output of 14.64 mW during the test period.

caption: Statistical results table summarizing grain boundary and recrystallization fraction for the top, middle, and bottom layers.
summary: This table presents the statistical results for grain boundary and recrystallization fractions across the layers. Due to rapid cooling at the lower environmental temperature, the deformation temperature remains mostly unchanged, resulting in a similar recrystallization fraction observed throughout the deposited layers of the build.

caption: Experimental and VPSC simulated pole figures for Cu-2.5Ni-0.6Si alloy, comparing initial texture with the deformed state after N = 1/2 turn of HPT processing.
summary: This panel displays the texture evolution for the Cu-2.5Ni-0.6Si alloy. It contrasts the initial crystallographic texture with the simulated deformed texture resulting from N = 1/2 turn of high-pressure torsion. The VPSC simulation provides a comparative view of how the material's orientation distribution changes under these specific severe plastic deformation conditions.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the HIP specimen illustrating the morphology of γ' phase precipitates.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph, collected using the <100> superlattice reflection, provides additional visual evidence of the γ' phase precipitates in the HIP specimen. The image confirms the presence of these particles within the grains, consistent with the microstructural evolution observed following the hot isostatic pressing process applied to the material.

caption: Reconstructed 3D microstructure of the LPBF-manufactured 15–5PH stainless steel sample generated using DREAM 3D software based on EBSD data.
summary: The reconstructed microstructure model represents the 3D grain morphology of the 15–5PH stainless steel sample. By processing the experimental EBSD data through the DREAM 3D software, this reconstruction provides a digital representation of the material's internal architecture, which is essential for performing accurate finite element analysis and mechanical simulations.

caption: Reflectance wavelength variation plot for 3D-printed HPCA objects across the tested temperature range.
summary: This plot illustrates the variation in reflected wavelength for 3D-printed HPCA objects as temperature increases. The data confirms that the reflectance wavelength remains stable, showing only a minor variation within a 10 nm range, which supports the observed structural and color stability of the printed objects under thermal stress.
