caption: Density measurements of samples, highlighting the near-theoretical density achieved by sample II-6.
summary: Density values for the samples are displayed, showing that sample II-6 achieved a density of approximately 100%. Despite this high density, the sample exhibited relatively low tensile properties, with a UTS of 984 MPa, YS of 817 MPa, and EL of 3.3%, indicating that density alone does not dictate mechanical performance.

caption: STEM micrograph of the heat-treated (HT) specimen illustrating carbide analysis spots and surrounding degraded MC-based carbides.
summary: STEM micrograph of the heat-treated specimen highlights carbide analysis spots and regions of degraded MC-based carbides. Evidence of microstructural reaction is visible, including the presence of gamma-prime and M23C6-based carbides surrounding the degraded MC-based carbides. This panel provides critical visual evidence of the phase transformation occurring within the heat-treated material.

caption: Hardness distribution of samples as a function of laser power and scanning speed, showing a gradual increase in hardness correlated with the density of finer α′-martensite structures.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the hardness variation in samples processed with varying laser power and scanning speed. The data indicates that hardness increases gradually as the population of finer α′-martensite structures grows, demonstrating a direct relationship between the processing parameters, the resulting martensitic microstructure, and the final mechanical hardness of the material.

caption: Optical image of an as-printed Diamond TPMS architecture fabricated via SLM using dual-coated Dia/Cu composite powder.
summary: Shown here is an optical image of a Diamond TPMS structure. The successful fabrication of this complex geometry using SLM-processed dual-coated Dia/Cu composite powder confirms the formability of the material system for architected structures, highlighting the versatility of the manufacturing process in producing diverse triply periodic minimal surface architectures.

caption: Microstructure of NiTi sample-B in the XY plane at a height of 3000 μm, showing the final steady-state grain distribution.
summary: This panel depicts the microstructure of NiTi sample-B in the XY plane at a height of 3000 μm. Similar to the structures at 1800 μm and 2400 μm, it features small non-red grains located randomly within a matrix of red grains, confirming the attainment of a steady-state microstructure after sufficient layer deposition.

caption: Polar plot quantifying cell alignment for 0% porosity constructs across 0, 50, and 250 mW·cm⁻² ultrasound conditions using a three-degree accumulation range.
summary: Polar plots quantify cell alignment for 0% porosity scaffolds under varying ultrasound intensities. By using a three-degree accumulation range to maintain accuracy and avoid overestimation, this quantitative analysis confirms the positive influence of ultrasound on cell alignment, providing a clear metric for comparing cellular responses across different stimulation levels.

caption: Photolysis-induced changes in the UV-Vis absorption spectra of O-16 upon exposure to 365 nm LED light in acetonitrile.
summary: The panel shows the steady-state photolysis of O-16 in acetonitrile. The absorption spectra track the cleavage process under 365 nm irradiation. Comparison with other oxime esters indicates that O-16 exhibits a lower photocleavage ability after 240 seconds compared to O-14, despite its higher molar extinction coefficient at 365 nm.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram for IN718 alloy, illustrating the transformation kinetics relative to the delta-phase and gamma-prime-phase solvus temperatures of 950 °C and 1050 °C, respectively.
summary: This TTT diagram for IN718 serves as a critical guide for heat treatment processes. By identifying the delta-phase and gamma-prime-phase solvus temperatures at 950 °C and 1050 °C, it enables precise control over alloy strength through the dissolution of intermetallic compounds and subsequent rapid cooling to immobilize precipitations.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curve displaying the normalized sample mass of activated carbon 3D structures as a function of temperature.
summary: This TGA curve illustrates the thermal degradation behavior of activated carbon 3D structures across the investigated temperature range. The data indicates that all tested samples exhibit a consistent trend of mass loss as temperature increases, confirming that the structures undergo progressive thermal degradation under the applied experimental conditions.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of alloy B-0 showing the distribution of 40 million atoms across the γ and γ′ phases following full heat treatment.
summary: This panel displays an atom probe tomography reconstruction of alloy B-0, containing approximately 40 million atoms. The visualization highlights the elemental distribution within the γ and γ′ phases after the material underwent a full heat treatment process, providing a representative view of the microstructure for subsequent partitioning analysis.

caption: Nb3p core-level XPS spectrum of 3DNP HEO after 14 h of heat treatment, corresponding to the Nb2O5 chemical valence state.
summary: This panel illustrates the Nb3p core-level XPS spectrum for the 3DNP HEO sample after 14 hours of heat treatment. The spectral features are consistent with the chemical valence state of Nb2O5, providing evidence for the oxidation state of niobium within the high-entropy oxide matrix.

caption: Total structure factor S(q) for Cu50Ag50 calculated via MD simulation, presented with a 0.5 x-axis offset.
summary: The total structure factor S(q) for the Cu50Ag50 alloy is presented based on MD simulation results. The curve is shifted by 0.5 on the x-axis to allow for clear visualization alongside other alloy compositions, reflecting the structural characteristics of the Cu-Ag system.

caption: Isofield magnetization versus temperature plots for the SPS sample, recorded during heating under fields from 0.1 to 2 T.
summary: The temperature dependence of magnetization for the SPS sample is shown across the magnetostructural transition. Data were collected on heating at a rate of 1.0 K/min under constant magnetic fields between 0.1 and 2 T, facilitating the determination of the isothermal entropy change through the Maxwell relation.

caption: Modulated nonlinear emission pattern showing triple focusing points forming an arrow pattern directed toward the left, optimized over 400 generations.
summary: Triple focusing points are arranged in an arrow pattern pointing to the left. This complex emission profile was generated using the genetic algorithm, requiring approximately 400 generations of evolution, which corresponds to an experimental time of about four hours.

caption: Dumbbell-shaped specimen undergoing a uniaxial tension test monitored by a GOM ARAMIS system.
summary: This photograph captures a dumbbell-shaped specimen during a uniaxial tension test. A GOM ARAMIS measuring system is utilized to monitor the mechanical response, specifically analyzing the initiation and growth of cracks within the material as the tensile load is applied to the specimen during the experimental procedure.

caption: SHAP summary plot demonstrating the impact of various input features on the joint shear capacity estimation using the AdaBoost algorithm.
summary: This SHAP summary graph for the AdaBoost model highlights the relative importance and effect of input variables on the joint shear capacity (Fmax). By displaying the distribution of SHAP values, the plot clarifies how specific features drive the model's predictions, revealing the sensitivity of the joint shear capacity to input variations.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting (001) compound twin laminates within the dark domain of the NiTi grain.
summary: This dark-field TEM image reveals the (001) compound twin laminates present within the dark domain of the NiTi grain. The visualization of these laminates is crucial for understanding the martensitic variant arrangement formed under 50 MPa stress, demonstrating the internal structural complexity of the transformed material.

caption: Nominal stress–strain response for Lat1 S configuration at 10% relative density, highlighting the mechanical differences between quasi-static and dynamic SHPB testing.
summary: Displayed is the nominal stress–strain response for the Lat1 S configuration at a 10% relative density. By comparing quasi-static curves with dynamic SHPB results from 3D analysis, the figure illustrates the effect of high strain rates on the mechanical properties of the material under the specified impact pressure conditions.

caption: Horizontal cross-section of LPBF-manufactured and peak-aged Al–Mn–Mg–Sc–Zr specimen produced with a 60 μm layer thickness.
summary: Horizontal cross-section of the 60 μm layer thickness specimen exhibits the characteristic laser scanning path pattern with a 67° rotation angle. This optical micrograph confirms that the scanning strategy remains consistent across different layer thicknesses during the LPBF manufacturing of the Al–Mn–Mg–Sc–Zr alloy.

caption: Overlay of 1H–13C HSQC HRMAS NMR spectra comparing F-BLK (blue) and F-CHES 1 (red) to demonstrate selective incorporation.
summary: This panel displays an overlay of 1H–13C HSQC HRMAS NMR spectra for F-BLK and F-CHES 1. The superimposed spectra provide evidence of selective CHES incorporation into the material. The carbon dimension is particularly effective at resolving overlapping hydrogen signals, confirming the successful chemical modification of the sample structure.

caption: Statistical analysis of twin thickness and twin boundary spacing across the depths shown in panels (a)–(d).
summary: This plot quantifies the gradient distribution of twin thickness and twin boundary spacing at different depths within the USGP6 sample. The data confirms an increase in both twin thickness and boundary spacing as the sectional depth increases, correlating with the microstructural observations made in the bright-field TEM images.

caption: Kissinger plot of ln(Tx^2/∅) versus 1000/Tx for alloys A1 through A7, used to determine the activation enthalpy (ΔH*) for the glass transition.
summary: This Arrhenius-style Kissinger plot displays the relationship between the heating rate and the glass transition temperature for seven amorphous alloy compositions. By plotting ln(Tx^2/∅) against the inverse of the transition temperature, the activation enthalpy (ΔH*) is derived, providing insight into the thermal stability and kinetic behavior of the metallic glasses.

caption: 13C-NMR spectrum (100.4 MHz, D2O) of the red seaweed extract, displaying signals in the carbonyl region attributed to proteins and identified sugar-related peaks.
summary: This 13C-NMR spectrum of the red seaweed extract exhibits signals in the carbonyl region, which are proposed to originate from proteins. While sugar-related peaks are identified, signals corresponding to pyruvylated carrageenan, such as the carboxyl at δ 175.1, acetal at δ 101.3, and methyl at δ 25.5/1.44, could not be significantly assigned.

caption: Fluorescence staining image of PA bacteria in Al0.8 HEA coating culture medium after 24 hours, showing a significant decrease in living bacteria.
summary: Fluorescence staining of the Al0.8 HEA coating culture medium reveals a substantial decrease in the population of living PA bacteria after 24 hours. This result highlights the antibacterial efficacy of the Al0.8 composition, which significantly limits bacterial viability compared to the 304ss blank group.

caption: Confusion matrix for the ensemble CNN1+CNN2+CNN3 quality monitoring model, comparing actual and predicted classification labels.
summary: The ensemble CNN1+CNN2+CNN3 model performance is summarized in this confusion matrix on the testing set. With actual labels on the y-axis and predicted labels on the x-axis, the matrix illustrates the classification accuracy of the full model combination, serving as a key metric for the quality monitoring analysis.

caption: LSCM micrograph of the dried green body after demolding from the PDMS mold.
summary: This LSCM micrograph depicts the dried green body following its removal from the PDMS mold. Roughness measurements on the flat horizontal areas reveal a surface roughness of 0.3 µm, indicating a significant increase compared to the original brass stamp, which exhibited a much lower roughness value of 0.06 µm.

caption: Yield strain (εyield) variation relative to the true relative density of the in-filled compression specimens.
summary: The yield strain (εyield) is plotted against the true relative density for the in-filled samples. This panel demonstrates how the strain at which yielding occurs changes with density, showing that mechanical properties generally improve in comparison to as-built samples as the relative density of the in-filled structures increases.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) profiles for the CM alloy specimen under various experimental testing conditions.
summary: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profiles for the CM alloy are displayed, highlighting the specific gas desorption behavior observed under different testing conditions. These curves allow for a comparative analysis of the CM alloy's thermal response, providing essential insights into the material's degassing characteristics when subjected to varied experimental parameters during the TDS analysis.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the combined influence of cutting speed (V c) and feedrate (f) on the maximum notch height wear (VB N).
summary: This contour plot visualizes the interaction between cutting speed and feedrate regarding their impact on notch height wear. It serves as part of a broader analysis to identify how specific machining parameters influence tool degradation, providing a graphical representation of the wear behavior under varying operational conditions for the studied material.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots measured at 1000 Hz for Cr-rich inner films formed on four distinct Cr-advanced steels exposed to CO2-saturated NaCl solutions at 25 °C.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots at 1000 Hz characterize the Cr-rich inner films on four Cr-advanced steels in CO2-saturated NaCl solutions. This frequency is selected to isolate the space charge region capacitance from the Helmholtz layer. These plots provide the linear slopes necessary to calculate the donor and acceptor densities of the semiconductor films.

caption: Strength versus ductility Ashby plot focusing on solid-state additive manufacturing processes, specifically binder jetting, metal extrusion, and the current study's Inconel 625 samples.
summary: Solid-state additive manufacturing processes are evaluated here, with the current study's Inconel 625 samples positioned at the leading edge of the strength-ductility trade-off curve. Additive-friction stir processing of Inconel 625 achieves superior strength through fine-grained microstructures and the effective breakdown of coarse intermetallics compared to other solid-state techniques.

caption: Live/Dead fluorescence staining of hMSCs cultured on HA-GA, HA-GA.Gel, and HA-GA.μCol hydrogels over 1, 4, and 7 days, with green indicating viable cells and red indicating dead cells.
summary: Live/Dead staining images demonstrate the viability of hMSCs seeded on three different hydrogel formulations over a 7-day culture period. Green fluorescence highlights viable cells, while red fluorescence identifies dead cells, providing a visual assessment of cell survival and biocompatibility across the HA-GA, HA-GA.Gel, and HA-GA.μCol hydrogel surfaces.

caption: Galvanostatic discharge profile of a 30 µm thick metallic Al foil electrode at room temperature, showing a two-stage lithiation process with a moderate current of 180 µA for β-LiAl formation and an extra low current of 9 µA for Li-rich phase formation.
summary: The galvanostatic discharge profile of a 30 µm Al foil electrode demonstrates a two-stage lithiation process. A moderate current of 180 µA facilitates rapid β-LiAl formation, while a subsequent low current of 9 µA enables the formation of Li-rich phases, resulting in a noisy plateau near 0 V vs. Li/Li+.

caption: Correlation plot for the Mean Squared Error (MSE) metric, highlighting the performance variance of LR, SVR, RF, and MLP models.
summary: This panel shows the correlation plot for the MSE metric. The MSE values for the LR, SVR, RF, and MLP models are 5.7 × 10-6, 6.25 × 10-6, 1.16.7 × 10-5, and 9 × 10-8 respectively, demonstrating the varying degrees of predictive accuracy achieved by these distinct machine learning architectures.

caption: Schematic representation of the extraction process for CT-derived geometric imperfections to inform finite element (FE) models with distributed mass.
summary: This schematic illustrates the methodology for extracting CT image data to implement realistic strut defects into finite element models. By incorporating a statistical distribution of these geometric imperfections, the models can predict the compressive Young's modulus and strength of lattice structures with approximately 10% accuracy, demonstrating the impact of manufacturing-induced structural variations.

caption: Box plot distribution of hardness values measured across various L-PBF scan strategies.
summary: Hardness values are presented as a box plot distribution for different L-PBF scan strategies. Statistical analysis reveals that these values remain relatively consistent across the tested strategies, showing no significant variation. Furthermore, there is no direct correlation between these hardness measurements and the performance of the material's passive layer.

caption: Normalized sheet resistance R/R0 of the SLS/CNT23 composite on substrate A plotted against 30 cycles of sandpaper abrasion.
summary: This plot illustrates the normalized sheet resistance R/R0 of the SLS/CNT23 composite on substrate A during 30 cycles of sandpaper abrasion. Experimental results indicate a linear, mild increase in the resistance value as the number of cycles progresses, despite the accumulation of surface defects and coating discontinuities throughout the test.

caption: ADF-STEM micrograph of the specimen deformed to 5% plastic strain at 900 °C, highlighting the coexistence of dislocation pairs (red arrows) and Orowan loops (green arrows).
summary: This ADF-STEM image captures the microstructure of a specimen subjected to 5% plastic strain at 900 °C. The visualization reveals the presence of both dislocation pairs, indicated by red arrows, and Orowan loops, marked by green arrows, demonstrating the active deformation mechanisms occurring at this lower strain level.

caption: Magnetic field dependence of magnetization for the 8Co sample, showing hysteresis loops acquired at temperatures ranging from 4.2 to 280 K under pulsed field conditions.
summary: The 8Co sample shows characteristic M-H hysteresis loops measured under pulsed magnetic fields between 4.2 and 280 K. By calculating the area of these loops, the energy dissipation (E dis) is derived, allowing for an assessment of how the magnetic properties and energy loss evolve with temperature for this specific composition.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot illustrating feature importance for the pH = 4.5 classification model, highlighting the red channel as the most influential feature.
summary: This SHAP beeswarm plot visualizes the feature importance for the pH = 4.5 classification model. Analysis reveals that the red channel exerts the largest effect on the model's prediction for this specific class, serving as the primary driver for identifying samples within this pH category.

caption: Fluorescence micrographs showing DAPI-stained nuclei of SAOS-2 osteoblast-like cells attached to Ti- and Zr-based surfaces after 2 hours of incubation.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images reveal the initial attachment of SAOS-2 osteoblast-like cells on Ti- and Zr-based surfaces after a 2-hour incubation period. DAPI-stained nuclei are visualized to assess cell adhesion patterns, demonstrating that cell attachment on these test surfaces follows a distinct, surface-dependent distribution as observed via 10x objective lens magnification.

caption: Temperature-dependent IR emission spectra of the Tm3+-doped sensor immersed in 2-propanol, measured between 22.8 and 49.4 °C under 700 nm excitation.
summary: The IR luminescence spectra of the sensor in 2-propanol were recorded from 22.8 to 49.4 °C under 700 nm excitation. The emission intensity at 1436 nm decreases as the temperature rises, while the emission at 1626 nm shows a corresponding increase, demonstrating the temperature-sensing capability of the Tm3+ ions.

caption: Volume loss of C56 alloy after a 6-hour Miller test using quartz powder abrasive medium, highlighting the highest removal for the 1.00 mass-% Al alloy.
summary: Volume removal results for C56 alloy subjected to a 6-hour Miller test with quartz powder are shown. The alloy system containing 1.00 mass-% Al exhibits the greatest volume loss. Overall, corundum abrasive causes significantly higher material removal than quartz powder due to its superior Mohs hardness and abrasivity.

caption: Surface analysis energy-dispersive X-ray spectra identifying the presence of Cu, Ni, Si, and Zr elements across the sample surface.
summary: Surface analysis via energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirms the elemental composition of the Cu-3.2Ni-0.7Si-0.05Zr alloy. The spectra clearly resolve the peaks corresponding to copper, nickel, silicon, and zirconium, providing a comprehensive overview of the chemical constituents present on the analyzed surface area of the material.

caption: Average yield strength and ultimate tensile strength values for various processing sets, including AB, SB, SVP, LSP, TF, CP, ECP, and T6 variants.
summary: Average yield and ultimate tensile strength values are plotted for multiple specimen sets, covering a wide range of processing conditions such as AB, SB, SVP, LSP, TF, CP, ECP, and T6. This bar chart provides a comparative overview of the strength improvements achieved through different surface and heat treatments.

caption: Summary of mechanical data extracted from tensile tests for PA1012 parts, quantifying the performance variations resulting from different PF concentrations.
summary: This table presents the mechanical data derived from tensile testing of PA1012 parts. It serves as a quantitative summary of the mechanical properties, allowing for a direct comparison of performance metrics across different PF contents to evaluate the impact of powder composition on the final mechanical integrity.

caption: M2P implementation showing peak and valley identification, fitting circles, reference lines, and tangents.
summary: This panel details the M2P implementation, where peaks and valleys are automatically identified and classified for each track. The visualization includes fitting circles, a substrate reference line, and tangents at intersection points. These features are essential for determining track width and characterizing the geometry based on the layer growth direction.

caption: Time to reach 1% creep strain for CMSX-4 Nickel superalloy under various constant stress and temperature conditions for loading along the 〈001〉 crystallographic direction.
summary: This panel presents creep performance data for the CMSX-4 superalloy, showing the time required to reach 1% creep strain under different stress and temperature regimes. These creep characteristics are essential for understanding the strain softening effects and slower creep deformation that occur during steady-state high-temperature engine operation.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results presented as a Nyquist plot, accompanied by an equivalent circuit schematic used for data fitting.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results are displayed alongside an equivalent circuit model. This circuit schematic is utilized to fit the experimental data obtained from the impedance measurements, providing a quantitative representation of the electrochemical behavior and interface characteristics of the passivation film under investigation in the study.

caption: Surface roughness parameter Sa for Ti and Zr surfaces, presented as median values with interquartile ranges.
summary: Surface roughness analysis using the Sa parameter indicates that sandblasting increases roughness compared to machined controls for both titanium and ceramic-based materials. The box plot displays the median and interquartile range for these samples, highlighting the impact of different surface treatments on the microscale topography of the materials.

caption: Summary table detailing the phase constitution observed in the Ti–5Cr base alloys and the Ti–6.0Bi binary alloy.
summary: The phase constitution of each alloy is systematically summarized in this table. It provides a clear overview of the phases present in the Ti–5Cr base alloys and the Ti–6.0Bi binary alloy, facilitating a direct comparison of the phase stability and composition across the entire set of materials studied.

caption: Bifurcation diagram illustrating equilibrium solutions with varying numbers of water belts, truncated at six belts, featuring a jagged branch structure.
summary: This bifurcation diagram displays a complex, jagged branch structure representing various equilibrium solutions for climate states. The diagram is truncated at six water belts, illustrating the mathematical complexity of finding these states. It serves as the primary reference for identifying specific equilibrium points analyzed in the subsequent inset temperature profiles.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of intergranular austenite in HT100-300 sample, where significant instability growth covers the allotriomorph, marked by red and yellow arrows.
summary: This EBSD IPF map shows intergranular austenite in the HT100-300 sample. Significant instability-induced protrusion growth is observed, covering almost the entire allotriomorph. This growth occurs despite minimal allotriomorph development, highlighting how tuning AM parameters significantly alters the transformation pathways and interface morphologies during the post-AM thermal treatment process.

caption: Non-isothermal dilatometric measurement curve for the homogenized sample.
summary: This panel displays the non-isothermal dilatometric measurement performed on the homogenized sample. The curve provides essential thermal expansion or contraction data, serving as a baseline for understanding the material's dimensional stability under varying temperature conditions before further processing or isothermal testing is conducted.

caption: Charge-discharge polarization curves comparing flat and indented metallic bipolar plate VRFB cells at a current density of 75 mA/cm2 and a convection velocity of 8 mm/s.
summary: This panel displays the fourth charge-discharge cycle polarization curves for flat and indented bipolar plate configurations at 75 mA/cm2. The data illustrates the electrochemical performance of the cells under identical electrolyte circulation velocities of 8 mm/s, serving as a baseline for evaluating the impact of plate geometry on battery capacity.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the natural logarithm of relaxation time (ln τ) versus the inverse of absolute temperature (1000/T) used to determine the activation energy and vitrification temperature.
summary: The relaxation times derived from the stress relaxation curves are plotted as ln(τ) versus 1000/T. The slope of this linear fit allows for the calculation of the activation energy (Ea) for the thermal process. Using this relationship, the vitrification temperature (Tv) for the vitrimer network was determined to be 71 °C.

caption: LC-MS profiles illustrating the chemical degradation products generated during the PS removal process.
summary: The LC-MS profiles presented in this panel identify the specific chemical degradation products resulting from the PS removal process. These mass spectrometry results provide insight into the transformation pathways and the nature of the breakdown products formed during the experimental treatment of the nanoplastics.

caption: Micro- and nano-XCT analysis of WE43-PEO1 scaffolds, showing (i) a minimum projection of 15 consecutive node slices revealing lack-of-fusion defects at strut intersections, (ii) a nano-XCT cross-section highlighting gas pores and irregular pores at oxide-matrix interfaces, and (iii) a 3D segmented reconstruction of oxide and precipitate distributions.
summary: WE43-PEO1 scaffolds exhibit significant structural defects, primarily lack-of-fusion at lattice nodes and irregular pores at oxide-matrix interfaces. Nano-XCT cross-sections and 3D reconstructions reveal the spatial distribution of these defects and secondary phases. Gas pores ranging from 15 to 50 micrometers are also identified within the Mg matrix.

caption: Case 3 presenting the final optimized structural geometry after the boundary smoothing post-processing step.
summary: Case 3 presents the final optimized structural geometry obtained after the boundary smoothing post-processing step. Consistent with the reference, this technique is utilized to improve the structural representation. The resulting image confirms that the adaptive mesh optimal structures are effectively processed to achieve smooth and accurate geometric boundaries.

caption: Spectral deconvolution of the R1 powder sample, highlighting the chemical bonding states of titanium oxides relative to the 458.6 eV reference.
summary: Spectral deconvolution for the R1 powder sample is illustrated, using the TiO2 2p 3/2 peak at 458.6 eV as the reference binding energy. The analysis identifies primary and secondary peaks corresponding to TiO2, with a tertiary peak assigned to metallic Ti, characterizing the chemical bonding state of the titanium oxides.

caption: Bode magnitude plots comparing impedance values of laser-annealed samples against as-printed L0, showing enhanced corrosion resistance due to thickened surface oxide films.
summary: Bode magnitude plots compare the impedance values of laser-annealed samples to as-printed L0 samples. In the low-frequency region, the laser-annealed samples show higher impedance values, which is attributed to a thickened surface oxide film induced by the laser treatment, thereby effectively enhancing the overall corrosion resistance of the material.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-built AE81 alloy at the bottom region, depicting the crystallographic orientation of the equiaxed grains.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the bottom region of the as-built AE81 alloy shows the orientation of the equiaxed grains. EBSD analysis indicates that the microstructure is consistent with the top and middle regions, with an average grain size measured at 51.11 ± 1.28 μm.

caption: Optical micrograph of the combined shot-blasted and chemically etched (SB + CE) sample showing the martensitic microstructure and modified edge profile.
summary: The combined shot-blasted and chemically etched (SB + CE) sample maintains a martensitic microstructure. The optical micrograph highlights the edge profile, where the reduction of surface valleys is observed. This improvement is critical as it minimizes stress concentration points that could otherwise promote crack initiation and premature tensile failure.

caption: Binary Ni-Al phase diagram illustrating the stability regions of intermetallic phases including NiAl3, Ni2Al3, NiAl, Ni3Al, and the non-equilibrium Ni5Al3 phase.
summary: The Ni-Al binary phase diagram displays the thermodynamic stability of various intermetallic compounds. It identifies four stable phases, NiAl3, Ni2Al3, NiAl, and Ni3Al, alongside a non-equilibrium Ni5Al3 phase. Among these, NiAl exhibits the highest stability, maintaining its structural integrity across a wide temperature range up to 1638 ℃.

caption: High-precision electronic balance employed for accurate mass measurements during the water absorption testing procedure.
summary: A high-precision electronic balance is shown as a key component of the testing equipment. This instrument is essential for obtaining accurate mass measurements of ceramic specimens before and after water immersion, ensuring the reliability of the water absorption data collected during the experimental evaluation process described in the study.

caption: Merged fluorescence micrograph of HGF cells cultured in indirect contact with various 3D printing resins, showing the overlay of F-actin filaments and nuclei.
summary: This merged fluorescence micrograph displays HGF cells after 24 hours of indirect contact with 3D printing resin extracts. The image combines F-actin filament staining and nuclear labeling to visualize overall cell morphology. Observations indicate that the HGF monolayer maintains a minimally altered morphology despite exposure to the resin extracts.

caption: Mott–Schottky plots representing the inverse square of capacitance versus potential for passive films on CrFeCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi coatings.
summary: This figure displays Mott–Schottky plots for passive films formed on CrFeCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi coatings. The measurements were conducted at 0 V Ref for 1 hour in a 0.5 mol/L H2SO4 solution. These plots are essential for characterizing the semiconducting properties of the passive films formed on these specific alloy coatings.

caption: RF inverse model assessment displaying parity plots with 1:1 line alignment and violin plots showing predicted concentration distributions.
summary: The RF model demonstrates improved predictive performance, as evidenced by parity plots showing closer alignment with the 1:1 reference line. Additionally, the violin plots highlight that the distributions of predicted concentrations more closely mirror the true experimental values across all six inks compared to the PLS model.

caption: Horizontal shift factors log(αT) as a function of temperature for neat PETG and its binary and ternary composites, demonstrating a successful fit to the Williams–Landel–Ferry (WLF) equation.
summary: The horizontal shift factors log(αT) are plotted against temperature for neat PETG and its various binary and ternary composites. The data points are well-fitted by the Williams–Landel–Ferry (WLF) equation, confirming the validity of the time–temperature superposition approach used to characterize the molecular dynamics and viscoelastic behavior of these reinforced polymer systems.

caption: Length measurements of as-printed S1 and S2 samples obtained via vernier callipers prior to substrate separation, showing deviations from design values.
summary: Length measurements for as-printed S1 and S2 samples, obtained using vernier callipers before wire-cut separation, are presented with error bars representing three replicates. The data reveals that both samples exceed intended design lengths, with S1 showing a deviation of less than 0.1% and S2 less than 0.04%, indicating S2 is more accurate.

caption: Effect of total monomer concentration on the properties of IEC gels, highlighting the range between 20.0 and 40.0 wt%.
summary: This plot illustrates the influence of total monomer concentration on IEC gels. Maintaining concentrations between 20.0 and 40.0 wt% is essential for ensuring sufficient electrostatic cross-linking sites and achieving cationic hyperbranched polymers with appropriate molecular weights, which are critical for the structural integrity and performance of the resulting gel materials.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of polycrystalline Alloy 600 oxidized at 350℃ for 1 minute, utilizing Bi+ primary ions and Cs+ sputtering.
summary: ToF-SIMS depth profiling of polycrystalline Alloy 600 oxidized at 350℃ for 1 minute reveals the initial surface composition. The analysis, conducted with Bi+ primary ions and Cs+ sputtering, provides critical data on the oxidation kinetics of the alloy during the early stages of the exposure process.

caption: Bode magnitude plots of the Ti-based metallic glass compositions, showing impedance values across a frequency range in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution at 37 °C.
summary: Bode magnitude plots display the impedance behavior of the Ti-based metallic glass compositions. The Pd5Pt5-bearing sample exhibits the lowest impedance modulus in the frequency range, reaching approximately 10 Ω cm2 at 100 kHz. This reduction in impedance corroborates the enhanced metal-electron interactions observed in the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements.

caption: K-space Ni K-edge EXAFS oscillations for Ni 0.001 Cu NPs, Ni 0.01 Cu NPs, and Ni foil standard, measured following an in-situ reduction treatment.
summary: K-space Ni K-edge EXAFS oscillations are displayed for Ni 0.001 Cu NPs, Ni 0.01 Cu NPs, and a Ni foil standard. The data were acquired after the samples underwent an in-situ reduction process using 4% H2 balanced in He at 350 °C for 1 hour to ensure consistent surface states.

caption: Surviving vacancies resulting from a 50 keV classical MD cascade in NiFe, visualized within a 196 Å cubic volume.
summary: Surviving vacancies from a 50 keV classical MD cascade in NiFe are shown within a 196 Å cubic volume. This snapshot illustrates the spatial distribution of vacancy-type defects, which serves as a reference point for evaluating the reduction in vacancy clustering observed in the 2T-MD simulation model.

caption: Performance evaluation radar chart summarizing the multi-faceted mechanical and structural characteristics of the BBLS lattice.
summary: The radar chart provides a comprehensive overview of the BBLS lattice performance across multiple evaluation metrics. By visualizing these diverse parameters simultaneously, the chart facilitates an overall assessment of the structure's capabilities, confirming the effectiveness of the BBLS design through a multi-dimensional performance comparison.

caption: 3D scatter plot of the first three principal components showing clear separation between resin-only samples and those containing 0.025%, 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1% graphene nanoplatelets, confirming distinct material compositions.
summary: A 3D scatter plot of the first three principal components derived from PCA demonstrates the successful discrimination between 3D-printed samples with varying graphene nanoplatelet concentrations. The plot shows distinct clustering for resin-only samples and those with 0.025%, 0.1%, 0.5%, and 1% GNP, confirming that material composition is effectively distinguishable.

caption: Weak-beam dark-field TEM image revealing widely dissociated Shockley partial dislocations in the 1473 K quenched specimen.
summary: Captured via weak-beam dark-field TEM, this image highlights the presence of widely dissociated dislocations within the 1473 K quenched specimen. These structural features are consistent with those found in the annealed specimen, demonstrating that the degree of short-range order does not significantly alter the dislocation dissociation behavior after deformation.

caption: Hydrogen TDS-GU spectra for a 5 μg/g LECO calibration pin under varying atmospheric exposure conditions, including as-received, re-tested without exposure, and re-tested after 1 minute or 7 hours of air exposure.
summary: Hydrogen TDS-GU spectra for a 5 μg/g LECO calibration pin are shown for four conditions: as-received, re-tested without atmospheric exposure, and re-tested after 1 minute or 7 hours of air exposure. The as-received sample exhibits a distinct shoulder near 340 °C, while subsequent measurements show only marginal increases in hydrogen signal.

caption: Capacitance response of G slab-based sensors embedded in a bicycle helmet during side loading conditions.
summary: This panel illustrates the sensor performance of G slab-based capacitors within a bicycle helmet subjected to side loading. Experimental results show that sensors located on both sides of the helmet exhibit heightened capacitance readings, reflecting the device's ability to detect mechanical stress applied to the lateral helmet regions.

caption: Nyquist plot of LDS-Ni immersed in 3.5% NaCl solution, highlighting a larger impedance arc radius compared to other samples after 3 days.
summary: The Nyquist plot for LDS-Ni immersed in 3.5% NaCl solution demonstrates its electrochemical impedance characteristics. Notably, the LDS-Ni sample exhibits a larger impedance arc radius than both the LDS-Cr and LDS-BM samples after 3 days of immersion, suggesting superior corrosion resistance properties compared to the other tested materials.

caption: Optical micrograph of the internal channel surface for specimen C2 following 20 minutes of electropolishing.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the internal channel surface of specimen C2 after 20 minutes of electropolishing. The visualization illustrates the surface quality resulting from the electropolishing process, which is influenced by complex factors such as the specific channel curvature and the distribution of conductive reaction products during the treatment.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module, demonstrating the impact of different environmental insolation and temperature settings as predicted by the PEC1 model.
summary: The P-V characteristics shown here illustrate the power output of the mSi0188 solar module across diverse temperature and irradiance levels. Using the PEC1 model, the graph compares rescaled power data against experimental values, highlighting the module's operational behavior in environments that simulate actual field conditions.

caption: X-Y cross-sectional tomography view of the Honeycomb strategy sample between layer 4 and layer 5.
summary: This X-Y cross-sectional tomography view between the fourth and fifth layers of the Honeycomb strategy sample provides a detailed look at the internal void distribution. Positioned 145-152 μm above the substrate, this section serves to illustrate the specific pore formation characteristics associated with the Honeycomb deposition strategy.

caption: EDS compositional map of the transverse fracture surface of the API heat-treated vertical CMT-WAAM specimen.
summary: This EDS map characterizes the elemental distribution on the fracture surface of the API heat-treated specimen. The analysis focuses on identifying precipitates within the fracture surface to understand the material's behavior under this specific heat treatment condition, providing a comparative view of the compositional variations across the different processing states.

caption: Structural model showing a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell based on the Zeolite ID 9590293 unit cell.
summary: Represented here is a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell configuration built from the Zeolite ID 9590293 unit cell. This visualization is part of a systematic modeling framework, utilizing VESTA software to expand the unit cell into a supercell, highlighting the structural complexity of the specific zeolite framework.

caption: Summary table of error factors associated with the DV2 model, detailing the standard deviation of the normal distribution for each factor with a mean set to zero.
summary: This table presents the various error factors inherent in the DV2 model, which indicate that achieving an end altitude of 0 km is an optimistic projection. Each factor is characterized by a normal distribution with a mean of zero and a defined standard deviation, providing a quantitative assessment of model uncertainty.

caption: Misorientation angle distribution histogram for the quasi-recrystallized (RX) state, detailing the frequency of grain boundary angles.
summary: This histogram presents the misorientation angle distribution for the quasi-recrystallized state. By comparing the frequency of LAGBs to the recovered state, it confirms a lower density of subgrain boundaries, providing a clear quantitative signature of the quasi-recrystallized microstructure observed in the laser-rescanned sample.

caption: IPF map overlaid with IQ map for the α-phase in the TCH sample, revealing grain morphology perpendicular to the build direction.
summary: This EBSD map of the α-phase in the TCH sample shows that while β grains are primarily equiaxed, some elongated grains are oriented perpendicular to the build direction. The IQ overlay provides structural context, confirming the presence of these elongated features within the highlighted section of the grip area.

caption: Temperature versus composition section for the Cu-Ni-Pb system, starting at a Cu:Ni ratio of 0.2 and extending to 1 at% Pb, featuring superimposed EPMA experimental data points.
summary: This temperature-composition section illustrates the phase equilibrium of the Cu-Ni-Pb system with up to 1 at% Pb. Experimental EPMA measurements are plotted against calculated thermodynamic parameters. Two data points marked with tails were excluded from the optimization process due to high scattering, highlighting preferential lead dissolution in solid copper-nickel.

caption: Optimized topology and fiber orientation for an MBB beam with discontinuous fibers.
summary: The MBB beam is depicted here with discontinuous fiber reinforcement. Red lines indicate the orientation of these fibers, showing how the optimization algorithm distributes discontinuous segments to achieve the desired structural topology, providing a comparison to continuous fiber designs in terms of load-bearing efficiency and material distribution.

caption: STEM-BFI image of CR35 showing B19′ nanodomains, with an inset SADP indicating the [111] B2 zone axis and the 1-11 B19′ diffraction spot used for dark-field imaging.
summary: STEM-BFI imaging of the CR35 sample reveals the presence of nanometer-sized B19′ domains within the austenite matrix. The corresponding SADP inset confirms a [111] B2 zone axis orientation, while the marked 1-11 B19′ diffraction spot serves as the basis for subsequent dark-field analysis of these nanodomains.

caption: XPS depth profile of the mechanically polished specimen surface following 2 minutes of oxidation at 250 °C in high-temperature deionized water.
summary: Representing the surface chemistry of a mechanically polished specimen, this XPS depth profile tracks elemental distribution after 2 minutes of oxidation at 250 °C. The data highlights how mechanical polishing influences the oxidation behavior and surface composition of the material when exposed to high-temperature deionized water environments.

caption: Uniaxial fatigue hysteresis loops for IN718 specimens during cycles characterized by maximum cyclic hardening.
summary: This panel displays uniaxial fatigue hysteresis loops obtained from IN718 experiments. The curves represent the specific cycles where the material exhibits maximum cyclic hardening. These loops illustrate the stress-strain response of the alloy under fatigue loading conditions, providing a baseline for analyzing the cyclic deformation behavior of the material.

caption: Room temperature photoluminescence emission spectra of SCC-1, SCC-2, and SCC-3 samples showing characteristic peaks at approximately 464.4 nm.
summary: The room temperature photoluminescence spectra for SCC-1, SCC-2, and SCC-3 samples are presented in panel a. These measurements reveal that all three composite samples exhibit similar emission signals centered at approximately 464.4 nm, indicating consistent optical properties across the different material variations synthesized for this study.

caption: Stress exponent n values for superalloys plotted against temperature, incorporating data from this study and literature sources [7, 27].
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the stress exponent n for various superalloys across a range of temperatures. Vertical and horizontal bars represent the scatter in n values and the specific temperature ranges investigated, respectively. A dashed line highlights the observed trend of decreasing stress exponent values as the temperature increases.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of rBMSCs on porous alloy scaffolds after 7 days of coculture, demonstrating complete surface coverage.
summary: By the 7-day mark, fluorescence microscopy shows that rBMSCs have proliferated extensively and covered the entire surface of the porous alloy scaffolds. This indicates successful long-term cell growth and colonization, with the cells forming a dense layer across the scaffold architecture, confirming excellent biocompatibility and support for cell expansion.

caption: Azimuthal intensity profile of the {200} lattice plane across the uniaxial to biaxial strain path change.
summary: The {200} lattice plane intensity is plotted against the azimuthal angle from 0° to 90° during the discontinuous loading process. This visualization tracks the development of specific crystallographic orientations as the material undergoes uniaxial deformation followed by a transition to biaxial strain, highlighting the resulting texture evolution.

caption: STEM bright-field image showing high-density twin structures within the FIB-prepared sample.
summary: This STEM bright-field image provides a clear visualization of the microstructure within the FIB-prepared sample. The analysis reveals the presence of high-density twins, which are characteristic of the material's internal structure and serve as the foundation for further investigation into the dislocation morphology and twin network characteristics observed in subsequent panels.

caption: Raman spectroscopy data for EOGO, highlighting the D and G bands used to calculate the intensity ratio.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of EOGO reveals a D to G band intensity ratio of approximately 0.26. This low ratio demonstrates that the basal plane of the EOGO maintains a relatively intact sp2 lattice structure with a low population of defects.

caption: Comparison of the volume fraction and average diameter of the γ′ phase across different casting and heat treatment conditions.
summary: This plot quantifies the volume fraction and average diameter of the γ′ phase under various casting and heat treatment conditions. It provides a comparative analysis that illustrates the trend of decreasing phase size and volume fraction as the heat treatment temperature increases, summarizing the overall impact of thermal processing.

caption: Beam finite element model developed in MATLAB, derived by projecting the shell model onto the sagittal plane to define specific contact nodes.
summary: The beam model, constructed in MATLAB, is created by projecting the shell model onto the sagittal plane. This projection defines specific nodes, including node-top, node-H, and node-F, which serve the same functional purpose as the node-top and the heel and forefoot contact partition lines utilized in the shell model.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of sample 900 post-deformation, utilizing (100) superlattice reflections to highlight the distribution of γ′ precipitates.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph of sample 900, captured after 3–4% plastic deformation, utilizes (100) superlattice reflections to visualize the γ′ precipitates. The image provides a clear identification of the precipitate morphology and distribution within the Ni-based superalloy matrix, serving as a basis for analyzing the interaction between dislocations and precipitates.

caption: Logistic regression model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: Logistic regression model performance is evaluated using a confusion matrix. This visualization displays the classification accuracy and error distribution for the algorithm after the training process, providing a clear representation of how well the model predicts the target classes based on the provided dataset.

caption: Detailed mapping of element distribution across grain boundary regions in FGH4097.
summary: The elemental distribution map highlights the chemical composition at the grain boundaries of the FGH4097 superalloy. By visualizing the spatial arrangement of specific elements, this panel helps clarify the chemical environment at the boundaries, supporting the analysis of how these elements influence grain boundary migration and pinning.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of PPI-SL thin films, illustrating the electrochemical response of the material in the absence of P3HT chain growth.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms of PPI-SL thin films are presented to characterize the electrochemical behavior of the material. These measurements provide essential data on the redox properties of the PPI-SL branches, serving as a baseline for comparison with the P3HT-modified samples to evaluate the impact of chain growth on electrochemical performance.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the 2Cr13 substrate and Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings.
summary: The potentiodynamic polarization curves of the 2Cr13 substrate and the Ti-containing coatings are shown in Fig. 11 a. These Tafel curves illustrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the substrate compared to the various Ti-based coatings, providing a comparative assessment of their respective corrosion resistance properties under the tested conditions.

caption: Dilatometry curve of a debinded sample illustrating dimensional changes during heating.
summary: Dilatometry performed on the debinded sample demonstrates the material's structural response to heat. The curve reveals a first significant shrinkage event occurring around 1000 °C, which is subsequently followed by a plateau, indicating the stabilization of the sample dimensions after the initial thermal contraction phase.

caption: Thermal evolution of lattice parameters for Ti-Nb alloys, illustrating the structural stability and response of the α″ phase.
summary: The temperature dependence of lattice parameters for the α″ Ti-Nb alloy is depicted, highlighting the structural response to thermal changes. These simulation results confirm that the ADP accurately reproduces the experimentally observed changes in the α″ lattice with varying temperature, providing a reliable representation of the alloy's thermal behavior.

caption: HFDB tool geometry featuring a convex surface design integrated with a spiral pattern.
summary: The HFDB tool design is presented, highlighting its specific geometric features. The tool is characterized by a convex surface profile that incorporates a distinct spiral pattern, which is essential for the hybrid friction diffusion bonding process described in the previous panel.

caption: Immunofluorescence micrographs of co-culture μvessels showing CD31 (red), γ-H2AX (blue), and Phalloidin (green) staining, highlighting the distribution of senescence markers in ECs under different transfection conditions.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging of the co-culture μvessels reveals the spatial distribution of CD31, γ-H2AX, and Phalloidin. Downregulation of Piezo1 in VSMCs within these vessels exposed to simulated microgravity resulted in a significant decrease in the number of γ-H2AX-positive staining cells in the ECs, indicating reduced cellular senescence.

caption: TG-DTG curves comparing P50B15 samples before and after solvent debinding, highlighting weight loss peaks at 250 °C, 360 °C, and 450 °C.
summary: This panel displays the TG-DTG curves for P50B15 before and after water debinding. Three distinct weight loss peaks are observed at approximately 250 °C, 360 °C, and 450 °C, which correspond to the thermal pyrolysis of PVB, PEG, and HDPE components, respectively, providing insight into the material's thermal degradation behavior.

caption: Comparison of total measured current density versus dissolution current density calculated from XRF data for Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb and Ni-18Cr-3Mo-20Fe-5Nb alloys.
summary: This graph compares the total current density with the dissolution current density derived from XRF data. The total current density for Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb is lower than that of Ni-18Cr-3Mo-20Fe-5Nb following passivity breakdown. For the former alloy, similar dissolution rates during potential cycling indicate efficient repassivation and lack of irreversible propagation.

caption: D-peak position relative to the diamond peak at 1332 cm-1 plotted against total pressure, highlighting the convergence toward the diamond line at high pressures.
summary: The D-peak position is plotted against total pressure to track structural changes in the carbon fibres. Observations indicate that at the highest pressures, the D-peak position approaches the diamond line at 1332 cm-1, suggesting a transition toward a diamond-like structural state under extreme compression conditions.

caption: Estimated dislocation cell size plotted against normalized enthalpy, derived from process-specific B and n values for various materials.
summary: Dislocation cell sizes are estimated using process-specific parameters and normalized enthalpy values. The plot demonstrates how varying LPBF process conditions influence the resulting cell dimensions across different alloy systems, highlighting the relationship between thermal input and the characteristic length scales of the dislocation structures formed during solidification.

caption: Resistance repeatability plot under saturated humidity conditions, highlighting transient noise attributed to droplet dynamics.
summary: The resistance repeatability plot shows the sensor's performance under saturated humidity. Despite experiencing transient noise characterized by ±1.5% resistance fluctuations due to rapid droplet condensation and evaporation, the sensor successfully maintains its original resistance response performance, confirming its robustness in high-humidity environments despite the observed dynamic interference.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) curve for Fe-based BMGs, demonstrating the relationship between cooling rates and phase stability during LPBF processing.
summary: The continuous cooling transformation curve for Fe-based bulk metallic glasses illustrates the thermal requirements for glass formation. Notably, the cooling rate achieved during the LPBF process is substantially higher than the critical cooling rate required for Fe-based BMGs, ensuring the retention of the amorphous structure during rapid solidification.

caption: Longitudinal profile of the race track area on an Ag target following the sputtering process, illustrating the erosion geometry.
summary: This confocal microscopy image displays the longitudinal profile of the race track region on an Ag target after sputtering. The analysis reveals a smooth, uniform erosion profile characterized by an average groove depth of 202.1 μm and a width of 9.5 μm, with no evidence of macroscopic cracks or pits.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the 60CRA condition illustrating lamellar/cellular L12 phase morphology formed via discontinuous precipitation in finer recrystallized grains, accompanied by the [011] FCC zone axis diffraction pattern inset.
summary: The dark-field TEM image of the 60CRA condition shows the lamellar/cellular L12 phase morphology characteristic of discontinuous precipitation in finer recrystallized grains. The inset diffraction pattern, taken from the [011] FCC zone axis, confirms the phase identification using the {001} superlattice reflection to highlight the lamellar structure.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for ER120S-G solid wire under Group C conditions.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation kinetics for ER120S-G deposited metal within the Group C experimental parameters. Developed to analyze the influence of solid-state phase transformation temperatures and resulting phase fractions on residual stress, this diagram provides critical data for understanding the microstructural evolution in WAAM-processed components.

caption: CCT diagram simulation for a steel specimen with a 1000 μm grain size at a 900 °C peak temperature.
summary: This CCT diagram simulation illustrates the predicted phase transformation behavior for a steel specimen with a 1000 μm grain size at a 900 °C peak temperature. Numerical modeling using JMatPro software incorporates specific grain size inputs to predict microstructural evolution, with red arrows marking reference cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction patterns obtained from the deformation twins presented in panel (b).
summary: This SAED pattern corresponds to the deformation twins shown in panel (b). The diffraction data provides crystallographic evidence of the twin structures, confirming their orientation and structural characteristics within the maximum strain sample, consistent with the observed thickening of the deformed atomic layers under high stress.

caption: Elevated temperature elongation performance of VIC-fabricated LW 4280 relative to Rene 80, MAR-M-247, and IN 738.
summary: Figure 13b illustrates the superior elongation of LW 4280 at elevated temperatures when compared to conventional Ni-superalloys Rene 80, MAR-M-247, and IN 738, all of which were fabricated using the vacuum investment casting (VIC) process. The data highlights the improved ductility characteristics of the LW 4280 alloy in this comparison.

caption: Elemental distribution map of sample number 4, illustrating the spatial variation of element concentrations through color intensity gradients.
summary: This elemental distribution map of sample number 4 visualizes the spatial concentration of elements, where higher color intensity corresponds to a greater percentage of the element. The analysis highlights the presence of a Nb-rich Laves phase dispersed within the ϒ matrix, confirming the microstructural composition of the material.

caption: 3D PCA scores plot illustrating the distribution of ABS, PLA, and PETG raw filaments and printed samples across PC1, PC2, and PC3 axes.
summary: This 3D PCA scores plot demonstrates that ATR-FTIR spectroscopy effectively distinguishes between different polymer groups, including PLA, ABS, and PETG. The analysis successfully identifies specific polymer sub-groups, such as PLA-Flex, which occupy distinct regions within the principal component space, confirming the capability of the method to classify various printed and raw materials.

caption: Diffusion trajectory of a single H atom near the NGI at 900 K over 5.0 ns.
summary: This trajectory plot shows the H atom displacement near the NGI at 900 K. The path is constructed from vectors between atomic positions at 10.0 ps intervals. The solute H exhibits long dwelling behavior, suggesting it is trapped by the NGI and potentially bonded to a surface C atom.

caption: Microstructure of Ta 30 alloy after aging at 1173 K for 168 h.
summary: Observed is the microstructure of the Ta 30 alloy following 168 hours of aging at 1173 K. This panel illustrates the structural response of the alloy to elevated temperature aging, contributing to the broader study of phase emergence and microstructural changes in Ta-modified alloys after extended thermal exposure.

caption: Pentagon diagram detailing the CPDP parameters of the 6-hour mechano-synthesized Al86Cr12Ni2 alloy system, tested within a 3.5% NaCl electrolyte.
summary: The pentagon diagram displays the CPDP parameters for the Al86Cr12Ni2 alloy system after 6 hours of mechanical synthesis, evaluated in a 3.5% NaCl electrolyte. This visualization captures key electrochemical metrics such as Ecorr, icorr, and pitting potential, allowing for an assessment of the alloy's corrosion resistance in a chloride-containing environment.

caption: Higher-magnification optical micrograph of the vertical cross-section of 316L stainless steel.
summary: This higher-magnification optical micrograph provides a detailed view of the 316L stainless steel vertical cross-section. It serves as a reference for the matrix microstructure, allowing for a clearer assessment of the grain morphology and the absence of interfacial defects when compared to the SiC-reinforced MMCs shown in subsequent panels.

caption: Reduction cyclic voltammogram of the 3-bisPh-B compound.
summary: This panel displays the reduction cyclic voltammogram for the compound 3-bisPh-B. The electrochemical behavior is characterized by measuring current response during the reduction process. This data, along with oxidation measurements, provides essential information regarding the redox potentials of the derivative, which are further summarized in the paper's Table 2.

caption: Pole figure of the reconstructed β phase in the Sub-transus state at 920℃, showing a maximum MUD value of 8.3, reflecting a weaker texture.
summary: This pole figure for the reconstructed prior β grains exhibits a maximum MUD value of 8.3. This value accounts for the weaker texture observed in the reconstructed β phase within the Sub-transus state, providing quantitative evidence of the reduced crystallographic alignment compared to the HIP state.

caption: Isothermal section of the Sn-rich region of the Sn-Cu-Ni ternary alloy system at 260 °C, featuring dissolution contact lines for Ni-50Cu and Ni-60Cu alloys represented by red dotted lines.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the Sn-rich region of the Sn-Cu-Ni alloy system at 260 °C. The plot highlights specific dissolution contact lines for Ni-50Cu and Ni-60Cu alloys, indicated by red dotted lines, which are critical for understanding the growth behavior of the (Cu,Ni)6Sn5 phase relative to Cu concentration.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the fifth row of a 10%_15% specimen, featuring a local relative density of 14.5%.
summary: Captured from the fifth row of the 10%_15% specimen, this SEM image reveals a local relative density of 14.5%. In contrast to lower density samples, the EBM 3D printer fails to accurately reproduce the octagonal geometry of the TAOR cell as the volume fraction increases, indicating significant manufacturing limitations.

caption: Schematic representation of the multi-material laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) process used to fabricate NiTi/AlSi12 bimetallic structures.
summary: This schematic illustrates the multi-material L-PBF fabrication process for creating NiTi/AlSi12 bimetallic structures. It provides a conceptual overview of the additive manufacturing approach used to integrate these distinct materials, highlighting the structural configuration achieved through the L-PBF technique as described in the research methodology for producing bimetallic components.

caption: Mott-Schottky curves for laser powder bed fusion produced Ti–6Al–4V (LTC4) after potentiostatic polarization at potentials ranging from 0.6 V to 1.0 V.
summary: Mott-Schottky curves for LTC4 exhibit positive slopes between -0.8 V and -0.4 V, confirming n-type semiconductive behavior in the passive film. These measurements were performed following potentiostatic polarization at various potentials, providing essential data for calculating the semiconductive properties of the passive film formed on the laser-produced alloy.

caption: Raman spectra of brazed diamond specimens utilizing a crystalline filler alloy with varying Nd concentrations.
summary: Raman spectra of brazed diamond specimens utilizing a crystalline filler alloy with varying Nd concentrations are presented. This analysis was performed to investigate the graphite transition on the diamond surface following the brazing process. The spectra provide insights into the structural changes occurring at the diamond-filler interface for crystalline alloys.

caption: C 1s XPS spectrum of the as-printed 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode, featuring an asymmetric peak at 284.5 eV attributed to graphitic carbon.
summary: The C 1s XPS spectrum for the as-printed 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode displays an asymmetric peak at 284.5 eV. This specific peak is assigned to the X-ray photoelectron emission of graphitic carbon within the composite material, providing insight into the surface composition of the as-printed electrode before any cleaning process.

caption: Raman spectra of solar salt observed during heating from 450 °C to 575 °C.
summary: Raman spectra of solar salt were recorded from 25 °C to 700 °C. Panel (c) presents the Raman spectral data for the solar salt sample as it undergoes heating between 450 °C and 575 °C, highlighting the material's spectroscopic response at these elevated temperatures.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for Ni-3d and O-2p orbitals in the ground state ferromagnetic (FM) ordering, showing strong hybridization near the Fermi level and an inset detailing Ni-atom magnetization.
summary: Partial density of states analysis for the Ni-3d and O-2p orbitals reveals a half-metallic solution for the trilinear coupled structure with FM ordering. Strong hybridization between Ni-3d and O-2p states is observed near the Fermi level, while the inset provides specific data on the orientation and magnitude of Ni-atom magnetization.

caption: Fluorescence micrographs of rBMSCs seeded on Control, 3-G, and 4-G scaffolds after 1 and 3 days of culture, illustrating cell distribution and viability.
summary: Representative fluorescence micrographs of rBMSCs-seeded scaffolds are displayed for the Control, 3-G, and 4-G groups at 1 and 3 days of culture. These images provide a visual assessment of cell viability and distribution across the different scaffold types, serving as the basis for subsequent quantitative analysis of cell health.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Cu-Ni system, highlighting the Cu-30Ni composition with a blue arrow.
summary: This binary phase diagram illustrates the complete solid-state solubility of copper and nickel across all compositions. The Cu-30Ni alloy, indicated by a blue arrow, is characterized by its equilibrium cooling behavior, where no significant precipitation occurs during casting due to the continuous solid solution nature of the Cu-Ni system.

caption: Long-term chronopotentiometric stability evaluation of the AgNiCu/g-C3N4 electrocatalyst performed over a 100-hour period at a higher current density of 100 mA cm-2.
summary: A 100-hour chronopotentiometric test was performed to determine the stability of the AgNiCu/g-C3N4 electrocatalyst at a current density of 100 mA cm-2. This extended duration test demonstrates the material's robust electrochemical behavior and sustained catalytic activity when subjected to significantly higher current density requirements over an extended operational timeframe.

caption: Voltage signals recorded by strain gauges mounted on the incident and transmitted bars during the Split-Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) test.
summary: This panel displays the raw voltage data captured by strain gauges on the incident and transmitted bars during a Split-Hopkinson Pressure Bar test. These measurements serve as the primary input for calculating the mechanical response of the specimen throughout the high-strain-rate impact duration.

caption: Ni-rich section of the binary Ni-Ce phase diagram, illustrating the equilibrium phase boundaries with specific alloy compositions indicated by vertical dotted lines.
summary: This figure displays the Ni-rich region of the binary Ni-Ce phase diagram. It serves as a reference for the thermodynamic stability of the system, with vertical dotted lines explicitly marking the specific compositions of the alloys prepared for the study, facilitating the correlation between phase equilibria and experimental alloy design.

caption: Creep-rupture performance of CF8C-Plus alloy represented as applied stress versus rupture time across multiple test temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep-rupture behavior of CF8C-Plus alloy by mapping applied stress against rupture time for various test temperatures. Analysis of these results reveals no consistent heat-to-heat variation in creep life across the tested temperature range, indicating stable performance characteristics for the material under the specified creep conditions.

caption: Weight change curves for AM, AM-HR, CM, and AM-CG IN 625 alloys exposed to air at 900 °C for up to 300 hours.
summary: This line graph compares the oxidation kinetics of various IN 625 alloy conditions at 900 °C. The data demonstrates that the AM-CG condition, characterized by gigantic grains, exhibits significantly lower oxidation kinetics compared to the as-built AM, hot-rolled AM-HR, and conventionally manufactured CM samples over a 300-hour exposure period.

caption: Concentration distribution across the Cu-0.15Ag/Cu-16.59Ni-1.70Ag diffusion couple annealed at 1223K for 96h, highlighting the fit between experimental data and simulated mobility models.
summary: This panel illustrates the concentration profile for the Cu-0.15Ag/Cu-16.59Ni-1.70Ag diffusion couple annealed at 1223K for 96h. By comparing experimental data with NI and MK method simulations, the figure validates the effectiveness of the current atomic mobility models in predicting diffusion kinetics within this specific alloy composition and experimental condition.

caption: Long-term stability test of NiCo-CNTs-30 showing current density and H2O2 accumulation over 24 hours at 0.1 V vs. RHE, with inset images showing electrolyte color changes.
summary: A 24-hour durability test was performed on the NiCo-CNTs-30 electrode in 0.1 M KOH at 0.1 V vs. RHE. The plot tracks the current density and cumulative H2O2 concentration over time, while inset photographs confirm the temporal variation of the electrolyte color, demonstrating the electrode's sustained catalytic performance.

caption: Orientation distribution diagram comparing the crystallographic textures of statistically deformed primary grains and newly formed DRX grains.
summary: This orientation distribution diagram contrasts the textures of primary deformed grains and DRX grains. It highlights the differences in crystallographic alignment between the two populations, offering insights into the texture evolution and the influence of dynamic recrystallization on the overall material orientation at 950 °C.

caption: Tabulated list of LPBF process parameters utilized for the fabrication of the experimental specimens.
summary: This panel presents the specific Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) process parameters applied during the manufacturing of the study's specimens. These parameters serve as the foundational settings for the subsequent printing of the cylindrical bars, ensuring consistency across the experimental conditions described in the research methodology.

caption: Measured coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) for A- through E-X unit cell structures compared against their respective simulation results, represented by dashed lines in matching colors.
summary: This plot displays the measured CTE values for various X-unit cell structures, A through E, alongside their corresponding simulation predictions shown as dashed lines. The data illustrates the thermal expansion behavior of these structures, highlighting discrepancies between experimental measurements and simulated results regarding the intensity and occurrence of CTE jumps.

caption: Array of 3 × 3 × 3 unit cells, each maintaining a uniform wall thickness while exhibiting different β-parameter values to show periodic structural arrangement.
summary: This panel presents a 3 × 3 × 3 array of unit cells configured to demonstrate periodic structural arrangement. Each unit cell within the array maintains the same wall thickness, while the β-values are varied to illustrate the impact of parameter modulation on the overall porous lattice structure.

caption: Evolution of the traction coefficient over time during a twin-disc test conducted at a 2.00 % longitudinal creepage, illustrating the performance across four distinct experimental stages.
summary: This plot displays the traction coefficient measured during a twin-disc test performed at 2.00 % longitudinal creepage. The data captures the tribological response across four sequential experimental stages, providing a comprehensive overview of the traction behavior throughout the entire duration of the creepage test under these specific loading conditions.

caption: Intermediate stage of the arc shape demonstrating the progression of the cathode spot climbing phenomenon along the cathode wire.
summary: Panel (b) illustrates the intermediate progression of the cathode spot climbing phenomenon. As the arc interacts with the cathode wire under pure argon shielding, the arc root continues to shift away from the wire end, providing visual evidence of the climbing behavior observed during the experimental analysis of the arc.

caption: Three-dimensional surface topography scan of the MJF printed sample obtained via Keyence VHX6000 light microscopy.
summary: This 3D scan illustrates the surface topography of an MJF printed sample following abrasive blasting with glass spheres. The visualization, captured via Keyence VHX6000 light microscopy, highlights the well-developed and rough surface morphology characteristic of these prints, which is essential for facilitating durable adhesive joints and ensuring effective mechanical adhesion.

caption: Combined analysis of spheroidization rate, flowability, yield percentage, and productivity for Ni-11.1Si-3Cr powder, identifying optimal processing windows.
summary: This comparative analysis identifies the ideal processing window for Ni-11.1Si-3Cr powder, balancing yield, spheroidization, and flowability. The optimal configuration at 12 kW plasma power and 14 g/min feed rate provides a high-quality powder, while increased power settings further enhance productivity without compromising key physical properties like yield and flowability.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for AM-CM hybrid NdFeB/SmFeN PA12 magnets, illustrating the performance shift between random as-printed samples and post-aligned samples at 300 K.
summary: The hysteresis loops for hybrid NdFeB/SmFeN PA12 magnets are shown, highlighting the transition from random particle orientation in the as-printed condition to an aligned state. Post-printing magnetic alignment improves the magnetic performance, yielding a remanence of 8.5 kG, an intrinsic coercivity of 11.05 kOe, and a maximum energy product of 116.18 kJ/m3.

caption: Neutron diffraction pattern of the C20 sample at 300 K, displaying measured data points, full spectrum fitting, and residual difference profiles.
summary: Neutron diffraction analysis performed at 300 K characterizes the crystal structure and phase distribution of the C20 sample after cycling. The plot displays the measured diffraction pattern alongside a full spectrum fit and the standard difference profile, providing quantitative insight into the post-cycling structural state of the alloy.

caption: Three-stage synthesis workflow for 3D printed BR-AC-DETA and BR-GO-DETA composites, illustrating adsorbent preparation, 3D template design and printing, and subsequent post-treatment.
summary: This schematic outlines the continuous three-step synthetic protocol developed for producing hierarchical amino-functionalized graphene oxide and activated carbon photopolymer composites. The process integrates adsorbent preparation, 3D template design and printing, and a final post-treatment stage, specifically engineered to create high-performance materials for efficient diclofenac adsorption applications.

caption: Structural phase transition of Cu-5at%Ni alloy during tensile deformation, illustrating the transformation of the FCC lattice into BCC, HCP, and other novel phases.
summary: Cu-5at%Ni alloy exhibits a structural phase transition when subjected to tensile deformation. The stretching process induces a conversion of the alloy's FCC structure into BCC, HCP, and other novel phase structures.
