This indicates that the addition of 5at% Ni does not prevent the stress-induced phase transformation observed in pure copper.

caption: OER stability test of the GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 catalyst evaluated using the cyclic voltammetry (CV) method.
summary: The OER stability of the GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 catalyst is assessed using the cyclic voltammetry (CV) method. This durability test evaluates the long-term performance and structural integrity of the catalyst material when subjected to repeated electrochemical cycling in an aqueous solution, confirming its potential for practical applications.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing an η particle adjacent to a C14 Laves phase precipitate containing multiple sets of planar faults, with basal planes aligned at the interface.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the structural relationship between an η particle and an adjacent C14 Laves phase precipitate. The micrograph highlights the presence of multiple sets of planar faults within the Laves phase, demonstrating that the basal planes of both phases are joined at the interface.

caption: High-resolution Cr 2p XPS spectrum of the passivation film, featuring deconvoluted peaks for metallic Cr (571.58 eV, 581.48 eV), Cr2O3 (577.38 eV, 585.98 eV), and Cr(OH)3 (573.38 eV, 591.08 eV).
summary: Analysis of the Cr 2p high-resolution XPS spectrum demonstrates the presence of multiple chromium species in the passivation film. The spectrum includes peaks corresponding to metallic Cr at 571.58 eV and 581.48 eV, Cr2O3 at 577.38 eV and 585.98 eV, and Cr(OH)3 at 573.38 eV and 591.08 eV.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the cladding layers displaying relatively straight, sparse dislocation structures compared to the HAZ.
summary: Bright-field STEM imaging of the cladding layers reveals a distinct dislocation configuration characterized by relatively straight and less numerous dislocations. This structural state contrasts sharply with the dense tangles observed in the primary HAZ, indicating a lower degree of dislocation accumulation within the printed cladding material.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot illustrating the distribution and impact of feature values on model predictions across the sample set.
summary: The SHAP beeswarm plot provides a nuanced visualization of how individual feature values influence model predictions across the entire dataset. By displaying the distribution of SHAP values, it reveals the specific impact of geometric variations on the predicted outcomes for each sample within the analyzed print quality dataset.

caption: Nyquist plots and the corresponding equivalent circuit model used for fitting electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the alloy samples.
summary: Nyquist plots display the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for both as-built and T4 heat-treated alloy samples in Hanks' solution. The data, fitted using an equivalent circuit model, reveal that both alloy conditions exhibit two distinct capacitive arcs, providing insight into the corrosion resistance characteristics of the material under these specific conditions.

caption: Comparison of H2O absorbance ranges showing the primary 1513–1503 cm−1 window and an alternative 3573–3563 cm−1 range used to avoid spectral overlap with H2S evolution.
summary: This FTIR spectrum illustrates an adjustment strategy for H2O absorbance measurements. By shifting the analysis from the 1513–1503 cm−1 range to the 3573–3563 cm−1 range, researchers can effectively build a calibration curve while avoiding significant peak overlap with H2S evolution, ensuring more accurate quantification of water vapor in the presence of other gases.

caption: Comprehensive research framework illustrating the systematic methodology and logical progression of the study.
summary: This schematic provides a comprehensive research framework that outlines the systematic methodology and logical progression of the study. It serves as a visual guide to the overall research process, ensuring that the experimental and analytical steps are clearly defined and structured for the investigation presented in the paper.

caption: Image quality (IQ) map of the AFMAR-10-13C alloy after undergoing sintering followed by austenitization at 1000 °C and water quenching.
summary: This panel presents an image quality map of the AFMAR-10-13C alloy after it has been sintered, austenitized at 1000 °C, and water quenched. This processing step is intended to achieve higher cooling rates, allowing for a direct comparison of microstructural changes relative to the as-sintered state shown in panel a.

caption: Optical micrograph and 3D topography of a single-track deposit produced at a carrier-gas flow rate of 14 L min-1, highlighting the track structure and surface topography.
summary: Representing the highest flow rate in the study, this panel shows the optical micrograph and 3D surface topography of a single-track deposit produced at 14 L min-1. The data illustrates the final track morphology, providing insight into how increased carrier-gas flow influences the deposition process and resulting surface profile.

caption: SRIM-calculated depth profiles for displacement damage (left axis) and atomic concentration (right axis) in a material subjected to 500 keV He ion irradiation at a fluence of 5 × 10^17 ions/cm^2, with the red box highlighting the damage peak region.
summary: Panel b illustrates the SRIM-calculated depth profile for displacement damage and He ion concentration resulting from 500 keV He irradiation. The calculated damage and concentration profiles are in good agreement with the SRIM predictions, with the red box clearly delineating the region where the damage peak occurs within the material.

caption: EBSD image of the L20 LPBF AlSi7Mg sample after heat treatment, viewed perpendicular to the build direction.
summary: Captured perpendicular to the build direction, this EBSD image of the L20 AlSi7Mg sample reveals an elongated and directional grain structure. Although columnar growth remains predominant, the formation of equiaxed grains is more pronounced here than in the parallel section, suggesting that successive layer thermal history influences grain growth.

caption: Predicted fatigue life N f versus laser power P, showing a positive effect on life below 250 W and a decrease at higher power levels.
summary: The relationship between laser power P and fatigue life N f is depicted, with black dashed lines indicating predictions outside the training database range. Results show that lower power levels, particularly below 250 W, enhance fatigue life, whereas higher power settings lead to a notable reduction in the fatigue performance of the material.

caption: Fluorescent imaging of NIH3T3 cells seeded on a CTFA sheet after one day of incubation.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy shows the morphology of NIH3T3 cells cultured on a CTFA sheet for one day. Consistent with the control, the cells on this surface are well-spread and flattened, displaying the typical morphology of adherent cells, indicating that the CTFA material supports normal cell attachment and growth.

caption: HAADF-TEM micrograph of the stir zone in the AM-PWHT specimen, highlighting the presence of MC carbides.
summary: This HAADF-TEM micrograph focuses on the stir zone of the AM-PWHT specimen. It specifically visualizes the presence of MC carbides within the microstructure. These carbides are distinct features observed in the stir zone, providing insight into the phase composition resulting from the post-weld heat treatment process.

caption: Isothermal section below 1473 K, showing the existence of two three-phase coexisting regions of γ + σ + P and γ + P + NiMo.
summary: Below 1473 K, the system exhibits two distinct three-phase coexisting regions. Specifically, the γ + σ + P region is located in the Cr-rich portion of the diagram, while the γ + P + NiMo region exists in the Cr-poor region, reflecting the final phase equilibrium states at lower temperatures.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the same specimen as in (a), illustrating the distribution of nano-sized γʹ precipitates near the grain boundary through chromium isocomposition surfaces.
summary: Visualized via chromium isocomposition surfaces, this reconstruction reveals the presence of nano-sized γʹ precipitates located in the vicinity of the grain boundary. This observation confirms the existence of these precipitates in the as-built microstructure, which were not detected in broader structural surveys, highlighting the sensitivity of the APT technique.

caption: Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) plot ranking the association degree between individual feature descriptors and the phase transition temperature.
summary: The GRA plot evaluates the association degree between feature descriptors and the phase transition temperature. By comparing this ranking with the PCC results, features with low association degrees are excluded from the final dataset. This ensures that only strongly correlated features are retained for training the predictive regression model.

caption: Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy of the Ni L-edge for Ni10/CeO2 and Ni8Co2/CeO2, showing the bulk (TFY) phase and the Ib/Ia intensity ratio.
summary: Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy of the Ni L-edge was conducted to explore the Ni electronic state in Ni10/CeO2 and Ni8Co2/CeO2 catalysts. The bulk (TFY) phase is shown, and a specific Ib/Ia ratio is provided to further analyze the electronic configuration and valence state of nickel within the bulk material.

caption: Equilibrium path and DIC-derived axial strain and out-of-plane displacement fields for specimen CS55 exhibiting local bulging.
summary: Specimen CS55 demonstrates a local bulging failure mode under axial loading. The figure displays the equilibrium path alongside DIC-captured axial strain and out-of-plane displacement fields at various load levels. These visualizations illustrate the development of localized deformation patterns as the specimen progresses toward failure during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Summary of mechanical properties including TYS, UTS, and total elongation for the MYZ alloy.
summary: Mechanical properties for the MYZ alloy are summarized, highlighting the influence of Y and Zn alloying elements. The data confirms that the formation of the 18R-LPSO phase contributes to a tensile yield strength of 98.8 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 160.6 MPa, and a total elongation of 2.6%.

caption: Initial yield surface plotted for the structure with a relative density (ρr) of 5.17%.
summary: This panel presents the initial yield surface for a material structure with a relative density of 5.17%. The yield envelope defines the boundary of elastic behavior, mapping the stress conditions that trigger initial yielding for this specific density, as determined by the experimental analysis of the structure.

caption: Density of states analysis for the pristine 3DGPC substrate.
summary: The density of states (DOS) analysis for the pristine 3DGPC substrate is shown. This electronic profile characterizes the material's intrinsic electronic properties, providing a reference point to evaluate the enhanced orbital overlap between N, C, and H atoms observed in the 3DGPC-PS system.

caption: Optical micrograph of the heat-treated AlTiVCr alloy demonstrating a stable single-phase structure.
summary: This optical micrograph depicts the central region of the heat-treated AlTiVCr alloy at x50 magnification. Consistent with the as-cast state, the heat-treated condition shows no evidence of secondary phase formation. The microstructure remains uniform, confirming that the heat treatment did not induce the precipitation of additional phases in this equiatomic alloy.

caption: Hardness depth profile measured via nanoindentation along the build direction, presented as a smoothed curve from the top surface to the bottom of the sample.
summary: Hardness values along the build direction are presented as a smoothed curve to reveal the overall profile shape. This nanoindentation data facilitates the estimation of affected zone depths within the sample cross-section. The profile illustrates the mechanical response variation from the top surface down to the bottom of the specimen.

caption: Creep life comparison for DD6 specimens, summarizing the total duration until failure for different FCH conditions.
summary: The results of the creep lifetimes for the DD6 specimens are presented in this panel. It provides a comparative overview of the creep life achieved by the different specimen groups, summarizing the total time to failure under the experimental conditions tested in the study.

caption: Side view of the Tetraspline (TS) unit cell showing the vertical profile.
summary: This panel displays the side view of the Tetraspline (TS) unit cell. The visualization illustrates the vertical profile of the structure, providing essential information regarding the spatial orientation and geometric characteristics of the unit cell as defined in the figure caption and the broader context of the TS structure.

caption: Contour map showing the residual stress distribution across the welded joint following the ultrasonic impact treatment process.
summary: Post-treatment residual stress distribution is visualized here, demonstrating the effectiveness of the ultrasonic impact treatment. The proliferation of dislocations during this process releases maximum residual stress in the weld metal and heat-affected zone, with the reduction effect being significantly more pronounced in the weld metal region.

caption: Minimal surface geometry enclosed within a pentagonal prism featuring tunnels directed toward its faces (F).
summary: The minimal surface shown is constrained within a pentagonal prism geometry. This specific configuration incorporates tunnels oriented toward the faces of the prism, demonstrating the boundary method for surface construction. It represents a foundational building block for creating aperiodic structures based on the Tile(1,1) construction approach.

caption: Elemental distribution map of corrosion products on 3Cr steel after 6 h of immersion in CO2-saturated NaCl solution at 90 °C.
summary: This elemental distribution map illustrates the chemical composition of corrosion products formed on 3Cr steel surfaces. Following a 6-hour immersion in a CO2-saturated NaCl solution at 90 °C, EDS mapping was utilized to analyze the internal and external corrosion layers, providing insights into the material's degradation behavior under these specific conditions.

caption: Architecture of the neural network model designed for predicting the cladding layer height.
summary: This schematic illustrates the network architecture diagram for the cladding layer height prediction model. It provides a visual representation of the model's structure, detailing the flow and organization of the neural network components used to estimate the height of the cladding layer during the manufacturing process.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms illustrating the growth of PANOA type I from the 50th to the 200th scan.
summary: Presented here is the growth progression of PANOA type I during the subsequent 50 to 200 scans. Conducted in 0.2 M aniline, 0.01 M o-aminophenol, and 0.6 M H2SO4 at 60 mV/s, these cyclic voltammograms track the electrochemical evolution of the polymer film as the scan count increases.

caption: Vickers microhardness (HV1) values measured across different regions of the 25%Cr-9.5%Ni-3.8%Mo wall.
summary: This panel displays the Vickers microhardness (HV1) values for distinct regions within the 25%Cr-9.5%Ni-3.8%Mo wall. The measurements characterize the mechanical properties across the wall structure, reflecting the material's consistency resulting from the low heat input and 100 °C interpass temperature used during the fabrication process.

caption: Radar plot comparing tensile strength, Young's modulus, and elongation at break of the developed composites against various PLA biocomposites reported in scientific literature.
summary: Comparing tensile properties against similar systems from the literature, this radar plot demonstrates that the developed CH and AIL composites consistently outperform many other PLA composites reinforced with natural fibers or comparable fillers, despite showing lower mechanical properties than pure PLA in some specific testing categories.

caption: High-resolution N1s XPS spectrum of the CA/3D-MCC sample after lead adsorption.
summary: The N1s high-resolution XPS spectrum for the CA/3D-MCC sample is shown after the lead adsorption process. This data allows for the assessment of changes in nitrogen-based surface species, helping to determine if nitrogen functional groups contribute to the overall adsorption mechanism of Pb(II) onto the material surface.

caption: Optical micrograph showing the Vickers hardness indentation mark on the AlSi10Mg alloy surface processed under sub-optimal conditions (A: 300, B: 1000, C: 0.13).
summary: This optical micrograph displays the Vickers hardness indentation mark on an AlSi10Mg alloy specimen. The material was processed under sub-optimal conditions defined by parameters A: 300, B: 1000, and C: 0.13. The resulting impression allows for the calculation of the material's Vickers hardness by measuring the diagonal length of the indentation.

caption: Precipitation-Time-Temperature (PTT) graph for the delta phase, showing the progression from initial to final precipitation.
summary: The PTT graph for the delta phase maps the precipitation kinetics, specifically marking the initial and final precipitation stages. Constructed using X-ray intensity data, this diagram characterizes the temporal and thermal conditions required for phase formation, offering critical insights into the precipitation behavior of the delta phase within the alloy.

caption: Atomic model of a Ni3Al supercell featuring a single Al vacancy, with navy blue spheres highlighting Ni atoms near the vacancy and red spheres highlighting Al atoms near the vacancy.
summary: Depicted is a Ni3Al structure containing a single Al vacancy site. Analysis reveals that the presence of this vacancy causes nearby Ni atoms to gain fewer electrons compared to the pristine structure, resulting in a less negative charge state, which validates the charge parameters used in the ReaxFF calculations.

caption: Procedural flowchart illustrating the steps involved in the Voronoi tessellation algorithm used for generating porous structures.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic process for generating porous structures through the Voronoi tessellation algorithm. It serves as a visual guide for the computational methodology employed in the study, detailing the sequential steps required to construct the porous geometry as summarized in the provided research documentation.

caption: Defect recombination fraction versus radiation dose for binary and ternary alloys, highlighting the non-monotonous evolution of recombination efficiency.
summary: The instantaneous recombination fraction is plotted against radiation dose for various ternary alloys. The results demonstrate a highly non-monotonous evolution of the recombination fraction. Increasing the B-C binding energy leads to a significant improvement in the recombination fraction in the ternary alloy compared to the binary A-B system.

caption: Continuous emission spectrum of LHAM material, indicating ionization of the substance.
summary: Panel b presents the continuous emission spectrum of the LHAM material. The presence of a continuous spectrum across the measured wavelength range serves as evidence that the material has undergone ionization. This spectral profile is essential for understanding the ionization behavior of the substance during the experimental process.

caption: Particle configuration at 0.055 s illustrating the onset of gathering, where particle 1 moves toward particle 7, and particles 4, 5a, 6a, and 6b begin to aggregate.
summary: By 0.055 s, the simulation shows dynamic particle movement. Particle 1 migrates toward particle 7, while particle 6d approaches particle 1. Simultaneously, particles 4, 5a, 6a, and 6b initiate a gathering process, marking the transition from a scattered state to the formation of distinct particle clusters within the bed.

caption: Visible light transmission spectra and photographic images of 1 mm thick DEICE films prepared with varying CEA and HEA mass ratios.
summary: This panel presents the visible light transmission spectra and corresponding photographs of DEICE films. The data illustrates the optical properties of the material obtained under different monomer mass ratios, providing a visual and quantitative assessment of the film transparency for the various compositions tested in the study.

caption: Comparison of predicted and experimental ratcheting curves for AM SS316 at 900 and 1023 K, contrasting conditions with (ψ < 1.0) and without (ψ = 1.0) the influence of dynamic strain aging.
summary: Panel b displays the impact of DSA on ratcheting strain for AM SS316 at 900 K and 1023 K. The presence of DSA (ψ < 1.0) leads to a decline in hysteresis loop progress over loading cycles, resulting in significant reductions in ratcheting strain compared to the DSA-absent condition.

caption: Bode diagrams illustrating impedance magnitude and phase angle for samples from different build regions, demonstrating consistent electrochemical responses.
summary: Bode magnitude and phase angle plots provide additional evidence of electrochemical similarity among the MoldJet 316L samples. These diagrams show consistent impedance responses across the top, middle, and bottom build regions, confirming that the electrochemical behavior remains uniform regardless of the sample's specific position within the build volume.

caption: Dark field TEM image and SAED pattern inset of solution-treated Ti-9Mo-1Fe alloy, demonstrating a similar distribution and size of the ω phase as observed in other compositions.
summary: The dark field TEM image of the solution-treated Ti-9Mo-1Fe alloy displays the ω phase. Comparison with the Ti-8Mo-2Fe and Ti-10.5Mo-1Fe alloys confirms that the ω phase is present in all three alloys with a very similar distribution and size, consistent with the experimental conditions applied to all samples.

caption: Cluster map visualizing the distribution trends and dimensional variations of primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite classifications.
summary: The cluster map provides a visualization of how different martensite types are classified by the model. It highlights distribution trends and shows how specific feature dimensions vary across primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite categories, with tertiary martensite exhibiting a relatively concentrated size distribution in length and width.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and corresponding EDX elemental maps of the cellular structure in (Fe₂Ni₂CrMn)₉₀ + (Mo₃Cu₇)₁₀ sample L 67.
summary: Sample L 67 displays a cellular structure visualized through HAADF-STEM imaging and EDX elemental mapping. The dendrites in this sample are enriched in Fe and Cr, which aligns with the broader experimental findings for the (Fe₂Ni₂CrMn)₉₀ + (Mo₃Cu₇)₁₀ alloy system under varying laser processing parameters.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ single-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 600°C thermal treatment, showing broad defect-related emissions.
summary: Cathodoluminescence spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures treated at 600°C reveal significant defect-related emissions. These broad signals are most pronounced in this first cycle compared to subsequent thermal treatments. The data compares Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ dopants at 2.5 mol% and 0.35 mol% concentrations, highlighting the influence of dopant type on luminescence behavior.

caption: Schematic representation of the static bath-PEP experimental setup, illustrating the configuration where a specimen is fully submerged in a stationary electrolyte for the duration of the polishing process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the static PEP experimental setup, where a specimen is fully submerged in a stationary electrolyte. The diagram provides a clear visual representation of the process, highlighting the static nature of the bath during the polishing period, which is essential for understanding the experimental methodology described in the study.

caption: Chronopotentiometry stability curves for Ru3Ni3 NAs recorded at a constant current density of 5 mA cm-2 in acidic and alkaline electrolytes, showing excellent durability with minimal degradation over a 10-hour testing period.
summary: Chronopotentiometry curves demonstrate the durability of Ru3Ni3 NAs at a constant current density of 5 mA cm-2. Tested in 0.5 M H2SO4, 0.05 M H2SO4, 1 M KOH, and 0.1 M KOH, the material shows excellent stability with limited degradation after a 10-hour operation period across these different pH conditions.

caption: Formation of bubbles within the molten pool due to Gaussian-distributed powder voids and recoil force-induced keyholes.
summary: During laser processing of IN718, this panel depicts how voids within the Gaussian-distributed powder and keyholes generated by evaporation recoil forces lead to bubble formation. These bubbles are critical precursors to defect development within the molten pool during the laser-based additive manufacturing process.

caption: Fluence distribution profile for the Lissajous 3 scan pattern using frequency control, achieving a maximum fluence of 59 J/mm2.
summary: Depicting the Lissajous 3 scan pattern under frequency control, this heatmap highlights a maximum fluence of 59 J/mm2. The visualization allows for the assessment of energy concentration patterns inherent to this specific scan geometry when processed with constant frequency parameters during the laser welding operation.

caption: High-speed camera observation of the metal wire center shifting toward the molten metal edge, facilitated by heat treatment to enhance wetting, resulting in contact angles of 29° on the bead and 88° on the substrate.
summary: This panel highlights the movement of the metal wire center toward the molten metal edge, supported by heat treatment to improve wetting. The process achieves specific contact angles of approximately 29° relative to the metal bead and 88° relative to the substrate, confirming effective wetting enhancement.

caption: Anodic current density response of Fe–Cr-X alloys monitored for 1 hour at a constant potential of 0.600 V.
summary: This plot shows the anodic current density response for Fe–Cr-X alloys maintained at a constant potential of 0.600 V. The chronoamperometric data, monitored over a 1-hour period, captures the current transient results, characterizing the electrochemical performance of the alloys under these specific high-potential conditions.

caption: Histogram of k-factor measurements at 500 °C, showing a Gaussian-like distribution with a limited sample size.
summary: The k-factor distribution at 500 °C is presented here as a histogram. The data follows a Gaussian-like distribution, similar to most other temperatures. However, the analysis of this panel is constrained by a comparatively low sample size, which is a noted limitation for the figures in the second row.

caption: Tensile testing setup showing the mechanical apparatus used to perform the tensile test process.
summary: The tensile testing setup is presented in this photograph, highlighting the mechanical equipment utilized during the experimental procedure. This visual documentation confirms the configuration of the testing apparatus, which is essential for understanding the methodology employed to subject the specimen to controlled tensile loading conditions.

caption: Surface-roughness profile of Pt measured via contact-mode atomic-force microscopy, exhibiting a root-mean-square (RMS) surface roughness of 0.535 nm.
summary: Atomic-force microscopy in contact mode was utilized to characterize the surface topography of a Pt specimen. The resulting surface-roughness profile indicates a root-mean-square roughness value of 0.535 nm, providing a quantitative assessment of the surface finish for this metallic material within the specified measurement area.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of TAN04HA and TAN06HA coatings deposited on rod, gyroid, and dodethick architectures following the firing process.
summary: This figure presents the X-ray diffraction patterns for TAN04HA and TAN06HA coatings applied to rod, gyroid, and dodethick substrates after firing. These diffraction results characterize the phase composition of the various coatings, providing essential data on the structural state of the materials following the high-temperature processing stage.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots measured at 1000 Hz for SLMed 316L stainless steel samples treated with various solid solution processes in 0.5 mol/L H2SO4 solution at 25 °C.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots at 1000 Hz characterize the semiconductor properties of passive films on SLMed 316L stainless steel. These measurements, conducted in a 0.5 mol/L H2SO4 solution at 25 °C, reveal how different solid solution treatments influence the electronic behavior and corrosion resistance of the material's surface layer.

caption: Residual stress distribution contour map for a molded component fabricated with a scanning distance of 120 μm.
summary: Represented here is the residual stress distribution contour map for a component manufactured with a laser power of 340 W, a scanning speed of 1200 mm/s, and a scanning spacing of 120 μm. This visualization allows for the assessment of stress patterns generated by these specific laser processing parameters.

caption: Boxplots illustrating the distribution of room temperature impact energy (J) across all test conditions, with each condition represented by three replicates.
summary: Impact energy values for three replicates of each test group are displayed as boxplots to visualize data variation. These plots provide a statistical summary of the impact energy distribution, highlighting the spread and central tendency of the data for each experimental condition tested at room temperature.

caption: Computational representation of a phase-field resolution algorithm applied to a two-dimensional domain.
summary: This visualization illustrates the computational implementation of a phase-field resolution algorithm within a two-dimensional domain. The simulation demonstrates the spatial discretization and numerical approach used to model phase evolution, providing a clear representation of the algorithmic framework designed for tracking interface dynamics in complex material systems.

caption: Conceptual illustration depicting the methodology for measuring the maximum crack length (am) via scanning electron microscopy analysis of fracture surfaces.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental approach used to determine the maximum crack length (am) by examining fracture surfaces under SEM. By analyzing these surfaces, researchers can accurately identify and measure the critical crack dimensions necessary for subsequent mechanical analysis and correlation with applied stress levels in the tested specimens.

caption: Pyramidal flat geometry featuring a truncated apex for the sonotrode tip surface.
summary: Depicted here is the pyramidal flat surface structure of the sonotrode tip. Consistent with the overall dimensions and structural configurations presented in Fig. 1, this design utilizes a flattened pyramidal apex, which modifies the contact area and pressure distribution compared to the pointed version during the sonotrode operation.

caption: Cycling performance of the LiCoO2|PVDF/LLZTO-CPE|Li battery, showing discharge-specific capacity and Coulombic efficiency over time at 0.4 C and 25 °C.
summary: The cycling performance of the LiCoO2|PVDF/LLZTO-CPE|Li battery is evaluated at 0.4 C and 25 °C. This plot displays the discharge-specific capacity and Coulombic efficiency, providing a clear assessment of the battery's stability and capacity retention over repeated charge-discharge cycles under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Learning curve displaying RMSE evolution relative to training dataset size, comparing training (orange) and test (blue) data performance with error bars derived from 20 iterations.
summary: This learning curve shows the dependence of prediction performance on training set size. By iteratively increasing the training data in increments of 50 up to 1100 points, the model's RMSE is tracked for both training and test sets. The inclusion of error bars from 20 repeated iterations provides a measure of statistical reliability.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the cathodic and anodic branches of AB, T5, and T6 samples before machining.
summary: PDP curves reveal the electrochemical behavior of the alloy samples. The AB and T5 samples demonstrate a higher degree of linearity in their cathodic and anodic branches. In contrast, the T6 samples exhibit significant fluctuations in both regions, confirming a less stable electrochemical behavior compared to the other conditions.

caption: Compressive strength of cast and 3D printed samples after 28 days of curing, highlighting the performance of printed samples.
summary: Compressive strength after 28 days of curing shows that cast samples generally outperform printed ones. However, printed samples tested perpendicular to the printing path show significant improvement, with strength increasing by up to 55% for EBA-modified mixtures and 42% for CBA-modified mixtures compared to their initial states.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Ni0.95Ce0.05 alloy electrode in 0.05 M H2O2 and 2 M NaOH, showing the electrochemical behavior at scan rates between 5 and 1000 mV s-1.
summary: The Ni0.95Ce0.05 alloy electrode exhibits a distinct electrochemical profile in the specified electrolyte. Analysis of the reduction peak potential, Ep, reveals that the shift in potential is less pronounced compared to other tested materials, while current densities increase consistently with higher potential scan rates across the tested range.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded between -1 and 1 V at a 100 mVs⁻¹ scan rate for a biophotovoltaic device comparing inkjet-printed PEDOT:PSS on PET against an ITO-coated PET anode, both containing Synechocystis sp PCC 6803 cells at 30 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry analysis is presented for the biophotovoltaic device, comparing the electrochemical behavior of an inkjet-printed PEDOT:PSS film on PET with an ITO-coated PET anode. The measurements were conducted in the presence of Synechocystis sp PCC 6803 cells at 30 °C, using a scan rate of 100 mVs⁻¹ across a -1 to 1 V range.

caption: Top and side views of the optimized slab model for the (111) facet of the hexagonal Ni3In bulk phase.
summary: This panel displays the optimized atomic structure of the (111) facet of the hexagonal Ni3In bulk phase. The slab model, presented in both top and side views, serves as a representative structure for the ordered Ni3In phase used in subsequent DFT calculations regarding carbon adsorption energetics.

caption: Color-coded 3D reconstruction of a one euro coin surface comparing wide field (WF) and LF-OS-SIM imaging modes.
summary: This panel presents a side-by-side comparison of a one euro coin surface using wide field (WF) and LF-OS-SIM imaging modes. The color-coded 3D reconstruction demonstrates the visual differences between the two techniques, with a scale bar of 100 μm provided to indicate the spatial dimensions of the imaged sample area.

caption: Reflection loss (RL) curves for four typical L8 GMSs composed of all eight AMMs.
summary: This plot displays the RL curves for four representative L8 GMSs, each composed of all eight types of AMMs. These curves demonstrate the performance characteristics of the stacked configurations, confirming that the absorption peak frequency variations align with the observed trends in material gradient evolution.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetisation profiles for CoFeMn0.5Alx samples recorded under an applied magnetic field of 40 kA/m.
summary: These temperature-dependent magnetisation curves provide the necessary data to determine the Curie temperature of the CoFeMn0.5Alx samples. By measuring magnetisation across a range of temperatures at a low applied field of 40 kA/m, the thermal stability and magnetic transition points of the alloys are effectively characterized.

caption: Surface topography of a premolar tooth milled at 440 m using scCO2 + MQL coolant.
summary: Confocal microscopy displays the surface topography of a premolar tooth milled at 440 m with scCO2 + MQL coolant. The resulting surface finish exhibits lower and more stable arithmetical mean height values, confirming that this cooling approach offers enhanced control over surface topography compared to traditional emulsion coolant methods.

caption: EBSD phase map of the quasi-isothermally processed specimen at 6 mm height, revealing a network-like microstructure of fcc-Fe austenite seams surrounding bcc-Fe martensitic cell cores.
summary: This EBSD map illustrates the microstructural arrangement of the quasi-isothermally processed specimen at a height of 6 mm. The analysis confirms that the bright network-like seams consist of fcc-Fe austenite, which effectively encloses the bcc-Fe martensitic cell cores, demonstrating the phase distribution within the material's cellular structure.

caption: Optical photograph of fabricated Ni-P wires featuring various design widths ranging from 50 μm to 1000 μm.
summary: This photograph showcases a series of Ni-P wires fabricated with varying design widths. The range of widths, spanning from 50 μm to 1000 μm, demonstrates the capability of the electroless plating process to produce patterned metallic structures with controlled dimensions for potential micro-scale applications.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarisation curves for AISI 304 stainless steel in 3.5 wt% NaCl, showing a shift toward higher corrosion potentials and lower current densities following TPN treatment at 400 °C.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for AISI 304 demonstrate the electrochemical response in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Post-TPN treatment at 400 °C, the alloy exhibits improved corrosion resistance, evidenced by a shift in Ecorr to higher potentials and a reduction in Icorr, alongside a sharp current density increase above Epit.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for Mg, MgCa, and MgCaMn alloys in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution at 37 °C.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves provide insight into the corrosion kinetics of the magnesium alloys. These electrochemical measurements are essential for elucidating the mechanism behind the excellent corrosion resistance of the MgCaMn sample, highlighting differences in anodic and cathodic behavior compared to the Mg and MgCa control samples.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of chitosan (CS) and methacrylated chitosan (CSMA), showing characteristic peaks at 5.6 and 6.0 ppm for the modified polymer.
summary: Chemical modification of chitosan was characterized using 1H NMR spectroscopy. The spectra of CS and CSMA display new peaks at 5.6 ppm and 6.0 ppm for CSMA. These distinct signals indicate the successful methacrylation of chitosan, confirming the structural modification of the polymer backbone.

caption: False negative error instance demonstrating a failure to detect a target feature.
summary: This panel illustrates a false negative error, representing a specific failure mode in the predictive model where a target feature is missed. Such errors are critical for evaluating model performance, and their main causes and impacts are summarized in Table 7 to provide a comprehensive overview of system limitations.

caption: Summary table of magnetic characteristic parameters for MGS-1 and MGS-1C simulants, crushed LIS green body, and sintered samples processed in air or simulated Martian atmosphere at various temperatures.
summary: This table presents the magnetic characteristic parameters extracted from hysteresis curves measured at 300 K with an applied field of ± 1 T. It compares pristine MGS-1 and MGS-1C simulants, crushed LIS green bodies, and samples sintered under different atmospheric conditions and temperatures, specifically 1170°C and 1190°C in air or Martian atmosphere.

caption: Ammonium ion concentration distribution across a 3 × 3 array of 3D columnar structures.
summary: Ammonium ion concentration distribution across a 3 × 3 array of 3D columnar structures is illustrated. The simulation confirms that generated ammonium ions are primarily distributed in the liquid phase, maintaining this specific phase preference even when the columnar structures are arranged in a 3 × 3 array format.

caption: Representative load vs. depth curves for the three deposits, featuring a 10s dwell time during the loading stage.
summary: This panel displays typical load versus depth curves obtained from nanoindentation experiments conducted on three distinct deposits. Each curve incorporates a 10-second dwell time during the loading phase, providing a standardized mechanical response profile that allows for a direct comparison of the indentation behavior across the different sample types.

caption: Three-class classification confusion matrix highlighting the model's ability to identify good and damaged samples while noting difficulties with the intermediate minor damage category.
summary: The three-class confusion matrix evaluates the model's performance across distinct sample categories. While the model maintains robust identification of good and damaged samples, it exhibits significant challenges in accurately classifying the intermediate minor damage category, revealing specific limitations in the model's discriminative power for this particular classification task.

caption: Steady-state creep stage microstructure exhibiting increased dislocation density and mutual blocking within the γ channels.
summary: As the alloy reaches the second or steady-state creep stage, the dislocation density within the γ channels increases significantly. TEM observations show that these dislocations begin to block one another, indicating a transition in the deformation mechanism as the material accommodates the applied stress of 137 MPa at 1070 °C.

caption: Comparison of current-voltage (I-V) characteristics for patterned (P) and un-patterned (U) segments at 8 K under a 10 mT magnetic field applied perpendicular to the bridge, demonstrating pronounced asymmetry in the patterned region that mirrors upon field polarity reversal.
summary: This plot displays I-V curves for patterned and un-patterned segments at 8 K and 10 mT. The patterned segment exhibits significant asymmetry, which is mirror-reflected when the magnetic field polarity changes. In contrast, the un-patterned segment shows weaker asymmetry, likely due to the proximity of a voltage contact.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrating the relative mass loss of three distinct TPU-regolith composite samples as a function of temperature under a nitrogen atmosphere.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrate the relative mass loss of three distinct TPU-regolith composite samples as a function of temperature under a nitrogen atmosphere. The data indicates that all three composite variants begin to undergo pyrolysis when the temperature exceeds 250 °C, demonstrating the thermal degradation behavior of these materials.

caption: Effect of holding time on the room-temperature shear strength of joints with 0.3 at.% boron brazed at 1273 K.
summary: This graph shows the shear strength of joints containing 0.3 at.% boron as a function of holding time at a constant temperature of 1273 K. The data highlights the impact of processing duration on the mechanical strength of the joints, providing critical information for determining optimal brazing cycle times.

caption: Spearman’s rank correlation heatmap illustrating the relationship between alloying elements and microstructural phases in the as-built (AB) condition.
summary: This heatmap displays Spearman’s rank correlation coefficients for the as-built microstructure. Ni content shows a strong negative correlation with the detrimental Laves phase, indicating its role in suppressing phase formation. Conversely, Ni correlates positively with δ and σ phases, while Al displays an inverse relationship with these specific microstructural constituents.

caption: Out-of-plane displacement map of a flat C0 SHS specimen flange at failure load, showing traditional local buckling with symmetric inward and outward waves.
summary: This DIC strain map illustrates the out-of-plane displacement of a flat C0 SHS specimen at its failure load. The visualization reveals a traditional local buckling failure mode, characterized by inward and outward buckling waves occurring at adjacent faces at approximately the same height along the column length.

caption: H/Er and H3/Er2 ratios as a function of indentation depth for AM IN718 plasma nitrided at 650 °C.
summary: Depicted are the mechanical ratios for AM IN718 nitrided at 650 °C, showing an average H/Er of 0.0724 and H3/Er2 of 0.0759, suggesting a hard system prone to cracking. However, an H3/Er2 value of approximately 0.1 at depths between 170 and 190 nm indicates a localized crack-resistant sub-layer.

caption: Higher magnification SEM-FIB cross-sectional view of the sample aged for 0.5 h, highlighting fine-scale precipitate features.
summary: This higher magnification SEM-FIB image focuses on the sample aged for 0.5 h. It provides a detailed look at the fine-scale precipitates present in the early stages of aging, establishing the starting point for the observed increase in average precipitate size from approximately 140 nm to 350 nm over time.

caption: Evolution of the full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of the 311 diffraction peak as a function of gauge volume position, highlighting changes in dislocation density during the building process.
summary: Neutron diffraction measurements demonstrate the evolution of FWHM for the 311 peak, reflecting changes in dislocation density. A significant decrease in FWHM is observed following the construction of Z1, where the beam probes both Z1 and the AB region, with the AB region also shown at its initial position.

caption: High-magnification view of dendritic grains located at the top layer of the melt pool, showing growth perpendicular to the perimeter.
summary: High-magnification bright-field TEM imaging reveals the dendritic grain morphology at the top layer of the S1 melt pool. These grains exhibit growth perpendicular to the melt pool perimeter and are characterized by very fine dendritic arms, each measuring less than 100 nm in thickness and reaching heights of 500–700 nm.

caption: Relative particle displacement of the TD_8 powder pile under 0.16 G gravity, derived from the Lagrangian approximation.
summary: Depicting the relative particle displacement under 0.16 G gravity, this panel utilizes the Lagrangian approximation to model the TD_8 powder pile. The primary supply of deposited particles occurs through the gap region, consistent with in-situ observations, highlighting the influence of low gravity on particle deposition dynamics.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) dislocation map and grain boundary distribution for NiTi alloy sample 3# viewed in the X-Y plane.
summary: This panel displays the KAM dislocation map and grain boundary distribution for NiTi alloy sample 3# in the X-Y plane. Variations in laser power during processing significantly influence the grain size, orientation consistency, and morphological characteristics of the alloy, as evidenced by the structural features captured in this EBSD-based visualization.

caption: Measurement schemas for determining the wear track length and the cross-sectional area of the wear track.
summary: This schematic illustrates the methodology for quantifying wear volume. The wear surface cross-section is measured using an Altisurf wide-field confocal microscope, and this value is integrated over the total length of the wear track to calculate the final wear volume, providing a precise approach for evaluating material degradation.

caption: Summary of the optimized process parameters utilized for the WAAM deposition of AISI316L stainless steel, based on previous research.
summary: This table presents the optimized process parameters employed for the WAAM deposition of AISI316L stainless steel. These parameters were derived from the author's previous work to ensure consistent material deposition. The data serves as the foundational settings for the subsequent fabrication of the experimental wall structures described in the study.

caption: Arrhenius plot of normalized minimum creep rate versus inverse absolute temperature (1000/RT) at a normalized stress of 2.2 × 10⁻⁴, illustrating the determination of apparent activation energy for upper and lower limit data.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the normalized minimum creep rate against the inverse absolute temperature to calculate the apparent activation energy. The analysis, performed at a normalized stress of 2.2 × 10⁻⁴, yields activation energies of 498 kJ/mol and 363 kJ/mol for upper and lower limit data, respectively, with a correlation coefficient of 0.97.

caption: LC–HRMS extracted ion chromatograms comparing the elution profiles of C6H8F2N4O2 isomers in artificial saliva after 24 hours and 3 months of incubation with Saremco print CROWNTECH specimens, alongside a 3-month control sample.
summary: Extracted ion chromatograms for putative C6H8F2N4O2 isomers (m/z 189.0582) demonstrate the temporal evolution of leachable species from CROWNTECH specimens. Global normalization reveals a clear increase in peak intensities for these fluorinated molecules between 24 hours and 3 months of incubation, confirming their release into the artificial saliva medium over time.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the linear relationship between the natural logarithm of the rate constant ln k i and the Zener-Hollomon parameter ln Z for the α-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the correlation between the natural logarithm of the rate constant ln k i and the Zener-Hollomon parameter ln Z specifically for the α-phase of the Ti6Al4V alloy. The linear trend observed in this plot characterizes the kinetic behavior of the α-phase under the tested conditions.

caption: Thermodynamic simulation results for the Al14Co41Cr15Fe10Ni20 alloy system, illustrating phase stability and transformation behavior across varying temperatures.
summary: This thermodynamic simulation provides a comprehensive overview of the phase stability for the Al14Co41Cr15Fe10Ni20 alloy. By utilizing CALPHAD-based modeling, the figure illustrates the equilibrium phase evolution and transformation characteristics of the material, serving as a critical reference for understanding the alloy's thermodynamic behavior and potential microstructural development under varying thermal conditions.

caption: Type V dislocation structure in the Re-containing alloy after pre-straining at 750 °C and 750 MPa, viewed along the [001] beam direction.
summary: TEM micrograph showing the type V dislocation structure in a Re-containing Ni-based single crystal superalloy after pre-straining at 750 °C and 750 MPa. The image highlights the formation of anisotropic dislocation structures within the γ/γ' microstructure, which are known to reduce the creep life of these single crystal superalloys.

caption: Molecular dynamics snapshot illustrating the pore distribution within the model subjected to a laser power of 300 eV/ps at a scanning speed of 4 Å/ps.
summary: This molecular dynamics snapshot displays the pore distribution resulting from a laser power of 300 eV/ps at a constant scanning speed of 4 Å/ps. The visualization provides insight into the structural morphology of the model under these specific processing conditions, contributing to the overall analysis of laser-induced porosity.

caption: In-situ NIR monitoring of the airfoil platform region, illustrating the persistent nature of the crack regardless of the specific scan path.
summary: In-situ NIR monitoring captures crack formation in the airfoil platform region. This observation is consistent across different geometries and scan directions. The crack location remains stable in this region, demonstrating a persistent structural defect during the initial stages of the build process as monitored by the NIR imaging system.

caption: Confocal images of DiO-labeled ApoVs within composite hydrogels and corresponding in vitro release profiles in PBS.
summary: Confocal microscopy was used to visualize the distribution of DiO-ApoVs within composite hydrogels. Additionally, the in vitro release profile of ApoVs from these hydrogels into PBS was measured, demonstrating the controlled release characteristics of the composite material for potential therapeutic delivery applications.

caption: Tafel plots showing the corrosion performance of Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples tested in a 0.5 M NaCl saline solution.
summary: Tafel curves for Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples are depicted for a 0.5 M NaCl solution. The Ni-Cr coating exhibits moderate corrosion resistance in this saline environment, characterized by an Ecorr of -0.08 V and a jcorr of 0.795 µA cm-2, as detailed in the supporting experimental data.

caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 25 °C, showing the distribution of solute elements.
summary: This panel displays the normalized mass spectrum for Inconel 718 samples tested at 25 °C. Analysis confirms that while other solutes are present in comparable amounts, atom probe tomography failed to resolve significant traces of carbon, necessitating this specific mass spectrum investigation to evaluate carbon content across different temperatures.

caption: Nanoindentation load-displacement curves for wrought and HT-LPBF NiTi samples, showing differences in hardness (H) and elastic modulus (μ).
summary: Nanoindentation curves demonstrate that HT-LPBF NiTi samples are softer than wrought samples. The wrought NiTi exhibits mean hardness and modulus values of 5.27 GPa and 0.54, respectively, while the HT-LPBF samples show lower values of 4.86 GPa and 0.5, confirming the reduced mechanical hardness of the additively manufactured material.

caption: Correlation curve demonstrating the relationship between tungsten concentration, grayscale intensity of the filament, and the XRF signal intensity (Lα W).
summary: The correlation plot displays the interdependencies between tungsten concentration, grayscale intensity, and XRF signal intensity. This graphical representation confirms the relationship between the physical color tone of the filaments and the elemental analysis results, providing a clear validation of the concentration gradient as measured by the X-ray fluorescence technique.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Fe-Ni-Cr system at 1600K, illustrating the equilibrium phase boundaries and compositional regions.
summary: This panel displays the ternary phase diagram for the Fe-Ni-Cr system at a constant temperature of 1600K. It provides a visual representation of the equilibrium phase relationships and compositional stability regions for this specific metallic alloy system, serving as a reference for phase behavior at high temperatures.

caption: Visible light transmittance measurements of acellular bioprinted structures compared against native human cornea and PBS controls.
summary: Transmittance values for the multi-material bioprinted structures range from 74.6% to 87.3% across the visible light spectrum. This quantitative analysis demonstrates that the acellular constructs maintain high optical transparency comparable to native human corneal tissue, validating their potential as effective substitutes in corneal tissue engineering applications.

caption: Combined absorbance and transmittance spectra of 3D-printed discs soaked for 3 hours in ethanol, containing RhB-HZ at concentrations of 0.01%, 0.03%, and 0.05% (w/v).
summary: This panel displays the absorbance and transmittance spectra for 3D-printed discs that were soaked in ethanol for 3 hours with varying RhB-HZ concentrations of 0.01%, 0.03%, and 0.05% (w/v). The results indicate that these spectra lack the characteristic visible absorption bands typically associated with RhB-HZ activation.

caption: Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) performance metric for the validation set across 50 training epochs.
summary: Performance evaluation of the improved U-Net model shows that the mIoU of the validation set exceeded 0.90 at Epoch 25. The metric continued to improve throughout the training process and eventually stabilized at 0.97 by the conclusion of the 50 epochs, indicating high segmentation accuracy for the model.

caption: Mean SHAP value distribution plot quantifying the contribution of individual morphological features to the model's predictive output.
summary: The mean SHAP value distribution plot illustrates the relative contribution of each morphological feature to the model's predictions. By quantifying the impact of individual instances on the output, this visualization provides insight into which specific martensite features are most influential in the model's classification of different martensite types.

caption: Finite element method heat transfer simulation results for the hemispherical FGCs, demonstrating the thermal response over a 10,000 s duration.
summary: Finite element method results display the heat transfer behavior of the hemispherical FGCs over a 10,000 s period. This simulation provides insight into the long-term thermal response of the material, demonstrating a trend consistent with rectangular FGCs and confirming the effectiveness of the material distribution in managing heat transfer.

caption: Reconstructed 3D volume of an undeformed cubic specimen showing crack morphology highlighted in blue shades.
summary: This reconstructed 3D volume of an undeformed cubic specimen utilizes X-ray computed micro-tomography to visualize internal crack morphology. Blue shades highlight the fissures within the material. The thresholding was specifically adjusted to emphasize these cracks, though this processing technique results in an overstatement of the actual crack size.

caption: Interferogram of the m = 1 vortex plate obtained via off-axis holography, showing a central fork indicating a topological charge of 1.
summary: This interferogram, generated using off-axis holography for the m = 1 vortex plate, clearly displays a fork at the center. This feature confirms a topological charge of 1 and demonstrates the wrapping of the phase, consistent with the expected behavior of the vortex phase plate design.

caption: Three-dimensional micro-CT reconstruction of a Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) tensile test sample section, highlighting internal voids formed between adjacent printed threads and layers.
summary: This 3D micro-CT reconstruction displays a section of a dog-bone tensile test sample manufactured via FFF. The visualization reveals internal voids generated during the printing process between adjacent threads and layers. These structural defects are significant, as they influence the mechanical properties of 3D-printed materials during tensile characterization.

caption: Temperature distribution map for an oval-shaped battery capsule, representing the varied thermal response of the PCM layer under specific airflow conditions.
summary: The oval-shaped battery capsule presented here exhibits a unique temperature distribution within the PCM layer. This panel contributes to the broader investigation of how different capsule geometries influence thermal profiles, confirming that oval-shaped designs show distinct thermal behaviors compared to their cylindrical counterparts under consistent airflow conditions.

caption: Temperature-dependent variation of the full-width at half maximum (FWHM) of the first sharp diffraction peak Q1 during heating at 0.33 Ks-1.
summary: The FWHM of the first sharp diffraction peak is plotted against temperature to track structural relaxation processes. Minor relaxation events are observable, particularly near the glass transition temperature Tg, even when the material appears fully relaxed to the equilibrium liquid state over longer timescales during the synchrotron diffraction experiment.

caption: Isothermal section of the Al-rich Al-Ce-Ni ternary system at 400 °C, showing phase equilibria at lower temperatures.
summary: Representing the Al-rich Al-Ce-Ni ternary system at 400 °C, this isothermal section illustrates the phase equilibria at lower temperatures. It is used for comparison with the corresponding Mn-containing system, highlighting how the phase stability regions evolve as the temperature decreases from 620 °C to 400 °C.

caption: XGBoost model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: XGBoost model performance is analyzed using a confusion matrix. As the data remains identical for all models tested, this matrix serves as a diagnostic tool to evaluate the classification accuracy of the XGBoost algorithm, revealing the distribution of correct and incorrect predictions across the various target classes.

caption: Simulated and measured centre deformation of the TS1 AM Ti6Al4V thin-walled part.
summary: This panel illustrates the simulated and measured centre deformation of the TS1 AM Ti6Al4V thin-walled part during a stable machining process. The data provides a comparison between predicted and experimental deformation values, highlighting the structural response of the TS1 specimen under the applied cutting forces.

caption: Parity plot showing the correlation between experimental and ANN-predicted mechanical property values for a secondary dataset.
summary: Representing the second part of the model validation, this parity plot displays the alignment between experimental results and ANN predictions. The strong correlation observed confirms that the constructed model maintains high predictive performance across different experimental datasets, reinforcing the robustness of the machine learning approach in modeling mechanical properties.

caption: FTIR spectra of native MP and MP-TA conjugates, highlighting characteristic peaks at 3293, 2963, 1655, and 1547 cm-1, with observed shifts in amide A and amide I bands indicating ultrasound-enhanced structural modifications.
summary: The FTIR spectra reveal characteristic protein peaks in native MP at 3293, 2963, 1655, and 1547 cm-1. Ultrasound-assisted conjugation with TA induces progressively larger shifts in the amide A and amide I bands compared to native MP, providing evidence of ultrasound-enhanced structural modifications and protein unfolding within the MP-TA conjugates.

caption: FTIR spectra of the 3D printed printlet and its individual components, illustrating the molecular interactions between the polymeric materials.
summary: FTIR analysis was performed to investigate the molecular interactions between various polymeric materials within the 3D printed object. The spectra provide a detailed view of the chemical composition and bonding characteristics of the printlet and its constituent components, facilitating a thorough understanding of the material interactions present in the final 3D structure.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot of Bi2MoO6 measured at various alternating current potential frequencies.
summary: This Mott-Schottky plot for Bi2MoO6 displays a positive slope, which confirms that the material acts as an n-type semiconductor. The measurement was conducted under different alternating current potential frequencies to characterize the electronic properties of the semiconductor interface, providing essential data for understanding its photocatalytic behavior in heterojunction systems.

caption: Enlarged HRTEM image of Area B, including FFT and IFFT analysis to resolve structural details.
summary: Area B is presented via an enlarged high-resolution transmission electron microscopy image, with accompanying fast Fourier transform and inverse fast Fourier transform analysis. This detailed imaging approach facilitates the investigation of the microstructural characteristics and atomic-scale features present within the TiN and Ti2N layers of the material.

caption: UV–VIS transmittance spectra comparing the shaped glass to a commercial microscope glass slide, showing a 10% difference in the visible light range.
summary: The shaped glass exhibits ultra-violet and visible transparency characteristics comparable to a standard commercial microscope glass slide. UV-VIS transmittance measurements reveal a 10% difference in performance within the visible spectrum, confirming the optical quality of the material produced through the stamping process on printed pre-forms.

caption: High-resolution Mn2p XPS region for the PEG-3–1500 specimen, featuring measured data and the corresponding fitting results.
summary: The high-resolution Mn2p XPS region for the PEG-3–1500 specimen is presented with measured red curves and black fitting results. This analysis is essential for evaluating the oxidation state of manganese, supporting the comprehensive investigation into the specimen's cation states through XPS and XAFS spectroscopic techniques.

caption: Schematic illustration of the Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) process, highlighting the sequential layer-by-layer deposition technique used to construct complex geometries.
summary: This schematic provides an overview of the Fused Filament Fabrication process. It illustrates the fundamental mechanism of layer deposition, which is repeated sequentially to build complex three-dimensional geometries. This additive manufacturing approach ensures high accuracy in the production of parts by stacking material layers one on top of another.

caption: Procedural flowchart detailing the experimental steps for determining the specific mass and accumulated mass reduction of nutshell samples.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic testing procedures employed to evaluate nutshell samples. The methodology includes determining specific mass using a 25 ml pycnometer according to ABNT NBR 6296 standards, with results averaged over three repetitions. The process also tracks the average percentage of accumulated mass reduction for various test conditions.

caption: Nyquist plot representing the electrochemical impedance response of the XY section of Wall 0.
summary: This Nyquist plot displays the electrochemical impedance response for the XY section of Wall 0. The data illustrates degradation properties through a reduction in semicircle diameter over time. Although corrosion phenomena are initially active, the accumulation of corrosion products after two days appears to decelerate the overall corrosion process.

caption: Comparison of nanohardness values for as-built (AB) and heat-treated (HT) samples, derived from the nanoindentation data.
summary: Nanohardness values for the as-built and heat-treated samples are summarized in this bar chart. The data points were extracted directly from the force–displacement curves shown in panel (a), allowing for a clear quantitative comparison of the material hardness changes resulting from the different processing conditions applied to the samples.

caption: Conductivity curves of 3D-printed PLA-CB composites measured at printing temperatures between 230 °C and 280 °C under varying applied voltages.
summary: This plot illustrates the electrical conductivity of 3D-printed PLA-CB samples as a function of applied voltage. Printing temperatures from 230 °C to 260 °C generally enhance electrical performance, whereas temperatures exceeding 270 °C result in performance degradation, highlighting the sensitivity of the material's conductive network to thermal processing conditions.

caption: Stress-life fatigue behavior of specimens fabricated in perpendicular orientation using 1X to 4X reused powders under force-controlled conditions at R σ = 0.1.
summary: Perpendicular-oriented specimens show stress-life fatigue behavior across different powder reuse conditions at R σ = 0.1. Consistent with parallel specimens, those fabricated with virgin powder generally achieve longer fatigue lives than those using reused powders, confirming that powder reuse negatively impacts the fatigue resistance of the fabricated components.

caption: CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram displaying the color coordinates for surfactant-assisted SnO2-CTAB nanoparticles.
summary: This CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram highlights the color coordinates for SnO2-CTAB nanoparticles. Derived from photoluminescence emission spectra, the plot demonstrates an emission shift compared to pure samples, with the resulting coordinates located in the blue region, confirming the influence of the CTAB surfactant on the nanostructure's optical emission.

caption: Detailed M(H) magnetization loop of polycrystalline erbium showing the coercive field Hc and remanent magnetization Mr, with insets displaying the full-scale magnetization loop and the calculated susceptibility χρ = dM/dH.
summary: This magnetization loop for polycrystalline erbium highlights the coercive field and remanent magnetization within the hysteresis region. The energy density is estimated at 213 × 10^-4 J kg^-1. Insets provide the full-scale metallic Er magnetization loop and the calculated susceptibility, illustrating the magnetic response and energy dissipation characteristics of the material.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the Mn2FeSn alloy unit cell, highlighting the specific configuration where Fe atoms occupy the P1 and P2 crystallographic positions.
summary: This visualization displays the crystal structure of the Mn2FeSn alloy, specifically illustrating the atomic configuration where Fe atoms are located at the P1 and P2 positions. This arrangement serves as the reference configuration for the alloy, providing essential structural information regarding the atomic distribution within the unit cell.

caption: High-pressure electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-1.8Si alloy at 138(4) GPa, measured up to 3402(250) K, including comparisons with hcp-Fe and hcp-Fe-2Si literature data.
summary: This panel presents the electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-1.8Si alloy at 138(4) GPa, extending to 3402(250) K. The resistivity increases quasi-linearly with temperature, following the Bloch-Grüneisen model. The results are compared with previous data for hcp-Fe at 142 GPa and hcp-Fe-2Si at 44 GPa, providing context for the alloy's electronic behavior.

caption: 3D micro-CT images of mandibular defect sites in a rat model, showing bone regeneration stages around Ti–5Cu implants compared to pure Ti.
summary: Micro-CT analysis of mandibular defect sites demonstrates the bone regeneration process. The Ti-5Cu implants significantly increased bone volume to total volume (BV/TV) ratios at 4 and 8 weeks compared to pure Ti, providing clear evidence that the 5% copper alloy enhances bone healing and integration in vivo.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of a polycrystalline Ni alloy oxidized at 250℃ for 1 minute, displaying initial stratification of the oxide layer.
summary: This ToF-SIMS depth profile illustrates the initial oxidation stage of a polycrystalline Ni alloy after 1 minute at 250℃. The data reveals the early onset of oxide layer stratification, providing insight into the initial chemical distribution and structural evolution of the surface oxide formed during the oxidation process.

caption: Convergence trajectory of the optimization process utilizing the improved large mutation genetic algorithm.
summary: This panel illustrates the optimization convergence path achieved through the improved large mutation genetic algorithm. It tracks the progress of the optimization process, demonstrating how the algorithm refines the model parameters over time to reach an optimal solution within the defined computational framework of the study.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of a graphene platelet (GP) sample.
summary: Atomic force microscopy imaging of the GP sample allows for the characterization of its morphology. The height profile analysis reveals that the GP material has an average thickness of approximately 350 nm, which is significantly larger than the thicknesses observed for the GO and rGO samples in this study.

caption: Magnified dark field TEM image highlighting the triple point junction.
summary: The magnified dark field TEM image offers a localized view of the triple point junction, enhancing the visibility of specific structural features. This approach complements the bright field observation by providing distinct contrast, which is essential for identifying the precise microstructural characteristics at the junction interface.

caption: Chronoamperometric response curves for different electrocatalysts measured at a constant potential of −0.2 V vs. SCE to evaluate long-term operational stability.
summary: Chronoamperometric responses are presented for various electrocatalysts held at a constant potential of −0.2 V vs. SCE. This measurement serves as a critical test for assessing the long-term operational stability of the catalysts, providing insight into how current density evolves over time under sustained electrochemical conditions.

caption: Others category orientation relationship interface map for intergranular austenite and ferrite in HT200-700 condition, utilizing unique color assignments for interface identification.
summary: This panel depicts interfaces categorized as Others for intergranular austenite and ferrite in the HT200-700 condition. By assigning unique random colors to each interface ID, the map highlights the diversity of boundary types. Such characterization is essential for evaluating the impact of thermal treatment on the material's grain structure.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the frequency-dependent electrochemical impedance behavior of the coated samples.
summary: Bode plots are presented alongside Nyquist plots to provide a comprehensive evaluation of the coating's corrosion resistance. These plots characterize the electrochemical impedance response of the samples across a range of frequencies, serving as a key diagnostic tool for assessing the protective performance of the applied coatings.

caption: EBSD grain structure map of a 1.0 mm L-PBF specimen, viewed perpendicular to the build direction with randomized grain colors.
summary: This EBSD map displays the grain structure of a 1.0 mm L-PBF specimen, captured perpendicular to the build direction. Randomized colors are used to distinguish individual grains. L-PBF specimens generally exhibit significantly smaller grains compared to LP-DED specimens, which is a key factor influencing their expected higher mechanical strength.

caption: Bode phase angle and impedance magnitude plots representing the frequency-dependent electrochemical response of the material.
summary: Bode phase angle and impedance plots are depicted to characterize the frequency-dependent electrochemical behavior of the material. These plots provide a detailed view of the impedance magnitude and phase shift across the tested frequency range, complementing the Nyquist data to fully describe the electrochemical system's impedance characteristics.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of LC-SPI25 and LC-SPI25GLY scaffolds at 1, 3, and 7 days of culture, displaying live cells in green and dead cells in red with a 200 μm scale bar.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of LC-SPI25 and LC-SPI25GLY scaffolds at 1, 3, and 7 days of culture, displaying live cells in green and dead cells in red with a 200 μm scale bar. These scaffolds demonstrate high cell confluence and a typical fibroblastic phenotype throughout the entire studied culture period.

caption: Rietveld refinement profile for the undeuterated Zr3Fe0.7Ni0.3 sample, displaying experimental neutron diffraction data as blue crosses, the calculated model as a red line, the background including stainless-steel cell peaks as a black line, and the residual difference as a lower black line.
summary: This panel presents the neutron diffraction pattern and Rietveld refinement results for the undeuterated Zr3Fe0.7Ni0.3 alloy. The plot compares experimental data against a calculated profile, accounting for background contributions from the stainless-steel pressure cell. The refinement confirms the structural model, with the difference curve indicating the quality of the fit.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of the Al–Mg-Sc-Zr alloy subjected to various heat treatment temperatures, highlighting the presence of Al3Sc, Al3Zr, and Al6Mn precipitated phases.
summary: This XRD analysis characterizes the phase evolution of an Al–Mg-Sc-Zr alloy across different heat treatment temperatures. The diffraction patterns confirm the successful precipitation of Al3Sc, Al3Zr, and Al6Mn phases within the alloy matrix, providing critical insights into the microstructural development resulting from the applied thermal processing conditions.

caption: Relative half effects of metamodel factors for melt pool dimensions in 316L stainless steel, derived from an FCCC design.
summary: This panel displays the relative half effects of metamodel factors influencing melt pool dimensions in 316L stainless steel. Calculated using an FCCC design, these effects are presented in a normalized parameter space where the model constant corresponds to the mean value of the data utilized for metamodel construction.

caption: Bar chart displaying the calculated percentage weights of various input variables for GPR mechanical property prediction models, derived from length-scale analysis.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the relative influence of different input variables on GPR model predictions. By calculating percentage weights based on length-scale, the figure identifies key features for selection, enabling the construction of accurate GPR models with reduced input dimensionality for predicting mechanical properties of LPBF AlSi10Mg.

caption: EDX elemental mapping of the HT2 heat-treated AISI 316L sample surface.
summary: EDX mapping of the HT2 sample provides a visual representation of the elemental distribution of Fe, Ni, Cr, Mo, Si, and Mn. The results confirm that the chemical composition remains consistent with the AISI 316L alloy specifications following the HT2 heat treatment process.

caption: Microhardness values measured for sintered, solution-treated, and aged samples, illustrating the variation in material hardness across different processing stages.
summary: Microhardness values for the sintered, solution-treated, and aged samples are presented in this panel. These results, which are also summarized in Table 4 of the study, provide a quantitative comparison of the material's hardness response following each specific thermal treatment step applied to the specimens.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the temperature-dependent diffusion coefficients of 7 and 19 SIA clusters in pure Fe and Fe-Ni alloys containing 0.8 and 2.5 at.% Ni, as determined by time trajectory decomposition (TTD) simulations.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the diffusion coefficients for 7 and 19 SIA clusters in pure Fe and Fe-Ni alloys. The data, calculated via TTD, shows that increasing Ni content significantly impacts both migration energies and cluster diffusivity. Notably, the cluster diffusivity exhibits deviations from the Arrhenius law at certain temperatures.
