caption: Cycling performance of D-3DP electrodes with varying thicknesses measured at a current density of 0.2 mA cm-2.
summary: This plot illustrates the cycling performance of printed-layered D-3DP electrodes with varying thicknesses. By measuring these performances, the study reveals the influence of electrode thickness on electrochemical behavior, providing critical data on how structural dimensions affect the long-term stability and capacity retention of the 3D-printed microbattery components.

caption: Compressive modulus values for GelMA/Fib composite hydrogel groups G5, G5F0.5, G5F1.0, and G5F1.5, demonstrating a significant reduction in stiffness as Fib concentration increases.
summary: The compressive modulus of GelMA/Fib composite hydrogels was evaluated across four groups. Results indicate that increasing Fib content significantly reduces the compressive modulus of the tissue blocks. Specifically, the G5F1.5 group exhibited the lowest modulus at 1.67 kPa, rendering it too fluid for practical printing applications.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns of as-fabricated ABD-850AM and ABD-900AM alloys obtained with 600 s exposure time.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns for as-fabricated ABD-850AM and ABD-900AM alloys are presented, utilizing a 600 s exposure time to characterize the initial microstructure. These long-exposure measurements reveal the specific phases present in both alloy conditions, providing a comprehensive overview of the structural state following the L-PBF fabrication process.

caption: HAADF-STEM image highlighting the interface between δ-ferrite and α’-martensite in the R2 specimen.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field STEM imaging is used to visualize the interface between δ-ferrite and α’-martensite in the R2 specimen. This mode is part of a comprehensive STEM analysis designed to elucidate the substructures of these phases, providing higher contrast and structural detail than conventional diffraction-based characterization methods.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of TT-D6 cells cultured on 3D-printed scaffolds for 1 day, showing cell viability.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of TT-D6 cells cultured on 3D-printed scaffolds for 1 day demonstrate cell viability. After 1 day of co-culture, abundant adherent cells were observed on all scaffold groups, with no evident dead cells, indicating that the scaffolds are biocompatible and support initial cell attachment and survival.

caption: Oxygen contamination levels in NiTi powders processed at 20 kHz and 40 kHz frequencies.
summary: Oxygen contamination levels in NiTi powders are compared across different processing frequencies. Mass spectrometry analysis reveals that oxygen absorption is significantly higher in powders processed at 40 kHz compared to those processed at 20 kHz, indicating that processing frequency has a substantial influence on the final impurity levels in the material.

caption: Final Mo atomic fraction distribution within the single-track Mo-Ti PBF process.
summary: This panel displays the final Mo atomic fraction distribution resulting from a single-track Mo-Ti PBF simulation. The simulation models the melting of a 25 μm thick powder layer deposited on a pure Ti substrate, providing insight into the compositional homogeneity achieved during the laser processing of the Mo-Ti alloy system.

caption: 4DSTEM image displaying the FCC (cF4) phase domains within the central region of the lamella.
summary: This 4DSTEM image highlights the presence of FCC (cF4) phase domains identified within the central region of the lamella. The technique allows for the precise mapping of these crystalline domains, providing structural insight into the material's composition as observed in the central lamella region during the experimental analysis.

caption: Room-temperature magnetization curves showing the magnetic response of NdFeB powder, wax/NdFeB printed magnet, and Fe3O4 powder as a function of applied DC magnetic field.
summary: Room-temperature magnetization curves illustrate the magnetic behavior of NdFeB powder, wax/NdFeB printed magnets, and Fe3O4 powder under varying DC magnetic fields. The Fe3O4 nanoparticles exhibit superparamagnetic behavior, as their size remains below the critical superparamagnetic limit of approximately 25 nm, confirming the magnetic properties observed in the hysteresis measurements.

caption: Systematic workflow diagram detailing the sequential fabrication process for a full-scale battery housing prototype.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the comprehensive methodology developed for the fabrication of a full-scale battery housing prototype. The proposed workflow is designed to be versatile, ensuring that the outlined procedural steps are applicable to any welding system, thereby providing a standardized framework for industrial battery housing assembly and manufacturing processes.

caption: EBSD IPF-z map and corresponding pole figures for PBF-LB/M/316L stainless steel subjected to HT900/1 annealing condition.
summary: This panel shows the EBSD IPF-z map and representative pole figures for the PBF-LB/M/316L austenitic stainless steel after HT900/1 heat treatment. The microstructure exhibits a polycrystalline pure austenitic structure with elongated grains oriented along the z-direction, consistent with the observation that heat treatments do not significantly alter grain morphology or texture.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the boron-free alloy tip showing the distribution of elements.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the microstructure of a boron-free alloy tip. According to Kontis et al., the absence of boron results in a distinct grain boundary composition, where M23C6 carbides are present, contrasting with the boride-enriched boundaries observed in alloys with higher boron concentrations.

caption: Microhardness measurements across the build-up layer and substrate interface, demonstrating a positive correlation between scan speed and hardness values at 100 W.
summary: Microhardness data for the 100 W specimen shows a clear trend where hardness increases with rising scan speed. This mechanical response is linked to the changes in input energy and the resulting microstructural features at the interface, providing a quantitative measure of the material's performance under varying fabrication parameters.

caption: STEM micrograph of a heat-treated unpeened specimen showing a coarsened microstructure with a high density of secondary γ’ precipitates within the γ channels.
summary: This STEM image reveals the microstructure of a heat-treated unpeened specimen. The material exhibits significant coarsening, characterized by a noticeably larger fraction of secondary γ’ phases embedded within the γ channels. This structural evolution is a direct consequence of the heat treatment process applied to the specimen.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the log of 3D bulk diffusion coefficients for Ni and Cr versus the inverse of temperature, comparing ∑3 and ∑9 grain boundaries against previous bulk calculations.
summary: The total bulk diffusivities for Cr and Ni are presented as an Arrhenius plot of log(D) versus inverse temperature. By incorporating vacancy rescaling factors for energy, this plot allows for the extraction of activation energies for Cr diffusion, facilitating a direct comparison between ∑3, ∑9 grain boundaries, and established bulk reference data.

caption: Detailed view of the column top and the integrated system of load cells for weight monitoring.
summary: This image highlights the column top and the integrated system of load cells employed for monitoring weight during the experiments. The visual documentation confirms the specific arrangement of the load cell system, which is critical for the accurate measurement of liquid holdup and pressure drop within the experimental pilot.

caption: Time-on-stream intensity profile for CO (m/z = 28) measured via in situ mass spectrometry during the catalytic reaction.
summary: Monitoring the intensity of CO (m/z = 28) over time-on-stream via in situ mass spectrometry allows for the assessment of carbon monoxide levels during the reaction. This data helps characterize the reaction pathways and the extent of CO formation or consumption occurring within the catalytic system under the defined parameters.

caption: Isometric and orthographic minimum intensity projection views of a very high-density PBF-EB-printed sample (Run 2, sample 11) showing the distribution of gas and lack-of-fusion (LoF) pores.
summary: This panel displays the orthographic projection of a very high-density sample, identified as Run 2, sample 11. The computed tomography images reveal the internal pore morphology, specifically highlighting the presence and distribution of gas pores and lack-of-fusion (LoF) defects within the PBF-EB-printed material structure.

caption: Energy release rates for PA 12/PACF samples, comparing G Uc and G SLB values across varying SLS_MEX layer thicknesses and initial layer orientations, showing a rising trend from 2_1 to 4_1 configurations.
summary: Energy release rates for PA 12/PACF samples are presented, highlighting the influence of SLS_MEX layer thickness and initial layer orientation on fracture performance. The data reveals a distinct rising trend in energy release rates as the configuration progresses from 2_1 to 4_1, with separate scales utilized for G Uc and G SLB.

caption: Crack length (a) versus number of cycles (N) for specimen n. 2, comparing data from back-face strain-gauge measurements (black curves) and crack-gauge sensors (red squares) during fatigue testing in air.
summary: Specimen n. 2 exhibits crack growth behavior characterized by the relationship between crack length and cycle count. Data collected via back-face strain-gauge and crack-gauge sensors are plotted to track fatigue progression in air, providing a comparative analysis of the two measurement techniques throughout the testing duration.

caption: Neural Network (NN) model confusion matrix evaluated on the unseen test set.
summary: Neural Network model performance is captured in this confusion matrix, which evaluates the model against the unseen test set. By displaying the frequency of correct and incorrect predictions, the matrix serves as a diagnostic tool to assess the network's learning efficacy and its generalization capabilities on new data.

caption: Topography measurement of the fracture surface for the boron-free alloy specimen tested at 750 °C and a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹.
summary: This confocal microscopy image displays the fracture surface of a boron-free alloy specimen after ETMT testing at 750 °C. The surface appears relatively flat, which is indicative of a brittle fracture mode. This topography measurement confirms the limited ductility of the boron-free material under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: X-axis cutting force profile during micro milling of LPBF Ti6Al4V at 60,000 rpm and 3 µm/flute with a 45 µm depth of cut.
summary: This plot illustrates the x-axis cutting force measured during the micro milling of LPBF Ti6Al4V. The machining parameters are set at 60,000 rpm, 3 µm/flute, and a 45 µm depth of cut. This data contributes to the experimental evaluation of force variations influenced by tool geometry and material properties.

caption: Temperature-dependent thermal expansion coefficients of as-cast Al–10Ni-xSi alloys with varying silicon content from 0 to 20 wt%.
summary: This plot illustrates the variation of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) for Al–10Ni-xSi alloys as a function of temperature. The thermal expansion performance of these alloys is characterized by a curve that evolves in two distinct stages across the tested temperature range for different silicon concentrations.

caption: Cyclic austenitization-aging (CA-A) treated steel sample displaying the distribution of intermetallic precipitates within the martensitic matrix.
summary: The cyclic austenitization-aging (CA-A) treated sample exhibits a distribution of intermetallic precipitates within the martensitic structure. Consistent with other heat-treated samples, this condition shows the same type of precipitates as the DA sample, with variations primarily in the size and morphology of the secondary phases present.

caption: Tabulated magnetic parameters for LPBF-built Nd-Fe-B magnets, demonstrating performance variations correlated with scanning strategies and relative density.
summary: Specified magnetic parameters for the LPBF-built Nd-Fe-B magnets are listed in this table. The data reveals a consistent change tendency in magnetic properties across different scanning strategies, which correlates directly with the relative density of the samples, highlighting the impact of processing conditions on the final magnetic performance.

caption: Selective laser drying of the deposited slurry to form the first layer of the green body.
summary: Laser-based selective drying is applied to the slurry layer to solidify the first section of the green body. This mechanism, which shares similarities with stereolithography, allows for precise, localized curing of the material, enabling the controlled construction of the initial layer within the LIS manufacturing framework.

caption: Computational model of a lever component subjected to two distinct load cases applied on cylindrical subdomains, with a fully fixed support condition imposed on the central cylindrical subdomain.
summary: This simulation model illustrates a lever component used to evaluate the computational efficiency of the FreeTO optimization framework. The setup features two specific load cases applied to the outer cylindrical subdomains, while the middle cylindrical subdomain is constrained by a fully fixed support condition to define the structural boundary.

caption: Charge-discharge profiles of carbon nanotube nanocomposite electrodes, demonstrating high-performance characteristics for lithium-ion battery applications.
summary: These charge-discharge curves characterize the electrochemical performance of carbon nanotube nanocomposite electrodes. The data confirms their suitability for high-performance lithium-ion batteries, showing efficient energy storage capabilities and stable cycling behavior, which are critical for the development of advanced energy storage devices using 3D printed components.

caption: Formation energies of solute H at various stable sites within the NGI core, identifying three distinct site types (S I, S II, and S III) near virtual hexagons.
summary: Formation energies for H atoms at stable sites within the NGI core are displayed, focusing on a subset of occupiable positions to reveal general hydrogen behavior. Three specific stable site types, labeled S I, S II, and S III, are identified and highlighted near virtual hexagons based on their distinct formation energy values.

caption: Ashby map illustrating the mechanical performance landscape of three distinct high-entropy alloys (HEAs) subjected to varying processing methods.
summary: This Ashby map highlights the significant dispersion in mechanical properties across three select high-entropy alloys. It demonstrates that the chosen processing route profoundly influences the underlying deformation behavior. The wide performance range underscores the inherent complexity of HEA microstructures and suggests that research remains in its nascent stages.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of a thin foil specimen lifted from a deformed micropillar in Grain 1, showing slip steps on the left side surface and the overall dislocation structure.
summary: This bright-field STEM image displays the dislocation structure within a deformed micropillar specimen from Grain 1. The visualization highlights visible slip steps along the left side surface of the pillar, providing a clear view of the structural deformation resulting from the mechanical testing process on the grain.

caption: 3D rendering of VSCP sample particles following morphological opening with a 7 px radius filter.
summary: This 3D rendering shows the VSCP sample after a 7 px radius morphological opening, which filters out agglomerations smaller than 9.1 µm. By increasing the diameter of the morphological operation, smaller features are removed, allowing for a focused assessment of the spatial homogeneity of the remaining larger particle agglomerations.

caption: Plot of burst size (Δh) versus displacement for a representative nanoindentation curve at 300 °C.
summary: This panel displays the magnitude of burst size, defined as the length of plateaus in the load-displacement curve, at 300 °C. These pop-in events provide critical information regarding the number, mobility, and interaction of dislocations generated beneath the indenter tip during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Ratio of FCNN-predicted to nTop-calculated maximum stiffness values plotted against relative density.
summary: This panel compares the S 1 values predicted by the FCNN model for maximum stiffness against those calculated using nTop software. The plot highlights the accuracy of the FCNN approach in predicting maximum stiffness across different relative densities, providing a direct validation against established numerical simulation methods.

caption: S-N curves for semicircular notched specimens across as-built (AB), stress relief (SR), and hot isostatic pressing (HIP) conditions.
summary: This S-N curve illustrates the fatigue performance of semicircular notched specimens under three material conditions: as-built, stress relief, and hot isostatic pressing. Fatigue strength remains remarkably similar across all series at shorter fatigue lives, likely due to higher strain levels that homogenize residual stresses during the cyclic loading process.

caption: Ductile-to-brittle transition (DBT) curve for the Fe-2 wt% Ni system, identifying the nil ductility temperature (NDT) relative to the stress intersection point.
summary: Representing the Fe-2 wt% Ni system, this DBT curve identifies the nil ductility temperature (NDT) where the material shifts from brittle to ductile behavior. The slope and width of the transition regime in this plot are directly correlated with the temperature sensitivity of the fracture stress shown in panel (b).

caption: EBSD orientation map of the SLM processed Fe-Ni-Si alloy top view, revealing an island microstructure formed by laser scanning in X and Y directions.
summary: Top view EBSD orientation mapping of the SLM processed Fe-Ni-Si alloy highlights a distinct island microstructure. This pattern is generated by the specific laser scanning strategy employed in the X and Y directions, demonstrating the influence of processing parameters on the resulting grain orientation and structural morphology of the alloy.

caption: Integrated AE-PN framework architecture combining AI-driven feature extraction with physics-informed modeling for end-to-end stress-strain curve prediction.
summary: This panel illustrates the integration of the AE and PN into a unified AE-PN framework. By combining AI-driven feature extraction with physics-informed modeling, the architecture enables the prediction of latent vectors that are decoded to reconstruct stress-strain curves, demonstrating robust end-to-end prediction capabilities for complex thermomechanical processing behavior.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for S1-HIP, S3-HIP, and S7-HIP specimens subjected to uniaxial tensile testing.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for S1-HIP, S3-HIP, and S7-HIP are presented to illustrate their uniaxial tensile properties. These curves provide a comparative overview of the mechanical response of the three different HIP-processed specimens under tensile loading conditions, serving as the primary data for evaluating their respective deformation behaviors.

caption: Scheil solidification curve for the HX-2TiC composite, indicating a distinct phase formation sequence where M6C forms prior to other phases.
summary: Calculated via Thermo-Calc, the Scheil solidification curve for HX-2TiC demonstrates a unique phase formation sequence compared to other samples. The simulation indicates that M6C forms first during the solidification process, highlighting how the addition of 2 wt% nano-TiC alters the thermodynamic pathway of carbide precipitation in the HX matrix.

caption: Evolution of Co K-edge XANES spectra for monometallic Co/ZrO2 catalysts during the dry reforming of methane (DRM) reaction.
summary: This panel displays the Co K-edge XANES spectra for the monometallic Co/ZrO2 catalyst. Data were collected at 0, 5, 60, and 600 minutes of the DRM reaction. These spectra illustrate the chemical state evolution of cobalt species in the catalyst system over the specified reaction duration.

caption: Temperature and resistance response of CB and CB/ZnO filled composites under applied voltages ranging from 1 to 24 V.
summary: Temperature and resistance values are recorded for TPU-B25 composites with CB and CB/ZnO fillers under varying voltages. This test ensures that the relative resistance changes observed during humidity sensing are not artifacts caused by Joule heating, confirming the stability of the sensor response across the tested voltage range.

caption: Tafel slopes derived from the polarization curves, demonstrating a decreasing trend in slope values as annealing temperature decreases under a reducing environment.
summary: Tafel slopes for the NiMo/NF electrodes are presented, showing a decreasing trend that correlates with improved HER kinetics at lower annealing temperatures. All tested electrodes exhibit slopes greater than 40 mV dec-1, which is consistent with the Volmer-Heyrovsky mechanism for the hydrogen evolution reaction pathway.

caption: Pyramid model illustrating slip systems and dislocation-twin interactions for the (0 0 1) compound twin in a BCC structure.
summary: A pyramid model demonstrates the slip systems during the interaction between an LPBF-dislocation and the (0 0 1) compound twin. This interaction results in the formation of partial dislocations δ1O and B'D (Oδ1), both possessing a Burgers vector of <10|Sc|>, where |Sc| represents the twinning shear of the compound twin.

caption: Methodological workflow outlining the systematic research approach taken to investigate the influence of printing strategies on the dynamic characteristics of additively manufactured thin-walled structures.
summary: The provided flowchart delineates the structured research methodology employed to address the study's core problem. It maps out the logical progression of the investigation, starting from the fabrication of Ti6Al4V blocks with distinct scanning strategies to the final analysis of how microstructural anisotropy impacts the dynamic performance of thin-walled parts.

caption: Crack susceptibility index (CSI) and freezing range plotted against the solidification range of the graded material, derived from Kou criterion and Gulliver-Scheil thermodynamic calculations.
summary: This plot illustrates the crack susceptibility index (CSI) alongside the freezing range across the entire solidification interval of the graded material. By integrating the Kou criterion with Gulliver-Scheil thermodynamic simulations, the graph provides a quantitative assessment of solidification cracking tendencies, highlighting the relationship between thermal behavior and susceptibility to cracking during processing.

caption: Dislocation structures identified through Dislocation Extraction Algorithm (DXA) analysis, illustrating the internal defect network within the Ni-rich model.
summary: Dislocation structures within the Ni-rich model are characterized using DXA analysis. This panel provides a detailed view of the defect network, which is essential for understanding how the material accommodates deformation and stress during the twin thickening process observed in the atomic-scale simulation.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HTHed Gyroid sample obtained at temperatures near the FM-PM transition.
summary: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HTHed Gyroid sample are shown, illustrating the magnetic response measured at temperatures near the ferromagnetic to paramagnetic transition. These measurements are critical for evaluating how the gyroid architecture influences the magnetic phase transition properties of the material during thermal cycling.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the impedance characteristics of LPBF-fabricated samples evaluated in a 0.1 M NaCl solution.
summary: Bode plots for the LPBF-fabricated samples in 0.1 M NaCl solution provide a detailed view of the impedance modulus and phase angle across a range of frequencies. These plots facilitate the analysis of the electrochemical system's response, complementing the Nyquist data to characterize the material's performance in this specific electrolyte.

caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 30% hemp content mix, showing a reduced environmental impact range with a maximum value of 0.667.
summary: The 30% hemp mixture shows a further pronounced trend in the Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. The distribution exhibits a reduced environmental impact, evidenced by a decrease in the maximum value of the range to 0.667, highlighting the effectiveness of higher hemp content in lowering the global warming potential.

caption: 3D surface topography profile of the as-received material sample.
summary: The 3D surface topography of the as-received sample is presented. This visualization provides a baseline for comparing surface roughness characteristics before the SPIF process. The profile serves as the initial state for evaluating how subsequent thermal and mechanical processing conditions influence the surface morphology of the material.

caption: Physical samples of 3D-printed hemipelvis and acetabular prostheses highlighting structural components including Trabecular Filler, Interface Filler, Shell Structure, and solid Bulk Structures with specified dimensions.
summary: This panel displays physical samples of custom orthopedic 3D-printed implants, specifically an acetabular and a hemipelvis prosthesis. The image highlights key structural components such as trabecular filler, interface filler, shell structures, and solid bulk structures, providing typical dimensions for these metal parts to illustrate the complex geometry of the prostheses.

caption: Heat-treatment cycle profile applied to coupons and toroids, illustrating the specific heating ramps, cooling rates, and dwell times required for post-processing.
summary: The heat-treatment procedure for the coupons and toroids is presented, detailing the thermal cycle including heating ramps, cooling rates, and dwell times. One coupon and one toroid for each set of process variables were subjected to this specific cycle to ensure consistent material properties across all experimental samples.

caption: K–L plots for commercial Pt/C catalyst at different potentials.
summary: The K–L plots for the Pt/C reference catalyst are presented to analyze the reaction kinetics at different potentials. These plots provide a baseline for comparing the electron transfer pathways and catalytic efficiency of the synthesized GF-CNT@Fe-Ni catalysts against the industry-standard platinum-based material.

caption: Time-dependent extrusion rate response of mortar during a double-perturbation experiment with an activated controller.
summary: This line graph illustrates the extrusion rate response of mortar during a double-perturbation experiment with an activated controller. Two replicates show over-extrusion immediately following perturbations at 150% and 200% rate increases, marked by asterisks. Recovery onsets are indicated by circles, demonstrating the system's dynamic response to controlled extrusion rate adjustments.

caption: High-speed camera sequence capturing the dynamic metal transfer process during a single CMT short-circuit cycle.
summary: This panel illustrates the dynamic metal transfer process during the CMT mode using high-speed camera imagery. The sequence captures a single short-circuit cycle, beginning at time T0, providing a detailed visual representation of the arc morphology and metal transfer behavior characteristic of the traditional CMT additive manufacturing process.

caption: Low magnification IPF+IQ map of the 1.1-Y + 1.4-Zr alloy, covering a scan area of 2456 × 2508 μm² to evaluate grain size distribution.
summary: EBSD scanning at low magnification was performed on the 1.1-Y + 1.4-Zr alloy to assess grain morphology. The resulting map, covering a large area of 2456 × 2508 μm², serves as the basis for determining the grain size distribution and structural characteristics of this specific multi-alloy system.

caption: DSC curves illustrating the thermal response of Ni–Co–Mn–Sn powders processed with varying cooling rates following SAT.
summary: This panel shows DSC curves for Ni–Co–Mn–Sn powders subjected to different cooling rates after the SAT process. These measurements are essential for determining how cooling kinetics influence the martensite transformation and austenite Curie temperatures, providing insight into the material's sensitivity to processing conditions and the resulting phase transition behavior.

caption: Proposed unit cell architectures for additively manufactured OIPLs, displaying the HV, RB, and OV lattice geometries from left to right.
summary: The proposed OIPLs are designed with three distinct unit cell architectures, identified as HV, RB, and OV lattices. These geometries serve as the foundational structural units for the additively manufactured components, providing the basis for subsequent investigations into varying cell sizes and cell numbers across the different lattice designs.

caption: Tafel voltammograms for stainless steels and nickel-based alloys tested in [EMIM][CF3SO3] electrolyte at 23 °C, illustrating the electrochemical response and passivation behavior.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical behavior of stainless steels and nickel-based alloys in [EMIM][CF3SO3] at 23 °C. The voltammograms indicate that a passivation layer forms readily on all tested alloys. These plots are essential for determining corrosion current densities and potentials, reflecting the dissolution of anodically polarized materials.

caption: Expanded view of the S0 sample resistivity showing a steady increase with temperature, fitted with a linear model.
summary: An expanded view of the S0 resistivity curve reveals a steady increase as temperature rises, approaching a linear dependence. This specific temperature variation is more clearly visible in this plot compared to the overall view, and the data is analyzed using a linear model fit to characterize the transport behavior.

caption: Magnified view of the Schaeffler diagram showing the dilution line trajectory from LCS (D=1) to SS316L (D=0), with specific positions for samples CS and A1 through A5.
summary: This magnified section of the Schaeffler diagram illustrates the dilution line connecting LCS and SS316L. Samples CS and A1 through A5 are plotted along this line, demonstrating how stepwise reductions in dilution shift the weld-metal composition away from the hot-cracking region toward the stable austenite and delta-ferrite zone.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the C14 Laves phase along the [100] zone axis, featuring distinct extra reflections aligned in the [021]* direction.
summary: Small angle CBED diffraction patterns acquired from the [100] zone axis of the C14 Laves phase reveal specific deformation characteristics. Panel d highlights the presence of distinct extra reflections that appear to lie in the [021]* direction, indicating a third observed behavior within the particle.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of 3D printed (AM) FPEA-ProGly samples, comparing the state of the material before and after the click chemistry reaction.
summary: Shown are the UV-Vis spectra for 3D printed FPEA-ProGly samples. These measurements indicate a behavior consistent with the film samples, highlighting the spectral shift induced by the click reaction with MMC in the presence of UV light and a photoinitiator within the 3D printed architecture.

caption: Compensating phase distribution map calculated for the metasurface aperture of layer 3, designed to generate an OAM beam with a topological charge of 3 at W-band frequencies.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the compensating phase distribution for layer 3 of the metasurface. Generated using MATLAB, the phase map is tailored to produce an OAM beam with a topological charge of 3. This specific phase profile provides the necessary compensation for the OAM beam at W-band operating frequencies.

caption: Time-dependent UV-vis absorption spectra of 4-NP reduction catalyzed by MoO2@C-AgNi, showing the decrease in reactant concentration over time.
summary: The UV-vis absorption spectra of the 4-NP solution are collected at various reaction times using MoO2@C-AgNi as the catalyst. The progressive reduction in peak intensity over time demonstrates the catalytic activity of the MoO2@C-AgNi composite in converting 4-NP to 4-AP throughout the experimental duration.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene nanohybrid material, illustrating the crystalline phase composition.
summary: The X-ray diffraction pattern provides structural characterization of the α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene nanohybrid material. This analysis confirms the crystalline nature and phase composition of the synthesized nanohybrid, serving as a fundamental physical characterization to identify the presence and structural integrity of the iron-based components integrated within the MXene framework.

caption: Live/dead staining images of rBMSCs cultured on composite scaffolds at 1 and 3 days, where green fluorescence indicates viable cells and red fluorescence denotes dead cells.
summary: Live/dead staining of rBMSCs at 1 and 3 days demonstrates high cell viability across all scaffold groups. The presence of predominantly green-stained cells confirms excellent biocompatibility and lack of cytotoxicity, indicating that the composite scaffolds provide a suitable environment for rBMSC survival during the initial three-day culture period.

caption: Boxplot illustrating the influence of varying PGF content on the flexural strength of composite scaffolds, showing an increasing trend as fiber concentration rises from 0 wt% to 10 wt%.
summary: This boxplot depicts the distribution of flexural strength data for PGF-PLA composite scaffolds at different PGF concentrations. The results demonstrate a clear positive correlation, where the flexural strength of the scaffolds increases as the PGF content is raised from 0 wt% to 10 wt%.

caption: Bode plot representing the impedance modulus and phase angle for as-built IN625 alloy, demonstrating high impedance values after 48 hours of salt-induced corrosion.
summary: This Bode plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance response of the as-built IN625 alloy exposed to molten KCl–Na2SO4 at 600 °C. The impedance modulus |Z| for this specimen is significantly higher than that of the forged alloy, reflecting superior corrosion resistance under the tested molten salt conditions.

caption: Impact toughness of ABS parts evaluated at different chemical treatment times.
summary: Impact toughness values are plotted against the chemical treatment duration. The results show that impact properties remain relatively unaffected by the treatment, although a slight increase in impact toughness is observed, which suggests a marginally higher resistance to brittle fracture in the treated ABS parts.

caption: Pole figure image showing the crystallographic texture of the α-phase in the TiC/Ti-alloy matrix for sample I80–V3.
summary: This pole figure image depicts the crystallographic texture of the α-phase in the TiC/Ti-alloy matrix for sample I80–V3. It offers insights into the orientation distribution of the phase, which is a key factor in determining the overall microstructural characteristics of the TiC/Ti-alloy composite.

caption: Z-score distribution for distinguishing statements associated with perspective 4 regarding C3DP growth potential and industry adoption.
summary: This bar chart displays the Z-scores for statements characterizing perspective 4, which maintains skepticism regarding the growth potential of C3DP and its ability to replace traditional construction methods. The data highlights a strong disagreement with replacement potential and a slight agreement regarding insufficient promotion due to limited human resources in China.

caption: STEM-micrograph displaying the cross-section of carbides located at a grain boundary following ion-irradiation, highlighting two distinct particles (labeled 1 and 2) characterized by unique morphological "arms".
summary: This STEM-micrograph reveals the cross-sectional morphology of carbides situated at a grain boundary after ion-irradiation. The image specifically highlights two particles, labeled 1 and 2, which exhibit distinct "arms." These specific particles were selected for detailed investigation to analyze the morphological alterations resulting from the irradiation process.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the yellow-boxed area in (m), revealing significantly coarsened carbides compared to lower tempering temperatures.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the 425 °C tempered specimen reveals a notable increase in carbide size, with particles approximately three to five times larger than those in the as-fabricated state (∼50 nm compared to ∼10 nm). This coarsening indicates significant microstructural evolution resulting from the higher tempering temperature.

caption: Three-dimensional micro-CT reconstruction of the rat skull defect site at 4 weeks post-implantation.
summary: Three-dimensional micro-CT reconstruction of the rat skull at 4 weeks provides a visual assessment of the defect site. This imaging technique allows for the systematic evaluation of scaffold implantation groups, including PCLSC3, CaSC, and SrSC, to monitor early-stage bone regeneration and structural changes within the cranial defect model.

caption: Evolution of local displacement paths for Point-A within the gamma matrix phase, showing a transition from perfect crystal (O) to stacking fault (SF) and back to the perfect crystal state.
summary: Point-A, located within the gamma matrix, exhibits a displacement path that transitions from the perfect crystal state (O) to a stacking fault (SF) and returns to the perfect crystal state. These movements are represented by colored circles in the plot, indicating slips produced by distinct sequential dislocations.

caption: Crystallographic orientation analysis of the as-built 316L steel, displaying the inverse pole figure map relative to the building direction alongside {100} and {110} pole figures.
summary: Crystallographic orientation of the as-built 316L steel is characterized through an inverse pole figure map oriented relative to the building direction. Supplemented by {100} and {110} pole figures, this analysis illustrates the texture and grain orientation distribution, which are critical for understanding the anisotropic properties of the additively manufactured component.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loop of as-cast (Fe70Ni30)85Nb0.5B14.5 ribbons showing a coercivity of approximately 40 A/m.
summary: The as-cast (Fe70Ni30)85Nb0.5B14.5 ribbons exhibit a magnetic hysteresis loop with a coercivity of approximately 40 A/m. This magnetic behavior is attributed to magnetoelastic anisotropies regulated by magnetostriction, with a coefficient of 10-15 ppm, and internal stresses resulting from the rapid solidification process used to produce the ribbons.

caption: Activation overpotentials for the 3D printed Ni–Cu electrode derived from LSV measurements at current densities of -10 and -20 mA/cm2, highlighting the lowest overpotential of 238 mV at -10 mA/cm2.
summary: Activation overpotentials for the 3D printed Ni-Cu electrode were determined via LSV measurements at current densities of -10 and -20 mA/cm2. The R2 Ni-Cu coated electrode achieved the lowest overpotential of 238 mV at -10 mA/cm2, indicating its efficiency in maintaining the reaction at the tested current densities.

caption: Two-dimensional surface roughness map of the FeS film obtained through atomic force microscopy to evaluate surface characteristics.
summary: Atomic force microscopy was utilized to assess the surface characteristics of the FeS film. This 2-dimensional roughness map provides a quantitative representation of the surface topography, serving as a critical measurement for understanding the film's texture and uniformity at the nanoscale level following the deposition process.

caption: Quantitative analysis of heterotopic ossification volume and density across four experimental groups, showing significant differences at 12 weeks.
summary: Quantitative analysis of heterotopic ossification volume and density reveals significant differences between treatment groups. While no significant difference was observed between 3D-CBD@LDN/Exos and 3D-LDN/Exos groups at 4 weeks, the 3D-CBD@LDN/Exos group exhibited a marked reduction in heterotopic ossification by 12 weeks, demonstrating the therapeutic efficacy of the scaffold system.

caption: Convergence plot illustrating the progression of three distinct optimization runs over 15 generations.
summary: This convergence plot tracks the progress of three separate optimization runs, demonstrating that the simulation successfully reaches convergence within 15 generations. The data highlights the efficiency of the optimization process, confirming that the model consistently stabilizes across all three repetitions within the specified timeframe.

caption: Elongation (EL) of Ti–48Al–2Cr–2Nb alloy specimens deformed at room temperature at loading angles of 0°, 45°, and 90°.
summary: Elongation measurements for Ti–48Al–2Cr–2Nb alloy specimens deformed at room temperature are shown for loading angles of 0°, 45°, and 90°. Notably, the elongation exhibits pronounced variation, with the value at 45° exceeding 2%, indicating significant anisotropy in the material's ductility at room temperature.

caption: Final state revealing the underlying Cr phase as the Cu nanodroplet fails to maintain a continuous spread across the IN718 surface.
summary: The final MD snapshot reveals the Cr phase exposed on the IN718 surface. Following the obstruction caused by the Nb-induced surface bump, the Cu nanodroplet is unable to fully wet the substrate, resulting in the exposure of the underlying Cr-rich regions as the droplet retracts or remains localized.

caption: Comparison of elongation, tensile strength, and hardness for FSP specimens processed under three distinct medium conditions.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of the mechanical properties of FSP specimens subjected to three different processing environments. The data highlights variations in elongation, tensile strength, and hardness, providing a comprehensive overview of how processing mediums influence the final mechanical performance and structural integrity of the FSP material.

caption: Fitness evolution curve plotted against increasing generations for the Mona Lisa pattern optimization case.
summary: This panel illustrates the performance of the inverse optimization model through the fitness evolution of the Mona Lisa pattern. As the generation count increases, the fitness curve tracks the convergence of the evolutionary algorithm, highlighting the model's effectiveness in optimizing complex target patterns.

caption: SEM micrograph and EDS elemental mapping of cast 17–4PH stainless steel, revealing significant elemental segregation at interdendritic regions, characterized by Cr, Mo, and Al enrichment and Ni depletion.
summary: Cast 17–4PH stainless steel displays pronounced elemental segregation near grain boundaries and interdendritic regions. EDS mapping identifies enrichment of Cr, Mo, and Al alongside Ni depletion, which corresponds to the formation of δ-ferrite. This compositional heterogeneity contributes to increased susceptibility to pit propagation during long-term degradation.

caption: Kissinger plots showing the relationship between heating rate and crystallization temperature for as-spun Mg70−xCe10Ni20Cux (x = 3, 7.5, 10) alloys.
summary: This panel displays Kissinger plots for as-spun Mg70−xCe10Ni20Cux alloys with varying copper content. These plots are utilized to analyze the thermal stability and crystallization kinetics of the as-spun samples, providing the necessary data points to determine the crystallization activation energy through the Kissinger equation method.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the as-cast N0 alloy showing needle-like and granular precipitates distributed within the grain interior.
summary: The as-cast N0 alloy microstructure is characterized by needle-like and granular precipitates. These features are uniformly distributed throughout the grain interior as observed in the dark-field TEM imaging. This morphology represents the baseline structural state of the N0 alloy prior to any subsequent T6 heat treatment processes.

caption: Surface roughness (Sa) measurements across five ProX DMP 200 samples, comparing values obtained at different sites using multiple instruments, with standard deviation bars representing part-to-part variation.
summary: This plot displays surface roughness (Sa) measurements for five ProX DMP 200 samples across various sites. The data reveals consistent trends, with top surfaces showing the lowest roughness (~6 μm) compared to upskin and side surfaces. Measurement uncertainty is evaluated by comparing results across different sites and instruments, highlighting variations in reproducibility.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the binary classification performance of the CNN model for detecting warping defects.
summary: This confusion matrix evaluates the binary classification performance of the CNN model specifically for warping defects. By analyzing the matrix components, the model's predictive accuracy for this defect type is determined, providing a clear visualization of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives in the classification process.

caption: Visual representation of the anti-buckling device, featuring a physical photograph on the left and a corresponding schematic diagram on the right.
summary: This panel presents the anti-buckling device designed for the test programme. It includes a photograph of the physical apparatus alongside a schematic diagram. The fixture incorporates a pair of 2 mm wide grooves specifically engineered to facilitate the installation of an extensometer during mechanical testing procedures.

caption: Piezoelectric signal bar charts for PVDF, PVDF/BTO, PVDF/PLA, and PVDF/PLA/BTO, with measured peak voltages of 25 mV, 31 mV, 42 mV, and 63 mV, respectively.
summary: Piezoelectric performance is quantified through bar charts of the measured output voltages. The results show a clear trend of increasing voltage across the materials, with the PVDF/PLA/BTO composite reaching the highest peak voltage of 63 mV, significantly outperforming the pure PVDF sample which produced 25 mV.

caption: Surface deformation morphology of irradiated high-strength nickel-base alloy X750 displaying slip bands.
summary: Irradiated high-strength nickel-base alloy X750 shows surface deformation morphology with visible slip bands. The density of these planar slip planes is significantly lower in this irradiated area compared to the unirradiated counterpart. Localized deformation in this alloy remains a key factor in understanding IASCC initiation mechanisms.

caption: Principal component analysis of macroscopic stress-strain curves from the test set, with data points colored by the L2 relative error of the predicted curves.
summary: This panel displays a principal component analysis of macroscopic stress-strain curves derived from the test set. The visualization maps the first two principal components, with individual data points color-coded to represent the L2 relative error of the predicted stress-strain curves, providing insight into the model's performance across different mechanical responses.

caption: EDX pattern and quantitative elemental composition for point A, identified as a Fe-rich precipitate such as AlFe6Si or Fe2Si2Al9.
summary: The EDX spectrum for point A confirms the presence of a Fe-rich precipitate within the H1 matrix. Quantitative analysis suggests the composition aligns with intermetallic phases like AlFe6Si or Fe2Si2Al9, characterizing the chemical nature of the precipitate observed in the FE-SEM micrograph of the material.

caption: Spatial transcriptomic mapping of the primary PDAC lesion (GSE205354) visualized via the STOmicsDB platform to illustrate the overall spatial cell atlas.
summary: This panel presents a spatial transcriptomic map of a primary PDAC lesion, derived from the GSE205354 dataset. Utilizing the STOmicsDB platform, the visualization provides an overall spatial cell atlas, establishing the structural context for subsequent analysis of cell clusters and gene expression patterns within the primary tumor environment.

caption: Raman spectra of UHS-sintered ceramic samples printed with a 0.4 mm nozzle, highlighting the evolution of characteristic D- and G-peaks under different currents.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals the presence of carbon in the UHS-sintered samples, showing the evolution of D- and G-peaks as a function of current. These results confirm the formation of well-ordered carbon features and align with the phase evolution observed in XRD, while also correlating with the specimen's darkening.

caption: Total power conversion efficiency (ηt) plotted as a function of phosphor film thickness, illustrating the performance variation across different film dimensions.
summary: This line graph displays the total power conversion efficiency (ηt) as a function of phosphor film thickness. The data illustrates how varying the thickness of the phosphor film influences the overall efficiency of the device, providing a clear trend for optimizing the film dimensions in the studied material system.

caption: Friction coefficient variation curves over time for pure resin and nanocomposite samples with 0.5 and 1% graphene nanosheets.
summary: Friction coefficient variation curves are illustrated for pure resin and nanocomposite samples with 0.5 and 1% graphene nanosheets. These curves track the dynamic evolution of the friction coefficient during testing, offering insight into the stability and consistency of the tribological response for each specific material composition under investigation.

caption: Crystallographic texture represented by (111), (200), and (220) pole figures for the SS316L sample after heat treatment at 900 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the (111), (200), and (220) pole figures for the SS316L sample subjected to heat treatment at 900 °C. The normalized XRD data highlights the crystallographic orientation changes. Min/Max values are included to quantify the texture intensity variations observed after this specific thermal processing stage.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of rectangular Ni electrodes, highlighting current density variations from 0 V to -1.2 V in alkaline electrolyte.
summary: Rectangular Ni electrodes exhibit electrochemical activity in alkaline media as shown by these cyclic voltammograms. The current density response from 0 V to -1.2 V shows a similar trend to circular Ni electrodes, providing insight into how geometry influences the electrochemical performance of the 3D printed Ni-based electrode materials.

caption: Surface morphology, power spectral density (PSD), and autocorrelation function (ACF) center-maximum values for 6082 aluminium alloy after 2.5 μm Gaussian regression filtering (GRF).
summary: This panel displays the surface characteristics of a fatigued 6082 aluminium alloy specimen following 2.5 μm Gaussian regression filtering. It presents the measured boundary area morphology, the corresponding power spectral density, and the center-maximum values of the autocorrelation function, providing a comprehensive quantitative assessment of the filtered surface topography.

caption: Indentation-induced fracture features exhibited by DED-LB deposited Ni-38Si alloy across a range of applied Vickers indentation loads.
summary: Depicted in this panel is the fracture response of DED-LB deposited Ni-38Si alloy under static, concentrated compressive loading. Using a Vickers indenter, the mechanical integrity of the material was characterized. The image captures the resulting fracture behavior, demonstrating how the Ni-38Si alloy performs under varying levels of indentation stress.

caption: Fatigue life N f as a function of hatch spacing h, demonstrating that smaller values yield a superior fatigue response.
summary: The influence of hatch spacing h on the fatigue life N f is shown, highlighting that smaller values of h contribute to a better fatigue response. The BNN model predictions, including those outside the training range marked by dashed lines, quantify the impact of hatch spacing on the overall fatigue performance.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation map of the Gd-containing alloy compressed at 1100 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ to a strain of 0.2, displaying high misorientation values in residual deformed dendrites.
summary: This Kernel Average Misorientation map at 0.2 strain reveals very high values within the residual deformed dendrites, particularly at the boundaries where they meet recrystallized regions. These high misorientation values signify significant localized plastic deformation and stored energy, which are subsequently relieved as the recrystallization process continues to progress.

caption: Misorientation map of the E2 region illustrating the distribution of grain boundaries.
summary: The misorientation map of the E2 region displays the distribution of grain boundaries within the FSAM microstructure. This visualization is essential for tracking the evolution of grain boundary characteristics, such as the fraction of LAGBs, as the material undergoes successive layers of re-stirring during the FSAM process.

caption: Line-scanning EDS spectra and corresponding cross-sectional backscattered electron image of GH3535 alloy immersed in liquid sodium at 700°C for 1500 h, indicating that Ni and Pt interdiffusion has reached a balanced state.
summary: Following 1500 hours of immersion, the line-scanning EDS spectra demonstrate that the interdiffusion of Ni and Pt elements within the coating has reached a balanced state. The backscattered electron image confirms the coating remains compact and well-adhered to the GH3535 alloy substrate without any cracking or peeling.

caption: Water droplet resting on a horizontal surface oriented in the perpendicular configuration.
summary: Captured in this image is a water droplet of 11 ± 0.5 × 10⁻⁹ m³ volume on a horizontal surface, specifically arranged in a perpendicular orientation. This setup is part of a series of ten drops processed per configuration to maintain consistency and ensure the repeatability of the experimental data.

caption: Thermographic map of the cutting zone during Conventional Machining (CM) performed at a cutting speed of 64 m/min.
summary: Representing the thermal state of the chip during Conventional Machining, this map utilizes a feed rate of 0.105 mm/rev and a depth of cut of 0.6 mm. By comparing this 64 m/min cutting speed condition to LAM, the figure highlights variations in chip temperature under different machining parameters.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image of the Ge-added alloy precipitates after 24 h of over-aging at 200 °C.
summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging characterizes the disordered precipitates in the Ge-added alloy following 24 h of over-aging at 200 °C. This panel provides a structural view of the precipitates within the Ge-modified matrix, serving as a comparison to the base and Ag-added alloy precipitate morphologies under identical aging conditions.

caption: Micro-CT cross-sectional image of a mold-cast sample showing the distribution and morphology of internal pores.
summary: This micro-CT image displays the internal structure of a mold-cast sample. Observations indicate that the pores within this cast material exhibit a predominantly spherical morphology. These structural characteristics are distinct from those found in 3D-printed counterparts, highlighting the influence of the manufacturing process on internal pore formation and geometry.

caption: Tabulated elastic property parameters utilized for defining the constitutive material model within FEA software.
summary: This table summarizes the specific elastic property parameters extracted from the mechanical characterization. These values serve as the essential input data for defining the constitutive material model in finite element analysis (FEA) software, ensuring accurate simulation of the stent's mechanical performance under various loading conditions.

caption: Creep rate versus strain behavior of the AMS alloy measured at a constant temperature of 600 ℃.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep rate as a function of strain for the AMS alloy at 600 ℃. The data characterizes the material's creep behavior, which is fundamentally dependent on the applied stress and temperature conditions during the mechanical testing process.

caption: HAADF-STEM overview of the oxide layer, highlighting three distinct regions of interest selected for detailed structural investigation.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image captures the cross-sectional morphology of the oxide layer formed on the AM alloy. By identifying three specific regions of interest, the image establishes the framework for localized high-resolution characterization, enabling a comparative study of the oxide layer's structural variations across different sites.

caption: Normalized compressive strength (σ/σs) plotted as a function of relative density for the lattice structures.
summary: Panel d presents the normalized compressive strength (σ/σs) versus relative density, featuring fitting curves derived from the Gibson-Ashby model. These curves demonstrate excellent agreement with experimental results, supported by high coefficients of determination (R2) exceeding 0.96, which confirms the model's accuracy in predicting the strength of the lattice structures.

caption: Comparison of partial pair distribution functions (PDFs) for Li–F, Na–F, and K–F ion pairs derived from ReaxFF MD at 600 °C against reference data from AIMD, machine learning force fields, and constant-potential MD.
summary: Partial pair distribution functions for Li–F, Na–F, and K–F ion pairs are presented to validate the ReaxFF MD results. The calculated PDFs are compared against established benchmarks from ab initio molecular dynamics, constant-potential MD, and machine learning force field simulations to assess the accuracy of the current computational model.

caption: Longitudinal residual stress profiles measured along the middle line of the sample top surface.
summary: Longitudinal residual stress profiles for the middle line of sample 1 show a constant 200 MPa tensile stress, which decreases sharply to 300 MPa compressive approximately 20 mm from the tip. The tip location is defined at 50 mm, illustrating significant stress gradients near the sample edge.

caption: 2PEM image of HDFs in a collagen gel at 0 h post-application of tensile strain in the strained test group.
summary: Captured via 2PEM, this image displays HDFs in the collagen gel at 0 h post-tensioning. Despite the application of a 0.05 tensile strain using the biaxial device, the cells in the test group maintain a morphology comparable to the unstrained condition, showing no immediate significant change in shape.

caption: Custom 90° raster pattern designed to align layers perpendicular to the applied load direction.
summary: The custom 90° raster pattern is shown, which aligns the material layers perpendicular to the expected load direction during mechanical testing. By removing standard borders and surface finishes, this configuration ensures that external tensile and compressive loads act primarily on the interlayers, facilitating a focused evaluation of interlayer bond strength.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction and proximity histogram for 2101-w alloy aged for 100 h at 427 °C, showing Ni-Si-Mn clusters.
summary: This panel displays an atom probe tomography reconstruction and a proximity histogram for the 2101-w alloy after 100 hours of aging at 427 °C. The observed clusters are primarily composed of Ni, Si, and Mn, exhibiting a composition consistent with G-phase precipitates, which are also identified in TEM observations.

caption: Fourier transform of k3-weighted Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra in R-space for E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 and E-Ni 0.2.
summary: Fourier transform analysis of the k3-weighted Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra in R-space reveals the local coordination environment of nickel in E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 and E-Ni 0.2. This transformation facilitates the identification of atomic scattering paths and bond lengths, highlighting structural differences between the two catalyst compositions.

caption: Coefficient of friction (CoF) evolution plotted against sliding distance for Ni-P + DLC coated disks under dry sliding conditions against Al2O3, comparing T5D, T6R_1D, and T6R_2D heat treatment conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the representative CoF behavior for Ni-P + DLC coated disks across different heat treatment conditions. The data shows that inadequate DLC adhesion can lead to topcoat delamination, which manifests as wider CoF fluctuations during the sliding distance test, reflecting the stability of the tribofilm formation.

caption: Live/Dead staining of hMSCs on cylinder design scaffolds, illustrating cell distribution and viability observed throughout the 7-day experiment.
summary: Live/Dead staining of hMSCs on cylinder design scaffolds illustrates cell distribution and viability observed throughout the 7-day experiment. The analysis qualitatively confirms a high proportion of viable cells and minimal cell death, supporting the conclusion that the scaffold facilitates statistically significant cell growth for bone implant applications.

caption: Arrhenius plot comparing experimental parabolic rate constants (kp) derived from isothermal TGA data (dots) against model-calculated values (lines) across varying oxidation temperatures and durations.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature dependence of the parabolic rate constant kp during oxidation. By comparing experimental TGA data points with model-predicted lines, the figure validates the kinetic model. These results enable the determination of Arrhenius laws for the parameters, facilitating a deeper understanding of the oxidation kinetics.

caption: Cyclic stability performance of the Ni-Co/rGO cathode evaluated at a current density of 10 A g-1 over 1300 cycles.
summary: Cyclic stability of the Ni-Co/rGO cathode is assessed by monitoring performance over 1300 cycles at a constant current density of 10 A g-1. This long-term testing demonstrates the durability and capacity retention of the electrode material under repeated charge-discharge conditions.

caption: Evolution of the mean square error (MSE) loss value during the training process of the metasurface inverse design model.
summary: This plot illustrates the progression of the mean square error loss during model training. After 500 iterations using the Adam optimizer, the MSE of the test data set reaches a value of 0.0018, demonstrating that the model achieves sufficient accuracy for the inverse design of metasurfaces.

caption: Indentation depth measurements across longitudinal sections of the alloy, with an inset displaying the macroscopic morphology of the indentations.
summary: This panel illustrates the indentation depth across longitudinal sections of the Ni46Mn33Ti17Fe4 alloy, providing a spatial representation of mechanical response. The included inset shows the macroscopic morphology of the indentations for each phase, further elucidating the mechanical property differences observed during the nanoindentation experiments performed on the alloy.

caption: Nyquist plot for L-PBF-produced NiTi alloy S3 immersed in pH 7 Hank's solution, where low-frequency diffusion impedance signifies passive film dissolution.
summary: This Nyquist plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance of the S3 NiTi alloy specimen following immersion periods of 24, 48, and 72 hours. Similar to S2, the presence of diffusion impedance in the low-frequency range confirms the dissolution of the passive film formed on the surface of the S3 alloy.

caption: Storage modulus retention plotted against temperature, highlighting the heat-deflection temperature region at 0.45 MPa.
summary: This plot illustrates the storage modulus retention as a function of temperature, providing critical insight into the material's thermal stability. Markers specifically delineate the heat-deflection temperature region at 0.45 MPa, which serves as a key indicator for assessing the mechanical performance and structural integrity of the material under thermal load.

caption: Dimension change (Δt) of neat PLA and PLA composites plotted against temperature, showing a plateau or slight increase near 100 °C indicative of cold crystallization.
summary: This panel displays the thickness change of neat PLA and its composites as a function of temperature. Each curve exhibits a plateau or slight increase starting around 100 °C, which is attributed to cold crystallization occurring within the material during the heating process.

caption: Three-dimensional cubic atomic model of the superalloy, illustrating the distinct unit cell compositions of the γ matrix phase (Ni) and the γ′ precipitate phase (Ni3Al).
summary: The three-dimensional cubic atomic model provides a detailed representation of the superalloy's internal structure. It demonstrates that the γ matrix phase is constructed from Ni unit cells, while the γ′ phase is composed of Ni3Al unit cells, establishing the foundational atomic configuration for subsequent analysis of the material.

caption: Bode phase angle plots demonstrating a decrease in phase angle from 60° to approximately 45° as immersion time increases from 3 to 14 days.
summary: Bode plots track the phase angle evolution of the Ti–Mg composite during immersion. The observed drop in phase angle from 60° to 45° as soaking time increases suggests the gradual dissolution of the protective Mg(OH)2 layer on the sample surface, reflecting the degradation of the surface film in the saline solution.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for Al-p orbitals in Ni27Al27 and Ni26Al27Cr supercells.
summary: The partial density of states (PDOS) for Al-p orbitals is compared between Ni27Al27 and Ni26Al27Cr supercells. This analysis is essential for understanding how Cr substitution at Ni sites influences the electronic bonding characteristics of the NiAl alloy, providing insight into the material's fundamental electronic structure and bonding behavior.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-printed L0 sample cross-section, highlighting the crystallographic orientation of the columnar grain clusters.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the as-printed L0 sample illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the columnar grain clusters. This map provides a visual representation of the grain structure, confirming the presence of the distinct columnar morphology observed in the corresponding SEM image of the as-printed material.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of pristine PCL compared to PCL subjected to alcoholysis at 60 °C for 24 hours.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra of PCL before and after alcoholysis at 60 °C are presented to evaluate chemical stability. The spectra appear very similar, which indicates that only minor hydrolysis of the PCL polymer occurs under these specific experimental conditions, confirming the material's relative stability during the recycling process.

caption: Level set function representation of the filament structure.
summary: This panel displays an example of the level set function used to model the filament. The function provides the mathematical foundation for defining the geometry of the filament line within the simulation framework, serving as the primary input for subsequent contour analysis and shape determination.

caption: Arrhenius plot of diffusion coefficients for Ni, Cr, Fe, and hydrogen versus temperature for a hydrogen concentration of 0.24%.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the diffusion coefficients for Ni, Cr, Fe, and hydrogen at 0.24% concentration. By plotting these values against temperature, the figure enables the identification of diffusion trends and activation energies for each species, contributing to the overall characterization of the material's diffusion properties.

caption: Cross-sectional view of a pore-free region where columnar grains advance diagonally from melt pool edges toward the center, exhibiting competitive growth.
summary: In this pore-free region, columnar grains advance diagonally upward from the melt pool edges toward the center. Competitive growth occurs in this area, suppressing adjacent grains. The resulting grain sizes are notably smaller than those observed in the vicinity of the pore, confirming the pore's role in promoting grain coarsening.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing cast-1100 and LPBF 316L stainless steel samples, including various heat-treated conditions, tested in a 3.5 wt% NaCl aqueous solution, with red arrows highlighting the superior breakdown potential observed in the LPBF-1300 specimen.
summary: This figure presents potentiodynamic polarization curves for cast-1100 and LPBF 316L stainless steel samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The data illustrates the electrochemical corrosion behavior across different heat treatments. Notably, the LPBF-1300 samples demonstrate the highest breakdown potential among all tested LPBF variants, as indicated by red arrows.

caption: Advanced continuous cooling transformation (CCT) curve generated via J-Mat Pro software to predict phase transformation kinetics during cooling.
summary: This advanced CCT curve, calculated by J-Mat Pro software, maps the transformation kinetics of the steel under continuous cooling conditions. It serves as a predictive tool to determine the microstructural evolution and phase constituents formed at different cooling rates, essential for optimizing the heat treatment processes of the experimental steel.

caption: Convergence history of objective values for Case 2 comparing DFL-TLBO and GA algorithms under various hyperparameter configurations.
summary: This panel presents the convergence history curves for Case 2, highlighting the optimization progress of the DFL-TLBO algorithm compared to GA. The visualization confirms the advantage of the proposed method by showing how different hyperparameter settings influence the convergence speed and final objective values during the optimization process.

caption: 3D CT scan image of the F0.L tensile sample showing internal defect distribution.
summary: This 3D CT scan image displays the internal defect distribution within the F0.L tensile sample. Comparison with the F0.Opt sample reveals that the F0.L specimen contains a significantly higher number and volume of internal defects, highlighting the impact of processing parameters on the structural integrity of the material.

caption: Side view of the tensegrity lattice illustrating the infinitesimal mechanism.
summary: Side-view schematic of the conventional tensegrity lattice demonstrating its infinitesimal mechanism. The initial state is depicted in blue, and the deformed state is shown in purple. This view complements the top-view panel by detailing the vertical and lateral structural shifts that characterize the lattice's response to mechanical deformation.

caption: Mass fraction distribution of elements derived from the EDS area map of the weld center.
summary: Mass fraction data extracted from the EDS area map of the weld center confirms the compositional homogeneity of the material. This quantitative analysis supports the stability of the CoCrNi-based FCC matrix, consistent with the structural observations made in the weld center region during the EDS analysis.

caption: Three-dimensional fracture surface topography of PLA 15B composite specimen following mechanical testing.
summary: This panel illustrates the 3D fracture surface morphology of the PLA 15B composite sample after mechanical testing. The image captures the specific topographical features resulting from the fracture process, enabling a comparative analysis of the failure behavior between the composite material and the pure PLA 0 control sample.

caption: Temperature versus incubation time plot for competing phases in Ti-49 at% Al alloy, demonstrating the phase nucleation kinetics.
summary: This panel displays the calculated temperature versus incubation time for competing phases in Ti-49 at% Al alloy. The plot provides a visual representation of the nucleation kinetics for the competing phases as a function of temperature, characterizing the primary phase stability regions for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of gradient materials tested in a 3.5% NaCl solution, highlighting the distinct passive region observed in the gradient 5 sample compared to other variants.
summary: This figure displays potentiodynamic polarization curves for various gradient materials in a 3.5% NaCl solution. The gradient 5 sample exhibits a unique passive region, attributed to its chromium content exceeding 16%. Overall, the solid-solution alloy elements facilitate optimal passivation and excellent corrosion resistance across the tested gradient material samples.

caption: Derivative of magnetization with respect to temperature (dM/dT) plotted against temperature during heating for the three Al-doped samples, highlighting the magnetostructural transformation.
summary: The dM/dT curves obtained during heating provide clear evidence of the magnetostructural transformation shift. The reduction in peak intensity for the Al 0.060 and Al 0.0685 samples is attributed to a more gradual change in magnetization compared to the lower aluminum content sample, confirming the composition-dependent transformation behavior.

caption: STEM HAADF micrograph and corresponding EDS elemental maps of an as-milled MA754 powder particle, illustrating the non-homogeneous distribution of alloying elements and the presence of nanoscale Y2O3 dispersoids.
summary: This STEM HAADF micrograph and associated EDS maps characterize an as-milled MA754 powder particle. The imaging reveals significant chemical non-homogeneity resulting from incomplete mechanical alloying. Notably, the Y-map highlights the uniform distribution of nanoscale Y2O3 dispersoids within the Ni-rich regions, confirming the structural state of the processed powder.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for MEX 17-4 PH samples, highlighting the correlation between raw and fitted EIS data.
summary: Bode plots for MEX 17-4 PH specimens, obtained from EIS measurements on the build direction plane, display frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle. These plots, alongside the Nyquist data, are used to evaluate the corrosion resistance of the specimens by comparing raw experimental measurements with the fitted data.

caption: Light microscopy images (top row) and SEM images of top surfaces (middle row) and cross-sections (bottom row) of ADA-GEL-MXene hydrogels, showing a color transition from transparent to grey as MXene concentration increases.
summary: Light microscopy and SEM images reveal the morphological characteristics of ADA-GEL-MXene hydrogels. The top row displays light microscopy images, where a color shift from transparent to grey indicates increasing MXene concentration. The middle and bottom rows provide SEM views of the top surface and cross-sections, respectively, illustrating the hydrogel structure.

caption: Variable importance analysis for plasma metabolites, highlighting the most influential markers for group differentiation.
summary: Variable importance analysis for the plasma metabolomics study identifies the most influential metabolites contributing to the separation of the Ti, Ti/EB 0.05, and Ti/EB 0.5 groups. This analysis highlights the specific plasma markers that are most sensitive to the experimental conditions, providing insight into the systemic inflammatory response.

caption: Strain evolution map of the HT specimen subjected to 3% global tensile strain.
summary: The strain evolution map at 3% global strain reveals the progression of deformation in the HT specimen. As global strain increases, the DIC technique highlights the developing strain localization patterns, providing insight into the material's mechanical response and local plastic strain redistribution during the tensile test.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles for Ni–Cu coated electrodes electrodeposited at -1.4 V in Ethaline ionic liquid, tested at current densities of 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, and 1 mA cm⁻².
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for Ni–Cu alloy films electrodeposited at -1.4 V in Ethaline ionic liquid are displayed. The electrodes were subjected to varying current densities ranging from 0.125 mA cm⁻² to 1 mA cm⁻². These results characterize the electrochemical performance and charge storage behavior of the specific alloy film composition.

caption: Prediction confusion matrix for the RF model incorporating missing values in the dataset.
summary: This confusion matrix displays the model's predictive performance when applied to datasets containing missing values. By comparing this matrix to the complete-data version, the impact of data gaps on classification accuracy can be assessed, providing a comprehensive evaluation of the model's reliability under less-than-ideal input conditions.

caption: Comparison of average strain-hardening rate versus yield strength for Al 6 Ti 6 alloys relative to various high-performance structural materials including FCC H/MEAs, superalloys, and steels.
summary: This Ashby-style plot compares the average strain-hardening rate and yield strength of Al 6 Ti 6 alloys against various FCC H/MEAs, Ni-based superalloys, and steels. The two-level L1 2 precipitation in the Al 6 Ti 6 alloys enables an ultrahigh strain-hardening ability combined with high yield strengths at 77 K and 298 K.

caption: Linear relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the flow stress (α σ) and the natural logarithm of the strain rate (ε ˙) at a constant strain of 0.7.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of flow stress and the natural logarithm of the strain rate. The data is derived from flow stress measurements taken at a strain of 0.7, providing a graphical representation of the material's constitutive behavior under deformation.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the linear relationship between the natural logarithm of grain size (ln Dg) and the inverse of heat treatment temperature (10^4/T) for the Ti–30Zr–5Mo alloy.
