summary: This Arrhenius plot demonstrates the thermodynamic relationship between grain size and heat treatment temperature for the Ti–30Zr–5Mo alloy. By fitting the linear data to the equation ln Dg = 12.49 - 7686/T, the diffusion activation energy Qg is determined to be 63.9 kJ/mol within the investigated temperature range.

caption: Arrhenius plot representing hydrogen trapping peak deconvolution for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 200 bar.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the hydrogen trapping characteristics for the CoCrFeMnNi-HEA material charged at 200 bar. Following peak deconvolution, the plot illustrates the individual trapping peaks identified for this high-entropy alloy. The results demonstrate a behavior similar to that observed in the 316L stainless steel samples under comparable conditions.

caption: Equiaxed grain morphology of the K4800 alloy observed after heat treatment.
summary: Equiaxed grain morphology of the K4800 alloy observed after heat treatment. The microstructure reveals large, equiaxed grains with an average size of 640 ± 53 μm. This structural characterization confirms the successful development of the desired grain architecture in the K4800 alloy following the applied heat treatment process.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the γ/γ′ interface in the 1.5Re alloy, illustrating coherent atomic alignment across the boundary.
summary: High-resolution TEM analysis of the γ/γ′ interface in the 1.5Re alloy shows that the atoms are arranged in the same crystallographic direction across the boundary. This coherent atomic alignment makes the interface boundary difficult to distinguish, reflecting the structural integrity of the phase interface under the tested conditions.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change curves for FeCoNi and Fe30Co30Ni30Cr10-xMnx alloys measured under a 3000 Oe magnetic field.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change for FeCoNi and Fe30Co30Ni30Cr10-xMnx alloys under a 3000 Oe field. Derived from M-T curves using the Maxwell relation, the results show that the maximum entropy change for the Mn-containing alloys reaches values between -1.85 and -2.24 JKg-1K-1, significantly outperforming reference cold-rolled FeCoCrNi HEAs.

caption: Pole figure of the as-deposited WA-DED VW63K alloy at room temperature, showing a weak and nearly random crystallographic texture.
summary: The as-deposited WA-DED VW63K alloy exhibits a weak and nearly random crystallographic texture at room temperature. Pole figures for this state display a maximum intensity of 2.33, which indicates minimal crystallographic alignment within the material, confirming that the as-deposited microstructure lacks significant preferred grain orientation.

caption: Mechanical force-strain curves for the W40_H20 Miura-Ori configuration featuring four cells, illustrating the alignment between experimental blue data and orange ANSYS simulation outputs.
summary: Illustrated here is the force-strain curve for the W40_H20 Miura-Ori structure with four cells. The plot contrasts experimental data, depicted as blue lines, against ANSYS simulation results, shown as orange lines, demonstrating the correlation between the physical testing and the computational model for this specific geometric configuration.

caption: Front-view strain distribution map of a PEEK sample with a stars infill pattern under 3% applied strain.
summary: Featuring the stars infill pattern, this strain distribution map for a PEEK sample is captured under 3% applied strain. The visualization contributes to the broader analysis of 3D-printed PEEK structures, allowing for a detailed evaluation of how the star-shaped geometry affects internal strain distribution and overall stress relaxation behavior.

caption: Nyquist plots and corresponding equivalent circuit fitting for the complete cell measured at open-circuit voltage (OCV) conditions.
summary: Nyquist plots representing the impedance behavior of the complete cell are presented for measurements taken at OCV. The data includes fitting results based on an equivalent circuit model, which is provided as an inset to describe the electrochemical processes occurring within the cell structure.

caption: Comparison of tensile strength values for various Al–Cu series heat-resistant aluminum alloys at elevated temperatures, highlighting the performance of the WA-DED 205B sample relative to literature data.
summary: This plot compares the high-temperature tensile strength of Al–Cu series heat-resistant aluminum alloys, incorporating data from multiple literature sources. It specifically benchmarks the WA-DED 205B sample against these established materials to evaluate its mechanical performance under thermal stress, demonstrating the relative strength characteristics of the alloy across different preparation methods.

caption: Engineering stress–strain curves comparing PLA and silk-inspired PLA-TPU printed coupons featuring a ±45° rectilinear raster pattern alongside Bouligand structures with pitch angles of 45°, 30°, and 15°.
summary: This engineering stress–strain plot illustrates the mechanical response of PLA and silk-inspired PLA-TPU coupons. The data compares standard ±45° rectilinear raster patterns against Bouligand structural architectures with varying pitch angles of 45°, 30°, and 15°, providing a comprehensive overview of the tensile performance across these distinct printed material configurations.

caption: Rate capability performance of the cell utilizing printed CPE films, evaluated across varying charging rates of 0.4, 1, 1.5, and 2 C.
summary: This plot illustrates the rate capability of a cell constructed with printed CPE films. By testing the device at specific charging rates of 0.4, 1, 1.5, and 2 C, the graph demonstrates the specific discharge capacities achieved, providing insight into the electrochemical performance and stability of the printed material under varying current loads.

caption: Cumulative strain response of HT3 annealed trabecular porous Ta, showing the relationship between cycle count and applied stress.
summary: The cumulative strain curves for HT3 annealed trabecular porous Ta are presented here, mapping strain against the number of cycles for various stress levels. This visualization allows for the assessment of cyclic deformation resistance in the HT3-treated material, demonstrating the impact of this specific annealing condition on structural performance.

caption: Three-dimensional surface morphology of the corroded Incoloy 840 metallurgical surface captured via atomic force microscopy.
summary: Captured using atomic force microscopy, this three-dimensional surface morphology image illustrates the topographical features of the corroded Incoloy 840 metallurgical surface. The visualization provides a detailed perspective of the surface degradation, allowing for a quantitative assessment of the corrosion-induced changes in the material's surface profile and roughness.

caption: Temperature gradient (G) distribution map for casting B after the melt is poured into the mold shell.
summary: Casting B presents the temperature gradient distribution after the melt is poured into the mold shell. Similar to other castings, the G value is not uniform throughout the material, demonstrating that the thermal gradient exists within a defined range rather than maintaining a constant value across the entire casting volume.

caption: Temporal evolution of current density for the STF-Ni SOC during 96-hour cycling under voltage pulses between 1.2 V and 0.85 V.
summary: STF-Ni SOC performance during the durability experiment mirrors the STF cell only during the initial cycle. A prominent decay in current density was observed specifically during the first 6 hours of operation in SOEC mode, followed by continued monitoring over the 96-hour cycling period.

caption: WPPM fit profile for the S-AB specimen, displaying experimental neutron diffraction data as black dots overlaid with the calculated model curve and the corresponding fit residual plotted above.
summary: The S-AB specimen's neutron diffraction pattern is analyzed using the WPPM procedure. Experimental data points are shown in black, with the refined model curve superimposed in color. The fit residual is displayed above the pattern, and the intensity is presented on a logarithmic scale to highlight microstructural parameters.

caption: Dark-field TEM image and diffraction pattern showing the nanocrystalline microstructure of Al88Y4Ni7Cu1 alloy ribbons after reaching the first DSC reaction temperature.
summary: Al88Y4Ni7Cu1 alloy ribbons heat-treated to the maximum temperature of the first DSC reaction show distinct nanocrystalline features. The dark-field TEM analysis, combined with the diffraction pattern, confirms the formation of nanocrystals within the amorphous matrix, illustrating the microstructural state of the alloy at this specific thermal processing stage.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the A01 film highlighting the fiber structure.
summary: The dark-field TEM image, obtained using a (200) diffraction spot with a d-spacing of 0.169 nm, displays a dense fiber structure. The individual fibers are measured to be less than 28 nm in width, confirming the fine-grained nature of the A01 thin film microstructure.

caption: Magnified bright-field TEM image of the middle film section, highlighting distinct columnar regions labeled BCC and AP, with a red arrow indicating the interface normal direction.
summary: This magnified bright-field TEM image reveals the complex microstructure in the middle part of the film. The visualization highlights the presence of alternate BCC and amorphous columns, as indicated by the labels BCC and AP. The red arrow marks the normal direction of the layer-substrate interface for reference.

caption: Microhardness profile of K447A specimens as a function of depth, comparing untreated substrate with samples subjected to LSP, USP, ULSP, and LUSP treatments.
summary: Microhardness profiles for K447A specimens show a consistent decrease with depth, stabilizing at approximately 500 μm. Treated samples exhibit significantly higher hardness than the substrate, with maximum values of 518 HV, 536 HV, 546 HV, and 568 HV for LSP, USP, ULSP, and LUSP treatments, respectively, within the 100 μm sub-surface layer.

caption: Time-temperature exposure diagram derived from steady-state temperatures and intrinsic heat treatment durations for specific layer numbers, contrasting ICS and CDS strategies.
summary: Time-temperature diagrams illustrate that earlier layers experience lower temperatures over longer durations, while later layers face higher temperatures for shorter periods. The CDS middle zone undergoes elevated temperatures for moderate durations, with exposure above 1000 °C lasting less than 0.1 hours, which is significantly shorter than conventional annealing treatments.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram for the alloy mixture containing 60% HSLA steel and 40% ASS.
summary: Representing the transformation kinetics for the 0.6 HSLA steel and 0.4 ASS mixture, this CCT diagram maps the phase changes expected during cooling. It serves as a critical tool for understanding how the addition of ASS to the HSLA steel base alters the cooling-dependent phase transformation characteristics.

caption: Photograph of the HSMZ-60 hydraulic drive linear friction welding machine utilized for joining Ni-based superalloy blocks.
summary: This photograph displays the HSMZ-60 hydraulic drive linear friction welding machine. The equipment was specifically designed and developed to join two Ni-based superalloy blocks of identical dimensions, serving as the experimental apparatus to validate numerical simulation results obtained during the study of the linear friction welding process.

caption: Voltage-time profiles comparing HP, NHP, and ICA@G/NHP scaffolds under LIPUS activation, including long-term retention data after 14 days of physiological soaking.
summary: Voltage-time profiles demonstrate that NHP and ICA@G/NHP scaffolds generate substantial alternating voltage signals compared to the HP control. The ICA@G/NHP scaffold maintains significant piezoelectric activity after 14 days of physiological soaking, retaining approximately 65% of its initial voltage response, confirming the durability of the functionalized composite.

caption: Profilometer images showing the scratch track behavior of nickel aluminide alloy processed at 50 W and 1000 mm/s in argon.
summary: Displayed are the 3D and cross-sectional profilometer images of a scratch track on laser-treated nickel aluminide alloy. The processing conditions involved a laser power of 50 W and a scanning speed of 1000 mm/s in an argon atmosphere, with the scratch performed under a 5 N load.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the as-cast Al-Ni-REM alloy with a 5/3 ratio, showing the primary presence of Al19Ni5REM3 and Al9Ni3REM crystalline phases.
summary: This XRD pattern characterizes the as-cast Al-Ni-REM alloy with a 5/3 ratio. The diffraction data indicates that the majority of the observed peaks correspond to the Al19Ni5REM3 and Al9Ni3REM phases, confirming the specific crystalline composition of the alloy under these casting conditions.

caption: KAM map of LP-DED HX specimen tested at 649 °C and 0.005 mm/mm strain amplitude.
summary: KAM mapping of the LP-DED HX specimen at 649 °C characterizes the plastic zone near the crack initiation site. The difference in plastic wake size between LP-DED and L-PBF specimens is insignificant at this elevated temperature, as the thermal conditions promote significant plastic deformation in both processed materials.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of C28/I2 cells cultured on scaffolds, showing live cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of C28/I2 cells cultured on scaffolds reveal cell viability, with live cells appearing green and dead cells red. Observations indicate minimal cell death and superior adhesion on P/G/Si samples compared to PVA and P/G groups, where higher numbers of red fluorescent cells were detected.

caption: Mean squared displacement (MSD) curves for substitutional impurities nickel (Fe87Ni12), sulfur (Fe93S6), and silicon (Fe93Si6) at 360 GPa and 5500 K.
summary: This plot compares the mean squared displacement of substitutional impurities nickel, sulfur, and silicon in iron alloys at 360 GPa and 5500 K. Sulfur exhibits notably faster diffusion rates compared to silicon and nickel, highlighting distinct mobility characteristics among these substitutional alloying elements within the iron lattice at extreme planetary conditions.

caption: S-N curve for 3D-printed PLA after 2 weeks of immersion in SBF, indicating a reduced fatigue limit of 9.1 MPa.
summary: Following a 2-week immersion in simulated body fluid, the fatigue resistance of the 3D-printed PLA specimen is evaluated. The resulting S-N curve shows a decline in the fatigue limit to 9.1 MPa, reflecting the initial impact of the corrosive environment on the material's mechanical performance under repetitive stress conditions.

caption: Thermal property performance map comparing Ni-based superalloys, SiC/SiC CMCs, alumina bulk, and nacre-like alumina ceramics.
summary: This radar chart evaluates the thermal performance indices of various materials. It demonstrates that ceramic systems, including nacre-like alumina, exhibit superior resistance to high temperatures compared to metallic Ni-based superalloys, characterized by minimal creep and corrosion, confirming their potential for use in the hot sections of turbine engines.

caption: Physical configuration of the L-CPBF experimental apparatus.
summary: This panel displays a photograph of the actual L-CPBF equipment used in the experimental work. It provides a visual reference for the physical setup and hardware configuration employed during the study, confirming the practical implementation of the L-CPBF process described in the schematic diagram.

caption: Concentration measurements of Cr, Fe, and Ni in molten chloride salt samples extracted at 500h and 2000h, obtained via Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS).
summary: This table presents the concentrations of Cr, Fe, and Ni in molten chloride salt samples, specifically for 500h-1 and 2000h exposure durations. Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) measurements indicate that all detected elemental concentrations remain significantly below the established detection limits of the AAS technique, confirming minimal metal dissolution in the salt.

caption: Relative strain distribution near the mould insert gate under a holding pressure of 275 bar.
summary: This panel depicts the relative strain distribution near the mould insert gate at a holding pressure of 275 bar. By mapping the Y-direction strain at this elevated pressure, the figure enables a comprehensive comparison with measured strain data, illustrating the mechanical response of the mould insert under the highest analyzed pressure condition.

caption: Temperature-displacement curves for as-deposited alloy 46 specimens, comparing samples oriented along the building direction (V) and the welding direction (H).
summary: This plot displays the temperature-displacement curves for as-deposited alloy 46 specimens in two distinct orientations: the building direction (V) and the welding direction (H). These curves serve as the primary data source for calculating the mean coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) values for the alloy in these specific orientations.

caption: Tensile stress-strain response of the mixed powder sample containing 25 wt% of D50: 5 μm particles added to the D50: 20 μm base powder.
summary: Presented here is the stress-strain curve for the mixed powder sample, which incorporates 25 wt% of 5 μm particles into the 20 μm base powder. This visualization allows for a direct comparison of mechanical properties between the single-sized and mixed-sized powder samples, highlighting the influence of particle size distribution on tensile behavior.

caption: Focus variation laser micrograph of BJAM fabricated WC-10Co after curing heat treatment, showing non-spherical particle morphology.
summary: This focus variation laser micrograph shows BJAM fabricated WC-10Co after curing heat treatment, characterized by non-spherical particles. By transitioning to this non-spherical morphology, capillary forces are amplified, which Kumar et al. demonstrated results in 5% to 12% greater density in the final sintered parts compared to spherical counterparts.

caption: Combined microcapillary potentiodynamic polarization and Mott-Schottky analysis of the passive layer in borate buffer solution, showing the anodic branch potential range from -693 to 832 mV SCE.
summary: This figure presents a combined electrochemical analysis of a passive layer in borate buffer solution. Mott-Schottky data reveals p-type behavior at low potentials, while a gradual capacitance decrease at higher potentials indicates n-type behavior and progressive passive layer degradation. These results characterize the semiconducting nature and stability of the layer.

caption: Dilatometric heating curves for the hot-rolled and LM steel plates, demonstrating the shift in the austenitization starting temperature (Ac1) from 717 °C to 711 °C.
summary: Dilatometric measurements during heating reveal the relative length change versus temperature for different initial microstructures. The data indicates that the austenitization starting temperature, Ac1, decreases from 717 °C to 711 °C when transitioning from a granular bainite microstructure to a lamellar martensite structure, reflecting changes in phase transformation behavior.

caption: Time-dependent cell voltage profile recorded during operation at a constant current intensity of 0.6 A using a 2 M NaCl electrolyte solution.
summary: The time course of the cell voltage is presented for a constant current intensity of 0.6 A. This measurement, conducted in a 2 M NaCl electrolyte, provides the necessary voltage stability data to complement the electrochemical production efficiency results observed during the CO2 electrolysis process described in the study.

caption: Reference model used for the dimensional analysis of the printed object.
summary: This panel displays the reference model used as the baseline for evaluating the dimensional accuracy of the printed sample. It serves as the geometric standard against which the reconstructed surface of the representative printed object is compared to identify deviations and structural inaccuracies resulting from the printing process.

caption: Collagen II/DAPI staining of C28/I2 cells showing chondrogenic differentiation markers.
summary: Collagen II/DAPI staining of C28/I2 cells is presented to visualize chondrogenic differentiation. The P/G/Si group demonstrated significantly enhanced fluorescence intensity, indicating a robust ability of the P/G/Si printing ink to promote chondrogenic differentiation. The scale bar for this microscopy image is 100 μm.

caption: Final loading stage atomic displacement map, revealing displacement deflection of atoms around the indentation site caused by shear stress flow within the shear transformation zones (STZs).
summary: This panel depicts the final stage of the loading process, where shear stress flow within the STZs triggers noticeable displacement deflection of atoms surrounding the indentation. The vector map effectively illustrates how internal shear stress influences atomic trajectories, leading to localized deviations from the previously observed symmetric movement patterns.

caption: Experimental configuration for the monotonic tensile testing of WAAM T-stub connections, featuring a 250 kN Instron 8802 machine integrated with a Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system for full-field strain measurement.
summary: The experimental setup for monotonic tensile testing of WAAM T-stub connections utilizes a 250 kN Instron 8802 testing machine. To address the undulating surface of the WAAM steel plates, a non-contact DIC measurement system is employed, providing a detailed, full-field response map of the connection during the loading process.

caption: BJ3DP316LSS gear components captured before sintering, showcasing the initial geometry and dimensional parameters.
summary: This panel presents the BJ3DP316LSS gear samples in their green state before sintering. The image provides a clear view of the initial gear geometry and dimensions. These samples were fabricated with varying coefficients of dimensional compensation to account for expected shrinkage during the thermal processing stage of the manufacturing.

caption: GMAW arc behavior at t+5.0 ms, demonstrating the stability of the concentrated arc zone.
summary: At t+5.0 ms, the GMAW arc remains short with a concentrated active area. This stability in arc behavior ensures that the heat input remains localized, resulting in a smaller molten pool volume. The concentrated nature of the arc is a defining feature of the GMAW process observed in this sequence.

caption: Partial phonon density of states (DOS) for hcp-Fe0.91Ni0.01 and Fe0.8Ni0.1Si0.1 alloys compared with the total phonon DOS of hcp-Fe, with spectra vertically offset for clarity and pressures derived from in situ unit-cell volume measurements.
summary: This plot displays the partial phonon density of states for hcp-Fe0.91Ni0.01 and Fe0.8Ni0.1Si0.1 alongside the total phonon DOS for hcp-Fe. The data, re-analyzed from Murphy et al. (2013), are offset for visibility. Pressures were determined via in situ unit-cell volume measurements, providing a comparative view of vibrational properties in these iron-based alloys.

caption: Pole figure showing the plane orientation relationship between the β-phase and the Ti2Cu intermetallic.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the crystallographic plane orientation relationship between the β-phase and the Ti2Cu intermetallic. The red circles highlight the parallel plane pairs, confirming the lattice correspondence between the two phases, specifically identifying the (1 1 0)β // (1 0 3)Ti2Cu relationship as discussed in the literature.

caption: Intensified strain concentration progressing toward the Al-Cu interface under continued tensile loading.
summary: As tensile loading increases, strain concentration intensifies and progressively advances toward the Al-Cu interface. This stage highlights the structural vulnerability of the interface region, where the accumulation of strain indicates the path of impending failure within the F-AFSD Al-Cu substrate assembly.

caption: FTIR spectra of polymer green bodies printed at 50 μm layer thickness, comparing baseline, 60% baseline, and 140% baseline energy dose levels, showing characteristic functional group peaks including C–H, C=O, C=C, Si–O–Si, Si–O–C, and Si–C.
summary: FTIR spectra for polymer green bodies printed at varying energy doses are displayed, identifying characteristic functional groups such as C–H, C=O, C=C, Si–O–Si, Si–O–C, and Si–C. These spectra demonstrate the chemical composition of the printed parts as a function of print exposure, providing a baseline for analyzing bond changes.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms (CVs) of a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) in reline deep eutectic solvent (DES) comparing the baseline (dashed line) with the addition of 50 mM Ni(II) and Cr(III) ions (blue line) at 328 K.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammograms recorded on a GCE in reline DES. The comparison between the blank electrolyte and the solution containing 50 mM Ni(II) and Cr(III) ions highlights the electrochemical response of the metal species. The scan was initiated at -0.25 V in the negative direction at 328 K.

caption: Maximum impact and pool disturbance at t = 0.2242 s.
summary: Representing the peak interaction phase at 0.2242 s, this snapshot shows the molten droplet fully impacting the pool surface. The arc current is maintained at 220 A, illustrating the intense fluid flow and morphological disturbance characteristic of the droplet impingement cycle within the molten pool during the welding process.

caption: Predicted spatial distribution of Secondary Dendrite Arm Spacing (SDAS) within the ingot cross-section under an alternating magnetic field intensity of B0 = 100 G.
summary: This panel presents the predicted spatial distribution of Secondary Dendrite Arm Spacing (SDAS) within the ingot cross-section under an alternating magnetic field intensity of B0 = 100 G. The visualization highlights the effect of higher AMF intensity on the solidification microstructure and the resulting dendrite arm spacing throughout the ingot.

caption: Experimental setup for strain sensing, demonstrating the linear sensor mounted on a finger and subjected to bending angles from 0 to 45°.
summary: The linear sensor is connected to metal wires and mounted on a finger to conduct a strain-sensing experiment. By bending the finger at angles ranging from 0 to 45°, the system measures changes in electrical resistance, validating the sensor's performance in a real-world, stretchable application.

caption: Physical flow diagram illustrating the intricate arrangement and geometry of the system under various significant parameters.
summary: This schematic provides a detailed physical flow diagram, visually representing the complex arrangement and geometric configuration of the system. It incorporates various significant parameters to define the flow characteristics, offering a comprehensive overview of the physical setup as described in the study's analysis of the system's structural geometry.

caption: Combined wear volume of CoO coating and Haynes 25 alloy measured after ball-on-flat tribological testing across varying temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the combined wear volume, including both flat surface and counterface contributions, following ball-on-flat tests. The CoO coating demonstrates superior stability with only a slight increase in wear as temperatures rise. Conversely, Haynes 25 shows a decrease in counterface wear, reaching values comparable to the CoO coating.

caption: UV-visible diffuse reflectance spectra of the TiO2 film measured in absorption mode.
summary: The absorption capacity of the TiO2 photoanode film was evaluated using UV-Vis-NIR diffuse reflectance spectroscopy in absorption mode. This technique provides critical data on the light-harvesting capabilities of the photoanode, which is essential for understanding the performance of the material when integrated with various quantum dots in the system.

caption: Large-area stitching optical micrographs displaying the top surface morphologies of as-printed bulk samples fabricated across a range of laser powers and scan speeds with a constant 80 μm hatch distance.
summary: Stitched optical micrographs reveal the macroscopic surface morphology of as-printed bulk samples produced under varying laser power and scan speed conditions. A golden yellow box highlights the optimized printing parameters, specifically 300 W laser power and 600 mm/s scan speed, which were maintained at a fixed hatch distance of 80 μm.

caption: I-V characteristic curve of the 3D-printed PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film measured between -5 V and +5 V.
summary: The I-V curve of the 3D-printed PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film is displayed over a voltage range of -5 to +5 V. The analysis reveals a low resistance Schottky behavior at room temperature, demonstrating the electronic transport properties of the composite material under the specified voltage sweep conditions.

caption: X-ray synchrotron diffractograms of the Fe-25Cr-5Mo-0.99C alloy after 100 h of isothermal oxidation at 800, 900, and 1000 °C.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns illustrate the phase evolution of the Fe-25Cr-5Mo-0.99C alloy following 100 hours of isothermal oxidation at temperatures ranging from 800 to 1000 °C. These diffractograms provide critical insights into the structural changes and phase stability of the material under the specified high-temperature oxidation conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of BTS bulk materials fabricated via the SLM process.
summary: The XRD spectra presented for BTS bulk materials, which were prepared through the SLM process, demonstrate that the crystal structure aligns with standard Bragg diffraction peaks of BTS. This confirms the phase stability of the bulk material following the additive manufacturing process used in the study.

caption: Radar chart comparing the stiffness, strength, and toughness of SQ, HC, EAM, HC-S1, HC-S2, and CAM-S composite designs.
summary: This radar chart evaluates the mechanical performance of various composite designs, including SQ, HC, EAM, HC-S1, HC-S2, and CAM-S. The CAM-S design demonstrates superior overall mechanical performance compared to the HC-S1 and HC-S2 structures, with radar chart areas that are 15.5% and 21.0% larger, respectively, indicating enhanced stiffness, strength, and toughness.

caption: High-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectrum of the IN713C superalloy, utilized for experimental phase analysis.
summary: This high-energy synchrotron XRD spectrum provides the experimental phase analysis for the IN713C superalloy. These diffraction results serve as a critical benchmark for validating thermodynamic simulations and predicted equilibrium phase compositions, ensuring the accuracy of the material's phase characterization through direct comparison with the experimental synchrotron radiation data.

caption: Ni K-edge EXAFS fitting curve for the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam, showing the second shell contribution.
summary: This panel presents the Ni K-edge EXAFS fitting curve focusing on the second shell contribution for the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam. The fit validates the structural model of the material, offering insights into the longer-range atomic ordering and the stability of the Ni-based metallic framework.

caption: Carbide phase distribution in the 0.2 mm stripe width sample, visualized through carbon isosurfaces within the nickel-based atom probe needle.
summary: This panel illustrates the carbide phase in the 0.2 mm stripe width sample using carbon isosurfaces. By mapping these features within the nickel matrix, the reconstruction facilitates a comparative assessment of carbide distribution and morphology between different manufacturing stripe widths, highlighting the impact of processing parameters on microstructure.

caption: Surface optical micrograph of the AlSi10Mg melt pool captured at a polar angle of 0°.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the surface of an AlSi10Mg specimen processed at a polar angle of 0°. The image reveals a hemispherical melt pool morphology, which corresponds to the Gaussian distribution of the laser beam power used during the manufacturing process, resulting in a symmetric and uniform melt pool shape.

caption: Projection image of the GB sample captured via phase-contrast micro-CT.
summary: This projection image displays the initial GB sample stage as captured by phase-contrast micro-CT. It serves as the baseline for the composite material analysis, providing the initial structural projection before subsequent processing steps are applied to the SiC and PR binder composite system.

caption: Stabilization temperature versus maximum applied stress for the unaged STEP_PA12_01 specimen, showing a bilinear trend and the fatigue limit identified at the intersection point of 31.8 MPa.
summary: This plot displays the stabilization temperature against maximum applied stress for the unaged STEP_PA12_01 specimen. By performing linear regression on two distinct sets of stabilization temperatures, a bilinear trend is observed. The fatigue limit for this PA12 specimen is identified at the intersection point, yielding a value of 31.8 MPa.

caption: Overview of the as-built GH4099 Ni-based superalloy microstructure captured via scanning electron microscopy.
summary: This scanning electron microscopy image provides an overview of the as-built GH4099 Ni-based superalloy microstructure. The image serves as the primary reference for identifying specific regions of interest, including grain boundaries and subgrain boundaries, which are further analyzed in higher magnification panels to reveal detailed carbide distribution and morphology.

caption: High-resolution CPD map focusing on cell boundaries, with yellow arrows indicating interdendritic regions.
summary: This high-resolution SKPFM potential map provides a detailed view of the interdendritic regions, specifically highlighting the cell boundaries with yellow arrows. The map confirms the presence of distinct potential variations at these boundaries, further supporting the observation that cell borders exhibit lower CPD values than the cell interiors.

caption: 3D rendering of VSCP sample particles following morphological opening with a 3 px radius filter.
summary: This 3D rendering displays segmented particles of the VSCP sample after applying a morphological opening operation with a 3 px radius. This processing step serves as a size filter to isolate specific particle agglomerations, facilitating the subsequent analysis of spatial distribution homogeneity for particles exceeding 3.9 µm in diameter.

caption: Single parabolic band (SPB) model calculation results for the material's electronic transport properties.
summary: Calculated results based on the single parabolic band (SPB) model are presented to characterize the electronic transport properties of the material. This simulation approach provides a theoretical framework to interpret the experimental data, offering insights into the band structure and carrier dynamics that govern the material's thermoelectric performance.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis (B-H) loops for Co79.43Ni20.57 and Co80.44Ni19.56 alloy thin films deposited on copper and tin oxide substrates.
summary: This figure displays the magnetic hysteresis (B-H) loops for Co79.43Ni20.57 and Co80.44Ni19.56 alloy thin films. The measurements compare the magnetic response of these specific cobalt-nickel compositions when deposited onto two distinct substrate materials, copper and tin oxide, illustrating the influence of substrate choice on the magnetic properties of the films.

caption: Failure morphology of the SHP-SN specimen, showing the notch boundaries in yellow and the localized plastic strain zones indicated by dotted arrows.
summary: The SHP-SN specimen failure is captured here, with yellow curve lines marking the notch boundaries. Yellow dotted arrows point to the softer regions of plastic strain localization. This visual evidence demonstrates the typical failure location and strain behavior associated with the SHP-SN processing condition under mechanical testing.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification accuracy of the CNN model across four distinct categories: stringing, cracking, warping, and no defect.
summary: This confusion matrix evaluates the CNN model's performance in identifying multiple printing defects. By mapping predicted versus actual classes, including stringing, cracking, warping, and no defect, the matrix provides a quantitative assessment of the model's classification accuracy, serving as a critical diagnostic tool for monitoring additive manufacturing quality control.

caption: High-magnification immunofluorescent view of vWF-positive HUVEC-c cells on PLCL+Amox/PVA + VEGF + LP scaffolds.
summary: This panel highlights vWF expression in HUVEC-c cells on drug-loaded scaffolds, where red arrows point to circular neovessel structures. The presence of these features confirms that the scaffold supports angiogenesis, providing a conducive environment for endothelial cells to organize into neovessels, distinct from the monolayer observed on control scaffolds.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve for CUG-LT lunar regolith simulant, illustrating thermal characteristics and melting behavior.
summary: The CUG-LT lunar regolith simulant exhibits specific thermal characteristics as shown in the DSC curve. Research indicates that titanium content influences the complete melting temperature and mass loss of these simulants. This panel provides the baseline thermal data for the low-titanium variant within the CUG regolith simulant series.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of PdNi on Ni RDE at 500 RPM in 2 M NaOH and 1 M glycerol, recorded at 10 mV s-1 across temperatures of 25, 40, 60, and 80 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms illustrate the temperature-dependent glycerol electro-oxidation reaction on PdNi catalysts. Increasing the temperature from 25 to 80 °C leads to a significant rise in peak current density before catalyst deactivation. These measurements, conducted at 500 RPM, demonstrate that the peak current density effectively doubles with each incremental temperature increase.

caption: Parity plot showing the agreement between experimental and model-calculated reduced fatigue lives for AA6082-T6 aluminum alloy specimens prepared with a 7.5% cutting clearance at R = −1 and R = 0.1.
summary: This parity plot assesses the model's accuracy in estimating the reduced fatigue lives of AA6082-T6 aluminum alloy. By plotting experimental versus predicted values for specimens with a 7.5% cutting clearance at R = −1 and R = 0.1, the figure confirms the reliability of the estimation approach for this material.

caption: Comparison of relative elongation at fracture and relative reduction of area for wrought and SLM-processed alloy 718, illustrating their comparable susceptibility to hydrogen embrittlement.
summary: This panel compares the relative elongation at fracture and relative reduction of area for wrought and SLM-processed alloy 718. The data indicates that both manufacturing methods exhibit a comparable susceptibility to hydrogen embrittlement, highlighting the mechanical performance consistency between conventional wrought material and additive manufacturing techniques under these specific testing conditions.

caption: High-resolution Ti2p XPS spectrum of the passive film surface on Ti6Al4V alloy, showing peaks at 463.94 eV and 458.54 eV corresponding to TiO2.
summary: The high-resolution Ti2p XPS spectrum for the Ti6Al4V alloy surface reveals the presence of TiO2. Specifically, the Ti2p 1/2 peak at 463.94 eV and the Ti2p 3/2 peak at 458.54 eV confirm the formation of a titanium dioxide passive film on the alloy surface.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern of the gamma phase located outside the binary phase structure.
summary: This selected area diffraction pattern captures the gamma phase located outside the binary phase structure. By comparing this pattern with the one shown in panel (c), researchers can analyze the differences in diffraction intensity and phase composition, specifically regarding the presence and distribution of gamma double-prime precipitates.

caption: Power versus temperature plot for alloy 42 specimen, displaying the Curie temperature marked as the average of the transition points.
summary: The power versus temperature plot for the alloy 42 specimen is shown in Fig. 10(a). The Curie temperature is determined by calculating the average of the two transition temperatures, which is then explicitly marked on the graph to indicate the magnetic transition point for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Unique heterogeneous unit cell structure of GSLS.
summary: This panel displays the unique heterogeneous unit cell structure of GSLS. It serves as a foundational design element for the proposed optimization strategies, which aim to improve mechanical properties and manufacturing precision by leveraging specific structural arrangements and geometric configurations within the unit cell design.

caption: EPMA point analysis of B4C-reinforced CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy composite, showing cell boundary and interior regions.
summary: EPMA point analysis of the B4C CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy composite reveals the distribution of elements across the microstructure. The analysis identifies specific regions, including the cell boundary (Point C) and the cell interior (Point D), to evaluate the partial elemental decomposition of B4C nanoparticles during the DED fabrication process.

caption: Experimental in-situ side-view image of the melt pool, showing the stable depression zone geometry that corroborates the simulated melt pool profile.
summary: Captured during the in-situ experiment, this image displays the melt pool profile from a side view. The morphology of the depression zone is consistent with the simulated results, further affirming the stability of the melt pool regime and the accuracy of the numerical model in predicting the RBP process.

caption: Two-dimensional projection of the feature map generated by the CM (CNN-1) network trained with contrastive loss on AE waveforms.
summary: This panel displays a 2D representation derived from the first two vectors of the feature map generated by the CM (CNN-1) network. The projection illustrates the lower-dimensional representation of AE waveforms learned through contrastive loss, providing a visual assessment of the model's performance in organizing the acoustic emission data.

caption: Simulated columnar grain morphology for the 11th layer at the middle position of the curved component.
summary: This simulation shows the columnar grain morphology for the 11th layer at the middle position. The model illustrates the solidification microstructure, which exhibits coarser dendrites compared to the 2nd layer, consistent with the reduced cooling rate observed at higher layers of the curved component.

caption: Compressive stress-strain behavior of pillars T1-T3, showing both experimental data and corresponding simulation results.
summary: The stress-strain curves for pillars T1-T3 illustrate the correlation between experimental testing and simulation outcomes. These results confirm the accuracy of the homogenized simulation model in predicting the mechanical response of the pillars, supporting the reliability of the calibration process across different pillar configurations during compressive deformation.

caption: Compositional dependence of α″ Ti-Nb lattice parameters at room temperature, comparing ADP-calculated values with experimental data.
summary: This panel illustrates the relationship between Nb content and lattice parameters for α″ Ti-Nb alloys at room temperature. The ADP simulation results align closely with experimental measurements, demonstrating that higher Nb concentrations or elevated temperatures facilitate a structural transition to the bcc lattice, confirming the accuracy of the ADP model.

caption: Representative dilatometry curve for a cooling rate of 40 °C/s, with critical transformation temperatures marked 1–6 based on slope changes in the dilatation profile.
summary: Representing the dilatometry curve at a 40 °C/s cooling rate, this panel highlights critical transformation temperatures labeled 1 through 6. These points are identified by slope changes in the dilatation data, which are used to characterize the material's phase transformation behavior during the cooling process.

caption: Two distinct login pop-up interfaces displayed on a HoloLens client, triggered upon the detection of networked 3D printers via QR code markers.
summary: This figure displays two examples of login pop-ups appearing on a HoloLens interface. These visual markers are triggered when the system detects a networked 3D printer via a QR code. This integration facilitates intuitive and parallel management of multiple 3D printers by identifying their physical positions and network locations.

caption: Evolution of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) values measured along the x, y, and z axes for 3 × 3 × 3 samples of the Model 1 architecture during a temperature transition from 30 to 80 ͦC.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermomechanical response of Model 1 architecture samples, specifically tracking the CTE values along the x, y, and z directions. The data, obtained for 3 × 3 × 3 sample configurations, characterizes the material's dimensional stability and expansion behavior across a temperature range of 30 to 80 ͦC.

caption: Diagram showing the designated observation positions across the additive zone and post-heat-treated additive zone, including bottom, middle, and top regions.
summary: The diagram identifies the specific observation positions used for specimen analysis. These include the bottom, middle, and top sections of both the additive zone (AZ-B, AZ-M, AZ-T) and the post-heat-treated additive zone (HTAZ-B, HTAZ-M, HTAZ-T), providing a comprehensive spatial framework for evaluating the material's microstructural evolution across different processing conditions.

caption: XRD diffraction pattern of the Au–Ge/Cu20Ni joint after 60 minutes of soldering, confirming the face-centered cubic crystal structure of the interfacial reaction products.
summary: XRD analysis after 60 minutes of soldering confirms the sustained presence of the solid solution phase with a face-centered cubic crystal structure. The diffraction pattern validates that this specific phase remains a primary reaction product at the Au–Ge/Cu20Ni joint interface throughout the extended 60-minute soldering process.

caption: Interferometry image of the AM-TS tool material disk wear scar after testing at 400 °C, showing dark areas that coincide with large valleys.
summary: This panel shows the interferometry imaging of the wear scar on the AM-TS tool material disk after testing at 400 °C. The dark areas observed in the image correspond to large valleys identified during the interferometry analysis, indicating significant surface topography changes and material wear at this high temperature.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for coatings S1 through S9 measured in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for coatings S1 through S9 measured in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These curves illustrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the various samples, providing insight into the corrosion kinetics and resistance of the coatings when exposed to the saline environment during the electrochemical testing process.

caption: STEM-HAADF image of the η-phase and matrix interface in 718Plus alloy, observed during the necking stage of tensile deformation at 704 °C.
summary: This STEM-HAADF image displays the η-phase and γ-matrix interface within the 718Plus alloy during the necking stage of tensile testing at 704 °C. It serves as a primary reference for subsequent atomic-scale imaging, FFT analysis, and GPA mapping to evaluate microstructural evolution under high-strain conditions.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots displaying the inverse square of capacitance versus potential for EB-PBF-manufactured Ti6Al4V and γ-TiAl alloys, recorded at a frequency of 1 kHz in a 0.9% NaCl solution during cathodic scanning.
summary: This Mott-Schottky analysis compares the electrochemical behavior of EB-PBF-produced Ti6Al4V and γ-TiAl alloys in a 0.9% NaCl electrolyte. The curves, measured at 1 kHz in the cathodic direction, provide insights into the semiconducting properties of the passive films formed on these materials after one hour of immersion.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the uppermost part of the third layer in sample 0–3, showing increased local misorientation levels.
summary: This KAM map of the uppermost region reveals an increased maximum misorientation level, which correlates with the higher LAB fraction observed in this area. The dense, tangled boundaries and fine equiaxed grains contribute to this elevated local misorientation, distinguishing the uppermost region from the lower parts of the sample.

caption: Absorbance spectra of a 50 mg/L methylene blue solution measured before and after 60 minutes of contact with 3D printed scaffolds in dark conditions.
summary: This panel displays the UV-Vis absorbance spectra of a 50 mg/L methylene blue solution. It compares the initial state of the solution with the state after 60 minutes of exposure to 3D printed scaffolds in the dark, illustrating the baseline adsorption performance of the materials without light activation.

caption: Minor axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for scanning strategy S5.
summary: This panel shows the minor axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for the S5 scanning strategy. The box and violin plot representation confirms that intermittent melt pool interference modes, such as S5, lead to larger average martensite sizes compared to continuous modes due to specific cooling rate effects.

caption: Room temperature X-ray diffraction pattern of gas-atomized Al0.3CrFeNiTi0.3 feedstock powders.
summary: This room temperature X-ray diffraction pattern characterizes the phase composition of gas-atomized Al0.3CrFeNiTi0.3 feedstock powders. The experimental spectrum serves as a critical validation tool, providing an empirical interpretation of the theoretical phase predictions previously derived from CALPHAD and Scheil simulations to confirm the material's structural state.

caption: Stress-strain performance curve for a PLA specimen constructed with a spinner-patterned infill.
summary: Presented is the stress-strain curve for a PLA specimen with a spinner-patterned infill. This mechanical test data reflects the material's strength and ductility. The study concludes that the look-ahead trajectory planning algorithm significantly improves the ultimate tensile strength of PLA specimens compared to the 17–4PH stainless steel specimens tested.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the investigated samples measured in Hank's solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the electrochemical behavior of the investigated samples when tested in Hank's solution. These curves provide essential data regarding the corrosion resistance of the materials, serving as a primary indicator of their performance in physiological environments as described in the experimental analysis of the study.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for NiTi-xNb alloys sintered at 1050 °C, where B19′ NiTi phase peaks remain detectable.
summary: Depicted here is the XRD pattern for NiTi-xNb alloys sintered at 1050 °C. Consistent with the lower temperature sintering results, the characteristic peaks of the B19′ NiTi phase are observed. This confirms that the B19′ phase persists in the alloy microstructure at this specific sintering temperature.

caption: Technical drawing of the tensile test specimens with dimensions provided in millimeters, machined from as-deposited blocks.
summary: The technical drawing details the dimensions of the tensile specimens used for mechanical testing. These specimens were machined from as-deposited blocks measuring 20 by 20 by 60 mm, ensuring standardized geometry for evaluating the mechanical properties of the material according to the specified dimensions shown in the diagram.

caption: IWP-type TPMS unit cell geometry depicted in its conventional cubic state (top) and as a tetrahedral segment (bottom) after Boolean processing.
summary: IWP-type TPMS unit cells are shown in both conventional cubic and tetrahedral segment forms. The tetrahedral segments are produced by a Boolean operation that retains only the solid material within a regular tetrahedron, enabling the construction of Level 2 cell hierarchies through coordinate transformation and reassembly into triangulated cubes.

caption: 31P MAS NMR spectrum of the 0.05 HAPA-CN sample, characterizing the phosphorus chemical environment.
summary: The 31P MAS NMR spectrum specifically characterizes the phosphorus environment within the 0.05 HAPA-CN sample. This spectroscopic analysis is essential for confirming the successful incorporation of phosphorus from the phytic acid precursor into the carbon nitride matrix, providing insight into the local bonding configuration of the dopant atoms.

caption: Ortho view of the R-Octet metamaterial model with a rotational degree of 30° (R-Octet-30).
summary: The R-Octet-30 model is presented in an ortho view, incorporating a 30° rotational degree between the upper and lower layers. This specific twist angle represents a variation in the bio-inspired design, allowing for the systematic study of how rotational degrees influence the metamaterial's structural and mechanical behavior.

caption: Measured reflection coefficient (S11) plotted against frequency for the cylindrical form FESA.
summary: This panel illustrates the measured reflection coefficient (S11) for the cylindrical form FESA. The plot provides critical data regarding the antenna's frequency response. When analyzed alongside simulated results, this measurement confirms the reflection behavior of the cylindrical geometry, allowing for a direct comparison of performance between the two antenna forms.

caption: Chemical composition data presented as the fraction of various oxides present in the HUST-2 lunar regolith simulant, determined through X-ray fluorescence spectrometry.
summary: The chemical composition of the HUST-2 lunar regolith simulant is quantified by determining the fraction of constituent oxides. This analysis was performed using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry, providing a precise breakdown of the elemental oxide content that defines the chemical makeup of the simulant material.

caption: Linear polarization curves for the three alloy electrodes, illustrating the charge transfer rate at the electrode surface.
summary: Linear polarization test curves for the La3MgNi14, La2.5Y0.5MgNi14, and La2YMgNi14 alloys are presented. These curves illustrate the charge transfer rate at the electrode surface, providing essential data on the electrochemical kinetics and surface reactivity of the different alloy compositions under linear polarization conditions.

caption: Droplet spatter event observed during the LPBF process, denoted by a pink dotted circle.
summary: Droplet spatter is captured during the laser powder bed fusion of the CuSn10 alloy, as indicated by the pink dotted circle. This event is one of the key spatter mechanisms documented through high-speed imaging, providing insight into the complex material dynamics and mass transport occurring within the molten pool region.

caption: Projection of printed object samples onto the PCA model established in panel (a), showing the formation of a third data cluster.
summary: Projection of printed object samples onto the PCA model established in panel (a), showing the formation of a third data cluster. This new group overlaps with both the inside and outside raw filament sample groups, although it exhibits a higher degree of overlap with the inside sample group.

caption: Square wave voltammetry responses of MN sensor arrays secured via a subcutaneous metallic plate, demonstrating robust and stable signal retention.
summary: Magnetic placement of MN sensor arrays using a subcutaneous metallic plate ensures robust retention of sensor signals throughout the entire measurement period. This approach maintains consistent electrochemical performance, as evidenced by stable square wave voltammetry outputs, effectively overcoming the disinsertion issues observed with tape and glue-based attachment methods.

caption: Response surface plot representing the Type-II meltpool width behavior with respect to hatch spacing (h) set at 0.1 mm.
summary: This response surface plot visualizes the quadratic relationship between hatch spacing and Type-II meltpool width at a fixed interval of 0.1 mm. The plot clearly demonstrates how process parameters dictate meltpool width, distinguishing these results from Type-I behavior and supporting the identification of optimal processing conditions.

caption: Neutron transmittance of fabricated alloys as a function of thickness under 1 eV incident neutron energy.
summary: The neutron transmittance of the fabricated alloys is plotted against increasing thickness for an incident energy of 1 eV. At this energy level, the shielding advantage previously observed in Gd-containing alloys begins to weaken, resulting in more similar linear absorption coefficients across the different alloy compositions tested in this study.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the A550 sample, indicating that the precipitates are enriched in Zr and Al while depleted in Ti and Nb.
summary: EDS analysis of the A550 sample provides chemical characterization of the observed precipitates. The results show that these needle-like precipitates are enriched in Zr and Al elements, while they are simultaneously depleted in Ti and Nb compared to the surrounding matrix, confirming their distinct chemical composition relative to the bulk material.

caption: Microhardness profile measured across the building direction within the cross-section of the functionally graded materials (FGMs) component.
summary: This plot illustrates the gradient change of microhardness values along the building direction in the cross-section of the FGMs component. By mapping the hardness across the deposition layers, the figure demonstrates the mechanical transition and structural variation inherent in the functionally graded material design, highlighting the specific hardness distribution achieved.

caption: Magnesium elemental distribution map obtained via EDS for the AZ91D alloy wear track at 10 N.
summary: The magnesium elemental distribution map for the AZ91D alloy wear track at 10 N provides insight into the surface composition. This map, alongside oxygen and aluminum data, confirms the formation of MgO and a thin oxide layer in the vicinity of the wear track during the testing process.

caption: Atomic configurations of ferromagnetic (FM) and antiferromagnetic (AFM) states for single-layer (SL) GeN, SnN, and PbN within a 2 × 2 supercell.
summary: This panel illustrates the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic magnetic configurations for single-layer GeN, SnN, and PbN using a 2 × 2 supercell model. By comparing the total energy differences between these configurations, the study confirms that all investigated single-layer XN materials possess a ferromagnetic ground state.

caption: HRTEM analysis of the microstructure at position 3, detailing the atomic arrangement and phase characteristics within the corroded layer.
summary: HRTEM analysis at position 3 provides high-resolution insights into the microstructural features of the corroded 316L surface. This examination of the atomic arrangement and phase characteristics contributes to a broader understanding of how the material's surface evolves under LBE corrosion conditions, specifically regarding the formation of oxide layers and precipitates.

caption: Current density versus voltage (J-V) characteristics of photovoltaic cells encapsulated with pure COC and various COCA coversheets under direct sunlight illumination.
summary: This panel displays the J-V characteristics of solar cells using pure COC and COCA coversheets under direct sunlight. The COCA3 sample achieves a peak power conversion efficiency of 17.21%. Increasing the alumina content in the COCA4 sample results in a 15.9% decrease in efficiency compared to the optimal configuration.

caption: Cross-sectional SEM image of the C3TAu32 sample accompanied by an EDX table detailing elemental composition at specific points.
summary: The SEM image of C3TAu32 shows gold particles distributed in the TiO2 layer and an interface layer. The EDX table confirms high oxygen and trace gold at points 1 and 2, while point 3 indicates 3.8% gold enrichment at the interface, demonstrating the successful incorporation of gold within the oxide layer.

caption: Binary phase diagram for the Fe-Mo system showing temperature versus composition.
summary: The Fe-Mo binary phase diagram maps the equilibrium phase fields for the iron-molybdenum system across a range of temperatures and compositions. It provides a comprehensive overview of the thermodynamic stability of different phases, facilitating the analysis of alloying effects and phase transformations in molybdenum-containing iron alloys.

caption: Deconvoluted Raman spectrum of the PEO Ce 2 sample before immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel shows the deconvoluted Raman spectrum for the PEO Ce 2 sample before immersion. Deconvolution of the spectral data allows for a deeper insight into the specific vibrational modes and chemical behavior of amorphous cerium within the PEO layer, establishing a clear reference for pre-corrosion structural analysis.

caption: Calculated weight fractions of elements in the liquid phase plotted against the solid fraction, distinguishing between coarse gamma-prime precipitates formed during solidification and those formed during subsequent cooling.
summary: This plot displays the evolution of elemental weight fractions within the liquid phase as solidification progresses, calculated using the Scheil model. It distinguishes between the coarse gamma-prime phase precipitated during solidification and the secondary gamma-prime phase that forms from the gamma matrix during the final cooling process, highlighting the complex microstructural evolution.

caption: Calculated enthalpy values for the amorphous, disordered bcc-A2, and ordered bcc-B2 phases in the Ni-50Ti-Cu ternary system at 773 K, plotted as a function of copper content.
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated enthalpy of the amorphous phase, disordered bcc-A2, and ordered bcc-B2 phases for the Ni-50Ti-Cu ternary system at 773 K. It provides a thermodynamic comparison of these phases as a function of copper content, establishing the baseline energy states for the system under these specific conditions.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of VG material at low resolution, accompanied by a high-resolution inset showing the internal microstructure.
summary: VG material is characterized via scanning electron microscopy at both low and high resolutions. The low-resolution image provides an overview of the material's morphology, while the high-resolution inset, featuring a 50 µm scale bar, allows for the detailed examination of the internal structural features and filler distribution within the VG sample.

caption: Temporal evolution of the coefficient of friction (COF) for synthetic fluids (SFs) modified with graphene (G), Ti3C2Tx, and hybrid G-Ti3C2Tx additives at varying concentrations.
summary: This plot displays the representative temporal evolution of the coefficient of friction for various lubricant formulations. It illustrates the dynamic response of SFs when supplemented with G, Ti3C2Tx, and hybrid G-Ti3C2Tx additives at concentrations of 0.5, 2, and 10 mg/mL, providing a clear visualization of the friction behavior over time.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of Ni56Ti36Hf8 alloy solution-annealed at 1050 °C and water-quenched, featuring an inset SAED pattern with weak super reflections along 1/3<011>.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of Ni56Ti36Hf8 after solution annealing at 1050 °C and water quenching. The inset SAED pattern reveals faint super reflections along the 1/3<011> direction, which are attributed to three distinct variants of H-phase precipitates, indicating a low volume fraction of these fine features.

caption: Normalized confusion matrix illustrating class-wise detection accuracy and misclassifications for the crack detection model at the default confidence threshold.
summary: This normalized confusion matrix provides a qualitative assessment of the crack detection model's performance. It visualizes class-wise detection accuracy and identifies specific instances of misclassification at the default confidence threshold. These results complement the quantitative statistical indicators, such as precision, recall, and F1-score, derived from the raw detection counts.

caption: Numerical simulation of the laser scanning strategy and temperature field cloud map for a horizontal cross-section of Ti–6Al–4V at a 0° rotation angle.
summary: Numerical simulation of the laser scanning strategy and temperature field cloud map for a horizontal cross-section of Ti–6Al–4V at a 0° rotation angle. This visualization depicts the thermal distribution during the selective laser melting process, providing insight into the thermal history and potential microstructural development within the fabricated metal sample.

caption: Linear extrapolation plot of minimum creep rate versus normalized stress for upper limit data, assuming a stress exponent of n = 4.
summary: This plot displays the linear extrapolation of minimum creep rate against normalized stress for upper limit data, assuming n = 4 to represent dislocation climb mechanisms. The x-axis intercept provides the normalized threshold stress values at 800, 900, and 1000 °C, calculated as 2.12 × 10⁻⁴, 7.43 × 10⁻⁵, and 1.95 × 10⁻⁵, respectively.

caption: Conceptual framework of the RKM version 1 for WAAM, illustrating the hierarchical clustering of knowledge domains including environment, deposition handles, part state, and evaluation metrics.
summary: This schematic presents the initial version of the RKM for WAAM, organizing knowledge into distinct clusters. It categorizes concepts into WAAM environment, deposition handles, part current state—covering geometrical, mechanical, and thermal properties—and evaluation concepts, which are further divided into process and part evaluation metrics for systematic knowledge elicitation.

caption: Circular dichroism spectra of MPL-MFGMP, EYL-MFGMP, and SL-MFGMP complexes subjected to varying ultrasonic conditions.
summary: Circular dichroism spectra are presented for MPL-MFGMP, EYL-MFGMP, and SL-MFGMP complexes under different ultrasonic treatment conditions. These spectroscopic measurements characterize the secondary structure of the ultrasound-treated PL-MFGMP complexes, providing insight into the conformational changes induced by the ultrasonic processing of these specific protein-polysaccharide complexes.

caption: Fatigue life distribution relative to fracture location for interrupt group specimens, with pause and interrupt locations marked by dashed and solid lines, respectively.
summary: Interrupt group specimens demonstrate strong clustering of failures near the unplanned interruption site. While the pause location shows no apparent influence on failure, specimens failing near the interrupt are identified as having failed from lack-of-fusion defects, with an average defect square root area of 213 μm and fatigue life of 2.91 × 10^5 cycles.

caption: Voltage efficiency (VE) profiles for V 3.5+ - Electrolysis, V 3.5+ - Pd/C, and V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) evaluated at current densities between 80 and 160 mA cm -2.
summary: Voltage efficiency (VE) decreases across all tested vanadium systems as the current density is elevated from 80 to 160 mA cm -2. Similar to the energy efficiency trends, this decline is driven by increasing overpotential and ohmic losses, reflecting the electrochemical limitations of the materials at higher current loads.

caption: EELS elemental intensity profiles across the matrix/precipitate interface, demonstrating the enrichment of carbon within the precipitated phase.
summary: EELS profiles show that at the precipitated phase/matrix interface, the intensities of Zr and B are low, while the intensity of C increases sharply. This confirms the strong enrichment of C in the precipitated phase, providing essential compositional data regarding the healing phase formed during the 750 °C/350 MPa fracture test.

caption: Two-dimensional PCA reduction of the acoustic emission dataset, overlaid with a fitted Gaussian mixture model for online defect detection.
summary: Principal component analysis was applied to reduce the dimensionality of the acoustic emission dataset. The resulting 2D projection is shown with a fitted Gaussian mixture model, which enables rapid, automated online defect detection by clustering signal features and facilitating the classification of various defect types within the H13 steel samples.

caption: Logarithmic plot of steady-state creep rate versus stress for the second creep experiment, used to determine the stress exponent.
summary: This log-log plot displays the steady-state creep rate against stress for the second creep experiment. The data points allow for the calculation of the stress exponent (n), providing insight into the creep behavior of the Nb-silicide alloy and confirming the consistency of the mechanical testing results across different experimental runs.

caption: Quantitative chemical composition analysis results derived from the SEM-EDX spectrum of the blade.
summary: This table presents the quantitative chemical composition analysis derived from the SEM-EDX data. By averaging the composition across the dendritic and inter-dendritic areas observed in the microstructure, these results provide a comprehensive overview of the elemental distribution within the blade, confirming the material's chemical makeup following the crystallization process.

caption: Reaction force (F R) versus time curves comparing the mechanical response of a single-branch HETENG before and after 20,000 fatigue cycles.
summary: Mechanical energy dissipation and device response were evaluated by comparing reaction force versus time curves before and after a 20,000-cycle fatigue test. Testing under 10 mm/s rate and 150 mm displacement revealed negligible changes in the mechanical behavior, confirming the structural integrity and consistent energy dissipation characteristics of the HETENG.

caption: False height color map of the Scr scenario extracted from STL data.
summary: Presented here is a false height color map corresponding to the Scr scenario. Extracted from STL data, this visualization highlights the surface topography and structural features characteristic of the Scr condition, illustrating the specific morphological details observed in the experimental analysis of this scenario.

caption: Fluorescence decay curve and biexponential fitting analysis for TPU/5 C composite.
summary: The TPU/5 C composite displays a nonlinear fluorescence decay curve monitored at 465 nm. This decay behavior is evaluated through a biexponential fitting function, allowing for the determination of the fluorescence lifetime for the highest coumarin concentration sample within the TPU composite series at room temperature.

caption: Detailed HAADF-STEM micrograph showing the morphology of intermetallic compounds within area X.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph provides a clear view of the intermetallic compounds located in area X. By utilizing high-angle annular dark-field imaging, the panel effectively captures the structural characteristics of the intermetallic phases, contributing to the overall microstructural characterization of the material under investigation.

caption: Three-dimensional laser scan reconstruction illustrating the overall geometric distortion of the specimen following the unclamping process.
summary: This 3D reconstruction, generated using a FARO Scan Arm laser scanner, provides a comprehensive visualization of the specimen's distortion profile. By capturing the surface geometry after the unclamping stage, the scan allows for a precise assessment of the dimensional changes and structural deviations resulting from the manufacturing or processing conditions.

caption: Enlarged morphology of gas pores in the Al-Ce-Mg alloy specimen following 3% tensile strain.

caption: Structural changes on prediction results, illustrating the combined influence of unexpected process events and geometric modifications on the interlayer infrared radiation intensity sequence features.
summary: This panel illustrates the combined effect of unexpected events and structural changes on the IIRI sequence features. caption: Overview of the concrete 3D printing process, illustrating the operational workflow and material flow through the system.
summary: The diagram depicts the overall operational principle of the concrete 3D printing process. caption: Cycling performance and Coulombic efficiency of TPU-LFP MSEs, demonstrating capacity retention before and after 50 stretch-release cycles.

summary: Upon heating to 1000 °C, the O 1s XPS spectrum of the NiTi powder shows that the lattice oxygen (O 2−) peak becomes the dominant feature. caption: Charge density difference distribution on the (010) lattice plane of the γ′/γ″ interface with a substituted Ir alloying atom at the γ-Ni-fc site.
summary: This panel shows the DFT-calculated charge density difference distribution on the (010) lattice plane of the γ′/γ″ interface. caption: Charge and discharge voltage curves for the conventional ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode tested at current rates ranging from 0.1C to 10C.
summary: The charge and discharge curves for the ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode are shown across current rates from 0.1C to 10C. caption: Specific wear rates of neat PEEK and PEEK composites measured during dry sliding and water-lubricated tribological tests.
summary: Specific wear rates for neat PEEK and PEEK composites are illustrated in this panel. The data compares the material degradation performance across dry sliding and water-lubricated environments. These results provide a quantitative assessment of the wear resistance for the different PEEK-based materials under the specified tribological testing conditions.

caption: Predicted as-cast grain sizes for Al-xZn-2Mg-2Cu alloys (x=2–12) inoculated with varying amounts of Al-5Ti-1B master alloy, validated against 30 experimental cases.
summary: This plot presents as-cast grain size predictions for a series of Al-xZn-2Mg-2Cu alloys with varying zinc content and Al-5Ti-1B inoculation levels. caption: Scanning electron micrograph of the NiAl-Ta-Cr alloy containing 2.5 at.-% Ta, revealing the initial microstructural state.
summary: This scanning electron micrograph displays the microstructure of a NiAl-Ta-Cr alloy with a 2.5 at.-% Ta composition. caption: Digital image correlation strain map of the CR30%/A500°C-1h sample at the tenth cycle, showing localized strain concentration.
summary: The DIC strain map for the CR30%/A500°C-1h sample at the tenth cycle reveals localized strain concentration. caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph obtained using reflection 1, revealing bright clusters and dark fringes within the Ni-Mn-Ga microstructure.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging using reflection 1 reveals distinct bright clusters and dark fringes within the Ni-Mn-Ga sample. These features are directly associated with the extra peaks and scattering observed in the diffraction patterns, providing insight into the microstructural characteristics of the as-built material.

caption: Designed 3D model of the 3 × 3 × 3 RD structure array.
summary: The 3D model shows a 3 × 3 × 3 arrangement of the rhombic dodecahedron unit cells. This lattice configuration is used to compare the performance of the RD design against the TO structure. caption: Enlarged transmission electron microscopy image capturing the Moiré pattern observed in the material at an elevated temperature of 400 °C.
summary: This enlarged TEM image displays the Moiré pattern formed at 400 °C. The visualization provides a detailed view of the lattice superposition within the Moiré region. caption: FTIR spectrum of the final synthesized microcapsule, identifying distinctive absorption peaks corresponding to the shell and core components.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of the synthesized microcapsule displays distinctive peaks that characterize both the shell and core components. caption: Normalized elastic modulus (E¯) plotted against relative density (ρ¯) for bioinspired rhombic nested lattices (RNLs) compared to conventional strut-based and surface-based lattice architectures.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the mechanical performance of RNLs by comparing their normalized elastic modulus against relative density. caption: Tafel slopes derived from HER polarization data for different Ni-Co alloy compositions, indicating the reaction kinetics.
summary: Tafel slopes for various Ni-Co alloys are presented to characterize the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction. These slopes provide insight into the electrocatalytic efficiency of the materials, complementing the LSV data obtained from linear sweep voltammetry measurements conducted in 1 M KOH solution.

caption: Geometric representation of the Aspect Ratio calculation for an irregular particle, defined by the ratio of the feret length to the feret width.
summary: The Aspect Ratio is calculated using the feret length, representing the largest particle dimension, and the feret width, representing the shortest dimension. caption: Energy absorption histogram showing the material's behavior throughout four repetitive compression cycles at an 80% compression ratio.
summary: This histogram depicts energy absorption during four repetitive compression cycles at an 80% compression ratio. caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of Ti particles in the AA condition showing grain orientation.

caption: Monolayer atomic arrangement of the deposited surface showing island-like structural features.
summary: This panel displays the monolayer atomic arrangement of the deposited surface. caption: WDS elemental mapping of Aluminum distribution in the HVOF 1 coating, revealing segregation and faint outlines of the lamellar structure.

caption: Neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain ε22 in a cold-machined specimen.
summary: Residual elastic strain ε22 for the cold-machined part is presented, as measured by neutron diffraction.
