caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 450 °C, highlighting the relative intensities of detected solutes.
summary: This panel shows the normalized mass spectrum for Inconel 718 samples tested at 450 °C. caption: JuggerBot 3D Tradesman P3–44 printer employed for large-format additive manufacturing.
summary: The JuggerBot 3D Tradesman P3–44 printer is presented as a key piece of equipment for printing full-size bat houses. caption: CCK-8 proliferation assay results for BMSCs and Ea.hy926 cells cultured on various sample surfaces over 1, 3, 5, and 7 days.
summary: The CCK-8 assay evaluates the proliferation kinetics of BMSCs and Ea.hy926 cells across different experimental groups. caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of human pre-osteoblasts stained for viability after seven days of cultivation on β-TCP foam, β-TCP/ZrO2 hybrid scaffolds, and control surfaces.

caption: Long-term cycling stability of the rGO aerogel, showing capacitance retention measured over 10,000 charge-discharge cycles at a constant current density of 10 A g-1.

summary: Absolute errors for two distinct S–P stress prediction models are plotted within the 95% confidence interval. This visualization allows for a direct assessment of how the inclusion of PC features influences the magnitude and consistency of prediction errors compared to a model relying solely on physical input features.

caption: Compensated all-pixel-on input image using a radial function and the resulting projected blue light profile.
summary: This panel presents the results of applying a radial function compensation method to the all-pixels-on input. By adjusting the input image, the resulting projected blue light profile at the vat platform shows enhanced accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of the radial compensation approach in correcting projection system distortions.

caption: Predicted evolution of Nb and Mo mass fractions in the FCC phase for the DED-B specimen as a function of the solid mass fraction, highlighting the similarity in partitioning compared to DED-A.
summary: Panel b illustrates the solute partitioning of Nb and Mo for the DED-B build during solidification. The data, generated via Scheil calculations, confirms that solute segregation behavior remains consistent across different DED builds, matching the trends observed in DED-A and supporting the validity of the thermodynamic modeling approach used.

caption: Raman spectrum of 3Cr+1Ni+0.5Mo steel exposed to CO2-saturated NaCl solution at 180 °C for 6 hours.
summary: This Raman spectrum represents the corrosion products on 3Cr+1Ni+0.5Mo steel after 6 hours of immersion in a CO2-saturated NaCl solution at 180 °C. The data is used to determine the composition of inner-layered films that remain undetected by XRD, facilitating a detailed understanding of the high-temperature corrosion mechanism.

caption: Calculated glass formation range for the Ni–Ti–Ta ternary system.
summary: This panel illustrates the calculated glass formation range for the Ni–Ti–Ta system. Thermodynamic calculations indicate that while the Ti–Ta system is immiscible with Ni, the addition of specific Ni concentrations alters atomic size and electron distribution, facilitating glass formation as predicted by Inoue's rules and the Miedema model.

caption: Power parameter validation as a function of build plate location, showing Batch 1 and Batch 2 distributions with ±3σ confidence intervals from Monte-Carlo simulation.
summary: Power parameter validation is presented relative to build plate location, incorporating ±3σ confidence intervals from Monte-Carlo simulations. The results demonstrate that even with identical manufacturing parameters, the ultrasound-captured variation differs based on sample placement, confirming that the build plate location plays a critical role in the overall manufacturing process.

caption: Capacitance retention of the CHBAC device over 10,000 cycles at a current density of 0.2 A g-1, with the inset displaying the equivalent series resistance (ESR) measured at 2,000-cycle intervals.
summary: The CHBAC device demonstrates stable cycling performance, maintaining its capacitance over 10,000 cycles at a current density of 0.2 A g-1. The inset provides additional insight into the device's electrochemical stability by showing the equivalent series resistance (ESR) values recorded at regular intervals throughout the testing period.

caption: Calculated concentration profiles for diffusion couple H4 annealed at 1073 K for 50 h, contrasting predictions from current mobility parameters (solid line) and ref. [20] (dash-dot line) with experimental literature values [53].
summary: Composition profiles for diffusion couple H4 are predicted using the atomic mobilities developed in this work and compared against literature ref. [20] and experimental measurements. These profiles, generated after 50 h of annealing at 1073 K, indicate that the current model provides a reasonable agreement with the experimental data reported in the literature.

caption: Al 2p XPS spectrum of the PN-545 sample, fitted into three peaks including AlN at 74.8 eV and Al2O3 at 76.9 eV.
summary: The Al 2p XPS spectrum for the PN-545 sample is fitted into three peaks to resolve the chemical composition after friction testing. Binding energies of 74.8 eV and 76.9 eV are identified, corresponding to the AlN phase and Al2O3, respectively, reflecting the surface chemistry changes induced by the seawater friction.

caption: 2D detector image and corresponding azimuthally integrated diffractogram for the ST condition specimen.
summary: The ST condition specimen is characterized using high-energy X-ray diffraction. Panel (a) displays the raw 2D detector image alongside the azimuthally integrated diffractogram, providing structural information derived from the synchrotron diffraction analysis. These results are part of the comprehensive HE-XRD investigation conducted to evaluate the material's structural state.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of CT-26 cells stained for viability after exposure to MGO-PEG-CET/DOX under magnetic targeting, where green denotes live cells and red indicates dead cells.
summary: Live/Dead staining of CT-26 cells reveals the efficacy of MGO-PEG-CET/DOX under magnetic guidance. The fluorescence microscopy image shows a distinct spatial distribution of cell viability, with green representing live cells and red representing dead cells, confirming the targeted therapeutic effect of the nanocarrier system within the magnetic zone.

caption: Tan δ rheological thermogram showing a secondary peak emergence near 130 °C.
summary: This panel displays the tan δ rheological thermogram, which characterizes the material's viscoelastic damping properties as a function of temperature. A notable feature is the observation of a second peak in the tan δ curve, which begins to manifest at approximately 130 °C, indicating a specific thermal transition event.

caption: Creep rate comparison of UT and HT90(2h) PLA samples at 47 °C under a holding stress of 12 MPa, showing reduced creep in the heat-treated specimen.
summary: At 47 °C, the HT90(2h) PLA sample demonstrates a lower creep rate compared to the UT sample under 12 MPa stress. This improved performance is attributed to the increased crystalline structure resulting from the 90 °C heat treatment, which effectively limits polymer chain mobility during the creep test.

caption: Unit cell topology corresponding to the RNFS:2:0 mono-RNL architecture.
summary: This panel illustrates the unit cell topology for the RNFS:2:0 mono-RNL architecture. The structural model provides the geometric basis for the corresponding anisotropic mechanical properties observed in the normalized Young’s modulus surface profile, facilitating the classification of mono-RNLs based on their specific architectural design.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of pure Ni electrode in 0.05 M H2O2 and 2 M NaOH electrolyte, recorded at scan rates ranging from 5 to 1000 mV s-1.
summary: Pure Ni electrode performance is evaluated through cyclic voltammetry in an alkaline peroxide solution. The recorded current densities increase noticeably as the potential scan rate rises from 5 to 1000 mV s-1, demonstrating the electrochemical response of the material under varying kinetic conditions within the specified electrolyte environment.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for V0.85FeCoNi and V0.85FeCoNiCu1.15 alloys measured under an applied field of 1 T, featuring an inset displaying the corresponding dM/dT derivatives.
summary: Magnetization measurements for V0.85FeCoNi and V0.85FeCoNiCu1.15 alloys from 10 to 375 K reveal magnetic transitions under a 1 T field. The inset shows dM/dT derivatives, where the larger derivative for V0.85FeCoNiCu1.15 suggests potential for magnetocaloric optimization. A measurement artifact is noted at 50 K due to chamber impurities.

caption: Absorbance spectra of methylene blue (MB) solution comparing the initial state to the state after 60 minutes of UV irradiation, both with and without the gyroid_dip scaffold.
summary: This panel displays the absorbance spectrum of the reference MB solution. It compares the initial state of the solution against the state following 60 minutes of UV irradiation. The data highlights the impact of the gyroid_dip scaffold on the absorbance characteristics of the MB solution under UV exposure conditions.

caption: Solubility data points for paracetamol Form I in PEG 1500, PEG 4000, and PEG 6000, plotted as a function of temperature and composition, with a red curve representing the global liquidus fit.
summary: This phase diagram illustrates the solubility behavior of paracetamol Form I across different PEG molecular weights. Experimental data points for PEG 1500, 4000, and 6000 are shown alongside a unified liquidus fitting curve. The data indicates that all solubility points follow a consistent trend, supporting the thermodynamic characterization of the system.

caption: Microstructural morphology of the SPHE-T steel showing equiaxed ferrite grains after annealing.
summary: Microstructure of the SPHE-T steel is captured in this micrograph, revealing the presence of fine and uniform equiaxed ferrite grains. The image confirms the effectiveness of the recrystallization annealing heat treatment in producing a homogeneous grain structure throughout the experimental steel strip, consistent with the observed material properties.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of live/dead stained cells on printed hydrogel rings 24 hours post-seeding, showing cell interaction and attachment characteristics.
summary: Live/dead staining evaluates the biocompatibility and cell interaction of the printed hydrogel rings. Fluorescence imaging reveals that when the ring structure is printed solely from HA-GA, cells are unable to effectively interact with or attach to the hydrogel surface, indicating limitations in the base material's bioactivity.

caption: Comparison of single score factors for conventional manufacturing (CM) and additive manufacturing (AM) processes evaluated at their respective baseline values.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the performance assessment of conventional manufacturing and additive manufacturing processes at their baseline states. By comparing the single score factors, the figure provides a direct evaluation of both manufacturing methods, establishing a current-state benchmark for further analysis of the respective production techniques.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions for martensitic stainless steel as a function of Cr/Ni equivalent ratios.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram maps the thermodynamic stability regions of martensitic stainless steel. It serves as a foundational reference for understanding how varying Cr/Ni equivalent ratios influence the phase composition and solidification behavior, providing the theoretical basis for the subsequent microstructural evolution observed during the solidification process.

caption: Non-convergence behavior of the anisotropic phase-field fracture parameter optimization process when fixing the parameter.
summary: This panel illustrates the optimization simulation results for the case where the parameter is fixed. In contrast to successful convergence strategies, this specific approach fails to reach the target solution, highlighting the sensitivity of the phase-field fracture model to the chosen parameter-fixing strategy during the optimization process.

caption: SRIM-calculated depth profiles for displacement damage and atomic concentration in a material subjected to 500 keV He ion irradiation at a fluence of 5 × 10^17 ions/cm^2, with the red box indicating the damage peak region.
summary: Calculated using SRIM, this panel illustrates the depth profile of displacement damage and He ion concentration for a 500 keV irradiation at 5 × 10^17 ions/cm^2. The results are in good agreement with the SRIM prediction, with the red box clearly marking the region where the damage peak occurs.

caption: Stokes parameters measurement for the 1st-order diffraction of a horizontal binary phase grating with a resolution of 12 pixels per period.
summary: Shown is the Stokes parameters measurement for the 1st-order diffraction mode of a horizontal binary phase grating. The analysis is performed at a resolution of 12 pixels per period, characterizing the polarization state of the light diffracted into the first positive order by the grating.

caption: Design and fabrication workflow for BFP-C and BFP-H prostheses, illustrating femoral modeling, anatomical parameter definition (D, L, H, W, CDA), and the resulting 3D-printed custom implants.
summary: This panel details the design and 3D printing process for BFP-C and BFP-H prostheses. It includes femoral modeling, prosthesis fitting simulations, and a schema defining key anatomical parameters such as femoral head diameter and neck length, culminating in the production of custom-designed 3D-printed implants for surgical use.

caption: Three-dimensional surface deviation map of the R-Octet-45 metamaterial, demonstrating the most significant surface deviations among the tested samples due to the 45° twist.
summary: The surface deviation map for the R-Octet-45 metamaterial shows the highest level of forming inaccuracy among the samples. The increased red area indicates that the 45° twist angle leads to greater deviations between the micro-CT data and the CAD model, reflecting the challenges in maintaining geometric fidelity during LPBF processing.

caption: Mass percentage composition data derived from the EDS analysis of the one pass FSPed HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe alloy.
summary: Presented here is the quantitative mass percentage breakdown of the Al-4Mg-2Fe alloy after one pass of friction stir processing. This table summarizes the elemental concentrations obtained from the EDS analysis, providing precise compositional data that characterizes the alloy's chemical state following the single-pass FSP treatment described in the study.

caption: Normalized UV sonoluminescence emission spectra of 85% phosphoric acid solution under Ar flow at 0 rpm and 1500 rpm, accompanied by corresponding 5-second exposure photographs showing bubble path streaks.
summary: Normalized UV sonoluminescence spectra for phosphoric acid under Ar flow reveal emission features including OH and PO* radicals. Comparison between 0 rpm and 1500 rpm shows that stirring increases light emission intensity. Photographs demonstrate that emission occurs along bubble streaks, which multiply significantly when the solution is stirred.

caption: Longitudinal strain map (ϵ xx) for a region of interest with a 50/50 composition ratio, captured at an applied macroscopic stress of 372.5 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the longitudinal strain distribution (ϵ xx) across a region of interest within a functionally graded material (FGM) specimen. The map corresponds to a 50/50 composition ratio under a macroscopic stress of 372.5 MPa, illustrating the localized strain response within the material gauge length during mechanical loading.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of region B, confirming the presence of the Ni phase.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from region B in the TEM micrograph confirms the presence of the Ni phase. This diffraction analysis provides structural evidence for the phase identification within the specified location of the material microstructure at the 90° angle.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for V and Cr dopants within the V6 and Cr6 amorphous alloy matrices, illustrating the electronic contribution of these specific transition metals.
summary: The PDOS for V and Cr dopants in the V6 and Cr6 amorphous alloys is shown here. These plots characterize the electronic states contributed by the transition metal dopants, providing insight into how these specific elements influence the overall electronic structure of the amorphous alloy system.

caption: Phonon dispersion relations for Al5Sc2Si plotted across the Brillouin zone.
summary: Phonon dispersion relations for Al5Sc2Si are plotted across the Brillouin zone. The absence of imaginary frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone confirms that the Al5Sc2Si structure remains dynamically stable under lattice vibrations, as indicated by the calculated dispersion curve which shows no unstable modes in the crystal lattice.

caption: Dimensionless magnetic susceptibility χ versus temperature for an as-received sample with the magnetic field applied parallel to the rolling direction, showing Curie paramagnetic behavior with a linear inverse susceptibility trend above 20 K.
summary: The as-received sample exhibits typical Curie paramagnetic behavior, characterized by a monotonic increase in magnetic susceptibility as temperature decreases. A linear relationship in the inverse susceptibility is observed across most of the temperature range, confirming the paramagnetic nature of the material when a temperature-independent component is subtracted from the data.

caption: Modulated nonlinear emission pattern demonstrating a single focusing point on the left, achieved after approximately 100 generations of genetic algorithm optimization.
summary: A single focusing point is observed on the left side of the emission pattern. This result was achieved through the genetic algorithm after approximately 100 generations, which corresponds to about one hour of optimization time, demonstrating the system's capability to steer nonlinear emission.

caption: Red fluorescence channel (10×) identifying dead HGF cells stained with Ethidium bromide, indicating cytotoxic effects after 24 hours of indirect contact with the samples.
summary: Utilizing Ethidium bromide red staining, this fluorescence microscopy image identifies dead HGF cells following 24 hours of indirect contact with the tested materials. The visualization of red fluorescence provides a clear indication of cytotoxicity, allowing for a comparative analysis of cell death rates across the different experimental sample groups.

caption: Atomic structure of the Σ11 (11-0) [113] grain boundary in FCC Ni, with the grain boundary plane marked by a dashed red line and tested hydrogen interstitial positions.
summary: The atomic model depicts the Σ11 (11-0) [113] grain boundary in FCC Ni. The dashed red line indicates the interface plane, while blue crosses represent the hydrogen sites tested for segregation energy. This structural model is essential for understanding how local atomic arrangements influence hydrogen interactions within the grain boundary region.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the temperature dependence of the backward reaction constant k b , assuming a single-adduct reaction pathway.
summary: Representing the backward reaction constant k b , this Arrhenius plot highlights the limitations of a single-adduct model in describing the reaction kinetics. Consistent with previous research, the plot demonstrates that the reaction behavior cannot be fully characterized by this simplified model over the complete experimental temperature range.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel under varying insolation levels, comparing measured data with predictions from the PEC2 model.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel. By applying the PEC2 model, the researchers successfully rescaled the performance data across different irradiance levels. The plot demonstrates a close agreement between the measured experimental values and the simulated results, validating the accuracy of the proposed modeling approach.

caption: Boxplot comparison of strut dimensions for Cell 6 lattice specimens fabricated from ZrO2 and HAp, with a reference line at the design target of 280 μm.
summary: This boxplot illustrates the distribution of strut dimensions for Cell 6 lattice structures, comparing ZrO2 and HAp materials. The data highlights the deviation of manufactured strut sizes from the intended design dimension of 280 μm, represented by the red line, providing a clear visualization of dimensional accuracy across the two material types.

caption: Surface topography image of the sample processed by UTPC for 30 minutes, acquired via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy.
summary: Surface topography of the sample processed by UTPC for 30 minutes is visualized using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy. This shape image provides a detailed view of the surface morphology resulting from the UTPC treatment, serving as a baseline for evaluating the subsequent corrosion potential variations observed in the same sample.

caption: Taber abrasion testing equipment setup featuring a ceramic-coated circular pan specimen mounted for wear evaluation.
summary: This image shows the Taber abrasion equipment mounted with a ceramic-coated circular pan. By utilizing this specific equipment configuration, the test facilitates a comparative analysis of the wear resistance of the ceramic coating, providing empirical data on the mechanical performance of the cookware surface under standardized rotary abrasion conditions.

caption: Experimental mean refractive indices of the composite samples measured between 0.5 and 2 THz, where error bars indicate the standard deviation calculated from five distinct scans per sample.
summary: Experimental refractive index data for the composite samples are presented for the 0.5 to 2 THz frequency range. The plot illustrates the mean values obtained from five separate scans per sample, with error bars representing the standard deviation to quantify measurement variability and ensure the reliability of the experimental results.

caption: Depth-dependent profile of deviatoric residual stress measured along the building direction using energy dispersive synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
summary: This panel displays the deviatoric residual stress profile as a function of information depth from the surface. Obtained via energy dispersive synchrotron X-ray diffraction, the data illustrates how residual stress varies along the building direction of the sample, providing a comprehensive view of the stress distribution relative to the surface depth.

caption: Bright-field TEM image displaying dislocation cells formed by multiple-slip in the HS zone, with slip systems highlighted by white dashed lines.
summary: This TEM image captures dislocation cells formed due to multiple-slip processes within the HS zone. The specific slip systems involved in this deformation mechanism are delineated by white dashed lines. These structures provide direct evidence of the plastic deformation history and the active slip systems within the material's microstructure.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the alpha-Mg matrix in the top AM region, oriented along the [11-20] zone axis.
summary: The SAED pattern of the alpha-Mg matrix, viewed along the [11-20] zone axis, reveals primary diffraction spots characteristic of the matrix. Notably, the absence of superlattice reflections indicates that the beta-prime phase is not observable in this topmost deposited layer, confirming the phase purity of the matrix.

caption: Manganese elemental map of the Ti-2.5Al–2Nb–2Mn alloy revealing the partitioning of Mn into the beta phase.
summary: The manganese elemental map highlights the distribution of Mn within the Ti-2.5Al–2Nb–2Mn alloy. Notably, the partitioning of manganese into the beta phase is clearly visible in this map, demonstrating that while the overall alloying elements are homogeneous, specific phase-related enrichment of Mn occurs within the microstructure.

caption: Orientation distribution map of the gamma phase in the XOZ plane for the UHFP-treated TiAl-4822 sample.
summary: This panel illustrates the orientation distribution map of the gamma phase in the XOZ plane for the TiAl-4822 sample subjected to ultrasonic excitation. The map highlights the microstructural changes induced by the UHFP process, which contributes to the observed reduction in crack formation during subsequent mechanical fracture testing.

caption: Polar plot illustrating the residual stress anisotropy for the as-fabricated specimen (t_a = 0 s) annealed at 573 K, where 0° and 180° represent the z-direction.
summary: The as-fabricated specimen at 0 s exhibits a compressive residual stress of approximately 60 MPa in the z-direction. The radar chart visualization indicates that this compressive stress state is relatively uniform across other directions, demonstrating the initial anisotropy profile of the material before any significant annealing time is applied.

caption: Longitudinal cross-section SEM micrographs of (TiB2 + TiC)/AlSi10Mg composite showing uniform grain distribution and powder dispersion.
summary: This panel displays the longitudinal cross-section of (TiB2 + TiC)/AlSi10Mg composites. The addition of 1.5 weight percent of nano-TiC and nano-TiB2 particles results in the formation of tiny, uniformly distributed grains. The imagery confirms effective powder distribution, contributing to the development of customized feedstock for high-strength additive manufacturing.

caption: Evolution of Δd311 anisotropy in pure IN718 and IN718-TiC specimens following 3 × 10^5 fatigue cycles at a maximum stress of 700 MPa, highlighting relaxation in pure IN718 versus accumulation in the TiC-reinforced alloy.
summary: This graph tracks the directional changes in d311 lattice spacing after 3 × 10^5 fatigue cycles at 700 MPa. The data reveals a distinct contrast in behavior: pure IN718 undergoes stress relaxation, whereas the IN718-TiC composite accumulates anisotropy, demonstrating the influence of reinforcement particles on the internal stress state during cyclic loading.

caption: Magnified view of the 2θ range from 39° to 51.5°, highlighting peak broadening in DED-processed Cu–Al alloys compared to NAB.
summary: Focusing on the 2θ range between 39° and 51.5°, this panel reveals that the diffraction peaks of the DED-processed Cu–Al alloys are broader than those of the NAB reference. This peak broadening indicates a finer microstructure within the deposited layer, consistent with the presence of eutectic structures observed in other analyses.

caption: Optimal orientation of the stiffest material direction, aligned with the major principal stress direction at ± 45° to the x-axis.
summary: The optimal orientation of the stiffest material direction is shown aligned with the major principal stress at ± 45° to the x-axis. This alignment is a key observation in the design optimization for pure shear stress, confirming that the stiffest direction consistently tracks the major principal stress direction.

caption: Real and imaginary parts of the magnetic permeability for SCC-2/PEEK composites.
summary: This panel illustrates the real and imaginary parts of the complex permeability for SCC-2/PEEK composites. The results demonstrate that the complex permeability increases with higher concentrations of SCF/Co@C-2 composites, confirming that the magnetic response of the material is effectively tuned by adjusting the filler content.

caption: Reference model used for the dimensional accuracy assessment of the printed object.
summary: The reference model serves as the baseline for evaluating the dimensional accuracy of the printed sample. It provides the geometric standard against which the reconstructed surface of the representative printed object is compared to identify deviations and structural inaccuracies resulting from the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Extinction coefficient (K) values for various nanocomposite specimens, including Nano 19, Nano 27, Nano 24, and EOGO, measured at a 1 wt% filler concentration and 405-nm wavelength.
summary: Extinction coefficients for different nanocomposites were determined using UV-vis spectrophotometry. At a 405-nm wavelength, the K-values were measured as 0.339, 0.403, 0.448, and 0.449 g/L-cm for Nano 19, Nano 27, Nano 24, and EOGO, respectively, providing quantitative data on the optical properties of the 1 wt% filler concentration specimens.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for copper layers in Cu/Ni multilayers with 2, 4, 8, and 16 layers, showing a lognormal fit with grain sizes ranging from 1.06 to 1.15 μm.
summary: Copper grain size distributions in Cu/Ni multilayers are represented by yellow histograms derived from EBSD measurements. These distributions, analyzed across 2, 4, 8, and 16 layers, demonstrate consistent grain sizes between 1.06 and 1.15 μm, indicating that copper grains remain relatively small and uniform regardless of the number of layers.

caption: Synchrotron diffraction plot of the 50 h annealed sample highlighting the (110) γ' peak region around 2θ = 24.8°.
summary: This panel presents the synchrotron diffraction data for the 50 h annealed sample, focusing on the (110) γ' peak located near 2θ = 24.8°. The plot captures the diffraction characteristics of the γ' phase, which is essential for understanding the microstructural evolution of the material after 50 hours of annealing.

caption: Optical micrographs showing the morphology of crystals synthesized at varying flow rates, revealing concentric ring inhomogeneities at lower flow rates due to intermittent growth or poor mass transfer.
summary: Crystals synthesized at different flow rates were evaluated to determine the influence of fluid dynamics on morphology. Optical microscopy reveals that lower flow rates result in crystals with concentric ring inhomogeneities, likely caused by intermittent growth or poor mass transfer to the crystal surface during the nucleation and growth process.

caption: CAD model representation of the flexural specimen geometry.
summary: This panel illustrates the 3D CAD model developed for the flexural specimen. Generated via Computer-Aided Design software, this digital model defines the specific dimensions and structural configuration necessary for the flexural testing phase, providing a standardized design framework for the experimental evaluation of the material's bending properties.

caption: Refined co-occurrence network map centered on the term continuous natural fiber, highlighting specific research links to FFF techniques and CFRTC materials.
summary: Focusing on the key term continuous natural fiber, this network map reveals critical research associations. It highlights connections between continuous natural fibers, fused filament fabrication (FFF) techniques, and continuous fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites (CFRTC). Additionally, links to machine learning, auxetic structures, and mechanical testing indicate emerging research streams in sustainable materials development.

caption: XPS spectrum displaying characteristic elemental peaks for the passive film of SLM 316L SS in the YZ orientation.
summary: The YZ orientation of the SLM 316L SS passive film is characterized by this XPS spectrum. It reveals distinct peaks corresponding to O 1s, Ni 2p, Mo 3d, Fe 2p, and Cr 2p, confirming the consistent chemical composition of the passive layer across different planes of the SLM-processed material.

caption: Rectangle packing geometry sample, shown as a 128 × 128 pixel image, which exhibits specific porosity characteristics.
summary: This 128 × 128 pixel image illustrates a rectangle packing geometry. Along with other samples in the dataset, it contributes to the study's goal of covering a full range of porosities. Notably, this sample shares a similar porosity level with the image generated by the QSGS algorithm.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot of ln [ sinh ( α σ ) ] versus inverse absolute temperature (1000/T) to calculate the constant n2 = 8.565.
summary: This Arrhenius plot depicts the dependence of the hyperbolic sine of the flow stress on the inverse temperature. Linear fitting of the curve allows for the determination of the material constant n2, which is found to be 8.565, reflecting the thermal sensitivity of the flow stress during deformation.

caption: Accumulated Integrated Gradients (IG) map generated by the deep learning model, showing high feature attribution in areas corresponding to simulated schlieren scattering near the lens boundaries and cladding head nozzle.
summary: The accumulated IG map reveals a strong correlation between the deep learning model's focus and the simulated schlieren effects. A comparable pattern to the difference image is visible, with the model identifying significant features in scattering regions near the lens boundaries and the cladding head nozzle during the process.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectra comparing commercial XG and GG powders, single-polysaccharide cross-linked hydrogels (XG/SA and GG/SA), and XG:GG 50:50 scaffolds (S–NC and S–SA), with an insert showing relative intensity changes of main bands.
summary: ATR-FTIR analysis reveals the chemical composition of XG and GG powders, their cross-linked hydrogels, and XG:GG scaffolds. The spectra demonstrate that hydroxyl groups in the polysaccharides participate in covalent bonding with succinic acid carbonyl groups, resulting in a broader and more intense carbonylic signal in the cross-linked S–SA scaffold.

caption: SplitP lattice geometry configured for a 20% relative density.
summary: The SplitP lattice structure is illustrated here, maintaining a consistent 20% relative density. This geometric model serves as a primary design candidate for investigating the structural performance of periodic lattice materials, with its specific dimensions and properties documented in the accompanying research data.

caption: Spatial distribution of oxygen atoms within the FeCrNi lattice for the 2 at.% oxygen concentration model.
summary: Shown is the atomic arrangement and oxygen site occupancy for the FeCrNi model containing 2 at.% oxygen. This configuration allows researchers to compare the impact of higher oxygen concentrations on the lattice structure and subsequent mechanical response during the simulated nanoindentation process.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF-X) maps showing the crystallographic orientation of grains relative to the X-direction, highlighting the preferred growth orientation near the substrate interface.
summary: IPF-X maps display the crystallographic orientation of 316L stainless steel grains relative to the X-direction. These maps reveal that grains nucleate near the carbon steel substrate interface and grow with a preferred crystallographic orientation, facilitating the analysis of texture development and the impact of laser beam velocity on the material deposition volume.

caption: Emission spectra of commercial GQDs measured across a range of varying excitation wavelengths.
summary: Presented here are the fluorescence spectra of commercial graphene quantum dots determined by applying various excitation wavelengths. These measurements highlight the excitation-dependent emission behavior of the nanoparticles. The absence of a characteristic absorption tail, typically associated with carbon nanoparticles, is noted in the context of these spectral observations.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry thermograms comparing the thermal transition behavior of TPU-B25/CB and TPU-B25/CB-ZnO composites.
summary: DSC analysis was conducted to examine the thermal properties of the composites. The curves illustrate the effect of adding different fillers on the crystallization peak of the EVA component within the TPU-B25 blend, helping to characterize the thermal behavior of the modified polymer matrix.

caption: Time-on-stream intensity profile for CO2 (m/z = 44) measured via in situ mass spectrometry during the catalytic reaction.
summary: This panel displays the real-time intensity of CO2 (m/z = 44) as a function of time-on-stream, captured using in situ mass spectrometry. The data provides a continuous monitoring of the reactant concentration throughout the reaction process, reflecting the stability and consumption rate of CO2 under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Cr-Si-O system at temperatures ranging from 373 to 1273 K, illustrating the presence of a tie-line connecting Cr and SiO2.
summary: This ternary phase diagram for the Cr-Si-O system at 373–1273 K demonstrates that local thermodynamic equilibrium is possible between Cr and SiO2. The existence of a direct tie-line between these two phases allows for stable interactions, which helps rationalize the observed experimental behavior in Cr-based systems.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the As-Built pure Ti specimen, displaying the characteristic acicular martensitic α′ morphology resulting from rapid solidification during the PBF-LB process.
summary: The As-Built pure Ti specimen exhibits an acicular martensitic α′ microstructure, which is a direct consequence of the rapid solidification inherent to the PBF-LB manufacturing process. This initial state serves as the baseline for evaluating microstructural evolution and grain morphology changes following subsequent hot isostatic pressing treatments.

caption: Comparison of mean plane-strain fracture toughness (K1C) values for the three nanocomposites, with error bars representing standard deviation (n=7) and statistical significance determined via one-way ANOVA and Tukey's test.
summary: The plane-strain fracture toughness (K1C) values for the three 3D printed nanocomposites are presented as a comparative plot. Data points represent the mean values with standard deviations based on seven replicates. Statistical analysis using one-way ANOVA and Tukey's multiple comparison test confirms the significance of the observed differences in toughness.

caption: Vertical logarithmic strain component ɛyy measured experimentally using 2D-DIC during the initial stage of monotonic loading.
summary: Experimental vertical logarithmic strain component ɛyy is visualized using 2D-DIC. This map captures the material response during the first stage of a monotonically increasing load, providing a baseline for validating the numerical model. The color scale is independently adjusted to highlight specific strain variations within the field.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the confidence levels of various parameters influencing the compressive strength of the printed specimens.
summary: This Pareto chart quantifies the confidence levels of different parameters affecting compressive strength. Analysis reveals that the outer infill pattern and raster angle exert a more significant influence on the mechanical performance of the specimens compared to the inner infill pattern and raster angle parameters.

caption: Potential map of the Mo-doped film surface.
summary: This panel shows the Volta potential map for a molybdenum-doped film. The SKPFM analysis confirms that for higher Mo concentrations, the potential gradient effect is no longer visible, reinforcing the observation that the electronic potential distribution becomes more uniform as the molybdenum content increases beyond 2 at%.

caption: Feature dependence analysis of the ridge regression model based on SHAP values, illustrating the influence of T ˆ m a x as the most significant feature on the predicted material property.
summary: The SHAP feature dependence plot reveals that T ˆ m a x is the most influential variable in the ridge regression model. High values of this feature correlate with increased material flow and deformation, confirming that elevated temperatures facilitate these processes, consistent with established material science principles and previous experimental observations.

caption: Linear sliding geometry on the NiFSS surface under dry conditions, visualized via optical profilometry with pseudo-colors representing wear scar depth.
summary: This optical profilometry image displays the linear sliding geometry on a NiFSS surface under dry conditions. Pseudo-colors indicate the depth of the wear scar, with magenta regions highlighting areas of greater worn depth. This visualization is used to obtain the wear volume for the linear sliding test condition.

caption: Cyclic life performance of the microsupercapacitor, with an inset showing the galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for the initial and final cycles.
summary: The cyclic life of the microsupercapacitor is evaluated over repeated charge-discharge cycles to assess long-term stability. The inset provides a direct comparison of the galvanostatic charge-discharge curves from the first and last cycles, confirming the device's ability to maintain consistent electrochemical performance throughout the duration of the testing.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the stress deformation mechanism, highlighting dislocation concentration at the κ-carbide boundary and subsequent carbide cracking.
summary: This mechanism diagram depicts stress deformation in Fe–Mn–Al–C steel. Larger κ-carbide sizes in the S650 sample cause dislocation concentration at the carbide boundary, leading to stress concentration and carbide cracking. In contrast, at 1400 mm/s, only a small amount of κ-carbide precipitates, while the C solute content remains abundant.

caption: FTIR spectra of gaseous pyrolysis products released from native and flame-retardant-treated rayon yarns at peak absorbance during thermal degradation.
summary: Rayon yarns, both native and flame-retardant-treated, are analyzed here via FTIR spectroscopy to identify gaseous pyrolysis products. The spectra represent the chemical composition of gases evolved at peak absorbance during thermal decomposition, providing insight into the degradation behavior of rayon fibers under a controlled nitrogen atmosphere during the TGA-FTIR process.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles at 0.5 mA cm⁻² for a parallel-connected array of three micro-supercapacitors compared to a single device, showing increased discharge duration.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves at 0.5 mA cm⁻² reveal that the discharge duration of the parallel-connected micro-supercapacitor array is approximately three times longer than that of a single device. This improvement is attributed to an increase in total capacitance from 37 mF to 133 mF.

caption: Comparison of experimental and predicted creep response curves for the UT sample subjected to an 8 MPa holding stress at temperatures of 27 °C, 37 °C, and 47 °C.
summary: This panel displays the creep behavior of the UT sample under a constant 8 MPa holding stress. By comparing experimental data with predicted curves at 27 °C, 37 °C, and 47 °C, the plot illustrates the accuracy of the predictive model in capturing the material's time-dependent deformation across these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the CL specimen showing grain orientation distribution.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the grain orientation distribution within the CL specimen. As part of the structural characterization of STA specimens, this map provides a visual representation of the crystallographic texture, serving as a baseline for comparing the microstructural evolution across different processing conditions in the study.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve demonstrating the classification performance of the machine learning model for BCC single-phase stainless steel.
summary: The ROC curve for BCC single-phase stainless steel classification illustrates the model's predictive capability. By evaluating the true positive rate against the false positive rate, this plot confirms the superior performance of the machine learning approach in identifying BCC phase structures, as supported by the AUC metric and overall model validation.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of the K4002 alloy during the heating process, showing thermal events associated with phase transformations.
summary: The DSC heating curve for the K4002 alloy characterizes the thermal response of the material during temperature elevation. This analysis provides essential data on phase transformation temperatures, which, when combined with cooling data and solidification diagrams, helps identify the specific solidification stages and phase transitions occurring within the alloy system.

caption: Performance-profile radar chart comparing seismic metamaterials against conventional seismic protection systems across five engineering metrics: technology maturity, broadband effectiveness, soil-condition independence, durability, and scalability.
summary: This radar chart evaluates seismic metamaterials against conventional protection systems using five key engineering metrics. The visualization highlights a significant development gap, particularly regarding technology maturity and large-scale deployability, despite the strong theoretical potential of seismic metamaterials for targeted wave attenuation in various seismic mitigation applications.

caption: Potentiodynamic-polarization curves of FeCoNiCr1-xAlx high-entropy alloys (HEAs) measured in a 3.5 mass% NaCl solution, illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior across varying aluminum concentrations.
summary: This figure displays potentiodynamic-polarization curves for FeCoNiCr1-xAlx HEAs in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, serving as a standard electrochemical characterization of corrosion performance. Observations indicate that for Al0, Al0.5, and Al0.75 alloys, the current density remains essentially constant between the corrosion potential (Ecorr) and the pitting potential (Epit) as voltage increases.

caption: Primitive structure model representing the design geometry for the sintered TPMS structure.
summary: This primitive structure model defines the intended design geometry for the sintered TPMS structure. Comparison between this design model and the final three-dimensional reconstruction confirms that the geometric characteristics of the fabricated ceramic parts remain largely consistent with the original design specifications during the sintering process.

caption: Experimental and numerical force–displacement curves for the axial crushing component.
summary: This panel displays the force–displacement curves obtained from both experimental testing and numerical simulation for the axial crushing component. The plot provides a direct comparison between the physical test results and the computational model, illustrating the mechanical response of the material under axial loading conditions during the crushing process.

caption: Bottom view of the 3D-printed solution compartment, emphasizing the aperture for electrode contact.
summary: This view of the solution compartment highlights the bottom hole, which measures 9 mm in diameter. This feature is critical for allowing the electrolyte to make contact with the geometric area of interest on the working electrode surface during the electrochemical testing process.

caption: Compressive strength of foam geopolymers evaluated across varying foaming agent concentrations.
summary: Compressive strength data for foam geopolymers is presented here. The results indicate that the addition of SDS, even in the absence of a dedicated foaming agent, leads to a more significant reduction in compressive strength compared to its observed effects on the material's overall density and porosity levels.

caption: Distribution of torque values categorized by varying cutting speed levels.
summary: This box plot illustrates the distribution of torque values across different cutting speed groups. Statistical analysis confirms that variations in cutting speed lead to significant differences in torque levels, with p-values near zero, highlighting the critical influence of this parameter on the overall machining process torque output.

caption: Evolution of the optimal ultimate tensile strength values across successive generations during the Genetic Algorithm optimization process.
summary: This plot illustrates the optimization process of ultimate tensile strength using a hybrid XGBoost-Genetic Algorithm framework. It tracks the iteration-wise progression of optimal mechanical property solutions, demonstrating how the Genetic Algorithm converges toward improved strength values over successive generations within the integrated machine learning optimization workflow.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectra of the pure binder and the filament evaluated before and after the solvent debinding process.
summary: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra are presented for the pure binder and the filament, capturing the chemical composition changes before and after solvent debinding. These spectra allow for the identification of functional groups and the monitoring of chemical modifications resulting from the debinding treatment.

caption: Additional Bode plots for the tested stainless steel samples, illustrating the frequency response and fitting accuracy for the electrochemical system.
summary: These Bode plots complement the electrochemical analysis of Cast-1100 and LPBF 316L stainless steel samples. By presenting experimental data and fitting results, the plots facilitate the interpretation of the passive film behavior and ionic transport characteristics within the 3.5 wt% NaCl solution environment.

caption: Crystal Orbital Overlap Population (COOP) curve illustrating the H–H interaction within the Fe55Cr25Ni20–H–H cluster.
summary: The COOP curve for the H–H interaction in the Fe55Cr25Ni20–H–H cluster is presented. This electronic structure analysis provides insight into the bonding characteristics between hydrogen atoms within the specified alloy cluster, serving as a key diagnostic tool for understanding the interaction energy and orbital overlap in this metallic system.

caption: (001) pole figure for the XY-plane of the 16 spots/mm2 sample, showing the crystallographic orientation perpendicular to the build direction.
summary: This (001) pole figure provides the crystallographic orientation data for the XY-plane of the 16 spots/mm2 sample. By capturing the plane perpendicular to the build direction, it complements the XZ-plane analysis to provide a comprehensive understanding of the grain texture developed during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of a Type-II inclusion with corresponding EDS elemental maps for Cr, Mn, and O.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image displays a Type-II inclusion sampled via FIB. Elemental mapping reveals the spatial distribution of Cr, Mn, and O within the inclusion. The results demonstrate a clear segregation of Mn and O, providing critical insights into the chemical composition and structural characteristics of the Type-II inclusion.

caption: Cutting force profiles obtained during machining experiments conducted within the lower speed range under both low and high temperature conditions.
summary: Cutting force profiles are presented for machining experiments performed in the lower speed range. By comparing these force measurements against the speed profiles from panel (a), specific cutting data can be identified at distinct workpiece locations, enabling an analysis of how temperature variations influence mechanical forces during low-speed cutting.

caption: Laser reflectivity comparison between pure IN718 powder and the 10 vol% TiCN-IN718 powder mixture, measured using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer to evaluate the impact of TiCN addition on laser absorption characteristics.
summary: Laser reflectivity measurements, obtained via UV-Vis spectrophotometry, compare pure IN718 powder with the 10 vol% TiCN-IN718 mixture. The results demonstrate that the addition of TiCN particles significantly improves the laser absorption of the composite powder, a property that is highly conducive to the subsequent laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process.

caption: Cross-sectional plane extracted from the simulation domain, detailing the temperature gradient development along the flow path.
summary: This panel shows a cross-sectional plane extracted from the simulation domain to provide a detailed view of the temperature gradient development along the flow path. The visualization helps characterize the thermal behavior within the bio-inspired heat exchanger, complementing the three-dimensional contours by isolating specific internal temperature profiles during operation.

caption: Percentile values and span data summarizing the particle size distribution metrics for the feedstock materials.
summary: This table displays the percentile values and span metrics for the particle size distributions of the feedstock powders. These values provide a statistical summary of the powder characteristics, confirming that the particle size distributions are similar between the grades, which helps isolate the effects of morphology and composition.

caption: Comparison of aluminum and carbon concentrations across various Ni-based superalloys, illustrating the compositional landscape of literature-reported materials.
summary: This scatter plot displays the aluminum and carbon content of representative Ni-based superalloys sourced from extensive literature. The distribution highlights compositional variations across different alloy systems. Such data is critical for understanding how alloying elements like Mo and Ta influence carbide formation and defect pathways in these high-performance materials.

caption: Extinction coefficient values for np-S thin films and solid Ag thin film plotted as a function of incident beam wavelength.
summary: Extinction coefficient values for both the nanoporous silver thin films and the solid silver thin film are presented as a function of wavelength. The data demonstrates a noticeable increase in extinction coefficient values as the wavelength of the incident beam increases for all tested samples.

caption: Data acquisition process showing CO2 sensor readings over time.
summary: The data acquisition process is illustrated by tracking CO2 sensor readings against time. A 30-second temporal average is extracted from a stabilized segment of the data to ensure that the system reaches equilibrium, providing a reliable basis for the experimental measurements conducted during the study.

caption: Full-range XRD patterns of CoCrFeNiTa x EHEAs spanning 20° to 100° 2θ, illustrating the overall phase composition and crystalline structure of the alloys.
summary: The XRD patterns of CoCrFeNiTa x EHEAs are displayed across a 2θ range of 20°–100°. These patterns provide a comprehensive overview of the crystalline phases present in the alloys, serving as the primary diffraction data for identifying the structural characteristics of the CoCrFeNiTa x system.

caption: Mean absolute error (MAE) performance evaluation for LNN-GKO, RNN-GKO, and Vanilla GNN models plotted against deposition layers for the entire evaluation dataset.
summary: The mean absolute error (MAE) is presented here to further characterize the surrogate models' behavior during the build process. By tracking MAE across all deposition layers, the graph provides a detailed comparison of the predictive error magnitudes for LNN-GKO, RNN-GKO, and Vanilla GNN models across the evaluation dataset.

caption: Ni K-edge XANES spectra comparing Ni foil, NiO, and various Ni-Co bimetallic catalysts (NiMAZ, si-NiCoMAZ, si-CoNiMAZ, and ci-NiCoMAZ), with an inset highlighting the white line peak energy shifts.
summary: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra reveal that reduced catalysts exhibit Ni0 pre-edge features alongside a white line peak indicating a more electropositive Ni0/Ni2+ mixed state compared to Ni foil. The inset zoom-in highlights specific photon energy shifts in the white line peak, reflecting electron transfer between Ni and Co species.

caption: Contour map illustrating the final plasticity distribution for a specimen with an offset distance of 2 mm.
summary: Representing the final plasticity distribution at an offset distance of 2 mm, this contour map highlights the spatial extent of deformation. The zone of maximum plasticity is governed by the material's crystallographic orientation and MWTCR, demonstrating how increasing the offset distance modifies the resulting plasticity profile compared to the 1 mm case.

caption: Detailed view of the composite diffraction pattern showing the specific arrangement of reflections at the interface.
summary: Detailed examination of the composite diffraction pattern provides a closer look at the specific arrangement of reflections at the interface. This magnified view clarifies the spatial distribution of diffraction spots, enabling a more precise analysis of the crystallographic relationship between the sigma precipitate and the adjacent phases.

caption: Bode plot showing the impedance response across the frequency spectrum for the X-Y section of the Wall 0 sample.
summary: Depicted here is the Bode plot for the X-Y section of the Wall 0 sample. Consistent with other sections, the initial impedance modulus is approximately 10⁴ Ω·cm² at low frequencies. The observed decrease of one order of magnitude after 14 days of immersion confirms a progressive loss of barrier performance over time.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) profiles for BAC and CHBAC devices obtained at a constant current of 1 mA.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for BAC and CHBAC devices are shown at a constant current of 1 mA. These profiles facilitate a direct comparison of the charge storage capacity and discharge behavior of the two devices, highlighting the impact of material composition on their overall electrochemical performance and efficiency.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of Ti30Ni50Hf20 pre-alloyed powders, exhibiting a significantly elevated transformation temperature of 171 °C.
summary: This DSC curve displays the thermal characteristics of Ti30Ni50Hf20 pre-alloyed powders. The data reveals a transformation temperature of 171 °C, which is remarkably higher than the 51 °C observed in the Ti50Ni50 sample, demonstrating the significant impact of Hf alloying on the transformation behavior of the NiTi-based powders.

caption: Detailed view of FTIR spectral shifts and peak broadening observed in the antisymmetric stretching (1007 cm-1) and bending mode (958 cm-1) of PO4 3- groups.
summary: Panel b focuses on the specific spectral changes resulting from the functionalization process. A peak broadening and a shift in the peak positions for the antisymmetric stretching at 1007 cm-1 and the bending mode at 958 cm-1 of the phosphate groups provide evidence of the chemical interaction between HAp and Targon 1128.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) pattern derived from the γ-matrix / GB-M2B interface, highlighting faults in the <020> directions.
summary: The FFT analysis of the γ-matrix / GB-M2B interface reveals the presence of structural faults oriented along the <020> directions. These diffraction features, indicated by arrows, provide evidence of lattice disruptions at the interface, which are likely associated with the observed changes in lattice parameters.

caption: Two-dimensional X–Y plane projection of the Hexanoid unit cell, illustrating the foundational geometry of the lattice architecture.
summary: This panel displays the X–Y plane projection of the Hexanoid unit cell. The structure is part of a novel class of lattice architectures inspired by smoothly curved geometries, such as Cassini Ovals and circular arcs, which serve as the fundamental building blocks for the Hexanoid scaffold design.

caption: Convergence history of objective values for Case 2 comparing DFL-TLBO and GA algorithms under various hyperparameter configurations.
summary: This panel displays the convergence history curves for Case 2, highlighting the objective value progression for both DFL-TLBO and GA optimization approaches. The visualization confirms the comparative performance of these algorithms across different parameter configurations, providing insight into their respective convergence rates when solving the specified optimization task.

caption: Temperature-dependent trend of CO2 adsorption capacity for geopolymer monoliths, showing a reduction as temperature increases from 0 °C to 20 °C.
summary: The CO2 adsorption capacity of the geopolymer monoliths is shown to decrease as the temperature rises from 0 °C to 20 °C. This trend highlights the temperature sensitivity of the adsorption process, indicating that lower temperatures are more favorable for the CO2 uptake capacity of these materials.

caption: Ashby-style comparison of adhesion strength and tensile properties of PAP hydrogels relative to reported values in existing literature.
summary: Adhesion strength and tensile properties of the PAP hydrogel are compared against a range of other published works. This comparative analysis highlights the material's performance profile, positioning its mechanical and adhesive characteristics within the broader context of current hydrogel research and development.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 1000 °C, featuring experimental symbols and calculated thermodynamic phase boundaries.
summary: At 1000 °C, the Cu–Ni–S system is depicted through an isothermal section showing experimental data points and calculated thermodynamic tie-lines. The integration of FactSage 8.3 modeling with experimental results from this study and literature provides a comprehensive view of the phase equilibria, as illustrated in the corresponding ternary diagram.

caption: Ni K-edge EXAFS curves of the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam and reference samples plotted in R space.
summary: The Ni K-edge EXAFS curves for the samples are presented in R space. These curves provide structural information regarding the local coordination environment of Ni atoms within the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam, serving as a basis for understanding the atomic arrangement and bonding characteristics of the synthesized material.

caption: Conceptual workflow diagram illustrating the systematic mapping process from service-induced processing conditions to the resulting microstructural state and subsequent residual material properties.
summary: This flowchart outlines the methodology used to establish a quantitative relationship between service processes and microstructural degradation. By mapping the transition from processing conditions to microstructural states and finally to residual properties, the framework provides a structured approach for evaluating material performance and degradation over time in service environments.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness values plotted against displacement for as-casted and AM-ed HEA samples, illustrating a general decreasing trend in hardness as penetration depth increases.
summary: This plot displays the nanoindentation hardness as a function of displacement for both as-casted and AM-ed HEA specimens. The data reveals a consistent decreasing trend in hardness values as the penetration depth increases, providing a clear comparison of the mechanical response between the two processing conditions.

caption: Strain distribution profile measured along the centerline of the gauge section corresponding to the DIC maps.
summary: The strain distribution along the centerline of the gauge section is plotted to quantify the deformation observed in the DIC maps. This profile provides a precise measurement of the strain variation across the specimen, supporting the analysis of inhomogeneous deformation and transformation patterns within the NiTi material.

caption: High-resolution EBSD map (0.5 µm step size) after PDP testing, confirming the presence of martensitic phases within the previously non-indexed regions.
summary: Post-PDP testing, high-resolution EBSD mapping confirms the presence of martensitic phases. The map effectively resolves the microstructure, showing the distribution of B2 austenite (blue) and B19' martensite (green). This confirms that the non-indexed regions observed in the orientation map are indeed martensitic phases present after the corrosion test.

caption: Two-point spatial autocorrelation functions calculated for the five simulated microstructures.
summary: Two-point spatial autocorrelation functions quantify the morphological variations observed in the simulated microstructures. These plots demonstrate distinct symmetry characteristics for each case, which directly correlate with the anisotropy or isotropy observed in the corresponding 2D scattering intensity patterns, providing a quantitative link between real-space structure and reciprocal-space scattering.

caption: Bode phase angle plots illustrating the phase shift as a function of frequency for CoCrFeNiX (X=Nb, Mo, B, Si) alloy ingots in 3.5% NaCl solution at 25°C.
summary: The Bode phase angle plots show the phase shift response for CoCrFeNiX alloy ingots in 3.5% NaCl solution at 25°C. These plots provide insight into the capacitive and resistive components of the electrochemical interface, helping to distinguish the corrosion behavior of the different alloy compositions tested in the study.

caption: Comprehensive phase transformation diagram illustrating the relationship between SLM processing, subsequent heat treatment parameters, and the resulting microstructure, strength, and ductility of Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary: This phase transformation diagram maps the correlation between SLM-fabricated Ti6Al4V alloy, specific heat treatment parameters, and the resulting mechanical properties. By integrating processing conditions with microstructural evolution, the figure serves as a guide for optimizing the strength and ductility of the alloy through controlled thermal treatment processes.

caption: Temperature-dependent real (χ') and imaginary (χ'') components of the AC magnetic susceptibility for the investigated compounds, measured at frequencies of 1, 10, and 120 Hz.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature dependence of the real and imaginary components of AC magnetic susceptibility for the studied compounds. Measurements were conducted at frequencies of 1, 10, and 120 Hz to investigate spin dynamics. The data provides critical insights into the magnetic behavior and relaxation processes within the material system.

caption: Isothermal time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram for GH4099, showing the kinetics of γ′ precipitation within the γ matrix during aging treatment.
summary: This isothermal TTT diagram, modeled with JMatpro, characterizes the transformation kinetics of the GH4099 alloy. Specifically, it indicates that after an aging treatment at 800 °C, the γ′ phase begins to precipitate from the γ matrix after approximately 5 minutes, subsequently diffusing throughout the material structure.

caption: Storage modulus curves of TPU filaments with varying chain extender ratios plotted against temperature.
summary: This panel displays the storage modulus curves for TPU filaments with different chain extender ratios. These curves, derived from dynamic mechanical analysis, illustrate the temperature-dependent mechanical response of the materials, providing essential data on the stiffness and viscoelastic behavior of the TPU samples as influenced by their specific chain extender compositions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the LHAM-HT specimen, highlighting the equiaxed grain structure with random orientations.
summary: The inverse pole figure map of the LHAM-HT specimen reveals equiaxed grains with random orientations. This structural feature confirms the absence of clear crystallographic anisotropy following the heat treatment process, distinguishing the LHAM-HT material from the textured states observed in the other specimens.

caption: Comparison of optimization performance between OA and GA for FE prediction, highlighting the convergence rate and stability of the R2 values.
summary: This panel illustrates the feature selection results for FE prediction. Similar to the UTS results, the OA algorithm converges to the optimal solution around the 10th iteration. In contrast, the GA shows persistent R2 value fluctuations, confirming that OA provides superior feature selection accuracy regardless of the target prediction.

caption: TEM micrograph of the copper side after pulse treatment at 550 °C, illustrating a reduction in dislocation density.
summary: Following pulse treatment at 550 °C, this TEM image reveals a decreased dislocation density in the copper side compared to the original sample. The electron wind force generated by the pulsed current facilitates dislocation glide and annihilation, contributing to the observed grain refinement in the copper matrix.

caption: Comparison of maximum transmitted stress (MTS) values estimated using the fixed strain method (assuming an OSD of 0.5) versus the energy-based method (HEM).
summary: This panel contrasts the maximum transmitted stress (MTS) values obtained via the fixed strain method, which assumes an OSD value of 0.5, against those calculated using the energy-based method (HEM). The comparison demonstrates how the fixed strain approach can lead to both overestimation and underestimation of stress values depending on the threshold OSD.

caption: Tafel potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing uncoated Ti felt and Au/Ti felt samples with varying R values.
summary: Tafel potentiodynamic polarization curves demonstrate the corrosion behavior of uncoated Ti felt and Au-coated Ti felt samples. The Au/Ti felt [R = 50] exhibits the lowest corrosion current density of 0.083 μA/cm2, which is significantly lower than the uncoated Ti felt (2.5 μA/cm2) and other gold-coated variants.

caption: Close-up of the (200) β peak using an exponential intensity scale, comparing observed data points with calculated profiles to evaluate BCC lattice positioning.
summary: This panel focuses on the (200) β peak using an exponential intensity scale to compare observed data with calculated profiles. The trace peak for Ti-1Fe appears shifted right relative to Ti-6Al-4V, suggesting potential BCC lattice compression, although the low signal-to-noise ratio limits the conclusiveness of this observation.

caption: FITC-based cell exclusion zone migration assay showing the mobilization capacity of stem cells into the designated migration zones.
summary: The FITC-based cell exclusion zone migration assay provides a precise visualization of stem cell mobilization capacity. By avoiding edge damage effects common in traditional scratch assays, this method clearly demonstrates the migration behavior of rBMSCs, highlighting the influence of scaffold composition on the cellular movement and recruitment potential.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of purified SWCNT samples, highlighting distinct optical signatures that vary according to the specific chirality and diameter of the nanotubes.
summary: The absorption spectra of single-walled carbon nanotubes demonstrate a clear dependence on their physical dimensions. As indicated by the optical properties, the absorption peaks are directly linked to the nanotube diameter and chirality, confirming that specific electronic transitions are characteristic of the unique structural configuration of each SWCNT species.

caption: DAPI staining of native muscle versus MdECM, revealing the near-complete removal of nuclear content in the decellularized scaffold compared to the native tissue control.
summary: DAPI staining was utilized to evaluate the efficacy of the decellularization process by visualizing residual nuclear content. The images demonstrate an almost complete disappearance of nuclear signals in the MdECM scaffold when compared to the native muscle tissue, confirming the successful removal of cellular components during the treatment.

caption: Phase region of Ti42Al5Mn alloy with 0–1 wt% W addition at 1000 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the phase region of the Ti42Al5Mn alloy modified with 0–1 wt% tungsten at 1000 °C. The specific point marked 'a' indicates the phase equilibrium state achieved after the addition of 0.8 wt% W to the base alloy, providing insight into the phase stability under these conditions.

caption: Double-logarithmic plot of minimum creep strain rate versus load-transfer-corrected effective stress for Al-0.1Sc-0.2Zr, utilizing a load transfer coefficient of α = 0.80.
summary: Representing the creep behavior of Al-0.1Sc-0.2Zr, this plot displays the minimum creep strain rate against the load-transfer-corrected effective stress. By applying a load transfer coefficient of α = 0.80, the data accounts for the load transfer effect, providing a corrected representation of the dislocation creep mechanism observed in the alloy.

caption: Microstructure of the 'c' region in a repair weld with a 30% length.
summary: The bottom area of the 30% length repair weld shows a martensitic and ferritic structure. The longer high-temperature action time associated with the 30% length increases the T 8/5 time, leading to a lower cooling rate that inhibits martensite formation compared to shorter repair lengths, thereby influencing the final weld toughness.

caption: Nyquist impedance plots for the hydrogel system, indicating a Randles equivalent circuit characteristic that deviates from the Warburg behavior observed in two-component salt systems.
summary: Nyquist plots characterize the electrochemical impedance of the hydrogel system. The results suggest a Randles equivalent circuit model, which represents a distinct electrochemical behavior. This observation marks a clear deviation from the Warburg region typically associated with simpler two-component salt systems, indicating complex ion-transfer dynamics within the hydrogel.

caption: Individual HS-AFM scan tile of the WQ900 surface, showing the morphology of γ’/γ’’ phases and the impact of cantilever tip degradation.
summary: Representing an individual scan tile from the WQ900 surface, this HS-AFM image provides a detailed view of the γ’/γ’’ phases. The triangular appearance of these features is attributed to the cantilever tip becoming blunt during the scanning process, which influences the morphological representation of the observed microstructural phases.

caption: SHAP interaction plot between the Bo parameter and the αʺ phase, revealing that low Bo values amplify the negative impact of the αʺ phase on YS.
summary: This interaction plot explores the synergistic effect between the Bo parameter and the αʺ phase on yield strength. The results demonstrate that the Bo parameter modulates the influence of the αʺ phase, with lower Bo values specifically amplifying the negative effect of the αʺ phase on the predicted yield strength.

caption: Impedance modulus (|Z|) versus frequency plot for L-PBF 316 L stainless steel in borate buffer electrolyte, showing temperature-dependent trends and an inset displaying the equivalent electrical circuit model.
summary: The impedance modulus plot for L-PBF 316 L stainless steel in borate buffer electrolyte reveals a clear trend across the tested temperature range. An equivalent electrical circuit, consisting of R s in series with a parallel combination of R ct and a constant phase element, was used to interpret the electrochemical response.

caption: Magnified view of the low-Zr content region of the Zr–Mg phase diagram, highlighting the limited solubility of Zr in Mg.
summary: This zoomed-in view of the low-Zr region demonstrates the restricted solubility of Zr in Mg. Specifically, the solubility is less than 0.002 at.% in liquid Mg at experimental temperatures and remains below 0.005 at.% in solid Mg near the peritectic temperature, confirming the limited interaction between these elements.

caption: Trimetric view of a compact BCC lattice structure composed of multiple unit cells.
summary: This panel illustrates a trimetric view of a compact BCC lattice structure formed by combining multiple unit cells. By showing the assembly of several cells, the visualization demonstrates the periodic nature and extended connectivity of the BCC crystal lattice, providing a broader view of the material's structural organization.

caption: I-V and I-P curves of single cells with different anodes operated at 700 °C using methanol as the fuel, showing OCVs between 1.00 and 1.08 V.
summary: When methanol is used as the fuel, the OCVs are in the range of 1.00–1.08 V. The cell with the Ni-SSn 10 DC anode exhibits the highest Pmax of 2.11 W cm−2, significantly outperforming the Ni-SDC anode, which achieves only 0.78 W cm−2 under identical operating conditions.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of MA316L stainless steel in the vertical section at 6% plastic deformation, displaying the final grain morphology and orientation distribution at this higher strain level.
summary: The IPF map at 6% plastic deformation provides a detailed view of the grain morphology and orientation distribution in MA316L stainless steel. This visualization captures the structural state of the material after significant strain, complementing the defect and boundary analysis observed in the other panels of the figure.

caption: Absorption intensity curves for characteristic functional groups plotted against temperature, overlaid with the DTG profile for correlation.
summary: Characteristic absorption curves for various functional groups are plotted against temperature in this panel, alongside the corresponding DTG profile. This comparison allows for the direct correlation between the thermal degradation rate of the P50B15 sample and the specific chemical species released during the heating process.

caption: Boxplot distribution of compressive specimen lengths across various print angles.
summary: This boxplot displays the length measurements for compressive specimens produced at varying print angles. The visualization allows for a comparative assessment of dimensional consistency across the different orientations, providing insight into the geometric variability of the printed samples relative to the intended design specifications.

caption: Evolution of LSV curves for the Ni II Fe III @NC catalyst after varying numbers of accelerated durability test (ADT) cycles performed between 1.2 and 1.9 V at a scan rate of 500 mV s–1.
summary: LSV curves for the Ni II Fe III @NC catalyst are tracked across multiple accelerated durability test cycles between 1.2 and 1.9 V. The catalyst activity shows an initial increase during these cycles, a behavior that is significantly different from the degradation typically observed in standard IrO2 catalysts.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of chondrocytes exposed to 5 µM H2O2, displaying predominant cell survival with minimal red-stained dead cells.
summary: Exposure to 5 µM hydrogen peroxide results in predominant cell survival among chondrocytes.
