caption: Distribution histogram of the α-lath length for the Ti–5Cu–1Si sample processed at a VED of 50.26 J/mm³.
summary: Shown is the length distribution of α-laths in the Ti–5Cu–1Si sample at a VED of 50.26 J/mm³. The data confirms that the addition of Cu and Si to pure Ti results in a significant reduction in the size of the α-laths compared to the pure Ti microstructure.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the beta phase viewed along the X direction at a height of 30 mm, illustrating the crystallographic texture.
summary: Representing the beta phase orientation along the X direction, this inverse pole figure map was captured at a height of 30 mm. The map provides a detailed view of the crystallographic texture within the 800 µm by 1200 µm analyzed region of the beta-annealed specimen.

caption: Bode plot depicting the electrochemical impedance magnitude and phase angle for the S3 NiTi alloy in pH 3 Hank's solution.
summary: The Bode plot for the S3 NiTi alloy characterizes the electrochemical impedance behavior in a pH 3 Hank's solution. Together with the Nyquist plots, this data supports the conclusion that the acidic environment and H+ ions released by lactic acid inhibit passive film formation and accelerate the degradation process.

caption: Frequency distribution histogram of carbide size for the LPBF ZGH4142 specimen, showing an average carbide size of approximately 44 nm.
summary: The LPBF ZGH4142 specimen exhibits a carbide size distribution centered around an average of 44 nm. This fine carbide dispersion is attributed to the rapid cooling rates inherent in the laser powder bed fusion process, which restricts carbide growth within the observed cellular and columnar microstructural features.

caption: Flatness deviation and surface roughness characterization of Charpy specimens performed using a Talysurf CLI-1000 3D surface profilometer with a 40 nm resolution inductive gauge.
summary: Flatness deviation and surface roughness are characterized on Charpy specimens using a Talysurf CLI-1000 3D surface profilometer. This instrument utilizes a high-resolution inductive gauge with a 40 nm resolution to provide detailed surface topography data, serving as a critical component of the quality control assessment for the manufactured specimens.

caption: Ellipsometric angles measured at a 60-degree incidence angle for a 150 nm thick bare permalloy sample, comparing experimental data points with modeled continuous lines.
summary: This plot displays the ellipsometric angles for a 150 nm thick bare permalloy sample at a 60-degree incidence angle. The experimental data, represented by scattered dots, shows a very good fit with the modeled continuous lines, as confirmed by a low mean squared error (MSE) value.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of the cured preceramic material, illustrating mass loss characteristics during thermal treatment.
summary: This panel displays the thermogravimetric test curve of the original preceramic material following the curing process. The data provides insight into the thermal stability and mass loss behavior of the material as it undergoes heating, serving as a critical characterization step for the subsequent ceramic conversion process.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the TA7 titanium alloy layer on the YOZ plane, revealing a significant dynamic recrystallization structure.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the TA7 titanium alloy layer on the YOZ plane. The visualization highlights the microstructural characteristics of the alloy, specifically demonstrating that the TA7 material produced via RTFI additive manufacturing exhibits a significant dynamic recrystallization structure within the observed grain orientations.

caption: FFT image of the TiBw cross-sectional interface.
summary: The FFT image of the TiBw cross-sectional interface provides crystallographic data regarding the reinforcement-matrix boundary. This diffraction analysis complements the TEM imaging to characterize the interface between the (101) TiBw plane and the α-Ti matrix after the material was subjected to 800 °C heat treatment.

caption: Damage profiles representing the displacement distribution in AISI-348 steel and FeCrMnNi CSA following 6 keV He and 134 keV Xe ion irradiation, as modeled by SRIM-2013.
summary: Damage profiles generated via SRIM-2013 Monte Carlo calculations illustrate the displacement distribution within AISI-348 steel and FeCrMnNi CSA. These profiles quantify the structural damage induced by 6 keV He and 134 keV Xe ion irradiation, facilitating a comparative analysis of the displacement damage sustained by both alloys during the irradiation process.

caption: Comparative stress–strain curves for Iroko shells, illustrating mechanical response under loading.
summary: The stress–strain behavior of the cast Iroko shells is depicted in this panel. These curves characterize the mechanical response of the materials under load, providing essential data on the deformation characteristics and structural integrity of the shells as they undergo mechanical testing during the experimental phase of the research.

caption: OER polarization curves for Ni3FeN, Ni3Fe alloy, NiFe LDH, NiFeO x, and RuO2 catalysts measured in O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH at a sweep rate of 5 mV s–1 and rotation rate of 1600 rpm.
summary: OER polarization curves for Ni3FeN, Ni3Fe alloy, NiFe LDH, NiFeO x, and RuO2 catalysts were measured in O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH at a sweep rate of 5 mV s–1 and rotation rate of 1600 rpm to evaluate the electrocatalytic activity of the hierarchically mesoporous Ni3FeN microspheres.

caption: Performance comparison between RNN and CNN architectures, demonstrating the superior error minimization capabilities of the RNN model.
summary: To explore the efficacy of RNN and CNN as forward prediction models, researchers analyzed their performance on the task of minimizing prediction errors. The comparative results demonstrate the clear advantage of using the RNN architecture over the CNN model for achieving lower prediction errors in this specific material simulation task.

caption: Cumulative reward per episode plotted across four distinct training phases, incorporating reward shaping and 70% simulated accuracy.
summary: This learning curve illustrates the cumulative reward per episode throughout a four-phase training process. The first three phases utilize progressively stricter reward shaping to guide the model, while the entire training regimen maintains a 70% simulated accuracy. The plot effectively captures the performance evolution and convergence behavior across these training stages.

caption: Physical instruments and customized silicone fixtures utilized for the FAE procedure.
summary: The photograph displays the actual instruments and customized silicone fixtures employed during the FAE process. These fixtures are critical for securing the porous structure within a silica tube and ensuring that the acidic solution flows uniformly across all scaffold surfaces for an equal duration during the treatment.

caption: Comparative cyclic voltammetry curves of the three cells with different modified separators at a scanning rate of 0.1 mV s-1.
summary: Comparative cyclic voltammetry curves for the three separator samples are depicted at a scanning rate of 0.1 mV s-1. This direct comparison further evaluates the electrochemical performance of the Ni-Cu@C, Ni-Cu@C/HC, and HC separators, highlighting differences in their redox peak characteristics and overall electrochemical activity under identical testing conditions.

caption: Atomic configurations of HCl adsorption on the ZnO (0001) surface, illustrating the solid-solution site of element E defined as the Zn atom adjacent to the adsorbed atomic cluster.
summary: This panel displays atomic models of HCl adsorption on the ZnO (0001) surface incorporating various solid-solution elements. The configuration highlights the specific solid-solution site of element E, which is identified as the Zn atom positioned directly adjacent to the adsorbed atomic cluster, providing a structural basis for the adsorption analysis.

caption: EDS spectrum obtained from position C1, located inside a dimple containing a 200-250 nm microsphere.
summary: The EDS spectrum at position C1 corresponds to a microsphere with a diameter ranging from 200 to 250 nm located inside a dimple on the fracture surface. This measurement provides compositional information about the spherical intermetallics found within the fracture morphology of the tensile specimens.

caption: Hirox HRX-01 optical microscope used for microstructural investigation, shown with a prepared sample mounted on a specimen holder.
summary: The Hirox HRX-01 optical microscope is presented as the primary instrument for microstructural analysis. The methodology involves preparing samples to specific dimensions and mounting them securely on a slide or specimen holder to ensure stability and clarity during the imaging process for detailed investigation of the material's microstructure.

caption: HR-TEM micrograph of the interface between the Cr₂B phase and the FCC matrix, illustrating the atomic-scale structural arrangement.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging captures the interface between the FCC matrix and the Cr-rich precipitate, identified as the Cr₂B phase. This visualization allows for the examination of the atomic-scale structural arrangement at the phase boundary, which is further characterized by the corresponding SAED patterns shown in panels (e) and (f).

caption: Absorption coefficient spectrum of MgZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles plotted against wavelength.
summary: The absorption coefficient spectrum for MgZnFe2O4 nanoparticles is presented, showing high values at short wavelengths that decline as the wavelength increases from 350 to 390 nm. This trend is consistent with the general behavior of the quaternary alloy nanoparticles, where absorption characteristics are influenced by the material's bandgap and specific constants.

caption: EDS element mapping of the remelted region in the as-built sample, highlighting elemental distribution near grain boundaries.
summary: EDS mapping of the as-built sample reveals the elemental distribution within the remelted region. This analysis is essential for understanding the occurrence of remelting and potential elemental segregation at the grain boundaries, providing a baseline for comparing the chemical homogeneity of the material prior to any subsequent LIHT treatment.

caption: Eutectic content variation in Cd microalloyed Al–Cu alloys plotted against Cu and Cd concentrations, indicating an increase in eutectic fraction with higher Cu levels.
summary: This graph shows the effect of Cu and Cd contents on the eutectic content of the alloys. As the Cu content rises from 5.0 wt% to 6.6 wt%, the eutectic content increases from 12.0–12.3 wt% to 16.2–16.3 wt%, while the eutectic temperature remains constant.

caption: Representative immunofluorescence images and topographical fluorescence intensity maps of Collagen II expression, highlighting the strongest fluorescence in CSK@P200 and CSK@P300 groups.
summary: Collagen II expression was evaluated via immunofluorescence and topographical mapping following two months of implantation. The results indicate that the CSK@P200 and CSK@P300 scaffold groups display the strongest fluorescence intensity, suggesting these specific pore sizes are more effective at promoting Collagen II deposition compared to the other tested scaffolds.

caption: Voigt profile fit of the measured optical linewidth at I MLL = 150 mA, I G = 200 mA, and V SA = −1.8 V.
summary: The optical linewidth of the BSOL device is characterized using the fiber-delayed self-heterodyne method. At operating conditions of 150 mA for I MLL, 200 mA for I G, and -1.8 V for V SA, the measured linewidth is fitted with Voigt profiles, yielding a -3 dB linewidth of 112 kHz.

caption: Kissinger plots and corresponding linear fitting curves for amorphous Mg70−xCe10Ni20Cux (x = 3, 7.5, 10) hydrides.
summary: Linear fitting curves derived from the Kissinger equation are presented for amorphous Mg70−xCe10Ni20Cux hydrides. These plots demonstrate the temperature-dependent crystallization behavior of the hydride samples, allowing for the calculation of crystallization activation energy as a function of copper concentration in the amorphous alloy matrix.

caption: Mott-Schottky curves for laser powder bed fusion produced Ti–6Al–4V (LTC4) passive films, measured after potentiostatic polarization at potentials ranging from 0.6 V to 1.0 V.
summary: Mott-Schottky curves for LTC4 passive films are presented, showing positive slopes between -0.8 V and -0.4 V. These results indicate n-type semiconductive behavior for the films formed after potentiostatic polarization at potentials from 0.6 V to 1.0 V, providing a basis for calculating semiconductive properties.

caption: MatCalc-simulated TTP diagram for the S4 steel, showing the predicted phase transformation boundaries.
summary: This panel shows the TTP diagram for the S4 steel, simulated using MatCalc. These findings are consistent with the broader experimental results of the TTP study. The diagram maps the transformation kinetics, providing a predictive basis for the phase evolution of the S4 steel under varying thermal conditions.

caption: Magnetization (M) versus magnetic field (H) curves for the Ni41.0Co5.0Mn43.5Sn10.0Ga0.5 alloy, measured at various temperatures ranging from 255 K to 308 K.
summary: This figure displays a series of M-H hysteresis loops for the Ni41.0Co5.0Mn43.5Sn10.0Ga0.5 alloy. The measurements were conducted at selected temperatures between 255 K and 308 K to characterize the magnetic response of the material. These curves illustrate the temperature-dependent magnetic behavior of the alloy across the specified thermal range.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of all investigated coating groups.
summary: This panel presents the potentiodynamic polarization curves for all investigated coating groups. These curves are used to evaluate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the samples, providing a comparative analysis of the corrosion resistance across the different experimental conditions tested in the study.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) plot comparing genomic profiles of GEMA-PB treated samples against control groups, demonstrating distinct clustering and significant variance.
summary: Unsupervised PCA analysis reveals distinct genomic profiles between the GEMA@PB hydrogel treated group and the control group. The plot demonstrates significant variance along the principal components, indicating that the hydrogel treatment induces a measurable shift in the intestinal regenerative microenvironment compared to the control samples.

caption: Visible spectrum transmission curves for polymer samples measured via UV-Vis-NIR spectrophotometry, showing normalized reference data.
summary: Visible spectrum transmission curves are presented for polymer samples, obtained through UV-Vis-NIR spectrophotometry. These curves provide normalized reference data essential for evaluating the optical performance of the materials. The data illustrates the spectral characteristics within the visible range, serving as a baseline for comparing integral transmission measurements.

caption: Proposed two-part multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework for identifying optimal build orientations (BOs) in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) manufacturing.
summary: This schematic illustrates a two-part MADM process designed to determine optimal build orientations for LPBF parts. The first stage involves quantifying the specific attributes of alternative build orientations, while the second stage details the sequential decision-making steps required to select the most suitable orientation for the manufacturing process.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF-X) maps showing the crystallographic orientation of austenitic grains along the X-direction for walls processed at different cooling rates.
summary: IPF-X maps visualize the crystallographic orientation of austenitic grains in 316L stainless steel walls. By comparing these maps across different cooling rates, the transition from columnar to equiaxed dendritic solidification morphology is observed, providing a detailed view of how thermal control influences the texture and grain orientation during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: TDA-spectrum of CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 1000 bar with a heating rate of 0.500 K/s, displaying the four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit.
summary: Depicting the TDA-spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA samples charged at 1000 bar, this panel uses a heating rate of 0.500 K/s. The four-peak deconvolution scenario is applied to the experimental data, with the cumulative fit function illustrating the hydrogen desorption behavior under high-pressure charging conditions.

caption: High-power (60 mW) PL emission spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample at 77 K, highlighting the emergence of an additional peak at 1.158 eV alongside the primary transitions.
summary: Increasing the excitation power to 60 mW for the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample at 77 K results in the appearance of a third emission peak at 1.158 eV. This high-power spectrum, fitted with Voigt profiles, demonstrates the evolution of the optical response as excitation intensity increases, revealing additional electronic transition states.

caption: Low-power (1 mW) PL emission spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample at 77 K, showing two distinct peaks at 1.085 eV and 1.115 eV fitted with Voigt profiles.
summary: The 77 K photoluminescence spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample under 1 mW excitation reveals two well-resolved emission peaks centered at 1.085 eV and 1.115 eV. These peaks, characterized by FWHM values of 38 meV and 60 meV respectively, are analyzed using Voigt-profile fitting to accurately determine their spectral features.

caption: Training loss evolution for the LCNN model during the pore status detection task across three distinct test samples (Test-1, Test-2, and Test-3).
summary: This plot displays the training loss progression for the LCNN model specifically applied to the pore status detection task. By tracking the loss across three different test samples, the visualization provides insight into the model's learning behavior and stability during the training process for this classification objective.

caption: Total and partial phonon density of states calculated for the austenite and martensite phases of Ni8Mn6Ti2 at 500 K.
summary: Total and partial phonon density of states for Ni8Mn6Ti2 at 500 K are displayed to investigate the underlying mechanism of the large vibrational entropy change. This analysis of austenitic and martensitic structures at a specific temperature offers a robust description of thermodynamic properties, effectively addressing challenges posed by imaginary phonon frequencies in unstable systems.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of the PN-485 sample surface over a 20 × 20 μm area.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image displays the surface topography of the PN-485 sample across a 20 × 20 μm region. The measurement was conducted to estimate the surface roughness of the material, providing a visual representation of the surface morphology for this specific processing condition.

caption: Spatial distribution of the ϵ xx strain component along the loading direction for a region of interest with a 50/50 composition ratio, captured at a macroscopic stress level of 372.5 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the ϵ xx strain map for a 50/50 composition ratio region of the FGM gauge length. The visualization, captured at 372.5 MPa, illustrates the localized strain distribution under macroscopic loading, providing insight into the mechanical response and deformation behavior of the material at this specific composition.

caption: Atomic percentage content of elements at six distinct points within the AlCrFeNi alloy cross-section shown in (a1).
summary: This analysis displays the atomic percentage content of each element measured at six different points within the AlCrFeNi alloy cross-section shown in panel (a1). These point-scan results provide a localized quantitative assessment of the elemental distribution, further characterizing the chemical composition of the oxide layers and the matrix.

caption: Bar plot illustrating the effect sizes of main factors HGT, v, and F on the interlaminar shear strength (ILSS).
summary: This bar plot quantifies the individual contributions of HGT, v, and F to the variability in ILSS. By isolating these main effects, the visualization highlights how each specific factor influences the mechanical performance of the material, providing a clear assessment of their relative impact on the overall interlaminar shear strength.

caption: EPMA chemical map of the specimen fabricated with a VED of 35 J mm-3, displaying significant chemical segregation.
summary: At the lowest energy density of 35 J mm-3, the EPMA map shows pronounced chemical inhomogeneity. The distribution of elements is highly irregular between melt pools, which is consistent with the presence of unmelted or enriched regions, indicating poor mixing efficiency under these specific laser processing conditions.

caption: Size distribution histogram of dry capsules, showing a narrow distribution centered at 3.3 ± 0.1 mm.
summary: The histogram displays the size distribution of the dry capsules, which exhibit a narrow range of 3.3 ± 0.1 mm. This uniform size distribution highlights the effectiveness of the microfluidic device in providing precise control over fluid flows during the capsule preparation process.

caption: Fast Fourier transform pattern derived from the red rectangular region indicated in panel (b).
summary: This FFT pattern corresponds to the red rectangular region highlighted in the interfacial image of panel (b). By analyzing the diffraction information from this specific area, the structural characteristics and crystallographic orientation of the precipitate shell can be determined, facilitating a deeper understanding of the local atomic arrangement at the interface.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing silmer formulations prepared with pure ethanol (EtH) versus a 9:1 ratio of ethanol to ethylene glycol (EG).
summary: FTIR spectroscopy analysis demonstrates the chemical changes in silmer conformation induced by different solvent systems. The spectra compare the silmer structure when dissolved in pure ethanol versus an ethanol-ethylene glycol mixture, providing evidence for the solvent-dependent conformational changes occurring within the silmer polymer network.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of E. coli bacteria stained with a live/dead kit on the composite scaffold surface, showing bacterial viability distribution at a 50 μm scale.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy using a live/dead bacterial staining kit allows for the visualization of E. coli viability on the composite scaffold. This imaging technique provides a clear distinction between live and dead bacterial populations, enabling the assessment of the scaffold's antimicrobial efficacy through direct observation of bacterial distribution at the 50 μm scale.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of the NiTi/Ni4Ti3 interface in the Ni52.5Ti45.2Cr2.3 alloy, with the interface boundary highlighted by a white dashed line.
summary: This high-resolution transmission electron microscopy image captures the NiTi/Ni4Ti3 interface within the Ni52.5Ti45.2Cr2.3 alloy. The interface is clearly delineated by a white dashed line, providing a detailed view of the structural transition between the two phases at the atomic scale, which is essential for understanding the alloy's microstructural characteristics.

caption: EBSD IPF map of the LPBF-HIP specimen after 1000 h of LBE exposure, highlighting the grain structure near the surface.
summary: This EBSD IPF map provides a detailed view of the grain structure in the LPBF-HIP specimen after 1000 h of LBE exposure. The map confirms that the grain orientation remains stable throughout the exposure period, with no significant changes observed despite the preferential dissolution processes occurring at the material boundaries.

caption: Mean radius of NbC precipitates in ferrite as a function of time, contrasting the present thermodynamic database results with the original mc_fe_v2.061 database and experimental measurements.
summary: The graph displays the mean radius of NbC precipitates in alpha-Fe over time. By comparing the present thermodynamic database against the original mc_fe_v2.061 database and experimental data from Perrard et al., the figure validates the kinetic precipitation model's ability to accurately predict the growth behavior of NbC particles in ferrite.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography of the pristine 3D-printed PEEK sample surface.
summary: Atomic force microscopy was utilized to characterize the surface morphology of the pristine 3D-printed PEEK sample. This analysis provides a baseline for surface roughness, which is compared with the treated sample in panel (d) to evaluate the structural changes induced by the supercritical carbon dioxide treatment process.

caption: Neutron diffraction strain map illustrating residual elastic strain (ε11) along the x-direction for the cold-machined specimen.
summary: Residual elastic strain (ε11) along the x-direction is mapped for the cold-machined specimen using neutron diffraction. This experimental visualization captures the internal strain state within the x-z cross-section, offering a direct measurement of the mechanical consequences induced by the cold-machining process for subsequent comparison with predictive model outputs.

caption: Magnified view of the initial ten hours of the isothermal thermogravimetric analysis for AM1, highlighting the early-stage mass gain kinetics during the dwell period.
summary: Providing a detailed zoom of the first ten hours of the thermogravimetric analysis, this panel focuses on the early-stage mass gain behavior of the AM1 alloy. The plot clarifies the initial oxidation kinetics observed during the isothermal dwell period, following the heating ramp to the specified test temperatures.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) measured xx total strain map at the conclusion of the first loading cycle, indicating the specific area selected for average strain extraction.
summary: This DIC strain map displays the xx total strain distribution across the specimen at the end of the first loading cycle. The highlighted red region identifies the specific area where average strains are calculated, facilitating a direct comparison between experimental DIC data and the crystal plasticity model predictions.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of forged Alloy 625 irradiated at 500 °C to 100 dpa, viewed along the [110] zone axis.
summary: Forged Alloy 625 irradiated at 500 °C to 100 dpa reveals the resulting dislocation loop and line microstructure. This bright-field STEM micrograph, oriented along the [110] zone axis, acts as a representative sample of the microstructural changes observed under these high-temperature and high-dose irradiation conditions in the forged material.

caption: HR-TEM micrograph illustrating the complex interface among the Cr₂B phase, (Ni,Co)Ti₂ phases, and the FCC matrix.
summary: This HR-TEM micrograph captures the interface region where the FCC matrix, Cr₂B phase, and Co/Ni/Ti-rich precipitates meet. The observed lattice misfit at this specific phase interface is approximately 166%, which indicates that the interface is incoherent. This complex structural arrangement is characteristic of the as-built material's multi-phase microstructure.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves illustrating the mass loss behavior of TPU/P-CNF composites as a function of temperature.
summary: The TGA curves presented in panel (a) characterize the thermal degradation profile of TPU/P-CNF composite samples. These curves provide essential data on the mass loss behavior of the materials across a temperature range, serving as a fundamental component of the thermal performance evaluation for the TPU/P-CNF system.

caption: Visual snapshots capturing the morphological state of the embryo sample before and after the melting process.
summary: These snapshots provide a visual comparison of the embryo sample's state before and after melting. The images document the physical transformation of the material during the laser-induced melting process, serving as a direct observation of the structural changes associated with the observed volatilization behavior.

caption: Axonometric view of the isolated horizontal layer extracted from the supercell.
summary: The axonometric view of the horizontal layer provides a three-dimensional perspective of the module's internal connectivity. This layer is part of a larger assembly that maintains a unit-level mechanism under vertical compression, resulting in a nonlinear stiffening response and an auxetic effect while minimizing overall volume density.

caption: Overview of the Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) facility at the Steel Structures Laboratory, University of Cyprus, featuring a 6-axis robotic arm, welding power sources, fume extraction systems, and base plate setup.
summary: This photograph displays the WAAM facility at the University of Cyprus, which integrates a 6-axis ABB robotic arm, Oerlikon and Fronius power sources, and a Plymovent fume extraction system. The setup includes welding curtains and base plates, demonstrating a comprehensive environment for robotic additive manufacturing and parallel component production.

caption: Tabulated chemical composition in weight percentage (wt.%) for the LPBF-fabricated HX alloy powder feedstock.
summary: The chemical composition of the HX alloy powder is detailed in this table, expressed in weight percentage (wt.%). This data provides the precise elemental makeup of the feedstock material used for LPBF fabrication, ensuring that the alloy meets the required specifications for its intended high-temperature applications and mechanical performance.

caption: Plateau stress values as a function of layer thickness for the tested specimens.
summary: Plateau stress is displayed in relation to layer thickness to characterize the energy absorption or deformation behavior of the fabricated samples. This plot captures the trend in stress levels during the plateau region of the compressive test, illustrating the influence of layer thickness on the material's overall mechanical performance.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution of the microstructure.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map provides a visual representation of the crystallographic orientations within the analyzed microstructure. It serves as the initial input data for the transformation process, capturing the spatial distribution of grain orientations necessary for subsequent conversion into a grain-wise graph representation of the material.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of tri-culture scaffolds, including a magnified view highlighting endothelial cells stained with acetylated LDL (magenta arrows) and cell-produced collagen fibers (stars) stretched across the scaffold.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of tri-culture scaffolds shows no visible differences between static and dynamic bioreactor conditions. Magnified views confirm the presence of endothelial cells, identified by acetylated LDL staining, distributed as single cells. Additionally, semi-transparent collagen fibers are observed stretched between the scaffold structures, indicating extracellular matrix production.

caption: Simulated reflection coefficient plotted against frequency, demonstrating the antenna response when immersed in various liquids that emulate the electrical properties of concrete at different curing stages.
summary: The graph displays the simulated reflection coefficient as a function of frequency for an antenna immersed in liquids representing concrete at various curing stages. These results, derived from the setup in panel a, characterize the radiation performance and electromagnetic response of the antenna system throughout the material curing process.

caption: Log-log plot of relative elastic modulus versus relative density for TAOR uniform lattices, illustrating the Gibson-Ashby power law relationship.
summary: This Ashby plot displays the relative elastic modulus against relative density for TAOR uniform lattices. By applying the Gibson-Ashby model, the researchers calculated the coefficient C1 and exponent n1 to define the power law function. These results demonstrate that functionally graded lattices locally follow the elastic modulus predictions established for uniform TAOR lattices.

caption: Isolated infiltrate phases segmented from the CT image to highlight their distribution within the sample matrix.
summary: Infiltrates present in the sample saturated after one cycle are segmented and extracted in this panel. By applying digital image processing to the original CT images, the spatial distribution and morphology of these infiltrates are successfully isolated from the surrounding material components for detailed structural examination.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of HPCA at DS = 1.0, with the wavelength increasing up to 775 nm, including an inset schematic of selective near-infrared reflectance.
summary: This reflectance spectrum for HPCA at DS = 1.0 shows the wavelength increasing to 775 nm. An inset schematic illustrates the selective reflectance of light in the near-infrared range. The findings confirm that the reflected wavelength becomes progressively more prominent as the degree of substitution increases in the HPCA.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of γ’ phase mole fractions versus tungsten content for Co-xNi-12Al-xW alloys at a constant temperature of 950 °C.
summary: Displayed is the calculated γ’ phase stability for the 12Al alloy series at 950 °C based on thermodynamic modeling. The results demonstrate how varying tungsten content influences the phase composition within the Co-Ni-Al-W system, specifically focusing on the γ’ phase fraction while excluding other potential phases like Co3W or B2.

caption: Tensile stress-strain curves comparing the mechanical response of thin-wall GH4099 alloy specimens extracted from the bottom, middle, and top regions of the component.
summary: This plot illustrates the macroscopic mechanical properties of thin-wall GH4099 alloy specimens. By comparing tensile stress-strain curves from the bottom, middle, and top regions, the figure highlights regional variations in mechanical performance. These curves provide essential data for evaluating the structural integrity and consistency of the alloy across different locations.

caption: Atomic force microscopy surface topography of needle-like primary Al13Fe4.
summary: Atomic force microscopy reveals the surface topography of the needle-like primary Al13Fe4 phase. This imaging technique allows for the precise localization of electrical measurements, enabling a detailed comparison of the conduction behavior across different morphologies of the Al13Fe4 intermetallic compound within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Predicted minimum creep rates for PBF-LB/M processed single crystals modeled with SISF-related slip systems for three tensile loading directions.
summary: Minimum creep rates for PBF-LB/M processed single crystals are presented here, focusing on the influence of SISF-related slip systems. The plot compares performance across three specific tensile loading orientations, utilizing the material parameter sets outlined in Table 3 to predict the mechanical behavior of the single crystal specimens.

caption: Magnified fluorescence image of the Rhodamine B film from the conventional electrospray process, highlighting the local intensity distribution.
summary: This magnified view provides a detailed look at the local fluorescence distribution of the Rhodamine B film deposited by conventional electrospray. The image confirms the deposition characteristics observed at a larger scale and serves as a reference for comparing the local uniformity with the anti-gravity printing process.

caption: Mechanical compression curve obtained for the GSx gradient structure.
summary: Mechanical compression curve obtained for the GSx gradient structure is displayed. The data demonstrates how the gradient distribution and relative density distribution dictate the mechanical properties of the Gyroid structure. This curve serves as a key indicator of the material's performance under compressive loading conditions within the experimental framework.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of a monocrystalline (110) Ni-based alloy after 300 minutes of oxidation in high-temperature water, revealing a duplex oxide layer structure.
summary: ToF-SIMS analysis of a monocrystalline (110) Ni-based alloy oxidized for 300 minutes in high-temperature water demonstrates the formation of a duplex oxide layer. This depth profile, obtained using Bi+ and Cs+ ion beams, confirms the layered oxidation structure in the absence of grain boundaries.

caption: Experimental displacement transmission spectrum of the metamaterial, where red shaded zones denote the measured band gaps.
summary: Experimental displacement transmission measurements for the metamaterial reveal the frequency response of the structure. Red shaded regions in the plot represent the band gaps, which demonstrate a strong correlation with the simulated band structure. These results provide insights into the attenuation mechanism for long waves in the manufactured parts.

caption: Representative single and doublet peak fitting routines applied to the diffraction data, demonstrating an intensity ratio of Iγ/Iγ' = 1.38.
summary: Data analysis involves Voigt single and doublet peak fitting routines, as shown here, to extract lattice strains for specific phases and planes. The example highlights the fitting process for a peak doublet, which exhibits an intensity ratio of 1.38, facilitating precise strain determination from the synchrotron diffraction measurements.

caption: Flow rate plotted against differential pressure, with a linear trendline applied to determine the absolute permeability of the sample based on Darcy's law.
summary: Flow rate values are plotted against differential pressure to characterize the sample's permeability. By applying Darcy's law to this linear dataset, the absolute permeability is derived from the slope of the best-fit straight line, effectively quantifying the fluid transport properties of the material under the tested experimental conditions.

caption: Exploded view of the flexible actuator assembly, consisting of a copper wire solenoid, a silicone rubber body, and a permanent magnet mounted on a flexible cantilever.
summary: The fabrication process for the flexible actuator is detailed, comprising a copper wire solenoid and a silicone rubber body. A permanent magnet is attached to a flexible cantilever, which is designed to respond to the oscillating magnetic field generated by the solenoid to induce controlled mechanical vibration.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the eutectic network in the AlMg8 alloy, generated via plasma-focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (PFIB-SEM).
summary: The 3D rendering obtained through PFIB-SEM provides a comprehensive visualization of the eutectic network within the AlMg8 alloy. This interconnected architecture surrounding the α-Al cells is critical for ensuring the mobility of healing agents. The network's geometry acts as a vascular system to transport material towards damage sites effectively.

caption: Isometric view of the thin plate lattice (TPL) obtained via X-ray microscopy, highlighting the internal 3-D channel architecture.
summary: This isometric XRM image provides a 3-D perspective of the thin plate lattice structure. The analysis confirms that the internal channels are clean and free from un-melted powder, demonstrating minimal occlusion within the struts. This visualization effectively illustrates the overall structural integrity and internal cleanliness of the fabricated lattice.

caption: Tafel curves comparing the electrochemical behavior of a-Si, a-Ge, and a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film electrodes.
summary: Tafel curves for a-Si, a-Ge, and a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-films are presented to evaluate their electrochemical characteristics. The corrosion current density (icorr) values for these three materials are explicitly marked on the plot, allowing for a direct comparison of their electrochemical performance and stability in the specified battery system.

caption: Comparative density of states plot for La2Ni7 and La1.5Mg0.5Ni7, both adopting the Ce2Ni7-type crystal structure.
summary: This plot compares the density of states for La2Ni7 and La1.5Mg0.5Ni7. Applying the rigid band approximation, the Fermi level of the Mg-substituted compound shifts toward higher binding energies compared to the parent La2Ni7 phase, illustrating the electronic impact of magnesium substitution within the Ce2Ni7-type lattice framework.

caption: High-resolution O1s core-level XPS spectrum detailing the oxygen chemical environment on the 3D-SiC surface.
summary: This panel displays the O1s core-level XPS spectrum for the 3D-SiC sample. The analysis of the oxygen peak provides critical information regarding the surface oxidation states and oxygen-containing species present on the material after the PIP3 process, contributing to the overall elemental characterization of the 3D-SiC surface.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map showing the crystallographic orientation distribution of the as-cast alloy.
summary: The EBSD IPF map demonstrates that adjacent core-shell structures within the 30–50 μm size range form groups sharing similar crystallographic orientations. This orientation mapping highlights the microstructural organization of the as-cast Al 7.7 Cr 25 Fe 25 Ni 42.3 MEA, providing a clear view of the grain-level structural arrangement.

caption: Free induction decay signal of 79 Br acquired during on-angle spinning at 2100 Hz, featuring an inset plot demonstrating the spinning rate stability within ± 1 Hz over a 5-hour experimental duration.
summary: The 79 Br free induction decay signal is recorded while the 42 mg KBr sample spins at the magic angle at 2100 Hz. The inset callout confirms high experimental stability, maintaining a consistent spin rate within ± 1 Hz throughout the 5-hour acquisition period required for the 16,384 scans.

caption: Validation of the M2P model for predicting DV values across O_10, O_30, and O_50 conditions.
summary: This parity plot validates the M2P model by comparing predicted versus experimental DV values for O_10, O_30, and O_50 samples. The results demonstrate the model's predictive accuracy across these specific conditions, confirming the reliability of the M2P approach in determining DV values as reported in the study's findings.

caption: Energy variation profile for an oxygen atom diffusing on the Ni-based alloy surface.
summary: This panel displays the energy variation for an oxygen atom diffusing on a Ni-based alloy surface. Part of the comprehensive results in Fig. 13, this simulation demonstrates the energetic pathway of oxygen diffusion, providing a basis for evaluating the surface reactivity of the Ni-based alloy system.

caption: FTIR spectra of starch samples showing broad absorption peaks in the 3000–3700 cm⁻¹ range.
summary: The FTIR spectra of the starch samples are presented, highlighting broad peaks within the 3000–3700 cm⁻¹ range. These spectral features indicate the presence of intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonding within the starch structure, as well as the existence of water molecules associated with the starch samples.

caption: Surface atomic model of the CoCrNi MEA viewed along the (111) crystallographic plane.
summary: Surface atomic model of the CoCrNi MEA is displayed for the (111) orientation. The structure is modeled using a 108-atom supercell with a 20 Å vacuum height along the z-direction to avoid periodic image interactions, providing a precise representation of the surface atomic configuration for the MEA.

caption: Shrinkage profile of the printed part measured via Hot Stage Microscopy (HSM) during heating, highlighting distinct plateaus and shrinkage events up to 900 °C.
summary: Hot Stage Microscopy reveals the shrinkage behavior of the printed part during heating. A plateau occurs between 575 °C and 660 °C, followed by a second plateau from 720 °C to 825 °C associated with lithium disilicate crystallization. A final shrinkage event is observed extending up to 900 °C.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification simulation of the Base alloy showing phase fractions versus temperature.
summary: This simulation illustrates the solidification behavior of the Base alloy within the 510–620 °C range. The results indicate that Si and Al9Fe2Si2 phases are the primary constituents predicted to form during the cooling process, providing a baseline for understanding the phase evolution in this specific alloy composition.

caption: Representative CMWP fitting result for TOF-ND data of the N-doped alloy subjected to three-pass hot-caliber rolling at 1000°C.
summary: This panel displays the representative CMWP fitting result for TOF-ND data obtained from the three-pass hot-caliber-rolled N-doped alloy at 1000°C. The fitting demonstrates that the CMWP analysis was properly conducted, providing a reliable basis for evaluating the microstructural characteristics of the alloy after the specified thermomechanical processing.

caption: Homogenization, aging, and surface finishing sequence, designated as HAS, incorporating a final surface finishing step after the aging process.
summary: The HAS processing group undergoes homogenization, water quenching, aging, and a concluding surface finishing procedure. This diagram outlines the chronological order of these thermal and mechanical treatments, highlighting the integration of surface finishing as the final step in the sample preparation sequence for this specific experimental group.

caption: DPV measurements obtained in 1 mM FcMeOH for FS electrodes following exposure to increasing concentrations of TNFα.
summary: Differential pulse voltammetry responses for the FS electrode were recorded in 1 mM FcMeOH after exposure to increasing concentrations of TNFα. The results show a consistent decrease in current as the TNFα concentration increases, confirming the electrochemical behavior of the FS electrode in response to the target protein.

caption: TEM observation of the Ni-15Cr-2.5Ti-1.1Y2O3 + 4.5Al specimen, highlighting a matrix populated by numerous coarse oxide particles.
summary: The TEM analysis of the Ni-15Cr-2.5Ti-1.1Y2O3 + 4.5Al alloy specimen is presented here. Observations of the matrix indicate the presence of many coarse oxide particles, demonstrating the impact of the specific alloy composition on the resulting oxide particle size distribution within the material microstructure.

caption: Load-deflection response of MC and printed specimens with 20% IBA substitution, showing a reduction in flexural-bearing capacity compared to MC specimens.
summary: Representing the 20% IBA substitution, this load-deflection curve highlights a decrease in flexural-bearing capacity for printed specimens relative to MC counterparts. This reduction is attributed to the combined influence of enhanced hydration and the porous nature of the IBA structure within the printed material matrix.

caption: Structural model 3 featuring the FeAl2 framework supplemented with Al atoms at the Al3 sites located at z = 0.1752 and z = 0.6752.
summary: Model 3 incorporates Al atoms into the Al3 sites at z = 0.1752 and z = 0.6752 within the FeAl2 framework. This model is utilized to evaluate the overlapped atomic volume during (001) slip, helping to uniquely determine the slip plane location when considering partial occupancies of c-axis chain sites.

caption: Loss factor (Tanδ) values for PAA, CASM-S1, CASM-S3, and CASM-S5 hydrogels, showing that all compositions maintain a Tanδ below 1, confirming dominant elastic behavior.
summary: The loss factor (Tanδ) for PAA and various CASM hydrogels (S1, S3, S5) is plotted to evaluate rheological properties. All tested hydrogels exhibit a Tanδ value less than 1, which confirms that elasticity is the dominant property of the synthesized materials, validating the successful synthesis of the hydrogel network structures.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for the sample heated to 1000 °C at 10 °C/min, highlighting the emergence of FCC phase peaks between 980 °C and 1000 °C alongside BCC and B2 phases.
summary: This panel presents neutron diffraction patterns for a sample heated to 1000 °C at a rate of 10 °C/min. In addition to the BCC and B2 phases observed throughout the cycle, the diffraction data clearly show the appearance of FCC phase peaks within the 980 °C to 1000 °C temperature range.

caption: EDS analysis result for point B, showing elevated levels of Cr, W, Si, and C compared to points A and C.
summary: EDS analysis at point B reveals higher contents of Cr, W, Si, and C compared to points A and C, while the Co content is lower. This indicates that the grain interior has lower concentrations of Cr, W, Si, and C, and a higher content of Co relative to the intergranular products.

caption: Dimetal-300 LPBF multi-material system featuring a 1 kW continuous-wave fiber laser with a 1064 nm wavelength and a print accuracy of ±0.05 mm.
summary: The Dimetal-300 LPBF system is designed for multi-material additive manufacturing. It integrates a 1 kW continuous-wave fiber laser operating at a 1064 nm wavelength, ensuring high-precision fabrication with a print accuracy of ±0.05 mm, which is essential for the controlled processing of diverse metallic powder feedstocks during the building process.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the 315 °C tempered specimen, indexed along the [111]α′ zone axis.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern for the 4340 steel tempered at 315 °C is indexed along the [111]α′ zone axis. This pattern reveals an Isaichev orientation relationship variant, indicating that the crystallographic relationship between the bainitic laths and the matrix remains consistent after tempering at this temperature.

caption: XRD pattern of the 1 h deposited Co on Cu substrate prior to heat treatment, showing exclusively Cu diffraction peaks.
summary: This XRD pattern represents the initial state of the 1 h deposited Co on Cu alloy. The diffraction analysis reveals that the sample exhibits only the characteristic peaks of the Cu matrix material, indicating that the deposited Co layer does not show distinct crystalline diffraction peaks at this stage.

caption: Tabulated mechanical properties data derived from the tensile testing of hydrogen-free and hydrogen-charged specimens.
summary: The mechanical properties data presented in this table summarize the quantitative results obtained from the tensile testing of both hydrogen-free and hydrogen-charged samples. These values provide a direct comparison of the material performance under different hydrogen charging conditions, complementing the flow stress-strain curves shown in the previous panel.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the classification accuracy and error distribution for the second model across various pH levels.
summary: The confusion matrix for the second model provides a detailed view of the classification results across the different pH level classes. It serves as a diagnostic tool to evaluate how effectively the model categorizes samples, revealing the specific distribution of correct predictions versus misclassifications within the tested pH range.

caption: Schematic illustration of the laser scan strategy and dimensions for the additively manufactured Ti–Zr–Nb–Sn alloy specimens.
summary: This schematic illustrates the laser scan strategy employed for the additive manufacturing of Ti–Zr–Nb–Sn alloy specimens. The process utilized closed-loop control to ensure uniformity and minimize defects. The figure defines the dimensions of the 50 mm by 10 mm by 10 mm fabricated specimens and the resulting plate-type tensile test samples.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the beta-phase in the (10:1) %Mo sample.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the (10:1) %Mo sample focuses on the beta-phase microstructure. This image provides a baseline for observing the matrix characteristics in the absence of the martensitic laths seen in the (3:1) %Mo sample, highlighting the effect of Mo concentration on phase formation.

caption: Backscatter electron SEM image and corresponding Ti EDS map of the CX sample surface.
summary: This panel displays the surface microstructure of the CX sample using backscatter electron SEM imaging alongside an EDS elemental map for titanium. These visualizations confirm the baseline state of the matrix material, providing a reference for the incorporation of TiC particles observed in the subsequent modified samples.

caption: Kissinger plots derived from crystallization peak temperatures for Ta7Zr30 and Ta8Zr20 samples.
summary: This Kissinger plot illustrates the kinetic analysis of crystallization for Ta7Zr30 and Ta8Zr20 alloys. By plotting the crystallization peak temperatures, the graph enables the calculation of activation energies for the distinct crystallization steps observed in the two samples, specifically analyzing two peaks for Ta7Zr30 and three peaks for Ta8Zr20.

caption: Actual strain map calculated from the (220) Bragg edge of the DP 1000 sheet at a 220 N/mm load case.
summary: Strain distribution within the DP 1000 sheet is quantified through an actual strain map derived from the (220) Bragg edge diffraction data. This map illustrates the localized mechanical response of the material under a 220 N/mm load, providing insight into the strain evolution during the in-situ lap shear test.

caption: Calculated mixing enthalpy at 0 K for the fcc lattice, illustrating the agreement between DFT-derived open symbols and CE-modeled solid symbols.
summary: Presented here is the configurational mixing enthalpy at 0 K for an fcc lattice. The plot contrasts DFT-calculated data points, indicated by open symbols, against CE-predicted values marked with solid symbols, demonstrating the predictive capability of the cluster expansion approach for this specific crystal symmetry.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ti-Cu system illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions and the formation of various intermetallic compounds.
summary: The binary phase diagram of the Ti-Cu system is presented, mapping the thermodynamic equilibrium states across varying compositions and temperatures. This diagram identifies the stable intermetallic compounds formed within the system, providing a comprehensive overview of the phase relationships and structural transitions characteristic of the titanium-copper alloy binary system.

caption: Bode plots for LPBF-fabricated specimens in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, showing impedance modulus variations where the alloy reaches a maximum of approximately 2.6 Ω cm² at 0.3 Hz.
summary: Bode plots illustrate the frequency-dependent impedance response of the magnesium alloy in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. At frequencies below 2.8 Hz, the alloy exhibits a higher impedance modulus compared to the composite, peaking at approximately 2.6 Ω cm² at 0.3 Hz, reflecting the electrochemical stability of the material under these conditions.

caption: Correlation between experimental and predicted flow stresses for AD_MS250 at a strain rate of 700 s-1, derived from the modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model.
summary: Experimental and predicted flow stress data for AD_MS250 at a strain rate of 700 s-1 are compared to evaluate the modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model. The analysis shows that the model provides enhanced predictive accuracy, effectively aligning the predicted mechanical behavior with the observed experimental results at this intermediate strain rate.

caption: Cumulative drug release profile (%) of free Bar, Nio-Bar, and Nio-Bar@CS-AL scaffolds at pH 5.4 and pH 7.4 over a 72-hour period.
summary: The release of Bar from Nio-Bar@CS-AL scaffolds was evaluated under different pH conditions in PBS solution over 72 hours. The plot compares the cumulative release percentages of free Bar, Nio-Bar, and the Nio-Bar@CS-AL scaffold, demonstrating the influence of pH and scaffold encapsulation on the drug release kinetics.

caption: Inverse pole figure map parallel to the normal direction (IPF//ND) illustrating the microstructure and crystallographic orientation for Case II following transient deformation.
summary: Panel b presents the IPF//ND map for Case II after transient deformation. Similar to Case I, the microstructure reflects the crystallographic orientations at higher strain levels. The presence of recrystallized grains with random orientations serves to reduce the overall microtexture intensity observed in the material after the deformation process.

caption: Computer-aided design model representing the geometric architecture of the gyroid structure.
summary: This panel displays a 3D CAD model illustrating the intended gyroid structure. The model serves as the foundational design geometry for the subsequent fabrication process, providing a clear visualization of the complex, periodic minimal surface architecture before physical realization through additive manufacturing techniques.

caption: Representative geometry of the Diamond lattice structure used for evaluating shell thickness.
summary: This panel illustrates the Diamond lattice structure, which serves as the base geometry for the subsequent shell thickness analysis. The structure provides the framework for evaluating how different process parameters influence the physical dimensions of the lattice struts during fabrication, as detailed in the following thickness measurements.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental hardness values against numerical predictions, demonstrating model accuracy with prediction errors of 10% and 12%.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the performance of a numerical model by comparing predicted hardness values against experimental data. The visualization highlights the predictive accuracy of the approach, with reported errors of 10% and 12%, confirming the reliability of the numerical simulation in capturing the mechanical hardness characteristics of the material.

caption: Raman spectrum of 85% porous carboHIPEs, providing data on the graphitic nature of the sample.
summary: Presented here is the Raman spectrum for 85% porous carboHIPEs. This spectroscopic analysis serves to characterize the degree of graphitization in the material. By examining the spectral features, researchers can assess the structural integrity and carbon arrangement within the 85% porous carboHIPE architecture.

caption: Numerical distribution of the upper domain for Case 4, calculated with the rotation matrix parameter set to π / 3 at a fixed angle of θ = π / 2.
summary: This panel shows the numerical distribution of the upper domain for Case 4. The simulation utilizes a rotation matrix parameter of π / 3 with a fixed angle of θ = π / 2. The resulting pattern provides insight into the domain behavior and structural arrangement when the rotation parameter is further increased.

caption: Vickers microhardness profiles measured across the interface along the X (recoating) and Y directions, with the interface position marked at the zero reference point.
summary: Vickers microhardness profiles are plotted across the interface in both X and Y directions. The data reveals a distinct difference in the width of the intermixing zone between the two orientations. The X direction, parallel to the recoating path, shows a different hardness distribution compared to the perpendicular Y direction.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis curves displaying storage modulus (solid lines) and loss factor (tan δ, dashed lines) as a function of temperature for 3D printed neat F80 and F60 resins.
summary: This figure presents the dynamic mechanical properties of neat photocurable F80 and F60 resins used in the study. The plot illustrates the temperature-dependent behavior of these materials, specifically tracking the storage modulus and loss factor (tan δ) to characterize their viscoelastic performance across the tested thermal range.

caption: Microstructure of Ni–20Cr–1.2Y2O3 alloy (alloy B) processed by 2 h of milling, revealing the presence of twin boundaries.
summary: This TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the Ni–20Cr–1.2Y2O3 alloy after 2 hours of milling. The image highlights the presence of twin boundaries within the sintered material. Quantitative analysis of this specific condition indicates an average twin width of 127 nm and a volume fraction of 11.6%.

caption: 3D scanning topography image of the cladding track processed at 160 W, illustrating the surface profile and bead height.
summary: This 3D scanning topography image depicts the surface profile of the cladding track processed at 160 W. It provides a detailed view of the bead height and geometry, complementing the top view photographs by visualizing the three-dimensional characteristics of the track formed under high laser power conditions.

caption: Logarithmic current density versus reciprocal charge density transient for a potential step from -0.815 to -0.465 V in the absence of dissolved H2.
summary: Shown is the re-passivation transient for a potential step to -0.465 V performed in the absence of dissolved hydrogen. The log(current density) versus reciprocal charge density plot is used to derive the cBV parameter, which is linked to the activation energy of mobile ion migration through the oxide film during the re-passivation process.

caption: Interaction plot depicting the relative importance and synergistic interactions between various process parameters.
summary: The interaction plot is generated to depict the significance and complex interdependencies of the process parameters. It highlights how different factors interact with one another, providing critical insights into the importance of these variables and their combined influence on the overall process performance and experimental results.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the LPBF-processed NMC, highlighting a mixture of small columnar and fine equiaxed grains.
summary: The LPBF-processed NMC microstructure is characterized by a combination of small columnar grains and fine equiaxed grains. This EBSD-based inverse pole figure map illustrates the grain orientation and morphology, demonstrating a significantly more refined grain structure compared to the LDED-processed material.

caption: Distribution analysis of the relative error between experimental and predicted stress values.
summary: Relative error distribution between experimental and predicted stress values is analyzed to evaluate model performance. The analysis reveals an Average Absolute Relative Error (AARE) of 4.06%, confirming that the predictive model maintains a high degree of precision with minimal deviation from the experimental stress measurements.

caption: Original grayscale cameraman image compared to the resulting light projection at the vat platform prior to compensation.
summary: Panel b illustrates the projection of a complex grayscale cameraman image onto the vat platform. The side-by-side comparison between the original input and the resulting light profile demonstrates the distortion and accuracy limitations of the system when projecting detailed grayscale patterns without applying any compensation techniques to the input.

caption: Standardized effect of the factors on the process output.
summary: This panel displays the standardized effects of the experimental factors, providing a quantitative assessment of their relative influence on the process output. By normalizing these effects, the plot allows for a direct comparison of how different parameters contribute to the overall variance observed in the Design of Experiments results.

caption: Experimental transmission response of beams A and B, demonstrating the measured transmission behavior and the corresponding flexural bandgap region.
summary: Experimental transmission response of beams A and B is shown, capturing the measured transmission behavior. The shaded region highlights the flexural bandgap, confirming the experimental validation of the wave propagation characteristics and demonstrating the consistency between the numerical predictions and the actual physical performance of the beam system.

caption: Visual comparison of wood-epoxy composite surfaces before and after four weeks of accelerated artificial weathering.
summary: Photographs illustrate the surface appearance of wood-epoxy composites prior to and following four weeks of accelerated artificial weathering. The samples exhibit noticeable surface lightening after the exposure period, which serves as a visual indicator of the material degradation processes occurring during the artificial weathering treatment.

caption: Bar graph illustrating the Mode I fracture toughness (G Ic) values measured prior to delamination across different material batches.
summary: This bar graph displays the pre-delamination Mode I fracture toughness (G Ic) values for various material batches. The data provides a comparative assessment of fracture resistance across the tested samples, serving as a baseline for evaluating the influence of particle density on the mechanical integrity of the material before delamination occurs.

caption: Energy dispersion spectroscopy (EDS) analysis of the self-shielded flux used in metallurgical processing with SS-316.
summary: This energy dispersion spectroscopy analysis characterizes the self-shielded flux utilized in metallurgical processes compatible with SS-316. The flux composition, which includes gas-forming, slag-forming, and alloying elements such as metal powders and ferro-alloys, is examined to provide insight into the elemental distribution and chemical makeup of the material.

caption: Magnified view of the TGA curves focusing on the initial decomposition region, identifying an onset temperature of 377 °C for pure PA6.
summary: Providing a detailed look at the initial thermal degradation phase, this magnified TGA plot highlights the onset temperature for pure PA6 at 377 °C. This specific view allows for a precise determination of the thermal stability threshold for the polymer before significant mass loss occurs.

caption: Summary table of histological assessment scores based on UNE-EN ISO 10,993–6:2017 standards, categorizing inflammatory response, fibrosis, fatty infiltrate, and neovascularization on a scale from 0 (absence) to 4 (severe presence).
summary: This table presents the semi-quantitative histological evaluation of local tissue effects following implantation, adhering to UNE-EN ISO 10,993–6:2017 standards. It systematically scores parameters including inflammatory response, fibrosis, fatty infiltrate, and new blood vessel formation, using a scale from 0 to 4 to quantify the severity of the observed biological response.

caption: Temperature-time-transformation diagram for the R725Nb* alloy, detailing the predicted kinetic phase transformations over exposure times at temperatures between 600 °C and 800 °C.
summary: The R725Nb* alloy is analyzed via this TTT diagram, which maps kinetic phase transformation predictions across the 600 °C to 800 °C temperature interval. By plotting exposure time against temperature, the diagram highlights the specific transformation characteristics of this modified alloy composition within the defined experimental thermal parameters.

caption: Atomic arrangement model of the Ti-27.0Mo (15.6 at% Mo) alloy, highlighting the spatial distribution of Ti and Mo atoms within the β-type lattice.
summary: Representing the Ti-27.0Mo (15.6 at% Mo) alloy, this atomic model shows the configuration of Ti and Mo atoms. Consistent with the β-type Ti-Mo alloy series, the atomic positions are significantly displaced from ideal bcc lattice sites, with Ti atoms showing larger mean atomic displacements than the Mo atoms.

caption: Bar chart displaying the mean absolute SHAP values, which quantify the relative importance of various input features in predicting the hardness of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs).
summary: This plot highlights the key features driving the hardness predictions for RHEAs by calculating the mean absolute SHAP values. By ranking these features, the visualization identifies which specific material parameters exert the most significant influence on the model's output, providing insight into the underlying physical drivers of alloy hardness.

caption: Transmittance measurements comparing the optical clarity of the soft and stiff bioink formulations.
summary: Transmittance data provides a quantitative comparison of the optical properties of the soft and stiff bioinks. This measurement characterizes the light-passing capability of the materials, which is a critical parameter for applications requiring optical transparency or monitoring of embedded cells within the printed scaffolds.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of cooling rate (CR) versus porosity in surface pixels, showing an hourglass-shaped correlation where lower CR values contribute significantly to increased porosity.
summary: This SHAP scatter plot illustrates the relationship between cooling rate and porosity in surface pixels. The data reveals an hourglass-shaped correlation, indicating that lower cooling rates are strongly associated with higher porosity levels. This trend highlights the significant influence of cooling rate on keyhole porosity formation in surface regions.

caption: Schematic representation of the additive manufacturing system architecture, highlighting the integration of the energy source, scanning mirror assembly, powder delivery mechanism, and the waste powder collection unit.
summary: This diagram illustrates the fundamental components of the additive manufacturing system. It details the functional layout, including the energy source, scanning mirror system, powder delivery mechanism, and the waste powder collector, providing a comprehensive overview of the hardware configuration required for the printing process as described in the system setup.

caption: Detailed confocal analysis of the deepest pits observed on the SLM as-built surface after exposure to a potentiostatic polarization test at +0.25 V vs. OCP in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Detailed confocal analysis reveals the topography of the deepest pits on the SLM as-built surface after potentiostatic polarization in 3.5 wt% NaCl at +0.25 V vs. OCP. This visualization provides insight into the localized corrosion damage sustained by the as-built material under the specified electrochemical test conditions.

caption: In-situ optical micrograph capturing the initiation stage of positive burr formation at a cutting speed of 60 m/min.
summary: This in-situ optical micrograph illustrates the initiation stage of positive burr formation during machining. Captured at a cutting speed of 60 m/min and a true chip thickness of 30 micrometers, the image provides a baseline for observing the transition from steady-state chip formation to the onset of burr development.

caption: Atomic model of the Cr23C6 precipitated phase identified in the annealed samples.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy confirms that the precipitates possess an FCC crystal structure. Analysis of the atomic ratio, approximately 4:1 for Cr to C, identifies the precipitated phase as Cr23C6. This crystal structure model represents the Cr-rich carbides formed at the grain boundaries during the annealing process.

caption: Ultrasonic scan of Sample C showing the longitudinal tungsten insert, transversal tungsten insert, and tungsten balls, with magenta rectangles highlighting ultrasonic shadows caused by surface undulations.
summary: This ultrasonic scan of Sample C represents a challenging inspection scenario for PAUT modalities. The image displays discrete high-amplitude indications for the longitudinal insert and circular features for the transversal insert. Magenta rectangles indicate ultrasonic shadows occurring where the acoustic beam deviates from the normal due to WAAM surface undulations.

caption: Comprehensive phase transformation diagram for SLM-processed Ti6Al4V alloy, illustrating the relationship between heat treatment parameters, resulting microstructural evolution, and the corresponding mechanical properties of strength and ductility.
summary: This phase transformation diagram maps the processing-structure-property relationships for SLM-fabricated Ti6Al4V alloy. It integrates heat treatment parameters with the resulting microstructural states to predict mechanical performance, specifically strength and ductility. The diagram serves as a guide for optimizing alloy properties through controlled thermal processing cycles as described in the study.

caption: Cyclic stability of CO2 adsorption capacity for geopolymer monoliths over multiple adsorption-desorption cycles at 20 °C.
summary: This plot tracks the CO2 adsorption capacity of geopolymer specimens across successive adsorption-desorption cycles at 20 °C. Consistent with the 0 °C findings, the data shows a slight reduction in capacity with an increasing number of cycles, demonstrating the material's durability and performance consistency during repeated usage at this temperature.

caption: Excitation and fluorescence spectra of undoped as-synthesized resins prepared via the non-hydrolytic pathway.
summary: This panel presents the excitation and fluorescence spectra for undoped liquid resins synthesized using a non-hydrolytic pathway. It serves to define the baseline optical properties of the bare resin, allowing for a direct comparison of photophysical characteristics between different synthesis routes prior to any further material modification.

caption: Predicted change in the critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) as a function of the Al:Nb ratio and temperature, where open symbols represent weak dislocation coupling and closed symbols denote strong dislocation coupling.
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated change in CRSS resulting from secondary γ′ precipitates across varying alloy compositions and temperatures. The data distinguishes between weak and strong dislocation coupling mechanisms using open and closed symbols, respectively, providing a comprehensive overview of how composition and thermal conditions influence the mechanical strengthening behavior of the alloy.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of as-cast Al0.5Ti2Nb1Zr1W0.5 RHEA showing the distribution of B2 nanoparticles within the BCC matrix.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph reveals the microstructure of the as-cast Al0.5Ti2Nb1Zr1W0.5 RHEA. The imaging technique highlights the presence of B2 nanoparticles that are evenly dispersed throughout the BCC matrix, confirming the dual-phase nature of the alloy as observed in the accompanying electron diffraction analysis.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of the DENV-Ag-Apt/GO-ZnO-NC/3DP-PAC electrode recorded in 10 mM MB and 0.1 M KCl at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹, showing the electrochemical response across a potential range of -1 V to +1 V for varying dengue virus antigen concentrations.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry analysis of the 3D-printed cassette-based aptasensor demonstrates its quantitative capabilities for detecting various concentrations of dengue virus antigen. The measurements were performed in a 10 mM MB solution with 0.1 M KCl at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ within a potential range of -1 V to +1 V.

caption: Statistical distribution of yield stress values represented as a box-and-whisker plot for specimens prepared using processing condition 2.
summary: Representing the yield stress for processing condition 2, this box-and-whisker plot highlights the mean and variance of the mechanical data. Because yield occurs before the first scan, the results demonstrate that continuous and interrupted testing protocols provide consistent and comparable measurements for this specific material processing state.

caption: Cumulative plastic strain profile along a node line crossing the shear region in coarse-grained polycrystalline aggregates, modeled with a micromorphic crystal plasticity approach using a gradient parameter of A = 0.004 N at a normalized displacement of 0.052 mm/mm.
summary: This panel illustrates the cumulative plastic strain variation in coarse-grained polycrystalline aggregates subjected to adiabatic heating. Using a micromorphic crystal plasticity model with a gradient parameter of 0.004 N, the simulation reveals significant strain localization along the node line crossing the shear region at a normalized displacement of 0.052 mm/mm.

caption: Z-directional average atomic coordinates of the Ni–Cr model during oxidation in a CO2 atmosphere.
summary: Z-directional average atomic coordinates are plotted for the Ni–Cr model in a CO2 atmosphere. The red dashed line indicates the initial metal surface position, while the black dashed line marks the deepest oxygen atom diffusion depth. This data helps quantify the oxide layer thickness resulting from the oxidation process.

caption: Radial distribution functions for Ni-Ni (bulk: red, GB: orange) and Cr-Cr (bulk: blue, GB: turquoise) averaged over the final nanosecond of the 1600 K simulation.
summary: Radial distribution functions at 1600 K reveal a loss of long-range organization in the grain boundary compared to the bulk fcc lattice. While Ni exhibits liquid-like behavior in the grain boundary, Cr shows distinct structural reorganization, confirming that the grain boundary environment significantly alters atomic arrangement relative to the bulk grain.

caption: SEM-EDX spectrum of the as-cast base material showing characteristic peaks for nickel, cobalt, aluminium, and tantalum.
summary: The reference spectrum obtained from the as-cast base material exhibits strong peaks corresponding to primarily nickel, cobalt, aluminium, and tantalum, consistent with the expected alloy chemistry. This baseline measurement confirms the elemental composition of the reference material before any surface scale formation or oxidation processes occurred on the specimen.

caption: Contour plot representing the maximum span observed across different speed and flow rate combinations.
summary: The contour plot reveals the distribution of the maximum span across various processing conditions. It demonstrates that a minimal maximum span of 13-14 mm is achieved when both speed and flow rate are maintained at moderate levels, suggesting an optimal parameter window for controlling the span of the layers.

caption: Comparison of the DMDc state-space model predictions against ground truth melt pool temperature time series for reproductive training data, accompanied by a residual distribution histogram.
summary: This panel displays the performance of the DMDc state-space model on training data. It features a time series comparison between experimental melt pool temperature measurements and model predictions, alongside a histogram illustrating the distribution of residuals, which quantifies the accuracy of the model during the reproductive training phase.
