caption: Annotated SADP highlighting three diffuse rings with white circles, characteristic of a cubic spinel structure.
summary: This annotated SADP highlights three diffuse rings, marked with white circles, which are consistent with reflections from a cubic spinel structure. These diffraction features confirm that the oxide layer is characterized by the presence of ultrafine crystallites, likely Cr-Fe spinel, formed during the caustic exposure.

caption: Topographical visualization of the SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy processed at 110 W laser power, characterized by a surface roughness of 5.29 μm.
summary: The P-110 specimen, produced with 110 W laser power, shows improved surface smoothness in its 2D and 3D topographical maps. The surface roughness value is recorded at 5.29 μm, demonstrating the ongoing trend of decreasing surface roughness as the laser power applied during SLM printing is increased.

caption: Von Mises stress distribution map for LPBF Ti6Al4V alloy during a tribological test conducted at a low sliding speed of 9.58 m/min.
summary: Displayed is the simulated von Mises stress distribution for LPBF Ti6Al4V at a sliding speed of 9.58 m/min. Compared to wrought material, the LPBF alloy exhibits a higher degree of stress reduction as sliding speed increases, a behavior attributed to its superior mechanical properties and lower adhesive tendencies under load.

caption: Experimental setup showing the s-FCPC attached to a human finger with adhesive to monitor relative resistance changes during cyclic bending at discrete angles of 20°, 50°, 70°, and 110°.
summary: The s-FCPC is mounted on a volunteer's finger using adhesive to ensure stable contact during cyclic bending tests. The sensor effectively measures relative resistance changes across various bending angles, specifically 20°, 50°, 70°, and 110°, confirming its capability to function as a reliable wearable strain sensor for human motion monitoring.

caption: Statistical box-and-whisker representation of prior beta-grain size variation as a function of build height (P1–P4) along the BD–TD plane.
summary: Prior beta-grain size is analyzed along the 80 mm build height on the BD–TD plane to assess potential build-height-dependent microstructural changes. This box-and-whisker plot displays the grain size distribution across four build heights, P1 to P4, characterizing the evolution of the prior beta-grain morphology throughout the sample height.

caption: Elemental composition distribution within the TCP phase of the 0Ru alloy.
summary: This compositional map details the elemental distribution within the topologically close-packed (TCP) phase of the 0Ru alloy. The analysis characterizes the chemical signature of these brittle phases, which form during the 500-hour treatment at 950 °C, helping to distinguish their composition from the surrounding matrix and dislocation regions.

caption: Mass spectrometry profile corresponding to the thermal decomposition products of the printed PEG-0 thermoset during the STA process in air.
summary: Mass spectrometry data is presented here to characterize the gaseous decomposition products released from the printed PEG-0 thermoset during thermal analysis in air. This analysis, performed in conjunction with STA, provides essential insights into the material's degradation behavior, which informs the design of the subsequent three-step thermal treatment process.

caption: μ-Raman spectra of KSER samples subjected to oxidation within the REHPTS facility, illustrating phase changes under diverse temperature and time conditions.
summary: This panel presents μ-Raman spectra of KSER samples oxidized in the REHPTS facility at various temperatures and durations. The analysis identifies specific phases such as silica, alumina, silicon, and molybdenum disilicide. These spectra demonstrate the sensitivity of the material's phase composition to the specific operating conditions applied during the oxidation process.

caption: Phononic band structure calculated for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction under a 10% compressive strain applied in the P to Q configuration.
summary: This panel displays the phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction. The system is subjected to a 10% compressive strain in the P to Q configuration. Red highlights indicate the presence of band gaps within the calculated dispersion relation for this specific structural deformation state.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra for Clear V4 resin after 60 minutes of UV treatment at 60 °C, contrasting the release of uncured monomers with and without parylene-C coating.
summary: Displayed are UV-Vis absorbance spectra for Clear V4 resin after 60 minutes of UV treatment at 60 °C. Comparison with heat treatment results reveals that heat is significantly more effective than UV treatment for this specific resin, as evidenced by the relative reduction in monomer absorption levels.

caption: Arrhenius-style plot of the natural logarithm of the rate constant k versus the inverse temperature -1000/RT for calculating the activation energy Q.
summary: By applying a natural logarithm to the kinetic equation, this plot of ln k versus -1000/RT is constructed to extract the activation energy Q. The slope of the fitted line in this Arrhenius-type representation provides the necessary value for Q based on the JMAK analysis.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of 1a (2.98 × 10^-5 M) in acetonitrile under 405 nm LED irradiation, showing negligible intensity changes over 2-minute intervals.
summary: Steady-state photolysis of 1a alone in acetonitrile under 405 nm LED irradiation demonstrates remarkable photostability. The absorption spectrum shows negligible intensity changes over time, confirming that the molecule remains stable without any additives during the irradiation process, as evidenced by the lack of spectral evolution in the recorded data.

caption: Isolated 5 at% Al isosurface reconstruction extracted from the bulk material to clarify the spatial distribution of the γ′ phase.
summary: Isolated 5 at% Al isosurfaces are presented to clarify the γ′ phase distribution within the bulk material. By separating the Al isosurfaces from the Nb data, the structural arrangement of the γ′ precipitates becomes more distinct, facilitating a clearer interpretation of the precipitate morphology and spatial density in the undeformed bulk.

caption: Electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-10Ni alloy measured at 86(2) GPa up to 2060(150) K, plotted as a function of temperature.
summary: Electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-10Ni alloy is presented at 86 GPa and temperatures reaching 2060 K. The data, represented by blue squares with crosses, demonstrates a quasi-linear increase above 1500 K. A blue curve fitted using the Bloch-Grüneisen formula and resonant impurity resistivity models the temperature-dependent behavior of the alloy.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation-based powder design and fabrication process involving plasma arc melting and gas atomization of Fe-based alloy ingots.
summary: This stage focuses on thermodynamic calculation-based powder design and fabrication. Spherical Fe–Co–Mo, Fe–Cr–Ni, and Fe–Co–Cr powders with particle sizes of 45–150 μm are produced by creating alloy ingots via plasma arc melting of elemental pellets, followed by gas atomization in an argon atmosphere to ensure precise powder composition.

caption: Classification hierarchy of various steel alloys and their corresponding industrial applications.
summary: This diagram illustrates the systematic categorization of steel alloys based on their composition and properties. It maps the diverse range of steels to their specific industrial applications, highlighting the versatility of iron-carbon alloys. The figure serves as a reference for understanding how material selection aligns with functional requirements in engineering.

caption: Principal residual stress components (σxx, σyy, σzz) plotted against build height along the edge path scan (TW1).
summary: Neutron diffraction data reveals the principal residual stress distributions along the edge scan path. The results demonstrate an increasingly compressive behavior as the build height increases. These tensile residual stresses toward the top of the build correlate with the overall increase in hardness observed through nanoindentation measurements.

caption: Correlation between Vickers hardness (HV 10) and cell structure size (μm) for CO2-Lattice, CO2-Solid, F-Lattice, and F-Solid manufactured specimens.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between Vickers hardness (HV 10) and cell structure size in micrometers for four distinct sample types: CO2-Lattice, CO2-Solid, F-Lattice, and F-Solid. The data provides a comparative analysis of how varying structural dimensions influence the mechanical hardness properties across these specific manufactured material conditions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of AlSi9Cu3 alloy, illustrating the active corrosion behavior of the material in the as-built and heat-treated conditions.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization testing confirms the active corrosion behavior of the AlSi9Cu3 alloy in the as-built condition. Comparison between the as-built and heat-treated specimens reveals that the heat treatment process does not induce any significant changes in the overall corrosion behavior of the material, as evidenced by the polarization curves.

caption: Comparison of R-squared values across three distinct predictive models for various material properties.
summary: This table presents the R-squared performance metrics for three different machine learning models developed to predict material properties. By evaluating these statistical coefficients, the figure provides a quantitative assessment of how well each model captures the variance in the data, facilitating a direct comparison of predictive accuracy across the investigated material properties.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectra of trypsin (1 g/L) obtained at 308 K with SL/trypsin mass ratios spanning 0 to 0.8 g/L.
summary: Measurements taken at 308 K reveal that trypsin maintains an emission peak at 327 nm. Increasing the SL concentration leads to a gradual decline in the peak fluorescence intensity, confirming that the quenching effect persists at this temperature as the SL/trypsin mass ratio is elevated.

caption: Melt pool aspect ratio distribution for 7A76 samples, identifying specific samples #19 and #20 with aspect ratios of 0.49 and 0.5, respectively, indicative of conduction mode processing.
summary: The melt pool aspect ratio for 7A76 samples is presented to characterize the solidification mode. Samples #19 and #20 exhibit aspect ratios of 0.49 and 0.5, respectively. These values are consistent with the conduction mode of laser processing, providing insight into the thermal dynamics during the fabrication of these high-density samples.

caption: MCR-ALS derived component spectra and concentration profiles for the Fe K edge during H2-TPR of 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4, showing three distinct components.
summary: The Fe K edge dataset reveals three components via MCR-ALS analysis. A starting component decreases at 280 °C, while a final component forms concurrently. An intermediate component reaches a maximum concentration of approximately 40% at 620 °C. These profiles provide insight into the reduction behavior of iron species during the thermal treatment.

caption: Minimum creep strain rate plotted against time for the AM state alloy at 950 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the minimum creep strain rate over time for the AM state alloy at 950 °C. It serves to characterize the creep behavior of the AM state at high temperatures, allowing for a direct comparison with the CM state under identical thermal and mechanical parameters.

caption: Conceptual mould design illustrating the positioning of recording cameras for experimental measurements.
summary: This schematic illustrates the conceptual mould design utilized for experimental measurements. It highlights the specific placement of recording cameras, including a frontal camera positioned on the right mould and a side camera on the left mould, which are emphasized in orange to provide clear visual guidance for the experimental setup.

caption: Diffusion paths for the 2L|2R couple plotted on a phase diagram, with the calculated beta-phase content shown below and blue squares marking end-member compositions.
summary: Diffusion paths for the 2L|2R couple are mapped onto the phase diagram, with blue squares denoting end-member compositions and the calculated beta-phase content displayed below. The simulation resulted in a zig-zag diffusion path, which shows a lack of full agreement when compared with the experimental results for this specific couple.

caption: Quaternary phase diagram of CrNbTiZr showing the influence of Cr-concentration on phase stability, where blue regions denote single-phase areas and orange regions indicate two-phase areas.
summary: This quaternary phase diagram illustrates the relationship between chemical composition and phase stability in CrNbTiZr samples. The visualization highlights how Cr-concentration dictates the formation of single-phase and two-phase regions, represented by blue and orange colors respectively. Symbols within the diagram correspond to individual experimental samples analyzed during the investigation.

caption: Copper (Cu) recovery efficiency from tailings comparing 7-day electrokinetic (EK) and static leaching (SL) treatments.
summary: Copper recovery efficiency is measured following 7 days of exposure to electrokinetic or static leaching processes. The data highlights the effectiveness of these treatments in extracting Cu from tailings, where a minor concentration of chalcopyrite was previously detected in the sample material.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph highlighting the formation of a eutectic network extending along the grain boundaries of the modified material.
summary: This scanning electron micrograph illustrates the microstructural evolution at the grain boundaries. It reveals a distinct eutectic network that has formed along these boundaries, providing evidence of the phase transformation and solute segregation processes that occur during the cooling phase of the laser surface-modification treatment.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the relative significance of various process parameters on the Material Removal Rate (MRR).
summary: This bar chart quantifies the impact of different process parameters on the Material Removal Rate (MRR). By visualizing the significance of these factors, the plot identifies which variables exert the most influence on the machining performance, providing a clear assessment of parameter sensitivity as described in the study's analysis of MRR.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the direct-aged sample highlighting localized γ″-rich zones with heterogeneous precipitation.
summary: Direct-aged samples exhibit a heterogeneous microstructure characterized by localized zones with a high number density of γ″ precipitates. TEM observations confirm that these γ″-rich regions contain variants oriented along [100]γ”, [010]γ”, and [001]γ”, contrasting with the uniform distribution observed in samples that underwent prior solution annealing.

caption: Hardness versus penetration depth curves obtained from nanoindentation tests conducted at varying loading rates.
summary: Hardness–penetration depth curves demonstrate the mechanical response under different loading rates. A distinct declining stage is followed by a stable hardness regime once the penetration depth exceeds 550–600 nm. This turning point indicates that the material hardness stabilizes consistently across the tested loading conditions at higher indentation depths.

caption: Simulated local density profiles of Ni3Si, Ni31Si12, and Ni2Si compounds following laser annealing at a fluence of 3.2 J/cm2.
summary: At a laser fluence of 3.2 J/cm2, the simulation shows that Ni3Si and Ni31Si12 exhibit similar weights within the silicide layer, while the Ni2Si phase appears less significant. This demonstrates the increasing relevance of Si-richer compounds as the laser annealing fluence is increased during the process.

caption: Total diffusion coefficient profile of Cr across the Σ = 3 / ( 111 ) grain boundary, projected on the x-dimension, with temperature-dependent variations from 1300 to 1600 K.
summary: The Cr diffusion coefficient profile across the Σ = 3 grain boundary is presented for temperatures between 1300 and 1600 K. The data highlights the spatial variation of Cr mobility, with a characteristic peak at the grain boundary position indicating localized high-diffusivity paths relative to the adjacent grain bulk.

caption: Charpy impact testing apparatus utilized for assessing the toughness and energy absorption of the 3D printed pieces.
summary: Charpy impact testing is depicted in this panel, highlighting the equipment used to determine the mechanical toughness of the 3D printed samples. This visual documentation of the impact test setup is essential for understanding the energy absorption capabilities of the printed pieces within the overall mechanical evaluation framework.

caption: Low-magnification HAADF-STEM micrograph of MgZn2 precipitates in the OA1 specimen.
summary: This low-magnification HAADF-STEM image displays the distribution of MgZn2 precipitates within the OA1 specimen. The micrograph serves as a baseline for observing the initial state of interfacial coherency, which is characterized as fully coherent in this specific aging condition before further evolution occurs in subsequent specimens.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots illustrating the passive film growth on HT-NAB alloy during extended immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky curves for the HT-NAB alloy demonstrate the evolution of passive film growth over an extended immersion period in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These plots serve as the basis for determining the semiconducting properties and carrier densities of the protective surface films formed on the alloy.

caption: Absorbance spectra of β-carotene in n-hexane extracted from XG/DD NCs, comparing concentration ratios (CR) of 0.4 (black) and 2.5 (red).
summary: Absorbance spectra of β-carotene loaded within XG/DD NCs are presented for two different concentration ratios. The data illustrates the spectral characteristics of the encapsulated β-carotene, providing insight into the loading efficiency and the chemical state of the guest molecules within the XG/DD nanocarrier matrix.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for the d-band of a labeled Ag atom on a clean Ag-Pt (1 0 0) alloy surface.
summary: This panel displays the PDOS for the d-band of a specific Ag atom within a clean Ag-Pt (1 0 0) alloy surface. The analysis, part of a broader study on orbital hybridization, provides a baseline for evaluating how spatial overlap between adsorbate frontier orbitals and metal surface states influences binding strength.

caption: Schematic representation of the prediction model architecture developed without the application of transfer learning.
summary: This schematic illustrates the architecture of the prediction model, which is designed without transfer learning. The model structure is identical to the wall prediction model but relies exclusively on the experimental dataset for training purposes, highlighting the specific data-driven approach used to generate predictions in this configuration.

caption: XRD tomographic slices showing the spatial distribution of the γ-phase within a pillar extracted from sample s0.
summary: This panel displays selected tomographic slices acquired for sample s0, illustrating the distribution of the γ-phase. The reconstruction is derived from XRD-contrast scanning imaging, providing a detailed view of the phase arrangement within the extracted pillar specimen, which serves as a basis for understanding the internal microstructural characteristics.

caption: Upconversion emission spectra of SL:Er,Yb powders and their composites with CsPbBr3, CsPbBr1.5I1.5, and CsPbBr2.25I0.75 under 980 nm excitation, showing intensity variations in green and red emission bands.
summary: This panel displays upconversion emission spectra for SL:Er,Yb and various CsPbX3-SL:Er,Yb composites under 980 nm excitation. Notably, the CsPbBr1.5I1.5+SL:Er,Yb composite exhibits a 65% reduction in green emission intensity and a 145% enhancement in red emission intensity, illustrating the significant impact of halide composition on the upconversion luminescence properties.

caption: Micro-CT image of a mold-cast sample showing the distribution and morphology of internal pores.
summary: This micro-CT image displays the internal pore structure of a mold-cast sample. Observations indicate that the pores within this cast material exhibit a predominantly spherical morphology, contrasting with the irregular shapes typically found in 3D-printed counterparts, as revealed through comparative tomographic analysis of the two processing methods.

caption: First-layer Cr segregation energies under the influence of cation-F molecular pairs, illustrating the increased energy barrier for segregation relative to the isolated F anion case.
summary: Calculated segregation energies for Cr are presented for cation-F molecular pairs. The results demonstrate that the presence of the cation increases the first-layer segregation energy relative to the single F anion case. This confirms the screening effect of the cation, which acts to inhibit Cr surface segregation in the system.

caption: Polar plot displaying the residual stress anisotropy for the specimen annealed at 573 K for 30.7 ks, showing a distribution comparable to the 120 s condition.
summary: Extended annealing for 30.7 ks at 573 K maintains a residual stress distribution that is similar to the specimen annealed for 120 s. The radar chart confirms that the stress relaxation achieved at shorter durations is stable, with no significant further evolution in the anisotropy of the residual stress.

caption: Strain-life (ε MAX - N f) fatigue performance comparison between LPBF SS316L LED and HED samples, with run-out tests marked by arrows.
summary: This panel illustrates the strain-life fatigue behavior of LPBF SS316L samples built with different energy densities. The plot compares the ε MAX versus number of cycles to failure (N f) for both LED and HED conditions, highlighting contrasting performance trends and identifying run-out tests with arrows to indicate samples that did not fail.

caption: Distribution of SHAP values across different samples, illustrating the influence of specific features on model predictions.
summary: This panel displays the SHAP value distribution for various samples, providing insight into how individual features contribute to the model's output. Reference analysis indicates that lower valence electron concentration (VEC) values correlate with higher SHAP values, highlighting the significant impact of VEC on the underlying material property predictions.

caption: Raman spectra of a PEDOT:PSS pellet, a blank PEDOT:PSS/TPU film, and a composite film containing paracetamol-loaded microparticles, evaluated both before and after drug release.
summary: Raman spectroscopy confirms the chemical structural presence of PEDOT:PSS within the 3D printed films. Post-release analysis reveals the continued presence of PEDOT and PSS functional groups, demonstrating that the conducting polymer does not degrade during the drug release process and maintains its chemical integrity within the composite structure.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of the cold-rolled Fe-24.1Ni-4.06Al-0.43C alloy microstructure in region C, viewed from the transverse direction at a cold-rolling strain of 2.07.
summary: This bright-field STEM micrograph displays the cold-rolled microstructure of an Fe-24.1Ni-4.06Al-0.43C alloy in region C, observed from the transverse direction at a cold-rolling strain of 2.07. The image reveals the internal structural characteristics developed during the cold-rolling process, providing a baseline for the detailed magnifications shown in subsequent panels.

caption: Time-transformation-temperature (TTT) diagram for Ni-based superalloy 718 generated by JMatPro 13.3, comparing precipitation kinetics between the dendrite core (dotted line) and interdendritic region (continuous line).
summary: The TTT diagram, modeled via JMatPro 13.3, highlights the influence of chemical composition gradients on precipitation kinetics. While differences exist between the dendrite core and interdendritic regions, the γ' precipitation kinetics remain approximately equivalent, explaining the consistent γ' content observed across various processing routes like AP-DED, cast, PBF, and wrought materials.

caption: Dynamic equilibrium assessment at LR impact velocity for the DYN-C-L8-tooling specimen, showing incident force F1, transmitted force F2, and the force disequilibrium percentage R.
summary: Dynamic equilibrium at LR impact velocity is demonstrated for the DYN-C-L8-tooling specimen. The plot displays incident force F1, transmitted force F2, and the force disequilibrium percentage R. Optimal dynamic equilibrium was achieved, confirming that the specimen maintains a consistent mechanical response during the high-strain-rate SHPB testing process.

caption: Integrated photoluminescence intensity versus excitation power density for sample P027 at 10 K, illustrating a nonlinear power-law dependence.
summary: Integrated photoluminescence intensity for sample P027 is presented as a function of excitation power density at 10 K. The experimental data, fitted with a solid line, reveals a nonlinear behavior, distinguishing it from samples exhibiting pure radiative recombination. This nonlinear trend is characteristic of the optical quality observed for this specific sample.

caption: Deformed morphology of both alpha and beta phases in the EM-L sample.
summary: The deformed morphology of both the alpha and beta phases in the low-oxygen sample is shown here. This structural arrangement demonstrates the material's enhanced ability to coordinate equiaxed microstructures under stress, resulting in a wider plastic deformation zone compared to the high-oxygen counterpart.

caption: Recovery strain as a function of temperature for SA samples aged at 850 °C following 4% pre-strain.
summary: Recovery strain (εrec) is plotted as a function of temperature for SA samples aged at 850 °C after 4% pre-strain. The curve illustrates the strain recovery upon heating to 120 °C and cooling to room temperature, characterizing the material's shape memory capability under this high-temperature aging condition.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the D120 sample quantifying local plastic strain at the ASB.
summary: The Kernel Average Misorientation map provides a quantitative visualization of the local plastic strain distribution within the D120 sample at the adiabatic shear band. This map complements the other EBSD data by highlighting the localized deformation gradients and misorientation accumulation resulting from the high-strain shear process.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves comparing calcined and spent powder catalysts (CAT-P and SUL-P).
summary: Panel D presents the TGA analysis results for calcined and spent powder catalysts, specifically CAT-P and SUL-P. This thermal characterization provides insight into the mass changes and stability of the powder catalysts, allowing for a comparison between their initial calcined state and their condition after the reaction process.

caption: STEM-BF image of the Ni-20Cr alloy crack tip at Location III after 20 s of molten KCl-MgCl2 corrosion, highlighting an undissolved alloy region near the crack tip indicated by a yellow arrow and a white dashed line tracing the salt/alloy interface.
summary: This STEM-BF image captures the Ni-20Cr alloy microstructure at a crack tip after 20 seconds of molten salt corrosion. A distinct undissolved alloy region is visible near the crack tip, marked by a yellow arrow. The salt/alloy interface is delineated by a white dashed line, illustrating the initial corrosion propagation mechanism.

caption: Velocity magnitude contour plot at an azimuth angle of 90° showing the flow field characteristics.
summary: The velocity magnitude contour plot at an azimuthal angle of 90° illustrates the flow field characteristics for the two-bucket Savonius turbine. This CFD-derived visualization helps characterize the aerodynamic behavior, specifically highlighting the flow patterns that contribute to the observed turbulence and reduced efficiency at this particular blade orientation.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curve obtained from an in-situ tensile test performed using a Deben Microtest stage.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curve obtained from an in-situ tensile test performed using a Deben Microtest stage. An ultrasensitive transducer was utilized to gather force and strain data instantaneously during the test, providing a precise record of the mechanical response of the material under uniaxial tensile loading conditions.

caption: Fe-V-Cr ternary phase diagrams at 480 °C and 700 °C, illustrating the measured chemical composition range within the TEM lamella as a gray region.
summary: The Fe-V-Cr ternary phase diagrams at 480 °C and 700 °C display the measured chemical composition range within the TEM lamella as a gray region. These diagrams, alongside the Fe-V-Al system, are utilized to deduce the phases formed within the material, given the relatively low Cr concentrations present.

caption: CO-DRIFT spectra of silica-supported Cu nanoparticles collected at various temperatures, showing a single characteristic peak at approximately 2128 cm⁻¹.
summary: The CO-DRIFT spectra for silica-supported Cu nanoparticles exhibit a single peak centered at 2128 cm⁻¹. This signal is attributed to either Cu⁺-CO carbonyl species or the atop binding of CO molecules on the copper nanoparticle surface, confirming the interaction of the probe molecule with the copper sites.

caption: Transverse width heat map for a single-bead, multi-layer wall-type sample subjected to a single milling intervention followed by the deposition of three additional beads.
summary: This heat map illustrates the transverse width measurements for a wall-type sample after milling and the subsequent deposition of three beads. The results demonstrate a clear increase in the transverse cross-sectional width, confirming that the addition of beads onto the milled surface significantly alters the final sample geometry.

caption: Contour profiles representing the depth of the melt pool across different energy densities, highlighting inherent variability between successive tracks.
summary: Melt pool depth contour profiles are shown for varying energy densities. These profiles demonstrate the geometric variations present between successive melt tracks. The data illustrates how different laser parameters influence the depth of the melt pool, accounting for the inherent variability observed during the laser processing of the material.

caption: Storage modulus curves as a function of temperature for 3D printed unfilled and BC-filled samples.
summary: The storage modulus curves for 3D printed unfilled and BC-filled samples are displayed as a function of temperature. These results demonstrate that the storage modulus values decrease with increasing temperature, which indicates a reduction in elastic energy storage for both the unfilled and filled material formulations during the DMA testing.

caption: Digital Model (DM) configuration illustrating non-real-time information flow where operators manually transfer data from the physical twin to the virtual twin for processing and subsequent procedure improvement.
summary: The Digital Model (DM) represents a non-real-time integration level. Operators manually bridge the physical and virtual twins by transferring data for processing. This analysis provides insights that allow operators to refine manufacturing procedures, thereby improving the physical twin's performance through a human-in-the-loop, offline feedback mechanism.

caption: Cumulative frequency distribution of the Si phase area measured in 1 mm casting samples.
summary: This plot displays the cumulative frequency of the Si phase area within 1 mm casting samples. The data illustrates how the Si phase area is distributed under these specific cooling conditions, providing insight into the structural characteristics of the Si phase compared to thicker 3 mm samples.

caption: Ternary composition space plot displaying the distribution of the 52 as-deposited Pd-Ag-Ni alloy samples, highlighting the compositional range and Ni-rich bias.
summary: This ternary composition plot illustrates the distribution of the 52 as-deposited Pd-Ag-Ni alloy films. The samples span composition ranges of 14–51 at.% Pd, 8–53 at.% Ag, and 21–74 at.% Ni, revealing a clear bias toward the Ni-rich region within the ternary composition space.

caption: Sensitivity analysis visualization for the evaluation of new EBMs across four distinct scenarios.
summary: This sensitivity analysis visualization provides a comparative evaluation of new EBMs across four defined scenarios. By illustrating both similarities and differences in performance metrics, the plot serves as a precise visual representation of the data summarized in Table 7, facilitating a clearer understanding of the model evaluation results.

caption: Temperature versus solid fraction (fs) curves for four distinct alloys, generated using Scheil solidification simulations with solute trapping via Thermo-Calc 2025a.
summary: This panel displays temperature versus solid fraction curves for four alloys, derived from Scheil solidification simulations incorporating solute trapping. The 738_STD alloy exhibits a unique behavior, retaining a small liquid fraction at lower temperatures compared to the other alloys, which indicates a steeper gradient at the end of the solidification process.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectra of PI-1-PPC and PI-2-PPC polymers, showing extinction coefficients of 84.3 cm−1 and 88.4 cm−1 at 405 nm, respectively.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectra demonstrate that the synthesized PPCs possess similar optical properties. Specifically, the extinction coefficients at 405 nm are measured at 84.3 cm−1 for PI-1-PPC and 88.4 cm−1 for PI-2-PPC, confirming consistent light absorption characteristics across the different polymer compositions under investigation.

caption: Raman analysis of the MXene-lubricated sample wear track, revealing amorphous carbon (zone 2) intermixed with spatially separated MXene-related species (zone 1).
summary: Raman analysis of the sample lubricated with 5 mg/mL Ti3C2Tx confirms the existence of amorphous carbon in zone 2. These carbon species are partially intermixed with spatially separated MXene-related particles or species found in zone 1, demonstrating the complex chemical composition of the tribofilm formed during the testing process.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay curve and corresponding fitting for TPU/5S composite at 490 nm emission.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime decay and fitting curves for the TPU/5S composite are presented at an emission wavelength of 490 nm. Monitored at room temperature with an excitation wavelength of 373 nm, this sample demonstrates the characteristic decay behavior of the TPU/SAOED composite system under the specified optical conditions.

caption: Relative growth area of granulation tissue measured at four distinct time points throughout the study.
summary: This bar chart quantifies the relative growth area of granulation tissue, confirming that 3DSC treatment promotes faster tissue formation than other groups. The data highlights the accelerated healing trajectory of 3D-printed scaffolds, where granulation tissue growth is most pronounced during the early stages of the 21-day healing period.

caption: Height-to-width ratio (h/w) of SiC–Fe3O4-PVA nanocomposite ink droplets on glass and PVA substrates at 25, 50, and 70 °C, comparing conditions with and without an applied magnetic field.
summary: This plot illustrates the droplet morphology of SiC–Fe3O4-PVA nanocomposite ink on glass and PVA substrates across varying temperatures. The data shows that applying a magnetic force underneath the substrate pins the ink, increasing the width and resulting in lower h/w ratios compared to non-magnetic conditions at the tested temperatures.

caption: High-resolution STEM observation of the specimen subjected to fatigue–creep conditions with a tensile strain dwell at 650 °C.
summary: High-resolution STEM imaging provides a detailed look at the material microstructure after fatigue–creep testing with a tensile strain dwell at 650 °C. This panel highlights the specific morphological changes and dislocation arrangements resulting from the combined cyclic loading and tensile hold period applied to the specimen.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of SL-NiNPs in DMSO solution containing 0.2 g of cotton, monitored over sonication times ranging from 1 to 30 minutes.
summary: UV-Vis spectroscopy tracks the interaction between SL-NiNPs and cotton fibers. As sonication time increases from 1 to 30 minutes, the intensity of the characteristic peak at 318 nm decreases significantly, particularly during the initial stage, before stabilizing. Additionally, the peak exhibits a noticeable shift toward lower wavelengths over time.

caption: Effective index variation plotted as a function of the normalized parameter d/λ.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the effective index and the d/λ ratio. When d/λ is significantly less than one, the normalized index remains low, causing the guided ray to approach its critical angle. Consequently, the effective index values converge toward the cladding refractive index, facilitating deep wave penetration.

caption: Coefficient of friction versus time measurement for Cu components fabricated via MFFF featuring a solid infill configuration.
summary: Wear analysis of Cu processed through the MFFF method is presented for a solid infill configuration. By recording the coefficient of friction over time, this plot demonstrates the tribological response of the fully dense, solid-infill material, serving as a baseline for comparing the performance of different internal structural infill patterns.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the glaze layer, confirming its amorphous nature and showing elongated α-Al nanograins embedded within the matrix.
summary: This high-resolution TEM image provides further evidence of the amorphous structure of the glaze layer. It reveals elongated nanograins embedded within the Al2O3 glaze matrix, which are identified as α-Al through FFT diffraction analysis, confirming the composite-like nature of the worn surface layer at the atomic scale.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the CR specimen showing a grain boundary region with significant Mg solute segregation.
summary: This APT reconstruction of the CR specimen reveals a grain boundary characterized by a high concentration of Mg atoms. The observed segregation of Mg to the grain boundaries in this specimen is consistent with the structural analysis provided by the atom probe tomography data collection.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a ruptured DS CM247LC specimen showing dislocation lines within the γ’ phase, visualized using a 6 at.% Cr iso-compositional surface.
summary: This APT reconstruction reveals the morphology of dislocation lines within the Al-rich γ’ phase of a ruptured DS CM247LC specimen. The dislocation structure is identified by a 6 atomic percent Cr isosurface, providing a three-dimensional visualization of atomic distribution and structural features following high-temperature creep deformation.

caption: Equilibrated BCC phase snapshot generated via Monte Carlo simulation, representing a 30 × 30 × 20 unit cell supercell with average post-annealing composition.
summary: This Monte Carlo simulation snapshot illustrates the equilibrated BCC phase structure, modeled using a 30 × 30 × 20 unit cell supercell based on average post-annealing compositions. The visualization reveals distinct atomic ordering tendencies, specifically showing Al atoms preferentially surrounded by Ni, Fe atoms by Co, and Cu atoms undergoing segregation.

caption: Steady-state coefficient of friction (COF) plotted against surface roughness (Ra) for UHMWPE specimens.
summary: This panel displays the steady-state coefficient of friction for UHMWPE tested against as-printed and mechanically polished surfaces. The COF, defined as the ratio of tangential to normal force during sliding, is plotted as a function of surface roughness (Ra), illustrating the frictional behavior under these two distinct surface conditions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of region D, demonstrating the orientation relationship between Ni and Ni3Al phases.
summary: The diffraction pattern from region D reveals a specific orientation relationship between the Ni and Ni3Al phases. It is observed that the [112] crystal axis of the Ni phase is parallel to the [001] crystal axis of the Ni3Al phase, defining their crystallographic alignment within the microstructure.

caption: Electron backscatter diffraction map of the SLMed IN718 superalloy, illustrating the grain structure and morphology.
summary: The EBSD analysis of the SLMed IN718 superalloy provides a detailed visualization of the grain structure. This map serves as the primary characterization tool to understand the grain size and overall microstructure of the material following the selective laser melting process, revealing the spatial distribution of grains within the sample.

caption: High-speed photographic observation of the molten pool during short-circuit transfer, showing final oscillation and stirring effects.
summary: This high-speed photographic image displays the molten pool during short-circuit transfer, showing the final stages of oscillation and stirring. The combined action of droplet impact pressure and arc impact pressure effectively enhances the flow of the molten pool, contributing to the overall dynamics observed during the welding process.

caption: Molybdenum (Mo) elemental map illustrating the distribution of heavy alloying elements.
summary: Molybdenum elemental mapping displays the distribution of Mo throughout the specimen. The map indicates that molybdenum is concentrated in specific regions, correlating with the presence of Mo-rich carbides. These findings align with established microstructural characteristics of similar alloys, where Mo contributes to the formation of complex carbide phases.

caption: 1H-13C CPMAS NMR spectrum of cross-linked GAn@HPC-24 h, accompanied by a structural sketch illustrating the cross-linking configuration.
summary: The 1H-13C CPMAS NMR spectrum of the cross-linked GAn@HPC-24 h material is presented alongside a structural sketch. This solid-state NMR analysis was performed on the fine powder form to confirm the successful cross-linking nature of the composite material, providing evidence of the chemical environment within the synthesized structure.

caption: In-plane grain reference rotation deviation (GRRD) map derived from Heaviside-DIC measurements, characterizing the rotation field within the specimen after 1.26% plastic deformation.
summary: The GRRD map provides a detailed view of the in-plane rotation field across the region of interest after 1.26% plastic deformation. Derived from Heaviside-DIC measurements, this map complements the EBSD data by quantifying the average rotation for each grain, effectively highlighting localized rotational deviations within the deformed microstructure.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of the 3D-printed Violet ink filter, detailing the wavelength-dependent transmission properties of the printed filter.
summary: Violet ink filters show a unique optical transmission spectrum that quantifies the light-filtering behavior of the 3D-printed structure. This data illustrates the specific transmission characteristics of the Violet ink, providing insight into its spectral response and performance as an optical filter.

caption: Live/dead fluorescence images of HUVECs and MSCs printed within 2Alg3GM hydrogels containing 0, 1, 5, and 10 mg mL-1 PSC after 24 hours of incubation.
summary: Live/dead staining images visualize the viability of HUVECs and MSCs printed in 2Alg3GM hydrogels with varying PSC concentrations. The results demonstrate similar cell viability values across every experimental group after 24 hours, indicating that the printing process and PSC concentrations are non-cytotoxic to the encapsulated cells.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for the steel simulated at a peak temperature of 900 °C with a grain size of 10 μm.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of steel simulated at 900 °C with a 10 μm grain size. Numerical modeling using JMatPro software predicts microstructural evolution under varying cooling rates, with red arrows highlighting reference cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s for comparative analysis.

caption: Thermo-magnetization (M-T) curve of the as-prepared Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwire measured under a magnetic field of 0.05 T or 0.3 T, highlighting the martensitic transformation and the ferromagnetic to paramagnetic austenite transition.
summary: The thermo-magnetization curve of the as-prepared Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwire displays distinct transitions between martensitic and austenitic phases. Blue arrows indicate the Hopkinson effect, characterized by sharp peaks near the Curie temperature, marking the transition from ferromagnetic austenite to paramagnetic austenite under applied magnetic fields of 0.05 T or 0.3 T.

caption: Potentiostatic discharge test results for Al-10 wt%RE binary alloys, where the Al-Nd alloy displays the highest potential, indicating the greatest initial resistance to corrosion.
summary: Potentiostatic discharge test results for the Al-10 wt%RE binary alloys reveal distinct electrochemical responses. The Al-Nd alloy demonstrates the highest potential during the test, suggesting that it possesses the greatest initial resistance to corrosion among the investigated binary alloys when subjected to the specified electrochemical testing conditions.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectra of trypsin (1 g/L) evaluated at 313 K for SL/trypsin mass ratios between 0 and 0.8 g/L.
summary: At 313 K, the trypsin emission peak remains centered at 327 nm. The peak fluorescence intensity of the protein solution decreases gradually with higher concentrations of SL, illustrating that the quenching phenomenon is maintained across the tested temperature range as the SL/trypsin mass ratio increases.

caption: Ternary projection of the Fe-Si-B system calculated via FactSage 8.1 using the FTlite database, highlighting specific alloy compositions.
summary: This ternary phase diagram projection for the Fe-Si-B system was generated using FactSage 8.1 and the FTlite database. It identifies the positions of FeSi24B11 (green circle), FeSi26B9 (pink triangle), and the pilot-scale FeSi21B10 alloy (orange diamond), providing a visual representation of these specific compositions within the system's equilibrium landscape.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph from the 0001 zone axis, demonstrating the end-on visualization of Type II defects.
summary: Imaging from the 0001 zone axis, this bright-field STEM micrograph confirms that Type II defects appear end-on in this orientation. This perspective is critical for characterizing the morphology of these linear defects, which show alignment within the (0001) basal plane and are distinct from other observed defect types in the material.

caption: EBSD IPF map of the 0.5 wt% ZrH4 alloy after heat treatment, viewed along the XZ cross-section.
summary: This EBSD IPF map depicts the heat-treated 0.5 wt% ZrH4 alloy in the XZ cross-section. High-angle grain boundaries are indicated by black lines. The grain size distribution and orientation in this heat-treated state provide insight into the structural changes occurring after the thermal treatment process compared to the as-built condition.

caption: Raman spectra of PLA, PLA-1CaP, PLA-2CaP, and PLA-12CaP scaffolds, highlighting characteristic PLA bands between 2000 and 200 cm-1 and the calcium phosphate symmetric stretching mode near 960 cm-1.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals the bonding configuration of PLA and composite scaffolds. PLA exhibits strong bands at 1769, 1455, 1126, 1043, 872, 398, and 298 cm-1. The addition of calcium phosphates introduces a distinct symmetric stretching mode near 960 cm-1, confirming the successful incorporation of inorganic phases into the polymer matrix.

caption: Representative flow cytometry plots showing the apoptotic cell populations for control, IOX1, PTT, and IOX1 + PTT treatment groups.
summary: Flow cytometry plots visualize the apoptotic percentage of OS cells under various conditions. The data reveal that the IOX1 + PTT group exhibits the highest proportion of apoptotic cells (71%) compared to the control (3%), IOX1 (4%), and PTT (31%) groups, confirming the superior efficacy of the combined therapeutic approach.

caption: TGA thermogram of pure HPC showing the thermal degradation profile of the cellulose backbone.
summary: The TGA thermogram of pure HPC displays the thermal degradation process of the cellulose backbone. The curve exhibits a major mass drop at 350 °C, characteristic of the polymer's thermal decomposition. This baseline data serves as a reference for comparing the thermal stability of the modified GAn@HPC samples.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of the surface nanocrystalline TiN layer.
summary: This high-resolution transmission electron microscopy image reveals the structural characteristics of the surface nanocrystalline TiN layer. The micrograph provides a detailed view of the nanocrystalline morphology, serving as the primary visual evidence for the surface layer's microstructure as described in the study of TiN layer properties.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction of an Optimized ZIRLO sample, highlighting the spatial distribution of Zr ions in purple and ZrO ions in green.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction of an Optimized ZIRLO sample displays the spatial distribution of Zr and ZrO ions. The wide field-of-view allows for the analysis of oxide layers along the specimen shank, with reconstruction parameters calibrated based on the geometry of a beta-Nb precipitate.

caption: Aggregated confusion matrix illustrating the predictive performance of the random forest classifier at k=5 for droplet type classification.
summary: This aggregated confusion matrix displays the classification performance of a random forest model at k=5 for identifying droplet types. The model demonstrates high predictive accuracy, maintaining a 98% success rate as confirmed by the experimental results, providing a clear overview of the classifier's ability to correctly categorize the droplet samples.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer, featuring numbered peaks from 1 to 19.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of the synthesized BBZ monomer, featuring peaks numbered 1 through 19, confirms the molecular structure. This analysis validates the presence of ArCH2N, OCH2N, alkylene chain carbons, as well as aromatic and alkene carbons, consistent with the expected chemical composition of the bio-based benzoxazine monomer.

caption: Nyquist plots representing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) response of 0-MAO, Zn-MAO, and Cu-MAO coatings immersed in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance behavior of 0-MAO, Zn-MAO, and Cu-MAO coatings in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These plots, fitted using the equivalent circuit model, characterize the impedance response of the bilayer MAO coating structure, providing insights into the charge transfer resistance and porous layer resistance of the samples.

caption: FTIR spectra of CFRP samples measured at 25 °C, 120 °C, and 200 °C.
summary: This figure displays the FTIR spectra of CFRP samples at three distinct temperatures: 25 °C, 120 °C, and 200 °C. These spectroscopic measurements provide insight into the chemical state and potential thermal degradation or structural changes of the CFRP material as it is subjected to varying thermal conditions.

caption: Feature importance ranking derived from the XGBoost model, illustrating the relative contribution of various input variables to the predictive performance of the algorithm.
summary: This feature importance plot highlights the key variables driving the XGBoost model's predictive performance. The analysis emphasizes that refining feature engineering and increasing dataset size are essential strategies to enhance the model's overall robustness and predictive power, as indicated by the learning process and model validation results.

caption: Relative length change (ΔL/L0) curve for the E-X structure over a complete thermal cycle, with pointed lines 1, 2, and 3 marking reproducible kinks observed at specific temperatures.
summary: The ΔL/L0 curve for structure E-X is presented over a full thermal cycle. Pointed lines 1, 2, and 3 highlight specific, reproducible kinks in the length change data. These features indicate distinct thermal response events occurring at consistent temperatures during the cycling process of the E-X unit cell structure.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of chondrocytes treated with PBS (0 µM H2O2) showing universal cell survival with green-stained live cells.
summary: Chondrocytes treated with PBS serve as a control group, exhibiting universal cell survival. The live-dead assay, visualized via fluorescence microscopy, shows green-stained cells, confirming that the baseline condition maintains high viability without the cytotoxic effects of hydrogen peroxide exposure.

caption: Measured transmission spectrum of the CuCrZr + 316L composite along the build direction, contrasted with the theoretical spectra for both CuCrZr and 316L components.
summary: The transmission spectrum for the CuCrZr + 15 wt% 316L specimen is presented following FOBI reconstruction. By comparing this result with theoretical spectra for both constituents, the analysis demonstrates that the strong texture characteristic of the pure CuCrZr alloy is significantly reduced in the mixed composite sample.

caption: Three-dimensional full-field strain nephogram showing the local strain variation in the middle region of the as-deposited specimen during tensile testing, where lower strength is observed.
summary: Representing the middle region of the as-deposited specimen, this three-dimensional full-field strain nephogram highlights local strain variations during tensile testing. The observed lower mechanical strength in this region is potentially linked to the occurrence of cracks at the criss-crossed interface, as revealed by the strain distribution analysis.

caption: Tensile strengths and elongations of NiTi alloys with different Ni contents measured in the building direction.
summary: Tensile strength and elongation data for NiTi alloys are plotted for the building direction. The results indicate that increasing the Ni content leads to a significant enhancement in tensile strength, while the elongation behavior follows a non-monotonic trend, first increasing and then decreasing as the Ni content varies.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of pre-deformed wrought IN 718 showing interaction between dislocations and coarse carbides.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph of pre-deformed wrought IN 718 demonstrates a reduced dislocation density relative to AM IN 718. The image highlights the interaction of dislocations with coarse carbides, as indicated by arrows. These observations confirm that dislocations in the wrought alloy are anchored by these larger, distinct carbide precipitates.

caption: Logarithmic amplitude-frequency characteristic diagram illustrating the impedance magnitude |Z| for 2507 DSS samples across different energy densities.
summary: This Bode plot displays the logarithmic amplitude-frequency characteristics of the 2507 DSS samples. The impedance magnitude |Z| values are consistently high across all three energy density groups, serving as a key indicator for characterizing the corrosion resistance of the material when evaluated alongside the phase-frequency characteristic data.

caption: Interfacial misfit dislocation network in the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al system doped with 2 at.% Re atoms, showing slightly bent dislocation lines compared to the pristine configuration.
summary: Incorporation of 2 at.% Re atoms into the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al system results in the formation of an interfacial misfit dislocation network. Compared to the pristine system, the dislocation lines appear slightly bent, indicating that the presence of Re atoms influences the interfacial dislocation morphology after the energy minimization process.

caption: Comparison of matrix hardness values for LPBF-processed DSS 2205 and WC/W2C reinforced DSS composites.
summary: This panel compares the matrix hardness of LPBF DSS 2205 and WC/W2C reinforced LPBF DSS composites. The reinforced composites exhibit hardness values exceeding 400 HV 0.5, attributed to solid-solution strengthening from the diffusion of W and C atoms into the matrix during the LPBF fabrication process.

caption: Schematic representation of the δ-Ni2Si precipitate crystal structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic arrangement within the unit cell of the δ-Ni2Si precipitate found in the alloy. The schematic provides a clear visualization of the crystal structure, which is one of the specific precipitate phases identified within the material system as described in the study.

caption: Load versus deflection curves derived from 3-point bending tests, indicating a decrease in flexural strength from 70.08 MPa to 53.80 MPa for CCFR-bronze.
summary: Load-deflection curves obtained from 3-point bending tests are plotted to compare bronze and CCFR-bronze. The experimental results demonstrate a 23% reduction in flexural strength, with values decreasing from 70.08 MPa in the bronze specimen to 53.80 MPa in the CCFR-bronze specimen, highlighting the impact of the reinforcement.

caption: Easy-axis (EA) magnetic hysteresis loops for 15 nm NiFe thin films deposited on Kapton substrates at sputtering powers ranging from 25 W to 100 W.
summary: Panel e displays the easy-axis magnetic hysteresis loops for NiFe films on Kapton. The coercive fields appear independent of the sputtering power, mirroring the behavior observed in the hard-axis loops for this substrate, indicating that the magnetic characteristics are stable despite changes in the thin film deposition power.

caption: Modified Prusa i3 3D printer architecture featuring two integrated U and V movement axes designed to support the APPJ system.
summary: This schematic illustrates the modified Prusa i3 3D printer configuration, which incorporates two additional movement axes, U and V, to accommodate the APPJ system. The original heated bed was replaced with a custom assembly to support these new axes, enabling precise positioning for the plasma jet experimental setup.

caption: Complex shear modulus of linear printed p-MRE plotted against magnetic field strength at 0.1% shear strain across various frequencies.
summary: This plot illustrates the complex shear modulus of linear printed p-MRE at a 0.1% shear strain amplitude. Peculiar phenomena manifest even at these extremely small strain amplitudes, which minimize nonlinearity. Furthermore, the shear modulus is observed to increase gradually as the frequency rises from 0.01 Hz to 100 Hz.

caption: Raman spectrum of 80% porous carboHIPEs used to evaluate the degree of graphitization.
summary: This panel displays the Raman spectrum for 80% porous carboHIPEs. The data was collected to investigate the degree of graphitization within the carbonaceous material. This spectroscopic analysis provides insight into the structural characteristics of the porous carboHIPE sample, serving as a baseline for comparing different porosity levels.

caption: Detailed FTIR spectra from 1800 to 500 cm⁻¹ showing protein-specific amide bands, where the intensity of the C=O stretching at 1635 cm⁻¹ increases with higher SPI content.
summary: Focusing on the 1800 to 500 cm⁻¹ region, these FTIR spectra illustrate protein-related characteristic bands. The intensity of the amide I band at 1635 cm⁻¹ increases with SPI content, while a shoulder at 1539 cm⁻¹ (amide II) and a C-N stretching band at 1240 cm⁻¹ are also observed.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of the worn surface of Ti2-HEA, revealing significant fold deformation and oxidation layers.
summary: Atomic force microscopy of the Ti2-HEA worn surface reveals significant fold deformation and the presence of an oxidation layer. These morphological features indicate a more severe wear process compared to the Ti16.6-HEA variant, consistent with the observed deeper grooves and higher surface roughness characteristic of lower titanium content alloys.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram showing the cooling curve for the advancing side of a friction stir weld processed at 450 rpm and 10 kN.
summary: This panel displays the CCT diagram for the advancing side of a friction stir weld under 450 rpm and 10 kN conditions. The cooling curve is plotted against the transformation regions, including martensite, austenite, ferrite, and carbide phases, to illustrate the thermal evolution and phase transformation behavior during the welding process.

caption: Quantitative elemental analysis profile measured along a line crossing the secondary γ′ precipitates and the γ matrix after 100 hours of exposure.
summary: Quantitative elemental analysis results are presented for a line scan crossing the secondary γ′ precipitates and the γ matrix after 100 hours of heating at 800 °C. This profile provides precise data on the elemental segregation occurring between the phases, confirming the diffusion-controlled nature of the γ′ particle growth.

caption: Deconvoluted C 1s XPS spectrum of carbon following a 30-minute plasma treatment process.
summary: Shown is the deconvoluted C 1s XPS spectrum for carbon after 30 minutes of plasma treatment. This plot characterizes the chemical state of the carbon surface at the longest treatment duration. The spectral analysis demonstrates the impact of prolonged plasma interaction on the surface chemistry and bonding configurations of the carbon sample.

caption: Bode plot representing the impedance modulus and phase angle for the X-Z section of the Wall 0 sample.
summary: This Bode plot displays the electrochemical impedance characteristics of the Wall 0 sample's X-Z section. Initial immersion tests reveal an impedance modulus of approximately 10⁴ Ω·cm² at low frequencies. Over a 14-day period, this value decreases by an order of magnitude, signifying a progressive degradation of the material's barrier properties.

caption: EDS elemental map showing the spatial distribution of Tungsten (W) within the analyzed region at point C.
summary: Tungsten (W) distribution is shown in this EDS elemental map at point C. By mapping the six constituents using TEM-EDS, the spatial arrangement of Tungsten is revealed, enabling a detailed comparison of the chemical composition between the amorphous and crystalline columns identified at the top of the layer.

caption: Confusion matrix evaluating action recognition performance for the image dataset at a resolution of 224x224 pixels.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the classification performance for the image dataset at 224x224 resolution. Diagonal values represent the proportion of correctly classified instances across 11 actions, while off-diagonal values indicate misclassifications. It serves as one of the four best-performing configurations, demonstrating the model's effectiveness in recognizing specific action classes.

caption: Over-parameterized CNN-1 architecture featuring 46,455 parameters, designed as a standard 1D convolutional model for LPBF monitoring.
summary: The CNN-1 architecture is depicted as a standard 1D convolutional design, specifically developed for AE-based LPBF monitoring frameworks. With 46,455 parameters, this model serves as an over-parameterized baseline to benchmark performance against capacity-constrained models, ensuring a literature-consistent evaluation of monitoring frameworks that do not incorporate zero-shot transfer learning capabilities.

caption: Confusion matrix for the CNN2 quality monitoring model, illustrating the distribution of predicted versus actual classification labels.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the classification accuracy of the CNN2 model on the testing set. By plotting actual labels on the y-axis and predicted labels on the x-axis, the matrix allows for a detailed assessment of how effectively the CNN2 architecture performs in the quality monitoring task.

caption: Normalised fatigue crack initiation lives and the number of cycles to reach a stable damage state plotted against the input variable derived from Monte-Carlo analysis.
summary: This plot displays the results of a Monte-Carlo analysis, showing normalised fatigue crack initiation lives and the number of cycles to reach a stable damage state as functions of input variables. Run-outs are represented by zero initiation lives, while the stable state increases with the input variable, indicating a delayed elastic-dominant tensile response.

caption: RMSF and B-factor profiles for Tcu3516 protein residues.
summary: The RMSF and B-factor curves for Tcu3516 are plotted to identify flexible regions within the protein structure. By analyzing these values, three specific non-regular structures, including Loop1, Loop2, and the C-tail, were initially selected for further investigation due to their high flexibility and potential for modification.

caption: Normalized S/N curve for MMJ and MBJ samples, demonstrating the relative fatigue performance across LCF and HCF regimes using experimentally determined fatigue limits.
summary: Normalized S/N curves reveal that the fitted MMJ curve consistently lies above the MBJ curve across both low-cycle and high-cycle fatigue regimes. Data points positioned above the normalized line indicate samples where applied stress exceeded the fatigue limit, confirming that fatigue failure is expected after a finite number of cycles.

caption: Time-dependent plot of the average laser speckle speed in the X-direction for wire collapses on tracks 316 and 306, derived from point tracking analysis.
summary: This line graph presents the average speed of laser speckles in the X-direction over time for two analyzed melt bridge collapses on tracks 316 and 306. The data, obtained through point tracking, quantifies the wire movement during the collapse process, providing a temporal profile of the wire's horizontal velocity components.

caption: One-dimensional concentration profile of Re across the γ/γ′ interface derived from APT reconstruction.
summary: The concentration profile of Re across the γ/γ′ interface is extracted from APT reconstruction data. Analysis indicates that Re partitioning behavior is significantly influenced by high boron additions, with observed concentrations in the γ phase of alloy B-2 being notably lower compared to those in alloys B-0 and B-1.

caption: Three-dimensional surface plot depicting the impact of applied load and sliding distance on wear rate, while maintaining a constant sliding velocity of 2 m/s.
summary: Depicted here is the 3D surface plot of wear rate versus applied load and sliding distance at a constant velocity of 2 m/s. A quadratic increase in wear rate occurs as both parameters rise, with the applied load demonstrating a more significant influence on the wear rate than the sliding distance.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curve of the two-step deposited Cu–Zn–Ni–Co alloy in 1 M KOH at 40 °C, showing multiple discernible oxidation peaks.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry curve for the Cu–Zn–Ni–Co alloy, prepared via a two-step deposition process, exhibits several discernible peaks when tested in 1 M KOH at 40 °C. These peaks reflect the complex electrochemical dissolution behavior of the alloy, which is analyzed to determine its specific dealloying parameters.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200-GT SPVM module, comparing experimental data from the FDM with results generated by the ADIPSO-VC optimization algorithm.
summary: This plot displays the I-V characteristics of the KC200-GT SPVM module. It compares experimental data obtained from the FDM against the results produced by the ADIPSO-VC algorithm. The visualization demonstrates the effectiveness of the ADIPSO-VC approach in accurately modeling the electrical performance of the specific photovoltaic module configuration.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF-Z) triangle displaying the distribution of relative corrosion depths for 91 grains of 90Cu-10Ni alloy, where color intensity indicates the relative height range following acid NaCl exposure.
summary: This inverse pole figure triangle maps the relative corrosion depths of 91 individual grains in a 90Cu-10Ni alloy. The distribution reveals a clear grain orientation dependence of the corrosion rate, allowing the triangle to be divided into three distinct regions based on the observed relative surface height variations.

caption: Raman spectrum of the uncured VAR resin sample.
summary: This panel displays the Raman spectrum of the uncured VAR resin. Raman scattering measurements were performed using a Renishaw inVia Qontor spectrophotometer to characterize the chemical state of the unpolymerized resin specimen, providing a baseline for comparison with the cured material treated with PP 5.

caption: Load-displacement (P-h) curve for SLM-316L steel subjected to a loading rate of 5 mN/min during nanoindentation.
summary: This load-displacement curve illustrates the indentation response of SLM-316L stainless steel at a 5 mN/min loading rate. The data demonstrates that indentation displacement increases rapidly with the applied load, providing a baseline for evaluating the material's creep behavior during the subsequent holding stage under constant load.

caption: Isometric view of the Kelvin unit cell, illustrating the variable strut diameter design which ranges between 3 mm and 5 mm.
summary: Isometric visualization of the Kelvin unit cell highlights the variable strut diameter, which is specified to range between 3 mm and 5 mm. This geometric variation is a critical parameter in the lattice design, influencing the mechanical performance and structural integrity of the final cast component produced via additive manufacturing.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing extracted QS and the synthesized QSGM1, highlighting a broad absorption peak at 3346 cm-1 in the QS spectrum attributed to hydroxyl groups and hydrogen bonding.
summary: FTIR analysis was performed to investigate the synthesis of QSGM. The spectrum for QS displays a characteristic broad peak at 3346 cm-1, which corresponds to hydroxyl groups and hydrogen bonding. Comparing the spectra of QS and QSGM1 allows for the identification of chemical changes resulting from the modification process.

caption: Single-cycle flexion signal response pattern for the affected side of the osteoarthritis-induced knee deformity group.
summary: Affected limbs in the osteoarthritis-induced knee deformity group demonstrate a 48% reduction in signal amplitude and a distinct blunting of peaks during single-cycle flexion. These findings indicate severe biomechanical impairment and altered load distribution characteristic of the pathological knee deformity.

caption: Scatter plot illustrating the relationship between Volumetric Energy Density (VED) and relative density, highlighting the specific VED range that achieves over 99% relative density based on 25 micrographic observation data points.
summary: This scatter plot displays the correlation between Volumetric Energy Density and relative density for 25 experimental data points. It specifically identifies the optimal VED range required to achieve a relative density exceeding 99%, providing a clear visualization of the processing window necessary for high-density material fabrication.

caption: ACE index representing alpha-diversity of the intestinal flora after 24 hours of fermentation.
summary: This box plot illustrates the ACE index, a measure of alpha-diversity, for the intestinal flora across all experimental groups. The data shows a decrease in the abundance of the intestinal flora in all groups, including the Blank group, following the 24-hour in vitro fermentation period.

caption: Bodipy staining images showing lipid peroxide generation in HCECs treated with Hy, Hy + D609, or Hy + D609 + Bru for 24 hours.
summary: Bodipy staining visualizes lipid peroxide generation in HCECs. The images demonstrate that Bru significantly elevates lipid peroxide levels in HCECs co-treated with D609 and Hy, further confirming that Bru promotes ferroptosis and counteracts the protective effects of D609 treatment under hyperosmolar conditions.

caption: Statistical distribution of porosity in L-DED deposited 2024 Al bulk samples, presented as a layer-by-layer analysis.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the layer-by-layer porosity statistics for L-DED deposited 2024 Al bulk samples. Statistical analysis reveals that pores are primarily located within columnar dendritic regions at the melt pool solidification front, with approximately 73.2% of the observed porosity concentrated specifically along the fusion line of the deposited layers.

caption: Metallurgical microstructure of the alloy under case V, showing the distribution of MDRX grains.
summary: This optical micrograph presents the metallurgical structure of the alloy under case V. The image provides a visual representation of the meta-dynamic recrystallization (MDRX) grains present in the alloy, contributing to the overall assessment of grain evolution during the inter-pass period under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve for the Al-Ni-REM alloy characterized by a 3/1 atomic ratio.
summary: This DSC curve illustrates the thermal behavior of the Al-Ni-REM alloy with a 3/1 ratio. The data provides insight into the phase transformation temperatures, with the reference noting that alloys containing Sm and Yb exhibit lower solidus temperatures compared to other compositions within the studied series.

caption: Comparison of material toughness and calculated temperature rise for AM 718 across various impact testing conditions, illustrating an inverse relationship where lower temperatures correlate with increased energy absorption and higher thermal spikes.
summary: This plot displays the toughness and calculated temperature rise for AM 718 under high strain rate loading. Toughness is derived from the area under the stress-strain curve, while temperature rise is calculated using material density and temperature-dependent specific heat. Results indicate that lower testing temperatures lead to higher stored energy and greater temperature increases.

caption: Vortex core trajectories following a 2 mT, 35 ns pulse, with cyan triangles indicating maximum deviations from a circular path relative to the pinning landscape.
summary: Trajectories of the vortex core are shown following a 2 mT, 35 ns pulse, mapped against the underlying pinning landscape. Cyan triangles highlight maximum deviations from circular motion. The background features illustrate pinning effects, including a notable 15 nm deviation observed in the lower left region of the disk.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the heat-treated sample, highlighting the distribution of γ′ precipitates within the γ matrix and identifying a specific dislocation feature.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the microstructure of a heat-treated sample, specifically visualizing the γ′ precipitates embedded within the γ matrix. The image identifies a dislocation feature, which serves as the focal point for subsequent compositional analysis to investigate solute segregation behavior following the full heat treatment process.

caption: Comparison of the original all-pixels-on input image and the resulting projected light profile at the vat platform without compensation.
summary: This panel displays the uncompensated projection of an all-pixels-on input image. By comparing the original input to the resulting light profile at the vat platform, it highlights the inherent inaccuracies in the projected blue light distribution before any corrective measures are applied to the digital micromirror device input.

caption: Dilatometric analysis of the uncoated GJL sample during austenitization, showing the temperature-dependent phase transformation range between Ac1 (695 °C) and Ac3 (809 °C).
summary: Dilatometric analysis of the uncoated GJL sample during austenitization reveals the temperature-dependent phase transformation range between Ac1 (695 °C) and Ac3 (809 °C). Within this specific thermal interval, the initial ferrite and pearlite microstructures are successfully transformed into austenite, as evidenced by the recorded dilatometer test data.

caption: Atomic structure visualization of stacking faults located within the γ matrix.
summary: This panel displays the atomic structure of stacking faults within the γ matrix of the CR10-DA specimen. By visualizing the atomic arrangement, this model provides insight into the structural nature of the defects that contribute to the internal stress concentrations observed within the matrix phase of the material.

caption: Thermal analysis overlays for PEEK dental implants printed at varying bedplate temperatures, highlighting differences in thermal behavior.
summary: Thermal overlays provide a comparative view of the thermal properties of PEEK dental implants printed at different bedplate temperatures. Consistent with the crystallinity data, these thermal profiles demonstrate that higher bedplate temperatures contribute to enhanced crystallinity, reflecting the influence of processing conditions on the final material properties of the implants.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the standardized effects of process parameters on relative density (RD) within the initial full quadratic model.
summary: This Pareto chart ranks the statistical significance of various process parameters on the relative density of the Cu–Cr–Zr alloy. By analyzing the full quadratic model, it identifies which factors contribute most to the response, serving as the initial step in the CCD analysis to optimize LPBF process parameters.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a 45° misorientation angle high-angle grain boundary specimen extracted from a heat-treated microstructure, where the grain boundary is highlighted by a boron isocomposition surface.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction displays a 45° misorientation angle high-angle grain boundary obtained from a heat-treated microstructure.
