The visualization specifically highlights the grain boundary interface using a boron isocomposition surface, providing a detailed 3D spatial representation of the atomic distribution at the boundary within the processed material.

caption: Computed tomography scan providing a cross-sectional view of the R20 sample internal morphology.
summary: Computed tomography scanning provides a detailed internal view of the R20 sample morphology. This scan acts as an experimental benchmark, allowing for a direct comparison between the internal structural features observed in the physical specimen and those predicted by various numerical modeling approaches.

caption: ANOVA statistical analysis plot with overlaid significance markers comparing surface roughness across different microneedle layer heights.
summary: The ANOVA plot in panel c provides a statistical comparison of surface roughness across various layer heights, featuring overlaid significance markers. The analysis confirms that there are no statistically significant differences in surface roughness metrics, such as R-squared and RSME, for microneedles manufactured with layer heights below 50 µm.

caption: Surface morphology of a single-layer NiTiCu deposit on a NiTi substrate processed at a current intensity of 70 A.
summary: This photograph presents the surface morphology of a single-layer NiTiCu deposit printed onto a NiTi substrate. The sample was processed using a current intensity of 70 A. The image illustrates the microstretch features observed on the substrate surface under these high-intensity printing conditions.

caption: Magnetisation hysteresis loop of the heat-treated sample acquired at ambient temperature using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM), demonstrating the magnetic response of the 3D lattice.
summary: The VSM-derived magnetisation hysteresis loop characterizes the magnetic properties of the heat-treated 3D lattice at ambient temperature. This measurement provides a visual representation of the material's magnetic response, confirming the magnetic behavior of the sample as part of the broader structural and thermal characterization of the Ni-Mn-Ga lattice.

caption: UV-Vis absorption profiles tracking the reduction of 4-NP over time in a 2.5 cm Pd/C CR with a 1.8 mm core diameter.
summary: UV-Vis absorption profiles track the reduction of 4-nitrophenol in a Pd/C coaxial reactor characterized by a 2.5 cm length and 1.8 mm core diameter. These spectral results, when analyzed through linear fitting of conversion versus time, contribute to the comparative study of how varying core diameters influence the overall catalytic reduction efficiency.

caption: Reproducibility assessment of the oxidation peak current for six independently fabricated Fe/Ni/N-CNT/GCE electrodes tested in 100 μM dopamine.
summary: Testing six independently fabricated electrodes in 100 μM dopamine yielded a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 4.73% for the oxidation peak current. This low RSD confirms good fabrication reproducibility for the Fe/Ni/N-CNT/GCE electrodes, indicating consistent performance across different batches of the sensor.

caption: EDS line-scan profile across the phase boundary of the delta ferrite grain, demonstrating a clear increase in Mo and Si atomic fractions consistent with the formation of Mo3Si silicides.
summary: An EDS line scan performed across the phase boundary of the delta ferrite grain quantifies the compositional changes in the irradiated 316 L specimen. The profile shows a distinct increase in Mo and Si concentrations, which corresponds to the segregation of molybdenum silicide in the form of Mo3Si.

caption: Phase stability map showing the Bo-Md positions for cpTi, Ti-6Al-4V, Ti42Nb, and Ti-20Nb-6Ta alloys.
summary: This phase stability map illustrates the calculated Bo and Md values for four titanium-based alloys: cpTi, Ti-6Al-4V, Ti42Nb, and Ti-20Nb-6Ta. By plotting these specific parameters against the established phase stability boundaries defined by Abdel-Hady et al. and Sidhu et al., the prevailing phase composition for each investigated alloy is accurately assessed.

caption: Survey XPS spectrum of the EME1.5N alloy corrosion products after immersion in 3 wt% KCl solution, showing peaks for Mg, O, Cl, and C.
summary: The survey XPS spectrum for the EME1.5N alloy with low Ni content reveals the presence of Mg, O, Cl, and C elements within the corrosion product film. Carbon is utilized for calibration purposes, while chlorine originates from the residual KCl solution trapped in the corrosion products after the immersion process.

caption: Force–displacement curves for Ni-based superalloy powders with varying particle sizes (<32 μm and 100–150 μm) subjected to a maximum indentation depth of 200 nm.
summary: This panel displays the force–displacement behavior of Ni-based superalloy powders with different particle sizes under a maximum indentation depth of 200 nm. The curves illustrate the mechanical response of these powders, providing essential data for evaluating their hardness characteristics compared to bulk alloy counterparts under identical loading conditions.

caption: 3D scatter plot of the first three principal components for a representative 0.1% GNP specimen, displaying overlapping data points from three different regions to demonstrate local material homogeneity.
summary: To evaluate local material homogeneity, a 3D scatter plot of the first three principal components is shown for a representative specimen containing 0.1% GNP. By comparing Raman spectra collected from three different regions of the same sample, the overlapping data points demonstrate a consistent and homogeneous material composition throughout the specimen.

caption: Neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain conducted with a 5x5x5 mm gauge volume in the build direction.
summary: Residual strain measurements are presented here, obtained using a 5x5x5 mm gauge volume oriented along the build direction. This experimental data provides a critical reference point for validating the coarse-mesh finite element model predictions, confirming the spatial distribution of strains within the cold-machined component.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectrum of the Ti 2p core level for the ADT25 sample, exhibiting characteristic Ti 4+ peaks.
summary: This panel displays the high-resolution XPS spectrum of the Ti 2p core level for the ADT25 sample. The spectra exhibit two dominant peaks corresponding to Ti 4+ 2p 3/2 at 458.8 eV and Ti 4+ 2p 1/2 at 464.6 eV, confirming the presence of Ti 4+ species on the ADT25 surface.

caption: Near-infrared (NIR) emission spectra recorded at 1538 nm for the SL:Er,Yb phosphor and the CsPbBr1.5I1.5+SL:Er,Yb composite, highlighting the spectral response in the NIR region.
summary: Near-infrared emission at 1538 nm is presented for both the SL:Er,Yb phosphor and the CsPbBr1.5I1.5+SL:Er,Yb composite. This spectral data confirms the presence of NIR emission characteristics for these materials under the specified excitation conditions, providing insight into the optical behavior of the phosphors beyond the visible range.

caption: Micro-CT image of a 3D-printed sample highlighting the irregular pore shapes and distribution.
summary: Micro-CT imaging of the 3D-printed sample reveals a high density of pores characterized by irregular shapes. This structural feature differs significantly from the more spherical pores observed in mold-cast samples, demonstrating that the additive manufacturing process fundamentally alters the internal porosity and pore geometry of the concrete structures.

caption: Cross-sectional morphology of Wrought-316L SS nitrided at 390 °C, characterized by uniformly distributed equiaxed grains and a thin, uneven nitrided layer.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the cross-section of Wrought-316L SS nitrided at 390 °C. The substrate consists of uniformly distributed equiaxed grains, distinct from the LPBF-processed material. The nitrided layer is relatively thin and exhibits significant structural defects, including obvious unevenness, severe local discontinuities, and spalling, indicating poor layer formation at this temperature.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves for Pd/C, PdNi/NrGO (1:1), and PdNi/NrGO (1:2) catalysts in 0.5 M formic acid and 0.5 M H2SO4 at a 50 mV·s⁻¹ scan rate, demonstrating their respective electrocatalytic activities for formic acid oxidation.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for Pd/C, PdNi/NrGO (1:1), and PdNi/NrGO (1:2) catalysts in 0.5 M formic acid and 0.5 M H2SO4 at a 50 mV·s⁻¹ scan rate, demonstrating their respective electrocatalytic activities for formic acid oxidation. These results confirm the electrocatalytic activity of the three Pd-based catalysts toward formic acid oxidation in acidic media.

caption: Taguchi experiment results for η as a function of duty cycle, maintaining a constant average current of 0.5 A/cm².
summary: Taguchi experimental results demonstrate the impact of duty cycle on the surface roughness reduction rate. By maintaining an average current density of 0.5 A/cm², the process achieves effective polishing performance, indicating that the reduction rate remains consistent and robust regardless of the specific duty cycle parameters applied.

caption: Schematic representation of the specimen geometry highlighting the specific longitudinal (L1, L2) and transversal (L3, L4, L5) lines selected for the residual stress analysis.
summary: This schematic illustrates the specimen geometry and identifies the specific longitudinal lines L1 and L2, along with transversal lines L3, L4, and L5, where residual stress distributions are analyzed. These selected locations serve as the reference framework for evaluating the longitudinal stress variations across the bridge structure before and after cutting.

caption: Detailed X-ray tomography view of the AB+TF specimen, emphasizing the near-surface pore structure and spatial arrangement.
summary: Detailed X-ray tomography view of the AB+TF specimen, emphasizing the near-surface pore structure and spatial arrangement. The image allows for a precise examination of how pores are distributed near the surface of the AB+TF sample, offering insights into the structural integrity and porosity characteristics of this specific specimen type.

caption: Calculated electronic band structure of pure ZnO, illustrating the intrinsic energy dispersion characteristics of the pristine material.
summary: This panel displays the calculated electronic band structure for pure ZnO. It serves as the baseline reference for evaluating the impact of solute elements on the electronic properties of the material, providing a clear visualization of the energy dispersion characteristics inherent to the pristine ZnO crystal lattice structure.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the JT0 alloy after solution treatment at 1170 °C and aging at 815 °C, revealing nanoscale γ precipitates embedded within the larger γ′ phase.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the JT0 alloy microstructure following solution treatment at 1170 °C and aging at 815 °C. It highlights the presence of nanoscale γ particles dispersed within the γ′ precipitates, a unique hierarchical metastable equilibrium microstructure that was experimentally observed in this specific superalloy composition.

caption: Predicted microstructural map and experimental validation for the Al-Fe-Cu ternary alloy system, identifying the CET boundary at β = 1.14.
summary: Representing the Al-Fe-Cu ternary system, this map correlates predicted microstructural features with experimental results. The data demonstrates that the Columnar-to-Equiaxed Transition (CET) is effectively predicted by the parameter β, with experimental compositions for the transition aligning at the threshold value of β = 1.14 across the ternary alloy space.

caption: Neovius TPMS unit cell oriented along the UVW axes.
summary: The Neovius TPMS unit cell is shown in the UVW orientation, mapping the structure to the x, y, and z axes. This representation highlights the specific geometric characteristics of the Neovius minimal surface unit, consistent with the orientation parameters applied to all unit cells in the software framework.

caption: Raman spectrum of the sintered material displaying characteristic D and G bands, confirming the presence of graphene.
summary: Raman spectroscopy confirms the presence of graphene within the sintered material through the detection of characteristic D and G bands. This spectroscopic evidence validates the successful incorporation of graphene into the composite, providing a clear signature of the carbon-based reinforcement phase within the tungsten-nickel-copper matrix.

caption: Surface strain distribution at the point of fracture for an as-built coupon oriented at θ = 0°.
summary: This panel displays the surface strain map of an as-built coupon tested at a 0° orientation. The visualization captures the localized strain distribution occurring at the moment of fracture, providing insight into the mechanical deformation behavior and failure characteristics of the material under this specific loading condition.

caption: Inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) images of the white dotted rectangular area from panel (c), processed using [1 1 ‾ 1] and [11 1 ‾ ] frequency vectors to isolate specific lattice features.
summary: Fourier-filtered IFFT images of the selected rectangular region in panel (c) are generated using specific [1 1 ‾ 1] and [11 1 ‾ ] frequency vectors. These filtered images provide a clearer visualization of the lattice distortions and structural features associated with the intersecting stacking faults identified in the high-resolution TEM data.

caption: Gradient evaluation of the drag function across the sample space, illustrating the relative influence of individual features (F) selected by the GEP model.
summary: This panel displays the gradient evaluation of the drag function, highlighting the specific features chosen by the GEP model to represent the output variables. By analyzing the gradients across the entire sample space, the plot identifies which features most significantly influence the drag function's behavior within the modeled system.

caption: Ashby plot comparing high cycle fatigue strength at 10^6 cycles against elastic modulus E for lattice materials in as-built and hirtisation-treated conditions.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the relationship between high cycle fatigue strength and elastic modulus for lattice materials. It demonstrates that hirtisation processing significantly enhances fatigue resistance compared to the as-built state for a given modulus. Specifically, hirtisation increases the fatigue strength to modulus ratio by approximately 90%.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the mid region, with an average density of 0.35.
summary: The GND density map of the mid region displays an average density of approximately 0.35. This spatial distribution of dislocations reflects the microstructural state at the middle of the build, providing quantitative insight into the local deformation characteristics compared to other regions.

caption: Case 3 numerical example of the upper domain distribution with a rotation matrix angle of pi/2.
summary: Case 3 presents the numerical distribution of the upper domain with the rotation matrix angle set to pi over two. This simulation visualizes the resulting domain morphology, allowing for a direct comparison of how different rotation matrix values influence the spatial arrangement of the upper domain in the model.

caption: Initial stage of the Cold Metal Transfer (CMT) process showing the arc plasma generation and the melting of the electrode tip and preceding deposited layer to form a molten pool.
summary: This high-speed image captures the initial phase of the CMT process. As the arc plasma is generated, the electrode end and the previously deposited metal layer melt to form a molten pool. This stage provides critical insight into the early mechanism of molten slag flow during the CMT process.

caption: Atomic model of the (Cr, Re)23C6 crystal structure in (001) projection, depicting Rhenium substitution at the Cr4 (48h) site.
summary: This model displays the (Cr, Re)23C6 crystal structure with Rhenium substituted at the Cr4 (48h) site in the (001) projection. It serves as the structural basis for the QSTEM simulation in panel (j), allowing for a comparative study of Rhenium site occupation effects.

caption: Visualization of detected internal defects within the ROI using VGEasyPore® software, including a detailed view of the fracture area.
summary: Visualization of detected internal defects within the ROI using VGEasyPore® software, including a detailed view of the fracture area. This analysis allows for the precise identification and spatial mapping of porosity and damage within the sample volume, providing critical insights into the internal integrity and failure mechanisms of the material.

caption: Fatigue failure cycle count for PLA bone scaffolds plotted against biodegradation time, showing a consistent decrease in fatigue resistance over the 30-day period.
summary: This plot illustrates the degradation of fatigue resistance in PLA bone scaffolds over a 30-day biodegradation period. It demonstrates that the cycle at which fatigue failure occurs decreases over time for all specimens, regardless of their specific topological design or surface-to-volume ratio, indicating a progressive loss of structural integrity.

caption: Time-dependent voltage and Faradaic efficiency for a Ni0.25Cu0.75-infiltrated cathode SOEC at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻², characterized by a continuous voltage increase.
summary: The electrochemical performance of a Ni0.25Cu0.75-infiltrated cathode SOEC is shown through voltage and Faradaic efficiency plots at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻². Consistent with other Cu-containing samples, the voltage profile exhibits a constant increase during the galvanostatic testing period, indicating specific degradation or activation behavior for this alloy.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe50 composite showing a minimum value of -9.63 dB.
summary: The Fe50 composite exhibits a reflection loss profile with a minimum value of -9.63 dB. This significant absorption enhancement, observed at 50 wt% Fe loading, highlights the effectiveness of increasing iron content in improving the electromagnetic wave absorption performance of the Fe/PLA/TPU composite materials within the tested frequency range.

caption: Vickers hardness values for 3D-printed PEEK specimens containing varying weight percentages of carbon fiber (CF).
summary: Vickers hardness measurements for 3D-printed CF/PEEK composites demonstrate that mechanical performance scales with carbon fiber content. The 30% CF/PEEK composite achieves the highest hardness, followed by the 15% CF/PEEK variant, while the pure PEEK specimen exhibits the lowest hardness, confirming the reinforcing effect of CF in the polymer matrix.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the distribution of strains in the load direction (εyy) for specimen TS-C2 at a compressive force of 300 kN.
summary: This contour plot displays the εyy strain distribution for specimen TS-C2 under a 300 kN compressive load. The visualization, derived from DIC measurements, highlights localized strain concentrations in the load direction, providing a spatial representation of the material's mechanical response near the bolt hole at the specified force level.

caption: Neutron diffraction pattern of the as-milled and treated alloy sample at 300 K, showing the austenite phase with experimental data points, Rietveld refinement profile, and the corresponding difference curve.
summary: Neutron diffraction measurements were performed to investigate the saturation magnetization evolution in austenite. The diffractogram at 300 K displays the experimental data points alongside the Rietveld refinement profile and the difference curve, confirming the structural characterization of the austenite phase within the as-milled and treated alloy samples.

caption: Hot processing map for WAAMed NiTi alloy at a true strain of 0.6, illustrating the final instability map configuration.
summary: The hot processing map at a true strain of 0.6 completes the series, with gray shaded areas marking the flow instability regions. These regions remain concentrated in the high strain rate area, demonstrating that the instability behavior of WAAMed NiTi alloys persists across the investigated range of true strains.

caption: Deformation behavior of NPR tubes, highlighting the transition between elastic and plastic platform regions as a function of wall thickness.
summary: The deformation characteristics of NPR tubes are shown, specifically focusing on the transition between elastic and plastic platform regions. The results indicate that this transition becomes smoother when the wall thickness is thin, providing insight into the structural response of the tubes under expansion loading conditions.

caption: Hydrogen charging behavior of Mg68Ni26M5X powder at 300 °C.
summary: This panel displays the hydrogen charging curve for Mg68Ni26M5X powder at 300 °C. Experimental data obtained from the MFM system demonstrates the activation of the compound under these thermal conditions. The curve represents the representative charging kinetics observed during the dynamic experimental process for this specific material composition.

caption: Reflectance spectral response of the sensor under 5 mW of 980 nm pump power, demonstrating a redshift from 1548.24 nm to 1557.88 nm across the humidity range.
summary: Under a 5 mW pump power at 980 nm, the sensor's reflection spectrum displays a redshift as the relative humidity increases from 14.1% to 85.2%. The resonance dip shifts from 1548.24 nm to 1557.88 nm, indicating that the pump power influences the spectral response characteristics of the humidity sensor.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Mg-Ni system, highlighting the temperature range of 650–750 °C as a shaded operating band.
summary: The Mg-Ni binary phase diagram illustrates the thermodynamic stability of various intermetallic phases. The shaded region between 650 °C and 750 °C represents the expected operating temperatures for molten salt systems. Formation of Ni-Mg intermetallic compounds is anticipated within this range, as confirmed by the phase diagram and associated literature.

caption: Refined K-means clustering output highlighting diffraction maxima in the Bi-Ronchigrams.
summary: Panel (f) provides a refined view of the K-means clustering output, specifically focusing on the localization of diffraction maxima within the Bi-Ronchigrams. This result demonstrates the effectiveness of the clustering sub-algorithm in isolating relevant signal features, which is essential for the accurate determination of centroid positions in later steps.

caption: Thermal strain versus temperature curves for pure ABS and ABS/Pyro composites containing 20, 30, and 40 vol% Zn1.6Mg0.4P2O7 filler, obtained via thermomechanical analysis.
summary: This TMA curve illustrates the thermal expansion behavior of pure ABS polymer compared to ABS/Pyro composites with varying filler concentrations of 20, 30, and 40 vol%. The data demonstrates how the incorporation of Zn1.6Mg0.4P2O7 filler influences the thermal strain characteristics of the ABS matrix across the measured temperature range.

caption: Precipitation-temperature-time (PTT) plot illustrating the kinetics of precipitate formation in Inconel 718 superalloy.
summary: This PTT diagram serves as a foundational guide for designing the heat treatment processes for Inconel 718 superalloy. By mapping the precipitation kinetics across temperature and time, it enables the precise selection of solution treatment parameters, such as the 900 °C to 980 °C range used for the as-built alloy specimens.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Cu in sample C2 at the 316L-Cu interface.
summary: Cu distribution in sample C2, visualized via EDS mapping, exhibits a smoother transition profile at the interface. This map confirms moderate diffusion and improved bonding over the C1 sample, as the Cu concentration changes more gradually across the 316L-Cu junction.

caption: Weibull fracture probability plot of compressive strength for LIS samples sintered in air at 1190°C for 3 hours.
summary: This panel displays the Weibull fracture probability plot for LIS samples sintered in air at 1190°C for 3 hours. The plot evaluates the characteristic compressive strength of the material, providing a statistically robust trend for the mechanical performance of the LIS ceramic under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) map of the cracking zone, highlighting the elemental distribution near the crack tip.
summary: This EPMA map illustrates the elemental distribution within the cracking zone. Analysis reveals distinct solidified protrusions, approximately 2–3 μm in length, located at the crack tips. These features are identified as deleterious phases resulting from W/Ta enrichment during the solidification process, providing insight into the crack formation mechanism.

caption: Sulphur and oxygen diffusion profile in alloy 1 at 1080 °C, showing a penetration depth of 410 ± 15 μm.
summary: This SEM-EDS analysis of alloy 1 illustrates the diffusion behavior of sulphur and oxygen at 1080 °C. The continuous line represents sulphur, while the dashed line indicates oxygen. The observed diffusion depth is measured at 410 ± 15 μm, providing insight into the elemental penetration within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Topographic surface map of the FeNiCr/PLA NC-Mg sample obtained via optical profilometry.
summary: This topographic map illustrates the surface roughness of the FeNiCr/PLA NC-Mg sample. The data was acquired using an optical profilometer to characterize the surface morphology. The visualization provides a detailed representation of the surface topography, which is essential for assessing the material's surface quality and roughness characteristics.

caption: Comparative Bode and Nyquist plots for S1, S2, and 5182 Al-alloy samples after 96 hours of immersion in 0.6 M NaCl.
summary: This comparative panel displays the final electrochemical state of all three samples after 96 hours of immersion. By overlaying the Bode and Nyquist plots, the figure highlights the differences in corrosion resistance and electrochemical impedance characteristics between the L-PBF fabricated S1 and S2 samples and the wrought 5182 Al-alloy.

caption: Variations of reduced modulus (Er) and hardness (H) as a function of cobalt concentration (cCo) for Sample A, with data points color-coded by crystal orientation according to the IPF map.
summary: This plot illustrates the dependence of reduced modulus and hardness on cobalt concentration in Sample A. Data points are color-coded by crystal orientation, with black spots indicating grain boundary indentations and gray bands representing multi-phase deformation. The measurements show an accuracy of approximately ±10 GPa for Er, with orientation-dependent hardness variations.

caption: Raman spectra of starch samples displaying all characteristic signals detected during the analysis.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was utilized to characterize the starch samples, with the resulting spectra displaying all expected characteristic signals. This analysis provides insight into the molecular vibrations and structural composition of the starches, confirming the detection of key spectral features across the samples.

caption: IPF map of LP-DED HX specimen tested at 204 °C, showing slip traces aligned with {111} planes.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map of the LP-DED HX specimen tested at 204 °C provides crystallographic orientation information near the fatigue crack initiation site. The map confirms that the slip traces observed in the corresponding BSE micrographs are aligned with the {111} planes of the material.

caption: 20-nm thick APT ion map slice showing the spatial distribution of Nb-rich clusters and Al-rich clusters within the material.
summary: This 20-nm thick APT ion map slice visualizes the spatial distribution of Nb-rich and Al-rich clusters. The reconstruction reveals that the locations of the Al-rich clusters do not coincide with those of the Nb-rich clusters, highlighting distinct segregation patterns of these solute-rich features within the analyzed material volume.

caption: Validation curves illustrating the percentage mean Dice Coefficient for dilution band and reprecipitated carbides across the evaluated models.
summary: This panel displays the performance of various models on the validation set during the training process. It specifically tracks the percentage mean Dice Coefficient for both dilution band and reprecipitated carbides, providing a clear metric to evaluate the segmentation accuracy and convergence behavior of the models under comparison.

caption: Simplified physical model of the 3D-printed differential photoacoustic cell, developed to minimize geometric complexity and reduce computational requirements for subsequent analysis.
summary: Representing a simplified physical model of the 3D-printed differential photoacoustic cell, this diagram serves to reduce geometric complexity. By streamlining the structural representation, the model effectively lowers computational costs, facilitating more efficient numerical simulations and analysis of the cell's performance characteristics within the photoacoustic system.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to cast Co-Cr alloy extracts.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the cast Co-Cr alloy group after 72 hours of exposure to extracts. The image reveals the viability of Human Gingival Fibroblasts, with green (live) and red (dead) cells, demonstrating the long-term cellular response to cast Co-Cr extracts after three days of incubation.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern obtained from the shark skin sample extracted from the trunk region.
summary: This XRD pattern characterizes the crystalline structure of shark skin harvested from the trunk region. As part of a broader investigation into the denticle crown composition, this diffraction data provides essential information regarding the mineralogical phase present in the biological material, serving as a primary structural analysis tool.

caption: Experimental yield strength values plotted against laser scanning speed for three distinct crystalline groups.
summary: Experimental yield strength data is presented as a function of laser scanning speed across three crystalline groups. The results demonstrate that yield stress varies significantly by crystallographic texture, with the <111> orientation exhibiting the highest strength, followed by <011> and <001>, which aligns with the theoretical predictions shown in the simulation.

caption: Schematic representation of the multilayer Ta/TaN thin film material and its specific thickness applied to the upper layer of the model.
summary: This schematic illustrates the multilayer Ta/TaN thin film structure integrated into the upper layer of the simulation model. The design specifies the material composition and layer thickness, providing the necessary parameters to evaluate the impact of the thin film on the overall surface CTE mismatch and structural integrity.

caption: FTIR spectra of the GEMA@PB composite hydrogel, displaying characteristic absorption peaks corresponding to both GEMA and PB components.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy analysis of the GEMA@PB composite hydrogel confirms the successful integration of its constituent materials. The spectrum reveals distinct characteristic peaks associated with both GEMA and PB, providing evidence of the chemical composition and successful synthesis of the composite hydrogel structure.

caption: Electron beam trajectory and corresponding surface electron density simulation at a beam current of 0.5 A, with 35 kV acceleration voltage and 0.9/0.3 A coil currents.
summary: This panel presents the electron beam trajectory and surface electron density at 0.5 A beam current. The reference states that increasing the beam current from 0.5 to 2.0 A at 35 kV enhances the electron density without affecting the beam trajectory, indicating stable focusing characteristics across these current levels.

caption: Equilibrium phase calculation for HEA-1 at 600 °C performed using the Thermo-Calc software with the TCHEA4 database.
summary: Equilibrium phase calculations for HEA-1 at 600 °C, generated using Thermo-Calc and the TCHEA4 database, indicate a complex phase constitution. The material consists of 47.8 mol% FCC, 25.0 mol% BCC, 21.2 mol% B2-NiAl (ordered BCC), and 6.0 mol% sigma-phase, providing a theoretical basis for the observed microstructural stability.

caption: Vickers hardness measurements for AFSD-deposited Ti-6Al-4V plotted against material feed rates of 111.8 mm/min, 83.6 mm/min, and 55.9 mm/min.
summary: This panel displays the Vickers microhardness results for AFSD Ti-6Al-4V builds, focusing on the influence of material feed rate. The box plot compares specimens B3 (111.8 mm/min), B4 (83.6 mm/min), and B5 (55.9 mm/min), illustrating the range and distribution of hardness values achieved under these different feed rate conditions.

caption: DF-TEM micrograph of the HT-2 sample showing the evolution of sub-grain structures resulting from the tempering of martensite.
summary: The DF-TEM micrograph of the HT-2 sample captures the evolution of sub-grain structures. By observing the changes in the martensitic packets, this image traces the structural tempering process, showing how the material develops into grains with defined boundaries, consistent with the observations made in the BF-STEM imaging.

caption: Detailed unit cell of the lattice structure highlighting key geometric parameters.
summary: This unit cell representation focuses on the key geometric parameters defining the bio-inspired lattice structure. Developed within the SolidWorks 2020 environment, this detailed view provides the fundamental building block dimensions necessary for characterizing the mechanical and thermal properties of the lattice, ensuring precise control over the heat exchanger's internal architecture.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) profiles and corresponding Ragone plot for the PPy/3D-IDCμE device, tested at current densities between 0.5 and 5 mA cm⁻².
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge characteristics were measured for the PPy/3D-IDCμE device at current densities ranging from 0.5 to 5 mA cm⁻². Based on these GCD results, the power density and energy density were calculated and presented in a Ragone plot, providing a comprehensive assessment of the device's energy storage capabilities.

caption: Raman spectra of PB and PB@QUE showing shifts in characteristic vibrational peaks.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals structural changes upon loading. The C≡N stretching vibration of PB at 2181 cm⁻¹ shifts to 2151 cm⁻¹, and the Fe–N/Fe–C bending vibration at 613 cm⁻¹ broadens to 624 cm⁻¹ in PB@QUE, indicating significant molecular interactions between the PB framework and the loaded QUE.

caption: Dynamic hardness (Hd) plotted against the tangent of the friction angle (tan ϕ), with an inset showing the evolution of the friction angle as a function of the major principal consolidation stress (σ1).
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between dynamic hardness and the internal friction angle for the tested material. The main graph demonstrates that dynamic hardness is highly sensitive to variations in the friction angle. The inset provides essential context by showing how the friction angle depends on the major principal consolidation stress.

caption: Scattering intensity versus scattering vector magnitude for a precipitate dissolution test conducted at a dissolution temperature of 875 °C, featuring experimental data points overlaid with solid-line mathematical fits.
summary: This plot displays a typical set of scattering curves obtained during a thermal cycle at 875 °C for a precipitate dissolution test. The experimental data points are represented alongside solid-line fits, illustrating the evolution of scattering intensity as a function of the scattering vector during the dissolution process.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of 316L/TiB2 composite on the longitudinal section showing grain morphology and orientation.
summary: Inverse pole figure map of the 316L/TiB2 composite on the longitudinal section reveals the grain morphology and size. EBSD analysis indicates that the columnar grains exhibit a preferred texture with a <001> orientation. This structural characterization provides insight into the grain distribution within the 6 wt% TiB2 reinforced material.

caption: Emission spectra of NiGa2O4:xEu films annealed at 950 °C under 325 nm excitation, displaying characteristic Eu3+ peaks ranging from 500 to 750 nm.
summary: Emission spectra for NiGa2O4:xEu films annealed at 950 °C, excited at 325 nm, reveal characteristic Eu3+ luminescence peaks. These transitions include 5D0 → 7F0 at 573 nm, 5D0 → 7F1 at 595 nm, 5D0 → 7F2 at 610 nm, 5D0 → 7F3 at 658 nm, and 5D0 → 7F4 at 700 nm.

caption: System block diagram illustrating the functional architecture and signal flow of the experimental setup.
summary: This system block diagram provides a high-level overview of the experimental architecture. It delineates the functional components and the pathways of signal flow within the setup, serving as a foundational schematic to understand the operational logic and connectivity of the system components used throughout the study.

caption: Atomic unit cell representations of the γ', γ'', and δ phases identified within the superalloy microstructure.
summary: This figure illustrates the distinct crystal structures of the γ', γ'', and δ phases found in the superalloy. These atomic models provide a structural basis for understanding the phase composition of the material, as confirmed by the reference sentences which explicitly identify these three phases within the analyzed microstructure.

caption: Heat map illustrating the Pearson correlation coefficients calculated for 21 selected features.
summary: This heat map displays the Pearson correlation coefficients for 21 features retained after a screening process. By reducing the initial set of 53 features to these 22, the visualization effectively mitigates the crowding issues found in the original confusion matrix, allowing for a clearer observation of the specific inter-feature relationships.

caption: Time-dependent cell voltage profile recorded during electrolysis at a constant current intensity of 0.6 A.
summary: This plot illustrates the cell voltage stability during electrolysis at a constant current of 0.6 A, corresponding to a current density of 150 mA cm-2. The voltage stabilizes rapidly at 5.45 ± 0.03 V within 30 seconds of operation, demonstrating consistent performance of the reversible electrochemical cell in electrolyzer mode.

caption: Temperature-dependent evolution of α and β phase fractions in a 40 wt% Zn alloy as predicted by Thermo-Calc calculations.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature dependence of α and β phase fractions for a 40 wt% Zn alloy, calculated using Thermo-Calc. It highlights the sensitivity of phase-fraction variations to temperature changes within the 350 °C to 550 °C range, providing a theoretical baseline for understanding phase stability in the alloy.

caption: Surface response plot showing the interaction between brushless motor type and flight duration on drone stability, with the frame length parameter maintained at its midpoint.
summary: Depicted here is the interaction between the brushless motor and flight duration variables regarding drone stability. With the frame length held constant at its midpoint, this surface response plot provides a clear view of how motor characteristics and flight time collectively impact the stability of the drone.

caption: Fast Fourier transform pattern of the γ′ precipitate from panel D, exhibiting characteristic superlattice reflections indicative of the L12 ordered structure.
summary: The FFT pattern of the γ′ precipitate displays distinct superlattice reflections, which are characteristic of the L12 ordered structure. This diffraction evidence confirms the ordered nature of the γ′ precipitates, providing a definitive crystallographic signature that supports the HRSTEM observations of the precipitate phase in the sample.

caption: Detailed optical path configuration for continuous laser additive manufacturing and ultrafast laser subtractive processing.
summary: This diagram delineates the specific optical paths utilized for both the continuous laser additive process and the ultrafast laser subtractive process. It highlights the individual pathways for each laser type, illustrating how the system manages distinct optical routes to facilitate both material deposition and material removal within a single platform.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the region shown in (a), acquired with the incident beam parallel to the [001] zone axis.
summary: The diffraction pattern corresponds to the region shown in the HAADF-STEM image of the track-track melt pool boundary. It was obtained using an incident electron beam aligned parallel to the [001] zone axis, providing crystallographic information about the local microstructure of the LPBF-processed 316L stainless steel sample.

caption: EEL spectra extracted from the entire data cube, highlighting the characteristic absorption edges for Co L3,2 and Ni L3,2 elements.
summary: This panel presents the EEL spectra extracted from the complete data cube, specifically identifying the Co L3,2 and Ni L3,2 absorption edges. These spectral features confirm the presence of cobalt and nickel in the VDM 780-b sample, facilitating the mapping of their spatial distribution across the analyzed microstructure.

caption: Tensile stress σ22 evolution at the left edge of the first layer (x1 = -60 mm, x2 = 0 mm) plotted against dimensionless time t* for build platform temperatures of 318 K (blue) and 318 K (orange).
summary: This plot illustrates the time-dependent tensile stress σ22 at the left edge of the first layer during the build process. The data is presented as a function of dimensionless time t* for two build platform temperature conditions, highlighting the stress evolution until the end of deposition and subsequent cooling.

caption: Short-circuit current curves for 3D-printed PVDF and PVDF nanocomposites, illustrating the electrical current response of the solid printed materials.
summary: Short-circuit current curves are presented for 3D-printed PVDF and PVDF nanocomposites. This panel provides a direct comparison of the current generation capabilities of the solid printed materials, serving as a baseline to understand the electrical performance improvements achieved through the integration of nanocomposite fillers within the PVDF matrix.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map showing grain orientation, with red regions highlighting annealing twins within green grains.
summary: The IPF map displays the crystallographic orientation of the cast sample grains. A key feature observed is the presence of annealing twins, indicated by red regions within the green-colored grains. This map provides insight into the grain structure and thermal history of the copper alloy.

caption: External power supply unit integrated with the enclosure, highlighting the power inlets and the emergency switch-off system mounted on the right side for rapid power termination.
summary: The image shows the external power supply connected to the 3D-printer via cables and inlets mounted on the enclosure. An emergency switch-off system is positioned on the right side of the enclosure, providing a manual mechanism to halt the power supply immediately in the event of an unexpected emergency.

caption: Pole figure of WAAM IN718 subjected to inter-pass rolling followed by SQA, displaying the lowest texture intensity of 1.73, indicating further randomization.
summary: Applying inter-pass rolling combined with SQA treatment to the WAAM IN718 walls results in the lowest observed texture intensity of 1.73. This indicates a high degree of texture randomization, which, combined with the refined grain size, ensures better statistical reliability for capturing macrostrain variations within the material.

caption: Impact strength measurements for FDM-printed ABS-FV specimens, illustrating the performance variation relative to PB content.
summary: Impact strength of vertical printing FDM parts (ABS-FV) is presented to evaluate mechanical performance. The data reveals the existence of dual thresholds for PB content in achieving optimal FDM performance, providing a quantitative assessment of the material's resistance to impact loading under vertical printing conditions.

caption: Third arc shape configuration of the SCA under CV power supply.
summary: Depicted here is the third arc shape of the SCA powered by a CV supply. The IWA and PMA continue to exhibit close coupling in a hybrid state, confirming that the arc maintains its structural integrity and hybrid characteristics despite the variations in the observed arc shape.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the AZ-B sample.
summary: This KAM map illustrates the local misorientation distribution within the AZ-B sample. The visualization provides insight into the spatial variation of dislocation density and lattice distortion, serving as a comparative baseline for evaluating the effects of different processing conditions on the internal strain state of the material.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the normalized strength and cost of room-temperature (squares) and high-temperature (circles) aluminum alloys, including three proposed designs relative to Wrought Al 7075.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the performance of various aluminum alloys by mapping normalized strength against cost. It highlights room and high-temperature alloys, including three novel designs. The data demonstrates that the proposed alloys achieve superior strength and cost-efficiency compared to the benchmark printable alloy, which is comparable to Wrought Al 7075.

caption: Laminar flame speed (SL,u) of R1234yf/air mixtures at an equivalence ratio of 1.1, initial pressure of 3 bar, and initial temperature of 333 K, comparing radiation-corrected (blue) and uncorrected (black) experimental data with optical method results (filled points) and simulation predictions (solid red line).
summary: This plot displays laminar flame speeds for R1234yf/air mixtures at 1.1 equivalence ratio, 3 bar, and 333 K. It compares radiation-corrected and uncorrected pressure-rise measurements with optical method results and simulation predictions. The extrapolated values from pressure and optical methods show high consistency, with pressure-derived results being slightly higher than optical ones.

caption: Diffusion path of the 1L|3R couple plotted on the Ni-Cr-Al ternary phase diagram, highlighting the Kirkendall plane and characteristic diffusion zone features.
summary: The diffusion path for the 1L|3R couple is presented on the Ni-Cr-Al phase diagram, showing an elongated path through the γ zone. Key markers include the Kirkendall plane, specific diffusion zone features, and the compositions of the end-members, demonstrating good qualitative agreement with theoretical postulates for interdiffusion.

caption: Creep strain rate plotted against time for S[100], S[210], and S[110] specimens, highlighting the minimum creep rate values observed at 850 °C and 450 MPa.
summary: The creep strain rate curves for S[100], S[210], and S[110] specimens are presented for the 850 °C/450 MPa test condition. This plot allows for the direct comparison of the minimum creep rates achieved by each specimen, demonstrating how secondary orientation influences the steady-state creep resistance of the material.

caption: Optimized structural result achieved with a volume fraction constraint of 0.09.
summary: This optimized structural geometry is produced using a volume fraction constraint of 0.09 and a fixed filter radius of 2 mesh elements. The result illustrates how the Optiworks framework effectively adapts to varying user-specific design requirements by producing distinct structural configurations based on the specified volume fraction parameters.

caption: FTIR spectra tracking the reaction between IBP and Mal-PEG 12 NHS in DMSO, highlighting the C=O stretching vibration at 1741 cm-1 used to monitor the succinimidyl ester consumption.
summary: FTIR spectra monitor the reaction kinetics between IBP and Mal-PEG 12 NHS. While most peaks are attributed to the DMSO solvent, the distinct peak at 1741 cm-1, corresponding to the C=O stretching vibration of the succinimidyl ester, serves as a critical marker to track the progress of the protein reaction.

caption: Nyquist plot illustrating the electrochemical impedance response of the XZ section of Wall 1.
summary: This Nyquist plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance of the XZ section of Wall 1. Consistent with the general behavior of the material, the impedance modulus starts near 10⁴ Ω·cm², followed by a decrease in the semicircle size after one day, reflecting the temporal evolution of the electrochemical interface.

caption: Field evaporation map of an Al 6026 tip acquired using the LEAP 4000 X Si instrument, highlighting specific crystallographic poles used for reconstruction calibration.
summary: This field evaporation map of an Al 6026 tip displays the detector space for the LEAP 4000 X Si instrument. Crystallographic poles marked in black were utilized to determine the reconstruction parameters zeta and k, while grey-labeled poles remain noteworthy but unused for calibration, ensuring accurate spatial orientation of the atomic data.

caption: Illustration of the nonlocal family and bond concept within peridynamic theory, depicting a circular horizon region surrounding a point of interest.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental nonlocal family and bond concept in peridynamic theory. It highlights a two-dimensional problem where the horizon is defined as a circular region, establishing the spatial domain for nonlocal interactions between points within the material continuum for subsequent mechanical analysis.

caption: Equilibrium solidification simulation of AA2024 waDED material assuming full atomic diffusion.
summary: Equilibrium solidification simulation for AA2024 waDED material assumes full diffusion, allowing atoms to redistribute according to thermodynamic equilibrium. This model highlights the presence of stable SPPs like AlCuMnFe(Si,Mg) and Al7Cu2(Fe,Mn,Mg), which persist in both non-heat-treated and heat-treated conditions because their dissolution requires temperatures exceeding 532 °C.

caption: Fatigue crack growth (FCG) curves comparing L-oriented (L_2) and T-oriented (T_4) brazed specimens tested at 950 °C.
summary: This plot displays the fatigue crack growth behavior of brazed specimens with different orientations, L_2 and T_4, at 950 °C. The experimental results demonstrate that grain orientation does not significantly influence the crack growth rate at this elevated temperature, indicating a lack of orientation dependency in the material's fracture performance.

caption: CD spectra comparing native lysozyme and PTL film, with insets showing Congo red-stained and ThT-stained fluorescent images of the nanofilm.
summary: CD spectra show that native lysozyme is predominantly α-helical, while the PTL nanofilm is composed of β-sheet structures. ThT staining confirms this, as fluorescence intensity at 484 nm significantly increases in the PTL film, indicating a higher concentration of β-sheet structures compared to the native protein.

caption: Detailed view of the tool geometry, including specific design features and physical dimensions.
summary: This panel provides a detailed schematic of the tool used in the FSW and FSP processes. It highlights the critical design features and physical dimensions of the tool, which are essential parameters for controlling the heat input and material flow during the welding and repair operations.

caption: Optical spectrum of the BOSL device under single-longitudinal mode (SLM) operation, showing a central wavelength of 1564 nm and a side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of 33 dB.
summary: This panel illustrates the optical spectrum during SLM operation, achieved by pumping both the MLL and TISE waveguides. The resulting spectrum features a central wavelength of 1564 nm and a high SMSR of 33 dB, confirming the successful transition to a stable single-mode state through electrical control of the TISE current.

caption: STEM bright-field image of the HEA/1 wt% HER composite displaying the formation of dislocation cell structures with high boundary density.
summary: STEM bright-field imaging demonstrates the formation of dislocation cell structures within the HEA/1 wt% HER composite. Observations indicate that the dislocation density at the boundaries of these cells is notably higher in the composite compared to the HEA matrix, suggesting enhanced dislocation storage capabilities.

caption: Transverse rupture strength (TRS) of green WC-Co parts as a function of binder saturation levels ranging from 20% to 50%.
summary: The transverse rupture strength of green WC-Co parts is evaluated across varying binder saturation levels from 20% to 50%. High green body strength is maintained through this process, indicating that the binder composition and saturation levels are optimized to ensure structural integrity and dimensional accuracy during the initial fabrication stages.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram for IN718 alloy, illustrating the transformation kinetics relative to temperature and time.
summary: This TTT diagram for IN718 alloy serves as a critical guide for heat treatment processes. It facilitates the control of alloy strength by identifying the solvus temperatures for delta and gamma-double-prime phases at 950 °C and 1050 °C, respectively, enabling precise dissolution of intermetallic compounds and subsequent rapid cooling.

caption: True stress-strain curves derived from tensile testing, highlighting the enhanced elongation of the Y-L-HX sample reaching approximately 36%.
summary: True stress-strain curves are displayed to provide a more accurate representation of the material's deformation behavior. The Y-L-HX sample demonstrates a significant increase in elongation, reaching 36 ± 2.6%, which reflects the improved plastic deformation capabilities and ductility resulting from the specific microstructural modifications described in the study.

caption: Peak-peak displacement (Δdp) versus cycle number for [001]//LD samples, illustrating failure behavior across varying stress levels and m values.
summary: This plot displays peak-peak displacement (Δdp) against cycle number for [001]//LD samples. At 220 MPa, the sample exhibits a distinct Δdp jump at failure, contrasting with the gradual increase observed in other conditions. For samples below 220 MPa, clear Δdp jumps are typically associated with low levels of distortion.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto425 dye, demonstrating the filtering effect of the printed material.
summary: The transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk incorporating Atto425 dye is shown. This measurement evaluates the optical filtering performance of the printed material, providing a standardized comparison point for the different dyes tested in the study.

caption: EDS line scan profile across the transition zone of a single track In718 deposit on a substrate after solution heat treatment.
summary: EDS line scan data for the transition zone of an In718 single track after solution heat treatment reveals the elemental content variation from the molten pool to the substrate. This analysis highlights the chemical distribution changes at the interface, providing insight into the bonding characteristics following the thermal treatment.

caption: Trimetric view of the 3D monostructure composition at θ = 10°, integrating the profiles from the -π/3, neutral, and +π/3 planes.
summary: This 3D reconstruction illustrates the final monostructure assembly at a θ value of 10°. By integrating the S-shaped profiles from the -π/3, neutral, and +π/3 planes, the visualization demonstrates how the individual geometrical parameters combine to form the complete, interconnected 3D unit cell proposed in the study.

caption: Tecnai TEM image at -3 °C, illustrating the grain as it becomes almost entirely composed of the B2 phase.
summary: As the temperature reaches -3 °C, the TEM analysis shows that the grain has become almost fully transformed into the B2 phase. This progression confirms the consistent advancement of the B19’ to B2 transition, with the majority of the grain structure now exhibiting the high-temperature B2 phase characteristics.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for the 50–100 μm powder fraction, with a calculated median particle size (D50) of 64.58 μm.
summary: This histogram displays the particle size distribution for the 50–100 μm screened RHEA powder fraction. The data indicates a median particle size (D50) of 64.58 μm. The distribution reflects the successful classification of the spherical powder, which exhibits high sphericity and surface quality suitable for additive manufacturing processes.

caption: Hysteresis cycles for a 3D printed toroid (T-AM) measured at 1 and 10 kHz frequencies.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic hysteresis behavior of a 3D printed toroid sample. The loops are captured at 1 kHz and 10 kHz frequencies to evaluate magnetic performance. These cycles illustrate the material's response under alternating magnetic fields, providing insight into the energy dissipation characteristics of the AM-processed core.

caption: Ni self-diffusion energy barriers for two different solute types, comparing the effects of a fixed Re atom (1Re1Mo) versus a fixed Mo atom (1Mo1Re) across seven inequivalent sites.
summary: This panel presents the Ni self-diffusion barriers tuned by two distinct solute species. The data compares configurations where either a single Re atom or a single Mo atom is fixed at the 1I site, demonstrating the sensitivity of diffusion energy to the specific combination and positioning of different solute atoms.

caption: UV-VIS absorbance spectra of Au@TA and Au@TA_Fe(III) nanoparticles, comparing samples before and after dialysis purification.
summary: The UV-VIS spectra illustrate the optical properties of Au@TA and Au@TA_Fe(III) nanoparticles. Spectral analysis confirms a characteristic maximum absorbance for the TA-Fe(III) complex at 620 nm before dialysis (pH < 3.0) and at 600 nm after purification (pH 3.0–7.0), demonstrating the successful formation and purification of the nanoparticle complexes.

caption: Thermal cycling profile utilized during the brazing process, featuring distinct holding times of 10, 30, and 60 minutes to investigate microstructural evolution.
summary: The thermal cycle curve illustrates the brazing process parameters, specifically the temperature profile over time. Holding times of 10, 30, and 60 minutes are implemented to study how these thermal conditions influence the microstructural development and subsequent mechanical properties of the brazed Ti4822 joints.

caption: Annular dark field electron image of LBP-DED IN718-NbC in the heat treatment A condition, revealing the microstructural morphology.
summary: This annular dark field electron image provides a high-resolution view of the LBP-DED IN718-NbC microstructure following heat treatment A. The imaging technique effectively highlights the distribution of secondary phases within the matrix, serving as the primary structural context for the subsequent diffraction and compositional analysis presented in the figure.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the high boron alloy tip highlighting element distribution.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction illustrates the microstructure of a high boron alloy tip. Research by Kontis et al. indicates that increasing boron content leads to the enrichment of M5B3-type borides along grain boundaries, while M23C6 carbides gradually disappear from these regions as the boron concentration increases.

caption: Temperature dependence of the low-field AC magnetic susceptibility, χ´(T), for a Ni-Mn-Ga single-crystal substrate measured during heating and cooling cycles between 30 and 120 °C.
summary: The temperature dependence of the AC magnetic susceptibility, χ´(T), is plotted for a Ni-Mn-Ga single-crystal substrate. Measurements were conducted during both heating and cooling cycles within the 30–120 °C range, characterizing the magnetic response of the substrate material as it undergoes thermal transitions.

caption: Wall shear stress distribution across the Offset Split-P structure with 90% porosity.
summary: Shown is the wall shear stress distribution for an Offset Split-P structure with 90% porosity. This final panel in the series completes the comparison of four distinct porosity levels, illustrating the spatial distribution of shear stress and providing insight into the performance characteristics of the highest porosity structure.

caption: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values for the catalyst samples, determined from the CV curves to estimate the electrochemical surface area (ECSA).
summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitances were employed to investigate the electrochemical surface areas of the catalysts. By analyzing the CV curves, the Cdl values provide a quantitative measure of the active surface area available for the electrochemical reactions, facilitating a comparative assessment of the different catalyst samples.

caption: Tafel slope analysis for the Mg–Er–Ni alloys, providing the kinetic parameters derived from the polarization curves to evaluate the corrosion behavior in 3 wt% KCl solution.
summary: The Tafel slope analysis provides essential kinetic parameters for the Mg–Er–Ni alloys in 3 wt% KCl solution. Together with the electrochemical parameters in panel c, these slopes confirm that the corrosion current density (Icorr) increases with Ni content, with the EME3N alloy exhibiting the most pronounced increase in corrosion rate.

caption: 3D reconstruction of the entire printed thick scaffold construct after two weeks of HUVEC incubation, visualizing the spatial distribution of cell nuclei (blue) and actin filaments (red) throughout the bioprinted structure.
summary: This 3D reconstruction provides a comprehensive view of the entire printed scaffold construct after 14 days of HUVEC incubation. The visualization highlights the successful proliferation and spatial distribution of cells throughout the thick construct, with nuclei stained blue and actin filaments red, confirming the bioactivity of the GelMA material.

caption: Calculated segregation free energies at 300 K for Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni in the CrMnFeCoNi alloy, comparing EMTO-based ferromagnetic (FM), paramagnetic (DLM), and non-magnetic (NM) states with PAW-based FM and NM states, where NM atomic positions remain unrelaxed.
summary: This plot displays the segregation free energies for the five constituent elements of the CrMnFeCoNi alloy at room temperature. The data compares results derived from EMTO and PAW computational methods across various magnetic states, including ferromagnetic, paramagnetic, and non-magnetic conditions, providing a comprehensive overview of elemental segregation tendencies in this high-entropy alloy.

caption: Corrosion potential of pre-oxidized Ni-30Cr alloy plotted against temperature in a 0.75NB2.75S environment, illustrating the influence of varying temperature increase rates following a 64-hour pre-oxidation treatment at 942 °C.
summary: This plot displays the corrosion potential of pre-oxidized Ni-30Cr alloy as a function of temperature within a 0.75NB2.75S environment. The data highlights how different temperature increase rates affect the electrochemical behavior of the material after it has undergone a standardized pre-oxidation process of 64 hours at 942 °C.

caption: Binary phase diagram for the Fe-Mo system depicting the phase stability regions for iron and molybdenum mixtures.
summary: The Fe-Mo binary phase diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the equilibrium phases present in the iron-molybdenum system. By defining the temperature and composition limits for different phases, this diagram facilitates the analysis of phase stability and the design of high-performance iron-based alloys containing molybdenum.

caption: Grain boundary distribution map for the FGH4096 side, categorizing boundaries into LAGBs (2–15°) and HAGBs (>15°) with an inset quantifying their relative proportions.
summary: Displaying the grain boundary distribution for the FGH4096 side, this map identifies LAGBs (2–15°) and HAGBs (>15°). The inset image provides the calculated ratio of these boundaries, facilitating a quantitative comparison of the grain boundary network across the different characteristic zones of the joint.

caption: Contact angle measurements over a 7-day monitoring period for PDMS, PDMS-O2, and SilMA/AA/PEGDMA composites containing 0 wt% and 1 wt% CNC.
summary: This bar chart displays the contact angle of various silicone-based materials over 7 days. The composite materials exhibit sustainable hydrophilicity with contact angles below 90º, contrasting sharply with the hydrophobic PDMS, which maintains a contact angle of 109.3 ± 4.9º throughout the monitoring period.

caption: Charge density map calculated for the Ni27Al27 supercell.
summary: The charge density map for the Ni27Al27 supercell illustrates the electronic distribution within the material. This visualization helps in evaluating the bonding strength between atoms, which is a key factor in determining the mechanical properties and dislocation slip behavior of the NiAl alloy system.

caption: Creep behavior characterization of the IN 718 alloy tested at 650 °C under a constant stress of 625 MPa.
summary: The creep behavior of the IN 718 alloy is characterized under high-temperature conditions of 650 °C and 625 MPa. This mechanical testing provides essential data on the alloy's deformation resistance, which is significantly influenced by the microstructural changes induced by the different heat treatment regimes applied to the material.

caption: Nyquist plot of the SOFC fed with ethanol, displaying a small high-frequency semicircle and an additional, significant low-frequency semicircle related to mass transport limitations.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the impedance response of an SOFC fed with ethanol at 800 °C. While the high-frequency semicircle remains small, a distinct, additional semicircle appears at very low frequencies. This low-frequency feature grows significantly when ethanol partial pressure is reduced, indicating relevant mass transport limitations during operation.

caption: Time-dependent derivative of MSD for species in a stack of five elemental layers modeled using the Choi interatomic potential.
summary: Panel c presents the derivative of MSD for species in a five-element layered stack using the Choi interatomic potential. Interdiffusion is non-constant, reflecting the time required for mixing. Manganese is observed to be the fastest diffusing component, whereas chromium is the slowest among the species modeled with the Choi potential.

caption: XRD patterns of printed A-aramid and S-aramid materials versus aramid fabric, showing diffraction peaks at 2θ = 20.5°, 23°, and 28.4°.
summary: XRD patterns for A-aramid, S-aramid, and the original aramid fabric are displayed to analyze crystalline structure. All three samples exhibit consistent diffraction peaks at 2θ = 20.5° (110), 23° (200), and 28.4° (004), indicating that the crystalline characteristics of the aramid fabric are maintained throughout the printing process.

caption: Quantitative data summary derived from EBSD analysis of T6-H samples across the specified strain rate range.
summary: Data table summarizing the quantitative EBSD analysis results for T6-H specimens tested at strain rates of 0, 3699, 5650, and 7452 s⁻¹. This table provides the numerical foundation for the microstructural observations, allowing for a direct comparison of crystallographic and dislocation-related metrics across the different experimental deformation conditions.

caption: Micro-CT reconstructed model of the R-Octet-30 metamaterial.
summary: The micro-CT reconstruction model of the R-Octet-30 metamaterial is displayed. This 3D rendering facilitates the analysis of the lattice geometry and structural fidelity, providing critical insights into the as-fabricated state of the R-Octet-30 specimen as reconstructed from the micro-CT scan data.

caption: Solid-state 31P CP-MAS NMR spectra comparing ODPA-modified NiTi nanoparticles to the pure ODPA phosphonic acid control.
summary: The 31P MAS-NMR spectrum of NiTi nanoparticles modified with ODPA exhibits a broad peak centered at 25.9 ppm, contrasting with the sharp 30.9 ppm peak of the pure ODPA control. This broadening indicates a disordered interface and diverse chemical environments for phosphonate groups resulting from NiTi-ODPA surface interactions.

caption: Storage and loss modulus evolution for 60 wt% Al2O3 composite resin during UV curing.
summary: DMA results for 60 wt% Al2O3 composite resin demonstrate a delayed gelation time of approximately 6 seconds after UV activation. This delay is attributed to the high amount of MMA in the resin. Furthermore, the storage modulus decreases with this concentration, indicating reduced mechanical properties for the cured composite.

caption: White light interferometer image showing the wear morphology of sample 1 after abrasion testing.
summary: Sample 1 wear morphology is visualized using white light interferometry to assess abrasion resistance. This technique provides a detailed surface profile, allowing for the calculation of wear rates based on the methodology proposed by Jin et al. The resulting data characterizes the material's performance under specific plasma in-situ thermal-assisted spraying conditions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of cast IN718 alloy measured in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at varying temperatures, highlighting the pitting potential (Epit) at 30 °C.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for cast IN718 in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution reveal the electrochemical behavior across different temperatures. At 30 °C, the anodic curve exhibits a distinct pitting potential (Epit) at approximately 1150.12 mV, where current density changes abruptly, indicating the onset of localized corrosion in the cast microstructure.

caption: Emission spectra of 0.1 mM luminol in 3 M NaCl aqueous solution under 21.2 kHz sonication for Ar and Kr gases, compared across different stirring velocities.
summary: This panel displays the emission spectra of luminol in a 3 M NaCl aqueous solution under sonication with Ar and Kr gases. The data demonstrate that stirring velocities significantly influence the sonochemiluminescence (SCL) intensity, with Ar and Kr showing distinct spectral responses despite the presence of minor Na* emission signals in all samples.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots for passive films on laser powder bed fusion produced Ti–6Al–4V (LTC4) measured after potentiostatic polarization at potentials ranging from 2.6 V to 3.0 V.
summary: Mott-Schottky measurements were performed on passive films formed on LTC4 samples under various potentials from 2.6 V to 3.0 V. These curves characterize the semiconductive properties of the passive films, providing essential data for calculating donor densities and other electronic parameters of the oxide layer formed on the alloy surface.

caption: Ashby plot illustrating the relationship between ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and solid fraction for the tested BCC lattices, including comparative literature data from Ref. [45].
summary: The Ashby plot correlates the plastic/crushing stress with the relative density of the studied BCC lattices. The slope of the lines in this plot corresponds to an exponent related to the specific loading mode of the lattice structure, providing a comparative analysis against established literature values for similar lattice configurations.

caption: Coefficient of friction curves plotted against time for the alloy tested at varied temperatures under a constant 10 N load.
summary: The coefficient of friction (COF) curves are presented as a function of time for the Al–La–Mg–Mn alloy under varied temperature conditions. These measurements were conducted at a fixed load of 10 N to evaluate the tribological performance and stability of the alloy across different thermal environments during sliding contact.

caption: Wear rate comparison for Cu75, Cu75–Si, Cu75–Sn, and Cu72–CrZr alloys.
summary: This plot compares the calculated wear rates for the four alloy compositions. The Cu75–Si alloy shows a remarkable reduction in wear rate to approximately 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹, while the Cu75–Sn and Cu72–CrZr alloys exhibit slightly higher wear rates, consistent with their respective two-dimensional contour curve profiles.

caption: Measured cutting force profile for the fast-tool-servo cutting process, plotted against the depth-of-cutting direction.
summary: This plot illustrates the measured cutting forces during the fast-tool-servo cutting process along the depth-of-cutting direction. The results reveal a significantly higher force variation compared to the slow-tool-servo method, with an average peak-to-valley value of 6.38 N, reflecting the distinct mechanical features of this high-speed cutting process.

caption: Distribution of social welfare outcomes across varying scenarios and proportions of untruthful manufacturers.
summary: This plot illustrates the distribution of social welfare across different scenarios and proportions of untruthful manufacturers. The data, derived from 10 random instances per size, provides a comprehensive overview of how manufacturer honesty impacts overall social welfare, highlighting the variability and trends observed within these simulated economic scenarios.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve for the GBDT model evaluated on the withheld test dataset, corresponding to a defect diameter of 310 µm.
summary: Displaying the detection performance for a 310 µm defect diameter, this ROC curve evaluates the GBDT model using the withheld test dataset. The analysis confirms that doubling the voxel bin length scale improves detection performance, as evidenced by the model trained and validated on the combined builds dataset.

caption: Comparison of stress rupture lives for smooth and notched plate specimens tested at 850 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the influence of geometric notches on the stress rupture life of plate specimens. Testing was performed at 850 °C following a 30-minute no-load heat preservation period. The data compares the performance of smooth versus notched configurations to evaluate how stress concentrations affect the material's long-term rupture resistance.

caption: Gumbel distribution curve representing the maximum corrosion charge q for the overlapping area and substrate prior to 24 hours of synthetic seawater exposure.
summary: This panel displays the Gumbel distribution curve for the maximum corrosion charge q of the overlapping area and substrate before 24 hours of synthetic seawater exposure. Prior to CE, the overlapping area exhibits a higher phase-selective corrosion rate compared to the substrate, as predicted by the Gumbel distribution function.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the A phase support, showing the nitrogen-doped carbon shell wrapping around the carbon core.
summary: The TEM image illustrates the interaction between the nitrogen-doped carbon shell and the carbon core within the A phase support. This wrapping morphology is a key characteristic of the support material, which influences the distribution and stability of the metal species deposited on the catalyst surface.

caption: Current waveforms recorded during a single discharge event on the substrate surface.
summary: Current waveforms for a single discharge event on the substrate surface are presented in this panel. These extracted waveforms characterize the electrical behavior during the discharge process, providing essential data on the temporal evolution of current specifically for the substrate surface under the experimental conditions described in the study.

caption: Hardness evolution of Cu–1.3Ni–0.3Si and Cu–1.3Ni–0.6Si–1.0Co alloys as a function of aging time at 420 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness variation of Cu–1.3Ni–0.3Si and Cu–1.3Ni–0.6Si–1.0Co alloys aged at 420 °C. The addition of Co significantly improves the mechanical properties of the alloy. The observed large increase in hardness is attributed to the Co addition, despite the limited volume fraction of precipitates present in the material.

caption: Cross-sectional HAADF-STEM image of the spin ice island heterostructure, highlighting the protective Pt layer and the 10 nm thick Py layer.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the cross-sectional geometry of the spin ice island heterostructure. The specimen was prepared using focused ion beam milling. The image reveals the layer stack, including a protective Pt layer, and allows for the measurement of the Py layer thickness, which is determined to be 10 ± 1 nm.

caption: Linear regression analysis and interpolation of wall thickness data plotted against extrusion multiplier, identifying the optimal EM value required to achieve a target wall thickness of 1.2 mm.
summary: The plot illustrates the relationship between wall thickness and extrusion multiplier. Through linear regression and interpolation of the collected experimental data, the optimal EM value was identified to meet the specific target wall thickness of 1.2 mm, providing a quantitative basis for the subsequent validation of the printing process.

caption: Microstructure of the alumina-silica specimen after 40 s of ultrafast sintering at 1100 °C.
summary: At a 40 s dwell time, the microstructure remains consistent with the 35 s specimen, showing no significant further changes. This confirms that extending the sintering duration beyond 30 s is unnecessary, as the material has already attained its most homogeneous and compact state.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the necked region of a tensile specimen prepared via abrasive waterjet cutting for porosity quantification.
summary: This photograph displays the sliced necked zone of a tensile testing specimen, which was prepared using abrasive waterjet cutting. This specific cross-sectional preparation allows for the precise quantification of porosity levels that developed within the material following the application of uniaxial tensile deformation during mechanical testing.

caption: Second derivative of the thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) curve for an LPBF-fabricated specimen, featuring a local enlargement highlighting the zero-crossing point used to determine the Curie temperature.
summary: This plot displays the second derivative of the thermal expansion coefficient curve for an LPBF-fabricated specimen.
