caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for Ti-6Al-4V alloy, illustrating phase evolution as a function of cooling rate and temperature relative to the beta-transus.
summary: This CCT diagram characterizes the phase transformation kinetics of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during cooling. It highlights the critical beta-transus temperature at 1000 °C, above which the microstructure consists of large prior beta grains. The diagram serves as a predictive tool for understanding microstructural development based on specific thermal processing conditions.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of ITGB1 (green), Phalloidin (red), and DAPI (blue) in HUVECs, highlighting cell adhesion and cytoskeletal organization.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging of ITGB1, Phalloidin, and DAPI reveals the structural organization of HUVECs on the scaffolds. These images demonstrate that all scaffolds facilitate cell adhesion, with the 1/2UiO-66/AHT group exhibiting the most favorable adhesion properties, as evidenced by the distribution of focal adhesion proteins and cytoskeletal filaments.

caption: Beeswarm plot displaying the SHAP values for the heat flow (Q ˙) feature, with observations ordered by feature importance and colored according to their actual target values.
summary: Representing the SHAP results for heat flow, this beeswarm plot organizes observations by feature importance. The color-coded dots reflect the actual target values, facilitating an interpretation of how heat flow influences the model's predictions from an overall standpoint, given the large sample size of the database.

caption: Violin plot distribution of oxygen segregation energies in titanium grain boundary sites as a function of the oxygen coordination number (Z).
summary: This violin plot illustrates the distribution of segregation energies for oxygen atoms within titanium grain boundary sites, categorized by their coordination number (Z). The data integrates results across various tilt axes and misorientations. Thick black bars and white lines indicate the interquartile range and median values, respectively, for each coordination state.

caption: Magnified view of the first force peak for the x0 = 0 configuration with debonding, showing the localized mechanical response.
summary: This panel displays a close-up of the first force peak for the x0 = 0 configuration when debonding is considered. By focusing on this region, the plot highlights how debonding influences the initial peak force and displacement, providing a clearer view of the mechanical behavior compared to the complete curve.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparison between GMA and DHPMA, highlighting the disappearance of epoxy moiety proton signals at 3.24, 2.84, and 2.65 p.p.m. and the emergence of two small unexpected peaks.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra compare the precursor GMA with the synthesized DHPMA. Successful conversion is evidenced by the complete disappearance of proton signals associated with the epoxy moiety at 3.24, 2.84, and 2.65 p.p.m., although two small, unexpected peaks are observed in the resulting DHPMA spectrum.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of cranium tissue sections at 4 weeks post-surgery, showing positive staining for CD31 (red), α-SMA (green), and DAPI (blue).
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of cranium tissue sections at 4 weeks post-surgery, showing positive staining for CD31 (red), α-SMA (green), and DAPI (blue). Increased angiogenesis is observed in the BMP-2/VEGF/BMSC and VEGF/BMSC groups, while the BMP-2/BMSC, BMSC, and Empty groups exhibit significantly fewer blood vessels within the defect area.

caption: Measured lattice strains of {111}, {200}, and {220} planes obtained via in situ neutron diffraction as reported in Ref. [29].
summary: Experimental lattice strains for {111}, {200}, and {220} planes are shown, as re-plotted from Ref. [29]. These measurements serve as the baseline for evaluating model accuracy. Observations indicate that while most strains are well-predicted, the transverse lattice strains of the {200} plane deviate during the elastic-plastic transition area.

caption: Raman spectroscopic analysis of the SPW10–20 electrode material.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is utilized to examine the structural characteristics of the printed SPW10–20 electrode. The resulting spectrum provides insights into the vibrational modes and structural order of the material, offering a complementary analytical perspective to the XPS data regarding the electrode's surface and bulk properties.

caption: Deconvoluted XPS spectrum of the R1 powder, highlighting the chemical bonding states of titanium oxides.
summary: The deconvoluted XPS spectrum for the R1 powder is shown in panel (c). Following the established reference binding energy of 458.6 eV for the TiO2 2p 3/2 peak, the spectrum reveals sequential peak assignments where primary and secondary peaks represent TiO2, and the tertiary peak indicates the presence of metallic Ti.

caption: Bode plot showing the frequency-dependent impedance response of the samples before and after the nitriding treatment.
summary: The Bode plot provides a frequency-dependent representation of the electrochemical impedance for the samples before and after nitriding. This visualization complements the Nyquist plot by detailing the impedance magnitude and phase characteristics across the tested frequency range, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of the electrode-electrolyte interface behavior.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the electrochemical current and coefficient of friction (CoF) for the TNZT/Al2O3 tribopair under a 2.74 N normal load at 1 Hz in a PBS buffer solution, maintained at a constant potential of 0.4 V Ag/AgCl.
summary: This tribocorrosion plot illustrates the simultaneous evolution of current and coefficient of friction for a TNZT alloy rubbing against an alumina counterface. Conducted in a PBS buffer at 0.4 V Ag/AgCl with a 2.74 N load, the data captures the material's passive response and frictional behavior during the sliding test.

caption: Higher magnification view of the geometrically necessary dislocation density for the LHT300 specimen.
summary: Higher magnification imaging of the LHT300 specimen reveals intricate details of the geometrically necessary dislocation density. This focused observation is crucial for identifying specific structural features and dislocation configurations that emerge under the LHT300 treatment, providing deeper insight into the material's microstructural response.

caption: Atomic morphology of the heat-affected zone (HAZ) after unloading, highlighting z-axis displacement variations.
summary: Atomic morphology of the heat-affected zone (HAZ) after unloading is displayed, where atomic color intensity represents the displacement in the z direction. Red indicates positive displacement and blue indicates negative displacement, illustrating the specific atomic morphology characteristics observed in this micro-zone following the nanoindentation test.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the hyperbolic sine of stress versus inverse temperature, used to calculate the activation energy for deformation.
summary: At a constant strain rate, this Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between the hyperbolic sine of stress and inverse temperature. The resulting mean slope of 6.205 allows for the calculation of the activation energy for the deformation process, which is determined to be 242.345 kJ/mol.

caption: Normal distribution analysis of fracture toughness (K IC) for ULW-ECC specimens reinforced with CFRP mesh at 0.3 h.
summary: This histogram displays the normal distribution analysis of fracture toughness for ULW-ECC specimens reinforced with CFRP mesh at a 0.3 h condition. The statistical analysis, defined by the mean and standard deviation, provides a clear representation of the fracture toughness, facilitating a comprehensive assessment of the composite's mechanical properties.

caption: Low-magnification HAADF-STEM image of the Ti/Steel interface showing the overall bonding region with SAED positions I and II.
summary: This low-magnification HAADF-STEM image illustrates the directly bonded Ti/Steel interface. SAED analysis at positions I and II confirms the presence of alpha-Fe on the steel side and beta-Ti on the titanium side, establishing the fundamental microstructural characteristics of the interface region.

caption: Surface electronic spectrum of the SnSbBiTe4 (111) cleavage surface, where red and blue dots indicate positive and negative in-plane spin projections, and shaded regions represent the projection of bulk states.
summary: The surface spectrum of the SnSbBiTe4 (111) cleavage surface reveals spin-polarized surface states, with red and blue dots denoting spin projections. On this projection, the conduction band minimum appears at the point of the 2D Brillouin zone, while the valence band maximum occurs at the - direction.

caption: Calculated phase map for the Ti-1023 alloy generated using Thermocalc software to guide the optimization of heat treatment parameters.
summary: The phase map, calculated using Thermocalc software, provides a theoretical guide for optimizing heat treatment process parameters. By visualizing the phase stability regions, this diagram assists in controlling the microstructural evolution of the Ti-1023 alloy, specifically targeting the desired characteristics of the ω and α phases during subsequent processing.

caption: Micro-CT images of longitudinal and transverse sections of porous scaffolds at twelve weeks post-implantation, demonstrating extensive bone filling.
summary: Micro-CT imaging of longitudinal and transverse sections of the porous scaffolds at twelve weeks post-implantation shows significant progression in bone growth. By this stage, new bone tissue has advanced into the deeper regions of the porous structure, ultimately filling all available pores within the scaffold.

caption: Statistical boxplot displaying the width variation of tensile samples for all tested print angles.
summary: Width measurements for tensile specimens are presented as a boxplot to demonstrate the variation across all print angles. This statistical representation allows for the assessment of dimensional stability and consistency in sample width, reflecting the impact of different print orientations on the final geometry of the tensile test specimens.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the electrochemical corrosion resistance of AB, T5, and T6 samples post-machining.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves are displayed for the AB, T5, and T6 samples to characterize their corrosion resistance after machining. These curves facilitate the extraction of key electrochemical parameters, which are further summarized in subsequent data tables, highlighting the influence of initial microstructural states on the overall electrochemical performance of the materials.

caption: Evolution of individual loss function components plotted against the generation number during the SNES optimization process for the training dataset.
summary: Panel (a) illustrates the convergence behavior of the SNES algorithm by tracking the evolution of various loss function terms across generations. This learning curve demonstrates how the optimization process refines the model parameters relative to the training dataset, providing insight into the stability and efficiency of the training procedure.

caption: Resistance stability profile of the SNPS sensor subjected to over 800 cyclic stretching events within the high-sensitivity strain range of 0 to 0.05.
summary: The SNPS sensor exhibits resistance stability during cyclic stretching within the high-sensitivity range of 0 to 0.05. During the initial stage, the resistance drops by nearly 0.2 MΩ and fails to fully recover to its initial value, indicating a stabilization period during the first 800 cycles of testing.

caption: Close-up of the continuous fiber extruder featuring replaced rubber rollers to prevent filament damage.
summary: The continuous fiber extruder is shown here, highlighting the hardware modifications made to the system. By replacing the original extruder components and installing rubber rollers, the setup effectively prevents damage to the filament during the extrusion process, ensuring consistent material delivery.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plots displaying the frequency-dependent impedance response of SS316L samples, where the non-3D printed sample exhibits the highest impedance magnitude at low frequencies.
summary: Bode impedance magnitude plots illustrate the frequency-dependent behavior of the samples. The data reveals that the non-3D printed commercial sample maintains the highest impedance magnitude, particularly in the low-frequency range, supporting the comparative analysis of corrosion resistance across the different powder layer thicknesses used in 3D printing.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of NiMn LH in 0.5 M NaOH, demonstrating the electrochemical response with and without 55 mM NH4Cl at 25 mV s-1.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry is employed to measure the electrochemical activity of NiMn LH toward the ammonia oxidation reaction. The plot shows the current response in 0.5 M NaOH electrolyte, comparing the presence and absence of 55 mM NH4Cl at a scan rate of 25 mV s-1 at room temperature.

caption: Printable region map for weave beads, defining the feasible parameter space of arc power versus printing speed for achieving stable bead geometry.
summary: The printable region is defined by mapping arc power against printing speed, identifying feasible parameters for stable bead fabrication. This plot was constructed by varying arc power and weaving width according to the designed path, and it serves as the basis for selecting parameters to investigate residual stresses and thermal deformation.

caption: AFM images of the PTL nanofilm after exposure to pH 2, pH 12, and organic solvent conditions to assess structural stability.
summary: AFM images demonstrate the structural stability of the PTL nanofilm under various environmental conditions, including acidic (pH 2), basic (pH 12), and organic solvent treatments. These images allow for the assessment of morphological changes or degradation, confirming the robustness of the PTL nanofilm structure under these specific conditions.

caption: Bright-field STEM diffraction contrast micrograph of the deformed microstructure beneath a microvoid in the uncharged specimen, highlighting subgrains elongated parallel to the void surface.
summary: This bright-field STEM micrograph displays the deformed microstructure beneath a microvoid in an uncharged specimen. The image reveals a distinct region of subgrains that are elongated parallel to the void surface, as indicated by the arrowhead. This structural feature characterizes the localized deformation occurring near the fracture surface.

caption: First heating DSC thermograms for pure Ecovio, pure PHBV, and their respective blends at 90/10, 80/20, 70/30, and 60/40 weight ratios.
summary: This DSC thermogram displays the first heating cycle for Ecovio, PHBV, and various Ecovio/PHBV blends. These measurements were conducted on extruded filaments to evaluate morphology and investigate potential changes in the thermal behavior of the polymer phases resulting from the mixing process, providing insight into the material's thermal characteristics.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the sample processed at 0.5 strain and 700 °C induction heating temperature.
summary: This IPF map depicts the microstructure of the sample treated at 0.5 strain and 700 °C. The microstructure is characterized by a combination of large deformed grains and numerous small static recrystallized (SRX) grains, indicating partial recrystallization under these specific processing parameters.

caption: Dark field electron micrograph of the PT718 sample showing precipitate morphology.
summary: This dark field electron micrograph of the PT718 sample clearly demonstrates the growth of both γ′ and γ'′ precipitates. When compared to the ST and PT621 samples, the image highlights the significant evolution in precipitate size and distribution resulting from the PT718 heat treatment condition.

caption: Surface roughness profile of sample 2 after laser shock peening, showing the characteristic imprint of individual LSP spots.
summary: After the laser shock peening process, sample 2 displays clear imprints of individual LSP spots. The removal of longer frequencies of form and waviness through wave analysis allows for the precise observation of these localized surface features, confirming the successful application of the laser treatment on the material.

caption: Mean square displacement (MSD) profiles of Ni atoms in pure Ni, binary Ni-Cr, and Ni-Fe alloys over a 5 ns simulation period.
summary: This plot compares the MSD of Ni in pure Ni, binary Ni-Cr, and Ni-Fe systems. Results indicate that adding Cr significantly enhances Ni diffusion, nearly doubling it compared to pure Ni. Conversely, the addition of Fe shows no discernible influence on Ni diffusion, reflecting differences in migration barriers.

caption: Sintering curves obtained via heating microscopy for debinded 70 wt% SiO2 and 70 wt% SiO2 + 20 wt% TIPO pieces, measured at 700 ºC for 1 hour.
summary: Sintering curves derived from heating microscopy show the shrinkage behavior of debinded 70 wt% SiO2 and 70 wt% SiO2 + 20 wt% TIPO samples. The low shrinkage observed in these curves is linked to the material composition, and the data confirms that increasing TiO2 content results in denser sintered samples.

caption: Isothermal TGA reduction curves of leach residue with graphite conducted between 800 °C and 1400 °C, showing mass loss over time.
summary: Isothermal reduction tests of leach residue with graphite were performed from 800 °C to 1400 °C. Results indicate that reduction is slow at 800 °C and 900 °C with limited mass loss. Higher temperatures accelerate the molten silicate reduction stage, evidenced by steeper slopes in the curves below -25 wt%.

caption: Molten pool morphology observed with a 4 mm groove gap, demonstrating reduced sidewall constraint and increased liquid metal flow.
summary: Increasing the groove gap to 4 mm reduces the constraint effect of the sidewalls on the liquid metal. Consequently, the flow range and capacity of the liquid metal are increased, facilitating the fusion of the sidewall and modifying the overall morphology of the molten pool.

caption: Reconstructed gamma-FCC phase map based on the Nishiyama–Wassermann (N–W) orientation relationship.
summary: This reconstruction displays the parent gamma-FCC phase derived from the experimental EBSD data using the Nishiyama–Wassermann orientation relationship. Consistent with the K–S reconstruction, this map uses the standard IPF color-coding to illustrate the parent grain structure, facilitating a comparative analysis of different potential orientation relationships in the material.

caption: Raman spectrum of the PEO sample after 504 hours of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel illustrates the Raman spectrum of the standard PEO sample after undergoing a 504-hour immersion test in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The spectrum serves as a control to compare against cerium-modified samples, helping to isolate the specific impact of cerium on the corrosion resistance of the PEO layer.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the Shore A durometer versus elongation to failure for FFF-printed elastomers and traditional castable elastomeric resins.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the performance gap between 3D printed FFF elastomers and traditional castable resins. It highlights that the range of commonly practiced FFF elastomers is significantly limited in terms of achievable Shore A durometer and elongation to failure when compared to the broader material properties available via castable resins.

caption: Yield stress radar plot for composites with face-to-core ratios ranging from 0 to 0.8, showing performance relative to the monolithic core material.
summary: Yield stress values for various multi-material configurations are presented in this radar plot. By comparing these results against the monolithic core baseline, the figure demonstrates how adjusting the face-to-core ratio influences the yield behavior of the composites, providing a consistent basis for material selection in structural applications.

caption: Phase angle response as a function of frequency for different scan strategies, illustrating the electrochemical behavior of the passive layer in borate buffer solution.
summary: Representing the phase angle component of the electrochemical impedance spectra, this plot illustrates the frequency-dependent response of the system across different scan strategies. Together with the impedance modulus, these results facilitate the evaluation of passive layer properties and electrochemical behavior within the borate buffer solution environment.

caption: {0001} α-phase pole figure for the XZ plane of ambient-pressure WAAM Ti64, reflecting the reduced texture intensity of the α-phase.
summary: This pole figure displays the {0001} α-phase orientation on the XZ plane of the ambient-pressure WAAM Ti64 sample. The data confirms that the α-phase grains exhibit a lower texture intensity compared to the β-phase grains, reflecting the influence of the phase transformation on the final crystallographic texture of the material.

caption: Enlarged orientation map of the 5 min sintered sample with an overlaid point-to-point misorientation plot specifically identifying Sigma 3 CSL twin boundaries.
summary: Detailed analysis of the 5 min sintered sample using enlarged orientation maps allows for the precise identification of Sigma 3 CSL twin boundaries. Point-to-point misorientation plots confirm the presence of these boundaries, which are essential for enhancing the strain-hardening capabilities of the Ni-based superalloy without compromising its overall ductility.

caption: Two-dimensional chemical structure of hydroxyapatite (HA) ligand, rendered using Chem3D 18.2 software.
summary: The 2D chemical structure of the hydroxyapatite (HA) ligand is illustrated, generated using Chem3D 18.2. This representation serves as the foundational chemical model for the ligand, which was subsequently prepared for 3D computational analysis by obtaining its SMILES code from PubChem and building the structure in Avogadro.

caption: Electron probe microanalysis mapping of the 3TiN as-built Inconel 718 sample, illustrating the highest observed concentration of Laves phase precipitates among the tested compositions.
summary: Electron probe microanalysis mapping of the 3TiN as-built Inconel 718 sample illustrates the highest concentration of light grey Laves phase precipitates. The observed increase in Laves phase with higher TiN content is attributed to the redistribution of Nb and Mo in the melt pool, driven by altered local chemistry from TiN decomposition.

caption: Temporal evolution of simulated powder mass flow rate at the nozzle exit compared to a 12 g min-1 target feed rate, evaluated across carrier-gas flow rates of 8, 10, 12, and 14 L min-1, with insets displaying instantaneous particle trajectories at the single-jet exit.
summary: Simulated powder mass flow rates fluctuate around the 12 g min-1 target across all carrier-gas flow conditions, demonstrating that aerodynamic drag primarily influences transient transport stability rather than the mean delivery rate. Insets visualize the particle trajectories, which, alongside the flow data, define the effective local feeding conditions for deposition.

caption: Hydrogen bubble evolution on a 3 mm thick 3D printed steel electrode at an applied potential of 0.7 V.
summary: Hydrogen bubble evolution is captured on a 3 mm thick 3D printed steel electrode at 0.7 V. The persistent bubbles on this flat surface are consistent with the higher effective blocking and lower efficiency observed in the study of 3D printed steel electrodes made from BASF Ultrafuse.

caption: Spatial distribution of damage along the beam length at varying load levels, contrasting the monolateral (dashed) and bilateral (solid) damage model predictions.
summary: This panel presents the spatial distribution of damage along the beam at different load levels. It contrasts the predictions of the monolateral damage model, represented by dashed curves, with the bilateral damage model, represented by solid curves, providing a visual comparison of damage progression across the beam structure.

caption: Flat interface destabilization stage characterized by the emergence of small grain protrusions.
summary: The flat interface destabilization stage is marked by the appearance of small grain protrusions along the solid-liquid interface. This phase-field simulation result demonstrates the transition from a planar growth front to a more complex morphology as the interface begins to lose its initial stability during the solidification process.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography profiles of grain boundary grooves observed in base materials following a simulated brazing cycle.
summary: Atomic force microscopy was utilized to characterize the topography of grain boundary grooves across various base materials. These profiles were measured after the materials underwent a brazing cycle to verify the underlying diffusion mechanism. The resulting data provides a detailed visualization of the groove morphology characteristic of the base materials.

caption: Fracture toughness (K Ic) of CTS samples as a function of healing time for various nozzle temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between fracture toughness and healing time for PA-6 samples processed at different nozzle temperatures. Results indicate a weak correlation between K Ic and reptation time, as healing time increases with nozzle temperature. Notably, samples produced at 260 °C exhibit significantly higher fracture toughness than those fabricated at 240 °C or 280 °C.

caption: Extracted 3D height data map generated via laser profilometry for the silver trace.
summary: Laser profilometry was utilized to generate this 3D surface map of the silver trace. The height data provides a detailed topographical representation of the printed feature, which allows for the extraction of multiple cross-sections at 1.7 μm intervals to accurately compute the average bead profile and cross-sectional area.

caption: Mean square displacement (MSD) of Ni atoms in ternary Ni-based systems, illustrating the effect of varying Cr composition on diffusion kinetics.
summary: The MSD profiles for ternary systems demonstrate that Ni diffusion rates increase progressively with higher Cr concentrations. These simulation results confirm that the migration barrier for Ni is lowered by the presence of Cr, leading to faster atomic diffusion as observed in the MSD plots over the 5 ns duration.

caption: Creep strain evolution over time for vertical specimens of 738_STD and 738_NZ alloys, evaluated under two distinct thermomechanical conditions: 760°C at 565 MPa and 982°C at 151 MPa.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep strain behavior of 738_STD and 738_NZ alloy specimens oriented vertically. The data, derived from creep strain tests, compares performance across two specific loading conditions: 760°C/565 MPa and 982°C/151 MPa, providing a clear visualization of the deformation kinetics for these materials under high-temperature stress.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the simulated pore morphology in a sample processed at 250 eV laser power and a substrate temperature of 900 K.
summary: At the highest substrate temperature of 900 K, the simulation shows a significant reduction in pore formation. This panel highlights the effectiveness of higher thermal energy in minimizing defects, resulting in a structure with minimal or no detectable pores compared to the lower temperature processing conditions.

caption: Top-view EBSD IPF-Z map of the AP sample showing the initial crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The top-view EBSD map of the AP sample, visualized using IPF-Z coloring, illustrates the initial crystallographic orientation distribution. This panel provides a baseline for understanding the interplay between texture orientation and microstructure in the as-processed material, serving as a reference for comparison with the 1000–24 sample's grain growth behavior.

caption: Molecular structure of the phospholipid 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DPPC).
summary: The molecular structure of DPPC, a primary phospholipid component, is illustrated here. This structural model highlights the arrangement of the lipid molecule, serving as a fundamental reference for the chemical composition of the lipid-based systems investigated throughout the study and providing context for its role in the formulation.

caption: Nearest-neighbor analysis of Al atoms, comparing the experimental distribution to a random distribution, with a determined d_max of 0.7 nm.
summary: Statistical analysis of the fifth nearest neighbor (5NN) distribution identifies Al nanoclusters by measuring distances between neighboring Al atoms. The broadening and shifting of the distribution compared to a random model, with a d_max of 0.7 nm, confirms that solute atoms within these clusters are connected at this fixed distance.

caption: Cu2p narrow scan XPS spectrum focused on the C4 sample.
summary: This narrow scan captures the Cu2p core-level region for the C4 sample. The resulting spectrum is essential for characterizing the copper oxidation state and chemical bonding environment, providing critical insights into the surface composition and potential catalytic or structural roles of copper within the C4 material.

caption: Alloy element spectrums derived from the SEM image of the LPBF-AB sample, confirming overall compositional consistency.
summary: This panel displays the alloy element spectrums obtained from the SEM image of the LPBF-AB sample. These spectra confirm that the alloying elements are generally distributed uniformly. While the quantitative content of C was overestimated, other elements remain consistent with the expected powder and sample composition.

caption: Normalised permeation current density transients for 4340 steel under varying fabrication conditions in 0.1 M NaOH, showing experimental data as dashed lines and MATLAB-generated mathematical fits as solid lines.
summary: This plot displays normalised permeation current density transients for 4340 steel in 0.1 M NaOH, comparing experimental data with mathematical fits. The high fitting accuracy across all curves suggests that hydrogen diffusion in these samples is not significantly hindered by trapping effects, providing a baseline for evaluating different fabrication processes.

caption: Resistance stability of the electrical insulation coating maintained at a constant temperature of 900 °C.
summary: Electrical performance of the insulation coating is demonstrated at a constant temperature of 900 °C. The resistance reaches a stable value of 3 MΩ, which is significantly higher than the resistance observed in the metallic sensitive layer, confirming the effectiveness of the coating as an electrical insulator under high-temperature conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the design principles for mycelium-bound composite foam (F) and perforated layer (P) samples produced using cardboard molds.
summary: This schematic illustrates the design principles for creating mycelium-bound composite foam samples, denoted as F, and perforated layers, denoted as P. These components are produced using cardboard molds, with specific geometric parameters like height, diameter, and cavity distribution varying between different sample designs to facilitate subsequent acoustic testing.

caption: Phase mapping of the A1060/SLM-SUS316 interface, identifying the spatial distribution of austenite, aluminum, ferrite, and A1 0.5 Fe 0.5 phases.
summary: Phase mapping of the A1060/SLM-SUS316 interface reveals the formation of multiple distinct phases. The analysis identifies the presence of pure austenite and pure aluminum phases originating from the base materials, alongside the formation of partial ferrite and A1 0.5 Fe 0.5 phases specifically localized at the weld interface.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram for the matrix of 420 steel, illustrating the austenite decomposition process as a function of cooling rate.
summary: Calculated using JMatPro, this CCT diagram illustrates the austenite decomposition process for the 420 steel matrix. It highlights how the cooling rate dictates the resulting martensitic transformation, providing essential data for predicting the microstructural evolution and phase constituents formed during the continuous cooling of the investigated steel.

caption: Box plot representing the variation of maximum height (Sz) for each contour theme, highlighting significant differences in surface topography.
summary: The box plot depicts the distribution of the maximum height (Sz) parameter across various contour themes. With a p-value below 0.05, the data confirms statistically significant differences between themes. Trends in the mean values suggest that the sequence of contour melting influences the resulting surface roughness measurements.

caption: Macroscopic Gibbs energy landscapes for elastic scaling parameters alpha=0.615 and beta=0.626 at a volume fraction of c=0.15.
summary: Depicting the energy landscape for an alternative set of elastic scaling parameters, this panel shows how mechanical stiffness influences the system. By decreasing the beta parameter, the austenitic state is stabilized due to pronounced mechanical energy barriers. This configuration correlates with local energetic minima that dictate the system's phase state.

caption: Vickers hardness values comparing the base material against surfaces machined via conventional EDM and NSMEDM processes.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the Vickers hardness measurements for three distinct conditions: base material, conventional EDM, and NSMEDM machined surfaces. The data demonstrates that the hardness of the machined surface increases following the EDM process, highlighting the influence of different machining techniques on the mechanical properties of the material.

caption: PXRD pattern of AlNi alloy particles subjected to high-intensity ultrasonic treatment in pure ethanol.
summary: AlNi alloy particles treated in pure ethanol show diffraction peaks consistent with Al3Ni2 and Al3Ni intermetallic phases. No evidence of Al2O3·nH2O formation is detected in this sample, indicating that the presence of ethanol prevents the oxidation observed in aqueous media during the high-intensity ultrasonic treatment process.

caption: Differential phase contrast STEM image of the spherical particles, showing the local magnetic flux distribution.
summary: Differential phase contrast STEM image of the spherical particles, showing the local magnetic flux distribution. This imaging provides insight into how the spherical particles, identified as Si-rich oxides, interact with the local magnetic environment within the Si 0.2 MEA, complementing the structural information obtained from other STEM imaging modes.

caption: Electron channelling contrast imaging of the L-PBF alloy treated at 300 °C, highlighting the continued accumulation of submicron inclusions within the preserved subgrain matrix.
summary: Electron channelling contrast imaging of the L-PBF alloy treated at 300 °C, highlighting the continued accumulation of submicron inclusions within the preserved subgrain matrix. The overall structural characteristics remain largely intact, and the subgrain structure is maintained, showing only a slight increase in average cell size at this elevated temperature.

caption: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra comparing reduced HTNi15, HTNi15Cu1, and HTNi15Cu4 materials against a Ni foil reference.
summary: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra are presented for reduced HTNi15, HTNi15Cu1, and HTNi15Cu4 materials. These spectroscopic measurements are compared directly against a Ni foil reference to evaluate the oxidation state and local electronic environment of the nickel species within the synthesized catalyst samples following the reduction process.

caption: Comparative data table detailing the weight and drug content specifications for both RP and MH-CSS formulations.
summary: This table presents a quantitative comparison of weight and drug content between RP and MH-CSS. It provides essential data to evaluate the consistency and quality of the MH-CSS formulation relative to the reference preparation, ensuring that the drug loading meets the required specifications for the study.

caption: Major strain distribution along the gauge length at a central strain of 0.2, conducted at 450 °C under varying strain rates.
summary: This panel presents the major strain distribution along the gauge length at a central strain of 0.2, tested at 450 °C under varying strain rates. Higher strain rates are shown to facilitate slightly more uniform strain distributions, although the overall strain profile across the gauge length remains nonuniform despite improved control methods.

caption: In situ Raman spectra of Cu8Ni2 catalyst during urea synthesis and HzOR, showing the detection of common reaction intermediates.
summary: The in situ Raman spectra for the Cu8Ni2 catalyst are presented to investigate the reaction mechanism of urea synthesis and HzOR. Analysis of the spectral data reveals the presence of several common reaction intermediates, providing insight into the surface chemical species involved during the catalytic process under experimental conditions.

caption: Oxidation cyclic voltammograms of pure BAPO and BAPO mixed with anatase or rutile nanoparticles, highlighting a single oxidation peak observed during the second cycle of the oxidational scan.
summary: Panel B presents the oxidation behavior of pure BAPO and BAPO-nanoparticle mixtures. The cyclic voltammetry measurements reveal that the second cycle results in a single oxidation peak during the oxidational scan. These electrochemical results correlate with observed conversion rates, particularly for rutile, which reached up to 88% efficiency.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy imaging of MC3T3-E1 cells co-cultured with bioactive-coated IFSs, evaluated using CCK-8 assay at days 1, 3, and 7.
summary: This panel displays the co-culture of MC3T3-E1 cells with bioactive-coated IFSs. The cells were monitored over a seven-day period using a CCK-8 assay in a complete medium. The imaging provides a visual assessment of cell growth and viability on the screw surfaces at the specified time intervals of 1, 3, and 7 days.

caption: Loss factor (tan δ) curves representing the energy dissipation characteristics of the scaffold materials.
summary: Tan δ curves illustrate the energy depletion characteristics of the scaffolds, where the observed peaks correspond to the amount of energy loss within the materials. These curves provide a quantitative measure of the damping properties, reflecting the internal friction and viscoelastic behavior of the scaffold structures.

caption: Bucket model featuring a wall thickness of 1.90 mm and a 5° tilt angle, subjected to a 30-minute water filling test to evaluate structural integrity.
summary: This bucket model, printed with a wall thickness of 1.90 mm and a 5° tilt angle, serves as a test for interlayer bonding. A 30-minute water filling test confirms the absence of leakage, indicating tight interlayer bonding and no through-holes within the printed bucket wall.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography image illustrating the surface morphology of the binary alloy specimen.
summary: Atomic force microscopy topography image illustrating the surface morphology of the binary alloy specimen. This visualization provides a baseline characterization of the binary alloy's surface structure, which serves as a comparative reference for the ternary alloy counterpart in the subsequent analysis of surface features and potential distributions.

caption: RMSE curve for the SVR algorithm in the MSAD prediction model, plotted as a function of descriptor count.
summary: The SVR algorithm's RMSE curve for the MSAD prediction model is shown here. It illustrates the variation in prediction error as the number of descriptors changes, providing a detailed look at the SVR model's performance and error dynamics within the MSAD dataset framework.

caption: Current density response over time at a constant potential of 0.5 V for fuel cell mode operation, comparing cross-linked PVA membranes with different Cs contents against Nafion 117.
summary: Current evolution at 0.5 V in fuel cell mode reveals that higher Cs concentrations in the PVA membranes lead to increased current output. Observed peaks in the current curves are attributed to stop/start cycles performed during impedance measurements, highlighting the dynamic performance characteristics of the tested membrane materials.

caption: Time-on-stream intensity profile for C2H6 (m/z = 30) measured via in situ mass spectrometry, highlighting the promotion of FTS for ethane formation at 400 °C.
summary: The intensity of C2H6 (m/z = 30) is tracked over time-on-stream using in situ mass spectrometry. The data confirms that the 2Ni-8Fe-13X catalyst promotes Fischer-Tropsch synthesis (FTS) for ethane formation specifically at higher reaction temperatures of 400 °C, as evidenced by the detected mass signal for ethane.

caption: Bright-field STEM image showing intermetallic compounds within the ultra-fine grain (UFG) region of the as-printed Al-alloy.
summary: This bright-field STEM image highlights the morphology and distribution of intermetallic compounds located within the ultra-fine grain regions of the as-printed Al-4.2Mg-0.7Mn-1.1Sc-0.5Zr-0.6Cu-0.1Zn-0.1Fe alloy. The visualization provides structural insight into the precipitation formation characteristic of the UFG microstructure observed in the printed material.

caption: Averaged COHP curves for H-Ni and H-Re atomic pairs in Ni Σ5 [001](210) grain boundaries, showing Fermi levels positioned within antibonding regions.
summary: This panel displays the averaged COHP for H-Ni and H-Re atomic pairs in segregated Ni grain boundaries. The Fermi levels for both H-segregated and H-Re co-segregated systems are clearly located within the antibonding regions, where -COHP values are less than zero, indicating the presence of occupied antibonding states.

caption: Summary table listing the calculated thicknesses in nanometers for the PLA and PCL specimens shown in panels a, b, and c, determined using Iakoubovskii's equation based on EELS measurements.
summary: This table provides the calculated thicknesses in nanometers for the PLA and PCL specimens presented in the previous panels. The values were derived from EELS measurements and calculated using Iakoubovskii's equation, offering a quantitative comparison of the specimen thicknesses achieved through UM, cryo-UM, and FIB preparation methods.

caption: Post-impact appearance of the PETG specimen following the Izod impact test.
summary: This photograph displays the PETG specimen after undergoing an Izod impact test. The visual evidence of the specimen's condition serves as a basis for evaluating its mechanical performance, which, when compared to Polyamide (6), indicates that the impact strength of the PETG material is slightly inferior to that of Polyamide (6).

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the AM-60 alloy showing intermetallic precipitates within the austenite matrix, with 5.5 at% Mo and 3.5 at% Ni iso-concentration surfaces highlighted in red and green.
summary: This APT reconstruction of the AM-60 alloy displays intermetallic precipitates captured within a cuboidal sub-volume. The visualization utilizes 5.5 at% Mo and 3.5 at% Ni iso-concentration surfaces, rendered in red and green respectively, to delineate the interface between the intermetallic phases and the austenite matrix within the representative tip.

caption: Bidirectional scanning strategy employed during the DED-LB process, featuring 100 welding tracks per layer.
summary: The bidirectional scanning pattern is depicted here, highlighting the specific deposition strategy involving 100 welding tracks per layer. This systematic approach defines the thermal history and grain growth orientation during the additive manufacturing of the IN718 parts, which is later analyzed in the context of the material's crystal structure.

caption: Fracture toughness of simulated polycrystalline material as a function of increasing pressure.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of a simulated polycrystalline material under varying pressure conditions. It specifically tracks the evolution of fracture toughness as pressure increases, providing a quantitative assessment of how structural integrity and resistance to crack propagation are influenced by the applied pressure within the simulation environment.

caption: Tool wear-related volume loss of the shoulder plotted against the number of welded cycles, comparing experimental measurements between 2750 and 3250 cycles with literature data from de Carvalho et al. and de Castro for lower cycle counts.
summary: This plot illustrates the progression of tool shoulder volume loss as a function of welded cycles. By integrating experimental data from 2750 to 3250 cycles with established literature values, the graph provides a comprehensive overview of tool degradation, effectively monitoring the loss of tool volume throughout the wear investigation process.

caption: Side view of 12-atom (2 1 1) slab supercells for Pt, Ag, and Cu FCC metals, highlighting step atoms in red and labeling unique atomic sites.
summary: This panel displays the (2 1 1) slab models for Pt, Ag, and Cu, identifying unique atomic sites within the 12-atom supercells. Step atoms, marked in red, are highlighted as the most sensitive to applied potential. The symmetric slab structure simplifies the analysis, with only six unique atomic positions per supercell.

caption: Shear force–displacement curve of the joining interface between Cf/SiC and SC CMSX-6 hybrid specimen tested at 750 °C.
summary: The shear force–displacement curve illustrates the mechanical response of the Cf/SiC/SC CMSX-6 hybrid specimen interface during testing at 750 °C. This plot provides critical data regarding the joining interface's load-bearing capacity and deformation behavior under shear stress, characterizing the mechanical integrity of the hybrid material system at elevated temperatures.

caption: Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra for CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC.
summary: The Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra for CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC are presented to analyze the local coordination environment of nickel. This data provides insights into the atomic structure and bonding distances of nickel atoms within the synthesized materials, complementing the XANES and XPS findings.

caption: Schematic representation of the heat treatment cycle, illustrating the thermal profile applied to the samples.
summary: This schematic illustrates the heat treatment procedure applied to the samples. The process involves heating the material under a vacuum at 850 °C for a duration of 2 hours, followed by a controlled furnace cooling stage. This thermal cycle is essential for the subsequent microstructural development of the investigated specimens.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the specimen manufactured with Parameter C, displaying the crystallographic texture relative to the building direction.
summary: Crystallographic texture for the specimen manufactured with Parameter C is shown in this inverse pole figure map. The orientation is mapped parallel to the building direction, revealing the specific grain alignment and texture characteristics induced by this processing condition, which can be contrasted with the results from Parameters A and B.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of a target excited by a cross-type illumination pattern, showing normalized intensity distributions and recognizable ununiformity.
summary: This panel displays a fluorescent target excited by a cross-type illumination pattern. The image, captured on the camera plane, shows normalized intensity distributions. Observations indicate that this specific illumination pattern generates recognizable ununiform intensity across the target, as highlighted by white arrows indicating imperfections in the captured image.

caption: Fracture toughness testing setup for waDED material, illustrating crack extension paths parallel to the building direction and parallel to the processing direction.
summary: This panel displays the fracture toughness testing orientation for waDED material. The testing involves crack extension perpendicular to the processing direction, which is parallel to the building direction, labeled PB, and parallel to the processing direction, labeled BP. These orientations define the crack propagation paths during the mechanical characterization.

caption: Optical images showing the hinge bridging area of the samples after undergoing 50 folding cycles.
summary: Optical microscopy of the hinge bridging area reveals the physical condition of the samples following 50 folding cycles. Notably, these images confirm that the samples maintained their structural integrity throughout the shape memory lifespan tests, as no visible defects or signs of damage were observed in the hinge regions.

caption: Strain path evolution for the GH4169 alloy thin sheet following solution treatment.
summary: Strain paths during the mesoscale forming limit of the GH4169 alloy thin sheet are depicted here. This panel specifically illustrates the load path behavior for the alloy after undergoing solution treatment, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of subsequent aging treatments on the material's forming limit characteristics.

caption: Plan view optical micrograph of the wear track on the TiAlN-M coating after sliding under a 5 N load for 20 m.
summary: Presented is the optical microscope image of the wear track for the TiAlN-M coating, captured in plan view after a 20 m sliding distance under a 5 N normal load. This visualization documents the surface wear characteristics of the coating under the defined experimental parameters.

caption: High-resolution STEM image of the fracture surface at the top of the foil, revealing the local atomic or near-atomic scale features of the failure site.
summary: This high-resolution STEM image focuses on the fracture surface located at the top of the foil. By examining this region, researchers can conduct a detailed crystallographic analysis of the failure site, providing insights into the material's response to the 645 MPa stress applied during testing.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for the HT2 condition, characterized by a continued preference for {100} boundary planes.
summary: The HT2 heat-treated random scan sample continues to exhibit an anisotropic grain boundary plane distribution. Similar to the as-built and HT1 conditions, the boundary planes predominantly terminate on {100} planes, demonstrating that this specific crystallographic preference is stable across these initial processing and heat treatment stages.

caption: Survey XPS spectrum of the SCF/Co@C composite showing four distinct peaks at 285.08 eV, 399.08 eV, 533.08 eV, and 781.08 eV.
summary: The survey XPS spectrum of the SCF/Co@C composite displays four primary peaks located at 285.08 eV, 399.08 eV, 533.08 eV, and 781.08 eV. These binding energy values provide an initial overview of the elemental composition and chemical states present within the synthesized material structure.

caption: Series of 79Br NMR spectra for 42 mg KBr samples, demonstrating the spectral evolution as the spinning axis angle is pneumatically adjusted through the magic angle (54.74°).
summary: This figure displays a series of 79Br NMR spectra for 42 mg KBr samples, illustrating the spectral progression as the spinning axis angle is pneumatically adjusted through the magic angle of 54.74°. Each spectrum represents 1024 scans, with the spinning axis angle deviations relative to the magic angle indicated along the baselines.

caption: Electronic temperature profiles for 50 keV 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFeCr.
summary: Shown is the electronic temperature evolution for a 50 keV 2T-MD cascade in NiFeCr. The curves illustrate temperature along the y-dimension of the MD box. The highest temperature values indicate the cascade development area, while the box edges are maintained at 300 K throughout the simulation period.

caption: Gripper manipulating a toy, illustrating its versatility in handling complex, non-standard geometries.
summary: The gripper is shown manipulating a toy, illustrating its versatility in handling complex, non-standard geometries. By successfully grasping such items, the gripper demonstrates its shape compliance and stable manipulation capabilities, confirming its effectiveness in handling a wide range of everyday objects during the performance assessment tests.

caption: Plastic equivalent strain (PEEQ) diagram of the unit cell, where blue regions represent elastic behavior and red regions indicate initiated plastic deformation.
summary: The plastic equivalent strain diagram illustrates the deformation behavior of the unit cell under 0.010 strain loading. Blue regions signify areas maintaining elastic behavior, while red regions clearly denote zones where plastic deformation has initiated, effectively mapping the progression of material yielding throughout the simulated unit cell structure.

caption: Mesh cube model viewed perpendicular to the cube face, highlighting the strut projection alignment.
summary: The mesh cube model is presented in a view perpendicular to the cube face. In this orientation, the projections of all struts onto the cube faces are aligned parallel to the face diagonal, illustrating the specific geometric configuration of the diamond-based tetrahedral structure within the 30x30x30 mm cube dimensions.

caption: Gaussian peak fitting analysis of the hydrogen desorption curve for the 290 K charged specimen, decomposed into two distinct Gaussian curves.
summary: Gaussian function fitting was applied to the hydrogen desorption curve of the 290 K charged specimen to decompose the data into two main components, labeled curve 1 and curve 2. This analysis, achieving a coefficient of determination higher than 0.99, effectively characterizes the two distinct hydrogen desorption peaks observed.

caption: Areal capacity retention of a 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode with a thickness of 1114 μm, measured at a 1C rate over 80 cycles.
summary: The cyclic performance of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode with a maximum thickness of 1114 μm is evaluated at a 1C rate. The plot demonstrates that the areal capacity remains stable at 2.66 mAh cm-2 after 80 cycles, indicating robust long-term cycling stability for the thick printed electrode.

caption: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO model at 2 T magnetic induction intensity.
summary: Shown are the pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO system subjected to a 2 T magnetic field. The seven identified chemical order types, including Co-Co, Co-Fe, Co-Mn, Cr-Cr, Cr-Mn, Cr-Ni, and Mn-Ni, are evaluated to determine the impact of magnetic induction on local atomic arrangements.

caption: Thermal camera image of the AlSi7Mg0.6 matrix material during PBF-LB/M processing at 510 W and 1850 mm/s.
summary: Thermal camera imaging of the pure AlSi7Mg0.6 matrix material during PBF-LB/M processing reveals the melt pool dynamics under standard parameters of 510 W and 1850 mm/s. This visualization serves as a baseline for comparing spattering behavior against the composite powder blend containing 5 wt% TiCnm under identical laser processing conditions.

caption: Oxidation mass gain measurements for LPBF-fabricated Inconel 625 at 1100 °C.
summary: Shown is the mass gain versus time for LPBF-fabricated Inconel 625 during isothermal oxidation at 1100 °C. The kinetic curve captures the oxidation behavior of the alloy at this high temperature, reflecting the material's performance and stability when subjected to prolonged oxidation in an oxygen-rich environment.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the natural logarithm of measured ion intensities for Ni, Co, Cr, and Al as a function of reciprocal temperature for the CMSX-4 alloy within the two-phase γ+γ′ region.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays KEMS-derived ion intensities for Ni, Co, Cr, and Al in CMSX-4 alloy. By plotting intensities against reciprocal temperature, the linear regression slopes are obtained, which are directly proportional to the sublimation enthalpies of these elements within the two-phase γ+γ′ region of the material.

caption: Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) curves for HT1 and HT2 samples measured across the temperature range of -100 °C to 300 °C.
summary: The CTE curves for HT1 and HT2 samples are presented over the temperature range of -100 °C to 300 °C. These curves characterize the thermal expansion properties of the materials, providing a detailed view of how the CTE evolves as the samples are subjected to varying thermal conditions.

caption: SEM micrographs of the machined surface morphology for the 1370 °C heat-treated specimen, processed at 2000 rpm and 6000 rpm, with blue arrows denoting scratch marks and orange arrows denoting Y2O3 particles.
summary: Machined surface morphologies for the 1370 °C heat-treated specimen are captured using SEM at 2000 rpm and 6000 rpm. These micrographs illustrate the influence of microstructure on surface integrity, specifically identifying scratch marks with blue arrows and Y2O3 particles with orange arrows to characterize the resulting surface finish.

caption: Case 4 numerical distribution of the upper domain when the rotation matrix angle theta is set to 0.
summary: This panel presents the numerical distribution of the upper domain for Case 4, evaluated with the rotation matrix angle theta set to 0. As the final example in the series, it completes the comparative set, demonstrating the domain distribution patterns resulting from the specified rotation matrix configuration.

caption: Integrated camera system mounted on the robotic printing apparatus via a 140 mm aluminum profile and custom 3D-printed connectors.
summary: This photograph displays the camera system integrated into the printing setup. The device is secured to the system using a 140 mm aluminum profile supported by 3D-printed connectors. This configuration ensures stable positioning of the camera, facilitating accurate monitoring and data acquisition during the robotic printing process.

caption: SAXS intensity I(q) plots representing various ageing conditions, illustrating the shift in scattering intensity and peak position.
summary: SAXS I(q)-plots demonstrate the evolution of precipitate structures during ageing. A significant intensity change occurs from the T7 condition to initial ageing stages, followed by a gradual shift toward lower scattering vectors as temperature increases, which indicates a progressive increase in the size of the precipitates within the material.

caption: EDS analysis results corresponding to the specific area marked at the primary powder boundary of the Cu–Ni/B4C compact shown in panel (b).
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) is employed to determine the elemental composition at the primary powder boundary marked in panel (b). These results clarify the chemical nature of the boundary region in the Cu–Ni/B4C compact following the 950 °C quenching process, contributing to the comprehensive phase composition characterization.

caption: Topography map of alloy B showing grain boundaries appearing as trenches across the matrix.
summary: Topography map of alloy B showing grain boundaries appearing as trenches across the matrix. The SKPFM topography map reveals the surface morphology of the etched sample, specifically highlighting that the grain boundaries manifest as distinct trenches within the surrounding matrix structure of the alloy.

caption: Magnified inverse pole figure map of the top region highlighting fine grains within the inter-layer.
summary: This magnified inverse pole figure map focuses on the fine grains located in the inter-layer of the top region of the FRAM-6061 component. The grains have refined into equiaxed structures after the FRAM process, with the inter-layer regions showing significantly smaller grain sizes compared to the intra-layer regions.

caption: Atomic model of a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell representing the primitive unit cell of the Cr47.5Fe6.96Ni alloy.
summary: Depicted is the 3 × 3 × 3 supercell of the primitive unit cell for the Cr47.5Fe6.96Ni alloy. This structural representation is essential for DFT investigations into how high chromium content modifies the crystal structure and mechanical properties of the alloy system compared to other compositions.

caption: High-magnification focus on the magnetic microstructure of the hexagonal antidot array, highlighting the local magnetic texture and domain distribution.
summary: Focusing on the magnetic microstructure of the hexagonal antidot array, this high-magnification image provides a detailed view of the local magnetic texture. It illustrates how magnetic moments are influenced by the array symmetry, with magnetic poles of opposite sign accumulating at each side of the holes along the 0° direction.

caption: Statistical peak-frequency heatmap for the q-space range of 38–43 nm⁻¹, demonstrating the identification of distinct diffraction peaks for phase analysis.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the 38–43 nm⁻¹ q-space region, offering improved clarity for distinguishing overlapping peaks compared to conventional XRD patterns. Along with panels (a) and (b), this data confirms the presence of the MC carbide phase for fully melted D Ni ≥ 30.2% and un-melted base Alloy 738LC.

caption: Predicted versus measured diffusion paths for diffusion couples after annealing at 1473 K for 120 h.
summary: Represented here are the diffusion paths for couples annealed at 1473 K for 120 h, comparing model-predicted solid lines against measured symbols. This comparison validates the mobility parameters used in the model, showing consistent agreement between the predicted paths and the experimental measurements across the tested diffusion couple conditions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of rabbit BMSCs cultured on a 3D-printed porous scaffold after 4 days, showing live cells stained in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Live/dead cell double staining of rabbit BMSCs on 3D-printed porous scaffolds at day 4 reveals cell viability. Fluorescence microscopy demonstrates that the Coral-hHAp scaffold supports significantly higher cell proliferation and exhibits fewer dead cells compared to other scaffold groups, indicating superior biocompatibility for bone tissue engineering applications.

caption: Hydrogen permeation curve for the SLAT steel specimen, showing the characteristic flux profile over time.
summary: Hydrogen permeation results for the SLAT steel specimen are shown, displaying the characteristic flux profile over time. These measurements are part of a comprehensive analysis of LPBF maraging steels, where key parameters derived from these curves are consolidated in Table 2 to evaluate the material's hydrogen permeation properties.

caption: STEM observation of the S3 sample demonstrating the spatial interconnectivity of the three-phase eutectic structure, marked by white arrows, through extensive fibrous formation of Al3Ni.
summary: This STEM image highlights the spatial interconnectivity of the three-phase eutectic structure in the S3 sample. Marked by white arrows, the extensive fibrous formation of Al3Ni creates an ultrafine interconnected network, which is a key structural feature distinguishing the S3 sample's eutectic morphology.

caption: Radar chart evaluating the overall performance of CG and SG structures through the energy absorption efficiency (EAE) metric.
summary: This radar chart provides a comparative evaluation of the overall performance of CG and SG structures by plotting the energy absorption efficiency (EAE). The visualization serves as a key component in the comprehensive assessment of the mechanical behavior of the different structural configurations presented in the study.

caption: Surface morphology of an AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.25, showing signs of degradation.
summary: Atomic force microscopy reveals a degrading surface morphology for the AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.25. This indicates that as the AlInN fraction decreases significantly, the surface quality of the superlattice structure begins to deteriorate compared to the bulk AlInN reference.

caption: Energy density comparison for different potential windows using 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H₂SO₄ at -20 °C, benchmarked against the energy density achieved at room temperature.
summary: Energy density analysis for the 5 wt% PEGDA electrolyte at -20 °C shows that optimized potential windows yield performance comparable to or exceeding that of the device operated at room temperature with a 0–0.8 V window. This confirms the high efficiency and viability of the PEGDA-based μSC at low temperatures.

caption: Yield strength as a function of relative density for stochastic and periodic lattice configurations.
summary: Yield strength is presented as a function of relative density for stochastic and periodic lattice configurations. Numerical data derived from defect-free lattice samples are fitted using Gibson-Ashby scaling power laws. Solid lines correspond to stochastic cellular structures, and dashed lines represent periodic lattices, illustrating the mechanical scaling trends across varying densities.

caption: Dark field TEM image obtained from the reflection indicated in the inset diffraction pattern, revealing plate-like nanograins within the oxide.
summary: This dark field TEM image highlights plate-like nanograins within the oxidized Ni-4Al structure. The presence of these nanograins, as indicated by the diffraction pattern, suggests a highly twinned oxide structure formed during the 72-hour oxidation process at 420 °C, providing insight into the oxide's crystalline nature.

caption: Orientation distribution function (ODF) map for the LDED-120 specimen, representing the texture evolution of recrystallized grains under the modified processing parameters.
summary: This ODF map characterizes the recrystallized grains in the LDED-120 specimen. By comparing this result with the LDED specimen, which showed a maximum ODF value of 18.2 and strong {100}<001> texture, the influence of the LDED-120 condition on the material's texture evolution and grain orientation is clearly demonstrated.

caption: Specific flexural modulus versus specific flexural strength map for 3D printed composites, comparing carbon fiber (CF) and glass fiber (GF) reinforced samples at 0° and 90° orientations across sub-ambient (SH), room (RH), and elevated (EH) temperature conditions.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the relationship between specific flexural modulus and specific flexural strength for 3D printed continuous fiber reinforced composites. The data compares carbon fiber and glass fiber reinforcements at 0° and 90° orientations, evaluated under sub-ambient, room, and elevated temperature conditions to assess the mechanical performance of these materials.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the CNT/Al–Cu–Mg composite processed via ball milling at 200 rpm for 6 hours, highlighting the distribution of carbon nanotubes.
summary: This TEM image displays the microstructure of the CNT/Al–Cu–Mg composite after milling at 200 rpm for 6 hours. The carbon nanotubes, indicated by red arrows, exhibit micro-level uniformity and selective alignment along the high-angle grain boundaries within the aluminum matrix, demonstrating the effect of the specific milling condition.

caption: M-H curves of the (Ni37Co13Mn34Ti16)99.2B0.8 alloy recorded at selected temperatures in the vicinity of the metamagnetic transition.
summary: The (Ni37Co13Mn34Ti16)99.2B0.8 alloy exhibits a clear metamagnetic transition behavior within the MT temperature range, as evidenced by these M-H curves. This indicates that boron doping maintains the reversible magnetic field-induced metamagnetic transition, which is essential for evaluating the effect of doping on the alloy's magnetic properties.

caption: Contour map illustrating the variation of the lattice parameter across different compositional regions of the Pd-Ag-Ni films.
summary: A contour map is presented to visualize the lattice parameter variations across the composition space of the Pd-Ag-Ni films. This plot provides a comprehensive overview of how the crystal lattice dimensions change as a function of the ternary alloy composition, supporting the structural analysis of the thin films.

caption: Al-Mg alloy phase diagram highlighting the processing temperature range.
summary: The Al-Mg alloy phase diagram is presented to contextualize the thermal processing conditions. Analysis indicates that the rolling temperature of 400 °C lies between the melting points of the α-Al phase and the β phase, providing a theoretical basis for the observed grain evolution and thermal behavior.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for the CrMn0.5FeCoNi alloy in the as-cast state, after 100 h of homogenization at 1200 °C, and following 1000 h of thermal exposure at 500, 700, and 900 °C.
summary: This panel presents X-ray diffraction patterns for the CrMn0.5FeCoNi alloy, comparing the as-cast, homogenized, and thermally exposed conditions. Consistent with the CrFeCoNi alloy, the homogenized state of this material exhibits reflections characteristic of a single fcc phase, confirming the structural stability of the alloy under the specified homogenization parameters.

caption: Magnified spatial map of Euler angle Φ focusing on selected cracked grain boundaries, with disorientation angles exceeding 40° indicated across the crack interfaces.
summary: This magnified view focuses on cracked grain boundaries, revealing that cracks are strictly correlated with high angle grain boundaries in the alloy. Quantitative analysis shows that the disorientation angle between grains adjacent to these cracks is consistently greater than 40°, confirming that intragranular fracture is not observed.

caption: Frequency range of half-absorption bandwidth at a 0.5 sound absorption coefficient (bar chart) and relative absorption bandwidth (scatter chart) for MPP-DSS and microperforated sandwich-polyurethane composite structures as a function of microperforated panel thickness.
summary: Panel b characterizes the bandwidth absorption performance of the structures relative to panel thickness. It presents the half-absorption bandwidth frequency range at a 0.5 coefficient using bar charts, while scatter plots represent the relative absorption bandwidth, effectively mapping the operational frequency range for both the MPP-DSS and the composite structures.

caption: Hydrogel disc printed with Bare SPIONs, demonstrating an inhomogeneous distribution and significant color gradient.
summary: This hydrogel disc, printed with Bare SPIONs without manual mixing, exhibits a pronounced color gradient. This visual feature confirms an inhomogeneous distribution of the magnetic nanoparticles throughout the printed structure, directly resulting from the severe agglomeration observed in the precursor photo-resin during the printing process.

caption: Diagram illustrating the defined exposed surface area of 0.9 cm2 (1.5 cm × 0.6 cm) for the NAB alloy specimens.
summary: The diagram highlights the specific exposed region of the NAB alloy specimens, which measures 0.6 cm by 1.5 cm, resulting in a total area of 0.9 cm2. This identical exposed area was maintained across all tested specimens, including as-built, HT-1, and HT-2, while remaining surfaces were masked with paint.

caption: Schematic illustrations of a continuous cooling transformation diagram showing various solid-solid phase transformation pathways dependent on cooling rates.
summary: This diagram details the phase transformation processes occurring under different cooling conditions. It highlights the sequence: α' (SLM-produced) transforming to α+Ti 2 Cu between 600–700 °C, M phase above 790 °C, and finally α+α'' upon water quenching. These pathways demonstrate the sensitivity of the final microstructure to specific thermal cooling rates.

caption: WPPM fit analysis for the S-200 specimen, illustrating the agreement between experimental neutron diffraction data and the modelled profile, with the residual shown in the upper section.
summary: The S-200 specimen's neutron diffraction data is modeled using the WPPM method. The experimental data, represented by black dots, is compared against the colored fitted profile. The fit residual is displayed above the pattern, and the intensity is plotted on a logarithmic scale to support microstructural parameter refinement.

caption: Evolution of training loss over time for the foundation model as it undergoes fine-tuning using the four distinct transfer learning schemes.
summary: The training loss evolution is tracked during the fine-tuning of the foundation model. By monitoring these curves across the four transfer learning schemes, the performance and stability of the model's convergence are assessed, ensuring that the final neurons are effectively optimized for the specific task of flow rate regression.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectral changes of methylene blue mixed with NaBH4 in the presence of SL-NiNPs.
summary: This panel presents the UV-visible absorption spectral alterations of methylene blue when combined with NaBH4 in the presence of SL-NiNPs. The spectral changes indicate the degradation of methylene blue, demonstrating the catalytic activity of the SL-NiNPs in facilitating the reduction process compared to the control condition.

caption: Pair distribution function plot for the borosilicate glass bulk, showing a characteristic Si-O first neighborhood distance of approximately 1.63 Å.
summary: The pair distribution function (PDF) for the borosilicate glass bulk is presented to verify the accuracy of the structural model. Analysis of the plot reveals a consistent Si-O first neighborhood distance of about 1.63 Å, confirming the structural integrity and local atomic arrangement within the simulated glass bulk.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of L-DED fabricated AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA specimen processed at an AED of 60.87 J/mm2.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map depicts the crystallographic orientation of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA specimen fabricated at an areal energy density of 60.87 J/mm2. It serves to visualize the grain structure and texture resulting from the L-DED fabrication process under these specific thermal and energy input conditions.

caption: Enlarged view of the solidification plateau for 3DTES-nn samples in R1, highlighting the duration difference between V-nn and Al2O3-nn variants.
summary: Focusing on the solidification plateau, this panel reveals that the phase transition lasts approximately 60 seconds for V-nn samples. In contrast, the Al2O3-nn variant exhibits a shorter plateau of 30 seconds, a difference attributed to the higher thermal conductivity of the alumina-enhanced material during the discharging process.

caption: Bode impedance plots of ATI718 Plus, where the phase angle reaches approximately 70° in the mid-frequency range, highlighting the protective nature of the passive film.
summary: Bode impedance plots for ATI718 Plus reveal that the phase angle approaches 70° within the mid-frequency range. This observation reflects the superior protective effect provided by the passive film formed on the alloy surface, with solid lines indicating the accuracy of the EEC model fitting to the experimental data.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for the line build specimen, showing intensity profiles across axial/build and transverse directions.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for the line build specimen are presented, covering both axial/build and transverse directions. The line build exhibits a relatively stronger presence of (311) planes compared to the spot build. These patterns reveal the dominant presence of {200} orientation, resembling a single crystal, with each run representing different loads.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the frequency dependence of impedance magnitude and phase angle for Ni–Mo coatings annealed at different temperatures in 15 wt. % HCl solution.
summary: Bode plots display the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for Ni–Mo coatings subjected to various annealing temperatures. These plots, alongside the Nyquist data, characterize the corrosion resistance of the coatings, with the 850 °C annealed coating exhibiting the best corrosion resistance in the 15 wt. % HCl solution.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) patterns of iHEAs before and after laser-melting, showing the presence of gamma-f.c.c. and NbC phases.
summary: SXRD patterns validate the phase evolution in iHEAs, confirming the presence of gamma-f.c.c. and NbC phases, both crystallizing in the Fm-3m space group. Lattice parameters are provided for the gamma-f.c.c. matrix and NbC carbides across different compositions, demonstrating the structural consistency and phase changes occurring during the laser-melting process.

caption: Full XPS survey spectra of Ag@PDA film-modified NiTi alloy samples, showing characteristic peaks for C 1s, N 1s, and O 1s across different dopant concentrations.
summary: Full XPS survey spectra of the Ag@PDA film-modified NiTi alloy are presented, illustrating the chemical composition of the surface. The spectra reveal characteristic peaks corresponding to C 1s, N 1s, and O 1s, confirming the successful formation of the PDA film across various dopant concentrations on the NiTi alloy substrate.

caption: Three-dimensional array configuration consisting of a 3 × 3 × 3 arrangement of the unit cells.
summary: Depicted here is the periodic assembly of the unit cells into a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell array. This configuration demonstrates the scalability of the metamaterial design, providing a comprehensive view of the structural features and spatial organization of the proposed 3D mechanical metamaterial system.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF-Y) and image quality (IQ) map of the 4 mm component, highlighting 60°/[111] (black) and 70°/[110] (white) boundaries, with an inset showing intra-grain lamellar morphological boundaries.
summary: This IPF-Y map overlaid with an IQ map reveals the crystallographic orientation of the 4 mm component. The microstructure is characterized by primarily γ-phase grains containing lamellar twins, as highlighted by the specific axis-angle boundaries. The inset provides a detailed view of these intra-grain lamellar morphological features.

caption: Partial electronic density of states for the first neighboring atoms of the site exhibiting the highest vacancy formation energy.
summary: This panel displays the partial electronic density of states (PDOS) calculated for the first neighboring atoms of the site with the highest vacancy formation energy.
