caption: Normalized resistivity plotted against temperature for (TiZrNbCu)1-xNix amorphous alloys, with an inset displaying the superconducting resistivity transitions observed at temperatures below 1.6 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent normalized resistivity of (TiZrNbCu)1-xNix amorphous alloys. The main graph highlights the semiconducting resistivity behavior across a broad composition range, while the inset confirms that all samples exhibit superconductivity with transition temperatures Tc ≤ 1.6 K, indicating a direct relationship between resistivity and electron-phonon interactions.

caption: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for SC-02 in acetonitrile, showing the spectral overlap used to determine the singlet excited state energy level.
summary: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for SC-02 in acetonitrile are presented. The crossing point of these two spectra is utilized to experimentally determine the singlet excited state energy level (S1) of the material, providing critical insight into its electronic transition properties within the solvent environment.

caption: Pourbaix diagram for the Fe-Ni-Cr-O system displaying the stability fields of NiO, Cr2O3, Fe2O3, FeCr2O4, and Fe3O4 under RAR conditions, with a red arrow highlighting the ECP transition from UR to IR.
summary: This Pourbaix diagram for the Fe-Ni-Cr-O system identifies the stable oxides under RAR conditions, including NiO, Cr2O3, Fe2O3, FeCr2O4, and Fe3O4. The diagram indicates that the inner oxide layer of FeCrAl-Ni IR is likely a complex mixture of these oxides, including NiFe2O4 and NiCr2O4, as the ECP shifts.

caption: Comparison of deviations between raw infrared temperature data and values processed via polynomial and least-squares fitting methods across specific column positions in the 30th layer.
summary: This plot illustrates the deviation between raw infrared temperature data and fitted data using polynomial and least-squares methods. The analysis covers specific column positions within the 30th layer of sample S2 30. These deviations quantify the accuracy of the fitting techniques used to clean the experimental temperature measurements during the cooling phase.

caption: Response surface contour plot depicting the relationship between dimension parameters D and T and the Energy Absorption Efficiency (EAE).
summary: Representing the Energy Absorption Efficiency (EAE) as a function of D and T, this response surface plot is part of the BBD analysis for compressive properties. The contour visualization highlights the sensitivity of EAE to changes in the specified dimension parameters within the experimental design space.

caption: FTIR spectra of the manufactured samples, featuring a vertically shifted presentation to facilitate direct comparison between different materials.
summary: The FTIR spectra of the manufactured samples are presented in this figure, with vertical shifts applied to the data to allow for easier comparison between the different specimens. An inset is included to highlight the specific wavenumber range between 2500 and 2000 cm-1, providing detailed insight into the chemical bonding characteristics.

caption: Star symbol plots comparing metabolite profiles of Ti, Ti/EB 0.05, and Ti/EB 0.5 groups in 48-hour cultured macrophages, normalized to the Ti group mean.
summary: Star symbol plots visualize the metabolic profiles of macrophages cultured on Ti, Ti/EB 0.05, and Ti/EB 0.5 surfaces. Fifteen metabolites showed common changes across groups, while seven specific metabolites exhibited greater variation in the Ti/EB 0.5 group. Anti-inflammatory and inflammatory metabolites were generally reduced in the Ti/EB 0.05 group compared to others.

caption: Magnified view of the Si-311 diffraction peak at approximately 2θ = 29°, highlighting the displacement observed in heat-treated samples (T5, T6, and SR) relative to the as-built condition.
summary: Focusing on the Si-311 diffraction peak at 2θ ≈ 29°, this magnified plot illustrates distinct peak displacements in heat-treated samples (T5, T6, and SR) compared to the as-built material. These shifts indicate lattice parameter changes or internal strain variations induced by the specific heat-treatment protocols applied to the samples.

caption: Conceptual block diagram illustrating the proposed methodology integrated with an optimization technique.
summary: This block diagram provides a high-level overview of the proposed research framework. It explicitly highlights the integration of an optimization technique within the workflow, serving as a foundational schematic to guide the reader through the systematic approach and logical progression of the study's methodology and computational process.

caption: Elastic modulus of the proposed OIPL structures plotted against varying numbers of unit cells.
summary: This panel illustrates the elastic modulus of the proposed OIPL structures as a function of the number of unit cells. The data demonstrates how the structural configuration, specifically the unit cell count, influences the mechanical stiffness of the material, providing insight into the mechanical performance of the proposed design.

caption: Near-infrared (NIR) reflectance spectra of pure copper and Dragon Copper, with reference values for 316L stainless steel and Inconel 718 at the 1064 nm laser wavelength.
summary: NIR reflectance spectra compare pure copper and Dragon Copper, highlighting the enhanced absorption of 1064 nm laser radiation enabled by CNTs. Reference values for 316L stainless steel and Inconel 718 are included at the 1064 nm wavelength to provide context for the laser absorption characteristics during PBF-LB processing.

caption: Comparison of capacitance retention for 5 wt% PEGDA and 15 wt% PVA electrolytes at various temperatures, normalized to the capacitance measured at room temperature.
summary: Capacitance retention plots compare the performance of PEGDA-based and PVA-based electrolytes across a range of temperatures. The data demonstrates that the PEGDA-based electrolyte exhibits superior performance in the sub-zero temperature range compared to the conventional PVA-based gel electrolyte, maintaining higher relative capacitance as temperatures decrease from room temperature.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetic entropy change for as-built PBF-EB/M samples calculated at various magnetic fields up to 5 T.
summary: The magnetic entropy change ΔS is plotted as a function of temperature for as-built PBF-EB/M samples. These values were derived using Maxwell's equation applied to isothermal magnetization data. The results illustrate how the entropy change varies with the applied magnetic field strength within the FOMST temperature range.

caption: Intensity distributions and beam propagation profiles for index BS4 at varying relative distances (Δz) from the waist radius.
summary: This panel displays the intensity distributions of beam propagation at various positions relative to the waist radius for index BS4. These profiles illustrate the optical behavior as the beam approaches the F-theta lens, with observations noting that asymmetry in irradiance profiles at the acquisition boundaries is specific to this optical configuration.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of the crack tip subjected to a hypergravitational force of 3.83 MPa at 472 °C.
summary: Scanning electron micrograph of the crack tip subjected to a hypergravitational force of 3.83 MPa at 472 °C. This image reveals the morphology of the crack tip under specific thermal and mechanical conditions. The magnification remains consistent across all panels, allowing for a direct comparison of crack tip evolution under varying hypergravitational forces.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy analysis of the PTM scaffolds to characterize chemical functional groups.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy is utilized to characterize the chemical composition and functional groups present within the PTM scaffolds. This analysis provides essential data regarding the molecular structure and chemical integrity of the scaffold materials, ensuring the successful incorporation of components during the low-temperature 3D printing process.

caption: Representative CLSM images showing the 3D organization and morphology of fibroblasts embedded in oxALG-RGD-PVGLIG hydrogels over a 14-day culture period, with F-actin stained in green and nuclei in blue, alongside immunofluorescence imaging of fibronectin (FN) deposition in red after 14 days.
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy reveals the 3D morphology and organization of fibroblasts cultured within oxALG-RGD-PVGLIG hydrogels over two weeks. F-actin and nuclei staining demonstrate cell viability and structural integration, while red-channel immunofluorescence highlights the successful deposition of fibronectin, confirming the cell-permissive nature of the hydrogel scaffold for ECM production.

caption: Mixing enthalpy of bcc random solution for Ta-based alloys as a function of composition, comparing MD calculations at 0 K or 1250 K with thermodynamic estimates.
summary: This panel displays the calculated mixing enthalpy for Ta-based bcc random solution alloys. The data compares MD simulation results at 0 K for W-Ta, Mo-Ta, and Nb-Ta systems against thermodynamic estimates derived from experimental data or DFT calculations. These results illustrate the composition-dependent energetic stability of these specific Ta-based alloy systems.

caption: Experimental polarisation curves comparing AM and sintered PTLs over five cycles in a single-cell PEMWE setup.
summary: Single-cell PEMWE performance was evaluated by measuring polarisation curves for both AM and sintered PTL plates over five cycles. This panel displays the experimental data, providing a direct comparison of the electrochemical performance between the two different PTL manufacturing methods under identical testing conditions.

caption: Radar plot evaluating multiple energy absorption metrics for the proposed OIS and OIHS, highlighting the superior performance of the COPH configuration in terms of maximum plateau stress and crush force efficiency.
summary: This radar chart provides a multi-dimensional comparison of energy absorption indicators for the proposed origami structures. It specifically highlights that the COPH configuration outperforms non-hybrid and other hybrid structures, achieving the highest values for maximum plateau stress and crush force efficiency, thereby demonstrating its superior mechanical energy absorption capabilities.

caption: Conceptual representation of the ZWT constitutive model, illustrating the parallel arrangement of a nonlinear spring element and two Maxwell (Mx) elements characterized by distinct relaxation times.
summary: This schematic illustrates the ZWT constitutive model, which describes nonlinear material behavior under high strain rate and large strain conditions. The model consists of a nonlinear spring element connected in parallel with two Maxwell elements, each featuring specific relaxation times to account for different strain rate responses in polymer materials.

caption: Stress-free reference lattice profiles of the {311} plane along the height of the inter-pass rolled wall specimen.
summary: This panel presents the stress-free reference lattice profiles for the {311} plane in the inter-pass rolled wall. The plot illustrates the difficulty of determining a reliable d0 reference in neutron diffraction experiments, reflecting the complexities introduced by the textured and coarse-grained nature of the processed material during measurement.

caption: Unit cell model showing the crystalline structure of Al13Fe4.
summary: Depicted is the unit cell model for the Al13Fe4 intermetallic phase. This structural representation allows for the examination of the atomic lattice, which is essential for understanding the material's properties, with its specific lattice constants being part of the comprehensive data set summarized in the referenced table.

caption: Thermal imaging of tumor-bearing mice demonstrating temperature elevation at the tumor site after intravenous administration of MGO-PEG-CET, magnetic targeting, and NIR light exposure.
summary: Thermal imaging of tumor-bearing mice provides evidence of effective photothermal heating at the tumor site. The observed temperature increase, resulting from MGO-PEG-CET administration, magnetic targeting, and NIR irradiation, confirms the therapeutic potential of this system for localized cancer treatment as suggested by the photothermal therapy findings.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of nitrogen solubility as a function of temperature.
summary: This panel presents the calculated effect of temperature on nitrogen solubility within the material. The data was derived using Thermo-calc thermodynamic software to model the solubility behavior, providing a theoretical baseline for understanding how thermal conditions influence nitrogen retention in the system during processing.

caption: Comparison of estimated load-to-failure values for LPBF-manufactured Ti6Al4V specimens subjected to various mechanical surface treatments followed by HIP, benchmarked against wrought Ti6Al4V material.
summary: This plot evaluates the fatigue performance of LPBF-manufactured Ti6Al4V specimens after undergoing HIP and mechanical surface treatments. By comparing these treated samples to wrought Ti6Al4V, the study validates the effectiveness of combining HIP and surface modification processes to optimize the mechanical integrity and load-bearing capacity of additively manufactured titanium components.

caption: Creep deformation prediction versus experimental results for AA2195-T3 creep-aged at 180 °C in the 45° loading direction under 120, 160, and 200 MPa stress levels.
summary: This panel illustrates the creep deformation prediction results for the 45° loading direction using the established NURBS curves. By comparing the model lines with experimental symbols at 120, 160, and 200 MPa, the figure demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach in predicting creep behavior for AA2195-T3 at 180 °C.

caption: Surface topography of the polished sample annealed at 550 °C, imaged using laser confocal microscopy.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy displays the surface topography of the polished sample after annealing at 550 °C. This panel allows for the evaluation of surface roughness and transformation grade, demonstrating how the initial polished state responds to the oxidising procedure at this specific thermal treatment condition.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for the d-band of a labeled Au atom on a clean Au-Ni (1 0 0) alloy surface.
summary: This panel presents the PDOS for the d-band of a labeled Au atom on a clean Au-Ni (1 0 0) alloy surface. This electronic structure data provides the necessary baseline to evaluate the hybridization effects and binding characteristics of the Au-Ni alloy surface during subsequent CO adsorption studies.

caption: Representative indentation load-displacement curves illustrating the mechanical response of the material layers during nanoindentation testing.
summary: Representative indentation load-displacement curves are shown for the major and minor layers. These curves reflect the mechanical response of the material during nanoindentation, corresponding to the measured hardness values of 9.3 ± 0.4 GPa and 10.4 ± 0.8 GPa, respectively, achieved at different penetration depths during the testing process.

caption: Predicted strain distribution in the loading direction at 6.8% engineering strain, highlighting the confinement of high deformation to the G91 base metal upon necking initiation.
summary: As the engineering strain reaches 6.8%, the simulation captures the onset of necking. The high deformation zone becomes restricted specifically to the G91 base metal, whereas the clad material exhibits a relatively uniform strain distribution, marking a transition in the mechanical response of the welded assembly.

caption: Porosity heatmap for the pure AlSi7Mg0.6 matrix, illustrating sample density variations across a range of laser powers and scanning velocities.
summary: This heatmap displays the parameter-dependent porosity of pure AlSi7Mg0.6 matrix samples fabricated on an Aconity MIDI+ machine. By evaluating various laser power and velocity combinations, the plot identifies optimal processing conditions, specifically suggesting P: 350 W and V: 1650 mm/s for achieving high-density samples based on Archimedes method measurements.

caption: Immunofluorescence images of EdU staining in HUVECs, visualizing cell proliferation activity.
summary: EdU staining was employed to assess the proliferative activity of HUVECs following ApoV treatment. The representative immunofluorescence images reveal that ApoV treatment significantly promoted HUVEC migration and proliferation, with the most notable effects observed at an optimal concentration of 2.0 μg/ml.

caption: Creep rate comparison of UT and HT90(2h) PLA samples at 47 °C, showing reduced creep rates for the heat-treated material.
summary: At 47 °C, the HT90(2h) PLA sample demonstrates a lower creep rate compared to the UT sample under 12 MPa stress. This improved performance is attributed to the increased crystalline structure induced by the 90 °C heat treatment, which effectively limits polymer chain mobility during the creep test.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topographies comparing the surface roughness of passive films on LTC4 and ATC4 alloys after potentiostatic polarization at 0.6 V.
summary: Atomic force microscopy topographies illustrate the surface roughness of passive films on LTC4 and ATC4. Distinct RMS roughness levels are observed on both samples, attributed to varying oxide growth rates on different phases. Notably, the passive film on ATC4 exhibits a higher surface roughness compared to that on LTC4.

caption: Finite element model illustrating the Darcy permeability coefficient calculation, showing fluid flow along the positive X-axis through interconnected pores and coolant channels.
summary: This finite element model visualizes the Darcy permeability coefficient calculation process. Fluid enters from the left, traverses the interconnected pores and coolant channels within the model, and exits through the right side. This simulation setup provides a structured approach to analyzing fluid transport properties within the specified porous material geometry.

caption: SEM micrograph of the H2 nanocomposite worn-out surface exhibiting shallow, longitudinal abrasion grooves.
summary: The SEM image of the H2 nanocomposite worn-out surface reveals a relatively uniform topography characterized by longitudinal and shallow grooves. These features are indicative of an abrasion wear mechanism, which is the dominant process observed for the nanocomposite samples during the conducted wear tests.

caption: Load-deflection response of an HPC plate without FRP reinforcement, demonstrating weak mechanical behavior.
summary: This panel displays the load-deflection curve for an HPC plate lacking FRP reinforcement. The data indicates that the specimen exhibits a weak mechanical response compared to reinforced counterparts. This baseline measurement highlights the limited structural capacity of the unreinforced material under the applied loading conditions during the mechanical test.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern characterizing the crystalline phases present at the interface between ER2205 stainless steel and Inconel 718 alloy.
summary: This X-ray diffraction pattern provides a structural analysis of the ER2205–Inconel 718 interface. The data serves to identify the specific crystalline phases formed at the junction of these two distinct materials, offering critical insights into the metallurgical characteristics and phase composition resulting from the joining process at the interface.

caption: Room temperature carrier mobility as a function of Ni alloying content in Bi2-xNixSe3, demonstrating a continuous decrease in mobility values as Ni concentration increases.
summary: This graph presents the room temperature carrier mobility for Bi2-xNixSe3 samples relative to Ni content. The data shows a continuous decrease in mobility as Ni addition increases. This trend correlates with the increased carrier concentration, reinforcing the role of Ni content and Se vacancies in modifying charge transport properties.

caption: Linear fitting of the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the product of alpha and peak stress versus the inverse of absolute temperature.
summary: This Arrhenius-style plot shows the linear relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of alpha-scaled peak stress and the inverse of absolute temperature. The slope of this fitted line is used to extract key material constants, facilitating the analysis of temperature-dependent deformation mechanisms in the studied material.

caption: Top-down atomic snapshot of graphene after 1000 recoil cascades, illustrating the final structural state in Stage IV.
summary: Representing the final stage of the damage analysis, this snapshot displays the graphene structure after 1000 cascades. The arrangement of purple and grey spheres illustrates the long-term impact of cumulative recoils on the intrinsic structure, completing the four-stage assessment of graphene's structural survival and damage behavior.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction depicting Fe, Ni, and Al atom maps and the Al–Ni 50 at.% iso-concentration surface for an 80% 316L composition sample processed at 650W-45IPM.
summary: Atom probe tomography of the 80% 316L sample processed at 650W-45IPM shows the Fe, Ni, and Al atom distribution. The Ni-Al 50 at.% iso-concentration surface indicates a significantly reduced fraction of B2 NiAl particles compared to the 90% 316L sample processed at higher energy density, confirming the influence of processing parameters.

caption: Correlation between the distance of fracture initiation and impact toughness values.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between fracture initiation distance and impact toughness. The data indicates that the distance of fracture initiation increases as the impact toughness of the material improves, demonstrating a positive correlation between these two mechanical properties during the fracture testing process.

caption: Steady-state strain rate versus true stress for CP and PM alloys at 400 °C, shown on a double logarithmic scale.
summary: The steady-state strain rate and true stress for CP and PM alloys at 400 °C are depicted on a double logarithmic scale. Following the general-power law constitutive creep equation, this plot enables the evaluation of creep behavior and the extraction of key parameters like the apparent stress exponent at 400 °C.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry curves of EAN electrolytes containing different ion concentrations, measured on FTO glass substrates at 60°C within a controlled glove box environment.
summary: Linear sweep voltammetry curves illustrate the polarization behavior of EAN electrolytes with varying ion contents. These measurements were conducted on FTO glass substrates at a constant temperature of 60°C inside a glove box, providing insight into the electrochemical response of the system under controlled experimental conditions.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves illustrating the phase transition characteristics for pure RT44 paraffin wax and the GF_RT44 composite material.
summary: This panel presents the DSC curves for RT44 and the GF_RT44 composite, providing a clear view of their phase transition behavior. The thermal analysis demonstrates the impact of the composite structure on the phase change characteristics of the RT44 paraffin wax, confirming the thermal response of the material system.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting the morphology and distribution of the deformation-induced alpha''-martensite planar traces.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging provides clear visualization of the deformation-induced alpha''-martensite plates. These plates, which form near the beta-Ti matrix and unmelted Nb particle interfacial regions, exhibit an intersecting morphology that suggests a significant role in the strengthening mechanisms active during the tensile deformation of the studied alloy.

caption: Nyquist plots of FeCoNiCr 1-x Al x HEAs in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at open circuit potential, showing consistent arc characteristics across all five alloys.
summary: Nyquist plots for FeCoNiCr 1-x Al x HEAs in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution reveal consistent arc characteristics, suggesting the passivation mechanism remains unchanged by Al addition. The semicircle diameters follow the order Al0 > Al0.5 > Al0.75 > Al0.25 > Al1, indicating variations in electrochemical impedance behavior among the different alloy compositions.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of SUS430 powder following hydrogen reduction at 750 °C and subsequent ammonia decomposition testing.
summary: This XRD pattern displays the structural state of SUS430 powder after undergoing hydrogen reduction at 750 °C and ammonia decomposition. Analysis confirms the formation of nitride species on the alloy surface as a result of the ammonia exposure, indicating significant chemical modification of the material during the decomposition process.

caption: Bar chart comparing the total grain boundary length statistics for T0 and C1–C5 specimens.
summary: This bar chart quantifies the total grain boundary length for T0 and C1–C5 specimens. The data demonstrates that the grain boundary length in C1–C5 progressively increases with increasing LED levels, highlighting the significant impact of processing conditions on the microstructural grain boundary network within the analyzed material samples.

caption: Inspection of the three calibration positions using a 1-inch SMR placed in the TriCal trihedral nest, captured by the laser tracker to verify system performance.
summary: The image illustrates the inspection process where a 1-inch SMR is placed in the TriCal trihedral nest. By utilizing the laser tracker to measure these three specific calibration positions, the system's positioning accuracy is verified, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed calibration method.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the Cu-Ni-Co-Si alloy deformed at 800 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹, revealing the presence of rod-shaped and spherical-shaped precipitates within the matrix.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of a Cu-Ni-Co-Si alloy after deformation at 800 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹. The image highlights the distribution of precipitates, which exhibit both rod-like and spherical morphologies, providing insight into the dynamic precipitation process occurring within the alloy during high-temperature deformation.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of the polycrystalline Ni alloy following 2 hours and 30 minutes of oxidation at 250℃, showing characteristic oxide signals beyond the metal-oxide interface attributed to reoxidation of the exposed reactive metal surface.
summary: Following 2 hours and 30 minutes of oxidation at 250℃, the ToF-SIMS profile shows persistent signals for characteristic oxides beyond the metal-oxide interface. These signals are attributed to the reoxidation of the reactive metal surface that remains exposed to oxygen during the in situ oxidation procedure.

caption: Full discharge profiles of the CX@Fe cathode at 0.1 mA/cm2, showing the initial discharge (solid line) and a subsequent discharge (dashed line) after electrode washing.
summary: The discharge profile of the CX@Fe cathode is presented at a current density of 0.1 mA/cm2. The solid line represents the initial full discharge until 2 V cut-off, indicating complete surface passivation. A subsequent discharge, shown as a dashed line, confirms the electrochemical behavior under identical conditions after the cathode was washed.

caption: High-magnification SEM micrograph of the XY plane showing acicular carbides in interdendritic regions and finer carbides within crack gaps, indicative of liquation cracking.
summary: High-magnification SEM analysis of the XY plane reveals acicular carbides approximately 4.7 μm long in interdendritic regions. The presence of finer carbides dispersed within the crack gaps confirms the occurrence of liquation cracking in the modified Hastelloy X alloy, contributing to the overall understanding of solidification cracking mechanisms.

caption: Measured blue wavelength pattern showing the intensity distribution at and beyond the focal plane.
summary: This panel displays the measured blue wavelength pattern, illustrating the intensity distribution observed at and beyond the focal plane. These results, alongside the UV and simulated data, serve as validation for the optical model and simulation method employed in the study to characterize the system's performance.

caption: Atomic resolution HAADF-STEM image derived from the dashed square in panel (a), showing the atomic structure at the dispersoid/matrix interface.
summary: Captured at atomic resolution, this HAADF-STEM image provides a detailed view of the dispersoid/matrix interface within the naturally aged alloy. Derived from the specific region marked in panel (a), the image allows for the precise observation of atomic arrangements and structural features at the interface after 30 days of aging.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra comparing pure PLA matrix against composites reinforced with 5 wt% untreated and chemically treated enset and sisal fibers.
summary: This FTIR spectral analysis evaluates the chemical composition of pure PLA and its composites reinforced with 5 wt% enset and sisal fibers. The plot highlights differences between untreated and chemically treated fiber reinforcements, providing insight into the chemical interactions and structural modifications within the PLA-based composite materials analyzed in the study.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the frequency-dependent phase angle response for BAC and CHBAC devices.
summary: Bode plots demonstrate distinct frequency responses between the two devices. While the phase angle for the BAC device approaches -90 degrees at low frequencies, the CHBAC device does not reach this value, highlighting differences in the capacitive behavior and electrochemical characteristics of the two materials.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for 3 wt% TiC/Ti6Al4V composite, illustrating that the material composition resides within the hypereutectic region.
summary: Representing the equilibrium phase diagram for a 3 wt% TiC/Ti6Al4V composite, this panel demonstrates that the material's chemical composition falls within the hypereutectic region. This classification highlights the phase behavior characteristic of this specific TiC addition level during the solidification of the composite.

caption: Monkman-Grant plot illustrating the relationship between uniaxial creep and SPCT data, with m and p parameters estimated according to Eq. (2).
summary: The Monkman-Grant plot presents a comparative analysis of SPCT and uniaxial creep test results. Parameters m and p are derived using the specified Eq. (2). This visualization serves to validate the consistency of the creep behavior observed across the different testing methods employed in the study.

caption: Binary phase diagram for the Fe-Nb system showing temperature versus composition.
summary: The Fe-Nb binary phase diagram delineates the equilibrium phase relationships for the iron-niobium system relative to temperature and composition. This representation is essential for understanding the solubility limits and intermetallic phase formation, which are key factors in the development and heat treatment of niobium-alloyed iron materials.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction diagram for the Al-Fe-Ce alloy, showing the predicted phase evolution as a function of temperature.
summary: The equilibrium phase fraction diagram for the Al-Fe-Ce alloy provides a thermodynamic prediction of phase stability. Comparison with experimental XRD patterns reveals that neither this equilibrium model nor the Scheil-Gulliver model could fully predict all phases observed in the actual material, indicating potential limitations in the current predictive models.

caption: Crack length evolution plotted against the number of loading cycles for a SEN-T specimen subjected to pure fatigue at 550 °C under two distinct loading conditions.
summary: Crack length evolution is presented as a function of loading cycles for a SEN-T specimen tested at 550 °C under pure fatigue conditions. The plot compares two different loading cases, illustrating the progression of crack growth over time as the specimen undergoes cyclic loading at 1 Hz frequency.

caption: HAADF-TEM image and cross-sectional EDS mapping of IN 625 alloy after 28 days of vapour salt exposure at 565 °C, displaying a thin, compact oxide layer.
summary: Exposed to vapour salt at 565 °C for 28 days, the IN 625 alloy exhibits a thin oxide layer measuring approximately 700 nm. The HAADF-TEM imaging and EDS mapping reveal a dense, homogeneous oxide scale characterized by minimal voids or structural defects, indicating high stability under these specific corrosive conditions.

caption: Infrared thermography image of two tungsten double tiles subjected to 15 MW m-2 high heat flux loading, captured during the 200th cycle, highlighting surface temperature variations and crack locations marked by black arrows.
summary: This infrared thermography image displays two tungsten double tiles under 15 MW m-2 high heat flux exposure at the 200th loading cycle. The visualization reveals surface temperature gradients and identifies crack locations with black arrows. Coated regions exhibit localized temperature increases, while cracks are visible across both coated and uncoated surfaces.

caption: Schematic representation of the printing path generation process, illustrating the geometric constraints imposed on the widths of chain primitives relative to the printed fibre filament.
summary: This schematic illustrates the printing path generation process, highlighting the geometric constraints between the width of a given chain primitive and the actual width of the printed fibre filament. It provides a visual framework for understanding how these parameters are controlled during the additive manufacturing of the fibre structure.

caption: Normalized reaction power versus temperature profiles for 11 distinct heating rates, with duplicate scans presented for each rate and curves vertically offset for visual clarity.
summary: This plot displays normalized reaction power as a function of temperature across 11 different heating rates, with two scans per rate. The curves are stacked to improve readability, though this normalization means the area under each curve does not represent total heat release. A broad shoulder is visible at the reaction onset.

caption: Evolution of Vickers hardness values across as-built, solution treated, and aged states for ST 900, ST 1040, and ST 1125 heat treatment conditions.
summary: This plot tracks the evolution of mechanical properties by displaying Vickers hardness measurements across three distinct heat treatment stages: as-built, solution treated, and aged. The data compares three specific solution treatment temperatures—900, 1040, and 1125 degrees Celsius—to evaluate how these processing steps influence the final hardness of the material.

caption: Calculated electronic band structure of Sn-soluted ZnO, revealing the electronic band modifications resulting from tin solute incorporation.
summary: The calculated band structure for Sn-soluted ZnO is shown, detailing the electronic energy dispersion changes associated with tin doping. This panel completes the comparative analysis of ZnO with different solute elements, enabling a comprehensive understanding of how Sn incorporation influences the electronic band structure relative to the pure material.

caption: Energy storage modulus (G′) as a function of frequency for PAA, CASM-S1, CASM-S3, and CASM-S5 hydrogels, characterizing the elastic response of the material compositions.
summary: This panel depicts the storage modulus (G′) for PAA, CASM-S1, CASM-S3, and CASM-S5 hydrogels. These measurements, performed to investigate the effect of SLS addition on rheological properties, characterize the elastic energy storage capacity of the hydrogels across different compositions, providing insight into the material's stiffness and structural integrity under dynamic loading.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the impact of individual input parameters on the accuracy of phase prediction models.
summary: This bar chart quantifies the influence of specific input parameters on phase prediction accuracy. By systematically removing individual features and measuring the resulting drop in model performance, the authors identified which parameters are most critical for accurate phase classification, providing insight into the sensitivity of the predictive model to specific input data.

caption: X-ray reflectivity profile and best-fit model for Ni-Zr thin alloy films annealed at 800 °C, including an inset of the electron scattering length density profile.
summary: X-ray reflectivity data for Ni-Zr thin alloy films annealed at 800 °C are represented by open circles with solid lines indicating the best fits. The inset shows the electron scattering length density profile, illustrating the final changes in electron density and thickness after high-temperature thermal annealing.

caption: Parity plot of experimental versus predicted DE for System-1, highlighting the impact of different δ values on prediction accuracy.
summary: This plot displays the experimental versus predicted DE for System-1 under varying δ values. The results show significant fluctuations in predicted DE at 200 °C and 3.75 MPa, demonstrating how the δ parameter influences the model's performance and the resulting alignment between experimental observations and computational predictions for System-1.

caption: Temperature-frequency sweep data for a PEI specimen heated from 30 to 235 °C at 5 °C increments, with frequencies ranging from 1 to 100 Hz.
summary: This panel displays a typical temperature-frequency sweep for a PEI specimen. The experimental setup involved heating the material from 30 to 235 °C in 5 °C steps while applying frequencies between 1 and 100 Hz. These measurements provide the raw data necessary for subsequent viscoelastic analysis and master curve construction.

caption: EBSD axial orientation map and corresponding inverse pole figure for the K447A region located 5 mm to the left of the fracture surface, showing equiaxed grains with multiple orientations.
summary: This panel displays the EBSD axial orientation map and inverse pole figure for the K447A region 5 mm to the left of the fracture surface. The analysis reveals a typical equiaxed crystal structure characterized by multiple grain orientations, providing insight into the microstructural state of the superalloy after creep rupture at 760 °C/725 MPa.

caption: Reflected wavelength change measurements for 3D-printed HPCA objects in acidic conditions (pH = 1).
summary: This panel presents the reflected wavelength data for 3D-printed HPCA objects exposed to acidic conditions at pH = 1. The measurements indicate almost no change in the reflective wavelength, consistent with the visual observation that the object maintains its original color and structure without any degradation or swelling.

caption: Log-log plot of the minimum creep rate versus the normalized effective stress for upper limit data, calculated assuming a true stress exponent of n = 4.
summary: This log-log plot illustrates the relationship between the minimum creep rate and the normalized effective stress for upper limit data. By incorporating a threshold stress into the effective stress calculation, the true stress exponent is determined, assuming a value of n = 4 for the creep mechanism analysis.

caption: Severe hardness variation observed in H13 ESR ingots processed at 700 A without an axial static magnetic field.
summary: Severe hardness variations are documented in H13 ESR ingots processed at 700 A without an axial static magnetic field. This panel illustrates the challenges of maintaining mechanical uniformity at higher current levels, where the lack of magnetic control exacerbates structural inconsistencies and leads to significant fluctuations in the final ingot hardness.

caption: Comparison of the storage modulus measured via DMA for cast and 3D-printed TPU/P-CNF3 samples.
summary: This DMA plot illustrates the storage modulus for both cast and 3D-printed TPU/P-CNF3 specimens. By comparing these curves, the study confirms that the 3D printing process effectively preserves the mechanical stiffness and functional integrity of the composite material when compared to the original cast form.

caption: I-V measurement at 300 K, demonstrating the recovery of the diode effect upon warming the sample from the remnant field state.
summary: Warming the sample to room temperature (300 K) results in the recovery of the magnetic diode behavior, as shown in this I-V plot. This observation confirms that the electrical memory effect is reversible and dependent on the thermal state of the permalloy honeycomb lattice following exposure to remnant magnetic fields.

caption: Distribution of total waste generation categorized by operative period, showing 19.8% during the pre-operative phase and 80.18% during the intra-operative phase.
summary: This pie chart illustrates the temporal distribution of waste generation across surgical phases. Data indicates that the pre-operative period accounts for 19.8% of total waste, while the intra-operative period contributes the majority at 80.18%, highlighting the significant waste production associated with the active surgical process.

caption: Mass-to-charge spectrum of the sample before irradiation, highlighting the 7 Da peak assigned to N2+ ions.
summary: The mass-to-charge spectrum obtained before irradiation shows the absence of Li+ ions, confirming that the peak observed at 7 Da is exclusively assigned to N2+ ions. This baseline measurement is essential for distinguishing between nitrogen and potential lithium signals in the irradiated samples during subsequent comparative analysis.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for the steel simulated at a peak temperature of 900 °C with a grain size of 500 μm.
summary: Simulated CCT diagram for steel at 900 °C peak temperature and 500 μm grain size. Using JMatPro, the diagram predicts microstructural changes during cooling. Reference cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s are indicated by red arrows, allowing for the evaluation of how larger grain sizes influence the transformation kinetics.

caption: Confocal profilometry map of the IJP 12L sample, displaying normalized, background-subtracted surface height with NaN values shown in white.
summary: This confocal profilometry map of the IJP 12L sample visualizes surface topography through normalized, background-subtracted height values. White regions in the image correspond to NaN values. This imaging technique is essential for quantifying surface features and preparing the data for subsequent binarization and crack fraction analysis.

caption: Time-dependent electrical signal responses recorded during cyclic stretching of hydrogels at strain levels of 100%, 200%, and 300%.
summary: Electrical signal stability is demonstrated through five cyclic stretching experiments performed at 100%, 200%, and 300% strain. The resulting charge-discharge curves indicate that the electrical signals remain stable across these varying deformation levels, confirming the reliability of the hydrogel's conductive response during repeated mechanical loading and unloading cycles.

caption: Convergence behavior of mean per atom energy for 15 at.% Al in a Ni matrix modeled with an HCP parent lattice structure.
summary: This plot illustrates the convergence behavior of the mean per atom energy for a 15 at.% Al in Ni alloy system. The simulation utilizes a Monte Carlo approach to evaluate energy stability within an HCP parent lattice, demonstrating how the energy values stabilize as the number of generated configurations increases.

caption: SHAP feature interaction plot for the setting radius, showing how its magnitude correlates with radius error contributions.
summary: This SHAP interaction plot displays the impact of the setting radius on radius error. The color-coded plot indicates that smaller setting radii provide a positive contribution to radius errors, a finding that aligns with experimental observations regarding the influence of setting parameters on the final printed geometry of CCFRP components.

caption: Load versus depth curves obtained from nanoindentation tests performed on the bimetallic interface.
summary: Load versus depth curves illustrate the mechanical response of the bimetallic interface during nanoindentation testing. These plots characterize the hardness behavior of the material at the interface, providing essential data on the resistance to deformation and the mechanical integrity of the transition layer between the two metallic components.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from nanoindentation testing for WAAM, LHAM, and LHAM-HT specimens.
summary: Nanoindentation load-depth curves are presented for WAAM, LHAM, and LHAM-HT specimens to assess nanoscale mechanical properties. The WAAM specimen exhibits the smallest indentation depth, indicating the highest hardness among the tested materials, while the LHAM specimen shows intermediate values for both indentation depth and hardness compared to the other samples.

caption: Schematic representation of the Fourier holography setup used to validate axicon-generated Bessel beams, featuring a fiber-coupled HeNe laser, collimating optics, a phase-only spatial light modulator (SLM), and a beam splitter for directing light to the camera.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Fourier holography experimental setup designed to validate axicon-generated Bessel beams. The configuration utilizes a fiber-coupled HeNe laser, collimation optics, and a phase-only SLM to modulate light. A beam splitter directs the reflected light toward the camera, enabling the capture of both lensed and lensless holographic reconstructions.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the AM-240 alloy, illustrating the distribution of intermetallic precipitates relative to the austenite phase using 5.5 at% Mo and 3.5 at% Ni iso-concentration surfaces.
summary: Captured intermetallic precipitates in the AM-240 alloy are shown in this cuboidal sub-volume extracted from an APT tip. The structural features are identified by 5.5 at% Mo and 3.5 at% Ni iso-concentration surfaces, which effectively map the spatial distribution of the intermetallic phases within the surrounding austenite matrix.

caption: Austenite transformation curves derived from dilatometry data, demonstrating the influence of heating rates on the transformation kinetics of 17-4 PH steel.
summary: Austenite transformation curves for 17-4 PH steel are shown across various heating rates. These curves characterize the austenitization behavior, though experimental noise introduces some error in the transformed fraction analysis. Furthermore, these sigmoid curves highlight limitations in the MKM model, which fails to accurately describe the initial transformation stage.

caption: Calculated band structure for the 3D PUC hexagonal lattice, highlighting the band gap (BG) within a shaded region and defining the frequency range via specific bounding values, with an inset showing the hexagonal Brillouin zone and its triangular prism irreducible Brillouin zone.
summary: This panel displays the band structure of a 3D PUC hexagonal lattice. The shaded region indicates the band gap, with specific frequency bounds defined. The inset provides a visualization of the hexagonal Brillouin zone and its corresponding irreducible Brillouin zone, illustrating the structural symmetry and electronic properties of the lattice.

caption: Pressure distribution curve along the extrusion direction, highlighting the pressure drop profile across the extrusion path.
summary: The pressure distribution curve along the extrusion direction provides a detailed view of the pressure profile. The data confirms that the melt extrusion pressure significantly decreases with higher extrusion temperatures, illustrating the relationship between thermal input and the mechanical pressure required for the extrusion of the composite melt.

caption: Volta potential map (CPD) of the 115 W laser-processed specimen, demonstrating a relatively uniform surface potential distribution resulting from rapid solidification.
summary: The Volta potential map, or Contact Potential Difference (CPD) map, illustrates the surface potential relative to the metal probe for the 115 W specimen. Observations indicate a relatively uniform potential distribution, which is attributed to the microstructural refinement achieved through the rapid solidification process inherent to the manufacturing technique.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph combined with EDX elemental mapping, highlighting the distribution of three distinct types of nanoscale precipitates within the cellular boundaries and interiors.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging paired with EDX mapping reveals the complex distribution of nanoscale precipitates in the TiB₂-reinforced MEA composite. Three distinct types of precipitates are identified, including TiB₂ and Cr₂B, which are primarily located near the cellular substructure boundaries, providing insight into the chemical heterogeneity of the as-built material.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar module measured under varying insolation levels.
summary: The I-V characteristics of the KC200GT module are presented for different irradiation levels. This plot illustrates the electrical response of the device, showing how current varies with voltage as insolation changes. These rescaled curves provide essential data for evaluating the performance and efficiency of the solar module under diverse environmental conditions.

caption: Thermal expansion coefficient data for a ceramic shell system utilizing silica sol, corundum powder, and corundum sand.
summary: Thermal expansion behavior of a ceramic shell made from silica sol, corundum powder, and corundum sand is presented. Analysis reveals that the Somos® Element resin exhibits a thermal expansion coefficient roughly 20 times greater than this specific ceramic shell composition between room temperature and 180 °C.

caption: Atomic model of a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell representing the primitive unit cell of the Cr10Fe20Ni alloy.
summary: This panel displays the DFT-predicted atomic configuration for a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell of the Cr10Fe20Ni alloy. The visualization serves as the structural basis for investigating how chromium content influences the lattice parameters and mechanical properties of the Cr-Fe-Ni alloy system through density functional theory calculations.

caption: Photograph of a rook tower prototype printed with D9G1M0.15 resin, showcasing complex architectural details.
summary: The printed rook tower prototype features a sophisticated architecture that was visually assessed to confirm high print quality. The photograph illustrates the clean surface finishing achieved with the D9G1M0.15 resin, demonstrating the effectiveness of the DLP 3D printing process for producing complex, high-resolution structural components.

caption: Calculated f versus h curves for NC Ni–Fe alloy in the CLR test, derived using Eq. (9) at four distinct indentation depths.
summary: This panel shows the calculated f versus h curves for the NC Ni–Fe alloy, determined via Eq. (9) at four different indentation depths. These results characterize the depth-dependent mechanical response of the alloy, providing insight into the material's behavior under the specific conditions of the CLR test.

caption: APT ion map of Alloy 625 Plus after aging at 650 °C for 300 h, marking the emergence of γ′ precipitates.
summary: Aging for 300 hours at 650 °C results in the appearance of Ti and Al-rich γ′ precipitates alongside the existing γ″ phase. These γ′ precipitates exhibit a significantly lower number density than the γ″ precipitates, representing a transition in the microstructural evolution of the Alloy 625 Plus material.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curves evaluating the predictive performance of the SPAT_SmSL model at 2- and 3-year intervals, with significance assessed via the DeLong test.
summary: The prognostic model achieves high AUC values of 0.824, 0.724, and 0.716 for 2- and 3-year overall survival in the training cohort. These results significantly outperform the stage model, confirming that the TIL-score stage serves as a robust and statistically significant prognostic factor for patient outcomes.

caption: Visualization of Ti–O and Ti-Cx-Oy chemical bonds formed during the reaction.
summary: Depicted here are the Ti–O and Ti-Cx-Oy chemical bonds formed during the reaction. These substances are key components of the reaction products observed on the Ti surface, alongside TiC and free C, confirming the chemical complexity of the layer formed during the CO2 exposure simulation.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of submicron particles, illustrating their morphology and composition in atomic percentage.
summary: This dark-field TEM image displays submicron particles, providing insights into their morphology and composition in atomic percentage. TEM observations suggest that a small fraction of these nanometric precipitates may form during processing, confirming the presence of spherical features that characterize the material structure at the submicron scale.

caption: Tabulated precision metrics evaluating classification performance across distinct categories during real-time testing procedures.
summary: This table presents the precision metrics calculated for each class during real-time testing. It provides a quantitative assessment of the model's classification accuracy, demonstrating the reliability of the system in identifying specific categories under operational conditions. These metrics serve as a key performance indicator for the real-time testing framework.

caption: Uniaxial compression engineering stress-strain curves for 8-mm cuboid specimens, showing the influence of build direction orientation on deformation behavior.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for 8-mm LPBF-manufactured cuboids are presented for compression axes parallel (black) and perpendicular (red) to the build direction. The data indicates that failure occurs at strains approximately equal to or smaller than 2%, consistent with the brittle failure characteristics observed across all tested specimen sizes.

caption: Diagram of the bidirectional scanning strategy featuring a 90° rotation between successive layers.
summary: The bidirectional scanning strategy employed during the LPBF process is depicted here. This method involves rotating the laser scan direction by 90° between adjacent layers to ensure uniform thermal distribution and microstructure development throughout the printed Haynes 188 bulk material.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for the as-built random scan condition, showing high anisotropy with a peak at {100} habit planes.
summary: The as-built random scan microstructure exhibits a highly anisotropic grain boundary plane distribution. Analysis reveals a distinct peak in the boundary plane population centered around the {100} habit planes, while minima are observed near the {111} planes, characterizing the initial state of the material before any heat treatment.

caption: Annular dark field scanning-transmission electron microscopy image of the sample aged at 650 °C for 192 h and deformed to fracture.
summary: This ADF-STEM image displays the microstructure of the sample aged at 650 °C for 192 hours after it has been deformed to fracture. The image provides a high-resolution view of the material's internal structure, serving as the primary context for the subsequent elemental and diffraction analyses presented in the figure.

caption: Crack propagation mechanism for a sinusoidal (W 1/2) interface DCB specimen, featuring adhesive ligaments L#1, L#2, and L#3 trailing the crack tip.
summary: This panel illustrates the crack propagation mechanism for a sinusoidal interface (A/λ = 1/2) DCB specimen. The diagram shows the crack tip progression and the associated adhesive ligaments, L#1, L#2, and L#3, which occur behind the main crack front, characterizing the failure mode for this specific sinusoidal interface geometry.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting the distribution of V8C7 nano-precipitations.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging is utilized to visualize the distribution of V8C7 nano-precipitations within the 40 mA specimen. This technique effectively highlights the presence and spatial arrangement of these fine-scale carbides, which are critical for understanding the strengthening mechanisms and microstructural features of the material under the investigated conditions.

caption: WLI profilometer topography map of the As-built specimen surface.
summary: This panel displays the areal surface roughness topographic map of the As-built specimen obtained via a 3D WLI profilometer. The image serves as the baseline reference for comparing the surface morphology and roughness characteristics of various post-processed specimens described in the study.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the ATZ641-350E32-HSR sample, providing high-contrast visualization of fine precipitates within the matrix.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image provides high-contrast imaging of the HSR-processed sample. This technique is utilized to visualize the fine-scale features within the magnesium matrix, specifically identifying the distribution of fine precipitates that contribute to the material's overall microstructural homogeneity and mechanical properties following the high-speed rolling process.

caption: Dark-field TEM image illustrating the interfacial region within the interlayer.
summary: This dark-field TEM image provides a visualization of the interfacial region located within the interlayer. It serves as the primary context for the subsequent high-resolution imaging and structural analysis of the interface between the matrix and the precipitates, establishing the spatial focus for the detailed characterization presented in the figure.

caption: EDS mapping of the weld seam containing 0.51 wt% Mg, showing a rough and continuous eutectic silicon network.
summary: This EDS map displays the weld seam microstructure at 0.51 wt% Mg concentration. The eutectic silicon network appears rough and continuous throughout the sample. Notably, no evident magnesium-enriched clusters are observed at this low concentration level, indicating a uniform distribution of alloying elements within the weld seam matrix.

caption: Rectangular unit cell geometry used for 2D lattice metamaterial construction.
summary: This panel illustrates the rectangular unit cell geometry, which serves as a fundamental building block for creating 2D lattice metamaterials. These unit cells are designed to be mirrored relative to the end rib in each direction and subsequently patterned in a 2x3 array to form the final lattice structure.

caption: Temperature programmed oxidation profiles of reacted catalysts showing weight loss as a function of temperature.
summary: Temperature programmed oxidation (TPO) was performed on reacted catalysts to investigate carbon deposition. The resulting TPO profiles illustrate the weight loss behavior of the catalysts across a temperature range, providing a basis for identifying the relative amounts and types of carbon species present on the catalyst surfaces.

caption: Tabular representation of the specific process parameters applied during the layering deposition procedure.
summary: This table outlines the specific process parameters employed during the layering deposition of the IN625 powder. By detailing the operational settings, the chart serves as a reference for the experimental conditions under which the deposition was performed, ensuring reproducibility and clarity regarding the manufacturing methodology used in the research.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph highlighting the precipitation of fine Cr-rich M23C6 carbides at the grain boundaries and the presence of additional MC carbides.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph focuses on the grain boundary regions within the stir zone of the AM-PWHT specimen. It clearly shows the precipitation of fine Cr-rich M23C6 carbides along these boundaries, alongside the presence of additional MC carbides, illustrating the complex carbide evolution occurring during the post-weld heat treatment.

caption: STEM micrograph of the AD specimen showing EDS point analysis locations within the dendrite core and interdendritic regions.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the AD specimen, highlighting specific EDS point analysis locations. Spots 1-6 and 7-12 are positioned within the γ matrix and γ′ precipitates of the dendrite core, while spots 13-18 and 19-24 are located in the interdendritic regions to reveal their respective chemical compositions.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology of the wear track for specimen III, detailing the scratch depth and pile-up profile along the measuring line.
summary: Specimen III presents a detailed three-dimensional morphology of its wear track. The scratch depth and pile-up height are evaluated along a measuring line perpendicular to the engraving direction. These features characterize the surface damage and material accumulation observed in the wear path, providing insight into the wear behavior of this specimen.

caption: Adjusted Bode phase angle plot for WAAM carbon steel, highlighting frequency-dependent phase shifts associated with surface degradation over time.
summary: This adjusted Bode phase plot for WAAM carbon steel demonstrates how phase angles shift toward lower degrees at frequencies between 10^3 and 10^2 Hz with prolonged exposure. These changes reflect the development of surface defects, providing insight into the corrosion evolution of the WAAM-fabricated material.

caption: Longitudinal section of the as-printed heat sink showing the morphology and orientation of internal voids.
summary: This longitudinal section provides insight into the morphology and size of internal voids within the as-printed heat sink. The image demonstrates that these voids often stretch along the filament winding direction, exhibiting various cross-sectional geometries that are difficult to fully characterize using only 2D cross-sectional pictures of the printed part.

caption: X-ray CT visualization of defect distributions within the LPBF-fabricated AZ91D magnesium alloy, highlighting the presence of large irregular pores on the X-Z plane.
summary: This X-ray CT analysis reveals the defect distribution in LPBF-fabricated AZ91D magnesium alloy. The visualization highlights the presence of large irregular pores on the X-Z plane. These defects are significant, as the alloy exhibits a relatively high porosity of approximately 0.47%, which is known to promote localized corrosion.

caption: Atomic model of the L12-ordered Ni3Al crystal structure featuring a Ru atom substituted at the beta site.
summary: This atomic model displays the L12-ordered Ni3Al crystal structure with a Ru modification at the beta site. The underlying lattice maintains the characteristic L12 arrangement where Ni atoms are surrounded by eight Ni and four Al atoms, and Al atoms are surrounded by twelve Ni atoms in the ordered matrix.

caption: Mean absolute SHAP value summary plot for the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model predicting build height.
summary: This summary plot displays the mean absolute SHAP values for the GPR model predicting height. The features are ranked by their influence on the predicted height, revealing that feeding rate has the highest importance, followed by laser power, and finally scan speed, which has the least impact on the model output.

caption: Material ratio height difference (Sdc) parameter values derived from the VIP plot.
summary: The Sdc parameter, representing the material ratio height difference, is displayed as a yellow bar chart, classifying it as a stratified surface functional parameter. Averaged from 12 specimens, this metric provides insight into the surface structure of the peg samples, contributing to the comprehensive evaluation of their dale region roughness.

caption: Macroscopic image of the melt pool observed during the experimental weave bead deposition.
summary: Panel d shows a macroscopic photograph of the melt pool during experimental weave bead deposition. The weaving process requires a significantly longer path than the stringer process. The multi-heat source model, calibrated with experimental data, was utilized to simulate this process efficiently while maintaining accuracy in predicting the resulting melt pool morphology.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectra of P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene (CB) solution, highlighting the n→π∗ transition of the azomethine group at 413 nm and the π→π∗ transition of the benzene ring at 328 nm for PPI-SL.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectra of P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene are presented. PPI-SL displays two distinct absorption bands at 413 nm and 328 nm, which are attributed to the n→π∗ transition of the azomethine group and the π→π∗ transition of the benzene ring, respectively, characterizing the electronic transitions of the material.

caption: Yield strength contribution (ΔYS Fe) as a function of the inverse square root of the average grain size (d−1/2) showing the impact of Fe content.
summary: Panel b displays the yield strength contribution of Fe relative to the inverse square root of the average grain size. The data demonstrates the mechanical response to grain refinement, mirroring the trends observed in region #1 where Fe addition significantly alters the grain structure and subsequent mechanical performance of the alloy.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the NC Ni(Fe) alloy annealed at 576 °C.
summary: Quantitative grain size distribution for the NC Ni(Fe) alloy annealed at 576 °C is provided in this histogram. The plot serves as a key data point in the series, illustrating the shift in grain size populations as the material undergoes significant thermal processing and grain growth.

caption: Bode-modulus plots displaying the impedance magnitude (|Z|) as a function of frequency for SLM-manufactured alloys in 0.3, 1.5, and 3.5 wt% NaCl solutions.
summary: Bode-modulus plots quantify the impedance magnitude of the SLM-manufactured alloys across varying chloride concentrations. The data shows a clear trend where the |Z| value decreases as the NaCl concentration increases, indicating reduced corrosion resistance and higher susceptibility to ion-induced degradation in more concentrated saline environments.

caption: Simulated Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram for 24CrNiMo low alloy steel generated via JMatPro software.
summary: This simulated TTT diagram for 24CrNiMo low alloy steel illustrates the kinetics of phase transformation. Analysis indicates that the transformation temperature remains below the bainite start temperature of 539.9 °C, suggesting that the phase transformation primarily occurs within the bainite region during the cooling process.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation density distribution map accompanied by a corresponding statistical histogram of the crack region.
summary: This map and histogram quantify the geometrically necessary dislocation density near the crack. Results reveal a substantial increase in dislocation density near the crack region, particularly at the crack tip. This distribution indicates severe localized plastic deformation and significant strain concentration occurring during the solidification crack development process.

caption: Pseudo-ternary diagram mapping feed ratios against phase information, with an overlaid micro-Vickers hardness plot to correlate composition, phase presence, and mechanical properties.
summary: The pseudo-ternary diagram displays the relationship between feed ratios and the resulting phase information for each sample. By overlaying a micro-Vickers hardness plot, the figure facilitates a direct investigation into the correlation between chemical composition, the presence of specific phases, and the resulting mechanical hardness of the alloyed samples.

caption: Average confusion matrix for Model III, illustrating the classification performance for deposit types associated with S-type magma.
summary: Model III identifies deposit types derived from S-type magma, including epithermal, granite-related U, and skarn deposits with 100% accuracy. However, identification of Sn–W-rare metal deposits and greisen is relatively lower, with accuracies of 0.872 and 0.846, respectively. Despite these variations, the model maintains generally robust performance across the testing datasets.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms for 2HEA alloy rods with diameters of 2 mm and 4 mm, recorded at a heating rate of 20 °C/min up to 650 °C.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry thermograms compare the thermal behavior of 2HEA alloy rods with 2 mm and 4 mm diameters. Scanned from 100 to 650 °C at a rate of 20 °C/min, these curves are utilized to investigate differences in crystallinity and glass formation characteristics between the two distinct rod sizes.

caption: Pareto plot demonstrating the relative importance of processing parameters on toughness.
summary: Toughness is evaluated using this Pareto plot, which emphasizes the significant influence of coolant, strain path, and temperature. These factors are identified as statistically meaningful, indicating that precise control over these specific processing parameters is essential for achieving desired toughness levels in the final material structure.

caption: Isothermal TTT diagram of X37CrMoV5-1 tool steel representing the conventional processing route, including casting and hot rolling, as sourced from literature.
summary: This panel displays an isothermal TTT diagram for X37CrMoV5-1 tool steel processed via conventional methods, specifically casting and hot rolling. The diagram serves as a baseline for comparison, illustrating the transformation behavior and phase evolution characteristic of traditional metallurgical manufacturing routes as documented in existing scientific literature.

caption: Optical image and surface roughness measurement of the AP-modified copper (Cu-AP) substrate, exhibiting a surface roughness value of Sa = 14 μm.
summary: Optical imaging and surface roughness analysis of the Cu-AP substrate are presented. The surface characterization reveals a roughness value of Sa = 14 μm. This measurement provides essential data regarding the surface topography of the modified copper, which is critical for understanding the subsequent adhesion properties of the applied slurries.

caption: Cartoon representation of the Tcu3516 active cavity with non-regular structures highlighted.
summary: The cartoon model illustrates the active cavity of Tcu3516, emphasizing the structural arrangement of the non-regular regions. Observations confirm that Loop2 and the C-tail are pressed closely to the entrance of the cavity. This configuration suggests that modifications to these regions may not adversely affect the active site conformation.

caption: Normalized transmission intensity measurements for four chip designs with varied spacing, normalized relative to the T-8 design.
summary: Transmission measurements for four designs with varied spacing are shown, normalized by the T-8 design. These designs, including T-8, T-9, and T-10, were developed based on the T-7 architecture with specific modifications to spacing and T-shape head thickness to optimize the optical transmission characteristics for the probing system.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the electrochemical impedance behavior of HEA and LA-HEA coatings following 3 hours of immersion.
summary: This Nyquist plot shows the electrochemical impedance behavior of HEA and LA-HEA coatings following 3 hours of immersion. Consistent with other time points, the samples exhibited Nyquist curves with similar shapes, which were used to evaluate the corrosion resistance of the coatings as they were exposed to the electrolyte over time.

caption: Schematic representation of the initial stage of hot corrosion in a NiCr porous alloy exposed to NaCl.
summary: This schematic illustrates the first stage of hot corrosion occurring in a NiCr porous alloy when subjected to NaCl exposure. The diagram serves as a foundational model for understanding the early degradation mechanisms and surface interactions that initiate the corrosion process within the porous structure of the NiCr alloy.

caption: Quantitative EDS analysis results detailing the elemental composition within the inter-dendritic regions of alloy-1.
summary: Quantitative EDS analysis results for the inter-dendritic area of alloy-1 are shown here. These data provide specific elemental composition measurements, which are essential for evaluating the distribution and concentration differences of elements within the inter-dendritic regions of the alloy samples.

caption: 3D surface texture of the turned surface, revealing regular grooves and periodic peaks and valleys parallel to the turning direction X.
summary: Captured via 3D optical interferometry, this panel shows the turned surface texture. It features obvious lays and regular grooves parallel to the turning direction X, creating a periodic arrangement of peaks and valleys along the Y axis. This structural regularity contrasts significantly with the random scratch pattern of the ground surface.

caption: Enlarged view comparing the experimental crack and phase field contour at a displacement of 30 mm, validating the model's predictive capability.
summary: This enlarged comparison between the experimental crack and the phase field contour at a displacement of 30 mm validates the explicit phase field model. The model accurately predicts the two localized bands of deformation. This panel confirms the high fidelity of the numerical simulation in capturing complex structural damage evolution.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph and elemental mapping of as-deposited Ni–Co–23Al alloy, revealing the coexistence of Al-rich β phase, (Ni, Al)-rich γ′ phases, and Co-rich γ/γ′ regions.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph of as-deposited Ni–Co–23Al alloy displays the microstructural distribution of three distinct regions. Elemental mapping identifies an Al-rich β phase, (Ni, Al)-rich γ′ phases, and Co-rich γ/γ′ regions. The image highlights the morphological complexity of the alloy, specifically showing elongated γ′ phases at the β and γ phase interfaces.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module, illustrating performance variations across different environmental insolation and temperature settings.
summary: Representing the P-V characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module, this panel illustrates the power output behavior under diverse temperature and irradiance levels. The data, derived from the PEC1 model, is compared against experimental measurements to validate the accuracy of the model in predicting power performance in actual solar environments.

caption: Scanning probe microscopy (SPM) force map of vertical (X–Z) LPBF IN718 highlighting indentation sites.
summary: This SPM force map provides a detailed view of indentation sites on the vertical (X–Z) plane of LPBF IN718. It complements the XPM hardness map by showing how secondary phases near the indentations influence the local mechanical response, confirming the structural influence of the elongated microstructure on the measured hardness values.

caption: Absorption spectrum of HEMA:PEGDA resin with Atto dyes, highlighting the specific absorption bands corresponding to the dye-resin mixture.
summary: The absorption spectrum of the HEMA:PEGDA resin containing Atto dyes is presented here. This plot characterizes the light-absorbing behavior of the dye-resin mixture, confirming the selective wavelength filtering properties of the fluorescent dyes as they are dissolved within the liquid polymer matrix.

caption: Laser power-dependent SERS spectra of patient subject samples measured using the 3D superstructure platform.
summary: Representative laser power-dependent SERS spectra were acquired for the patient group by placing actual AH samples within the 3D superstructure. These spectra illustrate the spectroscopic response of the patient samples under varying laser power conditions, enabling a comparative analysis of metabolite signatures between control and patient subjects.

caption: Microscopic observation of the neurovascular unit 72 h after cell seeding, demonstrating dispersed cell growth across the vascular structure.
summary: After 72 h of cultivation, the cells are observed to have grown in a dispersed manner across the 3D printed hydrogel vascular structure. This panel highlights the successful integration and proliferation of cells within the scaffold, confirming the suitability of the printed environment for supporting neural cell growth over three days.

caption: STEM/EDS image of the OPM sample illustrating its distinct microstructural arrangement.
summary: A STEM/EDS image of the OPM sample is shown, capturing the characteristic microstructural features of this material. This visualization provides the necessary context for understanding the spatial distribution of phases, which is essential for interpreting the subsequent compositional data obtained from the austenite and martensite regions.

caption: Al-Al partial radial distribution functions for Al-Cu-Ni melts, highlighting composition-dependent chemical interactions as modeled by AIMD and DNNP simulations.
summary: Panel e presents Al-Al partial radial distribution functions, which serve to demonstrate how chemical interactions between species vary with composition. By comparing these results with other panels, the analysis confirms that the character of atomic interactions is sensitive to the specific alloy composition within the Al-Cu-Ni melt system.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric analysis (DTGA) profiles showing the rate of weight loss for control and e-beam exposed commercial ABS samples, highlighting thermal decomposition characteristics for front and back surface exposures.
summary: Derivative thermogravimetric analysis profiles quantify the rate of weight loss for 3D-printed commercial ABS samples as temperatures reach 800 °C. By comparing control samples with those exposed to e-beam radiation on front and back surfaces, the data reveals specific thermal decomposition characteristics resulting from the applied surface treatment processes.

caption: Conceptual framework of the Digital Twin architecture for large-scale 3D printing, highlighting the integration of virtual-physical pairs and associated service modules.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Digital Twin architecture designed for large-scale 3D printing applications. It delineates the essential virtual-physical pairs and the interconnected service layers required for system operation.
