The architecture provides a comprehensive mapping from the general conceptual model to the specific implementation framework and data flow pathways.

caption: SAED pattern corresponding to the chromium carbide (Cr23C6) precipitates found in area 3.
summary: The SAED pattern from area 3 provides crystallographic confirmation of the chromium carbide (Cr23C6) precipitates. These carbides, which form during aging, are part of the complex inter- and intragranular phase distribution observed in the TEM micrographs, contributing to the material's structural properties after the 60-hour aging duration.

caption: Feature importance analysis of individual wall contributions to specific compressive load tolerance, derived from a Decision Tree Regressor model.
summary: This feature importance plot illustrates the relative contribution of each wall to the overall structural performance of the material. By utilizing a Decision Tree Regressor model, the analysis quantifies how specific wall characteristics influence the specific compressive load tolerance, providing insights into the structural design and mechanical behavior of the system.

caption: Depth distribution of atomic displacement damage (dpa) in 4Al10V alloy irradiated with 4 MeV Au ions, calculated using the SRIM software based on the Kinchin-Pease model.
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated depth distribution of atomic displacement damage in 4Al10V alloy following 4 MeV Au-ion irradiation. Derived from SRIM software using the Kinchin-Pease model, the profile quantifies dpa as a function of depth, though experimental observations indicate that actual damage extends deeper than the 600 nm predicted by this simulation.

caption: Top-view schematic illustrating the migration of the melt pool during the second laser pass, highlighting the hatch spacing (h = 120 μm) relative to the moving laser beam.
summary: This schematic depicts the top-view geometry of a migrating melt pool during the second laser pass of the LPBF process. It specifically highlights the hatch spacing of 120 μm, providing a clear visualization of the laser beam's movement and the spatial arrangement of the melt pool during the scanning phase.

caption: True stress-strain compression curves obtained at room temperature, 400 °C, and 800 °C, with an inset highlighting serrated flow behavior at 400 °C.
summary: True stress-strain compression curves are plotted for room temperature and elevated temperatures of 400 °C and 800 °C. The inset in the upper right corner provides a magnified view of the serrated flow observed at 400 °C, which is attributed to the Portevin–Le Chatelier (PLC) effect during deformation.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the Ni40Fe40Cr20 alloy using Thermo-Calc software and the TCHEA6 database.
summary: This panel displays the calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the Ni40Fe40Cr20 alloy. Derived using the Thermo-Calc software and TCHEA6 database, it serves as the baseline for comparing phase stability as aluminum content increases across the AlxNi(40-x)Fe40Cr20 alloy series, illustrating the fundamental phase evolution in this specific composition.

caption: HAADF-STEM imaging and corresponding EDXS elemental mapping of Cu-10Sn powder particles, highlighting the internal microstructure and the distribution of Cu, Sn, and P.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image reveals the internal microstructure of Cu-10Sn powder particles. Corresponding EDXS elemental maps for Cu, Sn, and P demonstrate the presence of large, irregularly shaped Sn-rich phases within the powder, confirming that P is also localized within these specific Sn-rich regions of the metal powder particles.

caption: Predicted bonding time curve for AA7075-T6 at 500 °C, illustrating the model-derived relationship between bonding pressure and time.
summary: This panel presents the machine learning-derived bonding time curve for AA7075-T6 at 500 °C. By plotting predicted bonding time against bonding pressure, the graph clarifies the influence of temperature on bonding behavior and demonstrates how the model follows experimental trends for this specific high-temperature condition.

caption: Correlation heatmap visualizing the input-output feature dependencies as determined by the Nonlinear Regression model.
summary: This heatmap depicts the correlation structure for the Nonlinear Regression model, which, similar to the linear version, exhibits a relatively simplistic pattern. It provides a visual representation of how nonlinear regression interprets the influence of mineralogical features on the target properties within the studied dataset.

caption: Principal component analysis scatter plot representing the compositional distribution of the alloy dataset in the PC2 and PC3 plane.
summary: This plot displays the compositional correlation between designed KG-SFA alloys and reference Ni-based self-fluxing alloys using PC2 and PC3. These components represent 19.7% and 11.6% of the total variance, respectively, contributing to the overall 84.5% variance coverage that enables effective visualization of multi-dimensional compositional relationships in 2D space.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan across the bonding gap of the 5 min brazed specimen, showing the distribution of Ni, Cr, Co, Mo, and B elements.
summary: The EDS line scan across the bonding gap for the 5 min specimen reveals a high nickel concentration within the interlayer. The analysis demonstrates sharp non-uniformity in element distribution, confirming that inadequate diffusion time prevents complete isothermal solidification and results in the formation of precipitated ASZ phases.

caption: Final numerical results of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) obtained after the iterative process for different constituent material combinations.
summary: Numerical results presented in this panel represent the final converged CTE values for the analyzed material combinations. These values demonstrate the impact of different thermal expansion ratios on the effective properties of the constituent materials, providing a quantitative summary of the final outcomes derived from the iterative calculation process.

caption: Schwarz Primitive (P) unit cell geometry.
summary: The Schwarz Primitive (P) unit cell is presented as a fundamental triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structure. This geometric representation illustrates the periodic arrangement and topological characteristics of the P-type unit cell, which serves as a primary subject of investigation in the study of periodic minimal surface architectures.

caption: Elemental EDS map of the transgranular failure region in the ME3 specimen, highlighting the distribution of titanium.
summary: Titanium distribution in the transgranular failure region of the ME3 specimen is shown through EDS mapping. The results indicate that the oxides in this region are leaner in Ti compared to the intergranular crack tip, reflecting the different oxidation behavior associated with the transgranular failure mode.

caption: UV-Vis transmittance curves for the resin samples across the 200–800 nm wavelength range, illustrating the relationship between light transmission and curing depth.
summary: The UV-Vis spectra for the resin samples, measured between 200 and 800 nm, reveal how light transmittance influences the degree of curing. The diminished curing observed in deeper resin layers is directly correlated with the UV transmittance characteristics of the material, as shown by these spectral curves.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image showing intracellular Col I expression in undifferentiated hASCs cultured in 2D.
summary: This panel displays the intracellular localization of Col I within undifferentiated hASCs cultured in a 2D environment. The fluorescence microscopy imaging confirms that Col I expression remains confined within the cells, contrasting with the extracellular fiber-like structures observed during the differentiation process of hASC-CSKs in subsequent experimental conditions.

caption: High-magnification TEM observation of the EA1 specimen, emphasizing the chaotic and jagged nature of the dislocation debris formed during deformation.
summary: This TEM panel provides a closer look at the EA1 specimen's microstructure. The dislocation pattern is characterized as chaotic and jagged, reminiscent of dislocation debris. This morphology contrasts sharply with the more organized, net-like or parallel dislocation structures observed in standard tensile specimens tested at room temperature or 250 °C.

caption: Phase formation pathways for the first and second layers, illustrating solidification lines for β-Ti formation and the precipitation of (M1-x Fex)Ti phases.
summary: The phase formation pathways for the first and second layers are represented here. Line I describes the solidification of β-Ti (L→ L1 +β-Ti), while line II details the subsequent precipitation of (M1-x Fex)Ti phases at the β-Ti boundary, providing a thermodynamic explanation for the observed microstructural evolution.

caption: Evolution of infrared absorption spectra for the resin as a function of exposure time.
summary: The evolution of infrared absorption spectra for the photosensitive resin is shown as a function of exposure time. These spectral changes provide direct evidence of the chemical transformation occurring within the material, illustrating the curing performance and the progression of the polymerization reaction over the specified exposure duration.

caption: Morphological analysis of voids in test sample 20, highlighting the 15 largest pores that meet the minimum detection criteria of volume (V ≥ 27 voxels) and sphericity (φ ≥ 0.7).
summary: This micro-CT analysis of test sample 20 identifies specific voids suitable for detection by applying thresholds of volume and sphericity. The 15 largest pores meeting these criteria are encircled, demonstrating that spherical voids with high sphericity are prioritized for identification, while flat voids are excluded based on the defined φ ≥ 0.7 threshold.

caption: Calculated Fermi level energy values for Co80B20 and the six transition metal-doped amorphous alloys, demonstrating that V, Cr, Mn, and Fe doping increases the Fermi level, while Ni doping decreases it.
summary: Fermi level energy values are compared across the six amorphous alloys. The data indicates that doping with V, Cr, Mn, or Fe shifts the Fermi level of the base Co80B20 alloy to higher energies, whereas Ni doping results in a reduction of the Fermi level energy.

caption: FTIR spectroscopic analysis of BHP/G and BHP/G@Met scaffolds, evaluating chemical bonding changes before and after printing.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy is employed to analyze the chemical composition of BHP/G and BHP/G@Met scaffolds. By comparing spectra before and after the printing process, the analysis confirms the stability of the chemical bonds and the successful incorporation of the drug-loaded hydrogel within the scaffold architecture.

caption: Four-wavelength composite image captured by a multi-sensor camera during the laser-leading molding process.
summary: This four-wavelength composite image provides a visual representation of the material surface during the laser-leading molding process. Captured via a multi-sensor camera, the image serves as a diagnostic tool to observe the molding dynamics, which are influenced by variations in liquid phase ratio and surface tension of the cobalt binder.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy images revealing the porous architecture of the titanium alloy and AMCI/PTi scaffold.
summary: Scanning electron microscopy images illustrate the porous structure of the scaffolds. The analysis confirms that the pores within the titanium alloy and AMCI/PTi scaffolds are uniform in distribution, with an average pore size measured at 600 μm, highlighting the structural consistency achieved through the 3D printing process.

caption: Transverse σ 33 residual stress component determined via ICHD, illustrating the shift in stress levels following thermal shock treatment.
summary: The σ 33 component of the near-surface residual stress is displayed for post-weld heat-treated plates. Data obtained through ICHD measurements compare the stress state before and after thermal shock. Error bars indicate the range of values from different measurements, highlighting the changes in transverse stress induced by the thermal shock process.

caption: Comparison of tensile strength and ductility for as-printed Alloy B against various recently developed L-PBFAM processed aluminum alloys and composites, with Alloy A included as a reference point.
summary: This panel compares the tensile strength and ductility of the as-printed Alloy B against several recently developed L-PBFAM high-strength aluminum alloys and aluminum-based composites. The plot demonstrates that Alloy B possesses superior strength compared to both Alloy A and the other referenced materials in the as-printed condition.

caption: Ordered L0 structure representing a perfectly periodic arrangement of TRD units without disordered layers.
summary: The L0 structure represents an ordered system generated using 3D Voronoi tessellation with strategic control of seed point distributions. This configuration serves as the baseline model, characterized by a perfectly periodic arrangement of trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron units that contains no disordered cell layers within the hierarchical system.

caption: Fluigent OxyGEN system configured for colorimetric mixing experiments.
summary: The OxyGEN system, purchased from Fluigent Company, is presented as the primary equipment for colorimetric mixing experiments. This sophisticated fluidic control system is utilized to manage the experimental reagents, ensuring accurate and controlled mixing processes necessary for the successful execution of the colorimetric analysis described in the research.

caption: Comparison of predicted and actual sequence features for the 17 to 18 mm height interval, showing improved accuracy under stable laser parameters.
summary: The plot displays the comparison between predicted and actual sequence features for the 17 to 18 mm height range. Prediction accuracy is shown to improve significantly once the laser parameters stabilize, confirming that the model performs more reliably when the manufacturing process conditions remain consistent.

caption: Statistical distribution of porosity in SiC/Ti6Al4V composites across seven distinct manufacturing processes, highlighting the influence of varying energy densities on material density.
summary: This plot illustrates the statistical distribution of porosity for seven different manufacturing processes used to create SiC/Ti6Al4V composites. By analyzing these variations, the figure demonstrates how specific energy densities influence spattering and porosity levels, ultimately identifying the processing conditions that achieve the highest density in the printed parts.

caption: Inhomogeneous γ/γ lamellar structure observed within a γ grain via transmission electron microscopy.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy reveals an inhomogeneous γ/γ lamellar structure within a γ grain. This layered morphology is characterized by lamellae separated by low-angle grain boundaries, which are distinct from the high-angle grain boundaries observed in other regions of the specimen, further supporting the massive transformation mechanism.

caption: Nyquist plots derived from Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) measurements on the BD plane of MEX 17-4 PH specimens, comparing raw experimental data with fitted model results.
summary: Nyquist plots were generated from EIS measurements performed on the BD plane of MEX 17-4 PH specimens to characterize their corrosion resistance. The plot displays the relationship between real and imaginary impedance components, with the fitted data demonstrating the accuracy of the equivalent circuit model in interpreting electrochemical behavior.

caption: HAADF-STEM images of Scalmalloy® samples in the FGZ zone, comparing the HT (325 °C/4h), HT1W (325 °C/4h + 150 °C/1 week), and HT3W (325 °C/4h + 150 °C/3 weeks) conditions.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging reveals the microstructural evolution of Scalmalloy® samples within the FGZ zone across three distinct heat treatment conditions. These images facilitate a direct comparison between the baseline HT sample and the aged HT1W and HT3W samples, highlighting the stability of various precipitates despite the extended thermal exposure.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum (600 MHz, CDCl3) of the isolated My-DMI Diels-Alder cycloadducts, featuring an inset that expands the cyclohexenic proton signal region to demonstrate a 90:10 regioisomeric ratio.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum (600 MHz, CDCl3) characterizes the isolated My-DMI Diels-Alder cycloadducts, which were obtained as a clear yellowish liquid. An expanded inset of the cyclohexenic proton region confirms the presence of two distinct regioisomers, quantified by their relative peak intensities to be in a 90:10 ratio.

caption: Shear stress-strain response for open-cell IN718 lattices fabricated using a 200 W laser power input.
summary: At a 200 W fabrication power, the lattices display clear peak shear stress values and rapid post-failure stress reduction. The observed mechanical behavior indicates a reduction in ductility, highlighting the complex interplay between energy input, resulting open-cell porosity, and the associated failure modes under shear loading conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves for HC modified separator cells recorded at scanning rates ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 mV s-1.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for the HC modified separator cell are displayed across scanning rates of 0.1 to 0.4 mV s-1. These measurements illustrate the electrochemical response of the HC material, serving as a baseline for comparison with the other modified separator configurations tested under identical experimental conditions.

caption: Accumulated open-circuit voltage (VOC,accum) versus time curves measured under varying extending displacement conditions.
summary: This panel shows the accumulated open-circuit voltage over time for the HETENG under different extending displacement magnitudes. The data demonstrates how varying the mechanical input displacement influences the total voltage accumulation, serving as a key metric for assessing the device's capacity to store or output electrical energy effectively.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of tenocytes on MEW wavy scaffolds during phase I culture, where green indicates live cells and red indicates dead cells.
summary: This fluorescence microscopy image displays tenocytes cultured on MEW wavy scaffolds during phase I. Live cells are visualized in green, while dead cells appear in red. Cell viability was well maintained throughout this phase, consistently exceeding the 93% threshold at all measured time points, demonstrating high biocompatibility of the scaffold.

caption: WDS-derived elemental concentration profiles for the initial Pt-aluminide coating microstructure.
summary: Initial WDS concentration profiles for the Pt-aluminide coating are shown. These profiles characterize the elemental distribution prior to oxidation, serving as a reference for assessing the stability of the PtAl2 phase and the subsequent diffusion of Pt, Al, and Ni during the high-temperature oxidation process.

caption: Visible camera image of a tungsten target and its holder assembly, including an incandescent hex nut, during exposure to deuterium plasma at 1000 K within the Pisces-RF linear plasma device.
summary: This visible camera image captures a tungsten target undergoing deuterium plasma exposure at 1000 K in the Pisces-RF device. The target and its holder assembly, notably an incandescent hex nut, are actively heated and terminated by the axial plasma flow, demonstrating the high-temperature conditions maintained during the experimental plasma interaction.

caption: STEM bright-field micrograph of the Mn20 CoCrFeNiMnX high entropy alloy, highlighting the morphology of secondary phases.
summary: The STEM bright-field micrograph of the Mn20 CoCrFeNiMnX alloy illustrates the distribution of secondary phases. These carbides are coarser than the oxidic particles present in the alloy, typically ranging from 100 to 600 nm. Their presence is critical as they contribute to the overall microstructural characteristics of the material.

caption: Magnetic free energy F mag of hcp Co obtained from Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: Represented here is the magnetic free energy F mag for hcp cobalt, derived from Monte Carlo simulation. The data illustrates the magnetic energy profile of the hcp lattice, offering a detailed look at the thermodynamic state of the material as simulated within the research framework.

caption: Early-stage velocity distribution on the transverse cross-section, illustrating the influence of surface tension and recoil pressure on the molten pool.
summary: Panel (b) illustrates the early-stage velocity distribution on the transverse cross-section. Similar to panel (a), the flow inside the molten pool is primarily governed by surface tension and recoil pressure before the molten droplet enters, providing insight into the pre-droplet entry flow equilibrium within the molten metal.

caption: Surface texture profile of the upskin region on a horizontal thin wall specimen.
summary: This panel illustrates the upskin surface topography of a horizontal thin wall. Similar to the downskin surface, this region exhibits process-related defects including spatter and partially melted powder particles. These features are indicative of the surface quality resulting from the specific manufacturing process and building orientation employed.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram for AA2017 alloy, depicting isothermal phase transformation boundaries as calculated by JMatPro software.
summary: This TTT diagram illustrates the isothermal transformation behavior of the AA2017 alloy. Derived from JMatPro simulations based on the alloy's specific chemical composition, the plot delineates the time-dependent phase stability regions, serving as a critical reference for understanding precipitate formation kinetics during isothermal heat treatment processes.

caption: Overview of the experimental systems categorized by processing method and condition, including L-PBF standard, L-PBF with hot isostatic pressing (HIP) standard, L-PBF degraded, and L-PBF with HIP degraded.
summary: This schematic provides a comprehensive overview of the four distinct material systems investigated in the study. The systems are classified based on their manufacturing process, specifically laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) with or without subsequent hot isostatic pressing (HIP), and their environmental condition, categorized as either standard or degraded.

caption: Calculated magnetic pair exchange interactions for Fe–Ni, Co–Ni, Fe–V, and Co–V atomic pairs within the FeCoNi base alloy and various V- and Cu-doped solid solutions.
summary: This plot displays calculated magnetic pair exchange interactions for specific atomic pairs in FeCoNi-based alloys. The data highlights that interactions involving V are relatively low at 0.25 mRy, contrasting with the significantly higher J Fe-Ni and J Co-Ni values observed in the FeCoNi and FeCoNiCu 1.15 alloy systems.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the classification performance of the supervised learning model on the training dataset.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the classification accuracy of the supervised learning model during the training phase. The results demonstrate strong performance, indicating that the model effectively learned the underlying patterns required to categorize the structural conditions of the specimens during the training process.

caption: Stress–temperature plane comparison of 20 MnMoNi 5 5 steel, showing curves of equal secondary creep strain rates alongside the ultimate tensile strength.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between short-term creep tests and hot tensile tests for 20 MnMoNi 5 5 steel. By mapping curves of equal secondary creep strain rates against ultimate tensile strength in the stress–temperature plane, the figure demonstrates a strong correlation between these mechanical properties under the specified loading conditions.

caption: Electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption performance plotted across the 12–18 GHz Ku-band frequency range for the Optimal structure compared against Cases 1–4.
summary: The absorption performance of the optimal structure and Cases 1–4 is illustrated across the 12–18 GHz frequency range. This plot demonstrates how the variations in design variables affect the EMW absorption capabilities of the 3D-printed BMMA structures, providing a comparative view of their performance within the Ku-band.

caption: Correlation between initial residual stress and lattice rotation at 4.26% global strain, showing that significant lattice rotations are concentrated in regions where initial residual stresses are near zero.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between initial residual stress and crystallographic lattice rotation at 4.26% global strain. The data reveals that substantial lattice rotations are primarily concentrated in zones where initial residual stresses are near zero, rather than in regions characterized by residual tensile stresses.

caption: Load-displacement data for a fibre pull-out test at an inclination angle of 20°, with grey curves representing complete pull-out and red curves indicating slipping rupture.
summary: The load-displacement plot for a 20° inclination angle distinguishes between failure modes. Grey curves represent specimens undergoing complete pull-out, characterized by a slip hardening factor of 0.00, while red curves denote specimens experiencing slipping rupture, which are associated with a slip-hardening factor of 0.20.

caption: Representation of the left-right (LR) structure, showing the allocation of different building block types to the left and right regions, with interfaces marked by yellow lines.
summary: The LR structure is designed by allocating different types of building blocks to the left and right regions of the 2x2x2 assembly. The interfaces between these blocks are highlighted by yellow lines, illustrating the lateral hierarchical arrangement of the components within the overall structure of the material.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from mode-I fracture testing of NER specimens, illustrating the mechanical response under tensile loading.
summary: The load-displacement curves for mode-I fracture specimens demonstrate the mechanical behavior of the NER material. The data reveals that the epoxy resin exhibits brittle characteristics, maintaining elastic behavior as the load increases until reaching a point of sudden fracture, confirming the material's failure mode under the applied test conditions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images showing live/dead staining of C2C12 cells cultured on rod- and spherical-shaped microgels after seven days, with live cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Live/dead staining images demonstrate high cell viability on both rod and spherical microgels after seven days of culture. The green fluorescence indicates live cells, while the absence of significant red staining confirms that the microgel materials are non-cytotoxic, supporting the conclusion that both geometries maintain high cell viability.

caption: Normalised change in 340 nm light absorbance over 4.5 minutes for EBM hydrogels prepared with varying human fibrinogen concentrations, reflecting the polymerization progress.
summary: This plot displays the normalized change in 340 nm light absorbance over a 4.5-minute interval for EBM hydrogels with varying human fibrinogen concentrations. The spectrophotometric data serves as a proxy for monitoring the polymerization process, providing insights into how fibrinogen concentration influences the rate of hydrogel network formation over time.

caption: SAED pattern corresponding to the θ′ phase precipitate shown in panel (e).
summary: The SAED pattern provides crystallographic confirmation of the θ′ phase precipitate identified in the HRTEM image. This diffraction data is essential for indexing the specific precipitate phases that form in the Al-Si-Mg-Cu-Zn alloy matrix during compression at 300 °C, ensuring accurate microstructural identification.

caption: Failure Assessment Diagram (FAD) for S275JR steel specimens tested across a temperature range from −120 °C to +70 °C.
summary: This FAD plot illustrates the fracture assessment results for 176 S275JR steel specimens evaluated across a broad temperature range from −120 °C to +70 °C. The data encompasses the lower shelf, ductile-to-brittle transition region (DBTR), and upper shelf regimes, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's fracture behavior under varying thermal conditions.

caption: Algorithmic evaluation workflow for characterizing defects within internal channels, structured into three sequential processing blocks.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the three-block evaluation algorithm designed to extract meaningful information from defects located inside internal channels. The final block, labeled Data analysis, focuses on evaluating the obtained profiles by assessing characteristic peaks and overall form deviations to ensure accurate defect characterization within the internal channel structures.

caption: Schematic representation of the seven observation points selected for Digital Image Correlation (DIC) analysis across the interface and two distinct zones of the tensile specimen.
summary: This diagram illustrates the experimental setup for DIC analysis, featuring seven evenly spaced observation points positioned across the interface and two zones of the tensile sample. These points are strategically selected to monitor local plastic deformation and strain distribution under room temperature tensile conditions for the forged and D+F samples.

caption: Fugitive grid representation highlighting particle escape pathways on the simulated surface.
summary: Fugitive grid panel represents the escape grid within the simulated material surface. By using different colors or symbols for various particles, the simulation achieves a high level of realistic complexity. This ensures that the resulting data is representative of actual conditions, providing a reliable model for the material surface.

caption: Variant map of deformation-induced martensite illustrating the localized variant distribution within a single parent austenite grain at a fatigue crack flank.
summary: This variant map visualizes the distribution of deformation-induced martensite child variants within a single parent austenite grain. Captured at a 0.4 µm step size, the map characterizes the microstructural response to fatigue loading, specifically identifying the variant orientations relative to the parent grain at the flank of a fatigue crack.

caption: Calculated phase fraction evolution for the 8Cr alloy during cooling, illustrating the temperature-dependent stability of constituent phases.
summary: This panel displays the calculated phase fractions for the 8Cr alloy as it undergoes cooling. The plot tracks the transformation and stability of various phases within the Fe-Cr-B system, demonstrating how the reduction in chromium content influences the phase precipitation sequence and the overall solidification behavior of the alloy.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectrum of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite, demonstrating a reduced band gap of 3.37 eV compared to individual components.
summary: This UV-visible absorption spectrum illustrates the optical characteristics of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite. The analysis indicates a reduced band gap energy of 3.37 eV, which facilitates a smoother charge transfer process due to the successful formation of a heterojunction between the two constituent materials.

caption: Thermo-kinetic E-pH diagram for Monel 400 in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 25 °C, with black dots indicating measured OCP values.
summary: Monel 400 behavior in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 25 °C is characterized by this thermo-kinetic diagram. Black dots represent the measured OCP values across various pH levels, providing a baseline for understanding the alloy's electrochemical stability and corrosion resistance compared to pure copper and nickel components at room temperature.

caption: Linear regression analysis of the hydrogen trap activation energy parameters for membrane samples, showing the temperature-dependent peak shift behavior.
summary: Representing the second peak in the series, this plot illustrates the linear fitting of ln(Φ/Tmax^2) against 1000/Tmax. The analysis focuses on characterizing hydrogen trap activation energies across varying grain sizes, confirming the consistent linear trend required to calculate trap-specific kinetic parameters for the membrane samples.

caption: FESEM-EDS spectrum acquired from the Ni-rich boride phase, corresponding to area A identified in the microstructure.
summary: This FESEM-EDS spectrum characterizes the chemical composition of the Ni-rich boride phase. Representing area A from the microstructure, the data provides specific elemental information for this phase, which is part of a zone containing two distinct phases with different chemical compositions as observed in the material analysis.

caption: Initial strontium isotope ratios (87Sr/86Sr)i plotted against MgO concentrations for Shitoukengde and Xiarihamu intrusions alongside worldwide continental arc volcanic rocks.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the correlation between initial strontium isotope ratios and MgO concentrations. By benchmarking the Shitoukengde and Xiarihamu intrusions against worldwide continental arc volcanic rocks, the figure facilitates an analysis of magmatic evolution and source characteristics within these specific tectonic environments, utilizing data from the PetDB database and Chen et al.

caption: Load-displacement (P-h) curves obtained from nano-indentation tests performed on the JG4 cladding specimen.
summary: This panel displays the load-displacement (P-h) curves derived from nano-indentation tests conducted on the JG4 cladding specimen. These curves characterize the mechanical response of the material under localized indentation, providing essential data regarding the indentation load-depth behavior across different zones of the Fe/Ni-based cladding specimen.

caption: Diagram illustrating the configuration of the closed vessel apparatus utilized for conducting explosion tests on ethanol and ethyl acetate fuel mixtures.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup employed for closed vessel explosion tests. The apparatus is specifically designed to measure pressure time histories for ethanol and ethyl acetate/air mixtures at an equivalence ratio of 1.1, providing the necessary framework for evaluating combustion characteristics during the experimental procedure.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the HX-B sample, featuring an inset plot displaying the grain aspect ratio.
summary: The grain size distribution for the HX-B sample is presented as a histogram. The average grain size for this specimen is recorded at 23.25 μm. Additionally, an inset plot illustrates the grain aspect ratio, which is defined as the ratio of the minor axis to the major axis of the grains.

caption: 1H-13C CPMAS NMR spectrum of cross-linked GAn@HPC-24 h, accompanied by a structural sketch illustrating the cross-linking configuration.
summary: The 1H-13C CPMAS NMR spectrum of the cross-linked GAn@HPC-24 h material is presented alongside its structural sketch. Solid-state NMR analysis was performed on the fine powder sample to confirm the successful cross-linking nature of the composite, providing spectroscopic evidence of the chemical environment within the synthesized GAn@HPC-24 h structure.

caption: ΔK evolution profile for a polished unnotched specimen, serving as a baseline for crack growth behavior.
summary: Panel d presents the ΔK evolution for a polished specimen, which acts as a reference for crack growth analysis. This data allows for comparison against the treated specimens shown in panels b and c, illustrating how surface preparation influences the stress intensity factor range during fatigue crack propagation.

caption: Comprehensive research methodology workflow illustrating the survey process and AHCA framework.
summary: This flowchart outlines the overall research methodology, detailing the survey process on the left, which encompasses pilot studies, final surveys, and expert evaluations. The right side presents the AHCA methodology and highlights the primary research contributions, providing a structured overview of the study's systematic approach and key analytical framework.

caption: Reflectance spectra of pre-alloyed Ni 52.1 at.% powder samples subjected to thermal treatment across a temperature range from 650 °C to 1450 °C.
summary: This figure displays the reflectance spectra of pre-alloyed Ni 52.1 at.% powder samples that have undergone thermal treatment at various temperatures ranging from 650 °C to 1450 °C. These spectral measurements provide insight into the optical properties of the powder as a function of the applied heat treatment conditions.

caption: Bode impedance and Bode angle plots corresponding to the 5-day immersion condition.
summary: Bode impedance and angle plots for samples immersed for 5 days are shown. These diagrams illustrate the frequency response of the electrochemical system at the intermediate immersion stage. The data is used to evaluate the corrosion resistance and surface film properties of the DED-produced NAB alloys under these specific conditions.

caption: HPI score radar chart illustrating nine sustainability dimensions for various PLA blends, highlighting performance gaps.
summary: This radar chart visualizes nine sustainability dimensions based on weighted performance gaps for different PLA blends. The HPI scores indicate that the V0:R100 blend, consisting of 100% rPLA, demonstrates superior environmental performance, characterized by minimal gaps in climatic conditions and natural resource depletion compared to other material configurations.

caption: Representation of the single-pass grain structure development during the additive building process, specifically excluding bulk nucleation effects.
summary: Depicting the grain structure formed during a single laser track pass, this schematic highlights the solidification process in the absence of bulk nucleation. It clarifies the structural evolution of the material under controlled additive manufacturing conditions, focusing on how grains develop within the melt pool during the building process.

caption: Correlation analysis of laser cladding process parameters, specifically laser power, powder feed rate, and scanning speed, against the resulting dilution rate.
summary: This analysis evaluates the influence of laser cladding parameters on dilution rate. Laser power and powder feed rate emerge as the primary driving forces, exhibiting strong correlation coefficients of 0.7167 and -0.5908, respectively. In contrast, scanning speed shows a negligible correlation coefficient of -0.0599, indicating minimal impact on the dilution rate.

caption: Tabulated summary of additive manufacturing process parameters and corresponding sample dimensions.
summary: This table presents the specific additive manufacturing process parameters and dimensions utilized for sample preparation. These parameters were systematically designed to guide the experimental process, including the initial preparation of the substrate bed without powder, ensuring consistent and controlled conditions for the subsequent fabrication of the material samples.

caption: STZ energy barriers calculated via Eq. (6) for cast and LPBF metallic glass specimens.
summary: Calculated STZ energy barriers for cast and LPBF samples are presented to evaluate the energetic requirements for STZ activation. The results demonstrate that the energy barriers are lower for the LPBF specimen, implying that STZ activation is energetically easier in the LPBF glass compared to the cast counterpart.

caption: Specific wear rate determined via the profile method based on the average of nine integrated cross-sectional areas.
summary: The specific wear rate is calculated by taking the average of the nine integrated cross-sectional areas. This value is then incorporated into formula (6) and combined with formulas (3) and (4) to derive the final specific wear rate, providing a quantitative measure of the material's wear resistance.

caption: EBSD-IPF map and misorientation distribution of the as-fabricated specimen at the top crack region, highlighting preferred <001> and <111> grain orientations.
summary: The EBSD-IPF map for the top crack region of the as-fabricated specimen demonstrates a consistent grain growth pattern. Similar to the non-crack region, the grains exhibit preferred orientations in the <001> and <111> directions. This visualization helps characterize the crystallographic orientation near the crack site in the top region.

caption: Calculated vertical cross-section of the Ti–Al–Mo–Zr–Si quinary phase diagram, generated using Thermo-Calc software, highlighting the specific composition of the Ti48Al1Mo0.45Zr0.3Si alloy.
summary: Calculated using Thermo-Calc software, this vertical cross-section of the Ti–Al–Mo–Zr–Si pentary phase diagram provides a detailed view of the phase stability for the Ti48Al1Mo0.45Zr0.3Si alloy. The diagram maps the phase evolution specifically for this complex quinary composition, facilitating the prediction of microstructural constituents under equilibrium conditions.

caption: Comparative Raman spectra of GO/PVA/Al and rGO/Al samples, illustrating the spectral signatures of the different carbon-based coatings.
summary: Raman spectra for GO/PVA/Al and rGO/Al samples are compared to characterize the carbon-based coatings. This analysis provides insight into the chemical state and structural characteristics of the graphene oxide and reduced graphene oxide layers deposited on the aluminum surfaces, facilitating a direct comparison of their respective spectral features.

caption: Micro-CT images of longitudinal and transverse sections of porous scaffolds at four weeks post-implantation, showing initial bone-scaffold contact.
summary: Micro-CT imaging of longitudinal and transverse sections of the porous scaffolds at four weeks post-implantation reveals the early stages of bone ingrowth. The images demonstrate that new bone tissue begins to make contact with the scaffold from all sides and extends into the shallower pores of the structure.

caption: Mould configuration utilized to define the geometry during the electrodeposition of the tensile specimen.
summary: This image shows the mould used to shape the sample during the electrodeposition process. By employing this specific mould, the manufacturing process ensures the production of net-shape tensile dogbone samples, maintaining the required gauge dimensions for accurate mechanical testing as per ASTM E8/E8M-16a standards.

caption: Initial emission and dissociation of the first full screw dislocation into two Shockley partials within the gamma phase, characterized by increased disregistry.
summary: The first full screw dislocation with a Burgers vector is emitted into the gamma phase. It immediately dissociates into two Shockley partials, as shown by the disregistry and dislocation density profiles. The inset highlights the dissociation process, marking the initial stage of the slip transmission sequence across the microstructure.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing the typical morphology of the R3 specimen, characterized by a matrix of lathy and blocky α’-martensite with dispersed retained-γ.
summary: This bright-field TEM image reveals the typical microstructure of the R3 specimen. The matrix is primarily composed of lathy and blocky α’-martensite, with a slight dispersion of retained-γ phase. This observation is consistent with EBSD results, confirming the presence of these specific martensitic and austenitic structural components.

caption: Ternary contour plot of log10 Cost for 40 Fe-Co-Ni alloy compositions, showing predicted compositions from ETR and NNR_4layers_Wen models for six target sets.
summary: This ternary contour plot maps the log10 Cost for 40 Fe-Co-Ni alloy compositions, including predicted compositions from ETR and NNR_4layers_Wen models. The data shows that Fe content increases as the target Cost value decreases, while Co content increases in predicted compositions when the set values for Cost and Tc are increased.

caption: Fatigue performance curves for the same four LPBF-manufactured aluminum alloys evaluated after undergoing a machining process to achieve a machined surface condition, tested at R = 1.
summary: Displayed are the S-N fatigue curves for four LPBF-manufactured aluminum alloys after surface machining. These tests, conducted under ASTM E606 standards with a stress ratio of R = 1, demonstrate how surface finishing influences the fatigue life and mechanical behavior of these specific additively manufactured aluminum alloy components.

caption: Estimated contribution of the CTE (Coefficient of Thermal Expansion) mismatch strengthening mechanism to the yield strength enhancement of Scalmalloy® after heat treatment at 325 °C for durations of 4, 24, and 48 hours.
summary: This panel displays the CTE strengthening contribution for Scalmalloy® samples subjected to heat treatment at 325 °C for 4, 24, and 48 hours. It quantifies the strengthening effect relative to as-built conditions, demonstrating the role of thermal expansion mismatch in the alloy's mechanical performance across different aging times.

caption: Apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions in 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during the delithiation process, calculated using Eq. (1).
summary: This panel displays the apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions during the delithiation process for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes. The data, calculated according to Eq. (1), provides a comparative analysis of ion transport kinetics within the different electrode architectures during the extraction phase of battery cycling.

caption: Coefficient of thermal expansion plotted against temperature for the W1 specimen containing 0 wt% Ni, comparing horizontal (H) and vertical (V) extraction orientations.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion for the W1 specimen, which contains 0 wt% nickel. Data are presented for samples extracted from both horizontal and vertical planes, providing insight into the thermal expansion behavior of the material at this specific composition within the interface region of the GT FGM.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of negative ions CrO2-, CrO3H2-, NiO2H2-, and Ni2- for the mechanically ground (M) sample after 4 h of potentiostatic passivation at 0.25 V vs. SCE in 0.5 M H2SO4.
summary: The ToF-SIMS depth profile for the mechanically ground sample reveals the distribution of Cr and Ni hydroxide species after electrochemical passivation. The CrO3H2- signal is more intense than the NiO2H2- signal, with a CrO3H2-/NiO2H2- intensity ratio of 4.5, indicating Cr enrichment at the interface between the inner and outer layers.

caption: Temporal evolution of simulated powder mass flow rate at the nozzle exit compared to a 12 g min-1 target, evaluated across carrier-gas flow rates of 8, 10, 12, and 14 L min-1, with insets displaying instantaneous particle trajectories at the single-jet exit.
summary: Simulated powder mass flow rates fluctuate around the 12 g min-1 target across all tested carrier-gas flow rates, demonstrating that aerodynamic drag primarily influences transient transport stability rather than the mean delivery rate. Insets visualize the instantaneous particle trajectories, which define the local feeding conditions and subsequent deposition track characteristics.

caption: Cross-validation performance of the pure data-driven energy surrogate model evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation.
summary: This figure presents the results of a 5-fold cross-validation analysis for the pure data-driven energy surrogate model. The plot illustrates the predictive accuracy and robustness of the model by comparing predicted energy values against ground truth data, demonstrating the effectiveness of the machine learning approach in surrogate energy modeling.

caption: Box plot illustrating the distribution of transverse transverse deviations.
summary: This box plot displays the statistical distribution of transverse transverse deviations. The data represents the second of two directional measurements presented in the study, providing a clear visualization of the spread and central tendency of the transverse deviation results as part of the comparative analysis of directional performance.

caption: Low-magnification microstructure of the BD cross-section showing the melt pool morphology.
summary: This panel displays the low-magnification microstructure of the BD cross-section, focusing on the melt pool morphology. The BD cross-section is characterized by specific melt pool features, providing a foundational view of the material's structural arrangement within this orientation before examining the interior crystal characteristics in subsequent panels.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) of martensite in layer-1, showing the initial emergence of the [341]M pole texture component along the Y-direction.
summary: Layer-1 represents the surface region subjected to LSP. The Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) for this layer reveals the initial emergence of the [341]M pole texture component aligned with the Y-direction, which corresponds to the laser loading direction. This indicates the onset of texture modification due to the laser impact.

caption: Open Circuit Potential (OCP) evolution of 17-4 PH stainless steel specimens immersed in seawater, plotted as potential versus time.
summary: The Open Circuit Potential (OCP) curve of 17-4 PH stainless steel in seawater is presented. Observed fluctuations in the potential indicate an active corrosion process occurring on the specimen surface and suggest dynamic changes in the properties of the passive film during the electrochemical testing period.

caption: H1 specimen average load-displacement response captured at the 10th cycle under dynamic sinusoidal displacement.
summary: Representing the steady-state response of the H1 specimen, this load-displacement curve is derived from the 10th cycle of dynamic sinusoidal testing. The plot characterizes the mechanical behavior of the material, highlighting the relationship between applied load and displacement during the steady-state phase of the cycle.

caption: STEM bright-field micrograph of the Ti6Al4V pin surface region, illustrating the nanograin layer situated between the surface oxide and the underlying martensitic substrate.
summary: This STEM bright-field micrograph reveals the microstructural evolution beneath the surface of a Ti6Al4V pin. It clearly documents a distinct nanograin layer sandwiched between the surface oxide and the bulk Ti6Al4V martensite. The dashed line effectively delineates the boundary between these nanostructured surface grains and the martensitic matrix.

caption: Nyquist diagrams showing the electrochemical impedance response of LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi samples after 1 hour of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, with solid lines representing the fitted data.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance behavior of LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi alloys following one hour of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These diagrams, which include fitted solid lines, are used to compare the corrosion resistance and electrochemical interactions of the passive films formed on these specific NiTi samples.

caption: Electron density difference map calculated for pure NiO.
summary: This panel presents the electron density difference map for pure NiO, derived from electronic structure calculations. The visualization illustrates the spatial distribution of charge redistribution within the NiO lattice, providing insight into the fundamental electronic properties of the material as explored through density functional theory methods.

caption: BMD Messwell 410V tool pre-setter utilized for Z-axis calibration with micron-level measurement accuracy.
summary: The BMD Messwell 410V tool pre-setter is depicted, which is essential for the hybrid micromachining processes described. This device enables precise Z-axis calibrations, providing the micron-level measurement accuracy required to maintain the integrity and precision of the machining operations.

caption: Conceptual overview of the online monitoring and feedback control architecture designed for the continuous fiber-reinforced polymer composite (CFRPC) 3D printing process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the global strategy for online monitoring and feedback control during the CFRPC 3D printing process. It provides a high-level conceptual overview of the integrated system architecture, which is essential for maintaining quality and precision throughout the additive manufacturing of fiber-reinforced composite materials.

caption: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns comparing the structural characteristics of as-synthesized powder versus thermally annealed material.
summary: The XRD patterns presented in this panel illustrate the structural differences between the as-synthesized powder and the material after thermal annealing. By comparing these diffraction profiles, the figure highlights changes in crystallinity and phase composition resulting from the heat treatment process applied to the synthesized graphitic material.

caption: X-ray microtomography cross-section of WA nickel-based alloy 625 powder particles.
summary: This X-ray microtomography cross-section of WA nickel-based alloy 625 powder particles reveals internal porosity. The 3D scan confirms the particle morphology and identifies irregularly shaped pores within the powder, providing a quantitative analysis of internal features that are not accessible through standard 2D characterization methods.

caption: Force-time (F-T) curves for the unit structure at an impact velocity of 1.0 m/s, demonstrating the influence of varying geometric parameter l on the dynamic response.
summary: This panel displays the contact force-time (F-T) curves for the unit structure under impact at 1.0 m/s. The data illustrates how variations in the geometric parameter l affect the structural response during the impact event, providing a baseline for comparing the mechanical behavior of the unit structure.

caption: Debye-Scherrer rings observed in the as-cast Al-5Ce-0.25Zr alloy.
summary: Debye-Scherrer rings observed in the as-cast Al-5Ce-0.25Zr alloy illustrate the two-dimensional diffraction pattern for this specific composition. This diffraction analysis is part of a broader investigation into how small additions of zirconium influence the structural characteristics of as-cast aluminum-cerium alloys, as evidenced by the recorded diffraction patterns.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of glass samples treated with different dopants and laser parameters, illustrating the optical response associated with nanoparticle formation.
summary: UV-Vis measurements of the differently treated glass samples provide quantitative data on their optical properties. These spectra characterize the light adsorption behavior resulting from the formation of gold and silver nanoparticles, confirming the relationship between the laser-induced nanoparticle density and the observed color changes in the printed glass.

caption: Micro-scale rough surface morphology resulting from acid etching.
summary: Acid etching is applied to the sanded TC4 surface to induce micro-scale roughness. This chemical treatment modifies the surface topography, creating the necessary micro-scale features that serve as the structural base for the final anodization process in the construction of the micro-nano composite surface.

caption: Control volume schematic of the liquid channel at the grain boundary, illustrating the feeding velocity, channel thickness, and width w at height z.
summary: This schematic represents a control volume of the liquid channel located at the grain boundary, which facilitates feeding during solidification. It defines key parameters including the feeding velocity, the channel thickness at height z, and the width w of the differential control volume taken perpendicular to the growth direction.

caption: Scaled and standardized regression coefficients illustrating the relative influence of individual predictors across three distinct models.
summary: This plot displays the scaled and standardized coefficients derived from three regression models, providing a quantitative assessment of how individual predictors influence the model outcomes. By utilizing standardized values, the relative impact of each variable is directly comparable, facilitating a clear evaluation of predictor significance within the study's analytical framework.

caption: Evolution of the α-AlFeMnSi (022) reference peak during cooling at a rate of 0.3 K s⁻¹.
summary: This panel illustrates the synchrotron diffraction signal for the α-AlFeMnSi (022) reference peak during cooling at 0.3 K s⁻¹. The measurement is characterized by significant noise levels, resulting from the combination of a low phase fraction and the low count intensity inherent to this specific HEXRD experimental setup.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot of the scale film on Inconel 625 in 1 mol/L phosphoric acid.
summary: The Mott-Schottky curve shown for the 1 mol/L phosphoric acid condition provides insight into the semiconductor properties of the scale film on Inconel 625. This measurement is critical for understanding how higher acid concentrations modify the electrochemical behavior and stability of the protective film on the alloy.

caption: Grain Average Misorientation (GAM) map illustrating sites of initial recrystallization in the sample deformed at 1100 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ strain rate.
summary: This GAM map highlights initial recrystallization sites in a sample deformed at 1100 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ strain rate. The analysis categorizes recrystallized grains into four distinct types: clean grain boundaries, clean grain interiors, Ni5Gd particles at grain boundaries, and Ni5Gd particles within grain interiors to facilitate statistical counting.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of bone sections revealing new bone growth, marked in fluorescent green, localized at the periphery and within the defect sites.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy of bone sections highlights new bone formation in fluorescent green. The images demonstrate that new bone is actively forming both at the periphery and within the interior of the defects. This technique complements the histological staining by providing a clear spatial distribution of the newly synthesized bone tissue.

caption: Spatial distribution of the Al diffusion potential (μAl) in Ni-14Al-3Mo alloy at t* = 400.
summary: This panel presents the Al diffusion potential distribution in Ni-14Al-3Mo alloy at a nondimensionalized aging time of 400. The potential includes chemical and elastic energy contributions. Dotted lines along y = 21 highlight the decrease in μAl within the regions between adjacent γ′ particles as the aging time continues to increase.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the BCC structural phase within the FeAlNiCrMn alloy model.
summary: This panel displays the atomic positions of the BCC structural phase for the FeAlNiCrMn alloy. Similar to the FCC model, every ball represents a mixture of Fe, Al, Ni, Cr, and Mn. This structural model provides a clear visualization of the BCC phase configuration used in the alloy analysis.

caption: Cycling performance of the D-3DP Si||NCM full-cell, with an inset photograph showing the battery powering lit bulbs.
summary: The D-3DP Si||NCM full-cell demonstrates robust electrochemical performance, delivering an initial areal capacity of 6.04 mAh cm-2 at 0.1 mA cm-2. It maintains a steady capacity of 3.68 mAh cm-2 after 70 cycles at 0.2 mA cm-2, as evidenced by the cycling plot and the successful demonstration of powering bulbs.

caption: Temperature-dependent mass-normalized magnetization curves for dense, mesoporous, and macroporous Ni–W films in the 100 K to 700 K range.
summary: The magnetization curves for Ni–W films show a distinct temperature dependence between 100 K and 700 K. These samples exhibit lower Curie temperatures compared to pure Ni, with measured values of 589 K, 607 K, and 585 K for the dense, mesoporous, and macroporous films, respectively.

caption: Chronoamperometry profile demonstrating the electrodeposition of cobalt onto a copper foil substrate.
summary: Chronoamperometry data for the electrodeposition of cobalt onto a copper foil is presented here. Analysis of this electrochemical profile allowed for the calculation of the cobalt yield, which was determined to be 1.14 × 10^-4 mol, confirming the efficiency of the deposition process on the copper substrate.

caption: Average magnetic flux density B y in the transverse direction of the permanent magnet before, during, and after a short circuit event, comparing the new model predictions against previous model data.
summary: This plot illustrates the average magnetic flux density in the transverse direction of a permanent magnet during a short circuit event. It compares the new model predictions with previous model results. Specifically, the transverse direction flux density is shown to change from 3.6 mT to 2.7 mT in the new model.

caption: Experimental setup of the AFE system integrated onto a Prusa i3 MK3s 3-axis printer, featuring the hot end inclined at a 45° angle and secured with custom 3D-printed fixtures.
summary: The AFE system is mounted on a Prusa i3 MK3s 3-axis printer to facilitate additive manufacturing. The hot end is specifically inclined at a 45° angle and secured using custom 3D-printed fixtures, establishing the baseline configuration for the AFE-based printing process described in the study.

caption: Permeability distribution for St facies highlighting the contrast between distinct lamina types.
summary: St facies permeability is displayed here, demonstrating a factor of 5 variation between different lamina types. Clay-poor laminae exhibit higher permeability values of approximately 1000 mD, while clay-rich laminae show lower values of approximately 200 mD, consistent with the observed trends in cross-bedded sandstone facies.

caption: Three-dimensional reflection loss surface plot for the SCC-2 sample, showcasing the enhanced electromagnetic wave absorption performance achieved through optimized material composition.
summary: This 3D plot illustrates the reflection loss of the SCC-2 sample. The data indicates that the SCC-2 composition exhibits superior electromagnetic wave absorption performance, likely due to the synergistic effects between impedance matching and attenuation constant, resulting in a more effective absorption profile across the tested frequency range.

caption: Evolution of strain distributions under LCF loading for specimen #1, showing the leftward migration of peak A1 and the transient emergence and subsequent disappearance of peak B1 at site B1.
summary: This panel displays the strain distribution evolution in specimen #1 during LCF loading. From the first to the 2650th cycle, strain peak A1 shifts leftward along the hole circumference. Concurrently, peak B1 emerges briefly before disappearing, illustrating the dynamic strain localization behavior occurring throughout the fatigue life of the material.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the middle region of the fast deposition along the <011> Al zone axis, highlighting the presence of very fine GP zones or precipitates within the dash circles.
summary: Unlike the slow deposition, the middle region of the fast deposition contains very fine GP zones or precipitates, as highlighted by the dash circles. These structural features, observed along the <011> Al zone axis, are similar in morphology to those found in the top area of the fast deposition.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectrum of 10 mM fluorescein measured with the double grating coupler configuration, exhibiting signal levels comparable to the single grating coupler setup.
summary: The measured emission spectrum for the double grating coupler configuration shows that the signal level is similar to that observed for the single grating coupler setup. This confirms that the integration of a second grating coupler does not cause further significant degradation in the fluorescence detection signal.

caption: Low-magnification TEM micrograph of the sample solution heat treated at 505 °C for 0.5 h and overaged at 175 °C for 512 h.
summary: This low-magnification TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the T6-like_0.5 sample. It provides an overview of the α-Al matrix, revealing the distribution of particles in terms of their shape and dimensions, which appears very similar to the distribution observed in the T6-like_4 sample.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for Ti6242 alloy, featuring a red dotted line that indicates the predicted cooling trajectory corresponding to the directed energy deposition (DED) process parameters utilized in this study.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of Ti6242 alloy. The superimposed red dotted line represents the specific cooling path during the DED process, which is estimated to occur at a rate between 320 and 365 K/s, providing critical insight into the resulting microstructure formation under these rapid solidification conditions.

caption: Mid-IR wavelength range absorptance spectra for pure Al2O3 and CuO/Al2O3 ceramic composite 3D structures.
summary: Panel (b) presents the measured absorptance spectra for pure Al2O3 and high-resolution CuO/Al2O3 ceramic composite 3D structures specifically within the mid-infrared wavelength range. This data, part of the broader 0.25–20 μm characterization, highlights the distinct optical absorption characteristics of the composite structures compared to the pure ceramic baseline.

caption: Raman spectra of UHS-treated samples showing D-band and G-band features at 1340 cm-1 and 1598 cm-1, respectively.
summary: Micro-Raman analysis reveals two distinctive features corresponding to the D-band and G-band at 1340 cm-1 and 1598 cm-1. The relative intensities and positions of these peaks indicate the presence of turbostratic carbon, which originates from the decomposition of the polymer binder during the UHS treatment process.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the interface region demonstrating continuous grain growth across the junction.
summary: The interface region of the Type II sample is characterized by continuous grain growth across the boundary, which is not clearly visible, signifying strong interfacial bonding. The microstructure features a mixture of elongated and refined grains, with dimensions ranging from 0.2 mm to 1 mm in length and 0.2 mm to 0.5 mm in width.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the comparative improvements in physical, static, and cyclic mechanical properties of MEX parts subjected to aging and shot peening treatments.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive summary of the impact of aging and shot peening treatments on MEX parts. It visualizes the enhancements across physical, static, and dynamic mechanical properties, allowing for a direct comparison of how these specific post-processing methods influence the overall performance characteristics of the material.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the bimetallic specimen, highlighting the structural characteristics of the interface between AISI 316L and IN625.
summary: The XRD pattern of the bimetallic specimen is presented to characterize the interface between AISI 316L and IN625. This analysis reveals structural features consistent with the FeSi 2.9–316L configuration, specifically noting the presence of melt pools from the upper material and the absence of epitaxial growth at the interface.

caption: Comparison of simulated and measured transmission spectra for the Si metasurface under normal incidence, showing close agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental results.
summary: The transmission spectra of the Si metasurface are presented to validate the design. Both simulated and measured data are plotted, demonstrating excellent agreement between the two. This confirms the accuracy of the numerical model in predicting the optical response of the fabricated Si nanodisk array at normal incidence.

caption: Density of states (DOS) analysis for the 3DGPC-PS system.
summary: Panel f displays the DOS analysis for the 3DGPC-PS system, revealing significantly enhanced orbital overlap between N, C, and H atoms compared to the pristine 3DGPC. This increased overlap indicates strong electronic interaction and hybridization between the adsorbent and the adsorbate, confirming the stability of the complex.

caption: Conceptual representation of the shear test setup, detailing the mechanical loading configuration applied to the brazed joint.
summary: The diagram depicts the mechanical shear test configuration used to evaluate the brazed joint. It illustrates the orientation and loading mechanism applied to the sample, providing a clear overview of the experimental setup required to measure the shear strength of the diffusion brazed interface in a controlled manner.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the N-free alloy rolled at 1000°C, highlighting the presence of nanoscale deformation twins.
summary: This dark-field TEM image highlights the formation of nanoscale deformation twins in the N-free alloy after hot-caliber rolling at 1000°C. These observations, alongside SFs, demonstrate that deformation features are produced preferentially at this temperature, providing critical insights into the microstructural evolution of the highly distorted alloy.

caption: Ashby plot comparing fracture toughness values of Ti-6Al-4V alloys across different processing conditions, including LPBF samples from this study, literature-derived LPBF data, and wrought alloy benchmarks.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the fracture toughness performance of Ti-6Al-4V alloys. It integrates experimental data from this study with literature values for LPBF and wrought specimens. By utilizing orientation-specific properties consistent with loading directions, the plot provides a comparative overview of material performance across various processing conditions and historical benchmarks.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of FNF@AuNP and enzyme solution demonstrating optical responses to levodopa concentrations ranging from 6 to 500 μM.
summary: UV-Vis spectroscopy reveals the optical sensitivity of the FNF@AuNP and enzyme sensor. Significant changes in absorbance at 525 nm are observed for levodopa concentrations as low as 6 μM, confirming the system's high sensitivity to the analyte across a broad concentration range up to 500 μM.

caption: Polarization curve of NIF(Na,Cr)-S recorded after 100 hours of stable operation at a current density of 150 mA cm-2, demonstrating long-term electrochemical durability.
summary: The polarization curve of NIF(Na,Cr)-S is shown following 100 hours of stable operation at a current density of 150 mA cm-2. This measurement serves to evaluate the long-term electrochemical durability and performance retention of the catalyst under continuous, high-current density operating conditions, confirming its stability for practical OER applications.

caption: Hierarchical classification structure of additive manufacturing (AM) methods specifically applied to metal forming processes.
summary: This figure presents a comprehensive classification of additive manufacturing methods utilized for metal forming. The schematic serves as a structured overview, organizing various AM techniques into a logical hierarchy to clarify the diverse approaches available for metal-based additive manufacturing processes within the broader context of materials science and engineering.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing solution-treated and aged Fe–Cr–Ni medium-entropy alloy (MEA) specimens.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for Fe–Cr–Ni medium-entropy alloy specimens subjected to both solution treatment and aging processes. The data provides a structural comparison between these two distinct metallurgical conditions, illustrating the phase evolution or stability of the MEA specimens as influenced by the thermal treatment history.

caption: Atomic-scale morphology of a Ni3Al precipitate in a nickel matrix generated via Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulation at 400 K, showing a cubic structure with (100) faces and (110) faceted edges.
summary: The KMC simulation at 400 K reveals a Ni3Al precipitate morphology that closely matches the Wulff construction prediction. The cluster adopts a cubic shape dominated by large (100) faces, while the edges exhibit (110) facets. Ni atoms are represented in black and Al atoms in grey, confirming the predicted structural configuration.

caption: Tabulated optimization output results generated by Design Expert-13 software, detailing the optimal process parameter settings, corresponding response values, and the calculated desirability value.
summary: This table presents the optimization output results obtained from Design Expert-13 software. It explicitly lists the optimal process parameter settings alongside the resulting response values. Furthermore, the inclusion of the desirability value provides a quantitative assessment of the optimization success, confirming the effectiveness of the chosen process parameters for the study.

caption: Engineering tensile stress-strain curves for sieved wide-range powder specimens in the as-HIPped condition.
summary: Engineering tensile stress-strain curves are presented for sieved wide-range powder specimens processed in the as-HIPped condition. These results, obtained from ET tensile tests, characterize the mechanical response of the material. The data provides a clear visualization of the tensile performance for the specific powder fractions evaluated in this study.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification performance of the GPT-4o model in detecting anomalies within G-code sequences.
summary: This confusion matrix evaluates the GPT-4o model's performance in identifying G-code anomalies using a deterministic approach. It provides a visual representation of the model's classification accuracy, highlighting true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives to assess the reliability of GPT-4o in this specific manufacturing-related anomaly detection task.

caption: Fluorescent staining images of DAPI (blue), Osterix (green), and Actin (red) in BMSC-seeded Gel/AM 3D bioprinted scaffolds after 21 days of induced osteogenic differentiation.
summary: Fluorescent staining of Osterix, DAPI, and Actin at day 21 illustrates the osteogenic differentiation status of BMSCs within the scaffold. The fluorescent intensity patterns of Osterix mirror those observed for Runx2, confirming consistent osteogenic marker expression across the scaffold groups following the 21-day induced differentiation culture period.

caption: Contour map showing the elastic energy increment ΔE relative to ϕ and ψ for needle-shaped ellipsoidal inclusions, where broken circles denote the coordinates corresponding to the minimum energy state.
summary: Representing the elastic energy landscape for needle-shaped inclusions, this contour plot maps ΔE against ϕ and ψ. The inclusion of broken circles highlights the specific parameter combinations that yield the minimum elastic energy, providing a clear comparison of energy minimization trends between needle and disk inclusion geometries.

caption: Comparison of deposition rates versus feature sizes for various fusion and solid-state additive manufacturing processes, highlighting the specific performance of the 30 mm width tool used in this study.
summary: This Ashby plot compares deposition rates against feature sizes for diverse metal additive manufacturing processes. It specifically highlights the 30 mm width tool utilized in this study, identifying the H = 4 mm and H = 1 mm builds, which achieve deposition rates of 890 cc/hr and 300 cc/hr, respectively.

caption: External morphology of the Ti–48Al–2Cr–2Nb alloy specimen produced via the LMD technique.
summary: The external morphology of the Ti–48Al–2Cr–2Nb alloy is presented in this photograph. The specimen was formed using the Laser Metal Deposition process, which was performed in a sealed argon chamber to prevent oxidation by keeping oxygen concentrations below 50 ppm, ensuring the quality of the resulting alloy structure.

caption: Time-dependent resistance signal captured during the tapping of the gel finger cup against a table surface, indicating the detection of specific finger movement states.
summary: This panel displays the resistance signal generated when the gel finger cup taps against a table. The data confirms that the sensor can accurately detect and distinguish the finger movement state, providing a reliable method for monitoring contact events through changes in the electrical resistance of the gel.

caption: Maximum height (Sz) parameter values derived from the VIP plot.
summary: This bar chart presents the Sz parameter, representing the maximum height of the surface profile. Categorized as a height parameter in purple, the values are averaged from 12 specimens. This metric is vital for characterizing the total vertical range of the surface topography of the peg samples.

caption: Irreversible relative length changes (ΔL/L0) of as-printed AM HEA samples during heating at 5 K/min, plotted against reference signals derived from the difference between the second and third heating cycles. Thick solid lines represent the primary measurement, while thin dashed lines indicate the baseline reproducibility.
summary: Dilatometry measurements reveal irreversible relative length changes in AM HEA upon heating to 873 K. The data, characterized by the reproducibility of reference curves across independent measurements, demonstrate distinct elongation behaviors for samples cut parallel to the TD and BD directions, reflecting the thermal stability of the as-printed microstructure.

caption: Simulated 3D temperature and velocity distributions for AlSi10Mg alloy during the first layer and first hatch fabrication at a 1000 mm/s scanning speed.
summary: Displayed are the computed three-dimensional temperature and velocity fields for AlSi10Mg alloy during the first layer and first hatch of a 20 mm long build. The simulation, conducted at a 1000 mm/s scanning speed, provides a detailed view of the thermal and velocity profiles within the melt pool for this aluminum alloy.

caption: Nyquist plot illustrating the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy of L-PBF-produced S3 NiTi alloy in pH 3 Hank's solution, highlighting low-frequency diffusion characteristics.
