caption: Pilot jet nozzle component designed specifically for the ignition of the afterburner system.
summary: This photograph displays the pilot jet nozzle component utilized within the RD-33 engine's annular combustor. Unlike the primary fuel nozzles used for standard engine operation, this specific nozzle is dedicated exclusively to the ignition process of the afterburner, ensuring reliable performance during high-thrust operational phases of the aircraft engine.

caption: Optical transmittance profile of the hydrogel.
summary: The optical transmittance profile of the hydrogel is shown in this panel. This measurement quantifies the light-transmitting properties of the material, providing insight into the optical clarity and potential transparency of the POAL hydrogel.

caption: Quantitative comparison of wear volume, wear rate, and hardness values for as-deposited versus LSP-treated OL-DED Inconel 718.
summary: This plot quantifies the wear volume, wear rate, and hardness for both as-deposited and LSP-treated OL-DED Inconel 718. The data confirms that the as-deposited alloy suffers from higher wear volume and rate, directly correlating with its lower surface hardness and unfavorable tensile residual stress state compared to the treated alloy.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of SLM-fabricated TA11 titanium alloy showing the crystallographic orientation of acicular α' martensite.
summary: The IPF map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of acicular α' martensite in SLM-fabricated TA11 titanium alloy. The microstructure exhibits significant texture, with the orientation of the martensite needles primarily concentrated along the [0001], [10-10], and [01-10] directions, with the [0001] direction showing the maximum pole density.

caption: Dispersion relation of the infinite-sized negative regulation MRM in the absence of an external magnetic field, highlighting a band gap between 67.5 Hz and 2507.9 Hz.
summary: The dispersion relation for the infinite-sized negative regulation MRM without an external magnetic field is presented. By applying lumped mass and stiffness parameters, the band gap is identified, starting at 67.5 Hz and ending at 2507.9 Hz, as indicated by the shaded gray region in the plot.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the sample deformed at 800 °C to 20% strain, revealing the coexistence of L12 and B2 phases.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the microstructure of the sample after 20% compressive strain at 800 °C. The analysis confirms the presence of eutectic L12 and B2 phases resulting from synergistic deformation. This characterization provides evidence of the phase distribution within the material following the high-temperature deformation process.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph showing a high density of paired dislocations in the sample after fatigue testing at 750 °C and 1200 MPa.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph reveals the deformation structure of the sample subjected to fatigue testing at 750 °C and 1200 MPa. The image highlights a high density of paired dislocations, indicating that dislocation slip is a dominant mechanism during the high-temperature fatigue deformation process in this material.

caption: Field-dependent resistivity ρ for Ni75Co25 alloy measured at 300 K, highlighting the differences between TMR and PMR magnetic field orientations.
summary: Measured at 300 K, the resistivity of the Ni75Co25 alloy shows clear orientation dependence between TMR and PMR configurations. The saturation field for TMR is observed at 3 kOe, whereas the PMR saturation field is nearly five times higher, consistent with the behavior observed at 3 K.

caption: 2D morphology map of the SLM sample surface, highlighting the localized corrosion features and the dotted line range used for depth analysis.
summary: This 2D morphology map provides a detailed view of the SLM sample surface topography following 24 hours of immersion. The map clearly delineates the surface features and identifies the specific dotted line range utilized for subsequent quantitative corrosion depth measurements, confirming the localized nature of the observed degradation.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) map illustrating the spatial distribution of Fe content across the melt pool.
summary: The EDS map displays the elemental distribution of Fe within the melt pool of the mixed sample. This compositional mapping is critical for identifying local variations in Fe concentration, which correlate with the different BCC phase morphologies observed in the corresponding phase map analysis.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing pure MPA ligands with MPA-capped ZCIS/ZnS quantum dots, highlighting the disappearance of the –SH stretching vibrational peak at 2573 cm⁻¹ in the functionalized QDs.
summary: This panel presents the FTIR spectra of pure MPA and MPA-capped ZCIS/ZnS quantum dots. The analysis confirms successful ligand exchange, evidenced by the absence of the characteristic –SH stretching vibrational peak at 2573 cm⁻¹ in the ZCIS/ZnS-MPA sample, demonstrating the effectiveness of the surface modification process on the quantum dots.

caption: Chronopotentiometric curves of Co-based alloy coatings measured over a 48-hour duration at a constant cathodic current density of -100 mA cm⁻².
summary: This figure displays the chronopotentiometric behavior of Co-based alloy coatings subjected to a constant current density of -100 mA cm⁻² for 48 hours. The recorded CP curves provide essential data regarding the electrochemical stability and potential evolution of the studied alloy surfaces under sustained cathodic polarization conditions over the specified test duration.

caption: Hardness and reduced modulus versus indentation depth for AM IN718 nitrided at 650 °C.
summary: Mechanical characterization of the AM IN718 alloy nitrided at 650 °C demonstrates hardness values ranging from 2.5 to 14.2 GPa. Compared to the 500 °C treatment, this specimen exhibits fewer variations in mechanical properties as a function of indentation depth within the nitrided hard layer.

caption: Rising transients of hydrogen permeation tests for the H860 aged state subjected to different charging currents.
summary: This panel presents the rising transients of hydrogen permeation tests for the H860 aged metallurgical state. By applying different charging currents, the permeation behavior is characterized, demonstrating the specific response of this aged state to hydrogen charging compared to the solution annealed and H1000 states.

caption: Frequency distribution of pore volume in 3D-printed cementitious composites, showing a broadening trend from Plain to Clay A, Optimized LC³, and Clay B samples.
summary: This histogram displays the frequency distribution of pore volumes in 3D-printed cementitious composites derived from XCT data. The distribution becomes progressively broader across different binder compositions, transitioning from Plain to Clay A, then to Optimized LC³, and reaching its widest extent in the Clay B sample, indicating significant mineralogical influence.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images visualizing intracellular ROS levels in cells treated with different hydrogel formulations under oxidative stress, where green fluorescence intensity serves as an indicator of ROS presence.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy reveals intracellular ROS levels in cells subjected to oxidative stress. Cells treated with H2O2 exhibit strong green fluorescence, indicating elevated ROS levels compared to untreated controls. The imaging demonstrates the efficacy of the hydrogel formulations in modulating ROS presence within the cellular environment under stress conditions.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization behavior showing the variation of magnetic moment M as a function of temperature.
summary: This figure illustrates the magnetic response of the material by plotting magnetization M against temperature. The data provides a clear visualization of the temperature-dependent magnetic behavior, confirming the relationship between thermal energy and magnetic moment as described in the experimental analysis of the material's magnetic properties.

caption: STEM cross-section of TiN/TaC superlattice with a nominal bilayer period of 2 nm, featuring wavy nanolayers and an inset SAED pattern.
summary: This STEM cross-section reveals a nanolayered structure in the TiN/TaC superlattice with a 2 nm bilayer period. The layers exhibit characteristic waviness. The corresponding SAED inset displays ring-shaped patterns, indicating a single-phase fcc crystal structure composed of nano-sized grains without a distinct preferred orientation or growth direction.

caption: Atom probe tomography iso-surface reconstruction of γ' Ni3(Al,Ti) and γ'' Ni3Nb precipitates in the unirradiated condition.
summary: This APT reconstruction displays the distribution of γ' and γ'' precipitates in the unirradiated material state. The γ' precipitates are rendered in cyan, while the γ'' precipitates are shown in brown. This visualization serves as a baseline to examine the morphology and spatial arrangement of these precipitates prior to irradiation exposure.

caption: Pi plane isometric projection of the Lode parameter for State 5 at 870 to 738 MPa, based on incompatible strain-derived principal stresses.
summary: At 870 to 738 MPa, this contour plot maps the Lode parameter derived from incompatible distortion. The visualization confirms that the stress state remains a complex mix of loading, showing no trend towards uniaxiality and highlighting the persistent multiaxiality required by the local micromechanical grain interactions.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the effect of various roughness parameters on fatigue life, with a statistical significance threshold of 2.10.
summary: This Pareto chart visualizes the effect of different roughness parameters on fatigue life, using a threshold of 2.10 to denote statistical significance at a 95% confidence level. The analysis indicates that these specific roughness parameters do not demonstrate statistical significance regarding their influence on the fatigue life of the material.

caption: Magnetic free energy F mag of bcc Co derived from Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: Representing the magnetic free energy F mag for bcc cobalt, this panel utilizes Monte Carlo simulation results. As referenced in the study, this plot contributes to the broader analysis of magnetic properties in cobalt phases, detailing the energetic state of the bcc structure within the simulation framework.

caption: Areal capacitance of 3D-IDCμE/PPy as a function of the current density applied during PPy electrodeposition for a 10-minute duration.
summary: This plot displays the areal capacitance of 3D-IDCμE/PPy electrodes derived from GCD measurements. The specific capacitance increases as the PPy electrodeposition current density is raised from 1 to 4 mA cm⁻², demonstrating an optimal range for enhancing the energy storage capacity of the 3D-IDCμE system.

caption: Optimization interface displaying the configuration settings and control parameters for executing design refinement algorithms.
summary: The optimization interface within Optiworks provides the necessary controls for users to configure and execute design refinement algorithms. This screen is central to the software's functionality, allowing for the systematic adjustment of parameters to achieve desired performance targets during the computational design process presented in the interface.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the as-built MMJ SS316L material, illustrating the grain orientation distribution and confirming the absence of preferred crystallographic orientation.
summary: This inverse pole figure (IPF) map characterizes the as-built MMJ SS316L material. The visualization demonstrates that the sample exhibits no preferred orientation, indicating a randomly distributed grain structure within the as-built material, which is consistent with the observed microstructural characteristics of the sintered sample.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization (M-T) curves for FeCoNi and Fe30Co30Ni30Cr10-xMnx alloys measured under a 3000 Oe applied magnetic field using HTVSM.
summary: Magnetization curves obtained via HTVSM reveal distinct magnetic behaviors for the investigated alloys under a 3000 Oe field. FeCoNi displays a sharp reduction in ferromagnetism near the Curie temperature (Tc), whereas Fe30Co30Ni30Cr10-xMnx exhibits a more gradual decline. These experimental results provide critical insights into the thermal stability of magnetic properties.

caption: Ashby map illustrating the normalized effective Young’s modulus ⟨ E ⟩ / E as a function of relative density ρ ¯ for various metamaterials, incorporating experimental data from multiple literature sources.
summary: This Ashby plot displays the relationship between normalized effective Young’s modulus and relative density for a variety of metamaterials. By aggregating experimental data from several studies, the figure provides a comprehensive overview of mechanical performance scaling, allowing for a direct comparison of stiffness characteristics across different metamaterial architectures and densities.

caption: Vickers hardness values plotted against the distance from the top surface, overlaid with the corresponding Nb content measured within the dendritic cores.
summary: Vickers hardness values are plotted as a function of distance from the top surface, alongside the Nb content evolution in the dendritic cores. The data indicates that the hardness does not exhibit a trend as clearly defined or obvious as the Nb content evolution observed within the dendritic core regions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves illustrating the electrochemical response of the specimen.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves are depicted in panel (b) to evaluate the corrosion kinetics. These curves provide essential data for determining the corrosion potential (Ecorr) and corrosion current density (icorr), which are subsequently quantified and listed in Table 1 to characterize the material's resistance to electrochemical degradation.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the hybrid evolutionary algorithm (HEA) architecture, which integrates genetic programming for model structure optimization and differential evolution for parameter refinement.
summary: This flowchart depicts the hybrid evolutionary algorithm (HEA) framework. It demonstrates the integration of genetic programming, used to determine the optimal model structure, with differential evolution, which is employed to refine the model parameters. This dual-approach methodology ensures both structural integrity and precise parameter optimization within the computational model.

caption: Raman spectrum of the carbon dots (CDs) showing characteristic vibrational modes.
summary: The Raman spectrum of the carbon dots is presented in panel A. This spectroscopic analysis provides insight into the vibrational characteristics of the CDs, serving as a fundamental characterization of the material's structural properties as described in the study.

caption: 1H NMR spectra (400 MHz, 298 K, CDCl3) of AO and AAO, highlighting resonances at 5.36 and 5.28 ppm for AO and new acrylate group resonances between 6.50 and 5.70 ppm for AAO.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of AO features resonances at 5.36 and 5.28 ppm, assigned to fatty acid C=C protons and triglyceride methine protons. In contrast, the AAO spectrum reveals three new resonances between 6.50 and 5.70 ppm, corresponding to the successful incorporation of acrylate groups into the oil structure.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the Al6061 specimen subjected to direct aging, illustrating the compositional homogeneity following this specific thermal process.
summary: The elemental distribution map for the direct aged Al6061 specimen is presented here. This visualization illustrates the compositional state of the alloy after the direct aging process, allowing for an assessment of how this specific heat treatment influences the distribution of elements within the material matrix.

caption: Tafel polarization curves for AAO, Co, Ni, and Co–Ni alloy nanoarray electrodes measured in a 0.025 mol/L H2SO4 electrolyte solution to evaluate kinetic parameters.
summary: Tafel curves are presented for AAO, Co, Ni, and Co–Ni alloy nanoarrays to characterize their electrochemical kinetics. These plots provide insight into the hydrogen evolution reaction behavior of the different electrode materials when tested in a 0.025 mol/L H2SO4 solution, highlighting the catalytic differences between the pure metals and the alloy.

caption: Color-coded legend representing the relationship between Euler angles and grain orientation.
summary: This legend serves as the reference for the EBSD IPF maps, correlating specific colors to unique combinations of Euler angles. It enables the interpretation of grain orientations relative to the lattice in the associated maps, ensuring consistent identification of crystallographic orientations across all analyzed LPBF-316 L samples.

caption: Elemental distribution maps of the L3 layer region, detailing the chemical makeup and spatial arrangement of elements within this specific upper layer.
summary: Elemental mapping of the L3 layer region reveals the chemical composition and distribution of elements within this specific zone. These maps complement the structural details provided in panel d, facilitating a comprehensive understanding of the chemical evolution and phase formation within the L3 layer after the wetting test.

caption: Stress distribution map of polycrystalline Fe showing atoms with plastic strain exceeding 0.1.
summary: Polycrystalline Fe is visualized through an MD snapshot highlighting atoms with plastic strain greater than 0.1. The atoms are colored according to their local stress distribution, illustrating the relationship between plastic deformation and stress concentration in high-strain regions as part of the analysis of crack directionality.

caption: Secondary 3D view of the internal crack structure for a BGS-CFRCs specimen at a 0.2–0.4 frequency.
summary: This 3D reconstruction provides a secondary view of the internal crack structure within a BGS-CFRCs specimen tested at a 0.2–0.4 frequency. The visualization supports the finding that frequency variations effectively redistribute damage patterns in the width direction, offering a comprehensive look at the internal failure morphology of the composite.

caption: Ultraviolet–visible absorption spectra recorded for the GP hydrogel system following the addition of Allura Red AC dye.
summary: This UV-Vis spectrum shows the absorbance characteristics of the GP hydrogel after the introduction of Allura Red AC dye. The spectral data provides a quantitative measure of dye presence or transmission, supporting the visual observations of permeability and confirming the hydrogel's interaction with the dye molecules.

caption: 3D-CLSM surface morphology of HT-W NAB specimen after 1 hour of exposure to 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Surface morphology of the HT-W NAB specimen visualized using 3D-CLSM after 1 hour of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The specimen displays localized attack, confirming that the HT-W sample maintains a similar corrosion pattern to the W sample throughout the duration of the CPP experimental testing.

caption: 2D detector images captured at various processing times during the additive manufacturing of layer L20, showing the evolution of Debye–Scherrer rings.
summary: These 2D diffraction patterns illustrate the structural evolution during the printing of the 20th layer. At 5.06 seconds, an amorphous pattern indicates the presence of a liquid phase, alongside Debye–Scherrer rings originating from the powder and the previously deposited layer, capturing the dynamic solidification process in real-time.

caption: Impact response curves for RC laminates, RC interleaved with aluminum foils, and RC interleaved with aluminized Mylar, tested at 7.5 J and room temperature.
summary: This plot displays the impact response curves for three distinct laminate types: RC, RC interleaved with aluminum foils, and RC interleaved with aluminized Mylar. The tests were conducted at room temperature with an impact energy of 7.5 J to evaluate and compare the mechanical performance of these specific composite configurations.

caption: Theoretical and experimental RL curves for optimized complex GMSs with a configuration yielding two absorption peaks.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical and experimental RL curves for the optimized complex GMSs with the configuration #4#0#10(#14) 2, which results in two distinct absorption peaks. The data confirms the successful implementation of the design strategy for achieving specific multi-peak absorption characteristics in the GMS material.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺:Er³⁺-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after the third thermal cycle at 1000°C, demonstrating further stabilization of the emission profile and minimized defect contributions.
summary: Panel c shows CL spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 1000°C thermal treatment. The spectra exhibit further reduction in defect-related emissions compared to previous cycles. These findings confirm that higher temperature thermal treatment cycles promote the reduction of defects and amorphous regions, leading to more stable luminescence behavior.

caption: Summary table of ultimate tensile strength and percent elongation rate for 2Cr13 stainless steel under various experimental conditions.
summary: Tabulated data provides a concise summary of the ultimate tensile strength and percent elongation rate for 2Cr13 stainless steel. The table organizes these key mechanical metrics across different experimental conditions, allowing for a direct comparison of ductility and strength performance for the various samples tested in this study.

caption: Measured reflection coefficient of the 2.4 GHz reconfigurable patch antenna compared against Ansys HFSS simulation results, showing a resonance peak at 2.56 GHz with a maximum return loss of 31.30 dB.
summary: This plot displays the reflection coefficient for the 2.4 GHz antenna design. The measured data indicates an antenna resonance at 2.56 GHz, achieving a maximum return loss of 31.30 dB. This performance is compared directly against the simulated results obtained from Ansys HFSS to validate the antenna design accuracy.

caption: Thermal phase map plotting temperature gradient versus solidification velocity, demonstrating the transition from epitaxial growth to nucleated grains.
summary: This thermal phase map plots the temperature gradient against solidification velocity for all locations along the melt pool arc. It illustrates the transition from epitaxial to nucleated grain growth, with the blue shaded region representing the outer edge and the red shaded region representing the trailing center of the melt pool.

caption: Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) plot demonstrating the diagnostic capability of the CNN model in distinguishing between the four defect classes.
summary: The ROC plot visualizes the CNN model's diagnostic performance by plotting the true positive rate against the false positive rate for each defect category. This analysis confirms the model's effectiveness in identifying stringing, cracking, warping, and no-defect conditions, providing a robust measure of its classification sensitivity and specificity.

caption: Photocurrent versus reverse bias voltage characteristic curve measured under 1-mW 532-nm laser excitation, with an inset displaying the log-scale I-V response across varying excitation intensities.
summary: This I-V curve illustrates the photocurrent response to reverse bias voltage under 1-mW 532-nm laser excitation. The inset highlights deformations at high excitation intensities, such as 10 mW. Notable increases in photocurrent at 1, 3.5, 8.5, 12.5, and 17 V indicate the emergence of new electron transport paths.

caption: Reflected light intensity measured by the violet channel of a colorimetric device plotted against varying ALP concentrations.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between ALP concentration and reflected light intensity captured by the violet channel. Because the violet channel is complementary to yellow, the increasing yellow color on the PAD as ALP concentration rises leads to an exponential decrease in the measured violet light reflection.

caption: Magnetic entropy change -ΔSm plotted against temperature for the x = 1.0 alloy, focusing on the structural phase transition region under magnetic field changes up to 7 T.
summary: The temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change -ΔSm for the x = 1.0 alloy is shown here. Calculated for magnetic field changes up to 7 T using Eq. (1), the plot captures the entropy variations near the structural phase transition, facilitating the determination of the relative cooling power for this alloy.

caption: Effect of hydrogen (H) element on the model prediction accuracy for titanium alloy phase transformation points.
summary: This plot illustrates the influence of hydrogen on the model's predictive accuracy. As a beta-stable element, hydrogen is shown to reduce the beta transus temperature of titanium alloys. The visualization highlights how the presence of H specifically affects the model's output regarding phase transformation behavior in the studied alloy system.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the interaction effect of ironing flow and ironing speed on the surface roughness of FFF-printed samples.
summary: This contour plot visualizes the interaction between ironing flow and ironing speed regarding surface roughness in FFF samples. Optimal smoothing requires a matched combination of these parameters; tighter spacing facilitates even distribution of extra flow, whereas wider spacing reduces smoothing benefits and may induce defects if flow is excessive.

caption: Total magnetic moment of FeCoNiCr 1-x Al x calculated via first-principles methods, comparing the contributions of FCC and BCC phases.
summary: First-principles calculations of the total magnetic moment for FeCoNiCr 1-x Al x are displayed. The results indicate that the BCC phase consistently exhibits a higher magnetic moment than the FCC phase, explaining the sharp increase in measured saturation magnetization observed when the BCC phase emerges in Al0.75 and Al1 compositions.

caption: Post-experiment light spot distribution on the screen, reflecting the changes induced by the pre-treatment process.
summary: Following the pre-treatment experiment, this panel illustrates the modified light spot distribution as projected on the screen via DMD reflection. Comparing this to the initial state allows for the assessment of how the pre-treatment process has altered the optical reflection pattern within the experimental setup.

caption: Comparison of Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase fraction diagrams with HE-XRD measurements for ST and STA conditions at 496 °C and 790 °C.
summary: This panel compares thermodynamic equilibrium phase fraction diagrams with HE-XRD data for ST and STA conditions. At 496 °C, measured α and β fractions are compared against equilibrium values. At 790 °C, the β-phase measurement aligns with equilibrium. Discrepancies exist for the STA condition, where the measured 64% α-phase deviates from the predicted 75%.

caption: Coherent potential approximation (CPA) method representing the replacement of randomly positioned atoms with an effective medium.
summary: The CPA method is depicted here as a strategy to model alloy systems by replacing randomly distributed atoms with an effective medium. This approach allows for the self-consistent calculation of parameters, simplifying the complex atomic environment into a solvable model for studying impurity effects on APB energy.

caption: Projected density of states (pDOS) for Fe, Co, and Ni in FeCoNi, FeCoNiCu1.15, and V1.15FeCoNi alloys, showing spin-up and spin-down channels.
summary: This plot displays the pDOS for Fe, Co, and Ni across three multicomponent alloys. Analysis reveals that extra electrons from Cu fill Fe spin-up states, increasing mFe, while extra electrons in Co and Ni occupy spin-down states, leading to a decrease in their respective magnetic moments.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the as-deposited Mg-RE alloy, showing an average grain size of 18.30 ± 9.89 μm.
summary: The grain size distribution of the as-deposited Mg-RE alloy is presented in this histogram. Quantitative analysis indicates that the grains are randomly oriented in various crystal directions, with an average grain size of 18.30 ± 9.89 μm, characterizing the microstructure of the alloy prepared by the CMT-WAAM system.

caption: CALPHAD-calculated phase stability diagram for the Grad 2 sample at a height of z = 5.5 mm, illustrating phase behavior from 700 °C to 1500 °C.
summary: Calculated via the CALPHAD method, this diagram displays the phase stability for the Grad 2 sample at a height of 5.5 mm. The plot covers the temperature interval from 700 °C to 1500 °C, characterizing the expected phase composition at this height for the analyzed material.

caption: Summary of stress relaxation ratios calculated for PEEK samples across different infill patterns.
summary: This bar chart provides a comparative summary of the stress relaxation ratios for PEEK samples with varying infill patterns. The visualization serves to quantify the extent of stress dissipation observed in each sample, allowing for a direct assessment of how structural geometry impacts the material's ability to lose initial stress.

caption: Partial electronic density of states for the first neighboring atoms of the site exhibiting the lowest vacancy formation energy.
summary: This panel illustrates the partial electronic density of states (PDOS) for the first neighboring atoms of the site with the lowest vacancy formation energy. By analyzing these electronic states, the study investigates the orbital distribution changes associated with vacancy formation at this specific, energetically favorable atomic site.

caption: UV–Vis absorbance spectra comparing aqueous suspensions of pure FNF and FNF@AuNP, highlighting the characteristic Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) band of the gold nanoparticles.
summary: UV–Vis spectroscopy of the FNF@AuNP suspension demonstrates the characteristic Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) band typical of gold nanoparticles. This spectral profile corroborates the successful incorporation of AuNPs into the fibroin matrix, aligning with established data for similar fibroin-AuNP materials and confirming the optical signature of the nanohybrid.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for Ti-xCu alloys, demonstrating spontaneous passive behavior and enabling the determination of corrosion current density and passive current density.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the LPBF-produced Ti-xCu alloys reveal that all samples exhibit spontaneous passive behaviors. These curves are utilized to extract critical electrochemical parameters, specifically the corrosion current density and the passive current density, which characterize the corrosion resistance of the various alloy compositions.

caption: Side view of the diamond cell structure used as a reference model for scaffold fabrication.
summary: The side view of the diamond cell structure serves as the baseline reference for comparing the geometry of fabricated scaffolds. This model provides the structural foundation for evaluating the dimensions and potential distortions of the green printed parts produced in subsequent experimental steps.

caption: Chronopotentiometric overpotential versus time (η-t) stability curves recorded at a constant geometric current density of -10 mA cm-2 for nanoNi-P op and CNT/nanoNi-P op electrodes.
summary: The η-t stability curves illustrate the long-term performance of the electrodes under a constant geometric current density of -10 mA cm-2. The CNT/nanoNi-P op modified electrode demonstrates high stability during the hydrogen evolution reaction, maintaining consistent performance over the recorded time period compared to the nanoNi-P op electrode.

caption: Comparison of physically-based quantitative strengthening mechanism analysis versus experimentally measured yield strength for IN718 arc-based DED specimens in vertical and horizontal orientations.
summary: This plot compares the predicted yield strength from a physically-based strengthening model against experimental measurements for IN718 arc-based DED samples. The analysis highlights that precipitation strengthening, particularly γ′′ coherency strengthening, is the primary mechanism governing the final mechanical strength of the material across both vertical and horizontal build directions.

caption: Reliability index of the additively manufactured titanium alloy wheel hub plotted against the number of impact cycles under comprehensive braking impact conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the reliability index of an additively manufactured titanium alloy wheel hub subjected to comprehensive braking impact. The data demonstrates that the reliability index exhibits a downward trend as the number of impact cycles increases, indicating a gradual degradation in the structural integrity of the wheel hub over time.

caption: Immunofluorescent staining of CD31 in HUVECs cultured with PCN membrane, highlighting endothelial marker expression.
summary: Immunofluorescent staining of CD31 in HUVECs cultured with PCN membrane reveals endothelial marker expression. The PCN group displays a 1.4-fold higher fluorescence intensity compared to the PC group, indicating that the PCN membrane significantly enhances the angiogenic potential of HUVECs through increased CD31 expression.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy micrograph illustrating the localized depletion of the γ″ phase in the immediate vicinity of a δ phase precipitate.
summary: This TEM micrograph provides visual evidence of the microstructural evolution occurring within the material. It specifically highlights the formation of a γ″ phase depleted zone surrounding the δ phase. This localized depletion is a direct consequence of the δ phase formation process, demonstrating the interaction between these two distinct phases.

caption: Tyrosinase-modulating activity of bxEPS and bxEPS-N at 0.2% (w/v), evaluated against aqueous kojic acid solutions as positive controls.
summary: Anti-tyrosinase or tyrosinase-enhancing activity of bxEPS and bxEPS-N was assessed at 0.2% (w/v) concentrations. Aqueous kojic acid solutions were used as positive controls. As shown in Fig. 3c, these experiments were performed in triplicate with deviation, identifying tyrosinase activity-promoting functions in the purified bxEPS-N sample.

caption: AFM image of a C60 (16 nm)/Py (15 nm) bilayer, demonstrating the surface characteristics of a thicker Py layer covering the C60 film.
summary: This AFM image displays the surface of a C60 (16 nm)/Py (15 nm) bilayer. By increasing the Py thickness to 15 nm, the surface morphology reflects the characteristics of the thicker Py layer as it fully covers the underlying C60 film, providing insight into the bilayer growth dynamics.

caption: Open circuit potential (EOCP) evolution for the heat-treated (HT) NAB alloy immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution over an extended duration.
summary: The EOCP curve for the HT-NAB alloy illustrates the electrochemical response of the heat-treated material during extended immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These results align with EIS findings, indicating that the observed potential trends accurately reflect the corrosion characteristics of the heat-treated NAB alloy.

caption: Comparison of the highest deposition rates (DRs) achieved for various Ti wire configurations, including 1.2 mm, 2.4 mm, and dual wire setups.
summary: This bar chart displays the highest deposition rates achieved for different Ti wire configurations. The 1.2 mm Ti wire, 2.4 mm Ti wire, and dual Ti wire configurations reached deposition rates of 1.224 kg/h, 1.53 kg/h, and 1.65 kg/h, respectively, demonstrating the efficiency of the employed wire feeding approach.

caption: Permutation-based feature importance analysis for the XG-2 model trained on dataset D2.
summary: Permutation-based feature importance analysis for the XG-2 model trained on dataset D2. This plot identifies the specific features that significantly impact the classification performance of the XG-2 classifier. It provides a clear visualization of the most informative content used by the model to achieve its predictive results.

caption: Dark field TEM image of MHA surface microstructure after CSFPB at 1.5 MPa for 60 seconds, with an inset grain size histogram.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging of the MHA surface after 1.5 MPa CSFPB treatment for 60 seconds provides insight into the grain morphology. The inset grain size histogram quantifies the distribution of the fragmented grains, characterizing the microstructural state resulting from the increased impact pressure applied during the surface SPD process.

caption: Tabulated estimates of viscosity and static yield stress derived from the rheological measurements of mortar samples at different hydration times.
summary: Presented in this table are the estimated viscosity and static yield stress values for the mortar samples. These parameters were calculated based on the rheological stress-strain data obtained at various hydration time intervals, providing a quantitative summary of the material's flow characteristics and resistance to initial deformation.

caption: Initial calibrated yield surface of bulk IN718 represented as an elliptical fit passing through four distinct experimental yield strength points: uniaxial tension, uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and confined compression.
summary: The initial calibrated yield surface for bulk IN718 is constructed by fitting an ellipse to four distinct experimental data points. These points represent the yield strengths measured under uniaxial tension, uniaxial compression, biaxial compression, and confined compression, establishing the MVHM yield surface model as described in the study.

caption: External quantum efficiency (EQE) spectra for the perovskite/Si tandem device, detailing the individual subcell contributions and the overall reflection spectra.
summary: The photocurrent contribution from each subcell of the perovskite/Si tandem device is further analysed by external quantum efficiency (EQE). This measurement provides insight into the spectral response of the individual subcells and the overall optical reflection characteristics of the monolithic tandem architecture under simulated sunlight.

caption: Synchronized data acquisition interface displaying concurrent infrared thermal imaging, optical camera feeds, and real-time force/torque measurements during sample machining.
summary: This screenshot demonstrates the system's synchronized data acquisition capability during the hybrid machining process. It displays a multi-modal dataset including infrared and optical camera images alongside real-time force and torque values. This integration allows for comprehensive monitoring of the manufacturing process through simultaneous capture of diverse sensor data streams.

caption: Weight loss percentage plotted against temperature for the 4D printed composites, illustrating the thermal degradation profile.
summary: This panel displays the weight loss versus temperature thermograms for the 4D printed composites. The data indicates that the thermal stability of the various prints remains largely consistent, with insignificant differences observed between the 100% BPR print and the 95% BPR 5% BBZ 15% PPy composite formulation.

caption: STEM-EDS line profile acquired across the multiple α-β-α-β-α interfaces.
summary: STEM-EDS line profile analysis across the α-β-α-β-α interfaces in the 920 RQ condition maps the elemental variations. This spectroscopic data quantifies the chemical partitioning across the multiple phase boundaries, illustrating how the rapid quench process influences the local composition and chemical homogeneity of the refined α and β phases.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetization for the HT sample measured under a 0.05 T magnetic field, including an inset showing the first derivative of the magnetization-temperature curve.
summary: The temperature-dependent magnetization curve for the HT sample, measured under a 0.05 T field, exhibits negligible magnetic hysteresis during heating and cooling cycles. The inset displays the first derivative of the magnetization-temperature curve, providing insight into the magnetic transition behavior of the material.

caption: Nav Camera view of the as-built tensile specimen showing the overall sample geometry prior to detailed microscopic inspection.
summary: This panel displays the as-built tensile specimen as captured by the SEM Nav Camera. The image provides a macroscopic overview of the sample's field of view, serving as the initial reference point for the subsequent microscopic characterization of the specimen's surface and interface structures.

caption: Temperature field distribution in the molten pool under a laser power of 350 eV/ps.
summary: Displayed is the temperature field distribution within the molten pool at a laser power of 350 eV/ps. The simulation highlights the thermal response of the material under this specific power condition, contributing to the overall analysis of how laser power dictates the molten pool dynamics in Cu50Zr50.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectra of trypsin (1 g/L) at 298 K with increasing SL/trypsin mass ratios ranging from 0 to 0.8 g/L, showing a characteristic emission peak at 327 nm.
summary: Trypsin exhibits a strong emission peak at 327 nm when excited at 280 nm. At 298 K, the fluorescence intensity of trypsin gradually decreases as the concentration of SL increases, indicating that interactions with SL molecules lead to fluorescence quenching of the trypsin protein.

caption: Vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) hysteresis loops for samples N1 through N13, which underwent field heat treatment (FHT), compared against sample N14, which was processed without FHT.
summary: The VSM hysteresis loops illustrate the magnetic performance of various samples from Experiment 1. Samples N1 to N13, subjected to field heat treatment, are contrasted with sample N14, which did not receive this treatment, highlighting the influence of FHT on the magnetic behavior of the materials tested.

caption: Schematic representation of the two-step compounding process utilized for the fabrication of PLA/oil palm fiber (OPF) composite filaments.
summary: This schematic illustrates the two-step fabrication process employed by Sekar et al. to produce PLA/OPF composite filaments. The diagram outlines the sequential compounding stages necessary for integrating oil palm fibers into the PLA matrix, providing a clear visual overview of the manufacturing methodology used for these specific composite materials.

caption: Y-Z cross-sectional view of the melt pool simulated at 130 W and 0.4 m/s, illustrating the effect of increased scanning speed.
summary: Doubling the laser scanning speed to 0.4 m/s while maintaining 130 W power alters the melt pool geometry and solidification front. The green dashed lines indicate the resulting widths of the equiaxed and columnar grain zones, demonstrating how processing parameters influence the transition from columnar to equiaxed grain structures.

caption: Rate performance comparison showing areal capacity versus current density for D-3DP and N-3DP electrodes.
summary: The rate capability of the D-3DP electrode is evaluated across increasing current densities from 0.1 to 1 mA cm⁻². The D-3DP electrode achieves high areal capacities of 3.11, 2.98, 2.71, and 2.04 mAh cm⁻², demonstrating superior rate performance compared to the N-3DP counterpart.

caption: Dilatometric curves showing the elongation (ΔL) of sample S3 as a function of temperature during three consecutive heating runs (I, II, and III) at a rate of 15 °C/min up to 1000 °C.
summary: This dilatometric analysis illustrates the thermal expansion behavior of sample S3 during three repeated heating cycles at 15 °C/min. The data reveals that elongation occurs consistently with increasing temperature. A maximum discrepancy of approximately 0.12 µm between the three experimental runs is observed at the peak temperature of 1000 °C.

caption: AFM topography of Ni95-Fe5 anode film displaying a percolating network of alloy particles.
summary: The Ni95-Fe5 anode film is visualized via AFM, revealing a surface structure composed of a partly percolating network of alloy particles. This morphology is consistent with the behavior observed under anodic bias, demonstrating how the alloy film organizes itself into a network structure under these specific electrochemical conditions.

caption: Residual stress profiles measured by neutron diffraction along the Tube-Top joint for as-built (AB) and heat-treated (HT) samples across three primary directions.
summary: Neutron diffraction analysis of the Tube-Top joint provides the residual stress components for as-built and heat-treated conditions. The results demonstrate that stress mitigation following heat treatment is inconsistent across the section, as evidenced by the independent axial, radial, and tangential stress components measured at various locations along the tube.

caption: Topography and contact potential difference images of the as-polished 1050 sample obtained via scanning Kelvin probe force microscopy.
summary: Topography and contact potential difference images for the as-polished 1050 sample are displayed, captured using scanning Kelvin probe force microscopy. These images reveal the surface morphology alongside the local electronic potential variations, which are essential for understanding the electrochemical surface properties and potential differences between the constituent phases of the material.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of the hydrogel contact lenses after immersion in a 1.5 mM gold precursor concentration.
summary: This absorption spectrum characterizes the optical properties of the hydrogel lens following immersion in a 1.5 mM gold precursor solution. The data contributes to the comparative analysis of how varying precursor concentrations influence the localized surface plasmon resonance and overall optical performance of the gold-loaded hydrogel contact lenses.

caption: Hierarchical dendrogram derived from the median waveform of each multiplet in time of arrivals for dataset n° 3 s 1.
summary: Representing the hierarchical agglomeration of acoustic multiplets, this dendrogram employs the median waveform of each multiplet in time of arrivals as the representative method. A high dissimilarity threshold, marked by a black dashed line, is applied to dataset n° 3 s 1 to categorize the data into distinct colored clusters.

caption: Plastic strain range measured from the mid-life hysteresis loop as a function of cycles to failure for Alloy 718plus at 450 °C and 550 °C.
summary: The plastic strain range derived from mid-life hysteresis loops is plotted against the number of cycles to failure for Alloy 718plus. These results encompass tests performed at both 450 °C and 550 °C, highlighting the influence of plastic deformation on the fatigue life of the material under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the influence of laser scanning strategies on the hardness values of batch 2 tube walls.
summary: This bar chart displays the hardness measurements for batch 2 tubes, specifically investigating how different laser scanning strategies affect mechanical properties. The data highlights the direct correlation between the chosen scanning method and the resulting tube wall hardness, providing a quantitative comparison between the continuous-scanned and contour-scanned build strategies.

caption: WDS concentration map of the interface in sample #8, an unsuccessful joint, showing the spatial distribution of elements.
summary: WDS concentration map of the interface in sample #8, an unsuccessful joint, showing the spatial distribution of elements. The WDS concentration profiles of the sample #8 are illustrated in the figure. Carbon was observed to be concentrated in the black agglomerations within the interface region of the unsuccessful joint.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spot analysis performed at point C.
summary: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis at point C in the S4 sample provides localized compositional information. This analysis is essential for tracking the reduction of Re content, which drops to 18.0% in the S4 sample after 1140 °C treatment, reflecting the significant chemical changes occurring during the high-temperature processing stages.

caption: Cyclic performance of Ni91Ir9/CeO2 catalyst during N2H4·H2O decomposition in 0.5 M NaOH at 50 °C, showing the evolution of catalytic activity over 15 cycles.
summary: This plot illustrates the cyclic stability of the Ni91Ir9/CeO2 catalyst during the decomposition of hydrazine hydrate in an alkaline environment at 50 °C. While the catalyst maintains 100% hydrogen selectivity throughout 15 cycles, the experimental data indicates a gradual decline in catalytic activity as the cycle number increases.

caption: Phase angle Bode plots derived from impedance measurements of Al-Mg-Sc-Zr alloys in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Phase angle Bode plots display the frequency-dependent phase shift for Al-4.2Mg-0.4Sc-0.2Zr alloys manufactured by LPBF. These plots are part of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis conducted in 3.5 wt% NaCl, helping to characterize the capacitive and resistive behavior of the alloy surface across different island size configurations.

caption: In-situ synchrotron GI-XRD pseudo-color plot for the 26Co alloy during heating at 100 °C/min and isothermal oxidation at 800 °C, showing the evolution of corundum and spinel oxide reflections.
summary: This pseudo-color plot displays in-situ synchrotron GI-XRD data for the 26Co alloy during a 100 °C/min heating ramp and 800 °C isothermal oxidation. Upon reaching 800 °C, indicated by the dashed line, reflections corresponding to corundum-type and spinel-type oxides are immediately detected, illustrating the rapid onset of surface oxidation.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles at 0.5 mA cm⁻² for three micro-supercapacitors connected in parallel compared to a single device, highlighting the increased discharge duration.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves at 0.5 mA cm⁻² compare three parallel-connected micro-supercapacitors to a single unit. The parallel configuration results in a discharge duration approximately three times longer than the single device, attributed to an increase in total capacitance from 37 mF to 133 mF.

caption: Nyquist impedance curves illustrating the electrochemical response of V2 cladding alloy and Q235 steel.
summary: Nyquist impedance curves are displayed for both V2 and Q235 steel specimens. These plots provide essential data regarding the electrochemical impedance behavior of the materials, serving as a basis for fitting the equivalent circuit model to characterize the interface properties and corrosion resistance of the tested steel samples.

caption: Workflow of the accelerated Monte Carlo simulation utilizing an f-NN energy model, starting from quasi-random structures and transitioning from 10 initial DFT steps to the f-NN model for efficient convergence to energetically stable configurations.
summary: This figure illustrates an accelerated Monte Carlo simulation strategy for materials modeling. By initializing with quasi-random structures and performing only 10 DFT steps before switching to an f-NN energy model, the process achieves energetically stable configurations more efficiently. This approach demonstrates the utility of the f-NN model in computational materials science.

caption: Calculated subband structure of the semiconductor heterostructure at an applied bias of 5.3 V, illustrating the spatial distribution of electron wave functions across quantum wells.
summary: This band structure diagram at 5.3 V highlights the spatial distribution of electron wave functions within the quantum wells. The Γ31 wave function exhibits significant probability density near the X72 state, while the Γ state induces wave function interference with Γ21, effectively shifting the electron wave function peak toward the Q5 region.

caption: Decomposition of yield stress contributions from distinct deformation mechanisms in wrought Alloy 718, highlighting the transition from precipitation hardening to solid-solution strengthening as temperatures exceed the solubility limit.
summary: This panel illustrates the contribution of various deformation mechanisms to the yield stress of wrought Alloy 718 under the conditions specified in panel a. It demonstrates that precipitation hardening effects are eliminated above the solubility limit of the precipitates, allowing dissolved Nb in the matrix to contribute to solid-solution strengthening.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of TPU/coumarin composites showing a broad absorption band between 200 and 400 nm.
summary: The UV-Vis absorption spectra of TPU/coumarin composites are presented, revealing a broad absorption band spanning the 200 to 400 nm range. This characteristic spectral feature is attributed to the inherent UV absorption properties of 7-hydroxy-4-methylcoumarin, demonstrating the effective incorporation and optical activity of the coumarin within the TPU matrix.

caption: Pressure distribution profile along the extrusion direction for the composite material.
summary: This panel presents the pressure distribution profile along the extrusion direction. A marked reduction in extrusion pressure is observed as the nozzle diameter increases, which aligns with established findings in literature. This indicates that nozzle geometry significantly impacts the pressure requirements during the extrusion of these composite materials.

caption: Top view (xy plane) of the thin plate lattice, displaying cross-sectional slices at depths of 7.56, 13.14, and 18.72 mm.
summary: The top view (xy plane) of the TPL structure allows for a detailed examination of channel uniformity and potential powder occlusion. By observing cross-sections at 7.56, 13.14, and 18.72 mm, the analysis confirms the internal channel quality and verifies the absence of significant powder accumulation within the lattice geometry.

caption: Optical microstructure of the Al–10Ni alloy produced by CDS mixing eutectic Al–6Ni and hypereutectic Al-xNi alloys at a mass ratio of 1:2.
summary: This optical micrograph reveals the microstructure of an Al–10Ni alloy processed by CDS using a 1:2 mass ratio of eutectic and hypereutectic precursors. The resulting structural refinement is a key outcome of the composite process, which synergistically controls nucleation and growth to enhance material properties.

caption: Calculated ultimate tensile load as a function of transverse in-situ tensile strength for specimen A30-6.
summary: This plot demonstrates the relationship between in-situ strength and ultimate tensile load for specimen A30-6. By adjusting the transverse in-situ tensile strength, the simulation produces a linearly increasing ultimate tensile strength curve. The calculation utilizes an allowable error of 2e−4 to model the mechanical response of the material.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectrum acquired from point 3# within the Fe-Al-Si intermetallic phase.
summary: Point 3# provides compositional data for the Fe-Al-Si intermetallic phase formed during corrosion. Analysis of this spectrum shows a specific elemental ratio that, when compared to points 2# and 4#, demonstrates the gradual compositional shift in Fe, Al, and Si content characteristic of the corrosion-induced IMC layers at the interface.

caption: In vitro wound healing assay of HUVECs, scale bar 200 µm.
summary: This optical micrograph illustrates the in vitro wound healing assay performed on HUVECs. The 3DSC group demonstrated the best performance in these assays compared to other experimental groups, highlighting the scaffold's superior ability to promote cell migration and wound closure in a controlled laboratory environment.

caption: Current versus time transients recorded by manually chopping the irradiation at different wavelengths to demonstrate stationary anodic photocurrent.
summary: Current versus time transients obtained through manual chopping of irradiation confirm the n-type semiconductor behavior of the anodic film. The observation of stationary anodic photocurrent during these measurements provides clear evidence of the electronic response of the oxide layer grown on the 3D printed Ti6Al4V samples.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the deformation behavior observed in the 3D-printed carbon fiber skin on the bottom surface of the sandwich structure during impact loading.
summary: This schematic illustrates the mechanical response of the 3D-printed carbon fiber skin located on the bottom surface of the sandwich structure during impact. It provides a visual representation of the deformation mechanisms that result in the back-surface displacement signatures recorded during the dynamic loading scenarios described in the study.

caption: Local analysis of fatigue strength under pure shear loading for gas pores, exhibiting an anisotropy factor of λ = 1.29.
summary: Local spherical plot analysis for gas pores under pure shear loading reveals an anisotropy factor of 1.29. This value serves as the local reference point for evaluating fatigue strength. Similar to LoF defects, this local measurement provides the initial basis for assessing how non-local analysis influences the observed anisotropy in fatigue.

caption: Atomic configuration of the FeCrNi solid solution model containing 1 at.% oxygen atoms.
summary: Represented here is the FeCrNi solid solution model doped with 1 at.% oxygen. This atomic structure is one of the three initial configurations established to investigate the effects of oxygen content on the mechanical behavior of SS316 during molecular dynamics simulations of nanoindentation.

caption: 3DAP reconstruction of the HT2000 sample aged at 800 °C for 2000 h, highlighting the evolved elemental partition between the γ and γ′ phases.
summary: Representing the HT2000 sample aged at 800 °C for 2000 h, this 3DAP reconstruction reveals the evolved elemental partitioning between the γ and γ′ phases. The visualization demonstrates the structural changes occurring within the material after prolonged thermal exposure compared to the initial state.

caption: Resistance measurements of the NiFe-SiO2 nanocomposite obtained immediately after receipt, comparing two distinct measurement configurations.
summary: This plot displays the electrical resistance characteristics of NiFe-SiO2 nanocomposite samples as measured immediately upon receipt. The data encompasses two different measurement configurations, providing a baseline assessment of the material's electronic behavior. These measurements serve to characterize the initial state of the nanocomposite structures before any further experimental processing.

caption: Calculated phase fractions for NiTi samples processed at 120 J/mm³ VED H, featuring 3rd-order polynomial trendlines for B2 and B19' phases and a reduction in NiTi2 phase content at higher ageing temperatures.
summary: Representing NiTi samples processed at 120 J/mm³ VED H, this plot shows the phase fraction distribution at room temperature. The B19' phase is dominant, while B2 and B19' trends are fitted with 3rd-order polynomials. Additionally, the NiTi2 phase fraction decreases at higher ageing temperatures, consistent with the observed material evolution.

caption: Nano-hardness distribution derived from Vickers scale measurements across the 0°, 90°, and 67° samples.
summary: Nano-hardness values derived from the Vickers scale are plotted for the three samples. The 67° sample displays the largest bulk hardness at probe 3, correlating with observed cutting edge damage. Conversely, the 0° and 90° samples show distinct hardening effects near the cut surfaces compared to the 67° sample.

caption: Storage modulus (E′) curves as a function of temperature for pure PLA, PLA + EtLa, and PLA-based nanocomposites reinforced with cCNC.
summary: The storage modulus (E′) curves for PLA, PLA + EtLa, and cCNC-reinforced nanocomposites are presented as a function of temperature. All samples exhibit a significant decrease in E′ within the 60–80 °C range, which corresponds to the glass transition temperature (Tg) of the PLA matrix.

caption: Time evolution of the critical ice-forming temperature functions Ta (blue) and Tr (red) in degrees Celsius over 5 Myr.
summary: These temperature functions, Ta and Tr, are plotted over 5 Myr to show the critical ice-forming thresholds. The use of these ramp functions facilitates the observed transition in the system's period and amplitude at 1 Myr BP, as evidenced by the corresponding trajectory and maximum ice extent.

caption: Shear strength of C/C-GH3230-(C-MN)-Ti joints evaluated across a range of elevated temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the high-temperature shear resistance of C/C-GH3230-(C-MN)-Ti joints, which is a critical performance index for their application in high-temperature environments. The data demonstrates how the shear strength of these joints evolves as the testing temperature varies, providing essential insights into the mechanical stability of the joint interface.

caption: 3D-Heisenberg model fit for the GdDyErAlFe high-entropy amorphous alloy.
summary: The 3D-Heisenberg model (β=0.365, γ=1.336) is applied to the GdDyErAlFe alloy in this panel. By plotting M^(1/β) versus (μ0H/M)^(1/γ), the graph characterizes the ferromagnetic system's behavior at various temperatures, illustrating the statistical fit of the Heisenberg model to the experimental magnetic data.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis performed on the sample sintered at 1500 ºC, corresponding to the region shown in panel (e).
summary: This EDS spectrum provides the elemental composition for the sample sintered at 1500 ºC. By analyzing the region corresponding to the high-resolution SEM image in panel (e), this data helps elucidate the chemical nature of the micro-morphology and supports the investigation into the material's density and shrinkage mechanisms.

caption: Anderson-Durling residual normality test results for the Ra model.
summary: The Anderson-Durling normality test for the Ra model demonstrates a p-value exceeding 0.05. This statistical result confirms that the model effectively captures the physical experimental data, validating the stochastic nature of the fit as described in the study's analysis of model performance and experimental consistency.

caption: Schematic representation of the crystallographic crack length L in the Kb1 specimen, highlighting three specific crack instances (L1, L2, and L3) along the crack path.
summary: This schematic illustrates the crystallographic crack length L in the Kb1 specimen, defined as the maximum distance from the transition point to specific crack instances. The white arrow indicates the evaluation path for L, which is measured in 3D space despite the 2D projection shown, facilitating the calculation of crystallographic fatigue crack growth rates.

caption: Average tensile properties of selected CoCrMo specimens, including yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to fracture.
summary: Average tensile properties for selected CoCrMo specimens are summarized, specifically highlighting yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to fracture. These values facilitate a comparison of mechanical performance across different process parameters, consistent with similar findings reported in literature for CoCrMo tensile samples produced via additive manufacturing.

caption: Absorption coefficient curve for the TPMS structure optimized for a target frequency of 700 Hz.
summary: This plot illustrates the absorption coefficient of the TPMS structure specifically optimized for 700 Hz. The curve demonstrates the frequency-dependent acoustic performance, highlighting the peak absorption efficiency achieved by the graded porosity design at the intended target frequency within the analyzed spectral range.

caption: Phase–temperature contour plot illustrating the evolution of detected phases during the second tempering step, with intensity mapped according to the color scale in (g).
summary: This contour plot captures the phase evolution during the second tempering step. By monitoring the diffraction peak intensities, it reveals the stability and transformation of phases within the tool steel as it transitions from the 1x to the 2x tempered state under the specified thermal profile.

caption: Tafel plots derived from LSV curves at 1600 rpm in 0.1 M KOH, showing kinetic slopes of 67, 55, and 61 mV/dec for PtFe, PtCo, and PtNi samples, respectively.
summary: Tafel plots for PtFe, PtCo, and PtNi samples were generated from LSV curves at 1600 rpm in 0.1 M KOH to evaluate ORR kinetics. The results indicate Tafel slopes of 67, 55, and 61 mV per decade for PtFe, PtCo, and PtNi, respectively, highlighting the influence of composition on electrochemical performance.

caption: Thermal analysis profiles obtained via DSC for neat PBAT and composites containing WPL-DH biofillers, recorded in a nitrogen environment.
summary: Thermal analysis profiles obtained via DSC for neat PBAT and composites containing WPL-DH biofillers, recorded in a nitrogen environment. These curves allow for the comparison of thermal characteristics between the pure polymer and the WPL-DH reinforced composites, highlighting the impact of different agro-waste fillers on the material's thermal stability.

caption: FCCxyz unit cell topology fabricated from AlSi10Mg alloy using investment casting.
summary: Depicted is an FCCxyz unit cell topology structure, which is part of the sample set fabricated via investment casting of AlSi10Mg alloy. The image illustrates the successful realization of this specific lattice architecture, demonstrating the structural integrity and geometric precision achieved through the casting process for this material system.

caption: Surface potential map of the as-built GZ112K alloy showing the potential distribution around Gd2O3 oxides.
summary: Surface potential mapping of the as-built GZ112K alloy reveals the electrochemical signature of Gd2O3 oxides. This map, paired with the topography in panel (d), demonstrates the significant potential contrast between these oxide particles and the α-Mg matrix, which is a key factor in the alloy's overall corrosion performance.

caption: Cross-sectional temperature and grain distribution at 0.4 ms, illustrating the evolution of the melt pool as solidification progresses.
summary: At 0.4 ms, the cross-sectional view reveals the ongoing evolution of the melt pool. As solidification progresses through cooling, the melt pool depth begins to decrease. The temperature distribution remains coupled with the grain structure, reflecting the thermal history of the material during the laser processing simulation.

caption: Equilibrium phase volume fractions as a function of temperature for the Fe–Co–Cr alloy system.
summary: Utilizing JMatPro software, this panel presents the calculated equilibrium phase volume fractions for the Fe–Co–Cr alloy. The graph maps the temperature-dependent phase distribution, allowing for the identification of phase stability regions and the relative amounts of constituent phases present in the alloy throughout the specified temperature range.

caption: Time-dependent pH modulation response of PANI in 0.1 M NaCl solution over five consecutive acidification-regeneration cycles, where gray regions denote acidification at +0.4 V for 300 s and white regions represent regeneration at -0.2 V for 600 s.
summary: This plot illustrates the electrochemical reversibility of PANI-induced pH modulation across five distinct cycles. By alternating between an acidification potential of +0.4 V and a regeneration potential of -0.2 V in a 0.1 M NaCl solution, the material demonstrates consistent and repeatable performance throughout the entire testing duration.

caption: Cooling reversal curves for the Ni50Mn34In16 Heusler alloy sample measured under a constant applied field of 1 T.
summary: This panel displays the cooling reversal curves for the Ni50Mn34In16 Heusler alloy. The data was collected under a constant applied magnetic field of 1 T. These curves serve as the primary experimental input for calculating the standard cooling TFORC distributions and subsequent loop reconstructions presented later in the figure.

caption: Validation loss curves for ELBO and regression, demonstrating training progress and the early-stopping mechanism triggered after 25 epochs of stagnation at 278 total epochs.
summary: Validation loss metrics, specifically ELBO and regression loss, are plotted to monitor model convergence. The training process incorporates an early-stopping criterion, which successfully halts optimization after 25 epochs of no improvement, concluding at 278 epochs. This ensures the model avoids overfitting while maintaining optimal performance for fatigue feature reconstruction.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the EB-DED fabricated NAB alloy superimposed on an image quality grayscale, where white and black lines denote high-angle and low-angle grain boundaries, respectively.
summary: Inverse pole figure mapping of the EB-DED fabricated NAB alloy reveals that the crystals display no distinct preferred orientation. The microstructure consists primarily of nearly equiaxed grains. High-angle grain boundaries are marked by white lines, while low-angle grain boundaries are indicated by black lines, providing a clear visualization of the grain structure.

caption: Spin-polarized d-orbital partial density of states for a Cr atom and its nearest neighbor Ni atom in Ni106CrVa, showing spin-up and spin-down components with resonant hybridization peaks.
summary: Panel b presents the spin-polarized d-orbital partial density of states for Cr and Ni atoms in Ni106CrVa, including spin-up and spin-down components. The inset illustrates the charge density difference. The gain in exchange energy results in a weakening of the bond and a decrease in the interaction energy.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of a Ni3Si precipitate accompanied by a compositional line scan.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the precipitate is paired with an EDS line scan to characterize the chemical composition. The analysis confirms that these nano-precipitates are significantly enriched in nickel and silicon, identifying them as Ni3Si phases within the alloy microstructure, consistent with the observed precipitate morphology.

caption: Dislocation network morphology at 2.4% strain, where black arrows indicate dislocations bypassing networks and shearing from the gamma phase into the gamma prime phase.
summary: At 2.4% strain, the MD snapshot captures the advanced stage of deformation. Dislocations are observed bypassing the interfacial networks and shearing from the gamma phase into the gamma prime phase, as highlighted by black arrows. This confirms the active mechanism of dislocation transmission across the phase boundaries under continued loading.

caption: Hydrogen micro-print (HMT) image of the as-built specimen showing Ag nanoparticle enrichment at the columnar dendrite walls, particularly near Laves phases.
summary: The HMT result for the as-built specimen reveals the hydrogen trapping behavior associated with the dendrite structure. Specifically, Ag nanoparticles are observed to be enriched at the columnar dendrite walls, with a notable concentration in the vicinity of Laves phases, indicating these regions act as effective hydrogen trapping sites.

caption: Evolution of measured material skeleton volume across different sample datasets.
summary: This plot illustrates the measured material skeleton volume for various sample datasets. During the sintering process, the total material volume exhibits a slight increase of 12.6%, rising from approximately 3.07E+08 µm³ to 3.46E+08 µm³. This volumetric expansion is particularly pronounced in samples subjected to sintering temperatures exceeding 1300 °C.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) thermographs of matrix and fiber filaments measured from 0 °C to 1000 °C, highlighting degradation stages between 400 °C and 600 °C.
summary: TGA thermographs for matrix and fiber filaments are presented from 0 °C to 1000 °C. Filaments exhibit degradation between 400 °C and 500 °C, with Kevlar showing extended degradation up to 600 °C. Onyx displays significant mass loss at 462 °C, indicating a composition of approximately 17% short carbon fiber and 83% Nylon.

caption: Tensile strength and modulus of elasticity plotted against varying filling angles for composite fabrications.
summary: This plot displays the tensile strength and modulus of elasticity for composite samples across different filling angles. The experimental results demonstrate that the optimal mechanical properties, including peak tensile performance, are achieved specifically at a filling angle of 0°, indicating a strong dependency of tensile behavior on the internal fabrication orientation.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the determination of apparent activation energies for creep behavior at a constant stress of 50.8 MPa across all investigated samples.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the creep behavior of various materials at a constant stress of 50.8 MPa to determine their apparent activation energies. The data indicates that the 1 vol% 50 nm-SiCp-AMC exhibits significantly higher activation energies compared to other materials, highlighting the unique strengthening role of nanoscale reinforcement.

caption: Face-centered cubic unit cell with an integrated Z-axis strut, denoted as FCCZ.
summary: The FCCZ unit cell is depicted here, featuring a face-centered cubic arrangement augmented with a Z-axis strut. As referenced in the study, this specific configuration is one of the primary unit cells employed to analyze the structural properties and mechanical behavior of the materials under investigation.

caption: Hybrid morphology of the SCA arc structure.
summary: Panel (d) presents the SCA arc shape as it assumes a hybrid morphology. This instance demonstrates the versatility of the arc structure when powered by the CC power supply, showcasing a distinct configuration compared to the integrated, separated, or partially linked states observed in the other panels.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparing collagen (Col) and methacrylated collagen (ColMA), highlighting new acrylic proton peaks at 5.3 and 5.6 ppm.
summary: Structural integrity of collagen was verified via 1H NMR spectroscopy. The ColMA spectrum exhibits new acrylic proton peaks at 5.3 and 5.6 ppm, which correspond to hydrogen on the methacrylamide alkene bond. These specific peaks confirm the successful chemical modification and synthesis of ColMA from collagen.

caption: Phase space trajectory of the KEMC model at a strain rate of 10^-5 s^-1 within the plastic strain interval [0.11, 0.12], showing a secondary sub-cycle and the relationship between aging time and plastic strain rate.
summary: This panel displays the phase space dynamics of the KEMC model at a low strain rate of 10^-5 s^-1. It highlights a secondary sub-cycle feature and the relationship between aging time and plastic strain rate, providing insight into the model's behavior within the specified plastic strain interval.

caption: Parameter K1 distribution map plotted as a function of the carbon-concentration gradient parameter p and the graded layer thickness dt.
summary: Parameter K1 is visualized as a function of the carbon-concentration gradient parameter p and the graded layer thickness dt. This map is part of a series of seven stress/strain parameter visualizations used to evaluate the design of carbon-concentration gradients and appropriate layer thicknesses for material optimization.

caption: TEM-EDS concentration profiles of Ni and Ce across the Ni5Ce intermetallic precipitate and surrounding matrix in a Ni-based alloy subjected to ENP treatment at 1.30 × 10^11 A/m^2 and 330 ns.
summary: TEM-EDS measurements, calibrated by the Cliff-Lorime factor, quantify the elemental concentration distributions of field-activated precipitates. The profiles illustrate the transition from the center of the Ni5Ce intermetallic to the surrounding matrix, providing empirical evidence of the chemical composition changes induced by the high-density electric pulse treatment in the Ni-based alloy.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum acquired from the 316L steel surface treated with LEHCEB at 5 J/cm2.
summary: The EDS spectrum shown here corresponds to the 316L steel surface after LEHCEB treatment at 5 J/cm2. It provides the elemental composition of the modified surface, allowing for a comparison of chemical signatures between the treated sample and the as-received material.

caption: Conceptual workflow illustrating the integrated pipeline for data extraction and subsequent machine learning modeling.
summary: This schematic provides a comprehensive overview of the methodology employed in the study. It visualizes the systematic process for data extraction and the implementation of machine learning modeling techniques, serving as a foundational guide for understanding the computational framework used to analyze the materials science data presented throughout the research.

caption: Microindentation hardness measurements shown as a function of the laser power to scan speed ratio for as-built, SR 800 °C, and SR 870 °C conditions.
summary: Microindentation hardness data is plotted against the laser power to scan speed ratio. The figure compares the mechanical response of as-built specimens with those subjected to stress-relief heat treatments at 800 °C and 870 °C, illustrating the impact of processing conditions on the micro-scale hardness of the material.

caption: Simulated melt track cross-section showing the spatial evolution of dispersoid sizes for an initial feedstock diameter of 100 nm, processed at 140 W and 1.2 m/s.
summary: Representing the melt track cross-section for 100 nm initial dispersoids, this simulation demonstrates the impact of thermal excursions on particle evolution. The central zone shows complete dissolution and uniform nanoscale dispersoid formation, while the surrounding region retains larger dispersoid sizes due to only partial dissolution of the initial oxide feedstock.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of porosity in the as-built sample.
summary: This panel displays a 3D Micro-CT reconstruction of the as-built sample, highlighting the spatial distribution of internal porosity in red. The visualization provides a baseline for assessing the initial defect structure before any post-processing treatments are applied to the material, as part of the comprehensive Micro-CT analysis results.

caption: Effective diffusivity (Deff) derived from lag time plotted against reciprocal temperature, demonstrating adherence to an Arrhenius relationship.
