These screw dislocations are shown intersecting each other, demonstrating the complex dislocation-SF interactions that characterize the material's microstructure, consistent with observations of dense dislocation arrangements and their interactions in the alloy.

caption: Schematic illustration of the digital light-processing (DLP) 3D bioprinting process used to fabricate PDAC-mimetic niches, utilizing GelMA and HAMA bioinks to replicate the desmoplastic tumor microenvironment with stiffness modulated by photocuring time.
summary: This schematic illustrates the DLP 3D bioprinting process used to construct stiffness-tunable niches. By utilizing GelMA and HAMA as cell-laden bioinks, the method replicates the desmoplastic tumor microenvironment. Stiffness is precisely modulated through photocuring time, allowing for the creation of niches that match the local biomechanical heterogeneity found within PDAC.

caption: Individual atom maps derived from 3D-APT reconstruction, illustrating the spatial distribution of specific alloying elements within the Hf20 weld metal microstructure.
summary: Individual atom maps obtained via 3D-APT reconstruction visualize the distribution of each alloying element within the Hf20 weld metal. These maps provide a detailed view of the atomic arrangement, complementing the isosurface data to characterize the elemental partitioning behavior across the island platforms and particle phases present in the weld metal.

caption: Energy absorption curves for BCTs and SSLCTs evaluated at a wall thickness of 1 mm.
summary: Energy absorption performance of BCTs and SSLCTs is depicted for a wall thickness of 1 mm. These curves quantify the total energy dissipated by each structure during the crashworthiness test, allowing for an assessment of the efficiency and capacity of the different designs in absorbing mechanical energy.

caption: Mott–Schottky plots measured at 1000 Hz for Cr-enriched inner films on three low-Cr steels exposed to CO2-saturated NaCl solutions at 25 °C.
summary: Mott–Schottky plots at 1000 Hz characterize the semiconducting properties of Cr-enriched inner films on low-Cr steels in CO2-saturated NaCl solutions. This frequency is specifically chosen to isolate the space charge region capacitance from Helmholtz layer contributions, providing a reliable basis for determining the donor and acceptor densities of the passive films.

caption: 3D atom probe tomography (APT) reconstruction showing the spatial distribution of individual elements within the Gr13–1.0% Ta alloy.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction visualizes the elemental distribution within the Gr13–1.0% Ta alloy. APT analysis was specifically applied to detect the presence of Ta oxide within the TiO2 passive film, providing direct evidence of the element's spatial arrangement and oxidation state within the complex oxide-structured film.

caption: Storage modulus E′ evolution for 0.1 wt% MWCNT reinforced nanocomposites, evaluated via DMTA before and after water exposure.
summary: The storage modulus E′ for 0.1 wt% MWCNT reinforced nanocomposites is shown here, derived from DMTA analysis. The curves illustrate the mechanical behavior of these reinforced specimens before and after water uptake tests, highlighting the influence of MWCNT reinforcement on the material's stability under moisture-rich conditions.

caption: Calculated electronic band structure for the Ru-Ni hexagonal alloy, demonstrating metallic behavior with uniform isotropic conductivity across the Fermi level.
summary: The simulated band structure for the Ru-Ni hexagonal alloy reveals metallic characteristics. It exhibits uniform isotropic conductivity across the Fermi level, confirming the electronic nature of the material as predicted by DFT simulations. This metallic behavior is a fundamental property of the Ru-Ni alloy system under investigation.

caption: Transverse oriented HSLA steel specimen exhibiting characteristic fracture surface morphology under fatigue loading.
summary: Representing a transverse oriented sample, this optical micrograph illustrates the macroscopic fracture features observed after fatigue testing. The image serves to highlight the distinct geometry of the interface layer on the crack plane, providing a comparative view against longitudinal samples to understand the influence of orientation on fracture behavior.

caption: Atomic model of the γ-Ni phase supercell viewed along the b-direction, featuring an alloying atom M doped directly at the slip plane.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the supercell configuration for the γ-Ni phase, specifically designed for calculating generalized stacking fault energy. The structure highlights the placement of an alloying atom M at the slip plane, providing a foundational geometry for evaluating the slip system behavior within the γ-Ni crystal lattice.

caption: Dendrite nucleation and growth in K439B alloy observed via HT-CLSM at a cooling rate of 100 °C·min⁻¹, where nucleation initiates at 1308.2 °C.
summary: HT-CLSM imaging demonstrates the solidification behavior of K439B alloy at a cooling rate of 100 °C·min⁻¹. Nucleation is observed at 1308.2 °C. During subsequent growth, the advancing dendrite arms partition the residual liquid into an interconnected network within the interdendritic regions, as indicated by the blue dashed lines in the micrograph.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum acquired from the SLM AlSi10Mg alloy sample B2, confirming the elemental composition of the material.
summary: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum presented for the SLM AlSi10Mg alloy sample B2 confirms its elemental composition. This analytical technique was performed on the specimen produced with a laser power of 200 W and a speed of 800 mm/s to verify the presence of constituent elements within the alloy matrix.

caption: Low-magnification SEM-BSE micrograph of splat-quenched Ti-15.3Cu ribbon showing a fully lamellar microstructure.
summary: This low-magnification SEM-BSE micrograph displays the microstructure of splat-quenched Ti-15.3Cu alloy. The material exhibits an entirely lamellar microstructure that is notably devoid of proeutectoid Ti2Cu phases. This specific morphology is achieved through the rapid cooling process inherent to the splat-quenching technique used for this ribbon specimen.

caption: Bode plots showing the frequency-dependent impedance response of Ti–45Nb, Ti–42Nb (LPBF-Gaussian), Ti–42Nb (LPBF-top hat), and Ti–6Al–4V ELI alloys.
summary: Bode plots characterize the passive films formed on the studied alloys under OCP conditions in PBS solution. Analysis of the high-frequency range, where the phase angle approaches zero between 10^4 Hz and 10^3 Hz, provides insight into the electrolyte resistance associated with the electrochemical interface of these metallic materials.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms showing the mass activity of G/Pt, G/Pt75–Ni25, G/Pt54–Ni46, and G/Pt40–Ni60 catalysts for the methanol oxidation reaction in 1 M KOH and 1 M CH3OH at a 50 mV/s scan rate, with current normalized to Pt loading or total metal loading in the inset.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram illustrates the electrocatalytic activity of various G/Pt-Ni catalysts for the methanol oxidation reaction. By comparing mass activity across different compositions in an alkaline methanol environment, the plot highlights performance variations. The inset provides additional normalization data, offering a comprehensive view of the catalysts' electrochemical efficiency.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot illustrating the distribution and impact of feature values across individual samples.
summary: The beeswarm plot provides a detailed visualization of how specific feature values influence model predictions across the dataset. By mapping individual sample points, it reveals the nuanced relationship between geometric feature variations and the resulting print quality predictions, offering a granular view beyond simple global importance metrics.

caption: Hysteresis loops measured at various temperatures for the annealed sample, demonstrating the high coercivity of the Sm3Ni2 phase, while the inset illustrates the significant separation between field-cooled (FC) and zero-field-cooled (ZFC) measurements at 5 T, confirming strong magnetic anisotropy.
summary: Hysteresis loops for the annealed sample, measured at various temperatures, demonstrate the high coercivity characteristic of the Sm3Ni2 phase. The inset displays a large separation between the zero-field cooled and field cooled thermomagnetic measurements at 5 T, which further confirms the strong magnetic anisotropy of the Sm3Ni2 phase.

caption: Parity plot comparing actual wear rate values against those predicted by the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) model to validate predictive accuracy.
summary: Validation of the developed RSM model is demonstrated through this predicted versus actual wear rate plot. The data points exhibit a close alignment with the regression line, confirming a high degree of correlation and indicating that the model accurately predicts the experimental wear rate values observed in the study.

caption: Transverse residual stress (σyy) field map determined by Energy Dispersive Diffraction (EDD) within the sample mid-plane.
summary: This EDD-derived 2D stress map illustrates the transverse residual stress distribution within the sample mid-plane. A distinct band of compressive stress is observed above the arch, extending into the bridge leg. The color scale used here is identical to that applied in the DCM map for direct comparison.

caption: Relative particle displacements in Area 2, calculated using the Lagrangian particle tracking approach.
summary: Relative particle displacements in Area 2, calculated using the Lagrangian particle tracking approach. These snapshots of the modified particle displacement, analyzed via the Lagrangian particle tracking approach, illustrate the powder pile dynamics for the sectioned areas during the recoating process.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the influence of line energy density and hatch distance on the Mn content of as-built bulk samples, modeled using a 2nd-degree polynomial regression (R2 = 0.8674, adjusted R2 = 0.8639, RMSE = 0.1623).
summary: The effect of process parameters on Mn evaporation in as-built bulk samples is visualized through this 2nd-degree polynomial model. The plot demonstrates the relationship between applied line energy density and hatch distance, providing a statistical fit with an R-squared value of 0.8674 to quantify the resulting Mn content variations.

caption: Storage modulus temperature sweep for PMMA-free feedstocks composed of PVB/PEG/ATBC.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent storage modulus of PMMA-free feedstocks. The data illustrates the mechanical response of the material across a temperature range. Values below 600 MPa at 25 °C are highlighted as a benchmark, demonstrating sufficient flexibility for optimal filament usability in additive manufacturing applications.

caption: Strain map illustrating the interaction between slip bands and grain boundaries at 650 °C, highlighting localized deformation patterns.
summary: This strain map displays the interaction between slip bands and grain boundaries at 650 °C. It serves as part of a comparative analysis to document various deformation behaviors, specifically focusing on how strain is distributed or accommodated at the intersection of slip bands and grain boundaries within the sample microstructure.

caption: Isothermal section of the Al–Ni–Fe system at 25 °C showing the specific compositional positions of samples C-1, C-2, and C-3.
summary: This panel displays the Al–Ni–Fe isothermal section at 25 °C, highlighting the precise locations of samples C-1, C-2, and C-3. These positions are critical for understanding the subsequent phase formation processes and cooling paths experienced by each sample during solidification, as dictated by their specific nickel and aluminum concentrations.

caption: Computed surface work function for the Ti(001) crystal surface.
summary: Displayed here is the computed surface work function for the Ti(001) crystal surface. Obtained through DFT calculations, this value characterizes the electronic work function of the titanium surface in the (001) orientation, contributing to the comparative analysis of work functions across different metallic and intermetallic surfaces.

caption: Sectional strain distribution map at the mid-span of the plate, illustrating the localized deformation behavior under loading conditions.
summary: This visualization displays the sectional strain distribution at the mid-span of the plate. The map provides a detailed representation of localized deformation, which is essential for determining the yield load of the plate using the drawing procedure method proposed by Feng et al. to analyze structural performance under mechanical stress.

caption: Electrical resistivity variation plotted against elevated temperature for both the initial and the Pr-Tb-Al-Cu diffused Nd-Fe-B magnets.
summary: Electrical resistivity is shown as a function of elevated temperature for the initial and Pr-Tb-Al-Cu diffused magnets. The data indicates that the grain boundary diffusion of Pr-Tb-Al-Cu alloys successfully enhances the electrical resistivity of the sintered Nd-Fe-B magnets, contributing to improved performance characteristics at higher operating temperatures.

caption: Stress distribution map showing intensification in a <110> b grain surrounded by <100> grains in an isotropic matrix, highlighting the effect of grain configuration.
summary: This panel displays a simulation of stress intensification within a <110> b grain embedded in an isotropic matrix. It illustrates how the surrounding <100> grain configuration influences local stress states. The visualization serves as a baseline for comparing stress intensification effects based on the relative positioning of neighboring grains.

caption: Crack driving force J-integral evolution showing a minimum value reached immediately after the crack tip penetrates the soft Cu phase.
summary: The crack driving force J-integral plot demonstrates how the inhomogeneous composite structure influences fracture behavior. Shielding and anti-shielding effects at the crack tip, caused by the soft phase, reduce the driving force for crack propagation. This mechanism effectively improves the overall fracture toughness of the Fe-based BMG composite.

caption: Electromagnetic wave absorption performance of the Optimal structure and Cases 1–4 across the 12–18 GHz Ku-band frequency range.
summary: The absorption performance of the five 3D-printed BMMA specimens is illustrated across the 12-18 GHz frequency range. This plot compares the electromagnetic wave absorption characteristics of the Optimal structure against the four variations, Cases 1-4, providing a visual assessment of how design modifications impact the overall absorption efficiency.

caption: Normalized austenite fraction evolution during isothermal transformation as predicted by MICRESS simulations, fitted with the JMAK model.
summary: MICRESS phase-field simulations demonstrate the evolution of the normalized austenite fraction during isothermal transformations. These results are fitted using the Johnson–Mehl–Avrami–Kolmogorov (JMAK) model to characterize the transformation kinetics at constant temperatures. The data provides a quantitative basis for understanding the phase transformation behavior under the specified isothermal conditions.

caption: Processing map illustrating the relationship between energy density (Ev), laser power (P), scanning speed (V), and hatch spacing (h).
summary: This processing map visualizes the variation of energy density (Ev) as a function of laser power (P) and scanning speed (V) for three distinct hatch spacings (60, 80, and 100 μm). The resulting surfaces are color-coded from yellow to purple, representing the lowest to highest energy density values, respectively.

caption: Electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) map of the cracking zone, highlighting the elemental distribution near the crack tip.
summary: This EPMA map illustrates the elemental distribution within the cracking zone. Analysis reveals distinct solidified protrusions, approximately 2–3 μm in length, located at the crack tips. These features are identified as deleterious phases resulting from W/Ta enrichment during the solidification process, providing insight into the crack formation mechanism.

caption: Total weighted acceptance rates for each constituent across different systems after 25,000 MC steps, serving as a comparative metric for atomic mobility within the lattice, with Fe consistently exhibiting the highest activity levels.
summary: The final weighted acceptance rates after 25,000 MC steps are compared across different systems to evaluate relative atomic mobility. The data indicates that Fe consistently demonstrates the highest activity level across all simulated systems, providing a clear quantitative measure of constituent movement within the lattice structure during the hMCMD simulation.

caption: Tan delta values representing the extensional loss factor for unfilled and BC-filled samples across the temperature range.
summary: Tan delta curves for the tested samples illustrate the transition from the glassy state to the rubbery state. The profiles suggest that this transition occurs more readily as the concentration of BC filler increases. These results provide insight into the viscoelastic properties and the influence of filler content on material transitions.

caption: Al–Cu equilibrium binary phase diagram illustrating the solidification pathway and liquidus-solidus temperature relationships.
summary: This Al–Cu equilibrium binary phase diagram serves as a reference for the local solidification pathway. It defines the biphase region between alpha-Al and theta-Al2Cu, which accounts for the majority of the melted track volume, thereby dictating the expected phase constituents within the solidified Al–Cu multimaterial microstructure.

caption: Infrared radiation thermometer for monitoring thermal conditions.
summary: The infrared radiation thermometer is employed to measure the temperature distribution during the WAAM process. This diagnostic tool is integrated into the experimental equipment to provide real-time thermal data, which is vital for understanding the cooling rates and thermal history of the printed material during the additive manufacturing cycle.

caption: Carbon K-edge electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectrum acquired from the interphase region labeled (3) in the corresponding micrograph.
summary: This EELS spectrum characterizes the carbon K-edge fine structure obtained from the interphase region of the sample. Analysis of the fine structure confirms the presence of amorphous carbon within this area. This finding is consistent with broader observations of carbon dispersion throughout the interphase in the studied samples.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of an intergranular crack in alloy 52M, displaying dislocation density near the crack tip.
summary: Intergranular cracking in alloy 52M is examined using bright-field TEM, with the image highlighting dislocations formed around the crack tip. Utilizing a two-beam condition, the analysis reveals the specific crystallographic defects present at the crack tip cross-section, characterizing the material's response to the cracking process.

caption: Hardness profile of the alloys measured over a 14-day period of natural aging at room temperature.
summary: The hardness profile over 14 days of natural aging is depicted, illustrating the material's evolution during storage. The data indicates moderate hardening occurs during room temperature storage, reflecting the natural aging behavior of the alloys. This measurement is consistent with the range of properties observed in widely used alloys.

caption: Optical fluorescence image showing the morphology of MG-63 cells cultured on SLMed 316L SS leach liquor.
summary: Morphological characteristics of MG-63 cell lines cultured on SLMed 316L SS leach liquor were observed using optical fluorescence imaging. This technique allows for the visualization of cell structure and health, providing qualitative insights into the biological response of the cells to the 316L SS material environment.

caption: Rate performance evaluation of the ink-casted Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//LiCoO2 full cell across varying current densities.
summary: The rate performance of the ink-casted Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//LiCoO2 full cell is illustrated across different current densities. When compared with the 3D-printed version, these results reveal that the overall rate capability of the full cell is significantly improved by utilizing the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 anode structure.

caption: EDS elemental map showing the distribution of Cobalt (Co) at location No. 4, demonstrating depletion at the crystallite boundaries.
summary: The EDS elemental map for Cobalt (Co) at location No. 4 illustrates the spatial distribution of the element within the MPEA. The mapping results indicate that the crystallite boundaries are depleted of Cobalt, consistent with the broader observation of elemental segregation at these specific structural features.

caption: Quantitative analysis of printing error as a function of groove width, ranging from 0.2 mm to 0.6 mm, with error bars indicating standard deviation across multiple measurements.
summary: The plot displays the relationship between groove width and printing accuracy for a 10 mm radius curve. Experimental results indicate that the smallest printing error is achieved at a groove width of 0.3 mm, demonstrating the sensitivity of the printing process to the dimensions of the guiding groove.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of MoS2 nanosheets.
summary: Atomic force microscopy is employed to characterize the surface topography and thickness of the MoS2 nanosheets. This technique provides critical data on the exfoliation state of the material, confirming the presence of few-layer structures as indicated by the morphological analysis of the dispersed MoS2 flakes.

caption: Segmented 2-D rendering of the MAR-M247 skeleton during Stage 2 infiltration at 1130 °C, with purple indicating infiltrated regions and red indicating un-infiltrated regions.
summary: During Stage 2 infiltration at 1130 °C, this 2-D rendering illustrates the distribution of the braze within the MAR-M247 skeleton. The purple regions represent the infiltrated portions, while the red regions denote the un-infiltrated areas, providing a clear visual distinction of the infiltration progress within the metallic skeleton structure.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparison of GMA and DHPMA, highlighting the disappearance of epoxy moiety proton signals at 3.24, 2.84, and 2.65 ppm after the reaction.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra compare the starting material GMA with the synthesized DHPMA. A key observation is the complete disappearance of proton signals associated with the epoxy moiety at 3.24, 2.84, and 2.65 ppm, confirming the successful conversion of the epoxide group during the hydrolysis reaction.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram illustrating phase transformation kinetics for the nominal HSLA steel alloy composition.
summary: The CCT diagram presented here characterizes the phase transformation behavior of the nominal HSLA steel alloy during continuous cooling. This diagram is essential for predicting the microstructural evolution of the alloy under various cooling rates, as indicated by the thermodynamic calculations and reference data provided in the study.

caption: Enlarged STEM image of the region immediately beneath the fracture surface, illustrating γ′ shearing by dislocations, with the corresponding [001] zone axis SADP inset.
summary: Focusing on the area directly beneath the fracture surface, this panel presents an enlarged STEM image demonstrating γ′ shearing by dislocations. The inclusion of a [001] zone axis SADP confirms the crystallographic orientation, supporting the observation that fracture propagation is predominantly aligned with the γ/γ′ interface parallel to {001} planes.

caption: Parity plot displaying the relationship between predicted and experimental values for the response metric μ.
summary: This parity plot visualizes the correlation between predicted and experimental values for the response metric μ. Derived from the Full Factorial analysis, the graph serves to evaluate the predictive accuracy of the model by comparing experimental observations with calculated predictions, highlighting the relationship between these two data sets for μ.

caption: Excitation spectra of NiGa2O4:xEu films annealed at 950 °C, monitored at 610 nm emission, showing a primary band at 266 nm and secondary features between 255 and 370 nm.
summary: The excitation spectrum of NiGa2O4:xEu films annealed at 950 °C, monitored at 610 nm, displays a broad intense band centered at 266 nm. Additional broad bands observed in the 255–370 nm range are attributed to f-f transitions of europium ions within the host lattice structure.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TG) curves of 3D-printed geopolymers at 4 hours of age, illustrating mass loss trends under varying microwave conditions.
summary: This panel displays the TG curves for 3D-printed geopolymers at 4 hours of age. The analysis evaluates mass changes to assess the impact of microwave heating on the geopolymerization process. The curves provide a baseline for understanding the thermal stability and mass loss characteristics at this early curing stage.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry scans of solar salt after isothermal corrosion testing of Ni-coated alloys at 600 °C for 500 h, showing a reduced melting temperature of 212 °C.
summary: DSC scans of solar salt exposed to Ni-coated alloys, including In800H, In718, and Ha230, demonstrate a decreased melting temperature of 212 °C. These results confirm the effectiveness of fractal structured Ni coatings in reducing the liquidus temperature of molten salts compared to those exposed to uncoated alloy surfaces.

caption: Comparison of the commercial blue optical filter and its printed counterpart, featuring measured transmission spectra and a predicted ink composition of 4.5 drops Navy Blue, 2.0 drops Violet, 1.0 drop Emerald Green, and 0.5 drop Ruby.
summary: This panel displays the blue optical filter, comparing a commercial sample with a printed version generated by an inverse RF model. The transmission spectra demonstrate the performance match, while the predicted ink formulation, consisting of Navy Blue, Violet, Emerald Green, and Ruby, highlights the model's capability to replicate specific optical characteristics.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the AC-ST sample illustrating the grain orientation after specific processing.
summary: The AC-ST sample microstructure is analyzed via EBSD to produce an inverse pole figure map. This map displays the grain orientation distribution following the AC-ST processing step, allowing for a direct comparison of microstructural evolution relative to the initial AC state and the deformed EXT sample.

caption: Force versus displacement curves for Design 1 and Design 2 under forefoot loading conditions, showing loading and unloading cycles with energy return percentages.
summary: Forefoot loading test results for Design 1 and Design 2 are presented as force-displacement curves. These plots include loading and unloading data, with energy return percentages indicated. An abrupt change in the slope of the curves is observed beyond 50 mm displacement, highlighting the mechanical response of the designs.

caption: Molecular dynamics snapshot showing the pore distribution in the model subjected to a laser power of 300 eV/ps at a scanning speed of 4 Å/ps.
summary: Representing the model at a laser power of 300 eV/ps and a scanning speed of 4 Å/ps, this snapshot displays the resulting pore distribution. The image provides a visual assessment of how the increased laser energy influences the internal structural integrity and void formation compared to lower power settings.

caption: 2D and 3D topography of the SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy processed at 150 W laser power, yielding the lowest surface roughness of 4.19 μm.
summary: The P-150 specimen, processed at 150 W laser power, presents its 2D and 3D surface topography. This condition achieves the lowest surface roughness of 4.19 μm, demonstrating that the surface of the SLM-printed alloy becomes progressively smoother with increasing laser power throughout the range of 70 W to 150 W.

caption: Comparison of transmission curves for phononic crystals and W-shaped metamaterials, illustrating the bandgap performance.
summary: This plot compares the transmission characteristics of traditional phononic crystals against W-shaped metamaterials. The data demonstrates that the W-shaped design achieves low-frequency bandgaps with a significantly smaller structural footprint. This efficiency makes the metamaterial an effective solution for advanced applications in vibration attenuation, wave manipulation, and noise control.

caption: Incident monochromatic photon-to-current conversion efficiency (IPCE) spectra for DSCs, highlighting the superior short-circuit current density (Jsc) achieved by the Cr-Pt3Ni/CNs counter electrode.
summary: The IPCE spectra reveal the wavelength-dependent conversion efficiency of the DSCs. The device incorporating the Cr-Pt3Ni/CNs counter electrode exhibits a higher Jsc value compared to the other tested counter electrodes. This observation is consistent with the J-V curve results, confirming the enhanced performance of the Cr-doped composite in the solar cell configuration.

caption: Creep strain response of AISI 316L at 500, 600, and 800 °C, showing constant stress test results and SSRT dwell-time accumulation.
summary: AISI 316L creep strain is plotted against time at constant applied stress levels. The data includes both conventional creep tests and SSRT tests with intermediate dwell times. Variations between these testing methods are evident, though the logarithmic scale obscures the distinct creep stages typically observed in such mechanical tests.

caption: Validation of manufacturing speed parameters relative to build plate location, with batch identifiers 1 and -1, displaying ±3σ confidence intervals derived from Monte-Carlo simulations.
summary: This panel illustrates the validation of manufacturing speed parameters against build plate location for two distinct batches. Using Monte-Carlo simulations, the plot presents ±3σ confidence intervals to quantify variability. Ultrasound scan data confirms that sample placement on the build plate significantly influences the manufacturing process, even when parameters remain consistent.

caption: Formation enthalpies at 0 K for various Co–Al system configurations, showing the convex hull connected by a black line and identifying ground state phases including Al, Al9Co2, Al5Co2, AlCo, and hcp Co.
summary: This diagram illustrates the formation enthalpies at 0 K for the Co–Al system. The convex hull, represented by a black line, connects stable ground state phases such as Al, Al9Co2, Al5Co2, AlCo, and hcp Co. Complex phases are highlighted with solid symbols, while DFT results are compared against cluster expansion predictions.

caption: Schematic illustration of the rat calvarial defect model, outlining the surgical procedure and the treatment groups, which incorporate ultrasound (US) stimulation at 15 min, 1 MHz, and 0.2 W cm-2 daily.
summary: This panel depicts the rat calvarial defect model, incorporating ultrasound stimulation as a therapeutic parameter. The study compares four groups—Control, BHP, G@Met, and BHP/G@Met—all subjected to daily ultrasound treatment to investigate the synergistic effects of the scaffolds and physical stimulation on bone defect repair capacity.

caption: Temperature distribution for intermittent melt pool interference mode under the S3 scanning strategy with perpendicular adjacent units.
summary: This simulation shows the temperature distribution for the S3 scanning strategy, characterized by an intermittent melt pool interference mode. The laser scanning paths in adjacent units are oriented perpendicularly, creating a distinct thermal profile that differs from continuous scanning modes and influences the resulting melt pool morphology.

caption: Point cloud representation of the wall surface generated via optical scanning, where gray and blue points distinguish measurements taken from two opposing faces.
summary: This 3D point cloud reconstruction illustrates the surface geometry of the walls obtained through optical scanning. By isolating relevant scene data, the visualization clearly distinguishes between measurements from two opposite faces, represented by gray and blue points, providing a precise spatial mapping of the wall surface topography.

caption: True stress–strain curves derived from engineering data for the Ni-22Al-7Ti alloy, highlighting that samples subjected to 50% strain remained intact without fracturing.
summary: True stress-strain curves transformed from engineering data illustrate the mechanical behavior of the Ni-22Al-7Ti alloy. Notably, the material exhibits significant ductility, as evidenced by the absence of fracture in samples compressed to 50% strain, confirming the alloy's capacity for large deformation during high-temperature processing.

caption: Initial three-dimensional concave hexagonal cell structure of the TPU auxetic honeycomb pad.
summary: This panel displays the initial three-dimensional concave hexagonal cell structure of the TPU auxetic honeycomb pad. This design was previously proposed by the research group as a foundational geometry for the pad, serving as the baseline configuration before the subsequent structural modifications were implemented to enhance performance.

caption: Double-tilt TEM holder used for in-situ experimental analysis.
summary: This panel displays the double-tilt TEM holder utilized for in-situ experimental analysis. The holder is a critical component of the Thermo Fisher/FEI Titan Cubed Themis TEM setup, enabling precise sample manipulation and orientation control during the heating experiments conducted at LNNano/CNPEM to investigate the Mar18Ni steel lamella behavior.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots for as-cast TC4 alloy after varying corrosion exposure durations in 0.6 mol/L NaCl solution.
summary: As-cast TC4 alloy exhibits n-type semiconductor behavior in 0.6 mol/L NaCl solution, as evidenced by the Mott-Schottky measurements. These curves demonstrate the influence of corrosion exposure duration on the passive film properties, confirming that the semiconductor characteristics persist regardless of the specific exposure time tested in this environment.

caption: Diagram showing how powder particle entrapment within the nozzle disrupts the homogeneous flow of gas and powder, leading to localized overheating, increased spatter, and schlieren formation.
summary: Partial nozzle blockage is shown to cause significant process instability. The entrapment of powder particles disrupts the homogeneous flow, creating an imbalance in power per powder mass. This leads to increased heating, spatter, and schlieren formation, as the equilibrium between the process gas and rising hot gas is compromised.

caption: Young's modulus variation plotted against changing ligament height h i and angle θ i for Set 1 simulations and analytical model predictions.
summary: Young's modulus values are presented for Set 1 simulations, demonstrating how geometric parameters influence the stiffness of the cubic RVE. The plot highlights regions where specific variable combinations are unrealizable under the defined structural constraints. These findings are consistent with the analytical model predictions for the system's principal directions.

caption: Calculated Si solute adsorption energy as a function of layer position for the B-terminated TiB2-Al interface, showing the weakest adsorption tendency among the studied substrates.
summary: The plot displays the Si adsorption energy profile for the B-terminated TiB2 substrate. Ab initio simulation results indicate that this interface exhibits the weakest Si adsorption tendency compared to Ti-terminated and Al3Ti-covered substrates, providing quantitative data on how Si solute atoms interact with the nucleation interface during solidification.

caption: Schematic illustration of the specific sampling locations within the material designated for subsequent microstructure observation and mechanical tensile testing.
summary: This schematic diagram identifies the precise sampling positions within the material intended for microstructure observation and mechanical property evaluation. By defining these specific locations, the figure ensures consistency between the microstructural analysis and the subsequent tensile testing procedures, providing a clear spatial reference for the experimental characterization of the material.

caption: Secondary electron (SE) micrograph of the René 95 alloy microstructure, highlighting the morphology of tertiary γ′ precipitates within the grains.
summary: Secondary electron imaging of the René 95 alloy reveals the distribution of tertiary γ′ precipitates located within the grains. These nanoscale precipitates are characteristic of the alloy's microstructure. The SE mode provides topographical contrast, allowing for the clear visualization of these fine-scale features within the metallic matrix.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the 50%-L-OHS sample focusing on the OS region, which exhibits coarser grains of approximately 8 μm.
summary: Focusing on the OS region of the 50%-L-OHS sample, this SEM image reveals a distinct grain structure. The region is characterized by significantly coarser grains, measuring approximately 8 μm in size, which contrasts with the finer grain morphology observed in the adjacent LS region.

caption: Calculated isopleth diagram for the nickel-free WC/Co-12Al-11W system, showing phase stability as a function of temperature and carbon content between 4.0 and 6.0 wt% C.
summary: This CALPHAD-calculated isopleth diagram illustrates phase stability for the nickel-free WC/Co-12Al-11W cemented carbide system. It maps temperature against carbon content from 4.0 to 6.0 wt%. Although the model predicts a three-phase region consisting of gamma, gamma prime, and WC, experimental observations indicate that no gamma prime precipitates are actually visible.

caption: Cyclic polarization scans for cast and printed 17–4PH and CORRAX® alloys conducted at 25°C, illustrating the electrochemical response before and after reaching the pitting potential.
summary: Cyclic polarization curves for cast and printed 17–4PH and CORRAX samples at 25°C are presented. The solid lines indicate the scan prior to pitting, while dashed lines represent the post-pitting behavior. These curves demonstrate the material's resistance to pit initiation, reflected in the observed metastable pitting nucleation characteristics.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification performance of the XGBoost model during the testing phase.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed evaluation of the XGBoost model's predictive accuracy during the testing process. By visualizing the classification results, it allows for a clear assessment of the model's performance, highlighting how well the algorithm correctly identifies and categorizes the data points within the test set.

caption: Structural similarity (SSIM) distributional comparison evaluating the performance of the super-resolution model.
summary: Structural similarity (SSIM) values are compared between HR-LR and HR-SR sample pairs to quantify the performance of the super-resolution task. This plot demonstrates the quantitative agreement between ground truth patch structures and predicted patch structures, providing a distributional view of how well the model preserves structural information.

caption: Close-up view of the participant's hand showing the specific placement of reflective markers used for motion tracking.
summary: This photograph displays the participant's hand with reflective markers strategically positioned to facilitate accurate motion tracking. The marker placement is critical for the Vicon system to register hand kinematics during the experimental trials, ensuring that the captured data accurately reflects the participant's physical movements throughout the study.

caption: Correlation between avalanche energy and apparent density for Ti powders measured at a constant rotational speed of 0.3 RPM.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between avalanche energy and apparent density for Ti powders at a fixed rotational speed of 0.3 RPM. The data confirms that flowability characteristics remain within the required 10 mJ/kg benchmark, supporting the compatibility of these powders for DED additive manufacturing processes.

caption: Predicted stress–strain response of Ni 11 Fe alloy, calculated using a hardening model that integrates edge and screw dislocation effects based on first-principles data.
summary: This plot illustrates the DFT-predicted stress–strain behavior for Ni 11 Fe, modified to account for large strains by combining edge and screw dislocation contributions. The hardening model parameters are derived from calculated Peierls-Nabarro stresses, with the initial yield stress assumed to be 300 MPa, consistent with pure Ni values.

caption: Incremental capacity analysis (ICA) plots for Al thin films, organized by temperature (columns: room temperature, 40 °C, 50 °C, 60 °C) and C-rate (rows: C/40, C/20, C/10, C/5), highlighting lithiation peak positions for Li3Al2 and Li2-xAl phases.
summary: This figure displays differential capacity curves derived from galvanostatic lithiation profiles of Al thin films. The data, arranged by temperature and C-rate, identify specific lithiation peaks for Li3Al2 and Li2-xAl phases. Notably, peak merging occurs at specific temperature and rate combinations, while no peak splitting indicative of Li9Al4 is observed.

caption: Plot of the maximum principal stress calculated at the phase interface across different positions, characterizing the I-type intergranular crack propagation behavior.
summary: This plot displays the maximum principal stress at the phase interface at various positions along the specimen. By modeling the intergranular crack as an I-type crack, the data identifies the stress distribution as a primary factor influencing the crack propagation direction, which is essential for understanding the material's failure mechanism under tensile stress.

caption: Complete force-displacement (F-u) response curve up to fracture for the third investigated design, incorporating cases where debonding is considered.
summary: Panel e illustrates the complete force-displacement curve up to fracture for the third design. It compares numerical simulations with experimental data, including dotted lines to represent cases where debonding was considered. Triangles mark the predicted onset of plastic deformation, which begins to influence the material response at small displacement values.

caption: Amplitude image loaded onto the DMD for pixel alignment in the horizontal orientation.
summary: The amplitude image is loaded onto the DMD to ensure accurate pixel alignment in the horizontal orientation. This configuration works in conjunction with the phase image to calibrate the optical setup, ensuring that the spatial distribution of the amplitude matches the required experimental parameters for the intended optical processing.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) pattern derived from the Ni(Mn,Al) matrix, confirming its body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal structure.
summary: FFT analysis of the matrix region confirms the presence of a body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal structure. This identification supports the classification of the dark grey phases as Ni(Mn,Al) matrix, which exhibits structural similarities to the strip-shaped intermetallic compounds previously observed in the ISZ.

caption: Training and validation loss curves plotted against epoch count, demonstrating the convergence behavior of the invertible neural network using 70 training samples.
summary: The training and validation loss curves are shown in Fig. 3 (a), which visualizes the training process using 70 training samples. This plot tracks the loss values across different epochs to monitor the convergence and stability of the invertible neural network during the model training phase.

caption: Predicted versus experimental Nusselt number for the ARM geometry under Case 2 conditions with a heat flux of 315 kW/m² and roughness εr,ARM = 0.017.
summary: Panel D shows the Nusselt number for the ARM geometry at the higher heat flux of 315 kW/m². Consistent with other cases, the simulation reproduces the experimental trend and HTD/HTE effects. The localized influence of microtube segment joins remains a distinct feature in the ARM model's predictive output.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 1100 °C, comparing experimental phase compositions from rapidly quenched spherical particles, flaky particles, and slow-cooled samples against FactSage 8.3 calculated phase boundaries and tie-lines.
summary: This ternary phase diagram displays the Cu–Ni–S system at 1100 °C, plotting experimental data points against calculated thermodynamic models. The diagram highlights the liquid-liquid miscibility gap and compares phase compositions from various cooling rates, including rapid quenching and slow cooling, to validate the accuracy of the FactSage 8.3 thermodynamic model.

caption: Transition zone between fatigue and instant fracture in a NiTi tube paired with an Al2O3 bushing, showing microvoid coalescence.
summary: Microscopic examination of the NiTi tube fracture surface paired with an Al2O3 bushing reveals the transition from fatigue to instant fracture. The instant fracture region is characterized by a rough morphology containing numerous microvoids that coalesce, indicating a ductile fracture mechanism occurring at the microscopic level during the final failure stage.

caption: Tabulated summary of the material properties and boundary conditions governing the unit cell optimization.
summary: This table lists the critical material properties and boundary conditions used to constrain the unit cell optimization. These parameters serve as the foundational data for the study, ensuring that the resulting structural model accurately reflects the physical constraints and mechanical characteristics required for the simulated loading scenarios.

caption: Load–displacement curve derived from nanoindentation testing of a heat-treated specimen, illustrating the mechanical response under applied force.
summary: This load–displacement curve represents the mechanical response of a heat-treated specimen subjected to nanoindentation testing. The data obtained from this curve are essential for calculating critical mechanical properties, including hardness, Young's modulus, and the elastic recovery parameter, providing a comprehensive assessment of the material's performance following the heat treatment process.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the pore-free region, showing columnar grains advancing diagonally from the melt pool edges toward the center, where competitive growth suppresses adjacent grains.
summary: In this pore-free cross-section, columnar grains advance diagonally upward from the melt pool edges toward the center. Competitive growth occurs in the central region, effectively suppressing adjacent grains. This region serves as a baseline for comparing grain size and morphology against the pore-affected microstructure shown in panel b.

caption: Mean percentage error and mean absolute error values across various testing temperatures are presented using solid-colored and dashed-line box plots, respectively.
summary: This panel displays the mean percentage error in solid-colored boxes and mean absolute error in dashed-line boxes across different temperatures. These box plots illustrate the error metrics, with t-statistic values confirming no significant deviations, indicating that the experimental results remain consistent and reliable across the tested temperature range.

caption: Raman spectra collected from the three distinct positions marked in the optical microscopy image, demonstrating the spectroscopic characteristics of the graphene film at different locations.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was performed at the three specific locations identified in the optical microscopy image. These spectra provide critical information regarding the structural integrity and quality of the graphene film. By comparing the data from the red, magenta, and blue marked regions, the uniformity of the growth is effectively assessed.

caption: Tensile stress-strain curves for the STA condition in vertical (BD) and horizontal (TD) orientations, illustrating significant work-hardening behavior prior to the onset of plastic softening and a marked increase in mechanical strength compared to the ST condition.
summary: Panel (b) displays the tensile curves for the STA condition, which demonstrate substantial work-hardening before plastic softening occurs. The mechanical strength of the STA condition is significantly improved relative to the ST condition, a result attributed to the extensive precipitation of the α-phase within the material microstructure.

caption: {0001} pole figure corresponding to the grain shown in panel (b), illustrating the crystallographic orientation of the parent grain and its associated twin variants.
summary: This {0001} pole figure provides a quantitative representation of the crystallographic orientation for the grain analyzed in panel (b). It confirms the orientation relationship between the parent grain and the identified twin variants, T1, T2, and T2-S1, which preferentially nucleate under the influence of high plastic strain.

caption: EDS elemental map highlighting the distribution of Nickel across the MC and Fine-G regions.
summary: This EDS map displays the Nickel distribution within the observed microstructure. It serves to characterize the chemical composition of the MC phase and the Fine-G region, supporting the observation that the MC phase decomposes into a gamma phase with subsequent gamma-prime formation within the newly formed gamma grains.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the as-sprayed vertical sample deformed at a strain rate of 0.001 s-1, highlighting the distribution of deformation twins within the microstructure.
summary: This dark-field TEM image provides a clear visualization of the deformation twins present in the as-sprayed vertical sample after quasi-static compression at a strain rate of 0.001 s-1. The imaging technique confirms the prevalence of these twins, which are a key feature of the deformed microstructure.

caption: Raman spectrum of the parental Zn-Al LDH coating on AA2024 alloy and the ZIF-8@LDH transformation product, highlighting the nitrate stretching mode at 1055 cm-1 and metal-oxygen-metal vibrations at 487 and 549 cm-1.
summary: The Raman spectrum of the initial Zn-Al LDH coating on AA2024 alloy displays a prominent signal at 1055 cm-1, attributed to NO3- stretching modes. Additionally, bands at 487 and 549 cm-1 correspond to Al-O-Al and Zn-O-Al stretching vibrations, respectively, providing evidence of the surface modifications during the Zn-Al LDH-to-ZIF-8 transformation process.

caption: Three-dimensional capacity surface envelope representing the sectional capacity of a structural column under combined bi-directional bending moments and axial forces, with dotted markers indicating specific design load combinations.
summary: This three-dimensional capacity surface illustrates the ultimate sectional strength of a structural column subjected to bi-directional bending and axial loading. Dotted points mapped onto the surface represent specific design actions determined for individual members, allowing for the direct identification of the loading state relative to the member's ultimate capacity.

caption: Pie graph illustrating the total distribution of non-recyclable waste weight percentages across different surgical subspecialties.
summary: This pie chart displays the total non-recyclable waste percentage across surgical subspecialties. Trauma surgery represents the highest production at 37.71%, followed by arthroplasty at 35.28% and oncology at 27.01%. These findings highlight the significant contribution of trauma and arthroplasty procedures to the overall non-recyclable waste generated in the clinical environment.

caption: Room temperature demagnetization curve for the LPBF-printed Alloy A specimen.
summary: This panel displays the room temperature demagnetization behavior of Alloy A fabricated via LPBF. The curve illustrates the magnetic response of the material under specific testing conditions, allowing for a direct comparison of its magnetic performance against other alloys processed under identical manufacturing parameters as described in the study.

caption: Temperature-dependent activities of Ni, Co, Cr, and Al species for the CMSX-10K alloy, presented on a reciprocal temperature scale using KEMS intensity data.
summary: Representing the CMSX-10K alloy, this Arrhenius plot shows the activity of Ni, Co, Cr, and Al species versus reciprocal temperature. These KEMS-derived intensity measurements provide the necessary data to determine the partial molar enthalpies of the species at the median temperature of the experimental dataset.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the TiFe0.9Ni0.1 specimen, showing the Ni-cap and the Ti-oxide surface layer.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction of the TiFe0.9Ni0.1 specimen illustrates the atomic structure of the needle-shaped tip. Green spheres represent the Ni-cap coating, while blue spheres indicate Ti-oxide species. The reconstruction confirms that the surface oxide layer is primarily composed of Ti oxides, providing 3D data for the alloy's surface.

caption: Digital porosity twin used as a reference for XCT internal feature assessment.
summary: This digital porosity twin represents a virtual reference model for XCT-based internal feature assessments. By providing a controlled digital environment, it enables the calibration and validation of XCT imaging techniques, ensuring that internal structural features are accurately captured and analyzed within the context of material characterization.

caption: Performance-profile radar chart comparing seismic metamaterials against conventional seismic protection systems across five engineering metrics: technology maturity, broadband effectiveness, soil-condition independence, durability, and scalability.
summary: This radar chart evaluates seismic metamaterials against traditional seismic protection systems using five key engineering metrics. The visualization highlights a significant development gap, particularly regarding technology maturity and large-scale deployability, despite the inherent theoretical advantages of metamaterials in achieving targeted wave attenuation for seismic mitigation strategies.

caption: Grain Reference Orientation Deviation (GROD) map of the Nb–2TiC alloy, highlighting internal grain misorientation.
summary: The GROD map of the Nb–2TiC alloy visualizes the internal grain misorientation, providing insight into the local strain and dislocation density within the grains. This map helps evaluate the structural integrity and the impact of the L-DED process on the crystalline lattice of the composite material.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Samarium (Sm) across the as-cast alloy microstructure.
summary: The elemental distribution map of Samarium (Sm) provides a spatial visualization of the alloy's composition. The intensity distribution of Sm in this map is in direct agreement with the concentration profile obtained from the EDS line scan, confirming the spatial arrangement of the distinct phases within the as-cast sample.

caption: Storage modulus (Eʹ) curves of PLA/hemp hurd fibre composites plotted against temperature, demonstrating the influence of varying recycling steps on the material's stiffness.
summary: The storage modulus (Eʹ) curves of the PLA/hemp hurd fibre composites are illustrated in this panel. These curves represent the mechanical response of the composites as a function of temperature, specifically highlighting how the storage modulus changes across different numbers of recycling steps performed on the material.

caption: Flexural modulus measurements for PLA/BiWF hybrid biocomposites across different fiber treatment durations.
summary: Flexural modulus values are presented for PLA/BiWF hybrid biocomposites treated with sodium bicarbonate for 24, 48, 72, 120, and 168 hours. These mechanical characteristics were extracted from the flexural curves of the produced composites, highlighting how specific treatment durations, such as 72 hours, optimize the structural integrity and mechanical response of the biocomposites.

caption: Measured time-temperature profiles for dilatometry experiments conducted at cooling rates ranging from 40 to 500 °C/s, illustrating the shift in martensitic transformation start temperature (Ms) as a function of cooling rate.
summary: This panel displays the time-temperature profiles for dilatometry experiments performed at cooling rates between 40 and 500 °C/s. The data demonstrates that the martensitic transformation start temperature (Ms) decreases as the cooling rate increases, providing essential thermal data for understanding phase transformation kinetics under varying cooling conditions.

caption: Comparison of stacking fault energy (SFE) estimation performance for CoCrFeMnNiVAl high-entropy alloys using classical machine learning algorithms including support vector classifier (SVC) and random forest (RF), alongside deep learning regression models such as the backpropagation neural network (BPNN).
summary: This figure illustrates the application of various machine learning models to predict the stacking fault energy of CoCrFeMnNiVAl high-entropy alloys. By employing classical algorithms like SVC and RF alongside deep learning approaches such as BPNN, the study demonstrates a comparative framework for accurately estimating critical material properties in complex FCC-structured HEA systems.

caption: Isothermal section of the Fe-Cr-Ni system at 1173 K, highlighting a wider predicted stability domain for the sigma-phase compared to the reference diagram by Tomiska.
summary: Representing the Fe-Cr-Ni system at 1173 K, this diagram displays the computed phase stability. A notable discrepancy exists regarding the sigma-phase, where the current simulation predicts a wider stability domain than that observed in Tomiska's diagram. Despite this specific difference, the overall phase topology remains consistent with experimental observations.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of CNF 12% showing the surface morphology and fibrillar structure.
summary: Atomic force microscopy image of CNF 12% showing the surface morphology and fibrillar structure. According to AFM images and the height distribution graph, all CNFs samples exhibit a consistent height distribution within the range of 1.5–3 nm, confirming the successful preparation of the cellulose nanofibrils.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) orientation map of the Al 7075 scratch site, illustrating the development of a distinct orientation gradient extending from the scratch surface into the specimen interior.
summary: This IPF orientation map demonstrates the microstructural response of Al 7075 to a 30 mN nanoscratch. It clearly shows the development of an orientation gradient that evolves from the scratch surface toward the interior of the specimen, indicating significant plastic deformation and crystal rotation induced by the mechanical contact.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of BMSCs on BG scaffolds, where green indicates live cells and red indicates dead cells.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of BMSCs on BG scaffolds reveals the distribution of live and dead cells. The presence of green-stained cells confirms that the BG scaffold supports cell viability and proliferation, with minimal cell death observed, demonstrating the cytocompatibility of the material for bone marrow stromal cell culture.

caption: UMAP projection of congruent TPMS no-flow regime features, demonstrating the presence of three distinct clusters.
summary: This UMAP projection represents the feature space for the congruent TPMS no-flow regime. Similar to the flow regime analysis, the data is partitioned into three distinct clusters highlighted by dashed lines. The reference confirms that these projections are abstract representations without physical axis values, complicating individual cluster group interpretation.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of CD86 (M1 marker) and CD206 (M2 marker) in wound tissue on day 7, accompanied by quantitative analysis of macrophage polarization.
summary: This panel presents immunofluorescence staining of macrophage markers to assess phenotypic polarization in vivo. The analysis confirms that the hydrogel effectively modulates the immune response by promoting M2 polarization and inhibiting M1 polarization, which is essential for creating a favorable environment for tissue regeneration and wound healing.

caption: Thermogravimetry (TG) curves of Cu1-xNix@C nanoparticles showing weight gain as a function of temperature.
summary: Thermogravimetry (TG) curves illustrate the thermal behavior of Cu1-xNix@C nanoparticles. As the nickel content increases, the onset temperature for weight gain shifts to higher values, and the temperature range characterized by rapid weight increase also moves toward a higher-temperature region, indicating improved thermal stability with higher nickel concentrations.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of co-cultured U2OS-MSC spheroids on β-TCP scaffolds, showing spheroids in red (cell tracker) and pBMSCs/endothelial cells in green (Calcein AM).
summary: Fluorescence microscopy reveals the spatial distribution of cells on β-TCP scaffolds. U2OS-MSC spheroids are identified by red cell tracker staining, while pBMSCs and endothelial cells are distinguished by green Calcein AM staining. This imaging technique allows for the clear differentiation between the osteosarcoma spheroids and the suspension-seeded cells within the scaffold structure.

caption: Partial radial distribution function gAl-Al(r) for Al50Cu25Ni25 melt at 1400 K, comparing AIMD (solid blue) and DNNP (red dashed) results.
summary: The partial radial distribution function gAl-Al(r) for the Al50Cu25Ni25 melt at 1400 K is presented. This plot compares the structural data derived from AIMD simulations, represented by solid blue lines, against the predictions from DNNP simulations, shown as red dashed lines, to validate the accuracy of the machine learning potential.

caption: Gas grid representation showing simulated material surface complexity.
summary: The gas grid panel illustrates a specific region of the simulated material surface. By utilizing distinct colors and symbols to represent particles, this visualization ensures that the simulated surface exhibits varied and realistic complexity, thereby making the overall simulation results more representative of actual physical conditions observed in the material.

caption: Raman spectrum of the wear track on the AM sample disk after subtractive baseline correction and curve fitting.
summary: Presented here is the Raman spectrum recorded from the wear track on the additive manufactured (AM) disk. By applying subtractive baseline correction and curve fitting, the spectrum characterizes the specific compounds present within the tribolayers formed on the disk surface, facilitating a detailed analysis of the wear-induced chemical modifications.

caption: Reflectance spectral response of the sensor under 5 mW of 980 nm pump power, showing a redshift from 1548.24 nm to 1557.88 nm as humidity increases.
summary: Under a 5 mW pump power, the sensor's reflection spectrum shows a clear redshift as relative humidity rises from 14.1% to 85.2%. The resonance dip moves from 1548.24 nm to 1557.88 nm, demonstrating that the sensor maintains its humidity-sensing capability even when subjected to external optical pumping.

caption: Pole figure representation for label 1 of the GSLS sample.
summary: This panel displays the pole figure for label 1 of the GSLS sample. As indicated in the reference, this figure is part of a series showing the crystallographic orientation distribution for GSLS materials, providing insight into the texture characteristics of the specimen under investigation.

caption: Atomic structure model of Mn6 amorphous alloy showing the local atomic distribution after Mn substitution for Co.
summary: The atomic structure of the Mn6 amorphous alloy is presented, highlighting the arrangement of atoms following the substitution of cobalt with manganese. The model illustrates that transition metals and boron atoms cluster around the central manganese, maintaining coordination numbers between 13 and 14, which is typical for this alloy series.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for scanning strategies S1-S5.
summary: This panel displays the major axis length distribution of primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite on XOY cross-sections using a combination of violin and box plots. The data compares five different scanning strategies, S1 through S5, to evaluate how melt pool interference modes influence the resulting martensite size distribution.

caption: Temperature distribution map corresponding to the lower part of the molten pool shown in panel (a).
summary: Temperature distribution at the lower part of the molten pool is visualized through phase-field simulation. The isotherm representing a supercooling degree of zero is located near the tips of the columnar dendrites. This thermal field data is essential for understanding the solidification process and the resulting microstructure of the deposition layer.

caption: Comparative tensile stress-strain curves for PT-3 hybrid resin, contrasting the mechanical response after initial UV curing versus the final photothermal curing process.
summary: Comparative tensile stress-strain curves for PT-3 hybrid resin illustrate the mechanical evolution after UV and photothermal curing. Initial UV-curing yielded 15.9 MPa stress and 34.9% elongation, which significantly improved to 59.6 MPa stress and 10.0% elongation following the second step of the thermal-curing process, indicating substantial material strengthening.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 10 m/min and constant travel speed.
summary: Shown is the current-voltage profile for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 10 m/min. This plot illustrates the electrical behavior of the deposition process at the highest tested feed rate, providing a comparison point for the peak current and duration characteristics observed in other samples.

caption: Comparative analysis of yield strength versus elongation for the studied superalloys against typical Ni-based superalloys.
summary: Comparative analysis of yield strength versus elongation highlights the balance of strength and ductility achieved by the pre-strain method. This plot benchmarks the studied superalloys against typical Ni-based superalloys, utilizing comparative mechanical properties data sourced from established literature to contextualize the performance improvements of the investigated materials.

caption: Pseudo-Voigt function fit applied to a single diffraction peak from the LaB6 standard pattern.
summary: A pseudo-Voigt function is used to fit a single diffraction peak from the LaB6 standard pattern. Although no single analytical function can perfectly describe the complex peak shape, this fitting method provides a reliable approximation for the peak shapes observed in the diffraction data collected at the ESRF.

caption: EPMA concentration profiles of Fe, Ni, Cr, Al, and Cu elements across the cross-section of the Fe-17Ni-17Cr-7.7Al-3.5Cu alloy after 100 h of oxidation at 1000 °C.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis concentration profiles for the Fe-17Ni-17Cr-7.7Al-3.5Cu alloy demonstrate the distribution of constituent elements following 100 hours of air oxidation at 1000 °C. These profiles characterize the elemental gradients near the surface, providing insight into the oxidation behavior and chemical stability of the alloy under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Ternary contour plot of log10 coercivity (Hc) for 40 Fe-Co-Ni alloy compositions, with predicted compositions from ETR and NNR_4layers_Wen models for six target sets.
summary: This ternary contour plot displays the log10 coercivity (Hc) for 40 Fe-Co-Ni alloy compositions. It highlights predicted compositions from ETR and NNR_4layers_Wen models for six target sets. The plot serves as part of the experimental validation for the inverse design strategy used to optimize these specific alloy properties.

caption: Comparison of micro-hardness values measured across different cutting environments, illustrating the influence of various lubrication and cooling procedures on surface hardening.
summary: This figure displays micro-hardness values obtained under diverse cutting environments, specifically highlighting the impact of different lubrication and cooling procedures. The observed increment in surface hardness is attributed to the rapid heating and cooling cycles experienced by the material during the machining processes, as depicted in the comparative analysis.

caption: Weight loss profiles of bamboo-filled PLA composites plotted against temperature, showing the thermal degradation behavior for varying filler sizes of 125 μm and 250 μm at loadings of 5, 10, 15, and 20 wt%.
summary: Weight loss profiles of bamboo-filled PLA composites are plotted against temperature to illustrate thermal degradation. The samples incorporate bamboo fillers of two distinct sizes, 125 μm and 250 μm, across various filler loadings ranging from 5 to 20 wt%, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's thermal stability under these conditions.

caption: Current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics of the monolithic perovskite/Si tandem solar cell with a 1 cm2 active area, measured under AM1.5 G illumination in both forward and reverse scan directions.
summary: The J-V characteristic of the monolithic tandem solar cells with a marked active area of 1 cm2 under AM1.5 G illumination is shown. The device performance is evaluated by scanning in both forward and reverse directions to assess the tandem solar cell's photovoltaic response under standard simulated sunlight conditions.

caption: Ti 2p XPS spectrum showing the binding energy features of titanium species.
summary: The Ti 2p XPS spectrum provides detailed information regarding the titanium chemical environment. By analyzing the binding energy peaks, the oxidation state and surface chemistry of titanium are determined, completing the high-resolution XPS characterization of the various metallic elements present in the investigated sample.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of PPI-SL showing chemical shifts for aliphatic, aromatic, imine, and hydroxyl protons.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of PPI-SL displays distinct chemical shifts corresponding to its molecular structure. Peaks at 1.372–2.502 ppm represent aliphatic protons, while signals at 3.596–3.628 ppm, 6.815–7.358 ppm, 8.233 ppm, and 13.578 ppm are assigned to imine-linked methylene, benzene ring, imine, and hydroxyl protons, respectively.

caption: iR-corrected HER polarization curves for Pt x Ni/C and Pt/C JM catalysts measured in N2-saturated 0.1 M KOH at 5 mV s-1, 1600 rpm, and 25 °C.
summary: The iR-corrected HER polarization curves for Pt x Ni/C and Pt/C JM catalysts are presented, illustrating their electrochemical performance. These measurements were conducted in an N2-saturated 0.1 M KOH electrolyte at a scan rate of 5 mV s-1, a rotation speed of 1600 rpm, and a controlled temperature of 25 °C.

caption: Electronic PDOS for Fe, O, and Ca atoms at the Fe/CaO interface.
summary: This panel presents the PDOS of Fe atoms, O atoms, and Ca atoms at the interface of the Fe/CaO pre-nucleation model. The electronic density of states plots characterize the atomic interactions and electronic environment of the iron and calcium oxide interface components.

caption: XCT reconstructions and bar plots for Alloy A, displaying the correlation between volumetric energy density, defect volume ratio, and coercivity.
summary: Alloy A samples processed via LPBF are characterized using XCT reconstructions and bar charts to evaluate the relationship between volumetric energy density, defect volume ratio, and coercivity. The panel provides 3D visualizations of internal porosity alongside quantitative trends, illustrating how varying energy densities influence the defect distribution and magnetic properties.

caption: STEM micrograph of the entire TEM lamella showing the characteristic cell structure formed in the sample processed at 250 W, 1400 mm s-1, and 50 μm hatch distance.
summary: This STEM image displays the overall cell structure of the TEM lamella for the sample processed with optimized parameters (VED = 60 J mm-3). Acquired along a <100> zone axis, the micrograph provides a comprehensive view of the microstructural morphology resulting from the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Calibrated yield surfaces for the long, short, and top sections, featuring comparisons with von Mises and Hosford yield criteria for uniaxial and equibiaxial tension states.
summary: Calibrated yield surfaces are presented for the long, short, and top sections, with the long section showing a minor shift at the biaxial point. The plot includes von Mises and Hosford yield surfaces as benchmarks, while specific loading conditions like uniaxial tension at various angles and equibiaxial tension are clearly denoted.

caption: Immunofluorescence visualization of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6 at 1 week post-implantation, highlighting local inflammatory microenvironment modulation.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining quantifies the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6 to assess hydrogel scaffold modulation of the local inflammatory microenvironment. At 1 week post-implantation, the control group displays extensive green fluorescence signals in IL-1β staining, indicating a robust early inflammatory response compared to the modified scaffold groups.

caption: High-magnification TEM image showing parallel dislocation arrays within ultrafine crystals of HST alloy, resulting from high-stress dynamic loading.
summary: Captured at a strain rate of 3000/s, this TEM image illustrates the presence of parallel dislocations within the ultrafine crystals of the HST alloy. These dislocation structures are a direct consequence of the high-stress environment experienced during dynamic compression, contributing to the material's overall deformation mechanism.

caption: Wire EDM cutting procedure applying an offset to account for kerf width and polishing allowance to achieve a near-center longitudinal section.
summary: To obtain a longitudinal section near the sample center, an offset is applied during the wire EDM cutting process. This offset accounts for the kerf width, which includes the wire diameter and spark gap, as well as a designated polishing allowance, ensuring the final section is accurately positioned for analysis.

caption: Experimental LUS B-Scan data showing particle velocity in the surface normal direction as a function of shifting unit position and time for an aluminum weld seam model.
summary: Experimental LUS B-Scan data for an aluminum weld seam model is presented, mapping particle velocity in the surface normal direction against the position of the linear shifting unit and time. This plot demonstrates the experimental response, which is compared against numerical simulations to validate the accuracy of the LUS technique.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of IN718 alloy samples subjected to plasma nitriding at varying temperatures, illustrating the evolution of crystalline phases.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns of IN718 alloy samples after undergoing plasma nitriding at different temperatures. The patterns reveal the influence of the nitriding process on the formation and transformation of crystalline phases, reflecting the structural changes occurring within the perfect and non-perfect crystals of the alloy.

caption: Deformation behavior of the B15-0.5 sample at different strain levels, illustrating the structural response during the two-step deformation process.
summary: The deformation behavior of the B15-0.5 sample is captured at various strain levels to illustrate the two-step process. These simulation results demonstrate how the structural geometry evolves under compressive loads, providing a visual validation of the mechanical response observed in the corresponding stress-strain curve for this specific lattice configuration.

caption: Chemical composition of the Ti64 powder feedstock expressed in weight percentage, as specified by the EOS M400-4 datasheet.
summary: This table details the chemical composition of the Ti64 powder in weight percent. Sourced from the EOS M400-4 datasheet, the data confirms the elemental constituents of the alloy, ensuring that the feedstock meets the required specifications for the fabrication of the additively manufactured base material used in this study.

caption: Electrical output performance of solar cells protected by pure COC and various COCA coversheets measured under controlled neodymium light conditions.
summary: Electrical output measurements for solar cells with pure COC and COCA coversheets are shown under regulated neodymium light conditions. Consistent with sunlight testing, increasing the alumina concentration in the COCA4 sample leads to a measurable decrease in the overall effectiveness of the photovoltaic device performance.

caption: Final state of the filling repair sample following the completion of the layer-by-layer deposition process, showing the filled groove.
summary: The final state of the filling repair is captured after the completion of the deposition process. The groove has been successfully filled layer-by-layer using the specified scan pattern, resulting in approximately 1 mm of excess deposition, confirming the successful restoration of the substrate surface geometry.

caption: DCPD evolution plotted against fatigue cycles for SSM and HPDC specimens during a run-out test at 95 MPa without failure.
summary: Run-out test results at 95 MPa show the DCPD curve fluctuating between 0.01 V and 0.025 V. Unlike the failure tests, this panel represents a condition where no specimen failure occurred, providing a baseline for stable DCPD behavior during long-term cyclic loading without structural degradation.

caption: STEM image of the TMAZ in 1561 alloy showing Al3Zr particles with pronounced coarsening exceeding 40 nm and limited number density.
summary: This STEM image displays the TMAZ microstructure of the 1561 alloy.
