summary: The phase field topology model provides a diffuse representation of the crack profile within the thermo-mechanical system. By utilizing a phase field approach, this simulation captures the crack evolution and topology, offering a continuous mathematical description of the fracture process that complements the sharp crack model shown in panel a.

caption: Experimental fatigue life data for Al 2024-T3 alloy plotted against predicted values generated by the proposed model, T–K model, and Miner’s rule.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between experimental fatigue life and predicted outcomes for Al 2024-T3 alloy. The proposed model exhibits good agreement with the experimental data, confirming its effectiveness in estimating fatigue life when compared against the T–K model and Miner’s rule across the tested experimental range.

caption: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-10Ni alloy at 102(2) GPa, reaching a maximum temperature of 2362(140) K.
summary: This panel displays the electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-10Ni alloy at 102 GPa up to 2362 K. The experimental data follows a quasi-linear trend at high temperatures, consistent with the Bloch-Grüneisen model. Comparisons are provided against previous experimental results for pure hcp-Fe at similar pressures to highlight the alloy's resistivity characteristics.

caption: Residual distribution plot for the width deviation prediction model trained on 10% of the input data using three features.
summary: Depicting the residuals for the best-performing model trained on a reduced dataset, this plot uses three input features while limiting the training input to 10% of the total data. The visualization highlights the model's predictive consistency and error distribution when operating under constrained training data availability.

caption: Particle size distribution of TA15 powder, indicating an average diameter of 72.06 μm.
summary: Particle size distribution analysis of the TA15 powder reveals a specific statistical spread of diameters. The calculated average diameter for the TA15 powder is 72.06 μm. This quantitative measurement confirms the size characteristics of the matrix material used prior to the mixing and milling processes with the B4C ceramic phase.

caption: Raman spectral data comparing supporting materials and different catalysts to evaluate structural disorder and defect density within the carbon framework.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is utilized here to characterize the carbon-based supports and catalysts. The spectral data serves to evaluate the structural disorder and the density of defects present within the carbon framework, which are essential factors in determining the overall quality and potential catalytic performance of the synthesized materials.

caption: Baseline classifier anomaly tracing results for the gear shaft at Layer 25, showing incomplete identification of insufficient gas and failure to detect collapse regions.
summary: At Layer 25, the baseline classifier demonstrates limited performance in process tracing. The model fails to fully identify the extent of the injected insufficient gas anomaly and entirely misses the collapse anomaly, resulting in incomplete and inaccurate tracing of the gear shaft fabrication process compared to the fused model.

caption: STEM micrograph of cured DMA1/PEMA formulation containing 5 wt% of BCP4, exhibiting significant nanoobject agglomeration.
summary: Visualized via STEM, this cured DMA1/PEMA resin incorporates 5 wt% of BCP4. The micrograph highlights the presence of nanoobject agglomerates, consistent with the structural behavior observed in the BCP3-containing material, demonstrating that these PMMA-PDMS-PMMA block copolymers do not achieve well-dispersed nano-scale structures in this resin.

caption: Heating profiles for the debinding and sintering of DLP-printed SiO2 bodies, with dashed lines representing the natural cooling process.
summary: The heating profiles illustrate the thermal cycles used for debinding and sintering the 3D-printed SiO2 bodies. This system enables the fastest overall heating for such green bodies, allowing for a controllable shrinking ratio. The dashed lines indicate the natural cooling phase following the ultra-rapid heating at 100 °C min−1.

caption: SAED pattern along the [1–10] zone axis of the surrounding host lattice, where the white arrowhead indicates diffraction spots characteristic of the γ′ phase.
summary: This SAED pattern corresponds to the host lattice crystal grain in dark contrast surrounding the precipitate. Careful inspection reveals faint diffraction spots at hhl positions with odd indices, marked by a tilted red arrowhead, which are allowed in the γ′ phase but forbidden in the γ phase, confirming the presence of γ′ hardening phase.

caption: Schematic illustration detailing the configuration and loading geometry of the three-point bending test setup.
summary: This schematic provides a clear visual description of the three-point bending test configuration used to evaluate the mechanical properties of the wrought and WAAM specimens. It outlines the fundamental experimental setup, including the support and loading points necessary to generate the force-displacement curves presented in the accompanying panels.

caption: Time-dependent indentation depth profiles for single crystalline Ni under 0.125 N and 0.088 N loads, comparing experimental measurements with finite element (FE) simulation results.
summary: This plot illustrates the indentation depth as a function of time for single crystalline Ni subjected to loads of 0.125 N and 0.088 N. By comparing experimental data with FE model predictions, the figure demonstrates that the simulation effectively reproduces the deformation behavior of the material across these different loading conditions.

caption: Al–Mg2Si pseudo-binary phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic equilibrium states for the 6063 aluminum alloy system.
summary: The Al–Mg2Si pseudo-binary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic framework for the 6063 aluminum alloy joint. This diagram maps the equilibrium phases present during the diffusion bonding process conducted at 570 °C, 4 MPa, for 90 minutes, establishing the baseline for understanding the alloy's compositional behavior and phase stability during bonding.

caption: Pole figure (PF) of the 250W sample, showing the texture intensity of the BCC phase.
summary: This pole figure analysis of the 250W sample characterizes the texture of the BCC phase. The data reveals that the martensite (BCC) texture exhibits maximum intensity at the <100> pole. This analysis is essential for understanding the texture characteristics of BCC and FCC phases within the as-deposited additive manufacturing samples.

caption: Mott–Schottky plots showing the inverse square of capacitance versus potential for L-PBF NiTi samples A2, A4, and A6 after 7 days of immersion in 0.9 wt.% NaCl solution.
summary: Mott–Schottky curves for L-PBF NiTi samples A2, A4, and A6 are presented after 7 days of immersion in a 0.9 wt.% NaCl solution. These plots characterize the electrochemical behavior of the passive films formed on the surfaces of the three different L-PBF NiTi specimens under the specified corrosive conditions.

caption: XZ-axis torch holder assembly designed for continuous welding speed.
summary: The XZ-axis torch holder assembly is coupled with the welding machine to maintain a consistent and continuous welding speed. By utilizing two distinct axes—X for horizontal movement and Z for vertical positioning—this CNC-controlled mechanism ensures the torch follows the required path accurately throughout the multi-layer WAAM fabrication process.

caption: Arrhenius plot of ln[sinh(ασ)] versus 1000/T for the HIP-1230 alloy, showing the average slope used to calculate the activation energy.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between ln[sinh(ασ)] and the reciprocal temperature 1000/T for the HIP-1230 alloy. The average slope derived from these relationships across various strain rates is used to determine the activation energy, a key parameter in the constitutive equations for hot deformation.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of initial pre-alloyed NiTi powders showing the baseline thermal response prior to processing.
summary: This panel displays the differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve for initial pre-alloyed NiTi powders. It serves as the baseline thermal characterization for the material before undergoing directed energy deposition (DED) fabrication, providing a reference point for evaluating the phase transformation behavior of the subsequent fabricated specimens.

caption: Cycle-averaged oxidation profiles derived from TGA data, comparing the material behavior at reduction temperatures of 750 °C and 850 °C, calculated as the average of three experimental repetitions for each cycle.
summary: Averaged oxidation curves are presented for reduction temperatures of 750 °C and 850 °C. These profiles represent the mean behavior derived from three complete redox cycle repetitions for each condition, highlighting the distinct kinetic differences observed when varying the reduction temperature during the experimental process.

caption: TDA desorption rate spectrum for 316L stainless steel charged at 1000 bar.
summary: Shown here is the TDA spectrum for 316L stainless steel charged at 1000 bar. The ion current indicates a higher desorption rate compared to the 200 bar charging condition. This measurement highlights the significant influence of charging pressure on the total hydrogen concentration and desorption kinetics within the 316L material.

caption: Experimental propagation of 3-spot triangle RPVBs with topological charge l=2 and power order n=10, measured at a constant distance d=200 mm with a propagation distance z=2000 mm.
summary: Panel d shows the experimental propagation of 3-spot triangle RPVBs with a topological charge of l=2 and a power order of n=10. The beam is analyzed at a propagation distance of 2000 mm and a measuring distance of 200 mm, highlighting the influence of the power exponent on spatial distribution.

caption: Enlarged view of the vertical section from panel (b), highlighting specific phase boundaries and precipitation regions in the Al-0.6Sc-xTi system.
summary: This enlarged section of the Al-0.6Sc-xTi equilibrium phase diagram provides a detailed view of the phase boundaries. Consistent with the broader diagram, it confirms the co-precipitation of Al3Ti and Al3Sc phases as titanium atoms diffuse into the aluminum, offering a clearer resolution of the phase transformation regions.

caption: Magnetization (M–H) curves of Ce60Ni25Al15-xGax ribbons measured at 5 K for x = 0, 4, 8, and 15, with an inset highlighting the slight reduction in magnetization as Ga content increases.
summary: The magnetization behavior of Ce60Ni25Al15-xGax glassy ribbons is characterized by M-H curves at 5 K. Analysis of these curves demonstrates that magnetization values decrease slightly as the Ga concentration increases from 0 to 15. The inset provides a magnified view of this trend, confirming the systematic reduction in magnetic response with Ga substitution.

caption: Temperature evolution curves recorded at the calibration point, comparing data from thermocouples and an infrared camera set to an emission coefficient of 0.32.
summary: This line graph compares the temperature evolution at the calibration point as measured by thermocouples and an infrared camera. By setting the emission coefficient to 0.32, the infrared camera's readings are validated against the thermocouple data, confirming the accuracy of the thermal monitoring system used for the thin-wall structures.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) curves for metamaterial matrices and their corresponding unit cells (C-T and C-X), comparing experimental dilatometry measurements with numerical simulation results.
summary: This panel displays the measured CTE of metamaterial matrices alongside their respective unit cells, C-T and C-X. Experimental dilatometry data are plotted as solid lines, while corresponding metamaterial and unit cell simulations are represented by dashed lines, illustrating the thermal expansion behavior of the 2x1 and 2x2 unit cell matrices.

caption: Fatigue crack growth curve for the PSP_3 specimen, characterized by a roughly linear progression without a discernible kink.
summary: The FCG curve for the PSP_3 specimen variant demonstrates a roughly linear progression throughout the test. Unlike the thinner variants, this specimen shows no discernible kink in the crack growth behavior, with data points below the lower validity limit excluded to ensure the accuracy of the results.

caption: Calculated minimum energy path for the third NbTaV sample realization, plotting energy against dislocation center position x1, with an inset showing the dislocation line configuration determined by atomistic NEB and PN slip distribution.
summary: The energy landscape for the third NbTaV sample realization is shown here, detailing the minimum energy path for dislocation glide. By comparing NEB and PN model results, the panel illustrates the energy barriers. The inset provides a structural view of the dislocation line at the local minimum energy position.

caption: Strength contribution of the ρ climb network at 788 °C, showing the ratio of network-induced strength to total climb resistance across different creep loading parameters.
summary: Displayed at 788 °C, this heatmap maps the proportion of resistance derived from the ρ climb network relative to the total climb resistance. By varying creep loading conditions, the plot reveals the temperature-dependent evolution of network strength, demonstrating how the accumulated network influences overall dislocation climb resistance at higher temperatures.

caption: W 4f XPS spectrum of Mo2WS6, featuring characteristic peaks at 37.8 eV and 35.8 eV corresponding to W 4f 5/2 and W 4f 7/2 orbitals.
summary: The W 4f XPS spectrum of the Mo2WS6 composite exhibits characteristic peaks at 37.8 eV and 35.8 eV, which are assigned to the W 4f 5/2 and W 4f 7/2 orbitals. These results, when compared to MoS2, suggest electron transfer and interactions occurring within the composite material structure.

caption: TGA analysis curve of CP, illustrating the thermal degradation profile and mass loss characteristics of the composite material.
summary: The TGA analysis curve provides a quantitative assessment of the thermal stability and degradation behavior of the CP composite. By monitoring mass loss as a function of temperature, this analysis characterizes the thermal decomposition profile of the material, offering essential data on the composite's structural integrity under increasing thermal stress.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the IJP 6L catalyst layer, featuring the distribution of void and solid phases supplemented by pore space skeletons.
summary: This panel displays a 3D reconstruction of the IJP 6L catalyst layer derived from FIB-SEM tomography. The visualization highlights the spatial distribution of void and solid phases within the material, further enhanced by the inclusion of pore space skeletons to characterize the internal structural morphology of the catalyst layer.

caption: TEM image of Ti–5Cu displaying acicular nanoparticles precipitated within the Ti matrix.
summary: Acicular nanoparticles are observed within the Ti matrix of the Ti–5Cu alloy as shown in this TEM micrograph. These precipitates are identified as Ti2Cu phases, which are dispersed throughout the matrix to serve as heterogeneous nucleation sites, effectively inhibiting grain growth during the material's thermal or mechanical processing.

caption: Time-dependent CO production rate and corresponding selectivity toward CO for CO2-PCECs, measured at 400 °C and 500 °C under a constant current density of 50 mA/cm2.
summary: The CO production rate and selectivity toward CO are plotted as a function of time for CO2-PCECs. Operating at 400 °C and 500 °C with a constant current density of 50 mA/cm2, these data points illustrate the catalytic efficiency and product selectivity stability of the SFM-Ni0.175 negative electrode system during testing.

caption: Parity plot comparing Gradient Boosting predicted permeability against CFD-calculated values for the training dataset, demonstrating a high correlation along the 1:1 line.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the performance of the Gradient Boosting algorithm on the training dataset. The results show that 99.8% of the cross-validated variance is explained by the model, as the predicted permeability values align closely with the CFD-evaluated data along the 1:1 parity line, confirming excellent training accuracy.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility (χ) validated through adjustment of experimental data.
summary: This panel illustrates the temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility, χ, validated through the adjustment of experimental data using Langevin’s model. This modeling approach allows for the accurate prediction of magnetic permeability at higher magnetic fields, ensuring consistency between experimental observations and theoretical projections across varying thermal conditions.

caption: Nyquist plot illustrating the electrochemical impedance behavior of the XZ section of Wall 0.
summary: Electrochemical impedance behavior for the XZ section of Wall 0 is shown in this Nyquist plot. The observed reduction in semicircle diameter serves as an indicator of material degradation. Despite this trend, the formation of corrosion products after two days of exposure acts to slow down the corrosion kinetics.

caption: Ashby map displaying the correlation between yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) for the alloys detailed in Table 4.
summary: Representing the relationship between yield strength and ultimate tensile strength, this Ashby map compares the mechanical characteristics of the alloys listed in Table 4. The visualization highlights the strength-related performance metrics of the materials, supporting the comparative analysis of the alloy series as described in the research findings.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Al–Ni–V system at 1300 K, incorporating experimental data points from Hong et al. and Cotton et al.
summary: This calculated isothermal section of the Al–Ni–V system at 1300 K illustrates phase relationships, including experimental data from Hong et al. and Cotton et al. The diagram highlights the Ni-based fcc region, which is cut off at the pseudo-eutectoid temperature, providing a comprehensive view of the system's phase stability at this temperature.

caption: Mechanical performance of NFC-alginate scaffolds crosslinked with metal carbonates, tested after 7 days of storage in a 0.9% NaCl saline solution.
summary: Panel h shows the mechanical testing results for NFC-alginate scaffolds stored in a 0.9% NaCl solution for 7 days. The figure compares the effects of different crosslinker ion concentrations on the mechanical properties, illustrating the performance of the scaffolds when subjected to an isotonic saline environment during the maturation process.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of extruded Alloy SZ3 showing partially coarsened Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates that retain thermal stability due to the Zr-shell.
summary: Unlike Alloy S3, extruded Alloy SZ3 retains partially coarsened Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates. Dark-field TEM analysis shows an average size increase of approximately 100% and a number density decrease of 42.2%. This enhanced thermal stability is attributed to the protective Zr-shell surrounding the Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates during the extrusion process.

caption: Position of the long spacing peak plotted against the applied strain.
summary: The position of the long spacing peak is tracked as a function of strain in this plot. This measurement characterizes the structural periodicity changes within the sample, reflecting how the internal spacing of the material responds to the mechanical cycles applied during the experimental testing procedure.

caption: SAED pattern obtained from the SAED2 region, indexed to the cubic α-Fe(Co,Si) phase within the dendritic morphology.
summary: The SAED pattern from the SAED2 region is successfully indexed to the cubic α-Fe(Co,Si) phase. This diffraction data confirms the crystalline nature of the dendritic morphology observed in the TEM image, providing a clear structural characterization of the secondary phase present within the AF sample.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the integration of machine learning with multiscale computational approaches within the Materials Genome Engineering (MGE) paradigm for additive manufacturing materials research.
summary: This schematic outlines the integration of machine learning and multiscale computational methods within the Materials Genome Engineering framework. It highlights how these advanced computational strategies are applied to accelerate materials research and development in additive manufacturing, reflecting the transformative advances enabled by AI in modern materials science and engineering.

caption: Comparative analysis of the elastic modulus and nano-hardness values for Nd-Fe-B magnets, highlighting the influence of distinct laser scanning strategies on mechanical properties.
summary: This panel presents the elastic modulus and nano-hardness values derived from nanoindentation testing of LPBF-built Nd-Fe-B magnets. By comparing these mechanical metrics across different scanning strategies, the results quantify how specific laser processing parameters affect the hardness and stiffness of the final magnetic components, reflecting the material's overall mechanical quality.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots for conventional and LPBF-fabricated samples with varying hatch spacing, showing potential versus capacitance behavior in sodium chloride solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots for conventional and LPBF-fabricated samples with varying hatch spacing are presented for tests in sodium chloride solution. All curves exhibit a negative slope before reaching a potential of -0.2 V, indicating p-type semiconductor behavior prior to entering the passivation region for these materials.

caption: Misorientation angle distribution plot for the BD sample, quantifying the frequency of grain boundary types present after tensile fracture.
summary: The misorientation angle distribution for the BD sample provides a quantitative assessment of the grain boundary population. By plotting the frequency of misorientation angles, this histogram characterizes the deformation-induced grain boundary evolution, serving as a comparative reference for evaluating the structural response of the material under different loading directions.

caption: Initial stage of the tool cutting into the γ′ phase at 100 m/s, revealing a large number of atoms distributed in the amorphous region.
summary: Captured at the start of the tool cutting into the γ′ phase at 100 m/s, this MD snapshot shows significant structural disruption. A large number of atoms are distributed within the amorphous region, indicating that the cutting process has induced substantial localized disorder as the tool interacts with the γ′ phase.

caption: Loss curve for the DeepCORAL unsupervised domain adaptation method.
summary: DeepCORAL displays a loss curve characterized by a rapid climb in accuracy within the first 20 epochs. This performance trend is directly linked to the decrease of its specific penalty terms during the initial training phase, illustrating the method's convergence behavior in the unsupervised domain adaptation framework.

caption: Overview of the Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) experimental configuration, featuring an ABB IRB 2600 robot, a 2-DOF workpiece positioner, a Fronius TransPuls Synergic 5000 CMT welder, and integrated monitoring sensors including a laser profilometer and camera.
summary: This experimental setup illustrates the integrated WAAM system used for fabrication and data acquisition. Key components include the ABB IRB 2600 robotic arm, a 2-DOF positioning table, and a Fronius CMT welding system. Monitoring is facilitated by a laser profilometer, a camera, and a welding electric signal sensor for process control.

caption: Correlation matrix derived from principal component analysis (PCA) illustrating the relationships between various laser cladding process parameters and the resulting clad characteristics.
summary: Principal component analysis (PCA) was employed to evaluate the interdependencies between process parameters and clad characteristics following process optimization. The resulting correlation matrix provides a quantitative visualization of these relationships, highlighting how specific input variables influence the final properties of the clad material within the studied experimental framework.

caption: De-convoluted high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectrum of the Fe 2p core level for FeCr2O4, showing multiple peak fitting to identify oxidation states.
summary: High-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis of the Fe 2p core level for FeCr2O4 is presented through de-convoluted peak fitting. This spectral data allows for the identification of the specific oxidation states of iron within the composite material, contributing to the overall characterization of the chromite sample's chemical composition.

caption: Fatigue behavior of the PLA/PCL blend after 6 weeks of SBF immersion, resulting in a fatigue limit of 11.5 MPa.
summary: At 6 weeks of immersion in the corrosive environment, the fatigue limit declines to 11.5 MPa, marking a 15.4% decrease from the initial state. This reduction is attributed to the accumulation of microcracks and structural changes within the material caused by the prolonged exposure to the simulated body fluid.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction versus temperature plot for the Al-2.3Fe-2.7Cr-1.6Si alloy calculated using the TCAL9 database, illustrating the thermodynamic stability of various silicides and the α-Al matrix.
summary: This equilibrium calculation, performed using the TCAL9 database, models phase fractions as a function of temperature for the Al-2.3Fe-2.7Cr-1.6Si alloy. It predicts the formation of several silicides, including Al15M4Si2, Al9Fe2Si2, and Al13Cr4Si4, under long-term thermal equilibrium conditions, providing a baseline for understanding the precipitation sequence during alloy processing.

caption: Three-dimensional rendering of Fe-rich IMC particles (blue) and voids (red) in the undeformed state (ε = 0) for AA6111 and IBA6111 alloys.
summary: 3D rendering of Fe-rich IMC particles in blue and voids in red are displayed for the undeformed state. In this initial condition, scattered voids are observed in both samples, although they are more pronounced in the AA6111 sample, providing a baseline for analyzing void evolution during subsequent deformation.

caption: Average cutting force profile observed during the VSM process of superalloy honeycomb at an inclination angle of β = 10°.
summary: This panel displays the average cutting force measured during the VSM process of superalloy honeycomb at an inclination angle of 10°. By comparing this result with other inclination angles, the figure demonstrates the sensitivity of the cutting force to the specific orientation of the honeycomb structure during machining.

caption: Top-down view of 3D structured alginate and cellulose aerogels compared with their corresponding birefringence patterns, highlighting the structural organization.
summary: Top-down views of 3D structured alginate and cellulose aerogels are displayed alongside their birefringence patterns. These images confirm that molded polymer contraction propagates 3D strains throughout the depth of the construct, with birefringence patterns agreeing with stress simulations to validate the encoded 3D structural anisotropy.

caption: Ashby plot of ultimate tensile strength versus elongation comparing this study to previously reported WAAM-prepared and as-cast/as-extruded AZ31 alloys.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the strength-ductility synergy of the UV specimens in relation to previously reported data for AZ31 alloys manufactured via WAAM or traditional techniques. The UV specimens demonstrate improved mechanical properties, showing performance that is comparable to or exceeds the benchmarks established in the existing literature.

caption: Extended filiform corrosion morphology on the SC sample surface after 30 minutes of immersion.
summary: Extended filiform corrosion morphology is observed on the SC sample surface after 30 minutes of immersion. The corroded region expands outwards from the edges, indicating a continuous propagation mechanism that would eventually lead to complete coverage of the sample surface as the corrosion process progresses.

caption: Isomorphic beta-stabilizing element effects on the Ti6Al4V phase diagram.
summary: Isomorphic beta-stabilizing elements, such as Mo, V, Ta, and Nb, are depicted reducing the beta-phase transformation temperature. These elements possess similar atomic radii and lattice structures to titanium, allowing for infinite solid solubility in the beta-phase and effectively expanding the beta-phase region in the Ti6Al4V system.

caption: Unit cell models representing pure material configurations with thicknesses ranging from 1 mm to 10 mm used for electromagnetic simulation.
summary: Unit cell models with thicknesses varying from 1 mm to 10 mm are depicted to represent the base material configurations. These models were imported into CST simulation software to analyze the influence of material thickness and CF concentration on electromagnetic absorption performance, serving as the foundation for subsequent reflection coefficient simulations.

caption: Storage modulus (E') versus temperature for PLA specimens aged at room temperature.
summary: Storage modulus measurements for PLA filters aged at room temperature demonstrate a minimal deterioration of 19% at the 35 °C starting point. This mechanical test highlights the relative stability of the pure PLA polymer matrix when subjected to aging conditions compared to the reinforced composite samples.

caption: Tabulated melting points and evaporation temperatures for the materials utilized in the study.
summary: This table presents a compilation of thermal properties for the materials used in the research. Specifically, it lists the melting points derived from reference [24] and the evaporation temperatures sourced from references [25,26]. These values provide essential thermal data for understanding the phase transition characteristics of the experimental materials.

caption: Pre-test configuration of the metamaterial array observed from the Y–Z plane perspective.
summary: Captured before the mechanical compression test, this image shows the metamaterial array oriented along the Y–Z plane. This setup is part of the Y–Z test series, where horizontal displacements in the Y direction are measured across five specimens to determine the Poisson's ratio of the metamaterial structure.

caption: FTIR comparison of silicate paste, PVA gels, and the final BSPC, identifying chemical bonding and functional group interactions.
summary: FTIR comparisons among the silicate paste, PVA gels, and the final BSPC identify the chemical bonding and functional group interactions present in the composite. This spectroscopic analysis confirms the successful integration of the components, providing evidence of the chemical environment at the interface of the silicate and PVA phases.

caption: Surface morphology of the 0° LPBF Inconel 625 sample after 24 hours of oxidation at 900 °C, showing a homogeneous oxide layer with ridges aligned along grain boundaries.
summary: The 0° LPBF Inconel 625 sample exhibits a homogeneous oxide layer covering the entire surface after 24 hours of oxidation at 900 °C. Notably, the oxide ridges are observed to grow specifically along the grain boundaries, indicating a distinct influence of the sample orientation on the oxidation morphology.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the C–Ni–Ta system at 1480 °C, highlighting the dissolution of TaC and the hypereutectic composition of the Ni–Ta binary system.
summary: This isothermal section of the C–Ni–Ta system at 1480 °C illustrates the phase equilibria calculated via Thermo-Calc and the GHEA database. It demonstrates that Ni dissolves TaC, with the liquid composition shifting toward a specific point, while identifying the hypereutectic Ni–Ta composition as a potential brazing filler candidate.

caption: Structural representation of the Ni-X 2 /C interface model with dopants integrated into the TiNi 3 (0001) lattice.
summary: Representing the Ni-X 2 /C interface, this model illustrates the atomic arrangement of the TiNi 3 (0001) slab under specific doping conditions. It serves as a computational tool to explore how the placement of dopant atoms affects the interfacial bonding behavior between the TiNi 3 slab and the carbon substrate.

caption: Reduced easy-axis remanence plotted against the saturating field angle θ relative to the average hard-axis, comparing experimental measurements with the best-fit model.
summary: This plot illustrates the easy-axis fallback measurement, showing a precipitous drop in remanence as the saturating field approaches the hard axis. Open squares represent measured data, while the solid line shows the best fit of Eq. (2), yielding a standard deviation of 0.28° and a FWHM of 0.67°.

caption: Simplified 2D schematic diagram depicting a quadrilateral element with perpendicular half-diagonals.
summary: This simplified 2D schematic diagram provides a clear geometric representation of a quadrilateral element characterized by perpendicular half-diagonals. It serves to clarify the underlying discretization geometry used within the coupled CA-FE-CP model, aiding in the visualization of the computational elements employed in the simulation framework.

caption: EDS elemental mapping overlay corresponding to the sample plated at pH 13, showing the spatial distribution of Cu, Ti, C, and O.
summary: This EDS elemental mapping overlay for the pH 13 sample displays the spatial distribution of Cu, Ti, C, and O. The mapping highlights significant surface defects and irregular elemental coverage, reinforcing the conclusion that the plating solution pH critically influences the final quality and homogeneity of the Cu coating.

caption: Cluster map displaying the distribution trends of primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite, providing a visual representation of how martensite feature dimensions vary across different classification categories.
summary: This cluster map reveals the distribution trends of martensite types classified by the model. It provides a clear visualization of how the dimensions of martensite features vary, effectively distinguishing between primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite categories based on the calculated morphological data.

caption: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values for NiMo@NF determined during the first set of electrochemical experiments, presented with 95% confidence interval error bars.
summary: This panel displays the measured Cdl values for NiMo@NF during the first experimental set, accompanied by 95% confidence interval error bars. These electrochemical measurements provide a quantitative assessment of the double-layer capacitance, which is observed to increase following stress tests such as CP or CV cycling.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of the sensor plotted alongside its calculated lower envelope curve.
summary: The reflectance spectrum of the sensor is shown, accompanied by its lower envelope curve. This plot characterizes the optical response of the sensor, providing essential data for analyzing the performance and spectral properties of the acrylate/GO composite film integrated into the device.

caption: HNMR spectrum of CP displaying chemical shifts at 0.84 ppm (-CH₃), 1.81 ppm (-CH₂-), 3.6 ppm (-OCH₃), and 5.3 ppm (double-bond containing material).
summary: HNMR analysis of the synthesized CP reveals specific chemical shifts corresponding to the MMA monomer and PS surface components. Signals at 0.84 ppm, 1.81 ppm, and 3.6 ppm are attributed to the methyl, methylene, and methoxy groups of the MMA unit, while the 5.3 ppm shift indicates double-bond presence on the PS surface.

caption: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectrum of the SLM-316L stainless steel surface.
summary: This XPS survey spectrum characterizes the surface chemical composition of SLM-316L stainless steel specimens. The data provides a comprehensive overview of the elemental constituents present on the material surface, serving as a primary analytical tool for evaluating the surface state of the additively manufactured 316L stainless steel samples.

caption: Nyquist plots representing the impedance behavior of pristine and soaked electrodes.
summary: The Nyquist plots for the pristine and soaked electrodes are displayed in this panel. These impedance measurements characterize the electrochemical behavior of the materials, providing a baseline for understanding the charge-transfer resistance and diffusion properties of the electrodes before and after the soaking process.

caption: SEM morphology and corresponding Ca (purple) and Sr (red) EDS elemental maps of β-TCP and SrTCP powders.
summary: The morphology of β-TCP powder is shown alongside SEM and EDX spectrum images of SrTCP powder with different Sr doping content. Gray images represent the SEM morphology, while purple and red colors indicate the distribution of Ca and Sr elements, respectively, confirming the successful incorporation and distribution of strontium within the powder.

caption: Underneath view of the coaxial WP-DED printing head, showing the nozzle arrangement for the laser-DED process.
summary: The underneath view of the coaxial WP-DED printing head reveals the specific nozzle arrangement utilized in the Meltio M450 laser-DED system. This perspective clarifies the spatial orientation of the coaxial components, which are essential for the precise delivery of materials during the laser-directed energy deposition fabrication process.

caption: Microhardness variations measured across the transverse direction relative to the building direction (BD).
summary: This plot illustrates the microhardness distribution across the transverse direction of the TiAl MMC. The data is part of a comprehensive mechanical evaluation showing that the material possesses excellent compressive and high-temperature tensile strength, which is attributed to the specific distribution of reinforcing phases within the matrix.

caption: Experimental current versus applied potential curves recorded at varying flow rates, with an inset showing the corresponding mass transfer coefficients derived from ferro-ferricyanide testing.
summary: Experimental current versus applied potential curves were generated at different flow rates to evaluate electrochemical performance. The inset displays mass transfer coefficients obtained through a typical ferro-ferricyanide test, which is critical for assessing the efficiency of electrochemical processes dependent on mass transport considerations within the cell.

caption: Measured circuit current as a function of substrate concentration at a fixed 3 V potential.
summary: This plot displays the circuit current response to changes in substrate concentration at a constant 3 V potential. Higher substrate concentrations enhance electrolyte conductivity, which effectively reduces internal resistance within the reactor, resulting in an observed increase in the measured circuit current during the electrochemical process.

caption: Measured UV wavelength pattern captured at and beyond the focal plane.
summary: The UV wavelength pattern is presented here, showing the measured intensity profile at and beyond the focal plane. This data is part of a broader set of results, including blue wavelength measurements and simulations, which collectively validate the accuracy of the optical model and the simulation methodology used.

caption: SEM fractograph of the H-charged SX12 specimen revealing cuboidal γ′ precipitates, alongside stitched STEM images showing the cross-sectional area of the FIB-lifted-out sample.
summary: This panel displays an SEM fractograph of an H-charged SX12 specimen, highlighting the cuboidal morphology of the γ′ precipitates. Stitched STEM images provide a detailed cross-sectional view of the fracture surface, revealing that the H-induced crack propagation occurs primarily along the γ/γ′ interface parallel to the {001} planes.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction of the Base+Mn alloy in the T5 condition, displaying the spatial distribution of various microstructural features.
summary: This three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction illustrates the microstructure of the Base+Mn alloy in the T5 condition. The visualization provides a comprehensive view of the spatial arrangement of various phases and precipitates, serving as the foundational dataset for the subsequent proximity histogram analyses of the alloy's specific constituent features.

caption: Schematic illustration of the hourglass specimen geometry utilized for mechanical testing.
summary: This schematic illustrates the hourglass specimen geometry used in experimental testing. The specimens were produced via laser-based powder bed fusion as 18 mm diameter cylindrical bars, then machined and polished to achieve an hourglass shape with a 6 mm diameter at the gauge section for precise mechanical evaluation.

caption: 3D Atom Probe Tomography map illustrating the spatial distribution of Cu, Ni, Si, and Cr elements within the specimen heat-treated at 500 °C for 3 hours.
summary: This 3D Atom Probe Tomography map visualizes the distribution of Cu, Ni, Si, and Cr elements in a specimen subjected to a 500 °C/3h heat treatment. The reconstruction provides a detailed spatial overview of the elemental arrangement, serving as a foundational analysis for identifying precipitate populations within the alloy matrix.

caption: Tabulated parameters and design constraints defining the optimization case for the sandwich structure prosthesis.
summary: This table outlines the specific design variables, constant parameters, and applied constraints utilized in the optimization process for the sandwich structure prosthesis. It serves as the foundational reference for the optimization case, establishing the mathematical and physical boundaries required to determine the optimal configuration for the various prosthesis types.

caption: Schematic diagram of heat dissipation pathways during the CDED process, highlighting sustained lateral heat dissipation through sample sidewalls.
summary: Thermodynamic modeling confirms that the CDED process utilizes unidirectional upward laser movement to facilitate sustained lateral heat dissipation through the sample sidewalls. This mechanism, illustrated in the schematic, is critical for managing thermal gradients and ensuring consistent solidification conditions during the additive manufacturing of the material.

caption: Principal stress σ1 distribution across the mid-plane under self-weight and a 10.0 kN prestressing load.
summary: This simulation depicts the mid-plane principal stress σ1 under the combined influence of self-weight and a 10.0 kN prestressing load. By increasing the post-tensioning force, the panel demonstrates the resulting shift in stress patterns, allowing for a detailed assessment of how higher loads affect the internal contact forces and stress distribution.

caption: Ni 2p XPS spectra of Ni/ZnO, Ni/ZrO2, and Ni-Zn/ZrO2 catalysts reduced at 800 °C, showing the presence of Ni0 species at a binding energy of approximately 852.0 eV.
summary: The Ni 2p XPS spectra for the reduced catalysts reveal the successful reduction of NiO to metallic Ni0 species. All catalysts exhibit a characteristic peak at a binding energy of approximately 852.0 eV, confirming the presence of Ni0 after the 800 °C H2/Ar reduction process.

caption: Third independent component (IC3) obtained through ICA, showcasing a localized thermal signature indicative of a tertiary defect feature within the v1 dataset.
summary: The third independent component, IC3, provides a localized thermal signature isolated from the v1 dataset. This component highlights specific thermal variations that are indicative of a tertiary defect feature. Together with IC1 and IC2, this result completes the decomposition of distinct thermal signatures associated with specific material defects.

caption: Stereographic representation of the Orientation Distribution Function (ODF) for the fcc phase, derived from the region marked by the white dashed line in panel a.
summary: Representing the crystallographic texture of the fcc phase, this pole figure shows the stereographic projection of the ODF. The data is extracted specifically from the interface region delimited by the white dashed line in the IPF map, providing a focused view of the fcc phase orientation at the interface.

caption: Interference fringes observed on a projection screen when the phase difference across the PLM is zero.
summary: This panel displays the interference fringe pattern captured on a projection screen under the condition of zero phase difference across the PLM. The projected image illustrates the optical interference behavior, providing a baseline visualization of the fringe distribution when the phase shift is nullified in the experimental setup.

caption: Finite element model illustrating the geometric configuration and the applied boundary constraints used for numerical analysis.
summary: This panel presents the finite element model setup, specifically highlighting the boundary condition configuration employed in the numerical simulations. It serves as the foundational representation of the physical system, defining the constraints necessary for the subsequent computational analysis of the material's mechanical response under the specified loading conditions.

caption: Effective area calculation for the single-layer line bead geometry based on 3D scan results.
summary: Effective area measurements for the single-layer line bead geometry are presented here, utilizing 3D scan data. As indicated by the reference, this specific measurement process is crucial for characterizing the bead geometry without destruction, providing a precise quantitative assessment of the effective cross-sectional area of the deposited material.

caption: Additional EDS-based weight percentage profile showing compositional variations within the as-fractured SLM316LSS microstructure.
summary: This panel provides further EDS-based weight percentage data for the as-fractured SLM316LSS specimen. By mapping the elemental distribution along the scan line, this profile complements the structural observations, offering detailed insights into the chemical homogeneity and potential segregation patterns present in the material after the laser melting process.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile and GP prediction for the <111> grain orientation at an axial position of r = 6 mm.
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction peak, represented by a red solid line, alongside the corresponding GP prediction for the <111> grain family. The data is acquired at a radial distance of 6 mm from the sample center, illustrating the alignment between experimental diffraction results and theoretical GP model predictions.

caption: Automated robotic arm performing the insertion of short reinforcing bars into a concrete structure.
summary: This photograph illustrates the automated robotic short rebar insertion process. A robotic arm is shown precisely placing reinforcement elements into a concrete matrix, demonstrating the integration of automated reinforcement techniques within the SC3DP manufacturing workflow to enhance structural integrity during the additive construction process.

caption: Projection of the O phase highlighted in blue, showing the orientation relationship between the O phase, B2 matrix, and alpha-2 phase.
summary: The O phase with a blue Euler orientation in the IPF map is analyzed here. Projections of the <110>O and <001>O directions show a high degree of coincidence with the < >B2 and <0001>alpha-2 directions, respectively, indicating specific crystallographic alignment between the O phase and the surrounding matrix.

caption: Scheil model-predicted phase weight fractions for case 5, indicating the formation of (Nb, Ti)C at 2 wt% and the emergence of σ and δ phases instead of carbides.
summary: For case 5, the Scheil model calculation predicts the weight fraction of phases, showing (Nb, Ti)C at 2 wt%. Notably, neither M23C6 nor M7C3 are calculated as stable phases in this case, while the model estimates the formation of other phases, specifically the σ and δ phases.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of HPCA at DS = 0.4, with an inset schematic of near-infrared selective reflectance.
summary: This reflectance spectrum for HPCA at DS = 0.4 shows the selective light reflectance properties. The inset schematic illustrates the mechanism of selective reflectance in the near-infrared range, confirming that the reflected wavelength becomes more prominent as the degree of substitution increases.

caption: Isothermal section of the ternary phase diagram at 1000 K, focusing on the specific concentration region of interest.
summary: This figure displays a portion of the ternary phase diagram at an isothermal temperature of 1000 K. The visualization focuses on a specific concentration range relevant to the study. These calculations were restricted to the region of the phase diagram around the concentrations of interest to provide precise thermodynamic insights.

caption: Progression of the out-of-channel cross-slip mechanism as the dislocation navigates around the preexisting line defect.
summary: The image displays the progression of the out-of-channel cross-slip mechanism in 316L stainless steel. As the dislocation encounters the preexisting line defect, it is forced to deviate from its original path, demonstrating the material's response to internal structural impediments during straining at elevated temperatures.

caption: Machined aluminum wall surface featuring transverse grooves prepared for subsequent friction stir processing.
summary: Following the WAAM process, the aluminum wall underwent transverse machining on both sides to ensure a uniform and smooth surface. This panel illustrates the resulting wall geometry, including the specific grooves created to facilitate the subsequent friction stir processing stage.

caption: Distribution of 20,000 virtual alloy samples generated by the VAE model.
summary: The distribution of 20,000 virtual alloy sample data points generated by the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) is visualized here. These blue dots represent the synthetic data produced by the model, allowing for an assessment of how well the VAE captures the underlying structure of the original alloy dataset.

caption: High-angle angular dark field (HAADF) image of SLM Al-50wt%Si alloy showing the Al matrix, primary Si, and eutectic Si phases.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image of the SLM Al-50wt%Si alloy reveals the distinct microstructural features of the material. The Al matrix, primary Si, and eutectic Si phases are clearly observable. A blue scanning line is superimposed across the interface of the primary Si and Al matrix to facilitate subsequent elemental analysis.

caption: Microhardness values as a function of interlayer time for tensile bars and cantilever specimens, showing the influence of layer thickness on heat accumulation.
summary: Microhardness measurements are plotted against interlayer time for different specimen geometries. The results reveal a geometry-agnostic effect where increased layer thickness facilitates heat accumulation, impacting microhardness more significantly than microstructure. While most data follows a consistent trend, specific conditions like the 60 µm layer thickness show occasional deviations.

caption: Zr1-MC25 composite surface at 70X magnification showing smooth fracture areas interspersed with microcapsule rupture cavities and matrix tearing.
summary: At 70X magnification, the Zr1-MC25 composite surface appears relatively smooth. The fracture morphology is defined by the presence of microcapsule rupture cavities and localized matrix tearing, indicating the interaction between the zirconia fibres and the self-healing microcapsules during the fracture process.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from Berkovich nanoindentation performed at the center of the TiNiCu deposit for varying laser power settings.
summary: This panel displays load-displacement curves derived from Berkovich nanoindentation tests conducted at the center of the TiNiCu deposit. The data illustrates the mechanical response of the material under varying laser power conditions, utilizing an indentor with an edge radius of approximately 100 nm to characterize the deposit's indentation behavior.

caption: Surface morphology of rolled TA31 alloy after polishing and potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) testing.
summary: Rolled TA31 alloy surface morphology is visualized after undergoing polishing and potentiodynamic polarization testing. This microscopy analysis serves to investigate the corrosion behavior and surface roughness of the material, providing a baseline for comparing the structural integrity and pit defects formed during electrochemical corrosion experiments.

caption: Grain orientation spread map and corresponding inverse pole figure for the HS zone.
summary: The HS zone exhibits a grain orientation spread map and corresponding inverse pole figure. Analysis of this region reveals the presence of low-intensity <111> //RD and <001> //RD fiber textures, which are characteristic of the strain zones observed within the material microstructure under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Box plot of the distribution skew for the ACS⊥ c parameter, indicating a trend related to the treatment.
summary: This box plot shows the skew of the ACS⊥ c distribution. The analysis indicates a trend suggesting that the treatment is important for the skew of the ACS⊥ c parameter, with a p-value of 0.0562.

caption: Partial pair correlation functions g_ij(r) for Ni50Al50 liquid alloys at various temperatures, with curves offset by 0.5 units along the x-axis.
summary: This panel displays partial pair correlation functions for Ni50Al50 liquid alloys derived from MD simulations at multiple temperatures. The radial distribution functions are presented with a 0.5-unit horizontal shift between successive curves to facilitate clear visualization of the structural data across the temperature range investigated in the study.

caption: Water contact angle measurements comparing as-printed and surface-textured PC and SS adherends, illustrating the wettability changes induced by the bio-inspired FS texture.
summary: This bar chart displays water contact angle measurements for as-printed and surface-textured PC and SS adherends. The bio-inspired FS texture significantly alters surface wettability, reducing the contact angle of PC from 106.8° to 93.5° and decreasing the SS adherend contact angle from 45.9° to 0°, indicating improved surface hydrophilicity.

caption: Z-directional average atomic coordinates of the Ni–Cr model during oxidation in an O2 atmosphere.
summary: Z-directional average atomic coordinates are plotted for the Ni–Cr model in an O2 atmosphere. The red dashed line indicates the initial metal surface position, while the black dashed line marks the deepest oxygen atom diffusion depth. This data helps quantify the oxide layer thickness resulting from the oxidation process.

caption: Test confusion matrix for the ResNet18 model, displaying true labels on the y-axis and predicted labels on the x-axis.
summary: The ResNet18 model confusion matrix illustrates classification performance across various classes. Notably, this model exhibits lower classification accuracy for class C, where four samples are misclassified as B, while other classes demonstrate robust performance. This visualization highlights specific limitations in the model's ability to distinguish between these particular categories.

caption: Gravimetric discharge capacity of graphite-LFP coin cells plotted against cycle count, comparing various 3D printed polymer gaskets to conventionally molded polypropylene controls.
summary: This plot displays the cycling performance of graphite/LFP full cells using different gasket materials. The data shows discharge capacity versus cycle count, highlighting that the APR gasket maintains stable cycling at 100 mAh/g for 20 cycles, despite some anticipated capacity fade observed during the coin cell experiments.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 1 fabricated via Aerosol Jet Printing (AJP).
summary: This panel displays the reflection coefficient of antenna design 1 produced using the AJP fabrication method. The data, plotted using Origin software, characterizes the electromagnetic performance of the printed antenna structure, providing a quantitative assessment of its reflection properties within the specified frequency range for the AJP-manufactured device.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping illustrating the uniform spatial distribution of manganese across the metal powder.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping illustrates the spatial distribution of manganese within the metal powder. The results confirm that manganese is distributed homogeneously across the powder particles. This uniform elemental distribution is essential for maintaining consistent material properties during the L-PBF process, as supported by the elemental analysis of the feedstock.

caption: Rietveld refinement analysis of the synchrotron XRD pattern for the HTHed Schwarz lattice, confirming the coexistence of alpha-Fe, LaFeSi-type, and NaZn13-type phases.
summary: Rietveld refinement of the synchrotron XRD pattern for the HTHed Schwarz lattice is shown. This analysis provides quantitative confirmation that the HTHed specimen contains a combination of alpha-Fe, LaFeSi-type, and NaZn13-type phases, consistent with the structural characterization results obtained from the broader XRD and synchrotron diffraction studies.

caption: Workflow diagram illustrating the empirical calibration process for deriving inherent strains through experimental testing and iterative fitting.
summary: This flowchart outlines the empirical methodology for determining inherent strains in materials. The process integrates experimental testing with iterative fitting techniques to calibrate strain values accurately. This systematic approach provides a reliable framework for deriving inherent strains, as demonstrated by the structured workflow presented in the calibration process diagram.

caption: Hardness profile across the TLP bonded region for samples processed at 1060, 1120, and 1180 °C with a constant bonding time of 45 min.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness measurement results used to evaluate the bonding region of TLP samples. The data compares the hardness profiles across the joint interface for three distinct bonding temperatures of 1060, 1120, and 1180 °C, all maintained at a constant bonding duration of 45 minutes to assess bonding quality.

caption: Fast Fourier transform diagram of the α-Mg matrix, showing increased internal lattice stripes indicative of dislocation formation.
summary: The Fast Fourier transform (FFT) diagram of the α-Mg matrix reveals an increased number of internal lattice stripes. This observation is attributed to the appearance of dislocations within the Mg matrix, providing evidence of microstructural deformation and strain accumulation within the WAAM deposited wall during the fabrication process.

caption: Coarse-grained model representation of the PLA polymer chain, illustrating the mapping of specific atomistic groups to individual beads.
summary: The coarse-grained model of PLA reduces the degrees of freedom inherent in the atomistic model, as illustrated by the bead-based representation. This simplification enables the efficient simulation of relatively large systems, providing a computationally feasible approach for modeling the polymer matrix while maintaining essential structural characteristics.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification curve for KG-SFA 1, featuring an inset showing the precipitate content in the near-solid state.
summary: The Scheil-Gulliver model simulates non-equilibrium solidification kinetics for KG-SFA 1. The curve illustrates the solidification process, while the inset highlights the primary precipitation of CrB. This early-stage precipitation provides heterogeneous nucleation sites, which promote a columnar-to-equiaxed grain transition and effectively reduce intergranular crack propagation during laser cladding.

caption: Tafel plots derived from HER polarization data for Ni–P/BC, Ni–P/GFP, and Ni–P/FP electrodes, showing slopes of 230 mV dec⁻¹ for Ni–P/FP and 194 mV dec⁻¹ for Ni–P/GFP.
summary: Tafel plots derived from HER polarization data for Ni–P/BC, Ni–P/GFP, and Ni–P/FP electrodes, showing slopes of 230 mV dec⁻¹ for Ni–P/FP and 194 mV dec⁻¹ for Ni–P/GFP. These higher Tafel slopes indicate that Ni–P/FP and Ni–P/GFP require higher activation energy for the hydrogen evolution reaction compared to the Ni–P/BC electrode.

caption: {111} pole figure corresponding to position 3 within a deformed grain, showing the crystallographic orientation after high-temperature deformation.
summary: This {111} pole figure captures the orientation at position 3 within a deformed grain. Together with the other pole figures, it confirms that the distorted twin and associated grains retain a common <111> direction, providing evidence of the crystallographic relationship between the deformed matrix and the newly nucleated DRX grains.

caption: Relative cell proliferation activity measured across varying heat treatment temperatures and durations.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the relative cell proliferation activity, demonstrating that cellular response is significantly dependent on the specific heat treatment parameters applied. The graphical results confirm that both the temperature and the duration of the heat treatment process exert a measurable influence on the overall proliferation behavior of the cells.

caption: Cycle performance evaluation showing specific capacities and Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles at a C-rate following the initial rate test.
summary: This panel presents the cycle performance of the cells, including specific capacities and Coulomb efficiency, measured over 100 cycles at a C-rate following the rate test. It serves to validate the long-term electrochemical stability and efficiency of the printed linear LCO cathode design compared to the tape-casted reference.

caption: Design schematics of isotruss unit cells representing four distinct scaffold configurations: empirical, uniform, vertical gradient, and lateral gradient architectures.
summary: These design schematics display the isotruss unit cell geometries utilized for different scaffold configurations. The configurations include empirical, uniform, vertical gradient, and lateral gradient designs. These structural variations are fundamental to the study's goal of optimizing bone scaffold performance for oro-maxillofacial applications through a dynamic machine learning-based framework.

caption: Atomic-resolution STEM-HAADF and STEM-BF images displaying the interface morphology between the rational approximant phase and the Al matrix along the pseudo-five-fold zone axis.
summary: Atomic-resolution STEM-HAADF and STEM-BF imaging reveals the interface morphology between the rational approximant phase and the Al matrix along the pseudo-five-fold zone axis. This visualization confirms that the grain boundary between the rational approximant and the aluminum matrix is coherent, as evidenced by the high-angle annular dark-field imaging.

caption: Identification of BPA degradation products obtained through UHPLC analysis.
summary: BPA degradation products are identified and characterized using UHPLC analysis. This panel displays the detected chemical species resulting from the degradation process. The data confirms the presence of specific intermediate or final products, validating the proposed degradation pathway and providing insight into the electrochemical breakdown of BPA.

caption: Coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) variation for as-LPBFed Invar 36 alloy, comparing x-y and z test orientations across deposited and stress-relieved conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the coefficient of thermal expansion for as-LPBFed Invar 36 alloy, highlighting differences between x-y and z orientations. It specifically compares the material behavior before and after residual stress relief treatments, providing a clear visualization of how processing conditions influence the thermal expansion characteristics of the alloy.

caption: EDS line scan analysis across the joint interface with a nanoscale nickel interlayer, showing elemental diffusion profiles.
summary: The EDS line scan analysis confirms the full mutual diffusion of elements across the joint interface containing a nanoscale nickel interlayer. The results show that nickel diffuses from the middle layer into the base material on both sides, with the elemental distribution tending toward uniformity at the 1000°C bonding temperature.

caption: EDS linescan composition profile extracted along the path indicated in (e), demonstrating the elemental variation across the matrix/particle/matrix interface, including an Nb-enriched shell.
summary: The EDS linescan profile across the matrix/particle/matrix region reveals the elemental distribution of Ti, Nb, and C. The data highlights a brighter shell in Z-contrast surrounding the TiC particle, which corresponds to an Nb-enriched interfacial zone within the matrix, providing insight into the particle-matrix interaction.

caption: Electronic temperature evolution for 30 keV 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFeCr.
summary: This panel depicts the temporal evolution of electronic temperature for a 30 keV 2T-MD cascade in NiFeCr. Curves show temperature along the y-dimension of the MD box. The highest temperature values correspond to the cascade development area, while the box edges remain at 300 K during the simulation.

caption: Ni-Al binary phase diagram demonstrating the absence of a stable eutectic region between the B2-NiAl and L12-Ni3Al intermetallic phases.
summary: The Ni-Al binary phase diagram is presented to evaluate the feasibility of forming a eutectic structure. Analysis of this diagram confirms that no eutectic point exists between the B2-NiAl and L12-Ni3Al phases, necessitating the addition of alloying elements like Ti to achieve the desired dual-phase composite structure.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram depicting the start of the δ-to-γ transformation at 1 vol% γ-austenite, with dashed lines indicating typical LPBF cooling rates.
summary: This CCT diagram displays the start of the δ-to-γ transformation, defined as the point where 1 vol% γ-austenite is formed. The plot evaluates the impact of typical LPBF cooling rates, ranging from 10^5 to 10^7 K/s, on the transformation kinetics, as indicated by the dashed lines.

caption: Cross-section roughness measurements for struts fabricated using various process parameter combinations, sizes, and orientations.
summary: Cross-section roughness measurements are presented for struts fabricated using various process parameter combinations, sizes, and orientations. This plot provides a quantitative assessment of surface quality across the different experimental conditions, highlighting the variability in roughness values resulting from the selected manufacturing parameters and geometric configurations of the printed struts.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to the negative control medium.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the negative control group after 24 hours of exposure to extracts. The image displays the baseline distribution of live cells, stained green, and dead cells, stained red, in the absence of any material sample, serving as the reference for subsequent material testing.

caption: Structural stiffness comparison of PETG metamaterials with re-entrant, hybrid, and hexagonal unit-cell configurations during the first cold programming compression cycle.
summary: Structural stiffness values for PETG metamaterials are compared across three unit-cell geometries. The re-entrant honeycomb demonstrates the highest stiffness at 692 N/mm, while the hybrid and hexagonal configurations exhibit lower values of 493 N/mm and 305 N/mm, respectively, representing significant reductions of 29% and 56% compared to the re-entrant design.

caption: Shapley values representing feature relevance for the EL GPR model at the first test point.
summary: Shapley values for the first test point are shown for the EL prediction model. These feature relevance weights illustrate the influence of specific input variables on the elongation prediction, offering a clear interpretation of the model's decision-making process for this particular test point.

caption: Box plot detailing the concentration ranges of metal(loid)s below 200 mg/kg in plastic materials, synthesized from this study and comparative research.
summary: Representing metal(loid) concentrations below 200 mg/kg, this box plot provides a statistical comparison of plastic material samples. The visualization highlights median values, interquartile ranges, and total data spread, facilitating a direct assessment of variability across multiple research studies including Abbasi et al., Battulga et al., Klöckner et al., and Walsh et al.

caption: Solid-state 31P CP-MAS NMR spectra of 12-NH2 PA modified NiTi nanoparticles compared to the 12-NH2 PA control.
summary: The 12-NH2 PA modified NiTi nanoparticles display a primary peak at 26.2 ppm with an additional shoulder at 23.3 ppm, whereas the pure 12-NH2 PA control shows a single peak at 30.3 ppm. These spectral shifts and features highlight the distinct chemical environment of the phosphonate groups after surface modification.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loop measured at 300 K with a 15 μA current bias.
summary: Magnetic hysteresis measurements performed at 300 K with a 15 μA current bias are compared to the unbiased state in panel h. The results indicate that the hysteresis loops in the unbiased and current biased states do not reveal any major differences in magnetic behavior.

caption: Single SUPR-V2 sampler unit equipped with 2L PFA bottles, utilized during a separate dive for the collection of particulate and dissolved metal samples, alongside whole water and filtrate sets.
summary: Shown is a third SUPR sampler unit configured with 2L perfluoroalkoxy bottles for specialized sampling. This setup, used on a different dive, facilitates the collection of particulate and dissolved metal samples, as well as whole water and filtrate sets, supporting the system's capability for up to 14 sample sets.

caption: Molybdenum elemental distribution map of the HT1-treated SS316L sample, providing insight into the chemical homogeneity of the alloy.
summary: Molybdenum elemental distribution map of the HT1-treated SS316L sample. This map provides insight into the chemical homogeneity of the alloy. The oxide particles dispersed throughout the microstructure are below the resolution limit of EDS detection and do not appear in this elemental map, despite their presence in the sample.

caption: SHAP value analysis demonstrating the feature dependence of the linear regression model on PP and MAT variables.
summary: Feature dependence analysis via SHAP values reveals that PP and MAT are the most critical variables for the model. The results indicate that low values of PP and high values of MAT correlate with higher values of M, highlighting the specific influence of these features on the predictive output.

caption: TOF-SIMS depth profile of an as-grown Cu-Ni alloy film with 150 nm Cu and 50 nm Ni, illustrating the elemental concentration gradients through the film thickness.
summary: This TOF-SIMS depth profile for a 150 nm Cu/50 nm Ni alloy film shows the distribution of Cu-, Ni-, and C- species. Consistent with other samples, carbon diffusion occurs during high-temperature growth, while the relative Ni- concentration reflects the influence of the increasing copper thickness on the alloy composition.

caption: Pseudo-ternary composition diagram depicting the MSAD value evolution for Co-Ni-Cr-Mo MPEAs with 20 at.% Co, calculated for a solvus temperature range of 650–850 °C.
summary: This diagram displays the MSAD values for Co-Ni-Cr-Mo MPEAs with 20 at.% Co, constrained by a solvus temperature range of 650–850 °C. It serves as part of a series illustrating how Co content influences lattice distortion in FCC single-phase alloys, providing insight into the compositional dependence of the MSAD values.

caption: Total density of states for Ti-Mo alloys calculated with structural relaxation using the SQS method.
summary: This panel illustrates the total density of states for Ti-Mo alloys after structural relaxation, as determined by the SQS method. By comparing these results with the unrelaxed state, the influence of atomic positioning on the electronic structure of the β-type Ti-Mo alloy system is explicitly characterized and analyzed.

caption: Calculated segregation energies for 3d, 4d, and 5d transition-metal alloying elements within the Ni Σ3 [110](111) grain boundary, plotted as a function of increasing atomic number.
summary: This plot displays the calculated segregation energies for 18 transition-metal alloying elements in the Ni Σ3 [110](111) grain boundary. The data shows that all considered elements exhibit negative segregation energies, confirming their thermodynamic tendency to segregate to the grain boundary. The energies are organized by atomic number across the 3d, 4d, and 5d series.

caption: F-actin staining in 13% scaffolds showing increased volume in +LIV samples compared to -LIV controls.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy of 13% scaffolds reveals the distribution of F-actin. Comparing +LIV samples to -LIV controls demonstrates an increase in F-actin volume. This staining highlights the structural response of the cells within the scaffold to low-intensity vibration, indicating a trend toward increased cytoskeletal organization under these specific mechanical conditions.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the as-received NiTi shape memory alloy, revealing a nanocrystalline microstructure with an average grain size of approximately 65 nm.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the microstructure of the as-received NiTi shape memory alloy. Analysis of the micrograph indicates a nanocrystalline structure, with the material exhibiting a mean crystalline grain size of approximately 65 nm, confirming the fine-grained nature of the plate prepared via ion milling.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the WR-L specimen, illustrating the crystallographic orientation surrounding the crack initiated at the drill-hole.
summary: The inverse pole figure map reveals the crystallographic orientation of the WR-L specimen in the vicinity of the drill-hole crack. This map allows for the analysis of grain misorientation effects on crack propagation, providing critical data on how local crystallographic structures influence fatigue resistance in the WR-L sample.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of AH-1050–60 specimen showing grain growth with a preserved columnar grain structure.
summary: At a homogenization temperature of 1050 ℃, the AH-1050–60 specimen exhibits clear grain growth. The inverse pole figure map demonstrates that while the grains have increased in size, the fundamental columnar grain structure remains unchanged, mirroring the structural behavior observed in the corresponding H-1050–60 heat treatment scheme.

caption: Surface electric current measurements for oriented SiC w composites, serving as the reference for surface conductivity settings.
summary: Panel b provides specific surface conductivity data for oriented SiC w composites. This measurement serves as a critical reference for determining the surface conductivity parameters used in the broader analysis of the composite materials, confirming the nonlinear and anisotropic electrical response observed across the oriented SiC whisker samples.

caption: Mott-Schottky response curves for SLM-316L stainless steel samples fabricated with varying construction directions.
summary: This plot displays the Mott-Schottky response curves for SLM-316L stainless steel specimens prepared with different construction directions. The data facilitates a comparative analysis of the electrochemical behavior of the passive films formed on these materials, highlighting how the manufacturing orientation influences the semiconductor properties of the stainless steel surface.

caption: Relative particle displacements in Area 4, highlighting the reverse direction displacement during powder deposition.
summary: Relative particle displacements in Area 4, highlighting the reverse direction displacement during powder deposition. The predominant displacement, aligned with the reverse direction, was observed as the diminished powder pile's magnitude, indicating a dominant powder deposition regime during the recoating process.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the decision-making process for designing corrosion test campaigns tailored to additively manufactured materials intended for nuclear reactor environments.
summary: This schematic outlines a structured decision-making process designed to guide the development of corrosion testing campaigns for additively manufactured materials in nuclear reactor applications. It serves as a conceptual framework to ensure systematic evaluation and deployment of these materials, providing a clear roadmap for researchers and engineers in the field.

caption: Tafel curves displaying overpotential versus the logarithm of absolute current density for Ni (green), Ni–Co (red), Ni–Zn (blue), and Ni–W (black) nanowire electrodes.
summary: This Tafel plot compares the electrochemical behavior of Ni and various Ni-alloy nanowire electrodes. The curves illustrate the relationship between overpotential and logarithmic current density. According to the study, these linear ranges were specifically derived from alloys synthesized using baths containing an equi-concentration of the two constituent elements.

caption: One-dimensional concentration profile and corresponding Sm and Ni elemental maps along the red dotted line in (c), showing chemical uniformity across the metastable region.
summary: The 1D concentration profile and elemental mapping performed along the dotted line in (c) demonstrate that there is no significant variation in chemical composition across the metastable intragranular region. This confirms that the observed phase contrast in the Sm3Ni precipitate is not driven by major chemical concentration gradients.
