caption: Weight loss profile of PMMA-M denture base resin evaluated via thermogravimetry under diverse aging environments.
summary: Weight loss profile of PMMA-M denture base resin is evaluated via thermogravimetry across multiple aging environments, such as TC, TBA, HCl, and NaOCl, compared to a non-aged control. TGA analysis confirms that weight loss occurs in this material, providing insight into the thermal degradation characteristics of the resin.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the IC specimen interface, illustrating the composition of the layer formed between the metallic bond layer and ceramic top layer.
summary: Elemental distributions obtained by EDS for the IC specimen show the composition of the layer growing between the metallic bond layer and the ceramic top layer during thermal cycling. This analysis confirms the presence of specific elements at the interface where damage and spallation are predominantly concentrated.

caption: Schematic representation of the four-point bending test configuration applied to steel I-section beams, detailing the loading points and span dimensions in millimeters.
summary: This schematic illustrates the four-point bending test setup for steel I-section beams. The configuration includes specific loading points and a defined span length, designed to evaluate the structural performance of IPE160 profiles strengthened with WAAM HSS under controlled vertical displacement loading conditions during the experimental testing phase.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectrum of the AuNP-modified castor oil solution, featuring a characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak centered at 535 nm.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectrum for the AuNP-modified castor oil solution is presented, revealing a distinct absorption peak centered at 535 nm. This peak is indicative of the presence of gold nanoparticles and shows good agreement with established literature values for AuNPs dispersed within this specific chemical environment.

caption: Process flowchart detailing the sputtering deposition of CrN thin films onto CoCrNiSi0.3 medium-entropy alloy surfaces to enhance wear and corrosion resistance.
summary: This flowchart outlines the experimental procedure for sputtering CrN thin films onto CoCrNiSi0.3 medium-entropy alloy surfaces. The process is designed to improve the material's surface properties, specifically targeting enhanced wear and corrosion resistance, providing a clear sequence of the deposition steps involved in the surface modification strategy.

caption: Top view (XY plane) of particle flow trajectories at various time intervals for the strip material.
summary: The top-down XY view of particle trajectories in the strip material reveals that, except for particles near the tool head end and axis shoulder, the directional movement is primarily governed by the tool head's rotation. This visualization clarifies the influence of processing parameters on the lateral flow of strip particles.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of CAMA used to verify the molecular structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of CAMA is presented to further demonstrate the structural integrity of the synthesized compound. By analyzing the proton signals, this spectrum provides critical evidence for the molecular configuration of CAMA, serving as a definitive method for structural identification alongside the previously discussed FT-IR spectroscopic results.

caption: Current density versus voltage (J-V) characteristics for OPVs utilizing PPI-SL and P3HT-PSL as donor materials with PC71BM as the acceptor, including an inset table of photovoltaic parameters.
summary: Current density-voltage plots compare the performance of PPI-SL and P3HT-PSL based OPV devices using PC71BM as the acceptor material. The figure includes an inset table that lists the specific photovoltaic parameters for both device types, providing a quantitative comparison of their electrical performance under the tested conditions.

caption: Dislocation distribution map of nano-polycrystalline Ni57Cr19Co19Al5 alloy with 18 nm grain size at 0.2 strain, showing the microstructure without twin boundaries.
summary: Displayed is the dislocation distribution for an 18 nm grain size Ni57Cr19Co19Al5 alloy at 0.2 strain without twin boundaries. In this larger grain size regime, the microstructure exhibits significant Stair-rod and Perfect dislocations, indicating that dislocation motion and associated reactions play a major role in the alloy's deformation process.

caption: Chronoamperometric current transient (solid line) recorded at a Pt microelectrode in 0.05 M H2O2 and 2 M NaOH at 0.18 V, alongside the corresponding normalized current ratio i/id plotted against the inverse square root of time (dashed line).
summary: This figure displays the electrochemical response of a Pt microelectrode during a chronoamperometry experiment in a H2O2 and NaOH electrolyte. The solid line represents the current transient at 0.18 V, while the dashed line illustrates the normalized current ratio i/id versus t^-1/2, providing essential kinetic data for the system.

caption: Raman spectrum of CNT powders combined with copper, showing broad vibrational bands indicative of partially disordered carbon structures.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of CNTs combined with copper reveals broad vibrational bands. These spectral features indicate the presence of partially disordered carbon structures within the composite material, providing insight into the structural state of the carbon nanotubes after integration with the copper powder matrix.

caption: Surface minor strain pattern of a fan-dried mycelium sample at the 410-minute sampling mark.
summary: Fan-dried mycelium displays a heterogeneous strain field after 410 minutes. While most areas show no strain, localized regions exhibit negative strains of approximately 0.5% (blue) and small areas reach nearly 1% (light green). This indicates moderate, non-uniform mechanical response to the fan-drying process compared to the oven-dried control.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map revealing the crystallographic grain orientation of the material at an AMF intensity of 25 mT.
summary: At an AMF intensity of 25 mT, this EBSD inverse pole figure map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of grains. The image contributes to the overall analysis of how higher magnetic field intensities influence the grain structure and orientation distribution within the specimen throughout the experimental series.

caption: I/V curves of the STF-Ni SOC in rSOC mode at 750 °C, illustrating the electrochemical response to H2O molar fraction changes between 14% and 45% with a fixed H2 concentration of 45%.
summary: Electrochemical performance in rSOC mode is assessed by varying the H2O molar fraction while maintaining a constant H2 supply. Results indicate that the variation of H2O content has a negligible impact on the I/V curves, which is consistent with findings from EIS measurements and the observed kinetic rate of the system.

caption: 1H NMR spectra (500 MHz, CDCl3, 500 K) comparing the chemical composition of ABS-CF recycling stages R0 (red), R1 (green), and R5 (blue).
summary: This figure displays the 1H NMR spectra acquired at 500 MHz in CDCl3 at 500 K for ABS-CF samples across three recycling stages: R0, R1, and R5. The spectra, color-coded as red, green, and blue respectively, allow for a comparative analysis of the chemical composition and structural integrity of the ABS-CF material throughout the recycling process.

caption: Magnetic Thermoelectric Power (MTEP) measurement performed at 178 K with a temperature gradient of 45 K along the c-axis of a 100 nm thick CrO2 thin film on a TiO2 substrate.
summary: This panel displays the MTEP data for a 100 nm thick CrO2 thin film on a TiO2 substrate, measured along the c-axis at 178 K with a 45 K temperature gradient. The MTEP behavior in this orientation is shown to faithfully mimic the magnetoresistance response of the material.

caption: Nickel (Ni) elemental distribution map highlighting the Ni-rich regions within the as-deposited-VP sample microstructure.
summary: Nickel (Ni) elemental distribution map highlighting the Ni-rich regions within the as-deposited-VP sample microstructure. This SEM-EDS elemental mapping test was performed to identify the chemical composition of the dendrite, providing essential data on the Ni distribution to better understand the overall chemical makeup of the as-deposited material.

caption: t-SNE projection of latent features comparing real (green) and synthetic (red) data distributions, where markers indicate set means and shaded ellipses represent real-data covariance.
summary: This t-SNE projection visualizes the latent space to evaluate the fidelity of synthetic samples against real data. By comparing centroid shifts and distribution spreads, the plot highlights the degree of overlap between the two sets. Substantial overlap indicates high synthetic fidelity, while deviations suggest potential domain gaps or additional modes.

caption: Density of states spectra for the O-phase Ti2AlW compound, illustrating the electronic band distribution.
summary: The density of states for Ti2AlW in the O-phase shows that the valence band near the Fermi level is mainly formed by the hybridization of Ti-d and W-d states. The s-states of the ternary element are located more than 6 eV below the Fermi level, following the established trend for these compounds.

caption: Isometric view of the thin plate lattice (TPL) obtained via X-ray microscopy, revealing the internal 3-D architecture.
summary: This isometric X-ray microscopy image provides a 3-D view of the thin plate lattice structure. The analysis confirms that the internal channels are clean and free from un-melted powder, demonstrating minimal occlusion within the struts. This visualization highlights the overall structural integrity and internal cleanliness of the fabricated lattice.

caption: Mesoscopic representation of inter-dendritic crack connection in Alloy-A with CMH, illustrating the progression of damage across the dendritic structure.
summary: This panel depicts the mesoscopic stage of fracture in Alloy-A with CMH, focusing on the inter-dendritic crack connection process. It serves as a critical link in the multi-scale fracture model, showing how localized microscopic cracks propagate and coalesce across the dendritic network under high-temperature stress.

caption: Hardness distribution of AM-fabricated 4340 steel specimens subjected to various tempering temperatures, highlighting the softening effect observed at 315 °C.
summary: This boxplot illustrates the hardness values of AM-fabricated 4340 steel following tempering treatments. The data demonstrates how tempering temperature influences mechanical properties, specifically showing a reduction in hardness at 315 °C due to the relaxation of thermal residual stresses. These intermediate hardness values suggest that bainitic transformations occurred during rapid solidification.

caption: Al–Cu equilibrium binary phase diagram illustrating the solidification pathway and liquidus-solidus temperature variations based on composition gradients.
summary: The Al–Cu equilibrium binary phase diagram displays the solidification pathway and temperature ranges for the Al–Cu system. This diagram is essential for understanding how composition gradients dictate local solidification, spanning the biphase region between alpha-Al and theta-Al2Cu, which accounts for the majority of the solidified track volume.

caption: Total density of states (DOS) for Cu-50 at.% Ni, comparing spin-polarized (black line) and non-spin-polarized (red line) calculations, with the latter scaled by a factor of two.
summary: The total density of states for Cu-50 at.% Ni is presented, highlighting the influence of spin polarization on the electronic structure. The Fermi level resides near the top of the 3d-orbital DOS, where spin-induced splitting alters the DOS shape, directly impacting the material's Young's and shear moduli.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for Fe, O, and Ti atoms at the Fe/TiO2 interface.
summary: This panel displays the projected density of states for Fe, O, and Ti atoms at the Fe/TiO2 interface. The PDOS plots provide insight into the electronic structure of the pre-nucleation model, illustrating the orbital contributions of each atomic species at the interface during the initial stages of Fe deposition.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectrum 59 obtained from the butterfly-shaped light phase, indicating a high chromium concentration characteristic of Cr5B3 precipitates.
summary: Spectrum 59 corresponds to a light-colored, butterfly-shaped phase observed within the sintered Colmonoy-5 alloy. The energy-dispersive X-ray analysis reveals a high concentration of chromium, confirming that this specific morphology represents Cr5B3 precipitates, which are distinct from the surrounding matrix and other boride structures present in the sample.

caption: Relative composition of Fe valence states within the passive film, derived from integrated peak areas of XPS spectra.
summary: Quantification of the passive film composition was performed by analyzing the integrated areas of XPS peaks. Panel (a) displays the relative composition of Fe valence states, providing insight into the chemical state of iron within the corrosion products formed on the surface of the hybrid alloy samples.

caption: Inverse pole figure map illustrating the texture of grains formed by the DDRX mechanism at a strain of 0.20.
summary: Depicting the texture at a strain of 0.20, this panel shows that grains formed via the DDRX mechanism display a <001> orientation. This observation contrasts with the CDRX mechanism results, underscoring the distinct influence of different DRX mechanisms on texture evolution at higher strain levels.

caption: EPMA elemental mapping of the β-NiAl coating after 80 hours of corrosion, highlighting the distribution of sulfidation zones at the coating/oxide interface and within the coating interior.
summary: This EPMA elemental map displays the β-NiAl coating after 80 hours of corrosion. Analysis reveals that sulfidation zones are primarily concentrated at the coating/oxide interface and extend into the coating interior, indicating significant susceptibility to internal sulfidation under the tested corrosive conditions.

caption: Terminal solidification cracking susceptibility index for sample B-3, derived from thermodynamic modeling of the melt pool.
summary: Sample B-3 shows the terminal solidification cracking susceptibility index calculated using Thermo-Calc. This simulation evaluates the variation in SCI for the melt pool region during the final solidification stage. The findings contribute to the assessment of cracking susceptibility in the nickel-based superalloy under defined LPBF process parameters.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs) stained for live/dead assessment after 72 hours of treatment with material extracts.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs) treated with material extracts for 72 hours reveals high cell viability. The presence of strong green Calcein-AM fluorescence and negligible red EthD-1 staining confirms that the soft robotic platform exhibits excellent biocompatibility with these dermal cells.

caption: Schematic representation of the in-house developed filament fabrication line used for producing CCF filaments.
summary: This schematic illustrates the in-house developed equipment utilized for the fabrication of CCF filaments. The setup is designed to facilitate the continuous production of composite filaments, serving as the foundational processing step for subsequent additive manufacturing applications as detailed in the referenced experimental methodology.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of Ta distribution across the interfacial region of zone B.
summary: The EDS mapping result for Ta in zone B confirms the elemental distribution across the interface. By highlighting the Ta substrate, this map complements the HAADF-STEM imaging to clearly delineate the boundary between the metallic substrate and the overlying surface oxide layer.

caption: Continuous printing configuration showing the part deposited directly onto a Nd–Fe–B permanent magnet.
summary: This photograph illustrates the continuous printing configuration used in the study. The setup features a part being deposited directly onto the surface of a Nd–Fe–B permanent magnet. This arrangement serves as one of the two primary printing configurations investigated to evaluate the influence of the magnetic field source.

caption: Surface morphology observed on the sample following the LAR process.
summary: Surface morphology of the LAR-processed sample is shown in this panel. The image provides a visual assessment of the material's surface state after the laser additive repair, highlighting the physical characteristics resulting from the deposition strategy and the initial processing phase of the repair sequence.

caption: Wear depth as a function of sliding distance for the combined AP + HT + LSP sample.
summary: The AP + HT + LSP sample exhibits moderate wear overall but shows a sharp increase at 350 °C during the initial sliding distance. This behavior suggests that combined thermal effects, including high temperature and friction-induced heat, significantly influence the hardened layer's performance under these specific testing conditions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of a twin boundary identified in the Ni65Cu35 alloy substructure.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern corresponds to the twin boundary observed in panel (e). This diffraction analysis confirms the crystallographic nature of the annealed twins found within the Ni65Cu35 alloy substructure at 320 K undercooling, providing definitive evidence of the twin boundary structure.

caption: Calculated Scheil solidification curve for the Nb–4Si–20Cr alloy, showing the temperature-dependent phase fraction progression and the total solidification interval marked in red.
summary: Representing the solidification pathway for the Nb–4Si–20Cr alloy, this Scheil model calculation tracks phase fraction changes as a function of temperature. Key phase reactions are annotated along the curve, while the red-highlighted region indicates the total solidification temperature range, facilitating comparison of thermal solidification characteristics between different alloy compositions.

caption: Three-dimensional confocal microscopy image illustrating the initial surface topography of the thin-walled sample.
summary: The confocal microscopy image provides a 3D visualization of the initial surface topography of the thin-walled sample. This technique allows for the characterization of the surface features in three dimensions, providing essential data for evaluating the surface quality and roughness of the L-PBF manufactured part.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the NbTiZr system at 900 °C, illustrating phase coexistence regions and a shift toward two-phase formation driven by increased Ti concentration.
summary: At 900 °C, Monte Carlo simulations indicate that higher Ti concentrations shift the ternary phase diagram, promoting two-phase formation. The free energy curvature eigenvalues effectively map these regions, confirming that specific compositions like Nb33Ti51Zr16 remain single-phase despite proximity to the miscibility gap, while other areas exhibit distinct phase separation.

caption: Low-viscosity water film behavior under ultrasonic excitation at 48 kHz and 5 W power, showing capillary wave formation and droplet detachment at a normalized thickness of h/hc = 2.
summary: Water, representing a low-viscosity liquid, exhibits specific capillary wave patterns and droplet detachment mechanisms when subjected to ultrasonic excitation at 48 kHz and 5 W. At a normalized film thickness of h/hc = 2, the fluid dynamics are characterized by these observed wave structures and detachment events.

caption: Nyquist plots for as-cast GZ112K alloys, highlighting significant semi-circle shrinkage and the emergence of a high-frequency feature after heat treatments.
summary: Nyquist plots for the as-cast GZ112K alloy show that semi-circles shrink significantly after solution and aging heat treatments, demonstrating a notable reduction in corrosion resistance. Additionally, a new small semi-circle appears in the high-frequency range, reflecting the charge transfer resistance at the interface between the Mg alloy and NaCl solution.

caption: Photographic image of 3D-printed CP and CP-0Co hydrogel scaffolds with varying concentrations of 10.6%, 13.4%, and 16.2%, displaying a uniform white appearance.
summary: This photograph displays 3D-printed CP and CP-0Co hydrogel scaffolds with varying concentrations of 10.6%, 13.4%, and 16.2%. The scaffolds exhibit a uniform white appearance, confirming the successful fabrication of the base composite hydrogel structures prior to the addition of cobalt-based nanowires.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of sample 3, demonstrating the absence of clear crystalline grains.
summary: HRTEM imaging of sample 3 shows a distinct lack of clear crystalline grains. This observation supports the hypothesis that the long-range order of the Ni crystal is progressively broken as phosphorus occupies more interfacial positions within the octahedron, eventually leading to the disappearance of discernible grain structures in the material.

caption: Pole figure of the WAAM specimen, highlighting the (001) texture intensity within the Al-matrix.
summary: This pole figure demonstrates the crystallographic texture of the Al-matrix in the WAAM specimen. The data indicates that the (001) pole figure possesses relatively strong textures, confirming that the processing conditions and the resulting solidification path significantly influence the final orientation distribution of the grains within the fabricated material.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the irradiated AISI-348 steel specimen following annealing at 673 K, showing the distribution of He bubbles at interfaces.
summary: Following annealing at 673 K, this bright-field TEM micrograph reveals the state of the AISI-348 steel previously irradiated with 6 keV He to 4 dpa. The image demonstrates the distribution and growth of He bubbles at the grain boundaries, confirming the persistence of these features after thermal exposure.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the gamma matrix in the L-1 sample, demonstrating a uniform solute distribution lacking evidence of precipitate formation.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the L-1 sample displays a uniform distribution of solute elements throughout the gamma matrix. Consistent with the L-11 sample, this region shows no signs of clustering or precipitation, indicating that the thermal cycling process effectively homogenized the microstructure by dissolving all pre-existing precipitates.

caption: Ni 2p high-resolution XPS spectra comparing LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi samples, deconvoluted into metallic Ni0, NiO, and Ni(OH)2 components after exposure to 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: Ni 2p high-resolution XPS spectra for LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi samples are shown after 1 hour of exposure to 3.5% NaCl solution. The spectra are deconvoluted into multiple components, specifically metallic Ni0, NiO, and Ni(OH)2, providing insight into the nickel oxidation states within the passive film.

caption: Individual EDX map for molybdenum (Mo) distribution, with white arrows indicating the location of scarce MoC phase pockets.
summary: Molybdenum distribution is mapped using EDX to identify the location of scarce MoC phase pockets, indicated by white arrows. These localized clusters of minor phases are consistent with broader SEM and EDX observations. The map confirms that molybdenum is concentrated in these specific regions within the ZrB2-20 material.

caption: Spatial distribution map of ‖ ∇ s ̃ θ ‖ corresponding to the MSP design shown in panel (c).
summary: This panel displays the spatial distribution of the gradient magnitude ‖ ∇ s ̃ θ ‖ for the MSP case design. The map visualizes the structural characteristics of the L-bracket optimized with both parallel misalignment and singularity penalties, directly corresponding to the design configuration shown in panel (c).

caption: Frequency dependence of the open-circuit voltage signals showing an increase in output with rising excitation frequency.
summary: The plot displays the frequency-dependent behavior of the open-circuit voltage signals. As the excitation frequency increases, the output voltage rises, which is attributed to the system approaching its natural frequency. This optimization of the vibrational response enhances the overall electrical output of the piezoelectric energy harvester.

caption: Calculated Ti-W binary phase diagram compared against experimental data points, highlighting the liquidus line and phase boundaries derived from the new parameterization.
summary: This Ti-W binary phase diagram illustrates the results of a new parameterization optimization, showing a strong fit with experimental data. The plot includes liquidus data points from Rudy, which are excluded from the assessment as they represent the onset of incipient melting rather than equilibrium phase boundaries.

caption: Overall design domain composed of multiple square modules arranged in a horizontal configuration.
summary: The overall design domain is constructed by arranging multiple small square modules horizontally. This panel demonstrates how individual design units are combined to form a larger, unified structure, establishing the modular basis for the LETO approach to structural design and optimization within the defined system boundaries.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry thermogram of the Ni–15Cr–6Al–4Nb alloy in the solution heat-treated condition, featuring an inset that provides a magnified view of the thermal response near the secondary γ′ solvus temperature.
summary: This DSC thermogram characterizes the thermal behavior of the Ni–15Cr–6Al–4Nb alloy following solution heat treatment. The primary plot displays the heat flow profile, while the inset specifically highlights the secondary γ′ solvus region. This data provides critical insight into the phase transformation temperatures for this specific alloy composition.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of the developed black PEO coatings, revealing the presence of AlPO4 and γ-Al2O3 as the primary crystalline phases.
summary: The X-ray diffraction patterns of the developed black PEO coatings are presented to identify their crystalline composition. Analysis of these patterns confirms that all studied PEO coatings consist primarily of AlPO4 and γ-Al2O3 phases. These results provide essential structural information regarding the phase composition of the synthesized black coatings.

caption: Experimental observation of a droplet interacting with a 2 mm diameter receiving stage, where the resin contacts the side and creates a side stream.
summary: Experimental results for a 2 mm diameter receiving stage show that the resin makes direct contact with the side of the stage. Because the stage diameter is smaller than the droplet's cross-sectional height, this contact results in the formation of a side stream along the stage surface.

caption: Nyquist plot of the substrate and SP1 sample, featuring an overlaid equivalent circuit model.
summary: This panel displays the Nyquist plot for the substrate and SP1 sample, incorporating a proposed equivalent circuit model to analyze their electrochemical impedance response. The plot serves as a baseline for comparing the corrosion protection performance of the substrate against the modified Ti-based film samples.

caption: Creep strain evolution over time for GH4169 superalloy at 873 K under a stress level of 860 MPa, comparing simulated model predictions against experimental test data.
summary: This panel displays the creep strain evolution over time for the Nickel-based superalloy GH4169 at a constant temperature of 873 K and a stress level of 860 MPa. The plot provides a direct comparison between the simulated creep strain model and the corresponding experimental test data to validate model accuracy.

caption: Detailed confocal view of the SLM as-built surface highlighting localized pitting corrosion features after exposure to the potentiostatic polarization environment.
summary: Providing a detailed view of the SLM as-built surface, this confocal microscopy panel highlights localized pitting corrosion features. The image captures the surface state after the specimen underwent potentiostatic polarization in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at +0.25 V vs. OCP, illustrating the extent of the corrosion damage.

caption: Landing site dispersion plot for a nominal trajectory angle of μ(t) = 0 degrees.
summary: This plot illustrates the landing site dispersion calculated using the Monte Carlo method for 300 individual cases. By evaluating the nominal landing sites at a trajectory angle of μ(t) = 0 degrees, the simulation provides a statistical distribution of potential impact points, which is essential for assessing the necessity of trajectory correction maneuvers.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a 30 nm cube processed at LED = 0.2 J/mm and h = 0.06 mm, exhibiting more isotropic structural features compared to lower energy density conditions.
summary: Representing the sample processed at 0.2 J/mm, this APT reconstruction shows a more isotropic distribution of Cr-rich regions and Al atoms compared to the 0.1 J/mm condition. The analysis confirms the absence of gamma-prime precipitation, with Cr-rich regions marked by 9.5 at.% iso-surfaces and Al atoms shown as points.

caption: Inverse pole figure map illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution of grains within the GH4169 superalloy microstructure.
summary: The inverse pole figure map reveals the orientation distribution of grains in the GH4169 superalloy. Acquired via EBSD technology, this visualization provides essential crystallographic data, characterizing the microstructural texture of the material as part of the comprehensive analysis of the alloy's grain structure and orientation properties.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the temperature dependence of hydrogen and deuterium permeability in the investigated material.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature-dependent permeability behavior for both hydrogen and deuterium isotopes. By plotting the logarithm of permeability against the inverse of temperature, the figure provides a clear visualization of the transport kinetics, allowing for the determination of activation energies associated with the diffusion of these isotopes.

caption: Comparison of experimental and model-predicted recrystallization fractions, highlighting the model's ability to capture accelerated kinetics at high strain rates of 5 s⁻¹.
summary: This panel displays a parity plot comparing experimental data with model predictions for the fraction of recrystallization. It demonstrates that the coupled CDRX + SRX model accurately captures the accelerated recrystallization kinetics observed during deformation at high strain rates of 5 s⁻¹, confirming the model's predictive capability for unseen validation data.

caption: Demagnetization curves of NdFeB samples processed under varying parameters, illustrating the magnetic response to external field strength.
summary: This panel displays the demagnetization behavior of NdFeB samples subjected to different processing conditions. The curves represent the magnetic field strength versus magnetization, providing essential data for calculating remanent magnetization and saturation magnetic field strength, which are critical for evaluating the magnetic performance of the fabricated materials.

caption: Specific capacitance plotted as a function of geopolymer aging time.
summary: Specific capacitance values are shown relative to the curing age of the geopolymer. The data demonstrates that electrochemical performance is highly dependent on the curing duration. A general trend of decreasing capacitance with increasing curing time is observed, reflecting the evolution of the geopolymer structure and its impact on ion storage.

caption: Conceptual overview illustrating the research methodology and its direct alignment with the defined research questions.
summary: This schematic provides a comprehensive overview of the research methodology employed throughout the study. It serves as a visual framework that maps the procedural steps taken to the specific research questions, ensuring a clear and logical connection between the experimental or analytical approach and the intended scientific objectives.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the shear strength of joints bonded at 1273 K for 10 minutes as a function of varying boron content.
summary: This bar chart displays the shear strength of joints processed at 1273 K for 10 minutes, highlighting the influence of boron content on mechanical performance. The data indicates how varying boron concentrations affect the joint strength, providing a quantitative assessment of the bonding conditions under high-temperature testing environments.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) diagrams for Al, Sc, and Si atoms, including magnified views near the Fermi level.
summary: Projected density of states diagrams demonstrate well-resolved orbital contributions from each constituent element, specifically Al, Sc, and Si. Magnified views near the Fermi level provide a detailed look at the specific electronic contributions of these elements, offering insight into the bonding and electronic properties of the Al5Sc2Si structure.

caption: Bode diagram illustrating the variation of impedance modulus as a function of frequency for AA2195 aluminum alloy, TC4 titanium alloy, and AA2195/TC4 composites.
summary: This Bode diagram displays the frequency-dependent impedance modulus for AA2195 aluminum alloy, TC4 titanium alloy, and AA2195/TC4 composites. The plot serves as a key component of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis, allowing for the comparison of impedance magnitude across the tested frequency spectrum for the three distinct material systems.

caption: Tafel plot illustrating the electrochemical behavior of austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys in [N1888][Tf2N] ionic liquid at 80 °C, showing the relationship between potential and current density.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical response of various austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys tested in [N1888][Tf2N] at 80 °C. The data, which serves as a basis for determining corrosion potentials, indicates that reversing polarization from anodic to cathodic directions reduces current values in the high anodic region near 1 V.

caption: Poly(AAm-co-NaA) hydrogel-coated structured packing showing the modified surface appearance.
summary: This panel presents the structured packing after being coated with a poly(AAm-co-NaA) hydrogel layer. The photograph illustrates the visual change in the packing surface resulting from the hydrogel application, which effectively covers the underlying polyamide powder particles and alters the surface texture of the manufactured structure.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel evaluated at various temperature levels using the PEC2 model.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel across different temperature values. The data, generated via the PEC2 model, demonstrates the performance behavior of the module under varying thermal conditions, providing a comparison between the proposed model predictions and measured experimental values for the solar panel.

caption: SAED pattern obtained from the FCC matrix, confirming its crystal structure.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponds to the FCC matrix identified in the HR-TEM images. This diffraction data provides crystallographic confirmation of the matrix phase, serving as a reference for analyzing the orientation relationships and lattice misfits at the interfaces with the secondary Cr₂B and (Ni,Co)Ti₂ phases.

caption: Radar plot displaying the statistical indicator scores for the training dataset of the hybrid models.
summary: This radar plot visualizes the performance metrics of the proposed hybrid models during the training phase. It provides a comprehensive statistical assessment of the model's predictive capabilities, allowing for a clear comparison of various indicators as part of the overall evaluation framework presented in the study's statistical analysis.

caption: Normalized specular reflectance signal intensity at 11,820 eV (red) and normalized Au L3-edge absorption step size at 11,919 eV (blue) plotted as a function of the applied electrochemical potential.
summary: Specular reflectance signal intensity measured at 11,820 eV is calculated as the ratio between reflected and incident beam intensity, normalized to the maximum experimental value. Concurrently, the absorption step size at the Au L3-edge is plotted, providing a comparative view of surface changes as a function of electrochemical potential.

caption: Quantitative map illustrating the solid solution strengthening effect of 35 distinct elemental additions within face-centered cubic (FCC) Ni matrices, derived from high-throughput density functional theory assessments.
summary: This figure presents a quantitative map derived from high-throughput density functional theory assessments of 35 elemental additions in FCC Ni matrices. It illustrates the solid solution strengthening effect of these alloying elements, highlighting that refractory elements generally demonstrate enhanced high-temperature strengthening efficacy as corroborated by the computational data.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction intensity map showing the phase evolution of Nb-free iHEA during laser melting.
summary: This panel displays a synchrotron X-ray diffraction intensity map for the Nb-free iHEA composition during laser melting. The visualization tracks the structural phase evolution in real-time, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of Nb alloying on the solidification behavior and phase stability of the high-entropy alloy system.

caption: Loss curve for the DANN unsupervised domain adaptation method.
summary: DANN presents a loss curve showing a rapid increase in accuracy during the initial 20 epochs of training. This behavior is attributed to the reduction of its penalty terms, which drives the model's early convergence and establishes the baseline performance for this specific unsupervised domain adaptation architecture.

caption: Raman scattering spectrum of the resins, showing additional spectral features attributed to the presence of 2-phenoxyethanol and 1-butanol porogens.
summary: Raman analysis of the resins reveals spectral features distinct from the membranes. These additional bands are associated with the porogens 2-phenoxyethanol and 1-butanol used during synthesis. The vertical dotted gray lines across both panels indicate specific bands selected for tentative assignment to identify the chemical composition of the materials.

caption: Choo-Lee plot derived from TDS data for the H1000 aged material, illustrating the linear relationship used to calculate trapping energies.
summary: This panel shows the Choo-Lee plot for the H1000 aged material, which is utilized to evaluate trapping energies. The slope of the plotted dataset allows for the calculation of trapping energies associated with individual peaks, providing insight into the hydrogen trapping characteristics of the H1000 aged material.

caption: Schmid factor distribution map for the {111}<110> slip system in the γ phase in the crack propagation region.
summary: Schmid factor values for the {111}<110> slip system in the γ phase are visualized for the crack propagation region. By calculating these values for the most commonly activated slip system in γ-TiAl, the map illustrates the crystallographic susceptibility to slip during the fatigue crack propagation process.

caption: Log-log stress-life diagram for a plain steel specimen comparing baseline data against an enhanced dataset generated with a synthetic noise factor.
summary: This log-log stress-life diagram illustrates the fatigue performance of a plain steel specimen. It compares baseline experimental data with an enhanced dataset, which was synthetically generated using a linear function with a noise factor ranging between -0.3 and 0.3 to augment the limited original sample size.

caption: Three-dimensional surface morphology of the 316 L steel specimen prepared via laser powder bed fusion.
summary: The three-dimensional surface morphology of the 316 L stainless steel specimen is displayed to illustrate the surface characteristics resulting from the laser powder bed fusion process. This topographical analysis serves as a baseline for the 316 L steel specimens before they undergo the diffusion bonding procedure.

caption: Chromatograms of extractables in ethanol/water for samples post-cured for 14 minutes, showing absorbance at 210 nm.
summary: This panel displays the chromatograms of extractables in an ethanol/water solvent for samples post-cured for 14 minutes. The analysis, measured at an absorbance of 210 nm, reveals that most extractables for the Graphy material are highly polar compounds, as indicated by the presence of mean peaks at short retention times below 10 minutes.

caption: Evolution of axial and radial lattice strains measured in situ for both A356 and 316 L constituents during the mechanical loading experiment.
summary: In situ measurements of axial and radial lattice strains for the A356 and 316 L constituents are presented. These strain data serve as the primary input for Eqs. 1 and 2, enabling the computation of corresponding lattice stresses and the rule-of-mixtures axial stress to characterize the composite's mechanical response.

caption: Ultimate strain predictions derived from empirical models as a function of welding current and travel speed.
summary: This contour plot visualizes the predicted ultimate strain of the weldment based on welding current and travel speed inputs. By mapping these processing variables, the empirical model provides insights into the ductility characteristics of the material, supporting the selection of parameters that optimize both strength and strain performance.

caption: Dynamical solution trajectory and time series at Ta = −9.99 °C, showing the system state in close proximity to the switching boundary.
summary: Representing the system at Ta = −9.99 °C, this panel illustrates the solution trajectory and time series near the switching boundary. As an example of a grazing bifurcation, the plot highlights the system's evolution as it nears the critical threshold defined by the black line under the given thermal conditions.

caption: Bar chart comparing the number of cycles to fatigue failure for NiTi shape memory alloys and various hybrid materials under a stress-controlled testing strategy.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the fatigue performance of NiTi shape memory alloys and hybrid materials subjected to a stress-based testing strategy. By comparing the number of cycles to failure, the data helps determine the efficiency of different fatigue testing strategies, providing insight into the durability of these specific material systems.

caption: Optimized structural model of the twin NiZnCu (111) surface.
summary: This panel illustrates the optimized structural model for the twin NiZnCu (111) surface. DFT calculations show a significant shift in the Ni d-band center to -1.61 eV relative to the twin Ni (111) surface, highlighting the influence of alloying elements on the electronic structure of the twin boundary.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve for the post-industrial recycled powder, highlighting the thermal transitions and sintering window.
summary: Thermal analysis of the post-industrial recycled powder is shown via this DSC curve. The sintering window is calculated by measuring the difference between the extrapolated onsets of the crystallization and melting processes, which characterizes the thermal stability and processing window for the recycled material in this study.

caption: ODF section of the austenite phase at 15% strain, illustrating the evolution of texture components under moderate deformation.
summary: At 15% strain, the austenite ODF section reflects the ongoing evolution of the material's crystallographic texture. This panel captures the intermediate state of the texture components as the sample undergoes deformation, serving as a baseline for comparing the subsequent transition and restoration of specific orientations observed at higher strain levels.

caption: Double logarithmic plot of steady-state strain rate versus true stress for CP and PM alloys tested at 100 °C.
summary: This panel displays the steady-state creep behavior of CP and PM alloys at 100 °C, represented on a double logarithmic scale. The data follows the general-power law constitutive creep equation, illustrating the relationship between strain rate and true stress, which is essential for determining the material's creep constant and stress exponent.

caption: Average coefficient of friction values with standard deviation for LPBF DSS 2205 and WC/W2C reinforced composites across different counterbody sizes.
summary: Average COF values for the stable sliding phase are summarized here, derived from three independent tests for each condition. This comparison highlights the influence of counterbody size on the tribological performance of the LPBF DSS 2205 and its WC/W2C reinforced composites, providing a quantitative overview of the friction stability.

caption: Adsorption model of carbon atoms on the (311) facet of pure Ni, illustrating the interaction energetics on this specific surface orientation.
summary: This panel presents the DFT-calculated adsorption of carbon atoms on the (311) facet of pure Ni. These results contribute to the broader study of carbon adsorption energetics across various pure Ni facets, confirming the baseline behavior against which the Ni-In surface alloy models are evaluated.

caption: Transmission spectra of aluminum nanoparticle samples deposited for 1, 3, 5, and 7 minutes, highlighting a plateau between 700 and 900 nm attributed to the aluminum interband transition.
summary: Transmission spectra for aluminum nanoparticle samples deposited at varying times (1, 3, 5, and 7 minutes) are presented. The data reveals a distinct spectral feature characterized by a plateau between 700 and 900 nm, which is identified as being related to the interband transition of the aluminum material.

caption: Workflow diagram illustrating the design process for an adaptive variable withdrawal rate strategy using the DS-Auto-V Python programming framework.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic workflow for designing an adaptive variable withdrawal rate strategy. By integrating Eq. (16) with the DS-Auto-V Python programming tool, the process enables the determination of optimal withdrawal rates under specified experimental conditions, providing a structured computational approach to achieving precise control in material processing applications.

caption: Thermodynamic prediction of the multilayered scale structure on steel A using FACTSAGE, illustrating the formation of external Fe-oxides, an internal Cr-Fe oxide mixture, and a continuous pure Cr-oxide sublayer adjacent to the metal matrix.
summary: FACTSAGE thermodynamic simulations predict the development of a multilayered scale structure on steel A. The model identifies distinct regions, including external iron oxides, an intermediate mixture of chromium and iron oxides, and a protective pure chromium oxide sublayer that maintains strong adherence to the underlying steel matrix at 1000 °C.

caption: Crystal violet staining images of HUVECs cultured for 24 hours with various scaffold extracts to visualize cell migration into the lower chamber.
summary: Crystal violet staining images of HUVECs cultured for 24 hours with various scaffold extracts to visualize cell migration into the lower chamber. The number of cells migrating to the lower chamber was significantly higher in the Mg@GAG group compared to the other groups, indicating enhanced cell migration capacity.

caption: Laser absorptivity measurements for pure Mo and Mo-TiC composite powders plotted against wavelengths ranging from 500 to 2000 nm.
summary: This plot displays the laser absorptivity of pure Mo and Mo-TiC composite powders across a 500–2000 nm wavelength range. Laser absorption is a critical parameter for L-PBF processability, as it dictates the energy density absorbed by the powder material during the laser-based manufacturing process at specific wavelengths.

caption: Ultramicro instrumented indentation response of SLM Ti-6Al-4V, illustrating the load-displacement characteristics under quasistatic loading conditions.
summary: The ultramicro instrumented indentation curve provides insight into the local mechanical properties of the SLM Ti-6Al-4V material. By measuring the load-displacement behavior at the micro-scale, this test complements the tensile data, offering a detailed assessment of the material's hardness and deformation resistance under controlled quasistatic indentation conditions.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography of the pristine 3D printed PEEK sample surface.
summary: Atomic force microscopy analysis of the pristine 3D-printed PEEK sample provides a detailed view of the initial surface topography. This imaging technique is employed to establish the baseline surface roughness, which is essential for assessing the structural changes induced by the subsequent supercritical carbon dioxide treatment process described in the study.

caption: IPF map of the repaired zone after 8 hours of aging at 780 ℃, depicting the final state of the repaired microstructure.
summary: Extended aging for 8 hours at 780 ℃ results in the final observed state of the repaired zone. The microstructure continues to be dominated by coarse polygonal and columnar grains, maintaining the structural contrast against the matrix as determined by the EBSD grain structure parameter calculations.

caption: Effect of μ-plasma torch travel speed on the deposition characteristics of Ti6Al4V5Cr alloy single-layer deposits.
summary: Faster travel speeds of the μ-plasma torch lead to a reduction in deposition width, height, efficiency, diluted depth, and percentage dilution. This decrease is attributed to the reduced interaction time between the heat input and the feedstock powder, which limits the amount of material melted during the deposition process.

caption: Surface roughness (Rq) values and 3D surface topography mapping of PVDF-HFP/TiO2 membranes.
summary: Atomic force microscopy was utilized to characterize the surface morphology of the PVDF-HFP/TiO2 membranes. The panel presents the calculated root-mean-square roughness (Rq) values alongside a 3D surface mapping inset, providing a detailed visualization of the membrane surface topography and the influence of the TiO2 nanoparticle incorporation on surface texture.

caption: Calculated evolution of the crystalline volume fraction X(t) at varying depths within the heat-affected zone (HAZ) under processing conditions of 100 W laser power and 10 mm/s scan speed.
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated evolution of the crystalline volume fraction X(t) at different depths within the HAZ. At a depth of 230 μm, just below the fusion zone, X(t) reaches 100% rapidly. Conversely, the inset indicates that at temperatures just below the melting point, the supercooled liquid maintains its amorphous state.

caption: Complex distribution of residual stresses in longitudinal, transverse, and normal directions across various thicknesses in the TR-AFSD 7075 repair, measured via neutron diffraction.
summary: This panel displays the complex residual stress distribution in longitudinal, transverse, and normal directions within the TR-AFSD 7075 repair. Neutron diffraction, chosen for its high penetration depth, allows for non-destructive measurement of d-spacings in multiple orientations. Data indicates significant transverse and longitudinal stress variations at a depth of 2.4 mm below the substrate surface.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of TCP and Ga-MBG/TCP scaffolds with varying Ga-MBG weight percentages.
summary: X-ray diffraction patterns of TCP and Ga-MBG/TCP scaffolds with varying Ga-MBG weight percentages. The patterns compare pure TCP with 5 wt%, 10 wt%, and 15 wt% Ga-MBG/TCP composites. This analysis evaluates the phase composition and structural consistency of the scaffolds as the concentration of the Ga-MBG additive is increased.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of site 1 in panel (e), demonstrating a well-ordered atomic arrangement of alpha-Ti.
summary: The diffraction pattern of site 1 confirms a well-ordered atomic arrangement of alpha-Ti. This observation is consistent with the high-resolution imaging, reinforcing the conclusion that this specific site maintains the crystalline characteristics of the alpha-Ti phase despite its proximity to the oxide film interface.

caption: Comparison of rupture time versus Larson–Miller parameters (LMP) for additively manufactured (AM) specimens and wrought materials, with a linear fit representing the wrought baseline.
summary: This plot evaluates the creep performance of AM materials against wrought counterparts using the Larson–Miller parameter. Experimental data indicates that as-built AM specimens exhibit inferior creep properties compared to wrought materials under tested conditions. A linear fit for wrought data serves as a reference to highlight the performance gap.

caption: Bode plots displaying impedance magnitude and phase angle versus frequency for wrought Ti–6Al–4V samples in HBSS, NaCl, and AS.
summary: Bode plots for wrought Ti–6Al–4V samples characterize the impedance magnitude and phase angle across the frequency spectrum. By comparing these results with the DED-LB samples, the plots highlight distinct variations in corrosion resistance, serving as a reference to evaluate the performance of the additively manufactured alloy against the conventional wrought material.

caption: Specific strength (SS) comparison across the different tested specimens.
summary: Specific strength (SS) values for the various specimens are presented in this bar chart to facilitate a direct comparison. This metric allows for the evaluation of the strength-to-weight ratio of the materials, providing insight into their relative mechanical efficiency as determined by the compression testing results.

caption: Evolution of the creep rate over time for both the DED specimen and the HIPed casting material, illustrating that the DED specimen maintains a lower creep rate throughout the duration of the test until the tertiary creep phase.
summary: Evolution of the creep rate over time for both the DED specimen and the HIPed casting material, illustrating that the DED specimen maintains a lower creep rate throughout the duration of the test until the tertiary creep phase. This lower creep rate is consistently maintained by the DED specimen compared to the casting.

caption: Numerical simulation of the TPMS-P specimen under varying load percentages.
summary: This panel displays the numerical simulation results for the TPMS-P specimen. The visualization characterizes the structural response and behavior of the TPMS-P architecture when subjected to different load percentages, providing insight into the mechanical performance and deformation characteristics of this specific lattice design under simulated loading conditions.

caption: Porosity distribution within the manufactured part assessed via X-ray computed tomography measurements.
summary: This panel displays the internal porosity of the manufactured part as evaluated through X-ray computed tomography. This non-destructive characterization technique provides a comprehensive assessment of the internal structural integrity, allowing for the quantification of void spaces and defects within the material volume as part of the post-process characterization workflow.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectrum of surfactant-assisted SnO2-CTAB nanostructures.
summary: Presented here is the UV-Vis absorption spectrum for SnO2 synthesized with the surfactant CTAB. This spectral data highlights how the inclusion of CTAB influences the ultraviolet and visible light absorption profile of the nanostructured SnO2 compound compared to the pure sample, reflecting changes in its electronic or structural properties.

caption: Magnified view of the B orientation fracture surface, revealing a pre-existing hot crack surrounded by localized dimple features.
summary: A magnified examination of the fracture surface in the B orientation reveals a pre-existing hot crack. The presence of dimple features surrounding this crack indicates that while a solidification defect was present, the surrounding material underwent ductile deformation during the tensile test, highlighting the local fracture behavior.

caption: Shot noise manifestation within the simulated diamond lattice structure.
summary: Shot noise is visualized here as a specific type of system noise affecting the diamond lattice structure. This representation highlights the stochastic nature of the noise present in the diamond lattice, distinguishing it from the band-like artifacts observed in other noise conditions.

caption: Open circuit voltage (OCV) profiles over three cycles for filament-based microbial fuel cells (MFCs) featuring a 0.4 mm membrane and 0.6 mm anode, comparing Layfomm-40, Layfomm-60, Lay felt, and Gel lay materials.
summary: This plot displays the open circuit voltage performance of four distinct filament-based MFCs over three cycles. The Gel lay material demonstrates superior performance with a maximum OCV of 0.41 V, followed by Lay fomm-60 at 0.4 V, Lay felt at 0.38 V, and Lay Fomm-40 at 0.32 V.

caption: Electronic density of states for the CoNi:N Ni alloy, illustrating the electronic state distribution following nitrogen doping at the nickel site.
summary: This panel presents the electronic density of states for the CoNi:N Ni alloy. By setting the Fermi level to zero, the plot reveals how nitrogen doping at the nickel site influences the electronic structure of the alloy, serving as a comparative point for the other nitrogen and oxygen doped variants.

caption: High-magnification STEM image of the redeposited layer showing high-density dislocation tangles within the underlying recast layer.
summary: This high-magnification STEM observation reveals the microstructure of the redeposited film. The underlying recast layer is characterized by the presence of high-density dislocation tangles, providing insight into the structural response of the material under the processing conditions described in the study.

caption: Wear coefficient and coefficient of friction (COF) plotted as a function of frictional power, featuring a second-order polynomial fit for wear volume and a third-order polynomial fit for COF.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between frictional power and tribological performance. The wear coefficient and COF are presented with polynomial regression lines to characterize the data trends. These results, derived from Eq. (1) and Eq. (2), demonstrate how frictional power quantitatively influences the wear behavior and friction characteristics of the material.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots illustrating the passive film growth on AP-NAB alloy during extended immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots characterize the growth of passive films on AP-NAB alloy during extended immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These curves provide essential data regarding the semiconductor properties of the surface film, reflecting the evolution of the protective layer over time in the corrosive chloride environment.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of pristine and KOH-soaked Ni-Co electrodes measured at a current density of 2 mA·cm⁻² within a potential window of 0 to 0.50 V.
summary: This panel displays the constant current charge-discharge curves for Ni-Co electrodes in a potential range of 0–0.50 V. By comparing pristine and soaked samples at 2 mA·cm⁻², the plot illustrates the evolution of capacitive behaviors, providing a baseline for evaluating the electrochemical performance of the electrodes before and after soaking.

caption: Trabecular number (Tb.N) measurements quantifying the density of new bone trabeculae at 4 and 8 weeks.
summary: Trabecular number values were recorded at 0.93 and 1.10 at week 4, rising to 1.82 and 2.15 at week 8 for the UI and GI groups. The data confirms an increase in the number of bone trabeculae, reflecting enhanced osseointegration and bone regeneration within the scaffold over the study period.

caption: STEM montage of a polished alloy variant exposed to 800 ºC for 2000 h, displaying elemental depletion beneath the surface oxide, internal Al2O3 precipitates in light contrast, and a planar interface separating the oxidation-affected region from the unaffected bulk alloy.
summary: This STEM montage illustrates the microstructural evolution of a polished alloy after 2000 hours of oxidation at 800 ºC. Key features include elemental depletion zones beneath the surface oxide, internal Al2O3 precipitates, and a distinct planar interface between the degraded sub-surface region and the unaffected alloy substrate.

caption: Normalized neutron diffraction patterns of the (200) plane for IN690 alloy across multiple strain states, highlighting the progressive peak broadening and positional shift.
summary: The (200) diffraction peak for IN690 is shown across strain levels ranging from 0% to 11.8%. The data indicates that peak broadening and lattice parameter shifts are consistent with the overall deformation behavior. These changes are critical for calculating dislocation density variations between the elastic and plastic regimes of the material.

caption: Immunofluorescent staining of FAK (green) and cytoskeleton (red) showing co-localization within the cells.
summary: Double fluorescent staining of FAK and F-actin reveals that green-labeled FAK co-localizes with the red-labeled cytoskeleton. Observations indicate that FAK fluorescence intensity is significantly higher in the stiff hydrogel group compared to other experimental conditions, highlighting the impact of substrate stiffness on focal adhesion formation and cytoskeletal organization.

caption: Comparison of overlaid part samples following an initial warp to approximate the perspective transformation from the original point-of-view to a top-down view, with displacement vectors Δs between high-resolution and low-resolution image fidelities.
summary: This panel displays the initial registration step where high-resolution and low-resolution images are overlaid after a perspective warp. By comparing the part samples from different orientations, the displacement vectors Δs are calculated, providing the necessary quantitative data to assess the misalignment between the two image fidelities before further correction.

caption: On-cooling dilatometry curves illustrating the martensitic transformation behavior across various cooling rates.
summary: Dilatometry experiments were performed at varying cooling rates to investigate the thermal stabilization of austenite. Panel (a) displays the resulting on-cooling dilatometry curves, which capture the martensitic transformation process. These readings provide the necessary data to evaluate how different cooling rates influence the transformation kinetics within the build center.

caption: Geometric illustration of columnar grain orientation, showing the [100] axis directed toward the melt pool center, while the [010] and [001] axes are randomly oriented orthogonally to the [100] axis.
summary: This illustration details the crystallographic orientation of columnar grains. The [100] axis is oriented toward the center of the melt pool, while the [010] and [001] axes are assigned random orientations orthogonal to the [100] axis, completing the geometric description of the grain texture within the simulated melt pool.

caption: Distribution of SHAP values for all selected features across individual samples, illustrating the impact of specific variables on fatigue life predictions.
summary: Detailed SHAP values for each sample are displayed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the predictor's significance. The plot reveals that high mean stresses negatively affect fatigue life, as indicated by negative SHAP values, which aligns with observed physical trends in the fatigue data analysis.

caption: Load-displacement response for pile LP2 with L/D = 3.0, comparing model predictions against Blessington pile test data.
summary: This plot displays the load-displacement response for pile LP2 with an L/D ratio of 3.0. The model effectively captures the yielding behavior of the pile, which the standard model fails to represent. The difference between model estimates is significant for this low L/D ratio pile.

caption: 3D topography of Ti-I small square patterns deposited via CSAM.
summary: Confocal microscopy provides a 3D topographic view of Ti-I small square patterns created by CSAM. By evaluating these surface profiles, the homogeneity of the Ti deposits is assessed, confirming the flow-field dimensions and structural integrity of the pins within this specific geometric configuration of the deposited material.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto565 dye, with an inset showing the printed samples.
summary: Transmission spectrum for a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto565 dye is shown, accompanied by an inset of the printed samples. This panel completes the characterization of the dye series, demonstrating the distinct optical filtering properties achieved in the 3D-printed polymer disks at a uniform thickness.

caption: Correlation between measured transition creep rates at 980 °C and 50 MPa and the interpolated stacking fault energy γSF of the matrix alloys.
summary: Transition creep rates for matrix alloys are presented as a function of the interpolated stacking fault energy γSF. These measurements were conducted at 980 °C and 50 MPa to investigate how stacking fault energy influences the creep performance of the tested alloy compositions within the experimental framework.

caption: Bright field TEM image showing the Cr2Al phase located at the lower region of the Ti2AlC MAX-phase within the TiAl48-2-2 alloy after 20 one-hour oxidation cycles at 850 °C.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging reveals the morphology of Cr2Al precipitates situated at the base of the Ti2AlC MAX-phase. The sample was extracted from a TiAl48-2-2 alloy subjected to 20 one-hour oxidation cycles at 850 °C in air, highlighting the microstructural evolution of the alloy under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Beeswarm plot of SHAP feature importance for surface pixels, highlighting the influence of cooling rate (CR) on local porosity prediction.
summary: This beeswarm plot displays SHAP feature importance for surface pixels, specifically focusing on the cooling rate (CR). Data points clustered near zero indicate minimal impact, while rare events with lower CR values show higher absolute SHAP values, demonstrating a significant contribution to increased local porosity in the analyzed material.

caption: Evolution of the friction coefficient over sliding time for TC4 and TaC/TC4 composites with varying TaC content.
summary: The friction coefficient of TC4 and TaC/TC4 composites is plotted against sliding time. Results indicate that the average friction coefficient increases progressively with TaC content, reaching values of 0.418, 0.435, 0.436, 0.439, and 0.455 for the respective samples. This increase is attributed to the exposure of hard particles enhancing surface roughness.

caption: In situ Raman spectra of Cu1Ni9 catalyst after the addition of 0.1 M N2H4, highlighting peaks at 734 and 1384 cm-1 corresponding to adsorbed *N2H4 and *NH2 species.
summary: In situ Raman spectroscopy of the Cu1Ni9 catalyst demonstrates the spontaneous adsorption of N2H4 molecules upon addition of 0.1 M N2H4. The emergence of distinct peaks at 734 and 1384 cm-1 is attributed to the N-N bond of adsorbed *N2H4 and the N-H bond of adsorbed *NH2, respectively.

caption: Rate performance comparison of a-Si, a-Ge, and a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-films across varying discharge current densities.
summary: Rate performance of a-Si, a-Ge, and a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-films is evaluated at different discharge current densities. The data demonstrates how the capacity of each material responds to increasing current, highlighting the superior rate capability of the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 alloy compared to the pure thin-film counterparts.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology and molten pool microstructure of LPBF-printed sample A2.
summary: Sample A2 displays a modified 3D molten pool morphology compared to A1, demonstrating the sensitivity of the molten pool structure to LPBF process parameter adjustments. The 3D reconstruction highlights the resulting microstructure, where only approximately one-fifth of the basal morphology remains observable due to the specific layer thickness used.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the ODS Ni–Cr–Al–Ti–0.5Y2O3 alloy aged at 850 °C, highlighting a Y2O2S dispersoid located within a γ-channel between two γ′ secondary precipitates, with Al and Y iso-surfaces rendered in blue and red, respectively.
summary: This APT reconstruction reveals the spatial distribution of a Y2O2S dispersoid within the alloy microstructure. Observations confirm that these dispersoids preferentially locate in γ-channels rather than within γ′ precipitates. Even at equilibrium γ′ fractions, a thin γ region persists between the γ′ phase and the Y2O2S dispersoid.

caption: EDS elemental maps of Ni, Mo, Fe, and Cr, showing the spatial distribution of elements across the transition zone.
summary: EDS elemental mapping reveals a transition zone approximately 81 μm wide between the NiMoCr cladding and the 316L substrate. The maps show increasing Ni and Mo concentrations alongside decreasing Fe and Cr levels from the substrate toward the cladding, confirming the presence of compositionally graded grains across the interface.

caption: Calculated formation energies for various cobalt phosphide phases as a function of cobalt and phosphorus content.
summary: This plot displays the formation energies of different Co-P compounds derived from atomistic calculations. The data highlights that the Co2P phase exhibits the lowest formation energy among the tested compounds, confirming its thermodynamic stability and suitability as a core component for the rationally designed nanowires in water electrolysis applications.

caption: Detailed atom map of the 4Al10V alloy highlighting the elemental distribution within the L21 phase.
summary: The atom map for the 4Al10V alloy demonstrates the specific elemental distribution within the L21 phase. Analysis confirms that this phase is rich in Al and V, whereas it is depleted in Fe and Cr, illustrating the chemical partitioning between the precipitate and the surrounding matrix.

caption: Contour plot visualizing the distribution of strains perpendicular to the load direction (εxx) for the TS-C2 specimen at peak load.
summary: Visualizing the εxx strain field, this contour plot highlights the distribution of strains perpendicular to the loading axis. Similar to the load-direction results, increased strain values are observed only in the region above the hole, directly adjacent to the contact interface between the bolt and the eye bar specimen.

caption: Fitness evolution curve plotted against increasing generations for the Christmas tree pattern optimization case.
summary: The fitness evolution for the Christmas tree pattern is shown as the generation count increases. This plot demonstrates the performance of the inverse optimization model, tracking how the fitness metric improves over time as the evolutionary algorithm iterates to refine the target pattern design.

caption: Chemical potential difference ΔμNi1/3 determined through thermodynamic integration of GCMC simulation data for the Ni-Cr binary system.
summary: This panel illustrates the chemical potential difference ΔμNi1/3, which is obtained via thermodynamic integration of GCMC simulation results for the Ni-Cr binary system. These calculations, presented alongside the ratio data, quantify the thermodynamic driving forces within the alloy system as determined by the computational modeling approach.

caption: Residual stress distribution map for the HVAF bond coat surface, illustrating stress concentrations around defects after 1 h of oxidation.
summary: This map illustrates the residual stress distribution across the HVAF bond coat surface following 1 h of oxidation. The data highlights how stress concentrations develop around defects, a phenomenon that mirrors the behavior observed in the APS bond coat, confirming consistent stress distribution patterns across these specific thermal spray coatings.

caption: High-resolution O1s XPS spectrum for CHBAC, highlighting the emergence of a carbonyl (C=O) peak at 531.5 eV due to catechin grafting.
summary: The O1s XPS spectrum for CHBAC shows a distinct carbonyl (C=O) peak at 531.5 eV. This peak emerges specifically due to post-catechin grafting, providing unequivocal evidence of successful catechin incorporation into the CHBAC composite structure, as supported by established scientific literature regarding these specific chemical interactions.

caption: False-colored tetramethylrhodamine isothiocyanate (TRITC) mixed isomers localized within the core cellulose nanocrystals (CNC), accompanied by a bright field inset.
summary: False-colored TRITC mixed isomers are visualized within the core cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) of the microcapsule. This imaging technique, supported by bright field microscopy, helps pinpoint the location of the nanoparticles and clarifies the internal composition of the phases within the microcapsules during the experimental analysis.

caption: Mechanical properties of AA7075 after hot forming and artificial aging, showing yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation as a function of tool temperatures ranging from 24 °C to 350 °C.
summary: Mechanical properties of AA7075 are evaluated following hot forming and artificial aging across a tool temperature range of 24 °C to 350 °C. Results indicate that a forming tool temperature of 24 °C achieves a yield strength of 490 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 575 MPa, alongside increased elongation after failure.

caption: {100}, {110}, and {111} pole figures for the 2 mm LMD stainless steel, demonstrating a strong <100> crystallographic texture with high concentrations of plane normals along the SD, TD, and BD axes.
summary: Pole figures for the 2 mm LMD stainless steel confirm a strong <100> crystallographic texture. High concentrations of {100} plane normals are observed along the SD, TD, and BD axes, particularly at φ = 0° and 90°. This preferred orientation indicates significant grain alignment resulting from the laser metal deposition process.

caption: Simulated uniaxial creep strain versus time curves for [001], [011], and [111] crystallographic orientations at 650 °C.
summary: Simulated uniaxial creep tests demonstrate the strain response over time for three distinct crystallographic orientations at 650 °C. In contrast to the indentation results, these simulations indicate that crystallographic orientation significantly influences the creep strain, leading to large differences in the mechanical behavior observed under uniaxial loading conditions.

caption: Distribution of scholarly publications regarding additive manufacturing of shape memory alloys (SMAs) categorized by academic discipline, based on data retrieved from the Scopus database.
summary: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of academic research publications focused on the additive manufacturing of shape memory alloys. By analyzing data from the Scopus database, the visualization provides a quantitative overview of the scholarly interest and investigation levels across various academic disciplines involved in SMA manufacturing processes.

caption: Current-time response recorded during a chronoamperometry experiment, illustrating the instantaneous electrical response of the samples to voltage switching through sharp vertical peaks.
summary: The chronoamperometry data demonstrates the material's rapid electrical response to voltage stimulation. Each time the voltage is switched on, the system exhibits a sudden, sharp rise in current, represented by vertical peaks in the multi-amperometry sweep plot, confirming the material's ability to respond instantaneously to external electrical signals.

caption: Schematic representation and microscopic image (scale bar: 1 mm) of the cone-shaped microneedle array sensor component.
summary: Depicted here is the cone-shaped microneedle array, fabricated using DLP 3D printing technology. The panel provides both a schematic design and a microscopic view of the component, which is part of the broader study to optimize sensor geometry for enhanced sensitivity in detecting small-scale mechanical displacements.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the solution-treated microstructure.
summary: Solution treatment effectively reduces the GND density to 21.8 × 10^12 m^-2. The map illustrates the reduction in dislocation accumulation within the grains, reflecting the relief of internal stresses and the structural recovery that occurs during the solution treatment process compared to the initial as-forged state.

caption: Steady-state tool temperatures recorded during the deposition of nine distinct blocks (B1–B9), illustrating the effectiveness of the temperature control system.
summary: This panel presents box plots of steady-state tool temperatures for nine separate builds, labeled B1 through B9. The data demonstrates the effectiveness of the implemented temperature control strategy during the deposition process, providing a clear visualization of the thermal stability achieved across all nine experimental blocks.

caption: Steady-state photoluminescence emission spectra comparing perovskite single crystals synthesized via batch (black) and flow-reactor (green) methods under 375 nm excitation.
summary: Steady-state photoluminescence emission spectra comparing perovskite single crystals synthesized via batch and flow-reactor methods under 375 nm excitation are presented. The flow-reactor crystal exhibits a two-fold increase in emission intensity compared to the batch-grown counterpart, demonstrating superior optoelectronic characteristics achieved through the continuous flow synthesis approach.

caption: TRIM simulation profile of 12 MeV proton interactions within a tungsten target, illustrating the calculation of the proton range limit.
