summary: This TRIM simulation profile models the interaction of 12 MeV protons with a tungsten target. The visualization demonstrates the methodology for determining the proton range limit, defined as the maximum distance where 99% or more of the protons travel through the sample rather than implanting into the material matrix.

caption: No-meltpool bead formation in Region III, featuring a thin reaction layer containing partially melted or unmelted powder particles.
summary: Region III of the CrMnFeCoNi HEA process map exhibits a no-meltpool type bead formation. Due to the high scanning speed employed during MBL-DED, partially melted or unmelted powder particles are visible near the bead surface, accompanied by a thin reaction layer formed during the deposition process.

caption: {100} pole figure for the specimen processed with a 0.3 T magnetic field, showing continuous, ring-shaped intensity distributions.
summary: The {100} pole figure for the specimen fabricated with a 0.3 T magnetic field displays continuous, ring-shaped distributions. This result contrasts significantly with the discrete pole patterns observed in samples fabricated without a magnetic field, highlighting the impact of magnetic processing on crystallographic texture.

caption: Detailed DSC thermograms highlighting the melting behavior of bamboo-PLA composites between 140 °C and 160 °C for different filler sizes and loading levels.
summary: This panel presents the DSC thermograms for bamboo-PLA composites within the 140 °C to 160 °C temperature range. These curves specifically capture the melting behavior of the composites, allowing for an analysis of how varying filler sizes and contents affect the thermal characteristics of the PLA-based material.

caption: Enlarged orientation map of the 4-hour sintered Inconel 625 sample, featuring a point-to-point misorientation profile along the indicated A-B arrow.
summary: This orientation map provides a detailed view of the 4-hour sintered microstructure. The point-to-point misorientation plot along the arrow identifies a Σ9 CSL boundary with a 38.2-degree misorientation near point A and a Σ3 CSL twin boundary with a 59.8-degree misorientation near point B, illustrating boundary coarsening and coalescence.

caption: Experimental setup featuring a sintered cylindrical sample mounted on a DTC-25 thermal conductivity meter, configured for the precise determination of thermal conductivity properties.
summary: This image depicts the experimental configuration used to measure thermal conductivity. A sintered cylindrical sample is mounted onto the DTC-25 thermal conductivity meter. This setup is essential for characterizing the thermal transport properties of the material after it has undergone the sintering process described in the previous panels.

caption: t-SNE embedding plot illustrating the distribution of melt pool samples based on energy density, demonstrating a clear trend in the latent space representation.
summary: This t-SNE embedding plot demonstrates that the model learns generalizable and intuitive representations of physical mechanisms, as evidenced by the clear trends observed regarding the energy density of each melt pool. These results confirm that the low-dimensional latent space effectively captures key physical properties of the simulated melt pool data.

caption: Superimposed IR-derived cooling curves color-coded by thermal cycle number plotted against measured continuous cooling transformation (CCT) data for HSLA steel.
summary: Cooling curves extracted from IR data during additive manufacturing are superimposed onto the measured CCT diagram for HSLA steel. The curves are color-coded by thermal cycle number, and the observed inflection points in these IR-based cooling profiles correspond directly to the transformation start temperatures identified in the CCT data.

caption: Phase fraction versus temperature plot for the Al-4.0Mn-0.6Sc-3.0TiN (wt. %) alloy calculated via CALPHAD methods.
summary: This CALPHAD-derived plot illustrates the phase fraction as a function of temperature for the Al-4.0Mn-0.6Sc-3.0TiN alloy. Thermodynamic calculations confirm the presence of the Al3Ti phase precipitated within the TiN-modified Al-Mn-Sc alloy system, providing essential insights into the equilibrium phase stability and precipitation behavior of the material at varying temperatures.

caption: Precipitation-Time-Temperature (PTT) graph for M23C6 carbide, illustrating the kinetics of initial and final precipitation stages.
summary: This PTT graph for M23C6 carbides delineates the transformation kinetics by identifying the initial and final precipitation points. These data points were derived from X-ray intensity measurements, providing a clear representation of the precipitation evolution over time and temperature, which is essential for understanding the phase stability of the material.

caption: Simulated fields of temperature, MCH, TOL, and H2 concentrations in a 50 mm diameter CSM–n/m reactor at 613 K and 6 bara.
summary: Simulated fields for temperature and concentrations of MCH, TOL, and H2 are visualized for a scaled 50 mm diameter, 250 mm length CSM–n/m reactor. The simulation is performed at 613 K and 6 bara, providing a spatial representation of the thermal and chemical gradients within the reactor system.

caption: Thermo-magnetization curves of the material measured under applied magnetic fields of 0.005, 1, 2, and 3 T, showing mass magnetization as a function of temperature between 125 and 325 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the mass magnetization behavior across a temperature range of 125 to 325 K under varying magnetic fields. The dual-axis representation highlights magnetization values for low and high fields. Observations indicate that magnetic phase transformation temperatures shift toward lower values as the applied magnetic field strength increases.

caption: Nucleation of new discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX) grains occurring at the sites of distorted twins through twinning phenomena.
summary: New recrystallized grains nucleate at the distorted twin boundaries shown in the previous stage. This process occurs via twinning phenomena specifically at locations where the boundary misorientation has substantially deviated from the ideal Σ3 condition. This mechanism highlights how twin distortion facilitates the formation of new grains during hot compression deformation.

caption: X-ray intensity map of Co K distribution across the IN939-3Si cantilever surface.
summary: Cobalt K X-ray intensity mapping provides insight into the elemental composition of the IN939-3Si cantilever. The observed distribution supports the identification of a columnar structure, which is a recurring feature in the material's microstructure, documented across multiple experimental observations and linked to the presence of specific precipitate cell structures.

caption: Rate capability performance showing specific capacitance as a function of increasing current density.
summary: Rate capability of the Ni-Co/rGO electrode is evaluated by measuring specific capacitance across increasing current densities. This plot demonstrates the material's electrochemical stability and performance retention when subjected to varying discharge rates, confirming its suitability for high-rate applications as indicated by the experimental data.

caption: Chronocoulometric Q-t curves and Q-t^1/2 linear plots for an FeNi@C/GCE in 0.1 M PBS, displaying the charge response in the absence of analytes (a, a') and with 0.3 μM AC (b, b') or 1 μM RT (c, c').
summary: FeNi@C/GCE electrochemical activity is characterized by chronocoulometric Q-t and Q-t^1/2 plots in 0.1 M PBS. The data illustrates the charge accumulation kinetics on the FeNi@C surface, providing a comparative analysis of the electrode's response to the presence of 0.3 μM AC and 1 μM RT versus the blank electrolyte.

caption: In-plane 3D-printed sandwich structure with a 1.6 mm surface thickness after bending, illustrating the characteristic failure mode of the core and skin assembly.
summary: This image captures the failure mode of an in-plane 3D-printed sandwich structure with a 1.6 mm surface thickness after a 3-point bending test. The specimen illustrates the typical bending behavior of these structures, where the failure mode is influenced by the orientation of the core relative to the applied load.

caption: Stress distribution map highlighting Von-mises values across the structure of Lattice 5.
summary: Lattice 5 is evaluated using the Abaqus static structural module to map its Von-mises stress distribution. This simulation is essential for understanding the stress analysis behavior of the lattice, providing a computational basis to validate the experimental results observed in the study of these specific structures.

caption: Fracture surface morphology of the cellular specimen with a 1.4 mm strut at 5.0 KX magnification.
summary: Fracture surface analysis of the cellular specimen with a 1.4 mm strut is captured at 5.0 KX magnification. Consistent with broader fractography observations, this sample exhibits particle-initiated fracture modes without layer delamination, confirming that the fracture process remains uniform across varying strut geometries during fatigue testing.

caption: Three-dimensional deviation map providing a comparative analysis of the CT reconstruction model against the engineering design specifications.
summary: This three-dimensional deviation map offers a detailed comparison between the CT reconstruction model and the engineering design. By visualizing the deviations in three dimensions, it allows for a comprehensive assessment of the manufacturing precision, ensuring that the final part adheres to the intended design specifications despite potential minor microscale variations.

caption: Ceramic scaffold architecture featuring a gradient pore structure generated via the Voronoi-Tessellation principle to accommodate localized mechanical requirements.
summary: This ceramic scaffold utilizes a Voronoi-Tessellation design to implement a gradient pore structure. By varying porosity spatially, the scaffold is engineered to match local mechanical demands within the mandibular region, as demonstrated in recent oro-maxillofacial reconstruction studies focusing on optimized structural design for bone tissue engineering applications.

caption: Assembly schematic illustrating the integration of an additive manufactured PHEV2 battery cell cap and its corresponding can housing.
summary: This schematic depicts the assembly process for an additive manufactured PHEV2 battery cell, specifically highlighting the structural integration between the cell cap and the can housing. The visualization provides a clear overview of the component alignment and mechanical configuration required for the final battery cell housing assembly in this manufacturing context.

caption: Bode plots displaying impedance magnitude |Z| and phase angle for Mg–Er–Gd–Ni alloys, highlighting lower values for extruded samples with low Gd content.
summary: Bode plots for Mg–Er–Gd–Ni alloys illustrate the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle. The data reveals that alloys with low Gd content, particularly after the extrusion process, exhibit a smaller |Z| value and a lower phase angle compared to other conditions, indicating distinct corrosion resistance characteristics.

caption: High-magnification HAADF-STEM image showing needle-shaped precipitates and micro-TiB2 particles in the A205 Al alloy.
summary: High-magnification HAADF-STEM imaging reveals the presence and distribution of needle-shaped precipitates alongside micro-TiB2 particles within the A205 Al alloy matrix. The image highlights the morphological characteristics of these phases across the three tested heat treatment conditions, providing insight into the microstructural evolution of the L-PBF processed material.

caption: Computational domain and mesh configuration for Solidworks Flow Simulation®.
summary: This visualization displays the computational domain and basic mesh used in Solidworks Flow Simulation®. The domain dimensions are defined as 66 × 30 × 74 mm, with a uniform mesh size of 2 mm applied throughout the model to facilitate the numerical analysis of the fluid flow behavior within the specified geometry.

caption: Postprandial salivary glucose levels plotted against blood glucose levels for diabetic subjects.
summary: Postprandial glucose dynamics are evaluated in this scatter plot, comparing salivary and blood glucose levels in diabetic patients. By examining these clinical samples, the figure highlights the correlation between glucose concentrations after food intake, contributing to the broader assessment of salivary glucose as a diagnostic indicator for diabetic subjects.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for the analyzed alloy compositions, displaying heat flow as a function of temperature.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for the analyzed alloy compositions, displaying heat flow as a function of temperature. The experimental results demonstrate that all analyzed compositions exhibit two distinct exothermic peaks, indicating specific thermal events occurring during the heating process for the materials under investigation in this study.

caption: Electrical resistivity comparison of as-prepared (AP) and 1000–24 processed samples determined via 4-point probe measurement.
summary: Electrical resistivity of as-prepared (AP) and 1000–24 samples was evaluated using a 4-point probe measurement method. This technique provides a precise assessment of the electronic transport properties for both material conditions, allowing for a direct comparison of the resistivity values between the AP and the 1000–24 processed samples.

caption: Elasticity modulus of the gyroid sheet network plotted against varying unit cell sizes as predicted by the Gibson-Ashby model.
summary: This plot illustrates the elasticity modulus of a gyroid sheet network with 70% porosity, calculated using the Gibson-Ashby model across different unit cell sizes. The data demonstrates that mechanical properties, specifically the elastic modulus, are primarily governed by porosity levels rather than variations in the unit cell dimensions.

caption: Calculated vertical section of the Al–Ni–V system along the AlNi–V join, featuring the experimentally determined eutectic point reported by Milenkovic et al.
summary: This vertical section of the Al–Ni–V system illustrates the phase relationships along the AlNi–V join. The diagram incorporates calculated phase boundaries alongside the measured eutectic composition previously established by Milenkovic et al., providing a comprehensive overview of the thermodynamic behavior and solidification characteristics within this specific ternary alloy system.

caption: Nyquist plot illustrating the impedance characteristics of HSLA-80 base metal (BM) and heat-affected zone (HAZ) tested in 0.6 M NaCl at 24 ± 1 °C.
summary: The Nyquist plot for the HSLA-80 group, including the base metal and heat-affected zone, is presented here. Tested in 0.6 M NaCl, these plots form a distinct group separate from the Inconel-625 samples, with the grouping determined by the specific size of the capacitive loop observed during electrochemical testing.

caption: Representative bright-field TEM image of deformation-induced stacking faults in the α-Nb2C carbide, with an inserted SAED pattern showing streaking indicated by a purple arrow.
summary: This bright-field TEM image illustrates deformation-induced stacking faults in the α-Nb2C carbide after tensile testing. The inserted SAED pattern exhibits characteristic streaking, highlighted by a purple arrow, which serves as definitive evidence for the presence of stacking faults within the carbide structure of the fractured specimen.

caption: Rotary torque performance comparison of HT and SMC materials at a 1 mm airgap length, highlighting the superior performance of Fe-3.5Si alloy under ferrite-excited weak magnetic fields.
summary: This plot compares the rotary torque performance of HT and SMC materials at a 1 mm airgap. Under strong NbFeB-excited fields, HT shows the second-highest torque. Conversely, in weak ferrite-excited fields, the additively manufactured Fe-3.5Si alloy demonstrates a 10% improvement in maximum rotary torque compared to SMC-1000-3P.

caption: Power versus temperature plot for alloy 42 specimen, displaying the Curie temperature marked as the average of transition points.
summary: The power versus temperature plot for the alloy 42 specimen is shown in this panel. The Curie temperature is determined by calculating the average of two transition temperatures, which is then explicitly marked on the graph to indicate the magnetic transition point for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Experimental setup featuring the impedance tube and data acquisition system used for measuring the sound absorption coefficient of the printed lattice samples.
summary: The experimental setup includes an impedance tube and a data acquisition system used to measure the sound absorption coefficient (SAC) of the printed lattice samples. Measurements were conducted using the BSWA SW4601 tube in strict accordance with the ASTM E1050-19 standards to ensure accurate and reproducible acoustic data.

caption: Nyquist plots of NiMo@NF electrodes measured at 0.528 V vs RHE, demonstrating the effect of CV cycling on impedance response.
summary: Impedance spectra for NiMo@NF are presented as Nyquist plots to evaluate the effects of CV cycling. These plots, alongside the Cdl measurements, confirm that CV cycling induces measurable changes in the electrode's electrochemical properties, consistent with the observed 16% increase in capacitance values following the accelerated degradation test procedure.

caption: Optimized HPLC chromatogram of standard SLM showing the baseline analyte signal.
summary: This panel displays the optimized HPLC chromatogram for standard SLM. It serves as the baseline reference for the analyte, establishing the characteristic retention time and peak profile used to verify the chemical identity of SLM in subsequent formulations and complex biological matrices throughout the experimental analysis.

caption: Adjusted ternary phase diagram of the Cu-Cr-Zr system, featuring non-equivalent axis ranges to enhance the visualization of the specific composition range of interest.
summary: This figure presents an adjusted ternary phase diagram for the Cu-Cr-Zr system. By utilizing non-equivalent axis ranges, the plot effectively highlights the specific composition range of interest. This focused representation improves the visualization of phase relationships within the system, facilitating a clearer understanding of the material's thermodynamic behavior.

caption: Comparison of experimental and theoretical ellipsometry data for Zn 0.90 Ni 0.10 Te thin films.
summary: This plot illustrates the ellipsometric curve fitting for Zn 0.90 Ni 0.10 Te thin films. Using the Cauchy and effective medium approximation model, the theoretical Psi and Delta values are calculated and compared against experimental measurements to accurately determine the optical constants and thickness of the 10% nickel-doped film.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the W-20Cu composite processed at 1200W.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a high-resolution visualization of the W-20Cu composite microstructure produced at 1200W laser power. The imaging technique effectively highlights the contrast between the constituent phases, serving as the foundational view for subsequent elemental mapping and detailed structural analysis of the tungsten and copper particle distribution.

caption: Radar plot illustrating the normalized yield strength, total elongation, and reduction in area for the ASP-Z specimen across unirradiated, 0.75 dpa, and 2.1 dpa irradiation conditions.
summary: This radar plot visualizes the mechanical property balance for the ASP-Z specimen. By normalizing yield strength, total elongation, and reduction in area to a 1-10 scale, it highlights the trade-off between hardening and ductility as a function of irradiation dose, comparing the unirradiated state against 0.75 dpa and 2.1 dpa conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the Ni/HZSM-5 catalyst showing the characteristic peak at 44.6°.
summary: The X-ray diffraction pattern of the Ni/HZSM-5 catalyst displays a characteristic peak at 44.6°, which corresponds to the (111) crystal plane of nickel. This result is consistent with the d-spacing measurements obtained from high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, confirming the crystalline nature of the nickel nanoparticles present in the catalyst.

caption: Unrolled 2D synchrotron HEXRD pattern at 900°C, where yellow arrows indicate semi-coherent γ particles exhibiting features characteristic of the Kurdjumov-Sachs orientation relationship.
summary: At 900°C, the diffraction pattern shows semi-coherent γ particles that have developed features characteristic of the Kurdjumov-Sachs orientation relationship. These observations, marked by yellow arrows, illustrate the advanced growth stages of the γ phase and the specific crystallographic alignment achieved at this elevated temperature during the in-situ experiment.

caption: Atomic model illustrating the crystal structure of Ni2Si and (Ni, Co)2Si, showing the substitution of Ni atoms by Co atoms.
summary: This atomic model depicts the crystal structure of Ni2Si and (Ni, Co)2Si. Further analysis indicates that approximately 0.7 wt% Co atoms occupy the positions of 20% of the Ni atoms, meaning eight Ni atoms per unit volume are replaced by roughly two Co atoms, demonstrating the specific lattice substitution mechanism.

caption: Raman intensity map of the selected area showing the spatial distribution of m-ZrO2-rich regions, highlighted in red.
summary: This Raman intensity map visualizes the spatial distribution of m-ZrO2-rich regions within the SC sample, represented by the red color. The mapping confirms the presence of these specific phases within the analyzed area, providing insight into the microstructural heterogeneity of the sintered material.

caption: Calculated DOS effective mass and band effective mass as a function of Ni alloying content in Bi2-xNixSe3.
summary: This panel displays the calculated density of states effective mass and band effective mass for Bi2-xNixSe3 samples as a function of Ni alloying content. The data illustrates how the electronic properties, specifically the effective masses, evolve with varying nickel concentrations within the bismuth selenide crystal structure.

caption: Profile of the atomic structure model for the Ni-based superalloy without Co addition, featuring a simulation box size of 140.8 Å × 140.8 Å × 140.8 Å.
summary: The atomic structure model for the Ni-based superalloy without Co addition is depicted here. The simulation box measures 140.8 Å × 140.8 Å × 140.8 Å, achieving a γ′ volume fraction of approximately 72.9%, which effectively mimics the microstructure of actual superalloy materials for computational analysis.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots displaying the inverse square of capacitance versus potential for LPBF-consolidated NAB alloys in as-built and two distinct annealed conditions.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots for LPBF-consolidated NAB alloys illustrate the relationship between space-charge capacitance and potential across three sample conditions. These curves reveal both positive and negative slopes, indicating complex semiconducting behavior. The donor and acceptor densities, labeled N1, N2, and N3, are derived from these specific regions of the plots.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PGA prepared from GAMes with a GA/TSA ratio of 1000:1 at 205 °C for 1 day.
summary: Representing entry 4A from Table 4, this mass spectrum illustrates the PGA product obtained at a higher temperature of 205 °C with a specific GA/TSA ratio of 1000:1. Catalysis with TSA under these conditions promotes the formation of monodisperse extended-ring crystallites, as evidenced by the resulting mass distribution profile.

caption: Pole figure representation for the P3 alloy under PS-1 conditions, showing the intensity distribution of crystallographic orientations with a scale ranging from 0 to 7.5.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the crystallographic orientation intensity for the P3 alloy processed with the PS-1 parameter set. With a color scale spanning 0 to 7.5, the plot confirms the presence of a strong texture associated with the columnar microstructure observed in the corresponding IPF map.

caption: Bubble plot showing GO enrichment analysis results for HUVECs, highlighting significant biological processes with an adjusted p-value (q-value) < 0.5.
summary: The bubble plot displays the GO enrichment analysis for HUVECs, identifying key biological processes influenced by the scaffold environment. With an adjusted p-value (q-value) < 0.5, the analysis reveals significant enrichment patterns, indicating that the PTMN group promotes specific gene expression profiles associated with cellular functions compared to the PT group.

caption: Radar chart comparing mechanical property isotropy of initial and optimized TAAMs at a relative density of ρ = 0.2.
summary: This radar chart illustrates the mechanical property isotropy for TAAMs at a relative density of 0.2. Experimental results confirm that the optimized design exhibits significantly improved isotropy and more uniform directional properties compared to the initial design, validating the effectiveness of the MBO framework in enhancing structural performance.

caption: Temperature-dependent yield stress of nanocrystalline Au micropillars measured at 23, 50, 75, and 100°C, showing two distinct strain rate sensitivity regimes fitted with quasistatic (dashed) and high strain rate (solid) lines.
summary: Nanocrystalline Au micropillars exhibit temperature-dependent yield stress across four temperatures. Analysis of the stress-strain data reveals two distinct regimes of strain rate sensitivity, characterized by quasistatic and high strain rate behaviors. These fitted regimes allow for the calculation of strain rate sensitivity parameters, providing insight into the material's mechanical response.

caption: Linear depth (μm) derived from electron CSDA ranges using the ESTAR database for EL, BL, and ICRP 116 phantoms.
summary: The graph illustrates the converted CSDA range in micrometers for EL, BL, and ICRP 116 phantoms, calculated by dividing ESTAR-based CSDA ranges by material density. This data provides the physical basis for the sharp increase in absorbed dose observed in the corresponding energy-dependent dose simulations.

caption: Substitutional atoms occupy high-symmetry positions within the crystal lattice structure.
summary: Substitutional atoms are distributed in high-symmetry positions within the crystal lattice. This atomic model represents one of the configurations used in the computational calculations, illustrating the specific arrangement of atoms within the material structure to facilitate accurate modeling of the system's properties during the simulation process.

caption: Weight gain measurements for Ni-20Cr-Si alloy versus undoped Ni-20Cr, highlighting oxidation performance in Ar-5H2O.
summary: The weight gain of Ni-20Cr-Si alloy is plotted against time during exposure to an Ar-5H2O environment. When contrasted with the undoped Ni-20Cr baseline, this data reveals how silicon additions modify the oxidation kinetics, providing insight into the protective nature of the oxide scales formed on the alloy surface.

caption: Macroscopic stress-strain response of the polycrystal model in the z-direction under a strain ratio of R = 0.
summary: This panel illustrates the macroscopic stress-strain behavior of the polycrystal model subjected to a strain ratio of R = 0. The data represents the mechanical response in the z-direction, providing insight into the material's deformation characteristics under these specific loading conditions as determined by the polycrystal model simulation.

caption: Extracted EXAFS oscillations at the Zn K-edge for all analyzed samples.
summary: This panel displays the extracted EXAFS oscillations measured at the Zn K-edge for every sample. These oscillations provide critical structural information regarding the local atomic environment of zinc atoms within the material, serving as the primary data for subsequent Fourier transform analysis and structural fitting procedures.

caption: Energy absorption of as-built and heat-treated lattice structures plotted against relative density, showing the impact of SHT and SHT + AA heat treatments.
summary: Energy absorption of the lattice structures is fitted to the Gibson-Ashby model without normalization. The plot demonstrates that energy absorption increases when SHT and SHT + AA heat treatments are applied to as-built lattice structures, reflecting the improved mechanical performance achieved through these specific thermal processing routes.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ni–Co system, identifying the fcc Ni-type (A1) and hcp Co-type (A3) structures, with triangular markers indicating the positions of various Ni-Co-GDC compositions at 800 °C.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the Ni–Co system delineates the stability regions for fcc and hcp structures. Triangular symbols represent specific Ni-GDC and Ni-Co-GDC compositions at 800 °C. The diagram predicts that all five compositions form fcc Ni–Co alloys in a reducing atmosphere, consistent with experimental observations of alloy formation.

caption: Unit cell configuration after the sixth thermomechanical cycle.
summary: Illustrated is the final unit cell configuration after six complete thermomechanical cycles. This panel concludes the observation of the structural evolution, showing the stabilized state of the material. The data confirms that the recovery characteristics are established after the initial cycles, completing the assessment of the thermomechanical cycling performance.

caption: Elemental composition line scan profile across the corrosion layer of SL Ni coated plain In800H after 100 h of immersion.
summary: This panel displays the elemental composition profile obtained via EDS line scan for SL Ni coated plain In800H after 100 h of immersion. The pink shaded region highlights the corrosion layer thickness, providing a baseline for assessing the protective performance of the coating during the initial stages of molten salt exposure.

caption: SEM-EDS elemental mapping of Ni and Ti, revealing the eutectic solidification structure where both elements are enriched in the same regions, including the fine Laves phase indicated by a red arrow.
summary: The SEM-EDS mapping visualizes the eutectic solidification structure characteristic of the 11 at. % Ti composition. Ni and Ti are shown to be enriched together within the eutectic constituent, which consists of austenite and Laves phase. A red arrow highlights a specific region containing fine Laves phase particles.

caption: NMR spectra comparing aqueous humor samples from control and patient groups, highlighting signal intensity variations across specific metabolites.
summary: NMR analysis validates the authenticity of aqueous humor samples by comparing control and patient groups. The spectra reveal increased signal intensities in regions corresponding to glucose, alanine, lactate, glutamine, creatine, and lysine, providing a metabolic profile that distinguishes the patient samples from the control group during the clinical study.

caption: Normal distribution plot of micro-Al particle sizes, showing an average diameter of 5.19 μm.
summary: Particle sizes of 100 micro-Al particles were analyzed to generate a normal distribution plot. The statistical analysis reveals an average particle size of 5.19 μm for the micro-Al sample. This histogram represents the size distribution data, highlighting the calculated average value for this specific material population.

caption: Temporal evolution of electronic and atomic temperatures in NiFe alloy for a 0.2 ps electron-phonon coupling activation time.
summary: This panel depicts the temporal evolution of electronic and atomic temperatures in a NiFe alloy system, utilizing a 0.2 ps electron-phonon coupling activation time. The data represents the thermal behavior within the center cell of the MD box for a cascade initiated near the corner of the simulation domain.

caption: Digital image and schematic representation of the Lithoz CeraFab 8500 ceramic 3D printer utilized for the fabrication of alumina slurry components.
summary: This panel displays the Lithoz CeraFab 8500 ceramic 3D printer through both a schematic diagram and a digital photograph. The equipment is specifically employed for the additive manufacturing of alumina slurry parts, serving as the primary hardware setup for the lithography-based ceramic manufacturing process described in the study.

caption: Locally enlarged emission spectrum of LHAM in the 250 nm–500 nm wavelength range, calibrated for ionization analysis.
summary: This panel shows a calibrated, locally enlarged view of the LHAM emission spectrum between 250 nm and 500 nm. This specific wavelength range was isolated and calibrated to facilitate a detailed investigation into the ionization behavior of the substance, providing clearer spectral features for subsequent analysis.

caption: Creep strain rate versus time curves for the three experimental alloys evaluated under identical conditions of 1100 °C and 130 MPa.
summary: Creep strain rate-time curves are presented for the three experimental alloys tested at 1100 °C and 130 MPa. These curves characterize the temporal evolution of the creep strain rate, providing insight into the deformation kinetics of the alloys as they undergo high-temperature mechanical loading during the creep testing process.

caption: Liquid bridge formation under 0 g gravity directed at -Z (0°) with 150 W laser power and 120 mm/min wire feeding and movement speeds.
summary: The transient metal wire melting process is shown during a single deposition. Under microgravity conditions (0 g) with a -Z (0°) orientation, the liquid bridge is formed at 150 W laser power and 120 mm/min wire feeding and movement speeds, revealing the melting dynamics in the absence of gravitational force.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectra of Ce3+ and Mn2+ doped YAG or Ce3+ doped YAG/Al2O3 particles, exhibiting a blue-shift in the Ce3+ yellow emission without Cr3+ signatures.
summary: This panel displays photoluminescence spectra for particles that lack Cr3+ emission signatures. Despite the absence of Cr3+, these particles exhibit a characteristic blue-shift in the 5d to 4f Ce3+ yellow emission, suggesting potential doping with Mn2+ or the presence of Ce3+ doped YAG/Al2O3 composite structures.

caption: Comparison of vacancy diffusion constants at 1373 K between current KMC simulations and previously reported results by Goswami and Grabowski.
summary: Panel b provides a comparative analysis of vacancy diffusion constants at a fixed temperature of 1373 K. By benchmarking current KMC simulation results against established data from Goswami and Grabowski, this plot validates the accuracy and consistency of the current computational model in predicting vacancy diffusion behavior in the studied system.

caption: Neutron diffraction pattern of the C20 sample at 300 K, featuring full spectrum fitting and residual difference profiles.
summary: Neutron diffraction analysis performed at 300 K provides detailed insights into the crystal structure and phase distribution of the C20 sample post-cycling. The measured pattern, represented by empty dots, is compared against a full spectrum fit, with the difference profile confirming the accuracy of the structural characterization.

caption: Western blotting analysis of osteogenesis-related protein expression, specifically COL1, OPN, and BMP2, in rBMSCs treated with scaffold extracts.
summary: Western blotting images display the protein expression levels of osteogenic markers COL1, OPN, and BMP2 in rBMSCs following treatment with different scaffold extracts. This analysis, combined with RT-PCR data, was conducted to evaluate the influence of the scaffolds on the osteogenic differentiation potential of the rBMSC cells.

caption: Ternary distribution map of the ultimate tensile strength for produced filaments, incorporating both experimental measurements and extrapolated data for specific formulations F1 and F7.
summary: This ternary distribution map illustrates the ultimate tensile strength of produced filaments across various formulations. The data indicates that both SEBS and LDPE components contribute positively to the tensile strength of the filaments. The plot integrates experimental results with extrapolated values for formulations F1 and F7 to provide a comprehensive overview.

caption: Local axial strain component Ɛyy contour map and crack morphology for the PD5% specimen oriented at 0°.
summary: This panel displays the local axial strain component Ɛyy contour map and post-fracture crack morphology for a PD5% specimen tested at a 0° orientation. The visualization provides insight into the strain distribution and failure behavior of the material under tensile loading conditions prior to and immediately following specimen fracture.

caption: X-Y cross-sectional view at a 30 μm depth showing the grain structure after the rescan process.
summary: This X-Y cross-sectional view, taken at a depth of 30 μm, illustrates the grain structure after the rescan. The simulation demonstrates how the secondary laser pass modifies the horizontal grain arrangement, allowing for a direct comparison with the initial scan results at the same depth within the material.

caption: Material dispersion curve of bulk CD-16 heavy metal oxide glass, illustrating the relationship between refractive index and wavelength.
summary: The material dispersion of bulk CD-16 glass is presented, demonstrating typical characteristics associated with lead borate glasses. This plot maps the refractive index as a function of wavelength, providing essential optical data for the material. These findings confirm that the dispersion behavior aligns with established properties of similar heavy metal oxide glass systems.

caption: Representative original µCT slice showing the raw cross-sectional intensity data of the material sample.
summary: The original µCT slice provides the foundational raw data for the segmentation process. Captured as a cross-sectional view, this image represents the initial state of the material before computational processing, serving as the primary input for the subsequent intensity histogram analysis and binary mask generation stages.

caption: Mott-Schottky analysis performed in a borate buffer solution, comparing the capacitance and charge carrier density of specimens subjected to tensile stress against those in an unstressed state.
summary: Mott-Schottky analysis conducted in borate buffer solution demonstrates the impact of mechanical loading on electrochemical properties. Comparing specimens with and without tensile stress reveals significant variations in capacitance and charge carrier density, providing insight into how mechanical strain influences the electronic structure of the passive film on the material surface.

caption: Stitched IPF map showing the microstructure after deformation to a strain of 0.6.
summary: The stitched IPF map at a strain of 0.6 displays the evolving grain structure. This visualization allows for the assessment of grain orientation changes and structural development across the specified sample area, contributing to the overall understanding of the material's response to higher levels of deformation.

caption: Wear track profile of 2WC composite demonstrating the surface geometry after tribological testing.
summary: The wear track profile for the 2WC composite is presented here, illustrating the surface geometry resulting from the wear test. This measurement contributes to the broader analysis of how WC reinforcement concentrations influence the abrasive wear resistance and track dimensions compared to the unreinforced SS316L stainless steel baseline.

caption: Manganese elemental distribution map across the well-joined interface cross-section.
summary: Manganese elemental distribution across the well-joined interface cross-section is visualized to complete the elemental profile of the junction. This map, alongside other elemental data, helps in understanding the chemical gradients present at the interface, which is essential for evaluating the metallurgical characteristics of the well-joined material system.

caption: HER overpotentials for MCo@NC (M: Mn, Fe, Ni, Zn) alloys, comparing 25% and 50% metal concentration to identify optimal transition metal incorporation.
summary: Simulations indicate that the incorporation of Ni into Co leads to a higher reaction rate than other transition metals, as shown by the HER overpotentials on MCo@NC alloys. This finding is consistent with the lowest overpotential observed for Ni1Co3@NC in experimental tests, confirming the superior catalytic activity.

caption: Tauc plot representation showing the relationship between (hνα)^1/2 and photon energy (eV) for TixOy films, yielding calculated band gap (Eg) values of 3.52, 3.55, 3.27, and 3.16 eV for treatments T1 through T4.
summary: The relationship between (hνα)^1/2 and energy in eV is plotted for TixOy films deposited on SLB substrates under four different treatments. The calculated energy band gap values for T1, T2, T3, and T4 are 3.52, 3.55, 3.27, and 3.16 eV, respectively, illustrating the influence of the factorial design on optical properties.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the Cu–Al binary system, highlighting the precipitation point at 11.8 wt% Al.
summary: This binary phase diagram illustrates the thermodynamic equilibrium of the Cu–Al system. It identifies the precipitation point at 11.8 wt% Al, which serves as a critical reference for evaluating the hyper-eutectoid nature of Cu-Al-based alloys, such as the Cu-12.5Al–3Mn alloy, which contains 12.5 wt% Al.

caption: Ni 2p3/2 XPS spectra for Cu1 and Cu5 steel samples, showing the nickel oxidation states within the corrosion products after 6 hours of galvanostatic polarization.
summary: Nickel 2p3/2 XPS spectra characterize the oxidation states of nickel in the corrosion product films of Cu1 and Cu5 steels. Following 6 hours of galvanostatic polarization at 10 mA/cm2, these spectra are used to clarify the existing forms of nickel and assess the impact of copper content on film composition.

caption: Chemical structure representation of epoxidized vegetable oils (EVOs) used in the UV-cationic curing process.
summary: This panel illustrates the chemical structure of epoxidized vegetable oils, which serve as the primary precursors for the UV-cationic curing process. These materials are specifically utilized in Hot Lithography, where their epoxy groups undergo ring-opening reactions to facilitate polymerization and network formation during the curing cycle.

caption: Long-term fatigue performance of G10P10 hydrogel over 1000 cycles of loading and unloading, with a focus on compressive strength stability.
summary: This fatigue test demonstrates the durability of G10P10 hydrogel over 1000 cycles. The compressive strength remains stable during the initial 100 cycles under a 1.8 N load, indicating that the material maintains its mechanical integrity under repeated stress, which is vital for its performance in physiological environments.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the SCC specimen longitudinal cross-section, illustrating the grain orientations along the path of corrosion hole propagation.
summary: This EBSD IPF map illustrates the propagation path of a corrosion hole into the specimen interior. The corrosion progresses through a <305> oriented grain followed by a <102> oriented grain. The martensite plates near the pitting hole are observed to be restricted, not extending through the entire grain volume.

caption: TOF-SIMS depth profile of an as-grown Cu-Ni alloy film with 750 nm Cu and 50 nm Ni, showing the elemental distribution of Cu-, Ni-, and C- counts.
summary: The TOF-SIMS depth profile for the 750 nm Cu/50 nm Ni alloy film displays the distribution of Cu, Ni, and C species. Carbon diffusion is evident within the alloy, and the Ni- concentration is further reduced, confirming the trend where Ni- concentration decreases as the copper thickness increases in the alloy.

caption: Common neighbor analysis of sample E7 after the first track completion.
summary: Common neighbor analysis of sample E7 after the first track completion reveals the initial crystal structure. This visualization provides a baseline for comparing structural evolution across different samples and processing stages, highlighting the atomic arrangement and phase distribution present at the end of the first track.

caption: Graphical comparison of measured tensile yield strength against calculated strengthening contributions from individual microstructural features.
summary: This bar chart provides a visual representation of the data presented in Table 4, comparing measured yield strengths from tensile tests with calculated strengthening components. It illustrates the relative contributions of various microstructural features to the overall yield strength, facilitating a direct assessment of the strengthening mechanisms within the material.

caption: Surface morphologies of the second dual-faced structured fabric observed after compression experiments.
summary: Surface morphologies of the second dual-faced structured fabric are presented following the completion of compression experiments. The images allow for the examination of the fabric's surface state and structural response, providing insight into the durability and potential failure modes of the material after undergoing significant compressive loading cycles.

caption: HAADF-TEM image and STEM-EDS elemental mapping of a Zr-rich region located at the grain boundary triple junction in a wire-arc DED-processed Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy.
summary: This HAADF-TEM image and STEM-EDS map reveal the microstructure of a wire-arc DED-processed Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy. The analysis focuses on irregularly shaped second-phase particles at grain boundary triple junctions, which are primarily enriched in Zr with minor Gd and Y content, confirming the partial dissolution of Zr particles during processing.

caption: Cathodic scans of cyclic voltammograms for the 3D-printed PPY:50 electrode in 0.05 M Na2SO4 (pH 5) solution, illustrating the impact of different activation times at –5.0 mA cm⁻² on the cathodic current response.
summary: The panel presents cathodic scans of cyclic voltammograms for the PPY:50 electrode in a 0.05 M Na2SO4 solution. These scans demonstrate how varying activation times at –5.0 mA cm⁻² influence the electrochemical characteristics of the PPY:50 material, helping to identify the optimal activation conditions for improved electrode performance.

caption: Isopleth phase diagram for the Fe(65-x)Co35(CrV)x alloy system (x = 0–20 at.%) showing phase stability as a function of temperature, with a dashed line indicating the Fe60Co35Cr2.5V2.5 composition.
summary: This isopleth phase diagram illustrates the temperature-dependent phase stability of the Fe(65-x)Co35(CrV)x system. It highlights the upward shift in the disorder-to-order transformation temperature from approximately 475 °C to 665 °C as Cr and V content decreases, demonstrating the suppression of σ phase formation when Cr+V levels drop below 5 at.%.

caption: Density values for Ni60 powder and 38CrMoAl steel substrate calculated through JmatPro software.
summary: Density values for the Ni60 powder and 38CrMoAl steel substrate are displayed, having been calculated using JmatPro software. These material properties are essential for the simulation of the deposition process and were sourced from relevant literature to provide accurate physical parameters for the computational model.

caption: 3D optical profilometry image showing the wear track topography of the Ti-6Al-4V ELI alloy subjected to anodic potentiostatic polarization at 0.6 V vs. Ag|AgCl.
summary: This 3D optical profilometry measurement illustrates the wear track topography for the Ti-6Al-4V ELI alloy. The surface profile was evaluated under anodic potentiostatic polarization conditions at 0.6 V vs. Ag|AgCl to assess the wear depth and volume loss, facilitating a direct comparison with the Ti-42Nb alloy performance.

caption: Geometric model of the Gyroid cell wall structure integrated into the K-G composite unit.
summary: The geometric model shows the Gyroid cell, which serves as the second structural component of the K-G composite cell. By integrating this Gyroid structure with the Kagome truss via a Boolean union, the design achieves a complex, interpenetrating lattice that defines the overall geometry of the composite material.

caption: Bar chart representing the half relative effects of normalized coefficients in the quadratic model, where a_i/a_0 denotes the ratio of the i-th coefficient to the constant term, highlighting the significant interplay between laser power and scanning speed.
summary: This diagram displays the half relative effects of normalized coefficients for the quadratic model. The large value of the normalized coefficient for the interplay term indicates a strong interaction between laser power and scanning speed, which significantly influences the fluid flow behavior observed within the melt pool during processing.

caption: Vickers hardness values measured across samples subjected to various cavitation processes.
summary: This figure presents surface hardness data obtained using a micro Vickers hardness tester to evaluate the mechanical response of materials following different cavitation treatments. The results provide a quantitative assessment of how these specific cavitation processes influence the surface hardness characteristics of the tested samples, as determined through standardized indentation testing.

caption: NanoSIMS 16O2H/16O ratio map representing the oxide layer distribution, summed from 30 planes within the selected region.
summary: This NanoSIMS 16O2H/16O ratio map provides a spatial representation of the oxide layer composition. The map is generated by summing data from 30 planes, effectively capturing the distribution of oxygen-related species within the selected region to correlate with the crack tip and grain boundary features observed in SEM.

caption: Master curve of the tanδ for the E-SSG composite, derived from time-temperature superposition to represent the material's viscoelastic damping response over an extended frequency range.
summary: This master curve represents the tanδ of the E-SSG composite, obtained through time-temperature superposition. It provides a comprehensive view of the material's damping characteristics across a wide frequency range, complementing the storage modulus data to fully characterize the viscoelastic performance of the E-SSG composite.

caption: Experimental setup for X-ray fluorescence computed tomography, featuring two energy-resolving Silicon Drift Detectors used to capture raw fluorescence spectra from the extracted sample.
summary: The X-ray fluorescence computed tomography setup is shown, utilizing two energy-resolving X-ray detectors based on multi-element Silicon Drift Detector technology. This configuration allows for the collection of raw X-ray fluorescence spectra, which are summed over the different detector elements to analyze the elemental composition of the extracted cylindrical sample.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the grain boundary zone (GBZ) revealing intersecting acicular precipitates.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph focuses on the grain boundary zone, specifically highlighting the presence of intersecting acicular precipitates. The image confirms that these T1-phases preferentially nucleate and grow at grain boundaries, particularly in areas characterized by high-density dislocations, providing insight into the precipitation mechanism in the HT sample.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of GG and GG-sialoglycan conjugates, highlighting proton environments and structural shifts.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra of GG and GG-sialoglycan conjugates are shown to elucidate the molecular structure. By comparing the proton signals of the base GG polymer with the conjugate, this analysis confirms the successful incorporation of sialoglycan and provides insights into the chemical environment of the modified polymer chains.

caption: SHAP summary diagram illustrating the influence of various printed variables on the green part output.
summary: This SHAP summary diagram visualizes the influence of different printed variables on the green part output. Based on the model's training outcomes, the plot provides a comprehensive overview of how specific input parameters contribute to the final results, serving as a key diagnostic tool for understanding the model's predictive behavior.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for post-processed Ni-Fe-Mo alloy samples at the [111] orientation, reflecting the magnetic performance after post-fabrication processing.
summary: Post-processing treatments, including heat treatment and HIP, exert a pronounced effect on the magnetic behavior of LPBF Ni-Fe-Mo alloy samples. The hysteresis loops at the [111] orientation quantify these changes, illustrating the shift in magnetic properties for the samples fabricated at a volumetric energy density of 4.68 J mm-3.

caption: 3D APT reconstruction cube (30 nm side length) displaying 16% Cr and 9% Al isoconcentration surfaces, highlighting the morphology of phase separation.
summary: A 30 nm cube of the APT reconstruction illustrates the phase separation through 16% Cr and 9% Al isoconcentration surfaces. These surfaces support the conclusion that the material undergoes spinodal decomposition rather than classic precipitation, confirming the formation of γ' phases during the 850 °C heat treatment.

caption: Activation volume measurements derived from nanoindentation creep tests at 300 mN, compared across different heat treatments and investigated planes.
summary: This panel presents the activation volume for nanoindentation creep tests performed at a constant load of 300 mN. The results are differentiated by the investigated plane and the heat treatment history of the PBF-fabricated Ti–6Al–4V ELI alloy, providing insight into the deformation kinetics under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profile obtained from area #2, confirming the elemental enrichment within the nanoprecipitates.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy of area #2 provides further confirmation of the chemical makeup of the nanoprecipitates. Consistent with area #1, the spectrum reveals that C, O, and Fe atoms are enriched in these nanoprecipitates, supporting the conclusion that these elements are key components of the grain boundary features.

caption: Pole figure representation of the texture orientation for the LPBF workpiece, exhibiting the lowest observed intensity among the analyzed samples.
summary: The pole figure for the LPBF workpiece displays the texture orientation of the material. Analysis indicates that this sample exhibits the lowest intensity of texture within its microstructure compared to the other processed samples, providing a baseline for evaluating the effects of subsequent swaging treatments on the material's crystallographic orientation.

caption: Local viability assessment of HUVECs via live/dead staining, comparing 2D (SC) and 3D (SC-Gel) culture conditions with a 200 μm scale bar and statistical significance markers (P < 0.05, P < 0.01).
summary: High-magnification live/dead staining images reveal the local viability of HUVECs in 2D and 3D culture conditions. The results demonstrate significant differences in cell survival between the SC and SC-Gel groups, supported by statistical analysis, providing a visual confirmation of the scaffold's impact on cell health.

caption: H&E staining images illustrating cellular infiltration of hBMSCs within Alg and ALG/CN-1% scaffolds after 7 days of culture.
summary: H&E staining images provide visual evidence of hBMSC infiltration into the interior of Alg and ALG/CN-1% scaffolds after 7 days of culture. The staining highlights the distribution and density of cells within the scaffold architecture, confirming the ability of the hydrogel structures to support cellular penetration.

caption: Storage and loss modulus evolution for 4 wt% of 3 in 2-HEA/PEGDA 250 resin, demonstrating the effect of light intensity on curing.
summary: The storage and loss modulus evolution for the 4 wt% additive 3 formulation is depicted across various light intensities. This graph illustrates the rheological changes occurring within the 2-HEA/PEGDA 250 resin, showing how higher additive concentrations and light intensities modulate the gelation behavior of the polymer network.

caption: Charge density distribution contour plot along the z-direction at 898 K.
summary: Representing the charge density distribution at 898 K, this contour plot highlights the progression of electron transport. As temperature increases, the emergence of additional red and blue peaks indicates active electron transport processes occurring between Ni, Al, and O atoms during the ongoing atom diffusion within the material structure.

caption: Calculated subband energy profile of a GaAs/AlAs heterostructure at a high bias voltage of 17.2 V, highlighting the alignment of the GaAs L-valley subband (Q1) with the AlAs X11 and X21 subbands.
summary: This band structure diagram illustrates the electronic configuration of a GaAs/AlAs heterostructure under a 17.2 V bias. Precise calculations reveal that the L-valley subband in GaAs Q1 aligns with the X11 and X21 subbands in AlAs, effectively causing the barrier between the X and L valleys to vanish.

caption: Full view of the experimental testing rig.
summary: This panel displays a comprehensive photograph of the full testing rig used for the experimental procedure. The image provides a clear overview of the equipment configuration, serving as the primary visual reference for the physical setup employed during the testing phase described in the study.

caption: Log-log plot of small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) data for Al-16Ce-1Mg, highlighting three distinct scattering regions and microstructural evolution following heat treatment at 400 °C.
summary: SAXS data presented in a log-log plot reveal three distinct scattering regions, shaded in gray, which correlate to microstructural features. At high scattering vectors Q > 0.2 Å-1, the data show a transition toward a flat background, accompanied by the emergence of initial Bragg peaks associated with the Al11Ce3 phase.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plots for AM TiZrNb-O and cast TiZrNb-O in SBF.
summary: Nyquist plots acquired in SBF reveal that AM TiZrNb-O displays a significantly larger capacitive arc than the cast alloy. This observation indicates higher interfacial impedance and slower charge-transfer kinetics at the metal/solution interface for the AM material, which correlates with the formation of a chemically robust, multi-component oxide layer.

caption: Mean coefficient of friction values for reference materials and MoS2-reinforced MMCs at 25 °C, calculated by averaging data excluding the initial stabilization period.
summary: Mean COF values at 25 °C demonstrate the reinforcing effect of MoS2 particles. Specifically, 1.5 µm MoS2 particles reduced the COF to 0.63 at 1 wt-% and 0.55 at 3 wt-% concentrations, corresponding to 6% and 18% decreases, respectively, compared to the reference value of 0.67.

caption: Elemental distribution line-scan across the 1.4 mm thickness of the S-Ni6.9–419 sample.
summary: S-Ni6.9–419 sample displays a uniform compositional distribution at the macroscopic scale across its 1.4 mm buildup thickness. The line-scanning data does not appear as a straight line due to the inherent segregation of Ni and Cr elements into the austenite and ferrite phases.

caption: Temperature distribution visualized as a contour map on a central plane cut at a dimensionless time of t = 1.
summary: This figure displays the temperature contour on a central plane cut at a dimensionless time of t = 1. The visualization provides a spatial representation of thermal gradients within the system at this specific temporal snapshot, illustrating the temperature distribution across the defined cross-section of the simulated domain.

caption: {0001} pole figure of the as-cast Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy, showing a maximum MUD value of 2.82.
summary: The {0001} pole figure for the as-cast Mg-Gd-Y-Zr alloy displays a maximum multiple of uniform distribution (MUD) value of 2.82. This result, combined with other pole figures, indicates that there is no apparent solidification texture present in the material, confirming a random distribution of grain orientations.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph obtained using reflection 2, showing the distribution of bright clusters and dark fringes in the Ni-Mn-Ga sample.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging using reflection 2 reveals distinct bright clusters and dark fringes within the Ni-Mn-Ga sample. These features are directly associated with the extra peaks and scattering observed in the diffraction patterns, providing insight into the microstructural characteristics of the as-built material.

caption: Averaged E modulus plotted as a function of indentation depth for both unirradiated and irradiated Al-doped Ti3SiC2 samples.
summary: This graph illustrates the averaged E modulus as a function of indentation depth for Al-doped Ti3SiC2. It provides a comparative analysis of the elastic properties between unirradiated and irradiated specimens across varying depths, serving as a key metric for evaluating the mechanical response of the material under indentation testing.

caption: Nyquist plots showing the electrochemical impedance response of TZ5 and TZ30 samples after 0, 14, and 28 days of immersion in Hanks' solution, with symbols representing experimental data and solid lines indicating fitted results.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance behavior of TZ5 and TZ30 samples across 28 days of immersion in Hanks' solution. The data, represented by experimental symbols and fitted solid lines, characterize the surface degradation and electrochemical stability of the materials throughout the specified immersion periods in the simulated physiological environment.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph of the BAA microstructure, highlighting the distinct morphologies of primary alpha (αp), secondary alpha (αs), and grain boundary alpha (GBα) phases, with precipitation-free zones (PFZs) marked by arrows.
summary: This backscattered electron micrograph reveals the complex BAA microstructure, characterized by primary alpha, secondary alpha, and grain boundary alpha phases. The β matrix appears in white, while the α phase is depicted in black. Arrows identify precipitation-free zones located around the primary alpha and grain boundary alpha regions.

caption: Three-dimensional response surface illustrating the interaction between printing temperature and layer height on the average rate of curvature change, with fixed passive layer thickness ratio and printing speed.
summary: This three-dimensional response surface demonstrates how printing temperature and layer height influence the average curvature change rate. The surface warps toward lower values for both parameters, indicating that the highest average rate of curvature change occurs specifically at the lowest printing temperature and the lowest print layer height.

caption: Magnified view of dislocation pile-ups localized at the γ'/γ interface after creep testing.
summary: A magnified TEM view highlights the accumulation of dislocations at the interface between the γ' precipitates and the γ matrix. These dislocation pile-ups are a primary feature of the creep-deformed microstructure, indicating that the interface acts as a significant barrier to dislocation motion during high-temperature exposure.

caption: Analysis of the stress relaxation ratio versus ultimate tensile strength for PEEK specimens across different infill patterns.
summary: This panel explores the balance between mechanical performance and long-term stress retention by plotting the stress relaxation ratio against UTS. The analysis focuses on the synergy between strength and stress retention, providing insights into how different infill patterns affect the mechanical stability of PEEK specimens over time.

caption: Mean absolute SHAP values for input features predicting the C D measure in kW m-2.
summary: This bar plot illustrates the mean absolute SHAP values for various input features, quantifying their average contribution toward predicting the C D measure. By representing the magnitude of each feature's influence, the visualization provides a clear overview of which parameters are most significant in the model's predictive performance for this specific target.

caption: Geometric layout of the Tóth unit cell.
summary: Depicting the Tóth unit cell, this panel highlights the parameters required for structural assessment. The cut-and-patch method is employed to calculate the volumes of the inner and outer units, allowing for a precise determination of the Tóth cell's geometric properties and internal volume distribution.

caption: Magnetic B(H) hysteresis loops for Alnico LNGT40, illustrating the preferred (EA) direction with a recoil line and knee point, alongside the transverse (HA) direction showing the virgin magnetization curve and knee point.
summary: This figure displays the magnetic B(H) hysteresis loops for an Alnico 8 LNGT40 sample. It highlights the preferred (EA) direction, featuring a representative recoil line and knee point, and the transverse (HA) direction, which includes the virgin magnetization curve and its corresponding knee point, based on experimental measurement results.

caption: Magnetic entropy change ΔSM as a function of temperature for as-solidified Ni0.895Cr0.105MnGe1.05 ribbons, with an inset showing the field dependence of refrigerant capacities RC-1, RC-2, and RC-3.
summary: This plot displays the temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change for as-solidified Ni0.895Cr0.105MnGe1.05 ribbons, highlighting the direct magnetocaloric effect near the structural-order transition. The inset illustrates how refrigerant capacities RC-1, RC-2, and RC-3 vary with the applied magnetic field change, providing insight into the material's potential for magnetic refrigeration applications.

caption: Real component of the Fourier transform of k2-weighted χ(k) spectra at Ni and Co K-edges for all samples.
summary: The real component of the Fourier transform of k2-weighted χ(k) spectra is displayed for Ni and Co K-edges. These data provide the best fit for the Ni1Co3@NC sample, offering detailed insights into the local atomic structure and coordination environment of the metallic components within the material.

caption: STEM-HAADF image of the FeCrTi alloy showing the microstructure in Z-contrast mode.
summary: This STEM-HAADF image displays the microstructure of the FeCrTi alloy in Z-contrast mode. The image provides a high-resolution view of the alloy's internal structure, serving as the base for identifying specific nanometric regions of interest that are further analyzed through elemental mapping in subsequent panels.

caption: Ballistic limit curves for configurations A through F, illustrating the comparative performance of each specimen design.
summary: This plot displays the ballistic limit curves for six distinct configurations, labeled A through F. By presenting these curves together, the figure facilitates a direct comparison of the ballistic performance across all tested specimen designs, with dashed line colors providing a consistent visual reference to the individual configuration data.

caption: Optimized aiMP phase diagram (black line) for the Ca-Li system compared against the curated SGTE reference phase diagram (red line).
summary: This panel presents the optimized aiMP phase diagram for the Ca-Li system, shown in black, plotted alongside the curated SGTE phase diagram in red. This comparison highlights the accuracy of the optimized model in capturing the phase equilibrium characteristics of the Ca-Li system as described in the study.

caption: Plane-polarized light (PPL) photomicrograph of sample CF04 showing the sharp reaction front between the PS vein and the host metadunite.
summary: This PPL photomicrograph of sample CF04 illustrates a sharp reaction front separating the PS vein from the host metadunite. The host material consists of fresh forsterite and relict antigorite domains, while the reaction zone is characterized by the alteration of olivine into lizardite and fine-grained magnetite.

caption: Top-view optical images of single-track deposits produced at 300 W and 400 W laser powers, with a red dashed box highlighting regions of transverse cracking or irregular track morphology.
summary: This panel displays top-view photographs of single-track deposits fabricated using laser powers of 300 W and 400 W. The visual data identifies specific process regimes where the deposited tracks exhibit structural defects, specifically transverse cracking or irregular track shapes, providing a qualitative assessment of the initial deposition experiments.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay curve and corresponding exponential fit for TPU/0.5S composite at room temperature, measured at an emission wavelength of 490 nm.
summary: The fluorescence lifetime decay curve for the TPU/0.5S composite is presented at room temperature with an emission wavelength of 490 nm. Experimental data and fitting curves indicate that for SAOED additions below 2 wt%, the average lifespan of the composite typically ranges between 3 and 5 ns.

caption: Comparison of predicted strain rates from the viscoelastic viscoplastic model against experimental creep data for RR1000 at 750 °C.
summary: This plot evaluates the accuracy of the viscoelastic viscoplastic model by comparing predicted strain rates with experimental creep data for RR1000 at 750 °C. Such comparisons serve to verify model parameters and calibrate flow rule terms, providing a robust validation of the constitutive model under specific high-temperature creep conditions.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the deformed alpha-phase in the EM-L sample.
summary: This high-resolution TEM image focuses on the deformed alpha-phase of the low-oxygen sample. It provides a detailed view of the lattice-level deformation and dislocation interactions that occur within the alpha grains, supporting the observation of improved plastic flow and toughness in the low-oxygen equiaxed microstructure.

caption: Qualitative process characteristic heatmap illustrating the influence of process parameters on the mass flow ratio (MR) at a feed rate of 0.5 mm s-1, with a grey box highlighting the feasible window for stable, damage-free extrusion.
summary: This heatmap provides a qualitative summary of the interdependencies between process parameters and the mass flow ratio during extrusion at a feed rate of 0.5 mm s-1. The grey region defines the stable, damage-free process window, while arrows indicate how increasing the feed rate shifts the characteristic behavior without altering the window.

caption: Polarization-electric field hysteresis loops for PTO and STO thin-film nanocomposites with varying volume fractions from 0.1 to 0.5 under a maximum electric field of 0.3 MV/cm.
summary: This panel displays polarization-electric field hysteresis loops for PTO/STO nanocomposites with volume fractions ranging from 0.1 to 0.5. The measurements are conducted under a maximum electric field of 0.3 MV/cm. These loops characterize the ferroelectric behavior and polarization switching characteristics of the nanocomposites as a function of their PTO content.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectra of 1a (2.98 × 10⁻⁵ M) in acetonitrile solution, demonstrating progressive quenching upon the incremental addition of EDB quencher under 400 nm excitation.
summary: Fluorescence quenching experiments were performed on 1a in acetonitrile to investigate interactions with the additive EDB. The spectra show a clear reduction in fluorescence intensity as the concentration of EDB increases, confirming the quenching effect of the additive on the BODIPY dye 1a under 400 nm excitation.

caption: Synchrotron XRD pattern of aged DAFA26 alloy.
summary: This panel displays the synchrotron XRD results for the aged DAFA26 alloy. The diffraction pattern provides structural information regarding the phases present in the material after the aging process, serving as a primary characterization tool for identifying the crystalline constituents within the sample.

caption: Aluminum elemental distribution map highlighting the spatial arrangement of Al in the alloy.
summary: Aluminum elemental distribution map highlighting the spatial arrangement of Al in the alloy. This visualization is utilized to monitor the distribution of main alloy elements, providing critical data on the aluminum phase's presence and uniformity within the selected region as part of the comprehensive elemental characterization of the material.

caption: Atomic configuration of the A4 supercell model, featuring a fully random atomic distribution simulated via the special quasi-random structure (SQS) method.
summary: Model A4 represents a fully random atomic configuration within the 2x2x2 supercell framework. By employing the special quasi-random structure (SQS) technique, this model simulates complete disorder, providing a critical baseline for evaluating how maximum entropy and atomic randomness impact the formation energy of the S2 material system.

caption: Fatigue strength of recycled PPMF/GF AM specimens at a load ratio of R = 0.05, illustrating the stress amplitude response compared to the reference fatigue curve of recycled IM specimens.
summary: Presented here are the fatigue test results for recycled AM specimens at a load ratio of R = 0.05. The graph illustrates the stress amplitude response and compares these findings to the relevant fatigue curves of recycled IM specimens, demonstrating consistent alignment despite differences in manufacturing processes and relative densities.

caption: Spatially resolved martensite start temperature (Ms) map estimated using combinatorial composition analysis (CCA) across the build bins.
summary: This panel displays the spatially resolved martensite start temperature (Ms) across the build, estimated using combinatorial composition analysis (CCA). Automated processing of the bins reveals the distribution of Ms values, indicating that the bottom of the build undergoes martensitic transformation early during the deposition process.

caption: Piezoresistive response of the 5CNT/RE composite adhesive, plotted as relative resistance variation against repeated bending cycles for maximum displacements of 1, 3, and 5 mm.
summary: The piezoresistive response of the 5CNT/RE composite is shown for maximum bending displacements of 1, 3, and 5 mm. The data demonstrates that after the initial cycle, the relative resistance variation exhibits a stable and repeatable behavior, confirming the material's potential as a reliable self-sensing adhesive in cantilever structures.

caption: Normalized transmittance spectra for the 550/145 mask configuration, comparing a double fiber pass at an 8-degree angle against a single fiber pass at a 15.2-degree angle.
summary: This plot displays the experimentally measured normalized transmittances for the 550/145 mask. It contrasts two distinct optical configurations: a double fiber pass at an 8-degree angle and a single fiber pass at a 15.2-degree angle, illustrating how varying the fiber pass count and incident angle affects the transmission characteristics.

caption: Systematic flowchart illustrating the proposed methodology for parameter determination and subsequent validation through bending experiments.
summary: This flowchart outlines the proposed methodological framework for determining material parameters. The process integrates a systematic approach to parameter estimation, which is subsequently validated through supplementary bending experiments. These experiments encompass diverse geometries to ensure the robustness and accuracy of the derived parameters across various structural configurations and loading conditions.

caption: Implanted range profiles for AISI-348 steel and FeCrMnNi CSA calculated using SRIM-2013 for 6 keV He and 134 keV Xe ion irradiation.
summary: SRIM-2013 Monte Carlo simulations determine the implanted range profiles for AISI-348 steel and FeCrMnNi CSA alloys. The calculations evaluate the depth distribution resulting from 6 keV He and 134 keV Xe ion irradiation, providing essential data for understanding the ion penetration depth within these specific metallic materials under experimental conditions.

caption: Particle motion trajectories within the granulation chamber, determined by solving equations of motion using finite difference methods.
summary: Particle trajectories within the granulation chamber are modeled using finite difference methods to solve the governing equations of motion. This simulation illustrates the falling regularity of the particles, providing insight into how individual particles move and interact with the flow field during the spheroidization process in the chamber.

caption: Aluminum concentration profile measured by EPMA as a function of depth beneath the surface of an LPBF-processed specimen.
summary: This line graph illustrates the aluminum concentration profile beneath the surface of an LPBF-processed specimen, as determined by EPMA analysis. The data reveals a distinct depletion of aluminum near the surface region, confirming the compositional changes induced by the laser powder bed fusion manufacturing process in the analyzed sample.

caption: Terminal voltage evolution of CO2-PCECs featuring SFM-Ni0.175 negative electrodes, recorded over time under a constant current density of 50 mA/cm2 at operating temperatures of 400 °C and 500 °C.
summary: This panel displays the stability of CO2-PCECs with SFM-Ni0.175 negative electrodes by tracking terminal voltage over time. The measurements were conducted at 400 °C and 500 °C under a constant current density of 50 mA/cm2, providing a direct assessment of the electrochemical performance and stability of the device under these specific conditions.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ single-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 1000°C thermal treatment, indicating persistent defect-related emission characteristics.
summary: Cathodoluminescence spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures after the 1000°C thermal cycle show that defect-related emissions persist with a profile similar to previous cycles. The comparison of Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ dopants at 2.5 mol% and 0.35 mol% concentrations confirms the stability of these luminescence features across the three thermal treatment cycles.

caption: Comparative trajectories of the cutting edge during conventional machining (CM) and ultrasonic assisted machining (UAM).
