caption: Dark-field TEM image generated using the (110) γ'' superlattice reflection, as highlighted by the yellow circle in the inset SAD pattern, confirming the precipitate phase.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging, performed using the (110) γ'' superlattice reflection identified in the inset SAD pattern, confirms that the continuous Ni, Nb, and Ti-rich phase observed along the sub-grain boundary is indeed a γ'' precipitate. This diffraction-based contrast confirms the phase identity within the cellular substructure.

caption: Final HAADF-STEM image (70th frame) of the specimen series acquired at a low electron dose of 3·10^2 e/Å^2.
summary: The 70th frame of the low-dose series confirms that no evident damage occurs despite a relatively large accumulated dose of 2·10^4 e/Å^2. This demonstrates the stability of the specimen under these specific imaging conditions, contrasting with the structural degradation observed at higher electron dose rates.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram derived from the EBSD analysis of the as-printed sample, quantifying the frequency of various grain sizes present in the microstructure.
summary: The grain size distribution histogram provides a quantitative representation of the microstructural features observed in the as-printed sample. By plotting the frequency of grain sizes, this panel complements the EBSD morphology map, offering a statistical overview of the grain refinement achieved during the printing process.

caption: Optimized unit cell model generated by the ant colony-large variation genetic fusion algorithm.
summary: The unit cell model shown in panel (a) is derived using an ant colony-large variation genetic fusion algorithm. This computational design serves as the foundational geometry for the subsequent fabrication of the multilayer honeycomb metastructure, ensuring the structural parameters are optimized for the intended application before physical production begins.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from Berkovich nanoindentation performed at the center of the TiNiCu deposit, illustrating the mechanical response under varying laser power conditions using an indenter with a 100 nm edge radius.
summary: Berkovich nanoindentation tests were conducted on the TiNiCu ternary SMA deposit to evaluate mechanical behavior. The load versus depth curves demonstrate the material's response across different laser power settings. Using an indenter with a 100 nm edge radius, these measurements provide insight into the local mechanical properties of the laser-processed material.

caption: 2D Debbye-Scherrer diffraction pattern of the AP-DED Ni-based superalloy 718, showing discontinuous rings with intense spotty features indicative of a coarse, highly oriented microstructure.
summary: The 2D Debbye-Scherrer diffraction pattern exhibits discontinuous rings and intense spotty features, which are characteristic of the coarse and highly oriented microstructure of the AP-DED Ni-based superalloy 718. These features correlate with the intense (200) diffraction peak of the γ-matrix, confirming the highly textured grain structure developed during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Flank wear morphology of UAT under wet cutting conditions.
summary: Flank wear morphology of the UAT tool under wet cutting conditions is illustrated. While the CT shows severe BUE, adhesion, and abrasion, these wear features appear significantly milder in the UAT, suggesting improved tool performance under wet conditions compared to the CT process.

caption: Comparison of tensile strength and elongation at break for Ti64, Ti64/Ti55511, and Ti55511 specimens, derived from three parallel tensile tests (Groups 1-3) per material.
summary: Tensile strength and elongation at break are quantified across three parallel test groups for each material type. The dual-titanium structure significantly improves elongation compared to the individual components, as the interface reconciles the mechanical contradictions between the ductile Ti64 phase and the high-strength Ti55511 reinforcing phase during tensile loading.

caption: Histogram showing the fractional occurrence of kink lengths in atomic units, derived from ten high-resolution images, with a black dashed line representing an exponential approximation.
summary: This histogram quantifies the distribution of kink lengths measured in atomic units across ten high-resolution images ranging from 50 nm to 200 nm in size. The data reveals the frequency of different kink lengths, with a black dashed line providing an exponential approximation to describe the observed statistical trend.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of grain boundary precipitates (GBPs) in the wrought specimen after peak aging treatment.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the nanostructure near grain boundaries in the wrought specimen following peak aging. The micrograph highlights the presence of rod-shaped precipitates along the grain boundaries, accompanied by a precipitate-free zone (PFZ), consistent with APT results showing comparable average sizes to the WAAM counterpart.

caption: Comparison of average atomic size mismatch and shear modulus mismatch for V33Nb33Mo34 and V25Nb25Mo25X25 bcc RMPEAs, represented by open and solid triangles respectively.
summary: This scatter plot compares the average atomic size mismatch and shear modulus mismatch for the V33Nb33Mo34 reference alloy and the V25Nb25Mo25X25 alloy series. The visualization distinguishes between the base alloy and the modified compositions, facilitating an analysis of how structural and elastic mismatches correlate with the observed mechanical properties of these refractory alloys.

caption: Comparative visualization of feature selection results across four distinct algorithms, illustrating both the unique differentiation in selection processes and the underlying similarities in feature preferences.
summary: This plot provides an intuitive comparative view of feature selection results generated by four different algorithms. It highlights how these algorithms differentiate during the selection process while simultaneously revealing commonalities in their feature preferences, offering a comprehensive overview of the model-specific selection behaviors within the study's analytical framework.

caption: Tan delta curves of PLA/hemp hurd composites showing the evolution of the damping peak as a function of the number of recycling steps.
summary: As seen in this panel, the tan delta peak increased as the number of recycling steps increased. This trend indicates changes in the viscoelastic damping properties of the PLA/hemp hurd composites, reflecting the impact of repeated processing cycles on the internal energy dissipation characteristics of the composite material.

caption: Thinnest network edges with cross-section height of 0.1 mm, showing a random spatial distribution throughout the specimen.
summary: Comprising the thinnest edges of the network, these elements feature a cross-section height of 0.1 mm. Unlike the more structured, thicker edge classes, these components are randomly distributed throughout the space, completing the hierarchical partitioning of the specimen's internal network structure.

caption: Comparison between target and EDS-measured elemental compositions for the #4_Bulk sample.
summary: The measured composition of the #4_Bulk sample is presented alongside its target composition to evaluate fabrication accuracy. The data confirms that the EDS-measured values closely match the target specifications, demonstrating excellent scalability and compositional control during the in-situ alloying process for this specific bulk sample.

caption: Transient voltage and current waveforms generated by the synergic deposition system, illustrating the pulse parameters controlled by the proprietary algorithm.
summary: This plot displays the transient voltage and current waveforms produced by the synergic deposition system. These pulse parameters are dictated by a proprietary algorithm from the equipment supplier. The data, extracted from the deposition process, provides a detailed view of the electrical characteristics maintained during the material synthesis procedure.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the 2024Sc alloy demonstrating significant microstructural refinement compared to the base 2024 alloy.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the 2024Sc alloy highlights substantial microstructural alterations induced by the addition of scandium. This modification leads to a refined grain structure, contrasting with the coarse columnar grains observed in the base 2024 alloy, as evidenced by the reduced mean grain size.

caption: Panoramic optical micrograph of the fracture surface for an AM material specimen after fatigue testing, where arrows denote the dominant crack propagation path.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the fracture surface of an additively manufactured (AM) material specimen after undergoing fatigue testing. The panoramic view allows for the observation of the fracture characteristics, while the included arrows indicate the major direction of crack growth, providing insight into the fatigue failure of the AM material.

caption: DCPD evolution plotted against fatigue cycles for SSM and HPDC specimens tested at a stress level of 135 MPa.
summary: DCPD measurement results for SSM and HPDC castings are presented at 135 MPa. Consistent with the higher stress test, SSM specimens demonstrate a longer fatigue life than HPDC specimens at this stress level. The graph illustrates the comparative degradation behavior of the two casting types during cyclic loading.

caption: Elemental distribution partition coefficient map of the NC25 alloy sample following in situ oxidation.
summary: Presented here is the elemental distribution partition coefficient for the NC25 alloy after in situ oxidation. This map highlights the distribution preference of various elements within the γ/γ′ phase, providing evidence of the elemental segregation behavior that occurs in the alloy during the oxidation process.

caption: Schematic representation of failure modes in the boundary effect model (BEM) as a function of nominal strength and equivalent crack length.
summary: This schematic illustrates the boundary effect model, which categorizes fracture failure into three distinct regimes: strength-controlled, quasi-brittle fracture, and fracture toughness-controlled criteria. The diagram maps nominal strength against equivalent crack length, demonstrating how these two fracture parameters, ft' and KIC, dictate the failure behavior of materials within the model.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns of IN718 alloy produced via additive manufacturing (AP-DED) following homogenization and subsequent aging heat treatments.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns characterize the IN718 AP-DED alloy after homogenization and aging heat treatments. These data confirm that the selected homogenization temperatures and soaking times successfully promote the precipitation of a significant volume fraction of hardening phases, specifically the gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime phases within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Ultraviolet band absorption rate profile of the PSN2/TiB2/CCP composite material.
summary: The light absorption characteristics of the PSN2/TiB2/CCP composite film were evaluated in the ultraviolet spectral range. This plot illustrates the material's ability to absorb incident light, which is a critical parameter for its application in laser-induced processes and energy dissipation through the ceramization reaction.

caption: Global Warming Potential (GWP) plotted against structure diameter for FDM-printed ABS formworks with a 0.8 mm wall thickness, including a dashed line representing structure-specific impacts normalized by concrete weight.
summary: This line graph illustrates the sensitivity analysis of total environmental impacts for 3D-printed ABS formworks with circular cross-sections of varying diameters. It displays the GWP relative to structure diameter, while the dashed line provides the structure-specific impacts, calculated as the total impact divided by the concrete weight in kg CO2 eq per kg.

caption: Damping values extracted from TRMOKE data as a function of the applied field, with an inset showing the linear fit of FMR linewidth versus frequency used to determine effective damping.
summary: Damping characteristics of the magnetic samples are presented as a function of the applied field. The inset provides a linear fit of FMR linewidth versus frequency, confirming that the extracted damping values align closely with those obtained from standard FMR measurements, validating the TRMOKE-based damping extraction method.

caption: Correlation of crack length measurements for artifacts printed using dry powder, showing the relationship between two repeated experimental builds.
summary: This scatter plot evaluates the repeatability of crack length measurements for artifacts printed with dry powder. The data points are compared against an ideal y=x agreement line and a linear fit. High R² values demonstrate a strong correlation between the two experimental builds conducted under identical process conditions.

caption: Ternary plot illustrating the influence of IBOA, HDDA, and ETMPTA monomer composition on the viscosity measured at a shear rate of 100 s⁻¹.
summary: This ternary diagram displays the viscosity η of monomer mixtures composed of IBOA, HDDA, and ETMPTA. The plot maps the viscosity values at a constant shear rate of 100 s⁻¹ across the entire compositional space, providing a clear visualization of how varying the monomer ratios affects the fluid flow behavior.

caption: Valence electron density plot of the V-doped TiNi3–V3/C interface along the (110) plane, highlighting strong electron cloud overlap between the first Ni layer and second Ti layer.
summary: The valence electron density plot for the TiNi3–V3/C interface along the (110) plane shows a bonding relationship similar to the clean interface. Notably, the first layer of Ni exhibits strong electron cloud overlap with the second layer of Ti, contributing to the highest work of adhesion for the V element.

caption: Tack test results for the reference mix, showing the evolution of peak tack values over time.
summary: The tack test results for the reference mix illustrate the mechanical behavior of the material. Peak tack values for this reference composition were observed to decrease between 30 and 60 minutes, indicating a reduction in tackiness over this specific time interval during the testing process.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of nickel-molybdenum coated 3D-printed electrodes evaluated in 1 mol KOH solution, illustrating the electrochemical response for varying molybdenum deposition levels.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammogram measurements for nickel-molybdenum coated 3D-printed electrodes. The data, collected in a 1 mol KOH electrolyte solution, characterizes the electrochemical behavior of the electrodes as a function of different molybdenum deposition amounts, providing insight into the surface redox activity of the modified electrode materials.

caption: Atomic model of the MgNi2 compound in the C36 structure.
summary: The C36 crystal structure of MgNi2 is shown, with Magnesium atoms colored yellow and Nickel atoms colored blue. This atomic model is part of the graphical representations of the constituent phases for the La2-xMgxNi7 system, offering insight into the structural configuration of this specific compound.

caption: Modulus versus frequency Bode plots demonstrating the impedance magnitude |Z| at 0.01 Hz for SLM-316L stainless steel across different construction directions.
summary: Modulus-frequency Bode plots show that |Z| 0.01 values follow the order 0° (1.09 × 10^5 Ω cm^2) > 90° (8.97 × 10^4 Ω cm^2) > 45° (7.88 × 10^4 Ω cm^2). These results verify that the surface film on the 0° construction direction specimen possesses superior barrier properties compared to others.

caption: TGA-DSC curves of impregnated Ni(NO3)2·6H2O/SiO2 particles under N2/air flow, showing a continuous 10% weight loss between 50 °C and 260 °C.
summary: This panel displays the thermal behavior of impregnated Ni(NO3)2·6H2O/SiO2 particles in a non-reducing atmosphere. The TGA-DSC data reveals a continuous weight loss of approximately 10% within the 50–260 °C temperature range, which is attributed to the gradual loss of four water molecules from the nickel nitrate precursor.

caption: Magnified view of the piezoresistive -ΔR/Ro versus strain response for the first three cycles of in-plane compressive loading.
summary: Magnified view of the piezoresistive -ΔR/Ro versus strain response for the first three cycles of in-plane compressive loading. This detailed visualization highlights the initial electrical resistance behavior of the MWCNT/PA12 HHS, capturing the specific piezoresistive trends during the early stages of the cyclic compression test.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of NiTi powder, illustrating the thermal transition behavior.
summary: The DSC analysis of NiTi powder reveals the thermal transition characteristics of the material. The results indicate an austenite finish temperature of approximately 16 °C, which confirms the pseudoelastic behavior of the powder at room temperature, demonstrating its suitability for applications requiring shape memory or superelastic properties under ambient conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+ in 0.1 M KCl at 100 mV s-1, comparing 35 wt% CB/TPU electrodes before and after 0.5 M NaOH cleaning against a commercial conductive TPU filament.
summary: Electrochemical testing of 35 wt% CB/TPU electrodes using [Ru(NH3)6]3+ demonstrates the efficacy of the NaOH cleaning process. The bespoke 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode significantly outperforms the commercial conductive TPU filament, which exhibits negligible electrochemical response, confirming the superior performance of the developed additive manufactured material for electrochemical applications.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra monitoring the reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) catalyzed by L-type Pd/C CR over time.
summary: This panel displays the UV-Vis spectra tracking the reduction of 4-NP using an L-type Pd/C catalytic reactor. The spectral data provides a time-resolved view of the reaction progress, which serves as a basis for determining conversion rates through linear fitting of the absorbance changes observed during the catalytic process.

caption: Minimum creep rates for PBF-EB/M processed specimens using SISF-related slip systems, highlighting the anisotropic response observed in experimental and simulated data.
summary: Anisotropic creep behavior is observed in PBF-EB/M manufactured materials when analyzed using SISF-related slip systems. The panel displays experimental solid lines and simulated dashed lines to illustrate this orientation-dependent response. Comparisons across different slip system families confirm that SESF-related mechanisms are the dominant deformation processes governing the creep behavior of these materials.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for scanning strategy S5.
summary: This plot illustrates the major axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for the S5 intermittent melt pool interference mode. Consistent with other intermittent strategies, S5 exhibits larger average primary and secondary martensite sizes compared to continuous modes, reflecting the influence of cooling rates on microstructural growth.

caption: Conceptual integration of bamboo-inspired HRA metamaterials within an automotive crash beam system.
summary: This schematic illustrates the practical application of bamboo-inspired HRA metamaterials in automotive crash beam systems. The design leverages the structural properties of the HRA metamaterial to enhance energy absorption and impact resistance, demonstrating significant potential for improving vehicle safety structures during collision events.

caption: 3D confocal microscopy image of the Nickel wear track surface after tribocorrosion testing at 1 V MSE in citrate buffer.
summary: Nickel wear track surface is displayed in 3D following tribocorrosion testing at 1 V MSE. Confocal microscopy allows for the observation of the worn volume on the metallic surface. This assessment, performed at 1 Hz and 2.74 N load, characterizes the wear behavior of the Nickel sample in citrate buffer.

caption: Y-direction displacement field for a 20%_10% functionally graded specimen at 10% global strain, highlighting localized layer-by-layer failure.
summary: The DIC displacement map for the 20%_10% functionally graded specimen at 10% global strain demonstrates a layer-by-layer failure mode. Lower density regions exhibit higher displacements, indicated by blue coloring, while the remaining specimen area shows displacements of approximately 0.5 mm, represented by the red region.

caption: 3D reconstruction image of the top surface at a 30 μm hatch spacing, highlighting the micro-humping phenomenon with a red dotted line.
summary: The 3D reconstruction image provides a detailed view of the top surface at a 30 μm hatch spacing. It specifically illustrates the micro-humping phenomenon, marked by a red dotted line. This reconstruction confirms the presence of surface irregularities resulting from the intense mass transfer and material stacking during the laser fabrication process.

caption: Body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice structure demonstrating the atomic configuration with an atom at the center of the cube.
summary: The body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice structure is presented, showcasing the characteristic atomic configuration where an atom is positioned at the center of the cubic unit. This structural model provides a clear visualization of the BCC arrangement, which is essential for comparative analysis of different lattice types.

caption: Maximum magnetic flux density (Bmax) plotted against Co substitution percentage for Fe, Ni, and FeNi alloy series, evaluated at three distinct annealing temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the Bmax values for Fe, Ni, and FeNi substitution series derived from BH loop tests at 400 Hz. The data demonstrates that promising magnetic performance is achievable with a 15-minute dwell at temperatures around 400-500 degrees Celsius, with specific compositions showing peak flux density values.

caption: Mean per atom energy convergence trend for 15 at.% Al in Ni, simulated using a DHCP parent lattice structure.
summary: This panel presents the convergence behavior of the mean per atom energy for a 15 at.% Al in Ni alloy system modeled with a DHCP parent lattice. The results demonstrate the relationship between the number of Monte Carlo generated configurations and the stabilization of the calculated mean energy values.

caption: Elemental distribution map across the Cu/V interface, highlighting the spatial arrangement of major elements and identifying trace amounts of Ti and Fe within the V zone (IV).
summary: The elemental distribution map provides a detailed view of the chemical composition across the Cu/V interface. It confirms the spatial arrangement of major elements and reveals the presence of trace amounts of Ti and Fe within the V zone (IV), providing insight into the chemical homogeneity of the weld.

caption: Posterior-anterior radiograph of the INNOTERE 3D scaffold wedge at 2 months post-owHTO, showing the progression of bone integration.
summary: Captured two months after the owHTO procedure, this posterior-anterior radiograph documents the ongoing osteointegration process. It provides a comparative view of the scaffold's interaction with the surrounding bone tissue, tracking the gradual development of the healing interface as the scaffold begins to integrate into the host bone.

caption: Force-displacement response of partially supported sandwich structures subjected to impact loading by 13 mm and 38 mm hemispherical impactors.
summary: This plot illustrates the force-displacement behavior of sandwich structures featuring 3D-printed skins and polyurea foam cores. The curves highlight distinct mechanical characteristics resulting from impact events with 13 mm and 38 mm hemispherical impactors, demonstrating the structure's effective impact mitigation performance under these specific loading conditions.

caption: Experimental workflow diagram illustrating the two distinct sets of procedures employed for the ZrCuAlNb alloy fabrication.
summary: This schematic provides a clear overview of the two sets of experiments conducted during the study. It serves as the foundational framework for the research methodology, outlining the procedural steps taken to investigate the ZrCuAlNb alloy system and establishing the experimental context for the subsequent material characterization and analysis.

caption: Raw IR intensity map (NUC values) of the C103 melt pool captured at 3.6 ms under 170 W laser power and 600 mm/s scanning speed.
summary: This raw IR intensity map displays the melt pool of C103 alloy during laser processing at 170 W and 600 mm/s. The intensity values, measured in NUC, represent the thermal radiation captured by the IR camera sensor within the 3–5.5 μm range, providing a baseline for subsequent temperature conversion analysis.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus experimental stability values (Y1) derived from the RSM-BBD model, showing data points tightly clustered around the diagonal line of perfect prediction.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the RSM-BBD model's accuracy in predicting stability (Y1). The visualization demonstrates a high degree of predictive reliability, as the experimental data points are tightly clustered along the diagonal line, indicating that the model successfully captures the stability metrics with minimal deviation from observed experimental values.

caption: Specific strength versus plastic elongation comparison of L-DED Nb-2TiC at 1000 °C against various Nb solid solution and refractory alloys.
summary: This Ashby-style plot benchmarks the specific strength and plastic elongation of the L-DED Nb-2TiC alloy against other refractory materials. The L-DED Nb-2TiC alloy, highlighted with a red star, demonstrates a superior combination of high specific strength and comparable ductility, outperforming several conventional Nb-based solid solution and refractory alloy counterparts.

caption: {001} and {111} pole figures representing the crystallographic orientation of the large grain identified as domain 2 in the orientation map.
summary: The {001} and {111} pole figures depict the texture of the large grain labeled as domain 2. This analysis confirms the specific crystallographic orientation of this grain within the HCPEB-treated surface, contributing to the overall understanding of the texture evolution and grain characteristics observed across the modified surface domains.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for 316L powder in ALF solution at pH 4.5, comparing virgin and reused samples after 1 hour of OCP stabilization.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for 316L powder in ALF solution at pH 4.5, comparing virgin and reused samples after 1 hour of OCP stabilization. Reused 316L powders exhibit higher electrochemical activity, characterized by lower corrosion potential, higher corrosion current, and higher anodic branch current compared to virgin powders, despite significant measurement variability.

caption: Digital Image Correlation strain field measurement for the second PA12 specimen set (S_PA12_03), showing multiple fracture zones highlighted by red circles.
summary: Digital Image Correlation strain field measurement for the second PA12 specimen set (S_PA12_03), showing multiple fracture zones highlighted by red circles. Comparing this to the first set demonstrates that aged PA12 specimens exhibit a distinct mechanical behavior characterized by the emergence of multiple fracture zones rather than a single propagation path.

caption: Instrumented mock limb and 3D-printed PLA socket integrated with seven force sensors.
summary: This photograph displays a mock limb and a 3D-printed socket fabricated from PLA using wire deposition. The socket design was specifically adapted to accommodate an instrumentation system consisting of seven force sensors, enabling the monitoring of pressure distribution within the prosthetic interface during experimental testing.

caption: Schematic illustration of a well-aligned atomic arrangement where an in-situ magnetic field induces a single dominating easy axis, resulting in uniaxial anisotropy.
summary: This diagram depicts an fcc (111) plane where an in-situ magnetic field during growth aligns Ni-Ni and Fe-Fe pairs. This process forces one orientation to dominate, establishing a clear easy axis and uniaxial magnetic anisotropy. The model assumes a characteristic length scale equal to one atomic layer.

caption: Schematic illustration of the height parameters defined for segment stack data evaluation and closed-loop control, including the hypothetical estimated layer height h_layer,est.
summary: This schematic illustrates the height definitions required for calculating control deviations within an individual segment stack. It provides a visual framework for the closed-loop control system, where the estimated layer height h_layer,est serves as a purely hypothetical measure used to facilitate the necessary data evaluation and process control calculations.

caption: t-SNE visualization of the ResNet18 model feature space showing significant overlap between classes B and C, as well as A and D.
summary: The t-SNE plot for the ResNet18 model illustrates the high-dimensional data in a 2D representation. It reveals substantial overlap between classes B and C, and between classes A and D, which indicates poor feature prediction capabilities for this specific model architecture in distinguishing between the different defect classes.

caption: TOF-SIMS depth profile of an as-deposited 500 nm Cu/50 nm Ni thin film, showing discrete elemental layers of copper and nickel as a function of sputtering depth.
summary: This TOF-SIMS depth profile illustrates the elemental distribution in an as-deposited 500 nm Cu/50 nm Ni thin film. The analysis reveals distinct layers, with a higher concentration of copper observed up to 500 nm, followed by a higher concentration of nickel, confirming the discrete nature of the deposited layers.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms comparing pure CXB, individual excipients (UFL2®, IR®, K12®, chitosan), blank formulation (BM1), physical mixture (PM1), and solid dispersion (SD1).
summary: DSC thermograms reveal thermal changes in the SD1 formulation. Comparison of melting peaks shows that CXB in PM1 exhibits behavior similar to pure CXB, whereas the melting peaks of SD1 and the blank formulation BM1 are similar, indicating significant thermal modification within the solid dispersion structure.

caption: Reflection spectra of opal films fabricated via the melt-shear technique, with corresponding film colors indicated by circles.
summary: Reflection spectra of opal films prepared using the melt-shear technique are displayed, with film colors shown alongside. The observed red-shift of the peaks from CSP2.1 to 2.4 is attributed to larger particle sizes, which is consistent with Bragg’s law of diffraction, confirming the structural characteristics of the films.

caption: Element content diagram for the S4 sample longitudinal section.
summary: The element content diagram for the S4 sample's longitudinal section provides quantitative data regarding the chemical composition of the observed particles. By correlating this spectral data with the SEM images, the particles situated at the grain boundaries are definitively identified as Nb-rich carbides (NbC).

caption: Box plots illustrating the distribution of head injury criteria for different SISC layouts compared to the original hood and ISSH.
summary: Box plots visualize the distribution of head injury criteria for the different SISC layouts compared to the original hood and ISSH. The analysis reveals that the PDMH values for SISC-L4-1, SISC-L4-2, SISC-L8, and SISC-L12 are 58.9%, 59.0%, 58.1%, and 54.0%, respectively, reflecting the effectiveness of each specific layout.

caption: Fourier transformed EXAFS spectra at the Fe K-edge for Ni2Fe1 before and after the OER stability test.
summary: Fourier transformed EXAFS spectra at the Fe K-edge demonstrate the local atomic environment of iron in Ni2Fe1. Post-OER stability testing results show increased signal amplitudes for Fe-O and Fe-Fe features, suggesting an increase in coordination numbers for metal-oxygen and metal-metal bonds compared to the freshly prepared sample.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 4 fabricated via standard PCB fabrication.
summary: This panel shows the reflection coefficient of antenna design 4 produced using standard PCB fabrication techniques. Plotted with Origin software, the graph provides the experimental reflection data for the PCB-fabricated antenna, serving as a reference point to evaluate the performance consistency across different manufacturing processes for this design.

caption: Charge density difference map for the HCP1 configuration of the HfC(011)/Ni(001) interface.
summary: The HCP1 configuration of the HfC(011)/Ni(001) interface is shown here via charge density difference mapping. The visualization highlights the formation of both Ni-C covalent bonds and Ni-Hf metal bonds at the interface, demonstrating complex interfacial bonding characteristics between the HfC and Ni components.

caption: Comparison of CSAM MK and traditional cold spray deposition strategies illustrating the gun path and resulting deposit geometry.
summary: This schematic contrasts the CSAM MK strategy with traditional cold spray methods. The MK approach utilizes varying impact velocities to create pyramid-like deposit shapes, whereas the traditional method maintains a perpendicular gun orientation and linear path, resulting in uniform layer growth as described in the referenced literature.

caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 250 °C, illustrating the elemental composition profile.
summary: Presented here is the normalized mass spectrum for Inconel 718 samples tested at 250 °C. The data indicates that other solutes remain present in comparable amounts, though carbon traces were not resolved by atom probe tomography, highlighting the importance of mass spectrum analysis for detecting carbon in these specific samples.

caption: Long-term potential stability of the optimized 3Dp-Na+-ISE sensor, showing the emf response monitored over an 8-hour period for transducers with the ion-selective membrane affixed to the front (red trace) and back (black trace).
summary: The long-term potential stability of the optimized 3Dp-Na+-ISE is evaluated through an 8-hour emf response monitoring test. By comparing the red trace (front-affixed membrane) and black trace (back-affixed membrane), the data demonstrates the sensor's ability to maintain stable potential output over time in a 62.5 mM Na+ solution.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for Tmax, revealing that beam power (P) dictates the maximum melt pool temperature, with higher power inputs (red) correlating to increased peak temperatures.
summary: The SHAP beeswarm plot for Tmax demonstrates that the maximum temperature within the melt pool is primarily dictated by beam power. Higher power inputs, represented by red values, are shown to elevate the predicted peak temperature, confirming a direct relationship between laser power and the thermal state of the melt pool.

caption: Three-dimensional topography map of the ablated feature P2.
summary: This panel displays a three-dimensional topography map of the ablated feature P2. The map illustrates the surface profile and geometric characteristics of the feature following the ablation process. These topographical measurements are essential for comparing the actual shape of the ablated feature against the intended target design.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of IN625 fractured at 980 °C, displaying significant dynamically recrystallized (DRX) grains marked by white arrows.
summary: The IPF map for IN625 tested at 980 °C reveals the grain structure near the fracture region. Dynamically recrystallized (DRX) grains are clearly visible, marked by white arrows, confirming that recrystallization is a dominant feature in the microstructure when the material is deformed at temperatures above 650 °C.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) for CMSX-4 and IN718 superalloys.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature dependence of the coefficients of thermal expansion for CMSX-4 and IN718 alloys. The data points are linearly interpolated between measured values, with the CTE assumed to remain constant above the highest specified temperature, providing a comprehensive overview of the thermal expansion behavior for these materials.

caption: Creep strain versus time curves for STA1080 and STA1150 specimens tested at 650 °C and 690 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the creep strain evolution over time for two microstructural variants, STA1080 and STA1150, under constant conditions of 650 °C and 690 MPa. The data demonstrates that STA1150 exhibits superior creep resistance, characterized by significantly higher rupture life and increased creep ductility compared to the STA1080 specimen.

caption: Immunofluorescent staining of iNOS and CD206 markers in RAW264.7 cells after 7 days of culture, highlighting the shift in macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype in the presence of the scaffolds.
summary: After 7 days of culture under inflammatory activation, RAW264.7 cells treated with PLA/GA and PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF scaffolds show a distinct shift in macrophage polarization. Immunofluorescent staining reveals lower expression of the M1 marker iNOS and higher expression of the M2 marker CD206, indicating an anti-inflammatory effect induced by the scaffold materials.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H IEA irradiated at approximately 342 °C.
summary: This panel displays the Monte Carlo simulation results for the F82H IEA material. The irradiation process was conducted at a target temperature of 300 °C, with SiC thermometry specimens indicating an actual irradiation temperature of approximately 342 °C for this specific specimen condition.

caption: Comparison of simulated and measured reflection coefficient performance for the 3.5 GHz antenna design, highlighting a frequency shift of 0.16 GHz between the two datasets.
summary: This panel presents the reflection coefficient performance for the 3.5 GHz antenna design. By comparing the simulated and measured data, a frequency shift of 0.16 GHz is observed. This plot illustrates the discrepancy between the theoretical Ansys HFSS simulation and the actual performance of the fabricated antenna structure.

caption: Interfacial shear strength (IFSS) and interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) values for T700/M-Epoxy composites measured at room temperature and -196 °C.
summary: Comparison of interfacial shear strength and interlaminar shear strength for T700/M-Epoxy composites at room temperature and -196 °C shows significant cryogenic enhancement. The data reveals that the IFSS and ILSS values increase by 16.08% and 6.57%, respectively, when the testing temperature is reduced to -196 °C.

caption: STEM micrograph of the as-built AlSi10Mg alloy sample following tensile deformation, highlighting significant dislocation accumulation around the cell walls.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the deformed microstructure of the as-built AlSi10Mg alloy. It reveals a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) that have accumulated around the cell walls, which contributes to strong back stress and kinematic hardening during the tensile deformation process.

caption: XGBoost gain-based feature importance ranking for yield strength prediction.
summary: This panel displays the feature importance analysis for yield strength using the XGBoost algorithm. The importance is quantified using the gain metric, where higher values signify a greater contribution of a specific feature to the model's predictive accuracy for yield strength, providing insight into the most influential variables.

caption: S-N curve for 3D-printed PLA tested in air, showing a fatigue limit of 9.4 MPa.
summary: This S-N curve illustrates the fatigue behavior of 3D-printed PLA in its unexposed, pre-corrosion condition. Tested in air, the specimen exhibits a fatigue limit of 9.4 MPa. This baseline measurement serves as the reference point for evaluating the subsequent degradation of mechanical resistance caused by immersion in simulated body fluid.

caption: Stability curve of the monolithic perovskite/Si/Ni foil/NiFe photoanode integrated with Ni NWs cathode during unassisted overall water splitting.
summary: Demonstrating long-term durability, the overall water splitting system maintains a current density of 12.3 mA cm-2 at 0 V for approximately 45 hours. This stability test was conducted under both continuous and chopped illumination in 1.0 M KOH, highlighting the robust performance of the integrated photoanode and cathode configuration.

caption: Three extracted eigenvectors representing the principal components of the grain geometry.
summary: Three eigenvectors, derived from the grain data pool, are exhibited to characterize the grain's spatial orientation. These vectors serve as the foundation for the Principal Component Analysis, enabling the systematic extraction of the grain's primary dimensions from the irregular shape observed in the simulation domain.

caption: Bode magnitude and phase plots for LPBF 316L stainless steel, showing frequency-dependent electrochemical behavior measured at open-circuit potential and under anodic polarization of OCP + 300 mV.
summary: Bode magnitude and phase plots detail the electrochemical behavior of LPBF 316L stainless steel across a range of frequencies. Measurements taken at open-circuit potential and under anodic polarization conditions reveal how laser power and alumina modification influence the electrochemical stability and surface impedance characteristics of the fabricated stainless steel samples.

caption: FTIR spectra of ABOHA@ZnO components, highlighting characteristic peaks at 1736 cm-1 and 1640 cm-1 for ester bonds and methacrylate groups, alongside peaks at 1200 cm-1, 1060 cm-1, and 790 cm-1 confirming successful boric acid introduction.
summary: The FTIR spectra confirm the chemical structure of the ABOHA@ZnO hydrogel. Key peaks at 1736 cm-1 and 1640 cm-1 indicate successful conjugation of methacrylate groups, while peaks at 1200 cm-1, 1060 cm-1, and 790 cm-1 verify the successful incorporation of boric acid into the hydrogel matrix.

caption: Volume fraction distribution for the finest mesh configuration with a voxel size of 0.5 mm.
summary: Depicting the finest mesh configuration with 0.5 mm voxels, this panel shows volume fraction values consistently close to 1 across the geometry. These findings confirm that the finer mesh provides a highly precise mesh-to-part fit, effectively minimizing the propensity for mesh-related errors as defined by the volume fraction parameter.

caption: Profilometer visualization of the scratch track for nickel aluminide alloy treated at 30 W and a reduced scanning speed of 1000 mm/s.
summary: Presented here are the 3D and cross-sectional profilometer images of a scratch track on laser-treated nickel aluminide alloy. The material was processed using a laser power of 30 W and a reduced scanning speed of 1000 mm/s in an argon atmosphere, tested under a 5 N load.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) curves for metamaterial matrices (2x1 and 2x2) compared against their respective C-T and C-X unit cells, showing both experimental dilatometry measurements and numerical simulation predictions.
summary: This plot displays the measured and simulated CTE values for metamaterial matrices and their constituent unit cells. Experimental dilatometry data for the 2x1 and 2x2 matrices are compared with the C-T and C-X unit cell curves, with dashed lines representing simulation results and short-dashed lines representing measured unit cell data.

caption: Testing accuracy variation plotted against epochs for ResNet-based feature fusion models compared to a standard ResNet18 baseline.
summary: Testing accuracy curves are presented here to illustrate model performance across training cycles. These curves follow a trend comparable to the training loss reduction, demonstrating the progression of predictive accuracy for the ResNet-based feature fusion models and the general ResNet18 model throughout the duration of the training process.

caption: Inverse pole figure-based microstructure map of nickel particles, highlighting the polycrystalline face-centered cubic structure with varied grain orientations.
summary: An inverse pole figure-based microstructure map reveals the crystallographic orientation of the pure nickel powder. The analysis confirms that the material is primarily face-centered cubic (FCC) and exists in a polycrystalline structure, characterized by various orientations of α-nickel grains throughout the powder particles.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HT LPBFed block sample processed at 53.33 J/mm3, measured near the austenite Curie temperature.
summary: This panel shows isothermal M-H curves for the 53.33 J/mm3 sample near the austenite Curie temperature. The data highlight the ferromagnetic-paramagnetic transition, with magnetization showing a linear dependence on the applied field followed by saturation at roughly 0.1 T, consistent with the expected ferromagnetic properties below the transition.

caption: Voltage and current curves corresponding to the droplet transfer frames, showing a short-circuit transfer frequency of approximately 5 kHz.
summary: The I-V curves illustrate the electrical characteristics during the metal transfer process. Panel b highlights that the frequency of the μ-GMA short-circuit transfer is approximately 5 kHz, which is significantly higher than the 20–200 Hz frequency typically observed in conventional GMA-based DED processes using larger diameter wires.

caption: Numerical and experimental load-displacement curves for sinusoidal DCB joints featuring an A/λ ratio of 1/4.
summary: This panel reports the mechanical testing results for sinusoidal interfaces characterized by an A/λ ratio of 1/4. By comparing numerical simulations with experimental load-displacement data, the plot validates the model's accuracy in predicting the mechanical response of these joints, demonstrating consistent behavior across the specified geometric configuration.

caption: HE-XRD strain map of the εxx component in the LPBF metallic glass, illustrating residual strain distribution correlated with the underlying melt pool structure.
summary: The HE-XRD strain map for the εxx component reveals the residual strain distribution within the LPBF metallic glass. The observed strain morphology closely resembles the melt pool structure identified in the optical micrograph, indicating that the thermal history of the laser processing significantly influences the internal strain state of the material.

caption: Simulated diffraction pattern for the L21 phase, which demonstrates a complete match with the experimental pattern.
summary: The simulated diffraction pattern for the L21 phase is shown to provide a perfect match with the experimental SAED pattern from panel a. This identification is critical, as the L21 phase exhibits a cube-on-cube orientation relationship with the ferritic matrix, making it difficult to distinguish from other phases.

caption: Decision path visualization illustrating the SHAP values for the full dataset used to predict yield strength in additive manufacturing.
summary: This panel displays the decision paths derived from a SHAP analysis applied to the full dataset for yield strength predictions. It provides a comprehensive overview of how various input features influence the model's output, serving as a foundational diagnostic tool for understanding the predictive behavior of the machine learning system.

caption: Flow stress curves of AM-DED and wrought Inconel 718 plotted against strain at varying temperatures and strain rates.
summary: Flow stress curves for AM-DED and wrought Inconel 718 demonstrate that differences in mechanical behavior are minimal at high temperatures and low strain rates. However, significant variations emerge at low temperatures and high strain rates, driven by dynamic recrystallization at extended strain levels and high peak stress values.

caption: Box-and-whisker distribution of grain sizes measured as equivalent circle diameter (ECD) across different processing conditions and cross-section orientations, highlighting quartiles and mean values.
summary: This box-and-whisker plot illustrates the distribution of grain sizes in equivalent circle diameter for various conditions and orientations. It highlights the first quartile, median, third quartile, and mean. Notably, the HIP_1250 condition exhibits a higher fraction of coarser grains in the Z cross-section, reaching a Q3 value of 159 µm ECD.

caption: Simple cubic unit cell oriented with [001] parallel to the loading direction (LD), showing both the original x'y'z' and the rotated xyz coordinate systems.
summary: This panel illustrates a simple cubic unit cell oriented with [001] parallel to the loading direction. The build direction is aligned with the z' axis. In this configuration, four vertical struts effectively support the load, while eight horizontal struts do not contribute significantly to the structural load-bearing capacity of the cell.

caption: Delta L/Lo versus temperature curves for materials in AB, T5, and T6 heat-treated conditions, showing initial tests as solid lines and repeated tests as dashed lines.
summary: This panel displays the thermal expansion behavior of materials subjected to AB, T5, and T6 heat treatments. The plot illustrates Delta L/Lo as a function of temperature, comparing initial measurements with solid lines against repeated test cycles represented by dashed lines to evaluate the stability of the thermal expansion response.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation (TTT) curve of GH4169 alloy, illustrating the kinetics of phase transitions as a function of temperature and time.
summary: The time-temperature-transformation (TTT) curve for the GH4169 alloy is presented, as originally documented by Brooks and Bridges. This diagram provides essential kinetic data regarding phase stability and transformation behavior, which is critical for understanding the microstructural evolution of the alloy during various thermal processing conditions.

caption: Normalised stress-life (S-N) curves for as-built and heat/surface-treated conditions.
summary: Normalised S-N curves are presented to compare the fatigue performance across different specimen conditions. Following the normalisation process, the curve for the as-built specimen aligns more closely with the heat-treated samples, although it remains the least performant among the tested conditions, highlighting the relative improvements achieved through various treatments.

caption: Equilibrium phase fractions for CoCrFeNi + 4 at% Ti alloy plotted against temperature from 500 to 1300 °C.
summary: Equilibrium phase calculations for the CoCrFeNi + 4 at% Ti alloy reveal the emergence of secondary phases, including η-Ni3Ti, σ, and ordered phases. These results, derived from Thermo-Calc simulations, highlight the impact of Ti addition on phase stability and the potential for phase engineering through post-heat treatment.

caption: Box plot of stress difference for Case 4, featuring a unidirectional scanning strategy with further increased hatch spacing compared to Case 3.
summary: Case 4 continues the trend of increasing hatch spacing under a unidirectional scanning strategy. The box plot shows a significant decrease in the occurrence of high stress differences at neighboring grains when moving from Case 1 to Case 4, indicating that these processing conditions effectively mitigate high stress concentrations.

caption: UV–vis absorbance curves depicting the catalytic conversion of 4-NP by 3 wt% Co-HPMC-C, showing total conversion after 100 minutes.
summary: The UV–vis spectra illustrate the catalytic reduction of 4-NP by 3 wt% Co-HPMC-C. This catalyst composition exhibits the highest performance among the tested HPMC-based samples, reaching 100% conversion in 100 minutes, confirming that higher cobalt content effectively accelerates the catalytic conversion process for this specific material system.

caption: Anode voltage evolution of Ni(100-x)Cox-GDC single cells over 50 redox cycles at 800 °C, showing a significant voltage drop for the pure Ni-GDC composition.
summary: This plot displays the anode voltage of Ni(100-x)Cox-GDC single cells during 50 redox cycles at 800 °C. The data reveals that pure Ni-GDC anodes experience a significant voltage drop, eventually reaching approximately 0.7 V, while early-stage fluctuations are likely attributed to the thermal history during the cell sintering process.

caption: Transmission spectrum measured for a 3D-printed multi-material disk incorporating Atto465, Atto495, and Atto565 dyes, featuring 0.5 mm thick sections.
summary: The transmission spectrum shown here corresponds to a 3D-printed multi-material disk fabricated with Atto465, Atto495, and Atto565 dyes. The sample consists of sections with a uniform thickness of 0.5 mm, providing insight into the optical performance of this specific dye mixture in the printed material.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the T40 alloy viewed along the normal direction (ND), accompanied by the corresponding standard triangle for crystallographic orientation identification.
summary: This panel presents the initial microstructural state of the T40 alloy through an EBSD-based inverse pole figure map. By displaying the orientation distribution along the normal direction alongside the standard reference triangle, the map provides a clear visualization of the grain orientations present in the material prior to further processing.

caption: High-resolution Co 2p3/2 XPS spectra comparing Co-MG and PS-grafted Co-MG nanoparticles, highlighting the emergence of Co-OOR states at 780.3 eV and Co-Fe-O bonds at 770.0 eV in the grafted sample.
summary: Comparison of the Co 2p3/2 XPS spectra between Co-MG and PS-grafted Co-MG nanoparticles reveals distinct chemical shifts. The PS-grafted nanoparticles exhibit new binding states corresponding to Co-OOR at 780.3 eV and Co-Fe-O bonds at 770.0 eV, indicating successful surface modification of the metallic glass nanoparticles with polystyrene chains.

caption: Training and validation loss evolution for six neural network models, showing the impact of parameter count on convergence behavior.
summary: Training curves illustrate the loss function evolution for six neural networks, with datasets split into 9000 training and 1000 validation samples. Vertical segments denote optimal epochs for validation loss, while circular markers indicate learning rate reductions. Models are categorized by parameter count, with MFFED_2, MFED_2, and MDED showing distinct convergence trends.

caption: Class B defect state exhibiting moderate unfused pores within the melt-pool structure.
summary: Class B displays moderate unfused pores resulting from lower energy density conditions. The melt-pool exhibits a progressively narrower geometry and a more pronounced necking phenomenon compared to higher energy states. These structural changes are characteristic of the unfused pore formation process observed in the melt-track numerical and experimental images.

caption: Infrared heatmap of layer 82, recorded prior to printing, showing the ghost face artifact present in the thermal distribution.
summary: Captured before the start of printing, this infrared heatmap of layer 82 illustrates the thermal distribution across the surface. Consistent with other pre-printing layers, the visualization reveals the presence of a ghost face artifact, demonstrating the stability of this thermal feature throughout the initial stages of the process.

caption: Faradaic efficiency and CO production rates for SOECs tested at 750 °C under current densities of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 A·cm⁻².
summary: This panel displays the Faradaic efficiency and CO production rates for SOECs at 750 °C. Galvanostatic testing was performed for 20–40 minutes at varying current densities. Some Faradaic efficiency values exceeded 100%, likely due to measurement errors during GC analysis of the cathode exhaust gas.

caption: Polarization curves of 316L stainless steel samples subjected to ultrasonic cavitation in distilled water containing varying concentrations of SDS.
summary: This panel displays polarization curves for 316L samples in distilled water with different SDS concentrations under ultrasonic cavitation. The data indicates that the addition of SDS shifts the polarization curves toward more anodic potentials. These curves were obtained after 15 minutes of cavitation to evaluate the electrochemical response of the material.

caption: Arc signal waveforms and transition cycle imaging for specimen #4, highlighting the arc behavior and droplet transfer dynamics under the applied ultrasonic vibration power.
summary: Specimen #4 is examined during the second layer of deposition, with high-speed camera imaging and electrical signal acquisition capturing the transition cycle and arc waveforms. The data illustrates the arc behavior under ultrasonic vibration, contributing to the overall study of how different power levels affect the droplet transfer process.

caption: Surface topography of the alumina tube's inner wall, obtained through laser scanning confocal microscopy to assess roughness.
summary: Laser scanning confocal microscopy is employed to analyze the inner wall surface of the alumina tube. By capturing the topography, this measurement provides quantitative data regarding the surface roughness, which is essential for evaluating the structural quality and finish of the tube component within the casting assembly.

caption: Relationship between relative chemical potential and surface energy for the Mg2Cu phase.
summary: The Mg2Cu phase is analyzed through a plot of surface energy versus relative chemical potential. This calculation is part of a systematic effort to determine the surface energy characteristics of multiple phases, facilitating a better understanding of their thermodynamic behavior.

caption: Geometry of the solid cylindrical specimen extracted from the welded cylinder, featuring the welded interface positioned at the center.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometry of the solid cylindrical specimens used for experimental testing. These specimens were machined and extracted from a welded solid cylinder, specifically ensuring that the welded interface is located at the specimen center to facilitate accurate tensile and fatigue testing of the joint region.

caption: Pareto chart of standardised effects for the width response, showing the relative impact of variables against a significance reference line.
summary: This Pareto chart depicts the standardised effects of parameters on the width response. Through the application of t-statistics to test the null hypothesis of zero impact, the chart highlights key variables. A reference line is provided to indicate which effects are statistically significant within the experimental dataset.

caption: Polar diagram of wire-arc DED NAB alloy displaying texture intensity.
summary: This polar diagram illustrates the texture intensity of the wire-arc DED NAB alloy. The results show a lower texture pole density compared to the cast NAB alloy, confirming that the additive manufacturing process results in a more randomized or less strongly textured grain structure than traditional casting methods.

caption: 1H-NMR spectrum (400 MHz, D2O) of the methanolic extract from Ahnfeltiopsis devoniensis, highlighting protein-related peaks in region I and a detailed zoom in region II.
summary: The 1H-NMR spectrum of the methanolic extract of Ahnfeltiopsis devoniensis reveals characteristic peaks attributed to carrageenan oligosaccharide residues. Specifically, anomeric protons are identified at δ 5.19 and δ 4.99, while sugar ring protons (H2-H6) appear between δ 4.2 and 3.0, alongside distinct protein-related signals in the specified regions.

caption: Optimization performance of combined versus individual radial and medial parameterization models.
summary: This plot displays the optimization progress for different parameterization models. The combination strategy reaches a better overall optimum compared to the individual radial or medial parameterizations. Although the combination approach requires a few additional generations to converge, it ultimately achieves a superior result relative to the other tested parameterization methods.

caption: Voltage-time evolution for PEO coatings in a P-based electrolyte system with increasing silicate content, showing a consistent breakdown voltage of approximately 260 V for specimens 2K2Si18P and 2K6Si18P.
summary: This panel presents voltage-time curves for PEO coatings formed in a P-based electrolyte system with a gradual increase in silicate content. The results indicate that specimens 2K2Si18P and 2K6Si18P exhibit a similar breakdown voltage of approximately 260 V, highlighting the influence of silicate concentration on the coating's electrical breakdown characteristics.

caption: Long-term cycling performance of Zn||Zn symmetric cells tested at a current density of 1 mA cm⁻² and an areal capacity of 1 mAh cm⁻², demonstrating enhanced stability with SL-contained electrolytes over 2000 hours.
summary: This panel displays the cycling stability of Zn||Zn symmetric cells at 1 mA cm⁻² and 1 mAh cm⁻². The inclusion of SL additives significantly boosts the stability of the electrolyte compared to pristine versions, allowing the symmetric batteries to maintain highly stable cycling for 2000 hours under these specific test conditions.

caption: Comparison of elastic modulus distribution histograms for micro elements across varying homogeneity levels (m values).
summary: This histogram compares the elastic modulus distribution of micro elements under different homogeneity levels. As the m value increases, the dispersion of the elastic modulus decreases significantly, demonstrating that higher homogeneity levels reduce material randomness and improve overall uniformity. The plot effectively illustrates the relationship between homogeneity parameters and mechanical property consistency.

caption: Gas temperature distribution upstream of the spray gun with an injector diameter (Di1) of 2 mm.
summary: Represented here is the gas temperature contour upstream of the spray gun for an injector diameter of 2 mm. The temperature distribution is significantly influenced by the injector diameter, which also correlates positively with the mass flow rate of the powder carrier gas as observed in the system.

caption: Von Mises equivalent strain distribution contour within the integrated sheep mandible and scaffold structure.
summary: The von Mises equivalent strain distribution within the sheep mandible-scaffold system is illustrated here. This analysis highlights that the stiffness in the critical size area is lower than that of the intact mandible, reflecting the significantly lower Young's modulus of the PEK scaffold material compared to cortical bone.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the natural logarithm of the diffusion coefficient (lnD) versus the inverse of temperature (1/T) for various diffusion couples.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between the natural logarithm of the diffusion coefficient and the inverse of temperature. By plotting lnD against 1/T for different diffusion couples, the graph facilitates the determination of diffusion activation energy, providing insight into the temperature dependence of diffusion processes in the studied materials.

caption: Visual documentation of the laser powder bed fusion processing environment within the building chamber during specimen fabrication.
summary: This photograph captures the laser powder bed fusion processing environment inside the building chamber during the fabrication of high-strength aluminum specimens. It illustrates the experimental setup and the physical conditions under which the laser-material interaction occurs, providing context for the manufacturing process described in the study's experimental parameters.

caption: Contour plot demonstrating the combined influence of Laser Scanning Distance (LSD) and Carrier Gas Flow (CGF) on the resulting powder spheroidization ratio.
summary: The contour plot highlights the relationship between LSD and CGF on the powder spheroidization ratio. Increasing the LSD from 2 mm to 10 mm at a constant CGF leads to a substantial increase in the spheroidization ratio, demonstrating that higher LSD values are critical for achieving over 90% spheroidization.

caption: Calculated concentration profiles of Al and Cr for the CC Alloy 247 variant at the conclusion of stage-I oxidation at 1100 °C, derived from DICTRA simulations.

caption: Three-dimensional CAD models of TPMS porous scaffolds at 60%, 70%, and 80% porosity, alongside an RDOD scaffold model at 70% porosity, all featuring a constant strut diameter of 0.3 mm.
summary: This panel displays 3D CAD models of TPMS and RDOD tantalum scaffolds. The TPMS structures are shown at 60%, 70%, and 80% porosity, while the RDOD structure is shown at 70% porosity. All scaffold designs maintain a consistent wall thickness or strut diameter of 0.3 mm for structural comparison.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the ST-treated SLM-fabricated HX alloy, revealing a γ matrix with reduced dislocation density and the absence of precipitates.
summary: Following solution treatment (ST), the SLM-fabricated HX alloy exhibits a distinct microstructure characterized by a γ matrix. TEM analysis reveals a lower dislocation density compared to the as-received state, and notably, the precipitates previously present in the as-received material have completely disappeared after this heat treatment process.

caption: Evaluation of modeling results against experimental measurements and theoretical phase boundaries at 1273 K.
summary: At 1273 K, the modeling results demonstrate close agreement with experimental measurements from Hasebe and Falkeno, represented by black triangles and diamonds, respectively. Furthermore, the calculated theoretical phase boundaries, shown as a solid line, align well with these experimental data points, confirming the reliability of the modeling framework at this elevated temperature.

caption: Carbon contamination levels in NiTi-20Hf powders processed at 20 kHz and 40 kHz frequencies.
summary: Carbon contamination levels in NiTi-20Hf powders are analyzed across different processing frequencies. The findings indicate that carbon absorption increases as the process advances, with significantly higher contamination observed in powders processed at 40 kHz compared to 20 kHz, demonstrating the substantial influence of frequency on the level of contamination.

caption: STEM-BF image of the LoHT A + SSP series showing the bulk microstructure.
summary: STEM-BF imaging of the LoHT A + SSP series reveals the bulk microstructure. High dislocation density is observed throughout the material, indicating significant plastic deformation. This panel provides a baseline for comparing the internal structural characteristics of the alloy after the specified aging and surface treatment processing sequence.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the as-built Al6061 specimen showing the initial compositional state prior to any heat treatment.
summary: This panel displays the elemental distribution map for the as-built Al6061 specimen. It serves as the baseline reference for the compositional state of the material before undergoing any subsequent heat treatment processes, providing a clear view of the initial distribution of elements within the alloy structure.

caption: Ellingham diagram illustrating the standard Gibbs free energy of formation for relevant nitrides (TiN, UN, AlN) at 1 bar N2, calculated using Thermo-Calc software.
summary: This Ellingham diagram displays the thermodynamic stability of nitrides at 1 bar N2. TiN is shown to be more stable than UN across all experimental temperatures. Additionally, AlN is thermodynamically more favourable than UN only at temperatures below approximately 700°C, indicating potential for nitrogen donation from sub-stoichiometric UN.

caption: Raman vibrational bands observed for CNT powders combined with copper.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of CNT powders combined with copper reveals broad vibrational bands. These spectral features indicate the presence of partially disordered carbon structures within the composite material, providing insight into the structural characteristics of the CNTs when integrated into the copper powder matrix.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the Nb–40Ti–20Ta alloy matrix showing a single-phase microstructure.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the matrix of the Nb–40Ti–20Ta alloy prepared by LPBF. The observation confirms the presence of a single-phase microstructure within the matrix region, providing a baseline for comparing the structural characteristics of the grain boundary zones in the alloy.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of PCL raw material, as-fabricated scaffold (SCF), and scaffold after 14 days of cell culture (SCF-CC), highlighting characteristic polymer signals.
summary: Presented here are the 1H NMR spectra for PCL in its raw, scaffold, and post-culture states. The spectra confirm the presence of characteristic polymer signals without evidence of degradation products after 14 days of cell culture, consistent with GPC findings, indicating the structural stability of the PCL scaffolds during the experiment.

caption: Refractive Fourier transform generator beam profile measured at a working distance of 250 mm, showing a 4 x 4 mm dimension with a 0.5 mm scale bar.
summary: The refractive Fourier transform generator produces a flattened beam profile, as observed on the Spiricon camera. Despite some intensity non-uniformity attributed to residual beam imperfections and optical misalignment, the profile demonstrates a significant flattening effect compared to the incident Gaussian beam, confirming the efficacy of the refractive transformation setup.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the as-built specimen highlighting the morphology and distribution of γ' precipitates.
summary: Captured via the <100> superlattice reflection, this dark-field TEM image provides a detailed view of the γ' phase morphology in the as-built specimen. The micrograph illustrates the structural characteristics of the precipitates, which are consistent with the expected γ' phase formation observed in EB-PBF processed Haynes 282 alloy specimens.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profile of P-W specimens illustrating the hydrogen release behavior across the measured temperature range.
summary: TDS measurements for the P-W specimen demonstrate a distinct hydrogen mapping profile compared to the HR-W specimen. Analysis of the desorption curve reveals three specific peaks, indicating a different distribution and nature of hydrogen trap sites present in the P-W material compared to the HR-W specimen's four-peak profile.

caption: STEM-EDS elemental mapping of Iron (Fe) distribution across the cross-section of the carbide rods.
summary: STEM-EDS analysis of the carbide rod cross-section reveals a negligibly low concentration of Fe within the rods. This elemental mapping confirms that the carbide rods are chemically distinct from the surrounding Fe-rich matrix, highlighting the localized nature of the eutectic phase formation.

caption: Representative morphology of the Metco 51060 A powder blend, illustrating the physical state and particle characteristics of the material.
summary: This image displays the typical morphology of the Metco 51060 A powder blend. The material, characterized by a specific nominal particle size distribution and an apparent density, is presented to show its physical state. This visual representation provides essential context regarding the powder's structural features prior to any further processing.

caption: Logarithmic voltage-time curves for S3 NiTi alloy, exhibiting the highest film formation rates with slopes of 0.05102, 0.09671, and 0.12034 at pH 3, 5, and 7.
summary: The S3 sample demonstrates the highest film formation rates among the tested alloys. The logarithmic voltage-time curves reveal slopes of 0.05102, 0.09671, and 0.12034 at pH 3, 5, and 7, respectively, highlighting the superior passive film formation kinetics of S3 compared to the other samples in the study.

caption: Line graph displaying microhardness values for laminates produced using tool T1 at 1200 rpm, showing higher hardness at the first measuring point compared to the second.
summary: Microhardness results for laminates processed with tool T1 at 1200 rpm are presented as a line graph. The data indicates that hardness values are higher at the initial measuring point than at the subsequent point. This trend reflects the influence of welding speed on precipitate dissolution and overall material strength.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profiles of complex oxide and hydroxide anions, specifically AlO2-, TiO-, CrO-, FeOH-, NiO-, NiOH-, TiO2-, CrO2-, and CrO3H-, for the inner surface of alloy 690 tubes corroded at 170°C, where the Ni2- signal peaks at 23 seconds of sputtering, corresponding to a 7 nm oxide thickness.
summary: This panel presents ToF-SIMS depth profiles for a range of complex oxide and hydroxide anions on the inner surface of alloy 690 tubes after 170°C corrosion testing. caption: Effective refractive index n_eff plotted against phonon frequency ω for a SiGe phononic crystal (PnC) cavity, illustrating the rapid growth of n_eff in the region where the PnC band structure flattens.
summary: This plot displays the effective refractive index n_eff as a function of phonon frequency ω within a SiGe phononic crystal cavity. The data demonstrates a rapid increase in n_eff corresponding to the flattening of the PnC band, which is a critical feature for driving the cross-section toward higher values at practical scales.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from iR-free cell voltage curves, comparing the electrochemical kinetics of uncoated Ti felt and gold-coated PTLs in a PEMWE cell environment.
summary: Tafel slope analysis provides insight into the electrochemical kinetics of the PTLs within the PEMWE cell. The gold-coated PTLs demonstrate a lower Tafel slope compared to the uncoated PTLs, as derived from the iR-free cell voltage curves, indicating improved catalytic activity and reduced charge transfer resistance for the coated samples.

caption: Electrical contact verification for the TPU-B25/CB-ZnO strip using a circuit with an LED light after thermal treatment.
summary: Electrical contact testing for the joined TPU-B25/CB-ZnO strips was conducted using a circuit with an LED light. The successful illumination of the LED confirms that a reliable electrical connection was established between the conductive elements following thermal treatment, validating the integrity of the fused interface in the composite strips.

caption: Tan δ (damping factor) curves for PLA + EtLa, PLA + 1.5% cCNC, and PLA samples with AcCNC at different degrees of substitution (DS).
summary: Tan δ curves are shown for PLA + EtLa, PLA + 1.5% cCNC, and PLA samples incorporating AcCNC with varying degrees of substitution. The analysis of the tan δ peak clarifies how the surface chemistry of the AcCNC fillers modulates the interaction between the PLA matrix and the reinforcing phase.

caption: Mapping of atomic displacement vectors in the z-direction for the Fe2Ti intermetallic structure.
summary: The panel presents the z-direction atomic displacement trajectories for the Fe2Ti intermetallic compound. These results visualize the internal structural shifts occurring within the hexagonal lattice, providing critical data on how the atomic arrangement responds during the molecular dynamics simulation process for this specific intermetallic phase.

caption: Confocal microscopy images of hMSCs on day 6, stained with Live/Dead assay reagents where live cells appear green and dead cells appear red.
summary: Confocal imaging of the Live/Dead assay performed on day 6 reveals a high proportion of viable cells across all tested groups. The visual evidence of green-stained live cells confirms that the PVA samples do not induce significant cytotoxicity, maintaining high cell health throughout the six-day experimental duration.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the binary classification results obtained by the CNN model for identifying stringing defects.
summary: The confusion matrix for stringing defects displays the classification outcomes of the CNN model. It serves as a diagnostic tool to assess the model's ability to correctly identify stringing instances versus non-stringing instances, contributing to the overall evaluation of the CNN's performance in detecting specific manufacturing defects.

caption: Radial distribution functions g(r) for various atom pairs in H2O-containing KCl-MgCl2 molten salt mixtures interacting with a (110)Ni surface slab at 700 °C, highlighting the formation of Ni-Cl covalent bonds at an average distance of 2.2 Å.
summary: This panel presents radial distribution functions for H2O-containing KCl-MgCl2 molten salt mixtures interacting with a (110)Ni surface slab at 700 °C. caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material disk containing Atto425, Atto465, and Atto565 dyes, with each section measuring 0.5 mm in thickness.
summary: This panel displays the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed multi-material disk composed of three distinct dyes: Atto425, Atto465, and Atto565.
