This comparison confirms the validity of using synthetic models with GB-phases to represent the magnetic behavior of real digitized microstructures.

caption: Violin plots illustrating the distribution of mean squared error (MSE) for various KH porosity metrics, comparing KHLineNum against alternative measures across SBD test samples.
summary: This figure displays violin plots comparing the predictive accuracy of different KH porosity metrics using a machine learning framework. The results demonstrate that KHLineNum achieves the lowest MSE, confirming its superiority as a target variable. The central markers indicate the median and interquartile range of the error distributions across test samples.

caption: Inverse pole figure map showing the crystallographic orientation distribution for the Z-Z welded joint.
summary: This inverse pole figure map characterizes the crystallographic orientation distribution for the Z-Z welded joint. It serves as a critical piece of the texture analysis, allowing for a direct comparison of the microstructural orientation outcomes between the Z-Z joint and the other welded joints examined in the research.

caption: K-space Cu EXAFS oscillations for Ni 0.001 Cu NPs, Ni 0.01 Cu NPs, Cu NPs, and Cu foil standard, demonstrating the local electronic environment after reduction.
summary: K-space Cu EXAFS spectra are shown for Ni-doped Cu nanoparticles, pure Cu nanoparticles, and a Cu foil reference. The data confirms the metallic state of the Cu species in the nanoparticle samples, consistent with the XANES results, reflecting the local atomic environment after the in-situ reduction treatment.

caption: Digital image correlation strain distribution map of the MIM NiTi alloy during the loading phase of a 5% tensile strain test at 15 °C.
summary: Digital image correlation analysis reveals the strain distribution of the MIM NiTi alloy during 5% tensile loading at 15 °C. The strain distribution across the specimen is observed to be relatively uniform, indicating consistent mechanical behavior during the tensile deformation process under the specified room temperature testing conditions.

caption: Representative CLSM images showing CAFs embedded in ALG-RGD, oxALG-RGD, and oxALG-RGD-PVGLIG hydrogels over 14 days, highlighting F-actin (green) and nuclei (blue) morphology, alongside ECM deposition (FN in red) at day 14.
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy reveals that CAFs exhibit a round morphology in non-degradable ALG-RGD hydrogels due to physical constraints. In contrast, oxALG-RGD and oxALG-RGD-PVGLIG hydrogels support cell spreading and ECM deposition, as evidenced by F-actin and fibronectin staining, demonstrating the impact of hydrogel degradability on cell behavior.

caption: Initial layers of an upright printed bending bar showing the base structure before significant build-induced misalignment occurs.
summary: This photograph displays the initial layers of a 3 mm by 4 mm cross-section bending bar during the printing process. The image captures the base of the green body, providing a reference for the structural alignment before the relative movement of the build platform leads to subsequent layer deposition errors.

caption: Slump flow values for concrete mixtures formulated with varying dosages of GGBS, comparing samples prepared with and without the addition of NS.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the slump flow measurements for concrete mixtures containing different GGBS concentrations, evaluated both with and without NS incorporation. These flow characteristics are essential for assessing the structural stability and workability of concrete mixtures, providing critical data for optimizing materials specifically intended for 3D printing applications.

caption: Pole figures of the FCC and HCP phases, illustrating the Shoji-Nishiyama (S-N) orientation relationship defined by (111)fcc // (0001)hcp and [110]fcc // [2-1-10]hcp.
summary: Pole figures for both FCC and HCP phases confirm the existence of the Shoji-Nishiyama orientation relationship. The alignment of specific crystallographic planes and directions, namely (111)fcc // (0001)hcp and [110]fcc // [2-1-10]hcp, provides evidence of the structural relationship between the two phases observed in the alloy.

caption: Initial reaction state at 0.79 msec showing the ignition point marked by a yellow spark at the bottom of the Double C pattern.
summary: This initial frame captures the reaction at 0.79 msec, highlighting the ignition point with a yellow spark. The reaction front begins its propagation from the bottom of the Double C pattern, establishing the starting condition for the subsequent observation of the reaction front movement through the structured foil geometry.

caption: Actual strain map calculated from the (220) Bragg edge of the DP 1000 sheet at a 300 N/mm load case.
summary: Strain distribution within the DP 1000 sheet is quantified through an actual strain map derived from the (220) Bragg edge diffraction data. This map illustrates the localized mechanical response of the material under a 300 N/mm load, highlighting the progression of strain as the applied mechanical force increases.

caption: DSC/TG analysis of the AR78-TiO2 filament in the as-extruded state, showing an endothermic LDPE melting peak at approximately 110 °C and overlapping exothermic polymer decomposition peaks between 320 °C and 450 °C.
summary: The as-extruded AR78-TiO2 filament exhibits characteristic thermal behavior during DSC/TG analysis. An endothermic melting peak for the LDPE binder occurs at 110 °C, followed by exothermic polymer decomposition starting at 180 °C. Notably, a sharp peak overlaps with other decomposition signals in the 320 °C to 450 °C temperature range.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the AM-240 alloy illustrating intermetallic/austenite interfaces, featuring 5.5 at% Mo and 3.5 at% Ni iso-concentration surfaces in red and green.
summary: Representing the AM-240 alloy, this APT reconstruction highlights intermetallic precipitates within a cuboidal sub-volume. The structural features are identified by 5.5 at% Mo and 3.5 at% Ni iso-concentration surfaces, shown in red and green, which effectively map the spatial distribution of the intermetallic phases relative to the austenite matrix.

caption: Diffusion path of layer (2) superimposed on a calculated isothermal section at 450 °C, demonstrating alignment with the two-phase region.
summary: Mapping the element distribution of layer (2) onto a calculated isothermal section at 450 °C reveals a strong correlation with the two-phase region of the Al–Cu–Zn system. This fit confirms the phase behavior of the layer at lower temperatures, consistent with findings reported in previous literature.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors with 5 OTU layers, demonstrating the electrochemical response in different liquid electrolyte media.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors with 5 OTU layers are presented to assess the impact of different liquid electrolytes. These measurements provide a direct comparison of the charging and discharging characteristics, facilitating the identification of the most effective electrolyte for maximizing the capacitive performance of the on-chip device.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of Platinum (Pt) distribution across the interface.
summary: The EDS mapping result for Platinum shows the distribution of the coating or protective layer material at the interface. This elemental map helps delineate the boundary between the TC4 substrate and the surface modifications, providing clear spatial context for the chemical composition analysis of the interfacial region.

caption: M(H) curve for the x = 1.0 alloy, depicting the magnetization (full circles) and demagnetization (empty circles) cycles from 0 to 7 T in the vicinity of the structural and magnetic transition.
summary: Representing the x = 1.0 alloy, this M(H) curve shows the magnetic response near transition regions during cooling. The data, consisting of magnetization and demagnetization paths up to 7 T, serves as the basis for calculating magnetic entropy changes and quantifying the average magnetic hysteresis loss through the enclosed loop area.

caption: Energy landscape E(x1) for dislocation glide in the second NbTaV sample realization, featuring comparative paths from NEB and PN models alongside an inset of the dislocation line at the local minimum energy position.
summary: Representing the second NbTaV sample realization, this panel displays the energy landscape for dislocation glide. It contrasts atomistic NEB paths with PN model predictions. The included inset visualizes the dislocation line at the local minimum energy position, providing insight into the atomic-scale configuration during the glide process.

caption: Three-dimensional surface topographic images of control and experimental PUF-modified 3D-printed composites, captured via tapping-mode AFM over a 20 µm × 20 µm scanning area.
summary: Three-dimensional reconstructed AFM images illustrate the surface micro-topography of the unmodified control and PUF-modified experimental 3D-printed composites. These images provide a detailed visualization of the surface characteristics, serving as a primary assessment tool for evaluating the surface morphology of the different composite groups within the study.

caption: PND Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 310 K.
summary: PND refinement results for the Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 composition at 310 K are presented. The plot features experimental black dots, a red calculated intensity line, and a blue difference plot. The diffraction pattern is indexed with tick marks corresponding to the TiNiSi, Ni2In, and MgZn2 phases.

caption: Cumulative CO2 emissions for electric and combustion vehicles over a 150,000 km, 10-year lifecycle, compared across five distinct electricity generation scenarios: coal (W1), natural gas (W2), renewable sources (W3), European average mix (W4), and Polish average mix (W5).
summary: This bar chart illustrates the total CO2 emissions generated by electric and combustion vehicles over a 150,000 km, 10-year lifespan. The analysis evaluates the environmental impact across five electricity generation sources, ranging from coal and natural gas to renewable energy and specific regional power mixes in Europe and Poland.

caption: Ni self-diffusion coefficients plotted against inverse temperature, contrasting experimental literature trends with simulation results for Ni-5Cr and Ni-20Cr alloys.
summary: Panel b illustrates Ni self-diffusion coefficients, showing that variations across different concentrations are minor compared to experimental spread in pure FCC Ni. The simulation results for Ni-5Cr and Ni-20Cr, using both rescaled single-vacancy and 16-vacancy models, demonstrate closer alignment with experimental diffusion coefficients than unscaled single-vacancy calculations.

caption: TG-DSC thermal analysis curve of the 3D printed Si3N4 body, illustrating the mass change and heat flow characteristics during the heating process.
summary: The TG-DSC curve of the 3D printed Si3N4 body is presented in panel (a). This thermal analysis provides critical data regarding the mass change and heat flow characteristics of the material during the heating process, which is essential for understanding the thermal behavior of the 3D printed ceramic body.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying temperature-dependent Cr tracer self-diffusion coefficients in effectively pure nickel, compiled from literature sources [52, 53, 80, 81, 85–88].
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature-dependent Cr tracer self-diffusion coefficients within effectively pure nickel. Data points are compiled from various literature sources, providing a baseline for diffusion behavior in the dilute limit. Certain measurements by Gruzin et al. and Murarka et al. are identified as outliers and excluded from further analysis.

caption: Geometric design and dimensions of the tensile test specimen used for mechanical characterization.
summary: This panel illustrates the specific geometry and dimensions of the tensile test specimens. The schematic provides the necessary structural details required for the mechanical testing procedure, ensuring consistent specimen preparation and alignment for the subsequent tensile evaluation as referenced in the study's experimental methodology.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of K4800W alloy deformed to 0.12% plastic strain at 850 °C, using g=(11-1) diffraction vector to observe reduced stacking fault density.
summary: Deformation of K4800W alloy at 850 °C with 0.12% plastic strain results in a microstructure characterized by a significant decrease in the number of stacking faults compared to 800 °C. This TEM image confirms the temperature-dependent reduction in fault density within the alloy matrix at higher thermal conditions.

caption: Feasible set of overshoot-cure duration for a 40 mm glass/epoxy prepreg laminate, comparing conventional curing methods against layer-by-layer (LbL) processing, with point A representing the optimized conventional cure condition.
summary: This diagram illustrates the feasible process window for curing a 40 mm glass/epoxy prepreg. It compares conventional curing with LbL scenarios, highlighting point A as the optimized conventional process design. The results confirm that the cure simulation is valid and the reported process efficiency metrics remain accurate for this configuration.

caption: Schmid factor distribution map of the bond coat sample subjected to a low stress amplitude of 300 MPa at 800 °C.
summary: Schmid factor distribution in the bond coat after low stress fatigue at 800 °C shows higher values compared to 700 °C tests. The IDZ consistently presents higher Schmid factor values than the outer layer, confirming that the IDZ is more prone to slip system activation, which is critical for crack nucleation.

caption: Detailed EPMA point analysis of the TiC CoCrFeMnNi composite, identifying characteristic regions A and B.
summary: This EPMA point analysis focuses on the TiC CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy composite, specifically characterizing regions A and B. Point A corresponds to a Ti-rich region, while Point B represents a C-rich region. These measurements confirm partial elemental decomposition of the TiC nanoparticles during the directed energy deposition manufacturing process.

caption: Displacement field map for a sharp tool (VB = 0 μm) at the moment of burr initiation during cutting at 6 m/min.
summary: This displacement field map illustrates the subsurface state for a sharp tool (VB = 0 μm) at the instance of burr initiation. Analysis indicates that no meaningful subsurface severe plastic deformation zone is present for this unworn tool condition, contrasting with the significant deformation observed in worn tool scenarios.

caption: Coefficients of friction (COF) curves for LPBF-ed and quenched samples, showing two distinct stages of sliding behavior.
summary: This panel displays the coefficients of friction (COF) curves for LPBF-ed and quenched samples during sliding tests. The data reveals that the COF variation occurs in two distinct stages, providing a clear representation of the tribological performance and frictional evolution of the materials under the specified testing conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the uniaxial compressive test configuration for a 3D-printed cube specimen with a side length of 100 mm.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup for a uniaxial compressive test. The specimen consists of a 3D-printed cube measuring 100 mm on each side. The diagram provides a clear visual guide for the loading orientation and geometry required to perform the compression test on the printed material sample.

caption: Atomic configuration after eight layers of deposition, showing advanced atomic-scale interaction, extensive dislocation activity, and twinning resulting in significant deformation at the interface.
summary: The final stage of eight layers shows advanced atomic-scale interaction and deformation. The nucleation of higher densities of dislocations and twinning from the surfaces of previous layers continues to impact the interface. This demonstrates the cumulative effect of the W-DED process on the atomic structure of the Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 system.

caption: XRD patterns of 316L/IN718 FGM regions 1, 2, and 3 in the as-deposited (AD) condition.
summary: This panel displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for the 316L/IN718 functionally graded materials in the as-deposited state. The data covers three distinct compositional regions, ranging from 0% to 100% IN718 content, providing a baseline structural characterization of the material before any subsequent heat treatment processes are applied.

caption: Comparison of ultimate tensile strength (UTS) versus elongation (EL) for Maraging steel workpieces, contrasting results from this study against previously reported literature data.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the mechanical performance of Maraging steel samples by comparing UTS and EL values. The data demonstrates that the samples produced in this study exhibit superior UTS and EL characteristics when evaluated against the range of values reported in previous research studies [16, 33–39].

caption: Species concentration profiles for the Fe–Cr–Ni–O system at 1300 °C under a hydrogen oxy–fuel atmosphere after 2.5 h of oxidation.
summary: Displayed here are the species profiles for the Fe–Cr–Ni–O system after 2.5 hours of oxidation at 1300 °C in a hydrogen oxy–fuel atmosphere. The profiles are highly comparable to those obtained from air–fuel simulations, noting that the interface positions vary due to the specific oxidation time and atmospheric conditions.

caption: Temperature-dependent evolution of the C66 elastic constant for six distinct pyC models compared to graphite.
summary: This line graph illustrates the temperature-dependent evolution of the C66 elastic constant for six distinct pyC models compared to graphite. The data highlights how the elastic properties of these carbon-based materials vary as a function of temperature, providing a comparative analysis between the pyC models and the reference graphite structure.

caption: Pole Figure (PF) of the US-300W Udimet-500 sample showing the development of new texture components.
summary: Ultrasonic assistance at 300 W leads to further degradation of the cubic texture and the emergence of new texture components in the Udimet-500 sample. The Pole Figure for the US-300W condition captures these structural changes, reflecting the influence of increased sonication power on the final grain orientation distribution.

caption: Temperature dependence of the parameter a derived from the Langevin analytical model.
summary: This panel displays the temperature dependence of the parameter a, which is extracted from experimental magnetic measurements using Langevin’s analytical model. The data illustrates how this specific parameter evolves with temperature, providing a basis for validating the adjustment of experimental measurements to predict magnetic permeability at higher magnetic fields.

caption: Directional dependence of Young's modulus measured for WAAM-fabricated bars at different build angles, demonstrating the presence of elastic anisotropy.
summary: This plot quantifies the directional variation in the Young's modulus of WAAM-fabricated bars across different build angles. The data confirms the existence of elastic anisotropy, indicating that the mechanical properties are intrinsically linked to the build orientation and the associated surface irregularities observed in the previous fabrication steps.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern obtained from the IN686 alloy sample to identify surface corrosion species.
summary: This panel displays the X-ray diffraction pattern for the IN686 alloy sample. The analysis was conducted to identify the specific corrosion species that formed on the alloy surface following exposure. This diffraction data provides critical structural information regarding the phase composition of the corrosion products on the IN686 material.

caption: Pole figure illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution for the as-built specimen processed with an applied magnetic field.
summary: The pole figure shows the crystallographic orientation distribution for the specimen fabricated with an applied magnetic field. This distribution mirrors the texture found at the bottom parts of the specimen, indicating that the magnetic field application maintains a consistent crystallographic texture throughout the vertical build of the material.

caption: Experimental setup showing the assessment body secured onto the sample holder at a fixed 55° orientation for analysis.
summary: This photograph displays the experimental configuration for scenario II, where the assessment body is mounted on the sample holder at a 55° orientation. This specific setup ensures consistent positioning for the subsequent analysis of the assessment body, as described in the study's methodology for this particular test scenario.

caption: Perspective view, surface plot of inner porosity, and segmented cross-section of cell wall junctions for a relative density of 50–60%.
summary: Representing a relative density of 50–60%, this panel provides a perspective view, surface plot of inner porosity, and a segmented cross-section of the cell wall junctions. Compared to lower density samples, these views illustrate the structural differences and increased cell wall thickness, which grows from 360 μm to 578 μm.

caption: STEM-HAADF image of the AlSi10Mg alloy cell structure, illustrating the distribution of Si and Al elements.
summary: The STEM-HAADF image provides a detailed view of the nano-scale cell structure within the AlSi10Mg alloy. This imaging technique, combined with elemental mapping, confirms that silicon is preferentially decorated along the cell boundaries, which is a critical feature of the solidification microstructure in this laser-processed aluminum alloy.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for effective mean stress versus specimen state, highlighting the influence of heat and machining treatments.
summary: This plot demonstrates the effect of effective mean stress on fatigue life, categorized by specimen state. When analyzed alongside panel (b), it becomes apparent that heat and machining treatments exert a stronger positive effect on fatigue life for samples subjected to mean stresses lower than the identified threshold.

caption: Pole figure analysis focused on the large blue grain identified in the cross-sectional orientation map, illustrating its specific crystallographic orientation.
summary: This pole figure provides a detailed crystallographic orientation analysis of the large blue grain identified in the cross-sectional EBSD map. By isolating this specific grain, the plot clarifies its orientation relative to the sample geometry, contributing to the overall understanding of the microstructural changes induced by the HCPEB treatment process.

caption: Chronopotentiometric stability profile of the AgNiCu/g-C3N4 electrocatalyst measured over a 24-hour duration at a constant current density of 10 mA cm-2.
summary: The stability of the AgNiCu/g-C3N4 electrocatalyst was assessed through a 24-hour chronopotentiometric test conducted at a current density of 10 mA cm-2. This measurement provides a clear indication of the material's electrochemical performance and durability under sustained operating conditions at this specific low current density level.

caption: t-SNE dimension reduction visualization of the testing set embeddings generated by the Deep SVDD model, showing a distinct sphere-like clustering of normal samples.
summary: Deep SVDD model embeddings are visualized here using t-SNE, revealing that normal samples form a characteristic sphere-like shape. This structural transition from the auto-encoder representation in panel (a) to the sphere-like distribution in panel (b) highlights the effectiveness of the finetuning step applied during the model training process.

caption: Temperature-time-transformation diagram for the R725-Control specimen, illustrating kinetic phase transformation predictions across a temperature range of 600 °C to 800 °C.
summary: The R725-Control specimen is characterized by a temperature-time-transformation diagram that predicts kinetic phase changes between 600 °C and 800 °C. This plot maps the relationship between exposure time and temperature, providing a visual representation of the material's phase stability and transformation kinetics under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Phase angle Bode plot depicting the phase angle versus frequency, featuring a wide mid-frequency region that indicates the superposition of two overlapping time constant peaks.
summary: The phase angle Bode plot displays the phase angle as a function of frequency. A wide feature observed in the mid-frequency region indicates the superposition of two undifferentiated overlapping time constant peaks, which provides insight into the electrochemical behavior and the complexity of the passive film on the alloy surface.

caption: Comparison of Young’s modulus and hardness values for as-coated HEA and Pt + HEA coatings derived from nanoindentation tests conducted at a 50 mN load.
summary: This panel displays the mechanical performance of as-coated HEA and Pt + HEA coatings subjected to a 50 mN nanoindentation load. It specifically highlights the resulting Young’s modulus and hardness values, providing a direct comparison of the mechanical properties between the two coating types based on their load-displacement characteristics.

caption: Simulated pole figure derived from the XY-plane microstructure, revealing a {110}〈001〉 Goss texture.
summary: The simulated pole figure, generated from the XY-plane microstructure, identifies a distinct {110}〈001〉 Goss texture. This crystallographic orientation pattern matches the experimental findings, indicating that the simulation successfully captures the texture development characteristic of the 316L sample under the specified building conditions.

caption: Comparative cycle performance of 3D-printed and ink-casted Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//LiCoO2 full cells at 1C, highlighting the superior capacity retention of the 3D-printed variant.
summary: Cycle performance at 1C is compared between 3D-printed and ink-casted Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//LiCoO2 full cells. The 3D-printed cell maintains 100% of its initial capacity, demonstrating exceptional Li+ storage behavior compared to the ink-casted counterpart, which highlights the structural and electrochemical advantages provided by the 3D-printing fabrication method for these battery materials.

caption: Tabulated values of the melting temperature for the different nanoparticle sizes investigated.
summary: This table provides a concise summary of the melting temperatures for each nanoparticle size. It serves as a reference for the specific numerical values derived from the melting curves and derivative analysis, allowing for easy comparison of the melting points across the range of nanoparticle sizes.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the natural logarithm of the growth rate constant (ln K) versus the inverse of absolute temperature (1/T) for borided Monel 400.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature dependence of the growth rate constant for borided Monel 400. The slope of the linear fit corresponds to -Q/R, where Q is the activation energy and R is the gas constant, while the y-axis intercept represents the pre-exponential constant Ko.

caption: Full-scale creep strain versus time curves for the Ni3Al-based single crystal alloy IC6SX, illustrating deformation behavior across various stress and temperature conditions.
summary: This panel displays the comprehensive creep curves for the IC6SX single crystal alloy at high temperatures. It captures the full deformation history of the material under diverse stress and temperature levels, providing a broad overview of the alloy's mechanical response and creep resistance characteristics throughout the testing duration.

caption: Deformation sequence of the B30 lattice showing initial contact irregularities, premature edge strut destruction, and final diagonal shear failure.
summary: Deformation of the B30 lattice initiates with uneven contact between the indenter and the structure, leading to premature edge strut destruction. As loading progresses to 1.10 MPa, shear failure emerges in the lower right corner, eventually resulting in total structural collapse along a diagonal shear band.

caption: Numerical tension test configuration employed for the calibration of the Concrete Damaged Plasticity Model (CDPM).
summary: This panel displays the numerical tension test setup used for calibrating the Concrete Damaged Plasticity Model (CDPM). The schematic outlines the specific loading arrangement and constraints necessary to model tensile response, ensuring accurate material parameter identification within the numerical framework established for the study's structural analysis.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay curve and corresponding fitting for TPU/1S composite at 490 nm emission.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime decay and fitting curves for the TPU/1S composite are presented at an emission wavelength of 490 nm. Monitored at room temperature with an excitation wavelength of 373 nm, this sample exhibits an average lifespan within the 3–5 ns range, consistent with low SAOED addition levels.

caption: Categorization of ECM-related proteins, including matrix-associated components, regulators, and sequestered secreted factors, identified as differentially expressed in CAF versus FIB co-cultures.
summary: This bar chart categorizes the ECM-related proteins that were differentially expressed in CAF versus FIB co-cultures. The identified proteins include matrix-associated components, various regulators, and secreted factors. These factors were likely sequestered within the ECM or the hydrogel 3D network, highlighting the distinct matrisome composition generated by CAFs.

caption: Room-temperature photoluminescence emission spectrum of pure SnO2 nanoparticles excited at 248 nm.
summary: Pure SnO2 nanoparticles exhibit a distinct photoluminescence emission profile when recorded at room temperature. Utilizing an excitation wavelength of 248 nm, the spectral data provides a baseline for evaluating the optical properties of the synthesized nanostructured compounds, serving as a reference for comparing the effects of various surfactant-assisted synthesis methods.

caption: Calculated total and partial density of states for the O-phase Ti2AlNb compound.
summary: For the Ti2AlNb O-phase, the density of states indicates that the valence band near the Fermi level is dominated by the hybridization of Ti-d and Nb-d states. Contributions from other orbitals, including M-s, M-p, Ti-s, Ti-p, Al-s, and Al-p, remain small throughout the electronic structure.

caption: Latent component Z1 extracted from stress-strain curves, illustrating its variation as a function of deformation temperature and strain rate.
summary: This panel displays the latent component Z1 extracted from stress-strain curves using the AE-PN model. It demonstrates how this low-dimensional representation varies across different processing parameters, specifically temperature and strain rate, highlighting the model's ability to efficiently reduce dimensionality while capturing essential features of the mechanical deformation data.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density distribution map across different layers of the as-deposited IN738 + IN718 specimen, calculated based on local misorientation data.
summary: The GND density distribution across various layers of the as-deposited IN738 + IN718 alloy is illustrated here. Calculated from misorientation data, this map highlights the spatial variation of dislocation density, which relates to the inner stress states and the precipitation behavior of the gamma-prime phase within the material.

caption: Bodipy staining images showing lipid peroxide generation in HCECs treated with Hy, Hy + D609, or Hy + D609 + Bru for 24 hours.
summary: Bodipy staining visualizes lipid peroxide generation in HCECs under different treatment conditions. The images reveal that Bru significantly elevates lipid peroxide generation in HCECs co-treated with D609 and Hy, providing direct evidence of increased oxidative stress and ferroptosis induction in the presence of Bru.

caption: Temporal variation of the γ′ phase nucleation density for Ni–20Co–14Al and Ni–20Co–14Al–8Cr alloys during isothermal processing at 900 °C.
summary: Depicting the number density of γ′ phase nuclei over time at 900 °C, this graph illustrates the nucleation kinetics for both alloys. The nucleation density of the γ′ phase in the Ni–20Co–14Al–8Cr alloy is considerably higher than in the Ni–20Co–14Al alloy, contributing to a smaller average γ′ phase radius.

caption: Bode diagram showing impedance modulus versus frequency for IN718 alloy in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution across temperatures ranging from 30 to 80 °C.
summary: The Bode plot displays the impedance modulus versus frequency for IN718 in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. High-frequency impedance represents solution resistance, while the film resistance (Rf) decreases significantly from 878.13 to 95.09 Ω cm2 as temperature increases, indicating enhanced chloride ion penetration and reduced protective film integrity.

caption: Isothermal section at the transition peritectoid reaction temperature (γ+P→oP6+α), illustrating the phase evolution involving the oP6 and α phases.
summary: This isothermal section represents the phase equilibrium at the transition peritectoid reaction temperature where γ and P phases transform into oP6 and α. It serves as a critical component in the overall reaction pathway analysis for the Ni-Cr-Mo system, detailing the structural evolution of phases at this specific thermal condition.

caption: CAD models representing five thin-walled structures, each measuring 25 mm in height and 800 mm in length with varying thicknesses.
summary: CAD models illustrate the design of five thin-walled structures. Each structure is engineered with a height of 25 mm and a length of 800 mm. The design incorporates varying thicknesses across the five specimens, providing a geometric basis for the subsequent fabrication and testing processes described in the study.

caption: Young’s modulus polar for the CLP unit cell, showing four sharp lobes indicative of orthogonal material alignment.
summary: The CLP unit cell exhibits a distinct Young’s modulus polar characterized by four sharp lobes, reflecting its orthogonal material alignment. This topology shows significant elastic anisotropy, as evidenced by the deviation from a perfect sphere. The polar is normalized by relative density and bulk stiffness, with t/L = 0.05.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis of 3D-printed SiOC(N) samples with 0.25- and 0.50 mm nozzle sizes during heating in an air atmosphere.
summary: This panel displays the high-temperature stability of 3D-printed SiOC(N) samples in air. The observed weight loss is attributed to the partial oxidation of free carbon within the SiOC(N) matrix. The data illustrates the oxidation behavior of these structures when subjected to high-temperature conditions in an oxidative environment.

caption: Onyx surface after 720 h of UV exposure, revealing increased roughness and the initiation of microcracks.
summary: Following 720 hours of UV exposure, the Onyx sample surface exhibits early signs of environmental degradation. SEM analysis reveals an increase in surface roughness compared to the reference, accompanied by the appearance of initial microcracks, marking the onset of structural embrittlement caused by the UV conditioning process.

caption: Absorbance spectra of β-carotene in XG/DD NCs solutions prepared with concentration ratios (CR) of 0.4 (black) and 2.5 (red).
summary: Absorbance spectra of β-carotene encapsulated in XG/DD NCs are presented for two different concentration ratios. The data illustrates the spectral characteristics of the encapsulated β-carotene, providing insight into the loading and stability of the hydrophobic guest molecule within the XG/DD nanocarrier architecture across varying concentration conditions.

caption: SHAP force plot visualizing the breakdown of the predicted yield strength for the same data instance, showing the shift from the base value.
summary: The SHAP force plot provides a visual breakdown of the predicted yield strength for the same data instance as panel (a). It initiates from the identical base value of 789.328 MPa, clearly demonstrating how individual feature contributions aggregate to reach the final predicted yield strength value for this specific instance.

caption: 1H-NMR spectrum (400 MHz, D2O) of the methanolic extract from Ahnfeltiopsis devoniensis, highlighting protein-related peaks in region I and a detailed zoom in region II.
summary: The 1H-NMR spectrum of the methanolic extract of Ahnfeltiopsis devoniensis reveals characteristic signals attributed to carrageenan oligosaccharide residues. Specifically, anomeric protons are identified at δ 5.19 and δ 4.99, while sugar ring protons (H2-H6) appear between δ 4.2 and 3.0, alongside distinct protein-associated peaks in the specified regions.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram for AA2017 alloy, illustrating phase evolution across temperature and time with superimposed cooling rates of 0.1 °C/s and 1 °C/s.
summary: The CCT diagram for AA2017, generated via JMatPro, maps phase transformation kinetics under varying cooling conditions. By superimposing cooling rates of 0.1 °C/s and 1 °C/s, the diagram describes the relationship between cooling profiles and the resulting microstructure, providing a predictive framework for precipitate formation based on specific thermal processing parameters.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology of a truss structure fabricated at a printing speed of 60 mm/s under low-temperature vacuum conditions.
summary: This panel displays the three-dimensional morphological characteristics of a truss structure fabricated at a printing speed of 60 mm/s. The structure was created under low-temperature vacuum conditions, illustrating the specific geometric outcome of the additive manufacturing process at this particular speed, as part of a broader study on printing parameters.

caption: BCC lattice structure represented as a 6 × 6 × 6 cell configuration, illustrating the geometric arrangement used to analyze samples with varying initial angles under compressive loading.
summary: This figure displays a 6 × 6 × 6 BCC lattice supercell configuration. This specific structural model was employed to investigate the mechanical behavior of samples characterized by different initial angles, as these configurations are known to exhibit inherent instability when subjected to compressive loading conditions during the simulation process.

caption: Raman spectra of CX, CX@Cu, CX@Fe, and CX@Co monoliths highlighting the characteristic D and G bands.
summary: Raman spectra for the CX, CX@Cu, CX@Fe, and CX@Co monoliths reveal the characteristic D and G bands of carbon xerogels. These bands are located at approximately 1350 cm-1 and 1590 cm-1, respectively, providing information on the carbonaceous structure of the monoliths across the different metal-incorporated samples.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image of a spherical Mn-rich oxide particle, with an inset displaying the selected area electron diffraction pattern.
summary: Spherical nano-sized particles, ranging from 50 to 200 nm, are identified in the PBF-LB FeCoNiCrMn alloy via TEM. The bright-field image, complemented by the SAED pattern inset, confirms the presence and crystalline nature of these Mn-rich oxide precipitates within the metallic matrix.

caption: Net causality matrix illustrating the influential relationships among various CEPs, ranked from CEP20 down to CEP13.
summary: This heatmap visualizes the net causality relationships among identified CEPs. The influential relationships are ranked in descending order of prominence, starting with CEP20, CEP18, CEP17, CEP16, CEP12, CEP14, CEP15, and ending with CEP13. The plot provides a clear representation of the causal hierarchy and interactions between these specific parameters.

caption: Initial fracture site observed in configuration 1 during iteration IV testing, indicated by an arrow.
summary: An in-situ photograph captures the initial fracture event in a configuration 1 sample during iteration IV testing. The fracture site is clearly marked by an arrow. This observation is part of a series showing that iteration IV maintains an invariant initial fracture position across different configurations.

caption: Maximum atomic and electronic temperatures for 30 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFe.
summary: This panel displays the maximum atomic and electronic temperatures observed during 30 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations within the NiFe alloy system. Data points represent results from twelve distinct cascade events, illustrating the thermal response of the material under high-energy irradiation conditions as captured by the two-temperature molecular dynamics model.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy point-mode analysis performed at point 2 within the cement matrix.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy point-mode analysis performed at point 2 within the cement matrix. This compositional analysis provides localized chemical information regarding the elemental distribution within the cementitious structure, complementing the microstructural observations made via SEM to characterize the impact of graphene oxide additives on the matrix composition.

caption: SHAPley values for features in dataset D3 computed over the trained SVM-3 model, illustrating the contribution of categorical dependent variables.
summary: SHAPley values for dataset D3, derived from the trained SVM-3 model, quantify feature impact on performance. Color-coded regimes (red, blue, and green) indicate the influence on categorical dependent variables, demonstrating that all three categories possess equal magnitude and significant importance in the model's predictive decision-making process.

caption: Final state of the phase-field simulation showing the sintered equal-sized particles.
summary: Concluding the Test I sequence, this panel depicts the final state of the non-conserved phase-field variable evolution for two equal-sized particles. The simulation results demonstrate the morphological changes occurring during the sintering process, establishing the reference case for comparing particle evolution under different size conditions.

caption: Microhardness distribution profiles measured along the Y-axis from the bottom to the top of the specimens, illustrating variations in mechanical properties across the build height.
summary: Microhardness distribution profiles measured along the Y-axis from the bottom to the top of the specimens illustrate variations in mechanical properties across the build height. The laser-remelted specimen exhibits a smoother and more continuous profile, indicating enhanced mixing, solute redistribution, and more uniform solidification conditions compared to the as-deposited specimen.

caption: APT ion map of Alloy 625 Plus after aging at 650 °C for 8 h, showing initial Cr depletion.
summary: Following 8 hours of aging at 650 °C, the APT ion map reveals the initial formation of γ″ precipitates. This structural change is characterized by a very faint depletion of Cr within the alloy matrix, marking the onset of precipitate evolution as observed through the APT characterization technique.

caption: Temperature evolution profile recorded over a two-hour duration at the central region of the sensor's straight section.
summary: This thermal analysis plot illustrates the temperature variation measured at the center of the sensor's straight section over a two-hour period. The data indicates that the temperature increase remains minimal, specifically less than the specified threshold, confirming the thermal stability of the sensor during the observed operational timeframe.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the CO2-Solid-S sample, displayed as Nyquist and Bode plots showing phase angle peaks that suggest the estimation of two-time constants.
summary: Nyquist and Bode plots for the CO2-Solid-S sample illustrate the electrochemical response over time. The presence of two phase angle peaks at intermediate frequencies indicates that two-time constants can be estimated for this sample. These plots provide insight into the resistance and stability of the surface passive film.

caption: I-V characteristic curve of the 3D-printed PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film measured between -5 V and +5 V.
summary: The I-V curve of the 3D-printed PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film is presented over a voltage range of -5 to +5 V. This analysis reveals a low resistance Schottky behavior for the composite material at room temperature, characterizing its fundamental electronic transport properties.

caption: Scattering intensity I plotted as a function of the scattering vector q, showing the raw SAXS data profile with dashed lines representing the mathematical fitting results.
summary: Panel (a) displays the raw SAXS intensity data plotted against the scattering vector q. The experimental data profile is accompanied by dashed lines, which represent the results of fittings performed using specific mathematical equations to characterize the scattering behavior of the analyzed material samples.

caption: Binarized cross-section of the Al10SiMg sample, where black regions represent voids and white regions correspond to the metallic phase.
summary: This binarized cross-section highlights the segmentation results of the Al10SiMg sample, where black regions represent voids and white regions represent the metallic phase. The segmentation process, performed using Dragonfly software, effectively isolates the porosity from the high-density metallic bulk material based on the observed absorption contrast differences.

caption: Simulated Selected Area Electron Diffraction (SAED) pattern for the 14H phase oriented along the [11-00] zone axis.
summary: The simulated SAED pattern for the 14H phase along the [11-00] zone axis is shown. This pattern serves as a computational benchmark for the crystal structure, facilitating the interpretation of experimental diffraction data obtained from the material under investigation in this study.

caption: Magnetic phase shift map (φmag) recorded from the Py islands, with color coding representing phase values in radians.
summary: This map illustrates the magnetic phase shift contribution (φmag) recorded from the Py islands. Derived from the difference between phase image pairs, the color-coded map in radians isolates the magnetic signal, providing the quantitative basis for evaluating the magnetic induction map and understanding the magnetic state of the islands.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for scanning strategies S1-S5.
summary: This panel displays the major axis length distribution of primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite on XOY cross-sections using a combination of violin and box plots. The data compares five different scanning strategies, S1 through S5, to evaluate how melt pool interference modes influence the resulting martensite size distribution.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the CuCrZr-0.5 wt% Y2O3 composite showing dispersed Y element signals.
summary: The elemental distribution map for the CuCrZr-0.5 wt% Y2O3 composite displays the spatial arrangement of the Y element. The signals are well-dispersed throughout the matrix, supporting the observation that low doping levels of Y2O3 particles enhance the material's forming quality and mechanical strength.

caption: Cr 2p XPS core-level spectrum of the passive film formed on LPBF DSS 2205, spherical WC/W2C reinforced composites, and angular WC/W2C reinforced composites after 6 hours of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Cr 2p XPS spectra provide insight into the chromium oxidation states present in the passive films of LPBF DSS 2205 and the two types of WC/W2C reinforced composites. The data was collected following a 6-hour immersion period in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution to assess passive film composition.

caption: Absorbance spectra of a 50 mg/L methylene blue solution measured before and after 60 minutes of contact with 3D printed scaffolds in dark conditions.
summary: This panel displays the UV-Vis absorbance spectra of a 50 mg/L methylene blue solution. It compares the initial state of the solution to the state after 60 minutes of exposure to 3D printed scaffolds in the dark, illustrating the baseline adsorption performance of the materials without light activation.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification curves for Al-8.0Zn-2.5Mg-xNi alloys (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 wt%) depicting phase fraction evolution during cooling.
summary: Non-equilibrium solidification curves for Al-8.0Zn-2.5Mg-xNi alloys identify T and Al3Ni as the primary secondary phases. Thermodynamic results indicate that the solidification range and residual liquid phases at the final temperature remain largely unchanged with increasing Ni content, suggesting consistent production feasibility and excellent surface quality for these specific alloy compositions.

caption: Rheological behavior of 50 wt% CaCO3 composite resin under UV exposure, showing a decrease in storage modulus.
summary: This panel displays the rheological behavior of a 50 wt% CaCO3 composite resin upon UV light exposure. Unlike lower weight percentages, the storage modulus decreases during the curing process, suggesting a different mechanical response or structural evolution within the composite resin as the filler concentration increases.

caption: Room temperature magnetic hysteresis loop curve for the LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy specimen.
summary: This panel displays the room temperature magnetic hysteresis loop curve for the LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy. The curve characterizes the magnetic response of the material, serving as the primary data source from which critical magnetic parameters, specifically the saturation magnetization and coercivity values, are subsequently derived for the alloy.

caption: Computational models of TPMS-P and BBLS structures, displayed as 4 × 4 × 4 arrays and 1 × 1 × 1 unit cells generated via Matlab.
summary: The panel displays computational models of both TPMS-P and BBLS hollow column structures. These models are presented in 4 × 4 × 4 arrays and 1 × 1 × 1 unit cell configurations, all of which were generated using Matlab software to facilitate the comparative analysis of their structural characteristics.

caption: Bode diagram of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy in seawater containing sulfide, showing frequency-dependent impedance response.
summary: This Bode plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy in seawater containing sulfide. The data provides a frequency-dependent view of the system, allowing for the analysis of the protective properties of the surface film formed under these specific corrosive conditions compared to natural seawater.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of rBMSCs on porous alloy scaffolds after 7 days of coculture, demonstrating complete surface coverage.
summary: By the 7-day mark, live/dead staining fluorescence images indicate that rBMSCs have proliferated extensively and covered the entire surface of the porous alloy scaffolds. This observation confirms the long-term biocompatibility and suitability of the scaffold structures for supporting dense cell populations, with scale bars set at 500 μm.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the natural logarithm of the diffusion coefficient (ln D) versus the inverse of absolute temperature (1/T), used to determine the activation energy (Ea) for the NiCr system based on calculated diffusion values.
summary: The temperature dependence of the diffusion coefficient is visualized by plotting ln D against 1/T. By fitting this linear relationship, the activation energy (Ea) for the NiCr system is estimated, utilizing diffusion values calculated from the slopes of the current density plots at different temperatures.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots for LPBF TC4 alloy after varying corrosion exposure durations in 0.6 mol/L NaCl solution.
summary: LPBF TC4 alloy displays n-type semiconductor behavior across all tested corrosion exposure times in 0.6 mol/L NaCl solution. The Mott-Schottky measurements reveal how the passive film's semiconductor properties evolve with exposure duration, consistently maintaining n-type characteristics throughout the experimental period for the laser powder bed fusion processed material.

caption: Stress-strain hysteresis loop captured at half of the total fatigue lifetime, maintaining identical test conditions of 750 °C, 1% strain amplitude, and R = -1.
summary: Representing the material state at half of its fatigue lifetime, this hysteresis loop shows a 10% change compared to the initial cycle. This evolution in the stress-strain response at 750 °C and 1% strain amplitude highlights the cyclic degradation, which is critical for predicting long-term mechanical behavior under these conditions.

caption: Confusion matrix evaluating the classification performance of the microphone-CNN model on the test abnormality dataset.
summary: Microphone-CNN classification performance is presented through this confusion matrix based on the test abnormality dataset. The visualization highlights the limitations of the microphone sound-based models, which fail to accurately detect and classify powder flow anomalies, contrasting sharply with the high performance achieved by the stethoscope-based CNN model.

caption: Comparison of dry and wet effective thicknesses for polymer brushes (PBs) synthesized in microfluidic stack reactors versus standard reactors, determined via spectroscopic ellipsometry.
summary: Spectroscopic ellipsometry measurements reveal that PBs synthesized in microfluidic stack reactors are consistently thicker than those prepared in standard reactors under identical polymerization conditions. The data, accounting for a 4 nm non-swelling initiator SAM layer, demonstrate distinct thickness variations between the two reactor systems, highlighting the impact of synthesis environment on polymer growth.

caption: Water contact angle measurements for P50, PH-P50-G0.25, PH-P50-G0.5, and PH-P50-G0.7 scaffolds, indicating statistically significant differences (P < 0.05).
summary: Wettability of the PH-P50, PH-P50-G0.25, PH-P50-G0.5, and PH-P50-G0.7 scaffolds was evaluated through water contact angle testing. The results demonstrate statistically significant variations in surface hydrophilicity across the different scaffold compositions, with a P-value of less than 0.05, highlighting the impact of graphene oxide concentration on the surface properties.

caption: Chromium (Cr) elemental STEM-EDS map of the framed region in panel (b), illustrating the distribution of chromium across the dendritic and inter-dendritic phases.
summary: This chromium elemental STEM-EDS map provides a detailed view of the chromium distribution within the framed region of the sample. The map complements the iron and nickel data to characterize the chemical composition of the austenite dendrites and the metastable delta ferrite phases found in the printed material's sub-granular structure.

caption: Atomic model of the Fe-doped Ni3Al supercell, where two Ni atoms in the fifth layer are replaced by Fe atoms.
summary: Representing the Fe-doped Ni3Al supercell, this model illustrates the substitution of two Ni atoms with Fe atoms in the fifth layer of the crystal lattice. This specific configuration is used to investigate how Fe doping influences the generalized stacking fault energy within the Ni3Al system.

caption: Scalar hysteresis cycle measured on Sample E7 along the hard magnetization direction.
summary: Sample E7 displays a distinct scalar hysteresis cycle when measured along the hard magnetization axis. This measurement highlights the magnetic anisotropy of the material, contrasting the response observed along the easy direction and characterizing the magnetic properties of the sample under different field orientations.

caption: High energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern of fine Ni-based superalloy powders, demonstrating near-ideal powder diffraction characteristics.
summary: This panel displays the synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern for fine Ni-based superalloy powders. The data, obtained using high-energy synchrotron radiation at a wavelength of 0.1631 Å, indicates that the fine powder sample exhibits near-perfect powder diffraction characteristics, serving as a baseline for the structural analysis of the superalloy material.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 0.5 mM [Fe(CN)6]3-/4- in 0.1 M PBS recorded at scan rates ranging from 10 to 90 mVs-1 within a potential window of -1V to +1V.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms of 0.5 mM [Fe(CN)6]3-/4- in 0.1 M PBS were recorded at scan rates from 10 to 90 mVs-1 between -1V and +1V. The observed shift from negative to positive maximum voltage with increasing scan rates indicates a primarily diffusion-controlled electrochemical reaction process for the biosensor.

caption: Pole figures demonstrating the texture distribution and evolution within the WE43 Mg alloy during SLM processing, categorized into three distinct regions.
summary: Pole figures are utilized here to reveal the texture evolution of WE43 Mg alloy during SLM processing. The data is categorized into three distinct regions, offering a comprehensive view of the crystallographic orientation distribution resulting from the specific fabrication technique employed in the study.

caption: Load-displacement curves illustrating the mechanical response of the Al-G1 single lap joint (SLJ) specimen under loading conditions.
summary: This panel presents the load-displacement curves for the Al-G1 single lap joint. These curves characterize the mechanical behavior and structural response of the specimen as it is subjected to increasing loads, providing essential data on the joint's stiffness and deformation characteristics prior to the onset of fracture.

caption: Electron probe micro-analysis elemental distribution map showing the spatial distribution of Tantalum (Ta) within the powder mixture.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis results for Tantalum are shown to characterize the elemental distribution within the W-3.5TaC powder mixture. This map allows for the evaluation of the dispersion of the TaC additive, ensuring that the powder feedstock maintains the intended composition and uniformity required for high-quality laser powder bed fusion.

caption: Vibrational free energy and phonon DOS for fcc Co, with L-S relationship predictions (black) and full phonon calculations (red) plotted for comparison.
summary: Presented are the phonon density of states and vibrational free energy for fcc Co. The black lines represent L-S relationship predictions, while the red lines show results from full phonon calculations. This comparison characterizes the vibrational properties of the fcc Co phase in the Co-Al system.

caption: Overpotential values and corresponding Tafel plots derived from the polarization curves of Ru3Ni3 NAs and reference catalysts in acidic and alkaline electrolytes.
summary: Panel B presents the overpotential data and Tafel plots for Ru3Ni3 NAs compared to Ir/C-Pt/C. These electrochemical metrics characterize the reaction kinetics and efficiency of the water splitting process under different pH conditions, highlighting the catalytic behavior of the Ru3Ni3 NAs in both acidic and alkaline media.

caption: Cumulative (Q3) and differential (q3) particle size distribution plots for the IN718 powder, measured via optical image analysis.
summary: Particle size volume distributions for the IN718 powder are presented as cumulative (Q3) and differential (q3) plots. These distributions were determined through optical image analysis using a Camsizer X2 particle analyzer, following the ISO 13322-2 protocol, to characterize the powder feedstock used throughout the experimental study.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to SLM-processed Co-Cr alloy extracts.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the SLM-processed Co-Cr alloy group after 24 hours of exposure to extracts. The image displays the distribution of live (green) and dead (red) cells, allowing for the assessment of cellular response to the SLM-manufactured Co-Cr surface extracts after 24 hours of incubation.

caption: Visualization of overheated islands at the cutting height with their respective minimum bounding rectangles and centers of area, showing the imprinting of a displacement vector between the centers of area of two subsequent islands to model mechanical shrink lines along the build direction z.
summary: This panel shows the overheated islands at the cutting height, including their bounding rectangles and centers of area. A displacement vector is imprinted between the centers of area of successive islands. This vector serves as a boundary condition to model mechanical shrink line formation along the build direction z.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the designed alloy showing a single-phase microstructure.
summary: This dark-field TEM image confirms the single-phase nature of the designed alloy. The analysis demonstrates the absence of γ′-precipitates within the microstructure, providing direct visual evidence that the material maintains a uniform γ-structure without the formation of secondary phases typically associated with γ′-precipitate development in such alloy systems.

caption: Quasi-static tensile stress-strain response of the additively manufactured Ti64 base material, fitted with a J2 plasticity model.
summary: The tensile stress-strain response of the additively manufactured Ti64 base material is shown alongside a J2 plasticity model fit. The model, incorporating isotropic power-law hardening, yields an initial yield strength of 1082 MPa, a hardening coefficient of 793 MPa, and a hardening exponent of 0.471, accurately describing the material's mechanical behavior.

caption: Magnified view of the 984 cm-1 peak, demonstrating the disappearance of vibrational bands associated with acrylate groups after 3D printing.
summary: The 984 cm-1 spectral region shows the disappearance of specific vibrational bands after the 3D printing process. This observation, observed in both neat and CNT-loaded resins, confirms the chemical transformation of acrylate groups into a three-dimensional crosslinked network, reflecting the structural modifications induced by the curing process.

caption: Estimated elastic strain component ɛyy at a depth of 4 mm, calculated using numerical initial guesses.
summary: This panel displays the estimated elastic strain component ɛyy at a depth of 4 mm. These values are derived from numerical results used as initial guesses for experimental correction. The data represents strain evolution during the addition of five layers, starting from the 20th layer of the material specimen.

caption: Mechanical response of η-Fe2Al5 micropillars with [1,2,29] orientation, showing the yield stress marked by an arrow.
summary: Mechanical response curves for η-Fe2Al5 micropillars with [1,2,29] orientation exhibit high yield stresses exceeding 2-2.5 GPa, indicated by an arrow. These results, alongside other orientations, demonstrate that η-Fe2Al5 does not show significant size dependence of yield stress, providing essential data for calculating critical resolved shear stress values for slip systems.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni–Cr–Mo ternary system providing insight into the solidification pathways.
summary: This isothermal section of the Ni–Cr–Mo ternary system is provided to explain the formation process of the weld microstructure. It serves as a theoretical framework to interpret the solidification sequences and phase transformations that occur during the laser welding process under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Relationship between surface free energy and bond strength for PEEK specimens processed using laser treatment with different spot overlap rates.
summary: This scatter plot displays the bond strength as a function of surface free energy for PEEK samples processed at various laser spot overlap rates. Consistent with the overall trend, the bond strength increases proportionally with the surface free energy, highlighting the influence of laser overlap parameters on surface properties and adhesion.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the substrate region near the Pt–Al bond coat, showing the absence of dislocations within γ' precipitates under 300 MPa stress.
summary: This TEM image focuses on the substrate region close to the Pt–Al bond coat under a low stress amplitude of 300 MPa. A key observation is the complete absence of dislocations within the γ' precipitates in this specific area, contrasting with the dislocation activity found in the core superalloy.

caption: Ex-situ SANS profiles for the alloy aged at 550 °C for 96 h, 144 h, and 240 h, with an inset showing the corresponding IQ^2 vs Q plots.
summary: This panel displays ex-situ SANS profiles for the alloy aged at 550 °C for durations of 96 h, 144 h, and 240 h. The inset provides the IQ^2 vs Q plots for these specific aging times, illustrating the scattered intensities and structural evolution of the H-phase during the aging process.

caption: Elastic response of 3D-printed silicone (SIL30) samples represented by nominal stress versus stretch (P-λ) data up to a stretch of 2.5.
summary: This panel displays the elastic mechanical response of 3D-printed silicone (SIL30) samples. The data, plotted as nominal stress versus stretch up to λ = 2.5, demonstrates the material's initial elastic behavior. These results were obtained through simultaneous fitting of constitutive equations to experimental data, as summarized in the accompanying table.

caption: STEM image of the EQ specimen in the as-built (AB) condition, highlighting the initial morphology of strengthening precipitates.
summary: This STEM image captures the EQ specimen in the as-built condition. The microstructure exhibits larger strengthening γʹ/γʺ precipitates, consistent with the as-built state of the material. These observations provide a baseline for comparing the microstructural changes that occur during subsequent thermal processing steps like solution treatment and aging.

caption: Ranked feature importance derived from SHAP analysis, identifying the most influential variables in the dataset.
summary: Ranked feature importance is presented here, determined through SHAP analysis to quantify the relative contribution of each input variable. This visualization identifies the primary drivers within the dataset, confirming that specific material parameters, such as VEC, play a critical role in the model's predictive performance and feature hierarchy.

caption: GPA strain map corresponding to panel (a), illustrating the magnitude of the εyy strain component at the precipitate-matrix interface.
summary: This GPA strain map displays the εyy strain component for the sample shown in panel (a). The surrounding matrix is strained up to 1% to accommodate the lattice mismatch, with strain fields extending approximately 3.1 ± 2 nm away from the precipitate-matrix interface, as indicated by the white arrows.

caption: Finite element model assembly illustrating the geometric configuration, mesh discretization, applied boundary conditions, and interaction definitions used to simulate interfacial microvoid closure.
summary: This finite element model assembly provides a comprehensive representation of the simulation framework for studying interfacial microvoid closure. It incorporates detailed mesh discretization, specific boundary conditions, and interaction parameters to accurately model the mechanical behavior of microvoids, facilitating a robust analysis of their closure mechanisms under defined loading conditions.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) curve for D2 substrate material.
summary: The CCT curve depicts the phase transformation characteristics of the D2 substrate under continuous cooling conditions. Calculated using JMatPro, this plot serves as a fundamental reference for predicting the microstructural evolution of the D2 material during various cooling rates, ensuring precise control over the resulting mechanical and physical properties.

caption: Al–Si binary phase diagram illustrating the selected heat treatment temperatures relative to the eutectic and liquidus lines.
summary: This panel displays a typical binary phase diagram for the Al–Si alloy system. Four distinct heat treatment temperatures are highlighted, all positioned above the eutectic temperature but below the liquidus temperature, providing a thermodynamic basis for the subsequent microstructural analysis of the extruded Al–50Si alloy samples.

caption: Confocal micrograph of a fully cured Light Engine printed sample produced with pulsed exposure at a 33% duty cycle over a two-second on-time.
summary: Representing a fully cured specimen, this confocal micrograph shows the result of a 33% duty cycle. The sample features a uniform surface with well-defined edges and corners, comparable to high-quality specimens, confirming that the pulsed exposure method effectively achieves complete curing when the appropriate duty cycle is applied.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the plating bath 1 on glassy carbon recorded at 50 mV s-1, showing the influence of varying cathodic potential limits from -1.17 V to -1.50 V on the deposition process.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms on glassy carbon reveal that CoNi deposition in DES requires significant overpotential for nucleation and growth. Increasing the negative potential limit develops a clear reduction peak and a corresponding oxidation peak. Further negative potential extension leads to solvent reduction and a loosening of the oxidation-to-reduction charge ratio.

caption: UV–vis to NIR wavelength range absorptance spectra comparing pure Al2O3 samples and high-resolution CuO/Al2O3 ceramic composite 3D structures.
summary: This panel displays the measured absorptance spectra of pure Al2O3 and CuO/Al2O3 ceramic composite 3D structures within the UV–vis to NIR wavelength range. The data illustrates the optical performance differences between the pure ceramic and the composite structures, highlighting the impact of the CuO modification on light absorption characteristics.

caption: EBSD phase distribution map of the SLM 18Ni-300 specimen following heat treatment, showing a significant reduction in the austenite γ phase content.
summary: Following heat treatment, the EBSD phase distribution map of the SLM 18Ni-300 specimen demonstrates a microstructure that is predominantly composed of martensite α phase. The austenite γ phase content is significantly reduced to 0.1%, indicating a substantial phase transformation occurred as a result of the applied heat treatment process.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curve recorded on a glassy carbon electrode in a 1ChCl:2Urea solution at a temperature of 90 °C.
summary: This cyclic voltammetry curve illustrates the electrochemical behavior of the 1ChCl:2Urea electrolyte system at 90 °C using a glassy carbon electrode. The measurement provides essential insight into the electrochemical window and stability of the solvent, establishing the baseline performance before the introduction of metal salt precursors.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map of Re in Astra-ReRu after solution heat treatment at 1340 °C for 32 hours, showing residual inhomogeneity.
summary: After undergoing long-term solution heat treatment at 1340 °C for 32 hours, the Astra-ReRu alloy is analyzed via EPMA. Unlike the Alloy-ReRu variant, this map reveals that Astra-ReRu retains a slightly inhomogeneous distribution of Re, indicating that the chosen heat treatment parameters were insufficient to achieve complete elemental homogenization.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental fatigue life data for GH4169 alloy against predictions derived from the proposed model, T–K model, and Miner’s rule.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the proposed fatigue life model for GH4169 alloy. By comparing experimental results with predictions from the proposed model, T–K model, and Miner’s rule, the data demonstrates that the proposed model achieves good agreement with the experimental fatigue life measurements.

caption: Correlation between the W/F ratio and the elliptic parameters a, b, and h for single-layer WAAM-processed profiles.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between the W/F ratio and the geometric elliptic parameters a, b, and h for single-layer WAAM-processed profiles. The data, derived from experimental conditions in Table 1, characterizes the profile geometry, providing a quantitative basis for understanding how process parameters influence the resulting layer shape.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of homogenized AlxCuyCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys, illustrating the phase evolution across varying aluminum and copper concentrations.
summary: X-ray diffraction patterns for homogenized AlxCuyCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys are presented to characterize their crystalline structure. Analysis of these patterns reveals that low and medium aluminum content alloys consist of a mixture of FCC and BCC phases, whereas high aluminum alloys are characterized by a full BCC phase structure.

caption: Enlarged dark-field TEM view of the region marked in (b), isolating the carbide phases for targeted chemical characterization.
summary: The enlarged dark-field TEM image isolates the carbide phases, allowing for precise chemical characterization. By focusing on the spots marked in the image, researchers performed EDS analysis to confirm that these structures possess significantly higher Cr and C contents compared to the surrounding matrix areas in the corroded alloy.

caption: Confusion matrix detailing the performance of the thermal history-based approach using an SVM, resulting in a prediction accuracy of 90.5%.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the performance of the thermal history-based approach when processed via an SVM model. The analysis indicates a prediction accuracy of 90.5%. This panel is used to compare the effectiveness of thermal history-based methods against real-time approaches in the context of the reported classification results.

caption: Calculated formation free energies of various candidate oxides at 300 K under an oxygen partial pressure of 0.2 atm, determined using the Projector Augmented Wave (PAW) method.
summary: This plot displays the formation free energies for a series of candidate oxides at 300 K and an oxygen partial pressure of 0.2 atm. The data, computed via the PAW method, provides a thermodynamic assessment of these materials, serving as a key reference for evaluating their relative stability in the specified conditions.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of the cellular structure in LPBFed CoCrNi, demonstrating a uniform distribution of alloying elements and the absence of significant elemental segregation.
summary: EDS elemental mapping of the cellular structure in LPBFed CoCrNi demonstrates a uniform distribution of alloying elements. The analysis indicates no significant elemental segregation within the LPBFed CoCrNi, confirming the chemical homogeneity of the cellular structure formed during the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Supercell model constructed for QSTEM HAADF image simulation.
summary: This panel displays the supercell model utilized for the QSTEM simulation of HAADF images. The structure serves as the foundational input for computational modeling, enabling the subsequent comparison between simulated and experimental HAADF imaging results to validate the atomic-scale features observed in the material under study.

caption: Rietveld refinement results for BZT-1300 ceramic, showing the observed, calculated, and difference intensity curves.
summary: Rietveld refinement results for the BZT-1300 ceramic are illustrated, featuring the observed, calculated, and difference intensity curves. As part of the comprehensive refinement results shown in Fig. 4, this plot demonstrates the fit between the experimental diffraction data and the calculated structural model for the BZT-1300 specimen.

caption: Coefficient of friction measurements recorded for different Al-SiC composite formulations during tribological testing.
summary: Coefficient of friction data for various Al-SiC composites are presented to evaluate their tribological performance. These measurements are essential for assessing the surface interaction properties of the composites, which, when optimized through specific scan speeds and VED, contribute to the significant wear rate reductions observed in SLM-processed Al-SiC materials compared to unreinforced alloys.

caption: Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) curves comparing five models, with AUC statistics calculated from the average of five experimental runs.
summary: ROC curves for five models are plotted to compare their diagnostic performance, with AUC values of 0.96 for Deep SVDD and 0.83 for the auto-encoder. These statistics, derived from five experimental runs, provide a quantitative measure of model accuracy and robustness in distinguishing between normal and anomalous data points.

caption: Base metal microstructure characterized by a fine cellular morphology, small grain size, and high density of dislocations resulting from the rapid solidification during LPBF processing.
summary: The base metal microstructure is defined by a fine cellular structure and high dislocation density, which are direct consequences of the extremely high heating and cooling rates experienced during the LPBF process. This initial state provides the foundation for subsequent microstructural changes during the GTAW thermal cycling.

caption: Isometric views of HCP and FCC unit cells, highlighting key geometrical parameters including the c/a axial ratio.
summary: Isometric representations of HCP and FCC unit cells are shown, defining essential geometrical parameters. The c/a axial ratio, representing the relationship between the total height and the hexagon edge length, is highlighted as a critical variable that varies significantly between different metallic materials with these crystal structures.

caption: Calculated ternary Ni-Cr-Al phase diagram at 1000 °C, showing the equilibrium phase fields for the Ni-Cr-Al system.
summary: Representing the equilibrium state of the Ni-Cr-Al system at 1000 °C, this ternary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic basis for understanding phase solubility. The diagram supports findings that the γ-(Ni) phase maintains high Cr solubility and structural similarity to γ′-Ni3Al, facilitating the incorporation of significant amounts of aluminium at elevated temperatures.
