caption: Capacitive currents of NiMo@NF plotted against scan rate, comparing fresh 1 M KOH electrolyte conditions with those measured before and after a constant potential (CP) test.
summary: This plot displays capacitive currents for NiMo@NF as a function of scan rate. By comparing fresh electrolyte conditions with those before and after a CP test, the panel illustrates the electrochemical stability of the material, with data points including 95% confidence intervals to quantify the reliability of the measured capacitive parameters.

caption: Lower detector two-dimensional diffraction pattern recorded at a 487 × 195 pixel resolution with a 172 μm pixel size for the three-layer composite.
summary: The lower detector displays a two-dimensional diffraction pattern for the three-layer composite material, comprising an Al-10 wt%Zn alloy sandwiched between Al-2.5 wt%Mg alloy layers aged for 60 minutes. Featuring a 172 μm pixel size, this pattern complements the upper detector data to provide a comprehensive diffraction profile of the composite.

caption: Elastic collapse stress as a function of relative density for 2DDG and UD honeycombs, compared against the Gibson-Ashby analytical model.
summary: The elastic collapse stress of 2DDG and UD honeycombs is presented relative to their density. By plotting the experimental data alongside the Gibson-Ashby analytical formula, the graph illustrates the relationship between structural density and collapse stress, allowing for an assessment of how these specific honeycomb geometries conform to established theoretical models.

caption: Composite imaging of Saos-2 cells on untreated and 72 h etched ribbons compared to glass controls, featuring live/dead fluorescence staining, SEM morphology analysis, and CLSM actin/nuclei distribution.
summary: Saos-2 cells cultured on untreated and 72 h etched ribbons were evaluated for cytocompatibility. Live/dead staining with calcein and ethidium bromide confirms cell viability, while SEM images demonstrate flat morphology indicating successful attachment. CLSM observations further reveal the orientation and distribution of actin stress fibers and nuclei within the adhered cells.

caption: Later stage reaction state of the Au-Ge-Cu-Ni joint superimposed on the isothermal tetrahedron at 400 °C, where the interfacial NiGe phase transforms into Ni2Ge.
summary: Representing the later stage of the reaction at 400 °C, this panel shows the evolution of the interfacial products. The NiGe phase formed during the early stage undergoes a transformation into the Ni2Ge phase, as indicated by the superimposed state on the Au-Ge-Cu-Ni isothermal tetrahedron.

caption: Creep strain versus time curves for unreinforced, micrometric SiC-reinforced, and nanometric SiC-reinforced composites tested at 723 K under constant applied stress.
summary: Displayed are creep curves obtained at 723 K for three different material systems. Consistent with the findings at higher temperatures, the nanometric SiC-reinforced material shows significantly lower creep strain rates than the unreinforced and micrometric SiC-reinforced composites, confirming the effectiveness of nanometric reinforcement in enhancing creep resistance across these tested temperatures.

caption: Textural properties table summarizing average pore size, pore volume, and BET surface area for Fe@C, FeCo@C, FeNi@C, and FeMn@C composites.
summary: This table highlights the significant influence of the secondary metal element on the porosity of FeM@C composites. Notably, the FeNi@C composite exhibits a larger average pore size but a smaller BET surface area compared to the other FeM@C variants, illustrating how metal composition modulates the final textural characteristics.

caption: Lattice constant of L1 2 Ni,Fe 3 Al as a function of Ni atomic concentration, comparing results from the developed potential and DFT calculations.
summary: This panel displays the lattice constant of L1 2 Ni,Fe 3 Al structures as a function of Ni atomic concentration. The data, derived from both developed potential and DFT calculations, shows a linear decrease in the intermediate concentration regions, consistent with Vegard’s law regarding alloy composition and lattice parameters.

caption: Thermomagnetic curve of unreacted SmCo26 showing a single Curie point.
summary: The thermomagnetic curve for the unreacted SmCo26 sample displays a single Curie point at 825 °C. This characteristic temperature represents the primary SmCo magnetic phase, serving as a baseline reference for comparing the magnetic behavior of the material before undergoing long-term reaction processes.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for AWS ER2594 feedstock, generated using JmatPro® software to illustrate phase evolution during cooling.
summary: AWS ER2594 feedstock phase transformation behavior is characterized through a continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram. This diagram, obtained via JmatPro® software, provides a comprehensive overview of the phase evolution expected during the cooling process, serving as a critical reference for understanding the microstructural development of the weld material.

caption: SAED pattern corresponding to the Cr2B nanoboride phase.
summary: This SAED pattern is identified as belonging to the Cr2B nanoboride phase. By analyzing this diffraction data, the presence and crystal structure of the chromium-rich nanoborides are confirmed, establishing their identity as the secondary particles observed decorating the grain boundaries within the boron-modified alloy.

caption: Specific strength comparison of TiC-modified Al–Mg–Li alloy against previously reported additive manufactured Al–Li alloys.
summary: Specific strength values for the TiC-modified Al–Mg–Li alloy are compared against various previously reported additive manufacturing Al–Li alloys. The data demonstrates that the TiC-modified alloy achieves superior specific strength performance, highlighting the effectiveness of the modification strategy in enhancing the mechanical efficiency of these additively manufactured materials.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of La2MgNi9 alloy annealed at 1223 K for 6 hours, revealing a multi-phase microstructure composed of (La,Mg)Ni3, (La,Mg)2Ni7, and LaNi5 phases.
summary: This SEM micrograph displays the multi-phase microstructure of La2MgNi9 alloy after annealing at 1223 K for 6 hours. The image identifies the presence of three distinct phases: (La,Mg)Ni3, (La,Mg)2Ni7, and LaNi5, which are distributed throughout the material as a result of the high-temperature heat treatment process.

caption: Displaced atom count as a function of time for NiCr alloy under 30 keV Ni cascade conditions, showing trajectories for classical MD, electronic-stopping-only, and 2T-MD models.
summary: This graph tracks the number of displaced atoms in NiCr during 30 keV Ni cascades. By comparing classical MD, electronic-stopping-only, and 2T-MD models, it reveals how different simulation frameworks predict defect formation. The findings highlight the specific damage evolution characteristics for the NiCr binary alloy system under these conditions.

caption: Lorenz-corrected SAXS scattering curves showing variations in peak intensity and area across starch samples.
summary: Lorenz-corrected SAXS curves illustrate the structural differences between starch samples. The data indicates that the peak intensity and area for MRS and MSS starches are notably lower than those observed for CRS and WCS, suggesting a less ordered lamellar structure in the former samples.

caption: Color-coded phase legend and orientation direction indicator used for interpreting the EBSD phase maps in the TC4-Ti48Al transition zone analysis.
summary: This panel provides the essential color-coded phase legend and orientation direction indicator required to interpret the EBSD maps presented in the figure. It serves as the reference guide for identifying the specific alpha, alpha2, and gamma phases and their respective crystallographic orientations across the transition zone regions.

caption: Chronoamperometric stability responses of Ni3FeN, Ni3Fe alloy, RuO2, and Pt/C catalysts at 0.7 V in O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH, showing the percentage of current retained over time.
summary: Chronoamperometric testing reveals the long-term stability of the catalysts at 0.7 V. Ni3FeN demonstrates superior durability with only a 5.7% current loss after 12,000 seconds, significantly outperforming the Ni3Fe alloy, RuO2, and commercial Pt/C, which exhibit higher current density losses of 11.2%, 9.7%, and 25.5%, respectively.

caption: Corrosion fatigue crack growth rate (da/dN) versus stress intensity factor range (ΔK) for three oil-grade alloy 718 specimens tested in 21 wt.% NaCl solution at 80 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the crack growth behavior of three oil-grade alloy 718 specimens in a concentrated 21 wt.% NaCl environment at 80 °C. Regression fits show that the aging-treated Alloy 718–OSA and Alloy 718–TSA specimens maintain lower crack growth rates compared to the Alloy 718–SA specimen throughout testing.

caption: Dispersion relation of the negative regulation MRM under varying external magnetic field strengths, showing a reduction in the starting frequency of the band gap as the field intensity increases.
summary: This panel illustrates the influence of an external magnetic field on the band gap of the negative regulation MRM. As the magnetic field strength increases, the starting frequency of the band gap decreases, a phenomenon attributed to the reduction of the LMRE part stiffness under the applied magnetic field.

caption: Surface topography of a 316L stainless steel specimen exhibiting a measured arithmetic mean roughness (Sa) of 4.33 μm.
summary: Surface topography of a 316L stainless steel specimen exhibiting a measured arithmetic mean roughness (Sa) of 4.33 μm. This measurement was obtained using a 3D optical surface profiler following a grinding process, characterizing the surface finish of the specimen as part of a comparative study of four distinct roughness levels.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness profile for the L-DED Ti55531 alloy modified with 0.10 wt% boron.
summary: This panel illustrates the nanoindentation hardness results for the L-DED Ti55531 alloy with a 0.10 wt% boron addition. The data serves to elucidate the contribution of specific phases to the material's strength, allowing for a comprehensive evaluation of how varying boron concentrations affect the mechanical hardness of the Ti55531 alloy.

caption: Cross-sectional view of 316L powder particles revealing internal pores with diameters ranging from 100 to 200 nm.
summary: Cross-sectional analysis of the 316L powder via secondary electron imaging highlights the presence of internal structural defects. Specifically, small pores with diameters measuring approximately 100–200 nm are observed within the spherical particles, indicating the internal porosity characteristic of the feedstock material used in this study.

caption: Ashby chart comparing the tensile strength and thermal conductivity of the experimental Al–2.5Fe–2Cu alloy against various reported literature values.
summary: This Ashby plot benchmarks the experimental Al–2.5Fe–2Cu alloy by mapping its tensile strength against thermal conductivity. By comparing these mechanical and thermal properties with a wide range of reported results from existing literature, the chart highlights the performance trade-offs and relative standing of the PBF-LB-produced alloy within the broader materials science landscape.

caption: Distribution of SHAP values for various compositional features, where the horizontal axis represents the contribution of each feature to the model's hardness predictions.
summary: This panel displays the distribution of SHAP values for different compositional features. The horizontal axis quantifies the contribution of each feature to the model's hardness predictions. These values illustrate how individual elements influence the output, providing insight into the model's decision-making process regarding alloy hardness.

caption: Calculated TTT curve for γ'' and γ′ phases at position 2, derived from STEM-EDS compositional data.
summary: This TTT diagram illustrates the calculated precipitation kinetics for γ'' and γ′ phases at position 2. Simulation results indicate that the minimum precipitation times are 3006 s for γ'' and 1003 s for γ′ phases, respectively, within the aging temperature range of 600 to 850 °C, based on the EDS analysis.

caption: Experimental inverse pole figure (IPF) map obtained from the x–y plane for a specimen subjected to a random scan strategy.
summary: This experimental inverse pole figure map characterizes the crystallographic texture resulting from a random scan strategy. By utilizing MTEX software, the analysis focuses on the grain orientation distribution, excluding baseplate-influenced grains to provide a clear view of the texture development within the material's x–y plane.

caption: Tafel polarization (E-logI) plot for amorphous-nanocrystalline and crystalline alloys measured in a 5% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel displays the potentiodynamic polarization behavior of amorphous-nanocrystalline and crystalline alloy samples tested in a 5% NaCl electrolyte. The Tafel plot, representing the relationship between potential and the logarithm of current density, illustrates the electrochemical corrosion characteristics of these materials under saline environmental conditions.

caption: Arrhenius-style plot of Cr self-diffusion coefficients in Ni-Cr alloys, comparing literature-derived linear fits with simulation data for Ni-5Cr and Ni-20Cr compositions.
summary: This plot displays Cr self-diffusion coefficients in Ni-Cr alloys. It compares literature-based linear fits against simulation results for Ni-5Cr and Ni-20Cr. Data points include single-vacancy simulations rescaled by vacancy concentration and simulations with 16 vacancies. Calculated diffusion coefficients show improved agreement with experimental values compared to unscaled single-vacancy results.

caption: Summary table detailing the experimental parameters and specimen count for the 15 samples evaluated during the transverse shear testing program.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive summary of the 15 specimens evaluated during the transverse shear test program. It serves as a reference for the experimental data, documenting the specific conditions and parameters applied to each of the tested samples to ensure consistent and accurate mechanical analysis.

caption: Galvanostatic discharge-charge profiles for the CCC interlayer battery at various C-rates, showing the evolution of potential plateaus.
summary: Galvanostatic discharge-charge curves for the CCC interlayer battery are presented at different rates. The data reveals that the discharge plateau at the lower potential is significantly shortened as the C-rate increases, which indicates a reduction in Li2S deposition during the electrochemical process at higher current densities.

caption: Strain distribution profiles along the central voxel bar for friction-welded specimens subjected to various heat treatments (Welded, T4, T6, T7) at 75% of their respective tensile strengths.
summary: Strain profiles extracted along the central voxel bar reveal distinct mechanical responses for different heat treatments. The non-heat-treated welded specimen exhibits the highest strain of 1.6% despite a lower nominal stress of 207 MPa, whereas the T6-treated specimen sustains a higher load of 254 MPa with lower relative strain.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles for Mg55Ni45, Mg55Pd3Ni42, and Mg55Pd4Ni41 alloys, showing discharge capacities of 488.65, 543.01, and 564.6 mAh/g, respectively.
summary: This panel displays the charge-discharge curves for three milled alloys. The electrochemical testing reveals that the discharge capacity increases with palladium substitution, reaching values of 488.65 mAh/g for the base alloy, 543.01 mAh/g for the Mg55Pd3Ni42 alloy, and 564.6 mAh/g for the Mg55Pd4Ni41 alloy, indicating improved electrochemical performance.

caption: Mo K-edge XANES spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7.
summary: This panel shows the Mo K-edge XANES spectra for Ni Alloy 59, collected using total reflection geometry at a neutral pH of 7. These spectra are part of a broader study investigating the surface electronic states of the alloy under varying environmental conditions using Refle-XAFS techniques.

caption: XRD pattern of EBM-PDME prepared MPC1 after dehydrogenation, illustrating the structural state of the alloy following the removal of hydrogen.
summary: The XRD pattern for EBM-PDME prepared MPC1 after dehydrogenation provides insight into the final structural state of the alloy. This analysis captures the diffraction characteristics of the material after the hydrogen removal process, completing the comparative study of the alloy's phase evolution.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of Hastelloy X powders, indicating a range of 48–120 μm.
summary: The particle size distribution of the Hastelloy X powders was analyzed three times using a Malvern Mastersizer 2000 Particle Size Analyzer. The data indicates that the powder particles fall within a size range of 48–120 μm, providing essential information for optimizing the laser directed energy deposition process parameters.

caption: Maximum load variation trends plotted against different roughness levels for indentation depths of 1500 nm, 2000 nm, and 3000 nm.
summary: This panel displays the variation in maximum load as a function of different roughness levels during nanoindentation. The data is presented for three distinct indentation depths: 1500 nm, 2000 nm, and 3000 nm, illustrating how surface roughness influences the load-bearing response of the material under varying penetration depths.

caption: Loss curve representing the training progress of the improved DeepLab V3+ model over 50 epochs.
summary: The loss curve illustrates the training performance of the improved DeepLab V3+ model across 50 epochs. Loss values are explicitly marked at 5-epoch intervals, providing a clear visualization of the model's convergence behavior and training stability throughout the entire optimization process for the segmentation task.

caption: Chemical structure of the sterol molecule cholesterol.
summary: Cholesterol is depicted through its chemical structure in this panel. As a key component in the lipid mixture, this structural model clarifies the molecular geometry of the sterol, which is critical for understanding its interaction with other lipid components and its influence on the physical properties of the system.

caption: Lateral principal strain distribution map for an RVE with a lattice-to-matrix stiffness ratio of 1.0 under vertical compression.
summary: Representing a balanced stiffness condition where the ratio is 1.0, this panel visualizes the lateral principal strain distribution under vertical load. The map highlights how the auxetic lattice and cementitious matrix deform together, demonstrating the strain field characteristics when both components possess equivalent stiffness properties within the RVE structure.

caption: IPF map of LP-DED HX specimen tested at 21 °C, confirming slip traces coincide with {111} planes.
summary: This IPF map of the LP-DED HX specimen tested at 21 °C provides crystallographic context for the observed slip. EBSD scans confirm that the slip traces coincide with the {111} planes, providing evidence of the cyclic slip behavior occurring near the fatigue crack initiation site.

caption: Segmenter model output on a 1280 by 960 pixel micrograph, highlighting misclassified pixels in red.
summary: This panel displays the output of a segmenter model checkpoint from the 5000th iteration, evaluated on a large-scale micrograph. Misclassified pixels are highlighted in red to visualize performance errors. The model struggled with small, diluted carbide particles at the bottom, which were misclassified due to their dense structure resembling other carbide features.

caption: Bar chart comparing the duration of the initial wear regime (DR1) across different scanning strategies, highlighting that the Ang90 strategy results in the longest duration.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the duration of the initial wear regime (DR1) for various scanning strategies. Analysis of the data reveals that the Ang90 strategy exhibits the longest duration compared to other tested scanning methods, providing a clear quantitative comparison of the initial wear behavior across different processing conditions.

caption: ODF plots at ɸ2=0° and ɸ2=45° for the C-HT sample, highlighting texture evolution in the left, centre, and right areas after high-temperature testing.
summary: High-temperature testing of the C-HT sample results in a transformation of the original Cube and Rotated Cube texture components. These are replaced by Goss and Brass textures in both the centre and side regions of the disc, characterized by deviations of approximately ±6° from the ideal orientations.

caption: Optical transmittance spectra of annealed Ce-doped YAG thin films (samples A–H) deposited on quartz substrates via double hollow cathode discharge, compared against a bare quartz reference.
summary: This plot displays the optical transmittance spectra for Ce-doped YAG thin films labeled A through H. A characteristic Ce3+ absorption band appears near 455 nm. Samples F–H exhibit reduced transmittance and strong absorption below 400 nm, likely due to excessive cerium loading and the potential formation of a CeO2 phase.

caption: UV–Vis absorbance spectrum of the PEGdiPDA crosslinker, demonstrating the spectral changes associated with photo-degradation reactions under UV irradiation.
summary: The UV–Vis absorbance spectrum of the PEGdiPDA crosslinker confirms the occurrence of photo-degradation reactions. By monitoring the spectral changes during UV exposure, the data indicates that the chemical structure of the crosslinker is actively modified, supporting the mechanism of light-triggered bond cleavage within the hydrogel network.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the variant pair A–B with λ ≈ 0.1, showing paired lamellae with a width of approximately 50 nm.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the microstructure of a variant pair A–B in a martensitic material where λ is approximately 0.1. The observation reveals that the width of the paired lamellae within a single variant increases to about 50 nm, characterizing the structural morphology under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Surface electric current characteristics of oriented SiC whisker composites.
summary: Surface electric current characteristics of oriented SiC whisker composites are shown. The data demonstrates that the electric current increases exponentially with voltage, confirming the nonlinear conductivity of the oriented SiC whisker composites. This panel serves as the reference for setting surface conductivity parameters in related analytical models.

caption: Surface roughness map for surfaces parallel to the building plane in samples with high layer thickness (tl).
summary: Quantitative mapping of surface roughness for surfaces parallel to the building plane is shown for samples processed with high layer thickness. This visualization provides a clear representation of the expected trends across the process window, allowing for an evaluation of how high layer thickness influences the resulting surface texture.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of Inconel 625 alloy specimens immersed in phosphoric acid solutions of varying concentrations.
summary: This plot displays the potentiodynamic polarization behavior of Inconel 625 when exposed to phosphoric acid at different concentrations. These electrochemical measurements are used to evaluate the corrosion resistance of the alloy, providing critical data on how varying acid concentrations influence the material's electrochemical response and surface stability during the polarization process.

caption: Orientation distribution function (ODF) at ϕ2 = 0, 45, and 65° for Haynes® 282® alloy in the as-received solution-annealed (SSA) condition.
summary: The as-received SSA condition of the Haynes® 282® alloy exhibits a random annealing texture. Analysis of the ODF sections at ϕ2 = 0, 45, and 65° reveals a lack of strong preferred orientation, with only a slightly pronounced Shear 1 {001}<110> component present in the microstructure.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the phase labeled H, providing crystallographic information for the identified interdendritic region.
summary: The SAED pattern for region H provides critical crystallographic data necessary for phase identification. By analyzing this diffraction pattern, researchers can characterize the specific phase present in the interdendritic region, contributing to the overall structural understanding of the material's microstructure as observed in the corresponding HAADF-TEM image.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profiles showing the mass response of hydrogen-based molecules as a function of increasing temperature for both charged and uncharged specimens.
summary: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profiles illustrate the mass response of hydrogen-based molecules released from charged and uncharged specimens during heating. The data reveals a distinct trap site at approximately 400 °C, which is observed in both as-received and hydrogen-charged samples, confirming the presence of strong hydrogen trap sites within the material.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of iron at the top section of the PSE + L5 processed titanium alloy.
summary: Top section EDS mapping of the PSE + L5 processed titanium alloy reveals the spatial distribution of iron. The results confirm that the Ti3662 alloy maintains uniform iron distribution at this location, further validating the success of the multiple homogenization processes in achieving chemical consistency throughout the entire alloy specimen.

caption: Detailed HRTEM view of the precipitate-matrix interface, with a red dotted box indicating the region selected for further structural analysis.
summary: This high-resolution TEM image focuses on the interface between the precipitate and the matrix. The area enclosed by the red dotted box is specifically targeted for inverse fast Fourier transform analysis to determine the crystal lattice parameters and structural relationship between the precipitate and the surrounding steel matrix.

caption: CNA visualization of Model B at 500 K and 0.8 loading, illustrating the transition to a rough fracture surface and void nucleation at the crack tip.
summary: At 500 K and 0.8 loading, Model B exhibits a significant change in fracture behavior. The fracture surface evolves from a smooth morphology to a rough state, which is accompanied by the nucleation of voids at the crack tip, indicating temperature-dependent stress accommodation and defect formation mechanisms.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of CNF 50% displaying the topographical features of the cellulose nanofibrils.
summary: Atomic force microscopy image of CNF 50% displaying the topographical features of the cellulose nanofibrils. Analysis of the AFM images and the height distribution graph confirms that all CNFs samples, including this one, exhibit a consistent height distribution within the range of 1.5–3 nm, indicating effective nanofibrillation of the cellulose.

caption: Confusion matrix evaluating the classification performance of the MobileNetV2 architecture in identifying thermal defect patterns.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the classification performance of the MobileNetV2 architecture when identifying thermal defect patterns. The results demonstrate that this lightweight model maintains high classification accuracy, confirming its effectiveness for detecting defects while remaining computationally efficient enough for practical implementation in edge deployment scenarios.

caption: Creep rate analysis for unreinforced-7775-Al at 673 K, plotted as ε ˙ 1/n against applied stress σ with a stress exponent of n = 5.
summary: This panel presents the creep rate data for unreinforced-7775-Al at 673 K, utilizing a stress exponent of n = 5. The plot of ε ˙ 1/n versus applied stress σ characterizes the creep deformation characteristics of the unreinforced material, facilitating a comparison of mechanical behavior under different assumed stress exponent values.

caption: Elongation at break plotted against metal content for filaments utilizing single-polymer binders, specifically PE or PLA matrices.
summary: This plot illustrates the elongation at break as a function of metal content for metal filaments (Ni and Fe) using single-polymer binders. The data specifically highlights the mechanical performance of filaments composed of either PE or PLA matrices, providing a baseline for comparing the ductility of single-polymer binder systems.

caption: Energy absorption capacity versus relative density for stochastic and periodic cellular structures, fitted with Gibson-Ashby scaling power law models.
summary: Energy absorption performance is evaluated against relative density for various cellular structures. The experimental results, covering a density range of 12.4% to 35.6%, are fitted using the Gibson-Ashby scaling power law. This plot highlights the relationship between structural density and the energy dissipation capabilities of the tested stochastic and periodic lattices.

caption: O 1s XPS spectral region displaying three features associated with lattice oxygen, surface-chemisorbed hydroxyls or carbonates, and adsorbed oxygen species.
summary: Three features are observed in the O 1s spectral region: a peak at 529.7 eV for lattice oxygen, a peak at 531.2 eV for surface-chemisorbed hydroxyls or carbonates and surface defects, and a peak at 532.9 eV attributed to adsorbed or chemisorbed oxygen species like O2 or H2O.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the parabolic oxidation rate constants (kp) for 300 series austenitic stainless steels in steam environments across varying pressures, comparing coarse-grain and fine-grain alloy behaviors.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays parabolic oxidation rates for 300 series stainless steels in steam. It compares literature data for coarse-grain and fine-grain alloys across a range of pressures. Fine-grain alloys often exhibit higher corrosion rates than at atmospheric pressure, sometimes approaching the behavior of coarse-grain alloys due to varying nucleation events.

caption: FTIR spectra of PVA, CSF, indomethacin, PC5.0, PC7.5, P–I, PC5.0-I, and PC7.5-I samples.
summary: This figure presents the FTIR spectra for a series of materials, including raw components like PVA, CSF, and indomethacin, alongside various composite formulations such as PC5.0, PC7.5, P–I, PC5.0-I, and PC7.5-I. These spectroscopic results provide a comprehensive overview of the chemical composition and structural characteristics of the selected samples.

caption: Distribution of yielding responses categorized by coupon extraction angle, showing that specimens with inclined yield plateaus predominantly feature angles of 30° or greater.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the distribution of yielding responses based on coupon extraction angles. Data indicates that specimens exhibiting inclined yield plateaus are characterized by angles of at least 30°. These specific configurations account for 8%, 23%, 7%, and 62% of the observed yielding responses within the analyzed dataset.

caption: Specific strength comparison of high-temperature alloys utilized in turbomachinery applications, adapted from existing literature.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific strength of various high-temperature alloys commonly used in turbomachinery. By comparing these materials, the figure provides a foundational assessment of performance capabilities for components subjected to extreme thermal and mechanical environments, highlighting the material selection criteria necessary for advanced aerospace and power generation applications.

caption: Conceptual design of the wall structure intended for 3D concrete printing (3DCP) buildability assessment.
summary: This schematic illustrates the designed wall structure used for 3D concrete printing. The geometry is specifically engineered to facilitate the quantification of buildability, incorporating considerations for early-age creep. The structure features a defined length of 350 mm, a width of 15 mm, and a layer height of 4 mm.

caption: Reflection loss curves for CNFs/SiBCN ceramics featuring four distinct structural configurations, annealed at 1300 °C with 6 wt% CNFs.
summary: These reflection loss curves show the performance of CNFs/SiBCN ceramics. The materials exhibit an ultrabroad effective absorbing bandwidth ranging from 7.6 to 40 GHz, with a minimum reflection loss of −46 dB at 9.08 GHz, attributed to the defect-rich structure of the carbon nanofibers incorporated into the ceramic matrix.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PGA isolated from GACam after 3 hours of reaction at 190 °C, illustrating the relative abundance of cyclic and linear chain populations.
summary: Representing the PGA polycondensate obtained from GACam after 3 hours at 190 °C, this mass spectrum demonstrates that cyclic and linear chains remain present in nearly equal quantities. The profile is noted to be almost identical to the polycondensate obtained from GAMes under the same thermal conditions.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the Bi1.8Ni0.2Se3 matrix, revealing the presence of NiSe2 inclusions embedded within the host structure.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the Bi1.8Ni0.2Se3 sample provides direct visual evidence of the microstructure. The micrograph confirms that NiSe2 particles are successfully embedded within the Bi2Se3 matrix, establishing the composite nature of the material and providing a foundation for further structural analysis of the individual phases.

caption: Calculated PDOS for Fe, O, and La atoms at the Fe/La2O3 interface.
summary: This plot shows the PDOS of Fe atoms, O atoms, and La atoms at the interface of the Fe/La2O3 pre-nucleation model. The data provides insight into the electronic state distribution of the constituent atoms at the interface between the iron and the lanthanum oxide substrate.

caption: Schematic representation of the powder spreading simulation model setup, featuring periodic boundaries along the Y direction and defined computational domain dimensions of 2.4 × 0.7 × 0.7 mm.
summary: This panel illustrates the geometric configuration for the powder spreading simulation. The model incorporates periodic boundary conditions along the Y-axis within a computational domain measuring 2.4 × 0.7 × 0.7 mm. This setup provides the foundational framework for analyzing the physical dynamics of the powder spreading process in the simulation.

caption: Latent component Z2 derived from original datasets (900–1200 °C/0.001–10 s−1) and additional datasets (900–1200 °C/0.1 s−1), with blue symbols highlighting the correlation with normalized peak stress.
summary: This panel identifies the physical significance of Z2 by comparing original and additional datasets. The blue symbols and lines represent Z2 values from additional datasets, which align closely with normalized peak stress patterns. This correlation, supported by an R2 of 0.9971, validates the AE-PN framework's predictive robustness.

caption: Schmid factor distribution histogram for as-deposited Ti–6Al–4V alloy measured 5 mm from the fracture site, representing the state before deformation.
summary: This histogram displays the Schmid factor distribution for as-deposited Ti–6Al–4V alloy at a distance of 5 mm from the fracture. As a physical quantity, the Schmid factor describes the activation probability of slip systems, providing critical insight into the slip system activation during the initial stages of tensile deformation.

caption: SEM-EDX elemental distribution map highlighting the chemical composition in the vicinity of a crack.
summary: SEM-EDX analysis of the crack region provides detailed insights into the local chemical environment. The mapping indicates a distinct local enrichment of Ta and Hf elements at the edge of the cracks, suggesting that compositional variations or segregation play a significant role in the observed crack propagation behavior during testing.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of deformed CrCoNi at 77 K, illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution along the rolling plane.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the crystallographic orientation of deformed CrCoNi at 77 K along the rolling plane. The orientation data provides insight into the microstructural evolution and texture development under cryogenic deformation conditions, serving as a basis for understanding the material's mechanical response and dislocation behavior at low temperatures.

caption: AFM 3D chorography of the COCA2 coversheet surface.
summary: This panel displays the AFM 3D chorography of the COCA2 coversheet. The visualization provides a detailed surface roughness measurement, characterizing the topography of the material. This data was procured from AFM 3D chorography, illustrating the surface features and structural characteristics of the COCA2 specimen as part of the comparative analysis.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the standardized effects of various input parameters on the tensile strength.
summary: The Pareto chart presented here illustrates the standardized effects of different input parameters on tensile strength. By ranking these effects, the plot identifies which variables exert the most significant influence on the mechanical performance, providing a clear visualization of the relative importance of each factor in the tensile strength model.

caption: SHAP explainability plot illustrating the global summary of feature impacts for the entropy (ΔS) model predictions.
summary: This SHAP plot displays the global summary of feature contributions for the entropy model. Through the application of SHapely Additive Prediction values, the visualization identifies the key drivers behind the model's entropy predictions, facilitating a deeper understanding of the underlying factors influencing the thermodynamic model's performance.

caption: Effective plastic strain contours for homogeneous yielding (HY) at three stages of overall strain, showing the full distribution and various cross-sectional cuts.
summary: This panel displays effective plastic strain contours for homogeneous yielding at three distinct stages of overall deformation. The visualization includes both full-field distributions and specific cross-sectional cuts to illustrate the internal strain state. These results demonstrate the robustness of the FFT solution during significant local porosity growth and plastic strain localization.

caption: Ashby-style plot comparing ultimate tensile strength versus elongation to failure for additively manufactured materials, highlighting variations induced by different scan strategies and build orientations.
summary: This Ashby-style plot illustrates the mechanical performance of additively manufactured materials by mapping ultimate tensile strength against elongation to failure. The data demonstrates that these mechanical properties are significantly influenced by the specific scan strategy employed and the build orientation of the specimens during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Continuous temperature profile and phase field distribution along the A–B line, calculated using a temperature-dependent free energy functional.
summary: This panel displays a bell-shaped, continuous temperature distribution across the melt pool, achieved through a temperature-dependent free energy functional. The profile demonstrates a smooth transition between liquid and solid phases, with a spatial lead of the temperature profile relative to the liquid phase due to differences in thermal and chemical diffusivity.

caption: Comparison of transformation enthalpies and enthalpy ratios for L-PBF samples oriented horizontally (H-built) and vertically (V-built) during austenitic and martensitic phase transitions.
summary: This plot illustrates the transformation enthalpies and enthalpy ratios for L-PBF samples with different build orientations. Analysis reveals that H-built samples consistently exhibit lower transition enthalpies and enthalpy ratios compared to their V-built counterparts, highlighting the significant influence of manufacturing orientation on the thermal transformation characteristics of the material.

caption: Weighted average concentrations of 18 transition metal elements at Ni grain boundaries, predicted for an initial bulk concentration of 0.01 at% across varying temperatures.
summary: Representing the lowest initial bulk concentration of 0.01 at%, this panel displays the predicted grain boundary concentrations for 18 transition metals. Consistent with the trends observed in panels (a) through (c), the concentrations of Mn, Fe, and Co remain stable with increasing temperature, reflecting the general segregation behavior of these elements.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map at approximately 0.15 true strain, showing overall low values indicative of minimal intragranular misorientation.
summary: The kernel average misorientation map at approximately 0.15 true strain displays low values across the microstructure. This observation supports the conclusion that the material undergoes homogeneous plastic deformation with minimal intragranular misorientation gradients, reflecting a stable microstructural response to the applied uniaxial tensile strain at this early stage.

caption: Binary Ti-Cu phase diagram illustrating the solidification range of beta-Ti and the eutectoid transformation point.
summary: This binary Ti-Cu phase diagram highlights critical compositions and temperatures, specifically showing that beta-Ti solidifies between 0 and 43 wt. % Cu. The diagram indicates that significant constitutional supercooling occurs in hypereutectoid compositions, while thermal cycling near the 7.5 wt. % Cu eutectoid point facilitates microstructural refinement during solid-state transformations.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of contact lenses following immersion in a 3 mM gold precursor concentration.
summary: This plot displays the optical absorption characteristics of the hydrogel contact lens after treatment with a 3 mM gold precursor solution. The spectrum provides data on the light absorption properties resulting from the in situ gold reduction process within the hydrogel matrix at this specific concentration.

caption: TEM image of the Fe3Ni8/Pal-700-0.0 catalyst, revealing significant coke deposition on the surface that covers active sites and hinders contact with toluene.
summary: The TEM image of the Fe3Ni8/Pal-700-0.0 catalyst highlights the presence of substantial coke deposition on the catalyst surface. This accumulation of carbonaceous material effectively covers the active metal sites, thereby hindering their contact with the toluene reactant and negatively impacting the overall catalytic performance.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of zone A, exhibiting a distinct nano-polycrystalline ring characteristic.
summary: The SAED pattern obtained from zone A reveals a distinct nano-polycrystalline ring. This diffraction feature confirms the presence of polycrystalline material within this specific region of the interface, providing essential information regarding the structural state of the grains observed in the bright-field TEM analysis.

caption: Combined neutron and X-ray diffraction data for the 45B C4 specimen at location L1, where surface-sensitive X-ray measurements are integrated with bulk-sensitive neutron diffraction results.
summary: This figure presents a comprehensive diffraction analysis of the 45B C4 material at location L1. By combining neutron diffraction data with surface-specific X-ray measurements, the plot provides a multi-scale structural characterization. This integrated approach allows for a more complete understanding of the material's crystalline properties across different depths.

caption: Normalized UV-visible absorption spectrum for O-12 in acetonitrile, noting the absence of a corresponding fluorescence signal.
summary: The normalized UV-visible absorption spectrum for O-12 in acetonitrile is displayed. Unlike the other compounds in this series, O-12 exhibits no detectable fluorescence signal, indicating distinct photophysical behavior regarding its excited state relaxation pathways compared to the fluorescent counterparts analyzed in the study.

caption: Experimental configuration for the DYN-C-L12.5 and DYN-C-L3 specimens mounted within the Split-Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) apparatus, featuring 3D-printed supports to ensure precise alignment of steel plates and specimens on the bar ends.
summary: This photograph illustrates the experimental setup for testing DYN-C-L12.5 and DYN-C-L3 specimens using a Split-Hopkinson Pressure Bar. Custom 3D-printed supports are utilized to maintain the accurate positioning of steel plates and specimens against the bar ends, ensuring consistent alignment and reliable mechanical testing conditions during the high-strain rate evaluation process.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectra of 20 nM Qdots in human plasma, comparing the performance of the first seven distinct design iterations.
summary: This photoluminescence spectrum shows the fluorescence response of 20 nM Qdots in human plasma across seven different designs. Based on peak intensities, the T-7 design demonstrated the most optimal performance, followed by T-3, which is consistent with the results obtained from the transmission measurements.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the LSV data, providing insight into the reaction kinetics of the catalyst samples.
summary: Tafel slope analysis was conducted to probe the reaction kinetics of the catalyst samples. By examining the Tafel plots, the study evaluates the charge transfer behavior and the efficiency of the oxygen evolution reaction, confirming the kinetic advantages provided by the specific synthesis method employed for the catalyst.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) heat flow curves for the as-built GH4099 Ni-based superalloy during heating and cooling cycles.
summary: This DSC analysis characterizes the thermal behavior of the as-built GH4099 Ni-based superalloy. The plot displays heat flow as a function of temperature, capturing the thermal response during both heating and cooling processes. These measurements provide essential data regarding phase transformations and thermal stability prior to any subsequent heat treatment.

caption: Contour plot of Cooling 1 temperature distribution for a 2.5 mm layer height sample.
summary: Represented here is the Cooling 1 temperature contour plot for a sample processed with a 2.5 mm layer height. This visualization is part of a systematic analysis of printing parameters, demonstrating how varying layer heights influence the inter-layer temperature profiles during the fabrication process of the DOE samples.

caption: Photograph of the printhead assembly, showcasing the mounted nozzle and a representative finished foam sample produced by the system.
summary: This photograph displays the printhead assembly, which includes the core-shell nozzle mounted for the printing process. A finished foam sample is visible, demonstrating the output of the fabrication setup. The nozzle is mounted on the printhead to facilitate the controlled extrusion of the monomer ink and gas.

caption: Detailed configuration of the grinding wheel positioning and actuation mechanism, showing the stepper motor interface used to manipulate the protective coolant sleeve.
summary: This panel details the grinding wheel positioning and actuation mechanism. A stepper motor is utilized to grip the protective coolant sleeve, which allows the system to force the spindle into the workpiece without inhibiting the rotation of the grinding wheel, ensuring precise control during the polishing process within the channel.

caption: Simulated HRTEM image generated for a non-overlapped twin structure.
summary: Simulated HRTEM imaging for a non-overlapped twin provides a theoretical benchmark for interpreting experimental micrographs. By comparing this simulation to actual HRTEM data, researchers can validate the structural models of the martensitic twins and distinguish between ideal and overlapped boundary configurations in the QWT-DZ alloy.

caption: Measured porosity and average strut diameter values for the face-centered cubic wick geometry.
summary: Data for the face-centered cubic wick geometry displays the measured porosity and average strut diameter. Consistent with the 325 μm as-built average, these measurements facilitate the analysis of how structural porosity influences permeability and pore radius, as determined through helium pycnometry and SEM imaging techniques.

caption: Solid-state grain growth observed in the XY plane after the seventh layer deposition, driven by repeated thermal cycling.
summary: During the seventh layer deposition, the grains at location A exhibit solid-state growth. This micrograph documents the structural changes resulting from the cumulative heating and cooling cycles, which promote grain coarsening in the selected sectional plane rather than the re-melting observed in earlier stages of the deposition process.

caption: Evolution of Vickers microhardness as a function of isothermal aging time for samples maintained at a constant temperature of 600 °C.
summary: The graph displays the relationship between isothermal aging duration and microhardness at 600 °C. The observed single-peak hardness profile indicates the strengthening contribution of two distinct types of precipitates, providing a clear mechanical response to the aging process over the specified time intervals during the material's heat treatment.

caption: Interrupted creep test results for specimens subjected to the same conditions as panel (a), focused on the initial 0.2% plastic strain regime.
summary: Creep tests interrupted at 0.2% plastic strain are presented to highlight early-stage deformation behavior under 700 °C and 690 MPa. This strain level marks the onset of the tertiary creep stage for these specimens. The observed trends in creep time at this early stage mirror those observed in the 3% strain data.

caption: Tabulated thermal properties and density values for the WC–NiCrBSiFe composite system.
summary: This table presents the essential thermal properties and density measurements for the WC–NiCrBSiFe material system. These data points are critical for understanding the thermal behavior and physical characteristics of the composite, providing the necessary parameters for subsequent processing and analysis within the study of this specific alloy system.

caption: 3D reconstruction of a Cantor powder particle featuring satellite structures, demonstrating high sphericity.
summary: This 3D reconstruction highlights a Cantor powder particle with satellite features. Due to the high volume ratio between the large central sphere and the smaller satellite spheres, these particles maintain a high sphericity value exceeding 0.9. Such features are distinct from the spherical and irregular particles found within the epoxy matrix.

caption: Iterative computational workflow designed for the numerical determination of the adhesion coefficient, µ adh, under varying tribological test conditions.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the iterative methodology utilized to numerically calculate the adhesion coefficient, µ adh. By systematically applying this process under diverse tribological test conditions, the researchers established a robust framework for determining adhesion parameters, ensuring consistent and accurate results across different experimental scenarios within the study's scope.

caption: Nyquist plot for the S6-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion in the electrolyte.
summary: The S6-6D specimen's electrochemical impedance response is shown after 6 days of immersion. Notably, the capacitive loop size and impedance values for this specimen are significantly lower than those observed for the S6-1H specimen, indicating reduced corrosion resistance compared to the shorter immersion period.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of a pure nickel sample oriented along the [1-11] zone axis, exhibiting diffuse-scattering signals.
summary: This panel displays the SAED pattern of a pure nickel sample along the [1-11] zone axis. The observed diffuse-scattering signals in this pattern show strong agreement with the homogeneous-matrix signals identified in the studied MEA, confirming that these features in the MEA are likely due to thermal diffuse scattering.

caption: True stress-true strain curves for the Al–Zn–Mg PM alloy compressed at 450 °C across various strain rates.
summary: Deformation behavior of the Al–Zn–Mg PM alloy is depicted via true stress-true strain curves at a temperature of 450 °C. By varying the strain rates, the plot reveals the flow characteristics of the alloy, offering insights into its mechanical stability and strength during high-temperature compression.

caption: Load-deformation curves for scaffolds A1 and A2, highlighting the distinct failure modes of each design.
summary: Load-deformation curves for scaffolds A1 and A2 demonstrate contrasting mechanical behaviors. Scaffold A1 shows moderate force increase followed by constant deformation, while the thicker A2 scaffold exhibits a steeper initial force increase and a sudden structural collapse. These results confirm that increased wall thickness significantly enhances mechanical strength and resistance.

caption: iR-corrected oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) polarization curves for Pt x Ni/C and Pt/C JM catalysts measured in O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH at 25 °C, 1600 rpm, and a scan rate of 5 mV s−1.
summary: This panel displays the iR-corrected ORR polarization curves for Pt x Ni/C and Pt/C JM catalysts. The measurements were conducted in an alkaline medium using O2-saturated 0.1 M KOH at 25 °C, with a rotation speed of 1600 rpm and a scan rate of 5 mV s−1 to evaluate catalytic performance.

caption: Nyquist plot for LPBF 316L steel samples after 30 minutes of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: This Nyquist plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance response of LPBF 316L steel after 30 minutes of immersion in a 3.5% NaCl solution. Analysis of the plot indicates that the electrochemical behavior of the sample is consistent with a two-layer passive film model, reflecting the surface corrosion state at this specific time.

caption: Chemical composition analysis of γ′ precipitates in DA and HA samples, illustrating minimal variation across different printing and post-processing parameters.
summary: This bar chart displays the chemical composition of γ′ precipitates in DA and HA samples. Small variations in the data confirm that printing and post-processing parameters have a negligible impact on the evolution of these precipitates. Error bars are included but remain largely invisible due to the chosen axis dimensions.

caption: Initial generation of beams at the starting point of the framework.
summary: This panel illustrates the first step of the CBSN lattice construction procedure. A starting point is established within the designated design space to initiate the framework generation. This initial beam serves as the foundational element from which subsequent network-like structures will be developed in the following procedural steps.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for ER120S-G solid wire under Group C conditions.
summary: This panel displays the CCT diagram for ER120S-G solid wire in Group C. Developed to analyze the influence of solid-state phase transformation temperatures and phase fractions on residual stress in WAAM components, this diagram provides critical data for understanding the thermal evolution and microstructural development of the deposited metal.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the FCC Ni crystal structure, highlighting the interlayer distance d_FCC and the P_Ni-Ni interaction parameter.
summary: This panel illustrates the FCC Ni crystal structure, which serves as a baseline for the system. The interlayer distance is specifically labeled as d_FCC, and the P_Ni-Ni parameter represents the interaction within the Ni layers, providing a fundamental structural reference for the subsequent multi-component slab models.

caption: Logarithmic plot comparing Young’s modulus against material strength for the homogeneous specimens.
summary: Young’s moduli and strength values derived from uniaxial tension tests are summarized in this logarithmic plot. Panel (c) illustrates the relationship between Young’s modulus and strength for the homogeneous materials, allowing for a comparative analysis of these fundamental mechanical properties across the different samples tested in the study.

caption: Boxplots displaying the distribution of defect roundness for each location after the build, accompanied by individual data points.
summary: Representing the after-build condition, these boxplots show the distribution of defect roundness for each location. The inclusion of all individual data points next to the boxplots allows for a comprehensive assessment of how defect shape characteristics are distributed across the build plate following the completion of the build process.

caption: Hardness profile of MHP surfaces after thermal exposure at 550 °C for 20 h, plotted against indentation depth.
summary: The hardness profile of MHP surfaces after thermal exposure at 550 °C for 20 hours is shown in this panel. These nanoindentation results, plotted up to 100 μm depth, characterize the hardness evolution of the material following the specified thermal treatment, allowing for comparison with the initial state.

caption: Equivalent stress distribution map during the failure stage, illustrating crack propagation as damage permeates throughout the entire structure.
summary: This FEA simulation panel depicts the equivalent stress distribution during the failure stage. It demonstrates how the initial failure propagates to neighboring regions, resulting in the formation of cracks that eventually permeate the entire structure, reflecting the progression of damage beyond the initial failure point.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for the HSLA steel, featuring superimposed experimental cooling curves indicated by arrows.
summary: This continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of the HSLA steel used in the investigation. Experimental cooling curves are superimposed on the diagram, with arrows highlighting specific cooling rates. These cooling rates serve as a reference for analyzing the resulting microstructures, such as acicular ferrite, grain boundary ferrite, and ferrite side plates.

caption: Schematic representation of the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process used for the fabrication of the aluminum alloy product.
summary: This schematic illustrates the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) manufacturing process employed to fabricate the aluminum alloy product. The diagram provides a conceptual overview of the additive manufacturing workflow, which serves as the foundational method for creating the experimental samples discussed in the study's subsequent material characterization and testing phases.

caption: Fatigue S-N data for transverse non-load-carrying attachments evaluated against standard design curves, including a custom fitted orange curve.
summary: Transverse non-load-carrying attachments are analyzed through their fatigue S-N response. The experimental data points are compared to established standards like Eurocode 3 and IIW. A bold orange design curve is fitted to the dataset to represent the fatigue strength with a 97.7% survival probability and minimized scatter index.

caption: Hydrogen microprint technique (HMT) image of the as-built specimen showing Ag nanoparticle enrichment at columnar dendrite walls near Laves phases.
summary: The HMT result for the as-built specimen reveals the hydrogen trapping behavior associated with the dendrite structure. Specifically, Ag nanoparticles are observed to be enriched at the columnar dendrite walls, particularly in the vicinity of Laves phases, indicating these regions act as effective hydrogen trapping sites in the as-built alloy.

caption: Time-dependent variation of the indentation depth change, ΔP(t), measured during creep tests at various temperatures, featuring a power-law fit represented by a solid green line.
summary: This plot illustrates the progression of creep under an indenter tip across different temperatures. The measured indentation depth change, ΔP(t), is plotted against time, with a green line indicating the power-law fit applied to the experimental data according to the specified mathematical model, capturing the material's time-dependent deformation behavior.

caption: SAED pattern demonstrating the twofold symmetry direction characteristic of the quasi-crystalline Al31Mn6Ni12 phase.
summary: The SAED pattern obtained from the inter-dendritic region indicates the presence of the quasi-crystalline Al31Mn6Ni12 phase. This specific diffraction pattern closely resembles the twofold symmetry direction previously reported in literature, confirming the structural identity of the quasi-crystalline phase within the alloy's complex inter-dendritic microstructure.

caption: Parity plot showing the deviation between predicted and observed relative density values.
summary: This panel presents a parity plot illustrating the deviation between predicted and observed relative density values. By comparing the model's output against experimental data, the plot provides a visual assessment of the predictive accuracy for density, highlighting the discrepancies between the calculated results and the actual observed measurements.

caption: Comparative analysis of BCC and disordered atomic proportions across [100], [110], and [111] orientations as shock velocity changes.
summary: This comparative plot focuses on the BCC and disordered atomic fractions across three distinct crystallographic orientations. By contrasting the [100], [110], and [111] directions, the graph elucidates how shock velocity influences the competition between ordered BCC structures and disordered states, emphasizing the anisotropy of the material's response to shock.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 1 fabricated via standard PCB fabrication.
summary: This panel shows the reflection coefficient of antenna design 1 produced using standard PCB fabrication methods. The data, plotted using Origin software, highlights the reflection performance of the PCB-based antenna, facilitating an analysis of how traditional manufacturing processes influence the electromagnetic response of the designed antenna structure.

caption: Lattice strain response for the line build cross-member, plotting (111), (200), (220), (311), and (420) reflections against cumulative load in axial and transverse orientations.
summary: Lattice strain behavior for the line build is presented as a function of cumulative load. The graph displays axial and transverse strain components for various crystal planes. The results are averaged across five specific cross-member locations, providing a statistical representation of the material's internal strain response during loading.

caption: Detailed configuration layout of the flow resistance test rig components.
summary: The configuration of the flow resistance test rig is detailed in this panel, illustrating the specific arrangement of components. As part of the designed test bench, this layout provides the necessary technical framework for conducting flow resistance measurements, ensuring the experimental setup is accurately represented for the research study.

caption: Isolated Al clusters identified within the Inconel 718 matrix, demonstrating a consistently small size and low atomic count across all tested temperatures.
summary: Identified Al clusters within the Inconel 718 samples are characterized by their small size and low atomic density. These clusters remain consistent in their limited scale regardless of the tensile testing temperature, indicating that Al clustering behavior is relatively stable under the applied experimental conditions.

caption: Atomic trajectory of the Fe93S6 alloy at 360 GPa and 5500 K, with red dashed circles indicating interstitial sites occupied by sulfur impurities.
summary: This simulation snapshot shows the trajectory of the Fe93S6 alloy at 360 GPa and 5500 K. Red dashed circles are utilized to highlight the interstitial sites occupied by sulfur impurities, allowing for an analysis of how sulfur diffusion occurs relative to the iron host lattice at high pressure.

caption: Confocal microscopy image providing a secondary view of the AlSi10Mg surface, further detailing the irregular distribution of unmelted powder and spatter defects.
summary: Confocal microscopy further illustrates the surface imperfections of AlSi10Mg. This panel confirms the presence of randomly positioned unmelted and partially melted powders, along with spatters, across the surface of both as-built and heat-treated specimens, reinforcing the findings regarding the surface quality of the powder bed fusion processed material.

caption: Fitted curves representing the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the stress-alpha product as a function of inverse absolute temperature.
summary: This plot shows the fitted curves of the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the stress-alpha product plotted against the inverse of absolute temperature. These curves are used to determine the activation energy for the deformation of the GH4151 alloy under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the electrochemical impedance response of laser powder bed fusion produced Ti–6Al–4V (LTC4) after potentiostatic polarization at potentials ranging from 2.6 V to 3.0 V, with an inset showing the R(Q(R(QR))) equivalent electrical circuit model used for data fitting.
summary: The Nyquist plot for LTC4 illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior following potentiostatic polarization between 2.6 V and 3.0 V. Data were fitted using an R(Q(R(QR))) equivalent electrical circuit model, as shown in the inset. This plot characterizes the passive film properties and impedance response of the laser-produced alloy under these specific electrochemical conditions.

caption: Energy barrier distributions showing a shift toward higher values for cast metallic glass compared to LPBF material.
summary: The energy barrier distribution is shifted toward higher energies for the cast metallic glass, with an average of 0.408 eV, compared to 0.308 eV for the LPBF material. This shift confirms that STZ activation is energetically easier in the LPBF glass and occurs at lower stresses than in cast BMG.

caption: EDS mapping of the H900 heat-treated 17-4 PH steel specimen showing Cu distribution.
summary: EDS mapping of the H900 specimen reveals a dense distribution of spherical or elliptical copper-rich precipitates within the matrix. These precipitates, ranging from 2 to 6 nm in size, exhibit high Cu signal intensity, demonstrating the effect of heat treatment on the nanoscale dispersion of copper.

caption: Raman spectra acquired from five distinct groups of TCP/BO/GO scaffolds, each coated with a different concentration of GO to evaluate chemical composition.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was performed on five groups of TCP/BO/GO scaffolds, which were coated with different concentrations of GO. The resulting spectra allow for the characterization of the chemical composition and structural integrity of the scaffolds, highlighting the differences across the various GO coating concentrations applied to the samples.

caption: Normal probability plot of standardized effects illustrating the relative influence of printing parameters on steady-state fracture toughness (G).
summary: This normal plot of standardized effects demonstrates how specific printing parameters influence steady-state fracture toughness. The analysis reveals that the build angle exerts a significantly higher standardized effect on the fracture toughness compared to the scan speed, highlighting the critical role of orientation in determining the material's steady-state fracture behavior.

caption: Feature importance results for architected beams with a slenderness ratio L/h = 15, considering the impact of modes [1,10].
summary: This panel illustrates the feature importance for architected beams characterized by a slenderness ratio of L/h = 15. By examining modes [1,10], the analysis highlights which structural features are most critical for determining the dynamic mechanical performance of these specific high-slenderness beams, facilitating a deeper understanding of their mechanical response.

caption: Contact force–displacement response of GFRP base samples and those embedded with bulk and triangular lattice sheets (neat and 0.1 wt% GNP) at an impact energy of 300 J.
summary: This panel displays the contact force–displacement response for various GFRP composites at 300 J. The base samples exhibit the lowest initial collapse load but demonstrate the highest peak contact force compared to the lattice-embedded samples, highlighting distinct mechanical behaviors during the impact event for the different material configurations.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) evolution over time for Ti–45Nb, Ti–42Nb (LPBF-Gaussian laser), Ti–42Nb (LPBF-top hat laser), and Ti–6Al–4V ELI alloys immersed in PBS solution.
summary: This panel displays the open circuit potential (OCP) evolution for various titanium-based alloys, including Ti–45Nb, Ti–42Nb produced via different LPBF laser strategies, and Ti–6Al–4V ELI, during immersion in a PBS solution. The data illustrates the electrochemical stability and potential changes of these materials over the measured time period.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum of the spent Ni@Al2O3 catalyst used to analyze elemental composition changes.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the spent Ni@Al2O3 catalyst provides insight into the elemental composition changes occurring during the reaction. This spectroscopic data serves as a diagnostic tool to evaluate the chemical state and potential degradation of the catalyst surface after exposure to the reaction environment.

caption: Hardness values measured at room temperature for samples processed with and without UHFP current.
summary: Hardness values for samples processed with and without UHFP current were measured at room temperature. This panel presents the comparative hardness results, illustrating the influence of the UHFP current on the mechanical properties of the material walls, as determined through experimental testing of the two distinct sample groups.

caption: Mass spectrum of FPEA-ProGly 3D-printed scaffold after CGRGDS peptide coupling.
summary: The mass spectrum illustrates the successful coupling of the CGRGDS peptide onto the FPEA-ProGly 3D-printed scaffold. This result confirms that the peptide immobilization technique is effective for complex 3D structures. The measurement was performed over a 500 µm by 500 µm area to ensure consistent surface analysis.

caption: Final loading stage highlighting the displacement deflection of atoms near the indentation site, driven by shear stress flow within the shear transformation zones (STZs).
summary: Depicting the final loading stage, this panel illustrates the displacement deflection of atoms around the indentation. This phenomenon is triggered by shear stress flow within the STZs. The atomic motion direction is indicated by arrows, while color intensity represents the magnitude of the displacement during the loading process.

caption: Tensile modulus radar plot comparing multi-material composites with varying face-to-core ratios (f = 0 to 0.8) against the monolithic core baseline.
summary: This radar plot illustrates the tensile modulus performance of multi-material composites relative to a monolithic core. The data shows how varying the face-to-core ratio from 0 to 0.8 influences mechanical stiffness. The gray area represents the monolithic baseline, while color-coded values quantify the percentage performance of each specific configuration.

caption: Schematic representation illustrating the loading and unloading sequence performed during the nanoindentation test.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the fundamental loading and unloading process utilized during nanoindentation testing. It provides a conceptual overview of the mechanical interaction between the indenter tip and the specimen surface, serving as a guide for understanding the force application and retraction phases of the experimental procedure.

caption: Voigt profile fit of the measured optical linewidth at I MLL = 150 mA, I G = 200 mA, and V SA = −1.8 V.
summary: The optical linewidth of the BSOL device is characterized using the fiber-delayed self-heterodyne method. At operating conditions of 150 mA for I MLL, 200 mA for I G, and -1.8 V for V SA, the measured linewidth is fitted with Voigt profiles, yielding a determined -3 dB linewidth of 112 kHz.

caption: Indentation load plotted against indent diagonal squared for MPI 25% Co, covering both quasi-static and dynamic strain rate data.
summary: MPI 25% Co is evaluated by plotting indentation load as a function of the square of the indent diagonal. This approach allows for a reliable hardness comparison across quasi-static and dynamic strain regimes, effectively managing the variability in dynamic indentation loads and the lack of pronounced indentation size effects observed.

caption: LIME significance values for 6 porous surfels within the 49.61–50 kHz frequency band, highlighting elements with positive significance exceeding 0.08.
summary: This panel displays LIME significance values for six porous surfels in the 49.61–50 kHz frequency band. Elements with high energy in this range demonstrate positive significance values greater than 0.08, indicating their contribution toward the presence of pores in the identified surfels as determined by the LIME analysis.

caption: Beeswarm plot illustrating the distribution of SHAP values (MPa) for all experimental instances, with features ordered by importance and color-coded to represent feature values from low (blue) to high (red).
summary: The beeswarm plot visualizes the SHAP values for all experimental observations related to the scan direction residual stress. Features are ordered by importance, with color-coded points indicating the magnitude of the feature value. Positive SHAP values signify a direct contribution to increasing the residual stress magnitude, while negative values indicate a reduction.

caption: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) distribution across seven machine learning models, assessing model prediction precision.
summary: Displaying the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for seven machine learning models, this box plot quantifies the average magnitude of errors in predictions. It is utilized alongside other metrics to comprehensively evaluate the predictive performance of the models, highlighting differences in precision across the various algorithms.

caption: Temperature-dependent reduction of area (RA) at rupture for ferritic spheroidal graphite iron (SGI) alloys B, E, G, and H, illustrating susceptibility to intergranular temper brittleness (ITB).
summary: This plot displays the reduction of area at rupture versus temperature for ferritic SGI alloys containing 2.2–2.6 wt% silicon. Data reveals that alloys B, E, and G exhibit significant ductility loss below 10% RA at 400–425 °C, whereas alloy H remains immune to ITB, demonstrating varying sensitivity among these materials.

caption: Schematic representation of four potential CO adsorption sites on the Au-Ni surface, identifying the Ni atop site as the most energetically preferred location.
summary: Four potential CO adsorption sites are modeled on the Au-Ni surface. While the Ni atop site is the most preferred for CO adsorption, it is not the site most sensitive to bias. This demonstrates that charge sensitivity to bias is not the sole determinant for binding strength in this system.

caption: Nanoindentation-derived elastic modulus and hardness map of the top region specimen in the XY plane at the core position.
summary: This panel displays the elastic modulus and hardness distribution for the top region of the specimen. Obtained via nanoindentation across a 2000 × 500 μm area at the core position, the map reveals spatial variations in mechanical properties, although distinguishing between the γ' phase and γ matrix remains impossible.

caption: Bioplotter additive manufacturing system utilized for the fabrication process, manufactured by Envision TEC.
summary: This panel displays the Bioplotter additive manufacturing system developed by Envision TEC. The equipment serves as the primary experimental setup for the fabrication process described in the study, providing the necessary hardware infrastructure to produce the samples analyzed in subsequent sections of the research.

caption: Weak-beam dark-field micrograph of NiFe irradiated to 1 dpa at 773 K, highlighting the accumulation of larger defect loops.
summary: At an ion dose of 1 dpa and 773 K, the NiFe alloy exhibits a significant population of defect loops. This weak-beam dark-field micrograph, imaged with g = (200), shows the accumulation of these features, which include both Frank loops with stacking-fault fringes and perfect loops, characterizing the ongoing microstructural evolution.

caption: Radar comparison model illustrating the performance metrics of various regression models evaluated in the study.
summary: This radar chart provides a comparative visualization of the performance metrics for multiple regression models. By mapping various evaluation criteria, the plot highlights significant differences in predictive capabilities across the models. These insights, alongside learning curves, facilitate a comprehensive assessment of the model development process and overall regression performance.

caption: Predicted versus experimental fatigue life using the proposed non-local Dang Van model.
summary: The proposed modified non-local Dang Van model is compared with experimental fatigue life results. This model yields the most accurate predictions among all evaluated methods, demonstrating superior performance and reduced scatter in the parity plot, which highlights its effectiveness in modeling multiaxial fatigue behavior for the studied materials.

caption: Optical micrograph of the Nimax substrate region within the as-built specimen.
summary: Optical imaging of the Nimax substrate region in the as-built specimen shows the baseline microstructure of the material. Observations indicate that this substrate remains stable, as there is no apparent microstructural change in the Nimax material through the solution treatment process, confirming that this specific material is not heat-treatable.
