The absence of evident signals related to degradation products indicates that the PCL material remains stable throughout the 14-day in vitro cell culture period.

caption: Voltage-Amperage (V-A) waveform recorded at 10 V, exhibiting linear characteristics indicative of resistance-based heating.
summary: Recorded via oscilloscope, the V-A waveform at 10 V displays typical linear characteristics. This linearity demonstrates that the material removal process during US-EAM at this voltage is primarily driven by resistance heat rather than arc heat, providing insight into the fundamental energy mechanism at lower operating voltages.

caption: Top-view projections of the TPMS and RDOD porous scaffold models, illustrating the geometric arrangement and pore distribution corresponding to the 60%, 70%, and 80% porosity levels.
summary: Top-view projections of the TPMS and RDOD porous scaffold models are presented to illustrate their geometric arrangement. These views highlight the pore distribution and structural configuration of the scaffolds designed with 60%, 70%, and 80% porosity, maintaining a uniform strut diameter of 0.3 mm across all variations.

caption: Confocal 3D render of HUVECs in the scaffold after two weeks of incubation, highlighting the progression of microvessel formation with nuclei (blue) and actin filaments (red).
summary: After 14 days of incubation, confocal imaging shows further proliferation of HUVECs within the mm-thick GelMA scaffolds. The 3D render displays the development of microvessels, with nuclei stained blue and actin filaments in red, confirming that extended incubation promotes increased cell growth and structural organization within the printed construct.

caption: Local charge density and Bader charge distributions for Bcc(Al,Fe) and Bcc(Al,Fe,Mn) phases along (001)Al and (111)Al orientations.
summary: Local charge density and Bader charge distributions are visualized for Bcc(Al,Fe) and Bcc(Al,Fe,Mn) phases along (001)Al and (111)Al orientations. Analysis reveals that Al atoms transfer electrons to Fe and Mn elements within these phases, a phenomenon attributed to the higher chemical reactivity of aluminum compared to the transition metal elements.

caption: Normalized mass spectrum and correlation histogram for M6C carbides acquired at 100 pJ, illustrating the distinct evaporation behavior compared to MC and M23C6 carbides.
summary: M6C carbides demonstrate a unique mass spectral profile that differs from both MC and M23C6 variants. The evaporation behavior of these carbides is distinct, reflecting the impact of carbide type on ion formation. These variations in mass spectra are attributed to complex processes including delayed evaporation and dissociation reactions during analysis.

caption: Representative FTIR spectrum of BC LOI at 600 °C, highlighting characteristic absorption peaks for CO2, H2O, and CO gases.
summary: This FTIR spectrum, collected at 600 °C during an LOI run, demonstrates the high spectral sensitivity of the analytical method. The plot clearly identifies evolved gas species, specifically CO2, H2O, and CO, by highlighting their respective integration windows, confirming the successful detection of gaseous decomposition products at elevated temperatures.

caption: Two-beam TEM image of dislocation configurations in the specimen after creep rupture at 1200 °C and 80 MPa, viewed with a [200] diffraction vector.
summary: This TEM image displays dislocation configurations following creep fracture at 1200 °C and 80 MPa. Under the [200] diffraction vector, the dislocations are invisible, which satisfies the g·b=0 extinction criterion. This observation is critical for confirming the Burgers vector of the observed a/2<110> super dislocations within the γ channels.

caption: Specific strength and specific energy absorption metrics for the second dual-faced structured fabric, evaluated across different vacuum confining pressures.
summary: This panel quantifies the specific strength and specific energy absorption for the second dual-faced structured fabric under vacuum interference. The data shows that the fabric achieves a specific strength of 13,387 N m kg⁻¹ and a specific energy absorption of 2522 J kg⁻¹, demonstrating its robust mechanical performance.

caption: Tafel voltammograms illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of various stainless steels and nickel-based alloys immersed in [P66614][Tf2N] electrolyte at 23 °C.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical response of stainless steels and nickel-based alloys in [P66614][Tf2N] at 23 °C. The data indicates that a passivation layer forms readily on all tested alloys. These voltammograms are essential for identifying corrosion mechanisms and determining critical parameters like corrosion current densities and potentials.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining images demonstrating the positive expression of α-SMA in CP-R237 cells treated with gel or Dopa-gel scaffolds.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining was performed to assess the expression of α-SMA in CP-R237 cells. The images visualize the presence and distribution of this protein, confirming that the cells positively express α-SMA when cultured on the gel and Dopa-gel scaffolds, which is critical for evaluating cellular differentiation or activation states.

caption: Intermediate downward position of the hammer during the initial phase of vertical movement.
summary: Panel b captures the hammer at an intermediate point during its vertical descent. The red cross on the bottom surface and the dashed line tracking the surface position illustrate the continuous downward trajectory, providing a sequential frame that documents the movement toward the lowest position before the final impact.

caption: Evolution of the a-axis lattice parameter for Cr2O3 as a function of temperature, derived from molecular dynamics simulations using various potentials.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent evolution of the a-axis lattice parameter for Cr2O3. The data is obtained from molecular dynamics simulations using different potentials and is compared against established reference values. This visualization illustrates how the lattice dimensions change under thermal influence as predicted by the computational models.

caption: Cyclic stability performance of 2 wt% Co-HPMC-C catalysts measured over multiple cycles of 4-NP conversion.
summary: This plot evaluates the cyclic stability of the ceramic-based catalysts during the conversion of 4-NP. By monitoring the conversion efficiency over repeated cycles using the 2 wt% Co-HPMC-C catalyst, the figure demonstrates the durability and reusability of the 3D-printed material in maintaining catalytic performance throughout the testing process.

caption: Processed interference fringe image captured when the phase difference across the phase-locked modulator (PLM) is π.
summary: This processed interference fringe image illustrates the optical state where the phase difference on both sides of the PLM is set to π. The visualization demonstrates the shift in fringe patterns resulting from this specific phase modulation, confirming the effectiveness of the processing technique under these controlled experimental conditions.

caption: STEM brightfield and HAADF micrographs of thinned Cu-50Ag pillars, featuring corresponding Ag and Cu EDX elemental maps and selected area electron diffractograms.
summary: STEM brightfield and HAADF micrographs of thinned Cu-50Ag pillars, featuring corresponding Ag and Cu EDX elemental maps and selected area electron diffractograms. The EDX maps and diffraction data indicate that the alloy exists as a single-phase fcc solid solution, deviating from the expected thermodynamic equilibrium state of separated phases.

caption: Orthogonal slices of the resulting synthetic graylevel volumetric image representing the strut with an imperfection.
summary: Orthogonal slices of the synthetic graylevel volumetric image are displayed, illustrating the strut structure and its incorporated imperfection. Derived from the indicator function, this 3D representation provides a detailed view of the internal and external geometry, effectively simulating the appearance of a physical strut within a volumetric dataset.

caption: Framework for assessing the keel component based on forefoot loading test criteria.
summary: This schematic illustrates the classification framework for the keel component during forefoot loading tests. It defines specific thresholds to categorize designs as Rigid, Flexible/Cushioned, or Dynamic. This systematic approach allows researchers to evaluate whether 3D-printed prosthetic designs meet the mechanical requirements necessary for dynamic performance in foot prostheses.

caption: Radar plot comparing mechanical properties across different structural designs, specifically highlighting specific elastic modulus and specific yield strength metrics.
summary: The radar plot provides a comparative visualization of mechanical properties for all evaluated structures. It specifically maps the specific elastic modulus and specific yield strength, illustrating the performance trade-offs and relative gains achieved by the HBCC design compared to other structural configurations in the study.

caption: LSV curves of Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL and Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni foam catalysts in 1.0 M NaOH and 0.5 M N2H4·H2O solution, highlighting the difference in onset potentials.
summary: The LSV curves illustrate the onset potential for the hydrazine oxidation reaction. The Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam exhibits a lower onset potential of approximately -0.15 V compared to the Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni foam, which shows an onset potential of approximately -0.10 V, indicating improved catalytic kinetics for the MEL-based structure.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the NbTiZr system at 700 °C, showing two- and three-phase BCC regions identified by free energy curvature eigenvalues.
summary: VCSGMC simulations at 700 °C reveal the phase stability of the NbTiZr system. The colormap of free energy curvature eigenvalues highlights regions where multiple phases coexist. This visualization demonstrates how oxygen content and alloy composition influence the formation of two- and three-phase BCC regions within the ternary compositional space.

caption: Raman spectra of the synthesized catalysts showing characteristic D- and G-bands of carbon at 1350 and 1575 cm-1.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals two prominent peaks at 1350 and 1575 cm-1 for the catalysts, which correspond to the characteristic D- and G-bands of carbon, respectively. These bands provide insights into the graphitic nature and defect density of the carbon-based support structures within the FeNi@HOMC-700 and related materials.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the F150 specimen acquired under a two-beam diffraction condition, with the g-vector indicated by an arrow to characterize the nature of the observed stacking faults.
summary: This dark-field TEM image characterizes the nature of stacking faults in the F150 alloy after creep deformation. Captured under a two-beam diffraction condition with the g-vector indicated by an arrow, the micrograph complements the bright-field imaging to provide a detailed analysis of the microstructural features present in the sample.

caption: TEM and STEM morphology of Cu3 steel illustrating the distribution of Cu-rich precipitates.
summary: The TEM and STEM morphology of Cu3 steel shows the local microstructure with Cu-rich precipitates indicated by yellow arrows. As with the lower Cu-content steels, Cu is mainly in a solid solution state, which inhibits the anode reaction and results in a decrease of the corrosion current density for the steel.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetization for a ribbon sample annealed at 873 K for 10 minutes, measured during cooling under various applied magnetic fields.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent magnetization behavior of an annealed ribbon sample during cooling. As the applied magnetic field increases, the magnetic transition (MT) becomes less observable. This suppression occurs because the saturation magnetization and atomic magnetic moments of the involved phases become increasingly similar under higher external fields.

caption: Tafel slope analysis showing Ni1Co3@NC achieving a lower slope of 57 ± 3 mV dec−1 compared to other bimetallic and benchmark catalysts.
summary: The Tafel slope analysis reveals that Ni1Co3@NC exhibits the lowest slope of 57 ± 3 mV dec−1, outperforming other bimetallic compositions like Ni3Co1@NC and Ni1Co2@NC. This value is also lower than the benchmark 20% Pt/C catalyst, indicating superior reaction kinetics for the hydrogen evolution process in this specific composition.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells co-cultured with scaffolds after 1, 3, and 5 days, showing live and dead cell distributions.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images visualize bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells co-cultured with scaffolds over a 5-day period. Live and dead staining assays reveal a higher proportion of dead cells in the 15 wt% scaffold group on days 3 and 5, indicating reduced cell compatibility compared to other experimental conditions.

caption: Elemental distribution mapping of the second phase particles located within the dimples of the VAM-316 fracture surface.
summary: Elemental mapping of the second phase particles found within the dimples of the VAM-316 fracture surface confirms their chemical composition. The analysis indicates that these particles are identical in type to those observed within the bulk material, suggesting a consistent distribution of secondary phases throughout the microstructure.

caption: XPS survey scan of the corrosion layer formed on sample T006 after 24 h of immersion in AUS.
summary: This XPS survey scan characterizes the corrosion layer on sample T006 after 24 hours in AUS. The analysis indicates the presence of Mg, O, C, and P as major elements. Notably, T006 shows a lower amount of corrosion layer products compared to the T004 and T005 samples.

caption: Chronoamperometric response of wrought 316L stainless steel polarized at four distinct passive film formation potentials in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Wrought 316L stainless steel exhibits a significant decrease in passive current density over a 600-second duration when polarized at four different passive film formation potentials. This behavior indicates the development and stabilization of a passive layer on the specimen surface, resulting in a steady-state current density of 185 nA/cm2.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction illustrating the spatial distribution of key alloying elements including Ni, Cr, Fe, Al, Ti, and Nb within the analyzed volume.
summary: The 3D-APT reconstruction provides a detailed visualization of the atomic-scale distribution of Ni, Cr, Fe, Al, Ti, and Nb. This volumetric data allows for the examination of elemental partitioning and segregation behavior across the phase interfaces within the analyzed needle-tip specimen.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the as-printed LPBF ZGH4142 specimen, highlighting high dislocation concentrations at grain boundaries.
summary: The LPBF ZGH4142 specimen exhibits a high dislocation density, particularly concentrated at grain boundaries, as shown in the GND map. This high density, with a value of 1.1 × 10 14 m −2, is attributed to localized thermal-mechanical stresses induced by the rapid heating and cooling cycles during the LPBF process.

caption: Ti–Al binary phase diagram used to analyze the formation process of α2, γ, and B2 phases in the Ti6Al4V/TiAl system.
summary: The Ti–Al phase diagram provides a theoretical basis for understanding the formation of α2, γ, and B2 phases in the studied alloys. Analysis indicates that increasing TiAl content elevates Al, Nb, and Cr levels while decreasing Ti and V, facilitating the diffusion of aluminum atoms into the α phase region.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Ni-Sn, Ni, and Sn nanoparticles recorded in 0.50 M KOH electrolyte at a scan rate of 50 mV s−1, showing that current densities of the first anodic and cathodic peaks decrease as the Sn content increases in the bimetallic nanoparticles.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammograms for Ni-Sn, Ni, and Sn nanoparticles in a 0.50 M KOH solution. The data, collected at a scan rate of 50 mV s−1, demonstrates that the current densities of the initial anodic and cathodic peaks systematically decrease as the Sn content within the bimetallic nanoparticles increases.

caption: Optical transmission spectra of the sample after initial UV exposure intervals.
summary: Optical transmission spectra of the sample are presented following initial UV exposure intervals. The measurements were conducted in a UV chamber with an intensity of 3.15 mW/cm2. These spectra illustrate the change in optical transmission characteristics as a function of the specific UV energy exposure applied to the material.

caption: EDX spectrum of the Cu-NiTi archwire surface after hydrothermal treatment in an aqueous phosphate solution.
summary: The EDX analysis of the Cu-NiTi archwire surface demonstrates a reduction in nickel, titanium, and copper to 16%, 28%, and 1.5%, respectively. The presence of 9% phosphorus and 45.5% oxygen confirms surface oxidation and the formation of titanium phosphate phases following the hydrothermal treatment in phosphate solution.

caption: Three-dimensional wear track topography of the as-built (AB) sample subjected to a 15 N load.
summary: Shown is the three-dimensional wear track topography for the as-built (AB) sample under a 15 N load. This 3D microscope image illustrates the surface degradation and wear profile of the as-built material when subjected to the highest load level in the experimental series.

caption: Dark field TEM micrograph of the XY plane, providing complementary contrast to the bright field image.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging of the XY plane is utilized to reveal specific microstructural details that are less apparent in bright field mode. This technique provides complementary contrast, allowing for a more comprehensive characterization of the material's internal structure and the distribution of phases within the observed plane.

caption: Raman spectra and corresponding Gaussian fitting curves for various ceramic samples after pyrolysis at 1300 °C.
summary: Raman spectra and Gaussian fitting curves are presented for different preceramic materials subjected to pyrolysis at 1300 °C. This panel illustrates the structural characterization of the ceramic parts, providing a baseline for analyzing the carbonaceous phases formed during the high-temperature treatment process through spectral peak fitting and identification.

caption: Fourth arc shape configuration of the SCA under CV power supply.
summary: This panel captures the fourth arc shape of the SCA under CV power supply. The IWA and PMA maintain their close coupling in a hybrid state, highlighting the stability of the hybrid arc configuration across the different shapes observed during the controlled power supply experiment.

caption: Optical transmittance and reflectance spectra of photovoltaic cells encapsulated with pure COC and various COCA coversheets, measured across a range of wavelengths and incident angles.
summary: This plot illustrates the optical performance of photovoltaic cells protected by pure COC and various COCA coversheets. By displaying both transmittance and reflectance spectra at different angles, the figure characterizes the light-management properties of these materials, which are essential for evaluating the efficiency and durability of the encapsulated photovoltaic devices.

caption: Intermediate build stage highlighting the build direction and the expanding heat conduction domain as the heat source moves.
summary: Depicted here is an intermediate stage of the additive manufacturing process, emphasizing the build direction and the progression of the heat source. The heat conduction domain expands accordingly, illustrating the thermal environment within the discretized finite element domain, which is analogous to density-based topology optimization design frameworks.

caption: Strain recovery and plastic strain evolution over cycling for samples P1 and P4, demonstrating the influence of varying laser power on training behavior.
summary: This panel displays the evolution of strain recovery and plastic strain across multiple cycles for samples P1 and P4. By varying the laser power during processing, the training curves illustrate distinct mechanical responses. The anchor point is highlighted in black, facilitating the extraction of key parameters for further material analysis.

caption: Comparative WF and LF-OS-SIM images of the specific region highlighted by the orange box in panel (a), captured across a depth range of 4.8 μm to 7.2 μm.
summary: Detailed comparison between wide-field and LF-OS-SIM imaging is presented for the region within the orange box from panel (a). The images illustrate microtubule morphology across five focal planes at z = 4.8 μm, 5.4 μm, 6 μm, 6.6 μm, and 7.2 μm, highlighting the superior resolution of the LF-OS-SIM method.

caption: Enlarged view of the atom map highlighting the specific region of interest (ROI) marked in light blue for compositional analysis.
summary: This enlarged atom map focuses on a specific region of interest marked in light blue within the M1 sample matrix. The visualization provides a detailed look at the atomic distribution near the grain boundary and the F phase interface, facilitating the subsequent 1D concentration profile analysis of the selected region.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module, comparing rescaled experimental measurements with the PEC2 model predictions across varying insolation and temperature conditions.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module under diverse insolation and temperature conditions. It provides a comparison between rescaled experimental data and the PEC2 model, illustrating the performance behavior of the module and validating the accuracy of the PEC2 model in predicting electrical output.

caption: Magnified view of the Nyquist impedance plot focusing on the high-frequency region for SS316L samples printed at different laser powers (A–E) and the commercial control.
summary: This zoomed Nyquist plot provides a detailed examination of the high-frequency electrochemical impedance response for SS316L samples. By isolating this region for specimens printed at varying laser powers (A–E) and the commercial sample, the plot allows for a clearer assessment of the specific impedance characteristics and surface-electrolyte interactions at play.

caption: Fourier transform infrared spectra comparing the chemical composition of the three scaffold groups.
summary: Fourier transform infrared spectra are presented for the bredigite, Bre@PDA, and Bre@PDA-Ful scaffolds. Analysis indicates no significant difference among the three groups, as the surface coating components, specifically PDA and fullerol, constitute only a small proportion of the total scaffold composition.

caption: Contour plot displaying the electrical resistivity (ρ) across the entire composition range of the annealed bulk alloy library.
summary: This contour plot provides a comprehensive overview of the electrical resistivity (ρ) across the entire composition space of the annealed bulk alloy library. It serves as a baseline for understanding the electronic transport properties of the various Fe-Co-Ni alloy compositions investigated in this study.

caption: Activation energy determination for the MHPCM/DGEBA system based on thermal analysis data.
summary: The activation energy of the MHPCM/DGEBA system is calculated to understand the energy barrier associated with the curing reaction. This parameter is fundamental for predicting the curing behavior and optimizing the thermal processing conditions required for the complete polymerization of the hybrid resin system.

caption: Maximum force values for overprinted PA HT-CF/PA6 specimens derived from rib-on-plate tension tests, with asterisks denoting statistically significant differences between experimental groups.
summary: This panel displays the maximum interface forces recorded during rib-on-plate tension tests for overprinted PA HT-CF/PA6 specimens. The data highlights variations in mechanical performance across different h/t combinations, with statistical significance indicated by p < 0.05, providing a quantitative comparison of the structural integrity of the overprinted material interfaces.

caption: Voltage and current curves synchronized with the high-speed imaging frames to identify specific stages of the droplet transfer mode.
summary: Synchronized voltage and current curves are presented to identify the specific frames of the droplet transfer mode observed during high-speed imaging. These curves provide the necessary electrical data to correlate the physical metal transfer events with the corresponding electrical signals recorded during the single-bead deposition process.

caption: Arrhenius plots displaying the natural logarithm of the parabolic rate constant (ln(kp)) as a function of the reciprocal absolute temperature (1/T) for TA15-x alloys with x = 0, 1, 5, and 9 across the 873–1073 K range.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature-dependent oxidation kinetics of TA15-x alloys. By plotting the natural logarithm of the parabolic rate constant against the reciprocal of absolute temperature, the figure characterizes the oxidation behavior for varying alloy compositions between 873 K and 1073 K, providing insight into the thermal activation of the oxidation process.

caption: EBSD orientation map and corresponding inverse pole figure of the sample vertical section processed at 0 T magnetic field intensity.
summary: This panel displays the EBSD orientation map and inverse pole figure for the sample vertical section under a 0 T magnetic field. At this condition, the microstructure maintains its initial state, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of higher magnetic field intensities on grain morphology and crystallographic orientation.

caption: Predicted EOS for vanadium (V) polymorphs, displaying the cohesive energy versus unit cell volume trend obtained from CTIP calculations in comparison to DFT data.
summary: Vanadium polymorphs are characterized by their equation of state, where cohesive energy is plotted against unit cell volume. The CTIP-derived predictions are benchmarked against first-principles DFT data, providing a clear comparison of the energetic trends and structural properties of V as predicted by the computational model.

caption: Vertical building orientation of the 316L stainless steel, highlighting intricate melt pool overlapping patterns.
summary: Vertical building orientation of 316L stainless steel is shown here using laser scanning confocal microscopy. The image illustrates the intricate overlapping pattern formed within the melt pools during successive laser beam tracks. This morphology confirms that grain structure in printed 316L SS layers is significantly correlated with the building orientation.

caption: Size distribution analysis of the α-phase in the TiC/Ti-alloy matrix for sample I60–V3, providing quantitative data on phase dimensions.
summary: Statistical data for the α-phase size in the matrix of sample I60–V3 is shown in this histogram. By analyzing the size distribution as a function of process parameters, this panel helps characterize the evolution of the α-phase, providing essential quantitative insights into the composite's microstructural properties.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of an undeformed specimen highlighting the distribution of annealing twins.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the microstructural characterization of an undeformed specimen. The visualization distinguishes between parent grains, represented in blue, and annealing twins, shown in red, while grey regions denote undefined areas. This identification process provides a clear spatial distribution of twin boundaries within the material's grain structure.

caption: Atomic arrangement model representing the low chemical short-range order (CSRO) system configuration.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configuration for the low CSRO model. It serves as a baseline example to analyze the elemental arrangement within the system, facilitating a comparative study against the high CSRO model to eliminate simulation randomness and understand the impact of chemical order on material properties.

caption: R-curve responses showing crack growth resistance for TA-37.5, TA-40, and TA-45 Al2O3-ZrO2 composite ceramic samples.
summary: R-curves for the TA-37.5, TA-40, and TA-45 samples are shown to characterize the crack growth resistance of the nacre-inspired ceramics. These curves provide insight into the fracture behavior of samples with higher PMMA content, which exhibit a step-like crack propagation pattern due to weak interconnections between the ceramic bricks.

caption: Mass distribution of 3D printed samples following silicone oil injection, demonstrating a coefficient of variation below 2%.
summary: This panel illustrates the mass of the samples after injection with silicone oil. The data shows a coefficient of variation below 2%, which indicates a highly consistent silicone oil filling process across the 72 samples. This confirms that the post-processing infiltration step effectively achieves uniform mass distribution.

caption: Equilibrium grain boundary concentration of solutes X (H, C, N, O, B, S) in Ni Σ5 [001](210) STGB as a function of bulk concentration at 1073 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the equilibrium grain boundary concentration of various nonmetallic solutes in Ni Σ5 [001](210) STGB at 1073 K, derived from McLean's equation and DFT-calculated segregation energies. Notably, the sulfur concentration remains constant at 100 at.% regardless of increasing bulk concentration, highlighting its strong segregation behavior in nickel grain boundaries.

caption: Surface topography of the vertical strut belonging to the additively manufactured FCCZ lattice structure.
summary: This panel presents the surface topography of a vertical strut in the FCCZ lattice structure. Using 3D morphometry, the surface morphology and roughness were measured to characterize the vertical strut's structural integrity, highlighting the surface finish achieved during the additive manufacturing of the lattice framework.

caption: Live inference frame captured without region-of-interest (ROI) filtering, showing scattered crack detections across the field of view.
summary: This live inference frame demonstrates the performance of the detection system without ROI filtering. Detections appear scattered across the entire frame, failing to localize effectively. The system primarily focuses on a few large cracks, indicating that the absence of ROI filtering leads to suboptimal detection coverage and precision.

caption: Diffusion path of the 3L|3R couple plotted on the Ni-Cr-Al ternary phase diagram, highlighting the Kirkendall plane, characteristic features 1-3, interdiffusion zone boundaries, and end-member compositions.
summary: The diffusion path for the 3L|3R couple is mapped onto the Ni-Cr-Al ternary phase diagram, revealing an elongated path through the γ zone. Key features include the Kirkendall plane, specific characteristic points within the diffusion zone, and the end-member compositions, demonstrating good qualitative agreement with theoretical diffusion postulates.

caption: Corrosion current density values derived from polarization measurements for forged and AM Ti–6Al–4V, contrasting pre-charged and hydrogen-charged conditions.
summary: Corrosion current density data provides a quantitative assessment of the corrosion resistance of Ti–6Al–4V. By comparing forged and AM samples before and after hydrogen charging, this plot helps determine the hydrogen susceptibility of the materials, revealing that the hydrogen effect is more pronounced in forged Ti–6Al–4V than in AM variants.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto465 dye.
summary: Transmission spectrum for a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto465 dye is shown. This dye is noted for its balanced filtering performance in the central region of the spectrum, providing effective wavelength modulation for color vision correction applications when printed at the standard 0.5 mm thickness.

caption: Optical micrograph of the SA2-NC SiC/Al composite surface, emphasizing the dislocation between SiC particles and the aluminum alloy due to residual carbon.
summary: This panel highlights the specific structural failure in the SA2-NC sample, where residual carbon prevents effective infiltration of the aluminum alloy into the SiC particle gaps. This lack of filling causes dislocations between the phases, consistent with the observed lamellar cracking and pore defects found in the composite material.

caption: Three-dimensional graph illustrating the particle flow trajectories and positions at different moments for the strip material.
summary: Three-dimensional trajectories of particle flow on the strip material are presented here. The visualization tracks the movement of particles over time, demonstrating how the strip material's flow is influenced by the rotational direction of the tool head, excluding particles near the tool head end and axis shoulder.

caption: Grain boundary ODF plot for the second area, depicting axis/angle relationships with a 5° misorientation tolerance.
summary: The grain boundary ODF plot for the second area illustrates the distribution of axis/angle relationships. Using a 5° misorientation tolerance, this visualization highlights the specific crystallographic relationships present, offering a statistical representation of the grain boundary network observed in the corresponding Taylor factor map.

caption: Pareto optimal solution set visualized through a point density mapping method, where darker color intensities represent regions of higher solution concentration.
summary: This visualization displays the Pareto optimal solution set using a point density mapping technique. The plot highlights specific regions where solutions are concentrated, with darker colors indicating higher densities. This approach effectively illustrates the distribution and clustering of optimal solutions within the design space, providing clear insight into solution density.

caption: High-speed imaging sequence of a melt bridge collapse on track 316, illustrating the progression of necking and subsequent separation into two melt droplets.
summary: Captured using high-speed imaging on track 316, this sequence illustrates the progression of necking in a melt bridge. The process continues until the melt separates into two distinct droplets, with one remaining attached to the wire end and the other adhering to the solidified track and the underlying substrate.

caption: Absorption coefficient spectrum of CoZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles plotted against wavelength.
summary: CoZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles exhibit an absorption coefficient spectrum characterized by high values at shorter wavelengths, which subsequently decline as the wavelength increases within the 350 to 390 nm range. This spectral behavior reflects the fundamental optical properties of the nanoparticles as they relate to their specific bandgap and electronic structure.

caption: Geometric representation of the honeycomb unit-cell dimensions.
summary: This figure illustrates the geometric configuration and specific dimensions of the honeycomb unit-cell. It provides a clear structural representation of the repeating unit, defining the spatial parameters necessary for understanding the honeycomb lattice architecture as referenced in the study of its fundamental unit-cell dimensions.

caption: Bode impedance diagram illustrating impedance magnitude and phase-angle frequency dependence for composites and pure copper after 1 h of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
summary: Bode plots reveal higher impedance magnitudes and broader phase-angle peaks for the composites, confirming enhanced corrosion resistance. The diagram highlights two distinct frequency regions: a low-frequency region associated with diffusion processes and a high-frequency region related to corrosion behavior, supporting the observation of a protective film formed on the composite surfaces.

caption: TEM image of the 15NNi2 Cu43.5Zr51Al3.5Ni2 alloy after pin-on-disc wear testing.
summary: The TEM image shows the 15NNi2 sample of the Cu43.5Zr51Al3.5Ni2 alloy after it has been subjected to pin-on-disc wear testing. This visualization is essential for evaluating the microstructural stability and potential phase changes occurring in the material under mechanical stress and wear, specifically for this nickel-containing composition.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing iso-concentration surfaces for alloy 4 aged at 510 °C for 16 h.
summary: This panel displays the atom probe tomography reconstruction for alloy 4 after aging at 510 °C for 16 h. The iso-concentration surfaces visualize the distribution of elements within the alloy, providing a 3D representation of the microstructure developed under these specific thermal processing conditions.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of 1a (2.98 × 10^-5 M) in acetonitrile under 405 nm LED irradiation, showing negligible intensity changes over 2-minute intervals.
summary: Steady-state photolysis of 1a alone in acetonitrile under 405 nm LED irradiation demonstrates remarkable photostability. The absorption spectrum shows negligible intensity changes over time, confirming that the molecule remains stable without any additives during the irradiation process, as evidenced by the lack of spectral evolution in the recorded data.

caption: Two-dimensional microhardness map generated from the indentation grid across the deposit, HAZ, and base plate regions.
summary: The microhardness map provides a spatial representation of mechanical properties across the deposit, HAZ, and base plate. By mapping the indentation results, the figure illustrates the hardness distribution throughout the sample, highlighting the transition between the different zones and providing the necessary data for the subsequent hardness profile analysis.

caption: Bode-Z impedance plots of as-built and as-cast Co25Cr5Mo5W alloy specimens measured at open-circuit potential in physiological saline.
summary: Bode-Z plots display the impedance magnitude of as-built and as-cast specimens in physiological saline. These observations align with the Nyquist plot analysis, supporting the superior corrosion resistance of the as-built specimen, which is attributed to its enhanced capacitive response and the formation of a stable passive film.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curves for as-cast and L-PBF Cu-10Sn samples up to 1200 °C at 10 °C/min, with an inset highlighting specific transformation peaks.
summary: DSC heating curves compare the thermal response of as-cast and L-PBF Cu-10Sn samples. The data identifies specific transformation temperatures, including the onset transformation temperature for the delta phase. The inset provides a magnified view of the peaks, facilitating a detailed analysis of phase changes during heating.

caption: Bright-field TEM cross-sectional micrograph of Sanicro 25 alloy after 600 hours of exposure to AUSC steam at 650 ℃.
summary: This bright-field TEM cross-sectional micrograph illustrates the microstructural state of Sanicro 25 after undergoing 600 hours of oxidation in AUSC steam at 650 ℃. The image provides a detailed view of the material's internal structure, serving as a primary observation for evaluating the oxidation behavior of the alloy under these specific conditions.

caption: Photographic evidence of successfully produced 10x10x5 mm3 cubic bimetals fabricated using low and medium process parameter sets without external defects.
summary: This photograph demonstrates the successful fabrication of 10x10x5 mm3 cubic bimetals. By utilizing selected low and medium process parameter sets, the samples were produced reproducibly. The visual evidence confirms that these cubic bimetals were manufactured without any noticeable external defects, validating the chosen process parameters for this geometry.

caption: Capacity-voltage curves representing the electrochemical performance of the Tongji dataset under charging cycles and the MIT dataset under discharging cycles.
summary: Capacity-voltage curves for the Tongji and MIT datasets reveal distinct electrochemical performance characteristics during charging and discharging cycles, respectively. These curves provide a detailed view of the voltage-capacity relationship, further demonstrating the variability in battery ageing patterns observed across cells, even when they are produced under identical experimental conditions.

caption: Quantitative WDS elemental analysis results for five specific locations along the upward building direction.
summary: Quantitative WDS analysis results are presented for five locations along the upward building direction, including the coarse-grained region, the junction, the fine-grained region, the lower edge, and black precipitation phases. These data points are essential for understanding the solid-solution concentration differences that contribute to the alloy's yield strength.

caption: Magnified mass spectrum segment highlighting specific ion peaks for the Al 6026 sample, demonstrating the spectral resolution achieved by the Invizo 6000 and LEAP 4000 X Si.
summary: This panel provides a magnified view of a selected mass-to-charge region for the Al 6026 sample. By comparing the spectra from the LEAP 4000 X Si and Invizo 6000, it showcases the instrument-specific peak characteristics and resolution capabilities observed during the collection of the first 20 million ions.

caption: Irregular cell configuration generated by applying Gaussian-distributed perturbations to seed point coordinates.
summary: This panel depicts the development of stochastic trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron cellular configurations. The irregularity is achieved through controlled perturbation of seed point positions along the three principal axes, governed by specific Gaussian distribution parameters, allowing for the creation of diverse cell geometries within the overall porous structure modeling framework.

caption: Precipitation-induced hardening contribution, defined as the difference in CRSS between samples with and without precipitates, plotted against precipitate radius.
summary: This panel displays the hardening contribution of precipitates, calculated as the difference in CRSS between samples with and without precipitates. Assuming grain size remains stable across heat treatments, the plot reveals three distinct regimes of hardening, each corresponding to the dominance of specific dislocation-precipitate interaction mechanisms.

caption: Load–displacement curve for the thin-walled structure without straight walls, exhibiting a continuous increase in compression load during the plastic deformation stage due to the sinx function shape.
summary: This load–displacement curve illustrates the mechanical response of a thin-walled structure without straight walls fabricated via the BMD process. The data shows a continuous increase in compression load during the plastic deformation stage, which is attributed to the specific sinx function geometry influencing the deformation mode of the structure.

caption: Enhanced view of the creep curves focusing on the discrete steps where changes in slope occur.
summary: This enhanced view provides a detailed examination of the creep curves, specifically focusing on the steps where the slope of the deformation curve changes. The visualization reveals that while the curves initially overlap, they progressively diverge with each subsequent step, indicating distinct stages of material deformation and damage accumulation.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curve of the PEEK filament, showing weight loss as a function of temperature.
summary: The TGA curve of the PEEK filament illustrates its thermal degradation behavior. A significant observation is the final residual weight of approximately 50% beyond 800 °C, which is attributed to the thermally stable aromatic content of the polymer, highlighting its suitability for high-temperature and flame-retardant applications.

caption: Side-view bright field STEM micrograph of the deformed AB specimen, showing the cellular structure and highly tangled dislocations within the cellular walls.
summary: This side-view bright field STEM micrograph of the deformed AB specimen illustrates the cellular structure and the highly tangled dislocations that compose the cellular walls. The inset provides a detailed view of a clean cellular wall region, where the wall thickness is measured to be approximately 30 nm.

caption: Chromatic dispersion profile of the fabricated fiber compared against the reference material dispersion of bulk CD-16 glass.
summary: This plot illustrates the measured chromatic dispersion characteristics of the fabricated fiber. By comparing these results to the reference material dispersion of bulk CD-16 glass, the figure highlights the specific optical performance of the fiber. The data confirms the successful characterization of the fiber's dispersion properties as reported in the study.

caption: Effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) profiles for the multilayer absorber samples, with color-coded data corresponding to the specific layer designs presented in panel (a).
summary: Panel (b) illustrates the effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of the multilayer absorbers, using color-coded data that correlates directly with the samples defined in panel (a). The results demonstrate the microwave absorption performance, with one configuration achieving a reflection loss of −11.59 dB at 16.6 GHz and an EAB of 3.2 GHz.

caption: PLS-DA score plot demonstrating the separation of metabolite profiles between Ti, Ti/EB 0.05, and Ti/EB 0.5 groups in in vitro macrophage cultures.
summary: The PLS-DA score plot illustrates a clear separation between the three experimental groups, indicating distinct metabolic profiles. The analysis achieved a correlation coefficient of 0.997 and an accuracy of 0.556, confirming that the metabolic responses of macrophages are significantly influenced by the different surface treatments applied in the study.

caption: Variations in melt pool geometry for a three-laser powder bed fusion setup printing a single track with 0.02 mm thickness, showing the formation of a singular long melt pool.
summary: Panel (a) displays the melt pool geometry resulting from a three-laser powder bed fusion process with a 0.02 mm track thickness. The image illustrates the formation of a singular, continuous long melt pool, highlighting the geometric characteristics achieved under these specific printing parameters for the multi-laser configuration.

caption: Training and validation accuracy and loss curves for the CNN model applied to the Stringing defect category.
summary: This panel presents the training and validation accuracy and loss curves for the CNN model as it learns to identify Stringing defects. The curves track the model's performance metrics over time, demonstrating how effectively the CNN architecture converges and validates its predictive accuracy when classifying this particular type of printing defect.

caption: Comparison of segregation energy (ΔEseg) values for Al, Zn, and Gd solutes in a magnesium matrix, derived from both an analytic model and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
summary: This figure presents the calculated segregation energy values for Al, Zn, and Gd solutes within a magnesium matrix. The data compares results obtained through an analytic model against those from previous DFT work. These values are essential for understanding solute behavior and distribution within the magnesium alloy system.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map along the build direction (BD) demonstrating a <001> texture in ferrite and a <101> texture in austenite.
summary: This IPF map along the build direction (BD) characterizes the crystallographic texture of the thermally treated LPBF DSS 2205. Ferrite exhibits a strong <001> texture along the BD, while austenite primarily displays a <101> texture. These distinct orientations suggest the potential existence of specific orientation relationships between the two phases.

caption: Predicted mean particle radius versus time using the SF z factor for isothermal aging at an alternative condition.
summary: Displaying the final set of predictions, this panel uses the SF z factor to model particle coarsening. The simulation results are compared with measured data, including error bars for 3D particle size approximations, to validate the model's ability to capture the plateau in mean particle radius during aging.

caption: Atomic morphology of the refined zone (RZ) post-unloading, with color intensity mapping z-direction displacement.
summary: Atomic morphology of the refined zone (RZ) post-unloading is presented, with atomic color intensity representing the displacement in the z direction. Red indicates positive displacement and blue indicates negative displacement, characterizing the atomic morphology of this micro-zone after the completion of the nanoindentation process.

caption: TG curves of 3D-printed geopolymers at 28 days of age, demonstrating increased mass loss in the initial 50–300 °C stage compared to earlier ages.
summary: At 28 days, the TG curves show a greater mass loss in the first stage (50–300 °C) compared to the 4-hour and 7-day samples. This indicates significant changes in the geopolymer structure and moisture content, reflecting the long-term impact of microwave heating on the final geopolymerization performance.

caption: IPF-Z orientation maps of the as-printed WAAM condition and specimens subjected to HIP 1–4 treatments, revealing grain orientation evolution across processing states.
summary: IPF-Z orientation maps illustrate the microstructural evolution of the WAAM-printed specimens across various HIP treatments. These maps provide a visual assessment of grain orientation changes resulting from thermal processing, complementing the high-resolution EBSD–EDS mapping and backscattered electron imaging used to evaluate the microstructural state of the studied specimens.

caption: Proteomics mass spectrometry analysis showing the total number of proteins adsorbed on the Ti-MgPi coated sample versus the uncoated Ti control.
summary: Proteomics mass spectrometry analysis demonstrates that the Ti-MgPi coated sample possesses a superior plasma protein adsorption capacity, successfully adsorbing 97 proteins. In contrast, the uncoated Ti control substrate shows a lower capacity, adsorbing only 76 proteins, highlighting the improved surface properties provided by the MgPi coating.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the IN718-0.5GNP composite showing a carbide particle located at a grain boundary.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays a selected region of the IN718-0.5GNP composite. The micrograph highlights a carbide particle situated at a grain boundary, which is characteristic of the microstructure in this composite material. The dashed line indicates the path used for subsequent compositional line profile analysis of the particle.

caption: Atom probe tomography (APT) reconstruction maps of Ti distribution at locations i (TW1), iv, and v, highlighting primary γ′ precipitates via 20.80 at% Al + Ti isoconcentration surfaces in blue and secondary γ′ precipitates via 6.00 at% Al + Ti isoconcentration surfaces in orange.
summary: This APT reconstruction displays the spatial distribution of Ti at specific locations within the material. Primary γ′ precipitates are identified by 20.80 at% Al + Ti isoconcentration surfaces, while secondary γ′ precipitates are delineated by 6.00 at% Al + Ti surfaces. These maps provide critical insights into phase chemistry and precipitation morphology.

caption: Bode magnitude and phase angle plots for Cast-1100 and LPBF 316L stainless steel samples, displaying experimental data points alongside theoretical fitting curves.
summary: Bode plots provide frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle data for Cast-1100 and LPBF 316L stainless steel in 3.5 wt% NaCl. These curves, representing experimental measurements and corresponding fitting results, are used to characterize the corrosion resistance and passive film properties of the different steel samples.

caption: Magnetization (M) versus magnetic field (H) hysteresis loops obtained from different spatial positions along the directionally solidified (DS) rod.
summary: Magnetization loops for the directionally solidified rod are presented to characterize its magnetic behavior and phase transformation properties. These M-H curves, measured at various positions along the rod, provide essential data for evaluating the magnetic response and structural consistency of the material across its length during the solidification process.

caption: Sensitivity analysis of TTR at 165 MPa showing the impact of input parameters.
summary: This sensitivity analysis evaluates the influence of various parameters on the time to rupture (TTR) at an applied stress of 165 MPa. Results indicate that the pre-factor of glide velocity (a1), the cavitation damage pre-factor (A), and the activation volume (Vr) exert the most significant impact on the TTR.

caption: Square wave voltammograms of Cr-doped and Cr-free N3S melts at 1150 °C, showing the matrix signal, Cr-doped signal, and their difference at 100 Hz and 100 mV pulse amplitude.
summary: Square wave voltammograms for N3S melts at 1150 °C illustrate the electrochemical response of Cr species. By subtracting the matrix signal from the Cr-doped signal, the reduction peaks for Cr VI/Cr III and Cr III/Cr II couples are identified at approximately -30 mV and -840 mV, respectively.

caption: Raman spectrum acquired from the wear track after tribo-testing with Ti3C2Tx, exhibiting signals from degraded MXene and carbonaceous species.
summary: Raman analysis of the wear track after tribo-testing with Ti3C2Tx additives reveals characteristic bands associated with degraded MXene alongside carbon-related signals. These spectral features confirm the formation of a mixed tribofilm, demonstrating the chemical transformation of the MXene additive within the contact zone during the tribological test.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image and corresponding fast Fourier transform patterns illustrating the interface orientation relationship between Al2Cu and β2-phases in Alloy B after 5 hours of annealing at 500 °C.
summary: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy imaging reveals the structural interface between Al2Cu and β2-phases in Alloy B following a 5-hour annealing treatment at 500 °C. Fast Fourier transform analysis of the interface provides critical insights into the orientation relationship between these two distinct phases within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Illustration of the proximal tibial bone tunnel ligament-bone healing model, depicting the surgical implantation of a tendon graft secured by an interference screw.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the surgical procedure for establishing a proximal tibial bone tunnel ligament-bone healing model. It specifically highlights the implantation of a tendon graft into the tibial tunnel, which is subsequently stabilized using an interference screw to facilitate the study of bone-implant integration.

caption: Long-term galvanostatic stability evaluation for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performed at a constant current density of 50 mAcm-2 for 125 hours.
summary: Presented here is the 125-hour galvanostatic stability test for the oxygen evolution reaction. Conducted at room temperature with a constant current density of 50 mAcm-2, the plot illustrates the electrochemical stability and performance retention of the catalyst during prolonged anodic operation, confirming its durability for the oxygen evolution process.

caption: Accumulated misorientation profile along the indicated arrow for a clearance of 0.186 mm, showing values below 1 degree.
summary: The line graph displays the accumulated misorientation measured along the specified arrow for a 0.186 mm clearance. The data confirms that the misorientation remains consistently below 1 degree, indicating minimal lattice distortion or orientation deviation at the seed edge under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Full-pattern neutron powder diffractogram of the HIP-4 treated specimen, representing the final stage of the hot isostatic pressing treatment series.
summary: The HIP-4 diffractogram completes the series of full-pattern measurements for the WAAM material. It provides critical volume-averaged data on the final phase state, illustrating the long-term stability of the matrix and secondary phases after the most intensive hot isostatic pressing condition applied in this study.

caption: Chronopotentiometry stability curve of Ru3Ni3NAs in 0.5 M H2SO4 at a constant current density of 5 mA cm-2.
summary: The chronopotentiometry curve for Ru3Ni3NAs in 0.5 M H2SO4 demonstrates the long-term electrochemical stability of the catalyst. By maintaining a constant current density of 5 mA cm-2, this test assesses the durability and potential degradation of the Ru3Ni3NAs material during the oxygen evolution reaction in a concentrated acidic electrolyte.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and EDS maps illustrating the dendrite regions of the Ni–Al-Re-W alloy under the [001] zone axis.
summary: Dendrite regions of the Ni–Al-Re-W alloy are analyzed via HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping along the [001] zone axis. This visualization reveals the elemental distribution and structural characteristics inherent to the dendrite phase, providing essential data on the compositional variations within the alloy's complex microstructure during the solidification process.

caption: Computer-aided design models of sheet-based gyroid TPMS structures featuring relative densities of 12.5%, 25.0%, 37.5%, and 50.0%, corresponding to wall thicknesses of 0.16 mm, 0.34 mm, 0.53 mm, and 0.75 mm, respectively.
summary: These CAD models illustrate the geometric design of sheet-based gyroid lattice specimens. The structures are defined by four distinct relative densities ranging from 12.5% to 50.0%. Corresponding wall thicknesses are precisely engineered at 0.16 mm, 0.34 mm, 0.53 mm, and 0.75 mm to achieve the desired volumetric density for each specific lattice configuration.

caption: Three-dimensional surface contour of the mechanically polished (MP) sample, achieving a significantly smoother finish.
summary: Mechanical polishing of the sandblasted sample results in a refined surface with a roughness value of approximately 0.6 μm. This panel presents the three-dimensional contour of the MP sample, highlighting the effective removal of surface peaks and valleys compared to the previous sandblasted state.

caption: Box plots illustrating the onset potentials required for 10 mA cm-2 current density, with yellow circles indicating mean values and black horizontal lines marking medians, demonstrating a trend consistent with quasi steady-state measurements at 500 mA cm-2.
summary: Onset potentials for a 10 mA cm-2 current density are presented via box plots, showing mean and median values for various Fe-based alloys. This data follows the same trend observed in quasi steady-state measurements at 500 mA cm-2, including specific variations noted for the 59 at. % Fe alloy composition.

caption: Initial configuration for Test II involving two particles of unequal size.
summary: This panel shows the starting point for Test II, which investigates the sintering behavior of two particles with unequal sizes. The simulation captures the initial spatial distribution of the phase-field variables, setting the stage for analyzing the temporal evolution of particles with asymmetric dimensions during the sintering process.

caption: Detailed dimensions and geometry of the tensile test bar specimens used for mechanical property evaluation.
summary: This panel provides the specific measurements and geometric dimensions of the tensile test bars utilized in the mechanical evaluation of the AFSD Al-Cu build. These standardized specimens are essential for determining the tensile properties of the material, ensuring consistency and accuracy in the mechanical testing procedures described in the study.

caption: Load-axial displacement curves of notched BMG specimens subjected to varying loading rates, with an inset highlighting discrete load drops (Δf) occurring during the plastic-flow plateau.
summary: Tensile-testing results for notched BMG specimens demonstrate load-axial displacement behavior across different loading rates. The inset reveals characteristic load drops (Δf) within the plastic-flow plateau, which signify the release of elastic energy during the loading process, typically associated with the initiation and propagation of shear bands in the material.

caption: Flexural strength of cast samples after 28 days of curing with varying EBA and CBA incorporation ratios.
summary: Flexural strength of cast samples after 28 days of curing is shown, demonstrating an increase from 6.4 MPa for the control sample to 10.3 MPa with increasing EBA incorporation. Similarly, the incorporation of CBA results in an increase in flexural strength, reaching values up to 9.6 MPa.

caption: Isothermal decomposition curve of TiH2 powder measured at 595 °C.
summary: The isothermal decomposition curve of TiH2 powder is presented at a constant temperature of 595 °C. This plot illustrates the kinetics of the decomposition process, capturing the mass loss or heat flow changes over time to characterize the stability and reaction rate of the hydride at this specific temperature.

caption: STEM-ADF image of the as-cast NiTi alloy, highlighting the B2 cubic matrix grains alongside a darker Ni4Ti3 intermetallic precipitate located on the right side.
summary: This STEM-ADF micrograph reveals the microstructural features of an as-cast NiTi alloy. The image clearly distinguishes the NiTi cubic B2 matrix grains from a darker Ni4Ti3 intermetallic precipitate situated on the right, providing a visual basis for subsequent elemental mapping of the alloy's phase distribution.

caption: True/logarithmic compression data for alloy 7175, illustrating yield strength, true stress at 0.5 strain, ultimate compression strength, and fracture compression for different heat treatments.
summary: This panel illustrates the true/logarithmic compression data for alloy 7175, specifically focusing on yield strength, true stress at 0.5 strain, ultimate compression strength, and fracture compression. The data reflects various heat treatment conditions applied after an initial 90 °C/8 h step, with the peak-aged condition clearly identified by a red box.

caption: BSE-SEM micrograph of the oxidation products formed on the surface of the AlCoFeNiCu1 alloy.
summary: Oxidation products on the surface of the AlCoFeNiCu1 alloy are presented in this BSE-SEM micrograph. The image highlights the microstructural features of the oxide layer, with specific points analyzed via EDS to determine chemical composition, as referenced in Table 3 for points 1 through 14.

caption: Architecture of the proposed convolutional neural network designed for lower-dimensional representation learning.
summary: This schematic illustrates the structural design of the proposed convolutional neural network architecture. The model utilizes a shared representation learning encoder backbone, which is specifically based on a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN). This framework is intended to facilitate effective lower-dimensional representation of the input data for subsequent analytical tasks.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of the as-built Fe12Cr6Al alloy without Y2O3 addition, highlighting the presence of Al–N and Al–N–O precipitates within the matrix and at grain boundaries.
summary: This bright-field STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of an as-built Fe12Cr6Al alloy fabricated without Y2O3. The imaging reveals the distribution of Al–N and Al–N–O precipitates within the metallic matrix and along grain boundaries, providing a baseline for understanding precipitate formation in the absence of yttrium oxide additions.

caption: Storage stability evaluation of the CNT-Pt composite sensor, tracked via daily electrochemical testing of DA over a 14-day period.
summary: Stability of the CNT-Pt composite electrochemical sensor was verified through daily testing of DA over a 14-day storage period. The data confirms the sensor maintains consistent performance over time, indicating robust storage stability for the composite material when used for the detection of dopamine analytes.

caption: Photographic image of a flat sample prior to anodization, designated as FLAT-0.
summary: This panel displays a photographic image of a typical flat sample before undergoing any anodization process, referred to as FLAT-0. The image provides a visual baseline for the material state prior to the experimental modifications described in the study, serving as the initial reference point for subsequent photocatalytic activity testing.

caption: Photoluminescence spectra identifying Cr3+ emission peaks originating from the alumina layer formed on the alloy surfaces.
summary: Photoluminescence spectroscopy detects Cr3+ luminescence signals, which serve as a diagnostic indicator for the presence of alumina on the oxidized alloy surfaces. These spectral features provide evidence of the oxide scale composition developed during the 500-hour exposure at 650 °C, complementing the phase identification obtained through Raman analysis.

caption: Band gap distribution of I-type phononic crystals as a function of the density of the filling metal materials.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the density of filling materials and the resulting band gap distribution in I-type phononic crystals. By analyzing how varying material densities influence the band gap, the figure provides critical insights into the structural performance and wave propagation characteristics of these specific phononic crystal configurations.

caption: Experimental EXAFS functions χ(k)k² measured above the K-Fe absorption edge for Fe58Ni25B17 alloy samples in the initial melt-quenched (MQ) state and after high-pressure torsion (HPT) at 77 K.
summary: The EXAFS functions χ(k)k² for the Fe58Ni25B17 alloy at the K-Fe edge reveal structural differences between the MQ and HPT states. Atomic ordering present in the MQ state disappears after HPT at 77 K, which corresponds to a state with higher free energy compared to the partially relaxed MQ state.

caption: Grain boundary Orientation Distribution Function (ODF) plot displaying axis/angle relationships of interest, calculated within a 5° misorientation tolerance.
summary: This grain boundary ODF plot characterizes the misorientation relationships within the AS steel microstructure. By focusing on specific axis/angle pairs within a 5° tolerance, the plot provides quantitative insight into the crystallographic nature of the grain boundaries, complementing the Taylor factor analysis to explain strain accommodation mechanisms during deformation.

caption: Fluorescence Intensity Ratio (FIR) measurement outcomes obtained during the cycling experiment, presented independently of the calibration curve to demonstrate the method's inherent repeatability.
summary: The FIR measurement results presented here reflect the repeatability of the method throughout the thermal cycling experiment. By showing these outcomes independently of the calibration curve, the panel provides direct evidence of the measurement technique's stability and consistency across the ten cycles performed during the cryogenic thermal cycling process.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing stretched martensite laths with obscured boundaries in a solution-aged sample following tensile fracture.
summary: This TEM image reveals the fracture microstructure of a solution-aged sample, specifically highlighting martensite laths within the matrix. These laths appear stretched due to applied force, resulting in unclear boundaries. This observation provides evidence of the dislocation strengthening mechanism contributing to the material's overall mechanical strength after tensile loading.

caption: Reflectance spectral response of the sensor under 10 mW of 980 nm pump power as the relative humidity increases.
summary: This panel illustrates the reflectance spectral response of the sensor when subjected to a 10 mW pump power at 980 nm while the relative humidity is increased. The data demonstrates how higher pump power levels modulate the sensor's spectral behavior in response to varying humidity conditions.

caption: Optimization tests for process parameters involving twelve distinct combinations applied to single-layer laser processing.
summary: Twelve different parameter combinations were evaluated during process parameter optimization tests for laser processing of single-layer materials. These tests were conducted prior to printing the experimental specimens to ensure optimal laser processing conditions. The diagram outlines the experimental matrix used to refine the laser-directed energy deposition parameters.

caption: Current density versus voltage curves for Ti 97 Nb 3 PVD coated titanium expanded metal PTLs, illustrating the electrochemical response and performance decline over time.
summary: The I-V curves for Ti 97 Nb 3 PVD coated titanium expanded metal PTLs are presented here. These measurements highlight the electrochemical performance and stability of the expanded metal substrate. The data indicates that performance variations between different PTL configurations were minimal, potentially attributed to inherent manufacturing-related fluctuations.

caption: Kissinger analysis plot showing the normalized scanning rate as a function of inverse peak temperature, used to determine activation enthalpies.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the normalized scanning rate against the inverse peak temperature on a logarithmic scale. By applying linear regression to the data, the activation enthalpies, denoted as Q I and Q I I, are calculated. These values represent the kinetic parameters derived from the DSC measurements for the analyzed material.

caption: Arrhenius plot of Ni grain boundary diffusion coefficients in AM-fabricated CoCrFeMnNi alloy, showing distinct diffusion paths (Dgb and Dfast) and an overlaid DSC heat flow curve indicating exothermic relaxation processes across three temperature intervals.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays Ni tracer diffusion coefficients in AM-fabricated CoCrFeMnNi alloy as a function of inverse temperature. It identifies two short-circuit diffusion paths and correlates diffusion rates with exothermic heat flow, revealing three distinct temperature intervals that correspond to the relaxation of the fabrication-induced non-equilibrium state in the alloy.

caption: TGA thermograms conducted under an air atmosphere for 3D-printed model samples containing varying TiO2 weight percentages.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis was performed under an air atmosphere to assess the thermal properties of the 3D-printed samples. The thermograms illustrate the mass loss behavior of the model samples as a function of temperature, specifically highlighting the influence of different TiO2 loading levels on the thermal stability of the printed nanocomposites.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the solvent-cast nanocellulose composite membrane.
summary: This panel displays the FTIR spectrum for the solvent-cast nanocellulose composite membrane. As part of the chemical analysis provided in Fig. 3, this spectroscopic data characterizes the molecular composition of the material, allowing for the identification of functional groups present within the solvent-cast membrane structure.

caption: EDS elemental maps for Cr, Mo, and Ni showing pronounced microsegregation in the as-printed state and progressive chemical homogenization through HIP 2–4 treatments.
summary: EDS elemental maps visualize the distribution of Cr, Mo, and Ni. The as-printed state exhibits significant Cr and Mo microsegregation alongside Ni depletion. Higher HIP temperatures drive solute redistribution, leading to complete elemental homogenization by the HIP-4 condition, which directly correlates with the reduction in microsegregation observed in the EDS analysis.

caption: Comparison of fatigue crack growth rates for vertical L-PBF samples at 650 °C between 1 s and 90 s dwell loading conditions.
summary: Vertical L-PBF samples exhibit significantly higher fatigue crack growth rates, approximately an order of magnitude greater, when subjected to 90 s dwells compared to 1 s dwells. This trend is observed once the crack progresses beyond the initial arresting periods, highlighting a strong orientation-dependent sensitivity to dwell-time loading.

caption: Scatter plot showing the relationship between grain aspect ratio and yield strength in LPBF AlSi10Mg, demonstrating a lack of correlation and low predictive weight.
summary: The scatter plot demonstrates that grain aspect ratio has no apparent relationship to the yield strength of LPBF fabricated AlSi10Mg. The low weight assigned to this input variable in the GPR model confirms that changes in grain aspect ratio do not directly affect the mechanical output results.

caption: Cross-sectional slice of powder batch P3 illustrating the overall particle morphology and internal porosity.
summary: Representing the third powder batch, this X-ray CT cross-sectional slice demonstrates the specific morphology and intra-particle porosity of P3 particles. By visualizing the internal structure, this panel enables the identification of structural features and porosity levels, contributing to the overall evaluation of powder quality across the studied batches.

caption: Stereographic projection of the stress-induced martensite product M1, showing the correspondence of (100)α″, (010)α″, and (001)α″ poles to the β1 parent grain.
summary: The stereographic projection for the M1 martensite variant illustrates the orientation relationship with the parent β1 grain. Specifically, the (100)α″, (010)α″, and (001)α″ poles align with the (001)β, (110)β, and (1–10)β poles of the β1 grain, respectively, allowing for the precise identification of the crystallographic variant formed during stress-induced transformation.

caption: Tabulated hardening parameters utilized for the calibration of the EPSC model.
summary: This table presents the specific hardening parameters used to calibrate the EPSC model. The model calibration is achieved by fitting the macroscopic stress-strain behavior obtained from tensile loading experiments on a Ni-superalloy sample with a random grain orientation distribution, ensuring the model accurately reflects experimental observations.

caption: Detailed current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 2 m/min, complementing panel (a).
summary: This panel provides additional detail on the current-voltage characteristics for the 2 m/min wire feed rate condition. Consistent with the broader findings for this feed rate, the data confirms the observation of a relatively higher peak current and a lower peak duration during the thin wall deposition.

caption: Potential-resolved Ni dissolution rates recorded during the second peak of the slow cyclic voltammogram in step 4, characterizing the electrochemical response after the accelerated stress test.
summary: Panel b displays the potential-resolved Ni dissolution rates during the second peak of the slow cyclic voltammogram in step 4. Captured after the accelerated stress test, these results confirm the degradation trends established in previous figures, highlighting the electrochemical stability and dissolution characteristics of the Ni component post-stress.

caption: Tensile strength comparison of virgin and recycled fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites printed via LFAM, evaluated along the OX and OZ build orientations.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the tensile strength of virgin and recycled fiber-reinforced thermoplastic composites manufactured through Large Format Additive Manufacturing. The data compares performance across OX and OZ orientations, demonstrating that recycled materials maintain mechanical properties comparable to virgin counterparts, with performance influenced by specific processing parameters like temperature and flow rate.

caption: Enlarged view of the load-displacement data from panel (c), focusing on the pop-in stage to provide a detailed look at the initial deformation behavior.
summary: This enlarged view focuses specifically on the pop-in stage of the load-displacement data. By magnifying this region, the panel allows for a more precise examination of the initial deformation behavior, which is critical for understanding the resistance force against dislocation glide and the material's response during the early stages of indentation.

caption: NanoSIMS oxygen isotope profiles across the oxide layer of Ni-30Cr oxidized at 900 °C for 100 h, showing the distribution of 16O (blue), 18O (green), and total oxygen (purple) along a line indicated by a red arrow.
summary: NanoSIMS analysis of Ni-30Cr oxidized for 100 hours reveals the spatial distribution of oxygen isotopes. The 16O signal is concentrated near internal and external interfaces, while 18O is primarily located within the oxide layer band and as islets at the oxide/alloy interface, indicating specific oxygen diffusion pathways during the oxidation process.

caption: Raman spectra of the investigated superlattice structures in the 230-290 cm⁻¹ range, showing the GaAs-like interface region and variations in Sb contamination.
summary: Representing the 230-290 cm⁻¹ range, this panel illustrates the GaAs-like interface region of the superlattice structures. The spectral data reveals that the GaAs-like interface for samples P027 and P028 exhibits lower Sb contamination compared to the P033 and P032 samples, providing insight into the structural quality of the interfaces.

caption: Intermediate fluid flow pattern within the K8 structure at 0.50 s.
summary: Representing the flow state at 0.50 s, this photograph shows the ongoing two-phase fluid dynamics through the K8 structure at a flow rate of 0.145 ml/min. The image highlights the continued movement and morphological changes of the fluid phases as they traverse the internal pathways of the K8 specimen.

caption: Frequency distribution of current density values measured during the V-PEP polishing mode.
summary: The histogram represents the frequency distribution of current density signals specifically for the V-PEP polishing mode. Comparative analysis indicates that the fluctuation amplitude and the range of the frequency distribution are significantly greater under these vibrating conditions compared to non-vibrating modes, highlighting the impact of vibration on signal behavior.
