caption: Elemental area distribution map of the as-built AlSi10Mg alloy identifying fine, coarse, and heat-affected zones across the melt pool.
summary: The elemental distribution map of the as-built AlSi10Mg alloy reveals three distinct zones across the melt pool: a fine zone with a cell size of 0.35 μm, a coarse zone with a cell size of 0.7 μm, and a heat-affected zone, resulting from varying thermal histories during processing.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 and Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 measured between 200 K and 350 K.
summary: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves measured at 1 T demonstrate that Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 exhibits significantly larger absolute magnetization values compared to Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05. These curves confirm that the compounds undergo a magneto-structural transition (MST) within the investigated temperature range, as evidenced by the distinct magnetic response observed in the data.

caption: Experimental magnetic field-dependent magnetization (M-H) curves for Phytherm260® measured across a range of temperatures.
summary: Experimental magnetic field-dependent magnetization (M-H) curves for Phytherm260® measured across a range of temperatures. These measurements, as presented in Fig. 3, characterize the magnetic response of the material. The curves illustrate how the magnetization behavior of Phytherm260® evolves under varying external magnetic fields and thermal conditions, providing essential data for understanding its magnetic properties.

caption: Strain at yield radar plot showing the mechanical response of composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8 compared to the monolithic core.
summary: Strain at yield for various multi-material configurations is visualized using a radar plot. By comparing ratios from 0 to 0.8 against the monolithic core, represented by the gray area, this plot illustrates the deformation characteristics of the composites, aiding in the systematic selection of materials for specific mechanical applications.

caption: Dilatometry curves illustrating the ε → γ reverse martensitic transformation, with an inset detailing the graphical method used to determine the start (As) and finish (Af) critical temperatures.
summary: Dilatometry curves are presented to characterize the ε → γ reverse martensitic transformation. The inset provides a graphical procedure for identifying the specific start (As) and finish (Af) critical temperatures. This method allows for the precise determination of transformation temperatures based on the observed thermal expansion behavior of the material.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectrum of the PEGdiPDA crosslinker, demonstrating changes in optical properties indicative of photo-degradation reactions.
summary: The UV-Vis absorbance spectrum of the PEGdiPDA crosslinker shows distinct changes upon UV irradiation. These spectral shifts indicate the occurrence of photo-degradation reactions within the material. The data confirms that the chemical structure of the crosslinker is actively modified by the UV light, facilitating the subsequent collapse of the hydrogel.

caption: Calculated phase fraction of the Cu-matrix in Cu–9Ni–6Sn-xAl alloys aged at 450 °C.
summary: The phase fraction of the Cu-matrix in Cu–9Ni–6Sn-xAl alloys aged at 450 °C is presented based on thermodynamic modeling. This result characterizes the stability and volume fraction of the matrix phase in the presence of varying Al concentrations under the specified aging conditions.

caption: Raw detector frame captured by the central Varex XRD 4343CT area detector, displaying the characteristic diffraction pattern generated during the in-situ oxidation experiment.
summary: An example of a raw detector frame obtained from the central Varex XRD 4343CT area detector is presented. This image captures the diffraction pattern resulting from the in-situ synchrotron GI-XRD oxidation experiment, serving as the primary data source for subsequent structural analysis and diffractogram calculation.

caption: Mott-Schottky (M-S) plot illustrating the electrochemical response of NiCu alloy coatings modified with 1 wt % h-BN in a 10 wt % NaNO3 solution.
summary: This panel presents the M-S curve for NiCu alloy coatings containing 1 wt % h-BN, tested in a 10 wt % NaNO3 solution. By comparing these results with the baseline, researchers can assess how h-BN additions influence the semiconductor properties and donor density of the passive film.

caption: Microhardness distribution map across the interface of the as-built (AB) multi-material sample.
summary: This microhardness distribution map covers a 0.5 × 0.5 mm2 area at the interface of the as-built multi-material sample. It provides a baseline for evaluating hardness variations across the interface region, showing the initial hardness values before any subsequent heat treatment processes are applied to the material.

caption: Depth of the melt pool represented as a function of varying laser power and scan speed conditions.
summary: This panel illustrates the depth of the melt pool as a function of laser power and scan speed. By mapping these processing variables, the plot characterizes the vertical penetration of the melt pool, which is essential for understanding the overall geometry and aspect ratio of the resulting material features.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 3 fabricated via standard PCB fabrication.
summary: This plot shows the reflection coefficient of antenna design 3 created using standard PCB fabrication methods. Plotted with Origin software, the data provides a benchmark for the reflection performance of the antenna, facilitating an evaluation of how traditional PCB manufacturing compares to additive manufacturing techniques like AJP and screen printing.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the twin boundary, oriented along the [110] beta zone axis.
summary: This selected area electron diffraction pattern, taken along the [110] beta zone axis, characterizes the twin boundary structure. The pattern confirms the crystallographic nature of the {332}<113> beta deformation twin observed in the lower area of the specimen after the bending deformation process.

caption: Electrochemical parameters derived from polarization curves for unrolled specimens, showing variations in corrosion current density, corrosion potential, and pitting potential as a function of heat treatment temperature.
summary: Electrochemical parameters for unrolled specimens demonstrate that increasing heat treatment temperature causes the corrosion current density to increase then decrease, while the corrosion potential decreases then increases. Additionally, the passivation region narrows and then widens, indicating complex changes in the corrosion resistance of the unrolled material due to thermal processing.

caption: Fracture evolution process of sample B under compressive strain ranging from 0 to 0.5.
summary: Sample B demonstrates a specific fracture evolution sequence during compressive testing between 0 and 0.5 strain. Documenting these changes allows for a detailed assessment of how the material responds to mechanical stress, contributing to the broader analysis of fracture characteristics across the different sample groups under identical loading parameters.

caption: STS spectra and normalized conductance (dI/dV)/(I/V) for the thermally grown oxide on alloy 600 after one week of oxidation at 623 K, demonstrating semiconductor behavior with a distinct potential gap.
summary: This panel displays the STS spectra and normalized conductance for an oxide layer on alloy 600 oxidized at 623 K for one week. The data reveals characteristic semiconductor behavior, featuring exponential current changes separated by a significant potential gap where current remains at zero within the experimental detection limit.

caption: Water TDS-GU spectra corresponding to the hydrogen measurements in panel a, demonstrating a 10-fold higher sensitivity and significant signal increases following atmospheric exposure.
summary: Water TDS-GU spectra corresponding to the hydrogen measurements in panel a are presented with a 10-fold increase in sensitivity. The data reveal a substantial rise in the water signal after 1 minute of atmospheric exposure, confirming that peaks observed in the hydrogen spectra are largely attributed to adsorbed surface water.

caption: Coefficient of friction trends for neat PEEK and composites as a function of sliding distance under distilled water lubrication.
summary: This graph displays the friction coefficient evolution for neat PEEK and composites when subjected to distilled water lubrication. Compared to dry sliding, the presence of water effectively reduces the running-in period, demonstrating the influence of liquid lubrication on the tribological stability and friction response of the tested materials.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of the composite materials.
summary: This graph displays the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) for the composite materials as a function of temperature. It characterizes the dimensional stability of the composites, highlighting how the material expands or contracts in response to thermal changes, which is critical for evaluating their reliability in thermal applications.

caption: C atom map featuring a 5 at.% isoconcentration surface, highlighting regions where carbon segregation is likely associated with the presence of carbides.
summary: This panel displays the C atom map with a 5 at.% isoconcentration surface. These highlighted regions indicate localized carbon enrichment, which is attributed to the presence of carbides within the as-built sample, providing insight into the microstructural features formed during the solidification process.

caption: Orthorhombic supercell representation of a rotated fcc lattice, highlighting the spatial arrangement of Ni atoms in gray and alloying element atoms at the corners in black, with defined lattice vectors.
summary: This visualization displays an orthorhombic supercell of a rotated fcc lattice, illustrating the atomic configuration where Ni atoms are depicted in gray and alloying elements in black. Each alloying element replaces a single Ni atom within the shear plane of the 12-atom supercell, which contains 12 unique atomic positions.

caption: SRIM-simulated energy loss profiles (MeV/μm) plotted against penetration depth for alpha particles with initial energies ranging from 6.5 MeV to 10 MeV.
summary: SRIM-simulated energy loss profiles are shown as a function of depth for alpha particles with energies between 6.5 MeV and 10 MeV. This plot illustrates the characteristic energy deposition behavior of alpha particles as they penetrate the material, highlighting the relationship between initial particle energy and depth-dependent energy loss.

caption: Cr L-edge NEXAFS spectra recorded in TEY mode for CoCrFeNi compared to pure Cr, showing a shift of -0.3 eV.
summary: Cr L-edge NEXAFS spectra in TEY mode reveal the electronic environment of Cr in CoCrFeNi. Compared to pure Cr, the CoCrFeNi alloy exhibits a shift of -0.3 eV. This shift provides indirect evidence of the peculiar surroundings of Cr and correlates with the presence of chemical short-range order in the alloy.

caption: Plastic vortex profile generated in steel, demonstrating the specific material flow characteristics during the VFSAM process.
summary: Steel undergoes the VFSAM process to form a distinct plastic vortex profile. As part of a broader demonstration of material versatility, this panel highlights how the internal friction generated by the rod results in a specific vortex geometry unique to the steel specimen during the plastic deformation process.

caption: Atomic structure after two layers of deposition, showing the onset of plasticity characterized by dislocation nucleation and glide along slip systems toward the interface.
summary: After two layers are deposited, the MD simulation reveals the onset of plastic deformation. Dislocation nucleation is observed, with these defects gliding along various slip systems and migrating toward the interface. This structural evolution marks the transition from initial atomic contact to more complex deformation mechanisms within the material.

caption: System architecture diagram illustrating the workflow for transmitting printing parameters and path data to the control system.
summary: This schematic illustrates the operational workflow for the printing control system. It details the specific steps required to transmit essential printing parameters and the designated printing path to the controller. This process ensures accurate execution of the printing instructions, facilitating precise control over the additive manufacturing system's hardware and software components.

caption: Discharge curves for annealed La1.8Mg1.2Ni9 alloy electrodes plotted as a function of discharge current density.
summary: This panel illustrates the discharge curves for the annealed La1.8Mg1.2Ni9 alloy electrode at various discharge current densities. The electrochemical behavior of this alloy is compared against the other compositions. While initial discharge capacities are similar across all studied alloys, this composition exhibits distinct variations as current density increases.

caption: Boundary map of the BCC phase for Alloy 3 deformed at 1100 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹, highlighting the distribution of grain boundaries within the microstructure.
summary: Representing the BCC phase of Alloy 3 deformed at 1100 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹, this boundary map visualizes the grain structure. The analysis focuses on the spatial distribution of boundaries, with the FCC phase appearing as black regions throughout the map to provide context for the BCC phase morphology.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for Mn, Fe, and Ni dopants in their respective amorphous alloys, showing spin-up and spin-down band peaks positioned on opposite sides of the Fermi level.
summary: This panel presents the PDOS for Mn, Fe, and Ni dopants. The peaks for the spin-up and spin-down bands are observed on both sides of the Fermi level, illustrating the distinct electronic configurations and magnetic characteristics introduced by these specific transition metal dopants into the amorphous alloy structure.

caption: Oscillation frequencies extracted from TRMOKE measurements and resonant frequencies from FMR measurements plotted against external magnetic field for 3Py/3Pt and 3Ta/3CoFeB samples, with Kittel equation fits shown as red curves.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic oscillation frequencies of 3Py/3Pt and 3Ta/3CoFeB samples as a function of the applied magnetic field. Data points derived from TRMOKE and FMR measurements are compared against Kittel equation fits, demonstrating the consistency between optical and resonance-based characterization techniques for these magnetic thin-film systems.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves showing the rate of mass loss for the PLA/LNR blend and PLA/LNR/CNC bionanocomposites.
summary: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves show the rate of mass loss for the PLA/LNR blend and PLA/LNR/CNC bionanocomposites. These curves provide insight into the thermal degradation kinetics of the materials, allowing for a direct comparison of the thermal stability between the control PLA/LNR blend and the CNC-reinforced bionanocomposites.

caption: Atomic model depicting an overlapped twin structure where two atomic columns appear to merge.
summary: The atomic model for an overlapped twin demonstrates how two atomic columns can appear to merge into a single position due to limitations in spherical aberration and spatial resolution. This model explains the visual characteristics observed in the HRTEM images of the twin boundary region in the QWT-DZ alloy.

caption: Common Neighbor Analysis (CNA) diagram of Ti6Al4V–NbZr1 alloy fabricated under high heat input (HHI) conditions.
summary: Shown is the CNA pattern for the Ti6Al4V–NbZr1 alloy processed with high heat input. By comparing this diagram with those from lower heat inputs, the influence of thermal energy on phase variation and atomic configuration is highlighted, supporting the comprehensive analysis of the WAAM fabrication process for this specific alloy.

caption: Western blot analysis of FAK-related proteins and ERK1/2 signaling pathway components in AD-MSCs after 7 days of treatment with gel or Dopa-gel.
summary: Western blot data confirm the significant upregulation of FAK-related proteins in the Dopa-gel group compared to other groups. Furthermore, the protein levels of ERK1/2 and the phosphorylated ERK2 at Thr202/Tyr204 sites were examined, demonstrating that the Dopa-gel treatment actively influences these critical intracellular signaling pathways within the AD-MSCs.

caption: Total generation and admissible region for the IEEE 69-node system represented as a contour plot.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the total generation and admissible region for the IEEE 69-node system. The visualization provides a clear representation of the operational constraints and generation capabilities within the specified electrical network, serving as a critical analytical tool for evaluating system performance and stability under defined conditions.

caption: Minimum creep rates for PBF-EB/M processed single crystals modeled with SESF-related slip systems across three tensile loading orientations.
summary: Minimum creep rates for PBF-EB/M processed single crystals are depicted using SESF-related slip systems. The graph shows the predicted rates for three tensile loading directions, [001], [011], and [111], derived from the material parameter sets in Table 3, highlighting the creep performance of these specific specimen orientations.

caption: Strain-time evolution recorded during the initial creep exposure phase prior to interruption at 5.0% strain.
summary: This panel displays the strain-time data collected during the first creep exposure. The experiment was interrupted at a strain level of 5.0% to facilitate subsequent cooling and potential rejuvenation treatments, providing a baseline for evaluating the material's creep behavior before any further processing or continuation of the mechanical test.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the MPI region in a 95 W LPBF-processed Nd-Fe-B magnet.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the microstructure of the MPI region within a 95 W LPBF-processed Nd-Fe-B magnet. The imaging technique highlights the local atomic structure, providing a clear view of the grain morphology and distribution characteristic of this specific laser power processing condition.

caption: Magnified STEM image of a single precipitate in A550, displaying internal stacking faults.
summary: High-magnification STEM imaging of a single precipitate in the A550 sample reveals the presence of internal stacking faults. These structural defects are associated with the low stacking fault energy characteristic of the C14 Laves phase, providing insight into the internal crystalline nature of the precipitates.

caption: Selective area diffraction pattern obtained from the deformed microstructure.
summary: The selective area diffraction pattern provides crystallographic evidence of the material's state after deformation at 5 s⁻¹. Analysis of the diffraction spots in this pattern, in conjunction with the corresponding calibration, confirms the presence of a deformation twin structure within the analyzed region.

caption: Integral breadth analysis results illustrating the calculated average crystallite size and lattice microstrain for the thermally compensated H13 steel variants.
summary: Integral breadth analysis is applied to the XRD data to determine the average crystallite size of coherent diffraction regions and the lattice microstrain in the H13 steel specimens. These parameters are critical for evaluating dislocation density, which is subsequently used to model the contribution of dislocation strengthening to the yield strength.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the FeCrMnNi CSA in its pristine state prior to ion irradiation.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the initial microstructure of the FeCrMnNi CSA before undergoing any 134 keV Xe ion irradiation. The image serves as a baseline reference for comparing the microstructural evolution and damage accumulation observed in subsequent panels after irradiation and thermal treatment.

caption: Glass object displaying an orange color achieved by mixing gold and silver dopants in a 1:2 ratio during the printing process.
summary: Mixing gold and silver dopants in a 1:2 ratio during the printing process results in a dark orange color for the glass object. This demonstrates the versatility of the method in producing a wide variety of colors by combining different metal precursors to achieve specific optical appearances.

caption: SEM characterization of CCF/epoxy filaments produced via a continuous fibre fabrication tapeline, demonstrating improved infiltration and reduced porosity.
summary: Utilizing a self-developed continuous fibre fabrication tapeline, CCF/epoxy filaments are produced with superior matrix infiltration. The SEM characterization confirms a high fibre volume fraction exceeding 45% and a significantly reduced porosity of less than 1%. This process leverages low-viscosity epoxy to achieve better structural integrity compared to thermoplastic-based composite filaments.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for the CrCoNi powder after ball milling, indicating negligible size change.
summary: The particle size distribution histogram for the CrCoNi powder after ball milling shows that the average particle size remains essentially unchanged compared to the raw powder. This quantitative assessment confirms that the ball milling process preserves the original particle dimensions while maintaining the spherical morphology observed in the feedstock.

caption: Pair spacing distribution n(Δs) comparing experimental data (purple) at 3000 W and 1200 mm/s with a Monte Carlo model (gray) plotted against separation distance Δs.
summary: This panel displays the pair spacing distribution n(Δs) for pores in a material processed at 3000 W and 1200 mm/s. It compares experimental measurements, shown in purple, against a Monte Carlo simulation model in gray, illustrating the statistical distribution of pore separations within the processed sample.

caption: Mo K-edge XANES spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 12.
summary: This panel illustrates the Mo K-edge XANES spectra for Ni Alloy 59, acquired in total reflection geometry at a basic pH of 12. These results are used to evaluate the influence of alkaline environments on the surface oxidation states of the alloy compared to the neutral pH conditions.

caption: Histogram showing the distribution of misorientation angles at hot crack tips, where the proportion is calculated as n/60.
summary: This histogram displays the misorientation angle distribution at 60 hot crack tips. The data reveals that misorientation angles between 30° and 60° are highly prevalent, accounting for approximately 91.7% of the observed crack tips, which suggests a strong correlation between higher misorientation angles and increased cracking susceptibility.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profiles of AlO2-, TiO-, CrO-, FeOH-, NiO-, NiOH-, TiO2-, CrO2-, and CrO3H- anions for the inner surface of alloy 690 steam generator tubes, where the Ni2- signal peaks at 150 seconds of sputtering, indicating an oxide thickness of 48 nm.
summary: Panel b presents ToF-SIMS depth profiles for a range of complex oxide anions on the inner surface of alloy 690 tubes after 325°C transient testing. The Ni2- signal reaches maximum intensity after 150 seconds of sputtering, which corresponds to an estimated oxide layer thickness of approximately 48 nm.

caption: Detailed view of the holding period segment, highlighting the specific data range utilized for fitting the three-parameter and four-parameter Burgers models to the experimental force-time response.
summary: Focusing on the holding phase of the nanoindentation test, this panel provides a detailed view of the force-time data. This specific segment was used to calibrate the Burgers models, allowing for a precise comparison between the three-parameter and four-parameter fits against the experimental force response during the relaxation period.

caption: Fluorescence spectroscopy measurement of the L-PBF degraded sample after 2,000 hours of exposure to a metal dusting atmosphere.
summary: Fluorescence spectroscopy of the L-PBF degraded sample after 2,000 hours of exposure to a metal dusting atmosphere is shown. This measurement characterizes the optical emission properties of the degraded surface, offering insights into the chemical composition and potential phase transformations occurring within the material due to the harsh metal dusting conditions.

caption: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values for NiMo@NF during the second set of electrochemical experiments, featuring 95% confidence interval error bars.
summary: The second set of electrochemical experiments for NiMo@NF is illustrated here, showing Cdl values accompanied by 95% confidence interval error bars. These measurements confirm the reproducibility of the electrochemical behavior observed in the first set, establishing a consistent dataset for analyzing the material's capacitance characteristics throughout the experimental stress testing process.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) weight versus temperature curves for ASA samples across six recycling courses.
summary: The TGA-derived graphs illustrate the weight loss behavior of ASA samples subjected to six distinct recycling cycles. These curves demonstrate that the majority of the samples exhibit very similar thermal degradation profiles, indicating consistent material stability across the different recycling courses examined in this study.

caption: High-resolution HAADF-STEM image of the interface between adjacent NiO and γ-Al2O3 grains viewed along the [001] zone axis, with white dashed lines marking the coherent interface.
summary: This high-resolution HAADF-STEM image captures the interface between NiO and γ-Al2O3 grains along the [001] zone axis. The interface is nearly coherent, as indicated by the white dashed lines. This structural arrangement demonstrates the crystallographic relationship between the oxide phases formed during the high-temperature oxidation of the NG sample.

caption: Nyquist plots obtained from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements to characterize charge transfer resistance.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was utilized to generate Nyquist plots, which characterize the charge transfer behavior of the catalyst. These plots are essential for probing the reaction kinetics and understanding the interface resistance, providing a clear comparison of the electrochemical properties between the different prepared catalyst samples.

caption: Snapshot of contact and cohesive forces in the gap region under 0.5 G gravity, illustrating decreased force arch formation and increased agglomeration.
summary: At 0.5 G gravity, the force arch formation decreases significantly compared to 1 G conditions. The reduced weight leads to increased agglomerate formation, causing the particle supply through the gap region to rely primarily on deposited particles, which results in lower packing density with numerous surface and internal pores.

caption: Geometric model of the Diamond triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) unit cell.
summary: This panel displays the geometric model of a Diamond TPMS unit cell. The structure was designed using MATLAB software with a defined cell size of 5 mm. This unit cell serves as a fundamental building block for the 15 mm cubic bracket designs discussed in the study.

caption: Combined TG and DSC curves for the LDH sample, illustrating decomposition stages including water release at 50–79 °C, dehydroxylation and organic anion decomposition at 200–400 °C, and final spinel structure formation above 450 °C.
summary: Thermal analysis of the LDH sample via TG and DSC curves identifies three distinct decomposition steps. These include the removal of physiosorbed water at low temperatures, the dehydroxylation and oxidative decomposition of organic anions between 200 and 400 °C, and the final formation of a spinel structure above 450 °C.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF-Y) map of the OL1 sample, showing the crystallographic texture along the Y-direction for the final layer.
summary: The IPF-Y map illustrates the crystallographic texture of the coarse austenitic grains in the final deposited layer of the OL1 sample. While EBSD analysis effectively captures the grain structure, it fails to resolve the internal cellular boundaries due to the identical orientation of adjacent cells after rapid solidification.

caption: Theoretical reflection loss curve for 1.50-4STi SiOC ceramics, depicted within the 2–18 GHz frequency range.
summary: The theoretical reflection loss curve for 1.50-4STi SiOC ceramics is shown here across the 2–18 GHz frequency spectrum. This visualization allows for a direct comparison of electromagnetic wave absorption properties, highlighting how specific material compositions and thicknesses influence the RL performance within the specified microwave frequency range.

caption: Inverse pole figure representation of B2 austenite crystal orientation in NiTi alloys fabricated via double-wire electron beam freeform fabrication, demonstrating a strong (001) texture.
summary: The crystal orientation of B2 austenite in NiTi alloys produced by double-wire EBF3 is shown, revealing a strong (001) texture. This preferred orientation significantly influences the mechanical response of the deposited samples, making them more susceptible to dislocation slip when subjected to loading along either the building or horizontal directions.

caption: Peak EQE values measured at 1.3 eV as a function of applied reverse bias for the four distinct absorber thickness configurations.
summary: This panel tracks the peak EQE response at 1.3 eV across different reverse bias voltages for devices with absorber thicknesses ranging from 250 nm to 1150 nm. It summarizes the essential relationship between bias-dependent charge collection and absorber layer thickness, highlighting the performance trends observed in the experimental EQE spectra.

caption: Initial stage of cellular growth showing the motion tendency of a bubble under the interaction of buoyancy force (Fb) and surface tension force (Fs).
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial stage of cellular growth during the BL-DED process. A bubble moves within the molten pool boundary, influenced by the interaction between buoyancy force (Fb) and surface tension force (Fs). This mechanism highlights the early-stage dynamics of pore formation before solidification interface interactions occur.

caption: Ni 2p core level XPS spectrum of the PTHE-treated PdNi/Ni RDE catalyst.
summary: This panel displays the Ni 2p core level XPS spectrum for the PTHE-treated catalyst. The spectrum characterizes the electronic state of nickel following the PTHE treatment, allowing for an assessment of how the treatment influences the surface composition and electronic properties of the catalyst material.

caption: Low-magnification ADF-STEM image of Pt1−x−yIrxNiy nanoparticle aggregates exhibiting uniform contrast.
summary: Low-magnification ADF-STEM imaging of Pt1−x−yIrxNiy nanoparticle aggregates reveals uniform contrast across individual particles. This consistent contrast indicates proper alloying within the ternary nanocrystals, as no abrupt differences are observed, confirming the structural homogeneity of the synthesized material at this scale.

caption: Schematic representation of the single lap joint geometry used for mechanical testing, illustrating the overlap region dimensions including width (W) and length (L).
summary: This schematic illustrates the single lap joint configuration utilized for mechanical testing. The diagram defines the critical dimensions of the overlap region, specifically the width (W) and length (L), which are essential parameters for calculating the apparent shear strength of the adhesive joints during experimental evaluation.

caption: Predicted 1st cycle crystallization percentage surface plot as a function of print head speed and nozzle temperature.
summary: The predictive surface plot for 1st cycle crystallinity shows that increased crystallinity is observed as the print head speed decreases and the nozzle temperature rises. This model represents statistically significant thermal transitions extracted from the ANOVA DSC measurements, demonstrating the relationship between processing parameters and material crystallization behavior.

caption: Dark field TEM image of the 10 hatch wall sample center, generated using the circled superlattice reflection from the corresponding diffraction pattern to highlight the distribution of gamma prime precipitates.
summary: This dark field TEM image utilizes the superlattice reflection identified in the central sample diffraction pattern to visualize the gamma prime phase. By isolating this specific reflection, the image successfully highlights the distribution of gamma prime precipitates within the columnar grain structure, which were otherwise obscured in bright field imaging.

caption: HAADF-TEM image and cross-sectional EDS mapping of In 825 alloy after 28 days of vapour salt exposure at 565 °C, showing a thicker, porous oxide scale.
summary: Following 28 days of exposure to vapour salt at 565 °C, the In 825 alloy develops a significantly thicker oxide layer of approximately 2 μm. HAADF-TEM imaging and EDS mapping demonstrate that this oxide scale is notably more porous compared to the compact layer observed in the IN 625 alloy.

caption: STEM-HAADF micrograph of the solutionized NiTi specimen, highlighting the spatial relationship between undissolved large-size precipitates and the surrounding matrix.
summary: Captured via STEM-HAADF, this image illustrates the microstructure of solutionized NiTi after 50 cycles. The visualization highlights the presence of undissolved large-size precipitates within the matrix. These precipitates are significant as they are associated with the formation of irreversible detwinned martensite phases observed in the surrounding material regions.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of residual uncured monomers leached from 3D printed Clear V4 (blue) and Biomed Clear (red) resins into a DPBS solution, showing characteristic absorption peaks near 225 nm.
summary: UV-Vis spectroscopy reveals the presence of residual uncured monomers in DPBS solutions for both Clear V4 and Biomed Clear resins. The spectra exhibit strong absorbance between 200 nm and 300 nm, with a distinct maximum absorption peak centered at approximately 225 nm for both materials, representing three representative samples each.

caption: Overlapped surface Raman spectra of the interfacial oxide scale, showing the narrow F2g vibration band of CeO2 and characteristic bands of NiAl2O4 spinel between 600 cm⁻¹ and 1100 cm⁻¹.
summary: Surface Raman analyses of the interfacial oxide scale were performed in open cracks to assess crystallization. The spectra confirm the presence of stoichiometric CeO2 fluorite through the narrow F2g vibration band. Additionally, characteristic vibration bands between 600 cm⁻¹ and 1100 cm⁻¹ indicate the presence of NiAl2O4 spinel on the alumina scale.

caption: Electron diffraction pattern of the heat-treated beta-type Ti alloy, with a white circle indicating the omega-spot used for subsequent dark field imaging.
summary: The electron diffraction pattern for the heat-treated beta-type Ti alloy is presented here. A white circle highlights the specific omega-spot used for subsequent dark field imaging, facilitating the targeted visualization of the omega phase distribution within the heat-treated material after the fatigue testing process.

caption: Fluorescent live/dead images of C2C12 cells cultured within AnisoInk and Isobioink on day 7, indicating cell viability.
summary: Live/dead fluorescent imaging of C2C12 cells on day 7 provides a visual assessment of cell health within the different bioink environments. These images complement quantitative viability data, showing the distribution and survival of cells cultured in the AnisoInk and Isobioink formulations.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectra of O-14 and ITX in acetonitrile, highlighting the lower molar extinction coefficient of O-14 at 395 nm compared to ITX.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectra in acetonitrile compare the optical properties of O-14 and ITX. The data reveals that the absorption of O-14 at 395 nm is significantly lower than that of ITX, with measured values of 270 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹ and 3030 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹, respectively, under identical conditions.

caption: In-situ view of the drilling process showing the top jig securing the handpiece and a universal angle vice holding the human skull sample in place during testing.
summary: Captured during the drilling procedure, this photograph displays the physical arrangement of the test components. The drill handpiece is secured by a custom-fabricated top jig attached to the Instron, while the skull model is firmly positioned at the bottom using a universal angle vice to ensure stability during testing.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectra of g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 composite compared to pure g-C3N4 and Bi2MoO6 samples.
summary: Photoluminescence spectra demonstrate that the g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 composite exhibits significantly lower photoluminescence intensity than pure g-C3N4. This reduction indicates a decreased recombination efficiency of photogenerated electron-hole pairs, suggesting that the heterojunction construction effectively enhances electron transfer and improves the separation efficiency of charge carriers within the photocatalytic material.

caption: Microhardness distribution map of the W1 hybrid sample across the deposit/substrate interface, with the substrate top surface defined as the 0 mm reference point.
summary: The W1 sample exhibits a 2D microhardness distribution map across the deposit/substrate interface. The vertical axis is calibrated with the substrate top surface at 0 mm. Blue-colored regions indicating lower microhardness are observed within the deposit, consistent with the general trend of hardness variation across all tested hybrid samples.

caption: Real-time atmospheric pressure plasma jet (APPJ) deposition of a zerovalent silver track onto a ceramic crucible using a 5-axis robotic system.
summary: This panel illustrates the real-time atmospheric pressure plasma jet deposition process. A zerovalent silver track is being deposited onto a ceramic crucible surface using a 5-axis system. The process involves a single pass of plasma deposition to create a conducting track on the substrate material.

caption: In K-edge XAS spectra recorded for the same three catalysts throughout the H2 reduction treatment.
summary: In K-edge XAS spectra are presented for the three catalysts during their reduction in H2. As indicated by the reference to Fig. 5, these data characterize the chemical state of indium within the catalyst materials, tracking changes in the local coordination environment during the active reduction phase of the experiment.

caption: Time-averaged intensity images representing laser beam cross-sections captured over a 1.8-second duration.
summary: These intensity images display the laser beam cross-sections at various focus settings. Each image represents a time-averaged capture of 16 frames recorded over approximately 1.8 seconds. The visualization provides the raw data output from the measuring software, serving as the basis for subsequent beam width and diameter calculations.

caption: Powder X-ray diffraction patterns comparing BGMA, amorphous silica control, and pure hydroxyapatite control, showing characteristic peaks of hydroxyapatite within an amorphous silica matrix.
summary: Powder X-ray diffraction analysis of BGMA, amorphous silica, and pure hydroxyapatite is presented. The diffraction patterns confirm that the synthesized nanoparticles consist primarily of pure hydroxyapatite embedded within an amorphous silica matrix, as evidenced by the specific peaks observed in the XRD data for the BGMA sample.

caption: Nyquist plot for SLMed TC4 alloys S1–1H, S2–1H, and S3–1H processed at 150 W scanning power after 1 h of immersion.
summary: This Nyquist plot displays the electrochemical impedance behavior of SLMed TC4 alloys S1–1H, S2–1H, and S3–1H after 1 h of immersion at 150 W. The capacitive loop size of S2–1H is notably larger than that of S1–1H and S3–1H, indicating superior corrosion resistance for the S2–1H specimen.

caption: Re-entrant lattice specimen featuring a carbon fiber reinforced polyamide (CF/PA) skin layer applied over the core.
summary: This photograph depicts a dual-component re-entrant sample characterized by a core structure encased in a carbon fiber reinforced polyamide (CF/PA) skin. The image illustrates the final configuration of the reinforced design, intended to enhance the mechanical properties of the lattice during standardized three-point bending test procedures.

caption: Benchmark comparison of ultimate tensile strength versus elongation at break for the three D-WAAM alloy samples against various high entropy alloys produced via alternative manufacturing techniques.
summary: This plot benchmarks the mechanical performance of the three D-WAAM samples against existing high entropy alloy literature. The data illustrates the trade-off between strength and plasticity, highlighting that samples 1 and 2 demonstrate superior strength and plasticity characteristics when compared directly to the performance of sample 3.

caption: Transversal view of the 25%Cr-9.5%Ni-3.8%Mo deposited wall showing epitaxial grain growth within the phase-field simulation domain.
summary: This phase-field simulation panel illustrates the epitaxial grain growth occurring within a 25%Cr-9.5%Ni-3.8%Mo deposited wall. The transversal view provides a detailed look at the microstructure development, serving as a foundational component of the simulation domain used to model solidification behavior in the weld pool system.

caption: Yield strength contribution from beta grain size in Ti55531 + x B alloys, comparing values of 8.9 MPa, 13.1 MPa, and 26.6 MPa for different boron concentrations.
summary: This bar chart compares the yield strength contributions derived from beta grain size in Ti55531, Ti55531 + 0.05B, and Ti55531 + 0.1B alloys. The calculated values are 8.9 MPa, 13.1 MPa, and 26.6 MPa, respectively, demonstrating the influence of boron content on the strengthening effect provided by the beta grain structure.

caption: Detailed schematic view of the fixation plate placement, illustrating the geometric relationship between the scaffold, the fixation hardware, and the mandibular bone structure.
summary: This panel provides a detailed view of the fixation plate placement, clarifying the geometric configuration between the scaffold and the host mandible. It complements the design parameters shown in panel (a), establishing the structural framework necessary for evaluating how different fixation heights and angles influence mechanical stimulus distribution.

caption: Load-depth response of the γ matrix phase comparing FEM simulation results with experimental nanoindentation data obtained using a Berkovich indenter.
summary: This panel displays the load-depth response for the γ matrix phase. It compares data derived from FEM simulation against experimental nanoindentation results performed with a Berkovich indenter. The graph illustrates the mechanical behavior and validation of the simulation model against physical testing for this specific strengthening phase component.

caption: Bright field TEM micrograph of the CoCrFeMnNi HEA specimen deformed at a strain rate of 4600 s-1, illustrating the increased density of heterogeneous deformation bands.
summary: Bright field TEM analysis of the CoCrFeMnNi HEA deformed at 4600 s-1 shows a larger amount of heterogeneous deformation bands compared to lower strain rates. This increased structural heterogeneity directly correlates with more evident serrated flow stress, resulting from the intensified interaction between moving dislocations and these deformation bands.

caption: Linear expansion coefficient trends determined through first-principles calculations for phases within the Al–22Si-xNi alloy system at different temperatures.
summary: Linear expansion coefficients for the phases in Al–22Si-xNi alloy are plotted against temperature, based on first-principles computational modeling. This analysis quantifies the thermal expansion behavior of each phase, which is critical for evaluating the dimensional stability and potential thermal stress development within the alloy during temperature fluctuations.

caption: Elemental profiles derived from the EDS line scan of the T1 alloy treated at 1120 °C, showing the distribution of constituent elements.
summary: This plot displays the EDS line scanning profiles for all elements in the T1 alloy after 1120 °C solution treatment. The profiles provide the necessary data to analyze the chemical composition of the stripe precipitates, showing how different elements are distributed across the observed microstructural features.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) for Gd2.00Ni2.60Si0.40, plotted as a function of temperature under applied magnetic fields of 1 T (black squares) and 2 T (red circles).
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic entropy change of the Gd2Ni2.6Si0.4 system, reaching a peak value of approximately 5.1 J kg-1 K-1 at the Curie temperature of 96 K under a 2 T field. The material maintains a high magnetocaloric effect over a broad temperature range of roughly 40 K.

caption: Magnified view of the unloading segment fitted with a linear function to extract the reduced Young’s modulus.
summary: This panel provides a magnified view of the unloading portion of the force-displacement curve. By applying a linear fit to this specific segment, the reduced Young’s modulus is determined using the Olivier and Pharr method, with the entire process automated via a Matlab script to ensure consistent elastic property evaluation.

caption: Surface morphology of SLM TA31-1000 alloy following polishing and PDP electrochemical corrosion.
summary: SLM TA31-1000 alloy surface morphology is displayed after polishing and potentiodynamic polarization. This microscopy image allows for the quantitative comparison of surface corrosion pit defects against other TA31 variants, facilitating an investigation into how the specific SLM processing condition influences the alloy's resistance to electrochemical corrosion.

caption: Back-side transmittance PCA score plot for MJT specimens, demonstrating a cumulative percentage variance of 95.78% and defined by 95% confidence ellipses.
summary: Back-side transmittance PCA score plot for MJT specimens, demonstrating a cumulative percentage variance of 95.78% and defined by 95% confidence ellipses. These results suggest two principal components of PC1 and PC2, which adequately explain the observed behavior in the spectral data for the MJT specimens.

caption: Topology of the f 2 ccz lattice structure represented by a linear arrangement of five stacked unit cells, highlighting the specific flow paths utilized in numerical simulations along the 1, 2, and 3-directions.
summary: This panel illustrates the f 2 ccz lattice topology using a stack of five unit cells. These cells define the flow directions for numerical simulations, which are conducted with inlet flow incoming from the 3-direction or the 1 and 2-directions to evaluate the permeability of the lattice structures.

caption: Inverse pole figure for the tetragonal rutile TiO2 (4/mmm) structure, with specific grain orientations highlighted by circles.
summary: This inverse pole figure displays the crystallographic orientations of the rutile TiO2 phase. By circling the orientations of individual grains, the plot allows for a direct comparison between the observed grain geometry in the orientation map and the fundamental symmetry zones of the tetragonal rutile crystal structure.

caption: Surface topography of the polished sample annealed at 550 °C, imaged by laser confocal microscopy.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy shows the surface topography of the polished sample after annealing at 550 °C. This panel provides insight into the surface roughness of polished material subjected to thermal oxidation. It is a key component in assessing the transformation and grade of mechanical treatment after the oxidising procedure.

caption: Pole figures of the S4 specimen showing higher intensity in the (0001) α′ and (11 0) α′ planes compared to the S1 specimen.
summary: Pole figures for the S4 specimen demonstrate a higher intensity in the (0001) α′ and (11 0) α′ planes relative to the S1 sample. These diffraction results indicate that the S4 processing condition leads to a more pronounced texture, as evidenced by the increased intensity observed in the pole figures.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the Ni3Al(1Fe) TEM specimen cross-section, showing the oxide scale on the left and the metal substrate on the right.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph provides an overview of the TEM specimen lifted from the Ni3Al(1Fe) sample. It clearly delineates the oxide scale on the left side from the metallic matrix on the right, establishing the spatial context for the subsequent detailed microstructural characterization of the oxide layers.

caption: Geometric representation of the re-entrant unit cell design used for lattice fabrication.
summary: This panel illustrates the re-entrant unit cell geometry utilized in the investigation. Three distinct unit cell designs were developed, with their specific geometric parameters defined in Table 1. These unit cells serve as the fundamental building blocks for the lattice formations used to construct the full-scale samples analyzed in this study.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Co, W, and Ni at the start of the laser-leading fabrication process for a mold containing a Ni-based alloy middle layer.
summary: This elemental distribution map displays the spatial arrangement of Co, W, and Ni at the beginning of the fabrication process. The EDX analysis confirms the presence of these elements within the cemented carbide structure, which maintains fine WC particles throughout the cross-section during the initial stage of the laser-leading method.

caption: SRIM-calculated implantation profile of H+ ions plotted against target depth for an AM SS target at normal incidence.
summary: This plot illustrates the simulated implantation profile of H+ ions as a function of target depth for an AM SS target at normal incidence, as determined by SRIM calculations. The data provides a quantitative representation of ion distribution within the material, which is essential for understanding subsequent radiation damage profiles.

caption: Dynamic friction coefficients of composite powders determined through constant-volume shear testing as a function of nano-Mo content.
summary: Dynamic friction coefficients of composite powders are determined through constant-volume shear testing as a function of nano-Mo content. This mechanism is strongly supported by the dynamic friction coefficients measured via constant-volume shear tests, providing insight into the tribological properties of the powders as the nano-Mo content varies.

caption: Close-up view of the primary infiltration nozzle, featuring a 1 mm diameter opening for the initial extrusion of the fiber-reinforced composite.
summary: This photograph displays the primary infiltration nozzle used in the fabrication process. The nozzle has a diameter of 1 mm and serves as the exit point for the infiltrated cellulose fiber composite before it is further processed by the rotation belt system and the secondary extrusion nozzle.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots (C^-2 vs. E) for annealed L-PBF NAB samples subjected to various surface treatments after 15 days of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky analysis reveals the semiconducting nature of the corrosion product films formed on annealed L-PBF NAB after 15 days in 3.5 wt% NaCl. The plots exhibit n-type behavior, attributed to oxygen vacancies and cation interstitials in the Al-rich oxide and impurities in the Cu-rich oxide, allowing for donor density calculations.

caption: SEM image of the etched surface of IN939 + 3.0%Si parallel to the build direction (x-z plane).
summary: Representing the IN939 alloy with 3.0% silicon, this SEM image shows the etched surface parallel to the build direction. It is used to observe the impact of higher silicon content on the microstructure and precipitate formation within the as-printed material.

caption: Absorption spectral monitoring of O-16 photolysis upon exposure to 365 nm LED irradiation in an air-saturated acetonitrile environment.
summary: The absorption spectrum of O-16 is presented during steady-state photolysis at 365 nm. The data shows the molecule's cleavage behavior over time. Although O-16 possesses a higher molar extinction coefficient than O-14, it exhibits a lower photocleavage ability after 240 seconds of irradiation, as indicated by the spectral consumption data.

caption: Ortho view of the conventional Octet lattice model.
summary: The ortho view of the conventional Octet lattice provides a standard geometric reference. This model represents the untwisted state of the lattice, which is used as a control structure to evaluate the impact of rotational degrees on the mechanical behavior of the bio-inspired R-Octet metamaterials.

caption: Macro-scale optical micrograph of the LPBF H13 steel specimen displaying the overall fatigue crack path, highlighted by a white dashed line.
summary: This macro-scale optical micrograph illustrates the overall fatigue crack path in an LPBF H13 steel specimen. The crack trajectory is clearly marked by a white dashed line, providing a macroscopic view of the failure site as referenced in the cross-sectional analysis of crack initiation and propagation.

caption: SAD pattern collected from the MC carbide region, indicating a lattice parameter of 4.547 Å.
summary: This selected area diffraction pattern was obtained from the MC carbide region identified in the inter-dendritic zone. Analysis of the diffraction spots allows for the determination of the carbide's lattice parameter, which is calculated to be 4.547 Å, characterizing the crystal structure of the carbide phase.

caption: Electrical conductivity ratio σr plotted as a function of the density ratio ρl/ρb, which is equivalent to 1-ε, for various structural configurations including curve-fitted data based on the Gibson-Ashby relation.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the electrical conductivity ratio and the density ratio for multiple structural configurations. By applying the Gibson-Ashby relation, the data demonstrates a consistent trend across all considered structures. The curve-fitted results confirm that this mathematical model effectively describes the electrical behavior of these materials.

caption: Complex modulation curve illustrating the evolution of the system as a function of increasing gray level.
summary: This panel presents the complex modulation curve derived from the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. The colorbar indicates the progression of the curve corresponding to increasing gray levels. This visualization highlights the dynamic evolution of the complex modulation, providing insight into the system's behavior under the specified optimization parameters.

caption: Relative impedance spectra (2500–500000 Hz) of glass beads within 96 microcavities, showing measurements from six different electrode configurations including opposite horizontal, vertical, and corner-to-corner combinations.
summary: This panel displays 576 relative impedance spectra obtained from glass beads positioned in 96 microcavities. Measurements were conducted across six distinct electrode orientations, including horizontal, vertical, and corner-to-corner configurations. These spectra, plotted with a uniform y-scale of 0–300%, provide the initial EIS-based characterization of the 3D objects within the microcavity array.

caption: Conceptual model illustrating the specific wear mechanism observed for specimens S3 and S4 during the friction testing process.
summary: Shown in this panel are the wear mechanisms for specimens S3 and S4. The diagram provides a visual explanation of the degradation processes occurring during friction, facilitating a comprehensive comparison of how these specific materials undergo wear relative to the other specimens evaluated in the study.

caption: Emission spectrum of sonoluminescence at 2000 rpm, highlighting a broad continuum, the sodium peak with a Na-Kr shoulder, and additional spectral features between 300 and 400 nm.
summary: The emission spectrum at 2000 rpm reveals a broad continuum alongside a prominent sodium peak, which includes a Na-Kr shoulder. Additionally, the spectrum displays larger features in the 300–400 nm range, providing a detailed breakdown of the spectral components present during high-speed stirring of the sonoluminescent system.

caption: Wear volume loss comparison between as-built and heat-treated samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the wear volume loss for as-built and heat-treated samples. The data indicates that as-built samples consistently exhibit lower volume loss compared to the heat-treated samples. This trend remains consistent across different normal loads, highlighting the impact of heat treatment on the wear resistance of the material.

caption: Electron backscatter diffraction image of the alloy microstructure following aging treatment at 350 °C for 10 hours.
summary: This EBSD image displays the microstructural state of the alloy after undergoing heat treatment at 350 °C for 10 hours. The visualization provides a clear view of the grain morphology and orientation distribution resulting from this specific aging process, serving as the basis for subsequent quantitative grain size analysis.

caption: Top-view AFM topography of the heat-treated Ta2O5 coating deposited at 0.4 Å s−1.
summary: Displayed here is the top-view AFM topography of the Ta2O5 coating deposited at 0.4 Å s−1. This view complements the 3D analysis, offering a detailed look at the surface distribution and texture of the heat-treated coating, which is essential for evaluating the impact of deposition rates on film quality.

caption: Diffraction intensity profiles for the HN sample, plotted against diffraction angle for positions A through D, illustrating the phase composition at different wall heights.
summary: Diffraction patterns for the HN sample, recorded at positions A, B, C, and D along the wall height, reveal the coexistence of austenite and ferrite phases. These results, obtained through X-ray diffraction analysis, indicate that the phase composition remains consistent across the different vertical sections of the HN sample.

caption: Fracture surface morphology of the ambient-pressure Ti64 specimen observed on the XY plane.
summary: This panel displays the tensile fracture surface of an ambient-pressure Ti64 specimen viewed on the XY plane. The morphology provides insight into the material's failure characteristics under tensile loading, serving as a baseline for comparing fracture behavior across different crystallographic orientations within the processed titanium alloy samples.

caption: Molybdenum (Mo) elemental distribution map illustrating the distribution of molybdenum across the joint interface.
summary: Molybdenum distribution is mapped to show its spatial concentration within the joint. The map highlights the presence of Mo, which is typically associated with the DD3 superalloy, and its distribution pattern across the interface with the pure Cu filler and the modified C/C composite.

caption: XRD contour plot illustrating the phase evolution of HPT-deformed IN718 during isochronal annealing up to 900 °C and subsequent isothermal treatment for 18 hours.
summary: This XRD contour plot tracks the structural phase evolution of HPT-deformed IN718 during heat treatment. The data covers both isochronal and isothermal stages, separated by a horizontal dashed line. The observed phase changes, including the precipitation of the δ-phase, are consistent with the recorded XRD patterns throughout the thermal treatment process.

caption: Nb 3d APXPS spectra of the Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb alloy measured in-situ within a 0.1 M NaCl electrolyte at various applied potentials.
summary: Nb 3d APXPS spectra are displayed for the Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb alloy under in-situ conditions in 0.1 M NaCl. These spectra, alongside other core level measurements, are utilized to determine the elemental composition of the passive film and the underlying subsurface alloy layer as the applied potential is varied.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of alpha-prime martensite grains within the XOY plane of the LPBF Ti-6Al-4V specimen.
summary: Representing the XOY plane of the LPBF Ti-6Al-4V alloy, this inverse pole figure map displays the alpha-prime martensite grain distribution. The visualization reveals how the refinement of the initial beta grains, as influenced by the LPBF process, dictates the resulting alpha-prime phase transformation behavior and overall microstructural morphology.

caption: Nanocrystalline FeCoCrNi high-entropy alloy model, showing the equimolar distribution of Fe, Co, Cr, and Ni atoms within a polycrystalline grain structure.
summary: Constructed by substituting atoms in the nanocrystalline Ni model, this FeCoCrNi HEA structure maintains an equimolar ratio of Fe, Co, Cr, and Ni. The model integrates both grain boundary features and chemical disorder, allowing for the investigation of synergistic effects between grain boundaries and alloy composition during collision cascades.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the mechanical performance metrics of mono-material honeycombs fabricated via d-FDM during the initial cold programming cycle.
summary: This radar chart displays the mechanical metrics derived from the force-displacement response of d-FDM printed mono-material honeycombs during the first cold programming cycle. It serves as a baseline for evaluating the cyclic performance and structural behavior of the printed specimens under initial loading conditions.

caption: Comparison of interfacial toughness between multi-material objects created by CMM-3DP and traditional 3D printing methods.
summary: This plot compares the interfacial toughness of multi-material objects produced via CMM-3DP versus traditional 3D printing. The results highlight the superior mechanical performance of the CMM-3DP approach, demonstrating enhanced interfacial bonding achieved through the capillary-driven assembly process.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the variant pair A–B viewed along the [1 1 ‾ 1 ‾ ] I zone axis with λ ≈ 0.37, showing slight deviations in diffraction spots.
summary: This SAED pattern of the variant pair A–B, taken along the [1 1 ‾ 1 ‾ ] I zone axis, reveals that diffraction spots from lamellae I and III deviate slightly. This observation confirms that the zone patterns are not perfectly coincident, indicating distinct orientation relationships for the observed λ value.

caption: Detailed TEM micrograph of the l-PBF sample showing dislocation-induced substructure fragmentation within acicular alpha-prime martensite.
summary: This TEM panel highlights the internal structure of the l-PBF TC11 titanium alloy. Dislocations are observed occupying the acicular alpha-prime martensite and passing through adjacent laths. This interaction causes a broken substructure within the deposited layer, illustrating the specific microstructural evolution and dislocation-driven fragmentation characteristic of the l-PBF processing method.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel evaluated at various temperature levels using the PEC2 model.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics for the KC200GT solar panel, comparing measured values with those obtained through the PEC2 model. The data illustrates the performance response of the solar module across different temperature conditions, demonstrating the accuracy of the proposed model in predicting electrical behavior under varying thermal environments.

caption: Coulombic efficiency (CE) of V 3.5+ - Electrolysis, V 3.5+ - Pd/C, and V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) systems plotted against current densities ranging from 80 to 160 mA cm -2.
summary: Coulombic efficiency (CE) for the three vanadium-based systems remains consistently close to 97% across the tested current density range of 80 to 160 mA cm -2. This high efficiency indicates that minimal side reactions and vanadium crossover occur during the charge-discharge cycling process for all tested electrode configurations.

caption: Processed stack of 2D images obtained from a sub-volume using 0.1 µm successive serial sectioning via FIB milling.
summary: A processed stack of 2D images is shown, representing a sub-volume extracted from the region of interest. These images were captured using FIB-SEM nano-tomography with a serial sectioning interval of 0.1 µm. This data stack provides the necessary spatial information to reconstruct the 3D geometry of the observed rectangular precipitates.

caption: Representative load-depth curves for the AM-ed HEA specimen tested at different strain rates with a maximum applied load of 10 mN.
summary: This panel illustrates the load-depth curves for the additively manufactured (AM-ed) HEA sample. By applying a maximum load of 10 mN across various strain rates, the plot captures the specific mechanical response of the AM-ed material, allowing for a direct comparison of indentation characteristics against the as-casted counterpart.

caption: Normalized Young's modulus (YM) of GelMA hydrogels as a function of layer exposure time (10–100 s), showing a continuous increase in stiffness with longer polymerization times.
summary: Normalized Young's modulus values for GelMA hydrogels are plotted against varying layer exposure times from 10 to 100 s. The data demonstrates that normalized YM values increase continuously with longer exposure times, indicating that polymerization duration is a critical parameter for controlling the mechanical stiffness of the printed hydrogel constructs.

caption: AFM topographic map showing the post-corrosion surface morphology of a near-(0 0 1) grain after 120 hours of immersion in an acidic NaCl solution.
summary: The AFM topographic map displays the surface morphology of a near-(0 0 1) grain following 120 hours of immersion in an acidic NaCl solution. The resulting surface appears smooth and uniform, confirming the layer-by-layer dissolution mechanism predicted by the model where atoms dissolve to expose fresh (0 0 1) planes.

caption: Degradation profile of ABOHA@ZnO hydrogel microspheres, showing the progressive decrease in remaining mass over time under controlled conditions.
summary: The degradation curve of the ABOHA@ZnO hydrogel microspheres indicates a progressive decrease in mass over time. This controlled degradation rate is advantageous for the sustained release of pharmaceuticals, ensuring that the hydrogel maintains its structural function while gradually releasing its cargo throughout the intended therapeutic duration.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve for as-received Inconel 718 powder, illustrating the thermal response during heating.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry analysis of the Inconel 718 powder reveals a melting point at approximately 1361 °C. The resulting DSC curve confirms that the material undergoes single-phase melting, consistent with the phase purity observed in the diffraction analysis of the as-received powder.

caption: ThermoCalc-simulated phase formation sequence for the IN738LC superalloy, illustrating the temperature-dependent evolution and stability ranges of constituent phases.
summary: This simulation provides a detailed evaluation of the phase formation sequence for IN738LC using ThermoCalc. By mapping the formation range of various phases, the analysis elucidates their influence on elemental segregation and the potential for defect formation, serving as a predictive tool for understanding microstructural evolution during processing.

caption: Two-dimensional histogram of shoreline slope values for Streedagh beach, utilizing a bin width of 0.05 for the dimensionless ratio.
summary: Representing shoreline slope data for Streedagh beach, this histogram employs a bin width of 0.05 for the dimensionless ratio. The plot visualizes the consistency of shoreline movements across transects. By mapping in-situ against satellite-derived points, the density function highlights frequent differences in shoreline position, supported by quantitative accuracy metrics.

caption: Accumulated condensate on the viewport window recorded at a temperature reading exceeding 800 °C.
summary: As heating continued and the melt reached a brighter orange color, the optical pyrometer recorded temperatures above 850 °C. This image shows the increased accumulation of vapor condensate on the viewport window, confirming that volatile species continued to evolve from the melt at these elevated temperatures.

caption: MCNPX-calculated absorbed dose per fluence (D/Φ) values comparing the SIL phantom against the standard ICRP 116 phantom.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis of the local skin dose per fluence derived from MCNPX simulations. By evaluating both the SIL phantom and the ICRP 116 phantom, the data illustrates the variation in absorbed dose values, providing a quantitative assessment of the dosimetric differences between these two specific phantom models.

caption: Emission spectra of trypsin (1 g/L) recorded at 303 K across varying SL/trypsin mass ratios from 0 to 0.8 g/L, illustrating the temperature-dependent quenching effect.
summary: At 303 K, the fluorescence emission spectra of trypsin show a consistent reduction in peak intensity as the SL concentration increases. This quenching phenomenon confirms that the interaction between SL and trypsin effectively reduces the fluorescence intensity of the protein at this specific temperature.

caption: Probability density plot showing the distribution of the shape factor (S) for the identified defect population.
summary: This histogram characterizes the distribution of the shape factor (S) for the 28,688 defects contained in the database. By analyzing the shape characteristics of the entire defect population, this plot contributes to the comprehensive assessment of defect morphology observed across the 11 samples involved in the CT optimization process.

caption: Simulated TTP diagram for steel S1, which also serves as an approximate representation for the S2 steel composition.
summary: This panel displays the simulated TTP diagram for the S1 steel variant. The diagram, generated using MatCalc software, provides a theoretical framework for understanding the transformation kinetics of the material. This specific plot is also considered approximately representative of the transformation behavior observed in the S2 steel alloy.

caption: Simulated ΔL and derived CTE curves for the C-T structure, where a transition in bulging direction at 20 °C manifests as a kink in the ΔL curve and a corresponding jump in the CTE.
summary: Simulated ΔL and CTE curves for the C-T structure demonstrate the relationship between bulging direction and thermal expansion. A transition in the bulging mode at 20 °C creates a distinct kink in the ΔL curve, which results in a sharp jump in the derived CTE curve.

caption: Effective activation energies derived from an Arrhenius-type analysis of tracer diffusion coefficients, highlighting quantitative discrepancies between MD and the k-ART/kMC models due to the omission of dynamic effects.
summary: Effective activation energies obtained from Arrhenius analysis of MD, k-ART, and kMC data are presented to evaluate diffusion kinetics. A notable quantitative difference exists between the MD results and the k-ART/kMC predictions, which is attributed to the absence of dynamic effects in the latter modeling approaches.

caption: Binary Ni-Si phase diagram illustrating thermodynamic equilibrium states across varying compositions and temperatures.
summary: The Ni-Si phase diagram provides essential thermodynamic insights for selecting material compositions. At a specific composition of 77.6 wt% Ni and 32.4 wt% Si, the diagram predicts the primary solidification of the NiSi phase, followed by eutectic solidification of NiSi and NiSi2 as the liquid composition shifts toward the eutectic point.

caption: Tabulated binary enthalpy values for atomic pairs within the CoCrFeNiMoTi high-entropy alloy system.
summary: This table presents the specific binary enthalpy values utilized for estimating thermodynamic parameters in the CoCrFeNiMoTi high-entropy alloy system. These values serve as essential input data for thermodynamic modeling, providing the foundational energetic interactions between atomic pairs required to characterize the phase stability and composition of this complex multi-component alloy system.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 1200 °C and 1 atmosphere, featuring black solid lines and grey dashed tie-lines calculated via the FactSage 8.3 thermodynamic model using FactPS and FTsulf databases.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 1200 °C. The plot displays phase boundaries and tie-lines calculated using the FactSage 8.3 thermodynamic model. These calculated lines provide a theoretical framework for understanding the equilibrium states of the system at the specified temperature and pressure.

caption: Confocal fluorescence images of Saos-2 cells on PCL, G, and GO scaffolds after 14 days, displaying cell morphology and distribution on the fibrous substrates.
summary: Confocal imaging of Saos-2 cells at 14 days post-seeding on PCL, G, and GO scaffolds reveals robust cell proliferation. The images show cells effectively bridging between fibers and growing along the scaffold structure, confirming that the material environment supports sustained cell viability and morphological development over the two-week period.

caption: Al 2p XPS spectra of the HEA1 coating worn surfaces, showing a dominant peak between 70 and 79 eV indicative of Al2O3 formation across the temperature range from RT to 900 °C.
summary: The Al 2p XPS spectra for the HEA1 coating worn surfaces reveal a primary peak within the 70–79 eV range. This spectral feature is attributed to the formation of Al2O3. These results demonstrate the presence of aluminum oxide on the worn surfaces across the entire temperature range from room temperature to 900 °C.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) evolution over time for SLMed TC4 alloy specimens subjected to plasma electrolytic polishing (PEP) and mechanical polishing (MP) treatments.
summary: This plot illustrates the open circuit potential (OCP) behavior of SLMed TC4 alloy samples processed via plasma electrolytic polishing (PEP) and mechanical polishing (MP). The experimental data tracks the potential as a function of time, providing a comparative assessment of the electrochemical stability of the alloy surfaces following these distinct polishing methods.

caption: Fluorescence photographs of g-C3N4 and modified catalyst suspensions captured under 365 nm UV irradiation.
summary: Fluorescence imaging shows that the aglow intensity of modified catalyst suspensions is significantly lower than that of pristine g-C3N4 under 365 nm irradiation. This reduction in fluorescence intensity corresponds with the photoluminescence outcomes, confirming suppressed charge recombination rates in the modified materials compared to the original carbon nitride.

caption: Comparison of strut and total density values for printed geopolymer monoliths subjected to various post-treatment conditions.
summary: This bar chart displays the strut and total density of printed geopolymer specimens following different post-treatment conditions. The results reveal distinct density variations among the monoliths, such as the reduction in density observed in HTG specimens from 0.77 to 0.71 g/cc, attributed to the development of micropores within the printed struts.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing the thermal degradation behavior of pure PEKK and PEKK/MRS composites, demonstrating the repeatability of thermal stability up to 800 °C.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrate the thermal stability of pure PEKK versus PEKK/MRS composites. The data confirms the repeatability of the thermal degradation profiles for these materials. Notably, the reference indicates that no significant thermal degradation occurs for the MRS filler material across the temperature range up to 800 °C.

caption: Tafel slope curves derived from the LSV data in panel a, comparing the reaction kinetics of Ni-Cr in different electrolytes.
summary: Derived from the LSV data, these Tafel slope curves characterize the reaction kinetics of the Ni-Cr alloy. The analysis reveals that the Tafel slope in H2SO4 is the smallest among the three tested media, indicating a more favorable reaction mechanism and significantly faster electron transfer kinetics for the hydrogen evolution reaction.

caption: Modulated nonlinear emission pattern featuring double focusing points arranged horizontally, optimized via the genetic algorithm over 200 generations.
summary: Double focusing points are arranged horizontally in the emission pattern. This complex spatial distribution required approximately 200 generations of genetic algorithm optimization, taking about two hours to achieve a clear pattern, illustrating the system's ability to generate multiple focal spots.

caption: AES depth profile spectrum of L-PBF NiTi processed at 56 J/mm3 (A2) after 7 days of immersion in 0.9 wt.% NaCl solution.
summary: This AES spectrum characterizes the passive film composition of L-PBF NiTi (A2) after 7 days in NaCl. The outer layer consists primarily of Ti and O, while the inner layer shows a distinct Ni peak. This depth-resolved analysis confirms the layered structure of the passive film formed on the specimen.

caption: CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram illustrating the color coordinates for surfactant-assisted SnO2-SLS nanoparticles.
summary: Depicting the chromaticity of SnO2-SLS nanoparticles, this diagram uses photoluminescence emission data to map the color coordinates. The plot visually demonstrates the emission shift caused by the SLS surfactant, with the coordinates consistently positioned within the blue region, as supported by the comparative analysis of the nanostructured compounds.

caption: Scatter plot visualizing the distribution of classification values across a feature space defined by the first three principal components for the three sign language classes.
