summary: The scatter plot demonstrates that the three sign language classes can be reliably separated using three principal components. The visualization highlights the feature space distribution, revealing that the most significant overlap occurs between classes B and I, which aligns with the classification results observed in the corresponding confusion matrix.

caption: Bright-field TEM image illustrating the interfaces between the metal substrate, the primary passive film, and the protective carbon layer, revealing a compact, polycrystalline film approximately 3 nm thick.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals a compact, polycrystalline primary passive film with a thickness of approximately 3 nm formed on the Alloy 718 deposit. The image clearly delineates the interfaces between the metal substrate, the passive film, and the protective carbon layer, confirming the formation of a steady-state passive film.

caption: Trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) values quantified via micro-CT to assess structural characteristics of the bone scaffolds.
summary: Trabecular thickness (Tb.Th) values quantified via micro-CT to assess structural characteristics of the bone scaffolds. These measurements provide insight into the geometric properties of the ingrown bone. The data suggests that specific scaffold designs facilitate better structural development, contributing to the overall finding that T9–T10 profiles support optimal bone ingrowth.

caption: Three-dimensional t-SNE projection comparing latent representations of cellular structures generated by the U3LDM model against the original training dataset.
summary: This three-dimensional t-SNE visualization maps the latent space representations of cellular structures. By comparing U3LDM-generated designs with the training samples, the plot demonstrates that the generated structures occupy distinct regions within the latent space, indicating that the model produces designs that are structurally unique from the original training data.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Ti–25Nb–25Mo system calculated for an isotherm at 600 °C.
summary: This panel displays the ternary phase diagram for the Ti–25Nb–25Mo alloy system at an isothermal condition of 600 °C. The diagram provides critical thermodynamic information regarding phase stability and equilibrium states, which corroborates the microstructural observations of the sintered Ti–Nb–Mo alloy specimens processed by milling for various durations.

caption: Optical micrograph of voxel lines transferred at 29 µJ with a pulse distance of 150 µm.
summary: Captured at 29 µJ, this optical micrograph reveals the pattern of voxel lines created with a pulse distance of 150 µm. The image highlights the structural arrangement of the transferred material as the spacing between pulses is further extended, allowing for observation of the resulting line continuity.

caption: Compensation coefficients for AUX cell topology as a function of lattice porosity and compensation length.
summary: This panel presents the compensation coefficients for the AUX cell topology. By plotting these coefficients against lattice porosity and compensation length, the graph provides insight into the compensation behavior of the AUX lattice, consistent with the broader analysis of cell topologies presented in the figure.

caption: 3D friction map detailing the multicycle galling test performance of the coating against AISI 316L stainless steel at elevated temperature.
summary: Represented here is the 3D friction map for the multicycle galling test against AISI 316L stainless steel at elevated temperature. This panel complements the room temperature data, enabling a comprehensive comparison of friction evolution and material adhesion under varying thermal environments during the multicycle testing mode described in the study.

caption: Box-plot distribution of B-PGNN model predictions for the K=2 fold, utilizing a functional prior trained via HMC.
summary: Representing the second fold (K=2), this box-plot displays the distribution of B-PGNN model predictions. The results are derived from HMC training that leverages a functional prior. This plot allows for a quantitative assessment of the model's predictive consistency and performance across the second subset of the data.

caption: Entropic potential profiles of NMC622 coin cells plotted against open-circuit voltage during the delithiation process at a C/10 rate.
summary: This panel displays the entropic potential as a function of open-circuit voltage for NMC622 coin cells during delithiation at a C/10 rate. The data indicates that the entropic potential profiles for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted electrodes overlap with negligible discrepancy, demonstrating consistent electrochemical behavior during the delithiation process.

caption: Optical images of the internal surface of an additively manufactured stainless steel 316 tube, comparing the pristine state to the post-jet fuel fouling condition.
summary: Stainless steel 316 tubes manufactured via powder layering exhibit a rough internal surface. Optical imaging reveals that the interior surface becomes significantly darker following the jet fuel fouling experiment, which serves as a clear indicator of the formation of uniform carbon deposits across the internal tube wall.

caption: Young's modulus profile of the sample treated at 850 °C for 4 hours, showing the variation of elastic modulus across the sample depth.
summary: This plot displays the Young's modulus profile for a sample processed at 850 °C for 4 hours. Each data point represents the average of eleven indentation tests. The region between 15 μm and 50 μm exhibits behavior similar to the substrate, with multiple points showing elastic modulus values exceeding 235 GPa.

caption: HEXRD spectrum of the RHTQ-STA state specimen, processed via RHTQ-STQ followed by aging at 570 °C for 180 s and air cooling.
summary: Presented here is the HEXRD spectrum for the RHTQ-STA material state. This state is achieved by subjecting the RHTQ-STQ specimen to an additional aging treatment at 570 °C for 180 seconds followed by air cooling, allowing for the observation of structural changes induced by the thermal process.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy cross-sectional view of the printed scaffold, confirming the presence of hollow channels resulting from the removal of the sacrificial core material.
summary: Scanning electron microscopy of the scaffold cross-section provides visual confirmation of the internal architecture. The images verify that the sacrificial core material was successfully removed, leaving behind well-defined hollow channels. This structural analysis reconfirms the successful fabrication of core/shell structures with open, perfusable channels within the printed tissue constructs.

caption: CORAL-DDA loss curve demonstrating delayed overfitting and a final achieved test accuracy of 78%.
summary: CORAL-DDA exhibits a robust training profile characterized by delayed overfitting. By managing the loss objectives effectively, the model maintains performance stability for an extended duration, ultimately achieving a notable test accuracy of 78%. This result highlights the method's capability to sustain learning progress without premature degradation of predictive performance.

caption: Normalized Raman spectra of various UV-treated Solmer resins following heat-treatment at 1100 °C for 1 h, highlighting the vibrational signatures of the sintered silica-based materials.
summary: Normalized Raman spectra are presented for multiple UV-treated Solmer resins after sintering at 1100 °C for 1 hour. This spectroscopic analysis identifies the vibrational modes of the resulting silica-based microstructures, allowing for a comparative assessment of the material composition and structural state after the high-temperature treatment.

caption: Bode-impedance plots showing the magnitude of impedance as a function of frequency for cladded coatings processed at different heat treatment temperatures.
summary: Bode-impedance plots provide a frequency-dependent view of the impedance magnitude for cladded coatings tested in a 3.5% NaCl solution. These plots complement the phase data to characterize the electrochemical behavior of the coatings, demonstrating how varying heat treatment temperatures affect the overall impedance response of the material system.

caption: Line scan profiles of Ti, Al, Co, and Cr concentrations across the interface between IN625 buildup and IN738LC base metal.
summary: This panel displays elemental concentration profiles for Ti, Al, Co, and Cr across the interface of IN625 and IN738LC. The depth axis starts at zero for the buildup and extends into the base metal. Elemental accumulation is clearly observed within the interface zone, which is highlighted by a gray box.

caption: Schematic representation of the solvus fitting methodology applied to a sigma phase solvus, highlighting the selection of endpoints on either side of the solvus event to define the fitting range.
summary: This schematic illustrates the systematic approach for fitting a sigma phase solvus. By selecting specific endpoints on both sides of the solvus event, the methodology establishes a defined interval for the fitting process. This visual guide clarifies the procedure for accurately determining solvus boundaries within the material's phase equilibrium data.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) analysis showing B p-orbitals of CuNi@BNC, B p-orbitals and NH₃ p-orbitals post-adsorption, and p-orbitals prior to adsorption.
summary: The projected density of states (PDOS) of NH₃ adsorbed on the catalysts was analyzed to gain a deeper understanding of the catalyst-NH₃ interaction. This analysis compares the electronic states of B p-orbitals and NH₃ p-orbitals before and after adsorption, elucidating the electronic coupling between the catalyst and the adsorbate.

caption: Central drone body design featuring nylon propeller blade spacing of 25.4 by 11.43 cm.
summary: The central drone body serves as the primary structural component, designed using SolidWorks to accommodate all arms and auxiliary components. It features a specific nylon propeller blade spacing of 25.4 by 11.43 cm, providing the necessary foundation for the drone's overall assembly and integration of various flight systems.

caption: Proportions of FCC, BCC, HCP, and disordered atomic structures plotted against increasing shock velocity for the [100] orientation.
summary: This plot illustrates the structural evolution of the material under shock loading along the [100] orientation. It tracks the relative fractions of FCC, BCC, HCP, and disordered atomic configurations as shock velocity increases, providing a quantitative measure of phase transformation and disordering induced by the high-velocity impact process.

caption: Thermal expansion behavior represented by relative displacement ΔL/L0 as a function of temperature T, derived from dilatometry cooling experiments.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermal expansion of the material, calculated from the average relative displacement during the cooling phase of dilatometry experiments. Because no densification-related shrinkage occurs during cooling, this curve provides a reliable measure of thermal expansion, which is subsequently used to correct anisotropy factors and model results.

caption: Histogram showing the particle size distribution and functional fit for carbides in H13 steel.
summary: The histogram illustrates the automatically counted particle size distribution for carbides found in H13 steel. Analysis of the distribution reveals that the particle sizes are predominantly concentrated in the 10–30 nm range, supported by a functional fitting curve that characterizes the size frequency of these specific nanostructures.

caption: STEM micrograph of a specimen after fatigue–creep testing at 730 °C with a tensile strain dwell, showing significant growth of thermodynamically stable phases.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of a specimen subjected to fatigue–creep testing at 730 °C with a tensile strain dwell. Compared to compressive dwell conditions, this specimen exhibits a higher tendency for the growth of thermodynamically stable phases, highlighting the influence of dwell type on microstructural evolution.

caption: X-ray tomography reconstruction of internal defects within the heat-treated (HT) sample.
summary: This panel presents the internal defect reconstruction of the heat-treated (HT) sample obtained via X-ray tomography. By comparing this visualization with the AF sample, the effectiveness of the crack healing process can be evaluated, highlighting changes in the internal defect morphology resulting from the applied heat treatment.

caption: Rietveld refinement of synchrotron high-resolution XRD data (λ = 0.2073 Å) for the PEG-3–1500 specimen, confirming an orthorhombic Pbnm crystal structure.
summary: This panel displays the Rietveld refinement results for the PEG-3–1500 specimen using high-resolution synchrotron XRD data collected at a wavelength of 0.2073 Å. The analysis confirms that the material adopts an orthorhombic Pbnm crystal structure, providing a precise fit to the experimental diffraction pattern for the specified composition.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of the Ti–10V–2Fe–3Al titanium alloy subjected to electron beam wire fabrication (EBWF) treatment under varying electron beam currents.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for the Ti–10V–2Fe–3Al titanium alloy following EBWF processing. The data illustrates the structural characteristics of the alloy under different electron beam currents, providing insight into the phase composition and distribution within the β matrix as influenced by the specific fabrication parameters applied.

caption: X-ray computed tomography reconstruction of specimen P1 processed at 100 W, 500 mm/s, and 0.09 mm hatch spacing, corresponding to a volumetric energy density of 74 J/mm³.
summary: Specimen P1, processed with a volumetric energy density of 74 J/mm³, is visualized using X-ray computed tomography. This panel displays the internal crack distribution and melt pool geometry resulting from the specific laser power of 100 W, scan speed of 500 mm/s, and hatch spacing of 0.09 mm.

caption: Grain boundary and GND density map of the horizontally printed AB specimen, tested at 222 MPa with a fatigue life of 2.27×10^6 cycles, showing a shallower depth of dislocation accumulation near the crack edges.
summary: The GND analysis for the horizontally printed AB specimen reveals a distinct distribution of dislocations near the crack edges. Compared to the HT specimen, this map shows a shallower accumulation depth, which is attributed to the presence of pre-existing dislocation patterns within the as-built microstructure prior to fatigue testing.

caption: Predicted values of the test set plotted against experimental values for the AC system regression model.
summary: This panel presents the results of the prediction step performed on the test set for the AC system regression. By plotting the predicted values against the experimental data, the graph validates the predictive capability and generalization performance of the regression model developed in the previous stages of the analysis.

caption: Elemental composition map of tungsten (W) highlighting the formation of a globular network within the alloy microstructure.
summary: This elemental composition map specifically illustrates the distribution of tungsten within the arc-melted sample. The visualization confirms that tungsten forms a distinct globular network throughout the microstructure, serving as the primary matrix phase in the alloy's complex elemental arrangement.

caption: Absorption cross-sections of SO2, H2O, and O2 plotted across the 240 to 325 nm wavelength range.
summary: This panel displays the absorption cross-sections for SO2, H2O, and O2 within the 240 nm to 325 nm range. Data is derived from the MPI-Mainz database, with concentrations scaled by factors of 300 for H2O and 210,000 for O2 to facilitate comparative analysis of spectral features.

caption: Comparison of θ ̅ - ε ̅ 0 p curves and corresponding ε ̅ p - σ ̅ profiles for Law 1 and Law 2 at a stress triaxiality η = 0, evaluated for three Lode parameter cases (θ ̅ = -1, 0, and 0.88).
summary: Representing the intersection of damage initiation surfaces at η = 0, this panel shows the predicted θ ̅ - ε ̅ 0 p curves and ε ̅ p - σ ̅ profiles. These results demonstrate how Law 1 and Law 2 capture the plastic and damage behaviors of IN718 at this specific stress state.

caption: FE-simulated and ANN-predicted topology element densities at 30° and 30% mass removal, highlighting the largest prediction error at location ID-6.
summary: This panel displays the FE-simulated and ANN-predicted topology element densities for a 30° boundary condition and 30% mass removal constraint. The darkest color at location ID-6, marked by a black dashed box, indicates the largest ANN prediction error, representing the maximum gap between FE analyses and ANN-predicted topology element densities.

caption: Comparison of photoluminescence spectra for neat HDPE polymer across multiple recycling cycles, acquired under 254 nm excitation to evaluate the impact of thermal oxidation and chain breakage.
summary: Spectra comparing neat HDPE polymer samples across all recycling cycles are displayed. Thermal oxidation during these processes leads to chain breakage, which significantly alters the molecular structure and mechanical properties of the polymer. These spectral changes provide insight into the degradation occurring throughout the mechanical recycling stages.

caption: Bode plots representing the impedance behavior of AP-NAB alloys across different frequency ranges, with low-frequency impedance values (|Z| at 0.01 Hz) increasing up to 48 hours of immersion.
summary: Bode plots characterize the impedance response of AP-NAB alloys across various frequency ranges during immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl. Analysis of the low-frequency region at 0.01 Hz shows that impedance values increase consistently up to 48 hours, which serves as a clear indicator of improved corrosion resistance for the alloy.

caption: Central transverse and longitudinal cross-sections of the CAFD simulation model for Al-7Cu at a nucleation undercooling of ΔT_N = 0.5 K.
summary: This panel displays the simulated grain structure for a nucleation undercooling of 0.5 K. The transverse section highlights the melt pool microstructure, while the longitudinal section shows the full model sample. These results capture key microstructural features observed in experimental LSR GR Al-7Cu samples, demonstrating qualitative model accuracy.

caption: Dark-field TEM image corresponding to the area shown in (e), providing contrast to distinguish the L12 precipitates and stacking faults.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging provides complementary contrast to the bright-field image in (e), allowing for the clear identification of L12 precipitates and stacking faults. This visualization confirms the spatial distribution of these features within the NiCoCrAlTi alloy after it has been deformed to fracture at 600 °C.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the corrosion behavior of Ar P and Ar O samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the corrosion response of Ar P and Ar O samples within a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The data reveal that both samples exhibit similar polarization behavior when exposed to chloride-containing environments, indicating comparable corrosion resistance characteristics for the two distinct processing conditions investigated in this study.

caption: Optical micrograph showing the side view of an etched DED-LB specimen fracture surface after fatigue testing at a total strain amplitude of ± 0.65 % until failure at 1,120 cycles.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the side view of an etched DED-LB specimen fracture surface. The material was subjected to fatigue testing at a total strain amplitude of ± 0.65 %, resulting in failure after 1,120 cycles. The image provides a macroscopic overview of the specimen's condition following the fatigue process.

caption: Observed trends in packing fraction versus density across the diverse set of printed nanocomposite samples.
summary: The scatter plot illustrates the relationship between packing fraction and density for the printed nanocomposite samples. This visualization provides a comparative overview of how these two metrics correlate across the different printing conditions and materials, serving as a basis for evaluating the consistency of the manufactured parts.

caption: Temperature increase versus exposure time under a 268 kHz, 200 Oe alternating magnetic field for FeCaP1–40 samples in non-calcined and calcined states (700 and 1000 °C).
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic hyperthermia response of FeCaP1–40 powders. Non-calcined samples show minimal heating, with a temperature increase of approximately 3.5 °C after 5 minutes. Calcination at 700 and 1000 °C significantly enhances the ferromagnetic behavior, leading to higher temperature increases compared to the non-calcined state.

caption: Green fluorescence channel image highlighting viable HGF cells stained with Calcein, demonstrating cell survival after 24 hours of indirect contact with the specified samples.
summary: This fluorescence microscopy image specifically highlights viable HGF cells using Calcein green staining. The visualization confirms the presence and distribution of living cells after 24 hours of indirect contact with the samples, serving as a key indicator of cell viability and biocompatibility for the materials tested in the study.

caption: Schematic representation of the roughness measurement methodology, illustrating the wire EDM cutting lines on channel sections (left) and the designated numbering system for the specific measurement zones along the channel axes (right).
summary: This schematic illustrates the methodology for assessing channel surface roughness. Sections were prepared by cutting along channels using wire EDM to ensure accessibility. Measurements were subsequently performed along the main axis of these channels at the specific locations identified by the numbering system shown in the diagram.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum of the T-5 part confirming the presence of TPPC within the matrix.
summary: The EDX spectrum of the T-5 part verifies the successful incorporation of TPPC into the PVDF matrix. By identifying the characteristic elemental peaks, this spectroscopic analysis supports the uniform dispersion of nanoparticles, confirming the chemical composition of the nanocomposite material used for the energy harvesting device.

caption: Compositional line profile across the grain boundary of an Al2O3–Ni3Al sample acquired via EELS.
summary: This EELS line profile displays the relative atomic composition of aluminum and oxygen across the grain boundary in an Al2O3–Ni3Al sample. The data, derived from Al-K and O-K edges, serves as a typical compositional reference for characterizing the chemical distribution at the interface under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Total strain amplitude versus LCF lifetime plotted for both strain-controlled and stress-controlled experimental conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between total strain amplitude and LCF lifetime. The data demonstrates that for both strain-controlled and stress-controlled LCF experiments, the relationship between total strain amplitude and lifetime is unique, indicating consistent fatigue behavior across these different control modes for the tested material.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curve illustrating the electrochemical performance of nickel alloy coated 3D-printed electrodes in 1 mol KOH.
summary: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) measurements are presented for the nickel alloy coated 3D-printed electrodes within a 1 mol KOH solution. This plot serves to evaluate the polarization characteristics and catalytic performance of the electrode material under controlled electrochemical conditions, complementing the CV data shown in the previous panel.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-built specimen processed at 125 W laser power, showing crystallographic orientations in the loading direction (XY plane) relative to the build direction (Z axis).
summary: This inverse pole figure map characterizes the as-built microstructure of the 125 W laser power specimen. Acquired in the loading direction with the Z axis parallel to the build direction, the map reveals the grain orientation patterns established during the laser processing of this specific material sample.

caption: Total density of states for Ti-Mo alloys calculated without structural relaxation using the SQS method.
summary: This panel displays the total density of states for Ti-Mo alloys calculated via the SQS method without structural relaxation. The data provides a baseline electronic structure representation for the alloy system, serving as a comparison point to evaluate the influence of structural relaxation on the electronic properties of the material.

caption: Non-equilibrium solidification simulation of AA2024 waDED material based on the Scheil model.
summary: This non-equilibrium thermodynamic simulation utilizes the Scheil model to predict solidification behavior in AA2024 waDED material, assuming no diffusion in the solid phase or at the solid-liquid interface. The lack of diffusion results in the enrichment of alloying elements within the remaining melt, leading to the formation of Cu-rich segregations.

caption: Continuous Fiber Fibrify (CFFF) trajectories generated by adjusting bar radii.
summary: The second row depicts two CFFF trajectories obtained by modifying the bars' radii. These trajectories ensure fiber continuity in each layer while successfully retaining the intersecting fiber trajectories within the design, demonstrating the capability to maintain structural integrity through controlled fiber path adjustments during the design optimization phase.

caption: Dilatometric strain curve for Alloy B illustrating the martensite-start temperature measurement.
summary: Dilatometric analysis of Alloy B identifies a martensite-start temperature of 164 °C. The graph utilizes a dashed line offset to mark the onset of the martensitic transformation, providing a consistent experimental basis for comparing the phase transition characteristics between the two alloy compositions under investigation.

caption: Hydrostatic and deviatoric residual stress distribution map for the WQ sample, showing the greatest degree of stress relief among the tested conditions.
summary: The WQ sample residual stress map displays hydrostatic and deviatoric components relative to the origin point. This specimen exhibits the most significant residual stress relief compared to the other conditions, as evidenced by the spatial distribution of stress magnitudes across the mapped coordinates.

caption: Dilatometric quenching curves representing the relative length change of the steel plate as a function of temperature during the cooling cycle.
summary: The dilatometric curves measured during quenching track the dimensional changes of the steel plate as it cools. These curves are essential for identifying the temperature ranges of phase transformations and provide the raw data necessary to calculate the martensite transformation kinetics during the final quenching stage of the treatment.

caption: Comparative bar chart displaying yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and elongation values for the substrate, WAAM, and interface regions.
summary: This bar chart quantifies the yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation for the substrate, WAAM, and interface regions. The data reveals a local increase in mechanical properties, which is attributed to grain refinement strengthening induced by re-melting and rapid solidification during the WAAM deposition process.

caption: Fluorescence images of live/dead stained osteoblasts incubated in 10% extract medium and normal medium for 24 hours (Group A) and 72 hours (Group B).
summary: Live/dead staining results for osteoblasts incubated in 10% extract medium and normal medium for 24 and 72 hours demonstrate high cell viability. Both experimental and control groups show that the osteoblasts remained viable with only a small percentage of dead cells, suggesting the scaffold extracts do not negatively impact cell viability.

caption: DMA results for TPS45A, illustrating the shear modulus as a function of load (1–30 N) and shear angle (0.001°–1°).
summary: TPS45A demonstrates a storage modulus that is strongly dependent on the applied normal forces and shear angles during DMA testing. These results confirm the material's suitability for robust liners, as it maintains mechanical integrity while responding to the varying stresses experienced during dynamic activities like walking or jumping.

caption: Nyquist plots for the SOEC with a Co-infiltrated cathode, measured at OCV during galvanostatic testing at 0, 24, and 48 hours.
summary: This panel displays the Nyquist plots for a Co-infiltrated cathode SOEC at 0, 24, and 48 hours of galvanostatic testing. These electrochemical impedance spectra are used to determine the ohmic resistance and polarization resistance values for the cell throughout the testing period.

caption: 3D morphology of corrosion pits on the surface of LPBFed CP-Ti after 7 days of dynamic immersion.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy reveals the 3D surface morphology of corrosion pits on LPBFed CP-Ti samples following 7 days of dynamic immersion and subsequent polarization testing. This visualization highlights the specific pitting behavior and surface degradation characteristics observed on the pure titanium specimen under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) results evaluating the influence of filler type, pin diameter, and W/D ratio on bearing stiffness (Kb).
summary: This panel presents the ANOVA results for bearing stiffness (Kb) as a function of filler type, pin diameter, and W/D ratio. Statistical analysis confirms that all investigated factors, including their interactions, exert a significant effect on the bearing stiffness, with all calculated p-values consistently remaining below 0.005.

caption: Saturation magnetization (Ms) and coercive force (Hc) values plotted as a function of annealing temperature for D30 HEA powder.
summary: Saturation magnetization and coercive force are plotted against annealing temperature to demonstrate the magnetic evolution of the D30 HEA powder. These measurements reveal how thermal treatment modifies the intrinsic magnetic properties of the alloy, highlighting the sensitivity of Ms and Hc to the specific annealing temperatures employed during processing.

caption: Calculated unit cell lattice parameters and volume plotted as a function of increasing nickel composition, reflecting structural changes.
summary: Calculated unit cell lattice parameters and volume are plotted against increasing nickel composition to quantify structural changes. These results support the observation of lattice contraction derived from the XRD peak shifts, providing a comprehensive view of how nickel alloying influences the unit cell dimensions of the Bi2Se3 host matrix.

caption: Failure surface of aluminium alloy EN AW-6014 T4 shown in green, mapping the dependence of failure strain on stress triaxiality and the Lode angle parameter.
summary: The failure surface for aluminium alloy EN AW-6014 T4 is presented here, incorporating calibrated material parameters. The plot captures the ductile failure characteristics of the alloy, highlighting the influence of stress triaxiality and Lode angle on failure strain, with distinct responses observed in shear, compression, and tension regimes.

caption: Confusion matrix detailing the predictive performance of the third model in identifying pH level classes.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed view of the classification results for the third model across different pH level classes. By mapping predicted versus actual pH categories, the matrix allows for a quantitative assessment of the model's predictive accuracy and identification of specific classes that are frequently confused.

caption: DSC curves for the P3F7 blend, displaying two distinct glass transition temperatures at approximately 69.97 °C and -43.73 °C.
summary: The P3F7 blend DSC curve reveals two distinct glass transition temperatures, specifically at 69.97 °C for the PLA component and -43.73 °C for the PVDF component. These separate transitions indicate the immiscibility of the two polymers within this specific blend composition during the thermal analysis.

caption: Cutaway view of the cryogen submersion fixture designed for tensile testing, illustrating the FFF cup configuration with a dogbone specimen positioned for direct liquid nitrogen contact.
summary: This schematic illustrates a custom FFF cup designed for cryogenic tensile testing. The cutaway view demonstrates how the fixture holds liquid nitrogen in direct contact with the neck of a dogbone specimen, ensuring sufficient coverage of the grip region to prevent premature failure outside the gauge length during mechanical testing.

caption: Relative density of AISI M2 tool steel samples sintered at 1270, 1280, and 1300 °C for a 120-minute holding duration.
summary: Relative density measurements for AISI M2 tool steel samples sintered at 1270, 1280, and 1300 °C for 120 minutes are presented. This plot illustrates the densification behavior of binder-jetted specimens under extended sintering durations, allowing for a direct comparison of density variations across the different tested sintering temperatures.

caption: Normalized room-temperature photoluminescence (PL) and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectra of HDPE, showing emission maxima at 370 nm and a structured blue emission profile with peaks at 411, 435, 464.5, 498, and 537 nm under 325 nm excitation.
summary: Normalized room-temperature PL and PLE spectra of HDPE are presented. Excitation at 325 nm reveals a low-intensity emission at 370 nm, followed by a dominant, well-structured blue luminescence with multiple peaks. These peaks exhibit vibronic sidebands separated by approximately 180 meV, corresponding to CH2 bending vibrations within the polymer structure.

caption: Pseudo-ternary diagram illustrating the specific powder feed ratios of Fe–Co–Mo, Fe–Cr–Ni, and Fe–Co–Cr systems utilized for each of the 27 in-situ alloyed samples.
summary: This pseudo-ternary diagram maps the precise powder feed ratios for 27 distinct samples synthesized via a single DED process. By adjusting hopper RPMs, the feed rates of Fe–Co–Mo, Fe–Cr–Ni, and Fe–Co–Cr powders were controlled to achieve specific target compositions, with each sample designated by a unique identifier corresponding to these ratios.

caption: Loss modulus (G’’) variation with temperature for DfD material specimens in the YXZ orientation.
summary: Loss modulus (G’’) is displayed as a function of temperature for DfD material specimens in the YXZ orientation. The data shows similar trends for all curves across the temperature range, confirming that the DfD material and TEMs have a negligible impact on the loss modulus for these specific samples.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of pure Ni electrode recorded in 0.05 M H2O2 and 2 M NaOH electrolyte at scan rates ranging from 5 to 1000 mV s-1.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical response of a pure Ni electrode in an alkaline peroxide solution. The voltammograms, collected across a wide range of scan rates from 5 to 1000 mV s-1, demonstrate a noticeable increase in recorded current densities as the potential scan rate is progressively increased.

caption: High-magnification view near the fusion boundary revealing distinct vermicular and lacy ferrite morphologies.
summary: Captured at higher magnification near the fusion boundary, this micrograph highlights the specific vermicular and lacy morphologies of the residual ferrite. These distinct structural features indicate that the material solidified through the FA mode, although the predicted amount of residual ferrite remains underestimated compared to the experimental observations.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the performance scores of virgin and carbon-blended grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V powders across seven qualitative and quantitative metrics, including segregation, spreadability, bulk flow, CBD, dynamic flow, and cohesion.
summary: This radar chart evaluates grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V powders by comparing virgin and carbon-blended samples. Performance is assessed through seven qualitative and quantitative metrics, including segregation, spreadability, bulk flow, CBD, dynamic flow, and cohesion. These scores facilitate the selection of suitable powders for LPBF part printing by identifying comparable material properties.

caption: Validation of the Peridynamic simulation model through a direct comparison of load–displacement curves against experimental data from cast specimen tests.
summary: This panel presents a validation of the Peridynamic (PD) simulation by comparing its predicted load–displacement curve against experimental data obtained from cast specimen tests. This comparison serves to demonstrate the accuracy and reliability of the PD model in capturing the mechanical response of the material under loading conditions.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the HTAZ-M sample.
summary: Displayed here is the KAM map showing the local misorientation distribution of the HTAZ-M sample. The map provides a detailed view of the dislocation density and lattice strain, facilitating an analysis of how the heat treatment and specific processing route affect the microstructural evolution of the HTAZ-M material.

caption: Chronopotentiometric response of the FG-3 experiment conducted on Inconel 600 in a LiCl–KCl–5-wt%-FeCl2 molten salt electrolyte.
summary: The chronopotentiogram for the FG-3 experiment illustrates the galvanostatic anodic dissolution behavior of Inconel 600 in the LiCl–KCl–5-wt%-FeCl2 molten salt. This result completes the series of galvanostatic tests, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of how constant current application influences the dissolution kinetics and potential stability of the Inconel 600 anode.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for as-fabricated NiTiHf samples processed with varying hatch spacing (h) while maintaining constant laser power (100 W) and scanning speed (0.8 m/s).
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for as-fabricated NiTiHf samples processed with varying hatch spacing (h) while maintaining constant laser power (100 W) and scanning speed (0.8 m/s). These results demonstrate a single-step forward and reverse transformation between austenite and martensite, highlighting how modifying hatch spacing influences the phase transformation behavior of the alloy.

caption: Schematic representation of the potential bio-mechanism underlying the synergistic interaction between osteogenesis and antibacterial properties in the composite materials.
summary: This mechanism diagram summarizes the integrated biological effects of the composite materials. It illustrates how the material surface properties influence cellular signaling pathways, specifically linking mTOR and FoxO activation to the observed improvements in osteogenic differentiation and antibacterial activity, providing a comprehensive overview of the material-cell interaction.

caption: Computational input model of the Bridge structure illustrating the applied boundary conditions and loading configurations.
summary: This panel displays the initial computational input model for the Bridge structure. It defines the geometric configuration and the specific boundary conditions and loads applied to the system, serving as the foundational setup for subsequent finite element analysis and optimization processes within the study.

caption: Transformation temperatures (TTs) displayed against stress levels for samples V1 and V5, reflecting changes in scanning speed during processing.
summary: Transformation temperatures for samples V1 and V5 are presented as a function of stress level. The data, extracted from the analysis of curves in Figure 5, shows a consistent trend in TTs, highlighting how scanning speed variations influence the thermal transformation characteristics of the material under different stress loads.

caption: Ashby-style comparison of the strength-ductility product versus fracture toughness for LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA against various cast and additively manufactured alloys.
summary: This Ashby-style plot illustrates the relationship between the strength-ductility product and fracture toughness for the LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA. By comparing these mechanical properties against a broad range of cast HEAs and additively manufactured steel, Ni, Al, and Ti alloys, the figure highlights the performance characteristics of the present EHEA.

caption: Comparative performance analysis of the MWCNT/PA12 metamaterial against standard energy-absorbing materials.
summary: This plot benchmarks the energy absorption properties of the developed MWCNT/PA12 metamaterial against conventional materials. It serves to validate the effectiveness of the SLS-printed structures, showing how the integration of MWCNTs into the PA12 matrix enhances performance metrics relative to standard materials used for impact protection and energy dissipation.

caption: KGT model predictions for 96.8 wt% Fe alloy illustrating the solidification growth mode transitions relative to measured experimental solidification rate ranges.
summary: KGT modeling evaluates the influence of high solidification rates on growth mode transitions for 96.8 wt% Fe alloys. The plot compares theoretical predictions against experimental solidification rate ranges, which vary from 5.4 to 66.4 mm/s depending on the travel speeds of 15, 50, and 100 mm/s.

caption: 2H NMR spectra comparing ZnSO4 electrolytes with and without the SL additive.
summary: The 2H NMR spectra reveal a shift in the water peak from 4.73 ppm upon the addition of 1% SL to a 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte. This shift confirms that the SL additive significantly influences the solvation coordination environment between Zn2+ ions and H2O molecules in the electrolyte solution.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curves for GBDT models evaluated across different build samples, utilizing a 2 mm voxel bin dataset with a 0.05% porosity threshold.
summary: Receiver operating characteristic curves illustrate the performance of GBDT models trained and tested on distinct build samples. Utilizing a 2 mm voxel bin dataset with a 0.05% porosity threshold, the results demonstrate that the model trained on dataset A achieved superior performance when transferred to build B compared to its own dataset.

caption: Temperature-time-transformation diagram for the R725-Nb alloy, displaying the predicted phase transformation kinetics as a function of exposure time within the 600 °C to 800 °C range.
summary: This TTT diagram for the R725-Nb alloy illustrates the kinetic phase transformation predictions for exposure times at temperatures ranging from 600 °C to 800 °C. It provides essential data on how niobium alloying affects the transformation timeline, allowing for a clear assessment of phase stability under these controlled thermal conditions.

caption: Calibrated GD-OES elemental depth profiles of Al-3at.%Cu surfaces following various surface treatment steps compared to the bare reference state.
summary: Calibrated GD-OES elemental depth profiles illustrate the chemical composition of Al-3at.%Cu surfaces after distinct treatment steps. The profiles compare treated surfaces against the bare reference, with right-hand y-axes specifically indicating the atomic percentage of surface aluminum and oxygen, revealing the elemental distribution changes induced by the pickling and conversion coating processes.

caption: Friction coefficient measurement for FeCoCrNiMn specimen processed with 200 W laser power and 800 mm/s scanning speed.
summary: Representing the tribological response of FeCoCrNiMn alloy, this panel shows the friction coefficient for a sample fabricated at 200 W and 800 mm/s. The data contributes to the broader evaluation of how varying laser parameters during SLM influence the surface friction characteristics and mechanical resistance of the material.

caption: Fluorescent intensity quantification of the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 per hMSC cell cultured for 7 days on Bare Pizza and AA Pizza discs.
summary: This bar chart quantifies the expression of the mechanosensitive Piezo1 ion channel in hMSCs after 7 days of culture. The data indicates that the nano-structured surface of the AA Pizza discs promotes Piezo1 activation, which is a critical step in facilitating calcium influx and subsequent bone matrix mineralization.

caption: Relationship between the Sutterby parameter and ternary PGW fluid motion for scenario-1.
summary: This panel illustrates the relationship between the Sutterby parameter and ternary PGW fluid motion for scenario-1. It serves as part of the artificial backpropagation network analysis, specifically examining how major parameter variations impact fluid motion within the PEOF-SNFF model framework to characterize the system's behavior under defined conditions.

caption: Microhardness testing procedure across the weld joint using a Vickers indentation meter.
summary: Microhardness measurements were conducted across the weld joint using a Vickers indentation meter (HVS-1000). The testing procedure involved applying a load of 200 g with a dwell time of 10 s to evaluate the mechanical properties of the welded interface.

caption: DMTA analysis of PEB578 showing the loss modulus (E") curve, which exhibits a relaxation peak at -19 °C and a storage modulus (E') of 465.6 MPa at 30 °C.
summary: DMTA analysis of the PEB578 specimen provides a storage modulus of 465.6 MPa at 30 °C. The loss modulus curve reveals a distinct relaxation peak at -19 °C, which is associated with the glass transition. This value is slightly higher than the DSC-derived Tg, consistent with typical polymer thermal analysis observations.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to milled Ti alloy extracts.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the milled Ti alloy group after 24 hours of exposure to extracts. The image shows the distribution of live (green) and dead (red) cells, providing a visual assessment of the biocompatibility of milled Ti extracts on fibroblast cells after 24 hours of exposure.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves obtained from tensile testing of the investigated material samples.
summary: This plot displays the engineering stress-strain behavior of the investigated samples as determined through tensile testing. The curves provide a quantitative representation of the mechanical response, illustrating the relationship between applied stress and resulting strain, which is essential for evaluating the material's performance and mechanical properties under tensile loading conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scanning profile taken across the yellow line segment indicated in panel (a), showing elemental concentration variations.
summary: The EDS line scanning profile across the selected yellow segment in panel (a) provides quantitative evidence of elemental concentration changes. These profiles reveal a major increase in Vanadium concentration within the light-grey phase, confirming the compositional identity of the β-Ti phase and supporting the observations from the elemental maps.

caption: Box plots quantifying protein levels of C1CP, OPG, IL-6, and IL-8 in pre-osteoblasts cultured on the three scaffold types, evaluated via paired t-test.
summary: Protein quantification results for C1CP, OPG, IL-6, and IL-8 are shown for the three scaffold conditions. Collagen content was highest in Foam 1 at all time points. Additionally, the study quantified pro-inflammatory mediators IL-6 and IL-8 to assess the impact of BMP-2 immobilization on the scaffold surface.

caption: Cross-sectional XY and XZ plane projections of CT-scanned samples at the critical point, highlighting fatigue crack initiation sites.
summary: Projected binary images along the XY and XZ planes illustrate the internal structure of CT-scanned samples at the critical point. These cross-sectional views reveal how as-built surface features and pore defects influence the development of critical cracks, providing a detailed visualization of the fatigue crack initiation process leading to final fracture.

caption: DSC cooling curves for raw powder and printed Al-bronze specimens.
summary: Cooling curves for raw powder and printed Al-bronze specimens are shown. The data demonstrates that HT-F samples exhibit lower heat flows compared to AS-F specimens. These thermal profiles highlight the variations in cooling behavior between the raw material and the printed forms of the Al-bronze alloy.

caption: Time-dependent COF variation for the tested LPBF specimens during sliding contact against a 7 mm diameter WC counter ball.
summary: Friction evolution for LPBF specimens tested with a 7 mm counter ball is shown over a 1800 s duration. The COF profile exhibits an abrupt initial rise, a subsequent rapid drop, and a gradual increase until the end of the test, reflecting the formation of a protective tribo-film during sliding.

caption: Flank wear progression measured as a function of total cutting time for various coated carbide grades.
summary: This plot illustrates the progression of flank wear in coated carbide tooling as a function of total cutting time. By comparing different carbide grades, the graph provides a quantitative assessment of tool degradation rates, highlighting how material composition influences wear resistance during the machining process under specified experimental conditions.

caption: Liquidus projection of the Al-Ce-Mn alloy system, highlighting the compositional regions associated with the formation of Al10Mn2Ce and Al20Mn2Ce phases.
summary: The liquidus projection for the Al-Ce-Mn ternary system is presented here. It delineates the phase fields for Al10Mn2Ce and Al20Mn2Ce, which are identified in the additively manufactured Al-10.5Ce-3.1Ni-1.2Mn alloy. This diagram provides the necessary thermodynamic context for understanding the solidification behavior and phase evolution in the Al-rich region.

caption: Calculated overlapped atomic volume for Model 2 with partial occupancies of 0.20 and 0.15 for the Al2 and Al3 sites, respectively.
summary: This simulation shows the overlapped atomic volume for Model 2, assuming partial occupancies of 0.20 and 0.15 for the Al2 and Al3 sites. The calculation is performed for slip on the (001) plane, illustrating the impact of these specific partial occupancies on the atomic volume during shear deformation.

caption: Displacement (ΔL) as a function of temperature for spark plasma sintered sample 2, highlighting the observed hysteresis effect during cyclic bending mode testing.
summary: Displacement (ΔL) as a function of temperature for spark plasma sintered sample 2, highlighting the observed hysteresis effect during cyclic bending mode testing. The data demonstrates the thermo-mechanical response of the sample, where the displacement varies with temperature over multiple cycles, confirming the presence of a characteristic hysteresis loop.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the heat-affected zone under B1 welding condition, showing the highest dislocation density of approximately 6.5 × 10¹⁴ m⁻².
summary: The heat-affected zone is characterized by this dark-field TEM image, which highlights the highest dislocation density of 6.5 × 10¹⁴ m⁻² observed across the weldment. This increased dislocation density is a primary contributor to the material's strengthening, accounting for 53% of the total strengthening effect in this specific zone.

caption: Hyperparameter optimization process for the neural network model developed to predict elongation (EL).
summary: This panel illustrates the hyperparameter optimization phase for the neural network model designed to predict elongation. The optimization process is a critical step in refining the model's architecture and configuration to ensure accurate performance in subsequent inferencing tasks, establishing the foundation for the model's predictive capabilities regarding material elongation.

caption: Detailed inset of the (4 2 0) diffraction peak for A1 HT2 and A2 HT2, demonstrating the variation in peak location due to compositional differences.
summary: A detailed inset of the (4 2 0) peak illustrates the variation in peak location between the A1 and A2 samples. This displacement is a direct consequence of the different compositions and their associated unit cell parameters. The visualization confirms the structural differences between the two alloys at 423 K.

caption: Representative photoluminescence spectra collected from the center of each of the five mapped regions (P0–P4), demonstrating consistent spectral profiles.
summary: Representative photoluminescence spectra are presented for the center of each of the five mapped regions, P0 through P4. These spectra confirm the uniformity of the emission properties across the MoWS2 alloy film, showing that the peak energy remains stable regardless of the specific location on the sample surface.

caption: EBSD orientation map of 24CrNiMoY alloy steel processed at a laser energy density of 72 J/mm³.
summary: This EBSD map characterizes the 24CrNiMoY alloy steel microstructure at a laser energy density of 72 J/mm³. The visualization highlights the lattice distortion and solid solution effects induced by the laser processing, serving as a key observation of the material's structural response to the highest energy density tested in this series.

caption: Spatial distribution of carbon atoms within the graphene layer extracted from the interface model, demonstrating the preservation of the two-dimensional planar structure.
summary: Extracted from the interface model, this snapshot highlights the spatial distribution of carbon atoms in the graphene layer. Despite potential carbide formation from nearby Cr and Fe segregation, the graphene maintains its intrinsic two-dimensional planar arrangement, confirming that the structural integrity remains intact after 100 ps of thermal relaxation.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of pure PPy films on dense SLM-Ti substrates, recorded at a scan rate of 100 mV/s, displaying well-defined reduction and oxidation peaks at -0.5 V and -0.35 V.
summary: The cyclic voltammogram of the pure PPy film on a dense SLM-Ti substrate shows well-defined reduction and oxidation peaks at -0.5 V and -0.35 V, respectively. The high symmetry along the potential axis indicates highly reversible redox behavior for the PPy film during electrochemical switching.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum of diamond-structured oxides in the unSMATed region, highlighting a dominant chromium peak alongside manganese, iron, and nickel signals.
summary: The EDS spectrum for the diamond structures in the unSMATed part reveals a composition dominated by Cr2O3 and spinels. The analysis shows a prominent chromium peak, with additional signals corresponding to basic alloying elements including manganese, iron, and nickel, confirming the chemical nature of these specific oxide surface structures.

caption: Spin-wave dispersion spectra for the squeezed permalloy dot structure with a squeeze ratio of s = 0.6, showing the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone.
summary: Representing the compressed magnetic system, this panel illustrates the ten lowest-frequency spin-wave modes for a squeeze ratio of 0.6. The dispersion spectra, calculated along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone, demonstrate how structural deformation influences the excitation behavior of the permalloy dots embedded within the cobalt matrix.

caption: DIC εyy strain field mapping for the [110] secondary orientation specimen after 40 hours of creep testing at 850 °C and 450 MPa.
summary: Digital image correlation analysis demonstrates the εyy strain field distribution for the [110] secondary orientation specimen after 40 hours of creep testing at 850 °C and 450 MPa. In contrast to the [100] orientation, this specimen displays a bilateral-symmetric strain field distribution, indicating a different mechanical response under identical creep conditions.

caption: Local strain evolution and DIC strain distribution maps for specimens tested at a nominal strain rate of 1000 s⁻¹.
summary: Dynamic tensile testing at 1000 s⁻¹ is characterized by the local strain evolution plotted against global strain levels. The corresponding DIC images at the bottom depict the strain distribution at the maximum global strain, facilitating an analysis of the deformation mechanisms and strain localization occurring at this high strain rate.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the AISI 316L HT1 heat-treated sample.
summary: Grain size distribution for the AISI 316L HT1 sample is represented in this histogram. Based on EBSD measurements performed perpendicular to the build direction at 100 μm magnification, the plot illustrates the shift in grain size statistics resulting from the HT1 heat treatment process.

caption: Sensitivity factor (SF) plotted against the N baseline values for various loading conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the sensitivity factor and the N baseline values across different loading conditions. By mapping these parameters, the figure provides a visual representation of how model sensitivity correlates with baseline performance metrics, as detailed in the corresponding data provided in the study's reference table.

caption: Correlation plot of local versus global strain for thin-hinge rotating-square structures tested at a strain rate of 5 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹.
summary: This plot illustrates the multiscale strain correlation for thin-hinge rotating-square structures. Local equivalent strains, extracted from four regions of interest at the center, are plotted against global strain. The data shows that hinge strain follows the global strain evolution in both trend and quantity, highlighting the structural feature's contribution to deformation.

caption: Unirradiated indentation modulus versus depth for as-cast HEAs, showing stable values at 300 nm depth where surface and substrate effects are negligible.
summary: The indentation modulus for unirradiated HEAs is plotted against depth. At a 300 nm indentation depth, the modulus data remains independent of depth, confirming that the area function calibration accurately captures the tip geometry while minimizing interference from surface or substrate effects during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform pattern corresponding to the secondary rod-like Al6(Mn,Fe) phase in S1.5.
summary: The FFT pattern derived from the rod-like Al6(Mn,Fe) phase confirms its crystal structure and semi-coherent orientation relative to the aluminum matrix. By calibrating this pattern and measuring crystal face spacing, the phase is identified as distinct from primary Al6(Mn,Fe) particles found in other processing conditions.

caption: Boxplot comparison of channel diameter widths and standard deviations for SLA-printed templates versus fabricated hydrogel channels across various target sizes.
summary: This boxplot provides a statistical summary of channel diameter widths and standard deviations, comparing the dimensions of SLA-printed templates with the resulting hydrogel channels. It illustrates the dimensional fidelity and variability across different target sizes, highlighting the consistency of the fabrication process for the hydrogel channels relative to the templates.

caption: Thermo-kinetic E-pH diagram for nickel in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 85 °C, with blue dots representing measured OCP values.
summary: Elevating the temperature to 85 °C significantly impacts nickel's electrochemical behavior. The blue dots show that OCP values shift to more negative levels across the pH 1–6 range compared to room temperature, indicating increased corrosion susceptibility and a reduction in the protective nature of the passive layer under these thermal conditions.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental stress values against predicted stress values derived from the model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the correlation between experimental stress and predicted stress values. The model demonstrates high predictive accuracy, evidenced by a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.9894. The close alignment of data points along the diagonal indicates that the predicted values effectively capture the experimental stress behavior observed in the study.

caption: Phase prediction results generated by a random forest machine learning model.
summary: This panel displays the phase prediction results derived from a random forest machine learning model. The visualization illustrates the model's performance in classifying material phases, providing a clear overview of the predictive accuracy and classification outcomes achieved through the applied machine learning approach as described in the study.

caption: UV–Vis DRS spectra of g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6, Bi2MoO6, and g-C3N4, with the inset displaying the corresponding Tauc plots of (F(R)hν)^2 versus photon energy.
summary: The UV–Vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy results demonstrate that the g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 heterojunction exhibits significantly stronger visible-light absorption compared to pure Bi2MoO6. This enhanced absorption indicates a superior photoresponse, which is further analyzed through Tauc plots in the inset to determine the optical band gaps of the materials.

caption: Averaged imaging results for large rectangular bonded objects subjected to a medium-frequency modulation range of 15, 17, and 19 kHz.
summary: This panel presents the averaged imaging results for large rectangular bonded objects using a medium-frequency modulation range of 15, 17, and 19 kHz. The imaging technique applies external modulation signals for 10 ms total duration to capture the vibration energy distribution across the bonded interface of the rectangular specimen.

caption: Dissipated energy density measured across successive loading blocks.
summary: Dissipated energy density is shown to decrease following each block transition, subsequently increasing slowly with progressive cycling in a steady-state manner. This behavior directly corresponds to the observed trends in damage strain, highlighting the relationship between energy dissipation and structural degradation during the staircase block cyclic testing process.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the A phase support, detailing the nitrogen-doped carbon shell layer over the graphene nanoplatelet sheets.
summary: This TEM image provides a detailed view of the A phase support structure, specifically showing the nitrogen-doped carbon shell wrapping over the graphene nanoplatelet sheets. This morphological feature is critical for understanding the support architecture that hosts the atomically dispersed metal sites and alloy nanostructures.

caption: Linear fitting curves of squared hardness (H^2) versus the inverse of indentation depth (1/h) based on the Nix-Gao model, with data points below 100 nm excluded to mitigate surface effects.
summary: The graph presents the Nix-Gao model fitting curves for as-casted and AM-ed HEA, plotting H^2 against 1/h to demonstrate linear behavior. To ensure accuracy and avoid surface-related artifacts, the analysis excludes indentation depth values less than 100 nm, confirming the validity of the model for the remaining data range.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of heat intensity (HI) versus porosity, displaying two opposing trends where increasing heat intensity can either promote or inhibit pore formation, suggesting complex competing physical effects.
summary: Heat intensity demonstrates two opposing trends in its impact on porosity, as shown in this SHAP scatter plot. Higher heat intensity values generally exhibit greater absolute SHAP values, reflecting a complex influence where heat can either increase or decrease porosity, likely due to the competing effects of keyhole and LOF-porosity.

caption: Temporal evolution of the electrical current measured over the duration of a single pulsation cycle.
summary: This panel displays the measured electrical current as it evolves throughout one complete pulsation cycle. The data was captured using a high-speed camera equipped with a bandpass filter to monitor the arc dynamics, providing a clear representation of the current fluctuations occurring during the specified electrical discharge process.

caption: Overview of the MTI Corporation MSK-AFA-I laminator apparatus utilized as the base experimental platform.
summary: This photograph displays the MTI Corporation MSK-AFA-I laminator apparatus, which serves as the foundational experimental setup. The system was specifically reverse-engineered to integrate a custom-designed 3D printed deposition head, enabling specialized material processing capabilities as described in the research methodology provided by CNR ITAE.

caption: Kikuchi pattern obtained from the M6C phase, providing crystallographic information regarding its structure.
summary: A Kikuchi pattern was acquired from the M6C phase to facilitate crystallographic identification. This diffraction technique provides essential structural data, allowing for the characterization of the M6C phase's crystal lattice. The pattern serves as a definitive indicator of the phase's crystalline nature within the examined material sample.

caption: Average number of surviving Frenkel pair defects in pure Ni following 50 keV cascades, comparing different electron-phonon coupling activation times against classical MD results.
summary: This plot displays the surviving Frenkel pair defects in pure Ni after 50 keV cascades. Activation of electron-phonon coupling at 1 ps results in higher defect counts compared to 0.2 ps activation. These results, identified via the Wigner-Seitz method, are compared against classical MD simulations to assess the impact of coupling timing.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) maps derived from EBSD analysis, focusing on the grain orientation distribution along the downward face of the notch for both as-built and post-processed specimens.
summary: Inverse pole figure maps generated via EBSD illustrate the crystallographic orientation distribution on the downward face of the notch. The visualization compares the as-built state against post-processed specimens, providing insight into how different thermal treatments influence the grain structure and orientation near the notch region of the material.

caption: TEM micrograph showing the striated microstructure of precipitates after aging at 320 °C for 30 min, characterized by a sharp contrast between alternating light and dark regions.
summary: TEM observation reveals the microstructure of precipitates after aging at 320 °C for 30 minutes. The image displays a distinct striated morphology, which is characterized by a sharp contrast between alternating light and dark regions, providing clear evidence of the microstructural evolution occurring during this specific thermal aging process.

caption: TEM micrograph displaying stacking faults (SFs) within the γ matrix channels.
summary: Abundant stacking faults are observed within the γ matrix channels of the fatigued alloy. These features are categorized based on their specific configurations, with straight fringes denoted as type A and zigzag fringes denoted as type B. This classification highlights the diverse nature of planar defects formed during high-temperature fatigue.

caption: Tanδ response curves for CP-PLA composites processed at different polystyrene (PS) preparation temperatures.
summary: This panel displays the Tanδ profiles of CP-PLA composites subjected to varying PS preparation temperatures. The curves highlight how thermal processing conditions during the preparation phase affect the damping performance of the composite material, providing insight into the relationship between processing parameters and the resulting viscoelastic properties of the polymer system.

caption: Optical micrograph of sample 3 scaffold seeded with MSCs at Day 3, visualized using live/dead assay staining.
summary: Sample 3 scaffold seeded with MSCs is captured at Day 3 using live/dead assay staining. This optical micrograph provides visual data on cell viability and scaffold dimensions, which are essential for evaluating the swelling extent of the material following the cell culture process in this study.

caption: Atomic configuration of the CN15 layer within the μ phase, identified as the layer with the most similar symmetry and atomic distance to the γ' phase.
summary: This panel displays the atomic layer of the CN15 structure, which serves as a potential interface layer for the μ phase. The C15 layer was specifically selected for misfit strain estimation because it exhibits the most similar symmetry and atomic distance to the γ' phase layer.

caption: Comparison of axial corrosion length (ΔC max) between CoCrMo femoral adapters (n = 17) and tibial trays (n = 15), where individual measurements are represented by diamonds and a statistically significant difference is noted (P = 0.041).
summary: This boxplot quantifies the extent of corrosion on CoCrMo components using the ΔC max metric. The analysis demonstrates significantly increased corrosion on femoral adapters compared to tibial trays, supported by a P-value of 0.041. Individual data points are plotted as diamonds to illustrate the spread and magnitude of corrosion measurements.

caption: 0.2% proof stress plotted against elongation for various CCWN alloys, highlighting the target performance region for next-generation balloon-expandable stents.
summary: This plot displays the 0.2% proof stress versus elongation for CCWN alloys. The gray shaded region represents the target mechanical performance for next-generation balloon-expandable stents, defined by a 0.2% proof stress below 600 MPa and elongation exceeding 60%, allowing for a direct comparison between current study results and existing literature.

caption: Weighted average diameter of γ′ precipitates plotted against various ion irradiation conditions.
summary: This plot displays the cluster weighted average diameter of γ′ precipitates across different ion irradiation conditions. Analysis indicates that the diameters of these precipitates remain relatively unaffected by the irradiation process when compared to the unirradiated baseline condition, demonstrating stability in precipitate size despite the applied ion irradiation treatment.

caption: Surface topography of the as-built GZ112K alloy highlighting the presence of Gd2O3 oxide particles.
summary: Surface topography of the as-built GZ112K alloy is visualized using AFM to identify Gd2O3 oxide particles. These oxides are noted as undesirable features that negatively impact the corrosion resistance of the as-built alloy, providing a clear structural basis for the subsequent potential measurements performed on these specific secondary phases.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) of microbial community structures across experimental samples.
summary: Principal component analysis illustrates that distinct experimental samples resulted in varying degrees of alteration in the microbiota of the elderly. The EBN and Blank groups exhibited similar community structures, while other treatments showed distinct clustering, indicating significant shifts in the overall microbial composition due to the experimental interventions.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the natural logarithm of the ratio of trapped hydrogen concentration to lattice hydrogen concentration as a function of reciprocal temperature.
summary: Panel (b) displays the natural logarithm of the ratio of trapped hydrogen to lattice hydrogen plotted against reciprocal temperature. This Arrhenius-style representation allows for the determination of the trap binding energy of the hydrogen within the material under a constant cathodic charging current density of -20 mA/cm2.

caption: Cycles-to-failure for specimens F-1 through F-10 subjected to HTLCF testing at strain amplitudes of 1.0%, 1.2%, 1.6%, and 2.0%, categorized by specimen location.
summary: This plot displays the cycles-to-failure for specimens F-1 to F-10 under HTLCF conditions at varying strain amplitudes. Results indicate that the innermost location consistently exhibits the highest fatigue life, followed by the middle location, while the outermost location demonstrates the lowest number of cycles to failure across all tested strain levels.

caption: Experimental effective shear strain map (εLD) of the keyhole defect region at 4.55% macroscopic strain, revealing the strain distribution after yielding.
summary: This experimental strain map at 4.55% strain illustrates the macroscopic strain distribution after the material has yielded. The map serves as a critical reference for evaluating the accuracy of the FEA simulation in capturing post-yield strain behavior and localized strain values within the keyhole defect region.

caption: Variation of the first characteristic parameter plotted against the area ratio Ab/Awl for Group A specimens.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the first characteristic parameter and the area ratio Ab/Awl for Group A. Data points extracted from FE models are shown alongside fitted curves, denoted with the subscript 'p', to represent the predicted parameter values across the range of area ratios analyzed in the study.

caption: Intermediate progression of the first spherical agglomeration development under laser processing conditions.
summary: Intermediate development of the first spherical agglomeration is shown for IN713LC processed at 452 W. By excluding recoil pressure, the simulation highlights that these unconnected, spherical weld beads are a purely surface-tension driven phenomenon, confirming the mechanism responsible for the characteristic weld bead morphology observed in experimental results.

caption: Ashby plot comparing Young's modulus versus material strength for various candidate materials, highlighting the region representing the elastic response of steel with dashed lines.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates potential model materials for simulating the elastic response of steel structures at scales of 1:40 to 1:60. The data, sourced from the Materials Data Book, demonstrates that no single homogeneous metal satisfies the required elastic criteria. Additionally, the plot includes concrete properties for comparative completeness.

caption: Imaginary wavenumber dispersion curves representing the attenuation coefficient for one-dimensional unit cell chains, plotted for frequency ranges where p(ω) ≤ −1 or p(ω) ≥ 1.
summary: This panel shows the magnitude of the imaginary part of the wavenumber q, which corresponds to the attenuation coefficient for the one-dimensional chain. These results are plotted for frequency ranges where the characteristic parameter p(ω) is outside the propagation band, specifically when p(ω) ≤ −1 or p(ω) ≥ 1.

caption: Cross-sectional optical micrograph of a Type II bimetallic sample fabricated via MM-LPBF, viewed parallel to the build direction.
summary: Representing the second heterogeneous structure in the study, this micrograph shows the cross-section of a Type II bimetallic sample. The view is oriented parallel to the build direction, allowing for the observation of the material's internal morphology and structural characteristics resulting from the MM-LPBF fabrication technique.

caption: Magnetoresistance (MR) of the CrO2 film on sapphire measured at 4.2 K in a parallel configuration (μ0H ‖ I), highlighting peaks at the coercive field.
summary: Magnetoresistance measurements at 4.2 K for the CrO2 film on sapphire reveal distinct peaks at the coercive field. These peaks are consistent with those observed in AMR measurements, confirming that the magnetic domain structure significantly influences the electronic transport properties of the thin film under an applied field.

caption: Normalized protein expression levels of MHC, α-actinin, and troponin T relative to GAPDH, quantifying the upregulation of myogenic markers under cyclic strain conditions.
summary: This bar chart presents the normalized protein expression levels of MHC, α-actinin, and troponin T relative to GAPDH. The data quantitatively confirm that cyclic strain leads to higher expression of these myogenic markers, supporting the conclusion that mechanical conditioning improves the biochemical profile of the engineered muscle blocks.

caption: Line scanning elemental distribution profile across the brazed joint interface for the 1.0 wt% Nd amorphous filler alloy.
summary: Line scanning profiles for the 1.0 wt% Nd amorphous filler alloy show significant fluctuations in elements other than Fe at the bonding interface. These results suggest that the addition of Nd effectively modifies the Cr diffusion process, thereby enhancing the overall bonding ability between the filler alloy and the diamond.

caption: High-speed image at 0.31 ms showing the onset of particle interaction with the melt pool.
summary: At 0.31 ms, the high-speed camera records the initial interaction between high-momentum particles and the 2024 Al melt pool. This stage marks the beginning of the dynamic process where particles strike the surface, initiating the local rupture of the surface film as described in the experimental observations.

caption: Detailed channel dimensions measured in millimeters.
summary: This schematic provides the precise dimensions of the internal channels, with all measurements specified in millimeters. By detailing the width, height, and spacing of the flow paths, this diagram establishes the geometric parameters necessary for understanding the fluid dynamics and thermal performance characteristics of the heat exchanger prototype.

caption: Transverse rupture strength of sintered cermets plotted against varying WC/Mo2C content.
summary: This plot illustrates the transverse rupture strength of sintered cermets as a function of varying WC/Mo2C content. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the flexural strength, highlighting how changes in the WC/Mo2C composition influence the mechanical performance and structural integrity of the sintered cermet materials under transverse loading conditions.

caption: Atomic configurations and calculated adsorption energies for single Cl (green) and Mg (orange) adatoms on a pure Ni (grey) surface.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configurations of single Cl and Mg adatoms adsorbed onto a pure Ni surface. The adsorption energies were calculated for these configurations, with positive values indicating an exothermic reaction. These results provide a baseline for understanding the individual interaction of Cl and Mg with the Ni substrate.
