caption: Finite element simulation of stress distribution in T III alloy under impact loading.
summary: Finite element simulation demonstrates the stress distribution in the T III alloy under impact conditions. The solid cylinder is shown to withstand a higher level of stress, illustrating how the optimized lattice design influences the dissipation and distribution of stress during high-energy impact events.

caption: Atomic representation of a 2 × 2 × 2 supercell constructed from a Zeolite ID 9566022 unit cell.
summary: This panel shows the atomic structure of a 2 × 2 × 2 supercell derived from a Zeolite ID 9566022 unit cell. The structural modeling procedure, facilitated by VESTA software, highlights the conversion from a single unit cell to a larger supercell, serving as a representative example of the zeolite modeling workflow.

caption: Enlarged view of the 2000 cm⁻¹ to 400 cm⁻¹ region of the FTIR spectra for Mn-BTC, highlighting specific vibrational modes and ligand-metal interactions.
summary: This panel provides a detailed, enlarged view of the FTIR spectra in the 2000 cm⁻¹ to 400 cm⁻¹ range. By focusing on this specific region, the plot allows for a clearer observation of the vibrational characteristics and ligand-metal interactions within the Mn-BTC framework synthesized at different temperatures.

caption: Reflection magnitude distributions for arbitrary combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 60 GHz and 63 GHz, showing values ranging from 0.68 to 0.97.
summary: This panel displays the reflection magnitudes for various combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 60 GHz and 63 GHz. The data indicates high reflection efficiency within the lower frequency band, with magnitudes consistently measured between 0.68 and 0.97, demonstrating the effective performance of the proposed meta-atom design.

caption: Confocal scanning laser microscopy image of the same Alloy 617 region shown in (a) after exposure to 1 bar Ar at 700 °C for 300 s.
summary: Captured after 300 seconds of exposure to 1 bar argon at 700 °C, this confocal scanning laser microscopy image shows the same region as panel (a). Comparison between the two images reveals no significant surface changes or degradation resulting from the argon exposure under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Magnetization versus applied magnetic field curves for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 and Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 measured at 4 K, showing a saturation magnetization of 2.6 µB/f.u. for the system.
summary: Magnetization curves as a function of the applied field are presented for two distinct compositions at 4 K. The data reveals a saturation magnetization of 2.6 µB/f.u., which serves as a reference point for comparing the magnetic behavior of the Mn-Fe-Ni-Si-Al alloy system under low-temperature conditions.

caption: Coronal, transverse, sagittal, and 3D reconstructed micro-CT images of rabbit femoral condyles at 6 weeks post-operation, highlighting newly formed bone tissue in blue within the HPDM scaffold defect site.
summary: Micro-CT imaging at 6 weeks post-implantation reveals new bone tissue ingrowth within the HPDM scaffolds. The HPDM group exhibits the most significant bone growth compared to other groups, as evidenced by the coronal, transverse, sagittal, and 3D reconstruction images showing the defect area with newly formed bone highlighted in blue.

caption: Equilibrium molecular dynamics snapshot of the F6 network, illustrating the largest percolated cluster in gray and secondary clusters color-coded by size.
summary: This molecular dynamics snapshot visualizes the equilibrium state of the F6 network. The largest percolated cluster is highlighted in gray, while all other clusters are represented in color based on their bead count. This visualization confirms the high degree of connectivity and minimal discrepancy between total and effective conversion.

caption: Experimental setup photograph displaying the integration of the 1070 nm fibre laser with the FEI Quanta 600 environmental-SEM.
summary: The photograph displays the physical experimental setup, featuring the coupling of a 200 W air-cooled fibre laser with an environmental-SEM. This configuration allows for high-vacuum laser scanning and characterization, providing the necessary infrastructure to perform controlled laser-material interaction experiments within the scanning electron microscope environment.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the L3.39 sample cross-section, highlighting fine equiaxed grains within the white box region.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the L3.39 sample identifies regions of fine equiaxed grains, marked by a white box, which result from recrystallization during laser annealing. This crystallographic data confirms the structural transition from the original microstructure to a refined grain state in the remelted zone.

caption: Hysteresis behavior in spark plasma sintered sample 3, represented by ΔL (μm) plotted against temperature during cyclic bending mode thermo-mechanical analysis.
summary: Hysteresis behavior in spark plasma sintered sample 3, represented by ΔL (μm) plotted against temperature during cyclic bending mode thermo-mechanical analysis. The graph captures the displacement response of the sample as it undergoes temperature changes, clearly showing the hysteresis effect that occurs throughout the multiple cycles of the test.

caption: Creep-rupture data for Alloy 740 base metal plotted against the Larson-Miller parameter, with 100,000-hour strength values calculated at 700°C, 750°C, and 800°C using a constant C value of 19.392.
summary: This plot displays creep-rupture data for Alloy 740 base metal as a function of the Larson-Miller parameter. Using a constant C value of 19.392, the 100,000-hour creep-rupture strength is evaluated at 214.1 MPa for 700°C, 123.7 MPa for 750°C, and 84.8 MPa for 800°C.

caption: Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectra of a 50 mg/L phenol solution undergoing degradation by the FeNi porous framework catalyst.
summary: Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectra demonstrate the catalytic degradation of a 50 mg/L phenol solution using the FeNi porous framework. The spectral data tracks the reduction of phenol concentration over time, providing direct evidence of the material's catalytic activity and efficiency in breaking down organic pollutants within the aqueous environment.

caption: Logical flow diagram detailing the sequential steps and operational stages of the experimental procedure.
summary: The flow diagram outlines the sequential steps and operational stages involved in the experimental procedure. By mapping out the process, it provides a structured overview of the methodology, ensuring that the workflow is clearly defined and reproducible for future investigations within the scope of this research study.

caption: Calculated absolute lattice mismatch values (|δ|) for first-, third-, and fourth-generation nickel-based powder superalloys at 850 °C, derived using the Gamma/Gamma' Mismatch module in JMatPro.
summary: This plot displays the calculated absolute lattice mismatch (|δ|) for various generations of nickel-based powder superalloys at 850 °C. Using the Gamma/Gamma' Mismatch module in JMatPro, the data compares first-generation, third-generation, and fourth-generation alloys, providing a quantitative assessment of the lattice parameter differences between the gamma and gamma' phases.

caption: Bode phase diagram for L-PBF-produced NiTi alloy S2, depicting the phase angle response in Hank's solution at 37 °C.
summary: This Bode phase diagram characterizes the S2 NiTi alloy's electrochemical impedance response. Consistent with the other samples, the phase angle in the mid-frequency range (10°–10^2 Hz) remains near -80°, providing essential data for fitting the equivalent electrical circuit models used to evaluate the alloy-solution interfacial information.

caption: Tuj1 fluorescent staining of cells seeded on the 3D printed hydrogel scaffold after 72 h, showing extensive staining.
summary: Cells seeded on the 3D printed hydrogel scaffold exhibit extensive Tuj1 staining after 72 h of culture. This result demonstrates that the 3D structure significantly enhances neural differentiation and cellular response compared to the flat control, confirming the scaffold's efficacy in replicating a favorable in vivo-like growth environment.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy images displaying the morphology and adhesion of rBMSCs cultured on various composite hydrogel scaffolds at days 1, 3, and 5.
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy images illustrate the adhesion and spreading of rBMSCs on composite hydrogel scaffolds over a five-day period. By day 5, cells on CP, CP-0Co-13.4%, CP-0Co-16.2%, CP-5Co-13.4%, and CP-5Co-16.2% scaffolds exhibit well-spread morphologies, confirming that these composite hydrogel scaffolds effectively support cell adhesion and growth.

caption: Transversal X-ray µ-CT slice of the CO50/40/10 specimen gauge section showing morphological changes.
summary: The transversal X-ray µ-CT slice of the CO50/40/10 specimen illustrates modifications of the initial cylindrical morphology after consolidation. This cross-sectional view is part of the tomography analysis used to evaluate the internal composite structure and the quality of the consolidated material within the gauge section.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern of the consolidated carbon sample.
summary: This panel displays the selected area diffraction pattern for the consolidated carbon sample. The diffraction rings are indexed to confirm the phase composition, providing a structural analysis that complements XRD results as part of the broader investigation into the consolidated material's crystalline characteristics and phase identification.

caption: Spatial distribution map of the Cr element, showing correlation with black spots in the joint.
summary: This map illustrates the distribution of the Cr element across the joint. Notably, the Cr distribution corresponds to most of the black spots observed in the joint structure. This correlation suggests that chromium-rich phases or precipitates are localized within these specific features of the HIP-DBed joint interface.

caption: Principal component analysis of the 3s1 + 3s2 dataset for R = 0.1 aluminum alloy fatigue tests, illustrating feature contributions and multiplet centroids with a scaling factor of 0.06 applied to observations.
summary: Principal component analysis of the 3s1 + 3s2 dataset for R = 0.1 aluminum alloy fatigue tests illustrates feature contributions and multiplet centroids with a scaling factor of 0.06 applied to observations. Similar to the 2s1 + 2s2 dataset, PCA fails to distinguish between type I and type II multiplets.

caption: In-situ XRD heat map of monolithic Ta2N during vacuum heating, showing the formation of TaSi2 silicides marked with green stars at elevated temperatures.
summary: This in-situ XRD heat map tracks the phase evolution of monolithic Ta2N during vacuum heating up to 1200 °C. The analysis identifies the formation of TaSi2 silicides at elevated temperatures, with the standard diffraction angle position for these phases clearly marked by green stars in the heat map.

caption: Composite specimen manufactured on an Anisoprint Composer A4, demonstrating the effect of varying infill densities within the toolpath.
summary: This panel displays a composite specimen manufactured on an Anisoprint Composer A4, highlighting the implementation of varying infill densities. By keeping fiber length constant, this experimental setup allows for a controlled investigation into how infill density adjustments within the toolpath affect the overall mechanical properties of the 3D-printed composite materials.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetization for as-milled and annealed samples measured under a low applied magnetic field of 7.95·10^3 A/m, featuring an inset showing the heating curve of the DSC thermogram.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent magnetization of as-milled and annealed samples under a 7.95·10^3 A/m magnetic field. The inclusion of a DSC thermogram heating curve in the inset provides complementary thermal data, characterizing the phase transition behavior of the materials under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Design schematic of a truss structure composed of three distinct materials.
summary: This panel presents the design schematic for a truss structure engineered with three different materials. The structure serves as a foundational model to demonstrate the capabilities of multimaterial levitation 3D printing, illustrating the geometric arrangement and material distribution required for the subsequent fabrication process.

caption: Stacked 31P NMR spectra of Gly-APdA-VE in pH 7.4 HEPES:D2O (9:1) buffer, tracking the degradation progress through the disappearance of the monomer peak at 17 ppm and the emergence of intermediate (8 ppm) and phosphate (2.5 ppm) signals.
summary: Stacked 31P NMR spectra demonstrate the hydrolysis progress of Gly-APdA-VE at pH 7.4. The data show the disappearance of the APdA-VE resonance at 17 ppm, the coincident emergence of an intermediate peak at 8 ppm, and the gradual development of a phosphate peak at 2.5 ppm over time.

caption: STEM-HAADF image of the ST 1040 microstructure, displaying the morphology of (Cr, Mn)-rich oxide particles.
summary: STEM-HAADF imaging of the ST 1040 microstructure captures the morphology of (Cr, Mn)-rich oxide particles. These oxides are identified as part of the segregation process at grain boundaries, providing insight into the microstructural state of the material following the 1040 degree heat treatment.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the heat-treated HT-2 alloy, highlighting the distribution and morphology of precipitates within the copper matrix.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the heat-treated HT-2 alloy. It specifically reveals the formation and spatial distribution of precipitates within the copper matrix. The imaging technique provides high-contrast visualization of these secondary phases, which are critical for understanding the microstructural evolution following the post-annealing heat treatment process.

caption: Normalized electronic specific heat Cel/γT versus temperature for Ta5+yW35-yMo5Re35Ru20C20 HEAs, including the α-model fitting curve.
summary: Normalized electronic specific heat data for the Ta5+yW35-yMo5Re35Ru20C20 HEA series are plotted as Cel/γT versus temperature. The phonon contribution is subtracted to isolate the electronic specific heat. The red solid line represents the fitting curve generated by the α-model, illustrating the temperature dependence of the electronic properties for this specific alloy series.

caption: Visual comparison of a PETG beam with N=8 layers, featuring experimental deformation and a cyan FEM simulation overlay.
summary: This panel presents an experimental photograph of a PETG beam with eight layers, illustrating the deformation profile. The overlaid cyan FEM simulation curve serves as a qualitative validation of the simulation fidelity, demonstrating that the layer-specific CTE model effectively captures the physical morphing observed in the experimental PETG beam.

caption: Emission spectra of BSA-Au NCs measured at 395 nm excitation, showing the evolution of fluorescence intensity across different incubation time points during synthesis.
summary: This panel displays the emission spectra of BSA-Au NCs at various incubation times under 395 nm excitation. These spectral measurements were used to modify and optimize the synthetic process for the BSA-Au NCs, ensuring the desired fluorescence characteristics were achieved during the formation of the nanoclusters.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction displaying the chemical composition of distinct phases, specifically highlighting Cu-rich clusters within the B2 host matrix.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction reveals the chemical composition of various phases, including Cu-rich particles. Cluster analysis indicates these features contain over 60 at. % Cu, while the surrounding matrix chemistry aligns with the host B2 phase, demonstrating a clear compositional distinction between the clusters and the bulk material.

caption: Morphological representation of fabricated defects in APMMC sample A1, visualized via X-ray CT reconstruction.
summary: X-ray CT reconstruction analysis provides a morphological view of fabricated defects within the APMMC. Comparison between samples A1 and A3 indicates that sample A1 exhibits larger defect dimensions, serving as a baseline for evaluating the effectiveness of custom processing parameters in reducing manufacturing defect content and improving overall material densification.

caption: Atom probe tomography (APT) reconstruction of the interface region in Meander-DA alloy, highlighting the spatial distribution of γ′ and γ′′ precipitates, Laves phase, and an MC carbide.
summary: This APT reconstruction reveals the complex microstructure of the Meander-DA alloy interface. The image displays the spatial arrangement of γ′ and γ′′ precipitates, which are delineated by Al+Ti and Nb concentration isovalues, respectively, alongside a Cr and Mo-rich Laves phase and an MC carbide particle within the direct-aged matrix.

caption: Current density versus the inverse square root of time (i-t^-1/2) plot for NiCu alloy coatings during the passivation process.
summary: This plot displays the i-t^-1/2 relationship for NiCu alloy coatings, demonstrating high linearity. This linear behavior confirms that the nucleation and growth mechanisms occurring during the passivation process are controlled by diffusion, providing critical insight into the electrochemical kinetics and surface film formation dynamics of the alloy system.

caption: Parity plot demonstrating the agreement between CatBoost-predicted elongation and experimental data.
summary: This parity plot assesses the CatBoost model's accuracy in predicting elongation by plotting predicted values against experimental literature data. The red line represents a perfect 1:1 fit, while the black line illustrates the regression obtained from the model, highlighting the model's effectiveness in predicting elongation for the analyzed alloys.

caption: Finite element mesh representation of the mandible model, constructed using tetrahedral volumetric elements.
summary: This visualization displays the mesh structure generated on a mandible model for computational analysis. The model utilizes tetrahedral volumetric elements to discretize the geometry, as specified in the study. This mesh configuration serves as the foundational framework for subsequent finite element modeling and structural evaluation of the mandibular bone.

caption: Displacement field map derived from images captured using an ordinary optical lens, showing significant radial distortion distribution.
summary: This panel displays the displacement field between near-infrared and color waveband images compared to a standard reference image using an ordinary optical lens. The results indicate that displacement values for near-infrared bands are notably higher than those for color bands, characterized by a distinct and non-uniform radial distortion distribution.

caption: Phonon density of states and vibrational free energy for fcc Al, comparing L-S relationship predictions (black) with full phonon calculations (red).
summary: This panel displays the phonon density of states and vibrational free energy for fcc Al. The black lines represent predictions derived from L-S relationships, while the red lines indicate results from full phonon calculations. These data points illustrate the vibrational characteristics of the fcc Al phase within the Co-Al system.

caption: Dilatometric cooling curves showing length change versus temperature for three SPS-sintered alloys (AFMAR-10-10, AFMAR-10-13, and AFMAR-12-14) cooled from 1100 °C.
summary: Dilatometry curves illustrate the length dependence on temperature during cooling from 1100 °C for three carbon-free alloys. AFMAR-10-10 exhibits both Ms and Mf transformation temperatures, whereas AFMAR-10-13 displays only Ms. AFMAR-12-14 shows no indication of martensitic transformation, providing experimental validation for the calculated Thermocalc phase stability predictions.

caption: 1H NMR spectral analysis comparing the chemical structure of printing ink before and after cross-linking.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum provides insight into the molecular changes occurring during the cross-linking of the printing ink. By comparing the uncrosslinked and crosslinked states, the spectrum identifies structural modifications, confirming the chemical transformation of the ink components into the final hydrogel network structure through the cross-linking reaction.

caption: Stacked bar chart illustrating the ratio of winning (light blue) to losing (dark blue) agents across various scenarios, demonstrating a decline in the win/loss ratio as scenario size increases.
summary: Panel (a) presents a stacked bar chart comparing the win/loss ratios of agents across different scenarios. The data indicates that the win/loss ratio decreases as the scenario size increases, which serves as an indicator of undesired behavior within the mechanism being analyzed in this study.

caption: Total density of states for pure Cu calculated using a 4 × 4 × 4 k-point mesh.
summary: This panel displays the total density of states for pure copper, computed using a 4 × 4 × 4 k-point mesh. The electronic structure calculation provides a baseline for comparing the effects of zinc alloying on the density of states in the copper matrix.

caption: Confocal maximum Z-projection of NES cells cultured on a 30% PEGDA/10% GelMA pedestal, stained with calcein AM (green) and SYTOX (red), where the printed pedestal material remains largely invisible.
summary: This panel shows NES cells on a 30% PEGDA/10% GelMA pedestal using live/dead staining. The printed pedestal is not visible in the confocal images, as the material requires high laser power and long exposure times to be visualized, highlighting the cell distribution relative to the underlying 3D printed bioink structure.

caption: Raman spectrum of a 2L MoWS2 film on SiO2 substrate, featuring a deconvolution analysis that identifies MoS2-like and WS2-like vibrational modes through red and blue Gaussian fitting components, respectively.
summary: This Raman spectrum characterizes a 2L MoWS2 film deposited on a SiO2 substrate. The analysis employs deconvolution to resolve the vibrational modes of the alloy, specifically highlighting MoS2-like and WS2-like contributions. These distinct Gaussian components, represented in red and blue, provide insight into the vibrational characteristics of the MoWS2 alloy.

caption: Dilatometry curves and calculated linear coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) trends for Fe100, Fe75Cu25, Fe50Cu50, and Fe25Cu75 as-built samples, featuring an inset highlighting a characteristic CTE bump peaking at approximately 275 °C followed by a decline up to 350 °C.
summary: This figure displays dilatometry plots and linear CTE trends for Fe-Cu alloys. The data reveals a consistent thermal behavior across all samples, characterized by a slight CTE increase peaking at 275 °C and a subsequent decline. These thermophysical properties contribute to thermal stresses during deposition, influencing solidification cracking in heterogeneous structures.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the MoNbTaWCr system illustrating phase stability and constituent development.
summary: Representing the MoNbTaWCr system, this pseudo-binary phase diagram details the formation of multiple intermetallic constituents. The plot serves as a critical reference for understanding the phase equilibrium and structural transformations occurring within the alloy, demonstrating how compositional changes influence the development of distinct intermetallic phases in this specific system.

caption: Radar diagram comparing the performance metrics of three distinct biphasic structures, including modulus, strength at 0.1% strain, post-impact thickness, thermal conductivity, and backside temperature after 1000 seconds of heating.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of three biphasic structures by evaluating their mechanical and thermal performance. Key metrics displayed include modulus, strength at 0.1% strain, residual thickness after impact, thermal conductivity, and backside temperature after 1000 seconds of heating, offering an intuitive visualization of their relative impact resistance and insulation properties.

caption: Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCoA) plot displaying the bacterial community structure at the ASV level, with data points differentiated by electrode type and biomass source.
summary: Bacterial community composition is represented through PCoA, highlighting variations across different electrode types and biomass sources. ANOSIM analysis was utilized to evaluate the significance of group separation, offering insights into how electrode configurations influence the bacterial community structure within the reactor environments.

caption: Photoluminescence spectra of the sample in the short-wavelength region under 1-mW 532-nm excitation, highlighting a 32-nm-wavelength-range emission spanning from 740 nm to 672 nm.
summary: This photoluminescence spectrum displays emission in the short-wavelength region under 532-nm excitation. A notable 32-nm-wavelength-range emission is observed between 740 nm and 672 nm. Peaks around 1 V and 3.5 V correlate with current increases in the I-V curve, indicating new electron transport paths and enhanced output current.

caption: Schematic representation of the base AA6061 alloy microstructure, illustrating the initial state prior to friction stir deposition processing.
summary: This panel depicts the base material state of the AA6061 alloy. It serves as the reference point for understanding the subsequent microstructural evolution and strengthening mechanisms introduced by the AFSD process and subsequent heat treatment, providing a baseline for comparing the initial material condition against processed samples.

caption: Bode plots for sample S5, displaying impedance spectra recorded in pure PBS and during 10 days of immersion in PBS + 1 M H2O2.
summary: Bode plots for sample S5 demonstrate the electrochemical response during exposure to PBS and 1 M H2O2. The spectra, including a pure PBS baseline, show the frequency-dependent impedance behavior of the sample as it undergoes degradation over a 10-day immersion period in the peroxide-containing electrolyte.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the produced samples measured in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Experimental potentiodynamic polarization curves are presented for the fabricated samples tested in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These curves illustrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the materials, highlighting significant variations in performance across the different samples as indicated by the comparative electrochemical data.

caption: Fast Fourier transform pattern corresponding to region c, highlighting the lattice characteristics of the interface.
summary: This FFT pattern of region c reveals the lattice characteristics of the heterojunction. Calculations of crystal plane spacing indicate a lattice mismatch of approximately 1.21% between TiC (111) and Ti2AlC (000-2), which confirms the existence of a coherent interface between the two materials at this specific location.

caption: Additional SAED pattern confirming the twinning characteristics within the primary γ′ phase.
summary: This SAED pattern serves as further crystallographic evidence of twinning within the primary γ′ phase. By analyzing the diffraction spots, the presence of twin boundaries is confirmed, which correlates with the microstructural changes observed in the primary γ′ phase during the high-temperature deformation process.

caption: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of region A in the as-forged condition, highlighting coarse, interconnected γ′′ precipitates along dislocation structures decorated by smaller γ′ precipitates.
summary: Region A in the as-forged condition displays coarse, interconnected γ′′ precipitates formed along dislocation structures, which are decorated by smaller γ′ precipitates. These coarse precipitates account for a 2.4% volume fraction, with major axis lengths ranging from 15 to 50 nm, significantly influencing the material's strengthening effects.

caption: Scanning probe microscopy image of the uncharged sample surface showing initial topography.
summary: Scanning probe microscopy was utilized to monitor the sample surface continuously during cathodic charging. Panel (a) displays the surface topography of the uncharged sample, serving as the baseline reference for subsequent polarization sequences. This initial state provides a clear view of the surface morphology before any electrochemical hydrogen charging was applied.

caption: Fatigue crack growth rate (da/dN) plotted against the stress intensity factor range (ΔK) for SEN-T specimens tested at 550 °C under varying loading frequencies of 0.1, 1.0, and 5.0 Hz.
summary: This plot illustrates the fatigue crack growth behavior of SEN-T specimens at 550 °C. The data demonstrates that loading frequency has no significant impact on the slopes of the da/dN versus ΔK curves within the Paris regime, indicating consistent crack growth kinetics across the tested frequencies under these specific fatigue conditions.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops measured along the easy axis (0°) for segments C1–C12, showing a progressive reduction in magnetic performance as print height increases.
summary: Magnetic hysteresis measurements along the easy axis (0°) for the continuously printed Nd–Fe–B specimen reveal the evolution of anisotropy with print height. Segments C1–C12, cut at increasing heights, show darker curves for lower indices (closer to the magnet) and lighter curves for higher indices, indicating a progressive loss of magnetic anisotropy.

caption: Transparency measurements of starch pastes derived from different rambutan seed starches, showing a decreasing trend in the order of BR-4, BR-5, and BR-7.
summary: This panel displays the transparency of starch pastes prepared from various rambutan seed starches. The results indicate that the transparency decreases sequentially across the samples, following the order BR-4 > BR-5 > BR-7. This variation highlights the distinct optical properties inherent to the different starch sources investigated in this study.

caption: Experimental verification of the LP11 mode excitation in the photonic crystal fiber at a wavelength of 1300 nm.
summary: Experimental verification of the LP11 mode excitation in the photonic crystal fiber at a wavelength of 1300 nm. This panel demonstrates that the LP11 mode can be selectively excited at this specific wavelength, confirming the modal properties of the developed fiber through experimental observation as described in the study.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of HPCA at DS = 0.4, with the reflected wavelength increasing from 457 nm.
summary: This reflectance spectrum shows the optical response of HPCA at a degree of substitution of 0.4. The reflected wavelength begins at 457 nm. The data demonstrates that the reflected wavelength becomes more prominent as the degree of substitution increases, reflecting the underlying changes in the material's helical pitch.

caption: t-SNE visualization of the ResPHN-type1 model feature space demonstrating improved clustering compared to ResNet18, though boundaries between classes B and C remain blurred.
summary: This t-SNE plot for the ResPHN-type1 model shows an improvement in clustering performance over the baseline ResNet18 model. Despite this enhancement, the visualization indicates that the boundaries between classes B and C remain blurred, suggesting that while feature extraction is better, class separation is not yet optimal.

caption: Cooling time Δt₈/₅ plotted against heat input for WAAM-deposited walls at the first deposition layer using CMT, S-GMAW, and P-GMAW transfer modes.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between cooling time Δt₈/₅ and heat input for the first layer of WAAM-deposited walls. Data is presented for CMT, S-GMAW, and P-GMAW transfer modes. The cooling time exhibits a linear increase as the heat input rises across these different welding transfer modes.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting (Ni-Cu)4Ti3 precipitates using the diffraction spot labeled 'c'.
summary: Captured using the diffraction spot labeled 'c', this dark-field TEM image specifically highlights the distribution of (Ni-Cu)4Ti3 precipitates within the matrix. This visualization technique isolates the signal from these specific particles, allowing for a clear observation of their morphology and spatial arrangement in the homogenized and aged printed material.

caption: Vallen AMSY-6 acoustic emission system configured for real-time signal acquisition during mechanical loading.
summary: The Vallen AMSY-6 acoustic emission system is depicted as the instrumentation used for monitoring acoustic emissions during the uniaxial compression test. This system captures transient elastic waves generated within the rock specimen, providing critical data on internal damage evolution and fracture processes occurring throughout the mechanical loading procedure.

caption: Matching list for corindon identification, with LIBS elemental signals indicated by blue text and molecular spectra by red text.
summary: Corindon identification is demonstrated through a matching list that categorizes LIBS elemental signals in blue and molecular spectra in red. This table provides a comparative analysis of the unknown sample against a database, facilitating the accurate classification of the mineral based on the provided spectral and elemental correlation values.

caption: XRD patterns of the Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy following heat treatment at 600 °C, showing the evolution of phase diffraction peaks.
summary: Following heat treatment at 600 °C, the XRD pattern shows the disappearance of the (110) diffraction peak associated with the residual β phase. Only a weak (002) diffraction peak remains, demonstrating that the Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy is primarily composed of the α/α′ phase after the thermal treatment process.

caption: Surface profile cartography of the material processed at 60 MPa water pressure and 10 m/min traverse speed.
summary: Surface texture cartography for the specimen processed at 60 MPa and 10 m/min is shown. This condition represents the baseline for the 60 MPa series. The intensity of material removal is observed to be higher at this lower traverse speed compared to higher speeds within the same pressure group.

caption: Relative error distribution for the Multi-Output Support Vector Regression (MOSVR) model evaluated on the test dataset.
summary: Relative error analysis for the MOSVR model on the test set is shown here. This plot supports the research findings by quantifying the predictive accuracy of the MOSVR approach, allowing for a direct comparison of error magnitudes against other models tested within the scope of the relative error analysis.

caption: Width characteristics of α/α′ and β/β phases determined through statistical analysis of 50 grains at distinct locations.
summary: Width measurements for α and β lamellae are presented in this box plot, derived from a statistical analysis of 50 grains per location. The data reveals the specific dimensional variations of these lamellar phases, offering insight into the microstructural features and grain size distribution across the examined material regions.

caption: Randomly selected functional data curves categorized into five distinct clusters identified by the GPmix algorithm.
summary: This panel displays randomly selected functions grouped into five distinct clusters as identified by the GPmix algorithm. These functional data curves illustrate the underlying patterns and variability captured by the model, providing a visual representation of the five identified clusters within the dataset analyzed by the GPmix framework.

caption: Operando EC-STM image of a Cu(100) surface, previously exposed to ambient air for 24 h, captured after 180 s of electrochemical treatment at -0.9 V in 1 mM K2SO4 solution adjusted to pH 9 with KOH.
summary: This steady-state, atom-resolved EC-STM image displays the surface morphology of a Cu(100) sample after 24 hours of air exposure followed by 180 seconds of electrochemical reduction at -0.9 V in a pH 9 K2SO4 electrolyte. The visualization provides a clear atomic-scale view of the surface under operando conditions.

caption: SEM-EDS elemental distribution maps of the PBF-LB sample vertical cross-section, revealing inhomogeneous magnesium distribution alongside uniform silicon and oxygen dispersion.
summary: SEM-EDS elemental distribution maps of the PBF-LB sample vertical cross-section reveal inhomogeneous magnesium distribution, while silicon and oxygen remain uniformly dispersed. This chemical fluctuation, likely induced by laser-driven magnesium evaporation during the PBF-LB process, contributes to the observed inhomogeneity of the alpha-Al/Mg2Si two-phase microstructure within the melt-pool structure.

caption: Complementary EELS intensity profiles focusing on Zr and B distribution, demonstrating low elemental content for these species at the precipitated phase/matrix interface.
summary: This panel provides additional EELS data focusing on the distribution of Zr and B. The profiles show that these elements maintain low intensity levels at the interface between the precipitated phase and the matrix, further characterizing the chemical environment and the specific composition of the healing phase.

caption: Confusion matrix showing action recognition performance for the image dataset at a resolution of 384x384 pixels.
summary: Action recognition results for the image dataset at 384x384 resolution are presented in this confusion matrix. Diagonal values quantify the proportion of correctly classified instances for each of the 11 classes, with off-diagonal values indicating misclassifications. This plot is part of the four best-performing configurations analyzed in the research.

caption: Schematic representation detailing the dimensions of the tensile specimen configured for high-temperature mechanical testing.
summary: This panel presents the geometric dimensions of the tensile specimen utilized for high-temperature testing. The diagram defines the specific specimen configuration required for mechanical evaluation under elevated thermal conditions, facilitating accurate tensile property measurements for the LPBF Inconel 625 alloy during high-temperature experimental procedures.

caption: Processed laser image of the AP_EPP2 component surface using a threshold of 0.5, showing enhanced boundary definition.
summary: This processed image of the AP_EPP2 component, using a 0.5 threshold, demonstrates the impact of the second EPP step. The semicircular black-and-white boundary on the right side is shown to have expanded inward and become more defined, confirming that the gloss coverage was significantly improved by the optimized polishing parameters.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of a 79.5 wt% Fe-Ni laser remelted sample at 100 mm/s travel speed, displaying lath-like martensitic morphology.
summary: Laser remelted 79.5 wt% Fe-Ni sample processed at 100 mm/s travel speed, revealing lath-like martensitic morphologies. The inverse pole figure map shows the grain structure, confirming that the martensitic transformation remains stable across varying solidification conditions for this iron-nickel composition.

caption: Scheil solidification diagram for the HN sample, demonstrating a shift toward austenitic primary solidification (L → γ) with FCC_A1 phase formation at the onset.
summary: This Scheil solidification diagram for the HN sample reveals a distinct shift in solidification behavior compared to the LN sample. The simulation shows that the solidification process proceeds via an austenitic primary mode (L → γ), characterized by the appearance of the FCC_A1 phase at the very onset of solidification.

caption: S-N fatigue performance curve for the HIP + STA specimen tested at 25 °C.
summary: This panel presents the S-N diagram for the HIP + STA specimen at 25 °C. It illustrates the fatigue life characteristics following hot isostatic pressing and solution treatment and aging, allowing for a direct comparison with the STA specimen to assess the influence of HIP on fatigue performance.

caption: Long-term cycling performance showing Coulombic efficiency (CE), voltage efficiency (VE), and energy efficiency (EE) for V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) over 100 cycles at 100 mA cm -2.
summary: Long-term stability testing of V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) over 100 cycles at 100 mA cm -2 reveals high efficiency metrics. The system maintains an average coulombic efficiency of 97.24%, an average voltage efficiency of approximately 78.92%, and an average energy efficiency of 76.74%, demonstrating excellent electrochemical durability.

caption: Expected value E[Fi] of the predictive posterior at the maximum time scale τmax.
summary: Panel (c) presents the expected value E[Fi] of the predictive posterior for the F1,16 model at the maximum time scale τmax. By comparing these contours to those at τmin, the figure demonstrates how the model's learned expected output evolves across different temporal scales within the DS(3) training framework.

caption: Diffusion coefficient D N and lifetime τ N of Cu-rich precipitates (CRPs) plotted against the number of Cu atoms per cluster, derived from kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations at 773 K compared with literature data.
summary: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations at 773 K characterize the mobility of Cu clusters by calculating their diffusion coefficients and lifetimes. These parameters are plotted as a function of the number of Cu atoms within the clusters, showing consistent trends when compared against established data from previous literature studies.

caption: Magnetization curves for Ni-Mn-In-based Heusler alloys measured at 5 T, with an inset displaying the M(H) hysteresis loop for Ni50Mn35In14.25B0.75 at 5 K.
summary: High-field magnetization measurements at 5 T demonstrate the temperature stabilization of the ferromagnetic austenitic phase, causing a shift in the martensitic transition temperature. The inset shows the M(H) curve at 5 K, confirming a ground state magnetization of 35–37 emu/g in the martensitic phase, which is significantly lower than the austenitic phase magnetization.

caption: Crack resistance R-curves plotting J-integral versus crack extension for CS900 and CS1000 samples.
summary: Fracture toughness is evaluated through R-curves, which plot the J-integral against crack extension for CS900 and CS1000 samples. The results demonstrate that the CS1000 deposit possesses a higher fracture toughness than the CS900 deposit, consistent with the higher KIC values observed in mechanical testing for the CS1000 material.

caption: Hardness profiles measured across the interface of two hybrid-built MS1-Nimax specimens, illustrating the variation in mechanical properties.
summary: This plot displays the hardness profiles across the interface of two hybrid-built MS1-Nimax specimens. The data reveals that the LPBF-built MS1 component experiences a hardness reduction from 38 HRC to 32 HRC following HT1 treatment, which is attributed to the microstructural transformation from fine cell-type to large lath structures.

caption: Weibull fracture probability plot of compressive strength for LIS samples sintered in air at 1190°C for 3 hours.
summary: This panel displays the Weibull fracture probability plot for LIS samples sintered in air at 1190°C for 3 hours. The plot evaluates the characteristic compressive strength of the material, providing a statistically robust trend for the mechanical performance of the LIS ceramic under these specific sintering conditions.

caption: Output voltage curves comparing 3D-printed PVDF and PVDF nanocomposites, demonstrating the influence of material composition on electrical performance.
summary: The output voltage curves for 3D-printed PVDF and PVDF nanocomposites are presented to evaluate their electrical performance. These measurements highlight how the incorporation of nanocomposites into the 3D-printed PVDF matrix influences the resulting voltage output, providing a comparative analysis of the materials' effectiveness in the TENG configuration.

caption: Random color grain map of the sample processed with 0.9 mm hatch spacing.
summary: This random color grain map shows the grain distribution for the sample produced with a 0.9 mm hatch spacing. Consistent with the broader trend observed in the study, samples with reduced hatch spacing exhibit smaller grain sizes and a more random texture compared to those processed with wider hatch spacing parameters.

caption: In-plane flux density norm distribution within a Ni/Fe Z-pinned coupon under a 10,000 A/m magnetic field.
summary: Finite element analysis illustrates the in-plane magnetic flux density distribution within Ni/Fe Z-pinned coupons. Subjected to a 10,000 A/m magnetic field, the simulation allows for the observation of internal flux density variations, providing a comprehensive view of how the magnetic field interacts with the pin geometry in-plane.

caption: Convergence behavior of the ERWCA algorithm represented as a 3D convergence curve.
summary: The ERWCA algorithm demonstrates its convergence characteristics through a 3D convergence curve. This visualization illustrates the optimization progress of the algorithm, providing insight into how the solution space is explored and refined over the course of the computational process as part of the comparative performance analysis of tested algorithms.

caption: Test confusion matrix for the ResPHN-type1 model, mapping true versus predicted labels.
summary: ResPHN-type1 model performance is visualized through this confusion matrix, which maps true labels against predicted outputs. The analysis reveals that misclassifications occur primarily within classes C and D, resulting in slightly lower overall accuracy for these specific categories compared to the performance observed in other classes.

caption: Pole figure of the {001} crystal plane for the H-1100–60 specimen.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the {001} crystal plane for the H-1100–60 specimen. As the homogenization temperature reaches 1100 ℃, the pole clusters along the BD direction shift downward, and the maximum pole figure value decreases to less than 10 MRD, indicating a transition in the crystallographic texture development.

caption: EBSD orientation map of heat-treated Invar 36 alloy showing the persistence of columnar grains.
summary: Heat-treated Invar 36 alloy microstructure is depicted in panel (d) via EBSD mapping. The results indicate that the columnar grain structure remains almost unchanged following the heat treatment process, demonstrating that while phase distribution is affected, the fundamental grain orientation and morphology are preserved after the thermal cycle.

caption: STEM-HAADF image of the 718Plus alloy microstructure following a creep test at 650 °C and 800 MPa.
summary: This STEM-HAADF image displays the microstructure of the 718Plus alloy after undergoing a creep process at 650 °C and 800 MPa. The imaging technique provides high-angle annular dark-field contrast to reveal the structural state of the material under these specific high-temperature and high-pressure deformation conditions.

caption: Comparison of FTIR spectra for resins synthesized with and without silver incorporation, highlighting specific peaks attributed to the nitrate anion.
summary: This FTIR spectral analysis compares resin formulations prepared with and without silver. The spectra reveal distinct peaks associated with the presence of the nitrate anion within the resin matrix. These findings demonstrate the chemical influence of silver incorporation on the resin structure as evidenced by the observed vibrational signatures.

caption: Comparison of inner diameters of nanotubes or collagen fibers within the matrix of IMNS, SRCP, and NHC, showing a mean diameter of 37.3 ± 7.9 nm for SRCP.
summary: This bar chart compares the inner diameters of nanotubes or collagen fibers across IMNS, SRCP, and NHC samples. The SRCP exhibits a mean nanotube inner diameter of 37.3 ± 7.9 nm, confirming that the engineered scaffold successfully mimics the structural dimensions found in the natural human corneal stroma.

caption: Representative immunofluorescence images and topographical maps of Collagen II expression in cartilage scaffolds, with nuclei stained blue and Collagen II in red.
summary: Collagen II immunofluorescence imaging and topographical mapping demonstrate that the CSK@P200 and CSK@P300 scaffold groups exhibit the strongest fluorescence intensity. These results indicate that specific pore sizes significantly influence the expression of Collagen II, a key marker for cartilage differentiation, compared to the other scaffold groups after two months.

caption: Differential interference contrast image showing the co-culture of HaCaT cells with PAMS hydrogel to evaluate biocompatibility.
summary: This differential interference contrast image displays the co-culture of HaCaT cells with PAMS hydrogel. Serving as a visual assessment of biocompatibility, the microscopy observation confirms the interaction between the hydrogel and the cells, providing a foundational evaluation of the material's suitability for biological applications within the experimental setup.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of a solution-treated sample (1250 °C for 24 h) showing thermal transitions during heating.
summary: This DSC analysis of the 24 h solution-treated sample investigates the α-Ti phase transition to determine the optimal aging temperature for maximum α-Ti precipitation. The curve provides critical thermal data to understand the transformation kinetics, which are essential for facilitating the extensive nucleation of α-Ti at the interface of ω/β phases.

caption: Quasi-steady melt pool morphology observed under Diagonal Ellipse (DE) beam shaping conditions.
summary: This image displays the quasi-steady melt pool geometry generated by a Diagonal Ellipse (DE) beam shape. The visualization captures the specific thermal footprint and liquid-solid interface characteristics during the laser processing, providing a clear representation of the melt pool shape resulting from this particular beam configuration during the experiment.

caption: Flow cytometric quantification of CD69+ expression as a percentage of total CD8+ T cells, highlighting increased activation marker expression in T cells co-cultured with AH1-pulsed, CpG ODN-activated DCs.
summary: Flow cytometric analysis of CD69+ CD8+ T cells shows increased expression in the presence of CpG ODN-activated DCs pulsed with AH1 peptide. This finding supports the observation that T cells co-cultured under these specific conditions exhibit higher activation marker expression compared to those co-cultured with non-activated DCs.

caption: Sc2p high-resolution XPS spectrum of the as-aged Al–6Ni-0.4Sc alloy after electrochemical testing.
summary: Sc2p high-resolution XPS spectrum for the as-aged Al–6Ni-0.4Sc alloy after electrochemical testing is illustrated. The aging treatment increases the density of coherent Al3Sc precipitates, facilitating the formation of Sc2O3 passive films, which are identified through this spectroscopic analysis following the electrochemical test.

caption: Beeswarm plot of SHAP values for SG and MPT features, demonstrating that higher melt pool area (MPA) values generally contribute to increased porosity, while lower values tend to decrease it.
summary: The beeswarm plot for SG and MPT features reveals the distribution of SHAP values, where most data points cluster near zero, indicating minimal feature contribution. However, higher MPA values are associated with larger SHAP values that increase porosity, whereas lower MPA values contribute to decreasing porosity, as evidenced by the color-coded feature distribution.

caption: Accuracy of SL material identification plotted against sampling methods using a threshold defined by the mean lead concentration of the non-LSL control group.
summary: This plot illustrates the identification accuracy for SL materials when applying a threshold based on the mean lead concentration of the non-LSL control group. By utilizing this specific statistical metric, the graph demonstrates how different sampling methods influence the overall precision of material classification within the study's control framework.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for Cu–10Ni-xAl alloys (x = 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt%) immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution after aging at 450 °C.
summary: Bode plots for Cu–10Ni-xAl alloys with varying aluminum content are shown to further analyze the electrochemical impedance behavior in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These plots provide frequency-dependent data on the impedance magnitude and phase angle, complementing the Nyquist analysis to clarify the corrosion process and surface film characteristics of the aged alloys.

caption: Comparative EDS analysis results detailing the elemental composition of the matrix across the substrate, the interface region, and the printed wall.
summary: This panel presents EDS analysis results for the matrix across different regions, including the substrate, the interface, and the printed wall layers. The reference sentences specify that this analysis covers the matrix from the substrate up to the 4th layers, providing a comprehensive chemical profile of the material's structural evolution.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness data normalized by relative density, calculated based on the Ashby-Gibson scaling relation.
summary: Hardness values are normalized by the relative density of the nanoporous silver, applying the Ashby-Gibson relation to account for porosity effects. This transformation helps isolate the influence of the solid volume fraction on the mechanical response, allowing for a more accurate comparison of intrinsic material strength across different samples.

caption: STEM-BF micrograph of Ti–42Nb+0.5C TMC revealing the distribution of TiC particles within the β-Ti grain boundaries and the interior of the grains.
summary: STEM-BF imaging of the Ti–42Nb+0.5C TMC composite reveals the spatial distribution of TiC particles. These particles are observed both at the grain boundaries and within the β-Ti grains, providing clear evidence of the microstructural arrangement of the carbide phase within the metallic matrix of the alloy.

caption: Projected interference fringes observed when there is no rotation angle between components.
summary: Absence of a rotation angle between the PLM and DMD results in the interference fringe pattern shown. This configuration is achieved during the adjustment process when the fringe offset reaches its maximum, confirming that the PLM and DMD have successfully attained a perfect alignment in the light path.

caption: Residual strain plotted against normalised crack length for various specimens, with a vertical dashed line indicating the crack tip location where plasticity effects become significant.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between residual strain and normalised crack length for various specimens. A vertical dashed line marks the specific crack tip location beyond which plasticity effects become significant, as defined by the governing equation. These results provide critical data for understanding strain evolution during crack propagation.

caption: In situ Ni K-edge QXANES spectra of 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst during H2-TPR, capturing the reduction behavior of nickel species under a linear temperature ramp of 10 °C/min up to 800 °C.
summary: This panel presents the in situ Ni K-edge QXANES spectra recorded for the 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst during H2-TPR. The spectra track the reduction of nickel species as the temperature is increased to 800 °C at 10 °C/min, providing insight into the structural changes occurring within the nickel-based active sites.

caption: Polarization curves comparing the electrochemical performance of LPBF-processed 316L SS BPPs under optimal ASPN, gold spraying, and untreated surface conditions.
summary: Polarization curves are presented to evaluate the electrochemical performance of LPBF-processed BPPs with different surface treatments. These curves provide the necessary data to assess the voltage-current density relationship for each surface condition, serving as the foundation for calculating the power density curves shown in the subsequent panel of the figure.

caption: Temperature profiles measured at four distinct positions along the height direction for the four bioinspired sandwich structures.
summary: Temperature data extracted at four different positions along the height of the D0, D1.4, D1.9, and D2.4 structures characterize their thermal insulation performance. This line graph illustrates the temperature changes across the height, allowing for a clear comparison of how each specific sandwich structure manages heat conduction internally.

caption: Grain size distribution for 0° hatch rotation at 200 W laser power, 70 µm hatch spacing, and 1000 mm/s scan speed.
summary: Representing the grain size distribution for 0° hatch rotation at 200 W and 70 µm hatch spacing, this plot shows a broad, multimodal distribution. This pattern is indicative of abnormal and epitaxial grain growth, which occurs in samples exhibiting strong thermal accumulation during the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Comparison of global and local elastic moduli for TAOR scaffolds against the target range of human bone across various anatomical sites.
summary: This plot illustrates the elastic moduli of TAOR scaffolds in relation to human bone requirements. By targeting relative densities between 0.07 and 0.12, these scaffolds are specifically engineered for interbody spinal fusion applications, ensuring their mechanical properties align with the physiological demands of different anatomical sites within the human skeletal system.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation diagram illustrating the kinetics of NbC precipitation in AM Inconel 718, showing curves for 50% and 99% transformed fractions.
summary: This time-temperature-transformation diagram characterizes the precipitation kinetics of NbC within the AM Inconel 718 superalloy. It specifically maps the time required to reach 50% and 99% transformed fractions across various temperatures, providing a comprehensive overview of the precipitation process and the temporal evolution of the phase transformation.

caption: Comparison of tensile strength and fracture toughness values for Cast, 3DP-Y, and 3DP-Z specimens.
summary: This panel displays the predicted tensile strength and fracture toughness for Cast, 3DP-Y, and 3DP-Z specimens. Results indicate that values for Cast and 3DP-Y/Z are comparable, with 3DP-Z exhibiting slightly higher performance. These findings align with established literature, confirming the mechanical consistency across these specific specimen fabrication methods.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum obtained from the rim region of the (Nb,W)C phase, indicating a higher tungsten content.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the rim region demonstrates a higher tungsten content compared to the core. This spectral confirmation validates the BSE contrast interpretation, showing that the rim of the (Nb,W)C phase is enriched in W following the sintering process at 1390 °C.

caption: Tafel polarization curves of symmetrical cells utilizing I-/I3- electrolyte and various counter electrodes (CEs) to evaluate catalytic activity.
summary: Tafel polarization curves are presented for symmetrical cells fabricated with different counter electrodes to assess their catalytic activity in an I-/I3- electrolyte system. These measurements complement electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data, providing a comprehensive evaluation of the electrochemical performance and catalytic efficiency of the various counter electrode materials tested.

caption: Breakdown of damage mechanisms for wire-arc DED NAB samples after 24 hours of cavitation erosion in artificial seawater.
summary: Presented here is the percentage breakdown of damage mechanisms for wire-arc DED NAB alloys following 24 hours of cavitation erosion in artificial seawater. The analysis reveals that corrosion interactions contribute to 52.3% of the incremental mass loss, underscoring the substantial impact of combined erosion and corrosion processes on material degradation.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for WAAM and WAAM + UI specimens along TD, illustrating the cathodic hydrogen evolution reaction and anodic α-Mg matrix dissolution branches.
summary: Figure 8(b) displays the PDP curves for WAAM and WAAM + UI specimens along the TD. The cathode branch represents the hydrogen evolution reaction, while the anode branch corresponds to α-Mg matrix dissolution. UI treatment increases the self-corrosion potential, indicating a decreasing self-corrosion trend for the AZ31 thin walls.

caption: SAXS pattern of the D-3DP electrode, with the inset showing the 2D-SAXS pattern.
summary: The SAXS pattern of the D-3DP electrode, including the 2D-SAXS inset, provides structural information at the nanoscale. This diffraction data characterizes the internal organization and pore features of the electrode, supporting the observations made through microscopic techniques regarding the material's porous architecture.

caption: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy survey spectra for 316H-3 and 316H-4 stainless steel coupons following the completion of sputtering, with relative signal intensity plotted against binding energy.
summary: This XPS survey spectrum displays the surface chemical composition of 316H-3 and 316H-4 stainless steel coupons after sputtering. These samples were exposed to salt environments containing added beryllium. The data provides insight into the surface elemental states of the coupons, complementing the compositional analysis detailed in the study's supplementary tables.

caption: Spectral normal emissivity of 316 stainless steel measured at 300 °C, comparing the unexposed reference sample (0.03 μm RMS roughness) to the sample exposed to supercritical CO2 at 650 °C for 400 hours (1.6 μm RMS roughness), accompanied by photographic insets of the respective surfaces.
summary: This plot displays the spectral normal emissivity of 316 stainless steel at 300 °C. Exposure to supercritical CO2 at 650 °C for 400 hours significantly increases emissivity compared to the unexposed reference, correlating with an increase in surface roughness from 0.03 μm to 1.6 μm, as shown in the accompanying sample photographs.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ni–Fe system highlighting the infinite solid solubility.
summary: The Ni–Fe binary phase diagram shows that Ni and Fe are infinitely solid-soluble. This complete solubility prevents the formation of brittle intermetallics, allowing Ni to effectively act as a diffusion barrier between Ti and Fe, which is essential for maintaining stable interfaces in multi-material systems.

caption: CALPHAD-calculated equilibrium phase stability diagram for the TiNbCr MPE alloy, generated using Thermo-Calc software and the HEA05 database.
summary: This CALPHAD-calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the TiNbCr MPE alloy predicts the thermodynamic stability of phases across varying temperatures. It indicates a high-temperature BCC matrix with Laves C14 phase, while at lower temperatures, it predicts a Nb-rich BCC matrix, Cr-rich Laves C15 phase, and a Ti-rich HCP phase.

caption: Electrical resistivity measurements comparing cTPU/PLLA and 1% MWCNTs-TPU/PLLA scaffolds to evaluate electrothermal conversion efficiency.
summary: This plot presents the electrical resistivity measurements for cTPU/PLLA and 1% MWCNTs-TPU/PLLA scaffolds. By testing the resistivity, the researchers evaluated the electrothermal conversion efficiency of the different scaffold formulations, providing quantitative data to compare the electrical performance and potential heating capabilities of the materials under test.

caption: Hole concentration measured at room temperature as a function of the graded layer thickness for the various contact structures studied.
summary: This panel displays the room temperature hole concentration for different contact structures. The data is plotted against varying thicknesses of the graded layer to evaluate the impact of structural modifications on carrier density, providing essential insights into the electronic properties of the studied materials as determined by Hall effect measurements.

caption: Optical micrograph of the Al 14.5 Co 25 Fe 35.5 Ni 25 alloy processed by DED-LB/M, illustrating the refined dendritic features.
summary: Optical microscopy of the DED-LB/M processed Al 14.5 Co 25 Fe 35.5 Ni 25 alloy shows a refined dendritic structure compared to the cast counterpart. The image illustrates the effect of the DED-LB/M process on the length scale and spacing of the intra- and interdendritic regions in this alloy.

caption: Length distribution of Laves particles showing the frequency of occurrence across different size ranges.
summary: Length distribution of Laves particles showing the frequency of occurrence across different size ranges. Statistical analysis reveals that large Laves particles exceeding 5 µm in length disappear entirely at oscillating frequencies exceeding 200 Hz, demonstrating a significant shift in the particle size distribution under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the HT2 specimen cross-sectional fracture surface subjected to a 0.4% strain amplitude.
summary: Inverse pole figure mapping of the HT2 specimen fracture surface at 0.4% strain amplitude reveals distinct alpha phase refinement zones. These regions contain fragmented alpha phase structures, and quantitative orientation analysis indicates that mechanical property gradients, rather than crystallographic alignment, dominate the observed crack deflection behavior in these titanium alloys.

caption: Pole figure (PF) and inverse pole figure (IPF) plots illustrating the preferred orientation of the (100) crystallographic direction for the Si 0.3 MEA sample.
summary: Representing the Si 0.3 MEA sample, this panel shows the pole figure and inverse pole figure for the (100) crystallographic direction. The results characterize the final texture state of the series, demonstrating the preferred orientation patterns observed in the material with the highest silicon concentration investigated in this study.

caption: Kissinger equation plots derived from the peak temperatures of the three fit curves in panel (a) for the SX1 specimen.
summary: Kissinger equation plots are presented for the SX1 specimen, mapping the relationship between peak temperatures and heating rates. By applying this analysis to the three distinct fit curves, the activation energy for hydrogen desorption from dislocation, γ′, and γ phases is determined, providing insight into the hydrogen trapping characteristics of the material.

caption: Convergence behavior of the machine learning model predicting strut node dislocation values.
summary: This panel illustrates the convergence study for the machine learning model focused on strut node dislocation. The plot demonstrates how the estimated values stabilize as the model undergoes training, providing a clear visualization of the convergence process for this specific structural parameter within the overall study of model performance.

caption: Cold work depths plotted against baseline KANM values for four different MSP samples, showing a variation range of approximately ±20%.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between cold work depth and baseline KANM values across four distinct MSP samples. The data reveals that cold work depths fluctuate within a ±20% range depending on the baseline, with lower baseline values typically corresponding to higher calculated cold work depths for the analyzed materials.

caption: Grain-boundary misorientation map of the oxide layer in LPBF-Haynes 230, accompanied by a histogram of fraction statistics.
summary: The oxide layer in LPBF-Haynes 230 exhibits a high density of high-angle grain boundaries. These include microcrack boundaries resulting from the additive manufacturing process and grain boundaries generated by deformation during oxide layer formation, which collectively contribute to an unstable surface structure as visualized in the misorientation map and statistics.

caption: Schematic representation of the cross-sectional dimensions of the examined specimens.
summary: This schematic illustrates the cross-sectional dimensions of the specimens analyzed in the study. These dimensions were determined through 3D laser scanning techniques as described in the reference literature. The resulting measurements provide the geometric basis for the data reported in the corresponding experimental tables within the study.

caption: Polar diagram representing the normalized directional permeability of the 25% volume fraction G network scaffold as a function of the rotation angle.
summary: The polar diagram displays the normalized permeability of the G network scaffold across various rotation angles. It identifies specific orientations corresponding to maximum and minimum permeability values, marked by black and white dots respectively, providing a clear visualization of the scaffold's anisotropic fluid transport properties.

caption: F-actin staining in 25% scaffolds demonstrating a significant increase in F-actin volume in +LIV samples versus -LIV controls.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of 25% scaffolds illustrate the F-actin distribution. The +LIV samples exhibit a more pronounced F-actin volume compared to the -LIV controls. This visual evidence corresponds with quantitative findings showing a 2.4-fold increase in F-actin volume, suggesting that 25% scaffolds are highly responsive to mechanical stimulation.

caption: Overlay of the LEAP 4000 X Si (red) and Invizo 6000 (blue) field evaporation maps, demonstrating the expanded field of view (FoV) provided by the Invizo 6000 system.
summary: Comparing the two instruments, this overlay illustrates the field evaporation maps of an Al 6026 tip from the LEAP 4000 X Si in red and the Invizo 6000 in blue. The visualization clearly highlights the significantly greater field of view achieved by the Invizo 6000 compared to the LEAP 4000 X Si.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus actual viscosity values.
summary: Viscosity values are compared between predicted and actual results in this parity plot. The data shows similar overall trends, which confirms that the model can effectively capture the underlying variations in the viscosity data, supporting the conclusion that the model is generally adequate for this response variable.

caption: Radar plot illustrating the normalized yield strength, total elongation, and reduction in area for the ASP-Z specimen across unirradiated, 0.75 dpa, and 2.1 dpa irradiation conditions.
summary: The ASP-Z specimen exhibits a distinct balance between hardening and ductility as a function of irradiation. The radar plot visualizes normalized values for yield strength, total elongation, and reduction in area, demonstrating how these mechanical properties evolve from the unirradiated state through increasing dpa levels of 0.75 and 2.1.

caption: Initial condensation of a clear liquid on the chamber viewport observed during the early stages of the first melt run at low temperatures.
summary: During the initial heating phase of the native fragments, a dull orange glow emerged within the crucible. Simultaneously, a clear liquid began to condense on the chamber viewport, as captured in this photographic image taken at low temperatures during the first melt run of the material.

caption: Representative immunohistochemical images of neo-tendon tissue sections at 4 and 12 weeks post-surgery, highlighting the spatial distribution and expression levels of Collagen I and Collagen III.
summary: Immunohistochemical analysis was performed to evaluate the expression of Collagen I and Collagen III in regenerated Achilles tendons at 4 and 12 weeks post-surgery. These representative images provide a visual assessment of the collagen composition within the neo-tendons, utilizing a 100 μm scale bar for structural reference.

caption: Linear regression performance for scenario 6 of the artificial backpropagation network.
summary: This panel displays the linear regression results for scenario 6 of the artificial backpropagation network. It is a key component of the eight graphs presented, illustrating the specific regression outcomes and the effectiveness of the backpropagation network in modeling the data associated with this particular scenario.

caption: Isothermal dilatometric measurement curves at 500 °C for 30 % and 43 % cold rolled samples, highlighting incubation times and peak aging.
summary: Isothermal dilatometry at 500 °C reveals the precipitation kinetics for 30 % and 43 % cold rolled samples. The curves demonstrate incubation times of 7200 s and 5400 s, respectively. Additionally, the 30 % cold rolled sample reaches its dilatation peak age after 2 hours, indicating the effectiveness of precipitation.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectra comparing the chemical signatures of AV, TSAV-0, and TSAV-10 hydrogel samples.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy was performed on AV, TSAV-0, and TSAV-10 hydrogels to elucidate the chemical interactions responsible for structural modifications. The spectra provide a comparative analysis of the functional groups present in the biocomposite hydrogels, highlighting the chemical changes associated with the incorporation of Aloe vera into the TSAV matrix.

caption: Fourier transform infrared curves showing chemical bonding modes in the powders.
summary: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy curves indicate that the spheroidized powder shares a strong similarity with the original powder. This suggests that the types of chemical groups and atomic bonding modes within the composites remain unchanged despite the spheroidization process, confirming chemical stability during the powder modification.

caption: Mo K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7.
summary: Mo K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra for Ni Alloy 59 are measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7. This technique provides surface-sensitive X-ray absorption data, allowing for the investigation of the alloy's electronic structure and oxidation states under specific environmental conditions, complementing the transmission mode reference data provided in the study.

caption: Proportional breakdown of waste categories including recyclable, non-recyclable, and biological waste.
summary: This pie chart displays the composition of waste across three categories. Biological waste was the most significant contributor at 452.14 kg (5.25 kg per case), followed by 145.37 kg of recyclable waste (1.69 kg per case) and 69.14 kg of non-recyclable waste (0.80 kg per case), with biological waste being the highest quantity.

caption: Three-dimensional surface topography of the laser shock peened (LSP) specimen.
summary: The 3D surface topography of the laser shock peened (LSP) specimen is shown, demonstrating the surface features resulting from the LSP treatment. This visualization is part of the comparative analysis of the five specimen groups, allowing for an assessment of how laser shock peening influences surface roughness.

caption: Friction coefficient evolution for Ni-PVD coating plotted against the number of laps for two distinct wear track radii.
summary: The friction coefficient for the Ni-PVD coating is plotted against the number of laps, illustrating the tribological performance under two different wear track radii. This measurement is part of a broader evaluation of friction force and wear volume for various coatings, providing insight into the material's wear behavior during testing.

caption: Selected-area electron diffraction pattern of the Al–2.5%Fe–2%Cu alloy annealed at 300 °C for 100 h, confirming the presence of the Al6Fe phase.
summary: The SAED pattern for the sample annealed at 300 °C for 100 h displays diffraction rings consistent with the as-manufactured state. This analysis confirms the presence of the Al6Fe phase, which possesses an orthorhombic structure (oC28), identifying the specific intermetallic phase formed during the thermal treatment process.

caption: Optical micrograph of the microstructure after short-time solid-solution treatment at 500 °C.
summary: This optical micrograph reveals the microstructure of the sample subjected to a short-time solid-solution treatment at 500 °C. The image is used to compare the formation of LPSO phases against samples treated at 480 °C and 520 °C, highlighting the temperature-dependent evolution of the material's internal structure.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-built specimen processed at 115 W laser power, showing crystallographic orientation in the XY plane relative to the build direction.
summary: Representing the as-built state for the 115 W laser power condition, this inverse pole figure map illustrates the grain orientation distribution. The analysis is performed in the loading direction (XY plane) with the Z axis aligned to the build direction, providing insight into the microstructure resulting from this specific laser power.

caption: WAXS pattern of Ti-BN composite displaying the diffraction intensity profile.
summary: This panel displays the WAXS results for the Ti-BN sample. By comparing this diffraction pattern with that of the cp-Ti sample, the influence of BN additions on the crystalline structure of the titanium matrix can be evaluated through the observed scattering intensity distribution.

caption: Bright field TEM image of sample A1 showing the distribution of lamellar nano-precipitates and irregularly shaped particulate precipitates within the microstructure.
summary: The bright field TEM image of sample A1 reveals the presence of a high density of lamellar nano-precipitates alongside irregularly shaped particulate precipitates. This visualization provides a clear overview of the microstructural features and the spatial arrangement of these distinct precipitate morphologies within the material matrix.

caption: High-field repassivation model validation for high VED and high VED_HT samples plotted in log(i) - Q-1 space.
summary: High VED and high VED_HT samples are plotted in log(i) versus reciprocal charge (Q-1) coordinates to validate the high-field repassivation model. By applying the equation involving potential drop and activation energy parameters, the characteristic cBV parameter is estimated, providing insight into the oxidation behavior and ion migration through the oxide film.
