caption: Bode plot of NAB alloy after 1 h of immersion, showing impedance magnitude and phase angle versus frequency, with solid curves representing equivalent circuit model fitting results.
summary: The Bode plot for the NAB alloy after 1 h of immersion displays a significantly widened peak in the phase angle diagram. Despite the Nyquist curve showing only one capacitive loop, the impedance spectrum is fitted using an equivalent circuit model, with the solid curve representing the simulated results.

caption: Cycling performance comparison illustrating areal capacity retention over 100 cycles for D-3DP and N-3DP electrodes.
summary: Cycling performance tests reveal that the D-3DP electrode maintains an excellent areal capacity retention rate of 82.2% after 100 cycles. In contrast, the N-3DP electrode exhibits severe degradation over the same period, underscoring the structural stability provided by the directional micro-channel design during long-term electrochemical cycling.

caption: Multi-material printing process sequence using prefabricated support structures, showing the CPC bone part (left), the interlocking zone (middle), and the final scaffold outcome (right).
summary: This panel displays the fabrication of trizonal implants using prefabricated support structures placed on the printing bed. The sequence shows the printing of the CPC bone part, followed by the interlocking zone of CPC and AlgMC, and finally the AlgMC cartilage part, with scaffold centers configured via GeSiM software.

caption: Optical micrographs illustrating the progression of Ag ink filling within the substrate as a function of filling time, demonstrating that increased jetting frequency effectively reduces the total processing time.
summary: Optical micrographs show the progression of Ag ink filling in relation to filling time. The images demonstrate that employing a higher jetting frequency allows for a significant reduction in the overall processing time required for the ink filling procedure, as evidenced by the visual evolution of the filling process.

caption: Reflection magnitude distributions for arbitrary combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 79 GHz and 82 GHz, exhibiting values between 0.69 and 0.96.
summary: This panel presents the reflection magnitudes for combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at the higher frequency band of 79 GHz and 82 GHz. The meta-atom demonstrates robust reflection efficiency, with magnitude values ranging from 0.69 to 0.96, confirming the design's effectiveness at these higher W-band frequencies.

caption: Reflection magnitude distribution for arbitrary combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 60 GHz and 63 GHz, showing values ranging from 0.68 to 0.97.
summary: This panel displays the reflection magnitudes for various combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 60 GHz and 63 GHz. The data indicates high reflection efficiency within the lower frequency band, with magnitudes consistently measured between 0.68 and 0.97, confirming the effective performance of the proposed meta-atom design.

caption: Schematic overview of crack initiation in LPBF 625 V, identifying Laves phase, grain boundaries, and slip bands as fracture sites.
summary: The schematic for the LPBF 625 V condition shows complex crack propagation paths. Cracks propagate intergranularly along high-angle grain boundaries and transgranularly through cellular/columnar substructures or {111} slip planes. This multi-modal fracture behavior involves Laves phase particles, grain boundaries, and slip bands as critical sites for crack initiation and propagation.

caption: Line graphs showing the variation of strains in the load direction (εyy) measured at different distances from the center of the bolt hole.
summary: Strain distributions in the load direction (εyy) are plotted along horizontal lines at varying distances from the hole center for specimen TS-C2. These graphs quantify the strain gradients induced by the 300 kN compressive load, offering a detailed profile of the material's deformation behavior relative to the bolt hole geometry.

caption: FT-IR spectra of raw ceramics and fabricated scaffolds, with arrows highlighting phosphate group bands.
summary: FT-IR spectra of the scaffolds exhibit characteristic absorption bands associated with PSU aromatic rings, including C-H stretching, C-C stretching, and various deformation modes. Arrows indicate specific bands relevant to phosphate groups, confirming the chemical composition of the fabricated scaffolds compared to the raw ceramic materials used in the study.

caption: Isolated 3D reconstruction of the fiber reinforcement phase within the composite, illustrating the distribution of fibers across individual printed layers.
summary: Focusing on the fiber reinforcement, this 3D reconstruction isolates the light green fibers from the matrix and pores. The visualization allows for the clear recognition of fiber distribution on individual layers of the printed composite, facilitating a qualitative assessment of the filler arrangement achieved during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the activation energy of bubble growth derived from experimental data by Cherinkov et al. [33], comparing three distinct physical scenarios.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the activation energy associated with bubble growth, calculated based on experimental data from Cherinkov et al. [33]. By applying an Arrhenius treatment across three distinct scenarios, the analysis reveals that the activation barrier increases and converges to a range of 0.21-0.24 eV as the damage rate decreases.

caption: Parity plot demonstrating the ANN model's performance in predicting the melting point of Fe–Ni based superalloys, with associated R2 and RMSE values.
summary: This panel features a parity plot comparing the ANN-predicted melting points of Fe–Ni based superalloys to their actual values. The performance of the model is evaluated using R2 and RMSE metrics, which quantify the alignment between predicted and experimental data, highlighting the model's utility in predicting thermal properties.

caption: High-speed imaging of the molten pool profile during synchronous laser remelting wire-arc DED, captured through quartz glass to observe dynamic behavior.
summary: High-speed imaging captures the dynamic molten pool profile during the synchronous laser remelting wire-arc DED process. Observed through quartz glass, this setup allows for the monitoring of molten pool stability under specific processing parameters, ensuring that the imaging conditions remain consistent throughout the experimental observation of the dynamic behavior.

caption: Cylindrical ingot of the CoCrFeMnNi HEA measuring approximately 100 mm by 75 mm following surface removal via lathe machining.
summary: This photograph displays the cylindrical CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy ingot after undergoing a lathe machining process to remove the surface layer. The specimen measures approximately 100 mm in diameter and 75 mm in height, representing the bulk material state prior to further microstructural and compositional characterization.

caption: Isofield magnetization (M–T) curves for sample 5# measured during heating and cooling cycles at 0.02, 1.0, and 5.0 T, with the magnetic field applied parallel to the build direction.
summary: This figure displays isofield magnetization (M–T) curves for sample 5# across a temperature range of 150 to 400 K. Magnetization differences (ΔM) between paramagnetic martensite and ferromagnetic austenite at 1.0 and 5.0 T are 75 and 81 A·m²·kg⁻¹, respectively, indicating strong magneto-structural coupling comparable to conventional Ni-Co-Mn-Sn alloys.

caption: Robustness comparison of baseline and optimized settings using violin and box plots to show predicted fatigue life under ±10% process noise.
summary: Process robustness is evaluated by comparing baseline and optimized settings under stochastic perturbations. The violin and box plots reveal that the optimized process achieves approximately twice the median fatigue life compared to the baseline, while simultaneously reducing the scatter in predicted outcomes under 10% process noise conditions.

caption: Load-displacement curves for multiple IN718 powder conditions showing parallel loading behavior up to 10 mN followed by divergent paths until maximum load.
summary: This panel displays typical nanoindentation load-displacement curves for various IN718 powder conditions. The curves exhibit a consistent starting point, characterized by parallel loading behavior up to 10 mN, after which the curves diverge until reaching their respective maximum loads, reflecting differences in the mechanical response of the tested powder samples.

caption: Top-down view of a 3D-printed gel grid deposited onto a glass substrate.
summary: A photograph showing a 3D-printed gel grid on a glass substrate. The grid is fabricated using a thixotropic ink composed of A200-filled PPG425 and PPG2000 dispersion. This printing method demonstrates the capability to produce regular shapes and smooth surfaces with high fidelity for polyurethane nanocomposite structures.

caption: Accelerated property mapping (XPM) hardness distribution for wrought IN718.
summary: This panel displays the hardness distribution for wrought IN718 obtained via accelerated property mapping. The hardness values are clearly distributed in accordance with the underlying grain structure of the material, which exhibits a slight relief profile resulting from the sample polishing procedure performed prior to the indentation testing.

caption: Surgical application and therapeutic mechanism of the CSC-DBM scaffold in a rat cranial defect model.
summary: This panel outlines the application of the 3D-printed CSC-DBM scaffold for repairing critical-sized cranial defects in a rat model. The mechanism highlights how the scaffold's structural and biological properties promote bone tissue repair, demonstrating the practical implementation of the bioceramic material in addressing challenging orthopedic and craniofacial bone regeneration needs.

caption: Selected XRD patterns for the 2K2Si18P electrolyte coating, illustrating the crystalline phase distribution across the coating thickness.
summary: Analysis of the 2K2Si18P coating via localized XRD patterns confirms that gamma-Al2O3 is the main crystalline phase present. The results align with integral XRD findings, showing high reflection intensities similar to the 18K2Si2P coating, which contrasts with the mullite-dominated structure observed in the 2K18Si2P specimen.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining targeting PPARγ expression in newly formed tissues following treatment with various scaffolds.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining highlights the expression of PPARγ, a marker for adipogenesis, within the newly formed tissues. The PCL + Cell group displays stronger PPARγ expression compared to the acellular PCL and 0.25%CoSi groups, indicating enhanced adipogenic differentiation when cells are incorporated into the scaffold architecture.

caption: Transverse section metallographic structure of K418 alloy processed at 160 W laser power.
summary: Corroded metallographic structure of the K418 sample is shown for a laser power of 160 W. This optical micrograph reveals the specific grain and phase morphology resulting from the lowest laser power setting, providing a reference point for evaluating the impact of increasing energy input on the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves showing the thermal stability of 3D-printed structures, bentonite, and SrCl2 samples.
summary: Thermal stability of the 3D-printed structures, bentonite, and SrCl2 was assessed through TGA curves shown in panel (b). These measurements track mass loss as a function of temperature, providing critical data on the decomposition behavior and thermal degradation limits of the printed composite materials and their raw components.

caption: Radar chart comparing water contact angle, air permeability, whiteness, tensile index, and folding endurance to demonstrate the multifunctional performance of SL-4/C/P coated paper.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive comparison of the water contact angle, air permeability, whiteness, tensile index, and folding endurance of the coated paper. The visualization confirms that the SL-4/C/P coated paper possesses exceptional optical, water barrier, and mechanical properties simultaneously, indicating a balanced and high-performance material design.

caption: Post-UV irradiation infrared spectra of methacrylate-siloxane products, highlighting the disappearance of the vinyl peak at 1635 cm-1 as an indicator of high photocuring completion.
summary: Following UV-induced photo crosslinking, the infrared spectra demonstrate the extent of the curing process. The negligible intensity of the vinyl peak at 1635 cm-1 confirms a remarkably high completion of the photocuring process for formulations containing dimethyl units, indicating effective conversion of the methacrylate groups into the siloxane network.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for the HT2 heat-treated linear scan condition, maintaining a peak intensity of approximately 1.6 MRD at the (100) plane.
summary: The HT2 heat-treated linear scan sample maintains a grain boundary plane distribution similar to the HT1 condition. The peak intensity remains at approximately 1.6 multiples of random distribution (MRD) at the (100) plane, suggesting that the grain boundary character distribution is relatively stable between these two heat treatment stages.

caption: EDS elemental map for Zr distribution, showing depletion of Zr in the lamellar regions.
summary: The EDS elemental map for Zirconium (Zr) demonstrates the chemical composition across the observed microstructure. Similar to the Nb distribution, the map reveals that the lamellae are depleted of Zr, confirming the specific chemical signature of these features relative to the surrounding matrix phases.

caption: Ternary projection of the ethanol-glycerol-water/alginate design space, displaying the distribution of aspect-ratio values across the composition triangle.
summary: This ternary projection maps the ethanol-glycerol-water/alginate design space to visualize aspect-ratio values. As noted in the reference, the 3D space of elongation is visualized using different colors, with darker colors indicating greater elongation. This projection effectively translates the 3D data into a 2D compositional space for easier interpretation.

caption: Cross-sectional STEM micrograph of the layer at point A, showing the lowest observed porosity.
summary: This STEM micrograph captures the layer cross-section at location A, which exhibits the least porosity among the five points analyzed. Similar to other regions, the image shows variations in darkness attributed to compositional Ni differences, requiring independent thresholding across 4x4 squares to effectively segment the material from the pores.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of N5 superalloy at the bottom height, showing crystallographic orientation relative to the [001] direction.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map illustrates the micro-scale crystallographic orientation of the N5 superalloy specimen at the bottom height. The map is oriented relative to the [001] direction, providing essential data on the single-crystal structure integrity and grain orientation distribution within the L-DED fabricated thin-wall specimen.

caption: Ranking of compositional feature importance based on average SHAP contributions, highlighting Al and V as the most influential elements for alloy hardness.
summary: This panel ranks the importance of each compositional feature based on average SHAP contributions. Higher values indicate a stronger influence on the model output. SHAP analysis reveals that Al and V are the most influential elements for alloy hardness, with Al showing significantly higher importance than V.

caption: N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms measured at -196 °C for CX, CX@Cu, CX@Fe, and CX@Co monoliths, showing a type Ia isotherm for the CX sample.
summary: The N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms at -196 °C for the monoliths are presented, with the CX monolith exhibiting a type Ia isotherm according to IUPAC classification. This indicates that the material is predominantly composed of narrow micropores, providing essential information regarding the textural properties of the synthesized monoliths.

caption: Simulated intergranular porosity generated via CA simulation, displaying a cluster of sub-micron pores occasionally adjacent to larger irregular voids.
summary: The simulated intergranular porosity is represented by a CA simulation model. This visualization reveals a characteristic morphology consisting of clusters of tiny pores smaller than one micron, which are sometimes positioned next to larger, irregular pore structures, providing a computational baseline for comparison with experimental observations of the material's microstructure.

caption: Geometric representation of a three-dimensional honeycomb structure, illustrating the characteristic length (l) and thickness (t) parameters defining a regular hexagonal cellular geometry.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometric configuration of a regular three-dimensional honeycomb structure. By defining the characteristic length l and thickness t, the diagram provides a foundational model for cellular materials. Such regular hexagonal honeycombs are recognized as isotropic structures, exhibiting equivalent extensional Young’s modulus properties as described by Gibson et al.

caption: Refined Pareto chart for relative density (RD) showing standardized effects after removing statistically insignificant second-order terms from the model.
summary: Following the identification of insignificant second-order terms, this refined Pareto chart presents an updated model for relative density. By focusing on linear and interaction terms, the chart provides a more effective representation of the most significant parameters influencing the RD response in the optimized LPBF process for the alloy.

caption: Geometric representation of the TiAl calibration sphere used for the four-detector ELO system, detailing its physical dimensions.
summary: This schematic illustrates the TiAl calibration sphere designed for the four-detector ELO system. The diagram highlights the specific geometric dimensions required for accurate calibration. According to the study, this sphere is essential for performing ELO image calibration, ensuring the system is properly configured for subsequent material analysis.

caption: Magnified view of the cut-out region marked with a red frame in panel (b), providing a detailed look at the phantom structure.
summary: This magnified view corresponds to the cut-out region marked in panel (b). By focusing on this specific area, the image provides a detailed look at the calibration phantom's structure at a 60-degree rotation angle, facilitating a more precise examination of the features within the red frame.

caption: Comparison of primary dendrite arm spacing (PDAS) on the downskin of supported (S) overhang bars for 30 µm and 60 µm layer thicknesses, demonstrating relatively similar spacing values.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the primary dendrite arm spacing (PDAS) measured on the downskin of supported overhang bars. Comparing 30 µm and 60 µm layer thicknesses, the data shows that the supported bars maintain relatively similar PDAS sizes on the downskin, contrasting with the trends observed in support-free configurations.

caption: Micro-CT reconstructed model of the R-Octet-15 metamaterial.
summary: This panel shows the micro-CT reconstruction model for the R-Octet-15 specimen. The 3D model offers a precise representation of the lattice architecture, enabling a thorough examination of the structural features and potential manufacturing defects inherent in the R-Octet-15 design after the LPBF fabrication process.

caption: Confusion matrices of the final network after training on the test dataset for flow rate classification.
summary: This panel presents the confusion matrices of the final network after training on the test dataset. It illustrates the classification accuracy of the model for each specific flow rate category, demonstrating the network's performance and ability to correctly identify different printing parameters within the 3D-printing experimental framework.

caption: Exponential traction-separation law illustrating the relationship between surface traction and crack surface displacement.
summary: This plot displays an exponential traction-separation law used to model crack surface displacement. The area under this curve represents the fracture energy of the slip system. Increasing the parameter h s reduces the area under the curve, thereby decreasing the fracture energy required for crack formation in this reversible cohesive model.

caption: Deviation of XCT-measured diameter from CMS-measured diameter for the turned outer region.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the deviation between XCT-measured and CMS-measured diameters for the turned outer region. The deviation is minimal, measured at 0.8 μm, which indicates that the impact of beam hardening on the external geometry of the turned specimen is trivial and negligible for measurement accuracy.

caption: Workflow diagram illustrating the structural organization of Module 3, focusing on the integration of analytical methods and software-optimized processing steps.
summary: This flowchart depicts the structured workflow of Module 3, which is designed to facilitate analyzing and software-optimal processing. The diagram outlines the systematic integration of analytical techniques and computational optimization steps, providing a clear visual representation of the procedural framework developed for the research methodology described in the study.

caption: Spider graph representing the A2N@95% property values across the tested recycling course levels.
summary: A2N@95% property values are summarized in this spider graph to evaluate the impact of ASA recycling course levels. The visualization allows for a comparative analysis of this specific metric, reflecting the material's behavior as it undergoes repeated recycling cycles, with notable variations observed between the third and sixth levels.

caption: Microhardness values of the Al-2Ti-2Fe-2Co-2Ni alloy measured after 2-hour isothermal annealing treatments at temperatures ranging from room temperature up to 600 °C.
summary: This panel displays the microhardness of the Al-2Ti-2Fe-2Co-2Ni alloy following 2-hour isothermal annealing treatments up to 600 °C. The data demonstrates the microstructural stability of the alloy, with minor hardness reductions observed at 300 °C, indicating that the microstructure remains largely unaltered compared to the as-printed state.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns (intensity vs. 2θ) comparing DED and HF-DED processed materials, derived from integrated 2D Debye-Scherrer rings.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns for DED and HF-DED processed materials are presented, showing integrated 2D Debye-Scherrer rings. The diffraction data confirms the presence of MC-type carbides and Laves phase, consistent with simulated solidification sequences. These results indicate that the HF-DED process maintains similar constituent phases to conventional DED processing.

caption: High-magnification LSCM image of SLM pure tungsten deposit B17, showing a higher density of pores compared to B13.
summary: High-magnification imaging of sample B17 reveals a higher concentration of pores compared to sample B13. This observation aligns with relative density measurements. The structural defects, including cracks and pores, are clearly visible, providing insight into the influence of processing energy density on the final microstructure of pure tungsten.

caption: STEM-BF micrograph of the AlMg9.3 alloy viewed along the [110] zone axis following a tensile strain of 0.7%.
summary: Presented is a STEM-BF image of the AlMg9.3 alloy, captured in the [110] zone axis after the material reached an engineering strain of 0.7% during tensile testing. The image illustrates the microstructural characteristics of this specific alloy composition under the defined strain, facilitating a direct comparison with the AlMg6.6 variant.

caption: Macro morphology of a three-layer thin-walled component fabricated using the CMT arc mode.
summary: This panel displays the macro morphology of a three-layer thin-walled component produced via the CMT arc mode. The image provides a visual representation of the surface characteristics resulting from this specific welding process, serving as a baseline for comparing the surface quality against other arc modes used in the study.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the as-built specimen highlighting the distribution of γ' phase precipitates.
summary: Captured using the <100> superlattice reflection, this dark-field TEM image provides further visualization of the γ' phase precipitates within the as-built specimen. The micrograph complements the structural analysis of the as-built material, confirming the presence and distribution of the γ' phase particles within the grains of the alloy.

caption: Derivative of weight (DTG) curves corresponding to the thermal degradation of raw polymers, HA/Cs physical mixture, and HA/Cs scaffolds under various conditions.
summary: The DTG curves provide the derivative of weight loss versus temperature for raw polymers, the HA/Cs physical mixture, and the HA/Cs scaffolds. These plots highlight specific thermal degradation events and peak temperatures, facilitating a detailed comparison of the thermal behavior of the materials before and after PBS incubation.

caption: Combined indentation force and interfacial potential energy versus indentation depth curves for a Ni/Ni3Al substrate, highlighting points A, B, and C as successive nucleation events of EDD pairs.
summary: This plot displays the indentation force and interfacial potential energy as functions of indentation depth for a Ni/Ni3Al substrate. The curve reveals four distinct stages of deformation. Points A, B, and C correspond to specific indentation depths where EDD pairs are nucleated, causing local minima in the indentation force.

caption: Additional Bode plot representation showing the frequency response characteristics of the EB-PBF Ti–6Al–4V scaffolds under physiological conditions.
summary: This Bode plot further details the frequency response of the EB-PBF Ti–6Al–4V scaffolds in PBS at 37 °C. By analyzing these plots alongside the Nyquist data, the electrochemical performance and surface stability of the scaffolds are evaluated, ensuring a thorough understanding of their behavior in a simulated physiological environment.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the MA + SPS alloy after annealing at 800 °C for 100 hours, revealing a stable and highly dispersed distribution of oxide particles.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the microstructure of the MA + SPS alloy following a 100-hour annealing treatment at 800 °C. The micrograph confirms that the oxide dispersion remains high within the matrix. TEM examination was specifically conducted to investigate potential σ-phase precipitation, which was not detected by prior XRD analysis.

caption: Cs-TEM bright-field micrograph of the HIP + STA specimen showing the microstructure.
summary: This Cs-TEM bright-field micrograph displays the microstructure of the HIP + STA specimen. The image provides a clear view of the grain boundaries and internal grain regions, serving as the base for subsequent elemental mapping to identify the distribution of various precipitates and phases within the material.

caption: Long-term electrochemical impedance data displayed as Nyquist plots for the three specimen conditions after 20 days of immersion in NaCl solution.
summary: After 20 days of immersion, the Nyquist plots capture the long-term electrochemical impedance behavior of the as-built and post-annealed NAB alloys. These plots serve to characterize the final state of the surface passivation and corrosion resistance for each specimen condition after an extended period of exposure to the NaCl solution.

caption: Time-resolved UV-vis absorption spectra for the reduction of V4+ using PdNi/NrGO (1:1) catalyst, illustrating the progressive decrease of the 770 nm absorption peak and the simultaneous increase of the 401 nm peak over time.
summary: Time-dependent UV-vis spectra demonstrate the reduction of V4+ using the PdNi/NrGO (1:1) catalyst. The absorption peak at approximately 770 nm gradually decreases with reaction time, while the peak at approximately 401 nm increases, confirming the progressive reduction of vanadium species as the reaction proceeds over the observed intervals.

caption: Comparative analysis of apparent fracture toughness (ζ), relative change in fracture toughness (Ω), and relative change in stiffness (Ψ) for pure stiff resin (RM) and various lithomer configurations (Lr, Li, Ld, Lb).
summary: This figure presents the fracture experiment results, comparing apparent fracture toughness and stiffness changes across different lithomer configurations against the pure stiff resin baseline. Statistical analysis confirms that all measured values for the lithomers differ significantly from the RM baseline, demonstrating distinct mechanical performance variations across the investigated material architectures.

caption: Structural phase transition of Cu-20at%Ni alloy during tensile deformation, highlighting the conversion of the FCC structure into BCC, HCP, and other novel phases.
summary: Cu-20at%Ni alloy experiences a structural phase transition during tensile deformation. The stretching process facilitates the conversion of the FCC structure into BCC, HCP, and other novel phase structures. This result demonstrates that even at 20at% Ni, the alloy's crystal structure remains responsive to tensile stress, resulting in phase transformation.

caption: XRD spectra obtained from three different cross-sectional planes of the sample, confirming the exclusive detection of α-iron peaks.
summary: XRD spectra obtained from three different cross-sectional planes of the sample, confirming the exclusive detection of α-iron peaks. The diffraction patterns collected from these cross-sectional planes exhibit nearly identical profiles to those at different heights, indicating a uniform phase distribution and confirming the homogeneity of the microstructure throughout the wall.

caption: Comparison of strain distribution along a center line at 12.2% engineering strain, contrasting experimental image correlation data against numerical models featuring heterogeneous (blue) and homogeneous (red) porosity distributions.
summary: This plot illustrates the strain distribution along a center line at 12.2% engineering strain. It compares experimental image correlation results with two numerical models: one incorporating heterogeneous porosity and another assuming homogeneous porosity. The data highlights how different porosity assumptions influence the predicted strain profile compared to experimental observations.

caption: Compressive stress-strain behavior of DW1 to DW5 scaffold structures.
summary: Mechanical performance of DW1 through DW5 scaffold structures is characterized by these uniaxial compression stress-strain curves. These plots represent the structural response of the scaffolds under compressive loads, serving as a key diagnostic tool for assessing the mechanical integrity and deformation characteristics of the DW series samples.

caption: XRD spectrum of the PLA-CF material illustrating shock-induced phase transformations through the analysis of diffraction peak positions and intensities.
summary: The XRD spectrum of the PLA-CF material is presented to characterize shock-induced phase transformations. By examining the diffraction pattern, researchers identify the precise locations and strengths of diffraction peaks, which provide essential information regarding the crystal structure of the material under shock loading conditions.

caption: Training loss progression for the PINN model during temperature prediction across training epochs.
summary: This panel displays the loss curves of the PINN model specifically for temperature prediction over the course of training epochs. It serves as a primary visualization of the model's convergence behavior during the training process, illustrating how the loss metric evolves as the model learns to predict temperature values.

caption: Creep strain versus time response for gamma-alloy single-crystals evaluated at 1150 °C and 10 MPa.
summary: This plot presents the creep curve for gamma-alloy single-crystals at 1150 °C and 10 MPa. The data highlights the strong temperature dependence of the creep rate, evidenced by the distinct time scales required for deformation compared to tests performed at higher temperatures like 1225 °C and 1288 °C under the same stress.

caption: Comparison of cyclic voltammograms for various biochar-loaded electrodes in 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+ and 0.1 M KCl at a fixed scan rate of 50 mV s−1.
summary: Comparing cyclic voltammograms at 50 mV s−1 across different biochar percentages reveals no significant variation in electrochemical performance. The results demonstrate that the SWP10–20 electrode maintains comparable activity to the SWP10–0 sample, confirming that surface accessibility remains stable regardless of the biochar loading levels in the electrode composition.

caption: Near-infrared (NIR) absorbance spectra comparing early-age and hardened cementitious material surfaces, with the sensor's spectral range highlighted against the broader electromagnetic spectrum.
summary: This NIR spectroscopic analysis illustrates absorbance variations across wavelengths for cementitious materials at different hydration stages. Prominent absorption peaks for H2O groups are identified at 1450 and 1940 nm, with a weaker feature at 1200 nm. Additionally, the figure contextualizes the spectral range of the LWIR detector within the broader electromagnetic spectrum.

caption: Complex frequency plane representation of reflection coefficients for the uniform porosity TPMS structure.
summary: This panel maps the reflection coefficients of the uniform porosity TPMS structure in the complex frequency plane. These data points characterize the reflection behavior of the uniform design, serving as a reference to evaluate the impact of porosity grading on the overall reflection characteristics of the TPMS structure.

caption: Isolated 3D reconstruction of newly formed bone tissue extracted from the scaffold complex at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation using specific thresholding values.
summary: New bone formation is quantified by extracting the mineralized tissue from the scaffold complex at 4 and 8 weeks using threshold-based segmentation. This reconstruction highlights the progression of osteointegration, confirming that the GI group scaffolds effectively support bone regeneration through synergistic mechanical and biochemical cues over the study period.

caption: Cu-distribution map of the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample obtained via EDS mapping.
summary: This Cu-distribution map highlights the spatial localization of copper within the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample. The map reveals how copper atoms are distributed across the microstructure, providing evidence of potential solute clustering or precipitate formation that significantly influences the strengthening mechanisms of the T6-treated alloy.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectrum of PLA and transmission spectrum of glass fiber (GF) plotted against wavelength.
summary: This panel displays the typical visible and UV absorption spectrum of PLA alongside the transmission spectrum of GF. These spectroscopic measurements are provided to illustrate the relationship between the PLA matrix, the GF reinforcement, and their respective interactions with UV-C light exposure during the experimental study.

caption: Schematic representation of the specimen clamping configuration utilized during the Digital Image Correlation (DIC) tensile testing procedure.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup for the DIC tensile test, specifically highlighting the clamping mechanism. The diagram indicates that the HGS layer (layer C) is positioned in close proximity to the extensometer, providing a clear visual reference for the specimen orientation and instrumentation placement during the mechanical evaluation.

caption: DSC curve for the NiTi sample fabricated at a wire feed speed ratio of 1:1.75, where transformation peaks M p1 and M p2 are shifted to 46.8 °C and 425.4 °C, respectively.
summary: Representing the thermal response of a NiTi sample with a 1:1.75 wire feed speed ratio, this DSC plot highlights the shift in transformation peaks. The data indicates that the transformation peak temperatures M p1 and M p2 occur at 46.8 °C and 425.4 °C, respectively, reflecting the influence of wire feeding rates.

caption: Lattice temperature evolution of the CuTi sample during 200 ps of laser ablation simulation, showing a surface temperature peak of approximately 3000 K within the initial 25 ps.
summary: The lattice temperature of the CuTi sample is tracked over a 200 ps laser ablation simulation. Results indicate an instantaneous surface temperature rise reaching a peak of 3000 K during the first 25 ps, which significantly exceeds the theoretical melting point of 1456 K calculated via the EAM potential.

caption: Geometrical model illustrating the extended parameters for filament deposition, including layer width, horizontal overlap interval, inter-layer bond width, and intra-layer bond height.
summary: This schematic represents an extension of the geometrical models proposed by Ahn et al. The model incorporates specific printing parameters such as layer width, horizontal overlap interval, inter-layer bond width, and intra-layer bond height. These geometric variables are essential for calculating interface properties and understanding the resulting porosity in printed filaments.

caption: Bright field TEM image showing the cellular grain structure of a nickel alloy print fabricated using high Y–Ti GARS powder in an argon atmosphere.
summary: This bright field TEM image displays the cellular grain structure of a nickel alloy print. The specimen was produced using high Y–Ti GARS powder processed in an argon atmosphere. The micrograph provides a lower magnification view of the distinct grain morphology characteristic of this specific printing condition.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the undeformed XY plane showing an equiaxed microstructure within the MPB zone and refined grains along the MPB boundaries.
summary: The EBSD micrograph of the undeformed XY plane displays an equiaxed microstructure within the MPB zone, complemented by refined grain structures along the MPB boundaries. This initial state serves as the baseline for evaluating the microstructural evolution and grain orientation distribution observed in subsequent deformation experiments.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the P1-A specimen, revealing the local plastic strain distribution at the crack edge.
summary: The KAM map of the P1-A specimen shows no elevated local misorientation at the crack edge compared to the surrounding bulk material. This lack of increased misorientation indicates that the plastic zone is essentially undiscernible in this aged specimen, confirming the limited extent of plasticity during stage II crack growth.

caption: Isopleth contour plot representing the composition-dependent frequency factor D0Nb in fcc Ni–Mo–Nb alloys across varying Mo and Nb compositions.
summary: The contour plot visualizes the frequency factor D0Nb within the fcc Ni–Mo–Nb alloy system. By mapping the isopleths of D0Nb against Mo and Nb concentrations, the figure provides a three-dimensional representation of how the pre-frequency factor varies across the compositional space of the ternary alloy system.

caption: Immunofluorescence imaging of retrieved unvascularized grafts showing cell morphology and expression of insulin (INS) and NKX6.1 markers.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging of retrieved unvascularized grafts displays the morphology of surviving cells within the microdevice. The detection of insulin (INS) and NKX6.1 markers confirms the presence and viability of the encapsulated islets, indicating that the microdevice successfully supports islet survival in the absence of pre-vascularization.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the Chess-DA sample showing the distribution of γ′ (turquoise) and γ′′ (brown) precipitates.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the microstructure of the Chess-DA sample. The γ′ precipitates are colored in turquoise, while the γ′′ precipitates are shown in brown. Unlike the Meander-DA condition, this sample does not contain the coarse, elongated γ′′ precipitates observed in other processing variants.

caption: Schematic representation of the Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) apparatus, detailing the configuration of the bars and the integrated data acquisition system used for high strain rate mechanical testing.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) apparatus, a specialized experimental setup designed for high strain rate testing. The diagram highlights the arrangement of the pressure bars and the associated data acquisition system, providing a clear overview of the instrumentation required to perform dynamic mechanical characterization of materials.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for the MWCNTs/Al–Mg–Sc–Zr mixed powder, indicating a size range from approximately 12.6 to 89.3 μm.
summary: The particle size distribution of the MWCNTs/Al–Mg–Sc–Zr mixed powder is presented as a histogram. The data indicates that the matrix material consists of particles ranging from approximately 12.6 μm to 89.3 μm in size, characterizing the physical dimensions of the powder used in the experimental study.

caption: Comparative cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM [Fe(CN)6]4- in 0.1 M KCl, showing the response of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode at the 1st and 100th cycles.
summary: Stability assessment of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode is demonstrated by comparing the 1st and 100th cyclic voltammograms using [Fe(CN)6]4-. This comparison highlights the electrochemical durability and consistency of the electrode material over repeated cycling, confirming its potential for long-term use in electrochemical sensing and related applications.

caption: Chemical composition table for Co-based laser-clad coatings on Invar 36 alloy, identifying specific specimen compositions labeled as YN1, YN2, and YN3.
summary: This table details the chemical composition of Co-based coatings applied to Invar 36 alloy via laser cladding. The specimens are categorized into three distinct compositions, designated as YN1, YN2, and YN3, providing the foundational material parameters for the subsequent wear and oxidation resistance evaluations presented in the study.

caption: Statistical distribution of alignment deviations for 96 microcavities, comparing the master tool against the iterated plug-in tool after individual xy-correction.
summary: This box plot presents a statistical analysis of alignment deviations across 96 microcavities. It compares the performance of the master tool with the iterated plug-in tool, which incorporates individual xy-correction. The data demonstrates the effectiveness of the iterative design in minimizing positional errors during the automated deposition process.

caption: TOF-SIMS depth profile of an as-grown Cu-Ni alloy film with 500 nm Cu and 50 nm Ni, demonstrating the elemental counts through the alloy layer.
summary: This TOF-SIMS depth profile of a 500 nm Cu/50 nm Ni alloy film tracks the Cu-, Ni-, and C- concentrations. Carbon atoms are detected within the alloy film, and the Ni- concentration continues to decrease as the copper thickness increases, illustrating the compositional changes inherent in the as-grown alloy samples.

caption: Quantification error (QE) values plotted against varying parameters including alpha, sigma, N, tau, and map size, with red indicating minimum QE for a 4x4 map and dark blue indicating minimum QE for a 14x14 map.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the quantification error (QE) across various parameter settings, specifically alpha, sigma, N, tau, and map size. The visualization highlights distinct performance regions, where red markers denote the lowest QE for a 4x4 map size, while dark blue markers identify the lowest QE for a 14x14 map size.

caption: Atomic model of the 48-atom Cu/Ni3Al interface supercell, highlighting specific substitution sites for alloying elements at the first nearest neighbor Al (Ni1) and second nearest neighbor Ni (Ni2) positions.
summary: This 48-atom supercell model represents the Cu/Ni3Al interface with 3D translational symmetry. The structure identifies specific substitution sites for alloying elements, categorized into the first nearest neighbor Al (Ni1) and the second nearest neighbor Ni (Ni2) positions, which are essential for evaluating the energetic impact of atomic substitutions at the interface.

caption: Fluorescence staining of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells using calcein-AM and propidium iodide on mono-phasic, bi-phasic, and multi-phasic scaffolds after 2 and 7 days of culture.
summary: Fluorescence staining with calcein-AM and propidium iodide was performed on bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells cultured on mono-phasic, bi-phasic, and multi-phasic scaffolds. Observed at 2 and 7 days post-culture, these images confirm the scaffolds' significant role as effective anchorage sites for cell attachment and viability throughout the experimental period.

caption: Transmission spectra of the immersion solution at pH 4, comparing results obtained at room temperature (left) and 37 °C (right), showing near 100% transmission.
summary: At a pH of 4, the transmission spectra for the immersion solution show no significant changes over time at either room temperature or 37 °C. The near 100% transmission values indicate that there is no significant leakage or release of Au NPs from the nanocomposite hydrogel into the medium.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns taken from the red rectangular interface area in panel (e), showing diffraction along the [001]gamma and [001]gamma-double-prime zone axes.
summary: This SAED pattern was obtained from the interface region marked in panel (e). The diffraction data, captured along the [001]gamma and [001]gamma-double-prime zone axes, provides structural evidence of the crystallographic relationship between the matrix and the disc-like precipitates in the heat-treated IN718 + 4 wt% CrFeNb alloy.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of 1a in the presence of EDB (8 × 10^-2 M) under 405 nm LED irradiation, exhibiting minor intensity increments after successive 2-minute exposures.
summary: Photolysis of 1a in the presence of EDB additive reveals only minor intensity increments in the absorption spectrum after 1800 seconds of 405 nm LED irradiation. This indicates that the addition of EDB alone does not trigger significant photochemical interactions or substantial product formation under the tested experimental conditions.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the dependence of steady-state creep strain rates on applied temperature for the DZ125 nickel-based superalloy within the 1030–1050 °C range.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between steady-state creep strain rates and temperature for the DZ125 nickel-based superalloy. Data within the 1030–1050 °C range indicates a high apparent creep activation energy, demonstrating the material's robust creep resistance under these specific thermal conditions, consistent with experimental creep measurements.

caption: Experimental setup showing the oven used for controlled heat treatment of materials.
summary: This photograph displays the oven utilized for the heat treatment process. The equipment is designed to provide a controlled thermal environment, ensuring consistent heating conditions for the samples during the experimental procedure. It serves as the primary apparatus for the thermal processing phase of the study.

caption: Optical micrograph of the SR490 post-treated pure Ti specimen, displaying the characteristic acicular martensite phase formed during the SLM process.
summary: Following the SR490 post-treatment, the pure Ti specimen retains the acicular martensite phase originally formed during the SLM manufacturing process. Optical microscopy confirms that the microstructure remains consistent with the as-built state, indicating that this specific stress-relief temperature does not significantly alter the martensitic morphology.

caption: Detailed EDX line scan spectra focusing on the distribution of Ti and Mo elements across the Al2O3/filler/Fe–Ni–Co braze joint, with specific emphasis on the composition of the enlarged layer A.
summary: The EDX line scan spectra highlight the distribution of Ti and Mo elements within the Al2O3/filler/Fe–Ni–Co braze joint of specimen 3. This analysis specifically targets the composition of layer A, which was previously identified in the SEM micrograph, providing insight into the elemental migration occurring during the brazing process.

caption: Percentage distribution of various cost items associated with RMfg operations, calculated with RR and other parameters set to 50%.
summary: This panel illustrates the percentage weights of all cost items involved in RMfg operations. The data is presented under the specific condition where RR and other parameters are fixed at 50%, providing a clear breakdown of the financial distribution across the different components of the manufacturing process.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the Co-40Ni-14.5Al-4Nb-xCr alloy system calculated using a thermodynamic database, with red points indicating the specific compositions of the 4Nb8Cr and 4Nb12Cr alloys.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram for the Co-40Ni-14.5Al-4Nb-xCr alloy system was generated using a thermodynamic database. The diagram illustrates phase stability across varying Cr concentrations, with specific alloy compositions for 4Nb8Cr and 4Nb12Cr marked as red points to guide experimental preparation and further analysis of phase transition behaviors.

caption: Spatial distribution of 103 microstructural images within the two-dimensional space defined by the first two principal components, PC1 and PC2.
summary: Visualizing the spatial distribution of 103 microstructural images in the first two principal component spaces reveals how different creep conditions cluster or separate. This scatter plot demonstrates the effectiveness of PCA in reducing the dimensionality of complex microstructural data while preserving the distinct characteristics associated with various creep experimental conditions.

caption: Central dark-field TEM micrograph of as-printed IN718, highlighting Laves phase particles along cell boundaries using the g = (1-101)Laves reflection.
summary: This central dark-field TEM micrograph visualizes the Laves phase particles within the as-printed IN718 alloy. Imaged using the specific reflection indicated in the panel (a) SAED pattern, the micrograph reveals irregularly shaped particles distributed along the cell boundaries, which exhibit a morphology similar to Nb-rich particles observed in other microstructural analyses.

caption: Electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectrum of the carbide precipitate, featuring a background-subtracted profile (dotted line) that indicates a carbon concentration of 27.4 ± 3.4 at.%.
summary: The EELS spectrum of the M7C3 carbide precipitate is shown, with intensity multiplied by a factor of five above 50 eV for enhanced clarity. The background-subtracted spectrum, indicated by the dotted line, reveals a carbon concentration of 27.4 ± 3.4 at.%, facilitating precise chemical quantification of the metal-carbide phase.

caption: Comparative strain-life fatigue plot for all material conditions, including F357 and AlSi10Mg fabricated via L-PBF and LP-DED, with run-out tests indicated.
summary: This plot compares fatigue lives across all conditions. At higher strain amplitudes, the order is LP-DED AlSi10Mg > L-PBF AlSi10Mg > LP-DED F357 > L-PBF F357. At lower amplitudes, the order shifts to L-PBF AlSi10Mg > L-PBF F357 > LP-DED AlSi10Mg > LP-DED F357. AlSi10Mg consistently outperforms F357.

caption: Multi-material 3D printing fabrication process for the high porous structure S3, highlighting the filling of internal voids.
summary: The fabrication process for structure S3 is detailed, emphasizing a multi-material 3D printing approach. This method is necessary to fill internal voids within the layers, ensuring the structural integrity and printability of subsequent layers. The inset provides a visual representation of the structure during and after the printing process.

caption: Cross-sectional SEM view of an as-received fiber showing the initial structural state prior to laser processing.
summary: This SEM image captures the cross-section of an as-received fiber, serving as a baseline for structural comparison. It demonstrates the initial state of the material before undergoing laser cutting. The micrograph highlights the original grain structure, which is essential for evaluating the subsequent effects of thermal processing on the fibers.

caption: DRT analysis for SOECs tested at 800 °C, illustrating the deconvoluted peaks corresponding to electrochemical sub-processes.
summary: At 800 °C, the DRT analysis of SOECs demonstrates four distinct peaks, P1 to P4, representing electrochemical sub-processes during CO2 electroreduction. These results were obtained by fitting the EIS spectra to an equivalent circuit model consisting of a single series resistance and four R-CPE elements to characterize the cell performance.

caption: Final reaction power profile obtained after performing manual baseline subtraction on the raw data.
summary: This final plot displays the reaction power after a manual baseline subtraction has been applied. This correction ensures that the reaction power curve begins and ends at zero, providing a clean representation of the thermal reaction power for the sample heated at 6600 K/s.

caption: Three-dimensional metallographic reconstruction of the K418 alloy sample.
summary: This panel presents a 3D metallographic reconstruction of the K418 alloy. The visualization provides a volumetric perspective of the material's internal structure, serving as a baseline for comparing the cross-sectional metallographic features observed in the subsequent panels under varying laser power conditions during the manufacturing process.

caption: Ashby map illustrating the normalized effective Young’s modulus ⟨E⟩/E as a function of relative density ρ¯ for various metamaterials, incorporating experimental data from multiple literature sources.
summary: This Ashby plot displays the relationship between normalized effective Young’s modulus and relative density for diverse metamaterials. By aggregating experimental data from various studies, the figure provides a comparative overview of mechanical performance across different density regimes, serving as a foundational reference for evaluating the stiffness-to-weight efficiency of these structures.

caption: UV–vis absorbance spectra of the SL solution measured before and after the photocatalytic co-activation process with PS.
summary: This UV-vis absorbance spectrum compares the SL solution state before and after the photocatalytic co-activation of PS. The spectral changes provide evidence of the conversion process, reflecting the transformation of SL into vanillic acid and other products within the reaction system.

caption: One-dimensional concentration profile of W across the γ/γ′ interface derived from APT reconstruction.
summary: This panel presents the W concentration profile across the γ/γ′ interface obtained via APT. The data provides a quantitative view of W distribution, contributing to the broader assessment of how alloying elements partition between the γ matrix and γ′ phase in the presence of varying boron concentrations.

caption: Comparison of cyclic voltammograms for 3D-printed and ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrodes at a scan rate of 0.1 mVs-1.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry was performed on 3D-printed and conventional ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 anodes at a scan rate of 0.1 mVs-1 between 1 and 2.5 V. This comparison highlights the electrochemical performance differences between the 3D-printed architecture and the standard ink-cast electrode configuration for the specified material system.

caption: Voltage-current dependence curves comparing a Mg/Zn:Al multilayer sample and a Zn:Al film of approximately 100 nm thickness.
summary: This graph illustrates the voltage-current dependence for two distinct samples: a Mg/Zn:Al multilayer and a Zn:Al film with a thickness of approximately 100 nm. The data highlights the electrical response characteristics of these thin-film structures, providing a comparative analysis of their respective voltage-current behaviors under applied current conditions.

caption: Convergence history curve showing the optimization process for Problem 2 over 100 iterations.
summary: The optimization convergence history curve for Problem 2 demonstrates that the solution successfully reaches a stable state within 100 iterations. This plot tracks the progress of the optimization algorithm, confirming that the design parameters are effectively refined to achieve the desired performance goals within the specified 12–18 GHz frequency range.

caption: Dark field TEM imaging identifying the morphology of α′′ martensite laths.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging identifies the α′′-phase martensite laths within the microstructure. These laths are characterized by a high aspect ratio, as noted in the reference. This visualization confirms the presence of martensitic transformation products within the as-printed SLM Ti6Al4V alloy, contributing to its complex oriented microstructure.

caption: Total wear volume as a function of cycle number for Stellite 6, C-GC, and C-LMD alloys tested at 25 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of total wear volume for Stellite 6, C-GC, and C-LMD alloys during tribological testing at 25 °C. Stellite 6 and C-GC exhibit a characteristic bilinear wear behavior, transitioning from an initial period of severe wear to a mild wear regime following the formation of a stable third-body layer.

caption: Full-pattern neutron diffractogram for the first HIP-treated condition, illustrating the phase evolution relative to the as-printed state.
summary: This diffractogram represents the neutron powder diffraction pattern for the first HIP-treated condition. It serves as part of the comparative series used to monitor phase evolution and secondary phase stability in the WAAM material following high-pressure thermal processing, providing volume-averaged structural information across the specimen volume.

caption: Pearson correlation heatmap illustrating the relationships between various input features, with a color scale representing the strength and direction of correlations.
summary: This Pearson correlation heatmap serves as a feature selection tool to identify redundant or highly correlated variables. The visualization highlights a cluster of features within the central white dotted box that exhibit strong correlations, facilitating the decision-making process for selecting optimal features for the underlying machine learning model.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the YZ plane for SLM Ti-55511 alloy, highlighting the grain orientation characteristics in this cross-section.
summary: Representing the YZ plane of the SLM Ti-55511 specimen, this inverse pole figure map characterizes the grain orientations. Consistent with the overall EBSD analysis, the map allows for the identification of both columnar and equiaxed grain morphologies, demonstrating the microstructural texture developed during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Crystal lattice representation of Ni3B, featuring nickel atoms depicted in blue and boron atoms in green.
summary: The Ni3B crystal structure is visualized here, showing the atomic positions of nickel and boron within the unit cell. This structural model serves to characterize one of the specific reaction products resulting from the interaction between cBN and the Ni-superalloy, detailing the stoichiometry and atomic arrangement of the phase.

caption: Tabulated values representing the estimated viscosity and static yield stress derived from the rheological measurements of mortar samples at different hydration times.
summary: Presented in this table are the estimated viscosity and static yield stress values for the mortar samples. These parameters were calculated based on the rheological stress-strain data obtained at various hydration time intervals, providing a quantitative summary of the material's flow properties and resistance to initial deformation.

caption: Creep performance comparison for Inconel 718 samples fabricated via single and multi-laser PBF-LB, highlighting the influence of build orientation and laser count on thermodynamic effects.
summary: This panel presents creep curves for Inconel 718 samples produced using single and four-laser PBF-LB strategies. The data demonstrates how varying the number of lasers and build orientations influences the resulting microstructure and thermodynamic properties, providing a means to control high-temperature mechanical performance in additively manufactured metallic components.

caption: PND Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 at 310 K.
summary: This panel displays the PND Rietveld refinement for the Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 sample at 310 K. Experimental data are represented by black dots, while the red line indicates calculated intensities and the blue line shows the difference plot. Tick marks denote the TiNiSi, Ni2In, and MgZn2 phases.

caption: Comparison of predicted and experimental fatigue strength values, where data points positioned above the dashed line signify unsafe predictions exceeding experimental results, and points below the line represent conservative estimates.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between predicted and experimental fatigue strength. The dashed line serves as a threshold for safety: points falling above this line indicate unsafe predictions where the model overestimates strength, while points below the line represent conservative predictions that align with safer engineering practices for fatigue characterization.

caption: Fracture toughness values for BJ-printed ZTA ceramics subjected to a 2 h sintering holding time.
summary: Fracture toughness results for BJ-printed ZTA ceramics are plotted for a 2 h sintering holding time. The data indicates a dependence on sintering parameters similar to that observed in flexural strength measurements, suggesting that optimized thermal conditions are critical for improving the fracture resistance of the material.

caption: Box and whisker plots detailing quartz trace-element concentrations across different deposit types related to A-type magmas.
summary: This panel displays the trace-element composition of quartz in deposits related to A-type magmas using box and whisker plots. The visualization captures the range of element concentrations, including quartiles and median values, to characterize the geochemical signatures of quartz found in these specific A-type magma-related geological settings.

caption: Summary table detailing the microstructure characteristics of the T1 alloy resulting from different heat treatment regimes.
summary: This panel provides a structured summary of the microstructural characteristics observed in the T1 alloy following various heat treatment regimes. It serves to correlate the specific processing conditions with the resulting physical features of the material, facilitating a deeper understanding of the underlying microstructural evolution during heat treatment.

caption: STEM-ABF micrograph and schematic of the diamond (111)/Cu-matrix interface with 0.25 mass% Zr, showing residual graphite and amorphous carbon.
summary: STEM-ABF imaging of the diamond (111)/Cu-matrix interface with 0.25 mass% Zr reveals that the limited concentration of carbide-forming metal is insufficient to fully consume the carbon at the interface. Consequently, residual graphite and amorphous carbon persist, as the limited solubility of carbon in molten copper prevents complete interfacial reaction.

caption: Percentage contribution of various input parameters utilized within the TOPSIS decision-making framework.
summary: This plot quantifies the relative influence of different input parameters on the TOPSIS model outcomes. By displaying the percentage contribution of each variable, the visualization provides critical insight into which factors most significantly drive the decision-making process, facilitating a clearer understanding of the model's sensitivity to its specific input parameters.

caption: Cross-sectional morphology and elemental distribution map of region A after 100 hours of hot corrosion exposure.
summary: Region A displays the cross-sectional morphology and elemental surface distribution following 100 hours of hot corrosion. This analysis provides detailed insights into the material's degradation behavior and chemical composition at this specific site, highlighting the localized effects of the corrosive environment on the sample's structural integrity and elemental arrangement.

caption: Two-dimensional projection of the 3D fatigue life data featuring beach contour lines to delineate performance regions.
summary: This panel provides a 2D contour representation of the fatigue life data, utilizing beach contour lines to map the influence of h and t. This visualization simplifies the complex 3D relationship, allowing for a clearer interpretation of how specific parameter combinations affect the fatigue life of the R90C90 material.

caption: Experimental transmission response of beams A and B, with the shaded region indicating the flexural bandgap.
summary: Experimental transmission response of beams A and B is shown, with the shaded region highlighting the flexural bandgap. This plot demonstrates the actual transmission performance of the beams, allowing for a direct comparison with the numerical results to validate the presence and extent of the flexural bandgap in the experimental setup.

caption: Localized stress distribution at the mandibular angle resulting from the combination of occlusal loading and elevator muscle forces, highlighting specific compressive and tensile stress regions.
summary: Combined occlusal and elevator muscle forces generate localized stress at the mandibular angle. Specifically, this loading condition induces tensile stress at the superior border and compressive stress at the inferior border, demonstrating how muscle-driven forces contribute to the complex mechanical environment of the maxillofacial skeleton during functional activity.

caption: High-resolution XPS fine scan of the Cr 2p region, characterizing the chromium oxidation states on the blackened surface.
summary: The Cr 2p fine scan characterizes the chromium oxidation states on the blackened surface. XPS analysis indicates that Cr2O3 is the most abundant metal oxide within this layer, highlighting the significant role of chromium oxidation in the formation of the dark, irregular surface features observed on the sample.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis pattern derived from the cellular structure, identifying the Ni5Y phase.
summary: FFT analysis of the cellular structure in the nickel alloy produced with high Y–Ti GARS powder in an argon atmosphere is presented. This diffraction-based technique confirms that the cellular structure is composed of the Ni5Y phase, providing definitive evidence of the phase identity within the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Load-displacement curves comparing AB and T6 NiTi samples before and after machining at a constant cutting speed of 93 m/min.
summary: This panel displays nanoindentation load-displacement curves for NiTi samples with different initial microstructures, specifically AB and T6 conditions. The data illustrates the mechanical response of these materials before and after undergoing a machining process at a cutting speed of 93 m/min, providing insight into the resulting surface mechanical properties.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the FSA2 alloy acquired using the (020)-type B2 + L21 shared reflection to visualize the combined ordered phase distribution.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph visualizes the FSA2 alloy microstructure by employing the (020)-type B2 + L21 shared reflection. This imaging technique allows for the simultaneous observation of both B2 and L21 ordered phases, providing insight into their collective distribution and morphology within the matrix after the 900 °C aging treatment.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve for the Random Forest (RF) model evaluated on the unseen test set.
summary: The Random Forest model performance is visualized through an ROC curve on the unseen test set. This plot includes five distinct curves representing four individual classes and a micro-average, illustrating the classification capability of the RF algorithm in distinguishing between the different categories within the dataset.

caption: Calculated electronic band structure of Mn-soluted ZnO, demonstrating the influence of manganese solutes on the electronic band configuration.
summary: This panel illustrates the calculated band structure for Mn-soluted ZnO. By comparing this result to the pure ZnO baseline, one can observe the shifts and changes in the electronic band configuration caused by the presence of manganese, providing insight into the electronic behavior of Mn-doped ZnO systems.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the compressive strength of Ti6Al4V GS lattice structures against various literature-reported metals, composite truss lattices, and foam structures.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the compressive strength performance of Ti6Al4V GS lattice structures relative to diverse materials found in literature, including composite truss lattices, aluminum and titanium alloys, and various foams. The data indicates that the GS structures exhibit superior compressive strength compared to these other reported metallic and composite materials.

caption: Calculated coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) derived from the differentiation of the thermal strain data for SRM 738, showing both raw and distortion-corrected curves relative to NIST standard data.
summary: The coefficient of thermal expansion for SRM 738 is determined by differentiating the thermal strain data. This panel presents the resulting CTE curves for both raw and corrected datasets. These values are compared to NIST standard data to demonstrate the impact of the distortion correction on the final material properties.

caption: Chronocoulometric Q-t curves and Q-t^1/2 linear plots for an Fe@C/GCE in 0.1 M PBS, illustrating the electrochemical behavior without analytes (a, a') and with the addition of 0.3 μM AC (b, b') or 1 μM RT (c, c').
summary: Fe@C/GCE performance is evaluated via chronocoulometry in 0.1 M PBS. The Q-t and Q-t^1/2 plots demonstrate the electrochemical charge accumulation behavior of the Fe@C modified electrode. Results are compared across blank electrolyte, AC-spiked, and RT-spiked solutions to assess the impact of these analytes on the electrode's charge response.

caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 650 °C, demonstrating the solute distribution at elevated temperatures.
summary: Displayed is the normalized mass spectrum for Inconel 718 samples tested at 650 °C. While other solutes are present in comparable amounts, atom probe tomography could not resolve significant carbon traces. Therefore, mass spectrum analysis was utilized to characterize the carbon content in the samples tested at this temperature.

caption: Double-logarithmic representation of potentiostatic polarization data for Inconel 625 alloy, measured at a constant potential of 0.5 V within phosphoric acid solutions of varying concentrations.
summary: This double-logarithmic plot illustrates the potentiostatic polarization behavior of Inconel 625 when exposed to phosphoric acid environments of different concentrations. By maintaining a constant potential of 0.5 V, the graph provides a clear visualization of the electrochemical response, facilitating the analysis of corrosion kinetics across the tested acidic conditions.

caption: Simulated morphology of columnar dendrites at a solid fraction of 10% during the early solidification stage.
summary: At the early stage of solidification, columnar dendrites quickly grow into the undercooled melt along the favorable orientation. This phase-field simulation shows the morphology of the dendrites at a solid fraction of 10% at the corner position of the 11th layer of the curvature component during the solidification process.

caption: Representative electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data showing the evolution of passive layers on the titanium alloy surface over a 7-day immersion period in PBS.
summary: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data tracks the formation and stability of passive layers on the titanium alloy surface. By monitoring the impedance response over a 7-day period in a simulated physiological environment, the study assesses the long-term electrochemical stability and passivity of the material under continuous immersion conditions.

caption: Bode phase angle plots for the Al0.5MnFeNiCu0.5 layer, Al–Ni layer, and substrate, demonstrating the capacitive response across a wide frequency range.
summary: Bode phase angle plots characterize the capacitive response of the Al0.5MnFeNiCu0.5 layer, Al–Ni layer, and substrate. The Al0.5MnFeNiCu0.5 layer displays high phase angles over a broad frequency range, suggesting a robust capacitive response and indicating that the corrosion reaction of its passive film is significantly more difficult to initiate.

caption: Side and top views of the (1 1 1) surface of the bimetallic NiZn catalyst, illustrating the atomic arrangement within the supercell.
summary: The (1 1 1) surface of the bimetallic NiZn catalyst is depicted in side and top views. This atomic model was generated from the optimized bulk NiZn material and fully relaxed to determine its relative stability. The visualization includes the specific supercell size and calculated surface energy for this orientation.

caption: HEXRD patterns for high Fe Inconel 625 in as-deposited and HIP conditions, showing the presence of nitride peaks following post-processing.
summary: High Fe Inconel 625 alloy diffraction patterns obtained via HEXRD demonstrate the structural evolution from the as-deposited to the HIP condition. Comparison of these patterns confirms that multiple nitride peaks are present in the HIP post-processed high Fe alloy, reflecting significant microstructural changes induced by the thermal treatment process.

caption: Raman spectroscopic analysis of HSCs, highlighting the D-band at 1340 cm⁻¹ and G-band at 1580 cm⁻¹.
summary: Raman spectroscopy of HSCs reveals two characteristic bands at 1340 cm⁻¹ and 1580 cm⁻¹, identified as the D-band and G-band, respectively. These peaks indicate the molecular structure and chemical bonding of carbon atoms, confirming the carbonaceous nature of the material and providing information on its structural disorder.

caption: View of the specimens oriented vertically on the LPBF build plate to eliminate the need for support structures.
summary: Specimens are shown arranged vertically on the LPBF build plate. This specific orientation is utilized during the additive manufacturing process to avoid the requirement for support structures beneath the parts, thereby simplifying post-processing and maintaining the integrity of the cone-feature geometries during the build.

caption: Raman spectra comparing 10Ni/ZrO2 and Ni-Zn/ZrO2 catalysts to confirm the presence of distinct zirconia phases.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was utilized to analyze the structural characteristics of the catalysts. The spectra for 10Ni/ZrO2 and Ni-Zn/ZrO2 are presented to support XRD findings by confirming the different zirconia phases present in the catalyst samples, providing insight into the structural composition of the modified and unmodified materials.

caption: Kissinger equation plots derived from the peak temperatures (Tp) of the two Gaussian curves identified in the desorption rate measurements, used to determine activation energies.
summary: Kissinger plots are generated using the peak temperatures (Tp) obtained from the two Gaussian curves across different heating rates. These plots allow for the calculation of activation energies for hydrogen desorption. The peak temperatures for the two curves consistently fall within the 240–291 °C and 358–407 °C ranges, respectively.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curve illustrating the weight loss percentage of an as-printed alumina sample as a function of increasing temperature.
summary: This TGA curve displays the weight loss percentage of an as-printed alumina sample during heating. The data shows a continuous decrease in mass as temperature rises, which signifies the thermal degradation and removal of photopolymer constituents. Most of the observed mass loss corresponds to the complete removal of these organic components.

caption: Real-part of AC susceptibility (χ′) cooling curve for the x = 0.3 composition, with an inset highlighting frequency dependence at lower temperatures.
summary: The real-part of the AC susceptibility (χ′) is frequency independent between T2 and T1, which excludes a spin-glass state. However, the inset shows that the peak in χ′(T) at the martensitic phase transition is frequency dependent, indicating complex magnetic behavior associated with the phase transformation process.

caption: Processed interference fringe image captured when the phase difference across the phase-locked modulator (PLM) is zero.
summary: This processed interference fringe image represents the optical state where the phase difference on both sides of the PLM is zero. The image, derived from the interference fringe analysis, provides a baseline visualization of the optical field under these specific phase-matched conditions as described in the experimental processing results.

caption: Storage modulus (E′) plotted against temperature for amorphous PEKK/MRS composites printed at 0° orientation.
summary: This panel displays the storage modulus (E′) as a function of temperature for amorphous PEKK/MRS composite samples printed at a 0° orientation. The data, obtained via DMA, illustrates the thermomechanical response of the amorphous material, providing insight into the stiffness characteristics of the composites under varying thermal conditions.

caption: Training and test loss evolution over training epochs for the CRONet model applied to a cantilever beam simulation.
summary: This learning curve illustrates the convergence behavior of the CRONet model during the training process for a cantilever beam.
