These carbides, specifically (Ti,Mo)C, contain approximately 70 at% Ti and 22 at% Mo, along with minor concentrations of Cr, Fe, Co, and Ni, contributing to the complex microstructural composition of the Udimet 500 alloy.

caption: Evolution of the lowest band gaps in a Py/Co 2D MC as a function of the squeeze ratio s, highlighting the presence of the 2nd and 4th band gaps.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of the lowest band gaps in a Py/Co 2D MC structure as the squeeze ratio s varies. The analysis identifies the presence of two distinct band gaps, specifically the 2nd and 4th ones, demonstrating the band gap behavior within this specific material composition.

caption: Top-view and 3D representations of in-situ synchrotron XRD patterns for the medium-strain rate tensile test.
summary: This panel displays top-view and 3D plots of in-situ synchrotron XRD patterns corresponding to the medium-strain rate tensile test. By visualizing the data in these formats, the structural response of the austenitic ⟨110⟩A and ⟨001⟩A orientations under uniaxial loading along the HD_x axis is clearly characterized and compared.

caption: 27Al NMR spectrum of the MAX-1 compound, showing signals attributed to the MAX phase and aluminum oxide impurities.
summary: The 27Al NMR spectrum for the MAX-1 compound, which contains a high content of the MAX phase, displays signals corresponding to the MAX phase and aluminum oxide forms. Simulation of this spectrum focuses on aluminum atoms located at the centers of trigonal prisms within the MAX phase structure.

caption: Notch strain at initiation measured in a BWR-HWC environment as a function of Zn concentration (0, 15, and 40 ppb).
summary: Notch strain at initiation in a BWR-HWC environment increases with Zn concentration. The value is approximately 1.1% at 0 ppb Zn, rising to 1.5% with 15 ppb Zn injection, and further increasing to 1.9% with 40 ppb Zn injection, demonstrating a mitigation effect of Zn on crack initiation.

caption: Polar plot illustrating the normalized in-plane elastic modulus ratios for quasi-isotropic modified honeycomb structures with a [±45°, 90°, 0°]s stacking sequence under compression.
summary: This polar plot demonstrates the mechanical response of modified honeycomb structures featuring a [±45°, 90°, 0°]s stacking sequence. The results confirm the effectiveness of this specific configuration in promoting quasi-isotropic behavior, as evidenced by the uniform distribution of normalized elastic modulus ratios under in-plane compressive loading conditions.

caption: Tensile stress-strain response of Cu50Ni50 alloy at 300 K under different strain rate conditions.
summary: At 300 K, the Cu50Ni50 alloy exhibits a linear increase in tensile stress relative to strain, culminating in a peak yield stress before undergoing a notable decline. This panel illustrates the mechanical deformation characteristics of the alloy at room temperature across multiple strain rate regimes.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing cast NAB and deposited Cu–Al alloys with varying Al concentrations, highlighting the passivation region.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the electrochemical behavior of cast NAB and deposited Cu–Al alloys. The passivation region, highlighted by yellow shading, reveals distinct differences between samples. Notably, the 10Al alloy exhibits a jagged curve and a rapid increase in passivation current, indicating unique corrosion resistance characteristics compared to other compositions.

caption: Thermomagnetic curve of the starting N42 Nd-Fe-B material, serving as the baseline reference for the reacted samples.
summary: This panel displays the thermomagnetic curve for the starting N42 Nd-Fe-B material. It acts as the control reference to evaluate the magnetic response changes in the coated and uncoated samples after an eight-month reaction period, allowing for a direct comparison of material degradation or phase stability.

caption: Line-scan profile showing element distribution in the S-Ni6.9–494 deposit over a 1.4 mm buildup height.
summary: The S-Ni6.9–494 deposit demonstrates uniform compositional distribution across the 1.4 mm buildup direction. The observed line-scanning data reflects the segregation of Ni and Cr between austenite and ferrite phases, preventing the profile from appearing as a perfectly straight line.

caption: Stochastic design scaffold seeded with hMSCs, visualized via Live/Dead staining to assess cell survival and proliferation over 7 days.
summary: Stochastic design scaffolds seeded with hMSCs are visualized via Live/Dead staining to assess cell survival and proliferation over 7 days. This analysis qualitatively confirms a high proportion of viable cells and minimal cell death, contributing to the finding that all scaffolds demonstrated statistically significant cell growth over the period.

caption: Localized force chain contour maps comparing unanchored and anchored sample behavior at loading moment t 60.
summary: During the intermediate loading phase at t 60, the force chain values are statistically evaluated within the central regions. The contour maps illustrate the spatial distribution of force chains, highlighting the differences in mechanical load distribution between the unanchored and anchored samples as the loading process progresses through this crucial moment.

caption: Extensional storage modulus E' and critical strain εc plotted as functions of static preload to characterize the linear viscoelastic (LVE) range limits.
summary: This figure illustrates the extensional storage modulus within the linear viscoelastic (LVE) range and the corresponding critical strain at the LVE limit. By analyzing the influence of static preload on these parameters, the plot provides a quantitative assessment of the material's mechanical stability and the boundaries of its linear elastic response.

caption: Light reflectance measurements recorded at a wavelength of 1068 nm for the various powder samples specified in Table 1, with a sample size of n = 6.
summary: This figure displays the light reflectance values measured at 1068 nm for the powders listed in Table 1. The data, based on a sample size of n = 6, provides a quantitative assessment of the optical reflectance properties for these specific materials, as referenced in the study's experimental results.

caption: Displacement vector map of a nano-polycrystalline Ni57Cr19Co19Al5 alloy model with 8 nm grain size and no twin structure at 0.2 strain.
summary: This MD snapshot illustrates the displacement vectors in a twin-free Ni57Cr19Co19Al5 alloy at 0.2 strain. Analysis of the grain highlighted in the black dotted box reveals that grain boundary sliding and grain rotation mechanisms occur simultaneously, indicating significant atomic rearrangement during the deformation process at this specific strain level.

caption: Simulated impedance spectra for varying microstructures at a beta-phase dissolution depth of 70 micrometers.
summary: Simulated impedance spectra are presented as Nyquist plots for different microstructural configurations at a fixed dissolution depth of 70 micrometers. These spectra, computed using a 1D FEM model, demonstrate how variations in microstructure scaling and conductivity influence the electrochemical impedance response of the system under investigation.

caption: NOM image of SP-DLW patterns fabricated with C5/TMPTA.
summary: Non-contact optical microscopy (NOM) images reveal the patterns created using the single-photon direct laser writing (SP-DLW) technique with C5/TMPTA. These images demonstrate the high-resolution capabilities of the photoinitiator system, showcasing its potential for precise micro-scale fabrication as part of the study on LED visible light photopolymerization and 3D printing.

caption: Three-dimensional surface reconstruction of a Ti-MK sample generated via confocal microscopy.
summary: This panel displays a three-dimensional surface reconstruction of a Ti-MK sample, captured using confocal microscopy. The image provides a detailed topographical view of the sample surface, serving as the primary visual data for subsequent linear profile analysis conducted through the Gwyddion software platform to characterize surface features.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HT LPBFed block sample processed at 18.52 J/mm3, measured near the martensitic transition temperature.
summary: This panel displays isothermal M-H curves for the 18.52 J/mm3 sample near the martensitic transition temperature. Data collected in 5 K increments reveal a small magnetic hysteresis between 135 and 195 K, characteristic of a first-order phase transformation resulting from structural changes during the cooling and heating cycles.

caption: Time to fracture for Alloy 400 variants including LPBF, bulk, and LPBF + Ti at 650 °C.
summary: This panel displays the time to fracture for three Alloy 400 variants—LPBF, bulk, and LPBF + Ti—subjected to creep experiments at 650 °C. The results highlight the enhanced creep properties achieved through TiN-precipitate-induced dislocation pinning, which effectively improves the material's resistance to deformation under sustained stress conditions.

caption: Nanoindentation force-displacement response measured for the MPEA6 alloy after aging at 560 °C.
summary: This panel displays the mechanical response of MPEA6 aged at 560 °C during nanoindentation testing. The force-displacement curve characterizes the material's resistance to indentation, reflecting the influence of the specific thermal treatment on the alloy's mechanical properties and its ability to accommodate deformation under localized stress conditions.

caption: Average coefficient of friction (COF) values for SLM-fabricated 316L stainless steel, calculated during the stable wear stage to assess the influence of different heat treatment conditions.
summary: Average COF values are presented to evaluate how specific heat treatment conditions affect the tribological performance of SLM-fabricated 316L stainless steel. These measurements were taken during the stable wear stage of the friction tests to provide a comparative assessment of the material's friction characteristics under different processing states.

caption: Schematic representation illustrating the process of hydrogen diffusion within a crystal lattice structure.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the fundamental mechanism of hydrogen diffusion as it interacts with the crystal lattice. By visualizing these atomic-scale movements, the figure provides a conceptual framework for understanding how lattice structures influence the transport and mobility of hydrogen atoms within a material, as described in the reference.

caption: Synchrotron transmission XRD map of a pillar sample extracted from a cuboid specimen, showing a periodic structural pattern with a 720 μm repeat distance.
summary: This synchrotron transmission XRD map reveals the formation of periodic mesostructures within the pillar sample. The pattern repeats every 720 μm along the build direction, corresponding to the 15° rotation angle between layers. These structures follow the meltpool track contours and span homogeneously throughout the sample volume.

caption: Statistical distribution of Sa roughness values comparing the horizontal upskin and vertical sides of the cuboid specimen.
summary: This box plot compares the Sa roughness statistics between the horizontal upskin and vertical sides of the cuboid. Higher roughness values observed at the rim of the horizontal upskin are attributed to perimeter bulging. The data confirms that roughness parameters vary systematically across different regions of the specimen surface.

caption: Comparative analysis of self-corrosion potential values for both LPBF-processed and Wrought-316L stainless steel specimens subjected to different ASPN temperature treatments.
summary: This plot compares the self-corrosion potential of LPBF-processed and Wrought-316L stainless steel across varying ASPN temperatures. By tracking these potential values, the figure facilitates an assessment of how different nitriding temperatures influence the electrochemical stability and corrosion initiation characteristics of the two distinct 316L stainless steel material forms.

caption: Magnetisation as a function of temperature for CoFeMn0.5Alx samples subjected to a high applied magnetic field of 2390 kA/m.
summary: High-field magnetisation versus temperature data for CoFeMn0.5Alx samples are presented here to complement the low-field measurements. These curves are utilized alongside the 40 kA/m data to accurately determine the Curie temperature, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the magnetic phase transitions across different field strengths.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curve for LPBF-produced Ti-6Al-4V cuboids, illustrating the specific compressive strain levels (S0, S5, S10, S20, S30, and S32) at which the mechanical testing was interrupted.
summary: This engineering stress-strain curve displays the mechanical response of LPBF-produced Ti-6Al-4V cuboids under compression. The plot highlights specific test termination points labeled S0 through S32, corresponding to strain increments from 5% at the yield point up to 32% just before failure, providing a clear overview of the deformation history.

caption: Raman spectrum of the HEA disc worn surface at room temperature, indicating the presence of V2O5 as the primary oxidation product.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the HEA disc worn surface at room temperature is presented. The spectrum confirms that V2O5 is the primary wear-induced oxidation product formed under these conditions. This result highlights the initial oxidation behavior of the HEA material during sliding wear at room temperature.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of negative ions CrO2-, CrO3H2-, NiO2H2-, and Ni2- for the H2 annealed (MH) sample, characterized by a pseudo intensity plateau of the Ni2- signal in the inner layer between 7 and 14 seconds.
summary: This ToF-SIMS depth profile for the H2 annealed sample tracks the intensity of negative ions, revealing a distinct pseudo intensity plateau for the Ni2- signal within the inner layer (7 s < t < 14 s). Similar to the M sample, the NiO2H2- intensity consistently exceeds that of the CrO3H2- signal.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the as-built AlFeCrSi alloy processed at an energy density of 112 J/mm3, revealing the internal microstructure.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of an as-built AlFeCrSi alloy fabricated via LPBF at an energy density of 112 J/mm3. The imaging technique provides a clear visualization of the internal structural features, including precipitates, within the aluminum matrix resulting from the rapid solidification process.

caption: Comparison of friction factors for cold-rolled stainless steel tubes against theoretical Darcy and Blasius models.
summary: This plot validates pressure drop results by comparing experimental friction factors of cold-rolled stainless steel tubes with established theoretical models. Specifically, the data is benchmarked against the Darcy friction factor and the Blasius equation, providing a verification of the measured hydraulic performance characteristics of the stainless steel specimens.

caption: Mechanical property trends for Type II interface specimens in R30 concrete, showing the influence of the notch-to-depth ratio on tensile strength and fracture toughness.
summary: Type II interface specimens in R30 concrete exhibit consistent tensile strength and fracture toughness values relative to the notch-to-depth ratio. While some individual data points may deviate due to specimen preparation uncertainties, the overall trend shows that these mechanical properties remain stable despite variations in the notch-to-depth ratio.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the 3Al5Ni sample after 5 dpa ion irradiation at room temperature, showing a disordered BCC matrix.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the 3Al5Ni sample following 5 dpa ion irradiation at room temperature. The imaging reveals the presence of a disordered BCC matrix, indicating that the B2-ordered NiAl precipitates have undergone complete dissolution as a result of the irradiation process.

caption: UV (red) and LC/MS (black) spectra of crude sophorolipid, accompanied by a data table detailing retention times, molecular masses, and chemical identifications.
summary: Crude sophorolipid analysis via UV and LC/MS spectra reveals a complex mixture of components. The accompanying table provides specific retention times and mass identifications for these constituents. LC/MS analysis highlights several distinct peaks that are not visible through UV spectroscopy alone, demonstrating the chemical diversity present in the crude sample.

caption: Discharge curves of annealed La1.8Mg1.2Ni9 alloy electrodes evaluated at different discharge current densities.
summary: This panel illustrates the discharge curves for the annealed La1.8Mg1.2Ni9 alloy electrode under various current densities. The alloy shows an initial discharge capacity of approximately 340 mAh/g at 0.33 C. Its discharge capacity variations become increasingly distinct from the other studied alloys as the discharge current density increases.

caption: Micro-CT reconstruction of a calvarial rabbit defect treated with a PLA-2CaP composite scaffold after 12 weeks, featuring the volume of interest in red.
summary: Micro-CT imaging of a calvarial rabbit defect treated with a PLA-2CaP composite scaffold at 12 weeks reveals the bone regeneration status within the highlighted volume of interest. These 3D images demonstrate the good biocompatibility of the scaffold implanted in vivo, providing a clear visualization of the bone-scaffold interface and tissue growth.

caption: Enlarged HAADF-STEM image of area X, revealing the microstructural details of the intermetallic compounds.
summary: This enlarged HAADF-STEM image focuses on area X, providing high-resolution visualization of the intermetallic compounds. The imaging technique highlights the atomic-scale structure of the material, allowing for a detailed examination of the morphology and distribution of the intermetallic phases within the sample matrix.

caption: Alternative perspective of the void fraction response surface demonstrating the interaction between printing speed and nozzle temperature.
summary: This alternative view of the void fraction response surface highlights the parabolic trend associated with the process parameters. The visualization confirms that both printing speed and nozzle temperature contribute equally to the resulting void fraction, providing a comprehensive understanding of how these variables interact during the printing process.

caption: STEM bright-field image and EDS maps of steel 2 showing a region devoid of elemental partitioning, where dislocations appear randomly arranged without specific structural organization.
summary: Displayed is a STEM bright-field image and EDS map of steel 2 in a region lacking elemental partitioning. Unlike the partitioned regions, the dislocations here exhibit no particular arrangement, and the EDS maps confirm the absence of Cr and Mo enrichment, indicating a homogeneous distribution of alloying elements.

caption: Irregularly shaped grain mapped within the global coordinate system to illustrate orientation variability.
summary: This panel displays an irregularly shaped grain within a simulation domain, highlighting the challenge of varying grain orientations. The grain is mapped into a global coordinate system, providing a visual representation of the geometric complexity that necessitates the use of Principal Component Analysis for accurate dimensional extraction.

caption: Nyquist plot of the CuCrZr alloy measured in a 5 wt% NaCl solution, displaying real (Z') and imaginary (Z") impedance components.
summary: The Nyquist plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance of the CuCrZr alloy when exposed to a 5 wt% NaCl solution. By plotting the real component (Z') against the imaginary component (Z") of the measured impedance, this graph provides critical insights into the corrosion resistance and interfacial kinetics of the alloy.

caption: Transverse cross-sectional optical micrograph of an IN625-medium clad sample at 10× magnification.
summary: This 10× magnification optical micrograph displays the transverse cross-section of an IN625-medium clad sample. The cladding is observed to be dense, crack-free, and visually uniform, exhibiting no signs of porosity within the coating or at the interface between the coating and the substrate, consistent with expected deposition results.

caption: Solid-state 1H NMR spectra of the paste sample monitored over a 22-week storage period, highlighting the persistence of sharp amine moiety peaks between 4.4 and 5.0 ppm.
summary: Solid-state 1H NMR analysis of the paste stored over 22 weeks reveals the chemical stability of the material. The spectra demonstrate that the sharp peaks corresponding to amine moieties, located in the 4.4 to 5.0 ppm range, remain largely unchanged throughout the entire storage duration, indicating minimal degradation of these functional groups.

caption: Ternary composition diagram mapping 50 superalloys manufactured via DED, categorized by Ni + Co, Ti + Al, and Mo contents, with filled black squares denoting compositions lacking γ' formation and red squares indicating those with γ' formation.
summary: This ternary composition diagram displays the chemical space of 50 superalloys produced by DED. The plot highlights the influence of Ni + Co, Ti + Al, and Mo concentrations on phase stability. Specifically, it distinguishes between alloy compositions that successfully form the γ' phase and those that do not.

caption: Double logarithmic plot illustrating the evolution of plastic-strain range versus cycle number for directionally-solidified DZ445 superalloy subjected to a 1.6% total strain range at 900 °C, incorporating dwell times ranging from 0 to 128 minutes.
summary: This double logarithmic plot characterizes the fatigue behavior of the DZ445 superalloy at 900 °C under a 1.6% total strain range. By plotting plastic-strain range against cycle number for dwell times between 0 and 128 minutes, the figure demonstrates the cyclic degradation and strain accumulation trends inherent to this specific superalloy.

caption: Galvanostatic potential profile of the Zn 44.4 electrode versus RHE, measured at a constant current density of -50 mA cm-2 over an 18-hour duration in a 30% w/w KOH aqueous electrolyte.
summary: This galvanostatic test evaluates the electrochemical stability of the Zn 44.4 electrode under hydrogen evolution conditions. The potential versus RHE is plotted over an 18-hour period at a constant current density of -50 mA cm-2 in a 30% w/w KOH aqueous solution, demonstrating the electrode's performance and stability during continuous operation.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Al–Mn–Cr system at 350 °C, incorporating experimental data from literature with specific color-coded markers.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the phase equilibria for the Al–Mn–Cr system at 350 °C. The plot integrates experimental data points from multiple external studies, represented by distinct color codes, to define the phase stability regions within the ternary composition space at this specific isothermal condition.

caption: Morphological representation of a typical internal defect identified via CT imaging.
summary: This panel displays a typical internal defect morphology captured through CT imaging. The defect is characterized by specific geometric parameters, including a surface area of 1.53 mm2, a volume of 0.06 mm3, and a sphericity value of 0.47, illustrating the nature of internal voids within the printed PLA structure.

caption: FT-IR spectrum of Z80BLA monolith sample, illustrating the vibrational features of the material.
summary: This panel provides the FT-IR spectrum for the Z80BLA monolith sample. Similar to the other monolith samples, it allows for the identification of key chemical bonds and structural features. The comparison with zeolite 13X and other monoliths helps characterize the material's chemical environment and the influence of the synthesis process.

caption: GND density distribution map of the HT1 specimen subjected to a 0.4% strain amplitude.
summary: This map displays the GND density distribution for the HT1 specimen at a 0.4% strain amplitude. The average GND density is measured at 5.2 × 10^14 m^-2. The microstructure exhibits alternating zones of high-density dislocations and dislocation-free regions, characteristic of the material's response to the applied strain.

caption: Temperature-dependent ac magnetic susceptibility for NiMn0.75Cr0.25Ge measured at selected hydrostatic pressures, demonstrating a first-order magnetic order-disorder transition with thermal hysteresis for pressures at or above 1 kbar.
summary: This panel illustrates the ac magnetic susceptibility of NiMn0.75Cr0.25Ge across a range of temperatures and pressures. For pressures of 1 kbar and above, the material exhibits a first-order magnetic order-disorder transition characterized by thermal hysteresis, where the critical temperature of this transition decreases as the applied hydrostatic pressure increases.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) results for VeroWhite (RGD835) showing the temperature-dependent evolution of storage modulus (E’) and loss factor (d).
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis of VeroWhite (RGD835) characterizes its viscoelastic behavior by plotting storage modulus and loss factor against temperature. These measurements are critical for modeling the thermal state of polymeric mould inserts, as the material's stiffness and creep compliance are highly temperature-dependent, necessitating accurate data for structural simulations.

caption: Calculated electron density difference (EDD) diagram of HAPA-CN with PS absorbed on the (001) lattice plane, showing charge accumulation in blue and depletion in yellow.
summary: Panel i shows the EDD diagram for HAPA-CN with PS absorbed on the (001) plane. Bader analysis reveals a migration of 1.71 electrons to PS, indicating that the introduction of P and O elements enhances the electron transfer capacity compared to the unmodified g-C3N4 catalyst.

caption: Dark-field TEM image corresponding to the region shown in (c), emphasizing specific phase contrast.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the region previously examined in bright-field mode highlights specific phase contrast within the aged Ni33Cr alloy. By isolating diffraction information, this technique provides enhanced visibility of the microstructural features, confirming the distribution and morphology of the phases present after the 4800-hour aging treatment.

caption: EDX analysis of Ni–Co alloy electrodeposited on copper at -1100 mV versus Ag/AgCl.
summary: This panel depicts the EDX analysis of a Ni–Co alloy electrodeposited onto a copper substrate at a potential of -1100 mV versus Ag/AgCl. The analysis demonstrates the effect of the applied electrochemical deposition potential on the stoichiometry and elemental composition of the alloy at pH 6.5 and room temperature.

caption: CLSM 3D surface topography of a PEG_IM peg produced by injection molding, showing visible mold-related surface features.
summary: Representing a peg manufactured through injection molding, this 3D CLSM image highlights specific surface features inherited from the molding process. The reference text indicates that this sample displays an average profile height of 17 µm, with the image clearly capturing the distinct surface textures characteristic of the injection molding mold.

caption: Banded structure observed within the Al-Mg alloy cross-section.
summary: The banded structure within the Al-Mg alloy cross-section is clearly visible, highlighting periodic variations in the microstructure. This feature is characteristic of the thermal cycling inherent in the WAAM fabrication process, where repeated heating and cooling cycles influence the grain morphology and distribution throughout the deposited thin wall.

caption: Hierarchical clustering heatmap displaying the top 100 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between samples, with red and blue indicating high and low relative expression levels, respectively.
summary: This hierarchical clustering heatmap visualizes the top 100 differentially expressed genes across experimental samples. The color-coded representation, where red denotes high expression and blue denotes low expression, provides a clear overview of the gene expression profiles, facilitating the identification of significant mRNA variations between the different treatment groups.

caption: Two-dimensional microhardness distribution map of as-deposited WE43-Mg fabricated via the CMT process mode.
summary: This panel displays the 2D microhardness distribution within the middle region of as-deposited WE43-Mg samples produced using the CMT process mode. The map provides a spatial visualization of the hardness values across the specimen, illustrating the mechanical properties resulting from this specific CMT-WAAM processing condition.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and solid fraction (fs) curves for the 2.5Hf sample.
summary: The 2.5Hf sample is analyzed through its DSC curve (solid line) and solid fraction curve (dashed line). These curves illustrate the thermal response and phase evolution of the material, enabling the determination of the specific temperature at which oxidation initiates, as established by the experimental DSC data analysis.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of CP-R237 cells stained for live (green) and dead (red) populations after 7 days of incubation with gel or Dopa-gel scaffolds.
summary: Live/dead staining of CP-R237 cells reveals the viability of cells cultured on gel and Dopa-gel scaffolds after 7 days. Green fluorescence indicates living cells, while red fluorescence marks dead cells. This visualization provides a qualitative assessment of biocompatibility and cell survival within the different hydrogel environments.

caption: Stereographic pole figure projections for (100), (110), and (111) planes of as-printed LPBF 17-4 PH stainless steel processed with a 0° rotation scanning strategy.
summary: Stereographic pole figure projections for (100), (110), and (111) planes of as-printed LPBF 17-4 PH stainless steel processed with a 0° rotation scanning strategy. The (110) plane aligns with the cutting direction, representing the most favorable condition for dislocation slip, enhanced texture evolution, and improved strain hardenability during subsequent machining.

caption: Isosurfaces of the normalized progress variable Yc = 0.7 for the second nozzle design, showing mixture stratification and flame wrinkling that locally suppresses heat release.
summary: Representing the second nozzle design, this panel shows a stabilized flame with distinct mixture stratification. Flame wrinkling is clearly visible in the region, which serves to locally suppress the heat release rate. These structural fluctuations are attributed to intrinsic instabilities inherent to the burner design and flow conditions.

caption: Hardness distribution box plot for varying Al elemental content.
summary: This box plot illustrates the hardness distribution of the alloy as Al content increases from low to high ranges. The centerline of the distribution rises significantly, demonstrating a clear upward trend in hardness as the concentration of Al increases within the material structure.

caption: Three-dimensional scatter plot illustrating the distribution of inverse design results, where axes represent normalized l, r, and d1 parameters, with color intensity indicating mechanical performance values.
summary: This 3D scatter plot visualizes the distribution of inverse design results using normalized l, r, and d1 parameters. The axes represent these normalized values, while color intensity maps to the mechanical performance of each point, providing a comprehensive overview of the design space and performance outcomes achieved through the inverse design process.

caption: Shear modulus of TPS60A measured via dynamic mechanical analysis across varying load (1–30 N) and shear angle (0.001°–1°).
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis of TPS60A shows that the shear modulus is highly dependent on the range of normal forces and shear angles applied. These findings highlight the material's mechanical response, making it a viable candidate for robust liners that must withstand significant stresses during various dynamic physical activities.

caption: Resistivity dependence on applied magnetic field for the aged sample measured at various temperatures, demonstrating field-independent behavior at 300 K and 77 K.
summary: Resistivity measurements for the aged sample as a function of magnetic field indicate that the material's electrical properties remain stable under varying magnetic field strengths. Specifically, at temperatures of 300 K and 77 K, the resistivity is observed to be almost entirely independent of the applied magnetic field.

caption: Distribution map of total dwell time above the melting temperature, identifying thermal bottlenecks within the vertical supports.
summary: This distribution map visualizes the total dwell time above the melting point across the structure. Two vertical supports exhibit the longest dwell times, indicating significant heat accumulation. This geometric influence confirms the presence of thermal bottlenecks, highlighting regions where heat dissipation is restricted during the thermal processing of the component.

caption: Polar plot displaying the normalized in-plane elastic modulus ratios for conventional honeycomb structures under compressive loading.
summary: This polar plot illustrates the directional dependence of the normalized in-plane elastic modulus for conventional honeycomb structures under compression. The data reflects consistent trends previously observed in tensile tests, highlighting the inherent anisotropy of the conventional honeycomb design when subjected to in-plane compressive forces during mechanical evaluation.

caption: Lattice cell configuration composed of six identical repeated segments, where each segment integrates two spiral trusses and one longitudinal truss, with relevant dimensions explicitly marked.
summary: The lattice cell is shown as an assembly of six identical repeated segments. Each segment is characterized by the integration of two spiral trusses and one longitudinal truss. The panel marks the relevant dimensions, providing a detailed breakdown of the repeating unit that constitutes the overall HLCS architecture.

caption: Decision function distribution plot for the Ti-6Al-4V alloy, color-coded based on the surface roughness Sq < 35 μm criterion (φ2), with an 'x' marking the identified optimum process parameters.
summary: This heatmap displays the decision function distribution for the Ti-6Al-4V alloy based on the Sq < 35 μm criterion (φ2). The optimal process parameters are marked with an 'x'. Large valleys and peaks with an Sq of 62.9 μm were observed in Case-3 due to overmelting from heat accumulation.

caption: Cross-sectional micro-CT slice in the x-y plane showing parallel alignment of cracks and minor deflections at inter-filament interfaces.
summary: Captured in the x-y plane, this cross-sectional slice demonstrates a pronounced parallel alignment of cracks within the PA1 sample. The visualization highlights how inter-filament interfaces cause only minor deflections, illustrating the interaction between the internal microstructure and crack propagation paths during the material's mechanical response.

caption: Nanoindentation load-displacement curves for the 2HEA2mm sample, showing data collected from the edge and center regions.
summary: This panel displays nanoindentation load-displacement curves for the 2HEA2mm alloy, comparing measurements taken at the edge and center of the sample. The mechanical response, characterized by indentation depth and slope, reflects the material's hardness, with an average value of 611.3 ± 2.2 HV for this specific composition.

caption: Diagnostic diagram for creep damage identifying the dominant mechanism, showing that all creep rupture data for the three alloys fall within the microstructural degradation domain.
summary: Utilizing the diagnostic diagram proposed by Ashby and Dyson, this panel identifies the dominant creep damage mechanism for the three alloys. The plot demonstrates that all experimental creep rupture data points are located within the microstructural degradation domain, indicating this is the primary failure mechanism for these materials.

caption: Atomic unit cell model representing the pure titanium (Ti) crystal structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the unit cell model for pure titanium. As with the aluminum model, this structure is utilized to analyze surface work function characteristics. Understanding these atomic configurations is essential for assessing how electron escape difficulty influences the overall corrosion resistance of the metallic surface.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the specimen interior after cyclic straining at a strain amplitude of 6 × 10⁻³ showing sparse precipitation particles with pinned individual dislocations.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph reveals the microstructure of the specimen following cyclic straining at a strain amplitude of 6 × 10⁻³. The intracellular region displays a limited density of precipitation particles, which serve as pinning sites for individual dislocations, highlighting the interaction between precipitates and dislocation structures under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing DA-PEG, AL, TOCN, and the synthesized LPNC-1, highlighting the disappearance of the C-C triple bond peak at 2122 cm-1.
summary: FTIR analysis of LPNC-1 demonstrates the successful consumption of the triple bond during the reaction, evidenced by the significant disappearance of the C-C stretching vibration peak at 2122 cm-1. This spectral comparison confirms the chemical transformation occurring between the precursors DA-PEG, AL, and TOCN during the synthesis process.

caption: Dual cross-sectional STEM images utilizing predominant element contrast to resolve distinct structural details in the TiAl, oxide, and platinum layers.
summary: These two STEM images employ predominant element contrast to resolve specific material layers. The upper image is optimized to visualize the TiAl and oxide layers, while the lower image focuses on the platinum layer. This comparative approach allows for detailed characterization of the interface and layer integrity after thermal loading.

caption: Training and testing loss curves for the R90C90 BNN, illustrating a steep descent and significant overlap between the two metrics.
summary: The R90C90 BNN shows optimal training performance, characterized by a steep descent in loss and a high degree of overlap between training and testing curves. This behavior confirms that the model is correctly trained and possesses a strong capability to generalize data, effectively eliminating the overfitting issues observed previously.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves comparing cast and AFSD processed samples, highlighting thermal behavior below 150 °C.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for cast and AFSD samples are presented to evaluate thermal behavior. Both materials exhibit an exothermic peak below 150 °C, which is attributed to the formation of the Al3Mg2-β phase. This observation aligns with ThermoCalc predictions, indicating consistent phase evolution characteristics across both processing conditions.

caption: Plasticity versus strength distribution diagram comparing near-beta titanium alloys produced via additive manufacturing techniques, such as DED and SLM, against traditional casting processes.
summary: This plasticity-strength distribution diagram benchmarks near-beta titanium alloys fabricated through various additive manufacturing methods, including DED and SLM, alongside conventional casting processes. The plot serves as a comparative framework to evaluate the mechanical trade-offs between strength and ductility in these advanced titanium materials relative to established manufacturing standards.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of a multi-layer sample processed at 275 W and 1000 mm/s.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map characterizes the multi-layer sample microstructure obtained using conduction mode parameters of 275 W and 1000 mm/s. Selected for its high density, the sample allows for a detailed assessment of grain orientation and solidification patterns within the multi-layer build under these specific processing parameters.

caption: Reconstructed HFB profile generated using the VWDM method, illustrating the spatial distribution of heat flux.
summary: This panel presents the reconstructed HFB profile calculated using the VWDM method. The visualization illustrates the spatial heat flux distribution derived from this specific design method, allowing for a direct comparison with the target HFB to evaluate the effectiveness of the VWDM in heat flux reconstruction.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for ER110S-G steel, featuring a shaded region representing the cooling rate range observed in the 15th layer of thin-wall structures, bounded by the highest (S1) and lowest (S6) heat input conditions.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of ER110S-G steel under varying cooling rates. The shaded region highlights the experimental cooling range for thin-wall structures, with S1 and S6 defining the bounds. These cooling rates correlate with a predominantly ferritic microstructure, as confirmed by the diagram and associated microstructural analysis.

caption: STEM HAADF image showing the interfacial region of a Type II dissimilar joint, highlighting the presence of TiC precipitates within the solid solution matrix.
summary: This STEM HAADF image captures the interfacial region of a Type II dissimilar joint. The micrograph reveals the formation of TiC precipitates alongside a solid solution phase at the interface. These structural features contribute to the increased hardness observed in the Type II sample compared to the Type I sample interface.

caption: Ashby plot displaying Young’s modulus as a function of polymer content, showing that mfDNGHs and mxDNGHs exhibit significantly higher stiffness than existing 3D printed hydrogel benchmarks.
summary: Young’s modulus is plotted against polymer content to evaluate the stiffness of various 3D printed hydrogels. The mfDNGHs and mxDNGHs, represented by the red shaded area, display higher stiffnesses compared to any previously reported 3D printed hydrogel, even when compared to materials with similar polymer content.

caption: Enlarged 10X view of the RDA triplot focusing on the explanatory vectors associated with build orientations (BOs) for the CMYK specimens.
summary: Providing a detailed 10X magnification of the RDA triplot, this panel highlights the specific explanatory vectors related to build orientations. By isolating these BO labels, the visualization clarifies the influence of build orientation on the CMYK specimen scores, complementing the broader analysis presented in the initial RDA diagram.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the irradiated zone of the 4Al10V sample shown in panel (a).
summary: Captured from the irradiated zone of the 4Al10V sample, this SAED map illustrates the crystallographic changes resulting from ion irradiation at 500 °C. When compared to the un-irradiated pattern in panel (c), it provides evidence of the structural evolution or phase stability within the alloy under irradiation.

caption: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the low CSRO model at 2 T magnetic induction intensity.
summary: This panel displays the pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the low CSRO system subjected to a 2 T magnetic field. The data tracks seven specific chemical order types, allowing for the observation of how magnetic induction influences the local atomic ordering during the Monte Carlo simulation cycles.

caption: Surface topography of the DLC_Si10% coating obtained via 3D profilometry.
summary: Surface topography of the DLC_Si10% coating is captured through 3D profilometry. This specific composition displays a surface roughness (Sa) of 6.69 nm and a maximum surface roughness height (Sz) of 81.5 nm, reflecting a higher degree of surface perturbation compared to the pure DLC and DLC-W variants.

caption: Rietveld refinement profile for the deuterated Zr3Fe0.7Ni0.3 (Zr3FeD6.7) sample, showing experimental neutron diffraction data as blue crosses, the calculated model as a red line, the background including stainless-steel cell peaks as a black line, and the residual difference as a lower black line.
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction pattern and Rietveld refinement for the deuterated Zr3Fe0.7Ni0.3 phase, identified as Zr3FeD6.7. The experimental data is fitted with a calculated profile, incorporating background signals from the pressure cell. The difference plot highlights the agreement between the experimental observations and the refined structural model.

caption: Comparative analysis of NbC particle characteristics between 5 min and 4 h sintered samples, illustrating differences in area fraction and particle size distribution.
summary: Particle analysis shows that the average area fraction of (Nb + Mo)C particles is higher in the 4 h sintered sample (2.8%) compared to the 5 min sample (~1%). The 4 h sample exhibits larger average particle area and size, indicating that metal carbide coarsening occurs via solid state diffusion.

caption: High-resolution C 1s and Cl 2s XPS spectra of AP surfaces subjected to plasma, distilled water, and methanol treatments, calibrated to adventitious carbon at 284.6 eV.
summary: High-resolution XPS spectra in the C 1s and Cl 2s regions demonstrate the effectiveness of plasma treatment on AP surfaces. Analysis reveals a significant reduction in carbonates and halogenated carbon species following plasma, distilled water, and methanol exposure, confirming that plasma treatment successfully removes adventitious carbon from the material surface.

caption: Visual documentation of the LBC test setup during active mechanical loading.
summary: This photograph captures the LBC test setup in operation. The system employs a universal mechanical testing machine to apply compressive forces to the specimen. A rigid tungsten carbide ball indenter, 12 mm in diameter, is used to perform the mechanical evaluation as part of the experimental characterization process.

caption: Printing accuracy of channel width for the second test model, showing performance consistency across different yellow dye (YD) dosages.
summary: This plot displays the printing accuracy of channel widths for the second test model. By utilizing a constant channel width design, the data confirms the printing performance of the silmer/AA/GMA polymer, providing a comparative metric for the resolution capabilities of the printing system.

caption: Atomic force microscopy images illustrating the etched grooves formed on CGHAZ, FGHAZ, and ICCGHAZ microstructures within NSC and SC materials after 16 minutes of immersion in a picric acid-based aqueous solution.
summary: Atomic force microscopy images illustrate the etched grooves formed on CGHAZ, FGHAZ, and ICCGHAZ microstructures within NSC and SC materials after 16 minutes of immersion in a picric acid-based aqueous solution. These AFM scans provide a visual representation of the surface topography resulting from the chemical etching process applied to the specimens.

caption: Cyclic stability performance of the encapsulated PPy/3D-IDCμE device over 5000 cycles at a constant current density of 2 mA cm⁻².
summary: Cyclic stability testing confirms the durability of the encapsulated μSC device. Using a 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H2SO4 electrolyte, the device maintains 75% of its initial capacitance after 5000 charge-discharge cycles, indicating robust long-term performance for the chosen gel electrolyte configuration.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for annealed PEKK coupons, illustrating the evolution of storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor over successive recycling rounds.
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for annealed PEKK coupons, illustrating the evolution of storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor over successive recycling rounds. These measurements highlight the impact of annealing on the viscoelastic behavior of recycled PEKK, allowing for a direct comparison of mechanical properties against the as-printed condition.

caption: Experimental and predicted flow stress profiles for WAAMed NiTi alloy during deformation at 850 °C.
summary: Deformation behavior of WAAMed NiTi alloy at 850 °C is illustrated through a comparison of experimental flow stress solid lines and SCAT model predicted scatters. The results highlight the correlation between the strain-compensated Arrhenius constitutive equation and actual material performance during hot deformation testing at this temperature.

caption: TGA–DTA profiles for Ni/ZrO2 and Ni-Zn/ZrO2 catalysts following 100 hours of DRM reaction to assess carbon deposition.
summary: TGA-DTA results provide a quantitative assessment of carbon deposits on the catalysts after 100 hours of operation. These thermal profiles are used to compare the extent of coke formation between the Ni/ZrO2 and Ni-Zn/ZrO2 samples, helping to explain the observed differences in long-term catalytic activity and stability.

caption: DIC-calculated strain distribution map showing shear strain localization in an Iosipescu shear test specimen with a 0° raster angle, recorded prior to the ultimate fracture point.
summary: This panel presents a DIC-calculated full-field strain map for an Iosipescu shear test sample featuring a 0° raster angle. The visualization captures the strain distribution across the specimen surface just before failure, demonstrating how the specific raster orientation influences the shear strain development and potential fracture initiation in the printed composite.

caption: Energy landscape E(x1) for the fifth NbTaV sample realization, displaying the minimum energy path for dislocation glide with an inset showing the dislocation line configuration at the local minimum energy position.
summary: The fifth NbTaV sample realization is depicted here, showing the energy landscape for dislocation glide. The panel compares NEB and PN model results and includes an inset that visualizes the dislocation line at the local minimum energy position, confirming the structural configuration obtained through the atomistic and PN simulations.

caption: Optical micrograph showing a type 1 sliver defect on the convex surface of a blade, characterized by a subgrain formed from a segment of a dendrite arm.
summary: This optical micrograph displays a type 1 sliver defect located on the convex surface of a blade casting. The defect is identified as a subgrain structure resulting from a segment of a dendrite arm. Its occurrence near the leading edge is consistent with theoretical predictions regarding blade casting defects.

caption: Microstrain and dislocation density values plotted against annealing conditions for N-type and O-type LPBF-printed samples, derived from high-energy X-ray diffraction patterns.
summary: This plot displays the evolution of microstrain and dislocation density in N and O samples produced via LPBF printing across various annealing conditions. The data, obtained from high-energy X-ray diffraction, reveals high initial microstrain levels in as-built samples, confirming the significant internal stress inherent to the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Immunocytofluorescence staining images of AG, AGWOM, and AGWM scaffolds using Calcein-AM and DAPI markers after 1 and 7 days of culture.
summary: Immunocytofluorescence imaging using Calcein-AM and DAPI staining demonstrates the cellular response on AG, AGWOM, and AGWM scaffolds. After 1 and 7 days of culture, the imaging reveals that all constructs are non-cytotoxic, effectively supporting cell attachment and proliferation across the different scaffold formulations throughout the experimental observation period.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of mBMSCs after 2 days of co-culture with Si-doped BCP powders, highlighting the distribution of live and dead cells.
summary: Live/dead staining results of mBMSCs co-cultured with the powders for 2 days are depicted. The images reveal a minimal presence of dead cells, which are stained in red, indicating that the silicon-doped powders exhibited no significant cytotoxicity and maintained high biocompatibility for the stem cells during the initial culture period.

caption: (0001) basal plane pole figure of the TaC7.5 specimen.
summary: This pole figure displays the (0001) basal plane texture of the α-Ti phase for the TaC7.5 specimen. The color intensity indicates the degree of preferred grain orientation, with red regions highlighting the prominent texture components that evolved under the influence of directional heat flow during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the WC-20vol%Fe system derived from the TCE_09 database, featuring dashed red lines that delineate the specific carbon compositions of the investigated alloys.
summary: This CALPHAD equilibrium phase diagram for WC-20vol%Fe illustrates the thermodynamic stability regions of the alloy system. Dashed red lines represent the carbon composition of the alloys, identifying the C-rich alloys within the 3-phase WC-M-C domain and the W-rich alloys within the WC-M-M6C domain, as defined by the TCE_09 database.

caption: Comparison of HAADF-STEM experimental results and corresponding STEM simulations for the η1 phase along the [110]Al //[0001]η orientation.
summary: This panel displays a direct comparison between experimental HAADF-STEM observations and STEM simulations for the η1 phase along the [110]Al //[0001]η orientation. These simulations were conducted to assess the fidelity of the calculated atomic model, confirming the structural accuracy of the proposed η1 phase configuration.

caption: Optical micrograph of a specimen showing discontinuous melt tracks, evaluated via gray-value-based image processing.
summary: This panel presents a specimen characterized by discontinuous melt tracks. The image processing algorithm, developed in MATLAB, utilizes the high contrast provided by the black spray coating to distinguish the section from the background, allowing for the precise measurement of the melt track geometry in this specific process window region.

caption: Transient current-time response curves for SLM-316L stainless steel specimens fabricated in three distinct construction orientations, evaluated in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at an applied potential of 0.1 V vs. SCE.
summary: This figure displays the transient current-time response curves for SLM-316L stainless steel specimens built in three different orientations. The measurements were conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution under an applied potential of 0.1 V vs. SCE, where j m and t m represent the peak current density and corresponding time coordinates.

caption: Interactive user interface designed for multi-objective optimization of the 17-4 stainless steel laser powder-bed fusion process.
summary: This interactive interface serves as a streamlined tool for end-users to perform multi-objective optimization of the laser powder-bed fusion process specifically for 17-4 stainless steel. Developed to promote wider industrial adoption of the LPBF technique, the framework relies on statistical models tailored to this specific alloy's processing parameters.

caption: HP geometry metastructure displayed in its rest state.
summary: The HP geometry metastructure is shown in its rest state, providing a clear view of the undeformed configuration. This image acts as a control for the cyclic loading experiments, allowing for the assessment of shape evolution and structural changes that occur as the metastructure transitions through various displacement states.

caption: Microhardness distribution measured along the deposition direction for samples fabricated using the CSD strategy.
summary: This panel illustrates the microhardness distribution along the deposition direction for the CSD strategy. The recorded hardness values are 215.34 HV, 210.35 HV, and 205.13 HV. These measurements provide insight into the mechanical consistency and property variations observed within the samples when processed using the CSD deposition method.

caption: Chronoamperometry measurement recorded during the Zn–Ni electrodeposition process onto a Co–Cu alloy substrate.
summary: This chronoamperometry plot captures the Zn–Ni electrodeposition process performed at a constant potential of -1.3 V/Ag/Ag+ over a duration of 2 hours. The resulting data provides a detailed record of the current response during the formation of the Zn–Ni deposit on the Co–Cu alloy electrode.

caption: Simulated residual stress variation trend calculated for the third proportional position.
summary: Simulated residual stress variation trend calculated for the third proportional position. This simulation result is compared to experimental data to validate the model. The consistency in stress variation trends between the simulation and experimental settings confirms the reliability of the model in predicting stress across different components and positions.

caption: Grain aspect ratio distributions for different conditions and cross-section orientations, displayed as box-and-whisker plots showing Q1, median, Q3, and mean values to characterize grain morphology.
summary: Grain aspect ratio distributions are presented via box-and-whisker plots to account for the wide variability inherent in AM materials. These plots provide a robust statistical summary of morphology. Specifically, fine elongated grains with a high median aspect ratio of 2.8 are observed in the Z cross-section parallel to the building direction.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of raw powder particles used as feedstock.
summary: This panel displays the morphology of the raw powder material prior to processing. The image provides a baseline characterization of the feedstock particles, which are subsequently subjected to L-DED and HIP processes to evaluate their structural evolution and chemical composition changes during additive manufacturing and post-processing treatments.

caption: Trace element concentrations in insoluble fraction blank solutions M I, M II, M III, and M IV.
summary: Panel b illustrates the trace element concentrations found in insoluble fraction blank solutions M I through M IV. Descriptive statistical parameters such as minimum, median, maximum, and standard deviation are plotted to characterize the background levels, ensuring accurate assessment of contamination within the insoluble fraction analytical procedures.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) contour map of the CM state, illustrating local misorientations within the 0° to 2° range.
summary: The KAM contour map illustrates the local misorientation distribution within the CM state after solution heat treatment. The analysis indicates complete recrystallization throughout the material, characterized by the absence of distinct heterogeneities in the misorientation profile, confirming a uniform microstructural state following the 1200 °C heat treatment process.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of martensitic stainless steel illustrating the coexistence of martensite, austenite, and precipitated phases including carbides and Laves phases at room temperature.
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram displays the phase composition of martensitic stainless steel at room temperature. It highlights the presence of martensite and austenite matrices alongside precipitated carbides and Laves phases, providing a theoretical basis for understanding the material's complex microstructural evolution and phase stability under equilibrium conditions.

caption: Three-dimensional surface topography of an SLM-processed TA15 thin plate containing 0.4 wt% additive.
summary: This panel displays the 3D surface morphology of an SLM-processed TA15 thin plate with a 0.4 wt% concentration. The visualization provides a detailed topographical reconstruction, illustrating the surface characteristics resulting from the selective laser melting process applied to the TA15 alloy material under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Traced trajectory of an irregular BM powder particle, highlighting laminar flow near the nozzle, a transition to turbulent flow, and a vortex behind the flow.
summary: This panel depicts the complex trajectory of an irregular BM powder particle. The flow begins as laminar near the nozzle, transitions to turbulent before impacting the Ti64 substrate, and exhibits a vortex behind the flow. The particle trajectory diverges significantly from the nozzle's center axis compared to PA powder.

caption: Surface profile z(x,y) of the SMAT-ed specimen displaying a spherically dimpled surface morphology resulting from the surface mechanical attrition treatment.
summary: Surface mechanical attrition treatment (SMAT) transforms the initial planar surface of the specimen into a spherically dimpled morphology. This modification helps decrease surface roughness by effectively breaking down the ridges present on the untreated surface, which significantly influences the run-in stage behavior during coefficient of friction (COF) testing.

caption: Fatigue crack propagation rate (da/dN) versus ΔK for Alloy A at 710 °C, demonstrating more pronounced FCPR overloading retardation effects compared to the 650 °C test.
summary: Displaying the da/dN versus ΔK relationship for Alloy A at 710 °C, this graph reveals significant FCPR overloading retardation effects. These effects are notably more pronounced than those observed at 650 °C, indicating a temperature-dependent sensitivity in the crack growth retardation behavior of the investigated superalloy material.

caption: QSTEM simulated HAADF-STEM image of the (Cr, Re)23C6 carbide with Re at the Cr4 (48h) site, calculated for a sample thickness of 20 nm.
summary: This simulated HAADF-STEM image corresponds to the structure in panel (e), where Rhenium is substituted at the Cr4 (48h) site. The simulation, performed for a 20 nm sample thickness, provides the final data point for comparing the effects of Rhenium substitution across the four distinct Wyckoff sites.

caption: Normalized XANES spectra at the Mn K-edge for the PEG-3–1500 specimen, featuring LCF fitting curves derived from SrMnO3, MnO2, and Mn2O3 standards.
summary: Normalized XANES spectra at the Mn K-edge are presented for the PEG-3–1500 specimen. The plot includes LCF fitting curves generated using SrMnO3, MnO2, and Mn2O3 as reference materials. These results facilitate the determination of the oxidation state of manganese cations in the specimen, specifically focusing on the XANES energy range.

caption: Cross-sectional view of specimen P4 (53 J/mm3) from X-ray computed tomography, illustrating the internal melt pool and crack distribution.
summary: The cross-sectional X-ray computed tomography image of specimen P4 displays the internal melt pool and crack distribution resulting from a 53 J/mm3 energy density. This panel serves as a key component in the comparative analysis of how different process parameters dictate the internal structural integrity and defect formation.

caption: One-dimensional composition profile quantifying the chemical distribution across the selected grain boundary precipitate shown in panel (c).
summary: The one-dimensional composition profile characterizes the chemical makeup of the grain boundary precipitate identified in panel (c). This quantitative analysis provides essential data on the solute concentration gradients, facilitating a comparison of the chemical composition of grain boundary features in the WAAM specimen relative to other material conditions.

caption: Arc plasma image and schematic for the 1st layer 2nd bead, where the arc's left end covers the substrate while the right end remains suspended in the air.
summary: Captured at a frequency of 30 Hz, the arc plasma image for the 1st layer 2nd bead reveals an asymmetric arc shape. The physical and schematic diagrams illustrate that the left end of the arc maintains contact with the substrate, whereas the right end is suspended in the surrounding air.

caption: Tafel extrapolation diagram illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the material across different vertical positions within the build.
summary: Tafel extrapolation was utilized to analyze the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the material. The resulting Tafel diagram reveals significant variations in corrosion characteristics depending on the specific vertical position within the build, demonstrating that the build orientation plays a critical role in determining the overall corrosion resistance of the specimen.

caption: Destabilization of the flat interface showing chromium concentration variations across small grains.
summary: During the flat interface destabilization stage, small grains form at the interface. Chromium concentration values at the center of the first solidification positions are observed to be lower than those at later solidification positions, indicating the onset of compositional variation during the early stages of grain formation.

caption: Final weighted material effectiveness scorecard for the aeronautics case study.
summary: This table presents the final weighted material effectiveness scorecard specifically developed for the aeronautics case study. It serves as a comprehensive summary of the evaluation metrics, providing a clear overview of how different materials perform when assessed against the specific requirements and criteria defined for aeronautical engineering applications.

caption: Mott–Schottky plots representing the capacitance behavior of passive films formed on Alloy 31 at 0.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl in 40 wt.% H3PO4 solution, measured across various temperatures.
summary: This Mott–Schottky plot illustrates the capacitance characteristics of passive films developed on Alloy 31. The films were formed at a constant potential of 0.8 V vs. Ag/AgCl in a 40 wt.% phosphoric acid solution. The data highlights how these electrochemical properties evolve under different temperature conditions during the passivation process.

caption: Mean cross-sectional image stack of the 45° inclined DNA 0.5 mm channel with the nominal channel boundary superimposed in red.
summary: Depicted here is the mean cross-sectional image stack for the 45° inclined DNA 0.5 mm channel, with the nominal channel boundary marked in red. This configuration indicates a significant degree of clogging, with the channel being more than half-clogged, demonstrating the impact of inclination and diameter on DNA artefact obstruction.

caption: Diffraction pattern of the polycarbonate specimen reinforced with 5 wt% carbon powder, featuring the polymer amorphous halo and weak graphitic peaks at 2θ ≈ 25–26° and 40–45°.
summary: The XRD pattern for the polycarbonate specimen reinforced with 5 wt% carbon powder displays the characteristic amorphous halo of the polymer. Additionally, weak graphitic peaks appear at 2θ values around 25–26° and 40–45°, which correspond to the presence of disordered or turbostratic carbon within the composite filament structure.

caption: Ni 2p 3/2 XPS spectrum of the fresh reduced-only catalyst, showing a peak at 852.8 eV for reduced Ni and a broader peak at 857 eV for surface oxidized Ni.
summary: The Ni 2p 3/2 XPS spectrum of the fresh reduced-only catalyst reveals a peak at 852.8 eV, indicating reduced Ni, and a broader peak at 857 eV, attributed to surface oxidized Ni. The small signal intensity suggests that Ni is dispersed within the fumed SiO2 pores, limiting detection to external crystallites.

caption: Hysteresis loop showing the variation of the piezoelectric coefficient (d33) as a function of the applied electric field for 3D printed BaTiO3 discs.
summary: The piezoelectric coefficient d33 is plotted against the electric field to demonstrate the electromechanical hysteresis behavior of the 3D printed BaTiO3 discs. Sintered at 1350 °C, the sample shows characteristic ferroelectric switching behavior, confirming the successful additive manufacturing of materials with functional piezoelectric properties at room temperature.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves illustrating the weight loss behavior of cured CF-hb-PFAEKs films as a function of temperature.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for cured CF-hb-PFAEKs films demonstrate their thermal degradation profiles. The experimental data reveals that the temperature at which 5% weight loss occurs (Td5%) for all tested films falls within the range of 338 to 341 °C, confirming that these materials possess relatively excellent thermal stabilities.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the Charpy impact strength values measured for five distinct specimen types.
summary: This bar chart presents a comparative analysis of the Charpy impact strength across five different material specimens. The visualization serves as a primary reference for evaluating the fracture resistance of these samples, providing a clear quantitative overview of their mechanical performance under impact loading conditions as described in the study.

caption: Latent space mapping of chemical elements using principal component analysis of word vectors, highlighting the positions of first and second principal elements.
summary: Chemical elements are projected into a latent space using principal component analysis of their word vectors. This panel specifically displays the spatial distribution and relative positions of the first and second principal elements, providing a foundational visualization for understanding element relationships within the design space of high-entropy alloys.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops measured along the hard axis (90°) for segments C1–C12, where the curve ordering reflects the loss of magnetic anisotropy with increasing print height.
summary: Hysteresis curves measured along the hard axis (90°) for segments C1–C12 reveal the loss of magnetic anisotropy in the continuously printed specimen. The ordering of these curves, which is opposite to that observed along the easy axis, confirms the progressive degradation of magnetic properties as the print height increases.

caption: Tensile stress-strain behavior of 5% Co and 0% Co models at 1200 K.
summary: This panel shows the tensile stress-strain curves for 5% Co and 0% Co containing models at a temperature of 1200 K. It captures the mechanical response of the materials at this high-temperature limit, allowing for an evaluation of the influence of cobalt on the tensile properties under extreme thermal conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curve of Ni wire in 1 M KOH at 40 °C, illustrating the electrochemical response of nickel.
summary: This panel presents the cyclic voltammetry curve for Ni wire measured in 1 M KOH at 40 °C. The analysis of this curve is part of a broader study to ascertain the dealloying parameters and electrochemical dissolution characteristics of the nickel component within the alloy system.

caption: Magnified view of the low-field region (H = 0–100 A/m) of the magnetization curves, emphasizing the initial magnetic response and hysteresis characteristics.
summary: Focusing on the low-field region from 0 to 100 A/m, this magnified plot reveals the initial magnetization behavior. It allows for a detailed comparison of the magnetic hardness between AF and HTed samples, specifically highlighting the differences in magnetic response at weak fields where grain structure effects are most pronounced.

caption: Temperature-dependent squareness ratio (MR/MS) of the hysteresis loops, with dashed lines delineating regimes well below, within, and well above the Morin transition (TM).
summary: The squareness of the hysteresis loops, defined as the ratio of remanence to saturation magnetization, is plotted against temperature. The data shows a decrease in squareness near the transition temperature, indicating a harder magnetic reversal. This trend suggests an isotopically distributed locally nonzero anisotropy influencing the magnetic coupling in the sample.

caption: Ashby plot comparing strength versus density for various engineering materials, highlighting the targeted performance goals for the hybrid implant in large-area bone defect repair applications.
summary: This Ashby plot compares strength versus density for various engineering materials, highlighting the targeted performance goals for the hybrid implant in large-area bone defect repair applications. The visualization demonstrates the design objective of achieving a lightweight, high-strength structure suitable for clinical sites such as the mandible and tibia.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for the HSLA steel, featuring superimposed experimental cooling curves indicated by arrows to represent specific cooling rates.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of the HSLA steel used in the investigation. Experimental cooling curves are superimposed on the diagram, with arrows highlighting the specific cooling rates utilized. This framework serves as a reference for analyzing the microstructural evolution and phase formation during the cooling process.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus actual compressive strength values in MPa, demonstrating high model accuracy with data points closely aligned to the ideal reference line.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the predictive performance of the SVR–ANN hybrid model for compressive strength. The data points show a strong correlation between predicted and actual values, indicating high model accuracy as the points are closely aligned with the ideal reference line, confirming the model's effectiveness for this property.

caption: Raman spectra within the 1000–1800 cm⁻¹ range comparing the surfaces of bare NAB alloy after immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution with electrosynthesized PANI-5 coatings on NAB electrodes before and after corrosion testing in the same saline environment.
summary: This Raman spectroscopy analysis, conducted in the 1000–1800 cm⁻¹ range, characterizes the surface chemistry of bare NAB alloy and PANI-5 coated NAB electrodes. By comparing the spectra of bare NAB in 3.5% NaCl with PANI-5 coatings before and after corrosion tests, the study effectively identifies corrosion products and coating stability.

caption: FTIR spectra of scaffolds after the biomineralization of HA-like layers.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy is used to analyze the chemical composition of the scaffolds following the biomineralization process. The spectra identify the characteristic functional groups associated with the formation of HA-like layers on the scaffold surfaces, confirming the successful deposition of mineralized material after immersion in SBF.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of triangular Ni electrodes in alkaline media, showing electrochemical performance and current density at -1.2 V.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram evaluates the electrochemical performance of 3D printed triangular Ni electrodes in alkaline media. The T3 geometry configuration achieved a current density of -10.11 mA/cm2 at -1.2 V, showing electrochemical activity consistent with the performance trends observed in other geometry configurations during the CV and LSV scans.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Al-Ce-(Ni,Mn) system at 400 ℃ with a fixed Mn concentration of 1.12 wt%.
summary: Represented here is the calculated isothermal section of the pseudo-ternary Al-Ce-(Ni,Mn) phase diagram at 400 ℃, maintaining a constant manganese concentration of 1.12 wt%. This diagram illustrates the phase equilibria and stability regions for the alloy system at this lower temperature, facilitating comparison with the 620 ℃ section.

caption: Solidification path for NiAl alloy containing 12 wt% Al, showing initial Ni nucleation followed by a peritectic reaction to form Ni3Al.
summary: The solidification path for the 12 wt% Al NiAl alloy is illustrated. Solidification initiates with the nucleation of Ni. Subsequently, the remaining liquid phase undergoes a peritectic reaction, which completes the solidification process by forming the Ni3Al phase, as depicted in the calculated solidification curve.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change profiles for four distinct powder samples measured under a constant applied magnetic field of 1.5 T.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic entropy change as a function of temperature for four different powder samples under an applied field of 1.5 T. The data provides a comparative analysis of the magnetocaloric response across the studied materials, highlighting the temperature-dependent behavior of the magnetic entropy change for each sample.

caption: Microstructure of the Re-containing sample pre-strained under compression for 0.5 h and then tension for 0.5 h along [001] after creep testing.
summary: This TEM image depicts the microstructure of a Re-containing sample after a complex pre-straining sequence involving 0.5 hours of compression followed by 0.5 hours of tension along [001], prior to creep testing. The sample exhibits P-type TCP precipitates, confirming that varied pre-straining histories consistently lead to these microstructural changes during creep.

caption: Atomic model representing the atomic layer spacing in a double Sc-doped Al–Mg–Si alloy.
summary: Featured is the atomic model of an Al–Mg–Si alloy doped with two Sc atoms. This visualization allows for the comparison of crystal layer spacing changes against other doping configurations, such as the Dy-doped variants, to determine the specific influence of Sc concentration on the alloy structure.

caption: Fully reversed (R = -1) constant amplitude fatigue test results for Ti6Al4V specimens, plotted as stress amplitude versus cycles to failure, including statistical fatigue curves for 2.3%, 50%, and 97.7% survival probabilities.
summary: This plot displays fatigue test results for Ti6Al4V specimens under fully reversed loading conditions. It presents nominal stress amplitude data alongside calculated fatigue curves for 2.3%, 50%, and 97.7% survival probabilities. These curves were derived from statistical analysis of seven broken specimens to characterize the material's fatigue performance and scatter.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the ω phase within the twin, captured using specific diffraction spots.
summary: This dark-field TEM image highlights the ω phase distribution within the twin structure. By utilizing diffraction spots corresponding to the ω phase, the image provides clear evidence of its presence within the twinning region, further elucidating the complex phase transformations occurring during the bending deformation of the material.
