The curves reveal distinct mass loss steps associated with the degradation of each polymer phase. Additionally, the residual mass at high temperatures indicates the presence of Ni or Fe content within the composite filaments.

caption: Agent performance metrics during the third phase of reward shaping under an extrusion error condition of 232% flow rate at 190 °C.
summary: This panel depicts the agent's performance during the final phase of reward shaping. Under the consistent extrusion error condition of 232% flow rate at 190 °C, the plot illustrates the agent's refined learning behavior and performance stability achieved by the conclusion of the three-phase reward shaping training process.

caption: Video frame capture documenting the printing process for the second layer case, showing the interface between adjacent lines.
summary: Panel d presents a video-based visual record of the printing process for the second layer. By documenting the interface between adjacent lines, this panel demonstrates the scalability of the void mitigation capability across multiple layers, confirming that the control system functions effectively beyond the initial layer of printing.

caption: Excess vacancy concentration plotted against true strain during deformation, with black dashed lines indicating the 5% strain threshold and gray/blue dashed lines representing the inclusion of cluster hardening effects.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of excess vacancy concentration as a function of true strain during deformation. Simulation results indicate that incorporating cluster hardening leads to higher vacancy annihilation rates. The 5% strain mark is highlighted, providing a reference point for the vacancy concentration behavior under these specific deformation conditions.

caption: Bode modulus plot displaying the impedance magnitude as a function of frequency for the tested samples.
summary: Displaying the impedance magnitude as a function of frequency, this Bode modulus plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance response of the samples. Together with the phase plot and Nyquist data, it facilitates a comprehensive evaluation of the material's electrochemical properties and the validation of the equivalent circuit models used for data fitting.

caption: Initial stage of microparticle chain formation showing the extraction of particles from a stationary dispersion meniscus at the conduit outlet under an applied 0.25 kV AC voltage.
summary: This panel captures the initiation phase where a 0.25 kV AC voltage is applied to a dispersion meniscus. This process extracts microparticles from the conduit outlet to begin the formation of a vertically aligned chain, as supported by the initial extraction phase described in the reference sentences.

caption: Atomic model of (001) Cu stimulated grains matched to a (001) Ni substrate.
summary: The panel displays the interface matching for (001) Cu stimulated grains on a (001) Ni substrate. Green balls denote Ni atoms in the stimulated grains, and blue balls denote Cu atoms in the substrate, providing a clear view of the atomic alignment at the interface for this crystalline orientation.

caption: Statistical distribution of α/α’ lath lengths for the specified Ti-1Fe(S) and Ti-6Al-4V builds, showing the range of lengths with area-averaged values marked by diamonds.
summary: This panel presents the distribution of α/α’ lath lengths across various processing conditions. The box plot format allows for a direct comparison of length variability between the different Ti-1Fe(S) and Ti-6Al-4V samples, while the diamond markers highlight the area-averaged length, facilitating an assessment of how processing parameters influence lath growth.

caption: Longitudinal strain εxx evolution as a function of macro strain for the annealed laminate.
summary: The longitudinal strain εxx increases nearly identically across all regions of the annealed laminate, confirming uniform tensile deformation during the test. This consistent strain distribution indicates improved plastic compatibility among the layers, as evidenced by the absence of sharp discontinuities or severe localization even at 30% macro strain.

caption: Tabulated CO2 gas emission data for alumina specimens templated with HMs and carbon powder.
summary: This table presents a comparative analysis of CO2 gas emissions generated from alumina specimens templated with HMs and carbon powder. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the gaseous byproducts released during the processing of these sacrificial porogen-containing materials, highlighting the differences in emission profiles between the two templating agents.

caption: Kissinger analysis plot displaying the normalized scanning rate as a function of inverse peak temperature, used to determine activation enthalpies Q I and Q I I.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the Kissinger analysis of DSC measurements, where the normalized scanning rate is plotted against the inverse peak temperature on a logarithmic scale. Linear regression analysis of this data allows for the precise estimation of activation enthalpies, denoted as Q I and Q I I, from the slope.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution after 3600 s of immersion.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization plots for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys are presented after 3600 s of EOCP measurement in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These curves serve as the basis for extracting key corrosion parameters, which are subsequently summarized in Table 2 to evaluate the electrochemical behavior and corrosion resistance of the tested materials.

caption: Micro-photoluminescence spectra of 1L-MoS2 and Mo0.5W0.5S2 alloy films excited at 532 nm, with grey vertical lines indicating reference exciton peak positions for 1L-MoS2 and 1L-WS2.
summary: Micro-photoluminescence spectra for 1L-MoS2 and Mo0.5W0.5S2 alloy films are presented, excited by a 532 nm laser. The plot includes reference vertical lines representing the expected PL peak energies for 1L-MoS2 and 1L-WS2, providing a comparative baseline for the observed emission characteristics of the monolayer and alloy samples.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the crystalline structure of anode foils in their initial state and following the anodizing process.
summary: This figure presents the X-ray diffraction patterns of anode foils, specifically comparing the material before and after the anodizing treatment. These diffraction profiles are utilized to characterize the crystalline structure and phase changes occurring within the foils as a result of the anodization process described in the study.

caption: Sintered spinel crucible produced from the Sp_CMg_95_5_S30 composition following thermal processing.
summary: Shown here is the spinel crucible after the sintering process. The component, manufactured via binder jetting with the Sp_CMg_95_5_S30 composition, exhibits the structural integrity achieved after thermal treatment, demonstrating the feasibility of using this additive manufacturing technique for producing complex refractory shapes like crucibles.

caption: Bruker UMT-TriboLab rotating tribo-tester system utilized for evaluating the wear behavior of Inconel 718 superalloy at 300 °C.
summary: This photograph displays the Bruker UMT-TriboLab rotating tribo-tester system. The equipment is specifically employed to examine the wear behavior of Inconel 718 superalloy samples at an elevated temperature of 300 °C, utilizing a ball-to-plate contact configuration to simulate high-temperature friction conditions during the experimental testing process.

caption: Stacked in situ XRD diffractograms showing the evolution of the γ′-(100) reflection at 800 °C over a 5-hour aging period.
summary: Stacked in situ XRD diffractograms acquired at 800 °C illustrate the evolution of γ′ precipitates over a 5-hour duration. By focusing on the isolated (100) reflection, the plot captures structural changes during aging. Every 30th pattern from the 5000 recorded measurements is displayed to visualize the precipitation kinetics clearly.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map highlighting two low-KAM channels within initially unrecrystallized grains, indicated by white arrows within the red rectangles.
summary: This KAM map reveals the presence of two distinct low-KAM channels situated inside initially unrecrystallized grains. These channels are characterized by a lower density of precipitates and reduced internal KAM values compared to the surrounding unrecrystallized matrix, suggesting localized structural evolution within the grain interior during the deformation process.

caption: Case 1 numerical example of the lower domain distribution when the rotation matrix angle is set to 0 and θ = π / 2.
summary: This panel illustrates the numerical distribution of the lower domain for Case 1. The simulation is performed with the rotation matrix angle set to 0 and θ fixed at π / 2. This result provides a specific spatial representation of the domain configuration under these defined geometric and rotational parameters.

caption: Circular plot illustrating the directional distribution of measured fluid flow at location L1.
summary: This circular plot demonstrates the directional distribution of fluid flow at location L1. The fluid flow at this specific site is shown to distribute primarily in three distinct directions. This analysis provides a qualitative representation of the complex flow dynamics occurring within the melt pool at this identified location.

caption: 3D atom probe tomography maps illustrating the spatial distribution of Fe, Cr, Ni, Mn, Si, and Nb elements within the 0.75Nb alloy aged at 560 °C for 2 h.
summary: Reconstructed 3D atom probe tomography maps for the 0.75Nb alloy aged at 560 °C for 2 h reveal the spatial distribution of Fe, Cr, Ni, Mn, Si, and Nb. These maps demonstrate that the G-phase precipitates are significantly enriched in Ni, Nb, and Si compared to the surrounding matrix.

caption: True stress-strain curves for FeCoCrNiMn specimens, showing the effect of varying scanning speeds at a constant laser power of 200 W.
summary: True stress-strain curves for FeCoCrNiMn specimens are displayed. At a constant laser power of 200 W, increasing the scanning speed results in a slight reduction in both tensile strength and ductility. These observations provide insight into the mechanical response of the printed specimens under true stress conditions.

caption: GPA strain map of the unaged Ni50.9Ti49.1 sample showing uniform lattice strain distribution.
summary: Geometric Phase Analysis strain mapping of the unaged Ni50.9Ti49.1 sample demonstrates a relatively uniform distribution of lattice strain across the observed area. This baseline measurement indicates that the crystal lattice is largely free of significant localized strain fluctuations before the material undergoes aging.

caption: Rietveld refinement of the powder neutron diffraction pattern for the A2 HT2 alloy in the ferromagnetic austenite state, showing experimental data as black circles, calculated and difference patterns as red and blue lines, and Bragg reflections as green markers.
summary: This panel displays the Rietveld refinement of powder neutron diffraction data for the A2 HT2 alloy in its magnetically ordered state. The visualization includes experimental data, calculated and difference patterns, and Bragg reflection markers. Such analysis is essential for identifying magnetic moments at the corresponding Wyckoff positions for this sample.

caption: Representative model of the lamellar spinodoid porous absorber, illustrating a non-periodic geometry that lacks a defined repeating unit cell.
summary: Shown here is a representative model of the lamellar spinodoid porous absorber. Unlike the gyroid variant, this geometry is non-periodic and does not possess a representative unit cell. This model highlights the structural complexity and lack of long-range order inherent in the lamellar spinodoid design used for acoustic absorption.

caption: Comparison of the neutron diffraction peak and GP prediction for the <311> grain family, obtained from the axial direction at a radial position of 6 mm.
summary: Presented here is the neutron diffraction peak for the <311> grain family, shown as a red solid line, compared against the GP prediction. These measurements were performed in the axial direction at a radial position of 6 mm, providing insight into the diffraction behavior of this specific grain orientation.

caption: Two-dimensional projection plot showing the distribution of porosity (P), surface-to-volume ratio (S/V), strain energy density (U), and Young's modulus (E), with color-coded E values and gray points representing projections onto specific parameter planes to highlight trends.
summary: This panel displays the distribution of porosity, S/V ratio, strain energy density, and Young's modulus, with E values represented by a color gradient. The inclusion of gray projection points onto the P-S/V, S/V-E, E-P, S/V-U, and P-U planes effectively highlights specific trends and correlations within these two-dimensional slices of the design space.

caption: In-line transmittance spectra of alumina ceramic samples A, D, E, and I, normalized to a 0.8 mm thickness, compared against literature benchmarks for templated grain growth and magnetic alignment methods.
summary: This plot displays the in-line transmittance of alumina ceramic samples A, D, E, and I, corrected for a 0.8 mm thickness. It compares these results with literature data, highlighting variations in transparency. Sample A shows a steeper decrease in transmittance with wavelength compared to sample D, while sample I achieves performance comparable to previous studies.

caption: Interference fringes in the projected image resulting from the presence of a rotation angle.
summary: Presence of a rotation angle between the PLM and DMD pixels causes the interference fringes on the projected image to appear misaligned. This image demonstrates the effect of rotational error on the light field, showing how the fringe pattern deviates from the ideal state achieved during perfect system alignment.

caption: Three-dimensional atomic map reconstruction of the oxide at the alloy/Cr2O3 interface (region A) on the NCMS specimen after 1 h of cyclic oxidation in air with 10% H2O at 950 °C.
summary: This APT reconstruction shows the alloy/Cr2O3 interface after exposure to wet air. Unlike the dry air specimens, no oxide grain boundaries or precipitates were isolated. The presence of Ni derivatives, such as Ni and NiOH, originating from the underlying alloy, characterizes the atomic distribution in this wet environment.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material sample containing Atto425 and Atto565 dyes, measured at a thickness of 0.5 mm.
summary: This panel displays the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed multi-material sample composed of Atto425 and Atto565 dyes. The sample was printed with a thickness of 0.5 mm to facilitate comparison with other multi-material configurations. This data provides insight into the light transmission characteristics of the specific dye combination.

caption: Fatigue test rig assembly featuring an induction heating coil, a NiCr/Ni thermocouple for temperature control, and alumina rods connected to a water-cooled capacitive extensometer for displacement measurement.
summary: The fatigue test rig is shown with the specimen mounted for testing. The setup includes an induction coil for heating the specimen between 1023 and 1223 K. A NiCr/Ni thermocouple monitors temperature, while alumina rods transfer displacements to a water-cooled capacitive extensometer, ensuring accurate strain control during the fatigue experiments.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the HT-2 sample showing sub-grain formation and structural tempering of the martensite.
summary: The dark-field TEM micrograph of the HT-2 sample illustrates the formation of sub-grains, providing further evidence of the structural tempering of the martensite. Together with the bright-field images, this panel confirms the transition of the super-saturated martensitic packets into grains with distinct orientations and defined boundaries.

caption: Raman spectrum of the steel surface at 90 °C, highlighting the Cr(OH)3 peak at 717 cm⁻¹.
summary: Raman analysis of the steel surface at 90 °C reveals an inner amorphous layer composed of Cr(OH)3. This is confirmed by the detection of a characteristic Cr(OH)3 peak at 717 cm⁻¹. This spectroscopic identification provides critical insight into the composition of inner-layered films formed under these specific environmental conditions.

caption: Three-dimensional distribution of pores specifically localized within the Cu phase of the composite.
summary: The 3D distribution of pores specifically within the Cu phase is showcased in this panel. This visualization isolates the void spaces associated with the copper component, allowing for a targeted analysis of how porosity is distributed within the metallic phase of the composite.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the Al–Mg–Si–Cu alloy, demonstrating the impact of UA, PA, and OA aging conditions on corrosion performance in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
summary: This panel displays the potentiodynamic polarization curves for the Al–Mg–Si–Cu alloy under various aging conditions. These curves characterize the corrosion behavior of the alloy in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, allowing for a comparison of the electrochemical performance across the different aging states of the material.

caption: EBSD pole figures displaying (001), (110), and (111) orientations for the as-built chessboard-F sample, captured from the XOY plane.
summary: Pole figures for the chessboard-F sample indicate a more random crystallographic orientation compared to the stripe-F sample. By adjusting the scanning pattern to a chessboard strategy, the material exhibits a broader distribution of grain orientations, as evidenced by the (001), (110), and (111) pole figure data.

caption: Microstructure of the Φ508VAR processed GH4151 alloy ingot at the mid-radius position.
summary: This micrograph of the Φ508VAR ingot at the mid-radius position reveals columnar grains with fully developed secondary dendrite arms. The structural change from the edge indicates the progressive decrease in cooling rate toward the center, which facilitates the growth of more defined dendritic features in the GH4151 alloy.

caption: Three-dimensional point cloud representation of the wall surface generated via optical scanning, with gray and blue points distinguishing measurements taken from two opposing faces.
summary: This 3D point cloud reconstruction illustrates the surface geometry of the walls obtained through optical scanning. By isolating measurements from two opposite faces, represented by gray and blue points respectively, the visualization provides a detailed spatial map of the wall surfaces after the removal of irrelevant scene data.

caption: Raman spectra of carbon materials grown at 600 °C over Ni, Ni8Co2, and Co catalysts, used to evaluate crystallinity and graphitization.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was performed on carbon materials grown at 600 °C over Ni, Ni8Co2, and Co catalysts. These spectra provide insights into the structural quality, specifically the crystallinity and degree of graphitization, of the carbon products formed on the different catalyst surfaces during the synthesis process.

caption: Chronoamperometric transients of CoNi deposition on Si/Ti/Au substrates using plating bath 4, with magnetic stirring initiated at 250 seconds to evaluate mass transfer influence.
summary: This panel illustrates the chronoamperometric transients for CoNi deposition from plating bath 4 onto Si/Ti/Au substrates. Magnetic stirring was applied at 250 seconds to investigate mass transfer effects. By comparing these transients, the impact of solution agitation on the deposition kinetics and electrochemical behavior of the system is clearly observed.

caption: Stress distribution map along the Z direction of a half-cylinder specimen at 50 ns simulation time.
summary: This panel presents the stress distribution along the Z direction of a half-cylinder specimen at 50 ns. The simulation snapshot highlights the ongoing development of stress patterns within the material, showing how the internal stress distribution evolves significantly as the simulation time reaches the 50 ns mark.

caption: Bibliometric network visualization displaying 37 keywords and their interconnected co-occurrence relationships.
summary: This bibliometric network illustrates the complex associations between 37 distinct keywords identified in the study. By mapping these terms based on their co-occurrence patterns, the visualization highlights the thematic structure and research connectivity within the dataset, providing a clear overview of how these specific keywords relate to one another.

caption: Surface plots representing the spatial distribution of DOX fluorescence intensity, where grey values on the z-axis correspond to signal intensity across the x-y image plane for both spheroid and tri-culture conditions.
summary: Surface plots quantify the localization of DOX fluorescence, highlighting a concentrated signal in the spheroid group compared to a scattered, low-intensity distribution in the tri-culture group. These plots confirm that DOX accumulates significantly in osteosarcoma spheroids cultured alone, while tri-culture conditions result in negligible drug uptake and background-level signals.

caption: LSV curves of the monolithic perovskite/Si/Ni foil/NiFe photoanode under continuous and chopped illumination, alongside the calculated ABPE curve.
summary: The monolithic photoanode exhibits a current density of approximately 14.21 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, with an onset potential of approximately -0.5 V at 500 μA cm-2. These LSV measurements, performed under simulated sunlight in 1.0 M KOH, demonstrate the photoelectrochemical performance and ABPE efficiency of the device.

caption: Pore distribution analysis for SC-10, displaying red-colored pore centroids in the axial view and a histogram of pore counts relative to the radial distance from the center.
summary: Panel (e) depicts the pore population for the SC-10 specimen, utilizing red centroids to represent pore locations overlaid in the axial direction. The radial histogram quantifies the number of pores from the center of the cylinder to the edge, providing a clear view of the spatial pore distribution.

caption: Electronic band structure diagram illustrating subbands at a bias of 12.3 V, highlighting the presence of X subbands at B1 and B7 barriers and their role in carrier transport via Γ-X transfer and relaxation.
summary: This electronic band structure diagram displays subbands at 12.3 V, emphasizing the contribution of X subbands at B1 and B7 barriers to carrier transport. The mechanism involves Γ-X transfer and relaxation among X states, which correlates with the Γ51 and X11 remote Γ-X-mixing observed at 13 V.

caption: Specific wear rate and average COF values for both non-inoculated and inoculated specimens.
summary: Specific wear rate and average COF values are presented for both specimen types. This plot summarizes the quantitative tribological performance, confirming the effectiveness of the inoculation treatment in reducing wear rates and friction, consistent with the morphological improvements observed in the cross-sectional profiles and wear trace analyses.

caption: Transformation enthalpies upon heating and cooling for NiTi samples, comparing the effects of PW and CW laser emission modes on energy values.
summary: Transformation enthalpies for NiTi samples are plotted, showing values reaching 20–21 J/g, comparable to as-cast or hot-rolled specimens. The data reveals that the PW laser emission mode induces higher enthalpy values (20–22 J/g) compared to the CW mode (16–20 J/g), indicating significant influence of processing parameters on transformation energy.

caption: 5 × 5 × 5 tessellated uniform sheet-based D-FRDu lattice, illustrating the relationship between the thickness parameter t and the relative density at each stage of the hybridization process.
summary: The 5 × 5 × 5 tessellated sheet-based TPMS lattices of Du and FRDu types are presented. This panel illustrates the relationship between the thickness parameter t and the relative density at each hybridization stage, providing a visual representation of the uniform sheet-based lattice structures developed for the study.

caption: Weighted loss evolution and convergence of the predicted exponential cohesive zone law for a stochastic gradient descent approach with p=0.25, showing noisy loss behavior and convergence only after epoch (iii).
summary: Panel (a) illustrates the training dynamics using Stochastic Gradient Descent with a constraint proportion of p=0.25. The weighted loss evolution exhibits significant noise throughout the training process. Consequently, the predicted traction-separation response requires until epoch (iii) to achieve convergence toward the ground truth data, highlighting the impact of stochastic sampling.

caption: Isotherms illustrating the variation of TEC values as a function of Al and Ti content in Ni alloys.
summary: Isotherms of TEC values are plotted against Al and Ti concentrations to visualize their compositional dependence. Theoretical results demonstrate that substituting Al with Ti atoms effectively reduces the thermal expansion of both the gamma matrix and gamma-prime phase, thereby contributing to a lower overall TEC value for the alloy system.

caption: Cell proliferation rates of HOb cells on sample surfaces measured by Alamar Blue assay at 1, 3, and 7 days of culture.
summary: Cell proliferation on the sample surfaces is quantified using the Alamar Blue assay at 1, 3, and 7 days of culture. This bar chart illustrates the growth trends of HOb cells over time, demonstrating the impact of the surface treatment on cell proliferation as measured after 3 and 7 days of incubation.

caption: Ternary contour plot of saturation magnetization (Ms) for 40 Fe-Co-Ni alloy compositions, highlighting predicted compositions from ETR and NNR_4layers_Wen models across six target sets.
summary: This ternary contour plot displays the saturation magnetization (Ms) for 40 experimentally synthesized Fe-Co-Ni alloys. It incorporates predicted compositions from ETR and NNR_4layers_Wen models for six target sets. The Fe content is shown to vary with target set values, specifically increasing when Ms and Cost parameters are adjusted.

caption: Isothermal entropy change as a function of temperature for the ORD sample under applied magnetic fields ranging from 1 T to 6 T.
summary: The isothermal entropy change for the ORD sample is plotted against temperature for applied magnetic fields between 1 T and 6 T. These curves characterize the magnetic behavior of the ORD sample, providing the necessary data to determine the full width at half maximum for calculating the material's refrigeration capacity.

caption: Regional feature importance analysis comparing the percentage contribution of various features to porosity prediction in core versus surface pixels.
summary: This feature importance plot illustrates the influence of specific variables on porosity prediction within core and surface regions. Analysis reveals that SL, MPA, MPT, and SG contribute more significantly to core pixel porosity, whereas CR, HI, and IT exert a greater influence on surface pixel porosity, highlighting distinct regional feature dependencies.

caption: Confusion matrix for the ResNet18 model, illustrating the classification performance across various defect categories in additive manufacturing.
summary: The confusion matrix for the ResNet18 model demonstrates consistent accuracy across all defect categories. Strong diagonal dominance within the matrix confirms reliable classification boundaries between distinct defect types, which is essential for ensuring effective automated quality control during additive manufacturing processes by minimizing misclassification errors across the evaluated defect classes.

caption: Bode-magnitude and Bode-phase plots characterizing the electrochemical impedance behavior of the DSS-7 and DSS-14 samples.
summary: Bode-magnitude and Bode-phase plots are presented to characterize the electrochemical response of the DSS-7 and DSS-14 samples. These plots, alongside the Nyquist data, provide a comprehensive view of the electrochemical behavior, with experimental data fitted using a dashed line to represent the electrochemical response of the sample surface.

caption: Absorption coefficient spectrum for a 30 mm thick sample with grading optimized for 2000-5000 Hz, comparing experimental and numerical results.
summary: This plot illustrates the absorption coefficient spectrum for a 30 mm thick sample with grading optimized for the 2000-5000 Hz range. The red measured lines and black dashed numerical lines demonstrate the performance of the optimized structure, highlighting the correlation between the design model and the physical test results.

caption: ODF φ2 section for α'' martensite in the 700-DS sample, exhibiting no significant orientation texture.
summary: The ODF section for α'' martensite in the 700-DS sample is presented here. Analysis of this section reveals that the martensitic phase yields no significant orientation texture, suggesting a random distribution of crystallographic orientations within the martensite phase following the applied heat treatment and processing conditions.

caption: Void denuded zone width in pure Fe plotted against inverse temperature, comparing measurements via average distance method (solid line) and slope variation (shaded band).
summary: This plot displays the void denuded zone width for pure Fe as a function of inverse temperature. Measurements utilize the average distance method and slope variation technique. Data points from 400–470 °C for 0.1 appm He/dpa irradiations show strong agreement with samples irradiated at 10 appm He/dpa.

caption: Electron microscopy image of a representative microneedle patch pore, captured from the side opposite to the needle tips to demonstrate structural integrity.
summary: The electron micrograph provides a detailed view of a representative pore within the microneedle patch. Captured from the side opposite the needle tips, the image confirms that all pores are unobstructed, demonstrating the high-quality fabrication and structural integrity of the 3D-printed device for its intended use.

caption: Surface mesh comparison between the tomography scan and the reference CAD model, color-coded by C2M signed distances to indicate geometric deviations.
summary: This panel displays a surface mesh comparison between the printed sandwich panel and its reference CAD model. The mesh is colored by C2M signed distances, where blue indicates inward deviations and red indicates outward deviations. Significant defects, shown in red, are located on the bottom surface of the top skin.

caption: Amount of terminal liquid present within the Fe-Cu-Ni ternary system, serving as a basis for estimating cracking susceptibility.
summary: The amount of terminal liquid in the Fe-Cu-Ni ternary system is mapped to evaluate material properties. Based on these calculated results, a map is generated to qualitatively estimate the cracking susceptibility of the alloys, facilitating a better understanding of the solidification characteristics and potential defects in this specific ternary system.

caption: Amplified bright-field TEM image of the δ-ferrite region, revealing dispersed sub-grain boundaries and curved dislocations.
summary: This magnified bright-field TEM image focuses on the δ-ferrite side of the interface. It reveals that sub-grain boundaries and curved dislocations are slightly dispersed within the δ-ferrite structure, providing detailed insight into the local defect distribution that characterizes the phase substructure in the R2 specimen.

caption: Additional snapshot from the electron tomography reconstruction revealing the morphology of WS2 layers, which reach lengths of up to 90 nm.
summary: Representing a snapshot from the reconstructed electron tomography data, this panel illustrates the morphology of the WS2 layers embedded in the acrylic resin. The analysis reveals that these layers can extend up to 90 nm in length, demonstrating the capability of ET to characterize the internal structure of SLA nanocomposites.

caption: 3D surface topography of the TiC-steel-based cermet wear track after sliding under a 10 N load at room temperature.
summary: Represented here is the 3D surface topography of the TiC-steel-based cermet wear track following a 10 N load application at room temperature. The image captures the structural changes and surface degradation patterns resulting from the increased mechanical load compared to the lower 5 N test condition.

caption: Detailed inspection of Zone 2 within the fracture surface of specimen HCF-M.
summary: This panel provides a detailed inspection of Zone 2 within the fracture surface of specimen HCF-M. By focusing on this specific area, the microscopy reveals distinct topographical features that help characterize the fracture behavior and material response observed in this particular section of the specimen.

caption: XGBoost model feature importance ranking, showing the gain or frequency-based contribution of features to the gradient boosting ensemble.
summary: XGBoost model feature importance is shown, detailing the contribution of features to the gradient boosting ensemble. This ranking identifies the most influential variables, reinforcing the study's findings that incorporating the interquartile range and kurtosis is vital for optimizing the predictive capabilities of the XGBoost algorithm in this context.

caption: Cycling performance of the D-3DP Si||NCM full-cell, with an inset photograph showing the battery powering lit bulbs.
summary: The D-3DP Si||NCM full-cell demonstrates an ultra-high initial areal capacity of 6.04 mAh cm-2 at 0.1 mA cm-2. It maintains a steady capacity of 3.68 mAh cm-2 after 70 cycles at 0.2 mA cm-2, while the inset photograph confirms its practical utility by successfully powering light-emitting bulbs.

caption: Sobol sensitivity analysis indices for the INV36-MK500 CGA transition, highlighting the relative contributions of individual elements to property variability.
summary: This Sobol sensitivity analysis for the INV36-MK500 transition quantifies the influence of various input parameters on material variability. The indices indicate that iron and aluminum are the dominant contributors to the observed property fluctuations in these complex concentrated alloys, providing critical insights into the underlying drivers of the transition.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for AA2024 powder, illustrating the frequency of various particle diameters.
summary: The particle size distribution for the AA2024 powder is presented in this histogram. By quantifying the diameter distribution, this plot allows for a direct comparison of the physical characteristics between the AA2024 and Ti6Al4V powders. This analysis is critical for understanding the influence of powder size on the subsequent processing results.

caption: EDS line scanning profile across the SiC particle and AZ31 matrix interface in the TS4-AGFR5 sample.
summary: EDS line scanning analysis of the TS4-AGFR5 sample demonstrates the chemical composition profile across the SiC particle and AZ31 matrix interface. The results confirm the presence of a transition zone, which enables the effective transfer of load from the matrix to the SiC particles, contributing to material strengthening.

caption: Implied open-circuit voltage (iV OC) calibrated photoluminescence images of the non-metallised precursor surface after the LCO process.
summary: Calibrated photoluminescence imaging reveals the iV OC distribution across the non-metallised precursor after LCO treatment. Observations indicate no significant differences in iV OC between LCO and control regions, confirming that the 257 nm fs UV laser effectively removes SiN X layers without damaging the underlying SiO 2 /poly-Si passivation.

caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 25% hemp content mix, demonstrating a bell-shaped curve with a substantial decrease in mean and median values.
summary: The 25% hemp content mix exhibits a bell-shaped probability distribution that shows a particularly pronounced decrease in both mean and median values. This shift signifies the substantial influence of increased hemp content on the global warming potential, as determined through the Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis performed on the mix design.

caption: Ultimate strength comparison for dot-45 specimens using design yield strength (fyd) across CL and EC0 approaches.
summary: Ultimate strength values for dot-45 specimens are shown here, comparing the CL approach for different CI amplitudes with the EC0 approach and percentile data. The analysis is conducted using the design yield strength (fyd), illustrating the performance variations across the different analytical approaches for this specimen type.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of relative melt pool area (MPA) versus porosity, displaying an hourglass-shaped distribution that highlights the dual role of melt pool size in influencing porosity.
summary: The scatter diagram for relative melt pool area reveals a complex, hourglass-shaped relationship with porosity. The data indicates that melt pool area can contribute to either increasing or decreasing porosity, reflecting competing physical effects. Certain regions show larger melt pool areas contributing to a reduction in porosity, while others increase it.

caption: Temperature sweeps of storage modulus for PMMA/PEG/ATBC feedstocks prepared at 30 rpm, showing consistent mechanical performance across varying ATBC levels.
summary: Temperature sweeps illustrate the storage modulus behavior for PMMA/PEG/ATBC feedstocks compounded at 30 rpm. The analysis confirms that the storage modulus for all tested filaments consistently exceeds 600 MPa at 25 °C, indicating stable mechanical performance across the different ATBC content variations included in the feedstock formulations.

caption: Storage and loss modulus curves for PLA-PBAT-Joncryl measured at 185 °C, showing an intersection of G′ and G″ at 2 rad/s.
summary: The PLA-PBAT-Joncryl sample exhibits storage and loss modulus curves measured at 185 °C. A distinct crossover between G′ and G″ occurs at a frequency of 2 rad/s, which is attributed to the shape relaxation of PBAT droplets within the polymer matrix at these low frequencies.

caption: Hydrogen discharging behavior of Mg68Ni26M5X powder at 350 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the hydrogen discharging curve for Mg68Ni26M5X powder at 350 °C. The data, captured via the MFM system, highlights the material's discharge performance. Thermal treatment above 300 °C is shown to be critical for the activation of the compound, facilitating the observed hydrogen release characteristics in this study.

caption: Tensile failure stress of aramid filaments versus FDM print radius, showing the percentage of strength retained relative to the straight filament condition.
summary: Aramid filament tensile failure stress is analyzed in relation to the FDM print radius. The panel displays the percentage of retained strength for curved filaments compared to straight ones, providing a clear metric for how print curvature influences the mechanical integrity and failure stress of the aramid material.

caption: Power-Voltage (P-V) characteristic curve comparing the ADIPSO-VC optimization results against experimental FDM data for the KC200-GT SPVM material.
summary: This plot displays the P-V characteristic curve for the KC200-GT SPVM material, comparing experimental FDM data with results derived from the ADIPSO-VC optimization method. The ADIPSO-VC approach demonstrates superior performance by producing specific outcomes with the lowest RMSD value when compared to other constraints used in the analysis.

caption: Glass transition temperature (Tg) analysis of 3D-printed PEEK under scCO2 conditions, comparing pristine (155.48 °C) and aged (156.84 °C) samples.
summary: Glass transition temperature (Tg) analysis of 3D-printed PEEK under scCO2 conditions, comparing pristine (155.48 °C) and aged (156.84 °C) samples. The data demonstrates that there are no substantial changes in the glass transition temperature for the 3D-printed PEEK samples under the current scCO2 aging conditions.

caption: Final spatial temperature variation along the middle axis of the ceramic tile body at 290 minutes of sintering.
summary: Concluding the sequence at 290 minutes, this heatmap illustrates the spatial temperature variation along the middle axis of the ceramic tile body. It provides a final view of the thermal distribution within the ceramic material at the end of the 1200 °C sintering process.

caption: Distribution of normalized additive manufacturing (AM) intensity across the German firm population in 2023.
summary: This histogram illustrates the distribution of normalized AM intensities among German firms in 2023. The data reveals a distinct right-skewed distribution, characterized by a high frequency of firms exhibiting very low intensity values. This visualization confirms that the majority of the analyzed population maintains low levels of AM adoption.

caption: Non-isothermal dilatometric measurement curve for the homogenized sample.
summary: This panel displays the non-isothermal dilatometric measurement performed on the homogenized sample. The curve provides essential thermal expansion or contraction data, serving as a baseline for understanding the material's dimensional stability under varying temperature conditions during the non-isothermal heating process described in the study.

caption: Gd elemental mapping of the 1Gd as-cast alloy surface, indicating that Gd is almost undetected within the corrosion products.
summary: Gd elemental mapping for the 1Gd as-cast alloy shows that Gadolinium is nearly absent from the corrosion products. This finding indicates that at low Gd concentrations, the formation of a protective Gd2O3 film is minimal or insufficient to be detected by EDS mapping on the alloy surface.

caption: Pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram of 420 martensitic stainless steel calculated via Thermo-Calc, illustrating phase stability as a function of carbon weight percentage.
summary: This pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram for 420 martensitic stainless steel, generated using Thermo-Calc, demonstrates the influence of carbon content on phase stability. It highlights critical transformations, including the primary solidification of δ-ferrite, subsequent solid-state δ→γ transformation, carbide precipitation, and austenite decomposition, which collectively define the alloy's equilibrium microstructure.

caption: SHAP value distribution for KW connections processed via LMD.
summary: This panel displays the SHAP values for KW connections fabricated using the LMD process. The magnitude and sign of these values indicate the strength and direction of each feature's effect on the model output, providing insight into how specific parameters influence the LMD manufacturing results for KW connections.

caption: Galvanostatic cycling performance of the Li/PVDF-LLZTO CPE/Li symmetric cell evaluated under varying current densities up to 0.4 mA/cm².
summary: Evaluating the electrochemical performance under varying current densities reveals the remarkable stability of the printed electrolyte. The symmetric cell maintains consistent voltage performance even at elevated current densities of 0.4 mA/cm², successfully avoiding catastrophic short-circuit failure and demonstrating the material's suitability for high-rate applications in lithium metal battery systems.

caption: 3D contour mapping of reflection loss for Fe10 composite.
summary: The 3D contour mapping of reflection loss for the Fe10 composite provides a visual representation of the absorption performance across different frequencies and thicknesses. This mapping quantifies the electromagnetic absorption enhancement, serving as a baseline for comparing the performance of the Fe/PLA/TPU composites as Fe loading increases.

caption: Depth-dependent hardness measurements for W-Zr-B coatings on LP AM Inconel 617 substrates, highlighting differences between virgin, RT irradiated, and 400 °C irradiated samples tested at 1mN load.
summary: Hardness as a function of depth is presented for W-Zr-B coatings on LP AM Inconel 617 substrates. The data contrasts the mechanical performance of virgin samples with those implanted with ions at room temperature and 400 °C, specifically evaluated through nanoindentation testing at a constant 1mN load.

caption: Cracking sensitivity of K417G alloy deposits processed with parameters 5, 6, and 12 across varying preheating temperatures, illustrating three distinct stages of cracking behavior.
summary: This plot evaluates the cracking sensitivity of K417G samples across different processing parameters and preheating temperatures. The data reveals three distinct stages of cracking behavior, providing a quantitative assessment of how thermal conditions and parameter selection influence the structural integrity of the deposited material during the fabrication process.

caption: UV-vis optical absorbance, transmittance, and reflectance spectra of MgZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles measured at ambient temperature across the 350–1150 nm wavelength range.
summary: The optical properties of MgZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles are characterized via UV-vis spectroscopy. The figure displays the absorbance, transmittance, and reflectance spectra collected at room temperature within the 350–1150 nm wavelength range, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's interaction with light across the measured spectral region.

caption: Principal component analysis of spatter ejection direction, with samples color-coded by their specific ejection angles.
summary: Principal component analysis of spatter ejection direction reveals distinct clustering patterns when samples are colored by ejection angle. Analysis indicates that larger ejection angles correlate with higher scanning speeds, which implies a lower input energy during the process, further supported by the high variance explained by the first two components.

caption: Residual charge amount measured as a function of applied voltage for NEFD versus EHD jet printing.
summary: This graph illustrates the relationship between applied voltage and residual charge accumulation. The results show that NEFD jet micro 3D printing produces significantly lower levels of residual charge compared to EHD jet printing as the voltage increases, indicating superior electric field stability and reduced charge-related interference.

caption: Fundamental zone of axis-angle space showing the disorientation distribution for the hexagonal η phase and hexagonal C14 Laves phase combination.
summary: Represented here is the fundamental zone of axis-angle space for the hexagonal η phase and hexagonal C14 Laves phase interface. The plot maps the specific disorientations found in the study, characterizing the crystallographic relationship between these two hexagonal structures as part of the broader analysis of C14 Laves phase microstructures.

caption: Azimuthally integrated 2D SAXS pattern obtained from sample nr 1, displaying distinct streaks indicative of aligned precipitates or ordered dislocation structures.
summary: This panel displays the 2D SAXS pattern for sample number 1, processed via the pyFAI library. The azimuthally integrated data reveals prominent streaks, which are interpreted as evidence of either aligned precipitates or ordered dislocation networks within the material structure, highlighting the anisotropic nature of the sample's scattering profile.

caption: Instantaneous tracer trajectory visualization for the Ar [Ti+Ta] 75-106 High sample, illustrating distinct movement patterns color-coded by direction and pore interaction.
summary: This visualization displays the instantaneous tracer trajectory within the Ar [Ti+Ta] 75-106 High sample. Green and white paths represent counterclockwise movement, while magenta paths indicate backward and downward motion. Light and dark blue paths denote forward movement, providing a clear example of tracer directionality changes during the simulation process.

caption: Surface plot of the interface zone, evaluating the mutual effects of scan speed and power on cobalt elemental concentration.
summary: Focusing on the interface zone, this surface plot evaluates the combined impact of scan speed and laser power on cobalt concentration. It serves to characterize the elemental behavior at the interface, providing insight into how these critical processing parameters dictate the resulting elemental distribution and accumulation patterns.

caption: Fluorescence intensity of fusion peptide solutions measured after 3 days of incubation at varying concentrations.
summary: The remaining fluorescence intensity of each group of fusion peptides after 3 days of incubation is displayed. This measurement helps quantify the concentration-dependent behavior of the peptides. Error bars represent the mean ± SD for n = 3, with statistical significance indicated by p-values.

caption: Micro-computed tomography reconstructions of lattice-structured parts sintered at 1445 °C and 1455 °C, illustrating the spatial distribution and morphology of internal pores.
summary: Micro-computed tomography reconstructions reveal the internal pore structures of lattice-structured parts sintered at 1445 °C and 1455 °C. These visualizations demonstrate how varying sintering temperatures modulate the extent of melting, which is critical for achieving full densification and minimizing porosity in the final sintered components.

caption: Taylor factor distribution map for the iHEA-V sample, calculated for uniaxial tension assuming {111} <110> slip systems in an fcc structure.
summary: Presented as a Taylor factor distribution map, this panel characterizes the iHEA-V sample before it undergoes deformation. The map was plotted based on the assumption of a uniaxial tensile test and the activation of {111} <110> slip systems within the fcc lattice, mapping the mechanical orientation factor spatially.

caption: Comparative micro-Raman spectra of worn products found on NiW-ED coatings (blue) and the pin (orange) after 10,000 laps.
summary: Micro-Raman spectroscopy is utilized here to examine the worn products on NiW-ED coatings and the corresponding pin after 10,000 wear laps. The spectra reveal the chemical nature of the wear debris, facilitating an understanding of the surface transformation and interaction between the electrodeposited NiW coating and the counterbody during sliding contact.

caption: Projected density of states for surface Fe atoms on the Fe(111) crystal surface, showing a calculated d-band center of −2.27 eV.
summary: This panel displays the projected density of states for surface Fe atoms on the Fe(111) surface. The electronic structure analysis reveals a d-band center located at −2.27 eV. This specific electronic configuration serves as a baseline for comparing the catalytic properties of pure metal surfaces against bimetallic Fe-Ni systems.

caption: Component analysis spectrum of the Al2Gd phase particles.
summary: Component analysis via EDS confirms the chemical composition of the blocky Al2Gd phase. The data indicates that these particles are primarily composed of Al, Gd, and Y. The atomic concentration of aluminum is found to be approximately double that of the gadolinium and yttrium elements present in the phase.

caption: Modification of the Rex12Cfz1 parameter as a function of m and M, illustrating the influence of the Hall effect on shear stress at the upper plate under a constant magnetic field.
summary: This plot displays the modification of the Rex12Cfz1 parameter relative to variables m and M. It demonstrates that the Hall effect significantly enhances the shear stress at the upper plate when the magnetic field is maintained at a constant value, highlighting the magneto-mechanical coupling within the system.

caption: Expansion force curve and deformation sequence of the expansion tube during the mechanical test.
summary: The expansion force curve illustrates the mechanical response of the expansion tube, revealing four distinct deformation stages. Due to large-area tearing, the load drops sharply after reaching the peak force, and no force platform is observed, indicating significant structural failure during the expansion process.

caption: Electron probe micro-analysis map illustrating the spatial distribution of Carbon (C) across the liquation crack region, including quantitative analysis results in the bottom-right corner.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis map illustrating the spatial distribution of Carbon (C) across the liquation crack region, including quantitative analysis results in the bottom-right corner. This map is part of a comprehensive elemental analysis performed to investigate the composition of the liquation crack, which is associated with the solidification of low melting point compounds.

caption: Load-penetration response of isotropic GRF-A lattice sandwich structure at 20% relative density, first random realization (r1), showing characteristic sharp peaks and valleys.
summary: The load-penetration response of the isotropic GRF-A lattice sandwich structure is depicted for the first random realization at 20% relative density. The curve is characterized by sharp peaks and valleys, which result from the progressive collapse and densification of the spinodoid lattice core during the impact event.

caption: Side-view schematic drawing of the CT specimen, including the 12.5 mm electro-discharge machined starter notch dimensions.
summary: This side-view schematic details the CT specimen geometry, explicitly labeling the 12.5 mm electro-discharge machined starter notch. The diagram provides critical dimensional data necessary for understanding the specimen preparation and the initial crack configuration prior to the fatigue pre-cracking process conducted at room temperature.

caption: Confusion matrix evaluating the classification performance of the ResNet-18 and Bidirectional LSTM model across the handwritten letter dataset.
summary: The confusion matrix provides a quantitative assessment of the classification task performance. It visualizes the accuracy of the ResNet-18 and Bidirectional LSTM model in correctly identifying handwritten letters, highlighting the model's ability to distinguish between different characters based on the extracted spatiotemporal features from the voltage signals.

caption: Overview of the Aconity Mini PBF system featuring the modular platform cylinder and the integrated water-cooled base plate.
summary: This photograph displays the Aconity Mini powder bed fusion system, highlighting the modular platform cylinder and the water-cooled base plate. The setup is designed to manage thermal conditions during the printing process, as the base plate cooling helps mitigate temperature rises caused by high energy laser input during build jobs.

caption: Constricted geometry model designed in Abaqus/CAE 2021 for finite element thermal analysis.
summary: This panel displays the constricted geometry model created using Abaqus/CAE 2021. The design serves as the basis for part-scale finite element thermal analysis, ensuring the virtual model dimensions accurately reflect the physical samples built for the study, facilitating precise thermal behavior predictions during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Cycling performance evaluation of a pouch cell configured with the Ni-Cu@C/HC separator.
summary: Cycling performance of the pouch cell utilizing the Ni-Cu@C/HC separator is presented. This plot demonstrates the practical application and stability of the separator in a pouch cell format, showing its ability to maintain electrochemical performance over repeated charge-discharge cycles in a larger-scale device configuration.

caption: FTIR spectra of LPNC samples synthesized with varying AL content, showing intensity changes at 1655 cm⁻¹ and 1630 cm⁻¹.
summary: This panel displays FTIR spectra for LPNC samples with varying AL concentrations. Analysis reveals that the intensities of absorption peaks at 1655 cm⁻¹ and 1630 cm⁻¹ increase as the mass ratio of AL to DA-PEG increases, indicating a direct correlation between precursor ratios and the resulting chemical structure.

caption: Schematic representation of the 2 × 2 × 2 fcc supercell SQS configuration, containing 20 Ni atoms, 10 Cr atoms, one impurity atom, and one vacancy, with highlighted nearest-neighbor atoms.
summary: This schematic illustrates the 2 × 2 × 2 fcc supercell SQS model, which includes 20 Ni atoms, 10 Cr atoms, one impurity, and one vacancy. The visualization highlights the nearest-neighbor atoms surrounding the impurity and vacancy, which are critical for defining the four distinctive rotation hops within the quasi-random structure.

caption: Bright-field TEM image highlighting the Cr2N phase as small black dots and identifying a distinct small white region within the alloy matrix.
summary: This TEM micrograph displays the FeCoCrNiMn-(N,Si) alloy microstructure, where small black dots represent the Cr2N phase. A specific small white region, indicated by a red arrow, is identified for further high-resolution investigation to characterize the local structural features formed during the tensile deformation process at 573 K.

caption: Failure Assessment Diagram (FAD) for 82 SENB specimens of granite and limestone, illustrating the fracture mechanics behavior under varying constraint levels.
summary: This FAD assessment displays the fracture mechanics results for 82 SENB specimens composed of granite and limestone. The data highlights the influence of specimen constraint, noting that plates with low a/W ratios of 0.25 experience lower constraint levels, which yields more conservative results compared to traditional high-constrained fracture mechanics specimens.

caption: Higher magnification TEM image of the martensite region viewed along the [011]α′ zone axis, revealing the internal nano-twinned substructure.
summary: A closer examination of the α′-laths reveals a distinct nano-twinned substructure, which is a typical hierarchical feature of high-carbon martensite. This higher magnification TEM image, taken close to the [011]α′ zone axis, provides detailed insight into the internal arrangement of the martensitic phase within the material's harder region.

caption: Optical micrograph of the as-cast 1Zr-1Y alloy microstructure, etched with Keller’s Reagent, revealing the distribution of the equiaxed α-Al matrix.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the as-cast microstructure of the 1Zr-1Y alloy after etching with Keller’s Reagent. The image highlights the presence of an equiaxed α-Al matrix, which is a characteristic feature of the initial as-cast state of this material composition as observed through optical microscopy analysis.

caption: Atomic configuration of the A3 supercell model, utilizing a special quasi-random structure (SQS) to simulate random Ti/Zr distribution at the 3f and 3g sites.
summary: The A3 supercell model incorporates atomic randomness at the 3f and 3g sites using the special quasi-random structure (SQS) method. This approach provides a realistic simulation of disordered Ti/Zr distributions, which is essential for assessing the stability of the S2 structure under conditions of partial atomic disorder.

caption: Magnetic free energy F mag of fcc Co calculated via Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: Depicting the magnetic free energy F mag for fcc cobalt, this panel is derived from Monte Carlo simulation data. It provides a quantitative view of the free energy landscape for the fcc phase, supporting the comprehensive evaluation of magnetic stability and thermodynamic properties of cobalt as discussed in the research.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the ATZ641-350E32 sample, revealing the presence of fine Mg2Sn precipitates.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging of the ATZ641-350E32 sample provides high-resolution visualization of the precipitate phases. The image reveals the presence of fine Mg2Sn precipitates, which coexist with Mg17Al12 precipitates along the grain boundaries and within the grain interiors of the alloy.

caption: Square wave voltammetry responses of MN sensor arrays secured with super glue, exhibiting improved but incomplete retention with approximately 80% signal loss.
summary: Deploying super glue around the device edges provides better retention than medical tape but fails to prevent MN retraction over the measurement period. Square wave voltammetry data indicates that while this strategy slows down sensor detachment, it still results in approximately 80% signal loss during the in vivo testing duration.

caption: SAXS diffractograms of 30% w/v PCL2-b-PEO2.1-b-PCL2 hydrogel recorded during heating at 2 °C/min.
summary: This panel presents the SAXS scattering profile for the 30% w/v linear triblock copolymer hydrogel PCL2-b-PEO2.1-b-PCL2. The data were obtained during a heating ramp of 2 °C/min, allowing for the observation of structural changes within the hydrogel network as the temperature rises throughout the experiment.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) comparison between Co@NC and NiCo@NC with 50% Ni concentration, highlighting electronic state shifts near the Fermi level.
summary: A comparison of the projected density of states for Co@NC and NiCo@NC with 50% Ni concentration reveals the impact of alloying on electronic structure. The results demonstrate an enhancement of localized electronic states close to the Fermi level, which is attributed to the alloying effect in the bimetallic system.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material disk containing a combination of Atto425, Atto465, and Atto565 dyes, with each section measuring 0.5 mm in thickness.
summary: This panel displays the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed multi-material sample composed of three distinct dyes: Atto425, Atto465, and Atto565. Each section of the disk has a thickness of 0.5 mm, illustrating the spectral characteristics of this specific multi-material combination within the printed structure.

caption: Comparison of experimental and simulated temperature values at four specific points (P1 through P4) on the sample surface.
summary: This line graph directly compares experimental and simulated temperature data at four distinct locations, P1 to P4. The plot demonstrates the level of agreement between the measured thermal response and the numerical simulation, confirming the reliability of the model in predicting temperature variations across the scanned surface.

caption: Three-dimensional surface profile visualization of the inkjet-printed PEDOT:PSS conductive lines, demonstrating the topographical morphology achieved through the printing process.
summary: The 3D surface profile provides a detailed topographical view of the inkjet-printed PEDOT:PSS lines. This visualization confirms the successful deposition and structural morphology of the conductive electrodes, which are essential components of the ferroelectric memory crossbar architecture described in the device fabrication process.

caption: TEM micrograph of the θ′ phase in the inoculated alloy after a tensile test at 453 K and a strain rate of 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, including an inset SAED pattern.
summary: Following tensile testing at 453 K, the inoculated alloy displays an average θ′ precipitate length of approximately 79.0 nm. The inset SAED pattern identifies the α-Al and θ′ phases. The refined precipitate size compared to the uninoculated alloy contributes to the superior high-temperature tensile performance observed in the inoculated material.

caption: Tabulated performance metrics for the half-sinusoid arch, including neutral axis coordinates, tension/compression centroids, cross-sectional stress profiles, and longitudinal S-11 tensile stress distribution.
summary: Numerical data for the half-sinusoid arch indicates a mechanical response analogous to the rectangular beam. The neutral axis coincides with the geometric centroid, resulting in a linear stress profile across the depth. Maximum tensile stress is observed at the beam midpoint, consistent with the behavior of standard rectangular beam geometries.

caption: Relationship between ultimate tensile strength and total elongation, benchmarking the present sandwich structures against various WAAMed low carbon low alloy high-strength steels.
summary: This plot maps the ultimate tensile strength against total elongation to benchmark the current sandwich structures against existing WAAMed low carbon low alloy high-strength steels. It includes comparative data from various studies, such as C-Mn-Si, C-Mn-Si-Mo, and C-Mn-Si-Ni-Cr-Mo steels, to demonstrate the relative mechanical performance of the designed materials.

caption: Raman spectra of the three CNF variants, displaying the characteristic D and G bands used to evaluate molecular structure and defect density.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is performed to compare the molecular structures of the three CNF types. The spectra display the characteristic D and G bands, which are essential for evaluating the graphitic quality and defect density of the materials. This comparative analysis complements the XRD and FTIR data to characterize the CNFs.

caption: Remanence-to-saturation ratio (Mr/Ms) of the Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixture plotted against annealing temperature.
summary: The relationship between the Mr/Ms ratio and annealing temperature is illustrated for the Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixture. This ratio serves as an important magnetic parameter, reflecting the evolution of the material's magnetic characteristics and the efficiency of the magnetization retention as a function of the applied thermal annealing treatment.

caption: EDX line profile plot illustrating the elemental distribution across the oxide layer, revealing enrichment of Nb and Mo alongside minor concentrations of Ti, Cr, and Fe.
summary: The EDX line profile analysis conducted within the passive layer confirms the presence of oxides enriched with Nb and Mo. The data also identifies minor quantities of Ti, Cr, and Fe, providing a detailed compositional characterization of the oxide layer structure as indicated by the line scan path.

caption: Radar diagram illustrating the relative performance of various Metal Additive Manufacturing (MAM) processes across multiple evaluation criteria.
summary: This radar diagram provides a comparative performance assessment of different MAM processes. By averaging scaled scores for each criterion, the visualization ensures a balanced evaluation. It serves as a foundational guide for SMEs to conduct nuanced assessments of MAM technologies, highlighting the distinct advantages and challenges inherent in each process.

caption: Ni 2p3/2 XPS spectra of the mechanical polished specimen after exposure to high-temperature, high-pressure deaerated deionized water at 250 ℃ for 2 min, demonstrating oxide cleaning after 30 s of sputtering.
summary: This panel presents the Ni 2p3/2 XPS spectra for the mechanical polished specimen. Analysis of the peak variations during the sputtering process indicates that Ni oxides were successfully cleaned from the surface after 30 seconds of Ar+ sputtering, following exposure to high-temperature, high-pressure deaerated deionized water.

caption: Measured transmission spectrum of the CuCrZr sample along the build direction compared against the theoretical CuCrZr spectrum.
summary: This panel displays the transmission spectrum for the CuCrZr specimen obtained via FOBI reconstruction. The measured data is plotted alongside the theoretical spectrum for the CuCrZr alloy. This analysis, performed along the build direction, serves as a baseline for evaluating the material's structural characteristics and texture properties.

caption: X-ray reflectivity data and corresponding best-fit curve for Ni-Zr thin alloy films annealed at 200 °C, with an inset displaying the electron scattering length density profile.
summary: X-ray reflectivity data for Ni-Zr thin alloy films annealed at 200 °C are presented as open circles with solid lines representing best fits. The inset shows the electron scattering length density profile, which is a function of the atomic number density, illustrating the film's electron density and thickness characteristics.

caption: Shape recovery performance of 3mm thick springs over 25 cycles, showing the average recovery trend and a 90% confidence interval.
summary: This panel illustrates the durability of 3mm thick springs through a 25-cycle shape recovery test. The data, represented by an average recovery line with a 90% confidence interval, demonstrates the material's consistent mechanical response over repeated loading cycles, confirming the structural reliability of the 4D-printed components under cyclic deformation.

caption: Optical transmission spectra of magnetron sputtered films S0, S3, and S15 measured across the 300–2500 nm wavelength range, illustrating the transition from metallic behavior in S0 to semiconductor or insulator characteristics in S3 and S15.
summary: Transmission spectra for magnetron sputtered films S0, S3, and S15 are displayed across the 300–2500 nm range. Sample S0 exhibits metallic characteristics with complete absorption, while samples S3 and S15 demonstrate semiconductor or insulator behavior. These optical measurements highlight the distinct electronic properties resulting from varying oxygen flow rates during deposition.

caption: Pie chart illustrating the total distribution of recyclable waste weight percentage across surgical subspecialties, highlighting that arthroplasty surgery contributes the highest proportion at 39.04%, followed by oncology at 30.67% and trauma at 30.29%.
summary: This pie chart displays the total recyclable waste weight percentage across different surgical subspecialties. Arthroplasty surgery is identified as the primary contributor to recyclable waste production at 39.04%, while oncology and trauma surgeries account for 30.67% and 30.29% of the total waste, respectively, providing a clear overview of waste distribution.

caption: Fatigue life data of AMZ4 bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) plotted as a function of equivalent von Mises stress amplitude across various loading conditions.
summary: This plot displays the observed fatigue cycles to failure for AMZ4 BMG samples under different loading conditions. The data is presented as a function of the equivalent von Mises stress amplitude, revealing that this parameter fails to reasonably predict fatigue life specifically under pure torsion and non-proportional loading scenarios.

caption: Creep strain evolution measured via strain markers for grains G1–G18 at 750 °C and 750 MPa.
summary: Creep strain evolution along the loading direction is evaluated for grains G1 through G18 at 750 °C and 750 MPa. These measurements, derived from strain marker tests, reveal distinct strain evolution patterns across individual grains, contributing to an overall strain fluctuation of approximately 1% early in the creep process.

caption: Hardness values measured for Cu-10Ni-xTi alloy samples following 2 hours of aging at temperatures ranging from 400 °C to 500 °C.
summary: Hardness measurements for the Cu-10Ni-xTi alloy are shown following 2 hours of aging at 400 °C, 450 °C, and 500 °C. The data reflects the influence of Ti chemical composition and thermal aging on the material's resistance to indentation, providing insight into the mechanical hardening behavior of the alloy.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the 18R-type LPSO phase observed in the EME3N alloy.
summary: The SAED pattern provides diffraction evidence for the 18R-type LPSO phase identified in the EME3N alloy. By analyzing the diffraction spots, the pattern confirms the long-period stacking ordered nature of the block-shaped phases found at the grain boundaries, consistent with the observed 1.6 nm lattice fringe spacing.

caption: Energy dispersive spectroscopy point analyses identifying specific phases in Alloy 2, including Ni4B3 in zone A, WB4 in zone B, and W2B5 in zone C.
summary: Energy dispersive spectroscopy point analyses performed on Alloy 2 identify three distinct phases: Ni4B3 in zone A, WB4 in zone B, and W2B5 in zone C. These findings are significant as they confirm the phase composition and highlight the partial decomposition of the WB4 phase observed during the material's processing.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of pristine Ni wire cross-section showing elongated grains oriented along the wire axis, with dimensions exceeding 1 μm in length and approximately 200 nm in width.
summary: Pristine Ni wire cross-section imaged via bright-field STEM reveals elongated grains along the wire direction. These grains, measuring over 1 μm long and 200 nm wide, are attributed to the wire drawing process, providing a baseline structural characterization before immersion in molten ZnCl2 at 593 K.

caption: Partitioning procedure executed on the preprocessed data to organize inputs for parallel model training.
summary: Following the preprocessing phase, the data undergoes a partitioning process. This step organizes the preprocessed original and residual data into segments suitable for parallel execution, facilitating the efficient distribution of computational tasks across multiple machines in the next stage of the proposed training pipeline.

caption: Atomic structural model representing the illite (YLS) mineral phase.
summary: This panel presents the atomic structural model of illite, referred to as YLS. The visualization depicts the layered atomic arrangement typical of this clay mineral, offering a clear structural representation that aids in identifying the crystalline features of illite within the analyzed material system.

caption: Classification table organizing the SA2+x samples based on their specific microstructure conditions.
summary: This panel provides a systematic classification of the individual SA2+x samples according to their respective microstructure conditions. It serves as a reference guide to organize and categorize the various precipitation hardening states observed throughout the experimental study.

caption: Fluorescence images of RAW264.7 cells stained with Hoechst 33,342 and DCFH-DA, illustrating intracellular ROS production under various scaffold treatments.
summary: RAW264.7 cells treated with PLA/GA and PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF scaffolds exhibit the lowest intracellular ROS production. This is indicated by reduced green fluorescence in the DCFH-DA stained images, demonstrating the anti-inflammatory potential of the scaffolds under inflammatory activation conditions.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profile showing potential evolution over time under constant current intensity.
summary: Galvanostatic charging and discharging are depicted here as a method for characterizing supercapacitors. By applying a constant current intensity, the system's potential is measured as a function of time. This profile provides essential data regarding the charge storage capacity and electrochemical stability of the supercapacitor under controlled operating conditions.

caption: Dilatometric curve and its corresponding derivative for the ZrSiO4/Al2O3 composite material, illustrating the densification behavior of green parts produced via slip casting.
summary: This dilatometric analysis characterizes the densification behavior of ZrSiO4/Al2O3 composite green parts fabricated through slip casting. The figure presents the primary dilatometric curve alongside its derivative, providing essential data on the thermal expansion and shrinkage characteristics of the material during the sintering process to evaluate its densification performance.

caption: Subsurface plot of the Fukui index f+ for BPA, highlighting regions prone to nucleophilic attack.
summary: The f+ Fukui index subsurface plot highlights atomic regions in BPA that are prone to nucleophilic attacks. Atoms exhibiting higher f+ values are identified as more vulnerable to damage by specific reactive species like hydroxyl radicals. This analysis helps in predicting the chemical stability and degradation behavior of the BPA molecule.

caption: Representative force–displacement curves for the I-2A TPMS sample, highlighting the linear regression analysis performed on the elastic portion of the data for each repetition.
summary: This plot illustrates the force–displacement behavior of the I-2A TPMS sample across three repetitions. By identifying the initial linear portion of the curve corresponding to the elastic deformation regime, a linear regression is applied to calculate the elastic stiffness, providing a consistent method for evaluating the mechanical response of the structure.

caption: Calculated vacancy migration barriers in pure Ni at 1573 K plotted against varying uniaxial stress states along the [001] direction, including comparisons to previous elasticity theory (ELT) results.
summary: This panel displays the calculated vacancy migration barriers for pure Ni at 1573 K under different uniaxial stress states along the [001] axis. The data shows a linear trend with stress, except at 5 GPa compression, aligning well with elasticity theory predictions and providing a basis for understanding migration trajectory changes.

caption: Overlaid EDS false-color map illustrating the elemental distribution across the oxidized A600 surface, highlighting Si enrichment adjacent to Cr-enriched oxide regions.
summary: This overlaid EDS false-color map visualizes the elemental distribution on the steam-oxidized A600 surface. The mapping confirms the presence of Cr-enriched oxide regions and identifies Si enrichment occurring specifically in the areas adjacent to these Cr-rich oxide zones, providing insight into the chemical composition of the oxidized surface layer.

caption: Inhibition zone assays showing bacterial growth suppression around PEEK, 40%HA-PEEK, and 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK samples cultivated with S. aureus and E. coli.
summary: Inhibition ring assays demonstrate clear zones of bacterial growth suppression surrounding the 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK samples. While a tiny inhibition ring exists for the 40%HA-PEEK group, the silver-doped composite exhibits a more pronounced and obvious inhibited zone, indicating superior anti-bacterial activity against both S. aureus and E. coli strains.

caption: Relationship between grain size reduction (GR%) and the percentage reduction in specific wear rate (SWR) for samples containing various reinforcing particles, relative to the WAAM sample.
summary: This panel presents the direct correlation between grain size reduction and the improvement in specific wear rate (SWR) for various reinforcing particles. It demonstrates that refining the grain structure through specific reinforcements effectively enhances wear resistance, providing a clear link between microstructural modification and the resulting mechanical performance improvements.
