caption: Phase image loaded onto the PLM for pixel alignment in the horizontal orientation, featuring a central region with a phase value of π, spanning 400 pixels in length and 4 pixels in width.
summary: This phase image is loaded onto the PLM to facilitate precise pixel alignment in the horizontal orientation. The pattern exhibits a distinct central region characterized by a phase value of π, which measures 400 pixels in length and 4 pixels in width, serving as a reference for the optical system alignment.

caption: Dislocation length density evolution as a function of irradiation dose for single-crystal and bicrystal NiCoFe at 580 °C.
summary: This plot displays the evolution of dislocation length density in NiCoFe under irradiation at 580 °C. Comparing single-crystal and bicrystal configurations, the data demonstrates that the presence of a Σ 5 (210) grain boundary leads to a reduction in dislocation length density for irradiation doses up to approximately 0.11 dpa.

caption: Atomic structural model representing the N-A-S-H gel phase.
summary: This panel displays the atomic structural model of the N-A-S-H gel phase. The visualization provides a detailed representation of the atomic arrangement within the N-A-S-H structure, serving as a reference for understanding the structural characteristics of this specific binder phase within the context of the study.

caption: Normalized S/N curve for MMJ SS316L samples showing the estimated fatigue limit and experimental run-out data.
summary: This normalized S/N curve for MMJ SS316L samples displays the estimated fatigue limit alongside experimental data. Most failed samples appear above the normal line, while run-outs fall below. The plot identifies two specific failures below the endurance limit, with the estimated value showing a 2.9% difference from the average run-out stress.

caption: Dark field TEM image of VDM® Alloy 780 after hot deformation at 1000 °C and cooling at 10 °C/min, showing γ′ precipitates with an average size of approximately 60 nm.
summary: This dark field TEM image displays VDM® Alloy 780 following hot deformation at 1000 °C and a slow cooling rate of 10 °C/min. Image analysis reveals that the γ′ precipitates exhibit an average size of approximately 60 nm, which is notably larger than the corresponding diffraction-derived average of 43 nm.

caption: High-resolution neutron diffraction patterns and LeBail fits for Haynes 282 in heat-treated and bar material states, alongside heat-treated IN 718, with markers identifying γ matrix, γ' phase, and δ phase reflections.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for Haynes 282 and IN 718 reveal distinct phase compositions. Heat-treated Haynes 282 displays clear γ' phase reflections, whereas IN 718 shows δ phase reflections and γ' phase presence through peak asymmetries. The inset highlights the (111) and (200) γ matrix reflections for detailed structural comparison.

caption: Top view of the single-pass multilayer thin-walled components fabricated using various CMT process modes.
summary: This panel displays the top view of thin-walled components, each measuring 200 mm by 60 mm by 7 mm. These components were fabricated using four distinct CMT process modes, with the layer width carefully controlled to 7 mm to ensure consistent geometry across the experimental samples.

caption: Fracture surface morphology of a room-temperature build sample, featuring dimples with second-phase particles embedded at their centers.
summary: Displaying the fracture surface of a room-temperature build sample, this SEM image shows dimple structures containing second-phase particles at their centers. The presence of these particles is a consistent feature observed across the tensile samples, contributing to the understanding of the fracture mechanism at room temperature.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Ni-Al-Cr system at 850 °C, extracted from the pentanary Ni-Al-Cr-Co-C system with fixed Co (34 wt.%) and C (0.02 wt.%) concentrations, showing experimental data points for different coating regions.
summary: This ternary Ni-Al-Cr phase diagram, calculated at 850 °C using TCNI7 thermodynamic data, illustrates phase stability within a pentanary system. Plotted symbols represent measured Al and Cr concentrations at four distinct locations: the near-surface and middle aluminide coating, the aluminide/MCrAlY interface, and the γ-phase within the MCrAlY coating layer.

caption: Fatigue life comparison of vertical ER70S-6 and multimaterial specimens after 4 months of seawater corrosion exposure.
summary: Fatigue resistance data after 4 months of corrosion exposure indicates that the multimaterial retains a relative advantage in the low-cycle regime. Consistent with previous conditions, the fatigue resistance of ER70S-6 may surpass that of the multimaterial in the high-cycle regime if the observed trends are extrapolated accordingly.

caption: Total structure factor S(q) for Cu25Ag75 obtained from MD simulation, shown with a 0.5 x-axis shift.
summary: The total structure factor S(q) for the Cu25Ag75 alloy is derived from MD simulations. The curve is shifted by 0.5 on the x-axis, and the overall shape is observed to be quite similar to the Ni-Al alloy system, except for values very close to zero.

caption: Curie temperature (Tc) values derived from Vibrating Sample Magnetometry (VSM) measurements for Fe, FeNi, and Ni substitution series.
summary: This panel displays the Curie temperature (Tc) as a function of composition for Fe, FeNi, and Ni substitution series, determined via VSM experiments. The data indicates that Co substitution in the base alloy leads to a continuous increase in Tc across the Fe and FeNi series.

caption: Force-displacement curve obtained from nanoindentation testing of the as-cast MPEA6 specimen.
summary: The force-displacement curve for the as-cast MPEA6 sample reveals distinct pop-in events during nanoindentation. These observations indicate that the initial microstructure contains effective barriers to dislocation movement, such as B2 nanoprecipitates and Ti segregations, which impede plastic deformation and influence the mechanical response of the material under load.

caption: Probability of Detection (PoD) curves for fatigue sample S11, comparing micro-CT performance at 10 μm and 35 μm voxel sizes with the 90/95 defect detection threshold indicated.
summary: This panel displays the Probability of Detection (PoD) analysis for fatigue sample S11. It evaluates the effectiveness of micro-CT imaging at two different voxel resolutions, 10 μm and 35 μm. The plot highlights the 90/95 defect detection threshold, providing a quantitative assessment of the inspection capability for this specific fatigue specimen.

caption: Representative fluorescence micrographs of MSCs cultured for 7 days, stained with Phalloidin (red) for cytoskeleton and DAPI (blue) for nuclei, demonstrating robust cell proliferation across all scaffold types.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images visualize the proliferation of MSCs after 7 days of culture on the scaffolds. Staining with Phalloidin and DAPI highlights the cytoskeleton and nuclei, respectively. The images confirm significant cell proliferation across all samples, with particularly notable growth observed in scaffolds containing CeNPs, supporting the efficacy of the material design.

caption: Vickers hardness values plotted against nitrogen content, demonstrating a strengthening response of approximately 25% as nitrogen concentration increases.
summary: Vickers hardness measurements are plotted against nitrogen content to evaluate the mechanical strengthening response. The data indicates that nitrogen enrichment raises the material hardness by approximately 25%. This strengthening effect is consistent with the systematic accommodation of nitrogen in the interstitial solid-solution, contributing to the overall mechanical performance of the alloy.

caption: Linear-linear transfer characteristics (ID-VGS) of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs comparing V-based and Ti-based ohmic contacts at a drain-source voltage (VDS) of 20 V.
summary: This plot displays the linear-linear transfer characteristics of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) at a drain-source voltage of 20 V. It provides a direct comparison between devices fabricated with V-based and Ti-based ohmic contacts, illustrating the performance differences in current-voltage behavior between these two distinct contact metallization schemes.

caption: Atomic model of the {111}-type coherent NiO/γ-Al2O3 interface, featuring Ni2+ (green), Al3+ (red), and O2- (blue) ions, with NiO and TBs-free Al2O3 phases highlighted in light green and light red.
summary: This atomic model displays the {111}-type coherent interface between NiO and γ-Al2O3. The O2- sublattice of NiO coincides with that of γ-Al2O3, allowing the Al2O3 beneath the NiO to inherit the oxygen sublattice directly. Ni2+, Al3+, and O2- ions are represented by green, red, and blue circles, respectively.

caption: Young's modulus plotted against relative density for stochastic and periodic lattice structures.
summary: Young's modulus is plotted against relative density for both stochastic and periodic lattice structures. Numerical results from finite element analysis of defect-free samples are fitted with Gibson-Ashby scaling power laws. Solid lines represent stochastic cellular structures, while dashed lines indicate periodic lattices, demonstrating the scaling behavior of elastic compressive modulus.

caption: Energy profile along the diffusion pathway for chromium vacancies in Cr2O3 calculated using the Pedone empirical potential.
summary: This panel shows the energy landscape for chromium vacancy diffusion in Cr2O3 using the Pedone potential. The results exhibit good qualitative agreement with other potentials, validating the diffusion pathway analysis. The plot provides a detailed view of the energy changes occurring as the chromium vacancy moves through the crystal lattice.

caption: Damping factor response for the second cryogenic aging protocol, highlighting 100% infilled coupons.
summary: Damping factor measurements for the second cryogenic aging protocol are presented. While overall variations are small, 100% infilled coupons exhibit more pronounced decreases after 10 cycles of 72 hours. This specific observation highlights a measurable impact on the damping characteristics of fully dense specimens under this particular aging condition.

caption: Magnetization curves of Mn2FeSn samples at 300 K and 5 K following field cooling of 80 kA/m.
summary: Magnetization curves for Mn2FeSn samples are presented at 300 K and 5 K. The dashed lines represent measurements at 300 K, while solid lines represent 5 K data after field cooling at 80 kA/m. These curves reflect the magnetic transition behavior observed in the material under these specific thermal and field conditions.

caption: Feature space distribution of photodiode signal data, plotting mean values against standard deviations to differentiate between nominal bulk layers, unexposed block layers, and anomalous layers.
summary: This visualization maps photodiode signal data into a feature space defined by mean and standard deviation. It distinguishes between nominal bulk layers, unexposed block layers, and anomalous layers. The signal array lengths vary significantly across these categories, ranging from 9,560 to 31,135, providing a clear separation of layer types.

caption: Atomic model depicting the asymmetric filling sequence of hydrogen trapping sites within the Σ11 grain boundary.
summary: This panel illustrates the asymmetric hydrogen trapping sequence in the Σ11 grain boundary. The model highlights how the initial hydrogen segregation to a specific site renders adjacent cross-plane sites energetically unfavorable due to strong repulsive interactions at short distances, confirming the observed filling behavior and site-specific hydrogen accumulation patterns.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for annealed PEKK coupons across multiple recycling rounds, showing the evolution of viscoelastic properties.
summary: This panel displays the dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) results for annealed PEKK coupons across successive recycling rounds. By tracking the storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor, the plot highlights how the annealing process influences the viscoelastic behavior and mechanical stability of the recycled PEKK material throughout the recycling cycles.

caption: WAAM system setup featuring a MIG 601Fi welding machine mounted on a three-axis CNC table.
summary: The WAAM system setup is shown, featuring a MIG 601Fi welding machine mounted on a three-axis CNC table. This equipment configuration facilitates the additive manufacturing process, providing the necessary mechanical control for the welding operation as described in the experimental setup for the WAAM process.

caption: Tetragonal crystal model of La0.6Ce0.05Sr0.1Ni0.1Ti0.9O3-δ projected to illustrate out-of-phase octahedral tilting along the z-axis, consistent with the I4/mcm space group.
summary: The tetragonal crystal model for La0.6Ce0.05Sr0.1Ni0.1Ti0.9O3-δ demonstrates atomic orientation and octahedral distortions. Specifically, the structure exhibits out-of-phase tilting along the z-axis, aligning with the I4/mcm space group. This model shows good correlation with experimental XRD patterns, confirming the proposed structural symmetry and octahedral tilting behavior within the material.

caption: Electrical conductivity of Al-Ni alloys as a function of heat-treatment temperature after 200 h, comparing Fe-containing and Zr-containing microalloyed specimens.
summary: This line graph illustrates the electrical conductivity of Al-Ni alloys subjected to 200 hours of heat treatment at various temperatures. It highlights the influence of Fe and Zr microalloying elements, noting that the Zr-containing alloy exhibits lower conductivity than the Fe-containing alloy in the as-cast condition before a crossover occurs.

caption: Bulk modulus K predictions derived from the GPR model, validated against independent FEA results for the F surface RVE at t / l = 0.09.
summary: Bulk modulus K predictions are mapped across the design space using a GPR surrogate and validated against independent FEA data. The plot shows the model's performance at a constant shell thickness of 0.09, where the 95% confidence interval narrows with larger RVE sizes, confirming the expected statistical homogenization behavior.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the as-built AlSi7Mg sample in the XY-HT condition, showing dislocation configurations under a diffraction vector g = [1 1 1] at 3% engineering strain.
summary: This bright-field TEM image captures the dislocation structure within an as-built AlSi7Mg grain subjected to 3% engineering strain. The XY-HT sample is imaged using a diffraction vector of g = [1 1 1], providing insight into the specific dislocation configurations present within the material's microstructure after mechanical deformation.

caption: Entropic potential evolution for 3D printed NMC622 working electrodes, showing the relationship between potential and open-circuit voltage across lithiation and delithiation cycles.
summary: This panel presents the entropic potential profiles for 3D printed NMC622 electrodes. The results establish that the electrochemical behavior of these electrodes is highly reversible when comparing the delithiation and lithiation cycles, confirming the stability and consistent performance of the 3D printed architecture under the tested C/10 rate conditions.

caption: Logarithmic resistivity comparison of S0 and S3 samples against copper as a function of measurement temperature.
summary: This panel displays the resistivity of S0 and S3 samples on a logarithmic scale compared to copper. The relative change in resistivity for S0 is small, appearing nearly flat, which indicates that the primary contribution to resistivity is temperature-independent residual resistivity resulting from alloy scattering due to chemical site disorder.

caption: Phase-field simulation of solidification microstructure at the corner of the 11th layer without NIAC, showing partial melting and regrowth of dendrites.
summary: This phase-field simulation depicts the solidification microstructure at the corner of the 11th layer without NIAC. It illustrates how previously solidified dendrites undergo partial melting at their upper regions due to new heat input, leading to the elimination of secondary dendrites and subsequent regrowth during the cooling process.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of the additively manufactured (AM-X) IN625 alloy specimen, viewed in the X-direction, after 1000 h of air oxidation at 900 °C.
summary: Displayed is the Kernel average misorientation map for the AM-X additively manufactured IN625 alloy after 1000 hours of air oxidation at 900 °C. The map reveals a significantly higher density of lattice misorientations compared to the CM specimen, which is attributed to the dense network of additional grain boundaries inherent in the AM microstructure.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluating the prognostic model's performance in training and TCGA validation cohorts, with significance assessed via the DeLong test.
summary: Prognostic model performance is illustrated through ROC curves, achieving AUC values of 0.824, 0.724, and 0.716 for 2- and 3-year overall survival in the training cohort. These results significantly outperform the stage model, confirming the TIL-score stage as a robust and statistically significant prognostic factor for patient survival analysis.

caption: Cost analysis of industrial production as a function of the number of impressions, demonstrating a significant reduction in price.
summary: This line graph illustrates the relationship between production costs and the number of impressions. By accounting for both fixed and variable cost items, the data demonstrates that industrial production can achieve substantial price reductions, with costs potentially decreasing to values near 600 euros as the number of impressions increases.

caption: Overlaid 1H NMR spectra of crude and purified AE, LH, and SL fucoidan samples, highlighting structural moieties including α-anomeric and β-anomeric protons, O-acetylated and O-sulfated positions, sugar ring protons, acetyl CH3 groups, and fucose CH3 protons, with asterisks denoting mannitol and free acetate impurities.
summary: This 1H NMR spectral analysis compares crude and purified AE, LH, and SL fucoidan samples. The spectra identify key structural moieties such as anomeric protons and various O-substituted sugar ring positions. Impurities like mannitol and free acetate are consistently observed across all purified samples, reflecting the presence of low molecular weight contaminants.

caption: Current-Voltage (I-V) performance curves for the KC 200GT PV module, recorded at 1000 W/m2 insolation while varying the operating temperature between 25 °C and 80 °C.
summary: Current-Voltage characteristics for the KC 200GT PV module are presented for temperatures ranging from 25 °C to 80 °C at 1000 W/m2 insolation. These curves highlight how thermal conditions modify the electrical output, confirming that temperature fluctuations between 25 °C and 80 °C directly impact the module's overall performance profile.

caption: FCC lattice unit cell illustrating the face-centered cubic arrangement utilized for the third homogeneous sample.
summary: Representing the third configuration, the FCC lattice unit cell is presented as a homogeneous sample within the 3 mm cubic RVE framework. This structure is part of the group of six lattices considered to evaluate the mechanical or physical properties of these specific representative unit cell designs.

caption: Synchrotron XRD measurements of lattice parameters for γ and γ' phases alongside calculated lattice misfit values for samples annealed for 5 and 50 hours.
summary: Synchrotron XRD analysis reveals the lattice parameters for γ and γ' phases in samples annealed for 5 and 50 hours. The lattice misfit, calculated from these parameters, is determined to be (3.5 ± 0.9) × 10⁻³ for the 5 h state and (3.2 ± 0.6) × 10⁻³ for the 50 h state, with error bars representing 2σ standard deviation.

caption: Ternary (Fe,Ni)0-(Fe,Ni)S-C phase diagram illustrating relations in the Fe-Ni-S-C system at 10 and 19 GPa under near-adiabatic conditions (1450–1600 °C), featuring the emergence of the Fe7C3 phase field at 19 GPa.
summary: This ternary phase diagram depicts the Fe-Ni-S-C system at high pressures of 10 and 19 GPa and temperatures between 1450 and 1600 °C. It highlights the appearance of the Fe7C3 phase at 19 GPa, while mapping Bulk Silicate Earth and depleted mantle compositions based on varying sulfur and carbon concentrations.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction plot for high Fe Inconel 625 without nitrogen, indicating a single-phase FCC structure at the HIP processing temperature.
summary: Equilibrium phase fractions for high Fe Inconel 625 are shown as a function of temperature, calculated without nitrogen. Similar to the low Fe variant, this alloy is predicted to maintain a single-phase FCC structure at the HIP processing temperature, demonstrating stability in the absence of nitrogen content.

caption: Pseudo-ternary composition diagram illustrating the distribution of high-temperature (HT) yield strength for the ZrNbMoHfTa alloy system.
summary: This pseudo-ternary composition diagram displays the distribution of HT yield strength for the ZrNbMoHfTa alloy system. The data indicates that increasing the Mo content significantly contributes to the strength of these refractory high-entropy alloys at elevated temperatures, consistent with established trends observed in metallic alloys and other high-entropy alloy systems.

caption: Reference 3D model of the triangular thin wall geometry.
summary: This panel displays a reference 3D model of the triangular thin wall structure used for the printing process. It serves as the baseline geometry for evaluating the deposition path and subsequent geometrical aberrations observed in the printed samples during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Solid-state 31P CP-MAS NMR spectra of COOH-PA modified NiTi nanoparticles alongside the bulk COOH-PA control sample.
summary: Comparison of the 31P MAS-NMR spectra for COOH-PA modified NiTi nanoparticles and the bulk COOH-PA control sample is presented. The analysis evaluates the chemical environment of the phosphonate groups on the nanoparticle surface relative to the pure phosphonic acid control to characterize the modification of the NiTi nanopowders.

caption: Magnified FTIR spectral region between 900 and 1100 cm⁻¹ highlighting the disappearance of the C-O-C stretching peak in chitosan-modified samples.
summary: Magnified FTIR spectra between 900 and 1100 cm⁻¹ reveal the elimination of a narrow peak or shoulder at 1033–1037 cm⁻¹ in SF4 and SF10 samples. This feature, attributed to C-O-C stretching within the epoxy/diacrylate network of S and SF, indicates significant structural changes resulting from the incorporation of chitosan into the resin blend.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram for AISI 4340 steel, illustrating cooling trajectories for oil quenching (purple) and additive manufacturing (AM) processes at 1000 mm/s (red) and 600 mm/s (orange) scanning speeds.
summary: This TTT diagram for AISI 4340 steel maps martensite formation between 300 °C and 200 °C. Cooling trajectories demonstrate how AM scanning speeds of 1000 mm/s and 600 mm/s can bypass bainite formation or lead to upper and lower bainite, mimicking isothermal treatment within the bainite transformation temperature range.

caption: Phase distribution map highlighting the volume fractions of austenite and martensite phases.
summary: This phase map illustrates the distribution of austenite and martensite within the printed NiTi alloy. Quantitative analysis reveals that the austenite phase is dominant, accounting for 46.6% of the total volume fraction, while the localized martensite phase constitutes 7.8% of the material's microstructure.

caption: Hysteresis loops derived from the stress-strain response of the CNT-filled Kelvin lattice, highlighting the viscoelastic behavior during cyclic compression.
summary: Panel b presents the stress-strain hysteresis loops for the CNT-filled Kelvin lattice. These loops demonstrate the viscoelastic nature of the nanocomposite material, as evidenced by the energy dissipation occurring during the 10 repeated compressive load cycles at a 10% strain amplitude, consistent with the material's mechanical damping characteristics.

caption: SHAP value distribution for EL prediction using SVR rbf modelling, where ageing temperature is ranked as the most significant factor affecting elongation.
summary: This SHAP plot provides a localized analysis of data records for EL prediction. The results demonstrate that ageing temperature is the most significant factor affecting the EL of Al alloys, allowing for a clear interpretation of how specific heat treatment parameters influence the mechanical property predictions within the model.

caption: Ashby plot comparing high cycle fatigue strength at 10^6 cycles against elastic modulus for lattice materials in as-built and hirtisation-treated conditions.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the correlation between high cycle fatigue strength and elastic modulus for lattice materials. Comparing as-built and hirtisation-treated conditions reveals that hirtisation significantly enhances fatigue resistance. Specifically, the hirtisation process increases the fatigue strength to modulus ratio by approximately 90% compared to the as-built state.

caption: Normalized hydrogen desorption spectra (appm s⁻¹) derived from mass-2 pressure data, showing a shift in the dominant peak from 465 °C (48 h) to 590-600 °C (72 h) and reduced low-temperature release.
summary: The desorption spectra reveal a significant shift in the primary hydrogen release peak toward higher temperatures after 72 hours of charging compared to 48 hours. This transition indicates a redistribution of hydrogen from reversible traps to deeper, irreversible hydride-associated traps, which effectively mitigates hydrogen embrittlement by reducing the mobile hydrogen fraction.

caption: Nyquist plot derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for 4% hydrogels, comparing samples with and without freeze-thaw cycling.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results, presented as a Nyquist plot, evaluate the electrical properties of the 4% hydrogels. The comparison between samples subjected to freeze-thaw cycles and those that were not highlights the impact of the structural changes on the electrochemical performance of the hydrogel material.

caption: Illustration of the boundary layer development and solute segregation profile at the solid/liquid interface during slow solidification.
summary: Depicted here is the development of the solute boundary layer during slow solidification. Ag atoms are rejected from the interface, leading to significant segregation in the liquid phase ahead of the solid front. This mechanism corresponds to cases where the solidification rate is small, allowing for local equilibrium at the interface.

caption: Angular distribution of scattered rays at a monitoring wavelength of 450 nm, showing the deflection angle for four simulated rays across various dome and process parameters.
summary: This Monte Carlo simulation displays the angular distribution of scattered rays at a 450 nm monitoring wavelength. The data accounts for all determined dome and process parameters, revealing a distinct directional dependency of scattering related to the feed direction, which highlights the influence of optical schlieren on coaxial ray deflection.

caption: Atomic model of the 36-atom orthorhombic FCC supercell, featuring Ni atoms in gray, alloying atoms X in purple, and Z in green, arranged in three {111} layers with 12 atoms per layer.
summary: The 36-atom orthorhombic (1x3x3) supercell is constructed from a rotated six-atom FCC lattice to model {111}〈112〉 shear deformation. The structure displays lattice vectors a, b, and c aligned with the [112], [110], and [111] directions, respectively, incorporating specific alloying elements to analyze their influence on the lattice configuration.

caption: Enlarged view of the solidification plateau for 3DTES-nn samples in R1, highlighting the duration difference between V-nn and Al2O3-nn variants.
summary: Focusing on the solidification plateau, this panel reveals that the phase transition lasts approximately 60 seconds for V-nn samples. In contrast, the Al2O3-nn samples exhibit a shorter duration of 30 seconds, a difference attributed to the higher thermal conductivity of the alumina-enhanced material during the discharging process.

caption: Immunofluorescence images showing Pax-7+ (green) and BrdU+ (red) satellite cells in d3D-BP scaffolds, with a bar graph depicting the percentage of BrdU+ proliferating cells.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging identifies proliferating satellite cells via BrdU incorporation. The data confirms a significantly higher number of Pax-7+ satellite cells stained with BrdU in d3D-BP compared to 3D-BP controls, with 63.96% versus 43.7% respectively, indicating that the d3D-BP platform effectively promotes satellite cell maintenance and proliferation.

caption: Evolution of the L2-norm metric plotted against training iterations for both training and validation datasets.
summary: This plot illustrates the progression of the L2-norm during the training and validation process. By tracking these values, the figure provides a clear visualization of the model's performance and convergence behavior throughout the training phase, as described in the corresponding results for the L2-norm during the training and validation process.

caption: SAED pattern obtained from the grain boundary region, identifying the crystalline phases present.
summary: The SAED pattern obtained from the grain boundary region provides structural evidence for phase identification. Along with the HAADF and HRTEM data, this diffraction analysis confirms that the main corrosion products at the grain boundary are Al2O3 and Cr2O3, consistent with the observed elemental enrichment of Al and Cr.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) graph of PUF microcapsules, depicting the thermal degradation profile and transitions of the material.
summary: The TGA graph of the PUF microcapsules illustrates the thermal transitions and degradation behavior of the material. This analysis is critical for understanding the thermal stability of the microcapsules, providing data on the temperature ranges at which the shell and core components undergo thermal decomposition or phase transitions.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of the L-DED fabricated AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA specimen processed at an AED of 32.69 J/mm2.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA specimen fabricated via L-DED at an areal energy density of 32.69 J/mm2. The map provides essential data regarding the grain structure and texture development resulting from this specific laser processing condition.

caption: Diffusion trajectory of a single H atom near the NGI at 1100 K over a 5.0 ns duration.
summary: At 1100 K, the H atom's diffusion trajectory near the NGI is tracked over 5.0 ns. The displacement vectors indicate the atom's random walk behavior. The NGI surface continues to exert a trapping influence, potentially forming sp3 C–H bonds that constrain the H atom's movement despite higher thermal energy.

caption: Correlation between intergranular crack growth rate at 35 MPa√m and the specific yield strength contributions derived from secondary and tertiary γ particles.
summary: Panel b examines the influence of secondary and tertiary γ particle contributions to yield strength on intergranular crack growth rates. By isolating these specific microstructural components, the figure demonstrates how individual strengthening phases affect the crack growth behavior, providing insight into the mechanisms governing intergranular fracture in these specific alloy microstructures.

caption: Refractive index dependency of the T(0,1) mode on stub height, evaluated at 20 mm axial position for a design frequency of 34 kHz.
summary: This graph depicts the refractive index of the T(0,1) mode as a function of varying stub heights. The evaluation is performed at an axial location of 20 mm with a design frequency of 34 kHz, demonstrating the tunable nature of the refractive index through geometric modifications of the phononic crystal.

caption: Neutron diffraction (200) peak profile for the axial direction at r = 12 mm, comparing experimental data with GP algorithm predictions and lattice parameter determinations.
summary: This plot displays the neutron diffraction (200) peak for the axial direction at r = 12 mm. It features experimental data (red line) alongside GP algorithm predictions (black symbols). A box plot illustrates deviations from the most probable solution, while vertical lines indicate lattice parameters derived from experimental, Rietveld, and GP methods.

caption: Wide-angle XRD pattern of the activated ilmenite sample, showing α-Fe2O3 as the dominant iron-containing crystalline phase.
summary: The wide-angle XRD pattern for activated ilmenite demonstrates that α-Fe2O3 is the dominant iron-containing crystal phase. While this phase differs from the calcined ilmenite, the diffraction results confirm that all other crystalline phases remain consistent between the two samples prior to undergoing CH4 redox cycling.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the Fe(316L)/Cu(CuCrZr) bilayer interface region viewed in the TD2 orientation, highlighting the grain structure and orientation distribution.
summary: The Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map illustrates the grain orientation distribution at the Fe(316L)/Cu(CuCrZr) bilayer interface. This visualization provides a clear overview of the microstructural characteristics in the interface region, serving as the primary reference for subsequent compositional and phase-specific analyses performed on the same sample area.

caption: Power-voltage (P–V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel derived from parameters estimated by the 19 optimization algorithms.
summary: Power-voltage (P-V) curves are illustrated for the Kyocera KC200GT panel, derived from the parameters estimated by the 19 different optimization methods. This panel provides a critical view of the power output performance, allowing for a direct comparison of how effectively each algorithm models the power characteristics of the solar panel.

caption: Mean Raman spectra of 3D-printed specimens highlighting bands at 1580 cm-1 and 1610 cm-1, with blue crosses indicating peaks identified by PCA as significantly different for discriminating graphene nanoplatelet concentrations.
summary: Mean Raman spectra are presented for 3D-printed specimens, focusing on the 1580 cm-1 and 1610 cm-1 bands. Principal component analysis was utilized to identify these specific peaks as statistically significant for discriminating between different graphene nanoplatelet concentrations, with the discriminating peaks marked by blue crosses for visual clarity.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of the SLM-UN sample surface over a 20 × 20 μm area.
summary: Atomic force microscopy image of the SLM-UN sample surface over a 20 × 20 μm area. This measurement was conducted to estimate the surface roughness of the material, providing a visual representation of the surface topography for the SLM-UN specimen as part of the comparative analysis presented in the study.

caption: Random selection of 3 nm radius dislocation loops oriented on {1 1 1} and {-1–11} planes, with red and blue lines representing distinct loop orientations.
summary: This panel illustrates the initial selection of 3 nm radius dislocation loops distributed across specific crystallographic planes. Red and blue lines serve as patterns to distinguish between different loop orientations, providing the foundational input for subsequent distribution modeling and simulation procedures within the McChasy2 framework to analyze defect depth-distributions.

caption: Shear yield stress of a concrete plate penetrometer plotted against time.
summary: Shear yield stress measurements over time demonstrate the penetrometer's sensitivity to concrete quality variations. The data captures the impact of water content and temperature on the material's structural build-up. These findings confirm that the instrument successfully reflects material quality changes and unavoidable temperature effects occurring within the concrete during printing.

caption: Tensile stress-strain curve of the initial recrystallised sample tested at 296 K, exhibiting a distinct Lüders-type stress-induced martensitic transformation characterized by a deformation stress plateau at approximately 95 MPa and a transformation strain of about 7%.
summary: The recrystallised sample displays a clear Lüders-type stress-induced martensitic transformation during tensile testing at 296 K. This behavior is characterized by a distinct deformation stress plateau at approximately 95 MPa, accompanied by a transformation strain of about 7%, serving as the baseline for comparing heat-treated samples.

caption: Complex plane impedance spectra of the specimens measured in a hydrogen atmosphere, where the parameter represents frequency in Hz.
summary: The complex plane impedance spectra for the investigated materials are presented in the presence of hydrogen. Experimental data points are plotted alongside solid lines representing best-fit calculations derived from the MCM. These results demonstrate a strong correspondence between the experimental measurements and the model predictions for the studied specimens.

caption: Nyquist plots comparing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results of the XZ and XY planes, highlighting the larger capacitive loop radius observed for the XZ plane.
summary: Nyquist plots derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveal distinct differences in the capacitive behavior of the material's planes. Specifically, the XZ plane exhibits a larger capacitive loop radius compared to the XY plane, indicating superior charge transfer resistance or capacitive characteristics for the XZ orientation under the tested conditions.

caption: High-speed imaging of the molten pool profile during synchronous laser remelting wire-arc DED, captured through quartz glass to observe dynamic behavior.
summary: High-speed imaging captures the dynamic molten pool profile during the synchronous laser remelting wire-arc DED process. Observed through quartz glass, this setup allows for the monitoring of molten pool behavior under specific processing conditions, providing visual evidence of the stability and characteristics of the arc-side dynamics during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Experimental EM tower setup used for systematic wall thickness measurements, featuring a range of extrusion multiplier values from 0.74 to 0.53 in 0.03 increments.
summary: This photograph displays the experimental EM tower setup utilized to establish a refined range for extrusion multiplier values. By varying the EM from 0.74 to 0.53 in 0.03 increments, the researchers successfully determined the appropriate parameters for subsequent wall thickness measurements and process optimization during the printing procedure.

caption: UV-Vis transmittance spectra comparing mold-casted and 3D-printed Elastic 50A samples, demonstrating the reduction in light transmittance caused by the presence and orientation of printed layers.
summary: UV-Vis spectrophotometry results reveal the optical transmittance of mold-casted versus 3D-printed Elastic 50A samples. The spectra highlight a distinct decrease in light transmittance for printed materials compared to casted ones, directly attributed to the presence of layers and their specific orientation within the printed structure.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure EBSD map overlaid on an SEM image of the fractured sample, revealing crystallographic orientation and twinning bands.
summary: An Inverse Pole Figure EBSD map is superimposed on the SEM image of the fractured sample to visualize crystallographic orientations. The mapping reveals parallel bands within single crystals, which are indicative of twinning formation during the manufacturing process. This analysis provides critical insight into the deformation mechanisms occurring within the material.

caption: HAADF image of the red circled region from panel (a), captured along the [001] zone axis to characterize the γ phase microstructure.
summary: Captured along the [001] direction, this HAADF image focuses on the red circled region identified in panel (a). It provides a high-resolution view of the γ phase, allowing for detailed structural characterization of the matrix in the alloy after it has undergone deformation at 1080 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram for Inconel 625, illustrating the precipitation kinetics of various phases including γ″, δ, Laves, MC, M6C, and M23C6 carbides.
summary: This TTT diagram characterizes the thermal aging behavior of Inconel 625. It maps the transformation kinetics of multiple secondary phases, specifically γ″, δ, Laves, and various carbides like MC, M6C, and M23C6, providing a comprehensive overview of the phase stability and precipitation sequences occurring within the alloy during heat treatment.

caption: Schematic representation of the alignment process between an input image pattern and a CMOS-measured image pattern using SURF feature matching to assess pixel-scale intensity projection accuracy.
summary: This schematic illustrates the methodology for aligning input image patterns with CMOS-measured patterns. By utilizing SURF feature matching, the process enables a quantitative evaluation of pixel-scale intensity projection accuracy. This alignment framework is essential for verifying the fidelity of optical projections captured by CMOS sensors in imaging systems.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topographic image of the electro polished oxide film surface, exhibiting a characteristic terraced surface structure.
summary: This AFM topographic image depicts the surface of an electro polished specimen after exposure to high-temperature deionized water. The surface is primarily characterized by a terraced morphology, indicating that the electro polishing process results in a distinct oxide film structure compared to mechanical or shot peened surface treatments.

caption: Topographic surface map of the surface-treated specimen gauge area, highlighting the modified surface morphology and the location of maximum stress concentration factor.
summary: Surface-treated topography is depicted following the unfolding process, revealing the modified gauge area morphology. Key features are segmented for stress concentration characterization, with a magenta circle identifying the site of the maximum stress concentration factor. This location serves as a critical indicator for potential crack initiation under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Comparison of proportional and experimental force-displacement relationships for the L120 specimen.
summary: Displayed is the force-displacement relationship for the L120 specimen, highlighting the alignment between experimental measurements and the proportional model. The proportional relationship is established for the range where linear behavior remains consistent with experimental records, effectively characterizing the mechanical performance of the L120 sample during the test.

caption: Gibson-Ashby model representation illustrating the correlation between porosity and mechanical properties for continuous gradient G cell scaffolds.
summary: This plot utilizes the Gibson-Ashby theory to analyze the relationship between the porosity of continuous gradient G cell structures and their corresponding mechanical properties. By applying this model, the figure provides a quantitative framework for understanding how structural gradients influence the mechanical performance of the scaffold design.

caption: LIME significance values for 6 porous surfels within the 49.61–50 kHz frequency band, showing positive contributions (|β*| ≥ 0.05) to pore identification.
summary: This panel displays LIME significance values for six porous surfels within the 49.61–50 kHz frequency band. Elements with high energy in this range exhibit positive significance values greater than 0.08, indicating a strong contribution toward the presence of pores in the identified porous surfels as determined by the model.

caption: Initial crystallographic textures of as-built 1 mm and 4 mm specimens displayed as pole figures.
summary: Initial crystallographic textures of as-built 1 mm and 4 mm specimens are displayed as pole figures. These plots demonstrate a clear texture difference between the two specimen sizes, confirming that the initial texture state is dependent on the specimen dimensions prior to any subsequent deformation processing at 700 °C.

caption: Isothermal differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves for Cu50Zr43Al7 metallic glass ribbon, illustrating heat flow behavior at various annealing temperatures.
summary: Isothermal differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves for Cu50Zr43Al7 metallic glass ribbon are presented, illustrating the heat flow behavior at various annealing temperatures. These curves provide the foundational data necessary for constructing the time-temperature-transformation diagram, capturing the thermal response of the material under specific isothermal holding conditions.

caption: Linear fitting of the relationship between ln Z and ln [sinh(ασ)] at a constant strain of 0.5 under varying deformation rates.
summary: This plot illustrates the linear relationship between the Zener-Hollomon parameter (ln Z) and the flow stress function ln [sinh(ασ)] at a strain of 0.5. By applying linear fitting across different deformation rates, the graph demonstrates the constitutive behavior of the material, providing a clear visualization of the deformation kinetics under these specific conditions.

caption: Absorption coefficient spectrum of NiZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles plotted against wavelength.
summary: NiZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles display an absorption coefficient spectrum that is high at short wavelengths and decreases as the wavelength increases from 350 to 390 nm. This observed decline in the absorption coefficient is indicative of the material's optical response and is governed by its characteristic bandgap and associated physical constants.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms at 5 mV s⁻¹ for on-chip μSC using 15 wt% PVA in 1M H₂SO₄ electrolyte, recorded at temperatures ranging from room temperature to -20 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry profiles for the 15 wt% PVA-based electrolyte illustrate the electrochemical response of the on-chip μSC across a temperature range from room temperature to -20 °C. These results serve as a baseline for comparison, showing the performance limitations of conventional PVA-based gel electrolytes in sub-zero temperature environments.

caption: Summary of eight distinct 3D-printed laminate configurations and their corresponding sample IDs, illustrating the relationship between ply stack-up sequences and mechanical performance.
summary: This table lists eight unique 3D-printed laminate configurations identified by specific sample IDs. Comparisons between sample pairs, such as ID1 versus ID2, reveal that increasing the number of layers oriented at 90° relative to the loading direction correlates with higher failure strain values across the different laminate stack-up sequences.

caption: Complete dilatometry data showing the evolution of shrinkage for cubical samples oriented along the X (binder deposition), Y (powder spreading), and Z (building) directions throughout the entire sintering cycle.
summary: This panel displays the full dilatometry dataset for cubical samples, illustrating the shrinkage evolution along the X, Y, and Z axes during the sintering process. These measurements reveal how the material dimensions change across different building orientations, providing a comprehensive overview of the sintering behavior throughout the entire thermal cycle.

caption: HEXRD patterns for the alloys aged at 800 °C for 16 h, showing the diffraction peaks of the γ and γʹ phases.
summary: HEXRD patterns for the alloys aged at 800 °C for 16 h are presented, illustrating the diffraction peaks of the γ and γʹ phases. Refinement of these patterns confirms an increased fraction of γʹ precipitates from ASC1 to ASC3, as evidenced by the intensity of the superlattice peaks.

caption: Compositional analysis table for the as-extruded AA6063-T6 alloy, detailing atomic percentages at locations 1, 2, and 3.
summary: This table lists the atomic percentage results obtained from SEM-EDS analysis of the AA6063-T6 alloy at the locations marked in the micrograph. These quantitative measurements characterize the chemical composition at the selected points, facilitating a comparison of the elemental distribution between the T4 and T6 alloy conditions.

caption: Extracted EXAFS oscillations at the Ni K-edge for all analyzed samples.
summary: This panel presents the extracted EXAFS oscillations measured at the Ni K-edge for every sample. These oscillations are essential for characterizing the local coordination environment of nickel atoms, facilitating the identification of phase compositions and structural arrangements within the investigated material system through further analytical modeling.

caption: Precision-recall curves illustrating damage detection performance categorized by location, specifically comparing corner, edge, and surface damage types.
summary: This precision-recall plot evaluates the efficacy of damage detection algorithms based on the spatial location of the damage. By distinguishing between corner, edge, and surface damages, the figure highlights significant variations in detection performance, providing a clear metric for assessing how damage location influences the reliability of the detection model.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry cooling curves for PEEK-based composites, illustrating phase change thermal transitions such as crystallization.
summary: Cooling DSC curves are presented to analyze phase change thermal transitions in PEEK-based composites. These curves provide essential data regarding crystallization behavior, allowing for the investigation of how filler inclusion influences the thermal properties and phase transition characteristics of the polymer matrix during the cooling process.

caption: Calculated Ti/Al and Nb/Al atomic ratios for both γ′ and η phases plotted against aging duration.
summary: This panel displays the evolution of Ti/Al and Nb/Al ratios within the γ′ and η phases during aging. These ratios provide insight into the relative stoichiometric shifts of these elements as the phases evolve, reflecting the significant compositional changes observed in the individual elemental concentrations of the η phase over time.

caption: Averaged density profile ρ(z) calculated over the final 10 ns of production time, illustrating the transition between the dense liquid phase and the less dense vapor phase.
summary: The density profile ρ(z) is averaged over the final 10 ns of the production simulation time. It clearly illustrates the transition from the denser liquid phase to the less dense vapor phase, demonstrating sufficiently broad bulk regions for both phases within the simulated CO2 system at 298.15 K.

caption: EBSD IPF map of tensile specimen TB2 before fracture, highlighting uniquely fine IN718 chill crystals and a high density of high-angle grain boundaries.
summary: Specimen TB2 is characterized by a distinct microstructure featuring fine IN718 chill crystals at the interface. EBSD analysis confirms a significantly higher density of high-angle grain boundaries compared to other specimens. This unique grain refinement is a key observation in the pre-fracture investigation of the tensile specimens.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of stainless-steel (SS) and various SS-supported electrodes (Cu, Ni, NiCu 1:1, and NiCu 3:1) in 0.010 M NH4OH and 1 M KOH at a 100 mV s-1 scan rate.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram compares the electrochemical activity of stainless-steel electrodes modified with different metal coatings in an alkaline NH4OH solution. The data, recorded at 100 mV s-1, reveals distinct current responses for each surface, notably demonstrating that the SS/Cu electrode exhibits minimal electrochemical activity compared to the other synthesized surfaces.

caption: Two-dimensional lattice image of the 24R structure in the Mg-8Li-4Gd-1Ni alloy.
summary: The two-dimensional lattice image confirms the LPSO structure of the Mg-8Li-4Gd-1Ni alloy as 24R. This structural identification is supported by the measured atomic layer thickness and aligns with previous studies, providing a clear visualization of the periodic stacking sequence within the material.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the ST condition sample near the fracture zone, where black lines delineate regions of localized shear band formation.
summary: This EBSD-based inverse pole figure map displays the microstructure of the ST condition sample near the fracture area. Darker contrast bands, highlighted by black lines, indicate regions of localized deformation. These features suggest the presence of shear bands, providing insight into the macro-mechanisms of deformation occurring within the material.

caption: HSQC spectrum of DHPMA showing two unexpected proton signals coupled with additional carbons at 61 and 75 ppm, confirming the chemical structure.
summary: The HSQC spectrum provides detailed structural confirmation for DHPMA by mapping proton-carbon couplings. The appearance of two specific signals at 61 and 75 ppm, representing protons coupled with additional carbons, validates the chemical structure of the synthesized monomer and confirms the successful transformation of the glycidyl methacrylate precursor.

caption: Faber-Ziman partial structure factor S_NiAl(q) for liquid Ni25Al75 derived from MD simulations, plotted alongside experimental neutron scattering data for Ni20Al80.
summary: Shown here is the partial structure factor S_NiAl(q) for Ni25Al75 from MD simulations, contrasted with experimental neutron scattering results for Ni20Al80. The MD simulation provides a theoretical prediction of the atomic correlations between Ni and Al, which is evaluated against experimental data to assess the accuracy of the simulation model.

caption: Melt pool aspect ratio plotted against laser power and scan speed parameters for samples processed without substrate preheating.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the melt pool aspect ratio for samples fabricated without substrate preheating. At low volumetric energy density (VED) conditions, specifically laser powers of 160–240 W and scan speeds of 1000–1400 mm/s, the melt pool width significantly exceeds its depth, resulting in a low aspect ratio below 0.6.

caption: Optical micrograph of sample 2 scaffold seeded with MSCs at Day 3, visualized using live/dead assay staining.
summary: Sample 2 scaffold seeded with MSCs is displayed at Day 3 via live/dead assay staining. This optical micrograph serves as a visual indicator of cell viability and scaffold morphology, contributing to the comparative analysis of swelling extent and cell-cell communication outcomes observed across the various scaffold samples.

caption: Atomic model of the L12-Ni3AlTi supercell structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic model of the L12-Ni3AlTi supercell. The structure was generated as a special quasi-random structure (SQS) to investigate the effects of varying Ti/Al stoichiometric ratios on the stability of the Ni3Al-based phase, with formation energies calculated via VASP software.

caption: FTIR-ATR spectra comparing chitosan (CS), sodium carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS-Na), and protonated carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS-H) polymers.
summary: This panel displays the FTIR-ATR spectra used to evaluate the carboxymethylation of chitosan. By comparing the characteristic bands of CS and CMCS polymers, the successful modification of the polysaccharide backbone is confirmed, providing a baseline for the chemical structural analysis of the subsequent scaffold materials.

caption: Calculated overlapped atomic volume for Model 4 with partial occupancies of 0.32 and 0.24 for the Al2 and Al3 sites.
summary: This simulation shows the overlapped atomic volume for Model 4, calculated for (001) slip with partial occupancies of 0.32 and 0.24 for the Al2 and Al3 sites. The findings are consistent with similar calculations, confirming the structural response characteristics when these specific Al site occupancies are applied.

caption: Framework of the LMA design approach for FGH4096 superalloy preparation.
summary: This panel illustrates the foundational framework for the LMA design approach used in the study. It serves as the initial step in the FGH4096 superalloy preparation process, establishing the systematic methodology for target composition selection and subsequent experimental characterization within the overall research workflow.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry profiles comparing virgin and hydrogen-charged WL-DED NiTi SMA samples, accompanied by a table detailing phase transformation temperatures for specimens subjected to 6-72 hours of hydrogen charging.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry profiles for virgin and hydrogenated WL-DED NiTi SMA samples are presented alongside a table of phase transformation temperatures. These results demonstrate the thermodynamic effects of hydrogen charging time on the alloy, showing how hydrogen exposure influences phase transformation behavior and contributes to irreversible transformations and functional degradation.

caption: Charge density distribution of N2H4 adsorbed on the twin NiZnCu (111) surface, with cyan indicating electrons and yellow indicating holes.
summary: The charge density distribution shows N2H4 adsorbed on the twin NiZnCu (111) surface. Observations indicate that Ni atoms near the N2H4 molecule shift from donating electrons to receiving them, resulting in a lower overall positive charge for the Ni atoms during the adsorption process.

caption: Schematic representation of the Hot Box apparatus, illustrating the arrangement of the cold chamber, black baffles, specimen panel, metering box, and hot chamber.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Hot Box experimental setup used for thermal testing. The apparatus consists of a cold chamber and a hot chamber, with the specimen panel positioned between them. Black baffles are integrated into the system to facilitate controlled environmental conditions during the 72-hour measurement period with 10-minute reading intervals.

caption: Fatigue ratcheting and damage strain evolution for the aged specimen with ST surface condition at 123 MPa.
summary: Aged specimens with ST surface conditions at 123 MPa exhibit significant initial fatigue ratcheting strain, followed by a plateau around 0.03% after 10^3 cycles. This plateau value is notably lower than that observed in the AB surface condition, demonstrating the influence of surface treatment on the fatigue ratcheting behavior.

caption: Dimensional accuracy analysis of IGS microchannels with features ranging from 0.2 to 0.05 mm, produced via opaque resin using industrial (white) and consumer (black) 3-D printing systems.
summary: Dimensional accuracy for smaller 0.05–0.2 mm microchannels is evaluated using opaque resin. Industrial 3-D printer performance shows a notable decrease in precision compared to larger features, with measured depths exhibiting a 13% difference and positive feature heights showing a 19% difference relative to the intended target dimensions.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of type I collagen in MC3T3-E1 cells, showing variations in fluorescence intensity across different scaffold groups.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining of type I collagen was conducted to assess the osteogenic activity of MC3T3-E1 cells. The HPDM group displayed relatively high fluorescence intensity, indicating robust collagen production. In contrast, the HPD and HP groups showed weaker fluorescence intensity, confirming that the HPDM scaffold effectively promotes collagen synthesis during osteogenic differentiation.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of the 3D-printed Violet filter, displaying the wavelength-dependent transmission profile of the printed ink.
summary: Violet ink filters are analyzed through their optical transmission spectrum, which maps the transmission intensity across the visible wavelength range. This data is part of a comprehensive set of measurements used to evaluate how the specific ink content influences the optical response of the 3D-printed filters.

caption: Yield strength plotted against shear modulus (G) for bcc RMPEAs, illustrating the scattered correlation between these two variables.
summary: This scatter plot examines the relationship between yield strength and shear modulus for bcc RMPEAs. The data reveals that shear modulus alone provides a scattered correlation with yield strength, highlighting the inherent limitations of using this single parameter for predicting mechanical performance across different alloy compositions.

caption: Intermediate state showing the progression of the intrusion interface as it interacts with the accumulating dislocation pile-up.
summary: Panel b illustrates the intermediate state of the interaction process between the intrusion interface and the pile-up of dislocations. The red line indicates the interface position, while the blue dot and ⊥ symbols represent the Frank-Read source and dislocations, respectively, showing the ongoing evolution of the dislocation structure.

caption: Atomic configuration of the Gr/GH3535 interface model following conjugate gradient minimization and equilibration at 700 K, highlighting the curved lattice distortion within the alloy matrix.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configuration of the Gr/GH3535 interface model after relaxation via conjugate gradient minimization and equilibration at 700 K. The alloy matrix exhibits slight lattice distortion, characterized by a non-linear, curved atomic arrangement, as shown in the inset, which helps alleviate internal stress at the interface.

caption: Comparative FTIR spectra of 3D-printed pure PLA composite and yucca fiber/PLA bio-composite powder.
summary: This FTIR analysis identifies chemical interactions and structural modifications within the materials. By comparing the absorption bands of the 3D-printed pure PLA composite against the yucca fiber/PLA bio-composite powder, the spectra reveal distinct variations in chemical composition and structural characteristics resulting from the incorporation of yucca fibers into the PLA matrix.

caption: Electromagnetic wave (EMW) reflection spectra comparing cast and 3D-printed material samples.
summary: This figure displays the electromagnetic wave reflection characteristics of materials prepared via casting and 3D printing. The data illustrates the performance of these distinct processing methods in an EMW absorption experiment, providing a comparative analysis of how the fabrication technique influences the reflection properties of the tested samples.

caption: Liquid-state specific heat capacity of encapsulated GF_PW composites determined via TGHPT.
summary: Liquid-state specific heat capacity values for encapsulated GF_PW composites are illustrated, obtained through TGHPT analysis. These values were determined by calculating the slope of linear regression lines fitted to cumulative heat enthalpy data, ensuring a high degree of precision with R-squared values consistently exceeding 0.997 across the measured temperature range.

caption: FTIR absorbance spectra of PGM/ALG beads prepared at varying concentration ratios of 5:20, 10:20, 20:20, and 40:20.
summary: FTIR analysis of PGM/ALG beads across four different concentration ratios provides further confirmation of PGM incorporation. By comparing the spectra of 5:20, 10:20, 20:20, and 40:20 ratios, researchers verified the presence of PGM within the bead structure, supporting the successful synthesis of the composite materials at varying concentrations.

caption: Three-dimensional surface morphology of the Ni-Fe-WC coating with a maximum profile height difference of 5.92 μm.
summary: The 3D surface morphology of the Ni-Fe-WC coating is presented, showing a maximum profile height difference of 5.92 μm. This quantitative measurement supports the visual observation of a smooth texture, indicating that the processing conditions successfully minimized surface irregularities compared to the grind arenaceous samples.

caption: Electrical impedance response of the cantilever-indenter structure measured at the sensing port.
summary: This panel illustrates the measured electrical impedance response of the cantilever-indenter resonator at the sensing port. Collected via an impedance analyzer, these measurements serve to validate the electrical response of the fabricated device, providing essential characterization data for the sensing port functionality of the cantilever-indenter structure.

caption: Instrumented Charpy load-displacement curve for the ST 900 treated sample, highlighting distinct crack propagation rates represented by blue and pink trendlines.
summary: The ST 900 sample exhibits an instrumented Charpy load-displacement curve characterized by varying crack propagation rates. A slower propagation rate, indicated by the blue trendline, corresponds to irregular microstructural zones near the notch that effectively deflect cracks, while the faster pink trendline reflects a flatter region with reduced crack advancement resistance.

caption: Bar chart representing the average friction coefficient calculated for each coating type.
summary: This bar chart displays the average friction coefficient for each coating. It provides a concise comparison of the frictional performance, reflecting the overall tribological efficiency of the different alloy compositions during the wear tests conducted in the study.

caption: Additional DSC curves for Ni–Co–Mn–Sn powders, highlighting the impact of cooling rate variations on transformation characteristics post-SAT.
summary: Panel d provides further DSC data for Ni–Co–Mn–Sn powders, focusing on the thermal behavior under different cooling rates after SAT. By comparing these curves, the study identifies shifts in transformation temperatures, which are critical for understanding the broader austenite-martensite phase transition region and the material's overall thermal performance.

caption: H^2 versus 1/h plot for SLM 316L stainless steel based on the Nix–Gao model.
summary: This graph shows the H^2 versus 1/h relationship for SLM 316L stainless steel, calculated using the Nix–Gao model. By translating the original nanohardness data into this format, the plot facilitates a deeper understanding of the indentation size effect in the SLM-processed stainless steel samples.

caption: Statistical distribution of percentage increases in cost per unit area (UA) for EOS M290 and EOS M400-4 machines.
summary: Box plots illustrate the percentage increase in median cost per unit area (UA) for heat exchangers manufactured using EOS M290 and EOS M400-4 systems. The data shows median cost increases of 4.12% and 18.5% for the respective machines, directly attributed to the increase in target effectiveness requirements.

caption: Distribution of Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, and Al concentration profiles at t* = 200.
summary: At t* = 200, the concentration profiles of Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, and Al highlight the diffusion and distribution behavior of solute atoms. This stage helps elucidate the formation mechanism of core-shell structure precipitates, providing insight into the long-term stability and spatial arrangement of elements within the Fe-7.5%Cu-3.0%Mn-1.5%Ni-1.5%Al alloy.

caption: Resistivity as a function of temperature for Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires after 10k cycles, showing distinct fluctuations near the martensite finish and austenite start temperatures.
summary: Resistivity measurements for Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires after 10k cycles reveal characteristic fluctuations near the Mf and As temperatures. These fluctuations, confirmed to be independent of instrumental error, occur alongside the general reduction in low-temperature resistivity caused by magnetic field-induced martensite reorientation and the suppression of spin electron scattering.

caption: Arrhenius plot of ln k versus -1000/RT derived from microstructural data to calculate activation energy Q.
summary: This Arrhenius plot determines the activation energy Q based on the rate constants derived from microstructural observations. The resulting value of 157.3 kJ/mol is consistent with the hardness-based results, further confirming that the diffusion of Nb is the rate-controlling mechanism for the formation of the γ″ phase.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry plot showing the thermal transitions of the filament before and after solvent debinding.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) plots characterize the thermal transitions of the filament before and after solvent debinding. The data reveals distinct thermal events, providing insight into the phase changes and energy absorption or release associated with the material's state during the debinding process.

caption: Magnetic moment distribution (MMD) of the V0 amorphous alloy (Co80B20) showing the relative contributions of Co and B atoms.
summary: The MMD of the V0 amorphous alloy, composed of Co80B20, is presented in panel a. This baseline configuration displays the magnetic moment distribution of Co and B atoms in the absence of V doping, serving as the reference for subsequent comparisons with V-doped amorphous alloy samples.

caption: Coercivity values plotted as a function of iron content in the alloy system.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between coercivity and iron content within the investigated alloy composition. By analyzing the variation of magnetic properties, the figure provides a clear trend of how coercivity responds to changes in Fe concentration, complementing the saturation magnetization data presented in related experimental results.

caption: Process flow chart outlining the operational sequence and functional stages of the cyclone reactor system.
summary: This flow chart delineates the operational sequence and functional stages of the cyclone reactor system. It serves as a guide for the reactive characterization process, illustrating how the cyclone design maintains intense and guided convection to effectively avoid the sedimentation of suspensions throughout the experimental testing phase.

caption: Reconstructed 3D model of extracted voids within the sample processed at 100 °C.
summary: Isolated 3D reconstruction of internal voids for the sample processed at 100 °C. This model provides a clear visualization of the void network, allowing for the analysis of how internal cavity formation evolves within the solid structure as the substrate temperature is increased during the fabrication process.

caption: Ashby plot comparing tensile test results of AESO/ACNC and AESO/MACNC composites against literature values for various cellulose-reinforced polymer systems.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the mechanical performance of AESO/ACNC and AESO/MACNC composites developed in this work. By comparing these results with literature data, including acrylate-functionalized CNC films, 3D-printed ethyl cellulose macromonomers, methacrylic-grafted CNCs, and epoxy-based composites, the figure highlights the relative tensile properties of the synthesized materials against established benchmarks.

caption: Lorentz-corrected one-dimensional SAXS patterns for rambutan and longan starches, providing insight into the periodic lamellar structure.
summary: Lorentz-corrected one-dimensional SAXS patterns for rambutan and longan starches are displayed in this panel. This technique is used to probe the lamellar architecture of starch while preserving its structural integrity, offering a detailed view of the periodic structural features within the starch granules across different varieties.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy photographs visualizing Ca2+ influx in MC3T3-E1 cells cultured on different scaffolds.
summary: Fluorescence photographs provide a visual representation of calcium ion influx in MC3T3-E1 cells on different scaffolds. These images correlate with the relative intensity measurements, offering spatial insight into how the scaffold composition influences intracellular calcium dynamics, a key factor in the osteogenic differentiation process of the seeded cells.

caption: Nyquist plots showing the electrochemical impedance response of conventional and as-fabricated samples immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, where the diameter of the semicircles reflects the resistance to electron transfer on the material surface.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance behavior of conventional and as-fabricated samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The diameter of the semicircles serves as a critical indicator of the electron transfer difficulty on the sample surface, providing insight into the corrosion resistance characteristics of the different fabrication conditions.

caption: Creep extension percentage plotted against time at 980 °C for four distinct initial stress levels, with the legend indicating the deviation angle from the [001] crystallographic direction for each specimen.
summary: This creep curve illustrates the percentage of creep strain over time at a constant temperature of 980 °C under four different initial stress conditions. The data demonstrates low scatter, evidenced by the close grouping of curves, and includes the deviation angle from the [001] direction for each tested specimen.

caption: Experimental irradiance of the diffracted field from an aperture illuminated with unpolarized light, captured without an analyzer.
summary: This panel displays the experimental irradiance of the diffracted field generated by an aperture under unpolarized laser illumination. The pattern confirms that the irradiance of the diffracted field does not distinguish between polarized or unpolarized light, appearing analogous to diffraction patterns observed with polarized input beams.

caption: Force–displacement responses for ABIS specimens 1 through 10, derived via Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS).
summary: This plot displays the force–displacement responses for ten distinct ABIS specimens generated using Latin Hypercube Sampling. The curves illustrate the mechanical behavior and variability across these samples, providing a comprehensive overview of the specimen performance under load as emphasized by the experimental data collected during the testing process.

caption: Strength versus density Ashby chart comparing Ni nano double gyroid lattices against macro Ti octet trusses, Cu micro octet trusses, and micro ceramic honeycombs.
summary: This Ashby chart illustrates the strength-density performance of Ni nano double gyroid lattices relative to other lattice materials. It highlights the superior strength-to-density ratios of Ti octet trusses reported by Dong et al. and provides context for the unattainable material space limited by the Voigt bound and parent material properties.

caption: Overview of technical gaps and proposed research directions for implementing a Cyber Supply Chain.
summary: This schematic illustrates the critical technical gaps currently hindering the implementation of a Cyber Supply Chain. It serves as a strategic roadmap, outlining potential solutions and future research directions necessary to address these systemic issues, thereby providing a structured framework for enhancing supply chain security and operational integrity.

caption: CO stripping voltammogram of the Pd/C catalyst measured in a 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte solution.
summary: This panel displays the CO stripping voltammogram for the Pd/C catalyst, which was recorded in a 0.5 M H2SO4 solution. This measurement serves as a standard electrochemical technique to evaluate the catalyst's resistance to CO poisoning, providing a baseline for comparing the performance of the as-prepared materials.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of K4800 alloy subjected to 0.27% plastic strain at 600 °C, imaged with g=(2-00) to visualize dislocation structures.
summary: This BF-TEM micrograph displays the dislocation configuration in K4800 alloy following 0.27% plastic strain at 600 °C. The specimen is oriented with the beam direction close to [011], and the imaging condition uses a g=(2-00) vector to reveal the underlying deformation microstructure developed during high-temperature loading.

caption: KAM distribution map highlighting the gradient of plastic deformation extending from the inner surface into the bulk material.
summary: This KAM map illustrates the localized plastic deformation gradient extending inward from the inner surface. The microstructure in this region, approximately 100 μm from the opening of Crack II, reveals distorted grains and increased deformation, confirming that the inner wall experiences higher oxidation rates and internal energy accumulation.

caption: Comparison of the synchrotron diffraction spectrum for a 4 mm rod specimen containing 1 at% S against the PDF 00–041–0898 reference structural data for a primary fcc-type Zr2Ni phase.
summary: This panel displays a direct comparison between the synchrotron diffraction spectrum of a 4 mm rod specimen with 1 at% sulfur and the PDF 00–041–0898 reference data. The analysis highlights the crystalline primary phase formation and its structural correspondence to the fcc-type Zr2Ni phase within the alloy system.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of Frenkel defect counts in pure Cu under 4 keV PKA energy at 300 K, showing the highest defect production in the [111] direction and the lowest in the [100] direction during the peak phase.
summary: This panel illustrates the temporal evolution of Frenkel defect pairs in pure Cu subjected to 4 keV PKA energy at 300 K. Simulation results indicate that the [111] direction exhibits the highest number of defects, while the [100] direction records the lowest count during the peak damage phase.

caption: Schematic representation of the push-out test procedure and the biological progression from monocytes and pre-osteoblasts to mature osteoblasts and osteocytes during bone repair.
summary: This schematic outlines the push-out test procedure for 3D-printed implants. It further illustrates the biological pathway of bone repair, showing how implants promote osteoclast formation by inducing the maturation of monocytes and pre-osteoblasts into osteoblasts and osteocytes to achieve effective bone regeneration.

caption: HRTEM image of γ population I at high magnification, including an FFT of the marked region in the βo [001] zone axis.
