summary: This HRTEM image of population I γ-precipitates includes a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) of the marked region along the βo [001] zone axis. The FFT analysis confirms the crystallographic orientation and phase identification, providing further evidence of the epitaxial relationship between the γ particles and the βo matrix.

caption: Micro-XRF mapping area image of the Sn-0.7Cu-0.05Ni solder ball sample.
summary: The micro-XRF mapping area image provides a visual overview of the Sn-0.7Cu-0.05Ni solder ball sample. This technique allows for the subsequent analysis and comparison of elemental composition and distribution within the solder ball, serving as the base region for the elemental mapping presented in the following panels.

caption: TDA-spectrum of CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 200 bar with a heating rate of 0.500 K/s, showing the four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit.
summary: This panel displays the TDA-spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA samples charged at 200 bar using a heating rate of 0.500 K/s. The data is presented through a four-peak deconvolution scenario, which includes the individual peak contributions and the resulting cumulative fit function to characterize the hydrogen desorption behavior of the alloy.

caption: Inverse pole figure of the HT1 specimen showing the initial microstructure composed of interlaced acicular-like and lamellar alpha laths forming a basketweave morphology.
summary: The HT1 specimen exhibits an initial microstructure characterized by interlaced acicular-like and lamellar alpha laths, which form a basketweave pattern. This inverse pole figure provides a crystallographic orientation analysis of the material prior to low-cycle fatigue testing, establishing the baseline structural state for the HT1 condition.

caption: Ni L-edge NEXAFS spectra recorded in TEY mode for CoCrFeNi compared to pure Ni, showing a shift of +0.6 eV.
summary: Ni L-edge NEXAFS spectra in TEY mode demonstrate the electronic state of Ni within the CoCrFeNi alloy. A shift of +0.6 eV is observed relative to pure Ni. This spectral shift serves as indirect evidence of the unique atomic surroundings of Ni and its correlation with chemical short-range order.

caption: Box plots illustrating the distribution of elemental contents in bulk-ore samples across different ore types at Hongge, highlighting significant variations in Cr, Cu, Co, and Ni concentrations.
summary: This box plot displays the elemental content distribution in bulk-ore samples from Hongge. Massive and OPH oxide ores exhibit significantly higher Cr, Cu, Co, and Ni concentrations compared to GH oxide ores. Sulfide ores also show elevated Co-Ni-Cu-S levels, reflecting their distinct geochemical association and preferential partitioning into the sulfide phase.

caption: Visual representation of tensile specimens fabricated at varying printing layer heights.
summary: This panel displays the physical appearance of tensile specimens manufactured using different printing layer heights. These specimens serve as the primary test subjects for subsequent mechanical characterization, providing a visual reference for the geometric variations introduced by the specific printing parameters employed during the fabrication process.

caption: Comparative analysis of mechanical property results for the porous TC4-5Cu alloy, summarizing the performance metrics across different sample configurations.
summary: A comparative summary of the mechanical results for the porous TC4-5Cu alloy is provided. This panel synthesizes the findings from the stress-strain, strength, modulus, and hardness tests, offering a comprehensive overview of how structural variations impact the overall mechanical performance of the porous TC4-5Cu material system.

caption: Comparison of output versus desired SMCF values, where input target values are plotted on the horizontal axis and the corresponding model-generated output values are on the vertical axis.
summary: This parity plot compares the desired SMCF target values against the actual values generated by the framework. By mapping input targets on the horizontal axis and model outputs on the vertical axis, the visualization allows for a direct assessment of the model's accuracy in reproducing specified mechanical property targets.

caption: S-N curve for PLA/20 wt%PCL specimens after 6 weeks of immersion in SBF, showing a fatigue limit of 11.5 MPa.
summary: The fatigue limit declines to 11.5 MPa after 6 weeks of immersion in SBF, marking a 15.4% decrease from the reference. This degradation is attributed to the accumulation of microcracks and significant structural changes within the PLA/PCL blend caused by the prolonged exposure to the corrosive environment.

caption: Torque values measured during drilling operations under dry, base fluid, and various nanofluid cutting conditions, including hBN-SDS, hBN, GNP-SDS, hBN-GA, GNP, and GNP-GA.
summary: This plot displays torque values during drilling across different lubrication conditions. Performance analysis reveals that hBN-SDS nanofluid is the most effective, achieving torque reductions of 41.19% and 32.10% compared to dry and base fluid cutting, respectively. These torque trends correlate directly with observed thrust forces and surface roughness measurement results.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profile of the system in 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte, conducted at a scan rate of 0.005 V/s and a current load of 200 mA g-1.
summary: This galvanostatic charge-discharge plot displays potential versus time for the system in 1 M H2SO4. The curve exhibits a linear response, characterized by a positive slope during the charging phase and a negative slope during the discharge phase, reflecting the electrochemical behavior under a 200 mA g-1 current load.

caption: DIC analysis showing the placement of two application markers used to track sample displacement over time.
summary: Digital Image Correlation analysis is performed by placing two specific application markers on the sample. These markers allow for the precise tracking of sample displacement as a function of time throughout the duration of the test, providing critical data for evaluating the mechanical behavior of the material under load.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of (TiZrNbTa)N x thin films against a bare Ti–6Al–4V substrate in a 3.5 wt% NaCl aqueous solution.
summary: This figure presents the potentiodynamic polarization curves used to evaluate the corrosion resistance of (TiZrNbTa)N x films relative to a Ti–6Al–4V substrate. Conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl aqueous solution, these measurements provide critical electrochemical data to assess the protective performance of the nitride coatings compared to the bare alloy.

caption: Faradaic efficiency for CO production plotted against Ag deposition potential at a current density of 50 mA/cm².
summary: This panel shows the Faradaic efficiency for CO production at a current density of 50 mA/cm² as a function of Ag deposition potential. The observed trend indicates that optimal deposition potentials significantly improve CO₂ reduction selectivity, whereas excessively negative potentials negatively impact the overall electrochemical performance of the electrode.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the T1000 superalloy representing local strain distribution.
summary: T1000 superalloy initial microstructure is analyzed using a Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map. This technique highlights local misorientations within the grains, which are indicative of the initial strain distribution and dislocation density present in the material before any subsequent mechanical testing or thermal treatment is applied.

caption: Strain-time evolution and corresponding strain rate variation for LPBF-built Ti–22Al–25Nb alloy samples subjected to isothermal tensile creep testing at 923 K under a quasi-steady-state stress of approximately 150 MPa.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep behavior of LPBF-built Ti–22Al–25Nb alloys during an isothermal tensile experiment at 923 K. By applying a quasi-steady-state stress of 150 MPa, the figure captures the strain-time curve and the subsequent variation of the strain rate over time, providing critical data on the material's high-temperature deformation characteristics.

caption: Root mean squared error (RMSE) plotted against the number of training epochs for the artificial neural network (ANN) model.
summary: This plot displays the RMSE values as a function of training epochs for an ANN model. The data indicates that the loss function and RMSE stabilize after approximately 130 epochs, which signifies the convergence point of the model training process achieved through gradient descent and backpropagation techniques.

caption: Compressive strength versus relative density for Ti–6Al–4V lattice structures, comparing hollow-walled TPMS lattices against truss, plate, and conventional TPMS architectures, with the Suquet yield strength bound and cortical bone strength zone marked.
summary: This Ashby plot compares the compressive strength of hollow-walled TPMS lattices against various Ti–6Al–4V metamaterials. The data demonstrates that hollow-walled TPMS structures exceed the typical strength range for cortical bone (100–230 MPa) and outperform most competing lattice metamaterials at comparable densities, establishing their superior mechanical performance in load-bearing applications.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of HUVEC cells co-cultured with extracts, demonstrating high cell viability with minimal dead cells across all tested concentrations.
summary: Live/dead staining images confirm the cytocompatibility of the SrSC extracts. The microscopy results show that almost no dead cells are present even at the lowest concentration of 0.0125 mg/mL, visually validating the high biocompatibility of the SrSC material when interacting with HUVEC cells in culture.

caption: Hardness profile across the interface of S1-S4 samples following solution annealing and aging (SAA) and alternative direct aging (ADA) treatments, highlighting the superior hardness achieved by SAA across IN718, HAZ, and WCB regions.
summary: This panel compares hardness profiles for S1-S4 samples after SAA and ADA treatments. SAA consistently achieves higher hardness across the IN718, HAZ, and WCB regions compared to ADA. The marked reduction in HAZ hardness after SAA, combined with lower MOS and grain refinement, confirms the effectiveness of the SAA process.

caption: SHAP value distribution for YTS prediction using SVR rbf modelling, highlighting the atomic average of Zunger pseudopotential radius (D5_mean) as the most significant feature.
summary: This SHAP plot illustrates the global feature importance for predicting YTS in Al alloys. The analysis identifies the atomic average of Zunger pseudopotential radius (D5_mean) as the most influential factor. Additionally, high aging temperatures show a positive impact on predicted YTS, as indicated by red dots on the positive side.

caption: Ortho view of the R-Octet metamaterial model with a rotational degree of 15° (R-Octet-15).
summary: The R-Octet-15 model is shown in an ortho view, featuring a 15° rotational degree between the upper and lower layers. This configuration demonstrates the implementation of the helicoidal twist strategy, which is designed to mimic the structural characteristics of the mantis shrimp telson.

caption: Time-temperature transformation profile for the H13 specimen processed with 0 mA thermal compensation, showing a steady-state deposition temperature maintained near 300 °C.
summary: The 0 mA H13 specimen exhibits a consistent thermal history during the deposition process, maintaining a temperature of approximately 300 °C. This time-temperature transformation profile is critical for understanding the subsequent microstructural evolution, as the thermal cycle directly influences phase transformations and carbide precipitation within the as-printed material.

caption: SVR test set regression plot demonstrating enhanced R2 performance following PSO parameter optimization.
summary: This test set parity plot for the SVR model shows improved R2 values compared to training and validation sets. The use of PSO optimization facilitated the model's learning of the true data distribution, allowing for better predictive performance on relative density and dimensional change despite the limited dataset.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the 0.5 mm thin-walled LB-PBF SS316L sample in the XZ plane after HT2 heat treatment at 1150 °C for 135 minutes.
summary: This inverse pole figure map characterizes the 0.5 mm thin-walled SS316L sample after HT2 heat treatment. The microstructure reveals significant recrystallization and abnormal grain growth, which are typical outcomes for LB-PBF SS316L samples treated at 1150 °C, as documented in the study's microstructural analysis of these thin-walled components.

caption: EDS line scanning profile along line 1, showing the compositional transition across a TiC particle.
summary: The EDS line scan along line 1 demonstrates the compositional variation across a specific TiC particle in the 3 wt% TiC/Ti6Al4V composite. The profile exhibits a clear transition from the α phase to the TiC particle and back to the α phase, confirming the chemical nature of the observed precipitates.

caption: Full-range mass spectra of the first 20 million ions collected from Al 6026 samples, comparing data acquired on LEAP 4000 X Si and Invizo 6000 instruments up to the 65Cu+ peak.
summary: This panel displays the full mass spectra for Al 6026 samples obtained from two different atom probe instruments, LEAP 4000 X Si and Invizo 6000. The spectra cover the range up to the heaviest observed peak at 65Cu+, providing a comprehensive overview of the ion collection performance for the first 20 million ions.

caption: Confusion matrix detailing the classification results and error patterns for the fifth model across different pH levels.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed view of the classification results for the fifth model across the different pH level classes. It serves to quantify the model's predictive performance, enabling a clear comparison of how well the fifth model distinguishes between the various pH categories during the testing phase.

caption: Peak shear resistance and ultimate relative displacement plotted against varying nodular pile node widths.
summary: This panel illustrates the relationship between nodular pile node widths and the peak shear resistance alongside ultimate relative displacement at the interface. The data demonstrates how node geometry influences the load transfer mechanism, confirming that the presence of nodes is essential for maintaining effective interlocking between the pile and cemented soil.

caption: Arrhenius plots illustrating the temperature dependence of methane pyrolysis rates within molten Sn and SnNi alloy media, demarcated by their respective lower and upper experimental temperature boundaries.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the kinetic data for methane pyrolysis experiments 1–5 conducted in molten Sn and SnNi alloys. The visualization highlights the temperature-dependent reaction rates, clearly defining the lower and upper experimental temperature limits for each alloy system to characterize the catalytic performance of the molten metal environments.

caption: Solid solution strengthening of the gamma-prime phase as a function of bulk Ti content, with the RR1000 patent range shaded.
summary: This panel illustrates the predicted solid solution strengthening of the gamma-prime phase as the bulk Ti content is varied. The shaded region denotes the RR1000 patent range, which serves as a benchmark for the alloy's composition and its associated mechanical strengthening characteristics within the precipitate phase.

caption: Magnified view focusing on the initial pop-in events observed in the load-displacement graphs.
summary: This magnified view highlights the first pop-in events observed in the load-displacement graphs. Analysis of these features reveals that as the testing temperature increases, the first pop-in event occurs at a higher load, reflecting the temperature-dependent nature of the localized yielding behavior in the material under investigation.

caption: Snoek relaxation profiles comparing simulated internal friction (IF) in martensitic Fe-2C and Fe-25Ni-2C alloys, showing filled points for Fe-2C and unfilled points with moving average lines for Fe-25Ni-2C at 1 Hz oscillation frequency.
summary: This panel displays simulated internal friction profiles for martensitic Fe-2C and Fe-25Ni-2C alloys. The comparison highlights the impact of nickel alloying on Snoek relaxation behavior. Results indicate distinct relaxation profiles between the binary and ternary systems, with moving averages provided for the Fe-25Ni-2C data to clarify the trend.

caption: Temperature-dependent CTE curves for Fe30Co30Ni30Cr5Mn5, demonstrating the experimental deviation from calculated models during the ferromagnetic to paramagnetic transition.
summary: This plot illustrates the CTE for Fe30Co30Ni30Cr5Mn5 near the Curie temperature. The experimental solid line deviates from the calculated dash and dot-dash lines during the transition from ferromagnetism to paramagnetism. This deviation is attributed to thermal agitation affecting magnetic coupling, which is essential for understanding the dimensional stability of the HEA system.

caption: Backscattered electron micrographs and corresponding WDS elemental maps for Fe, Ni, Cr, Mn, Mo, Cu, and O in the HEA powder.
summary: Electron Probe Micro-Analysis (EPMA) using WDS mapping illustrates the elemental distribution within a representative HEA powder particle. These maps visualize the spatial arrangement of Fe, Ni, Cr, Mn, Mo, Cu, and O, providing a detailed assessment of potential elemental segregation patterns present in the powder prior to further processing.

caption: Geometric dimensions of the ASLS unit cell, defined by a nominal cell height of 5 mm, an arch-shaped support diameter of 1.2 mm, and a spiral support diameter of 0.8 mm.
summary: The unit cell dimensions are precisely defined by three key parameters: a nominal cell height of 5 mm, an arch-shaped support diameter of 1.2 mm, and a spiral support diameter of 0.8 mm. These specifications provide the necessary geometric constraints for the ASLS lattice structure, ensuring consistent structural integrity and design accuracy.

caption: Atomic configuration of the CaO(110)/Fe(111) interface representing the plane pair with the lowest calculated mismatch.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configuration of the CaO(110)/Fe(111) interface. It highlights the contacting planes that achieve the minimum lattice mismatch between the calcium oxide substrate and the δ-Fe phase, aligning with the calculated results summarized in the study.

caption: Transient normalized stress distribution across the fourth layer of the thin-wall TZM alloy during WAAM.
summary: Representing the fourth layer of the thin-wall TZM alloy, this 3D simulation illustrates the transient normalized stress distribution as the torch completes the layer. The data highlights how stress evolves during the early stages of the WAAM process as the thin-wall structure begins to build up vertically.

caption: Side view of the Ti2AlV (110) surface atomic structure.
summary: This panel displays the side view of the atomic structure for the Ti2AlV (110) surface. The visualization provides a clear representation of the atomic arrangement, which serves as the foundational geometry for evaluating potential adsorption sites for various adsorbates on the material surface as described in the study.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of the electrolyte after 1 hour of electrolysis, comparing samples saturated with CO2+K14NO3 and CO2+K15NO3 to confirm urea formation.
summary: 1H NMR spectroscopy was utilized to verify urea synthesis by comparing isotopic labeling. The 15N-labeled urea (15NH2CO15NH2) exhibits two characteristic peaks at 5.73 and 5.50 ppm, whereas the 14N-labeled urea (14NH2CO14NH2) shows a single peak at 5.62 ppm, confirming the successful incorporation of nitrogen into the final product.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry scan rate study (15–150 mV s-1) of 1 mM [Fe(CN)6]4- in 0.1 M KCl performed on the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode, featuring the Randles–Ševčík plot as an inset.
summary: Electrochemical performance evaluation of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode using the inner-sphere redox probe [Fe(CN)6]4- across scan rates from 15 to 150 mV s-1. The resulting cyclic voltammograms and the Randles–Ševčík plot provide further evidence of the electrode's consistent performance and suitability for diverse electrochemical sensing applications.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves illustrating the mass loss profiles of CA, MCC, and the pCA/MCC/peroxide system as a function of temperature.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves compare the thermal degradation behavior of CA, MCC, and the pCA/MCC/peroxide system. The data indicates that CA 2.25 exhibits a degradation temperature of 378.8 ± 3.04 °C, which aligns with the expected thermal stability range of 350 °C to 400 °C for cellulose acetate materials.

caption: Single cell tracking analysis of C3H10 T1/2 cells treated with C5, monitoring morphological evolution and movement patterns.
summary: Single cell tracking analysis for the C5-treated group monitors cell morphology and migration speed over time. These observations confirm that C5 provides enhanced migration capacity and lower cytotoxicity in C3H10 T1/2 cell lines compared to TPO, as evidenced by the detailed kinetic and morphological tracking data.

caption: Phase angle versus frequency plots for L-PBF 316L stainless steel in borate buffer electrolyte, demonstrating a single time constant characteristic of a simplified Randles-like circuit model.
summary: Bode phase angle plots for L-PBF 316L stainless steel exhibit a single time constant across the investigated temperature range. This observation justifies the application of a simplified Randles-like equivalent electrical circuit model to analyze the electrochemical response of the material when subjected to varying thermal exposure conditions.

caption: Crystallinity percentages of 3D-BPs (10%, 15%, and 20% PCL) derived from DSC endothermic peaks compared to 3D-DP.
summary: Crystallinity of the 3D-BPs is determined via differential scanning calorimetry, showing values of 24.29%, 27.09%, and 29.74% for 10%, 15%, and 20% PCL concentrations, respectively. These results indicate that crystallinity decreases with lower PCL content and remains lower than the 33.83% observed in the 3D-DP control sample.

caption: Isothermal section at the ternary eutectoid reaction temperature (γ+P+Ni3Mo→oP6), highlighting the formation of the oP6 phase.
summary: This panel displays the ternary isothermal section at the eutectoid reaction temperature. It demonstrates the phase transformation where the oP6 phase is formed via the ternary peritectoid reaction involving γ, P, and Ni3Mo phases, providing insight into the lower-temperature phase stability and equilibrium pathways within the Ni-Cr-Mo ternary system.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for silica fume (SF) content.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the contribution of silica fume (SF) content to the model's prediction of compressive strength in 3DPFRC. It serves as part of the comprehensive feature analysis provided in the study to understand the influence of various input parameters on the mechanical properties.

caption: Elemental mapping of a single powder particle in the 75–106 μm size range, showing the element distribution and the Cr segregation region marked by a white arrow.
summary: This panel presents the elemental mapping of a single powder particle sized between 75 and 106 μm. The distribution of elements is clearly visualized, and the white arrow highlights a specific Cr segregation region, allowing for a detailed examination of the chemical structure within this particular particle size category.

caption: Bode diagram depicting the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results for the CoCu 30 FeMnNi base metal (BM).
summary: Bode diagram depicting the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results for the CoCu 30 FeMnNi base metal (BM). This plot is used to evaluate the electrochemical impedance properties of the CoCu 30 FeMnNi alloy in its base metal state, contributing to the broader study of the welded joint's electrochemical performance.

caption: FFT pattern of the interface between bcc grain (8) and fcc grain (9) from (m).
summary: The FFT pattern derived from the HRTEM image of the bcc-fcc interface shows the diffraction spots for both phases. This analysis confirms the orientation relationship between grain (8) and grain (9), serving as the basis for the subsequent IFFT filtering of specific diffraction spots.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of the MAX-1 sample showing the presence of sp2 hybridized carbon.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of the MAX-1 sample confirms the presence of carbon in sp2 hybridization. This spectroscopic analysis is part of a broader study characterizing the carbon bonding states across various MAX phase samples, where the carbon content is observed to be slightly lower in samples containing the MAX phase.

caption: Equivalent electrical circuit model used to simulate the impedance spectra of as-printed 3D samples, featuring a one-time constant configuration with electrolyte resistance in series with a parallel polarization resistance and constant phase element.
summary: The panel illustrates the equivalent electrical circuit used to simulate the impedance spectra of as-printed 3D samples. It employs a simple one-time constant model, where electrolyte resistance is in series with a parallel combination of polarization resistance and a constant phase element representing the non-ideal double layer capacitance.

caption: Representative load-displacement curves illustrating the mechanical response of hybrid single-lap joints in both quasi-static and post-fatigue run-out conditions.
summary: Representative load-displacement curves are presented for hybrid single-lap joints, contrasting quasi-static performance with post-fatigue behavior. The data confirms that run-out PC/AlSi10Mg hybrid joints, subjected to fatigue testing at 30% ULSF, retain 93% of their original quasi-static strength, highlighting the minimal degradation in mechanical performance after extensive cyclic loading.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of Biomed Clear resin samples subjected to 120 °C heat treatment for 24 h, comparing uncoated (blue) and parylene-C coated (red) specimens.
summary: This panel displays UV-Vis absorbance spectra for Biomed Clear resin treated at 120 °C for 24 h. The data assesses the release of uncured monomers into DPBS. Comparing coated and uncoated samples reveals how the parylene-C layer influences monomer leaching, with heat treatment generally reducing absorption levels compared to untreated controls.

caption: STEM-EDS quantitative elemental analysis and corresponding spectra for the identified phases, highlighting the chemical composition of the Al9Fe(Cu)Ni phase.
summary: This panel presents STEM-EDS quantitative elemental analysis and spectra for the three phases identified in the FG region. It specifically details the chemical composition of the Al9FeNi phase, noting that the Cu solid solution is indexed as Al9Fe(Cu)Ni, providing essential chemical verification of the observed microstructural constituents.

caption: Geometric model of the Ni-X 3 /C interface, highlighting the atomic positions within the doped TiNi 3 (0001) slab.
summary: The Ni-X 3 /C interface model is presented to facilitate the study of interfacial bonding behaviors. By constructing this specific configuration of the TiNi 3 (0001) slab with dopant atoms, researchers can evaluate the influence of atomic positioning on the stability and electronic properties of the interface with carbon.

caption: EDS line scan profiles showing the elemental composition evolution across the Invar/MnCu interface.
summary: This panel displays the elemental distribution across the Invar/MnCu interface obtained via EDS line scanning. The profiles provide raw compositional data that characterize the transition layer between the two materials, serving as the foundational measurements for subsequent mathematical modeling and gradient extraction of the interface region.

caption: Moduli profiles for F3–BM, F4–BM, and F6–BM at 90 °C, highlighting the rapid gelation and subsequent modulus increase for higher functionality variants.
summary: Measured at 90 °C, the storage and loss moduli demonstrate the gelation behavior of the BM mixtures. F6–BM exhibits the fastest percolation. The storage modulus for F4–BM and F6–BM continues to rise after the critical gel conversion is reached, indicating ongoing reaction kinetics compared to the F3–BM variant.

caption: Linear grading strategy for hollow octet-truss lattices, showing the thickness variation, internal hollow sections, and the mathematical definition of wall thickness as a function of the z-coordinate.
summary: This panel illustrates the linear grading strategy for hollow octet-truss lattices. It details the thickness grading and internal hollow sections, where wall thickness is defined as a function of the z-coordinate. The design involves subtracting varying interior channel diameters, ranging from 0.6 mm to 1.2 mm, from the exterior strut.

caption: Mechanical strain field in the tensile direction for the OP cycle, measured via DIC at maximum cyclic stress with a 3 mm crack length.
summary: Digital image correlation reveals the mechanical strain field during the OP cycle at maximum cyclic stress. The strain distribution is averaged over three cycles near the crack tip. Level curves at 0.5% and 0.75% strain highlight the deformation, confirming the thermo-mechanical constitutive behavior observed under these specific test conditions.

caption: Residual stress distribution in the LPBF Inconel 625 alloy measured as a function of depth.
summary: The residual stress profile of the LPBF Inconel 625 alloy is presented as a function of depth. This measurement is vital for understanding the internal stress states induced by the rapid solidification and thermal gradients inherent in the laser powder bed fusion process, which significantly influence the material's mechanical behavior.

caption: Overview of the newly developed long-term wear simulator apparatus.
summary: This panel displays the newly developed long-term wear simulator used for experimental testing. The apparatus is designed to facilitate extended wear studies, providing a controlled environment for evaluating material durability over prolonged periods as part of the experimental setup described in the study.

caption: Ni K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 12.
summary: Ni K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra for Ni Alloy 59 are measured in total reflection geometry at pH 12. This measurement facilitates the assessment of Ni surface chemistry in highly alkaline environments, contributing to the comprehensive X-ray absorption study of Ni Alloy 59 across different pH levels and measurement geometries.

caption: Load-displacement curves for Onyx relative density graded lattices, highlighting the response of the most severely graded configuration.
summary: This panel presents the load-displacement behavior of Onyx relative density graded lattices. The force profiles exhibit multiple peaks, reflecting the failure mechanisms that contribute to crashworthiness. The plot specifically characterizes the response of the most severely graded configuration, demonstrating how structural grading influences the mechanical load-bearing capacity of Onyx.

caption: Scatter band plot illustrating the correlation between predicted and experimental fatigue lifetime values.
summary: This parity plot serves as a validation tool for the model's predictive accuracy regarding fatigue lifetime. By comparing predicted values against experimental data within a scatter band, the figure demonstrates the model's performance and reliability in estimating fatigue life, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed computational approach in material fatigue analysis.

caption: Feature importance analysis detailing the dynamic mechanical performance of Gyroid TPMS architectures for a slenderness ratio L/h = 8.
summary: This panel presents the feature importance results specifically for Gyroid TPMS architectures with a slenderness ratio of L/h = 8. The plot identifies the primary structural drivers of dynamic mechanical performance for this geometry, allowing for a comparative understanding of how Gyroid designs behave under these specific mechanical conditions.

caption: Fracture locus of 3.5 mm WAAM ER70S-6 steel plotted in the stress triaxiality (η) versus equivalent fracture strain (ε‾f) plane, comparing MMC, H-C, and L-H model predictions against experimental test data.
summary: This plot displays the fracture locus for 3.5 mm WAAM ER70S-6 steel in the η-ε‾f plane. By comparing MMC, H-C, and L-H model predictions with experimental test data, the figure demonstrates that these models effectively capture fracture initiation, as evidenced by the close proximity of test points to the predicted loci.

caption: Normalized force-depth curves derived from MD simulations and experimental nanoindentation, with arrowheads indicating the specific depths where pop-in events occur.
summary: Normalized force-depth curves illustrate the mechanical behavior during nanoindentation, with arrowheads marking the precise locations of pop-in events. Comparison between MD simulation and experimental data indicates that the relative positions of these pop-in events do not coincide, suggesting differences in the underlying dislocation dynamics between the two methods.

caption: Quasi-static compression stress-strain curves for ZrCu, 0.5ZrCu–Ti6Al4V, and 0.25ZrCu–Ti6Al4V specimens measured at room temperature in the direction perpendicular to the layers.
summary: This panel displays the quasi-static compression stress-strain behavior of ZrCu and two ZrCu–Ti6Al4V composite variants at room temperature. The tests were conducted in the direction perpendicular to the material layers to evaluate the mechanical response of these laminated structures under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe10 composite showing a minimum value of -4.8 dB.
summary: The Fe10 composite exhibits a reflection loss profile with a minimum value of -4.8 dB. This measurement quantifies the absorption characteristics of the material at a 10 wt% Fe loading, serving as a baseline for evaluating the absorption enhancement achieved with higher iron concentrations in the Fe/PLA/TPU composite system.

caption: Experimental transmission response of beams C and D, showing the measured transmission levels across the frequency spectrum.
summary: Experimental transmission response of beams C and D is shown, displaying the measured transmission levels across the frequency spectrum. The shaded region highlights the longitudinal bandgap, allowing for a direct comparison between the numerical predictions and the actual experimental performance of the beams under the tested conditions.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of RhB-HZ, providing complementary structural information to the proton NMR data.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of RhB-HZ serves as complementary evidence to the 1H NMR data, confirming the carbon-based structural framework of the compound. Together, these spectroscopic analyses validate the chemical composition and molecular integrity of RhB-HZ, ensuring it is properly characterized for subsequent integration into the contact lens material.

caption: Side view of the sample holder assembly positioned within the analysis chamber of a local-electrode atom-probe (LEAP) tomograph.
summary: This image illustrates the final configuration of the copper grid mounted within the LEAP tomograph analysis chamber. It provides a clear view of the sample holder assembly, confirming the readiness of the prepared specimen for high-resolution 3D reconstruction and correlative analysis within the atom-probe system.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the as-built HP-LPBF Ti6Al4V sample, illustrating the initial microstructural grain orientation and morphology prior to any thermal processing.
summary: The as-built HP-LPBF Ti6Al4V sample is characterized via EBSD-IPF mapping to establish the baseline microstructural state. This map provides a visual representation of the initial grain orientations and morphology, serving as the reference point for evaluating the subsequent effects of various annealing treatments on the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the SS/NiCu(1:1) electrode recorded in 1 M KOH at 100 mV s-1, showing the evolution of current density over successive cycles.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry of the SS/NiCu(1:1) electrode in 1 M KOH reveals an increase in current density from 6.9 mA cm-2 to 19.3 mA cm-2 over repeated cycles between +1.0 V and +1.7 V. This evolution indicates the progressive development of active sites on the electrode surface, with the anodic peak detailed in the insert.

caption: Comparison of cycles to failure for A205 alloy specimens across as-fabricated, Standard T7, Commercial, and Rapid heat treatment conditions, evaluated for both vertical and horizontal build orientations.
summary: This panel presents the fatigue performance of A205 alloy at room temperature. It compares the cycles to failure for specimens produced with vertical and horizontal build orientations across four distinct processing conditions: as-fabricated, Standard T7, Commercial, and Rapid heat treatments, providing a comprehensive overview of fatigue life variations.

caption: Time-resolved 2D Small-Angle Scattering (SAS) patterns for Case 1, displaying the evolution of scattering intensity I(q, t) in arbitrary units over time intervals of 10^4.
summary: This panel illustrates the time evolution of 2D SAS patterns for Case 1. The scattering intensity I(q, t) is presented in arbitrary units, with time increments of 10^4. These patterns capture the structural transition occurring within the material as it evolves over the specified experimental time duration.

caption: Energy dispersive spectroscopy analysis detailing the elemental content variation across seven distinct positions within the oxide layer around the 90° film cooling holes after 100 h of oxidation.
summary: Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) analysis provides a detailed profile of elemental content variations across seven distinct positions within the oxide layer. By correlating these compositional findings with Raman spectral data, the structural characteristics and chemical evolution of the oxide layer around the 90° film cooling holes are effectively elucidated.

caption: Surface of an as-cast Al4Fe0.3Zr alloy sample after 50% hot deformation at 400 °C with ultrasonic processing (USP), demonstrating a smooth surface free of cracks.
summary: This photograph shows an Al4Fe0.3Zr alloy sample processed with USP after 50% hot deformation at 400 °C. Unlike the untreated sample, this specimen exhibits a smooth surface with no visible edge or surface cracks, indicating that USP effectively mitigates the cracking susceptibility during the hot rolling process.

caption: Elastic buckling stage of the honeycomb, featuring PEEQ contours that highlight local plastic deformation at the weak end corners of outer cells.
summary: During the elastic buckling stage, stress in the weak end corners of outer honeycomb cells exceeds the material yield point, resulting in local plastic deformation. PEEQ contours clearly visualize these plastic regions, while red and yellow boxes highlight similar deformation patterns observed in experimental and numerical results.

caption: Solute B concentration evolution as a function of dose for A-1%B-1%C ternary alloys under varying defect production rates, simulated with fixed binding energy of 0.1 eV and E2(C) of 0.8 eV.
summary: This plot illustrates the impact of defect production rates on solute B concentration in A-1%B-1%C ternary alloys. Increasing the defect production rate from 10^-5 dpa/s to 5*10^-4 dpa/s extends solute retention kinetics by approximately a factor of two, demonstrating the significant influence of irradiation conditions on solute stability in these systems.

caption: EBSD Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of sample 7, mapping the local misorientation intensity.
summary: The KAM map for sample 7 maps the local misorientation intensity, providing insight into the plastic strain distribution. This analysis supports the investigation into how grain size and internal structure affect the yield strength of the material as presented in the study.

caption: σ phase crystal structure and its simulated XRD pattern.
summary: The σ phase is represented by its crystal structure and simulated XRD pattern. This panel contributes to the comprehensive diffraction library, allowing for the identification of this prospective phase in the system based on its unique structural arrangement and the resulting diffraction peak positions.

caption: Performance trends of the XGBoost model across various datasets during the optimization of ultimate tensile strength.
summary: Performance trends of the XGBoost model across various datasets during the optimization of ultimate tensile strength are illustrated. This figure highlights the effectiveness of the hybrid XGBoost-Genetic Algorithm framework in predicting and optimizing mechanical properties, specifically focusing on the ultimate tensile strength within the context of the described computational model.

caption: Structural layout for N=20 with isotropic material, color-coded by the optimized time field to indicate the fabrication sequence.
summary: Illustrating the fabrication sequence for an isotropic material with N=20, this panel displays the structural layout color-coded by the optimized time field. This visualization highlights the temporal order of the structure's fabrication, derived from the space-time topology optimization approach applied to the vertical beam design.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrating cyclohexanol chemisorption on bimetallic 20Ni-Fe/MCSs catalysts with varying Ni/Fe ratios.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves demonstrate the chemisorption behavior of cyclohexanol on bimetallic 20Ni-Fe/MCSs catalysts. Experimental results indicate that the cyclohexanol uptake on these catalysts increases from 129 μmol g cat −1 to 187 μmol g cat −1 as the Ni/Fe ratio decreases, highlighting the influence of metal composition on surface adsorption capacity.

caption: Electrical transport characteristics of a graphene-based field-effect transistor (FET) device, showing a high hole mobility of 2769 cm²/V·s measured at room temperature.
summary: Electrical characterization of the graphene-based field-effect transistor demonstrates a high hole mobility of 2769 cm²/V·s at room temperature. This performance confirms the electronic viability of the graphene grown on Cu-Ni alloy, with an average mobility of approximately 2593.6 ± 156.5 cm²/V·s across tested devices.

caption: Final frame at 2.27 msec showing the completed reaction across the Double C pattern geometry.
summary: The final frame at 2.27 msec displays the reaction after completion across the entire Double C pattern. This image confirms the total consumption of the material following the propagation path, marking the end of the observed reaction sequence within the structured foil geometry under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification performance of the 3DCNN model trained in the DP setting.
summary: Displayed is the confusion matrix for the 3DCNN model utilizing the DP setting. This visualization allows for a direct comparison with the non-DP model, highlighting how the DP configuration influences the model's ability to correctly classify objects and mitigate errors arising from the resemblance among different object categories.

caption: Design layout of the infill pattern used for the internal structure of the printed components.
summary: The infill design configuration is shown, highlighting the internal structural arrangement of the printed Mg-BASE parts. This design parameter is crucial for controlling the density and mechanical properties of the final 3D-printed structure, complementing the slicing strategy to achieve the desired material performance.

caption: Enlarged BSE image and corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental maps highlighting the spatial distribution of the η phase and Hf-rich oxides.
summary: The enlarged view provides a detailed look at the η phase and associated Hf oxides. EDS mapping confirms the chemical composition of these features, identifying the particles as nano-sized HfO2. The homogeneous distribution of these small, Ni- and Hf-rich oxides is critical for the material's structural integrity.

caption: Crystallographic pole figure showing the orientation relationship between the σ phase and the γ matrix, defined by [011]γ || [140]σ and (111)γ || (001)σ.
summary: Panel (d) specifically illustrates the crystallographic orientation relationship between the σ phase and the γ matrix. The determined relationship, [011]γ || [140]σ and (111)γ || (001)σ, confirms findings from previous research. This pole figure is critical for understanding the structural interface and lattice alignment between the precipitate and the matrix.

caption: Two-beam bright-field TEM micrograph showing the dislocation structure within γ grains at the bottom-edge position of the billet.
summary: This two-beam bright-field TEM micrograph illustrates the dislocation structure within the γ grains of the bottom-edge sample. Observations indicate that only a small number of dislocations are present, suggesting that these dislocations bypass the secondary γ′ precipitates during the deformation process within this specific region of the billet.

caption: Pareto chart of standardized effects for surface roughness (Sa) in the PBD analysis of Cu–Cr–Zr alloy.
summary: This Pareto chart illustrates the standardized effects of various process parameters on the surface roughness of the Cu–Cr–Zr alloy. Statistical analysis identifies layer thickness as the most significant parameter affecting Sa, which is essential for controlling the surface quality of components produced via the LPBF manufacturing process.

caption: Loading-unloading curves for printed Ti6Al4V powder on an LPBFed AlSi12 substrate, showing variations across different distances from the interface.
summary: Loading-unloading curves for LPBFed Ti6Al4V powders are displayed at various distances from the interface. By referencing the fifth printed layer, it is observed that moving toward the interface correlates with a significant increase in tensile residual stresses, indicating a gradient in mechanical state within the powder layers.

caption: SAED pattern from the interface between bcc grain (1) and fcc grain (2) along the [111]α and [110]γ zone axes, demonstrating a Kurdjumov–Sachs orientation relationship.
summary: This SAED pattern, taken from the interface between bcc grain (1) and fcc grain (2), confirms that the two phases share a Kurdjumov–Sachs orientation relationship: (111)γ ‖ (110)α and [110]γ ‖ [111]α. This crystallographic alignment is a key feature of the phase interface in the aged material.

caption: DMA temperature ramp curve for VeroWhite showing the storage modulus and tan delta response.
summary: The DMA temperature ramp measurement for VeroWhite is presented, illustrating the material's viscoelastic behavior. Analysis of the tan delta peak, which represents the maximum loss factor, identifies a glass transition temperature of 66.5 °C for this specific polymer specimen under the applied thermal conditions.

caption: Raman spectrum of the PEO-X sample after 504 hours of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Displayed is the Raman spectrum for the PEO-X sample following 504 hours of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. This measurement provides critical data on the chemical stability and surface composition of the PEO-X material, contributing to the overall assessment of how different PEO modifications influence corrosion behavior.

caption: Total Ah-throughput of second-life batteries plotted as a function of C-rate.
summary: This plot illustrates the usable total Ah-throughput of second-life batteries across varying C-rates. By analyzing the relationship between discharge rates and cumulative capacity, the figure provides critical data on the performance degradation and operational longevity of battery systems when subjected to different electrical load conditions during their second-life phase.

caption: Isothermal section at the ternary eutectoid reaction temperature, illustrating the formation of the oP6 phase via the reaction γ + P + Ni3Mo → oP6.
summary: This panel displays the isothermal section at the ternary eutectoid reaction temperature. It demonstrates the phase transformation pathway where the oP6 phase is formed through the ternary peritectoid reaction involving γ, P, and Ni3Mo phases, marking a significant change in the equilibrium state of the Ni-Cr-Mo system at lower temperatures.

caption: Cr–Fe–Ni ternary equilibrium phase diagram at 650 °C, illustrating the specific chemical composition regions corresponding to the first and second layers of the two-layered printing process.
summary: This ternary equilibrium phase diagram for the Cr–Fe–Ni system at 650 °C provides a critical overview of the phase stability for the two-layered printing process. By mapping the chemical compositions of the first and second layers, the diagram identifies the equilibrium phases present during the fabrication of the printed alloy.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HTHed Diamond sample measured at temperatures around the FM-PM transition.
summary: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HTHed Diamond sample are presented, detailing the magnetic behavior at temperatures near the ferromagnetic to paramagnetic transition. These results facilitate a comprehensive analysis of the magnetic phase transition nature within the diamond-structured sample, providing insight into its specific magnetic response.

caption: Force-displacement curves for the P structure under axial compression, demonstrating the sensitivity to the length scale parameter l c with a constant mesh size ratio of h = 0.3 l c .
summary: This panel displays force-displacement curves for the P structure under axial compression, illustrating the sensitivity analysis of the length scale parameter l c . The mesh size was maintained at 3/10 of l c to evaluate the global response, showing how varying l c influences the mechanical behavior of the structure.

caption: Visual appearance of the sintered copper sample geometry used for tensile testing.
summary: This photograph displays the physical geometry and appearance of the sintered copper sample used for tensile testing. The image provides a clear view of the specimen's form, confirming the sample preparation quality prior to the mechanical evaluation of its tensile properties and fracture behavior.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the HIP+STA specimen highlighting fine and coarse γ' precipitates.
summary: Utilizing the <100> superlattice reflection, this dark-field TEM image shows the γ' phase in the HIP+STA specimen. The micrograph highlights a higher content of fine γ' precipitates compared to other specimens, with particles of 50 nm and 300 nm coexisting, illustrating the complex microstructure achieved through the HIP+STA treatment.

caption: Schematic representation of the Failure Assessment Diagram (FAD) approach, illustrating the Failure Assessment Line (FAL) and two specific assessment points, A and B, which denote unacceptable, unsafe conditions for analyzed components.
summary: This schematic illustrates the FAD methodology used to evaluate component safety. Points A and B represent average assessment points at failure for experimental tests, with and without notch correction, respectively. Points located above the FAL are considered unsafe, while those within the area defined by the FAL and axes are safe.

caption: Texture map displaying fracture stress and strain for different infill patterns, highlighting the performance difference between designs with one or two outer perimeters.
summary: This texture map visualizes the fracture stress and strain characteristics of the cryogel designs. A consistent trend is observed where infill patterns featuring two outer perimeters exhibit increased fracture stress compared to those with a single perimeter, indicating that perimeter thickness is a critical factor in determining the mechanical failure limits of these structures.

caption: Normalized emission spectra of ZCIS/ZnS quantum dot colloidal dispersions synthesized at varying temperatures with a 30-minute shell addition reaction time.
summary: Normalized emission spectra for ZCIS/ZnS quantum dot colloidal dispersions are presented, highlighting the optical response of samples prepared at different synthesis temperatures. These spectra demonstrate the characteristic photoluminescence behavior of the quantum dots following a 30-minute shell addition process, providing insight into the electronic transitions influenced by the synthesis conditions.

caption: GDMS signal intensity of 27 Al, 48 Ti, and 109 Ag isotopes measured across M-0, M-C, M-S, and SLM configurations at a discharge voltage of 2.0 kV and pressure of 6.50 mPa.
summary: This mass spectrum displays the signal intensities for 27 Al, 48 Ti, and 109 Ag across four different configurations. The measurements were conducted under controlled conditions of 2.0 kV discharge voltage and 6.50 mPa pressure to compare the analytical performance and signal response of each sputtering setup.

caption: FTIR spectra of the scaffolds displaying characteristic peaks at 874 cm-1, 1090 cm-1, and 3444 cm-1, corresponding to Si–O bending, Si–O symmetric stretching, Si–O–Si stretching, and OH group vibrations, respectively.
summary: FTIR analysis characterizes the chemical composition of the organic and inorganic components within the scaffolds. The spectrum reveals specific vibrational modes, including Si–O bending at 874 cm-1, symmetric Si–O stretching at 1090 cm-1, and OH group vibrations at 3444 cm-1, confirming the presence of these functional groups in the scaffold material.

caption: Synchrotron in-situ X-ray image showing pore distribution in the melt pool processed at 350 W and 500 mm/min.
summary: This synchrotron in-situ X-ray image displays the pore distribution at 350 W and 500 mm/min. At this lower scanning speed, the number of residual bubbles increases dramatically compared to higher speeds. Bubbles concentrate at the front wall and bottom of the melt track boundary, becoming trapped as pore defects.

caption: High magnification metallographic photograph of 18Ni300 maraging steel in the CA-SO-AG condition.
summary: This high magnification metallographic photograph illustrates the microstructure of 18Ni300 maraging steel after undergoing the CA-SO-AG processing sequence. The image captures the specific structural state of the material, facilitating a detailed comparison with other processing conditions to understand the evolution of the steel's microstructure under these parameters.

caption: BNN PSN testing set curve displaying the R50 experimental fit, Owen R90C90 curve, and BNN predictions, illustrating the model's generalization capability on unseen data.
summary: Representing a testing set, this plot evaluates the BNN model's predictive accuracy on unseen data. By comparing the BNN mean prediction and individual outputs against the R50 experimental fit and Owen R90C90 curve, the figure confirms that the results are significantly improved for this specific testing set.

caption: EBSD-derived Taylor factor map for the transverse direction (TD) of the as-LPBF-ed specimen.
summary: This EBSD-derived map displays the Taylor factor distribution across the transverse direction of the as-LPBF-ed material. By mapping these factors, the panel provides insight into the macroscopic hardening behavior and the resistance to plastic deformation, reflecting the influence of the LPBF fabrication process on the material's internal grain structure.

caption: Nyquist plots comparing the electrochemical impedance response of the Al0.5MnFeNiCu0.5 layer, Al–Ni graded coating, and substrate, highlighting the high-frequency arc radius.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for the Al0.5MnFeNiCu0.5 layer, Al–Ni layer, and substrate. The Al0.5MnFeNiCu0.5 layer exhibits the largest arc radius in the high-frequency region, indicating superior corrosion resistance compared to the Al–Ni layer and the substrate, which show similar impedance behavior in that frequency range.

caption: Extract ion thermograms of Cs raw material identifying fragment ions at m/z 59, 67, and 114 corresponding to specific degradation products.
summary: Extract ion thermograms for Cs raw material track the release of specific degradation products during EGA-MS analysis. Key fragment ions identified include m/z 59 for acetamide, m/z 67 for pyrrole, and m/z 114 for methyl N-acetyl-d-glucosamide, providing a detailed chemical profile of the material's thermal decomposition pathway.

caption: Pareto chart displaying the most significant factors influencing the fatigue performance of Hastelloy X.
summary: Hastelloy X fatigue performance is analyzed through this Pareto chart, which ranks the most effective factors of interest. The plot clearly distinguishes the primary drivers of fatigue behavior, offering a concise representation of the most impactful variables that govern the mechanical performance of this alloy under fatigue conditions.

caption: Raman spectra of 3D YSZ microarchitectures annealed at temperatures ranging from 600 °C to 1200 °C for a duration of one hour, highlighting the F2g mode region and the presence of a silicon substrate peak.
summary: Raman spectra for 3D YSZ microarchitectures annealed for one hour at temperatures between 600 °C and 1200 °C are presented. The data, collected within the 50–850 cm⁻¹ range, show the F2g mode centered at approximately 612 cm⁻¹, indicating a crystallographic phase resembling ZrO2 stabilized with ≥17 wt% Y2O3.

caption: Factor information table detailing the parameters utilized in the regression analysis for 3D printing roughness.
summary: This table presents the factor information used in the regression analysis to evaluate the impact of parameter settings on the surface roughness of 3D printed components. It serves as the foundational data structure for the subsequent statistical modeling and analysis of variance presented in the study.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of RhB-HZ, providing complementary structural information to the proton NMR data.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of RhB-HZ serves as a complementary analytical tool to the 1H NMR data. By providing distinct carbon resonances, it confirms the molecular framework of the RhB-HZ compound, ensuring a comprehensive spectroscopic characterization of the material's chemical structure and composition.

caption: Maximum displacement s m before crack initiation for Ti5553 specimens during impact testing at 293 K and 20 K.
summary: Maximum displacement s m before crack initiation is shown for Ti5553. This panel illustrates the extent of deformation the material undergoes before the onset of cracking during impact testing at 293 K and 20 K, serving as a key indicator of the material's displacement capacity under high-rate loading at different temperatures.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the dissolution rate characteristics of the gamma phase in Super duplex stainless steel weld metal.
summary: This Arrhenius plot details the dissolution rate of the gamma phase in Super duplex stainless steel weld metal. The visualization highlights the temperature-dependent dissolution behavior, showing that despite differences in absolute magnitude between experimental and calculated data, the observed trends remain consistent across the studied duplex stainless steel grades.

caption: Dark-field TEM image corresponding to the γ reflection of population I precipitates marked in panel (c).
summary: This dark-field TEM image highlights the distribution of population I γ-precipitates by utilizing the specific γ reflection identified in the SAED pattern from panel (c). The image provides visual confirmation of the precipitate morphology and spatial arrangement within the βo matrix for the first population of particles.

caption: Mean squared error (MSE) plotted against varying window sizes to determine the optimal number of preceding time steps for the predictive model.
summary: This plot illustrates the mean squared error (MSE) performance on the validation dataset across different window sizes. Analysis of the results indicates that a window size of three achieves the lowest MSE, leading to its selection as the optimal number of preceding time steps for the model input configuration.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy elemental mapping of the powder cross-section for Al, O, Co, and Ni, demonstrating the spatial distribution of elements and confirming the location of the NiAl-rich bcc region via Al enrichment.
summary: WDS elemental mapping of the powder cross-section provides spatial distribution data for Al, O, Co, and Ni. These maps confirm the chemical heterogeneity of the powder, specifically identifying the NiAl-rich bcc region through the localized enrichment of aluminum, which correlates with the lamellar features observed in the cross-sectional micrograph.

caption: SEM image at a 30° tilt of a 200 μm thick support beam.
summary: This SEM image, captured at a 30° tilt, displays a support beam with a reduced thickness of 200 μm. The image provides a detailed view of the printed structure's geometry before the nitrogen stream is applied, serving as a baseline for comparison with the thicker 300 μm beams.

caption: Multiple arrest events in as-quenched Ni55Fe18Nd2Ga25 ribbons, with labels h1 through h4 denoting the chronological sequence of incomplete heating cycles.
summary: Multiple magnetic arrest phenomena are illustrated for the as-quenched Ni55Fe18Nd2Ga25 alloy ribbons. The plot tracks the chronological progression of four distinct incomplete heating cycles, labeled h1 to h4, which characterize the complex thermal memory effect exhibited by the sample during sequential thermal treatment processes.

caption: Misorientation distribution histogram derived from the grain boundary data in panel (a).
summary: This histogram quantifies the grain boundary misorientation distribution for the Ni–45%Cu alloy at 90 K. By analyzing the orientation differences between adjacent grains, the plot provides a statistical overview of the misorientation angles present in the microstructure following the specified undercooling treatment.

caption: Comparative compressive deformation behavior of as-built and HT-1050 samples observed at varying strain levels.
summary: This panel illustrates the compressive deformation behavior of as-built and HT-1050 samples at different strain levels. It provides a visual representation of how the structural integrity and load-bearing capacity of the samples evolve throughout the compression process, reflecting the differences in their mechanical responses as observed in the stress-strain curves.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) comparison for Fe3C, Ni, and Fe/Ni alloy, demonstrating an upward shift in the d-band center for the alloy.
summary: PDOS analysis reveals the electronic structure differences between Fe3C, Ni, and the Fe/Ni alloy. The data indicates that the d-band center of the Fe/Ni alloy shows a pronounced upward shift relative to Fe3C, which is a critical factor in modifying the catalytic activity of the material.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the SA l-PBF Ni-based superalloy showing the spatial distribution of internal defects and representative morphologies.
summary: This panel presents the micro-CT test area and a 3D reconstructed image of an SA l-PBF Ni-based superalloy. It visualizes the spatial distribution of internal defects within the material volume, highlighting various typical defect shapes identified through the reconstruction process to characterize the internal structural integrity of the superalloy.

caption: Radar chart presenting the relative TF–IDF scores for keywords and keyphrases, reflecting their statistical relevance within the analyzed research text.
summary: The radar chart displays the relative TF–IDF scores for key terms, providing a measure of their statistical importance. By setting the TF-DF weight to 1.0, this visualization highlights the most statistically relevant concepts in the research, offering a weighted perspective on the strength–ductility paradigm in additively manufactured alloys.

caption: Shear modulus G predictions derived from the GPR surrogate model, showing the relationship between RVE size and mechanical response at a fixed shell thickness of t/l = 0.09.
summary: Representing the shear modulus G, this panel illustrates the GPR surrogate model's performance in mapping the V surface design space. The results demonstrate that increasing the RVE size leads to a reduction in variance, consistent with the expected statistical homogenization behavior observed across the mechanical property predictions for this specific geometry.

caption: Coupling relationship between Reference Points (RPs) and node sets, where RP1 governs X-direction displacement and RP2 governs Y-direction displacement.
summary: The diagram depicts the coupling mechanism between specific Reference Points and node sets within the RVE model. RP1 is explicitly assigned to control displacement along the X-axis, while RP2 manages displacement along the Y-axis, facilitating precise control over the deformation behavior of the binary unit cell with stepped boundaries.

caption: Explained variance ratio of principal components derived from feature set f.
summary: This plot illustrates the explained variance ratio for each principal component calculated from the feature set f. By visualizing the contribution of individual components, the figure provides insight into the dimensionality reduction process, highlighting how much information is retained by each principal component within the analyzed dataset.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy images of white nanophases in 13Co + Sc alloys, paired with corresponding EDS elemental mapping results.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy images of white nanophases in 13Co + Sc alloys, paired with corresponding EDS elemental mapping results. These maps confirm the presence of elements such as B, C, Al, and Ti within the nanophases, providing insight into the composition of the precipitates.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ single-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 1000°C thermal treatment, showing consistent defect-related luminescence.
summary: Cathodoluminescence spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures after a 1000°C thermal cycle. The defect-related emission remains consistent with the 750°C cycle results. The spectra compare Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ dopants at 2.5 mol% and 0.35 mol%, providing insight into the luminescence behavior of the microarchitectures under high-temperature treatment conditions.

caption: Target image representing the reference conductivity distribution for the lung phantom center slice.
summary: This target image serves as the reference conductivity distribution for the center slice of the lung phantom. It provides a comparative baseline for evaluating the accuracy of the absolute EIT reconstruction images, illustrating the expected conductivity patterns within the phantom structure under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of a vertical specimen subjected to cyclic straining at a strain amplitude of 6 × 10⁻³.
summary: Bright-field STEM imaging reveals the microstructural state of a vertical specimen following cyclic straining at a strain amplitude of 6 × 10⁻³. This visualization highlights the specific dislocation arrangements and structural features developed under these loading conditions, serving as a comparative baseline for assessing orientation-dependent deformation behavior in the material.

caption: Load-displacement response for the T-RT specimen, highlighting the similarity in deformation regions compared to the C-RT specimen.
summary: The load-displacement curve for the T-RT specimen illustrates the mechanical behavior at room temperature. The plot confirms that the plasticity onset and membrane stretching regions are very similar to those observed in the C-RT specimen, indicating consistent mechanical performance under these test conditions.

caption: Top-down interfacial bonding configuration after 1000 cascade collisions, showing the final state of the bonding network.
summary: This final top-down snapshot displays the interfacial bonding configuration after 1000 cascades. It confirms that the dual bonding patterns observed throughout the irradiation process remain consistent, even as the spatial distribution of metal-carbon bonds continues to evolve significantly due to the cumulative effects of the cascade collisions.

caption: Bar chart comparison summarizing the mechanical and damping performance metrics of TPU/PLA filaments with different ratios.
summary: Bar chart comparison summarizing the mechanical and damping performance metrics of TPU/PLA filaments with different ratios. This chart synthesizes the findings from the mechanical and damping property tests, allowing for a direct quantitative comparison of how varying the PLA content affects the overall performance of the composite filaments.

caption: Representative fluorescence images of DCFH-DA stained cells following a 2-hour H2O2 treatment.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images reveal the intracellular ROS levels after H2O2 exposure. Compared to the Bre control group, the fluorescence intensity within cells is significantly reduced in both the Bre@PDA and Bre@PDA-Ful groups, indicating effective ROS scavenging activity provided by the PDA and fullerol components within the scaffold materials.

caption: Magnified view of the IP loading substructure, highlighting prominent cell boundaries and dislocation-free cell interiors.
summary: Magnified TEM imaging of the IP loading condition provides a detailed look at the dislocation cell structure. The cells are defined by prominent boundaries and notably contain dislocation-free interiors. This observation confirms that the IP loading mechanism effectively restricts dislocation accumulation within the interior regions of the formed cells.

caption: Bode-phase angle diagrams for repaired samples and substrate in a 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: Bode-phase angle diagrams are analyzed alongside impedance modulus data to characterize the electrochemical behavior of the samples in a 3.5% NaCl solution. These trends align with the Nyquist curves, collectively confirming that sample A2 possesses the optimal corrosion resistance, supported by a validated equivalent circuit model fitting.

caption: Residual shear resistance and residual relative displacement as functions of nodular pile node widths.
summary: Residual shear resistance and residual relative displacement are presented to show the long-term shear behavior of the interface. The results indicate that the disappearance of the node invalidates the interlocking effect, which serves as evidence for the load transfer mechanism at the nodular pile-cemented soil interface proposed in this study.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the performance scorecards for grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V powders, comparing virgin and carbon-blended variants across seven qualitative and quantitative metrics including segregation, spreadability, bulk flow, CBD, dynamic flow, and cohesion.
summary: This radar chart evaluates grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V powders by comparing virgin and carbon-blended samples. Performance is assessed through seven qualitative and quantitative metrics, such as segregation, spreadability, and various flow properties. These scorecards facilitate the selection of blended powders that are comparable to virgin counterparts for LPBF printing applications.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to extracts from SLM-processed Ti.
summary: Human Gingival Fibroblasts incubated for 72 hours with extracts from SLM-processed Ti are visualized using fluorescence microscopy. The Live/Dead staining technique distinguishes between live (green) and dead (red) cells, offering an assessment of the cellular viability and biocompatibility of the SLM-processed titanium over an extended 72-hour period.

caption: Comparative SHAP summary plot showing the collective influence of various trace elements on the overall discrimination of parental magma types in quartz-bearing deposits.
summary: This SHAP summary plot provides a comprehensive view of how multiple trace elements in quartz collectively influence the discrimination of parental magma types. By visualizing the contribution of each element, the plot clarifies the model's decision-making process, supporting the identification of specific deposit types based on trace element signatures.

caption: Bar chart comparing the Young's modulus of samples B.1.F, B.2.E, B.3.U, C.1.F, and C.3.U, determined via extensometer, strain gauges, and DIC.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the Young's modulus for various samples, including bending (B) and compression (C) specimens. Data were derived from integrated extensometers, strain gauges, and DIC techniques. The results, averaged from two strain gauges, provide a comparative overview of elastic properties across different testing configurations and material conditions.

caption: Tensile strength and fracture toughness data for Type I interface specimens in R60 concrete plotted against the initial notch-to-depth ratio.
summary: The mechanical response of R60 concrete with a Type I interface is analyzed by plotting tensile strength and fracture toughness against the notch-to-depth ratio. The data demonstrates that the loading direction and notch-to-depth ratio have a marginal effect on these properties, with average values remaining consistent across the tested ratios.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of IN625 tested at 870 °C, displaying the microstructure away from the fracture surface with small cavities marked by black arrows.
summary: Representing the region away from the fracture surface for IN625 tested at 870 °C, this inverse pole figure map confirms the presence of small cavities. These features, marked by black arrows, are associated with dynamic recrystallized grains, consistent with the cavitation mechanism observed throughout the specimen at this temperature.

caption: Contour map of the effective Young’s modulus (E*) plotted against j/i and k/i, identifying regions of maximum modulus near k/i = 0.55, j/i = 0.5 and minimum modulus at j/i = 2.5, k/i = 3.5.
summary: The contour plot provides a top-down view of the effective Young’s modulus distribution. It clearly delineates the parameter space, pinpointing the specific regions where the modulus reaches its maximum and minimum values, thereby facilitating the identification of optimal structural configurations based on the j/i and k/i ratios.

caption: Temperature versus mole fraction of solid (T-Fs) curve for the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr alloy, illustrating the solidification path and sequence of phase formation including primary Al3(Ti,Zr) and Al-Al3Ni eutectic.
summary: The T-Fs curve derived from Scheil-Gulliver solidification simulation reveals the solidification path of the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr alloy. It highlights the formation of primary Al3(Ti,Zr) precipitates, which act as heterogeneous nucleation sites, and the subsequent Al-Al3Ni eutectic, which helps prevent lack of fusion defects during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Tan delta (δ) as a function of temperature, highlighting the glass transition temperature (Tg) values of -2.9 °C for GME and -4.2 °C for FFF, alongside a broad peak indicating minimal distinction between glassy and rubbery states.
summary: The Tan delta versus temperature plot reveals the glass transition temperatures for the two materials, with GME at -2.9 °C and FFF at -4.2 °C. The broad, flat δ peak suggests an unclear transition between the glassy and rubbery states, reflecting the material's viscoelastic behavior and chain dynamics.

caption: Frequency locking ratios plotted to reveal the characteristic structure of a partial devil’s staircase, demonstrating the transition dynamics within the system.
summary: The frequency locking ratios are visualized to reveal a partial devil’s staircase, which characterizes the RFL mechanism behind the transition from 41-kyr to 100-kyr cycles. This plot illustrates the complex locking behavior observed in the system as it evolves according to the data-derived approximations.

caption: Boxplot of vector length deviations for SLA-processed surgical guides printed in a horizontal orientation after steam sterilization.
summary: Horizontal SLA-printed surgical guides are analyzed via a boxplot showing vector length deviations from the CAD file. Measuring 17 reference points post-steam sterilization, this visualization captures the dimensional variance inherent to the SLA process, offering insight into how horizontal orientation influences the structural stability of the guides after sterilization.

caption: Report generated from the GSMobile software for strut measurement.
summary: This panel displays a report generated by the GSMobile software, detailing the measurements of the lattice struts. The report provides quantitative data derived from the analysis, supporting the characterization of the strut dimensions and ensuring consistency in the measurement protocol applied across different sample types.

caption: Heatmap illustrating the evolution of absolute prediction error for layer coding across 17 incremental update rounds, with the vertical axis representing ground truth layer numbers (1–50) and the color scale indicating the magnitude of deviation.
summary: This heatmap visualizes the performance evolution of a layer coding model over 17 update rounds. By plotting ground truth layer numbers against update rounds, it demonstrates that prediction errors are initially high but systematically decrease as the model adapts to the acoustic signal distribution and structure-induced modulation over time.

caption: Cross-entropy loss evolution plotted against training epochs for the CNN-2 model.
summary: This panel displays the cross-entropy loss trajectory for the CNN-2 model over 100 training epochs. The curve illustrates the convergence behavior of the model during the training process for two distinct data distributions, providing a quantitative measure of the optimization progress achieved by the network throughout the learning phase.
