caption: Young’s and shear moduli of fcc Fe-Ni alloys as a function of composition, showing calculated values from SQS models alongside experimental and theoretical literature data.
summary: Calculated Young’s and shear moduli for fcc Fe-Ni alloys are presented in this panel. The data, derived from 16- and 32-atom SQS models, show reasonable agreement with existing literature values. The plot demonstrates the compositional dependence of these elastic moduli, validating the computational approach against established experimental and theoretical datasets.

caption: Reconstructed prior β-phase inverse pole figure map for the Ti–5Cu specimen.
summary: Reconstructed prior β grains for the Ti–5Cu alloy are displayed in this inverse pole figure map. The prior β grain structure shows continued refinement with the increased copper addition, confirming the trend observed in the Ti–3Cu sample and aligning with the structural data obtained from XRD measurements.

caption: Statistical analysis of scaffold resistance versus channel radius, demonstrating no significant difference across all tested scaffold groups.
summary: This plot presents the electrical resistance of the scaffolds as a function of channel radius. Statistical analysis using the Kruskal-Wallis test confirms that there is no significant difference in resistance between the various scaffold groups, indicating that the manufacturing process maintains consistent electrical properties across the different sizes tested.

caption: Normalized neutron diffraction patterns of the (220) plane for IN690 alloy, demonstrating the characteristic peak broadening and shift associated with increasing mechanical strain.
summary: Panel (c) presents the (220) diffraction peak evolution for IN690 during deformation up to 11.8% strain. The observed broadening and shifts in the diffraction patterns reflect the underlying lattice parameter changes. These diffraction features are essential for accurately determining dislocation density as the material progresses through elastic and plastic deformation stages.

caption: Three-dimensional representation of coefficient C versus strain and strain rate for the solution-treated state.
summary: Three-dimensional mapping of coefficient C against strain and ln ε ˙ * for the solution-treated state highlights the coupled influence of these variables. The visualization reveals significant dependencies of C on both strain rate and strain, illustrating the material's mechanical response surface under varying deformation conditions.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the WC/HEA cermet containing 30 wt% binder, illustrating phase stability within the 600–1200 °C application range.
summary: The pseudo-binary phase diagram for the WC/HEA cermet with 30 wt% HEA binder content was plotted to verify the stability of the phases present. This analysis confirms the material's phase behavior within the intended application temperature range of 600–1200 °C.

caption: Detailed analysis of thermally treated (TT) Ti10Nb samples within the 38.5° to 41.5° 2θ range, with vertical markers indicating expected peak positions for specific phases.
summary: Focusing on the thermally treated Ti10Nb alloy, this panel provides a closer inspection of the angular range around the main α-phase peak. Small vertical traces are used to indicate the expected peak positions for the phases present, facilitating a clearer identification of the structural components resulting from the thermal treatment process.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the cavitation erosion surface shown in panel (g), illustrating the depth and topography of the pits.
summary: This 3D reconstruction provides a topographical view of the cavitation erosion surface after 24 hours of exposure. It effectively illustrates the depth and spatial distribution of the pits, confirming the maximum measured pit depth of 271 micrometers and providing a comprehensive visualization of the final state of material degradation.

caption: Three-dimensional grain structure volume generated via Toucan simulation, representing a 2 mm x 1 mm x 0.25 mm sample composed of five 50 μm layers at a 2.5 μm resolution.
summary: This simulation result illustrates a predicted grain structure volume spanning multiple additive manufacturing meltpools. Generated using the Toucan software on dual NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, the model captures complex grain morphologies and sizes. Such simulations are essential for evaluating how process inputs, including scan patterns, influence the final microstructure in additive manufacturing.

caption: Reflection spectra of opal films produced via the melt-shear technique, with corresponding film colors displayed as circles adjacent to the legend.
summary: Reflection spectra of opal films prepared using the melt-shear technique reveal the optical properties of the compounds. The data shows that reflection peaks for additive-containing compounds are slightly red-shifted compared to the original material, with the resulting film colors indicated by circles next to the figure legend.

caption: Voltage profiles of discharge for printed linear LCO cathodes compared to tape-casted counterparts during the second cycle at various current rates.
summary: This panel displays the voltage profile of discharge at different current rates during the second cycle for cells with printed linear LCO cathodes versus tape-casted cathodes. It provides a direct comparison of the electrochemical discharge behavior between the two cathode fabrication methods under identical testing conditions.

caption: Pole figure representation illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution of the as-deposited TC11 bulk sample.
summary: This pole figure provides a visual representation of the crystallographic orientation distribution within the as-deposited TC11 bulk sample. It serves as a critical diagnostic tool for understanding the texture development resulting from the coaxial WLDED manufacturing process, complementing the microstructural observations obtained from the IPF maps and mechanical testing data.

caption: Theoretical elastic modulus of negative-upsilon structures derived from the Ashby model.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical elastic modulus for negative-upsilon structures, determined through the application of the Ashby model. The visualization highlights the predicted stiffness properties of the material, offering a clear comparison of elastic performance metrics essential for understanding the mechanical behavior of these structures in engineering applications.

caption: Box plot showing the mineral-to-matrix ratio, derived from the area ratio of the phosphate and amide I bands.
summary: The mineral-to-matrix ratio is quantified and displayed as a box plot for all groups. This ratio, calculated by dividing the area of the phosphate band by the area of the amide I band, serves as a critical metric for assessing the relative composition of mineral versus organic matrix in bone.

caption: Response surface showing the influence of interaction terms on the product λ * N.
summary: This panel illustrates the response surface for the interaction term product λ * N. As part of the systematic evaluation of interaction terms in Fig. 9, this plot characterizes how these variables collectively influence the mechanical behavior, providing a clear visualization of the parameter space and its associated response trends.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph focusing on MX precipitates, which are observed to adorn the cell boundaries within the SA + PT LPBF A709 microstructure.
summary: Dark-field TEM analysis specifically highlights the MX precipitates within the SA + PT LPBF A709 sample. These precipitates are shown to be preferentially located along the cell boundaries, demonstrating the specific microstructural positioning of MX carbonitrides following the solution annealing and precipitation treatment process applied to the alloy.

caption: Thermal cycling process showing the alignment between reference temperatures and experimental temperatures across ten cycles, with observed reference temperature drifts from the sixth cycle onwards.
summary: This panel illustrates the cryogenic thermal cycling process, comparing reference temperatures to experimental values over ten cycles. The data demonstrates high alignment, though slight reference temperature drifts appear from the sixth cycle onward, likely caused by mechanical disruptions affecting the thermal coupling of the sample stage's thermocouples during the experiment.

caption: Lattice strain evolution as a function of true stress for the horizontal sample along the loading direction, highlighting the delayed load-bearing response of the HCP phase.
summary: Depicted is the lattice strain evolution for the horizontal sample under tensile loading. Similar to the vertical sample, FCC reflections deviate from linearity before the macroscopic yield point. However, the HCP phase shows poor initial fitting and does not effectively sustain load until the macroscopic yield point is nearly reached.

caption: EDS elemental analysis corresponding to the highlighted regions on the GCr15 ball surface shown in panel (d).
summary: EDS analysis of the GCr15 ball surface at 70°C confirms the presence of transferred material. The elemental mapping validates that a significant amount of wear debris from the Cu-10Sn alloy has been transferred onto the GCr15 counterface, directly influencing the lubrication and wear characteristics of the contact interface.

caption: Atomic unit cell model of the TiAl2 intermetallic compound, constructed based on established literature reports.
summary: This panel presents the unit cell model for the TiAl2 intermetallic phase. Created using data from relevant scientific reports, this model facilitates the study of surface work functions. By analyzing these structures, researchers can better understand the relationship between atomic configuration and the material's inherent corrosion resistance.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction patterns confirming the crystallographic presence of bcc Nb and β-Nb5Si3 phases within the weld track microstructure.
summary: SAED analysis provides definitive crystallographic identification of the phases present in the weld tracks. The diffraction patterns confirm the presence of both bcc Nb and the silicide phase β-Nb5Si3. This phase analysis is consistent across all weld tracks, establishing the fundamental eutectic composition of the alloy system.

caption: Observation of single-mode guidance in the photonic crystal fiber at a wavelength of 1550 nm, where only the fundamental mode is present.
summary: Observation of single-mode guidance in the photonic crystal fiber at a wavelength of 1550 nm, where only the fundamental mode is present. This result confirms that for longer wavelengths, the fiber transitions to a single-mode regime, a behavior that was experimentally validated at the 1550 nm wavelength.

caption: Printing temperature and velocity profiles for melting PEEK during the extrusion process.
summary: This graph displays the printing temperature and velocity associated with melting PEEK. Cross-sectional analysis of the hot zone reveals that the temperature in the center of the flow channel is generally lower than the external temperature, providing insight into the thermal gradients experienced by the material during the printing process.

caption: Enlarged view of the average atomic and chemically disordered grain boundary structure following the relaxation process.
summary: This enlarged view focuses on the grain boundary structure after relaxation, specifically highlighting the average atomic arrangement and chemical disorder. The visualization provides a clear look at the local atomic environment within the grain boundary, which is essential for understanding the stability and mechanical properties of the interface.

caption: Detailed view of the (4 2 0) diffraction peak for A1 HT2 and A2 HT2 samples, demonstrating the displacement resulting from distinct unit cell dimensions.
summary: This inset provides a detailed view of the (4 2 0) diffraction peak for the A1 and A2 samples. The displacement of the peak reflects the different unit cell parameters inherent to the varying compositions of the alloys. This observation confirms the influence of composition on the crystal structure of the samples.

caption: High-angle annular dark field (HAADF) image of the W-20Cu composite powder.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a high-contrast visualization of the W-20Cu composite powder structure. As a primary characterization tool, the HAADF technique highlights the atomic number contrast between the tungsten and copper phases, serving as the foundational view for subsequent elemental mapping and detailed microstructural analysis of the composite particles.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparing synthesized GMA to gelatin, highlighting acrylic proton signals between 5 and 6 ppm and methylene proton signals near 2.9 ppm.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra of synthesized GMA compared to gelatin demonstrate successful functionalization. This is confirmed by an increase in the double peak signal between 5 and 6 ppm, corresponding to acrylic protons from the methacrylate, and a decrease in the single peak signal around 2.9 ppm, representing methylene protons from lysine.

caption: In-situ HEXRD pattern evolution for Scalmalloy under AS6 heat-treatment conditions, highlighting the increased intensity of diffracted peaks compared to the AS3 condition.
summary: This panel illustrates the in-situ HEXRD pattern evolution for Scalmalloy under AS6 heat-treatment conditions, comprising 1713 total diffraction patterns. Comparison with the AS3 condition reveals that time at temperatures above 300 °C has a major impact on precipitation, resulting in a higher number of diffracted peaks in the final profile.

caption: Creep strain response (thin red line) at 950 °C and 300 MPa, shown with the predicted creep curve (thick dashed red line) and the reference fit (thick drawn-out red line) used for parameter calibration.
summary: The red curves represent the creep behavior at 950 °C and 300 MPa. The panel includes the experimental data, the model prediction, and the specific fit used for calibration. The predicted strain for this condition is noted to be highly accurate, validating the underlying model parameters.

caption: Temperature distribution histogram derived from 100 measurements at a fixed temperature of 23.5 °C, fitted with a Gaussian curve to determine the sensor's temperature uncertainty.
summary: This histogram displays the distribution of 100 temperature measurements taken at a fixed 23.5 °C. The data follows a Gaussian distribution with a standard deviation of 0.5 K, which defines the temperature uncertainty of the sensor used in the experiment, confirming the precision of the thermal measurement system.

caption: Sequential photographic documentation of the compression process performed on the D7.5 samples.
summary: Sequential photographic documentation of the compression process performed on the D7.5 samples. These images provide a visual record of the material's deformation behavior during the mechanical testing procedure, capturing the progressive structural changes as the load is applied to the specimen throughout the duration of the compression test.

caption: Watershed segmentation basins corresponding to the 3 px radius opening, where blue represents smaller basins and red represents larger ones.
summary: Watershed segmentation basins derived from the 3 px opening are visualized here, with color-coding indicating basin size. Blue regions denote smaller basins, while red regions indicate larger ones. These basins are essential for quantifying the spatial distribution and homogeneity of particles larger than 3.9 µm in the VSCP sample.

caption: Galvanostatic testing results for a Ni0.50Cu0.50-infiltrated cathode SOEC at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻², displaying a steady increase in voltage over the testing duration.
summary: Voltage and Faradaic efficiency are plotted for a Ni0.50Cu0.50-infiltrated cathode SOEC tested at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻². The data confirms a constant increase in voltage throughout the galvanostatic testing period, which is a characteristic trend observed for all SOECs featuring Cu-based infiltrated cathodes in this study.

caption: FTIR spectra of regenerated 3D-printed honeycomb after 1,2,4-TMB adsorption (blue) versus pure 1,2,4-TMB (red), showing specific aryl and alkyl vibrational modes.
summary: The FTIR spectrum for the 1,2,4-TMB regenerated sample displays distinct vibrational peaks, including C-H aryl stretching near 3000 cm-1, C-C aryl vibrations between 1500 and 1600 cm-1, and C-H deformation between 700 and 900 cm-1. These peaks confirm the presence of residual 1,2,4-TMB adsorbed on the honeycomb structure.

caption: LSV curve of the monolithic perovskite/Si/Ni foil/NiFe photoanode integrated with Ni NWs cathode for unassisted overall water splitting.
summary: The overall water splitting system, utilizing a monolithic photoanode and Ni NWs cathode, achieves a current density of 12.3 mA cm-2 at 0 V under continuous illumination. This measurement confirms the capability of the integrated device to perform unassisted water splitting in a 1.0 M KOH electrolyte under simulated sunlight.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells stained with live/dead markers at day 1 and day 5 post-seeding.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells stained with live/dead markers at day 1 and day 5 post-seeding demonstrate the biocompatibility of the material. Observations reveal negligible dead cells across all treatment groups, confirming that the material exhibits low biotoxicity and supports cell viability throughout the five-day experimental period.

caption: Pseudo binary phase diagram for the MoNbTaWCr x system illustrating phase stability and constituent development.
summary: Representing the MoNbTaWCr x system, this pseudo binary phase diagram highlights the formation of multiple intermetallic constituents. The plot serves as a critical reference for understanding the phase transformations and structural complexity that arise within this specific alloy system as the concentration of chromium is systematically varied.

caption: Friction coefficient evolution over sliding time for nitrided layers tested against ZrO2 balls in a seawater environment.
summary: This plot illustrates the tribological performance of a nitrided layer by tracking the coefficient of friction (COF) over time. The test involves sliding the nitrided material against ZrO2 balls while submerged in seawater, providing a quantitative assessment of the surface layer's wear resistance and frictional stability under corrosive conditions.

caption: E-pH diagram of the Fe-Cr-Mn-H2O system at 288 °C, highlighting the stability regions of iron, chromium, and manganese oxides.
summary: The E-pH diagram for the Fe-Cr-Mn-H2O system at 288 °C illustrates the thermodynamic stability of oxide phases. Notably, the diagram shows the absence of NiFe2O4, which is replaced by a narrow stability region of MnFe2O4, reflecting the very low nickel content in the steels under investigation.

caption: Representative CLSM image of hMSC cultured on AA Pizza C350 segments for 14 days, displaying nuclei (blue), collagen type 1 (green), and cytoskeleton (red) staining.
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy illustrates hMSC behavior on AA Pizza C350 segments after a 14-day culture period. Staining for nuclei, cytoskeleton, and collagen type 1 allows for the evaluation of cellular attachment and matrix production, demonstrating the impact of the AA treatment on the scaffold's biological performance.

caption: Calculated subband structure at an applied bias of 3.8 V, highlighting the third highest Γ subband (Γ31) in green, which demonstrates significant Γ-X mixing with the X11 state.
summary: This figure displays the electronic subband structure at 3.8 V bias. The green-colored wave function, identified as the Γ31 state, originates from a 10-ML QW pair despite its energy line placement in Q6. The visualization specifically illustrates the Γ-X mixing occurring between the Γ31 and X11 states.

caption: Thin and transparent resin islands observed on the surface of a laser-cleaned (LC) sample.
summary: Laser-treated joints (LC) exhibit several thin and transparent resin islands distributed across the surface. These deposits appear as distinct, separate areas, providing visual evidence of the residual resin distribution remaining on the substrate after the laser cleaning process has been applied to the joint surfaces.

caption: Atomic model of SL-Si2O stacking mode III, illustrating the third high-symmetry stacking arrangement.
summary: Stacking mode III is one of the four high-symmetry configurations constructed for the SL-Si2O vdW structure. This model is defined by its unique symmetry properties, providing a distinct geometric arrangement of the layers compared to the other modes, which is essential for analyzing the material's multi-directional NPR effects.

caption: Three-dimensional CT reconstruction of the Base-LF alloy, demonstrating a total pore volume of 0.139 mm3 and a porosity of 0.02%.
summary: This three-dimensional micro-CT reconstruction of the Base-LF alloy displays the internal defect structure. Quantitative analysis of the specimen reveals a total pore volume of 0.139 mm3 and a low porosity of 0.02%, indicating that the specific alloy processing effectively minimizes pore formation within the material's interdendritic regions.

caption: Schematic representation of an isomorphous-type phase diagram for a β Ti-alloy system.
summary: The schematic phase diagram depicts the equilibrium behavior of an isomorphous-type β Ti-alloy. This diagram serves as a foundational reference for understanding the thermodynamic stability and phase boundaries expected in the alloy system, providing a theoretical framework for interpreting the solidification and transformation paths observed in the experimental samples.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve illustrating the thermal behavior of a semi-crystalline polymer, highlighting the sintering window.
summary: This DSC curve characterizes the thermal transition profile of a semi-crystalline thermoplastic. Such materials are preferred in selective laser sintering due to their wider sintering window compared to amorphous counterparts. The curve provides essential data for optimizing preheating and energy input to ensure successful consolidation during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: EPMA-WDS elemental distribution maps of an LBM sample cross-section in the XY plane, oxidized at 850 °C for 3000 h in static air, revealing the spatial arrangement of Al, Ti, and Nb-rich oxide phases.
summary: EPMA-WDS analysis of the LBM sample cross-section reveals the presence of Al and Ti-rich oxides at grain boundaries. Additionally, the maps demonstrate the formation of (Ti,Nb)-rich oxides near the metal-oxide interface, confirming that Nb oxidation occurs after 3000 h of exposure at 850 °C in static air.

caption: Boxplot distribution of KG-MT model performance metrics evaluated on test set 1 and test set 2, generated using seven different random seeds.
summary: Performance metrics for the KG-MT model on two separate test sets are presented as boxplots, reflecting results from seven unique random seeds. These plots demonstrate the model's generalization ability, with the source domain performance serving as an upper-bound benchmark for evaluating the transfer learning effectiveness of the KG-MT approach.

caption: Quantification of vascular density and total vessel length, showing a 10% increase in density and a 1.6-fold increase in length for HEAL with veins compared to printing alone.
summary: Quantitative analysis reveals that incorporating vein structures into the HEAL design significantly enhances angiogenesis. The data show a 10% increase in average vessel density and a 60% increase in total vessel length compared to standard HEAL printing, confirming the efficacy of the modified design in promoting vascular growth.

caption: Bulk texture pole figure for the as-built WAAM-IN718 specimen, exhibiting a maximum texture intensity of 7.5 MRD.
summary: The as-built WAAM-IN718 specimen displays a bulk texture measured via neutron diffraction, which provides a statistically representative analysis of the sample thickness. This condition exhibits a maximum texture intensity of 7.5 MRD, serving as the baseline for comparing the effects of subsequent heat treatments on the material's crystallographic orientation.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves comparing the endothermic evaporation peaks of pure water and water interacting with different LPNC surfaces.
summary: DSC analysis reveals distinct evaporation profiles for pure water and water at the LPNC surface. Pure water exhibits a sharp endothermic peak during evaporation, whereas water at the LPNC surface displays a broader peak, indicating a modified evaporation profile resulting from the interaction between the water molecules and the LPNC material.

caption: Internal view of the experimental chamber capable of reaching temperatures as low as -180 °C and vacuum levels below 1.33 Pa.
summary: This photograph displays the interior of the experimental chamber. The system is designed for high-performance testing, achieving a vacuum environment of less than 1.33 Pa. Furthermore, the chamber supports extreme cryogenic conditions, with internal temperatures capable of reaching -180 °C to facilitate specialized material characterization under controlled environmental parameters.

caption: Functional relationship between microstructural relative density κ and aspect ratio a, comparing least-squares fitting results from a naive approach against data derived from Monte Carlo integration.
summary: This plot illustrates the functional dependence of microstructural relative density κ on the aspect ratio a. It highlights a significant discrepancy between the naive least-squares fitting approach and the more accurate data obtained through Monte Carlo integration, demonstrating the limitations of simplified modeling techniques in capturing complex microstructural characteristics.

caption: Raman spectrum of a carbon fibre grown at 34 bar total pressure, demonstrating an sp3-content of approximately 42% with a D-peak centered at 1337 cm⁻¹.
summary: This Raman spectrum corresponds to a carbon fibre deposited at 397 mW and 34 bar pressure. The analysis indicates an sp3-content of 42% and a D-peak centered at 1337 cm⁻¹. The fibre is also characterized by a hydrogenation level of 15 at.%, reflecting high-pressure growth effects on microstructure.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the standardised effects of process parameters on dilution, with a reference line denoting the threshold for statistical significance.
summary: This Pareto chart displays the standardised effects of various process parameters on dilution. By applying t-statistics to evaluate the null hypothesis of zero impact, the chart identifies significant factors. A reference line is included to clearly distinguish between statistically significant effects and those that do not meet the threshold.

caption: Fatigue test results for notched Scalmalloy specimens (R = 1.5 mm, diameter = 6 mm), displaying stress amplitude versus cycles to failure, categorized by failure initiation sites including surface cracks (solid circles) and internal defects (hollow circles).
summary: Fatigue testing of notched Scalmalloy specimens with a 1.5 mm radius notch reveals the impact of geometry on failure modes. The plot displays stress versus cycles to failure, identifying surface cracks and internal defects as the primary failure drivers, consistent with the observed fatigue behavior in the tested net section.

caption: Fitted curves of H^2 versus 1/h used to determine the average nano-hardness while mitigating indentation size effects.
summary: To determine the intrinsic hardness of the irradiated surface while avoiding indentation size effects, the nano-hardness data is plotted as H^2 against 1/h. This fitting technique allows for the extraction of the real hardness values, providing a more accurate assessment of the material's mechanical performance following He ion irradiation.

caption: Heating and cooling DSC curves for pure PVDF, exhibiting a glass transition temperature at -44.69 °C.
summary: Pure PVDF exhibits a glass transition temperature at -44.69 °C in its DSC heating and cooling curves. This thermal signature is consistent with the flexible nature of the PVDF amorphous phase, serving as a reference point for evaluating the thermal properties of the polymer blends.

caption: Comparative absorption spectra of methylene blue solution initial state versus 60-minute contact with 3D printed scaffolds under UV light exposure.
summary: This panel presents the UV-Vis absorption spectra of methylene blue after 60 minutes of contact with scaffolds under UV light. The results show intensified dye removal in PGMs+TiO2 and PGMs+TiO2+Si samples, achieving removal efficiencies of 73% and 77%, corresponding to final C/C0 ratios of 0.27 and 0.23.

caption: Frequency-dependent capacitance behavior for 15 wt% YP50F flow electrodes evaluated at the end of the experimental run.
summary: This graph displays the capacitance of 15 wt% YP50F flow electrodes measured at the end of the FCDI experiment across a range of frequencies. Consistent with other concentrations, the electrodes show no capacitance at high frequencies, but significant differences in capacitance values are evident at frequencies below 10 mHz.

caption: Raman spectroscopy analysis of IN617 surfaces following 24 hours of immersion in MgNaK chloride at 700ºC in air, used to identify potential spinel phases.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was employed to analyze the IN617 surface after 24 hours of immersion in MgNaK chloride at 700ºC. As shown in panel b, this technique provides critical data to identify potential spinel phases formed during corrosion, which serves to support and confirm the findings from thermodynamic simulations.

caption: Average load-displacement curves for four Cu-based thin foil materials subjected to a 10 mN peak load.
summary: Presented here are the average load-displacement curves for the four Cu-based thin foil materials tested at a 10 mN peak load. Compiled from 50 indents for each material, these curves illustrate the mechanical deformation response of the foils, allowing for a direct comparison of their resistance at higher loading levels.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni-Cr-Mo system at 1573 K, illustrating the phase equilibrium and reaction pathway involving the liquid phase.
summary: This isothermal section at 1573 K provides a detailed view of the phase equilibrium and reaction pathways within the Ni-Cr-Mo system. It serves as a central reference point for understanding the liquid phase behavior and the surrounding phase fields at this specific temperature in the ternary system.

caption: Hardness and reduced modulus versus indentation depth for AM IN718 nitrided at 650 °C.
summary: Mechanical characterization of the nitrided layer on AM IN718 treated at 650 °C shows hardness values ranging from 2.5 to 14.2 GPa. Compared to the 500 °C treatment, this specimen exhibits fewer variations in mechanical properties as a function of indentation depth within the hard surface layer.

caption: Inverse fast Fourier transform image of the red box area in panel (b), highlighting the atomic lattice arrangement of the Cu-rich particle.
summary: The inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) image, processed from the red box region of the high-resolution TEM micrograph, provides a filtered view of the atomic lattice. This visualization emphasizes the structural periodicity of the Cu-rich particle, supporting the identification of its FCC crystal arrangement within the matrix.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Ni-Ti-W system, representing the phase stability and solubility limits for these components.
summary: This ternary phase diagram represents the Ni-Ti-W system. The reference indicates that W exhibits high solubility in the liquid Ni62Ti38 phase, allowing it to migrate from the GH3044 superalloy into the joining layer. This process results in a liquid phase containing Ni, Ti, Cr, and W elements.

caption: Extended continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram constructed from dilatometry results, incorporating predicted transformation temperatures at high cooling rates.
summary: The extended CCT diagram is constructed using dilatometry data to map phase transformation kinetics during cooling. It integrates experimental measurements with predicted transformation temperatures at 500 °C/s, indicated by open symbols, which were derived from log-log linear regression to provide a comprehensive overview of the material's phase transformation behavior.

caption: Linear regression of the natural logarithm of the 50% transformation time versus the inverse of the product of the gas constant and temperature, used to calculate the activation energy.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between the natural logarithm of the 50% transformation time and the inverse of the product of the gas constant and temperature. This graphical representation is utilized to determine the activation energy for the transformation process based on the kinetic data derived from the homogenization experiments.

caption: EDS cross-section map corresponding to the CVD1 coating sample.
summary: The EDS cross-section map for the CVD1 coating sample provides elemental distribution data that complements the SEM structural analysis. This map confirms the layered composition of the coating, ensuring that the chemical distribution aligns with the well-defined layered structure observed in the corresponding SEM fractured cross-section image.

caption: {001} pole figure of the β-phase on the XY plane of the ambient-pressure WAAM Ti64 sample, showing a strong <001> fiber texture.
summary: The {001} pole figure for the β-phase on the XY plane reveals a strong <001> fiber texture. This indicates that the primary β-phase grains undergo continuous growth along the deposition direction, which is oriented perpendicular to the projection plane of this specific pole figure analysis.

caption: Point cloud representation of part #1 at layer 20, illustrating the initial surface flatness state during the printing process.
summary: This point cloud visualization captures the surface state of part #1 at layer 20. It serves as a baseline for monitoring printing quality, where the surface flatness is relatively stable before the subsequent deterioration observed in later layers, providing a reference for the initial stages of the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Intermediate stage of the FIB cutting process demonstrating the protective role of the Pt deposit during ion beam milling.
summary: During the FIB cutting process, the Pt deposit serves as a sacrificial barrier. This step is essential for preventing the Ga ion beam from damaging the delicate carbide hardening layer structure, thereby allowing for the precise extraction of the cross-sectional foil required for detailed microstructural characterization.

caption: Absorbance spectra of TPO, TPO-L, BAPO, and CQ photoinitiators measured across the 350–500 nm wavelength range.
summary: This panel displays the absorbance spectra for TPO, TPO-L, BAPO, and CQ photoinitiators within the 350–500 nm range. The data indicates that CQ would demonstrate superior effectiveness compared to the other tested photoinitiators if the light source utilized in the equipment operates at a wavelength of 450 nm.

caption: Timing diagram illustrating the fluctuating physical phenomena and dynamic equilibrium during the selective laser melting (SLM) of 316L stainless steel powder.
summary: This timing diagram illustrates the evolution of physical phenomena during the SLM process of 316L stainless steel powder. It highlights that the process is characterized by fluctuations and dynamic equilibrium, with metal powder melting approximately 40 microseconds after laser emission, leading to a steady increase in heat accumulation.

caption: Isometric representation of the engineered economizer component geometry.
summary: This figure presents an isometric view of the designed economizer geometry. The schematic illustrates the specific structural configuration and spatial arrangement of the component, providing a clear visual representation of the design intended for the economizer system as described in the technical documentation of the study.

caption: Force-displacement (f vs. h) relationship for Rene N4 alloy subjected to 18 dpa ion irradiation, illustrating the correlation between theoretical calculations and experimental measurements.
summary: Representing the mechanical response of Rene N4 alloy at 18 dpa, this panel plots force against indentation depth. The alignment of theoretical lines with experimental dots confirms that the developed model effectively captures the material's behavior under this higher irradiation dose, validating the model's predictive capability for irradiated samples.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing the morphology of Ti2Ni precipitates distributed along low-angle boundaries (LABs) in the B2 matrix.
summary: This bright-field TEM image illustrates the typical morphology of low-angle boundaries within the grains. Ti2Ni precipitates are clearly observed to be distributed along these boundaries, providing visual evidence of their spatial arrangement within the B2 matrix structure as validated by the TEM observations of the material.

caption: Origami-inspired structure positioned within the dual-column tabletop INSTRON 5969 machine for quasi-static compression testing.
summary: This image illustrates the experimental configuration for the quasi-static compression testing of fabricated origami structures. The dual-column INSTRON 5969 machine is employed to subject these samples to significant deformation, reaching up to 80% strain, allowing for the evaluation of the mechanical response of the origami-inspired design under compressive loads.

caption: Cu 2p3/2 XPS spectra of corrosion products on 70/30 Cu-Ni alloy after 10 days of immersion in natural seawater.
summary: This panel illustrates the Cu 2p3/2 XPS spectrum for the 70/30 Cu-Ni alloy after 10 days of immersion in natural seawater. It completes the series for natural seawater conditions, contributing to the identification of surface corrosion products through the analysis of spectral peaks observed over the 3, 7, and 10-day periods.

caption: MCR-ALS derived component spectra for reduced 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 during DRM at 750 °C and 1 atm with a CH4/CO2 ratio of 1/2.
summary: This panel displays the MCR-ALS derived XANES component spectra for 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 under DRM conditions with a 1/2 CH4/CO2 ratio. The analysis identifies specific components, where the lineshape of component 2 indicates an oxidized Fe state, although the presence of FeOx during the reaction remains ambiguous based on these results.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of interpass temperature (IT) versus porosity, demonstrating a clear positive correlation between increasing IT and higher porosity levels in surface pixels.
summary: This SHAP scatter plot highlights a clear positive correlation between interpass temperature and surface porosity. The data indicates that higher interpass temperatures consistently lead to increased porosity, underscoring the critical role of local thermal accumulation and heating in the formation of keyhole-type pores during the surface scanning process.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph of Ni0.90Dy0.10 alloy showing the microstructural features characteristic of the higher dysprosium-doped nickel composition.
summary: This backscattered electron image displays the microstructure of the Ni0.90Dy0.10 alloy. As part of the systematic investigation into Ni-RE alloys, the micrograph captures the phase morphology and distribution resulting from the specific dysprosium concentration, providing insight into the structural characteristics of this nickel-based alloy system.

caption: Mole fraction of the BCC phase during non-equilibrium solidification modeled via the Scheil–Gulliver approach.
summary: Utilizing the Scheil–Gulliver model, this simulation predicts the evolution of the BCC phase mole fraction during non-equilibrium solidification. The results indicate that a single BCC solid solution phase is formed throughout the entire solidification process, demonstrating the phase stability under these specific non-equilibrium cooling conditions for the alloy.

caption: Atomic structure model of Ni6 amorphous alloy showing the local atomic arrangement after Ni substitution for Co.
summary: The atomic structure of the Ni6 amorphous alloy is shown, depicting the configuration after nickel replaces cobalt. The model confirms that transition metals and boron atoms are distributed around the central nickel atoms, with coordination numbers between 13 and 14, consistent with the structural trends observed in the other amorphous alloys.

caption: Bode phase plot for Ti-6Al-4V/Nb2O5, where the phase angle peaks at approximately -75° within the frequency range of 10 to 10³ Hz.
summary: The Bode phase plot for the Ti-6Al-4V/Nb2O5 sample shows a peak phase angle of approximately -75°. This behavior is evidenced by distinct plateaus within the frequency range of 10 to 10³ Hz, reflecting the stable electrochemical characteristics of the coated surface in the HBSS environment.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the JT0 alloy needle, highlighting the transition through the γ'→γ→γ' phase regions with Cr atoms in red and Al atoms in green.
summary: This APT reconstruction of the JT0 alloy needle illustrates the spatial distribution of elements across the γ/γ' interface. By visualizing Cr and Al atoms, the image clearly demonstrates the partitioning of solutes, where Al preferentially segregates into the γ' precipitates and Cr concentrates within the γ matrix phase.

caption: 1H NMR spectroscopic analysis confirming the successful chemical modification and structural composition of the synthesized PAA-CD-DA polymer.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum provides structural confirmation of the synthesized PAA-CD-DA polymer. This spectroscopic characterization verifies the successful grafting of functional groups onto the PAA backbone, which is a critical step in preparing the water-soluble drug carrier for subsequent therapeutic applications in ocular surface treatment.

caption: HT-CLSM snapshot during heating showing the initiation of γ′ dissolution at grain boundaries and grain interiors, indicated by white arrows.
summary: During heating, γ′ dissolution initiates at the grain boundaries and progresses into the grain interior. This process is identified by a distinct change of contrast within the grains, as highlighted by the white arrow in this HT-CLSM snapshot, marking the onset of microstructural evolution at elevated temperatures.

caption: Chromatographic profile of the reaction products obtained after 7 hours of incubation, showing the detection of 6′-galactosyl lactose, 4′-galactosyl lactose, and 3′-galactosyl lactose.
summary: The chromatographic profile displays the reaction products formed after 7 hours of incubation. By comparing these peaks with laboratory standards, the presence of specific galactooligosaccharides, including 6′-galactosyl lactose, 4′-galactosyl lactose, and 3′-galactosyl lactose, is successfully identified and confirmed within the reaction mixture.

caption: Comparative radar chart illustrating the performance characteristics of shape-memory polymers (SMPs), shape-memory alloys (SMAs), and shape-memory hydrogels (SMHs).
summary: This radar chart provides a comparative overview of key properties for shape-memory polymers, alloys, and hydrogels. It highlights that shape-memory hydrogels offer a superior balance of functional attributes, including biodegradability, self-healing capabilities, and biocompatibility, when evaluated against the performance metrics of competitive shape-memory materials like polymers and alloys.

caption: Concentration gradient profile from the matrix to the oxidation layers in a stress-free sample, highlighting the distribution of Al and Cr.
summary: This panel details the concentration gradient from the matrix to the oxidation layers in a stress-free sample. It provides a comparative view of how Al and Cr are distributed within the layers, establishing the baseline concentration gradients observed in the absence of mechanical loading after 900 hours of oxidation.

caption: Recrystallization distribution map highlighting the spatial arrangement of recrystallized, substructured, and deformed grains in the transition layer.
summary: This recrystallization distribution map displays the spatial arrangement of recrystallized, substructured, and deformed grains within the transition layer. By categorizing the grain states, the map offers insight into the microstructural evolution and the extent of deformation or recovery processes occurring at the transition zone of the material.

caption: Phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction in the unstrained (0% strain) reference configuration.
summary: The phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction is shown for the unstrained state. This baseline configuration serves as a reference for comparing the effects of applied strains on the band gap characteristics, with specific frequency ranges of the band gaps highlighted in red.

caption: Phase map of the Type II crack tip region, illustrating the phase distribution along the crack path.
summary: This phase map displays the Type II crack tip characteristics, focusing on the phase distribution along the crack path. By identifying the phases present, this map facilitates a comparison with Type I, highlighting the structural differences in how cracks interact with the matrix and interfaces during the testing process.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of the CHBAC electrode measured at various scan rates from 1 to 20 mV s⁻¹, revealing a combination of EDLC and pseudocapacitive characteristics.
summary: The CHBAC electrode is analyzed via cyclic voltammetry at scan rates from 1 to 20 mV s⁻¹. Unlike the BAC electrode, the CHBAC material displays a combination of electric double-layer capacitor (EDLC) and pseudocapacitive characteristics, as evidenced by the distinct features in the recorded voltammetric curves.

caption: Melting progression of CuSn20 particles surrounding the diamond particle at t = 0.216 ms, showing reduced y-direction migration speed.
summary: At t = 0.216 ms, the CuSn20 particles surrounding the diamond particle begin to melt. Specifically, melting on the right side of the diamond particle results in a slower migration speed in the y-direction compared to the initial state, illustrating the influence of local phase changes on particle dynamics.

caption: Statistical distribution of shear band spacing values for explosion-tested specimens, generated via backpropagation neural network data expansion.
summary: This panel presents a statistical summary of shear band spacing values obtained from explosion specimens. The data is processed using a backpropagation neural network model for expansion. For specimens lacking visible shear bands, the perimeter is utilized as a substitute metric to ensure a comprehensive dataset for microstructural evolution analysis.

caption: Fatigue crack growth rate (FCGR) data for additive manufactured (AM) and wrought Ti-6Al-4V alloys, compiled from various literature sources and tested under both air and vacuum environmental conditions.
summary: This plot displays a comprehensive collection of fatigue crack growth rate data for Ti-6Al-4V alloys, comparing additive manufactured and wrought specimens. The data, sourced from multiple literature studies, illustrates the influence of environmental conditions, specifically air versus vacuum, on the crack propagation behavior of these titanium alloy variants.

caption: Cell adhesion and morphology on AISI 304 stainless steel.
summary: Cell adhesion and morphology on AISI 304 stainless steel are presented as a reference standard. The results demonstrate comparable cell adhesion and morphology to the electrodeposited Fe-Cr-Ni samples, confirming that the surface properties of the electrodeposited material are suitable for biological environments relative to established industrial stainless steel benchmarks.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Nb at the Ni/Ni3Nb interface.
summary: This elemental distribution map illustrates the spatial arrangement of Nb at the Ni/Ni3Nb interface. Together with the Ni map, it confirms the absence of other elements and shows no significant Ni-depletion or Nb-depletion features at the microvoid sites, indicating a clean interface structure.

caption: Fractured tensile samples processed with a 0 mm air gap, exhibiting filament breakage and combined fracture modes.
summary: This photograph displays fractured tensile samples processed with a 0 mm air gap. Experimental observations indicate that samples oriented at 0° and 15° undergo filament breakage with fracture surfaces perpendicular to the tensile direction, while samples at 30° to 60° exhibit a combined fracture mode involving both filament breakage and interface failure.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the polarization curves of Ru3Ni3NAs, Ru3Ni2NAs, Ru3Ni1NAs, Ru NAs, and Pt/C in 0.1 M KOH.
summary: These Tafel plots correspond to the polarization curves measured in 0.1 M KOH. By analyzing the slopes, the panel characterizes the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction for the various Ru-Ni nanoarray compositions and the Pt/C catalyst, confirming the superior performance of the Ru3Ni3NAs under these specific alkaline conditions.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine (BBZ) monomer, highlighting characteristic peaks at 1.3, 3.9, 4.0, and 4.8 ppm.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer is presented, displaying prominent peaks at 1.3, 3.9, 4.0, and 4.8 ppm. These specific signals, labeled b, f, g, and h, provide a useful basis for confirming the presence of benzylic and aromatic protons within the BBZ monomer structure.

caption: Comparative charge/discharge capacitance profiles for V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1), V 3.5+ - Pd/C, and V 3.5+ - Electrolysis at a constant current density of 80 mA cm -2.
summary: Comparing the performance of three different V 3.5+ electrolytes at a current density of 80 mA cm -2 reveals distinct differences in electrochemical behavior. Among the tested samples, the V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) electrolyte exhibits the highest discharge and overall capacities, underscoring its superior performance characteristics.

caption: Overall EBSD image quality (IQ) map of the surface layer (SL) in the GHS625 sample, showing the deformation morphology up to a depth of approximately 260 μm after 10% engineering strain.
summary: This EBSD image quality map illustrates the global deformation microstructure of the GHS625 sample surface layer following 10% tensile strain. The visualization captures the overall deformation morphology across a cross-sectional depth of approximately 260 μm, providing a comprehensive view of the microstructural evolution within the surface region.

caption: Total and partial phonon density of states calculated for the austenite and martensite phases of Ni8Mn5Ti3 at 300 K.
summary: Calculated total and partial phonon density of states for Ni8Mn5Ti3 at 300 K are presented to elucidate the mechanism behind the large vibrational entropy change. Comparing the austenitic and martensitic structures at this targeted temperature provides insight into the vibrational properties of the dynamically unstable system, overcoming limitations of traditional harmonic approximations.

caption: Inverse pole figure and corresponding grain size distribution histogram for the C9NS coating sample, showing refined grain structure.
summary: Inverse pole figure and grain size distribution histogram for the C9NS coating sample. As nickel content exceeds 6 wt%, grain refinement occurs, increasing grain boundary density. This structural change is critical, as high free energy atoms at these boundaries can facilitate electrical coupling and promote local corrosion in the coating material.

caption: Final Inconel 713 metallic lattice structure following the chemical dissolution of the ceramic mold material.
summary: The final metallic lattice structure is shown after the successful chemical dissolution of the residual ceramic material. The resulting Inconel 713 component is defect-free and exhibits a smooth surface topology, demonstrating the efficacy of the post-casting chemical processing in achieving a high-quality, clean metallic lattice structure.

caption: Atomic-resolution STEM HAADF image and EDS elemental profiles across the Al/TiB2 interface in an Al-9.947Si-3.94Ti-0.79B alloy, showing the elemental segregation characteristics.
summary: This panel presents atomic-resolution STEM HAADF imaging and EDS elemental profiles for the Al-9.947Si-3.94Ti-0.79B alloy. The data maps the distribution of Si, Ti, and Al across the Al/TiB2 interface, facilitating a comparative analysis of elemental segregation and interfacial structure in high-Ti and high-Si content materials.

caption: Optimized microstructure of Y2O3 sintered at 1700 °C with an appropriate proportion of spherical powder.
summary: Blending an appropriate proportion of spherical powder into the Y2O3 mixture efficiently fills interparticle gaps. This results in the formation of continuous sintering necks throughout the structure, demonstrating an optimized densification process compared to samples with lower or higher spherical powder content.

caption: 31P NMR spectrum of K4P2O7 acquired at 11 T using a 6 mm spherical rotor spinning at 2.1 kHz within a MAS insert inside a solution-state NMR tube.
summary: This 31P NMR spectrum of potassium pyrophosphate (K4P2O7) demonstrates the feasibility of using a MAS insert within a solution-state NMR probe. The experiment, conducted at 11 T with a 2.1 kHz spin rate, utilizes a 6 mm spherical rotor containing 40 mg of sample and 10 mg of KBr for magic angle calibration.

caption: End-on view of the same Fe+Cr iso-concentration surface, rotated 90° from the edge-on perspective to confirm the rod-like geometry.
summary: Rotating the APT needle 90 degrees provides an end-on perspective of the Fe+Cr iso-concentration surface. This view confirms the rod-like morphology of the irradiation-induced precipitates. The consistent orientation of all rods within the alpha-Zr grain is demonstrated by the clear transition between the edge-on and end-on views.

caption: Magnetization curves comparing M-NPs, MP-NPs, and Pegylated MP-NPs to assess magnetic behavior.
summary: Magnetization curves are presented for the magnetic seeds, the gold-decorated MP-NPs, and the final pegylated MP-NPs. These curves characterize the magnetic response of the systems, ensuring that the decoration and pegylation processes maintain the desired magnetic properties required for the intended applications of these hybrid nanostructures.

caption: Chronoamperometric transients of CoNi deposition on glassy carbon from plating bath 3, showing current density versus time at various applied potentials.
summary: Chronoamperometric transients for CoNi deposition on glassy carbon from plating bath 3 are displayed at different applied potentials. The recorded current profiles confirm a nucleation and 3D growth mechanism, evidenced by current peaks that emerge earlier and shift in magnitude as the applied potential becomes more negative.

caption: Dark-field transmission electron microscopy image captured under a two-beam diffraction condition, with the g-vector indicated by an arrow to define the specific imaging reflection.
summary: Captured under a two-beam diffraction condition, this dark-field transmission electron microscopy image utilizes a specific g-reflection to characterize the nature of the stacking faults. The inclusion of the g-vector arrow provides essential crystallographic orientation, allowing for a detailed analysis of the defect structure within the observed material phases.

caption: Tabulated elemental compositions for each region identified in the SEM-BSE micrographs shown in panels (a) and (b).
summary: This table presents the quantitative elemental compositions for the specific regions marked in the SEM-BSE micrographs. The data confirms significant compositional variation across the sample, correlating the bright regions to a Ti-42Nb composition and the dark regions to a Ti-5553 composition, as determined by the point EDS analysis.

caption: Inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT) image derived from the HRTEM data in (e), highlighting lattice periodicity.
summary: The IFFT image, processed from the HRTEM data, visualizes the lattice periodicity of the aged Ni33Cr alloy. This filtered representation clarifies the atomic-scale structural features, reinforcing the identification of the superlattice structure and providing a clearer view of the ordered phase distribution within the crystalline matrix.

caption: Combined DAPI and phalloidin-rhodamine stained images highlighting cell nuclei and cytoskeletal organization of MG-63 cells on L-MS and H-MS scaffolds at 10x magnification.
summary: DAPI and phalloidin-rhodamine staining at 10x magnification allows for the detailed examination of MG-63 cell nuclei and cytoskeletal structure after 72 hours of culture. These images complement the MTT assay data by confirming the morphological integrity and spatial arrangement of the bone cells on the tested scaffold architectures.

caption: Specific compressive strength values plotted against volume fractions, comparing experimental findings with finite element simulation results.
summary: Specific compressive strength values are plotted against volume fractions, comparing experimental findings with finite element simulation results. The comparison shows that the specific compressive strength at various volume fractions has similar results between the experimental and simulation data, reinforcing the reliability of the finite element model for predicting specific mechanical properties.

caption: XRD patterns of Mg100-xNix alloys after hydrogen desorption, indicating the complete decomposition of hydrides into Mg and Mg2Ni phases.
summary: Post-desorption XRD patterns demonstrate the full recovery of the alloy constituents. The disappearance of hydride peaks and the detection of only Mg and Mg2Ni phases confirm that the hydrogenated samples have undergone complete dehydrogenation, returning the material to its original metallic phase composition after the desorption process.

caption: Close-up of the (4 2 0) diffraction peak for the A1 noHT, A1 HT1, and A1 HT2 samples at 423 K.
summary: This close-up displays the (4 2 0) diffraction peak for the A1 noHT, A1 HT1, and A1 HT2 samples at 423 K. The presence of internal stresses in the material can be deduced by carefully inspecting these diffractogram peaks, which correspond to the cubic austenite phase of the samples.

caption: Electronic density of states for the CoNi:O Ni alloy, demonstrating the electronic configuration resulting from oxygen doping at the nickel site.
summary: The electronic density of states for the CoNi:O Ni alloy is shown with the Fermi level set to zero. This plot characterizes the electronic structure changes induced by oxygen doping at the nickel site, completing the set of individual and total DOS comparisons for the studied CoNi-based alloy systems.

caption: Surface roughness profile of the as-built additively manufactured workpiece, exhibiting an initial Ra value of 1.98 μm.
summary: The as-built additively manufactured workpiece surface is characterized by a 2D surface roughness profile. Stylus-based contact measurements using a Phase Grating Interferometer reveal an initial surface roughness Ra value of 1.98 μm, representing the baseline condition of the specimen prior to any post-processing surface finishing techniques.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of CMA used to verify the molecular structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of CMA is provided to further demonstrate and verify the molecular structure of the synthesized compound. This spectroscopic technique, used in conjunction with FT-IR, confirms the identity of the CMA material, providing detailed structural information essential for characterizing the synthesized product in this study.

caption: APT reconstruction of a 5 nm thick slice through the dendritic region, visualizing the local Ti atom distribution.
summary: This APT reconstruction focuses on the dendritic region of the 5 at. % Ti alloy. By visualizing a 5 nm thick slice of the reconstruction, the map provides a detailed look at the Ti atom distribution, which is essential for understanding the chemical variations across the dendritic solidification structure.

caption: EBSD image showing the IQ and grain boundary distribution of the base metal (BM) from the as-received Ti–6Al–4V sheet.
summary: This EBSD image displays the microstructure of the as-received Ti–6Al–4V sheet base metal. The analysis reveals a typical mill-annealing structure characterized by elongated equiaxed-α grains and retained-β grains, providing a baseline for comparing the microstructural evolution across different weld regions of the sample.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Ni1-xCux (x = 0.1–0.5) layered hydroxides recorded in 0.5 M NaOH at a scan rate of 25 mV s-1 at room temperature.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms of Ni1-xCux layered hydroxides with varying copper content are presented in 0.5 M NaOH electrolyte. These measurements characterize the electrochemical behavior of the materials in an alkaline environment at room temperature, providing a baseline for assessing their catalytic performance across different compositions of nickel and copper.

caption: Tensile stress–strain curves comparing the mechanical response of TPU7/PLA3 samples fabricated with different infill patterns.
summary: Tensile stress–strain curves illustrate the mechanical behavior of 3D printed TPU7/PLA3 samples under load. The data indicates that the chosen infill pattern significantly influences fiber orientation within the printed structure, which in turn exerts a substantial effect on the overall mechanical properties and performance of the tested specimens.

caption: Schematic representation of the 15 × 15 × 50 mm³ mechanical test samples fabricated on a 316L stainless steel substrate using the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometry and fabrication method of the mechanical test specimens. The samples, measuring 15 × 15 × 50 mm³, were built directly onto a 316L stainless steel substrate using the LPBF additive manufacturing technique to ensure consistent material properties for subsequent mechanical testing and evaluation.

caption: Al-rich portion of the calculated liquidus projection for the Al–Mg–Si ternary system, highlighting the primary solidification regions and the α-Al/Mg2Si eutectic line.
summary: This Al-rich liquidus projection displays the phase boundaries for the Al–Mg–Si system. It identifies the primary solidification phases, specifically labeling Mg2Si and α-Al regions. The diagram serves as a reference for plotting alloy compositions, distinguishing between hyper-eutectic and hypo-eutectic regimes based on the primary solidified phase.

caption: HR-TEM image showing the interface between the quasi-symmetry Al-Ni-Cu-Fe-Sc phase and the Al9FeNi phase.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging displays the semi-coherent interface between the Al-Ni-Cu-Fe-Sc phase and the Al9FeNi phase. This interaction is significant as it helps minimize local stress concentrations at the incoherent Al/Al9FeNi interfaces, thereby enhancing the overall mechanical stability and structural integrity of the alloy at grain boundary junctions.

caption: Overhanging zone thickness measurements plotted against inclination angles for thin-wall specimens.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the overhanging zone thickness and the inclination angle of thin-wall specimens. The data indicates that the total thickness is highly dependent on the overhanging zone, which is directly influenced by the inclination angle, as further detailed in the supplementary data tables.

caption: Emission and excitation photoluminescence (PL) spectra characterizing the optical properties of PPI-SL and P3HT-PSL materials.
summary: Photoluminescence spectra, including both emission and excitation profiles, are presented for PPI-SL and P3HT-PSL. These measurements provide insight into the optical characteristics of the materials, allowing for a comparative assessment of their electronic transitions and light-emitting properties as part of the broader electrochemical and optical investigation.

caption: Cropped volume image focusing on the specific lattice cell of interest to minimize rotational artifacts.
summary: Focusing on the specific lattice cell of interest, this panel presents a cropped volume image. By isolating this region, the workflow effectively excludes areas prone to high uncertainties caused by inherent rotational artifacts in tomography, thereby improving the accuracy of the subsequent feature extraction and calibration steps.

caption: FIB-SEM cross-sectional analysis of the Ni-5Ag-10MoS2 wear track surface after testing at room temperature under an 800 N load.
summary: FIB-SEM analysis of the Ni-5Ag-10MoS2 wear track reveals the surface morphology after room temperature testing at 800 N. This technique identifies the presence of Cr2S3/Cr3S4 phases, which contribute to the coating's galling resistance by preventing adhesion of the Al-alloy during the wear process.

caption: 1H-NMR spectra comparing unmodified pectin, bis(3-aminopropyl)amine (APA) reagent, and the resulting APA-modified pectin product.
summary: The 1H-NMR spectra provide a comparative analysis of the chemical modification process. By examining the signals for unmodified pectin, the APA reagent, and the final APA-modified pectin, the successful incorporation of the amine groups into the pectin backbone is confirmed through the spectral features observed in the modified sample.

caption: Compass graphs illustrating neurite distribution for groups S150, S300, and S500, where red line length denotes neurite length and the angle represents orientation relative to the x-axis.
summary: Compass graphs visualize the directional distribution and length of neurites for PC12 cells in groups S150, S300, and S500. The data indicates that neurites of cells near fibers preferentially extend along the fiber axis, whereas neurites of cells distant from the fibers show a random distribution of orientation and length.

caption: Shear moduli of Ni-Al solid solutions plotted against Al solute concentration, featuring experimental data points and corresponding linear regression lines.
summary: This panel displays the Voigt-Reuss-Hill (VRH) shear modulus for Ni-Al solid solutions as a function of Al concentration. The data includes experimental measurements alongside linear regression fits, illustrating the relationship between solute concentration and the mechanical shear modulus for this specific binary alloy system.

caption: Deconvolution of the first-order Raman D-G region using the Sadezky-5 band model to extract specific carbon component contributions.
summary: To extract the exact contributions of the carbon components, the Sadezky-5 band model was employed to deconvolute the D-G region of the Raman spectra. This analytical procedure allows for a detailed assessment of the structural disorder and graphitic nature of the nanocomposite materials.

caption: 3D morphology of corrosion pits on the surface of LPBFed Ti–5Cu after 7 days of dynamic immersion.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy captures the 3D surface morphology of the Ti–5Cu alloy after 7 days of dynamic immersion and polarization testing. This panel demonstrates the pitting behavior and surface degradation patterns observed on the Ti–5Cu sample, providing insight into the corrosion resistance of this specific alloy composition.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph and WDS elemental maps of Cu and Mn for sample H 133, highlighting Mn-Cu segregation at high-angle grain boundaries (black arrows), coarse interdendritic segregation (blue arrows), and specific melt pool Mn segregation (red arrows).
summary: Sample H 133 exhibits distinct segregation patterns as visualized through high-resolution WDS elemental mapping. Black arrows indicate Mn-Cu enrichment at high-angle grain boundaries, while blue and red arrows denote interdendritic and melt pool-specific segregation, respectively. These maps provide clear evidence of elemental distribution variations within the printed microstructure.

caption: Transmittance measurements of cell-free and cell-laden composites recorded on day 1 and day 7, indicating a slight decrease in optical transparency over the culture period.
summary: Transmittance data for cell-free composites ranged from 76–87% on day 1 to 70–87% on day 7, while cell-laden composites ranged from 74–86% on day 1 to 67–84% on day 7. The results indicate that transmittance is slightly decreased during culture for both structure types.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics of the resonant tunneling diode (RTD) featuring symmetric barrier thicknesses of 2 nm, 3 nm, and 4 nm.
summary: This plot displays the I-V characteristics of an RTD with varying symmetric barrier thicknesses. Narrower 2 nm barriers facilitate greater current flow due to increased transmission, while thicker 4 nm barriers reduce current and shift the resonant peak bias to 0.2 V compared to the 3 nm baseline.

caption: Higher magnification STEM-DF micrograph emphasizing the nanocrystalline nature of the Al-2.3Ni-2.3Y microstructure.
summary: This high-magnification STEM-DF micrograph provides a detailed view of the nanocrystalline microstructure in the Al-2.3Ni-2.3Y alloy. Analysis of this image reveals an average grain size of 13.6 ± 7.7 nm, with the largest grains reaching approximately 40 nm, confirming the effective stabilization of nanograins through the observed solute co-segregation.

caption: H&E stained histological section of the original AgNPs material implant site after 3 weeks of implantation.
summary: Original AgNPs implant site evaluated at 3 weeks post-implantation using H&E staining. This longitudinal histological assessment within the Beagle root-defect model helps determine the progression of tissue response and infection status, providing a comparative baseline for evaluating the long-term biological impact of the AgNPs material surface.

caption: Calculated refractive indices of PTFE-filled composite samples derived from MG-EMA modeling across the 0.5 to 2 THz frequency range, with neat photopolymer data provided as a baseline reference.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical refractive index values for PTFE-filled composite materials calculated using the MG-EMA model. Spanning a frequency range of 0.5 to 2 THz, the plot includes the neat photopolymer as a reference, providing a baseline for evaluating the impact of PTFE filler on the composite's optical properties.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the measured average size of intragranular γ’ precipitates across various experimental conditions, with error bars indicating the corresponding standard deviations derived from image analysis.
summary: This bar chart presents the measured average size of intragranular γ’ precipitates for different experimental conditions. Image analysis was employed to quantify these sizes, and the results are displayed with error bars representing the standard deviations, providing a clear comparison of precipitate growth across the studied sample conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+ in 0.1 M KCl comparing 35 wt% CB/TPU electrodes before and after 0.5 M NaOH cleaning, alongside a commercial conductive TPU filament.
summary: Electrochemical testing of 35 wt% CB/TPU electrodes using [Ru(NH3)6]3+ demonstrates the impact of NaOH cleaning on performance. The bespoke 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode significantly outperforms the commercial conductive TPU filament, which exhibits negligible electrochemical response, confirming the superior sensitivity and effectiveness of the developed additive manufactured electrode material.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and corresponding EDS elemental maps of the sample cross-section, highlighting the distribution of elements within the multi-oxide layers and the presence of Ni- and Cr-enriched particles.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field imaging and EDS elemental mapping characterize the sample cross-section after 600 hours of corrosion. The analysis identifies a layer of particles on the exterior, with distinct Ni-enriched and Cr-enriched regions observed as the microstructure transitions toward the matrix, illustrating the elemental segregation within the oxide layers.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of Human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) cultured on DHNAS substrates, showing healthy cell morphology.
summary: Human dermal fibroblasts were cultured on additively manufactured DHNAS surfaces under standardized conditions. Fluorescence microscopy confirms that the as-prepared DHNAS substrates provide a suitable environment for these cells, demonstrating excellent biocompatibility and supporting healthy cell morphology across the tested surface area.

caption: Comparison of relative densities for np Ag structures derived from FIB tomography versus those calculated via Ashby-Gibson scaling based on measured Young's modulus values.
summary: This plot compares relative density measurements of nanoporous silver structures obtained through FIB tomography against theoretical values calculated using the Ashby-Gibson scaling law applied to experimental Young's modulus data. The visualization provides a quantitative validation of the structural density characteristics by correlating direct tomographic observations with mechanical property-based estimations.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram of the Ti–25Al-xNb system showing phase stability regions.
summary: The pseudo-binary phase diagram of the Ti–25Al-xNb system maps the phase stability regions relevant to the solidification process. This diagram supports the observation that the resulting coating is primarily composed of the B2 phase, O phase, and TiC phase, providing a thermodynamic basis for the observed microstructure.

caption: Ternary composition plot illustrating the volume percentage distribution of ASH-G composite constituents.
summary: This ternary diagram displays the compositional selections for ASH-G composites, expressed in volume percentages. The plot serves as a primary reference for the material formulations used in the study, providing a clear visual representation of the relative proportions of the constituent phases within the composite system.

caption: Design schematics of isotruss unit cells representing four distinct scaffold configurations: empirical, uniform, vertical gradient, and lateral gradient architectures.
summary: These design schematics depict the isotruss unit cell geometries utilized for various scaffold configurations. The configurations include empirical, uniform, vertical gradient, and lateral gradient designs, which serve as the structural building blocks for the personalized functionally graded bone scaffolds developed within the machine learning-based optimization framework.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for Mo-added MEAs at open circuit potential.
summary: The Bode plot provides a frequency-domain representation of the impedance behavior for Mo-added MEAs at open circuit potential. By showing both the magnitude and phase angle across a range of frequencies, this plot complements the Nyquist data to characterize the electrochemical system's response and validate the electrical equivalent circuit model.

caption: Overall conformation of the trypsin–SL complex showing the SL molecule docked into a hydrophobic cavity on the protein surface.
summary: This panel displays the overall docking conformation of the trypsin–SL complex. The simulation reveals that the SL molecule binds into a hydrophobic cavity on the trypsin surface, providing a structural basis for understanding the interaction between the ligand and the protein as predicted by AutoDock Vina.

caption: Relative electrical resistance change (R–R0)/R0 versus number of bending cycles N at 0.5 Hz and 12.8% strain, with an inset showing detailed resistance variation over six cycles.
summary: Dynamic bending performance is evaluated by tracking relative resistance changes over multiple cycles. The inset highlights resistance fluctuations across six cycles, revealing that peak resistance values decrease with higher microfiber weight fractions. These findings are consistent with static three-point bending test results, confirming the material's electromechanical stability under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Chronopotentiometric response of the FG-1 experiment, showing an anode potential 60 mV higher than the applied potential of FP-1.
summary: The chronopotentiogram for FG-1 demonstrates the galvanostatic dissolution of Inconel 600 in the LiCl–KCl–5-wt%-FeCl2 electrolyte. Notably, the anode potential is 60 mV higher than the potential applied in the FP-1 experiment, indicating that a greater amount of iron has dissolved, which subsequently leads to observable microstructural changes in the alloy.

caption: Dark-field TEM image showing ellipsoidal Al3Sc precipitates within the aluminum matrix.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the WAAM-processed specimen reveals the distribution of ellipsoidal Al3Sc precipitates embedded within the matrix. This technique effectively highlights the formation of these secondary phase particles, providing clear visual evidence of their morphology and spatial arrangement within the microstructure following the inter-pass rolling process.

caption: Time-dependent creep rate variation for STA1080 and STA1150 specimens under constant conditions of 650 °C and 690 MPa.
summary: Creep rate variation over time is shown for both microstructural variants at 650 °C and 690 MPa. STA1150 exhibits an order of magnitude lower minimum creep rate than STA1080, confirming its enhanced creep resistance and superior performance during high-temperature mechanical testing.

caption: Thermal strain versus temperature curves for 16Cr8Ni-LTT-27% and KA36 alloys.
summary: Thermal expansion behavior of 16Cr8Ni-LTT-27% and KA36 materials is illustrated through strain-temperature curves. These measurements provide critical data on the dimensional stability of the alloys across the tested temperature range, allowing for a direct comparison of their thermal expansion characteristics as presented in the experimental results.

caption: Identification matching list for sodalite, featuring LIBS elemental signals represented in blue and molecular spectra in red.
