summary: This panel displays the identification matching list for sodalite. The data includes LIBS elemental signals highlighted in blue and molecular spectra shown in red. This structured list serves as a similarity test to confirm the identity of the unknown mineral sample against a database of known reference materials.

caption: Visual appearance of the fabricated cTPU/PLLA porous composite scaffold, featuring a layered co-continuous structure with dimensions of 12 mm by 10 mm.
summary: The final cTPU/PLLA composite scaffold is shown, highlighting its porous and layered co-continuous architecture. Measuring 12 mm in diameter and 10 mm in height, the scaffold demonstrates the successful outcome of the SLS fabrication process, confirming the structural integrity and physical dimensions achieved through the described manufacturing methodology.

caption: Wide-view camera perspective capturing the nozzle during live inference.
summary: This wide-view camera perspective captures the nozzle during live inference operations. The image demonstrates the real-time integration of nozzle tracking, defect segmentation, and visualization capabilities within the system. It provides a broad visual context for monitoring the nozzle's position and performance during the active manufacturing or processing sequence.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the as-fabricated CM247LC-M alloy showing γ′/γ eutectic phases at dendrite boundaries and within the dendrite, indicated by white arrows.
summary: This dark-field TEM image illustrates the γ′/γ eutectic phase distribution in the CM247LC-M alloy. White arrows mark the phases at dendrite boundaries and within the dendrite. Compared to the base CM247LC alloy, this modified composition exhibits a reduced content of small-sized γ′ phases within the dendrite regions.

caption: High-magnification STEM image and corresponding EDS elemental maps of the blue rectangle region identified in Fig. 6 (f), highlighting the corrosion attack around globular κ-phases.
summary: High-magnification STEM imaging and EDS elemental mapping of the blue rectangle region from Fig. 6 (f) demonstrate the extent of corrosion around globular κII phases. These findings confirm that the corrosion attack is similar in severity to that observed around the needle-like κV phases in the corroded area.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of the Sn-Cu-Ni ternary alloy electrodeposited from the ILEG-3 electrolyte system at 60 °C for 30 minutes with a current density of 8 mA cm⁻² on a Ti substrate.
summary: This thermogravimetric analysis curve characterizes the thermal behavior of an electrodeposited Sn-Cu-Ni ternary alloy. The sample was prepared using an ILEG-3 electrolyte system at 60 °C for 30 minutes at 8 mA cm⁻². This measurement is specifically utilized to determine the melting point of the synthesized ternary alloy material.

caption: Micro-CT scan images revealing the internal structure of Al2O3 fibers printed in horizontal and vertical modes.
summary: Micro-CT scan images visualize the internal structure of Al2O3 fibers fabricated using horizontal and vertical printing modes. These images provide a non-destructive look at the fiber architecture, confirming the structural integrity and geometric variations resulting from the different printing orientations employed in the ON-3D printing strategy.

caption: Isothermal section of the phase diagram at 775 K, showing the distribution of compositions of interest as black points.
summary: The isothermal section of the phase diagram at 775 K is illustrated in this panel. Small black points are plotted to highlight the compositions of interest. This diagram provides critical information regarding the phase relationships and equilibrium states present at 775 K for the studied material system.

caption: Overview of the in-house experimental system used for the study.
summary: This image displays the in-house experimental system utilized throughout the research. The photograph provides a comprehensive view of the apparatus configuration, serving as the primary visual reference for the experimental setup described in the study. It illustrates the physical arrangement of the equipment employed to conduct the reported investigations.

caption: 3 × 1 × 1 supercell lattice structure with the central RVE highlighted.
summary: This image displays a 3 × 1 × 1 lattice supercell, constructed by repeating the star-shaped RVE along the x-direction. The central cell is explicitly marked to distinguish it within the periodic arrangement, demonstrating how the individual RVEs combine to form the larger, extended lattice structure of the material.

caption: Wide-field (WF) fluorescence microscopy image of 3D agarose fluorescent microspheres, showing the sample structure with a scale bar of 50 μm.
summary: This wide-field fluorescence microscopy image displays 3D agarose fluorescent microspheres. The imaging demonstrates the baseline performance of the wide-field technique for visualizing these thick samples. The axial range of the sample is color-coded from 0 to 150 μm to provide depth information within the agarose gel structure.

caption: Wide-angle XRD pattern of activated ilmenite after 30 minutes of CH4 reforming with 3.8 vol% CO2, indicating FeTiO3, Fe2TiO4, FeO, or Fe3O4 as the primary Fe-containing crystal phases.
summary: At a higher CO2 concentration of 3.8 vol%, the XRD pattern confirms that FeTiO3, Fe2TiO4, FeO, or Fe3O4 are the dominant Fe-containing phases. The absence of Fe0-containing species at this level of CO2 exposure correlates with the observed weaker catalytic activity of these Fe2+-containing phases in the reforming reaction.

caption: STEM micrograph of the H300 sample after tensile deformation, demonstrating a reduced density of GNDs near the Al/Si interfaces compared to the as-built condition.
summary: This STEM micrograph depicts the deformed microstructure of the H300 sample. Observations indicate that fewer geometrically necessary dislocations were introduced near the Al/Si interfaces following tensile deformation, representing a distinct microstructural difference in dislocation accumulation behavior compared to the as-built sample under similar loading conditions.

caption: Horizontal strain field map computed via the finite difference method from conventional DIC displacement data, highlighting fluctuations at the discontinuity.
summary: Horizontal strain fields are displayed, calculated from conventional DIC displacement data using the finite difference method. Significant strain fluctuations are observed along the discontinuity, which the study attributes to the limitations of conventional DIC processing when handling sharp displacement gradients in the synthetic image analysis.

caption: SAED pattern obtained from the precipitate, displaying superlattice reflections characteristic of the γ’ phase within the γ matrix.
summary: This SAED pattern confirms the presence of the γ’ phase within the γ matrix. The observed superlattice reflections are diagnostic of the ordered crystal structure of the γ’ precipitates. This diffraction data validates the identification of the precipitates observed in the STEM micrographs across the various aging conditions.

caption: Grad-CAM visualization demonstrating the interpretability of the multimodal attention fusion network by highlighting critical regions within the life cycle inventory (LCI) data during EC prediction.
summary: Grad-CAM overlays are utilized here to interpret the decision-making process of the multimodal attention fusion network. By mapping the attention weights onto the LCI data, the panel provides visual evidence of how the model identifies significant features during the test phase to accurately predict energy consumption in additive manufacturing.

caption: Comparison of laminar burning velocities for ethanol-ethyl acetate/air mixtures derived from Eq. (3) and Cantera software using the Dayma et al. (2012) kinetic mechanism, featuring RMSE and R2 values across the specified range of equivalence ratios and ethanol fuel concentrations.
summary: This parity plot assesses the accuracy of Eq. (3) against Cantera-computed values using the Dayma et al. (2012) kinetic mechanism. By analyzing data across diverse equivalence ratios and ethanol mole fractions, the plot provides RMSE and R2 metrics that validate the predictive performance of the model for these specific fuel mixtures.

caption: Simulated trajectory of a 1 μm powder particle within the flow path.
summary: This panel illustrates the simulated trajectory of a 1 μm powder particle. By analyzing these specific particle paths, the study aims to explain the particle size distribution observed at the nozzle exit during tube testing, providing insight into how smaller particles behave within the flow environment.

caption: STEM ADF image illustrating the cellular microstructure of the material, with a green dashed line indicating the path for the EDX line profile analysis.
summary: The STEM ADF image provides a detailed view of the material's cellular microstructure, which consists of submicron-sized cells with decorated boundaries. A green dashed line is overlaid on the image to define the specific trajectory for the subsequent EDX line profile analysis across these distinct cell boundaries.

caption: Immunofluorescence co-staining of F-actin (green), DAPI (blue), and RUNX-2 (red) in BMSCs after 7 days of culture on matrix scaffolds.
summary: Immunofluorescence co-staining of F-actin, DAPI, and RUNX-2 in BMSCs after 7 days of culture on matrix scaffolds. Similar to the ALP staining results, these images confirm that the osteoinductive activity of the matrix scaffolds has been removed, as indicated by the lack of RUNX-2 expression associated with osteogenic differentiation.

caption: High-pressure electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-10Ni alloy at 143(3) GPa, recorded across a temperature range peaking at 3006(178) K.
summary: Electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-10Ni alloy is plotted at 143 GPa up to 3006 K. The results show a quasi-linear increase at high temperatures, closely matching the behavior of pure iron. The blue fitted curve, based on the Bloch-Grüneisen formula and resonant impurity resistivity, effectively captures the temperature-dependent trend of the alloy.

caption: Specific areal capacitance values derived from galvanostatic charge-discharge curves, plotted as a function of the number of OTU layers for the 3D-IDCμE-based micro-supercapacitors.
summary: Specific areal capacitance values for 3D-IDCμE micro-supercapacitors are calculated from galvanostatic charge-discharge curves and presented for different OTU counts. These results quantify the impact of electrode stacking on energy storage density, highlighting the performance optimization achieved by varying the number of OTU layers in the on-chip device architecture.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating hydrogen diffusivity normal to the Σ5{100} grain boundary, where diffusion aligns with the composition gradient.
summary: This Arrhenius plot depicts hydrogen diffusion perpendicular to the Σ5{100} grain boundary in a Fe-Ni-Cr system. The results show that when diffusion aligns with the composition gradient, composition nonuniformity leads to a measurable reduction in diffusivity, suggesting that these structural factors contribute to decreased hydrogen mobility in the material.

caption: Total charge density map of the clean EDC system viewed along the (010) plane.
summary: This panel displays the total charge density map for the clean EDC system in the (010) plane. As part of the broader analysis of doped EDC systems, this baseline visualization provides a reference for evaluating the pronounced charge redistributions that occur upon the introduction of dopants into the crystal structure.

caption: Strain at yield for composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8, showing performance relative to the monolithic core reference.
summary: Strain at yield for multi-material composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8 is presented in a radar plot. The visualization shows performance relative to the monolithic core material, offering a consistent basis for material selection. These results contribute to the overall mechanical performance analysis of the samples under flexural loading.

caption: Optimised manufacturing parameters for filament production across varying glass fibre weight fractions, including the resulting output speeds following double extrusion.
summary: This table presents the optimised manufacturing parameters for filaments with different glass fibre weight fractions. It details the specific processing conditions required for each composition and reports the corresponding output speeds achieved after the double extrusion process, providing a comprehensive overview of the production settings for the studied materials.

caption: Fracture propagation behavior observed during material testing.
summary: This panel presents the experimental results of the crack propagation investigation conducted on the material. The data illustrates the mechanical response and failure characteristics observed during the testing process, providing essential insights into the material's fracture behavior and structural integrity under the applied experimental conditions described in the study.

caption: Tafel slope evaluation derived from polarization curves for untreated and modified Inconel 625, providing kinetic insights into the OER performance enhancement.
summary: Tafel slope evaluation provides critical kinetic data regarding the OER performance of the modified Inconel 625. By comparing these slopes against untreated samples and commercial IrOx, the analysis quantifies the catalytic efficiency gains, confirming that the surface modification effectively lowers the energy barrier for the oxygen evolution reaction.

caption: Tafel plots comparing the Ni-Cr system across 0.5 M H2SO4, 0.5 M KOH, and 0.5 M NaCl solutions, alongside individual Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples tested in these specific electrolytes.
summary: This panel displays Tafel curves for Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples electrodeposited and tested in NaCl, KOH, and H2SO4 solutions. The data illustrates the electrochemical corrosion behavior of these materials. Notably, the Ni-Cr coating demonstrates moderate corrosion resistance in NaCl, characterized by an Ecorr of -0.08 V and jcorr of 0.795 µA cm-2.

caption: HPLC chromatograms of PM methanol extract and PL ethanol extract recorded at wavelengths of 205 nm and 330 nm.
summary: Panel B presents the HPLC chromatograms for PM methanol and PL ethanol extracts, measured at 205 nm and 330 nm. The analysis successfully quantifies the four standards identified in panel A. Additionally, the chromatograms reveal the presence of several unidentified compounds, indicating a complex chemical composition within the extracts.

caption: Arrhenius plots of ln(k) versus 1000/RT derived from the kinetic data to calculate the apparent activation energies for the dehydrogenation processes of the alloys.
summary: Arrhenius plots of ln(k) versus 1000/RT are presented to determine the apparent activation energies for the dehydrogenation of the T35V35Cr20-xMn5+xFe5 alloys. These plots synthesize the kinetic data from the previous panels, allowing for the calculation of energy barriers associated with the hydrogen desorption process across the different alloy compositions.

caption: Residual plot for the ultimate tensile strength regression model, illustrating the error distribution across the dataset.
summary: The residual plot for ultimate tensile strength demonstrates that the model satisfies basic statistical requirements. Analysis confirms the absence of significant outlying observations, ensuring the model is not distorted and providing confidence in the accuracy of the ultimate tensile strength predictions derived from the regression analysis.

caption: Rate performance of the Ni 0.9 Sn electrode evaluated through galvanostatic measurements at varying current densities ranging from 0.1 to 2.0 A g-1.
summary: The rate capability of the Ni 0.9 Sn NP-based electrode is demonstrated through galvanostatic measurements conducted at current densities between 0.1 and 2.0 A g-1. This plot illustrates the electrochemical performance of the material under varying load conditions, highlighting its capacity retention and stability across different discharge rates.

caption: UV-vis absorption spectrum of DA-CDs showing a broad range from 200 to 900 nm with a characteristic peak at 279 nm.
summary: The UV-vis absorption spectrum of DA-CDs exhibits a broad range spanning from 200 to 900 nm, indicating potential for near-infrared photothermal conversion. A distinct characteristic absorption peak at 279 nm is observed, which corresponds to π-π* electronic transitions within the aromatic systems of the carbon dots.

caption: GROD map of the fine-grained (FG) region in CA800 alloy deformed to a true strain of 5%.
summary: Displayed is the GROD map for the fine-grained region of the CA800 alloy after undergoing 5% true strain. This map serves to visualize the heterogeneous deformation behavior inherent to the FG structure, allowing for a comparative analysis of strain-induced orientation deviations within the CA800 material system under these conditions.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curve of the uncoated electrode demonstrating its electrochemical activity towards the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).
summary: The electrochemical activity of the uncoated electrode is evaluated via LSV measurements. This panel serves as a baseline for comparison, showing that the uncoated electrode exhibits significantly lower current densities during the hydrogen evolution reaction compared to the Ni-NiZnFe4O4 coated electrodes tested under identical experimental conditions.

caption: Ashby-type evaluation chart plotting yield strength versus uniform elongation for GHS samples relative to previously reported CrCoNi MEA data.
summary: An Ashby-type mechanical property evaluation chart displays the yield strength versus uniform elongation balance. The GHS samples are compared against reported data for CrCoNi MEAs, demonstrating that the combination of gradient and heterogeneous features leads to a more significant HDI stress effect and superior tensile properties compared to single hetero-structures.

caption: Architecture of the proposed CNN model, highlighting the integration of the Multi-Level Spatial Attention (MLSA) block and the configuration of filter counts (C).
summary: This schematic illustrates the structural design of the developed CNN model, specifically emphasizing the incorporation of the Multi-Level Spatial Attention (MLSA) block. The architecture details the network flow and the distribution of filter counts (C), providing a comprehensive overview of the model's configuration for spatial feature extraction and processing.

caption: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectra comparing the surface chemical composition of virgin carbon fibers (CF) and surface-modified carbon fibers.
summary: This figure presents the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectra used to analyze the surface chemical composition of carbon fibers. By comparing the virgin CF with the surface-modified CF, the results illustrate the chemical changes induced by the modification process on the fiber surfaces, as detailed in the study.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 700 °C, displaying experimental data points from pure metal-sulfur and metal-sulfide mixtures alongside thermodynamic calculations.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the Cu–Ni–S system at 700 °C. Experimental data, represented by red squares and green circles, align with black solid lines and grey dash tie-lines calculated via FactSage 8.3. Consistent tie-lines across both experimental sets confirm the reliability of the thermodynamic model at this temperature.

caption: Failure envelopes for sand-PP sheet and sand-PLA grid interfaces, illustrating shear stress versus normal stress relationships.
summary: The failure envelope for the sand-PP sheet interface exhibits an interface friction angle of 31.8° with a zero adhesion intercept. In comparison, the sand-PLA grid interface demonstrates an interface friction angle of 28.8°. These plots characterize the shear response and frictional behavior of the respective sand-polymer interfaces under test conditions.

caption: Fracture toughness as a function of oxidation maximum temperature in dry air for the surveyed material classes, highlighting the performance gap in extreme environments.
summary: This plot maps fracture toughness against maximum oxidation temperature to assess material durability under extreme thermal conditions. By comparing Ni-based alloys with SiC/SiC, Ti3SiC2, and MoSi2, the figure demonstrates the critical need for materials that can withstand high-temperature oxidation while maintaining sufficient structural integrity for advanced solar receiver applications.

caption: Box-Cox transformed fatigue life distribution across different printing orientations and phase conditions.
summary: This box plot illustrates the Box-Cox transformed number of cycles to failure for specimens with varying layer orientations and phase conditions. Results indicate that for 0° and 45° phase loads, specimens printed in the Z orientation exhibit the lowest fatigue life compared to those printed in the X and Y orientations.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns of additively manufactured Inconel 625 along the axial direction, illustrating structural evolution during heating, compressive loading, and stress relaxation, with an inset highlighting (200) peak shifts.
summary: This figure displays neutron diffraction patterns for additively manufactured Inconel 625 during a stress relaxation test. The data tracks structural changes from heating through compressive loading to stress relaxation. An inset specifically demonstrates the shifting of the (200) diffraction peak, providing insight into the lattice response under these specific thermomechanical conditions.

caption: Magnetic force microscopy image showing the continued evolution of vortex and antivortex structures within the Py square under lower applied field conditions.
summary: Magnetic force microscopy image showing the continued evolution of vortex and antivortex structures within the Py square under lower applied field conditions. The presence of these multiple vortices and antivortices confirms the ill-defined nature of the final domain state compared to samples prepared at lower argon pressures.

caption: Analytical approximation of the maximum local tensile stress within the struts of all tested samples, highlighting data scatter below 100,000 cycles.
summary: Maximum local tensile stress values within the scaffold struts are approximated analytically for all tested samples. The data exhibits a higher degree of scatter at lower cycle counts, specifically below 100,000 cycles, which is attributed to the complex tension distribution occurring within the scaffold architecture during the fatigue testing process.

caption: Individual dislocation cell showing dislocation slip traces (black dashed lines) and zones of low dislocation density on CWs-WoM (blue arrows).
summary: This panel illustrates the slip behavior within an individual dislocation cell. Black dashed lines indicate clear dislocation slip traces, while blue arrows point to specific zones on the CWs-WoM that maintain low dislocation densities. These observations provide insight into the localized deformation mechanisms and the heterogeneous distribution of dislocations during straining.

caption: Reaction scheme detailing the preparation process for acetyl-terminated novel PCSZ.
summary: The provided diagram outlines the specific chemical scheme for preparing acetyl-terminated novel PCSZ. This process represents a targeted modification strategy to produce functionalized polycarbosilazane materials, building upon the foundational polycondensation techniques used for standard PCSZ synthesis to achieve specific terminal group chemistry.

caption: TEM image of the g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 composite, illustrating the nanostructural arrangement of the catalyst.
summary: The TEM image of the g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 composite provides a detailed view of the catalyst nanostructure. This visualization confirms the successful integration of the catalytic components, which are designed to work synergistically to improve interfacial interactions and accelerate mass transfer of reactants to the active sites.

caption: Friction coefficient evolution over wear time for SLM-fabricated tungsten specimen B17, fabricated with an energy density of 800 J/mm3.
summary: Depicted here is the real-time friction coefficient curve for SLM-fabricated pure tungsten deposit B17. Fabricated at an energy density of 800 J/mm3, the curve tracks the friction behavior of the sample during the wear test, allowing for an assessment of the material's tribological stability under these specific processing parameters.

caption: Compressive stress–strain response of the FCC Inconel718 lattice structure in the peak-aged condition, showing a pronounced stress drop after yielding.
summary: The FCC lattice structure exhibits a compressive stress–strain response characterized by a distinct stress decrease immediately following the yield point. This behavior, observed at room temperature with a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, reflects the mechanical response of the peak-aged material, where buckling-induced fracture of struts governs the deformation process.

caption: Rheological behavior of 10 wt% CaCO3 composite resin under UV exposure, showing an increase in storage modulus.
summary: This panel illustrates the rheological response of a 10 wt% CaCO3 composite resin during UV curing. Upon exposure to UV light, the material undergoes a transition from a liquid to a solid state, characterized by a significant increase in the storage modulus, indicating improved mechanical properties for the composite.

caption: Geometric representation of the BCC-like unit cell, illustrating the rod-based connection node architecture and the defining design parameters Ø, ω, and H.
summary: This schematic illustrates the BCC-like unit cell design, which features a central connection node similar to 3D-Kagome structures but composed of four rods. The structural geometry is precisely defined by three key design variables: Ø, ω, and H, which dictate the positioning and orientation of the rods within the unit cell.

caption: Learning curve for the XGBoost model, plotting MSE against training set size to demonstrate convergence and model stability.
summary: The learning curve for the XGBoost model shows low MSE values for both training and validation sets. The gap between these sets narrows as the training size increases, indicating that the model performance stabilizes and saturates, which confirms that the dataset size is sufficient to support robust learning.

caption: Static plantar pressure distribution map recorded for the V4 insole design.
summary: Static plantar pressure distribution map recorded for the V4 insole design. Analysis of the pressure results indicates that the V4 insole provides a significant reduction in plantar pressure, highlighting its performance in optimizing pressure distribution across the foot during static testing protocols.

caption: Isothermal section of the Al-Si-Ni ternary system at 633 K calculated using the FactSage 7.3 program, with the specific alloy composition marked by a red spot.
summary: Thermodynamic calculations performed using the FactSage 7.3 program generated this isothermal section of the Al-Si-Ni system at 633 K. The specific composition of the Al63Si25Ni12 alloy investigated in this study is highlighted as a red spot on the diagram to illustrate its position within the ternary phase space.

caption: 1D GradShim spin-density profile of the saddle coil, illustrating the projection of H signal and applied gradient along the z-axis.
summary: This 1D GradShim spin-density experiment encodes spatial information relative to H magnetization along the sample. By applying a gradient during the acquisition period, the technique results in a projection of both the H signal and the applied gradient along the z-axis, characterizing the coil's rf homogeneity profile.

caption: Comparison of observed and LSTM-predicted stress–strain curves at the 20th percentile MAPE.
summary: Representing the 20th percentile of prediction error, this plot compares the observed stress–strain curve against the LSTM model output. It serves as one of the six representative results used to evaluate the performance of the neural network in predicting mechanical deformation characteristics.

caption: Melt pool width of AlSi10Mg single tracks plotted against varying magnetic field intensities.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between applied magnetic field intensity and the resulting melt pool width for AlSi10Mg single tracks. As the magnetic field intensity increases, the melt pool width exhibits a decreasing trend, indicating that the magnetic field significantly influences the track geometry during the deposition process.

caption: Short-circuit current (I_SC) versus time curves for the HETENG under loading rates ranging from 0.033 Hz to 2.75 Hz.
summary: The I_SC-t curves demonstrate the HETENG's response across different loading frequencies. Minor fluctuations observed in the current output are attributed to differences in the transferred charge amount during the pulling and retracting phases of the triboelectric strip, which periodically result in negative current outputs during the harvesting cycles.

caption: In-situ observation of a 0.5 mm gold-coated electrode during electrolysis at 1 V.
summary: Operating at 1 V, this 0.5 mm gold-coated electrode is visualized during an electrolysis experiment. The research focuses on how surface modifications, including gold coatings, influence bubble release. The results demonstrate that these patterned and coated electrodes effectively produce smaller, more transient bubbles, improving performance relative to flat electrode surfaces.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectra recorded for the samples, showing the optical response characteristics of the PtNi/g-CN composite.
summary: UV-visible spectra are presented to characterize the optical properties of the samples. This spectroscopic analysis provides insight into the electronic transitions and light absorption behavior of the PtNi/g-CN composite, which is critical for understanding its potential performance in photocatalytic or related optical applications.

caption: Comparison of yield strength versus fracture toughness for the current additively manufactured (AM-ed) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) against various reference materials, including FCC, dual-phase, and BCC-structured HEAs, as well as other conventional alloys.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical performance trade-off between yield strength and fracture toughness for the studied AM-ed HEAs. By benchmarking against FCC, dual-phase, and BCC-structured HEAs, the data highlights the superior toughness of the current material, which is attributed to increased stacking faults and twinning mechanisms during deformation.

caption: Elastic fracture toughness (K Im) in MPa√m as a function of specimen size and alloy composition, distinguishing between stable and unstable crack propagation via symbol fill status.
summary: The elastic fracture toughness (K Im) is presented as a function of specimen size and alloy composition. In contrast to the elastic-plastic fracture toughness (K Jp), the K Im values for 90–95W alloys demonstrate an increasing trend as the specimen size increases, as indicated by the plotted experimental data.

caption: Reconstructed surface model derived from the processed point cloud data.
summary: Reconstructed surface model derived from the processed point cloud data. This surface representation serves as the foundation for the integrated workflow, enabling precise in-place 3D printing for missing building components without requiring prior knowledge of the existing geometry of the wall during the automated repair and construction process.

caption: IRRAS absorbance spectra of pHPMAA homopolymer synthesized over 30 minutes, comparing samples E and G.
summary: The IRRAS absorbance spectra for pHPMAA homopolymer samples E and G, synthesized over 30 minutes, are shown. These results confirm that the polymer composition is consistent across different reactor setups. The absence of contamination and the presence of identical spectral features validate the efficacy of the microfluidic stack reactor.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of Mo2C precipitates.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping reveals the elemental distribution within the Mo2C precipitates. This compositional analysis, presented alongside EBSD data, confirms the chemical nature of the observed carbide phases. The mapping highlights the spatial arrangement of elements, supporting the identification of the Mo2C precipitates within the material microstructure.

caption: Two-terminal memory crossbar architecture illustrating the arrangement of memory elements at the intersections of conductive lines.
summary: This schematic depicts a two-terminal memory crossbar structure, a fundamental configuration for high-density memory arrays. The design utilizes intersecting conductive lines to address individual memory elements. A significant technical challenge inherent to this specific crossbar architecture is the presence of sneak currents flowing through unintended paths within the device.

caption: Base CAD model representing the fundamental geometry of the headless compression screw prior to lattice integration.
summary: This panel displays the base CAD model used as the foundation for the porous dual pitch headless compression screws. It serves as the structural template before the incorporation of the BCC, gyroid, or Voronoi lattice patterns, establishing the primary dimensions and form factor for the proposed screw designs.

caption: Comparative yield strength analysis of Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy against conventional AlSi10Mg, Ti-6Al-4V, and SS316 materials at relative densities ranging from 17% to 27%.
summary: This plot compares the yield strength of the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy against conventional materials like AlSi10Mg, Ti-6Al-4V, and SS316 at similar relative densities. caption: Quantitative compositional data derived from the energy spectrum surface scanning of the FGH4097 superalloy.
summary: The table presents the quantitative chemical composition of the scanned surface area of the FGH4097 superalloy. This data provides a precise breakdown of the elemental concentrations, supporting the qualitative observations made in the EDS maps and confirming the overall chemical makeup of the analyzed microstructural regions.

caption: Solubility of [bmim][PF6] in supercritical CO2 with various co-solvents (ethanol, acetone, acetonitrile, hexane, methanol) at 313 K and 15 MPa, comparing ε*-mod SL-EoS predictions (solid lines) against previous PR-EoS calculations (dashed lines).
summary: This figure illustrates the solubility of [bmim][PF6] in supercritical CO2 systems containing different co-solvents at 313 K and 15 MPa. caption: Comparison of activation peak currents for different planes of LPBF 316L and R 316L stainless steel under identical applied potentials, demonstrating a specific hierarchy of current magnitudes.
summary: This panel illustrates the activation peak currents for different planes of LPBF 316L and R 316L stainless steel under identical applied potentials. caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing solid IN718 samples produced via selective laser melting (SLM) and casting, plotted as intensity versus diffraction angle.
summary: The XRD patterns for both cast and SLM-processed IN718 samples exhibit diffraction peaks at identical angles to the as-received powder. caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of region B, focused on crystal plane spacing analysis.
summary: To verify the presence of compressive strain near the crack, the spacing of crystal planes in area B was measured via HRTEM. caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe30 composite showing a minimum value of -6.58 dB.
summary: The Fe30 composite displays a reflection loss profile characterized by a minimum value of -6.58 dB. This result demonstrates an absorption enhancement compared to the 10 wt% loading, reflecting the impact of increased Fe content on the electromagnetic wave attenuation properties of the Fe/PLA/TPU composite material.

caption: Hf-Ni binary phase diagram spanning 300 to 3000 K, highlighting the high-temperature B2 phase region between 45 and 75 at.% Hf, incorporating experimental data from DTA, solubility measurements, and phase observations.
summary: This Hf-Ni binary phase diagram illustrates thermal and compositional stability from 300 to 3000 K. It specifically details the high-temperature B2 phase between 45 and 75 at.% Hf. caption: Nyquist plots comparing SLM 316L SS and R 316L SS, displaying incomplete arcs indicative of charge transfer processes at the electrode-solution interface.
summary: Nyquist plots for SLM 316L SS and R 316L SS are presented, revealing incomplete arcs for all samples. caption: Pole figure representation of SLM-printed Ti6Al4V, detailing the crystallographic texture and preferred orientation of grains in the analyzed regions.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the crystallographic texture of SLM-printed Ti6Al4V, mapping the preferred orientation of grains within the material. caption: Tanδ versus temperature curves for printed PA samples evaluated in dried and various humid conditions (30%RH, 50%RH, 80%RH).
summary: This panel displays the representative DMTA curves for printed PA samples, illustrating the temperature-dependent tanδ behavior. summary: The normalized mass spectrum of an M6C carbide, obtained at a laser energy of 100 pJ, displays the presence of complex ions. Specifically, the C2+ and C6 4+ peaks are identified and marked with arrows at 6 Da and 18 Da, respectively, illustrating the ion composition under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Experimental Co–Al phase diagram contrasted with a calculated diagram derived using only configurational entropic contributions.
summary: Shown here is the experimental Co–Al phase diagram plotted against a calculated version that considers only configurational entropy, represented by blue lines. The thick black dashed lines denote the liquid phase. Comparison with panel (a) suggests that the contribution of magnetic entropy is lower than that of vibrational entropy.

caption: Orientation distribution function map for the AB-V sample in the initial state at a strain rate of 0 s⁻¹.
summary: This panel presents the orientation distribution function map for the AB-V specimen at a strain rate of 0 s⁻¹. It serves as the baseline reference for evaluating texture evolution in the material under subsequent high-strain-rate deformation conditions as described in the study of orientation distribution functions.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL, Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni, and Ni-Zn/Ni foam catalysts in 1.0 M NaOH and 0.5 M N2H4·H2O solution at 30 °C, showing current density versus potential after iR compensation.
summary: The LSV curves demonstrate the electrocatalytic performance of various foam catalysts. Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam exhibits superior current density, reaching 200 mA·cm⁻² at -0.05 V, which significantly outperforms the Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni foam (32 mA·cm⁻²) and Ni-Zn/Ni foam (13 mA·cm⁻²), highlighting its enhanced activity for the hydrazine oxidation reaction.

caption: UV-Vis transmission spectra of the immersion solution at pH 4, comparing room temperature and 37 °C conditions, showing near 100% transmission.
summary: Transmission spectra for the immersion solution at pH 4 are presented for both room temperature and 37 °C. The data indicates no significant changes in the LSPR spectra over time, confirming that the transmission remains near 100% and suggesting minimal Au NP leakage from the nanocomposite hydrogel.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from nanoindentation experiments performed at a maximum load of 10 mN.
summary: Load-displacement curves for inclusion particles were measured at a maximum load of 10 mN. The data reveals distinct mechanical responses, including a notable pop-in event observed on the red curve for Al2O3 at 8–9 mN, which is directly attributed to the cracking behavior of the material.

caption: Thermal and electrochemical data for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during lithiation at 1C, showing heat generation rates, cell potential, and open-circuit voltage.
summary: Panel d shows the thermal and electrochemical behavior of 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during lithiation at 1C. The data, including heat generation and voltage profiles, serves as a reference for evaluating the mass transfer and interfacial resistance differences between conventional tape-casted electrodes and the 3D printed NMC622 counterparts.

caption: EEL spectrum extracted from the spectral imaging area covering the 170–500 eV range, highlighting the Nb M4,5 absorption edge at 205 eV and the Ti L3,2 absorption edge at 456 eV.
summary: Extracted from the EELS-SI data cube, this spectrum focuses on the 170–500 eV range. It clearly identifies the Nb M4,5 edge at 205 eV and the Ti L3,2 edge at 456 eV, which are essential for mapping the elemental composition of the analyzed material area.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) plotted against 0.2% offset yield strength (Rp0.2) for various metal matrix composites (MMCs) categorized by feedstock production method.
summary: This Ashby plot compares the ultimate tensile strength against the 0.2% offset yield strength for MMCs. Data points are distinguished by feedstock production techniques, specifically mechanical mixing versus pre-alloying and in-situ reaction methods. The visualization effectively summarizes mechanical property trends observed in this study alongside relevant literature data for similar materials.

caption: Total and partial density of states for the O-phase Ti2AlMo compound.
summary: In the Ti2AlMo O-phase, the density of states demonstrates that the valence band near the Fermi level is primarily formed by the hybridization of Ti-d and Mo-d states. The s-states of the ternary element are located more than 6 eV below the Fermi level, with minimal contributions from other orbitals.

caption: External quantum efficiency (EQE) spectra plotted against photon energy for 3 nm period superlattice devices, comparing absorber thicknesses of 250, 500, 800, and 1150 nm under varying reverse bias conditions.
summary: Experimental EQE curves demonstrate the performance of superlattice devices with varying absorber thicknesses under reverse bias. At zero bias, the EQE reaches a maximum for the 500 nm absorber thickness before declining for thicker layers. This plot illustrates how device efficiency is modulated by both absorber thickness and applied reverse bias.

caption: Stress nephogram of the vertically printed sample during the first loading cycle under IP conditions.
summary: This panel displays the stress distribution nephogram for a vertically printed sample subjected to the first loading cycle under IP conditions. The visualization illustrates the initial mechanical response and stress localization patterns within the material structure as it undergoes the primary stage of the specified loading protocol.

caption: Decomposition-optimized structure resulting from iterative partitioning of cuboids based on density and boundary existence thresholds.
summary: This panel presents the final decomposition-optimized structure achieved after iterative partitioning. The layout of cuboids is determined by applying thresholds to both optimal elemental density and cuboid boundary existence values. This post-processing step effectively visualizes the final distribution of void, undecomposed, and joint elements within the optimized design domain.

caption: Ternary chemical heatmap for E110 specimen overlaid on a CALPHAD ternary phase diagram.
summary: The E110 specimen exhibits a relatively narrow composition distribution, which is primarily centered around the nominal alloy composition. This heatmap, plotted in ternary composition space, demonstrates high compositional uniformity compared to lower volumetric energy density conditions, indicating more complete melting and stability during the processing of the Ti-Zr-Cu alloy.

caption: Measured diameters of 72 3D printed samples illustrating dimensional variation.
summary: The measured diameters of 72 3D printed samples are presented to illustrate the dimensional variation inherent in the printing process. This plot allows for the evaluation of geometric uniformity across the sample set, which is critical for ensuring consistent performance in subsequent experimental applications.

caption: Average local wall heat flux as a function of flow length, showing distinct variations across four tile regions.
summary: Average local wall heat flux changes abruptly between the four tiles in each water pass. Higher water flowrates yield higher average heat flux because the water thermal resistance is lower, resulting in a higher convective heat transfer coefficient and an increased log mean temperature difference between the water and refrigerant.

caption: Elemental mapping of the GH3230/Ni-75W-5B-20/GH3230 joint brazed at 1413 K for 1800 s, illustrating the initial distribution of alloying elements across the brazed seam and interface.
summary: This elemental mapping displays the distribution of elements in a GH3230 joint brazed at 1413 K for 1800 s. It serves as a baseline for understanding the initial phase distribution within the brazed seam and diffusion-affected zones before higher temperature processing induces significant atomic migration.

caption: Relative density plotted against the arithmetic mean height (Sa) for keyhole and non-keyhole samples.
summary: This scatter plot displays the correlation between relative part density and the surface roughness parameter Sa. By analyzing keyhole and non-keyhole samples, the figure demonstrates how surface topography metrics relate to porosity percentages, assisting in the identification of defect levels and the underlying surface characteristics of the fabricated parts.

caption: Atomic configuration at 0.05 strain, highlighting the emergence of a stacking fault within the grain boundary, indicated by a yellow arrow, resulting from dislocation slip and absorption into the boundary.
summary: At a strain of 0.05, the atomic configuration reveals the formation of a stacking fault at the grain boundary, marked by a yellow arrow within a white dotted ellipse. This structural change occurs as dislocations slip toward the grain boundary, where they are either absorbed or leave behind stacking faults and surface steps.

caption: Computational time difference map comparing the efficiency of the proposed proxy function against the ray-based approach.
summary: This plot demonstrates the computational efficiency gains of the proposed proxy function compared to the ray-based approach. By mapping the time difference, it highlights that the projection-based method offers a significant improvement in computational speed, making it more suitable for iterative optimization tasks than traditional, expensive ray-based methods.

caption: Nominal stress–strain curves for Lat1 S configuration at 5% relative density, contrasting quasi-static performance with dynamic SHPB test data.
summary: This panel shows the nominal stress–strain curves for the Lat1 S configuration at a 5% relative density. The plot compares quasi-static results with dynamic SHPB data derived from 3D analysis, providing a direct assessment of how high strain rates impact the mechanical properties of this specific lattice configuration.

caption: Waterfall plot of WAXS radial integration profiles showing 1D scattering intensity across multiple loading cycles.
summary: This WAXS waterfall plot displays the radial integration of complete diffractograms, providing 1D scattering profiles throughout the loading cycles. The data indicates that crystals oriented perpendicular to the stretching direction remain intact during the experiment, allowing for the observation of structural stability under mechanical loading conditions.

caption: 3D optical profilometer image of the wear track on cast IN718.
summary: Presented here is the 3D optical profilometer image of the wear track observed on a cast IN718 sample. This visual representation allows for the characterization of surface degradation and wear track geometry, serving as a comparative baseline for evaluating the wear resistance of cast materials against other manufacturing methods.

caption: Optical stereomicroscope fractography of the Base specimen from build job J2 at 40x magnification.
summary: This optical stereomicroscope image displays the fracture surface of the Base specimen from build job J2 at 40x magnification. The micrograph provides a low-magnification overview of the fracture morphology, serving as a baseline for comparing the surface characteristics of the Base material against the High CT specimen.

caption: Cross-sectional view at 5 ns demonstrating increased Nb and Ti atomic interaction.
summary: Representing the 5 ns simulation time, this panel shows an increase in the interaction between Nb and Ti atoms at high temperatures. This interaction leads to enhanced Nb diffusion into the Ti phase through the initial interface, demonstrating the progressive nature of the diffusion process as the simulation time advances.

caption: Optical layout of the PLDIC system, illustrating the configuration where the optical axis is aligned perpendicular to the rear surface of the biprism to ensure light deflection occurs exclusively at the front surface.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the optical configuration of the PLDIC system. It highlights the specific alignment where the optical axis intersects the edge of the biprism's front surface, ensuring that imaging light is deflected solely by the front surface, which is critical for the system's operational functionality.

caption: Grain-size distribution histogram for Ni-20W thick film processed at 1200 °C, derived from SEM imaging analysis.
summary: This histogram illustrates the grain-size distribution of Ni-20W thick films fired at 1200 °C. The data, obtained from SEM images, characterizes the microstructural state of the material. This distribution serves as a baseline for evaluating the influence of tungsten content on grain growth suppression in Ni-W alloy systems.

caption: Measured 3D AFM images of the two-axis VLS grating patterns across a 5 μm × 5 μm region for substrates A, B, and C.
summary: Measured 3D AFM images demonstrate the actual surface topography of the two-axis VLS grating patterns on substrates A, B, and C. Each image covers a 5 μm × 5 μm region, providing experimental validation of the grating structures and allowing for direct comparison with the corresponding simulated profiles.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction illustrating the chemical composition of the BCC matrix within the Al 13.6 Cr (x) Fe (75.2-x) Ni 11.2 alloy system.
summary: Atom probe tomography results characterize the chemical composition of the BCC matrix in the Al 13.6 Cr (x) Fe (75.2-x) Ni 11.2 alloy. These experimental findings align with thermodynamic calculations, confirming that the matrix composition varies according to the Cr content while maintaining a high degree of interface coherency.

caption: Phase and inverse pole figure maps of the 80% 316L composition processed at 650 W and 45 IPM, illustrating the refined grain structure.
summary: The phase and inverse pole figure maps for the 80% 316L composition processed at 650 W and 45 IPM are depicted. This sample exhibits a finer grain size compared to the 90% 316L composition and samples processed at higher energy densities, confirming the influence of energy input on the final microstructure.

caption: Magnetic entropy change (ΔS) of the HT sample calculated via the Maxwell relation for magnetic field variations of 0-1 T, 0-2 T, and 0-5 T.
summary: The magnetic entropy change (ΔS) for the HT sample is calculated using the Maxwell relation across magnetic field ranges of 0-1 T, 0-2 T, and 0-5 T. This plot quantifies the magnetocaloric effect, demonstrating the material's potential for magnetic refrigeration applications under varying field strengths.

caption: Side-by-side fracture comparison for the SF2 specimen, highlighting the alignment between experimental testing and simulation.
summary: The SF2 specimen fracture is presented here to demonstrate the correlation between experimental outcomes and simulation results. This comparison serves to validate the accuracy of the computational approach in capturing the specific fracture characteristics observed during physical testing, confirming the reliability of the simulation framework for this material variant.

caption: Tabulated mass loss and notch radius diameter measurements for as-built, stress-relieved, and T6 heat-treated specimens subjected to AFM, TF, CP, ECP, and CM surface finishing processes.
summary: This table presents quantitative data regarding mass loss and notch radius diameter across various specimen conditions, including as-built, stress-relieved, and T6 heat-treated states. It specifically evaluates the impact of different surface finishing techniques—AFM, TF, CP, ECP, and CM—on these physical parameters, providing a comparative overview of material removal and geometric changes.

caption: Parity plot showing the UTS prediction performance of the RF algorithm.
summary: The RF algorithm successfully predicts UTS values with an R2 exceeding 0.8 on the test set. While the model demonstrates effective predictive accuracy, its performance remains slightly lower than that of the GBR algorithm, which serves as the primary benchmark for UTS prediction in this comparative analysis.

caption: Binary phase diagrams for Cu with Ni, Cr, Mo, and Nb, highlighting the miscibility characteristics of IN625 alloying elements.
summary: These binary phase diagrams illustrate the thermodynamic interactions between copper and the primary alloying elements of IN625. The data shows full miscibility in the Ni-Cu system, whereas Cr-Cu, Mo-Cu, and Nb-Cu systems exhibit strong immiscibility, providing a fundamental basis for understanding the observed liquid-state miscibility gap.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for Ni50.3Ti29.7Hf20 alloy samples aged at 550 °C for various durations, showing single-stage martensitic transformation behavior.
summary: DSC curves for Ni50.3Ti29.7Hf20 alloy aged at 550 °C demonstrate single-stage martensitic transformation across all aging durations. This behavior contrasts with binary NiTi alloys, which often exhibit multiple peaks. The curves confirm consistent transformation characteristics during both forward and reverse processes for the specified aging temperature and time intervals.

caption: Slip distance versus applied shear stress for a 100 Å edge dislocation, derived from 20 independent Peierls-Nabarro (PN) simulations.
summary: This panel displays the stress-slip behavior of a 100 Å edge dislocation calculated through 20 independent Peierls-Nabarro simulations. The plot illustrates the relationship between applied shear stress and dislocation slip distance, providing a baseline for understanding dislocation mobility at this specific length scale within the studied material system.

caption: Raman spectrum of the steel surface at 180 °C, confirming the presence of FeCO3 crystals at 1084 cm⁻¹.
summary: The Raman spectrum at 180 °C confirms the presence of outer-layered FeCO3 crystals through the peak at 1084 cm⁻¹. This observation, combined with the detection of FeCr2O4, characterizes the complex corrosion product layer formed on the steel surface under high-temperature, CO2-saturated conditions during the 6-hour immersion test.

caption: Partial current densities of Re and Ni plotted against Ni2+ concentration, illustrating a steady increase for Re and a slight increase for Ni.
summary: Panel (b) illustrates the electrochemical behavior of the system by plotting the partial current densities of Re and Ni as a function of Ni2+ concentration. The results demonstrate that increasing the Ni2+ concentration leads to a steady rise in the partial current density of Re, accompanied by a slight increase in the partial current density of Ni.

caption: Effective migration energy (Qeff) as a function of the LRO parameter, calculated by applying an Arrhenius treatment to the tracer diffusion coefficients obtained at various temperatures.
summary: Effective migration energy (Qeff) is presented as a function of the LRO parameter, determined through an Arrhenius analysis of tracer diffusion coefficients across multiple temperatures. The data indicates a flat or non-monotonic behavior, reflecting how diffusion kinetics are influenced by the degree of order within the material system.

caption: Simulated pole figure derived from the XY-plane microstructure, indicating the crystallographic texture of the NiTi sample.
summary: This simulated pole figure, generated based on the microstructure in the XY-plane, illustrates the crystallographic texture of the NiTi sample. A weak texture is observed, which is consistent with the experimental pole figure, further validating the simulation's ability to capture the material's grain orientation distribution.

caption: Cumulative capacity fading of second-life batteries plotted against Ah-throughput across various C-rates.
summary: This plot illustrates the cumulative capacity fading observed in second-life battery cells as a function of total Ah-throughput. The data highlights the degradation behavior under different C-rate conditions, providing a clear visualization of how cycling intensity influences the long-term capacity retention and usable life of the battery systems.

caption: Average Schmid factor distribution map for the as-deposited AZT6115 alloy.
summary: This Schmid factor diagram illustrates the distribution of deformation potential within the as-deposited AZT6115 alloy. The analysis reveals two distinct peaks in the Schmid factor values, which is indicative of the mixed grain structure present in the material following the laser-additive-manufacturing process, reflecting varying susceptibility to slip activation.

caption: Complete cyclic voltammograms for the PPY:50 electrode comparing non-activated and 3-minute activated states in O2-saturated solution, with an additional N2-saturated scan demonstrating the hydrogen evolution reaction onset at –1.10 V vs. RHE.
summary: The panel presents complete cyclic voltammograms for the PPY:50 electrode in O2-saturated and N2-saturated solutions. By comparing non-activated and 3-minute activated electrodes, the plot demonstrates the impact of activation on ORR kinetics. The N2-saturated scan identifies the hydrogen evolution reaction onset at –1.10 V vs. RHE, characterizing the electrode's electrochemical limitations.

caption: Synchrotron XRD patterns comparing SPS and LB-DED processed FeCrAl to VCrAl interface regions, highlighting the presence of L21 and bcc phases without detectable sigma phase formation.
summary: Synchrotron XRD patterns for SPS and LB-DED specimens reveal the phase composition at the FeCrAl to VCrAl interface. The analysis confirms the coexistence of L21 and bcc phases in both processing conditions. Notably, no sigma phase formation is detected, demonstrating consistent phase evolution across both manufacturing methods.

caption: Box plot comparing HIC 15 values for head injury across different materials in the original hood and ISSH configurations.
summary: This box plot presents the HIC 15 values for head injury, corresponding to the acceleration curves shown in panels (a) through (i). It provides a statistical comparison of head injury metrics across different materials used in the original hood and the ISSH design, highlighting the performance variations between these configurations.

caption: Summary mean absolute SHAP value plot derived from the SVM model, illustrating the relative importance of input variables in determining porosity types.
summary: This SHAP value plot provides a comprehensive overview of feature importance within the SVM model. It quantifies the extent to which each input variable influences the classification of porosity types, serving as a primary diagnostic tool for understanding the model's decision-making process regarding defect formation in the analyzed material.

caption: Precipitation map showing the degradation products of primary MC carbides in superalloys as a function of the (W + Mo)/Cr ratio.
summary: This diagram illustrates the precipitation range of M6C, M23C6, and TCP phases based on the (W + Mo)/Cr ratio. Blue, red, and orange regions represent transitions in carbide types during MC degradation. The red region indicates the formation of M6C + M23C6, while the yellow region signifies susceptibility to TCP phase formation.

caption: Ashby plot depicting the correlation between Yield Strength (YS) and Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) for Invar 36 alloy samples fabricated through distinct processing routes.
summary: Displaying the relationship between YS and CTE, this Ashby plot highlights the performance variations of Invar 36 alloy samples. It serves as a comparative tool to evaluate how different fabrication techniques affect the yield strength relative to the thermal expansion characteristics of the material under investigation.

caption: Arrhenius-style plot showing the natural logarithm of dynamic recrystallized grain size (ln d_drx) as a function of the inverse absolute temperature (1/RT).
summary: This Arrhenius plot depicts the linear dependence of the natural logarithm of dynamic recrystallized grain size on the inverse of the product of the gas constant and absolute temperature. This graphical representation facilitates the calculation of the activation energy parameter Q3 for the dynamic recrystallization process under specific experimental conditions.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of HA-SH/P(AGE-co-G) constructs after 21 days of chondrogenic differentiation, demonstrating homogeneous ECM distribution throughout the hydrogel matrix.
summary: Live/dead staining of HA-SH/P(AGE-co-G) constructs reveals a 3% (m/v) formulation that supports homogeneous ECM distribution after 21 days of chondrogenic differentiation. This result represents a significant improvement over previous studies, which typically achieved only pericellular ECM distribution, confirming the effectiveness of this specific ink formulation for cartilage tissue engineering.

caption: Differential scanning calorimeter curves comparing original and spheroidized powders.
summary: Differential scanning calorimeter curves are presented for both original and spheroidized powders. These thermal analysis results characterize the thermal behavior of the materials, providing essential data on phase transitions or stability differences between the two powder processing states as part of the material characterization process.

caption: Radiographic images comparing preoperative and immediate postoperative states to confirm the precise placement of the porous Ta cage.
summary: Radiographic assessments were performed to evaluate the surgical outcome. These images demonstrate the preoperative and immediate postoperative conditions, specifically verifying the correct positioning of the porous Ta cage within the patient. This visual confirmation is essential for assessing the structural integration of the implant following the surgical procedure.

caption: Fluorescent double staining images of rat bone defect sites using calcein (green) and alizarin red (red) to visualize mineralization lines after 10 weeks.
summary: Fluorescent double staining with calcein and alizarin red reveals new bone formation at the defect sites. The MAO-Si, MAO-Si/PDA, and MAO-Si/PDA@BMP2 groups exhibit mineralization lines closer to the scaffolds compared to the MAO control group, indicating enhanced bone growth and improved integration between the implant and the host bone.

caption: Vickers hardness distribution map for the deposited ultra-high strength steel processed with a 100 μm ultrasonic amplitude, highlighting the effect of high-intensity ultrasonic treatment on mechanical properties.
summary: Vickers hardness distribution map for the deposited ultra-high strength steel processed with a 100 μm ultrasonic amplitude, highlighting the effect of high-intensity ultrasonic treatment on mechanical properties. The data confirms that varying ultrasonic amplitudes significantly alter the cross-sectional hardness distribution, consistent with the experimental mechanical properties observed in the study.

caption: Relationship between thermal power and the hot-side aspect ratio (α hot) for the lowest unit cost heat exchanger designs.
summary: This panel shows the correlation between thermal power and the hot-side aspect ratio. Along with other geometric variables, this parameter is critical in defining the design space where high heat transfer coefficients are maintained, ensuring that the heat exchanger operates at the minimum production cost per unit power.

caption: Latent component Z3 extracted from stress-strain curves, reflecting its sensitivity to deformation conditions.
summary: Panel c shows the latent component Z3 extracted from stress-strain curves. Similar to Z1 and Z2, this component is plotted against processing parameters like temperature and strain rate, demonstrating the AE-PN model's capability to capture complex mechanical data through robust, low-dimensional representations of the original stress-strain curves.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the UNSM-treated sample, showing a refined microstructure with reduced alpha lamellar width and elongated, uniformly distributed beta phases.
summary: The UNSM-treated sample exhibits a significantly refined microstructure compared to the LSP-treated sample. TEM analysis reveals a reduced alpha lamellar width and a more uniform distribution of beta phases, which appear as elongated features dispersed throughout the matrix, highlighting the effectiveness of ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification on the alloy.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to SLM-processed Ti alloy extracts.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the SLM-processed Ti alloy group after 72 hours of exposure to extracts. The image illustrates the viability of Human Gingival Fibroblasts, indicated by green (live) and red (dead) staining, following contact with extracts from SLM-manufactured Ti material after 72 hours.

caption: Average temperature distribution map across the specimen surface.
summary: This panel presents the average temperature map of the specimen. The visualization provides a spatial representation of thermal distribution, which serves as a basis for understanding the experimental conditions. This data is derived from the analysis of the specimen's thermal state as described in the study's findings.

caption: Impact energy values measured for LMD and BK steel specimens across varying strain rates.
summary: Impact energy values for LMD and BK steel specimens are plotted against varying strain rates. The data demonstrates that additive manufacturing of high-strength steel LMD-BK provides superior impact energy absorption capabilities compared to traditional wrought steel, while also preventing the formation of adiabatic shear bands under high-speed impact conditions.

caption: Temperature-dependent TEC curves for γ′-strengthened alloys 5.6H and 5.6L from 100 °C to 900 °C.
summary: Illustrated here are the TEC curves for γ′-strengthened alloys 5.6H and 5.6L between 100 °C and 900 °C. Similar to the 3.2 series, these alloys show a pronounced declining trend in TEC, confirming that replacing Al with Ti atoms reduces thermal expansion in both the γ matrix and γ′ phase.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan performed across the features observed in the BSE image, confirming the chemical composition of the Al and Al-Zn patches on the HSLA surface.
summary: The EDS line scan analysis conducted across the features identified in the BSE image confirms the chemical composition of the fracture surface. The results demonstrate the presence of both Al and Al-Zn patches on the HSLA surface, supporting the conclusion that an Al-Zn eutectic structure formed during the welding process.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from nanohardness tests comparing the LPBF-fabricated AZ91D magnesium alloy and the TiC/AZ91D composite.
summary: This panel displays the load-depth curves derived from nanohardness testing of the LPBF-fabricated AZ91D magnesium alloy and the TiC/AZ91D composite. These curves provide the foundational mechanical data used to evaluate the indentation response and determine the hardness and elastic modulus properties of the as-built materials.

caption: First Order Global Sensitivity Coefficient (FOGSA) analysis for the smart MRFs-7 sample.
summary: This panel displays the FOGSA results specifically for the smart MRFs-7 material. Consistent with the broader findings of the study, the sensitivity coefficients highlight the primary drivers of the system's behavior, confirming that the same pattern of sensitivity observed in other samples persists within this specific MRF configuration.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of the specimen middle region processed without an external magnetic field.
summary: This scanning electron micrograph displays the microstructure of the specimen middle region in the absence of an external magnetic field. The material exhibits a specific distribution of second-phase particles, with a measured theta-phase area fraction of 7.65%, serving as a baseline for comparing magnetic field-induced microstructural changes.

caption: Long-term stability assessment of the 3DP-PWC sensor via electrochemical testing conducted on days 0, 7, 15, and 30, showing consistent performance in ketamine detection with error bars (n=5).
summary: The stability of the 3DP-PWC sensor is monitored over a 30-day period using electrochemical testing. Measurements taken on days 0, 7, 15, and 30 indicate that the sensor maintains performance comparable to the initial Ket/Apt/ZnO nanoparticle baseline, confirming its reliability for long-term ketamine detection applications with n=5 replicates.

caption: Total density of states (DOS) calculated for β-type Ti-Mo alloys using the SQS method without structural relaxation.
summary: This panel displays the total density of states for β-type Ti-Mo alloys as determined by the SQS method. The data represents the electronic structure of the alloy system prior to any structural relaxation, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of atomic rearrangement on the electronic properties of the material.

caption: Reconstructed 3D CAD geometry of the printed component highlighting identified heat accumulation zones (SZ) color-coded by their standard deviation values.
summary: This 3D reconstruction illustrates the geometry of a printed part post-processed from real-time printing frames. The visualization identifies specific heat accumulation zones (SZ) across the structure. These zones are color-coded based on standard deviation values, with regions exhibiting a standard deviation of 0.105 or higher explicitly mapped within the geometry.

caption: Flank wear progression (VB Max) versus cutting time for PCD(B) grade at 500 m/min and 0.012 mm/z, highlighting the influence of edge hone radius on tool degradation.
summary: This graph illustrates the flank wear progression for the PCD(B) grade tested at a cutting speed of 500 m/min and a feed rate of 0.012 mm/z. The data demonstrates how varying edge hone radii influence the wear rates of the PCD tool grade over the duration of the cutting time.

caption: Thermo-Calc stable phase prediction for the 20:20 ratio cross-section at 723 K, depicting the standard phase boundaries.
summary: This panel illustrates the Thermo-Calc stable phase prediction for the 20:20 ratio cross-section at 723 K. By comparing these standard phase boundaries with the elastic-modulated miscibility gaps, the figure highlights how the appearance of a second FCC phase leads to a sudden increase in the miscibility gap.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms obtained for a fixed TMA⁺ concentration of 150 µM across varying scan rates ranging from 0.005 to 0.035 V·s⁻¹.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry measurements at a fixed TMA⁺ concentration of 150 µM illustrate the influence of scan rate on the electrochemical current response. By varying the scan rate between 0.005 and 0.035 V·s⁻¹, the data characterizes the kinetic behavior of the ion transfer process at the supported liquid-liquid interface.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the Co–Ni–Mo coating measured at a sweep rate of 50 mV s−1 in 1 M KOH solution across the potential range of −0.08 to −0.58 V vs RHE.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry of the Co–Ni–Mo coating in 1 M KOH at 50 mV s−1 reveals that cathodic current densities at −0.58 V vs RHE increase as the number of cycles progresses. This behavior, observed within the potential range of −0.08 to −0.58 V vs RHE, confirms the electrochemical characteristics of the Mo-containing alloy.

caption: Correlation between specific modulus and specific strength for PEEK specimens, calculated by normalizing modulus and UTS by material density.
summary: This plot depicts the correlation between specific modulus and specific strength for PEEK samples, where values are normalized by density. The analysis reveals that the Hilbert curve pattern exhibits lower modulus and strength, indicating less efficient load distribution capabilities compared to other infill patterns evaluated in the study.

caption: SRIM-calculated displacement per atom (dpa) profile as a function of proton irradiation depth.
summary: This plot illustrates the proton irradiation damage profile generated using the K–P quick calculation mode in SRIM software. It displays the displacement per atom (dpa) values across varying irradiation depths, providing a quantitative assessment of the radiation-induced damage distribution within the material specimen under the specified simulation parameters.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of L-DED Ti55531 + 0.10B alloy showing TiB particles as distinct long hexagonal features.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the microstructure of L-DED Ti55531 + 0.10B alloy. TiB particles are clearly visible as bright white, long hexagonal shapes approximately 500 nm in width. In contrast, the surrounding α phase and β matrix appear as grey-black regions, making them difficult to distinguish from one another.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for post-processed Ni-Fe-Mo alloy samples at the [111] orientation, reflecting the modified magnetic properties after thermal processing.
summary: Post-processing treatments, including heat treatment and HIP, are shown to significantly influence the magnetic behavior of LPBF Ni-Fe-Mo alloy samples. The hysteresis loop for the [111] orientation demonstrates the resulting magnetic performance, confirming that these sequential treatments effectively modify the material's magnetic characteristics relative to the as-fabricated condition.

caption: Opening load ratio U plotted against normalized crack length a/W for Aluminium CT specimen A1 tested at an R-ratio of 0.1.
summary: This plot illustrates the variation of the opening load ratio U as a function of the normalized crack length a/W for an Aluminium CT specimen A1 at an R-ratio of 0.1. The data demonstrates the experimental procedure's effectiveness in evaluating the opening load ratio and the effective stress intensity factor range.

caption: T = 0.5 ms: Molten pool solidifies following laser departure, effectively halting all diamond particle motion.
summary: At T = 0.5 ms, the simulation depicts the final solidification of the molten pool after the laser has departed. This cooling process halts all diamond particle motion, finalizing the morphological structure. This stage confirms the successful infiltration of gaps, contributing to the control of interfacial defects in the material.

caption: False color map illustrating the calculated geometry deviation in the z-direction between the 3D models of the cantilever before and after support removal, as determined by GOM Inspect Professional software.
summary: This panel displays a false color map representing the geometry deviation in the z-direction for a cantilever specimen. The 3D models, captured before and after support removal, were aligned and compared using GOM Inspect Professional software to evaluate the target/actual dimensional accuracy of the manufactured component.

caption: Exploded and assembled views of the 3D tissue device, illustrating the structural components and the final configuration used for tissue model assembly.
summary: This panel presents the 3D tissue device, detailing both the assembled model and its constituent parts. The schematic provides a clear overview of the hardware configuration required to construct the 3D tissue model, serving as the foundational setup for the subsequent drug toxicity and media flow experiments described in the study.

caption: Three-dimensional grain structure volume generated via Toucan simulation, representing a 2 mm x 1 mm x 0.25 mm specimen composed of five 50 μm layers at a 2.5 μm resolution.
summary: This simulation result demonstrates the capability of the Toucan code to predict complex grain structure volumes spanning multiple additive manufacturing meltpools. The generated 3D microstructure, produced in 1.6 seconds on dual NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, highlights the software's efficiency in capturing grain size and shape features influenced by specific scan patterns.

caption: Distribution of the four thermal treatment conditions in a three-dimensional principal component (PC) space, showing distinct clustering of samples with similar thermal histories.
summary: Principal component analysis is utilized to represent the distinct thermal profiles in a consistent low-dimensional space. By using three PC scores, the different heat treatment conditions are mapped, demonstrating that samples with similar thermal histories cluster together, which validates the effectiveness of PCA for characterizing complex multi-step thermal processing data.

caption: Tribo-data map illustrating the spatial distribution of the friction force measured during the wear test.
summary: This tribo-data map provides a spatial visualization of the friction force generated during the tribological testing of the Ti6Al4V-3 sample. By mapping the friction force, the figure highlights regions of varying frictional resistance, which correlates with the surface wear characteristics and the mechanical interaction between the sample and counter body.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the NC Ni(Fe) alloy after annealing at 646 °C.
summary: This bright field TEM image captures the microstructure of the NC Ni(Fe) alloy after annealing at 646 °C.
