caption: Engineering stress-strain curves comparing LPBF-printed Ti-6SS specimens in the as-built state versus those subjected to post-processing stress relief.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of LPBF-printed Ti-6SS specimens under tensile loading. It directly compares the stress-strain behavior of the material in its as-built condition against specimens that have undergone stress relief treatment, highlighting the influence of thermal post-processing on the alloy's deformation characteristics and overall mechanical performance.

caption: Comparison of maximum working temperature versus specific strength for various materials.
summary: This Ashby plot compares the maximum working temperature and specific strength of the Bouligand ceramic structures against various other materials. The visualization highlights the competitive performance of the Bouligand structure, illustrating its capability to maintain mechanical integrity while providing thermal insulation in demanding high-temperature environments.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing SL:Er,Yb phosphor and composite powders, highlighting vibrational bands between 1000 and 1750 cm-1, with the CsPbBr2.25I0.75+SL:Er,Yb composite displaying additional characteristic bands for CH2 and OH functional groups.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy identifies functional groups on the composite surfaces. The SL:Er,Yb phosphor shows two absorption bands. The CsPbBr2.25I0.75+SL:Er,Yb composite exhibits the most intense vibrational bands in the 1000–1750 cm-1 range, including two extra bands attributed to CH2 and OH groups, suggesting their role in quantum dot attachment.

caption: Conceptual flowchart illustrating the model inadequacy framework, where a target shape serves as input for an ANN inverse design tool to predict shear modulus distributions for FEM-based shape reproduction, accounting for inherent bias discrepancies.
summary: This flowchart outlines the inverse design process for elastic rings, where a target shape is processed by an ANN to determine shear modulus inputs for FEM simulations. The framework explicitly incorporates a bias term to quantify the model inadequacy, representing the discrepancy between the desired target shape and the final FE output.

caption: Instability map of the as-forged nickel-based superalloy at a strain of 1.0.
summary: Shown is the instability map for the as-forged nickel-based superalloy at a strain of 1.0. This contour plot delineates the zones of flow instability at this high strain level, providing a comprehensive view of the material's processing stability limits and potential failure modes during the forging process.

caption: Z-directional average atomic coordinates showing the diffusion depth of carbon atoms into the Ti substrate.
summary: The z-directional average atomic coordinates reveal the diffusion depth of carbon atoms into the Ti substrate. By the conclusion of the simulation, the data indicates that a 2.3 Å thick carbide layer has successfully formed, quantifying the extent of carbon penetration and reaction within the titanium material.

caption: Impact dynamics of a droplet on a clean aqueous glycerol pool at We = 256 and Re = 2314, showing the formation of a smooth, uniform crown.
summary: This panel displays the impact dynamics of a droplet on a clean aqueous glycerol pool at a Weber number of 256 and Reynolds number of 2314. The experimental observation reveals the formation of a smooth, uniform crown, serving as the baseline reference for comparing surfactant-laden and alternative liquid pool impacts.

caption: Micro-photoluminescence spectra of 1L-MoS2 and Mo0.5W0.5S2 alloy films excited at 532 nm, with vertical grey lines indicating reference peak positions for 1L-MoS2 and 1L-WS2.
summary: Micro-photoluminescence spectroscopy evaluates the optical quality and excitonic bandgap of the grown materials. Spectra for 1L-MoS2 and Mo0.5W0.5S2 are compared against reference peak positions for 1L-MoS2 and 1L-WS2, represented by vertical dashed lines, to characterize the optical response of the alloy film under 532 nm laser excitation.

caption: Semiquantitative analysis of total CD206+ macrophage counts in wound beds, illustrating the distribution of M2 phenotype cells across the different treatment conditions.
summary: Semiquantitative analysis of total CD206+ macrophage counts in wound beds, illustrating the distribution of M2 phenotype cells across the different treatment conditions. The total number of CD206+ macrophages exhibited an opposite trend compared to the total CD68+ macrophage population across the blank, gel, and Dopa-gel treatment groups.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the transverse (X–Y) plane for forged Ti-6Al-4V.
summary: Forged Ti-6Al-4V is characterized by its specific crystallographic orientation distribution as shown in the inverse pole figure map of the transverse plane. This map provides a baseline for comparing the microstructural texture and grain characteristics against the cast and EBM variants of the same titanium alloy.

caption: Deconvoluted Se 3d XPS spectra showing peak shifts for different Ni concentrations.
summary: Se 3d spectra in Fig. 3(c) reveal peaks at 54.43 eV and 53.55 eV for x = 0.00. The preferential formation of NiSe2 and resulting Se deficiency lead to a shift toward lower binding energies, with peaks recorded at 54.17 eV and 53.23 eV for x = 0.20.

caption: Comparison of P–h curves between simulation and theoretical model under the third loading condition.
summary: This panel presents the P–h curve comparison between simulation and theoretical results under the third loading condition. The obtained P–h curve is substituted into Eq. (24) to verify the proposed theoretical model, showing that the theoretical predictions align well with simulation results under varying displacement control loading conditions.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of GelMA and GelMA-ALN variants, showing the emergence of a methylene proton peak at 2.8 ppm that increases in intensity with higher ALN input.
summary: The 1H NMR analysis confirms the successful modification of GelMA with ALN. The spectra reveal a distinct methylene proton peak at 2.8 ppm, which demonstrates a clear increasing trend corresponding to the amount of ALN input, providing direct evidence of the successful incorporation of ALN into the GelMA backbone.

caption: Design and filling pattern of the hollow strut with thin plate lattice (TPL) architecture.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental design and filling pattern of the hollow strut with thin plate lattice (TPL) architecture. As described in the literature, this simple cubic unit cell design was selected for the current study to investigate the structural characteristics of the TPL configuration.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of region VIII in the peak-aged Cu-4Ni-0.9Si-0.5Ti alloy, revealing the lattice structure of the precipitates.
summary: This HRTEM image of region VIII provides atomic-scale insight into the nanoscale precipitates within the peak-aged Cu-4Ni-0.9Si-0.5Ti alloy. Combined with SAED analysis, this image confirms the presence of Ni16Ti6Si7 and Ni2Si phases, which are essential components of the alloy's microstructure and contribute to its overall precipitation strengthening.

caption: Backscatter electron image of the E5Gd as-extruded Mg–Er–Gd–Ni alloy surface after 600 s of immersion in 3.0 wt.% KCl solution.
summary: This backscatter electron image shows the surface of the E5Gd as-extruded Mg–Er–Gd–Ni alloy after 600 seconds of immersion in a 3.0 wt.% KCl solution. It serves as the final comparison point to evaluate the impact of extrusion on surface corrosion products in high-Gd content alloys.

caption: Optical transmission measurements taken at five distinct locations (A through E) across a U-shaped hydrogel sample to assess Au nanoparticle distribution.
summary: Optical transmission measurements were performed at different sites, denoted as A through E, across a U-shaped hydrogel sample. This assessment aimed to determine the spatial distribution of Au nanoparticles within the hydrogel matrix by comparing the transmission values at these specific locations across the sample geometry.

caption: Fracture surface of Alloy B at high temperature, showing structural features comparable to the room temperature condition.
summary: Alloy B exhibits high-temperature fracture characteristics that are similar to those observed at room temperature, demonstrating its thermal stability. The fracture surface contains both cleavage planes and ductile dimples. This consistency indicates that the underlying failure mechanism, initiated by intermetallic particles, is not significantly altered by elevated temperature exposure.

caption: Random Forest (RF) model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: Random Forest model performance is depicted via a confusion matrix. This visualization, derived from the uniform dataset shared by all models, allows for a clear assessment of the model's classification precision and recall, providing insight into how the Random Forest algorithm handles the specific data distribution provided.

caption: DNST creep curves for EBM Ti–6Al–4V specimens tested at 650 °C, illustrating deformation behavior across different build directions.
summary: This panel displays DNST creep curves for EBM Ti–6Al–4V at 650 °C, comparing different build directions. The curves show that creep deformation initially overlaps but progressively diverges with each step, suggesting that damage accumulates differently depending on the build orientation, which results in the observed diverging creep behavior.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing the Hf atom distribution within a cylindrical region of interest, 15 nm in diameter and 135 nm in length, oriented perpendicular to the γ′-γ interface.
summary: This panel displays an atom probe tomography reconstruction of Hf atoms within a defined cylindrical volume. The region of interest, measuring 15 nm in diameter and 135 nm in length, is oriented perpendicular to the γ′-γ interface to facilitate the analysis of Hf atomic distribution at maximum distances from the interface boundary.

caption: Cumulative mass loss as a function of total particle throughput for TUFC60 M alloy during impact erosion testing with HSP 40/70 particles at 800 °C.
summary: The erosion performance of the TUFC60 M alloy is characterized by measuring cumulative mass loss against total particle throughput at 800 °C. The slope of this relationship defines the erosion ratio, allowing for a direct assessment of the material's resistance to impact erosion under the specified experimental test conditions.

caption: STEM-HAADF micrograph of the cast AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy, featuring red circles indicating specific regions selected for EDS chemical composition quantification.
summary: This STEM-HAADF micrograph displays the microstructure of the cast AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy. Red circles highlight specific areas chosen for EDS analysis to quantify the chemical composition of the constituent phases. These measurements, derived from multiple read-outs, provide essential data for characterizing the alloy's elemental distribution and phase chemistry.

caption: Schematic representation of the two primary build orientations utilized for sample fabrication, specifically highlighting the vertical (Z) direction perpendicular to the build plate and the horizontal (XY) direction along the length of the build plate.
summary: This schematic illustrates the two primary build orientations, vertical (Z) and horizontal (XY), employed during the additive manufacturing process. The vertical orientation involves printing samples perpendicular to the build plate, while the horizontal orientation involves printing samples along the length of the build plate, as depicted in the figure.

caption: Gamma surface energy profile for a 4-layer twin formation in Ni3Al and a complex composition γ′ phase along the ⟨121⟩ CSF direction.
summary: This panel displays the gamma surface energy profile for a 4-layer twin formation in Ni3Al and a complex composition γ′ phase along the ⟨121⟩ CSF direction. The energy cost for twin formation in the complex γ′ phase is significantly lower than in Ni3Al, indicating easier twin grain formation.

caption: Optical micrograph of a pure Cu sample fabricated via LPBF using a high volumetric energy density of 625 J/mm³.
summary: This optical micrograph depicts the microstructure of pure Cu printed at a high volumetric energy density of 625 J/mm³. The image is used to visually compare the relative density and defect distribution against samples produced at lower energy levels, demonstrating the influence of VED on the final printed sample quality.

caption: Eclipsed adsorption geometry of hydrazine on the NiZn(1 1 1) surface, showing the most stable configuration with an adsorption energy of -2.71 eV.
summary: The eclipsed geometry of hydrazine on the NiZn(1 1 1) surface represents the most stable adsorption configuration identified. DFT calculations reveal a highly exothermic adsorption energy of -2.71 eV for this specific binding mode, highlighting the strong interaction between the hydrazine molecule and the bimetallic catalyst surface at this orientation.

caption: TRL2 error evolution over a 500-step rollout for the full HMO model compared against Jacobian+density (J), density-only (DO), and metric-only (MO) variants.
summary: This plot illustrates the TRL2 error over a 500-step rollout for the full HMO model and three ablation variants. The full HMO model achieves the lowest error, while the DO variant diverges rapidly due to insufficient directional information. Both J and MO variants remain stable but exhibit higher overall error rates.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the W–C–Co system, specifically constrained to a 10% cobalt content, indicating the thermodynamic stability regions for sintering.
summary: The ternary phase diagram for the W–C–Co system with 10% cobalt content provides the thermodynamic framework for processing cemented carbides. It indicates that the sintering temperature for these materials is generally maintained above 1200 °C to ensure proper liquid-phase formation and densification during the manufacturing process.

caption: Raman spectra of ZTA samples sintered at various temperatures with a 5 h holding time.
summary: Raman spectra of ZTA samples sintered at different temperatures under a holding time of 5 h are presented. These patterns allow for the evaluation of phase evolution in the ZTA material when subjected to extended sintering durations, facilitating a direct comparison with the 2 h holding condition.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the as-forged microstructure.
summary: The as-forged condition exhibits a high GND density of 30.9 × 10^12 m^-2. This map visualizes the spatial distribution of these dislocations, providing a quantitative baseline for the internal strain and defect density present in the material prior to the application of solution treatment and aging heat cycles.

caption: Iron loss measurements for P 10/50 conditions in Fe-6.5 wt% Si alloy rings subjected to various annealing protocols.
summary: Iron losses for P 10/50 are compared across different annealing conditions using AC test experiments. These measurements provide critical data on the energy dissipation characteristics of the Fe-6.5 wt% Si alloy rings, reflecting how specific thermal processing parameters influence the overall magnetic efficiency and performance of the material under alternating current.

caption: Absolute derivative of magnetization (dM/dT) plotted against temperature, demonstrating the transition characteristics for FeCoNi, Cu-modified, and V-containing alloys.
summary: The absolute derivative of magnetization (dM/dT) versus temperature reveals transition characteristics for the alloys. FeCoNiCu1.15 exhibits behavior similar to FeCoNi, while the introduction of V significantly modifies the derivative, hindering magnetocaloric properties. This plot allows for a direct comparison of magnetic transitions across the different alloy modifications.

caption: Evolution of the IOLa segmentation loss during the training process, comparing training (blue) and validation (orange) datasets.
summary: This learning curve illustrates the loss evolution for the single-task IOLa segmentation model across training and validation phases. caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the LPBF-produced Al–Mg–Zr alloy, highlighting the microstructure with a dashed rectangle indicating the specific area selected for subsequent EDS elemental mapping.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the representative microstructure of the LPBF-produced Al–Mg–Zr alloy. The image provides a clear overview of the grain structure, with a dashed rectangle marking the specific region chosen for detailed EDS elemental mapping to analyze the distribution of alloying elements and secondary phase particles.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the anodic polarization curves of Ni-Fe alloys, showing consistent electrochemical kinetics across three repeated measurements with negligible variation.
summary: Tafel plots derived from the anodic polarization curves of the fabricated Ni-Fe alloys are presented here. These plots characterize the electrochemical kinetics of the materials. The measurements were repeated three times to ensure reliability, showing negligible variation in the results across the different iron-ratio samples.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the natural logarithm of measured ion intensities versus inverse temperature for pure Ni, Co, Cr, and Al metals as determined by Knudsen Effusion Mass Spectrometry (KEMS).
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature-dependent ion intensity measurements for pure Ni, Co, Cr, and Al obtained via KEMS. Linear regression analysis of these plots yields slopes that are directly proportional to the sublimation enthalpies of the respective metals, providing essential thermodynamic data for the median temperature ranges investigated.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis performed under TEM on selected Al2Cu phases within the Alloy B microstructure.
summary: EDX analysis conducted under TEM confirms the chemical composition of the Al2Cu phases identified in Alloy B. caption: Initial electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS 1) Bode phase plot showing the baseline electrochemical response of LPBF planes before passivation.
summary: This initial EIS 1 Bode phase plot establishes the baseline electrochemical impedance characteristics for the LPBF planes. caption: STEM image showing the microstructure of the as-fractured SLM316LSS specimen processed at 140 W laser power.
summary: This STEM image displays the microstructure of an as-fractured SLM316LSS specimen fabricated via selective laser melting at 140 W. The observation highlights the characteristic structural features present in the material following the fracture process, providing insight into the microstructural state of the stainless steel under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Time evolution of the normalized x-component of magnetization (mx/m) under an external magnetic field H0 of 900 Oe applied along the y-axis.
summary: This plot illustrates the time-dependent behavior of the x-component of magnetization, mx/m, for a system subjected to a 900 Oe external field applied along the y-axis. caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves recorded at 5 mV s⁻¹ for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors featuring varying numbers of stacked OTU layers in 1 M H₂SO₄ electrolyte.

caption: Unit cell topology corresponding to the RNFS:2:0 mono-RNL architecture.
summary: This panel displays the unit cell topology for the RNFS:2:0 mono-RNL architecture. caption: Magnetic specific heat C mag of bcc Co calculated via Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic specific heat C mag for bcc cobalt as determined through Monte Carlo simulation. summary: TGA curves illustrate the single-stage thermal degradation of the PLA matrix in both pure and composite filaments. The residual mass measured at 450 °C is primarily attributed to the rCF content within the composite, providing a quantitative assessment of the filler loading in the PLA/rCF material system.

caption: Top-view SEM micrograph of the Inconel 625 surface following the corrosion test.
summary: Captured after corrosion testing, this top-view SEM image reveals the altered surface morphology of Inconel 625. Comparison with the pre-corrosion state allows for the identification of surface damage, pitting, or other degradation features resulting from the corrosive environment, highlighting the impact of the test on the material's surface integrity.

caption: SKPFM analysis of Cu3 steel showing morphology (c1), Volta potential map (c2), and a line scan (c3) identifying Cu-rich precipitates with a potential fluctuation range of -14 to 34 mV.
summary: SKPFM analysis of Cu3 steel illustrates the surface morphology and Volta potential distribution. caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves for nickel-molybdenum coated 3D-printed electrodes, illustrating electrochemical behavior across varying molybdenum deposition levels in a 1 mol KOH electrolyte solution.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements for nickel-molybdenum coated 3D-printed electrodes. caption: Bode impedance and phase angle plots for LPBF-deposited NAB alloys in as-built and annealed states after 20 days of immersion.

caption: Primary creep strain of CMSX-4 superalloy plotted against time at 750 °C under various stress levels, showing experimental data points (solid circles) compared to the model fit derived from Eq. (21).
summary: Experimental primary creep strain data for CMSX-4 at 750 °C are compared against the model defined by Eq. (21). summary: This panel presents the fatigue crack growth rate as a function of the fracture toughness range for PA-6 specimens printed at 240 °C. summary: The IPF map of the interface demonstrates epitaxial growth occurring across the fusion boundary between the Ni-based weld metal and the Inconel 625 base metal. caption: Polar diagram illustrating the texture and grain orientation of K418 alloy subjected to 200 W laser power.
summary: Representing the K418 alloy at 200 W, this polar diagram highlights the grain orientation characteristics. summary: Region 7 of the blunt bridge extrudate cross-section displays a 2D plane stress yield surface. caption: Volta potential difference map corresponding to the Al 65 Zr 20 Fe 15 alloy ingot surface.
summary: Representing the electronic surface properties, this Volta potential difference map corresponds to the Al 65 Zr 20 Fe 15 alloy ingot. summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the degradation kinetics of AFRP in water. caption: Apparent crystallite size parallel to the c-axis (ACS∥c) for the normal Ti miniscrew, mapped across a range of 11.5–28.6 nm.
summary: The apparent crystallite size parallel to the crystallographic c-axis is mapped for the normal Ti miniscrew. The color scale represents values ranging from 11.5 to 28.6 nm. caption: Dark-field TEM image revealing activated nano-twins within the coarse cellular structure of the melt-pool boundary, with specific twin domains highlighted by red circles.
summary: This dark-field TEM image captures the microstructure of the melt-pool boundary, specifically highlighting activated nano-twins within the coarse cellular regions. caption: Thermo-Calc simulated time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram depicting the precipitation kinetics of M23C6 carbides at the grain boundaries of the IN738 superalloy.
summary: Thermo-Calc simulation results are displayed as a time-temperature-transformation diagram for the IN738 superalloy. caption: Cr Kα elemental distribution map showing the localization of chromium within the oxidized layer.

caption: Surface electric current characteristics of oriented SiC w composites showing anisotropic conductivity behavior.

summary: The EBSD map of heat-treated IN718 in the building direction demonstrates that the material has undergone complete recrystallization. summary: Magnified SEM imaging of the 40-minute bonding interface confirms the presence of a wider interface transition zone. summary: This plot displays the secondary stage creep behavior of tested specimens, contrasting experimental measurements with CPFE modelling predictions. Different colors and line styles distinguish between various stress levels and m values, providing a comparative view of displacement trends under cyclic loading conditions for this specific orientation.

caption: Comparison of EDS spectra for the as-printed and reduced 7 wt.% NiCl2 loaded samples, illustrating quantitative changes in elemental composition.
summary: This panel provides a quantitative comparison of the EDS spectra obtained from the 7 wt.% NiCl2 loaded samples before and after the reduction process. The spectral data allows for an assessment of the elemental composition changes resulting from the treatment, offering insights into the chemical evolution of the composite.

caption: Comparison of diameter differences between the two ends of CHT_MS250 samples after impact testing at 298 K and 823 K across various strain rates.
summary: This plot quantifies the diameter difference between sample ends to assess deformation uniformity. At 298 K, differences range from 0.23% to 0.79%, indicating uniform deformation. At 823 K, differences increase from 1.73% at 700 s-1 to 3.37% at 1200 s-1, before stabilizing at 1700 s-1, reflecting non-uniformity at elevated temperatures.

caption: Crystallographic grain structure analysis extracted from EBSD data collected at six representative locations on the part.
summary: Electron backscatter diffraction data were acquired at six specific locations to characterize the material's crystallographic aspects. Four distinct grain-structure quantifiers, including grain orientation, aspect ratio, and texture, were extracted from these maps to provide a detailed understanding of the microstructural evolution resulting from the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: XCT imaging of rCF-H filaments showing long fiber morphology and the presence of large internal voids.
summary: XCT imaging of rCF-H filaments reveals the internal morphology of the composite. Long fibers are clearly observed, exceeding the threshold size of the XCT scan. Furthermore, the imaging highlights the presence of larger voids within the filament structure, which are distinct from the smaller void regions found in printed coupons.

caption: Potential response of individual pulses during a 40 s timeframe around 5 h.
summary: This panel presents the potential response of individual pulses during a 40 s timeframe around the 5 h mark. By zooming into the pulse level, the data provides a detailed view of the electrochemical behavior of the Fe alloy disk during the active and inactive phases of the pulsed galvanostatic current.

caption: Localized TEM view of the SB-Ti2.9Cu alloy showing the eutectoid lamellar structure found within the heterogeneous matrix.
summary: This localized TEM image highlights the eutectoid lamellar structure within the SB-Ti2.9Cu alloy. The presence of these structures, alongside a coarser alpha-Ti lath matrix and higher density of Ti2Cu nanoparticles, indicates an unstable melt pool and localized phase separation during solidification, which characterizes the heterogeneous nature of this alloy.

caption: Internal planetary vacuum chamber used for the OMOTENASHI thermal vacuum test conducted at JAXA in November 2019.
summary: This photograph displays the internal planetary vacuum chamber utilized during the OMOTENASHI thermal vacuum testing program. The equipment was operated at JAXA in November 2019 to simulate space environment conditions, providing the necessary experimental setup for evaluating the thermal performance of the OMOTENASHI mission hardware under vacuum.

caption: 2D planar deformation charge density for Mn-segregated Ni Σ3 [110](111) grain boundaries, oriented along the plane defined by Ni3, Ni5, and alloying atom X.
summary: Focusing on the bonding environment, this 2D map provides a detailed view of the charge density redistribution around the Mn solute. The accumulation of electrons between Mn and its first-nearest neighbor Ni atoms indicates the creation of strong Mn–Ni bonds, directly correlating with segregation-induced changes in fracture strength.

caption: Equilibrium and Scheil solidification curves for Ti-4Cu and Ti-7Cu binary alloys, illustrating the temperature-dependent solid fraction evolution.
summary: This plot displays the equilibrium and Scheil solidification curves for Ti-4Cu and Ti-7Cu alloys. These curves are used to calculate the Q true values for the specified compositions. Additionally, a secondary parabolic fit is applied to the initial data points within the 0 to 0.01 solid fraction range.

caption: Cr 2p 3/2 XPS spectra of a mechanically polished specimen after exposure to high-temperature, high-pressure deionized water at 250 ℃ for 1 h, illustrating surface oxide cleaning dynamics.
summary: Mechanically polished specimen surface analysis via Cr 2p 3/2 XPS spectra reveals the sputtering dynamics of the oxide layer. The observed peak variations confirm that the Cr oxide layer is effectively removed from the surface after 60 seconds of Ar+ sputtering, indicating the depth of the oxidation layer.

caption: Nyquist representation of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for specimens polished to a 1 μm finish.
summary: This Nyquist plot presents the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for specimens polished to a 1 μm finish. Observed differences between these 1 μm polished samples and conventional specimens suggest that the material's microstructure plays a potential role in determining its overall corrosion behavior during electrochemical testing.

caption: Horizontal 10 nm thick slice of the APT reconstruction, highlighting the spatial distribution of 18O, 16O, and Y ions within the alumina scale.
summary: A horizontal 10 nm thick slice of the APT reconstruction provides a detailed view of the oxide scale microstructure. Yttrium atoms serve as markers for grain boundaries, where 18O ions are localized on one side, extending 10–15 nm from the Y-rich regions, confirming the preferential oxide growth along these specific grain boundaries.

caption: Three-dimensional micrograph illustrating the indentation surface morphology on the He-deposit.
summary: This 3D micrograph provides a detailed visualization of the indentation surface on the He-deposit. It serves as a foundational view for understanding the surface topography and the physical impact of the indentation process, which is further analyzed through subsequent load-displacement and profilometry measurements at various deposit locations.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Co–Ni system at 1510 K, displaying calculated phase boundaries overlaid with experimental data points.
summary: This isothermal section at 1510 K for the Cu–Co–Ni system demonstrates the accuracy of the thermodynamic database. The calculated phase boundaries show excellent agreement with experimental data, confirming that the updated Cu–Ni interaction parameters are fully compatible with the ternary interaction parameters used in the Pandat software calculations.

caption: Experimental permeability test platform used for characterizing Sine structure samples.
summary: Experimental permeability test platform used for characterizing Sine structure samples. This photograph shows the physical apparatus used to conduct permeability measurements, demonstrating the practical implementation of the test setup described in the schematic, and confirming the experimental validation of the fluid flow properties of the printed porous structures.

caption: Elemental mapping showing the spatial distribution of Cu and Al within the bonding area.
summary: Elemental mapping showing the spatial distribution of Cu and Al within the bonding area. This visualization highlights the chemical composition across the interface, allowing for the identification of boundary precipitates and the assessment of elemental segregation or diffusion patterns occurring at the junction of the two materials.

caption: Average strain to failure plotted against printing orientation and strut diameter, with shaded regions representing standard deviation and dashed lines indicating quasi-static literature values.
summary: This plot illustrates the average strain to failure as a function of printing orientation and strut diameter. The data reveals increased ductility compared to quasi-static counterparts, potentially influenced by surface defects at specific orientations. The results highlight how structural parameters and loading directions significantly impact the mechanical failure behavior of the printed specimens.

caption: Cyclic stability performance of the 2 wt% Co-HPMC-C catalyst measured over multiple cycles of 4-NP conversion.
summary: This plot illustrates the cyclic stability of the 2 wt% Co-HPMC-C ceramic-based catalyst during the conversion of 4-NP. The data tracks the performance of the catalyst over repeated cycles, providing insight into the durability and reusability of the 3D-printed material for this specific catalytic application.

caption: Laser confocal microscopy observations illustrating the surface topography and roughness variations of electrodeposited copper foils subjected to different ultrasonic amplitudes.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy was utilized to quantify changes in surface roughness for the electrodeposited copper foils. By measuring the surface topography at different ultrasonic amplitudes, this technique provides a quantitative assessment of how the ultrasonic processing conditions influence the final surface roughness of the deposited copper foil samples.

caption: Immunofluorescent visualization of HFFs seeded on a polished Ti-6Al-4V surface (P1) after 48 hours, showing DAPI-stained nuclei in blue and F-actin filaments in green.
summary: Human foreskin fibroblasts (HFFs) were seeded onto a polished Ti-6Al-4V surface (P1) and cultured for 48 hours. The cells were stained with DAPI for nuclei and Phalloidin for F-actin. Fluorescence microscopy reveals the morphology and distribution of the fibroblasts as they attach and spread across the polished metallic substrate.

caption: Experimental and numerical force-displacement behavior for spar E.
summary: Spar E illustrates the force-displacement behavior comparing experimental findings with numerical simulation results. A strong correlation between the experimental and numerical curves is evident, demonstrating that the numerical model provides a precise representation of the mechanical response for spar E, consistent with the overall validation of the study.

caption: Overlay of EDX elemental mapping for C, O, Si, and Ca on the SEM image of composite S1.
summary: This panel presents an overlay of EDX elemental mapping for carbon, oxygen, silicon, and calcium on the SEM image of composite S1. The mapping technique effectively differentiates the sand grains from the surrounding resin, providing a comprehensive view of the elemental distribution within the composite structure.

caption: TEM image of Ru3Ni3 NAs showing the overall assembly and morphology.
summary: The TEM image of the Ru3Ni3 NAs provides a comprehensive view of the sample morphology. This characterization is part of the detailed study conducted to determine the 3D assembly structure of the Ru3Ni3 NAs, complementing the STEM and elemental mapping data to confirm the hierarchical nature of the product.

caption: Hydrolysis grid configuration depicting particle distribution on the simulated surface.
summary: Hydrolysis grid visualization displays a distinct region of the simulated material surface. Different particles are represented by specific colors or symbols to ensure varied and realistic complexity. This approach is essential for maintaining the accuracy of the simulation, ensuring that the results remain representative of actual material surface conditions.

caption: Representative volume elements (RVEs) of the four porous structures: Fischer-Koch S, Octet, Diamond, and Double Gyroid.
summary: The RVE modes for four distinct porous structures are displayed. These include the Fischer-Koch S, Octet, Diamond, and Double Gyroid geometries. These representative volume elements serve as the fundamental building blocks for constructing the orthopedic implants and scaffold models used in the subsequent experimental and computational analyses.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph displaying the core-Mg3(TiAl9)2 shell-Mn structure, which measures approximately 1 μm × 1 μm.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging confirms the presence of the core-Mg3(TiAl9)2 shell-Mn structure previously identified. The micrograph provides high-resolution visualization of these particles, which exhibit a consistent size of approximately 1 μm × 1 μm, further validating the structural characteristics of the second phase observed within the material.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the influence of line energy density and hatch spacing on crack density.
summary: This contour plot identifies the optimal processing parameters by mapping crack density as a function of line energy density and hatch spacing. It serves as a diagnostic tool to determine the most suitable combination of these variables to minimize cracking during the manufacturing process.

caption: Gas chromatography profile of LaNi5 after 224 h of ball-milling, demonstrating intensified CH4 generation.
summary: Extended ball-milling for 224 h results in a more pronounced CH4 peak in the gas chromatography spectrum. This observation confirms that prolonged mechanical processing under the specified atmosphere continues to drive the generation of methane, indicating a sustained chemical reaction between the LaNi5 catalyst and the reactant gases.

caption: XRD pole figure for the Ang90 scanning strategy, showing a pronounced (200) crystallographic texture.
summary: The pole figure for the Ang90 scanning strategy is shown in panel (c). The results indicate a pronounced (200) texture, which characterizes the crystallographic orientation developed under this specific scanning condition during the production process.

caption: Energy absorption curves for BCTs and SSLCTs evaluated at a wall thickness of 1 mm.
summary: Energy absorption performance is depicted for both BCTs and SSLCTs at a 1 mm wall thickness. These curves quantify the total energy dissipated by the structures during the crashworthiness test, allowing for an assessment of their respective efficiency in absorbing impact energy throughout the displacement process.

caption: Schematic representation of the nanofluid preparation process involving sequential ultrasonic dispersion, oscillation, and stirring steps.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the systematic preparation process for Fe3O4 and SiO2 nanofluids. By employing sequential stages of ultrasonic dispersion, oscillation, and stirring, stable nanofluid suspensions are successfully synthesized. The diagram provides a clear visual guide to the experimental methodology required to achieve consistent and stable nanoparticle dispersion in the base fluid.

caption: Bode phase angle plots showing the relationship between frequency and phase angle (θ) for CS, C3NS, C6NS, C9NS, and C12NS coatings in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Bode phase angle plots depict the frequency versus phase angle (θ) for coatings with varying nickel contents in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These results highlight how excessive nickel addition impacts the corrosion product film quality, as evidenced by the shifts in phase angle across the tested frequency range.

caption: Faradaic efficiency for CO and H2 production measured at current densities from 12 to 100 mA cm-2 for Ag-based electrodes prepared at -0.1 V vs Ag/AgCl.
summary: This panel displays the CO and H2 Faradaic efficiency for Ag-based electrodes deposited at -0.1 V. Results indicate that CO selectivity decreases as current density increases from 12 to 100 mA cm-2, a trend attributed to the increasing dominance of the hydrogen evolution reaction during the bicarbonate electrolysis process.

caption: Surface strain distribution at the point of fracture for an as-built coupon oriented at θ = 45°.
summary: This panel presents the surface strain map of an as-built coupon tested at a 45° orientation. The visualization captures the localized strain distribution at the point of fracture, demonstrating the material's mechanical response and failure behavior under this specific orientation, which is critical for understanding anisotropic properties in as-built coupons.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for 2024-T3 alloy measured at 1 mV s-1 in 10 g L-1 NaCl, comparing bare metal to samples pitted for 1 and 8 hours at -400 mV.
summary: This panel displays potentiodynamic polarization curves for 2024-T3 aluminum alloy in a 10 g L-1 NaCl solution. It compares the electrochemical behavior of bare alloy against samples subjected to pitting corrosion for 1 and 8 hours at a potential of -400 mV, highlighting the impact of prior corrosion on polarization.

caption: TS500 Cu-40Zn TC region displaying the Kernel Average Misorientation map combined with image quality data.
summary: TS500 Cu-40Zn TC region displaying the Kernel Average Misorientation map combined with image quality data. This panel is one of several analyzed to confirm structural trends across processing conditions from TC to BC regions, highlighting the specific local misorientation state observed in the TS500 processed material sample.

caption: Polar distribution of parameter l for the superalloy pre-serviced at 1050°C/100 h.
summary: This polar distribution plot represents the parameter l for the superalloy subjected to 1050°C for 100 hours. The plot quantifies the geometric changes in the γ' precipitates resulting from thermal exposure. It serves as a comparative metric to evaluate the extent of coarsening and morphological degradation compared to the as-received condition.

caption: SAED pattern confirming the presence of NbC precipitates through diffraction spot comparison.
summary: The SAED pattern presented in this panel confirms the identity of the spherical precipitates as NbC. Through systematic diffraction spot comparison, the crystalline nature of these precipitates is verified, supporting the microstructural observations of NbC accumulation at the grain boundaries of the martensitic matrix.

caption: Measured heat generation, calculated heat components, cell potential, and open-circuit voltage for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at 1C.
summary: Panel c presents the thermal and electrochemical characteristics of 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at 1C. The plot includes total heat generation, calculated heat components, and voltage profiles as a function of lithium composition, providing a baseline for comparing the performance of conventional tape-casted electrodes against 3D printed alternatives.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves showing mass loss as a function of temperature for 3D-printed PCL scaffolds.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves illustrate the thermal degradation behavior of 3D-printed PCL scaffolds. The measured data reveals a consistent single-step thermolysis process across all scaffold samples, demonstrating minimal deviation in thermal stability and indicating that the structural integrity of the polymer matrix remains uniform during the heating process.

caption: Schematic representation of the grinding process showing material removal through the synergistic action of numerous abrasive particles on the grinding wheel.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental grinding process, where material is removed from the workpiece through the collective action of tens of thousands of minute abrasive particles located on the rotating grinding wheel. It provides a macroscopic view of the interaction between the tool and the workpiece during material processing.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of H13 steel powder confirming the presence of a dominant martensitic α phase and a minor austenitic γ phase.
summary: The X-ray diffraction pattern reveals that the H13 powder primarily consists of the martensitic phase (α phase) alongside a small amount of the austenitic phase (γ phase). This phase composition is consistent with the expected metallurgical state of H13 tool steel powder following the rapid cooling of atomization.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms recorded at a heating rate of 10 °C/min for polycarbonate (PC) samples extracted from PC/AA6061 joints after 1, 7, and 30 days of hygrothermal aging in water at 80 °C, compared against an unaged control sample.
summary: DSC curves illustrate the glass transition temperature (Tg) variations in PC samples following hygrothermal aging. These thermal profiles reveal how water absorption and physical aging influence the polymer's stiffness over time. The data provides insight into the material stability of PC/AA6061 joints subjected to prolonged exposure to aqueous environments at elevated temperatures.

caption: Cyclic mean stress evolution for Diamond 90°/−90° TMF tests conducted at strain amplitudes of Δɛ = 0.8% and 1.0%.
summary: Evolution of cyclic mean stress under Diamond 90°/−90° loading shows no significant stress level shift or asymmetry in deformation mechanisms. Because both minimum and maximum stresses occur near the mean temperature, the mean stress remains stable throughout the cycling process for both strain amplitudes of 0.8% and 1.0%.

caption: EDS analysis results for spot 1, spot 2, and spot 3, confirming the elemental composition of the matrix phases and the precipitated W grains.
summary: The EDS analysis results for spot 1, spot 2, and spot 3 provide chemical characterization of the alloy. These spectra substantiate the identification of the matrix phases and confirm that the white spots and strips observed in the SEM image are indeed composed of tungsten (W) precipitates.

caption: Coefficient of friction (CoF) evolution against the number of strokes for samples under a 1 N load, highlighting running-in and steady-state stages.
summary: This plot displays the CoF variation against the number of strokes under a 1 N load. The Cr 1250-200 sample shows a steady character with values between 0.9 and 1.3. Running-in and steady-state stages are indicated by dashed lines, with higher mean CoF values recorded under this 1 N condition.

caption: Pole figure representation illustrating the crystallographic texture orientation for the 5-5 welded joint specimen.
summary: This panel displays the pole figure analysis for the 5-5 welded joint. It provides a visual representation of the crystallographic texture orientation within the weld region, serving as a key component of the comprehensive texture analysis performed on the three distinct types of welded joints investigated in the study.

caption: Loss modulus profiles for PEKK/LRS composites, highlighting the shift of peak values to higher temperatures with increased filler loading.
summary: Loss modulus profiles for PEKK/LRS composites reveal the influence of ceramic filler content on viscoelastic behavior. Increasing the LRS content mitigates the magnitude of the loss modulus and shifts its peak to higher temperatures, likely due to the reinforcing effect of ceramic particles restricting polymer chain mobility within the composite matrix.

caption: Schematic illustration of a rigid cylinder-on-flat surface contact configuration.
summary: The rigid cylinder-on-flat surface contact model is shown here as a schematic. This geometry is utilized to represent specific tribological conditions, providing a simplified physical framework for analyzing contact mechanics and pressure distribution between a curved rigid body and a flat surface in lubrication and wear studies.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the HIP-treated WMoNbTa RHEA, illustrating the coexistence of columnar grains and refined equiaxed grains approximately 5 μm in diameter with random crystallographic orientations.
summary: The IPF map reveals the crystallographic orientation distribution within the HIP-treated WMoNbTa RHEA sample. It highlights a mixed microstructure consisting of columnar grains alongside numerous refined equiaxed grains, which measure about 5 μm in diameter. These grains exhibit a random orientation distribution, confirming the complex grain structure resulting from the processing.

caption: SAED pattern of the selected HX matrix zone with a zone axis of [02-2].
summary: This SAED pattern corresponds to the selected HX matrix zone, captured with a zone axis of [02-2]. The diffraction analysis of the matrix, in conjunction with the nanoparticle data, confirms the successful fabrication and structural characterization of the HX-3 wt. % TiC nanocomposite material.

caption: Proxigram analysis of the Mo-rich phase in alloy 6, defined by a 5 at.% Mo iso-concentration surface.
summary: The proxigram illustrates the compositional variation across the 5 at.% Mo iso-concentration surface within the Mo-rich phase of alloy 6. This analysis, derived from atom probe tomography, provides a detailed spatial profile of the Mo-rich region, corresponding to the iso-concentration surfaces identified in the broader microstructural characterization of the material.

caption: Demonstration of the flexible polymer shim wrapped around an imprinting roller, showing conformal contact.
summary: The flexible properties of the high-thickness polymer mold are demonstrated by wrapping it around an imprinting roll. The image confirms that the mold maintains conformal contact with the roller surface, which is essential for achieving high-fidelity pattern transfer during the roll-to-roll imprinting process.

caption: SEM image and corresponding EDS elemental distribution maps for the WAAM specimen, highlighting significant precipitates at grain boundaries.
summary: The WAAM specimen exhibits significant precipitates located at grain boundaries. EDS mapping reveals that these precipitates are enriched in Mo with minor amounts of W, while Ni and Fe concentrations remain lower. This elemental distribution analysis provides insight into the microstructural composition and phase segregation within the WAAM-processed material.

caption: Magnetization versus temperature curves for C x N 100-x -A70 samples measured at 40 mT in a reductive atmosphere, with data extrapolated using a polynomial approximation to illustrate thermal stability.
summary: Magnetization versus temperature curves for C x N 100-x -A70 samples were measured at 40 mT in a reductive atmosphere and processed using polynomial extrapolation. For the majority of the investigated compositions, the magnetization values remain relatively high even when the temperature is increased up to 400 °C, demonstrating significant thermal magnetic stability.

caption: Visual documentation of hydrogen bubble evolution on a platinum electrode surface at an increased potential of 1.5 V.
summary: Captured at an applied potential of 1.5 V, this in-situ photograph illustrates the hydrogen bubble evolution on the flat platinum electrode surface. The image demonstrates the morphological changes and bubble density resulting from the increased electrochemical driving force compared to the lower potential state shown in panel a.

caption: DSC measurement of the CoCrFeNiHf0.4 EHEA, detailing the heat flow response across the investigated temperature range.
summary: The DSC curve for the CoCrFeNiHf0.4 EHEA records the thermal transitions occurring during heating and cooling. By comparing these experimental results with database predictions, it is observed that the database tends to slightly overestimate the transition temperatures relative to the values measured in this DSC experiment.

caption: TEM observation of ordered nanoporous CrFe alloy at 0.25 compression strain, illustrating the rhombus-shaped skeleton geometry and interface development.
summary: TEM observation of ordered nanoporous CrFe alloy at 0.25 compression strain, illustrating the rhombus-shaped skeleton geometry and interface development. The skeleton shape changes from approximately 90 degrees to 107 degrees, confirming that the overlapped skeletons form many interfaces as a result of the compressive deformation process.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops representing the easy and hard axis magnetization behavior of an electrolessly deposited Ni81Fe19 permalloy film.
summary: This panel displays the easy and hard axis magnetic hysteresis loops for a Ni81Fe19 permalloy film deposited via an electroless process. The data, obtained using a BH loop tracer under a 100 Oe saturating field, characterizes the magnetic response and anisotropy of the permalloy thin film sample.

caption: Comparative TGA degradation profiles for cured DDDA (dotted) and PGTA (solid) resins before (black) and after (red) a 2-hour scCO2 extraction process.
summary: TGA results for cured DDDA and PGTA resins reveal structural changes following scCO2 extraction. The onset temperature of the primary degradation step increases by 5°C, and the degradation process becomes steeper, concluding 5°C earlier. These shifts indicate that the removal of initial degradation steps is not solely due to moisture evaporation.

caption: In-situ FT-IR spectra of CC+50%SL highlighting the degradation of organic bonds.
summary: In-situ FT-IR spectra of CC+50%SL track the thermal degradation of the sample. The intensity of methyl and methylene peaks gradually decreases as the pyrolysis temperature increases. This observation confirms the progressive breakdown of these specific organic bonds as the material is subjected to higher thermal energy levels.

caption: Thermal and electrochemical profiles including total heat generation, calculated heat rates, cell potential, and open-circuit voltage for 3D printed NMC622 electrodes during lithiation at 1C.
summary: Panel b illustrates the thermal and electrochemical response of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes during lithiation at 1C. By comparing measured heat generation rates with calculated values and potential profiles, the figure demonstrates that 3D printed electrodes exhibit smaller internal resistance, attributed to enhanced interfacial kinetics and faster lithium ion transport.

caption: TEM-EDS elemental mapping of Manganese (Mn) showing its segregation within the intercellular regions of the Si-rich network.
summary: Manganese segregation is clearly observed within the intercellular structure of the Si-rich network in the Base+Mn alloy. This mapping confirms that Mn remains localized in these regions during the T5 condition, contributing to the formation of α-Al(Mn,Fe)Si intermetallic particles at the cell boundaries.

caption: Galvanostatic mid-term stability test results for Ni, Ni–Co, Ni–Zn, and Ni–W nanowire electrodes, conducted at a constant current density of 0.05 Acm⁻² in 30% w/w KOH solution over a 1-hour duration.
summary: Galvanostatic tests were performed on nanostructured Ni and Ni-alloy electrodes to evaluate mid-term stability. Using a 30% w/w KOH electrolyte at room temperature, electrodes were subjected to a constant current density of 0.05 Acm⁻² for one hour, demonstrating the electrochemical performance of the optimized alloy compositions.

caption: Normalized radar chart comparing the compressive strength, flexural strength, and yield stress of LC 3 composites containing different dominant fillers, highlighting Kaolinite's superior performance across all metrics and Montmorillonite's peak yield stress.
summary: This normalized radar chart evaluates the mechanical performance of LC 3 composites with varying fillers. Kaolinite is shown to dominate across compressive strength, flexural strength, and yield stress metrics. Additionally, the plot reveals that Montmorillonite exhibits the highest yield stress among all tested constituents, providing a clear comparative overview of material properties.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of methylene blue solution (50 mg/L) comparing the initial state to the state after 60 minutes of contact with printed glass-based composites in dark conditions.
summary: This panel displays the UV-Vis absorption spectra of a 50 mg/L methylene blue solution. It compares the initial absorbance levels against those measured after 60 minutes of exposure to printed glass-based composites in the dark, illustrating the baseline reduction in dye concentration due to adsorption processes without light-induced photocatalysis.

caption: Binary Al-Yb phase diagram computed via Pandat software, indicating the specific compositions of the experimental alloys.
summary: The binary Al-Yb phase diagram, generated using Pandat software, serves as a foundational reference for the alloy compositions used in this study. It provides the thermodynamic equilibrium context necessary for understanding the solidification behavior and phase stability of the Al-Yb eutectic system under investigation.

caption: Rietveld refinement of the powder neutron diffraction pattern for the A1 HT2 alloy in the ferromagnetic austenite state, displaying experimental data as open circles, calculated and difference patterns as lines, and Bragg reflections as green markers.
summary: This panel presents the Rietveld refinement of powder neutron diffraction data for the A1 HT2 alloy in its magnetically ordered state. The plot illustrates the experimental data, calculated fit, and difference pattern, providing essential structural information. Magnetic Rietveld analysis of these patterns allows for the determination of magnetic moments at specific Wyckoff positions.

caption: Traced trajectory of a PA powder particle colliding with a Ti64 substrate, showing a straight-line path.
summary: This panel illustrates the trajectory of a PA powder particle as it moves toward a Ti64 substrate. The particle follows a distinct straight-line path during the collision process, demonstrating the characteristic flow behavior of PA powder under the specified experimental conditions without the laser being activated.

caption: Phase distribution map of S77 specimen under dynamic compressive loading at a strain rate of 2500/s, demonstrating the extent of martensitic transformation.
summary: This map displays the phase distribution of S77 subjected to dynamic compressive loading at a strain rate of 2500/s. The results reveal that the extent of martensitic transformation in the S77 sample follows a consistent trend under dynamic conditions, reflecting the material's microstructural evolution during high-rate deformation.

caption: Measured neutron diffraction patterns for the as-printed material, displaying black symbols for experimental data and a red line for the Rietveld refinement fit across a range of interplanar spacings.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for the as-printed material are presented, with black symbols representing measured data and a red line showing the Rietveld refinement fit. The analysis confirms that the material possesses a single body-centered cubic (BCC) martensitic structure, with several specific hkl planes identified within the diffraction range.

caption: Initial atomic configuration of Ni atoms at the crack tip for L1 and L2 regions at 2.5% strain, representing the onset of crack propagation at peak stress.
summary: Panel (b) captures the initial state of the crack tip at 2.5% strain, marking the onset of propagation. Ni atoms are visualized within the L1 and L2 sections, revealing closely spaced Ni atom clusters in L1, while Ni atoms in L2 appear more evenly dispersed at this peak stress condition.

caption: Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) results for the MnS phase.
summary: The EDS results for the MnS phase provide the elemental distribution required to confirm its identity. This spectroscopic data is used in conjunction with the IFFT image and SAD pattern to characterize the phase within the material microstructure.

caption: Microporous structure of PEEK specimens processed at different platform temperatures.
summary: This panel presents the 3D CT reconstruction of micropores in PEEK specimens influenced by platform temperature. While platform temperature affects both porosity and average pore size, the specific influence laws are less distinct compared to nozzle temperature and scanning speed, reflecting complex thermal effects on the final specimen microstructure.

caption: Training gradient progression for the ANN-BR model under the fourth parameter scenario, highlighting stable convergence and absence of validation errors.
summary: This panel illustrates the training performance for the fourth parameter scenario, where the gradient steadily decreases and stabilizes. Similar to the other scenarios, the model achieves effective convergence without any validation failures, confirming the reliability of the ANN-BR algorithm across the tested physical conditions.

caption: Atomic model illustrating slip deformation mechanisms along { 111 } planes in FCC Ni-based superalloys, showing dislocation shear directions for microtwinning, detwinning, and superlattice intrinsic stacking faults (SISF).
summary: This atomic model depicts deformation mechanisms in FCC Ni-based superalloys by sliding atomic layers along closed-packed slip directions. It illustrates octahedral slip via antiphase boundaries, microtwinning (SESFs) indicated by red arrows, and detwinning or SISF formation represented by green arrows, providing a fundamental basis for understanding dislocation-mediated plasticity.

caption: Transmittance spectra of RhB-HZ@CL demonstrating a progressive reduction in light transmission within the 500–600 nm wavelength range as the concentration of RhB-HZ increases.
summary: Transmittance spectra for RhB-HZ@CL reveal a concentration-dependent decrease in light transmission between 500 and 600 nm. The corresponding full-width at half-maximum values of 28.1, 31.3, and 51.1 nm quantify the spectral broadening observed as the concentration of the RhB-HZ component is systematically increased in the sample.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the HIP_Y specimen following Hot Isostatic Pressing.
summary: Post-HIP treatment, the L-DED_Y specimen exhibits a significant rearrangement of grain boundaries. This IPF map highlights the resulting grain polygonization and coarsening of the austenite grain sizes compared to the as-built state, demonstrating the structural evolution induced by the high-pressure and high-temperature processing conditions.

caption: Trapezoidal displacement-controlled loading path used for nanoindentation testing, illustrating the temporal evolution of displacement through loading, holding, and unloading phases.
summary: This plot displays the trapezoidal displacement history applied during nanoindentation tests. The loading path is defined by specific time intervals for loading, holding, and unloading phases. The model evaluates this perfectly trapezoidal load history, which includes a holding phase that begins precisely at 10 seconds to characterize material response.

caption: UV-Visible absorption spectra comparing the Schiff base ligand (SL) and the synthesized SL-NiNPs in DMSO solvent.
summary: UV-Visible absorption spectra comparing the Schiff base ligand (SL) and the synthesized SL-NiNPs in DMSO solvent. This spectral analysis is employed to validate the formation of the SL-NiNPs by comparing the optical characteristics of the ligand against the final nanoparticle product, illustrating the changes in absorption profiles upon nanoparticle synthesis.

caption: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra of the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam compared to Ni foil, demonstrating a near-zero valence state for Ni.
summary: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra for the synthesized foam are compared against Ni foil. The spectra exhibit a high degree of similarity, suggesting that the valence state of Ni in the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam is nearly zero, indicating a metallic character for the nickel species within the composite.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of CoCrFeNi alloy after heat treatment at 800 °C for 6 hours.
summary: The inverse pole figure map illustrates the grain microstructure of the CoCrFeNi alloy following a post-heat treatment at 800 °C for 6 hours. This visualization provides insight into the microstructural evolution and grain morphology changes occurring in the bulk alloy under these specific thermal processing conditions near the fracture zone.

caption: Hysteresis loops generated from loading–unloading–reloading (LUR) tests performed on Al–Si based HPDC alloys to evaluate mechanical behavior.
summary: Loading–unloading–reloading (LUR) tests were conducted on Al–Si based HPDC alloys to characterize their mechanical response. The resulting hysteresis loops, shown in this panel, provide the necessary data to evaluate the HDI stress and effective stress components within the material during the deformation process.

caption: De-convoluted high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectrum of the Cr 2p core level for FeCr2O4, with peaks at 583/588 eV and 572/578 eV confirming the coexistence of Cr3+ and Cr6+ states.
summary: The high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectrum of the Cr 2p core level reveals distinct peaks at 583 and 588 eV for Cr 2p 1/2 and 572 and 578 eV for Cr 2p 3/2. These results confirm the presence of both Cr3+ and Cr6+ oxidation states within the FeCr2O4 sample.

caption: KAM map of L-PBF HX specimen tested at 649 °C and 0.005 mm/mm strain amplitude.
summary: KAM mapping of the L-PBF HX specimen at 649 °C shows the plastic zone near the crack initiation site. At this elevated temperature, the difference in plastic wake size between L-PBF and LP-DED specimens becomes insignificant, likely due to the temperature promoting more extensive plastic deformation across both processes.

caption: Volumetric thermal strain ε plotted for Fe84, Fe78Ni6, and Fe78Co6 metallic glasses following annealing at 630 K, calculated based on the shifts in G(r) peak positions.
summary: Volumetric thermal strain ε is presented for Fe84, Fe78Ni6, and Fe78Co6 metallic glasses after annealing at 630 K. These strain values are determined by analyzing the shifts in G(r) peak positions, which were identified through Gaussian fitting, providing a quantitative measure of the structural changes induced by the thermal treatment process.

caption: Polar plot displaying the distribution of normalized elastic modulus ratios for modified honeycomb structures, highlighting the uniformity achieved via finite element analysis and experimental validation.
summary: This polar plot illustrates the distribution of normalized elastic modulus ratios for modified honeycomb structures. By comparing experimental and finite element analysis data, the plot demonstrates the improved uniformity of the mechanical response in the modified design, confirming that the structural modifications successfully mitigate the directional variation observed in conventional honeycombs.

caption: Detailed TEM micrograph of the sample aged at 540 °C, displaying the analyzed points with red arrows marking nanoparticles and red circles marking the matrix.
summary: This high-magnification TEM micrograph shows the microstructure of the sample aged at 540 °C. Red arrows indicate the presence of nanoparticles, and red circles delineate the matrix regions. These points were specifically analyzed to determine the chemical composition, providing data on the evolution of precipitates at this temperature.

caption: Power versus temperature plot for alloy 52 specimen, showing the Curie temperature marked at the average of the transition temperatures.
summary: The power versus temperature plot for the alloy 52 specimen is illustrated in Fig. 10(c). The Curie temperature is determined by averaging the two transition temperatures, and this specific value is marked on the plot to characterize the magnetic transition behavior of the alloy 52 material.

caption: Irreversible relative length changes (ΔL/L0) of as-printed AM HEA samples during heating at 5 K/min, comparing the first heating cycle (thick solid lines) against reference signals derived from the difference between the second and third heating cycles for both TD and BD orientations.
summary: Dilatometry measurements show the relative length changes of AM HEA samples upon heating to 873 K. The irreversible elongation observed in the first heating cycle is compared against reference curves, which demonstrate high reproducibility across independent measurements, confirming the validity of the thermal expansion data for both sample orientations.

caption: KAM map of Ti5553 deformed at a strain rate of 1300 s-1, displaying a broader distribution of elevated misorientation regions.
summary: Increasing the strain rate to 1300 s-1 leads to a more widespread distribution of elevated KAM regions throughout the Ti5553 microstructure. This broader spatial extent of higher misorientation values indicates an enhanced accumulation of geometrically necessary dislocations as the intensity of the dynamic impact loading increases.

caption: Individual radar plots displaying raw performance values for compressive strength, flexural strength, and yield stress, confirming that Kaolinite-based mixes achieve compressive strengths up to 49 MPa and flexural strengths exceeding 5 MPa.
summary: Individual radar plots present the raw mechanical data for the LC 3 composite mixes. These plots confirm the superior performance of Kaolinite-based composites, which reach compressive strengths of 49 MPa and flexural strengths greater than 5 MPa, validating the trends observed in the normalized comparison of the composite materials.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the as-built SLM specimen showing a cellular microstructure with an average cell diameter of approximately 500 nm.
summary: This TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the as-built SLM specimen. The material exhibits a distinct cellular morphology characterized by an average cell diameter of approximately 500 nm. This image serves as the baseline structural reference for comparing the effects of subsequent heat treatments on the specimen's cellular features.

caption: Vickers microhardness values plotted against aging temperature for samples subjected to a 100-hour isochronal aging treatment.
summary: This plot illustrates the influence of aging temperature on the microhardness of the material after 100 hours of treatment. The data reveals a peak hardness value of 722 ± 12 HV achieved at 600 °C, which serves as the optimal condition for subsequent experimental investigations into the material's mechanical properties.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for intragranular austenite-ferrite interfaces categorized as 'Others' orientation relationships, plotted in the austenite crystal lattice frame.
summary: Shown is the habit plane distribution for intragranular austenite-ferrite interfaces classified as 'Others' orientation relationships. The intensity is notably lower, at approximately 1.35 MRD, compared to the K-S/N-W categories. Mapped in the austenite lattice frame, these interfaces exhibit an inverse correlation between their curvature and the habit plane distribution intensity.

caption: Dislocation nucleation at 10,000 simulation steps in the trace B2 phase alloy, showing dislocations forming around B2 particles with initial parallel alignment.
summary: At 10,000 simulation steps, this MD snapshot captures the nucleation of dislocations around the B2 phase particles in the trace B2 phase alloy. The visualization highlights the early stages of deformation where dislocations begin to emerge and exhibit a tendency to align parallel to one another within the matrix.

caption: Overall perspective views of the longitudinal residual stress distribution within the non-symmetrical interweaving layers of the Ti6Al4V/AA2024 alloy component.
summary: This panel presents the overall longitudinal residual stress distribution of the Ti6Al4V/AA2024 alloy component from two distinct perspectives. Due to the non-symmetrical material combination of the interweaving layers, these views provide a comprehensive observation of the stress state outside the deposited layers, highlighting the complex mechanical behavior of the interface.

caption: Two-dimensional schematic illustrating the experimental geometry for CBED and EDX measurements on a thin foil specimen prepared via FIB.
summary: This schematic depicts the experimental setup for acquiring CBED patterns and EDX spectra from a thin foil sample. It highlights the potential for experimental error due to the different tilt angles required for each measurement, specifically 0 degrees for CBED and 20 degrees for EDX acquisition.

caption: Optical micrograph of the side heat-affected zone in the 304 stainless steel additive manufacturing component, representing sample #3.
summary: This optical micrograph captures the side heat-affected zone of a 304 stainless steel additive manufacturing component, designated as sample #3. Examination of the interface between the additive manufacturing component and the weld shows no significant heat-affected zone, consistent with the overall structural observations of the component's interface regions.

caption: 3D surface morphology of the MPA-250 object following exposure to a 10^6 Gy gamma-radiation dosage.
summary: Post-radiation 3D surface morphology of the MPA-250 object is shown here, revealing a significant increase in surface roughness. Exposure to 10^6 Gy of gamma-radiation nearly doubles the root-mean-square roughness (Rq) of the sample, which increases from the initial 156±28 nm to a final value of 378±6 nm.

caption: Neutron diffraction WPPM fit results for the S-5 specimen, featuring experimental data points, the fitted profile, and the residual plot shown on a logarithmic intensity scale.
summary: The S-5 specimen is characterized via neutron diffraction, with the WPPM model fitted to the experimental data. The resulting profile is overlaid on the black experimental dots, and the fit residual is reported above the pattern. The intensity axis is logarithmic, facilitating the extraction of refined microstructural parameters.

caption: Confocal laser microscopy images of BMSCs stained for live/dead viability assessment to evaluate in vitro biosafety.
summary: Confocal laser microscopy is utilized to assess the biosafety of the material by observing BMSC viability. The imaging results confirm that the survival and growth rates of BMSCs treated with ABOHA@ZnO hydrogel microspheres are comparable to other groups, indicating no systemic toxicity and confirming the material's safety for bone applications.

caption: Live/Dead fluorescence visualization of gyroid design scaffolds, displaying the viability of hMSCs maintained over the 7-day observation window.
summary: Live/Dead fluorescence visualization of gyroid design scaffolds displays the viability of hMSCs maintained over the 7-day observation window. The analysis qualitatively confirms a high proportion of viable cells and minimal cell death, indicating that the scaffold supports statistically significant cell growth for potential bone implant applications.

caption: Secondary electron micrograph of RRAlH alloy following ageing at 900 °C for 1.5 h.
summary: Secondary electron micrograph of RRAlH alloy following ageing at 900 °C for 1.5 h. This SEM image displays the microstructure of the RRAlH alloy after the 900 °C ageing treatment, facilitating an evaluation of the material's structural evolution under high-temperature conditions relative to the 750 °C aged state.

caption: Cyclic stress response of the material under symmetric (R = -1) loading conditions at 350 °C.
summary: This panel displays the cyclic stress response of the material subjected to symmetric loading at 350 °C. The plot illustrates the evolution of stress over cycles, providing insight into the material's cyclic behavior and hardening characteristics under these specific test conditions, which are essential for evaluating dynamic strain aging activity.

caption: Charging curve of a capacitor powered by the S2 structure over a duration of 250 seconds.
summary: This curve tracks the voltage accumulation in a capacitor charged by the S2 structure over a 250-second interval. The data confirms the capability of the bio-inspired piezoelectric harvester to effectively store energy, demonstrating its practical utility in powering electronic components.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of an SSCC device produced by industrial 3-D resin printing, showing 0.1 mm high features and prominent layer lines.
summary: Industrial 3-D resin printing of SSCC devices results in visible layer lines and less reliable channel formation between grids compared to photolithography. Although the surface detail remains relatively smooth, the structural integrity of the channels is compromised, as evidenced by this SEM analysis of the 0.1 mm high features.

caption: Cooling scans of DSC curves for extruded filaments and printed PEEK composites, highlighting a crystallization temperature (Tc) increment of up to 8 °C for printed composites compared to neat PEEK.
summary: Cooling scans of DSC curves are presented for extruded filaments and printed PEEK composites. A significant finding is the noteworthy increment of the crystallization temperature (Tc) observed for printed composites, which increases by up to 8 °C compared to printed neat PEEK, indicating altered crystallization kinetics in the composites.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the cathodic and anodic branches of AB, T5, and T6 samples, highlighting variations in electrochemical stability.
summary: PDP curves reveal that AB and T5 samples exhibit a higher degree of linearity in their cathodic and anodic branches. In contrast, the T6 samples display fluctuations in both regions, indicating a less stable electrochemical behavior compared to the other conditions before machining.

caption: Ashby chart illustrating the relationship between compressive strength and density for printed trabecular architectures (L3, L6, L10) compared against various commercial core structures.
summary: This Ashby chart benchmarks the mechanical performance of printed trabecular architectures, specifically variants L3, L6, and L10, against standard commercial core materials. By plotting compressive strength versus density, the figure validates the structural efficiency of these printed designs, providing a comparative overview of their mechanical properties relative to existing industrial alternatives.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) evolution over time for AA2060-T8 alloys electrografted at pH 3, 4, 5, and 6 compared to a bare alloy control in 0.1 M NaCl.
summary: The OCP evolution over time for AA2060-T8 specimens electrografted at pH values of 3, 4, 5, and 6 is shown in 0.1 M NaCl. These specimens exhibit relatively similar OCP values between -0.55 and -0.65 V, which are significantly more positive than the -0.95 V observed for the bare alloy control.

caption: Pole figure (PF) of the HWF deposit, showing the texture misorientation characteristics.
