The intersecting morphology of these plates, observed near the beta-Ti matrix and unmelted Nb particle interfaces, suggests a mechanism for enhanced strengthening during plastic deformation, consistent with the BCC to orthorhombic martensitic phase transformation.

caption: 13C CP-MAS NMR spectrum of the PET oligomer, showing characteristic intensity peaks for aromatic carbons between 125–135 ppm and the carbonyl region at 160–165 ppm.
summary: This 13C CP-MAS NMR spectrum characterizes the PET oligomer by identifying specific chemical environments. The data shows concentrated signal intensity corresponding to aromatic carbons in the 125–135 ppm range, alongside a distinct carbonyl region located between 160–165 ppm, providing a baseline for the material's chemical composition.

caption: Room temperature magnetization versus magnetic field hysteresis loop for Ni x Co 1−x powders.
summary: This panel displays the room temperature magnetic field dependence of magnetization for Ni x Co 1−x powders. The hysteresis loop illustrates the magnetic response of the powder samples under an applied field, providing essential data on the magnetic behavior of the material composition at room temperature.

caption: Methodological flowchart detailing the data preparation and training strategy for the Bayesian LSTM model, utilizing high-fidelity simulation data generated via Monte Carlo Markov Chain and Latin Hypercube Sampling.
summary: The training methodology for the Bayesian LSTM model is outlined in this flowchart. It relies on high-fidelity simulation data produced through Monte Carlo Markov Chain and Latin Hypercube Sampling techniques, which generate a comprehensive set of laser power sequences to train the predictive model effectively.

caption: Principal curvature map of the Primitive stochastic TPMS surface with a characteristic length of 5 mm.
summary: The Primitive stochastic TPMS surface is shown with its principal curvature map at a 5 mm characteristic length. The minimal surface character of this topology is verified by the mean curvature remaining near zero, confirming the structural integrity of the designed stochastic TPMS.

caption: HexC lattice structure assembly in a 4x4x4 configuration.
summary: The HexC lattice structure is presented as a 4x4x4 assembly. This visualization highlights the geometric arrangement and periodic unit cell repetition of the HexC design, offering a detailed view of its structural configuration within the specified lattice dimensions as outlined in the research findings.

caption: Instantaneous pressure profile across the spatial domain x ∈ [0,10] at a normalized time t / t f ≈ 0.61.
summary: Representing the pressure state at a normalized time of approximately 0.61, this plot illustrates the spatial variation over the interval x ∈ [0,10]. Similar to other snapshots, the visible step-like features in the pressure curve are confirmed to be artifacts caused by floating-point precision constraints during the post-processing stage.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the phase composition of 15CrMo alloy and laser-clad Inconel 625 coating after 1000 hours of exposure to supercritical CO2.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for both 15CrMo alloy and laser-clad Inconel 625 coating samples. These materials were subjected to a 1000-hour exposure test in a supercritical CO2 environment. The patterns provide a comparative analysis of the resulting phase compositions following this long-term high-pressure gas exposure.

caption: Yield strength values for T6-treated Al-Si-Mg-Cu and Al-Si-Mg-Cu-Ni alloys measured at room temperature, 200, 250, 300, and 350 °C.
summary: Yield strength measurements for T6-treated Al-Si-Mg-Cu and Al-Si-Mg-Cu-Ni alloys are presented across five distinct temperature points up to 350 °C. The results demonstrate a clear trend where the yield strength of the alloys diminishes with increasing testing temperature, consistent with the observed reduction in overall mechanical strength at elevated temperatures.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results identifying the elemental composition of the precipitates, which contain Nb, Cr, Fe, and Mo, confirming their identification as Laves phase.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the precipitates reveals a composition dominated by Nb, Cr, Fe, and Mo. Based on these elemental results and relevant literature, the second-phase particles are identified as Laves phase, providing critical insight into the microstructural evolution of the repaired zone after 8 hours of aging.

caption: Factor information table detailing the parameters used in the regression analysis for 3D printing roughness.
summary: This table presents the factor information utilized in the regression analysis to evaluate the impact of parameter settings on the surface roughness of 3D printed components. It serves as the foundational dataset for the subsequent statistical modeling and analysis of variance performed to optimize the printing process.

caption: Hardness distribution box plot for varying V elemental content.
summary: Hardness distribution for varying V content is illustrated in this box plot. As V content increases from low to high ranges, the centerline of the distribution rises significantly, indicating a clear upward trend in the hardness of the alloy with increasing V concentration.

caption: Raman spectroscopy profiles for the synthesized catalysts, highlighting the degree of graphitization via the I_G/I_D ratio.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the catalysts is shown, with the Fe/Ni/N-CNT sample exhibiting a higher I_G/I_D ratio compared to the others. This result indicates a greater degree of graphitization in the Fe/Ni/N-CNT catalyst, reflecting the structural impact of incorporating both Fe and Ni into the N-CNT framework.

caption: Feature importance analysis focusing on the dynamic mechanical performance of Primitive TPMS architectures with a slenderness ratio L/h = 8.
summary: This feature importance plot isolates the Primitive TPMS architecture, evaluating the factors that drive its dynamic mechanical performance at a slenderness ratio of L/h = 8. The visualization provides a targeted analysis of the specific structural features that govern the mechanical response of this particular triply periodic minimal surface design.

caption: Schematic representation of the experimental setup utilizing argon gas as both carrier and protection gas.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental configuration employed for the process. Argon gas serves dual roles, functioning as the carrier gas at a volumetric flow rate of 10 l/min and as the protection gas at a volumetric flow rate of 25 l/min, ensuring controlled atmospheric conditions during the procedure.

caption: Magnified SEM micrograph of the wear scar at 37 °C highlighting surface irregularities.
summary: Magnified SEM imaging of the wear scar at 37 °C reveals horizontal striations similar to those observed at lower temperatures. However, this view also highlights additional surface irregularities, including pits, plastic deformation, and ridges, indicating a more complex degradation profile under the elevated temperature conditions of the tribological test.

caption: Temporal evolution of Frenkel defect pairs in pure Cu (Cu-0at%Ni) under varying PKA energy irradiation at 300 K.
summary: This panel illustrates the temporal evolution of Frenkel defect pairs in pure Cu under different PKA energy irradiation at 300 K. The data tracks the accumulation and stabilization of defects over time, providing a baseline for understanding radiation damage kinetics in the Cu-Ni alloy system under specific energy conditions.

caption: Viscosity as a function of shear rate for suspensions prepared with different particle sizes.
summary: The graph illustrates the rheological behavior of suspensions by plotting viscosity against shear rate for varying particle sizes. These curves demonstrate that the viscosity remains below 25 Pa s at a shear rate of 0.01 s⁻¹, which is a critical requirement for maintaining printability and achieving high-resolution green parts.

caption: Unit cell representation of the face-centered cubic (fcc) Ni crystal structure.
summary: The unit cell of fcc Ni is illustrated with a lattice constant of aNi = 3.52 Å. This structure serves as the base material for the Ni layers in the composite simulation models. The orientation relationship is defined such that the Cartesian axes align with the [100], [010], and [001] crystallographic directions.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectrum of PCN-224, showing a band gap energy of 1.38 eV derived from Tauc plot analysis.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectrum of the PCN-224 material is presented. Tauc plot analysis of this spectral data reveals a band gap energy of 1.38 eV for the PCN-224 sample, providing fundamental electronic information regarding its light absorption characteristics and potential for photocatalytic or sensing applications.

caption: Detailed STEM view of the conventional material after ER cycling at 0.4% strain amplitude and 7001 cycles, focusing on γ'' precipitate morphology.
summary: Detailed STEM view of the conventional material after ER cycling at 0.4% strain amplitude and 7001 cycles, focusing on γ'' precipitate morphology. The observation shows that the general morphology of the γ'' precipitates remains very similar to the initial state, indicating stability despite the applied mechanical fatigue cycling.

caption: Three-dimensional graph depicting the relationship between LPCS process variables and the resulting coating adhesion strength.
summary: This 3D graph illustrates the complex interplay between LPCS process variables and the resulting coating adhesion strength. It serves to visualize the experimental data, confirming that the gas temperature at the nozzle inlet is the most critical factor influencing the adhesion strength of the Ni + Al2O3 coating.

caption: Enthalpy of mixing for the Cu-Zr binary system at 1873 K, comparing WAFW potential simulations against experimental reference data from Turchanin, with an inset highlighting the low Zr concentration range (0-20 at.%).
summary: This plot illustrates the enthalpy of mixing for the Cu-Zr system at 1873 K. The WAFW potential successfully reproduces the experimental trends reported by Turchanin. An inset provides a detailed view of the 0 to 20 at.% Zr range, confirming the potential's accuracy in capturing concentration-dependent thermodynamic variations.

caption: Dark-field TEM image illustrating the interface region within the interlayer between Ti-6Al-4V alloy and pure Cu.
summary: This dark-field TEM image provides a detailed visualization of the interface region located within the interlayer. The micrograph serves as a foundational view for identifying structural features and phase distribution at the junction between the Ti-6Al-4V alloy and pure Cu, facilitating further magnified analysis of the reaction layer.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction of the Base alloy in the T5 condition, illustrating the spatial distribution of solute atoms and precipitates.
summary: This three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the representative data volume for the Base alloy in the T5 condition. The visualization provides a comprehensive view of the internal microstructure, serving as the foundational dataset for identifying specific particle populations and their associated chemical compositions within the alloy matrix.

caption: Relative intensity evolution of γ-f.c.c. peaks for iHEA-0.5Nb during cooling from the liquid phase, demonstrating altered peak intensity behavior compared to the base iHEA alloy.
summary: Incorporating 0.5Nb into the iHEA alloy significantly alters the solidification behavior observed during cooling from the liquid phase. The synchrotron X-ray diffraction analysis shows that the relative intensity evolution of the γ-f.c.c. peaks deviates from the base iHEA composition, indicating a shift in the solidification pathway driven by Nb addition.

caption: Real (Z’) and imaginary (-Z”) impedance components for Li-poor β-LiAl plotted against ω −1/2 at room temperature.
summary: This plot displays the real and imaginary parts of the complex impedance for Li-poor β-LiAl at room temperature. The data demonstrate that both impedance components are proportional to the inverse square root of frequency, consistent with the expected electrochemical behavior for this material phase under the specified test conditions.

caption: Precision-Recall (PR) curve for the RF model without missing values, showing trade-offs between precision and recall.
summary: The PR curve evaluates the model's classification capability by plotting precision against recall. Achieving AUC values of 0.95, 0.93, and 0.89 for FCC, BCC, and FCC+BCC phases respectively, the model demonstrates excellent classification performance. These metrics confirm the model's robustness, effectively compensating for limitations inherent in evaluating precision or recall individually.

caption: Continuous-Cooling-Transformation (CCT) diagram for EQ2.30 steel at 1% phase transformation, showing the sensitivity of cooling-dependent phase evolution to interfacial energy parameters.
summary: This CCT diagram for EQ2.30 steel at 1% phase transformation highlights the sensitivity of cooling-dependent phase evolution to interfacial energy. Variations in interfacial energy lead to significant changes in the CCT curves, reflecting the underlying impact of these energy parameters on the nucleation rate and final transformed phase volume fraction.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram illustrating the eutectoid decomposition kinetics of the solution nitrided alloy, highlighting the instability of austenite below 775 °C.
summary: The TTT diagram characterizes the eutectoid decomposition of the solution nitrided alloy. It provides a visual representation of the phase transformation kinetics, confirming that austenite is no longer stable at temperatures below 775 °C, which aligns with the experimental observations of the transformation behavior in the alloy.

caption: Average absorbed energy values obtained from Charpy impact tests conducted at 500 °C for conditions A–D of both alloys.
summary: Charpy impact test results at 500 °C are presented for four conditions (A-D) of two alloys. The data illustrates how elevated temperature affects the absorbed energy compared to room temperature. These measurements are critical for assessing the mechanical performance and impact resistance of the alloys under moderate thermal exposure.

caption: Dynamic tension specimen geometry for Split-Hopkinson Tension Bar (SHTB) testing, designed as a dog-bone shape with M8 threads.
summary: This panel displays the dog-bone specimen geometry with M8 threads specifically utilized for dynamic tension tests via the SHTB method. These specimens are part of a comprehensive experimental suite designed to assess material performance, accounting for build orientation and material processing parameters across multiple testing configurations.

caption: Generalized stacking fault energy curve illustrating unstable stacking fault energy and stacking fault energy, with insets showing atomic configurations colored by structure type.
summary: This generalized stacking fault energy curve displays the unstable stacking fault energy and stacking fault energy, calculated based on the lattice parameter for each composition. Atomic configurations in the insets are colored by structure type, where green represents FCC, red represents HCP, and gray represents unknown structural arrangements.

caption: Two-dimensional slice of the WAAM-T6 Al-Li alloy specimen showing advanced crack growth and fracture at 4.26% strain.
summary: At 4.26% strain, the 2D slice captures the final stages of crack growth leading to specimen fracture. The interaction between near-surface crack sources and internal microporosity, which acts as a medium for expansion, ultimately results in the failure of the WAAM-T6 Al-Li alloy under the applied tensile stress.

caption: Atom probe tomography map of Hf atoms featuring a cylindrical analysis region with a diameter of 15 nm and a length of 135 nm, oriented perpendicular to the secondary γ′-γ interface.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the spatial distribution of Hf atoms within a defined cylindrical volume. The analysis region, measuring 15 nm in diameter and 135 nm in length, is positioned perpendicular to the secondary γ′-γ interface to facilitate a detailed examination of the atomic distribution profile at significant distances.

caption: Vickers hardness profile measured along the building direction at the middle region of the 304 SS specimen.
summary: Vickers hardness values for the CMT-WAAM 304 SS sample are presented for the middle region. A minor deviation of approximately ±10 HV is observed in this section. The fluctuation in hardness is attributed to layer stacking and thermal cyclic heating, which cause hardening and softening of adjacent layers.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to extracts from SLM-processed Ti.
summary: Human Gingival Fibroblasts incubated for 24 hours with extracts from SLM-processed Ti are shown via fluorescence microscopy. The Live/Dead staining method differentiates between live (green) and dead (red) cells, facilitating an analysis of the cellular response and viability when exposed to the SLM-processed titanium extract.

caption: Partial Li-Al phase diagram aligned with the discharge profile to correlate capacity with the formation of specific Li-Al phases.
summary: The partial Li-Al phase diagram is presented alongside the galvanostatic discharge profile to clarify the relationship between capacity and phase formation. A notable mismatch in the β-LiAl solubility range between the experimental data and the phase diagram suggests localized nucleation of Li3Al2 occurs before full saturation of the β-LiAl phase.

caption: Cooling DSC thermograms illustrating the thermal behavior of 3D-printed CFRP specimens, highlighting differences between thermally treated and non-treated groups.
summary: Cooling cycle DSC curves are presented for both thermally treated and non-treated 3D-printed CFRP specimens. These plots characterize the exothermic behavior during the cooling phase, allowing for a direct comparison of how thermal treatment history influences the crystallization or solidification kinetics of the polymer matrix within the composite.

caption: Vacancy formation energies for the disordered Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy structure generated via MC simulations at 2000 K, showing significantly lower values compared to the 300 K ordered structure.
summary: Vacancy formation energies for the disordered Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy structure generated via MC simulations at 2000 K are presented. These values are significantly smaller than those obtained for the 300 K structure, highlighting the impact of structural order and temperature on the energetic stability of vacancies within the alloy system.

caption: Radar chart displaying the performance scorecards for grade 23 Ti-6Al-4V powders, evaluating virgin versus carbon-blended samples based on seven distinct powder property assessments.
summary: Performance scorecards for grade 23 Ti-6Al-4V powders are presented, contrasting virgin and carbon-blended materials. The radar chart visualizes qualitative and quantitative data, including bulk flow, cohesion, and dynamic flow properties. These metrics are averaged to determine the best overall powder quality for use in LPBF part printing processes.

caption: Normalized Cu K-edge XANES spectra for Ni 0.001 Cu NPs, Ni 0.01 Cu NPs, Cu NPs, and Cu foil standard, all measured after in-situ reduction at 350 °C.
summary: Normalized Cu K-edge XANES spectra are presented for Ni-doped Cu nanoparticles and pure Cu nanoparticles compared to a Cu foil standard. These spectra confirm that the Cu species in all nanoparticle samples exist in a metallic state following the in-situ reduction process performed at 350 °C for 1 hour.

caption: ODF section at phi2 = 0° representing the fcc orientations derived from the (223)[1-10] alpha' precursor.
summary: This panel illustrates the fcc orientations at phi2 = 0° resulting from the transformation of the (223)[1-10] alpha' orientation. The formation of the G gamma orientation is driven by the selection of variants V5, V6, V8, V9, and V12, confirming the specific crystallographic path taken during the reverse transformation process.

caption: Thermal expansion coefficients of the γ and γ' phases as a function of temperature, illustrating the contrasting expansion behaviors of the two phases.
summary: This panel presents the thermal expansion coefficients for both γ and γ' phases derived from MD simulations. The results demonstrate that lattice constants for both phases increase with rising temperature, driven by enhanced atomic thermal vibrations. These contrasting thermal expansion behaviors are fundamental to the observed systematic decrease in lattice misfit.

caption: M-H curves for the 4Co sample, illustrating the magnetic response under pulsed fields at various temperatures from 4.2 to 280 K.
summary: For the 4Co sample, M-H curves are presented across a temperature range of 4.2 to 280 K using pulsed magnetic fields. The data highlights the magnetic behavior associated with the martensitic transformation, driven by the presence of both ferromagnetic P and weakly magnetic M phases in the material.

caption: Crystal orientation map of forged Ti–25Cu, demonstrating the fragmentation of the coarse interconnected proeutectoid phase due to plastic deformation.
summary: The IPF map for the forged Ti–25Cu alloy reveals the impact of plastic deformation on the microstructure. The analysis shows that the forging process successfully fragmented the coarse, interconnected proeutectoid phase, resulting in a refined structural morphology compared to the as-cast state, as evidenced by the orientation distribution.

caption: SHAP interaction plot for the twisted angle parameter, highlighting the range of values where negative contributions to radius error occur.
summary: This SHAP interaction plot visualizes the influence of the twisted angle on radius error. The data indicates that SHAP values predominantly fall within the negative range when the twisted angle is between 5° and 12°, demonstrating the specific impact of yarn twist on the printing accuracy of the CCFRP.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure map of the δ-ferrite matrix phase in the Ar P sample.
summary: This Inverse Pole Figure map displays the δ-ferrite matrix phase within the Ar P sample. As the primary constituent, the δ-ferrite structure is clearly visualized, providing insight into the crystallographic orientation and distribution of the matrix phase under the specified Ar P processing condition.

caption: Hardness and elastic modulus of the DLC topcoat plotted against indenter penetration depth, derived from instrumented indentation tests performed at varying peak loads.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of the DLC topcoat through instrumented indentation tests. Hardness and elastic modulus values are presented as functions of indenter penetration depth across different peak loads. These values reflect the combined properties of the outer C-rich layer and the underlying Cr-W bond layer.

caption: Average temperature history of the representative volume element (RVE) during a solid-state thermal cycle, showing a rapid linear temperature increase at 5 × 10^5 K s^-1 followed by an exponential decay back to room temperature.
summary: This plot illustrates the nonlinear temperature evolution within the polycrystal during a solid-state thermal cycle. The RVE experiences a rapid linear heating rate of 5 × 10^5 K s^-1 to a peak of 750 K, followed by an exponential cooling phase, effectively capturing the two primary stages of the thermal cycle.

caption: Identification of the crack initiation point for specimen A2 using the second derivative of AE counts, where the red arrow marks the onset of crack extension occurring before 400 s.
summary: The crack initiation point for specimen A2 is identified through the second derivative approach applied to the AE count data. This analytical method successfully pinpoints the onset of crack extension, which is observed to occur before the 400 s mark during the fracture toughness test, as indicated by the red arrow.

caption: Succession of binary phase diagrams for the Cu-Ni-Cr-Mo-W multi-principal element alloy system, illustrating the thermodynamic relationships between constituent elements.
summary: This figure presents a series of binary phase diagrams for the Cu-Ni-Cr-Mo-W alloy system, sourced from the ASM database. These diagrams highlight the miscibility of Mo with Cr and W, supporting the strategic inclusion of Mo to mitigate Cr vaporization risks during the transition to W in the MMCI material.

caption: High-magnification TEM view of the coating revealing 20–80 nm grains, including an HRTEM inset of the yellow-boxed area and a reconstructed FFT pattern from a single 2/1AC grain.
summary: High-magnification TEM imaging reveals that the coating consists of grains ranging from 20 nm to 80 nm in size. The HRTEM inset of the yellow-boxed area displays two neighboring 2/1AC phase crystallites with distinct orientations. A reconstructed FFT pattern from a single 2/1AC grain is also provided for structural analysis.

caption: Thermographic measurement results for the second specimen design of layer 1380, highlighting the thermal profile observed during the EOS M400-1 manufacturing job.
summary: Representing the second specimen design, this panel shows the thermographic results for layer 1380. The heatmap captures the thermal profile during the EOS M400-1 build job, allowing for a direct comparison of thermal behavior between the second design and the other specimens evaluated within the experimental framework of the study.

caption: Raman spectrum of Python Flex TPU produced by FFF, showing the fingerprinting region and the high-frequency peak observed at 2880–2900 cm⁻¹.
summary: Python Flex TPU, manufactured via FFF, displays a Raman spectrum centered on the fingerprinting region. The data reveals a distinct high-frequency peak in the 2880 cm⁻¹ to 2900 cm⁻¹ range, aligning with the spectral signatures typically observed in rubbers and polyester-based materials, confirming the consistency of the analysis.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of U2OS cell spheroids on β-TCP scaffolds at day 7, stained with Calcein AM, illustrating central arrangement and partial surface coverage.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy of U2OS cell spheroids on β-TCP scaffolds at the 7-day time point demonstrates that cells are primarily arranged in the center of the scaffold. The spheroids partially cover the scaffold surface and are supported by collagen or extracellular matrix, highlighting distinct spatial organization compared to hBMSCs.

caption: Corner crack specimen geometry utilized for isothermal force-controlled crack growth testing, highlighting the gauge section and the plane of symmetry.
summary: The corner crack specimen geometry is illustrated, showing the gauge section designed for isothermal force-controlled crack growth tests. A half-model approach is employed to exploit the plane of symmetry running parallel to the crack plane, facilitating accurate experimental data collection under controlled loading conditions for the crack growth analysis.

caption: Mixing enthalpy at 0 K for configurations in an fcc lattice, showing the agreement between DFT-calculated data (open symbols) and CE-predicted values (solid symbols).
summary: Configurational mixing enthalpy at 0 K for an fcc lattice is presented here. The plot contrasts DFT-calculated results, marked with open symbols, with CE-predicted values indicated by solid symbols. This comparison highlights the effectiveness of the cluster expansion method in modeling the energetic landscape of fcc-based alloy configurations.

caption: B-scan elastogram of the MAS4 phantom at -0.2 pre-strain, revealing spatial variations in modulus.
summary: At -0.2 pre-strain, the MAS4 phantom shows significant contact, yet spatial variations in the tangent modulus are clearly visible. This B-scan elastogram demonstrates how local regions of the sample experience different levels of compression due to the variable surface height, complicating the interpretation of the mechanical data.

caption: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 HT2 (red) and A2 HT2 (green) samples measured at 423 K, illustrating the overall diffraction profiles.
summary: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 HT2 and A2 HT2 samples are presented at 423 K. These profiles demonstrate the structural characteristics of the alloys under identical heat treatment conditions. The data provides a comprehensive view of the diffraction patterns, serving as the basis for comparing the crystalline structures of the two distinct compositions.

caption: Electrical conductivity of the TiB2/Cu composite, showing a significant increase from 19.4 % IACS to 80.8 % IACS following the sintering process.
summary: Electrical conductivity measurements demonstrate a substantial improvement from 19.4 ± 0.1 % IACS in the as-fabricated state to 80.8 ± 0.4 % IACS after sintering. This increase is attributed to the in-situ reaction of Cu4Ti and B, which effectively enhances the conductive properties of the TiB2/Cu composite material.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction and 1D composition profile across the cell boundary for LPBF 316L stainless steel processed with low power and low scan speed (LP&LS).
summary: Shown here is the APT reconstruction and 1D composition profile for 316L stainless steel produced by LPBF under low power and low scan speed conditions. The data corroborates the segregation of Cr, Ni, Mo, and Si at cell boundaries, supporting the broader analysis of segregation behavior in LPBF-processed materials.

caption: Wavelength shift analysis of the TC film upon exposure to acetone, showing a distinct red shift in the absorption signal.
summary: This graph quantifies the red shift of absorption signals from 308 nm to 316 nm upon acetone binding. This shift is driven by charge transfer effects, surface plasmon resonance changes, and structural distortions that lead to bandgap modification, confirming the sensitivity of the 2D chromite material to acetone.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map corresponding to the Long-Short vector strategy, highlighting grain structures with typical grains marked by black rectangles.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the Long-Short vector strategy illustrates the grain structure in the XZ plane. Typical grains are highlighted by black rectangles to emphasize the microstructural features. This map provides a detailed view of the orientation distribution resulting from the alternating vector length strategy.

caption: Linear frequency initialization of 18 Morlet filters illustrating the starting magnitude responses before training.
summary: Linear frequency initialization of 18 Morlet filters illustrates the starting magnitude responses before training begins. Although the initial frequency distribution is distinct, the learned filter responses after 100 training epochs converge to comparable frequency allocations, indicating that the model effectively adapts to reach a consistent state from this linear starting point.

caption: Stability curve of the monolithic perovskite/Si/Ni foil/NiFe photoanode integrated with Ni nanowire cathode, showing current density over 45 hours of operation.
summary: The overall water splitting system maintains a stable current density of 12.3 mA cm-2 at 0 V for approximately 45 hours. This stability test, conducted under both continuous and chopped illumination, confirms the long-term durability and operational reliability of the integrated photoanode and cathode configuration.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the SMATed part, showing altered crystallographic orientations extending to a depth of 200 μm.
summary: Following SMAT processing, the inverse pole figure map reveals that the crystallographic orientation of grains has been significantly altered to a depth of 200 μm. Although the gradient-structured surface layer is difficult to observe, the map confirms that the SMAT process effectively modifies the grain orientation throughout the affected zone.

caption: Ni 2p XPS spectrum of a freshly prepared CoNi deposit, showing a primary metallic nickel peak centered at 852.8 eV.
summary: The Ni 2p XPS spectrum for the freshly prepared CoNi deposit displays a characteristic metallic nickel peak at 852.8 eV. This spectral feature confirms the presence of nickel in its metallic state within the as-prepared sample, serving as a baseline for comparison with post-service samples.

caption: Comparative compressive stress-strain curves for AISI M2 tool steel across all cooling conditions.
summary: This combined graph overlays the compressive stress-strain curves for furnace-cooled, air-cooled, and water-cooled AISI M2 tool steel. Analysis reveals that furnace-cooled samples demonstrate approximately 1.5 to 2 times greater ductility compared to the air-cooled and water-cooled specimens, highlighting the significant impact of cooling rates on mechanical properties.

caption: Minimal energy path for oxygen diffusion in a bcc molybdenum lattice containing a nitrogen interstitial, determined by NEB calculations.
summary: This panel displays the minimal energy path for oxygen diffusion in a bcc molybdenum lattice modified by the presence of a nitrogen interstitial. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal how the nitrogen atom influences the oxygen migration barrier, demonstrating the impact of interstitial interactions on the diffusion kinetics within the molybdenum matrix.

caption: Normal map of the powder bed surface, serving as the foreground layer for image synthesis.
summary: Representing the normal map of the powder bed, this panel acts as the foreground component in the synthesis process. By capturing surface orientation data, it complements the depth difference map to facilitate the creation of a realistic synthesized image of the powder bed surface.

caption: Finite element mesh distribution and geometric configuration of the plate segments used for numerical simulations.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometric configuration and finite element mesh distribution employed for numerical simulations. Each plate is divided into three distinct segments to optimize mesh density, transitioning from a fine mesh within the fusion zone to a coarser mesh in the base metal region to enhance computational accuracy.

caption: Discharge potential curves at the maximum discharge capacity for the three alloy electrodes, highlighting the presence of wide and flat discharge plateaus.
summary: Discharge potential curves for the La3MgNi14, La2.5Y0.5MgNi14, and La2YMgNi14 electrodes are shown at their maximum discharge capacity. All three electrodes exhibit a wide and flat discharge plateau, indicating stable electrochemical potential characteristics during the discharge process for these specific alloy compositions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images comparing cell adhesion of hMSCs and hDFs on sandblasted DMLS 3D-printed Ti-64 alloy versus machine-cut control samples.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images demonstrate the biological performance of DMLS 3D-printed Ti-64 alloy after sandblasting. By comparing hMSCs and hDFs adhesion on these samples against machine-cut controls, the study confirms excellent biocompatibility, including vinculin intensity and adherent cell numbers, indicating that the printed alloy performs equivalently to the machine-cut counterpart.

caption: 3D surface topography map of the wrought Ti–6Al–4V sample obtained via atomic force microscopy.
summary: Atomic force microscopy reveals 3D surface topography for the wrought Ti–6Al–4V sample. The results highlight small topographical variations at phase boundaries, sub-grain surfaces, and mechanical polishing marks. These features are captured with higher sensitivity than standard back-scattered SEM, providing detailed insights into the surface morphology of the wrought material.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the sintered AZ91D-Ni alloy microstructure shown in panel (a).
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the base AZ91D-Ni alloy confirms the presence of key alloying elements. Aluminum is identified as the second dominant element after magnesium, which suggests the formation of the Mg17Al12 strengthening phase. Other trace elements present in the matrix exhibit minimal influence on the overall microstructure.

caption: Workflow diagram illustrating the design and manufacturing pathway for custom bone implants, with the blue-highlighted section representing the specific scope of this research.
summary: This flowchart outlines the comprehensive process for designing and manufacturing custom bone implants. The blue-marked segment highlights the specific scope of this study, which involves importing a 400 mm-long male femur bone CT scan as a DICOM file to facilitate a comparative analysis of the implant design process.

caption: Hardness and reduced modulus versus indentation depth for cast IN718 nitrided at 650 °C.
summary: Cast IN718 samples treated at 650 °C display distinct hardness and reduced modulus trends across the nitrided layer depth. These nanoindentation results illustrate the mechanical behavior of the hard layers formed under high-temperature plasma treatment, allowing for an assessment of the material's surface hardening performance relative to other processing conditions.

caption: Predictor importance ranking for residual stress based on bagged regression tree models, demonstrating that plate thickness is the most influential parameter, consistent with ANOVA findings that also identify welding sequence and cooling rate as statistically significant factors.
summary: The feature importance plot for residual stress, modeled using bagged regression trees, confirms that plate thickness is the most significant parameter. This result aligns with ANOVA analysis, which further validates that welding sequence and cooling rate are statistically significant contributors to residual stress, whereas clamping is found to be non-significant.

caption: Cathodic scans of cyclic voltammograms for the CB:30 electrode in pH 5 Na2SO4 solution, showing the evolution of electrochemical response after varying activation times at a constant current density of –5.0 mA cm–2.
summary: This panel displays cathodic scans of cyclic voltammograms for the CB:30 electrode in a 0.05 M Na2SO4 solution at pH 5. The data illustrates the electrochemical behavior of the electrode following different activation durations at –5.0 mA cm–2, providing insight into the activation process and its impact on electrode performance.

caption: Simulated powder bed configuration for the TD_4 condition, presented as a 3D snapshot with particles color-coded by their relative height.
summary: Representing the TD_4 condition, this panel provides a 3D snapshot of the simulated powder bed. Particles are color-coded by height to illustrate the vertical arrangement and morphology of the bed. This simulation snapshot facilitates the analysis of particle distribution characteristics specific to the TD_4 processing parameters.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of 4340 steel (1200 mm/s) showing finer carbides (blue arrows) dispersed within ferrite plates (white dashed lines).
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the 1200 mm/s sample highlights the dispersion of finer carbides within the ferrite plates. These carbides are oriented specifically relative to the α’-laths, indicating a lower bainite transformation mechanism facilitated by the faster scanning speed, which results in a more refined carbide distribution compared to slower processing.

caption: Parity plot comparing measured current density values against predictions derived from the Butler–Volmer (BV) model for various electrode geometries and surface treatments.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the accuracy of the Butler–Volmer model in predicting current density across different electrode designs. Most experimental data points cluster near the parity line, indicating that the BV framework effectively captures observed HER performance trends, including the enhanced kinetics observed in gold-coated samples after accounting for specific multipliers.

caption: Microstructural state displaying perfect dislocations at [110] planes after hydrogen diffusion at 500 K with an initial hydrogen concentration of 0.16%.
summary: Representing the microstructural change during hydrogen diffusion, this panel depicts the formation of perfect {1/2[110]} dislocations at 500 K. With an initial hydrogen concentration of 0.16%, the image captures the specific dislocation arrangement, contributing to the broader analysis of how hydrogen concentration influences dislocation behavior at lower thermal conditions.

caption: Yield strength versus density comparison for the Al80Mg10Si5Cu5 alloy at 200 °C, highlighting performance metrics against benchmark aluminium alloys.
summary: Displaying the yield strength to density relationship at 200 °C, this plot evaluates the thermal stability and mechanical performance of the Al80Mg10Si5Cu5 alloy. By comparing these values against other aluminium alloys produced by HPDC and alternative processes, the figure demonstrates the material's strength characteristics under elevated temperature service conditions.

caption: Live/Dead staining images showing the distribution of MFCs on PCL and PCL-Fib scaffolds after 3 days of incubation.
summary: Live/dead cell staining performed after 3 days of incubation reveals that MFCs are evenly distributed across the surfaces of the internal filament diameters of both PCL and PCL-Fib scaffolds. The staining confirms the viability and spatial arrangement of the cells within the scaffold architectures.

caption: Comparison of the original all-pixels-on input image and the resulting projected blue light profile at the vat platform without compensation.
summary: This panel displays the uncompensated projection of an all-pixels-on input image. It serves as a baseline to demonstrate the inherent inaccuracies in the projected blue light profile at the vat platform, highlighting the need for image compensation techniques to improve the fidelity of the light delivery system.

caption: Regression plot of fatigue life versus kurtosis (Sku) with R-squared and p-value annotations.
summary: This regression plot illustrates the relationship between kurtosis (Sku) and fatigue life, providing R-squared and p-value statistics. The analysis evaluates whether the peakedness of the surface height distribution, measured by Sku, serves as a statistically significant predictor for the fatigue life of the investigated material samples.

caption: Temperature dependence of the void denuded zone width for Fe-3Cr alloy, illustrating the range between X30 and X50 as a shaded yellow band.
summary: The void denuded zone width for Fe-3Cr is presented against inverse temperature. The data incorporates the average distance method and a shaded yellow band representing the slope variation range between X30 and X50. This visualization characterizes the denuded zone behavior under dual ion irradiation conditions for this specific alloy composition.

caption: EDX analysis of the fracture surface of the slag inclusion samples.
summary: This EDX analysis provides compositional information regarding the fracture surface of the slag inclusion samples. By identifying the elemental constituents present at the fracture site, this spectroscopic technique helps characterize the nature of the slag inclusions and their role in the anisotropic reduction and fracture causes observed in the UTS.

caption: Overview of the experimental test equipment and data acquisition systems utilized for the study.
summary: This photograph displays the comprehensive experimental test equipment and integrated data acquisition systems employed throughout the research. The setup serves as the primary hardware configuration for conducting the experiments described in the study, ensuring accurate measurement and recording of the necessary data parameters during the testing process.

caption: Front-facing view displaying the height and structural dimensions of the thin-walled part.
summary: The front view provides the vertical geometric dimensions of the thin-walled part. This structural representation complements the top view, establishing the physical framework necessary for studying the thermal evolution of the sample, including the first, fifth, and tenth layers, as well as specific substrate points A, C, D, and E.

caption: Bode modulus plots comparing the impedance magnitude (|Z|) of SLM and RA samples across the frequency range.
summary: Bode modulus plots illustrate the impedance magnitude (|Z|) values for both samples. The RA sample demonstrates a higher |Z| value compared to the SLM sample, providing clear evidence that the RA treatment significantly improves the corrosion resistance of the SLM sample when exposed to a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.

caption: 3D topography and cross-sectional profile of the wear scar on the LN17 surface, oriented perpendicular to the microgroove.
summary: This panel illustrates the 3D topography and cross-sectional profile of the wear scar on the LN17 surface, measured perpendicular to the microgroove. The increased roughness characteristic of nitrided surfaces is shown to hinder wear debris deflection, resulting in noticeable debris accumulation around the wear scar in this orientation.

caption: TDA-spectrum of CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 1000 bar with a heating rate of 0.250 K/s, showing the four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit.
summary: This panel presents the TDA-spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA samples charged at 1000 bar at a heating rate of 0.250 K/s. The four-peak deconvolution scenario and cumulative fit function are utilized to analyze the hydrogen desorption, specifically highlighting the spectral features observed in samples subjected to high-pressure hydrogen charging.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot showing the electrochemical response of the scale film on Inconel 625 in 0.2 mol/L phosphoric acid.
summary: The Mott-Schottky curve displayed here illustrates the electrochemical characteristics of the scale film formed on Inconel 625 in a 0.2 mol/L phosphoric acid environment. This plot is part of a broader investigation into how varying acid concentrations influence the semiconducting nature of the protective surface film.

caption: Morphology of Cu precipitates in Fe-2.5%Cu-3.0%Mn-1.5%Ni-1.5%Al alloy simulated without elastic energy.
summary: This panel displays the simulated morphology of Cu precipitates in an Fe-2.5%Cu-3.0%Mn-1.5%Ni-1.5%Al alloy. The simulation is performed without considering elastic energy effects, providing a baseline for understanding the precipitate evolution in the absence of eigenstrain-induced mechanical interactions within the alloy matrix during the aging process.

caption: Schematic illustration of the complex thermal interactions occurring between a high-energy laser beam and amorphous powder particles during the LPBF process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the complex thermal interactions between a laser beam and amorphous powder during the LPBF process. These interactions are fundamental to the subsequent formation of distinct microstructural regions, including molten pools and heat-affected zones, which experience varying cooling rates and develop unique microstructural characteristics during solidification.

caption: Tafel slope analysis comparing the electrochemical kinetic properties of g-C3N4, Ag/g-C3N4, AgNi/g-C3N4, AgCu/g-C3N4, and AgNiCu/g-C3N4 catalysts.
summary: This Tafel plot evaluates the electrochemical kinetic properties of various synthesized catalysts, including g-C3N4, Ag/g-C3N4, AgNi/g-C3N4, AgCu/g-C3N4, and AgNiCu/g-C3N4. By comparing the Tafel slopes of these materials, the figure provides a quantitative assessment of the catalytic performance and reaction kinetics for each specific sample composition under electrochemical testing conditions.

caption: Temperature versus Gibbs free energy relationship for IN718 alloy and associated carbides.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermodynamic relationship between temperature and Gibbs free energy for the IN718 alloy and its constituent carbides. The low Gibbs free energy of (Nb,Ti)C facilitates its formation at grain boundaries, as the melting of TiC increases local Ti and C concentrations, driving the consumption of Nb from the solution.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the sample fabricated without magnetic field assistance, showing a range of 10 to 90 μm.
summary: This histogram quantifies the grain size distribution for the interlayer region without magnetic field assistance. The grains are relatively large, predominantly ranging from 10 to 90 μm, with a calculated average grain size of 21.58 μm, characterizing the coarse microstructure resulting from the standard fabrication process.

caption: Regression line coefficients for pure PLA specimens.
summary: This table presents the regression line coefficients for pure PLA, providing quantitative data to evaluate the influence of specific printing parameters on the tensile modulus. These coefficients serve as a foundational reference for understanding how individual processing variables affect the mechanical performance of the PLA material during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Evolution of Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores for six distinct image augmentation techniques plotted against training progress measured in thousands of images (kimg).
summary: This panel displays the progression of FID scores for six different augmentation types applied to residual stress distribution images. The curves illustrate how the model performance evolves as a function of training steps up to 25,000 kimg, providing a comparative view of how various transformations impact the generative model's convergence.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots of bare Fe2O3 and Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 electrodes recorded in the dark, demonstrating an 80 mV cathodic shift in the effective flat-band potential (EFB) for the Ni-Bi loaded sample.
summary: Mott-Schottky analysis of bare Fe2O3 and Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 electrodes reveals the electronic influence of the Ni-Bi coating. The Ni-Bi-loaded sample exhibits an 80 mV shift in the cathodic direction of the effective flat-band potential compared to the bare Fe2O3, indicating significant modification of the semiconductor's electronic properties.

caption: Rate performance comparison of LSBs with 5 mg cm-2 sulfur loading using CCC and ZnS@CCC interlayers, tested from 0.1C to 1C.
summary: This rate capability plot compares the performance of LSBs with 5 mg cm-2 sulfur loading using CCC and ZnS@CCC interlayers. The ZnS@CCC interlayer demonstrates superior rate performance, maintaining specific capacities of 928, 817, 721, and 649 mAh g-1 at 0.1C, 0.2C, 0.5C, and 1C, respectively, significantly outperforming the CCC interlayer.

caption: HRTEM micrograph of sintered particles processed under N2/H2 atmosphere, showing crystalline structure with inset FFT.
summary: HRTEM imaging of particles sintered in a N2/H2 atmosphere reveals the crystalline structure of the material. The inset FFT provides structural information, confirming the crystalline nature of the sintered particles. This technique is essential for determining the specific crystalline phases present within the sample after the reduction process.

caption: TEM image of a MAR-Al4C3 nanorod alongside its corresponding SAED pattern, confirming the crystalline characteristics of the nanostructure.
summary: This panel presents a TEM image of a MAR-Al4C3 nanorod. The accompanying SAED pattern provides diffraction data that confirms the crystalline structure of the nanorod. This analysis is essential for characterizing the phase and orientation of the Al4C3 nanostructures within the as-built 10% sample.

caption: Solidified polyurethane mix after 30 minutes of mixing, indicating the achievement of the material's pot life.
summary: Solidified polyurethane mix after 30 minutes of mixing, indicating the achievement of the material's pot life. At this stage, the polyurethane has reached a fully solidified state, marking the completion of the curing process and confirming that the pot life has been achieved for the subsequent extraction of the MFCs.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of Pt3Ni/SBA15-C and commercial Pt/C catalysts measured in N2-saturated 0.1 mol/L HClO4 at a scan rate of 10 mV·s⁻¹.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves compare the electrochemical performance of Pt3Ni/SBA15-C and Pt/C catalysts in an acidic environment. The test evaluates the electrochemically active surface area, revealing that the Pt3Ni/SBA15-C catalyst exhibits a significantly larger ECSA, approximately 2.13 times that of the commercial Pt/C, indicating superior electrochemical activity.

caption: Enlarged bright-field TEM image illustrating a deformation twin initiated by the μ phase at the cellular boundary, characterized by minimal dislocation entanglement.
summary: An enlarged bright-field TEM view reveals the initiation of a deformation twin at the cellular boundary, specifically associated with the presence of the μ phase. The observation shows that twin formation occurs with very few dislocations entangled at the boundary, suggesting a specific nucleation mechanism for these twins during material deformation.

caption: Relative density response surface for 13Ni-400 maraging stainless steel showing the influence of layer thickness and laser power.
summary: The influence of layer thickness and laser power on the relative density of 13Ni-400 maraging stainless steel is shown in this response surface plot. By mapping these parameters, the figure clarifies how layer thickness adjustments, in conjunction with laser power, affect the densification behavior of the material during the SLM process.

caption: Layered configuration of the D022 Ni3Nb structure, showing the P Ni-Nb interaction parameter and the total number of layers in the subsystem.
summary: The D022 Ni3Nb structure is depicted as a layered system where the bulk energy is determined by the interaction between pure Ni and Ni3Nb layers. The P Ni-Nb parameter represents these specific interactions, and the total number of layers in the Ni3Nb subsystem is accounted for in the model.

caption: Modular parallel implementation flowchart for density-based filtered topology optimization with integrated manufacturing constraints.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the modular parallel implementation of density-based filtered topology optimization. It explicitly incorporates manufacturing constraints into the computational workflow. The diagram outlines the systematic process for executing these complex optimizations using parallel computing, providing a clear visual guide for the structural design and constraint-handling methodology employed in the study.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve evaluating the CNN model performance in detecting warping defects.
summary: This ROC curve illustrates the diagnostic capability of the CNN model specifically for identifying warping defects. By plotting the true positive rate against the false positive rate, the graph provides a quantitative assessment of the model's classification accuracy and sensitivity for this particular type of manufacturing defect.

caption: Live/Dead staining of the whole multi-material bioprinted structure on days 1 and 7 post-printing, showing cell viability and morphology.
summary: Live/Dead staining of the bioprinted structure on days 1 and 7 demonstrates excellent cell viability. The number of dead cells remains consistent between time points. Furthermore, the staining reveals that the morphology of live hASC-CSKs transitions from a rounded state to an elongated form after 7 days of post-printing culture.

caption: Atomic force microscopy height micrograph of the standard finish (A1) aramid fiber surface.
summary: Atomic force microscopy height micrograph of the standard finish (A1) aramid fiber surface. This 10x10 μm image reveals the characteristic wavy surface texture of the aramid fiber. Arrows highlight the presence of processing aids or surface artefacts, providing a detailed topographical view of the fiber's surface morphology at the nanoscale.

caption: Photograph showing the dogbone-shaped specimens extracted from the rectangular WAAM-printed components, prepared according to ASTM E8M standards for tensile testing.
summary: This panel presents the dogbone-shaped specimens that were extracted from the rectangular WAAM-printed components. These samples were prepared in strict accordance with the ASTM E8M specifications to ensure standardized results during subsequent tensile testing, allowing for accurate evaluation of the mechanical properties of the printed material.

caption: Schematic illustration of a thick table configuration featuring two crossing 1000 N/mm line loads applied along the top surface center XZ- and YZ-planes.
summary: This diagram depicts a thick table benchmark test problem. The structure is loaded with two crossing 1000 N/mm line loads positioned along the center XZ- and YZ-planes of the top surface. Similar to the beam model, the topmost layer is excluded from the overhang constraint and optimization processes.

caption: Photograph of the tungsten-tiled component integrated into the JUDITH 2 electron beam facility cooling circuit prior to thermal loading.
summary: This photograph displays the tungsten-tiled component following the brazing process, now successfully connected to the cooling system of the JUDITH 2 electron beam facility. The image captures the experimental setup shortly before the initiation of thermal loading, providing a clear view of the component's integration within the testing environment.

caption: Yield strength values as a function of build number and orientation, illustrating a consistent downward trend in material resistance to plastic deformation across successive builds.
summary: Yield strength is presented as a function of build number and orientation. The results demonstrate a consistent reduction in yield strength as the build number increases, independent of the build orientation. This trend indicates that the mechanical properties of the parts are sensitive to the cumulative build process history.

caption: Friction coefficient profile for the Invar alloy coating containing 1 wt% B under a 30 N loading condition.
summary: This plot illustrates the friction coefficient behavior of the 1B Invar alloy coating subjected to a 30 N load. The data provides a comparative baseline for evaluating the influence of boron content on the tribological performance and stability of the alloy coating during wear testing.

caption: Quantitative analysis of OCN fluorescence intensity in BMSCs cultured on PT, PTM, and PTMN scaffolds at 14 days.
summary: Quantitative analysis of OCN fluorescence intensity confirms the observations from immunofluorescence staining. The results show that BMSCs cultured on the PTMN scaffold exhibit significantly higher OCN expression levels compared to those on PT and PTM scaffolds at 14 days, providing further evidence of the enhanced osteogenic differentiation promoted by the PTMN scaffold.

caption: Superimposed half-life hysteresis loops of as-LPBFed Invar 36 alloy plotted in relative coordinates to demonstrate Masing behavior.
summary: Relative coordinates are used to plot the half-life hysteresis loops for all tested strain amplitudes. These curves exhibit almost perfect Masing behavior, an intriguing characteristic of the as-LPBFed Invar 36 alloy under cyclic loading, indicating a consistent scaling of the hysteresis loops across the different strain levels investigated.

caption: Real-time discharge curves showing anode voltage evolution over time for varying CeO2 contents.
summary: Real-time discharge curves demonstrate the voltage evolution of anodes with different CeO2 contents. The anode voltage exhibits minimal time lag and maintains relatively stable discharge characteristics within the electrolyte, which indicates that the anode interface sustains high voltage discharge activity throughout the electrochemical testing process.

caption: Metallic tree device assembly featuring uniform corrosion coupons secured with washers to prevent galvanic corrosion.
summary: This photograph displays the metallic tree device used for corrosion testing. Uniform corrosion coupons are mounted onto the structure, utilizing washers to effectively mitigate galvanic corrosion phenomena. The assembly ensures that the coupons remain properly positioned and isolated during the experimental procedure, maintaining the integrity of the corrosion test setup.

caption: Building direction inverse pole figure for the specimen fabricated with an applied magnetic field.
summary: This building direction inverse pole figure represents the crystallographic orientation of the specimen fabricated under a 0.3 T magnetic field. It provides essential data for comparing the texture evolution and grain alignment relative to the build direction when magnetic forces are introduced during the fabrication process.

caption: Grain orientation spread (GOS) map of the top layer produced at low temperature.
summary: This GOS map provides insight into the grain orientation spread of the top layer. Along with other maps, it contributes to the microstructural observation of the build produced at low temperature, helping to characterize the internal grain state and the effects of the cooling environment.

caption: UMAP clustering visualization displaying the global aggregation and distribution of 20 identified cell clusters from various sources, with distinct colors representing individual clusters.
summary: This UMAP plot provides an overview of the single-cell RNA sequencing data, identifying 20 distinct cell clusters. The visualization demonstrates the overall aggregation and distribution of cells from various sources, with each color representing a unique cluster identified through the clustering analysis of the conjunctival tissue samples.

caption: Au 4f X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy profile of fresh Au/SiO2 catalyst, showing deconvoluted peaks corresponding to metallic Au0 at 83.8 and 87.8 eV and oxidized AuI species at 84.5 and 88.7 eV.
summary: The Au 4f XPS spectrum for fresh Au/SiO2 catalysts reveals the presence of both metallic Au0 and oxidized AuI species. Deconvolution of the photoemission peaks at 83.8/87.8 eV and 84.5/88.7 eV confirms the coexistence of these states, providing a baseline for evaluating the electronic state of the gold nanoparticles before reaction.

caption: Lattice strain evolution in the loading direction (LD) and transverse direction (RD) as a function of elevated applied stress.
summary: Lattice strain evolutions in both the loading direction and the transverse direction are plotted against elevated applied stress. These measurements, derived from in-situ neutron diffraction, allow for the evaluation of elastic constants for specific crystallographic planes such as <111>, <200>, <220>, and <311> under various loading conditions at 700 °C.

caption: Light absorbance spectra comparing the 95%BPR5%BBZ1%PPy composite to other prints, highlighting a significant enhancement in the NIR region due to PPy incorporation.
summary: This absorbance spectrum demonstrates the optical properties of the developed composites. The addition of PPy leads to a dramatic improvement in the light absorbance capacity of the 95%BPR5%BBZ1%PPy print, particularly within the NIR region, which effectively prepares the composite to function as an excellent NIR-light responsive material.

caption: Bar chart comparing the hardness values of the investigated alloys across three distinct material states.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the hardness performance of the investigated alloys. By comparing the mechanical properties across three different states, the figure provides a clear quantitative assessment of how processing or treatment conditions influence the material hardness, serving as a primary indicator of the alloys' mechanical strength and structural integrity.

caption: Superposition of theoretical {002} B19' pole positions calculated via PTMC onto the measured pole figure, assuming ⟨011⟩B19' twin boundaries and {942}B2 habit planes, with majority variants in red and minority variants in blue.
summary: Theoretical intensity maxima calculated using PTMC are superimposed on the measured pole figure to validate the martensite structure. The model considers ⟨011⟩B19' twin boundaries and {942}B2 habit planes, with red and blue dots representing majority and minority variants, respectively, showing good agreement with the experimental high-intensity maxima.

caption: Profilometer image of the scratch track on alloy B4, treated at 50 W and 1000 mm/s in an argon atmosphere.
summary: Alloy B4, treated at 50 W and 1000 mm/s in argon, exhibits a significantly narrowed scratch track width of 65 μm and a reduced depth of 5.32 μm. This specific combination of laser parameters results in the most refined scratch profile observed among the argon-shielded samples.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map for Aluminum (Al).
summary: This EPMA elemental map shows the distribution of Aluminum in the AP cubic sample. The mapping confirms that Aluminum is uniformly distributed throughout the matrix without apparent segregation, providing a baseline for comparing the localized concentration of other elements like Copper within the identified precipitate phases.

caption: Linear regression analysis of predicted crack direction, derived from weighted x,y coordinates of maximum temperature event probabilities.
summary: Panel b presents a linear regression line constructed from the x,y locations of maximum temperature events. These points are weighted by their respective probabilities to determine the crack orientation. This regression analysis serves as the basis for extracting the crack region and predicting the specific path of the crack.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of live (green) and dead (red) cells within the three encapsulated islet groups after 7 days of in vitro culture, demonstrating high cell viability.
summary: Live/dead staining assays performed after 7 days of in vitro culture demonstrate that all three encapsulated islet types maintain high cell viability. The fluorescence microscopy images, showing live cells in green and dead cells in red, confirm that the encapsulation process and the presence of vascularizing components do not negatively impact the survival of the islet cells.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of functionally graded TaN/CrN/ZrN coatings synthesized at deposition temperatures ranging from 250 °C to 550 °C.
summary: This panel displays the XRD patterns for TaN/CrN/ZrN coatings deposited at 250 °C, 350 °C, 450 °C, and 550 °C. These diffraction profiles illustrate the structural evolution of the functionally graded coatings as a function of the deposition temperature, providing insight into the crystalline phases present across the different thermal processing conditions.

caption: Phase-field simulation of the Fe-15at.%Cu-1at.%Ni-1at.%Mn alloy at t* = 6000, showing the system dominated by a bcc structure with small crystal structure fluctuations in Cu-rich particles.
summary: At t* = 6000, the phase-field simulation reveals that the Fe-15at.%Cu-1at.%Ni-1at.%Mn alloy system remains in a bcc structure. Small crystal structure fluctuations are observed within Cu-rich particles, which have a diameter of approximately 5 nm, while the precipitates and the matrix maintain a coherent bcc relationship.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) of the L2 layer demonstrating the preferred crystallographic texture of the deformation zone.
summary: The inverse pole figure for the L2 layer indicates that the grains are highly textured. This preferred orientation in the L2 zone is a key finding when compared to the randomly oriented grains observed in the L1 layer, providing insight into the deformation-induced microstructural evolution of the GH3535 alloy.

caption: Parity plot comparing measured and MLR-predicted L 10 noise indicator values.
summary: This parity plot displays the relationship between measured and predicted L 10 sound levels based on the multiple linear regression (MLR) model. By plotting the predicted values against the measured data, the figure highlights the effectiveness of the MLR approach in capturing the variability of the L 10 noise indicator.

caption: Three-dimensional surface plot illustrating the spatial variation of mean particle size across the build plate, derived from a 2D contour surface fit to experimental data points.
summary: This 3D surface plot visualizes the mean particle size distribution across the build area. A 2D contour surface was fitted to the measured data points, revealing that the average particle size increases from the right to the left side of the build chamber and decreases from the back to the front.

caption: CAD model (orange) overlaid with the original XCT scan (green) in xy and xz planes.
summary: This panel displays the initial alignment between the CAD model and the original XCT scan. By overlaying the orange CAD geometry onto the green XCT data, the visualization highlights the baseline spatial correspondence between the design and the manufactured specimen before any non-linear registration processes are applied to the data.

caption: Ti-Al binary phase diagram illustrating the phase transformation regions relevant to the Ti-48Al-2Cr-8Nb alloy.
summary: The Ti-Al binary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic basis for understanding the phase evolution of the Ti-48Al-2Cr-8Nb alloy. It indicates that the metastable α2 phase in as-LPBFed samples transforms into the γ phase at approximately 800 °C, eventually evolving into a coexisting γ + α phase region at higher temperatures.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images showing cell morphology and live/dead staining of cells cultured in 100% and 50% extract groups over 1, 4, and 7 days, with live cells appearing green and dead cells appearing red.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images illustrate the morphology and viability of cells cultured in 100% and 50% extract groups over a 7-day period. Live cells are stained green, while dead cells are stained red, providing a visual assessment of cell health and distribution across the different extract concentrations and time points.

caption: Comparative bar chart illustrating the post-laser polishing surface roughness (Ra) values obtained across 13 distinct experimental trials.
summary: This bar chart provides a comprehensive overview of the Ra response values measured across 13 distinct experiments. It serves to quantify the effectiveness of different laser polishing parameters, allowing for a direct comparison of surface roughness outcomes derived from varying scan speeds and hatch distances across the experimental set.

caption: XRD diffraction pattern recorded for the machined surface subjected to a higher cutting speed of 150 m/min.
summary: Representing the machined surface processed at 150 m/min, this XRD diffraction pattern allows for the quantitative analysis of phase volume fractions. By comparing the intensities of the diffraction peaks against those from other machining parameters, the influence of higher cutting speeds on the surface phase composition is effectively evaluated.

caption: Dark field electron micrograph of the PT621 sample captured in the [001] direction.
summary: Captured in the [001] direction, this dark field electron micrograph provides structural insight into the PT621 sample. This imaging is performed as part of a broader STEM investigation to characterize the morphology and distribution of γ′ and γ'′ precipitates within the alloy matrix.

caption: Live/dead staining images and corresponding quantitative analysis of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured on porous scaffolds.
summary: Live/dead staining images and quantitative analysis of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured on porous scaffolds are presented. The results indicate no significant differences in the live cell rate or dead cell ratio among the four experimental groups, demonstrating consistent biocompatibility across the tested scaffold conditions during the co-culture period.

caption: Quantitative bar graph comparing the percentage of CD206-positive macrophages across different scaffold groups, highlighting significant M2 polarization in ICA@G and ICA@G/NHP.
summary: Quantitative analysis of CD206-positive cell percentages confirms significant M2 polarization in ICA@G and ICA@G/NHP groups. Statistical data shows CD206-positive proportions of 38.7% and 35.9% respectively, compared to 4.2% in controls, demonstrating that these scaffold formulations effectively promote the M2 phenotype in RAW264.7 macrophages.

caption: Optimized temperature profile for a streamlined oval-shaped battery capsule, highlighting enhanced flow attachment in the wake region.
summary: This panel showcases a more streamlined oval-shaped battery capsule design. The temperature distribution reflects an optimization of flow attachment in the wake region, demonstrating how refined geometric shaping can further improve the thermal performance and flow characteristics of the battery capsule under left-to-right airflow conditions.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting specific crystalline features within the alloy after the second aging.
summary: This dark-field TEM image complements the bright-field observation by isolating specific diffraction conditions to highlight crystalline features. It provides enhanced contrast for identifying the distribution and morphology of the nanocrystalline grains and dislocation structures formed during the second aging process, confirming the structural refinement achieved in the alloy.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the classification outcomes for the Llama 405B model during G-code anomaly detection tasks.
summary: This confusion matrix details the classification accuracy of the Llama 405B model when applied to G-code anomaly detection. Utilizing a deterministic approach, the matrix provides a clear breakdown of the model's predictive success, allowing for a direct comparison of its performance against other LLMs in identifying critical G-code errors.

caption: Training loss and accuracy evolution for the optimal DADDA model.
summary: The training process for the optimal DADDA model is illustrated through loss and accuracy curves. These metrics track the model's performance improvement over the course of the training iterations, providing insight into the convergence behavior and overall effectiveness of the DADDA architecture as described in the study's training methodology.

caption: Time-dependent voltage and Faradaic efficiency profiles for a Ni0.50Co0.50-infiltrated cathode SOEC operating at 750 °C under a current density of 0.2 A·cm⁻².
summary: Performance metrics including voltage and Faradaic efficiency are plotted against time for a Ni0.50Co0.50-infiltrated cathode SOEC. The cell was subjected to galvanostatic testing at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻², illustrating the electrochemical stability and efficiency characteristics of this specific bimetallic infiltration composition during the testing period.

caption: Gas temperature distribution upstream of the spray gun at a chamber length of 140 mm and a powder injector length of 40 mm.
summary: Presented is the gas temperature contour for a chamber length of 140 mm and a powder injector length of 40 mm. Heat exchange between the two streams is almost completed as the mixed gas propels toward the convergent section of the nozzle, indicating efficient mixing due to increased residence time.

caption: Blue light profile at 450 nm wavelength displayed as a checkerboard pattern on the focal plane, captured via CMOS camera.
summary: This panel displays the 450 nm blue wavelength light profile projected as a checkerboard pattern. The image, captured by a CMOS camera, confirms the spatial distribution of the light at the focal plane, with the pattern measuring approximately 16.01 mm by 9.01 mm at a magnification factor of 0.77.

caption: Explained variance ratio of principal components derived from feature set f.
summary: This plot illustrates the explained variance ratio for each principal component calculated from the feature set f. By visualizing the contribution of individual components, the figure provides insight into the dimensionality reduction process, highlighting how much information is retained by each principal component within the analyzed dataset.

caption: Fluorescence distribution map of a Rhodamine B film deposited via conventional electrospray, exhibiting a center-bright and edge-dim intensity profile.
summary: The fluorescence distribution of a Rhodamine B film deposited via conventional electrospray is visualized in this panel. The film displays a characteristic center-bright and edge-dim profile, reflecting the droplet deposition behavior. This distribution pattern serves as a reference for evaluating the uniformity and quality of the deposited fluorescent material.

caption: Nanohardness map of the TC11 alloy side in the deformed HT specimen.
summary: Capturing the TC11 alloy side of the deformed HT specimen, this nanohardness map details the hardness variations resulting from deformation. The map allows for an assessment of how the HT-treated microstructure, characterized by wider phases, responds to mechanical stress, providing a clear view of the localized hardness changes.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plot for the ZT-based single cell, measured in wet 10% C3H8-Ar fuel to assess internal resistance.
summary: This panel provides the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plot for the ZT-based single cell. Measured in a wet 10% C3H8-Ar fuel atmosphere, the plot allows for the evaluation of the cell's internal resistance and electrochemical behavior, contributing to the overall assessment of the ZT catalytic layer's performance.

caption: Statistical summary table presenting the quantitative results for grain boundary characteristics and recrystallization fraction across the three build layers.
summary: Statistical results for grain boundary characteristics and recrystallization fraction are presented for the top, middle, and bottom layers. The data indicates that the deformation temperature of the deposited layers remained mostly unchanged due to rapid cooling, resulting in a similar recrystallization fraction across all three layers of the build.

caption: Log-log plot of relative elastic modulus (E*/Es) versus relative density (ρ*/ρs) for AlSi10Mg TPLs, CO, TO, and RCO topologies, benchmarked against reported metal SSLs.
summary: Relative elastic moduli for the AlSi10Mg TPLs are plotted against relative density to evaluate structural performance against established metal SSLs.
