caption: Plastic strain distribution map of Material #6 at an early stage of quasi-static tensile loading, highlighting reduced nucleation points and increased strain amplitude.
summary: This DIC strain map illustrates the evolution of plastic strain in Material #6 during a quasi-static tensile test. At this stage, the nucleation points of plastic deformation are observed to decrease, while the amplitude of the plastic strain increases, indicating the initial localization of deformation within the representative zone.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Fe-rich corner in the Fe-Nb-C system at 1273 K, compared against established thermodynamic models and experimental data.
summary: This panel displays the calculated isothermal section of the Fe-rich corner in the Fe-Nb-C system at 1273 K. The diagram integrates thermodynamic modeling with experimental data to map phase equilibria. It highlights the sensitivity of the Fe-Nb-C extension to the specific Fe-Nb descriptions chosen for the ternary system parameters.

caption: Combined TG-DSC profile of laser-sintered polystyrene showing mass loss and heat flow as a function of temperature.
summary: This TG-DSC profile of laser-sintered polystyrene illustrates critical thermal transitions, including a glass transition at 112 °C and a decomposition onset at 380 °C. The data indicates a maximum degradation rate at 420 °C, culminating in complete decomposition by 480 °C with no residual mass, informing controlled pyrolysis protocols.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Copper (Cu) across the SiC side fracture surface.
summary: Copper elemental distribution across the SiC side fracture surface is visualized in this map. This panel, along with others in the series, illustrates the surface distribution of fracture elements, providing critical information regarding the chemical composition and elemental segregation at the brazing joint interface after the 910 °C treatment.

caption: Detailed view of isolated Cu clusters dispersed within the Al–Ni–Cu-rich matrix region.
summary: This panel focuses on the formation of almost pure Cu clusters within the ordered B2 phase of the Al–Ni–Cu-rich matrix. These clusters are clearly resolved through APT measurements, demonstrating the localized chemical decomposition and the specific partitioning of copper atoms within the ordered crystal structure of the magnet material.

caption: Full energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum acquired from the ablated scan line region.
summary: Full energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum acquired from the ablated scan line region. This spectrum provides a quantitative overview of the elemental composition present in the ablated area, confirming the presence of Fe, Cr, C, and O, which supports the findings observed in the individual elemental distribution maps.

caption: Principal component analysis score scatter plot comparing t[1] and t[3] components for various peg samples, featuring a 0.05 significance level Hotelling's T2 confidence ellipse to identify outliers.
summary: This PCA score plot of t[1] and t[3] components reveals distinct clustering patterns among peg samples. CNC, IM, and chemical vapor smoothed samples exhibit similarities, while as-printed and tumbled samples show high dispersity on the right. The Hotelling's T2 ellipse at a 0.05 significance level effectively identifies statistical outliers within the dataset.

caption: Chronoamperometric response of SLMed and sintered AlSi10Mg alloys immersed in a 0.5 M HCl solution.
summary: This panel illustrates the chronoamperometric behavior of additive-manufactured and sintered AlSi10Mg alloys when exposed to a 0.5 M HCl solution. The measurement is performed to assess the stability of the passive film and the susceptibility of the alloys to pitting corrosion within this acidic environment.

caption: Spectral response of a pure PMMA fiber optic sensor under maximal point force, showing minimal evanescent wave interactions and weak spectral modulation determined by the notched geometry.
summary: Pure PMMA fiber optic sensors exhibit minimal evanescent wave interactions, resulting in weak spectral modulation primarily dictated by the notched structure. The spectral response, measured at maximal point force before mechanical breakdown, serves as a baseline for comparing the functionalized sensors, demonstrating the limited optical sensitivity of the unmodified polymer matrix.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the resonant tunneling diode (RTD) comparing first barrier thicknesses L B 1 of 2 nm (orange dashed), 3 nm (black solid), and 4 nm (blue dotted), with a constant second barrier thickness L B 2 of 3 nm.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of an RTD as the first barrier width L B 1 is varied between 2 nm, 3 nm, and 4 nm while keeping the second barrier width constant at 3 nm. The plot illustrates how these structural variations influence the resonant tunneling behavior and current flow.

caption: Polar distribution of parameter ω for the superalloy pre-serviced at 1050°C/100 MPa/30 h.
summary: This polar distribution of parameter ω characterizes the superalloy after pre-servicing at 1050°C and 100 MPa for 30 hours. The plot illustrates the PR value distribution under stress-assisted conditions, offering a comparative view of how the γ' precipitate-matrix channel configuration evolves when mechanical stress is applied alongside elevated temperature exposure.

caption: 3D point cloud sample illustrating a simulated dent defect on the cylinder.
summary: This panel presents a 3D point cloud representation of a dent defect simulated on the surface of a cylinder. Following the specified pre-processing workflow, the dent is clearly captured within the point cloud data, providing a distinct morphological feature for testing surface defect detection algorithms.

caption: Calculated phase fraction diagram for the quaternary Cr-Co-Re-Ni system at 900 °C, assuming a fixed Ni concentration of 8 mol%. The plot illustrates the stability regions and relative amounts of α-Cr and σ-(Co,Cr) phases, with gray-shaded regions representing compositions where phase definitions are currently undefined.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram displays the phase fractions of α-Cr and σ-(Co,Cr) in the quaternary Cr-Co-Re-Ni system at 900 °C with 8 mol% Ni. Thermodynamic calculations confirm the formation of the σ-(Co,Cr) phase within the Cr-rich precipitate concentration range, providing a theoretical basis for interpreting the observed microstructural phase evolution.

caption: Confocal images of DiO-ApoVs within composite hydrogels and data on the in vitro release profile in PBS.
summary: Confocal microscopy images show the distribution of DiO-ApoVs within composite hydrogels. Additionally, the panel presents the in vitro release profile of ApoVs from these hydrogels in PBS, demonstrating the feasibility of using the hydrogel as a delivery vehicle for the vesicles.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions for a martensitic stainless steel as a function of Cr/Ni equivalents.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram depicts the thermodynamic stability regions for martensitic stainless steel. It serves as a foundational reference for understanding how varying Cr/Ni equivalents influence the phase composition and solidification behavior of the alloy, providing the necessary context for interpreting the subsequent microstructural evolution observed during the solidification process.

caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 25 °C, showing the distribution of detected solutes.
summary: This panel displays the normalised mass spectrum for Inconel 718 samples tested at 25 °C. Analysis of carbon content was performed across various temperatures to investigate solute presence. The data indicates that while other solutes are present in comparable amounts, carbon traces remain unresolved by atom probe tomography.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of Ti–6Al–4V powder prepared for the PBF method.
summary: This histogram illustrates the particle size distribution for Ti–6Al–4V powder intended for PBF processing. The powder exhibits a smaller diameter range relative to the DED powder. The distribution confirms a variety of particle sizes, which aligns with the observed characteristics of the powder used in the PBF method.

caption: Intermediate HAADF-STEM image (35th frame) of the specimen series acquired at a low electron dose of 3·10^2 e/Å^2.
summary: The 35th frame of the low-dose acquisition series (3·10^2 e/Å^2) shows the specimen's appearance during the experiment. No evident damage is observed at this stage, supporting the finding that lower electron doses effectively preserve the structural integrity of the material throughout the 70-frame acquisition process.

caption: Box plots comparing trace element content variations within magnetite grains (Mt1, Mt2, and Mt3) from Fe-Ti oxide ores, showing differences in Cr concentrations across the three magnetite types.
summary: Trace element variations in magnetite grains from Fe-Ti oxide ores span 6–7 orders of magnitude. The box plots reveal that Mt2 and Mt3 contain significantly higher Cr concentrations (median 13,956 ppm) compared to Mt1 (median 86.9 ppm), demonstrating distinct geochemical signatures among the different magnetite populations within the ore samples.

caption: Parity plot comparing total energy values calculated via DFT against those predicted by the ACE machine learning interatomic potential for training and test datasets.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the ACE machine learning interatomic potential by comparing its total energy outputs against DFT reference values. Data points for both training and test sets are displayed, with an inset providing the mean absolute error to quantify the model's performance in energy prediction.

caption: Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) evolution plotted against the number of training iterations.
summary: This panel displays the PSNR change result as a function of the number of iterations during the training process. The curve illustrates the performance improvement of the model, showing how the PSNR metric evolves as the optimization progresses, providing a clear indication of the convergence behavior of the loss function.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of human skin fibroblasts (HSFs) stained with live/dead markers following incubation with hydrogel treatments.
summary: Live/dead cell staining of HSFs is utilized here to evaluate the biocompatibility and potential cytotoxicity of the prepared hydrogels. The fluorescence images provide a visual assessment of cell viability, confirming the suitability of the hydrogel materials for supporting fibroblast growth in vitro.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of macrophage activation using the CDg16 probe, showing strong staining in Ti-treated cells compared to controls.
summary: Macrophage activation was assessed using the CDg16 fluorescent probe. The imaging results indicate that CDg16 strongly stains Ti-treated macrophages, similar to the positive control treated with lipopolysaccharides. This confirms that the CDg16 probe effectively tracks the activation state of macrophages in response to the titanium implant surface.

caption: Spin-wave dispersion spectrum for the base permalloy dot structure with a squeeze ratio of s = 1.0, showing the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone.
summary: This panel displays the spin-wave dispersion spectrum for the base permalloy dot structure at a squeeze ratio of 1.0. It highlights the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone. The spectrum illustrates the characteristic spin-wave behavior in the 2D magnetic crystal composed of Py dots in a Co matrix.

caption: Binary Ni-V phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium temperature ranges for the nickel-vanadium system.
summary: The Ni-V binary phase diagram displays the equilibrium temperature ranges for the nickel-vanadium system. Analysis of this diagram indicates that vanadium has little effect on enhancing the solidification temperature range of the initial IN625 superalloy, suggesting it does not modify the solidification zone or final grain morphology.

caption: Galvanostatic cycling performance of the Li/PVDF-LLZTO CPE/Li symmetric cell evaluated under varying current densities up to 0.4 mA/cm².
summary: This plot illustrates the galvanostatic cycling performance of the printed electrolyte within a symmetric cell configuration. The electrolyte exhibits remarkable stability when subjected to elevated current densities reaching 0.4 mA/cm². The cell maintains consistent performance throughout the test without experiencing any catastrophic short-circuit failure, confirming the robustness of the electrolyte.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of GSC after 24 h of incubation with PMMA and 3D-printed resin specimens, showing live cells in green and dead cells in red at 100-fold magnification.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images reveal the viability of GSC after 24 hours of exposure to PMMA and 3D-printed resin specimens. The staining shows that cells in all sample groups maintain intact membranes and are propidium iodide-negative, confirming the absence of cytotoxicity across all tested GNP concentrations and print orientations.

caption: Recoverable strain plotted against volumetric energy density (VED) for a 50 MPa stress level, highlighting variations induced by laser power, scanning speed, and hatch space adjustments.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the recoverable strain as a function of VED at a 50 MPa stress level. Data points represent modifications in laser power, scanning speed, and hatch space, with the anchor point marked in black. This demonstrates the material's transformation behavior sensitivity to specific laser processing parameters.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping illustrating the distribution of constituent elements across the surfaces of pTi, pTi–CZCs, and pTi–CZCs–ZOL samples.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping provides a visual representation of the surface elemental composition for the untreated pTi, pTi–CZCs, and pTi–CZCs–ZOL coatings. This analysis confirms the presence and distribution of specific elements within the hierarchical zeolite coatings and the drug-loaded scaffold surfaces, validating the successful functionalization of the titanium alloy.

caption: Projection of phase equilibria in the Cu–Ni–S system onto the Cu2S–Ni3S2 section, comparing experimental results from the present study (red circles) and literature (remaining symbols) with FactSage 8.3 calculations (diamonds and solid lines).
summary: This figure illustrates phase equilibria within the Cu–Ni–S system, specifically projected onto the Cu2S–Ni3S2 section. It compares experimental matte and solid phase compositions from the current study and literature against FactSage 8.3 thermodynamic calculations. The plot effectively demonstrates the alignment between experimental data and predicted phase boundaries in this system.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the HT-2 sample, calculated from local EBSD misorientation measurements.
summary: This map illustrates the geometrically necessary dislocation density of the HT-2 sample, determined through local misorientation data from EBSD. The analysis focuses on identifying strain distribution patterns within the fractured specimen, offering a detailed view of the dislocation structures present after the creep fracture process.

caption: Maximum atomic and electronic temperatures for 50 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFe.
summary: Thermal data for 50 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFe are presented here, showing the peak atomic and electronic temperatures across twelve separate events. These results highlight the influence of increased cascade energy on the thermal evolution of the NiFe system during the simulated irradiation process.

caption: Detailed view of Ni-Mn-Si 20% iso-concentration surfaces after 50 hours of aging, illustrating the onset of clustering.
summary: This panel isolates the Ni-Mn-Si-rich regions at the 50-hour aging mark. The visualization demonstrates the emergence of clusters enriched with these elements, confirming that the Ni, Mn, and Si content has reached the 20% threshold, which signifies the development of localized compositional features within the ferrite matrix during the aging process.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the AZ91/GWZ831K interface used for compositional analysis.
summary: This SEM image focuses on the AZ91/GWZ831K interface, revealing a 10 μm thick transition zone. The region exhibits significant segregation of precipitates and variations in grain morphology. This structural transition zone is the site of elemental diffusion and compositional gradients, which are further analyzed through subsequent EDS line scanning and mapping techniques.

caption: Intermediate-magnification TEM image highlighting the darker regions corresponding to 2D MXene layers acting as the core material.
summary: Intermediate-magnification TEM imaging reveals the internal architecture of the Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene hybrid nanostructure. A distinct darker region is observed, which indicates the presence of 2D MXene layers serving as the core material within the hybrid, confirming the structural role of the MXene component in the composite.

caption: Maximum shear stress τmax profile at t = 17.9 ps, illustrating the stress state as the shock front reaches the free plane.
summary: The maximum shear stress τmax profile is presented at 17.9 ps as the shock front arrives at the right boundary free plane. Plastic theoretical predictions regarding interfacial discontinuities for this stress state are consistent with the MD simulation results, confirming the validity of the theoretical model.

caption: Kappa-carbide crystal structure illustrating the specific atomic arrangement within the lattice framework.
summary: The kappa-carbide crystal structure is presented as a distinct phase within the lightweight austenitic steel system. This atomic model highlights the specific geometric configuration of the constituent elements, providing a structural reference for understanding the carbide formation in these complex alloy systems.

caption: Reflection coefficient plot of the optimized antenna design featuring sidelobe suppression.
summary: This plot displays the reflection coefficient of the optimized antenna design, which incorporates sidelobe suppression techniques. The data illustrates the electromagnetic performance characteristics of the antenna, providing a clear representation of the reflection behavior across the relevant frequency range as part of the overall design optimization process.

caption: Skewness (Ssk) distribution indicating surface topography characteristics before and after Hirtisation®.
summary: Skewness (Ssk) values shift from positive to negative after Hirtisation®, with medians decreasing from 0.33, 0.44, and –0.11 to –0.33, –0.71, and –0.38. This transition indicates a fundamental change in surface topography from peak-dominated to valley-dominated surfaces as a result of the Hirtisation® treatment applied to the samples.

caption: DSC/TG analysis of the AR78-TiO2 filament after partial debinding in alumina powder, highlighting the thermal decomposition profile with overlapping peaks.
summary: Thermal analysis of the AR78-TiO2 filament after partial debinding in alumina powder shows the DSC/TG signal profile. The data clearly exhibits overlapping peaks in the decomposition temperature range, confirming that the pre-debinding procedure influences the thermal response of the binder mixture within the filament structure during subsequent heating.

caption: Galvanostatic discharge profile of an Al thin film electrode on Cu foil, recorded at a slow rate of 1.5 µA to observe lithiation regimes.
summary: This galvanostatic discharge profile of an Al thin film electrode on Cu foil was obtained at a very slow rate of 1.5 µA, requiring approximately 800 hours for full lithiation. The plot highlights distinct lithiation regimes, with a shaded region indicating potential noise attributed to mechanical energy from Li-rich phase formation.

caption: Benchmark of Mixed-Mode I/II fracture toughness values from this study against literature data at a mixed-mode ratio of approximately 50%.
summary: Experimental results for Mixed-Mode I/II fracture tests are compared with literature values specifically at a mixed-mode ratio of around 50%. This comparison highlights the consistency of the current study's findings with established data, providing a clear validation of the mixed-mode fracture behavior observed in the tested specimens.

caption: Creep displacement trends for solution-treated and aged samples, demonstrating the stabilization of creep properties after prolonged aging.
summary: Creep displacement data for solution-treated and aged samples are shown to evaluate long-term stability. The results indicate that creep displacement and strain rate sensitivity initially increase, then decrease, and finally stabilize with increasing aging time, confirming that the creep properties become stable after longtime aging.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of N90 alloy following 1000 h of cyclic oxidation in dry air at 800 °C, showing an external Cr2O3 scale with Ti-rich oxide inclusions and spinel phases.
summary: N90 alloy subjected to 1000 h of cyclic oxidation in dry air at 800 °C develops an external Cr2O3 oxide scale. EDS analysis reveals the formation of Ti-rich oxide inclusions and Ti-enriched spinel oxides, alongside (Ti, Al)-rich intergranular oxides, providing insight into the alloy's oxidation resistance and surface degradation.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for melt-spun ribbons measured under constant magnetic fields ranging from 0.1 to 2 T.
summary: This panel displays the temperature dependence of magnetization for melt-spun ribbons across the magnetostructural transition. Measurements were conducted on heating at a sweep rate of 1.0 K/min under constant magnetic fields from 0.1 to 2 T, providing essential data for calculating the isothermal temperature change associated with the transition.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni-Fe-W ternary system calculated at 1473 K, extrapolated from Ni-Fe, Ni-W, and Fe-W binary systems.
summary: This panel illustrates the calculated isothermal section of the Ni-Fe-W ternary system at 1473 K. Consistent with the lower temperature model, these phase boundaries are extrapolated from the Ni-Fe, Ni-W, and Fe-W binary systems to provide a comprehensive view of the ternary phase stability at this higher temperature.

caption: Residual stress measurements taken at the center of the gauge volume for HCF specimens, plotted for axial, lateral, and 45-degree directions at four distinct measurement points labeled I, II, III, and IV.
summary: Residual stress states within the gauge volume of HCF specimens are quantified across three orientations: axial, lateral, and 45 degrees. Measurements are localized at the center of the gauge volume at four specific points (I, II, III, and IV), providing a detailed spatial profile of the internal stress distribution.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of iNOS and CD206 in skull tissue 4 weeks post-implantation, revealing macrophage polarization states.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining of iNOS and CD206 in the defect area 4 weeks after scaffold implantation demonstrates macrophage polarization. Observations indicate that the 10% PBT group exhibits higher CD206 expression and lower iNOS expression compared to the control group, suggesting a shift toward an anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage phenotype in the treated tissue.

caption: Fluorescence micrographs of SAOS-2 cells cultured for 72 hours on titanium and zirconia surfaces, showing actin filaments stained with phalloidin-FITC (green), vinculin-labeled focal adhesions (red), and nuclei stained with DAPI (blue).
summary: Fluorescence micrographs visualize SAOS-2 cell morphology on titanium and zirconia surfaces after 72 hours of incubation. The staining highlights actin filaments in green, vinculin-associated focal adhesions in red, and cell nuclei in blue. These images provide a qualitative assessment of cellular structural characteristics and focal adhesion distribution on the test surfaces.

caption: Simulated Ta distribution map highlighting punctual enrichments in intercellular regions.
summary: Simulated Ta distribution map for LP processing conditions demonstrates punctual enrichments within the intercellular regions. These localized concentrations, visualized with color scales mimicking TEM-EDS mappings, indicate the formation of carbides during the solidification process, consistent with the multiphase-field simulation results for the specified thermal boundary conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the Co2Si precipitate crystal structure.
summary: This panel displays the atomic unit cell configuration for the Co2Si precipitate phase. As part of the structural analysis of precipitates in the alloy, this schematic highlights the specific crystalline geometry of the Co2Si phase, distinguishing it from other precipitates present in the material microstructure.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) visualization of bulging behavior at 200 °C, highlighting concave deformation in the C-X structure and convex deformation in the C-T structure.
summary: Digital image correlation (DIC) provides experimental evidence of the bulging effect at 200 °C. The images reveal distinct deformation modes, specifically concave bulging for the C-X structure and convex bulging for the C-T structure, confirming the phenomena observed in the numerical simulations.

caption: Geometry and nominal dimensions of the as-printed tensile specimens, highlighting specific regions designated for X-ray computed tomography (blue), optical tomography (green), and bulk chemistry analysis (grey).
summary: The diagram details the geometry and nominal dimensions of the as-printed tensile specimens. It identifies specific regions allocated for X-ray computed tomography, optical tomography, and bulk chemistry characterization. These designated zones facilitate systematic material evaluation, including tensile testing of specimens from various build plate positions like 1C, 7C, and 12C.

caption: Technical drawing of the modified second Sandia fracture (MSSF) specimen, featuring a 3.12 mm thickness to prevent out-of-plane bending during testing.
summary: This MSSF specimen schematic illustrates the geometry used for validating the phase field model. The design incorporates a 3.12 mm thickness to ensure structural stability by suppressing out-of-plane bending. Red dots are marked on the specimen to serve as reference points for accurate displacement tracking during the fracture propagation experiments.

caption: LSCM image at 1200 °C revealing the onset of melting within the element segregation zone while the surrounding matrix remains solid.
summary: At 1200 °C, the LSCM observation indicates that the element segregation zone begins to melt. Despite the localized melting observed in this specific region, the surrounding matrix maintains its solid state, demonstrating a temperature-dependent phase transition localized to the segregation zone.

caption: Log-log plot of stress versus strain rate for the thin-hinge structure at various axial compressive strains, including base material data for comparison.
summary: This plot displays the stress-strain rate relationship for thin-hinge structures at specific compressive strains. The fitted line slopes represent rate sensitivity exponents. Quantitative analysis indicates that the thin-hinge structure exhibits a higher degree of apparent rate-hardening compared to the base material, demonstrating significantly elevated strain rate sensitivity in the 0.25–0.3 strain range.

caption: Hydrogen desorption spectrum measured at a heating rate of 1200 °C/h, illustrating the experimental data and the Gaussian-fitted curve used for peak analysis.
summary: This panel presents the hydrogen desorption spectrum obtained at a heating rate of 1200 °C/h. Through Gaussian peak deconvolution, the spectrum is analyzed to characterize hydrogen trapping sites. This data is essential for calculating desorption activation energies and quantifying the total hydrogen released from the material's microstructure.

caption: Synchrotron in-situ X-ray image displaying pore distribution in the melt pool processed at 350 W and 600 mm/min.
summary: Captured via synchrotron in-situ X-ray imaging, this panel illustrates the pore distribution in the melt pool at 350 W and 600 mm/min. The image highlights how bubbles concentrate at the front wall and bottom of the melt track boundary, contributing to the formation of residual pore defects after solidification.

caption: PCA biplot illustrating the distribution of acid digestion samples for principal components 2 and 3, where PET samples exhibit distinct clustering behavior.
summary: The PCA biplot for components 2 and 3 highlights the clustering patterns of different polymer types within the acid digestion dataset. PET samples, in particular, demonstrate an overall clustering effect when observing these specific components, providing insight into the structural and chemical similarities between the analyzed polymer-based samples.

caption: Complete 3D molecular structure of the alkaline phosphatase (ALP) receptor, energy-minimized following retrieval from the Protein Data Bank.
summary: The complete 3D structure of the ALP receptor is presented, derived from the Protein Data Bank. This model underwent energy minimization using UCSF Chimera and AutoDock to achieve its final, stable conformation, providing a reliable structural basis for subsequent molecular docking and interaction studies within the research framework.

caption: XRD patterns of Nb–40Ti–20Ta samples processed at varying energy densities.
summary: These XRD patterns illustrate the structural response of the Nb–40Ti–20Ta alloy to different energy densities during the LPBF process. By comparing these plots, the influence of processing parameters on the resulting crystalline structure is evaluated, providing insight into how energy input affects phase stability and material characteristics.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the composite material prior to the crosslinking process, displaying characteristic peaks associated with nano-HA, Gel, and CMC components.
summary: This FTIR spectrum characterizes the chemical composition of the composite material before the crosslinking process. It identifies the presence of nano-HA, Gel, and CMC components through their respective spectral peaks. These results provide a baseline for understanding the chemical state of the 3D-printed bone scaffold materials prior to further processing.

caption: Selected Area Electron Diffraction pattern of the TGO layer, confirming a close-packed hexagonal Al2O3 crystal structure with diffraction streaks indicating the presence of stacking faults.
summary: The SAED pattern confirms that the TGO layer possesses a close-packed hexagonal structure, identified as Al2O3. Diffraction streaks observed in the pattern provide clear evidence of stacking faults within the TGO, consistent with the structural analysis of the material during thermal cycling.

caption: Creep strain versus time curves for PBF-LB/M specimens tested at 850 °C.
summary: This panel displays the experimental creep strain evolution over time for PBF-LB/M specimens at 850 °C. These results are part of a broader investigation into the creep performance of additively manufactured materials, illustrating the material's deformation behavior under constant temperature conditions as part of the comparative analysis presented in the figure.

caption: Transmittance spectra of 0.1 wt% A-CNC/CTFA resin samples subjected to varying ultrasonication durations.
summary: This panel displays the transmittance spectra of A-CNC/CTFA resin at different sonication times. The data demonstrates that increasing the ultrasonication duration enhances the transparency of the composite resin ink, which serves as a direct indicator of improved dispersion of A-CNC particles within the resin matrix.

caption: Room temperature magnetization profiles (M-H loops) measured on composite mats with dimensions of approximately 5×5 cm².
summary: This panel displays room temperature magnetization profiles obtained from composite mats measuring 5×5 cm². These magnetic characterization results provide the foundational data for analyzing the magnetic behavior of the composite materials, serving as the basis for extracting key parameters like saturation magnetization and coercive field in subsequent panels.

caption: Training loss evolution for the uni-variate TiDE model over the training horizon.
summary: This panel presents the training loss curve for the uni-variate TiDE model. The plot serves as a metric to evaluate the model's convergence and performance during the training process, providing insight into how effectively the uni-variate architecture learns the melt pool dynamics relative to the simulation ground truth.

caption: Pareto chart detailing the significance of process parameters on melt pool width for a 100 μm spot size.
summary: This Pareto chart presents the significance of various process parameters regarding melt pool width for a 100 μm spot size. The red line represents the threshold of significance, highlighting which factors contribute most to the variation in melt pool width during the laser processing experiment.

caption: Magnified view of the (2 0 0) diffraction peak for the A1 noHT, A1 HT1, and A1 HT2 samples at 423 K.
summary: This panel provides a magnified view of the (2 0 0) diffraction peak for the A1 noHT, A1 HT1, and A1 HT2 samples at 423 K. Inspecting these specific diffractogram peaks corresponding to the cubic austenite phase is essential for identifying and deducing the presence of internal stresses in the material.

caption: Atomic arrangement model of the Ti-40.0Mo (25.0 at% Mo) alloy, showing the relative positions of Ti and Mo atoms in the high-molybdenum concentration β-phase structure.
summary: The atomic arrangement of the Ti-40.0Mo (25.0 at% Mo) alloy is depicted here, with Ti and Mo atoms shown as gray and blue spheres. The structure confirms that atomic positions are significantly displaced from ideal bcc lattice sites, with Ti atoms exhibiting approximately twice the mean displacement of Mo atoms.

caption: Microscopic examination of printed HDPE with 15 wt% glass fibre, showing the increased density of reinforcement.
summary: This optical microscopic image displays the printed HDPE composite with 15 wt% glass fibre. The increased density of the reinforcement is visible compared to lower weight fractions, allowing for an analysis of how the fibre loading affects the overall structural integrity and morphology of the printed layers.

caption: Comparative I-V analysis of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film measured in air versus an atmosphere containing 1.32 ppm of formaldehyde.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of the composite film under ambient air and 1.32 ppm formaldehyde exposure. The observed increase in current upon exposure to formaldehyde indicates the n-type semiconducting behavior of the sensor, demonstrating its sensitivity to the target gas.

caption: Representative load-displacement curves for the {110} grain orientation comparing as-casted and AM-ed HEA samples.
summary: This panel displays representative load-displacement curves obtained from nanoindentation testing of {110} grain orientations. The data compares the mechanical response of as-casted and AM-ed high-entropy alloy (HEA) specimens, illustrating the influence of processing conditions on the load-bearing behavior of specific grain orientations within the material microstructure.

caption: Digital image correlation strain map of the CR43%/A500°C-1h sample at the tenth cycle, demonstrating limited strain localization.
summary: Representing the sample with the lowest temperature change, the CR43%/A500°C-1h specimen shows distinct strain behavior at the tenth cycle. The DIC map reveals that only the upper portion of the gauge length has reached its maximum strain, indicating restricted development of Lüders-like bands compared to other processing conditions.

caption: CALPHAD-calculated solidification profile for Ni48.9Ti51.1 (at.%) showing the evolution of B2-matrix Ni-content and solid mole fraction as a function of decreasing temperature, including the onset of Ti2Ni precipitation.
summary: This CALPHAD simulation illustrates the solidification behavior of Ni48.9Ti51.1 powder. The B2-matrix Ni-content decreases until 1050 °C, while the solid mole fraction rises sharply between 1307 °C and 1280 °C. Additionally, Ti2Ni precipitation initiates at 985 °C, reaching a final concentration of 8 mol.% during the cooling process.

caption: Ragone plot comparing energy density (kJ/kg) versus power density (W/kg) for beta-emitting radioisotopes (green) and chemical sources (blue).
summary: This Ragone plot illustrates the performance gap between beta-emitting radioisotopes and conventional chemical energy sources. Radioisotopes exhibit theoretical energy densities 1000 times greater than chemical sources, offering potential for extended operational lifetimes. The plot highlights the research objective of advancing nuclear battery technology toward these theoretical energy and power density limits.

caption: Overview of the RPS100 UA 21 refill friction stir spot welding machine, highlighting the integration of a cooling module and servo motor system.
summary: This panel displays the configuration of the refill friction stir spot welding (RFSSW) machine. It specifically features the RPS100 UA 21 equipment, which is equipped with a cooling module and a servo motor to facilitate the welding process, providing a clear view of the industrial setup used for the experiments.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the as-casted Zr55Cu30Al10Ni5 bulk metallic glass (BMG) workpiece, showing a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 681 K.
summary: The DSC curve characterizes the thermal behavior of the as-casted Zr55Cu30Al10Ni5 bulk metallic glass workpiece. Analysis of the thermal profile reveals a distinct glass transition temperature (Tg) measured at 681 K, providing critical information regarding the thermal stability and amorphous nature of the investigated metallic glass sample.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the γ′ phase.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern provides crystallographic evidence for the γ′ phase. By analyzing the diffraction spots shown in this pattern, the phase is definitively confirmed as the γ′ phase, validating the structural identification derived from the associated microstructural observations.

caption: Al5Co2–AlCo two-phase region boundary plotted across a range of temperatures, derived from common tangent analysis.
summary: The Al5Co2–AlCo two-phase region is plotted as a function of temperature. The phase boundary is determined by identifying the equilibrium compositions from the common tangent construction shown in panel (a) across various temperatures, effectively mapping the stability region for these two intermetallic phases.

caption: Line graph displaying the evolution of principal strain components e11 and e22, alongside shear strain e12, measured at the intersection of the crack plane and the boundary as a function of the normalized distance.
summary: This line graph displays the evolution of principal strain components e11 and e22, alongside shear strain e12, measured at the intersection of the crack plane and the boundary as a function of the normalized distance. The data quantifies the effect of an approaching crack on the local strain state at the boundary.

caption: Off-specular neutron reflectometry data for the unbiased state, displaying the sum of spin-up and spin-down components with the out-of-plane scattering vector Qz on the y-axis and the difference between incident and outgoing wave vectors on the x-axis.
summary: This panel presents experimental off-specular neutron reflectometry data for the unbiased magnetic state. The plot maps the scattering intensity as a function of the out-of-plane scattering vector and the difference between incident and outgoing wave vectors, providing a baseline for analyzing magnetic charge patterns in the honeycomb sample.

caption: Tabulated process parameter settings for 20 distinct manufacturing conditions, featuring a constant hatch distance of 140 and a layer thickness of 30.
summary: This table presents the comprehensive matrix of 20 process parameter combinations utilized for manufacturing cubic samples. Key manufacturing parameters, specifically the hatch distance of 140 and layer thickness of 30, were held constant across all trials to ensure consistency in the experimental design for subsequent microstructural observations.

caption: I–V relationship diagram illustrating the narrow process window for surface quality.
summary: Fig. 3 (d) illustrates the relationship between I–V parameters and surface quality, showing a narrow process window. This plot demonstrates how variations in current and voltage directly influence the resulting surface quality, emphasizing the sensitivity of the process to these specific electrical parameters.

caption: XRD pattern of the silver deposit displaying characteristic peaks that match the FCC crystal structure of silver according to JCPDS 04–0783.
summary: XRD analysis provides structural confirmation of the silver deposit by displaying characteristic peaks consistent with the FCC crystal pattern of silver metal. The observed diffraction pattern aligns with the JCPDS 04–0783 standard, further supporting the XPS findings that the plasma jet effectively produces high-purity metallic silver.

caption: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity of CeNiZn and its hydride derivative CeNiZnH1.2, presented as normalized values relative to the resistivity measured at 325 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent electrical resistivity behavior for both the precursor CeNiZn and the hydride CeNiZnH1.2. Data are normalized to the resistivity values at 325 K, allowing for a direct comparison of the electronic transport properties between the two materials across the measured temperature range.

caption: Summary table detailing layer stacking performance and the calculated printability index for the investigated hydrogel inks.
summary: This table summarizes the layer stacking performance and printability index for H_Zn/Alg, H_Ca/Alg, and H_Ba/Alg. Layer stacking serves as a critical parameter for evaluating self-standing ability, describing deformation at layer intersections caused by the combined influence of gravity and surface tension during the material deposition process.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the 4Al10V alloy showing the iso-concentration surface of the precipitate phase.
summary: This APT reconstruction of the 4Al10V alloy visualizes the iso-concentration surface of the precipitate phase within the matrix. Atom maps reveal that the L21 phase is enriched in Al and V while showing depletion in Fe and Cr, providing a clear 3D spatial distribution of the elemental constituents.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for dilution, showing the impact of input parameters where laser power (P) and scan speed (V) are the primary governing factors.
summary: This SHAP beeswarm plot visualizes the influence of various input parameters on the dilution output variable. The analysis indicates that dilution is strongly governed by laser power and scan speed, highlighting the critical role these processing parameters play in determining the final dilution characteristics during the material fabrication process.

caption: Rietveld refinement of the powder neutron diffraction pattern for the A2 HT2 alloy in the ferromagnetic austenite state, showing experimental data, calculated and difference patterns, and Bragg reflections.
summary: This panel displays the Rietveld refinement of powder neutron diffraction data for the A2 HT2 alloy in the magnetically ordered state. The visualization includes experimental data, calculated fit, and difference patterns, with Bragg reflections marked. These results are critical for determining the magnetic moments at each Wyckoff position for the alloy.

caption: Time-dependent electric current measurements for FCDI stacks configured with 3D-printed and CNC-milled flow channels, evaluated at a 10 wt% YP50F electrode loading in a 1.5 g/L NaCl aqueous environment.
summary: Electric current behavior is shown for FCDI stacks operating with 10 wt% YP50F flow electrodes. The plot contrasts the performance of 3D-printed non-conductive, 3D-printed conductive, and CNC-milled graphite flow channels during the desalination of a 1.5 g/L NaCl solution, highlighting the impact of channel material on electrochemical current stability.

caption: Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulation results showing the evolution of the order parameter S(t, T) over time at four distinct temperatures, with solid lines representing the best-fit KJMA model.
summary: This plot displays the time-dependent evolution of the order parameter S from KMC simulations at four different temperatures. The data are fitted with the KJMA model, yielding specific kinetic parameters including a pre-exponential factor of 2.04 × 10^11 Hz, a migration energy of 0.9 eV, and an Avrami exponent of n = 1.

caption: Global research methodology flowchart illustrating the systematic collection of WAAM trajectory elements and the identification of quality assessment criteria.
summary: This flowchart outlines the global research methodology applied to the WAAM deposition process. It details the systematic collection of trajectory-defining elements and the identification of specific criteria used to assess the quality of manufactured parts, ultimately resulting in a comprehensive knowledge mapping of the WAAM additive manufacturing process.

caption: Raman spectroscopic analysis of the sintered gel-casted electrolytes.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is employed to investigate the vibrational modes and chemical bonding environment within the sintered gel-casted electrolytes. This spectral data complements the XRD results, offering insights into the molecular structure and potential phase characteristics of the electrolyte material after the sintering treatment described in the study.

caption: Reflection phase response of Cell 1 across the 79 to 90 GHz frequency range while Cell 2 remains constant.
summary: Displayed is the reflection phase behavior of Cell 1 in the higher frequency band of 79-90 GHz. The results indicate that the phase remains almost unchanged throughout this range when Cell 2 is constant, highlighting the independent control of the meta-atom response across the dual-band reflect array design.

caption: Contour plot mapping the austenite start temperature (As) across different laser power and scanning speed combinations.
summary: Mapping the austenite start temperature (As) against laser power and scanning speed, this contour plot demonstrates the processing window for NiTi alloys. The data reveals that the austenitic phase tends to form under conditions characterized by high laser power and high scanning speed, contrasting with the martensitic phase formation conditions.

caption: Algorithmic flowchart illustrating the generalized quadratic cross-correlation process for time delay estimation.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic steps involved in the generalized quadratic cross-correlation method for time delay estimation. The diagram serves as a foundational representation of the proposed algorithm, which was developed to verify the practicality of the method through subsequent simulation analyses conducted in the study.

caption: Surface plot of cobalt concentration at 100 W laser power, illustrating elemental distribution versus scan speed and distance from the build-up layer.
summary: This surface plot displays cobalt elemental concentration variations at 100 W laser power. It maps the distribution relative to scan speed and distance from the build-up layer, providing a visual representation of how processing parameters influence elemental homogeneity within the material during the build process.

caption: Fracture toughness (K Ic) of CTS samples plotted against the ratio of material contact at the fracture plane.
summary: Fracture toughness values are shown relative to the percentage of void content measured via X-ray CT at the fracture plane. The data reveals that lower K Ic values strongly correlate with specimens manufactured at 240 °C and 280 °C, which exhibit higher void contents of 7.08% and 5.76%, respectively, demonstrating a clear dependence of static toughness on void content.

caption: Calculated trajectories of droplets with a 5π/8 contact angle under zero-gravity conditions.
summary: The trajectory plot for droplets with a 5π/8 contact angle illustrates the effect of electric fields on splash-back behavior. While uncharged droplets rebound and drift away, the application of an electric field to charged droplets effectively pulls them back to the substrate, demonstrating the field's importance in low-wettability conditions.

caption: Comparative analysis of process parameter contributions regarding Burr Width across three distinct machining domains.
summary: This panel illustrates the relative influence of various process parameters on Burr Width across three machining domains. The trends demonstrate a domain-specific evolution of parameter influence, highlighting how different machining conditions contribute uniquely to the resulting burr dimensions as observed in the comparative analysis of the machining process parameters.

caption: Baseline GSLS-I unit cell structure.
summary: This panel depicts the baseline GSLS-I unit cell structure. It provides the starting point for structural reinforcement strategies, which involve adding specific geometric features to the unit cell to mitigate failure modes during initial compression and improve the overall mechanical response of the lattice.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of Sample 8 surface morphology after N = 4 scanning cycles.
summary: Sample 8 surface morphology is captured via confocal microscopy after four scanning cycles. This visualization reflects the melting and flowing processes of the molten metal under laser action, demonstrating the mechanism of shallow surface melting as the material responds to the thermal energy applied during the scanning process.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) evolution over time for H13-550/4h specimen subjected to a 9.8 N applied load.
summary: This plot illustrates the temporal evolution of the coefficient of friction for the H13-550/4h material during a wear test conducted at a 9.8 N load. It provides critical data on the frictional behavior of the specimen under these specific experimental conditions as part of the broader wear process analysis.

caption: 3D topography of Ti-S small square patterns deposited via CSAM.
summary: Confocal microscopy reveals the 3D topography of Ti-S small square patterns fabricated using CSAM. This visualization allows for the assessment of deposit homogeneity and flow-field dimensions, providing a detailed characterization of the surface profile and structural characteristics of the deposited pins within the specified pattern geometry.

caption: UV-Vis spectroscopic analysis of gallic acid-conjugated hyaluronic acid (HA-GA) identifying the first pKa value of 5.85, corresponding to the deprotonation of the phenolic hydroxyl group at the para position.
summary: UV-Vis spectroscopy was employed to characterize the chemical properties of HA-GA conjugates. The analysis identified a spectral shift corresponding to the first pKa value of 5.85, which is attributed to the deprotonation of the phenolic hydroxyl group located at the para position of the aromatic ring in the GA moiety.

caption: Reflection spectra of opal films fabricated via the melt-shear technique, with colored circles indicating the visual appearance of films with varying ALMA content.
summary: Reflection spectra demonstrate the optical properties of opal films prepared using the melt-shear technique. The data indicates that reducing the ALMA content from 10 wt% to 7.5 wt% or 5 wt% is feasible, as the resulting films exhibit only minor changes in color quality, maintaining their structural integrity and optical performance.

caption: Naive deposition strategy illustrating sequential feature printing with fixed starting points and consistent scanning directions.
summary: This schematic depicts a naive deposition strategy where features are printed sequentially. The tool path is represented by dashed lines, with arrows indicating scanning directions. Starting points are marked with circles and kept constant for structural integrity, though this approach lacks the spatial distribution optimization found in more advanced methods.

caption: Cross-section of a printed H-ABS specimen showing characteristic inter-raster voids.
summary: This panel illustrates the cross-section of a printed H-ABS specimen, highlighting the presence of inter-raster voids. These structural features are consistent across the printed samples and are responsible for the observed reduction in load transfer efficiency between the rasters in the final printed components.

caption: Calculated Al–Ni binary phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic equilibrium states across varying compositions and temperatures as determined by Yang et al.
summary: This figure presents the calculated Al–Ni binary phase diagram, which provides a comprehensive overview of the thermodynamic equilibrium states for the system. The diagram, originally developed by Yang et al., maps the phase stability across different compositions and temperatures, serving as a fundamental reference for understanding the Al–Ni material system.

caption: Equilibrium solidification path and volumetric phase percentage for Ti–42Nb+1.0C computed via CALPHAD methods.
summary: The CALPHAD-derived diagram for the Ti–42Nb+1.0C composition displays the predicted solidification path and the corresponding volumetric percentage of phases under equilibrium conditions. This computational model serves to characterize the thermodynamic behavior and phase distribution expected during the cooling process of this specific metal matrix composite formulation.

caption: Punch displacement versus temperature plot for the TNTH sample during the sintering process.
summary: This panel displays the punch displacement as a function of temperature for the TNTH sample during sintering. The plot illustrates the dimensional changes occurring in the material as it is heated, providing a baseline for comparing the sintering behavior of the base alloy against the molybdenum-modified compositions.

caption: Geometric phase analysis (GPA) mapping profile of the εxx strain component in the 1# specimen.
summary: The geometric phase analysis mapping profile displays the local εxx strain distribution within the 1# specimen. By quantifying local lattice distortions, this map provides insight into the strain state of the material, complementing the dislocation distribution data derived from the same high-resolution TEM observations.

caption: EPMA elemental mapping of the second corrosion characteristic, highlighting the precipitation of Cr2O3.
summary: EPMA mapping analysis of the second corrosion characteristic demonstrates the chemical environment surrounding the precipitates. The results indicate that gray Cr2O3 is precipitated adjacent to the AlN phases. This mapping provides clear evidence of the oxidation products formed during the intergranular corrosion process described in panel (b).

caption: Fitted parameters derived from the electrical equivalent circuit model for MoldJet 316L samples extracted from top, middle, and bottom build regions.
summary: Fitted parameters for the electrical equivalent circuit model are presented for samples from each build region. These values, derived from the best-fit model with a chi-square value below 10^-3, quantify the electrochemical characteristics of the MoldJet 316L samples, supporting the observation of consistent surface layer properties across all heights.

caption: Reflectance map for the TM polarization mode under multi-angle incidence, showing stable absorption characteristics across a broad range of frequencies and angles.
summary: Under the TM horizontal polarization mode, the reflectance map shows that the reflection coefficient gradually decreases as the incident angle increases from 0° to 45°. This trend demonstrates enhanced absorption performance and confirms that the metastructure maintains stable absorption characteristics across a wide range of frequencies and incident angles.

caption: SHAP summary diagram illustrating the influence of various printed variables on the green part output.
summary: This SHAP summary diagram visualizes the influence of different printed variables on the green part output. Based on the model's training outcomes, the plot provides a comprehensive overview of how specific input variables contribute to the final model predictions, highlighting the relative impact of each parameter on the green part quality.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel, illustrating output power variations across different temperature settings.
summary: Representing the P-V characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel, this panel shows how output power fluctuates with voltage at different temperatures. By utilizing the PEC2 model, the plot provides a clear comparison between the calculated power output and the actual measured values, highlighting the model's accuracy in predicting thermal effects.

caption: FT-IR imaging map of a titanium sample surface modified with CIPRO, displaying the distribution of chemical bands in the 1510–1435 cm⁻¹ range.
summary: FT-IR imaging of a titanium sample surface modified with CIPRO is shown, focusing on the 1510–1435 cm⁻¹ spectral range. This mapping provides insight into the surface topography and chemical composition after the final modification step, demonstrating the spatial distribution of the CIPRO agent on the solid titanium cube surface.

caption: Optical micrograph of the Fe–Mn–Si SMA sample fabricated via LPBF at a VED of 69 J/mm³.
summary: Optical microscopy of the Fe–Mn–Si SMA sample fabricated at a VED of 69 J/mm³ displays a dense microstructure. Non-molten or insufficient molten regions are entirely absent, and only a small number of spherical pores remain, indicating that the high energy input successfully achieves a more uniform and consolidated material state.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profiles displaying the signal intensity of specific oxide anions including 18O-, Cr2-, Ni2-, OH-, and O2- measured on the initial surface state of the alloy 690 steam generator tube.
summary: ToF-SIMS analysis was utilized to characterize the native oxide layer on the alloy 690 steam generator tube. Panel a presents the depth profiles for specific oxide anions, including 18O-, Cr2-, Ni2-, OH-, and O2-, providing essential data on the chemical composition and thickness of the initial surface oxide state.

caption: Refractive index values for AlxGa1-xAsySb1-y alloys lattice-matched to GaSb, plotted as a function of wavelength with Al content varying from 0 to 1 in increments of 0.1.
summary: This panel displays the refractive index profiles for AlxGa1-xAsySb1-y alloys lattice-matched to GaSb. The data covers a range of aluminum compositions from 0 to 1, incremented by 0.1 steps. These modeled interpolations provide essential optical constants for characterizing the material system across the specified compositional range.

caption: Detailed FTIR spectral interval from 1750 to 2450 cm⁻¹ showing trace Si–H vibrational bands in the 2100–2360 cm⁻¹ range for consolidated samples.
summary: This panel presents an enlarged FTIR spectral interval between 1750 and 2450 cm⁻¹. It reveals the presence of Si–H vibrational bands located in the 2100–2360 cm⁻¹ range. These signals indicate trace amounts of silicon-hydrogen species within the consolidated Ti–Nb–Mo samples, exhibiting lower transmittance compared to primary metallic oxide bonds.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the heat-treated Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy.
summary: The IPF map for the heat-treated Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy displays the modified microstructure following thermal processing. This map captures the changes in α variant orientation resulting from the decomposition of acicular α′ phases into α and discontinuous β phases, highlighting the evolution of the alloy's crystallographic texture after heat treatment.

caption: EDX line scan profile across the oxide-matrix interface of the PM-HIP specimen after 1000 h of LBE exposure.
summary: PM-HIP specimen interface characterization using EDX line scanning demonstrates the elemental distribution after 1000 hours of LBE exposure. Comparative analysis indicates that this sample exhibits the highest extent of Ni, Cr, and Fe dissolution into the LBE environment among the four investigated specimen processing conditions.

caption: EBSD IPF map of tensile specimen TB1 after fracture at the interface, showing the termination of long IN718 columnar grains.
summary: Post-fracture analysis of specimen TB1 reveals the interface where failure occurred. The EBSD map shows the termination of long IN718 columnar grains at the fracture site. This observation supports the finding that fracture sites coincide with the termination of these columnar structures at the interface after tensile testing.

caption: Fast-Fourier transformation pattern of the FCC–D019 interface, revealing a Shoji–Nishiyama orientation relationship between the {111}FCC and {0002}HCP close-packed planes.
summary: The FFT pattern from the interface region demonstrates that the FCC matrix and D019 phase maintain a specific Shoji–Nishiyama orientation relationship. This is evidenced by the alignment of their respective close-packed planes, specifically the {111} planes of the FCC matrix and the {0002} planes of the HCP-based D019 structure.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the AB + HT alloy before deformation, revealing lamellae with dark contrast.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the AB + HT alloy prior to deformation. The image highlights the presence of distinct lamellae characterized by a dark contrast, providing an initial overview of the material's structural state before any mechanical testing or further processing is applied.

caption: Body-centred cubic (BCC) unit cell geometry used for lattice construction.
summary: The body-centred cubic (BCC) unit cell is depicted as a fundamental building block for constructing functionally graded lattice structures. This topology serves as one of the three primary unit cell designs employed to engineer the proposed lattice architectures, providing a specific geometric configuration for structural analysis and material design.

caption: Normalized room-temperature photoluminescence (PL) and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectra of HDPE, showing a low-intensity emission at 370 nm and a structured blue emission with peaks at 411, 435, 464.5, 498, and 537 nm under 325 nm excitation.
summary: Normalized room-temperature PL and PLE spectra of HDPE are presented. Excitation at 325 nm reveals a low-intensity emission at 370 nm, followed by a dominant, well-structured blue luminescence with multiple maxima. These peaks exhibit vibronic sidebands separated by approximately 180 meV, corresponding to CH2 bending vibrations within the polymer structure.

caption: Metallic component 3D scan displaying substantial torsional distortion after fabrication with a constant printing direction, 0.1 mm layer height, and 60 mm/s printing speed.
summary: Metallic component analysis via 3D scanning reveals clear deviations from the intended CAD geometry when using a constant printing direction. With a layer height of 0.1 mm and a printing speed of 60 mm/s, the resulting structure exhibits pronounced torsional distortion, indicating suboptimal control over the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Temperature-dependent average magnetic moment of single-layer GeN predicted via Monte Carlo simulation, with an inset showing the specific heat capacity (CV) versus temperature.
summary: Monte Carlo simulations are used to predict the average magnetic moment of single-layer GeN as a function of temperature. The accompanying inset displays the specific heat capacity curve, providing further insight into the thermal properties and magnetic phase transition behavior of the single-layer material.

caption: Schematic representation of the shear test assembly used to evaluate the mechanical performance of the brazed joint.
summary: The schematic diagram depicts the experimental setup for the shear test assembly. This configuration is designed to evaluate the mechanical integrity and shear strength of the brazed joint, providing a standardized method for assessing the bonding performance between the SiCf/SiC composites and the GH536 superalloy using the high-entropy alloy filler.

caption: Constant potential amperometry at E = +0.25 V vs PLA-CB for as-printed eF 4 D (black) and activated eF 4 D EC-20 (blue) electrodes, measured at increasing flow rates.
summary: Constant potential amperometry is performed at +0.25 V vs PLA-CB to compare the current response of as-printed and activated eF 4 D electrodes. The data shows how current varies with fluid velocity, confirming the influence of hydrodynamic conditions on the electrochemical activity of the different electrode types.

caption: In situ calorimetry comparison of CAC C$ and A$ 3 systems at varying dosages, illustrating the cumulative heat evolution over time.
summary: This in situ calorimetry comparison evaluates the reaction kinetics of CAC C$ and A$ 3 systems at different dosages. By determining the time at half the cumulative heat value of 1 hour, the reaction half-life is estimated. Results indicate that the CAC C$ reaction half-life increases with higher dosages, suggesting a reaction order n < 1.

caption: Storage and loss modulus evolution for 2 wt% of 3 in 2-HEA/PEGDA 250 resin, plotted against increasing light intensities.
summary: The evolution of storage and loss moduli for the 2 wt% additive 3 formulation is shown here under varying light intensities. This plot tracks the viscoelastic transition of the resin mixture, demonstrating how the curing kinetics are influenced by the light intensity levels applied during the polymerization process.

caption: Hydrogen permeation transients for Alloy 625 measured at 60 °C under a cathodic current density of -20 mA/cm2.
summary: Three consecutive hydrogen permeation transients were recorded for Alloy 625 at 60 °C with a cathodic current density of -20 mA/cm2. The high coincidence of these transients indicates that no irreversibly trapped hydrogen is present in the material, and the data serves as a basis for calculating hydrogen diffusion parameters.

caption: Initial density field ρ representing the starting state of the material model.
summary: The initial density field ρ serves as the baseline state for the subsequent filtering and projection operations. This field represents the starting configuration of the material model before any mathematical transformations are applied to define the eroded, intermediate, or dilated structural features within the simulation framework.

caption: Current-Voltage characteristics of Ti-based TLM structures plotted for varying inter-electrode spacings L.
summary: This panel displays the current-voltage characteristics of Ti-based transmission line model (TLM) structures. The data illustrates how the electrical response of the device changes as a function of the inter-electrode spacing L, providing the foundational measurements required to evaluate the contact and sheet resistance of the material system.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve recorded during heating from room temperature to 1200 °C, utilizing a two-stage heating rate of 20 °C/s up to 700 °C and 10 °C/s thereafter.
summary: This DSC curve illustrates the thermal response of the material during a controlled heating process from room temperature to 1200 °C. The measurement employs a dual-rate heating profile, specifically 20 °C/s up to 700 °C followed by 10 °C/s, providing essential data regarding the dissolution temperature of the γ′ phase.

caption: Bar chart comparing the normalized weight loss of unfilled PP, PP-CF, and PP-GR samples after 10 minutes of isothermal exposure at 230 °C in air.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the thermal degradation behavior of polypropylene composites by comparing normalized weight loss at 230 °C. Results demonstrate that unfilled PP exhibits the highest weight loss, while the incorporation of carbon fibers (CF) or graphite (GR) significantly improves thermal stability, thereby reducing polymer degradation during isothermal exposure.

caption: Overview of the experimental apparatus utilized for evaluating the stiffness of fiber-jamming-based cylindrical structures.
summary: This photograph displays the experimental setup used to evaluate the stiffness variation in fiber-jamming-based cylindrical structures. The image provides a clear view of the physical arrangement required to apply different pressure conditions, serving as the primary platform for conducting the stiffness evaluation experiments described in the study.

caption: Schematic representation of the deep contrastive learning methodology, including contrastive and triplet loss functions, compared against t-SNE clustering for quality monitoring.
summary: This panel illustrates a contrastive learning-based CNN designed to discriminate between stable and defective deposition conditions. The framework utilizes contrastive and triplet loss functions, demonstrating superior feature clustering compared to t-SNE analysis, which achieved only 23.5% accuracy, thereby highlighting the efficiency of the proposed deep learning approach for quality monitoring.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of methylene blue solution in contact with printed glass-based composites under UV light exposure, showing the reduction in absorbance over 60 minutes.
summary: This panel presents the UV-Vis absorption spectra of methylene blue solution while in contact with printed glass-based composites under active UV exposure. The spectra demonstrate the progressive reduction in dye absorbance over a 60-minute period, indicating the photocatalytic degradation of the organic molecules facilitated by the UV-exposed composite structure.

caption: Laser confocal scanning microscopy of rBMSC cytoskeleton and nuclei on scaffolds after 7 days of coculture.
summary: Laser confocal scanning microscopy was utilized to examine the cytoskeleton and cell nuclei of rBMSCs after 7 days of coculture on the porous scaffolds. The resulting images reveal satisfactory cell growth and morphology, confirming that the scaffolds provide a suitable environment for long-term cell adhesion and structural development.

caption: Nyquist plot of impedance spectra normalized by the effective cross-sectional area (A T A), demonstrating the assumed specific normalized solution impedance.
summary: Depicting impedance spectra normalized by the effective cross-sectional area (A T A), this Nyquist plot provides a more accurate assessment of electrochemical impedance. By utilizing this specific normalization method, the plot reveals the assumed specific normalized solution impedance, enabling a more precise interpretation of the electrochemical behavior across different surface roughnesses.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot of g-C3N4 measured at various alternating current potential frequencies.
summary: The Mott-Schottky curve for g-C3N4 exhibits a positive slope, indicating that it functions as an n-type semiconductor. By analyzing the curve under different alternating current potential frequencies, the electronic nature of the material is established, which is critical for evaluating its role within the photocatalytic heterojunction architecture.

caption: Fe 2p core-level XPS spectrum of the CX@Fe monolith, displaying the 2p 1/2 and 2p 3/2 peaks indicative of iron doping within the monolith structure.
summary: Fe 2p core-level spectra for the CX@Fe monolith exhibit the 2p 1/2 and 2p 3/2 peaks, which confirm the successful doping of the monolith with iron. This analysis is part of a broader investigation into the chemical surface composition of the transition metal-doped carbon monoliths presented in the study.

caption: Nyquist plot for SLMed TC4 alloys S7–1H, S8–1H, and S9–1H after 1 h of immersion, representing the third group of process parameters.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of TC4 alloys S7–1H, S8–1H, and S9–1H after 1 h of immersion. The data is part of a comprehensive set of EIS measurements used to analyze the influence of different SLM process parameters on the corrosion resistance of the TC4 alloy specimens.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of S. aureus bacteria stained on PEGDA/GMA flat surfaces, where green indicates live and red indicates dead cells.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy reveals the distribution of S. aureus bacteria on PEGDA/GMA flat surfaces using a LIVE/DEAD assay. Green fluorescence identifies viable bacteria, while red fluorescence marks dead cells. Observations indicate that control PEGDA/GMA surfaces primarily support viable colonies with minimal dead bacteria attached, highlighting the baseline bacterial adhesion characteristics.

caption: Temporal evolution of UV-Vis spectra during 4-NP reduction catalyzed by a 2.5 cm Pd/C CR featuring a 2.8 mm core diameter.
summary: Temporal UV-Vis spectral data demonstrate the reduction of 4-nitrophenol using a Pd/C coaxial reactor with a 2.5 cm length and 2.8 mm core diameter. Linear fitting of these spectral changes enables the calculation of conversion versus time, which is essential for evaluating the impact of core diameter on catalytic performance.

caption: Bode representation of EIS spectra for 3D samples after the anodizing process, compared across inflammatory and severe inflammatory conditions.
summary: Bode plots characterize the impedance spectra of 3D samples post-anodizing treatment. By comparing the response in inflammatory and severe inflammatory conditions, the electrochemical performance of the anodized surface is evaluated. These spectra serve as a basis for determining the fitting parameters related to the anodized sample's electrochemical behavior.

caption: Calculated TTP diagram illustrating the transformation kinetics for the S3 steel variant.
summary: The TTP diagram for the S3 steel is presented here, as simulated by MatCalc. This plot characterizes the time-temperature-precipitation behavior of the alloy, offering insights into the phase transformation kinetics expected during thermal processing of this specific steel composition within the investigated experimental series.

caption: Calculated reaction potentials for redox couples of Ni, Co, and Mn as a function of pH, derived from the Nernst equation.
summary: This panel presents the Pourbaix diagram for Ni and Co, alongside calculated reaction potentials for various redox couples across different pH values. These theoretical values, derived from the Nernst equation and detailed in Table 2, provide the thermodynamic foundation for understanding the electrochemical behavior of the metal ions in the leachate.

caption: Initial strain evolution region for the AD specimen at 0% global strain, with a white dashed line indicating the center of the graded interfacial region.
summary: The initial strain distribution for the AD specimen is captured at 0% global strain. A white dashed line identifies the center of the graded interfacial region, serving as a reference point for observing how local plastic strain redistributes and localizes within the TC4 region below the interface during loading.

caption: Calculated H+ ion implantation profile as a function of target depth for an AM SS target at normal incidence, derived using SRIM simulation software.
summary: This plot illustrates the H+ ion implantation profile within an AM SS target under normal incidence conditions. The data, generated via SRIM simulation, maps the ion concentration as a function of target depth, providing a quantitative assessment of the expected ion distribution within the material structure for experimental analysis.

caption: Magnified digital optical profile (50x) of the adhesive joint at the hard tooth tip for the 11.3° suture frequency, highlighting the interface between the gold-colored soft material and white hard material.
summary: This 50x magnified optical micrograph reveals the adhesive bonding at the hard-phase tooth tip for the 11.3° suture frequency. The image provides a detailed view of the interface between the gold-colored soft material and the white hard material, which is critical for understanding the joint's structural integrity.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping highlighting the chromium distribution across the slag layer surface.
summary: Chromium distribution within the surface slag layer is visualized through energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping. This data confirms the presence of chromium as a key constituent of the Mn-Cr-O spinel oxides identified in the slag layer, contributing to the overall understanding of the oxide composition in the additive material.

caption: Force-displacement response of the DAA structure subjected to annealing and T6 heat treatment processes.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical force-displacement response of the DAA structure following specific post-heat-treatment conditions, namely annealing and T6 treatment. The data provides a comparative view of how these thermal processing routes influence the structural mechanical behavior under load, highlighting the resulting performance characteristics of the material.

caption: STEM-ABF image and corresponding Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) pattern of the selected η-γ interface region.
summary: The STEM-ABF image provides a detailed view of the η-γ interface in the 718Plus sample. The accompanying FFT pattern for the selected area confirms the atomic structural arrangement, facilitating further investigation into the interface interaction mechanism and the lattice strain distribution present after the creep test.

caption: Power-voltage (P–V) characteristics derived from the parameters estimated by the 20 optimization algorithms for the PHOTOWATT-PWP 201 solar panel.
summary: Power-voltage (P-V) curves are presented to demonstrate the performance of the 20 optimization algorithms in modeling the PWP 201 solar panel. These curves are derived from the estimated parameters, allowing for a direct comparison of how effectively each method captures the power output characteristics of the photovoltaic device.
