caption: Transmittance values measured at 405 nm for A-CNC/CTFA composite resins as a function of the acrylation reaction time.
summary: Transmittance at 405 nm for the A-CNC/CTFA composite resin is plotted against acrylation reaction time. The data indicates that increasing the reaction time leads to a progressive improvement in transparency, with values reaching up to 93%, highlighting the direct correlation between reaction duration and optical performance.

caption: Spatial distribution map of Manganese (Mn) concentration relative to the average value in a B-400 W sample prior to heat treatment, with the scan origin centered 4 mm above the bottom edge, indicating build (BD) and melting (MD) directions.
summary: This elemental distribution map illustrates the spatial variation of Manganese within an as-deposited B-400 W sample. Analysis reveals that Mn fluctuations remain within the measurement accuracy of the XRF system, demonstrating high chemical homogeneity across the scanned area before heat treatment, consistent with the observed spatial scales of the sample.

caption: Relative abundance of m/e = 18, 12, and 44 ions, corresponding to H2O, C, and CO2 byproducts, measured via mass spectrometry during heating.
summary: Mass spectrometry data tracks the off-gassing behavior during reductive sintering. Binder decomposition generates pronounced H2O (m/e=18) and C-based byproducts including CO and CO2 (m/e=12 and 44). Following decomposition above 500 °C, the H2O peak provides evidence of deoxidation occurring via H2-based redox reactions.

caption: IPF map of the EQ STA specimen, showing a zigzag crack propagation path through the microstructure.
summary: This IPF map of the EQ STA specimen illustrates a zigzag crack propagation path. The irregular path is attributed to the specific crack propagation resistance of the EQ microstructure. This observation contrasts with the transgranular, flatter paths seen in other specimens, highlighting the influence of microstructure on fatigue failure.

caption: Reflectance spectra of pre-alloyed Ni 52.1 at.% powder samples subjected to thermal treatment across a temperature range from 650 °C to 1450 °C.
summary: This figure presents the reflectance spectra of pre-alloyed Ni 52.1 at.% powder samples that have undergone thermal treatment at various temperatures ranging from 650 °C to 1450 °C. These spectra provide insight into the optical properties of the powder as a function of the applied heat treatment conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy point analysis spectrum detailing the elemental composition of phase B.
summary: The EDS spectrum shown here characterizes the elemental composition of phase B, located in the interdendritic region. This analysis is essential for distinguishing the various precipitates found in the as-cast EBS Ni-Co superalloy, as part of the broader investigation into the material's complex phase distribution.

caption: Angled view of the reconstructed volume of a 20 at% Ag PVD sample, featuring dimensions of 2 μm width, 750 nm depth, and 300 nm height.
summary: This panel shows an angled view of the reconstructed volume for a 20 at% Ag PVD sample. The reconstruction covers a specific region with dimensions of 2 μm width, 750 nm depth, and 300 nm height, providing a clear 3D representation of the Ag structures within the PVD-deposited material.

caption: Stress intensity factors derived from near-tip stress measurements for a specimen containing a 7.4 mm crack during thermal shock.
summary: This plot displays the stress intensity factors calculated from near-tip stress measurements for a specimen with a 7.4 mm crack subjected to thermal shock. The data illustrates the evolution of these factors during the thermal loading process, with threshold values indicated to characterize the fracture behavior of the cracked specimen.

caption: Calculated fcc composition profiles for Al10.5Co25Fe39.5Ni25, mapping the relative distance from the dendrite core to the interdendritic region.
summary: Calculated composition profiles for the fcc phase in Al10.5Co25Fe39.5Ni25 illustrate the spatial distribution of elements from the dendrite core to the interdendritic region. These profiles provide insight into the chemical homogeneity and solute partitioning behavior within the microstructure during the solidification process of the selected alloy composition.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the Invar 36 alloy processed via Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF).
summary: This panel displays the XRD pattern for Invar 36 alloy fabricated using the LPBF additive manufacturing process. As a rapid forming technique, LPBF involves non-equilibrium solidification, which influences the resulting crystalline structure of the alloy compared to traditional manufacturing methods like casting or forging.

caption: Sensitivity indices for the δ phase in AB alloy 718, demonstrating that independent variations in Ni and Al concentrations account for 55% and 26% of the phase fraction variance, respectively.
summary: Sensitivity analysis for the δ phase reveals significant dependencies on alloy composition. Specifically, independent changes in the nickel (Ni) and aluminum (Al) concentrations are shown to introduce variance in the δ phase fraction by approximately 55% and 26%, respectively, highlighting their critical roles in phase stability.

caption: Al 2p high-resolution XPS spectrum showing three distinct peaks at 67.5 eV, 68.1 eV, and 73.3 eV, corresponding to Al 2p and Al2O3 2p.
summary: The Al 2p high-resolution XPS spectrum of the DD6BM superalloy reveals three distinct peaks at binding energies of 67.5 eV, 68.1 eV, and 73.3 eV. The first two peaks are attributed to Al 2p, while the 73.3 eV peak corresponds to Al2O3 2p, indicating the presence of aluminum oxide in the passive film.

caption: Box-and-whisker plots illustrating the dried volume of jetted carbon and AgNP inks after 500 drops at 25 °C, accompanied by representative images of the printed spots.
summary: At 25 °C, both carbon and AgNP inks exhibit stable jetting performance, characterized by interquartile ranges well below 10%. The box-and-whisker plots demonstrate consistent dried volumes across various idle durations, confirming that ambient temperature conditions maintain jetting stability for these materials during the printing process.

caption: Energy storage modulus (E') profiles of CP-PLA composites processed at different preparation temperatures.
summary: This panel illustrates the energy storage modulus of CP-PLA composites as a function of varying PS preparation temperatures. The data provides insight into how thermal processing conditions during the preparation phase affect the viscoelastic properties and the resulting storage modulus of the final composite material structure.

caption: Deconvolution of the 29Si MAS NMR spectrum for potassium-activated slag 3 paste with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 2.15.
summary: The 29Si MAS NMR spectrum for the potassium-activated slag 3 paste with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 2.15 shows significant broadening compared to the original slag. Deconvolution analysis identifies resonances corresponding to (1Al) and (2Al) configurations, indicating that the activation process modifies the silicon environment through increased aluminum coordination.

caption: Raman spectra of NiAlxFe2-xO4 spinel catalysts with x = 0, 1, and 2, synthesized using nitrate salt precursors.
summary: This figure displays the Raman spectra for NiAlxFe2-xO4 spinel catalysts, specifically those prepared from nitrate precursors for compositions x = 0, 1, and 2. These spectroscopic measurements characterize the vibrational modes of the spinel structure, providing insight into the structural influence of varying aluminum and iron content within the catalyst series.

caption: Quantified cross-sectional area of the melt pool calculated from 50 observed cross-sections.
summary: This plot illustrates the distribution of the melt pool cross-sectional area based on 50 analyzed cross-sections. As a primary geometric value, the area provides insight into the overall size and energy distribution within the melt pool, supporting the comprehensive geometric characterization presented in the study.

caption: Surface topography of F30C70 Y2O3 ceramic sintered at 1700 °C, revealing the surface morphology of the 30% additive grade.
summary: The surface topography of F30C70 Y2O3 ceramic sintered at 1700 °C is displayed. This evaluation is integral to understanding the surface roughness evolution in sintered Y2O3 cores, which acts as a critical factor for ensuring optimal surface finish quality during the casting of titanium components.

caption: Repose angle measurement of the powder feedstock.
summary: Repose angle measurement of the powder feedstock. The repose angle of the powder was determined to be 51.7° ± 3.4°. This specific value indicates a relatively low flowability for the material, providing a quantitative assessment of the powder's handling characteristics based on the measured angle of repose.

caption: Manual annotation of nine major cell clusters identified within the primary PDAC lesion based on specific marker gene expression profiles.
summary: Nine distinct cell clusters are displayed and manually annotated in this panel. These clusters were identified based on marker gene expression, providing a detailed breakdown of the cellular composition within the primary PDAC lesion and facilitating the subsequent identification of specific cancer stem cell populations.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the NiW-3 coating surface following two days of immersion in a NaCl solution.
summary: Captured via scanning electron microscopy, this image illustrates the NiW-3 coating surface after two days of exposure to a NaCl solution. The micrograph documents the progression of surface changes and structural evolution of the coating material as it undergoes immersion, providing insight into the early stages of environmental interaction.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetic entropy change ΔSm(T) curves for bamboo-grained microwires under various fields, featuring a tiny positive entropy peak at low fields and the full width at half maximum δTFWHM indicated at 5 T.
summary: Temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change ΔSm(T) curves are plotted for bamboo-grained microwires under magnetic fields up to 5 T. A tiny positive entropy peak is observed at low fields, while the full width at half maximum δTFWHM is marked at 5 T to characterize the magnetocaloric effect performance.

caption: Compressive strength versus density diagram for the 200 °C condition, highlighting the Al80Mg10Si5Cu5 alloy in green to demonstrate its superior balance of properties.
summary: Representing the compressive strength and density relationship for the Al80Mg10Si5Cu5 alloy treated at 200 °C, this plot identifies the material with a green marker. The data confirms that this specific alloy achieves the best balance between density and compressive strength when compared to other multi-component aluminium alloys reported in literature.

caption: GND density distribution map of the HT2 specimen subjected to a 0.8% strain amplitude.
summary: Visualized here is the GND density distribution for the HT2 specimen at a 0.8% strain amplitude. The average GND density is 4.9 × 10^14 m^-2. Observations indicate the presence of alternating high-density dislocation zones and dislocation-free zones, with the latter becoming more prominent compared to lower strain amplitudes.

caption: Energy absorption efficiency as a function of strain rate for the micro-honeycomb structure developed in this study.
summary: Energy absorption efficiency is plotted against strain rate to characterize the mechanical performance of the micro-honeycomb structure. This graph illustrates how the efficiency of the material changes under different dynamic loading conditions, offering insight into the energy dissipation characteristics of the micro-honeycomb design across the tested range of strain rates.

caption: Dielectric permittivity of in situ 3D-printed PVDF nanocomposite foams measured within the frequency range of 10^1 to 10^5 Hz.
summary: This plot depicts the broadband real permittivity of in situ 3D-printed PVDF nanocomposite foams measured between 10^1 and 10^5 Hz. The measurements characterize the dielectric properties of the foamed nanocomposite structures across the specified frequency spectrum.

caption: Loss factor (tan δ) versus temperature for pure PA12 and composites, illustrating damping properties.
summary: Loss factor (tan δ) versus temperature plots are used to evaluate the damping properties and energy dissipation capabilities of pure PA12 and its composites. These DMA curves highlight the material's viscoelastic behavior, providing a clear indication of how energy is dissipated as heat during cyclic thermal loading conditions.

caption: Principal component analysis of spatter ejection velocity data, where individual samples are color-coded to represent varying ejection velocities.
summary: This PCA plot visualizes the spatter ejection velocity dataset, with samples colored by their respective velocities. The first two principal components capture over 95% of the total variance, demonstrating that this dimensionality reduction effectively represents the underlying data structure and provides strong explanatory power for the observed spatter behavior.

caption: Load versus displacement curves for the surface white layer, showing a maximum penetration depth of 370 nm at a 20 mN load.
summary: Load-displacement curves obtained from nano-indentation testing on the surface white layer indicate a maximum penetration depth of 370 nm under a 20 mN load. This depth exceeds the 10% threshold relative to the polished layer thickness, yet remains within a reliable range for accurate mechanical characterization of the material.

caption: Tornado-style sensitivity chart quantifying the impact of ±10-20% variations in welding and microstructural parameters on predicted fatigue life.
summary: This sensitivity analysis uses a tornado chart to evaluate how fluctuations in key parameters, including heat input, travel speed, interlayer thickness, preheat, and cooling rate, influence fatigue life. The results identify welding heat input and travel speed as the dominant drivers affecting the predicted fatigue performance of the joint.

caption: Comprehensive overview of the research workflow illustrating the sequential steps and methodology employed in the study.
summary: This figure presents a complete overview of the research workflow, serving as a methodological guide for the study. It outlines the systematic progression of the work, providing a clear visual representation of the procedural steps and the overall experimental or analytical framework adopted to achieve the research objectives.

caption: Bright-field TEM image illustrating rod-shaped Mg17Al12 precipitates observed within the Mg matrix of the T6-state AE81 alloy.
summary: This BF-TEM image reveals rod-shaped Mg17Al12 precipitates dispersed within the Mg matrix of the T6-state AE81 alloy. Along with plate-shaped variants, these rod-shaped precipitates are observed throughout the matrix, demonstrating the diverse range of precipitate morphologies that form during the T6 heat treatment process in this specific alloy.

caption: Deep contrastive learning methodology schematic showing contrastive and triplet loss functions, alongside a t-SNE visualization demonstrating superior feature clustering for quality monitoring compared to standard approaches.
summary: This panel presents a contrastive learning-based CNN architecture designed to classify stable versus defective deposition conditions. The methodology utilizes contrastive and triplet loss functions to achieve clear feature clustering. Comparison with t-SNE analysis highlights the superior separability and efficiency of the proposed model over conventional classification techniques.

caption: Dark field transmission electron microscopy image of the Ti 48.5 Ni 41 Co 9 Nb 1.5 alloy, generated using the encircled diffuse scattering intensity identified in the diffraction pattern.
summary: The dark field TEM image reveals the presence of bright, particle-like dots within the microstructure of the Ti 48.5 Ni 41 Co 9 Nb 1.5 alloy. These features, observed near 1/3[110] B2 positions, indicate that the addition of 1.5 at. % Nb effectively suppresses the B2 to R-phase martensitic transformation.

caption: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) heatmap illustrating the correlation strength between various features relevant to fatigue life prediction.
summary: This heatmap displays the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) for features used in fatigue life prediction models. Analysis indicates that specimen state, applied stress amplitude, effective defect area, and the distance of the defect center to the surface are uncorrelated features, confirming their suitability for inclusion in the developed machine learning models.

caption: Magnetic field line configuration after magnetizing the sample in a 1.4 T field applied in a North upward direction.
summary: Magnetization in a 1.4 T North upward field maintains the existing south and north orientation of the central zones. However, the maximum magnetic remanence increases significantly, reaching 50 mT and 30 mT in the north and south pole regions of the central NdFeB matrix, respectively.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography of the electrolessly plated nickel surface on Plexiglas®, highlighting the modified surface morphology.
summary: Atomic force microscopy of the electrolessly plated surface reveals the topographical changes resulting from the nickel deposition. This image confirms the presence of a metallic film on the functionalized Plexiglas® substrate, providing a direct comparison to the pristine surface and illustrating the structural transformation achieved after the immersion process.

caption: High-speed observation of droplet ejection from the liquid surface, highlighting elongated, high-velocity streaks that are potentially indicative of cavitation-driven phenomena.
summary: This optical micrograph captures the ejection of droplets from the liquid surface during ultrasonic excitation. The presence of elongated, high-velocity streaks, distinct from near-spherical droplets, suggests that cavitation effects contribute to the ejection process. These observations provide evidence for the role of cavitation in influencing droplet dynamics at higher power levels.

caption: Moisture diffusion kinetics of polyamide exposed to 80% relative humidity, plotted as absorbed moisture content versus the square root of time.
summary: Polyamide moisture diffusion at 80% relative humidity is characterized by absorbed moisture content plotted against the square root of time. The data follows Fickian diffusion behavior, starting with a rapid, linear absorption phase followed by a slower, non-linear transition toward a stable equilibrium state, indicating the material reaches saturation.

caption: X-ray intensity map of Si K distribution, highlighting the alignment of silicon-rich precipitates along the cantilever long axis.
summary: The Si K X-ray intensity map highlights the distribution of silicon across the cantilever surface. Silicon-rich precipitates are observed to align along the long axis of the cantilever, consistent with the precipitate cell structure documented in the material, which influences the crack propagation path through these brittle interspersed features.

caption: Site-projected and spin-separated total density of states (t-DOS) for a Cr atom (red) and a Ni atom (blue) on the (100) surface of a spin-polarized Ni substrate, with the Fermi energy set to zero.
summary: This plot displays the site-projected total density of states for Cr and Ni atoms on a spin-polarized Ni(100) surface. The Cr atom exhibits a high abundance of unoccupied spin-up states above the Fermi level, while the Ni atom shows significant occupied spin-up and spin-down states below the Fermi level with minimal unoccupied states.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements acquired for as-built samples in solution S2, with orientations parallel (XZ) and perpendicular (XY) to the printing direction.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements in solution S2 evaluate the stability of the superficial oxide layer on as-built samples. Comparing these spectra with those from solution S1 indicates that the oxide layer exhibits lower stability in S2, highlighting the influence of the electrolyte composition on the electrochemical behavior of the material.

caption: Projected density of states for Fe, O, and Zr atoms at the Fe/ZrO2 interface.

caption: Bragg edge ratio of H sample to H powder for (111) and (200) planes in the bilayer Fe(316L)/CuCrZr sample, measured along the TD2 and BD directions.
summary: This panel displays the Bragg edge ratio for (111) and (200) planes in the Fe(316L)/CuCrZr bilayer sample. Measurements were taken along the TD2 and BD directions to evaluate crystallographic texture. The data provides a quantitative basis for assessing texture alignment when compared with EBSD results in the subsequent panel.

caption: Comparison of Raman spectra for as-printed microstructures and those exposed to O2 plasma for 10 and 40 minutes, highlighting the absence of D and G peaks in the 1300–1600 cm⁻¹ range.
summary: This panel displays Raman spectra comparing as-printed microstructures with samples exposed to O2 plasma for 10 and 40 minutes. The results demonstrate the absence of graphitic or disordered carbon, as no D or G peaks are detected in the 1300–1600 cm⁻¹ region, indicating structural stability under plasma exposure.

caption: Cross-sectional morphology of Wrought-316L SS nitrided at 400 °C, showing significant layer discontinuities and spalling on the equiaxed grain substrate.
summary: Optical microscopy of the Wrought-316L SS nitrided at 400 °C reveals a thin, uneven nitrided layer with severe local discontinuities and spalling. The substrate is composed of uniformly distributed equiaxed grains. These structural defects in the nitrided layer are consistent with the challenges observed in the wrought material under these specific nitriding temperature conditions.

caption: Relative density measurements obtained via Archimedes’ principle plotted against varying PBF-LB/M processing parameters.
summary: This plot illustrates the distribution of relative density measurements for samples fabricated via PBF-LB/M. By utilizing Archimedes’ principle, the data maps density variations across the evaluated processing parameter matrix. These results serve as a baseline for comparing porosity trends with other material properties like grain size and maximum pore diameter.

caption: Strain distribution map of a 60% infill PICN sample at the fracture point.
summary: This DIC strain map reveals the strain distribution of a 60% infill PICN sample at the fracture point. The visualization is instrumental in understanding the failure mechanisms of the PICN material, showing how strain is distributed throughout the structure just before the final failure occurs.

caption: Magnified atom probe tomography reconstruction of a region containing Al, B, and C-rich phases, displaying atomic positions of Ni, Al, Co, Cr, W, Ti, Ta, Hf, Mo, Zr, C, and B from 450 to 650 nm, with surfaces marking specific concentration thresholds for Al, Cr, W, Ti, Ta, and Hf.
summary: This magnified atom probe tomography reconstruction displays a complex region containing Al, B, and C-rich phases. Atomic positions for multiple elements including Ni, Al, Co, Cr, W, Ti, Ta, Hf, Mo, Zr, C, and B are mapped between 450 and 650 nm, with isoconcentration surfaces identifying distinct elemental enrichment zones.

caption: SEM micrograph revealing the γ′ phase morphology of the 2.72 wt.% Ta alloy after solution treatment at 1240 °C and aging.
summary: Representing the highest solution temperature of 1240 °C for the 2.72 wt.% Ta alloy, this SEM image demonstrates the resulting γ′ phase morphology. The cubicity of the γ′ phase is notably reduced at this temperature, confirming the established trend that higher solution temperatures lead to decreased cubicity in this specific alloy composition.

caption: Yield stress radar plot for composites with face-to-core ratios ranging from 0 to 0.8, highlighting performance relative to the monolithic core material.
summary: Yield stress values for composites with face-to-core ratios between 0 and 0.8 are displayed in this radar plot. The gray region denotes the monolithic core performance, and color-coded percentages indicate the relative yield stress of each multi-material configuration, providing a consistent basis for evaluating material selection under tensile loading.

caption: Micro-CT visualization of internal defect distribution within the PLA specimen.
summary: Micro-CT imaging reveals the internal morphology of the PLA specimen, demonstrating a widespread distribution of defects. The defect density is notably higher in the middle section of the specimen, attributed to uneven material accumulation and rapid direction changes during the printing process across the upper, middle, and bottom regions.

caption: Microstructure of Hastelloy N after exposure to pure FLiBe salt, showing a uniform surface without a distinct reaction layer.
summary: Hastelloy N exposed to pure FLiBe salt exhibits a uniform microstructure at the surface. Unlike samples treated with additional beryllium, this specimen shows no evidence of a modified surface layer, confirming that the absence of extra beryllium prevents the formation of the reaction product observed in other conditions.

caption: Nyquist plots for rolled TA31, SLM TA31-1000, and SLM TA31-900 alloys in simulated seawater, featuring an equivalent circuit model.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of rolled TA31, SLM TA31-1000, and SLM TA31-900 in simulated seawater. The semicircular capacitive loop size follows the order SLM TA31-900 > rolled TA31 > SLM TA31-1000. An equivalent circuit model is utilized to further investigate the corrosion resistance of these three TA31 alloys.

caption: 3D profilometer optical micrograph showing the surface morphology of the Si3N4 ball counterpart after a 30 N wear test.
summary: This 3D profilometer optical micrograph displays the surface morphology of a Si3N4 ball counterpart following a 30 N wear test. Characterization via this technique, integrated with a tribometer, reveals the absence of a substantial material transfer layer on the ball surface after the contact sliding process.

caption: Pseudo-time analysis of iPSCs and endoderm lineage cells categorized by specific cell types.
summary: This panel categorizes iPSCs and endoderm lineage cells to visualize their specific positions within the pseudo-time framework. The investigation demonstrates that precursor cells located in the apical areas of several branches are responsible for the formation of alveolar cells and mature endocrine cells during the differentiation process.

caption: Surface plot representing the specific energy absorption (SEA) values influenced by fold angle and relative density.
summary: This surface plot visualizes the specific energy absorption (SEA) across different fold angles and relative densities. A specific region characterized by the darkest shades indicates SEA values falling within the range of 17.6 J/g to 19 J/g, demonstrating the energy absorption performance under varying structural parameters.

caption: Comparison of measured crack growth rates against Model 2 predictions for IP-TMF tests across the 100–850 °C temperature range, with hold times of 1 h and 6 h.
summary: Panel b illustrates the crack growth rate versus ΔK eff for IP-TMF tests at temperatures between 100 and 850 °C, evaluating the accuracy of Model 2. The graph contrasts measured data with predicted values for both 1 h and 6 h hold times, providing a visual assessment of the model's predictive performance.

caption: Storage modulus curves for PEKK/LRS composites in amorphous and annealed states, showing a sharp decline near the glass transition region.
summary: Storage modulus curves for PEKK/LRS composites illustrate the thermomechanical response across varying filler contents. In the amorphous state, samples exhibit a sharp decline in modulus as temperatures approach the glass transition region (∼150–160 °C), indicating significant softening. Annealed samples demonstrate enhanced thermal stability compared to their amorphous counterparts.

caption: Tafel polarization curves comparing the electrochemical behavior of the monolithic FeCoCrNiMo HEA coating and the FeCoCrNiMo HEA/CNTs composite coating.
summary: Tafel polarization curves reveal distinct electrochemical differences between the monolithic HEA coating and the HEA/CNTs composite. Although the composite coating demonstrates a cathodic shift in corrosion potential compared to the monolithic HEA, this shift does not necessarily imply inferior corrosion resistance, highlighting the complex electrochemical response of the composite material.

caption: Cleaved grain boundary structure model, where colored circular outlines denote distinct atomic layers along the in-plane dimension.
summary: Depicted is the cleaved grain boundary structure used to calculate the work of separation. The atomic layers are distinguished by colored circular outlines in the in-plane dimension. This configuration, containing the same number of atoms as the intact grain boundary, is essential for evaluating the energy required for grain separation.

caption: Ensemble mean normalised OH-PLIF images of C2H4-CF3Br premixed flames, illustrating the spatial distribution of OH radicals as the inhibitor volume fraction increases.
summary: Ensemble mean OH-PLIF images, averaged over 500 frames, visualize the C2H4 flame structure under varying CF3Br inhibitor concentrations. The images demonstrate a clear shortening of the flame length as inhibitor volume fraction increases, providing insight into the chemical response of the flame front towards blow-off conditions.

caption: Structural diagram of a compression-dominated beam design, utilizing arch-like geometry to minimize tensile stress.
summary: This panel illustrates a compression-dominated structural design, such as an arch bridge. By focusing on geometry that promotes predominantly compressive forces, this method reduces the reliance on tensile strength, as exemplified by existing unreinforced structures like the Striatus bridge and various arch bridge designs fabricated by researchers.

caption: Nyquist plots of Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings and the 2Cr13 substrate, showing single, nearly semicircular capacitive arcs.
summary: Nyquist plots for the Ti0.1, Ti0.2, and Ti0.15 coatings and the 2Cr13 substrate are displayed. The coatings exhibit single, nearly semicircular capacitive arcs, which are characteristic of stable passive films formed on their surfaces, indicating effective corrosion resistance and stable electrochemical behavior across the tested coating compositions.

caption: Scanning probe microscopy (SPM) force map for LPBF IN718 in the horizontal (X–Y) orientation.
summary: Visualizing the indentation sites on the horizontal X–Y plane, this SPM force map confirms the presence of secondary phases near the indents. These features are shown to correlate with the hardness variations observed in the XPM map, providing insight into how the LPBF microstructure dictates local mechanical behavior in this orientation.

caption: Failed specimens, DIC strain maps, and micro-CT cross-sectional slices of PL-PLA and PL-CFRCs.
summary: This panel displays failed specimens, DIC strain maps, and micro-CT slices for PL-PLA and PL-CFRCs. These materials exhibit homogeneous internal structures, resulting in negligible differences in CT slices across various locations. The visual data provides a comprehensive overview of the failure modes and internal structural integrity of these specific material systems.

caption: Hardness distribution profile measured across the as-welded joint for different welding processes.
summary: This figure illustrates the microhardness distribution across the as-welded joint for various welding processes. The data provides a comparative analysis of the mechanical properties resulting from different fabrication techniques, serving as a primary indicator of the joint's structural integrity and consistency across the weld zone and base material interfaces.

caption: Positional error distribution histogram for a conformal cooling system.
summary: The positional error distribution for a conformal cooling system is shown in this histogram. The data confirms that the implementation of conformal cooling leads to a significant reduction in positional error distributions compared to conventional cooling methods, highlighting the improved precision and stability provided by the conformal design approach.

caption: Goodman model representation of mean stress effects for both IM and AM materials.
summary: This panel illustrates the fatigue behavior of IM and AM materials using the Goodman model to account for mean stress effects. The experimental data is expressed in terms of equivalent maximum stress, providing a synthesis of fatigue performance across different stress conditions for both manufacturing methods.

caption: EDS spectrum acquired from the TaN/CrN/ZrN graded coating to verify elemental composition.
summary: The EDS spectrum provides quantitative confirmation of the elemental presence within the TaN/CrN/ZrN graded coating. Consistent with the elemental mapping results, this spectroscopic analysis supports the finding of a uniform distribution of Ta, Cr, Zr, and N, ensuring the chemical integrity of the coating deposited at 450 °C.

caption: Transmission XRD mapping of a pillar sample extracted from a cuboid specimen, performed at the microXAS beamline, revealing periodic austenite phase mesostructures along the 3 mm sample height.
summary: This panel displays a 2D synchrotron transmission XRD map of a pillar sample. The data reveals that austenite phase crystallites are organized into periodic mesostructures spanning the full 3 mm height of the specimen. These wall-like structures are identified as the stripes observed throughout the sample's vertical axis.

caption: STEM-EDS elemental mapping of Titanium distribution, demonstrating the partitioning of alloying elements within the microstructure of the 282 side.
summary: The STEM-EDS map for Titanium reveals the elemental distribution within the Sample A microstructure. This compositional mapping, when correlated with the HAADF image, highlights how Titanium partitions within the γ/γ′ structure of the as-printed 282 alloy, contributing to the overall understanding of the material's phase morphology.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of SMCs (positive control), undifferentiated ADSCs, and ADSCs differentiated into dSMCs using TGF-β1 PODS® at day 7, highlighting αSMA expression (green) and DAPI-stained nuclei (blue).
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging confirms the successful differentiation of ADSCs into dSMCs after 7 days of culture with TGF-β1 PODS®. The dSMCs exhibit αSMA expression levels comparable to the positive control SMCs, demonstrating effective lineage commitment. DAPI staining provides clear visualization of cell nuclei across the control and experimental groups.

caption: Viscosity of as-spun Al86Ce10TM4 (TM = Ti, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu) amorphous alloys (A1–A7) plotted against inverse temperature near the glass transition region Tx,20.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the viscosity of seven Al-Ce-TM amorphous alloys as a function of inverse temperature near Tx,20. The data reveals distinct theoretical glass transition temperatures (Tg*) for each alloy, ranging from 470.2 K to 565.5 K, and highlights the passivation behavior observed in alloys A1 through A6.

caption: Superimposed lattice model showing the matrix lattice in white and the superlattice in yellow, viewed near the [110] zone axis.
summary: This structural model illustrates the relationship between the matrix lattice and the superlattice, visualized near the [110] zone axis. The matrix is represented in white, while the superlattice is highlighted in yellow. This orientation reveals a reciprocal superstructure lattice with specific reflections in positions {1/2 1/2 1/2}, {1 0 0}, and {1 1 0}.

caption: Temperature contour plot representing the top view of the melt pool during the SLM process at Point 1.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the temperature distribution on the top surface of the melt pool during the SLM process at observation Point 1. It provides a spatial visualization of thermal gradients within the melt pool, serving as a baseline for comparing thermal behavior during additive manufacturing processes.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image of area 2, captured with the sample tilted along the g-vector to visualize dislocation distribution.
summary: Area 2 is examined using bright-field TEM with specific g-vector tilting to enhance dislocation contrast. This imaging approach allows for the characterization of the dislocation density immediately ahead of the crack tip, which correlates with the higher misorientation observed in the corresponding misorientation map of the same region.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the middle region of the WAAM specimen.
summary: Representing the middle section of the WAAM specimen, this histogram illustrates the grain size distribution derived from equivalent circle diameter measurements. Consistent with the overall findings in Fig. 13, the grain sizes in this region are larger than those observed in the corresponding middle region of the HASM specimen.

caption: Ink shape retention capacity evaluated through a 3-interval thixotropy test (3ITT), demonstrating the recovery behavior of the Co-YDZ inks.
summary: Shape retention capacity is assessed using a 3-interval thixotropy test (3ITT) to evaluate the recovery performance of the Co-YDZ inks. The viscoelastic properties identified in the amplitude sweep test facilitate nearly complete recovery during the third phase of the 3-ITT, confirming the material's suitability for maintaining printed shapes.

caption: Al-Cu binary phase diagram showing the coupled zone (dashed area) derived from Thermo-Calc 2020b using the TTAL7 database.
summary: This Al-Cu binary phase diagram, generated using Thermo-Calc 2020b and the TTAL7 database, highlights the coupled zone as a dashed region. The diagram predicts the formation of a eutectic structure within this zone, spanning a wide range of hypo- and hyper-eutectic compositions, providing a theoretical basis for understanding solidification behavior.

caption: Force-depth curves illustrating the mechanical response of the material under three distinct force levels during indentation testing.
summary: This panel displays force-depth curves obtained from representative nanoindentation tests performed at three different force levels. These curves characterize the mechanical response and deformation behavior of the specimen, providing essential data on the material's resistance to indentation and its elastic-plastic properties under varying load conditions.

caption: Dielectric and magnetic loss tangent values for SCC-2/PEEK composites.
summary: The dielectric loss tangent and magnetic loss tangent of the SCC-2/PEEK composites are plotted here. Observations show that both the dielectric loss tangent and the magnetic loss tangent increase as the SCF/Co@C-2 content rises, indicating improved energy dissipation capabilities at higher filler concentrations.

caption: Out-of-plane displacement map of a wavy-patterned SHS specimen flange at failure load, illustrating asymmetric buckling wave locations.
summary: The out-of-plane displacement for a wavy-patterned SHS specimen at failure is shown here. The DIC results indicate that inward and outward buckling waves on adjacent plates occur at different heights along the column, which is a distinct failure characteristic for specimens featuring the applied wavy pattern.

caption: Deconvolution results for the 27Al MAS NMR spectrum of potassium-activated slag 3 paste prepared with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 2.15.
summary: Analysis of the 27Al MAS NMR spectrum for potassium-activated slag 3 paste with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 2.15 shows the aluminum coordination state. The spectrum indicates that a significant portion of Al is in tetrahedral coordination, resonating at 62.5 ppm, likely due to the presence of Al-OH species.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves at 4 hours, highlighting three distinct endothermic peaks within the 50–800 °C temperature range.
summary: The DTG curves at 4 hours reveal three key endothermic peaks occurring at 50–300 °C, 300–600 °C, and 600–800 °C. These peaks indicate specific thermal decomposition events, including the decomposition of various salts and the carbonation of geopolymers and raw-material carbonates, providing insight into the material's chemical evolution under microwave treatment.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms comparing the LLDPE/EG/PCM composite in its melt-mixed state versus its 3D-printed form, revealing a significant reduction in measured enthalpy for the printed sample.
summary: DSC curves illustrate the thermal behavior of LLDPE/EG/PCM composites before and after 3D printing. The analysis indicates that the measured enthalpy of the 3D-printed sample is approximately 50% lower than the theoretical value, suggesting changes in the composite's thermal properties or PCM content during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Endurance test of a Ni-perovskite coated SOFC operating in H2 and dry ethanol, showing current density (red) and cell potential (black) over a 100-hour duration.
summary: This 100-hour endurance test evaluates the stability of a Ni-modified perovskite-based SOFC under dry ethanol feed. The plot tracks the evolution of current density and cell potential over time. Electrochemical diagnostics, including polarization curves and impedance spectroscopy, were performed at specific intervals to monitor performance degradation and stability throughout the test.

caption: EBSD grain boundary map showing increased strain, with black rectangles highlighting regions of high LAGB density and concentrated recrystallized grains.
summary: At this strain level, LAGBs accumulate significantly at pre-existing HAGBs, promoting recrystallization. The regions marked by black rectangles exhibit the highest density of recrystallized grains and the largest concentration of LAGB substructures, demonstrating that these substructures are critical for the nucleation of recrystallization during the compression process.

caption: Ternary representation of the industrial matte composition plotted on the (Ni+Fe)-Cu-S system coordinates.
summary: Industrial matte composition is mapped onto the (Ni+Fe)-Cu-S ternary phase diagram to visualize its chemical state. This plot provides a clear overview of the material's constituent balance, which is critical for understanding the subsequent conversion steps required to effectively remove iron and excess sulfur from the liquid matte.

caption: Microhardness distribution map of the laser-peened Scalmalloy® surface region, illustrating the increased hardness profile within the hardened layer compared to the un-peened state.
summary: This panel presents the microhardness map for the laser-peened Scalmalloy® specimen. The data reveals the depth and extent of the hardened layer, which correlates with the compression zone. These measurements, taken 15 μm below the surface, demonstrate the effectiveness of laser peening in modifying the surface mechanical properties of the material.

caption: High-resolution Ni 2p 3/2 XPS spectrum of the reduced anode sample, showing deconvoluted peaks at 852.3 eV and 854.0 eV corresponding to Ni0 and Ni2+ chemical states.
summary: The Ni 2p 3/2 XPS spectrum of the reduced anode sample reveals the surface chemical states of nickel. Deconvolution of the spectrum identifies two distinct peaks at 852.3 eV and 854.0 eV, which are attributed to the presence of metallic Ni0 and oxidized Ni2+ species, respectively, on the sample surface.

caption: k3-weighted Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra in k-space for the catalysts.
summary: The k3-weighted Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra in k-space characterize the local atomic structure around nickel atoms. These spectra, alongside the corresponding Fourier transform in R-space, provide essential data for analyzing the coordination environment and bond distances within the E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 and E-Ni 0.2 catalyst systems.

caption: Expanded circuit schematic showing the connection interface between the AC generator and the wearable actuators.
summary: This panel provides an expanded view of the circuit connections between the frequency-adjustable AC generator and the wearable actuators. The schematic details the electrical interface required to maintain a uniform current sine wave, ensuring consistent and controlled performance of the actuators within the wearable electronic system.

caption: Physical configuration of the GVSM002 galvanometer system used for experimental validation.
summary: The physical unit of the galvanometer system is shown, specifically the GVSM002 model from Thorlabs. This hardware serves as the primary experimental platform for validating the proposed all-pass based IMP controller, providing the physical foundation for the mechatronic system architecture described in the subsequent system analysis.

caption: Equivalent plastic strain field and load-displacement curve for the PS-3.5 fracture specimen.
summary: Equivalent plastic strain fields for the PS-3.5 specimen are presented here, accompanied by the associated load-displacement curve. The data, obtained through digital image correlation, highlights the specific patterns of strain localization and deformation occurring within the specimen, effectively capturing the mechanical behavior and evolution of the material during fracture testing.

caption: Contour diagram illustrating the influence of hatch distance on material density within an energy density range of approximately 30 to 100 J/mm 3.
summary: The contour plot displays the relationship between hatch distance and material density for LPBF IN718 within an energy density range of 30 to 100 J/mm 3. Dark blue regions represent areas of higher density, identifying a robust processing window and confirming the optimal parameter set for minimizing porosity and boundary defects.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for the hydrazine-NiZn (1 1 1) system, indicating electronic interactions.
summary: The projected density of states for the hydrazine-NiZn (1 1 1) system is shown here. Consistent with the chemisorption observed in the charge density plots, this analysis reveals electron density accumulation within the Ni-N and Zn-N bonding regions, confirming strong hybridization between the metal d-orbitals and the hydrazine N p-orbitals.

caption: Differential mass susceptibility χ ρ plotted against magnetic field H for Ni50Ti42.5Er7.5 alloy specimens subjected to different thermo-mechanical treatments, including as-cast, homogenized, and extruded conditions.
summary: This plot displays the differential mass susceptibility of Ni50Ti42.5Er7.5 alloy under various processing conditions. Homogenized and as-cast samples exhibit similar linear susceptibility, while homogenization induces non-linear behavior near zero field. Extruded specimens show a distinct susceptibility shift of 1 × 10^-6 4π/10^3 m^3 kg^-1 compared to the as-cast material.

caption: Incremental strain test (IST) stress-strain curves for specimens extracted perpendicular to the rolling direction (90° RD).
summary: Incremental strain test (IST) stress-strain curves are shown for specimens extracted perpendicular to the rolling direction (90° RD). These results represent a critical component of the mechanical analysis, summarizing the material's behavior under incremental loading conditions as part of the broader investigation into the hot-rolled condition's mechanical properties.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curve and fitted Tafel curves for a nickel electrode in 0.1 M NaAc solution at pH 1 and 25 ℃.
summary: Nickel electrode behavior in 0.1 M NaAc solution at pH 1 is characterized by these polarization and Tafel curves. The calculated corrosion potential is approximately 0 V. Furthermore, the current density associated with nickel dissolution at the open circuit potential is 2×10^-5 A.cm^-2, representing a significant electrochemical dissolution rate.

caption: Correlation between uniform elongation and normalized ring slip, featuring a linear regression line with an R2 value of 0.993 and a p-value of 1.7e-17.
summary: Uniform elongation and normalized slip are plotted against each other to directly compare these two quantities. The trends are very similar, as evidenced by the linear regression analysis which yields a high R2 value of 0.993 and a significant p-value of 1.7e-17, confirming a strong statistical correlation between the variables.

caption: Ni K-edge EXAFS fitting curve for the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam, showing the first shell contribution.
summary: The Ni K-edge EXAFS fitting curve for the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam is displayed. This fit confirms the local structural parameters, such as bond distances and coordination numbers, providing quantitative evidence of the atomic arrangement and the successful incorporation of Ni into the metallic foam structure.

caption: Randomly distributed nucleation sites appearing within the liquid phase as the temperature drops below the liquidus point.
summary: This panel illustrates the initial stage of the solidification process, where nucleation occurs randomly throughout the material. These sites emerge specifically in regions where the local temperature falls below the liquidus point, representing the beginning of the phase transformation process as described by the cooling simulation model.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction plot for Al0.5CoCrFeNi as a function of temperature, with a red dashed line indicating the 1250 °C thermal condition.
summary: Equilibrium calculations for Al0.5CoCrFeNi are presented as a function of temperature to analyze phase-transformation behavior. The diagram shows the evolution of phase fractions, including the formation of compounds below 600 °C. A red dashed line at 1250 °C provides a specific reference for the alloy's thermodynamic state during heat treatment.

caption: Optical micrograph illustrating the competing cellular growth directions within a 70 μm thick splat.
summary: Optical microscopy of a 70 μm thick splat demonstrates the competing cellular growth directions. Similar to the thicker splat, this etched sample allows for the visualization of larger cellular subgrains, facilitating the comparative analysis of subgrain diameters and growth patterns across different deposition splat thicknesses.

caption: Misorientation distribution histogram at deformation stage Ⅴ, highlighting the emergence of a peak near 60°.
summary: At the beginning of stage Ⅴ, this histogram reveals a significant concentration of misorientations appearing around 60°. This specific structural feature is a critical indicator of the formation of deformation twins within the FeCoNiCrMn alloy, marking a transition in the dominant plastic deformation mechanisms during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Room temperature mechanical testing configuration utilizing an Instron 68TM50 electromechanical machine equipped with a 50kN load cell for ASTM E8 tension and double-edge-notched tension tests.
summary: This photograph displays the room temperature mechanical testing setup, featuring an Instron 68TM50 electromechanical machine with a 50kN load cell. The equipment is configured to perform ASTM E8 tension and double-edge-notched tension tests, providing a controlled environment for evaluating material performance under standard ambient conditions during the experimental procedure.

caption: Backscattered electron image of the HIP + S + DA condition, highlighting the absence of delta phase at grain boundaries and retained lattice distortion in unrecrystallized grains.
summary: The HIP + S + DA microstructure is shown via backscattered electron imaging, revealing a distinct lack of intergranular or intercellular delta phase precipitates. Despite the absence of these precipitates, the image demonstrates that lattice distortion, similar to that observed in the LPBF S + DA condition, persists within retained, unrecrystallized grains.

caption: Secondary view of the hybrid friction diffusion bonding post-processed AA7075 sample, emphasizing defect morphology.
summary: This secondary micro-CT view of the AA7075 sample, processed via friction surfacing and hybrid friction diffusion bonding, highlights the morphology of internal defects. Red volumes represent defects of 64 μm or larger. White arrows indicate the deposition and rotation directions, providing insight into the effectiveness of the bonding process.

caption: Statistical distribution of the angular coefficients (m) derived from the linear regression fits of P/ht versus scan speed, represented as average values with 95% confidence intervals for optical configuration 2.
summary: Panel b presents the angular coefficients (m) extracted from the linear regression fits shown in the previous graph. These values, representing the slope of the P/ht versus scan speed relationship, are displayed as averages with 95% confidence intervals, providing a quantitative comparison of the process efficiency across the tested optical configuration 2 parameters.

caption: Visible camera view of a tungsten target assembly during exposure to deuterium plasma at 1000 K within the PISCES-RF linear plasma device.
summary: This photograph captures a tungsten target undergoing deuterium plasma exposure at 1000 K in the PISCES-RF device. The image highlights the target and its holder assembly, including an incandescent hex nut, which serves to terminate the plasma flow while being heated by the incident plasma ion and heat flux.

caption: Bode plots representing the impedance modulus and phase angle distributions for the Ti-based coatings and 2Cr13 substrate.
summary: The impedance modulus (|Z|) and phase angle distributions of the specimens are shown in Fig. 11 c. These Bode plots provide a detailed frequency-dependent analysis of the electrochemical impedance, characterizing the protective performance and capacitive behavior of the Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings relative to the 2Cr13 substrate.

caption: Schematic illustration of the neutron diffraction scan directions, defining the longitudinal (L), transversal (T), and normal (N) stress components.
summary: This schematic defines the coordinate system for stress characterization in the specimens. The longitudinal (L), transversal (T), and normal (N) directions are identified as the principal axes for stress analysis, providing the necessary geometric framework for interpreting the subsequent neutron diffraction measurements performed on the material samples.

caption: Measurement configuration for electrical conductivity using the eddy current method, showing probe application on planes parallel and normal to the building (z) direction.
summary: This diagram depicts the experimental setup for measuring electrical conductivity using a SIGMATEST 2.069 device based on the eddy current method. The measurements were performed on planes parallel and normal to the building direction to evaluate microstructural anisotropy, accounting for potential surface porosity effects on the vertical surfaces of the printed parts.

caption: Long-term cycling performance showing charge-discharge capacity and corresponding coulombic efficiency for the Ni 0.9 Sn electrode over 120 cycles at 0.1 A g-1.
summary: Long-term cycling performance of the Ni 0.9 Sn NP-based electrode is demonstrated over 120 cycles at a current density of 0.1 A g-1. The plot tracks both the charge-discharge capacity and the coulombic efficiency, providing a comprehensive view of the electrode's stability and Na-ion storage performance over extended operation.

caption: Raman analysis performed at the edges of the reference wear track, identifying the presence of amorphous carbon species.
summary: Raman spectroscopy conducted at the edges of the reference wear track identifies the presence of amorphous carbon species. These signals provide evidence of chemical changes occurring within the wear track during tribo-testing, confirming the formation of carbonaceous reaction products on the CoCr surface under the reference test conditions.

caption: Ternary viscosity distribution map of the Ti–Al–Ni alloy system at 2033 K, where solid spheres denote experimental data points and color gradients represent viscosity variations across the composition space.
summary: This ternary diagram illustrates the viscosity distribution of the Ti–Al–Ni alloy system at 2033 K. Solid spheres represent specific experimental data points, while color mapping visualizes viscosity variations across compositions. Analysis of elemental iso-content cross-sections reveals that individual elements exert significantly different degrees and modes of influence on viscosity.

caption: Overlapping predictions error instance highlighting spatial or categorical ambiguity in model output.
summary: This panel depicts an instance of overlapping predictions, indicating ambiguity where the model generates conflicting or redundant outputs for a single region. These types of errors are analyzed alongside other failure modes, with their main causes and impacts summarized in Table 7 to guide future improvements in model accuracy.

caption: Geometric comparison of the Wing 2 model, overlaying the original CAD design in navy against the final manufactured model in gray.
summary: This panel presents a geometric comparison of the Wing 2 model. It illustrates the alignment between the original CAD design, represented in navy, and the corresponding final manufactured model, shown in gray. This visualization highlights the structural fidelity achieved in the final model relative to the initial design specifications.

caption: Fragmentation pattern of a steel wire mesh bumper subjected to a 7 km/s impact velocity.
summary: Fragmentation pattern of a steel wire mesh bumper subjected to a 7 km/s impact velocity. Observed at time τ, the debris cloud demonstrates the specific interaction between the mesh geometry and the projectile. The debris cloud is shown at a similar distance from the bumper as other tested configurations.

caption: Storage modulus (E') versus temperature for ChNF/PLA composite specimens aged at 50 °C.
summary: ChNF/PLA composite filters show an 89% drop in storage modulus after 3 weeks of aging at 50 °C. This mechanical test confirms that the ChNF/PLA material experiences significant performance loss at elevated temperatures, though it remains slightly more resilient than the TCNF/PLA composite under the same aging conditions.

caption: Relaxed atomic configuration showing the formation of a single nitrogen vacancy (V N) after the titanium atom initially at a nitrogen site migrates into the vacancy.
summary: Following the relaxation of atomic positions from the initial state, this panel demonstrates the resulting V N configuration. The titanium atom, originally positioned at a nitrogen site, successfully migrates into the corresponding vacancy, effectively forming a single nitrogen vacancy point defect within the TiN crystal structure.

caption: Regression analysis of the GPR model showing predicted values against actual experimental data points.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the regression performance of the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model. By comparing predicted values against actual experimental data, the visualization demonstrates the predictive accuracy of the model, serving as a key metric for evaluating the overall performance of the machine learning approach described in the study.

caption: Radar chart comparing the physicochemical properties of Cu, Al, Ti, Ni, and stainless steel current collectors across five metrics: electrical conductivity, lightweight, cost competitiveness, thermal conductivity, and stable potential range.
summary: This radar chart evaluates five current collector metals—Cu, Al, Ti, Ni, and stainless steel—across key performance metrics. The visualization highlights that combining Al and Cu covers a broad performance range, justifying their commercial use. Additionally, it illustrates the superior stable potential window of Ti and the cost advantages of aluminum.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure and phase map of the fractured 1473-d12 LTHT alloy specimen.
summary: This panel illustrates the EBSD inverse pole figure and phase map for the fractured 1473-d12 LTHT alloy. The data contributes to the comparative microstructural analysis of strain-induced ε-phase formation, specifically examining how the LTHT treatment influences the phase distribution in the 1473-d12 alloy system after fracture.

caption: Inertia plot generated via the elbow method, displaying the relationship between the number of clusters and the sum of squared distances within clusters to determine the optimal cluster count.
summary: The elbow plot illustrates the relationship between the number of clusters and the inertia, defined as the sum of squared distances within clusters. This analysis was performed on unlabelled data to determine the optimal number of clusters, providing a quantitative basis for the subsequent classification of the mixture data.

caption: Rendered image of the FCCxyz lattice structure based on a modified unit cell configuration.
summary: This panel displays a rendered image of the FCCxyz lattice structure. The design is derived from a modified unit cell configuration, representing one of the final lattice structure designs presented in the study. The visualization highlights the geometric arrangement characteristic of the FCCxyz unit cell architecture.

caption: SRIM-calculated depth profiles for displacement damage and atomic concentration in a material subjected to 3 MeV Ni ion irradiation at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2, with the red box highlighting the damage peak region.
summary: This panel displays the SRIM-calculated depth profile for displacement damage and Ni ion concentration following 3 MeV irradiation at 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2. The total injected Ni ion amount is low, peaking at 0.2 atomic % at the projected range, indicating that significant effects from excess Ni are not expected.

caption: AFM surface topography of sample H11 after thermal strain recovery.
summary: Thermal strain recovery applied to sample H11 results in a highly rugged surface topography as observed via AFM. This post-recovery state is notably more irregular than the post-compression stage, confirming that the thermal recovery process leads to increased surface roughness rather than a return to the initial as-fabricated surface condition.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized DMA material.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized DMA material is presented to characterize its chemical structure. This spectroscopic analysis provides the necessary data to confirm the successful synthesis and chemical composition of the DMA polymer, serving as a reference for the material's structural integrity and functional group identification.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map and corresponding geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density statistics for the Al-Cu-Ni alloy at position II.
summary: Representing the dislocation state at position II, this KAM map illustrates local misorientation gradients. The related statistical analysis of GND density provides quantitative data on the dislocation content, enabling an evaluation of the microstructural deformation and dislocation density variations across the fractured Al-Cu-Ni alloy sample at this specific position.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of forged Alloy 625 irradiated at 400 °C to 100 dpa, viewed along the [110] zone axis.
summary: Forged Alloy 625 irradiated at 400 °C to a higher dose of 100 dpa exhibits distinct dislocation loop and line features. This bright-field STEM micrograph, taken along the [110] zone axis, provides a representative view of the microstructural state resulting from this specific irradiation condition within the experimental series.

caption: ODF section of the austenite phase at 30% strain, demonstrating the significant decrease and transition of {100} < 011>, Cube {100} < 0.01>, RD Rotated Cube {001} < 310>, and Rotated cube {210} < 100> components.
summary: As strain increases to 30%, specific texture components undergo significant reduction and transition. The {100} < 011>, Cube {100} < 0.01>, RD Rotated Cube {001} < 310>, and Rotated cube {210} < 100> orientations decrease in intensity, indicating a shift in the crystallographic orientation distribution of the austenite phase during the deformation process.

caption: Variation in ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elongation (EL) values corresponding to the twelve tensile specimens extracted from different heights of the bimetallic component.
summary: The variation in ultimate tensile strength and elongation is plotted for the twelve tensile specimens. These results demonstrate how mechanical properties change across the component's height. Combined with microhardness data, these findings indicate that the FGM region exhibits improved strength compared to the ASS region, attributed to α’-martensite formation.

caption: FTIR spectra showing the O-H vibrational band intensity for 2 M ZnSO4 electrolytes with and without SL.
summary: FTIR analysis demonstrates a decrease in the intensity of the O-H vibrational band when 1% SL is added to the 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte. This reduction indicates that the activity of H2O molecules is lower in the presence of the SL additive compared to the pure 2 M ZnSO4 electrolyte.

caption: FT-IR spectra comparing the CuO–ZnO–ZrO2 precursor, clear resin, and the final precursor-loaded ink to evaluate chemical stability.
summary: FT-IR spectroscopy was performed on the CuO–ZnO–ZrO2 precursor, clear resin, and the mixed precursor-loaded ink. This analysis was conducted to ascertain whether the ink preparation process induced any chemical changes in the ingredients, ensuring the chemical integrity of the components during the formulation of the printing ink.

caption: Bar chart comparing the average Interlaminar Shear Strength (ILSS) of thermoplastic matrix composites (TMCs) reinforced with fresh, one-time recycled, and four-times recycled rods.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the average ILSS values for TMC samples reinforced with rods of varying recycling histories. The results indicate that TMCs stiffened with fresh rods achieve 47.1 MPa, while those with one-time and four-times recycled rods exhibit slightly lower ILSS values of 46.7 MPa and 46.5 MPa, respectively.

caption: Selected-area electron diffraction pattern of Coating A, showing structural features.
summary: This SAED pattern represents a specific region within Coating A. TEM analysis was utilized to verify the phase constitution of the coating. The diffraction data obtained from this region contributes to the overall characterization of the material's crystalline structure and phase distribution within the studied coating system.

caption: Isothermal section at the two ternary eutectic reaction temperatures (L1 → γ + P + NiMo and L2 → γ + P + σ).
summary: This schematic illustrates the isothermal section at the temperatures corresponding to two distinct ternary eutectic reactions. The diagram maps the transformation pathways L1 → γ + P + NiMo and L2 → γ + P + σ, defining the phase boundaries and equilibrium states for these specific eutectic reactions within the ternary system.

caption: Storage modulus evolution across a temperature range for 100% BPR, 95% BPR 5% BBZ, and 95% BPR 5% BBZ 1% PPy prints.
summary: Storage modulus versus temperature plots are shown for the 100% BPR, 95% BPR 5% BBZ, and 95% BPR 5% BBZ 1% PPy prints. These DMA results demonstrate the viscoelastic response of the materials, with the recovery temperature noted to be slightly above the glass transition temperature of the composite.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops of PEI/Ni-10%vol susceptor samples measured at 25 °C, 100 °C, and 200 °C under a constant field amplitude of 32 kA/m.
summary: Magnetic hysteresis behavior of the PEI/Ni-10%vol susceptor is compared across three distinct temperatures: 25 °C, 100 °C, and 200 °C. All measurements were conducted under a fixed applied field amplitude of 32 kA/m, providing insight into how thermal conditions influence the magnetic loop characteristics of the composite.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the heat-treated SLM 18Ni-300 material showing the martensitic microstructure.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the heat-treated SLM 18Ni-300 material reveals a complex microstructure. The analysis shows a high density of dislocations and lath martensite, with no discernible austenite present in the sample. This structural characterization provides a baseline for understanding the material's state following the heat treatment process.

caption: High-angle grain boundary (HAGB) mapping of the HS700 sample, illustrating the grain boundary network and the bimodal grain structure.
summary: High-angle grain boundary mapping of the HS700 sample provides a clear visualization of the grain network. This analysis supports the identification of a bimodal grain structure, which is a characteristic feature of the HS700 sample developed through cold rolling and subsequent annealing processes prior to SMGT.

caption: 1H NMR spectra (500 MHz, CDCl3, 500 K) comparing the chemical composition of PC-CF recycling stages R0 (red), R1 (green), and R5 (blue).
summary: This figure displays the 1H NMR spectra for the PC-CF recycling stages R0, R1, and R5, acquired at 500 MHz in CDCl3 at 500 K. The spectra allow for a direct comparison of the chemical composition across these different recycling stages, illustrating the structural integrity of the material throughout the recycling process.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the US-600W sample displaying a partially dissolved carbide.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals an irregular shaped (Ti,Mo)C carbide in the US-600W sample. The observed morphology suggests partial dissolution of the carbide in an intrinsic heat-affected zone resulting from the maximum sonication power of 600 W, highlighting the thermal and mechanical impact of the processing on carbide stability.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the bcc-W coordination rhombic dodecahedron and the corresponding CPGA cluster model.
summary: This panel displays the CPGA model for bcc-W, featuring a central W atom coordinated by 14 nearest neighbor W atoms. These atoms are arranged at the 14 vertices of a rhombic dodecahedron, serving as the basic structural cluster model for describing the bcc-W crystal lattice configuration.

caption: Spider graph illustrating the tensile strength performance across various ASA recycling course levels.
summary: This radar chart summarizes the tensile strength of specimens subjected to different ASA recycling course levels. The data indicates that most recycling levels show an increase in tensile strength relative to the first course, with specific variations observed across the third and sixth levels for the M-H material system.

caption: Longitudinal dimensional change of pyC models and crystalline graphite as a function of temperature, represented by the ratio of simulation cell length a to its reference value a0 at 300 K.
summary: Longitudinal dimensional evolution of pyC models is plotted against temperature, showing the ratio of the simulation cell length a to its reference value a0 at 300 K. Crystalline graphite data is included for comparison, illustrating how the longitudinal axis responds to thermal changes in these simulated carbon structures.

caption: Supercooling temperature (T–) estimation for defective Ni systems, demonstrating that this lower bound value remains independent of the initial vacancy concentration.
summary: The supercooling temperature (T–) is estimated from the supercooling of defective Ni systems. As indicated by the data, this lower bound temperature is independent of the initial vacancy concentration, confirming that the cooling behavior of the liquid phase Ni is consistent regardless of the starting defect density.

caption: Normalized specular reflectance signal intensity at 11,820 eV and Au L3-edge absorption step size at 11,919 eV plotted as a function of applied electrochemical potential.
summary: This plot illustrates the measured specular reflectance signal intensity at 11,820 eV, calculated as the ratio of reflected to incident beam intensity, alongside the absorption step size at the Au L3-edge (11,919 eV). Both datasets are normalized to their respective maximum values to compare their trends as a function of applied electrochemical potential.

caption: Weight loss percentage plotted against temperature for 4D printed composites, illustrating the thermal degradation profile.
summary: This panel displays the weight loss versus temperature thermograms for the 4D printed composites. The data indicates that the thermal stability of the various prints remains largely consistent, with insignificant differences observed between the 100% BPR print and the 95% BPR 5% BBZ 15% PPy composite formulation.

caption: Detailed current-voltage waveform for the 10 m/min wire feed rate condition, highlighting transient electrical behavior.
summary: Displayed is the detailed current-voltage waveform for the 10 m/min wire feed rate condition. This panel captures the electrical characteristics of the deposition process at the highest feed rate, serving as a critical component in evaluating the relationship between wire feed rates and the resulting thin wall structure properties.

caption: Comparison of experimental EIS data and the corresponding equivalent circuit fitting results for the bare 2024-T3 alloy, demonstrating high agreement between the model and measurements.
summary: This plot displays the experimental electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the bare 2024-T3 alloy alongside its equivalent circuit fitting results. The visualization demonstrates a strong agreement between the theoretical model and the recorded experimental data, confirming the validity of the circuit parameters used for the bare alloy analysis.

caption: Cathodic polarization curve illustrating the electrochemical behavior of the TA31 alloy.
summary: This figure displays the cathodic polarization curve for the TA31 alloy, which was obtained through electrochemical testing. The plot characterizes the alloy's cathodic response, providing essential data regarding its electrochemical performance and behavior under the specified experimental conditions prior to further testing procedures described in the study.

caption: Block diagram illustrating the closed-loop fuzzy logic control system architecture implemented for the Directed Energy Deposition (DED) manufacturing process.
summary: This block diagram depicts the closed-loop fuzzy control system specifically engineered for the DED process. It serves as a visual representation of the control architecture, which is further detailed through the corresponding algorithm pseudo-code provided in the appendix of the study to facilitate process monitoring and regulation.

caption: Cu-covered state showing the formation of a surface bump induced by atomic clusters with high vacancy energy, as highlighted by the red circle.
summary: The MD snapshot displays the Cu-covered state on the IN718 surface. A distinct bump is visible, created by atomic clusters with high vacancy energy induced by Nb in the IN718 alloy. This structural feature, marked by a red circle, initiates the obstruction of Cu spreading across the substrate.

caption: Volta potential difference map of the CoCrFeNiSi alloy ingot, revealing local potential variations despite the homogeneous appearance observed in SEM imaging.
summary: The Volta potential difference map for the CoCrFeNiSi alloy ingot reveals local potential variations across the surface. Although XRD analysis identified a binary-phase structure and SEM imaging suggested a homogeneous appearance, the SKPFM map successfully detects local differences in Volta potentials, providing deeper insight into the alloy's microstructural electrochemical nature.

caption: Arrhenius-style plot showing the temperature dependence of Li diffusivity within various Li-Al phases, derived from EIS-based Warburg coefficient calculations.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent Li diffusivity within Li-Al phases, calculated from EIS data. The error bars represent discrepancies in Warburg coefficients derived from real and imaginary impedance components. A monotonic relationship between diffusivity and temperature is observed, indicating that higher temperatures are advantageous for utilizing Li-rich phases.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of SWCNTs exhibiting distinct profiles for various chiralities, highlighting the dependence of optical properties on tube diameter.
summary: The absorption spectra of SWCNTs demonstrate a clear correlation between optical response and tube diameter. These spectroscopic measurements reveal that the electronic transitions, which dictate the absorption characteristics, are intrinsically linked to the specific chirality of the nanotubes, as evidenced by the distinct spectral features observed for different species.

caption: Procedural flowchart illustrating the criteria and decision-making process for determining bead availability for MLSB deposition based on width and height fluctuations.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic identification of bead availability for MLSB deposition. It utilizes width and height fluctuation calculations as primary metrics, where fluctuations below 10% indicate stable and available beads. This screening method serves as a critical step for evaluating process parameters and validating classification model predictions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images showing live/dead staining of C2C12 cells cultured on rod- and spherical-shaped microgels after seven days, with live cells in green and dead cells in red (Scale bars: 500 μm).
summary: Live/dead staining images demonstrate high cell viability on both microgel geometries after seven days. The fluorescence microscopy results confirm that neither rod-shaped nor spherical microgels induce significant cytotoxicity, as indicated by the prevalence of green-stained live cells across both culture conditions throughout the one-week experimental period.

caption: Asymmetric transverse domain wall (ATDW) structure in a soft ferromagnetic cylindrical nanowire, featuring a specific head-to-head magnetization arrangement and an inset cross-section.
summary: This panel illustrates the ATDW configuration, which represents one of the three primary head-to-head domain wall structures found in soft ferromagnetic cylindrical nanowires.
