caption: Elemental distribution map of AlCrFe2Ni2.1 alloy illustrating the partitioning of Ni and Al into the B2 phase and Fe and Cr into the FCC phase, with a minor Cr-enriched disordered BCC phase.
summary: The AlCrFe2Ni2.1 alloy shows clear phase separation where Ni and Al segregate to the B2 phase. Fe and Cr are found in the FCC phase. A duplex BCC structure is also observed, featuring a disordered BCC phase enriched in Cr, which constitutes about 5% of the total volume.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the temperature dependence of the Ni self-diffusion coefficient in dilute Ni-P alloys with impurity concentrations ranging from 0 to 1 at.%.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the temperature-dependent Ni self-diffusion coefficient in Ni-P alloys. Data indicates that P impurities significantly accelerate solvent diffusion even at concentrations below 0.1 at.%. The diffusion coefficients were calculated using DFT methods, demonstrating a strong sensitivity of the solvent diffusion rate to the presence of phosphorus.

caption: HAADF-mapping image of the second phase at the grain boundary, highlighting the elemental distribution of Sc and Ti.
summary: Elemental mapping reveals the chemical composition of the cubical second phase at the grain boundary. Scandium elements are primarily enriched in the center of the phase, while titanium elements are distributed at the outer layer. Additionally, discontinuous Sc-rich zones are observed outside the main phase, appearing as striped patterns.

caption: Hyperbolic secant (HS) profile representing the refractive index distribution used for the L(0,2) mode at 30 kHz.
summary: This panel displays the hyperbolic secant refractive index profile, which serves as the foundational model for the L(0,2) mode at 30 kHz. This specific index distribution is essential for comparing conventional and non-planar GRIN theories, providing the baseline parameters required for subsequent ray trajectory calculations and focal point predictions.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of an AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.845.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image depicts the surface morphology of an AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.845. The surface remains similar to the bulk AlInN reference, consistent with the trend of maintaining stable surface morphology across high AlInN fractions in the superlattice structure.

caption: TDA desorption rate spectrum for 316L stainless steel charged at 200 bar.
summary: This panel displays the TDA spectrum for 316L stainless steel after hydrogen charging at 200 bar. The desorption rate, represented by the ion current, is lower compared to the 1000 bar condition. This data reflects the material-specific hydrogen concentration and desorption behavior under these specific experimental charging parameters.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the USC 10L catalyst layer, illustrating the complex arrangement of void and solid phases alongside pore space skeletons.
summary: Represented here is the 3D reconstruction of the USC 10L catalyst layer obtained via FIB-SEM tomography. The image provides a detailed visualization of the reconstructed void and solid phases distribution, with pore space skeletons integrated to clarify the complex internal architecture and connectivity of the catalyst layer structure.

caption: HT-CSLM image depicting the progression of MgAl2O4 inclusion agglomeration on the steel surface in the M1 sample.
summary: Captured via HT-CSLM, this image illustrates the ongoing aggregation of MgAl2O4 inclusions in the M1 sample. The study of these pairs helps analyze the interactive forces between inclusions, showing that smaller inclusions are attracted to larger, stationary ones, with capillary forces influencing the process at distances up to 45 μm.

caption: Magnetic specific heat C mag of fcc Co obtained from Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: Shown is the magnetic specific heat C mag for fcc cobalt, computed via Monte Carlo simulation. This visualization captures the temperature-dependent magnetic heat capacity characteristics of the fcc phase, providing essential data for understanding the magnetic thermodynamic properties of cobalt in this specific crystal arrangement.

caption: Time-resolved evolution of synchrotron X-ray diffractograms during in situ post-deposition heat treatment (PDHT).
summary: This panel displays the temporal evolution of synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns collected during in situ PDHT. These diffractograms provide a continuous record of structural changes occurring within the material throughout the heat treatment process, serving as the primary dataset for analyzing phase stability and microstructural transformations over the specified time duration.

caption: Theoretical elastic modulus of negative-upsilon structures derived from the Ashby model.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical elastic modulus for negative-upsilon structures, calculated using the Ashby model. The graph represents the predicted stiffness characteristics of the material, offering a clear visualization of how the structural parameters influence the elastic response within the framework of the applied theoretical model.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve demonstrating the CNN model's predictive accuracy for stringing defects.
summary: Representing the performance of the CNN model, this ROC curve visualizes the trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in detecting stringing defects. The plot serves as a key metric for evaluating how effectively the machine learning algorithm distinguishes between the presence and absence of stringing in the analyzed dataset.

caption: Larson-Miller diagrams comparing the creep performance of three experimental alloys against reference data for CMSX-4 and René N5 superalloys.
summary: The Larson-Miller diagram compares the creep performance of three experimental alloys against established CMSX-4 and René N5 benchmarks. Despite containing only half the rhenium content of the reference alloys, the experimental materials exhibit comparable creep performance across the three tested conditions, highlighting their potential as high-temperature structural materials.

caption: Specific flexural modulus versus specific flexural strength map for 3D printed composites, comparing carbon fiber (CF) and glass fiber (GF) reinforced samples at 0° and 90° orientations across sub-ambient (SH), room (RH), and elevated (EH) temperatures.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the relationship between specific flexural modulus and specific flexural strength for continuous fiber reinforced composites. The data compares CF and GF composites at 0° and 90° orientations under sub-ambient, room, and elevated temperature conditions, providing a comprehensive overview of mechanical performance variations across these distinct environmental and structural parameters.

caption: Top-view optical micrograph of the VN56 3DTES structure showing the patterned design of the EV support.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the top-view morphology of the VN56 3DTES structure. The image confirms that the NaNO3 molten salt successfully infiltrated the support, effectively filling the open channels of the 3D structure, which is a critical observation for evaluating the structural integrity and performance of the composite material.

caption: Cycling stability of the 2# alloy under 5 MPa H2 pressure, achieving a maximum hydrogen capacity of 1.131 wt% at the second absorption cycle.
summary: The 2# alloy displays robust cycling stability during hydrogenation tests conducted at 5 MPa H2 pressure. The material maintains consistent performance across cycles, reaching a maximum hydrogen storage capacity of 1.131 wt% during the second absorption cycle, which highlights its superior durability compared to the annealed alloy.

caption: Effective shear strain map of the 910 STA specimen at 1.10% macroscopic strain, showing initial strain localization within individual alpha-p lamellae.
summary: This panel displays the effective shear strain distribution in a 910 STA specimen at an early deformation stage of 1.10% macroscopic strain. HRDIC analysis reveals that strain localization is initially confined to single alpha-p lamellae, highlighting the early-stage mechanical response of the material under tensile loading conditions.

caption: Magnified interface region between the HCP-Ti (blue) and BCC (purple) phases in layer 2 of sample HP, highlighting the presence of Cr2Ta and TiAl intermetallic agglomerations.
summary: This magnified view of the interface between HCP-Ti and BCC phases in sample HP layer 2 provides detailed insight into the local chemistry. Agglomerations of Cr2Ta and TiAl intermetallic phases are clearly detected at the boundary, indicating complex phase interactions occurring during the deposition process in the high-power sample.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of Carbon (C) distribution within the SC material, where purple regions represent C-rich areas.
summary: Carbon elemental mapping via EDS highlights the distribution of C within the SC material, with purple regions indicating C-rich areas. The consistent elemental distribution observed here, alongside the Si map, confirms the microstructural homogenization of the sample, which is attributed to high-temperature Si infiltration and the resulting pore elimination.

caption: Double-logarithmic plot of minimum creep strain rate versus effective compressive stress for Al-0.2Sc-0.4Zr alloys, highlighting the dislocation creep regime with n = 4.4.
summary: This panel presents the double-logarithmic relationship between minimum creep strain rate and effective compressive stress for Al-0.2Sc-0.4Zr alloys. The slope of n = 4.4 indicates a dislocation creep mechanism. The plot facilitates a direct comparison between Ni-containing and Ni-free samples, demonstrating the influence of Ni on the creep strain rate.

caption: Vickers hardness profile of the IN625/Al2O3 functionally graded material plotted as a function of the distance along the thickness direction.
summary: This plot displays the Vickers hardness measurements across the thickness of the IN625/Al2O3 functionally graded material. The data indicates that there are no significant hardness differences observed within the individual IN625 and Al2O3 deposition layers, demonstrating a consistent mechanical response throughout the thickness of the fabricated FGM structure.

caption: Raman spectra of graphene grown on pure Cu substrates between 800 °C and 1000 °C, highlighting the presence of a conspicuous D band at 900 °C.
summary: Raman analysis of graphene grown on pure Cu reveals a prominent D band at 900 °C, indicating defect formation. This suggests that C2H2 transforms into intermediate species that interfere with the growth process. Notably, no graphene growth occurs on pure Cu substrates at temperatures below 800 °C.

caption: Low-magnification surface SEM image of the A4 alloy after 15 cycles of hot corrosion at 750 °C, illustrating the general surface state of the oxide layer.
summary: Low-magnification SEM imaging of the A4 alloy surface after 15 cycles of hot corrosion at 750 °C illustrates the overall morphology of the oxide scale. This panel contributes to the comparative assessment of surface degradation across the alloy series under the specified hot corrosion test parameters.

caption: Cyclic voltammetric curves of the W-R2 alloy recorded in the non-faradic region at scan rates of 10, 20, 50, 80, and 100 mV/s.
summary: This panel displays the cyclic voltammetry curves for the W-R2 alloy across five distinct scan rates ranging from 10 to 100 mV/s. These measurements focus specifically on the non-faradic region of the electrochemical response, providing the necessary data to evaluate the electrode double-layer behavior of the material.

caption: C 1s XPS spectrum of FeNi-CA showing distinct peaks corresponding to various carbon species present in the material.
summary: The C 1s XPS spectrum of FeNi-CA is presented in panel (a). This spectroscopic analysis reveals distinct peaks that represent different carbon species within the sample. These findings provide insight into the chemical state and composition of the carbonaceous framework of the FeNi-CA material.

caption: BEI transmission spectra obtained from the Fe (316 L) and Cu (CuCrZr) layers of the multilayer specimen oriented in the TD2 direction.
summary: Presented here are the BEI transmission spectra for the Fe and Cu layers of the multilayer sample in the TD2 orientation. These spectroscopic measurements allow for the characterization of the material layers in this specific orientation, complementing the data obtained from the TD1 orientation for comprehensive material assessment.

caption: Idealized powder layer configuration and corresponding velocity field for a uniform spreading process.
summary: This schematic represents an ideal powder layer and its associated velocity field. It serves as a baseline for comparison, illustrating the expected uniform flow and layer deposition in the absence of the stress fluctuations, dynamic wall effects, or cohesive forces that typically cause imperfections in real-world powder spreading.

caption: ERR values for G15 DCB samples, where solid and dashed horizontal lines denote the mean ERR and mean peak ERR, respectively, reflecting the toughening contributions from extrinsic bridging.
summary: G15 DCB samples show distinct ERR values, with mean and peak levels marked by horizontal lines and shaded regions. These mechanical test results support the correlation between peak ERR and extrinsic OC bridging, illustrating the toughening behavior inherent in the G15 samples as part of the updated experimental analysis.

caption: Simulated X-ray depth distribution profiles for Ni Kα and Ni Lα emission lines in a γ′ Ni-based superalloy at 15 kV, with the sample surface tilted 38° relative to the electron beam.
summary: Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate the depth distribution of Ni Kα and Ni Lα X-rays in a γ′ Ni-based superalloy at 15 kV. The L shell requires less ionization energy, resulting in Lα X-rays being generated from deeper within the sample. This significant difference in absorption and generation depth is critical for accurate 3D EDS quantification.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the central area of the Ni–Ti sample fabricated at a 1:2 wire feed speed ratio.
summary: The Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map depicts the central area of the Ni–Ti sample fabricated at a 1:2 wire feed speed ratio. The microstructure shows a transformation to smaller equiaxed and dendritic grains, with an average grain size of 5.89 μm and no significant deviation in preferred orientation.

caption: Conductivity decay rates for M-1#, M-2#, M-4#, and M-6# membranes during aging in 1 M KOH solution at 80 °C.
summary: Conductivity decay rates for specific crosslinked membranes (M-1#, M-2#, M-4#, and M-6#) were evaluated in 1 M KOH at 80 °C. The results demonstrate decay patterns similar to those observed at 60 °C, providing further confirmation of the robust chemical stability inherent to these crosslinked electrolyte systems.

caption: Composite HS-AFM image of the WQ900 sample surface, constructed by stitching multiple individual scan tiles together.
summary: This composite HS-AFM image of the WQ900 sample surface was generated by stitching together several individual scan tiles acquired during high-speed atomic force microscopy. The resulting micrograph highlights the distribution of larger white particles, which are identified as δ phase needles within the material's microstructure.

caption: Interferometry image of the AM-TS tool material disk wear scar after testing at 200 °C.
summary: This panel presents the interferometry imaging of the wear scar on the AM-TS tool material disk after a tribotest performed at 200 °C. The visualization allows for the assessment of surface wear patterns and material removal occurring at this elevated temperature for the AM-TS specimen.

caption: Logarithmic dependence of the current density measured at 0.70 V vs Hg/HgO on the methanol concentration for the NiSn (2:1) electrode.
summary: The logarithmic dependence of current density at 0.70 V vs Hg/HgO on methanol concentration is shown for the NiSn (2:1) electrode. While the system exhibits saturation at relatively low methanol concentrations, the electrode achieves very high current densities and mass current densities during the methanol oxidation reaction process.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for Mo0 and Mo23 Co-free non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys tested in a 3.5 wt% NaCl aqueous solution at ambient temperature.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of Mo0 and Mo23 high-entropy alloys in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The data reveals positive hysteresis for both alloys, indicating susceptibility to pitting corrosion. Comparative analysis demonstrates that Mo23 exhibits superior general corrosion resistance compared to the Mo0 alloy in this environment.

caption: Norton plot displaying the relationship between minimum creep rate and engineering stress for various alloys and conditions.
summary: This Norton plot illustrates the minimum creep rate as a function of engineering stress for each tested alloy and condition. By analyzing the slope of these data points, the creep stress exponent is determined for each material, providing critical insights into the deformation mechanisms governing the creep behavior under different experimental conditions.

caption: XRD pattern of the Al0.5CrFeNi2.5Si0.25 alloy after annealing at 1473 K for 60 minutes followed by water quenching.
summary: The XRD pattern for the Al0.5CrFeNi2.5Si0.25 high-entropy alloy annealed at 1473 K for 60 minutes and water quenched is shown. This diffraction profile provides evidence of the phase constitution and structural characteristics of the alloy at this highest tested annealing temperature, facilitating analysis of thermal stability.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Mg-Al-Gd ternary system at 673 K, derived using the CALPHAD approach and compared against experimental data.
summary: The isothermal section of the Mg-Al-Gd ternary system at 673 K is presented, generated through the CALPHAD calculation method. This diagram integrates theoretical phase equilibrium predictions with previously reported experimental data, providing a comprehensive overview of the phase stability and composition ranges within this specific ternary alloy system.

caption: Summary of the design cases solved, detailing the specific configurations and parameters applied to the prosthesis models.
summary: This panel presents the comprehensive summary of the design cases solved, providing the necessary parameters for the four distinct prosthesis types. It details the specific configurations, such as the C-shaped and J-shaped models with or without heel-support, which were evaluated to identify the optimal sandwich structure design solutions.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe70 composite.
summary: The Fe70 composite reflection loss profile characterizes the electromagnetic absorption behavior at a 70 wt% Fe loading. This plot contributes to the overall assessment of how varying iron concentrations influence the reflection loss values and absorption capabilities of the Fe/PLA/TPU composite materials across the investigated loading range.

caption: Calculated heat capacities (Cp) of Yb2Ni17, YbNi5, YbNi3, YbNi2, and α-YbNi intermetallic phases plotted against temperature, with YbNi2 data compared against experimental measurements from 4.2 K to 300 K.
summary: This plot displays the calculated heat capacities for various Yb-Ni intermetallic compounds as a function of temperature. The simulation results for the YbNi2 phase show strong agreement with experimental measurements reported by Rojas et al. in the 4.2 K to 300 K range, validating the first-principles approach used for these thermodynamic predictions.

caption: Probabilistic S-N curves for the SB geometry, plotting the median trend line with 10-th and 90-th percentile bounds for fatigue life estimation.
summary: SB geometry fatigue performance is evaluated through P-S-N curves, featuring median, 10-th, and 90-th percentile estimates. By applying the maximum likelihood principle to failure and runout data, the resulting curves effectively capture the experimental fatigue response, with roughly 80% of the data points residing within the 10-th and 90-th percentile boundaries.

caption: ODF section of the austenite sample at 40% strain, where the transformation of texture components initiated at lower strains appears to be completed.
summary: At 40% strain, the ODF section indicates that the texture transformations observed during the earlier stages of deformation have reached completion. This panel highlights the stabilized state of the austenite texture following the significant component transitions that occurred between 0% and 30% strain levels.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of live/dead stained rat BMSCs on GC, G365, G270, and GU implants after 3 days, with green indicating live cells and red indicating dead cells.
summary: Live/dead staining was employed to evaluate the viability of rat bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells on GC, G365, G270, and GU implants after a 3-day culture period. The fluorescence imaging distinguishes live cells in green and dead cells in red, providing a visual assessment of cell survival on the scaffolds.

caption: Histogram showing the statistical distribution of Si particle size in untreated (UT) Al–27Si alloy based on optical microscopy.
summary: This histogram illustrates the particle size distribution of silicon phases within the untreated Al–27Si alloy. Derived from optical microscopy data, the plot provides a quantitative baseline for the size characteristics of the silicon particles before the application of any T6 heat treatment processes.

caption: Hardness values of CoCrFeNiZr x eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) plotted as a function of Zr content.
summary: This figure illustrates the hardness characteristics of CoCrFeNiZr x EHEAs. The data provides a quantitative assessment of how varying the Zr concentration influences the mechanical hardness of these high-entropy alloy systems, serving as a primary indicator of the material's resistance to deformation under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Representative transmission FTIR spectra showing the characteristic decrease of the acrylate peak during the UV-light irradiation process for the tested formulations.
summary: Representative transmission FTIR spectra illustrate the chemical evolution of the formulations during UV-light irradiation. The magnification of the acrylate peak highlights the progressive decrease in double bond concentration over time, providing direct spectroscopic evidence of the polymerization process occurring within the bio-glass containing resin formulations.

caption: Schematic illustration of the linear scanning strategy employed during the selective laser melting process to minimize thermal gradients.
summary: A linear scanning strategy is schematically illustrated to demonstrate the approach used during selective laser melting. This method is specifically adopted to reduce the temperature gradient across the specimen during the printing process, thereby helping to control the thermal history and microstructure of the resulting FeCoCrNi alloy component.

caption: Indexed SAED pattern of a quasi-spherical Cr-rich particle in S2_3, demonstrating the diffraction relationship with the Cu-matrix.
summary: This indexed SAED pattern represents the diffraction relationship between the Cu-matrix and the quasi-spherical Cr-rich phase particles in the S2_3 sample. The reciprocal crystallographic relationship is characterized by (110) Cr-rich || (111) Cu-matrix and (100) Cr-rich || (110) Cu-matrix, confirming the structural alignment between the precipitate and the matrix.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Fe-Ni-Mo system at 1600K, detailing the phase equilibria for the ternary alloy composition.
summary: Displayed is the ternary phase diagram for the Fe-Ni-Mo system at 1600K, which details the equilibrium phase relationships for this specific alloy combination. The diagram provides essential insights into the phase stability and compositional boundaries, facilitating a comprehensive understanding of the material's behavior at the specified high-temperature state.

caption: STEM-ADF image and EDS elemental maps of the R725-Control alloy after 10,000 h of exposure at 700 °C, highlighting the presence of δ, α-Cr, and μ phases.
summary: The R725-Control alloy microstructure after 10,000 h at 700 °C is characterized by plate-like δ, blocky α-Cr, and wavy γ′ phases. STEM-ADF imaging reveals that μ phase precipitates are attached to the δ phase, providing a detailed view of the in-grain microstructure and elemental distribution within the control sample.

caption: Principal component analysis of elemental contents in bulk-ore samples from Hongge, illustrating the clustering of OPH and massive oxide ores based on V-Ti-Nb-Ta associations, while GH oxide ores form a distinct cluster enriched in P, and sulfide ores are characterized by a Cu-Co-Ni-Fe-Cr-S association.
summary: Principal component analysis of bulk-ore elemental data reveals distinct geochemical groupings. OPH and massive oxide ores cluster together due to V-Ti-Nb-Ta associations, whereas GH oxide ores are separated by P enrichment. Sulfide ores form a unique cluster defined by a Cu-Co-Ni-Fe-Cr-S association, reflecting their distinct elemental composition and phase partitioning.

caption: Dark field TEM micrograph of the RHEAN3 coating cross-section.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging of the RHEAN3 coating cross-section confirms the amorphous nature of the material. The absence of columnar features is consistent with the bright field TEM observations, reinforcing the conclusion that the RHEAN3 coating lacks crystalline columnar growth in its cross-sectional structure.

caption: Microhardness distribution (HV0.1) across the middle reheated region of the specimen.
summary: This panel presents the microhardness map (HV0.1) for the middle reheated region. It highlights the mechanical property distribution within this specific zone, offering insights into how the reheating process has influenced the hardness profile compared to other regions of the processed material.

caption: Arrhenius plot of ln(k) versus -1000/RT derived from hardness data, utilized to calculate the activation energy Q for the precipitation process.
summary: Utilizing the slope from the Arrhenius plot of ln(k) versus -1000/RT, the activation energy Q for the precipitation process was determined to be 160.1 kJ/mol. This result is highly consistent with the established diffusion activation energy of 160 kJ/mol for Nb in SLM-manufactured IN718 superalloys.

caption: Relative density plotted as a function of alpha, comparing the proposed exponential fitting model against the traditional Gibson–Ashby equation.
summary: This plot illustrates the relative density of the material as a function of alpha. It demonstrates that the final density results follow an exponential trend, which is evaluated by comparing the proposed fitting model against the established Gibson–Ashby equation to determine the accuracy of the density predictions.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength plotted against fracture elongation for SEBM-fabricated 316L stainless steel compared to various additive manufacturing and conventional processing methods, highlighting the strength–ductility trade-off boundary.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical performance of SEBM-fabricated 316L stainless steel relative to other manufacturing techniques. Most samples follow a standard inverse correlation between ultimate tensile strength and fracture elongation, forming a trade-off envelope. Notably, the SEBM-fabricated samples (red stars) exceed this boundary, demonstrating a simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility.

caption: Elevated temperature elongation performance of VIC-fabricated LW 4280 relative to Rene 80, MAR-M-247, and IN 738.
summary: Comparison of high-temperature elongation shows that LW 4280, fabricated through a VIC process, maintains higher elongation values at elevated temperatures compared to traditional Ni-superalloys including Rene 80, MAR-M-247, and IN 738. This demonstrates the superior ductility performance of the LW 4280 alloy under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Summary table of magnetic characteristic parameters for MGS-1 and MGS-1C simulants, crushed LIS green body, and various sintered samples processed in air or simulated Martian atmosphere.
summary: This table presents the magnetic characteristic parameters extracted from hysteresis curves measured at 300 K with an applied field of ± 1 T. It compares pristine MGS-1 and MGS-1C simulants, crushed LIS green bodies, and samples sintered under different atmospheric conditions, specifically air and simulated Martian atmosphere at various temperatures.

caption: Specific wear rate of the steel-bonded TiC-based cermets plotted as a function of temperature.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific wear rate of the steel-bonded TiC-based cermets across the tested temperature range. It provides a quantitative measure of material loss, which correlates with the observed morphological changes, such as debris compaction and thermal softening, occurring in the wear tracks at elevated temperatures.

caption: Cumulative strain versus cycle number for HT1 annealed trabecular porous Ta, demonstrating the influence of stress on cyclic deformation.
summary: Representing the HT1 annealed condition, this plot tracks cumulative strain relative to the number of cycles at various stress levels. It characterizes the mechanical stability and cyclic strain accumulation of the trabecular porous Ta after the HT1 heat treatment process, highlighting the material's response to cyclic stress application.

caption: Quasi-static compression load-displacement profile for the bionic hierarchical cellular structure designed with a cell wall thickness of 0.4 mm.
summary: Shown is the quasi-static compression load-displacement curve for the bionic hierarchical cellular structure with a 0.4 mm cell wall thickness. This result demonstrates the mechanical response of the structure, allowing for a direct comparison with other wall thickness configurations to evaluate the influence of geometry on the material's mechanical performance.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation map of heat-treated DSS 1.4462, viewed parallel to the build direction.
summary: The IPF orientation map, captured parallel to the build direction, provides a detailed visualization of the crystallographic texture in heat-treated DSS 1.4462. Analysis of this map, in conjunction with corresponding inverse pole figures, reveals a strong <111> texture specifically within the δ-ferrite phase of the material's microstructure.

caption: Derivative melting curves between 60 and 95 °C for the second cycle (left) paired with schematic diagrams illustrating the specific melting events associated with each peak (right).
summary: Derivative melting curves between 60 and 95 °C highlight distinct thermal transition peaks for the hydrogels. These peaks are correlated with specific melting events depicted in the accompanying schematics, providing a mechanistic view of how different DNA hydrogel compositions undergo structural dissociation during the second heating cycle.

caption: Longitudinal side-view of the AlCoCrFeNiMn high entropy alloy after 1100 °C heat treatment, highlighting phase transformation and strain characteristics.
summary: This longitudinal side-view shows the AlCoCrFeNiMn high entropy alloy after 1100 °C heat treatment. Phase maps demonstrate an increase in fcc phase volume fraction to approximately 70%, confirming precipitation from the bcc phase. Additionally, KAM maps characterize the micro-elastic strain and dislocation density changes resulting from the heat treatment process.

caption: LCO pattern layout for rear-Al cell fabrication, showing the specific alignment of LCO dots beneath the rear side fingers of front-metallised precursors.
summary: The schematic depicts the LCO pattern configuration specifically designed for rear-Al cell fabrication. In this setup, the LCO dots are precisely aligned to be positioned directly beneath the rear side fingers of the front-metallised precursors, facilitating the integration of the LCO structure into the rear-Al TOPCon cell architecture.

caption: Local hardness measurement map characterizing the mechanical consistency of WAAM-fabricated 316L stainless steel.
summary: Local hardness measurements are shown for 316L stainless steel fabricated via the wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) process. This map illustrates the spatial variation of hardness across the material, allowing for an assessment of the mechanical uniformity achieved through this specific additive manufacturing technique compared to other methods.

caption: Bottom x-z cross-section hardness map showing the Vickers microhardness profile, separated by a 0.5 mm gap from the middle section.
summary: The bottom x-z cross-section hardness map displays Vickers microhardness measurements taken with a 0.5 kg load. This section, separated by 0.5 mm from the middle layer, confirms that the mechanical properties remain stable, as little variation in hardness and elastic modulus was observed within the subsequent build layers.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of mechanically treated samples across various annealing levels, with long-dashed lines marking Cr2O3 and y-Fe positions, and short-dashed lines identifying Fe2O3 in the 1000 °C ground sample.
summary: This panel presents a comprehensive summary of X-ray diffractograms for mechanically treated samples subjected to different annealing levels. Key phase markers are identified, with long-dashed lines indicating Cr2O3 and y-Fe positions, while short-dashed lines highlight Fe2O3 in the 1000 °C ground sample, facilitating detailed phase composition analysis.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry response of L-PBF NiTi specimen A4 (87 J/mm3) immersed in 0.9 wt.% NaCl solution, featuring a small anodic current peak at approximately 0.3 V SCE when the cathode scanning range is reduced.
summary: Sample A4, fabricated with an energy density of 87 J/mm3, exhibits a cyclic voltammetry curve similar to other samples in wide potential ranges. However, reducing the cathode scanning range to -1 V SCE reveals a small anodic current peak at approximately 0.3 V SCE, indicating specific electrochemical behavior.

caption: Cooling dilatometry curve for specimen S1 showing the linear contraction segment and the tangent-intersection method used to determine the martensite-start temperature of 277 °C.
summary: Specimen S1 exhibits a martensite-start temperature of 277 °C as determined by the tangent-intersection method applied to the cooling dilatometry curve. This thermal analysis technique identifies the onset of the phase transformation by analyzing the deviation from the linear contraction segment observed during the cooling process after austenitizing at 1150 °C.

caption: Tabulated EDS compositional analysis results corresponding to the four points identified in the magnified SEM image of the Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy.
summary: This table presents the quantitative EDS compositional analysis results obtained from the four specific spots marked in the magnified SEM image. These data points provide the chemical composition of the secondary phase and the matrix, confirming the presence of Mg and Zn within the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Optimization progress showing the minimization of root mean square (RMS) error between predicted and in-situ measured vat substrate temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the optimization process by tracking the reduction of RMS error between predicted and in-situ measured vat substrate temperatures. The curve demonstrates the convergence behavior of the model, providing a quantitative assessment of the accuracy achieved during the temperature prediction optimization phase for the vat substrate system.

caption: Long-term cycling stability profiles of Zn-air batteries with Ni3FeN and RuO2 catalysts, tested at 10 mA cm-2 with 20-minute cycles.
summary: This panel presents the discharge and charge voltage profiles over time, demonstrating the cycling stability of the batteries. The Ni3FeN-driven battery exhibits superior performance, maintaining stability over 310 cycles (100 hours), significantly outperforming the RuO2-driven battery, which only achieved 90 cycles over 30 hours under identical testing conditions.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction obtained via laser scanning confocal microscopy, demonstrating the uniformity in height and contour of the micro bionic CE lens structure.
summary: Laser scanning confocal microscopy (LSCM) was utilized to generate a 3D observation of the lens. This visualization confirms the high degree of uniformity in both the height and the contour of the micro bionic CE lens, validating the precision of the manufacturing process used to create the structure.

caption: Specific wear rate measurements for as-built and heat-treated specimens.
summary: Specific wear rate values are presented for both as-built and heat-treated conditions. Consistent with the volume loss data, the as-built samples demonstrate superior wear performance, showing lower specific wear rates than the heat-treated samples regardless of the applied normal load during the tribological testing process.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the average γ′ phase radius at 900 °C for Ni–20Co–14Al and Ni–20Co–14Al–8Cr alloys, calculated via TC-PRISMA.
summary: This plot illustrates the growth kinetics of the γ′ phase at 900 °C. TC-PRISMA calculations reveal that after 10 s, the coarsening rate of the average radius in the Ni–20Co–14Al alloy significantly exceeds that observed in the Cr-containing Ni–20Co–14Al–8Cr alloy, indicating a slower coarsening process in the latter.

caption: Pearson correlation analysis evaluating the influence of CW laser processing parameters on the elongation (EL) of the processed materials.
summary: Pearson correlation analysis is utilized here to determine the impact of CW laser processing parameters on material elongation. This visualization highlights the statistical dependencies between input variables and the resulting ductility, offering insights into how specific laser settings correlate with the elongation properties observed in the manufactured samples.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for intergranular austenite-ferrite interfaces represented in the ferrite crystal lattice frame, with color intensity indicating multiples of random distribution (MRD).
summary: This heatmap displays the grain boundary plane distribution for intergranular austenite-ferrite interfaces within the ferrite lattice frame. The color scale represents MRD values, providing a quantitative measure of preferred orientations. These distributions are essential for understanding the crystallographic relationship and habit planes formed during the intergranular transformation path.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) versus sliding velocity in a helium (He) atmosphere at 750 °C, where values consistently exceed 1.0 and exhibit a slight decreasing trend at 20 N.
summary: In a helium atmosphere at 750 °C, the coefficient of friction consistently remains above 1.0 across all tested conditions. While most loading conditions show no specific trend, a slight, steady decrease in the COF is observed as the sliding velocity increases under a high load of 20 N.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of the 15-5PH stainless steel powder, highlighting characteristic D10, D50, and D90 values.
summary: The particle size distribution of the 15-5PH stainless steel powder is quantified with specific diameter thresholds. The D10, D50, and D90 values are measured at 19.4 μm, 33.2 μm, and 50.9 μm, respectively. These metrics confirm a controlled distribution range, ensuring optimal packing density and process stability during the LPBF manufacturing process.

caption: Local transformation sequence of Point-C within the gamma-prime phase, demonstrating a path through O, CSF, APB, CSF, and back to O.
summary: Point-C, located inside the gamma-prime phase, undergoes a specific local transformation sequence. The displacement path follows the progression O to CSF, then to APB, back to CSF, and finally returning to the perfect crystal state O, as clearly depicted in the corresponding GSF energy surface plot.

caption: Coercive field (Hc) as a function of layer thickness for Py (5 nm) covered by variable C60 (blue closed circles) and C60 (16 nm) covered by variable Py (red open squares), with a 0.5 nm thickness uncertainty.
summary: Coercive field measurements are plotted for two distinct bilayer configurations. The data illustrates the magnetic response of Py layers relative to C60 thickness variations. The analysis accounts for a 0.5 nm thickness error, providing a clear comparison of how layer sequence and thickness influence the coercive field in these magnetic heterostructures.

caption: Drag ratios LVB/LVV (solid line) and LVB/LBB (dashed line) for an A-1 at.% B alloy, calculated via KineCluE across a temperature range of 300 to 800 K with a fixed vacancy concentration of 10^-5.
summary: Calculated drag ratios for an A-1 at.% B alloy demonstrate the influence of bound vacancy-solute pairs on transport coefficients LVB and LBB. These KineCluE simulations, performed at a fixed vacancy concentration of 10^-5, illustrate that the alloy experiences significant solute drag under irradiation conditions between 300 and 800 K.

caption: Rhombic dodecahedron (RD) lattice unit cell geometry.
summary: The rhombic dodecahedron (RD) unit cell is depicted as the fundamental building block of the lattice structure. This geometry belongs to the BCC crystal system and features a maximum connectivity of Z = 8. The porous lattice is constructed by repeating this 3.3 mm x 3.3 mm x 3.3 mm unit cell.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum of the CCNZ powder, indicating elemental concentrations of 2.06 ± 0.05 wt% Cr and 1.11 ± 0.13 wt% Nb.
summary: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum provides a quantitative elemental analysis of the CCNZ feedstock powder. The results confirm the presence of alloying elements, specifically identifying concentrations of 2.06 ± 0.05 wt% for Chromium and 1.11 ± 0.13 wt% for Niobium within the powder composition.

caption: STEM-BF micrograph of the Alloy 2120 oxide layer, displaying the interface between the Pt coating and the bulk material, alongside corresponding EDXS elemental maps and a high-resolution TEM-BF image featuring indexed FFT diffraction patterns.
summary: This STEM-BF micrograph characterizes the oxide layer formed on Alloy 2120. It highlights the interface between the protective Pt coating and the bulk material. The analysis includes EDXS elemental mapping and high-resolution TEM-BF imaging, with superimposed indexed FFT diffraction patterns confirming the structural characteristics of the observed oxide phases.

caption: STEM-HAADF image illustrating stacking faults and microtwins within the matrix of the 718Plus alloy after creep deformation.
summary: This STEM-HAADF image captures the internal structural features of the 718Plus matrix after a 650 °C/800 MPa creep test. Stacking faults and microtwins are clearly observed within the matrix, providing evidence of the plastic deformation mechanisms active during the high-temperature creep process in this superalloy.

caption: Time sweep measurements of the filament at 130 °C, conducted for 30 minutes at 1 Hz under 0.1% and 1% strain amplitudes.
summary: Time sweep measurements at 130 °C reveal the temporal evolution of viscosity, elastic modulus, and loss modulus. These tests, performed at 0.1% and 1% strain, highlight the material's stability over 30 minutes, although low strain amplitudes are noted to present challenges regarding data quality during the testing process.

caption: Latent variable distribution showing TRS separability across the dataset, with an overlaid line graph representing the mean reduction in Co pool size as a percentage of the maximum value relative to latent dimension shifts.
summary: This latent variable plot demonstrates clear separability among TRS values, where high TRS images cluster around -1 and low TRS images around 1.5 on latent dimension 6. The overlaid line graph illustrates how changing latent dimensions correlates with a reduction in Co pool sizes, highlighting structural refinement across the dataset.

caption: Boxplot comparing green density variations across different coupon sizes relative to their placement along the build depth, with asterisks marking mean values and dots representing outliers.
summary: This boxplot demonstrates how green density and in-plane deviation range fluctuate based on sample placement and coupon size. Data indicates that taller parts, specifically the 15x10x10 mm³ samples, experience a shift toward lower mean and median green density values despite having an increased sample volume compared to smaller coupons.

caption: Elemental composition (wt%) of the BG and BG AC3D scaffolds.
summary: This table presents the quantitative elemental composition in weight percentage (wt%) for both BG and BG AC3D scaffolds. The data provides a precise comparison of the chemical makeup, confirming the successful incorporation of elements and the relative proportions of constituents in the final printed scaffold materials.

caption: Comparative analysis of mechanical properties between the current semi-solid sintered alloys and representative Ti-based composites featuring typical microstructures.
summary: Mechanical properties of the current semi-solid sintered samples are compared against representative Ti-based composites with typical microstructures in this plot. This visualization serves to benchmark the performance of the newly developed alloy against established materials, highlighting its relative mechanical standing within the broader context of Ti-based composite research.

caption: SHAP dependence plot displaying the influence of specimen state on the effective stress ratio, with dot colors representing the effective stress ratio.
summary: Analyzing this plot alongside panels (e) and (f) is essential because stress amplitude, mean stress, and stress ratio are highly interrelated. The SHAP values for each state appear on the same vertical line, and potential overlaps between data points are noted due to the discrete nature of the state variable.

caption: 3D cloud map of the reconstructed profile for the W2 sample.
summary: The 3D cloud map of the reconstructed profile for the W2 sample illustrates the geometric morphology of the deposited hybrid structural part. The reconstruction indicates a smooth deposition process, confirming the absence of defects like humps, splashes, or collapses during the EB-DED fabrication of the Al–Si–Cu/Al–Cu material.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image focusing on the first intersection point of two superlattice extrinsic stacking faults (SESF-SESF).
summary: This atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image highlights the first intersection point between two superlattice extrinsic stacking faults. The visualization allows for the detailed examination of the atomic configuration at the intersection, which is critical for understanding the interaction mechanisms of stacking faults within the γ′ precipitate structure.

caption: HR-MAS NMR spectra comparing the chitosan-based hydrogel CS-AD-1 with a physical cross-linked control; panels (I) and (III) display 1H and 13C spectra for the seaweed-derived hydrogel, while (II) shows the 1H spectrum for the control sample.
summary: High-resolution magic angle spinning NMR spectroscopy confirms covalent bond formation in the CS-AD-1 hydrogel. Comparing 1H and 13C spectra of the seaweed-derived hydrogel against a physical cross-linked control reveals distinct structural differences. A shoulder peak in the 13C spectrum of CS-AD-1 specifically supports the assignment of covalent cross-linking between chitosan and seaweed extract.

caption: Calculated workfunctions for (111) surfaces with 0.25 ML atomic oxygen adsorbed at fcc sites, comparing systems with and without Mo doping.
summary: This panel displays DFT-calculated workfunctions for (111) surfaces following oxygen adsorption at 0.25 ML coverage. The data compares undoped and Mo-doped surfaces, revealing that Mo-doping is consistently associated with stronger oxygen binding when oxygen atoms are directly bonded to the Mo dopant atoms within the surface structure.

caption: Deconvolution of the Raman spectrum from the central grain region (1) using pseudo-Voight functions to identify four distinct peaks (I-IV) and their cumulative fit.
summary: The Raman spectrum from the central grain region is fitted using pseudo-Voight functions to resolve four specific peaks. Peaks (I) and (II) correspond to the TO phonon band, while peaks (III) and (IV) are attributed to LO phonons, providing a detailed breakdown of the vibrational modes within the less-reacted core.

caption: Atomic configuration of the Σ3 (11-1) [110] grain boundary in FCC Ni, highlighting the grain boundary plane with a dashed red line and tested hydrogen interstitial sites.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the Σ3 (11-1) [110] grain boundary structure in FCC Ni. The dashed red line marks the interface plane, while blue crosses denote tested hydrogen positions. This structural representation provides the basis for calculating segregation energy profiles and assessing electronic interactions within three atomic layers of the interface.

caption: Tafel plot illustrating the electrochemical polarization behavior of various austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys tested in [EMIM][CF3SO3] ionic liquid at 80 °C.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical polarization behavior of austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys in [EMIM][CF3SO3] at 80 °C. These plots are essential for determining corrosion potentials, as referenced in the study, and highlight the varying corrosion resistance of different alloys, such as the relatively poor performance of Inconel 625.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of PCL/BT composites with varying BaTiO₃ concentrations.
summary: Current-voltage curves for PCL/BT composites show the electrical response of the material under varying BaTiO₃ concentrations. Consistent with the conductivity measurements, these I-V curves reflect the changes in electrical behavior as the filler content is adjusted within the PCL matrix.

caption: Equation of state (EOS) curves for ternary compounds comparing CTIP-predicted lines against DFT-calculated data points.
summary: This plot displays the equation of state for various ternary compounds, illustrating the predictive performance of the CTIP model. By comparing CTIP-predicted lines with DFT-calculated data points, the figure demonstrates excellent consistency and validates the model's capability in accurately predicting alloy interactions between metals within the ternary system.

caption: UMAP projection plot IV showing the classification of deposits related to A-type magmatic sources.
summary: This UMAP plot illustrates the classification of deposits associated with A-type magmas. The clustering pattern reveals the geochemical distinctiveness of these deposits. Overlaps within the plot indicate that quartz trace-element patterns are similar in adjacent clusters, pointing to consistent geochemical signatures across the A-type magma-related deposit categories.

caption: Reflectance spectral response of the sensor under 10 mW of 980 nm pump power, illustrating the spectral shift behavior across the tested humidity range.
summary: This panel displays the reflectance spectral response of the sensor when subjected to a 10 mW pump power at 980 nm. As the relative humidity increases, the spectral characteristics of the sensor are recorded, providing insight into how higher pump power levels influence the sensor's response to humidity variations.

caption: Static magnetization curves for M300 alloy before and after heat treatment, measured within a 25 kA/m field intensity range.
summary: Panel a displays the static magnetization curves for the M300 alloy, tested across a 25 kA/m field intensity range. These curves illustrate the magnetic response of the material, providing a baseline for comparing the magnetic properties before and after the applied heat treatment process.

caption: Decay curve and biexponential fit of fluorescence lifetime for TPU/3 C composite.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime measurements for the TPU/3 C composite are shown as a nonlinear decay curve at 465 nm. The data is fitted using a biexponential function to characterize the emission decay, reflecting the influence of the 3% coumarin concentration on the composite's fluorescence properties at room temperature.

caption: EDS map showing Cr distribution in the HIP + HT condition, highlighting improved elemental uniformity.
summary: Chromium distribution in the HIP + HT condition is presented in this EDS map. The results show substantial homogenization of chromium throughout the microstructure, confirming that the combined HIP and heat treatment processes successfully mitigate the solute segregation observed in the as-sintered state.

caption: Nano-topology visualization captured via atomic force microscopy, highlighting the surface features located between unmelted powder particles on the AM Ti–6Al–4V specimen.
summary: Nano-topology of the additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V surface is characterized using atomic force microscopy. This panel focuses on the specific surface morphology found between unmelted powder particles. The imaging provides detailed insight into the micro-scale surface state, which complements the macro-roughness data and contributes to the overall surface integrity assessment.

caption: Current-Voltage characteristics of V-based TLM structures measured at varying inter-electrode spacings L, demonstrating linear behavior indicative of high-quality ohmic contact formation.
summary: The I-V characteristics of V-based TLM structures are presented for different inter-electrode spacings L. The observed pronounced linearity of these curves confirms the successful formation of high-quality ohmic contacts within the test structures, establishing a reliable baseline for subsequent electrical resistance analysis and material characterization.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the β-Ti phase, corresponding to the blue square region in the TEM micrograph.
summary: This SAED pattern corresponds to the blue square region in the TEM micrograph, identifying the β-Ti phase in the [113] zonal axis. The analysis confirms the presence of the β phase in the heat-treated Ti–6Al–4V alloy, demonstrating the coarsening of both α and β phases following stress relief annealing.

caption: Block diagram illustrating the dual-stage plasma current control architecture, which integrates vision-based width measurements to calculate the width error and determine the desired plasma current input.
summary: This block diagram depicts the dual-stage plasma current control system. The controller utilizes vision-based width measurements to compute the width error, which is then used to calculate the desired plasma current input. This input is formulated as a combination of feedforward and feedback components to ensure precise plasma current regulation.

caption: Atomic configuration of the [11-2] plane within the intrinsic stacking fault (ISF) structure of the Al–Mg–Si alloy.
summary: This panel displays the atomic arrangement of the [11-2] plane specifically for the intrinsic stacking fault (ISF) structure. It serves as a comparative model to the perfect structure, allowing for the calculation and analysis of the generalized stacking fault energy within the Al–Mg–Si alloy system under investigation.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of the osteogenic marker OCN in BMSCs cultured on P and ZP scaffolds.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining of the osteogenic marker OCN provides visual verification of the pro-osteogenic potential of the ZP scaffold. The presence and distribution of OCN in the BMSCs cultured on ZP scaffolds further support the conclusion that the material environment successfully drives the osteogenic differentiation process.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of Ni-Cr coatings electrodeposited on a copper substrate at applied potentials of -1.04 V, -1.08 V, and -1.12 V.
summary: This panel displays the XRD patterns for Ni-Cr alloy coatings electrodeposited at potentials of -1.04 V, -1.08 V, and -1.12 V. The diffraction data reveals that characteristic peaks of the copper substrate predominate with strong intensity and distinct shapes as the 2θ value increases across the measured potential range.

caption: Surface topography of the polished sample visualized through laser confocal microscopy.
summary: Polished sample surface topography is shown here, captured by laser confocal microscopy. This image illustrates the surface state following a polishing treatment, allowing for a detailed assessment of roughness. It contributes to the overall analysis of how mechanical preparation methods affect the material's surface integrity before thermal exposure.

caption: Cross-sectional view of a clad deposited with LBID at a mean surface-energy density of 94 J/mm2.
summary: Presented is the cross-section of a clad deposited at a mean surface-energy density of 94 J/mm2. This final example in the series confirms that higher energy densities consistently lead to increased clad width and dilution, providing a clear visual representation of the process outcomes at high energy inputs.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a conventionally aged sample after 19.1 h of ageing, demonstrating significant precipitate growth.
summary: Following 19.1 h of ageing, this atom probe tomography reconstruction reveals a clear increase in both the overall volume fraction and the size of the γ′ and γ′′ precipitates compared to earlier time points. The turquoise and brown interfaces demonstrate the progression of precipitate development throughout the conventionally aged sample.

caption: Horizontal displacement distribution at a final shearing state of u/L = 0.1 for a corrugated surface with d/l = 0.240.
summary: Depicted here is the horizontal displacement field for a surface with a corrugation depth ratio of 0.240 at a final shearing state of u/L = 0.1. The DIC analysis captures the displacement distribution, demonstrating the influence of this specific corrugation geometry on the interface micromechanics of the sand mass.

caption: Topographic height map of the fracture surface for the peened sample, exhibiting an average surface roughness (SA) of approximately 10 μm.
summary: The topographic height map displays the fracture surface of the peened sample. Analysis reveals an average surface roughness (SA) of approximately 10 μm, consistent with the as-built condition. The measurement covers a 3 × 5 mm2 area located 5 mm from the crack starter notch tip.

caption: STEM-HAADF image, SAED pattern, and EDS elemental maps of the internal oxidation zone in CGA-CoNi, showing dark-contrast oxide particles dispersed within a (Co,Ni)O scale matrix.
summary: This panel illustrates the internal oxidation zone of the (Co,Ni)O scale in CGA-CoNi. The microstructure features dark-contrast oxide particles embedded within gray-contrast oxides. The oxidation process elevates local oxygen partial pressure, which drives the formation of spinel oxides at the Cr2O3 interface within the internal oxidation zone.

caption: Optical reconstructions of 26 binary computer-generated holograms (CGHs) captured at a 6.3 kHz pulse-to-pulse modulation rate.
summary: This panel displays the optical reconstructions of 26 binary computer-generated holograms. These images represent the 26 alphabet characters, which were consecutively captured by an image sensor during the 6.3 kHz pulse-to-pulse spatial light modulation process, demonstrating the capability of the holographic system to generate distinct, high-speed optical patterns.

caption: Angle-dependent reflection spectra of the CSP4 opal film, demonstrating its characteristic goniochromic behavior.
summary: Angle-dependent reflection spectra of the CSP4 opal film are presented to illustrate its goniochromic behavior. This optical property indicates that the reflected color of the material changes depending on the viewing angle, a characteristic feature of the opal film structure composed of the optimized polymer compound CSP4.

caption: DIC-resolved axial strain-time history for fully supported top-clad and sandwich samples under low-velocity impact.
summary: Digital Image Correlation (DIC) is utilized to resolve the axial strain-time history for top-clad and sandwich samples during low-velocity impact. This plot provides a detailed temporal evolution of the strain response, complementing the force-time data to characterize the deformation behavior of the samples under the specified loading conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms obtained in the BRB buffer/1,2-DCE LLI at pH 6, showing the electrochemical response for the baseline, 150 µM BIL, and 150 µM BIL with 50 µM TMACl conditions.
summary: Electrochemical behavior at pH 6 remains consistent with the observations at pH 4, where the introduction of BIL results in no significant changes to the recorded cyclic voltammograms. The comparison between the solid red and dashed black curves confirms that BIL does not disrupt the electrochemical signal in this acidic environment.

caption: One-axis equilibrium phase fraction versus temperature diagram for 420 steel calculated using Thermo-Calc.
summary: Displaying the phase fraction as a function of temperature, this diagram identifies the critical phase transformations governing the equilibrium microstructure of 420 steel. It confirms the sequence of δ-ferrite formation, austenite formation via δ→γ transformation, carbide precipitation, and austenite decomposition, providing a quantitative view of phase evolution during thermal processing.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the grain structure evolution in IN 718 during single-layer DED-L processing at 840 W and 10 mm/s, showing the longitudinal section and curved top surface.
summary: This 3D reconstruction illustrates the development of grain structure in IN 718 during the first layer of DED-L deposition. The visualization reveals how the solidification process is physically constrained by the geometry of the moving molten pool, providing a comprehensive view of grain evolution across the longitudinal and top surfaces.

caption: Frequency distribution histogram of GND values for the HT2-treated ZGH4142 specimen, reflecting the moderate reduction in dislocation density.
summary: This histogram for the HT2-treated ZGH4142 specimen shows a distribution of GND values centered at 0.7 × 10 14 m −2. This confirms a moderate reduction in dislocation density compared to the as-printed condition, highlighting the impact of the HT2 treatment on the microstructure of the superalloy.

caption: Polarization curves illustrating electrochemical behavior across cathodic, active, and passivation zones for cold-sprayed Ti coatings.
summary: The polarization curves demonstrate the electrochemical response of cold-sprayed Ti coatings within a potential range of -0.1 V to 1.8 V vs Ag/AgCl. The data highlights three distinct stages: cathodic, active, and passivation. The observed electrochemical behavior is attributed to the formation of a stable, thick superficial oxide layer.

caption: Dielectric permittivity comparison between un-poled and poled LIG/PVDF-TrFE composite samples.
summary: This plot compares the dielectric permittivity of LIG/PVDF-TrFE composites before and after the poling process. Structural changes observed via XRD correlate with these variations in dielectric permittivity. The data indicates that poling successfully aligns dipoles within the material, resulting in a higher dielectric constant and improved overall dielectric performance.

caption: Maximum wear depth measurements for Stellite 6, C-GC, and C-LMD alloys as a function of temperature.
summary: Maximum wear depth values for Stellite 6, C-LMD, and C-GC are presented as a function of sample temperature. These measurements, taken under standardized tribological conditions of 23 N load and 20 Hz frequency, provide a quantitative assessment of the surface damage evolution across the different alloy specimens tested.

caption: Extracted tensile parameters including yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to failure for straight-edged samples.
summary: Extracted tensile parameters for straight-edged samples are presented here, specifically highlighting yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to failure. These metrics quantify the mechanical properties derived from the stress-strain data, allowing for a direct comparison of strength and ductility across different sample configurations tested in the study.

caption: Representative unit cell of the BCC lattice subjected to uniaxial compression.
summary: This panel illustrates the representative unit cell of a BCC lattice structure under uniaxial compression. A force analysis is performed on this structure to determine the mechanical response of the lattice members, providing the foundational geometric basis for evaluating the axial and shear forces acting within the unit cell.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) profile of Mg–15Ni alloy after exposure to pure hydrogen gas.
summary: This panel displays the thermal desorption spectroscopy results for the Mg–15Ni alloy sample following exposure to a pure hydrogen environment. The plot serves as a baseline measurement for hydrogen release characteristics, illustrating the specific desorption behavior of the material under these controlled experimental conditions without additional atmospheric contaminants.

caption: Schematic illustration of the laser metal deposition process for the HY282 + SiC functionally graded metal matrix composite, highlighting the back and forth scanning strategy used to fabricate a 100 mm long and 8 mm tall wall on a 1020 steel substrate.
summary: This schematic depicts the laser metal deposition process for fabricating a functionally graded metal matrix composite wall. The process utilizes a back and forth scanning strategy on a 1020 steel substrate to create a 100 mm long and 8 mm tall deposit, with SiC content increasing by 1 wt% per 0.5 mm layer.

caption: 3D laser microscopic surface topography of the alumina powder bed after the addition of 0.5 wt% flow agent.
summary: 3D laser microscopy reveals the surface topography of the alumina powder bed after the addition of 0.5 wt% flow agent. The image confirms that the powder bed exhibits a uniform and smooth surface layer after spreading, validating the positive impact of the flow agent on the powder bed's structural quality.

caption: Contour map showing the pressure drop as a function of cell size and relative density for Bccz DOE cells.
summary: This contour plot maps the pressure drop across a design space defined by cell size and relative density. It reveals the interaction between these two geometric variables, allowing for the identification of optimal regions where pressure drop is minimized or maximized within the Bccz DOE cell architecture.

caption: Electronic density of states (DOS) comparison between austenitic and martensitic structures for Ni8Mn5Ti3 and Ni8Mn6Ti2, with the Fermi level indicated by a dashed line.
summary: Electronic density of states plots reveal that the lower symmetry of the martensitic phase induces energy level splitting. This structural change results in a reduced electronic DOS value near the Fermi level compared to the austenite phase, consistent with the Jahn-Teller effect explaining the relative stability of the martensite.

caption: Ductile-to-brittle transition temperature (DBTT) curves fitted with the Boltzmann function for the heat-treated specimens.
summary: Impact toughness of the heat-treated specimens is characterized by DBTT curves fitted using the Boltzmann function. These curves illustrate the transition in impact energy across varying temperatures, which correlates with macroscopic observations of reduced plastic deformability and shear lip area as the impact testing temperature decreases during the mechanical evaluation.

caption: Temperature-dependent 2NN N–N SRO parameter for 1 at.% N in Fe70Ni10Cr20, where negative values signify the formation of 2NN N–N pairs.
summary: This graph illustrates the 2NN N–N SRO parameter as a function of temperature. The observed negative values reflect the formation of 2NN N–N pairs, which is consistent with established theoretical and experimental findings regarding the local atomic structure and short-range ordering of nitrogen in this specific alloy composition.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from polarization curves for Ni1Co3@NC catalysts synthesized at different temperatures.
summary: Tafel analysis for the Ni1Co3@NC catalysts at various temperatures is presented to evaluate reaction kinetics. The results indicate that the Ni1Co3@NC-800 sample achieves the lowest Tafel slope of 57 ± 3 mV/dec, confirming its enhanced electrocatalytic activity and favorable reaction mechanism compared to the other synthesized temperature variants.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the FeCoCrNiMn-(N,Si) high-entropy alloy after tensile deformation at 873 K, revealing the presence of shear bands and microbands.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging of the FeCoCrNiMn-(N,Si) high-entropy alloy following tensile deformation at 873 K reveals the formation of shear bands and microbands. Selected area electron diffraction analysis confirms that these observed deformation bands are distinct from deformation twinning, indicating specific localized plastic deformation mechanisms within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Normalized histogram of grain aspect ratio for the 20 K undercooling condition, showing the distribution of grain shapes.
summary: The histogram presents the aspect ratio distribution for grains formed at 20 K undercooling. The data characterizes the shape of the columnar grains, confirming the structural shift toward elongated morphologies as the nucleation undercooling increases and the equiaxed grain zone is eliminated.

caption: Quasi-static compression load-displacement response for the bionic hierarchical cellular structure featuring a cell wall thickness of 0.2 mm.
summary: This panel displays the quasi-static compression load-displacement curve for the bionic hierarchical cellular structure with a 0.2 mm cell wall thickness. The data illustrates the specific mechanical response of this configuration, contributing to the comparative analysis of how varying wall thicknesses influence the structural performance of these novel bionic designs.

caption: Arrott plot of magnetization versus magnetic field for Ni2.82Fe0.18Al (x = 0.18) showing the magnetic response near the inflection point.
summary: Representing the magnetic characteristics of Ni2.82Fe0.18Al (x = 0.18), this Arrott plot is constructed from magnetization curves around the inflection point. The analysis of these magnetic data points allows for the determination of the Curie temperature, which is estimated to be 194 ± 2 K for this specific iron concentration.

caption: Storage and loss moduli comparison between base and bioactive PCL polymer formulations.
summary: This panel displays the storage and loss moduli for base and bioactive PCL materials. These viscoelastic properties are presented to characterize the mechanical response of the polymer matrix, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of bioadditives on the structural integrity and energy dissipation capabilities of the PCL-based samples.

caption: Atomic model illustrating a silicon atom substituting for an aluminum atom at a representative (001) face-center site (1/2, 1/2, 0).
summary: This panel presents the atomic model where a silicon atom substitutes for an aluminum atom at a representative (001) face-center site, specifically at the fractional coordinate (1/2, 1/2, 0). The upper and lower face-centered positions are translationally equivalent under periodic boundary conditions, completing the structural representation of the Al5Sc2Si phase.

caption: Thermal unfolding transition curves for HSA and HSA-CXCL9(74–103) obtained by monitoring circular dichroism (CD) signals at 221 nm during heating at a rate of 2 °C/min.
summary: Thermal unfolding analysis confirms the structural integrity and stability of the fusion protein. HSA and HSA-CXCL9(74–103) display virtually identical thermal transition points, determined to be 67.96 ± 0.11 °C and 67.93 ± 0.14 °C, respectively. This confirms that the fusion process does not alter the thermal stability of the HSA scaffold.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) plot for the sample treated with ultrasound, indicating an overall increase in KAM values compared to the untreated condition.
summary: The KAM plot for the sample treated with ultrasound shows an increase in Kernel Average Misorientation values. This observation suggests that the ultrasonic treatment induces higher levels of local misorientation and plastic strain within the microstructure compared to the sample processed without ultrasound.

caption: Initial state of the film on the CF plate prior to the onset of atomization.
summary: This initial frame captures the top view of the film resting on the CF plate before the high-speed atomization sequence begins. It serves as the baseline reference for observing the subsequent development of Faraday ripples and droplet ejection processes recorded at a 10 kHz acquisition rate.

caption: Optical transmittance spectrum of the CNF 25% film, showing a high transmittance value of 84.5% at a wavelength of 550 nm.
summary: The CNF 25% film demonstrates excellent optical properties, characterized by a high transmittance of 84.5% at 550 nm. This performance is comparable to previously reported TEMPO-CNFs films, indicating that the produced cellulose nanofibril film maintains high optical clarity suitable for applications requiring transparency.

caption: Radar chart illustrating environmental, economic, and social KPI scores for various recycled PLA blends, highlighting performance across metrics such as global warming potential, life cycle cost, and local employment.
summary: This radar chart visualizes multi-dimensional KPI scores across environmental, economic, and social categories. Environmental indicators show clear improvements as recycled content increases, with the V0:R100 blend demonstrating the smallest deviations from sustainability thresholds. The chart provides a comprehensive overview of sustainability performance for different recycled PLA material compositions.

caption: Charging and discharging power profiles for second-life battery packs at the 2400-th cycle, illustrating four distinct operational types.
summary: This figure displays the charging and discharging power profiles of second-life battery packs at the 2400-th cycle, categorized into four distinct types. Type 1 battery packs demonstrate the most significant fluctuations in energy levels throughout the operational cycle, highlighting the variability in performance among different battery pack configurations during extended use.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of a glassy carbon working electrode in a ChCl:malonic acid eutectic mixture at 60 °C, recorded at a scan rate of 20 mV s⁻¹.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram characterizes the electrochemical behavior of a glassy carbon electrode in an ILM solvent at 60 °C. The plot demonstrates a wide electrochemical window spanning from 1.2 V to -1 V, which is sufficient for identifying the reduction potentials of tin, copper, and nickel ionic species.

caption: Raman scattering spectrum of the uncured VAR resin.
summary: Raman scattering measurements were performed on the uncured VAR resin using a Renishaw inVia Qontor spectrophotometer. This spectrum provides the baseline chemical signature for the unpolymerized VAR material, serving as a reference for subsequent analysis of the cured specimens treated with PP 5.

caption: Real in-line transmittance (RIT) plotted as a function of wavelength for sintered discs, including pure alumina discs as a reference.
summary: This plot displays the real in-line transmittance (RIT) of sintered samples across a range of wavelengths. By comparing the sintered discs against pure alumina discs used as a reference, the graph illustrates the optical performance and transparency characteristics of the materials, providing a clear assessment of their light transmission properties.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of the oxides observed within the LPBF-850 matrix.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping reveals the chemical composition of the white particles identified in the LPBF-850 sample. The analysis confirms that these particles are rich in chromium, manganese, and oxygen, identifying them as oxide inclusions dispersed within the metallic matrix of the heat-treated sample.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images (scale bar: 150 μm) visualizing intracellular ROS levels in cells treated with hydrogel formulations under oxidative stress, where green fluorescence intensity correlates with ROS presence.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images reveal intracellular ROS levels in cells subjected to oxidative stress. Cells treated with H2O2 exhibit strong green fluorescence, indicating high ROS levels compared to the untreated negative control. These images demonstrate the effectiveness of the hydrogel formulations in mitigating oxidative stress within the cellular environment.

caption: Confocal micrograph of the composite fracture surface.
summary: This confocal micrograph provides a detailed view of the fracture surface of the composite test sample. It serves as part of the broader characterization of failure modes across different composite formulations, contributing to the overall assessment of how internal structural features influence the mechanical response of the material.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material sample containing Atto425 and Atto495 dyes, measured at a thickness of 0.5 mm.
summary: This panel shows the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed multi-material sample incorporating Atto425 and Atto495 dyes. The sample was printed at a thickness of 0.5 mm to facilitate comparison with other dye combinations. The resulting spectrum characterizes the light transmission properties of this specific multi-material dye system.

caption: Load-depth indentation data for LPBF Scalmalloy tested at a maximum load of 400 mN.
