summary: This feature importance plot highlights the critical parameters influencing the prediction of dimensional deviations in the x, y, and z directions. By ranking these features, the visualization provides insight into which variables most significantly impact the geometric accuracy of parts manufactured using the S2 printer system across different spatial axes.

caption: Schematic representation of the experimental selective laser melting setup, illustrating the bidirectional zigzag scanning strategy and the 67° scan rotation applied between successive 30 μm thick layers.
summary: The experimental SLM setup is depicted here, highlighting the bidirectional zigzag scanning strategy employed to print each of the n layers. A critical feature of the process is the 67° scan rotation performed before the deposition of each new 30 μm thick layer to ensure uniform material consolidation.

caption: Confusion matrix showing the binary classification accuracy of the CNN model regarding the detection of cracking defects.
summary: This confusion matrix details the binary classification accuracy of the CNN model for cracking defects. By examining the distribution of predictions against actual defect states, the matrix quantifies the model's effectiveness in identifying cracks, which is essential for validating the reliability of the CNN-based defect detection system.

caption: Calculated Cu-Ni binary phase diagram featuring solidus and liquidus boundaries with a characteristic lens shape and a narrow two-phase region, overlaid with compiled experimental data and the accepted Curie temperature line.
summary: This calculated Cu-Ni binary phase diagram displays a characteristic lens-shaped solidus and liquidus region with a narrow two-phase gap. The plot incorporates experimental data points and the accepted Curie temperature line as reviewed by Chakrabarti et al. Thermodynamic parameters were derived from the MTOX database, version 7.0, to ensure accurate phase boundary representation.

caption: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity of SAOS-2 cells measured at days 0, 10, and 14 of mineralization, presented as median values with interquartile ranges.
summary: Alkaline phosphatase activity in SAOS-2 cells was assessed at days 0, 10, and 14 to evaluate osteogenic potential. The data, represented as medians with interquartile ranges, demonstrate an overall upward trend across all surfaces over time, with the most significant increase occurring between day 0 and day 10 of the mineralization process.

caption: EDX elemental mapping of the crack tip region in AA2024 rolled T6 material in the TL orientation, highlighting the presence of iron-intermetallic particles.
summary: This EDX map illustrates the chemical composition near the crack tip of rolled AA2024 T6 material. Iron-intermetallic particles are identified, which exhibit a significant elastic-plastic property mismatch with the α-Al matrix. This mismatch induces deformation incompatibility during loading, leading to interface decohesion or brittle fracture of these particles.

caption: Faradaic efficiency for CO and H2 production measured at current densities from 12 to 100 mA cm-2 for Ag-based electrodes prepared at -0.5 V vs Ag/AgCl.
summary: This plot illustrates the CO and H2 Faradaic efficiency for electrodes deposited at -0.5 V. The data shows a significant reduction in CO selectivity as current density increases, with the hydrogen evolution reaction becoming dominant and reaching up to 90% efficiency at these specific electrochemical conditions in the bicarbonate electrolyte.

caption: Infrared luminescence spectra of the temperature sensor immersed in water, recorded between 21.0 and 49.4 °C under 700 nm excitation, with an inset highlighting the emission peak at 831 nm.
summary: This panel displays the IR luminescence spectra of a temperature sensor in water across a range of 21.0 to 49.4 °C under 700 nm excitation. As temperature increases, the emission intensity at 1626 nm rises, while the emission at 831 nm decreases, demonstrating the sensor's temperature-dependent optical response.

caption: Weibull plot representing the failure strength distribution for total lattice failure in ZrO2 specimens.
summary: This Weibull plot illustrates the failure strength distribution for ZrO2 lattice structures under tension, specifically focusing on the total failure of the lattice. The statistical analysis provides insight into the reliability and fracture behavior of the ZrO2 material when subjected to complete structural breakdown during mechanical testing.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the horizontal section of sample A2, showing the grain orientation characteristics in the horizontal plane.
summary: The horizontal section of sample A2 is depicted in this inverse pole figure map. Together with other panels, it illustrates the impact of LPBF process modulation on crystallographic orientation and texture evolution, which is essential for understanding the superior crack resistance achieved in this sample.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of MitoTracker Red CMXRos-stained hBMSCs encapsulated within EASYGEL INX© hydrogel, which has been injected into a PDLLA/PCL scaffold and cultured for one day.
summary: This fluorescence microscopy image displays the distribution of MitoTracker Red CMXRos-stained hBMSCs within an EASYGEL INX© hydrogel construct. The hydrogel was injected into a PDLLA/PCL scaffold and cultured for one day. This representative visualization confirms the successful encapsulation and distribution of cells within the scaffold prior to further biological experiments.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectra of XSB + CD composites, identifying chemical signatures of recycled versus pristine materials.
summary: This panel presents ATR-FTIR spectra for XSB + CD composites, revealing similar chemical trends to the neat XSB samples. The emergence of aldehyde functions and modifications in C-C bending vibrations indicate that thermal reprocessing facilitates further curing of double bonds and partial cleavage of Schiff-base linkages in the composite.

caption: Damping coefficients determined at various positions along the transducers using the developed calculation method.
summary: Damping coefficients are plotted for different positions along the transducers, calculated using the specific method developed in this study. These values provide insight into the energy dissipation characteristics across the transducer structures, complementing the vibration velocity data and confirming the consistency of the transducer performance under varying operational driving conditions.

caption: Normalized impact toughness K C for Ti5553 at 293 K (red) and 20 K (blue) across varying energy levels.
summary: Normalized impact toughness K C for Ti5553 is illustrated for testing conditions at 293 K and 20 K. The red bars represent data collected at room temperature, while the blue bars indicate values obtained at the ultra-cryogenic temperature of 20 K, showing the impact of energy levels on toughness.

caption: Magnetization curve showing M z versus H z for Sample E7 during the reset-to-one protocol.
summary: Magnetization curve M z versus H z for Sample E7 is shown as part of the reset-to-one protocol. Mediated across the four quadrants, this plot captures the magnetic response along the z-axis, offering insight into the sample's magnetization dynamics during the specified experimental reset procedure.

caption: Adiabatic temperature change (ΔT AD) plotted against temperature for Ni2.15Mn0.70Cr0.15Ga under magnetic field variations up to 9 T, derived from heat capacity measurements.
summary: This panel displays the adiabatic temperature change (ΔT AD) as a function of temperature for the Ni2.15Mn0.70Cr0.15Ga alloy. The data, obtained from heat capacity measurements under magnetic field changes up to 9 T, illustrates the magnetocaloric response of the material across the measured temperature range.

caption: Experimental Co–Al phase diagram compared with a calculated version incorporating both configurational and vibrational entropic contributions.
summary: This panel displays the experimental Co–Al phase diagram alongside a calculated version that accounts for configurational and vibrational entropy. The comparison highlights the influence of these entropic terms on phase stability. Notably, the effect of magnetic entropy is observed to be less significant than that of vibrational entropy in this system.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the overall yield of formaldehyde as a function of reaction temperature and modified residence time under isothermal conditions.
summary: This contour plot visualizes the optimization of formaldehyde production by mapping the overall yield against varying reaction temperatures and modified residence times. The data demonstrates the potential performance benefits achievable under specific isothermal reaction conditions, providing a clear guide for identifying the optimal parameters for maximizing the formaldehyde yield.

caption: Hexagonal unit cell configuration of the Al5Co2 phase, corresponding to the P63/mmc space group.
summary: Displayed is the Al5Co2 phase, which exhibits a hexagonal P63/mmc space group symmetry. As a complex crystal structure in the Co–Al system, its atomic arrangement is displayed alongside other phases to support the study of formation enthalpies and experimental data reported for these specific intermetallic compounds.

caption: EPMA map showing the spatial distribution of Chromium (cCr) within the indented region of Sample C.
summary: This EPMA map visualizes the Chromium distribution across the indented region of Sample C. The map complements the Cobalt distribution data, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of the elemental gradients present in the sample's microstructure as it relates to the mechanical indentation and the observed compositional variations.

caption: Geometry of the uniaxial microtensile test specimen featuring a dog-bone shape for microscale evaluation.
summary: Shown is the geometry of the uniaxial microtensile test specimen, which is fabricated in a dog-bone shape on dissimilar joints. This microscale specimen allows for precise mechanical evaluation at the smallest length scale, complementing the miniature and macroscopic test geometries to investigate the temperature dependence of the joints.

caption: Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve illustrating the trade-off between true positive rate and false positive rate for a high-performance predictive model with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9, contrasted against a diagonal baseline representing random guessing.
summary: This ROC curve demonstrates excellent predictive performance with an AUC of 0.9, significantly outperforming the diagonal baseline that represents a 1:1 trade-off characteristic of poor models. Such high scores indicate robust model accuracy, distinguishing it from random guessing and confirming its effectiveness in classification tasks as described in the study.

caption: Schematic representation of a liquid droplet impacting a convex spherical surface.
summary: This schematic illustrates a liquid droplet with initial diameter D0, temperature T0, and velocity U0 approaching a convex spherical surface at temperature Ts. The setup defines the axisymmetric domain of interest, bounded by a red dashed line, where pressure outlet conditions are applied at the top and side boundaries.

caption: Grain morphology observed in the PS21-HT TEM specimen, featuring at least two grains with distinct crystallographic orientations.
summary: The TEM micrograph shows the grain morphology of the PS21-HT specimen. Each specimen contains at least two grains with distinct orientations, enabling a detailed examination of how heat treatment influences the grain structure and boundary characteristics compared to the non-heat-treated PS21 condition.

caption: Convergence behavior of the ERWCA algorithm represented as a 3D convergence curve.
summary: The ERWCA algorithm demonstrates its convergence characteristics through a 3D convergence curve. This visualization illustrates the optimization progress of the algorithm, providing insight into how the solution space is explored and refined over the course of the computational process as part of the comparative performance analysis of tested algorithms.

caption: Evolution of peak current values for the PEDOT:PSS/TPU/paracetamol:PLGA microparticle film measured across 100 cyclic voltammetry cycles.
summary: The peak current evolution plot quantifies the electrochemical stability of the composite film over 100 cycles. The material maintains approximately 80% of its initial conductivity, a performance level comparable to previous studies involving charged molecule loading, confirming the robustness of the composite for electrochemical applications.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum recorded after a third UV exposure duration, demonstrating the cumulative effect of UV energy on the sample.
summary: This panel shows the optical transmission spectrum of the sample after a third UV exposure interval. By maintaining a constant UV intensity of 3.15 mW/cm2, the graph captures the ongoing modification of transmission characteristics. The results illustrate the cumulative impact of UV energy on the material's optical performance.

caption: Resistance response profile demonstrating stable performance at a constant temperature of 40 °C.
summary: The resistance response curve confirms the sensor's operational stability when subjected to a thermal load of 40 °C. This measurement demonstrates that the device maintains its original resistance response performance, indicating high tolerance to body-relevant thermal environments without significant degradation in its electronic signal output.

caption: Experimental configuration of the continuous biocatalytic flow reactor, featuring a syringe pump for substrate delivery and a water bath for precise temperature regulation.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup for the continuous biocatalytic flow reactor. A syringe pump drives substrate molecules through the 3D-printed reactor, while a thermostatically controlled water bath ensures precise temperature maintenance. This configuration allows for controlled flow rates and consistent reaction conditions during the biocatalytic process.

caption: 3D profilometry image of the T5 heat-treated AlSi10Mg sample tested at a 5 Hz frequency.
summary: This 3D profilometry image captures the surface topography of the T5 heat-treated AlSi10Mg sample after wear testing at 5 Hz. The visualization serves as a critical data point for evaluating how the T5 treatment influences wear morphology and volume loss compared to other heat treatment conditions at this frequency.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the cladding sample processed at an energy density of 138 J/mm³.
summary: This panel presents the inverse pole figure (IPF) map for the cladding sample processed at an energy density of 138 J/mm³. The IPF diagram illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the grains, allowing for a comparative analysis of how reducing the laser energy density influences the grain structure and orientation distribution.

caption: Deformation stages captured during the 3-point bending test of the 3D printed material formulations.
summary: Deformation stages captured during the 3-point bending test provide a visual record of the material's structural response under load. These images illustrate the physical behavior of the 3D printed formulations as they undergo flexural stress, complementing the quantitative stress-strain data and mechanical property extractions obtained from the experimental testing process.

caption: Airfoil surface of the first-stage turbine rotor blade showing localized overheating at the leading edge after 625 hours of service.
summary: This photograph displays the airfoil surface of a first-stage turbine rotor blade. The component was removed from service after 625 hours of operation due to visible degradation. A key observation is the localized overheating identified specifically at the leading edge of the turbine blade in the top section.

caption: Poisson’s ratio of the Fe-Ni binary system calculated via SQS models, compared with experimental and theoretical literature values across varying compositions.
summary: Poisson’s ratio for the fcc Fe-Ni binary system is plotted against nickel composition in this panel. The calculated values, obtained from 16- and 32-atom SQS models, are compared with experimental and theoretical data from the literature. This metric provides insight into the elastic deformation characteristics of the alloy system across different compositions.

caption: Second harmonic generation spectrum illustrating the influence of pressure, temperature, and aluminum concentration for a nanostructure with n = 3, R x1 = 11 nm, R y1 = 12 nm, w = 12 nm, H = 5 nm, F = 0, and B = 0.
summary: This figure displays the second harmonic generation spectrum for a specific nanostructure configuration defined by n = 3, R x1 = 11 nm, R y1 = 12 nm, w = 12 nm, H = 5 nm, F = 0, and B = 0. It highlights how variations in pressure, temperature, and aluminum concentration affect the optical response.

caption: Oxygen energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis performed on the thermally affected powder particles.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the thermally affected 6061-Zr alloy powder particles confirms that the dark spots observed on the surface are rich in oxygen. This compositional data establishes a direct link between the thermal history of the powder and the localized formation of oxygen-rich surface species.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of a Type 3 representative microtube, illustrating its specific internal morphology.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of a Type 3 microtube in the Al20Si20Mn20Fe20Ga20 melt-spun ribbon reveals its characteristic internal morphology. By comparing this to other types, the study classifies the structural diversity of the microtubes, with this panel serving as a key reference for the Type 3 classification.

caption: Cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy view of an aluminum particle showing a dense internal structure free of trapped gas pores.
summary: This cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy image reveals the internal structure of an ultrasonically atomized aluminum particle. The observation confirms that the atomization process successfully produces powders that are entirely free of trapped gas pores, demonstrating high structural integrity within the produced aluminum material.

caption: Average Raman spectra and band deconvolution for PPY powder and PPY:50 electrode.
summary: Presented here are the average Raman spectra for PPY powder and the PPY:50 electrode, calculated from 441 recorded spectra to minimize noise. The solid lines illustrate the deconvolution of the D and G bands, which provide critical insights into the carbonaceous lattice defects and the sp2 hybridized carbon vibration modes.

caption: Side and top views of the γ-Al2O3 (1 1 0) surface showing exposed O2c, O3c, Al3c, and Al4c coordination sites.
summary: This panel displays the side and top views of the γ-Al2O3 (1 1 0) surface. It highlights the specific coordination environments of the surface atoms, including 2-fold-coordinated oxygen, 3-fold-coordinated oxygen, 3-fold-coordinated aluminum, and 4-fold-coordinated aluminum, which are available for binding with bimetallic elements.

caption: {001} pole figures and inverse pole figure (IPF) for the vertical section of Alloy 718, demonstrating a strong <001> cubic texture with a maximum MUD value of 9.18.
summary: Pole figures and the inverse pole figure for the vertical section of Alloy 718 confirm a strong <001> cubic texture. The analysis indicates a maximum multiple of the uniform distribution (MUD) value of 9.18, highlighting the preferred crystallographic orientation developed during the laser solid forming process of the alloy.

caption: High-magnification dark-field TEM image of region d1 showing needle-like titanium hydride precipitates.
summary: This high-magnification dark-field TEM image of region d1 highlights the presence of typical needle-like titanium hydrides within the hydrogen-charged matrix. These precipitates are key indicators of the hydrogen embrittlement process, demonstrating how hydrogen interacts with the titanium alloy microstructure to form brittle phases that facilitate crack initiation and propagation.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots displaying the inverse square of capacitance versus potential for spontaneous passive films formed on Mo0 and Mo23 alloys in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This figure presents Mott-Schottky plots for spontaneous passive films formed on Mo0 and Mo23 alloys within a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These electrochemical measurements characterize the semiconducting properties of the passive films, providing essential data on the electronic structure and defect density of the films formed on these specific molybdenum-containing materials.

caption: Acoustic absorption coefficient for the 30 mm thick sample optimized for 2000-5000 Hz, comparing measured red data with numerical black dashed predictions.
summary: This graph displays the acoustic absorption coefficient for the 30 mm thick sample optimized for the 2000-5000 Hz range. The red line denotes measured values, while the black dashed line represents numerical results, confirming the effectiveness of the optimization strategy in achieving the desired acoustic absorption profile.

caption: Absorbance spectra of MJT specimens, illustrating how the shifting behavior of the absorbance profile is dependent on the specific digital material used.
summary: Panel b presents the absorbance spectra for MJT specimens. The results demonstrate that the shifting behavior of the absorbance profile is inherently dependent on the digital material composition. This indicates that the optical absorption characteristics of the specimens are sensitive to the specific material properties employed in the fabrication process.

caption: Mass spectrum of FPEA-ProGly film following the click reaction with CGRGDS peptide.
summary: This mass spectrum demonstrates the successful immobilization of the CGRGDS mimicking peptide on the surface of the FPEA-ProGly film. Detection of the peptide after the click reaction confirms the efficacy of the coupling process. The measurement area for this analysis was 500 µm by 500 µm.

caption: Particle composition and contact model showing the partitioning of Al and PPA adherends into two distinct size regions.
summary: This panel details the particle composition and contact model for the SLJ system. It explicitly shows how Al and PPA particles, representing the adherends, are partitioned into two distinct regions characterized by different particle sizes, providing the necessary parameters for accurate contact modeling within the DEM simulation.

caption: Final ODF section for the HT1 Invar 36 alloy sample, providing a comprehensive view of the texture characteristics under this condition.
summary: Providing a final perspective on the HT1 Invar 36 alloy, this ODF section completes the textural assessment for this specific sample. By analyzing the orientation distribution, the panel contributes to a broader understanding of how the IR-LDED process and subsequent heat treatment define the final crystallographic structure of the alloy.

caption: Pole figure and inverse pole figure of initial β grains in the XOY plane of LPBF Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
summary: This panel displays the initial β grain texture for LPBF Ti-6Al-4V in the XOY plane. The data, presented as pole figures and inverse pole figures, establishes the baseline crystallographic orientation of the parent β phase prior to the martensitic transformation, serving as a reference for the subsequent α' phase analysis.

caption: Resistance response profile during the slippage event, showing a drastic change in the specimen's electrical resistance.
summary: The plot captures the significant electrical resistance shift occurring during object slippage. This drastic change demonstrates the capability of conductive foams to detect and predict slippage in real time. The signal reflects the total resistance measured along the finger actuator, confirming the sensor's sensitivity to dynamic mechanical contact conditions.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of the CoCu 20 FeMnNi high-entropy alloy fusion zone.
summary: The EBSD inverse pole figure map for the CoCu 20 FeMnNi high-entropy alloy illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution within the fusion zone. This map provides essential data on the grain structure and texture development, which is critical for understanding the mechanical and microstructural properties of the alloy after fusion processing.

caption: Selected-area electron diffraction pattern of the austenite phase, indicating an FCC crystal structure.
summary: The selected-area electron diffraction pattern shown for the austenite phase indicates an FCC crystal structure. This crystallographic identification is essential for characterizing the phase composition of the H0 sample, distinguishing the austenite morphology from the surrounding lath martensite matrix observed in the material.

caption: Magnetization curves of MnAl and MnAl-C alloys quenched at 950 °C, illustrating the magnetic response to varying external magnetic fields.
summary: This plot displays the magnetic behavior of MnAl and MnAl-C alloys quenched at 950 °C by showing the change in magnetization as a function of the applied magnetic field. The data reveals that carbon doping significantly enhances the saturation magnetization of the MnAl alloy compared to the undoped sample.

caption: Support Vector Machine (SVM) model confusion matrix evaluated on the unseen test set.
summary: Support Vector Machine model results are summarized in this confusion matrix, derived from the unseen test set. The plot illustrates the alignment between predicted and actual classifications, providing insight into the model's ability to separate classes effectively and identifying any systematic errors present in the classification process.

caption: Force-displacement curves comparing water-filled samples under ambient conditions and elevated temperatures of 50 °C.
summary: This panel displays force-displacement test results for water-filled samples. Comparing ambient conditions to an elevated temperature of 50 °C, the data reveals a notable increase in mechanical properties. The curves demonstrate how thermal changes influence the structural response of the material under applied mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Pole figure of GH4169 alloy fabricated using the long-range quasi-steady heat input mode.
summary: This pole figure displays the texture of GH4169 specimens processed through the long-range quasi-steady heat input mode. The analysis of this panel contributes to the broader investigation of how different thermal input modes affect the stability of solidification conditions and the overall crystallographic texture of the fabricated alloy.

caption: Phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium states of the alloy system relevant to the observed microstructural degradation.
summary: The phase diagram provides a theoretical framework for understanding the thermodynamic stability of the alloy phases. It supports the observation that microstructural degradation, such as the formation of γ′-depleted zones and η-phase growth, is linked to the alloy's phase equilibrium and the development of preferential sites for microcracking.

caption: Normalized confusion matrix representing the relative predictive accuracy of the random forest classifier at k=5 across different droplet categories.
summary: Representing the normalized predictive accuracy, this confusion matrix highlights the random forest classifier's performance at k=5. Consistent with the aggregated data, the model achieves a 98% accuracy rate, effectively demonstrating its reliability in distinguishing between various droplet types through normalized proportions of correct and incorrect classifications.

caption: Surface morphologies of the first dual-faced structured fabric observed after compression experiments.
summary: Post-compression surface morphologies of the first dual-faced structured fabric are shown. These images provide a visual assessment of the structural integrity and surface condition of the fabric following mechanical testing, helping to identify any permanent deformation or damage sustained during the compression experiments under the applied vacuum confining pressures.

caption: FIB-SEM reconstructed 3D volume of forged Ti-6Al-4V alloy showing the spatial distribution of α-phase in red and β-phase in white.
summary: This 3D reconstruction derived from FIB-SEM tomography visualizes the complex microstructure of forged Ti-6Al-4V alloy. The volume highlights the distinct spatial arrangement of the equiaxed α-grains and residual β-phase lamellae, providing a comprehensive view of the alloy's internal morphology and phase distribution within the reconstructed sample volume.

caption: 3D EBSD IPF-Z map of the sample processed with 90° hatch rotation, 200 W laser power, 70 µm hatch spacing, and 1000 mm/s scan speed, visualizing the grain orientation.
summary: Representing the 90° hatch rotation condition with 70 µm hatch spacing, this EBSD IPF-Z map illustrates the grain structure across multiple planes. The microstructure is sensitive to the process parameters, and the map provides a detailed view of the grain orientation and the presence of cracks marked by black lines.

caption: Charge density difference map for the γ′/γ″ interface at the Center Ni + Z terminal (Model G) depicting charge transfer from surrounding Nb and Al atoms to Ni.
summary: Depicting the γ′/γ″ interface at the Center Ni + Z terminal, this map shows the transfer of charges from surrounding Nb and Al atoms to the Ni atoms at the interface. This electronic redistribution contributes to the increased stability of the Model G interface compared to the Model F configuration.

caption: Visual appearance of the tensile samples following the grinding process, showing the polished surfaces prepared to remove machining marks prior to mechanical testing.
summary: Post-grinding appearance of the tensile samples is shown here. Each specimen was polished with sandpaper to remove machining marks and achieve a bright surface finish, a critical preparation step intended to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the results obtained during the subsequent tensile testing phase.

caption: Strain distribution contour map and local strain curve for the forged substrate sample, showing clear strain concentration and necking in the central region.
summary: The forged sample, characterized by a uniform bimodal microstructure, displays significant strain localization during tensile testing. The DIC strain contour map reveals a distinct concentration of strain in the middle of the specimen, indicative of necking behavior under room temperature tensile conditions as the material undergoes plastic deformation.

caption: Reduced modulus profile of MHP surfaces following thermal exposure at 550 °C for 20 h, measured up to 100 μm depth.
summary: This panel illustrates the reduced modulus of MHP surfaces after undergoing thermal exposure at 550 °C for 20 hours. The data, plotted up to 100 μm depth, provides insight into the mechanical stability of the peened surfaces when subjected to elevated temperature conditions over an extended duration.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the ternary eutectic microstructure in Alloy B, illustrating the spatial arrangement of α-Al, Si, and Al2Cu phases.
summary: This panel presents a 3D reconstruction of the fine ternary eutectic microstructure in Alloy B obtained via FIB-SEM tomography. It highlights the complex spatial distribution and morphology of the three constituent phases, specifically α-Al, Si, and Al2Cu, providing a comprehensive view of the eutectic network within the alloy matrix.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of K4800W alloy at 0.15% plastic strain and 800 °C, highlighting isolated stacking faults within the γ' phase.
summary: Captured at 800 °C with 0.15% plastic strain, this TEM micrograph reveals the internal structure of K4800W alloy. A key observation is the generation of many isolated stacking faults specifically within the γ' phase, illustrating the distinct deformation behavior of the alloy under these specific thermal and mechanical conditions.

caption: Comparison of experimental fatigue life results for TC11 alloy with values calculated using the proposed model, T–K model, and Miner’s rule.
summary: The parity plot illustrates the correlation between experimental fatigue life data for TC11 alloy and the predicted values. The proposed model shows good agreement with the experimental data, outperforming or aligning better than the T–K model and Miner’s rule in predicting the fatigue life of this specific material.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of a monocrystalline Ni alloy (111) oxidized at 350℃ for 30 minutes, highlighting compositional changes over time.
summary: Representing the oxidation state after 30 minutes at 350℃, this ToF-SIMS profile tracks the elemental depth distribution in the (111) oriented monocrystalline Ni alloy. The data, collected under consistent experimental conditions, allows for a comparative assessment of the oxidation kinetics and compositional evolution relative to the shorter 5-minute exposure.

caption: Linear relationship between ln(sinh(α1σss)) and ln Z for the β-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary: Representing the constitutive behavior of the β-phase in Ti6Al4V alloy, this plot displays the correlation between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the stress parameter and the natural logarithm of the Zener-Hollomon parameter. The observed linearity confirms the consistent relationship between flow stress and deformation parameters.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of the DIW printed Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene//α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene ASC device recorded at varying potential windows with a fixed scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammetry curves for the DIW printed Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene//α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene ASC device. The measurements were conducted at a constant scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ across different potential windows to evaluate the electrochemical behavior and potential range of the fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor device.

caption: Time-dependent wall temperature profiles for thruster chamber cases 1 (Ṁ ox = 6.2 g/s, Ṁ f = 2.2 g/s, O/F = 2.8) and 2 (Ṁ ox = 6.9 g/s, Ṁ f = 2.1 g/s, O/F = 3.3).
summary: This plot displays the wall temperature variation over time for cases 1 and 2. Case 2, utilizing downstream swirl injection, exhibits significantly lower temperatures compared to case 1, which uses upstream injection. Both configurations maintain temperature ranges below 60 °C, demonstrating the cooling effectiveness of the vortex flow within the chamber.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for a ternary Mn-Al-C alloy in the as-received state and after annealing at 1100 °C followed by water quenching.
summary: This panel presents magnetic hysteresis loops for a ternary Mn-Al-C alloy containing 50 at.% excess Mn. The data compares the as-received condition with samples subjected to high-temperature annealing at 1100 °C and subsequent water quenching in an ampule to evaluate the resulting magnetic properties of the material.

caption: Aspect ratio trends of the α′ phase evaluated under different laser power conditions.
summary: This panel shows the aspect ratio of the α′ phase as a function of laser power. The data indicates that the aspect ratio decreases with increasing laser power, which is consistent with the observed reduction in grain length relative to the increasing width of the α′ phase structures.

caption: Interferometry image of the Ref-TS tool material disk wear scar after testing at 40 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the interferometry imaging of the wear scar on the Ref-TS tool material disk following a tribotest at 40 °C. The image captures the surface wear characteristics of the reference material, providing a baseline for comparison with other tool materials tested under identical low-temperature conditions.

caption: Surface morphology of the Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy printed at 90 W laser power, displaying a reduction in the density of unfused powder particles and pores compared to the 70 W condition.
summary: Surface morphology of the Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloy printed at 90 W laser power, displaying a reduction in the density of unfused powder particles and pores compared to the 70 W condition. As laser power increases, the number of unfused powder particles and pores gradually decreases, reflecting improved metal-fusion characteristics.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe50 composite achieving a minimum value of -9.63 dB.
summary: The Fe50 composite exhibits a reflection loss profile with a minimum value of -9.63 dB. This significant absorption enhancement, achieved at 50 wt% Fe loading, demonstrates the positive correlation between iron concentration and the electromagnetic wave absorption efficiency within the Fe/PLA/TPU composite framework as quantified by the reflection loss profiles.

caption: Ammonium ion concentration profile within a single 3D columnar structure.
summary: Ammonium ion concentration profile within a single 3D columnar structure is shown. Simulation results reveal that the generated ammonium ions are primarily distributed within the liquid phase, contrasting with the nitrogen gas distribution and demonstrating the localized accumulation of ionic species within the liquid medium of the column.

caption: Processing window for Ni45 superalloy fabricated via DED-L at a powder feeding rate of 9.3 g/min.
summary: Representing the processing window for Ni45 superalloy at a powder feeding rate of 9.3 g/min, this plot demonstrates the stability zone. As the powder feeding rate increases from 7.0 g/min, the stability zone expands, indicating improved processing conditions for the DED-L additive manufacturing process.

caption: Hardness profile as a function of distance from the surface for samples heat-treated at 800 °C for 0, 1, 4, and 8 hours, showing the transition between the NiTi layer, NDL, GBD, and titanium substrate.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness variation across the cross-sections of heat-treated coatings. Indentation tests reveal distinct hardness values at varying depths, specifically highlighting the NiTi layer at 15–20 μm. The data confirms the depth of the NDL region, which aligns with microstructural observations, demonstrating the evolution of mechanical properties over time.

caption: TGA curves showing the thermal degradation profiles of the 3D printlet and its precursor materials.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis was employed to study the thermal degradation behavior of the 3D printlet and its precursors. The resulting TGA curves demonstrate the weight loss characteristics as a function of temperature, offering essential data regarding the thermal stability and decomposition kinetics of the materials involved in the printing formulation.

caption: Effective material loss (EML) of the proposed photonic crystal fiber (PCF) as a function of frequency, calculated for both polarizations using TOPAS as the background material.
summary: This plot illustrates the effective material loss (EML) characteristics of a proposed photonic crystal fiber design. By utilizing TOPAS as the background material, the fiber achieves a condensed EML profile. The data displays the frequency-dependent loss behavior across both polarizations, highlighting the performance of the proposed fiber structure.

caption: Sku versus Ssk amplitude parameter distribution for the sample subjected to sandblasting, centrifugal tumbling, and electrolytic polishing.
summary: This scatter plot displays the Sku and Ssk amplitude parameters for the sample treated with sandblasting, centrifugal tumbling, and electrolytic polishing. The larger scattered values observed in this map signify a greater improvement in surface quality compared to other post-processing techniques, indicating a distinct surface roughness profile for this specific treatment.

caption: Yield strength versus elongation for AZT6115 and reference Ti alloys at ambient temperature.
summary: Yield strength is plotted against elongation for AZT6115 and various Ti alloys at ambient temperature. The AZT6115 alloy shows significantly higher yield strength than many as-deposited and forged Ti alloys, including Ti-6Al-4V and Ti65, though this performance is achieved at the expense of a relatively low elongation of 1.8%.

caption: KAM map derived from the μXRD scan, where blue lines delineate grain boundaries with misorientation angles larger than 15°.
summary: This KAM map, obtained via synchrotron μXRD, delineates cell boundaries and outlines the size and shape of cell colonies. These findings are consistent with observations from optical microscopy and SEM. The blue lines mark grain boundaries exceeding 15°, providing a clear structural map of the sub-grain and cell colony organization.

caption: Stress-strain curve of P7F3 composite sample during tensile testing.
summary: P7F3 composite material is characterized by its stress-strain curve, which depicts the mechanical deformation behavior under tensile load. This plot serves as a comparative metric to evaluate how the incorporation of PVDF into the PLA matrix influences the overall mechanical performance and material response of the P7F3 sample.

caption: Initial ModelNet40 geometry represented as a raw voxel grid prior to structural modifications.
summary: This panel displays the initial state of a ModelNet40 geometry, which has been converted into a raw voxel grid representation. This visualization serves as the baseline configuration before any additional structural elements, such as baseplates or support layers, are integrated into the geometric model for further processing or analysis.

caption: Distribution of intercept lengths measured perpendicular to the building direction for SLM and SLRM (6) samples, featuring an inset showing the central section of the SLM microstructure.
summary: This histogram displays the distribution of intercept lengths measured perpendicular to the building direction for SLM and SLRM (6) samples. The population of these intercept lengths becomes broader when each layer is remelted. An inset provides a visual representation of the SLM sample's central section to contextualize the grain structure.

caption: Volumetric shrinkage percentages for various recycled and virgin monoliths measured after the calcination process.
summary: This bar chart displays the volumetric shrinkage percentages of recycled and virgin monoliths following calcination. Most monoliths exhibit comparable shrinkage values, indicating consistent processing behavior. Notably, the 7Co monolith demonstrates a distinct trend, showing approximately 10% lower shrinkage compared to the other tested monolith samples in the study.

caption: Bode magnitude and phase angle plots for the 316L and 18Ni300 samples, showing experimental data points alongside fitted solid lines to evaluate electrochemical performance.
summary: Bode plots provide a frequency-dependent analysis of the electrochemical impedance for the investigated multi-material samples. By comparing experimental data with fitted solid lines, these plots help elucidate the electrochemical characteristics of the LPBF-fabricated 316L and 18Ni300 specimens across various heat-treated conditions.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) of the three cells with different modified separators, showing the internal and polarization resistance.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectra for the three samples are shown, where the intersection in the low-frequency region indicates internal resistance. The polarization impedance represents charge transfer resistance during redox, with lower values indicating superior charge transfer behavior. The Ni-Cu@C/HC sample demonstrates the highest efficiency in physical transport and chemical conversion.

caption: Heat flow profile of PMMA-M denture base resin subjected to different aging protocols, represented by distinct color-coded lines.
summary: PMMA-M denture base resin exhibits a specific heat flow profile when analyzed via differential scanning calorimetry. The experimental results demonstrate that the various aging protocols applied to the material result in only minor variations in the measured heat flow, confirming the material's relative stability under these conditions.

caption: Comprehensive process flowchart illustrating the optimization strategy for 3D printing geopolymer composites by integrating rheological characterization with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic approach for optimizing 3D printing of geopolymer composites. It details the integration of rheological data, specifically storage modulus, loss modulus, and frequency from oscillatory rheology, into a user-defined function (UDF) for CFD modeling, ensuring a robust framework for process development and material performance prediction.

caption: Detailed STEM micrograph of a dendritic cell in IN718 R67, distinguishing the outer interdendritic zone populated by geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) networks from the central cell zone containing statistically stored dislocations (SSDs).
summary: This STEM micrograph provides a detailed view of a single dendritic cell in an IN718 R67 sample. It clearly distinguishes between the outer interdendritic zone, characterized by GND networks, and the central cell zone, which contains SSDs. Both dislocation types contribute to the overall network structure within the material.

caption: Galvanostatic discharge-charge curves for CCC-based LSBs at 0.1C and 1C, highlighting the discharge plateau behavior.
summary: Galvanostatic discharge-charge curves for CCC-based LSBs at 0.1C and 1C are shown. The CCC interlayer exhibits a vanishing discharge plateau at 1C, indicating poor electrochemical performance compared to the ZnS@CCC interlayer, which maintains a longer and more stable charging and discharging plateau under the same high-rate conditions.

caption: Mass spectrum of pristine FPEA-ProGly polymer film serving as a negative control.
summary: The mass spectrum of the pristine FPEA-ProGly polymer film is presented as a negative control. Analysis confirms that this sample shows no evidence of peptide attachment, establishing a baseline for the subsequent coupling experiments. The measurement was conducted over a 500 µm by 500 µm area.

caption: Comparison of monotonic and 1000th cycle load-displacement loops for various Ti-6Al-4V variants tested at a maximum load of 500 N, R = -1, and 20 °C.
summary: This plot displays the hysteresis behavior of different Ti-6Al-4V material variants under uniaxial fatigue conditions. By comparing the initial monotonic loading with the 1000th cycle at a maximum force of 500 N and a stress ratio of R = -1, the figure illustrates the evolution of mechanical strain-stress response during cyclic testing.

caption: Comparison of the theoretical Rosenthal temperature distribution (green), the raw experimental temperature profile of a defective sample (blue), and the Gaussian-smoothed experimental data (red) along the laser path.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature profile along the laser path during the SPIT process. It compares the theoretical Rosenthal curve with raw experimental data from a defective sample. A Gaussian filter is applied to the noisy measured data to mitigate signal fluctuations, facilitating the identification of negative temperature deviations indicative of defects.

caption: EBSD grain structure map of the Cr2O3 oxide scale on AM alloy IN625 after 1000 h of air exposure at 900°C, showing detailed grain morphology.
summary: This EBSD map provides a detailed view of the Cr2O3 grain structure in AM alloy IN625 after 1000 h of air exposure at 900°C. Small grains are present at the base of oxide ridges near the oxide-metal interface, while the grain size increases significantly towards the outer gas-oxide interface.

caption: AFM visualization of the ZK60 magnesium alloy surface following ion implantation at a higher dose of 5 × 10^16 ions/cm^2.
summary: AFM visualization of the ZK60 magnesium alloy surface following ion implantation at a higher dose of 5 × 10^16 ions/cm^2. This treatment produces a smooth and dense morphology, demonstrating that ion implantation effectively reduces the root mean square roughness of the alloy surface compared to the untreated condition.

caption: Rose diagram displaying the angular dependence of the average intercept size of γ' phases across the original sample, region A, and region B, highlighting variations relative to the β angle.
summary: The rose diagram quantifies the average intercept size of γ' phases as a function of the β angle for different sample regions. Data for the original component shows a stable distribution centered around 0.75 μm, while variations in regions A and B reflect the influence of dislocation networks on phase rafting.

caption: Elemental distribution map of a spherical MgO inclusion identified in the nickel-based superalloy.
summary: This panel presents the elemental distribution map of an MgO inclusion within the nickel-based superalloy. The map illustrates the localized concentration of magnesium and oxygen, characterizing the chemical nature of this typical inclusion type as part of the broader investigation into inclusion morphology and distribution in the material.

caption: Temperature dependence of the coercivity field for the CNCV sample, measured across the range of 5 K to 335 K.
summary: This graph represents the temperature evolution of the coercivity field (Hc) for the CNCV alloy in the range of 5 K to 335 K. The data illustrates the thermal sensitivity of the magnetic properties, showing how the coercivity changes as the material is subjected to varying temperature conditions.

caption: Load capacity F(X) of the joint as a function of feed rate and tool plunge depth at a constant rotational speed of 800 rpm.
summary: This plot illustrates the joint load capacity F(X) influenced by feed rate and tool plunge depth at 800 rpm. Experimental results identify specific process parameters, such as point P1 with 5.36 kN and point P2 with 5.52 kN, demonstrating the sensitivity of joint strength to these mechanical processing variables.

caption: 3D morphology of corrosion pits on the surface of LPBFed Ti–7Cu alloy after 7 days of dynamic immersion.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy shows the 3D surface morphology of corrosion pits on LPBFed Ti–7Cu alloy samples after 7 days of dynamic immersion and polarization testing. The image documents the pitting behavior and surface degradation observed on the Ti–7Cu alloy, providing insight into its corrosion resistance characteristics.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for effective stress ratio versus effective mean stress, with dot colors representing the effective mean stress values.
summary: This plot illustrates the interaction between the effective stress ratio and effective mean stress. As part of a series of interrelated stress features, it provides insight into how these variables collectively influence fatigue life predictions. The analysis of this plot is meaningful when considered alongside panels (d) and (e).

caption: Feature visualization of the MIT dataset using the supervised learning method.
summary: This panel presents the feature extraction results for the MIT dataset obtained via the supervised learning approach. It acts as a reference point for assessing the model's performance on a different dataset, highlighting the distribution patterns of battery user features when trained using standard supervised learning techniques.

caption: Melt pool area of 316L stainless steel plotted against the normalized energy density parameter (P/v*r^3), where r represents the beam radius calculated via the 86% method.
summary: This plot shows the melt pool area for 316L steel against the normalized parameter P/v*r^3. By incorporating the beam radius, the data points for each beam profile exhibit clustering behavior. This normalization approach helps in understanding how beam geometry influences the melt pool size relative to the input energy density.

caption: In-situ FTIR spectra monitoring the adsorption of ethylguaiacol on CN@γ-Al2O3, 10Ni-5Mo/γ-Al2O3, and 10Ni-5Mo/CN@γ-Al2O3 surfaces.
summary: In-situ FTIR spectra were collected to analyze the adsorption behavior of ethylguaiacol on the surfaces of CN@γ-Al2O3, 10Ni-5Mo/γ-Al2O3, and 10Ni-5Mo/CN@γ-Al2O3. These spectra provide information on the surface interactions and binding modes of the probe molecule on the different catalyst supports and metal-loaded systems.

caption: Optical microscope image of Ti-10Cu alloy sintered at 1100 °C for 14.4 ks and aged at 400 °C for 86.4 ks.
summary: Optical microscopy of the Ti-10Cu alloy, sintered at 1100 °C for 14.4 ks and aged at 400 °C for 86.4 ks, reveals the presence of thin, discontinuous strips located at the boundaries of the martensitic α′-Ti plates within the microstructure.

caption: EELS spectra of the Ni-L 2,3 edge acquired at points S1-S4, demonstrating local variations in nickel chemistry within the porous film.
summary: These EELS spectra of the Ni-L 2,3 edge, acquired at points S1-S4, reveal local variations in nickel chemistry within the porous film. By correlating these spectroscopic signatures with the specific points identified in the elemental maps, the analysis provides insight into the chemical state of nickel at the crack site.

caption: Unique grain color map of the specimen under liquid cooling, demonstrating a reduction in localized coarse grains compared to the heat sink condition.
summary: Liquid cooling is shown in this EBSD unique grain color map to effectively reduce the presence of localized coarse grains. While higher cooling rates may not significantly decrease the average grain size, this visualization confirms their efficacy in suppressing the formation of abnormally large grains within the material microstructure.

caption: Time-dependent deuterium signal buildup observed in a mouse flank tumor model following injection, plotted over a duration of several minutes.
summary: This panel illustrates the in vivo acquisition of a deuterium signal buildup within a hepatocellular carcinoma flank tumor in a mouse. The time series plot tracks the signal intensity over several minutes post-injection, demonstrating the feasibility of monitoring metabolic tracers in tumor tissues using this spectroscopic approach.

caption: EDS analysis of Colmonoy-5 alloy sintered at 900 °C, highlighting a specific point 43 where Ni content decreases and Cr content increases.
summary: This EDS analysis of Colmonoy-5 alloy sintered at 900 °C reveals localized chemical variations. At point 43, the observed decrease in Ni content alongside an increase in Cr concentration suggests the potential formation of a solid solution within the sintered microstructure of the alloy.

caption: Cross-sectional view of scaffolds containing 25% SPI incorporated with DES or glycerol, showing the internal distribution of SPI particles.
summary: Cross-sectional SEM analysis of the scaffolds confirms a similar internal microstructure to the surface. The SPI particles, marked with red arrows, are well-dispersed throughout the resin. The addition of either DES or glycerol shows no significant influence on the internal morphology or the dispersion of the SPI phase.

caption: Infrared thermographic images visualizing the surface temperature distribution across various LPNC evaporator samples under 1 sun illumination.
summary: Infrared thermography was utilized to precisely monitor surface temperature changes across different evaporators. These heatmaps provide a spatial visualization of the thermal distribution on the LPNC samples under 1 sun illumination, allowing for a direct comparison of the thermal management and heat localization capabilities of the different evaporator designs.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation diagram illustrating the kinetics of γ''-phase formation in LAM-Inconel 718 as a function of aluminum concentration.
summary: This TTT diagram illustrates the relationship between temperature and time for γ''-phase formation in LAM-Inconel 718. Higher aluminum levels are shown to necessitate longer aging treatments and higher temperatures to initiate the formation of the γ''-phase, highlighting the significant influence of Al concentration on the material's phase transformation kinetics.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the AM-L-HIP sample illustrating the γ″ phase distribution.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the AM-L-HIP sample provides a clear view of the γ″ phase morphology. The micrograph reveals fine particles dispersed within the γ matrix, allowing for a precise assessment of the microstructural state of the material following the AM-L-HIP processing treatment.

caption: Three-dimensional surface profile of a straight channel after electropolishing at 25 V for 20 minutes.
summary: This panel displays the 3D surface profile of a straight channel following an electropolishing treatment at 25 V for a duration of 20 minutes. The visualization illustrates the surface topography resulting from this specific processing condition, providing a detailed representation of the channel's surface state after the electropolishing procedure.

caption: Fourier-transformed 79 Br spectrum derived from the free induction decay in panel a, displaying characteristic spinning sidebands marked with asterisks and a magnified callout highlighting sidebands with lower signal-to-noise ratios.
summary: This 79 Br spectrum is the Fourier transform of the free induction decay signal obtained from 16,384 scans of a 42 mg KBr sample. The plot identifies spinning sidebands with asterisks, while a specific callout provides a detailed view of the sidebands that exhibit relatively low signal-to-noise characteristics.

caption: Load-depth response of LPBF Al5X1 alloy subjected to 400 mN constant load indentation testing.
summary: Indentation data from 50 indents on LPBF Al5X1, tested at a maximum load of 400 mN, show an average maximum depth of 3604 ± 38 nm. This depth corresponds to an average indentation hardness of 1.39 ± 0.03 GPa, which is equivalent to a Vickers hardness of 131.30 ± 2.84 kgf/mm².

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the diffusion coefficients of a single H atom in pure Ni across various temperatures, including directional components.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the diffusion coefficients of a single H atom in pure Ni. MD data points across three crystallographic directions demonstrate excellent alignment with the linear Arrhenius model, confirming the convergence of the simulations and providing a reliable basis for extracting diffusion activation energies in the pure Ni system.

caption: Overview of the complete tensile testing configuration, featuring a tensile testing machine integrated with a camera, lens, and LED illumination system.
summary: This experimental setup comprises a tensile testing machine equipped with a camera, lens, and an illumination system. The configuration is designed to facilitate mechanical testing while simultaneously capturing visual data, as shown in the provided setup. This integrated arrangement allows for precise monitoring and documentation during the tensile testing process.

caption: Modulus of elasticity (solid black line) and tensile strength (dashed red line) plotted as a function of resin layer exposure time.
summary: Modulus of elasticity and tensile strength trends are illustrated for neat resin across different exposure times. The data confirms that mechanical properties improve as exposure time increases, reflecting the formation of a more tightly interconnected and rigid material structure resulting from the higher degree of crosslinking within the resin.

caption: Calculated electron density difference (EDD) diagram of g-C3N4 with PS absorbed on the (001) lattice plane, showing charge accumulation in blue and depletion in yellow.
summary: Panel h displays the calculated electron density difference for g-C3N4 with PS absorbed on the (001) plane. Bader analysis indicates that 1.01 electrons migrate from g-C3N4 to PS. The visualization highlights charge accumulation in blue and depletion in yellow, illustrating the electronic interaction at the interface.

caption: HER activity of NiCo@NC nanoalloys evaluated across varying Ni concentrations to determine the influence of stoichiometry on catalytic reactivity.
summary: To achieve more insight into the role of stoichiometry in the catalytic reactivity of encapsulated bimetallic alloys, the HER activity of NiCo@NC is compared for different concentrations of Ni. This analysis helps clarify how varying the Ni content modulates the catalytic performance of the nanoalloy system.

caption: EPMA line scan profile illustrating the elemental distribution of Ni and Cr within the deposited layer after preheating at 400 °C.
summary: Depicted is the EPMA line scan profile for the deposited layer subjected to 400 °C preheating. The scan path highlights the distribution of Ni and Cr. Observations show that Ni- and Cr-depleted zones near the substrate interface become more pronounced compared to the non-preheated condition, indicating temperature-dependent elemental migration.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction patterns acquired from the internal oxidation products identified within the (Ni, Al, Cr)5Y phase shown in panel (d).
summary: SAED patterns from the internal oxidation zone in panel (d) identify the presence of specific oxide phases. These diffraction results, combined with EDS data, confirm the formation of NiO2, Cr3O8, and Y2O3 within the (Ni, Al, Cr)5Y phase, characterizing the severe internal oxidation process occurring at 750 °C.

caption: In-situ HEXRD analysis of the AS1 sample heated at 0.167 °C/s to 400 °C, displaying the evolution of lattice parameter, its derivative, FWHM, and temperature.
summary: The AS1 sample, heated at 0.167 °C/s, shows in-situ HEXRD data including lattice parameter, FWHM, and temperature. The lattice derivative curve remains steady initially before exhibiting a positive inclination change, which signifies the onset of Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitation. This precipitation is characterized by a larger lattice parameter compared to the aluminum matrix.

caption: TEM-CDF image of cast Haynes 282 showing γ′ precipitates with bright contrast, featuring an inset SAED pattern with an ignited (100) superlattice reflection at B ≈ [011]M.
summary: This TEM-CDF image reveals the microstructure of cast Haynes 282, highlighting coarse- and fine-scale γ′ precipitates through bright contrast. The inset SAED pattern confirms the coherent L12 crystallographic orientation relationship with the γ matrix, specifically identifying the (100) superlattice reflection at a zone axis of B ≈ [011]M.

caption: Calibration procedure for the thermal camera used to monitor and maintain temperature control during the irradiation experiment.
summary: The image illustrates the thermal camera calibration process. This step is vital for the irradiation stage setup, as it ensures accurate temperature monitoring of the specimen during proton exposure, thereby maintaining the integrity of the experimental conditions and the validity of the resulting irradiation damage data.

caption: Comparison of load-lateral displacement curves at mid-span between experimental test data and FE model results.
summary: Load-lateral displacement curves at mid-span are plotted to compare experimental test data with FE model predictions. The strong correlation between the two curves confirms the reliability of the finite element analysis in capturing the structural response and displacement characteristics of the C25025DL-4.0m-1 specimen under the applied loading conditions.

caption: In-depth microhardness distribution profile measured across the cross-section of the specimen deposited at 400 mm/min WFS and 3 mm/s TS.
summary: Presented is the in-depth microhardness distribution for the specimen deposited at 400 mm/min WFS and 3 mm/s TS. This measurement provides critical data on the mechanical properties of the deposited layers and the substrate interface, allowing for a detailed assessment of the material's performance under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Geometric arrangement of a 2 × 2 × 2 supercell generated from the Zeolite ID 9566022 unit cell.
summary: Displayed is a 2 × 2 × 2 supercell model created from the Zeolite ID 9566022 unit cell. The modeling process, facilitated by VESTA software, illustrates the conversion from a single unit cell to a supercell, serving as a representative example of the sequential structural modeling procedures for zeolite materials.

caption: Storage modulus curves for pure TPU and TPU bio-composites as a function of temperature.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent storage modulus for pure TPU and its bio-composites obtained via DMTA. The curves illustrate the comparative stiffness behavior of the materials across the tested temperature range, providing essential data on the mechanical performance and thermal stability of the TPU-based composite systems.

caption: Temperature dependence of the magnetic entropy change (ΔSm–T) calculated from magnetization data for field changes up to 5.0 T, with the double-sided arrow indicating the full width at half-maximum (δT FWHM) at 5.0 T.
summary: Temperature dependence of the magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) is shown for magnetic fields ranging from 0.5 to 5.0 T. The peak value of ΔSm increases with the applied field without saturation, as the martensite-to-austenite transformation remains incomplete at 5 T. The δT FWHM is highlighted for the 5.0 T curve.

caption: Calculated mixing enthalpies of high-entropy alloys at 0 K compared against their decomposition products and unary reference states, utilizing VASP-SQS predictions validated by EMTO-CPA calculations.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermodynamic stability of high-entropy alloys by comparing their mixing enthalpies at 0 K to those of their decomposition products and unary reference states. The data integrates VASP-SQS predictions with EMTO-CPA results, providing a comprehensive assessment of alloy stability through computational simulation methods.

caption: Bright field transmission electron microscopy micrograph revealing the morphology of the SS-0 sample.
summary: Bright field transmission electron microscopy is utilized to examine the SS-0 sample, providing detailed visual information regarding its internal structure. This micrograph specifically highlights the morphology of the spherical particles, allowing for a direct observation of the sample's microstructural features at the nanoscale as part of the broader compositional analysis.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the mechanical anisotropy of Ti–6Al–4V specimens fabricated via WAAM-R, PWAAM-R, WAAM-C, and PWAAM-C processes.
summary: This radar chart provides a visual representation of the mechanical anisotropy observed in Ti–6Al–4V samples produced through different wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) and post-processed (PWAAM) conditions. The plot highlights the variation in mechanical properties across the R and C specimen orientations, effectively demonstrating the influence of processing on material performance.

caption: Conceptual honeycomb model illustrating the influence of activator demands on the dissolution process within the printed structure.
summary: This schematic diagram utilizes a honeycomb analogy to explain the effect of activator demands on the dissolution process. In unsaturated states, numerous unfilled cells indicate insufficient activator content, whereas saturated conditions facilitate more uniform access to reactive particle surfaces, thereby influencing the overall dissolution and polycondensation reaction kinetics.

caption: Calculated HOMO, LUMO, and energy gap (ΔE) distribution for the 1ChCl:2Urea deep eutectic solvent system.
summary: This DFT simulation illustrates the electronic structure of 1ChCl:2Urea, specifically highlighting the HOMO, LUMO, and ΔE distributions. The HOMO region is primarily localized on the oxygen and carbon atoms of the heterocyclic ring, which serve as the main adsorption sites for the molecule within this eutectic solvent system.

caption: STEM-HAADF micrograph of the as-printed 282 side of the 282-HN dual material, revealing the characteristic γ/γ′ microstructure with spherical γ′ precipitates.
summary: This STEM-HAADF image displays the microstructure of Sample A, taken from the 282 side of the as-printed 282-HN dual material. The micrograph reveals a distinct γ/γ′ structure, characterized by the presence of spherical γ′ precipitates within the matrix, providing insight into the material's phase morphology after the printing process.

caption: Detachment peak force plotted against time for pure resin, highlighting a distinct crawling signal prior to the primary peak, which corresponds to a region of Teflon deformation.
summary: This plot illustrates the detachment force profile for pure resin over time. It identifies a specific crawling signal occurring before the major detachment peak. This initial signal is attributed to the deformation of the Teflon interface, providing insight into the mechanical behavior of the resin during the fabrication process.

caption: Viscosity-temperature relationship for a conventional crystalline alloy melt, demonstrating adherence to the Arrhenius equation as temperature decreases.
summary: This plot illustrates the viscosity-temperature relationship for a conventional crystalline alloy melt. The data demonstrates a clear adherence to the Arrhenius equation, where the melt viscosity gradually increases as the temperature decreases. This behavior is characteristic of crystalline materials, contrasting with the non-linear trends observed in amorphous alloy systems.

caption: Time-dependent variation of the creep rate for STA1080 and STA1150 specimens at 650 °C and 690 MPa.
summary: Creep rate profiles over time are shown for STA1080 and STA1150 at 650 °C and 690 MPa. The results indicate that STA1150 maintains a minimum creep rate approximately one order of magnitude lower than STA1080, confirming its enhanced creep resistance and improved mechanical performance under these specific high-temperature test conditions.

caption: Hardness versus indentation depth curves for the ODS Fe-Cr steel before and after irradiation by 6 MeV Au+ ions to peak displacement damage of 20, 40, and 80 dpa, showing markedly lower hardening increments of 16.2%, 66.0%, and 70.6%.
summary: The ODS Fe-Cr steel hardness-indentation depth curves illustrate the mechanical response under varying irradiation damage levels. Compared to the Fe-Cr counterpart, the ODS steel demonstrates superior radiation resistance, evidenced by significantly lower hardening increments of 16.2%, 66.0%, and 70.6% at 20, 40, and 80 dpa, respectively.

caption: Comparison of solidus (Tm) and liquidus (TL) temperatures for FexCoCrMnNi HEAs (open symbols) and FexCoCrMnNiCy HE cast iron alloys (filled symbols) as a function of iron concentration.
summary: This plot compares the experimental solidus and liquidus temperatures for FexCoCrMnNi HEAs and FexCoCrMnNiCy HE cast iron alloys. The data shows that Tm and TL values for the carbon-added alloys are significantly lower than those of the base HEAs, with Tm increasing linearly with iron concentration.

caption: Scheil solidification diagram for the Ti–42Nb+2.0C composition, revealing the early formation of primary TiC.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram for Ti–42Nb+2.0C depicts the solidification path under Scheil conditions. It reveals that approximately 3 vol% of primary TiC forms at the very beginning of the solidification process, while the subsequent transformation of the remaining liquid into TiC and β phases dominates the rest of the solidification.

caption: Finite Element Modeling model curves plotted against experimental total strain-stress results for the UD 0° specimen.
summary: Experimental total strain-stress data for the UD 0° specimen are plotted alongside corresponding Finite Element Modeling results. This comparison validates the model's predictive capability for the unidirectional composite in the longitudinal direction, highlighting the alignment between the simulated mechanical response and the actual tensile test measurements.

caption: Nano-indenter hardness profiles comparing the slightly damaged and damaged specimens, revealing work-hardening depths of ~20 μm and ~220 μm, respectively.
summary: Nano-indenter hardness profiles provide a high-resolution comparison of work-hardening depths. The slightly damaged specimen exhibits a 20 μm hardened depth, while the damaged specimen shows a 220 μm depth. In the damaged sample, hardness values reach 140% of the baseline, localized within 20 μm of the surface.

caption: Transmission spectrum of sample 3, documenting the optical performance after UV light exposure.
summary: The transmission spectrum of sample 3 is provided to document its optical performance following UV light exposure. Consistent with the other samples, the data shows stable transmission trends, confirming that the material's optical properties are preserved and do not exhibit signs of degradation throughout the duration of the UV test.

caption: Wear rates for Ti and hydrogel-coated samples, showing the optimal performance of the ATO + PB + NIR group.
summary: Wear rates are compared across all groups to evaluate durability. Both ATO and ATO + PB coatings effectively reduce wear rates compared to the Ti plate. The ATO + PB + NIR coating exhibits the optimal performance, achieving a wear rate of 0.138 × 10⁻³ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹, a 94.79% reduction from Ti.

caption: Cumulative reward trajectory over 500 training episodes, demonstrating the convergence and performance improvement of the RL agent on the cube geometry.
summary: Cumulative reward evolution is shown for the cube geometry training case. By tracking this metric alongside the step count, the plot illustrates the agent's success in optimizing its policy over 500 episodes, reflecting the overall learning progress and the effectiveness of the reinforcement learning approach for this specific geometry.

caption: Voltage-time profile of a Li/PVDF-LLZTO CPE/Li symmetric cell cycled at a constant current density of 0.1 mA/cm² at 25°C.
summary: The Li/PVDF-LLZTO CPE/Li symmetric cell exhibits excellent electrochemical stability during galvanostatic cycling at 0.1 mA/cm². Over a 140-hour duration, the cell maintains consistent voltage parameters, demonstrating no detectable short-circuit phenomena or deleterious increases in interfacial impedance, confirming the robust performance of the printed electrolyte under these specific test conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental map showing the distribution of C within the grain boundary precipitates, confirming the presence of carbides.
summary: Carbon mapping via EDS confirms the presence of carbides within the grain boundary precipitates. The correlation of C enrichment with Cr and Mo, as indicated by red arrows, supports the identification of these particles as Cr-rich carbides. This analysis is critical for characterizing the complex precipitate population in the AA condition.

caption: Mass-loss profiles of various SS316L rods measured via thermogravimetric analysis at a heating rate of 10 °C/min between 50 °C and 600 °C.
summary: This TGA curve illustrates the mass-loss profiles for SS316L rods heated at 10 °C/min from 50 °C to 600 °C. The analysis aims to evaluate the decomposition behavior of the polymer-wax binder and determine how recycling processes or ceramic additions influence the thermal degradation characteristics of the material.

caption: Agent performance metrics during the second phase of reward shaping for an extrusion process with a 232% flow rate at 190 °C.
summary: This panel depicts the second phase of agent performance during reward shaping. By monitoring the agent under a 232% flow rate at 190 °C, the learning curve highlights the intermediate progress of the model as it refines its strategy to mitigate extrusion errors during the training process.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectrum of the Ti3C2Tx MXene dispersion, featuring distinct peaks at 770 nm and 320 nm, with an inset photograph showing the stable aqueous colloidal solution.
summary: The UV–vis absorption spectrum of the Ti3C2Tx MXene dispersion exhibits characteristic absorption peaks at approximately 770 nm and 320 nm, consistent with reported data. Additionally, the inset photograph displays a dilute aqueous dispersion of the material, which typically exhibits a distinct greenish color, confirming the stability of the colloidal solution.

caption: Microstructure of the bottom region characterized by a fairly rounded grain morphology.
summary: The bottom region of the section displays a fairly rounded grain structure. This morphology is distinct from the finer and dendritic structures observed in the upper layers, reflecting the specific thermal conditions and processing history experienced by the material at the base of the section.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the X-Z section for a sample processed at 220 W, 1500 mm/s, and 80 μm hatch spacing.
summary: This EBSD IPF map displays the X-Z section for a sample processed at 220 W, 1500 mm/s, and 80 μm. The map illustrates the grain morphology and orientation, providing data on how this specific combination of laser power, speed, and hatch spacing dictates the resulting microstructure in the fabricated material.

caption: STEM micrograph displaying the material microstructure at the maximum range of the control factor.
summary: This STEM micrograph illustrates the material microstructure observed at the maximum range of the control factor. TEM analysis, as shown in Figure 10, serves to verify the findings obtained from EBSD, providing a comprehensive structural characterization that confirms the microstructural state under these specific experimental control conditions.

caption: IPF-Z orientation map of the second nanohardness indent, displaying the orientation of grains and coarser alpha laths oriented along distinct crystallographic directions.
summary: The IPF-Z orientation map for the second nanohardness indent displays the crystallographic orientation of grains. Unlike the first indent, this region shows coarser alpha laths oriented along several distinct crystallographic directions, illustrating the variability in microstructural features and their influence on the material's response to the nanohardness test.

caption: Relationship between the cyclic hardening/softening ratio (R) and total strain amplitudes for SLM Inconel 718 across various temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the cyclic hardening/softening ratio, temperature, and total strain amplitude.
