The inset dimensions for the IJP CL and MPL are 2945 nm by 1855 nm by 1405 nm and 3415 nm by 1955 nm by 1405 nm, respectively.

caption: Orthogonal axis alignment for CT-based fit assessment, showing four measurement points positioned tangentially to the CPC surface across axial, sagittal, and coronal sectional planes to quantify the implant-bone interface.
summary: Determination of the fit between the CPC implant and subchondral bone is achieved by placing two orthogonal axes tangential to the CPC surface within CT images. This methodology utilizes four specific measurement points across three anatomical planes to ensure precise alignment and consistent evaluation of the implant's fit within the bone.

caption: Atomic model depicting the hydrogen interstitial sites within the Mo2C crystal structure.
summary: This panel presents the atomic model of Mo2C, focusing on the interstitial sites available for hydrogen atoms. By illustrating these specific locations, the figure provides a clear representation of the hydrogen distribution within the Mo2C lattice, facilitating the study of hydrogen behavior in this material.

caption: High-speed photographic sequence of the ODMP detachment mode synchronized with corresponding current and voltage waveforms over three pulses.
summary: This high-speed photographic sequence captures the ODMP detachment mode, illustrating the formation and detachment of a drop across three distinct electrical pulses. The imaging period is precisely synchronized with the recorded current and voltage signals, providing a detailed temporal correlation between the physical droplet evolution and the electrical parameters.

caption: FT-IR spectra comparing the chemical structure of printed materials fabricated from various PA12 powder grades.
summary: This figure presents the FT-IR spectra used to characterize the chemical structure of printed materials derived from different PA12 powder grades. The spectroscopic analysis confirms the chemical consistency across the various powder grades used in the printing process, providing essential data on the material composition of the printed parts.

caption: 3D-APT reconstruction of Si distribution in the HH specimen after tensile testing to 3% strain.
summary: This 3D-APT reconstruction displays the Si distribution in the HH specimen following tensile testing interrupted at 3% strain. The visualization complements the TEM observations by providing a three-dimensional view of the Si precipitates, further elucidating the impact of environmental conditions on the dynamic aging behavior of the alloy.

caption: Maximum thruster temperature versus oxidizer-to-fuel ratio for injection case 2, illustrating consistent thermal behavior under varying flow rates.
summary: Maximum temperatures for injection case 2 are plotted against the oxidizer-to-fuel ratio. Similar to case 1, the data demonstrates that when enough oxidizer and coolant are supplied, specifically at ratios between 4 and 8, the cooling performance differences between injection configurations become negligible, resulting in stable thermal profiles for the thruster.

caption: Storage modulus E′ profiles for 0.1 wt% DWCNT reinforced nanocomposites, measured by DMTA to assess changes following water uptake.
summary: This plot presents the storage modulus E′ for 0.1 wt% DWCNT reinforced nanocomposites obtained through DMTA. By comparing the mechanical performance before and after water uptake tests, the panel demonstrates the effect of DWCNT reinforcement on the mechanical integrity of the nanocomposite when subjected to environmental moisture exposure.

caption: Absorbance-time profile measured via UV-Vis spectroscopy, illustrating the sedimentation kinetics for all compositions.
summary: The absorbance-time curve demonstrates the sedimentation behavior of the mixtures. A marked drop in absorbance is observed between approximately 5 and 7 minutes for all tested compositions, indicating a consistent kinetic trend in the settling process across the different samples analyzed in the study.

caption: Surface roughness (Sa) distribution for the EMEN1.5-TD alloy in the TD orientation after 600 s of immersion in 3 wt.% KCl solution.
summary: This panel illustrates the surface roughness (Sa) for the EMEN1.5-TD alloy in the TD orientation after 600 s of immersion in 3 wt.% KCl. The data is part of a trend where Sa values in the TD orientation decrease with increasing Er and Ni content, suggesting improved surface protection.

caption: Capacitance versus frequency (C-f) plots derived from impedance spectra measured at CE potentials corresponding to the four logic gate states.
summary: The C-f plot displays capacitance variations as a function of frequency for different applied bias voltages. These measurements were obtained from impedance spectra at CE potentials identified in panel (a). The results confirm that cycling under specific polarization conditions leads to distinct capacitance responses for the G-CAPode system.

caption: Schematic representation of an auxetic plate subjected to uniaxial tensile loading along the longitudinal x-direction, demonstrating the characteristic lateral expansion behavior.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental behavior of auxetic materials, which possess a negative Poisson's ratio. Under uniaxial tensile loading, the material exhibits lateral expansion rather than the contraction typically observed in conventional materials. This panel highlights the basic mechanical response of an auxetic plate when stretched along its longitudinal axis.

caption: Cole-Cole circle plot for SCF/Co@C composites illustrating polarization behavior.
summary: The Cole-Cole curve for SCF/Co@C composites is shown, featuring multiple semicircles. This specific morphology in the plot demonstrates the presence of multiple polarization mechanisms within the material, which contribute significantly to the overall dielectric loss characteristics of the composite system.

caption: APT reconstruction of the matrix region in the AA-HTA sample, focusing on the distribution of fine tertiary γ′ precipitates approximately 5 nm in size.
summary: This APT reconstruction focuses on the matrix region of the AA-HTA sample, which is devoid of larger secondary γ′ phases. It allows for the characterization of fine tertiary γ′ precipitates, which measure approximately 5 nm in size, providing a clear view of their distribution within the γ matrix.

caption: Optical micrograph of the as-built sample condition showing the presence of cracks and defects prior to the Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) treatment.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the as-built condition of the material, highlighting the presence of cracks and defects. Comparison with post-HIP conditions confirms that the HIP treatment is highly effective at eliminating these internal structural flaws, demonstrating a significant improvement in the material's integrity following the processing step.

caption: Elemental line scan analysis along the rake face of the TSN tool under SFNF-0.5 lubrication.
summary: This elemental line scan analysis tracks the composition along a 300 μm path from point S to point F on the tool rake face. Under SFNF-0.5 lubrication, the scan characterizes the reduced material transfer and adhesive wear, reflecting the improved performance of the textured tool in mitigating surface adhesion.

caption: Normalised load–displacement curves for SHS stub columns with n1m1 wave pattern at a slenderness ratio of b/(tε) = 60.
summary: Represented here are the normalised load–displacement responses for SHS stub columns with an n1m1 wave pattern at a higher slenderness ratio of 60. The curves illustrate how varying wave amplitudes influence the structural performance and ultimate load capacity compared to the perfectly straight specimen baseline for this specific slenderness.

caption: SHAP value distribution for KW connections processed via WAAM.
summary: This panel illustrates the SHAP values for KW connections produced through the WAAM process. By analyzing the magnitude and sign of these values, the plot reveals the strength and direction of individual feature effects on the model output, highlighting the specific influence of WAAM processing parameters on KW connections.

caption: Molecular structure representation of the CGRGDS peptide used for immobilization.
summary: The molecular structure of the CGRGDS mimicking peptide is displayed to illustrate the chemical species being immobilized. This peptide serves as the functional agent in the coupling reactions performed on both the FPEA-ProGly films and 3D-printed scaffolds, facilitating the surface modification observed in the corresponding mass spectra.

caption: Calculated density of states (DOS) for Al3Ni, showing the distribution of electronic states across the energy range relative to the Fermi level.
summary: The density of states (DOS) for Al3Ni is displayed to complement the band structure analysis. This plot provides insight into the electronic state distribution, supporting the observation that Al3Ni possesses metallic properties. The DOS data confirms the electronic behavior of the material as studied in the context of Fig. 10.

caption: Molecular dynamics snapshot at t = 4.2 ns showing the W-NP entrapment process, where the grain boundary, solid/liquid interface, and the ring around the nanoparticle are highlighted in yellow.
summary: This molecular dynamics snapshot at 4.2 ns illustrates the W-NP entrapment process. The grain boundary, solid/liquid interface, and the ring surrounding the nanoparticle are marked in yellow. The grain boundary exhibits a distinct bending behavior to trap the particle as it encounters the solid/liquid interface during the solidification process.

caption: Monte Carlo density field ρ, which is inversely proportional to the determinant of the Jacobian matrix J.
summary: This panel illustrates the auxiliary Monte Carlo density field ρ, which is inversely proportional to the determinant of the Jacobian matrix J. It provides a bounded and numerically robust complement to the metric tensor G, particularly near singular features, ensuring stability in the numerical representation of the polygon's geometry.

caption: Comparative analysis of wear-resistance performance for the current study against recently published literature [256–259], highlighting significant improvements in tribological properties.
summary: This plot evaluates the wear-resistance effectiveness of the developed samples compared to recent studies. Tribological testing demonstrates substantial performance gains, specifically achieving improvements of up to 78.51% regarding applied load, 68.42% in sliding distance, and 76.66% in sliding velocity, confirming the superior durability of the investigated coated materials.

caption: Microstructure of carbon steel deformed to a strain of 0.2 and annealed for 20 s, where recrystallized blue grains and deformed red grains are distinguished based on grain orientation spread (GOS) values.
summary: Carbon steel deformed to 0.2 strain and annealed for 20 s is visualized through reconstructed EBSD data. The microstructure is segmented into deformed (red) and recrystallized (blue) grains using GOS criteria. This map illustrates the progression of recrystallization within the steel matrix after the extended 20 s annealing duration.

caption: Minimal energy path for oxygen diffusion in a pure bcc molybdenum lattice calculated via the nudged elastic band method.
summary: Calculated using the nudged elastic band method, this panel illustrates the minimal energy path for interstitial oxygen diffusion within a pure bcc molybdenum crystal lattice. The simulation provides a baseline diffusion barrier value for oxygen migration in the absence of other interstitial species, serving as a reference for comparison.

caption: Surface morphology of the Ti model after 50 ps of exposure to a CO2 atmosphere.
summary: This MD snapshot illustrates the initial surface morphology of the Ti model after 50 ps of exposure to a CO2 atmosphere. As the simulation progresses, CO2 molecules continuously react with the titanium surface, initiating the formation of an oxide layer on the material's surface.

caption: S-N fatigue life curve for the EA treated LPBF Al alloy sample.
summary: The S-N fatigue life curve for the EA treated LPBF Al alloy sample is displayed. This plot is part of a comparative analysis of fatigue properties for different processing conditions, demonstrating that the LPBF-fabricated aluminum alloys exhibit limited anisotropy in their mechanical properties across the tested samples.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of the formation enthalpy for the Ti–Nb–Al ternary system within a melt pool containing a 0.10 mm thick Nb foil at 2250 K.
summary: Thermodynamic calculations of the Ti–Nb–Al ternary system formation enthalpy at 2250 K reveal the energetic landscape of the melt pool. The data indicates that metallurgical reactions between titanium and niobium are thermodynamically unfavorable in the absence of aluminum, highlighting the critical role of alloying elements in phase formation.

caption: Energy dissipation evolution for specimens surviving 1 million fatigue cycles at varying ambient temperatures.
summary: Energy dissipation is plotted for specimens that survived 1 million fatigue cycles while subjected to varying ambient temperatures. The stable trends observed in these samples confirm that the material maintains a consistent fatigue response under different thermal conditions, provided the specimens do not fail during the test.

caption: Three-dimensional finite element model of the four-point bending CAF process, illustrating the specimen geometry, loading and supporting head reference points (RP), and specific integration point (IP) at (0, 9, 0) for stress-strain evolution analysis.
summary: This three-dimensional finite element model represents the four-point bending CAF process, incorporating experimental dimensions and symmetry relative to the X′Z′ plane. It highlights the reference points for loading and support heads, alongside a specific integration point at (0, 9, 0) used to investigate stress and strain evolution during the process.

caption: Current density versus voltage (J-V) characteristics of photovoltaic cells encapsulated with pure COC and various COCA coversheets under direct sunlight illumination.
summary: This panel displays the J-V characteristics of solar cells using pure COC and COCA coversheets under direct sunlight. Sample COCA3 achieves a peak power conversion efficiency of 17.21%, while increasing the alumina proportion in COCA4 results in a 15.9% decrease in efficiency, demonstrating the impact of composition on performance.

caption: Cyclic ratcheting and damage evolution plot for the TO structure subjected to a cyclic stress of 46 MPa.
summary: Cyclic ratcheting and fatigue damage evolution are depicted for the TO structure under a 46 MPa stress level. The third stage of this process involves excessive crack propagation or damage accumulation, which ultimately leads to fatigue failure, providing critical insight into the material's long-term structural integrity under cyclic loading.

caption: EDX pattern and quantitative elemental composition for point B, representing the reinforcement particle.
summary: Quantitative EDX results for point B characterize the reinforcement particle. Notably, the carbon content exceeds the titanium content, which is attributed to the 50% contribution of nanographene within the initial Nano-powders mixture, providing insight into the chemical composition of the reinforcement phase incorporated into the H1 material.

caption: Interference fringes observed in the projected image under horizontal alignment conditions.
summary: Horizontal alignment of the PLM and DMD components results in the interference fringes shown here. During the adjustment process, this configuration represents a state where the offset of the interference fringes reaches its maximum, indicating that the PLM and DMD have achieved a perfect alignment in the light path.

caption: Schematic representation of the circular cone-beam CT acquisition geometry, illustrating the X-ray source rotating at distance D from the rotation center and the projection onto detector plane ω.
summary: This schematic illustrates the circular cone-beam CT acquisition geometry, where an X-ray source rotates around an object at distance D. It defines the object coordinate system (x, y, z) and the detector plane ω parameterized by (p, q), showing how rays intersect the plane to facilitate 3D line integral calculations.

caption: CCT diagram of EQ2.30 steel at 1% phase transformation, showing the shift in transformation curves under different interfacial energy conditions.
summary: The CCT diagram for EQ2.30 steel at 1% phase transformation illustrates the impact of interfacial energy on cooling transformation behavior. Variations in interfacial energy lead to significant shifts in the CCT diagram, confirming that these energetic differences are critical factors in determining the transformed phase volume fraction.

caption: Overview of thermal cycles monitored at point An over the full duration of 0–260 s, illustrating the global temperature evolution for different island sizes.
summary: This panel displays the comprehensive thermal cycle profile at point An across the entire 260-second duration. It serves as the baseline for understanding the temperature fluctuations experienced by the material under varying island sizes, providing a broad context for the subsequent high-resolution temporal snapshots presented in the following panels.

caption: Initial compressive shock wave propagation through the [100] model at a shock velocity of 1.0 km/s, visualized via atomic stress nephograms.
summary: This panel illustrates the initial stage of the spallation process in a [100] model subjected to a shock velocity of 1.0 km/s. It displays the compressive shock wave propagation using atomic stress nephograms, providing a foundational view of the stress distribution within the material at the onset of the shock event.

caption: HPLC chromatogram of the SLM-SnO2-NP formulation, exhibiting a prominent peak at the same retention time as the standard.
summary: The chromatogram of the SLM-SnO2 NP formulation displays a prominent peak at the identical retention time observed in the standard SLM. This result indicates that the encapsulation process within the nanoparticles did not alter the chemical identity of the analyte, confirming the stability of the SLM during formulation.

caption: 2D Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) plot illustrating the correlation between stress and incompatibility in the loading direction during the first cycle of loading.
summary: This 2D KDE plot visualizes the relationship between stress and incompatibility along the loading direction during the initial cycle. The contours represent the 0, 25th, 50th, 75th, and 100th percentiles of the density distribution, providing a baseline for understanding the correlation between stress states and material incompatibility at the start of cyclic loading.

caption: Logarithmic relationship between steady-state creep rate and applied stress for K4648 alloy specimens evaluated before and after corrosion exposure.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the natural logarithm of the steady-state creep rate and the applied stress for the K4648 alloy. By comparing the data before and after corrosion, the figure highlights how environmental degradation influences the creep behavior and mechanical performance of the alloy under steady-state conditions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for pure Zn and SLM-ed Zn-Cu alloys tested in simulated body fluids (SBF), illustrating the electrochemical response characterized by two distinct branches.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for pure Zn and SLM-ed Zn-Cu alloys tested in simulated body fluids (SBF) illustrate the electrochemical response characterized by two distinct branches. The observed narrow passivation region indicates that the ZnO/Zn(OH)2 films formed in the Cl-rich environment provide only limited protection to the alloy surface.

caption: Close-up view of the 1800–1400 cm-1 spectral range, highlighting the C=O stretching region of PLA.
summary: High-resolution spectral analysis between 1800 and 1500 cm-1 corroborates the embedding of PLA into filler lumens. A strong absorbance peak around 1750 cm-1, attributed to the C=O stretching of ester groups in PLA, remains clearly evident in the spectra of the extracted fillers, confirming successful matrix infiltration.

caption: Fluorescence imaging and quantitative analysis of HUVEC tube formation following 7-day co-culture with macrophage-conditioned media, scale bar 200 μm.
summary: Fluorescence images show that HUVEC in the piezoelectric scaffold group formed more extensive blood vessels and tubular structures compared to the PCL group. This quantitative analysis confirms that piezoelectric scaffolds, when binding to macrophages, significantly enhance the angiogenic capacity of HUVEC in vitro through improved tube formation.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves comparing the tensile behavior of as-built and as-cast specimens.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the tensile performance of as-built and as-cast specimens. The data reveals that the tensile properties of these two conditions differ significantly, highlighting the impact of the manufacturing process on the mechanical response of the material under uniaxial loading conditions during tensile testing.

caption: Plot of the strain rate raised to the power of 1/4.3 versus stress, used to determine the threshold stress for the titanium alloy.
summary: This panel displays a plot of the strain rate raised to the power of 1/4.3 against stress for a titanium alloy. By identifying the x-intercept on this curve, the threshold stress of the material is evaluated, providing a critical parameter for understanding the creep behavior of the alloy.

caption: Time-resolved snapshots of the reflected SPIFI light cursor captured at the processing plane, illustrating the dynamic evolution of the beam's spatial structure.
summary: These snapshots demonstrate the successful image-relayed SPIFI beam as it interacts with the processing plane. The sequence captures the spatial structure of the light cursor as it evolves over time, providing a clear visualization of the beam's behavior and stability during the processing operation as described in the experimental observations.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) curve for M4 material derived from JMatPro calculations.
summary: The CCT diagram depicts the phase transformation characteristics of M4 under continuous cooling conditions. Generated through JMatPro thermodynamic modeling, this plot identifies the critical cooling rates and temperature ranges required to achieve specific microstructural phases, serving as a fundamental guide for controlling the material's final properties during cooling processes.

caption: Transverse section of the weld bead morphology captured at a pulse frequency of 12 Hz.
summary: Captured at a pulse frequency of 12 Hz, this transverse section illustrates the weld bead morphology. The macrostructure appears free of voids or other structural irregularities. By examining this macrograph, the oscillation mode employed during the welding procedure can be effectively identified and characterized for the given frequency.

caption: Comparison graph showing predicted versus actual values for Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS).
summary: This graph compares the predicted UTS values against the actual experimental values. By plotting these data points, the panel illustrates the predictive accuracy and correlation of the UTS model, providing a visual representation of how well the statistical model captures the variance observed in the mechanical testing of the material.

caption: Inverse pole figure and pole figure maps of the as-built Ti–6Al–4V sample on the XZ plane, featuring insets for grain size and (0001) pole figure characterization.
summary: The EBSD analysis of the XZ plane reveals the initial microstructure of the as-built sample parallel to the building direction. By presenting the inverse pole figure and pole figure maps alongside grain size and (0001) orientation data, this panel characterizes the grain structure and texture developed during the fabrication process.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the W working electrode in LiCl-KCl at 450 °C, focusing on the -1.5 V to -0.3 V range, comparing the ZnCl2/Zn0 system (red) with the subsequent Ti addition (black).
summary: Cyclic voltammetry on a tungsten electrode at 450 °C reveals the ZnCl2/Zn0 soluble/insoluble system after adding ZnCl2. Subsequent addition of Ti shows the reduction of Ti III to Ti II, characterized as a fast, quasi-reversible one-electron exchange process with a cathodic-anodic potential difference of 0.18 V.

caption: True stress–strain curve for the LPBF-produced pure Cu specimen characterized by a relative density of 99.8%.
summary: The true stress–strain curve for the 99.8% relative density pure Cu sample is shown, reflecting the material's deformation behavior. This measurement indicates a true ultimate tensile strength of 392 MPa, averaged across three separate tests, providing a detailed representation of the mechanical properties of the as-printed pure Cu.

caption: Orthogonal experimental matrix detailing the systematic variation of laser power and scanning velocity parameters.
summary: This table presents the orthogonal experimental design used to optimize laser processing parameters. By systematically varying laser power and scanning velocity, the study establishes a structured approach to determine the ideal conditions for material fabrication, as illustrated by the experimental matrix designed to refine these critical manufacturing variables.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺:Er³⁺-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures following the second thermal cycle at 750°C, illustrating a reduction in defect-related emission intensity compared to the initial cycle.
summary: Panel b presents CL spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 750°C thermal treatment. The results show minor changes in emission profiles and a decrease in defect-related emissions across all doping ratios. This suggests that the second thermal cycle effectively reduces defects and amorphous regions within the microarchitectural structure.

caption: X-ray slice of the assembly featuring steel inserts, illustrating the impact of denser metallic elements on the reconstruction contrast.
summary: This panel displays an X-ray slice of the assembly incorporating steel inserts. The presence of denser elements, which appear brighter in the reconstruction, influences the overall contrast of the image. This visualization highlights how the inclusion of steel affects the ability to distinguish between the background and the polymer components.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H IEA steel irradiated in the JP25 experiment at a target temperature of 300 °C, with an actual measured irradiation temperature of approximately 380 °C.
summary: This panel presents Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H IEA steel subjected to irradiation within the JP25 experimental framework. Although the target irradiation temperature was 300 °C, the actual temperature recorded by SiC thermometry was approximately 380 °C, providing the necessary thermal context for interpreting the simulated material behavior.

caption: Laser absorptivity measurements for pure Mo and Mo-TiC composite powders plotted against wavelengths ranging from 500 to 2000 nm.
summary: This plot displays the laser absorptivity of pure Mo and Mo-TiC composite powders across a 500–2000 nm wavelength range. Laser absorption is a critical parameter for L-PBF processability, as it dictates the energy density absorbed by the powder material during the laser-based manufacturing process at specific wavelengths.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of IN718 lattices fabricated via LPBF under varying normalized enthalpy conditions, specifically low (50 W, 1200 mm/s), moderate (100 W, 450 mm/s), and high (200 W, 200 mm/s) energy inputs.
summary: This XRD analysis of IN718 lattices fabricated under low, moderate, and high normalized enthalpy conditions investigates the influence of heat flow on crystallographic orientation. By comparing experimental data against the Rigaku XRD database, the study provides insights into how different processing modes—LOF, conduction, and keyhole—affect the material's surface characteristics and structural properties.

caption: Roll bonding schematic demonstrating joint formation via parallel pressure application and plastic deformation of Al and Ti bonding partners.
summary: Roll bonding achieves joint formation by applying parallel pressure to the interface of Al and Ti partners. This schematic illustrates how the process induces significant plastic deformation in the bonding partners, which is essential for creating an intimate contact and a metallurgical bond between the two dissimilar materials.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of QS (bottom) and QSGM1 (top) acquired in D2O, demonstrating the structural changes following the modification process.
summary: 1H NMR spectroscopy was utilized to investigate the synthesis of QSGM1. By comparing the NMR spectra of the original QS and the modified QSGM1, researchers were able to confirm the successful modification. This technique provides detailed structural information regarding the chemical changes occurring during the reaction between QS and GM.

caption: Cubic octahedron coordination geometry representing the bcc-W CPGA unit cluster, featuring 12 nearest neighbor atoms positioned at the vertices.
summary: The bcc-W CPGA unit cluster is defined by a cubic octahedron coordination geometry, which serves as the dual polyhedron to the rhombic dodecahedron. This configuration comprises 12 nearest neighbor atoms located at the 12 vertices of the cubic octahedron, illustrating the distinct coordination environment of the bcc crystal structure.

caption: STA curve for the feedstock with 62 vol.% solid loading, exhibiting an intermediate mass loss of 6.9% and identifying maximum degradation speeds at 300 °C for PW and 450 °C for HDPE.
summary: This STA curve for the 62 vol.% feedstock shows an intermediate mass loss of 6.9%. The data identifies specific thermal degradation peaks at 300 °C for PW and 450 °C for HDPE, which were used to design a second printing cycle within the optimal temperature window for the material.

caption: Comparative Raman micro-spectroscopy profiles for standard white m-ZrO2 (thermally crystallized), black m-ZrO2 (thermally crystallized), and black m-ZrO2 (laser-converted at 532 nm and 270 W/mm2).
summary: This Raman micro-spectroscopy plot compares the structural signatures of three distinct ZrO2 samples: thermally crystallized standard white m-ZrO2, thermally crystallized black m-ZrO2, and laser-converted black m-ZrO2. The spectra provide a comparative analysis of the monoclinic phase characteristics and the impact of different crystallization methods on the oxygen-deficient nanoparticle structures.

caption: Room-temperature photoluminescence emission spectrum of PVA-assisted SnO2 nanostructures using an excitation wavelength of 248 nm.
summary: PVA-assisted SnO2 nanostructures display a characteristic photoluminescence emission spectrum when measured at room temperature with 248 nm excitation. The data illustrates how the incorporation of PVA surfactant modifies the optical emission properties of the SnO2 nanoparticles, allowing for a detailed assessment of surfactant-induced changes in the nanostructured material.

caption: Beeswarm plot of SHAP feature importance for surface pixels, illustrating the dual influence of heat intensity (HI) on porosity prediction.
summary: This beeswarm plot illustrates the SHAP feature importance for heat intensity (HI) regarding surface pixels. The distribution reveals two opposing trends where HI influences porosity either positively or negatively. Higher HI values are associated with greater absolute SHAP values, indicating a more substantial impact on the porosity prediction model.

caption: Atomic model of the M6C crystal structure.
summary: This panel presents the atomic model of M6C, which is included as one of the supercells used for the computational calculations. The structural representation highlights the atomic configuration of the M6C phase, contributing to the comprehensive set of models analyzed throughout the research presented in the figure.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of circular Ni electrodes in alkaline media, showing current density versus potential between -1.2 V and 1.2 V.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram displays the electrochemical activity of circular Ni electrodes in alkaline media. Testing within a potential range of -1.2 V to 1.2 V, the C3 electrode configuration achieved a peak current density of -11.31 mA/cm2 at -1.2 V, demonstrating superior performance compared to the C1 and C2 geometries.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the SnSbBiTe4 compound showing the stacking of septuple-layer blocks along the vertical axis, where the pnictogen sublattice is uniformly occupied by Sb and Bi atoms.
summary: The SnSbBiTe4 compound crystallizes in a trigonal structure with a hexagonal unit cell. The crystal structure consists of septuple-layer blocks [Te-Sb/Bi-Te-Sn-Te-Sb/Bi-Te] stacked along the vertical axis. The pnictogen sublattice is ideally occupied by Sb and Bi atoms, as visualized in this atomic model representation.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the EIS response of as-cast B30-x Fe alloys following 1 day of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: The EIS Bode plot for the B30-x Fe alloy after 1 day of immersion is shown here. This measurement captures the early-stage electrochemical impedance characteristics of the alloy surface as it begins to interact with the 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, reflecting initial changes in the protective surface layer.

caption: Hirtised strut surface visualization at a relative density of 5.0%, showing the modified surface texture following the post-processing treatment.
summary: Following the hirtisation process, this 3D micro-CT reconstruction shows a lattice strut with a relative density of 5.0%. The visualization illustrates the changes in surface morphology compared to the as-built state, providing the necessary data to quantify the reduction in surface roughness achieved through the hirtisation treatment.

caption: Step-by-step procedural flowchart illustrating the Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) algorithm used for the simultaneous optimization of output responses.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic procedure of the Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) algorithm. The methodology is applied to optimize output responses, specifically bead width and bead height, in thin-walled structures. This approach aims to enhance fabrication efficiency, reduce operating costs, and ensure optimal material usage during the manufacturing process.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) plot for Al, Ni, and Cu atoms in the Al7Cu4Ni precipitate, derived from DFT simulations.
summary: This PDOS plot illustrates the electronic structure of Al, Ni, and Cu atoms within the Al7Cu4Ni precipitate. Derived from DFT simulations, these data characterize the electronic states of the constituent elements, offering a fundamental understanding of the atomic bonding characteristics that influence the precipitate's mechanical stability.

caption: Dark-field transmission electron microscopy image of the same region, providing enhanced contrast for the carbide precipitates.
summary: Dark-field transmission electron microscopy (DF-TEM) imaging complements the bright-field observations by providing enhanced contrast for the carbide precipitates in the 550 °C tempered M2 high-speed steel. This technique allows for a clearer visualization of the carbide distribution, facilitating a more detailed investigation into the microstructural features of the material.

caption: Semi-logarithmic plot of the drain current modulus versus gate voltage, comparing the switching behavior across different deposition techniques.
summary: This semi-logarithmic plot compares the drain current modulus against gate voltage for various deposition techniques. It provides a clear visualization of the switching performance, showing that spin-coated devices achieve the highest ON current (-9.5 ± 0.9 mA), followed by AJP (-8.0 ± 0.5 mA) and IJP (-4.8 ± 0.6 mA) methods.

caption: BCC lattice unit cell structure rendered in purple.
summary: This panel displays the BCC lattice structure, which is one of the three POCS architectures investigated in this study. The BCC unit cell is represented in purple and serves as a comparative model for evaluating the thermohydraulic performance of different lattice geometries within the scope of this research.

caption: Pressure distribution contour of the nanoenhanced [HMIM][BF4] coolant sprayed from a nozzle at 1000 s.
summary: Pressure variation contours for the ionanocoolant fluid are presented at 1000 s. This simulation snapshot captures the final stage of the observed time sequence, showing the stabilized pressure distribution within the sprayed fluid as it exits the nozzle, reflecting the long-term fluid dynamics of the nanoenhanced coolant system.

caption: PND Rietveld refinement pattern for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 240 K, illustrating the fit between experimental data and the calculated structural model.
summary: This panel displays the PND Rietveld refinement for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 240 K. The plot features experimental data, a calculated intensity line, and a difference plot. This refinement is part of a combined approach with SR-PXD data to accurately determine the nuclear and magnetic structure of the specified alloy composition.

caption: Standard Ti–Al binary phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium phase fields as a function of temperature and aluminum concentration.
summary: This panel displays the Ti–Al binary phase diagram, which serves as the foundational reference for understanding the equilibrium phase relationships between titanium and aluminum. It maps the stability regions of various phases across different temperatures and compositions, providing essential thermodynamic context for the more complex alloy systems discussed in the study.

caption: Bright field TEM micrograph of the Ni/Ni2Al3 composite sheet showing the overall microstructure.
summary: This bright field TEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the Ni/Ni2Al3 composite sheet. The composite is composed of distinct Ni and Ni2Al3 phases, and the image reveals an obvious interface between these two phases, confirming the structural arrangement of the material as described in the study.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of irradiated single-crystal NiCoFe displaying the irradiation profile and FIB-induced defect clusters.
summary: This bright-field STEM image of irradiated single-crystal NiCoFe highlights the irradiation profile and identifies FIB-induced defect clusters. TEM investigations confirm the absence of significant voids in this material under the specified irradiation conditions, establishing that dislocation structures are the primary defects present in the irradiated regions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 in N2-saturated (dotted) and O2-saturated (solid) 0.1 M KOH electrolyte.
summary: The CV response of GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 in N2-saturated media displays a smooth rectangular shape, while the O2-saturated media exhibits a strong cathodic peak at +0.67 V. This shift confirms an effective oxygen reduction reaction occurring on the electrode surface, characteristic of high-performance electrocatalytic materials.

caption: Total reflection (TR) spectra of Ni-P coatings plotted as a function of wavelength.
summary: This panel displays the total reflection (TR) spectra for Ni-P coatings across various wavelengths. Total reflection measurements are typically associated with smoother surface morphologies. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the optical response of the Ni-P coatings, serving as a baseline for evaluating surface characteristics and light interaction properties.

caption: Absorptance spectrum of the second-layer HMCM featuring thirteen distinct units, where colored dashed lines indicate the specific absorption profiles of the constituent subunits.
summary: The absorptance spectrum for the second-layer HMCM, which incorporates thirteen diverse subunits, is presented. Individual absorption capabilities of these coupled subunits are highlighted by colored dashed lines. These results confirm the presence of continuous quasi-perfect absorption bands, matching the intended performance criteria for advanced metamaterial design and functionality.

caption: Light absorbance spectra comparing the capacity of different prints, highlighting the NIR region.
summary: This absorbance spectrum demonstrates a significant improvement in the light absorbance capacity of the 95%BPR5%BBZ1%PPy print compared to other formulations. The enhancement is particularly notable in the near-infrared (NIR) region, indicating that the addition of PPy effectively prepares the composite to function as an excellent NIR-light responsive material.

caption: Radial distribution function (RDF) plot representing the structural arrangement of a simulated polycrystalline material following the completion of an equilibrium process.
summary: This plot illustrates the radial distribution function (RDF) for a simulated polycrystalline material after it has undergone an equilibrium process. The RDF provides critical insight into the atomic-scale structural arrangement and local ordering of the simulated system, confirming the state of the material following the computational equilibration procedure.

caption: Radar chart comparing energy absorption indicators for OIPLs with varying numbers of cells, where efficiency peaks at N = 4.
summary: Energy absorption indicators for OIPLs are displayed in this radar chart, demonstrating the impact of the number of cells on performance. The analysis reveals that energy absorption efficiency reaches its maximum value at N = 4 for all tested OIPL configurations, identifying an optimal cell count for energy dissipation.

caption: Hierarchical classification scheme outlining various methodologies employed for the mechanical strengthening of adhesive joints.
summary: This schematic provides a comprehensive classification of techniques designed to improve the strength of adhesive joints. It highlights diverse strategies, including transverse joint reinforcement, which serves as a critical approach to mitigate delamination. The diagram organizes these methods to illustrate the systematic options available for enhancing structural adhesive performance.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for the thermosets and their corresponding monomers, showing degradation onset temperatures ranging between 110 °C and 127 °C.
summary: TGA curves for all thermosets and monomers are shown in panel c. As observed in the figure and corresponding data tables, all thermosets exhibit an onset of degradation, defined by T deg1% and T deg2%, occurring within the range of 110–127 °C, indicating similar thermal stability profiles for these materials.

caption: Evolution of the cost function for the Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) algorithm compared against the best and worst possible path planning solutions.
summary: This plot illustrates the cost evolution of MCTS-discovered strategies during path planning optimization. The algorithm rapidly approaches the optimal path, achieving a near-optimal solution within 21 iterations and reaching the global optimum in approximately 41,000 iterations, significantly outperforming previous benchmarks that required hundreds of thousands of iterations for similar geometries.

caption: Non-equilibrium solidification curve for the Si 0 MEA calculated using the Thea-3 database.
summary: The non-equilibrium solidification curve for the Si 0 MEA is presented, calculated using the Thea-3 database and thermal calculation software. This plot illustrates the solidification behavior of the alloy under non-equilibrium conditions, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of varying silicon content on the phase evolution of the material.

caption: Hyperparameter tuning results for the FE prediction model, with an inset table providing the final optimized hyperparameter values.
summary: This panel presents the hyperparameter optimization results for the FE prediction model, accompanied by an inset table listing the final optimized values. These findings detail the specific hyperparameter configurations achieved through the tuning process, which are essential for maximizing the predictive accuracy of the elongation model.

caption: Three-dimensional part fabricated via continuous ultrasonic jetting at a 2.5 mm nozzle-substrate distance, 10 mm/s speed, 390 °C, and 50 V, with visible upper-half remelting.
summary: This three-dimensional part was formed by continuous ultrasonic jet ejection at a 2.5 mm nozzle-substrate distance, 10 mm/s speed, 390 °C, and 50 V. The upper half of the part displays excessive remelting due to heat accumulation, suggesting that further research is required to optimize the forming quality of these parts.

caption: Shear stress distribution map across the sCFRTP–64Ti interface, visualized at the specific time step where macroscopic shear stress aligns with the failure stress observed in lap-shear testing.
summary: This panel displays the shear stress distribution at the sCFRTP–64Ti interface, analyzed at a time step corresponding to the macroscopic failure stress from lap-shear tests. The simulation reveals that the maximum shear stress at the crack tip reaches approximately 58 MPa, significantly exceeding the macroscopic failure stress of the material.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the twin interface in the as-deposited alloy, highlighting stacking faults growing from the boundary via slipping partial dislocations.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging of the twin interface in the as-deposited alloy demonstrates the presence of stacking faults. These defects are observed to grow directly from the twin boundary, driven by the movement of slipping partial dislocations, which characterizes the local deformation mechanism within the as-deposited material structure.

caption: Schematic representation of the horizontal load tester apparatus used to evaluate horizontal load capacity.
summary: This schematic illustrates the horizontal load tester configuration. The apparatus evaluates horizontal load capacity by converting standard weights into a horizontal force applied directly to the slider. This setup provides a controlled method for measuring mechanical load performance by translating vertical gravitational force into a horizontal testing vector.

caption: Raw neutron diffraction data for a textured stainless steel sample, plotted as intensity versus neutron arrival time and scattering angle (2θ).
summary: This panel displays raw neutron diffraction data collected from a textured stainless steel sample at the POLDI instrument. The data is presented as a plot of intensity versus neutron arrival time and scattering angle, where each Bragg reflection appears as a series of parallel lines corresponding to individual chopper slits.

caption: Ti K-edge XANES spectra for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys and hydrides with x=0 and x=0.10, compared against pure Ti metal reference.
summary: Normalized XANES spectra at the Ti K-edge for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys and their corresponding dihydrides are presented for x=0 and x=0.10. The absorption edge is clearly recognizable, although the EXAFS region remains ill-defined. Pure Ti metal is included as a reference to characterize the local electronic environment.

caption: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity measurements for the CrMnFeCoNiAg alloy film.
summary: This panel shows the temperature-dependent resistivity curve for the CrMnFeCoNiAg alloy film. By plotting resistivity against temperature, the graph highlights the electronic transport behavior of the Ag-doped Cantor alloy, contributing to the comparative analysis of how different elemental additions influence the resistivity of these high-entropy alloy films.

caption: Gravimetric discharge capacity versus cycle count for graphite-LFP coin cells comparing various 3D printed polymer gaskets against conventionally molded polypropylene controls, cycled between 2.5 and 3.8 V at C/20 for the first cycle and C/5 thereafter.
summary: This plot displays the cycling performance of graphite/LFP full cells using different gasket materials. The data shows that the APR gasket maintains stable cycling at 100 mAh/g for 20 cycles. These results demonstrate the electrochemical viability of 3D printed polymer gaskets compared to conventional polypropylene controls under standard cycling conditions.

caption: Cycling stability performance of the La0.6Y0.15Ca0.9Mg1.05Ni9Co0.45 alloy, showing the discharge capacity as a function of cycle number.
summary: The cycling stability of the La0.6Y0.15Ca0.9Mg1.05Ni9Co0.45 alloy is evaluated through a discharge capacity retention test. This specific alloy was selected for testing due to its superior overall hydrogen storage performance compared to other alloys in the series, providing a clear assessment of its long-term electrochemical durability during repeated charge-discharge cycling.

caption: Recoverable strain plotted against VED for a 200 MPa stress level, illustrating the impact of laser power (blue), scanning speed (green), and hatch space (red) on actuation, with the anchor point marked in black.
summary: At a 200 MPa stress level, the recoverable strain is plotted against VED to show the impact of different processing parameters. By adjusting laser power, scanning speed, and hatch space, the transformation behavior is modified. The black anchor point provides a reference for evaluating these specific processing parameter adjustments.

caption: Fatigue behavior of wrought Ti6Al4V variations, illustrating the impact of surface polishing on fatigue strength.
summary: Wrought Ti6Al4V samples exhibit minimal sensitivity to surface finish improvements. Although polishing reduces surface roughness compared to machined samples, the fatigue strength at runout to 1 million cycles shows only modest improvement, indicating that surface finish has a limited impact on the fatigue performance of this material.

caption: Nyquist plots displaying capacitive arc features for as-built and HIP LPBF 316L stainless steel, including the equivalent electrical circuit (EEC) used for data fitting.
summary: Nyquist plots for as-built and HIP LPBF 316L stainless steel samples exhibit capacitive arc features, indicating similar passive mechanisms. The fitting parameters for these electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements were derived using the equivalent electrical circuit model inserted directly into the plot to assess passive layer stability in chloride solution.

caption: Eclipsed adsorption configuration of hydrazine on the Zn(0 0 1) surface.
summary: Displayed is the eclipsed adsorption configuration of hydrazine on the Zn(0 0 1) surface. DFT modeling reveals an adsorption energy of -0.49 eV for this configuration. This value confirms that the Zn(0 0 1) surface releases lower adsorption energies than the Ni(1 1 1) surface, indicating reduced overall surface reactivity.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for N2H4 adsorption on the twin Ni (111) surface.
summary: This PDOS plot characterizes the electronic states of the twin Ni (111) surface after N2H4 adsorption. The data confirms a d-band center shift to -1.66 eV, reflecting the modified electronic environment induced by the twin boundary compared to the perfect Ni (111) surface.

caption: Average coefficient of friction (COF) values for SLMed 316L SS, CoCrMo, and Ti6Al4V samples measured under varying loads in FBS media.
summary: This plot displays the average coefficient of friction for three distinct SLMed metallic alloys—316L SS, CoCrMo, and Ti6Al4V—tested under different loading conditions in a simulated biological environment (FBS media). The data provides a comparative assessment of the tribological performance of these materials for potential biomedical applications.

caption: Dark-field TEM image showing rod-shaped and granular theta-Fe3C carbides dispersed across the ferrite plate at various orientations.
summary: This dark-field TEM image reveals numerous rod-shaped or granular theta-Fe3C carbides dispersed across the ferrite plate. These carbides are oriented at various angles, exhibiting an approximate 55° deviation between them, which provides detailed insight into the secondary-phase precipitation morphology within the pro-eutectoid ferrite matrix.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation diagram illustrating the kinetics of NbC precipitation in AM Inconel 718 superalloy, showing curves for 50% and 99% transformed fractions.
summary: This time-temperature-transformation diagram characterizes the precipitation kinetics of NbC in AM Inconel 718. By calculating the times required to reach 50% and 99% transformed fractions, the plot provides a comprehensive overview of the transformation behavior across various temperatures, serving as a critical reference for understanding phase evolution in this superalloy.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance modulus and phase angle for the Y-Z section of the Wall 0 sample.
summary: The Y-Z section of the Wall 0 sample is characterized by this Bode plot. At the start of the immersion test, the impedance modulus is measured at approximately 10⁴ Ω·cm² at low frequencies. A subsequent reduction of one order of magnitude after 14 days indicates a degradation of the surface barrier.

caption: Cutting force (FC) variation as a function of cutting speed for different nozzle designs, showing a 35% reduction with the straight converging nozzle D1 compared to D0 at 160 m/min.
summary: Cutting force measurements demonstrate the impact of nozzle geometry on machining efficiency. At a cutting speed of 160 m/min, the straight converging nozzle D1 significantly reduces cutting force by 35% compared to the conventional D0 design and by 37% relative to flood cooling, highlighting the effectiveness of optimized nozzle design.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining for CK5 and CK18 markers in undifferentiated MSCs, differentiated MSCs, and primary tracheal epithelial cells.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining for CK5 and CK18 markers confirms the successful differentiation of MSCs into an epithelial phenotype. The expression levels observed in the differentiated MSCs are only slightly lower than those in primary tracheal epithelial cells (P < 0.05), demonstrating the efficacy of the differentiation protocol at a 100 μm scale.

caption: GD-OES depth profile of A59 alloy showing elemental mass concentration after polarization at 700 mV vs Ag/AgCl.
summary: The GD-OES depth profile for A59 alloy polarized at 700 mV demonstrates a layered elemental distribution within the passive film. Similar to A625, molybdenum is enriched at the outermost surface, while chromium serves as the primary component of the passive layer beneath this surface region, indicating a consistent passive film structure.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of mono-vacancy counts in pure Ni and Ni-Fe/Ni-Cr alloys at 1200 K, showing a consistent decrease in single vacancy populations across all systems as simulation time progresses from 1 ns to 5 ns.
summary: This panel illustrates the temporal evolution of mono-vacancy populations in pure Ni and various Ni-Fe and Ni-Cr alloy systems at 1200 K. Data collected at 1, 3, and 5 ns reveal a general decrease in the number of single vacancies as the simulation progresses, indicating vacancy migration and clustering behavior.

caption: Aperiodic V minimal surface constructed from the pentagonal prism-based unit cell.
summary: The aperiodic V minimal surface is shown as a complex assembly derived from the pentagonal prism unit cell with vertex-oriented tunnels. This structure exemplifies the application of Tile(1,1)-based construction techniques to generate non-periodic minimal surfaces, demonstrating the spatial complexity achievable through the systematic arrangement of these geometric patches.

caption: O 1s core-level XPS spectrum of the Al2O3–TiO2 coating deconvoluted into contributions at 532.26 eV, 531.2 eV, and 529.7 eV.
summary: The O 1s XPS spectrum of the Al2O3–TiO2 coating shows a main peak at 532.26 eV (Al–O) with additional contributions at 531.2 eV (Ti–O) and 529.7 eV (Al–O–Ti). The combined binding energy of 530.87 eV confirms a complex mixture of Ti–O and Al–O–Ti chemical species.

caption: Pole figures representing the crystallographic texture development in samples processed at 1050 °C, 1150 °C, and 1230 °C HIP temperatures.
summary: Pole figures characterize the crystallographic texture development resulting from different HIP temperatures. These plots provide insight into the preferred orientations of the grains, confirming that the processing temperature significantly influences the crystallographic texture of the samples, consistent with the observed changes in grain structure and overall material properties.

caption: Two-dimensional projection of the supercell along the [111] direction, illustrating the configuration where the primary alloying element X (purple) and the secondary alloying element Z occupy the same atomic layer.
summary: This panel displays a 2D projection of the supercell along the [111] direction, highlighting the atomic arrangement where alloying elements X and Z reside on the same layer. The purple atoms represent element X, while numbered sites indicate potential positions for element Z, facilitating the study of independent configuration energies.

caption: Line chart demonstrating the model stability and prediction efficiency.
summary: This line chart provides a visual assessment of the model's performance, specifically highlighting its stability and prediction efficiency. By plotting these metrics, the figure illustrates how effectively the model converges and maintains consistent results, serving as a key indicator of the computational reliability and efficiency of the proposed machine learning approach.

caption: Schematic representation of the dual-laser scanning experiment, highlighting the 200 µm offset between laser beams and the resulting vapour depression zone within the substrate.
summary: This schematic illustrates the dual-laser experimental setup used to study pre- and post-heating strategies. It depicts the 200 µm offset between the two laser beams, each with an 80 µm spot diameter, and shows the formation of a vapour depression zone in the substrate during the scanning process.

caption: Bar chart summarizing the average indentation hardness and elastic modulus values obtained from nanoindentation tests performed on the 7 wt%Co-coated BNi-2 joint interface after 30 minutes of brazing.
summary: This chart summarizes nanoindentation test results for the 7 wt%Co-coated BNi-2 joint interface. It presents average values for indentation hardness and elastic modulus, specifically highlighting a hardness of approximately 8 GPa and an elastic modulus of about 230 GPa for the interface region after 30 minutes of brazing time.

caption: Voltage-current characteristics of patterned and un-patterned bridge segments measured at 7.6 K under transverse magnetic fields of 30 and 50 mT, with critical current values Jc identified at the 0.1 µA departure threshold.
summary: This plot displays the VI-characteristics for patterned and un-patterned bridge segments at 7.6 K under 30 and 50 mT transverse magnetic fields. Patterned regions exhibit earlier departures from zero voltage and shallower slopes beyond Jc compared to un-patterned segments. The inset provides an expanded view of negative current regions near Jc.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Fe in the heat-treated radial plane, showing the effect of thermal processing on segregation.
summary: Iron elemental mapping of the heat-treated radial plane provides insight into the chemical homogenization achieved through thermal processing. This map illustrates the distribution of Fe within the 316L SS microstructure after heat treatment, allowing for a comparison with the depletion patterns observed in the as-fabricated condition.

caption: Cumulative spacetime proximity plotted against measured melt-pool signal values, featuring a third-order polynomial fit with an R-squared value of 0.67.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between cumulative spacetime proximity and measured melt-pool signal values. A third-order polynomial regression is applied to the dataset, yielding an R-squared value of 0.67. This visualization demonstrates the correlation between the calculated proximity metric and the empirical melt-pool data collected during the process.

caption: Computed methanol electro-oxidation reaction pathway on Pd(111) surface, highlighting the minimum energy path in red, H-removal steps in green, and OH-coupling in blue.
summary: This panel displays the DFT-calculated methanol oxidation reaction pathway on Pd(111) at 0 V vs. RHE. The minimum energy path is highlighted in red, while green and blue arrows denote deprotonation and OH-coupling steps, respectively. Thermodynamic analysis reveals that CH2O is not an intermediate on the minimum energy path.

caption: Design chart representing the parameter space for the J-shaped prosthesis configuration.
summary: This design chart maps the parameter space for the J-shaped prosthesis. It is utilized to locate optimal solutions for Design Case II. The chart corresponds to Config. 58, which represents the specific design parameters where a valid solution for the J-shaped prosthesis geometry was successfully identified.

caption: Temperature-dependent normalized electronic specific heat for the Ta5+yW35-yMo5Re35Ru20C20 HEA series, with the α-model fit indicated by a red solid line.
summary: This panel displays the temperature dependence of normalized electronic specific heat for the Ta5+yW35-yMo5Re35Ru20C20 HEA series. The data, plotted as Cel/γT versus T, are isolated by removing phonon contributions. The red solid line indicates the theoretical fit obtained using the α-model, providing insight into the electronic behavior of the material.

caption: Maximum nozzle displacement limit δ max defined for a contact angle θ s ≥ π /2.
summary: Shown is the maximum nozzle displacement limit, δ max, for conditions where the contact angle θ s is greater than or equal to π /2. Establishing this upper bound is essential for optimizing the printing process, ensuring that the nozzle remains within a range that prevents trace discontinuity and droplet buildup.

caption: Particle size distribution curve for the 1 wt% B4C-modified powder.
summary: This particle size distribution curve characterizes the 1 wt% B4C-modified powder. The uniform decoration of nanoparticles on the powder surface, as shown in the corresponding SEM images, plays a crucial role in achieving controlled enhancement in laser absorption and scattering for this specific powder concentration.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the oxide layer on Y-doped TiAlCr alloy oxidized at 1000 °C for 100 h, demonstrating improved layer flatness and a distinct two-layer structure containing external equiaxed and internal columnar grains.
summary: Doping the TiAlCr alloy with Yttrium significantly improves the flatness of the oxide layer compared to the un-doped alloy. The cross-sectional SEM morphology reveals a characteristic two-layer structure, featuring an outer region of equiaxed grains and an inner region of columnar grains formed after 100 hours of oxidation.

caption: H&E and fluorescence staining images illustrating the stepwise construction of SRCP from decellularized porcine cornea (DPC), with scale bars of 50 μm.
summary: Stepwise construction of the SRCP was evaluated using H&E and fluorescent staining. The images show the primary component changes during the construction process starting from decellularized porcine cornea. These histological and fluorescence staining techniques provide visual confirmation of the structural evolution and composition of the scaffold during its fabrication.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance profiles for Biomed Clear resin subjected to 60 minutes of UV treatment at 60 °C, illustrating the effect of parylene-C coating on monomer leaching.
summary: Shown here are UV-Vis absorbance profiles for Biomed Clear resin after 60 minutes of UV treatment at 60 °C. The spectra compare monomer release in DPBS for coated and uncoated samples. Similar to heat treatment, UV exposure reduces absorption levels, indicating decreased monomer concentration in the solution.

caption: Thermal strain curves of pure ABS and ABS/Pyro composites containing 20, 30, and 40 vol% Zn1.6Mg0.4P2O7 filler, obtained via thermomechanical analysis.
summary: This thermomechanical analysis (TMA) plot illustrates the thermal strain behavior of pure ABS polymer compared to ABS/Pyro composites with varying filler concentrations of 20, 30, and 40 vol%. The data demonstrates how the incorporation of Zn1.6Mg0.4P2O7 filler influences the dimensional stability and thermal expansion characteristics of the ABS matrix across the measured temperature range.

caption: Rigidity measurements for long fiber CFRP, titanium alloy, cobalt-chromium, short fiber CFRP, and PEEK rods.
summary: Rigidity values are compared across five different material types. The cobalt-chromium rods demonstrate the highest rigidity at 56.7 kN/m ± 0.2 kN/m, while the long fiber CFRP, titanium alloy, PEEK, and short fiber CFRP rods show significantly lower values of 33.8, 27.8, 0.7, and 0.4 kN/m, respectively.

caption: Tensile stress-strain response of the welded specimen repaired with a length of 30%.
summary: Shown is the stress-strain curve for the specimen repaired with a 30% length. The curve maintains a shape consistent with the original and 20% repair samples, showing no yield platform and fracturing in the weld zone. While strength properties decrease after re-welding, the elongation remains relatively stable across these conditions.

caption: Transmittance spectra of S-CNC/CTFA composite resins evaluated at different filler concentrations.
summary: The transmittance spectra of the S-CNC/CTFA composite resins are presented to evaluate the effect of filler concentration on optical properties. The data confirms a significant reduction in the transparency of the S-CNC/CTFA composite, highlighting the impact of S-CNC concentration on the overall optical performance of the resin.

caption: HFR Sol. changes during the OER active and inactive phases, showing a variation of approximately 80 mΩ within a 40 s timeframe.
summary: The HFR Sol. evolution is shown for a 40 s timeframe around 5 h. The data indicates that HFR Sol. changes by approximately 80 mΩ between the OER active and inactive phases, highlighting the rapid resistance fluctuations occurring during the individual pulses of the stability measurement.

caption: Average load-depth curves obtained from nanoindentation testing across distinct material zones, featuring error bars representing the statistical variation derived from 25 individual measurements per area.
summary: This plot displays the average load-depth curves acquired through nanoindentation across different zones of the specimen. By averaging 25 individual measurements for each area, the data provides a reliable mechanical characterization. Error lines are included to illustrate the statistical spread and precision of the measured results across the tested regions.

caption: Complex plane impedance spectra of the specimens following a H2–no H2–H2 sequence, where experimental data points are compared against best-fit lines derived from the MCM model.
summary: Complex plane impedance spectra for the studied specimens are presented following a H2–no H2–H2 sequence. The experimental data points are plotted alongside solid lines representing best-fit calculations based on the MCM. These results illustrate a strong correspondence between the experimental measurements and the model predictions for the investigated materials.

caption: Pareto plot illustrating the statistical significance of processing parameters on yield stress.
summary: This Pareto plot identifies the factors influencing yield stress. Statistical analysis reveals that pressing speed, temperature, and lubricant choice are the most significant parameters affecting this mechanical response. These findings highlight the critical variables that must be controlled to optimize the yield stress of the material during the manufacturing process.

caption: Logarithmic plot of steady-state creep rate versus applied stress at temperatures of 1240°C, 1260°C, and 1280°C.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between steady-state creep rate and applied stress across three distinct temperatures: 1240°C, 1260°C, and 1280°C. Represented as a logarithmic graph of ln(creep rate) versus ln(stress), the data provides critical insights into the creep behavior and stress sensitivity of the material under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Combined DSC and TG curves for precursor P1 measured at a heating rate of 10 °C/min under an argon atmosphere.
summary: Thermal behavior of precursor P1 is characterized by simultaneous DSC and TG analysis conducted at a heating rate of 10 °C/min in an argon environment. These curves provide essential data on the mass loss and heat flow transitions occurring during the thermal decomposition process of the precursor material.

caption: Cross-sectional micro-CT visualization confirming the internal structure of a regolith cluster located near the filament surface.
summary: X-ray microtomography provides internal confirmation that the surface bumps observed on the filaments correspond to distinct clusters of regolith material. These clusters are situated near the filament surface, validating the hypothesis that particulate inclusions are the primary cause of the observed surface irregularities and diameter inconsistencies.

caption: Relationship between applied heat flux and the resulting temperature gradient distribution.
summary: This panel illustrates the experimental data distribution of temperature gradients as a function of heat flux. As a critical input variable, the heat flux data helps define the thermal response of the system, providing essential insights into the relationship between external thermal loading and internal temperature gradients.

caption: Comparative cross-sectional wear track depth profile, summarizing the geometric evolution of the wear track under varying test conditions.
summary: This profile summarizes the cross-sectional wear track geometry, reflecting the influence of applied loads and sliding duration. The observed fluctuations in the depth profile are directly linked to the accumulation and elimination of wear debris, providing insight into the material's wear behavior during the in-situ tribological testing.

caption: Comparison of PINN model predictions at varying hidden layers against experimental temperature data at the TC1 probe location.
summary: This plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model by comparing its output at different hidden layer configurations against experimental data from the TC1 probe. Shallow network architectures often fail to capture transient cooling dynamics, resulting in significant errors during peak or tail regions.

caption: Reconstruction slice of the part after 20 iterations of OSMO optimization.
summary: This reconstruction slice demonstrates the high-quality dose distribution achieved after 20 iterations of OSMO. Compared to ZDO, OSMO provides superior homogeneity and resolution. While ZDO maintains higher energy density, OSMO effectively optimizes the dose distribution, resulting in a more precise and uniform final printed part structure.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) projection of the sixteen-dimensional FDM formulation space into two dimensions, comparing original formulations (orange diamonds) with AI-generated formulations (blue, red, and green circles representing models 1–9, 10–18, and 19–27, respectively).
summary: This PCA plot visualizes the high-dimensional FDM formulation space reduced to two dimensions. It contrasts original formulations with AI-generated variants, categorized by model groups. The visualization demonstrates how AI-generated compositions expand the existing formulation space, identifying new printable regions and providing a framework for evaluating the novelty and realism of generated materials.

caption: Creep-rupture data for Alloy 617 plotted against the SLST parameter, which incorporates stress, log(stress), and inverse temperature terms.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep-rupture behavior of Alloy 617 by utilizing the SLST parameter model. By integrating stress, log(stress), and inverse temperature terms, the assessment provides a comprehensive representation of the material's creep performance, effectively correlating experimental rupture data with the defined SLST parameter framework for structural analysis.

caption: Comparative X-ray diffraction patterns for wrought and SLM-processed Ti-64 alloys, identifying the presence of alpha, alpha-prime, and beta phases.
summary: Comparative XRD patterns for wrought and SLM-3D printed Ti-64 alloys are displayed to characterize their crystalline structure. The diffraction data confirms the presence of both alpha/alpha-prime and beta phases within the material, highlighting the structural differences resulting from the distinct manufacturing processes used for the two alloy samples.

caption: 3D surface topography of the Ni–Mo–W coating electrodeposited at a current density of 40 mA/cm2.
summary: Captured using atomic force microscopy, this panel shows the 3D surface topography of the Ni–Mo–W coating prepared at 40 mA/cm2. The image highlights the specific surface features and roughness characteristics developed under these electrodeposition parameters, allowing for evaluation of the coating's structural evolution.

caption: Tensile modulus measurements for printed PET oligomer, vitrimer, and PETG materials.
summary: Tensile modulus values are centered around 1.5–1.6 GPa across all tested materials. The observed differences remain within a 3–5% range, indicating that the stiffness of the printed specimens is effectively preserved following the network formation process and the incorporation of silica additives into the vitrimer matrix.

caption: Comparative analysis between detected micro-CT defects, represented by black marks, and the established acceptability condition.
summary: This plot compares the actual defects detected via micro-CT, indicated by black marks, against the defined acceptability condition. By overlaying experimental defect data onto the theoretical acceptance map, the panel facilitates a direct assessment of whether specific structural flaws exceed the safety thresholds required for the bracket's operational integrity.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves comparing pure-Cu and composite samples measured at room temperature.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for pure-Cu and composite samples are presented at room temperature. These results illustrate the electrochemical behavior of the materials, providing a comparative analysis of the pure-Cu and composite specimens under identical experimental conditions to evaluate their respective electrochemical responses and performance characteristics in the specified environment.

caption: Hard-axis (HA) magnetic hysteresis loops for 15 nm NiFe thin films deposited on Kapton substrates at sputtering powers ranging from 25 W to 100 W.
summary: Panel b shows the hard-axis magnetic hysteresis loops for NiFe films on Kapton. While the coercive field is higher than that observed on Si substrates, the HA loop inclinations and coercive fields remain unaffected by variations in sputtering power, suggesting a consistent magnetic behavior across the tested power range.

caption: Heat flow curves demonstrating the thermal effects associated with the debinding process across different atmospheric conditions.
summary: Heat flow curves present the thermal effects of debinding in different atmospheres. The results show that oxidative degradation contributes to mass loss, with stable intermediate products being removed at temperatures between 300 °C and 350 °C. Larger samples exhibit reduced oxidative degradation due to their decreasing specific surface area.

caption: Three-dimensional X-ray computed tomography reconstruction of the pLS sample illustrating internal porosity distribution.
summary: The three-dimensional X-ray computed tomography reconstruction of the pLS sample highlights the internal porosity distribution. By utilizing XCT, the morphology of the pores is clearly visualized, allowing for a comparative assessment of the structural integrity and pore characteristics inherent to the pLS fabrication method compared to the DBLS sample.

caption: Parameter K6 distribution plotted as a function of the carbon-concentration gradient parameter p and the graded layer thickness dt.
summary: Parameter K6 is visualized as a function of the carbon-concentration gradient parameter p and the graded layer thickness dt. This map is part of a set of seven stress/strain parameters used to optimize the carbon-concentration gradient and layer thickness for material design.

caption: Raman spectra of Ba(Ti 1-δ Zr δ )O 3 ceramic samples, illustrating the influence of varying stoichiometric ratios and sintering temperatures on vibrational modes.
summary: This figure displays the Raman spectra for Ba(Ti 1-δ Zr δ )O 3 ceramics. The data highlights how different stoichiometric compositions and varying sintering temperatures affect the material's vibrational characteristics. These spectroscopic results provide insight into the structural variations induced by chemical substitution and thermal processing conditions within the ceramic samples.

caption: Nyquist plot detailing the electrochemical impedance characteristics of the YZ section of Wall 0.
summary: Electrochemical impedance data for the YZ section of Wall 0 is presented in this Nyquist plot. The reduction of the semicircle diameter reflects the degradation of the material. Despite the progression of corrosion, the formation of corrosion products after two days acts to decelerate the observed corrosion phenomena.

caption: Normal probability plot of residuals for flexural strength of transverse specimens.
summary: This normal probability plot of residuals for the flexural strength of transverse specimens indicates that the normality assumption is acceptable. The residuals are distributed approximately along a straight line, demonstrating that the quadratic model explains a significant portion of the response variation and provides a good fit for the data.
