caption: High-resolution Ti 2p XPS spectra comparing the material state before and after alkali metal adsorption and desorption processes.
summary: High-resolution Ti 2p spectra are shown in panel b, recorded for materials before and after alkali metal adsorption. This comparison highlights changes in the chemical state of titanium, providing insight into the electronic environment and surface interactions occurring during the adsorption and desorption cycles of the alkali metal.

caption: Nonlinear fluorescence decay profile and corresponding biexponential fit for TPU/1 C composite.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime data for the TPU/1 C composite is presented as a nonlinear decay curve measured at 465 nm. The experimental data is modeled with a biexponential function to extract the lifetime parameters, illustrating the decay behavior of the coumarin-doped TPU composite under room temperature conditions.

caption: Peak resultant force trends as a function of iterations for both cutting fluid types at a surface speed of 45 m/min.
summary: At a surface speed of 45 m/min, the peak resultant force is tracked against the number of iterations until tool failure. The nanobubble-based cutting fluid exhibits a consistently higher peak resultant force than the normal cutting fluid, even though the nanobubble fluid contributes to a reduction in tool flank wear.

caption: Permutation-based feature importance analysis for the XG-1 model trained on dataset D1.
summary: Permutation-based feature importance analysis for the XG-1 model trained on dataset D1. This plot identifies the specific features that significantly impact the classification performance of the XG-1 classifier. It provides a clear visualization of the most informative content used by the model to achieve its predictive results.

caption: Tabular representation of adhesive shear strength values for depth-defined porous samples at six distinct depths ranging from 0.50 mm to 6.00 mm.
summary: The table presents quantitative shear strength data for depth-defined porous samples. For the smallest pore size, measured strengths are 26, 23, 23, 22, 20, and 7 MPa at depths of 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 2.00, 4.00, and 6.00 mm, respectively, highlighting the performance variation across different porous layer thicknesses.

caption: Normalised permeation current density decay transient from -50 to -35 mA for AM-fabricated AISI 4340 steel tempered at various temperatures in 0.1 M NaOH, showing experimental data as dashed lines and MATLAB-fitted curves as solid lines.
summary: This panel displays the decay transient of normalised hydrogen permeation current density for AM-fabricated AISI 4340 steel. The experimental data, fitted with high accuracy (R2 > 99%), demonstrates that tempering at 425 °C significantly accelerates the transition to a steady state, resulting in steeper permeation curves compared to other conditions.

caption: Service decomposition, model mapping, and implementation workflow for Service 1, illustrating the integration of global in-situ monitoring images for detection tasks.
summary: This flowchart details the service decomposition and model mapping for Service 1. It highlights that Layer Shifting, Warping, and Extrusion Interruption detection processes utilize global in-situ monitoring images. These images serve as the foundational data required by the pre-trained spaghetti detection model to ensure effective monitoring during the implementation phase.

caption: Evaluation of Mode II fracture toughness results using the ENF method, contrasted with existing literature values for 3DPCM.
summary: Mode II fracture toughness results obtained via the ENF method are compared with values reported in the literature. Although the ENF method is less frequently analyzed than the DCB method for 3DPCM fracture analysis, this plot provides a necessary benchmark for the experimental results presented in this research.

caption: Hardness values of SLM-formed Ti2AlNb alloy plotted against varying solution treatment temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness response of Ti2AlNb alloy fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) when subjected to different solution treatment temperatures. The data highlights how thermal processing parameters directly influence the mechanical hardness of the alloy, providing a baseline for understanding the material's structural evolution during subsequent heat treatments.

caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 60% hemp content mix, representing the uncertainty analysis for the highest hemp concentration.
summary: The 60% hemp content mix is analyzed via Monte Carlo simulation to determine the probability distribution of its global warming potential. This panel provides the uncertainty profile for the highest hemp concentration tested, completing the comparative assessment of environmental impacts across the various hempcrete mix designs presented in the study.

caption: XRD diffraction pattern of the LPBF Inconel 625 alloy used to identify the constituent crystalline phases.
summary: The XRD diffraction pattern provides a comprehensive phase analysis of the LPBF Inconel 625 alloy. By identifying the characteristic peaks, this analysis confirms the crystalline structure and phase composition of the material, serving as a fundamental component of the overall microstructural characterization of the laser-processed alloy.

caption: Non-supported sintered sample within the powder bed, highlighting a material gap surrounding the contour as indicated by the red arrow.
summary: This photograph displays a non-supported sintered sample still embedded in the powder bed. A distinct gap of material is visible surrounding the sample contour, as indicated by the red arrow. This observation was made after the laser was turned off but prior to the removal of the sample from the bed.

caption: High-speed camera capture of the droplet bursting stage during the CMT-WAAM deposition process.
summary: Documented by high-speed camera, this final panel shows the droplet bursting stage during the CMT-WAAM deposition process. The image captures the moment of material transfer, completing the observed transition cycle. This stage is essential for understanding the dynamics of metal deposition and the overall stability of the arc process.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of HCS-2/8 tumor cells stained with live/dead markers after exposure to various hydrogel scaffolds.
summary: Live/dead staining images reveal the viability of HCS-2/8 tumor cells treated with different hydrogel scaffolds. Living cells are identified by green fluorescence, while dead cells exhibit red fluorescence. These images provide an intuitive observation of the cytotoxic effects exerted by the hydrogel treatments on the human chondrosarcoma tumor cells.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the as-received Alloy 718 microstructure obtained via Electron Back-scatter Diffraction (EBSD).
summary: This EBSD-based Inverse Pole Figure map characterizes the microstructure of the as-received Ni-base superalloy 718. The visualization provides a representative view of the grain orientation and structural distribution within the material, serving as a baseline for understanding the initial state of the alloy prior to further processing or testing.

caption: Nyquist plots displaying the imaginary versus real components of impedance for Cu75, Cu75–Si, Cu75–Sn, and Cu72–CrZr alloys.
summary: Nyquist plots for Cu75, Cu75–Si, Cu75–Sn, and Cu72–CrZr alloys are displayed to characterize their electrochemical impedance response. These plots provide essential data for fitting equivalent electrical circuit models, which help explain the corrosion behavior and charge transfer processes occurring at the electrode-electrolyte interface during the corrosion process.

caption: Representative load-displacement curve for an instrumented Charpy test, highlighting critical parameters including general yield load, maximum load, and loads at the onset and conclusion of unstable crack growth.
summary: The load-displacement curve displays key mechanical parameters derived from instrumented Charpy tests. Specifically, it identifies the general yield load (Fgy) for the elastic-plastic transition, the maximum load (Fm) for crack initiation, and the loads at the onset (Fiu) and conclusion (Fa) of unstable crack growth during the fracture process.

caption: Thermo-magnetisation behavior of the HTH sample processed at 250 J/mm3, measured under an applied magnetic field of 0.01 T.
summary: This thermo-magnetisation curve illustrates the magnetic response of the HTH sample, fabricated with an energy density of 250 J/mm3, under a 0.01 T field. The inset provides experimental confirmation of the Curie temperature (Tc), characterizing the magnetic phase transition behavior of the material as it responds to temperature changes.

caption: Nyquist plot for forged IN625 alloy, featuring a high-frequency capacitive loop and a low-frequency line, reflecting the lowest corrosion resistance among the tested specimens.
summary: The Nyquist plot for the forged IN625 alloy exhibits a high-frequency capacitive loop and a low-frequency line after 48 hours of corrosion in molten salts at 600 °C. This electrochemical response is associated with the poorest corrosion resistance observed among all the tested IN625 alloy conditions.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profile of the Laves phase, demonstrating elevated concentrations of niobium, molybdenum, and silicon relative to the surrounding interdendritic regions.
summary: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy of the Laves phase demonstrates significantly elevated concentrations of niobium, molybdenum, and silicon. These chemical signatures allow the Laves phase to be clearly distinguished from the surrounding interdendritic zone, confirming the specific elemental enrichment characteristic of this phase within the material's microstructure.

caption: Wave absorption profile of the pure Ti powder, indicating the material's interaction with electromagnetic radiation.
summary: This plot illustrates the wave absorption characteristics of the pure Ti powder. By measuring how the powder interacts with incident waves, the data provides insight into the energy absorption efficiency of the material, a critical parameter for optimizing the laser-powder interaction during the selective laser melting manufacturing process.

caption: Comparison of curing degrees for pentagonal microstructures fabricated via single-step and double-step laser scanning processes across varying laser power levels.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between laser power and the degree of curing for pentagonal microstructures. It compares single-step and double-step laser scanning methods, highlighting how different power levels influence the structural curing outcomes. The data provides a clear assessment of process efficiency for these specific micro-scale manufacturing techniques.

caption: Thermal cycle monitoring after the fourth layer scan (60.015–60.09 s), showing that both X2 and X7 specimens maintain a single peak temperature that remains higher than the martensite transformation temperature (TM).
summary: Following the fourth layer scan (60.015–60.09 s), the thermal cycles for both X2 and X7 specimens converge to a single peak. This peak temperature is maintained above the TM threshold, confirming that the material remains in a specific thermal regime after the completion of the fourth layer processing.

caption: High-power (60 mW) photoluminescence spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample at 77 K, displaying Voigt-profile fits for emission features including higher-energy peaks E3 and E4.
summary: This high-power 60 mW photoluminescence spectrum at 77 K reveals additional emission peaks, labeled E3 and E4. These peaks exhibit energy separations of 100 meV and 92 meV from the primary E0 and E1 peaks, respectively, providing further insight into the electronic structure of the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample.

caption: Arrott plot of the LPBF block sample annealed for one week, focused on the Curie temperature region.
summary: Representing the magnetic response of the one-week annealed LPBF sample near the Curie temperature, this Arrott plot facilitates the determination of the magnetic transition nature. The plot serves as a diagnostic tool to characterize the magnetic state and phase transition behavior of the material under these specific conditions.

caption: Rel-rod dark-field TEM image of faulted dislocation loops in 21Cr32Ni model alloy, highlighted for comparison with BOR-60 neutron-irradiated samples, in a 100 nm thick foil.
summary: This rel-rod dark-field TEM image shows faulted dislocation loops in the 21Cr32Ni model alloy after dual-ion irradiation to 16.6 dpa, with a foil thickness of 100 nm. These loops are highlighted for comparison with those formed by BOR-60 neutron irradiation to 17.1 dpa, demonstrating the impact of irradiation conditions on microstructure.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of NiV7 alloy at 96.6% thickness reduction, illustrating the final state of grain refinement and orientation distribution.
summary: Displaying the NiV7 alloy after 96.6% cold rolling, this IPF map provides insight into the extreme deformation state. The image reflects the cumulative effect of extensive plastic deformation, where neighboring grains with lower Schmid factors impose constraints, necessitating grain rotation and dislocation generation to accommodate orientation differences.

caption: EDS analysis of the NMI observed in panel b, confirming an irregular shape and alumina-based stoichiometry.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) results for the non-metallic inclusion identified in panel b are presented. The analysis reveals that the inclusion possesses an irregular morphology and an alumina-based chemical composition. This confirms the nature of the defect responsible for the failure observed in the FP02 specimen.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the weld metal (WM) region in the SLM + EBW (S-RAFMs) joint, displaying grain orientation and columnar crystal formation.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the weld metal of the S-RAFMs joint reveals grain morphology and distribution. Similar to the R-RAFMs joint, a preferred orientation in the (001) and (111) directions is observed, alongside the formation of coarse columnar crystals characteristic of this electron-beam-welded region.

caption: Box-plot distribution of B-PGNN model predictions for the K=1 fold, utilizing a functional prior trained via HMC.
summary: This box-plot illustrates the quantitative assessment of B-PGNN model predictions for the first fold (K=1). The model incorporates a functional prior and is trained using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) methods. This visualization provides a statistical summary of the prediction performance, serving as a key metric for evaluating the model's accuracy.

caption: Hf L3-edge XANES spectra for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys and hydrides with x=0 and x=0.10, compared with pure Hf metal.
summary: Hf L3-edge XANES spectra are presented for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys and their dihydride phases at x=0 and x=0.10. These spectra characterize the Hf local environment within the complex alloy system, with pure Hf metal included to facilitate comparison of the absorption edge features.

caption: Phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction in the unstrained (0% strain) reference state.
summary: Represented here is the phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction under zero strain conditions. The band gaps are highlighted in red, providing a baseline for comparing how structural deformation influences the wave propagation characteristics and the resulting frequency gaps within the material's elastic wave spectrum.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the as-built and HIP-processed SUS316L-10Cu alloy specimens.
summary: The X-ray diffraction patterns for the SUS316L-10Cu alloy are presented for both as-built and HIP-treated conditions. Analysis of these diffraction results confirms that an austenite phase is consistently observed across all samples, indicating that the phase composition remains stable despite the application of the hot isostatic pressing process.

caption: Height distribution map of the wear track on the AP_NC component surface.
summary: This height distribution map shows the topography of the wear track on the AP_NC component. The data illustrates a significant reduction in wear depth compared to the untreated component, confirming that the LTNC treatment effectively improves the wear resistance and surface durability of the material under reciprocating sliding conditions.

caption: Superimposed high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns collected across the welded joint, illustrating the spatial evolution of phases.
summary: This panel displays a superimposition of diffraction patterns across the welded joint, revealing minor microstructural variations between the base metal and heat-affected zone, while highlighting significant changes within the fusion zone. The data provides a comprehensive overview of phase distribution and structural evolution across the entire welded region.

caption: Cross-sectional FE-SEM morphology of the RHEAN3 coating.
summary: The cross-sectional FE-SEM morphology of the RHEAN3 coating is displayed. This image provides a detailed view of the coating's structural characteristics as part of the comparative analysis of five distinct RHEAN coatings, illustrating the specific microstructural features present in the RHEAN3 sample under high-resolution field emission scanning electron microscopy.

caption: High-speed imaging frames capturing the droplet transfer mode during a single-bead deposition process.
summary: High-speed imaging was utilized during a single-bead deposition to develop a comprehensive understanding of the characteristics of the μ-GMA transfer mode. This panel displays specific frames from the high-speed recording of the deposition process, providing visual evidence of the droplet transfer mode as it occurs during the metal deposition.

caption: Fatigue test specimen geometry designed according to ASTM standard E466-21 for vertical and horizontal orientations.
summary: Depicted is the fatigue test specimen geometry, designed and tested following the ASTM standard E466-21. The specimen configuration is intended for both vertical and horizontal orientations, providing a standardized approach for assessing the fatigue performance of the material as outlined in the study's experimental design protocols.

caption: Cross-sectional optical micrograph of a weld joint with AA1050 positioned on top, processed at an oscillation width of 1.5 mm.
summary: Displayed here is the weld cross-section for the AA1050-on-top configuration at 1.5 mm oscillation width, with the fusion boundary highlighted by a white dashed line. Compared to the AlSi10Mg-on-top configuration, this setup exhibits a lower quantity and smaller scale of pores within the fusion zone.

caption: Confusion matrix evaluating the classification accuracy, achieving a sensitivity of 92.05% and a specificity of 93.51% on the test dataset.
summary: Classification accuracy is detailed in this confusion matrix, which summarizes the model's performance on test data. The results show a sensitivity of 92.05% and a specificity of 93.51%, highlighting the model's high reliability in correctly identifying glaucoma patients while minimizing false positives among healthy individuals.

caption: Experimental pole figure derived from the XY-plane microstructure, confirming a strong <100> texture.
summary: The experimental pole figure, generated based on the XY-plane microstructure, confirms a strong <100> texture. This observation is consistent with the simulated pole figure, indicating that both the simulation and the experiment exhibit similar crystallographic texture characteristics in the NiTi sample.

caption: Modified particle displacement map for TD_8 powder calculated via Lagrangian approximation, showing irregular flow at the v3 region.
summary: Modified particle displacement for the TD_8 powder pile is calculated via Lagrangian approximation. Irregular particle flow is observed at the v3 region. This result suggests that the particle supply with intermediate velocity in the TD_8 powder is facilitated by free-falling in the front of the blade region.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of the MAX-2_1 sample, indicating the characteristic sp2 carbon signal.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum for the MAX-2_1 sample demonstrates the presence of sp2 hybridized carbon. Consistent with the other studied compounds, this sample exhibits carbon bonding characteristics typical of the series, contributing to the overall assessment of carbon content and structural integrity within the MAX phase materials.

caption: In situ FTIR spectra of Ru 1% CoB catalyst during CO2 hydrogenation at 100°C, monitored over varying reaction durations in a continuous CO2/H2 flow.
summary: This panel displays in situ FTIR spectra for the Ru 1% CoB catalyst during CO2 hydrogenation at 100°C. The data tracks the evolution of surface species over different reaction periods in a continuous CO2/H2 flow, providing insight into the catalytic activity and surface intermediates formed during the hydrogenation process.

caption: Experimental attractor reconstructed from tensile test data at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, projected onto the first three principal directions.
summary: This panel displays the experimental attractor for a tensile test on a flat specimen at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1. The attractor is reconstructed by projecting the trajectory matrix onto the first three principal directions, which effectively capture the dominant dynamical modes of the Portevin-Le Chatelier effect.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of a glassy carbon electrode in a Co/L-Ser electrolyte at a scan rate of 10 mV s-1.
summary: The electrochemical response of a glassy carbon electrode in a Co/L-Ser electrolyte is shown here. Performed at room temperature with a graphite rod counter electrode and Ag wire pseudo-reference, the data was collected at a scan rate of 10 mV s-1 to characterize the redox activity in this specific electrolyte.

caption: Sobol’ sensitivity indices illustrating the influence of various alloying elements on the Laves phase fraction in AB alloy 718, highlighting Ni concentration as the primary driver of microstructural variability.
summary: This panel displays Sobol’ sensitivity indices for the Laves phase in AB alloy 718. Global sensitivity analysis results indicate that the majority of the observed variability in the Laves phase fraction within the microstructure is primarily attributed to fluctuations in the Ni percentage, as shown in the sensitivity plot.

caption: Side view of the elemental distributions within the as-deposited MP35N thin film obtained via atom probe tomography.
summary: Atom probe tomography analysis of the as-deposited MP35N thin film reveals the three-dimensional elemental distribution. The side-view reconstruction demonstrates that the constituting elements are distributed uniformly throughout the analyzed volume, with no noticeable inhomogeneity observed in the as-deposited state of the thin film material.

caption: Secondary orientation view illustrating the spatial registration between the scanned mesh and the nominal CAD geometry.
summary: Representing the second stage of the 3D scan alignment process, this view provides a different perspective of the scanned ADAM electrode mesh relative to the nominal CAD file. The alignment highlights the spatial relationship between the physical scan data and the theoretical design model for subsequent deviation analysis.

caption: Mean Raman spectra of 3D-printed specimens highlighting bands at 1580 cm-1 and 1610 cm-1, with blue crosses indicating peaks identified by PCA as significantly different for discriminating graphene nanoplatelet concentrations.
summary: Mean Raman spectra are presented for 3D-printed specimens, focusing on the 1580 cm-1 and 1610 cm-1 bands. Principal component analysis was utilized to identify these specific peaks as statistically significant for discriminating between different graphene nanoplatelet concentrations, with the discriminating peaks marked by blue crosses for clear visualization.

caption: List of descriptor symbols used in the study.
summary: This panel presents the corresponding codes or symbols for the 14 descriptors utilized throughout the study. It serves as a reference key to identify the specific descriptors analyzed in the subsequent correlation matrix and histogram plots, ensuring clarity in the interpretation of the feature relationships.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility curves for as-cast R2Ni2.6Si0.4 (R = Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er) alloys measured at 0.05 T, comparing field-cooled (FC) and zero-field-cooled (ZFC) protocols, with an inset displaying Curie temperatures plotted against the de Gennes factor for each rare-earth element.
summary: Magnetic susceptibility measurements for R2Ni2.6Si0.4 systems reveal distinct M(T) behaviors under ZFC and FC conditions. The observed Curie temperatures demonstrate a clear correlation with the de Gennes factors of the trivalent rare-earth elements, confirming that the magnetic transition trends are consistent with the theoretical expectations for these specific rare-earth series.

caption: Architecture of the proposed deep learning pipeline, illustrating the integration of an autoencoder for latent embedding generation and a ResNet34 convolutional neural network for image analysis.
summary: This schematic illustrates the proposed deep learning pipeline designed for high-speed melt pool image analysis. The architecture integrates an autoencoder, which converts raw images into latent embeddings, with a ResNet34 model. This combination was identified through a parametric study as the optimal configuration for processing and interpreting melt pool data.

caption: Evolution of the first-order storage modulus (E1') and loss modulus (E1'') for UV-cured resin as a function of additional UV exposure time.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of UV-cured resin by tracking the first-order storage and loss moduli across varying additional UV exposure durations. The data demonstrates how the viscoelastic properties of the material evolve as the curing process progresses, providing insight into the material's stiffness and energy dissipation characteristics under oscillatory loading.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots representing the semiconductive behavior of passive layers on Ni-Cr-based alloys subjected to varying scan strategies in a borate buffer solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky analysis of Ni-Cr-based alloy passive layers reveals the semiconductive nature of the surface films under different scan strategies. The data, obtained in a borate buffer solution, indicates that specimens with higher dislocation densities exhibit lower defect densities, providing critical insights into the electrochemical stability of the passive layer.

caption: EDX spectrum of the machined surface corresponding to experiment No. 3, showing higher weight contents of O, Cu, and Zn compared to the optimal process parameters.
summary: This EDX spectrum represents the machined surface from experiment No. 3. Analysis reveals higher weight concentrations of oxygen, copper, and zinc compared to the optimal process parameters. These compositional differences are attributed to a worse discharge status during the machining process, which influences the surface element distribution.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of the sample surface treated with ultrasonic cavitation combined with 6.5 μm micro-abrasive particles.
summary: Confocal microscopy displays the surface of the sample after ultrasonic cavitation combined with 6.5 μm micro-abrasive particle modification. The image allows for the assessment of surface features resulting from the smallest abrasive particle size used, showing the combined effect of cavitation and fine-scale abrasive action on the material surface.

caption: Atomic force microscopy height micrograph (10x10 μm) displaying the surface texture of the adhesion-activated finish (A2) aramid fiber.
summary: Atomic force microscopy height micrograph (10x10 μm) displaying the surface texture of the adhesion-activated finish (A2) aramid fiber. The image captures the wavy surface morphology characteristic of the material. Arrows point to surface artefacts or processing aids, offering a clear visualization of the topographical features present on the A2 fiber.

caption: Algorithmic representation of the elasto-viscoplastic partitioned solver procedure.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the computational framework for the elasto-viscoplastic partitioned solver. The diagram outlines the systematic solver procedure, which integrates a sub-stepping algorithm to manage complex material responses. This structured approach ensures numerical stability and accuracy in simulating time-dependent deformation processes within the context of the described elasto-viscoplastic model.

caption: Sensitivity indices for the η phase in AB alloy 718, showing extreme sensitivity to Ti concentration with approximately 74-75% of phase fraction variation linked to Ti content.
summary: The η phase sensitivity analysis demonstrates an extreme dependence on Ti concentration. Approximately 73.98% and 75.11% of the variation in the η phase fraction is expected due to independent and combined variations of Ti percentage, respectively, confirming Ti as the dominant factor controlling the η phase in this alloy.

caption: Representative fluorescence microscopy images of L929 cells stained for live (green) and dead (red) cells after 24 hours, showing no observable differences between experimental groups and the unconditioned medium control.
summary: Live/Dead staining was utilized to visualize cell viability following exposure to the conditioned medium. The fluorescence microscopy images confirm that there are no observable differences in cell survival between L929 cells incubated with the composite-conditioned medium and those in unconditioned medium, supporting the lack of observed cytotoxicity.

caption: Logarithmic plot of relative yield strength versus relative density for DCC lattices compared against BCC, FCC, and Octet literature benchmarks.
summary: Relative yield strength is plotted against relative density on a logarithmic scale for DCC lattices. The data demonstrates that the DCC lattice aligns with bending-dominated predictions when evaluated alongside established BCC, FCC, and Octet lattice results, confirming its mechanical performance characteristics relative to these common structural benchmarks.

caption: Selected area diffraction patterns (SADPs) illustrating the crystallographic relationship between the [011] austenite and [011] κ carbide phases.
summary: The selected area diffraction patterns demonstrate the specific crystallographic orientation relationship between the [011] austenite matrix and the [011] κ carbide phase. These patterns confirm the presence of κ carbide within the microstructure, establishing the structural alignment between the matrix and the secondary phase particles.

caption: Bode impedance plot showing the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude of coatings, where corrosion resistance initially increases and subsequently decreases as oscillation frequency rises.
summary: This Bode impedance plot illustrates the relationship between impedance magnitude and frequency for coatings in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The data demonstrates that the coating's corrosion resistance is frequency-dependent, showing a characteristic trend where resistance increases initially before decreasing as the oscillation frequency continues to rise during the electrochemical analysis.

caption: Reconstructed M(T) loops derived from TFORC distributions using standard derivative formulas for both original and extended data sets, compared against the original experimental loop.
summary: Panel (a) displays reconstructed M(T) loops derived from TFORC distributions compared to the original experimental loop. The non-extended standard TFORC distribution accurately reproduces the hysteretic behavior, showing deviations only where the reversible Curie transition of the austenitic phase significantly influences the magnetic response of the material.

caption: Atomic model of the HighIndex-2 supercell showing the Al/Al3Ni interface characterized by the orientation relationship (001) Al // (102) Al3Ni and [210] Al // [010] Al3Ni.
summary: The HighIndex-2 supercell model illustrates the Al/Al3Ni interface structure. It is defined by the orientation relationship (001) Al // (102) Al3Ni and [210] Al // [010] Al3Ni. This configuration is part of a set of three high-index interfaces constructed to investigate the structural properties observed in earlier directional solidification experiments.

caption: Weight measurements of green samples across different printing parameters.
summary: Weight measurements for green samples are shown to evaluate printing consistency. Analysis of the data reveals that density differences between the various samples are primarily driven by variations in weight rather than differences in volume, highlighting the significant impact of mass distribution on the final green density results.

caption: Atom map of the base alloy aged for 0.5 h, illustrating the spatial distribution of solute atoms.
summary: This atom map displays the spatial distribution of solute atoms within the base alloy after 0.5 hours of aging. As part of the APT elemental mapping analysis, this visualization provides insight into the atomic arrangement of the base material, serving as a reference for comparing solute behavior in modified alloys.

caption: Load-depth indentation profiles for powder particles sized between 75 and 106 μm, obtained from six individual test measurements.
summary: Mechanical indentation profiles for powders in the 75–106 μm size range are shown through load-depth curves generated from six selected particles. These results provide a consistent representation of the indentation behavior for this intermediate size group, facilitating a comparative analysis of mechanical properties across the different powder size distributions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the aqueous phase containing 10 mM BRB at pH 11, showing the electrochemical response in the absence (red dashed line) and presence of BIL at concentrations ranging from 20 to 200 µM (black solid lines) at a scan rate of 20 mV/s.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry demonstrates the electrochemical behavior of BIL in a BRB solution at pH 11. The comparison between the blank solution and increasing concentrations of BIL reveals significant peak-to-peak separation exceeding 250 mV, which is notably larger than the theoretical value expected for diffusion-limited ion transfer processes.

caption: Charging and discharging power profiles for second-life battery packs at the 2400-th cycle, illustrating four distinct operational types.
summary: This figure displays the charging and discharging power profiles of second-life battery packs at the 2400-th cycle, categorized into four distinct types. Type 1 battery packs demonstrate the most significant fluctuations in energy levels throughout the operational cycle, highlighting the variability in performance among different battery pack configurations during long-term usage.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of platelets deposited at the base of large hemisphere microstructures, with the orange circle outlining the base.
summary: Platelets stained for P-selectin and CD41+ are observed accumulating at the base of large hemisphere microstructures. The orange circle highlights the base area, confirming that platelets predominantly deposit at the bottom of these large-sized structures, consistent with the observed behavior across other large-scale micropatterned surface geometries.

caption: Live and dead cell assay of MG-63 cells co-cultured with various scaffolds under NIR irradiation.
summary: This panel displays the results of live/dead cell staining for MG-63 cells co-cultured with different scaffolds under NIR irradiation. The assay provides a visual assessment of cell viability and mortality, serving as a primary indicator of the cytotoxic effects induced by the experimental scaffold treatments in the tumor cell model.

caption: Visual documentation of the cracked slab cast specimen 1, highlighting the failure condition observed after the bending test.
summary: This photograph displays the cracked slab cast specimen 1 following a bending test. The visible cracks extend parallel to the specimen length, indicating concrete shrinkage and subsequent slip between the rebar and concrete. This visual evidence illustrates the post-bending test failure condition and the resulting structural damage within the slab.

caption: Activation plot comparing PEG and PEG-Ag hybrids of varying molecular weights, highlighting distinct VFT and Arrhenius kinetic behaviors.
summary: This activation plot analyzes the glass transition kinetics for both the bulk matrix and the interfacial layer in PEG and PEG-Ag hybrids. The bulk matrix exhibits VFT behavior, while the interfacial layer displays Arrhenius behavior, indicating restricted segmental mobility within the hybrid material structure across different molecular weights.

caption: SHAP dependence plot showing the relationship between effective mean stress and stress amplitude, where dot colors represent stress amplitude values.
summary: Effective mean stress values in the range of 200-400 MPa exhibit a negative effect on fatigue life, as indicated by negative SHAP values. The plot demonstrates the interaction between effective mean stress and stress amplitude, revealing that the range of SHAP values for effective mean stress is smaller than for stress amplitude.

caption: High-magnification TEM morphology of Sn-rich precipitates dispersed within the α-Cu matrix, accompanied by an inset table detailing EDS point compositions at locations P1 through P3.
summary: High-magnification TEM imaging reveals the morphology of Sn-rich precipitates embedded within the α-Cu matrix. An inset table provides quantitative EDS point composition data for locations P1, P2, and P3, confirming the chemical nature of these precipitates as predicted by the equilibrium Cu-Sn phase diagram.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of the 3D-printed Navy Blue ink filter, showing a transmission peak near 450 nm and a distinct dip at approximately 625 nm.
summary: The Navy Blue filter's optical transmission spectrum is characterized by a transmission peak located near 450 nm. Additionally, the spectrum exhibits a notable dip in transmission at approximately 625 nm, illustrating the specific spectral response of this 3D-printed ink formulation within the visible light range.

caption: Magnetization curves (M-H loops) for Ni36Fe64 thin films with 54 nm thickness and 2 mm width on glass substrates.
summary: Magnetization curves illustrate the magnetic response of Ni36Fe64 thin films on glass. The specimen, characterized by a thickness of 54 nm and a width of 2 mm, exhibits magnetic behavior typical of these thin film dimensions. The plot provides essential data regarding the magnetic properties of the Ni36Fe64 material.

caption: APT reconstruction tip of the Ni56Ti36Hf8 alloy showing a 60 at.% Ni iso-composition surface, highlighting the spatial distribution of cubic Ni-rich phases in dark blue and Hf-rich phases in light red.
summary: The APT reconstruction tip visualizes the 3-phase microstructure of the Ni56Ti36Hf8 alloy using a 60 at.% Ni iso-composition surface. This 3D representation clearly distinguishes between the cubic Ni-rich precipitates and the Hf-rich phases. The chemical composition of these distinct phases is quantified alongside the bulk composition of the APT sample tip.

caption: Monitoring procedure for keyhole formation.
summary: Keyhole monitoring is represented through this schematic diagram, which outlines the procedure for observing keyhole dynamics during the process. This visual guide clarifies the experimental approach used to track keyhole behavior, facilitating a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms during the material processing or testing phase.

caption: Updated Ni-Zn phase diagram compared to the calculated model by Xiong et al. [10], highlighting refined phase boundaries for solid phases and invariant reactions, including the narrowed β1 phase region.
summary: This panel displays the Ni-Zn phase diagram updated against the model by Xiong et al. [10]. It highlights refined phase boundaries for solid phases and invariant reactions. Notably, it shows a more pronounced narrowing of the β1 phase boundary at temperatures below 550 °C, consistent with the authors' experimental findings.

caption: Principal component analysis of the 2s1 + 2s2 dataset for R = 0.1 aluminum alloy fatigue tests, showing feature contributions as blue lines and multiplet centroids as colored dots.
summary: Principal component analysis of the 2s1 + 2s2 dataset for R = 0.1 aluminum alloy fatigue tests displays feature contributions as blue lines and multiplet centroids as colored dots. The analysis demonstrates that PCA on these feature centroids fails to effectively separate type I from type II multiplets.

caption: Comparison of simulated and measured reflection coefficient curves for the 5 GHz antenna design.
summary: This plot displays the reflection coefficient as a function of frequency for the 5 GHz antenna design. It compares simulated data against actual experimental measurements. The results demonstrate good agreement between the theoretical simulation and the physical measurement, validating the performance characteristics of the antenna design at the target frequency.

caption: TKD-derived BC + IPF + GB diagram of the 3DHT-XY sample, revealing a lamellar microstructure where the main crack propagates along the lamellae.
summary: The TKD-derived BC, IPF, and GB diagram illustrates the lamellar microstructure of the 3DHT-XY sample. Analysis of this map indicates that the upper portion of the main crack grows and extends specifically along the lamellar structure, highlighting the influence of grain orientation and boundaries on crack propagation.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the 3D printed PEEK–HA–Mg2SiO4 composite, illustrating the retention of characteristic functional groups after thermal processing.
summary: FTIR analysis of the 3D printed PEEK–HA–Mg2SiO4 composite confirms the retention of characteristic functional groups from both the PEEK matrix and the ceramic fillers. This indicates that stable chemical interactions were maintained during the thermal processing of the composite material, ensuring the integrity of the chemical structure.

caption: Classification framework for diverse methodologies employed to determine the contact tip-to-workpiece distance (CTWD) during welding operations.
summary: This diagram presents a structured classification of various approaches used to measure the contact tip-to-workpiece distance (CTWD) during welding processes. By categorizing these investigations based on the specific measuring principles applied, the figure provides a systematic overview of the different technical strategies available for monitoring this critical welding parameter.

caption: Initial stage of the first-layer building process showing the temperature field distribution.
summary: This panel illustrates the initial phase of the first-layer building process during single track formation. The visualization depicts the temporal evolution of the temperature field within the simulated material, providing insight into the thermal conditions present at the start of the additive manufacturing process.

caption: STEM image of the medium γ′ microstructure after failure at 750 °C, where stacking faults are confined strictly to the γ′ precipitates and dislocation density is elevated in the γ channels.
summary: Deformation in the medium γ′ microstructure at 750 °C results in stacking faults confined to the precipitates, highlighting a shift in deformation behavior compared to the fine microstructure. Additionally, a higher dislocation density and dislocation accumulation are observed within the γ channels, indicating increased resistance to dislocation movement.

caption: Live/Dead and immunofluorescence imaging of cell-laden printed constructs, illustrating cell viability and structural integrity after one day and one week of culturing.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of cell-laden constructs confirms that the printing process does not detrimentally affect cell viability, as shown by Live/Dead staining at one day and one week. Furthermore, the printed structures maintain their shape in the presence of HDFs after one week of culturing, demonstrating high structural fidelity.

caption: Swelling ratios of the hydrogel coatings.
summary: Swelling ratio measurements quantify the water uptake capacity of the hydrogel coatings. This property is essential for evaluating the hydrogel's performance in aqueous environments, reflecting the cross-linking density and hydrophilic nature of the different coating formulations tested in the study.

caption: Initial region of the load vs end-shortening curve for EAS stub columns, highlighting early-stage deformation behavior normalized by A av.
summary: Focusing on the initial region of the mechanical response, this plot illustrates the early-stage load versus end-shortening behavior of EAS stub columns. The axial load is normalized by A av, and the data is extracted from virtual extensometer measurements on DIC data, providing a detailed view of the initial deformation.

caption: Optical micrograph of the HT2 heat-treated AISI 316L sample, highlighting the significant microstructural evolution.
summary: This image depicts the HT2 heat-treated AISI 316L sample. The microstructure is strongly influenced by the heat treatment, resulting in the complete disappearance of the original melting patterns and substructure boundaries. This indicates a substantial microstructural transformation driven by the specific thermal processing conditions applied to the material.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) of gene expression profiles across all bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell samples.
summary: Principal component analysis was performed on the gene expression profiles of all samples to facilitate a deeper transcriptome analysis. This statistical approach allows for the visualization of variance between the different experimental groups, providing a foundational overview of the transcriptomic differences observed in the bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells.

caption: Strain distribution map of a 60% infill scaffold sample at the point of fracture.
summary: Captured at the fracture point, this DIC strain map shows the deformation of a 60% infill scaffold. The visualization reveals the strain patterns leading to failure, offering insights into the mechanical performance and structural limitations of the scaffold under high-density printing conditions during compression.

caption: Tafel potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing uncoated Ti felt and Au/Ti felt samples with varying R values.
summary: Tafel potentiodynamic polarization curves demonstrate the corrosion behavior of uncoated Ti felt and Au-coated samples. The Au/Ti felt [R = 50] exhibits the lowest corrosion current density of 0.083 μA/cm2, which is significantly lower than the uncoated Ti felt (2.5 μA/cm2) and other Au-coated variants, indicating superior corrosion resistance.

caption: Cr segregation energies for cation-O molecular pairs, highlighting the dampening effect of the cation on Cr-anion interactions compared to the isolated O anion baseline.
summary: This panel illustrates the impact of cation-O molecular pairs on Cr segregation energies. Consistent with other anion types, the cation presence increases the segregation energy relative to the isolated O anion. This screening effect suggests that cation-anion pairs generally promote less surface segregation of Cr compared to isolated anion species.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the TiC-steel composite worn surface subjected to a 25 N load at room temperature, revealing oxygen presence.
summary: Elemental mapping of the TiC-steel composite worn surface at 25 N load demonstrates oxygen content between 9 and 12 wt%. This oxygen presence is attributed to friction-induced heating in the atmospheric environment. At this lower load, the lack of a sustained tribolayer may contribute to increased wear rates and fatigue.

caption: EDX line scans illustrating the Al and Ti diffusion profiles within the metal sublattice of annealed Ti0.34Al0.66N coatings, measured after 1, 5, 15, and 30 hours.
summary: This panel displays EDX line scans for annealed Ti0.34Al0.66N coatings, focusing on the relative distribution of Al and Ti elements. By tracking these profiles after 1, 5, 15, and 30 hours, the figure effectively highlights the diffusion characteristics of the metal sublattice at the coating surface over time.

caption: 3D worn surface topography of TiC-steel composite after sliding at 50 N load at room temperature (RT).
summary: Representing the wear scar morphology at 50 N load and room temperature, this 3D topography reveals relatively shallow and narrow abrasion marks. These features are consistent with the general observation that RT sliding results in less severe surface degradation compared to elevated temperature testing conditions.

caption: Microhardness profile across the welded joint for condition A1, displaying a characteristic M-shaped distribution with peak values in the heat-affected zone.
summary: Microhardness profile across the welded joint for condition A1, displaying a characteristic M-shaped distribution with peak values in the heat-affected zone. All joints exhibit this typical M-shaped microhardness distribution, characterized by the lowest values in the weld zone, highest in the heat-affected zone, and intermediate values in the base metal.

caption: EDS elemental map highlighting the distribution of Manganese (Mn) within the coarsened Al 6 Mn precipitates for the 325 °C/2 h aging condition.
summary: This EDS elemental map confirms the presence and concentration of Manganese within the coarsened Al 6 Mn precipitates observed in the 325 °C/2 h aging condition. The analysis validates the TEM findings, showing that the increased aging time leads to larger precipitates with a distinct Mn-rich chemical signature.

caption: Room temperature zoom of the damping factor curve highlighting the tanδ increment due to hybridization.
summary: This zoomed-in view of the damping factor curve at room temperature highlights the performance improvements achieved through hybridization. The Hybrid-B and Hybrid-S samples exhibited tanδ increments of 55.7% and 58.8%, respectively, compared to the neat laminate, demonstrating the enhanced damping capabilities resulting from the specific material hybridization strategy.

caption: Ashby diagram comparing ultimate tensile strength versus ductility for various metallic alloys fabricated via laser powder bed fusion, electron beam melting, and directed-energy deposition.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the mechanical performance landscape of common additive manufacturing alloys, including Al, Fe, Ni, Ti, and high-entropy systems. It highlights the trade-off between ultimate tensile strength and ductility across three primary manufacturing techniques, providing a comparative baseline for evaluating the mechanical properties of as-built metallic materials.

caption: Raman spectra of untreated and SF6 plasma-treated carbon samples, illustrating the structural changes induced by varying plasma treatment durations.
summary: The Raman spectra of untreated and SF6 plasma-treated carbon at different durations are shown in Fig. 2 (a). These spectra provide a comparative analysis of the carbon material's structural integrity and defect density before and after exposure to plasma treatment, highlighting the impact of processing time on the material's vibrational characteristics.

caption: iV OC calibrated photoluminescence imaging of a rear-metallised TOPCon precursor featuring conventional Al pastes with varying contact area fractions.
summary: This photoluminescence image displays the surface passivation quality of a TOPCon precursor metallized with conventional Al pastes. The imaging technique, calibrated for iV OC, reveals how different contact area fractions influence recombination behavior, demonstrating that conventional Al pastes lead to significantly higher contact recombination compared to specialized alternatives under identical firing conditions.

caption: Transformation temperatures (TTs) as a function of stress level for samples P1 and P4, demonstrating the influence of laser power on thermal stability.
summary: Transformation temperatures are displayed as a function of stress level for samples P1 and P4, which correspond to variations in laser power. A consistent trend is visualized for these TTs, with the anchor point highlighted in black, providing insight into the material's thermal behavior under different stress conditions.

caption: Fluorescent imaging of BMSC cytoskeleton stained with FITC-phalloidin and DAPI, highlighting morphological changes.
summary: Fluorescent imaging of the BMSC cytoskeleton using FITC-phalloidin and DAPI reveals distinct morphological variations. The length of filopodia increases as hydrogel stiffness decreases, while cells on the bottom plate exhibit a typical spreading pattern, illustrating how substrate mechanical properties directly influence the structural organization of the BMSC cytoskeleton.

caption: Shrinkage cavity morphology identified within the original Al-Ce-Mg alloy specimen using XRM reconstruction.
summary: Shrinkage cavities are clearly visualized in this XRM reconstruction of the original Al-Ce-Mg alloy specimen. These cavities, alongside gas pores, constitute the primary metallurgical defects in the material. This image documents the initial state of these shrinkage features before the specimen undergoes tensile deformation and subsequent structural evolution.

caption: Bar chart displaying the calculated electrical resistivity values for the four alloy samples.
summary: This bar chart displays the calculated electrical resistivity for the four alloy samples. These results align with experimental findings, validating the computational approach used in the study. The data highlights the variation in resistivity across the samples, providing essential insights into the electronic properties of the investigated materials.

caption: Strain at flexural strength for varying face-to-core ratios, with performance indicated as a percentage of the monolithic core material.
summary: Strain at flexural strength is evaluated for composites with face-to-core ratios ranging from 0 to 0.8. The radar plot compares these values to the monolithic core performance, represented by the gray area. These results are part of a consistent basis for material selection across various multi-material configurations.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe10 composite showing a minimum value of -4.8 dB.
summary: The Fe10 composite exhibits a reflection loss profile with a minimum value of -4.8 dB. This measurement quantifies the electromagnetic absorption characteristics of the material at a 10 wt% Fe loading level, serving as a baseline for evaluating the absorption enhancement observed with higher iron concentrations in the composite series.

caption: Pearson correlation coefficient heatmap illustrating the interdependencies between 21 selected material features.
summary: This heatmap displays the Pearson correlation coefficients for 21 features derived from a larger dataset of 53 initial variables. Following a Pearson coefficient screening process, these 22 remaining features were analyzed to visualize their statistical relationships, providing a clearer representation of feature interactions compared to the original, overly crowded confusion matrix.

caption: Distribution of SHAP values illustrating the impact of individual input features on the predicted height.
summary: The full distribution of SHAP values for each input feature is visualized here to show how specific parameters influence the height prediction. This plot provides a detailed view of the feature effects, confirming that scan speed specifically acts to decrease the predicted height value within the GPR model framework.

caption: Fracture strain plotted against average stress triaxiality for AM-H and AM-V copper specimens, showing the experimental data points used to calibrate the fracture model parameters D1 through D3.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between fracture strain and average stress triaxiality for AM-H and AM-V copper specimens. Experimental data from three to five specimens per material were utilized to calibrate the D1-D3 parameters of the exponential fracture model, providing a quantitative basis for characterizing the material's fracture behavior.

caption: {001} pole figure for the AF sample, quantifying the crystallographic texture intensity.
summary: The {001} pole figure for the AF sample demonstrates the crystallographic texture intensity. Analysis confirms the presence of a <100> texture, which is consistent across all examined specimens. This pole figure serves to quantify the preferred orientation of the grains within the as-fabricated material structure.

caption: Energy–momentum dispersion of pristine SnSbBiTe4 along the Γ-M direction of the first surface Brillouin zone, measured via ARPES at 17 eV photon energy.
summary: ARPES data acquired at 17 eV photon energy reveals the energy-momentum dispersion of pristine SnSbBiTe4 along the Γ-M direction of the first surface Brillouin zone. This measurement provides a baseline for the electronic band structure of the material before any surface modification or doping processes are applied.

caption: Elongation to failure plotted against hydrogen pressure for conventional specimens (CS) and hollow specimens (HS), modeled using an exponential growth function.
summary: This plot illustrates the elongation to failure as a function of hydrogen pressure for both conventional and hollow specimens. The data is fitted with an exponential growth function incorporating a time constant. Notably, the hollow specimens tested in air exhibit lower elongation to failure compared to the conventional specimens.

caption: Geometric representation of the honeycomb unit cell structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental geometric parameters of the honeycomb unit cell. The cut-and-patch method is utilized to determine the volumes of the inner and outer units within this specific lattice configuration, providing a basis for structural analysis of the honeycomb cell architecture.

caption: Normalized HE-XRD intensity profiles plotted against 2-theta angles for five distinct specimens, highlighting variations in peak intensities for gamma-prime precipitates and MC-carbides.
summary: This HE-XRD plot displays normalized diffraction intensities across 2-theta angles for five specimens. The data reveals that intensity peaks for gamma-prime precipitates and MC-carbides are lowest for the HS specimen, followed by LP and HP. These results confirm the presence of gamma-prime precipitates and indicate an increase in their volume fraction.

caption: Cell voltage evolution during the first charge/discharge cycle for Setting B, featuring a main plot of potential versus time, a top inset detailing charge phase fluctuations influenced by electrolyte fluid dynamics, and a bottom inset illustrating the impact of room temperature variations on cell performance under different stirrer conditions.
summary: This figure displays the cell voltage profile during the initial charge/discharge cycle for Setting B. It highlights how electrolyte fluid dynamics and ambient temperature fluctuations induce variations in the potential. The insets provide a granular view of these effects during the charge phase, comparing performance with tank stirrers ON and OFF.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of a typical region in the STFN5 oxide after the exsolution process.
summary: This high-resolution TEM image displays a typical region of the STFN5 oxide following the exsolution process. The image serves as a comparative structural analysis of the STFN5 material, illustrating the morphology of the oxide lattice after the reduction-induced formation of nanoparticles on the surface.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve for as-fabricated NiTi sample S1, displaying the austenitic finish temperature.
summary: Sample S1 exhibits an austenitic finish temperature below room temperature as determined by DSC analysis. The curve indicates the thermal response of the as-fabricated NiTi part, confirming that the material remains in a specific phase state at room temperature following the fabrication process.

caption: Spatial distribution of 103 microstructural images under various creep conditions plotted in the two-dimensional space defined by the first two principal components, PC1 and PC2.
summary: The scatter plot displays the distribution of 103 microstructural images within the PC1-PC2 space. These two principal components represent the majority of microstructural features derived from two-point statistics, serving as effective supplementary features to characterize and differentiate the microstructures observed under different creep conditions in this study.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOZ cross-sections for scanning strategies S1-S5.
summary: This plot depicts the major axis length distribution of martensite on XOZ cross-sections. The data confirms that intermittent melt pool interference modes (S3-S5) promote larger average primary and secondary martensite sizes compared to continuous modes (S1, S2), as higher cooling rates facilitate growth along the main axis of the martensite.

caption: Nitrided surface layer of alloy 718 showing microstructural features.
summary: This panel displays the nitride layer formed on the surface of nickel-based alloy 718 after the nitriding process. The TEM imaging captures the structural characteristics of this modified surface region, providing a baseline for comparing the microstructural evolution as a function of depth within the alloy.

caption: Model-predicted grain structure in the central x-z cross-section for the H-RBP mode, featuring columnar grains growing upwards from the melt pool boundary.
summary: The H-RBP mode simulation shows columnar grains growing upwards from the planar melt pool root region, parallel to the z-direction. These grains exhibit a misorientation angle of less than 20° between the sample and crystal coordinate systems, resulting in a distinct crystallographic orientation compared to the H-GBP mode.

caption: Comparison of experimental and simulated Bragg-edge profiles, with the grey scale indicating normalized neutron beam intensity versus wavelength.
summary: Experimental and simulated Bragg-edge profiles are compared to characterize the material's diffraction behavior. The grey scale represents normalized neutron beam intensity as a function of wavelength at the POLDI guide exit, where black and white indicate the absence and maximum intensity of neutrons, respectively, validating the experimental diffraction data.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the 0.77Cu-NA alloy specimen.
summary: This selected area electron diffraction pattern characterizes the 0.77Cu-NA alloy. It serves as a baseline for analyzing diffuse spot positions, which are compared against the NA-AA condition to identify structural variations related to atomic clusters and their associated weak reflections within the material's microstructure.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map and point-to-point misorientation profile along a characteristic line in the BD sample.
summary: This panel displays the crystallographic orientation via an IPF map alongside a point-to-point misorientation profile. These EBSD-derived results identify specific twin types within the AZ91 layer, providing a detailed look at the local lattice rotation and structural changes occurring along the characteristic line during tensile deformation.

caption: Relational database schema illustrating the structural organization of data, including the Reports table which captures issuer details, issuance dates, order status, and supplementary report comments.
summary: This relational database schema provides a structured overview of the system's data organization. It specifically highlights the Reports table, which serves as a central repository for tracking critical information such as the issuer, issuance date, order status, and additional qualitative comments associated with each report.

caption: Representative neutron diffraction pattern and corresponding fitting, with the grayscale background indicating normalized neutron beam intensity versus wavelength at the guide exit.
summary: The panel displays a representative neutron diffraction pattern alongside its fitting results. The background grayscale intensity map visualizes the neutron beam profile as a function of wavelength, where black and white regions denote maximum and zero intensity, respectively, providing context for the diffraction data quality and the beam characteristics at POLDI.

caption: Overall parity plot comparing predicted and actual stress values for the test dataset, which constitutes 20% of the total experimental data.
summary: This parity plot summarizes the MLP model's predictive performance on the unseen test dataset, representing 20% of the total data. It serves as a critical validation step, demonstrating the model's ability to accurately predict stress values for conditions not included in the training phase, thereby confirming its overall robustness.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of rBMSCs on porous alloy scaffolds after 3 days of coculture, showing effective cell spreading and proliferation.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of rBMSCs on porous alloy scaffolds after 3 days of coculture reveals that the cells effectively spread and proliferated across all four scaffold types. The staining confirms high cell viability and successful initial colonization of the porous structures, as evidenced by the widespread distribution of cells.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of as-printed Ni-free stainless steel.
summary: This KAM map illustrates the local misorientation in the as-printed Ni-free stainless steel. When compared to the heat-treated sample in panel (i), this map helps demonstrate the reduction in geometrically necessary dislocation density that occurs following the heat treatment process in the Ni-free stainless steel specimens.

caption: FTIR spectrum of GAn exhibiting characteristic anhydride peaks at 1804 cm-1 and 1748 cm-1.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of GAn displays distinct peaks at 1804 cm-1 and 1748 cm-1, which correspond to the symmetric and asymmetric stretching vibrations of the C=O bond in the cyclic anhydride. These characteristic peaks serve as markers for the anhydride functionality before it undergoes ring-opening and subsequent esterification.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the temperature dependence of the extended cluster size parameter Q_CE, calculated with a scaling factor of β = 5.31.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the temperature-dependent behavior of the extended cluster size parameter, denoted as Q_CE, using a fixed parameter of β = 5.31. The data demonstrates that these specific values can be effectively described through an Arrhenius relationship, providing insight into the thermal evolution of the cluster size.

caption: Microhardness trend observed with increasing B2O3 content from 25% to 100%, demonstrating a consistent reduction in material hardness.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between B2O3 content and microhardness. Unlike the TiO2-reinforced samples, the data shows a steady and continuous reduction in hardness as the B2O3 proportion increases, extending through to the mono-reinforced B2O3 composition, indicating a softening effect with higher B2O3 concentrations.

caption: Measured lattice strains of {111}, {200}, and {220} planes obtained via in situ neutron diffraction as reported in Ref. [29].
summary: Experimental lattice strains for {111}, {200}, and {220} planes are shown, as re-plotted from Ref. [29]. These measurements serve as the baseline for evaluating model accuracy. Observations indicate that while most strains are well-predicted, the transverse lattice strains of the {200} plane deviate during the elastic-plastic transition area.

caption: Radiographic testing (RT) images revealing internal defects within weave parts (W9, W12, W18) fabricated above the critical heat input threshold for each respective weaving width.
summary: Radiographic testing images visualize internal defects in weave parts labeled W9, W12, and W18. These parts were fabricated using parameters exceeding the critical heat input required for each specific weaving width. The RT analysis confirms the presence of internal structural defects in these samples following the deposition process.

caption: IRRAS spectrum of the pHPMAA (bottom)/pCBMAA (top) di-block copolymer brush sample F.
summary: Sample F, consisting of a pHPMAA bottom layer and a pCBMAA top layer, is characterized by IRRAS. The spectrum displays the characteristic bands associated with both pCBMAA and pHPMAA, confirming the successful synthesis and composition of the di-block copolymer brushes prepared within the microfluidic stack reactors.

caption: Hardness profile measured 10 μm from the surface of borided samples treated at 800 °C for 1, 2, and 4 hours.
summary: Hardness profiles for samples borided at 800 °C are displayed. Samples treated for 1 and 2 hours show a missing region I, while the 4-hour treatment exhibits a hardness of 1200 HV 0.01, indicating the formation of Ni3B and Ni2B borides. No hardness reduction was observed at 25 μm.

caption: Correlation between Brinell hardness and mechanical properties, specifically yield strength (filled symbols) and compressive stress at 10% strain (open symbols), for samples prepared via gravity casting (red), centrifugal casting (violet), and laser-based powder bed fusion (blue).
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the empirical and physical correlation between Brinell hardness and mechanical strength metrics for various processing methods. Yield strength and compressive stress at 10% strain are plotted against hardness for gravity casting, centrifugal casting, and PBF-LB/M samples, with a dashed line provided as a visual guide.

caption: In-situ reaction and isothermal solidification process within the brazing zone.
summary: This panel depicts the third stage of the joining process, characterized by in-situ chemical reactions and isothermal solidification. These mechanisms are critical for transforming the infiltrated liquid phases into a stable, solid joint structure, ensuring metallurgical continuity between the Cf/C composite and the GH3044 superalloy substrate.

caption: Strain-temperature response of 15 ms NiTi wire subjected to a thermal cycle under a constant 300 MPa stress.
summary: This panel illustrates the strain-temperature response of a 15 ms NiTi wire during a thermal cycle while under a constant 300 MPa stress. The plot characterizes the material's thermomechanical behavior, specifically highlighting the strain variations associated with temperature changes under significant external loading conditions during the transformation process.

caption: Top-view image processing sequence, showing the conversion of raw filament data into grayscale and subsequent binarization using a predetermined threshold.
summary: Top-view images captured by Camera 1 are processed through a specific sequence to facilitate neck width measurement. The raw image is first converted to a grayscale format and then subjected to binarization using a predetermined threshold, enabling the clear identification of filament boundaries for accurate geometric analysis.

caption: Rhombus-based base structures for Bi:(N0, N2)-RNLs.
summary: Rhombus-based nested base structures for the Bi:(N0, N2)-RNLs are depicted. These base structures serve as the foundation for the bimodal lattice, incorporating fractal rhombus struts to establish the geometric framework necessary for creating advanced lattice architectures that exhibit improved directional consistency compared to conventional truss-based designs.

caption: Retardance map for the LCoS-SLM at a gray level (GL) of 100, with a maximum retardance of 719° and a minimum of 659°.
summary: At a gray level of 100, the LCoS-SLM retardance map displays a maximum of 719° and a minimum of 659°. These spatial inhomogeneities are common in such devices and are influenced by manufacturing imperfections, boundary conditions, and residual stress within the liquid crystal layer, contributing to the observed range of spatial variation.

caption: Evolution of the orientation field η8 for grain 8, characterized by an inclination angle of 52.5°, during solidification.
summary: The orientation field η8 for grain 8 is plotted to show its development during solidification. The curves for the final time steps indicate that grain 8 stops growing at t = 0.25ms, demonstrating the cessation of boundary movement at the specific sites marked in the simulation.

caption: Longitudinal cross-section of a fractured (HEA+Ni)-S600 tensile specimen exhibiting limited necking and microcracks at prior particle boundaries.
summary: Optical imaging of the (HEA+Ni)-S600 specimen reveals microcracks frequently occurring at the prior particle boundaries of the HEA particles. The macroscopic view of the fractured specimen half shows limited necking, which correlates with the material's mechanical performance and fracture characteristics observed during the tensile testing process.

caption: Conceptual representation of the initial parallelization stage implemented across two computational nodes.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental architecture of the first level of parallelization, specifically demonstrating how computational tasks are distributed across two distinct nodes. The diagram provides a clear visual overview of the parallel processing framework, highlighting the structural organization required to achieve efficient load balancing in a multi-node environment.

caption: Multimodal sensor array integrated into the DED system, highlighting the specific acoustic emission, accelerometer, and thermal sensors used for porosity prediction.
summary: This panel illustrates the array of multimodal sensors integrated into the hybrid machine. Specifically, an accelerometer, an acoustic emission sensor, and a thermal sensor are highlighted in yellow. These instruments are utilized to monitor and explain the occurrence of porosity in localized surface elements during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Polarization-electric field hysteresis loop for an STO thin film under an applied electric field of 6.4 MV/cm.
summary: Depicted here is the polarization-electric field hysteresis loop for an STO thin film under a 6.4 MV/cm electric field. The data shows that the STO material exhibits low remanent polarization, which is a key characteristic used to evaluate the energy storage performance of the nanocomposite system.

caption: Geometry of the polished and slotted in-situ Inconel 718 workpiece sample, featuring variably spaced slots designed to suppress harmonic vibrations during cutting.
summary: This panel illustrates the geometry of an in-situ Inconel 718 workpiece sample. The design incorporates variably spaced slots, which are specifically engineered to suppress harmonic vibrations that typically occur during cutting processes with constant step widths, thereby ensuring stability during the machining of the turbine-grade material.

caption: Feature importance analysis for the XGBoost model, illustrating the relative contribution of various input variables to the model's predictive decision-making process.
summary: This feature importance analysis provides a quantitative evaluation of the XGBoost model's decision-making process. By identifying the relative influence of different input variables, the plot clarifies which features are most critical for the model's predictions, offering essential insights into the underlying logic and performance drivers of the machine learning framework.

caption: Detailed current-voltage waveform for the 6 m/min wire feed rate condition, highlighting transient electrical behavior.
summary: Presented is the detailed current-voltage waveform for the 6 m/min wire feed rate condition. The plot demonstrates the specific electrical response during deposition, which is marked by a relatively higher peak current and a lower peak duration, aligning with the trends observed across the different wire feed rates.

caption: Logarithmic plots of relative modulus and relative strength versus relative density, comparing the current DLP-printed TPMS structures against literature data from EBM, SLM, and DIW technologies, alongside the Gibson-Ashby theoretical model.
summary: This panel presents logarithmic plots relating relative modulus and relative strength to relative density. It benchmarks the DLP-printed Ti-6Al-4V porous materials against various manufacturing techniques, including EBM, SLM, and DIW, while also evaluating the experimental data against the theoretical predictions of the Gibson-Ashby model for porous structures.

caption: 1H NMR spectra (500 MHz, CDCl3, 500 K) comparing the chemical composition of ABS-CF composites across recycling stages R0 (red), R1 (green), and R5 (blue).
summary: This figure displays the 1H NMR spectra for ABS-CF composites at different recycling stages, specifically R0, R1, and R5. The spectra, acquired at 500 MHz in CDCl3 at 500 K, allow for a direct comparison of the chemical composition and structural integrity of the ABS-CF material throughout the recycling process.

caption: HAADF-TEM image of spherical TiC nanoparticles, typically ranging from 20 to 40 nm in diameter.
summary: HAADF-TEM imaging of TiC nanoparticles confirms their spherical morphology. The particles are observed to be in the nanometer scale, with most diameters falling between 20 and 40 nm. This structural characterization is essential for understanding the reinforcement phase morphology within the composite system being investigated.

caption: Interaction effect of layer height and nozzle temperature on fatigue life.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the interaction between layer height and nozzle temperature regarding fatigue life. The highest fatigue life values are achieved when both nozzle temperature and layer height are set to their highest investigated values, demonstrating a synergistic effect between these two specific process parameters during the manufacturing process.

caption: Summary table comparing fragment velocity, impact point position, and peak pressure across five valid experimental tests.
