summary: This table provides a comprehensive summary of the experimental data collected from five valid tests. It specifically correlates fragment velocity, impact point location, and peak pressure measurements. These parameters serve as the primary metrics for evaluating the performance and response characteristics observed during the conducted impact testing series.

caption: Isothermal equilibrium phase diagram of the Ti–V–Cr ternary system at 900 °C, constructed through fitting of experimental data.
summary: This figure presents the isothermal equilibrium phase diagram for the Ti–V–Cr ternary system at 900 °C. The diagram is derived from experimental data fitting, providing a comprehensive representation of the phase stability and equilibrium conditions for this specific alloy system at the designated temperature of 900 °C.

caption: Wöhler curve for sharp notched specimens, demonstrating a reduced fatigue resistance compared to the blunt notch geometry under identical fully reversed fatigue conditions.
summary: Fatigue resistance for the sharp notch geometry is plotted as stress amplitude versus cycles to failure. The data indicate a clear reduction in fatigue performance when compared to the blunt notch specimens. The curve includes fitted experimental data and scatter bands representing the 10%-90% failure probability range.

caption: Post-treatment light spot distribution on the screen, demonstrating the effect of the pre-treatment experiment on the DMD reflection pattern.
summary: This panel illustrates the light spot distribution on the screen following the completion of the pre-treatment experiment. By comparing this image to the initial state, one can observe the influence of the experimental pre-treatment on the DMD reflection, as captured through the optical setup described in the study.

caption: Top view of the conventional Octet model.
summary: This top view of the conventional Octet model provides a clear perspective of the lattice geometry without any rotational twist. It serves as the reference point for comparing the structural changes observed in the top-down projections of the twisted R-Octet metamaterial variants.

caption: R-curves illustrating fracture toughness (KJC) versus crack extension (Δa) for pure epoxy and various biomimetic ceramic composites, determined according to ASTM standards.
summary: R-curves derived from force-displacement data track the evolution of fracture toughness as cracks extend through the material. This analysis quantifies the crack growth resistance of different biomimetic architectures, providing a standardized metric to compare the toughening mechanisms inherent in the various nanoplate alignment configurations.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of Ni II Fe II @NC catalyst after accelerated durability testing, highlighting severe nanoparticle size growth.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging of the Ni II Fe II @NC catalyst post-ADT reveals significant nanoparticle coarsening. This observation confirms that the Ni II Fe II @NC catalyst experiences more severe size growth compared to the Ni II Fe III @NC catalyst, indicating inferior structural durability under the applied electrochemical testing conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the bottom region of Deloro60 alloy, illustrating grain orientation distribution under specific laser processing parameters.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map displays the grain orientation distribution within the bottom region of the Deloro60 alloy. The visualization provides a structural characterization of the material's microstructure as influenced by the applied laser processing parameters, serving as a baseline for comparing grain morphology across different sample regions.

caption: Phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions of the shape memory alloy (SMA) system.
summary: This panel presents the phase diagram of the shape memory alloy. It serves as the foundational thermodynamic representation, defining the stability regions and phase boundaries that govern the material's behavior under varying conditions, which is essential for understanding the subsequent transformation processes described in the study.

caption: Inverse pole figure-based microstructure map of the spheroidized tungsten carbide powder.
summary: The inverse pole figure-based microstructure map reveals the crystallographic orientation distribution within the spheroidized tungsten carbide powder. This visualization provides insight into the internal grain structure and orientation characteristics of the particles, complementing the morphological data obtained from the cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy analysis.

caption: Distribution of Taylor factor range across different scanning strategies.
summary: This plot summarizes the Taylor factor range for various scanning strategies, providing a comparative view of the texture strengthening effect. By considering {111}<110> slip systems and critical resolved shear stress, the distribution validates the intrinsic strength of the alloy and highlights the variability in texture across different fabrication methods.

caption: Stress amplitude versus number of cycles to failure (S/N) curves comparing surface ground MMJ and MBJ SS316L samples, with solid lines representing Basquin’s equation fits and arrows indicating run-out tests.
summary: This S/N plot illustrates the fatigue behavior of surface ground MMJ SS316L compared to MBJ SS316L samples. The data shows that MMJ SS316L significantly outperforms MBJ SS316L in the low-cycle fatigue regime, defined as approximately less than 10^4 cycles to failure, as evidenced by the Basquin's equation fits.

caption: Isopleth phase diagram of Scalmalloy® calculated using Thermo-Calc® software, focusing on the Al, Sc, Zr, and Mg components.
summary: This isopleth phase diagram, generated via Thermo-Calc® simulations, illustrates the phase stability of Scalmalloy® containing Al, Sc, Zr, and Mg. The simulation predicts the formation of intermetallic phases such as Al3(Sc,Zr) and Al12Mg17 within the temperature range of 200 °C to 500 °C.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of a monocrystalline Ni alloy (111) oxidized at 350℃ for 4 hours and 30 minutes, demonstrating long-term oxidation effects.
summary: Captured after 4 hours and 30 minutes of oxidation at 350℃, this ToF-SIMS profile details the final elemental depth distribution for the (111) monocrystalline Ni alloy. These results, obtained under identical conditions to previous samples, provide a comprehensive view of the long-term oxidation behavior and structural compositional changes in the material.

caption: PND Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 at 240 K, displaying experimental data points, calculated intensity, and difference plot.
summary: PND Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 at 240 K, displaying experimental data points, calculated intensity, and difference plot. This combined refinement, performed alongside SR-PXD data, provides a simultaneous description of the nuclear and magnetic structure for the specified alloy composition, with tick marks indicating the TiNiSi, Ni2In, and MgZn2 phases.

caption: Region 2 (111) equal area projection pole figure displaying the crystallographic texture of the blunt bridge extrudate.
summary: Region 2 presents a (111) equal area projection pole figure representing the crystallographic texture at this specific location of the blunt bridge extrudate. This visualization provides insight into the orientation distribution of the material grains within the cross-section, contributing to the overall understanding of the extrusion process.

caption: SHAP summary plot detailing the influence of input parameters on the joint shear capacity as determined by the SVM model.
summary: This SHAP summary graph for the SVM model illustrates the relationship between input variables and the joint shear capacity (Fmax). The plot serves to quantify the impact of each feature on the model's output, allowing for an assessment of how different inputs affect the predicted shear capacity of the joints.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the additively manufactured constant wavy fin geometry obtained via optical scanning.
summary: This 3D reconstruction illustrates the structural geometry of the constant wavy fin design. The cold plate was analyzed using a top-view optical scan to capture the precise morphology of the additively manufactured components, providing a detailed visualization of the constant wavy fin configuration for further geometric assessment.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining and quantitative analysis of CD86 and CD206 markers in macrophages cocultured with HP, HPD, and HPDM scaffolds.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining visualizes macrophage polarization regulation by the scaffolds. The HP group is predominantly polarized towards M1-type macrophages, characterized by high CD86 and low CD206 expression. The study quantifies these markers to assess the immunomodulatory effects of the different scaffold compositions on macrophage phenotype.

caption: Maximum current and power output of the reversible electrochemical cell as a function of electrolyte pH, maintained at a constant 2 M NaCl concentration.
summary: This panel illustrates the performance of a reversible electrochemical cell operating as a fuel cell under varying pH conditions at a fixed 2 M NaCl concentration. The data tracks the maximum current and power output, providing insight into how electrolyte acidity influences the electrochemical efficiency and overall power generation capabilities.

caption: Extract ion thermograms of HA raw material highlighting fragment ions at m/z 59 and 125 associated with evolved gases.
summary: The extract ion thermograms for HA raw material reveal the evolution of specific gaseous products during thermal degradation. The detection of fragment ions at m/z 59, corresponding to acetamide, and m/z 125, corresponding to 3-amino-2-isopropyl-5-methyl-2H-pyrazole, characterizes the chemical species released throughout the heating process.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the full width at half maximum (ΔqFWHM) of the 1D scattering intensity profile for four distinct experimental cases.
summary: This line graph illustrates the temporal evolution of the full width at half maximum (ΔqFWHM) for 1D scattering intensity profiles across four experimental cases. The data demonstrates a consistent decrease in ΔqFWHM over time as precipitates grow, indicating that the microstructures develop a more uniform precipitate size distribution as aging progresses.

caption: Synchrotron XRD pattern collected at the x = 250 μm position, revealing the presence of small Cr23C6 carbide peaks within the base material following the 600 °C-100 h heat treatment.
summary: Collected at a spatial position of x = 250 μm, this synchrotron XRD pattern identifies the formation of very small Cr23C6 carbide peaks within the base material. This diffraction data highlights subtle phase evolution occurring in the MPEA-brazed Alloy 600 coupon after 100 hours of thermal exposure at 600 °C.

caption: XRD profile obtained from the vertical cross-section of the PBF-LB sample, identifying constituent phases.
summary: The XRD profile represents the constituent phases present within the vertical cross-section of the PBF-LB sample. This diffraction data is part of the basic characterization results summarizing the densification behavior, microstructure, and phase composition of the material, confirming the crystalline phases formed during the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Tafel fitting results derived from the polarization curves, highlighting the corrosion current density (i_corr) values for the five steels.
summary: Tafel fitting results extracted from the polarization curves provide quantitative corrosion parameters for the five steels. The mean corrosion current density (i_corr) of 10 μA/cm2 was used to calculate test durations. Notably, the Cu3 steel exhibits the smallest i_corr, confirming the beneficial dual effects of Cu on corrosion resistance.

caption: Conceptual representation of the F-1 score metric derived from a classification task confusion matrix.
summary: This schematic illustrates the F-1 score metric within a classification confusion matrix. By calculating the harmonic mean of precision and recall, the metric effectively penalizes both false positive and false negative misclassifications. This balanced approach provides a robust performance estimation, making it highly desirable for evaluating multi-class classification problems.

caption: Engineering stress–strain curves for L-DED Ti–6Al–4V + 1.0 wt% Nb specimens, comparing as-built and post-processed conditions to illustrate the influence of heat treatment on the strength–ductility balance.
summary: Engineering stress–strain responses for L-DED Ti–6Al–4V + 1.0 wt% Nb are presented for as-built and post-processed states. These curves represent the averaged mechanical behavior derived from five tensile specimens per condition. The data demonstrates the impact of heat treatment on the alloy's strength–ductility balance, with no statistically significant outliers observed.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of unirradiated alloy 725 viewed along the [112] zone axis, displaying distinct superlattice reflections corresponding to the presence of γ' and γ'' phases.
summary: This diffraction pattern represents the unirradiated state of alloy 725 along the [112] zone axis. It serves as a baseline, clearly exhibiting the superlattice reflections associated with the γ' and γ'' phases, which are characteristic of the alloy's microstructure prior to any ion irradiation exposure.

caption: Normal map of the powder bed surface, serving as the foreground layer for image synthesis.
summary: The normal map provides the foreground surface orientation data for the powder bed. By capturing the directional surface vectors, this map acts as a critical layer that, when combined with the depth difference background, allows for the realistic synthesis of powder bed features and surface characteristics.

caption: Surface profile of the ODL3600 sample after sliding under a 15 N normal load.
summary: Surface profile analysis of the ODL3600 sample subjected to a 15 N normal load reveals no detectable wear damage. The 2D profile indicates that the surface remains intact under these specific testing conditions, demonstrating the wear resistance of the ODL3600 material during the sliding process.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the deposited material along the X-Z plane, revealing the internal structural integrity and layer distribution.
summary: The cross-sectional view in the X-Z plane provides an internal look at the deposited material. This micrograph allows for the assessment of the structural integrity and the distribution of layers resulting from the additive manufacturing process, confirming the successful consolidation of the composite wire.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curve for the base 6061 aluminum alloy sample, recorded over a temperature range extending up to 700 °C.
summary: This DSC heating curve illustrates the thermal response of the base 6061 aluminum alloy sample when heated to 700 °C. The plot provides a baseline for understanding the melting behavior of the alloy, serving as a reference for comparing the effects of iron additions on the material's thermal characteristics.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot displaying the natural logarithm of the surface-area-normalized H2 formation rate versus inverse temperature for silica-supported monometallic Cu NPs, Ni0.001Cu NPs, Ni0.01Cu NPs, np-Cu (SSM), np-Ni0.01Cu (SSM), and np-Ni0.003Cu (DL) catalysts during ethanol dehydrogenation.
summary: This Arrhenius-type plot illustrates the temperature dependence of H2 formation rates for various Cu and NiCu alloy catalysts. Normalized by copper surface area, the data demonstrates that highly dilute NiCu alloys exhibit significantly higher reactivity than monometallic Cu, consistent with the calculated apparent activation energies derived from these slopes.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of CS and CS-MA, focusing on the resonance peaks associated with the double bond protons of the MA group.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum for CS-MA displays specific resonance peaks at 5.77 ppm and 5.42 ppm. These signals are attributed to the protons on the double bond of the MA group, labeled as 'g', providing clear evidence of the successful incorporation of the MA group into the CS structure.

caption: Schematic representation of the DMTA experimental setup, illustrating the joint geometry with a 5.6 × 3.0 mm² cross-section and the associated kinematic analysis of the structure.
summary: This schematic illustrates the joint geometry and kinematic configuration used in the DMTA experimental setup. The design features a specific cross-section of 5.6 × 3.0 mm². This visual representation provides the necessary structural and geometric context required to understand the kinematic analysis performed on the test assembly during mechanical evaluation.

caption: Surface morphology of ATO-TiO2 doped substrate activated with 2 W laser power, showing isolated ablated pits.
summary: Surface morphology of the ATO-TiO2 doped substrate treated with 2 W laser power reveals a series of independent pits created by the laser irradiation. These localized ablation features indicate that low-power activation results in discrete surface modifications rather than a continuous or uniform removal of the photopolymer matrix.

caption: Experimental angular spectrum |p|^2(kx, ky) corresponding to the off-axis configuration of the passive cavitation detector.
summary: The heatmap presents the experimental angular spectrum |p|^2(kx, ky) for the off-axis configuration. By showing the normalized angular distribution of energy for each wavevector component, this visualization highlights the spectral characteristics and directional energy distribution inherent to the off-axis setup of the passive cavitation detector.

caption: Storage modulus curves as a function of temperature for TPU/PLA samples prepared with different material ratios.
summary: Storage modulus curves for TPU/PLA samples with different ratios are shown. These DMA results characterize the mechanical stiffness of the composite filaments across a temperature range, providing essential data on the viscoelastic behavior and structural integrity of the TPU/PLA blends developed for 3D printing applications.

caption: Performance evaluation of the predictive model using the offline test dataset.
summary: This panel illustrates the predictive performance of the developed model when applied to the offline test dataset. By comparing predicted values against actual experimental results, the visualization provides a quantitative assessment of the model's accuracy and reliability in capturing the underlying material properties or behaviors within the specified test conditions.

caption: Calculated results derived from reference [62] providing quantitative data on the hot cracking phenomenon.
summary: These calculated results, sourced from reference [62], provide a quantitative analysis of the hot cracking phenomenon. By presenting these computational findings alongside the phase field contours, the figure establishes a comprehensive view of the cracking mechanisms and thermal conditions associated with the small molten pool processing technique.

caption: Digital image correlation strain mapping of the region surrounding grain G2 at 4.26% global strain, highlighting intense strain localization at the interfaces between G2 and its neighbors, G3 and G4.
summary: Digital image correlation strain mapping of the region surrounding grain G2 at 4.26% global strain, highlighting intense strain localization at the interfaces between G2 and its neighbors, G3 and G4. Dislocations tend to pile up at these interfaces, which promotes the development of significant strain localization around grain G2 during deformation.

caption: EBSD pole figure and inverse pole figure inset for the heat-treated S5 sample, depicting the orientation distribution of the austenitic phase.
summary: Representing the heat-treated S5 sample, this panel shows the EBSD pole figure and inverse pole figure. The austenitic cubic symmetry crystals exhibit a uniform distribution across the <100>, <110>, and <111> orientations. The inset highlights the crystallographic texture differences compared to the as-built condition and the reference sample.

caption: Ductility versus ultimate tensile strength (UTS) comparison of the fabricated non-equiatomic HEA against various additively manufactured CoCrFeNi alloys reported in literature [23–30].
summary: This plot compares the ductility and ultimate tensile strength of the newly developed non-equiatomic HEA against existing additively manufactured CoCrFeNi alloys from references [23–30]. The results demonstrate that the in-situ alloying approach successfully produces a material with a superior combination of high strength and high ductility simultaneously.

caption: Loss modulus (E'') profiles illustrating the energy dissipation characteristics of PPcoPE and TPU binders loaded with 60 vol% Mg across multiple frequencies.
summary: Loss modulus (E'') curves reveal distinct differences in the viscous and energy-dissipating behaviors of PPcoPE and TPU composites containing 60 vol% Mg. These measurements, taken at 1, 5, and 10 Hz, highlight how the choice of binder influences the material's ability to dissipate energy during dynamic mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Initial peak force and its remaining percentage for PLA and PETG hexagonal honeycombs during cyclic cold programming.
summary: Initial peak force measurements reveal that the PLA hexagonal honeycomb experiences a substantial 76.5% reduction, falling from 734 N to 172 N after six cycles. In contrast, the PETG counterpart demonstrates superior stability, with its initial peak force decreasing by only 25% from 548 N to 411 N.

caption: Transmission (T) spectra of SL-Ti3C2/cotton composites showing the light-blocking efficiency of the different evaporator samples.
summary: Transmission spectra for SL-Ti3C2/cotton evaporators with 1, 5, and 10 wt% concentrations are presented. These measurements quantify the amount of light passing through the samples, providing essential data for calculating the total absorption capacity of the evaporators when combined with reflection data in the energy balance equation.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of four carbonaceous electrode samples measured in 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte at a scan rate of 0.005 V/s.
summary: This figure displays the cyclic voltammetry performance of four distinct carbonaceous electrode systems. The measurements were conducted in a 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte solution at a constant sweep rate of 0.005 V/s. These voltammograms provide a comparative analysis of the electrochemical behavior for the four prepared cell samples.

caption: Calculated total density of states (DOS) comparing pure aluminum with various Al-based alloy compositions.
summary: This plot displays the calculated total density of states for pure aluminum and its corresponding alloys. By analyzing these electronic structures, the figure provides essential insights into the fundamental electronic behavior and characteristics of these materials, serving as a key component in understanding the properties of Al-based systems.

caption: Equilibrium binary Ni–Ti phase diagram computed using the TCTI3 database, illustrating the stability regions of intermetallic phases and NiTi solid solution phases.
summary: This binary Ni–Ti phase diagram, computed via the TCTI3 database, displays the equilibrium stability regions for intermetallic phases and NiTi solid solution phases. The diagram predicts two distinct intermetallic phases and indicates that the liquid temperature decreases when the titanium concentration exceeds 40 at%, providing essential thermodynamic data for the system.

caption: Horizontal and vertical cross-sectional views of the ADDmeth3.1 reactor layout, featuring a single central heat pipe integrated within the reaction channel.
summary: The ADDmeth3.1 reactor design utilizes a triangular footprint with a reaction channel containing a single central heat pipe. Gas flows along the outer wall, entering the catalyst bed through a grid located on the bottom 10 mm of the channel wall, supported by a diamond lattice structure.

caption: In situ coefficient of friction (COF) measurements for Alloy 800HT recorded over sliding time at various temperatures in a helium environment, maintaining a 0.04 m/s sliding velocity and 5 N normal load.
summary: This plot displays in situ COF data for Alloy 800HT in a helium atmosphere. The results indicate that COF fluctuations are temperature-dependent, reaching the highest levels at 750 °C and the lowest at 500 °C, reflecting the dynamic frictional behavior of the material under these specific sliding conditions.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve validating the machine learning model's ability to classify FCC + BCC dual-phase stainless steel structures.
summary: Validation of the machine learning model for FCC + BCC dual-phase stainless steel is presented through this ROC curve. The plot demonstrates the model's high efficacy in distinguishing dual-phase structures from other classes, reflecting its robust ability to correctly identify complex phase compositions within the studied stainless steel alloy system.

caption: Interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) variation relative to hatch spacing.
summary: This plot depicts the evolution of interlaminar shear strength as hatch spacing increases. The data reveals a non-monotonic trend where the ILSS first increases and then decreases, ultimately reaching a maximum value of 22.25 MPa, which identifies an optimal hatch spacing for maximizing the mechanical integrity of the specimen.

caption: Isoconcentration surface set at 25 at. % Ni, highlighting the morphology and spatial arrangement of NiAl-rich precipitates.
summary: A 25 at. % Ni isoconcentration surface is utilized to delineate the NiAl-rich precipitates within the material. This visualization technique effectively isolates the precipitate phase from the surrounding matrix, providing a clear view of the morphology and distribution of these features as captured by atom probe tomography.

caption: Ti–Al binary alloy phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium relationships between various phases as a function of temperature and composition.
summary: The Ti–Al binary alloy phase diagram provides a comprehensive overview of phase stability across different compositions and temperatures. Analysis of this diagram reveals that decreasing the aluminum content shifts the phase equilibrium point toward the α2 phase region, highlighting the critical influence of composition on the resulting microstructural phase constituents.

caption: Custom-designed fixture utilized for supporting metal sheets and monitoring working forces during the incremental sheet forming (ISF) process.
summary: This photograph displays the custom-designed fixture developed for the incremental sheet forming process. The equipment is specifically engineered to provide structural support for metal sheets while simultaneously recording the working forces applied during the forming operation, ensuring precise monitoring and control of the experimental parameters throughout the manufacturing procedure.

caption: Mean squared displacement (MSD) components of a single H atom in pure Ni plotted along the x, y, and z directions across a temperature range of 500–1200 K.
summary: This panel displays the MSD components for a single hydrogen atom within a pure nickel lattice. The data, decomposed along the x, y, and z Cartesian directions, illustrates the diffusion behavior of the hydrogen atom as the temperature increases from 500 K to 1200 K, providing insight into atomic mobility.

caption: Bode plot showing the electrochemical impedance response of L-PBF-produced NiTi alloy S3 after immersion in pH 7 Hank's solution for 24, 48, and 72 hours.
summary: The Bode plot for the S3 NiTi alloy specimen captures the electrochemical impedance behavior over the specified immersion periods. By analyzing the frequency-dependent magnitude and phase angle, the plot contributes to the overall assessment of the passive film's performance and degradation kinetics for the S3 alloy in Hank's solution.

caption: Plot depicting the correlation between the heater pattern pitch and light transmission, highlighting the optical transparency characteristics of the device.
summary: This panel evaluates the optical properties of the curved transparent glass heater by plotting light transmittance against the pattern pitch. Together with square resistance, light transmission serves as a vital performance metric, ensuring that the heater maintains high transparency while achieving the desired electrical resistance for its intended functional application.

caption: CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram showing the color coordinates for pure SnO2 nanoparticles.
summary: The CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram for pure SnO2 nanoparticles illustrates the emission characteristics derived from photoluminescence spectra. These color coordinates are positioned within the blue region of the diagram, providing a visual representation of the optical emission properties of the synthesized nanostructured material as detailed in the study.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of Cu50Ti50 powder mixture after 30 hours of milling, revealing distinct lattice fringes.
summary: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy imaging of the Cu50Ti50 powder mixture subjected to 30 hours of milling reveals clear periodicity in the lattice fringes. This structural observation signifies the development of well-defined crystallinity within the material as a result of the extended mechanical milling process.

caption: Fundamental unit cell geometry for the Gyroid TPMS lattice.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental unit cell geometry for the Gyroid TPMS lattice. The unit cell is modeled using 3592 elements, representing one of eight identical copies that constitute the complete TPMS lattice structure as defined in the structural modeling parameters for periodic minimal surface architectures.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the electrochemical impedance response of L-PBF-produced NiTi alloy S1 after immersion in pH 7 Hank's solution for 24, 48, and 72 hours.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of the S1 NiTi alloy specimen. Data collected after 24, 48, and 72 hours of immersion in pH 7 Hank's solution reveal the passive film characteristics, with the specimen exhibiting the lowest protectiveness among the tested samples throughout the 72-hour duration.

caption: Live/Dead fluorescence staining of BMSCs cultured on matrix scaffolds at day 2, where live cells appear green and dead cells appear red.
summary: Live/Dead fluorescence staining was performed on BMSCs cultured on matrix scaffolds at day 2 to assess biotoxicity. Live cells were visualized with green fluorescence, while dead cells were stained with red fluorescence. The results indicate that the prepared matrix scaffolds were not biotoxic to the cultured cells.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography and corresponding depth profile of LCO dots subjected to the lowest thermal budget after Al paste removal.
summary: Atomic force microscopy topography and corresponding depth profile of LCO dots subjected to the lowest thermal budget after Al paste removal. This measurement investigates the etching effects of Al particles on the LCO morphology, providing a quantitative assessment of the surface profile under the specified low-temperature processing condition.

caption: Average confusion matrix for Model I, which classifies parental magmas into I-, S-, and A-type categories.
summary: Model I demonstrates robust performance in distinguishing between I-, S-, and A-type parental magmas of deposits. The confusion matrix indicates high identification accuracy, with most results exceeding 0.95, confirming the model's effectiveness in categorizing the magmatic origins of the studied geological deposits based on the provided testing datasets.

caption: Magnified view of the microfluidic channel, revealing a measured width of 165–170 µm.
summary: Microscopic examination of the microfluidic channel shows a slight deviation from the design specifications. While the intended width was 150 µm, the actual fabricated channel width ranges between 165 and 170 µm. This image highlights the dimensional accuracy achieved during the 3D printing of the internal channel features.

caption: Charge transfer resistance attributed to the electric double-layer (Rct–EDL) derived from the second semi-circle of Nyquist plots.
summary: Panel b illustrates the charge transfer resistance associated with the electric double-layer (Rct–EDL). This resistance is extracted from the second semi-circle observed in Nyquist plots, which is suggested to arise from electrochemical double-layer processes, such as charge transfer occurring at grain boundary dislocations within the material.

caption: Log-linear plot showing the evolution of creep rate as a function of strain for the initial test (black squares) and the rejuvenated specimen (red circles) under identical high-temperature, low-stress conditions.
summary: This log-linear plot illustrates the evolution of the creep rate relative to strain for the specimen. It highlights the consistency in creep behavior between the first test and the second test performed after rejuvenation, confirming the restoration of material properties in the high-temperature, low-stress creep regime.

caption: Norton plot displaying the minimum creep rate as a function of engineering stress for various alloys and conditions, used to determine the creep stress exponent.
summary: This Norton plot illustrates the relationship between minimum creep rate and engineering stress for multiple alloys and experimental conditions. By analyzing the slope of these data points, the creep stress exponent is derived for each material, providing critical insights into the deformation mechanisms governing the creep behavior under different stress levels.

caption: Dilatometry curves showing length change versus temperature for as-cast and HIPed TiNbCr MPE alloys during heating and cooling cycles up to 1200 °C.
summary: Dilatometry tests conducted on as-cast and HIPed TiNbCr MPE alloys reveal phase transformation behavior during controlled thermal cycling. The curves demonstrate microstructural redistribution, specifically highlighting the formation of the HCP phase at approximately 640 °C. These results provide critical insights into the thermal stability and phase evolution of the alloys.

caption: Atomic model of SL-Si2O stacking mode II, characterized by the accumulation of Pauli repulsive forces due to head-to-head orbital overlaps.
summary: Stacking mode II is a high-symmetry configuration of the SL-Si2O vdW structure. In this arrangement, the modified pz orbitals between layers tend to form head-to-head overlaps. This specific alignment leads to an accumulation of Pauli repulsive forces, distinguishing it from the other stacking modes in the series.

caption: Predicted phase evolution during rapid solidification of a mixture containing 80% AlSi12 and 20% Ti6Al4V.
summary: Shifting toward the Al-rich zone with an 80% mass fraction of AlSi12, this panel demonstrates the elimination of all conventionally known titanium phases. Despite this shift, the simulation anticipates the continued presence of Ti-Al intermetallic compounds within the rapidly solidified microstructure.

caption: AFM topography and surface roughness analysis of the CNF membrane.
summary: Atomic force microscopy of the CNF membrane provides a detailed topographical map and surface roughness measurement. These data characterize the surface texture of the CNF material, offering a baseline for evaluating how surface roughness influences the deposition and performance of subsequent selective layers in composite membrane systems.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetic entropy change for heat-treated (HT) PBF-LB/M samples, showing a maximum ΔS of 3.95 J/kg K at 5 T and 328 K.
summary: This graph illustrates the magnetic entropy change (ΔS) for heat-treated PBF-LB/M samples across the FOMST temperature range at fields up to 5 T. A peak entropy change of 3.95 J/kg K is observed at 328 K under a 5 T field, highlighting the material's performance following the heat treatment process.

caption: Sensitivity analysis of neuron nodes independence, illustrating the relative impact of individual nodes on model performance.
summary: This figure presents the results of a comprehensive sensitivity analysis conducted to evaluate the independence of neuron nodes within the model. The visualization highlights how varying specific nodes influences overall performance, providing critical insights into the structural dependencies and functional contributions of individual components within the neural network architecture.

caption: Transmittance spectra of A-CNC/CTFA composite resins evaluated at different filler concentrations.
summary: The transmittance spectra of the A-CNC/CTFA composite resins are presented to evaluate the effect of filler concentration on optical properties. These measurements provide insight into how varying the concentration of A-CNCs influences the transparency of the composite resin system compared to the S-CNC counterparts.

caption: Confusion matrices evaluated at epoch 73, detailing classification performance across three distinct flow rate classes and five temperature ranges.
summary: These confusion matrices provide a granular assessment of the model's predictive accuracy at epoch 73. By mapping the classification results across three flow rate categories and five temperature ranges, the visualization highlights the model's capability to correctly identify and distinguish between the various experimental conditions.

caption: Dilatometric expansion curves representing the dimensional changes of heat-treated samples as a function of temperature.
summary: This plot displays the dilatometric curves for heat-treated samples, illustrating their dimensional response to thermal processing. These measurements are essential for characterizing phase transformations, as the observed expansion behavior correlates with the austenite fraction present in the material, providing a macroscopic view of the microstructural evolution during heat treatment.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping showing the spatial distribution of carbon (C) on the SCC-2 composite surface.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping illustrates the spatial distribution of carbon across the SCC-2 composite surface. As part of a broader elemental analysis, this map confirms that carbon is evenly distributed, contributing to the overall chemical homogeneity of the SCF/Co@C composite material as observed in the surface analysis.

caption: Dark-field TEM images at low and high magnifications of omega nanoprecipitates in conventionally processed samples, with corresponding SAED patterns in the insets.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging reveals the distribution of omega nanoprecipitates in conventionally processed samples. The analysis, supported by SAED patterns shown in the insets, provides a detailed view of the precipitate morphology at both low and high magnifications, confirming the formation of these phases during the final water quench process.

caption: Smooth layer formation observed after the material has maintained contact with the support plane for a sufficient duration.
summary: Extended contact time between the deposited material and the support plane facilitates the formation of a smooth, uniform layer. This simulation illustrates the transition to a stable morphology, highlighting how sufficient residence time allows the material to overcome initial deposition constraints and achieve a continuous, smooth surface finish.

caption: SHAP value distribution for five features predicting the FCC+BCC dual phase, highlighting the preference for moderate feature values.
summary: This SHAP plot displays the feature contributions for predicting the FCC+BCC dual phase. The results indicate that only moderate feature values are favorable for the formation of this dual-phase structure, contrasting with the directional trends observed for the individual BCC and FCC phase predictions in the other panels.

caption: Inverse pole figure map showing grain orientation in the H11/Cu composite.
summary: The inverse pole figure map reveals grain orientation within the composite, highlighting a preferential orientation within single primary powder particles. Specifically, the map demonstrates this orientation along the 101-direction, providing insight into the crystallographic texture of the H11/Cu composite material.

caption: Sample image generated using the QSGS algorithm, presented as a 128 × 128 pixel grid.
summary: Generated via the QSGS algorithm, this 128 × 128 pixel image serves as a sample within the study's dataset. Despite having a similar porosity to the rectangle packing sample, the behavior of the resulting curves remains complex, making it difficult to determine which variables best fit the data.

caption: Magnetization versus temperature profiles for #AC-168AC Ni-Co-Mn-Sn powders, aged for 168 hours and air-cooled, under 50 Oe, 1 T, and 5 T fields.
summary: The #AC-168AC Ni-Co-Mn-Sn powders, subjected to 168 hours of aging and subsequent air cooling, are analyzed via M-T curves at 50 Oe, 1 T, and 5 T. These results highlight the magnetic response following extended aging, with detailed parameters listed in the research documentation for further comparison.

caption: High-frequency zoom of the Nyquist plot from panel (b), with all impedance spectra shifted to zero ohmic resistance to highlight specific electrochemical processes.
summary: This high-frequency zoom of the Nyquist plot isolates specific electrochemical processes by shifting all spectra to zero ohmic resistance. The data, derived from the impedance measurements presented in panel (b), allows for a clearer analysis of the cell's internal kinetics and charge transfer characteristics during the multi-chronopotentiometry experiments.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image demonstrating Bi atoms adsorbed at the steel surface.
summary: Atomic-scale HAADF-STEM imaging shows Bi atoms adsorbed at the surface of the LPBF 316L steel. This observation, combined with the higher defect density in LPBF 316L, suggests that Bi segregation is a key feature of the interfacial structure, with atoms either adsorbing or incorporating into the steel lattice.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern for Sample 1, integrated at a 15° azimuth in the X direction.
summary: This panel displays a synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern obtained from Sample 1. The data is integrated around a 15° azimuth in the X direction. This specific diffraction pattern serves as a substitute for a single-shot Time-Of-Flight neutron diffraction pattern to facilitate subsequent analysis of texture effects within the material.

caption: B-H hysteresis loop comparison across different strain levels at a small applied field of 400 A/m.
summary: This panel compares B-H loops at 400 A/m. Under this small applied field, the maximum magnetic induction of the 14% strain sample is 65.3% of the 0% strain sample, demonstrating that strain significantly affects the B-H curve shape and magnetic performance depending on the external field strength.

caption: Isothermal oxidation kinetics represented by weight gain versus time for various alloys at 900 °C.
summary: Isothermal oxidation kinetics at 900 °C show weight gain behavior for the tested alloys. The kinetic curves exhibit a rapid initial increase in weight change that gradually decreases over time. Notably, IN718 and MAR-M247 demonstrate higher weight changes during this initial stage of oxidation compared to the other alloys.

caption: Relative strength (H/E) as a function of indenter penetration depth for QC and 2/1AC coatings.
summary: This plot illustrates the variation in relative strength, defined as the H/E ratio, for QC and 2/1AC coatings across different indenter penetration depths. The data demonstrates how the material's relative hardness evolves as the probe penetrates deeper into the coating structure, providing insight into the mechanical response of these specific coating systems.

caption: Calculated Zn–Fe binary phase diagram generated using the TCFE12 thermodynamic database.
summary: This panel presents the equilibrium Zn–Fe phase diagram calculated using the TCFE12 thermodynamic database. It serves as the baseline reference for understanding the phase stability and transformation behavior within the Zn–Fe system, providing the foundational thermodynamic framework for the subsequent analysis of alloying element influences on phase boundaries.

caption: Mean Square Displacement (MSD) plots comparing the diffusion kinetics of choline, chloride ions, and urea in the 1ChCl:2Urea system at 90°C.
summary: This panel displays the Mean Square Displacement analysis for choline, chloride ions, and urea at 90°C. By comparing these results with the 60°C data, the analysis reveals the temperature-dependent diffusion and material transport characteristics of the 1ChCl:2Urea system, highlighting how increased thermal energy influences molecular mobility.

caption: Cell viability of hMSCs after 24 hours of exposure to scaffolds pre-treated in PBS, compared against a control group of hMSCs alone.
summary: Human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) exhibit high viability when cultured in contact with the scaffolds for 24 hours. Statistical analysis confirms that there are no significant differences in cell viability between the scaffold-treated groups and the control group, indicating excellent biocompatibility of the materials after organic acid removal.

caption: Comparative PL spectra of the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample and reference InAs/GaAs quantum dots measured at 77 K under a constant 100 mW excitation power.
summary: Comparative photoluminescence measurements at 77 K under 100 mW excitation demonstrate the spectral differences between the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample and reference InAs/GaAs quantum dots. This comparison highlights the impact of the bilayer structure and capping layer composition on the optical emission characteristics of the quantum dot system.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the JT2 alloy needle, showing the path through the γ'→γ phase region with Cr atoms in red and Al atoms in green.
summary: The APT reconstruction of the JT2 alloy needle reveals the distinct partitioning of elements across the γ/γ' interface. Consistent with the observed elemental distribution, Al is shown to partition into the γ' precipitates, while Cr is concentrated in the γ matrix, providing a clear visual representation of the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Chronoamperogram of the NP-2 experiment displaying the decay of anodic current density as a function of time.
summary: This chronoamperogram tracks the anodic current density for the NP-2 experiment over time. The results demonstrate a continuous decline in current density, reaching a final stage value that is 70.8% lower than the initial stage, which characterizes the kinetics of the anodic dissolution process under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Piezoresistive response represented by -ΔR/Ro versus strain for the MWCNT/PA12 HHS during seven cycles of in-plane compressive loading.
summary: Piezoresistive response curves, plotted as -ΔR/Ro against strain, track the electrical resistance changes of the MWCNT/PA12 HHS throughout seven cycles of in-plane compression. These measurements correlate the mechanical deformation of the structure with its electrical performance, capturing the cyclic sensitivity of the conductive MWCNT network within the polymer matrix.

caption: Ternary feedstock formulation map illustrating the distribution of ten distinct binder volume ratios composed of SEBS, LDPE, and paraffin wax, with binder concentrations reaching up to 45 vol% of the total feedstock volume.
summary: This ternary formulation map visualizes the experimental design space for ten feedstock compositions comprising SEBS, LDPE, and paraffin wax. By plotting these binder volume ratios, the study assesses the combined influence of binder components on the production and printability of ceramic filaments, with eight specific formulations subsequently tested in MEX processes.

caption: Response surface plot depicting the effect of infill density and layer thickness on compressive strength at a 0.2 mm layer thickness.
summary: Depicting the effect of infill density and layer thickness on compressive strength, this plot focuses on a 0.2 mm layer thickness for FDM-printed PEEK-carbon fibre composites. The response surface analysis demonstrates how these parameters interact to influence the compressive performance, offering insights into the optimization of printing parameters for mechanical strength.

caption: Electronic band structure and projected local density of states for a 2 × 2 supercell of single-layer GeN subjected to 2% in-plane biaxial tensile strain, calculated using the PBE functional.
summary: Calculated using the PBE functional, this panel displays the electronic band structure and projected local density of states for a 2 × 2 supercell of single-layer GeN under 2% in-plane biaxial tensile strain. This analysis is part of a broader investigation into emerging half-metallic properties in single-layer GeN.

caption: XPS depth profile of the passive film on the Ni-doped Fe-based AAC, demonstrating that the film is nearly devoid of Ni despite the doping.
summary: The XPS depth profile for the Ni-doped AAC reveals the elemental distribution within the passive film. Notably, the cation concentration data indicates that the passive film is nearly devoid of Ni, providing critical insights into the surface composition and 3D elemental distribution of the doped alloy after polarization.

caption: Nanoindentation profile demonstrating a peak hardness value of 5.07 GPa.
summary: This panel displays the results of a nanoindentation test performed on the material, specifically targeting a region of interest. The measurement yields a high hardness value of 5.07 GPa, which is identified as the highest value recorded in the study, reflecting the mechanical response of the localized microstructure.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of Co in the 14Ni-AT sample, showing the distribution of cobalt.
summary: Cobalt distribution within the 14Ni-AT sample is illustrated in this EDS map. This elemental mapping, when analyzed in conjunction with the HAADF image and other compositional data, confirms the chemical characteristics of the nanoscale reverted austenite and provides a comprehensive view of the alloy's elemental partitioning.

caption: Schematic representation of one-dimensional wave or particle propagation through a system composed of two distinct material layers.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental concept of one-dimensional propagation through a two-material system. It serves as the baseline model for understanding how waves or particles interact with interfaces between two different media, providing a simplified framework for analyzing transmission and reflection characteristics in basic layered material configurations.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for as-prepared Ni-Fe alloy powders with nickel-rich compositions ranging from 60 to 90 atomic percent.
summary: The XRD patterns for as-prepared Ni x Fe 100-x alloy powders, where x ranges from 60 to 90%, are presented. These diffraction results indicate that the synthesized Ni-Fe solid solutions predominantly exhibit a face-centered cubic (fcc) or simple cubic crystal structure, corresponding to an iron content band of approximately 18–30 atomic percent.

caption: Temperature-dependent plots of flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus for the sixth ASA recycling course sample.
summary: Temperature-dependent plots of flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus are provided for the sixth ASA recycling course sample. These DMA test results complete the set of data for all six recycling courses, offering insight into the mechanical performance and thermal stability of the final recycled ASA material.

caption: Phase angle Bode plot of uncoated 316L steel in diluted H2SO4 (pH 5.5) at 60 °C, showing the evolution of low-frequency phase angles over 168 hours of exposure.
summary: The phase angle Bode plot illustrates the electrochemical response of uncoated 316L steel in a diluted sulfuric acid solution over a 168-hour period. A gradual increase in low-frequency phase angles is observed over time, which suggests the development of capacitive behavior resulting from surface passivation during the exposure.

caption: FT-IR spectra displaying the chemical bonding and functional group profiles of Ca-PA and Ca-PA-F.
summary: FT-IR spectra of the fillers are presented in this panel. These spectroscopic measurements characterize the chemical composition and functional groups present in Ca-PA and Ca-PA-F. By analyzing the infrared absorption patterns, the spectra provide essential information regarding the molecular structure and chemical bonding environments of the investigated filler materials.

caption: Accuracy of predicted fatigue life as a function of the number of neurons per layer, comparing SNN architectures with one and two hidden layers.
summary: This plot demonstrates how increasing the number of neurons per layer impacts the accuracy of fatigue life predictions in SNNs. By comparing architectures with one and two hidden layers, the results emphasize the sensitivity of model performance to network width, providing guidance for optimizing SNN configurations for fatigue analysis.

caption: Simulated concentration profiles of Al and Cr for the PBF-EB Alloy 247 variant at the end of stage-I oxidation at 1100 °C, as determined by DICTRA modeling.
summary: The DICTRA simulation for the PBF-EB Alloy 247 variant shows the Al and Cr concentration profiles at the end of stage-I oxidation (t = 15000 s). The Al concentration at the alloy/oxide interface is 11.8 at%, matching the CC variant and characterizing the oxidation kinetics for this specific processing method.

caption: Training loss evolution for the LCNN model during the pore status detection task across three distinct test samples (Test-1, Test-2, and Test-3).
summary: This panel displays the training loss progression for the LCNN model during the pore status detection task. The graph tracks the performance of three separate test samples, providing a visual representation of the model's learning process and convergence behavior during the training phase for this specific classification task.

caption: Evolution of glass transition temperature (Tg) and melting temperature (Tm) for TPMS samples and tensile coupons, with the initial Tg of the TPMS sample recorded at 58.8 degrees Celsius.
summary: This panel displays the Tg and Tm values for TPMS samples and tensile coupons. The initial glass transition temperature of the TPMS sample was measured at 58.8 degrees Celsius, providing a baseline for evaluating the thermal stability and phase transition characteristics of the material throughout the aging process.

caption: Magneto-thermoelectric power (MTEP) of a 50 nm thick Co thin film at 178 K with a 45 K temperature gradient, highlighting a sign inversion relative to the Py film.
summary: MTEP measurements for a 50 nm thick Co thin film at 178 K show distinct peaks at -0.7 mT and 3.8 mT. This response exhibits a sign difference compared to the Py film, demonstrating that the magneto-thermoelectric effect is sensitive to the specific magnetic material composition.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the MoNbTaWTix system illustrating phase evolution with increasing Ti content.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram for the MoNbTaWTix system depicts a phase evolution similar to the vanadium-doped system. The addition of titanium influences the equilibrium state, maintaining the stability of the BCC_B2 structure. Initial equilibrium assessments indicate that no high-temperature transformations are expected for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Relative density map showing processing regimes as a function of laser power and scanning speed, with regions labeled for gas-entrapped pores, lack-of-fusion defects, and keyhole defects.
summary: This relative density map visualizes the processing space defined by laser power and scanning speed. It identifies distinct regimes characterized by dominant defect types, specifically gas-entrapped pores, lack-of-fusion defects, and keyhole defects, providing a comprehensive overview of how process parameters dictate the structural integrity and defect formation in Ti6Al4V samples.

caption: Isolated unit cell geometry featuring a Y-shaped slot with three legs, shown without the MXene coating layer.
summary: Depicted here is the unit cell structure prior to the application of the MXene coating. The design features a hexagonal dielectric substrate integrated with a Y-shaped slot consisting of three distinct legs, establishing the baseline geometry for the frequency selective surface unit cell before functionalization.

caption: Nyquist plot for SLMed TC4 alloy specimen S4 after 12 days of immersion in a corrosive medium.
summary: Specimen S4 presents electrochemical impedance results after 12 days of immersion. Within the S4-S6 series, this sample shows higher low-frequency impedance modules and phase angles, indicating better corrosion resistance. These findings are consistent with the comparative analysis of the SLMed TC4 alloy process parameters.

caption: TGA and DTG profiles for the third catalytic sample, demonstrating the relationship between temperature and mass loss to characterize decomposition behavior.
summary: Panel c shows the TGA and DTG curves for the third catalyst sample. The data provides detailed information about the quality and purity of the synthesized CNT by highlighting weight loss patterns and decomposition rates. This analysis is fundamental for understanding the thermal stability and decomposition behavior of the catalyst.

caption: Electron energy loss spectroscopy data for the 1000–24 sample, displaying O Kα, Cr L, and Fe L edges to confirm the nanoparticle composition as a FeCrO compound.
summary: Electron energy loss spectroscopy data for the 1000–24 sample, displaying O Kα, Cr L, and Fe L edges to confirm the nanoparticle composition as a FeCrO compound. This chemical characterization confirms the specific elemental makeup of the nanoparticles identified within the heat-treated alloy microstructure through precise edge detection.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction versus temperature plot for the 89 wt.-% secondary AlSi10MnMg alloy, showing phase development up to 0.10 wt.-%.
summary: Representing the 89 wt.-% secondary AlSi10MnMg alloy, this JMatPro-calculated diagram shows the equilibrium phase fraction evolution during solidification. It highlights low-fraction phases up to 0.10 wt.-%. The predicted phase path follows a progressive sequence: Liquid, Al2Si2M, alpha-Al, Alpha, Silicon, and Mg2Si, confirming the alloy's solidification behavior under equilibrium conditions.

caption: In-situ Raman spectra of the CuNi@BNC catalyst acquired at various working potentials to evaluate structural stability and reaction intermediates.
summary: In-situ Raman spectroscopy was conducted to identify key reaction intermediates and possible reaction pathways for the CuNi@BNC catalyst. Furthermore, these spectra were collected at varying potentials to explore the structural stability of the CuNi@BNC material, providing a comprehensive view of its behavior under electrochemical stress.

caption: Ashby plot comparing tensile properties of 2-layer Biomid-PLA and Cordenka-PLA composites against a literature-derived dataset of additively manufactured continuous glass, aramid, carbon, and short cellulose fiber-reinforced PLA composites.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the tensile performance of 2-layer Biomid-PLA and Cordenka-PLA composites. By benchmarking these materials against a comprehensive dataset of additively manufactured continuous and short fiber-reinforced PLA composites, the plot highlights the relative mechanical positioning of the natural fiber composites within the broader landscape of existing literature.

caption: Reflection coefficients of the spherical FESA as a function of frequency, demonstrating the impact of varying arch thickness (t) and ring width (w1).
summary: The reflection coefficients of the spherical FESA are presented here to show the sensitivity of the device to geometric parameters. By systematically varying the arch thickness and the ring width, the plot captures the resulting shifts in the reflection response, highlighting the influence of structural dimensions on the resonance characteristics.

caption: Magnified ABF-STEM image highlighting the specific precipitate-dislocation region identified in panel (a).
summary: Providing a higher-magnification view of the precipitate-dislocation architecture, this ABF-STEM image focuses on the specific region of interest. It serves as the basis for subsequent compositional mapping and high-resolution imaging, detailing the local arrangement of dislocations and precipitates within the PBF-EB sample.

caption: Visual overview of sample variability in additive manufacturing, showcasing various specimens fabricated using distinct scanning strategies and parameters.
summary: This photograph showcases a range of samples fabricated utilizing distinct scanning strategies and parameters. The image highlights the inherent sample variability encountered in additive manufacturing processes, demonstrating how different processing conditions influence the final physical appearance and characteristics of the manufactured parts within the experimental build volume.

caption: Experimental setup showing the biaxial straining device secured within a tensile rig, positioned inside a Petri dish containing complete media without phenol red.
summary: This photograph illustrates the experimental configuration where a biaxial straining device is clamped into a tensile rig. The device is submerged in complete media lacking phenol red within a Petri dish, facilitating controlled mechanical testing of the gel surface while maintained in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.

caption: I-V and I-P characteristics of single cells featuring various anodes, measured at 700 °C using dry hydrogen as the fuel.
summary: The I-V and I-P characteristics of the single cells with dry H2 as the fuel at 700 °C are presented in Fig. 1a. These curves illustrate the electrochemical performance of various anode materials under hydrogen-fed conditions, providing a baseline for evaluating the catalytic activity and power density of the tested single cells.

caption: Normalized XAFS spectra at the Mn K-edge for the PEG-3–1500 specimen compared against SrMnO3, MnO2, and Mn2O3 reference materials, featuring an inset with LCF fitting results for the entire spectral range.
summary: Normalized XAFS spectra at the Mn K-edge are displayed for the PEG-3–1500 specimen alongside reference materials SrMnO3, MnO2, and Mn2O3. The analysis includes LCF fitting curves for the entire spectrum, providing insight into the oxidation state of manganese cations within the specimen as part of the broader XAFS characterization.

caption: EDS spectrum identifying the chemical composition of the γ-phase and Laves phase, highlighting enrichment of Nb and Mo in the Laves phase.
summary: The EDS spectrum provides quantitative chemical analysis of the phases present. Point P1, representing the γ-phase, is composed of Ni, Cr, and Fe. In contrast, Point P2, corresponding to the Laves phase, shows significant enrichment in Nb (33.40 wt%) and Mo (2.90 wt%), confirming the distinct elemental composition of these phases.

caption: EELS elemental map revealing the distribution of nickel (Ni) at the crack tip, showing significant enrichment on the crack wall.
summary: This EELS elemental map highlights the distribution of nickel (Ni) at the crack tip. Point analysis confirms the presence of almost pure Ni on the crack wall, indicating that the corrosive medium causes dealloying and the formation of a Ni-rich layer after the main crack propagates.

caption: Stress-displacement response of FeCrNi nanoparticles with varying oxygen content during molecular dynamics nanoindentation.
summary: Molecular dynamics simulation results for the nanoindentation process of the FeCrNi model demonstrate a characteristic stress profile. The stress exhibits a trend of first increasing and then decreasing, followed by another increase and decrease, illustrating the mechanical response of the nanoparticles under varying oxygen concentrations.

caption: Comparison of experimental and simulated magnetic flux density B in the airgap of Alnico 8 LNGT40 magnets within an iron core, plotted against varying coil currents.
summary: This plot illustrates the demagnetization behavior of Alnico 8 LNGT40 magnets integrated into an iron core. By comparing experimental measurements with simulation results from the proposed model, the figure demonstrates the accuracy of the model in predicting magnetic flux density B in the airgap under different coil current conditions.

caption: Comparison of the 3D scanned surface to the CAD model, where green indicates null deviation, blue represents inward deviation, and red represents outward deviation.
summary: This 3D scanned mesh comparison quantifies the geometric fidelity of the printed vase relative to the CAD model. The colormap highlights deviations in signed distances, with predominantly green regions indicating high dimensional accuracy, while localized blue and red areas reveal minor deviations resulting from the printing process and slight overextrusion.

caption: Evolution of peak and valley stresses for HT-AB and RT-AB HX specimens during cyclic loading at strain amplitudes of 0.8 % and 0.4 %.
summary: Evolution of peak and valley stresses during cyclic loading is plotted for AB-HX specimens at both room and elevated temperatures. By comparing these stress ranges across 0.8 % and 0.4 % strain amplitudes, the plot characterizes the cyclic hardening or softening behavior of the material under different thermal conditions.

caption: In-situ HEXRD analysis of the AS1 sample heated at 0.167 °C/s to 400 °C, displaying the evolution of lattice parameter, its derivative, FWHM, and temperature.
summary: The AS1 sample, heated at 0.167 °C/s, shows in-situ HEXRD data including lattice parameter, FWHM, and temperature. The lattice derivative curve remains steady initially before showing a positive inclination change, which signifies the onset of Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitation, as these intermetallics possess a larger lattice parameter than the aluminum matrix.

caption: Specific capacitance values of the ASC device plotted as a function of various current densities, highlighting the rate capability performance.
summary: Specific capacitance values are plotted against different current densities to demonstrate the rate capability of the ASC device. This graph quantifies how the energy storage capacity of the DIW printed Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene//α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene device changes as the discharge current increases, indicating its efficiency at different power levels.

caption: O 1s XPS spectra for Ni@Al2O3 and CeNi BA@Al2O3 catalysts, illustrating the surface oxygen environment.
summary: O 1s XPS spectra are presented for both Ni@Al2O3 and CeNi BA@Al2O3 catalysts. These spectra provide insight into the surface oxygen environment, which is part of the broader spectroscopic characterization showing that the modified catalyst optimizes Ni valence states to favor active Ni 0 center formation for improved dry reforming.

caption: Elasticity limit measured in stress for Ethocel- and Zein-based formulations, demonstrating performance differences between the two materials.
summary: This bar chart displays the elasticity limit in terms of stress for Ethocel- and Zein-based formulations, based on five replicates. The results demonstrate a statistically significant difference between the two materials, with Ethocel showing distinct mechanical properties compared to Zein, supported by a p-value of less than 0.05.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the temperature dependence of the forward reaction constant k f, assuming a single-adduct reaction mechanism.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the forward reaction constant k f as a function of temperature. The initial activation energy was estimated from this data, though the plot reveals that a single-adduct model fails to accurately describe the reaction kinetics across the entire temperature range investigated in the study.

caption: Relative frequency distributions of normalized equivalent diameter (ED) values for precipitates in AlSi7Mg samples, comparing top and bottom regions in both as-built and peak-aged (175 °C-1 h) conditions.
summary: This histogram illustrates the precipitate size distributions for AlSi7Mg samples, specifically comparing top and bottom regions across as-built and peak-aged conditions. By plotting the relative frequency of normalized equivalent diameter values, the figure highlights the microstructural variations resulting from different processing states and spatial locations within the cast material.

caption: Full-width at half-maximum (Δq) values derived from synchrotron XRD patterns of as-spun ribbons, calculated via nonlinear Voigt fitting of diffraction maxima.
summary: This figure displays the FWHM (Δq) values extracted from synchrotron XRD patterns of as-spun alloy ribbons. By applying a nonlinear Voigt fitting function to the diffraction maxima, the magnitudes of Δq were determined. Notably, the Ti60Zr15Si10B5Pt10 alloy exhibits the smallest Δq value, indicating a dense atomic structure despite its large negative heat of mixing.

caption: Schematic representation and 3D topography of the plasma-assisted-polished (PAP) SiC surface.
summary: This panel displays the 3D topography of SiC after undergoing plasma-assisted polishing. Compared to the plasma etched surface, this processing technique results in a distinctly better surface quality. The schematic highlights the structural improvements achieved through the PAP method, demonstrating its effectiveness in refining the SiC surface finish.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Pt 5 Pr electrodes recorded in Ar-saturated 0.1 M HClO4 electrolyte.
summary: This panel presents the cyclic voltammogram of Pt 5 Pr electrodes measured in an Ar-saturated 0.1 M HClO4 solution. The electrochemical data serves as a baseline for characterizing the electrode behavior, facilitating a direct comparison with polycrystalline Pt electrodes under identical experimental conditions to evaluate electrochemical performance.

caption: EBSD map of the HEA specimen annealed at 800 °C, revealing the grain structure and orientation distribution.
summary: This EBSD map illustrates the microstructural state of the high-entropy alloy after annealing at 800 °C. The image provides a visual representation of the grain morphology and crystallographic orientation distribution within the material, serving as a baseline for comparing the effects of different thermal processing temperatures on the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves comparing the electrochemical response of (i) NCG-PNC, (ii) NCCG-PNC, and (iii) NCCTG-PNC samples.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves were recorded to characterize the electrochemical behavior of NCG-PNC, NCCG-PNC, and NCCTG-PNC. These plots illustrate the redox activity and capacitive characteristics of the different PNC samples, allowing for a comparative assessment of their electrochemical performance and surface reaction kinetics under cyclic potential scanning conditions.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image revealing the size and shape of individual titanium carbide nanoparticles.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy imaging is utilized here to visualize the morphology of titanium carbide nanoparticles. This panel highlights the characteristic size and shape of the individual nanoparticles, which are essential components for the subsequent fabrication of the molybdenum-titanium carbide composite powders described in the study.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the random as-built sample extracted from the xy plane, displaying a near-random texture distribution.
summary: The random as-built sample shows an almost random texture distribution in the xy plane. Unlike the linear sample, this lack of preferred crystallographic orientation means that the dominance of (100) habit planes cannot be explained by texture, suggesting other factors govern the habit plane formation in these random-built samples.

caption: Phase distribution map highlighting the spatial arrangement of austenite and martensite phases within the printed NiTi alloy.
summary: This phase map illustrates the microstructural composition of the printed NiTi alloy. The analysis reveals a dominant austenite phase, which constitutes 46.6% of the total volume fraction, while the localized martensite phase accounts for 7.8% of the material volume within the analyzed region.

caption: Total density of states for Cu-13.9 at.% Zn calculated using a 4 × 4 × 4 k-point mesh.
summary: Total density of states for the Cu-13.9 at.% Zn alloy is presented, calculated with a 4 × 4 × 4 k-point mesh. This plot illustrates the electronic state distribution in the alloyed system, incorporating smearing parameters of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 eV to resolve the spectral features.

caption: Global root mean squared error of cross-validation (RMSECV) plotted against the number of components for the AC system regression.
summary: This plot illustrates the optimization of the AC system regression model by tracking the global root mean squared error of cross-validation (RMSECV). The data indicates that the error decreases progressively as the number of components increases, reaching an optimal performance level when the number of components is equal to eight.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curve of Cu foil in 1 M KOH at 40 °C, displaying oxidation peaks at 0.75 V, 1.0 V, and 1.16 V/RHE.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry curve for Cu foil in 1 M KOH at 40 °C reveals distinct oxidation peaks at 0.75 V, 1.0 V, and 1.16 V/RHE. These features indicate that the electrochemical oxidation potential range for copper under these specific experimental conditions extends from 0.65 to 1.2 V/RHE.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curve showing the rate of mass loss for pectin hydrogels across the temperature range.
summary: This DTG curve represents the derivative of the mass loss with respect to temperature for pectin hydrogels. By analyzing this plot in conjunction with the TG curve, it is confirmed that the material exhibits three specific stages of mass loss, highlighting the kinetics of the thermal degradation process.

caption: High-resolution XPS C 1s spectrum detailing the carbon chemical environments within the GCN@CD-A composite.
summary: High-resolution XPS analysis of the C 1s region was conducted to elucidate the specific chemical environments of carbon atoms in the GCN@CD-A composite. This detailed spectral data allows for the identification of various carbon-based functional groups and bonding states present on the surface of the material.

caption: Tabulated summary of the mechanical parameters defined for the material model.
summary: This table lists the specific mechanical parameters required for the material model calculations. By organizing these values, the panel provides a clear reference for the quantitative inputs used in the study, ensuring transparency regarding the mechanical properties assigned to the material during the simulation process.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the classification performance of the semi-supervised learning model trained on a limited set of labeled data.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the classification accuracy of a semi-supervised learning model. By utilizing a limited amount of labeled data during the training process, the model demonstrates its predictive performance. The matrix provides a visual breakdown of correct and incorrect classifications, serving as a key metric for evaluating the model's effectiveness.

caption: Initial reheating stage showing grain growth and nucleation of new grains, initiating the columnar-to-equiaxed transition.
summary: During the initial reheating phase, the microstructure begins to evolve as grain growth and new grain nucleation occur. This process initiates a columnar-to-equiaxed transition by transforming some of the previously formed lath structures into nearly equiaxed grains, as observed in experimental studies of the LPBF process.

caption: GWP 100a characterization results for a 12 mm wall thickness, presented as percentage values.
summary: This table displays the GWP 100a characterization results for a 12 mm wall thickness, expressed as percentages. These data points serve as an example of output analyses for the 12 mm case, providing a quantitative comparison against 1–5 mm Traditional FSAM benchmarks as reported in the study's findings.

caption: Experimental configuration for the real-world case study featuring a Polyga Compact S1 structured-light scanner and a rotary table.
summary: This experimental setup utilizes a Polyga Compact S1 structured-light scanner, which provides a scanning accuracy of 35 μm, to capture point cloud data from fabricated struts. The struts are mounted on a rotary table during the scanning process to ensure high-quality data acquisition for the real-world case study.

caption: Binary representation scheme where soft and hard materials are encoded as 0s and 1s for digital processing in simulation and model training.
summary: The simulation and forward prediction model training employ binary numbers to represent the material composition. Specifically, hard materials are represented by 1s and soft materials by 0s, creating a digital map that allows the computational model to interpret the structural arrangement of the composite materials effectively.

caption: Fast Fourier transform (FFT) result derived from the framed area in (c), representing the diffraction pattern of the matrix and precipitate.
summary: The FFT analysis of the framed area in (c) provides the diffraction pattern for the matrix and precipitate regions. This result serves as the foundation for identifying the crystalline phases present, specifically allowing for the subsequent measurement of interplanar spacings to confirm the material composition.

caption: Distribution of force chain values for the unanchored sample subjected to uniaxial compression.
summary: This histogram illustrates the statistical distribution of force chain values within an unanchored sample during uniaxial compression.
