caption: Red square highlighting the specific region selected for elemental mapping within the microstructure.
summary: The red square indicates the precise region selected for elemental analysis. This area was chosen to investigate the distribution of intermetallic phases within the material, as the EDS maps provide critical insights into the chemical composition and phase identification across the analyzed microstructure.

caption: Long-term stability assessment of CASM-S4 hydrogel electrical signals over 100 consecutive stretching cycles using a tensile machine and electrochemical workstation.
summary: To ensure the accuracy of strain measurements, 100 cycles of stretching were performed on CASM-S4 hydrogels. The resulting electrical signals were monitored using a tensile machine and an electrochemical workstation, demonstrating the material's robust performance and signal consistency over extended periods of mechanical fatigue and repeated deformation.

caption: Temperature-dependent evolution of the loss modulus (E'') for neat PETG and all composite materials, highlighting a relative increase in E'' attributed to frictional interactions.
summary: This panel illustrates the temperature-dependent evolution of the loss modulus (E'') for neat PETG and various composite materials. The results show a relative increase in E'', which is associated with frictional interactions occurring between the polymer chains and the added reinforcements within the composite structure during the DMA testing process.

caption: Combined influence of strut thickness and length on the peak crush force, identifying the maximum force at peak geometric parameters.
summary: This visualization displays the interdependence of strut thickness and strut length on the peak crush force of the auxetic structure. The combined effect shows that the highest PCF values are achieved when both the thickness and length parameters are at their maximum, providing a comprehensive view of the structural performance.

caption: Calculation and subsequent subtraction of a compensation polynomial applied to the DSC curve to correct for residual measurement deviations.
summary: In this stage, a compensation polynomial is calculated and subtracted from the measurement curve. This mathematical correction is essential for refining the DSC data, as it accounts for remaining deviations, ensuring the final curve accurately reflects the thermal properties of the material under investigation.

caption: Box charts illustrating the distribution of k-factor values obtained from cyclic measurements conducted at elevated temperatures.
summary: This box plot displays the k-factor values derived from cyclic measurements performed at higher temperatures. Each box chart represents a distinct cyclic measurement series, providing a statistical visualization of the k-factor distribution. These results characterize the material's performance consistency under thermal cycling conditions as referenced in the study.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the bottom region of the 2300W-DCT15 LMD sample, displaying nanotwins marked by yellow arrows and an inset SAED pattern along the [011] zone axis.
summary: The bottom region of the 2300W-DCT15 LMD build is presented in this bright-field TEM image, with nanotwins marked by yellow arrows. An inset SAED pattern along the [011] zone axis is included. Nanotwins are observed at the bottom portion of the DCT15 treated build, as expected.

caption: Correction factors, peak integrated intensities, and resulting pole figure intensities for the (200) diffraction peak, demonstrating the data processing steps applied to neutron experimental results.
summary: Panel b details the processing of neutron diffraction data for the (200) peak. It presents the correction factor, peak integrated intensities, and pole figure intensities. These components are critical for calculating experimental pole figures, ensuring that raw intensity data is properly adjusted for the specific measurement geometry and sample characteristics.

caption: Schematic representation of the MC carbide crystal structure.
summary: The crystal structure of the MC carbide identified at the grain boundary is illustrated in this panel. This structural model complements the diffraction data, providing a clear visualization of the atomic arrangement characteristic of the MC phase found within the solution-treated alloy microstructure.

caption: Schematic representation of the applied heat treatment cycles used to process the material.
summary: This schematic illustration provides a detailed overview of the heat treatment routes employed in the study. It serves as a visual guide to the specific thermal cycles applied to the specimens, ensuring clarity regarding the processing conditions and sequences described in the experimental methodology of the research.

caption: STEM image of the IN738LC alloy processed at 210 W and 1500 mm/s, showing the cellular dislocation structure and the path of an EDS line scan marked by an orange line.
summary: Representing the 210 W-1500 mm/s condition, this STEM image illustrates the cellular dislocation structure typical of the as-built alloy. An orange line indicates the specific path of an EDS line scan used to analyze the composition across the cell boundaries, which exhibit high dislocation density.

caption: Grain orientation map of K418 alloy processed via SLM at a laser power of 240 W, highlighting the vertical section grain distribution.
summary: Depicting the vertical section of K418 alloy produced at 240 W laser power, this grain orientation map reveals the influence of process parameters on microstructure. The solidification morphology is governed by the gradient temperature and solidification rate, demonstrating how varying laser power alters the grain structure during the SLM forming process.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram for high-strength steel wire, generated using dilatometric data with a heating rate of 100 °C/s, a peak temperature of 900 °C, and a 3-minute holding time.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of high-strength steel wire under specific thermal processing conditions. Derived from dilatometric measurements across cooling rates from 0.2 to 100 °C/s, the diagram confirms that austenite transformation to product phases is consistently completed by 200 °C for all tested cooling rates.

caption: STEM-DF image of the ODS Fe-Cr steel at higher magnification compared to panel (b), showing detailed microstructural morphology.
summary: Captured at a higher magnification than panel (b), this STEM-DF image provides a more detailed view of the ODS Fe-Cr steel's microstructural morphology. The technique effectively highlights the contrast between different phases, contributing to the overall assessment of the material's heterogeneous microstructure and the distribution of its constituent components.

caption: Local enlargement of the 5Ru alloy microstructure, confirming the absence of TCP phases and the relative stability of the γ′ phase distribution.
summary: Providing a local enlargement of the 5Ru alloy microstructure, this panel confirms the absence of TCP phase precipitation after 2000 hours of thermal exposure at 1100 °C. The image highlights the effectiveness of Ru addition in maintaining microstructural stability and inhibiting the degradation processes observed in lower-Ru content alloys.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing Fe, Ni, and Al atom maps and the Al–Ni 50 at.% iso-concentration surface for a 90% 316L composition sample processed at 950W-15IPM.
summary: This APT reconstruction of a 90% 316L sample processed at 950W-15IPM displays the spatial distribution of Fe, Ni, and Al atoms. The Al–Ni 50 at.% iso-concentration surface highlights the presence of B2 NiAl particles, demonstrating that higher energy density processing promotes the formation of these intermetallic precipitates.

caption: Underfocused bright-field TEM micrograph of the non-equiatomic thin film showing speckled Fresnel contrast indicative of surface roughening.
summary: This underfocused bright-field TEM micrograph of the non-equiatomic thin film, captured at a defocus degree of -0.95 μm, reveals surface roughening through characteristic speckled Fresnel contrast. The image provides detailed visualization of the nanocrystallites within the TEM lamella, confirming the presence of surface irregularities in the non-equiatomic material structure.

caption: Bode diagram showing impedance modulus versus frequency for IN718 in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution across temperatures from 30 to 80 °C.
summary: The Bode plot illustrates the impedance modulus versus frequency for IN718 in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. As temperature increases from 30 to 80 °C, the film resistance (Rf) decreases significantly from 878.13 to 95.09 Ω cm2, indicating enhanced Cl- ion penetration and reduced protective film resistance at higher temperatures.

caption: Modified Soderberg diagram for the l-shaped beam optimized under fatigue constraints using defective lattice 2.
summary: Representing the fatigue-constrained design, this modified Soderberg diagram incorporates defective lattice 2. The plot serves to illustrate the distinction in performance characteristics when the beam geometry is subjected to specific fatigue constraints, highlighting how the presence of the second defective lattice configuration influences the overall design safety margins.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of PLA showing mass loss as a function of temperature.
summary: The thermogravimetric analysis curve of PLA illustrates the thermal degradation behavior of the polymer. Experimental results indicate that PLA undergoes decomposition at 374 °C, while softening of the material is observed at approximately 80 °C. This data provides critical thermal stability information for processing the PLA-based material.

caption: Thermogravimetric (TG) and derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves for 3D printed AESO-IBOMA samples, comparing the unfilled reference material with composites loaded with 0.5, 1, and 2 wt% of BC.
summary: This figure displays the thermal degradation behavior of 3D printed AESO-IBOMA samples. It presents TG and DTG curves for the unfilled reference material alongside composites containing 0.5, 1, and 2 wt% of BC. These plots illustrate the mass loss and degradation rates of the materials under thermal analysis conditions.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the pure IN718 sample, revealing the distribution of nanoscale precipitates.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image of the pure IN718 sample provides a clear visualization of the fine, uniform dispersion of nanoscale γ′/γ″ precipitates. This imaging technique serves as the foundation for subsequent elemental mapping, supporting the identification of distinct precipitate morphologies within the heat-treated matrix.

caption: Plateau strength measurements across different lattice structures, providing insight into the energy absorption characteristics of the metamaterials.
summary: This bar chart displays the plateau strength of various lattice structures, which serves as a key metric for evaluating their energy absorption capabilities. By comparing these values alongside normalized stress data, the plot facilitates a comprehensive assessment of how different structural architectures influence the mechanical energy dissipation performance of these metamaterials.

caption: Simulated TTR diagram for the CM state at 750 °C compared with experimental data.
summary: This panel illustrates the time to rupture (TTR) diagram for the CM state at 750 °C. By plotting both simulated solid lines and experimental dashed lines, the figure provides a direct comparison to evaluate the performance of the simulation in predicting the rupture life of the CM material state.

caption: Detailed STEM view of the AD specimen illustrating the distribution of EDS analysis spots across the γ matrix and γ′ precipitates.
summary: Focusing on the AD specimen, this STEM image provides a detailed view of the EDS analysis spots. The analysis targets the γ matrix and γ′ precipitates in both the dendrite core and interdendritic regions, with spots 1-24 systematically distributed to characterize the chemical composition of these distinct microstructural features.

caption: Confocal microscopy images of hASCs in GCs, GC-BG, and GC-BGMA scaffolds, highlighting cell morphology and nucleus integrity via DAPI (blue) and Phalloidin (green) staining.
summary: Cellular morphology and nucleus integrity of hASCs are visualized using DAPI and Phalloidin staining to assess the impact of scaffold composition. The results confirm that the presence of BG or BGMA does not negatively affect the structural integrity or morphology of the cells, maintaining consistent cellular health across all tested conditions.

caption: Optical microscope image of the SMAW weld metal microstructure.
summary: This optical microscope image displays the microstructure of the weld metal produced via the shielded metal arc welding (SMAW) process. The visualization provides a clear view of the grain structure and phase distribution within the weld metal, serving as a primary characterization of the material's metallurgical state after welding.

caption: XGBoost (XGB) model confusion matrix evaluated on the unseen test set.
summary: XGBoost model classification accuracy is depicted in this confusion matrix using the unseen test set. The visualization maps predicted labels against actual labels, allowing for a comprehensive evaluation of the model's precision and recall across different categories, thereby demonstrating its overall predictive performance on new, unseen data.

caption: Polar plot showing the residual stress distribution for the specimen annealed at 573 K for 120 s, highlighting the reduction in stress magnitude.
summary: Annealing the specimen for 120 s at 573 K results in a significant reduction of residual stress. The polar plot demonstrates that the residual stress in the z-direction is nearly eliminated, reaching a maximum value of only 20 MPa, indicating a rapid relaxation of the initial compressive stress state.

caption: Full-pattern neutron diffractogram for the second HIP-treated condition, demonstrating the ongoing phase transformation and stability of the matrix.
summary: Representing the second HIP-treated condition, this diffraction pattern contributes to the comprehensive analysis of phase evolution in the WAAM material. By comparing these full-pattern diffractograms, the study tracks the stability of the FCC γ-austenite matrix and the reduction of secondary phases throughout the various HIP processing stages.

caption: Grain boundary size distribution for the D45 specimen fabricated via LPBF.
summary: This histogram illustrates the grain size distribution for the D45 specimen. The data represents the equivalent circle diameter of the grains within the Invar 36 alloy. With an average grain size of 66.19 μm, this plot characterizes the microstructural scale achieved under the D45 processing condition in the LPBF-fabricated material.

caption: EBSD grain structure map of the Sol_1135 condition in the XY cross-section, highlighting high-angle grain boundaries in black and twin boundaries in red.
summary: The Sol_1135 condition exhibits a distinct columnar grain structure as revealed by EBSD analysis. This map displays the grain morphology in the XY cross-section, with high-angle grain boundaries marked in black and twin boundaries in red, providing a clear visualization of the microstructural arrangement resulting from this specific processing condition.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 300 °C annealed sample microstructure, captured within a melt pool.
summary: Representing the microstructure inside a melt pool after 300 °C annealing, this bright-field TEM image allows for the assessment of solute silicon distribution. The measured silicon content in the alpha-Al matrix serves as a key indicator of the microstructural evolution occurring during this specific thermal treatment.

caption: Microscopic strain distribution profile across the surface of an LA-DED deposit during longitudinal tensile testing.
summary: This panel presents the microscopic strain distribution on the surface of an LA-DED deposit. Observed during longitudinal tensile testing, the map highlights the localized strain profile, allowing for a comparative analysis of the mechanical response and deformation patterns of the LA-DED material under stress at specific tensile test intervals.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms comparing the acrylate benchmark blend without oxime ester to the formulation containing 1 wt% oxime ester.
summary: This panel displays DSC curves for an acrylate benchmark blend, contrasting the thermal behavior of the neat resin against a formulation modified with 1 wt% oxime ester. The data illustrates the impact of the additive on the thermal polymerization characteristics of the acrylate system as measured by heat flow.

caption: Thermal expansion strain dL/L0 as a function of temperature for the V90 specimen, with the black dashed line denoting the linear extrapolation from 0 to 300 °C.
summary: The V90 specimen displays a thermal expansion strain dL/L0 curve relative to temperature. A black dashed line illustrates the linear extrapolation of the strain data between 0 °C and 300 °C, which helps in analyzing the thermal expansion characteristics of the LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy under these specific conditions.

caption: Advanced temperature distribution and morphology at t = 4.200 s, showing the molten pool nearing the end of the scan path.
summary: Representing the state at t = 4.200 s, this panel illustrates the temperature distribution and morphology as the scan approaches the end of the first layer. The thermal profile highlights the molten pool's behavior as it nears the boundary, influencing the final shape of the deposited layer.

caption: Binary phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium relationships within the plagioclase mineral series.
summary: This panel displays the binary phase diagram for the plagioclase mineral series, which is a key component of lunar regolith. The diagram delineates the equilibrium phase boundaries for the mineral series, providing essential thermodynamic data for understanding the crystallization and composition of plagioclase minerals found in lunar geological samples.

caption: Current density versus applied voltage plot for a vertical device with an 8-nm-thick C60 interlayer and Py top electrode, showing increased resistance and stability up to 1 V.
summary: The I-V curve for the 8-nm-thick C60 interlayer device reveals a more resistive state with an RA value of 50 Ω/cm2. The device exhibits improved stability under applied voltage up to 1 V, confirming that 5 nm represents the limiting thickness between short-circuited and stable resistive device operation.

caption: Oxygen exchange capacity profiles for in-situ reduced CAP-P and SUL-P samples over 10 repetitive oxidation and reduction cycles.
summary: This panel illustrates the cyclic reversibility of pre-reduced CAP-P and SUL-P powder samples. The plot tracks oxygen gain and loss across ten consecutive oxidation and reduction cycles, demonstrating that both materials maintain a constant, stable reversible performance throughout the entire testing duration under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the drill bit cutting edge after machining a wrought workpiece.
summary: This panel displays the SEM image and EDX spectrum of a drill bit used on a wrought workpiece. The analysis focuses on the cutting edge condition, providing visual and compositional data to evaluate the wear or material interaction resulting from the drilling process on this specific material state.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the as-printed HEA sample showing a cellular microstructure.
summary: The as-printed HEA sample exhibits a distinct cellular microstructure as visualized by HAADF-STEM imaging. This morphology is characterized by the presence of FCC phases, labeled as A, which are enriched in Ni, Al, and Ti, alongside BCC phases, labeled as B, which are enriched in Cr and Fe.

caption: Toughness values as a function of matrix grain size for cases 1 and 2, evaluated at a constant, optimal volume fraction of the second phase.
summary: This graph displays the relationship between toughness and matrix grain size for cases 1 and 2 at an optimal volume fraction. The results indicate that the matrix grain size has only a modest effect on the overall toughness of the composite material under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of (NiFeMo)99Cu1 permalloy processed via selective laser melting, displayed across a 2θ range of 20° to 100°.
summary: This XRD pattern characterizes the (NiFeMo)99Cu1 permalloy alloy produced through selective laser melting. The analysis covers a 2θ range from 20° to 100°, providing structural information about the material. Complementary EDS analysis confirms that no significant elemental segregation or precipitation occurred under these specific laser processing parameters.

caption: Simulated columnar grain morphology for the 2nd layer at the corner position of the curved component.
summary: This simulation depicts the columnar grain morphology at the corner position of the 2nd layer. The model captures the solidification microstructure, reflecting the thermal conditions at this specific location of the curved component, consistent with the 3-hour computational duration used for all simulated positions.

caption: Relationship between path pitch and the void fraction for dewaxed and sintered specimens.
summary: This graph displays the void fraction as a function of path pitch in dewaxed and sintered specimens. Comparison reveals that the void fraction is remarkably high for the 0.5 mm path pitch, exceeding 40% on average, while smaller path pitches like 0.3 mm are more prone to void formation.

caption: Ternary isothermal section at the transition peritectoid reaction temperature (γ+NiMo→Ni3Mo+P), illustrating the formation of γ+P+Ni3Mo and P+NiMo+Ni3Mo three-phase regions.
summary: Representing the ternary peritectic reaction occurring above 1073 K, this diagram depicts the phase equilibrium at the transition temperature. The reaction γ+NiMo→Ni3Mo+P leads to the emergence of distinct three-phase coexisting regions, specifically γ+P+Ni3Mo and P+NiMo+Ni3Mo, which are critical for understanding the reaction pathway in the Ni-Cr-Mo system.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of AlInN/GaN superlattices with an AlInN fraction of 0.992 grown on a GaN-on-sapphire substrate.
summary: This AFM image displays AlInN/GaN superlattices grown on a GaN-on-sapphire template with an AlInN fraction of 0.992. The surface morphology is influenced by the substrate, where pits from the GaN-on-sapphire template propagate through the superlattice structure during the growth process, resulting in observable surface pits.

caption: Areal capacity variations of Ni-Co electrodes as a function of applied current density, comparing pristine samples against those soaked in KOH solution.
summary: The areal capacity of the Ni-Co electrodes is plotted against varying current densities to assess rate capability. This graph demonstrates how the capacity changes for both pristine and soaked electrodes, highlighting the impact of KOH soaking on the electrochemical storage performance across different discharge rates.

caption: Longitudinal section view of the molten pool morphology along the scanning direction, showing the lower boundary of the scan track.
summary: This longitudinal section provides an enlarged view of the molten pool along the scanning direction. The lower boundary of the scan track is clearly visible, illustrating the processing stability of the material. This specific view serves as a reference for evaluating the molten pool change during the scanning process.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying parabolic rate constants as a function of inverse temperature for AM Rene 65 oxidized in air (full symbols) and Ar (empty symbols), compared against literature data for pure chromium, disk turbine alloys, and AM IN718.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the oxidation kinetics of AM Rene 65 in synthetic air and argon environments. By plotting parabolic rate constants against inverse temperature, the figure facilitates the calculation of activation energies. These experimental results are benchmarked against established literature values for pure chromium, disk turbine alloys, and AM IN718.

caption: AFM topography of Ni95-Fe5 cathode film showing a percolating network of alloy particles.
summary: Atomic force microscopy reveals the surface morphology of the Ni95-Fe5 cathode film. Under cathodic bias, the electrode structure breaks apart, forming a partially percolating network of alloy particles. This structural evolution highlights the instability of the Ni-Fe alloy composition when subjected to cathodic electrochemical conditions.

caption: Frequency distribution and cumulative frequency of pore parameters De, Fc, and Fs for 2205 DSS samples sintered at 1150 °C for 4 hours.
summary: This histogram displays the pore parameter distributions for 2205 DSS samples sintered at 1150 °C for 4 hours. Comparing this to the 1350 °C condition reveals that lower sintering temperatures result in a higher frequency of smaller pores around 5 μm, indicating that temperature significantly influences pore coalescence behavior.

caption: Polarization curves for Pt/Gr.C catalyst measured at 80 °C, 2.5/2.5 bar abs., and 100/100% RH before and after the accelerated stress test (AST), with an insert showing RHF and RH+ values derived from EIS fitting.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical performance of the Pt/Gr.C catalyst under wet operating conditions. Polarization curves recorded before and after the AST demonstrate the baseline stability of the catalyst. The included insert provides critical resistance parameters, RHF and RH+, calculated from EIS spectra, characterizing the electrode layer's ohmic and protonic resistance changes.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of contact lenses following immersion in a 0.75 mM gold precursor concentration.
summary: This plot displays the optical absorption characteristics of the hydrogel contact lens after treatment with a 0.75 mM gold precursor solution. The spectrum provides data on the light absorption properties resulting from the in situ gold reduction process within the hydrogel matrix at this specific concentration.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the interdendritic region in as-cast RR3010, illustrating the arrangement of Cr, Al, Co, Ni, Re, and Ta atoms.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the interdendritic region in as-cast RR3010, illustrating the arrangement of Cr, Al, Co, Ni, Re, and Ta atoms. The map clearly distinguishes the γ and γ’ phases, with the γ’ phase demarcated by Al, Ni, and Ta, and the γ matrix characterized by Cr, Co, and Re.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for the pH = 7 classification model, demonstrating that three distinct features contribute with relatively similar magnitudes to the model's decision-making process.
summary: The beeswarm plot for the pH = 7 class reveals that three features possess close effects on the model's classification. This behavior contrasts with the pH = 4.5 class, where a single feature, specifically the red channel, dominates the model's decision-making process for the sample classification.

caption: Cross-sectional SEM-SE micrograph of an EBM-processed sample ground with P600 SiC paper after 3000 h of oxidation in static lab air.
summary: This SEM-SE micrograph shows the cross-section of an EBM-processed sample after 3000 hours of oxidation at 850 °C in static lab air. The sample, ground with P600 SiC paper, exhibits significant structural degradation, characterized by voids ranging from 2 to 15 μm located in the Cr and δ-phase depletion zones.

caption: Bode phase plot for patterned CP-Ti and Ti–6Al–4V layers exposed to simulated severe inflammatory conditions for 1 and 12 h.
summary: This Bode phase plot shows the electrochemical response under severe inflammatory conditions. Phase angles of approximately 40° to 60° indicate the near-complete destruction of the passive film on the patterned specimens. These findings confirm the significantly reduced electrochemical stability and protective capacity of the surface layers in severe inflammatory environments.

caption: Pareto chart showing the standardized effects of 3D printing parameters on the densification strain of bone scaffolds.
summary: Displaying the standardized effects of 3D printing parameters on densification strain, this Pareto chart highlights the significance and correlation of printing variables. It provides a statistical overview of how different 3D printing parameters impact the densification strain behavior, which is critical for understanding the mechanical properties of bone scaffolds.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for 18Ni300 powder samples, illustrating the electrochemical behavior in ALF solution after 1 hour of OCP stabilization.
summary: Polarization curves for 18Ni300 powder demonstrate the electrochemical response in ALF solution at pH 4.5. Measurements were performed after a 1-hour stabilization period at the open circuit potential. The data, collected from at least duplicate samples, provides a baseline for evaluating the corrosion resistance of the 18Ni300 alloy powder.

caption: Non-linear fitting of the experimental Tafel plot for the HNWF1 sample using the Butler-Volmer equation to evaluate fitting accuracy.
summary: Experimental and fitted Tafel plots for sample HNWF1 are compared in this panel to evaluate the accuracy of the nonlinear fitting. By applying the Butler-Volmer equation, the non-linear fitting process demonstrates the correlation between the theoretical model and the actual electrochemical data obtained from the potentiometric test.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of MC3T3-E1 cells stained for live (green) and dead (red) populations after seeding on the membrane surfaces.
summary: Live/dead staining analysis reveals that the vast majority of MC3T3-E1 cells remain viable on all membrane surfaces. The images show predominantly green-stained live cells with minimal red-stained dead cells, confirming that the MNP-PCL membranes support high cell survival rates and maintain a biocompatible environment for the seeded cells.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength data for the four alloys, comparing vertical and horizontal specimen orientations at 750°C and 980°C.
summary: Ultimate tensile strength results are displayed for four alloys, highlighting the influence of orientation and temperature on material performance. By comparing vertical and horizontal samples at 750°C and 980°C, this panel illustrates the ultimate tensile strength variations observed during the tensile testing of the investigated alloy series.

caption: Nano-hardness profile plotted against depth from the milling surface for DD5 specimens exposed to 1000 °C.
summary: Nano-hardness values are measured at varying depths from the milling surface of DD5 superalloy specimens. This panel specifically illustrates the mechanical response of the SRX, CRX, and transition layers following thermal exposure at 1000 °C, providing insight into the subsurface hardening behavior under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Battery ageing trajectories showing capacity degradation over cycles for the Tongji dataset during charging and the MIT dataset during discharging.
summary: Battery ageing trajectories illustrate the capacity degradation over cycles for both the Tongji and MIT datasets. These plots demonstrate significant variability in battery ageing patterns, even among cells produced under identical conditions, highlighting the inherent complexity and stochastic nature of degradation processes observed across different experimental battery cycling datasets.

caption: Negative TOF-SIMS spectra comparing g-C3N4 and 0.05 HAPA-CN to identify surface chemical species.
summary: Negative TOF-SIMS spectra are utilized to compare the surface chemical composition of g-C3N4 and 0.05 HAPA-CN. This technique identifies the presence of specific ionic species on the sample surfaces, confirming the chemical modifications introduced during the synthesis of the HAPA-CN material compared to the pristine g-C3N4.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the fracture surface from the 1000 °C tensile sample, revealing grain size and deformation characteristics.
summary: The IPF map of the fracture surface at 1000 °C reveals larger, less deformed grains compared to room temperature samples. This microstructural observation correlates with the reduced elongation measured during the 1000 °C tensile test, indicating that grain size and deformation state significantly influence the material's high-temperature mechanical performance.

caption: Magnified view of the surface deviation vectors, emphasizing localized geometric variations between the nominal design and the actual XCT-scanned BCC surface.
summary: Focusing on a higher magnification of the surface deviation vectors, this panel emphasizes localized geometric variations between the nominal design and the actual XCT-scanned BCC surface. These detailed vector representations help characterize the part shrinkage and structural features that potentially influence the shearing fracture behavior of the BCC lattice.

caption: Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram illustrating the probability distribution of individual rays on a simulated sensor field at a 200 mm coaxial distance from the process zone, using a 450 nm wavelength across four distinct analyzed points.
summary: This Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram displays the probability distribution of ray scattering on a simulated sensor field at a 200 mm distance from the process zone. Utilizing a 450 nm wavelength, the plot reveals directional scattering dependencies related to the feed direction, incorporating all determined dome and process parameters.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the corrosion behavior of a bare 16Mn substrate and NiP amorphous coatings prepared at different deposition times in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the corrosion resistance of 16Mn substrate versus NiP amorphous coatings in 3.5 wt% NaCl. The NiP-3h sample exhibits improved corrosion resistance, with the corrosion potential shifting to a more noble value of -0.413V and the corrosion current density decreasing to 7.415 μA/cm2 compared to the substrate.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the paracetamol-PEG 4000 system constructed from second heating DSC data, displaying experimental liquidus points in blue, the ideal liquidus curve calculated via the Schroder-van Laar equation in red, and the eutectic invariant point marked by a black square.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the paracetamol-PEG 4000 system illustrates the thermal equilibrium behavior derived from DSC measurements. It compares experimental liquidus data against the theoretical Schroder-van Laar ideal model. The plot highlights the eutectic invariant point, providing a clear representation of the phase boundaries during the second heating cycle.

caption: Computational model representing the crash box structure used for evaluating energy absorption performance.
summary: This computational model illustrates the crash box structure utilized in the study. The primary objective of this simulation is to evaluate the energy absorption (EA) parameter, which serves as the fundamental metric for assessing the structural performance and deformation behavior of the crash box under simulated impact conditions.

caption: Selected cyclic voltammetry scans recorded during the electropolymerization of PANOA on an ITO electrode within a potential window of -0.2 to 1.1 V at a scan rate of 60 mV/s.
summary: Selected cyclic voltammetry scans illustrate the electrochemical growth of PANOA on an ITO substrate. The process was conducted in a solution containing 0.2 M aniline, 0.01 M o-aminophenol, and 0.6 M H2SO4, utilizing a potential window of -0.2 to 1.1 V at a scan rate of 60 mV/s over 20 cycles.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase volume fractions for the Fe–Co–Mo alloy system plotted against temperature.
summary: This panel displays the thermodynamic calculation results for the Fe–Co–Mo alloy, generated using JMatPro software. It illustrates the evolution of equilibrium phase volume fractions as a function of temperature, providing a quantitative overview of the phase stability and transformation behavior within this specific alloy system across the studied thermal range.

caption: Full-pattern neutron powder diffractogram of the as-printed WAAM specimen, showing indexed reflections for the FCC γ-austenite matrix and BCC δ-ferrite phase.
summary: The as-printed WAAM specimen exhibits distinct reflections from both the FCC γ-austenite matrix and the BCC δ-ferrite secondary phase. Full-pattern Rietveld analysis of this diffractogram estimates the δ-ferrite fraction at approximately 6.3%, which aligns well with independent microscopy-based analysis, confirming the phase composition of the as-printed material.

caption: Tensile engineering stress-strain curves for Al–18Si–10Cu–10Ni–5Mn–5Mg alloy comparing states before and after T6 heat treatment.
summary: Tensile engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the mechanical response of the Al–18Si–10Cu–10Ni–5Mn–5Mg alloy. Significant changes in the curves are observed following T6 heat treatment, indicating that the material exhibits relative brittleness under tensile loading conditions. These results highlight the impact of thermal processing on the alloy's tensile deformation behavior.

caption: XRD pattern of MPC3 synthesized via arc-melting, exhibiting a BCC Im3m crystal lattice with noticeable asymmetry in diffraction reflections at high angles.
summary: The XRD pattern for arc-melted MPC3 confirms a single-phase BCC Im3m crystal structure. A key feature observed in this diffraction data is the presence of noticeable asymmetry in the reflections at high angles, which characterizes the structural state of the material following the arc-melting synthesis process.

caption: Immunofluorescence imaging of OPN protein localization in BMSCs, showing specific protein expression in red/green and nuclear counterstaining in blue.
summary: The localization of the osteogenic-related protein OPN in BMSCs was examined using confocal laser scanning microscopy. The immunofluorescence analysis reveals the spatial distribution of OPN, marked by red or green fluorescence, while the blue-stained nuclei serve as a reference for cellular localization within the analyzed BMSC samples.

caption: Pole figures of {100}, {110}, and {111} crystal plane families for SLM-formed (NiFeMo)99Cu1 permalloy processed at a volume energy density of 101.59 J/mm3.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the crystallographic texture of SLM-formed (NiFeMo)99Cu1 permalloy processed at 101.59 J/mm3. Derived from EBSD data, the {100}, {110}, and {111} pole figures characterize the grain orientation distribution, providing insight into how high volume energy density influences the resulting crystal texture of the alloy.

caption: Phase shift versus frequency plot for the E1 PEO coating on AZ31 magnesium alloy, highlighting the presence of two distinct time constants between 1-10 Hz and 10^3-10^4 Hz after the first hour of testing.
summary: This Bode phase shift plot characterizes the E1 PEO coating on AZ31 magnesium alloy. After the first hour of exposure, the data reveals two separate time constants, with one appearing in the 1 to 10 Hz range and the second in the 10^3 to 10^4 Hz range, indicating complex electrochemical behavior.

caption: Temperature-displacement curves for as-deposited alloy 46 specimens, comparing samples oriented along the building direction (V) and the welding direction (H).
summary: This plot displays the temperature-displacement curves for as-deposited alloy 46 specimens oriented in the building direction (V) and welding direction (H). These curves serve as the primary data source for calculating the mean coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) values for the alloy across these two distinct specimen orientations.

caption: Atom probe tomography 3D reconstruction of the as-deformed alloy showing iso-compositional surfaces for 4.0 at.% Mg (blue) and 3.0 at.% Si (green) precipitates, accompanied by a histogram of the Mg/Si atomic ratio distribution.
summary: This 3D reconstruction displays the distribution of Mg-rich and Si-rich precipitates in the as-deformed state. The accompanying histogram reveals a broad peak in the Mg/Si ratio, indicating a diverse range of cluster compositions with a slight dominance of Mg-rich phases within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Localized dark-field TEM image of a 316L stainless steel rapid solidification cell.
summary: This dark-field TEM image displays the rapid solidification microstructure of a 316L stainless steel specimen. The visualization highlights the characteristic cellular morphology formed during the rapid solidification process, providing insight into the localized microstructural features of the base alloy before further modification or reinforcement.

caption: Calculated dispersion band diagram for a 30 percent infill RVE excited in the XZ-direction, highlighting the linear low-frequency region used for sound speed homogenization.
summary: This calculated band diagram for a 30 percent infill RVE, excited in the XZ-direction, displays the dispersion characteristics of the structure. The low-frequency region exhibits approximately linear slopes, indicated by dashed lines, which are utilized to calculate homogenized sound speeds for the material through the described homogenization approach.

caption: Enlarged view of the Ti64 substrate microstructure, highlighting specific grain boundaries and internal phase features.
summary: This enlarged optical micrograph offers a detailed examination of the Ti64 substrate microstructure. By focusing on a specific region, it reveals finer structural details, including grain boundaries and internal phase features, which are essential for understanding the material's overall microstructural characteristics as presented in the research.

caption: Comparison of experimental and predicted creep response curves for UT and HT90(2h) samples tested at 27 °C under a constant holding stress of 8 MPa.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep behavior of UT and HT90(2h) material samples subjected to a constant stress of 8 MPa at 27 °C. The experimental data are compared against predicted curves derived from optimized mathematical constants, demonstrating a high degree of agreement between the observed and modeled creep responses.

caption: Visualization of a 20 mm AlSi10Mg channel showing the removal of an obstruction and the restoration of a continuous void passage after etching.
summary: Imaging of a 20 mm length AlSi10Mg channel reveals the successful removal of a previously existing obstruction. Post-etching, the channel exhibits a continuous void passage, confirming that the bath etch process effectively clears internal blockages and improves the connectivity of the printed channel network within the sample.

caption: Local strain field distribution calculated for the BVP II specimen using a local approach method.
summary: This panel displays the local strain field distribution for the BVP II specimen. By employing a local approach, the visualization highlights specific strain concentrations within the material structure. These results provide a detailed view of the mechanical response, as supported by the corresponding strain field observations in the study.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the MHT-MS specimen crack path, revealing propagation in a crystallographic shearing mode under 850°C and 360 MPa conditions.
summary: This SEM image displays the crack path of an MHT-MS specimen tested at 850°C and 360 MPa. The visualization confirms that the crack propagates through the material following a typical crystallographic shearing mode, providing direct evidence of the failure mechanism under these specific high-temperature and high-stress test conditions.

caption: Elemental composition map of Chromium (Cr) showing its concentration at the globular matrix boundaries.
summary: Chromium distribution is visualized in this compositional map, confirming its presence at the boundaries of the globular tungsten matrix. Along with titanium and vanadium, chromium segregates away from the tungsten-rich globular regions, contributing to the distinct elemental partitioning observed throughout the arc-melted W-Ti-Cr-V alloy microstructure.

caption: Statistical distribution of geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) densities calculated using the kernel average misorientation (KAM)–based method.
summary: Representing the GND density distribution via the KAM-based method, this box plot summarizes the statistical spread of the data. Together with the Nye tensor results, this visualization facilitates a comprehensive assessment of measurement variability, highlighting the differences in density distributions obtained through distinct analytical approaches for the same material.

caption: EnvisionOne XL continuous stereolithography printer utilized for the fabrication of lattice structure samples.
summary: This photograph displays the EnvisionOne XL continuous stereolithography printer used in the study. The equipment was employed to manufacture five samples for each lattice structure design, utilizing EnvisionTec’s E-RigidForm Charcoal material. This setup represents the primary additive manufacturing platform for the experimental investigation of the printed lattice specimens.

caption: Temperature-dependent thermal expansion coefficients (CTE) showing experimental data points and least-squares fitted curves.
summary: Thermal expansion coefficients are plotted against temperature from 100 K to 673 K, demonstrating that the CTE is not constant. Experimental data points are fitted using Eq. (5) to characterize the expansion behavior. Manganese-containing alloys like MnFeNi and MnCoNi exhibit the highest CTE values, reaching approximately 21–23 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹ at 673 K.

caption: Enlarged cross-sectional view of the as-printed part highlighting characteristic voids, including raster gaps (A) and sub-perimeter voids (C).
summary: This enlarged cross-section identifies specific pore types within the printed heat sink. It clearly displays raster gaps, marked as A, resulting from sparse infill patterns, and sub-perimeter voids, marked as C, caused by physical limitations during the turning of rasters around the layer perimeter, which contribute to the overall internal porosity.

caption: Simulated multi-layer mixing pattern resulting from a scanning strategy with 45° angle increments between successive layers.
summary: This simulation visualizes the resulting mixing patterns for multiple layers deposited with 45° angle increments. The model demonstrates how specific scanning strategies influence the spatial distribution of materials across layers, providing a predictive understanding of the mixing behavior achieved through controlled rotation of the laser scanning path during the process.

caption: Tensile creep curves of the hot-extruded, forged, and heat-treated GH4151 superalloy at 750 °C under varying stress levels.
summary: Tensile creep curves for the GH4151 superalloy are shown at a constant temperature of 750 °C. Results demonstrate that increasing the applied stress level results in a constantly reduced creep rate and a decreased creep lifetime. Additionally, the creep rupture strain is observed to increase as the applied stress level decreases.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectra of SB+ME thermosets comparing the as-printed state with samples after the first and second reprocessing cycles.
summary: ATR-FTIR spectra for SB+ME thermosets are presented for the as-printed, first, and second reprocessing cycles. Analysis reveals an increased intensity of the peak at 1684 cm-1 in reprocessed samples compared to the original, suggesting that the observed reduction in mechanical properties may result from the opening of imine bonds.

caption: Vickers hardness contour map of the EPT-2 specimen displaying the hardness distribution resulting from the applied EPT treatment.
summary: Vickers hardness contour map of the EPT-2 specimen displaying the hardness distribution resulting from the applied EPT treatment. Observations confirm that the hardness of the sample decreases with increasing distance from the substrate, which is consistent with the overall trend of hardness variations observed in all samples in the figure.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) curve for the geopolymer sample prepared with a modulus of 1.4.
summary: This GCD curve displays the electrochemical performance of the geopolymer sample with a modulus of 1.4. The triangular behavior confirms high capacitance, though the voltage drop is more pronounced compared to the modulus 2 sample, which is attributed to differences in ion flow and alkali content within the material.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph and WDS elemental maps of Cu and Mn for the L 48 sample, where Mn segregation is observed within specific melt pools, while HAGB segregation is largely absent.
summary: In the L 48 sample, which represents a lower VED condition, the segregation of Cu and Mn at the high-angle grain boundaries is largely absent. However, red arrows highlight localized Mn segregation within specific melt pools, demonstrating that elemental distribution patterns vary significantly depending on the specific energy input parameters.

caption: Measured laser beam profiles captured by a CCD camera-based profiler across different scanner positions, revealing deviations from the ideal Gaussian shape due to optical chain misalignment.
summary: The corresponding beam shapes, as measured by the camera-based beam profiler, are reported in this panel. These experimental measurements demonstrate that small misalignments within the optical chain cause a noticeable deviation from the theoretical Gaussian profile in both defocus directions across the various scanner positions considered.

caption: XRD patterns of pure Mg samples immersed in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution for 1, 3, 7, and 14 days, showing the presence of Mg and Mg(OH)2 peaks.
summary: The XRD pattern for pure Mg reveals the presence of Mg and Mg(OH)2 peaks following immersion in a 0.9 wt% NaCl solution. Notably, the intensity of Mg(OH)2 diffraction peaks is relatively low after one day of immersion, with specific peaks observed at 2θ = 38° and 2θ = 68°.

caption: Confusion matrix for the CNN3 quality monitoring model, showing the correspondence between actual and predicted classification outcomes.
summary: The CNN3 model's classification performance is depicted through this confusion matrix on the testing set. With actual labels on the y-axis and predicted labels on the x-axis, the plot provides a quantitative assessment of the model's predictive accuracy for the specific quality monitoring tasks performed in the research.

caption: Arrhenius plot of integrated PL intensity for SQD and TQD layers in the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample as a function of inverse temperature.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the temperature-dependent integrated PL intensity for SQD and TQD layers in the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample. The experimental data, plotted against inverse temperature, are fitted to a thermal activation model, allowing for the extraction of parameters that describe the thermal quenching mechanisms of the quantum dot layers between 77 and 300 K.

caption: Local true strain rates versus global true strain for a multi-material 2D diamond lattice configuration, highlighting the strain rate response at the horizontal strut, frame, and connecting node under varying nominal strain rates.
summary: Representing the multi-material configuration, this panel illustrates local true strain rates versus global true strain at three critical locations. A notable discrepancy in strain rates within the horizontal strut is observed when comparing these multi-material results to the single-material configuration, highlighting the influence of material heterogeneity on lattice deformation behavior.

caption: Schematic representation illustrating the sequential fabrication process of the PHCZ scaffold.
summary: This schematic provides a visual overview of the scaffold preparation process. It serves as the foundational guide for understanding how the PHCZ scaffold is constructed, detailing the systematic steps involved in the fabrication workflow to ensure the final material structure is achieved as intended for subsequent characterization and testing.

caption: Experimental monotonic force-displacement curve for the HP geometry until failure, showing the transition to axial tension.
summary: Experimental monotonic loading of the HP geometry until failure reveals a distinct transition point where axial tension is carried directly by the struts. This curve characterizes the mechanical response of the HP configuration under uniaxial tensile stress, highlighting the structural behavior and load-bearing capacity prior to final material failure.

caption: Detailed view of composite powders with 42 wt% nano-Mo, highlighting the high-density nanoparticle coating on the powder surfaces.
summary: This detailed SEM view confirms the high-density coverage of nano-Mo particles on the Mo and Ti powder surfaces at a 42 wt% concentration. The image provides clear evidence of the extensive surface modification achieved at this higher loading level, consistent with the observed morphology in panel c.

caption: Reconstruction of the prior-β grains for the heat-treated Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy, highlighting the grain structure post-heat treatment.
summary: This reconstruction diagram depicts the prior-β grains of the heat-treated Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy. By analyzing the grain structure post-heat treatment, researchers can observe how the thermal cycle influences the parent grain morphology and the subsequent transformation into α phases and discontinuous β phases within the L-PBF processed alloy.

caption: Indentation load-displacement curve for the heat-treated (HT-1) powder sample.
summary: This panel displays the nanohardness load versus displacement curve for the HT-1 heat-treated powder. By measuring the load response during indentation with a Berkovich tip, the plot captures the specific mechanical deformation characteristics of the HT-1 condition, allowing for a direct comparison of hardness properties against other powder states.

caption: Emission spectra of trypsin (1 g/L) at 313 K for SL/trypsin mass ratios of 0–0.8 g/L, demonstrating the quenching behavior at the highest tested temperature.
summary: At 313 K, the fluorescence emission peak of trypsin at 327 nm continues to show a gradual decrease in intensity as the SL concentration increases. This confirms that the quenching effect persists across the entire temperature range of 298–313 K as SL interacts with the trypsin molecules.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PEB43-i synthesized with two equivalents of BnOH, demonstrating the predominance of the benzyloxide-terminated series [C] within the end-group mixture.
summary: The sample prepared with two equivalents of BnOH, PEB43-i, displays the same mixture of end-groups as the previous sample. However, the benzyloxide-terminated series [C] becomes the predominant species, clearly highlighting the significant influence of the coinitiator concentration on the final end-group composition of the polymer.

caption: Immunofluorescence micrographs of VSMC-based mono-culture μvessels stained for α-SMA (green), γ-H2AX (red), and DAPI (blue), highlighting elevated γ-H2AX-positive staining in vascular smooth muscle cells under simulated microgravity.
summary: Microscopic analysis of VSMC-based mono-culture μvessels using α-SMA, γ-H2AX, and DAPI staining demonstrates the impact of simulated microgravity on vascular smooth muscle cells. The results show a significant increase in γ-H2AX-positive staining, indicating that these cells undergo senescence when exposed to the simulated microgravity conditions for 48 hours.

caption: Creep strain rate versus stress for AISI 316L at 600 °C, showing data from standard creep, stress-relaxation, and SSRT tests assessed using the decoupled inelastic strain partitioning assumption.
summary: AISI 316L creep strain rate data at 600 °C is presented, incorporating standard creep, stress-relaxation, and SSRT results. The SSRT data is assessed using a decoupled assumption. Notably, stress-relaxation data points occasionally fall outside the trend band defined by the conventional creep tests, unlike the more consistent SSRT results.

caption: Quasi-static magnetic hysteresis loops for samples A and B, illustrating the magnetic coercivity (Hc) and magnetic remanence (Br) values.
summary: Quasi-static magnetic hysteresis loops for samples A and B are plotted to compare their magnetic properties. Key parameters, including magnetic coercivity (Hc) and magnetic remanence (Br), are explicitly denoted on the graph. These cycles demonstrate the magnetic response differences between the two samples based on their distinct chemical compositions.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the parabolic rate constants (kp) versus the reciprocal of absolute temperature (1/T) for the 900–1100 °C range.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the natural logarithm of the parabolic rate constants (kp) against the reciprocal of absolute temperature. By applying the Arrhenius equation to this linear relationship, the apparent activation energy for the oxidation process is derived, characterizing the temperature dependence of the material's oxidation kinetics.

caption: Top-down view of the process zone showing the starting points for Monte Carlo analysis rays, marked at 1 mm intervals along the axes.
summary: This top-view schematic identifies the specific starting coordinates for the Monte Carlo analysis rays. By marking these points at 1 mm intervals along the axes of the process zone, the figure provides a structured spatial grid necessary for executing the computational simulation of the ray paths.

caption: Hyperparameter optimisation results for the Extra Trees Regressor (ETR) algorithm, where sphere diameters represent the relative accuracy of the model.
summary: This panel displays the hyperparameter optimisation process for the ETR algorithm. The visualization uses sphere diameters to indicate the accuracy achieved by the model during the tuning phase. This systematic approach allows for the identification of optimal parameters to improve the predictive performance of the machine learning model.

caption: Equilibrium binary phase diagram of the U–Fe system illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions for pure uranium, U6Fe, UFe2, and pure iron phases.
summary: This equilibrium binary phase diagram of the U–Fe system defines the thermodynamic stability regions for pure uranium, U6Fe, UFe2, and pure iron. The diagram serves as a reference for identifying intermetallic phases like U6Fe and UFe2, which are observed in diffusion couples and consistent with established equilibrium phase data.

caption: Indentation depth versus applied force for cartilage samples treated with Ostenil® compared to PBS control.
summary: Cyclic bio-indentation experiments reveal that HA exposure via Ostenil® incubation leads to a significant decrease in indentation depth across the range of applied forces compared to the PBS control. This reduction in depth is particularly pronounced at forces exceeding 3.35 mN, indicating a change in material-level mechanical properties.

caption: Surface view of an LH scaffold at day 14, showing pore occlusion and a lack of cell bridging across the larger macropores compared to the LL variant.
summary: Surface imaging of the LH scaffold at day 14 shows pore occlusion and a distinct lack of cell bridging across the larger macropores. This observation contrasts with the LL scaffold, indicating that the scaffold pore size and filament spacing significantly influence the ability of cells to bridge across the open spaces.

caption: EDS mapping of Cu distribution in a simply blended Ti-2.9Cu powder mixture.
summary: This EDS map illustrates the Cu distribution within a simply blended Ti-2.9Cu powder feedstock. The visualization highlights the inhomogeneous nature of the Cu powder within the mixture, underscoring the inherent limitations of mechanical mixing techniques when preparing elemental powder blends for advanced manufacturing and in situ alloying applications.

caption: Macroscale deformation patterns and axial strain evolution (ϵyy) in the composite, comparing experimental DIC analysis with numerical microscale model results under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions.
summary: Panel b displays macroscale deformation and axial strain evolution, correlating experimental DIC strain maps with numerical model predictions. Under dynamic loading, the specimen exhibits a barreling effect and microcrack formation, with shear cracks highlighted by yellow dashed lines. These macroscale features contribute to the observed strain hardening and stress-bearing capacity changes.

caption: Autocorrelation comparison between predetermined input data and generated output data at a specific lag coordinate of (16, 0), showing a maximum absolute error of 0.045.
summary: This panel illustrates the autocorrelation comparison between predetermined input data and generated output data for a Monte Carlo simulation at the coordinate (16, 0). The results demonstrate that the proposed approach successfully generates realizations with autocorrelation properties very similar to the input, with a maximum observed absolute error of 0.045.

caption: Absorbance spectrum of RhB-HZ@CL showing a distinct absorption band with a maximum peak at 562 nm.
summary: The absorbance spectrum of RhB-HZ@CL is presented, highlighting a strong absorption band centered at 562 nm. This peak indicates the characteristic optical response of the material in the solution state, confirming the presence and activation of RhB-HZ within the CL matrix as described in the experimental analysis.

caption: Arrott plot of the LPBF block sample annealed for two weeks, focused on the Curie temperature region.
summary: This Arrott plot illustrates the magnetic behavior of the two-week annealed LPBF sample in the vicinity of the Curie temperature. By plotting the magnetic data in this format, the nature of the magnetic transition is evaluated, providing insight into the electronic and magnetic properties of the annealed alloy.

caption: Confusion matrices for training, validation, and test datasets comparing nozzle and side camera model performance, where blue indicates correct classifications and red denotes misclassifications.
summary: These confusion matrices visualize the predictive accuracy of the nozzle and side camera models across training, validation, and test datasets. The matrices highlight model performance, revealing that approximately 9% of good print images are misclassified as unclear in the nozzle model, providing a clear metric for evaluating classification success.

caption: Asymptotic profile of the rupture front ϕ for a crack under applied stress conditions of τ a p / μ = 0 . 2 and σ a p / μ = − 0 . 01 with a regularization parameter ϵ = 0 . 01.
summary: This simulation illustrates the asymptotic profile of the rupture front ϕ for a crack subjected to specific normalized shear and normal stresses. The profile demonstrates stabilization between the specified time intervals, confirming that the rupture front remains localized under the applied loading conditions of τ a p / μ = 0 . 2 and σ a p / μ = − 0 . 01.

caption: Fatigue life N f variation with layer thickness t, evaluated by the BNN model across the training range of 20 μm to 50 μm.
summary: Layer thickness t influences the fatigue life of the R90C90 specimens as predicted by the BNN model. The plot displays the trend within the 20 μm to 50 μm range, with black dashed lines representing extrapolations beyond the TDB data, providing a comprehensive view of how thickness affects the overall fatigue performance.

caption: Grid of positron beam spots at 21 keV energy, captured on a phosphorous screen positioned at the sample location, demonstrating a uniform mesh with 1.66 mm spacing.
summary: This image displays a grid of positron beam spots generated at 21 keV, recorded on a phosphorous screen located at the sample position. The visualization confirms a highly uniform mesh pattern with equidistant points spaced at 1.66 mm in both directions, as observed from outside the experimental chamber via camera.

caption: Tafel plot showing the nucleation potential as a function of the logarithm of lithiation current, demonstrating strong linear relationships across multiple temperatures.
summary: This Tafel plot illustrates the relationship between the nucleation potential and the logarithm of the lithiation current. The data exhibits strong linearity with R-squared values exceeding 0.99 across various temperatures. This confirms the correlation between the nucleation potential and the overpotential, supporting the analysis of Li-rich phase formation.

caption: Phase map of the S2 sample interlayer region.
summary: This phase map identifies the distribution of constituent phases within the S2 sample interlayer. By mapping the spatial arrangement of different phases, it provides insight into the phase composition and structural organization of the S2 interlayer region as determined by EBSD characterization.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the (Ni, Ti)-(Si, C) region showing the microstructural morphology of the phase.
summary: This bright field TEM image captures the (Ni, Ti)-(Si, C) region, providing a detailed view of the phase's microstructural morphology. The imaging technique was employed to further identify the products formed within this specific area, facilitating a clearer understanding of the material's structural characteristics and phase composition.

caption: Flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus plotted against temperature for the fifth ASA recycling course sample.
summary: DMA test results for the fifth ASA recycling course are displayed, showing the temperature dependence of flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus. This panel provides the necessary data to evaluate the viscoelastic properties of the material after five cycles of the ASA recycling process.

caption: WDS elemental mapping of the (Ti,V,Nb,Ta,W)C-12 vol% Ni cermet sintered at 1420 °C, showing the final elemental distribution.
summary: WDS elemental mapping of the (Ti,V,Nb,Ta,W)C-12 vol% Ni cermet sintered at 1420 °C presents the elemental distribution at this higher temperature. Comparison with the 1390 °C sample indicates a lower tungsten concentration in the binder phase, reflecting the temperature-dependent dissolution and redistribution of elements within the cermet microstructure.

caption: Transmitted energy attenuation plotted as a function of glass thickness for conditions with and without a 40 μm spacer.
summary: This plot illustrates the energy transmittance, defined as the ratio of transmitted energy to incident energy on the glass surface, against varying glass thickness. Data are presented for two experimental configurations: a no-spacer condition and a 40 μm gap condition, demonstrating the impact of the transparent receiver on energy attenuation.

caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 10% hemp content mix, showing a minimally left-skewed distribution with a negative mean and median.
summary: The 10% hemp content mix displays a probability distribution derived from Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. This distribution is characterized as minimally left-skewed, with the calculated mean and median values reflecting modest deviations from zero, indicating the environmental impact uncertainty associated with this specific hempcrete mix design.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot showing the dependence of ln[sinh(ασ)] on the inverse absolute temperature (1/T) for the α+β phase.
summary: The Arrhenius plot in panel c depicts the relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the flow stress and the inverse absolute temperature for the α+β phase. By analyzing the slope of this linear fit, the activation energy for the α+β phase is determined to be 299.61847 kJ mol⁻¹.

caption: Calculated Al–Mg–Si ternary phase diagram at 500 °C highlighting the shift of the eutectic composition toward the Al-rich region, as indicated by the measured composition of the eutectic network.
summary: This plot displays the measured eutectic network composition on the calculated Al–Mg–Si phase diagram. The location of this composition in the hypo-eutectic range indicates that rapid solidification and high undercooling conditions cause a shift in the eutectic composition toward an Al-rich portion of the ternary system.

caption: Raman spectrum of the FLAT-15 sample, highlighting the vibrational modes characteristic of the material composition.
summary: The Raman spectrum of the FLAT-15 sample is presented to characterize its vibrational properties. This spectroscopic analysis provides essential information regarding the molecular structure and chemical bonding present within the material, serving as a primary diagnostic tool for identifying the specific phases contained in the synthesized sample.

caption: Geometric configuration of the interlocking features, defined by diameter D* and a height of 80 µm.
summary: This panel details the geometry of the interlocking features, which consist of metal and polymeric cylindrical components. The design features a diameter denoted as D* and a fixed height of 80 µm, incorporating a single anchoring BLF to facilitate the mechanical interlocking mechanism analyzed in the simulation.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis of the AlSi10Mg alloy surface corresponding to Case 3 of multi-objective optimization.
summary: This EDS analysis provides compositional information for the AlSi10Mg alloy surface under Case 3 of the multi-objective optimization. The spectrum identifies the elemental distribution and chemical composition present on the surface, complementing the morphological observations made in the corresponding SEM image for this specific processing condition.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profile acquired from point 6 in panel (f), confirming the chemical composition of the observed oxide particles.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profile acquired from point 6 in the SEM map confirms the chemical composition of the oxide particles. These particles are solidified within the material after being involved in the melt by the shocking behavior of the molten pool during the GWZ941 alloy welding process.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves of Ni49.6Ti45.4Ta5 alloy subjected to various thermal cycles, illustrating the B2 ↔ B19' phase transformation behavior.
summary: The DSC curves for the Ni49.6Ti45.4Ta5 alloy demonstrate a single-step B2 ↔ B19' phase transformation during heating and cooling cycles following solution treatment. These thermal analysis results confirm the reversible martensitic transformation characteristics of the alloy across multiple thermal cycles, providing insight into the material's phase stability and transformation kinetics.

caption: STEM micrograph of a thin-walled specimen following creep rupture at 980 °C and 180 MPa, revealing the associated microscopic deformation characteristics.
summary: Captured via STEM, this image displays the microscopic deformation mechanism of a thin-walled specimen after creep rupture at 980 °C and 180 MPa. As part of the comprehensive STEM analysis of creep-ruptured specimens, this panel demonstrates how varying temperature and stress parameters influence the resulting microstructural deformation features.

caption: Electrical response of the sample at 150 K after cooling in a remnant magnetic field, illustrating the disappearance of the diode behavior.
summary: This panel illustrates the I-V response of the permalloy honeycomb lattice at 150 K following cooling in a remnant magnetic field. The results demonstrate a significant change in the electrical properties, specifically the disappearance of the diode behavior previously observed at higher temperatures and different magnetic field conditions.

caption: Concrete 3D printer system utilized for the additive manufacturing of artificial reef structures.
summary: Concrete 3D printing represents an advanced additive manufacturing technique for artificial reef fabrication. This automated process allows for the precise deposition of concrete layers to form complex reef geometries, illustrating the modern technological methods currently employed in the construction of artificial reefs for marine conservation.

caption: Coefficient of friction (CoF) versus time for L-PBFed HX samples tested under a 10 N loading condition.
summary: At the highest applied load of 10 N, the CoF fluctuations are significantly reduced for the L-PBFed HX samples. Furthermore, the differences in mean CoF values between the various samples become less pronounced, suggesting a convergence in friction performance under higher wear loading conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded at 5 mV s−1 for an on-chip μSC utilizing a 15 wt% PVA electrolyte in 1M H2SO4 across a temperature range from room temperature down to −20 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms at 5 mV s−1 illustrate the electrochemical performance of an on-chip μSC using a 15 wt% PVA electrolyte in 1M H2SO4. Data collected from room temperature to −20 °C reveal the temperature-dependent behavior of the PVA-based gel electrolyte compared to the PEGDA-based system.

caption: Electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity values for Al–10Ni alloys fabricated by CC, CDS, and CDS with Sm modification.
summary: Experimentally determined electrical and thermal conductivity values are shown for Al–10Ni alloys across three processing conditions. The data highlights the synergistic effects of combining CDS with Sm modification, demonstrating how these specific fabrication strategies influence the electrical and thermal transport properties compared to the baseline CC and CDS processing methods.

caption: Ni2p core-level spectrum of the calcined samples, indicating the presence of Ni2+ species without additional metallic content.
summary: The Ni2p spectra exhibit characteristic peaks ascribed to Ni2+ species. The absence of additional signals for metallic nickel confirms the oxidation state of the nickel in the calcined samples, indicating that the nickel is fully oxidized within the catalyst structure as expected for this synthesis method.

caption: Contour map showing the dependence of Ti6Al7Nb alloy melt pool track depth on laser power and scanning speed.
summary: Representing the melt pool depth, this contour map demonstrates the influence of laser power and scanning speed on the vertical dimension of the Ti6Al7Nb alloy tracks. The data indicates that these process parameters directly dictate the depth, with Marangoni convection effects resulting in deeper melt pools under specific conditions.

caption: Tafel polarization (E-logI) plot for amorphous-nanocrystalline and crystalline alloys measured in a 0.5 M H2SO4 solution.
summary: This panel presents the potentiodynamic polarization curves for amorphous-nanocrystalline and crystalline alloys evaluated in a 0.5 M H2SO4 acidic solution. The Tafel plot provides essential electrochemical data regarding the corrosion resistance and polarization kinetics of the tested alloys when exposed to a highly acidic environment.

caption: Comparison of experimental data and generated I-V curves for the PhotoWatt-PWP201 PV module, derived using TSEC methods and DDM parameters extracted via the SNF-TSEC approach.
summary: This panel displays the I-V curves for the PhotoWatt-PWP201 PV module generated using the TSEC method with DDM parameters extracted through the SNF-TSEC approach. The generated curves demonstrate a close match to the experimental data, validating the accuracy of the extracted physical parameters for the module's performance modeling.

caption: XCT-derived porosity distribution within the Voronoi lattice structure, demonstrating a sparse and widespread pore arrangement throughout the entire lattice volume.
summary: The Voronoi lattice structure displays 1173 pore counts that are sparsely distributed all over the structure. It shares identical defect volume, average pore diameter, and maximum/minimum pore dimensions with the BCC structure, specifically 0.15 mm3, 0.08 mm, 0.10 mm, and 0.05 mm respectively, as determined by XCT analysis.

caption: Schematic illustration of enhanced heat conduction in MoTi powder bed with 10% nano-Mo substitution, highlighting the formation of a transient liquid film.
summary: Incorporating 10% nano-Mo substitution promotes early melting, which facilitates the formation of a transient liquid film between powder particles. This liquid phase significantly enhances heat conduction throughout the powder bed compared to the base alloy, demonstrating how compositional modifications can effectively optimize thermal transport during the melting process.

caption: Second quadrant demagnetization curves comparing the initial sintered Nd-Fe-B magnet and the Pr-Tb-Al-Cu diffusion-processed magnet at 20 °C.
summary: This panel displays the second quadrant demagnetization curves for sintered Nd-Fe-B magnets at 20 °C. It highlights the magnetic performance differences between the initial magnet and the Pr-Tb-Al-Cu diffusion-processed variant, demonstrating that the grain boundary diffusion process effectively enhances the coercivity of the material compared to the initial state.

caption: Representation of the crystallographic texture for specimen S4, showing the orientation distribution within the melt pool.
summary: Panel d illustrates the texture of specimen S4, with colors indicating crystal orientation and blue arrows showing the solidification direction. At 300W laser power, the curvature at the melt pool bottom is increased, reflecting the influence of higher energy input on the solidification mechanism and resulting texture.

caption: Potentiostatic current density versus time plot for Fe-based AACs and 316L SS in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at an applied potential of 0 V SCE.
summary: Current density profiles for Fe-based AACs and 316L SS at 0 V SCE exhibit an initial rapid decrease followed by a slower decline. These curves eventually stabilize at a steady-state current density, as highlighted in the enlarged view, demonstrating the electrochemical stability of the materials in the saline environment.

caption: Grain size distribution map of the WAAM specimen showing a mean grain size of 249.20 μm.
