summary: The grain size distribution map for the WAAM specimen provides a quantitative assessment of the initial grain structure. With a mean grain size of 249.20 μm, this distribution serves as the reference point for evaluating the grain refinement achieved in the LHAM and LHAM-HT specimens during subsequent processing steps.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis performed on the 4th IN718 layer to determine elemental composition.
summary: This EDS analysis provides the elemental composition of the 4th IN718 layer. By identifying the chemical constituents present in the microstructure, this spectroscopic data complements the morphological observations, ensuring a thorough characterization of the as-deposited IN718 layers within the multi-material structure.

caption: Evolution of the coefficient of friction over time for LPBF and wrought Ti6Al4V alloys subjected to an applied potential of -0.2 V vs. SCE.
summary: The graph displays the coefficient of friction trends for LPBF and wrought Ti6Al4V alloys over the duration of the sliding test. By applying a potential of -0.2 V vs. SCE, the study captures the friction response of the alloys, facilitating a comparison of their tribological performance under these conditions.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe30 composite demonstrating a minimum value of -6.58 dB.
summary: The Fe30 composite displays a reflection loss profile with a minimum value of -6.58 dB. This result indicates an improvement in absorption performance compared to the 10 wt% loading, reflecting the impact of increased Fe content on the electromagnetic wave attenuation capabilities of the Fe/PLA/TPU composite material system.

caption: Total density of states for Cu-13.9 at.% Zn calculated using a 6 × 6 × 6 k-point mesh.
summary: Total density of states for the Cu-13.9 at.% Zn alloy is shown, calculated using a 6 × 6 × 6 k-point mesh. The data incorporates smearing parameters of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 eV, demonstrating the influence of mesh density on the electronic structure resolution for the alloyed material.

caption: Micro-CT scan of the 3DBCP-Ti implant site in the rabbit femur at 4 weeks, showing localized bone mineralization.
summary: Micro-CT analysis of the 3DBCP-Ti implant after 4 weeks of implantation illustrates the implant's position within the rabbit femur. The yellow dotted line marks the extent of bone mineralization, providing visual evidence of the bone-implant interface and the biological response to the 3DBCP-Ti material during the initial healing phase.

caption: Comparison of the QC-based vc model and phase-field simulation results for a process condition of 230A, 15V, 2.5 mm/s, and 4 wt% C0.
summary: This panel displays a comparison between the QC-based vc model and phase-field simulation results under specific processing parameters of 230A, 15V, 2.5 mm/s, and 4 wt% C0. These results are evaluated against the calculated values of vc and N points derived from the proposed model to validate the predictive accuracy.

caption: Stable phase diagram for the Ni-H2S-H2 system, illustrating the influence of sulfur-containing species on the thermodynamic stability of nickel phases.
summary: Focusing on the Ni-H2S-H2 system, this diagram displays the stability regions of nickel phases in the presence of hydrogen sulfide. It serves to characterize the thermodynamic behavior of nickel under sulfur-rich conditions, which is vital for predicting corrosion and degradation mechanisms in industrial environments containing H2S and H2.

caption: Al-rich segment of the Al-Pt binary phase diagram, detailing the equilibrium phase relationships in the aluminum-rich composition range.
summary: The Al-rich region of the Al-Pt binary phase diagram is presented, mapping the equilibrium phase relationships within the aluminum-rich composition range. This diagram provides a reference for the phase stability and structural transitions occurring in the Al-Pt system, consistent with established literature data for these specific binary alloys.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for Powder B, showing the structural characteristics of the material in the raw calcined condition and following sintering at 1,270 °C.
summary: X-ray diffraction patterns for Powder B, showing the structural characteristics of the material in the raw calcined condition and following sintering at 1,270 °C. The comparison between these diffraction profiles highlights the impact of the sintering process on the crystalline structure and phase composition of the powder.

caption: Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) lattice structure illustrating the close-packed arrangement.
summary: The Face-Centered Cubic (FCC) lattice is a traditional cubic design. Although these lattices are well-understood, TPMS structures are more complex and offer significant advantages over cubic lattice designs like the FCC, SC, and BCC configurations.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus actual ultimate tensile strength (UTS) values for as-cast samples, showing data points clustered along the linear line of best fit.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the UTS model for as-cast samples. The graphical relationship between predicted and actual responses demonstrates strong agreement, as evidenced by the linear distribution of data points clustered closely along the line of best fit, confirming the model's reliability for this mechanical property.

caption: Fatigue ratcheting and damage strain evolution for the annealed specimen with AB surface condition at 247 MPa.
summary: This panel illustrates the fatigue response of annealed specimens under AB surface conditions at a higher stress level of 247 MPa. The data tracks the concurrent development of fatigue ratcheting and damage strain, showing the rapid escalation of damage strain that signifies the onset of crack initiation and propagation.

caption: FT-IR spectra of hydrogel inks, highlighting intense peaks near 1100 cm⁻¹ for Gel@nHA–SA and Gel–SA groups, which confirm the successful incorporation of nHA.
summary: FT-IR spectroscopy was employed to analyze the chemical composition of the hydrogel inks. The observation of intense peaks around 1100 cm⁻¹ in the Gel@nHA–SA and Gel–SA groups provides definitive evidence for the presence of nHA within the hydrogel matrix, confirming the successful integration of the mineral component.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of AB, T5, and T6 samples after machining.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves are presented for the AB, T5, and T6 samples to evaluate their corrosion resistance after machining. These curves characterize the electrochemical response of the different microstructural states, with corresponding quantitative values derived from these plots summarized in subsequent data tables.

caption: Time-of-flight neutron diffraction spectrum for the 2Ta alloy at room temperature under zero stress conditions.
summary: This panel displays the time-of-flight neutron diffraction spectrum for the 2Ta alloy, recorded at room temperature without applied load. The data was analyzed to account for tertiary precipitates with a 48% volume fraction, confirming that lattice parameters remain insensitive to minor variations in the volume fraction of these phases.

caption: Isopleth section of the Cu-Ni-Pb ternary system spanning from a Cu:Pb ratio of 2:3 to a Ni:Pb ratio of 2:3, featuring an enlarged view of the Cu-rich region. The plot compares the current study's calculated liquidus (solid line) against previous parameter sets from [43] (dashed) and [44] (dotted), with experimental data points from [51–53] superimposed.
summary: This isopleth of the Cu-Ni-Pb system illustrates the liquidus temperature across a specific composition range. The current study's model provides improved agreement with experimental data from Nemilov and Strunina [52] compared to previous assessments. One outlier data point from [52] was excluded to prevent inaccurate depression of the lead-rich liquidus temperature.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Zr–Nb alloy system indicating the phase transformation temperatures used to select annealing parameters.
summary: The Zr–Nb binary phase diagram serves as the foundation for selecting five distinct annealing temperatures: 550, 650, 750, 850, and 950 °C. These temperatures were chosen based on critical phase transformation points to effectively tailor the microstructure of the fabricated Zr–2.5Nb alloy parts.

caption: Later stage reaction state of the Au-Ge-Cu-Ni joint superimposed on the 400 °C isothermal tetrahedron, illustrating the transformation of NiGe to Ni2Ge.
summary: During the later stage of the reaction, the interfacial products evolve as the previously formed NiGe phase transfers into the Ni2Ge phase. This progression is mapped onto the Au-Ge-Cu-Ni isothermal tetrahedron at 400 °C, highlighting the thermodynamic shift in the reaction products within the joint system.

caption: Cumulative frequency distribution of endurance data for plain cylindrical specimens subjected to stabilised stress levels derived from a 0.9% strain control test at R = 0, with individual data points annotated by their respective total exposure times in air at elevated temperatures.
summary: This plot displays endurance data for cylindrical specimens tested at a stabilised stress level determined by a 0.9% strain control test. The cumulative frequency distribution incorporates various load control tests, with each data point representing a specific specimen's total exposure time in air at elevated temperatures, ranging up to 27.5 hours.

caption: Additional selected area electron diffraction pattern from the FSAM zone, further characterizing the crystallographic features of the Al/Ni ESM without CuO.
summary: This SAED pattern serves as an additional diagnostic tool to characterize the crystallographic properties of the FSAM zone in the Al/Ni ESM. It provides further evidence of the structural state of the material, reinforcing the findings regarding the crystalline phases present in the sample without CuO particles.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves for BAC and CHBAC electrodes recorded at 5 mV s⁻¹ across an extended potential window of 0–1.0 V.
summary: At a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ and a 1.0 V potential window, the cyclic voltammetry curves illustrate the redox characteristics of the electrodes. The inclusion of the hydroquinone-quinone redox couple within this potential range highlights the differences in electrochemical performance between the BAC and CHBAC materials under these conditions.

caption: Upskin surface topography maps for S F 30 and S F 60 configurations showing parallel peaks and valleys.
summary: Upskin surface topography maps for S F 30 and S F 60 configurations reveal parallel peaks and valleys forming horizontal ridges, indicated by dashed lines. Additionally, small globules of adhered powder are visible on the surface, which contribute to the overall surface roughness of the overhanging bars.

caption: Combined image quality and inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the crack initiation zone, illustrating grain orientation distribution.
summary: The combined IQ and IPF map characterizes the grain orientations within the crack initiation zone of the AM/HIP/REC-2 specimen. This visualization helps identify the crystallographic texture and grain morphology, providing insight into the local microstructural conditions that contributed to the fatigue failure at 4.9 x 10^9 cycles.

caption: Bar chart comparing the wear volume of Inconel 718 samples, both uncoated and coated, when tested against Stellite 6, C-GC, and C-LMD alloys at 650 °C under a 23 N load, 20 Hz frequency, ±450 μm stroke, and 200k cycles.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the wear volume performance of Inconel 718 samples against various counterface alloys at 650 °C. By comparing uncoated and coated specimens under standardized tribological conditions—including a 23 N load and 200k cycles—the figure highlights the relative wear resistance provided by different coating materials on the Inconel counterface.

caption: EDS line scan profiles for O, Mg, Al, Si, Cr, and Fe across the bonding interface, demonstrating a non-homogeneous elemental distribution and a sharp chemical-composition gradient characteristic of the FSAM process.
summary: EDS line scans across the bonding interface show non-homogeneous distributions of O, Mg, Al, Si, Cr, and Fe. The sharp chemical-composition gradient observed indicates a distinct reaction zone. Compared to the AFED process, these profiles suggest a comparatively weaker locally formed interfacial q-glass region in the FSAM-processed sample.

caption: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//3D-printed LiCoO2 full cell measured at a 0.1C rate for the initial three cycles.
summary: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//3D-printed LiCoO2 full cell are presented for the first three cycles at a 0.1C rate. These curves characterize the initial electrochemical behavior and voltage response of the 3D-printed full cell architecture during the early stages of cycling.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of TPU/coumarin composites showing a broad absorption band in the 200–400 nm range.
summary: The UV-Vis absorption spectra of TPU/coumarin composites reveal a broad absorption band spanning the 200 to 400 nm wavelength range. This characteristic spectral feature is attributed to the intrinsic UV absorption properties of 7-hydroxy-4-methylcoumarin, confirming the successful incorporation and optical activity of the coumarin derivative within the TPU matrix.

caption: Relative spectral radiance response of the camera's red, green, and blue channels to blackbody radiation across three distinct temperature regimes, demonstrating the wavelength-dependent sensitivity of the CMOS sensor.
summary: Panel b displays the relative sensed spectral radiance for the red, green, and blue color channels as a function of blackbody temperature. These curves characterize the sensor's response to thermal radiation, providing the necessary data to calculate the ratio of red to green signals for temperature-dependent spectral analysis.

caption: Domain realignment driven by the combination of a bias magnetic field and applied mechanical stress, resulting in a detectable ΔB signal.
summary: When mechanical stress is applied to the composite, it is transferred to the Terfenol-D particles. This panel shows the remaining domains realigning in the direction of the stress, a process that manifests as a measurable ΔB signal, highlighting the material's sensitivity to mechanical loading under bias.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the 0.3 mm thick LB-PBF SS316L sample on the XZ plane after HT1 treatment.
summary: Presented is the XZ plane microstructure of a 0.3 mm thick LB-PBF SS316L sample subjected to HT1 conditions (1050 °C, 135 min). The thermal treatment reduces the density of smaller nucleating grains, a characteristic microstructural evolution observed in these thinner samples as they undergo the specified heat treatment process.

caption: Live/Dead staining images of SSCs Timp2 encapsulated within Gtn-HPA hydrogels, where white arrows highlight the presence of dead cells.
summary: Live/Dead staining images of SSCs Timp2 encapsulated within Gtn-HPA hydrogels, where white arrows highlight the presence of dead cells. Cultivation over 1, 4, and 7 days revealed no significant differences in survival rates, confirming that Gtn-HPA hydrogels provide a suitable 3D culture platform for human retinal progenitor cells without compromising viability.

caption: SAED pattern of the fcc A1 phase (indicated by a green dot) in the 1000HT sample compressed at 600 °C.
summary: This SAED pattern corresponds to the fcc A1 phase, marked by a green dot, within the 1000HT sample after 32% compression at 600 °C. The diffraction data was used to characterize the phase structure as part of the systematic TEM analysis of the deformed thin foil.

caption: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO model at 0 T magnetic induction intensity.
summary: This panel displays the pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO system at 0 T. The analysis focuses on the seven chemical order types—Co-Co, Co-Fe, Co-Mn, Cr-Cr, Cr-Mn, Cr-Ni, and Mn-Ni—establishing the baseline chemical ordering for the high CSRO system prior to magnetic field exposure.

caption: As-printed ClearVue fracture surface exhibiting violent failure, characterized by shattering and crack propagation across multiple planes.
summary: As-printed ClearVue samples show evidence of violent fracture, resulting in significant shattering and cracks extending across multiple planes. This morphology highlights the material's tendency toward brittle failure, with the fracture surface displaying complex crack patterns that deviate from the standard mirror, mist, and hackle features observed in other samples.

caption: Annotated photograph of the mechanical test frame and dual-camera imaging configuration, highlighting the whole-sample and interface-specific fields of view.
summary: This annotated photograph illustrates the experimental setup utilized for mechanical testing. The configuration incorporates a dual-camera imaging system designed to capture both the entire sample length outside the grips and a high-resolution view of the interface region, ensuring comprehensive observation of deformation and failure mechanisms during the mechanical tests.

caption: High-energy X-ray diffraction patterns collected with diffraction vectors perpendicular to the loading direction (⊥ LD) under varying tensile stress levels.
summary: Panel (b) presents high-energy X-ray diffraction patterns recorded during the tensile loading process. These patterns are integrated from an azimuthal angle of η = 0 ± 5°, capturing the material's structural evolution with diffraction vectors oriented perpendicular to the loading direction across different applied tensile stress states.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the electrodes recorded at various scan rates, demonstrating quasi-reversible redox behavior of the [Fe(CN)₆] 3−/4- probe.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms recorded at various scan rates illustrate the redox behavior of the [Fe(CN)₆] 3−/4- probe. The peak potential separation (ΔEₚ) varies across electrodes, with the Ref electrode showing the lowest value of 67.5 mV at 50 mV s⁻¹, indicating the fastest electron transfer kinetics among the tested samples.

caption: TEM investigation of Alloy 625 Plus following 418°C aging for 10,000 h, featuring <001>-zone diffraction patterns and bright/dark-field imaging of γ″ precipitates and ordered phases.
summary: After aging at 418°C for 10,000 h, Alloy 625 Plus maintains stable γ″ precipitates. The formation of a Pt2Mo-type ordered phase is evidenced by specific superlattice diffraction spots at {2/3 2/3 0}, {4/3 4/3 0}, and {2/3 4/3 0} positions within the <0 0 1>-zone TEM diffraction pattern.

caption: Axial strain field at fracture for the low temperature machined coupon N3.5M-40, demonstrating necking patterns.
summary: The DIC axial strain field for the low temperature machined coupon N3.5M-40 displays necking behavior similar to that observed in room temperature machined specimens. This indicates that the machining process maintains consistent deformation characteristics across different thermal conditions, with necking serving as the primary mechanism leading to fracture.

caption: Terahertz imaging of the bottom surface of the sample, illustrating the signal transmission and reflection characteristics from the underside.
summary: Presented here is the terahertz image of the sample's bottom surface. This view allows for the evaluation of the material's underside, highlighting how THz waves interact with the bottom interface. The image provides insight into the uniformity and structural integrity of the sample as viewed from the reverse side.

caption: Average friction coefficients derived from the stabilized regions of the experimental curves for distinct texture shapes.
summary: Average friction coefficients are derived from the stabilized regions of the experimental curves for distinct texture shapes. These mean values quantify the tribological performance of each geometry. By calculating these averages from the stabilized portions of the friction curves, the data provides a concise comparison of the different textures.

caption: DSC and M-T curves for bulk Ni-Mn-Ga alloy, featuring sharp martensitic transformation peaks and a narrow transformation range.
summary: Bulk Ni-Mn-Ga alloy exhibits sharp martensitic transformation in both DSC and M-T curves. While this sharpness suggests higher magnetocaloric effect potential according to the Maxwell equation, the resulting narrow working temperature range of 1–3 K limits its suitability for practical applications compared to processed particle alternatives.

caption: Tabulated values for the estimated radius and center coordinates of a precision ball derived from seven distinct scanning groups.
summary: This table presents the calculated average radius and center coordinates for a precision ball, determined through seven separate scanning groups. These quantitative results serve as the foundational calibration data for validating the sensor's accuracy in reconstructing the sphere's geometry during the experimental validation process.

caption: Friction-coefficient evolution over time for fish-scale textures featuring different apex angles (α).
summary: Friction-coefficient behavior is presented for textures with varying apex angles. As the angle α increases, the texture geometry transitions from an elongated configuration to a more compact one, which significantly alters the lubricant-flow patterns and pressure-distribution characteristics, thereby impacting the resulting friction coefficient of the fish-scale textured surface.

caption: Digital image correlation strain field map of an X-built specimen during tensile loading.
summary: Digital image correlation strain field map of an X-built specimen during tensile loading. DIC analyses demonstrate that the specimen exhibits a uniform strain field up to the 5% deformation level. This visualization provides a representative view of the material's deformation behavior and strain distribution under tensile stress conditions.

caption: Transversal spin-spin relaxation times (T2) in milliseconds for the three alginate hydrogel variants, illustrating the mean values and standard deviations alongside Tukey's test results indicating statistical differentiation.
summary: Transversal spin-spin relaxation times (T2) for H_Ca/Alg, H_Ba/Alg, and H_Zn/Alg hydrogels are presented as histograms. The data includes average values and standard deviations, with Tukey's test results highlighting significant differences between the materials. These measurements provide insight into the spin-spin relaxation dynamics within the crosslinked alginate network structure.

caption: Test results comparing predicted versus ground truth values for the UTS GPR model.
summary: Test results for the UTS GPR model are presented, illustrating the relationship between the predicted values and the ground truth data. This plot serves to validate the predictive performance of the model across the test dataset, providing a visual assessment of the accuracy of the UTS predictions.

caption: Extracted filler distribution map derived from the 2D tomography slice of the SiO2-SCF-PEEK composite.
summary: This panel illustrates the extracted filler distribution within the SiO2-SCF-PEEK composite, derived from the 2D tomography slice. By isolating the filler phase from the matrix and pores, this map provides a clear visualization of the spatial arrangement and dispersion of the fillers throughout the polymer matrix structure.

caption: Sheet diamond structure model generated with an iso-value C of 0.25, displayed as a 2x2x2 unit cell.
summary: Representing the sheet diamond structure at an iso-value C of 0.25, this 2x2x2 unit cell model demonstrates the geometric progression of the lattice. The design, created via Mathmod, highlights specific pore size adjustments in the green and blue subdomains compared to the baseline structure.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of binary Co–Mo alloy coating obtained at 50 mV s−1 in 1 M KOH, showing electrochemical response across the potential range of 1.0 to −0.58 V vs RHE.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram displays the electrochemical characteristics of the binary Co–Mo alloy coating in 1 M KOH at a 50 mV s−1 sweep rate. The potential range spans from 1.0 to −0.58 V vs RHE, reflecting the specific redox activity of the Co–Mo system under these experimental conditions.

caption: Comparative galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for pristine MXene, Cu-Ni-LDHs/MXene, and Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene at a constant current density of 1 mA cm⁻².
summary: Comparative galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for pristine MXene, Cu-Ni-LDHs/MXene, and Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene at a constant current density of 1 mA cm⁻². The enhanced electrochemical behavior of the Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene hybrid relative to the other materials is attributed to improved ion/electron transport and increased redox activity within the nanostructure.

caption: Temperature distribution at 10×10⁻⁴ s, highlighting the re-melting process and increased liquid phase volume following jet collapse.
summary: At 10×10⁻⁴ s, the simulation shows the laser re-melting the material, which increases the volume of the liquid phase. This stage follows the collapse of the previously formed liquid metal jet, demonstrating the dynamic nature of the melt pool transformation during the laser processing sequence at 250 W.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Fe-Ni-Mo system at 1600K, delineating the phase stability and equilibrium regions for the ternary alloy.
summary: The Fe-Ni-Mo ternary phase diagram at 1600K is illustrated in this panel. It delineates the various phase stability regions and equilibrium boundaries for the system, providing essential thermodynamic data for understanding the phase behavior of Fe-Ni-Mo alloys at this elevated temperature.

caption: Chemical composition data for alloy B in the as-atomized powder state, highlighting the measured concentrations of alloying elements and the lack of nitrogen content.
summary: This table displays the chemical composition of alloy B in the as-atomized powder condition. It lists the concentrations of all alloying elements measured in the particles. Consistent with the findings for alloy A, the analysis confirms that no detectable nitrogen is present in the particles of powder B.

caption: Cross-sectional view through the track of sample L4, revealing internal structural features and Cu distribution within the solidified melt pool.
summary: This cross-sectional view through the track of sample L4 provides detailed insight into the internal structural features of the solidified melt pool. The visualization highlights the distribution of Cu within the track, offering a clear perspective on the material's internal morphology as captured by microtomography experiments.

caption: Deconvoluted micro-photoluminescence emission spectrum of 10 mol% YSZ octet-truss lattices following a 1-hour annealing treatment at 600 °C.
summary: This panel displays the deconvoluted micro-photoluminescence emission spectrum for 10 mol% YSZ octet-truss lattices annealed at 600 °C for 1 hour. The data confirms that no carbon-related point defect emissions are present in the spectra, indicating that the emission characteristics remain independent of the specific annealing temperature applied to the lattice.

caption: STEM-EDS point scan spectrum acquired at location X, revealing a chemical composition dominated by nickel.
summary: STEM-EDS point analysis performed at location X confirms that the crack initiation site consists of approximately 98 wt% nickel. This chemical characterization highlights the presence of a Ni-rich surface nanoporosity that extends beneath the material surface, providing critical insight into the local composition where crack initiation occurs.

caption: High-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectrum of Ni2Fe1 nanofoams, detailing the chemical state of iron within the material.
summary: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of Fe in Ni2Fe1 nanofoams is shown in panel C. This analysis provides insight into the chemical state of iron within the nanofoam structure, complementing the nickel and boron spectral data to characterize the surface composition of the Ni2Fe1 catalyst.

caption: Experimental workflow illustrating the isolation of sEVs from BMSCs cultured in 2D dishes, 3D scaffolds without EMF, and 3D scaffolds with EMF stimulation.
summary: This schematic outlines the isolation process for sEVs derived from BMSCs under three distinct conditions: standard 2D culture, 3D scaffolds without EMF stimulation, and 3D scaffolds with EMF stimulation. These sEVs are essential for cell communication and tissue repair, serving as the foundation for subsequent characterization and biological analysis.

caption: Radar plot showing the statistical indicator scores for the testing dataset of the hybrid models.
summary: This radar plot illustrates the statistical performance indicators for the testing phase of the hybrid models. By mapping these scores, the figure facilitates a direct assessment of model generalization and accuracy, serving as a key component of the statistical evaluation provided for the suggested hybrid modeling approach.

caption: Hall-Petch relationship plot for high-purity Cu welded zones, illustrating the dependence of hardness on grain refinement.
summary: The Hall-Petch relationship for high-purity Cu after RFSSW processing is presented here. The data confirms that the Cu alloy follows the Hall-Petch relation, where grain refinement leads to a significant increase in hardness, highlighting a clear strengthening effect consistent with classical metallurgical theory for this material.

caption: HRTEM and selected area diffraction pattern (SADP) analysis of region A, confirming the Blackburn orientation relationship of (0001) α 2 // (111) γ.
summary: High-resolution TEM and selected area diffraction pattern analyses performed on region A confirm the specific Blackburn orientation relationship between the γ and α 2 phases. The identified (0001) α 2 // (111) γ relationship is consistent with previous findings, validating the crystallographic alignment within the observed lamellar colony structure.

caption: Final steady-state representation of dislocation pile-up, confirming the consistent accommodation of defects at grain boundaries.
summary: Representing the final stage of the steady-state analysis, this panel shows the continued pile-up of dislocations at grain boundaries. The simulation results consistently demonstrate that grain boundary dislocation accommodation is a fundamental feature of the polycrystalline fatigue process under the tested conditions, confirming the observed structural evolution.

caption: Energy dispersive spectroscopy analysis performed at the edge area of a microhole prior to femtosecond laser processing.
summary: Energy dispersive spectroscopy analysis performed at the edge area of a microhole prior to femtosecond laser processing. This measurement provides baseline compositional data for the microhole entrance region before the material undergoes laser-induced modification, serving as a reference point for evaluating the chemical changes induced by the subsequent processing steps.

caption: X-ray computed tomography visualization of the void distribution within a polyamide-6 (PA-6) CTS sample, highlighting the fracture plane region ahead of the crack tip.
summary: This X-ray computed tomography visualization displays the internal void content within a polyamide-6 CTS sample. Pink regions represent the voids, while green indicates the polymer matrix. The analysis focuses on the fracture plane ahead of the crack tip, providing a 3D spatial distribution used to calculate the total void content.

caption: Deconvolution results for the 27Al MAS NMR spectrum of potassium-activated slag 3 paste prepared with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 1.9.
summary: Potassium-activated slag 3 paste with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 1.9 is analyzed via 27Al MAS NMR spectroscopy. The deconvolution results reveal the coordination environment of aluminum in the activated paste, where a significant portion of Al remains in tetrahedral coordination, resonating at 62.5 ppm.

caption: FTIR spectrum of DPFNP showing characteristic absorption peaks associated with its chemical functional groups.
summary: The FTIR analysis of DPFNP is utilized to investigate the characteristic chemical composition of the material. By identifying specific absorption peaks, the spectrum provides insight into the functional groups present within the DPFNP structure, confirming its chemical identity and composition through this spectroscopic characterization technique.

caption: Arrott plot of the LPBF block sample annealed for one week, focused on the martensitic transformation temperature region.
summary: This Arrott plot displays magnetic data for the one-week annealed LPBF sample near the martensitic transformation temperature. The analysis reveals a second-order phase transition nature in this region, attributed to the presence of a weak first-order phase transition, as indicated by the specific magnetic behavior observed.

caption: Chronological sequence of optical frames capturing a single particle falling under laser beam irradiation, illustrating the formation and subsequent disintegration of a flame tail caused by vapor jetting.
summary: This sequence of optical micrographs tracks a single particle as it falls under laser irradiation. The images demonstrate the particle's acceleration driven by vapor jetting, which produces a distinct flame tail. Over time, this tail is observed to disintegrate, providing a clear visual record of the particle's dynamic behavior.

caption: Initial magnetization curves measured at room temperature for melt-mixed polypropylene-based thermoplastic magnetic composites containing various iron loadings, derived by averaging the ascending and descending branches of the VSM magnetization loops.
summary: Initial magnetization curves for melt-mixed polypropylene-based thermoplastic magnetic composites are presented, measured at room temperature using VSM. These curves represent the average magnetization between the ascending and descending branches of the hysteresis loops for various iron loadings, providing a baseline for characterizing the magnetic response of the composite materials.

caption: Optimized cantilever structure generated via BFTO with a 35% volume constraint and a 2 mm filter radius.
summary: This optimized cantilever structure, produced using the BFTO method with a 35% volume constraint and a 2 mm filter radius, exhibits smooth, well-defined boundaries. The minimum length scale for this specific design is measured at 2.33 mm, demonstrating the effectiveness of the optimization process in achieving structural integrity.

caption: Stress-free reference lattice profiles of the {311} plane along the height of the wall after SQA treatment, showing the variation across different orientations.
summary: This panel provides additional stress-free reference lattice profiles for the {311} plane in the SQA-treated wall. These results emphasize the complexity of obtaining a consistent d0 reference in neutron diffraction experiments, confirming that textured and coarse-grained microstructures introduce substantial variability that must be accounted for in diffraction-based stress analysis.

caption: Nominal stress-nominal strain curve for the gyroid solid network architecture.
summary: Mechanical response of the gyroid solid network is depicted through its nominal stress-nominal strain curve. Evaluated per ISO 13314, the data demonstrates how structural porosity influences performance. In alignment with the Gibson-Ashby model, the gyroid solid network exhibits a reduction in elastic modulus and yield strength as the relative density decreases.

caption: Force-displacement response of the CH specimen, illustrating the fit between experimental measurements and the phase field model.
summary: The force-displacement curve for the CH specimen is displayed, comparing experimental findings with the proposed phase field model. The results confirm that the numerical model provides a reliable representation of the mechanical behavior observed in the additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V titanium specimen.

caption: Magnified Nyquist plots comparing the capacitive loop radii of FeNiCr/PLA NC-Mg and FeNiCr/PLA NC-BB-Mg samples against H Mg and BB Mg controls.
summary: Magnified Nyquist plots highlight the differences in capacitive loop radii among the tested samples. The FeNiCr/PLA NC-Mg and FeNiCr/PLA NC-BB-Mg samples exhibit significantly higher radii compared to the H Mg and BB Mg control samples, indicating superior corrosion resistance for the nanocomposite-coated specimens in the electrochemical impedance analysis.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the relative TF–IDF scores of significant words and phrases, calculated with full weightage given to statistical relevance.
summary: This radar chart presents the relative TF–IDF scores for significant words and phrases, reflecting their statistical relevance in the research. With the TF-IDF weight set to 1.0, the plot highlights the most statistically significant terms, providing a weighted perspective on the core informatics findings regarding additively manufactured alloy research.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for the Ti–22Al-xNb (at%) alloy system, illustrating the phase stability regions as a function of niobium content.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the Ti–22Al-xNb alloy system serves as a reference for understanding the phase composition and stability of the material. It provides the necessary thermodynamic context to interpret the phase transitions observed in the Ti2AlNb alloy during thermal processing and heat treatment analysis.

caption: Comprehensive fatigue data for all tested specimens, including both IM and AM series, presented as normalised maximum stress versus number of cycles to failure.
summary: All collected fatigue data are shown here, comparing IM and AM specimens. Despite differences in manufacturing and relative density, all data points align within a single scatter band for a given load ratio. The curves, calculated with an inverse slope k = 20, confirm that normalised fatigue behavior is consistent across all series.

caption: Distribution of DFT prediction RMSE for individual part designs (bracket, clip, and plug) specifically for the N=9 factory scenario, highlighting performance variations based on the part type produced.
summary: This box plot displays the RMSE distribution for bracket, clip, and plug designs at N=9 factories. The analysis reveals that bracket factories contribute the most significantly to the average RMSE, indicating that the specific part design produced at a factory influences the overall prediction error of the global model.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of pure Mg and Ti–Mg composite in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution, highlighting a lower anodic corrosion current density for the composite.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves demonstrate the electrochemical corrosion characteristics of pure Mg and Ti–Mg composite in a 0.9 wt% NaCl solution. The results reveal that the Ti–Mg composite exhibits a lower anodic corrosion current density compared to pure Mg, indicating improved corrosion resistance for the composite material.

caption: Diffraction profile of the 1-19 peak from the parent CMSX-4 micropillar before compression, showing distinct reflections A and B corresponding to the γ' and γ phases.
summary: This diffraction profile displays the 1-19 peak of a parent CMSX-4 micropillar prior to mechanical testing. The presence of two distinct reflections, labeled A and B, confirms the coexistence of the γ' and γ phases within the microstructure, providing a baseline for subsequent analysis of dislocation density and phase behavior.

caption: 3D EBSD IPF-Z map for the sample processed with 67° hatch rotation, 200 W laser power, 70 µm hatch spacing, and 1000 mm/s scan speed.
summary: This EBSD IPF-Z map shows the microstructure resulting from 67° hatch rotation and 70 µm hatch spacing. The implementation of rotation interrupts columnar growth at each layer change, promoting grain refinement and the formation of equiaxed-like grains. Cracks are clearly delineated by the sharp black lines in the map.

caption: SEM micrograph of tool wear morphology for sample S-185 under cryogenic LCO2 cooling conditions.
summary: Scanning electron microscopy displays the tool wear morphology for sample S-185 under cryogenic LCO2 cooling. Observations indicate that this sample experiences reduced adhesion and abrasion relative to sample S-175, demonstrating a distinct difference in wear behavior and surface integrity between the two cryogenic cooling conditions tested.

caption: Excitation and fluorescence spectra of doped, UV-cured solid resin disks prepared by the hydrolytic pathway, with excitation collected at 380 nm.
summary: Doped and UV-cured solid samples prepared via the hydrolytic pathway are characterized here. The excitation spectra, collected at 380 nm, reveal an intense signal between 280 and 340 nm, which is consistent with the excitation of PPO, confirming the successful incorporation and photophysical activity of the dopant within the matrix.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern (SADP) of the M6C carbide phase.
summary: This panel displays the selected area electron diffraction pattern (SADP) of the M6C carbide phase. The diffraction pattern confirms the face-centered cubic structure of the M6C carbide, which possesses a lattice parameter of 1.07 nm and forms during the aging process of the alloy studied.

caption: Electrical resistivity as a function of temperature for the CrMnFeCoNiCu alloy film.
summary: Presented here is the temperature-dependent resistivity curve for the CrMnFeCoNiCu alloy film. The plot characterizes the electronic behavior of the Cu-doped Cantor alloy, showing the specific trend of resistivity changes as the temperature varies, which is essential for understanding the material's conductive characteristics in this high-entropy system.

caption: Young's modulus comparison between A-CNC and S-CNC composite resins.
summary: Young's modulus values are compared between A-CNC and S-CNC composite resins to evaluate the stiffness enhancement provided by each filler type. This metric helps quantify the efficiency of the reinforcement phase in improving the elastic response of the composite resin under low-strain conditions.

caption: Detailed STEM view of the LCF-tested specimen showing PSBs shearing through the matrix and precipitates, alongside the presence of deformation nanotwins.
summary: Detailed STEM imaging reveals that PSBs shear both the matrix and the precipitates during LCF testing at 650 °C. Additionally, the presence of deformation nanotwins is observed. Notably, this testing condition does not result in the coarsening of the precipitates, maintaining the structural integrity of the material's phase distribution.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the statistical significance of process parameters on porosity within the C1 section, identifying rotational speed as the primary influencing factor with a p-value of 0.021.
summary: This Pareto chart evaluates the impact of process conditions on porosity in the C1 section. Statistical analysis reveals that rotational speed is the sole significant factor affecting percentual density in the first 2 mm from the specimen surface, supported by a calculated p-value of 0.021.

caption: Backscattering Raman spectra of TiN powder after 40 hours of milling, comparing the background-corrected signals from the central grain region (blue) and the grain boundary region (red).
summary: Backscattering Raman spectra obtained from the TiN powder after 40 hours of milling reveal distinct vibrational features. The comparison between the central grain region and the grain boundary region highlights variations in the Raman response, which are consistent with characteristic features of off-stoichiometric TiN and computed TiN 1-x spectra.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the γ′ phase following compression at 1050 °C, indicating a highly randomized grain orientation state.
summary: Representing the γ′ phase orientation after deformation at 1050 °C, this map confirms a highly randomized grain orientation distribution. The progression of randomization from 1000 °C to 1050 °C highlights the temperature-dependent evolution of the microstructure during hot compression at a strain rate of 0.1 s⁻¹ and 0.6 strain.

caption: Fluorescence staining image of PA bacteria in 304ss culture medium after 24 hours, showing a high density of living bacteria.
summary: Fluorescence staining of the 304ss blank group reveals a large population of living PA bacteria after 24 hours of incubation. This panel serves as a control, demonstrating significant bacterial viability in the presence of 304ss compared to the reduced bacterial counts observed in the HEA coating environments.

caption: Overall thermal resistance plotted against solid thermal conductivity for varying water flowrates, accompanied by an inset schematic illustrating the thermal resistance network within a single fin.
summary: This plot displays the overall thermal resistance as a function of solid thermal conductivity across different water flowrates. The data, calculated using average heated surface and fluid temperatures, demonstrates how thermal performance varies with material properties. An inset schematic provides a visual representation of the thermal resistance network within an individual fin.

caption: Al–Cu equilibrium binary phase diagram illustrating the relationship between composition and solidification pathways, including liquidus and solidus temperatures.
summary: This panel displays the Al–Cu equilibrium binary phase diagram. It serves as a reference for understanding how composition gradients dictate local solidification pathways, influencing liquidus and solidus temperatures. The diagram is essential for evaluating whether the local Cu concentration in the melt pool remains hypoeutectic during the solidification process.

caption: Detailed creep dwell response for a 3-bar system (N=3) showing initial elastic loading during thermal ramp-up and subsequent stress relaxation at constant thermal load.
summary: The 3-bar system response is characterized by an initial elastic loading phase during thermal load increase, followed by stress relaxation at a fixed thermal load. During the dwell, stresses redistribute to allow long-term creep at a constant stress ratio, specifically illustrated for cases where bar 3 does not creep.

caption: Simulated time-to-rupture (TTR) diagram at 700 °C, plotted against experimental data from this work, ECCC datasheet 2017, and literature values from Speicher et al.
summary: This panel presents a simulated TTR diagram at 700 °C, providing a validation of the creep model. The simulation results are compared against established experimental data points from the ECCC 2017 datasheet and research by Speicher et al., demonstrating the model's capability to predict rupture times under these specific conditions.

caption: Radar map illustrating the absolute atomic size mismatch (|εri|) for equiatomic V25Nb25Mo25X25 alloys compared to the V33Nb33Mo34 reference system.
summary: This radar chart displays the absolute atomic size mismatch values for various alloying elements in V25Nb25Mo25X25 bcc RMPEAs. The data reveals that Zr, Hf, and Cr exhibit notably larger size mismatch values compared to other elements, a finding that aligns with established experimental measurements reported in the literature.

caption: 2D Gaussian-smoothed synchrotron XRD phase-evolution map of the Ti 2 Ni phase across the composite weld zone.
summary: This panel illustrates a 2D Gaussian-smoothed synchrotron XRD phase-evolution map of the Ti 2 Ni phase across the composite weld zone. The map characterizes the spatial evolution of this phase within the composite weld, utilizing high-flux monochromatic synchrotron radiation to resolve the complex phase distribution.

caption: Creep rate curves for NBSC specimens with diffusive cooling holes subjected to three different loading stress magnitudes.
summary: Creep rate behavior for NBSC specimens with diffusive cooling holes is shown under three different loading stress levels. The data reveals that the creep rate increases as the loading stress increases, demonstrating a clear correlation between applied stress and the rate of deformation in the tested plate specimens.

caption: Endogenous fluorescence emission spectra of MFGM-SL complexes subjected to varying sonication treatments.
summary: This plot displays the endogenous fluorescence spectra of MFGM protein, primarily composed of whey protein, and SL complexes under different sonication conditions. The spectral data illustrates how sonication influences the structural environment of the protein-lipid complex, providing insights into the conformational changes occurring within the MFGM-SL system during processing.

caption: Principal curvature map of the P + N stochastic TPMS surface with a characteristic length of 5 mm.
summary: This panel displays the principal curvature map for the P + N stochastic TPMS topology at a characteristic length of 5 mm. Calculations of principal curvature confirm that the mean curvature remains near zero, verifying the minimal surface character of the designed stochastic TPMS structure as described in the methodology.

caption: Operando XRD patterns for a single-track wall sample (sW) showing phase evolution: initial powder state (blue), high-temperature austenitic phase immediately post-lasing (orange), and final BCC phase (yellow).
summary: Operando synchrotron XRD measurements track the phase evolution of sW-type thin wall samples during PBF printing. The data displays the initial powder signal, the high-temperature austenitic structure observed immediately after laser melting, and the final transition back to a pure BCC phase, illustrating the rapid structural changes during the printing process.

caption: UMAP projection plot II illustrating the specific classification of deposits related to I-type magmatic sources.
summary: This UMAP plot focuses on the classification of deposits derived from I-type magmas. The clustering highlights the specific geochemical grouping of these deposits. Similarities in quartz trace-element patterns between adjacent clusters contribute to the observed overlaps, reflecting the underlying geochemical relationships within the I-type magma-related deposit dataset.

caption: TGA weight loss curves for synthesized TP and pectin, showing multi-stage degradation including water loss (50-150 °C) and polymer chain depolymerization (200-280 °C).
summary: TGA curves for both pectin and TP demonstrate multiple weight loss stages. Initial mass loss occurs between 50 and 150 °C due to water evaporation, followed by depolymerization of pectin chains between 200 and 280 °C, and subsequent decomposition, illustrating the thermal stability profile of the synthesized TP compared to pectin.

caption: Numerical and experimental load-displacement curves for the HV lattice structure.
summary: This panel displays the mechanical response of the HV lattice, comparing numerical predictions with experimental load-displacement data. The stress-strain response is derived from the load normalized by effective area and crosshead displacement normalized by gauge length, illustrating the structural performance of the HV configuration under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Convergence curve of the distortion constraint function g, where the blue reference line marks the zero-constraint boundary.
summary: This graph displays the convergence of the thermal-induced distortion constraint function g. The blue reference line indicates the zero-value threshold, allowing for the assessment of constraint satisfaction throughout the optimization process. The data confirms how the algorithm manages the distortion constraint to ensure the final design meets specified requirements.

caption: GOS map of the AMS specimen representing the grain orientation spread.
summary: Grain orientation spread is visualized in the AMS specimen using a GOS map. This technique highlights the internal misorientation within the large lamellae alpha grains, offering a detailed assessment of the initial microstructural state. The map is essential for understanding the uniformity of grain orientations before deformation.

caption: Hardness-displacement (H-h) curves recorded during the creep-holding phase at peak loads of 100, 200, and 300 mN.
summary: This plot illustrates the variation in material hardness as a function of displacement during creep deformation. The data captures the mechanical response of the specimen under sustained peak loads of 100, 200, and 300 mN, providing a clear visualization of how hardness evolves throughout the creep-holding regime of the nanoindentation test.

caption: Thermal response curves for PC-CF composites, showing heat flow measurements recorded during the second heating cycle for each recycling stage.
summary: Representing the thermal characteristics of PC-CF composites, this panel presents heat flow curves from the second heating scan. The data captures the thermal behavior of the material throughout multiple recycling stages, serving as a key component in the comparative analysis of the recycled polymer composite samples presented in the study.

caption: Proximity histogram derived from 16 at.% Cr iso-concentration surfaces showing the elemental distribution across γ″ precipitates in Alloy 625 Plus aged at 650 °C for 1000 h, highlighting comparable Nb and Ti concentrations and slight Al enrichment.
summary: This proximity histogram, generated from 16 at.% Cr iso-concentration surfaces, characterizes the γ″ precipitates in Alloy 625 Plus after 1000 h of aging at 650 °C. The data reveals that Nb and Ti concentrations are comparable, while Al exhibits only slight partitioning into the γ″ phase, with no significant Mo partitioning observed.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating hydrogen diffusivity as a function of inverse temperature for a GB-free Fe-Ni-Cr alloy, measured parallel to the composition gradient.
summary: Hydrogen diffusivity measured parallel to the composition gradient is shown in this Arrhenius plot. Results demonstrate that composition nonuniformity notably diminishes diffusivity in this orientation. The reduction is more pronounced for linear composition variations compared to stepwise variations, while maintaining a similar activation energy barrier of approximately 0.64 eV.

caption: Side surface topography maps at 90° overhang for 30 µm and 60 µm layer thicknesses.
summary: Side surface topography maps at a 90° overhang angle are presented for both 30 µm and 60 µm layer thicknesses. These maps illustrate the surface characteristics of the side walls of the bars, providing a visual comparison of the morphology resulting from the two different layer thickness processing parameters.

caption: Cr distribution map for the as-cast alloy subjected to multi-stage deformation at 1s-1 with 5 min holding.
summary: Cr elemental distribution is presented for the as-cast alloy after multi-stage deformation at 1s-1 with a 5-minute holding period. This compositional map illustrates the chromium distribution in the deformed sample, allowing for a comparison of how different deformation histories affect the chemical arrangement within the alloy's microstructure.

caption: XRD patterns obtained from the oxide layers of Fe–9Cr–0.1Ce alloy, identifying a multi-layered structure consisting of an outer Fe2O3 layer, an intermediate Fe3O4 layer, and an inner layer composed of FeO and FeCr2O4.
summary: XRD analysis of the oxide scales on Fe–9Cr–0.1Ce alloy confirms a complex, multi-layered composition. The scales are identified as having an outer Fe2O3 layer, an intermediate Fe3O4 layer, and an inner layer containing FeO and FeCr2O4, providing insight into the phase distribution within the oxidation products.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) and spatial charge density difference analysis for the relaxed pristine graphene/Ti system.
summary: The PDOS analysis of the relaxed pristine graphene/Ti system reveals significant orbital hybridization between carbon p-orbitals and titanium d-orbitals. This interaction is observed within the energy range of -0.84 eV to 5 eV relative to the Fermi level, highlighting the electronic coupling between the graphene substrate and the titanium atoms.

caption: TG-DSC thermal analysis profile of the pure PA filament.
summary: Thermal analysis of the pure PA filament via TG-DSC provides baseline data for comparison with composite materials. This measurement characterizes the thermal degradation behavior of the polymer matrix, establishing a reference point to confirm the mass fraction of carbon fiber reinforcements in subsequent composite filament analysis.

caption: TBL score radar chart displaying aggregated performance metrics across environmental, economic, and social sustainability pillars.
summary: Aggregated scores across environmental, economic, and social pillars are presented in this TBL radar chart. These findings support the HPI score observations, providing a comprehensive view of the sustainability performance for each PLA blend configuration across the three primary pillars of the Triple Bottom Line framework.

caption: Microstructure of A16 ceramic and corresponding Raman spectrum, identifying a third phase characterized as residual carbon within the silicon-silicon carbide matrix.
summary: The microstructure of A16 ceramic is shown alongside its Raman spectrum. The imaging reveals the presence of a distinct third phase within the silicon and silicon carbide matrix. Raman spectral analysis confirms that this additional phase is residual carbon, providing insight into the composition of the A16 ceramic after processing.

caption: Delta L/Lo versus temperature curves for materials in AB, T5, and T6 heat-treated conditions, showing initial tests as solid lines and repeated tests as dashed lines.
summary: This panel displays the thermal expansion behavior of materials subjected to AB, T5, and T6 heat treatments. The plot illustrates Delta L/Lo as a function of temperature, comparing initial test runs represented by solid lines against subsequent repeated tests shown as dashed lines to evaluate thermal stability and repeatability.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of FSA2 alloy viewed along the <110> zone axis after homogenization and aging at 900 °C for 5 h, with an inset showing the etched SE-SEM microstructure.
summary: This panel presents the microstructure of the FSA2 alloy following homogenization and aging at 900 °C for 5 hours. The main image is a bright-field TEM micrograph captured along the <110> zone axis, while the inset provides a complementary SE-SEM view of the etched surface, illustrating the material's structural state.

caption: Current density–voltage (J-V) characteristic curve of the MAPbI3-based perovskite solar cell, illustrating the agreement between experimental data and device simulation under standard AM1.5G illumination conditions.
summary: This panel presents the current density–voltage (J-V) characteristic curve for the MAPbI3-based solar cell device. The device simulator successfully reproduces the experimentally measured J-V curve when tested under standard AM1.5G light spectrum conditions, confirming the accuracy of the simulation model in predicting the electrical performance of the perovskite solar cell.

caption: CAD model of the SC_SB lattice topology featuring a solid cross-section for both columns and beams at 15% relative density.
summary: This CAD model depicts the SC_SB lattice topology, which utilizes solid cross-sections for both vertical columns and horizontal beams. Designed with a 15% relative density, this simple cubic unit cell was manufactured using laser powder bed fusion to facilitate a comparative assessment of its structural integrity and mechanical response.

caption: Top-down perspective of the Markforged MarkTwo® 3D printer printing head assembly.
summary: This top-down photograph displays the printing head of the Markforged MarkTwo® FDM printer used to fabricate CF-nylon laminates. The image highlights the specific hardware configuration of the printing head, providing a clear view of the mechanical components involved in the additive manufacturing process utilized throughout this experimental study.

caption: Linear fitting of the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the product of alpha and peak stress versus the inverse of absolute temperature.
summary: This Arrhenius plot shows the linear relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of alpha times peak stress and the inverse of absolute temperature. The slope of this fitted line is used to calculate specific material parameters, facilitating a deeper understanding of the temperature-dependent deformation mechanisms.

caption: SAXS pattern obtained from the dentin-like region of the printed structure, showing specific orientation characteristics.
summary: The SAXS pattern for the dentin-like region reveals distinct orientation characteristics. These diffraction results confirm that the nanorods within the dentin-like parts are successfully aligned according to the printing parameters, demonstrating the effectiveness of the shear-induced alignment process during the fabrication of the composite structure.

caption: Detected image reflected from the device with the quarter-wave plate QWP2 set to -90 degrees.
summary: Reflected pattern captured at a QWP2 angle of -90 degrees demonstrates the device's alignment capabilities. Analysis of this image confirms that the reflected pattern coincides with the original calibration image with subpixel accuracy, indicating that the mechanical rotation of the QWP2 does not negatively impact the alignment of acquired images.

caption: Austenite finish temperature (Af) parity plot depicting the comparison between GRNN model predictions and literature-reported values for NiTi alloys.
summary: The Af parity plot provides a visual comparison between the GRNN model's predicted austenite finish temperatures and experimental literature values. This analysis is essential for assessing the model's generalizability across various NiTi compositions, ensuring that the predicted phase transition temperatures align closely with the actual values reported in literature.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy image of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured on an acid-etched NT/TC4 substrate for 3 days, with nuclei (blue) and F-actin/vinculin (red) staining.
summary: Fluorescence imaging via confocal microscopy displays MC3T3-E1 cells on an acid-etched NT/TC4 substrate after a 3-day culture period. Staining of nuclei in blue and F-actin/vinculin in red allows for the observation of cellular attachment and cytoskeletal organization on the modified NT/TC4 surface compared to the control.

caption: SHAP dependence plot illustrating the impact of stress amplitude on fatigue life, with dot colors indicating the specimen state.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the influence of stress amplitude on fatigue life predictions. The color-coded dots represent different specimen states, highlighting the interaction between stress amplitude and state. As one of the two most important features, stress amplitude shows a significant effect on the fatigue life of the tested specimens.

caption: Magnified Inverse Pole Figure (IPF//LD) map derived from EBSD-HKL data, illustrating the crystallographic orientation of the grains within the specific area analyzed in panel a.
summary: This magnified IPF map displays the crystallographic orientation of grains relative to the loading direction for the area analyzed in panel a. It highlights a relatively soft grain, G1, surrounded by a combination of hard and soft grains, providing essential context for the observed dislocation density and slip behavior.

caption: Line-scan microanalysis profile conducted across an elongated Hf4 alloy precipitate.
summary: This figure presents a line-scan microanalysis performed along an elongated precipitate within an Hf4 alloy sample. The profile provides a detailed compositional assessment of the precipitate structure, illustrating the spatial distribution of elements across the feature as captured by the microanalysis technique to characterize the alloy's local chemical composition.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the primary structure at 500X magnification, illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The inverse pole figure map provides a detailed view of the primary structure of the selective laser melted specimen at 500X magnification. This visualization characterizes the crystallographic orientation of the grains within the material, offering insight into the primary structural arrangement resulting from the additive manufacturing process described in the study.

caption: Variance explained as a function of the number of components included in the PLSR model, showing a rapid increase from one to two components followed by a plateau.
summary: The PLSR model performance is evaluated by maximizing explained variance. As shown in the learning curve, retaining a single component recovers significant variance, but at least two components are required to surpass the 90% threshold, with no further benefit observed from including additional components beyond this point.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry cooling curves for PCL, TPU, and the UC polymer blend.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry cooling curves are displayed for PCL, TPU, and the UC polymer blend. These thermal analysis results are used to evaluate the crystallinity and miscibility of the developed UC filament, highlighting the differences in thermal response between the pure polymers and the composite blend.

caption: CALPHAD temperature–phase volume fraction plot for the 80 wt% GRCop42, 20 wt% Inconel 718 alloy system, showing the solidification path [C].
summary: This CALPHAD temperature–phase volume fraction plot illustrates the solidification path [C] for an alloy composed of 80 wt% GRCop42 and 20 wt% Inconel 718. The diagram predicts the formation of various intermetallic phases, including Cr-Ni-Mo P phase, NiNb5, BCC α Mo-Nb-Cr, and C14-Laves phases, within the Cu-deprived liquid during solidification.

caption: AFM image of a Py (5 nm)/C60 (25 nm) bilayer, illustrating the increased lateral grain size of the thicker C60 layer.
summary: This AFM image shows a Py (5 nm)/C60 (25 nm) bilayer. The lateral grain size of the C60 layer increases to an average of 25 nm compared to the 3 nm thick sample. Despite the increased thickness, the root-mean-square roughness remains stable between 0.4 and 0.5 nm.

caption: Simple cubic (SC) lattice structure representing a standard periodic design.
summary: The Simple cubic (SC) lattice is a conventional design. While simpler than TPMS structures, it serves as a baseline for comparison. TPMS structures are generally more complex and offer significant advantages over these traditional cubic lattice designs.

caption: Scatter plot of 10,000 generated samples produced by the G P ε ′ model, where individual points are color-coded according to their volumetric energy density (VED) values.
summary: This scatter plot visualizes the distribution of 10,000 samples generated by the G P ε ′ model. Each data point is color-coded based on its volumetric energy density (VED), providing a comprehensive overview of the model's generative output space and the resulting energy density characteristics across the entire sample set.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of MC3T3 cells on neat PLA and PLA/INT-WS₂ scaffolds 24 hours post-seeding, showing viable cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Live/dead staining performed 24 hours after seeding reveals a high proportion of viable cells on both neat PLA and PLA/INT-WS₂ surfaces. Fluorescence microscopy confirms successful cell attachment, with only a few dead cells observed, demonstrating that both materials support initial cell viability and attachment shortly after the seeding process.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of cell monolayers exposed to material extracts, demonstrating high cell viability across various samples.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of cell monolayers exposed to material extracts are presented to evaluate cell viability. Quantitative analysis indicates high and statistically comparable viability percentages for SC, CC, TQ, CS, and ZR samples, ranging from 93.2% to 98.8%. Statistical significance between materials is confirmed by ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD tests.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the CaO–SiO2–MgO–25%Al2O3 slag system, illustrating the equilibrium relationships between components.
summary: This ternary phase diagram represents the CaO–SiO2–MgO–25%Al2O3 slag system. Analysis of the diagram reveals that increasing the MgO content leads to a rise in the slag's melting temperature and a corresponding increase in slag viscosity, demonstrating the significant influence of composition on the thermal and rheological properties of the material.

caption: Mean yield surface of WAAM steel with superimposed red arrows indicating the direction of plastic strain development for various loading cases.
summary: This plot displays the mean yield surface for WAAM steel, derived from four individual yield surfaces to eliminate loading sequence effects. Red arrows are overlaid on the plot to illustrate the specific directions of plastic strain development observed across all tested loading cases, providing a comprehensive view of the material's plastic behavior.

caption: Fluorescence micrographs of hiPSC-LSCs in the epithelial layer on days 1, 6, and 12, highlighting ABCG2 expression to confirm the epithelial phenotype.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of the epithelial layer tracks hiPSC-LSCs on days 1, 6, and 12 post-printing. The inclusion of ABCG2 staining confirms the maintenance of the hiPSC-LSC phenotype within the bioprinted structure. Cell nuclei are visualized with Hoechst, providing a clear view of cell distribution and density over the observation period.

caption: Mean squared displacement (MSD) curves plotted against simulation time for MgO, Al2O3, ZrO2, CaO, TiO2, and La2O3 oxide nanoparticles during aggregation and collision processes.
summary: This plot illustrates the mean squared displacement (MSD) of six metal oxide nanoparticles as a function of simulation time. Derived from molecular dynamics trajectory data during aggregation and collision, the results indicate that MgO and CaO exhibit the highest diffusion coefficients, while Al2O3 displays the lowest, with La2O3, TiO2, and ZrO2 showing intermediate values.

caption: Three-point bending test configuration featuring support wedges and electrode probes.
summary: The three-point bending test setup is depicted, showing the specimen centered on two support wedges. Probes are attached directly to the electrode joints at the ends of the specimen, facilitating precise measurement and data acquisition during the mechanical loading process as the specimen undergoes controlled bending deformation.

caption: Transformation temperatures (Ms, Mf, Mp, As, Af, Ap) plotted against hatch spacing for samples H1-H5, showing a decreasing trend with larger hatch spacing.
summary: Transformation temperatures for samples H1-H5 are plotted against hatch spacing. The results demonstrate that increasing the hatch spacing from 28 to 85 micrometers leads to a consistent decrease in the transformation temperatures. This confirms that hatch spacing is a critical processing parameter influencing the thermal transformation behavior of the NiTi alloy.

caption: Residual stress intensity factor (SIF) curves as a function of normalised crack length for the tested Aluminium CT specimens.
summary: Calculated residual SIF values are presented against normalised crack length, revealing the magnitude of stress intensity during fatigue. These values are essential for evaluating the actual R-ratio. The data indicates that the discrepancy between stress intensity parameters is most significant at normalised crack lengths between 0.3 and 0.35.

caption: Final design iteration result for a density filter radius R to conductivity domain radius κ ratio of 1/6, exhibiting structural gaps.
summary: Shown here is the design result for a ratio of 1/6 between the density filter radius and the conductivity domain radius. Similar to the 1/4 ratio, this configuration is insufficient to define the internal feature length scales, leading to the presence of gaps in the final conductivity estimation design.

caption: Comparison of nanohardness and elastic modulus values measured via nanoindentation on the polished top surface of TiSS samples relative to printed Ti6Al4V reference material.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of mechanical properties, specifically nanohardness and elastic modulus, obtained through nanoindentation on the top surface of TiSS samples. By including printed Ti6Al4V as a benchmark, the data evaluates the influence of rescanning processes on the mechanical performance of the material perpendicular to the build direction.

caption: Resistance repeatability plot under saturated humidity conditions, highlighting minor transient noise attributed to droplet dynamics.
summary: The sensor exhibits consistent resistance repeatability when exposed to saturated humidity. Although transient noise, characterized by ±1.5% resistance fluctuations, occurs due to rapid droplet condensation and evaporation, the sensor maintains its original resistance response performance, demonstrating resilience against environmental moisture variations during testing.

caption: Schematic representation of the Laser Metal Deposition (LMD) additive manufacturing process, illustrating the layer-by-layer deposition of melted powders delivered via a nozzle.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Laser Metal Deposition (LMD) additive manufacturing process, which involves the layer-by-layer deposition of melted powders. The diagram highlights the delivery of powder and gas through a deposition nozzle, which can be configured in various shapes to facilitate the manufacturing of components.

caption: Intersection-over-Union (IoU) metric plotted against the volume of training data for models initialized with random weights compared to those transfer-learned from FLOW-3D and Eagar-Tsai melt pool simulations.
summary: This plot illustrates the IoU performance metric as a function of training data quantity. It compares models using random weight initialization against those pre-trained on FLOW-3D and Eagar-Tsai simulation datasets. The data demonstrates that pre-training significantly enhances the IoU score of predicted cross-sections compared to randomly initialized networks.

caption: Distribution of longitudinal residual stress in sample S4 100, determined through synchrotron X-ray diffraction analysis.
summary: Residual stress distribution for sample S4 100 is characterized using synchrotron X-ray diffraction. This method provides a detailed mapping of the longitudinal stress components within the thin-wall structure, complementing the hole-drilling measurements used for lower-layer samples by providing high-resolution data for the 100-layer specimen configuration.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) strain maps illustrating the deformation behavior of straight-edged AB-S, FHP-S, and SHP-S samples within a nominal strain range of 1% to 10%.
summary: Digital image correlation strain maps visualize the localized deformation patterns in straight-edged AB-S, FHP-S, and SHP-S samples during tensile loading between 1% and 10% nominal strain. These maps reveal distinct strain localization behaviors across the different sample types, highlighting variations in material response that are critical for evaluating mechanical performance.

caption: Bright-field TEM overview of the cross-sectional tribo-layer formed at 200℃ and 150 N.
summary: This bright-field TEM overview displays the cross-sectional structure of the tribo-layer formed at 200℃ and 150 N. The total thickness of the tribo-layer reaches 4.83 µm, demonstrating that elevated temperatures significantly enhance the growth of the layer compared to lower temperature conditions.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics of CNF and CNF/CoNi nanocomposites measured via the four-point probe method.
summary: The current-voltage curves for CNF and CNF/CoNi nanocomposites were obtained using the four-point probe method. These electrical measurements provide fundamental data on the conductive behavior of the materials, which is essential for evaluating their potential performance in applications such as electromagnetic interference shielding as discussed in the study.

caption: Time-lapse snapshots showing the locomotion and actuation behavior of a biohybrid soft robot, featuring sarcomeric longitudinal muscle layouts that guide contraction dynamics parallel to CNT/GelMA hydrogel lines during a single-stroke motion.
summary: Biohybrid soft robot actuation is illustrated through sequential snapshots of locomotion. The sarcomeric longitudinal muscle arrangement within the CNT/GelMA hydrogel structure is shown to guide the robot's dynamics, enabling effective soft robotic motion during upward contraction cycles, as observed in a one-second recording on day seven.

caption: Detailed view of the (111) and (110) diffraction peaks highlighting the phase transformation sequence from liquid to austenite and finally to martensite (α’).
summary: Focusing on the (111) and (110) peaks, this panel highlights the specific phase transformation from liquid to austenite and then to α’-martensite. In situ measurements demonstrate the direct formation of austenite from the liquid phase, with no evidence of initial δ-ferrite formation observed during the L-PBF process.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental map showing the distribution of Ni in the Ni60 alloy, demonstrating that the γ-phase is rich in nickel.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping of the Ni60 alloy reveals the spatial distribution of nickel. The results demonstrate that the γ-phase is enriched with nickel compared to the surrounding martensite. This compositional analysis confirms the chemical partitioning between the phases observed in the microstructure of the Ni60 model material.

caption: Differential Raman spectra obtained by subtracting the pure PETG signal from the total Raman spectra of PETG/RFPG composites (0.0 wt%–12.0 wt%).
summary: Presented here is the outcome of subtracting the neat PETG Raman spectrum from the spectra of all PETG/RFPG composite samples.
