This differential analysis isolates the spectral contributions of the RFPG filler within the polymer matrix, allowing for a clearer observation of the specific Raman bands associated with the additive.

caption: Horizontal strain εxx distribution for a corrugated surface (d/l = 0.427) at a final shearing state of u/L = 0.1.
summary: Displaying the horizontal strain distribution for a d/l = 0.427 corrugated surface at u/L = 0.1, this DIC map reveals the strain field at the final deformation stage. The observed shear zones, characterized by alternating contraction and dilation, demonstrate the impact of high-corrugation geometry on the interface micromechanics of the granular material.

caption: Cumulative number of dissolved metal elements from NiCr alloys into the salt medium as a function of simulation time, with shaded regions representing standard deviation.
summary: This panel illustrates the number of metal elements dissolved in the salt over the course of the simulation. The data shows the progression of metal dissolution, which is linked to the selective dissolution of chromium caused by fluorine chemisorption on the alloy surface as observed in the simulation.

caption: Fatigue life N f as a function of hatch spacing h, demonstrating that smaller values correlate with a superior fatigue response.
summary: Hatch spacing h is a critical parameter for fatigue life, where smaller values are shown to achieve a better fatigue response. The BNN model evaluates this relationship within the training range of 60 μm to 150 μm, with dashed lines indicating predictions made outside the observed TDB data range.

caption: EELS elemental distribution map of the cuboidal nanoparticle, highlighting an oxide core surrounded by a nitride shell.
summary: EELS elemental mapping of the cuboidal nanoparticle in the TiN/5/800 alloy provides clear evidence of chemical segregation. The analysis reveals a core-shell structure where the inner region is composed of oxide species, while the outer shell consists of a nitride phase, confirming the heterogeneous nature of the particle.

caption: Neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain in the cold-machined part.
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain within the cold-machined part. The data serves as an experimental baseline for evaluating the accuracy of numerical models, specifically highlighting the characteristic strain distribution features observed in the physical specimen during the experimental analysis.

caption: Arrhenius plots illustrating the temperature-dependent ionic conductivity behavior of 3D-printed PVDF/LLZTO composite electrolytes with different LLZTO loading levels.
summary: Arrhenius plots are presented for the 3D-printed PVDF/LLZTO composite electrolytes, highlighting the relationship between ionic conductivity and temperature for various LLZTO contents. These plots facilitate the determination of activation energies for ion transport, demonstrating how the incorporation of LLZTO filler affects the temperature-dependent electrochemical behavior of the printed composite electrolyte system.

caption: Non-site-specific atom probe tomography Cu atom map showing a 20 × 20 × 20 nm selection from the CA dataset.
summary: The Cu atom map for the CA heat-treated sample illustrates the spatial distribution of copper atoms within the microstructure. By examining these non-site-specific APT datasets, the study characterizes how the CA heat treatment influences the behavior and local concentration of Cu within the High N 17–4 alloy.

caption: LR test set regression plot showing improved predictive performance due to the model's simplicity.
summary: This LR test set parity plot demonstrates improved performance, as the model's simplicity allows it to capture the true data distribution more effectively. By avoiding the noise-fitting issues seen in training, the LR model achieves better predictive results for relative density and dimensional change on unseen data.

caption: Equiaxed Voxel RVE configuration employed for creep anisotropy simulations.
summary: This equiaxed Voxel RVE is part of a series of simulations performed to investigate the effect of deformation mechanism choices on creep anisotropy. By utilizing this specific RVE, the study isolates the impact of grain shape and orientation on the mechanical performance of the material under creep conditions.

caption: Optical micrograph of the TO specimen edge showing a thermally affected adiabatic shear band (TASB) that has propagated into a crack.
summary: Captured at the edge of the TO specimen, this micrograph reveals a thermally affected adiabatic shear band (TASB) transitioning into a crack. Tiny ASBs are also visible in the top right corner, consistent with observations of shear localization at the specimen boundaries following the high-velocity impact event.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves for electrochemically reduced Ni-Al alloys with varying heat-treatment times, measured in 1.0 M KOH at 25 °C, showing the HER performance of the catalysts.
summary: Linear sweep voltammetry curves illustrate the HER performance of electrochemically reduced Ni-Al alloys in 1.0 M KOH. Among the tested catalysts, the RN30-LR variant demonstrates superior performance, achieving an overpotential of 54 mV at a current density of 10 mA/cm2, highlighting the impact of heat-treatment duration on catalytic activity.

caption: Current-voltage (I–V) characteristics of the PHOTOWATT-PWP 201 solar panel estimated by 20 different optimization algorithms, with blue square markers indicating experimental measured data points.
summary: This panel displays the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics for the PWP201 solar panel, comparing experimental data represented by blue square markers against estimations from 20 distinct optimization algorithms. The curves illustrate the performance of various methods listed in the study, providing a visual assessment of how well each algorithm fits the measured data.

caption: 2D opacity map derived from CT scan data for sample R20.
summary: Sample R20 is represented by a 2D opacity map generated from processed CT scan data. This visualization provides a cross-sectional view of the internal structure, allowing for a direct comparison with simulated structural grids to evaluate the accuracy of the melt pool modeling process for this specific specimen.

caption: Thermomagnetization M(T) curves for the oscillating Ni-Mn-Ga “O” sample in as-built and annealed states, recorded during ZFC and FC processes at 50 Oe.
summary: Thermomagnetization M(T) curves for the oscillating Ni-Mn-Ga “O” sample are shown for as-built and heat-treated states under a 50 Oe magnetic field. These curves, recorded during ZFC and FC processes, demonstrate the magnetic response and phase transformation characteristics of the oscillating sample before and after the applied heat treatment process.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+ in 0.1 M KCl at scan rates from 5 to 500 mV s-1 for the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode at Angle 1, with an inset showing the corresponding Randles–Ševčík plot.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms for the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode at Angle 1 demonstrate electrochemical behavior across scan rates from 5 to 500 mV s-1 in a [Ru(NH3)6]3+ solution. The Randles–Ševčík plot inset confirms the relationship between peak current and scan rate, serving as a baseline for evaluating strain effects on performance.

caption: Honeycomb composite structure specimen subjected to fatigue testing protocols.
summary: This panel illustrates the honeycomb composite structure specimen used during the fatigue test. Conducted in accordance with ASTM 3479 M, the testing of this structural configuration provides critical data on the fatigue life and mechanical response of composite architectures, complementing the material-level tests performed in the overall experimental framework.

caption: Layer-wise RMSE comparison of LNN-GKO, RNN-GKO, and Vanilla GNN surrogate models across all structural cases in the evaluation dataset.
summary: This plot displays the root mean square error (RMSE) for three surrogate models—LNN-GKO, RNN-GKO, and Vanilla GNN—evaluated across different deposition layers. By comparing these metrics layer-by-layer, the figure elucidates the performance and predictive accuracy of each model throughout the additive manufacturing build process for all structural cases.

caption: UV-vis absorption spectra of 3D-Ze-600 and 3D-Ze-900 samples after 180 minutes of contact with MB dye solutions, featuring an inset photograph demonstrating the de-coloration effect.
summary: The UV-vis spectra reveal a significant decrease in absorption intensity for the 3D-Ze-600 sample after 180 minutes, indicating substantial MB dye adsorption. This reduction is visually confirmed by the inset photograph. Conversely, the 3D-Ze-900 sample shows minimal change in absorption intensity and de-coloration, suggesting lower adsorption efficiency.

caption: Side view of a brazed diamond specimen containing 1.5 wt% Nd in an amorphous state.
summary: This side view photograph displays a brazed diamond specimen with 1.5 wt% Nd in an amorphous state. The visual evidence confirms that the amorphous filler alloy achieves a significantly higher climbing height on the diamond surface than the crystalline filler alloy, underscoring the superior wettability of the amorphous state.

caption: Wear rate versus normal load at a frequency of 8 Hz, highlighting the performance difference between LP and CP materials.
summary: At 8 Hz, the wear rate increases with load for both materials. Specifically at 20 N, the LP material exhibits a wear rate of approximately 0.0092 mm3/m, which is significantly higher than the 0.0069 mm3/m observed for the CP material, demonstrating distinct wear resistance characteristics under these specific test conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the subband configuration within a 10-ML quantum well structure under a 0-V reverse bias condition.
summary: This diagram illustrates the subband configuration of a 10-ML quantum well at 0-V reverse bias. It serves as a reference for understanding the Γ21-h11 radiative recombination transition and the behavior of negative-order Stark-ladder transitions, where the energy separation between electron and hole subband states decreases as the electric field increases.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the track-track melt pool boundary (MPB) in the YZ plane of LPBF-processed 316L stainless steel, highlighting the dislocation-rich microstructure.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image captures the microstructure near the track-track MPB in LPBF-processed 316L stainless steel. The bright contrast observed in the image indicates a high density of dislocations, which are known to govern the strengthening mechanisms in this material. The specific MPB location is clearly identified for detailed structural analysis.

caption: Measured third-harmonic generation (THG) emission spectrum obtained from the Si metasurface under femtosecond laser excitation at 1510 nm.
summary: This panel displays the measured THG emission spectrum generated by the Si metasurface. Upon illumination with a femtosecond laser at 1510 nm, a distinct nonlinear emission peak is observed at approximately 507 nm, demonstrating the effective frequency conversion capabilities of the fabricated metasurface structure.

caption: J-integral evolution for varying stiffness gradient profiles (n=1 to 10), showing a consistent plateau value of 0.1 during stable crack growth.
summary: The J-integral is plotted for different stiffness gradient profiles where n ranges from 1 to 10. Results show that the J-integral maintains a constant plateau value of 0.1 during stable crack growth, verifying that the framework successfully captures intrinsic toughness independently of the specific stiffness gradient profile used.

caption: Concentration distribution map within the x-y plane of the K8 microreactor at Reynolds numbers of 2.5, 7.5, 25, and 75.
summary: This contour plot displays the concentration distribution within the x-y plane of the K8 microreactor at Reynolds numbers of 2.5, 7.5, 25, and 75. By mapping the concentration streamlines, the figure demonstrates how the K8 microreactor geometry influences fluid flow and concentration profiles across the specified range of Reynolds numbers.

caption: Phase image loaded onto the PLM for pixel alignment in the horizontal orientation, featuring a central region with a phase value of π, spanning 400 pixels in length and 4 pixels in width.
summary: This phase image is utilized for pixel alignment within the PLM system. The pattern is characterized by a central region exhibiting a phase value of π, which measures 400 pixels in length and 4 pixels in width, providing the necessary spatial configuration for precise horizontal orientation alignment.

caption: Bone volume fraction (BV/TV) measurements for newly formed bone across different scaffold groups.
summary: Bone volume fraction (BV/TV) analysis of newly formed bone indicates significant differences between experimental groups. The PGCL@5%Ti3C2/5%Van group exhibited significantly greater BV/TV values compared to the PGCL and PGCL@5%Van groups, demonstrating enhanced osteogenic performance as confirmed by statistical analysis with P < 0.05.

caption: Wavelet transform EXAFS plots comparing Ni foil, NiO, and E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05, illustrating the absence of Ni-O bond signals.
summary: Wavelet transform EXAFS plots provide structural insights into the local environment of nickel. Comparison between Ni foil, NiO, and the E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 catalyst confirms the absence of Ni-O bond signals in the catalyst, distinguishing its local coordination environment from that of the NiO standard.

caption: Arrhenius plot of ln(k) versus -1000/RT derived from hardness data, utilized to calculate the activation energy Q for the precipitation process.
summary: Utilizing the slope from the ln(k) versus -1000/RT plot, the activation energy Q is determined to be 160.1 kJ/mol. This value is highly consistent with the established diffusion energy of 160 kJ/mol for Nb in IN718 superalloys manufactured via selective laser melting, confirming the reliability of the hardness-based kinetic analysis.

caption: Friction coefficient evolution history for the PBAAM manufactured CoCrFeNiMnTi 0.3 HEA coating.
summary: This panel shows the friction coefficient evolution history for the PBAAM manufactured CoCrFeNiMnTi 0.3 HEA coating during sliding wear. The plot tracks the variation of the friction coefficient as a function of the wear testing time, providing insight into the tribological stability of the HEA coating during the test.

caption: Transmission spectra of the samples, showing significant dips that indicate the presence of differential coloration.
summary: The transmission spectrum for the samples is presented, revealing significant dips toward the left side of the plot. These spectral features serve as a clear indication of the differential color presence within the samples, directly correlating the optical transmission characteristics to the observed physical changes after pH immersion.

caption: COF curve demonstrating the frictional behavior of J9B material against an SLA alumina ball.
summary: The coefficient of friction (COF) curve for the J9B sample is presented, documenting its frictional performance during tribological testing with an SLA alumina ball. This plot serves as a representative measure of the material's surface interaction and wear characteristics as observed during the experimental evaluation described in the research.

caption: Surface energy variation relative to chemical potential for the Al8Mn5 phase.
summary: This panel displays the calculated surface energy of the Al8Mn5 phase plotted against relative chemical potential. The systematic approach ensures consistent evaluation of surface energy trends across different intermetallic phases, supporting the broader investigation into material properties.

caption: Comparison of CTE measurements for the CoCrFeNi alloy across the first and second heating cycles, highlighting the reversibility of observed thermal discontinuities.
summary: This plot compares the CTE of the CoCrFeNi alloy during two consecutive heating cycles to assess the reversibility of observed discontinuities. A sudden rise in CTE occurs during the second heating cycle within the same temperature range where a minimum was previously identified during the first heating cycle.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of the β-tricalcium phosphate-filled green body, showing mass loss as a function of temperature.
summary: This thermogravimetric analysis curve illustrates the thermal decomposition of the β-tricalcium phosphate-filled green body. Significant weight loss is observed between 200 °C and 700 °C, which is attributed to the thermal removal of binders, photoinitiator residues, dispersants, and other organic contaminants present within the composite material structure.

caption: Statistical distribution of void volumes within the free surface structure.
summary: This histogram presents a quantitative statistical analysis of void volumes observed in the free surface structure. Due to the limited size of the gaps present in this material configuration, the analysis focuses specifically on characterizing the dimensions of these voids to provide a clear understanding of their structural distribution.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy Nyquist plots for HT-W alloy immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, recorded at 5-hour intervals up to 60 hours.
summary: Representing the AC response of the HT-W alloy, these Nyquist plots illustrate the evolution of the depressed semi-circle over 60 hours of immersion. The data reflects the charge transfer resistance at the alloy/oxide film/solution interfaces, providing insight into the corrosion behavior of the heat-treated tungsten alloy in a saline environment.

caption: Nyquist plots for NiMo@NF measured at 0.528 V vs RHE, illustrating impedance behavior before and after CP testing, CV cycling, and stirring in 1 M KOH.
summary: Nyquist plots are presented for NiMo@NF at a constant potential of 0.528 V vs RHE. The data tracks impedance variations before and after CP testing, CV cycling, and stirring in 1 M KOH, highlighting the impact of these durability tests on the charge transfer resistance of the electrode material.

caption: SAXS intensity profiles of P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene solvent, featuring an inset Guinier plot used for molecular weight estimation.
summary: SAXS profiles for P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene reveal supramolecular structural features of the aggregates. The inset Guinier plot, generated using BioXTAS RAW software, provides the necessary data to estimate the molecular weight of the P3HT-PSL sample, confirming the structural analysis of these large molecules in solution.

caption: Grain boundary orientation difference distribution diagram for the solidified structure of Cu60Ni40 alloy processed at an undercooling of 222 K.
summary: This histogram displays the grain boundary orientation difference distribution for a Cu60Ni40 alloy solidified at an undercooling of 222 K. The distribution provides quantitative insight into the misorientation characteristics of the grain boundaries within the solidified microstructure, reflecting the crystallographic relationships established during the rapid solidification process at this specific undercooling.

caption: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Random_AB specimen showing γ’ precipitates and a grain boundary.
summary: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Random_AB specimen reveals the distribution of γ’ precipitates and a grain boundary. The microstructure exhibits a clear distinction between coarse primary and fine spherical secondary γ’ phases, providing insight into the microstructural characteristics of the material following the specific scanning strategy and heat treatment.

caption: Immunofluorescence visualization of mono-culture μvessels, displaying ECs stained for ZO-1 (green), CD31 (red), and DAPI (blue), alongside VSMCs stained with phalloidin (green), illustrating endothelial barrier formation and cell morphology.
summary: This panel displays mono-culture μvessels where the upper channel was subjected to 12 dyn/cm2 shear stress for 24 hours. Staining for CD31 and the tight junction marker ZO-1 confirms the formation of an endothelial barrier, while phalloidin staining clearly demonstrates the morphological characteristics of the VSMCs.

caption: Pole Figure (PF) of the US-300W Udimet-500 sample showing the development of new texture components.
summary: The Pole Figure for the US-300W sample confirms the further degradation of the cubic texture and the emergence of new orientation components. This structural evolution demonstrates that 300 W of ultrasonic power significantly alters the grain orientation distribution compared to the lower power and non-sonicated conditions.

caption: Overview of the Eazao Bio 3D printer setup, highlighting the printer hardware, integrated switch, and manometer.
summary: The Eazao Bio 3D printer is shown in this photograph, which captures the primary hardware components including the printer itself, the switch, and the manometer. This equipment is utilized for the additive manufacturing of alumina parts, serving as the foundational setup for the printing process described in the study.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for four distinct powder samples, recorded under a constant external magnetic field of 1.5 T.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetization versus temperature (M(T)) behavior for four different powder samples. The measurements were conducted under a consistent magnetic field of 1.5 T to characterize the thermal response of the materials' magnetic properties, providing a comparative overview of their magnetic stability across the studied temperature range.

caption: Fatigue lifetime versus applied stress normalized by weight for solid and metamaterial samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the fatigue characteristics of solid and metamaterial structures by comparing the applied stress relative to weight against the fatigue lifetime. Data points represent individual testing samples. Observations indicate that increasing the force and the level of applied stress results in an increase in the structural lifetime.

caption: Initial loading of the Re-Alloy feedstock into the alumina-based crucible prior to vacuum induction melting.
summary: The Re-Alloy feedstock is shown loaded into the 1.25 L alumina-based crucible. The material was prepared by cutting it into suitable sizes and cleaning it in an ultrasonic bath to ensure purity before being placed into the VIM furnace for the subsequent melting and alloying process.

caption: Absorbance values at 420 nm for DA, heparin, and Hep-DA solutions in tris buffer (pH 8.5) measured at the 60-minute mark.
summary: The absorbance at 420 nm is measured for DA, heparin, and Hep-DA solutions after 60 minutes in a tris buffer at pH 8.5. The data confirms the color transformation observed in the photographic analysis, highlighting the distinct optical properties of the dopamine-containing samples compared to pure heparin.

caption: Selected Area Electron Diffraction (SAED) pattern of the blocky Al6(Mn,Fe) precipitates, confirming their structural characteristics.
summary: Selected Area Electron Diffraction analysis of the blocky precipitates confirms their identity as primary Al6(Mn,Fe) phases. These particles are located at the grain boundaries and exhibit no clear orientation relationship with the aluminum matrix, distinguishing them from the coherent Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates formed during the aging treatment.

caption: Diffraction pattern from the heat-affected zone (HAZ) near the fusion zone, with an insert detailing the detection of trace precipitates.
summary: Representing the heat-affected zone near the fusion zone, this diffraction pattern provides critical phase identification data. The inset highlights the presence of trace precipitates, which are essential for understanding the microstructural evolution and phase stability in the region transitioning toward the fusion zone of the weld.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of Colmonoy-5 alloy powder from batch B, showing a spherical particle form and regular morphology.
summary: Confocal microscopy imaging of the Colmonoy-5 precursor powder from batch B demonstrates particles with a distinct spherical form and regular morphology. This observation confirms the structural consistency of the batch B alloy powder, contrasting with the irregular morphology observed in batch A through the same confocal microscopy analysis.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram measurements for three distinct nickel alloy-coated 3D-printed electrodes with a nickel mass deposition of 0.133 g/cm2, performed in a distilled water electrolyte.
summary: This panel displays the cyclic voltammogram measurements for three nickel alloy-coated 3D-printed electrodes, each featuring a nickel mass deposition of 0.133 g/cm2. The electrochemical performance of these samples was evaluated specifically within a distilled water environment to assess their behavior under these conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of the binary Co–Ni coating recorded at a sweep rate of 50 mV s−1 in 1 M KOH within the potential range of −0.02 to −0.58 V vs RHE, showing stable current behavior across multiple cycles.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram displays the electrochemical response of a Co–Ni alloy coating in 1 M KOH. The potential range is set between −0.02 and −0.58 V vs RHE at a 50 mV s−1 sweep rate. The CV curves for this binary coating remain consistent and similar for each recorded cycle.

caption: Pole figures of Sample 2 obtained through single-shot synchrotron X-ray diffraction, showing improved matching with EBSD data for specific plane groups.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction pole figures for Sample 2 are shown in this panel. The results exhibit a high degree of matching with the referential EBSD texture pole figures, particularly for the {111} and {220} plane groups, confirming the reliability of the synchrotron technique for texture characterization.

caption: Absorption (SE A) portion of CF/Ni-Fe/CNT/silicone composites as a function of frequency from 8.2 GHz to 12.4 GHz, highlighting the influence of different plating durations.
summary: The absorption portion of the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness for CF/Ni-Fe/CNT/silicone composites is shown across the X-band frequency range. The data highlights how different plating times affect the absorption behavior of the material, serving as a key component in understanding the overall shielding mechanism of the composite in the 8.2–12.4 GHz band.

caption: Nyquist plots illustrating the electrochemical impedance response of the stir zone specimen after immersion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution for various time intervals up to 7 days.
summary: Nyquist plots for the stir zone specimen are presented, showing the electrochemical impedance response during immersion in a 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution for up to 7 days. These measurements facilitate the evaluation of the stir zone's corrosion resistance and the evolution of its surface properties over the immersion duration.

caption: STEM bright-field image of the V1 sample viewed along the [001] zone axis, revealing the cellular structure morphology.
summary: This STEM bright-field image displays the cellular structure of the V1 sample along the [001] zone axis. Observations indicate that the material does not form a dislocation cellular pattern, distinguishing it from typical cellular structures found in other studies, while providing a baseline for analyzing dislocation distribution and segregation.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the bracelet-style 3DP-PWC electrode in 0.5 mM [Fe(CN)6]3-/4- solution, comparing bare, ZnO NPs, Aptamer/ZnO NPs, and Ket/Aptamer/ZnO NPs modified surfaces at a scan rate of 50 mVs-1 within a potential range of -1V to +1V.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry analysis of the bracelet-style 3DP-PWC electrode demonstrates the electrochemical characterization of modified surfaces. By comparing bare, ZnO NPs, Aptamer/ZnO NPs, and Ket/Aptamer/ZnO NPs modified electrodes in a redox probe solution, the successful integration and electrochemical response of the ketamine-aptamer-ZnO NP system are clearly illustrated.

caption: Polar diagram illustrating the supercardioid sensitivity pattern of the acoustic emission sensor.
summary: This polar pattern plot characterizes the directional sensitivity of the supercardioid acoustic emission sensor. To maintain optimal sensitivity during in-situ monitoring, a specialized fixture is used to orient the sensing side of the device directly toward the build plate, ensuring accurate signal capture during the manufacturing process.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the LSV curves in alkaline solution, showing the overpotential versus log current density for CoPNi-N/C, CoDNi-N/C, and Pt/C.
summary: Tafel analysis reveals the kinetic performance of the catalysts in alkaline solution. The CoPNi-N/C and CoDNi-N/C samples exhibit Tafel slopes of 43 and 53 mV dec-1, respectively, which are significantly lower than the 70 mV dec-1 observed for the Pt/C reference, indicating superior reaction kinetics for the synthesized materials.

caption: EBSD analysis of the trailing edge of the weld pool in DED Alloy 718, exhibiting larger substrate grains in the HAZ relative to the wrought material.
summary: DED Alloy 718 is characterized at the trailing edge of the weld pool using EBSD. The analysis confirms that substrate grains in the heat-affected zone are larger than those observed in the wrought Alloy 718. This finding demonstrates consistent grain coarsening trends across different additive manufacturing processing conditions.

caption: Comparison of yield strength versus relative density for Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy thin plate lattices against conventional AlSi10Mg, Ti-6Al-4V, and SS316 materials within the 17–27% relative density range.
summary: This plot compares the yield strength of the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy TPL against conventional materials like AlSi10Mg, Ti-6Al-4V, and SS316 at similar relative densities of 17–27%. The data demonstrates a significant improvement in yield strength for the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr-Mn alloy compared to AlSi10Mg and PBF-LB Ti-6Al-4V alloys at equivalent densities.

caption: Histogram showing the distribution of absolute errors for S–P models, contrasting the performance of models with and without PC features.
summary: The distribution of absolute errors for the two S–P stress prediction models is presented to evaluate accuracy. By comparing the concentration of minor errors and the magnitude of maximum errors, the histogram demonstrates that the S–P model incorporating PC features achieves superior predictive accuracy over the model without them.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heat flow curves comparing unannealed PLA and Sample 13, which exhibits optimal mechanical properties.
summary: This DSC analysis presents a comparative evaluation of heat flow curves for unannealed PLA and Sample 13. The plot highlights thermal behavior differences resulting from the annealing process, specifically focusing on Sample 13, which was identified as having optimal mechanical properties, providing insight into the material's thermal stability and phase transitions.

caption: Arc plasma image and schematic representation of the arc shape during the deposition of the 3rd layer 1st bead.
summary: The physical and schematic diagrams for the 3rd layer 1st bead illustrate the arc plasma configuration during the third layer deposition. Captured at a shooting frequency of 30 Hz, the image characterizes the arc shape under the same arc length conditions maintained throughout the thick-wall part fabrication process.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the theoretically-calculated Mean Square Atomic Displacement (MSAD) values across the Cr-Co-Ni ternary composition space.
summary: This contour plot displays the theoretically-calculated MSAD values mapped onto the Cr-Co-Ni ternary phase diagram. By representing these values as a function of composition, the visualization provides a clear overview of how atomic displacement behavior varies across the entire ternary system, facilitating the identification of specific compositional trends.

caption: Electrical resistivity plotted against temperature for as-received and aged samples, with current flowing along the rolling direction, compared against literature data and Bloch-Gruneisson T^5 model simulations.
summary: Electrical resistivity measurements from 300 K to 20 K reveal a decrease in resistivity as temperature drops, attributed to reduced phonon-electron scattering. The aged sample exhibits higher resistivity than the as-received material, consistent with its increased mechanical strength. Experimental data show good agreement with literature values and Bloch-Gruneisson model simulations.

caption: STEM bright-field image revealing dislocation cell structures within the CoCrFeMnNi matrix.
summary: STEM bright-field imaging reveals that the CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy matrix contains well-defined dislocation cells. These cells are composed of high-density dislocation networks with an average cell diameter measured at approximately 0.37 ± 0.08 μm, highlighting the significant plastic deformation substructure present within the material matrix.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the transverse (X–Y) plane for the cast C263 material, highlighting its bimodal microstructure.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the cast C263 material reveals a distinct bimodal microstructure. This structural characteristic is significant as it helps explain the substantial differences observed in the F MAX versus N f fatigue curves for this specific material variant compared to the heat-treated samples.

caption: Solution energy profiles for a hydrogen atom at the coherent interface, calculated for positions 1 through 3 as defined in panel (a).
summary: This plot presents the calculated solution energy profiles for hydrogen atoms positioned at the coherent Al3Sc‖Al interface. By evaluating energy levels across specific tetrahedral sites, the simulation determines the thermodynamic stability of hydrogen solutes, providing quantitative insights into how the coherent interface structure influences hydrogen trapping and diffusion behavior.

caption: Numerical phase field contour of the G structure, highlighting the predicted damage localization and the specific unit cell selected for further analysis.
summary: The numerical phase field contour illustrates the predicted damage localization within the G structure under oblique compression. The model successfully identifies two localized bands of deformation. A specific unit cell located in the middle of the thickness direction is highlighted for detailed investigation in subsequent sections of the study.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 alloy obtained using the (110) diffraction spot, with the inset showing the SAED pattern along the [001] zone axis, revealing a two-phase γ-γ' microstructure.
summary: Captured using the (110) diffraction spot, this dark-field TEM image reveals the two-phase γ-γ' microstructure of the Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 alloy. Homogenization has dissolved the Ni-Ti rich η phase and the Al-Ni rich Heusler type phase previously found in interdendritic regions, leaving only the stable γ-γ' structure visible.

caption: Bright-field TEM imaging, SAED pattern, and FFT analysis illustrating the blocky, faceted morphology and sharp interfaces of Nb-rich MC carbides.
summary: TEM bright-field imaging characterizes the Nb-rich MC carbides located in the interdendritic regions. These carbides exhibit a distinct blocky, faceted morphology with sharp, well-defined interfaces relative to the surrounding γ matrix. Complementary SAED and FFT analyses provide structural confirmation of the carbide nanostructure within the alloy matrix.

caption: Model predictions and experimental creep deformation data for Udimet 720Li, NiSup1, and NiSup3 alloys, illustrating the influence of stacking fault energy variations.
summary: This panel presents a comparison between model predictions and experimental creep results for Udimet 720Li and its derivatives, NiSup1 and NiSup3. These alloys, which differ in cobalt content, are used to explore the combined effects of stacking fault energy and microstructure on the creep response of the material.

caption: Spearman correlation matrix displaying the strength and direction of relationships between variable pairs, including process parameters P and V and morphological variables G, R, and U.
summary: This Spearman correlation matrix visualizes the interdependencies between input variables, clarifying the relationships among G, R, U, P, and V. It demonstrates how increasing energy input P and velocity V influences grain morphology parameters G and R, providing essential context for understanding the underlying process-structure correlations within the ANN model.

caption: Example results illustrating the phase change observed during the directed energy deposition (DED) process.
summary: These results demonstrate the phase change occurring during directed energy deposition. By utilizing the high spatial resolution of the diffraction setup, the evolution of phase fractions and strain states is mapped through the melt pool and solidification front, providing quantitative data on the material's structural transformation during the DED process.

caption: Incident low-power Gaussian beam profile captured on a CCD camera, serving as the baseline reference for the beam shaping experiment.
summary: The incident low-power Gaussian beam profile is captured on a CCD camera to serve as a baseline reference. This initial measurement provides the necessary comparison for evaluating the performance of the refractive Fourier transform generator in subsequent beam shaping experiments, as described in the experimental setup for profile analysis.

caption: HNMR analysis of CP-PLA showing characteristic proton signals at 5.17 ppm and 1.58 ppm for PLA, alongside MMA-related peaks at 3.59 ppm, 1.69 ppm, and 1.02 ppm.
summary: HNMR analysis of CP-PLA reveals distinct chemical shifts corresponding to its constituent polymers. Signals at 5.17 ppm and 1.58 ppm are attributed to methylene and methyl protons in the PLA unit, while peaks at 3.59 ppm, 1.69 ppm, and 1.02 ppm confirm the presence of the MMA unit within the composite structure.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the elemental distribution near the grain boundary in HIP plus solution-treated LPBF Inconel 625 alloy after tensile testing at 900 degrees Celsius.
summary: This three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the elemental distribution near the grain boundary for the HIP plus solution-treated LPBF Inconel 625 alloy after undergoing tensile testing at 900 degrees Celsius. The image highlights the atomic-scale elemental configuration resulting from the combined effects of thermal processing and high-temperature mechanical deformation.

caption: Dark field STEM image of the cubic specimen top region showing irregular arc-shaped dislocations within the laths.
summary: This dark field STEM image reveals the microstructure of the cubic specimen's top region. Observations indicate the presence of irregular arc-shaped dislocations located within the laths, providing insight into the defect structure resulting from the processing conditions applied to the material at the top parts of the specimen.

caption: Alcian blue and toluidine blue staining images of NPs, highlighting ECM integrity across different treatment groups.
summary: Alcian blue and toluidine blue staining provide visual evidence of ECM integrity in NPs. The images show that DEPGM treatment effectively reduces ECM degradation caused by oxidative stress. This staining technique confirms that the hydrogel provides a protective environment, maintaining the structural components of the NPs against oxidative damage.

caption: Overview of the primary thematic sections and structural organization of the review paper.
summary: This figure provides a comprehensive overview of the primary thematic sections and structural organization of the review paper. It serves as a roadmap for the reader, illustrating the main chapters that define the scope and logical progression of the topics discussed throughout the document.

caption: Calculated band structure of the Si metasurface plotted against normalized frequency fa/c, highlighting high-symmetry points X, M, and Γ within the Brillouin zone to characterize resonant dispersion.
summary: The band structure of the Si metasurface is calculated to determine the resonant dispersion in k-space. The plot displays the normalized frequency fa/c across high-symmetry points X, M, and Γ in the Brillouin zone, providing essential information regarding the photonic properties and resonant behavior of the metasurface array.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of sample E 63 showing cellular structures with boundaries defined by high densities of tangled dislocations.
summary: Sample E 63 exhibits distinct cellular structures as visualized by HAADF-STEM. The cellular boundaries are primarily composed of tangled dislocations, whereas the interiors of these cells contain significantly fewer dislocations, highlighting the heterogeneous distribution of defects within the microstructure of the material.

caption: Time-resolved S-XCT 3D reconstructions of the WE43-PEO1 scaffold immersed in SBF, showing the evolution of hydrogen bubble formation and entrapment within the porous network across a 125-minute duration.
summary: This 3D reconstruction visualizes the degradation of the WE43-PEO1 scaffold in SBF. Hydrogen bubbles are observed forming and lodging within the porous structure. Notably, individual bubbles remain trapped for up to 30 minutes before release, demonstrating a qualitative method to assess the material's degradation behavior over time.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of zein, showing the weight percentage remaining during the heating process.
summary: The TGA curve for zein illustrates its thermal degradation characteristics. This analysis was conducted to evaluate the thermal stability of the formulations and assess drug-polymer interactions, providing insights into how the zein matrix influences the thermal performance of the loaded drug components compared to the pure materials.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram of AISI 4340 steel illustrating the cooling trajectory during additive manufacturing, marked by a purple zigzag arrow representing cyclic heating and cooling cycles.
summary: The TTT diagram for AISI 4340 steel displays the transformation kinetics, where the purple zigzag arrow highlights the complex thermal history of additive manufacturing. Rapid cooling bypasses the pearlite region, while subsequent cyclic heating promotes bainite formation, preventing residual austenite from transforming into martensite during final cooling stages.

caption: UV–vis absorption spectrum of DA-CDs showing a broad range from 200 to 900 nm with a characteristic peak at 279 nm.
summary: The UV–vis absorption spectrum of DA-CDs exhibits a broad range spanning from 200 to 900 nm, indicating potential for near-infrared photothermal conversion. A characteristic absorption peak at 279 nm is observed, which corresponds to π-π* electronic transitions within the aromatic systems present in the carbon dot structure.

caption: Wavelength-dispersive spectroscopy concentration profile of Cobalt across the tri-junction region.
summary: Cobalt elemental concentration distribution is mapped via WDS across the Ni/12Ti/15V MCDM tri-junction. The profile reveals that Cobalt exhibits a nearly complementary concentration distribution relative to Nickel. This analysis is part of a broader investigation into the elemental diffusion behavior within the multi-component diffusion multiple system.

caption: Dilatometric heating and cooling curves of additively manufactured maraging steel showing characteristic transformation temperatures.
summary: Dilatometric analysis of additively manufactured maraging steel reveals the thermal response during heating and cooling cycles. The curves identify critical transformation temperatures, specifically A C1 , A C3 , M s , and M f , which are essential for characterizing the phase evolution and thermal stability of the material during processing.

caption: Calculated band structure of the I-WP unit cell at a geometric parameter β = ± 0.5, showing the evolution of the fundamental flexural (A), torsional (B), and longitudinal (C) bands and their associated band gaps.
summary: This panel illustrates the band structure of the I-WP unit cell under the condition β = ± 0.5. Similar to the previous panel, it tracks the fundamental flexural, torsional, and longitudinal bands labeled A, B, and C, while highlighting the shaded regions that represent the band gaps for these modes.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy (WDS) mapping of iron distribution in sample 0–3 at 5,000x magnification, arranged by vertical height from the substrate.
summary: This WDS map illustrates the iron distribution within sample 0–3, captured at 5,000x magnification. The arrangement reflects the vertical height from the substrate rather than actual sample location. Analysis of this map reveals a clear trend in Fe concentration from the CI–Cu interface toward the center of the third layer.

caption: Radiographic inspection of a polyurethane (PU) tank revealing internal structural defects.
summary: This radiographic image provides a non-destructive inspection of a polyurethane tank. The visualization highlights specific defect spots within the material structure, demonstrating the utility of X-ray imaging for quality control and failure analysis in industrial polymer components by identifying internal anomalies that are not visible to the naked eye.

caption: Light intensity distribution profile captured outside the focal plane using a UV-sensitive CCD sensor.
summary: This panel displays the light distribution profile captured outside the focal plane using a UV-sensitive CCD sensor. Such measurements are critical for predicting the 3D curing region, including cured width and depth, which helps prevent asymmetric overcuring defects and ensures the geometric fidelity of fabricated microstructures like cantilevers and microchannels.

caption: Binder mass loss profile for 15 mm diameter cylindrical specimens subjected to debinding at varying temperatures in nitrogen and air atmospheres.
summary: This graph illustrates the binder mass loss behavior of cylindrical bodies with a 15 mm diameter during the debinding process. The data compares the mass loss performance across different thermal conditions, specifically evaluating the impact of nitrogen versus air atmospheres on the binder removal efficiency at various debinding temperatures.

caption: Infrared thermal camera images captured at select intervals during a fixed processing build, showing surface temperature distributions across multiple parts after layer melting.
summary: Infrared thermal camera images reveal surface temperature variations during a fixed processing build. Despite identical processing conditions, temperatures fluctuate between parts at the same layer and layer-to-layer for individual parts. Notably, the cone-shaped part exhibits a prominent increase in surface temperature throughout the deposition process compared to other parts.

caption: Correlation curves illustrating the relationship between laser spot size and compressive yield strength for LPBF 316LSS.
summary: This correlation plot summarizes the relationship between varying laser spot sizes and the resulting compressive yield strength of LPBF 316LSS. It serves to synthesize the mechanical performance data across different processing parameters, highlighting how spot size adjustments influence the material's strength characteristics within the investigated laser power and scanning speed windows.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni-Fe-Mo ternary system calculated at 1373 K.
summary: This panel presents the calculated isothermal section of the Ni-Fe-Mo ternary system at 1373 K. The diagram illustrates the phase equilibria for this specific composition at the designated temperature, providing thermodynamic insight into the stability of phases within the ternary system as determined by computational modeling methods.

caption: Difference map for the vector matching approach, where white pixels represent mislabelled regions.
summary: This difference map displays mislabelled pixels for the vector matching approach. The reference indicates that this method struggles with patterns from overlap and interface areas, which is reflected in the distribution of white pixels. This visualization confirms the limitations of vector matching in accurately classifying complex microstructural phase boundaries.

caption: Convergence analysis of the machine learning model for predicting radius variation.
summary: Radius variation convergence is depicted in this panel, showing the progression of the machine learning model's estimated values. The graph highlights the stability and accuracy of the model as it iterates, confirming the convergence of the predictions for radius variation as part of the broader model evaluation presented.

caption: Vickers hardness measurements as a function of hatch spacing, showing values of 506.2 ± 4.8 HV for d0.01, 483.6 ± 12.5 HV for d0.06, and a minimum of 433.8 ± 10.6 HV for d0.02.
summary: Vickers hardness testing demonstrates the effect of hatch spacing on bulk mechanical performance. Samples d0.01 and d0.06 exhibit high hardness values due to significant volume fractions of hard β phase and massively transformed α2 phase, whereas d0.02 shows the lowest hardness, attributed to a reduced volume fraction of these hard phases.

caption: Temperature measurement trends for blended Ni 52 at.% powder, comparing emissivity-corrected absolute temperatures and uncorrected IR pyrometer readings relative to the thermal stage temperature.
summary: The graph for blended Ni 52 at.% powder demonstrates the clear discrepancy between thermal stage temperature, IR pyrometer readings, and absolute temperatures. This comparative analysis highlights the significant impact of emissivity variations on temperature accuracy, confirming that uncorrected IR measurements are insufficient for determining the true absolute temperature of the powder.

caption: Multiple random distribution (MRD) plot for the annealed WAAM NAB alloy, quantifying the crystallographic texture.
summary: The Multiple Random Distribution (MRD) plot serves as a quantitative measure of the crystallographic texture in the annealed WAAM NAB alloy. In conjunction with the IPF map, this data confirms that the alloy possesses a random crystallographic orientation, reflecting the microstructural state achieved after the annealing process.

caption: Williamson–Hall plots utilized for the determination of Statistically Stored Dislocation (SSD) density via X-ray diffraction analysis.
summary: Williamson–Hall plots are shown to characterize the Statistically Stored Dislocation (SSD) density. By analyzing the peak broadening in the XRD patterns, these plots facilitate the extraction of dislocation density values, serving as a critical diagnostic tool for assessing the internal strain and crystallite characteristics of the material.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Fe-Ni-Cr system at 1600K, illustrating the equilibrium phase boundaries and compositional regions.
summary: This panel presents the ternary phase diagram for the Fe-Ni-Cr system at a constant temperature of 1600K. It delineates the equilibrium phase boundaries and compositional regions within the system, providing a clear visualization of the phase stability and distribution for these specific metallic elements under the defined thermal conditions.

caption: Chemical composition data for alloy A following secondary thermal treatment (TT) and subsequent processing via LPBF and DED methods.
summary: This table details the chemical composition of alloy A after undergoing secondary thermal treatment and processing through LPBF and DED techniques. It provides a comprehensive overview of the alloying element concentrations in the printed specimens, allowing for a comparison of composition changes resulting from the secondary treatment and printing processes.

caption: Age-hardening curves for AA6082 alloy specimens subjected to single-stage aging (SA) and double-stage aging (DA) processes.
summary: This panel displays the age-hardening behavior of AA6082 aluminum alloy under two distinct heat treatment conditions: single-stage aging and double-stage aging. The curves illustrate the evolution of microhardness over time, providing a comparative analysis of how these specific processing routes influence the mechanical hardening response of the material.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profiles of specific oxide anions 18O-, Cr2-, Ni2-, OH-, and O2- for the inner surface of alloy 690 steam generator tubes after transient testing at 325°C.
summary: This panel displays ToF-SIMS depth profiles for various oxide anions, including 18O-, Cr2-, and Ni2-, measured on the inner surface of alloy 690 steam generator tubes. These profiles were obtained following transient testing in the BOREAL loop at 325°C, providing insight into the chemical composition of the oxide layer.

caption: UV/vis absorbance spectra of DPPH solutions following 120 minutes of degradation treatment, with an inset photograph showing the visual color change of the solutions.
summary: Panel F displays the UV/vis absorbance spectra of DPPH solutions after 120 minutes of treatment with different MgCu-MOF74 samples. The inset photograph provides a visual representation of the color change in the solutions, confirming the degradation of DPPH radicals and the varying antioxidant efficacy of the tested materials.

caption: Helical rotor geometry characterized by twisted blade profiles.
summary: The helical rotor design is presented as a specific blade geometry type for vertical axis wind turbines. This configuration utilizes twisted blades to optimize performance, distinguishing it from the straight-bladed H-type or the simple S-shaped Savonius rotors within the broader classification of VAWT rotor design features.

caption: CAD design file representing a grid-like lattice architecture characterized by sharp edges.
summary: This CAD model illustrates a grid-like lattice architecture designed for ceramic additive manufacturing. The design features sharp edges, which are noted as a potential limitation for subsequent coating adhesion and gas-surface contact efficiency during functionalization processes, as highlighted in the study of lattice ceramic architectures.

caption: Cross-sectional morphology and elemental distribution map of the DT-316SS alloy.
summary: This figure presents the cross-sectional morphology and elemental distribution of the DT-316SS alloy. The visualization provides a detailed view of the material's internal structure and the spatial arrangement of its constituent elements, offering critical insights into the compositional homogeneity and microstructural characteristics of the DT-316SS specimen under investigation.

caption: Side-view X-ray tomography observation of a single unit cell layer within the printed packing structure.
summary: This side-view X-ray tomography image provides a detailed look at a single unit cell layer at the center of the packing. The visualization supports the conclusion that the 3D printed packing maintains high structural fidelity, with the central cavity pores remaining clear and accurately reproduced according to the CAD model.

caption: Three-dimensional band structure of the Lieb lattice along the high-symmetry path Γ-X-M-Γ, highlighting dispersive green bands and a purple flat band (FB).
summary: This panel displays the three-dimensional band structure of the Lieb lattice, calculated along the high-symmetry path Γ-X-M-Γ. The visualization distinguishes between dispersive bands, shown in green, and a flat band, represented in purple, which originates from the three-site primitive unit cell of the lattice structure.

caption: Multiphase-field simulation maps showing the solidification microstructure of Al 14.5 Co 25 Fe 35.5 Ni 25 alloy under ingot casting, DED-LB/M, and PBF-LB/M thermal conditions, with B2-NiAl area fractions indicated in black boxes.
summary: Multiphase-field simulations illustrate the solidification morphology of the Al 14.5 Co 25 Fe 35.5 Ni 25 alloy across three distinct processing conditions. These maps reveal the stabilization of the B2-NiAl phase within interdendritic regions, with specific area fractions quantified for each process to characterize the resulting microstructural evolution.

caption: Visual representation of deformation modes corresponding to stages ①–⑩, including elastic response, cell and torsional deformation, local densification, rod buckling, debonding, fracture, and final low-damage regions.
summary: This panel displays the deformation states of the S-II-T honeycomb at key displacement points. The sequence captures the structural evolution from initial elastic behavior and cell deformation to complex failure mechanisms such as rod buckling, debonding, and fracture, ultimately leading to a low-damage region during the continuous flexural loading process.

caption: PDOS plot of the Pt atom on the Ag-Pt (1 0 0) alloy surface after CO adsorption, where the d-band splitting indicates a strong interaction.
summary: This panel depicts the PDOS for the Pt atom after CO adsorption on the Ag-Pt (1 0 0) alloy surface. The observed splitting of the Pt d-band indicates a significantly stronger interaction with the CO molecule compared to the Ag site, highlighting the role of orbital hybridization in binding strength.

caption: Ablated module trajectory on Part 3 without PCGH, exhibiting fragmented and misaligned path segments.
summary: This panel illustrates the trajectory on Part 3 when the PCGH module is omitted. The resulting paths show significant deterioration in conformity, characterized by fragmented and misaligned trajectories that fail to follow the local geometry, underscoring the importance of PCGH for maintaining path continuity and alignment during the deposition process.

caption: Interaction effect between wall thickness and cell height on the ultimate strength of TPMS-based scaffolds, showing negligible variation in strength across the tested parameter range.
summary: This contour plot examines the interaction between wall thickness and cell height regarding the ultimate strength of TPMS-based scaffolds. The data indicates that variations in cell height exert a negligible influence on the mechanical performance, suggesting that wall thickness remains the primary driver of strength in this specific geometric configuration.

caption: Comparison of elongation versus ultimate tensile strength (UTS) for the current Fe-based alloy against literature data for various additively manufactured Fe-based alloys.
summary: This plot compares the mechanical performance, specifically the ultimate tensile strength and elongation, of the current alloy against a range of additively manufactured Fe-based alloys reported in the literature. It serves to benchmark the current material's property profile within the broader context of existing additively manufactured Fe-based alloy research.

caption: Hardness maps displayed as insets for cuboid samples, with dashed lines delineating the specific regions subjected to mapping analysis.
summary: Hardness maps are presented as insets for cuboid samples printed under the same processing conditions as the tensile specimens. These maps, with dashed lines indicating the specific areas analyzed, provide a spatial distribution of hardness values, offering insight into the mechanical uniformity and local properties resulting from the different manufacturing parameters.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots showing the inverse square capacitance versus potential for Ni-Cr-based alloy specimens prepared via different scan strategies in a borate buffer solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky analysis of Ni-Cr-based alloys in borate buffer solution reveals the semiconductive nature of the passive layer. The plots demonstrate that varying scan strategies significantly influence the defect density within the passive film, with higher dislocation densities correlating to lower defect densities as determined by the electrochemical measurements.

caption: Confocal microscopy imaging of 3D bone analogs composed of PLA trabeculae and MSC-encapsulated HA hydrogels, subjected to 14 days of low-intensity vibration (LIV) at 100 Hz and 1 g.
summary: Bone analogs were fabricated by encapsulating primary MSCs within HA hydrogels containing integrin-binding motifs and metalloproteinase-sensitive crosslinkers, integrated with 3D-printed PLA trabeculae. Following a 14-day LIV regimen of 100 Hz at 1 g, the scaffolds were analyzed using volumetric confocal microscopy to assess the cellular environment.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of WC-9%Ni-Cr cemented carbides in 1 N H2SO4 solution, illustrating the anodic behavior and pseudopassive regions.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the potentiodynamic polarization curves for WC-9%Ni-Cr cemented carbides tested in a 1 N H2SO4 solution. The data reveals characteristic anodic behavior, specifically highlighting the presence of pseudopassive regions, which are critical for evaluating the corrosion resistance of these cemented carbides under acidic conditions.

caption: CMOD versus force curve for mono-material HSLA steel specimens, showing repetition tests in grey.
summary: Represented here is the load-CMOD curve for mono-material HSLA steel. The graph highlights the load-displacement characteristics of the specimen, with multiple grey lines included to show the consistency of the mechanical response across several repetition tests performed on the HSLA steel material.

caption: AFM and FESEM micrographs of the Ti-Fe-Cu thin film metallic glass deposited on SS316L and Ti substrates, with an inset displaying the surface roughness (Ra) value.
summary: Ti-Fe-Cu thin film metallic glass samples are characterized using AFM and FESEM imaging techniques. The micrographs reveal the surface morphology of the co-sputtered film on SS316L and Ti substrates. An inset within the panel provides the specific surface roughness (Ra) value, quantifying the topographical features of the deposited metallic glass.

caption: Logarithmic plot illustrating the evolution of crack length as a function of the normalized number of cycles for non-peened DN specimens.
summary: This logarithmic plot displays the crack length evolution versus the normalized number of cycles for non-peened DN specimens. It provides a clear representation of how main cracks propagate throughout the fatigue testing process, serving as a foundational dataset for analyzing the mechanical degradation of the material under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Overview of additive manufacturing (AM) virtual twin services categorized based on a comprehensive literature review.
summary: This schematic illustrates the various services provided by additive manufacturing virtual twins. By synthesizing findings from a literature review, the diagram categorizes the typical functionalities and capabilities inherent in virtual twin frameworks, providing a structured summary of how these digital models support additive manufacturing processes and decision-making workflows.

caption: Three-dimensional atomic distribution map of the IC31H alloy after creep at 1200 °C and 80 MPa, highlighting the γ/γ′ interface and the cylindrical region selected for compositional analysis.
summary: This 3D atomic distribution map illustrates the microstructure of the IC31H alloy following creep rupture at 1200 °C and 80 MPa. A cylindrical region perpendicular to the γ/γ′ interface was specifically selected to analyze atomic concentrations, with isoconcentration surfaces defined by Mo content exceeding 3.7% to delineate phase boundaries.

caption: Predicted 100,000-hour creep rupture stress as a function of temperature for CF8C-Plus, comparing Larson-Miller and Wilshire model predictions across the full dataset.
summary: This plot illustrates the predicted 100,000-hour creep rupture stress for CF8C-Plus across varying temperatures. While both the Larson-Miller and Wilshire models show minimal divergence below the yield strength, the Larson-Miller model provides more conservative rupture stress estimates for applied stresses exceeding the material's yield strength.

caption: Calculated phase stability diagram for the (Ti6Al4V)50(NiCo)50 alloy system, illustrating the thermodynamic equilibrium regions for B2 and cubic phases.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram evaluates the thermodynamic stability of B2 and cubic phases within the (Ti6Al4V)50(NiCo)50 alloy system. Based on this analysis, the specific composition of Ti6Al4V (50 wt%) + Ni (42 wt%) + Co (8 wt%) was determined for further experimental investigation, establishing the foundation for the alloy's phase development.

caption: Thermo-magnetization curves measured at an applied field of 0.01 T for HTHed specimens.
summary: Thermo-magnetization behavior of HTHed samples, fabricated with an energy density of 238.1 J/mm3, is illustrated through these curves. The data, collected under an applied field of 0.01 T, characterizes the magnetic response of the specimens as a function of temperature, providing the foundational data for subsequent phase transition analysis.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of relative melt pool area (MPA) versus porosity, displaying an hourglass-shaped distribution that reflects the competing effects of melt pool size on porosity.
summary: The scatter diagram for relative melt pool area reveals a complex, hourglass-shaped relationship with porosity. While larger melt pools can contribute to increased porosity, they also exhibit instances where they contribute to decreasing porosity. This indicates that melt pool area has competing effects on the formation of porosity in core pixels.

caption: OIM map of the sample processed at 0.1 strain and 750 °C induction heating temperature, showing increased length of Σ 3 boundaries compared to 700 °C.
summary: Representing the sample treated at 0.1 strain and 750 °C, this OIM map illustrates the evolution of grain boundary character. At this strain level, Σ 3 boundaries become longer as the induction heating temperature increases from 700 °C to 750 °C, with coherent Σ 3 boundaries clearly recognizable in the microstructure.

caption: Refractive index values of SL samples as a function of AlInN fraction, ranging from 0 (bulk GaN) to 1 (bulk AlInN), measured via spectroscopic ellipsometry at 401, 501, and 601 nm.
summary: Spectroscopic ellipsometry measurements reveal the refractive index of SL samples across a composition range from bulk GaN to bulk AlInN. Data points are plotted for light wavelengths of 401, 501, and 601 nm, illustrating the dependence of the refractive index on the AlInN fraction within the superlattice structure.

caption: 3D topography and 2D cross-sectional profile of the wear track on the Ti/TiCp coating processed under 180 A current.
summary: Presented here is the 3D topography and line scan of the wear track for the Ti/TiCp coating processed at 180 A. This visualization illustrates the wear track dimensions, which, when compared to the substrate, demonstrate the influence of the coating and processing current on wear resistance.

caption: Validation of predicted versus experimental tensile strength (TS) values.
summary: This parity plot displays the relationship between experimental tensile strength (TS) measurements and the predicted values generated by the regression model. The comparison highlights the deviation between the model's output and actual experimental data, providing a quantitative verification of the model's predictive capability for tensile strength properties.

caption: Quantitative mass ratio distribution of HA, β-TCP, and α-TCP phases in Si-doped BCP powder treated at 1000 °C.
summary: Quantitative analysis of phase ratios for samples subjected to heat treatment at 1000 °C for 2 h is depicted. This bar chart illustrates the mass distribution of HA, β-TCP, and α-TCP phases in relation to varying silicon doping levels, providing a clear overview of the phase composition at this temperature.

caption: Segmentation of geometric data using k-means clustering, modified Cs algorithms, and Reeb graph topological analysis methods.
summary: This panel illustrates geometric segmentation techniques applied to additive manufacturing data. It compares three distinct computational approaches: k-means clustering, modified Cs algorithms, and Reeb graph methods. These methods are utilized to partition complex geometric structures, facilitating more efficient processing and optimization in the context of additive manufacturing workflows.

caption: Calculated H ion implantation profile in AM 316H stainless steel subjected to 0.5 MeV H+ irradiation at normal incidence, showing depth-dependent concentration.
summary: This SRIM-calculated profile illustrates the H ion implantation depth in AM 316H stainless steel under 0.5 MeV H+ irradiation. The simulation reveals a relatively uniform ion distribution between 0 and 3.5 μm depth, with a distinct peak concentration occurring at a depth of 2.5 μm within the target material.

caption: Cyclic crack resistance curve showing the relationship between cyclic stress intensity factor (SIF) and crack length for AlSi10Mg mini-bending specimens.
summary: This panel displays the cyclic crack resistance curve for AlSi10Mg mini-bending specimens. It plots the cyclic stress intensity factor against the change in crack length to evaluate short crack propagation behavior. This data provides essential insights into the fatigue crack growth characteristics of the material under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Local EDS linescan profile across the 70Ti/30Ta composition in the as-printed condition.
summary: Local EDS linescan measurements for the 70Ti/30Ta composition are presented for the as-printed condition. This analysis provides a compositional profile across the specified region, serving as a baseline for evaluating the effects of subsequent heat treatment conditions on the elemental distribution within the Ti-Ta alloy system.

caption: Atomic configurations of the Ni-Al superalloy system, displaying a single-crystal supercell on the left and a nano-crystalline model on the right.
summary: This figure illustrates the atomic configurations used in simulation, featuring a single-crystal supercell on the left and a nano-crystalline Ni-Al superalloy model on the right. The models are derived from a supercell containing 3433 Ni and 729 Al atoms, representing a phase volume fraction of 27.1% gamma and 72.9% gamma-prime.

caption: Peak stress variation of the Cu-7Ni-7Al-4Fe-2Mn alloy plotted against varying deformation conditions.
summary: Peak stress values for the base Cu-7Ni-7Al-4Fe-2Mn alloy are displayed across different strain conditions. By comparing this plot with the Cr-modified alloy data, the figure qualitatively analyzes the influence of Cr on rheological behavior, confirming that the base alloy exhibits less significant dynamic recrystallization characteristics than the modified version.

caption: Loading of non-compliant stud bolts and nuts into an alumina crucible for powder production.
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial loading phase of the powder production route. Non-compliant stud bolts and nuts are placed into an alumina crucible. The recovered parts are sized appropriately for the crucible, allowing for complete filling without the need for additional cutting or fractionation steps prior to melting.

caption: Simulated IN625 microstructure cross-section near the top surface at a build plane depth of 300 μm, illustrating grain orientation distribution.
summary: This panel illustrates the simulated IN625 microstructure near the top surface, captured at a build plane depth of 300 μm. The grains are colored according to their crystal orientation, demonstrating the structural characteristics of the simulated material at this specific depth within the build volume.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) curves comparing SLM-fabricated and as-cast Ti-64 alloys, showing stabilization after 3600 seconds of immersion in various electrolytes.
summary: The OCP curves for SLM-fabricated and as-cast Ti-64 alloys are presented, demonstrating that the potential reaches a steady-state plateau after 3600 seconds of immersion. This behavior is attributed to consistent RedOx reactions occurring at the electrochemical interface across multiple tested electrolytes, including NaOH, SBF, NaCl, and H2SO4.

caption: Nyquist plots showing the imaginary versus real impedance components for LPBF and cast ZK60 Mg alloy samples.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance behavior of LPBF and cast ZK60 Mg alloy specimens. These plots represent the imaginary impedance component against the real impedance component, providing insight into the electrochemical characteristics and corrosion resistance of the two different processing conditions for the ZK60 magnesium alloy.

caption: Variation of the Nusselt number predicted by the ANNs-BR algorithm plotted against the Reynolds number.
summary: Panel (a) illustrates the predicted Nusselt number values generated by the ANNs-BR algorithm. This plot specifically highlights the functional variation of the Nusselt number with respect to the Reynolds number, serving as the primary baseline for evaluating the performance of the neural network model against the physical parameters of interest.

caption: Indentation fracture toughness measurements for DIW lithium disilicate samples across different sintering temperatures.
summary: Indentation fracture toughness data for DIW lithium disilicate samples sintered at various temperatures is displayed. Similar to the hardness results, the fracture toughness values do not appear to be greatly affected by the sintering temperature, exhibiting only minimal variations between the different groups tested in this study.

caption: Gyroid design scaffold surface populated with hMSCs, displaying cell viability results obtained from Live/Dead staining over 7 days.
summary: Gyroid design scaffold surfaces populated with hMSCs display cell viability results obtained from Live/Dead staining over 7 days. The analysis qualitatively confirms a high proportion of viable cells and minimal cell death, indicating that all scaffolds, including the gyroid design, demonstrated statistically significant cell growth over the 7-day period.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 4 fabricated via Aerosol Jet Printing (AJP).
summary: This panel displays the reflection coefficient of antenna design 4 produced using the AJP technique. The data, plotted via Origin software, characterizes the electromagnetic performance of the printed structure, providing a baseline for evaluating the reflection characteristics of the aerosol-jet-printed antenna design within the specified frequency range.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve for the Al–Mg–Si alloy in the peak-aged (PA) condition, showing characteristic thermal peaks associated with precipitate formation.
summary: Representing the peak-aged (PA) state of the Al–Mg–Si alloy, this DSC curve illustrates the thermal response during heating. The presence of Roman numerals indicates specific precipitation events, allowing for the identification of phase transformations that occur within the material after reaching its peak-aged condition during the aging process.

caption: Epifluorescence microscopy images of Live/Dead stained cells on HC-A scaffolds at day 7, comparing static and dynamic culture conditions.
summary: Epifluorescence microscopy of Live/Dead stained cells on HC-A scaffolds at day 7 demonstrates cell viability under both static and dynamic culture conditions. The imaging results indicate that transitioning from static to dynamic culture does not induce excess cell mortality, confirming the suitability of the scaffold for dynamic environments.

caption: Temperature-dependent partitioning coefficient of Cr in the AlCo1-xCr1-yFe1+yNi2.1+x EHEA, as determined by ThermoCalc TCHEA5 database calculations.
summary: This panel presents the temperature-dependent partitioning coefficient of Cr for the AlCo1-xCr1-yFe1+yNi2.1+x EHEA system. Derived from the ThermoCalc TCHEA5 database, the plot characterizes the thermodynamic partitioning behavior of Cr, offering essential insights into how temperature influences the elemental distribution and phase stability within this complex concentrated alloy framework.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel, showing the relationship between output power and voltage across different temperature settings.
summary: Representing the P-V characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel, this plot compares experimental measurements with predictions from the PEC2 model at various temperatures. The visualization highlights how temperature fluctuations influence the power output of the solar panel, confirming the reliability of the PEC2 model for characterizing solar module performance.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results for the MC phase, showing significant presence of C and Nb elements.
summary: EDS results for the MC phase particles demonstrate a significant concentration of carbon and niobium. This compositional analysis confirms the identity of these particles as MC-type carbides, which are distinct from the Laves phases identified in the other regions of the microstructure based on their specific elemental signatures.

caption: Optical micrograph of the as-deposited SS 316L-IN 625 bimetallic interface, where a black dashed line delineates the transition zone between the two alloys.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the as-deposited bimetallic interface between SS 316L and IN 625. A black dashed line clearly marks the transition zone between the two materials. The interface is characterized by rapid heat dissipation, which influences the formation of skeletal delta-ferrite within the melt pool boundaries.

caption: Thermogravimetric (TG) and derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves for 3D printed AESO-IBOMA samples, comparing the unfilled reference material with composites containing 0.5, 1, and 2 wt% BC filler.
summary: This figure presents the thermal degradation behavior of 3D printed AESO-IBOMA samples. It displays TG and DTG curves for the unfilled reference material alongside composites loaded with 0.5, 1, and 2 wt% BC. These plots illustrate the mass loss and degradation rates of the materials under thermal analysis conditions.

caption: Diamond sheet network unit cell structure displaying the interconnected thin-walled geometry characteristic of the diamond minimal surface.
