summary: This diamond sheet network unit cell is evaluated alongside other morphologies to determine the linear correlation between porosity and pore size. The findings indicate a high coefficient of determination, suggesting that the geometric parameters of the diamond sheet network are predictable and consistent across the tested range of unit cell sizes.

caption: Nyquist diagram illustrating the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) characteristics of the CoCu 20 FeMnNi base metal (BM).
summary: Nyquist diagram illustrating the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) characteristics of the CoCu 20 FeMnNi base metal (BM). This plot serves as a key component of the EIS measurements performed on the base metal, facilitating the analysis of charge transfer resistance and double-layer capacitance within the electrochemical system.

caption: Experimental transient current curve for the 90° construction direction specimen, contrasted with standard progressive and instantaneous nucleation models.
summary: This panel illustrates the transient current curve for the 90° construction direction specimen of SLM-316L stainless steel. The experimental results, denoted by blue upright triangles, are compared to the black solid line representing the progressive nucleation model and the red solid line representing the instantaneous nucleation model to determine the film's growth kinetics.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for the pH = 9.5 classification model, indicating that higher green channel feature values increase the probability of a sample being assigned to this class.
summary: This beeswarm plot highlights the feature contributions for the pH = 9.5 classification. In contrast to the pH = 7 class, the model relies on the green feature, where an increase in its value significantly enhances the likelihood of a sample being correctly classified as belonging to the pH = 9.5 class.

caption: Three-dimensional scan of nine printed single-track wall samples arranged on a single build plate, illustrating the geometric outcomes of varied processing parameters.
summary: This 3D scan provides a comprehensive visualization of nine distinct single-track wall samples fabricated on a single build plate. By capturing the geometry of these samples, the figure effectively demonstrates the results of the 3D scanning procedure, highlighting the structural outcomes associated with the nine different processing parameters tested.

caption: Magnified 1800-1650 cm-1 region of the ATR-FTIR spectra highlighting characteristic PHBV absorption peaks.
summary: Zoomed view of the 1800-1650 cm-1 region reveals that no new absorption bands emerge in the blends. As the PHBV content increases, its characteristic peaks become clearly visible, while the Ecovio bands exhibit only minor changes in intensity and sharpness, confirming the successful integration of components without new chemical bonding.

caption: Proxigram analysis of the Y2O2S dispersoid showing the concentration profile of constituent elements, where oxygen signals originate from the decomposition of YO and OS species, confirming a stoichiometric Y:O:S ratio of approximately 37:39:20.
summary: Proxigram analysis of the Y2O2S dispersoid provides a quantitative composition profile. The data shows a Y:O:S ratio of 37:39:20, which is consistent with the Y2O2S phase. caption: 3D confocal imaging of the 45°/Bottom build angle surface, revealing large clusters of partially melted parasitic particles up to 100 μm in diameter.
summary: The 45°/Bottom surface exhibits a distinct topology characterized by large clusters of partially melted parasitic particles, reaching up to 200 μm in height. These clusters are composed of particles up to 100 μm in diameter, indicating significant agglomeration effects that differentiate the bottom surface from other orientations.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the composite sample.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the composite sample microstructure, where tungsten elements appear as bright regions due to their high atomic number, while silicon elements appear as dark regions. The image provides a clear visualization of the distribution of these elements within the composite matrix at the nanoscale.

caption: Reflectivity dynamics measured at the center of the laser beam for fluences of 1.36 J/cm2 and 2.69 J/cm2.
summary: Reflectivity dynamics at the laser beam center are plotted for two distinct fluences. The data reveals that reflectivity initially increases before declining. Notably, during the observed process, the reflectivity measured at 2.69 J/cm2 remains consistently lower than the reflectivity observed at the lower fluence of 1.36 J/cm2.

caption: Two-dimensional t-SNE projection of the [CLS] vector derived from the SaTNC model, where color intensity corresponds to the natural logarithm of creep rupture life.
summary: This panel displays a two-dimensional t-SNE projection of the [CLS] vector from the SaTNC model. The color mapping represents the natural logarithm of creep rupture life, illustrating how the model organizes high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional space to interpret creep performance characteristics of the analyzed superalloys.

caption: Atomic model of the Al2O3(0001)/Fe(111) interface, representing the optimized orientation for minimal mismatch.
summary: The Al2O3(0001)/Fe(111) interface is depicted here, highlighting the specific crystallographic orientation that minimizes lattice mismatch between the alumina substrate and the δ-Fe phase. This model provides a visual representation of the contacting planes identified as having the lowest mismatch in the study.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy plot illustrating the measured weight percentage of Nickel in the undeformed 70-30 sample.
summary: Nickel weight percentage distribution is presented via wavelength dispersive spectroscopy mapping for the undeformed 70-30 sample. By measuring these values, the study aims to confirm the precise chemical composition and detect any signs of elemental segregation, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the alloy's homogeneity in its initial undeformed state.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of 1a with Iod (8 × 10^-2 M) under 405 nm LED irradiation, displaying minor intensity increments over 2-minute irradiation periods.
summary: Investigation of the 1a/Iod system under 405 nm LED irradiation shows only minor intensity increments in the absorption spectrum after 1800 seconds. Similar to the 1a/EDB system, the presence of Iod alone does not lead to significant photochemical changes, suggesting limited reactivity under the specified irradiation conditions.

caption: Ambient-temperature magnetic hysteresis loop for the HT UMS sample, with an inset displaying the saturation magnetization and coercivity as a function of Mn content.
summary: The HT UMS sample exhibits a magnetic hysteresis loop measured at ambient temperature. An inset provides a detailed analysis of the saturation magnetization and coercivity values plotted against varying Mn content. These results, including the central section used to estimate coercivity, characterize the magnetic behavior of the UMS material series.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectra of the amorphous red-ZrO2 powder, highlighting a broad absorption band spanning from 340 nm to 600 nm.
summary: This panel displays the UV-visible absorption spectra of the amorphous red-ZrO2 powder. The data reveals a broad absorption band extending from 340 nm to 600 nm, which is characteristic of the optical properties induced by the presence of oxygen vacancies within the amorphous zirconium oxide matrix.

caption: Comparison between experimental wear rate data and predicted values generated by LR, SVM, and GPR machine learning models.
summary: This panel presents the performance metrics for three machine learning models, specifically Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), used to predict wear rates. The evaluation is based on the R-squared and root mean-square error (RMSE) values derived from the comparison with experimental data.

caption: Force-time (F-T) curves for the unit structure at 1.0 m/s impact velocity, showing the effect of varying the geometric parameter α.
summary: The F-T curves for the unit structure with different α values (16°, 20°, and 24°) are presented for a 1.0 m/s impact velocity. This plot characterizes the mechanical response of the unit structure as the parameter α is adjusted, serving as a reference for evaluating structural impact performance.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of MC3T3-E1 cells after live/dead staining, demonstrating high cell viability when cultured with 0.025 mg/mL extract.
summary: Live/dead staining images reveal the viability of MC3T3-E1 cells co-cultured with scaffold extracts. Observations confirm that the 0.025 mg/mL extract concentration is non-toxic, as evidenced by the presence of almost exclusively live cells, providing visual validation of the biocompatibility of the SrSC material for cellular applications.

caption: Chemical composition of the medium carbon steel substrate material.
summary: The substrate material utilized in the experiment is medium carbon steel. Panel (a) presents the specific chemical composition of this substrate, which serves as the base material for the subsequent surface treatment and experimental procedures described in the study.

caption: Flexural strength response surface showing the interaction between printing speed and layer thickness at a fixed printing speed of 20 mm/s.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the combined effect of printing speed and layer thickness on the flexural strength of the printed material. Specifically, panel (a) examines these parameters at a printing speed of 20 mm/s, providing insight into how these processing variables interact to influence the mechanical performance of the specimen.

caption: Spatial distribution of von Mises stresses across the completed TR-AFSD repair, with a white line indicating the cross-sectional plane analyzed in panel c.
summary: The distribution of von Mises stresses in the TR-AFSD repair is visualized after the completion of the process. The SPH model provides a detailed map of these stresses throughout the entire repair zone, with a white line marking the specific cross-section that is further examined in the subsequent panel.

caption: Schematic representation of the debonding defect geometry for specimen A180-AD, featuring a bonded length of 180 mm.
summary: This schematic illustrates the specific geometry of debonding defects observed in specimen A180-AD. With a defined bonded length of 180 mm, the diagram provides a clear visual representation of the defect configuration, which differs from other tested specimens as noted in the study by Wang et al.

caption: Close-up view of the 1500–700 cm-1 spectral range for the analyzed filler and polymer samples.
summary: This high-resolution view of the 1500–700 cm-1 spectral region further supports the morphological analysis of fillers extracted from the composites. The spectral data corroborates the embedding of PLA into the filler lumens, providing detailed chemical information regarding the filler-matrix interface within the composite system.

caption: Box plot illustrating the change in Sr/Ca level near the miniscrew surface, ΔSr/Ca0, showing a statistically significant difference between sample types (p=0.0036).
summary: This box plot compares the ΔSr/Ca0 parameter, representing the change in Sr/Ca levels near the miniscrew surface. The analysis reveals a statistically significant difference between the Ti-Sr-O and Ti miniscrew samples, with a p-value of 0.0036, highlighting the distinct impact of the surface treatment on local strontium levels.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profile confirming the elemental composition of a Ni17Y2 intermetallic particle.
summary: This panel presents the EDX spectrum of a Ni17Y2 particle, confirming its elemental identity. The spectroscopic data validates the presence of this specific intermetallic phase within the microstructure, supporting the characterization of the sample's secondary phases as observed in the associated microscopy analysis.

caption: Evaluation of the purple optical filter, displaying the commercial sample alongside the printed version predicted by the inverse RF model, which utilized a mixture of 0.5 drops of Navy Blue, 3.5 drops of Orchid, 3.0 drops of Ruby, and 4.5 drops of Violet.
summary: Presented here is the purple optical filter, showing both the commercial product and the printed version derived from the inverse RF model. The predicted ink formulation, consisting of Navy Blue, Orchid, Ruby, and Violet, was rounded for printing. Measured transmission spectra confirm the spectral characteristics of the resulting printed filter.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of a monocrystalline Ni alloy (111) oxidized at 350℃ for 5 minutes, showing elemental distribution trends.
summary: This ToF-SIMS profile illustrates the elemental distribution within a monocrystalline Ni alloy oriented along the (111) plane after 5 minutes of oxidation at 350℃. The analysis utilizes Bi+ and Cs+ ion beams to characterize the surface composition, providing insight into the initial stages of oxidation on the monocrystalline substrate.

caption: Overview of the LLM-based workflow designed for the detection of G-Code modifications in additive manufacturing systems.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the systematic workflow for detecting G-Code modifications using a Large Language Model. The solution is optimized for deployment on resource-constrained hardware, such as Raspberry Pi, enabling enhanced security monitoring for legacy manufacturing systems and older firmware versions that typically lack modern built-in security features.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) plot comparing the interfacial Si atom and its nearest-neighbor Ti atom on the α-Ti side.
summary: Partial density of states analysis for the bonding atom pairs at the interface demonstrates pronounced overlap and hybridization between the Si p-orbitals and Ti d-orbitals. These electronic interactions are specifically observed at energy levels of approximately -2.0 eV and -0.9 eV, confirming the nature of the interfacial chemical bonding.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of the as-built AM specimen, highlighting the presence of fine Ti-rich MC carbides and confirming the Ti- and Al-rich nature of the γ′ precipitates.
summary: The EDS elemental mapping of the as-built AM specimen reveals the chemical distribution of key alloying elements. The high contrast observed for Ti and Al confirms the presence of Ti- and Al-rich γ′ precipitates, while also allowing for the visualization of fine Ti-rich MC carbides within the microstructure.

caption: Experimental dependence of Young's modulus on indentation load for the cellular dendritic substructure.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between Young's modulus and indentation load for a cellular dendritic substructure composed of an aluminum matrix reinforced by an Al-Si network. Experimental nanoindentation data are presented, showing how elastic properties vary with load, with specific modulus values of 76.2 and 102.4 GPa falling within this range.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PEB236 synthesized without a coinitiator, showing a series of peaks corresponding to the composition {(C15H26O4)n + Na}+ from n = 3 to n = 14.
summary: The MALDI-TOF spectrum for the polymer obtained without coinitiator, PEB236, reveals a series of peaks corresponding to the composition {(C15H26O4)n + Na}+. These peaks range from n = 3 at m/z = 833 g/mol to n = 14 at m/z = 3807 g/mol, indicating the polymer's specific molecular weight distribution.

caption: Box-and-whisker distribution of intraventricular dyssynchrony (DYS) for left and right ventricles, alongside interventricular dyssynchrony (LVRV_S and LVRV_L), comparing Cardiac Performance Analysis (CPA) and prototype software (PS) across fetal cohorts of mothers with diabetes mellitus (FDM) and fetal controls (FC).
summary: This box-and-whisker plot compares DYS parameters measured by CPA and PS in FDM and FC cohorts. PS consistently shows lower scattering and values than CPA, though differences are not statistically significant. Notably, PS demonstrates a superior ability to distinguish between FDM and FC cohorts compared to the more comparable CPA results.

caption: Simulated kinetic evolution of MC and M6C precipitate radii within the FCC matrix of Inconel 625 at 800 °C as a function of isothermal holding time.
summary: This simulation illustrates the growth kinetics of MC and M6C precipitates in an Inconel 625 FCC matrix during isothermal holding at 800 °C. The results demonstrate that both precipitate phases stabilize within the γ matrix, reaching nanometer-scale diameters within a few hundred seconds, consistent with observed microstructural evolution in zone III.

caption: High-resolution Cu2p XPS spectrum of the Ti5Al3V6Cu alloy surface, displaying peaks at 931.62 eV and 951.82 eV attributed to Cu2O.
summary: The high-resolution Cu2p XPS spectrum for the Ti5Al3V6Cu alloy surface identifies the formation of Cu2O. The observed Cu2p 3/2 peak at 931.62 eV and the Cu2p 1/2 peak at 951.82 eV provide clear evidence of copper oxide species within the surface passive layer of the alloy.

caption: Grain orientation map of the solution heat-treated Inconel 625, with colors representing crystallographic orientations.
summary: The grain orientation map for the solution heat-treated condition illustrates the crystallographic texture following the homogenization process. By comparing this to the as-deposited state, the map confirms that the directional solidification characteristics are maintained, while the overall grain structure remains consistent with the DED fabrication method used for the sample.

caption: FT-IR ATR spectra comparing pure PLA, CH filler extract, AIL filler extract, CH virgin, and AIL virgin materials.
summary: FTIR-ATR spectroscopic analysis was performed on fillers extracted from the matrix to support morphological investigations. The spectra compare pure PLA with virgin and extracted CH and AIL fillers, providing chemical evidence of the filler-matrix interactions and the presence of PLA within the filler structures.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of BMSCs stained with live/dead dyes, Hoechst 33342, and DCFH-DA after 24 hours of exposure to 100 μM H2O2, showing reduced cell death and lower intracellular ROS levels in the presence of PLA/GA and PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF scaffolds.
summary: BMSCs exposed to 100 μM H2O2 demonstrate improved viability and reduced oxidative stress when cultured with PLA/GA and PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF scaffolds. Live/dead staining and DCFH-DA assays reveal that these scaffolds effectively mitigate H2O2-induced cell death and intracellular ROS production, as evidenced by the fluorescence microscopy images after 24 hours.

caption: Comparison of yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and elongation (EL) for HT1 and HT2 samples at room temperature.
summary: Yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation values are compared for HT1 and HT2 samples at room temperature. This bar chart summarizes the key mechanical properties, where numerical suffixes denote reproducible samples for each group, facilitating a direct assessment of the tensile performance variations between the two distinct sample sets.

caption: Atomic model of the L12-Ni3Al supercell structure.
summary: This panel displays the atomic model of the L12-Ni3Al supercell. The structure was constructed as part of a special quasi-random structure (SQS) supercell modeling approach to facilitate subsequent computational analysis of formation energies using VASP software, providing a baseline for comparing different Ni-based intermetallic phases.

caption: Evaluation of predictive expressions for the strain hardening exponent n using proof stresses σ0.03, σ0.04, and σ0.05.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the accuracy of predictive expressions for the strain hardening exponent n. Predicted values calculated from equations (9), (28), and (42) are plotted against experimental test values. The assessment incorporates different additional proof stresses, specifically σ0.03, σ0.04, and σ0.05, to determine the reliability of these models.

caption: X-ray diffraction spectra for AA, SA + AA, and HA + SA + AA samples, measured in the parallel direction relative to the building axis (z).
summary: This figure presents XRD spectra for AA, SA + AA, and HA + SA + AA samples, evaluated in the parallel building direction (z). These diffraction patterns are used to identify specific phases within the heat-treated samples, confirming the presence or absence of precipitates like g I and g II in the matrix.

caption: Synchrotron XRD patterns of samples processed by HPT for 50 revolutions at varying temperatures, displayed with logarithmic intensity scaling.
summary: Synchrotron XRD measurements are presented for samples deformed for 50 revolutions at various temperatures. The patterns, shown with logarithmic intensity scaling, reveal the structural evolution of the material under high-pressure torsion. These diffraction results provide the foundational data for analyzing phase formation and lattice parameter changes across the studied temperature range.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram of the 316L-AlSi10Mg system showing equilibrium phases across the full composition range.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram illustrates the equilibrium phases for the 316L-AlSi10Mg system. A red shaded region highlights compositions between 35% and 75% AlSi10Mg where primary intermetallic solidification occurs. The diagram serves as a reference for predicting phase formation, including B2 FeAl and NiAl intermetallics, in multi-material deposits.

caption: Spatial distribution of the powder flow and the corresponding temperature field calculated for the optimal injection point.
summary: This panel displays the coupled distribution of powder flow and temperature fields at the optimal injection point. By mapping these variables, the simulation demonstrates how the injection geometry influences thermal gradients and powder concentration, which are essential factors for achieving uniform material deposition and consistent sample quality.

caption: Crack density as a function of energy density for as-PBF Ni-based superalloy samples.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the baseline crack density in as-PBF Ni-based superalloy specimens across varying energy densities. The data, adapted from previous studies, establishes the initial state of microcracking before any post-processing treatments are applied, serving as a reference point for evaluating the effectiveness of subsequent healing procedures.

caption: Frequency-dependent viscoelastic response measured by sweeping angular frequency from 0.1 to 100 rad s−1 at a constant 1% strain.
summary: The frequency-dependent viscoelastic response of the hydrogel is examined by sweeping the angular frequency from 0.1 to 100 rad s−1 at a fixed strain of 1%. This plot characterizes the material's dynamic mechanical properties, providing insight into the frequency-dependent behavior of the 3D-printed hydrogel formulations.

caption: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) curve illustrating the tangent method used for the extraction of transformation temperatures (TTs).
summary: This panel displays a Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) curve, which serves as the basis for determining transformation temperatures. By applying the tangent method to the thermal data, researchers can precisely extract the numerical values of the TTs, as demonstrated in the associated experimental analysis and summarized in the study's data tables.

caption: Band gap energy determination for Zn1-xNixTe films derived from k-spectra analysis.
summary: This panel displays the band gap energy determination for Zn1-xNixTe films using k-spectra analysis. The experimental results indicate that the band gap energy values for these films range from 2.24 eV to 1.72 eV as the nickel concentration is systematically varied from 0.0 to 0.20.

caption: Dilatometric measurements of the AS1 specimen during a 0.167 °C/s heating ramp to 400 °C, showing dilation values and their corresponding derivative.
summary: Dilatometric analysis of the AS1 alloy during heating to 400 °C reveals dilation values and their derivatives. These thermal expansion characteristics, when analyzed alongside HEXRD data, provide evidence of precipitation kinetics. Specifically, the derivative analysis confirms that precipitation initiates near 250 °C and significant precipitate growth occurs above 300 °C.

caption: Alumina balls utilized as pins during the tribological wear tests.
summary: Alumina balls utilized as pins during the tribological wear tests are shown. To print these balls, a custom support structure was designed to prevent material displacement caused by the movement of the blades during the layer spreading process. These components serve as the counter-body pins in the wear experiments.

caption: Microhardness profile of the Case-4 specimen measured along the build direction at the middle cross-section.
summary: This panel displays the microhardness variation of the Case-4 specimen as a function of position along the build direction. The measurements were taken at the middle cross-section, providing a quantitative assessment of the mechanical properties and their spatial distribution resulting from the fabrication process.

caption: Two-dimensional SAXS patterns of PVDF-HFP at the polymer/polymer welding zone interface, displayed for 0.2, 1, 2, and 20 seconds post-deposition of the top 5th printed line.
summary: Captured at the welding zone interface, these SAXS patterns demonstrate the rapid crystallization kinetics characteristic of the polymer/polymer interface. The data confirms that structural development is faster at this location than in the bulk, supporting the analysis of orientation effects and crystallization behavior in 3D printed polymer materials.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of nitrogen distribution across the cBN and Ni-superalloy interface, highlighting the concentration gradient within the reaction zone.
summary: The EDS map for nitrogen reveals its specific distribution at the interface between cBN and the Ni-superalloy. Nitrogen is a primary constituent of the cBN phase, and its mapping helps delineate the reaction layer boundaries where the concentration of nitrogen shifts as it interacts with the superalloy components.

caption: Bode impedance plots for CP30 samples after 0, 14, and 28 days of immersion, illustrating the evolution of impedance magnitude.
summary: Bode impedance plots for CP30 samples show the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude over 28 days of immersion. Symbols represent experimental data, while solid lines indicate fitted results. These measurements provide insight into the electrochemical behavior of the porous surface, complementing the phase angle data and confirming the two-layer surface structure.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the compressed T III alloy.
summary: The GND density map for the compressed T III alloy reveals the spatial distribution of dislocation density. Reference data indicates that this state shows a specific level of dislocation accumulation at the node position, which is subsequently compared to the higher density observed under impact loading conditions.

caption: Material flow pattern during the third stage of ultrasonic vibration grinding.
summary: This panel illustrates the material flow during the third stage of the grinding process. As the process concludes, the simulation shows that the plastic deformation induced by grinding in the ground subsurface is weakened, reflecting the final state of material displacement and structural change within the workpiece.

caption: Optical micrograph of the alloy in the homogenized state, exhibiting a dual-phase FCC + BCC microstructure.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the alloy after homogenization, which results in a distinct dual-phase microstructure. The presence of both FCC and BCC phases is clearly observable in this state, confirming that the homogenization process successfully established the intended dual-phase configuration within the material's microstructure.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of DZ445 superalloy subjected to 32 min dwell time at 900 °C, illustrating dislocation configurations and interactions within the γ/γ′ microstructure.
summary: Following 32 minutes of dwell time at 900 °C, the DZ445 superalloy displays evolving dislocation configurations. The TEM imaging reveals how dislocation movement continues to influence the γ/γ′ microstructure under the applied 1.6% total strain range, contributing to the ongoing structural changes observed during the creep-fatigue deformation process.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the irradiated W-Ti-Cr-V specimen, highlighting small He cavities and a boundary-like feature in the upper right corner.
summary: Bright-field STEM imaging provides a clearer view of the He cavities within the irradiated W-Ti-Cr-V alloy. Despite an irradiation dose of approximately 10 dpa, the cavities remain small and show no signs of coalescence, even near the boundary-like feature observed in the upper right corner of the region.

caption: Surface topology map of the polished cone-like Ni-Co coating after a 1-week corrosion test in a CO2-saturated 3.5 wt % NaCl solution at 60 °C.
summary: Following a one-week corrosion test in a CO2-saturated 3.5 wt % NaCl solution at 60 °C, the surface topology of the cone-like Ni-Co coating remains intact. 3D laser confocal microscopy confirms the absence of pitting corrosion, demonstrating the coating's structural stability under these specific sweet corrosion test conditions.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectra of the Ni 2p region for the FeNi porous framework, highlighting shifts in valence states following degradation.
summary: High-resolution XPS spectra for the Ni 2p region are presented to illustrate the valence state changes of the Ni element in the FeNi porous framework. These spectra provide a detailed view of the surface chemical state modifications that occur as a result of the material degradation process.

caption: Phase angle Bode plot for the B10-0.1 wt% La alloy specimen after varying immersion durations in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This phase angle plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy characteristics of the B10-0.1 wt% La alloy during immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl. The frequency-dependent phase angle data highlights the electrochemical interface dynamics and surface stability of the alloy as it undergoes corrosion testing over various immersion time periods.

caption: Tauc plot representation showing the relationship between (hνα)1/2 and energy in eV, derived from diffuse reflectance measurements for various multilayer configurations.
summary: This panel displays the relationship between (hνα)1/2 and energy in eV for different TiO2 multilayers. Obtained via diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, these plots are used to determine the optical bandgap (Eg) of the deposited films, characterizing the electronic transition properties of the multilayered material system.

caption: Woehler (S-N) curve illustrating the fatigue performance of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V TPMS lattice structures with a relative density of 69.55%.
summary: This S-N curve characterizes the fatigue behavior of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V TPMS lattice structures with a density of 69.55%. The plot provides essential data for understanding the damage evolution and crack initiation processes, which are critical for evaluating the long-term mechanical performance of these complex lattice geometries under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Cross-sectional view and atomic displacement map of Ni50Co50 nanocrystalline models at 0.2 tensile strain, highlighting grain boundaries in purple and displacement vectors in red.
summary: This panel displays the microstructural evolution of Ni50Co50 nanocrystalline models at 0.2 tensile strain. The left side shows grain boundaries identified via PTM, while the right side maps atomic displacement vectors. Yellow arrows indicate macroscopic grain boundary motion along the tensile direction, illustrating the structural response to deformation.

caption: FTIR spectra of pristine n-HAP, gelatin, CNC, and CA materials.
summary: This panel displays the FTIR spectra of the pristine constituent materials, specifically n-HAP, gelatin, CNC, and CA. These spectra serve as the baseline reference for identifying characteristic chemical functional groups present in the raw components before they are processed into 3D-printed scaffolds.

caption: Conventional in-focus laser geometry configuration showing the convergence of six laser beams at the substrate surface.
summary: The diagram displays the conventional in-focus condition for the MBL-DED system. In this configuration, the six laser beams are focused directly onto the substrate surface, representing the standard geometric approach for laser beam alignment and energy delivery during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the starting materials with the resulting composite powder mixture.
summary: This panel displays the XRD patterns of the starting materials and the composite powder mixture. These results are used to evaluate phase formation and changes in plastic deformation occurring during the mixing process, providing insight into the structural evolution of the powders before and after the composite synthesis.

caption: Measured static toughness values for Ti 0, Ti 1, and Ti 2 alloys derived from room-temperature tensile testing.
summary: Static toughness values for Ti 0, Ti 1, and Ti 2 alloys were determined based on room-temperature tensile test results. The mechanical performance analysis indicates that the Ti 0 alloy displays insufficient strength, highlighting the impact of its small B2 precipitate fraction on overall mechanical properties.

caption: Tafel polarization curves illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of TiZrTaAg alloy samples.
summary: This figure displays the Tafel polarization plots for TiZrTaAg alloy samples, providing a visual representation of their electrochemical corrosion characteristics. These plots are essential for evaluating the corrosion resistance of the material, with the corresponding quantitative corrosion parameters detailed in the accompanying data table provided in the study.

caption: Complementary MAP analysis of the yellow boxed region from panel (c), illustrating the spatial arrangement of elements in the AlCr 1.3 TiNi 2 MEA.
summary: This MAP analysis complements the structural investigation by mapping the spatial arrangement of elements in the AlCr 1.3 TiNi 2 MEA. The results highlight the chemical variations present within the multi-scale hierarchical heterostructure, further validating the complex nature of the SPS-processed alloy's microstructure.

caption: Simulated solidification microstructure for the 11th layer at the corner position.
summary: Simulated solidification microstructure for the 11th layer at the corner position. Higher peak temperatures are observed, yet the larger temperature gradient relative to the surroundings results in a higher cooling rate than the middle region. This simulation, requiring 20 hours, illustrates the resulting microstructure for this specific layer and location.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric curves of PEEK-Ax samples highlighting the rate of mass loss.
summary: Derivative thermogravimetric curves of PEEK-Ax samples provide insight into the rate of thermal degradation. Analysis of these curves confirms that the peak degradation temperature for the PEEK-Ax series consistently exceeds 400 °C, demonstrating the robust thermal resistance of the printed polymer structures under the specified testing conditions.

caption: Surface flow behavior of the molten pool under a 4 mm groove gap condition.
summary: This panel illustrates the molten pool surface flow behavior specifically for a 4 mm groove gap. The visualization captures the fluid dynamics and surface flow patterns characteristic of the laser welding process under this specific geometric constraint, reflecting the influence of the gap width on molten metal movement.

caption: Detailed bright-field TEM image of the microstructure, identifying specific regions corresponding to the bcc β-phase and hcp α-phase lamellae.
summary: This detailed bright-field TEM image focuses on the microstructure of the AB + HT alloy, specifically distinguishing between the bcc β-phase and hcp α-phase regions. These structural areas serve as the basis for subsequent elemental analysis, allowing for a direct correlation between the observed phases and their local chemical compositions.

caption: Axial and radial lattice stresses for A356 and 316 L constituents, alongside nominal stress and rule-of-mixtures axial lattice stress, derived from in situ neutron diffraction data.
summary: This plot displays axial and radial lattice stresses for A356 and 316 L phases in a 50 vol% PrintCast composite. By comparing nominal stress with the rule-of-mixtures axial lattice stress, the results validate the lattice stress calculations, demonstrating excellent agreement and providing insight into load transfer mechanisms during in situ deformation.

caption: Long-term cycling performance of LSBs at 1C and 0 °C for 600 cycles with a sulfur loading of 1 mg cm-2.
summary: Long-term cycling performance of LSBs at 1C and 0 °C is evaluated over 600 cycles with a sulfur loading of 1 mg cm-2. This test demonstrates the robust performance and stability of the battery system under low-temperature conditions, highlighting the effectiveness of the ZnS@CCC interlayer for practical, high-rate applications.

caption: Fluorescence imaging providing confirmation of localized drug delivery within the porcine liver tissue.
summary: Fluorescence confirmation of localized drug delivery in a porcine liver is shown here, following the application of sono-ink hydrogels. This result supports the feasibility of using ultrasonic 4D printing for precise, in situ biomedical applications, ensuring that therapeutic delivery is achieved with minimal damage to surrounding tissues.

caption: Mass spectrum of FPEA-ProGly 3D-printed scaffold after CGRGDS peptide coupling.
summary: Coupling of the CGRGDS peptide onto the FPEA-ProGly 3D-printed scaffold is confirmed by this mass spectrum. The data illustrates that the peptide immobilization technique is effective not only on films but also on complex 3D-printed architectures. The measurement was performed over a 500 µm by 500 µm area.

caption: Interaction plot showing the combined effects of wall thickness and cell height on the yield strength of the scaffold design.
summary: The interaction plot highlights the combined influence of wall thickness and cell height on the yield performance of the scaffold. Both parameters exhibit negative quadratic relationships with yield strength, although wall thickness remains the principal determinant of yield performance, with cell height having a secondary, diminishing effect on the overall mechanical strength.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing iso-concentration surfaces for alloy 5 aged at 510 °C for 16 h.
summary: Represented here is the atom probe tomography reconstruction for alloy 5 following an aging treatment at 510 °C for 16 h. The iso-concentration surfaces illustrate the spatial arrangement of elements, allowing for a comparative analysis of the precipitate morphology and distribution within the alloy matrix.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map overlaid with a matching index map, highlighting the crystallographic orientation of the carbide phase.
summary: The IPF and matching index map provides crystallographic orientation data for the carbide phase. This map confirms the presence of a twinned carbonitride structure adjacent to the boride particles, further validating the structural identification of the phases observed in the carbon replica through the ACOM mapping technique.

caption: Geometric rendering of the Schoen Gyroid TPMS surface, visualized with polygonal facets and Z-axis color gradients.
summary: This panel displays the Schoen Gyroid surface, a widely utilized TPMS structure. The model is rendered using a simplified polygonal approach, with color variations applied to represent different Z-coordinates. This representation provides a clear view of the Gyroid's characteristic curvature and periodic structural arrangement.

caption: Two-dimensional Debye-Scherrer diffraction pattern showing four distinct hkl rings (111, 200, 220, 311) with highlighted gaps between detector modules.
summary: This 2-D diffraction pattern captures four quarter Debye-Scherrer rings corresponding to the 111, 200, 220, and 311 crystal planes. The image highlights two small regions where data collection was interrupted due to the three-module detector configuration, providing a visual representation of the experimental diffraction data acquisition process.

caption: Variation of the corrosion rate with respect to grain size in the manufactured nanocomposites.
summary: The corrosion rate is plotted against grain size for the nanocomposite samples. Increasing the tool rotation speed from 1200 to 1500 rpm results in larger grain sizes, which reduces corrosion-prone areas and significantly influences the overall corrosion rate observed in the H4 sample during the experimental testing.

caption: Time-averaged irreversible heat generation rates for NMC622 working electrodes in calorimetric cells, comparing 3D printed and 2D tape-casted architectures as a function of applied current.
summary: This plot displays the time-averaged irreversible heat generation rates for calorimetric cells featuring NMC622 working electrodes. By comparing 3D printed and 2D tape-casted samples, the data illustrates how these distinct manufacturing methods influence thermal dissipation behavior across varying current levels during constant current cycling of the electrochemical cells.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the LRM sample obtained from a gamma reflection, highlighting the distribution and morphology of the retained austenite laths.
summary: Utilizing a gamma reflection, this dark-field TEM image specifically highlights the retained austenite laths within the LRM microstructure. The visualization confirms the presence and spatial arrangement of these austenite regions, which align with Ni-enriched areas as noted in the supporting reference material for this characterization.

caption: Comparison of interfacial toughness between multi-material objects created by CMM-3DP and those produced via traditional 3D printing methods.
summary: This plot compares the interfacial toughness of multi-material objects fabricated using CMM-3DP versus traditional 3D printing. The results highlight the superior mechanical performance of the capillary-driven approach in creating robust interfaces between different materials within the printed structures.

caption: Measured hardness versus displacement curve for the as-casted HEA, demonstrating a linear log-log relationship.
summary: The hardness versus displacement (HD-h) curve for the as-casted HEA is presented in a log-log format, which reveals a linear relationship. This plot is essential for determining the h p * values, facilitating a deeper understanding of the indentation size effect and mechanical hardness characteristics of the alloy.

caption: CALPHAD-calculated phase stability diagram for the Ni-Ti alloy composition corresponding to point 5, containing 98.6% Ni and 1.4% Ti.
summary: This CALPHAD-calculated phase stability diagram represents the thermodynamic equilibrium for the Ni-Ti alloy composition at point 5, which consists of 98.6% Ni and 1.4% Ti. The diagram is based on EDS-analyzed alloys from welded specimens brushed with 70% Ni powder, highlighting the phase stability characteristics of this high-nickel content alloy.

caption: Young’s modulus variation as a function of the applied DC magnetic field, highlighting the suppression of magneto-mechanical coupling due to crystallization.
summary: Young's modulus dependence on the applied DC magnetic field reveals a significant reduction in sensitivity following crystallization. The data confirms that the variation in Young's modulus is nearly completely suppressed in some cases, demonstrating that the crystallization process effectively stabilizes the mechanical response of the alloys against external magnetic fields.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of Alloy S3 after aging, displaying the reprecipitated, finer dispersoid distribution.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of Alloy S3 following aging at 350 °C for 4 hours shows the reprecipitation of finer α-AlMn-dispersoids. This aging step results in an increased number density of dispersoids compared to the extruded state, effectively refining the microstructure and reversing some of the coarsening effects observed after extrusion.

caption: Atomic model of the Ni2B crystal structure, illustrating the arrangement of nickel atoms in blue and boron atoms in green.
summary: This panel displays the atomic unit cell structure of the Ni2B reaction product formed between cBN and Ni-superalloy. The visualization highlights the specific spatial arrangement of nickel and boron atoms, providing a clear representation of the crystal lattice configuration identified in the reaction zone of the material interface.

caption: Visual representation of a 4×8 mm cubic sample manufactured by PBF-LB/M, highlighting the spatial distribution of the h d 50 and h d 70 scanning parameter domains.
summary: The 4×8 mm cubic sample is shown here, manufactured through PBF-LB/M processing. The image illustrates the integration of h d 50 and h d 70 scanning parameter sets, which are represented by different shades of gray. This panel provides a clear view of the sample dimensions and the distinct parameter-defined regions.

caption: Vertical centerline hardness map of the NiTi sample manufactured with an interlayer temperature of 400 °C, demonstrating the influence of thermal history on mechanical properties.
summary: This hardness map depicts the mechanical property distribution along the vertical centerline of a NiTi sample fabricated via wire arc additive manufacturing. By applying an interlayer temperature of 400 °C, the map illustrates how specific thermal processing parameters influence the resulting hardness variation throughout the cross-section of the additively manufactured material.

caption: Wave profile of Pxx stress component at t = 8.9 ps, showing the shock front arrival at the marked plane I2.
summary: At t = 8.9 ps, the shock front arrives at the I2 interface. The incident wave magnitude is approximately 22.9 GPa, while the transmitted wave strength reaches 24.25 GPa. This observation confirms the ongoing reflection-unloading processes caused by interfacial reflections within the Ni/Ni3Al multilayer structure during shock compression.

caption: Optical transmission profile of a 3D-printed multi-material disk utilizing Atto425, Atto495, and Atto565 dyes, with 0.5 mm thick sections.
summary: This panel presents the optical transmission profile for a 3D-printed multi-material disk containing Atto425, Atto495, and Atto565 dyes. With a section thickness of 0.5 mm, this configuration is noted for being closer to the intended spectrum for Pilestone applications compared to other tested three-dye combinations.

caption: Confocal microstructure of an AA F Ti particle following the compression test, highlighting deformation features.
summary: Post-compression confocal imaging of the AA F Ti particle demonstrates the resulting morphological changes. The microstructure reveals deformation patterns, specifically noting that oxide fracture patterns at highly strained sides are closely related to the presence of shear bands formed during the compression process applied to the Ti powder.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of the coarse-grained (CG) zone located at the bottom section of the as-built specimen, displaying dislocation entanglement around precipitate pairs.
summary: This bright-field STEM image captures the coarse-grained zone within the bottom section of the as-built specimen. The microstructure reveals clear entanglement of dislocations surrounding Mg-rich and Fe-Mn-rich precipitate pairs. These structural features, resulting from rapid thermal cycling during the PBF process, effectively hinder dislocation movement within the material matrix.

caption: Circulating flow pattern established as a SiC particle returns to the central melt pool after reaching the boundaries, demonstrating the interaction of relevant forces.
summary: This panel visualizes the interaction of all relevant forces acting on the particle, which leads to the establishment of a circulating flow within the melt pool. The particle is shown returning to the central region after reaching the melt pool boundaries, completing a cycle of fluid motion.

caption: TGA thermograms showing the thermal degradation behavior of composites formulated with CNC concentrations ranging from 1% to 15%.
summary: Thermal degradation profiles for composites containing varying CNC concentrations from 1% to 15% are presented in this panel. The TGA curves demonstrate how increasing the loading of cellulose nanocrystals influences the overall thermal stability of the resin composites, allowing for an assessment of the concentration-dependent degradation characteristics.

caption: Reconstruction slice of the part produced without optimization, showing non-uniform dose distribution.
summary: The reconstruction slice reveals significant inhomogeneity, with the ring and central shaft regions receiving lower doses compared to the top and bottom sections. This lack of optimization results in poor dose uniformity and a wider overlap between in-part and out-of-part voxels, which ultimately reduces the resolution of the printed part.

caption: Atomic configuration of a fracture model consisting of 4 atomic layers with a 10 Å vacuum slab.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configuration of a fracture model containing 4 atomic layers. The simulation setup incorporates a vacuum slab with a thickness of 10 Å to facilitate the study of fracture behavior within the material structure, providing a baseline for comparing different layer thicknesses in the computational model.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry response of the asymmetric supercapacitor device recorded at various scan rates to evaluate electrochemical behavior.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves are presented at various scan rates to characterize the electrochemical performance of the Co-Ni/rGO //3D rGO aerogel asymmetric supercapacitor. These measurements help assess the capacitive behavior and kinetic response of the electrode materials across different operational speeds.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the Ta4HfC5 sample fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), displaying characteristic peaks of a single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure.
summary: The XRD pattern confirms that the Ta4HfC5 sample produced by LPBF consists of a single-phase solid solution with a face-centered cubic crystal structure. The analysis reveals no impurity peaks and identifies a lattice constant of 4.49128 Å, demonstrating the successful synthesis of a high-purity phase through the LPBF process.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation diagram depicting the formation kinetics of γ′-phase in LAM-Inconel 718, showing accelerated precipitation compared to γ''-phase.
summary: This TTT diagram depicts the formation kinetics of the γ′-phase in LAM-Inconel 718. The data indicates that the γ′-phase forms earlier during the aging treatment compared to the γ''-phase, emphasizing the distinct temporal requirements for the precipitation of these two secondary phases based on the material's Al concentration.

caption: {111} and {200} pole figures for the as-homogenized reinforced specimen, featuring Al2O3 nanoparticles and a central concentration of high-intensity poles in the {200} diagram.
summary: The {111} and {200} pole figures for the as-homogenized reinforced alloy containing Al2O3 nanoparticles are shown. Similar to the base alloy, the {200} pole diagram exhibits a concentration of poles with high relative intensity located at the center, indicating the initial crystallographic texture of the reinforced material.

caption: Normalized transmission intensity measurements for seven distinct chip designs featuring a 350 µm spacing, with intensities normalized relative to the T-7 design.
summary: Transmission intensity measurements for seven chip designs with 350 µm spacing are presented, normalized against the T-7 design. The flat chip design, T-1, exhibits the lowest transmission intensity, which is consistent with simulation results, highlighting the impact of design geometry on the overall optical performance of the probing system.

caption: Schematic illustration of the HPCA ink design, featuring the esterification of hydroxypropyl cellulose with acryloyl chloride to incorporate photo-cross-linkable vinyl groups for the formation of stable, temperature-insensitive, and acid-resistant chiral nematic liquid crystalline structures.
summary: This schematic illustrates the synthesis of HPCA ink, where acryloyl chloride is esterified with hydroxypropyl cellulose to introduce photo-cross-linkable vinyl groups. This design enables the creation of chiral nematic liquid crystalline structures that exhibit exceptional stability, maintaining their color under varying temperatures and in highly acidic conditions (pH = 1).

caption: Diffusion paths for the 3L|1R couple plotted on a phase diagram, where blue squares indicate end-member compositions and dashed lines highlight concentration jumps within the simulated path.
summary: Diffusion paths for the 3L|1R couple are mapped onto the phase diagram in this panel. Blue squares represent the specific compositions of the end-members, while dashed lines clearly mark the concentration jumps observed along the simulated diffusion path, providing a visual representation of the phase evolution during the diffusion process.

caption: Angle of Linear Polarization (AOLP) image captured by a polarisation camera at the initial starting position, illustrating the defined fibre orientations.
summary: This panel displays an AOLP image acquired via a polarisation camera at the starting position. It serves as the primary visual representation for defining fibre orientations within the material, providing the foundational data necessary for subsequent image processing and the derivation of orientation statistics.

caption: Refractive index measurements for the commercial eye drops compared against the physiological range of the human cornea.
summary: This plot displays the refractive index values for the four HA-based eye drops. All measured values, ranging from 1.3348 to 1.3410, are within the physiological range of the human cornea (1.3350–1.4291). These findings indicate that the optical properties of the eye drops are well-aligned with human corneal requirements.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectra of O-16 and ITX in acetonitrile, highlighting the significantly higher molar extinction coefficient of ITX (3030 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹) compared to O-16 (200 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹) at 395 nm.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectra in acetonitrile reveal the optical properties of the components. ITX exhibits much stronger photon absorption at the 395 nm irradiation wavelength compared to the oxime ester O-16, confirming its role as an effective sensitizer for the photopolymerization process in the benchmark blend.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map and corresponding pole figures at the 50-50 | 25-75 interface of the F25 sample.
summary: This panel displays the IPF map and pole figures for the 50-50 | 25-75 interface. The structural analysis indicates a transition back to a randomized texture, marking a specific phase in the sinusoidal evolution of grain structure observed along the building direction of the F25 sample.

caption: X-ray computed tomography (XCT) reconstruction of Specimen #4, highlighting specific internal morphology that contributes to prediction discrepancies.
summary: Specimen #4 is visualized via XCT reconstruction to examine its internal morphology. Similar to Specimen #1, this specimen contains unique mesoscopic characteristics not present in other samples from the same built wall. These structural variations are identified as a primary source of discrepancy in the interface strength prediction model.

caption: Infrared absorbance spectra plotted against wavenumber for the testing zone rectangle, highlighting the characteristic Fe-O stretching vibration band between 565 and 580 cm-1 for various Fe3O4 concentrations.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy is employed to analyze the testing zone squares containing different Fe3O4 concentrations. The spectra reveal the characteristic Fe-O stretching vibration band located between 565 and 580 cm-1, which is indicative of highly crystalline Fe3O4 nanoparticles, allowing for the correlation of absorbance intensity with the nanoparticle weight percentage.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the MgO(100)/Fe(100) interface showing the plane pair with minimum lattice mismatch.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic configuration of the MgO(100)/Fe(100) interface. It represents the specific crystallographic plane pair identified as having the minimum lattice mismatch between the metal oxide substrate and the δ-Fe phase, as determined by the calculated results summarized in the study's supporting data.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer, highlighting chemical shifts at 1.3, 3.9, 4.0, and 4.8 ppm.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer is presented, with prominent peaks identified at 1.3, 3.9, 4.0, and 4.8 ppm. These specific chemical shifts provide a useful basis for confirming the presence of benzylic and aromatic protons within the molecular structure of the BBZ monomer.

caption: Height maps visualizing the dynamic evolution of Ti nanoparticle arrangement during laser irradiation, capturing pore filling, particle coalescence, and layer densification.
summary: These height maps capture the atomic rearrangements of Ti nanoparticles during the laser heating stage. The visualization tracks the evolution of the material structure, specifically highlighting key densification mechanisms such as pore filling and particle coalescence as the laser irradiation progresses through the nanoparticle bed.

caption: Biaxial strain path segment of a discontinuous loading sequence, displaying a slope of 5.08 ± 0.03 N/μm with regular force drops indicating elongation pauses.
summary: This biaxial segment of the discontinuous loading sequence exhibits a high slope of 5.08 ± 0.03 N/μm. The force-displacement curve is marked by regular drops in force, confirming that the specimen elongation was systematically interrupted every 0.2 mm to facilitate the collection of XRD data during the biaxial test.

caption: Schematic representation of the Ni-Sn peritectic region highlighting the liquidus lines and constrained equilibrium conditions at temperature T exp.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Ni-Sn peritectic region, showing the peritectic temperature Tp and the liquidus lines for the alpha and beta phases. It highlights the constrained equilibrium at the annealing temperature T exp, defining the melt compositions at the beta melting front and alpha growth front during phase transformation.

caption: Feature importance evaluation for ultimate tensile strength using the drop-column method, highlighting positive contributors in blue and negative contributors in red.
summary: The drop-column method is applied here to evaluate feature importance for ultimate tensile strength. Blue bars denote features that enhance prediction accuracy, whereas red bars indicate features that detract from it. This visualization clarifies the relative contribution of each input feature to the ultimate tensile strength model.

caption: Decomposition of a representative TDS spectrum into four distinct Gaussian distributions, where each peak represents a specific hydrogen population associated with a unique trapping energy.
summary: The TDS spectrum is mathematically decomposed into four Gaussian peaks to isolate individual hydrogen populations. Each of these peaks corresponds to a specific hydrogen population sharing a common trapping energy, providing a detailed breakdown of the various binding sites present within the material's microstructure during the thermal desorption process.

caption: Van't Hoff curves derived from the hydrogen desorption platform pressures of the La0.6Y0.15Ca0.9Mg1.05Ni9Cox alloys.
summary: The van't Hoff curves are plotted based on the hydrogen desorption platform pressures obtained from the PCT measurements at different temperatures. These curves allow for the calculation of thermodynamic parameters, such as enthalpy and entropy changes, providing insight into the effect of cobalt substitution on the hydrogen storage properties.

caption: Fracture surface of an AAP specimen, displaying the fracture features and crack path development under fatigue loading conditions.
summary: This panel presents the fracture surface of the AAP specimen, highlighting the structural response to fatigue loading. The high-magnification inset, indicated by the colored rectangular box, provides detailed insight into the fracture surface topography, confirming the crack initiation and propagation behavior observed in the AAP material under the applied stress.

caption: HFR Cell evolution during the 40 s timeframe around 5 h, detailing individual pulse responses.
summary: This panel focuses on the HFR Cell evolution during the 40 s timeframe around 5 h. By presenting individual pulses, it provides a detailed look at the resistance behavior of the FeNi alloy disk, complementing the broader observations of the 10 h stability test.

caption: Niobium XPS spectrum for WA IN625 powder, showing the absence of NbC.
summary: This panel displays the Niobium XPS spectrum for WA IN625 powder. The absence of NbC on the surface is attributed to higher cooling rates during atomization and negligible carbon concentration in the pre-alloyed powders, distinguishing the surface chemistry of WA powder from the other variants presented.

caption: Output power (P) versus MLL current (IMLL) characteristics for the BOSL device, measured at a reverse bias of VSA = -1.8 V and IG = 0 mA.
summary: This panel displays the typical output power versus MLL current characteristics for the BOSL device. The measurement is performed under MLM operation with a reverse bias of VSA = -1.8 V applied to the saturable absorber and an IG of 0 mA, establishing the baseline performance for the device's mode-locking behavior.

caption: Rietveld refinement of SR-PXD data for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 at 310 K during heating, highlighting the fit between experimental and calculated diffraction patterns.
summary: Rietveld refinement results for the Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 alloy at 310 K during heating are shown. The plot compares experimental diffraction data with calculated intensities and includes a difference plot. Structural phases, including TiNiSi, Ni2In, and MgZn2, are identified by tick marks positioned below the diffraction patterns.

caption: STEM-DF micrograph of an MC carbide particle processed with HT_32 thermal exposure.
summary: This STEM-DF micrograph displays an MC carbide particle subjected to HT_32 thermal exposure. The image provides structural visualization of the particle, which is identified as an intragranular-type MC carbide. The particle exhibits distinct morphology under these specific thermal conditions, serving as the basis for subsequent elemental mapping analysis.

caption: Ashby chart comparing the compressive strength versus density for various commercial core structures and printed trabecular architectures (L3, L6, L10).
summary: This Ashby chart benchmarks the mechanical performance of printed trabecular architectures, specifically variants L3, L6, and L10, against standard commercial core materials. By plotting compressive strength as a function of density, the figure validates the structural efficiency of these printed designs relative to established industrial core alternatives.

caption: Arrhenius plot comparing the first-principles calculated self-diffusion coefficient of nickel against experimental literature values.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the self-diffusion coefficient of nickel calculated from first principles. The calculated data shows strong agreement with experimental literature values in the intermediate temperature regime, while maintaining consistency within an order of magnitude in the high-temperature regime, validating the accuracy of the first-principles computational approach.

caption: Box plot illustrating the distribution of prediction accuracies for Model 1, which utilizes signal spectrograms exclusively from printing cycles across training, validation, and testing datasets.
summary: Model 1 performance is evaluated using box plots representing training, validation, and testing accuracies derived from 8-fold cross-validation. These plots visualize the distribution of prediction accuracy when the model is trained solely on printing cycle spectrograms, showing statistically similar performance results when compared to the combined Model 3 approach.

caption: Surface view micro-CT image of a thin wall fabricated with low energy density and high hatch distance, showing significant lack-of-fusion defects.
summary: Micro-CT imaging reveals that thin walls produced with low energy density and high hatch distance exhibit high defect fractions exceeding 14%. These defects are primarily attributed to insufficient powder melting during the LPBF process, which results in numerous lack-of-fusion voids visible within the thin-walled structure.

caption: Absorption characteristics of individual photoinitiating system components, highlighting the new compound's visible light absorption extending up to 520 nm.
summary: This UV-Vis spectrum illustrates the absorption characteristics of individual components within the investigated photoinitiating systems. The new compound demonstrates significant radiation absorption in the visible range, reaching up to 520 nm. This spectral profile indicates its potential as an effective photosensitizer for iodonium salts when utilizing visible light sources.

caption: Schematic representation of the laser powder bed fusion process showing the laser beam interacting with IN625 powder on a steel substrate, highlighting the associated thermal evolution during deposition.
summary: This schematic illustrates the laser powder bed fusion process for IN625 alloy deposition onto a steel substrate. It highlights the interaction between the laser beam and the powder, which leads to material amalgamation and subsequent temperature evolution, providing a foundational view of the thermal dynamics involved in the printing process.

caption: Effective refractive index n_eff plotted against phonon frequency ω for a SiGe phononic crystal (PnC) cavity, illustrating the rapid growth of n_eff in the region where the PnC band structure flattens.
summary: This plot displays the effective refractive index n_eff as a function of phonon frequency ω within a SiGe phononic crystal cavity. The data demonstrates a rapid increase in n_eff corresponding to the flattening of the PnC band, which is a critical feature for driving the cross-section toward higher values at practical scales.

caption: Binary Ni-Si phase diagram illustrating thermodynamic equilibrium states across varying compositions and temperatures.
summary: The Ni-Si phase diagram provides essential thermodynamic insights for selecting material compositions. At a specific composition of 77.6 wt% Ni and 32.4 wt% Si, the diagram predicts the primary solidification of the NiSi phase, followed by the eutectic solidification of NiSi and NiSi2 as the liquid composition evolves toward the eutectic point.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the middle layer illustrating grain morphology after thermal cycling.
summary: This IPF map displays the middle layer of the build produced at room temperature. Following repeated thermal cycling, the morphology of the equiaxed grains remains unaltered compared to the top layer, maintaining consistent structural characteristics throughout the middle section of the material build.

caption: Climb velocity profiles for the initial material conditions during creep testing at 622 MPa.
summary: Climb velocity profiles are displayed for the initial material conditions during creep testing at 622 MPa. This panel characterizes the contribution of dislocation climb to the overall creep performance, illustrating how the initial microstructure affects the rate of these diffusion-assisted processes under the specified loading conditions.

caption: 3D point cloud data generated from the surface contour scanning of the bead.
summary: The 3D point cloud data shown here is generated directly from the surface contour scanning procedure. This representation provides the foundational spatial information necessary for subsequent cross-sectional analysis, capturing the complex geometry of the deposited bead in a three-dimensional digital format.

caption: High-resolution TEM image focusing on the interface between the short rod-like κ Ⅲ phase and the α-matrix.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging reveals the interface between the short rod-shaped κ Ⅲ phase and the α-matrix. This observation is critical for understanding the structural relationship between these phases, as it demonstrates that the κ Ⅲ phase maintains a specific Kurdjumov-Sachs orientation relationship with the surrounding α-matrix within the alloy.

caption: Refractive index n and extinction coefficient k as a function of electronic temperature (0–30,000 K) for crystalline alloys at a laser wavelength of 400 nm.
summary: This plot illustrates the refractive index and extinction coefficient for various crystalline alloys at a laser wavelength of 400 nm. The data shows that the refractive index exhibits a radically different response to electronic excitation within the temperature range of 0 to 30,000 K compared to other wavelengths.

caption: Radar plot comparing the normalized mechanical performance metrics of yield strength, total elongation, and reduction in area for the ASP-X specimen under varying irradiation doses.
summary: The ASP-X specimen's mechanical property evolution is depicted here through a radar chart. It maps the relationship between yield strength and ductility metrics (total elongation and reduction in area) across three irradiation levels, providing a clear visual representation of how irradiation history influences the material's hardening and ductility balance.

caption: Antibacterial plate assay images displaying inhibition zones against Pseudomonas aeruginosa for TSdECM-0 and TSdECM/AV composite scaffolds.
summary: Antibacterial performance of 3D-printed scaffolds was evaluated against Pseudomonas aeruginosa using a disc diffusion assay. Panel a presents the visual plate assay results, showing the inhibition zones formed by TSdECM-0 and TSdECM/AV composite scaffolds, which demonstrate the antibacterial efficacy of the materials against the tested bacterial strain.

caption: Bar chart comparing the wear volume of four distinct Ni@Gr/Ni-based coating specimens.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the comparative wear volume performance of four different Ni@Gr/Ni-based coatings. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the tribological resistance for each coating variant, highlighting the specific wear volume values obtained during testing to evaluate the effectiveness of the Ni@Gr/Ni-based material composition.

caption: Energy-volume (E–V) curve and the corresponding relaxed crystal structure for the Ni25Co75 alloy.
summary: Calculated via DFT, this panel shows the E–V curve for the Ni25Co75 alloy composition. The plot reflects the energy response across six fixed volumes during relaxation, allowing for the identification of the equilibrium volume and energy state characteristic of this specific nickel-cobalt atomic ratio.

caption: Arrhenius plots illustrating methane pyrolysis kinetics in molten Sn and SnNi alloy systems, demarcated by their respective lower and upper experimental temperature limits.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the kinetic data for methane pyrolysis experiments 1–5 conducted in molten Sn and SnNi alloys. The visualization highlights the temperature-dependent reaction rates, clearly defining the lower and upper experimental temperature boundaries for these specific molten metal systems as detailed in the supporting information.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the 13 μm SiC raw material.
summary: This X-ray diffraction pattern identifies the main phase compositions of the 13 μm SiC raw material. The diffraction peaks confirm the crystalline structure and phase purity of the SiC powder, providing essential baseline data for the material characterization performed in this research.

caption: Microhardness distribution profile measured across the bottom region of the WAAM structure.
summary: The microhardness variation in the bottom region of the WAAM structure is presented. This specific area exhibits higher hardness values, which is attributed to a higher dislocation density within the material microstructure. These measurements provide critical insight into the mechanical property gradients inherent in the fabricated WAAM component.

caption: Aberration distribution profile at a depth of 400 um, accompanied by the corresponding wavefront sensor image used to characterize the optical distortion.
summary: Panel b illustrates the spatial distribution of aberrations at a depth of 400 um within the glass. It includes the raw image captured by the wavefront sensor, which serves as the basis for calculating the aberration profile and evaluating the optical performance at this specific depth.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the distribution of strains in the load direction (εyy) for specimen TS-C2 at maximum compressive force.
summary: This contour plot displays the εyy strain distribution for a 16 mm bolt specimen under compressive loading at maximum force. The DIC measurements reveal that significant strain concentrations are localized exclusively above the hole, specifically in the region adjacent to the contact surface between the bolt and the eye bar component.

caption: Magnetic B-H hysteresis loop characterizing the magnetic performance of the as-printed additive manufacturing (AM) core.
summary: This panel displays the B-H hysteresis loop for the as-printed additive manufacturing core. The plot illustrates the magnetic response and characteristic behavior of the material in its initial state following the printing process, providing a baseline for evaluating the magnetic properties of the core before any subsequent thermal treatment.

caption: Virtual cross-sectional cut through the as-built (AB) cylinder, showing the initial morphology of lack of fusion defects.
summary: A virtual cross-sectional cut through the as-built cylinder reveals the initial morphology of lack of fusion defects. The random coloring applied to the pores facilitates the visualization of their spatial distribution and size, establishing the baseline state for the porosity evolution analysis.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the specific impact strength of sandwich samples to provide a normalized comparison across different configurations.
summary: Specific impact strength values for the sandwich samples are presented in this bar chart. By normalizing the impact data, this comparison provides clearer insights into the performance of the sandwich structures, confirming the influence of infill distribution on the mechanical integrity and energy absorption capabilities of the tested specimens.

caption: Logarithmic current density versus inverse charge density plot for PM-HIP3, illustrating the re-passivation kinetics under high-field conditions.
summary: Representing the re-passivation kinetics for PM-HIP3, this log(i) versus Q^-1 plot validates the high-field model. The estimated re-passivation rates are closely similar to those of PM-HIP1 at both applied potentials, indicating that the powder metallurgy processing route results in consistent electrochemical re-passivation characteristics for these specific alloy samples.

caption: Digital image correlation strain map showing the development of crazing in compressed molded ABS during a tensile test, visualized through red color intensity.
summary: Digital image correlation strain mapping reveals the progression of crazing in compressed molded ABS specimens subjected to tensile loading. The visualization highlights the localized deformation through red color intensity, providing experimental evidence of damage evolution that is consistent with the internal length scale parameters used in fracture modeling.

caption: Laser absorptivity measurements for pristine and TiN-doped IN 718 composite powders, plotted as a function of wavelength between 1000 and 1200 nm.
summary: Laser absorptivity of pristine and TiN-doped IN 718 composite powders is analyzed using UV-Vis spectroscopy. The data shows that absorptivity progressively increases with higher TiN content within the 1000–1200 nm wavelength range, highlighting the critical influence of TiN doping on the optical properties of the composite powders.

caption: Surface plot depicting elemental enrichment and diffusion characteristics in the region behind the melt pool interface, independent of input energy.
summary: This surface plot characterizes the elemental enrichment and diffusion dynamics occurring in the region behind the melt pool interface. It illustrates the influence of process parameters on material composition, maintaining independence from the total energy input to isolate the specific effects of scan speed and power on the build-up.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the as-built surface of a vertically printed LPBF SS316L sample, highlighting the grain orientation distribution.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the as-built surface microstructure of a vertically printed LPBF SS316L sample. The visualization reveals large columnar grains formed under high thermal gradients during the additive manufacturing process, characterized by a significant fraction of <111> crystallographic orientation within the printed material structure.

caption: Top view of a single unit cell featuring a central circular hollow cavity designed for tensile specimen integration.
summary: This top view illustrates the geometry of a single unit cell containing a circular hollow cavity.
