summary: This plot illustrates the fracture limit curve for a material characterized by a density ratio of ρ = 0.25. The curve serves as a predictive criterion for failure, with results derived from the GE-RIS and UDAD methods, providing a comparative analysis against experimental data to validate the accuracy of these fracture criteria.

caption: Comparison of microhardness values for IN718 reinforced with 4 wt% CrFeNb against previously reported IN718 variants processed via LPBF and traditional manufacturing techniques.
summary: This plot illustrates the microhardness performance of IN718 alloy modified with 4 wt% CrFeNb particles. By benchmarking these results against established data for IN718 produced through both LPBF and traditional methods, the figure highlights the mechanical impact of the specific particle reinforcement on the alloy's overall hardness characteristics.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph illustrating the internal microstructure of the as-built sample within the melt pool interior.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a detailed view of the microstructure within the melt pool interior of the as-built sample. The high-angle annular dark-field imaging technique highlights the structural features present in the middle layer of the specimen, serving as a baseline for further localized elemental and crystallographic analysis.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the initial raw powder, illustrating the heat flow as a function of temperature during heating and cooling cycles.
summary: The DSC curve of the raw powder reveals two distinct transformation steps during both heating and cooling processes. These thermal events correspond to the phase transitions between the austenite (B2) phase, the R phase, and the martensite (B19′) phase, characterizing the transformation behavior of the initial material.

caption: Half-cell resistances for NMC622 and lithium metal electrodes estimated at constant C-rates for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted cell configurations.
summary: Panel (b) displays the estimated half-cell resistances for the NMC622 and lithium metal components. These values are derived at constant C-rates to evaluate the electrochemical performance of the 3D printed and 2D tape-casted electrodes, serving as a basis for verifying consistency with total cell resistance measurements.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric analysis (DTGA) curves showing the rate of mass loss for CA, MCC, and the pCA/MCC/peroxide system, highlighting specific degradation peaks.
summary: Derivative thermogravimetric analysis curves provide the rate of mass loss for CA, MCC, and the pCA/MCC/peroxide system. These plots complement the TGA data by identifying the precise temperatures at which maximum degradation rates occur, confirming the thermal behavior of the CA 2.25 sample within the established 350-400 °C range.

caption: EBSD phase map overlaid with image quality for as-deposited Cu-40Zn in the TC region processed at 500 °C.
summary: Captured from the TC region, this EBSD phase map and image quality overlay depicts the microstructure of as-deposited Cu-40Zn processed at 500 °C. This image is part of a systematic study examining how varying processing temperatures influence the phase distribution and structural quality of the Cu-40Zn alloy.

caption: Experimental deformation pattern of 2DDG honeycombs captured via video imaging during mechanical testing.
summary: Experimental deformation patterns of 2DDG honeycombs are captured through video images during mechanical testing. These images reveal a distinct layer-by-layer collapse mechanism that characterizes the structural response of the material under load, providing a direct visual record of the deformation process for comparison with numerical simulation results.

caption: Transverse strain εyy evolution as a function of global tensile strain for Al, Ti, and interfacial regions.
summary: Transverse strain εyy is shown as a function of global tensile strain for Al, Ti, and interfacial regions. The results demonstrate that the lateral strain becomes increasingly negative as global strain increases, with the Al region exhibiting the largest magnitude of negative strain compared to the Ti and interfacial zones.

caption: Magnified inset of the post-heat-treated Ti-6242 XRD pattern between 34° and 42°, showing a significant increase in the β-phase peak intensity compared to the as-built state.
summary: Focusing on the 34° to 42° range, this inset highlights the post-heat-treated Ti-6242 XRD pattern. A substantial increase in the β-phase peak intensity is observed, indicating a higher proportion of this phase. This change is attributed to the partial decomposition of the α’ martensite into α and β phases.

caption: Comparison of room temperature Charpy V-notch (CVN) impact energy between WAAM-fabricated and wrought AISI 310 stainless steel, with WAAM samples oriented along the build direction (BD) and notched along the deposition direction (DD).
summary: This bar chart compares the room temperature CVN impact energy of wrought AISI 310 and WAAM-fabricated samples. The wrought material exhibits an average energy of 150 J, whereas the WAAM-fabricated samples show a 33% reduction, resulting in an average value of 100 J, indicating lower fracture toughness in the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of HS-27 fibroblasts stained for live (green) and dead (red) cells after 1 and 3 days of culture on TSAV-0, TSAV-5, and TSAV-10 hydrogels.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of HS-27 fibroblasts stained for live (green) and dead (red) cells after 1 and 3 days of culture on TSAV-0, TSAV-5, and TSAV-10 hydrogels. Live/Dead staining revealed a predominance of viable cells across all groups, with negligible numbers of dead cells, indicating the absence of cytotoxicity.

caption: Comparison of the segmented tomography scan to the reference CAD model, where color-coded C2M signed distances indicate geometric correlation and deviations.
summary: The segmented tomography scan is compared against the reference CAD model to evaluate geometric accuracy. The surface mesh is color-coded by C2M signed distances, where blue regions represent inward deviations and red regions indicate outward deviations, primarily caused by bridging defects on the bottom surface of the top skin.

caption: Schematic representation of the XOY surface middle position selected for EBSD analysis.
summary: This panel illustrates the specific region selected for EBSD analysis on the XOY surface of the sample. By focusing on the middle position of the surface, the researchers ensured a consistent and representative area for subsequent microstructural characterization and grain orientation mapping across the different processing states.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the μ phase viewed along the [1 1 ¯ 0] zone axis, highlighting distinct atomic column sites.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the μ phase along the [1 1 ¯ 0] zone axis. The structural analysis reveals specific atomic column sites, where the 6c3 sites within the green frame exhibit higher brightness compared to the 6c2 sites located in the yellow frame, indicating differences in atomic column composition or density.

caption: Short-lateral surface topography of the sintered specimen with reduced peak heights.
summary: Sintering has substantially reduced the prominent peaks previously observed on the short-lateral surface. This 3D profilometry image confirms the resulting improvement in Fltq values, demonstrating that the thermal process effectively mitigates the surface irregularities caused by acceleration and deceleration during the initial 90° directional changes.

caption: Physical depiction of the PAMS hydrogel sensor integrated into a knee joint application model during experimental testing.
summary: This photograph shows the PAMS hydrogel sensor model mounted on a knee joint application platform. The setup utilizes a six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm to perform controlled experiments, enabling the evaluation of the sensor's ability to monitor knee joint motion through real-time physical interaction and data acquisition during simulated movement.

caption: Representative fluorescence images showing the formation of tube-like structures by HUVECs on different scaffold surfaces.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of tube-like structure formation reveals that tube networks are better connected on 1/4/UiO-66/AHT and 1/2/UiO-66/AHT scaffolds. This indicates that the modification of AHT with a medium concentration of UiO-66 nanocrystals has a significant positive impact on the angiogenic differentiation process of the cultured HUVECs.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of a 20 at% Ag PVD sample after the dealloying process.
summary: Bright-field STEM micrograph of a 20 at% Ag PVD sample after the dealloying process. The image reveals the morphological changes induced by dealloying, providing a clear view of the resulting microstructure compared to the as-deposited state shown in panel (a) for the same material composition.

caption: Contour plot of power output for N6 heater/cooler plate surface finish as a function of applied module interface force and temperature difference.
summary: Displayed here is the power output contour map for the N6 surface finish, plotted against applied module interface force and temperature difference. This visualization allows for the identification of performance trends and optimal operating points for the N6 finish within the defined range of mechanical and thermal inputs.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of PPI-SL showing characteristic chemical shifts for the imine group carbon at 163.685 ppm and the hydroxyl-bonded carbon at 160.443 ppm.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of PPI-SL provides structural confirmation of the synthesized material. Key spectral features include a distinct peak at 163.685 ppm, corresponding to the imine group carbon (─N═C─), and a secondary peak at 160.443 ppm, attributed to the carbon atom bonded to the hydroxyl group (─C─OH).

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the solution-treated MEA viewed along the [1-14] zone axis, where 1/2{311} signals are identified by red arrows.
summary: Captured along the [1-14] zone axis, this diffraction pattern reveals the homogeneous-matrix structure of the solution-treated MEA. The 1/2{311} signals, indicated by red arrows, are clearly observable in this orientation. These findings demonstrate that the specific superlattice reflections are consistently present across different zone axes in the material.

caption: EPMA line scan profile showing the elemental distribution of Ni and Cr across the deposited layer without preheating.
summary: This panel displays the EPMA line scan results for a deposited layer processed without preheating. The scan path reveals the initial distribution of Ni and Cr elements. Analysis indicates that the elemental distribution is uneven, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of subsequent preheating conditions on the deposited layer.

caption: Long-term current stability measurement under constant UV illumination for 90 min at a 5 V bias, highlighting the saturation current level of the printed sensor.
summary: Constant UV illumination for 90 minutes is applied to the printed t-ZnO sensor at a 5 V bias to assess its steady-state performance. The measurement reveals the saturation current level, providing insight into the device's stability and long-term response characteristics under continuous light exposure conditions.

caption: Heatmap visualization of the expression patterns of identified DEGs across the two experimental groups.
summary: This heatmap provides a clustered representation of differentially expressed genes, showcasing distinct expression patterns between the ApoEVs and control groups. The visualization effectively highlights the consistency of gene regulation within each group, facilitating the identification of gene clusters that respond specifically to the ApoEVs treatment in vivo.

caption: Fracture strength of heat-treated AM718 and W718 alloys measured at various testing temperatures.
summary: Fracture strength for heat-treated AM718 and W718 alloys is presented as a function of testing temperature. This plot details the stress level at which the specimens ultimately failed, offering a comprehensive view of the mechanical integrity and failure resistance of the alloys under the specified experimental thermal conditions.

caption: Elemental mapping results for O, Fe, C, and N, confirming the homogeneous integration of metal powders with the polymer matrix.
summary: Elemental mapping via EDS reveals the spatial distribution of O, Fe, C, and N within the composite. These results provide clear evidence for the successful and homogeneous integration of the metal powders with the polymer matrix, confirming the chemical composition and uniformity of the prepared composite materials.

caption: Pole figures representing the crystallographic texture evolution of the material across the three specified HIP processing temperatures.
summary: Pole figures display the crystallographic texture evolution for samples processed at 1050 °C, 1150 °C, and 1230 °C. These plots reveal significant temperature-dependent effects on the crystallographic texture, providing insight into how the HIP processing conditions influence the preferred orientation of grains within the material structure.

caption: Stereographic pole figure projections for (100), (110), and (111) planes of as-printed LPBF 17-4 PH stainless steel processed with a 67° rotation scanning strategy.
summary: Stereographic pole figure projections for (100), (110), and (111) planes of as-printed LPBF 17-4 PH stainless steel processed with a 67° rotation scanning strategy. This model utilizes stereographic projections to effectively visualize the orientation preference of the AM crystal structures, highlighting the distinctive texture characteristics of the printed material.

caption: Experimental configuration of the deflection test apparatus designed for evaluating the mechanical response of a pre-twisted cantilever beam.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup used for the deflection testing of a pre-twisted beam. The beam is securely fixed as a cantilever within the apparatus, allowing for controlled mechanical evaluation. This configuration provides the necessary structural support to perform precise deflection measurements on the pre-twisted specimen during testing.

caption: Aluminum wall fabricated via Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) using a constant strike location strategy.
summary: This aluminum wall was produced using WAAM with a constant strike location for each layer. The planar path strategy results in stacked strike locations, which causes a significant sloping effect from left to right across the structure, demonstrating the geometric limitations of this specific additive manufacturing build approach.

caption: Isometric view of a single wrapped PSHM unit cell.
summary: This panel presents an isometric view of a single wrapped PSHM unit cell. The visualization illustrates the fundamental geometric building block of the PSHM structure, providing a clear representation of the unit cell's spatial configuration and wrapping characteristics essential for understanding the hierarchical assembly of the larger cylindrical structure.

caption: Raman spectra of SCC-1, SCC-2, and SCC-3 samples, utilized to characterize the degree of graphitization within the SCF/Co@C composites.
summary: Raman spectra of SCC-1, SCC-2, and SCC-3 samples, utilized to characterize the degree of graphitization within the SCF/Co@C composites. The Raman data provides a comparative assessment of the graphitic quality across different samples, offering critical information regarding the structural evolution and carbon ordering in the synthesized materials.

caption: Normalized Raman spectrum and corresponding optical micrograph of the gray region in pyrolyzed PP05 PEDOT:PSS film.
summary: This panel illustrates the Raman spectrum and optical micrograph for the gray region of the PP05 PEDOT:PSS film. Consistent with other samples, the ID/IG ratio is measured at approximately 1.26, suggesting that the pyrolyzed material maintains a glass-like carbon structure regardless of the specific processing conditions or regional morphology.

caption: Relative change η(λ) presented as a function of concentration variables x, y, and z for the (Co0.5Ni0.5)3(Al0.5TizTa0.5-z) system.
summary: The relative change η(λ) is shown as a function of concentration variables x, y, and z. In contrast to the general trend observed in the L12 phase, the (Co0.5Ni0.5)3(Al0.5TizTa0.5-z) system exhibits an opposite trend, highlighting the complex influence of alloying elements on the phase properties.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for region 1, quantifying the frequency of various grain sizes observed in the welding joint.
summary: The grain size distribution for region 1 is presented as a histogram. Significant gradient variations in grain size are observed between regions, attributed to the temperature difference of the base materials before laser welding. This quantitative data illustrates the microstructural heterogeneity inherent in the laser-welded joint.

caption: 3D cubic structural sample of the alloy with Re addition at t = 0.5 ns, illustrating dislocation distribution restricted to the γ matrix channels.
summary: For the sample with Re addition at 0.5 ns, the 3D structural simulation demonstrates that dislocations are confined to the γ matrix channels. Similar to the sample without Re, no dislocations are observed in the γ′ precipitates phase, indicating that Re addition does not alter the initial dislocation confinement behavior.

caption: Goldner's trichrome stained longitudinal section of a Zn scaffold showing tight bonding to bone at the edges and abundant unmineralized collagen within pores.
summary: Goldner's trichrome staining of the Zn scaffold longitudinal section shows the material is completely surrounded by bone or collagen. The edges are tightly bonded to the bone, and the internal pores contain a large amount of unmineralized collagen tissue, demonstrating significant biological interaction and tissue colonization within the Zn scaffold.

caption: Fourier transform modules of the experimental EXAFS functions for the Fe58Ni25B17 alloy measured above the K-Ni absorption edge, contrasting the structural states of the initial MQ sample and the sample subjected to HPT at 77 K.
summary: The Fourier transform of EXAFS data at the K-Ni edge illustrates structural changes in the Fe58Ni25B17 alloy. Comparing the MQ and HPT-77 K states reveals that the HPT process disrupts the atomic ordering present in the initial melt-quenched state, reflecting the higher free energy state induced by cryogenic deformation.

caption: Reconstructed micro-CT image showing bone tissue in-growth in PEEK-PAR and PEEK/HA-PAR scaffolds, with orange indicating the ingrown bone.
summary: Micro-CT reconstruction illustrates the effectiveness of bone tissue in-growth within the PEEK-PAR and PEEK/HA-PAR scaffolds. The ingrown bone tissue is highlighted in orange, allowing for a visual comparison of the osteointegration performance between the two scaffold groups within the porous regions of the implant.

caption: S-N fatigue data for vertically printed PBF-LB 70/30 Cu–Ni specimens in both as-built (AB) and heat-treated (HT) conditions under fully-reversed (R = −1) loading.
summary: Vertically printed Cu-Ni specimens are evaluated here through fully-reversed fatigue testing. The graph illustrates stress versus cycles to failure for both AB and HT conditions, highlighting runout specimens with arrows. Fatigue results in the early HCF regime reflect the material's monotonic tensile behavior, consistent with the horizontally printed counterparts.

caption: EPMA elemental maps of the LSP-treated surface of the HT + LSP sample, illustrating local enrichment of Ti, Ni, and O.
summary: EPMA elemental mapping of the LSP-treated surface reveals noticeable local enrichment of Ti, Ni, and O elements in several micro-regions. These maps demonstrate the chemical heterogeneity introduced by the LSP process, contrasting with the uniform distribution of elements observed in the untreated HT sample.

caption: Areal capacitance values of Cu–Ni alloy electrodes plotted against scan rates, derived from cyclic voltammetry data for films deposited at voltages ranging from −1.2 V to −1.8 V.
summary: This plot displays the areal capacitance of Cu–Ni alloy electrodes as a function of scan rate. The data, calculated from cyclic voltammetry, reveals that films synthesized at lower deposition voltages exhibit higher areal capacitance values, indicating that the deposition potential significantly influences the electrochemical performance of the alloy electrodes.

caption: Spatial Vickers microhardness map of the recycled SS316L specimen reinforced with 5 wt.% alumina.
summary: The Vickers microhardness map for the recycled SS316L composite with 5 wt.% alumina shows a further increase in hardness compared to the 1 wt.% sample. This consistent trend confirms that increasing the ceramic content effectively enhances the mechanical hardness of the recycled material relative to the ceramic-free baseline.

caption: 3D surface morphology of SLM-ed TA15 alloy following pure mechanical wear.
summary: This panel displays the 3D surface morphology of SLM-ed TA15 alloy after undergoing pure mechanical wear. Observed via laser scanning confocal microscopy, the topography reveals the wear track characteristics. SLM-ed TA15 exhibits lower COF values compared to LMD-ed and forged counterparts, attributed to its superior hardness under these specific mechanical conditions.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental fatigue life to PM-estimated values for notched specimens at the second in-fill level.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the PM model by comparing experimental fatigue life data against estimated values for notched specimens. The visualization highlights the model's performance in capturing fatigue life variations specifically for specimens manufactured with the second in-fill level configuration.

caption: Calculated isopleth section of the Cu-Ni-Pb ternary system spanning from a Cu:Ni ratio of 3 to pure lead, comparing the current study's solid line results against previous parameter sets by [44] (dotted line) and [43] (dashed line) alongside experimental data points from [51].
summary: This isopleth diagram illustrates the phase equilibrium behavior of the Cu-Ni-Pb ternary system along a specific composition path from Cu:Ni=3 to pure lead. The plot compares the current thermodynamic calculations with two prior parameter sets and experimental data, highlighting the variations in phase boundary predictions across different modeling approaches.

caption: Simulated grain structure of the second layer after the deposition of the 10th layer, representing state II of the intrinsic heat treatment.
summary: Depicting state II, this panel shows the grain structure of the second layer following the deposition of the 10th layer. The grains exhibit further elongation into columnar structures compared to state I, demonstrating the cumulative effect of cyclic thermal exposure on the microstructural morphology of the WAAM-processed material.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) spectrum of the 2Ta alloy at room temperature and zero load, showing overlapping γ and γ' peaks.
summary: This SXRD spectrum, collected at the I12 beamline at Diamond, characterizes the 2Ta alloy at room temperature and zero load. The fitting routine assumes Co in the FCC γ matrix and alloying elements in the L12 phase. Notably, the γ and γ' peaks are overlapped in this specific synchrotron dataset.

caption: Lack of adhesion and interlayer delamination visible in a DED-fabricated structure.
summary: Insufficient adhesion or interlayer delamination in DED structures manifests as visible discontinuities across deposited layers. This defect indicates inadequate energy delivery or local surface contamination during the fabrication process, which significantly compromises the mechanical strength and structural integrity of the final component by preventing proper bonding between successive layers.

caption: Phase angle versus frequency plot for Ti–6Al–4V, NiTi7, and NiTi5 samples.
summary: Depicted here is the phase angle Bode plot for Ti–6Al–4V, NiTi7, and NiTi5 samples. The data shows that these specific materials reach phase angles close to -90° within the 150,000 Ohm to 10 Ohm frequency range, indicating highly capacitive behavior at the electrode-electrolyte interface during the electrochemical impedance measurements.

caption: Comparison of BAM emission spectra under 285 nm and 365 nm excitation wavelengths, highlighting excitation wavelength insensitivity.
summary: BAM emission spectra under 285 nm and 365 nm excitation wavelengths demonstrate the material's broad UV excitation spectrum. Its relative insensitivity to excitation wavelengths ensures compatibility with a wide range of commercial UV light sources, making it a versatile candidate for various optical and photonic applications requiring stable emission characteristics.

caption: Measurement sequence diagram outlining the procedural steps followed during the experimental testing of the metamaterial cell.
summary: The measurement procedure is depicted in this sequence diagram, which outlines the systematic steps followed during the experimental testing. This flow ensures that all properties of the metamaterial cell are assessed consistently within the established experimental framework, facilitating accurate data collection throughout the entire testing process.

caption: Magnified TEM view of the framed area within the microstructure shown in panel (d).
summary: High-magnification TEM imaging of the framed area from the left side of the interface reveals fine-scale structural details. This observation is vital for identifying the specific phases present in the reaction layer, supporting the broader analysis of the interface between the Ti-6Al-4V alloy and pure Cu.

caption: Control chart of surface elevation for Sample S2, demonstrating fewer extreme peaks and valleys relative to pure WWR.
summary: The control chart for Sample S2 displays surface elevation data, confirming a reduction in extreme peaks and valleys compared to pure WWR. This indicates that the addition of Kevlar promotes a more stable and uniform surface profile, contributing to the overall structural homogeneity of the composite material.

caption: Thermomagnetization M(T) curves for the normal Ni-Mn-Ga “N” sample in as-built and annealed states, measured under ZFC and FC conditions at 50 Oe.
summary: Thermomagnetization M(T) curves for the normal Ni-Mn-Ga “N” sample are presented for both as-built and annealed conditions under a 50 Oe field. The as-built sample exhibits a wide transformation range of approximately 27 K with two distinct humps, whereas heat treatment results in flatter regions and a narrower transition range.

caption: Normalized elastic modulus plotted against time for quasi-isotropic PETG specimens subjected to a constant 1% deformation over a 40-minute duration, comparing dry and water-immersed environmental conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the time-dependent relaxation behavior of quasi-isotropic PETG specimens under constant 1% elastic deformation. The data reveals that specimens immersed in water exhibit a significantly faster rate of elastic modulus relaxation compared to those tested in dry conditions, indicating that moisture exposure accelerates stress relaxation and energy dissipation in the polymer.

caption: Tafel plots of cell voltage versus the logarithm of current density for a 5 cm2 PEFC comparing catalyst A and a Pt/C reference under O2 and air feeds, with an inset highlighting cell voltage at log10(current density) = -2.55.
summary: This Tafel plot compares the kinetic performance of catalyst A against a Pt/C reference in a 5 cm2 PEFC. The inset shows that at a current density of 2.8 mA cm-2, catalyst A exhibits a cell voltage 60 mV lower than the reference, while maintaining a Tafel slope of 60-70 mV dec-1.

caption: Side-view perspective showing the orientation and angle of the aluminum and nickel wire feeding mechanisms during the deposition process.
summary: This side view clarifies the vertical and angular orientation of the aluminum and nickel wire feeding systems. By feeding these wires through separate motors into the GTAW torch arc, the system facilitates the controlled melting and deposition of materials onto the AISI 1010 steel substrate for additive manufacturing applications.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the build produced at low temperature, exhibiting a higher density of dislocations compared to room temperature samples.
summary: This TEM image shows the microstructure of a build produced at low temperature. Observations indicate a significantly higher density of dislocations compared to the room temperature build. These crystalline imperfections act as fast diffusion paths and preferential nucleation sites for the second-phase particles distributed throughout the material matrix.

caption: Vickers microhardness indentation located within the ferrite phase of a 2205 wrought DSS plate after 200 hours of aging at 400 °C.
summary: This panel displays a Vickers microhardness indentation performed on the ferrite phase of a 2205 wrought DSS plate. The sample underwent 200 hours of aging at 400 °C. Precise positioning ensures the indentation is contained entirely within the ferrite to avoid any influence from the austenite phase during measurement.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves illustrating the thermal phase transition behavior of various starch samples.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves are presented to evaluate the structural changes occurring within starch granules during thermal phase transitions. These curves provide a detailed thermal profile of the starch samples, allowing for the assessment of their specific phase transition characteristics and structural stability under heating conditions.

caption: Theoretical temperature distribution for the thermal double expander metadevice under a background thermal conductivity of 5 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹.
summary: Representing the theoretical simulation for the thermal double expander metadevice, this panel shows the temperature distribution when the background material conductivity is reduced to 5 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹. This result highlights the device's robustness and consistent thermal behavior across varying background material properties within the specified thermal boundary conditions.

caption: Digital photograph of the three-electrode electrochemical cell configuration, highlighting the arrangement of the working, counter, and reference electrodes.
summary: This digital image displays the experimental setup for the three-electrode electrochemical measurement. It clearly identifies the physical arrangement of the working, counter, and reference electrodes used throughout the study to characterize the electrochemical performance of the BAC and CHBAC materials under investigation in the subsequent electrochemical tests.

caption: Methodological flowchart illustrating the BVP Midrich technique for determining temperature, velocity, and concentration profiles.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic BVP Midrich procedure used to calculate precise values for temperature, velocity, and concentration profiles. By following this methodological sequence, researchers can obtain exact physical parameters, ensuring a rigorous approach to modeling the transport phenomena described within the study's analytical framework.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for alloys milled for 15, 30, and 45 minutes, showing experimental data (red dots), Rietveld refinement calculations (black lines), difference profiles (blue lines), and Bragg reflection positions (green marks) at 300 K.
summary: This figure presents neutron diffraction patterns for alloys subjected to 15, 30, and 45 minutes of milling. The data includes experimental points, calculated fits, and difference curves at 300 K, with green marks indicating Bragg reflections. These results facilitate the analysis of how milling-induced defects influence the magnetization of the samples.

caption: Calculated density of states for fcc Ni, serving as a reference for the valence band structure of the nickel-based compounds.
summary: The density of states for fcc Ni is presented as a reference. The valence band structure of the La1.5Mg0.5Ni7 compound exhibits similarities to this fcc Ni profile. This comparison helps identify the contribution of nickel 3d bands to the overall electronic properties of the complex intermetallic phases.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from cyclic voltammograms recorded at a 5 mV s-1 scan rate for four Fe-based alloy samples, showing standard deviation error bars and highlighting slopes below 40 mV dec-1 for compositions between 40 and 60 at. % Fe.
summary: Tafel slope analysis was performed on four Fe-based alloy samples using cyclic voltammetry at a 5 mV s-1 scan rate. The results demonstrate that for iron concentrations ranging from 40 to 60 at. %, the measured Tafel slopes are consistently below 40 mV dec-1, serving as a key electrochemical benchmark.

caption: Pentagon diagram showing the CPDP parameters for the Al86Cr12Ni2 alloy system, which underwent 6 hours of mechano-synthesis, measured in 0.1 mol/L Na2SO4.
summary: This pentagon diagram illustrates the CPDP parameters for the Al86Cr12Ni2 alloy system after 6 hours of mechanical synthesis. Tested in a 0.1 mol/L Na2SO4 electrolyte, the plot provides a visual summary of electrochemical parameters including corrosion potential, pitting potential, and current density, facilitating a comparative analysis of the alloy's corrosion characteristics.

caption: Conceptual flowchart illustrating the model inadequacy framework for inverse design of elastic rings.
summary: This flowchart depicts the inverse design process where a target shape serves as input for an ANN tool. The ANN generates a shear modulus distribution, which is then used in FEM simulations. The bias term quantifies the discrepancy between the target shape and the resulting FE output, representing model inadequacy.

caption: Fracture characteristics of the β-sheet structure plotted against varying printing speeds.
summary: The influence of printing speed on the fracture characteristics of the β-sheet structure is shown here. As the printing speed increases, with the printing temperature held at 100 °C and extrusion pressure at 590 MPa, both the maximum stress and ultimate tensile strain exhibit an initial increase followed by a subsequent decrease.

caption: Capacitance performance as a function of scan rate, demonstrating a decrease in capacitance for both capacitors as the scan rate increases.
summary: This plot illustrates the rate capability of the capacitors, showing a decline in capacitance with increasing scan rates. This trend is attributed to the limited time available for K+ ions to diffuse into the KGP matrix, which hinders effective absorption and desorption on the electrode surfaces during operation.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and individual EDX maps for Mo, Ni, Co, O, and Sr in the Sr2Ni0.5Co0.5MoO6 sample.
summary: Sr2Ni0.5Co0.5MoO6 is analyzed via HAADF-STEM and EDX mapping to evaluate morphology and chemical homogeneity. TEM evidence indicates that co-alloying with Ni promotes the exsolution of Co-rich Ni–Co alloy nanoparticles, resulting in a higher concentration of metallic Co in the surface-near regions of the material compared to the parent compound.

caption: EDS line scanning result across the straight line indicated in panel (b), revealing the elemental distribution of club-shaped IMCs.
summary: This panel shows the EDS line scanning result performed along a straight line in region C. The data demonstrates how Marangoni convection drives Ti elements from the bottom of the melt to the upper molten pool, resulting in the formation of club-shaped intermetallic compounds aligned with the local temperature gradient.

caption: Principal component analysis of spatter ejection velocity data, where individual samples are color-coded according to their specific ejection velocity values.
summary: This PCA plot visualizes the spatter ejection velocity dataset, with samples colored by their respective velocities. The first two principal components capture over 95% of the total variance, demonstrating that this dimensionality reduction effectively represents the underlying data structure and provides strong explanatory power for the observed spatter behavior.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of an Al-rich region showing atomic positions of Al, Co, and Cr within a 25–125 nm depth range, with isoconcentration surfaces highlighting Al-rich (≥35 at.%) and Cr-rich (≥25 at.%) domains.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of an Al-rich region reveals the spatial distribution of Al, Co, and Cr atoms between 25 and 125 nm. Isoconcentration surfaces clearly delineate Al-rich and Cr-rich domains, providing evidence of local enrichment within the specimen structure as observed in the experimental analysis.

caption: Dilatometry curves illustrating the temperature-dependent dimensional changes in secondary hardening steel samples with varying nickel concentrations.
summary: Dilatometry curves reveal the thermal expansion behavior of secondary hardening steels. Analysis of these curves demonstrates that critical transformation temperatures, specifically the martensite start (Ms) and Ar3 temperatures, exhibit a consistent downward shift as the nickel content within the steel samples increases, indicating a significant influence of Ni on austenite stability.

caption: Temperature dependence of the 0.2% proof stress for the TiZrNbHfTa alloy, where solid symbols represent successful yielding and open symbols denote brittle fracture occurring prior to yielding.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent 0.2% proof stress of the TiZrNbHfTa alloy. It distinguishes between specimens that successfully yielded, marked by solid symbols, and those that underwent brittle fracture before yielding, indicated by open symbols. This distinction provides critical insight into the material's mechanical behavior across varying thermal conditions.

caption: HRSTEM micrograph displaying a Cr7C3 carbide particle embedded within the γ-Co solid-solution matrix.
summary: High-resolution STEM imaging reveals the presence of Cr7C3 carbide particles dispersed within the γ-Co solid-solution matrix. This microstructure is a result of the rapid solidification process inherent to laser additive manufacturing, which also influences the formation of structural defects like stacking faults and nanotwins throughout the cobalt-based matrix.

caption: EBSD analysis of the sample after solution treatment at 1260 °C for 6 h, revealing significant grain growth in the top and edge isoaxial crystal regions.
summary: Following solution treatment at 1260 °C for 6 h, the sample exhibits significant grain growth, particularly within the top and edge isoaxial crystal regions. EBSD analysis confirms that the microstructure undergoes substantial coarsening compared to the as-deposited state, highlighting the impact of high-temperature solution treatment on the material's grain morphology.

caption: Surface energy of Ni2Si and (Co0.5Ni0.5)2Si precipitates calculated at the upper limit of Co chemical potential (μCo) as a function of Ni chemical potential (μNi).
summary: Surface energy values for Ni2Si and (Co0.5Ni0.5)2Si are shown at the upper limit of Co chemical potential. The energy of Si-terminated (Co0.5Ni0.5)2Si surfaces increases significantly with higher μCo, whereas the (100) Ni-terminated surface of Ni2Si emerges as the surface with the lowest energy under these specific conditions.

caption: Magnified view of a single particle event detected at 120 s, utilizing a y-axis break to simultaneously visualize the transient signal profiles of 238U and 235U isotopes within the same particle.
summary: Focusing on a single particle detected at 120 seconds, this zoomed-in view highlights the simultaneous detection of 238U and 235U isotopes. The use of a y-axis break allows for the clear observation of both isotopic signals within the same transient event, confirming the instrument's ability to perform multi-elemental analysis on individual particles.

caption: Mass flow rate plotted against rotational speed for varying nozzle diameters in a pellet-based 3D printing system.
summary: This line graph illustrates the relationship between mass flow rate and rotational speed in a pellet-based 3D printing system. The data indicates that mass flow rate increases linearly with rotational speed for a given nozzle diameter. Larger nozzle diameters maintain flow rates below critical thresholds, ensuring safe operation without overloading the motor.

caption: Digital image correlation strain map for a transverse sample, illustrating local strain values and stress distribution across the gradient zones.
summary: The DIC strain map for the transverse sample demonstrates how local strain is distributed relative to the tensile stress. Observations indicate that elastic deformation is more pronounced in the Inconel 625-rich zones, effectively illustrating the heterogeneous stress distribution inherent in the layered gradient material during the tensile loading process.

caption: 3D SECM surface scan of the 316L stainless steel coating modified with 8% Cu.
summary: This 3D SECM image characterizes the surface of the 316L coating containing 8% Cu. The scan, performed over a 0.2 x 0.2 mm area, maps the normalized current distribution. Red areas denote the highest current intensities, reflecting the specific electrochemical activity of this higher copper-content coating surface.

caption: EPMA compositional map demonstrating microsegregation resulting from non-equilibrium solidification in the as-built #40HSLA steel.
summary: EPMA measurements reveal that non-equilibrium solidification during additive manufacturing induces significant microsegregation in the #40HSLA steel. This compositional mapping confirms the presence of a dual-phase cellular solidification structure characterized by a 5 µm cell size, illustrating how solute distribution varies across the microstructure in the as-built condition.

caption: Comparative HPLC chromatograms for UA2, UC2, UA8, and UC8 hydrogel samples, demonstrating the depletion of sodium benzoate during the crosslinking process.
summary: HPLC chromatograms provide analytical characterization of residual sodium benzoate in printed hydrogels. The data compares samples UA2 and UC2 with UA8 and UC8. The results indicate that at 8 minutes of irradiation, sodium benzoate is depleted by over 95%, which correlates with radical saturation and successful crosslinking of the hydrogel network.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot for the Ti-6Al-4V alloy, showing the relationship between inverse capacitance squared and potential.
summary: The Mott-Schottky plot for the Ti-6Al-4V alloy displays a linear region with a positive slope. This characteristic indicates that the oxide film formed on the alloy surface behaves as an n-type metal oxide semiconductor, consistent with the electrochemical analysis of the material's semiconducting properties.

caption: Stress evolution over time recorded after a 1-minute inter-stage holding period.
summary: Stress evolution over time is depicted for the 1-minute inter-stage holding condition. Observations show that stress relaxation occurs more rapidly for this shorter holding duration compared to the 5-minute tests. The relaxation rate consistently decreases as the strain increment increases during the intermediate holding stages of the test.

caption: Magnetostriction response of CoFe2O4-spattered Fe–Co alloy and Fe–Co/Ni clad plates plotted as a function of magnetic field strength.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetostriction behavior of CoFe2O4-spattered Fe–Co alloy and Fe–Co/Ni clad plates. The data provides a comparative analysis of the magnetic response for these specific material configurations, highlighting how the spattered coating and cladding influence the overall magnetostrictive performance of the Fe–Co alloy base material.

caption: Schematic representation of the arc voltage sampling and protection circuit designed to isolate the acquisition system from high-frequency and high-voltage interference during WAAM processes.
summary: This schematic illustrates the arc voltage acquisition and protection circuit utilized in WAAM. The design is specifically engineered to mitigate the adverse effects of high-frequency and high-voltage signals on the sampling circuit, ensuring accurate voltage measurements which are essential for determining deposition height and enhancing overall detection precision.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from the nano-indentation experiments.
summary: Load-displacement curves are presented to characterize the mechanical response of the material during the indentation process. These curves correlate the applied force with the resulting penetration depth, providing essential data for calculating the nano-hardness and evaluating the elastic-plastic behavior of the tested material.

caption: Load-displacement (P-h) curve for SLM-316L steel subjected to a nanoindentation creep test at a loading rate of 20 mN/min.
summary: This curve displays the P-h response of SLM-316L steel at a 20 mN/min loading rate. Rapid loading facilitates higher contact stress, promoting dislocation nucleation and motion. This results in increased creep displacement during the saturation stage compared to slower loading rates, reflecting the influence of heterostructure on creep behavior.

caption: Digital image correlation results obtained using the Ncorr function in MATLAB for displacement measurement.
summary: The DIC results presented here were generated using the Ncorr function within the MATLAB environment. This technique allows for precise displacement measurement across the specimen surface by tracking the random pixel patterns applied in panel (a), providing a detailed quantitative analysis of the deformation behavior during the mechanical test.

caption: Comparative load-displacement curves showing the minimum, median, and maximum load values achieved for each distinct failure mode identified in the shear lap testing.
summary: These load-displacement curves summarize the mechanical performance of specimens across different failure modes, regardless of grade or extrusion temperature. The plot highlights the range of load-bearing capacities by displaying the minimum, median, and maximum values, offering a quantitative overview of how failure modes correlate with the applied mechanical load.

caption: Schematic representation of bidirectional fluid flow within the DLTMC binary tube configuration.
summary: This panel illustrates the bidirectional flow capability of the DLTMC binary tube. When configured in a standard orientation, the units facilitate fluid transport in both directions, serving as the baseline for understanding the directional control mechanisms inherent in the DLTMC system design for fluidic applications.

caption: Top view of the longitudinal section of a SolidWorks model for a bending specimen featuring hexagonal internal cavities with 10% hollowness.
summary: Representing the longitudinal section of a bending specimen, this SolidWorks model displays a 10% hollowness configuration characterized by hexagonal cavities. These unit cells are distributed throughout the entire length of the specimen, consistent with the experimental design requirements for assessing bending performance in porous structural materials.

caption: Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectra of PB and PB@QUE nanoparticles.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectra demonstrate the successful loading of QUE onto PB nanoparticles. The characteristic peak of QUE at 378 nm disappears in the PB@QUE spectrum, confirming that QUE was successfully loaded onto the PB structure through intermolecular interactions, indicating a stable composite formation for the drug delivery system.

caption: Schematic of the HLAW process arc behavior during the laser scanning cycle.
summary: This panel illustrates the arc behavior during the HLAW process cycle. The rotating laser influences the arc dynamics through time-sharing attraction, which alters the droplet transfer behavior. This mechanism is essential for achieving the divergent drop point distribution that characterizes the HLAW process and improves weld penetration width.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of melt pool temperature (MPT) versus porosity, demonstrating that higher MPT values correlate with increased porosity, suggesting a connection between spatter landing and lack-of-fusion (LOF) porosity.
summary: The SHAP scatter diagram for melt pool temperature shows that higher feature values lead to increased porosity. This trend suggests a functional link between spatter landing and the formation of lack-of-fusion porosity. The plot quantifies the contribution of MPT to porosity variations observed within the core pixels of the material.

caption: Pole figure (PF) map detailing the crystallographic orientation relationship between the continuous α grain boundary and the adjacent α lamellae.
summary: The pole figure map reveals the crystallographic orientation relationship between the continuous α grain boundary and adjacent α lamellae. The lamellae maintain a {11 0} pole parallel to adjacent lamellae to minimize strain during the β to α transformation, while other lamellae lose their specific orientation relationships with the grain boundary.

caption: Energy distribution profile measured outside the focal plane to characterize the curing region.
summary: Energy distribution outside the focal plane is visualized here to assist in the quantitative prediction of the 3D curing region. By analyzing these patterns, researchers can effectively avoid defects like asymmetric overcuring, thereby ensuring the geometric fidelity of fabricated microstructures such as cantilevers and microchannels during the DMD-based curing process.

caption: Capacitance measurements (CEIS) for PVDF membranes filled with air, dodecane, and paraffin plotted against relative permittivity (εr), showing a linear regression trend where the y-intercept represents the intrinsic capacitance of the PVDF substrate.
summary: This panel displays the measured capacitances (CEIS) of SLMs for three different media with varying relative permittivities. A linear regression of the average CEIS values reveals a y-intercept of 0.025 nF, which corresponds to the capacitance contribution solely from the pristine PVDF membrane substrate.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from nano-indentation testing on the 67° sample.
summary: The load-displacement curves for the 67° sample show a high degree of coincidence, indicating the lowest dislocation density and minimal anisotropy. Unlike the other samples, this orientation exhibits no obvious hardening and a more uniform hardness distribution, consistent with the absence of a significant child texture.

caption: Hysteresis loops for the AB sample measured at 50 Hz under varying magnetic induction levels.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic hysteresis behavior of the additively manufactured Fe–3Si core processed under AB conditions. The loops are plotted at a constant excitation frequency of 50 Hz across different magnetic induction values, illustrating the magnetic response and energy loss characteristics of the material under these specific testing parameters.

caption: Elemental profile of Mo across the interface of Ni-50Al and Ni-50Al-10Ru alloys, demonstrating an increase in maximum Mo concentration from 0.46 at. % to 0.96 at. % upon Ru addition.
summary: The elemental profile of Mo at the Ni-50Al and Ni-50Al-10Ru sides is presented to show the effect of Ru on Mo solubility. The data indicates that the addition of Ru increases the maximum Mo concentration in the β-NiAl phase from 0.46 at. % to 0.96 at. %.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) for the (Ni37Co13Mn34Ti16)99.2B0.8 alloy under different magnetic field changes.
summary: Applying the Maxwell equation to the M-H data, the maximum magnetic entropy change for the (Ni37Co13Mn34Ti16)99.2B0.8 alloy is determined to be 40.9 J kg-1 K-1 under a 70000 Oe magnetic field. This result demonstrates that boron doping slightly enhances the magnetocaloric performance compared to the undoped alloy.

caption: Surface profile image of AISI 316L stainless steel captured at 20× magnification using a confocal microscopy profiler after 6 hours of dry mass finishing with nutshells at 300 RPM.
summary: Confocal microscopy imaging at 20× magnification reveals the surface topography of AISI 316L stainless steel following 6 hours of dry mass finishing with nutshells at 300 RPM. This visualization provides a detailed profile measurement, allowing for the assessment of surface texture and roughness characteristics post-processing in the specified experimental condition.

caption: Isothermal reduction mass change curves of the leach residue treated with CO gas.
summary: This plot displays the isothermal reduction kinetics of the leach residue using CO gas. By analyzing these mass change curves, the reduction behavior is evaluated. Notably, the slow reduction rate observed at 1200 °C is attributed to the partial dissolution of hematite into the silicate melt, which reduces hematite activity.

caption: Iterative solution flow diagram illustrating the computational process for determining the diffusion coefficient.
summary: The flowchart depicts the iterative computational cycle used to determine the diffusion coefficient. It illustrates the logical progression of the calculation process, specifically highlighting that if the initial approximation criteria are not met, the iteration cycle continues until a stable solution is reached for the interfacial temperature-dependent diffusion coefficient.

caption: Area-weighted grain size distribution for the hot17.5 sample, swaged at a ratio of 0.7, resulting in a mean grain size of 4.0 μm.
summary: Swaging the AM sample at a ratio of 0.7 under hot conditions results in a significant reduction of the mean grain size to 4.0 μm. This histogram illustrates the area-weighted fraction of grain sizes, highlighting the structural refinement achieved through the hot swaging process compared to the initial AM state.

caption: Micro-Raman spectra of the wear debris, showing a main peak at 960 cm-1 and secondary peaks at 865, 717, and 357 cm-1, indicating the presence of amorphous oxides.
summary: The Raman spectra for the wear debris exhibit a main peak at 960 cm-1 corresponding to WO3·xH2O, with secondary peaks at 865, 717, and 357 cm-1. The large breadth of these peaks suggests that the oxides are primarily amorphous in nature.

caption: Fracture locus of 6.0 mm nominal thickness WAAM ER70S-6 steel plotted in the stress triaxiality (η) versus equivalent fracture strain (ε‾f) plane, comparing experimental test data with predictive model results.
summary: This plot displays the fracture locus for 6.0 mm WAAM ER70S-6 steel in the stress triaxiality versus equivalent fracture strain plane. The comparison between experimental test data and predicted results demonstrates good predictive accuracy for the material, with the exception of the PS specimens as noted in the study.

caption: Raman spectrum of the initial CNT powder mixture with copper prior to the PBF-LB processing.
summary: This panel displays the Raman spectrum of the CNT powder mixture with copper before undergoing the PBF-LB process. The spectrum serves as a baseline for evaluating the structural changes and ordering of the carbon nanotubes within the copper matrix prior to the laser-based additive manufacturing treatment.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the as-built Haynes 230 alloy, characterizing the crystalline nature of the L-PBF processed material.
summary: The SAED pattern provides structural information regarding the as-built Haynes 230 alloy fabricated by L-PBF. This diffraction data confirms the crystalline state of the material, serving as a fundamental characterization of the microstructure observed in the XOY plane of the laser-powder bed fusion processed sample.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the AH-1050–60 specimen, demonstrating grain growth with a retained columnar grain structure.
summary: Subjected to a homogenization temperature of 1050 ℃, the AH-1050–60 specimen shows clear evidence of grain growth. The inverse pole figure map indicates that while the grains have increased in size, the fundamental columnar grain structure remains unchanged, consistent with the observations made at this temperature level.

caption: XRD pattern of the specimen with 20 vol% solid content, showing distinct peaks corresponding to Al2O3, SiO2, and mullite phases.
summary: The XRD pattern for the 20 vol% solid content specimen reveals the presence of Al2O3, SiO2, and mullite phases. Analysis indicates that these peaks are prominent at this lower solid content level, providing a baseline for phase composition before the observed reduction in secondary phases at higher solid concentrations.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the large-size twins shown in panel (b).
summary: Diffraction spots obtained via transmission electron microscopy confirm the presence of the large-size twins identified in panel (b). This diffraction pattern provides crystallographic evidence of the twin structures that traverse the matrix and precipitate phases within the SA-1240 alloy near the fracture region.

caption: Specific discharge capacity plotted against cycle number for various tape-casted Si and Si-C anodes, comparing different binders (PEDOT:PSS at varying pH levels and CMC with different molecular weights) tested at 30 °C with initial formation cycles at 0.05C followed by 100 cycles at 0.2C.
summary: This capacity retention plot evaluates the electrochemical performance of tape-casted Si and Si-C anodes using different binders. PEDOT:PSS-based samples demonstrate superior performance, achieving a cutoff lithiation capacity of 2000 mAh g-1 immediately after formation. The data highlights the influence of binder chemistry and pH on long-term cycling stability.

caption: EBSD band contrast image of the oxide scale formed on R41 after 72 hours of isothermal exposure and 100 cycles of 1-hour duration in wet air at 950 °C.
summary: This EBSD band contrast image shows the oxide scale on R41 following 72 hours of isothermal exposure and 100 thermal cycles in wet air at 950 °C. The grain size and morphology are comparable to N80A, with no notable differences observed in the Cr2O3 grain structure between these alloys.

caption: Rhombic repeating unit of the HE-core consisting of a thin plate supported by four pin fins with non-orthogonal axes.
summary: The repeating unit of the heat exchanger core is depicted as a rhombus formed by a thin plate supported by four pin fins. This unit features non-orthogonal axes, which define the geometry of the unsupported plate area, calculated as b squared multiplied by the sine of the angle theta.

caption: Reflection coefficient (S11) plot for the cylindrical FESA, illustrating the performance variation between the wire-only and wire-with-support configurations.
summary: This panel presents the reflection coefficient (S11) for the cylindrical FESA design. The graph compares the performance of the wire-only structure with the wire-with-support structure, allowing for an analysis of how the dielectric support influences the resonance frequency and overall reflection characteristics of the cylindrical antenna system.

caption: Residual stress distribution for specimen 06, calculated via GPR in scan (x) and step (y) directions, with propagated uncertainties shown at ±1σ.
summary: Residual stress maps for specimen 06 are generated in the scan and step directions using GPR techniques. These distributions provide insight into the internal stress state, with the associated ±1σ propagated uncertainties offering a clear indication of the precision and reliability of the calculated stress values across the scan area.

caption: Three-dimensional spatial distribution of sample points generated using the Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) method.
summary: This panel displays the three-dimensional spatial distribution of sample points generated via the Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) method. As part of a comparative analysis, this visualization serves as a baseline to evaluate the filling characteristics of sample spaces within the defined parameter space compared to improved sampling techniques.

caption: Cartoon representation of the catalytic site highlighting the KLac-specific loop and residues involved in lactose moiety interaction.
summary: The cartoon representation of the catalytic site emphasizes the extra loop present in KLac and identifies specific residues that interact with the lactose moiety. This structural insertion is hypothesized to account for the higher catalytic rate observed in KLac compared to TmLacS, providing insight into the enzyme's functional efficiency.

caption: Compressive stress–strain curve and deformation snapshots of the Octet structure, demonstrating a characteristic stretching-dominated mechanical response followed by post-peak softening and layer-by-layer collapse.
summary: The Octet structure exhibits a stretching-dominated mechanical behavior under compression. The stress-strain curve shows a distinct peak followed by softening. Deformation is characterized by a layer-by-layer collapse mechanism, as evidenced by the snapshot highlighting the failure of the first layer during the test.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan profile across the Al-Fe intermetallic particles, showing the relative intensity distribution of Fe, Al, and Zn elements.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan analysis confirms the chemical composition of the rod-shaped particles observed on the fracture surface. The profile tracks the elemental distribution of Fe, Al, and Zn across these features, providing evidence that they are Al-Fe-rich intermetallic phases formed during the welding process.

caption: Mean SHAP value distribution plot showing the relative contribution of each martensite feature to the model's predictive output across various instances.
summary: The mean SHAP value distribution plot illustrates the contribution of each individual feature to the model's predictions. By quantifying the impact of various instances, this plot clarifies which morphological features are most influential in the classification of martensite within the XGBoost framework.

caption: Slip distance of an edge dislocation segment of length ζc under applied shear stress, calculated using the Peierls-Nabarro (PN) model incorporating solute-induced stress τ13sol derived from five NEB atomistic samples.
summary: This panel illustrates the slip distance of an edge dislocation segment under shear stress, modeled via the Peierls-Nabarro approach. By integrating solute-induced stress from five NEB atomistic samples, the model determines the yield stress at the point where slip reaches half the critical barrier width of 6.12 Å.

caption: Optical micrograph of the aged Al4Fe0.3Zr alloy cross-section through the fracture region without ultrasonic processing (USP).
summary: This optical micrograph depicts the fracture surface of an aged Al4Fe0.3Zr alloy without ultrasonic processing. The crack propagation is observed to occur through primary intermetallics within the alloy. Precipitation hardening with Al3Zr did not alter the fundamental character of the fracture, maintaining the brittle-like propagation through the intermetallic phases.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the distribution of the average absolute relative error (AARE) across varying temperatures and strain rates.
summary: The contour plot visualizes the distribution of the average absolute relative error (AARE) as a function of temperature and strain rate. The ANN-based model exhibits very minor fluctuations in error, demonstrating high accuracy in developing an algorithm to describe the dataset across the investigated experimental parameter space.

caption: Frequency-transmissibility performance of the type-II double-layer QZS metastructure, measured experimentally across five different payload conditions to evaluate vibration isolation efficiency.
summary: This panel illustrates the vibration isolation performance of the type-II double-layer QZS metastructure through frequency-transmissibility curves. By utilizing the same five payloads as the type-I configuration, the data allows for a direct evaluation of how the compact unit arrangement affects the dynamic isolation capabilities of the metastructure under varying loads.

caption: NMR hydrogen spectra of PEGNB and HAMA polymers, highlighting characteristic peaks confirming successful functionalization of the hydrogel precursors.
summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the successful functionalization of the hydrogel precursors. The spectra display characteristic peaks corresponding to the methacrylate groups in HAMA and the norbornene groups in PEGNB, validating the chemical structure of the synthesized components used for subsequent hydrogel fabrication.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a 30 nm cube processed at LED = 0.1 J/mm and h = 0.03 mm, showing anisotropic elongated Cr-rich regions and Al-rich regions with an E* value of 2.61.
summary: This APT reconstruction displays a 30 nm cube processed at 0.1 J/mm. The sample exhibits anisotropic elongated features along the build direction. Cr-rich regions are highlighted by 9.5 at.% iso-surfaces, while Al-rich regions are marked by cyan points. No gamma-prime precipitation was detected in this specific processing condition.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the Ni0 alloy disk periphery after 1/2 turn of HPT, revealing a significantly refined microstructure with an average grain size of approximately 225 nm.
summary: Captured at the periphery of the Ni0 alloy specimen after 1/2 turn of HPT, this dark-field TEM image reveals a significantly refined microstructure. Quantitative analysis indicates an average grain size of approximately 225 nm, demonstrating the localized effect of the deformation process at the disk edge.

caption: 3D cross-sectional view illustrating the accumulation of magnetically labelled cells at the channel sidewalls in the presence of a permanent magnet.
summary: This 3D cross-sectional view visualizes the accumulation of magnetically labelled cells at the channel sidewalls. The presence of a permanent magnet drives the cells toward the sidewalls, where they aggregate. This observation is consistent with the measured sorting efficiency, which showed a strong decrease in absorbance at 250 μL/min.

caption: Representative bcc unit cell geometry used for modeling bending-dominated lattice behavior.
summary: This panel displays the representative bcc unit cell geometry. This specific lattice architecture is utilized in the experimental study to characterize bending-dominated mechanical behavior, providing a fundamental structural unit for analyzing the performance of the lattice structures under investigation.

caption: Changes in magnetic moment induced by a vacancy in Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy structures at 300 K and 2000 K, evaluated relative to the local coordination environment and benchmarked against fcc Ni-Fe.
summary: Changes in magnetic moment induced by a vacancy in Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy structures at 300 K and 2000 K are evaluated relative to the local coordination environment. The data is benchmarked against fcc Ni-Fe, illustrating how the presence of a vacancy alters the magnetic properties of the alloy based on its local environment.

caption: Weibull distribution plot of nanohardness values for HVAF-sprayed coatings, exhibiting two distinct slopes corresponding to low and high hardness regimes.
summary: This Weibull plot illustrates the nanohardness distribution for HVAF-sprayed coatings, revealing two distinct slopes that represent low and high hardness values. The high-hardness section of this distribution aligns closely with the hardness range observed in pure HVAF-sprayed WC–Co samples, indicating consistent mechanical behavior within this specific coating subset.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing solute clusters within a 10 × 20 × 20 nm³ volume at a depth of 600 nm under single-energy ion irradiation.
summary: This 3D reconstruction captures solute clusters at a depth of 600 nm under single-energy irradiation. Despite an increase in damage dose and implanted Fe content compared to shallower depths, the cluster number density remains stable, illustrating the complex interplay between irradiation-induced damage and solute cluster evolution in the material.

caption: Nyquist plots of the electrochemical impedance spectra for HP Ti, Ti64, TiCr, and TiCr3Sn samples, illustrating the impedance response in PBS after 4 hours of immersion.
summary: Nyquist plots of the impedance spectra for HP Ti and the Ti alloys demonstrate the electrochemical stability of the surface protective layers. The Ti alloys exhibit significantly higher polarisation resistance compared to HP Ti, confirming enhanced corrosion resistance and stability of the passive films formed on the alloy surfaces in PBS.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot for the Ti-6Al-4V/Nb2O5 composite, illustrating the electrochemical response of the modified surface.
summary: This Mott-Schottky curve for the Ti-6Al-4V/Nb2O5 composite exhibits a linear segment with a positive slope. This trend confirms that the surface film on the modified alloy also functions as an n-type metal oxide semiconductor, demonstrating the semiconducting nature of the Nb2O5-containing layer.

caption: Color variation (ΔE) values of black flash-PEO samples measured before and after 10 days of immersion in a 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: This bar chart displays the ΔE values representing the blackness of flash-PEO samples. The data compares the color stability of these samples before and after a 10-day immersion in a 3.5% NaCl solution, providing a quantitative assessment of the coating's color retention and overall environmental stability.

caption: CALPHAD-modeled solidification path and volumetric phase percentage for Ti–42Nb+2.0C under equilibrium conditions.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram depicts the equilibrium solidification path and volumetric phase fractions for the Ti–42Nb+2.0C composition. By modeling the thermodynamic state, the figure illustrates the phase transformation behavior and the final phase distribution, highlighting the impact of a 2.0% carbon addition on the solidification characteristics of the titanium-niobium matrix.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of a monocrystalline (110) Ni-based alloy after 100 hours of oxidation, showing a highly hydrated outer layer rich in nickel and iron oxides.
summary: Following 100 hours of oxidation in high-temperature water, the monocrystalline (110) Ni-based alloy exhibits a duplex oxide layer. ToF-SIMS profiling indicates that the outer layer, extending from 0 to 12 seconds of sputtering, is characterized by a high concentration of nickel and iron oxides and significant hydration.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of neat PET filaments, exhibiting a characteristic melting peak at 76 °C.
summary: This DSC curve characterizes the thermal response of neat PET filaments used in 3D printing. The plot identifies a specific melting peak located at 76 °C, providing essential data regarding the melting behavior and solidification characteristics of the PET resin during the printing process.

caption: Comparative Raman spectra of Ti3C2Tx and Mo2TiC2Tx nano-sheets, displaying characteristic bands that indicate the presence of -OH, -O, and -F surface terminations.
summary: Raman spectroscopy performed on the Ti3C2Tx and Mo2TiC2Tx nano-sheets reveals characteristic bands that confirm the chemical composition of the samples. These spectral features align with the expected stoichiometry and provide evidence for the existence of -OH, -O, and -F surface terminations on the synthesized nano-sheets.

caption: EBSD grain structure map of AlSi3.5Mg2.5 alloy at medium build height, printed at a platform temperature of 100 °C.
summary: This EBSD map characterizes the grain structure of the AlSi3.5Mg2.5 alloy at a medium build height for samples printed at a platform temperature of 100 °C. The visualization provides detailed information on the grain morphology and orientation, offering a clear view of the material's internal crystalline structure after additive manufacturing.

caption: Comparison of pressure drop values in kPa between CFD predictions and experimental measurements for HV Chevron and HV Diagonal designs at a constant flow rate of 7 m/s.
summary: This table compares CFD-predicted pressure drops against experimental data for HV Chevron and HV Diagonal designs at a 7 m/s flow rate. For the HV Chevron, CFD predicted 29 kPa in WD1 and 32 kPa in WD2, while experiments consistently showed 32 kPa, indicating no significant influence of chevron fin orientation.

caption: SEM-EDS elemental distribution profile showing an oxygen diffusion depth of 342 ± 13 μm in alloy 1 at 1180 °C.
summary: This SEM-EDS analysis of alloy 1 illustrates the diffusion behavior of sulphur and oxygen. At 1180 °C, the oxygen diffusion depth is measured at 342 ± 13 μm. The continuous line represents sulphur, while dashed lines indicate oxygen, providing a clear visualization of the elemental penetration depth within the alloy matrix.

caption: Distribution map of Cr showing its presence in the NA and extension into the WC-Co interface.
summary: Chromium (Cr) is naturally present in the NA and extends into the WC-Co near the NA interface. The concentration of Cr is observed to decrease with increasing distance from the NA, reflecting the gradient of elemental diffusion across the interface during the high-temperature treatment.

caption: SHAP value summary plot illustrating feature importance for multitask DNN predictions across 1250 test RVE samples, where red and blue dots represent high and low feature values respectively.
summary: This SHAP summary plot quantifies feature importance for multitask DNN predictions using 1250 test RVE samples. Fiber volume fraction emerges as the most significant predictor with a mean absolute SHAP value of 0.314, followed by porosity at 0.221. Color-coded dots indicate the directional impact of high versus low feature values.

caption: Phase distribution map of 3DHT-XY Ti–6Al–4V, highlighting the presence of β-phase regions.
summary: The phase diagram for 3DHT-XY Ti–6Al–4V shows that the α phase remains the primary constituent, exceeding 96% of the volume. Compared to the 3DHT-Z sample, this XY-oriented specimen exhibits a higher β-phase content, demonstrating the influence of fabrication orientation on the resulting phase composition of the alloy.

caption: Experimental creep rupture time (tf) as a function of inverse temperature (1/T) at a constant stress of 30 MPa, used to independently derive the Larson-Miller constant.
summary: Experimental data showing the relationship between rupture time and inverse temperature at a constant stress of 30 MPa are presented. This plot serves as an independent method to determine the Larson-Miller constant, validating the material's creep behavior based on observed temperature-dependent failure times under specific stress conditions.

caption: Normal spectral emissivity of four distinct samples measured using a Perkin Elmer 950 spectrometer across the 250–2500 nm wavelength range.
summary: This panel displays the normal spectral emissivity for four different samples measured via a Perkin Elmer 950 spectrometer in the 250–2500 nm range. These spectral data are essential for calculating solar absorbance and thermal emissivity at 300 K, facilitating the identification of spectral zones requiring high emissivity to maximize solar absorbance.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Fe 3 CoCrMnNiC 0.8 HE cast iron ingot prepared under Ar flow, illustrating the chemical segregation patterns within the microstructure.
summary: This elemental map displays the distribution of elements in the Fe 3 CoCrMnNiC 0.8 HE cast iron ingot. The visualization highlights the chemical segregation resulting from the solidification process, where metallic and carbonaceous elements partition between the dendritic FCC phase and the interdendritic regions during cooling under Ar flow.

caption: Overview of widely utilized metallic alloys categorized by their primary alloy types and corresponding general industrial applications.
summary: This figure provides a comprehensive overview of the most commonly used metallic alloys, organized by their specific alloy categories and general industrial applications. The selection of these representative materials was based on the availability and reliability of experimental data reported in the literature to ensure accurate representation of metallic behavior.

caption: Main effect plots of means and their ranks illustrating the relative influence of variables x7 and x8 on the system response.
summary: The main effect plots of means and their ranks demonstrate the sensitivity of the system to various input variables. Specifically, the gentler slopes observed for variables x7 and x8 indicate that these parameters exert a minimal influence on the overall response, highlighting their relative insignificance compared to other factors in the model.

caption: 3D worn surface topography of TiC-steel composite after sliding at 25 N load at elevated temperature (ET).
summary: This 3D wear scar morphology of the TiC-SS cermet pin after sliding at 25 N and elevated temperature shows prominent wear features. The surface is characterized by deep and wide abrasive grooves, indicating more severe wear compared to the scars observed after room temperature sliding.

caption: EBSD IQ, IPF, KAM, and GOS maps of cold-sprayed Cu deposits processed at an inlet gas temperature of 700 °C and 50 bar pressure.
summary: EBSD maps for Cu deposits at 700 °C illustrate the microstructural evolution of the cold-sprayed material. As the inlet gas temperature increases, the localization of plastic deformation primarily at inter-particle boundaries, which drives dynamic recrystallization, begins to diminish compared to the lower temperature conditions observed in the study.

caption: Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) plot ranking the association degree between individual feature descriptors and the phase transition temperature.
summary: The GRA plot quantifies the association degree between feature descriptors and the phase transition temperature.
