caption: Representative nano-indentation load-depth curves for Nb–16Si–20Ti–3Al alloys containing varying weight percentages of nano-ZrC (0, 2.5, 5.0, and 10.0 wt.%).
summary: Nano-indentation load-depth curves are displayed for Nb–16Si–20Ti–3Al alloys with different nano-ZrC additions. These curves characterize the mechanical response of the material at the nanoscale, showing how varying the ZrC content from 0 to 10.0 wt.% influences the indentation resistance and deformation behavior of the alloy matrix.

caption: Al–Al9Co2 phase boundary region derived from the common tangent construction method, showing the two-phase equilibrium region as a dashed line.
summary: The Al–Al9Co2 phase boundary is presented in this panel, illustrating the two-phase region as a dashed line. This boundary was systematically obtained by applying the common tangent construction method across various temperatures to the Gibbs free energy curves shown in the previous panel.

caption: Loss curve of the DeepLab V3+ model training process over 50 epochs, with specific loss values highlighted at 5-epoch intervals.
summary: The loss curve illustrates the training progress of the improved DeepLab V3+ model across 50 epochs. Loss values are explicitly marked at 5-epoch intervals, providing a clear visualization of the model's convergence behavior and performance improvement throughout the training duration as presented in the training results.

caption: Matrix of 30 selected fluid–metal combinations used for chemical compatibility testing via the Gas Plug Test.
summary: This table presents the 30 fluid–metal combinations selected for chemical compatibility investigations using the Gas Plug Test. To ensure experimental redundancy, three identical devices were manufactured for each of the listed combinations, resulting in a total of 90 individual samples used to evaluate material interactions across the study.

caption: Frequency-dependent total magnetic losses for 3D printed (T-AM) and standard (T-Std.) toroids measured at a constant induction of 50 mT within the 200–1000 kHz range.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of total magnetic losses as a function of frequency for 3D printed and standard processed toroids. Measured at a constant induction of 50 mT between 200 and 1000 kHz, the data shows that total magnetic loss levels become greater in the standard sample above 300 kHz.

caption: EBSD phase mapping of the A2 repaired sample showing a microstructure dominated by martensite with a low austenite fraction of 7.07%.
summary: EBSD phase mapping of the A2 repaired sample reveals a microstructure dominated by martensite. The austenite fraction is measured at only 7.07%. This result highlights the influence of the LTT strategy, which facilitates the retention of martensite to room temperature by lowering the transformation temperature during the repair process.

caption: Raw 2D diffraction pattern of the heat-treated condition, illustrating the α-Al ring morphology and small-angle signal intensity.
summary: This raw 2D diffraction pattern represents the heat-treated material condition. The spottiness of the α-Al rings indicates the grain characteristics of the sample. A small-angle signal is also present, allowing for a qualitative comparison of structural changes between the as-built and heat-treated states through the 2D diffraction data.

caption: Immunostaining of BMSCs on scaffolds showing vinculin expression in red and nuclei in blue to evaluate cell adhesion.
summary: Fluorescence micrographs depict the expression of vinculin, a focal adhesion protein, alongside the distribution of cell nuclei in BMSCs cultured on scaffolds. This immunostaining technique allows for the evaluation of cell adhesion mechanisms, which are critical for modulating cellular behaviors such as migration and adaptive responses to the extracellular matrix.

caption: Temperature-dependent shear moduli (G' and G'') profiles for the bioinks, recorded at a heating rate of 1 °C/s, highlighting thermal responsiveness and gel state stability.
summary: Rheological measurements show that the bioinks remain in a gel state (G' > G'') between 4 and 20 °C. A noticeable decrease in G' occurs between 20 and 30 °C, though the interlocking of rod-shaped microgels restricts flow even when the continuous GelMA phase becomes fully solubilized between 20 and 40 °C.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms illustrating the electrochemical response of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode after the 1st and 2nd cleaning procedures at a scan rate of 100 mV s−1.
summary: Evaluation of the cleaning process efficiency for the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode is shown through cyclic voltammograms comparing the 1st and 2nd cleaning cycles. These results confirm the effectiveness of the cleaning protocol in maintaining or restoring the electrochemical activity of the electrode surface for consistent performance.

caption: Finite element model configurations for five distinct structural members, including a conventional member, an isolated DCE-1, and three hybrid member versions.
summary: This panel displays the finite element model configurations developed for five distinct structural members. These include a conventional member, an isolated DCE-1, and three hybrid member versions. The illustration incorporates essential modeling parameters such as geometric dimensions, boundary conditions, section properties, material characteristics, and FE mesh sensitivity for each configuration.

caption: Previously reported interface structure of the η1 precipitate, which assumes a uniform planar interface without considering the V-shaped structural sub-units.
summary: This previously reported model assumes a uniform planar interface for the η1 precipitate, failing to account for the V-shaped structural sub-units observed in experimental data. It predicts ten aluminum atomic columns based on interplanar distances, contrasting with the nine columns observed in the presence of periodic interfacial segregation layers.

caption: Correlation plot illustrating the relationship between the total processing duration and the resulting density of the metal parts.
summary: This scatter plot examines the relationship between processing duration and metal part density. Given that thermal debinding is the most time-intensive stage, this analysis highlights the temporal trade-offs required to achieve higher densities, providing a critical discussion point regarding the efficiency and optimization of the overall manufacturing process.

caption: Experimental measurement configuration designed for the heatsink sector.
summary: This figure illustrates the experimental measurement setup utilized for the heatsink sector. The diagram provides a clear overview of the physical arrangement and components involved in the testing process, ensuring that the experimental conditions are accurately represented for the subsequent analysis of the heatsink's thermal performance and operational characteristics.

caption: MTEP measurement conducted along the b-axis of the 100 nm thick CrO2 thin film under identical thermal conditions of 178 K and 45 K.
summary: Representing the MTEP behavior along the b-axis, this panel illustrates the magnetic thermoelectric response of the CrO2 thin film. Consistent with the c-axis measurements, the MTEP data here effectively mirrors the magnetoresistance behavior, confirming the consistency of the electronic transport properties across the different in-plane axes.

caption: Small Angle X-Ray Scattering (SAXS) profiles comparing NoBPH and BPH specimens, demonstrating an increased volume fraction of secondary precipitates while primary precipitates remain unchanged.
summary: Small Angle X-Ray Scattering (SAXS) data reveal the precipitation and cluster characteristics of NoBPH and BPH specimens. The results indicate that while primary precipitates remain stable, there is a notable increase in the volume fraction of secondary precipitates in the BPH specimen compared to the NoBPH control sample.

caption: Raman spectral profile of carbon-based materials synthesized using the M1 preparation method, highlighting the presence of characteristic D and G bands.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of samples prepared via the M1 method reveals the presence of characteristic D and G bands. These spectral features are indicative of carbon-based materials, confirming the successful identification of the surface chemistry and structural characteristics of the synthesized samples through this spectroscopic technique.

caption: DRIFT spectra of silica-supported Ni 0.01 Cu nanoparticles in the C-O stretching region (1600–1800 cm⁻¹) after exposure to ethanol, highlighting the development of the acetaldehyde peak at 1723 cm⁻¹.
summary: Panel b presents the C-O stretching regime of the DRIFT spectra for silica-supported Ni 0.01 Cu nanoparticles following ethanol exposure. The data clearly demonstrate the development of a distinct peak at 1723 cm⁻¹, which corresponds to the C-O stretching vibration of acetaldehyde species formed at elevated temperatures of 150 and 250 °C.

caption: Microhardness profile for the weld produced at 4.2 kW and 1.5 m/min, exhibiting an atypical trend of increasing hardness from the fusion boundary toward the base metal.
summary: Representing a specific welding condition of 4.2 kW and 1.5 m/min, this panel highlights an abnormal microhardness profile. Unlike typical joints, this specimen shows a distinct increase in hardness values as the measurement moves from the fusion boundary outward into the base metal, indicating unique microstructural evolution during processing.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of the cutting edge on a drill bit under the first experimental condition.
summary: This EDS map of the cutting edge shows the chemical species present after the 50th hole under the first experimental condition. Analysis of the cutting edges across varying conditions reveals that no pronounced differences in Built-Up Edge (BUE) characteristics occur regardless of the specific cutting fluid utilized during machining.

caption: False height color map illustrating the surface topography of the Scr scenario extracted from STL data.
summary: Presented here is a false height color map of the Scr scenario, derived from STL data extraction. This visualization highlights the specific surface topography features associated with the Scr condition, illustrating the structural morphology observed during the experimental analysis of the sample.

caption: Conceptual illustration detailing the evolution of bubble cavitation and the associated micro-jetting action.
summary: This diagram depicts the evolution of bubble cavitation. The micro-jetting action generated during this process is critical for expelling bubbles from the liquid phase. By acting before solidification occurs, these mechanisms effectively reduce porosity by promoting the removal of bubbles from the molten pool during the manufacturing process.

caption: Elemental composition of the surface corrosion products on G3 alloy after 72 hours of exposure to a H2O-CO2-H2S-H2 atmosphere.
summary: Surface analysis of the G3 alloy corrosion products reveals a crystalline structure primarily composed of nickel and sulfur. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirms these elements are present in proportions of 51.5% for nickel and 31.5% for sulfur, indicating the formation of a specific nickel-sulfide corrosion product layer on the alloy surface.

caption: Thermal intensity profile for the full build of a 6-hatch wall, filtered with a 100-point moving mean and a 0.2 × 10^7 intensity threshold.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermal intensity for the full build of a 6-hatch wall. Following the removal of values below 0.2 × 10^7 and the application of a 100-point moving mean, the data shows a gradual increase in intensity over time, requiring more layers than the prism to reach a plateau.

caption: Conceptual representation of two segments joined at their corners, illustrating the configuration of the Cauchy slice Σ G as the union of left and right segments Σ L and Σ R.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometric configuration of two segments joined at their corners to form a Cauchy slice. The diagram defines the Hilbert space associated with the combined system Σ G, which is represented as a proper subspace within the tensor product of the individual left and right Hilbert spaces.

caption: Logarithmic relationship between rheological stress and strain rate for 316L steel, highlighting the linear correlation observed during the final stage of load retention.
summary: Panel d depicts the logarithmic relationship between rheological stress and strain rate for 316L steel during creep. A linear relationship is revealed in the final stage of load retention, which is consistent with established studies linking the stress index to the duration of creep retention time.

caption: Chemical potential of Cr in the Amdry365/IN792 sample after 150 minutes of oxidation at 1100 °C.
summary: The chemical potential of Cr in the Amdry365/IN792 sample after 150 minutes of oxidation at 1100 °C is shown. This final stage simulation reflects the long-term thermodynamic state of Cr within the material, completing the analysis of the three typical stages of the phase transformation process.

caption: HAADF-STEM image demonstrating LBE penetration along a twin boundary, characterized by a finger-like channel with negative curvature at the root.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image reveals that LBE preferentially penetrates along mechanical nanotwin boundaries in the steel. The resulting finger-like channel exhibits a distinct negative curvature at its root, a feature consistent with atomic-scale imaging of interfacial structures at penetration tips along mechanical nanotwin boundaries in these materials.

caption: Comparative 3D visualizations of parts from Dataset B, illustrating the progression from low-resolution webcam segmentations and bicubic interpolation to model-predicted super-resolution and high-resolution Basler ground-truth images.
summary: Visualizations of 3D parts from Dataset B are presented, showcasing the iterative stacking of build-layer masks. The panel highlights the visual quality differences between low-resolution webcam captures, bicubic upscaling, and the super-resolution model predictions, evaluated against high-resolution Basler ground-truth images to demonstrate the accuracy of the reconstructed 3D structures.

caption: Voltage evolution over a 500-hour mid-term galvanostatic stability test for a 3-SRU stack in SOEC mode, maintained at a constant current of -11 A.
summary: Demonstrating long-term stability, this galvanostatic test tracks the voltage of a 3-SRU stack over 500 hours at -11 A in SOEC mode. Despite minor fluctuations attributed to steam generation instability, the stack maintains consistent operation at approximately 1.1 V per cell, confirming the durability of the 3D printed cell architecture.

caption: Electronic PDOS profiles for Fe, O, and Mg atoms at the Fe/MgO interface.
summary: Presented here are the PDOS plots for Fe atoms, O atoms, and Mg atoms at the interface of the Fe/MgO pre-nucleation model. These electronic density of states profiles characterize the interaction between the iron atoms and the magnesium oxide surface at the atomic interface.

caption: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) plotted against training epochs for recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures varying from one to four layers.
summary: This plot illustrates the convergence behavior of RNN models by tracking the MAPE across training epochs for architectures with one to four layers. The visualization highlights how network depth influences both the rate of convergence and the final predictive accuracy, providing a comparative analysis of model performance during the training process.

caption: V CPD map and line profile of as-forged Al0.5CoCrFeNi at the phase boundary, highlighting a steep potential gradient of approximately 50 mV between the A1 and A2/B2 phases.
summary: In the as-forged Al0.5CoCrFeNi sample, distinct V CPD values are observed between the A1 phase and the A2/B2 phases. A steep potential gradient of approximately 50 mV exists across the inter-phase boundary, demonstrating significant electronic or compositional differences between these regions as captured by the SKPFM map.

caption: Crystal Orbital Overlap Population (COOP) curves illustrating the bonding and antibonding interactions between hydrogen and metal atoms within the Fe55Cr25Ni20–H–H cluster.
summary: The COOP curves for the H–metal interactions are presented for the Fe55Cr25Ni20–H–H cluster. These curves provide a detailed visualization of the electronic bonding and antibonding states resulting from the interaction between hydrogen and the metallic components, offering insight into the stability and chemical bonding characteristics of the hydrogen-metal system.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) in reline deep eutectic solvent (DES) comparing the baseline (dashed line) with the electrolyte containing 50 mM Ni(II) and Cr(III) (blue line) at 328 K.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry performed on a GCE in reline DES reveals that the pure solvent exhibits negligible current density. In contrast, the addition of 50 mM Ni(II)-Cr(III) results in a significant increase in current density, characterized by a distinct reduction peak during the forward scan, indicating the successful electrodeposition of Ni-Cr alloy.

caption: TDS-GU hydrogen release spectra for 3.5NiCrMoV steel specimens charged at 2, 20, 80, and 200 bar hydrogen pressures for 24 hours.
summary: This plot displays TDS-GU hydrogen spectra for 3.5NiCrMoV steel discs charged in gaseous hydrogen at pressures ranging from 2 to 200 bar. The data, which underwent numerical fitting to a chi-square tolerance of 1x10^-6, illustrates the hydrogen release behavior as a function of the initial charging pressure.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized DMA material.
summary: This panel displays the 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized DMA material. The spectrum serves as a characterization tool to confirm the chemical structure of the synthesized DMA, providing a baseline for comparison and verification of the synthesis process as described in the experimental analysis.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for ferrite-austenite interfaces classified as Others, plotted in the ferrite crystal lattice frame.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the habit plane distribution for intergranular interfaces categorized as Others within the ferrite reference frame. The habit planes terminate on (110) orientations. Minimal MRD values are observed at the (111) ferrite plane, corresponding to the highest curvature distribution identified for this specific interface category.

caption: Magnetization (M) versus magnetic field (H) hysteresis loops for Ni50Ti42.5Er7.5 samples, comparing the homogenized state with the extruded condition.
summary: This plot displays the magnetization behavior of Ni50Ti42.5Er7.5 alloys. The extrusion process, represented by red squares, maintains the linear shape of the M-H loop while inducing a slight increase in magnetic susceptibility. Conversely, homogenization treatment introduces non-linearity into the magnetic response, demonstrating the influence of processing history on magnetic properties.

caption: Rhenium elemental distribution map of the II-100 (98%) sample surface.
summary: Rhenium distribution across the II-100 (98%) sample surface is visualized in this WDS map. By comparing this distribution with the molybdenum map, one can assess the elemental composition and potential segregation patterns within the material, confirming the chemical makeup of the analyzed sample.

caption: Extract ion thermograms of PMVEMA raw material showing fragment ions at m/z 67, 77, and 91 linked to volatile degradation products.
summary: Extract ion thermograms for PMVEMA raw material identify the release of volatile degradation products. The analysis tracks fragment ions at m/z 67 for 2-methyl-2-cyclopenten-1-one, m/z 77 for p-xylene, and m/z 91 for toluene, mapping the specific chemical evolution of the polymer during the thermal degradation process.

caption: Mixing index variation for the K1 microreactor plotted against mixing distance at Reynolds indexes of 2.5 and 7.5.
summary: The K1 microreactor performance is evaluated by plotting the mixing index against the mixing distance. Simulations conducted at Reynolds indexes of 2.5 and 7.5 reveal similar trends in mixing efficiency, providing a baseline for comparing the K1 design against other microreactors in the series under varying flow conditions.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for fully hydrogenated Ti Gd-2, Ti Gd5, and Ti-5553 alloys, recorded under argon flow at a heating rate of 5 °C/min.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for fully hydrogenated Ti Gd-2, Ti Gd5, and Ti-5553 alloys are presented, measured under argon flow at a 5 °C/min heating rate. These results demonstrate that the hydrogen capacity of the hydride materials derived from these alloys is slightly lower than that of pure titanium.

caption: Stress-time evolution illustrating time-dependent phenomena for the second loading cycle at 750 °C, contrasting experimental results with model predictions.
summary: Depicted here is the stress-time behavior for the second loading cycle at 750 °C, highlighting time-dependent phenomena. By comparing experimental measurements with viscoelastic-viscoplastic model predictions, the plot illustrates the accuracy of the calibrated model in capturing temporal material responses during the specified isothermal loading cycle.

caption: Saturation loading of Ni and Co as a function of MgAlOx (MA) content in MAZ supports, comparing single-precursor impregnation with co-impregnation methods.
summary: This plot illustrates the saturation loading behavior of Ni and Co on MgAlOx supports. Blue circles and red rectangles denote single-precursor loading, while green markers represent co-impregnation. The orange dashed line indicates the 7.9% MA loading selected for subsequent catalyst synthesis to ensure MA is not the limiting factor.

caption: SHAP dependence plot showing the impact of NPD on residual stress predictions along the step direction σy.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the effect of NPD on residual stress predictions along the step direction σy. Each dot represents a single prediction, with the x-axis showing the feature value and the y-axis representing the SHAP value in MPa, colored by the strongest interacting feature.

caption: Electronic band structure calculated for the BL-Si2O layered material.
summary: Electronic band structure calculated for the BL-Si2O layered material. This plot represents the energy dispersion relations for the BL-Si2O phase within the Family-II materials group. The band structure provides critical insight into the electronic properties of this specific layered configuration as part of the broader study on Si2O-based materials.

caption: EDS spectrum of particle-shaped crystals (F) showing the presence of Gd, O, and Zr.
summary: This EDS spectrum provides the elemental analysis for particle-shaped crystals (F). The results indicate that these crystals are primarily composed of Gd, O, and Zr elements, differing in composition from the other crystal types analyzed in the figure.

caption: EPMA point analysis of TiC-reinforced CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy composite, highlighting specific elemental regions.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis (EPMA) was performed on the TiC-reinforced CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy composite to investigate elemental decomposition during the DED process. This analysis identifies distinct regions, including Ti-rich zones and carbon-rich areas, providing insight into the microstructural evolution and elemental distribution within the composite matrix after laser processing.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction patterns corresponding to the individual γ′ and γ′′ phases observed in the dark-field image.
summary: These SAED patterns provide specific crystallographic identification for the γ′ and γ′′ phases shown in the dark-field image. The diffraction data confirms the presence and orientation of these precipitates, consistent with observations of similar alloy systems, facilitating a deeper understanding of the phase evolution.

caption: UV-vis absorbance spectra of DPPA and AESO resins, highlighting absorption peaks within the 450 nm blue-wavelength range corresponding to the LED emission.
summary: The UV-vis absorbance spectra for DPPA and AESO resins are presented, demonstrating distinct absorption peaks in the blue-wavelength range. These peaks align with the emission range of the LED light source used for photopolymerization, which is attributed to the presence of the blue-light absorbing photoinitiator CQ.

caption: Nyquist plot for untreated and treated samples in 3.5% NaCl solution, featuring an inserted equivalent circuit model.
summary: The Nyquist plot for untreated and treated samples in a 3.5% NaCl solution displays characteristic capacitive semicircles. An equivalent circuit model is integrated into the plot to represent the electrochemical behavior, providing insights into the corrosion resistance of the tested materials under the specified saline environment.

caption: Sympathetic austenite-ferrite interface visualization categorized by the Nishiyama-Wassermann (N-W) orientation relationship, highlighted with unique interface ID coloring.
summary: Representing sympathetic austenite-ferrite interfaces, this panel illustrates structures conforming to the Nishiyama-Wassermann (N-W) orientation relationship. The interfaces are rendered in unique colors to denote specific IDs. These needle-shaped features are consistent with the N-W classification, demonstrating the spatial arrangement of sympathetic austenite within the surrounding ferrite grain structure.

caption: Experimental pole figure of the 316L sample, confirming the {110}<001> Goss texture.
summary: Experimental pole figure analysis of the 316L sample confirms the presence of a {110}<001> Goss texture. This experimental observation matches the simulated texture, providing critical evidence that the simulation accurately reproduces the crystallographic characteristics of the material produced during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Iterative GPR model framework for LPBF AlSi10Mg process optimization, illustrating the feedback loop between mechanical property prediction, error estimation, and experimental validation.
summary: This schematic outlines an iterative GPR model framework designed for LPBF AlSi10Mg. It demonstrates how the model predicts mechanical properties and associated errors to guide experimental selection. This feedback loop improves prediction accuracy, explores unknown process windows, and establishes PSP relationships by incorporating new experimental data into the database.

caption: Cross-sectional imaging of the Gyroid lattice structure illustrating internal porosity.
summary: Gyroid structures achieve a high density of 99.72% as confirmed by cross-sectional imaging. The analysis indicates that this structure comprises only a few decent to smaller-sized porosities. This minimal presence of larger defects is consistent with the high density values recorded for this specific lattice geometry.

caption: Fatigue life N f response to variations in scan speed v, with predictions extended beyond the training database range indicated by dashed lines.
summary: This panel displays the effect of scan speed v on the fatigue life N f as evaluated by the BNN model. The plot includes predictions extending outside the training range observed in the TDB, represented by black dashed lines, to characterize the sensitivity of fatigue life to variations in scan speed.

caption: Visualization of the first four principal component bases, representing the fundamental 2D SAS patterns used for reconstructing the dataset.
summary: Depicting the first four principal component bases, this panel shows the fundamental patterns required for reconstructing the SAS data. As noted in the study, eight principal components are sufficient to capture 95% of the explained variance, demonstrating the efficiency of this basis set in representing the complex microstructural dataset.

caption: Artificial microstructure consisting of a matrix containing spherical voids, utilized to evaluate potential limitations and pitfalls of the methodology.
summary: Panel (b) presents a fully artificial microstructure composed of a matrix embedded with spherical voids. This model is specifically examined to identify potential limitations and pitfalls of the proposed methodology, providing a controlled environment to observe effects that contrast with those found in the real-world lattice structures studied in the manuscript.

caption: Ternary plot illustrating the volumetric binder composition of ten distinct feedstocks, defined according to a simplex centroid mixture design.
summary: This ternary plot displays the volumetric binder compositions for ten specific feedstocks. The experimental design follows a simplex centroid mixture approach, defining the compositional fields for the test matrix. These compositions represent the specific formulations used to evaluate the fracture surfaces of the middle points and edges of the test specimens.

caption: Cyclic softening and hardening curves comparing HT1, HT2, and HT3 specimens across different strain amplitudes.
summary: This comparative plot highlights the cyclic softening and hardening behavior of HT1, HT2, and HT3 specimens. At a strain amplitude of 0.4%, all three specimens exhibit slight cyclic hardening during the early stages of the cycle, providing insight into the initial deformation response of the different heat-treated materials.

caption: Box plot distribution of α-colony size across varying layer thicknesses, specifically comparing B2 (0.5 mm), B3 (1.0 mm), and B6 (1.5 mm).
summary: This panel displays the α-colony size distribution for different layer thicknesses. Quantitative analysis indicates that the thinnest layers (B2, 0.5 mm) and the thickest layers (B6, 1.5 mm) exhibit colony size distributions comparable to the baseline B3 (1.0 mm), suggesting minimal sensitivity of colony size to layer thickness variations.

caption: Histogram illustrating the distribution of strain localization events across various microstructural features for three distinct grain sizes.
summary: This histogram quantifies strain localization per area, categorizing events by microstructural features across three grain sizes. Findings indicate that in very fine-grain microstructures, 73% of microplasticity occurs at grain boundaries, compared to 42% and 22% for fine- and coarse-grain samples, respectively. Additionally, coarser grains exhibit increased slip band development within grain interiors.

caption: High-magnification HAADF-STEM image focusing on the region within the yellow rectangle of panel (a), revealing detailed precipitate morphology.
summary: Captured from the yellow rectangular region in panel (a), this high-magnification HAADF-STEM image provides a detailed view of the precipitate morphology. The image serves as a basis for subsequent elemental mapping, confirming that the observed nanoparticles are primarily composed of Mo, Ti, and C, with a notable enrichment of Ti.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the KPI gap across environmental, economic, and social sustainability indicators for various rPLA blends.
summary: This radar chart visualizes the KPI gap across environmental, economic, and social indicators. Environmental metrics, including global warming potential and cumulative energy demand, show clear improvements as recycled content increases. The V0:R100 blend demonstrates the smallest deviations from the sustainability threshold, highlighting the positive impact of higher recycled content.

caption: Nano-computed tomography reconstruction of the 5% specimen, showing a relative density of 99.994%.
summary: Nano-computed tomography reconstruction of the 5% specimen, showing a relative density of 99.994%. This image provides insight into the internal pore distribution analysis. The high density value indicates that the specimen was manufactured effectively, maintaining structural integrity consistent with the study's requirement for densities exceeding 99.95%.

caption: Capacitance response of G slab-based sensors embedded in a bicycle helmet during front loading conditions.
summary: This panel presents the sensor performance of G slab-based capacitors embedded in a bicycle helmet under front loading conditions. The data captures the electrical response of the sensor array as the helmet undergoes compression from the front, providing a quantitative measure of the sensor's sensitivity to frontal impact forces.

caption: Statistical distribution of dendrite metrics for all dendrites, equiaxed dendrites (ED), and columnar dendrites (CD) across varying printing parameters.
summary: Statistical analysis of dendrite metrics reveals the influence of printing parameters on microstructure. Higher scanning power and lower volumetric energy density promote finer dendritic cells due to increased cooling rates. This box plot compares metrics for all dendrites, equiaxed dendrites, and columnar dendrites, demonstrating the statistical significance of these processing-induced structural variations.

caption: Distribution of the IFV across the nozzle temperature parameter space, showing the mean value as a blue line and the 95% confidence interval as a shaded region derived from Gaussian Process Regression.
summary: This panel illustrates the IFV distribution as a function of nozzle temperature, optimized via BOIF. The blue line represents the mean IFV, while the shaded area indicates the 95% confidence interval calculated through GPR. This visualization effectively captures the uncertainty and trend of the IFV within the explored parameter space.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curve for the Fe-Mn-Al-Ni-Cr alloy, showing the anodic region with characteristic secondary or ternary minima (E corr,2 and E corr,3) observed during the electrochemical test.
summary: This potentiodynamic polarization curve characterizes the electrochemical behavior of the polycrystalline Fe-Mn-Al-Ni-Cr specimen. The anodic region exhibits distinct secondary and ternary minima, denoted as E corr,2 and E corr,3, which provide insight into the corrosion resistance and surface reaction kinetics of the material under the tested electrolytic conditions.

caption: Strain at yield radar plot displaying the mechanical response of composites with varying face-to-core ratios compared to the monolithic core reference.
summary: Strain at yield performance is visualized for composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8. The gray area represents the monolithic core performance, allowing for a direct assessment of how different configurations deviate from the baseline, which is essential for evaluating the ductility of the multi-material samples.

caption: STEM high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) micrograph of the sintered AlCoCrFeNi alloy, showing a dense distribution of black Al2O3 oxide particles, most of which are smaller than 30 nm in diameter.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image of the sintered AlCoCrFeNi alloy demonstrates a significant reinforcement effect provided by a dense population of Al2O3 particles. These particles appear as black features within the matrix, with the majority of the oxide precipitates measuring less than 30 nm in diameter throughout the alloy microstructure.

caption: Creep strain rate versus stress for Hastelloy X at 800 °C, illustrating results from standard creep, stress-relaxation, and SSRT tests assessed via the unified inelastic strain partitioning assumption.
summary: Hastelloy X creep strain rate behavior at 800 °C is depicted, combining standard creep, stress-relaxation, and SSRT measurements. The SSRT data is processed using a unified inelastic strain partitioning assumption. While SSRT results remain within the conventional trend band, stress-relaxation data points are observed to fall outside this established range.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) profiles for the LPBF alloy specimen under varying experimental conditions.
summary: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profiles for the LPBF alloy are presented, illustrating the hydrogen release behavior across different experimental conditions. These TDS curves provide critical data on the desorption characteristics of the laser powder bed fusion processed material, serving as a baseline for comparing hydrogen trapping and release kinetics in the alloy.

caption: Tabulated data summarizing the influence of adjusted process parameters on the mechanical variability and microstructural integrity of additively manufactured metal components.
summary: Table 3 presents a systematic evaluation of how specific modifications to additive manufacturing process parameters directly influence the resulting mechanical characteristics and microstructural uniformity of metal parts. This data demonstrates that optimized parameter control effectively diminishes mechanical variability while simultaneously enhancing the overall microstructural properties of the fabricated metallic materials.

caption: Initial state of the VL-0.8 pattern at t = 0.94 msec, showing the ignition point marked by a yellow spark.
summary: This initial frame captures the VL-0.8 pattern at 0.94 msec. The ignition point is clearly indicated by a yellow spark, establishing the starting condition for the subsequent reaction propagation. The direction of the reaction front is oriented from the bottom toward the top of the structured region.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the GH4151 sample creep-tested at 750 °C/540 MPa/1%, displaying dislocation loops formed by interactions with tertiary γ′ precipitates.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph illustrates the deformed substructure of the GH4151 sample creep-tested at 750 °C and 540 MPa to 1% strain. Dislocation loops are observed in the γ matrix, likely resulting from the interaction between dislocations and tertiary γ′ precipitates during the steady creep stage.

caption: High energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern of coarse Ni-based superalloy powders, revealing the presence of γ′ phases and MC carbides alongside the γ matrix, with evidence of preferential orientation in the low-angle region.
summary: Panel (b) displays the synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern for coarse Ni-based superalloy powders. The data reveals the distinct presence of γ′ phases and MC carbides within the γ matrix. Additionally, the pattern indicates preferential orientation in the low-angle region, highlighting structural differences compared to the fine powder samples.

caption: Training error evolution of the initial policy network, plotted as a function of training iterations with associated confidence intervals derived from 15 independent experimental trials.
summary: This plot illustrates the training error curve for the initial policy network. To ensure statistical robustness and mitigate the contingency of individual runs, the results from 15 separate experiments were aggregated. The curve displays the error trend over time, accompanied by confidence intervals to represent the variability across these trials.

caption: Raman spectrum of the TiO₂-coated SLB (Multilayer 3) showing the persistence of carbon D and G bands alongside new peaks at 144, 399, and 639 cm⁻¹ corresponding to anatase TiO₂.
summary: Following the deposition of the TiO₂ film, the Raman spectrum of the SLB substrate retains detectable D and G bands. New vibrational modes at 144, 399, and 639 cm⁻¹ confirm the presence of anatase TiO₂. The marked decrease in the ID/IG ratio from 1.87 to 0.35 indicates improved structural order or coverage.

caption: Confocal fluorescence image of 63% porosity construct stained with DAPI (blue) and F-actin (magenta) under 0 mW·cm⁻² ultrasound stimulation.
summary: Confocal imaging of 63% porosity constructs under 0 mW·cm⁻² ultrasound stimulation displays the distribution of nuclei and F-actin filaments in high-porosity environments. This qualitative observation is essential for understanding the baseline cellular response to scaffold architecture in the absence of ultrasound, facilitating comparisons with stimulated samples in subsequent experimental conditions.

caption: TGA and DTG curves comparing untreated and plasma-treated carbon samples, highlighting a distinct decomposition peak at approximately 210 °C in the derivative weight percentage plot for the treated material.
summary: This figure presents the thermal stability of carbon samples through TGA and DTG analysis. The derivative weight percentage plot reveals a specific peak at 210 °C for plasma-treated carbon, which is attributed to the thermal decomposition of semi-ionic C-F bonds formed during the plasma treatment process compared to untreated carbon.

caption: Open circuit voltage curves for in situ 3D-printed PVDF foam and PVDF nanocomposite foams, showing the effect of structural foaming on voltage output.
summary: Open circuit voltage curves are shown for in situ 3D-printed PVDF foam and PVDF nanocomposite foams. The data illustrates the impact of the foam structure on the electrical output, with specific nanocomposite formulations containing 5 and 7 wt% graphene achieving notable voltage outputs of approximately 460 V and 380 V, respectively.

caption: Grain size distribution histograms for LPBF Inconel 625 alloy samples fabricated at 0°, 45°, and 90° orientations within the vertical cross-section.
summary: This histogram illustrates the grain size distributions in the vertical cross-section of LPBF Inconel 625 alloy samples. Quantitative analysis reveals average grain sizes of 13.27 µm, 18.19 µm, and 22.42 µm for the 0°, 45°, and 90° samples, respectively, demonstrating a clear trend of increasing grain size with build orientation.

caption: Bode phase angle plot depicting the variation of the system's phase angle as a function of frequency for as-built SLM, HT SLM, and wrought 316 L samples.
summary: The Bode phase plot shows how the phase angle of the system's impedance, related to charge transfer resistance, varies with frequency for the tested samples. These results, obtained in a 3.5 wt % NaCl solution, highlight the distinct electrochemical behaviors of as-built SLM, HT SLM, and wrought 316 L materials.

caption: Stereographic projection of the parent β phase for the 7% strained specimen.
summary: This stereographic projection shows the parent β phase orientation for the 7% strained specimen. It is used to analyze the variant selection process, specifically where the martensitic variant CV5 is identified as having the highest transformation strain of 2.71% under these specific loading conditions.

caption: K-S orientation relationship interfaces between intragranular austenite and ferrite in the HT100-300 condition, highlighting needle-shaped boundary structures.
summary: Focusing on the HT100-300 condition, this panel displays intragranular austenite-ferrite interfaces classified under the K-S orientation relationship. The boundaries are predominantly needle-shaped, consistent with the observed transformation pathways in this thermal treatment condition. Distinct interface IDs are color-coded to provide a clear spatial representation of the boundary network.

caption: Surface topography of CuOF powder oxidized at 300 °C, displaying an increased surface roughness of 25.3 ± 4.1 nm.
summary: Surface topography of CuOF powder oxidized at 300 °C, displaying an increased surface roughness of 25.3 ± 4.1 nm. AFM measurements indicate that the surface of the powder particles is not entirely smooth, illustrating how the oxidation process at higher temperatures contributes to the evolution of the particle surface roughness.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map of Aluminum (Al) showing enrichment within the interface zone of the FGH98 superalloy joint.
summary: Aluminum distribution is mapped via EPMA, revealing significant enrichment within the interface zone. As a γ′ phase forming element, Al concentration at the interface is critical for phase stability. The results confirm that Al, alongside Ti, accumulates in the interface zone, influencing the local microstructural evolution of the bonded superalloy.

caption: Nyquist plots representing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy response of commercial and SLM HX samples immersed in 3.5 wt % NaCl solution at 25 °C.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements for commercial and SLM HX samples are presented as Nyquist plots at 25 °C. These plots, derived from tests in a 3.5 wt % NaCl solution, serve as a basis for evaluating the corrosion response of the different HX materials under ambient temperature conditions.

caption: Tabulated data summarizing the quantitative EBSD analysis results for AB-H samples across the tested strain rates.
summary: This table compiles the quantitative data derived from the EBSD analysis of AB-H samples subjected to dynamic impact compression. It provides a structured summary of the microstructural parameters measured at strain rates of 0, 3699, 5650, and 7452 s⁻¹, facilitating a direct comparison of the material's response to varying impact intensities.

caption: Raman spectroscopic analysis comparing the structural integrity of intact diamond particles versus damaged diamond particles.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is utilized to evaluate the structural state of diamond particles within the composite. The spectrum provides a comparative analysis between intact diamond particles and those identified as damaged in previous imaging, serving as a diagnostic tool for carbon allotrope identification where XRD analysis remains inconclusive.

caption: PLA printed grid pattern at 75% density exhibiting visible deformation in the square-shaped porosities.
summary: Depicted is a PLA grid pattern printed at 75% density. The structural integrity of the grid is compromised, as evidenced by clear deformation observed in the square shape of the porosities, indicating that increasing the pattern density significantly alters the geometric uniformity of the printed material.

caption: Linearity range of cathodic QSSP for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) conducted at a scan rate of -0.1667 mV s⁻¹ in 30 wt% KOH aqueous solution, with potentials scanned from -0.1 to 0.6 V vs. RHE.
summary: This plot illustrates the linear potential range for cathodic QSSP during the hydrogen evolution reaction. The test was performed in a 30 wt% KOH solution at room temperature with a scan rate of -0.1667 mV s⁻¹. The potential interval for this cathodic measurement was scanned from -0.1 to 0.6 V vs. RHE.

caption: Dark-field TEM image obtained using the 111 reflection of the Si phase, highlighting the distribution of silicon precipitates.
summary: Captured using the 111 ring reflection of the Si phase, this dark-field TEM image highlights the distribution of nanosized equiaxed silicon precipitates. These particles, measuring between 19 and 54 nm, are clearly visible both along the dendrite boundaries and uniformly dispersed within the dendrite branches of the cellular structure.

caption: Isothermal dilatometric measurement curves at 500 °C for 30 % and 43 % cold rolled samples, showing incubation times of 7200 s and 5400 s, respectively.
summary: Isothermal dilatometry at 500 °C assesses precipitation effectiveness in cold-rolled samples. The curves demonstrate distinct incubation times of 7200 s for the 30 % cold-rolled sample and 5400 s for the 43 % cold-rolled sample. Additionally, the 30 % cold-rolled sample reaches its dilatation peak age after 2 hours.

caption: Summary table detailing the unique laser power and dwell time adjustments applied to each of the four processed parts.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive overview of the specific process parameters, including laser power and dwell time, utilized for the controlled fabrication of four distinct parts. It highlights that laser power reductions are maintained consistently throughout the remainder of the layer processing, ensuring unique and precise control for each individual component.

caption: Zero-field cooling magnetic susceptibility data plotted against temperature for the Ta5+xMo35-xW5Re35Ru20C20 series, demonstrating the magnetic response across the transition region.
summary: Magnetic susceptibility measurements under zero-field cooling conditions are presented for the Ta5+xMo35-xW5Re35Ru20C20 high-entropy alloy series. The plot characterizes the magnetic properties of the material as a function of temperature, providing insight into the superconducting transition characteristics observed across the varying compositions of the alloy series.

caption: Tabulated characterization data for Al2O3 specimens sintered at varying temperatures, detailing key material properties including porosity, grain size, Vickers hardness, and fracture toughness.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive characterization of Al2O3 materials sintered at different temperatures. It lists essential physical and mechanical properties, specifically porosity, grain size, hardness, and fracture toughness, serving as a foundational dataset for evaluating the influence of sintering temperature on the final material performance and structural integrity.

caption: STEM bright-field image of the γ-Ni region, revealing phase separation between light and dark contrast areas within the thermally sprayed microstructure.
summary: This STEM bright-field image displays the γ-Ni region of a thermally sprayed material, which exhibits distinct phase separation. The microstructure is characterized by intimately mixed regions of light and dark contrast, where the lighter phase is identified as γ-Ni and the darker phase as (Mo, Si)-rich γ-Ni.

caption: AuxC lattice structure assembly in a 4x4x4 configuration.
summary: The AuxC lattice structure is displayed as a 4x4x4 assembly. This visualization illustrates the geometric arrangement and periodic unit cell repetition of the AuxC design, providing a clear representation of its structural configuration within the specified lattice dimensions as described in the research findings.

caption: Storage modulus curves of TPU/PLA samples with different ratios, illustrating the temperature-dependent mechanical stiffness.
summary: Storage modulus curves for TPU/PLA samples with varying ratios are displayed. These curves characterize the mechanical stiffness of the composite filaments across a temperature range, providing essential data on the material's elastic response and structural integrity as part of the comprehensive dynamic mechanical analysis conducted on the samples.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the phase composition of pure Ti6Al4V powder and the 2 wt% Mo2C/Ti6Al4V mixed powder.
summary: X-ray diffraction analysis was performed on the mixed powders to characterize their phase composition. The resulting patterns provide a comparison between the pure Ti6Al4V matrix and the 2 wt% Mo2C/Ti6Al4V composite, confirming the presence of the constituent phases prior to the selective laser melting process.

caption: Elemental scanning image of the 20–0.15–30 sample surface following friction testing.
summary: This panel presents an elemental scanning image of the 20–0.15–30 sample surface after friction testing. By comparing this map with the pre-friction state, researchers can assess the surface compositional changes resulting from mechanical wear, which helps in understanding the degradation of material properties and long-term operational performance in engineering applications.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the as-deposited coating showing the initial nano-lamella structure with a lamellae width of approximately 1.8 nm, oriented along the [101] zone axis.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph displays the as-deposited coating's nano-lamella structure. The grains are oriented along the [101] zone axis. The lamellae exhibit a width of approximately 1.8 nm, providing a baseline for the structural evolution observed in the subsequent annealed samples described in the study.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of variant A viewed along the [2 0 1 ‾ ] I zone axis.
summary: This SAED pattern, collected from variant A along the [2 0 1 ‾ ] I zone axis, is used to analyze the crystallographic characteristics of the lamellae. By examining such patterns at specific tilt angles, researchers can determine the orientation relationships between the lamellae, which differ for varying λ values.

caption: Peak cutting and thrust forces measured during orthogonal machining of neat and fiber-reinforced PEEK with a 45° filament orientation, plotted across varying machining speeds and depths of cut.
summary: This plot displays peak cutting and thrust forces for neat and fiber-reinforced PEEK specimens with 45° filament orientations. The data illustrates how machining parameters, specifically speed and depth of cut, influence force magnitudes. These results provide a comprehensive overview of the mechanical response of PEEK materials during orthogonal cutting processes.

caption: Bright-field (BF) TEM image corresponding to the STEM-HAADF view in (g).
summary: The bright-field TEM image provides complementary structural information to the HAADF-STEM view, highlighting the morphology of the ST 900 microstructure. This image serves as a reference for identifying specific zones of interest, such as zones 1, 2, and 3, which are further examined at higher magnification in subsequent panels.

caption: Progression at t = 7 ms illustrating continued droplet growth and further reduction of the leading arc length.
summary: At t = 7 ms, the leading wire tip continues to be heated and melted by the leading arc. The droplet size increases significantly, leading to a further reduction in the arc length. This process highlights the rapid growth phase of the droplet during the leading arc operation.

caption: 3D topography of the laser-irradiated surface at 7.68 W average power.
summary: The 3D topography at 7.68 W average power shows the continued generation of hierarchical micro/nanostructures on the irradiated surface. Even at this highest power level, the laser irradiation process effectively maintains the formation of complex, multi-scale topographical features across the treated surface area.

caption: ILEEMS spectrum of 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst recorded at room temperature following dry reforming of methane at 750 °C and 1 atm for 30 minutes, showing experimental data points fitted with a Ni-Fe alloy S sub-spectrum and an Fe3+-substituted MgAl2O4 spinel D doublet sub-spectrum.
summary: This ILEEMS spectrum characterizes the 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst after dry reforming of methane. The experimental data is deconvoluted into two primary components: a blue-line Ni-Fe alloy sub-spectrum representing metallic phases and an orange-line D doublet sub-spectrum corresponding to Fe3+ ions substituted within the octahedral and tetrahedral sites of the MgAl2O4 spinel lattice.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the classification performance of the real-time approach utilizing an SVM model, which achieves a prediction accuracy of 92.3%.
summary: This confusion matrix evaluates the real-time approach using an SVM model. The visualization illustrates the classification performance, demonstrating a prediction accuracy of 92.3%. This result is part of a comparative analysis between real-time and thermal history-based approaches for material classification tasks as presented in the study.

caption: Three-dimensional rendering of the eutectic network within the AlMg8 alloy, reconstructed using plasma-focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (PFIB-SEM).
summary: The 3D rendering provides a comprehensive visualization of the eutectic network within the AlMg8 alloy. By utilizing PFIB-SEM, the interconnected nature of the eutectic phase surrounding the α-Al cells is clearly demonstrated. This architecture is critical for maximizing healing efficiency by enabling the transport of the eutectic phase to damaged areas.

caption: Detailed current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 10 m/min, complementing panel (c).
summary: This panel displays the detailed current-voltage characteristics for the 10 m/min wire feed rate condition. It serves as a comparative reference for the electrical performance of the deposition process, illustrating the specific current and duration profiles associated with this higher wire feed rate setting.

caption: Atomic model of SL-Si2O stacking mode IV, representing the final high-symmetry stacking configuration.
summary: Stacking mode IV completes the set of four high-symmetry configurations constructed for the SL-Si2O vdW structure. Like the other modes, it is based on the symmetry of the system. This model provides the final structural variation required to evaluate the impact of stacking on the material's physical properties.

caption: HNMR analysis of CP-PLA showing characteristic proton signals at 5.17 ppm for methylene protons and 1.58 ppm for methyl protons in the PLA unit.
summary: The HNMR analysis of CP-PLA identifies specific chemical environments within the polymer structure. Signals at 5.17 ppm and 1.58 ppm are assigned to methylene and methyl protons in the PLA unit, respectively, confirming the successful characterization of the polymer's molecular composition through proton resonance spectroscopy.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental map showing the distribution of Magnesium (Mg) within the 3# alloy.
summary: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy map illustrates the spatial distribution of Magnesium within the 3# alloy. Analysis indicates that Magnesium, along with other constituent elements, is evenly distributed across the surface of the alloy particle, confirming a homogeneous elemental composition throughout the observed microstructure of the material.

caption: Identification key corresponding to the specific samples shown in the experimental series.
summary: This table provides the identification key for the samples used in the study. It correlates the visual data from the post-cycling photographs with specific sample designations, allowing for systematic tracking and analysis of the 3D-printed porous black zirconia specimens throughout the thermochemical testing process.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted creep strain from the DNN model against actual experimental test data on the validation set.
summary: This parity plot visualizes the agreement between the creep strain values predicted by the DNN model and the actual experimental test results. By plotting predicted versus actual values, the panel demonstrates the high predictive accuracy and reliability of the trained DNN model when applied to the test data set.

caption: Synchrotron XRD patterns comparing AF Gyroid, HTHed Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond lattices, revealing the presence of alpha-Fe, LaFeSi-type, and NaZn13-type phases in the AF Gyroid specimen.
summary: Synchrotron XRD patterns for various lattice architectures, including AF Gyroid, HTHed Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond, are presented. The data confirms that the AF Gyroid specimen is composed of a complex mixture of alpha-Fe, LaFeSi-type, and NaZn13-type phases, distinguishing its phase composition from other tested lattice geometries.

caption: Average friction coefficient values for AM-TS, Ref-TS, and AM-MR materials across different test temperatures.
summary: This plot displays the average friction coefficient for AM-TS, Ref-TS, and AM-MR materials under varying temperature conditions. It highlights that AM-TS and Ref-TS exhibit similar friction behavior, whereas AM-MR demonstrates higher fluctuations and less stability, particularly during the initial running-in phase at 40 °C, as indicated by standard deviation data.

caption: BF-STEM micrograph of proton-irradiated Alloy 690, illustrating the nanoindent orientation and the lobes of extreme strain observed under the indentation.
summary: Proton-irradiated Alloy 690 is analyzed using BF-STEM to reveal the deformation microstructure resulting from nanoindentation. The panel marks the nanoindent orientation with a white triangle and highlights the lobes of extreme strain with red dashed lines, showing that larger lobes of extreme strain are present directly under the nanoindents.

caption: Absorption-desorption profile illustrating the estimated hydrogen concentration in the sample over a four-hour charging and one-hour discharging cycle.
summary: The plot displays the estimated hydrogen concentration profile within the sample throughout a specific electrochemical cycle. It tracks the absorption phase over four hours followed by a one-hour desorption period, providing essential context for the hydrogen-induced changes observed in the dislocation patterns and hardness measurements presented in the figure.

caption: Inverse pole figure map and corresponding pole figures for AM3D7+BN alloy, evaluated in a plane parallel to the building direction, displaying equiaxed grain morphology.
summary: The inverse pole figure map of AM3D7+BN demonstrates a transition to fine equiaxed grains, promoted by the addition of BN. This structural change is attributed to the CET transition, which is further supported by the presence of Cu- and Si-rich zones at the grain boundaries and increased undercooling.

caption: Transverse cross-section of the melt pool front showing heat transfer pathways in unmodified metal powders.
summary: This schematic illustrates the heat transfer phenomena occurring at the melt pool front for unmodified metal powders. It highlights how powder-to-powder conduction dictates thermal behavior during the melting process, providing a baseline representation of the thermal environment encountered by standard metallic particles before any surface modification is applied.

caption: Tessellated 5 × 3 × 5 Dspc lattice structure showing the uniform sheet-based minimal surface arrangement, with the right-hand plot illustrating the through-thickness parameter variation and the corresponding mathematical curve-fit at 20% relative density.
summary: This panel displays a 5 × 3 × 5 tessellated Dspc lattice structure, representing a uniform hybrid sheet-based minimal surface-lattice core. The accompanying plot details the through-thickness parameter variation, providing a mathematical expression derived from curve-fitting at a 20% relative density, which characterizes the structural geometry of the Dspc lattice.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental flow stresses of CHT_MS250 against predictions derived from the original Johnson-Cook model, showing a correlation coefficient of 0.9293.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the correlation between experimental and predicted flow stresses for CHT_MS250 using the original Johnson-Cook model. The data points demonstrate a correlation coefficient of 0.9293, indicating the predictive accuracy of the standard model when compared against experimental mechanical test results for this specific material.

caption: Rheological temperature sweep of Ca-EMP-K 67 mM gel showing storage modulus (G') and loss modulus (G") from 25 °C to 80 °C.
summary: Rheological analysis of the Ca-EMP-K 67 mM gel reveals its gel-to-sol transition behavior across a temperature range of 25 °C to 80 °C. The data shows that G' consistently exceeds G", confirming that the gel does not exhibit melting behavior and the cross-linked network remains intact during heating.

caption: Demagnetization curves of an as-built Nd-Fe-B magnet fabricated via a bidirectional strategy, measured across a temperature range of 20–120 °C.
summary: This figure displays the demagnetization behavior of an as-built Nd-Fe-B magnet produced using a bidirectional strategy. The curves, plotted across a temperature range of 20–120 °C, demonstrate the thermal stability of the material. Analysis of these results confirms a coercivity temperature coefficient of -0.35 %/°C for the magnet.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of Au-NSps, M-NPs, and MP-NPs, highlighting the emergence and growth of the plasmonic peak.
summary: The UV-Vis spectra demonstrate the optical response of the nanoparticles during gold decoration. A distinct plasmonic peak appears at 534 nm for MP1-NPs, with subsequent growth steps leading to increased absorption intensity in the 534–539 nm range, confirming the successful plasmonic tuning of the magnetic-gold hybrid nanostructures.

caption: On-cooling dilatometry curves demonstrating the martensitic transformation behavior across varying cooling rates.
summary: Dilatometry experiments were performed at different cooling rates to investigate the thermal stabilization of austenite. Panel (a) displays the resulting on-cooling dilatometry readings, which illustrate the progression of the martensitic transformation. These curves provide essential data for identifying how cooling rates influence the transformation kinetics and the associated temperature shifts.

caption: Grain boundary (GB) map of the micro region A, distinguishing between high-angle and low-angle grain boundaries across the dual-phase interface.
summary: The GB map provides a detailed view of the high-angle and low-angle grain boundaries within micro region A. Analysis of these boundaries reveals significant differences in microstructural orientations on either side of the BCC/FCC dual-phase interface, which is essential for understanding the bonding conditions of the heterogeneous bi-metallic structure.

caption: Final deposition stage at t = 11 s, marking the moment the bead is cut from the nozzle and the rapid deformation phase concludes.
summary: Captured at 11 seconds, this panel shows the bead at the moment it is cut from the nozzle. This event marks the cessation of the rapid vertical contraction observed in the earlier stages. At this point, the material temperature remains significantly above the glass transition temperature.

caption: Fracture micromorphology of 80%CuSn15 + 20%Co specimen sintered at 810 °C, featuring uniform grain refinement and high density of tough nests.
summary: This SEM image of the 80%CuSn15 + 20%Co fracture surface shows significantly smaller and more uniform grain sizes alongside an abundance of tough nests. The comparison of fracture sections confirms that increasing the cobalt content leads to a more refined microstructure and improved toughness in the sintered specimens.

caption: Stacked XRD profiles for the Al-5Ce alloy integrated over an azimuth range of -5° to 5°.
summary: Stacked XRD profiles for the Al-5Ce alloy are shown in a top-down view, integrated across an azimuth angle range of -5° to 5°. This visualization allows for the observation of diffraction peak evolution during the in-situ experiment, providing insight into the structural changes occurring within the alloy under load.

caption: Fracture toughness values for BJ-printed ZTA ceramics processed with a 2 h sintering holding time.
summary: This panel presents the fracture toughness of BJ-printed ZTA ceramics sintered for 2 h. The data reveals a dependence on sintering parameters similar to that observed in flexural strength measurements, highlighting how the chosen thermal holding time and temperature conditions dictate the final mechanical toughness of the printed ceramic material.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns collected during the tensile deformation of Ti-18Nb alloy at a cryogenic temperature of -50°C.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns are presented for Ti-18Nb alloy subjected to tensile testing at -50°C. These data illustrate the structural evolution of the material under mechanical load at cryogenic conditions, displaying behavior consistent with previously reported experimental results for similar alloy systems under comparable testing parameters.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the TiAlN-H coating, highlighting the deposited layer structure alongside its corresponding SAED pattern.
summary: This bright-field TEM image of the TiAlN-H coating, combined with its SAED pattern, reveals the structural features of the deposited layer. Unlike the lower-content variants, this sample shows diffraction signals for both cubic and hexagonal AlN, indicating a more complex phase composition within the nitride coating structure.

caption: Texture plot derived from the LPBF A709 sample built in the parallel direction.
summary: This texture plot represents the crystallographic orientation distribution of the LPBF A709 sample processed in the parallel build direction. The data highlights the preferred grain orientations developed during the additive manufacturing process, serving as a quantitative measure of the material's texture and its potential impact on mechanical properties.

caption: Side view of the reconstructed volume obtained from FIB tomographic analysis of a 20 at% Ag PVD sample.
summary: This panel displays a side view of the reconstructed volume from a FIB tomographic analysis performed on a 20 at% Ag PVD sample. The reconstruction provides a detailed 3D visualization of the internal structure, allowing for the examination of the spatial distribution of Ag within the PVD-deposited material.

caption: Conceptual illustration depicting the vacuum induction brazing process for diamond joining.
summary: This schematic illustrates the vacuum induction brazing process used to join diamond materials. The procedure involves placing the brazing specimen into a vacuum induction furnace, maintaining specific vacuum and holding time conditions, and performing the brazing at a temperature of 1000 °C to achieve the final brazed diamond connection.

caption: Vickers microhardness profile across the CRA-LWDED interface, showing a distinct hardness spike near the substrate.
summary: Vickers microhardness measurements across the CRA-LWDED interface reveal a localized spike in hardness. This behavior is attributed to an increased cooling rate, as the CRA substrate functions as an effective heatsink, conducting heat away from the LWDED melt pool and resulting in a narrower columnar grain width.

caption: Surface EDS elemental distribution map of the UnEPT specimen interface.
summary: This surface EDS scanning profile illustrates the elemental distribution at the interface of the UnEPT specimen. The analysis reveals specific characteristics of elemental diffusion under the UnEPT condition, serving as a baseline for comparing the interfacial diffusion behavior observed in specimens subjected to different EPT parameters.

caption: Triangular bilinear cohesive traction–separation law representing Mode I interface loading.
summary: This schematic illustrates a Mode I triangular bilinear cohesive zone model (CZM) used to define the traction–separation behavior of an interface. The plot characterizes the relationship between normal stress and separation distance, providing a fundamental mathematical framework for modeling fracture and debonding processes in materials under normal loading conditions.

caption: Exemplary 4D simplices of distinct geometries represented as 3D objects, accompanied by their corresponding adjacency matrices used to determine phase co-existence.
summary: Detailed 3D representations of 4D simplices demonstrate the phase calculation process. The algorithm utilizes a universal criterion with a threshold of 0.1 to generate adjacency matrices based on Euclidean distances between vertices. These adjacent simplices, defined by five equidistant vertices, effectively delineate the single-phase domains within the composition space.

caption: Surface topography of a premolar tooth milled at 330 m using emulsion coolant.
summary: Confocal microscopy displays the surface topography of a premolar tooth after milling at 330 m with emulsion coolant. This image provides data for assessing surface finish quality, which is further supported by arithmetical mean height measurements to determine the stability and control of the surface texture during milling.

caption: Precipitate size distribution histogram for the Cu-Ni-Co-Si-Fe-Mg alloy after pre-aging at 500 °C for 4 h.
summary: Representing the precipitate size distribution after 4 hours of pre-aging at 500 °C, this histogram is based on TEM image statistics. It serves as a critical data point for monitoring the growth and coarsening behavior of precipitates within the alloy matrix during the initial stages of heat treatment.

caption: Li2S deposition profiles comparing the Ni-Cu@C cell and the Ni-Cu@C/HC cell.
summary: Li2S deposition curves for the Ni-Cu@C and Ni-Cu@C/HC cells are displayed. These curves illustrate the deposition behavior during the discharge process, highlighting the impact of the HC component on the electrochemical deposition kinetics and the overall performance of the cell during the formation of Li2S.

caption: Immunocytochemical analysis of HT-144 spheroids stained for β-tubulin (red) and DAPI (blue), with EdU assay (green) highlighting cell proliferation under increasing cisplatin concentrations.
summary: Confocal microscopy images reveal the spatial distribution of β-tubulin and nuclei within the HT-144 spheroids. The EdU assay specifically visualizes proliferating cells, allowing for the assessment of cisplatin's impact on cell division within the 3D structure as the drug concentration increases, providing insight into the mechanism of growth inhibition.

caption: N 1s core-level spectrum of SCF/Co@C, characterized by two primary peaks at 400.68 eV and 400.98 eV, attributed to Co-N and C-N bonding configurations.
summary: The N 1s XPS spectrum of the SCF/Co@C composite exhibits two characteristic peaks at 400.68 eV and 400.98 eV. These signals are assigned to Co-N and C-N bonding interactions, indicating the successful integration of nitrogen within the carbon matrix and its coordination with cobalt species.

caption: Average grain size distribution observed under a laser power treatment of 12.5 J/mm2.
summary: This panel displays the average grain size resulting from a 12.5 J/mm2 laser power treatment. Due to the extremely high heating rate of the laser, the melting and rapid cooling processes restrict grain growth time, leading to a finer grain structure compared to slower thermal processing methods.

caption: Cycling stability curves comparing the capacity retention of La3MgNi14, La2.5Y0.5MgNi14, and La2YMgNi14 alloy electrodes over 500 cycles.
summary: Cycling stability curves for La3MgNi14, La2.5Y0.5MgNi14, and La2YMgNi14 alloy electrodes demonstrate varying performance. Capacity retention rates after 500 cycles are recorded at 18.32%, 37.85%, and 29.88% for the Y0, Y0.5, and Y1 alloys, respectively, highlighting the influence of yttrium substitution on the long-term electrochemical stability of these materials.

caption: Ion mobility spectrometry spectra for binary mixtures of 2-pentanone/2-octanone and 2-butanone/2-hexanone at 30 °C, illustrating the distinct peaks corresponding to monomer and dimer species.
summary: This spectrum displays the analytical performance of an IMS device during the simultaneous injection of ketone mixtures. At 30 °C, the data reveals distinct peaks for monomers and dimers. Notably, the dimer of the smaller ketone and the monomer of the larger ketone exhibit varying degrees of spectral overlap.

caption: Bode magnitude plot representing the impedance modulus as a function of frequency for AA2024/Cu joints and as-received base metals.
summary: The Bode magnitude plot depicts the impedance modulus across varying frequencies for AA2024/Cu joints and as-received base metals. Analysis of the curves reveals that the as-received copper exhibits the largest low-frequency impedance, reflecting superior corrosion resistance or different surface electrochemical properties compared to the other tested metallic specimens.

caption: Comparison of experimentally measured area percentage of resolidified regions (dots) and DICTRA-predicted liquid fraction volume percentage (solid lines) across isothermal holding times at 1345 °C, 1350 °C, and 1362 °C.
summary: This plot displays the experimental area percentage of resolidified regions alongside DICTRA-simulated liquid fraction evolution at super-solidus temperatures. Results indicate that resolidified regions decrease with longer holding times. DICTRA calculations show that the liquid phase generated at 1345 °C undergoes full resolidification after 5.6 hours of isothermal treatment.

caption: Creep deformation model validation for ME3, showing the correlation between predicted and experimental results.
summary: This panel provides additional validation for the creep deformation model by presenting results for the ME3 alloy. The plot demonstrates the model's capability to predict creep behavior in this specific superalloy, further supporting the broader investigation into the effects of stacking fault energy and microstructure on creep response.

caption: Pie chart illustrating the total weight percentage distribution of non-recyclable waste across surgical subspecialties, highlighting trauma surgery as the primary contributor at 37.71%, followed by arthroplasty at 35.28% and oncology at 27.01%.
summary: This pie chart displays the total non-recyclable waste distribution across surgical subspecialties. Trauma surgery accounts for the highest proportion of non-recyclable waste production at 37.71%, followed by arthroplasty at 35.28% and oncology at 27.01%. These findings quantify the relative contributions of different surgical fields to total non-recyclable waste generation.

caption: Schematic representation of the Laser-Direct Energy Deposition (LMD) test-bed framework.
summary: This panel illustrates the experimental LMD setup through a schematic presentation. It provides a comprehensive overview of the test-bed framework, detailing the arrangement of components necessary for the laser-based additive manufacturing process, which serves as the foundational configuration for the subsequent thermal monitoring and measurement experiments described in the study.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph illustrating the interior microstructure of the as-built melt pool.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a detailed view of the interior microstructure within the as-built melt pool. The high-angle annular dark-field imaging technique highlights the contrast between different phases present in the sample, serving as the foundational observation for subsequent high-resolution characterization of the material's internal structure.

caption: Optimized unit cell geometry corresponding to the third design result with the lowest L2 relative error.
summary: This panel shows the third optimized unit cell geometry, which achieved one of the lowest L2 relative errors among the 500 generated solutions. The structure serves as a physical realization of the target mechanical properties defined by the Ramberg-Osgood equation, highlighting the effectiveness of the inverse diffusion design approach.

caption: Comparison between experimental minimum creep rates and those predicted by the P-parameter method for temperatures ranging from 800 to 900 °C.
summary: The P-parameter method is utilized to construct a predictive model for the minimum creep rate of the LPBF IN738LC superalloy.
