This panel compares these calculated values against actual test data, demonstrating the accuracy of the P-parameter approach in predicting creep behavior within the 800 °C to 900 °C temperature range.

caption: Pole figure of the GSLS sample surface oriented parallel to the building direction.
summary: This panel shows the pole figure for the GSLS surface parallel to the building direction. Supported by the reference, this plot characterizes the texture of the GSLS sample relative to its manufacturing orientation, offering essential data on the crystallographic alignment resulting from the building process.

caption: Electronic density of states for Fe2VAl showing a semimetallic character with a distinct pseudogap at the Fermi level and a band structure inset.
summary: Fe2VAl exhibits a semimetallic electronic density of states characterized by a profound pseudogap at the Fermi level. The inset provides a sketch of the electronic band structure, illustrating a slight overlap between the valence and conduction bands at specific points in the Brillouin zone, as extracted from The Materials project.

caption: Atomic configuration model illustrating the adsorption of an oxygen atom on the Ti2AlV (110) surface at distinct T, H, and B sites.
summary: This panel displays the DFT-calculated adsorption configurations for an oxygen atom on the Ti2AlV (110) surface. The model highlights three specific adsorption sites, labeled T, H, and B, which are used to evaluate the adsorption strength and surface interaction characteristics of oxygen on this specific intermetallic substrate.

caption: Dimensionless diagram representing the scaling behavior for single-track-exposure across various alloy compositions.
summary: This dimensionless plot presents a material-independent scaling law for single-track-exposure, utilizing experimental data from previous studies. By normalizing the parameters, this approach aims to simplify the characterization of different alloys, providing a highly desirable alternative to the effortful process of determining specific coefficients for every individual material and strategy.

caption: Probability of failure (POF) over a 30-year service period for a 32-inch corroded pipeline with defect interaction parameter S l = 0.
summary: This line graph illustrates the probability of failure for a 32-inch corroded pipeline over 30 years when the defect interaction parameter S l is set to 0. The data demonstrates that performance degradation due to defect interactions necessitates reducing the maximum allowable operating pressure (MAOP) four years earlier than otherwise required.

caption: Comparative overview illustrating the distinction between traditional roughness prediction models and the proposed methodology developed in this study.
summary: This schematic provides a comparative overview of traditional roughness prediction models versus the proposed methodology introduced in this study. It serves as a foundational summary of the key contributions and primary aspects that distinguish this research from existing approaches, highlighting the unique advancements made in the predictive modeling framework.

caption: Tensile strength enhancement of cold-spray additively manufactured (CSAM) AA6061 deposits, comparing conventional processing against those utilizing in situ shot-peening based on simulation data.
summary: This panel presents a comparison of the actual tensile strengths of CSAM AA6061 deposits. By contrasting conventional manufacturing with in situ shot-peening methods, the data demonstrates the strength gains achieved, confirming the effectiveness of the shot-peening process in enhancing the overall mechanical performance of the additively manufactured material.

caption: Normalized ultimate strength distribution for a simple cubic lattice at relative density 0.3 and Weibull modulus 8, compared against normal and two-parameter Weibull statistical models.
summary: Representing the normalized ultimate strength for a simple cubic lattice with a relative density of 0.3 and a Weibull modulus of 8, this histogram evaluates the data against normal and two-parameter Weibull distributions. The best fit is identified as a normal distribution with a mean of 0.500885.

caption: Spatial temperature deviation map for PB at 4 bara, detailing the thermal gradients and measurement point deviations.
summary: Operating at 4 bara, the PB configuration's thermal profile is visualized through this heatmap of temperature deviations. It maps the absolute differences from set points and relative variations between surface and core measurement points, providing insight into the spatial temperature distribution and reactor stability under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Evaluation of microhardness trends along the ξ-path comparing model predictions against experimental data under varying laser power P.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between laser power P and the resulting microhardness along the ξ-path. By comparing predicted values from the S-H module with experimental data, the figure validates the model's effectiveness in predicting alloy hardness based on process parameters derived from the P-S grain size module.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for as-spun Al86Ce10TM4 (TM = Ti, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu) ribbons, labeled A1 through A7, recorded at a heating rate of 20 K/min.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for as-spun Al86Ce10TM4 ribbons (A1-A7) were measured at 20 K/min to evaluate thermal stability and glass-forming ability. Results indicate no distinct glass transition temperature prior to crystallization, suggesting that the glass transition temperature equals the crystallization temperature due to initial nanocrystalline precipitation or weak thermal signals.

caption: Top-down atomic snapshot of graphene after 500 recoil cascades, marking the transition into Stage II.
summary: At 500 cascades, this snapshot reveals a pronounced structural change where holes in region A nearly disappear and parts of the graphene-like structure are restored. This observation highlights the unique damage behavior in Stage II, where the decay rate of the structural survival varies compared to earlier stages.

caption: Bright-field TEM image displaying the spatial arrangement of two C14 Laves phase particles positioned on opposite sides of an η phase precipitate.
summary: This bright-field TEM image reveals the microstructural configuration of two C14 Laves phase precipitates situated on either side of an η phase particle. The spatial relationship between these phases was investigated to determine the crystallographic orientation, as the proximity of these precipitates suggests a potential strong orientation relationship between them.

caption: P 2p XPS core-level spectrum of the nanoNi-P modified electrode prepared at a deposition current density of -2,000 μA cm⁻².
summary: P 2p XPS core-level spectrum for the nanoNi-P modified electrode prepared at -2,000 μA cm⁻² is shown. This data is used to analyze the phosphorus species present on the electrode surface, contributing to the comprehensive study of how deposition current density affects the properties of the nanoNi-P modified electrodes.

caption: TEM EDS analysis of the carbides observed within the IL zone, confirming their enrichment with Hf and Ta.
summary: TEM EDS analysis performed on the IL zone confirms the chemical composition of the fine particles observed at the prior particle boundaries and in the matrix. The results demonstrate that these particles are carbides significantly enriched with Hf and Ta, which formed during the cooling stage of the HIP bonding process.

caption: Morse potential energy curves for pure and mixed alloy components, highlighting the first three coordination sphere distances.
summary: This plot displays Morse type pair potentials used to model alloy components. The curves illustrate the short-range interaction energy as a function of distance, with arrows marking the specific positions of the first three coordination spheres. These potentials are essential for calculating nodal lattice energies in random alloy models.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of MDCK–YFP-keratin-8 cells cultured on an ABIKO iron coiled wire after 3 days, showing cell localization primarily on the wire segments in contact with the plate bottom.
summary: After 3 days of culture, MDCK–YFP-keratin-8 cells were observed using fluorescence microscopy on an ABIKO iron coiled wire. The imaging reveals that the cells were mainly localized on the wire sections touching the bottom of the culture plate, indicating initial attachment and growth patterns on the metallic substrate.

caption: Evolution of flank wear area plotted as a function of iteration count for both nanobubble-based and normal cutting fluids at a surface speed of 45 m/min.
summary: At a surface speed of 45 m/min, this graph quantifies the flank wear area development over the number of iterations until tool failure. The data allows for a direct comparison between the effectiveness of nanobubble-based cutting fluid and normal cutting fluid in mitigating tool wear under these specific machining conditions.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of solutionized NiTi after 50 shape memory cycles, revealing the presence of detwinned martensite.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays solutionized NiTi alloy following 50 shape memory cycles. The microstructure reveals the persistence of detwinned martensite even after heating to 423 K, which exceeds the austenite finish temperature of approximately 386 K, indicating that the transformation to austenite is effectively suppressed in this sample.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing PCL, PP20W, and PP20CS50W samples, highlighting distinct peak variations and the presence of specific functional groups in the composite materials.
summary: The FTIR spectra of PCL, PP20W, and PP20CS50W are presented, showing visually similar profiles with sharp, characteristic peaks. While the spectra are generally comparable to existing literature, a specific observable peak is identified in the PP20CS50W composite that is absent in the pure PCL sample, indicating distinct chemical differences.

caption: EDS spot analysis performed at point A on the S3 sample cross-section.
summary: Point A analysis via EDS provides compositional data for the S3 sample. This measurement is part of a broader investigation into the Re content, which shows a significant reduction to 38.1% in the S3 sample following the 1020 °C treatment compared to the initial S2 sample composition.

caption: Isotropic spinodoid cellular structure and its corresponding normalized elastic uniaxial modulus polar plot, demonstrating uniform stiffness distribution.
summary: The isotropic spinodoid cellular structure is shown alongside its normalized elastic uniaxial modulus polar plot. This visualization confirms a uniform stiffness distribution across spatial directions, resulting from the specific wave vector parameters applied during the generation of the lattice at a characteristic length scale of 5 mm.

caption: Quantitative chemical composition data derived from EDS point analysis for the top and sub-surface layers of shot-peened states.
summary: This table presents quantitative results of EDS analyses, showing the fractions of Al and Si phases in the top and sub-surface layers of shot-peened states. These data provide a numerical comparison of the chemical composition changes induced by the surface treatment processes.

caption: Experimental mean refractive indices of the composite samples measured from 0.5 to 2 THz, where error bars indicate the standard deviation calculated from five distinct scan locations per sample.
summary: Experimental refractive index data for the composite samples are presented here for the 0.5 to 2 THz range. The plot features mean values derived from five separate scans per sample, with error bars representing the standard deviation to quantify measurement variability and demonstrate the consistency of the experimental results.

caption: Visualization of the 2nd order Peano-Gosper fractal curve implemented as a scan strategy, maintaining the specified 100 μm characteristic scan vector length.
summary: The 2nd order Peano-Gosper curve is depicted as an alternative fractal scan strategy. Consistent with the overall design parameters, the path utilizes a 100 μm characteristic vector length. This approach adheres to the strict requirement that no single scan vector length is permitted to exceed the 300 μm threshold.

caption: Storage modulus (E') plotted against frequency for various materials at 25 °C, highlighting the material-specific reduction in modulus.
summary: The storage modulus (E') was evaluated during a frequency scan at 25 °C. Pure PLA exhibits a significant 32% loss in E' at 1 Hz, whereas i-PLA-g-MAOC demonstrates a more stable elastic response with a lower reduction of 9.5%, indicating improved mechanical performance under isothermal conditions.

caption: Compression strength of Al0.5CrFeNiV0.5 high-entropy alloy plotted against varying compression test temperatures.
summary: Compression strength of the Al0.5CrFeNiV0.5 high-entropy alloy is shown as a function of temperature. The data indicates that increasing the test temperature leads to a reduction in mechanical strength, which decreases the material's load-carrying capacity and increases its susceptibility to plastic deformation during sliding contact loading conditions.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of the MAX-2_3 sample, showing a virtual absence of the signal around 600 ppm.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of the MAX-2_3 sample displays a virtual absence of the signal near 600 ppm. This feature indicates partial decomposition of the Ti3C2 layers, a finding supported by the low signal-to-noise ratio and consistent with data obtained from 47,49 Ti NMR analysis of the same material.

caption: Temperature-programmed desorption (TPD) spectra of H2 molecules from Au-Ni bimetallic surface alloys, plotted as desorption rate versus temperature for varying Au coverages on Au-15 ML Ni/Mo(110) surfaces.
summary: This figure displays H2 TPD spectra obtained from Au-Ni bimetallic surface alloys with varying Au coverages on a Ni/Mo(110) substrate. The detected peaks correspond to the desorption of recombined atomic hydrogen from the surface. The data illustrates how the surface composition, specifically the Au coverage, influences the hydrogen desorption behavior.

caption: Raman spectra highlighting the TiO2 phases present in Ti834 and Ti6242S alloys after 500 hours of oxidation at 650 °C.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of Ti834 and Ti6242S alloys oxidized at 650 °C for 500 hours reveals the presence of specific TiO2 phases. The spectra confirm the transformation of metastable anatase to stable rutile, a process expected as temperatures exceed 600 °C, with anatase content decreasing over the extended oxidation duration.

caption: EDS overview map displaying the distribution of main alloying elements Fe, Cr, and Ni across the fracture surface.
summary: The EDS overview map illustrates the spatial distribution of primary alloying elements, specifically Fe, Cr, and Ni, across the fracture surface. The composition is biased towards preferential fracture in the IN718 component, demonstrating how the elemental distribution correlates with the observed failure modes and the structural integrity of the multi-material interface.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the top portion of the 1400W-DCT4 build at 0% strain, including a [011] zone axis SAED pattern inset.
summary: Top portion of the 1400W-DCT4 build is examined using bright-field TEM at 0% strain. The accompanying [011] zone axis SAED pattern characterizes the initial crystal structure. This image serves as the starting point for evaluating defect structure evolution in the top section of the tensile specimen during deformation.

caption: Transmittance spectra of S-CNC/CTFA composite resins across a range of concentrations, showing the impact of S-CNC loading on optical transparency.
summary: The transmittance spectra of the S-CNC/CTFA composite resins are presented to evaluate the effect of varying S-CNC concentrations. These results confirm a significant reduction in the transparency of the S-CNC/CTFA composite resin, highlighting the optical limitations associated with these specific particles when dispersed within the CTFA resin matrix.

caption: Compass graphs illustrating the spatial distribution of neurite growth, where radial length corresponds to neurite extension and angular position represents the orientation relative to the x-axis.
summary: Compass graphs visualize the directional distribution of neurite growth for each fiber diameter group. The radial length of the red lines indicates the extent of neurite elongation, while the angular orientation relative to the x-axis provides a clear representation of how fiber diameter influences the directional growth patterns of PC12 cells.

caption: Yield strength versus density comparison for the Al80Mg10Si5Cu5 alloy at room temperature (TA) relative to other aluminium alloys processed via HPDC and alternative methods.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the yield strength to density relationship for the Al80Mg10Si5Cu5 alloy at room temperature. It serves as a comparative benchmark, positioning the alloy's mechanical performance against various other aluminium alloys produced through high-pressure die casting and other manufacturing processes to evaluate its relative strength-to-weight efficiency.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the YZ section for heat-treated sample Q, illustrating grain orientation distribution.
summary: Sample Q is analyzed via EBSD to visualize grain orientation in the YZ section following heat treatment. The IPF-X map provides a detailed spatial distribution of crystallographic orientations, serving as a baseline for comparing the microstructural evolution of the heat-treated samples as described in the experimental results.

caption: Van't Hoff plot showing the relationship between the natural logarithm of equilibrium pressure and inverse temperature for the TiFe0.8Mn0.2 alloy.
summary: The Van't Hoff plot for the TiFe0.8Mn0.2 alloy illustrates the thermodynamic behavior derived from temperature-dependent PCT curves. This analysis allows for the determination of essential thermodynamic constants, providing insight into the hydrogen storage characteristics of the material based on the linear relationship between pressure and temperature.

caption: PDOS plot of the Ag atom from the Ag-Pt (1 0 0) alloy surface following CO adsorption, showing the electronic state modification.
summary: Following CO adsorption on the Ag-Pt (1 0 0) alloy surface, this panel shows the PDOS for the Ag atom. By comparing this to the clean surface, the plot helps visualize the hybridization of adsorbate frontier orbitals with the metal surface states, which is critical for determining the binding strength.

caption: Pole figure of the α phase in the HIP state, showing preferred orientation.
summary: The pole figure for the α phase confirms a strong preferred orientation relative to the Z-build direction. A maximum MUD is identified at a 10.5° tilted angle with respect to the Z-direction, providing quantitative evidence of the crystallographic texture developed during the HIP process at 920℃ and 100 MPa.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map illustrating the crack propagation path relative to the microstructure, highlighting preferential crack advancement along fine-grained regions (FGRs).
summary: The EBSD-based inverse pole figure map reveals the crack propagation path through the microstructure. It demonstrates that cracks preferentially propagate along fine-grained regions (FGRs). Occasionally, the crack exhibits trans-granular propagation through dendritic cells, evidenced by consistent IPF orientations on both sides of the crack front, indicating a complex interaction with the grain structure.

caption: Multidimensional performance evaluation of BBLS lattice structures represented via a radar chart.
summary: The radar chart provides a comprehensive overview of the BBLS lattice structure's performance across multiple metrics. This visualization allows for an integrated assessment of the material's capabilities, facilitating a direct comparison of its overall performance characteristics as established in the study's evaluation framework.

caption: Pole figure representation of crystallographic texture for SEBM 316L stainless steel processed under Sample S1 conditions.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the crystallographic texture evolution for SEBM 316L stainless steel subjected to Sample S1 processing parameters. The visualization provides a detailed representation of the material's orientation distribution, serving as a primary diagnostic tool for assessing the microstructural characteristics resulting from the specific manufacturing conditions applied to this sample.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectra comparing the chemical compositions of SA, OSA, OG, and MOG hydrogel samples.
summary: FTIR spectra are presented to characterize the chemical composition and structural changes across SA, OSA, OG, and MOG hydrogel samples. These spectra provide evidence of the chemical modifications and crosslinking processes involved in the formation of the OG polymer network within the nanocomposite hydrogel system.

caption: Pole figure map illustrating the crystallographic texture of the top layer in the CW-LMD fabricated SMSS deposit.
summary: This pole figure map displays the crystallographic texture of the top layer of the CW-LMD fabricated SMSS deposit. According to the reference, the texture strength in these deposits exhibits a decreasing trend along the thickness from the top layer down to the bottom layer of the material.

caption: Differential pulse voltammograms of 100 µM uric acid in 0.1 M Britton-Robinson buffer (pH 5.0) obtained using a sterilised commercial PLA additive manufactured electrode under identical conditions to the rPETg sensor.
summary: This panel presents differential pulse voltammograms for the detection of 100 µM uric acid in a pH 5.0 Britton-Robinson buffer using a sterilised commercial PLA additive manufactured electrode. These results serve as a comparative baseline for the rPETg electrode performance, confirming the sensor's capability to detect uric acid in the specified buffer solution.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the NiO–CoO system, showing the temperature-dependent phase stability and the specific positions of Ni-Co-GDC compositions at 800 °C.
summary: The NiO–CoO binary phase diagram illustrates the formation of a solid solution at elevated temperatures. Triangular markers denote the compositions of Ni-GDC and Ni-Co-GDC samples at 800 °C. The diagram predicts that all five compositions will form a single-phase NiO-type solid solution when exposed to an oxidizing atmosphere.

caption: Nyquist diagrams of Alloy 31 under identical electrochemical conditions, highlighting an unfinished capacitive arc at 20 °C and the emergence of a low-frequency inductive loop as the solution temperature increases.
summary: Nyquist diagrams for Alloy 31 demonstrate that two distinct electrochemical equivalent circuits are required to model the data across different temperatures. The 20 °C plot displays an unfinished capacitive arc, while higher temperatures reveal a low-frequency inductive loop, confirming the system's compliance with linear system theory through experimental and calculated agreement.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the MIX specimen displaying its specific crystallographic texture.
summary: Displaying the crystallographic texture of the MIX specimen, this inverse pole figure map highlights the grain orientation characteristics. It is a key component of the comparative analysis of STA specimens, allowing for the assessment of how the MIX processing condition influences the resulting microstructure compared to other experimental variants.

caption: Cross-sectional YZ-plane at x = 200 μm showing the grain structure for a time step parameter of ξ = 0.04.
summary: Displaying the YZ-plane cross-section at x = 200 μm, this panel illustrates the grain morphology resulting from a simulation with ξ = 0.04. The microstructure is similar to the ξ = 2.0 case, though minor differences are observable in the center of the domain.

caption: Equilibrium solution at intersection point f, plotting temperature against latitude with the critical isotherm −Ts (magenta) and Hadley cell edges r1 and r2 (gray). Open ocean (blue) and snow/ice-covered (white) latitudes are highlighted.
summary: Equilibrium solution f illustrates the temperature profile at intersection point f. The magenta line indicates the critical isotherm −Ts, while gray lines denote Hadley cell edges. The plot distinguishes between open ocean (blue) and snow/ice-covered (white) regions, reflecting the climate model's state at this specific intersection point.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of Region 1 at room temperature, highlighting high-angle grain boundaries in black and low-angle grain boundaries in red.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map of Region 1 at room temperature displays grain boundary distribution. Black lines represent high-angle grain boundaries, while red lines indicate low-angle grain boundaries. Elliptical regions at the top reveal a higher density of low-angle grain boundaries compared to specimens tested at 200 °C.

caption: Load-slip behavior of the shear reinforcement measured on the side where the critical shear crack developed in the T-beams.
summary: Load-slip behavior of the shear reinforcement is depicted for each T-beam, specifically focusing on the side where the critical shear crack developed. This measurement captures the interaction between the reinforcement and the concrete matrix, providing insight into the shear transfer mechanism and the onset of localized structural failure.

caption: PM-IRRAS spectra of the C–H stretching region (3050–2800 cm⁻¹) for ODPA adsorption on PDMS-grafted AlSi10Mg surfaces over time, highlighting the PDMS-specific asymmetric CH3 stretching peak at 2966 cm⁻¹.
summary: This panel displays PM-IRRAS spectra focusing on the C–H stretching region between 3050 cm⁻¹ and 2800 cm⁻¹. The presence of PDMS grafting is confirmed by the characteristic asymmetric CH3 stretching peak observed at 2966 cm⁻¹, providing evidence of the surface modification prior to ODPA adsorption measurements.

caption: Technical drawing illustrating the geometry and configuration of the electron detector plate utilized for data acquisition in this experimental study.
summary: This technical drawing provides a detailed representation of the electron detector plate used throughout the experimental study. It serves as a primary reference for the hardware configuration, ensuring clarity regarding the physical geometry and design of the detector component employed to capture electron signals during the research process.

caption: Linear combination fitting of the Ni L-edge XAS data used to estimate the valence change of nickel in the prepared catalysts.
summary: Linear combination fitting is applied to the Ni L-edge XAS data to better estimate the valence change of nickel in the prepared catalysts. This analytical approach allows for a more precise determination of the nickel oxidation states, facilitating a deeper understanding of the electronic properties of the catalyst system.

caption: Pole figure of SLM-316L stainless steel fabricated with a 45° build direction, displaying a lack of annular contouring.
summary: Representing the texture of SLM-316L stainless steel fabricated at a 45° build direction, this pole figure lacks annular contouring. This specific crystallographic feature confirms that a plate-type texture is dominant in the sample, which is a critical factor for understanding the passive film heterogeneity of the SLM-fabricated material.

caption: Isothermal section at the ternary transition peritectoid reaction temperature (Ni3Mo + oP6 → γ + P), noting that the oP6 + P + Ni3Mo region was not experimentally identified.
summary: Depicting the isothermal section at the transition peritectoid reaction temperature, this diagram shows the interaction between Ni3Mo and oP6 phases to form γ and P. Notably, the study indicates that the oP6 + P + Ni3Mo three-phase region was not experimentally identified during the investigation of this specific reaction pathway.

caption: Photograph of the light-tight enclosure designed to house the experimental assembly during measurement.
summary: This photograph shows the light-tight enclosure used to house the experimental assembly during measurement. As noted in the reference, the entire assembly is placed inside this enclosure to ensure controlled conditions, effectively isolating the components from external light interference during the data collection process.

caption: Performance comparison of the optimized die-cast aluminum alloy against various commercial aluminum alloys reported in literature.
summary: This comparative plot benchmarks the optimized die-cast aluminum alloy against established commercial aluminum alloys from literature. The data highlights a significant improvement in the comprehensive performance of the optimized alloy, confirming its superior mechanical and thermal properties relative to existing industrial standards for die-cast aluminum materials.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for Ru-Ni, showing the downshift of Ni-3d and Ru-4d states relative to bulk references due to orbital repulsion.
summary: The PDOS comparison shows that Ni-3d states downshift compared to bulk FCC Ni due to repulsion with overlapping Ru-4d orbitals, weakening Ni-O and Ni-H bonds. Similarly, Ru-4d states, particularly the 4d-eg component above the Fermi level, exhibit a downshift, indicating significant electronic modification in the alloy.

caption: DRIFT spectra of unsupported np-Cu in the O-H stretching regime after ethanol exposure at various temperatures, showing the absence of the 3744 cm-1 silanol band.
summary: This panel displays DRIFT spectra of unsupported np-Cu in the O-H stretching regime following ethanol exposure at varying temperatures. The data confirms the absence of the 3744 cm-1 band, which is expected as silanol groups are not present on the unsupported np-Cu material surface.

caption: Magnified view of the (110) diffraction peak for additively manufactured and conventional stainless steel samples.
summary: Magnified views of the (110) diffraction peaks for both additively manufactured and conventional stainless steel are presented. These detailed profiles allow for a precise comparison of peak broadening, which does not follow a monotonic relationship with the diffraction vector due to the material's inherent anisotropy.

caption: Comparison of residual-stress anisotropy (Δd311 = dLD − dTD) across different heat treatment conditions, showing that the as-built (AB) state exhibits maximum anisotropy, stress relief (SR) significantly reduces it, and full heat treatment (HT) maintains positive values.
summary: The plot displays the residual-stress anisotropy, Δd311, for various heat treatment conditions. The as-built (AB) condition shows the highest anisotropy, while stress relief (SR) is the most effective at reducing these values. Full heat treatment (HT) results in a moderate reduction, retaining positive anisotropy values compared to the stress-relieved state.

caption: HRTEM image and corresponding SAED pattern of region III in Fig. 10d, identifying the precipitate phase as δ-Ni2Si.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns were obtained from region III to characterize the precipitate phase. The diffraction data, in conjunction with EDX results, provides definitive identification of the precipitates as the δ-Ni2Si phase, which forms during the aging treatment of the alloy.

caption: Cross-sectional slice of the crack profile corresponding to the line profile location b in the 3D rendering.
summary: Representing a specific cross-sectional slice of the crack profile, this panel corresponds to the line profile location b identified in the 3D rendering. It provides a detailed view of the crack geometry within the interrupted T sample after the specified 96-hour fatigue test at 650 °C.

caption: Statistical analysis summarizing the short-circuit current results obtained from the five experimental SMFC groups.
summary: This panel presents a statistical analysis of the short-circuit current measurements collected across all five experimental groups. By aggregating the data from the seven-day testing period, this plot facilitates a comparative evaluation of the performance variations resulting from the different electrode spatial arrangements employed in the study.

caption: Schematic representation of rastered structures produced by varying hatch spacing and laser power, categorized into three distinct zones (I-III) based on processing parameters.
summary: This panel illustrates the structural evolution of rastered wicks as a function of laser processing parameters. By systematically adjusting hatch spacing and power, three distinct zones are identified. These variations in processing conditions directly influence the resulting morphology and pore structure of the material, providing a basis for subsequent performance analysis.

caption: DFT-calculated electronic band structure of the FeCoNiCuGe high-entropy alloy (sample S0) plotted near the Fermi level.
summary: This panel displays the DFT-calculated band structure for the FeCoNiCuGe alloy, identified as sample S0. The plot reveals band segments with both positive and negative curvature near the Fermi level, demonstrating that both electrons and holes contribute significantly to the charge conduction properties of this specific material system.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for 90/10 Cu–Ni alloy in 3.5% NaCl solution at 30 °C under varying hydrostatic pressures.
summary: This panel displays potentiodynamic polarization curves for 90/10 Cu–Ni in 3.5% NaCl at 30 °C. The data illustrates how hydrostatic pressure influences electrochemical kinetics, specifically accelerating the anodic dissolution rate. These curves provide the basis for determining corrosion potential and current density values, highlighting the temperature-dependent nature of the corrosion process.

caption: X-ray diffraction analysis of 7 mm diameter rods with varying sulfur concentrations, illustrating the transition to crystalline phases as the critical casting thickness is exceeded.
summary: XRD analysis of 7 mm rod specimens reveals the crystalline nature of the samples, indicating that this diameter surpasses the critical casting thickness for the alloy. These results demonstrate the structural transition from amorphous to crystalline phases as the specimen size exceeds the glass-forming limit of the material.

caption: Magnetic force microscopy image of a 5 μm Py square prepared at low sputter pressure, displaying a reproducible Landau domain pattern in the remanent state.
summary: This MFM image shows the remanent magnetic domain configuration of a 5 μm Py square fabricated at low Ar sputter pressure. The visualization reveals the formation of a reproducible Landau domain pattern, which serves as the baseline state for comparing domain structures across different sputter pressure conditions.

caption: Texture density evolution of H_E-5 specimen during in-situ neutron diffraction loading, showing the relationship between peak intensity and strain.
summary: Texture density evolution for the H_E-5 specimen is tracked via in-situ neutron diffraction. By monitoring the peak height evolution relative to the stress-free state, the pole density of specific crystallographic planes is determined as a function of strain, providing insight into the material's deformation behavior under load.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectrum acquired from the specific spot marked in the SEM image.
summary: Energy dispersive X-ray spectrum acquired from the specific spot marked in the SEM image. This spectroscopic data confirms the chemical composition of the analyzed region, revealing the presence of Al-Mn particles alongside significant amounts of oxygen and localized traces of calcium, consistent with the observed material characteristics.

caption: Boxplot analysis of IL-1α expression levels (pg ml−1) in oral mucosal models following 24 h exposure to d.Sign®10, d.Sign®15, and d.Sign®30 alloy discs compared to untreated controls.
summary: IL-1α expression levels are depicted for untreated and alloy-treated oral mucosal models. Exposure to Ni–Cr alloy discs significantly increased cytokine expression compared to Co–Cr discs. Elevated IL-1α levels following Ni–Cr exposure highlight the activation of epithelial inflammatory responses, serving as a key indicator of cellular damage in the mucosal tissue.

caption: Pole figure representation for the SLM sample on the X–Y cross-section, demonstrating a lack of preferred crystal orientation.
summary: The pole figure for the SLM sample on the X–Y cross-section illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution. Analysis of this plot confirms that there is no preferred crystal orientation present in the material, indicating a random distribution of grain orientations within the horizontal plane of the SLM-processed sample.

caption: Calculated Mg–Ni binary phase diagram derived from the FTlite database in FactSage 7.1, illustrating the equilibrium phase relationships and solubility limits across the composition range.
summary: This Mg–Ni binary phase diagram, generated using the FTlite database in FactSage 7.1, maps the equilibrium phase relationships between magnesium and nickel. Notably, the diagram indicates that the solubility of metallic Ni in molten Mg at 800 °C reaches a significant value of 31.5 at%, highlighting high-temperature phase behavior.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction displaying Cr-based M2O3 oxides as pink isosurfaces and Ti-based oxides as dark green isosurfaces within the specimen.
summary: This APT reconstruction visualizes the spatial distribution of oxide phases within the specimen. Cr-based M2O3 oxides are represented by pink isoconcentration surfaces (75 at.%), while Ti-based oxides are shown as dark green isoconcentration surfaces (80 at.%), providing a clear 3D perspective of the oxide morphology and phase separation.

caption: Storage modulus of pure PLA plotted against temperature from -110 °C to 20 °C at frequencies of 1, 30, and 70 Hz.
summary: This panel displays the storage modulus of pure PLA as a function of temperature ranging from -110 °C to 20 °C. The data is presented for three distinct frequencies: 1, 30, and 70 Hz, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's viscoelastic response under these specific thermal and mechanical conditions.

caption: Evolution of the absorption spectrum for SC-02 during photolysis under 365 nm LED irradiation in acetonitrile.
summary: This panel displays the UV-Vis absorption spectrum of SC-02 as it undergoes steady-state photolysis. The experiment, conducted under air in acetonitrile, demonstrates the capacity of the photoinitiator to undergo cleavage upon exposure to 365 nm light, as evidenced by the progressive changes in the absorption profile over time.

caption: Final temperature distribution across the build surface, highlighting specific bin locations labeled 300, 625, and 1205.
summary: This panel displays the final temperature profile of the build as captured by infrared thermography. The visualization identifies specific bin locations across the build, including bins 300, 625, and 1205, which are used to track thermal history throughout the manufacturing process and provide spatial context for subsequent thermal analysis.

caption: Pareto chart of standardized effects showing the relative influence of design variables.
summary: The Pareto chart illustrates the standardized effects of three pivotal design variables identified within the stress-driven lattice generation system. By ranking these variables, the analysis highlights their relative impact on linear stiffness, offering critical insights into which parameters most significantly influence the performance of the generated lattice structures.

caption: Expanded small angle region (2θ range from 9 to 18°) of the XRD pattern for aged DAFA26.
summary: This expanded small angle region of the XRD pattern for aged DAFA26 highlights specific diffraction peaks. Within the 9 to 18° 2θ range, peaks corresponding to L12, B2-NiAl, and Laves phases are clearly identified, facilitating a more precise structural analysis of the aged material.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Ni corresponding to the AISI 316L/IN718 interface window, supporting the accuracy of the interface position identified in the IPF map.
summary: This Ni elemental distribution map provides chemical confirmation of the AISI 316L/IN718 interface location. By aligning with the IPF map, it validates the structural boundary identification. The distribution highlights the compositional shift between the two materials, which is critical for understanding the multi-material solidification behavior.

caption: Nanoindentation topographic surface profile and corresponding hardness distribution map for the as-cast alloy specimen.
summary: This panel displays the nanoindentation topographic surface profile and the corresponding hardness distribution map for the as-cast alloy. These visualizations provide a spatial representation of the mechanical properties across the microstructure, serving as a baseline for evaluating the material's initial state before any thermal exposure treatments are applied.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the percentage change in phase change material (PCM) mass during a metal melting process, evaluated across various grid resolutions.
summary: This line graph illustrates the percentage change in PCM mass as a function of time during a metal melting simulation. The data compares results across different grid resolutions, maintaining a uniform time step of 10^-3 s and a temperature interval of 10 K to assess numerical consistency and convergence behavior.

caption: Cross-sectional views at various locations, where black spots denote unmelted Mo powder particles and white spots represent pores.
summary: These cross-sectional views at different locations within the sample provide a detailed look at the internal defects. Black spots represent unmelted Mo powder particles, while white spots indicate pores. This analysis helps characterize the internal quality and the distribution of unmelted material throughout the printed component.

caption: Evolution of the lowest spin-wave band gaps as a function of the squeeze ratio s for the Py/Co 2D MC structure.
summary: This plot displays the evolution of the lowest spin-wave band gaps in a Py/Co 2D MC structure as the squeeze ratio s varies. The data indicates that the 2nd and 4th band gaps open within this specific base structure, demonstrating the sensitivity of the spin-wave spectrum to structural deformation.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the powder active phase and the 600/Rh/Ce0.9Pr0.1O2/circles monolithic catalyst before and after catalytic testing.
summary: This figure displays X-ray diffractograms for the powder active phase and the 600/Rh/Ce0.9Pr0.1O2/circles monolithic catalyst, evaluated both before and after catalytic tests. The XRD analysis confirms the crystallinity of these materials. Notably, the diffraction patterns show no detectable peaks corresponding to praseodymium or rhodium species within the catalyst structure.

caption: Comparative analysis of flexural strength for oriented SiC whisker composites from this study against recent literature values.
summary: Flexural strength of the oriented SiC whisker composites developed in this work is benchmarked against various reports from recent years. This comparison highlights the performance of the current 3D printed composites relative to existing literature, contextualizing the effectiveness of the in-plane orientation strategy for enhancing mechanical properties.

caption: Surface topography images and cross-sectional profile curves obtained via AFM for substrates A, B, and C under a reduced concentrated load of 3.3 N.
summary: Surface topography images and cross-sectional profile curves obtained via AFM for substrates A, B, and C under a reduced concentrated load of 3.3 N are shown. This panel illustrates the morphological response of the substrates to lower mechanical stress, allowing for a comparative analysis of deformation across different loading conditions.

caption: Atomistic representation of the cubic γ / γ ′ interface model used for computational analysis.
summary: This panel displays an atomistic model of the cubic γ / γ ′ interface. It serves as the structural basis for investigating uniaxial tensile stress-strain behavior at varying temperatures and a constant strain rate, providing a foundational geometry for understanding the mechanical response of the Ni-based superalloy system.

caption: Atomic configuration of the HI γ″-Ni3Al phase representing a stable interface structure.
summary: This panel displays the geometrical atomic model for the HI γ″-Ni3Al phase. Selected for its structural stability, this configuration serves as a representative model for interface analysis in the study. The model illustrates the specific atomic arrangement characteristic of this phase within the investigated material system.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectra of GCN and GCN@CD-A, displaying a strong emission peak at 460 nm related to charge carrier recombination.
summary: PL spectroscopy was employed to investigate the recombination behavior of photogenerated electron–hole pairs. Both GCN and GCN@CD-A display a strong emission peak centered around 460 nm, attributed to the direct recombination of photoexcited charge carriers and n → π* transitions associated with lone electron pairs on nitrogen atoms in the GCN framework.

caption: Initial straight-line trajectory of an electron moving toward the anode under the influence of an electric field.
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial phase of electron motion toward the anode. Driven solely by the electric field force, the electron follows an approximately straight-line trajectory. This fundamental movement pattern serves as the baseline for understanding how sputtering craters form on the sample surface in the absence of magnetic regulation.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength plotted against elongation for the GO/Ti1553 build, benchmarked against conventional and additive manufacturing beta-type Ti alloys.
summary: This plot compares the ultimate tensile strength and elongation of the GO/Ti1553 build against existing beta-type titanium alloys used in biomedical applications. The GO/Ti1553 composite demonstrates superior ultimate tensile strength compared to previously reported materials, with dashed lines indicating the general distribution trend of mechanical properties across these alloys.

caption: Non-site-specific atom probe tomography Cu atom map showing a 20 × 20 × 20 nm selection from the as-built dataset.
summary: The Cu atom map provides a localized visualization of copper distribution within the as-built High N 17–4 sample. By analyzing these non-site-specific APT datasets, the behavior of Cu within the microstructure is revealed, offering insight into the atomic-scale arrangement of alloying elements in the as-printed state.

caption: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for O-16 in acetonitrile, highlighting the spectral overlap used to identify the singlet excited state energy.
summary: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for O-16 in acetonitrile are provided. By identifying the crossing point of these spectra, the singlet excited state energy level (S1) is experimentally determined, facilitating a comparative analysis of the electronic excited states across the different compounds in the series.

caption: Isofield magnetization (M–T) curves for the Ni47Co5Mn40Sn8 alloy before aging, measured during heating and cooling cycles at 0.05 T, 1.0 T, and 7.0 T.
summary: This panel displays M-T curves for the unaged Ni47Co5Mn40Sn8 alloy across a 200–400 K range. The data demonstrates that magnetic transformation temperatures are field-dependent, shifting toward lower values as the magnetic field increases. Specifically, the transformation exhibits a field-induced shift, with ΔTB reaching -16.5 K at 7 T.

caption: Comparison of yield strength (σy) versus ductility for various Al-alloys fabricated by additive manufacturing (AM) in the as-built condition.
summary: This plot compares the yield strength and ductility of various Al-alloys fabricated via additive manufacturing in the as-built condition. It benchmarks the performance of the Al-Ni-Ti-Zr alloy against existing literature data, highlighting its mechanical property profile relative to other AM-produced aluminum alloys within the field.

caption: Skin/core strength as a function of welding speed for sandwich panels joined with a printed susceptor layer, determined via FWT tests.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between welding speed and skin/core strength for sandwich panels fabricated with a printed susceptor layer. The data, obtained through FWT testing, highlights the mechanical performance of the joints. Notably, the solid black diamond indicates a specific sample that experienced failure within the core material.

caption: Nyquist plot of the 16Mn substrate immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, showing a high-frequency capacitive loop and a low-frequency inductive loop.
summary: The Nyquist plot for the bare 16Mn substrate in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution reveals distinct electrochemical behavior. It exhibits a high-frequency capacitive loop alongside a low-frequency inductive loop, which is characteristic of metastable pitting corrosion, indicating the substrate's susceptibility to localized attack in the chloride-containing environment during the electrochemical measurement.

caption: Arrhenius plot of H atom diffusion coefficients in the NGNC system, highlighting the transition from a linear regime below 900 K to a nonlinear regime at higher temperatures.
summary: The NGNC system exhibits a linear Arrhenius relationship for H diffusion at temperatures below 900 K. However, a nonlinear downtrend emerges above 900 K, indicating that the Arrhenius equation is no longer satisfied. This plot effectively distinguishes between the linear low-temperature regime and the nonlinear high-temperature regime for further investigation.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparing synthesized GMA to gelatin, highlighting the emergence of acrylic protons between 5 and 6 ppm and a reduction in lysine methylene protons at 2.9 ppm.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra of synthesized GMA compared to gelatin confirm successful functionalization. Key spectral changes include an increased double peak signal between 5 and 6 ppm, corresponding to acrylic protons from the methacrylate, and a decreased single peak signal around 2.9 ppm, representing methylene protons from the amino acid lysine.

caption: High-resolution HAADF-STEM image of a grown, coherent disk-like precipitate in Ti-2.3Cu alloy aged at 400 °C for 200 h.
summary: This high-resolution HAADF-STEM image displays a grown, coherent disk-like precipitate within a Ti-2.3Cu alloy matrix after aging at 400 °C for 200 hours. The observation highlights the radial growth of these precipitates, which occurs due to a reduced driving force for thickening during the aging process.

caption: Tabulated comparison of the HMCM against mainstream mechanical and acoustic metamaterials based on five performance indexes, with scores derived from carefully analyzed literature data.
summary: This table presents a quantitative comparison of the HMCM against mainstream mechanical and acoustic metamaterials using five distinct performance indexes. Data extracted from referenced literature were carefully analyzed and scored to provide a reasonable assessment, confirming that the HMCM maintains high performance standards relative to other leading metamaterial technologies.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping of the Ni-12Si powder demonstrating uniform elemental distribution of nickel and silicon.
summary: EDS mapping of the Ni-12Si powder confirms a uniform distribution of nickel and silicon throughout the spheroidized particle. This chemical analysis supports the identification of distinct phases, including Niss and nickel-silicide intermetallics, by demonstrating that the elemental constituents are well-dispersed across the observed dendritic and cellular microstructural features.

caption: Long-term cycling performance of the different cells evaluated at a current density of 0.5C.
summary: Long-term cycling performance of the different cells is shown at a current density of 1C. This plot tracks the capacity retention over extended cycles, providing a comparative assessment of the durability and stability of the cells with different separators under continuous electrochemical operation.

caption: DSC curves for the P7F3 blend, exhibiting glass transition temperatures of approximately 69.99 °C and -44.17 °C.
summary: The P7F3 blend DSC curve displays glass transition temperatures of approximately 69.99 °C for PLA and -44.17 °C for PVDF. These distinct values confirm the immiscibility of the polymers in this composition, maintaining thermal characteristics similar to the pure components despite the blending process.

caption: Atomic structure and displacement vector map of the nanocrystalline model, identifying FCC and HCP atoms with green and purple spheres respectively.
summary: This panel illustrates the local atomic environment of the nanocrystalline model using PTM identification. Green spheres represent FCC structured atoms, while purple spheres denote HCP atoms. Red arrows indicate individual atomic displacement vectors, providing a detailed view of the internal structural changes occurring within the grains during tensile deformation.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of a needle-shaped precipitate within the internal oxidation zone (IOZ) of Ni-20Cr-4Al alloy after 500 h of reaction in Ar-5H2O.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image reveals the morphology of needle-shaped precipitates formed within the internal oxidation zone of a Ni-20Cr-4Al alloy after 500 hours of exposure to an Ar-5H2O environment. These precipitates represent the internal oxidation products resulting from the oxidation of Al- and Cr-rich phases within the nickel matrix.

caption: Hardness distribution map of the transverse cross-section for the COM-2024-T3 friction surfacing deposit.
summary: This hardness map illustrates the spatial distribution of micro-hardness across the transverse cross-section of the COM-2024-T3 friction surfacing deposit. Measurements indicate higher hardness values at the top surface and lower values in the center, consistent with literature trends for these types of friction surfacing deposits.

caption: Correlation analysis between the relative mRNA ratios of iNos/Mrc1 and Rankl/Opg in cells adherent to the implant surface.
summary: The relationship between the relative mRNA ratios of iNos/Mrc1 and Rankl/Opg was analyzed in implant-adherent cells. This plot illustrates the correlation between macrophage polarization states and bone remodeling signaling pathways, helping to characterize the biological impact of the implant degradation products on the local bone microenvironment.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of osteogenic markers (ALP, BMP2, RUNX2, OCN, OPN) in MC3T3-E1 cells on PEEK, 40%HA-PEEK, and 40%HA-2%Ag-PEEK.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging shows the spatial distribution and intensity of key osteogenic antibodies. Fluorescence intensity for ALP, BMP2, and RUNX2 was notably more apparent in cells cultured on 40%HA-PEEK and 40%HA-2%Ag-PEEK compared to PEEK, suggesting that these modified surfaces effectively promote early-stage osteogenic antibody expression in the MC3T3-E1 cell line.

caption: Ashby map illustrating the relationship between yield strength (YS) and elongation for the various alloys specified in Table 4.
summary: This Ashby map visualizes the mechanical performance of the alloys listed in Table 4 by plotting yield strength against elongation. The plot serves as a comparative tool to evaluate the ductility and strength trade-offs of the materials, providing a clear overview of their mechanical properties as referenced in the study.

caption: Isochoric heat capacity of Cr2O3 as a function of temperature, derived from MD simulation potentials.
summary: Isochoric heat capacity values for Cr2O3 are presented, highlighting the performance of different MD potentials. In contrast to the isobaric results, lattice dynamics calculations using these potentials yield significantly lower values. These results align more closely with DFT-based literature values and correctly trend toward zero near absolute zero temperature.

caption: Pole figure representation of the as-built (AB) sample showing crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The pole figure for the as-built (AB) sample illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution. This visualization provides insight into the texture and preferred grain orientations present in the material following the additive manufacturing process, serving as a baseline for comparing the effects of subsequent heat treatments on the microstructure.

caption: Continuous melt pool interference mode for S1 scanning strategy.
summary: This schematic illustrates the continuous melt pool interference mode observed in S1. Multi-layer alternate scanning directions in this configuration effectively disrupt the continuity of unmelted powders or pores, preventing the formation of lack of fusion defects that typically arise from inconsistent melt pool overlap during the LPBF process.

caption: Force-displacement response of the PLA hexagonal honeycomb during the first six cycles of cold programming, showing significant curve shrinkage and mechanical degradation.
summary: The PLA hexagonal honeycomb exhibits significant mechanical degradation during the first six cold programming cycles. As the cycle number increases, the force-displacement curve progressively shrinks towards the bottom right, indicating a substantial reduction in energy dissipation capacity and overall mechanical performance compared to the initial loading state.

caption: Unit cell geometry showing a constant length and width of 5 mm with variable height dimensions.
summary: The unit cell design maintains a uniform length and width of 5 mm for all cells, while the height is the primary variable dimension. This geometric consistency across the different lattice structures allows for controlled gradient properties within the overall 3D model design.

caption: High-rate force–displacement curves from in-plane shear experiments performed at 2.5 m/s, showing the influence of temperature on the mechanical response.
summary: Force-displacement curves for in-plane shear experiments at a high displacement rate of 2.5 m/s are displayed for various temperatures. These results serve as validation for the experimental methodology, showing that the shear data follows trends comparable to uniaxial tension tests, confirming the reliability of the high-rate mechanical characterization.

caption: Compressive strength of foam geopolymers evaluated across varying foaming agent concentrations.
summary: Compressive strength data for foam geopolymers is presented here. The results indicate that the addition of SDS, even in the absence of a dedicated foaming agent, leads to a more significant reduction in compressive strength compared to its observed impact on the material's overall density and porosity levels.

caption: Flexural modulus performance of multi-material composites with face-to-core ratios ranging from 0 to 0.8, compared against the monolithic core baseline.
summary: Flexural modulus performance is evaluated for multi-material composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8. The radar plot illustrates performance relative to the monolithic core baseline, with enhancements exceeding 100% in specific configurations. This analysis provides a consistent basis for material selection under flexural loading conditions as presented in the study.

caption: Non-visible surface of the as-printed (AP) component captured via laser imaging.
summary: The non-visible surface of the as-printed (AP) component is shown here using laser imaging. This panel serves as the raw data source for the subsequent image processing step, illustrating the initial surface condition of the component before any electrochemical polishing treatments are applied to the material surface.

caption: Phase distribution obtained through the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm.
summary: This panel displays the phase distribution derived from the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. The visualization represents the optimized phase state, serving as a foundational component of the Monte Carlo analysis presented in the figure, illustrating the effectiveness of the optimization approach in determining the phase configuration of the system.

caption: Atomic model of the (111) γ-Ni//(010) δ-Ni3Nb interface supercell, featuring seven layers of Ni and eight layers of Ni3Nb, with orange and green dots indicating substitutional and interstitial sites for alloy atoms.
summary: This panel displays the supercell structure of the γ-Ni//δ-Ni3Nb interface, constructed with seven layers of Ni and eight layers of Ni3Nb. The atomic model highlights specific substitutional and interstitial sites for alloying elements using orange and green markers, providing a structural basis for evaluating microalloying effects on nucleation barriers.

caption: Histogram representing the quantitative grain size distribution of the CSAM Cu-N 2 sample, illustrating the bimodal nature of the grain structure.
summary: Quantitative analysis of the grain size distribution in the CSAM Cu-N 2 sample is presented in this histogram. The data confirms the presence of a bimodal grain size distribution, consistent with the EBSD observations of both microcrystalline and nanocrystalline grain populations within the processed metallic sample.

caption: Ashby-type classification of specific energy absorption versus thermal conductivity for CuCrZr single-phase lattices at 20% relative density.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the mechanical and thermal performance of CuCrZr single-phase lattice structures at 20% relative density. At this density, IWP Sheet structures demonstrate superior performance, achieving a specific energy absorption of 3.4 kJ/kg and a peak stress of 3.7 MPa, outperforming both Gyroid Solid and IWP Solid designs.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of E. coli and MRSA stained to distinguish between dead (red) and surviving (green) bacterial cells after treatment.
summary: Fluorescence staining of live and dead bacteria was performed to evaluate the bactericidal effects of the treatments. The resulting images confirm that PPG exhibits clear bactericidal activity against both E. coli and MRSA, as evidenced by the presence of red-stained dead cells compared to green-stained surviving bacteria.

caption: Decision Fusion Model architecture components including weight matrices, neuronal activation thermograms, and weight correlation graphs.
summary: This panel details the Decision Fusion Model, which integrates predictions from MLP and ResNet architectures. The model features a self-attention module with query, key, and value matrices, alongside three fully connected layers. Visualizations include weight matrices, neuronal activation thermograms, and weight correlation graphs to represent the fusion process.

caption: EPMA-measured microsegregation profile across a segregation cell in #40HSLA steel, with the measurement location overlaid on the background image.
summary: Experimental microsegregation data obtained via EPMA scanning across a segregation cell is presented here. The measured profile shows a fair agreement with the classical Scheil model calculations, although some significant discrepancies are observed specifically regarding the carbon distribution within the as-built #40HSLA steel microstructure.

caption: Fatigue test data showing the total strain progression modeled by Eq. (1), with load cycles N0 and Ni defining the damage phase and specific modeling parameters P1=0.4919, P2=2e7, P3=7e4, and P4=2e-4.
summary: This plot illustrates the total strain progression during a fatigue test, modeled using Eq. (1) with defined parameters. The curve captures the damage progression phase between load cycles N0 and Ni. Based on these fitting curves, the total strain per cycle is calculated as the average strain increase between these cycles.

caption: Simulated mole fraction distribution of Vanadium in region 1 at the conclusion of the 700 ∘ C isothermal plateau.
summary: This panel displays a phase-field simulation result illustrating the spatial distribution of Vanadium concentration within region 1. The data represents the state of the material at the end of an isothermal plateau held at 700 ∘ C, providing insight into the compositional evolution under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: DC B-H hysteresis loops comparing the magnetic properties of CS1000 pure iron deposit and a cold-drawn low-carbon steel bar reference.
summary: This plot displays the DC B-H hysteresis loops for CS1000 pure iron deposit and a cold-drawn low-carbon steel bar. The data reveals that the CS1000 pure iron deposit exhibits slightly harder magnetic characteristics compared to the cold-drawn low-carbon steel bar reference, illustrating the relative magnetic performance of the two materials.

caption: Close-up visualization of an Eden cluster growth model (ECGM) output, highlighting distinct grain boundary types within the simulated microstructure.
summary: This simulation result displays the Eden cluster growth model output, where specific boundary types are color-coded for structural analysis. Red lines represent Σ3 twin boundaries, black lines denote TRD boundaries, and gray lines indicate all other boundaries. The background color effectively distinguishes each individual TRD within the simulated cluster growth.

caption: Normalized electrical resistance versus temperature curves for Ti50Ni41Co9 and Ti48.5Ni41Co9Nb1.5 alloys, normalized at 300 °C.
summary: Normalized electrical resistance-temperature curves demonstrate the transformation characteristics of the two alloys. These measurements reveal a small amount of B2→R phase transformation in the Ti50Ni41Co9 alloy that was otherwise undetectable by DSC, while confirming that the B2→R phase transformation is completely suppressed in the Ti48.5Ni41Co9Nb1.5 alloy.

caption: Elemental distribution map at a constant energy of 0.333 J/mm, illustrating the concentration range and homogenization at varying scan speeds.
summary: At a constant energy of 0.333 J/mm, this panel shows the elemental concentration range. Evidence suggests that higher scan speeds increase the concentration range. Consistent with other low-energy samples, the homogenization of elements is limited at low power, confirming that power is the primary driver for elemental diffusion enhancement.

caption: Al-rich liquidus projection of the Al–Mg–Si ternary system, highlighting the solidification paths and phase fields for the investigated alloy compositions.
summary: This ternary phase diagram displays the Al-rich liquidus projection for the Al–Mg–Si system. It identifies the primary solidification phases for various alloy compositions, including the hyper-eutectic initial powder and the hypo-eutectic PBF-LB sample. The diagram illustrates the liquid composition trajectory along the two-phase eutectic line toward the terminal three-phase eutectic point.

caption: Comparison of predicted and true creep rupture times for the CNN model, highlighting significant outliers for samples exceeding 150 hours.
summary: Predicted creep rupture times by the optimized CNN model are compared with true values from experimental testing. A dashed box highlights a cluster of serious outliers representing alloy samples with creep rupture times exceeding 150 hours, indicating specific performance limitations of the CNN model for long-duration creep rupture predictions.

caption: Electrical resistance versus temperature plot for an 8.5 nm thick permalloy honeycomb lattice, measured in zero field and an applied in-plane field of 0.5 T, with an inset showing resistivity versus temperature in zero field.
summary: Electrical resistance is plotted as a function of temperature for an 8.5 nm thick permalloy honeycomb lattice under zero and 0.5 T magnetic fields. The data, including the resistivity inset, demonstrate that electrical resistance decreases as temperature decreases, consistent with the observed forward voltage behavior in the magnetic diode.

caption: Atom probe tomography (APT) reconstructions illustrating the 3D distribution of elements in the alloy before and after high-temperature exposure, highlighting the γ matrix, γ' precipitates, and TCP phases.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstructions visualize the 3D elemental distribution within the alloy. These maps distinguish between the Cr-rich γ matrix, Al-rich γ' phase, and TCP phases. By comparing unexposed and exposed samples, the reconstructions reveal structural changes and phase evolution occurring during the high-temperature exposure process in the material.

caption: Variation of the mode I stress intensity factor range as a function of crack length for specimens tested under water and oil lubrication conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the mode I stress intensity factor range plotted against crack length. The data compares water and oil contact conditions, highlighting how lubrication regimes influence fracture mechanics. The results demonstrate distinct propagation behaviors, with water-lubricated specimens showing higher propagation rates due to hydraulic pressurization and mixed-lubrication effects.

caption: Van't Hoff plot showing the linear relationship between median plateau pressure and inverse temperature for La2YMgNi14.
summary: Van't Hoff plot for La2YMgNi14 presents the linear fit between the median plateau pressure and the inverse temperature. This analysis characterizes the thermodynamic behavior of the alloy during hydrogen absorption, confirming the expected linear relationship and enabling the calculation of enthalpy and entropy changes for the hydrogen storage reaction.

caption: Final packing density of particles vibrated via method 2 as a function of the particle-wall coefficient of rolling friction, with each data point representing the average of five independent trials using randomized initial arrangements.
summary: This line graph illustrates the relationship between the particle-wall coefficient of rolling friction and the final packing density for particles subjected to vibration method 2. Results indicate a minor decrease in packing density as the rolling friction coefficient increases, with each data point averaged across five distinct random initial particle configurations.

caption: Storage and loss modulus evolution for 20 wt% Al2O3 composite resin during UV curing.
summary: DMA analysis for 20 wt% Al2O3 composite resin shows the transition from liquid to cured state. The storage modulus is initially lower than the loss modulus, confirming good flowability. Upon UV lamp activation, the storage modulus increases, confirming that the Al2O3 concentration contributes to improved mechanical properties of the composite.

caption: Isothermal thermogravimetric analysis curves for neat PEKK measured between 300 °C and 550 °C, demonstrating high thermal stability with less than 1 % weight loss observed below 450 °C.
summary: Isothermal thermogravimetric analysis of neat PEKK is presented in this panel, showing the material's weight loss behavior across a temperature range of 300–550 °C. The data confirms high thermal stability, as the polymer exhibits less than 1 % weight loss when heated at temperatures below 450 °C.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) measurement of a 3D-printed electrode coated with a nickel bath of composition Y, showing improved electrochemical properties.
summary: Presented here is the LSV measurement for a 3D-printed electrode coated with composition Y. The results indicate improved electrochemical properties compared to composition X, suggesting that doubling the chemical composition in the bath enhances performance. Furthermore, the data highlights molybdenum's superior electrochemical properties for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).

caption: Fe-V-Cr ternary phase diagrams at 480 °C and 700 °C, illustrating the measured chemical composition range within the TEM lamella as a gray region.
summary: The Fe-V-Cr ternary phase diagrams at 480 °C and 700 °C display the measured chemical composition range within the TEM lamella as a gray region. These diagrams, alongside the Fe-V-Al system, are utilized to deduce the phases formed within the material, given the relatively low Cr concentrations observed.

caption: Side-by-side view of a three-dimensional BCC unit cell with R = 0.70 mm (Vf,3D = 0.457) and a two-dimensional unit cell with Re = 0.25 mm (Vf,2D = 0.322).
summary: This panel presents the final BCC unit cell configuration with a length of 4 mm, comparing a 3D structure to its 2D numerical counterpart. The volume fractions are defined for both geometries. Consistent with other configurations, the numerical simulation curves show a close match to experimental data during elastic loading.

caption: EBSD orientation map of the bottom WAAM sample, revealing distinct columnar crystals oriented along the building direction.
summary: The EBSD orientation map of the bottom WAAM sample displays a microstructure dominated by columnar crystals aligned with the building direction. This structural feature is characteristic of the initial deposition layers, providing a baseline for comparing grain morphology changes observed in the middle and top regions of the wall.

caption: Percentage enhancement of yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation for horizontal samples comparing double-pulse versus single-pulse laser shock processing conditions.
summary: This panel quantifies the performance gains achieved by utilizing double-pulse laser shock processing over single-pulse methods for horizontal samples. By calculating the percentage enhancements in yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation, the data provides a direct comparison to evaluate the effectiveness of the double-pulse treatment strategy on mechanical properties.

caption: Reconstructed stereographic projection of lattice strain ε lat ( φ , ψ ) derived from full pattern Pawley refinement, utilizing the mean lattice parameter a 0 lat as the reference state.
summary: This contour plot displays the reconstructed stereographic projection of lattice strain, ε lat ( φ , ψ ), calculated via full pattern Pawley refinement. The strain values are normalized against a 0 lat, which is defined as the mean lattice parameter across the entire projection, providing a comprehensive visualization of the lattice strain distribution.

caption: X-ray reflectivity measurements and best-fit analysis for Ni-Zr thin alloy films after thermal annealing at 400 °C, featuring an inset of the electron scattering length density profile.
summary: Reflectivity data for Ni-Zr thin alloy films annealed at 400 °C are plotted with open circles and fitted with solid lines. The included inset provides the electron scattering length density profile, reflecting changes in the film's thickness and electron density resulting from the 400 °C thermal treatment.

caption: Global SHAP value bar chart ranking geometric feature importance for print quality prediction.
summary: This bar chart displays the mean absolute SHAP values to quantify the influence of geometric features on print quality. It identifies deviations in layers 7, 9, and 10 as the most significant variables, demonstrating the model's high sensitivity to inconsistencies occurring within the upper layers of the printed structures.

caption: Total Ah-throughput of second-life batteries plotted as a function of varying C-rates.
summary: This plot illustrates the usable total Ah-throughput of second-life batteries across different C-rates. By analyzing the relationship between discharge rates and cumulative capacity, the figure provides critical data on the remaining operational capacity of the batteries, highlighting how varying C-rates influence the overall performance and longevity of second-life energy storage systems.

caption: Taylor factor map of as-built CG-10 specimen under tensile loading along the SD direction.
summary: Representing the CG-10 specimen, this Taylor factor map highlights the relationship between grain structure and mechanical response. The refined grain boundaries observed in this configuration correlate with higher Taylor factor values, which reduce the average dislocation energy per unit grain boundary and improve the overall strength of the material.

caption: Full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) values as a function of applied strain measured in the bulk structure of the HSP-treated specimen.
summary: This plot shows the FWHM versus applied strain for the bulk structure of the HSP-treated specimen. The data tracks how the peak broadening, indicative of microstructural state changes, evolves under load. This allows for a direct comparison of bulk material response between high-intensity and low-intensity shot peening treatments.

caption: Linear regression analysis of α Tu 0 → Tu versus ( T u − T u 0 ) / ln ( T u / T u 0 ) for 40%H 2 +60%NH 3 +air flames at a rich equivalence ratio of ϕ = 1.2 and 1 atm pressure, displaying the linear fit and residual deviations.
summary: For rich 40%H2+60%NH3+air flames at 1 atm, this plot displays the correlation between temperature parameters alongside linear fitting residuals. The data shows that simulation results accurately represent experimental tendencies. Notably, the absolute fitting residuals for this condition peak at approximately 0.025, reflecting the model's performance at higher equivalence ratios.

caption: Microhardness of PBF-LB Ti6Al4V specimens as a function of the normalised energy input rate (NEIR).
summary: Microhardness values are plotted against the NEIR metric for various PBF-LB Ti6Al4V geometries. The results show a clear decrease in microhardness as NEIR increases, consistent with the observed alpha-lath coarsening. This demonstrates the potential for site-specific control over mechanical properties using the NEIR metric.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of Fast Green FCF dye sensitizer within a photo-galvanic electrolytic solution containing Fructose, NaOH, and SLS, comparing non-illuminated and illuminated states.
summary: The UV-Vis absorbance spectra reveal three prominent bands at 305 nm, 360 nm, and 600 nm for the un-illuminated electrolyte. These bands exhibit specific optical densities and molar absorptivities, such as 0.318 at 610 nm.
