The spectra demonstrate the chemical constituents' absorption characteristics across the 205 nm–320 nm range.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of TPCSU45 and TPCSU38 samples acquired after rheological testing at 200 °C for 1.5 hours under a nitrogen atmosphere.
summary: 1H NMR spectroscopy was performed on the TPCSU45 and TPCSU38 samples following their exposure to rheological testing at 200 °C for 1.5 hours. These spectra provide chemical evidence of the structural state of the polymers after thermal treatment, supporting the findings observed in the rheological mechanical tests.

caption: Axial strain field contour map for a thick vertical hinge structure with a thickness of 2 mm, demonstrating the impact of increased hinge thickness on local strain variations during compression.
summary: Representing a thicker vertical hinge (t = 2 mm), this contour map illustrates the axial strain fields developed during compression. The increased thickness restrains auxeticity and induces a stiffening effect. Furthermore, the map captures the rapid changes in local strain variations that occur when physical contact is established between the bent cell hinges.

caption: Curing degree nephograms of HFMLs, visualizing the spatial distribution of curing progress across the specimen.
summary: These curing degree nephograms provide a spatial visualization of the curing process within HFMLs. The data confirms that extending the primary insulation time leads to more uniform curing across the material, as evidenced by the smoother distribution patterns observed in the curing degree maps compared to shorter insulation periods.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) spectrum characterizing the elemental composition of the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample.
summary: The EDS spectrum provides a quantitative and qualitative analysis of the elemental constituents within the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample. This spectroscopic data confirms the presence of specific elements, serving as a foundational measurement for the subsequent elemental mapping and compositional analysis performed on the material during the TEM investigation.

caption: Ashby-type plot correlating ultimate tensile strength (UTS) with average fatigue life for several Al-Si alloys at a total strain amplitude of 0.4%.
summary: The Ashby-type plot maps the relationship between ultimate tensile strength and average fatigue life for various Al-Si alloys. By focusing on a constant total strain amplitude of 0.4%, the plot provides a comparative overview of how different alloy compositions and states perform in terms of strength-fatigue trade-offs.

caption: Load versus displacement plots for 3D-printed BG and BG AC3D scaffolds, showing maximum displacement values of 293 ± 47 and 256 ± 51, respectively.
summary: The load versus displacement behavior of 3D-printed BG and BG AC3D scaffolds is illustrated in this panel. Experimental results indicate that the BG scaffolds reached a maximum displacement of 293 ± 47, while the BG AC3D scaffolds exhibited a maximum displacement of 256 ± 51 during the nanoindentation testing process.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy (WDS) elemental mapping of aluminum (Al) distribution, highlighting the NiAl-rich lamellar regions within the coating.
summary: WDS elemental mapping of aluminum in the CS 1 coating reveals the distribution of NiAl-rich regions. The mapping confirms that the lamellar structure observed in the BSE micrograph is chemically distinct, with aluminum concentrated in specific lamellae, consistent with the preserved microstructure of the feedstock powder.

caption: Normalized infrared melt pool emission map for sample S7 processed with a 300 ms time delay, demonstrating homogenized temperature distribution across the printed layer due to effective cooling between tracks.
summary: Normalized infrared melt pool emission for sample S7, processed with a 300 ms time delay, demonstrates effective cooling between tracks. This extended delay limits heat accumulation, resulting in a more homogenized temperature distribution across the printed layers 46 and 66 compared to samples processed with shorter time delays.

caption: Atomic structure snapshots and dislocation line length variation as a function of initial substrate temperature, comparing states at 300 K and 1100 K.
summary: This simulation snapshot illustrates the atomic structure of the substrate at 300 K and 1100 K, highlighting the prevalence of FCC atoms. A significant increase in internal dislocation density occurs above 700 K. Specifically, at 1100 K and 900 m/s impact velocity, two primary Shockley dislocations with 1/6 [-1 2 1] Burgers vectors emerge.

caption: Absorbance spectra showing the catalytic reduction of 4-NP by 2 wt% Co-HPMC-C, with full conversion achieved after 120 minutes.
summary: This panel presents the UV–vis absorbance data for the catalytic conversion of 4-NP using 2 wt% Co-HPMC-C. The spectral evolution confirms that increasing the cobalt content to 2 wt% in the HPMC-based catalyst results in a faster reaction, reaching 100% conversion of 4-NP in 120 minutes.

caption: Quantitative analysis of bone volume to tissue volume (BV/TV) ratio at 4 weeks post-implantation for P, PC, PCN, and Ti groups.
summary: Quantitative analysis of BV/TV at 4 weeks reveals significant differences in new bone formation. The PCN group shows enhanced osteogenic effects compared to P and Ti groups. Micro-CT quantification confirms the percent of new bone formation as 8.8% for P, 14.9% for PC, 17.6% for PCN, and 10.3% for Ti.

caption: Force–displacement curves for Ni-based superalloy powders tested at a reduced maximum indentation depth of 50 nm.
summary: Force–displacement curves for Ni-based superalloy powders are presented at a shallower maximum indentation depth of 50 nm. These measurements allow for the assessment of surface-level mechanical properties, contributing to the comparative analysis of hardness values between fine powders and bulk alloys across different indentation depths.

caption: WDS chemical mapping illustrating persistent inhomogeneity across dendrites in the AM3 superalloy when heat treatment duration is insufficient.
summary: WDS mapping reveals that chemical composition distribution remains inhomogeneous within the AM3 superalloy microstructure. This panel highlights the persistence of chemical segregation across dendrites, indicating that the applied heat treatment duration is insufficient to achieve complete chemical homogenization throughout the material volume.

caption: Tomographic cross-section of the heat sink sample immediately following the MEX 3D-printing stage.
summary: This tomographic cross-section displays the internal structure of the heat sink sample directly after the MEX 3D-printing process. The image provides a baseline view of the as-printed morphology, allowing for the subsequent assessment of structural changes and void evolution during the solar-sintering heat treatment stages at higher temperatures.

caption: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra for all samples, showing the oxidation state characteristics.
summary: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra are presented for all samples. The spectrum of Ni1Co3@NC is nearly identical to that of Ni foil, indicating that nickel exists in a metallic state. This observation is consistent with complementary XRD and XPS analyses, confirming the metallic nature of the nickel species.

caption: Predicted 2D section of the IN718 grain structure generated via simulation using a laser power of 1450 W, laser speed of 12.7 mm/s, powder feed rate of 0.283 g/s, and laser diameter of 2.286 mm.
summary: Representing a 2D section extracted from a 3D grain structure, this simulated microstructure corresponds to specific laser processing parameters for IN718. By comparing the cumulative distribution function of this simulated case against experimental EBSD data, researchers identified optimal nucleation density and undercooling values that minimize prediction errors.

caption: Maximal relative strain plotted against irradiation dose for various holding pressures.
summary: This line graph illustrates the relationship between maximal relative strain and irradiation dose under different holding pressure conditions. The data demonstrates how varying the applied pressure during irradiation influences the resulting material strain, providing a quantitative assessment of the mechanical response across the tested range of irradiation doses.

caption: Debye-Scherrer diffraction rings for the 1000HT sample at 25 °C, showing the state before and after deformation, with azimuthal integration performed along the loading direction using ± 15° segment masks.
summary: Diffraction images of Debye-Scherrer rings for the 1000HT sample at 25 °C are presented before and after deformation. The analysis involves azimuthal integration along the loading direction using ± 15° segment masks, facilitated by Fiji and Fit2d software. This process captures the evolution of diffraction patterns resulting from the applied mechanical load.

caption: Dilatometric heating curves and derivative analysis for steel S4, establishing an operational T A of 1067 °C.
summary: Thermal analysis of steel S4 provides the RLC–T heating curve and its first derivative, which are used to define the austenitizing behavior. The operational austenitizing temperature T A is calculated as 1067 °C, identified at the temperature where the derivative peak decays and the curve returns to linearity.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph illustrating the fine-grained (FG) zone located within the bottom section of the PHT-treated specimen.
summary: This bright-field STEM image provides a structural overview of the fine-grained zone in the bottom section of the PHT-treated specimen. It serves as the primary context for the subsequent higher-resolution elemental and morphological analyses presented in the figure, establishing the microstructural baseline for the PHT condition.

caption: Variations in alpha-lath size and beta-phase fraction relative to the build direction (BD) for the representative middle section of the TCH tensile sample.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between alpha-lath size, beta-phase fraction, and build direction for the TCH tensile sample. The data highlights how these microstructural parameters evolve across the middle section. The observed trends are consistent with the formation of HAZ bands, which manifest as alternating bright and grey contrasted layers.

caption: Maximum deflection in the Z-direction of cantilever specimens plotted against interlayer time, categorized by batch size n and layer height t.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between interlayer time and maximum deflection in the Z-direction for cantilever specimens. Results indicate that deflection decreases as batch size n is reduced and layer height t is increased. These findings confirm that shorter layer intervals effectively minimize residual stress during the manufacturing process.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy elemental maps illustrating the distribution of C, W, Cr, and Mo within the cellular microstructure.
summary: WDS elemental mapping reveals the spatial distribution of carbon, tungsten, chromium, and molybdenum across the cellular microstructure. These maps provide critical insights into the chemical composition of the grain boundaries and cellular regions, complementing the morphological observations obtained from the corresponding SEM imaging of the printed material.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curves comparing raw PEEK powder (blue) and heat-treated PEEK powder (red), highlighting the melting temperature at 344 °C and the presence of a second endothermic melting peak in the heat-treated sample.
summary: This DSC analysis compares the thermal behavior of raw and heat-treated PEEK powder. The heating curves reveal a melting temperature of 344 °C for the material. Notably, the heat-treated PEEK powder exhibits a second endothermic melting peak, which is eliminated during the subsequent laser melting process in DED-LB/P manufacturing.

caption: Vickers microhardness values of GH3536 superalloy specimens plotted against varying cold rolling reduction ratios.
summary: Vickers microhardness measurements for the GH3536 superalloy demonstrate a clear hardening trend as the cold rolling reduction increases. The hardness values rise significantly from 213 HV for the initial specimen to 375 HV for the RR60 specimen, indicating substantial strain hardening resulting from the cold rolling process.

caption: Pressure drop versus mass flow rate scatter plot, with data points color-coded by Wa (average directional waviness).
summary: This plot displays the pressure drop as a function of mass flow rate, with individual data points colored according to the average directional waviness (Wa). The results confirm that the trends for waviness are generally as expected, demonstrating the impact of surface waviness on the measured pressure drop values.

caption: High-magnification 3D reconstruction of pore morphology in a Ti-6Al-4V cube fabricated using Mode 3 beam profile at a volumetric energy density of 204.30 J/mm³.
summary: This high-magnification 3D micro-CT reconstruction illustrates the representative pore morphology observed in Ti-6Al-4V cubes processed with a Mode 3 beam profile. The image provides a detailed view of the internal structural features resulting from the specific volumetric energy density of 204.30 J/mm³ applied during the manufacturing process.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curve for sample S2 evaluated in Hank's solution at 37 °C across varying pH levels.
summary: Presented here is the potentiodynamic polarization curve for sample S2, measured in Hank's solution at 37 °C. The plot captures the electrochemical response of the specimen across different pH conditions, facilitating an analysis of how varying acidity levels influence the polarization behavior of this specific material.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of M6C carbides, providing evidence of the M6C and γ phase orientation relationship.
summary: Diffraction analysis of the M6C carbides reveals a complex face-centered cubic structure. The pattern demonstrates a specific crystallographic orientation relationship with the γ phase, defined by M6C ≈ 3aγ along the [200] direction. This structural data, combined with EDS results, confirms the identity of the W-rich M6C phase.

caption: Schematic representation of conventional planar 3D printing, illustrating the fixed layer height and constant extrusion rate that ensure stable material deposition.
summary: Conventional planar 3D printing is depicted as a process utilizing fixed layer heights. This configuration allows for a constant optimal extrusion rate and consistent printing speed, which together facilitate stable material deposition throughout the fabrication process, serving as a baseline for comparing multi-axis printing techniques.

caption: Measured porosity and strut diameter values for the face-centered cubic wick geometry.
summary: Face-centered cubic wick geometry data is presented, detailing the measured porosity and strut diameter. These metrics are derived from helium pycnometry and SEM analysis. The strut diameter is maintained at approximately 325 μm, consistent with as-built wick specifications, providing a baseline for evaluating the structural characteristics of this specific lattice configuration.

caption: Creep test results for RR1000 comparing typical (red dots) and fine (blue dots) γ' microstructures against model predictions.
summary: This panel displays creep test results for RR1000, contrasting typical and fine γ' microstructures represented by red and blue dots, respectively. The data serves as a validation for model predictions, highlighting the influence of initial microstructure on creep behavior and identifying potential model mismatches related to grain size effects.

caption: Constant potential amperometry results for the eF 4 D EC-20 device at a fixed anodic potential of +0.60 V vs PLA-CB, demonstrating the limiting current response across the same range of flow rates used in panel B.
summary: Panel C shows constant potential amperometry for the eF 4 D EC-20 device at a fixed anodic potential of +0.6 V. This measurement establishes the limiting current values at different flow rates, providing the necessary data to analyze the relationship between hydrodynamic conditions and the electrochemical current output of the device.

caption: Misorientation profile along the line X-Y extracted from the EBSD map at point E3, demonstrating the presence of deformation twins within the microstructure.
summary: The misorientation profile along the line X-Y in the EBSD map of point E3 provides quantitative evidence of deformation twinning. This analysis confirms that the microstructural evolution at high strain levels includes the formation of deformation twins, contributing to the material's complex hardening behavior during the tensile test.

caption: S-N diagram comparing pure-torsional fatigue tests (circular symbols) with torsional fatigue tests under superimposed static tensile stress (rhomboidal symbols).
summary: This S-N diagram illustrates the fatigue behavior of materials under pure-torsion and static-tension-superimposed torsional loading. Experimental results indicate that the fatigue strength at 10^8 cycles for ST and PH specimens is nearly equivalent, and the fatigue strength measured under static tension is notably identical to that of pure-torsion fatigue tests.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra comparing the GO resin (TPO/TT/GO/PEGDA) and the reference composition REF4 (TPO/TT/H2O/PEGDA).
summary: The UV-Vis absorption spectra demonstrate the optical characteristics of the GO resin compared to the REF4 control composition. Analysis reveals that the incorporation of GO nanoadditives does not induce any significant deterioration in the spectroscopic properties of the resin, confirming that the material maintains its intended optical performance after modification.

caption: Peak arc voltage (AV) curve recorded during the printing of the 7th layer of a 10-bead thick wall.
summary: Peak arc voltage measurements for the 7th layer demonstrate an increasing difference between the arc starting and ending regions. As the printing process proceeds, the peak AV values rise, indicating a gradual increase in arc length caused by the inherent characteristic of lower bead height at the arc ending area.

caption: Pie chart illustrating the proportional distribution of direct energy consumption during the printing process for experimental conditions Exp 4 and Exp 7.
summary: This pie chart visualizes the energy consumption breakdown during the printing process for Exp 4 and Exp 7. The data reveals that the heated bed is the primary contributor to total energy usage, highlighting its dominant role in the overall power requirements during the fabrication of these specific experimental samples.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ni–V system.
summary: The Ni–V binary phase diagram illustrates the equilibrium relationships between nickel and vanadium. According to the study, this system, along with other Ni-X diagrams, shows that vanadium has a negligible effect on the solidification temperature range, indicating no significant modification to the initial IN625 superalloy's grain morphology or solidification characteristics.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profile of the HR-W specimen showing hydrogen desorption rate as a function of temperature.
summary: The TDS profile for the HR-W specimen reveals four distinct hydrogen desorption peaks occurring at approximately 130 °C, 348 °C, 450 °C, and 540 °C. These peaks indicate the presence of four different types of hydrogen trap sites within the HR-W material structure, providing insight into hydrogen binding characteristics.

caption: High-speed camera image of the coaxial powder flow above the machining plane with active laser irradiation.
summary: With the laser turned on, tracks of hot particles become visible in the frame at a distance of 7–11 mm from the nozzle. These particles appear considerably brighter than in the non-laser condition, indicating significant thermal excitation of the powder stream as it approaches the processing surface.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay data and biexponential fit for TPU/2 C composite at room temperature.
summary: Measured at an emission wavelength of 465 nm, the TPU/2 C composite exhibits a nonlinear fluorescence decay curve. This experimental data is fitted with a biexponential function to quantify the fluorescence lifetime, reflecting the impact of the 2% coumarin concentration on the composite's optical properties.

caption: STEM annular dark-field image and corresponding EDX elemental count maps of the as-built microstructure carbon replica, revealing the spatial distribution of aluminum, titanium, and chromium particles.
summary: This STEM annular dark-field image and EDX elemental mapping of the as-built microstructure carbon replica visualize the distribution of aluminum, titanium, and chromium particles. The X-ray count maps demonstrate that these particles are distinct, with some carbonitrides observed attached to alumina particles, consistent with the identified microstructural features.

caption: Calculated surface work function for the Al(111) crystal surface.
summary: This panel presents the calculated surface work function for the Al(111) crystal surface. The result is derived from density functional theory calculations, providing a quantitative measure of the energy required to remove an electron from the Al(111) surface, which is a fundamental electronic property of the material.

caption: Atomic model showing six distinct types of interstitial sites considered for hydrogen within the M6C phase.
summary: This panel illustrates the M6C phase, highlighting six different types of interstitial sites evaluated for hydrogen occupancy. As indicated by the reference, these sites were specifically considered to model hydrogen behavior within the M6C structure, providing a comprehensive view of potential interstitial positions in this complex carbide.

caption: Sequential representation of the phosphating process steps.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the systematic operating sequence involved in the phosphating process. The diagram provides a clear visual guide to the individual stages required for surface treatment, ensuring a structured understanding of the procedural workflow as described in the experimental methodology for sample preparation and subsequent immersion treatments.

caption: Second mode-oriented parallelogram unit cell for investigating complex mechanical performance.
summary: The second-mode oriented parallelogram unit cell completes the set of six configurations analyzed in this study. By systematically modifying the geometry of the parallelogram architecture, this design allows researchers to evaluate how specific structural changes influence mechanical performance, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of the lattice's deformation characteristics under various loading conditions.

caption: 2D AFM topographic map showing the post-corrosion morphology of a near-(1 1 1) grain after 120 hours of immersion in acidic NaCl, with five lines indicating the paths for topographic profiling.
summary: The 2D AFM topographic map displays the surface morphology of a near-(1 1 1) grain following 120 hours of immersion in acidic NaCl. The image includes five marked lines with arrows that define the specific paths used to extract topographic profiles across the ridges of the observed triangular pyramid structure.

caption: Full view of the CeraMultic 3D printer 300, an independently developed multi-material ceramic laser-curing additive manufacturing system.
summary: The CeraMultic 3D printer 300 is shown in a full-view photograph. This equipment, developed independently for this study, utilizes a multi-material ceramic laser-curing additive continuous forming process. The image provides a comprehensive overview of the printer's physical configuration and structural design as used in the experimental setup.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the HER profiles of initial and HIUS-treated AlNi alloy particles, illustrating the electrocatalytic performance and intrinsic electron transfer rates.
summary: Tafel coordinates are utilized here to evaluate the electrocatalytic performance of the modified AlNi particles. By replotting the HER profiles, the exchange current density values were calculated, providing a quantitative measure of the intrinsic rate of electron transfer between the analyte and the electrocatalyst for the different sonication treatments.

caption: Comparative displacement-force and displacement-efficiency plots for SOS and HOS structural designs.
summary: Panel b illustrates the energy efficiency and mechanical response of SOS and HOS configurations. By plotting displacement against both force and energy efficiency, the graph allows for a direct comparison of structural performance. These curves provide critical data for assessing the energy absorption capabilities of the OIS structural variants.

caption: Chemical composition data for the bioactive glass according to Japanese patent JP5870086, presented alongside a ternary phase diagram illustrating the glass-forming region within the CaO-SiO2-P2O5 system.
summary: Chemical composition data for the bioactive glass is provided based on Japanese patent JP5870086. This panel includes a ternary phase diagram of the CaO-SiO2-P2O5 system, which highlights the specific glass-forming region. These data points are referenced from Ohtsuki et al. (1991) to characterize the material properties of the bioactive glass particles.

caption: Load-displacement curve measured during nanoindentation of the Cr3C2 carbide phase.
summary: This load-displacement curve characterizes the mechanical response of the Cr3C2 carbide phase during nanoindentation. These tests were conducted to verify the strengthening mechanism of the joints by the introduction of a Mo-Ni skeleton, providing insight into the deformation behavior of this specific phase.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves illustrating the thermal degradation behavior of PLA/hemp hurd filaments subjected to varying numbers of recycling steps.
summary: The TGA curves presented in panel a characterize the thermal degradation profiles of PLA/hemp hurd filaments. These measurements were conducted to evaluate the impact of different recycling steps on the thermal stability of the composite material, providing a clear visualization of mass loss as a function of temperature.

caption: SAED pattern of the γ matrix in the AD specimen along the [001] zone axis.
summary: This SAED pattern represents the γ matrix of the as-deposited specimen, captured along the [001] zone axis. The absence of extra diffraction spots in this specific pattern indicates an FCC crystal lattice, which serves as a clear structural distinction from the L12 lattice observed in the γ′ precipitates.

caption: Tabulated material parameters for AlSi10Mg, including plastic constants (A, B, C, n, p) and fracture parameters (D1 through D5) used in the constitutive modeling.
summary: This table presents the specific material properties for AlSi10Mg used in the simulation. It lists the plastic parameters A, B, C, n, and p, alongside fracture parameters D1 through D5. These values are essential inputs for the constitutive equations governing the mechanical behavior of the material in the finite element model.

caption: Close-up representation of the printing nozzle, illustrating the final material deposition point for the additive manufacturing system.
summary: This panel provides a detailed view of the printing nozzle, which acts as the terminal component for material extrusion. By focusing on this specific part of the modified FDM printer, the diagram clarifies the precise point of material deposition required to form the 3D-printed specimen configuration.

caption: CCT diagram simulation for a steel specimen with a 100 μm grain size at a 900 °C peak temperature.
summary: This CCT diagram simulation illustrates the predicted phase transformation behavior for a steel specimen with a 100 μm grain size at a 900 °C peak temperature. Numerical modeling using JMatPro software incorporates specific grain size inputs to predict microstructural evolution, with red arrows marking reference cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s.

caption: SED distribution map revealing a highly localized energy concentration at the interiors of slip traces.
summary: SED distribution map revealing a highly localized energy concentration at the interiors of slip traces. The SED exhibits a more diffuse distribution compared to the DED, while both remain consistently localized at slip trace interiors, mirroring the behavior observed in LCF loading conditions for this specific specimen.

caption: Molecular dynamics snapshot of the EDPS alloy at 6.4% global strain, showing partial dislocation emission from grain and phase boundaries.
summary: Representing the EDPS alloy at 6.4% global strain, this simulation shows partial dislocations emitted from both grain and phase boundaries on multiple slip systems. The high-angle grain boundary effectively blocks dislocation transmission, contrasting with the as-cast behavior and demonstrating the influence of alloy design on defect distribution.

caption: Longitudinal resistivity profile plotted against magnetization rotation for a Hall-bar patterned at 90° to the easy axis, with solid and dashed lines representing the analytical fit and average resistivity, respectively.
summary: This plot illustrates the longitudinal resistivity variation for a Hall-bar patterned at 90° to the easy axis. The experimental data is compared to an analytical fit and an average resistivity value. The consistent maintenance of magnetic anisotropic axes in these large Hall-bars is critical for the observed resistivity behavior during rotation.

caption: Microstructure morphology at the bottom of the weld, where high temperature gradients and low crystallization rates result in a large G/R ratio.
summary: The bottom region of the weld displays a specific microstructure morphology resulting from a relatively high temperature gradient and a low crystallization rate. This combination creates a large G/R ratio, which dictates the grain growth characteristics and solidification behavior observed in this lower portion of the weld pool.

caption: Three-dimensional Gyroid lattice structure generated through topology optimization.
summary: This panel displays the three-dimensional Gyroid lattice structure developed for the bone implant. The structure was created using nTopology software, incorporating a topology optimization model that extracts natural gradient features from bone to ensure the porous architecture is both functional and bioinspired.

caption: Diamond and Gyroid porous architectures featuring uniform, positive, and negative gradient porosity variations.
summary: Six distinct porous structures were designed using Matlab with an average relative density of 40%. The panel displays Diamond and Gyroid unit cells, showcasing variations in porosity distribution, including uniform porosity, positive gradient porosity ranging from 30% to 50%, and negative gradient porosity ranging from 50% to 40%.

caption: Three-dimensional surface map of microhardness distribution for the HNWF1 sample, highlighting the concentration of nanoparticles within the stirred zone as large agglomerated clusters.
summary: This 3D surface map illustrates the microhardness distribution for the HNWF1 sample. The analysis reveals that nanoparticles are primarily concentrated within the stirred zone, where they exist in large agglomerated clusters. This distribution pattern provides insight into the initial state of nanoparticle dispersion following the first FSP pass.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the tetragonal YSZ layer, verifying its crystal structure.
summary: This selected area diffraction pattern confirms the crystal structure of the YSZ layer. The diffraction data indicates that the YSZ material possesses a tetragonal crystal structure, consistent with the expected phase for this thermal barrier coating component in the as-coated specimen.

caption: Artificial density distribution map illustrating the spatial arrangement of every element within the modeled system.
summary: This panel presents the artificial density distribution of every element within the modeled system. As an output of the finite element modeling process, this map provides a detailed visualization of the elemental arrangement, serving as a primary diagnostic tool for evaluating the initial spatial configuration of the material model.

caption: 3D response surface plot showing the relationship between screw speed and PEG loading on the MFI response parameter.
summary: This 3D response surface plot visualizes the impact of varying screw speed and PEG loading on the MFI of the material. The data indicates that the response parameter follows a pattern similar to that observed in the fiber loading and screw speed analysis, showing a consistent trend in MFI behavior.

caption: Ablated module trajectory on Part 3 without Post-Processing, featuring redundant segments and unmerged boundaries.
summary: This panel displays the trajectory on Part 3 when Post-Processing is disabled. While coverage remains acceptable, the path exhibits redundant segment boundaries and discontinuities between adjacent paths. This leads to an increased total traversal length and reduced continuity efficiency, illustrating the role of Post-Processing in optimizing the final path.

caption: Creep rupture curves of experimental Ni-based single-crystal superalloy samples subjected to 1150 °C and 120 MPa, comparing specimens with varying solution heat treatment durations (0H, 2H, 4H, 8H, and 16H).
summary: This plot illustrates the creep rupture behavior of Ni-based single-crystal superalloy samples under 1150 °C and 120 MPa. The rupture lives for the 0H, 2H, 4H, 8H, and 16H samples are 45, 46, 68, 62, and 40 hours, respectively, with the 0H sample showing an indistinct primary creep region.

caption: Histogram depicting the total powder particle distribution for the 45–150 μm PSD sample.
summary: This histogram provides a comprehensive overview of the total powder particle distribution for the 45–150 μm PSD sample. It serves as a baseline representation of the particle size frequency, illustrating the overall distribution characteristics of the powder bulk used in the study without specific focus on porosity or aspect ratio.

caption: Histogram of equivalent diameter (dₑ) distribution with cumulative frequency curve for LPBF Ti-6Al-4V.
summary: This histogram, accompanied by a cumulative frequency curve, details the distribution of defect equivalent diameters in LPBF Ti-6Al-4V. It provides a statistical overview of the defect size range, establishing the reference distribution against which the defect mitigation performance of the LIF-AM processing conditions is evaluated.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image combined with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping of the top region of the printed cylindrical component.
summary: This panel shows the top region of the printed cylindrical component using SEM and EDS analysis. The elemental distribution map provides insight into the chemical composition at the upper section, completing the comparative analysis of the printed component's elemental consistency across its vertical axis from bottom to top.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curves for as-cast Al-8.0Zn-2.5Mg-2.0Cu and Al-8.0Zn-2.5Mg-xNi (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 wt%) alloy strips.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curves illustrate the thermal behavior of as-cast Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys with varying nickel content. These DSC results were utilized to establish optimal homogenization heat treatment conditions. The analysis highlights the influence of nickel on the thermal characteristics of the aluminum matrix during the heating process.

caption: Comparison of optimization speeds across the four different transfer learning schemes during the model fine-tuning process.
summary: This plot displays the optimization speeds achieved by the different transfer learning schemes during the fine-tuning phase. By comparing these curves, the efficiency of each retraining configuration can be evaluated, providing insight into how different sub-block selections impact the convergence rate of the foundation model during the optimization process.

caption: Two-dimensional PCA projection of ZM-feature data illustrating k-means clustering results, where four distinct clusters are formed with compact, spherical groupings separated by linear boundaries.
summary: This PCA projection visualizes the ZM-feature data clustered via the k-means algorithm. The plot demonstrates the formation of four distinct, compact clusters separated by linear boundaries, which is characteristic of the k-means method's tendency to generate spherical groupings within the feature space.

caption: Geometric representation of the individual unit cell designed for the nonreciprocal mechanical metamaterial.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental unit cell geometry of the proposed 3D mechanical metamaterial. The design serves as the building block for the larger array structure, establishing the structural features necessary for achieving nonreciprocal mechanical behavior in the fabricated micro-lattice samples as described in the research.

caption: Experimental configuration for in situ X-ray computed tomography (XCT) degradation studies of WE43-PEO scaffolds within simulated body fluid (SBF) at the ID19 beamline.
summary: This schematic illustrates the in situ XCT experimental setup used at the ESRF ID19 beamline to monitor scaffold degradation. WE43-PEO1 and WE43-PEO2 scaffolds were scanned using synchrotron radiation, with a sample-to-detector distance of 3000 mm and a 1 s scan time, enabling high-resolution observation of the degradation process in SBF.

caption: Isothermal section below 1473 K, featuring two distinct three-phase coexisting regions of γ + σ + P and γ + P + NiMo.
summary: Below 1473 K, the Ni-Cr-Mo system exhibits two stable three-phase coexisting regions. Specifically, the γ + σ + P region is observed in the Cr-rich portion of the system, while the γ + P + NiMo region is present in the Cr-poor region, defining the low-temperature phase equilibrium.

caption: Relative particle displacements in Area 3, showing the dominant powder deposition regime via Lagrangian particle tracking.
summary: Relative particle displacements in Area 3, showing the dominant powder deposition regime via Lagrangian particle tracking. The predominant displacement, aligned with the reverse direction, was observed as the diminished powder pile's magnitude, indicating a dominant powder deposition regime during the recoating process.

caption: Distribution and percentage analysis of the pore phase within the three-phase structure.
summary: This panel presents the morphology of the pores within the three-phase structure. The porosity of the system was meticulously analyzed to determine the distribution and percentage of the pore phase, offering a clear view of the void space and its spatial arrangement within the sintered material matrix.

caption: Time-dependent COF profile for H13-PT500 °C material subjected to a 9.8 N applied load.
summary: The COF evolution for H13-PT500 °C is presented as a function of sliding time under a 9.8 N load. Monitoring these changes in the COF during the wear process provides essential insights into the dominant wear mechanisms and the transitions that characterize the material's tribological performance under these specific conditions.

caption: Static dielectric constant of the cross-linked models as a function of H/R ratios.
summary: Static dielectric constant values are calculated for the cross-linked models at different H/R ratios. This parameter provides insight into the electrical response of the cross-linked network, complementing the structural and mechanical data to characterize the overall physical properties of the models developed through molecular dynamics simulations.

caption: Partial dependence plots illustrating the relationship between each of the four surface parameters and the predicted probability of keyhole mode formation, with the y-axis representing the mean probability.
summary: Partial dependence plots for the four surface parameters are presented, showing how each feature influences the predicted probability of keyhole mode formation. The y-axis represents the mean probability of the keyhole mode prediction, allowing for an assessment of how variations in individual surface parameters affect the overall model output.

caption: Extended TTT diagram analysis showing the influence of solution temperature on δ phase growth duration.
summary: This diagram demonstrates that while the nucleation rate and incubation time remain constant at a fixed cooling rate, the growth duration of the δ phase is sensitive to thermal history. Specifically, the growth period progressively lengthens as the solution temperature declines, providing critical insights into phase evolution kinetics.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for series ➁ as-cast alloys, displaying melting and solidification behavior alongside an inset Co-elemental EDX map revealing the dendritic microstructure of the γ Co*-5Ni alloy.
summary: Series ➁ alloys demonstrate a narrower, higher melting range of 1475–1500 °C compared to series ➀. Solidification behavior differs significantly, requiring approximately 200 °C of undercooling. The inset EDX map provides representative Co-elemental distribution, confirming that the as-cast γ Co*-5Ni alloy maintains a dendritic microstructure after the solidification process.

caption: Shrinkage rate curves derived from dilatometric data for Alloys 2, 3, 4, and 5, highlighting the kinetics of dimensional reduction.
summary: Shrinkage rate curves for Alloys 2, 3, 4, and 5 processed at 100 rpm provide insight into the rate of dimensional change during the heating process. These curves complement the dilatometric data, showing that materials with higher Co + Ni content undergo significantly greater shrinkage than those with lower concentrations.

caption: Normal residual plot for hardness (HV) data.
summary: This panel displays the normal residual plot for hardness (HV) measurements. As part of the ANOVA framework, this graph allows for the assessment of residual normality, which is essential for validating the statistical assumptions underlying the hardness model and ensuring the reliability of the experimental results obtained during testing.

caption: Theoretical reflection loss curves plotted against frequency and thickness for the SiCN honeycomb ceramic.
summary: The reflection loss curves demonstrate the electromagnetic wave absorption performance of the SiCN honeycomb ceramic. It achieves a minimum reflection loss of –49.0 dB at 10.2 GHz and an effective absorbing bandwidth of 3.02 GHz at 11.4 mm, indicating the material absorbs over 99.99% of incident electromagnetic waves.

caption: STEM-BF image of the OPM microstructure displaying martensitic laths, reverted austenite regions, and spherical Al-Ti-O enriched particles.
summary: This STEM-BF image of the OPM microstructure illustrates martensitic laths and pockets of reverted austenite. The white dashed box highlights spherical particles enriched in Al, Ti, and O. These features characterize the OPM microstructure, demonstrating the structural arrangement and the presence of specific strengthening precipitate phases within the material.

caption: Statistical distribution of dendrite metrics for all dendrites, equiaxed dendrites (ED), and columnar dendrites (CD) across varying printing parameters.
summary: Statistical analysis of dendrite metrics reveals that higher scanning power and lower volumetric energy density promote finer dendritic cells. This trend is consistent with grain size observations, as demonstrated by the box plots comparing all dendrites, equiaxed dendrites, and columnar dendrites under different printing parameters, confirming the statistical significance of these structural changes.

caption: Ti 2p XPS spectrum of NiTi powder heated to 750 °C, exhibiting notable chemical changes in the surface oxidation state.
summary: Heating the NiTi powder to 750 °C results in a Ti 2p XPS spectrum that demonstrates significant chemical changes compared to the 650 °C sample. These spectral modifications indicate a shift in the surface oxidation states of the titanium within the powder as the annealing temperature increases.

caption: Raman spectra acquired from the surface of a steam-oxidized A600 specimen, featuring two distinct peaks at 550 cm-1 and 683 cm-1, compared against reference spectra for Fe(3-x)CrxO4, Fe3O4, and Cr2O3.
summary: This Raman spectroscopy analysis characterizes the surface oxide composition of steam-oxidized A600. The spectra reveal key shifts at 550 cm-1 and 683 cm-1, which correlate with Fe- and Cr-enriched oxide species including Fe(3-x)CrxO4, Fe3O4, and Cr2O3. The 550 cm-1 peak exhibits a sharp feature within broad shoulders at 519 and 580 cm-1.

caption: Optical transmittance spectra of inkjet-printed PEDOT:PSS films formulated with 0.2 wt% Polysorbate 80, comparing layer counts of N L = 2, 4, and 6 across the 400–800 nm visible wavelength range, with black shaded envelopes representing standard deviation for n = 3 replicates.
summary: This plot displays the optical transmittance of inkjet-printed PEDOT:PSS films with 0.2 wt% Polysorbate 80 across the visible spectrum from 400 to 800 nm. Data for layer counts of 2, 4, and 6 are presented, with black shaded envelopes indicating the standard deviation calculated from three independent measurements for each wavelength.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of HR CoCrNi with a corresponding SAED pattern, confirming the presence of nano-twins after fatigue testing.
summary: The dark-field TEM image and associated SAED pattern for HR CoCrNi provide definitive evidence of nano-twins formed during fatigue testing. These results, combined with other microstructural observations, confirm that the formation of numerous nano-twins is responsible for the observed changes in peak intensities and FWHMs in diffraction data.

caption: Three-dimensional reflection loss (RL) plot for the SCC-1 sample, demonstrating the impact of structural modification on electromagnetic wave absorption.
summary: The 3D reflection loss plot for the SCC-1 sample illustrates the electromagnetic wave absorption performance. By comparing this 3D representation with the 2D curves, the absorption characteristics of the SCC-1 sample are evaluated, highlighting the influence of the structural modifications on the overall electromagnetic wave absorption performance.

caption: Avrami plot derived from DSC data for nanocomposites at 100 °C.
summary: Representing the second set of DSC-derived Avrami data at 100 °C, this panel complements the kinetic analysis of the nanocomposites. It serves as a critical component of the comprehensive Avrami study, which evaluates the crystallization characteristics of PLA, cCNC/PLA, and AcCNC/PLA nanocomposite materials at specific isothermal temperatures.

caption: High-resolution image of precipitates and characterization of phase interfaces in sample C-Ⅱ.
summary: This panel displays high-resolution imaging of the precipitates and their interfaces in the LPBF-fabricated sample. The detailed characterization of these phase boundaries provides insight into the microstructural evolution and the effectiveness of the precipitation behavior under the rapid cooling conditions inherent to the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: False-colored rhodamine-tagged kappa-carrageenan (KC) within the microcapsule structure, featuring a corresponding bright field inset.
summary: Rhodamine-tagged kappa-carrageenan (KC) is shown via false-colored fluorescence microscopy, with a bright field inset for structural context. This visualization is part of a series of experiments designed to gain a clearer understanding of the phase composition and nanoparticle distribution within the fabricated emulsion microcapsules.

caption: Belov-Arrott plot (M^2 versus μ0H/M) for the HTHed Schwarz sample, characterizing the FM-PM phase transition.
summary: Belov-Arrott plots, representing M^2 versus μ0H/M, are constructed for the HTHed Schwarz sample to investigate the nature of the ferromagnetic to paramagnetic phase transitions. This graphical analysis is essential for determining the specific characteristics of the magnetic transition occurring within the Schwarz-structured sample.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of WAAMed NiTi alloy deformed at 750 °C and a strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the microstructural state of WAAMed NiTi alloy following compression deformation at 750 °C and a strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹. The visualization provides insights into the dynamic softening mechanism by illustrating the grain orientation distribution within the specimen under these specific thermal and mechanical conditions.

caption: Conductance measurement of the silver metallic tracks on the glass hemisphere, with a two-probe resistance value of 1.4 Ω.
summary: This image illustrates the conductivity measurement of the silver tracks over a short distance. Two-point conductivity measurements performed on the curved surface yielded a resistance of 1.4 Ω. This result confirms the high electrical performance of the silver tracks produced via the atmospheric pressure plasma jet process.

caption: Representative EDS analysis of the grain interior corresponding to samples in panels c-f.
summary: This EDS spectrum provides a chemical analysis of the grain interior regions observed in samples c through f. The data serves as a baseline for the bulk material composition. Chromium peaks observed in the spectrum are identified as artifacts resulting from the sputtering process used during sample preparation.

caption: Atomic structure model of Cr6 amorphous alloy illustrating the local atomic arrangement following the substitution of Co with Cr.
summary: Representing the Cr6 amorphous alloy, this atomic model shows the structural configuration after chromium replaces cobalt. The visualization confirms that transition metals and boron atoms are distributed around the central chromium atoms, with coordination numbers falling within the 13 to 14 range, characteristic of these transition metal-based amorphous systems.

caption: Residual plot for the BP model depicting the error distribution.
summary: The residual plot for the BP model is shown in panel (c). Consistent with the findings for the BH and BW models, this plot illustrates the distribution of residuals, which helps in evaluating the predictive accuracy and identifying potential patterns in the errors generated by the BP model.

caption: Raman spectra of CNT, CNT-AR, and PMTA-CNT acquired with a 532 nm excitation laser, showing characteristic D, G, 2D, and 2G bands that confirm the structural integrity of the nanotubes after modification.
summary: Raman spectra for CNT, CNT-AR, and PMTA-CNT are presented, utilizing a 532 nm excitation laser. The spectra exhibit characteristic D, G, 2D, and 2G bands. The consistent intensity of the D band indicates that PMTA modification does not introduce additional defects, confirming the coexistence of PMTA and CNTs.

caption: Profilometry cross-sectional profiles comparing the wear tracks of as-printed and as-received IN718 alloys following tribological testing.
summary: Profilometry cross-sectional profiles are presented for both as-printed and as-received IN718 alloys after undergoing tribology testing. These wear cross-profiles illustrate the material loss and surface deformation characteristics of the two distinct alloy conditions, providing a quantitative comparison of their respective wear resistance and track geometry after the mechanical wear process.

caption: Precipitation-time-temperature (PTT) plot for type 316 stainless steel, synthesized from multiple experimental data sources.
summary: This precipitation-time-temperature (PTT) plot for type 316 stainless steel was developed by integrating data from several previous studies. It serves as a reference for understanding the kinetics of phase precipitation and its influence on the microstructural evolution of the stainless steel samples under various thermal conditions.

caption: High magnification SEM image and corresponding EDS elemental maps of spherical WC-10Co powder, showing the distribution of W and Co.
summary: This panel presents a high-magnification SEM image and EDS elemental maps for spherical WC-10Co powder, detailing the distribution of tungsten and cobalt. Kumar et al. noted that transitioning from such spherical morphologies to non-spherical shapes amplifies capillary forces, resulting in 5% to 12% greater density in sintered parts.

caption: EBSD orientation map of LPBF Alloy 718 at 2% strain, illustrating grain structure in the bending region.
summary: LPBF-processed Alloy 718 is characterized in this EBSD orientation map at 2% strain. Captured from the bending region of a transverse varestraint test, the map reveals the grain structure and orientation distribution of the additively manufactured material as it undergoes deformation and develops cracking under the applied strain.

caption: Contour plots illustrating the optimal design parameters (t, l) that minimize the total exergy destruction rate for four distinct system velocities: 0 m/s, 25 m/s, 200 m/s, and 1000 m/s.
summary: These contour plots visualize the relationship between unit cell geometry parameters (t, l) and total exergy destruction across four velocity scenarios. By mapping the design space, the figure identifies optimal configurations that minimize energy loss, demonstrating how system velocity influences the geometric requirements for efficient unit cell performance in the design space.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the longitudinal section of in-situ TiB particles, showing growth along the c-axis.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the longitudinal section of in-situ TiB particles confirms that the reinforcement grows along the c-axis. This structural observation complements the transverse section analysis, establishing the overall morphology and growth direction of the TiB phase within the titanium matrix composite material.

caption: Rear side 3D scan of the rear wall for Test #9, showing the structural integrity of the Al foam and Al 6061-O face sheet configuration.
summary: The 3D scan of the rear side of the rear wall for Test #9 demonstrates the structural state of the Al foam and Al 6061-O face sheet assembly. Consistent with the front side analysis, the rear wall shows no signs of global deformation after the experimental test.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image of the ZrB2/Al–4Fe composite specimen.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging provides a clear view of the microstructural features within the ZrB2/Al–4Fe composite. This visualization technique highlights the interaction between the matrix and the reinforcement particles, offering insights into the structural integrity and phase distribution within the composite material at the nanoscale.

caption: Optical absorption spectrum of HEMA:PEGDA resin containing Atto dyes, including an inset showing the liquid resin samples.
summary: Optical absorption characteristics of Atto dyes in liquid HEMA:PEGDA resin are presented here. The inset provides a visual reference for the liquid resin samples. These measurements confirm the selective wavelength filtering capabilities of the dyes when dissolved in the resin medium, supporting their potential for optical applications.

caption: Hardness distribution profile measured across the deposition heights for three distinct cross-sections of a five-layer DED wall fabricated with closed-loop spatial cooling rate control.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness distribution across the deposition heights of a five-layer DED wall. By utilizing closed-loop spatial cooling rate control, the figure demonstrates the mechanical consistency achieved across three different cross-sections, providing a quantitative assessment of the material's hardness uniformity throughout the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Fluorite crystal unit cell geometry rendered by nTopology.
summary: This panel displays the fluorite crystal unit cell structure as generated by nTopology software. It serves as one of the distinct unit cell configurations presented in the figure to illustrate specific lattice arrangements used in the study, providing a clear visualization of the fluorite atomic framework for structural analysis.

caption: Geometric parameters defining the groove dimensions, specifically the diameter (D) and depth (H), used to analyze tube embedding characteristics.
summary: This schematic illustrates the groove diameter (D) and depth (H) parameters established for the FE simulations. These specific dimensions are critical for quantitatively analyzing tube embedding characteristics, as they directly influence the resulting channel cross-section geometry, as well as the subsequent tube deformation and fixing conditions during the assembly process.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the normalized strength and cost of room-temperature and high-temperature aluminum alloys, highlighting three proposed designs relative to a wrought Al 7075 benchmark.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the performance of various aluminum alloys by mapping normalized strength against cost. It contrasts room-temperature and high-temperature variants, including those strengthened by metastable ternary phases. The three proposed designs demonstrate superior cost-to-strength ratios compared to the benchmark printable alloy, which exhibits strength comparable to wrought Al 7075.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the standardized effects of layer thickness and extrusion multiplier on green density and volume deviation responses.
summary: This Pareto chart displays the standardized effects of layer thickness and extrusion multiplier on green density and volume deviation. It identifies the significance and impact of each term and their interactions on the responses. The analysis provides a clear visualization of how these processing parameters influence the final material quality metrics.

caption: Pseudo-ternary composition diagram illustrating the MSAD value distribution for Co-Ni-Cr-Mo MPEAs containing 10 at.% Co, evaluated across a solvus temperature range of 650–850 °C.
summary: Representing the lattice distortion effect, this diagram maps MSAD values for Co-Ni-Cr-Mo MPEAs with 10 at.% Co. The solvus temperature is limited to 650–850 °C. The visualization demonstrates how varying composition influences the MSAD values within the FCC single-phase region, highlighting the complex relationship between alloying elements and lattice distortion.

caption: J-V performance curves for solar cells protected by pure COC and various COCA coversheets measured under controlled neodymium light conditions.
summary: Performance curves for solar cells with pure COC and COCA coversheets are shown under regulated neodymium light conditions. Similar to the sunlight results, the data indicates that increasing the alumina concentration in the COCA4 sample leads to a reduction in the overall effectiveness of the photovoltaic device.

caption: Simulated atomic configuration of the material at 300 K, illustrating the structural arrangement prior to or during lattice analysis.
summary: This panel displays the simulated atomic configuration at 300 K. The non-uniform lattice strain fields observed in these models substantiate the existence of lattice distortion caused by excessive Ni atoms. These configurations serve as the baseline for evaluating structural changes and lattice compression effects within the material system.

caption: Spin-wave dispersion spectrum for the squeezed permalloy dot structure with a squeeze ratio of s = 0.6, illustrating the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone.
summary: This panel presents the spin-wave dispersion spectrum for the squeezed permalloy dot structure at a squeeze ratio of 0.6. It maps the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone, demonstrating how structural deformation influences the spin-wave characteristics compared to the base structure shown in panel a.

caption: Geometric profile of the 3D S-shaped monostructure unit cell for a strut thickness of 1 mm, highlighting the two perpendicular 0° and 90° planes.
summary: The S-shaped unit cell comprises two curved struts in perpendicular planes, each featuring two arches connected by a middle beam at a 10° angle. With a characteristic diameter of 16 mm and an eccentricity of 1.8 mm, this design ensures controlled movement and densification before contact occurs during mechanical loading.

caption: Macroscopic view of the NiTi tube after 32 million cycles of fatigue testing, shown with the 1.2210 steel bushings removed to reveal the wear surface.
summary: The NiTi tube is shown following 32 million cycles of fatigue testing against 1.2210 steel bushings. This preliminary test demonstrates that the tube did not fail catastrophically, maintaining its functional integrity despite the prolonged cyclic loading, as evidenced by the post-test condition of the tube surface after bushing removal.

caption: HPLC chromatograms of PM methanol extract and PL ethanol extract recorded at wavelengths of 205 nm and 330 nm, showing the separation of identified standards and additional unidentified compounds.
summary: Panel B presents the HPLC chromatograms for PM methanol and PL ethanol extracts at 205 and 330 nm. The analysis confirms the presence and quantification of AUC, CAT, VER, and PMJ. Additionally, the chromatograms reveal several other unidentified compounds, indicating a complex chemical profile within the analyzed plant extracts.

caption: In-situ interlayer hot forging system integrated with a directed energy deposition 3D printer, featuring pneumatic actuators labeled ① and ②.
summary: This panel displays the in-house developed directed energy deposition 3D printer prototype, which incorporates an in-situ interlayer hot forging system. The setup utilizes a gas metal arc welding power source integrated with a 3-axis CNC machine, with pneumatic actuators clearly identified as the primary components for the forging mechanism.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram illustrating the cooling curve for the retreating side of a friction stir weld processed at 450 rpm and 10 kN.
summary: Representing the retreating side of the friction stir weld at 450 rpm and 10 kN, this CCT diagram highlights the specific cooling path. By mapping the cooling curve onto the phase transformation fields, it provides insight into the microstructural evolution and potential martensitic transformation occurring at this specific weld location.

caption: Load-displacement behavior under quasi-static compression for the bionic hierarchical cellular structure designed with a circular hole diameter of 0.6 mm.
summary: Presented here is the quasi-static compression load-displacement curve for the bionic hierarchical cellular structure characterized by a circular hole diameter of 0.6 mm. This plot captures the mechanical deformation characteristics of the specimen, allowing for comparison with other hole diameters to assess structural integrity and load-bearing capacity.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of MoO3-x nanorods showing a distinctly defined rod-like morphology.
summary: The scanning electron microscopy image reveals that the as-synthesized MoO3-x exhibits a distinctly defined rod-like nanostructure. These microrods possess a width ranging from 300 to 700 nm and a length extending into tens of micrometers, confirming the successful synthesis of the rod-like nanostructure.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map with overlaid grain boundaries, illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution at the recrystallization front.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map displays the crystallographic orientation at the recrystallization front for a draw rate of 3. Overlaid grain boundaries highlight the complex interface where recrystallization and grain growth occur, demonstrating that the process does not follow a localized isotherm across the sample during directional recrystallization.

caption: Weighted acceptance rates for individual species plotted against MC steps on a logarithmic scale, illustrating the transition from an initial cluster-formation epoch to a steady-state regime where atomic mobility decreases due to M-B or M-C cluster formation in the +TiC system.
summary: This panel displays the activity levels of various species throughout the hMCMD simulation for the +TiC system. The log-scale plot reveals a distinct transition from an initial cluster-formation phase to a steady-state epoch, where the formation of M-B or M-C clusters significantly hinders atomic swaps and reduces overall mobility.

caption: Electrical resistance measurements for printed specimens 1 through 4 show consistent values between 2.5 and 3 Ω, whereas specimens 5 and 6 exhibit insulative behavior at approximately 1 × 10^8 Ω, confirming nozzle failure.
summary: Electrical resistance measurements for printed specimens 1 through 4 show consistent values between 2.5 and 3 Ω, whereas specimens 5 and 6 exhibit insulative behavior at approximately 1 × 10^8 Ω, confirming nozzle failure. These measurements further confirmed the inconsistency in AgNP jetting observed during the printing process for these specific samples.

caption: Optical emission spectra comparing Ar and Kr saturated solutions with and without 1500 rpm stirring, identifying key emission features including a tentative C2 peak.
summary: This spectral plot compares the emission characteristics of Ar and Kr saturated solutions under varying stirring conditions. The data shows that luminol addition results in the total absorption of the UV component previously observed in EG/NaCl solutions. Notable emission features are identified, including a tentative assignment for the C2 species.

caption: Procedural flowchart illustrating the algorithmic steps implemented in ImageJ for the automated segmentation of densification flaws.
summary: This flowchart outlines the specific algorithmic workflow developed by the authors to segment densification flaws within material samples using ImageJ software. The diagram provides a systematic representation of the image processing steps required to identify and isolate these structural defects, facilitating consistent and reproducible analysis of material densification characteristics.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the LS2 CoCrFeNi disk edge, illustrating grain distribution after 10 turns of high-pressure torsion.
summary: This dark-field TEM image illustrates the grain distribution at the edge of the LS2 CoCrFeNi disk following 10 turns of high-pressure torsion. By focusing on specific diffraction conditions, the image provides a detailed look at the refined crystalline structure resulting from the severe plastic deformation process.

caption: Average distance between individuals during the GA optimization process for sample 01, alongside the corresponding stiffness test comparing the printed sample, DNN output, and desired stiffness curve.
summary: Sample 01 optimization progress is tracked via the average distance between individuals during the GA process. The mechanical validation confirms the inverse design approach by comparing the printed sample's stiffness curve against the DNN-predicted output and the target design, ensuring the physical configuration adheres to the desired mechanical characteristics.

caption: Distribution of the four thermal treatment conditions in a three-dimensional principal component (PC) space, showing distinct clustering of samples with similar thermal histories.
summary: Principal component analysis is utilized to represent the distinct thermal profiles in a consistent low-dimensional space. By using three PC scores, the different heat treatment conditions are mapped, demonstrating that samples with similar thermal histories cluster together, which validates the effectiveness of PCA for characterizing complex multi-step thermal processing data.

caption: Geometric representation of a re-entrant unit cell structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the geometric configuration of a re-entrant unit cell. As part of the broader analysis of conventional and modified unit cells, this schematic defines the structural parameters essential for understanding the mechanical behavior of the re-entrant lattice design within the context of the study's geometric entities.

caption: High-magnification LSCM image of SLM pure tungsten deposit B23, showing a low density of pores.
summary: High-magnification imaging of sample B23 indicates a low density of pores, consistent with the relative density results. The image provides a clear view of the grain boundaries and crack paths, supporting the analysis of how processing energy density influences the defect structure and mechanical properties of pure tungsten deposits.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of AM IN718 after SHT-1, revealing a cell-like substructure defined by lenticular precipitates and δ phase precipitates located along intercellular boundaries.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of AM IN718 following SHT-1 processing. The image highlights a distinct cell-like substructure characterized by lenticular precipitates and δ phase precipitates situated along the intercellular boundaries. These features indicate the formation of specific precipitate scales that mark the cell boundaries within the material.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of as-synthesized Pt2Zn nanocrystals.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy imaging displays the morphology of the as-synthesized Pt2Zn nanocrystals. This characterization study provides visual evidence of the catalyst structure, serving as a primary structural assessment alongside the PtCu nanocrystals to confirm successful synthesis and particle distribution for subsequent electrochemical or catalytic performance evaluations.

caption: Spectrophotometric absorbance measurements at 405 nm comparing products generated from the MMV ELISA test using p-NPP and p-APP substrates.
summary: Spectrophotometric analysis at 405 nm quantifies the products of the MMV ELISA test. The enzymatic reaction product, p-NP, exhibits a characteristic yellow color, allowing for concentration measurement. Tests performed in 96-well plates with 1 M DEA buffer at pH 9.8 demonstrate the efficacy of using p-NPP and p-APP as substrates.

caption: Load-depth curves derived from the points of maximum nanohardness identified at the interfaces of each sample.
summary: Load-depth curves are presented for the points of maximum nanohardness identified at the interfaces across the samples. These curves characterize the indentation response, providing insight into the mechanical resistance and deformation behavior of the material at the specific locations where the highest hardness values were recorded.

caption: Loss factor (tan delta) curves showing damping performance, where TPU5 exhibits the highest peak value of 1.13 and TPU3 achieves a peak of 0.724 with an effective range from -0.02°C to 49.58°C.
summary: Loss factor curves reveal the damping characteristics of the TPU filaments. TPU5 demonstrates the highest damping peak at 1.13 and the widest temperature range. Additionally, TPU3 shows a damping peak of 0.724, maintaining effective damping performance between -0.02°C and 49.58°C, highlighting the material's suitability for ambient temperature applications.

caption: Normalized reflectivity images of the superalloy surface captured at delay times ranging from 1 ps to 100 ps following laser irradiation.
summary: This panel displays normalized reflectivity images of the superalloy surface across a temporal range of 1 ps to 100 ps post-irradiation. These images illustrate the transient reflectivity behavior, showing that the reflectivity increases and subsequently declines over the observed time interval following the single-pulse laser excitation.

caption: Confocal immunofluorescent imaging of VE-cadherin expression at cell-cell junctions in HUVEC cells cultured on control, solvent-cast, and electrospun nanocellulose composite membranes at days 3 and 21.
summary: Confocal microscopy reveals the expression of VE-cadherin, a critical junctional protein, in HUVEC cells across different substrates. Imaging performed at days 3 and 21 demonstrates the maintenance of endothelial monolayer integrity. These results highlight the spatial distribution of adherent junction molecules when cells interact with various nanocellulose-based composite membrane environments.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining images of EMCN and CD31, highlighting type H vessels as yellowish areas, with quantitative analysis of vessel density relative to the scaffold (S).
summary: Immunofluorescence staining was utilized to visualize type H vessels, identified by the dual expression of EMCN and CD31, which appear as yellowish regions. Quantitative analysis of these vessels provides insight into the vascularization process within the scaffold, with statistical significance indicated by p-values compared to the TI and AHT groups.

caption: TDS-GU spectra of hydrogen calibration standards, plotting hydrogen partial pressure as a function of temperature.
summary: This plot displays typical TDS-GU spectra obtained from the analysis of hydrogen calibration standards. The data represents the measured hydrogen partial pressure against temperature, providing a baseline for quantifying hydrogen content. These spectra are essential for establishing the calibration curves used to determine hydrogen concentrations in subsequent experimental samples.

caption: Electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) map of the impending cracking zone, showing the chemical state of the material prior to fracture.
summary: This EPMA map displays the impending cracking zone, serving as a comparison to the cracked regions. The analysis focuses on the chemical composition near the crack tip, where W/Ta enrichment leads to the formation of deleterious phases. These observations help characterize the material state preceding crack propagation and failure.

caption: SAED pattern of the second phase, indexed to the [021] zone axis of bct X5SiB2.
summary: The SAED pattern obtained from the second phase is indexed to the [021] zone axis of the bct X5SiB2 phase (D81, I4/mcm). This diffraction data confirms the presence of this specific borosilicide phase within the outer layer, contributing to the understanding of the coating's complex phase evolution during high-temperature exposure.

caption: Arrhenius plot of integrated PL intensity for SQD and TQD layers in the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample as a function of inverse temperature.
summary: This Arrhenius plot shows the temperature dependence of integrated PL intensity for SQD and TQD layers in the BL-InAs/GaAs-C sample. Experimental data points, represented by circles and squares, are fitted with solid lines using a thermal activation model to determine key parameters, illustrating the quenching behavior of the photoluminescence over 77–300 K.

caption: Contour representation of XRD data showing structural evolution.
summary: The contour plot illustrates the dynamic transitions observed in XRD patterns. It provides a clear visualization of the structural changes occurring within the La2.5Y0.5MgNi14 alloy throughout the hydrogenation and dehydrogenation processes, highlighting the internal structural shifts as the material transitions between different states of hydrogen content.

caption: Architecture of the SINUMERIK 840D control system, illustrating the integration of two OP TCUs with HMI and MCP units, a PCU with HMI and MCP, and the connected actuators and motors.
summary: This diagram displays the SINUMERIK 840D architecture, highlighting its core components. The system configuration includes two OP TCUs and one PCU, each equipped with HMI and MCP interfaces. These control units are linked to various actuators and motors, demonstrating the interconnected nature of the industrial control system's hardware components.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the architecture of the DRL model.
summary: This panel presents the fundamental framework of the DRL model. It serves as a visual representation of the system architecture, providing a clear overview of the DRL methodology as described in the research. The schematic outlines the structural components and logical flow inherent to the DRL approach.

caption: Molybdenum elemental distribution map of the II-100 (98%) sample surface.
summary: The molybdenum distribution map for the II-100 (98%) sample illustrates the spatial arrangement of molybdenum atoms across the polished surface. This WDS mapping technique confirms the presence and homogeneity of molybdenum, which is a critical component in identifying the single-phase state of the material.

caption: Electron beam trajectory at 10 kV acceleration voltage with 1 A beam current and 0.9/0.3 A coil currents.
summary: This panel illustrates the electron beam trajectory simulated at an acceleration voltage of 10 kV. Maintaining constant beam and coil currents, the visualization demonstrates how the focusing point shifts in response to the acceleration voltage, providing insight into the beam dynamics under these specific experimental parameters.

caption: Representative fluorescence images of F-actin morphology in hBMSCs cultured on 3D-printed hydrogels after 3 days.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of F-actin stained hBMSCs provide a detailed view of cellular morphology after 3 days of culture. These images allow for the observation of actin cytoskeleton organization, which is critical for assessing how the 3D-printed hydrogel scaffolds influence cell shape and structural alignment.

caption: Calculated isopleth section of the Fe-V-Al ternary system at a fixed aluminum concentration of 15 at%, derived from the Wang et al. database.
summary: This CALPHAD-calculated isopleth section for the Fe-V-Al system, with aluminum fixed at 15 at%, illustrates the phase stability regions. The diagram is utilized to analyze solidification behavior, specifically identifying the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds that contribute to hot-cracking during the solidification process from the liquid phase.

caption: Energy absorption versus stress performance map for CG structures.
summary: This plot illustrates the energy absorption (EA) and stress performance for CG structures. By comparing these metrics at the RPL, the visualization identifies critical design regions, specifically distinguishing between the crash absorption zone for high EA requirements and the force-limiting protection zone where minimizing peak load is essential.
