caption: Pole figure representation of the prior austenite grain orientations corresponding to the heat-treated microstructure shown in panel (c).
summary: Representing the crystallographic texture of the heat-treated DED PH15-5 SS, this pole figure is derived from the grain orientation data in panel c. It illustrates the change in grain orientation distribution resulting from the recrystallization process, which produced the refined equiaxed grain structure observed after heat treatment.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) pattern of the material in its initial, as-received condition.
summary: The initial state of the material is characterized by the synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern shown in panel a. This SXRD analysis provides essential structural information regarding the material's phase composition and crystallinity before any further processing or testing, serving as a baseline for the subsequent microstructural investigation of the initial condition.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results obtained at point 1 in the overlap region.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results at point 1 provide localized compositional data for the overlap region. These findings support the broader observation that the wire deposition process maintains consistent elemental composition across the overlap zone, ensuring that the microstructure differences are not driven by chemical variations.

caption: 3D point cloud representation of the cut surface for the vertically quenched plate, measured via CMM using a point-by-point hen-pick method.
summary: This 3D point cloud illustrates the surface profile of a vertically quenched plate measured by CMM. The dataset, acquired through a point-by-point hen-pick method, shows a clean surface profile with minimal outliers at the edges, providing a precise representation of the cut surface geometry for subsequent residual stress distribution analysis.

caption: Detailed high-angle annular dark-field imaging of the modified Hastelloy X alloy, revealing specific microstructural features.
summary: Providing a closer look at the modified Hastelloy X alloy, this HAADF image highlights specific microstructural features. The application of high-angle annular dark-field imaging confirms the structural characteristics of the modified alloy, aligning with the study's overall findings regarding the microstructural analysis of the as-fabricated and modified alloy samples.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) traces comparing the thermal behavior of FEG, DS rods, and PF samples.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry traces for FEG, DS rods, and PF samples are presented to evaluate their thermal characteristics. Analysis using a NETZSCH DSC 404 instrument reveals that the characteristic temperatures across these distinct materials are remarkably similar, indicating consistent thermal behavior despite the different sample forms and processing histories.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of F-actin stained MC3T3-E1 cells cultured on a TC4 substrate, displaying typical multipolar extensions and organized actin filaments.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of cells on the TC4 substrate confirms normal cytoskeletal organization. The cells exhibit characteristic osteoblastic spreading with well-developed actin stress fibers and multipolar extensions, indicating that the TC4 substrate supports healthy cell adhesion and morphology consistent with the control group.

caption: Stability test of the RN30-LR electrode conducted at a constant current density of 0.4 A/cm² over a 100-hour duration.
summary: The stability test confirms the excellent single-cell durability of the RN30-LR electrode during continuous operation at 0.4 A/cm² for 100 hours. This remarkable performance is attributed to the stable and optimized Ni(OH)2/Ni ratio within the electrocatalyst, ensuring consistent electrochemical activity throughout the extended testing period.

caption: Ni K-edge XANES spectra of the catalysts, demonstrating the presence of primary metallic Ni.
summary: Ni K-edge XANES spectra confirm that Ni exists primarily in a metallic state within both Ni II Fe III @NC and Ni II Fe II @NC catalysts. This observation is consistent with XPS data, suggesting that there is likely no significant electron transfer from the Ni to the encapsulating carbon shells.

caption: BSE image and EDS analysis of wear debris on the Al2O3 ball surface after sliding against the T6R_1 disk, identifying the oxide-based nature of the adhered debris.
summary: BSE imaging and EDS analysis of the Al2O3 ball surface after sliding against the T6R_1 disk demonstrate mild wear damage. The analysis confirms that the dark-brown wear debris adhered to the exit side of the scar is oxide-based, consistent with the observed surface morphology.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curve for the as-cast Nb6 alloy during thermal cycling.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curve for the as-cast Nb6 alloy during thermal cycling. This DSC chart, obtained during the thermal cycling of the alloy, demonstrates a stable transformation behavior. The heating profile provides critical data on the thermal response and phase transformation characteristics of the material under controlled experimental conditions.

caption: Shear cell flowability index plotted against the Hausner Index for various powder materials, including TiAl, IN738, and H282.
summary: This scatter plot evaluates powder flowability by comparing shear cell results with the Hausner Index. While TiAl and IN738 are classified as easy flowing, they exhibited irregular powder distribution during SLM 280 printing, suggesting that the Hausner Index alone may not fully predict processing performance for these specific materials.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the white marked circle in the martensitic matrix shown in panel (a).
summary: The SAED pattern corresponds to the diffraction spots of the martensitic matrix identified in the V2 sample. This diffraction analysis confirms the crystalline nature of the martensite phase observed in the TEM imaging, providing essential crystallographic information regarding the lath structure within the cladding substrate.

caption: BCC_A2 mixing energy of W-Ti alloys as a function of composition, comparing the CALPHAD assessment derived via MCMC with EMTO–CPA calculations and Jonsson’s previous assessment, including a 95% Bayesian credible interval.
summary: This plot displays the BCC_A2 mixing energy for W-Ti alloys, highlighting the fit between the MCMC-based CALPHAD assessment and EMTO–CPA data. The inclusion of a 95% Bayesian credible interval provides an uncertainty estimate for the model, which shows a clear minimum that influences the common tangent construction between HCP_A3 and BCC_A2 phases.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map derived from EBSD analysis of LPBF-manufactured 15–5PH stainless steel.
summary: This inverse pole figure map provides a crystallographic orientation analysis of the LPBF-manufactured 15–5PH stainless steel sample. Obtained through EBSD characterization, the map serves as the foundational experimental data for subsequent microstructure reconstruction and numerical modeling, illustrating the grain structure and orientation distribution within the additively manufactured material.

caption: Elongation at break percentages for MoldJet 316L and diverse manufacturing methods plotted against relative density to illustrate ductility variations.
summary: This plot displays the elongation at break versus relative density for dense 316L samples. By comparing MoldJet 316L with conventional, MIM, and various AM techniques, the chart illustrates the balance between ductility and densification, providing a comprehensive overview of mechanical performance across different processing routes for 316L stainless steel.

caption: Normalized AESEC dissolution profiles and open circuit potential variations for Al-3at.%Cu during acid pickling and subsequent Zr-conversion coating processes.
summary: This panel displays normalized AESEC dissolution profiles and corresponding open circuit potential variations for Al-3at.%Cu. The data tracks electrochemical behavior during nitro-sulfuro-ferric acid pickling and subsequent Zr-conversion coating on both bare and benchtop acid-pickled surfaces, providing a comprehensive view of the surface treatment kinetics and potential evolution over time.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the longitudinal section of an in-situ TiB reinforcement, showing growth along the [010] axis.
summary: Longitudinal section imaging of the in-situ TiB reinforcement demonstrates that the phase grows preferentially along the [010] axis. This structural orientation provides insight into the growth kinetics and morphology of the TiB reinforcements formed in-situ within the titanium matrix.

caption: Systematic flowchart illustrating the sequential steps involved in the slurry preparation process.
summary: This flowchart provides a comprehensive overview of the slurry processing methodology. It outlines the specific sequence of operations required to prepare the slurry, serving as a visual guide for the experimental procedure described in the study. The diagram clarifies the workflow and ensures reproducibility of the material preparation steps.

caption: Test confusion matrix for the ResPHN-type2 model, illustrating the classification accuracy across all classes.
summary: ResPHN-type2 model classification performance is depicted in this confusion matrix, with true labels on the y-axis and predicted labels on the x-axis. Similar to the ResPFSN-type1 model, this architecture demonstrates varied accuracy values across the different classes, providing insight into its specific strengths and weaknesses in label prediction.

caption: Randomly packed circle structure generated for the dataset, displayed as a 128 × 128 pixel image.
summary: This panel displays a 128 × 128 pixel image representing a structure of randomly packed circles. This geometry is part of a generated dataset designed to cover a wide range of porosities, which helps in effectively capturing the full spectrum of thermal conductivities for the study.

caption: Main effects plot from Taguchi analysis for PEKK, displaying parameter rankings and red-marked optimal levels that correspond to the highest signal-to-noise ratios.
summary: Main effects plot from Taguchi analysis for PEKK displays parameter rankings and red-marked optimal levels that correspond to the highest signal-to-noise ratios. Consistent with the PEEK results, the parameter levels that achieved the greatest signal-to-noise ratios align with the conditions observed in the highest performing specimen group.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots comparing conventional and as-fabricated samples processed at 375 W and 200 mm/s with varying hatch spacing in sodium chloride solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots for conventional and LPBF-fabricated samples reveal electrochemical behavior in sodium chloride solution. All curves demonstrate a negative slope before reaching a potential of -0.2 V, indicating p-type semiconductor behavior prior to the passivation region. These plots characterize the electronic properties of the samples under different hatch spacing conditions.

caption: Storage and loss modulus evolution for 50 wt% Al2O3 composite resin during UV curing.
summary: DMA analysis for 50 wt% Al2O3 composite resin shows the modulus response during UV curing. The storage modulus decreases as the concentration increases to this level, suggesting that higher Al2O3 loading negatively impacts the mechanical properties of the cured composite resin compared to the lower concentration samples.

caption: Thematic evolution map of research trends in the AM-CFRC field, generated via Bibliometrix, illustrating the progression and fragmentation of topics such as continuous natural fiber reinforcements and pre-impregnated filament development.
summary: This thematic evolution map, generated using Bibliometrix, visualizes the research trajectory within the AM-CFRC field. It highlights the fragmentation of additive manufacturing into diverse composite development topics, specifically tracking the emergence of continuous natural fiber reinforcements, pre-preg filaments, and FFF-in-situ impregnation techniques as significant research areas by 2023.

caption: V-notch impact toughness comparison between as-built and hot-isostatic pressed (HIP) material states.
summary: This panel displays the V-notch impact toughness results for the material in both as-built and hot-isostatic pressed conditions. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the energy absorption capabilities of the specimens, highlighting the influence of the hot-isostatic pressing process on the overall impact toughness of the tested material.

caption: Multifractal spectra and corresponding spatio-temporal diagrams for simulated strain rates of 10^-5, 10^-3, and 10^-2 s^-1.
summary: Multifractal spectra are presented for simulated spatio-temporal diagrams across three distinct strain rates. The insets display the underlying spatio-temporal patterns used for the computation. Analysis reveals that the width of the multifractal spectrum narrows as the strain rate increases, effectively characterizing the transition from CB to A band-types.

caption: Dynamic response–recovery curve of the sensor exposed to 5 ppm NO2 concentration.
summary: The dynamic response–recovery curve demonstrates the sensor's performance when exposed to 5 ppm NO2 concentrations. This testing confirms the sensor's ability to detect and recover from gas exposure, validating the functional efficacy of the integrated conformal NO2 gas sensor developed through the proposed HAM fabrication technology.

caption: Intermediate-magnification cross-sectional view of a PETG-CF filament post-tensile test, highlighting fiber morphology.
summary: Intermediate-magnification imaging of the PETG-CF filament cross-section post-tensile test reveals the internal structure of the composite. Observations indicate that PETG-CF exhibits significantly longer fibers compared to PLA-CF samples. The presence of voids remains a critical feature, contributing to the stress concentrations observed during the mechanical failure process.

caption: Raman spectra highlighting the vibrational signatures of the manganese-doped whitlockite powder.
summary: Raman spectra of the scaffolds exhibit similar trends across all groups, featuring consistent characteristic peaks associated with Si–O–Si, Ca–O, and Mg–O bonds. These results confirm that the incorporation of Mn2+ ions does not induce significant structural changes within the strontium-magnesium whitlockite lattice.

caption: Arrhenius plots showing the natural logarithm of the diffusion-limited current density (ln jd) versus the reciprocal of absolute temperature (1/T) for all tested electrodes.
summary: Arrhenius plots are constructed by plotting the natural logarithm of the diffusion-limited current density against the reciprocal of the absolute temperature for all tested electrodes. This graphical representation allows for the determination of the apparent activation energy for the hydrogen peroxide reduction reaction based on the temperature-dependent chronoamperometric data.

caption: Atomic stress contour map within the (1 1 1) slip plane of a screw dislocation at 1100 K with 17 at.% Re, exhibiting Interaction Mode I.
summary: This atomic stress contour map at 1100 K and 17 at.% Re displays Interaction Mode I characteristics. A pronounced tensile stress band forms ahead of the screw dislocation along the slip plane as it approaches the phase interface, with prominent stress concentration zones visible near the dislocation core.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the C-R3-DA condition, illustrating the arrangement of turquoise γʹ and brown γʹʹ precipitates through Nb and (Al + Ti) iso-surfaces.
summary: This APT reconstruction of the C-R3-DA condition highlights the morphology of γʹ and γʹʹ precipitates using Nb and (Al + Ti) iso-surfaces. The 3D dataset provides a clear view of the precipitate distribution, facilitating the analysis of phase morphology and structural characteristics within the material under this specific processing condition.

caption: XRD patterns of as-crushed and spheroidized Ni-32.4Si powders, showing characteristic peaks for NiSi, Ni3Si2, and NiSi2 phases compared against crystallographic reference data.
summary: This panel displays the XRD patterns for as-crushed and spheroidized Ni-32.4Si powders. Analysis of these patterns, in conjunction with EDS data, confirms the presence of specific nickel silicide phases, namely NiSi, Ni3Si2, and NiSi2. These results provide a structural characterization of the powders following different processing conditions.

caption: Arrangement of substitutional atoms is shown occupying high-symmetry positions in the lattice.
summary: Arrangement of substitutional atoms is shown occupying high-symmetry positions in the lattice. This model is one of several used in the calculations, providing a clear visualization of the atomic placement that defines the structural parameters for the subsequent computational analysis of the material's properties.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the as-printed beta-type Ti alloy with TO structure after fatigue testing, showing regions of the omega phase marked by white dash contours.
summary: This high-resolution TEM image displays the microstructure of an as-printed beta-type Ti alloy following fatigue testing. The presence of the omega phase is highlighted by white dash contours, illustrating the microstructural evolution and emergence of this phase within the beta-type matrix as a result of the applied fatigue loading.

caption: Loss factor curves obtained from Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) for TPU7/PLA3 filaments printed with varying infill patterns.
summary: Loss factor curves derived from DMA testing demonstrate that 3D printed TPU7/PLA3 samples exhibit improved damping peaks and expanded effective damping temperature ranges compared to injection molded counterparts. While these performance metrics show enhancement, the glass transition temperature (Tg) remains consistent across the different infill patterns and manufacturing methods.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of as-deposited IN738 clearly resolving the γ′ particles.
summary: Utilizing dark-field TEM imaging, this panel clearly resolves the γ′ particles that were otherwise indistinguishable in the bright-field mode. This technique effectively highlights the distribution and morphology of the strengthening precipitates within the as-deposited IN738 matrix, confirming their presence and size range at the nanoscale.

caption: Atomic concentration profile of Si across a grain boundary located within the gamma matrix phase.
summary: This line graph illustrates the atomic concentration profile of Si across a grain boundary situated within the gamma matrix. The data, derived from a broader dataset of alloy compositions, characterizes the segregation behavior of Si at this specific interface following wrought processing and aging heat treatments.

caption: Eddy current scan of Sample C, illustrating the detection of tungsten inserts and balls within the WAAM specimen.
summary: The eddy current scan provides an alternative inspection modality for Sample C. This panel captures the spatial distribution of tungsten inserts and balls, serving as a complementary dataset to the ultrasonic scan. It highlights the challenges of interpreting complex defect geometries within the WAAM material during the scanning process.

caption: Microstructure of the 100 L sample in the building direction, displaying irregular cracks and complex features including N-doping, transition, and free N layers with acicular structures and flower-like precipitates.
summary: The 100 L sample exhibits irregular cracks and distinct layers, including N-doping, transition, and free N zones. Acicular structures appear in the free N layer, while supersaturated nitrogen leads to flower-like precipitates and thicker TiN clusters, contrasting significantly with the simpler morphologies observed in the 10 and 10 L samples.

caption: Equilibrium molecular dynamics snapshot of the F3 network, showing the largest percolated cluster in gray and various smaller clusters in color, reflecting a more fragmented network structure.
summary: This molecular dynamics snapshot shows the F3 network at equilibrium, with the largest percolated cluster in gray and smaller clusters in color. The visual evidence of more fragmented clusters supports the quantitative finding of a pronounced discrepancy between total and effective conversion, indicating a less efficient network formation process.

caption: Cumulative thermal expansion rates of Fe-Ni alloys plotted as a function of temperature during heating and cooling cycles.
summary: This plot illustrates the cumulative thermal expansion rates for Fe-Ni alloys, calculated as the ratio of length change to room temperature length. The data provides a quantitative representation of material expansion behavior across varying temperatures, serving as a fundamental characterization of the alloy's thermal response during heating and cooling processes.

caption: SEM image of LPBF-NiTi alloy precipitates after annealing at 600 ℃ for 1 h.
summary: Displayed is the SEM image of LPBF-NiTi alloy annealed at 600 ℃ for 1 h. This visualization is critical for assessing the impact of higher annealing temperatures on the alloy's microstructure, specifically focusing on the size and distribution of precipitates formed during this short-duration high-temperature treatment.

caption: Compressive stress-strain behavior of single-material 17–4PH and 316L OCT lattices, highlighting the sequential local fracture and crushing of the 17–4PH lattice.
summary: Compressive stress-strain curves for single-material 17–4PH and 316L OCT lattices are presented. The 17–4PH lattice exhibits a distinct mechanical response characterized by a sequential series of local fracture and crushing events, which leads to a significant reduction in stress following the initial peak yield point.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized epoxy vinyl resin, acquired using deuterated acetone as the solvent to characterize the chemical structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of the epoxy vinyl resin is presented, providing detailed structural information about the synthesized material. The analysis was conducted using deuterated acetone as the solvent, allowing for the identification of chemical shifts associated with the molecular structure of the epoxy vinyl resin.

caption: Comparative UV-Vis absorption spectra of the contact lenses subjected to different post-processing techniques.
summary: This panel presents a comparison of absorption spectra for contact lenses treated with various post-processing techniques. The data highlights how different post-fabrication methods influence the optical properties and the final state of the gold nanoparticles embedded within the hydrogel matrix, allowing for the selection of the most effective processing route.

caption: Fitness curve for scenario 3, displaying error trends across input values ranging from 0 to 5 at 0.5 intervals.
summary: Scenario 3 fitness analysis is presented, showcasing the application of the ANN-BLMA approach. The plot visualizes error trends across input values from 0 to 5 at 0.5 intervals, providing a clear representation of the network's performance and convergence behavior within this specific critical scenario for the artificial backpropagation network.

caption: EXAFS χ(r) spectrum of Y, displaying characteristic features that exhibit similar structural characteristics to the Co and Ni spectra, despite quantitative differences in peak height and sharpness.
summary: The EXAFS χ(r) spectrum for Y is presented, showing structural characteristics that parallel those observed in the Co and Ni spectra. Although the Y spectrum exhibits similar overall features, it displays quantitative variations in the height and sharpness of the peaks compared to the Co and Ni K-edge data.

caption: Tafel plots comparing the Ni-Cr system across 0.5 M H2SO4, 0.5 M KOH, and 0.5 M NaCl electrolyte solutions.
summary: This panel displays Tafel curves for the Ni-Cr system in various electrolytes, including H2SO4, KOH, and NaCl. These electrochemical measurements characterize the corrosion behavior of the Ni-Cr coating, which demonstrates moderate resistance in NaCl with an Ecorr of -0.08 V and a jcorr of 0.795 µA cm-2.

caption: Violin plots illustrating the distribution of Q scores for four distinct laser powder bed fusion energy density conditions, ranging from high energy (Case 1: 370 W, 250 mm/s) to low energy (Case 4: 150 W, 1200 mm/s).
summary: This figure displays violin plots of Q scores across four printing conditions defined by varying laser power and scan speed. The analysis demonstrates that the proposed machine learning pipeline maintains generally high prediction quality, although higher energy density cases, such as Case 1, may correlate with slightly lower prediction accuracy.

caption: Live/dead assay images and quantitative viability analysis of BMSCs seeded for 3 days on TCPs, 3D-LDN/Exos, and 3D-CBD@LDN/Exos scaffolds.
summary: Live/Dead assays demonstrate high cell viability of BMSCs cultured on both 3D-CBD@LDN/Exos and 3D-LDN/Exos scaffolds. Representative images display live cells in green and dead cells in red, showing that cytotoxicity levels are comparable to those observed on control TCPS surfaces, confirming the biocompatibility of the fabricated scaffolds.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map and inverse pole figure of the as-built 316L stainless steel sample subjected to conventional shot peening (CSP) in a transversal section.
summary: This panel displays the KAM results and inverse pole figure for the CSP-treated SLM 316L sample. The visualization highlights the microstructural state following plastic deformation, illustrating the grain orientation and dislocation distribution within the transversal section of the as-built material after the conventional shot peening process.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology of the molten pool generated by the simulation of Model C-2.
summary: This 3D reconstruction shows the molten pool morphology for Model C-2. Compared to Model C-1, this model exhibits a larger high-temperature zone exceeding 2800 °C and an increased molten pool length of 320 μm, indicating that the model parameters significantly enhance the thermal dimensions of the pool.

caption: GOS map of the Cu-FeNi36 region following continuous dynamic recrystallization, where recrystallized grains are depicted in blue and are distinctly separated by high-angle grain boundaries, contrasting with the substructure observed in the strain-hardened state.
summary: This panel displays the microstructure of Cu-FeNi36 after undergoing continuous dynamic recrystallization. Recrystallized grains, shown in blue, are delineated by high-angle grain boundaries. This structural evolution, coupled with GOS mapping, supports the conclusion that the material undergoes continuous dynamic recrystallization during the cold rolling process.

caption: Magnetization curves of MnAl and MnAl-C alloys quenched at 950 °C, illustrating the magnetic response to varying external magnetic fields.
summary: This plot displays the magnetic behavior of MnAl and MnAl-C alloys quenched at 950 °C by showing the change in magnetization as a function of the applied magnetic field. The data reveals that carbon doping leads to an enhanced saturation magnetization compared to the undoped MnAl alloy sample.

caption: Full-scale FEA model of the square lattice structure illustrating loading and boundary conditions, necessitated by the loss of symmetry during buckling.
summary: The FEA model of the S-U design is shown in Fig. 3a. This full-scale simulation captures the square lattice structure's deformation behavior, specifically accounting for the loss of symmetry that occurs at the onset of buckling, which prevents the use of reduced-order models for this specific geometry.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing hydrogen diffusivity parallel to the Σ5{100} grain boundary in Fe-Ni-Cr alloy, where diffusion aligns with iso-composition planes.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates hydrogen diffusion parallel to the Σ5{100} grain boundary in a Fe-Ni-Cr system. The data demonstrates that when diffusion occurs along iso-composition planes, composition nonuniformity does not significantly influence the diffusivity, indicating that grain boundaries in this orientation do not impede hydrogen transport as expected.

caption: Maximum resolved shear stress distribution around hole No. 1 under varying blowing ratios, highlighting the influence of temperature fields on peak stress values.
summary: This panel displays the maximum resolved shear stress around hole No. 1. Analysis indicates that peak stress values are significantly lower at a blowing ratio of 1.5 compared to 0.5 and 1.0, primarily due to elevated temperatures on the acute side of the hole affecting the local stress state.

caption: Critical strain for the onset of the Portevin-Le Chatelier (PLC) effect as a function of strain rate, derived from DIC analysis, showing both normal and inverse behaviors.
summary: Critical strain values for the onset of the PLC effect in AA5182 are plotted against strain rate using DIC analysis. The data, represented by black squares for individual tests and a red mean line, reveal both normal and inverse strain-rate dependencies, corresponding to the onset of strain localization into PLC bands.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) for Ru-Ni, showing the downshift of Ni-3d and Ru-4d states relative to bulk references due to orbital hybridization.
summary: The d-orbital PDOS comparison indicates that Ni-3d states downshift below bulk FCC Ni levels due to repulsion with overlapping Ru-4d orbitals, weakening Ni-O and Ni-H bonding. Additionally, Ru-4d states, particularly the 4d-eg component above the Fermi level, show a downshift compared to hex-Ru metal, regardless of local symmetry variations.

caption: Thermal state of the sample immediately prior to the next recoating step, characterized by a transition to an orange glow as the layer cools.
summary: Captured just before the deposition of the subsequent layer, this image shows the sample cooling from its peak exposure temperature to an orange glow. This cooling phase occurs within the 10-second interval between layers, highlighting the persistent heat accumulation characteristic of the single-part build condition for this tensile bar.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry profile of as-received un-milled copper powder.
summary: This panel displays the differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) response for the as-received, un-milled copper powder. The profile provides baseline thermal data for the initial state of the material, serving as a reference point for comparing the thermal behavior of the copper powder after undergoing 20 hours of mechanical milling.

caption: Frontal 3D rendering of the β-TCP bone implant region of interest, scanned at a 1 μm voxel resolution, highlighting the presence of large pores situated between two concentric outer layers.
summary: This 3D rendering displays a frontal view of the β-TCP bone implant region of interest, captured via high-resolution micro-CT at a 1 μm voxel size. The visualization clearly reveals the internal architecture, specifically identifying larger pores located between the two concentric outer layers of the implant structure.

caption: Manganese elemental distribution maps showing the spatial arrangement of Mn in the as-received and CGPed Al 3105 alloy.
summary: Manganese elemental mappings reveal the distribution of manganese across the Al 3105 alloy microstructure. These maps identify specific regions where Al6(Fe,Mn) and alpha-Al(Fe,Mn)-Si phases have precipitated, enabling an assessment of how manganese distribution changes between the as-received and CGPed states.

caption: Atomic model of the unit cell where a Cr atom occupies the 6c1 site, with Ni atoms at 3a and 18h positions and Mo atoms filling the remaining sites.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the unit cell configuration used for DFT calculations, specifically highlighting the 6c1 site occupied by a Cr atom. Ni atoms are positioned at 3a and 18h sites, while Mo atoms occupy the remaining lattice positions, providing a structural basis for comparing Cr and Mo substitution preferences.

caption: Average hardness (H) and Young's modulus (E) values measured across the Ni56Ti44–Ni56Ti22Al22 diffusion couple, reflecting the mechanical properties resulting from the compositional gradient.
summary: This panel illustrates the average hardness and Young's modulus of the Ni56Ti44–Ni56Ti22Al22 diffusion couple. These mechanical properties are plotted to show how the material's resistance to deformation and its elastic response vary across the interdiffusion zone, directly correlating with the compositional changes induced by the two-step annealing treatment.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of SAC305 solder joints featuring varying paste volumes applied to an OSP surface finish.
summary: Scanning electron microscopy image of SAC305 solder joints featuring varying paste volumes applied to an OSP surface finish. This image depicts the specific joint morphology associated with OSP surface finishes, allowing for a direct comparison of how different paste volumes influence the final structure of the SAC305 solder joints.

caption: Three-dimensional confocal reconstruction of the blood vessel model immunostained with Alexa Fluor 568 phalloidin.
summary: This 3D confocal image reveals the structure of the blood vessel model after labeling the cytoskeleton with Alexa Fluor 568 phalloidin. The visualization confirms the successful formation of the microvessel structure, providing a detailed view of the lumen and the spatial arrangement of the adhered HUVEC cells.

caption: Surface deformation contour map of the back plate tested with a 2.90 mm ABS equivalent cover plate.
summary: Represented here is the back plate deformation profile resulting from a ballistic impact test using a 2.90 mm ABS equivalent cover plate. Laser scans with 0.3 mm accuracy were performed to map the contour, allowing for a direct comparison of the deformation characteristics against other cover plate configurations.

caption: Intensity distribution of 3-spot triangle RPVBs with a constant topological charge (l=3) comparing power orders of n=5 and n=10.
summary: Investigating the influence of the power order n on multiple spatial arbitrary distribution RPVBs reveals that the 0-th ring’s light intensity gradually concentrates towards the optical axis as n increases. This concentration effect is consistent with observations in other configurations, demonstrating the predictable modulation of intensity profiles through power order adjustments.

caption: Temperature-dependent CTE profile for the W3 specimen containing 15.57 wt% Ni, highlighting differences between horizontal and vertical extraction planes.
summary: This panel displays the coefficient of thermal expansion for the W3 specimen, which features a 15.57 wt% nickel composition. By plotting the CTE against temperature for both horizontal and vertical sample orientations, the figure demonstrates how the thermal expansion characteristics evolve at this specific mixing ratio within the FGM interface.

caption: Bacterial colony formation of S. aureus on the surface of as-fabricated 316L-4.5Cu antibacterial stainless steel.
summary: Presented in this panel are the bacterial colonies of S. aureus formed on the 316L-4.5Cu antibacterial stainless steel. The image provides visual evidence of the material's antibacterial activity against this specific strain, demonstrating a significant inhibition of colony development compared to the control stainless steel surface under identical experimental conditions.

caption: Chronoamperometric response of WAAM 316L stainless steel polarized at four distinct passive film formation potentials in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: WAAM 316L stainless steel shows a marked reduction in passive current density during a 600-second polarization period across four different potentials. The formation of a stable passive layer is observed, though the specimen exhibits a higher steady-state current density of 335 nA/cm2 compared to the wrought counterpart.

caption: Variation of Ni content in wt% and Faradaic current efficiency as a function of deposition conditions for Zn-Ni plating.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the Ni content in wt% and the Faradaic current efficiency during Zn-Ni plating. The Faradaic efficiency is calculated as the ratio of the sum of Zn and Ni partial current densities to the total measured current density, providing insight into the electrochemical deposition process.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the USGP6 sample at the uppermost surface, exhibiting an ultrafine grain structure resulting from the interaction between twins and dislocations.
summary: This bright-field TEM image of the uppermost surface of the USGP6 sample displays an ultrafine grain structure. This refined microstructure is attributed to the cumulative interaction between twins and dislocations, demonstrating the significant grain refinement achieved at the surface due to the treatment process.

caption: Statistical analysis of the average depth and width of keyholes observed under different laser power conditions.
summary: Statistical analysis of the average depth and width of keyholes. This plot provides a quantitative assessment of keyhole geometry, illustrating how different laser power settings impact the depth and width dimensions, which are critical parameters for understanding the stability and formation of keyholes during laser processing.

caption: Orientation distribution map of the gamma phase in the XOZ plane for the non-UHFP TiAl-4822 sample.
summary: This panel displays the orientation distribution map of the gamma phase within the XOZ plane of an as-fabricated TiAl-4822 sample processed without ultrasonic excitation. The map provides a visual representation of the crystallographic orientation distribution, serving as a baseline for comparing the microstructural effects of the UHFP treatment.

caption: Temperature-dependent free energy profiles for alloy B, showing the disordered BCC solid solution (black), B2 ordered compound (blue), and primary dendrite phase (red) from 300 K to 1800 K.
summary: Panel b presents the calculated free energy for alloy B, comparing the disordered BCC solid solution, B2 ordered compound, and primary dendrite phase across the 300 K to 1800 K temperature range. These curves highlight the thermodynamic relationships between the different phases as a function of temperature for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Scatter plot of the first versus second principal component scores derived from 2D SAS patterns for Cases 1–4.
summary: This scatter plot displays the first versus second principal component scores for four distinct cases. The distribution of data points in this principal component space demonstrates that each case is uniquely identifiable, illustrating the effectiveness of PCA in differentiating between the various 2D SAS patterns analyzed in the study.

caption: Continuous creep curves for MCSS [11-2](111) at a constant stress of 300 MPa across varying temperatures of 730, 750, and 780 °C.
summary: Continuous creep curves are presented for the MCSS [11-2](111) specimen maintained at a constant stress of 300 MPa. The plot demonstrates the temperature sensitivity of the creep process by comparing deformation results obtained at 730, 750, and 780 °C, highlighting the influence of thermal activation on creep rates.

caption: Debris cloud morphology for the Nextel AF-10 configuration, showing experimental and numerical results at 7 km/s (6 μs) and 3 km/s (20 μs) post-impact.
summary: Nextel AF-10 debris cloud morphology is presented through both experimental and numerical simulation data. The comparison highlights the structural evolution of the debris at 7 km/s and 3 km/s. The numerical simulations generally align with experimental findings, capturing the key characteristics of the debris cloud for this specific configuration.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the MC carbide, demonstrating its crystalline nature.
summary: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the MC carbide, demonstrating its crystalline nature. This diffraction data serves as critical evidence to confirm the identity of the second phase as MC carbide, supporting the structural analysis presented in the research findings regarding the material's phase composition and crystalline characteristics.

caption: Vickers hardness (HV) evolution plotted against exposure time for static (black lines) and dynamic (orange and red lines) conditions at temperatures ranging from 450 to 600 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the Vickers hardness evolution under static and dynamic conditions at temperatures between 450 and 600 °C. Dynamic precipitation of α-Ti3Al during creep at 500 °C significantly accelerates the aging peak compared to static conditions, reducing the time required to reach peak hardness from 128 hours to 1 hour.

caption: Comparison of ohmic-corrected EIS responses for STF0, STF-2, and STF-5 anodes at 750 °C under a low H2 partial pressure of 0.097 atm.
summary: At a low H2 partial pressure of 0.097 atm and 750 °C, the EIS results for STF-based anodes show a dominant response at 1–3 Hz. The data indicates that the total resistance increases as the H2 partial pressure decreases, with STF0 demonstrating that higher B-site deficiency negatively impacts electrochemical performance.

caption: Bode phase plot of the Zr–2.5Nb alloy, showing the phase angle variation across the tested frequency range in SBF.
summary: Representing the phase angle response of the Zr–2.5Nb alloy in SBF, this Bode phase plot is part of the EIS test results obtained under stable OCP conditions. It serves as a critical component for analyzing the corrosion behavior and validating the equivalent circuit model used for the alloy.

caption: Thermal compression diagram for the Ti6Al4V-SiCw composite material.
summary: This panel illustrates the thermal compression diagram for the Ti6Al4V-SiCw composite. The inclusion of SiCw reinforcements alters the material's deformation characteristics compared to the base alloy. This diagram captures the specific thermal compression response, reflecting how the composite structure influences the flow stress and overall mechanical behavior during deformation.

caption: Load versus slip curve at the loaded end for a CFRP-to-steel joint with a brittle adhesive and a bond length of 50 mm, illustrating the accuracy of the FDM model.
summary: Representing the mechanical response of a CFRP-to-steel joint with a 50 mm bond length, this plot illustrates the load-slip curve at the loaded end. The data confirms the precision of the proposed FDM in capturing the joint's behavior when utilizing a brittle adhesive during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Stress-strain curve representing the mechanical performance of the primitive uniform structure.
summary: The stress-strain curve for the primitive uniform structure illustrates its specific mechanical response under load. This data is part of a broader comparative study of TPMS lattices, highlighting the unique deformation behavior and structural strength associated with the primitive geometry compared to other tested lattice types.

caption: Thermo-mechanical response of spark plasma sintered sample 4, displaying ΔL (μm) versus temperature and the associated hysteresis effect under bending mode.
summary: Thermo-mechanical response of spark plasma sintered sample 4, displaying ΔL (μm) versus temperature and the associated hysteresis effect under bending mode. This panel illustrates the displacement as a function of temperature for multiple cycles, providing evidence of the hysteresis effect observed in the spark plasma sintered sample during testing.

caption: Maximum magnetic flux density values recorded in Clearance 2 using a Hall probe.
summary: Measured using a Hall probe, the maximum magnetic flux density in Clearance 2 is presented to validate simulation results. These experimental values confirm the magnetic performance trends observed in the computational model, demonstrating the accuracy of the simulation in predicting the magnetic flux density within the specified clearance region.

caption: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles of the hybrid device measured at different current densities between 1 and 30 mA·cm⁻² within a 0–1.4 V potential window.
summary: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles of the hybrid device measured at different current densities between 1 and 30 mA·cm⁻² within a 0–1.4 V potential window. These profiles illustrate the charge storage behavior of the ASC device under varying current loads, confirming its operational stability within the specified potential range.

caption: Ashby plot displaying flexural properties of 10-layer Biomid-PLA and Cordenka-PLA composites, evaluated alongside a reference dataset of various additively manufactured continuous and short fiber-reinforced PLA composites.
summary: Flexural properties of 10-layer Biomid-PLA and Cordenka-PLA composites are presented in this Ashby plot. The visualization incorporates a wide range of literature data for additively manufactured continuous glass, aramid, carbon, and short cellulose fiber-reinforced PLA, allowing for a direct comparative assessment of the flexural performance of the studied natural fiber composites.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of nickel-coated 3D-printed electrodes (Ni1x, Ni2x, Ni3x, and Ni4x) measured in 1 mol KOH solution.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms illustrate the electrochemical behavior of four nickel-coated 3D-printed electrodes, labeled Ni1x through Ni4x, tested in a 1 mol KOH electrolyte. These measurements characterize the electrochemical response of the varying nickel deposition levels, with observations indicating similar current density profiles among the Ni1x, Ni2x, and Ni3x samples.

caption: Quantified austenite percentage plotted against the scan position relative to the fracture surface for the AB, AR 3, and ARA 2 specimens.
summary: Austenite percentage is quantified as a function of position relative to the fracture surface for the AB, AR 3, and ARA 2 specimens. The resulting line graph demonstrates the variation in phase content from the fracture vicinity to regions further away, illustrating the extent of transformation across different experimental conditions.

caption: ODF intensity distribution profiles along the fibers defined by φ1 = 0°, Φ = 35°, φ2 and φ1 = 180°, Φ = 35°, φ2.
summary: Intensity distributions along the fibers, corresponding to the dashed lines marked in panel c, are illustrated here. These profiles provide a clear view of how the ODF intensity evolves along the fiber paths, supporting the comprehensive analysis of texture components and their distribution within the studied material sample.

caption: Fluorescence intensity at 590 nm for three samples: unconjugated MP-NPs (sample 1), unconjugated MP-NPs with free AlexaFluor568-streptavidin (sample 2), and biofunctionalized MP-NPs with assembled AlexaFluor568-streptavidin (sample 3).
summary: Fluorescence intensity measurements reveal a significant 10-fold signal increase for sample 3, where the probe is molecularly assembled on biotinylated MP-NPs, compared to samples 1 and 2. This confirms the effective assembly of the fluorescent probe on the bioconjugated MP-NPs, yielding a much higher signal than control conditions.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of the as-cast B30–2Fe sample, displaying the spatial distribution of constituent elements.
summary: This EDS mapping provides a visual representation of the elemental distribution within the as-cast B30–2Fe sample. The results illustrate how the constituent elements, specifically Cu, Ni, and Fe, are organized spatially, providing critical insight into the compositional homogeneity and phase distribution characteristic of this specific alloy composition.

caption: Load-displacement response for a DCB joint with a W 1/2 sinusoidal interface.
summary: This panel displays the numerically obtained load-displacement response for a DCB joint featuring a W 1/2 sinusoidal interface. The plot illustrates the mechanical behavior of the joint under loading conditions, providing a quantitative assessment of the structural response as a function of the specific interface geometry defined by the aspect ratio.

caption: Evolution of the CMA optimization score over 100 runs in the Rene 65 dataset, showing the mean score as a dark blue line with light blue shading representing the minimum and maximum values across iterations.
summary: The optimization process demonstrates high precision and repeatability, with an average similarity score of 0.9353 across 100 runs. The dark blue curve illustrates the mean score evolution throughout the iterations, while the light blue shading indicates the range between minimum and maximum values, confirming the stability of the CMA optimization.

caption: Absorption spectra characterizing the gold nanoparticle solutions used in the study.
summary: This plot presents the absorption spectra for the gold nanoparticle solutions. These measurements serve as a reference to characterize the optical response of the gold nanoparticles, which are generated during the in situ reduction process within the hydrogel contact lenses.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the average number of 1st nearest neighbor (NN) vacancy pairs in pure Ni and various Ni-Fe-Cr ternary alloys.
summary: This panel illustrates the average number of 1st NN vacancy pairs as a function of MD time. The data shows that vacancy accumulation increases with higher Cr concentration in the ternary systems. This trend is attributed to enhanced vacancy migration induced by the presence of Cr atoms within the alloy matrix.

caption: EDS composition profile across the Al0.3CoCrFeNi alloy sintered at 1100 °C, demonstrating consistent elemental distribution between micrometric and nanometric grains.
summary: This EDS profile analysis of the 1100 °C sintered Al0.3CoCrFeNi alloy reveals that the chemical composition remains uniform when transitioning from micrometric to nanometric grains. This observation indicates that the observed micrometric grains are the result of grain growth processes rather than phase transitions occurring during the sintering treatment.

caption: Contour map depicting the predicted MSAD values across the FCC single-phase composition space, with color gradients representing the magnitude of MSAD.
summary: This contour map visualizes the predicted MSAD values across the FCC single-phase composition space. The color scale indicates a gradual increase in MSAD from blue to red. Observations confirm that MSAD values generally increase in response to higher concentrations of Cr and Mo within the specified alloy composition range.

caption: Pareto chart of standardized effects for relative density (RD) in the PBD analysis of Cu–Cr–Zr alloy.
summary: This Pareto chart displays the standardized effects of process parameters on the relative density of the Cu–Cr–Zr alloy. According to ANOVA results, the specific energy of skin-exposure is identified as the most significant parameter influencing RD, providing critical insight into the optimization of the LPBF process parameters.

caption: Random Forest (RF) model confusion matrix evaluated on the unseen test set.
summary: The Random Forest model's performance on the unseen test set is visualized through a confusion matrix. This matrix provides a detailed breakdown of the classification accuracy, illustrating the distribution of predicted versus actual labels to assess the model's predictive capability and identify potential misclassifications within the unseen dataset.

caption: Intermediate loading stage illustrating the progressive development of symmetric atomic displacement patterns around the advancing indenter.
summary: Representing the intermediate loading stage, this panel illustrates the atomic displacement vector map. As the loading force increases, atomic displacements within the sample gradually exhibit a conspicuous symmetry relative to the advancing indenter. The direction of arrows denotes atomic motion, and color intensity represents the magnitude of the displacement.

caption: Computer-aided design rendering of the in-situ preparation instrumentation, highlighting the functional levels for transport in purple and modification in pink.
summary: This CAD model illustrates the in-situ preparation instrumentation design. The system is divided into two distinct functional levels: a transport level shown in purple and a modification level shown in pink. This setup facilitates the integration of various experimental components for material processing within the vacuum environment.

caption: Raman spectrum of multilayer WS2 islands, identifying the 2LA(M), E2 2g, 2LA(M) + E1 2g, and A1g vibrational modes, with a frequency difference of 71 cm-1 between the characteristic modes.
summary: The Raman spectrum confirms the multilayer thickness of the WS2 islands. A large frequency difference of approximately 71 cm-1 between the 2LA(M) + E1 2g and A1g modes, combined with a low 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio of 0.69, provides definitive spectroscopic evidence of the multilayer structure.

caption: Schematic representation of the band gap structure for g-C3N4 and the modified catalyst variants.
summary: The band gap structure diagram illustrates the relative energy levels of the valence and conduction bands for the g-C3N4 and modified catalysts. This visualization helps in understanding the charge carrier dynamics and the alignment of energy levels, which are critical for the photocatalytic performance of the materials.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for 1% w/v paracetamol-loaded 10% w/v PLGA microparticles.
summary: This histogram displays the particle size distribution for the paracetamol-loaded PLGA microparticles. It allows for a quantitative assessment of how the incorporation of the model drug affects the size profile of the microparticles compared to the blank control, confirming the consistency of the spray drying production process.

caption: Trypsin fluorescence emission profiles measured at 308 K with SL/trypsin mass ratios between 0 and 0.8 g/L, highlighting the progressive intensity decline.
summary: Measurements taken at 308 K demonstrate that the peak fluorescence intensity of trypsin at 327 nm decreases gradually with higher concentrations of SL. This trend of fluorescence quenching is consistent with the behavior observed at other temperatures, reflecting the interaction between the protein and the added SL.

caption: Elemental distribution map of W highlighting the WC particle core and its surrounding carbide structures.
summary: This tungsten distribution map clearly delineates the WC particle. The surrounding regions exhibit blocky and cross-flower-shaped carbide morphologies, which are characteristic of the reaction products formed at the interface between the WC particle and the surrounding molten pool during the cladding solidification process.

caption: Initial time-resolved snapshot of dislocation movement within a channel in 0.5 dpa heavy ion-irradiated 316L stainless steel at 288°C, showing early-stage pinning interactions.
summary: This initial snapshot captures dislocation channeling in irradiated 316L stainless steel at 288°C. Radiation-induced defects significantly pin dislocation motion, resulting in heavily tangled and jerky dislocation lines. The observation highlights the pinning-overcome-pinning mechanism that leads to significant stress localization within the material during the straining process.

caption: Regional intensity map detailing the density of FDM-related scientific literature contributions by country.
summary: Representing the density of scientific literature, this regional intensity map identifies the primary countries contributing to FDM research. Based on Web of Science data, the visualization complements the global distribution analysis, offering a clear perspective on the geographic concentration of scholarly output and research engagement in this additive manufacturing domain.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra showing the reduction of 4-NP catalyzed by W-type Pd/C CR, demonstrating the highest reduction rate among the tested reactor types.
summary: This panel shows the UV-Vis spectra for the reduction of 4-NP using a W-type Pd/C reactor. Analysis of these spectra indicates that the W-type catalyst achieves a greater reduction rate for 4-NP compared to the U-type and L-type reactors, as confirmed by subsequent conversion versus time data.

caption: Filament winder setup used for the collection of extruded composite materials.
summary: This panel illustrates the filament winder component of the extrusion system. It serves as the primary mechanism for collecting the composite filaments after they have been processed, providing a clear view of the experimental setup used to manage the continuous production of the filament materials during the manufacturing process.

caption: Strain-temperature curves derived from isostress heating experiments performed under various constant stress levels.
summary: Panel f depicts strain-temperature curves obtained from isostress heating tests conducted at different constant stress levels. These curves illustrate how varying stress influences the thermal transformation behavior of the NiTi wire, serving as a key dataset for determining the critical conditions for deformation and transformation processes shown in panel e.

caption: Bode and phase angle plots for 95-6h coated AA2024 aluminium alloy after 1, 24, and 168 hours of immersion in 0.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 °C.
summary: Bode and phase angle plots characterize the 95-6h coated AA2024 aluminium alloy during immersion in 0.5 wt.% NaCl solution. As noted in the study, this specific coating condition was found to be less protective compared to the parental Zn-Al LDH coating over the 168-hour testing period.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) patterns comparing Aged-T50 and WQ-T50 LRHEAs, confirming a BCC crystal structure for both processing conditions.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns for T50 LRHEAs reveal that both the water-quenched and aged samples maintain a BCC crystal structure. These patterns confirm the phase stability of the alloy following recrystallization at 973 K or aging at 573 K for 7 days, providing a baseline for structural analysis.

caption: Imaginary part of the complex dielectric function (ε2) as a function of wavelength for np-S samples with different average ligament sizes.
summary: This plot displays the imaginary part of the dielectric permittivity for dealloyed films derived from ellipsometry measurements. The data illustrates the optical response of nanoporous silver samples with varying ligament sizes, providing a comprehensive view of the dielectric characteristics across the measured wavelength range compared to a solid silver comparator.

caption: Measured coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) values for A- through E-X unit cell structures compared against their respective simulation results, represented by dashed lines of matching colors.
summary: This panel displays the measured coefficient of thermal expansion for various X-unit cell structures (A-E) alongside their corresponding simulation predictions. The data highlights discrepancies between experimental measurements and simulated values, noting that CTE jumps in the measured cells do not necessarily align with the intensity or frequency predicted by simulations.

caption: 1D in-situ synchrotron diffraction profiles for the HZ25 alloy, fitted with B19' and B2 lattice structures.
summary: 1D in-situ diffraction profiles for the HZ25 alloy are shown, with data successfully fitted to the expected B19' and B2 lattice structures using GSASII software. These profiles track the structural evolution of the alloy, confirming the presence and transformation of these specific phases during the in-situ thermal experiment.

caption: Detailed TKD map of the region shown in (a) after precision ion polishing, displaying the Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) relative to the vertical loading direction and the estimated angle Ω between the c-axis and loading axis.
summary: Following precision ion polishing, this high-resolution 40 nm step size TKD map reveals the crystallographic orientation of grains. The IPF highlights the c-axis alignment relative to the loading direction, denoted by Ω. Three grains marked with asterisks were specifically analyzed for Schmid factors to investigate the presence of tensile-twinning.

caption: FTIR spectra of gaseous pyrolysis products released from native and flame-retardant-treated flax yarns at peak absorbance during thermal degradation.
summary: This panel displays the FTIR spectra of gaseous pyrolysis products for native and flame-retardant-treated flax yarns. The data, captured at peak absorbance during thermal degradation under a nitrogen atmosphere, illustrates the chemical evolution of gaseous species released from the flax fibers as they undergo thermal decomposition during the TGA-FTIR analysis.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the HCr-2 alloy annealed at 900 °C for 256 h, showing the γ-γ′ interface delineated by a 6 at.% Al isosurface with Co (blue) and Ta (pink) ions.
summary: Representing the HCr-2 alloy microstructure after 256 h of annealing at 900 °C, this 3D reconstruction utilizes a 6 at.% Al isosurface to delineate the γ-γ′ interface. The spatial arrangement of Co (blue) and Ta (pink) ions illustrates the specific microstructural characteristics of the HCr-2 alloy under these conditions.

caption: Optical morphology of the BOT plane showing surface corrosion pits after 5 minutes of exposure to molten ADC12 aluminum alloy.
summary: Optical morphology of the BOT plane reveals the surface state after 5 minutes of corrosion in molten ADC12 aluminum alloy. Corrosion pits are observed to be concentrated in the RZ and MPZ regions near the HAZ, providing a baseline for evaluating the surface degradation of the H13 steel specimen.

caption: Distribution of maximum wall values derived from a finite element method (FEM) simulative campaign.
summary: This plot displays the maximum wall values obtained through a finite element method simulative campaign. The observed dispersion of these values underscores the significant impact of the tool path on the achievable part accuracy, highlighting how variations in simulation parameters directly influence the final structural outcomes of the modeled components.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the integrated deuterium (D) retention values as a function of reciprocal temperature, derived from the release data presented in Figure 9.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the relationship between integrated deuterium retention and reciprocal temperature. By utilizing release data from Figure 9, the graph provides a quantitative representation of how D retention behaves across varying thermal conditions, offering insights into the temperature-dependent release mechanisms of the material under investigation.

caption: Partial radial distribution function gAl-Cu(r) for Al50Cu25Ni25 melt at 1400 K, comparing AIMD (solid blue) and DNNP (red dashed) results.
summary: The partial radial distribution function gAl-Cu(r) for the Al50Cu25Ni25 melt at 1400 K is displayed. This plot compares the structural data derived from AIMD simulations, represented by solid blue lines, against the predictions from DNNP simulations, shown as red dashed lines, to validate the accuracy of the machine learning potential.

caption: Comparison of ultimate tensile strength versus elongation to failure for HX materials from the present study against literature values reported in references 8, 9, 19, 35, and 39.
summary: This plot compares the ultimate tensile strength and tensile elongation to failure of the HX materials synthesized in this study against various literature results. By mapping these key mechanical parameters, the figure contextualizes the performance of the fabricated HX alloys relative to previously reported data from multiple research sources.

caption: DSC curves comparing the thermal behavior of the three SLM Ti–Ni sample types, highlighting variations in phase transformation characteristics.
summary: Panel b presents the DSC curves for the three types of SLM Ti–Ni samples. These curves are used to analyze the thermal behavior and phase transformation characteristics of the materials, showing that the phase transformation temperatures of Ms and As decrease following the HIP treatment process.

caption: Precipitation temperature ranges for mineral phases modeled under Scheil-Gulliver cooling conditions, showing the metal phase as the initial crystallizing component and augite as the first silicate phase to precipitate.
summary: Modeled using Scheil-Gulliver cooling, this panel illustrates the precipitation temperature ranges for various mineral phases. The metal phase initiates crystallization first, followed by augite, which removes CaO from the melt. This model suggests a silicate liquidus temperature of at least 1220°C, consistent with geothermometry estimates and observed silicate-metal contact textures.

caption: EDS elemental map showing the distribution of Aluminum (Al) in the HIP + STA specimen.
summary: Aluminum distribution within the HIP + STA specimen is visualized through this EDS elemental map. The map highlights the spatial arrangement of Al, which is a key constituent of the γ' phase (Ni3(Ti, Al)) distributed within the grains, providing insight into the chemical homogeneity of the processed alloy.

caption: Schematic representation of tie-lined alloys within a pseudo-binary phase diagram, illustrating the equilibrium compositions of individual phases at specific temperatures.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram illustrates the concept of tie-lined alloys, which are equilibrium alloys fabricated with individual phases. The diagram highlights the importance of considering the temperature dependence of equilibrium compositions when analyzing elastic misfit between phases at elevated temperatures, even beyond the temperatures where these specific tie-lined alloys are defined.

caption: Atomic model of the (Cr, Re)23C6 crystal structure in (001) projection, highlighting Rhenium substitution at the Cr3 (32f) site.
summary: Depicting the (Cr, Re)23C6 crystal structure, this model shows Rhenium atoms occupying the Cr3 (32f) site within the (001) projection. This configuration is used to generate the simulated HAADF-STEM image shown in panel (i) to analyze the effect of site-specific Rhenium occupation.

caption: Time-series plot of measured cutting forces, highlighting specific data points p1, p2, and v1 alongside the defined 0.65 s time window Tw.
summary: Measured cutting forces are displayed as a function of time, identifying critical data points p1, p2, and v1. A time window Tw of 0.65 s is applied to these measurements, facilitating the extraction of force data required for subsequent harmonic analysis and process modeling within the proposed method.

caption: Uncorrected mean Raman spectra of HCT 20% filament in blue and HCT 20% in DMSO in red, displaying raw spectral data prior to alignment.
summary: This panel presents the raw mean Raman spectra for HCT 20% filament and HCT 20% in DMSO before any correction. These spectra serve as the baseline data, illustrating the initial spectral alignment prior to the application of SG, ALS, and EMSC preprocessing techniques to address the liquid-to-solid phase change shift.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the BM-Ti-25V–15Cr specimen showing α/β-Ti grains located near β-Ti grain boundaries, including marked SAED positions and elemental distribution maps obtained via EDS.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field imaging highlights the distribution of α/β-Ti grains near the β-Ti grain boundaries in the solution-treated alloy. The inclusion of EDS elemental mapping and SAED site markers provides a detailed view of the local chemical and structural environment, confirming α-Ti grain precipitation at the grain boundaries.

caption: Reconstructed 3D surface profiles of ground adherends obtained from laser scanning data.
summary: Reconstructed 3D surface profiles of ground adherends are presented, providing a detailed visualization of the surface topography. These profiles are derived from the laser scanning process, which follows established industrial standards to ensure measurement accuracy. The resulting 3D data allows for the quantitative assessment of the adherend surface roughness characteristics.

caption: Full-pattern neutron diffractogram for the third HIP-treated condition, highlighting the structural response to increased HIP processing intensity.
summary: This diffraction pattern for the third HIP-treated condition illustrates the structural state of the material under specific processing parameters. It is part of a sequence of neutron powder diffraction measurements designed to provide global, volume-averaged phase information, complementing localized microscopy results to characterize the microstructural changes induced by HIP treatment.

caption: Arrhenius plots illustrating hydrogen diffusivity as a function of inverse temperature for three uniform alloys: Fe0.50Ni0.40Cr0.10, Fe0.50Ni0.10Cr0.40, and Fe0.70Ni0.11Cr0.19.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays hydrogen diffusivity for three distinct uniform alloys. Analysis reveals that while these compositions share similar activation energy barriers ranging from 0.62 to 0.65 eV, they exhibit notable differences in their pre-exponential factors, which are calculated as 80.56, 61.53, and 67.48 Å²/ps, respectively.

caption: Ternary composition plot for the Al-Cu-Ni system displaying training dataset compositions as blue bullets, with associated AIMD configuration counts, and testing compositions as red bullets used for evaluating DNNP transferability.
summary: This ternary diagram illustrates the Al-Cu-Ni system's training dataset, where blue bullets represent included compositions and their respective AIMD configuration counts. Red bullets denote testing compositions selected for their distance from training points to assess the compositional transferability of the DNNP model, ensuring robust evaluation of the machine learning framework.

caption: Hot processing map for WAAMed NiTi alloy at a true strain of 0.3, displaying regions of flow instability as gray shaded areas.
summary: This hot processing map for WAAMed NiTi alloy at a true strain of 0.3 illustrates the relationship between processing parameters. The gray shaded area represents the flow instability region, which is primarily concentrated in the high strain rate regime, providing critical data for optimizing the alloy's thermomechanical processing conditions.

caption: Thermomagnetic ZFC and FC curves for annealed (FC773) Mn2FeSn samples measured at 80 kA/m, including an inset for 800 kA/m field conditions.
summary: Annealed Mn2FeSn samples show distinct magnetic properties compared to the as-cast state. At 80 kA/m, the ZFC curve exhibits significantly lower magnetization at low temperatures, indicating a stronger ferrimagnetic phase. The inset confirms a paramagnetic-to-ferromagnetic transition at 800 kA/m, highlighting the sensitivity of magnetic properties to thermal treatment.

caption: Hysteresis cycles of the material after heat treatment at 1200 °C, measured at varying frequencies.
summary: This plot displays the magnetic hysteresis behavior of the material following a 1200 °C heat treatment. The data, acquired using LabVIEW software and a National Instruments data acquisition card, illustrates how the hysteresis cycles evolve across different frequencies, providing insight into the material's magnetic response under varying operational conditions.

caption: Pole figure plot corresponding to the building direction (BD) sample, illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution at 20% engineering strain.
summary: This pole figure plot provides a quantitative representation of the crystallographic orientation distribution for the sample strained to 20% in the building direction. It serves as a critical diagnostic tool for understanding the texture development and preferred grain orientations resulting from the applied mechanical deformation.

caption: Asymmetrical PDI-Mw-φ diagram illustrating the sol-gel transition boundaries for A200/PPG dispersions at volume fractions of 0.029, 0.044, and 0.064.
summary: This diagram maps the colloidal sol-to-gel transition region for A200/PPG dispersions as a function of polydispersity index (PDI), molecular weight (Mw), and volume fraction (φ). The curves represent the mixing behavior of bimodal PPG oligomers, while symbols denote the gelation region, which occurs within specific ranges of the PDI-Mw mixing curve.

caption: Surface topography of the Ni–Mo–W coating electrodeposited at a current density of 20 mA/cm2.
summary: Surface topography of the Ni–Mo–W coating electrodeposited at a current density of 20 mA/cm2. This AFM image illustrates the initial surface morphology of the coating formed at the lowest current density, highlighting the structural features and roughness characteristics resulting from the specific electrodeposition parameters applied during the synthesis process.

caption: Bright field TEM image and SAED pattern of Ti46.8Ni33.6Hf19.6 thin film annealed at 600 °C, showing relatively blurred grain boundaries.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging of the Ti46.8Ni33.6Hf19.6 thin film annealed at 600 °C reveals a microstructure characterized by relatively blurred grain boundaries. The corresponding SAED pattern provides structural information for the sample processed at this lower annealing temperature, highlighting the initial state of the material's grain development.

caption: Electronic band structure calculated for the BK-Si2O layered material.
summary: Electronic band structure calculated for the BK-Si2O layered material. This plot details the energy dispersion characteristics of the BK-Si2O phase. By examining this band structure alongside other Family-II materials, the study establishes the electronic framework for these Si2O-based layered systems, facilitating a comparative analysis of their fundamental physical properties.

caption: Validation of manufacturing parameters including speed, hatch distance, and power in the build direction, represented with ± 3 σ confidence intervals derived from Monte-Carlo simulations.
summary: This plot validates manufacturing parameters such as speed, hatch distance, and power along the build direction. Using Monte-Carlo simulations, 1000 estimates of the response variable Y were generated to calculate deviations from actual values. The results are presented with ± 3 σ confidence intervals to quantify the reliability of these parameters.

caption: EDS spectrum of the bright phase identified as MC carbides within the microstructure.
summary: Displaying the EDS spectrum of the bright phase, this panel provides chemical evidence for the presence of MC carbides. Comparison with the cell interior area confirms that these bright features are indeed carbides, which formed from the liquid phase during the high-temperature processing of the IN738LC superalloy.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and EELS chemical composition maps of PtNi/g-CN, showing the distribution of Ni (red, 855 eV) and Pt (green, 2122 eV) within the selected square area.
summary: EELS chemical composition mapping of the PtNi/g-CN sample provides a visual representation of the elemental distribution. The maps confirm the presence and spatial arrangement of Ni (L 2,3-edge at 855 eV) and Pt (M 4,5-edge at 2122 eV) within the analyzed red squared area of the HAADF-STEM image.

caption: Longitudinal section showing the general morphology of internal creep cracks in the IP-TMF specimen.
summary: Longitudinal sectioning reveals the overall morphology of internal creep cracks within the IP-TMF specimen. This overview provides the necessary context for characterizing the crack details, serving as the primary observation point for identifying the spatial distribution and progression of damage within the material under the applied mechanical load.

caption: Ashby map comparing yield strength (YS) against elongation for the alloys specified in Table 4.
summary: This Ashby map illustrates the mechanical performance of the alloys listed in Table 4 by plotting yield strength against elongation. The visualization serves to benchmark the materials, providing a clear comparison of their ductility and strength characteristics as reported in the study to support the overall material evaluation.

caption: Evaluation of the NN model using unseen data, representing cases not exposed to the model during the training phase for particle velocity and occurrence.
summary: Panel c evaluates the NN model's performance on unseen data, specifically cases not exposed to the model during training for particle average velocity and occurrence. The plot includes horizontal red dashed lines indicating calculated critical and erosion velocities, serving as a benchmark for the model's predictive capability on entirely new datasets.

caption: Temperature ramp DMA test showing the tan delta curve and storage modulus profile used to identify the glass transition temperature.
summary: This DMA temperature ramp test characterizes the viscoelastic behavior of the material. By analyzing the storage modulus profile and the tan delta curve, the glass transition temperature (Tg) is determined to be approximately 65°C, providing critical insight into the thermal transition properties of the specimen under investigation.

caption: Reflection spectra of opal films prepared via the melt-shear technique, comparing CSP4 to CSP1 and CSP3.1, with corresponding film colors shown as circles.
summary: Reflection spectra are used to characterize opal films prepared using the melt-shear technique. The spectrum of CSP4 is compared against previously prepared films made of CSP1 and CSP3.1. The visual color of each opal film is represented by circles, illustrating the optical properties resulting from the different particle compositions.

caption: Tessellated TPMS unit cells exhibiting trigonal and hexagonal symmetry, prepared for additive manufacturing and subsequent mechanical testing.
summary: This figure displays a collection of TPMS unit cells characterized by trigonal and hexagonal symmetries. These structures are designed for additive manufacturing and are intended to be tessellated in R³ to form larger cell arrays, which are then subjected to mechanical testing to evaluate their structural performance and material properties.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of scaffold surfaces at days 3 and 7, where green calcein-AM staining represents live cells and red propidium iodide staining represents dead cells.
