summary: Live/dead viability staining provides direct visualization of cellular survival on the scaffold surfaces. Quantitative analysis shows that the live/dead ratio consistently exceeds 95% across all groups and conditions, confirming the excellent biocompatibility of the scaffold formulations and the absence of cytotoxic effects from both materials and the ultrasound stimulation.

caption: Reflectance RL curves showing the simultaneous optimization of multiple absorption peaks for L8 GMSs.
summary: L8 GMSs enable the simultaneous optimization of one to three absorption peaks as shown in this panel. This result further demonstrates the effectiveness of the customized method proposed in this work for absorption peak tailoring, highlighting the capability to manipulate multiple peaks within the L8 gradient structure.

caption: Stress-strain relationship for a triangular infill Cu sample indicated by dashed lines.
summary: Illustrated here is the stress-strain curve for a copper sample featuring a triangular infill geometry. The mechanical performance is represented by dashed lines, which delineate the link between applied stress and resulting strain. This plot highlights the specific mechanical characteristics associated with the triangular infill design.

caption: Viscous parameters of the Burgers model for solid lignin, plotted with gray points for specific indentation depths, red points for depth-averaged values, and a green line indicating the universal lignin parameter average.
summary: Panel b illustrates the viscous parameters of the Burgers model for solid lignin. The plot includes gray points for specific indentation depths and red points for the average across these depths. A horizontal green line represents the universal viscoelastic properties of solid lignin, calculated by averaging all parameters and indentation depths.

caption: Raman spectra of carbon materials synthesized over various catalysts, displaying characteristic D, G, and G' peaks with intensities dependent on catalyst temperature.
summary: This Raman spectroscopy analysis of carbon materials reveals the presence of D, G, and G' peaks. The relative intensities of these peaks vary with catalyst temperature. Specifically, the weaker Raman signal observed at 900 °C suggests the formation of carbon nanofibers, which typically exhibit broader spectral features than nanotubes.

caption: Atomic snapshot of the alloy at 850 K, illustrating the emergence of B2-ordered NiAl-rich regions within the disordered matrix.
summary: Equilibration at 850 K results in the formation of localized NiAl-rich regions characterized by B2 order embedded in a disordered matrix. This temperature corresponds to the regime between the first and second ordering reactions, marking the transition from a homogeneous A2 configuration toward a B2 + A2 phase field.

caption: Cycling performance curves of the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film electrode over 300 cycles at a discharge current density of 14 A g-1.
summary: Cycling curves for the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film electrode over 300 cycles at a higher discharge current density of 14 A g-1 are shown. This panel highlights the material's performance and stability under more demanding high-rate conditions, confirming its suitability for applications requiring rapid charge and discharge capabilities.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image showing the fine, equiaxed sub-grain structures within the copper grains.
summary: This TEM image reveals the internal structure of the copper grains, which exhibit a significant quantity of fine, equiaxed sub-grain features. These sub-grains are characterized by particle sizes not exceeding 100 nm, demonstrating the refined microstructure achieved in the copper phase of the W-20Cu composite processed at 1200W.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) patterns of as-printed bulk samples across various processing conditions, with line colors indicating specific parameter sets.
summary: This figure displays the SXRD patterns for as-printed bulk samples, where consistent line colors represent identical processing parameters. Analysis of these diffraction spectra confirms that the addition of B4C does not induce the formation of new phases, as both alloys maintain a predominantly γ-f.c.c. dual-phase microstructure in the as-printed state.

caption: Optical micrograph of the outer surface of an LPBF-ed sample showing oxidation and corrosion pits after 500 thermal cycles.
summary: Surface oxidation and the formation of numerous corrosion pits are visible in this optical micrograph of an LPBF-ed sample after 500 thermal cycles. Exposure to air during the cycling process leads to the degradation of the surface, which is a precursor to the subsequent crack growth and material failure.

caption: Dilatometry measurements of length change versus temperature for WQ, T10, T20, and T3h alloy samples, illustrating the shift in martensitic transformation temperatures.
summary: Dilatometry measurements for WQ, T10, T20, and T3h alloys reveal the impact of ageing on martensitic transformation. The martensitic start temperature (Ms) shifts from -6 °C for the water-quenched sample to -21 °C and -96 °C for aged samples T10 and T20, respectively, while magnetic ordering transitions remain undetected by this technique.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the cross-section near the fracture surface following tensile deformation at 750 °C.
summary: Captured from the cross-section near the fracture surface after tensile deformation at 750 °C, this inverse pole figure map displays the grain orientation distribution. Thermal etching grooves are present within the grains, indicating the microstructural response to the elevated temperature and mechanical stress during the tensile deformation process.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells cultured on various scaffolds, stained with phalloidin to visualize the cytoskeleton in red and nuclei in blue.
summary: Cell morphology on different scaffolds is visualized using fluorescence microscopy with phalloidin staining. The cytoskeleton is highlighted in red, while the nuclei are stained blue. This imaging technique allows for the observation of cell attachment and structural organization on the scaffold surfaces, providing insights into the cellular response to the materials.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of SLM-processed IN718 in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, demonstrating enhanced passive behavior and the absence of pitting potential at elevated temperatures.
summary: SLM-processed IN718 samples exhibit superior passive behavior in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution compared to cast samples. The faster solidification during SLM suppresses niobium segregation, preventing film breakdown. Consequently, no pitting potential (Epit) is observed at 50 and 80 °C, reflecting more uniform oxide layers and reduced porosity in the material.

caption: Design of the toughness predictor ResNet, which integrates configuration data and the stress field output from the feature generator to estimate the final toughness of the composite material.
summary: The toughness predictor is a ResNet-based model that functions as the second stage of the hierarchical DNN. It concatenates the original configuration data with the stress field data generated by the first model to estimate the toughness of the composite material, completing the hierarchical prediction process.

caption: Scatter plot displaying the first versus second principal component scores for Cases 1–4, demonstrating distinct clustering of SAS patterns in the reduced-dimensional space.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the distribution of SAS patterns across Cases 1–4 by plotting the first principal component score against the second. The distinct separation of data points in this principal component space confirms that the PCA effectively differentiates between the various microstructural datasets analyzed in the study.

caption: Correlation plot of predicted versus experimental bead width (w) values, with a dashed red line indicating ideal parity.
summary: Bead width predictions are validated against experimental data in this parity plot. The alignment of data points along the 1:1 reference line, supported by R² and error metrics, indicates that the model exhibits high predictive accuracy for bead width, consistent with the overall validation results for all target variables.

caption: EBSD pole figure representing the crystallographic orientation distribution in area A of the as-deposited specimen.
summary: Area A exhibits a weak texture strength with a maximum pole density within the range of 1.451 to 2.258. The EBSD pole figure indicates that the building blocks fail to achieve an optimal orientation, resulting in nearly isotropic characteristics within the crystal structure of this specific region.

caption: Optical micrograph of the Ang0 building strategy showing broad, banded melt pools characterized by a homogeneous cellular structure.
summary: The Ang0 strategy microstructure is visualized via optical microscopy, revealing broad, banded melt pools. These features exhibit a homogeneous cellular structure throughout the observed area. The melt pool boundaries are clearly delineated by red lines, providing a clear representation of the solidification morphology resulting from this specific scanning strategy.

caption: Schematic representation of the active cooling configuration for an oval specimen, featuring an array of compressed air nozzles positioned along one side to facilitate cooling between successive layer depositions.
summary: This schematic illustrates the active cooling setup implemented for oval specimens during the printing process. Compressed air is delivered via an array of nozzles positioned along one side of the oval, providing controlled cooling after each layer is completed and before the subsequent layer is deposited on the steel substrate.

caption: Corrosion current density (Icorr) trends measured over varying immersion times for three samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Corrosion current density (Icorr) values are presented for three samples across different immersion times in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Obtained through Tafel curve fitting, these measurements quantify the rate of corrosion, allowing for a comparative analysis of the electrochemical degradation kinetics among the tested material specimens.

caption: Atomic force microscopy surface morphology of the ST + AT sample, illustrating the topographical features of the precipitates within the matrix.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image captures the surface morphology of the ST + AT sample. The visualization provides a detailed topographical view of the precipitates embedded within the matrix, serving as the basis for subsequent SKPFM analysis to determine the electrochemical potential differences between these features and the surrounding material.

caption: Full-pattern neutron powder diffractogram of the HIP-2 treated specimen, demonstrating the structural state of the material after the second HIP processing condition.
summary: Representing the HIP-2 condition, this diffractogram is part of the series used to monitor phase evolution. It provides volume-averaged microstructural data, allowing for a global assessment of the material's phase stability and the progressive reduction of secondary phases as the intensity of the HIP processing increases.

caption: Ray trajectories and heat distribution within the keyhole at 1286 μs, showing high-energy red rays impacting the front wall bottom and multiple reflections at the tail and rear wall.
summary: At 1286 μs, the simulation reveals ray trajectories and heat distribution within the keyhole. A bundle of high-energy red rays directly strikes the bottom of the front wall, causing localized heat concentration. Simultaneously, multiple reflections occur at the keyhole tail and the upper section of the rear wall.

caption: Prediction confusion matrix for the model evaluated with missing values present in the dataset.
summary: This confusion matrix displays the model's predictive performance when missing values are included in the dataset. It serves as a visual tool to evaluate how the model handles incomplete data during the classification process, allowing for a direct comparison of predictive accuracy against the model trained without missing values.

caption: Dark field STEM micrograph of the 1210HIP specimen illustrating the deformation substructure associated with coarser secondary gamma-prime precipitates.
summary: This dark field STEM micrograph reveals the deformation substructure of the 1210HIP specimen following thermal treatment. The image captures the presence of coarser secondary gamma-prime precipitates. These features demonstrate the strengthening mechanism where dislocations interact with the precipitates, providing insight into the material's response to deformation under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Polarization curves displayed in semi-logarithmic coordinates for the samples tested in Ringer’s solution.
summary: This panel presents the electrochemical behavior of the tested samples in Ringer’s solution. The data is visualized through polarization curves plotted in semi-logarithmic coordinates, commonly referred to as Tafel curves. These plots are essential for evaluating the corrosion resistance and electrochemical kinetics of the materials under these specific physiological conditions.

caption: Desired layer height profile for the WP3 demonstrator represented in WP-coordinates (αWP, zWP).
summary: This contour plot illustrates the desired layer height profile for the complex WP3 demonstrator using WP-coordinates. The map assigns a corrected height to each point on the workpiece for star-convex geometries, showing a desired layer height of approximately 0.5 mm for the central section, with variations in converging and diverging regions.

caption: Temperature field distribution on the cross-section of the rear part during the final layer deposition with a heat input of 900 J/mm.
summary: This panel displays the simulated temperature field on a cross-section of the rear part during the final layer deposition process. With a heat input of 900 J/mm, the thermal profile illustrates the localized heat distribution, providing insight into the thermal history and potential microstructural evolution during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Potentiostatic polarization curve of the WAAMed specimen measured at 0.40 V SCE in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution for 1500 s.
summary: The WAAMed specimen displays a potentiostatic polarization curve characterized by a large number of anodic current spikes when subjected to 0.40 V SCE in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution for 1500 s. These frequent current transients indicate significant metastable pitting activity occurring throughout the duration of the electrochemical test.

caption: Evolution of the single-task glistening segmentation loss during training (blue) and validation (orange) for a baseline configuration with 90-10 weights and a 20-pixel radius.
summary: This learning curve illustrates the training and validation loss progression for a single-task glistening segmentation model. Using a 90-10 weight distribution and a 20-pixel radius, the plot demonstrates the convergence behavior of the model. This specific case serves as a representative example for all considered training scenarios in the study.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) profile for the 3D printed composite, confirming the elemental composition of the printed part.
summary: The EDS spectrum for the 3D-printed composite confirms the elemental composition of the final printed part. By comparing this profile with the filament's EDS data, the analysis verifies that the chemical integrity of the composite is maintained throughout the 3D printing process, confirming the successful incorporation of the fillers.

caption: Lattice strain profile of the {311} plane along the vertical centerline for the inter-pass rolled specimen.
summary: This panel illustrates the {311} lattice strain profile along the vertical centerline of the inter-pass rolled specimen. The measurement highlights how the inter-pass rolling process modifies the internal strain state of the material, providing insight into the effectiveness of this mechanical treatment in altering the residual stress profile.

caption: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Linear_HT1 specimen showing the distribution of γ′ precipitates and the grain boundary (GB) region.
summary: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Linear_HT1 specimen reveals the spatial distribution of γ′ precipitates and the grain boundary region. This visualization provides a detailed look at the microstructure of the EPBF INC738 alloy, specifically focusing on the characteristics of the γ/γ HAGBs following the specified heat treatment.

caption: Bode diagrams showing the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for TC4 base metal and TC4 weld metal in 3 wt% H2SO4 solution.
summary: Bode diagrams demonstrate that TC4 base metal maintains higher low-frequency impedance and a maximum phase angle near 90° compared to the weld metal's 67°. These results confirm that the base metal forms a more stable passivation film, providing enhanced corrosion resistance in the simulated flue gas environment.

caption: Bright field TEM image illustrating the FCC/BCC two-phase distribution with high-density tangled dislocations in the FCC phase and fewer dislocations in the BCC phase, including an inset SAED pattern.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging reveals the microstructural distribution of the FCC and BCC phases. Observations indicate that the FCC phase contains a high density of tangled dislocations, whereas the BCC phase exhibits significantly fewer dislocations. An inset SAED pattern provides crystallographic confirmation of the two-phase structure within the deformed material.

caption: Corrosion current density of 316L stainless steel samples measured in quiescent and ultrasonic cavitation conditions across various solutions.
summary: This plot displays the corrosion current density of 316L stainless steel in stagnant and ultrasonic cavitation environments. Data indicates that the corrosion rate in stagnant solutions increases with SDS addition due to higher water conductivity, while the reduced corrosion rate under cavitation suggests complex interactions beyond simple SDS effects.

caption: Reconstructed 3D model of Ti–20Nb–6Ta displaying the detected internal porosity.
summary: This 3D model of Ti–20Nb–6Ta, derived from CT imaging, maps the internal defect population. The analysis shows that the material contains only a few pores, with maximum sizes up to 0.005 mm³. These results contribute to the overall observation that optimized processing achieves high relative densities across all materials.

caption: Equation of state for HCP Ni polymorph calculated using ReaxFF NiAl-S22, compared against DFT, ReaxFF-2012, EAM-2009, and EAM-2012 potentials, with an inset showing the atomic structure.
summary: The equation of state for HCP Ni is modeled using the ReaxFF NiAl-S22 potential and compared to DFT and literature-reported potentials. This calculation, which includes an atomic structure inset, serves as a benchmark for evaluating the accuracy of the new potential against established EAM and ReaxFF methods.

caption: Oxygen Reduction Reaction (ORR) polarization curves for PtNi cp/Gr.C HT900 catalysts subjected to varying HNO3 concentrations during acid leaching, with mass activities at 0.9 V vs RHE shown in the inset.
summary: ORR polarization curves demonstrate the electrochemical performance of PtNi cp/Gr.C HT900 catalysts after acid leaching at different HNO3 concentrations. The anodic scans, performed at 1600 rpm and 20 mV/s, reveal the impact of acid concentration on catalytic activity, with specific mass activity values at 0.9 V vs RHE highlighted.

caption: Surface topography of the as-cast GZ112K alloy obtained via scanning kelvin probe force microscopy.
summary: Surface topography of the as-cast GZ112K alloy is visualized using scanning kelvin probe force microscopy. This image provides the structural baseline for analyzing the secondary phases within the as-cast alloy, which are subsequently characterized by their surface potential maps and Volta potential profiles in the following panels.

caption: Inverse pole figure maps derived from EBSD scans of COM-2024-T3, COM-2024-SS, and FE-2024 studs, illustrating microstructural variations across specific zones including top center, top edge, bottom center, bottom center +6.5 mm, and flash regions.
summary: Inverse pole figure maps visualize the microstructural evolution of COM-2024-T3, COM-2024-SS, and FE-2024 studs following friction surfacing. Scans at the tip of consumed studs, specifically at bottom center positions, reveal significant grain refinement compared to the base material. Black dashed lines delineate the analyzed bottom center regions within the respective maps.

caption: Interaction effects of Prandtl number (Pr), temperature ratio (T), and diameter factor (Df) on the Nusselt number (Nu).
summary: This contour plot illustrates the complex interaction between Prandtl number, temperature ratio, and diameter factor in determining the Nusselt number. As part of a comprehensive sensitivity analysis, the visualization highlights how these influential factors collectively impact heat transfer performance, providing critical insights into the system's optimal operating conditions.

caption: Reflection loss profile for Fe70 composite illustrating the high-loading absorption characteristic.
summary: The Fe70 composite reflection loss profile characterizes the absorption behavior at the highest iron loading level. This panel completes the series, illustrating the trend of absorption enhancement as Fe content increases within the Fe/PLA/TPU composite, providing a comprehensive view of the material's electromagnetic response across varying iron concentrations.

caption: Atomic model representing a non-overlapped twin structure.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the idealized configuration of a non-overlapped twin. It serves as a structural reference for comparing the atomic arrangements found in the experimental HRTEM images, specifically distinguishing the standard twin boundary geometry from the more complex overlapped configurations observed in the QWT-DZ martensite.

caption: XZ-plane cross-sectional view comparing the nominal Pink Gyroid STL model with the grey XCT-scanned STL geometry.
summary: This panel presents an XZ-plane cross-sectional comparison between the nominal Pink Gyroid STL model and the actual grey XCT-scanned geometry. The visualization highlights the structural alignment and potential deviations between the designed CAD model and the fabricated specimen, providing a basis for assessing manufacturing accuracy and structural integrity.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image displaying the morphology of AISI 430L ferritic stainless steel powder particles.
summary: Scanning electron microscopy image displaying the morphology of AISI 430L ferritic stainless steel powder particles. This visualization captures the structural characteristics of the metallic binder phase, illustrating the particle size and surface texture of the stainless steel component intended for the cermet feedstock mixture.

caption: Nyquist curves showing the electrochemical impedance response of HEA coatings and NAB substrate immersed in 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: The Nyquist curves for HEA coatings and NAB substrate are presented, illustrating their electrochemical behavior in a 3.5% NaCl solution. These curves exhibit a semi-circular shape, with the size of the semi-circles varying between the HEA coatings and the NAB substrate, indicating differences in their respective electrochemical impedance characteristics.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of pitting corrosion on SLM 316L stainless steel processed at 800 mm/s after 15 days in Locke's solution.
summary: Confocal imaging of SLM 316L stainless steel processed at 800 mm/s reveals the geometry and depth of corrosion pits following a 15-day exposure to Locke's solution. This technique provides detailed visualization of the surface degradation, allowing for the characterization of pit morphology resulting from the specific laser processing parameters used.

caption: Consolidated heatmaps of {100} pole m.r.d. values across XZ, YZ, and XY planes for scanning strategies ST1–ST4 under LPHD and HPLD processing conditions.
summary: This figure displays consolidated heatmaps representing m.r.d. values for the {100} pole. The data covers all three primary planes (XZ, YZ, and XY) for four distinct scanning strategies (ST1 to ST4). These results are compared across two specific processing conditions, LPHD and HPLD, to evaluate texture variations.

caption: Transmittance absorption curves for glass samples produced via ammonia combustion (TC1–TC4) and an electric furnace, normalized to a standardized thickness of 10.0 mm.
summary: This plot displays the transmittance absorption curves for various glass samples, including those melted by ammonia combustion (TC1 to TC4) and an electric furnace. All data are normalized to a uniform thickness of 10.0 mm to allow for direct comparison of the optical properties across different melting methods.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the 316L/IN718 system, where the abscissa denotes the mass fraction of IN718 ranging from 0.0 (pure 316L) to 1.0 (pure IN718).
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram for the 316L/IN718 system was generated using Thermo-Calc simulations. It employs a dual-database approach, utilizing TCFE12 for the 316L side and TCNI12 for the IN718 side. The diagram maps phase stability across the entire composition range, with the x-axis representing the mass fraction of IN718.

caption: Projection of the (Cr, Re)23C6 carbide unit cell along the [001] direction, illustrating the complete substitution of Re atoms into the Cr2 (8c) lattice sites.
summary: This panel displays the [001] projection of the (Cr, Re)23C6 carbide unit cell. It specifically highlights the structural configuration where Re atoms have fully substituted the Cr atoms at the 8c sites, providing a theoretical model for the carbide structure used in subsequent HAADF-STEM image simulations.

caption: Temperature-programmed reduction (TPR) profiles monitoring the m/z 18 signal for catalysts synthesized via 390 s of electrodeposition, recorded under a 5% H2/Ar atmosphere with a 10 °C/min heating rate.
summary: This TPR profile, obtained under a 5% H2/Ar gas mixture at a heating rate of 10 °C/min, tracks the m/z 18 signal to characterize the reduction behavior of catalysts prepared by 390 s of electrodeposition. The results provide essential insights into the thermal reduction characteristics of the deposited material.

caption: Sample undergoing the liquid penetrant (PT) test during the initial penetrating stage.
summary: The sample is shown during the penetrating stage of the liquid penetrant (PT) test, performed according to ASTM E1417:21. This non-destructive evaluation is critical to ensure the additively manufactured part is free of surface-breaking cracks or excessive surface roughness, maintaining the integrity of the specimens used for subsequent testing.

caption: Point estimate fatigue prediction for IN718 superalloy without incorporating uncertainty modeling.
summary: This panel displays the fatigue characteristics of IN718 nickel-based superalloy using a deterministic point estimate approach. By excluding uncertainty modeling, the plot provides a baseline prediction for material performance, demonstrating the framework's capability to handle specific material characteristics under standard fatigue conditions without accounting for aleatoric or epistemic variability.

caption: In situ SKPFM potential map showing hydrogen exclusion from the specimen after 120 hours at room temperature.
summary: Representing the result of in situ SKPFM after 120 hours at room temperature, this map demonstrates hydrogen exclusion from the specimen. The visualization captures the final state of the potential distribution, providing evidence of the long-term interaction dynamics between hydrogen and the carbide particles within the material matrix.

caption: Comparison of fracture toughness (KIC) values for Al2618 and Al2618+TiB2 composites against literature data, highlighting variations in manufacturing methods and material orientations.
summary: This panel displays fracture toughness values for Al2618 base and TiB2-reinforced composites. It includes data for T6-treated cast samples, forged Al2618 in T6 condition with CL and CR orientations, AM AlSi10Mg in various orientations and conditions, and AM Scalmalloy in T5 treatment, providing a comprehensive benchmark against existing literature.

caption: BD-IPF map of the specimen processed under ANN-HIP conditions, depicting the crystallographic texture of the grains.
summary: The microstructure of the specimen is revealed by the building direction – inverse pole figure (BD-IPF) map. Panel g displays the grain orientation distribution for the ANN-HIP condition, providing a visual representation of the crystallographic texture within the material as captured by the BD-IPF mapping technique at a 50 µm scale.

caption: Optimized MBB beam topology showing fiber paths and scalar field contours, incorporating both parallel misalignment and singularity penalties at a 6 mm print width.
summary: This panel depicts the optimized MBB beam design for the MSP scenario, accounting for both parallel misalignment and singularity penalties with a 6 mm print width. The visualization highlights the fiber paths and scalar field contours, reflecting a design optimized for enhanced manufacturability compared to the MP case.

caption: 3D APT reconstruction of the CZ region in the AB condition, highlighting the uniform atomic arrangement and lack of secondary phase formation.
summary: Representing the CZ region in the AB condition, this 3D APT reconstruction reveals a uniform atomic distribution. The lack of nanoscale precipitation in this zone confirms that the microstructure remains stable, with the supersaturated solutes effectively maintained in the Al matrix without forming Mn or Zr-rich secondary phases.

caption: Magnified SEM micrographs comparing grain morphologies at different track heights: (i) bottom region showing columnar grains, (ii) middle region exhibiting cellular structures, and (iii) top region, with grain dimensions measured along the transverse direction.
summary: These magnified SEM images reveal height-dependent grain evolution within the track. The bottom region (i) features columnar grains due to a low solidification rate and high G/R ratio. The middle region (ii) displays cellular grains resulting from the equilibrium of thermal gradients and solidification rates, demonstrating distinct microstructural transitions.

caption: Atomic-scale visualization of the five nanocrystalline models at 0.2 tensile strain, highlighting twin formation, dislocation emission, and Lomer-Cottrell locks at triple junctions and grain boundaries.
summary: During later stages of deformation at 0.2 tensile strain, grain boundaries and triple junctions act as pivotal sources for dislocations and twins. The Ni-rich (20%) model demonstrates the earliest twin formation at these sites, indicated by yellow arrows. Circles highlight regions of active twin formation and dislocation emission within the nanocrystalline structure.

caption: Strain-temperature recovery curves for as-built and heat-treated tensile specimens subjected to a 4% total pre-strain, measured from room temperature to 300 °C.
summary: Thermomechanical strain-temperature curves illustrate the heating recovery behavior of as-built and heat-treated tensile specimens after a 4% total pre-strain. The results indicate that the plastic strain (PE) values increase with Ta addition in both as-built and heat-treated samples, with the recovery performance being further enhanced by the heat treatment process.

caption: Digital Image Correlation (DIC) snapshots illustrating strain distribution across the welded joint at sequential loading stages leading up to failure.
summary: Digital Image Correlation snapshots provide a clear visualization of strain distribution within the welded joint during tensile testing. These cloud maps capture the evolution of deformation at different loading steps until failure, supporting the inference that stress concentration at the weld toe is the primary cause of joint failure.

caption: Atomic model illustrating the atomic layer spacing in a Dy + Sc co-doped Al–Mg–Si alloy.
summary: Displayed is the atomic model of an Al–Mg–Si alloy co-doped with Dy and Sc. This panel allows for the examination of synergistic effects on the crystal lattice, providing insight into how the combination of these two elements influences the atomic layer spacing compared to their individual doping effects.

caption: Pole figure of GH4169 alloy fabricated using the continuous repeated heat input mode.
summary: Representing the continuous repeated heat input mode, this pole figure characterizes the texture development in GH4169 specimens. Along with other thermal modes, this configuration is analyzed to assess how specific heat input strategies influence the resulting crystallographic orientation and residual stress levels during the solidification of the material.

caption: TEM-DF micrograph of the R725-Ta alloy displaying intragranular gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime co-precipitates, imaged along the [100] gamma zone axis.
summary: This TEM-DF micrograph of the R725-Ta alloy, captured along the [100] gamma zone axis, highlights the intragranular gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime co-precipitates. The imaging condition effectively demonstrates the representative features of these precipitates within the alloy matrix, contributing to the understanding of the complex microstructural development in Ta-modified alloys.

caption: Peak shear resistance and ultimate relative displacement plotted against varying nodular pile node angles ranging from 26.6° to 68.2°.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between nodular pile node angles and the peak shear resistance and ultimate relative displacement of the interface. By testing angles of 26.6°, 45.0°, 56.3°, 63.4°, and 68.2°, the data reveals how geometric variations in the pile nodes influence the peak mechanical response of the cemented soil interface.

caption: Transcharacteristics of the electronic device measured at a drain-source voltage of Vds = -0.2 V.
summary: The transfer characteristics of the electronic device are shown for a drain-source voltage of Vds = -0.2 V. Data were collected across four distinct scan rates for three sets of devices, providing insight into the device's electrical response and operational behavior under the specified bias conditions.

caption: Cycling performance curves of the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film electrode over 300 cycles at a discharge current density of 6 A g-1.
summary: The 300-cycle discharge curves for the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film electrode at a current density of 6 A g-1 demonstrate the long-term stability and capacity retention of the material. These curves provide evidence of the electrode's structural integrity and electrochemical durability under sustained high-rate cycling conditions.

caption: Strong alignment of magnetic moments parallel to the direction of a strong applied magnetic field.
summary: Subjecting the paramagnetic material to a strong magnetic field forces the magnetizable axes to align more decisively with the field direction. This process demonstrates the material's response to increasing magnetic intensity, where the internal axes move to align with the external field as described in the reference.

caption: Absorbance spectra of the samples, highlighting the dye's absorption efficiency.
summary: This absorbance spectrum corroborates the findings from the transmission data by highlighting the specific absorption efficiency of the dye within the samples. The plot provides a detailed view of the material's light-absorbing properties, confirming the underlying optical behavior associated with the different pH-treated samples shown in the figure.

caption: Biological inspiration derived from the stomatopod dactyl club of the peacock mantis shrimp, highlighting the sinusoidally architected helicoidal microstructure.
summary: This panel illustrates the biological inspiration for the dual-phase lattice cylindrical tubes, specifically the stomatopod dactyl club of the peacock mantis shrimp. It highlights the sinusoidally architected helicoidal microstructure that serves as the foundational design principle for the subsequent lattice structures developed in this study.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of an intergranular L12-Al3Zr precipitate, accompanied by an EDS line profile (orange arrow) confirming the Zr-rich composition of the nanoscale feature.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging identifies a nanoscale intergranular precipitate within the microstructure. The accompanying EDS distribution profile, indicated by the orange arrow, confirms that the feature is a Zr-rich precipitate, specifically identified as Al3Zr. This chemical analysis validates the presence of these precipitates at the grain boundaries of the material.

caption: Load versus slip response at the loaded end for a mechanically anchored specimen with a bond length of 70 mm, ductile adhesive, and a rotation angle of 1.0 rad, comparing FDM predictions with experimental data.
summary: This plot illustrates the load-slip behavior of a mechanically anchored CFRP-to-steel joint with a 70 mm bond length and ductile adhesive. The graph demonstrates the accuracy of the proposed FDM model in predicting the mechanical response of the specimen under a rotation angle of 1.0 rad.

caption: Bar chart comparing the 7-day and 28-day compressive strength of mould cast specimens, evaluating the effects of encapsulated NaOH and nano clay additives against a control mix.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the 7-day and 28-day compressive strength of various printable mixes. The data reveals that the M-P mix exhibits improved strength compared to the control specimen (Mix M). Conversely, the direct addition of NaOH to the mixes results in a significant reduction in compressive strength at both ages.

caption: Deconvoluted TDS spectrum for a membrane sample heated at 800 K/h, showing the separation of the total signal into two distinct peaks corresponding to specific hydrogen trap sites.
summary: Deconvolution of the TDS spectrum obtained at a heating rate of 800 K/h reveals two individual peaks. Each of these peaks represents a specific type of hydrogen trap site within the membrane material. This analytical approach allows for the identification and characterization of distinct trapping mechanisms present in the saturated samples.

caption: Geometric representation of the Gyroid unit cell used as the fundamental building block for the lattice.
summary: The Gyroid unit cell serves as the fundamental building block for the porous bone implant structure. This geometric representation defines the repeating architectural unit that is subsequently utilized to construct the larger lattice structures, ensuring a consistent bioinspired design throughout the implant's volume.

caption: Weight change kinetics of AM and CM IN625 alloys measured during discontinuous exposure at 900 °C in stagnant lab air and Ar-4%H2-2%H2O environments.
summary: This panel displays weight change curves for AM and CM IN625 alloys at 900 °C. The data, collected over 1000 hours, shows that oxidation kinetics are virtually identical for both alloy types in both gas environments, confirming that AM does not inherently trigger accelerated oxidation compared to CM at this temperature.

caption: Reflection phase response of Cell 1 across the 60 to 70 GHz frequency range while Cell 2 remains constant.
summary: This plot illustrates the reflection phase delay for Cell 1 within the lower frequency band of 60-70 GHz. The data demonstrates that Cell 1 effectively covers the 2π phase range during this interval, while the reflection phase for Cell 2 is held constant, confirming the meta-atom's suitability for dual-band reflect array designs.

caption: Nyquist plots for Cu–35Zn and Cu–35Zn-E alloys after 14 days of corrosion, with an inset detailing the Cu–35Zn alloy response to demonstrate long-term immersion effects.
summary: Nyquist plots for Cu–35Zn and Cu–35Zn-E alloys after 14 days of immersion are shown. As corrosion progresses, the impedance arc radius of Cu–35Zn–Al and Cu–35Zn–Mn alloys becomes larger than that of the base Cu–35Zn alloy, confirming that Al and Mn additions enhance long-term corrosion resistance in brass.

caption: Loss convergence history comparing the proposed model against a standard U-Net architecture.
summary: This plot illustrates the loss convergence history during the training process for three distinct models. By comparing the proposed architecture directly against a standard U-Net, the graph highlights the relative performance and training efficiency of the models, providing a clear visual representation of how each architecture minimizes loss over time.

caption: Log-log plot demonstrating the scaling relationship between relative compressive strength and relative density for 3D RATH structures.
summary: This plot demonstrates the scaling relationship between relative compressive strength and relative density for 3D RATH structures. Analysis shows that the exponent n is 1.82, with a geometric constant of proportionality C2 of 0.36, providing a quantitative measure of the strength-to-density scaling for these specific 3D structural designs.

caption: Distribution of total waste generated during pre-operative and intra-operative periods.
summary: This pie chart illustrates the temporal distribution of waste generation. Approximately 19.8% of the total waste was produced during the pre-operative period, while the majority, 80.18%, was generated during the intra-operative period. These proportions highlight the significant difference in waste output between the two distinct surgical operative phases.

caption: Systematic design workflow illustrating the sequential steps for generating self-supporting vaulted structures across various printing stages.
summary: This flowchart outlines the comprehensive design workflow for creating self-supporting vaulted structures. The process initiates by establishing specific design objectives and subsequently adjusting predefined parameters as detailed in the methodology. This systematic approach ensures structural integrity and feasibility throughout every stage of the additive manufacturing print process.

caption: Ex situ SANS differential cross section dΣ/dΩ as a function of scattering vector Q for IN738LC superalloy samples subjected to fatigue cycling at various temperatures, measured at room temperature.
summary: This plot displays ex situ SANS data for IN738LC superalloy samples after fatigue cycling at different temperatures. The scattering intensity, measured as a differential cross section, reveals that the majority of the signal originates from large γ′ precipitates, manifesting as Porod-like scattering characterized by an intensity decrease proportional to Q to the power of negative four.

caption: Evolution of the UV-Vis absorption spectra for SC-02 during photolysis under 365 nm LED irradiation in acetonitrile.
summary: This panel displays the steady-state photolysis of SC-02 in acetonitrile. The absorption spectra demonstrate the capacity of the photoinitiator to undergo cleavage upon exposure to 365 nm light. The spectral changes track the consumption of the molecule over time, confirming its photochemical activity under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Electronic heat capacity of MoNbTaVW and HfNbTaTiZr alloys as a function of electronic temperature, computed using the XTANT-3 simulation framework.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific electronic heat capacities for MoNbTaVW and HfNbTaTiZr alloys calculated at elevated electronic temperatures. By utilizing the density of states and numerically evaluated chemical potential, the XTANT-3 simulation framework provides a quantitative assessment of the thermal response of these complex concentrated alloys under varying electronic excitation conditions.

caption: 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction of the wrought specimen showing the spatial distribution of elements.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction visualizes the wrought specimen. The analysis reveals an uneven distribution of magnesium within the matrix, contrasting with the uniform distribution observed in additively manufactured samples. This structural characterization provides critical insights into the microstructural differences resulting from distinct processing methods at room temperature.

caption: Evolution of training loss, represented by MSE, plotted against the number of training epochs across various learning rates.
summary: This panel illustrates the training loss evolution measured as MSE against the number of epochs for different learning rates. The data indicates that 300 epochs are required to effectively minimize the loss function, providing a clear metric for evaluating the training progress and convergence behavior of the machine learning model.

caption: Infrared spectra of NiTi nanoparticles modified with COOH-PA compared to the acid control sample, highlighting shifts in the PO region.
summary: This panel displays the PO region for COOH-PA modified NiTi nanoparticles. Bound COOH-PA exhibits P=O stretches at 1229 cm-1, P-O stretches at 1077 cm-1 and 1010 cm-1, and POH vibrations at 970 cm-1 and 935 cm-1, showing distinct spectral shifts compared to the solid acid control sample.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the deformed Ti–15Mo alloy with an average grain size of 7 μm, confirming the material is primarily composed of the β phase.
summary: The XRD pattern for the deformed Ti–15Mo alloy with a 7 μm grain size is displayed here. Analysis of the diffraction peaks confirms that the material, which exhibits lath structures, is primarily composed of the β phase, providing insight into the crystallographic nature of the deformed alloy structure.

caption: Dilatometric strain curves recorded during isothermal treatment at 500 °C for 2 hours for AB, HA, and HA+SA samples.
summary: Dilatometric curves illustrate the dimensional changes of AB, HA, and HA+SA samples during a 2-hour isothermal treatment at 500 °C. These measurements were conducted to clarify the specific phases that precipitate at this temperature, providing insight into the precipitation kinetics and structural stability of the different material conditions.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms of Vit105 metallic glass in as-cast, rejuvenated, and relaxed states, showing structural relaxation and glass transition overshoot.
summary: DSC scans of Vit105 reveal distinct thermal behaviors across as-cast, rejuvenated, and relaxed states. The deepest annealed sample exhibits partial crystallization, evidenced by an earlier crystallization onset. Structural relaxation is observed as an endothermic effect upon heating, while the glass transition overshoot highlights enthalpy recovery, which intensifies at lower annealing temperatures.

caption: Detailed view of the precipitate-free zone situated between secondary and tertiary γ′ precipitates in the ODS alloy.
summary: A detailed view of the precipitate-free zone between secondary and tertiary γ′ precipitates is provided. Consistent with the tertiary precipitate distribution, these features are less than 5 nm in diameter and appear more prominently in wider channels, specifically in regions further away from the larger secondary γ′ precipitates.

caption: TEM micrograph of Inconel 625 processed with bottom cooling, showing additional dislocation activity features.
summary: TEM analysis of the CMT Inconel 625 component under bottom cooling conditions displays various structural features. This panel further confirms the emergence of features indicating enhanced dislocation activity, consistent with the overall observation that bottom cooling conditions promote distinct microstructural developments compared to those observed under natural cooling conditions.

caption: Parity plots comparing predicted versus true values for yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, uniform elongation, and hardness using RBF, Matern, and ARDSE kernels in the CP-P model.
summary: Parity plots for yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, uniform elongation, and hardness demonstrate the predictive performance of RBF, Matern, and ARDSE kernels. These plots indicate that all three kernels exhibit similar predictive capabilities, providing reasonable prediction accuracies for the mechanical properties evaluated across the 108 data points used for model training.

caption: Current density versus voltage characteristics for OPVs utilizing PPI-SL and P3HT-PSL as donor materials paired with PC71BM as the acceptor, with an inset table summarizing the key photovoltaic performance parameters.
summary: Current density-voltage plots compare the performance of OPVs using PPI-SL and P3HT-PSL as donor materials with PC71BM as the acceptor. The figure includes an inset table that lists the specific photovoltaic parameters for both device types, providing a direct comparison of their electrical output under the tested conditions.

caption: Calculated cross-correlation coefficients for the IMF components corresponding to the SRAS signal data presented in Fig. 10(b).
summary: The bar chart illustrates the cross-correlation coefficients for the IMF components of the SRAS signal from Fig. 10(b). In this specific analysis, the maximum values identified through the signal determination criteria correspond directly to the highest values among all calculated IMF cross-correlation coefficients, confirming the signal's primary components.

caption: WRC diagram showing the specific area of interest for the filler wire, which exhibits an estimated ferrite number (FN) of approximately 8, indicating a ferritic-austenitic (FA) primary solidification mode.
summary: The WRC diagram provides a detailed estimation of the weld metal's solidification characteristics. Based on the assessment of the filler wire, a ferrite number of approximately 8 is determined. This result suggests a ferritic-austenitic (FA) primary solidification mode, confirming the microstructural expectations for the weld metal in this study.

caption: WDS elemental mapping of Oxygen distribution in the HVOF 1 coating, highlighting concentration at particle and splat interfaces.
summary: Wavelength-dispersive spectroscopy elemental mapping of Oxygen within the HVOF 1 coating reveals that oxides are preferentially concentrated at the interfaces between particles and splats. This distribution confirms the presence of various oxides throughout the coating, which are formed during the thermal spray process and contribute to the overall microstructure.

caption: Mo 3d high-resolution XPS spectra for Sr2NiMoO6, displayed for calcined, hydrogen-reduced, and post-DRM conditions.
summary: Mo 3d high-resolution XPS spectra for Sr2NiMoO6 are shown for calcined, hydrogen-reduced, and post-DRM states. These measurements track the molybdenum oxidation state changes throughout the material's processing history, offering a detailed view of the surface chemistry as the catalyst transitions from its calcined state to its active catalytic form.

caption: MS/MS spectrum confirming the presence of lactylation at the K193 site of the STAT1 protein.
summary: The MS/MS spectrum provides direct validation of lysine lactylation at the K193 position of the STAT1 protein. This spectroscopic evidence confirms the specific modification site identified through 4D proteomics, supporting the role of STAT1 in the signaling pathways associated with the observed lactylation-driven cellular responses in the material system.

caption: Grain boundary distribution map for the SLM-316L specimen constructed at 90°, showing yellow LAGBs (2-10°) and blue HAGBs (>10°).
summary: This map displays the grain boundary distribution for the 90° construction direction specimen, categorizing boundaries into LAGBs and HAGBs. The 90° specimen shows intermediate values compared to other orientations, with an LAGB fraction of 51.27% and a geometrically necessary dislocation density of 2.57 × 10^14 m^-2.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of a grain boundary in the AA condition, highlighting the presence of fine precipitates.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image captures a typical grain boundary in the AA condition, revealing the morphology and distribution of fine precipitates. Due to their small size, TEM-based analysis was necessary to resolve these features, which include Cr-rich carbides, γ′ phases, and potential σ phase particles located along the boundary.

caption: First-order Sobol’ indices illustrating the individual sensitivity of temperature-dependent crystal plasticity parameters on the machine learning model output across various strain levels.
summary: This panel displays the first-order Sobol’ indices, which quantify the individual impact of temperature-dependent crystal plasticity parameters on the machine learning model's stress predictions. By evaluating these indices at different strain levels, the plot demonstrates how the sensitivity of the model output to specific input parameters evolves during deformation.

caption: Longitudinal cross-sectional view of the modified Revo nozzle, highlighting the integrated M6 male thread at the lower end designed for modular gas injection unit attachment.
summary: This technical drawing illustrates the structural modification of a standard Revo nozzle. By replacing the original outlet orifice with an external M6 male thread, the design enables the modular integration of a custom gas injection unit, facilitating flexible experimental configurations for gas-assisted processing within the nozzle assembly.

caption: Calculated subband structure of the electronic system at an applied bias of 8.5 V, highlighting the distribution of heavy hole states.
summary: This plot displays the subband structure at an applied bias of 8.5 V. The valence band details are simplified, as most heavy hole states are concentrated into the h11 subband state (Q1). The visualization demonstrates how remote Γ states can reach the X11 location under these specific electrical conditions.

caption: 3D surface scan of the rear wall rear side for the Al foam with an Al 6061-O face sheet bumper configuration at 7 km/s impact velocity.
summary: Deformation of the rear wall for the Al foam and Al 6061-O face sheet bumper configuration is shown through a 3D surface scan at 7 km/s. Consistent with other tests, the displacement is mapped along the +x-axis, allowing for a direct comparison of the rear wall's response to the high-velocity impact.

caption: Energy convergence profile for 15 at.% Al in Ni calculated using an FCC parent lattice configuration during Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: Displayed is the convergence of mean per atom energy for a 15 at.% Al in Ni alloy system based on an FCC parent lattice. The data shows the progression of energy values as a function of the number of configurations generated by the Monte Carlo method, highlighting the system's stability.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve evaluating the CNN model performance for detecting warping defects.
summary: This ROC curve illustrates the diagnostic performance of the CNN model specifically for identifying warping defects. By plotting the true positive rate against the false positive rate, the graph provides a quantitative assessment of the model's classification accuracy and sensitivity for this particular defect type within the dataset.

caption: Schematic representation of the finite element model illustrating the applied load and boundary conditions for the quasi-static compression simulation.
summary: This panel displays the finite element model setup used for quasi-static compression analysis. It explicitly defines the load and boundary conditions applied to the sample geometry. The model, implemented in Abaqus/Explicit 2019, is designed to replicate the specific geometry of the experimental samples for accurate computational simulation of mechanical behavior.

caption: Mott-Schottky curves for annealed Ti–6Al–4V (ATC4) passive films, obtained following potentiostatic polarization at potentials between 0.6 V and 1.0 V.
summary: Mott-Schottky curves for ATC4 passive films are displayed, exhibiting positive slopes within the -0.8 V to -0.4 V range. This confirms the n-type semiconductive nature of the passive films formed on the annealed alloy after potentiostatic polarization at potentials ranging from 0.6 V to 1.0 V.

caption: Distribution of shade frequency percentages for 92 super shades (SS) evaluated in the study.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the frequency distribution of 92 super shades (SS). The data represents the percentage occurrence of these specific shades, providing a quantitative overview of their prevalence. This analysis complements the CE and CEP results for VC and 3D shade guides, highlighting the specific distribution characteristics of the super shades.

caption: Schematic representation of the projection process condition required to achieve an amplification factor that results in a rectangular function with a thickness defined by the parameter.
summary: This schematic illustrates the specific condition required for the projection process to generate a rectangular function. By satisfying this condition, the process ensures the resulting function maintains a thickness equal to the specified parameter, providing a clear visual representation of the mathematical requirements for the amplification factor in this system.

caption: Linear portions of the polarization curves focused within a ±0.03 V range around the corrosion potential, with solid lines indicating the linear regression fits.
summary: Linear segments of the voltammograms are shown near the corrosion potential to facilitate the determination of polarization resistance. Slopes derived from these linear portions provide an estimate of Rp that shows good agreement with the values obtained from the Tafel analysis presented in the previous panel.

caption: EBSD grain type map of the HTAZ-B sample.
summary: EBSD analysis of the HTAZ-B sample reveals the distribution of grain types. This map provides a visual representation of the microstructural characteristics, allowing for the determination of grain type percentages as part of the comprehensive study of the various sample conditions presented in the figure.

caption: MitoTracker staining of osteoblasts after 4 hours of H2O2 stimulation, highlighting mitochondrial network morphology.
summary: MitoTracker staining reveals the state of the mitochondrial network under oxidative stress. Treatment with Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA significantly mitigates H2O2-induced damage, resulting in a more intact and interconnected mitochondrial network compared to untreated cells. This demonstrates the protective role of the material in maintaining mitochondrial structural integrity during oxidative challenge.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the polymer derived from 2-carboxyethyl acrylate.
summary: The DSC analysis of the polymer sample derived from 2-carboxyethyl acrylate reveals a glass transition temperature of 7.3 °C. This value, which is well below room temperature, indicates that the resulting polymer possesses high elasticity, confirming its thermal and mechanical characteristics as determined through the thermal analysis.

caption: Annual publication frequency regarding conformal cooling technologies extracted from the SCOPUS database between 1990 and 2024.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the temporal evolution of research interest in conformal cooling, based on 851 documents identified in the SCOPUS database. Spanning from 1990 to 2024, the data highlights the growing academic and industrial focus on this specific engineering and material science topic within the specified timeframe.

caption: Hardness distribution profiles for WAAM samples #1 through #9, plotted as a function of distance along the cross-section from the testing point to the component top.
summary: Hardness distributions for WAAM samples #1 through #9 are presented, illustrating variations along the cross-section from the testing point to the top of the component. Significant hardness differences exist between samples #1 and #9, although sample #4 consistently exhibits higher hardness values across the majority of the tested locations.

caption: Temporal evolution of electronic and atomic temperatures in pure Ni for a 0.2 ps electron-phonon coupling activation time.
summary: This panel illustrates the temporal evolution of electronic and atomic temperatures within the center cell of an MD box for a representative cascade in pure Ni. The simulation assumes a 0.2 ps electron-phonon coupling activation time, providing insight into the thermal response of the system following a cascade initiated near the box corner.

caption: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for SC-02 in acetonitrile, showing the spectral overlap used to determine the singlet excited state energy level.
summary: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for SC-02 in acetonitrile are presented. The crossing point of these spectra is utilized to experimentally determine the singlet excited state energy level (S1), providing critical insight into the electronic transition properties of the SC-02 material within the solvent environment.

caption: Total energy of the Ni/NiO interface system plotted as a function of the interface gap distance d, demonstrating a clear energy minimum at d = 1.9 Å.
summary: The total system energy is plotted against the interface gap distance d to identify the optimal structural configuration. The results indicate that the system energy reaches a minimum at a gap distance of 1.9 Å, which is subsequently used to perform a full relaxation of the Ni/NiO interface system.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the AlFeCrSi alloy, highlighting the contrast between the matrix and secondary phases.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image provides high-contrast visualization of the AlFeCrSi alloy microstructure. This technique is utilized to identify the distribution and morphology of various precipitates within the aluminum matrix, which were formed under optimized processing parameters of 112 J/mm3 to achieve maximum microhardness and bulk density.

caption: Geometric representation of the rhombic dodecahedron unit cell architecture alongside photographs of the resulting porous metallic cages.
summary: The rhombic dodecahedron unit cell structure is presented as the basis for the porous Ta and Ti scaffolds. Photographs of the actual printed cages demonstrate the successful realization of this open-pore architecture, confirming that the designed geometry maintains consistent connectivity throughout the scaffold as produced by the SLM manufacturing process.

caption: Electron work function (EWF) plot for the α-Ti (101) surface, showing a calculated value of 3.76 eV.
summary: Calculated EWF values for α-Ti (101) are derived from first-principles simulations. The resulting value of 3.76 eV is lower than that of the β-Ti (110) surface. This smaller EWF value is directly linked to the more delocalized and active electron state observed in the α-Ti crystal structure.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution maps of the oxidized Inconel 625 alloy cross-section after 1080 h of exposure at 1100 °C, showing the presence of NiFe2O4 within the Cr2O3 oxide layer.
summary: EPMA elemental mapping characterizes the cross-sectional oxidation of Inconel 625 at 1100 °C after 1080 h. The maps show NiFe2O4 oxide, represented by darker gray regions, embedded within the Cr2O3 layer. Differences in peak intensities indicate that higher oxidation temperatures significantly increase both the oxidation rate and the extent of spallation.

caption: Spatial distribution of aberrations at a depth of 400 um, accompanied by the corresponding image captured by the wavefront sensor to visualize the optical distortion profile.
summary: Panel b illustrates the aberration distribution at a 400 um depth within the glass sample. The visualization includes the raw image captured by the wavefront sensor alongside the processed aberration map. This data confirms the specific optical impact of the material at this depth after system calibration.

caption: Room temperature mass density of melt-mixed polypropylene-based thermoplastic matrix composites plotted against iron volumetric content, comparing experimental scatter data with the theoretical density line.
summary: This plot illustrates the room temperature mass density of melt-mixed polypropylene-based thermoplastic matrix composites as a function of iron volumetric content. The experimental scatter data exhibits a quite-linear trend, which aligns well with the theoretical density line, indicating that the filler and matrix phases are effectively stacked together.

caption: Sectional elemental distribution map of HT700 alloy containing 5 wt.% Al, showing the formation of a continuous Al2O3 layer after 200 hours of corrosion at 700 °C.
summary: This map reveals the sectional elemental distribution of HT700 alloy with 5 wt.% Al after 200 hours of corrosion at 700 °C. As aluminum content increases, a closer and uninterrupted Al2O3 layer forms on the surface, effectively hindering the outward diffusion of chromium and reducing the thickness of the diffusion layer.

caption: Nb concentration gradient observed across the transition zone of the Ti60–Ti2AlNb graded material produced by L-DED.
summary: Nb element content displays a linear distribution within the transition zone of the L-DED graded material. Similar to Al, the Nb content in the melt pool is lower than that of the feeding powder, indicating that mixing between neighboring zones leads to compositional deviation and extended transition zone widths.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the PLA-CB-based sensor in 0.1 M PBS and cell culture media, comparing the electrochemical response in the absence (black line) and presence (blue line) of 1 mM dopamine at a scan rate of 50 mV/s.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms demonstrate the electrochemical response of the PLA-CB-based sensor to dopamine. Measurements were conducted in 0.1 M PBS and cell culture media at a scan rate of 50 mV/s. The presence of 1 mM dopamine (blue line) is compared against the baseline (black line) to show the sensor's detection capability.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of a polymer/Ag/Pb composite anode with a triangular porous lattice, demonstrating the electrochemical response under zinc electrowinning conditions at 10 mV s-1.
summary: This panel shows the cyclic voltammogram for the triangular porous lattice composite anode. Similar to the square lattice, this 3D meta-structure exhibits broader electrochemical peaks than the bulk lead benchmark, reflecting the influence of the porous geometry on the electrowinning process and the resulting electrochemically active surface area.

caption: XRD patterns for six sintered scaffold groups (TCP, 20M, 40M, 60M, 80M, and M) compared against standard reference cards for HA, MgO, and WL phases.
summary: XRD patterns were recorded for six sets of sintered scaffolds to identify phase composition. Analysis reveals that Ca3(PO4)2 reacts with MgO to form the whitlockite (WL) phase, with higher WL content in 20M and 40M scaffolds compared to 60M and 80M, where WL peaks are nearly invisible.

caption: Isometric view of the full pyramidal lattice panel, illustrating the arrangement of multiple unit cells.
summary: This isometric view displays the full pyramidal lattice panel, which is composed of multiple unit cells. The structure is designed such that the four struts within each unit cell do not share common nodes with adjacent cells, allowing the response of a single unit cell to approximate that of the larger panel.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for WAAM and WAAM + UI AZ31 thin-wall specimens along the TD, illustrating cathodic hydrogen evolution and anodic matrix dissolution.
summary: PDP curves for WAAM and WAAM + UI AZ31 thin-wall specimens along the TD are displayed. The cathode branch represents the hydrogen evolution reaction, while the anode branch corresponds to α-Mg matrix dissolution. UI treatment increases the self-corrosion potential, indicating a decreasing self-corrosion trend for the processed AZ31 thin walls.

caption: Prediction profiler for the PAD model illustrating the relationship between predictor values and model output, with grey shaded regions representing 95% confidence intervals.
summary: The prediction profiler for the PAD model demonstrates the model's accuracy across the range of predictor values. Grey shaded regions indicate 95% confidence bands, providing a visual representation of the prediction uncertainty. This analysis confirms the model's performance characteristics and reliability throughout the entire studied domain of the PAD system.

caption: Relationship between powder oxidation condition and average UTS for different mean particle sizes, including data inserts for individual strength values.
summary: Heat treatments reduce the strength of all powder batches regardless of the air environment oxidation, while maintaining the trend that finer powders are stronger. The included data inserts provide specific individual strength values for the different batches, summarizing the overall impact of oxidation conditions on the mechanical performance.

caption: Quantification of the angle difference between fibrous tissue orientation and scaffold orientation (n=5), showing no statistically significant difference (ns) across the groups.
summary: Statistical evaluation of the angle difference between fibrous tissue orientation and scaffold orientation shows no significant deviation across the experimental groups. This finding, supported by a sample size of five, indicates that the fibrous tissue consistently aligns with the scaffold structure regardless of the specific matrix type used in the implantation.

caption: Measured specific capacitance, calculated surface area via the Helmholtz equation, and predicted specific capacitance based on a close-packed model for anode foils with varying PSM contents.
summary: This plot displays the measured specific capacitance of anode foils with varying PSM contents alongside surface area values derived from the Helmholtz equation. It compares these experimental results against predicted values from a close-packed model, revealing that the foil without PSM reaches only 52% of its predicted specific capacitance.

caption: Schematic illustration of the solidification path, highlighting the final state of the material after the DED process.
summary: This schematic completes the illustration of the microstructural evolution during the DED process. It depicts the final solidification path, where the high-temperature melt pool conditions influence the final distribution and state of TiB2 particles, determining the resulting microstructure of the bulk IN718/TiB2 deposited material.

caption: Surface coverage percentage of the adhered Inconel 718 metallic transfer layer on a ceramic substrate as a function of sliding velocity.
summary: This plot illustrates the surface coverage percentage of the adhered Inconel 718 metallic transfer layer on a ceramic surface plotted against varying sliding velocities. The data indicates that the amount of metallic transfer layer remains almost similar across both room temperature (RT) and high temperature (HT) testing conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the mineralized layer, demonstrating the phase purity and crystallinity of the hydroxyapatite coating.
summary: The XRD pattern of the mineralized layer confirms the phase purity and crystalline nature of the hydroxyapatite coating. This diffraction data serves as a definitive structural characterization, validating the successful synthesis of HAp on the PEEK scaffold using the PTL nanofilm template.

caption: Kissinger plot representing the relationship between ln(Φ/Tmax²) and 1000/Tmax for membrane samples to determine activation energy of hydrogen traps.
summary: This Kissinger plot displays the linear relationship between ln(Φ/Tmax²) and 1000/Tmax for membrane samples. By applying Kissinger's approach to the linear fitting of these variables, the activation energy of hydrogen traps is determined. This analysis provides critical kinetic data regarding trap behavior within the membrane material structure.

caption: Temporal evolution of dislocation line length in pure Cu during stretching under varying PKA energy irradiation.
summary: This line graph illustrates the dislocation line length in pure Cu as a function of time during stretching under different PKA energy irradiations. The data indicates that the dislocation line length reaches a minimal value at 50 ps when the PKA energy is 0 keV, reflecting the material's response to irradiation.

caption: STEM micrograph at 40k magnification providing a higher resolution view of the as-printed oriented microstructure.
summary: Captured at 40k magnification, this STEM image offers a detailed view of the as-printed oriented microstructure in the SLM Ti6Al4V alloy. The increased magnification allows for a clearer examination of the microstructural features, facilitating a more precise analysis of the material's internal organization following the printing process.

caption: Areal capacitance of 2D- and 3D-IDCμE electrodes as a function of PPy electrodeposition time, conducted at a constant current density of 1 mA cm⁻².
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between PPy electrodeposition time and the resulting areal capacitance for both 2D and 3D electrode architectures. The data demonstrates that extending the electrodeposition duration consistently enhances the capacitive performance of both electrode types, confirming that PPy deposition effectively increases capacitance compared to pristine carbon electrodes.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of secondary L12-Al3Sc nanoparticles in the S1.5 sample aged at 350 °C for 240 min.
summary: This dark-field TEM image displays the microstructure of the S1.5 sample after aging at 350 °C for 240 minutes. It reveals a high density of secondary L12-Al3Sc nanoparticles precipitated from the aluminum matrix, demonstrating the effective precipitation behavior of the scandium-containing alloy under these specific heat treatment conditions.

caption: Temporal evolution of displaced atom counts for 1, 10, and 50 keV energy levels with a velocity vector parallel to the {111} plane.
summary: Displacement atom profiles are plotted against simulation time for three distinct energy levels: 1 keV, 10 keV, and 50 keV. The simulation accounts for a threshold displacement energy of 45 eV, representing the minimum recoil energy required to form stable defects, with the velocity vector oriented parallel to the {111} crystallographic plane.

caption: Primary dendrite arm spacing (PDAS) distribution across samples processed with varying hatch spacings, highlighting the reduced average and range observed in 0.7 samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the primary dendrite arm spacing (PDAS) for samples processed at different hatch spacings. Measurements indicate that 0.7 samples exhibit a smaller average PDAS and a narrower range compared to other conditions. These findings suggest a higher probability of achieving a smaller average grain size in these specific samples.

caption: Performance evaluation chart illustrating the predictive accuracy of the Artificial Neural Network model.
summary: This panel presents a performance chart for the Artificial Neural Network, providing a visual representation of the model's predictive capabilities. The chart serves as a primary metric for assessing the effectiveness of the ANN architecture in processing the data, highlighting the overall accuracy achieved during the training and evaluation phases.

caption: Raman spectra illustrating the variation in the intensity ratio of the D and G bands (ID/IG) across samples with different graphene oxide (GO) contents.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis reveals the structural characteristics of samples with varying graphene oxide contents. The intensity ratios of the D band and G band, denoted as ID/IG, are observed to fluctuate between 0.98 and 1.07, providing insight into the degree of disorder and graphitic nature within the investigated materials.

caption: Overall cell type annotation mapped onto the UMAP clustering results, identifying specific populations including tenocytes, fibroblasts, myofibroblasts, macrophages, and vascular endothelial cells.
summary: This panel displays the annotated cell types across the entire UMAP clustering result. The identified populations, which include tenocytes, fibroblasts, myofibroblasts, macrophages, and vascular endothelial cells, are mapped onto the clusters to provide a comprehensive overview of the cellular composition within the conjunctival tissue samples.

caption: Hysteresis loop of the composite, showing a maximum saturation magnetization (Ms) value of 353.5 emu/g for Fe70.
summary: The magnetic hysteresis loop of the composite is presented to characterize its magnetic properties. The Fe70 sample exhibits a maximum saturation magnetization (Ms) value of 353.5 emu/g, which is associated with a wide band of electromagnetic wave-absorbing frequency, highlighting the material's potential for high-frequency wave absorption applications.

caption: 2D Gaussian-smoothed synchrotron XRD phase-evolution map of the FCC phase across the composite weld zone.
summary: This panel presents a 2D Gaussian-smoothed synchrotron XRD phase-evolution map of the FCC phase across the composite weld zone. The FCC phase is a dominant component of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy, with non-close-packed (200) and (400) reflections exhibiting distinct peak broadening behavior sensitive to lattice strain.

caption: EDS elemental map showing the distribution of Al (red) at the Al/(0001)TiB2 interface.
summary: Aluminum distribution at the Al/(0001)TiB2 interface is visualized using EDS mapping. The red-colored map highlights the Al matrix surrounding the TiB2 particles, providing a clear spatial reference for the interface structure in the master alloy when viewed along the [1120] direction.

caption: Microwave absorption performance of the multiscale resonant labyrinth metastructure across the 2–18 GHz frequency range.
summary: This plot displays the microwave absorption performance of the multiscale resonant labyrinth metastructure within the 2–18 GHz frequency range. The design incorporates strategically combined labyrinth cavity dimensions, specifically wall thicknesses of 0.4 mm, 1.6 mm, 3.2 mm, and 4.8 mm, to achieve enhanced absorption characteristics compared to individual unit configurations.
