caption: Bacterial colony formation of S. aureus on the surface of control casting 316L stainless steel.
summary: This panel illustrates the bacterial colonies of S. aureus formed on the control casting 316L stainless steel. By providing a reference for standard bacterial growth on non-antibacterial steel, this image allows for a direct assessment of the performance improvements achieved by the 316L-4.5Cu alloy in suppressing S. aureus colonization.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry profile of Fe(III)-Ti electrode measured against Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry profile for the Fe(III)-Ti specimen is presented to evaluate the onset of reduction. This electrochemical test is essential for determining the potential at which hydrogen production begins, providing critical data on the reduction behavior of the material under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Faber-Ziman partial structure factor S_AgAg(q) for liquid Cu25Ag75 derived from MD simulations, highlighting the structural differences relative to Ni-Al alloys.
summary: Displayed is the partial structure factor S_AgAg(q) for liquid Cu25Ag75 obtained through MD simulations. The data confirms that the Faber-Ziman structure factors for Cu-Ag liquid alloys possess very different shapes compared to those of Ni-Al, reflecting the distinct liquid structure and atomic ordering present in the Cu-Ag binary system.

caption: Custom-designed FFF printing apparatus mounted on the ESRF synchrotron beamlines for in situ X-ray microtomography.
summary: This photograph displays the specialized FFF printing device engineered for in situ synchrotron X-ray microtomography experiments at the BM05 and ID19 beamlines. The setup allows for the extrusion of molten material without a deposition bed, enabling precise structural imaging of the printing process during operation.

caption: ABS sample surface after 5 seconds of exposure to hot acetone vapors, displaying the transformation of spikes into coarse, wavy structures.
summary: Following 5 seconds of exposure to hot acetone vapors, the initial spike-like surface features of the ABS sample undergo a structural transformation. These features evolve into coarse, wavy textures, marking the beginning of the chemical treatment process's impact on the surface morphology and overall roughness of the material.

caption: Bode plots showing the frequency-dependent impedance modulus and phase shift for HX-B and HX-M samples in 10 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: These Bode plots characterize the electrochemical response of HX-B and HX-M samples in 10 wt% NaCl. The data includes both impedance and phasor curves, which corroborate the Nyquist plots. The phase shift behavior reflects resistive characteristics at low and high frequencies, transitioning to non-ideal capacitive behavior at intermediate frequencies.

caption: Fluorescence decay kinetics and biexponential model fit for TPU/2 C composite at room temperature.
summary: The TPU/2 C composite exhibits a nonlinear fluorescence decay curve at an emission wavelength of 465 nm. By applying a biexponential fitting function, the fluorescence lifetime kinetics are determined, providing insight into the emission behavior of the composite material at the specified coumarin concentration.

caption: Simulated HRTEM image generated for an overlapped twin model.
summary: This simulated HRTEM image represents the expected appearance of an overlapped twin boundary. It serves as a computational validation tool to confirm that the observed atomic column merging in experimental images is consistent with the structural model of an overlapped twin boundary in the QWT-DZ martensite.

caption: Physical 3D-printed Voronoi sphere fabricated using the coarse-only optimized geometry.
summary: This photograph shows the physical print result of the Voronoi sphere model based on the coarse-only optimization geometry. It demonstrates the practical realization of the simulated design, allowing for a direct visual and physical assessment of the model's structural integrity and support requirements after the printing process.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line profile spanning from the precursor through the second reaction region, with vertical dashed lines marking the boundaries of the reaction layer.
summary: This energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line profile provides a quantitative analysis of the chemical composition across the reaction layer. Spanning from the precursor to the region formed after the second reaction, the profile uses vertical dashed lines to clearly delineate the boundaries of the reaction layer within the sample.

caption: FTIR spectra of gaseous pyrolysis products released from PLA and PLA-flax composites at peak absorbance during thermal degradation.
summary: Comparison of gaseous pyrolysis products for pure PLA and PLA-flax composites is presented through FTIR spectra. These measurements, taken at peak absorbance during thermal degradation under nitrogen, highlight the influence of flax reinforcement on the volatile species generated during the decomposition of the polylactic acid matrix.

caption: EBSD grain boundary map of LB-PBF AlSi10Mg in the as-built (AB) condition, revealing the heterogeneous and anisotropic microstructure resulting from the rapid solidification process.
summary: The EBSD grain boundary map illustrates the microstructure of LB-PBF AlSi10Mg in the as-built condition. Due to the complex thermos-physical phenomena inherent in the LB-PBF process, such as directional thermal history and rapid solidification, the material exhibits a notably heterogeneous and anisotropic grain structure throughout the analyzed sample area.

caption: Two-dimensional raw data plot of intensity versus neutron arrival time and scattering angle for a textured stainless steel sample measured at POLDI.
summary: This panel displays the raw neutron diffraction data collected at POLDI for a textured stainless steel sample. The intensity is plotted against neutron arrival time and scattering angle, where each Bragg reflection appears as a series of parallel lines corresponding to individual chopper slits, providing the foundational dataset for further analysis.

caption: FOBI-retrieved transmission spectra for the Fe and Cu layers, demonstrating a consistent crystallographic texture trend when the neutron beam is aligned along the TD2 direction.
summary: These FOBI-retrieved transmission spectra characterize the distinct Fe and Cu layers within the multilayer sample. The data indicates a consistent crystallographic texture trend observed when the neutron beam is oriented along the TD2 direction, providing quantitative insight into the material properties of the individual layers within the specimen.

caption: Release rates of Met from G@Met and BHP/G@Met scaffolds with and without ultrasound (US) stimulation, alongside PBS absorbance measurements at 233 nm.
summary: This panel evaluates the drug release kinetics of Met from G@Met and BHP/G@Met scaffolds. The study compares release rates under conditions with and without ultrasound stimulation. Absorbance measurements of PBS at 233 nm are used to quantify the concentration of released Met, demonstrating controllable drug release.

caption: Radar chart illustrating various energy absorption metrics for OIPL structures across a range of cell sizes.
summary: This radar chart visualizes multiple energy absorption indicators for proposed OIPL structures as a function of varying cell sizes. The data highlights how structural dimensions influence performance metrics, providing a comprehensive overview of the energy absorption capabilities inherent to the OIPL design across different geometric configurations.

caption: Surface topography of polished Alloy 617 sheets prior to DFW, showing a stack of 15 layers with measured roughness values of Rz = 603.26 nm and Rt = 779.70 nm.
summary: Surface morphology analysis of the polished Alloy 617 sheets, conducted via a Veeco profilometer, characterizes the initial state of the 15-layer stack before DFW. The topography reveals specific surface roughness metrics, with Rz measured at 603.26 nm and Rt at 779.70 nm, providing baseline data for the bonding process.

caption: Bar chart comparing the two-body abrasive wear performance of SAW, PTAW, and TIG hardfacing specimens.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the two-body abrasive wear resistance of SAW, PTAW, and TIG hardfacings. The results demonstrate a direct correlation with hardness measurements, where lower hardness in unreinforced SS and Ni samples leads to higher wear ratios. PTAW samples exhibit the shallowest abrasive grooves, indicating superior abrasion resistance.

caption: Top view of the Cu (110) surface supercell geometry, showing the step monolayer (magenta) atop the underlying planes (blue), with white arrows indicating the specific corner and edge atoms targeted for electronic structure analysis.
summary: The Cu (110) surface supercell is presented here, detailing the step monolayer configuration on the underlying planes. By marking the corner and edge atoms with white arrows, the figure facilitates the study of how these specific geometric sites influence the electronic properties and potential corrosion behavior of the copper surface.

caption: Profile of the nano-indent for the LPBF horizontal (X–Y) IN718 variant, showing the surface displacement.
summary: The profile of the nano-indent for the LPBF horizontal (X-Y) IN718 variant illustrates the surface displacement after indentation. This profile demonstrates a sharper gradient and less pile-up than the wrought variant, confirming that the LPBF processing route results in distinct indentation behavior compared to the wrought IN718 material.

caption: Calculated time-temperature-transformation (TTT) curves for as-built IN718 alloy, highlighting the kinetics of phase precipitation.
summary: This TTT diagram illustrates the transformation kinetics for as-built IN718 alloy, generated using JMatPro software. The plot identifies the transformation behavior of the δ phase, with the peak transformation temperature estimated at 900 ℃. This data provides critical insights into the thermal stability and phase evolution of the alloy.

caption: Deconvolution of the 27Al MAS NMR spectrum for pure slag 3, highlighting a prominent resonance centered at approximately 60 ppm.
summary: The 27Al MAS NMR spectrum for pure slag 3 displays a large resonance centered at about 60 ppm. This peak corresponds to tetrahedrally coordinated AlO4 4- units, indicating that a significant portion of the aluminum within the slag structure exists in tetrahedral coordination.

caption: Cross-sectional view of a BeAM sample built with 3 L min-1 carrier gas, 6 L min-1 shield gas, and 6 L min-1 secondary gas, showing altered geometry.
summary: This optical micrograph displays a sectioned BeAM sample produced with 3 L min-1 carrier gas, 6 L min-1 shield gas, and an additional 6 L min-1 secondary gas flow. The inclusion of secondary gas significantly alters the track geometry compared to the sample without secondary gas flow.

caption: Low magnification STEM HAADF micrograph of location iv viewed along the <110> zone axis, demonstrating the distribution of primary and secondary γ′ precipitation.
summary: This low magnification STEM HAADF micrograph of location iv, taken along the <110> zone axis, provides a broad view of the microstructure. It confirms the presence of spherical secondary γ′ precipitates, which are less than 5 nm in diameter and distributed throughout the entirety of the build.

caption: UV-vis absorption spectrum of PIs in DMSO solution at a concentration of 5 × 10^-4 M.
summary: The UV-vis absorption spectrum of PIs is presented, illustrating the optical characteristics of the material. The measurement was conducted using PIs dissolved in DMSO at a concentration of 5 × 10^-4 M, providing essential data on the molar extinction coefficient and the electronic transition properties of the polyimide samples.

caption: Hexagonal x precipitate arrangement characterized by a point-symmetry center indicated by a red dot, identified as the energetically most favorable configuration.
summary: The hexagonal x precipitate arrangement is shown in panel c, featuring a point-symmetry center marked by a red dot. This specific configuration is identified as the energetically most favorable superstructure among those investigated. The arrangement is defined by the point-symmetric operation applied to the phase-field and tangential strains.

caption: Three-dimensional rose diagram visualizing the orientation distribution of the force chains within the network.
summary: A three-dimensional rose diagram is utilized to visualize the orientation of the force chains. This statistical representation effectively maps the directional distribution of the force chains, providing critical insights into the structural anisotropy and the spatial arrangement of the force chain network within the analyzed material.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for HAA measured under a 1 mT field, showing both Zero-Field Cooled (ZFC) and Field Cooled (FC) protocols. The inset displays the inverse magnetic susceptibility (1/χ) corrected for diamagnetism, with a blue line representing the Curie–Weiss law fit.
summary: Magnetization measurements for HAA reveal the temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility under a 1 mT field. The ZFC and FC curves characterize the magnetic response, while the inverse susceptibility inset, corrected for a diamagnetic constant, demonstrates adherence to the Curie–Weiss law, providing insight into the material's magnetic behavior and phase characteristics.

caption: Hardness versus displacement (H-h) curves for NC Ni obtained from CSR tests at three different strain rates.
summary: Panel (a) displays the hardness versus displacement (H-h) curves for nanocrystalline (NC) Ni, derived from constant strain rate (CSR) tests conducted at three distinct strain rates. These experimental data points illustrate the mechanical response of the material under controlled indentation conditions, providing a basis for analyzing hardness variations with displacement.

caption: Normalized K-edge XANES spectra for Cr, Mn, Fe, and Ni comparing aerosol particles collected on filters against metallic stainless steel standards.
summary: This figure displays normalized K-edge XANES spectra for Cr, Mn, Fe, and Ni, comparing aerosol particles collected on filters to metallic stainless steel standards. The spectra reveal that edge features for Cr, Mn, and Fe are smaller than those of metallic references, indicating a significant presence of oxidized metal species in the aerosol samples.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of the pre-alloyed powder obtained via laser diffraction, showing the frequency of particle diameters.
summary: The powder size distribution is presented as a histogram derived from laser particle diffraction measurements. Analysis of this distribution yields specific characteristic values, with D10, D50, and D90 determined to be 22.3, 68.9, and 135.2 μm, respectively, providing a quantitative assessment of the powder particle size range.

caption: EDS line scan profile across the interface at the first additive zone position (b), illustrating compositional variations.
summary: This EDS line scan profile characterizes the elemental distribution across the interface at the first additive zone position. The analysis provides critical data on the chemical composition gradients, which are essential for evaluating the intermetallic compound formation and thickness variations observed across different additive manufacturing zones in the material.

caption: Room-temperature magnetic hysteresis loops for C x N 100-x -A70 samples with varying Co/Ni ratios, pre-reduced at 400 °C in hydrogen, showing narrow loops characteristic of magnetically soft ferromagnetic materials.
summary: Room-temperature magnetic hysteresis loops for C x N 100-x -A70 samples demonstrate narrow curves, indicating magnetically soft ferromagnetic behavior. Increasing the Co content in the alloy nanoparticles leads to higher saturation magnetization, remanence, and coercivity. These alloy nanoparticles exhibit intermediate magnetic properties that are directly dependent on their specific elemental composition.

caption: Equilibrium solidification path for the Al–12Si–4Cu-2.7Ni-0.2Sc alloy, showing the sequence of phase formation during cooling.
summary: The equilibrium solidification path for the Al–12Si–4Cu-2.7Ni-0.2Sc alloy is presented here. This plot tracks the sequence of phase formation during the cooling process, providing insight into the thermodynamic evolution of the alloy composition under equilibrium conditions as calculated by the Pandat software.

caption: Immunofluorescent staining of iNOS and Arg1 markers in scaffold-implanted tissue at 7 days post-implantation.
summary: Immunofluorescent staining at 7 days post-implantation reveals the inflammatory response within the scaffolds. The PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF group exhibits significantly reduced iNOS expression and enhanced Arg-1 expression compared to the PLA and PLA/GA control groups, indicating a shift toward an anti-inflammatory and pro-regenerative environment within the implanted material.

caption: Final 3D reconstruction of microporosity at the point of fracture, highlighting morphological changes in large-sized pores.
summary: The final 3D reconstruction captures the state of microporosity at the point of fracture. While most defects remain stable, this panel highlights that some large-sized micropores undergo significant morphological changes at the final fracture stage. The color-coded representation confirms the persistence of the aggregation band observed in the initial state.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot displaying the inverse square of capacitance (C^-2) versus potential (E) for base metal and stir zone samples after 7 days of immersion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots (C^-2 vs E) are shown for both base metal and stir zone samples following a 7-day immersion period in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. This analysis provides insights into the semiconducting properties of the passive films formed on the surfaces of the specimens after prolonged exposure.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of a commercial carbon steel (S45C) plate surface, displaying corrosion and a lack of cell growth.
summary: MDCK–YFP-keratin-8 cells were cultured with a commercial carbon steel (S45C) plate for 3 days. The surface of the S45C plate was corroded, and fluorescence imaging confirms that cells did not grow on the plate, highlighting the cytotoxic or inhibitory nature of the corroding steel surface.

caption: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of the GH4698 surface after electrochemical modification.
summary: The Ni 2p XPS spectrum for the GH4698 surface is shown following electrochemical modification. Analysis of the spectral data indicates the presence of metallic Ni peaks at 852.7 eV and 869.8 eV, while Ni 2+ oxide species are identified by peaks located at 855.9 eV and 875.3 eV on the surface.

caption: UV–Visible diffuse reflectance spectra of the prepared g-C3N4 and modified catalyst samples.
summary: The UV–Visible diffuse reflectance spectrum illustrates the optical absorption characteristics of the prepared g-C3N4 and the various modified catalysts. This measurement is essential for evaluating the light-harvesting capabilities of the materials and determining how modifications influence the electronic structure and optical response of the carbon nitride photocatalysts.

caption: Fourier transform modules of the experimental EXAFS functions for the Fe58Ni25B17 alloy measured above the K-Fe absorption edge, comparing the initial melt-quenched (MQ) state with the state after high-pressure torsion (HPT) at 77 K.
summary: This plot displays the Fourier transform of EXAFS functions at the K-Fe edge for Fe58Ni25B17. The HPT-processed sample at 77 K exhibits a higher first-peak amplitude than the MQ sample, indicating increased iron and boron atom density in the nearest coordination sphere and a loss of long-range atomic ordering.

caption: UV–vis transmittance spectra of printed silica disks treated at various temperatures (100–1100 °C) compared to commercial Suprasil® 2B, alongside photographs of disks treated at 100, 250, and 1100 °C.
summary: UV-Vis transmission spectra reveal that printed silica maintains consistent transparency up to 600 °C. Heating to 1100 °C significantly increases density and light transmittance, reaching levels comparable to commercial fused silica. Accompanying photographs illustrate the visual clarity of the disks, confirming the transition toward a denser, more transparent glass state.

caption: Depth profile showing 16O- and 18O- intensity peaks for the 15Cr–10Al alloy oxidized at 800 °C for 200 h, demonstrating high signal intensity at the oxide/alloy interface.
summary: The depth profile plot illustrates the intensity variations of 16O- and 18O- ions across the oxidized 15Cr–10Al alloy surface. Analysis of the intensity peaks confirms that both oxygen isotopes exhibit high signal intensity specifically at the oxide/alloy interface, consistent with the localized enrichment observed in the mapping data.

caption: TGA and DTG data for the sixth catalytic sample, characterizing the thermal decomposition process and identifying stability thresholds.
summary: Panel f displays the TGA and DTG curves for the sixth catalyst sample. These results provide detailed information about the quality and purity of the synthesized CNT. By highlighting weight loss patterns and decomposition rates, the plot offers insights into the thermal stability and decomposition behavior of the catalytic material.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of the 0 wt% Fe sample cross-section, highlighting the chemical composition of the oxide scale.
summary: Representing the 0 wt% Fe sample, this EDS map reveals the elemental distribution within the cross-sectional oxide scale. The analysis provides critical insights into the chemical composition of the layer formed after 10 h of oxidation, supporting the broader microstructural characterization of the oxidized samples presented in the study.

caption: Derivative of dilation curve for a 140 C/s cooling rate, showing the Bi-Gaussian fit applied to characterize the delta to gamma transformation kinetics.
summary: At a cooling rate of 140 C/s, the derivative of dilation is plotted alongside a Bi-Gaussian fit. This analysis allows for the accurate determination of the delta to gamma transformation temperatures, including the start, 80% completion, and finish points, providing insight into the phase change kinetics.

caption: Zoomed-in neutron diffraction patterns at 77 K in the 1.7–2.2 Å range, plotted on a log-scale to highlight peak asymmetry and the emergence of the HCP (10.1) peak.
summary: Detailed neutron diffraction patterns at 77 K, zoomed into the 1.7–2.2 Å range, emphasize peak asymmetry and the emergence of the HCP (10.1) peak. The influence of planar faults on peak asymmetry becomes evident at a true strain of approximately 0.11, confirming the martensitic transformation mechanism.

caption: Normal load response and frictional force profiles recorded during progressive loading scratch experiments on the artificial joint material.
summary: Normal load and frictional force responses are shown for the scratch test. Because the applied mode was progressive loading, the loading force for the four specimens exhibits a linearly increasing trend, which is further evidenced by the scratch morphologies observed in subsequent characterization of the tested material surfaces.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves (M–T) for Ce60Ni25Al15-xGax alloys under a 0.5 T field, featuring an inset that zooms into the low-temperature region below 70 K to show the effect of Ga substitution.
summary: Temperature dependence of magnetization for Ce60Ni25Al15-xGax ribbons was investigated using field-cooling measurements under a 0.5 T magnetic field. The M-T curves reveal that magnetization decreases with increasing Ga content. The inset specifically highlights the low-temperature regime below 70 K, where the sensitivity of magnetization to Ga concentration is clearly observable.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the substrate, EAM, and ECM surfaces.
summary: XRD patterns reveal the phase composition of the substrate, EAM, and ECM surfaces. TiO2 formation is identified across processed surfaces due to melting and dissolving of the titanium alloy. Additionally, the V2C peak is uniquely observed on the ECM surface, distinguishing its phase composition from the EAM.

caption: XPS survey scan of the corrosion layer formed on sample T006 after 24 hours of immersion in AUS.
summary: This XPS survey scan characterizes the corrosion layer on sample T006 after 24 hours in AUS. The analysis indicates the presence of Mg, O, C, and P as major elements. Notably, T006 shows a lower amount of corrosion layer products compared to the T004 and T005 samples.

caption: Energy profiles representing the equation of states for D022 site configurations, comparing a randomly distributed alloying element baseline against scenarios where Ti, Mo, or Al atoms are relocated from Ni sites to Nb sites.
summary: This plot displays the energy profiles derived from equation of state calculations for D022 site configurations. It contrasts a randomly distributed alloying element baseline, labeled as original, with specific atomic relocation scenarios where Ti, Mo, or Al atoms are shifted from Ni sites to Nb sites to evaluate structural stability.

caption: STEM bright-field image of the conventional material after ER cycling at 0.4% strain amplitude and 7001 cycles.
summary: STEM bright-field image of the conventional material after ER cycling at 0.4% strain amplitude and 7001 cycles. This imaging technique confirms the presence of mainly planar dislocation arrangements distributed across multiple slip systems, providing further evidence of the microstructural evolution occurring within the material during the fatigue test.

caption: Frontal view 3D isosurface rendering of sample S4, revealing extensive interlaminar delamination spreading across both concentric rings.
summary: Sample S4 is depicted through a 3D micro-CT isosurface rendering at a 10 μm voxel size. The analysis identifies significant interlaminar delamination that propagates across both concentric rings of the component, illustrating the severity of structural defects detectable through this volumetric porosity assessment technique.

caption: Region 10 (111) equal area projection pole figure displaying the crystallographic texture of the streamlined bridge extrudate.
summary: This (111) equal area projection pole figure depicts the crystallographic texture of region 10 in the streamlined bridge extrudate. The analysis confirms that this region contributes to the complex, non-uniform texture distribution observed across the bridge cross section, which is essential for understanding the local mechanical properties of the material.

caption: Training and validation evaluation metrics for the MPM modality, demonstrating its independent classification performance.
summary: Panel c shows the training and validation metrics for the MPM modality. Although the MPM modality independently achieves strong results, it still exhibits confidence gaps similar to the OT modality. These metrics, including precision and recall, indicate that the model struggles with the Δ +30% VED condition compared to other classes.

caption: Appearance of the initial crack within the HPC-P1 sample under load.
summary: Visible in this panel is the appearance of the first crack in the HPC-P1 sample during the loading test. This stage marks the transition from the intact state to the onset of structural failure, demonstrating the sample's behavior under the applied mechanical stress.

caption: Relative particle displacement map for PSD-3, with green arrows indicating displacement near the gap region.
summary: Relative particle displacement for the PSD-3 condition is shown, with green arrows highlighting movement near the gap region. The expanded energy dissipation zone facilitates the direct supply of intermediate-velocity particles to the gap, consistent with the reduced A h value of 0.421 observed in this specific powder pile configuration.

caption: Boron isopleth diagram for duplex stainless steel showing phase stability as a function of boron content, highlighting compositions at 0.3, 0.6, and 1.2 wt% B.
summary: This isopleth diagram illustrates the thermodynamic solidification pathway for duplex stainless steel as a function of boron content. It identifies primary and secondary boride formation, guiding the selection of hypoeutectic compositions (0.3 and 0.6 wt% B) to assess the influence of boron as a solute on grain refinement.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the INZ region in the XZ-plane, showing grain orientation and morphology.
summary: Inverse Pole Figure mapping of the INZ region in the XZ-plane characterizes the grain orientation and morphology. In this zone, the average grain sizes for CEG and FEG are approximately 22.56 ± 3.32 μm and 10.58 ± 1.27 μm, respectively, highlighting the distinct grain size distribution within the alloy.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of Inconel 718 deformed at temperatures above 900 °C, illustrating clear evidence of dynamic recrystallization.
summary: Captured at temperatures exceeding 900 °C, this inverse pole figure map shows the microstructural evolution of Inconel 718 across a strain rate range of 0.001–10 s⁻¹. The map provides clear evidence of dynamic recrystallization, characterized by lower Kernel Average Misorientation values compared to those observed at the 900 °C deformation temperature.

caption: STEM-EDS elemental distribution mapping of the 4Fe alloy after aging at 1000 °C for 1000 h.
summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping of the 4Fe alloy illustrates the elemental distribution within the γ/γ′ microstructure after aging at 1000 °C for 1000 h. This visualization highlights how the addition of iron influences the chemical partitioning and microstructural stability of the alloy compared to the iron-free baseline composition.

caption: Loading plot derived from Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of all samples, illustrating the contribution of variables to the principal components.
summary: This loading plot represents the results of a Principal Component Analysis performed on all samples. It visualizes the contribution of variables to the defined principal components, providing insight into the underlying structure of the dataset as part of the broader PCA analysis of the experimental samples.

caption: TEM image showing irregular black blocky precipitates exhibiting a wavy morphology characteristic of a eutectic structure.
summary: This TEM image captures irregular black blocky precipitates that exhibit a wavy morphology. These features are indicative of a eutectic structure formed within the material, providing evidence of the solidification behavior and phase distribution characteristics observed in the transition layer interface region.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PGA isolated from GACam after 3 hours of reaction at 190 °C, illustrating the relative abundance of cyclic and linear polymer chains.
summary: Representing the PGA polycondensate obtained from GACam after 3 hours at 190 °C, this mass spectrum demonstrates that cyclic and linear chains remain present in nearly equal quantities. The profile is noted to be almost identical to the polycondensate obtained from GAMes under the same thermal conditions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of pBMSCs cultured on 3D-printed β-TCP scaffolds after 7 days, highlighting increased cell density and ECM production.
summary: At 7 days of culture, pBMSCs on β-TCP scaffolds exhibit high viability and metabolic activity. Fluorescence imaging reveals elongated, oriented cell populations and abundant extracellular matrix synthesis. The green Calcein AM signal confirms that the cells remain healthy and proliferate effectively across the scaffold surface over the one-week period.

caption: Elemental line scanning profile across the bonding interface of DD6 joints processed at 1170 °C and 55 MPa for 6 h, demonstrating a uniform chemical composition across the interface.
summary: After 6 h of bonding at 1170 °C and 55 MPa, the elemental line scan reveals a uniform chemical composition across the joint interface. This indicates that extended bonding time successfully promotes chemical homogeneity, consistent with the observed microstructural uniformity in the DD6 joint.

caption: Predicted creep-fatigue crack growth rates (da/dN) versus stress intensity factor range (ΔK) for annealed AISI 316 stainless steel at 593 °C, comparing SYM-CFCG model predictions with experimental data for various hold times.
summary: This plot displays the SYM-CFCG model predictions for crack growth rates in annealed AISI 316 stainless steel at 593 °C. Observations indicate that crack growth rates remain similar between 0 s and 6 s hold times due to minimal opening stress changes, while 60 s hold times show significantly increased growth rates.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the TiAl MMC at the bottom position, showing crystallographic texture.
summary: Crystallographic orientation at the bottom of the TiAl MMC is visualized through an EBSD IPF map. This data is used to track the evolution of grain size, which demonstrates an ascending trend from the bottom to the top of the sample along the building direction at constant laser power.

caption: Inverse pole figure and constant φ2 = 45° ODF cross-section of reconstructed β grains in SLM samples.
summary: The reconstructed β grains are analyzed via EBSD, with the resulting inverse pole figure and constant φ2 = 45° ODF cross-section presented here. This visualization highlights the specific crystallographic orientation of the columnar grains formed during the selective laser melting process, offering insight into the microstructural evolution of the material.

caption: Polar distribution of parameter l on the 〈011〉 plane for the as-received superalloy, exhibiting a rhombic distribution.
summary: The polar distribution of parameter l on the 〈011〉 plane reveals a characteristic rhombic pattern for the as-received superalloy. Quantitative analysis indicates that the parameter l reaches its maximum values along the [001] and [010] crystallographic orientations, providing a baseline metric for the geometric distribution of the γ' precipitates in the initial state.

caption: Creatbot F430 dual extruder printer utilized for the additive manufacturing of multi-material spar specimens.
summary: The Creatbot F430 dual extruder printer is presented as the primary hardware used for the additive manufacturing process. This equipment enables the fabrication of multi-material spar specimens, highlighting the capability of the dual extrusion system to produce complex structural components through precise layer-by-layer deposition techniques in a controlled environment.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of the culture dish surface near a commercial carbon steel (S45C) plate after 3 days.
summary: MDCK–YFP-keratin-8 cells were cultured with a commercial carbon steel (S45C) plate for 3 days. Fluorescence imaging of the culture dish surface near the plate confirms that the cells did not grow, consistent with the observed corrosion of the S45C plate and its negative impact on cell viability.

caption: Steady-state photolysis profile of TOXE-1 under 365 nm LED irradiation, illustrating the photochemical degradation behavior.
summary: The photochemical properties of TOXE-1 were evaluated through steady-state photodegradation investigations. This panel displays the specific photolysis profile of TOXE-1 when subjected to 365 nm LED light, providing essential data on its degradation kinetics and stability under controlled illumination conditions as part of the broader assessment of TOXE materials.

caption: Topographic map of the HH-TU specimen, highlighting the surface texture post-treatment.
summary: The HH-TU specimen topography map, obtained via 3D profilometry, illustrates the surface characteristics following the HH-TU process. This panel serves to document the surface finish quality, contributing to the overall analysis of how different finishing methods and heat treatments influence the final topography of the specimens.

caption: Predicted radial distribution of LST at the middle ingot height of Z = 0.3 m within the longitudinal section X = 0.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the predicted radial distribution of LST at the middle height of the ingot, specifically at Z = 0.3 m within the longitudinal section X = 0. The visualization provides insight into the thermal state of the material following the solidification process at this specific vertical position.

caption: Non-equilibrium Al-Yb phase diagram at the Al-rich side, highlighting the extended coupled zone (ECZ) in green and experimental data points in purple.
summary: This non-equilibrium Al-Yb phase diagram focuses on the Al-rich region, specifically identifying the extended coupled zone (ECZ) shaded in green. Experimental data points, represented in purple, are plotted with temperatures derived from a eutectic growth model. These results confirm the reliability of the diagram for determining hypoeutectic microstructures.

caption: Engineering power factor (PF)eng plotted as a function of hot side temperature TH.
summary: The engineering power factor (PF)eng is presented as a function of the hot side temperature TH. This plot illustrates the performance characteristics of the material, specifically showing how the engineering power factor evolves as the temperature of the hot side increases during the thermoelectric characterization process.

caption: Stress corrosion cracking (SCC) growth rates of stress-relieved AM SS 316L with 20% cold work compared to wrought SS 316L under NWC (2 ppm DO) and HWC (63 ppb DH) environments.
summary: This plot compares SCC growth rates of AM SS 316L against wrought 316L. Results indicate that HIP + SA LPBF 316L samples exhibit SCC growth rates comparable to those of wrought 316L in both annealed and 20% cold-worked conditions, demonstrating similar environmental resistance in NWC and HWC test environments.

caption: Temperature programmed oxidation profiles of Ni-Fe/γ-Al2O3 catalysts subjected to varying steam to plastic ratios.
summary: Temperature programmed oxidation analysis of Ni-Fe/γ-Al2O3 catalysts reveals the impact of steam injection on carbon deposition. The TPO profiles demonstrate a clear decrease in the amount of carbon deposited on the catalyst surface as the steam to plastic ratio increases, confirming the effectiveness of steam in mitigating carbon formation.

caption: Quantified concentrations of VEGF and bFGF secreted by BMSCs into the culture medium, measured via ELISA for different scaffold groups.
summary: ELISA results quantify the secretion of VEGF and bFGF by BMSCs on various scaffolds. The data validates that BMSCs adhered to AHT scaffolds with UiO-66 modification, particularly the 1/4UiO-66/AHT and 1/2UiO-66/AHT groups, secrete significantly higher levels of these angiogenic growth factors compared to the control.

caption: Cross-sectional EDS elemental mapping of the Gr/AlNiTiCrNb0.15 coating.
summary: This panel presents the cross-sectional EDS elemental mapping of the Gr/AlNiTiCrNb0.15 coating. The visualization provides a detailed spatial distribution of elements within the coating structure, confirming the compositional integrity and elemental arrangement across the cross-section as part of the broader microstructural characterization performed on the material.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profile for Mg–5Ni alloy subjected to pure hydrogen, highlighting peak evolution over successive cycles.
summary: Thermal desorption spectroscopy results for Mg–5Ni alloy in pure hydrogen demonstrate the evolution of desorption peaks across cycles. Notably, the third peak is absent during initial hydrogen cycles but emerges as cycling progresses, indicating structural or chemical changes within the alloy that influence hydrogen release mechanisms over time.

caption: Fracture surface morphology of the HT2000 alloy tested at room temperature.
summary: SEM analysis of the HT2000 alloy fracture surface after 2000 hours of thermal exposure at 800 °C. The surface displays secondary cracks along grain boundaries, tearing ridges, and sparse shallow ductile dimples, consistent with the fracture behavior observed in the HT500h alloy under room-temperature testing conditions.

caption: Optical micrograph of the Ta1 NiTiTa alloy, illustrating the microstructure resulting from vacuum arc remelting.
summary: Ta1 NiTiTa alloy microstructure is visualized through optical microscopy, revealing the matrix phase and reticulated eutectic regions typical of this alloy series. Fabricated via vacuum arc remelting, the sample demonstrates the initial structural characteristics observed in the NiTiTa system with low tantalum content.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile and GP prediction for <200> grains in the axial direction at a radial position of 12 mm.
summary: Presented here is the neutron diffraction peak for <200> oriented grains at the 12 mm radial position. The plot compares the experimental neutron diffraction data, shown as a red solid line, with GP model predictions, providing insight into the lattice strain behavior of these specific grains along the axial direction.

caption: GD-OES depth profile of A59 alloy following transpassive polarization at 1100 mV vs Ag/AgCl, indicating the oxide thickness and elemental distribution changes associated with high-potential anodic treatment.
summary: The GD-OES depth profile for A59 alloy at 1100 mV vs Ag/AgCl illustrates the elemental distribution within the oxide film under transpassive conditions. As shown in the graph, the oxide film undergoes significant changes in its characteristics at this increased anodic polarization potential compared to the passive range results.

caption: Calculated density of states for the γ′ phase with complex composition, highlighting electronic structural features.
summary: This panel displays the density of states for the γ′ phase, which features a complex composition. By comparing this electronic structure to that of bulk Ni3Al, the influence of alloying elements on the electronic properties and potential mechanical performance of the γ′ phase can be evaluated through these computational results.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of HA, HAD, and HADA components acquired in D2O solvent to elucidate the chemical structure and conjugation of the hydrogel microsphere precursors.
summary: 1H NMR spectroscopy was utilized to characterize the structural composition of the hydrogel precursors, specifically HA, HAD, and HADA. By employing D2O as the solvent, the analysis provides detailed insights into the molecular structure and successful chemical modifications achieved during the synthesis of the ABOHA@ZnO hydrogel microspheres.

caption: Illustration of the semi-continuous starved-feed emulsion polymerization process utilized for the synthesis of CSP.
summary: This schematic illustrates the semi-continuous and stepwise emulsion polymerization method employed for the synthesis of CSP. The process is designed to provide controlled particle growth, serving as the foundational methodology for the subsequent preparation of the core-shell particles described in the experimental procedure.

caption: Load versus crack mouth opening displacement (F-CMOD) curve for the 3D printed AARSC specimen with 30% recycled sand content (R30).
summary: The F-CMOD curve for the R30 specimen illustrates the mechanical response of the 3D printed AARSC fracture beam. With a notch-to-depth ratio of 0.2, this plot demonstrates the characteristic quasi-brittle fracture behavior observed consistently across various bonding interfaces and recycled sand contents within the experimental series.

caption: Combined main effect plot illustrating the ideal values for each adjusted process parameter.
summary: This combined main effect plot serves to identify and illustrate the optimal values for each process parameter that requires adjustment. By visualizing these effects, the plot provides a clear guide for determining the ideal settings necessary to achieve desired outcomes within the experimental framework described in the study.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 900 °C, illustrating the phase boundaries and tie-lines calculated via thermodynamic modeling.
summary: Representing the Cu–Ni–S system at 900 °C, this isothermal section integrates experimental data with thermodynamic calculations. The diagram utilizes solid black lines and grey dashed tie-lines derived from FactSage 8.3 and associated databases to illustrate phase relationships, consistent with findings confirmed by Bruwer and the experimental results of this study.

caption: Areal capacitance of microsupercapacitors plotted as a function of ceria nanoparticle loading at a scan rate of 5 mV s-1.
summary: Areal capacitance of the fabricated microsupercapacitors is shown as a function of ceria nanoparticle concentration in the electrodes. This result illustrates that there is an optimum range of ceria nanoparticle concentration to maximize the capacitance of the microsupercapacitors, highlighting the impact of loading on overall electrochemical energy storage performance.

caption: ATR-IR spectra comparing GPTMS, pectin, HAp, Pect1, Pect2, and Pect1-HAp, highlighting the formation of a GPTMS-based network through Si-O-Si and Si-OH bond signals.
summary: The ATR-IR spectra of Pect1, Pect1-HAp, and Pect2 reveal the chemical composition of the pectin-based scaffolds. Analysis confirms the successful formation of a GPTMS-based crosslinking network within the pectin matrix, evidenced by the characteristic appearance of Si-O-Si and Si-OH bonds across the Pect1 and Pect2 samples.

caption: Load-displacement (P-h) curves for the solution-treated Fe–Cr–Ni MEA sample subjected to varying loading rates.
summary: The P-h curves for the solution-treated Fe–Cr–Ni MEA sample demonstrate the influence of loading rate on indentation behavior. As the loading rate increases, the P-h curve shifts toward the left, indicating that the indentation displacement is significantly affected by the rate of load application during the testing process.

caption: Hardness and reduced modulus versus indentation depth for AM IN718 nitrided at 500 °C.
summary: Nanoindentation testing of AM IN718 nitrided at 500 °C reveals significant mechanical property variations within the first 100 nm of the surface layer. Hardness values fluctuate between approximately 7.5 and 19 GPa, with notable scattering observed in measurements at indentation loads exceeding 5 mN up to 10 mN.

caption: Inverse pole figure map showing the grain orientation characteristics observed along the longitudinal section of the ER2209 filler wire.
summary: Representing the longitudinal section of the ER2209 filler wire, this inverse pole figure map provides detailed crystallographic orientation data. The EBSD analysis conducted on this plane highlights the microstructural grain arrangement, contributing to the comprehensive characterization of the filler wire's internal structure as described in the experimental study.

caption: Pole figure representation for label 1 of the GLLS sample, illustrating the crystallographic texture orientation.
summary: This pole figure displays the crystallographic texture for label 1 of the GLLS sample. As part of the broader analysis of GLLS and GSLS samples, this visualization provides insight into the preferred orientation of the material's crystal structure, serving as a key indicator of the sample's microstructural characteristics.

caption: Linear thermal expansion (dL/L) plotted as a function of temperature for FeCoNi and Fe30Co30Ni30Cr10-xMnx alloys.
summary: Linear thermal expansion (dL/L) is plotted against temperature for FeCoNi and Fe30Co30Ni30Cr10-xMnx alloys. These measurements illustrate the thermal expansion behavior across different temperature regimes, including ferromagnetic and paramagnetic states, providing insight into the Invar effect and atomic spacing characteristics within these FCC phase 3d transition metal alloys.

caption: Elastic modulus measurements as a function of irradiation state for 316L steel specimens processed at 1066 °C and 1150 °C.
summary: Elastic modulus data for 316L steel samples are presented, comparing unirradiated and irradiated conditions across two heat treatment temperatures. The measurements reveal that unirradiated samples consistently show a lower elastic modulus than their irradiated counterparts, while the overall values remain consistent with expected mechanical properties for this steel grade.

caption: Stacked bar plot illustrating the feature importance of geochemical elements for Model I, which classifies I-, S-, and A-type parental magmas.
summary: Model I utilizes a stacked bar plot to visualize the relative importance of various geochemical features. This model is specifically designed to distinguish between I-, S-, and A-type parental magmas associated with different deposit types, providing a foundational assessment of feature contributions to the classification task.

caption: Mean Square Displacement (MSD) of the systems during the MD and MC hybrid simulation process under different magnetic induction intensities.
summary: The MSD of the system during the MD and MC hybrid simulation is plotted here to characterize atomic mobility. Notably, the MSD value at 0 ps is excluded from the plot, reflecting the dynamic behavior of the system as it evolves under different magnetic induction intensities throughout the simulation process.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the Al-Zn-Cr alloy manufactured at 100 W laser power, showing distinct peaks corresponding to both pure Al and pure Zn phases.
summary: The XRD pattern for the 100 W LPBF-manufactured Al-Zn-Cr specimen displays characteristic peaks for both pure Al and pure Zn phases. The presence of double peaks is attributed to Kα2 reflections. This sample does not exhibit the solid solution behavior observed at higher laser power processing conditions.

caption: Aggregated confusion matrix illustrating the performance of the support vector machine classifier at k=5 for droplet type prediction.
summary: This aggregated confusion matrix evaluates the support vector machine classifier at k=5. The model demonstrates perfect classification accuracy for no-droplet types and achieves a 99% success rate in identifying normal droplets, representing a notable improvement over the 98% accuracy previously observed at k=3 for the same classification task.

caption: High-resolution image of precipitates and characterization of phase interfaces in sample C-Ⅱ.
summary: This high-resolution image provides a detailed view of the precipitates and their associated phase interfaces in the LPBF-fabricated superalloy. The characterization of these interfaces is vital for understanding the stability and mechanical properties of the precipitated phases within the nickel-based matrix after the rapid solidification process.

caption: Statistical distribution of grain lengths in logarithmic scale, highlighting the emergence of short grains near the melt pool boundary and center alongside an increase in long grains in Zone II.
summary: The grain length distribution shows a complex evolution following the rescan. While there is a notable emergence of shorter grains near the melt pool boundary and center, the data also indicates an increment in the number of longer grains within Zone II, demonstrating a shift in the grain morphology distribution.

caption: CV reversibility test of 1.6 M V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) performed at varying scan rates to evaluate electrochemical kinetics.
summary: This reversibility test evaluates the electrochemical kinetics of the V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) electrolyte by applying different scan rates. The data demonstrates the redox behavior and kinetic response of the system, supporting the conclusion that the PdNi/NrGO (1:1) catalyst provides superior catalytic site accessibility and enhanced redox activity.

caption: Detailed view of the cutting path along the header area of the prototype.
summary: This schematic illustrates the specific cutting path utilized along the header area of the heat exchanger prototype. By defining the sectioning process, this view clarifies how the internal header geometry is accessed and inspected, providing essential context for the structural evaluation of the prototype's fluid distribution components.

caption: STEM image of rGO/Al with corresponding EELS spectra collected from five distinct positions, featuring an HRTEM inset.
summary: This panel presents a STEM image of the rGO/Al composite following the thermal reduction of GO/PVA/Al. EELS spectra were acquired from five specific points to analyze the composition. The HRTEM inset confirms that rGO remains present at the interface even after the thermal treatment process used for GO reduction.

caption: Laboratory-scale centrifuge unit utilized for experimental testing at Fraunhofer IKTS.
summary: This laboratory centrifuge serves as one of the two primary testing apparatuses available at the Fraunhofer IKTS facility. It is specifically employed for experimental procedures requiring controlled centrifugal forces, as documented in the research study to support the evaluation of material processing parameters under laboratory conditions.

caption: Absorbance spectrum of a PEDOT:PSS solid thin film measured from 250 to 3000 nm.
summary: This panel displays the optical absorbance spectrum of a PEDOT:PSS solid thin film. The data was acquired using a UV–VIS-NIR spectrometer across a broad wavelength range from 250 to 3000 nm, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's optical absorption characteristics in the ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared regions.

caption: Simulated Selected Area Electron Diffraction (SAED) pattern for the 14H phase oriented along the [0001] zone axis.
summary: Displayed is the simulated SAED pattern for the 14H phase along the [0001] zone axis. This simulation completes the set of diffraction patterns for the primary zone axes, providing a comprehensive theoretical basis for confirming the crystal structure and orientation of the analyzed 14H phase.

caption: Calculated subband energy profile of a GaAs/AlAs heterostructure at a high bias voltage of 17.2 V, highlighting the alignment of the L-valley subband in the GaAs Q1 layer with the X11 subband in the AlAs barrier and the X21 ground state in the B2 layer.
summary: This band structure diagram illustrates the electronic configuration of a GaAs/AlAs heterostructure under a 17.2 V bias. Precise calculations reveal that the L-valley subband in GaAs Q1 aligns with the AlAs X11 subband. This energy proximity causes the barrier between X and L states to vanish, facilitating inter-layer electronic coupling.

caption: Solute B concentration evolution in pre-annealed A-1%B-1%C ternary alloys, where initial solute clusters are present, plotted against dose for different sink plane separation distances.
summary: This panel displays solute B concentration evolution in pre-annealed A-1%B-1%C ternary alloys, which were pre-seeded with solute clusters. The simulation accounts for a defect production rate of 10-5 dpa/s. Comparisons across different sink plane separation distances reveal that larger L3 values lead to increased recombination fractions during the irradiation process.

caption: Annular dark field STEM micrograph of the Al83.5Ni8.0Sm6.5Pb2.0 ribbon, highlighting the orange square region selected for elemental mapping.
summary: This annular dark field STEM micrograph provides a magnified view of the Al83.5Ni8.0Sm6.5Pb2.0 alloy microstructure. The image highlights a specific orange square region that serves as the area of interest for subsequent X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy elemental mapping, allowing for a detailed correlation between the observed structural features and chemical composition.

caption: Magnified view of the 316L-rich region of the pseudo-binary phase diagram, providing detailed equilibrium phase predictions for low AlSi10Mg concentrations.
summary: The magnified portion of the 316L-rich side of the pseudo-binary phase diagram provides a detailed view of equilibrium phase predictions at lower AlSi10Mg concentrations. This region is critical for analyzing metastable microstructures, such as the supersaturated B2 FeAl matrix observed in 80% 316L compositions, which deviates from the predicted two-phase equilibrium.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the copper side, highlighting the spatial arrangement of constituent elements.
summary: The elemental distribution map reveals the chemical composition across the copper side of the 550 °C sample. By visualizing the spatial arrangement of elements, this map supports the characterization of Fe-rich precipitates, confirming their presence and distribution within the copper matrix as part of the overall microstructural evolution analysis.

caption: Strength–conductivity map comparing the performance of processed aluminum wires.
summary: This strength–conductivity map evaluates the performance trade-offs in the processed aluminum wires. By plotting strength against electrical conductivity, the figure illustrates the effectiveness of the dual-gradient architecture in achieving optimized properties, providing a clear visualization of how the processing parameters influence the material's functional performance.

caption: Transient fluorescence decay curves comparing the charge carrier lifetimes of g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 and pure Bi2MoO6.
summary: Transient fluorescence spectra reveal a prolonged photogenerated carrier lifetime in the g-C3N4/Bi2MoO6 heterojunction compared to pure Bi2MoO6. This extended lifetime correlates directly with a higher charge carrier separation efficiency, providing a mechanistic explanation for the enhanced photocatalytic activity observed in the composite catalyst system.

caption: Core roughness parameter Rk values for fan samples produced via standard and assisted L-PBF modes.
summary: Core roughness values relative to the profile center are displayed for various L-PBF modes. The data indicates that Rk values remain similar across all sound modes and are closely aligned with the MSH mode, demonstrating consistent core surface characteristics regardless of the specific assisted or standard L-PBF processing technique employed.

caption: Bulk atomic model of amorphous silica, illustrating the disordered atomic arrangement utilized for particle extraction.
summary: Shown here is the bulk atomic model of amorphous silica. This structure is used alongside the borosilicate glass model to derive silica particles, with surface atoms slightly modified to maintain electrical neutrality. The model represents the disordered, amorphous state of silica required for the study's structural investigations.

caption: Thermal analysis curves contrasting the DSC profiles of IN-F and SF 3D printed materials.
summary: This panel shows the DSC curves for IN-F and SF composites, contributing to the evaluation of thermal properties in the 3D printed samples. By comparing these specific curves, the study characterizes the thermal response of the materials, consistent with the overall DSC testing methodology described in the research findings.

caption: Random Forest model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: Random Forest model performance is evaluated using a confusion matrix. This visualization displays the classification accuracy and error distribution for the algorithm after the training process, providing a clear representation of how well the model predicts the target classes based on the provided dataset.

caption: Evolution of axial and radial lattice strains measured in situ for both A356 and 316 L constituents during the mechanical loading experiment.
summary: In situ measurements of axial and radial lattice strains for the A356 and 316 L constituents are presented. These strain data serve as the primary input for Eqs. 1 and 2, enabling the calculation of corresponding lattice stresses and the rule-of-mixtures axial stress to characterize the composite's mechanical response.

caption: Surface topography of a Py (5 nm)/C60 (3 nm) bilayer, showing the C60 layer with an average lateral grain size of approximately 15 nm.
summary: The AFM image reveals the surface of a Py (5 nm)/C60 (3 nm) bilayer. Although the average lateral grain size of the topmost C60 layer is around 15 nm, the surface roughness increases significantly compared to the bare Py film, reaching a root-mean-square value of 0.43 nm.

caption: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) orientation map of the region highlighted in (a), colored by crystal orientation relative to the X-axis, with solid black lines indicating the location of the FIB cross-sectional cut.
summary: The EBSD map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the S150 specimen in the region highlighted in panel (a), with colors representing orientations relative to the X-axis. Solid black lines delineate the specific site where a FIB cross-sectional cut was performed to facilitate subsequent microstructural analysis of the material.

caption: Porosity distribution analysis for sample 25.1.
summary: Sample 25.1 is analyzed for porosity, completing the set of eight samples examined in this study. This histogram illustrates the void distribution, providing necessary structural context for the average overall mechanical responses observed, thereby facilitating a deeper understanding of the material's properties and its performance consistency.

caption: XPS spectrum of GH4169 alloy processed via continuous repeated heat input mode.
summary: XPS analysis of the GH4169 specimen fabricated using continuous repeated heat input mode reveals surface chemical states. This technique is highly sensitive to variations in crystal structure, allowing for a detailed investigation of the material's surface composition as influenced by the specific thermal input mode applied during the fabrication process.

caption: SHAP values representing the relative influence of various features on yield strength (YS) predictions, identifying the presence or absence of the αʺ phase as the most significant factor across all evaluated models.
summary: This SHAP summary plot illustrates the relative importance of different features in predicting yield strength. The analysis highlights that the presence or absence of the αʺ phase is the most influential factor across all models, demonstrating its critical role in determining the mechanical performance of the studied materials.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loop illustrating the magnetization behavior of the annealed or heat-treated LPBF Fe-Co-2 V alloy specimen.
summary: Presented here is the M-H hysteresis curve for the Fe-Co-2 V alloy following an annealing or heat-treatment process. The graph maps magnetization against the applied magnetic field, providing a clear comparison of the magnetic properties of the material after undergoing thermal processing compared to the as-built condition.

caption: Nine-cell series SMFC configuration connected to the low-power IoT node.
summary: A nine-cell series SMFC is depicted, which is connected to a customized low-power IoT node capable of conducting sensing and communication tasks. This configuration serves as the primary power source for the IoT node, demonstrating the practical application of SMFCs in powering remote sensing electronics.

caption: Surface normal direction inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the R2 region following hot torsion deformation at 1070 °C and a strain rate of 0.1 s⁻¹.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution within the R2 region of a sample subjected to hot torsion at 1070 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹. The map provides a detailed visualization of the surface normal direction, characterizing the microstructural state resulting from these specific thermomechanical processing conditions.

caption: Nyquist plots comparing the electrochemical impedance of P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL electrodes, featuring an inset circuit model used for fitting charge transfer resistance.
summary: Nyquist plots for P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL electrodes reveal electrochemical performance differences. The PPI-SL electrode exhibits a larger semicircle diameter, indicating higher charge transfer resistance (Rct) at the electrode-electrolyte interface. Rct values were determined by fitting the EIS data to the equivalent circuit model shown in the inset.

caption: Young's modulus plotted against relative density for stochastic and periodic cellular structures, showing numerical results fitted with Gibson-Ashby scaling power laws.
summary: This panel displays a Gibson-Ashby chart illustrating the scaling of the elastic compressive modulus for cellular materials relative to their density. The data, derived from finite element analysis of defect-free lattice structures, compares stochastic and periodic architectures, with solid and dashed lines representing the respective power law fits for each.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectral changes of methylene blue mixed with NaBH4 in the absence of SL-NiNPs.
summary: This panel displays the UV-visible absorption spectral alterations of methylene blue when combined with NaBH4 without the presence of SL-NiNPs. The data illustrates the baseline behavior of the dye solution under these specific conditions, serving as a control to evaluate the catalytic degradation performance of the SL-NiNPs.

caption: Correlation between free volume fraction and the natural logarithm of viscosity for the Ti–Al–Ni ternary alloy system, featuring a solid line fit derived from the Doolittle equation.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between free volume fraction and the natural logarithm of viscosity in Ti–Al–Ni ternary alloys. The data points are fitted to the Doolittle equation, which is represented by a solid line, confirming an exponential correlation between the free volume fraction and the material's viscosity.

caption: Calculated phase diagram for the local chemical composition of the first 316L layer deposited on Inconel 625 substrate at low laser power.
summary: This phase diagram depicts the equilibrium phases for the first 316L layer deposited on Inconel 625 at low laser power. By comparing this to the high-power variant, the influence of varying processing parameters on the local chemical composition and subsequent phase evolution at the material interface can be effectively analyzed.

caption: Three-dimensional response surface depicting the cure depth response under the interaction of reactive monomer and reactive diluent combinations.
summary: Representing the interaction between reactive monomers and reactive diluents, this response surface highlights the resulting variations in cure depth. The matrix construction allows for a systematic dissection of synergistic effects, demonstrating how the choice of these specific resin components dictates the final optical-curing-rheological performance of the material.

caption: Modified Ellingham diagram illustrating oxide reduction temperatures for AISI-4340 using H2 and C-based redox reactions, with thermodynamic data derived from literature and the SGTE database.
summary: This modified Ellingham diagram evaluates the reducibility of oxides in AISI-4340. It quantifies reduction temperatures for H2 and C-based reductants, excluding Si-based oxides due to their high thermal stability. The diagram establishes a densification threshold for C-based reactions, approximated by the solidus temperature range of 1435–1445 °C.

caption: Macroscopic view of the PC/AA6061 joint failure mode following fatigue testing at 40%, 50%, and 70% of the ULSF, highlighting the transverse brittle fracture of the polycarbonate component adjacent to the metal insert edge.
summary: This photograph illustrates the failure mode of PC/AA6061 joints produced under optimized C4 conditions after fatigue testing at various ULSF levels. The specimens exhibit a characteristic transverse brittle fracture in the polycarbonate section near the AA6061 insert interface, which corresponds to the net-tension failure observed during cyclic loading experiments.

caption: X-ray diffraction peak profiles of as-received non-stick cookware samples from various manufacturers, highlighting the presence of α-Al and FeAl3 phases.
summary: This XRD pattern analysis of as-received non-stick cookware from different manufacturers identifies the crystalline phases present in the material. The diffraction profiles reveal the existence of α-Al and FeAl3 phases, which are consistent with the standard processing conditions and metallurgical composition of the corresponding aluminum alloys used in these pans.

caption: Surviving Ni, Fe, and Cr vacancies in a NiFeCr alloy after a 50 keV classical MD cascade simulation at 80 ps.
summary: Represented in this panel are the surviving vacancy defects in a NiFeCr alloy following a 50 keV classical MD cascade simulation at 80 ps. The distribution of Ni, Fe, and Cr vacancies serves as the reference point for evaluating the impact of electronic stopping and 2T-MD models on vacancy formation.

caption: Polycrystalline structure GS20 generated via Voronoi tessellation with a mean grain size of 20 nm, where colors indicate varying grain orientation angles.
summary: The GS20 polycrystalline model is established using the Voronoi tessellation method, representing a structure with a mean grain size of 20 nm. Distinct colors are applied to the grains to visualize varying orientation angles, providing a clear structural representation of the material at this specific grain size scale.

caption: Tensile stress–strain curves comparing MEX D2 and Wrought D2 steel specimens.
summary: Tensile stress–strain curves are presented for D2 tool steel produced via Material Extrusion (MEX) and wrought processing. This comparison illustrates the mechanical response of the two manufacturing routes, providing a baseline for evaluating the performance of the MEX-fabricated material against the conventional wrought standard under tensile loading conditions.

caption: Atomic model of the hcp Fe0.84Ni0.04Si0.04S0.08H0.3 alloy unit cell, illustrating the substitutional occupancy of Fe sites by Ni, Si, and S atoms alongside the interstitial occupancy of octahedral sites by H atoms.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the hcp crystal structure of an Fe0.84Ni0.04Si0.04S0.08H0.3 alloy. Fe, Ni, Si, and S atoms occupy substitutional sites, while H atoms occupy octahedral interstitial sites. The visualization, generated via VESTA, demonstrates the KKR-CPA method's capability to model partial site occupancy for complex compositional ranges.

caption: Dark-field TEM image revealing the presence of cuboidal large γ′ phases in the HIP sample.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the HIP sample highlights the morphology of the γ′ precipitates. Specifically, this panel reveals the presence of cuboidal large γ′ phases. This technique complements the bright-field and diffraction data by isolating specific phase contributions to the microstructure, confirming the successful growth of these strengthening precipitates.

caption: In situ SANS scattering curves for sample VB73, previously fatigue-cycled at 700 °C, during a thermal cycle of RT-700 °C-RT.
summary: Sample VB73, which underwent prior fatigue cycling at 700 °C, shows SANS scattering curves during an in situ thermal cycle to 700 °C. The analysis confirms that the sample already contained small precipitates measuring approximately 60 Å prior to the in situ heating measurement.

caption: Energy absorption efficiency (η) versus density for SLS 3D-printed MWCNT/PA12 honeycombs compared to various lightweight lattice structures under out-of-plane (OP) and in-plane (IP) loading conditions.
summary: This Ashby plot compares the energy absorption efficiency of MWCNT/PA12 honeycombs against literature data. The structures exhibit high efficiency values of 53% and 37% under OP and IP loading, respectively. Results indicate a weak dependence on density, with only specific nylon gyroid and CNT/PPR lattices showing superior performance in this range.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification curves illustrating the phase evolution during cooling.
summary: Scheil-Gulliver solidification curves provide a predictive model for the phase evolution during the cooling of the alloy interface. These calculations confirm that the phase composition at the interface differs significantly from the surrounding deposited layers, highlighting the non-equilibrium nature of the solidification process at the heterogeneous junction.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image of the nanocrystalline Ni(Fe) specimen after heating to 375 °C in the DSC, a temperature corresponding to the completion of the exothermic peak B.
summary: Microstructural examination via bright-field TEM was performed on the nanocrystalline Ni(Fe) alloy after it was heated to 375 °C in the DSC. This temperature marks the completion of the exothermic peak B, allowing for the observation of the specimen's microstructure following the thermal energy release associated with that specific peak.

caption: Fatigue crack growth rates for S + DA samples at 650 °C, 0.1 Hz, and R = 0.5, comparing X-Z and Z-X orientations, with an inset showing the crack deflection path.
summary: This plot displays fatigue crack growth rates at 650 °C for S + DA samples. The X-Z orientation shows high initial growth rates following deflection, while Z-X samples exhibit threshold growth at 12 MPa m 1/2 before extreme crack path deflection. Inset images confirm significant crack deflection from the mode I plane.

caption: KPFM image of the sample containing precipitates, revealing the spatial distribution of surface potential.
summary: The KPFM image displays the surface potential of the sample containing precipitates. Observations indicate that Laves phases are consistently located within the channels of intergranular oxidation. This spatial correlation suggests that these precipitates play a significant role in the localized corrosion processes occurring within the oxidized grain boundary regions.

caption: Parity plots comparing predicted versus experimental mechanical property values for the CP-S-P model across different kernels.
summary: These parity plots visualize the agreement between predicted and experimental mechanical property values using the CP-S-P model. By comparing different kernels, the plots demonstrate how the inclusion of microstructural descriptors alongside composition and thermal history influences the predictive accuracy of the model across various mechanical properties.

caption: Polar plot of Young’s modulus and shear modulus for a comparative cubic orthotropic material, illustrating maximum stiffness aligned with or perpendicular to the material deposition direction.
summary: This polar plot presents the Young’s modulus and shear modulus for a different cubic orthotropic material across various deposition directions. Unlike the stainless steel sample, this material exhibits maximum stiffness when aligned either parallel or perpendicular to the deposition direction, serving as a comparative reference for the observed anisotropic mechanical behavior.

caption: Ti–Al binary phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions of various intermetallic compounds as a function of temperature and composition.
summary: The Ti–Al binary phase diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the thermodynamic stability of titanium-aluminum alloys. It serves as a critical reference for identifying intermetallic compounds, specifically designating those with an aluminum atomic percentage exceeding 10% as TiAl-based alloys, which are essential for understanding phase transformations in this material system.

caption: Digital reconstruction of the fracture surface profile highlighting the non-flat topography and crack plane transition.
summary: Digital reconstruction of the fracture surface reveals a non-flat topography. A distinct change in the crack plane occurs in the middle of the surface, highlighted in red at a higher altitude. This 3D representation confirms the complex crack path and surface variations observed in the 0/90 Vertical configuration.

caption: As-built thin-wall structure S2 51, fabricated with a 50 mm deposition length and 51 layers, exhibiting visible macro-cracks circled in blue.
summary: The S2 51 thin-wall structure, with a 50 mm deposition length and 51 layers, displays visible macro-cracks on its surface. The reference confirms that macro-cracks are observed in samples with a 50 mm deposition length when the number of layers exceeds 30, highlighting the susceptibility of this specific geometry to cracking.

caption: Schematic representation of the 2:1 MBB beam design domain, illustrating the boundary conditions and the distribution of 231 CS-RBF support points marked by blue crossmarks.
summary: This schematic illustrates the 2:1 MBB beam design domain and its associated boundary conditions. The domain is discretized into 80,000 quadrilateral finite elements, with 231 CS-RBF support points, indicated by blue crossmarks, distributed on a regular grid to define the support radius and structural constraints for the beam design problem.

caption: Atom maps overlaid with an 8 at. % Ni iso-concentration surface, highlighting the morphology and distribution of the Ni-rich G-phase precipitates.
summary: The 8 at. % Ni iso-concentration surface, visualized within the 3D atom probe reconstruction, clearly delineates the Ni-rich G-phase precipitates in the 0.75Nb alloy aged for 2 h. This surface confirms the presence of distinct precipitates, which exhibit a square morphology after this specific aging duration.

caption: Normalised confusion matrix illustrating the predictive performance of the tuned model across all defined classes.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed visualization of the predictions generated by the tuned model. By presenting the data in a normalized format, it effectively illustrates the model's classification accuracy and performance across each specific class, serving as a key diagnostic tool for evaluating the model's overall predictive capability.

caption: Z-orientation Al-bronze block fabricated via CSAM from a Cu-Al powder mix, showing the build direction relative to the substrate.
summary: This panel displays a Z-oriented Al-bronze block produced through CSAM using a Cu-Al powder mixture. The image illustrates the specific printing orientation relative to the substrate, which is one of the two distinct conditions used to evaluate the structural characteristics of the 3D printed metallic components in this study.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a 30 nm cube processed at LED = 0.2 J/mm and h = 0.06 mm, featuring more isotropic Cr-rich and Al-rich regions with an E* value of 5.22.
