summary: Representing the sample processed at 0.2 J/mm, this APT reconstruction shows a more isotropic distribution of Cr-rich and Al-rich regions compared to the lower energy density sample. The analysis confirms the absence of gamma-prime precipitation, with Cr-rich regions defined by 9.5 at.% iso-surfaces and Al-rich regions by cyan points.

caption: EBSD-IPF map of the SLM sample produced at a lower energy density, revealing a refined grain structure on the XOZ plane.
summary: Characterization of this SLM sample on the XOZ plane reveals a distinct refinement in grain size associated with the decrease in energy density. This EBSD-IPF map confirms that lower energy input during the selective laser melting process effectively promotes the formation of finer grains within the material microstructure.

caption: EEL spectra extracted from the entire data cube, displaying the characteristic absorption edges for Nb M4,5, Ti L3,2, and Cr L3,2 elements.
summary: Extracted from the full EELS data cube, this spectrum highlights the presence of Nb, Ti, and Cr within the VDM 780-b sample. The identified Nb M4,5, Ti L3,2, and Cr L3,2 absorption edges confirm the elemental composition, which was subsequently utilized to map the spatial distribution of these specific elements.

caption: Frank loop interaction with a neighboring perfect loop in NiFe after 4 minutes and 10 seconds of ion irradiation, corresponding to a dose of 1.2 dpa.
summary: At an irradiation time of 4 minutes and 10 seconds, equivalent to a dose of 1.2 dpa, the Frank loop is shown contacting a neighboring perfect loop. This TEM micrograph highlights the structural interaction between the loops within the NiFe specimen under the specified WBDF imaging conditions.

caption: Experimentally determined displacement transmission of the metamaterials, where red shaded zones denote the observed band gaps.
summary: Experimental displacement transmission measurements for the metamaterials reveal the actual band gaps, indicated by red shaded regions. These results show good agreement with the simulated band structures, confirming the effectiveness of the attenuation mechanism for long waves in the quasi-zero stiffness elements manufactured by laser powder bed fusion.

caption: Voltage-time charging curves for a 1 μF capacitor using lattices obtained by solvent exchange (PVDF/VB2-0.8 H2O) and solvent evaporation (PVDF/VB2-0.8) over a 300-second interval.
summary: The charging curves illustrate the performance of the lattices in powering a 1 μF capacitor. The solvent-exchanged lattice (PVDF/VB2-0.8 H2O) demonstrates superior charging capability, reaching 5 V within 300 seconds. This highlights the efficiency of the solvent-exchange-assisted printing method in producing high-performance piezoelectric energy harvesters compared to solvent evaporation.

caption: Pole figure illustrating the crystallographic orientation relationship between the delta phase and the matrix.
summary: This pole figure depicts the crystallographic orientation relationship between the delta phase and the matrix at the serrated grain boundary. It confirms the specific orientation of the delta phase precipitates, which is essential for understanding the mechanism behind the formation of the observed saw-tooth grain boundary patterns.

caption: Storage and loss moduli profiles for base and bioactive PLA materials, highlighting differences in viscoelastic behavior.
summary: Both storage and loss moduli of the bioactive PLA materials demonstrate distinct differences relative to the base PLA polymer. These variations in the mechanical response curves indicate that the addition of the bioadditive alters the viscoelastic properties of the PLA matrix, affecting its overall performance under dynamic mechanical testing conditions.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectra comparing rPET specimens printed with varying infill ratios to assess structural integrity.
summary: ATR-FTIR spectroscopy was utilized to investigate structural modifications in rPET specimens following the 3D printing process. The spectra illustrate the chemical characteristics of rPET samples printed at different infill ratios, providing insight into potential polymer degradation or structural changes induced by the additive manufacturing process compared to the raw material.

caption: Radar chart providing a comparative assessment of mass-specific energy dissipation capabilities, represented by specific energy absorption (SEA), for CG and SG samples.
summary: Specific energy absorption (SEA) is visualized in this radar chart to assess the mass-specific energy dissipation capabilities of all CG and SG samples. This plot serves as a comparative tool to evaluate how effectively different structural configurations dissipate energy relative to their mass.

caption: Simulated temperature evolution profiles across 25 deposited layers (L1 to L25) for three distinct dwell time conditions (τ = 10, 40, and 180 s), plotted against normalized time t*.
summary: This simulation illustrates the thermal history of 25 individual layers during a deposition process. By normalizing time as t* = t / (t0 + τ), the plot compares temperature evolution across three specific dwell times (10, 40, and 180 s), providing critical insight into the thermal profiles experienced by each layer during fabrication.

caption: Catalyst conversion in resin ECC-8 plotted against 405 nm irradiation time, derived from the normalized C-H peak intensity at 1640 cm-1 at 25 and 50 °C.
summary: Catalyst conversion in resin ECC-8 is monitored by tracking the normalized C-H peak at 1640 cm-1 over 405 nm irradiation time. The data, collected at 25 and 50 °C, demonstrates the kinetics of catalyst release. The 1595 cm-1 peak was specifically chosen for calculation due to its flat baseline, minimizing measurement error.

caption: Hardness values measured via nanoindentation for the main phases within a sample treated at 700 MPa and 1200 °C.
summary: Hardness data for the main phases are displayed for a sample processed at 700 MPa and 1200 °C. The results were gathered using specific nanoindentation techniques, with care taken to discard any indentations made in pores or at the interfaces between adjacent phases to ensure precise phase-specific mechanical characterization.

caption: Reconstructed 3D atomic model of the η-Cu6Sn5 crystal structure represented as a 1 × 1 × 5 supercell.
summary: This panel displays the 3D atomic model of the η-Cu6Sn5 crystal structure. The model is constructed as a 1 × 1 × 5 supercell, which contains a total of 10 Sn atoms and 12 Cu atoms, providing a detailed visualization of the stoichiometric arrangement within the crystal lattice.

caption: Intermediate-magnification HAADF-STEM image of the Al-Zn-Cr specimen, highlighting the substructure and the distribution of Zn particles within the cell interiors.
summary: Captured at intermediate magnification, this HAADF-STEM image provides a clearer view of the substructure in the Al-Zn-Cr specimen. It specifically illustrates the presence of nanosized Zn particles located at the cell interiors, alongside Zn solute segregation at the grain and cell boundaries, confirming the complex microstructural arrangement of the alloy.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of amorphous Vit105 following the PECM process, displaying surface topography over a 10 μm × 10 μm area.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image captures the surface topography of amorphous Vit105 after the PECM process. The visualization covers a 10 μm × 10 μm area, utilizing a representative absolute height scale and relative color coding to illustrate surface height variations, which remain within the nanometer range typical for this material.

caption: Grain Orientation Spread (GOS) maps of the Cu-2.5Ni-0.6Si alloy after N = 0.5, 1, 5, and 10 turns of HPT processing.
summary: GOS maps provide a visualization of the grain-level orientation homogeneity in the Cu-2.5Ni-0.6Si alloy. As the number of HPT turns increases, the maps demonstrate the evolution of the microstructure, showing a progressive increase in the fraction of dynamically recrystallized (DRX) grains throughout the processed alloy samples.

caption: Confusion matrix showing the LCNN model's classification outcomes for pore status in Test-3, providing a quantitative assessment of detection reliability under the third brightness condition.
summary: This confusion matrix details the LCNN model's pore status detection accuracy for Test-3. By comparing correct and wrong detection samples, it highlights the model's strong resistance to brightness change interference, confirming that the detection performance remains consistent and reliable across the different brightness conditions tested in the study.

caption: Schematic representation indicating the specific longitudinal section position used for EBSD mapping in the as-built Ti-6Al-4V samples.
summary: This schematic diagram defines the precise location and orientation of the EBSD mapping performed on the longitudinal sections of the as-built samples. It serves as a reference for interpreting the spatial context of the microstructural data presented in the corresponding inverse pole figure maps for samples T0 through T4.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectra of P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene, highlighting the n→π∗ transition of the azomethine group at 413 nm and the π→π∗ transition of the benzene ring at 328 nm for PPI-SL.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectra for P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene are presented. PPI-SL exhibits two distinct absorption bands at 413 nm and 328 nm, which are attributed to the n→π∗ transition of the azomethine group and the π→π∗ transition of the benzene ring, respectively, providing insight into the electronic transitions.

caption: Summary table of the laser parameters utilized during the LPBF fabrication process.
summary: Laser parameters applied during the LPBF process are detailed here, specifically highlighting a powder layer thickness of 60 μm and a hatch spacing of 90 μm. These parameters are essential for controlling the thermal history and solidification characteristics of the specimens during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Averaged pyrometer cooling curves for ten layers across various laser power settings, plotted on a semi-logarithmic scale to highlight the solidus, crystallization, and glass-transition temperatures.
summary: Averaged pyrometer cooling curves for ten layers across various laser power settings are plotted on a semi-logarithmic scale. The data reveals an approximately linear trend, indicating that cooling dynamics follow a power-law relationship rather than simple exponential decay. Horizontal lines denote the solidus, crystallization, and glass-transition temperatures for each setting.

caption: EDS point analysis results summarizing the elemental composition of the corrosion products identified in the thin scale (a) and the multi-layered nodule (b) on the Fe-25Cr surface.
summary: This table presents quantitative EDS point analysis data for the corrosion products observed in panels (a) and (b). By comparing the elemental compositions of the thin scale and the multi-layered nodule, the analysis provides insight into the chemical differences between the protective scale and the localized nodular corrosion products.

caption: Correction factors, peak integrated intensities, and resulting pole figure intensities for the (200) diffraction peak, illustrating the data processing workflow.
summary: This panel details the processing steps for the (200) diffraction peak, including the application of correction factors, peak integrated intensities, and the calculation of pole figure intensities. These components are critical for refining experimental neutron diffraction data, ensuring accurate representation of the material's crystallographic texture and orientation distribution.

caption: Corrosion resistance evaluation showing self-corrosion current density for PF-LB-PBF-processed TiZrHfTa RHEA versus unprocessed alloy and various HEAs.
summary: The PF-LB-PBF-processed TiZrHfTa RHEA exhibits a significantly lower self-corrosion current density compared to both the unprocessed alloy and the majority of HEAs documented in the literature. This result confirms that the PF-LB-PBF processing technique substantially enhances the corrosion resistance of the TiZrHfTa RHEA material.

caption: Width distribution of the α′ phase as a function of laser scanning speed.
summary: Statistical results for the width of the α′ phase are presented for various laser scanning speeds. The data reveals that higher scanning speeds lead to a reduction in the width of the α′ phase, consistent with the observed trend of decreasing grain dimensions under increased processing speeds.

caption: Magnetic susceptibility χ versus temperature for the aged sample, featuring a significantly weaker response and reduced temperature dependence compared to the as-received state, with an inset showing the non-linear inverse susceptibility curve.
summary: The aged sample displays a magnetic susceptibility that is significantly weaker and less temperature-dependent than the as-received sample. The inverse susceptibility versus temperature curve shown in the inset deviates from linearity, indicating that the aged material exhibits complex magnetic behavior that differs substantially from the Curie paramagnetism observed previously.

caption: Designed 3D model of the 3 × 3 × 3 RD structure array.
summary: The 3D model depicts a 3 × 3 × 3 array of the rhombic dodecahedron unit cells. This representation illustrates the macroscopic lattice structure resulting from the periodic arrangement of the RD unit cell, facilitating an assessment of the overall structural morphology and porosity of the RD design.

caption: Time-dependent UV-Vis absorption spectra showing the photolysis of O-12 under 365 nm LED irradiation in air.
summary: The panel illustrates the steady-state photolysis of O-12 in acetonitrile. The absorption spectra highlight the molecule's capacity to undergo cleavage at 365 nm. This specific photoinitiator exhibits the fastest cleavage rate among the tested compounds, consistent with its high molar extinction coefficient at the irradiation wavelength.

caption: Bright field TEM image of Fe–Mn–Al–C steel processed at a laser scanning speed of 1400 mm/s.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging of the Fe–Mn–Al–C sample processed at 1400 mm/s demonstrates the microstructural evolution at high scanning speeds. Observations indicate a reduction in dislocation density within the bright field image compared to samples processed at lower speeds, reflecting changes in the material's defect structure.

caption: Specific yield strength comparison between the investigated alloy and various commercial Ni-superalloys.
summary: This plot benchmarks the specific yield strength of the developed material against established commercial Ni-superalloys. By comparing these mechanical performance metrics, the figure highlights the competitive strength-to-weight ratio of the studied alloy, positioning it within the context of current high-performance materials used in demanding structural applications.

caption: Velocity autocorrelation function for Al atoms in Al50Cu25Ni25 melt at 1400 K, comparing AIMD (solid blue) and DNNP (red dashed) results.
summary: The velocity autocorrelation function for Al atoms in the Al50Cu25Ni25 melt at 1400 K is shown. This plot compares the dynamic data derived from AIMD simulations, represented by solid blue lines, against the predictions from DNNP simulations, shown as red dashed lines, to validate the accuracy of the machine learning potential.

caption: Mapping of un-melted powder distribution within a NiTi alloy sample processed under low energy density conditions.
summary: Elemental mapping reveals the spatial distribution of un-melted powder particles in NiTi alloy samples produced with low laser energy density. These un-melted regions serve as critical defects, confirming that inadequate energy input during the laser processing stage prevents the formation of a homogeneous and fully dense material structure.

caption: Transmittance spectrum of sintered C30 SZ glass doped with 0.20 wt% CuO, demonstrating significant visible light transmission.
summary: The transmittance spectrum for C30 SZ glass doped with 0.20 wt% CuO is shown here, revealing a transmittance value of 85% at 405 nm. This measurement underscores the ability of the sintered SiO2-ZrO2 glass components to retain high transparency in the visible range even when modified with copper coloring agents.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing the elemental distribution near the grain boundary in HIP plus solution-treated LPBF Inconel 625 alloy.
summary: This three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction illustrates the spatial arrangement of major elements within the HIP plus solution-treated LPBF Inconel 625 alloy. The visualization focuses on the elemental distribution specifically near the grain boundary region, providing a detailed view of the atomic-scale structure following the specified thermal processing conditions.

caption: Visual appearance of the final fabricated In718 cantilevers, highlighting the integration of various designed support structures.
summary: The photograph shows the final appearance of the fabricated In718 cantilevers, demonstrating the successful integration of different support designs. These specimens represent the culmination of the sample preparation process, illustrating the geometric accuracy and structural integrity achieved through the SLM manufacturing sequence described in the study's experimental methodology.

caption: Electrochemical polarization data for WC-FeNiCrMoCu coatings, illustrating I Corr and E Corr values in comparison to WC-CoCr and WC-FeCrAl reference standards.
summary: Electrochemical polarization testing of WC-FeNiCrMoCu coatings provides specific corrosion current density and potential metrics. These values are plotted alongside WC-CoCr and WC-FeCrAl references to evaluate performance. The analysis highlights how Fe-based matrix coatings generally exhibit higher corrosion current densities, indicating lower corrosion resistance compared to other tested compositions.

caption: Dark field TEM image emphasizing the M23C6-type carbide structure through specific diffraction contrast.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging highlights the M23C6-type carbide structure using specific diffraction contrast. This technique is essential for identifying the two types of carbides observed in the matrix or grain boundaries of the IL area, providing clear visual evidence of the M23C6-type carbide following the heat treatment.

caption: Energy absorption efficiency plotted against strain to identify the onset strain of the densification stage, defined as the strain level where efficiency reaches its local maximum.
summary: The energy absorption efficiency curve is utilized to determine the onset strain of the densification stage for the cementitious composites. By identifying the strain level where the efficiency function reaches its local maximum, the transition point into the densification stage is precisely determined, facilitating quantitative analysis of the material's energy absorption capacity.

caption: Hydrogen permeation transients for Alloy 625 samples, comparing specimens with the largest (center) and smallest (edge) grain sizes under a cathodic current density of -20 mA/cm² at 60 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the hydrogen permeation transients for Alloy 625 samples, specifically comparing the largest center grain sizes against the smallest edge grain sizes. Conducted at 60 °C with a cathodic current density of -20 mA/cm², the data highlights the influence of grain size on hydrogen diffusion behavior in the alloy.

caption: Comparison of specific room temperature tensile strength versus elongation for LPBF-K4750 against various nickel-based superalloys, including IN 738LC, IN 718, Haynes 282, and Hastelloy X.
summary: This plot compares the room temperature tensile strength and elongation of LPBF-K4750 with established nickel-based superalloys like IN 738LC, IN 718, Haynes 282, and Hastelloy X. The visualization highlights the relative mechanical performance of the K4750 alloy, positioning it within the broader context of existing LPBF-processed superalloy materials.

caption: Simulated trajectory projected onto the (η, ξ) phase plane, featuring invisible equilibria marked by green and red circles.
summary: This panel displays a simulated trajectory within the (η, ξ) phase plane. The dynamics of the oscillation are governed by two virtual equilibria, represented by green and red circles. These equilibria serve as critical reference points for understanding the system's behavior within the TEAMIX model framework.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph displaying the nanoscale γ″-phase precipitates distributed within the γ-phase matrix, accompanied by corresponding EDS elemental maps.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging reveals the presence of nanoscale γ″-phases within the γ-phase matrix, characterized by a distinct particle-like morphology. Accompanying EDS elemental maps provide spatial distribution data for these precipitates, confirming their integration within the γ-matrix structure as observed in the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy analysis.

caption: Pareto chart displaying the standardised effects of process parameters on weld height, where the reference line indicates the level of statistical significance.
summary: Presented as a Pareto chart, this panel evaluates the standardised effects of process parameters on weld height. Utilizing t-statistics to test the null hypothesis of zero impact, the plot incorporates a reference line to highlight which parameters exert a statistically significant influence on the resulting height of the weld.

caption: Observation of the melt pool surface at time t + 0.1 ms, showing the fluctuating liquid metal successfully engulfing the impacting powder particle.
summary: Following the initial impact, the molten liquid engulfs the powder particles after a time interval of 0.1 ms. This frame demonstrates the rapid wetting and incorporation of the BM powder into the melt pool, highlighting the dynamic nature of the liquid metal surface during the deposition process.

caption: Structural damage patterns observed in beams following three-point bending, highlighting localized cracking in single-lattice designs versus the 45° failure mode.
summary: Visual inspection of damaged beams reveals distinct failure modes. Single-lattice structures exhibit localized high stresses leading to catastrophic cracks at the beam center, often manifesting as Y- or semi-Y-shaped patterns under the indenter. In contrast, the hybrid structures demonstrate a distinct 45° cracking pattern upon reaching ultimate failure.

caption: {100} pole figure for the specimen processed without a magnetic field, illustrating the crystallographic texture with four distinct <111> poles.
summary: This {100} pole figure characterizes the crystallographic orientation of the specimen fabricated without a magnetic field. The data exhibits four distinct <111> poles, providing a clear representation of the texture developed in the as-built material under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation diagram depicting the formation kinetics of the γ'-phase in LAM-Inconel 718 across varying aluminum concentrations.
summary: Representing the temperature-time relationship for γ'-phase formation, this diagram demonstrates that the γ'-phase forms earlier during the aging treatment compared to the γ''-phase. The data confirms that aluminum concentration is a critical factor in determining the specific timing and thermal conditions required for the precipitation of these secondary phases.

caption: Optical micrograph of sample 4 scaffold seeded with MSCs at Day 3, visualized using live/dead assay staining.
summary: Sample 4 scaffold seeded with MSCs is presented at Day 3 using live/dead assay staining. This optical micrograph allows for the observation of cell viability and scaffold morphology, facilitating the comparison of swelling extent between the scaffolds before and after the cell culture period.

caption: Fluorescence decay curve and biexponential fitting for TPU/0.5 C composite at 465 nm emission.
summary: The fluorescence lifetime of the TPU/0.5 C composite is characterized by a nonlinear decay curve monitored at an emission wavelength of 465 nm. This decay profile is analyzed using a biexponential fitting function to determine the specific fluorescence lifetime characteristics of the material at room temperature.

caption: Digital image correlation strain distribution map of an FGM-P sample at 20% compressive strain, showing sequential strain propagation.
summary: In the FGM-P sample, the DIC strain map reveals that strain gradually extends from the topmost FCCZ-free layer down to the lower layers in sequence at 20% compressive strain. This sequential deformation pattern demonstrates the influence of the FGM-P design on the compressive performance of the LPBF Corrax lattice.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the beam assembly formed by joining I-WP unit cells with varying relative densities of 32% and 22% on opposite sides, featuring a zoomed-in view of the interface.
summary: This schematic illustrates the structural design of a beam composed of I-WP unit cells with distinct relative densities of 32% and 22%. The diagram highlights the interface between these two regions, providing a clear conceptual representation of how the unit cells are arranged to form the composite beam structure.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of PdNi on Ni RDE at 500 RPM in 2 M NaOH and 1 M glycerol, recorded at 10 mV s-1 across temperatures of 25, 40, 60, and 80 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms demonstrate the temperature effect on GEOR performance for PdNi on Ni RDE. Increasing temperature from 25 to 80 °C results in a significant rise in peak current density, which increases nearly tenfold from 127 to 1100 mA cm-2, highlighting enhanced catalytic activity at higher thermal conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms at 100 mV s-1 comparing the electrochemical performance of the new rPETg filament (11 wt% CB, 11 wt% MWCNT, 11 wt% GNPs) against a previously reported rPETg formulation and a commercial conductive PLA benchmark in a 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+/2+ solution.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammograms comparing three different conductive filaments in a [Ru(NH3)6]3+/2+ redox probe. The new rPETg filament demonstrates superior electrochemical performance, characterized by improved peak reduction currents and reduced peak-to-peak separation compared to the previously reported rPETg and the commercial conductive PLA benchmark electrodes.

caption: Data model illustrating a third variation of a complex SiC ceramic structure.
summary: This panel presents a third data model of a complex SiC ceramic structure. These digital models are critical for the DLP process, which utilizes SiC powder coated with SiO2 to minimize ultraviolet energy loss, thereby facilitating the successful fabrication of these intricate ceramic green bodies.

caption: Series of intensity versus 2θ diffraction patterns for Fe-Cr-V-B-C steel acquired during in situ synchrotron high-energy X-ray diffraction (HE-XRD) under quasi-static compression.
summary: This panel displays a series of intensity versus 2θ diffraction patterns for Fe-Cr-V-B-C steel, captured during in situ synchrotron high-energy X-ray diffraction (HE-XRD) experiments. These patterns illustrate the structural evolution of the material as it undergoes quasi-static compression, providing a clear visualization of the diffraction peaks as a function of increasing engineering compressive stress.

caption: Statistical box plot representation of normalized printed area for node primitives with a 1 mm nominal diameter, segmented by print orientation.
summary: Node primitives with a 1 mm nominal diameter are evaluated through this box plot, which depicts the normalized printed area. The data is organized by print orientation, with whiskers indicating the absolute maximum and minimum values observed across all struts, providing a clear view of the geometric variability.

caption: Schematic representation of the experimental configuration used for uniaxial compression testing.
summary: The experimental setup for uniaxial compression testing is depicted in this panel. It illustrates the arrangement of the P1-thick ACCCs specimen within the testing apparatus, highlighting the orientation and loading conditions applied during the compression process to ensure consistent and reproducible mechanical data collection across different material mixtures.

caption: Distribution of research categories in FDM, visualized as a network graph where node size represents frequency and distinct colors indicate primary research clusters.
summary: This network graph illustrates the distribution of research categories within FDM studies. The visualization utilizes node size to denote the frequency of specific categories, while distinct colors highlight the primary research clusters identified through CiteSpace analysis, providing a clear overview of the thematic landscape in the field.

caption: Overview of the five-phase processing pipeline for generating SEM datasets of additively deposited Ni-WC metal matrix composite powders on a steel substrate.
summary: This schematic illustrates the comprehensive workflow for creating SEM datasets from Ni-WC MMC powders processed via DED. The pipeline encompasses deposition (Phase A), metallographic sectioning (Phase B), optical microscopy (Phase C), SEM analysis (Phase D), and image labeling using the Supervisely software platform (Phase E) to ensure systematic data preparation.

caption: Normalized neutron diffraction patterns of the (111) plane for IN690 alloy subjected to increasing strain levels from 0% to 11.8%, showing peak broadening and shifts.
summary: This panel displays the (111) neutron diffraction peak evolution for IN690 under varying strain levels up to 11.8%. The raw data, represented by crosses, shows significant broadening and shifts in lattice parameters as strain increases. CMWP fits are overlaid to illustrate the structural changes occurring during the transition from elastic to plastic deformation.

caption: High-magnification STEM BF image revealing that precipitates in the irradiated X-750 alloy are heavily decorated by dislocation loops.
summary: High-magnification STEM BF imaging demonstrates that precipitates in the irradiated X-750 alloy are highly decorated by dislocation loops. Compared to the surrounding matrix, these precipitates contain a significantly higher density of dislocation loops, indicating that the precipitates act as preferential sites for the accumulation of irradiation-induced defects.

caption: First-nearest-neighbor (1NN) short-range order (SRO) parameters between nitrogen and metal atoms in Fe70Ni10Cr20 with 10 at.% N.
summary: This panel displays the 1NN SRO parameters for nitrogen and metal atoms in the Fe70Ni10Cr20 alloy containing 10 at.% nitrogen. These parameters quantify the local atomic arrangement, providing insight into the chemical short-range ordering behavior within the alloy system as determined through Monte Carlo simulation methods.

caption: Averaged residual Young’s modulus values derived from all cyclic nano-indentation tests, demonstrating the trend of modulus evolution and increasing data scatter with a higher number of indents.
summary: Panel b presents the averaged residual Young’s modulus calculated from all cyclic indentation tests. The plot highlights the overall trend of the modulus over the cycle number. Notably, the results indicate that the scatter in the measured values increases as the number of indents progresses throughout the testing procedure.

caption: Cross-sectional SEM micrograph of the Ti/Mo bilayer on Al2O3 substrate sintered at 900 °C, exhibiting a smooth interface structure.
summary: This cross-sectional SEM micrograph reveals the internal structure of the metallized Al2O3 ceramic sintered at 900 °C. The image shows a smooth Ti/Mo bilayer structure, where a ~300 nm Ti layer borders the substrate and a ~400 nm Mo layer forms the outer film, confirming the designed sputtering sequence.

caption: Arrhenius plot for AFRP in seawater, showing a lower R-squared value due to a restricted retention window that limits the dynamic range of the natural log of time.
summary: This Arrhenius plot depicts the degradation of AFRP in seawater. The observed lower R-squared value is attributed to a narrow retention window, which reduces the dynamic range of the natural log of time and increases the sensitivity of the data to scatter in the extracted time values.

caption: Validation of DNN-predicted creep curves against experimental data at specific conditions: 800 °C/480 MPa, 850 °C/320 MPa, and 900 °C/240 MPa.
summary: This panel validates the trained DNN model by comparing predicted creep curves with actual experimental test curves under three distinct conditions: 800 °C/480 MPa, 850 °C/320 MPa, and 900 °C/240 MPa. The close agreement between predicted and actual curves confirms the model's reliability for predicting creep behavior under varied conditions.

caption: Deconvoluted Thermal Desorption Spectroscopy (TDS) spectrum for the thick sample, recorded at a heating rate of 1000 K/h to characterize hydrogen desorption behavior.
summary: The deconvoluted TDS spectrum, obtained at a heating rate of 1000 K/h, reflects the rate-determining process of hydrogen diffusion and surface desorption. Because the sample was not saturated, the peaks in this spectrum are specifically linked to the diffusion-controlled release of hydrogen rather than trapping-related desorption mechanisms.

caption: Tafel voltammograms illustrating the electrochemical behavior of various stainless steels and nickel-based alloys immersed in [N 1888][Tf 2 N] electrolyte at 23 °C, showing current density responses across a range of applied potentials.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical response of stainless steels and nickel-based alloys in [N 1888][Tf 2 N] at 23 °C. The data indicates that a passivation layer forms readily on all tested alloys. These voltammograms are essential for identifying corrosion mechanisms and determining critical parameters like corrosion current densities and potentials.

caption: Anodic overvoltage trends for Ni(100-x)Cox-GDC anodes during redox cycling, demonstrating that cobalt addition effectively suppresses the increase in non-ohmic overvoltage.
summary: The anodic overvoltage is tracked across 50 redox cycles at 800 °C for various cobalt-doped Ni-GDC anodes. Results indicate that the incorporation of cobalt into the anode material successfully suppresses the increase in non-ohmic anodic overvoltage, which is otherwise observed during the redox cycling of pure Ni-GDC cells.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for as-printed PEKK coupons, displaying storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor across multiple recycling rounds.
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for as-printed PEKK coupons, displaying storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor across multiple recycling rounds. These curves characterize the viscoelastic properties of the material in its amorphous state, providing essential data on the mechanical performance and thermal stability of the polymer throughout the recycling process.

caption: Deconvoluted TDS spectrum for a membrane sample heated at 800 K/h, showing the separation of the total desorption signal into two distinct peaks representing specific hydrogen trap sites.
summary: Deconvolution of the TDS spectrum obtained at a heating rate of 800 K/h reveals two individual peaks. Each of these peaks corresponds to a specific type of hydrogen trap within the membrane sample, providing insight into the trapping characteristics of the material at the saturation level.

caption: Binary phase diagram for the Fe-Ni system showing temperature versus composition relationships.
summary: The Fe-Ni binary phase diagram illustrates the thermodynamic equilibrium states between iron and nickel across varying temperatures and compositions. This plot serves as a fundamental reference for understanding the phase stability and transformation behavior within the Fe-Ni alloy system, providing essential data for metallurgical processing and alloy design applications.

caption: Specific wear rate of the steel-bonded TiC-based cermets plotted as a function of temperature under a 10 N load.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific wear rate of the steel-bonded TiC-based cermets across the tested temperature range. The data provides a quantitative measure of material loss, which correlates with the observed changes in surface morphology and debris compaction occurring as the temperature increases during the wear test.

caption: Loss modulus of CF-PLA composite recorded from -110 °C to 20 °C at frequencies of 1, 30, and 70 Hz.
summary: The loss modulus of the CF-PLA composite is depicted for temperatures between -110 °C and 20 °C. Data points collected at 1, 30, and 70 Hz demonstrate the frequency-dependent energy dissipation properties of the composite, providing insight into the damping behavior of the reinforced polymer system under these conditions.

caption: Yield strength versus elongation benchmark plot comparing Ti–6Al–4V produced via various manufacturing routes, including EB-PBF, L-PBF, DED, wrought/forged references, and AFSD studies.
summary: This Ashby plot benchmarks the mechanical performance of Ti–6Al–4V across diverse manufacturing methods. The as-built AFSD block, highlighted by a red star, achieves approximately 906 MPa yield strength and 13% elongation. These results demonstrate superior ductility compared to forged materials and performance parity with wrought alloys without requiring post-deposition heat treatment.

caption: DMA storage modulus profile for the original resin system, exhibiting a storage modulus of 405 MPa at 25 °C.
summary: Panel b presents the DMA storage modulus curve for the original 3D-printed resin system. The analysis reveals a storage modulus of 405 MPa at 25 °C. This serves as the baseline measurement for comparing the mechanical properties of the various modified thermoset systems investigated in the study.

caption: FTIR spectra of the manufactured samples, featuring a vertical offset for comparative analysis and an inset highlighting the 2500–2000 cm⁻¹ wavenumber range.
summary: This figure presents the FTIR spectra obtained from the manufactured samples to characterize their chemical composition. The spectra are shifted vertically to facilitate direct comparison between different samples. Additionally, an inset is provided to specifically detail the spectral features within the 2500–2000 cm⁻¹ wavenumber range for closer inspection.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the Nimolloy-202-H alloy viewed along the [001] zone axis, highlighting the γ matrix spots and the γ’ phase superstructure reflections.
summary: This diffraction pattern, captured along the [001] zone axis of the Nimolloy-202-H alloy, reveals the characteristic spots of the γ matrix. Additionally, the presence of superstructure spots, highlighted in blue, confirms the existence of the γ’ phase, providing evidence of the ordered structure within the material's crystalline lattice.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve depicting the crystallization behavior of filament composites.
summary: This panel presents the crystallization behavior of filament composites obtained through DSC analysis. The curve characterizes the material's thermal response during the cooling phase, offering insights into the crystallization kinetics and phase transformation processes essential for understanding the overall thermal profile of the filament composites.

caption: Micro-CT volumetric reconstruction of slip cast TCP capillary suspension (CS-SC) revealing long mm-scale crack-like defects.
summary: Micro-CT volumetric reconstruction of slip cast CS-SC reveals long mm-scale crack-like defects. These defects are likely attributed to uneven drying rates during the slip casting process or inhomogeneous thermal distributions during sintering, which compromise the structural integrity of the slip-cast TCP compared to the DIW-printed counterparts.

caption: CAD model (orange) overlaid with the non-linearly registered XCT scan (blue), with pink circles indicating registration failures in the xz-plane.
summary: Panel c presents the final alignment between the CAD model in orange and the non-linearly registered XCT scan in blue. In the xz-plane, pink circles highlight specific regions where registration fails, attributed to the severe splitting of TPMS periodic voids caused by the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Reduction of area values derived from tensile testing, categorized by heat treatment and process themes.
summary: Reduction of area values exhibit a trend comparable to elongation, characterized by significant scatter. The HIP 920C high productivity theme achieves the highest absolute median reduction of area at approximately 48%, surpassing the minimal porosity built material, illustrating the superior ductility performance under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Bode magnitude plot displaying the frequency-dependent impedance response of the samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl electrolyte.
summary: The Bode magnitude plot displays the frequency-dependent impedance response of the samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl electrolyte. This plot, alongside the phase plot, confirms the presence of two time constants for the coated samples, which is essential for accurately modeling the electrochemical behavior of the protective coatings.

caption: Typical force-displacement curves for pure epoxy and biomimetic ceramic composites, providing data for fracture toughness analysis.
summary: Force-displacement curves for pure epoxy and various biomimetic ceramic composites serve as the primary data source for tracking fracture toughness. By analyzing these curves, researchers can quantify the crack extension behavior and evaluate the energy dissipation mechanisms inherent in the different architectural designs of the ceramic-reinforced nanocomposites.

caption: Side view of the BCC lattice structure showing atomic positioning.
summary: Represented here is the side view of the BCC lattice structure. This orientation highlights the specific atomic positioning within the unit cell, allowing for a detailed examination of the lattice arrangement from a lateral perspective. It complements the isometric view by providing a two-dimensional projection of the three-dimensional crystal structure.

caption: Cycle stability test of the CoNi-0.5 catalyst conducted at a potential of -0.7 V versus RHE.
summary: A cycle stability test was performed on the CoNi-0.5 catalyst at -0.7 V versus RHE to determine its performance retention over repeated operation. This test confirms the robustness of the catalyst under cyclic electrochemical conditions for the nitrate reduction reaction.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto495 dye, showing the specific spectral attenuation achieved by this dye.
summary: The transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto495 dye is illustrated. This plot characterizes the specific wavelength-filtering behavior of the printed sample, contributing to the comparative analysis of different Atto dyes within the 3D-printed polymer matrix.

caption: Confocal fluorescence images of hADSCs cultured on PCL, G, and GO scaffolds after 7 days, showing nuclei stained in blue and actin filaments in red.
summary: Confocal fluorescence imaging of hADSCs after 7 days of culture on PCL, G, and GO scaffolds reveals cell morphology and distribution. The staining of nuclei in blue and actin in red demonstrates that these cells are successfully sustained by the scaffolds, proliferating effectively along the fibers and bridging gaps between them.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile and GP prediction for <111> grains in the axial direction at a radial position of 12 mm.
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction peak for <111> oriented grains measured at a radial distance of 12 mm from the sample center. The red solid line represents the experimental diffraction data, which is compared against GP model predictions to evaluate the structural response of the material under axial loading conditions.

caption: XPS depth profile focusing exclusively on metallic ions in the LPBF 350/700 sample, excluding oxygen contributions to highlight the distribution of pure metals.
summary: This XPS depth profile isolates metallic ions in the LPBF 350/700 sample by excluding oxygen signals. The data illustrates the distribution of pure metals alongside the oxide film, confirming that the inner region is characterized by a combination of pure metals and predominantly Mn oxide components.

caption: Simulated continuous cooling transformation (CCT) plot for HSLA-50 steel, calculated using Thermo-Calc to predict microstructural constituent formation during cooling.
summary: A simulated CCT plot calculated using Thermo-Calc is presented in panel (b) to identify different microstructural constituents. This diagram serves as a predictive tool for understanding phase transformations, indicating that the SZ contains a combination of α-ferrite, pearlite, and bainite, consistent with a cooling rate of approximately 10 K/s.

caption: Evolution of the resultant cutting force Fr relative to cutting length L for Ti-64 +MoS2, with an inset highlighting the specific contributions of force components Fx, Fy, and Fz during representative machining segments.
summary: The resultant force profile for Ti-64 +MoS2 samples is presented here, showing the relationship between cutting force and length. A magnified view of representative segments is provided to clarify the relative contributions of the Fx, Fy, and Fz force components to the total resultant force profile during machining.

caption: Peak fitting results for the γ-FCC (311) diffraction peak within the base metal (BM) region.
summary: Peak fitting analysis of the γ-FCC (311) diffraction peak is performed for the base metal (BM). This analysis, conducted within the 6.9 to 7.8 degree 2θ range, characterizes the structural state of the FCC phase, providing a stable reference for peak center distribution compared to the fusion zone.

caption: Load-axial deformation curves derived from full cross-section tensile testing of the material.
summary: This plot displays the mechanical response of the material under tensile loading, specifically showing the relationship between applied load and axial deformation. These curves were obtained through full cross-section tensile tests, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's deformation behavior and structural integrity under uniaxial stress conditions during the experimental procedure.

caption: Specific energy absorption plotted against relative density for I-shaped pyramidal lattice structures compared to various strut-based lattice geometries.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the specific energy absorption (SEA) performance of tailored I-shaped pyramidal lattices relative to common strut-based lattice architectures. By mapping SEA against density, the figure demonstrates the mechanical efficiency of the proposed design, highlighting its competitive performance against diverse strut cross-sections documented in existing literature.

caption: Conceptual schematic illustrating the proposed mechanism of magnetic charge-mediated conduction within the individual honeycomb elements.
summary: This schematic provides a conceptual representation of the magnetic charge-mediated conduction mechanism occurring within the honeycomb elements. It serves as a theoretical framework to explain the observed electrical transport behavior, specifically detailing how magnetic charges contribute to the conductivity enhancement observed in the experimental measurements of the artificial lattice system.

caption: Surface topography map of the machined specimen obtained via profilometry after 11 minutes of machining under liquid nitrogen (LN2) conditions.
summary: Representing the surface topography after 11 minutes of machining under LN2, this scan demonstrates the final stage of the observed process. Profilometer data at this interval confirms an increase in the average areal roughness, Sa, providing evidence of the surface degradation occurring over the extended machining duration.

caption: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles for the 3D LFP electrode at varying C-rates.
summary: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles for the 3D LFP electrode are presented at varying C-rates. These electrochemical measurements, conducted in a full cell configuration with LTO/LP30, illustrate the voltage versus specific capacity behavior of the 3D LFP material, providing insight into its performance characteristics under different current densities.

caption: Top site configuration for an O adatom on the NiCr(1) surface, showing the charge transfer and surface distortion.
summary: Shown is the top site adsorption of an oxygen atom on the NiCr(1) surface. The panel captures the charge transfer and structural distortion, supporting the observation that top site configurations facilitate the highest levels of charge transfer, which correlates with a decrease in the first layer segregation energy.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve for the virgin powder, illustrating the thermal transitions used to calculate the sintering window.
summary: This DSC curve displays the thermal behavior of the virgin powder. By identifying the extrapolated onsets of the crystallization and melting processes, the sintering window is determined. This analysis provides the necessary thermal parameters to evaluate the processing range for the virgin material during sintering applications.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of Magnesium in 1-pass FSPed HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe, showing improved uniformity.
summary: Magnesium elemental distribution in the 1-pass FSPed HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe alloy is visualized through this EDS map. Following the friction stir processing, a significant improvement in the distribution of magnesium is observed, demonstrating a visibly more uniform elemental dispersion compared to the as-received condition of the alloy.

caption: Force-displacement curves for gyroid main structure TPMS specimens, showing the mechanical response under loading.
summary: This panel displays the force-displacement behavior of gyroid main structure TPMS specimens. Experimental results indicate that the gyroid configuration exhibits distinct mechanical characteristics, with the GP specimen achieving the highest first peak load of 1300 N, demonstrating the structural performance of this specific TPMS geometry under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the natural logarithm of the grain growth rate constant (ln K) versus the reciprocal of the absolute temperature (1/T) for SS316L specimens.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the relationship between the grain growth rate constant and temperature for SS316L. By calculating the slope of the trend line, the activation energy for grain growth is determined. The data incorporates fine cellular sub-grains for temperatures ≤ 600 °C and evolving cells/equiaxed grains for temperatures > 600 °C.

caption: Size distribution histogram of cuboidal coprecipitates in the HIP treated sample, showing an average length of 18.5 ± 3.6 nm.
summary: This histogram displays the size distribution of cuboidal coprecipitates within the HIP treated sample. Statistical analysis indicates an average length of 18.5 ± 3.6 nm for these particles. The data provides a baseline for evaluating the morphological stability of the precipitates prior to subsequent thermal treatments.

caption: Histological and immunofluorescence staining images of native, UVD, and VAD tracheal scaffolds, including H&E, MT, Col-II, Safranin O, and Laminin staining, with DAPI-stained nuclei in blue.
summary: Histological and immunofluorescence staining images of native, UVD, and VAD tracheal scaffolds are presented, including H&E, MT, Col-II, Safranin O, and Laminin staining. Laminin immunofluorescence staining demonstrated primary localization of laminin in the mucosal layer, with a slight decrease in the UVD group and a more pronounced reduction in the VAD group.

caption: Atom map slice (4 nm diameter) through a secondary γ′ precipitate, revealing the Ni3Al lattice structure with Hf atoms substituted on Al lattice sites.
summary: This 4 nm diameter atom map slice through a secondary γ′ precipitate displays the ordered Ni3Al lattice structure. The visualization confirms the presence of Hf atoms specifically occupying Al lattice sites. This atomic-scale reconstruction provides direct evidence of the chemical ordering and site-specific substitution within the γ′ phase.

caption: Line scanning profile of 316 L stainless steel powder reinforced with 0.1 wt% graphene.
summary: This panel displays the elemental line scanning profile conducted on a 316 L stainless steel powder sample containing 0.1 wt% graphene. The analysis focuses on characterizing the composition of a specific precipitated area within the powder, providing insight into the distribution of elements at this graphene concentration level.

caption: Surface morphology of A2 powder captured using white light interferometry combined with confocal microscopy.
summary: Surface morphology of the A2 powder is analyzed via white light interferometry and confocal microscopy. This approach enables the assessment of surface characteristics, contributing to the overall evaluation of the A2 powder feedstock quality and its potential impact on the printed specimen properties.

caption: Pareto plot of standardized effects for significant factors influencing extruded line thickness, confirming the dominant role of nozzle diameter.
summary: This Pareto plot illustrates the standardized effects of significant process terms on the extruded line thickness. Consistent with the line width analysis, the results demonstrate that nozzle diameter is the most influential factor affecting the formation characteristics of the extruded ceramic paste material during the manufacturing process.

caption: Two-dimensional feature space visualization of the HEA dataset using the mixing parameter (Ω) and valence electron concentration (VEC) as axes.
summary: This scatter plot maps the 322 as-cast HEAs into a two-dimensional feature space defined by the mixing parameter Ω and VEC. Along with other features like δ, Tm, ΔH mix, and configurational entropy, these parameters provide a systematic way to visualize and analyze the structural characteristics of the alloy dataset.

caption: Optical micrograph of as-printed Ti-6Al-4V alloy showing the morphology of prior β grains.
summary: Optical micrograph of the as-printed Ti-6Al-4V alloy reveals the initial morphology of prior β grains. This baseline microstructure serves as a reference for comparing the effects of manganese additions on grain structure evolution under identical deposition process parameters, as the growth restriction factor is varied across the alloy series.

caption: Cyclic evolution of minimum, mean, and maximum stresses during isothermal LCF testing at 650 ∘C.
summary: This plot displays the cyclic stress evolution during isothermal LCF testing at 650 ∘C. Observations indicate that stress amplitudes are higher at this temperature compared to 730 ∘C. The material exhibits cyclic softening under these loading conditions, with consistent trends observed regardless of the applied mechanical strain amplitude.

caption: Top view of a section cut through a HIRT RLD 10% lattice structure.
summary: A top-view section cut of a HIRT RLD 10% lattice structure is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the Hirtisation® treatment. The image confirms the successful removal of attached powder particles from the inner geometry, indicating that the treatment process achieves uniform results throughout the entire lattice volume.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of nitrogen solubility in X50CrMoVN15 melt at 0.103 MPa, compared with experimental nitrogen content in PBF-LB/M samples processed at an exposure time of 80 µs.
summary: This CALPHAD-based thermodynamic calculation estimates nitrogen solubility in X50CrMoVN15 melt at 0.103 MPa. The plot correlates these theoretical values with experimental nitrogen content measured in PBF-LB/M samples. Specifically, samples processed at an 80 µs exposure time exhibit a nitrogen content of 0.474 mass%, illustrating the relationship between processing parameters and nitrogen retention.

caption: Current density (J) plotted as a function of the depletion width (w) for the investigated device.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between current density and depletion width, denoted as J-w. The visualization provides a quantitative representation of the device's electrical characteristics, specifically mapping how current density evolves in response to variations in the depletion region width, which is critical for understanding the underlying charge transport mechanisms.

caption: Visualization of high-speed TiC particles passing directly through the arc zone and entering the melt pool, with some particles being captured by molten droplets.
summary: High-speed imaging reveals TiC particles traversing the arc zone to enter the melt pool. Some of these particles are successfully captured by the molten droplets. This behavior highlights the interaction between the reinforcement particles and the molten metal during the droplet transfer phase of the deposition process.

caption: Geometric configuration of the interlocking features, highlighting the characteristic diameter D* of the cylindrical components.
summary: The geometry of the interlocking features is defined by metal and polymeric cylindrical parts, each possessing a diameter D* and a height of 80 µm. This structural design incorporates one anchoring BLF, which is essential for the mechanical interlocking mechanism analyzed within the finite element simulation framework.

caption: Anodic stripping voltammograms of underpotentially deposited Cu monolayers on polycrystalline Pt and Pt 5 Pr surfaces in 4 mM Cu2+ and 0.1 M HClO4.
summary: Anodic stripping voltammograms are used to compare Cu monolayers formed at 0.33 V vs RHE on Pt 5 Pr and polycrystalline Pt electrodes. The experiment, conducted in 4 mM Cu2+ and 0.1 M HClO4 at a scan rate of 50 mV/s, highlights differences in the stripping behavior of the deposited monolayers.

caption: Workflow architecture of the active learning framework designed for single-track parameter optimization in Directed Energy Deposition, integrating human-in-the-loop decision-making with Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the active learning framework for Directed Energy Deposition parameter optimization. It incorporates a human-in-the-loop component to refine decision-making and process accuracy. The methodology utilizes off-axis image data from ROS 2, processed via Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization using the Nextorch wrapper library based on Botorch to enhance single-track manufacturing outcomes.

caption: Low-magnification optical micrograph of the HPHT-SB-EP specimen in the X-Y plane, showing an isotropic macrostructure of equiaxial parent β grains.
summary: This low-magnification optical micrograph of the HPHT-SB-EP specimen in the X-Y plane displays an isotropic macrostructure. The structure consists of equiaxial parent β grains, which are formed due to quenching from the β field during the LPBF processing of the Ti6Al4V alloy under these specific conditions.

caption: Comparison of mechanical property ranges for 316L stainless steel produced via various additive manufacturing routes, highlighting the performance distribution of binder-jetting versus selective laser melting.
summary: This plot compares mechanical property ranges for 316L stainless steel across different additive manufacturing processes. The data indicates that binder-jetting samples exhibit a distinct performance cloud characterized by slightly lower overall strength compared to selective laser melting, while simultaneously demonstrating superior ductility, illustrating the trade-offs inherent in these manufacturing routes.

caption: Comparison of experimental porosity versus predicted porosity derived from the Linear Regression (LR) model.
summary: This parity plot displays the correlation between experimental porosity and the values predicted by the Linear Regression model. By mapping the predicted data as a function of experimental data, the plot allows for a visual assessment of how effectively the LR model fits the observed porosity measurements.

caption: DC four-probe conductivity measurements for PCL/BT composites with varying BaTiO₃ concentrations.
summary: DC four-probe data for PCL/BT composites demonstrate a numerical decrease in resistivity and a corresponding increase in electrical conductivity as the BaTiO₃ content increases. These results highlight the influence of filler concentration on the electronic transport properties of the PCL-based composite materials.

caption: Nyquist plot for LEHCEB-treated LPBF 316L steel samples after 60 minutes of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of LEHCEB-treated LPBF 316L steel after 60 minutes of immersion in a 3.5% NaCl solution. The change in the plot's character confirms that the corrosion mechanism is governed by a two-layer passive film model, demonstrating the effect of surface treatment on electrochemical performance.

caption: Tafel plots derived from LSV data, showing NIF(Na,Cr)-S with a lower Tafel slope of 63.3 mV dec-1 compared to P-treated, Se-treated, and pristine samples, indicating faster OER kinetics.
summary: Tafel slope analysis derived from linear sweep voltammetry data demonstrates the OER kinetics of the catalysts. NIF(Na,Cr)-S exhibits a lower Tafel slope of 63.3 mV dec-1 compared to NIF(Na,Cr)-P (68.8 mV dec-1), NIF(Na,Cr)-Se (74.1 mV dec-1), and pristine NIF (121.1 mV dec-1), which indicates significantly faster OER reaction kinetics.

caption: Photoluminescence peak energy dependence on excitation power density for sample P027 at 10 K, featuring a nonlinear trend.
summary: Photoluminescence peak energy for sample P027 is plotted against excitation power density at 10 K. The data, accompanied by a solid line fit and dashed visual guides, demonstrates a nonlinear dependence. This result is consistent with the observed nonlinear intensity behavior for this sample, reflecting its specific optical properties under varying excitation.

caption: Carbon and oxygen K-edge EELS spectra of PLA polymer subjected to increasing electron doses of 5, 89, 231, and 594 e/Å², with an inset showing the Cπ*/Cσ* intensity ratio as a function of accumulated dose.
summary: PLA polymer EELS spectra reveal carbon K-edge peaks at 283 eV (π*) and 290 eV (σ*), alongside oxygen K-edge peaks at 530 eV and 537 eV. These features decrease during irradiation, with oxygen peaks nearly vanishing above 231 e/Å². The Cπ*/Cσ* ratio inset quantifies these radiation-induced chemical degradation changes.

caption: Optical micrograph of a printed line with a layer thickness of 0.3 mm, demonstrating a stable capsule-shaped cross section.
summary: This optical micrograph displays a printed line with a layer thickness of 0.3 mm. Within the 0.3–0.4 mm layer thickness range, the cross sections exhibit a stable capsule shape, indicating that these parameters result in good printing quality and structural integrity for the printed material.

caption: Bode impedance modulus plots for bare C-steel and Ni-Co coated steel samples immersed in 1.0 M HCl for 30 minutes at 30 °C and corrosion potential.
summary: Bode impedance modulus plots compare bare C-steel and Ni-Co coated steel in 1.0 M HCl after 30 minutes of immersion. The Ni-Co coatings exhibit the highest Z modulus values compared to the uncoated substrate. C-steel displays a single time constant, indicating a single mechanism for the corrosion process.

caption: Initial temperature profile for parameter set #8, showing the melt pool and laser trajectory.
summary: The initial temperature profile for parameter set #8 is presented, showing the melt pool geometry and the laser trajectory. This simulation serves as a baseline for evaluating the thermal behavior and melt pool stability, which are critical for understanding the interaction between the laser and the material.

caption: Validation dataset parity plot showing the relationship between predicted and measured normalized hardness and Young's modulus, where the solid line denotes the target parity.
summary: Validation dataset results are presented in this parity plot, illustrating the alignment between predicted normalized hardness and Young's modulus and their corresponding measured values. The solid line serves as a reference for perfect prediction accuracy. Good agreement between the predicted and measured values is observed for this validation set.

caption: Arrhenius-style representation of activation energy (Q) values across distinct sintering shrinkage regimes (m1 and m2) for samples fabricated along X, Y, and Z printing orientations, evaluated up to a sintering temperature of 1390 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the activation energy (Q) behavior within two specific sintering shrinkage regimes, m1 and m2, for samples printed in X, Y, and Z orientations. The data demonstrates that activation energies remain consistent across varying printing orientations for all sintering temperatures up to 1390 °C, indicating isotropic sintering kinetics.

caption: R-curves for the 90-0500 batch samples, illustrating crack growth resistance.
summary: The R-curves for the 90-0500 batch samples are presented, detailing the crack growth resistance behavior. This dataset includes the vertical sample 90-0500 1, which notably did not exhibit crack deflection. These curves characterize the fracture toughness evolution for each sample, highlighting variations in crack propagation resistance across the tested batch.

caption: Raman spectra of Ni/YSZ, Ni/GDC, and HEA/GDC catalysts after 30 hours of time-on-stream, highlighting characteristic peaks at 1345 and 1595 cm⁻¹.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the post-test catalysts reveals two distinct characteristic peaks at 1345 and 1595 cm⁻¹. The Ni/YSZ catalyst exhibits the highest intensity for both amorphous and graphitic carbon peaks, which correlates with the observed catalyst deactivation during the 30-hour time-on-stream test.

caption: Calculated phase fraction diagram for Sicoat 2453 showing the evolution of constituent phases as a function of temperature from 500 °C to 1500 °C.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the thermodynamic phase stability of Sicoat 2453 between 500 °C and 1500 °C. It serves as a baseline for evaluating experimental peak intensity ratios and SEM/EDS imaging results, providing a theoretical framework to understand the dissolution of γ′-Ni3Al and σ-(Co,Cr) phases observed at elevated temperatures.

caption: Schematic representation illustrating the geometry of as-printed alumina samples compared to warped samples, highlighting the warpage height (Hwarpage) measured at the center.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometric deformation of alumina samples following the printing process. It specifically defines the warpage height, denoted as Hwarpage, which is measured at the center of the sample to quantify the extent of structural distortion occurring during the fabrication of the green parts.

caption: Welding torch trajectory generation for the thick section of the component, derived from isothermal surface analysis and corresponding height maps.
summary: This schematic illustrates the path followed by the welding torch during the fabrication of the thick part. The trajectory is systematically created by utilizing isothermal surfaces and their associated height maps, ensuring precise control over the additive manufacturing process to achieve the desired geometry and structural integrity of the component.

caption: Atomic model of the (110) surface slab illustrating eight distinct hollow adsorption sites, with a bridge site specifically highlighted by a 'B' label in the upper right corner.
summary: This atomic model depicts the (110) surface slab, providing a detailed visualization of the eight hollow adsorption sites available for chemical interaction. A bridge adsorption site is explicitly marked with a 'B' in the upper right corner to distinguish it from the hollow sites where chlorine atoms typically settle.

caption: Numerical creep curves for polycrystal simulations at 800 °C, comparing tensile and compressive loading at various stress levels.
summary: Simulated creep curves at 800 °C demonstrate an antisymmetric mechanical response between tension and compression. The material exhibits inferior creep strength under tensile loading compared to compression. These differences in creep strength are attributed to the activation of distinct deformation mechanisms within the grains under the different loading conditions.

caption: High-speed camera image of the welding arc and droplet transition captured perpendicular to the travel direction without the application of an oscillating magnetic field (SOAM).
summary: This high-speed photograph captures the baseline welding arc shape and droplet transition cycle without the influence of an oscillating magnetic field. The image provides a reference for comparing arc stability and droplet behavior against processes utilizing auxiliary magnetic fields, as observed from a perspective perpendicular to the welding torch travel direction.

caption: DSC heat flow profile for CCF filaments during initial and subsequent heating-cooling cycles, showing a glass transition temperature (Tg) of approximately 72°C and irregular patterns due to water evaporation.
summary: The DSC curve for CCF filaments shows thermal behavior during cycles from 25°C to 300°C. A glass transition temperature of approximately 72°C is recorded. Irregular heat flow patterns observed during the initial cycle are attributed to the evaporation of water present within the polymeric matrix of the samples.

caption: Three-dimensional strain rate sensitivity (m) map for the Fe–25Al-1.5Ta alloy at a true strain of 0.8, illustrating the variation of m values across different deformation temperatures and strain rates.
summary: This 3D strain rate sensitivity map for the Fe–25Al-1.5Ta alloy at a true strain of 0.8 reveals the influence of deformation conditions on material stability. A specific region of negative m values, reaching a minimum of -0.027 at 800 °C and 1 s⁻¹, indicates flow instability and potential damage mechanisms during processing.

caption: EPMA elemental map showing the distribution of Silicon (Si) within the eutectic vein.
summary: Silicon mapping via EPMA confirms its enrichment within the eutectic vein network. The concentration of Si in this region is significantly elevated compared to the gamma-dendrite core and the adjacent matrix, supporting the identification of this network as a complex multi-element phase enriched with Si, Nb, Ti, and Mo.

caption: Tabulated elemental composition data for the ER2205–Inconel 718 interface, detailing the weight percentages of constituent elements.
summary: This table provides the quantitative elemental composition of the ER2205–Inconel 718 interface region. It lists the specific weight percentages for each element identified during the EDAX analysis, serving as a reference for the compositional distribution observed across the interface fabricated by the GMAW-based WAAM process.

caption: Predicted yield strength (σy) plotted against various alloying elements X for equiatomic V25Nb25Mo25X25 bcc refractory multi-principal element alloys (RMPEAs).
summary: This scatter plot displays the predicted yield strength for equiatomic V25Nb25Mo25X25 bcc RMPEAs across ten different alloying elements (X = Al, Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, Ta, Cr, Mo, and W). Dotted lines indicate the reference yield strength of the V33Nb33Mo34 alloy, illustrating the influence of specific alloying elements on mechanical performance.

caption: Calculated interface energy for the HfC(111)/Ni3Al(111) structure, identifying the Bridge1 model as a relatively stable interface.
summary: Analysis of the HfC(111)/Ni3Al(111) interface structure reveals that the Bridge1 model serves as a relatively stable configuration. The interface energy for this specific model is determined to be between 4.612 J/m2 and 4.309 J/m2, reflecting the energetic stability of this particular atomic interface arrangement.

caption: Grain orientation map of 316L SS-5%WC-AF sample processed with acoustic field assistance.
summary: This EBSD map displays the grain orientation for the 316L SS-5%WC-AF specimen. The application of an acoustic field promotes convection and stirring within the melt pool, leading to a more uniform temperature distribution that helps reduce microstructural inhomogeneities and enhances the overall mechanical properties of the material.

caption: Potentio-dynamic polarization curves for LPBF 22Cr DSS specimens subjected to various heat treatments, measured in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at 60 ℃.
summary: Potentio-dynamic polarization curves illustrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of LPBF 22Cr DSS in 3.5 wt% NaCl at 60 ℃. These curves demonstrate how different heat treatments influence the pitting potential and passive current density, providing a dynamic assessment of the material's corrosion resistance across varying annealing conditions.

caption: Initial microstructure of the superalloy showing needle-like delta phases, equiaxed grains, and annealing twins.
summary: The initial microstructure of the researched superalloy is characterized by the presence of needle-like delta phases distributed within the matrix. Additionally, the material exhibits equiaxed grains and distinct annealing twins. These structural features collectively define the starting state of the superalloy prior to any subsequent processing or experimental testing.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted deformation values against actual experimental deformation data derived from a non-linear regression model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the performance of a non-linear regression model by comparing predicted deformation values against actual experimental deformation data. The visualization serves to validate the accuracy of the model's predictive capabilities, demonstrating how well the non-linear approach captures the deformation behavior observed in the experimental dataset.

caption: Tilt distortion of the oxygen octahedra characterized by the Q T mode with M 5 − irrep symmetry.
summary: The Q T mode, corresponding to the M 5 − irrep symmetry, depicts the tilt distortion of the oxygen octahedra. This structural feature acts as a key component in the trilinear coupling process, contributing to the formation of the low-symmetry P m c 2 1 ground state structure.

caption: Projected image displaying interference fringes when the system is not aligned horizontally.
summary: Misalignment between the PLM and DMD pixels causes the interference fringes on the projected image to appear distorted. This visual representation demonstrates the effect of horizontal pixel mismatch, which is distinct from the aligned state and indicates that the optical path requires further adjustment to achieve optimal system performance.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot illustrating feature importance for the pH = 4.5 classification model, where the red channel exhibits the most significant influence on model predictions.
summary: This SHAP beeswarm plot visualizes the feature importance for the pH = 4.5 classification model. Analysis indicates that the red channel feature exerts the largest effect on the model's predictive output for this specific class, highlighting its primary role in distinguishing samples at this pH level.

caption: First simulated microstructure generated using a noise parameter of n ord = 0.01.
summary: This panel displays the first simulated microstructure produced with a noise parameter of n ord = 0.01. The simulation utilizes a consistent random number generation algorithm and seed to ensure computational repeatability. This visual representation serves as the initial data point for assessing the consistency of the modeling approach.

caption: Dynamic Negative Stepped Test (DNST) curve illustrating the stepwise loading profile, where the red solid line represents the experimental stress-time evolution used to determine rupture time and hold time parameters.
summary: The Dynamic Negative Stepped Test (DNST) curve is presented as a red solid line, characterizing the stepwise stress application during creep testing. This profile allows for the calculation of the average strain energy density rate, incorporating rupture time, hold time, and changes in ductility at each individual step.

caption: Terahertz imaging of the metal plate component, showing the signal reflection profile of the metallic surface.
summary: This panel shows the terahertz image of the metal plate used in the experimental setup. The high reflectivity of the metal surface to THz radiation is clearly depicted, serving as a reference for the signal response of metallic components within the imaging system and their interaction with the incident waves.

caption: Numerical absorption spectra for metapyramids with an apex angle of α = 60° across incident angles of 0°, 30°, 45°, and 60°.
summary: Numerical absorption spectra for metapyramids with an apex angle of α = 60° are presented for incident angles of 0°, 30°, 45°, and 60°. The absorptivity reaches over 0.9 within 7.5 to 18.9 GHz at 45° and preserves values above 0.8 within 7.4 to 18.6 GHz at 60° under TE polarization.

caption: Nyquist plots recorded after 3 days of immersion, highlighting a sudden enlargement of capacitive loops specifically for the HT-2 heat-treated alloy.
summary: At the 3-day immersion mark, the Nyquist plots demonstrate a significant evolution in the electrochemical response. A sudden enlargement of the capacitive loops is identified for the HT-2 specimen, indicating a distinct shift in the corrosion behavior and surface passivation characteristics of this specific heat-treated alloy after three days.

caption: Full-range Raman spectra comparing as-printed microstructures with samples subjected to thermal treatment (60 °C for 20 min) and O2 plasma etching at 35 °C, 50 °C, and 60 °C.
summary: This panel displays Raman spectra for as-printed microstructures alongside samples treated with temperature alone or O2 plasma at varying temperatures. The data illustrates the chemical changes induced by these treatments, providing a baseline for evaluating the degree of conversion across different experimental conditions maintained during the plasma exposure process.
