caption: Macroscopic visual documentation capturing the physical state of the specimen during the active welding process.
summary: This macroscopic photograph provides visual documentation of the specimen's physical state during the active welding process. It captures the real-time appearance of the material under processing conditions, offering a direct observation of the experimental setup and the macroscopic changes occurring throughout the duration of the welding operation.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) spectra of membrane samples charged with hydrogen for 14 days at 60 °C, plotted as intensity versus temperature for heating rates of 400, 800, 1000, and 1200 K/h.
summary: TDS spectra for hydrogen-charged membrane samples are presented across four distinct heating rates. These curves demonstrate that hydrogen reached saturation levels within the samples after 14 days of charging. The observed spectral profiles differ significantly from previous results, confirming the effectiveness of the applied hydrogen charging conditions and a homogeneous distribution.

caption: Low-field thermomagnetic ZFC and FC curves for annealed (FC773) Mn2FeSn samples recorded under an applied magnetic field of 8 kA/m.
summary: Annealed Mn2FeSn samples subjected to an 8 kA/m field display ZFC and FC curves that characterize the material's magnetic transitions post-thermal treatment. These results confirm the presence of multiple magnetic transitions, illustrating how post-synthesis thermal treatment induces structural changes that significantly influence the alloy's overall magnetic response.

caption: Geometric representation of a single unit cell of the VCH lattice, defined by a side length L of 50 mm.
summary: A single unit cell of the VCH lattice is presented, highlighting the fundamental repeating geometric unit of the structure. The cell is defined by a side length L of 50 mm, serving as the building block for the larger variable cross-section hollow lattice assembly described in the study.

caption: Surface roughness parameters Rmax, Rz, Ra, and Pt for the cylinder honed at 500 RPM.
summary: This panel displays the quantitative surface roughness results for a cylinder processed at 500 RPM. The measurements include Rmax, Rz, Ra, and Pt values, which characterize the surface quality achieved through the honing process. These metrics reflect the effectiveness of the honing tools in targeting and removing sharp surface hills.

caption: Comparative analysis of the adjustable permeability range in multiple directions between Sine structures and human bone tissue within the bone-growth-compatible design space.
summary: This panel compares the permeability range of Sine structures against that of human bone. By mapping these values within the design space suitable for bone growth, the visualization demonstrates how the adjustable permeability of the sinusoidal architecture aligns with the physiological requirements of natural bone tissue.

caption: Transmittance spectra of S, M, and L cones under normal trichromatic vision conditions, demonstrating the overlap and separation of spectral responses.
summary: Under normal trichromatic vision, the combined activation of S, M, and L cones enables the recognition of the complete visible spectrum. This panel displays the transmittance spectra of these cones, illustrating the specific overlap and separation of their spectral responses that facilitate full color perception.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) spectra of the vertical SS316L sample tested at a 10^-1 s^-1 strain rate, including an inset showing an enlarged spectral section.
summary: The SXRD spectra confirm the absence of strain-induced martensite (α′) at the higher strain rate, as the austenitic peak set remains unchanged. This diffraction analysis provides critical evidence regarding phase stability, demonstrating that the austenitic structure is maintained during the high-temperature tensile testing of the LPBF-fabricated SS316L material.

caption: Calculated weight fraction of the γ′ phase as a function of Nb content, derived from Thermo-calc software using the TTNi8 database.
summary: This panel displays the calculated weight fraction of the γ′ phase in Ni-Co-based superalloys as a function of Nb content. Using the Thermo-calc software and TTNi8 database, the results indicate that the γ′ phase fraction decreases with increasing temperature, showing a sharp decline at specific thresholds for varying Nb concentrations.

caption: Digital Image Correlation strain field contour for the first PA12 specimen set (S_PA12_02) at the incipient failure instant, highlighting the onset of fracture within the cross-section.
summary: Digital Image Correlation strain field contour for the first PA12 specimen set (S_PA12_02) at the incipient failure instant, highlighting the onset of fracture within the cross-section. This visualization captures the strain field in X and Y directions, clearly identifying the localized fracture zone marked by a red circle.

caption: Survey X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectrum of FeNi@N-CNTs, confirming the presence of C, O, N, Fe, and Ni elements.
summary: The survey XPS spectrum confirms the elemental composition of the FeNi@N-CNTs hybrid. Analysis reveals the presence of carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, iron, and nickel. The atomic percentage of nitrogen is approximately 4.52%, demonstrating successful nitrogen doping within the carbon nanotube framework, which contributes to the material's overall chemical state and active defect sites.

caption: Geometric representation of the fundamental unit cell defining the Gyroid lattice architecture.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental unit cell of the Gyroid lattice structure. It serves as the geometric basis for the more complex lattice configurations discussed in the study, providing the foundational architectural parameters required for the design and subsequent fabrication of the Gyroid-based samples described in the research.

caption: Atomic configuration snapshot at 500 K from the pseudo-ferrimagnetic (FiM) simulation, highlighting Fe-Cr ordering.
summary: This snapshot at 500 K shows the atomic configuration of the pseudo-ferrimagnetic (FiM) state. The FiM state favors Fe-Cr ordering and suppresses the formation of B1-type CrN-like domains. Fe, Ni, Cr, and N atoms are marked with red, green, blue, and dark blue, respectively.

caption: Comparative analysis of strength-ductility performance between the developed Al-Cu-Ni alloy and previously reported aluminum alloy literature.
summary: Performance comparison between the Al-Cu-Ni alloy and previously reported works is illustrated here. The results demonstrate that the Al-Cu-Ni alloy achieves a well-coordinated strength-ductility balance, positioning it favorably in comparison to existing aluminum alloy data compiled from the literature and supplementary material tables.

caption: Relative resistance change rate plotted against applied load for DIW-based 8Y–ZrO 2 sensors, comparing different filament orientations.
summary: Experimental data are presented as a plot of relative resistance change rate versus applied load. This graph analyzes the sensor response under mechanical stress for DIW-based 8Y–ZrO 2 sensors, specifically highlighting how varying filament orientations influence the electrical resistance behavior when subjected to different levels of applied load.

caption: Relative frequency distribution of the Schmid factor values calculated for the S1 specimen.
summary: This histogram quantifies the relative frequency of Schmid factor values for the S1 specimen. By plotting the distribution of these factors, the panel provides a statistical overview of the slip system orientation, facilitating a comparison of the mechanical potential across different regions or samples within the study.

caption: Circuit diagram illustrating the experimental setup for surface electrical insulation testing, featuring a DC high-voltage source with negative polarity and a picoammeter for current measurement.
summary: This schematic depicts the experimental circuit used to evaluate surface electrical insulation properties. A DC high-voltage source with negative polarity is applied to the sample, while a Keithley 6517B picoammeter measures the resulting surface electric current. This configuration serves as the basis for both experimental testing and the geometric model used in numerical simulations.

caption: HFR Cell response during individual pulses in the 40 s timeframe at 5 h.
summary: This panel displays the HFR Cell response during individual pulses within the 40 s timeframe around 5 h. It complements the other pulse-level data to provide a complete picture of the cell's resistance fluctuations during the rapid cycling of the galvanostatic current applied to the Fe alloy disk.

caption: Three-dimensional rendering illustrating the overall chip design architecture.
summary: This panel presents a three-dimensional rendering of the chip design. It serves as a foundational visual representation of the device architecture, providing a clear overview of the structural layout and configuration of the microfluidic system intended for sample retention and analysis within the experimental setup.

caption: Hardness profile plotted as a function of distance from the treated surface, illustrating the mechanical property gradient resulting from the hybrid treatment.
summary: This plot displays the hardness evolution of the material following a hybrid treatment, as determined by nanoindentation measurements. The data reveals a distinct gradient in mechanical properties, showing how hardness varies with increasing distance from the surface, which highlights the effectiveness of the applied surface modification process.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectrum of SLS-assisted SnO2 nanostructures measured at room temperature with 248 nm excitation.
summary: SLS-assisted SnO2 nanostructures exhibit a unique photoluminescence emission profile under 248 nm excitation at room temperature. This spectral measurement provides insight into the impact of SLS surfactant on the electronic and optical properties of the SnO2 nanoparticles, completing the comparative analysis of surfactant-aided synthesis effects on the material's luminescence.

caption: Three-dimensional distribution of pores specifically located within the Cu phase.
summary: The 3D distribution of pores within the copper phase of the composite is showcased in this panel. By isolating the porosity associated with the copper component, the image allows for a detailed examination of how pores are localized and distributed within this specific phase of the material.

caption: Training loss evolution for LNN-GKO and RNN-GKO surrogate models plotted against epoch count.
summary: The training loss curves for the LNN-GKO and RNN-GKO surrogate models demonstrate their learning behavior over time. Both models exhibit rapid convergence within the first 200 epochs, successfully stabilizing to low training loss values, which indicates effective training performance for these specific surrogate architectures during the model development process.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for the Al10Ni30Fe40Cr20 alloy, showing the initial formation of the FCC phase from the melt.
summary: The equilibrium phase diagram for the Al10Ni30Fe40Cr20 alloy demonstrates that the FCC phase forms first upon cooling from the melt. This diagram highlights the phase stability regions for this specific composition, providing insight into the solidification sequence and the initial structural development of the alloy system.

caption: Double logarithmic plot illustrating the steady-state strain rate versus true stress for CP and PM alloys at 350 °C.
summary: This panel presents the steady-state creep data for CP and PM alloys at 350 °C using a double logarithmic scale. By plotting strain rate against true stress according to the general-power law constitutive creep equation, the figure facilitates the determination of creep constants and stress exponents at this temperature.

caption: Weibull distribution plot illustrating the failure probability of rodded alumina disks (n=18) as a function of applied stress, with Hertzian contact stress failures excluded and dashed lines indicating confidence intervals.
summary: This Weibull plot characterizes the failure statistics of rodded alumina disks, excluding samples that failed due to Hertzian contact stress. The graph displays the failure probability against stress levels for eighteen specimens, with dashed lines representing the calculated confidence bounds to provide a statistical assessment of the material's mechanical reliability.

caption: Arrhenius plot of ln(Φ/Tmax^2) versus 1000/Tmax for membrane samples, utilized to extract activation energies for specific hydrogen traps.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the linear relationship between ln(Φ/Tmax^2) and 1000/Tmax for membrane samples. By performing linear fitting on these data points, the activation energies associated with different hydrogen traps are determined, providing critical insights into the hydrogen trapping behavior within the material's microstructure.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the A550 specimen showing a flat fracture surface characterized by numerous cleavage planes.
summary: This scanning electron microscopy image displays the tensile fracture surface of the A550 specimen. The morphology is characterized by a flat appearance and the presence of numerous cleavage planes, which are indicative of a typical brittle fracture mechanism occurring during the tensile test of this specific material condition.

caption: Cellular automaton grid representing the alloy corrosion process.
summary: This cellular automaton grid illustrates the progression of alloy corrosion. During the simulated corrosion process, metal grid sites are replaced by different particles, effectively modeling the degradation mechanism. The visualization provides a spatial representation of the material state changes as the corrosion front advances through the simulated alloy structure.

caption: Lower magnification STEM bright field image of an alpha-lath in the 800HIP sample, illustrating the distribution of alpha grain boundary interface dislocations.
summary: This lower magnification STEM bright field image captures an alpha-lath within the 800HIP microstructure. The visualization specifically highlights the arrangement of grain boundary interface dislocations associated with the alpha phase, offering insight into the dislocation density and distribution patterns observed at the boundaries of the lath structures.

caption: Micro-CT image of a commercial dental implant after 4 weeks of alveolar bone implantation, providing a cross-sectional view of the bone-implant interface.
summary: Micro-CT imaging reveals the interaction between the commercial dental implant and the surrounding alveolar bone tissue after a 4-week implantation period. The white regions in the scan indicate the presence of bone tissue attached to the surface of the commercial dental implant, demonstrating the osseointegration performance in vivo.

caption: Tensile strength and elastic modulus plotted against varying printing speeds, showing optimal performance at 30 mm/s.
summary: This plot displays the tensile strength and elastic modulus of composite fabrications as a function of printing speed. Experimental results indicate that the optimal mechanical performance, specifically for tensile strength and elastic modulus, is achieved at a printing speed of 30 mm/s, highlighting the influence of processing parameters on material integrity.

caption: Conceptual layout of the integrated high-speed and thermal imaging system designed for in situ monitoring of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processes in CuSn10 alloy.
summary: This schematic illustrates the self-developed LPBF equipment used to observe laser-matter interactions. By integrating high-speed imaging with thermal imaging, the setup enables multi-dimensional in situ analysis of the CuSn10 alloy during the additive manufacturing process, providing a comprehensive view of the dynamic thermal and physical phenomena occurring during laser processing.

caption: Micro-hardness distribution profile across repaired samples, comparing conditions before and after direct aging heat treatment.
summary: This figure illustrates the micro-hardness distribution of repaired samples, specifically evaluating the impact of direct aging heat treatment on mechanical properties. By comparing the hardness profiles before and after the aging process, the data provides insight into the effectiveness of the heat treatment in modifying the material's mechanical performance.

caption: Backward trajectory of a floating SiC particle transitioning from the central zone to the transition zone, driven by Marangoni forces.
summary: This panel illustrates the backward motion of a floating SiC particle within the melt pool. Driven by Marangoni forces, the particle transitions from the central zone to the transition zone. This trajectory highlights the influence of surface tension gradients on particle transport during the melting process at 4 wt% SiC.

caption: Oil-lubricated COF-time curve for the B1 textured sample, maintaining stability throughout the test.
summary: The B1 texture exhibits an oil-lubricated COF-time curve that remains stable throughout the entire testing process. This consistent frictional behavior indicates that the B1 surface modification provides robust performance, avoiding the fluctuations often seen in the running-in or wear phases of less optimized surface textures.

caption: DSC thermogram of the PLA/CNT filament displaying thermal transitions including glass transition, cold crystallization, and melting temperatures.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry thermogram of the filament highlights critical thermal transitions such as glass transition, cold crystallization, and melting temperatures. These thermal characteristics are essential for determining optimal 3D printing process parameters, ensuring that the material behaves predictably during the extrusion and deposition phases of the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map showing the crystallographic orientation of the as-deposited HNS at the bottom layer.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the crystallographic orientation of the as-deposited HNS at the bottom layer. As part of the EBSD micrograph series, this panel allows for the assessment of grain orientation and potential structural variations occurring at the base of the deposited material compared to the upper layers.

caption: Misorientation angle distribution histogram for the specimen processed at 1010 °C with a strain rate of 0.1 s⁻¹, TSOFS of 0.36, and SROSS of 0.001 s⁻¹.
summary: Depicting the misorientation angle distribution at 1010 °C, 0.1 s⁻¹ SROFS, 0.36 TSOFS, and 0.001 s⁻¹ SROSS, this plot demonstrates the effect of temperature. By comparing this with panel (b), it is evident that raising the deformation temperature from 980 °C to 1010 °C causes a slight decrease in mean misorientation angles.

caption: Low-magnification STEM-BF image revealing the heterogeneous distribution of the dislocation substructure throughout the single-crystal CrCoNi alloy.
summary: A low-magnification STEM-BF image provides a broad overview of the heterogeneous dislocation substructure in the single-crystal CrCoNi alloy. The image confirms the presence of varied dislocation features distributed throughout the material, supporting the observations of complex node and fault formations seen at higher magnifications.

caption: DSC second heating scans at 10 °C/min for PEB samples synthesized with varying BnOH equivalents, maintaining a fixed [EB]:[Cat]:[BnOH] ratio of 100:1:X.
summary: This panel displays DSC second heating scans for PEB samples prepared with variable BnOH equivalents. The thermal analysis reveals multiple melting peaks upon heating, following the initial crystallization exotherms. These curves illustrate the thermal behavior of the polymer samples as a function of the specific BnOH concentration used during synthesis.

caption: Overview of the fracture surface morphology for specimen HCF-M.
summary: This panel provides a comprehensive overview of the fracture surface morphology for specimen HCF-M. The image captures the overall topography and failure characteristics of the material, serving as the primary visual context for the subsequent detailed magnifications of specific zones observed across the fractured surface.

caption: Phase angle values calculated from the ratio of loss to storage moduli within the linear viscoelastic region for all paste samples.
summary: The viscoelastic phase angle is presented for all paste samples, derived from the ratio of loss to storage moduli within the linear viscoelastic region. This metric provides insight into the damping characteristics and the relative contribution of viscous versus elastic components in the control and graphene-modified paste suspensions.

caption: Comparative cycling performance of 3D-printed and ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrodes evaluated at a 1C rate, showing capacity retention over 100 cycles.
summary: This plot compares the cycle performance of 3D-printed and ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrodes at 1C. The 3D-printed electrode demonstrates high reversibility, maintaining a discharge capacity of 216.06 mAh g-1 when the current density is reduced to 0.1C, confirming superior electrochemical stability compared to the conventional ink-cast electrode.

caption: Normalized mass spectra of samples exposed to the atmosphere for 0–14 days, plotted on a logarithmic y-axis scale to compare vacuum properties after equivalent pump-down times.
summary: Normalized mass spectra for samples exposed to the atmosphere for 0–14 days demonstrate consistent vacuum properties when pump-down times match exposure durations. The similarity in species distribution across these spectra indicates that water re-adsorption is limited to the surface, confirming that vacuum performance remains stable despite varying atmospheric exposure times.

caption: AFM topographic surface image of an electro-polished oxide film specimen after 1 hour of exposure to high-temperature deionized water, exhibiting a surface with large particles at a low density.
summary: This AFM topographic image shows the surface of an electro-polished oxide film following 1 hour of exposure to high-temperature deionized water. The surface features large particles distributed at a low density, highlighting the unique surface topography resulting from the electro-polishing treatment compared to other surface preparation methods.

caption: Temperature sweeps showing the storage modulus of PMMA/PEG-based filaments with varying ATBC content, compounded at 30 rpm.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent storage modulus for various PMMA/PEG filaments compounded at 30 rpm. The experimental results confirm that the storage modulus for all tested filaments consistently remains above 600 MPa at a temperature of 25 °C, indicating stable mechanical performance across the varying ATBC content levels.

caption: Temporal graph snapshots representing the HIs at each cycle t, generated using PyTorch Geometric v2.3.1.
summary: This figure displays the temporal graph snapshots of HIs at each cycle t. These snapshots, which incorporate defined nodes and edges, were processed using PyTorch Geometric v2.3.1. The visualization illustrates the evolution of the graph structure across different timesteps, providing a clear representation of the system's state at each cycle.

caption: Regression curves fitted to fatigue data for FFF-printed PEEK, illustrating the material's performance under various experimental testing conditions.
summary: Regression curves are presented to illustrate the fatigue behavior of FFF-printed PEEK under different testing conditions. These fitted curves provide a visual representation of how varying parameters influence the fatigue life of the material, supporting the broader analysis of the mechanical performance of the printed polymer samples.

caption: Comparative analysis of defect quantity and volume fraction across UnEPT, EPT-1, and EPT-2 samples, highlighting the reduction in porosity.
summary: This bar chart displays the number of defects and their corresponding volume fractions for UnEPT, EPT-1, and EPT-2 samples. The results show that EPT-1 and EPT-2 parameters reduce defect volume fractions by up to 51.93% in the cladding region and 83.73% at the interface, effectively enhancing material density and load-bearing continuity.

caption: DSC analysis curves for CS, KC, CNC, curcumin, and the formulated 3D printlet, used to evaluate their respective thermal behaviors.
summary: DSC analysis was conducted on CS, KC, CNC, curcumin, and the formulated 3D printlet to characterize their thermal behavior. These curves reveal phase transitions and thermal events, allowing for a comparative assessment of the thermal properties of the individual components versus the final 3D printed composite material.

caption: Elemental composition table of ferrosilicon used as a precursor for Al-Si-Ni-Fe-V alloy synthesis.
summary: Ferrosilicon serves as a critical source of elements for developing Al 0.44 Si 0.32 Ni 0.09 Fe 0.05 V 0.05 alloys. The composition includes 22.32% Fe, 5.8% Al, 0.87% K, and a balance of 71.01% Si, as detailed in the elemental analysis table provided for the alloy development process.

caption: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of the Ni-rich Pt-Ni alloy, deconvoluted into five doublets to reveal a highly oxidized surface state.
summary: The high-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum for the Ni-rich Pt-Ni alloy indicates a highly oxidized surface. Deconvolution of the spectrum into five distinct doublets reveals that 57.6% of the nickel atoms exist in an oxidized state, confirming the susceptibility of Ni to oxidation in the presence of dissolved oxygen.

caption: EDS spectra obtained from spot locations on the MC100 specimen identifying newly formed inorganic gels.
summary: EDS analysis of the MC100 specimen confirms the formation of a mixture of C–S–H and N–S–H gels. These phases exhibit high Ca/Si and Na/Si ratios of 3.5 and 3.0, respectively, with very low aluminum content, demonstrating the chemical evolution of the polymeric network following the calcination of the marly soil.

caption: Bright field TEM image revealing the internal microstructural features of the inversed pyramidal specimen.
summary: The bright field TEM image captures the internal microstructural morphology of the inversed pyramidal specimen. By utilizing transmission electron microscopy, this panel offers a clear view of the specimen's internal features, complementing the STEM observations and providing context for the high-resolution imaging and elemental mapping performed on the same region.

caption: Predicted fatigue life values for the entire experimental dataset plotted against observed life, utilizing a Walker strain equation with a constant exponent of 0.72 across all tested temperatures.
summary: This plot displays predicted versus observed fatigue life for the complete dataset using a Walker strain equation with a single exponent of 0.72. The analysis incorporates a U value of 0.84 derived from the simple Walker approach, demonstrating the model's performance in predicting fatigue behavior across varying temperature conditions.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the interfacial zone, revealing white polygonal phases distributed throughout the bond interface.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the interfacial zone clearly reveals the presence of white polygonal phases distributed along the bond interface. These fine particles were targeted for further investigation to determine their chemical identity, as they represent distinct structural features formed during the diffusion-welding process at 1100°C.

caption: Sunlight absorption spectrum of an aqueous fructose solution, displaying a characteristic absorption maximum at approximately 240 nm and a limited absorption range extending up to 340 nm.
summary: The UV-Vis absorption spectrum of an aqueous fructose solution reveals a distinct absorption maximum at approximately 240 nm. Experimental data indicates that the absorption for this solution is limited to wavelengths up to 340 nm, distinguishing it from other chemical materials like water, NaOH, and sodium lauryl sulphate.

caption: Comparison of experimental test results for DED-Arc CHS specimens against design predictions derived from the EN 1993-1-6 standard.
summary: This plot evaluates the structural performance of DED-Arc CHS specimens by comparing experimental test results with theoretical design predictions according to EN 1993-1-6. The analysis incorporates data from literature, including specimens with documented local imperfection amplitudes, to assess the accuracy and reliability of the standard's predictive capabilities for these specific components.

caption: Illustration of the indicator function used to define the geometry of a strut containing a structural imperfection.
summary: This panel presents a schematic illustration of the indicator function employed to define the geometric boundaries of a strut. The function specifically incorporates a structural imperfection, providing the mathematical basis for generating the synthetic volumetric model of the component as described in the study's methodology.

caption: 2D distribution of sonoluminescence (SL) intensity at 3 MPa hydrostatic pressure, showing the spatial variation of photon counts under 2000 W power.
summary: Representing the sonoluminescence intensity at 3 MPa, this heatmap illustrates the photon counting distribution captured by the emICCD. The data reflects the spatial characteristics of the cavitation cloud under these specific pressure conditions, serving as a comparative point for analyzing how increased pressure influences the intensity and concentration of light emission.

caption: Traction equilibrating method applied to the coarse mesh domain.
summary: The second stage of the optimization framework involves the application of a traction equilibrating method. This process bridges the coarse-level discretization and the subsequent fine-level analysis, ensuring that the mechanical boundary conditions are appropriately balanced across the domain elements before proceeding to the final high-resolution topology optimization step.

caption: Schematic representation of the adopted manufacturing workflow, highlighting the integration of re-engineering and CAD stages to optimize geometric parameters and address manufacturing challenges.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the adopted manufacturing workflow, which incorporates re-engineering during the CAD stage to minimize geometric iterations. By considering various parameters early in the design process, the workflow effectively addresses complex geometrical features, ensuring a more efficient and robust manufacturing approach for challenging components.

caption: Lowest band gaps plotted against the squeeze ratio s for a Co/Py 2D MC, where only the 2nd and 4th gaps are observed to open.
summary: The graph displays the lowest band gaps for a Co/Py 2D MC structure relative to the squeeze ratio s. In this reversed material composition, the band gap regulation is significantly poorer compared to the Py/Co structure, with only the 2nd and 4th band gaps opening during the process.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the area circled in panel (a), demonstrating the coexistence of nanocrystalline and amorphous phases within the deformed microstructure.
summary: High-resolution TEM analysis of the selected region from the deformed alloy reveals a dual-phase microstructure. The image clearly shows the presence of both nanocrystalline and amorphous phases, confirming that the severe deformation process has induced a complex, heterogeneous structural state within the material at the nanoscale level.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of Ti-2.5Al-xNb-xCu quaternary alloys, showing the predominance of the alpha phase and the presence of the Ti2Cu intermetallic phase.
summary: The XRD pattern for the Ti-2.5Al-xNb-xCu alloy system confirms that the alpha phase remains the predominant constituent. Despite the presence of the Ti2Cu intermetallic phase, the alloy exhibits significant ductility, indicating that the intermetallic phase is not the primary factor controlling the fracture elongation of these quaternary titanium alloys.

caption: Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram showing the distribution of simulated rays at a 200 mm coaxial distance from the process zone for Point 0,0 at 450 nm wavelength, utilizing stable dome parameters for probe 1.
summary: This Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram illustrates the ray distribution at a 200 mm coaxial distance for Point 0,0 at 450 nm. Using stable dome parameters from probe 1, the analysis beams exhibit minimal deflection, hitting the detector center with a 99.78% probability, confirming high process stability.

caption: Fabricated agarose hydrogel part resting on the SAM printing substrate, maintained in a humidified environment via blue hoses to prevent dehydration.
summary: This photograph displays an agarose hydrogel structure immediately following the fabrication process while still positioned on the SAM printing substrate. To preserve the hydrogel's physical properties and prevent water evaporation, the environment is actively controlled using a humidifier connected via blue hoses, ensuring the part remains hydrated during the post-fabrication stage.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to the negative control medium.
summary: This fluorescence microscopy image displays Human Gingival Fibroblasts cultured for 24 hours in a negative control environment. The visualization utilizes Live/Dead staining to distinguish between viable cells, shown in green, and non-viable cells, shown in red, providing a baseline for assessing the biocompatibility of the tested materials.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay profile and fitting curve for TPU/1S composite, recorded at 490 nm emission wavelength.
summary: This panel displays the fluorescence lifetime decay profile and fitting curve for the TPU/1S composite at 490 nm. Consistent with the 3-5 ns average lifespan observed for SAOED additions below 2 wt%, this measurement characterizes the temporal decay behavior of the material under room temperature excitation.

caption: Fourier-transformed Cu K-edge EXAFS spectra for CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC, showing a prominent peak at approximately 2.3 Å.
summary: Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra at the Cu K-edge for both CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC are shown. A prominent peak is observed at approximately 2.3 Å, which is consistent with the characteristic Cu-Cu bonding peak found in metallic Cu foil, indicating the presence of metallic copper clusters.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of an Al-rich region showing atomic positions of Al, Co, and Cr within a 25–125 nm depth range, with isoconcentration surfaces highlighting Al-rich (≥35 at.%) and Cr-rich (≥25 at.%) domains.
summary: This APT reconstruction reveals the spatial distribution of Al, Co, and Cr in an Al-rich region. Isoconcentration surfaces delineate Al-rich and Cr-rich phases within the 25–125 nm depth range. The analysis confirms Cr and Al enrichment, providing insight into the local chemical heterogeneity of the specimen.

caption: Evolution of strain distributions under LCF loading for specimen #1, showing the leftward shift of peak A1 and the transient emergence and subsequent disappearance of peak B1 at site B1.
summary: Strain distributions for specimen #1 under LCF loading reveal dynamic changes in local deformation. From the first cycle to the 2650th cycle, strain peak A1 shifts leftward along the hole circumference. Concurrently, peak B1 emerges and eventually disappears, indicating significant strain redistribution within the material during the fatigue process.

caption: High-resolution electron microscopy (HREM) image and corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) electron diffraction patterns (EDPs) of the two-phase boundary.
summary: High-resolution electron microscopy imaging of the two-phase boundary demonstrates that the interface is coherent. The corresponding FFT electron diffraction patterns provide further insight into the structural relationship at this boundary, which is noted to be less flat than the twin boundaries typically observed in pure ZrCu martensite laths.

caption: HLAW arc behavior at t+0 ms, where the laser spot is at the 9 o'clock position and the dynamic filament spacing reaches its maximum.
summary: At t+0 ms, the HLAW arc is deflected toward the laser beam due to strong attraction. The laser spot is positioned at 9 o'clock, resulting in the maximum dynamic filament spacing. This interaction between the laser and the arc is a key feature of the HLAW welding process.

caption: Atomic configuration at an elevated temperature, where brown arrows indicate increased disorder within the grain boundaries and new grey atoms emerge within the grain interior.
summary: At an elevated temperature, the atomic configuration reveals increased disorder within the grain boundaries, as highlighted by brown arrows. Additionally, new grey atoms appear within the grain interior, indicating structural changes compared to the 300 K state. This snapshot captures the initial configuration evolution as temperature increases in the sample.

caption: Transmittance values at 405 nm for composite resins containing various concentrations of S-CNCs and A-CNCs, processed with 120 s of ultrasonication.
summary: Transmittance at 405 nm is compared for composite resins with various S-CNC and A-CNC concentrations after 120 s of ultrasonication. The results demonstrate the differences in optical clarity between the two CNC types, confirming that S-CNC/CTFA resins exhibit a significant reduction in transparency compared to A-CNC/CTFA resins.

caption: Elastic modulus trend along the corrosion depth for AlCrFeNi and 316L, highlighting the sudden modulus increase in 316L at 10 μm.
summary: Elastic modulus trends along the corrosion depth are compared for both materials. While AlCrFeNi shows a relatively smooth transition, 316L exhibits a sudden change in elastic modulus at a depth of 10 μm, where the value increases significantly from 146.23 GPa to 190.97 GPa, reflecting the transition to the matrix.

caption: Atomic configuration of the A5 supercell model, representing a Zr-free variant of the S2 structure.
summary: The A5 supercell model is a Zr-free configuration constructed to evaluate the structural stability of S2 in the absence of zirconium. This model serves as a comparative reference point to understand the specific contribution of Zr to the thermodynamic stability of the overall S2 material system.

caption: BEI transmission spectra acquired from the Fe (316 L) and Cu (CuCrZr) layers of the multilayer specimen oriented in the TD1 direction.
summary: This panel displays the BEI transmission spectra for the Fe and Cu layers within the multilayer sample oriented in the TD1 direction. These spectroscopic measurements provide essential data regarding the electronic or structural state of the constituent layers, serving as a basis for subsequent residual strain profile analysis.

caption: XPS survey spectra of the shaped glass, verifying its chemical purity relative to commercial fused SiO2.
summary: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) provides further confirmation of the chemical purity of the shaped glass. The spectra, when compared to commercial fused SiO2, demonstrate that the material retains the expected elemental characteristics of pure silica, supporting the efficacy of the printing and shaping methodology.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for the Ti–22Al-xNb (at%) alloy system, illustrating the phase stability regions as a function of niobium content and temperature.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the Ti–22Al-xNb alloy system serves as a reference for understanding the phase composition and stability of the material. It provides the necessary thermodynamic context to interpret the phase transitions observed during the thermal analysis of the Ti2AlNb alloy samples.

caption: Diffusion trajectory of a single H atom near the NGI at 1000 K over 5.0 ns.
summary: Visualizing the H atom diffusion at 1000 K, this panel maps the displacement vectors over 5.0 ns. The solute H remains trapped near the NGI, a behavior linked to the formation of a sp3 C–H bond with a graphene surface C atom, which significantly impedes the atom's long-range diffusion.

caption: Parity plot comparing ML-predicted normalized hardness and Young's modulus against measured values for the training dataset, with a solid line indicating perfect model-target agreement.
summary: This parity plot displays the correlation between machine learning predicted normalized hardness and Young's modulus versus measured values for the training dataset. The solid line represents ideal model performance where predictions match target data. The neural network achieved a low RMS error of 5.69 × 10^-3 after 29 training rounds.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification model for Inconel 625 calculated using Thermo-Calc software and the TCNI11 database.
summary: This panel presents the Scheil-Gulliver solidification model for Inconel 625, generated via Thermo-Calc and the TCNI11 database. The model predicts the formation of Laves, MC-type carbides, and δ phases during solidification, although the δ phase formation predicted here was not experimentally observed in related studies of melting pool solidification.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing <c+a>-type dislocations within the grain.
summary: This bright-field TEM image highlights the presence of <c+a>-type dislocations within the grain. These dislocations are essential for accommodating strain in the c-axis direction, indicating complex slip interactions that contribute to the localized stress concentration and subsequent crack initiation.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the AH-1100–60 specimen obtained via energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.
summary: This panel displays the elemental distribution map for the AH-1100–60 scheme, as determined by EDS mapping analysis. The visualization provides a spatial representation of the chemical composition within the material under the specified AH-1100–60 processing condition, facilitating an assessment of elemental homogeneity and distribution across the sample surface.

caption: Bar chart representing the anodic peak current values extracted from the cyclic voltammograms for the different activation conditions.
summary: Anodic peak current values are plotted to quantify the electrochemical performance of the electrodes following NA, D, and I activation processes. This data, derived from the cyclic voltammograms, provides a clear comparison of the oxidation current magnitudes to identify the most effective activation method for the working electrode.

caption: Initial three-dimensional concave hexagonal cell structure of the TPU auxetic honeycomb pad.
summary: This panel displays the initial three-dimensional concave hexagonal cell structure of the TPU auxetic honeycomb pad. This design was previously proposed by the research group as the foundational geometry for the pad, serving as the baseline for subsequent structural modifications aimed at enhancing mechanical performance.

caption: Phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic relationship between the low-temperature martensitic phase and the high-temperature austenitic phase in shape memory alloys.
summary: This phase diagram delineates the structural transition between the martensitic and austenitic phases in shape memory alloys. It highlights the fundamental thermodynamic states, specifically the low-temperature martensite and high-temperature austenite, which are essential for understanding the material's phase transformation behavior and its associated shape memory properties.

caption: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra for all samples, indicating the metallic state of Ni in Ni1Co3@NC.
summary: The normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectrum for the Ni1Co3@NC sample is presented. Comparison with Ni foil standards reveals that the Ni species exists in a metallic state. This observation is consistent with complementary XRD and XPS characterization, confirming the chemical state of the nickel within the composite material.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental and predicted deposition efficiency for System-2, featuring labeled test IDs and open yellow points denoting calibration tests.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the agreement between experimental and predicted deposition efficiency for System-2. Consistent with a drag coefficient of 0.65, the data points are labeled by test ID, while open yellow points identify the calibration tests, allowing for a direct comparison of predictive performance across the system.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction of κ-carbide plotted as a function of temperature for the base steel plate and the 3D-printed surface layer.
summary: This plot illustrates the equilibrium phase fraction of κ-carbide in both the base steel plate and the 3D-printed surface layer. Thermodynamic calculations indicate that κ-carbide precipitation is more pronounced in the 3D-printed surface layer compared to the base material, highlighting the influence of processing conditions on phase stability.

caption: Microstructure of NiTi sample-B in the XY plane at a height of 1200 μm, illustrating the grain morphology.
summary: Representing the microstructure of NiTi sample-B in the XY plane at a height of 1200 μm, this panel provides insight into the grain morphology at this stage of deposition. It is part of the series demonstrating the steady-state microstructure development as the height of the sample increases.

caption: STEM image and corresponding Al, Ni, and Fe elemental maps of the red rectangle region identified in Fig. 6(f), illustrating the corrosion morphology around needle-like κV phases.
summary: This STEM image and associated elemental mapping of the red rectangle region from Fig. 6(f) reveal the corrosion characteristics around needle-like κV phases. The results indicate that the severity of anodic dissolution in this area is comparable to that observed around globular κII phases, demonstrating similar corrosion attack extents.

caption: DSC cooling curves for the lower and middle regions of a homogeneous NiTi wall, showing two distinct phase transformation peaks.
summary: DSC cooling curves for the lower and middle regions of a homogeneous NiTi wall are presented. The experimental results indicate that both the middle and lower regions of the homogeneous NiTi alloy sample exhibit two distinct peaks during the cooling process, characterizing their specific martensitic phase transformation behavior.

caption: Stokes parameters measurement for the -1st-order diffraction of a vertical binary phase grating with an 8 pixel/period resolution.
summary: This panel shows the Stokes parameters for the -1st-order diffraction of a vertical binary phase grating. The grating period is set to 8 pixels. The visualization provides a map of the polarization state, demonstrating the diffraction behavior and polarization modulation of the -1st-order light at this resolution.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of RA800 alloy grain interior illustrating homogeneously distributed γ′ particles.
summary: The dark-field TEM image of the RA800 alloy grain interior demonstrates a homogeneous distribution of γ′ particles. Similar to the RA600 condition, these precipitates are identified via the (100) superlattice spots shown in the inset diffraction pattern, confirming the consistent formation of the γ′ phase within the grains.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the 7Co10Ni plating bath on glassy carbon at 50 mV s-1, showing current response variations across cathodic potential limits from -1.17 V to -1.50 V.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms for the 7Co10Ni plating bath on glassy carbon demonstrate that bulk CoNi deposition requires significant overpotential for nucleation and growth. Increasing the negative potential limit reveals a clear reduction peak, while further extension to -1.50 V induces massive solvent reduction currents and significant broadening of the oxidation peak.

caption: Nyquist plots illustrating the electrochemical impedance response of Inconel 625 base metal and weld metal specimens during corrosion testing.
summary: Nyquist plots are presented to characterize the electrochemical impedance response of the Inconel 625 base metal and weld metal specimens. These plots provide essential data regarding the corrosion resistance and interfacial properties of the materials, serving as a comparative metric for the electrochemical performance of the base and weld regions.

caption: Calculated mechanical indices representing the ratios of hardness to modulus (H/E) and the H3/E2 parameter for the three sample types.
summary: To further evaluate the resistance of each material to elastic and plastic deformation, two key mechanical indices, H/E and H3/E2, were calculated. These parameters provide critical insights into the material's ability to withstand deformation, allowing for a comparative assessment of the mechanical durability across the different processing methods.

caption: Cyclic stability test of the encapsulated μSC with PPy/3D-IDCμE over 5000 cycles at a constant current density of 2 mA cm⁻².
summary: Cyclic stability testing evaluates the long-term performance of the encapsulated μSC. Following 5000 charge-discharge cycles at a current density of 2 mA cm⁻², the device utilizing the 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H2SO4 electrolyte demonstrates robust performance, successfully retaining 75% of its initial capacitance throughout the testing period.

caption: Correlation graph displaying predicted against actual elongation values for the heat-treated material condition.
summary: Elongation performance is assessed in this parity plot, which maps predicted values against actual experimental results. This graphical representation is used to verify the agreement between the design model and the observed material behavior, confirming the reliability of the model for predicting elongation in the heat-treated condition.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile for specimen 4, contrasting the BD (red) and SD (black) diffraction patterns.
summary: Specimen 4 is analyzed via its neutron diffraction peak profile, with red and black lines representing the BD and SD conditions, respectively. This initial profile provides essential information regarding the specimen's crystalline structure, completing the set of diffraction data used to characterize the four specimens in this study.

caption: XPS Co 2p core-level spectrum of the Ru 1% CoB catalyst.
summary: The XPS Co 2p core-level spectrum of the Ru 1% CoB catalyst provides detailed information regarding the chemical state of cobalt. This spectroscopic analysis is used to characterize the surface electronic environment of the amorphous alloy, contributing to the overall understanding of the catalyst's surface composition and oxidation states.

caption: Time-dependent dilatometry data showing the partitioning behavior as a function of duration.
summary: Dilatometry data presented here tracks the partitioning behavior as a function of time. The curves demonstrate how the material evolves during the isothermal holding period, highlighting the sensitivity of the partitioning process to temperature and duration, which directly influences the resulting microstructural development during the overall QP heat treatment cycle.

caption: Specific heat capacity (Cp) of 3D printed ACs plotted against temperature up to 473 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific heat capacity of 3D printed ACs as a function of temperature, reaching up to 473 K. The data was derived from differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) measurements, providing a quantitative assessment of the thermal properties of the printed materials across the investigated temperature range.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of MC3T3 pre-osteoblast cells cultured on the surface of sample S2 after 72 h of incubation, showing cell morphology.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of MC3T3 pre-osteoblast cells cultured on the S2 sample surface after 72 h of incubation reveals the cellular morphology. The image confirms that cells cultured on this substrate exhibit healthy characteristics, consistent with the biocompatibility assessment performed via the Alamar Blue assay for the tested material.

caption: Emission spectra of the sensor responding to varying AA concentrations from 0.0 to 1.2 mmol L-1 in artificial tear fluid at pH 7.4, demonstrating the fluorescence quenching effect.
summary: The emission spectra show a clear concentration-dependent fluorescence quenching of the BSA-Au NCs in the presence of ascorbic acid. These results confirm the sensor's sensitivity to AA within the physiological range of artificial tear fluid, providing a reliable optical signal for quantitative detection at room temperature.

caption: Comparison of apparent density and Hall flow velocity for copper powders synthesized via pulsed arc and continuous arc methods.
summary: This table presents the physical characteristics of copper powders produced by different arc methods. The pulsed arc copper powder exhibits an apparent density of 4.11 g/cm3 and a Hall flow velocity of 21.19s/50g, whereas the continuous arc powder shows lower density at 3.92 g/cm3 and slower flow velocity at 23.5s/50g.

caption: Comparative performance evaluation of fatigue life prediction accuracy across SNN, DNN, and SADNN model architectures, highlighting the effect of varying hidden layer depth.
summary: This comparison evaluates the predictive accuracy of SNN, DNN, and SADNN models. By examining how varying the network depth through the number of hidden layers influences results, the analysis identifies the most effective architecture for fatigue life prediction, demonstrating the impact of model complexity on overall predictive capability.

caption: N-Cadh immunofluorescence staining of BMSCs on 3D-printed scaffolds, highlighting pronounced expression in the P-CaSiO3 group.
summary: N-cadherin immunofluorescence staining of BMSCs cultured on 3D-printed scaffolds demonstrates the influence of scaffold chemistry on early chondrogenic commitment. The P-CaSiO3 group displays the most pronounced N-Cadh expression, suggesting that this scaffold composition is particularly effective at promoting early-stage chondrogenic differentiation compared to the other tested scaffold groups.

caption: Geometrically Necessary Dislocation (GND) density map of the HX sample.
summary: The Geometrically Necessary Dislocation density map of the HX sample provides a spatial visualization of the dislocation density. This map, derived from the sample's crystallographic data, illustrates the distribution of GNDs, which are fundamental to understanding the mechanical behavior and strain hardening characteristics of the HX material.

caption: Photographic documentation of the printing processes utilized for the Bunny-Head model, highlighting the implementation of force-based adaptive deposition.
summary: These photographs capture the actual printing processes for the Bunny-Head model. The images demonstrate the practical application of the force-based adaptive deposition technique, providing a visual record of how the printing system handles the 251 curved layers during the fabrication of the complex geometry described in the study.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for ODS-316L alloy processed at a laser energy density of 132.3 J/mm3.
summary: This histogram illustrates the grain size distribution of ODS-316L alloy fabricated at a laser energy density of 132.3 J/mm3. The data serves as a baseline for comparing microstructural evolution, as the grain size is measured at 129.0 μm under these specific processing conditions before further energy density increases.

caption: Evolution of dislocation lines resulting from simulated box deformation, illustrating the progression of internal structural defects.
summary: Following the initial microstates, dislocation lines grow as a direct consequence of the simulation box deformation. This panel captures the dynamic response of the atomic model to the applied mechanical stress, highlighting the progressive development of defects within the polycrystalline structure as the fatigue test proceeds.

caption: EELS mapping data representing the elemental distribution across the analyzed microstructure.
summary: The EELS mapping data provides high-resolution elemental information for the Ti-6Al-4V-1.0B alloy. This panel, along with the subsequent EELS-based images, illustrates the distribution of light elements, offering a detailed view of the chemical composition that complements the EDS results and confirms the structural features observed in the TEM bright-field images.

caption: In-situ observation of an electrode with gold coating and large dimples during electrolysis at 0.7 V.
summary: This image shows an electrode combining a gold coating with large dimples during electrolysis at 0.7 V. The research investigates the synergistic effects of coating and patterning. The findings indicate that such modified electrodes promote the release of smaller, more transient bubbles, outperforming flat surfaces in electrochemical bubble management.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the H282 alloy dataset acquired using an Invizo 6000 instrument, containing approximately 350 million atoms.
summary: Representing a significantly larger field of view and atom count, this panel shows an APT reconstruction of the H282 sample collected on the Invizo 6000. The volume contains 350 million atoms, with Al positions and (Al, Ti) 10 at.% isoconcentration surfaces visualized to highlight the enhanced data collection capabilities of the Invizo 6000.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of the coating after annealing at 1000 °C, showing near-complete transformation into h-AlN and TiN.
summary: At 1000 °C, the (Ti,Al)N coating has almost entirely decomposed into h-AlN and TiN. The HAADF-STEM image reveals that while the bulk is transformed, small remnants of the original (Ti,Al)N grains persist throughout the structure, along with a thin strip of (Ti,Al)N located above the lower coating interface.

caption: Current transients and j vs. t^-1/2 plots for a Ni0.95Ce0.05 alloy electrode under constant potential conditions of 0.73 V.
summary: The electrochemical behavior of the Ni0.95Ce0.05 alloy electrode is characterized by chronoamperometry at 0.73 V. The plot includes the measured current transient and the derived j vs. t^-1/2 relationship, which are used to evaluate the catalytic performance of the cerium-doped nickel material for the hydrogen peroxide reduction reaction in alkaline media.

caption: Partial density of states for a C solute atom and a Ni atom located near the solute at the Σ 5 (310) grain boundary.
summary: This panel illustrates the PDOS for a C solute atom and a Ni atom near the grain boundary. The spin-polarized p-orbital DOS for C and d-orbital DOS for Ni are shown. A distinct peak overlap between C 2p and Ni 3d states becomes evident, indicating strong hybridization.

caption: LC–HRMS extracted ion chromatograms comparing the elution profiles of two C6H8F2N4O2 isomers (m/z 189.0582) in artificial saliva after 24 hours and 3 months of Saremco print CROWNTECH specimen incubation, alongside a 3-month control sample.
summary: Extracted ion chromatograms demonstrate the presence of two fluorinated C6H8F2N4O2 isomers leached from CROWNTECH specimens into artificial saliva. Global normalization reveals that the relative peak intensities for these leachable molecules increase significantly between 24 hours and 3 months of incubation, confirming time-dependent release compared to the 3-month control sample.

caption: Thermal expansion coefficient evolution of the composite during the third heating run (III) up to 1000 °C, compared across heating rates of 5 °C/min (S1), 10 °C/min (S2), and 15 °C/min (S3).
summary: This plot illustrates the thermal expansion coefficient of the composite during the third heating run up to 1000 °C. A smooth increase occurs between 100 and 500 °C for all heating rates. Notably, a significant decrease in the coefficient is observed at 500 °C for the 5 °C/min rate, followed by subsequent increases.

caption: Demonstration of the dimensional measurement process using a micrometer.
summary: This photograph demonstrates the measurement process using a RexBeti 0–25 mm micrometer, which features a resolution of 0.001 mm. This equipment was employed to accurately determine the dimensions of the printed plates, ensuring precise data collection for the experimental evaluation of the samples.

caption: Final structure of Fiber A on a carbon substrate after a 5-minute FAD spraying duration, showing no fiber lamination.
summary: This photograph displays the result of applying Fiber A via the FAD method onto a carbon substrate. After a 5-minute spraying duration, the sample shows no evidence of fiber lamination, indicating that Fiber A does not successfully form a deposit under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Diagram illustrating the generation of thermal undercooling in alloy systems characterized by small versus large solute rejection at the solidification front.
summary: This diagram demonstrates how solute redistribution influences thermal undercooling zones during solidification. Alloys exhibiting greater solute rejection generate larger thermal undercooling zones and higher thermal undercooling values. This relationship underscores the critical role of solute redistribution in determining the thermal conditions required for nucleation during the solidification of various alloy systems.

caption: Calculated phase map of the Ti-1023 alloy generated using Thermocalc software to guide the optimization of heat treatment parameters.
summary: This phase map, calculated using Thermocalc software, provides a theoretical guide for optimizing heat treatment process parameters for the Ti-1023 alloy. It serves as a critical reference for understanding phase stability and transitions, which is essential for controlling the alloy's microstructure during subsequent thermal processing steps.

caption: Grain and cell size distribution histogram for the HX sample.
summary: This histogram displays the grain and cell size distribution for the HX sample. Analysis of the microstructure reveals that the HX sample exhibits a grain size of approximately 10 μm and a cell size of 0.65 μm, serving as a baseline for comparison with the modified HX-C sample.

caption: In situ Fe K-edge QXANES spectra of reduced 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst during DRM at 750 °C and 1 atm with a CH4/CO2 ratio of 1/1.
summary: This panel illustrates the in situ Fe K-edge QXANES spectra for the 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst during DRM at a CH4/CO2 ratio of 1/1. The experimental spectra, depicted by solid lines, evolve over the 30-minute reaction duration at 750 °C, as indicated by the bold arrows relative to the reference spectra.

caption: Impedance modulus versus frequency plot for the fibre-like Ni-Co coating after 1 week of exposure.
summary: This Bode plot displays the impedance modulus of the fibre-like Ni-Co coating measured after a 1-week exposure period. The data provides insight into the electrochemical impedance characteristics of the coating surface, serving as a key component in evaluating the material's performance and stability over the specified duration of the electrochemical test.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of rBMSCs on porous alloy scaffolds after 3 days of coculture, highlighting cell spreading and proliferation.
summary: Live/dead staining fluorescence images reveal the distribution of rBMSCs on the surface of four porous alloy scaffolds after 3 days. The findings indicate that the cells effectively spread and proliferated across all scaffold types, demonstrating successful initial colonization and biocompatibility of the porous structures at this early stage.

caption: TEM image of as-deposited HNS subjected to dynamic compression at a strain rate of 4012 s⁻¹.
summary: Dynamic compression at a strain rate of 4012 s⁻¹ results in high-density twinning within the as-deposited HNS. Significant dislocation accumulation near twin boundaries leads to blurred boundary features, while the overall microstructure confirms that twinning and twin intersections remain the primary deformation modes under these extreme loading conditions.

caption: Focal series exit-wave reconstructed phase image of the Al2O3–NiAl3 grain boundary, showing a sharp and clean interface without intergranular films.
summary: This focal series exit-wave reconstructed phase image illustrates the interface in the Al2O3–NiAl3 sample. Unlike the Ni3Al-wetted sample, this boundary appears sharp and clean. The reconstruction confirms the absence of any intergranular films, indicating a different wetting behavior at the alumina grain boundary when paired with the NiAl3 phase.

caption: Orientation maps of the P60V150 tensile sample obtained via EBSD analysis.
summary: Orientation maps of the P60V150 tensile sample are obtained via EBSD analysis. These maps provide a spatial representation of the crystallographic orientations within the material, serving as a basis for understanding the texture and grain structure evolution that occurred during the tensile deformation process.

caption: Tensile stress-strain response of the PA polymer, demonstrating a non-linear hardening behavior characteristic of the material.
summary: The tensile stress-strain curve for the PA polymer illustrates a distinct non-linear hardening response. This mechanical behavior is essential for accurately modeling the material's performance in simulations. The data, derived from mechanical testing and manufacturer specifications, highlights the intrinsic deformation characteristics of the polymer under load.

caption: Tan delta curves as a function of temperature for the specified 4D printed composite formulations, highlighting viscoelastic damping properties.
summary: Tan delta versus temperature plots are shown for the 100% BPR, 95% BPR 5% BBZ, and 95% BPR 5% BBZ 1% PPy prints. These curves help identify the glass transition temperature, with the recovery temperature of the composite noted to be slightly above the Tg of the 95% BPR 5% BBZ 1% PPy print.

caption: Indexed 1D HEXRD patterns for the (Ni42.5Ti50Cu7.5)99Co1 alloy, displaying the B2 austenite phase at 373 K and the B19′ martensite phase at 213 K.
summary: This alloy follows the same transformation sequence as the Cu6.5 variant. At 373 K, the B2 austenite lattice parameter is 3.032 Å. Upon cooling to 213 K, the B19′ martensite phase forms with lattice parameters a=2.908 Å, b=4.164 Å, c=4.622 Å, and β=96.00°, as confirmed by the indexed diffraction peaks.

caption: Live/Dead staining images of the whole bioprinted corneal structure on days 1 and 7, demonstrating high cell viability and consistent dead cell counts over time.
summary: Live/Dead staining of the multi-material corneal structure on days 1 and 7 reveals excellent cell viability. The number of dead cells remains stable between these time points. Furthermore, the staining illustrates that live hASC-CSKs undergo a morphological transition from a rounded shape to an elongated state after 7 days post-printing.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loop measured at ambient temperature for the HT BMS sample, featuring an inset that illustrates the dependence of saturation magnetization and coercivity on Mn concentration.
summary: HT BMS samples show distinct magnetic hysteresis behavior at ambient temperature. The included inset provides an enlarged central section used to estimate coercivity, while also plotting saturation magnetization against Mn content. These results, supported by standard measurement deviations, characterize the magnetic properties of the BMS series under ambient conditions.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing steady-state creep rates normalized according to Eq. (4) plotted against inverse temperature for the same aluminum alloy specimens.
summary: This plot presents the creep rates normalized by Eq. (4) as a function of inverse temperature. Following normalization, the variation in creep rates decreases to less than a factor of 4, which provides significant experimental support for the Thouless model regarding creep mechanisms in thin film aluminum alloys.

caption: Faradaic efficiency for CO production at 12.5 mA/cm² current density as a function of Ag deposition potential.
summary: This panel illustrates the Faradaic efficiency for CO production at a current density of 12.5 mA/cm² across varying Ag deposition potentials. The data reveals a distinct trend where optimal deposition potentials enhance CO₂ reduction selectivity, while excessively negative potentials compromise performance, highlighting the sensitivity of the catalyst to synthesis conditions.

caption: S-N fatigue data for vertically printed PBF-LB 70/30 Cu–Ni specimens in both as-built (AB) and heat-treated (HT) conditions, with arrows highlighting runout specimens.
summary: Vertically printed PBF-LB 70/30 Cu–Ni specimens are evaluated under fully reversed stress-life conditions for both as-built and heat-treated states. Fatigue results during the early high-cycle fatigue regime reflect the material's monotonic tensile behavior. Specimens surviving beyond 5×10⁶ cycles are identified as runout data points using arrows on the plot.

caption: Proton NMR spectra of AGE-M samples prepared with varying degrees of substitution, showing enhanced proton peaks corresponding to the melamine-AGE interaction.
summary: The NMR spectra demonstrate the successful synthesis of AGE-M with different substitution levels. As the AGE content increases, specific proton peaks are significantly enhanced, confirming that the primary amino groups on the melamine are effectively replaced by the ring-opened AGE, as evidenced by the spectral intensity changes.

caption: DIC strain map showing localized deformation in the CR43%/A500 °C -1h sample at the end of the initial loading stage.
summary: DIC strain map showing localized deformation in the CR43%/A500 °C -1h sample at the end of the initial loading stage. The local bands are oriented between 42° and 55° relative to the loading axis, corresponding to the planes of maximum resolved shear stress.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from the polarization curves of Ni1Co3@NC catalysts prepared at different temperatures.
summary: The Tafel analysis for Ni1Co3@NC at different temperatures reveals the reaction kinetics of the catalysts. The Ni1Co3@NC-800 sample exhibits the lowest Tafel slope of 57 ± 3 mV/dec, indicating superior HER kinetics compared to the other synthesized temperatures, which is consistent with its overall enhanced electrocatalytic performance.

caption: Orientation image map of Ni-based superalloy 718 fabricated via AP-DED after homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 hours.
summary: Representing the microstructure after a 1100 °C homogenization treatment, this EBSD map illustrates the grain morphology of the AP-DED Ni-based superalloy 718. The results demonstrate that this specific heat treatment condition successfully maintains the typical coarse, oriented microstructure and cube texture observed in the as-built material.

caption: Higher magnification STEM micrograph and associated EDS elemental maps providing a detailed view of the ZrO2 dispersoid morphology in the SLM processed Nb521 sample.
summary: Detailed higher magnification STEM imaging and EDS elemental analysis characterize the morphology of ZrO2 dispersoids in the SLM processed Nb521 sample. The HAADF-STEM mode confirms the presence of these oxide particles, while EDS mapping verifies their composition, distinguishing them from potential Nb-based carbides which were absent in the material.

caption: Hydrogen peroxide production performance comparison between HEC and VEC electrochemical systems.
summary: This panel evaluates the hydrogen peroxide generation capability of two distinct electrochemical cell configurations, HEC and VEC. The data illustrates the comparative efficiency of these systems in producing hydrogen peroxide, providing a baseline analysis for the electrochemical performance of the proposed experimental setups in the study.

caption: Mass loss curves for hazelnut shell, PLA, and their composites, showing the initial pyrolysis temperature of PLA-HSC filaments as a function of hazelnut shell carbonization temperature.
summary: The mass loss curve illustrates the thermal degradation behavior of hazelnut shell, PLA, and their composites. Analysis indicates that the initial pyrolysis temperature of the PLA-HSC filament decreases as the carbonization temperature of the hazelnut shell increases, providing insight into the thermal stability of the composite materials during heating.

caption: Linear plots of anodic peak current versus the square root of scan rate for LNPs-CFC, demonstrating Li-ion diffusion kinetics based on the Randles-Sevcik equation.
summary: Anodic peak current values derived from CV measurements are plotted against the square root of scan rates. According to the Randles-Sevcik equation, this analysis confirms that LNPs-CFC electrodes exhibit a superior Li-ion diffusion coefficient compared to control electrodes, highlighting enhanced electrochemical performance and efficient ion transport properties.

caption: Differentiation potential of SSCs evaluated via Oil Red O, Alcian Blue, and immunofluorescence staining for Nestin expression post-transfection (scale bar = 50 μm).
summary: Microscopic evaluation using Oil Red O, Alcian Blue, and Nestin immunofluorescence staining demonstrates that Timp2 mRNA transfection does not impair the differentiation capacity of SSCs. The cells retain their ability to undergo adipogenic, chondrogenic, and neurogenic differentiation, showing no significant impact on lineage commitment compared to non-transfected control groups.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for SLMed and sintered AlSi10Mg alloys evaluated in a 0.5 M HCl solution.
summary: This panel shows the potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for all fabricated AlSi10Mg alloys tested in a 0.5 M HCl solution. The plot provides essential electrochemical data regarding the corrosion resistance and polarization characteristics of the additive manufactured and sintered materials when exposed to this specific acidic environment.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectra of ZCIS/ZnS quantum dot colloidal dispersions, showing broad absorption bands across different synthesis temperatures.
summary: UV–Vis absorption spectra for ZCIS/ZnS quantum dot colloidal dispersions reveal broad absorption bands that remain consistent across different synthesis temperatures. The data indicates that there are no significant shifts in the absorption features, suggesting that the core-shell structure maintains stable optical properties despite variations in the preparation temperature.

caption: Boundary character maps of Ni samples annealed at 900C, highlighting twin boundaries in red, TRD boundaries in black, and all other grain boundaries in gray.
summary: This panel displays boundary character maps for nickel samples annealed at 900C, distinguishing between different types of grain boundaries. Twin boundaries are marked in red, TRD boundaries are indicated by black lines, and all other grain boundaries are shown in gray, facilitating the analysis of boundary evolution during the annealing process.

caption: Azimuthally integrated SXRD patterns comparing as-built conditions with post-heat treated samples at 723 K for varying durations, evaluated in both undeformed states and after tensile testing.
summary: This panel displays azimuthally integrated SXRD patterns for samples in as-built and heat-treated conditions at 723 K. The data includes both undeformed and tensile-tested specimens, with analysis focused on fracture tips. Interpreting these patterns is difficult due to low intensity, broad peak characteristics, and significant phase overlap.

caption: Semipolar coordinate plots representing BMSC cytoskeleton orientation (0°–180°) versus anisotropic degree (0–1) for different scaffold groups.
summary: Semipolar coordinate plots visualize the cytoskeleton orientation and anisotropy of BMSCs on various matrix scaffolds. The polar angle represents the orientation relative to the horizontal axis, while the radius indicates the degree of anisotropy. Results show that cells on groups H and R exhibit a wider, more disordered distribution.

caption: Property diagram illustrating the relationship between density and yield strength, featuring a dashed isocontour line representing specific strength performance.
summary: This property diagram displays the relationship between density and yield strength to evaluate specific strength. The inclusion of a dashed isocontour line allows for the visualization of performance trends, where movement from the lower right toward the upper left of the plot indicates an increase in specific strength values.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the corroded sample, identifying the presence of M2C carbides.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern provides crystallographic evidence regarding the particles observed in the corroded samples. Combined with element distribution analysis, the diffraction data confirms that these particles are M2C carbides. This identification is critical for characterizing the phase evolution and intergranular corrosion behavior of the material.

caption: One-dimensional long period structure (1D-LPS) method showing D022 and D023 structures derived from L12 by introducing periodic APBs.
summary: The 1D-LPS method is demonstrated by showing how D022 and D023 structures are derived from the L12 parent structure. This is achieved by systematically introducing {100} APBs at specific intervals, specifically every one or two L12 cubes, to model long-period ordered phases in the alloy system.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the final synthesized microcapsule, highlighting distinctive absorption peaks corresponding to both the polyurea formaldehyde shell and the encapsulated core components.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of the synthesized microcapsule displays distinctive peaks that correspond to both the shell and core components. This spectroscopic analysis confirms the successful incorporation of the core material within the polyurea formaldehyde shell, validating the chemical integrity and composition of the final microcapsule product.

caption: Three-dimensional X-ray computed tomography reconstruction of the Invar alloy phase within the composite structure.
summary: This panel displays a 3D X-ray computed tomography reconstruction of the Invar alloy component. The visualization provides a detailed spatial representation of the alloy's morphology within the as-sprayed Cu50 composite, serving as a baseline for comparing the distribution of different phases and structural features throughout the material volume.
