caption: Binary particle map showing regions with element concentrations exceeding the threshold, labeled with values of 1 after noise filtering.
summary: The binary particle map is derived from the intensity map by applying noise filtering and a specific threshold. Regions where the element concentration exceeds the threshold are labeled with a value of 1, effectively isolating the particles from the matrix to facilitate automated detection and further structural analysis of the carbides.

caption: Thickness variation measurements obtained via EELS for the NC60 alloy throughout the oxidation process.
summary: This panel illustrates the thickness changes of the NC60 alloy phase before and after oxidation. Through EELS measurements, the figure captures the specific material response to the oxidation treatment, highlighting the variation in thickness that occurs within the NC60 alloy as it undergoes the oxidation process.

caption: Thermal gradient map within the loading bars at 1600 °C, where the axial axis OA denotes distance from the specimen/bar interface and the radial axis OB indicates the radial direction.
summary: The temperature change within the loading bars at 1600 °C is visualized in this panel. The axial axis OA represents the position relative to the specimen/bar interface, while the radial axis OB shows the distribution along the radial direction, providing insight into the thermal environment of the loading assembly.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from the LSV curves for the three catalyst materials to evaluate their oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity.
summary: Tafel slope analysis is performed for the three catalyst materials to further demonstrate their oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. By calculating these slopes from the LSV data, the electrochemical kinetics and the efficiency of the catalytic process for each material can be quantitatively compared and evaluated.

caption: Overview of the modified FFF x350 pro printer setup used for additive manufacturing experiments.
summary: This photograph displays the modified FFF x350 pro printer, which serves as the primary experimental apparatus for the study. The image provides a clear visual representation of the hardware configuration utilized during the additive manufacturing process, highlighting the specific modifications made to the standard printer model for research purposes.

caption: Simulation model of a ∑5 (210) tilt-symmetric grain boundary in a BCC metal, showing defect atoms following a 3.0 keV primary knock-on atom collision.
summary: This MD snapshot illustrates a BCC metal simulation model featuring a ∑5 (210) tilt-symmetric grain boundary. A primary knock-on atom is initiated 30 Å from the boundary with 3.0 keV of kinetic energy. Only defect atoms are visualized to highlight the structural response to the collision event.

caption: Micro-CT reconstruction images of the bone defect site at 4, 8, and 12 weeks post-implantation, visualizing the progression of bone tissue regeneration.
summary: Micro-CT scanning and reconstruction were performed on tissue samples harvested at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after implantation. These images provide a longitudinal view of the bone defect site, allowing for the visualization and assessment of new bone tissue growth and scaffold integration over the 12-week period.

caption: Nano-hardness variation with applied load for TaN/CrN/ZrN coatings deposited at a substrate temperature of 350 °C.
summary: Nano-hardness values for the TaN/CrN/ZrN coating system deposited at 350 °C are plotted against the applied load. This graph characterizes the mechanical hardness behavior of the functionally graded material, allowing for an assessment of how the increased substrate temperature influences the coating's resistance to indentation compared to the 250 °C sample.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the HIP+STA specimen revealing a bimodal distribution of γ' precipitates with sizes of approximately 50 and 300 nm.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph, taken with the <100> superlattice reflection, highlights the γ' phase in the HIP+STA specimen. The image reveals a distinct bimodal distribution where particles of approximately 50 nm and 300 nm coexist, likely resulting from the slow cooling rate during the HIP process and subsequent heat treatment.

caption: Pareto front analysis comparing density versus creep resistance for training samples and designed candidates, with red dashed lines indicating baseline performance thresholds of 8.3 g/cm³ and 150 hours.
summary: This plot presents the Pareto front for density and creep resistance, evaluating both training samples and newly designed alloys. By marking baselines at 8.3 g/cm³ and 150 hours, the figure demonstrates the performance trade-offs and identifies candidate alloys that meet or exceed these specific design criteria for high-temperature applications.

caption: Thermomagnetization M(T) curves for the normal Ni-Mn-Ga sample in as-built and annealed states, recorded under ZFC and FC conditions at 50 Oe.
summary: Thermomagnetization M(T) curves for the normal Ni-Mn-Ga sample are shown for both as-built and annealed conditions under a 50 Oe field. The as-built sample exhibits a wide transformation range of approximately 27 K with two distinct humps, while heat treatment results in flatter curves and a significantly narrower transition temperature range.

caption: Electronic band structure of the pristine Bi2Te3 sample.
summary: The electronic band structure of the pristine Bi2Te3 sample is shown here. A comparison with the Al-containing system reveals that the presence of Al slightly narrows the bandgap from 0.1 eV to 0.04 eV, while maintaining the overall electronic characteristics of the reference system near the Fermi level.

caption: Emission spectra of TPU/SAOED composites with varying SAOED concentrations measured under 365 nm excitation.
summary: This plot displays the emission spectra of TPU/SAOED composite prints under 365 nm excitation. The curves illustrate how varying the amount of SAOED additive influences the photoluminescence characteristics of the TPU matrix, providing a clear comparison of the optical emission behavior across different composite formulations within the study.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) profile for as-printed Invar single material cylinders.
summary: Invar specimens in the as-printed state exhibit the specific CTE values plotted against temperature in this panel. These measured thermal expansion characteristics are utilized as critical input parameters for thermo-mechanical FEM simulations, ensuring that the computational models accurately reflect the physical properties of the printed components during thermal analysis.

caption: Clip maintaining the vessel phantom under a sustained internal pressure of 150 mm Hg.
summary: The clip successfully holds the vessel phantom under an internal pressure of 150 mm Hg. This photograph demonstrates the device's ability to maintain hermeticity, confirmed by the absence of liquid droplets on the phantom tip, indicating effective sealing performance at human body temperature.

caption: Final time-resolved snapshot depicting the completion of the observed dislocation movement sequence at the grain boundary.
summary: Panel d displays the final time-resolved snapshot of the three consecutive dislocation movements at the intersection of active slip traces and the grain boundary. This sequence confirms the dynamic nature of dislocation interactions in unirradiated wrought 316L stainless steel during straining at 288°C, completing the observed deformation event.

caption: Nyquist plots for the 2D-NP Sn-Ni electrode, showing impedance characteristics before cycling and after 50 cycles, including a magnified inset of the high-frequency range.
summary: This panel presents the Nyquist plot for the 2D-NP Sn-Ni electrode, comparing impedance before and after 50 cycles. The data, characterized by a high-frequency semicircle and low-frequency tail, reveals changes in charge transfer resistance and Li+ diffusion kinetics at the electrode/electrolyte interface, with the inset detailing high-frequency impedance features.

caption: Diagram detailing the extraction orientation of vertical tensile specimens relative to the build direction (BD) of the SEBM-fabricated bulk material.
summary: This schematic illustrates the sampling location and orientation for extracting vertical tensile specimens from the SEBM-fabricated bulk material. The extraction is defined relative to the build direction, ensuring that the mechanical testing captures the properties of the material along the principal axis of the fabricated bulk sample.

caption: Tan delta curves plotted against temperature for neat PBAT and WPL-DH composites, illustrating the glass transition behavior.
summary: Tan delta curves for PBAT-based composites containing WPL-DH biofillers are shown as a function of temperature. DMA analysis reveals that the glass transition temperature values for these composites exhibit insignificant variation compared to the neat PBAT matrix, indicating that the filler incorporation does not significantly alter the polymer transition.

caption: Atomic force microscopy phase image of the pristine ABS-4 sample surface.
summary: Atomic force microscopy phase image of the pristine ABS-4 sample surface. This visualization provides significant insights into the internal morphology of the pristine ABS series. The phase imaging technique is utilized here to characterize the surface structure of the ABS-4 specimen, contributing to the comparative analysis of the ABS series.

caption: Three-dimensional spatial distribution of sample points generated using the MaxiMin-LHS method.
summary: This panel illustrates the three-dimensional spatial distribution of sample points produced by the MaxiMin-LHS method. Comparison with the standard LHS method demonstrates that this improved sampling approach significantly enhances the filling characteristics of sample spaces within the parameter space, leading to a more uniform distribution of the generated samples.

caption: Schematic representation of element doping within a NiAl supercell, highlighting interstitial sites including two octahedral sites (2Al-4Ni and 4Al-2Ni) and one tetrahedral site (2Al-2Ni) surrounding Ni-substituted elements.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic configuration of element doping in a NiAl supercell. It specifically identifies three distinct interstitial sites around Ni-substituted elements, comprising two octahedral sites (2Al-4Ni and 4Al-2Ni) and one tetrahedral site (2Al-2Ni), providing a structural basis for understanding dopant incorporation in the NiAl lattice.

caption: Predicted pole figure generated by the model for the configuration θ = 45°, α = 22.5°, and β = 45°.
summary: Generated via the rotation matrix in Equation (4), this predicted pole figure corresponds to the configuration θ = 45°, α = 22.5°, and β = 45°. The close alignment between this simulation and the experimental results highlights the model's ability to accurately predict crystallographic textures under the specified rotation parameters.

caption: Tensile stress–strain curves comparing as-built AlSi10Mg and AlSi10Mg–Nb samples.
summary: Tensile stress–strain curves for as-built AlSi10Mg and AlSi10Mg–Nb alloys are presented, derived from three repeated tests per material. These curves illustrate the mechanical response of the samples, highlighting the influence of Nb addition on the tensile behavior of the LPBF-processed aluminum matrix compared to the base alloy.

caption: Confocal microscopy image displaying platelet accumulation within the bottom surface of large grid microstructures, marked by an orange square.
summary: Confocal microscopy imaging demonstrates that platelets, stained for P-selectin and CD41+, preferentially deposit at the base of large grid-patterned surfaces. The orange square highlights the bottom region of the grids where the platelets have accumulated, consistent with the observed behavior of platelets on large-sized microstructures.

caption: Confocal 3D reconstruction of the photolithographic micropore array showing the spatial arrangement of the hydrogel features.
summary: The hydrogel microstructure was reconstructed into a 3D image using confocal microscopy. This visualization provides a detailed spatial representation of the photolithographic micropore array, confirming the successful formation of the periodic structures within the hydrogel matrix.

caption: RMS radii distribution of nanoentities derived from angular light-scattering signals using Debye formalism, showing size ranges for the different solution treatments.
summary: Derived RMS radii distributions for the sodium carbonate solutions are presented, calculated via Debye formalism applied to angular light-scattering data. The analysis reveals that all tested solutions exhibit nanoentities with radii consistently distributed between 40 and 120 nm, confirming the similarity in the nature of the scatterers across conditions.

caption: Co chemical potential evolution at the interface as a function of increasing Cr content.
summary: Calculated Co chemical potential trends show a distinct response to increasing Cr content, contrasting with the behavior observed under Al enrichment. This thermodynamic analysis clarifies how specific elemental additions modify the interface, supporting the broader investigation into phase transitions and the ACI effect within the Amdry365/IN792 system.

caption: Energy filtered elemental map of Samarium (Sm) distribution within the Al83.5Ni8.0Sm6.5Pb2.0 alloy microstructure.
summary: The energy filtered elemental map for Samarium illustrates its spatial distribution across the Al83.5Ni8.0Sm6.5Pb2.0 alloy microstructure. This map, generated using plasmon energy edges, provides critical information regarding the elemental segregation and phase composition of the melt-spun ribbon alongside the other elemental maps.

caption: Correlation between the coercive force (Hc) and the square root of engineering strain (ε eng) for 9Ni steel, showing a linear increase as strain progresses from 2% to 14%.
summary: This plot demonstrates the relationship between coercive force and the square root of engineering strain in 9Ni steel. As strain increases from 2% to 14% at 50 Hz and 1.0 T, the coercive force rises linearly, reflecting how plastic deformation significantly alters the magnetic properties of the alloy.

caption: Grain boundaries map of 24CrNiMo steel after SLM-SR treatment.
summary: This grain boundary map illustrates the structural state of 24CrNiMo steel following SLM and subsequent SR treatment. By visualizing the boundaries, this panel supports the comparative analysis of grain consistency and refinement, forming a critical part of the EBSD phase diagram evaluation for the SLM-SR processed specimens.

caption: In-situ synchrotron X-radiography experimental result at approximately 6 min, showing dendrite morphology and solute plumes.
summary: This in-situ synchrotron X-radiography image, captured at approximately 6 min, provides experimental validation for the simulation. A red circle labels the dendrite tip used for growth velocity measurements, while white arrows indicate solute plumes. This experimental data allows for a direct comparison of dendrite morphology and convection patterns with simulation results.

caption: Electronic density of states projected onto Fe, O, and Mg atoms at the Fe/MgO interface.
summary: Represented here is the projected density of states for Fe, O, and Mg atoms at the Fe/MgO interface. These plots characterize the electronic environment of the pre-nucleation model, highlighting how the Fe atoms interact with the MgO surface atoms through their respective electronic states at the interface.

caption: Bode phase angle plots comparing the frequency-dependent impedance behavior of 1-h and 4-h sintered samples, highlighting the stable passive film formation in the 4-h sample.
summary: The Bode phase angle plot reveals that the sample sintered for 4 h exhibits a phase angle approaching -90° across low to medium frequencies. This behavior indicates the successful formation of a stable passive film on the material surface, demonstrating the influence of sintering duration on the electrochemical stability of the samples.

caption: Battery temperature profile over four cycles without BCP, showing a peak temperature of 48 °C at the end of discharge followed by cooling during CC-CV charging.
summary: This plot displays the battery temperature variation during four discharge-charge cycles at a 2.9C discharge rate without any BCP. The temperature reaches 48 °C at the end of the discharge process and gradually decreases to ambient conditions during the subsequent CC-CV charging phase, serving as a baseline for comparison.

caption: Vickers microhardness measurements for as-built samples, highlighting the mechanical strength consistency across specimens with identical TiB/TiC ratios.
summary: Vickers microhardness values are plotted for as-built samples that share the same TiB/TiC ratio. This data, referenced in Fig. 10 and Table 3, quantifies the hardness of the material, demonstrating the mechanical consistency achieved in the as-built state for the specified composition of TiB and TiC reinforcements.

caption: Enlarged view of the calculated liquidus and solidus boundaries, featuring a characteristic lens-shaped two-phase region with superimposed experimental data points compiled from the MTOX database version 7.0.
summary: This figure displays an enlarged section of the calculated liquidus and solidus boundaries, which exhibit a characteristic lens shape and a narrow two-phase region. Experimental data points are superimposed onto the calculated phase diagram, utilizing thermodynamic parameters sourced from the MTOX database, version 7.0, to validate the theoretical boundaries.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves of the ASC device measured at various current densities to determine performance under different load conditions.
summary: This panel depicts the galvanostatic charge-discharge curves of the ASC device at different current densities. These measurements are essential for evaluating the device's ability to handle varying power demands, reflecting the charge-discharge behavior and overall electrochemical stability of the printed supercapacitor under diverse operational current loads.

caption: SEM image of the Y-Z vertical-section of the HX-2TiC sample, demonstrating a refined microstructure following the addition of nano-TiC particles.
summary: Addition of nano-TiC to the HX alloy effectively suppresses the formation of the light-colored interdendritic second-phase zones and cellular structures found in the base material. This SEM image of the HX-2TiC sample confirms the structural refinement achieved through the introduction of the nano-TiC particles into the alloy matrix.

caption: 3D elemental map showing the distribution of clusters and precipitates in a Cu-free Mg/Si alloy specimen in the T6 condition, visualized using an 8% MgSi-isosurface.
summary: This 3D elemental map illustrates the cluster and precipitate structure within a Cu-free Mg/Si alloy specimen subjected to T6 heat treatment. The visualization utilizes an 8% MgSi-isosurface to highlight the spatial distribution of these features, providing a clear representation of the microstructure in the absence of copper.

caption: EPMA X-ray line scans illustrating elemental distribution across the IDR and DCR regions.
summary: EPMA X-ray line scans illustrating elemental distribution across the IDR and DCR regions. These scans were performed using an electron probe equipped with WDS to determine the segregation coefficient of elements. The analysis provides quantitative data on compositional variations between the IDR and DCR regions of zone 2.

caption: Relative importance of input parameters influencing material removal rate (MRR).
summary: This feature importance plot displays the relative influence of different input parameters on the material removal rate (MRR). By quantifying the proportional relevance of these variables, the visualization clarifies which factors are the primary drivers of the material removal process during the experimental investigation.

caption: Overall microhardness profile across the welded joint, illustrating the transition from the GT35 base metal to the weld center.
summary: The overall microhardness profile of the welded joint is presented, demonstrating the successful formation of a TiC gradient transition layer. This profile captures the significant hardness variation across the joint, ranging from approximately 1199.3 HV 0.3 in the GT35 base metal down to about 205.4 HV 0.3 at the weld center.

caption: Heating curves showing temperature rise over time for FeCaP powders synthesized at 40 °C and 90 °C with varying total Fe content (4.8 wt% and 9.8 wt%), all calcined at 1000 °C, compared against a water control.
summary: Magnetic hyperthermia curves demonstrate the influence of synthesis temperature and iron content on the heating efficiency of FeCaP powders calcined at 1000 °C. The data, plotted against a water control, reveal distinct temperature profiles based on the specific synthesis parameters, providing insight into the magnetically induced heating capabilities of these materials.

caption: Dark-field (DF) transmission electron microscopy image generated using the incommensurate 1/4 diffraction spot circled in (a), showing randomly distributed bright nanosized domains within the austenite matrix.
summary: This dark-field TEM image, obtained by selecting the incommensurate 1/4 diffraction spot from the SAED pattern, visualizes the microstructure of the austenite. The image reveals bright, nanosized domains randomly distributed throughout the matrix, a morphology characteristic of strain glass alloys, confirming the presence of local strain order.

caption: Ternary composition map of the Ti–Al–Ni alloy system at 2033 K, displaying the spatial distribution of free volume fraction via color mapping and discrete data points represented by open diamonds.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the free volume fraction distribution across the Ti–Al–Ni alloy system at a constant temperature of 2033 K. The visualization utilizes a color-coded map to represent variations in free volume, with open diamonds marking specific experimental data points analyzed within the ternary composition space.

caption: Partial binary phase diagram of the Al-Mg system highlighting the healing temperature conditions.
summary: The Al-Mg binary phase diagram serves as a proof-of-concept for the healing approach. It demonstrates that the eutectic temperature of 450 °C is significantly lower than the melting point of the α-Al phase at 660 °C, allowing for selective melting of the healing agent during heat treatment.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the triple melted (TM) Ti–40Nb sample, showing an evolved microstructure with elongated and coarse needle-shaped phases.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image of the triple melted (TM) Ti–40Nb sample demonstrates a distinct morphological change compared to the SM condition. The microstructure is characterized by elongated and coarse needle-shaped phases. This observation is consistent with SEM data, confirming the impact of the triple melting process on the phase morphology.

caption: Bivariate kernel density estimate correlating mean local curvature with mean normal velocity for grain boundaries, filtered to remove triple junction proximity effects.
summary: This bivariate kernel density estimate presents the correlation between mean local curvature and mean normal velocity for grain boundaries. The analysis utilizes surface representations excluding points within a distance of four from triple junctions, offering insight into the relationship between boundary geometry and kinetic behavior.

caption: Tafel curves for Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings compared to the 2Cr13 substrate.
summary: Tafel curves are presented for Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings alongside the 2Cr13 substrate. These electrochemical measurements characterize the corrosion behavior and polarization characteristics of the different coating compositions relative to the base substrate material, providing insight into the protective performance of the passive films formed on the surfaces.

caption: Experimental procedure for injecting high-viscosity silicone oils into 3D-printed samples with 20%, 30%, and 40% infill densities prior to retesting.
summary: Following initial stress relaxation tests, samples with varying infill densities of 20%, 30%, and 40% were injected with silicone oils of three different viscosities: 1 kPa s, 5 kPa s, and 10 kPa s. This step prepares the specimens for retesting to evaluate the influence of internal fluid viscosity on mechanical response.

caption: Comparative performance metrics including average flow rate and MSE deviations for five geometries, contrasting iterative learning against simple transfer learning.
summary: Performance metrics for five distinct geometries demonstrate the efficacy of the iterative learning algorithm. Results show that this approach outperforms simple transfer learning in terms of MSE convergence speed and data efficiency, often achieving target print precision in as few as three iterations, as evidenced by the flow rate and MSE data.

caption: Calculated solidification curve for the Al–5Mg–2Si-0.7Mn-1.2Fe alloy derived from the Scheil model, indicating the primary phase formation of α-Al15(Fe,Mn)3Si2 and a solidification range of approximately 50 °C.
summary: The Scheil model calculation reveals the solidification sequence of the Al–5Mg–2Si-0.7Mn-1.2Fe alloy. The primary phase to solidify is α-Al15(Fe,Mn)3Si2, which establishes a solidification range of about 50 °C. This model predicts the sequential formation of various Fe-IMCs and eutectic phases throughout the cooling process.

caption: Magnetization field dependence of the magnetization intensity for the CNCV sample measured at various temperatures.
summary: This plot shows the magnetization field dependence of the magnetization intensity for the CNCV sample measured at different temperatures. The measured coercivity field (Hc) of the CoCrNiV alloy is reported here, illustrating the magnetic response of the material as a function of the applied magnetic field and thermal conditions.

caption: Beeswarm plot of SHAP values for ST regression descriptors, showing the distribution and impact of individual feature values.
summary: The beeswarm plot visualizes the distribution of SHAP values for each feature in the ST regression model. It reveals how specific feature values influence the prediction, notably demonstrating that higher Tm values correlate with larger SHAP values, which directly corresponds to an increase in the predicted ST value.

caption: Arrhenius plot of logarithmic shear rate versus inverse absolute temperature, showing data for continuous and stress change experiments at early and later creep stages.
summary: The Arrhenius plot displays the relationship between the logarithmic shear rate and the inverse absolute temperature. By comparing continuous and stress change experiments at both early and later creep stages, this panel provides insight into the thermal activation energy associated with the creep mechanisms of the MCSS material.

caption: HPLC chromatogram of SLM-SnO2-NP formulation exhibiting a prominent peak at the identical retention time as the standard.
summary: The chromatogram of the SLM-SnO2 NP formulation displays a prominent peak at the same retention time as the standard SLM. This observation confirms that the encapsulation process within the nanoparticles did not alter the chemical identity of the analyte, maintaining its structural integrity during the formulation procedure.

caption: Dilatometry curve for a cooling rate of 200 °C/s, highlighting the transformation profile and the six critical temperature points identified through slope changes.
summary: This panel illustrates the dilatometry curve for a 200 °C/s cooling rate, with critical transformation temperatures 1–6 clearly marked. The curve captures the material's response during cooling, providing specific data points that are essential for mapping the transformation behavior and validating the CCT diagram construction.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of P0-HIPed pure Cu, revealing a random orientation distribution and numerous annealing twins.
summary: Following HIP at 600 °C and 2000 bar, the P0-HIPed specimen exhibits a microstructure formed by solid-state sintering. The EBSD inverse pole figure map shows a largely random orientation distribution and the presence of numerous annealing twins, confirming significant microstructural evolution compared to the as-built state.

caption: Representative load-displacement curves comparing the mechanical response of auxetic joints against equivalent stiffness joints.
summary: This panel displays representative load-displacement curves for both auxetic and equivalent stiffness joints. The plot illustrates the mechanical behavior of these structures under loading conditions, providing a direct comparison of their deformation characteristics and structural response to applied forces, which is essential for evaluating their performance in engineering applications.

caption: Composition-dependent tracer diffusion coefficients for Ni-Fe alloys at 500 K, comparing k-ART results (blue tip-up triangles) against kMC simulations using variable (blue tip-down triangles) and constant (magenta squares) activation energy barriers.
summary: This plot illustrates the composition dependence of tracer diffusion coefficients in Ni-Fe alloys at 500 K. It compares k-ART results with kMC simulations using both variable and constant activation energy barriers. The constant energy barriers, derived from NEB calculations for an equiatomic alloy, demonstrate a monotonic trend consistent with previous kMC studies.

caption: Stress nephogram of a horizontally printed sample during the 50th loading cycle under IP conditions, showing localized stress reduction.
summary: Representing the 50th loading cycle under IP conditions, this stress nephogram reveals localized decreases in stress within specific grains. This observation indicates that certain regions of the horizontally printed sample have entered the softening stage prematurely, reflecting the progressive mechanical degradation occurring during cyclic fatigue testing.

caption: Uniform sheet-based double gyroidal (DGu) lattice structure tessellated in a 5 × 5 × 5 array at 20% relative density.
summary: The double gyroidal (DGu) lattice is shown as a 5 × 5 × 5 tessellated structure at a relative density of 20%. This specific topology is characterized by a surface-area density that is 1.88 times higher than that of the uniform gyroid (Gu) topology, highlighting the effect of compaction on the lattice geometry.

caption: High-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph highlighting nano-sized NiSe2 grain clusters in the Bi1.8Ni0.2Se3 sample.
summary: High-magnification bright-field TEM imaging demonstrates that NiSe2 is present as nano-clustered grains within the Bi2Se3 matrix. This observation confirms that the in situ precipitation process successfully creates a hierarchical interface architecture, characterized by these distinct nano-sized grain clusters rather than isolated bulk particles within the Bi1.8Ni0.2Se3 sample.

caption: Boxplot summarizing the average drag measurements across all sides of the drag squares, demonstrating the influence of artifact dimensions.
summary: This boxplot quantifies the average drag values measured across all sides of the drag square samples. The data indicates a clear trend where drag increases with greater artifact width and decreases as the thickness of the sample increases, confirming the relationship between geometric dimensions and the observed drag effect.

caption: Confusion matrix showing the classification outcomes for the fourth model across the tested pH levels.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed view of the classification results for the fourth model across different pH level classes. It facilitates the analysis of model performance by visualizing the frequency of correct and incorrect classifications, helping to identify potential biases or weaknesses in the model's predictive capabilities.

caption: Three-dimensional response surface representation of energy consumption plotted against printing speed and nozzle temperature.
summary: Energy consumption is modeled in this three-dimensional response surface plot as a function of printing speed and nozzle temperature. The visualization highlights a pronounced linear trend with marked growth corresponding to increases in printing speed, whereas the impact of printing temperature on energy consumption remains relatively limited throughout.

caption: Parity plot comparing actual versus predicted values of the coefficient of friction, demonstrating the accuracy and fit of the developed response surface methodology (RSM) model.
summary: The parity plot compares actual versus predicted values of the coefficient of friction to validate the RSM model. Data points closely follow the regression line, confirming a high degree of correlation and a good fit. This plot serves as a critical indicator of the model's reliability and predictive accuracy.

caption: Semi-logarithmic dependence of the HER rate, calculated as the inverse of total resistance from EIS data, plotted against the applied overpotential for the Co-based coatings.
summary: This plot displays the semi-logarithmic dependence of the hydrogen evolution reaction rate, derived from total resistance values obtained via EIS, versus the applied overpotential. Comparison with the potentiodynamic scan results confirms that this method yields a similar trend to the Tafel plot, validating the consistency between the two electrochemical measurement techniques.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the eutectic area within the yellow square frame from Fig. 6a.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the eutectic area marked by the yellow square frame in Fig. 6a. The imaging technique highlights the structural features of the eutectic region, providing a clear view of the interface and the surrounding material morphology for further compositional and crystallographic characterization.

caption: Trend analysis of non-dimensional effective strength (σt/σhard) plotted against tip angle θ, highlighting the impact of material property variations.
summary: Trend analysis displays the non-dimensional effective strength (σt/σhard) as a function of the tip angle θ. The results show how varying material properties affect the strength of the suture interface. Consistent with theoretical predictions, the strength exhibits a nonlinear increase as the tip angle decreases, enhancing the interface performance.

caption: Al 11 at.% iso-surface visualization highlighting the presence of nanometric ternary γ′ precipitates dispersed within the γ-channels of the ODS alloy.
summary: The Al 11 at.% iso-surface visualization demonstrates the presence of nanometric tertiary γ′ precipitates within the γ-channels of the ODS alloy. These tertiary precipitates are less than 5 nm in diameter and are observed to be more prominent in wider channels, located further away from the secondary γ′ precipitates.

caption: Scatter plot showing the relationship between crack initiation energy and tensile strain for samples processed with different oxygen contents.
summary: The plot displays the correspondence between crack initiation energy and tensile strain for equiaxed samples containing varying amounts of oxygen. By mapping these two mechanical parameters, the figure highlights how oxygen content influences the initiation phase of fracture within the material's equiaxed microstructure during tensile deformation.

caption: General view of the assembled hourglass specimen mounted within the fatigue testing rig.
summary: The machined Haynes 282 specimen is shown clamped securely within the fatigue testing apparatus. This setup allows for the application of cyclic mechanical loads to the hourglass-shaped sample, enabling the observation of fatigue life and the subsequent analysis of fracture surfaces and microstructural evolution post-testing.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) coloring map of the HT770 heat-treated sample, illustrating the grain structure and orientation on the transverse section.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) coloring map represents the HT770 heat-treated sample, illustrating the grain structure and orientation on the transverse section. Together with the pole figures, it provides detailed texture information, confirming that the peak intensity of the HT770 sample shows little difference compared to the AB sample.

caption: Nanoindentation creep response curve for sample B-T, reflecting the creep characteristics of the thermally treated sample.
summary: Sample B-T presents its nanoindentation creep response in this plot, documenting the time-dependent deformation of the thermally treated submicrometric-scale sample. The curve provides insight into the material's creep behavior, demonstrating the impact of thermal processing on the mechanical response and stability of the sample under constant load.

caption: Illustration of the 90° rotation serpentine scanning strategy employed during the SEBM fabrication process to enhance build uniformity and minimize residual stress.
summary: This schematic illustrates the serpentine scanning strategy used during SEBM fabrication. By rotating the scan direction by 90° between successive layers, the process aims to minimize residual stress and enhance build uniformity throughout the material, providing a controlled approach to the additive manufacturing of the bulk samples.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PGA prepared by SCP from glycolide monomers at 205 °C for 1 day, showing a distinct profile compared to the 190 °C sample.
summary: This MALDI-TOF mass spectrum corresponds to PGA synthesized at 205 °C for 1 day. The spectral profile is notably different from the sample prepared at 190 °C, indicating that the polymerization temperature significantly influences the resulting molecular weight distribution and the presence of cyclic species in the final PGA product.

caption: Comparison of Tensile and Compression Young’s modulus for Flexa Black TPU material, represented by black squares and blue triangles respectively.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of Flexa Black TPU, comparing tensile and compression Young’s modulus values. Compression modulus significantly increases from 12.98 MPa to 18.57 MPa after ethanol treatment and 19.18 MPa following Suma Tab D4 solution exposure, demonstrating statistically significant changes in material stiffness under different chemical conditions.

caption: Liquidus projection of the Ni-B-Ti ternary system showing the positions of alloys A, B, C, D, and E, along with ternary eutectic point 1 and solidus line 2–3.
summary: The liquidus projection of the Ni-B-Ti ternary system illustrates the compositional landscape for alloys A through E. It highlights critical features including ternary eutectic point 1, where solidification terminates for specific compositions, and solidus line 2–3, which defines the boundary conditions for the formation of Ni3Ti and TiB2 phases.

caption: Training and validation evaluation metrics for the OT modality, highlighting performance across different VED conditions.
summary: This panel displays the training and validation performance for the OT modality. Evaluation metrics, including balanced accuracy and MCC, reveal modality-dependent confidence gaps. The model demonstrates difficulty in classifying the Δ +30% VED condition due to confusion with the Standard VED, while the Δ -30% VED condition is classified with high ease.

caption: Enlarged schematic of the Ni-Sn peritectic region showing the β liquidus extension (red dashed line) and α liquidus (blue line), with vertical dotted lines indicating constrained equilibrium at annealing temperature T exp.
summary: This schematic illustrates the peritectic region of the Ni-Sn phase diagram, highlighting the β and α liquidus lines. It defines the constrained equilibrium at the annealing temperature T exp, where the melt compositions at the β melting front and α growth front, denoted as x β / L eq and x α / L eq , are determined.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing silmer (S) with various monomer formulations (S:A, S:G, and S:A:G) to identify chemical bonding changes.
summary: FTIR analysis confirms the presence of siloxane chains in silmer through characteristic peaks at 1260, 1010, and 800 cm-1. The inclusion of acrylamide is verified by the emergence of a peak at 1680 cm-1, corresponding to the C=O stretching of the amide group within the silmer/AA/GMA polymer network.

caption: Test confusion matrix for the ResPFSN-type1 model, showing the distribution of true and predicted class labels.
summary: ResPFSN-type1 model classification results are presented in this confusion matrix, which plots true labels on the y-axis and predicted labels on the x-axis. The data indicates that this model exhibits varied accuracy values across the different classes, reflecting its specific predictive capabilities and limitations in the classification task.

caption: Normalized stress–strain curves for Schwarz P lattices under Z and T orientations, highlighting distinct deformation behavior compared to G lattices.
summary: Schwarz P lattices exhibit unique stress–strain characteristics under Z and T orientations as shown in these curves. The data demonstrates that Schwarz P lattices display different mechanical behavior compared to Schwarz G lattices, providing insight into how specific lattice architectures dictate the material's response to compressive loading in different orientations.

caption: Phase angle versus frequency plot for UNS S30400, UNS S31600, and QN1803 steels, highlighting the capacitive characteristics.
summary: This Bode plot presents the phase angle response for UNS S30400, UNS S31600, and QN1803 steels. The curves demonstrate phase angles approaching -80° within the mid-frequency range, providing evidence of highly capacitive behavior and confirming the integrity of the passive films formed on these steel surfaces during electrochemical testing.

caption: Al–Fe binary phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium relationships between aluminum and iron, including the solid solubility range of Fe in Al and the formation of various intermetallic compounds.
summary: The Al–Fe binary phase diagram displays the equilibrium states of the system, highlighting a solid solubility range for Fe in Al of 0.01–0.022% between 225 and 600 °C. It further identifies two distinct groups of intermetallic compounds: Fe-rich phases like Fe3Al and FeAl, and Al-rich phases including Fe2Al5, FeAl2, and FeAl3.

caption: Post-HIP microstructural state showing modified γ′ precipitate morphology.
summary: Post-HIP microstructural state is shown, confirming the alteration of γ′ morphology due to the HIP process. This processing step is critical for controlling the final precipitate shape, ensuring that the alloy achieves the desired microstructural characteristics for improved performance by refining the distribution and geometry of the γ′ phase.

caption: Projected density of states (DOS) for the lone pair of an NH3 molecule adsorbed onto a CoPt surface.
summary: This plot illustrates the electronic structure of an NH3 molecule adsorbed on a CoPt surface by displaying the projected density of states associated with the lone pair. The data highlights the electronic interaction between the molecule and the metallic substrate, providing insight into the bonding characteristics of the adsorption system.

caption: High-magnification STEM bright field image of the melt-spun Al 83.5 Ni 8.0 Sm 6.5 Pb 2.0 alloy, providing detailed structural information at the nanoscale.
summary: This high-magnification STEM bright field image offers a detailed examination of the Al 83.5 Ni 8.0 Sm 6.5 Pb 2.0 alloy ribbon. By utilizing STEM mode, the image provides enhanced structural clarity of the melt-spun material, allowing for a more precise observation of the nanocrystalline features within the amorphous matrix.

caption: Comparison of data distributions for Ni 63.7 V 36.3 atomic configurations between DFT-based Monte Carlo simulations and inverse neural network (i-NN) model reconstructions.
summary: This panel displays the data distribution of approximately 1500 atomic configurations for the Ni 63.7 V 36.3 alloy. It compares ground truth configurations obtained via DFT-based Monte Carlo simulations against those reconstructed by the inverse neural network model, illustrating the effectiveness of the i-NN approach in capturing the alloy's structural characteristics.

caption: Bright-field TEM image displaying positions 3, 4, and 5 within the material matrix.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the microstructural features at positions 3, 4, and 5. These specific locations were selected for further point scanning and EDS analysis to elucidate the elemental distribution within the matrix, providing a foundational view for subsequent high-resolution structural and compositional investigations of the dendritic regions.

caption: Al 1060 aluminum alloy powder used as the feedstock material for the RSAM process.
summary: Al 1060 powder serves as the primary feedstock for the RSAM process. caption: Root mean square height (Sq) parameter values obtained from the VIP plot.
summary: This bar chart displays the Sq parameter, representing the root mean square height of the peg samples. Classified as a height parameter in purple, the values are derived from 12 specimens. This metric serves as a key indicator of surface roughness, reflecting the overall height distribution of the analyzed surfaces.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the LT70 shell-printed sample revealing macro voids and localized silicon accumulation.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the cross-section of an LT70 shell-printed sample after debinding and LSI. The structure exhibits macro voids devoid of residual powder particles, alongside localized accumulations of silicon. These features indicate incomplete infiltration and the presence of residual voids and silicon lakes within the core.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing as-built and 700 °C heat-treated SS316L samples, highlighting identical peaks at 43.6°, 50.8°, 74.7°, and 90.7°.
summary: The XRD patterns for as-built and 700 °C heat-treated SS316L samples are presented, revealing consistent diffraction peaks at 43.6°, 50.8°, 74.7°, and 90.7°. These results confirm that both processing conditions maintain a single-phase iron structure belonging to the Fm-3m (225) space group, indicating no phase transformation occurred during heat treatment.

caption: Rounded molten pool morphology observed at 150 W laser power and 300 mm/s scanning speed.
summary: At a laser power of 150 W and a scanning speed of 300 mm/s, the SLM molten pool exhibits a rounded shape. This morphology is attributed to the upper portion of the molten pool reaching a higher temperature during the selective laser melting process, characterizing the thermal behavior under these specific parameters.

caption: xx strain distribution map captured during the final 1000 cycles of the fatigue test.
summary: This panel illustrates the xx strain distribution within the inclusion agglomerate region during the final 1000 cycles of the fatigue test. By comparing this to earlier cycles, the map reveals the evolution of strain patterns and the progression of mechanical degradation within the material as it approaches failure.

caption: Venn diagram-style overlap analysis identifying stiffness-responsive m6A writers, erasers, and readers (WERs) targeting YAP1 by intersecting TCGA-PAAD gene correlation data with RM2Target predictions.
summary: Stiffness-responsive WERs targeting YAP1 are identified through an intersectional approach. By overlapping genes positively correlated with LOX and YAP1 in TCGA-PAAD datasets with RM2Target predictions, this analysis isolates key regulatory candidates that potentially mediate the mechanical response of YAP1 mRNA in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

caption: FTIR spectra acquired during the four-hour synthesis reaction of PUF microcapsules, tracking the chemical evolution of the polymerization process.
summary: FTIR spectra obtained during the four-hour synthesis reaction track the chemical changes occurring within the PUF microcapsules. These spectra provide insight into the polymerization kinetics and the formation of the shell structure, confirming the chemical progression from the initial reactants to the final encapsulated product over the reaction duration.

caption: Fatigue life performance under multiaxial loading conditions with a stress amplitude ratio of 0.99, featuring regression curves to assess the influence of out-of-phase shifts.
summary: Displaying the fatigue life response at a stress amplitude ratio of 0.99, this plot compares regression curves to determine the influence of out-of-phase shifts. Consistent with the 0.49 ratio, the phase shift between axial and torsional components is found to be insignificant regarding the overall fatigue life performance.

caption: Bode magnitude curves representing the frequency-dependent impedance modulus for WAAM and its FSP-modified composite variants.
summary: Bode magnitude plots provide a frequency-dependent view of the electrochemical impedance for the WAAM and FSP-modified samples. These curves corroborate the corrosion behavior observed in the Nyquist plots and polarization tests, confirming the relative performance differences between the base WAAM material and the various SiC and ZrO2 reinforced composites.

caption: Inlens SEM macrograph of the transition layer interface processed with 100°C induction heating, showing improved interface continuity.
summary: Displayed is the transition layer interface under 100°C induction heating. The substrate provides thermal buffering during the solidification of the molten pool, which suppresses crack initiation. This thermal management results in a more continuous transition layer interface compared to the condition without auxiliary heating, as observed via Inlens SEM imaging.

caption: Processing efficiency and instability contour map for the Ni48Cu10Co2Ti38Ta2 alloy at a true strain of 0.3, showing defined instability zones within dark solid black lines.
summary: Representing the processing efficiency at a true strain of 0.3, this contour plot identifies specific instability zones for the Ni48Cu10Co2Ti38Ta2 alloy. The regions enclosed by dark solid black lines delineate areas where the material exhibits unstable behavior, which is essential for determining safe processing windows during the alloy's deformation.

caption: Raman spectrum corresponding to the CoO coating surface after the 800 °C wear test, confirming the formation of Co3O4.
summary: This Raman spectrum demonstrates the chemical shift associated with the oxidation of the cobalt oxide coating at 800 °C. The data confirms the formation of Co3O4 on the unworn surface, consistent with the observed changes in the oxidation state of the coating after high-temperature testing.

caption: Exchange bias as a function of temperature for the top and bottom FM-layers in NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with HNiPy.
summary: Temperature-dependent exchange bias measurements are presented for the top and bottom ferromagnetic layers in NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with HNiPy. The data highlights the influence of AFM-layer thickness on the magnetic response, where thicker layers induce a more convex temperature dependence in the exchange bias curves observed during the experiment.

caption: Visible and UV (inset) sonoluminescence (SL) emission spectra of 3 M NaCl aqueous solutions at 21.2 kHz and 13 °C, comparing Ar and Kr atmospheres under varying stirring velocities.
summary: This panel displays sonoluminescence emission spectra for 3 M NaCl solutions under Ar and Kr gases. The spectra reveal a broad continuum rising toward the blue, the Na* line at 589 nm, exciplex emissions (Na·Ar and Na·Kr), and a small OH* peak at 310 nm, demonstrating gas-dependent emission characteristics.

caption: Surface texture profile of the downskin region on a horizontal thin wall specimen.
summary: This panel displays the surface topography of a horizontal thin wall's downskin surface. The profile reveals characteristic process defects, specifically spatter particles and partially melted powder particles, which are typical of the manufacturing process used for these specimens. The surface texture is characterized by these attached metallic particles.

caption: Ion mobility spectrometry spectra for binary mixtures of 2-pentanone/2-octanone and 2-butanone/2-hexanone at 30 °C, illustrating the distinct peaks corresponding to monomer and dimer species.
summary: This spectrum displays the analytical performance of an IMS device during the simultaneous injection of ketone mixtures at 30 °C. The data reveals distinct peaks for monomers and dimers, noting that the dimer of the smaller ketone and the monomer of the larger ketone overlap to varying degrees in both mixtures.

caption: Dark-field STEM image of the 21Cr32Ni model alloy irradiated to 17 dpa at 376 °C, emphasizing the distribution of precipitates and cavities.
summary: This dark-field STEM image provides a detailed view of the 21Cr32Ni model alloy microstructure after 17 dpa neutron irradiation at 376 °C. The imaging technique effectively highlights the distribution of irradiation-induced cavities and precipitates, confirming the formation of these features within the alloy as a result of the BOR-60 reactor exposure.

caption: Carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen K-edge EEL spectra for PLA, PCL, ABS, and ASA, collected at a low electron dose of 5 e/Å² to minimize beam-induced degradation.
summary: Panel b presents the carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen K-edge EEL spectra for PLA, PCL, ABS, and ASA. Collected at a low electron dose of 5 e/Å², these spectra reveal characteristic peaks at 283 eV and 290 eV, reflecting electronic transitions associated with specific chemical bonds within the polymer structures.

caption: Loss factor (tan(δ)) as a function of frequency at 25 °C, demonstrating the dominance of elastic behavior over viscous response.
summary: Frequency-dependent loss factor (tan(δ)) measurements at 25 °C reveal a consistent decrease as frequency increases. This trend indicates that the elastic response of the materials becomes increasingly dominant over the viscous component, reflecting the viscoelastic nature of the samples during the dynamic mechanical analysis.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of the AM sample tested at 1600°C, highlighting further dislocation recovery.
summary: Captured at 1600°C, this KAM map for the AM sample reveals the continued impact of thermal recovery on the microstructure. The reduction in KAM values reflects the ongoing annihilation of dislocations at higher temperatures, although the map confirms that subgrain structures persist even under these extreme thermal conditions.

caption: XPS survey spectrum of the interior surface of a conventionally manufactured copper tube following fuel fouling testing.
summary: This panel displays the XPS survey spectrum for a conventionally manufactured copper tube specimen. The data was collected to analyze the interior surface composition after the sample underwent fuel fouling testing. This broad survey provides a baseline for comparing surface chemical states against various stainless-steel tube specimens tested under identical conditions.

caption: Voltage and current profiles over time for a DIW-T50/W142 cathode cell during a charge/discharge cycle at a 7C rate.
summary: Operating at a higher 7C current density, the cell exhibits increased resistance voltage consumption and incomplete charging capacity. The profile highlights the necessity for extended constant voltage (CV) charging durations to compensate for the kinetic limitations encountered at this elevated rate, contrasting with the performance observed at lower current densities.

caption: Atom map of the 3Al5Ni alloy illustrating the spatial arrangement of elements at the precipitate interface.
summary: The atom map of the 3Al5Ni alloy provides a detailed view of the elemental distribution at the interface between the matrix and the precipitates. This 3D representation allows for the identification of structural features and chemical gradients present within the alloy's microstructure.

caption: High-magnification STEM view of an individual oxide particle within the dispersed oxide layer of the recast layer.
summary: This high-magnification view captures an individual oxide particle located in the upper part of the recast layer. caption: XPS spectrum of Cr in the H 282 1400 component, exhibiting a characteristic peak at 574.7 eV indicative of metallic Cr⁰.
summary: The XPS analysis of chromium in the H 282 1400 component reveals a characteristic peak at 574.7 eV. caption: Histogram illustrating the γ′ precipitate area fraction in AM and cast samples, evaluated both after heat treatment and following fracture.
summary: This histogram presents the γ′ precipitate volume fraction, which is determined by the area fraction in SEM images. Following stress rupture testing, the mean γ′ volume fraction decreases as a new equilibrium is established at high temperatures.

caption: Coulombic efficiency and cyclic stability plot for TPU/WS2/CB composite supercapacitor devices, evaluating long-term operational performance.
summary: Cyclic stability of the supercapacitor devices is illustrated, serving as a key parameter for assessing long-term performance. This plot tracks the Coulombic efficiency of the TPU/WS2/CB composite devices over repeated cycles, providing critical data on the durability and reliability of the energy storage system under operational conditions.

caption: Reference depth map of a powder bed surface exhibiting no observable defects.
summary: This panel displays the reference depth map of a powder bed surface, characterized by the absence of any obvious defects. As the baseline measurement, this image serves as the standard against which other powder bed states are compared to identify surface irregularities during the powder spreading process.

caption: Dilatometry curve for specimen D1 tested in a nitrogen atmosphere at 1.1 bar and a flow rate of 4 L/h.
summary: Specimen D1 was subjected to dilatometry testing under a controlled nitrogen atmosphere maintained at 1.1 bar with a flow rate of 4 L/h. This curve represents the thermal expansion behavior of the material under these specific environmental conditions, providing essential data for understanding its dimensional stability during thermal processing.

caption: Pareto plot displaying the statistical significance of standardized input variables and their interactions on the linear loss (Δh) output.
summary: This Pareto plot displays the statistical significance of input variables and their interactions regarding linear loss (Δh). summary: Diffusion paths for the 3L|3R diffusion couple are mapped onto a phase diagram to illustrate the compositional evolution. caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 20% hemp content mix, exhibiting a bell-shaped curve with a shift toward negative values.
summary: For the 20% hemp content mix, the Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis results in a bell-shaped probability distribution. This distribution shows a more pronounced shift toward negative values for both the mean and median compared to lower hemp content mixtures, reflecting the impact of increased hemp content on global warming potential.

caption: Compensated all-pixel-on input image using a radial function and the corresponding improved resulting light profile.
summary: This panel shows the effect of applying a radial compensation function to the all-pixel-on input image. caption: In-situ photograph capturing the spiral geometry during the volumetric additive manufacturing (VAM) printing process.
summary: This in-situ photograph illustrates the spiral structure as it is being formed during the volumetric additive manufacturing process. caption: Atomic structure model representing the crystalline arrangement within area Q.

caption: Initial state of the auxetic lattice specimen prior to the application of mechanical testing loads.
summary: This photograph displays the auxetic lattice specimen in its undeformed, initial state before the commencement of mechanical testing. caption: Friction coefficient profiles for heterogeneous NiTi wall samples across lower, middle, and upper regions, highlighting stability in the upper section.
summary: Friction coefficients for heterogeneous NiTi wall samples are compared across three deposition regions. caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the SLM-processed Al-50wt%Si alloy, showing a single endothermic peak during the heating process.
summary: The DSC curve of the SLM Al-50wt%Si alloy displays a single endothermic peak, which corresponds to the phase transition from the eutectic Si and Al matrix to the liquid phase. caption: GDMS depth-profiling analysis of Ag:TiN/Al samples using the M-0 configuration at a discharge pressure of 6.50 mPa.
summary: The GDMS depth-profiling analysis for the M-0 configuration at 6.50 mPa is shown here. caption: Bar chart illustrating the relative importance of various molten pool features as determined by a random forest algorithm.
summary: This bar chart displays the feature importance scores for molten pool characteristics, calculated using a random forest algorithm. caption: Corrected Raman spectra of SWCNT water dispersion across four distinct polarization configurations.
summary: This panel presents the Raman spectra of the SWCNT water dispersion after applying necessary corrections to the four polarization configurations. caption: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model confusion matrix evaluated on the unseen test set.
summary: Long Short-Term Memory model classification outcomes are presented in this confusion matrix for the unseen test set. caption: Distribution of SHAP values illustrating the impact of individual input features on the predicted porosity.
summary: The distribution of SHAP values for porosity prediction is shown to illustrate the range and direction of feature impacts. caption: Statistical distribution of true stress values derived from mechanical testing.
summary: This panel presents a statistical analysis of true stress values obtained from mechanical testing. caption: Comparison of cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves for BAC and CHBAC devices measured at a scan rate of 5 mVs-1.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis of the electrochemical performance of BAC and CHBAC devices using cyclic voltammetry. caption: Inverse pole figure map of the R1 sample demonstrating the transformation of the microstructure into a mixture of coarse and fine equiaxed grains.

caption: Ashby map comparing ultimate tensile strength (UTS) versus toughness (a ku) for the current AT steels against reported ultra-high strength steels (UHSS).

summary: This schematic details the strengthening behavior in the Cr-containing Al–Mn–Cr–Zr alloy. It maps the relationship between precipitate size and strength contribution over time, demonstrating how the combined effects of Al–Mn and Al3Zr precipitates determine the total peak strength. This model serves as a guide for optimizing novel alloys produced via PBF-LB.

caption: Non-linear fitting of the experimental Tafel plot for the HNWF1 sample using the Butler-Volmer equation to evaluate fitting accuracy.
summary: Experimental and fitted Tafel plots for the HNWF1 sample are compared to assess the accuracy of the non-linear fitting process. By applying the Butler-Volmer equation, the analysis validates the electrochemical model used to characterize the corrosion kinetics of the specific HNWF1 hybrid nanocomposite sample under investigation.

caption: Temperature-dependent self-diffusion coefficients for Ti, Nb, Mo, Ta, and W elements, calculated using the Arrhenius equation.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature-dependent self-diffusion coefficients for Ti, Nb, Mo, Ta, and W. Calculated using the intrinsic diffusion constant and activation energy, these values explain the observed Ti-rich phase concentration at grain boundaries and interdendritic regions, highlighting how varying diffusion rates influence microstructural evolution in these materials.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the heat-treated sample, highlighting the distribution of γ′ precipitates and a dislocation within the γ matrix.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the heat-treated sample reveals the spatial distribution of γ′ precipitates and a dislocation within the γ matrix. This visualization provides a 3D perspective of the microstructural features formed after the full heat treatment process, serving as the basis for subsequent compositional analysis of the dislocation.

caption: Radar plot visualizing the multi-dimensional intensity features (μ I, σ I, σ 3 I) relative to each specific process regime.
summary: This radar plot visualizes the multi-dimensional intensity features, including mean, standard deviation, and skewness, relative to each specific process regime. It allows for a comparative overview of how these features characterize different regimes. A large overlap was observed in these features between the stable and stubbing process regimes.

caption: Measured third-harmonic generation (THG) emission spectrum obtained from the Si metasurface under femtosecond laser excitation at 1510 nm, showing a peak at approximately 507 nm.
summary: The nonlinear optical response of the Si metasurface is characterized by measuring the THG emission spectrum. Under 1510 nm femtosecond laser illumination, a distinct emission peak is observed at approximately 507 nm, demonstrating the efficient frequency conversion capabilities of the fabricated Si nanodisk metasurface structure.

caption: Three-dimensional distribution and cross-sectional views of internal defects within the as-built sample.
summary: This panel presents the three-dimensional distribution and cross-sectional views of internal defects in the as-built sample. The CT analysis results reveal that the spatial arrangement of these internal defects is relatively random throughout the printed material, providing a comprehensive visualization of the sample's internal structural integrity and defect morphology.

caption: Rate capability performance of the cell utilizing printed CPE films, evaluated across varying charging rates of 0.4, 1, 1.5, and 2 C.
summary: This panel illustrates the rate capability of a cell constructed with printed CPE films. By testing the device at charging rates ranging from 0.4 C to 2 C, the specific discharge capacities are determined, providing essential data on the electrochemical performance and stability of the printed electrolyte material under different load conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of TAN04HA and TAN06HA coatings deposited on rod, gyroid, and dodethick architectures following in vitro testing.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for TAN04HA and TAN06HA coatings applied to rod, gyroid, and dodethick structural geometries. These patterns were acquired after the samples underwent in vitro testing to evaluate the phase composition and structural stability of the coatings under simulated physiological conditions.

caption: Vertical cross-sectional slice extracted from the 3D microstructure along the plane indicated by black lines, revealing the internal columnar grain structure.
summary: A vertical cross-sectional cut through the 3D microstructure reveals the internal grain morphology. The simulation demonstrates a columnar grain structure, which typically forms during solidification in the direction perpendicular to the melt pool interface, confirming the expected growth patterns within the finalized material volume.

caption: Yield strength distribution across all tested samples represented as a violin plot.
summary: Yield strength distribution across all tested samples is represented as a violin plot. This visualization effectively illustrates the spread, central tendency, and potential outliers within the dataset for this specific mechanical response variable, providing a comprehensive overview of the yield strength performance across the entire experimental sample set.

caption: Berkovich hardness profiles for Samples C, T, and K plotted against the reverse building direction, highlighting a distinct hardness jump between 50 μm and 550 μm depths.
summary: Berkovich hardness profiles for Samples C, T, and K reveal a consistent hardness jump between 50 μm and 550 μm depths. Hardness values at the 50 μm depth are notably lower than in deeper regions. This jump indicates that precipitation zone strengthening dominates over cellular structure and austenite fraction effects in LPBF maraging steel.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted creep strain from the DNN model against actual experimental test data.
summary: This parity plot visualizes the correlation between the DNN-predicted creep strain and the actual experimental test values. The close alignment of the data points along the diagonal indicates high predictive reliability and accuracy of the trained DNN model when applied to the test dataset for the LPBF IN738LC superalloy.

caption: XPS spectrum of Coating A wear scar highlighting Al 2p and Y 3d binding energies.
summary: Analysis of the wear scar on Coating A via XPS reveals Al 2p and Y 3d binding energies at 73.8, 158.5, and 157.2 eV. These spectral features correspond to the formation of Al2O3 and Y2O3, which are critical for understanding the wear mechanisms and surface composition of the coating.

caption: Algorithmic flowchart detailing the incremental step calculation procedure for the VUMAT user material subroutine.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the systematic incremental step calculation procedure implemented within the VUMAT user material subroutine. Developed using the Fortran language, this subroutine facilitates the numerical solution of the MJC model, providing a structured computational framework for simulating material behavior through precise, iterative updates during the analysis process.

caption: Geometric representation of the Dode-medium unit cell showing the repeating structural element.
summary: Representing the fundamental repeating unit of the lattice, this Dode-medium unit cell is defined by a 2 mm size. The design incorporates specific geometric parameters, including an open-cell porosity of 80%, an open-pore size of 1.13 mm, and a strut thickness of 0.26 mm, ensuring consistent structural properties throughout the lattice.

caption: Absorbed energy over time for the structural designs, demonstrating the impact energy dissipation performance.
summary: The energy absorbed by the structure over time during the impact is shown in this plot. The Baseline design, characterized by its rigidity and minimal deformation, demonstrates poor energy absorption capabilities. This panel effectively quantifies the efficiency of each design in dissipating energy throughout the duration of the impact.

caption: Tabulated lattice parameters and cohesion energies for 15 distinct bulk configurations, showing mean values of 3.54 ± 0.01 Å and -7.78 ± 0.01 eV, respectively.
summary: This table presents the calculated lattice parameters and cohesion energies for 15 inequivalent bulk configurations. The data reveals highly consistent values across configurations, with mean results of 3.54 ± 0.01 Å for the lattice parameter and -7.78 ± 0.01 eV for the cohesion energy, confirming the stability of the bulk properties.

caption: Top-down view of a 50-layer GO/PLA filter with 40% infill ratio, illustrating the flow area geometry.
summary: Top-down optical imaging of a 50-layer GO/PLA filter reveals the structural arrangement of the material. The area available for water flow is shown to increase with the rotation angle of the filter layers. This visual data provides insight into how layer orientation influences the internal flow pathways.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots illustrating the capacitance response of passive films synthesized at diverse DC bias potentials within a 1.00 mol/L HNO3 solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots for passive films formed in 1.00 mol/L HNO3 are shown to evaluate the capacitance behavior at different DC bias potentials. By characterizing the structure of these passive films, the plots allow for a deeper understanding of the electrochemical properties and film stability in high-concentration nitric acid media.

caption: Synchrotron XRD pattern of un-melted Alloy 738LC, serving as the reference material for the 100% nickel dilution condition.
summary: The XRD pattern for un-melted Alloy 738LC provides the baseline diffraction data for the base material. This panel acts as a control for the fully melted samples, allowing for the comparison of peak intensities and phase identification across the full range of experimental nickel dilution values achieved in the study.

caption: IPF map and grain size distribution for the 5 wt% Al3Zr as-built sample, revealing a fully refined microstructure consisting entirely of fine equiaxed grains.
summary: The 5 wt% Al3Zr as-built sample exhibits a fully refined microstructure composed entirely of fine equiaxed grains. This result, supported by EBSD analysis, demonstrates that a 5 wt% addition of D023-Al3Zr is sufficient to achieve complete grain refinement, eliminating the columnar grain structure observed in lower concentration samples.

caption: TDA-spectrum of CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 200 bar with a heating rate of 0.250 K/s, illustrating the four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit.
summary: Representing the TDA-spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA samples charged at 200 bar, this panel utilizes a heating rate of 0.250 K/s. The analysis employs a four-peak deconvolution model to fit the experimental data, providing a cumulative fit function that highlights the specific hydrogen release characteristics at this lower heating rate.

caption: Architecture of the deep learning framework for predicting nodal thermal histories in STEAM, illustrating the integration of geometry-based descriptors, simulation LOG data, and node-heat-source interaction features into a sequence model.
summary: This schematic illustrates the deep learning framework used in STEAM to predict nodal thermal histories. It details the extraction of geometry and simulation-based descriptors, the processing of node-heat-source interactions, and the sequence model architecture. The final stage demonstrates the 3D mapping unit used to reconstruct the thermal history of the part.

caption: Pseudo-2D GradShim spin-density profile revealing the spatially-encoded rf field along the transceiver coil axis, with contours indicating optimal pulse regions.
summary: The pseudo-2D GradShim experiment reveals the spatially-encoded rf field along the transceiver coil axis. Contours highlight the optimal pulse region, which disappears where the B1 field drops. On the right side, the optimal pulse region is visible as an additional set of contours, as indicated by the red arrow.

caption: Young's modulus depth profile derived from nanoindentation measurements, showing a trend across the sample cross-section from the top surface to the bottom.
summary: Young's modulus values are plotted as a function of depth, mirroring the pattern observed in the hardness profile. These nanoindentation measurements provide a comprehensive view of the elastic modulus variation across the sample cross-section, extending from the top surface to the bottom of the build direction.

caption: Heating curves for Ni53Fe21Ga26 ribbons subjected to three sequential thermal arrests at 25 °C, 23 °C, and 21 °C, followed by a final heating curve h4 that demonstrates the material's thermal memory capability.
summary: Panel b presents DSC heating curves for Ni53Fe21Ga26 ribbons, highlighting the material's ability to record multiple temperatures. By performing thermal arrests in decreasing order at 25 °C, 23 °C, and 21 °C, the final heating curve h4 successfully recovers the thermal memory of these specific arrest points at 10 K/min.

caption: Representative mechanical response curves obtained during cutting and compression tests, demonstrating the quantification of textural properties derived from the material's structural behavior.
summary: Mechanical response curves are presented to illustrate the quantification of textural properties extracted from cutting and compression tests. These plots serve as the basis for evaluating the material's mechanical behavior, where textural parameters are derived directly from the recorded load-displacement responses during the experimental testing of the printed samples.

caption: Microhardness distribution profile across the welded joint for condition D1, highlighting the M-shaped hardness variation observed across the different microstructural regions.
summary: Microhardness distribution profile across the welded joint for condition D1, highlighting the M-shaped hardness variation observed across the different microstructural regions. All joints exhibit this typical M-shaped microhardness distribution, characterized by the lowest values in the weld zone, highest in the heat-affected zone, and intermediate values in the base metal.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectra of O-16 and ITX in acetonitrile, highlighting the low photon absorption of O-16 at 395 nm compared to the ITX sensitizer.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectra reveal the optical properties of O-16 and ITX in acetonitrile. O-16 shows low photon absorption at 395 nm (200 L mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹) compared to the ITX sensitizer (3030 L mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹), explaining the necessity of ITX for effective sensitization during the photopolymerization process.

caption: Surface profile of a polished TMCA sample over a 1 x 1 mm2 area.
summary: This panel displays the surface profile of a polished TMCA sample captured via optical roughness measurement over a 1 x 1 mm2 area. The image serves as a baseline for evaluating surface topography before any oxidation treatment, providing a characteristic view of the material's initial polished state.

caption: Bright Field TEM image of the AB-V-5650s-1 sample highlighting dislocation interactions.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging captures the interaction between dislocations and nanoscale θ'/θ-Al2Cu phases within the AB sample after impact compression at 5650 s-1. This visualization demonstrates how the microstructure responds to high-rate deformation, specifically focusing on the pinning or movement of dislocations near secondary phase precipitates.

caption: Time-averaged irreversible heat generation rates for NMC622 and lithium metal electrodes plotted against current density for 3D printed and 2D tape-casted calorimetric cells.
summary: This plot illustrates the time-averaged irreversible heat generation rates for both NMC622 and lithium metal electrodes as a function of current.
