The data compares calorimetric cells fabricated using 3D printing versus traditional 2D tape-casting methods, providing insight into the thermal behavior of these electrodes under constant current cycling conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of raw and treated tungsten carbide powder, highlighting phase decomposition.
summary: The X-ray diffraction pattern indicates partial decomposition of tungsten carbide during the melting process, which occurs between 1600 °C and 2200 °C. This transformation results in the formation of tungsten phases and unsaturated carbide phases, specifically WC0.5 and WC0.82, as evidenced by the diffraction peaks.

caption: Operational settings consisting of 1300 W laser power, 8 mm/s scanning speed, and 9 g/min powder feed rate.
summary: The fourth experimental condition is defined by a laser power of 1300 W, a scanning speed of 8 mm/s, and a powder feed rate of 9 g/min. These parameters were selected to refine the deposition process and provide comparative data for the study of single-track clad morphology.

caption: Zoomed-in region of the (2 0 0) diffraction peak for A1 HT2 and A2 HT2 samples, showing the shift in peak position due to composition-dependent lattice changes.
summary: The (2 0 0) diffraction peak is presented in this zoomed-in inset to compare A1 and A2 samples. The observed shift in peak position is attributed to the different compositions and corresponding unit cell parameters of the alloys. This detail confirms the structural sensitivity of the diffraction pattern to material composition.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern corresponding to the bright Ni3Ta intermetallic phase identified at the interface.
summary: The SAED pattern provides crystallographic evidence for the presence of the Ni3Ta intermetallic compound at the interface. Combined with EDS analysis, this diffraction data confirms that the bright phase observed in the STEM imaging corresponds to the Ni3Ta intermetallic phase formed during the thermal exposure process.

caption: Uniaxial compressive stress–strain curves obtained from simulations for snap-fit foam prototypes of a third relative density, analyzed along three characteristic directions.
summary: Simulated stress–strain curves for snap-fit foam prototypes are presented here, focusing on a third relative density variant. The data, generated under periodic boundary conditions, highlights the mechanical deformation characteristics along three characteristic directions, contributing to the comprehensive evaluation of the foam's structural integrity and compressive response across different density configurations.

caption: Viable cell count of S. aureus on various peg surfaces after 4 hours of incubation in LB media, highlighting the impact of surface class on initial attachment.
summary: This box plot depicts S. aureus adhesion after 4 hours, showing significant differences between class I and class II surfaces. The findings indicate that abrasive media processing times do not significantly reduce cell counts for class II pegs. These results underscore the influence of surface characteristics on early bacterial attachment phases.

caption: Transmission synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern of the pristine consolidated Ni-Cr-Al-Ti alloy plate prior to laser scanning, showing the characteristic γ/γ’ structure of the matrix.
summary: The transmission synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern of the pristine consolidated Ni-Cr-Al-Ti alloy plate is shown prior to laser scanning. This analysis confirms the presence of a γ/γ’ structure within the alloy matrix, which results from the slow cooling process following the spark plasma sintering (SPS) consolidation of the material.

caption: Raman spectrum indicating the potential presence of breyite and Ca2SiO4-larnite in sample B20–1, noting signal attenuation due to inclusion depth.
summary: This panel displays Raman data suggesting the presence of breyite and larnite in sample B20–1. The spectral quality is limited by the significant depth of the inclusions within the diamond bulk, which results in lower signal intensity compared to surface-proximal inclusions, complicating the definitive identification of the mineral phases.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectra of DA-CDs under varying excitation wavelengths from 260 to 290 nm, displaying a singular peak at 316 nm.
summary: Fluorescence spectroscopy analysis demonstrates that DA-CDs exhibit excitation wavelength-independent emission behavior. When excited at varying wavelengths between 260 and 290 nm, the material consistently displays a singular emission peak centered at 316 nm, confirming stable optical properties across the tested excitation range.

caption: Comparative analysis of Biosynth® commercial Lactonic Sophorolipid standard using UV (red line) and LC/MS (black line) detection methods, showing the first major peak corresponding to acidic diacetylated C18:1 sophorolipid and late-eluting peaks around 40 minutes representing residual fatty acids.
summary: This figure compares UV and LC/MS spectra of a commercial Lactonic Sophorolipid standard. While UV detection shows limited sensitivity, LC/MS reveals a wider range of sophorolipid species. The primary peak represents acidic diacetylated C18:1 sophorolipid, while late peaks at 40 minutes indicate the presence of residual fatty acids in the commercial product.

caption: Mo 3d APXPS spectra of Ni-18Cr-3Mo-20Fe-5Nb alloy recorded in 0.1 M NaCl at varying applied potentials.
summary: Mo 3d APXPS spectra for the Ni-18Cr-3Mo-20Fe-5Nb alloy are shown across different applied potentials in 0.1 M NaCl. The data tracks the evolution of molybdenum surface states, confirming the presence of metallic and hydroxide peaks, with the latter becoming more pronounced following polarization at 1400 mV.

caption: Neural Network (NN) model ROC curve performance on the unseen test set.
summary: Neural Network model performance is shown through an ROC curve on the unseen test set. Comprising five curves, including four for individual classes and one for the micro-average, this plot highlights the classification effectiveness of the NN model when applied to the unseen test set for predictive analysis.

caption: Particle size distribution in volume percent for WA powder analyzed using the straw method.
summary: WA powder particle size distribution is illustrated using the straw method for micro-CT scanning. By utilizing volume percent for the analysis, the curve slope is improved, effectively limiting the influence of noise. This scan method provides a consistent approach for evaluating the powder characteristics across different resolutions.

caption: Transmittance spectra of GAn@HPC-2 h sheets plotted against varying sample thicknesses, demonstrating enhanced transparency as thickness decreases.
summary: This plot illustrates the transmittance of GAn@HPC-2 h sheets as a function of their thickness. The data confirms that the transparency of the films is significantly enhanced as the thickness of the material is reduced, validating the optical performance of the crosslinked films.

caption: Parity plot evaluating the agreement between actual and predicted viscosity values for graphene-based nanofluids using a Grid Search-optimized GB model.
summary: This parity plot highlights the model's effectiveness in predicting viscosity for graphene-based nanofluid systems. A significant degree of agreement is observed between the expected and actual values, confirming that the Gradient Boosting model is well-suited for this application due to the minimal error in its predictions.

caption: Representative fluorescent images of ocular surface frozen sections from DED mice treated with Rho B or Rho B cL for 2 or 25 minutes, showing differential tissue uptake.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of mouse corneal tissue sections demonstrate the distribution of Rho B and Rho B cL after topical administration. The images compare uptake at 2 and 25 minutes, revealing the spatial localization of the fluorescent markers within the ocular surface tissues of DED mice.

caption: Logarithmic plot illustrating the progression of crack length as a function of the applied number of cycles for shot-peened DN specimens.
summary: This panel displays the crack length evolution versus the number of cycles for shot-peened DN specimens. The data is presented on a logarithmic scale, providing a clear visualization of how the crack length increases throughout the fatigue testing process for these specific material conditions.

caption: Thermal expansion and expansion rate curves for SDP-15FeNi samples pre-sintered under a N2/10%H2 reducing atmosphere.
summary: Dilatometry results for SDP-15FeNi samples pre-sintered under a reducing N2/10%H2 atmosphere are displayed, illustrating the thermal expansion (Δl/l) and thermal expansion rate (Δl/Δt) versus temperature. This plot highlights the influence of the reducing atmosphere on the thermal behavior and dimensional changes of the pre-sintered compacts.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing the distribution of all ions in Ni-60Fe alloy following Ni ion irradiation at a fluence of 5 × 10^15 cm^-2.
summary: This APT reconstruction displays the spatial distribution of all ions within the Ni-60Fe alloy after exposure to Ni ion irradiation at a fluence of 5 × 10^15 cm^-2. The visualization confirms that the material maintains a homogeneous solid solution phase, with no evidence of segregation or phase separation occurring during irradiation.

caption: Comparison of creep strain evolution between γ-alloy crystals of varying orientations (solid lines) and a [001] CMSX-4 specimen (dashed line) under identical test conditions of 1288 °C and 10 MPa.
summary: Comparing creep behavior, this panel contrasts γ-alloy specimens of multiple orientations with a [001] CMSX-4 specimen. The data reveals that CMSX-4 exhibits remarkable softening during creep, a phenomenon that is barely distinguishable in the γ-alloy specimens. The results are presented using normalized time to facilitate a direct comparison of creep strain.

caption: Evolution of peak current values over 100 cyclic voltammetry cycles for the PEDOT:PSS/TPU/paracetamol:PLGA microparticle composite film.
summary: The change in peak current over 100 CV cycles indicates the electrochemical stability of the composite. The material maintains approximately 80% of its initial conductivity after 100 cycles, a performance level comparable to previous studies involving charged molecule loading, confirming the suitability of the composite for sustained electrochemical applications.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of HDPE HX17 powder measured via laser diffraction.
summary: Particle size analysis of HDPE HX17 powder was performed using a Beckman Coulter LS 13 320 XR dry powder system. The resulting histogram illustrates the distribution of particle sizes, revealing an average powder particle size of 69.62 μm, which characterizes the physical dimensions of the material for further processing.

caption: Confocal microscopy images showing BMSC cytoskeleton morphology (blue) adhered to the scaffold walls at one, three, and five days of culture.
summary: BMSCs exhibited a well-stretched morphology and a good proliferation state on the scaffold walls. These confocal microscopy images highlight the cytoskeleton in blue, confirming that the cells successfully adhered to the scaffold structure and maintained a healthy morphology throughout the five-day observation period.

caption: Stress rupture life and elongation data for alloys subjected to 1100 °C and 160 MPa across four distinct heat-treatment conditions.
summary: This panel displays the stress rupture life and elongation properties of various heat-treated specimens tested at 1100 °C and 160 MPa. The data provides a comparative assessment of how different heat-treatment states influence the mechanical performance and durability of the alloys under these specific high-temperature creep conditions.

caption: 2PEM image of HDFs in the test group after 18 h of culture in an unstrained collagen gel, showing a mix of round cells and those with protrusions.
summary: This 2PEM image displays the test group HDFs after 18 hours of culture in an unstrained collagen gel. Similar to the control group, the majority of cells remain round, though some have developed protrusions, demonstrating that cellular morphology evolves slightly over time despite the lack of external strain.

caption: Ternary formulation map illustrating the optimum region for printability, projected onto the distribution of key mechanical properties.
summary: This ternary formulation map identifies the optimal composition range for filament printability, specifically located within the backbone-rich region. By projecting this optimum zone onto mechanical property distribution maps, the figure correlates material formulation with performance, providing a clear guide for optimizing printability based on the characterization and testing of various filament compositions.

caption: Schematic representation of the CNN-based architecture designed for real-time indexing of crystallographic orientations from EBSD patterns.
summary: This schematic illustrates a CNN model developed for the real-time indexing of crystallographic orientations from EBSD patterns. By employing region transformation and transfer learning techniques, the model effectively restructures crystal orientation data. This approach represents a cutting-edge advancement in automating the analysis of electron backscatter diffraction data for materials characterization.

caption: Creep-rupture data for MARBN, P92, and P122 steels tested at 650°C, comparing base metal and welded joint performance.
summary: This plot displays creep-rupture data for MARBN, P92, and P122 steels at 650°C. The data includes both base metal and welded joint specimens, providing a comparative analysis of their long-term mechanical stability. MARBN, containing 120-150 ppm of B and 60-90 ppm of N, is evaluated alongside established P92 and P122 alloys.

caption: Galvanostatic polarization potential-time curve for the as-built specimen without applied tensile strain.
summary: This panel displays the galvanostatic polarization potential-time curve for the as-built specimen under zero strain. The potential-time curves for both L-PBF and conventional materials exhibit a similar trend in this unstrained condition, providing a baseline for evaluating the performance of the materials under controlled current conditions.

caption: Effective shear strain map of the bulk region at an applied global effective shear strain (ε LD) of 0.50%.
summary: This map illustrates the effective shear strain distribution in the bulk region at an early deformation stage of 0.50% ε LD. It captures the initial stages of strain localization, providing insight into the material's response before significant slip patterning is established across the bulk microstructure.

caption: DSC/TG analysis of the 316L-AR78 filament after partial debinding in coke grit (C).
summary: This panel presents the DSC/TG thermal analysis for the 316L-AR78 filament subjected to partial debinding within a coke grit medium. The results indicate that the specific debinding procedure preserves the material's thermal characteristics, as confirmed by the comparative analysis of the thermal profiles presented in the study's findings.

caption: Von Mises stress distribution within the upper joining partner subjected to a pointed grove sonotrode tip.
summary: This panel presents the simulated von Mises stress distribution in the upper joining partner interacting with a pointed grove sonotrode tip. The stress distribution is shown along a central section in the direction of deflection, demonstrating the mechanical stress concentration patterns resulting from the pointed grove contact interface.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curve of the permalloy honeycomb lattice under a forward-biased current (I+) at an applied field of 0.01 T, showing the total magnetization response.
summary: Magnetic measurements of the permalloy honeycomb lattice under a forward-biased current (I+) reveal the temperature-dependent magnetization behavior at an applied field of 0.01 T. This panel demonstrates the total magnetization response of the lattice, which exhibits a larger magnitude compared to the reverse-biased state shown in the subsequent panel.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of LPBFed CoCrNi, indicating an average grain size of 25.5 ± 0.3 µm.
summary: The IPF map of the LPBFed CoCrNi sample illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution of the grains. Quantitative analysis of this map determines an average grain size of 25.5 ± 0.3 µm, providing a baseline for comparing the grain refinement effects observed in the subsequent MMC samples within the study.

caption: Load-displacement curves comparing the fresh alloy against the α-Cu phase at 20 μm and 100 μm from the alloy edge following 24 hours of CE in synthetic seawater.
summary: This panel displays load-displacement curves for fresh alloy samples and the α-Cu phase at specific distances from the alloy edge after 24 hours of CE. The data reveals that samples subjected to CE exhibit significantly reduced indentation depths under maximum load, indicating increased hardness compared to the fresh alloy samples.

caption: Low-magnification dark-field TEM image revealing the particulate distribution of precipitate phases within the dendrites.
summary: A low-magnification dark-field TEM image reveals that precipitate phases are distributed within the dendrites in a particulate form. This visualization provides insight into the sub-micron scale distribution of phases, confirming the presence of precipitates within the dendritic regions of the printed K417G superalloy sample.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of as-deposited and heat-treated GH3536 alloy specimens in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel displays the potentiodynamic polarization curves for GH3536 alloy samples subjected to different heat-treatment conditions. The electrochemical corrosion performance was evaluated at room temperature in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, providing a comprehensive overview of the corrosion resistance characteristics for both as-deposited and heat-treated alloy variants.

caption: Tanδ versus temperature curves for printed PA samples evaluated in dried and various humid states (30%RH, 50%RH, 80%RH).
summary: This panel displays the representative DMTA curves for printed PA samples, illustrating the temperature-dependent tanδ behavior. The data compares the material response across different moisture conditions, specifically the dried state versus 30%RH, 50%RH, and 80%RH environments, providing insight into the viscoelastic properties of the printed polyamide under varying humidity levels.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics of a direct formic acid fuel cell (DFAFC) equipped with serpentine graphite interconnectors featuring right-angled trapezoidal baffles, evaluated across various spatial orientations.
summary: This panel displays the current-voltage polarization curves for a DFAFC utilizing serpentine graphite interconnectors with right-angled trapezoidal baffles. The data illustrates performance variations across different spatial orientations. These characteristics, when analyzed alongside power data, suggest that the fuel cell performance benefits significantly from a diverse slug size distribution within the flow field.

caption: Chronoamperometry response of 3D-printed patterned electrodes compared to flat electrodes at a constant potential of 0.7 V.
summary: Chronoamperometry results at 0.7 V demonstrate that patterned electrodes exhibit higher current densities than flat electrodes. Although hydrogen bubble formation is absent at this potential, the amperometry graphs confirm that the patterned designs consistently outperform the 3D-printed 3 mm flat electrode in electrochemical performance under these specific test conditions.

caption: Microhardness profile across the FGM10 sample, where the horizontal arrow denotes the extent of the graded material region.
summary: This panel displays the microhardness distribution for the FGM10 sample. The graded region, demarcated by a horizontal arrow, illustrates the mechanical transition between the base materials. This profile serves to characterize the hardness evolution across the sample length, reflecting the influence of the specific composition gradient used.

caption: Resistance evolution of the electrical insulation coating at a constant temperature of 900 °C, demonstrating a stable resistance value of 3 MΩ, which is significantly higher than the metallic sensitive layer.
summary: This panel illustrates the electrical performance of the insulation coating at a sustained temperature of 900 °C. The data shows that the resistance reaches a stable value of 3 MΩ, confirming that the coating provides significantly higher electrical resistance compared to the underlying metallic sensitive layer during high-temperature operation.

caption: High-magnification electron channeling contrast imaging (ECCI) of the as-printed sample, highlighting a high density of dislocation substructures, where red arrows indicate stacking faults and blue arrows denote dislocation cells.
summary: High-magnification ECCI analysis reveals the presence of significant defect substructures within the as-printed alloy. The image highlights band-like features accompanied by a high density of dislocations, specifically identifying stacking faults and dislocation cells through red and blue arrows, respectively, which characterize the internal deformation state of the material.

caption: Surface model of the β-Mg24Y5 phase illustrating the spatial distribution of magnesium and yttrium atoms.
summary: This surface model illustrates the atomic arrangement of the β-Mg24Y5 phase. Green spheres denote magnesium atoms, while light blue spheres represent yttrium atoms. The model serves as a structural reference for understanding the surface characteristics of this intermetallic phase within the context of the investigated alloy system.

caption: Two-dimensional neutron scattering intensity map of 25Cr-7Ni super duplex stainless steel aged at 300 °C for 48,000 hours, acquired under a 1.5 T horizontal saturating magnetic field.
summary: This 2D intensity map displays neutron scattering data for aged 25Cr-7Ni super duplex stainless steel under a 1.5 T magnetic field. Horizontal sectors represent pure nuclear scattering, while vertical sectors capture combined nuclear and magnetic contributions. The data reduction includes mirror sectors for both horizontal and vertical orientations to isolate specific scattering components.

caption: Three-dimensional spatial distribution of sample points generated using the Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) method.
summary: This panel displays the three-dimensional spatial distribution of sample points generated using the Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) method. As illustrated in the figure, the comparison of these distributions demonstrates that the improved sampling method significantly enhances the filling characteristics of sample spaces within the parameter space compared to this baseline.

caption: Self-corrosion current density plotted against varying prestrain levels.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between self-corrosion current density and prestrain levels. The data demonstrates how mechanical prestraining influences the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the material, with the passivation potential variations correlated to the observed current density trends across different prestrain conditions as described in the study.

caption: Nyquist plot for SLMed TC4 alloy S1 after 12 days of immersion in a corrosive environment.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the S1 specimen after 12 days of immersion. The plot characterizes the corrosion resistance of the SLMed TC4 alloy, with higher low-frequency impedance modules and phase angles indicating superior corrosion resistance compared to other process parameters.

caption: Functional architecture of an in-situ manufacturing process monitoring system, illustrating the integration of physical and digital assets.
summary: This schematic illustrates the functional architecture of a typical in-situ manufacturing process monitoring system. It highlights the essential integration of physical and digital assets required for real-time monitoring. The diagram serves as a foundational representation of how these components interact to facilitate effective process control and data acquisition during manufacturing.

caption: Experimental pole figure generated from XRD measurements of NiTi sample-C, showing a strong <100> texture.
summary: The experimental pole figure, generated via XRD measurement, confirms the presence of a strong <100> texture in NiTi sample-C. This experimental data aligns with the simulated pole figure, demonstrating that the computational model successfully predicts the crystallographic texture observed in the high laser power processed material.

caption: Arc morphology observed during the first cladding layer deposition without an auxiliary energy field, exhibiting significant left, right, backward, and forward deflections.
summary: Arc morphology during the first cladding layer without induction heating shows significant instability. The arc exhibits sequential left, right, backward, and forward deflections. Quantitative analysis reveals that the left deflection magnitude reaches 67°, while the right deflection magnitude reaches 64°, indicating substantial arc wandering in the absence of external thermal control.

caption: Williamson–Hall plot for 4340 steel samples, displaying Gaussian peak-fitting results as red circles and a linear regression fit represented by a central blue box.
summary: This Williamson–Hall analysis of 4340 steel demonstrates a strong linear fit across all experimental data points. The plot utilizes Gaussian peak-fitting results, shown as red circles, to derive the linear relationship indicated by the blue box, confirming the validity of the calculation method for the investigated steel fabrication conditions.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of van der Waals forces and morphological changes during the 100 ps molecular dynamics adsorption process.
summary: Monitoring the adsorption progression over 100 ps reveals the dynamic change in van der Waals energies and particle morphology. The simulation demonstrates a clear correlation where increasing van der Waals forces directly correspond to the strengthening of bonds between the particles, providing insight into the adsorption mechanism over time.

caption: Elemental distribution maps of Fe, Cr, Mo, and V in the X40CrMoV5-1 single layer weld, illustrating microsegregations.
summary: Elemental distribution maps of Fe, Cr, Mo, and V characterize the microsegregations within the X40CrMoV5-1 single layer weld. These EDS measurements reveal local changes in chemical composition, which correlate with the different etching behaviors observed in the material, providing a detailed view of the elemental distribution across the weld microstructure.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) distribution map for the specimen processed at 500 °C and a strain rate of 10,000 s⁻¹.
summary: This KAM map displays the dislocation distribution for the specimen deformed at 500 °C and 10,000 s⁻¹. By analyzing the KAM values, the degree of plastic deformation is assessed, revealing that grain boundaries exhibit higher misorientation values, which corresponds to a higher density of defects and localized plastic deformation.

caption: Storage modulus (G') as a function of temperature for PP and PP composites, showing the onset of solidification through a sharp slope variation.
summary: This panel displays the storage modulus of PP and its composites during oscillatory temperature ramps. The data, collected at a cooling rate of 3 °C/min, highlights the onset of solidification, which is identified by a sharp change in the slope of the G' versus temperature curve between 135 and 144 °C.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength of SLM-EF specimens across the 20–700 °C range, highlighting the room temperature strength of approximately 650 MPa.
summary: Ultimate tensile strength for SLM-EF blocks is presented from 20 to 700 °C, with a recorded value of approximately 650 MPa at room temperature. The plot demonstrates consistent strength characteristics across different fabrications and orientations, while providing a benchmark against established reference materials like EUROFER97 and other literature-sourced data.

caption: Box plots comparing the energy distribution within peaks and valleys of the high-frequency acoustic emission band (49.61–50 kHz) across four distinct printing tracks.
summary: This box plot illustrates the energy variance in high-frequency acoustic emission signals during printing. Analysis reveals a significant disparity in signal intensity, where the median energy for peaks reaches 26.73 dB/Hz, while the median energy for valleys is substantially lower at 2.62 dB/Hz across the four evaluated printing tracks.

caption: Phase fraction distribution in the Amdry365/IN792 sample after 20 minutes of oxidation at 1100 °C.
summary: Representing the intermediate stage of phase transformation, this panel illustrates the phase fraction distribution in the Amdry365/IN792 sample after 20 minutes of oxidation at 1100 °C. The simulation captures the progression of phase development within the material as the oxidation time increases from the initial state.

caption: Repeatability study of PANOA type II acidification cycles in 0.1 M NaCl, showing pH modulation over eight cycles.
summary: This panel displays the repeatability of PANOA type II acidification cycles in 0.1 M NaCl. The electrochemical modulation, involving potential steps of +0.4 V and -0.2 V, resulted in a pH change of 2.82±0.06 over eight cycles, with a higher initial shift of 2.96±0.18 for the first three cycles.

caption: Weldability evaluation of Ni-based superalloys represented by the combined concentration of Al + Ti versus Cr + Co, as reported in Ref. [21].
summary: Representing the weldability of Ni-based superalloys, this diagram correlates the sum of Al and Ti against the sum of Cr and Co. According to Ref. [21], this specific mapping allows for the identification of welding process performance, such as the 'fair' rating observed for the IN 939 superalloy.

caption: Conductivity and current response curves plotted against varying CNT-AR weight ratios in PMTA-CNT, with an inset showing LED luminescence intensity; blue markers denote reference values for a copper wire conductor.
summary: The plot illustrates that increasing the CNT-AR weight ratio in PMTA-CNT enhances both the material's conductivity and the resulting current, leading to brighter LED emission. Comparative data shows that while pure copper wire achieves a current of 1580 mA, the PMTA-CNT composites demonstrate effective conductive properties for circuit applications.

caption: Correlation-based fusion analysis of multi-source heterogeneous signal feature values.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the fusion analysis of key multi-source heterogeneous signal feature values, derived through correlation calculations. The visualization demonstrates that features extracted from the four distinct sensing signals exhibit complementary relationships, providing a comprehensive overview of how these diverse data sources interact and contribute to the overall signal analysis framework.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of the synthesized FITC-amoxicillin drug-encapsulated gelatin hydrogel beads, displaying a uniform green fluorescent appearance indicating successful drug loading.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy confirms the successful synthesis of drug-encapsulated gelatin hydrogel beads. The homogeneous green fluorescent appearance of each bead, observed at a 1 mm scale, serves as evidence of the uniform distribution of FITC-amoxicillin within the hydrogel matrix, validating the effectiveness of the fluidic mixing and extrusion process.

caption: Conductivity retention of various crosslinked membranes measured at 60 °C during aging in 1 M KOH solution.
summary: This plot illustrates the conductivity changes of crosslinked membranes aged in 1 M KOH at 60 °C. The data shows only slight decreases in conductivity over the measurement duration, indicating that the crosslinking process effectively enhances the alkaline stability of the electrolyte membranes under these specific testing conditions.

caption: Local density of states (LDOS) map for the resonant peak at 0.22 V, featuring the energy-dependent transmission function overlaid as a red vertical line.
summary: The LDOS for the resonant peak at 0.22 V shows the ground quantum well eigenvalue aligned with the emitter Fermi level. This alignment causes the energy-dependent transmission function, represented by a red line, to reach a local maximum. White dashed lines indicate the conductance band minima bounding the GaAs quantum well.

caption: Storage modulus E′ versus temperature for undoped resin specimens, comparing performance before and after water uptake tests.
summary: This panel displays the storage modulus E′ for undoped resin specimens as measured by DMTA. The plot compares the mechanical response of the material before and after undergoing water uptake tests, providing a baseline for evaluating the impact of moisture on the mechanical properties of the neat resin matrix.

caption: Calculated concentration profile for Ti across the austenite-martensite interface during isothermal holding at 500 °C for various durations up to 36000 s.
summary: This panel presents the simulated Ti concentration profile across the austenite and martensite interface. The data illustrates the evolution of Ti distribution over holding times ranging from 0 to 36000 s, providing insight into the long-term elemental partitioning behavior of Ti within the maraging steel microstructure at 500 °C.

caption: Partial 1H NMR spectrum of RhB-HZ, featuring an inset displaying the molecular structure of the compound.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of RhB-HZ provides structural characterization, exhibiting characteristic proton resonances that correspond to both the aromatic and aliphatic domains of the molecule. The inset within the panel further clarifies the molecular structure of RhB-HZ, confirming the successful synthesis and chemical identity of the material.

caption: Bode-phase plot illustrating the phase angle variation with frequency for the as-deposited and 600 °C-annealed coatings.
summary: Bode-phase plots reveal the phase angle response of the coatings in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The annealed coating demonstrates a stronger barrier effect, evidenced by a higher phase angle at low frequencies, confirming the enhanced protective properties achieved through the 600 °C annealing process.

caption: Reflection magnitude distribution for arbitrary combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 86 GHz and 90 GHz, showing values between 0.67 and 0.98.
summary: Concluding the higher frequency band analysis, this panel shows the reflection magnitudes for meta-atom combinations at 86 GHz and 90 GHz. The results highlight the robust performance of the design, with reflection magnitudes reaching up to 0.98, demonstrating consistent high reflection efficiency across the evaluated W-band frequency range.

caption: Tafel plots illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys, including AISI 316L, AISI 347, AISI 321, and Inconel 625, measured in [EMIM][Tf2N] ionic liquid at 80 °C.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical corrosion characteristics of various stainless steels and nickel-based alloys in [EMIM][Tf2N] at 80 °C. AISI 316L exhibits relatively poor corrosion resistance compared to the other tested alloys. These plots are essential for determining corrosion potentials and evaluating the polarization behavior of these materials.

caption: Creep behavior of René 95 at 650 °C, comparing the performance of as-received specimens against those subjected to shot peening (SP) processing.
summary: Creep performance of René 95 is evaluated at 650 °C in this plot, contrasting the as-received material with shot peened specimens. The analysis demonstrates the influence of the SP-processing on high-temperature creep characteristics, providing insight into how surface treatment affects the long-term deformation resistance of the alloy under load.

caption: Measured porosity and average strut diameter values for the fluorite wick geometry.
summary: Presented here are the measured porosity and average strut diameter for the fluorite wick geometry. By maintaining a constant strut diameter of 325 μm, these results allow for a direct comparison of how varying porosity affects the permeability and pore radius of the wick structure as measured by helium pycnometry.

caption: Corrosion current density (Icorr) trends for different titanium alloys across varying temperatures in a pH=1.5 acidic solution.
summary: Corrosion current density (Icorr) for titanium alloys is shown across a temperature range at pH=1.5. For Ti-6Al-4V, the current density initially decreases slightly before rising rapidly as temperature increases. This behavior highlights a corrosion resistance threshold for the alloy between 60 °C and 80 °C, consistent with established literature.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph obtained using the (201̅)AlTi3 reflection to identify AlTi3 core particles.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph, utilizing the (201̅)AlTi3 reflection, confirms the presence of AlTi3 core particles within the TiC carbides of the US-0W sample. This imaging technique, alongside SAED and EDS, provides definitive evidence of the AlTi3 phase within the complex carbide structures of the Udimet 500 alloy.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curve of the Onyx filament, showing the weight fraction of carbon fibers.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) results indicate the weight fraction of the Onyx filament. Based on these measurements, the material exhibits a fiber weight fraction of 13.51%, which corresponds to a calculated fiber volume fraction of 11.5% when considering the densities of the carbon fiber and the matrix.

caption: Distribution of γ channel width in 1100S dendrite cores.
summary: Quantifying the γ channel width for the 1100S sample, this histogram illustrates the spacing between γ′ precipitates. The results show that the evolution of the γ channel width remains consistent with the γ′ phase size distribution, supporting the observed microstructural trends across different primary aging temperatures.

caption: Dilatometric analysis of the GJL-316L–316L + WC composite sample, showing thermal expansion behavior between 820 °C and 900 °C.
summary: This dilatometer test characterizes the thermal expansion behavior of the GJL-316L–316L + WC composite sample. Analysis of the temperature range between 820 °C and 900 °C suggests the presence of an intermetallic τ1 phase, providing insight into the probable phase states within this specific thermal regime for the material.

caption: Immunofluorescence images showing Pax-7+ (green) and BrdU+ (red) satellite cells in d3D-BP scaffolds, with a bar graph depicting the percentage of proliferating BrdU+ satellite cells.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging identifies proliferating satellite cells via BrdU incorporation. The data confirms a significantly higher number of Pax-7+ satellite cells stained with BrdU in d3D-BP compared to 3D-BP controls, with 63.96% versus 43.7% respectively, indicating that the d3D-BP scaffold effectively promotes satellite cell maintenance and proliferation.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Oxygen (O) across the Nimolloy-202-H cross-section, showing no evidence of surface oxidation or depletion.
summary: Oxygen elemental distribution mapping across the Nimolloy-202-H cross-section confirms a uniform presence of the element. The lack of depletion near the surface indicates that the material undergoes homogeneous and congruent dissolution during the corrosion testing process, maintaining its structural integrity without localized loss of alloying elements.

caption: Snapshots of the irreversible volume fraction illustrating the evolution of transformation-induced plasticity at the conclusion of each subloop, demonstrating the continuous expansion of the sweeping zone.
summary: Snapshots of the irreversible volume fraction illustrate the evolution of transformation-induced plasticity at the end of each subloop. As shown in the figure, the sweeping zone continuously expands from one subloop to the next, providing a clear visualization of the progressive structural changes occurring within the NiTi wire.

caption: SAXS experimental profiles of P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL in chlorobenzene solvent, featuring an inset Guinier plot used to estimate the molecular weight of P3HT-PSL.
summary: Small-angle X-ray scattering profiles for P3HT-PSL and PPI-SL are presented, highlighting their supramolecular structural features in chlorobenzene. The inclusion of a Guinier plot inset, generated via BioXTAS RAW software, allows for the precise estimation of the P3HT-PSL molecular weight, providing critical insight into the aggregate characteristics of the solution.

caption: Velocity field map illustrating material flow patterns within the weld cross-section during the welding process.
summary: This velocity field map represents the numerical results for the weld cross-section in the central region of the tool for Test 3. The scale of the velocity data is consistent with the macrography presented in panel a, providing a visual representation of material flow during the welding process.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the area shown in (c), illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution within the unrecrystallized grain and the channel.
summary: The IPF map of the region corresponding to panel (c) displays the crystallographic orientation of the unrecrystallized grain and the associated channel. Analysis of the misorientation profiles within this region indicates the formation of sub-grain boundaries, which generate point-to-point orientation changes exceeding 2 degrees.

caption: High-resolution Cr 2p XPS spectrum with peaks at 587.10, 583.40, 577.39, and 574.21 eV, assigned to Cr 3+ 2p 1/2, Cr 0 2p 1/2, Cr 3+ 2p 3/2, and Cr 0 2p 3/2.
summary: Analysis of the Cr 2p XPS spectrum identifies peaks at 587.10, 583.40, 577.39, and 574.21 eV. These binding energies correspond to Cr 3+ 2p 1/2, Cr 0 2p 1/2, Cr 3+ 2p 3/2, and Cr 0 2p 3/2, indicating the coexistence of metallic and oxidized chromium states.

caption: FT-IR spectra of avocado oil (AO) and acrylated avocado oil (AAO) showing characteristic vibrational bands at 3007, 1740, and 1655 cm⁻¹.
summary: The FT-IR spectrum of avocado oil displays characteristic vibrational bands at 3007, 1740, and 1655 cm⁻¹, which are consistent with literature values. These spectral features are used to investigate the acrylation process of the oil, providing a baseline for comparing the chemical structure of AO against the modified AAO sample.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curve and fitted Tafel curves for a copper electrode in 0.1 M NaAc solution at pH 1 and 25 ℃.
summary: This panel displays the potentiodynamic polarization and fitted Tafel curves for copper in a 0.1 M NaAc solution at pH 1. The anodic and cathodic current curves intersect at 0.18 V, a value closely matching the best-fit equilibrium potential for the Cu/Cu2+ redox couple, which is calculated at 0.201 V.

caption: Contour map illustrating the powder layer density distribution achieved using a silicone blade spreading mechanism.
summary: This contour plot displays the powder layer density (PLD) achieved using a silicone blade. Compared to the rotating roller, the silicone blade results in lower overall powder layer density values for identical powder characteristics, highlighting the influence of the spreading mechanism on the final powder bed quality and uniformity.

caption: Entropic potential profiles of NMC622 coin cells plotted against open-circuit voltage during the lithiation process at a C/10 rate.
summary: Shown here is the entropic potential versus open-circuit voltage for NMC622 coin cells during lithiation at a C/10 rate. The results reveal that the profiles for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted electrodes overlap with negligible discrepancy, confirming highly similar electrochemical characteristics during the lithiation phase of the battery cycle.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the Al–Fe binary system showing the thermodynamic stability regions.
summary: The Al–Fe binary phase diagram illustrates the thermodynamic stability regions for the system. According to the reference, this diagram indicates that an Al–4Fe alloy composition is expected to form the Al13Fe4 intermetallic phase at equilibrium, providing a baseline for understanding the phase evolution in more complex alloy systems.

caption: Progression of the liquid layer formation along the high angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) within the heat-affected zone (HAZ).
summary: The diagram depicts the progression of liquid layer formation along the high angle grain boundaries within the heat-affected zone of the Hastelloy X alloy. This continuous liquid film is a direct consequence of the remelting of γ-M23C6 eutectics, which facilitates the eventual development of liquation fissures during the alloy's deposition procedure.

caption: Higher magnification cross-sectional BSE image of the PM-HIP3 316 L oxide layer.
summary: Detailed BSE imaging of the PM-HIP3 316 L oxide layer provides a closer examination of the bilayer structure. The micrograph confirms the presence of distinct inner and outer oxide layers resulting from exposure to the simulated PWR hydrogenated coolant, consistent with the general findings for all materials in this study.

caption: O 1s XPS spectra of NIF(Na,Cr)-S and NIF(Na)-S, highlighting a significant increase in the peak strength of M–OH bonds, which suggests Cr doping promotes the formation of metal hydroxide active species.
summary: The O 1s XPS spectra indicate that Cr doping enhances the formation of active metal hydroxide species. A notable increase in the peak intensity associated with M–OH bonds is observed in the doped sample, suggesting that the doping process promotes the development of these catalytically active surface groups.

caption: Three-dimensional surface plot illustrating the dependency of shear strength on process parameters, modeled using a 3rd-degree polynomial fit.
summary: This 3D surface plot visualizes the relationship between process parameters and shear strength. A 3rd-degree polynomial function was applied to fit the experimental data points, providing a continuous representation of how these variables influence the mechanical shear strength of the processed material under investigation.

caption: XRD patterns of Pure-LPBF, 0.3B-LPBF, and 0.6B-LPBF alloys analyzed in the plane parallel to the building direction, with a zoom-in highlighting M2B boride peaks.
summary: XRD patterns for the three L-PBF alloys are shown for the plane parallel to the building direction. The Pure-LPBF specimen exhibits variations in δ-ferrite peak intensities, with the most prominent peak at approximately 45° ({110}). The zoom-in highlights the emergence of M2B peaks in the boron-modified alloys.

caption: Comparison of crack growth rate predictions from the present model, Shyam model, and Ye model against experimental fatigue test data at stress magnitudes of 540 and 612 MPa.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis of crack growth rate predictions using the proposed model, the Shyam model, and the Ye model. By incorporating local yield strength and grain inhomogeneity, the present model is validated against experimental fatigue data at 540 and 612 MPa, demonstrating improved predictive accuracy for short crack propagation.

caption: Radar chart comparing the mechanical properties of PC, ABS, and their respective blends.
summary: This radar chart provides a comparative analysis of the mechanical properties for PC, ABS, and their blends. By visualizing multiple performance metrics simultaneously, the diagram facilitates a direct assessment of how blending these polymers influences their overall mechanical behavior, highlighting the relative strengths and weaknesses of each material composition.

caption: Stress-strain curves for 3D filament-based scaffolds, illustrating the mechanical response of PCL, PP20, and PP20CS50 variants before and after the leaching process.
summary: The stress-strain curves for 3D filament-based scaffolds, including PCL, PP20, and PP20CS50, are presented to characterize their mechanical behavior. These curves demonstrate the response of the constructs before and after leaching, providing the necessary data to calculate the elastic modulus based on the slope within the linear region.

caption: Quasi-static J-H hysteresis loops comparing the magnetic performance of AP and 1000–24 samples.
summary: Quasi-static J-H hysteresis loops for AP and 1000–24 samples are presented to evaluate magnetic performance. The area enclosed by these loops at an applied magnetic field strength of 3000 A/m is used to calculate the hysteresis core energy loss, representing the energy dissipated per unit volume during a single magnetization cycle.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe reconstruction of the CR750 condition featuring an Al 9.8 at.% iso-concentration surface, which delineates a fine-scale B2 precipitate within a non-recrystallized FCC grain.
summary: Representing the non-recrystallized region of the CR750 sample, this APT reconstruction utilizes an Al 9.8 at.% iso-concentration surface to isolate and visualize a fine-scale B2 precipitate. The map provides a detailed view of the precipitate morphology and its spatial relationship with the surrounding non-recrystallized FCC matrix structure.

caption: Yield strength values plotted against porosity levels for 15 design modifications, including comparisons with traditional CU and CR structures, the old HH design, and the new MH design, alongside the human cortical bone reference threshold.
summary: Yield strength is presented as a function of scaffold porosity for multiple design iterations. The results demonstrate a declining trend in yield strength as the dumbbell length increases. While the design modifications influence porosity, they exhibit only a marginal impact on the yield strength compared to the cortical bone target.

caption: Isothermal transformation-time-temperature (TTT) diagram illustrating the processing temperature range of the part, which accounts for heat accumulation to reach 425 °C at the bottom and 575 °C at the top.
summary: The TTT diagram demonstrates that the processed part remains within the transformation gap of 400 to 620 °C. By accounting for a heat accumulation of 150 °C, the temperature profile of the part, ranging from 425 °C at the bottom to 575 °C at the top, is safely positioned within this critical range.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from nanoindentation testing for WAAM, LHAM, and LHAM-HT specimens.
summary: Nanoindentation testing was performed to assess mechanical properties on the nanoscale. The load-depth curves for WAAM, LHAM, and LHAM-HT specimens are presented. The WAAM specimen exhibited the smallest indentation depth, indicating the highest hardness, while the LHAM specimen showed intermediate values for both indentation depth and hardness.

caption: Band contrast map of CS-Ti2.9Cu providing structural detail on the α-lath arrangement and grain boundaries.
summary: The band contrast map of CS-Ti2.9Cu provides detailed visualization of the α-lath arrangement. Together with the IPF map, it demonstrates the role of Cu in promoting the columnar-to-equiaxed transition and enhancing grain refinement, confirming the effectiveness of the core-shell approach in controlling the microstructural outcome.

caption: Unit cell schematics illustrating the geometric configurations of the SQ, HC, EAM, CAM-S, CAM-BI1, and CAM-BI2 designs used in the mechanical performance analysis.
summary: Geometric unit cell schematics are provided for the SQ, HC, EAM, CAM-S, CAM-BI1, and CAM-BI2 designs. These diagrams illustrate the structural variations between the benchmark specimens and the bio-inspired interlocking composites, facilitating an understanding of how specific design features influence the mechanical interlocking effects observed in the stress-strain analysis.

caption: Force versus log10(time) plot for a Nimonic 90 spring at 600 °C with a deflection of 9 mm, illustrating the analytical stress relaxation model fit.
summary: Representing the force response on a logarithmic time scale, this panel provides a clearer visualization of the stress relaxation behavior for the Nimonic 90 spring. This format is utilized throughout the remainder of the study to evaluate the accuracy of analytical models against experimental spring data at 600 °C.

caption: High-angle annular dark field STEM image of oxide dispersoids within the bulk as-fabricated microstructure at 63kx magnification, where some dispersoids are unmarked to maintain image clarity.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph depicts oxide dispersoids in the bulk as-fabricated microstructure at 63kx magnification. While yellow arrows indicate some dispersoids, others remain unmarked to preserve the overall clarity of the image. This visual data contributes to the comprehensive analysis of the dispersoid population within the bulk material microstructure.

caption: Entropy change (ΔS) as a function of temperature for Ni2.15Mn0.70Cr0.15Ga, calculated from heat capacity data under magnetic field changes reaching 9 T.
summary: The temperature dependence of the entropy change (ΔS) is shown for the Ni2.15Mn0.70Cr0.15Ga composition. These values were extracted from heat capacity measurements under magnetic field variations up to 9 T, providing insight into the entropy-related magnetocaloric properties of the material across the investigated temperature range.

caption: Random Forest model performance metrics, specifically RMSE and R2, plotted against varying training data ratios.
summary: The Random Forest model demonstrates improved predictive accuracy as the training data ratio increases. By evaluating RMSE and R2 metrics, this learning curve illustrates the model's capability to generalize deposit geometry predictions, establishing it as a robust framework for modeling air-based CSAM processes with superior performance compared to neural networks.

caption: Parity plot of predicted versus reference concentrations for Riboflavin using a 5 mm path length measuring chamber.
summary: Riboflavin concentration data is presented in this parity plot, comparing predicted values against reference concentrations for a 5 mm path length. The plot demonstrates the accuracy of the measuring chamber, facilitating an assessment of the dynamic range and the ability to quantify this specific analyte effectively within the experimental setup.

caption: T300 carbon fiber cross-sections analyzed by SPM, showing the fiber surface characteristics in transversal (90°), 45°, and longitudinal (0°) orientations.
summary: T300 carbon fiber cross-sections analyzed by SPM, showing the fiber surface characteristics in transversal (90°), 45°, and longitudinal (0°) orientations. Following specimen preparation, the morphology of the fiber cross-sections was examined using SPM. These images provide a detailed look at the T300 carbon fiber morphology across the specified cutting angles.

caption: High-resolution XPS C 1s spectrum of 3Dp-H-BNC, illustrating the carbon bonding environment.
summary: The high-resolution C 1s XPS spectrum of 3Dp-H-BNC provides detailed information regarding the carbon bonding environment within the co-doped material. This analysis complements the B 1s and N 1s spectra to fully elucidate the chemical state and structural integration of the dopants within the carbon matrix.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation snapshot of the equilibrated BCC phase, modeled as a 30 × 30 × 20 unit cell supercell with an average composition derived from post-annealing data.
summary: This Monte Carlo simulation snapshot illustrates the equilibrated BCC phase structure, modeled using a 30 × 30 × 20 unit cell supercell based on post-annealing composition. The visualization reveals that the BCC structure stabilizes when Al atoms are surrounded by Ni and Fe by Co, while Cu atoms exhibit segregation.

caption: Frequency-dependent birefringence characteristics of the proposed petrochemical materials.
summary: This plot illustrates the birefringence behavior of various proposed petrochemicals as a function of frequency. The data highlights the optical response of these materials, providing essential insights into their refractive properties across the specified frequency range, which is critical for evaluating their potential applications in optical and photonic systems.

caption: Temperature-dependent rheological measurements of CSP1 under ambient atmosphere, showing viscosity decrease upon heating from 35 °C to 165 °C, with Arrhenius-law fitting and extrapolated values for higher temperatures indicated by a dotted line.
summary: Rheological measurements demonstrate a rapid decrease in viscosity for CSP1 upon heating from room temperature. Data collected between 35 °C and 165 °C were fitted to an Arrhenius-law model. Extrapolated values for temperatures exceeding 165 °C are represented by a dotted line to highlight the divergence between expected and observed behavior.

caption: Experimental matrix detailing the systematic naming convention and classification of the various samples utilized in the study.
summary: This figure presents the comprehensive experiment matrix, which serves as a foundational reference for the naming and identification of all samples investigated. By organizing the samples into a structured format, the matrix ensures clarity and consistency in the experimental design, facilitating accurate tracking and analysis throughout the research process.

caption: Maximum stress versus fatigue life curves for IN713C alloy, highlighting temperature-dependent fatigue resistance at 25 °C, 750 °C, and 1000 °C.
summary: Maximum stress-based S-N curves reveal a distinct temperature dependency in the fatigue resistance of the IN713C alloy. The data shows an initial increase in fatigue resistance when the temperature is raised to 750 °C, followed by a subsequent decline in performance as the testing temperature reaches 1000 °C.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectrum of surfactant-assisted SnO2-PVA nanostructures.
summary: Shown is the UV-Vis absorption spectrum for SnO2 nanostructures prepared with PVA assistance. The data provides insight into the light absorption behavior of the SnO2-PVA compound across ultraviolet and visible wavelengths, demonstrating the impact of the PVA surfactant on the optical response of the resulting nanostructured material.

caption: Time-resolved photoluminescence (TRPL) decay traces recorded at the peak emission wavelength for both InGaN PD types, fitted using a bi-exponential decay model.
summary: Time-resolved photoluminescence decay traces for both InGaN photodetectors are shown, captured at their respective peak emission wavelengths. These decay curves are analyzed using a bi-exponential fitting model to extract fast and slow component lifetimes, represented by tau1 and tau2, along with their corresponding amplitude constants, A1 and A2.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys measured in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution after 3600 s of immersion, serving as the basis for extracting key corrosion parameters.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization plots for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys are presented after 3600 s of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature. These curves are utilized to extract essential corrosion parameters, providing a quantitative assessment of the electrochemical behavior and corrosion resistance of the two alloy conditions in the saline environment.

caption: Dimensional changes measured along different spatial directions as a function of sintering temperature.
summary: Dimensional changes in all directions are shown to increase with rising sintering temperatures. Among the measured directions, the Δz direction consistently exhibits the lowest magnitude of dimensional change, highlighting the anisotropic nature of the shrinkage or expansion behavior during the sintering process under an N2 atmosphere.

caption: Comparative photoluminescence spectra of BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C and reference SL-InAs/GaAsSb-C samples measured at 77 K under 100 mW excitation, highlighting differences in peak splitting.
summary: Comparative photoluminescence spectra for BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C and the single-layer reference SL-InAs/GaAsSb-C are shown at 77 K under 100 mW excitation. The reference sample exhibits a ground state to excited state splitting of approximately 72 meV, which supports the interpretation that the BL sample features emission from two distinct layers.

caption: Heating profile for thermal dilation testing of LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V, featuring a heating rate of 1 °C/s to 940 °C with variable holding durations of 0, 5, and 30 minutes before quenching.
summary: This panel displays the thermal dilation testing protocol for LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V specimens. The samples are heated at a rate of 1 °C/s until reaching 940 °C. They are then held at this peak temperature for durations of 0, 5, and 30 minutes, respectively, before undergoing quenching to room temperature.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the diffusion coefficient for Co, illustrating the temperature-dependent diffusion behavior.
summary: This panel presents the Arrhenius relationship for Co diffusion, plotting log D against inverse homologous temperature. The graph incorporates both calculated diffusion coefficients and literature-based tracer data. Shaded regions indicate the range of the diffusion coefficients, providing a clear visualization of the experimental and model-derived data bounds for Co.

caption: Spider chart comparing the VEGF binding capacity in ng mg−1 of the developed microscaffolds against previously published heparinized scaffold results.
summary: This spider chart illustrates the superior VEGF binding performance of the developed microscaffolds compared to previously reported heparinized scaffolds. Quantitative analysis reveals that this method achieves 3–3000x higher VEGF binding per unit mass and approximately 177x increased bound VEGF per volume, demonstrating significant improvements in scaffold functionalization efficiency.

caption: Planar trajectory generation for the hourglass-shaped case study within the slicing coordinate system s for the first layer.
summary: Represented here are the planarly generated trajectories for an hourglass-shaped case study, defined in the slicing coordinate system s for the first layer. The diagram showcases the software-generated pathing, including solid violet lines that indicate travel moves, which are not interpolated by the current algorithm and may cause implementation deviations.

caption: Isothermal entropy change plotted against temperature during heating for various magnetic field changes, with an inset showing the temperature averaged entropy change (TEC) calculated over a 5 K span.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature dependence of the isothermal entropy change upon heating under different magnetic field conditions. The inset provides a quantitative evaluation of the magnetocaloric performance by displaying the temperature averaged entropy change (TEC) calculated for the alloy series over a 5 K temperature interval.

caption: Temperature versus Gibbs free energy relationship for IN718 alloy and associated carbides.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermodynamic relationship between temperature and Gibbs free energy for IN718 and its constituent carbides. The low Gibbs free energy of (Nb,Ti)C facilitates its formation at grain boundaries, as the melting of TiC increases local Ti and C concentrations, leading to the consumption of Nb from the solution.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph highlighting the interactions between Cr₂B and (Ni,Co)Ti₂ phases and dislocations.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals a significant accumulation of dislocations near Cr₂B and (Ni,Co)Ti₂ nanoscale precipitates. These precipitates actively participate in the deformation process by impeding dislocation motion, confirming their role as structural obstacles that contribute to the overall mechanical response of the material under tensile loading.

caption: TEM micrograph of the LDED-100 specimen displaying the formation of distinct subgrain structures.
summary: Panel (d) provides a detailed view of the LDED-100 specimen, focusing on the evolution of the microstructure. The image clearly shows the presence of distinct subgrain structures, which represent a significant microstructural feature developed under these specific processing conditions, contrasting with the simpler defect structures observed in the LDED sample.

caption: Elementary cell of the Gyr7.5 gyroid structure formed by the repetition of base units.
summary: The elementary cell of the Gyr7.5 gyroid structure is shown here, constructed by repeating the base units. This specific configuration represents one of three distinct cell sizes, with dimensions of 7.9 mm, illustrating the periodic arrangement required to form the larger, functional TPMS lattice structure for further engineering applications.

caption: Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) and Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) curves for Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixtures subjected to varying mechanical milling durations ranging from 2 to 72 hours.
summary: Thermal analysis curves for Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixtures are presented across various milling times from 2 to 72 hours. These TGA and DSC measurements serve as the foundation for determining reaction kinetic parameters. By applying the Coats-Redfern method to these curves, researchers can effectively characterize the thermal behavior of the mechanically alloyed powders.

caption: Numerical absorption spectra for metapyramids with an apex angle of α = 30° across incident angles of 0°, 30°, 45°, and 60°.
summary: Numerical absorption spectra for metapyramids with an apex angle of α = 30° are evaluated at incident angles of 0°, 30°, 45°, and 60°. At 45°, absorptivity exceeds 0.9 between 9.8 and 19.1 GHz, while at 60°, it remains above 0.8 within the 8.4 to 19.1 GHz range under TE polarization.

caption: Sequential fracture progression observed in the edge-notch composite design model A + A + B.
summary: This schematic illustrates the step-by-step fracture process within the A + A + B sandwich composite design. Unlike the one-step fracture behavior typical of model A, this configuration demonstrates a progressive failure mechanism, highlighting the structural advantages of the composite design in managing crack propagation and energy dissipation during mechanical loading.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PEB106-i synthesized with one equivalent of BnOH, displaying a mixture of end-chain groups including species [A], benzyloxide residues [C], and a minor fraction of ethylene glycol-terminated units [D].
summary: In the presence of one equivalent of BnOH, the MALDI-TOF spectrum for PEB106-i reveals a mixture of end-chain groups. The identified species include [A], benzyloxide residues [C], and a minor fraction terminated by an ethylene glycol unit [D], which indicates that transesterification occurred during the polymerization process.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction evolution plotted against temperature for the T2 alloy (44Ti-20Mo-15Ta-15Cr-6Al) derived from FactSage simulations.
summary: FactSage thermodynamic modeling predicts the phase fraction evolution for the T2 alloy across a range of temperatures. The results indicate significant C15 Laves phase formation within the 1000–1300 °C range, aligning with prior studies on the Ti-Mo-Ta-Cr-Al system and its subsystems, providing insight into the material's high-temperature phase stability.

caption: 3D optical microscopy surface topography of the mild carbon steel wear track after testing at room temperature.
summary: This 3D optical microscopy image displays the wear track morphology of mild carbon steel tested at room temperature. The visualization highlights the surface topography and depth of the track, providing a baseline for comparing wear damage against higher temperature conditions where pile-up height and track dimensions are significantly altered.

caption: Focused examination of parameter importance influenced by SPTs across as-built, stress-relieved, and T6 heat-treated material conditions.
summary: Surface residual stress consistently emerges as the most critical factor, accounting for 60-75% of the influence regardless of material strength or ductility. This focused analysis highlights the dominant role of surface RS across diverse processing states, including as-built, stress-relieved, and T6 heat-treated conditions, demonstrating its robust impact on material performance.

caption: Random Forest feature importance ranking plot illustrating the relative contribution of various alloying elements to the hardness prediction of the investigated alloys.
summary: This Random Forest feature importance ranking plot quantifies the influence of different elements on alloy hardness. Analysis reveals that elements such as Al and V significantly improve hardness, with these findings showing strong consistency with SHAP prediction results, confirming the reliability of the feature importance ranking in predicting material mechanical properties.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluating the performance of s-CAE and m-CAE anomaly detection models.
summary: This plot displays the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves for both s-CAE and m-CAE models. These curves provide a quantitative assessment of the anomaly detector's performance, illustrating the trade-off between true positive and false positive rates for the different CAE configurations used in the diagnostic framework.

caption: Open-circuit potential (OCP) evolution over time for the composite coatings, illustrating initial fluctuations and subsequent stabilization.
summary: This panel displays the open-circuit potential (OCP) of the composite coatings over time. The data reveals that the OCP for H40 and H20 coatings initially decreases before reaching a stable state, a behavior likely attributed to corrosion processes triggered by surface inhomogeneities or the presence of micropores within the material structure.

caption: Physical implementation of the vertical test bench showing the actual hardware configuration.
summary: This panel displays the physical implementation of the vertical test bench. It captures the actual hardware configuration, providing a visual confirmation of the assembled equipment. The photograph demonstrates the practical realization of the design shown in the previous panel, highlighting the tangible components used in the experimental setup.

caption: Fiber placement layout 2 showing continuous fibers crossing through the failure point to mitigate crack propagation, with adhesion damage highlighted by a red circle.
summary: Panel b presents the second fiber path layout, where continuous fibers are strategically placed to cross through the failure point. This design aims to prevent cracks from propagating through the intersection. Adhesion damage is indicated by a red circle, demonstrating the effectiveness of this layout in managing structural failure.

caption: Energy absorption (EA) and specific energy absorption (SEA) values calculated before the densification strain for varying sub-structure heights (c).
summary: Energy absorption (EA) and specific energy absorption (SEA) values are presented for structures with different sub-structure heights (c). These metrics are evaluated specifically before the densification strain point, providing insight into the energy dissipation capabilities of the structures as a function of their sub-structure height.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots displaying the inverse square capacitance versus applied potential for passive films on Ti–45Nb, 96(Ti–45Nb)-4Ga, and 92(Ti–45Nb)-8Ga alloys, measured in PBS solution after 1 hour of film formation at 0.6 V (vs. SCE) across a potential range of 1 V to -1 V (vs. SCE).
summary: Mott-Schottky plots characterize the passive films formed on Ti–45Nb and Ga-modified alloys in PBS solution. By measuring the inverse square capacitance against potential from 1 V to -1 V (vs. SCE), the electrochemical behavior of the films grown at 0.6 V is evaluated to determine their semiconducting properties.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness profile for the L-DED Ti55531 alloy modified with 0.05 wt% boron.
summary: This panel presents the nanoindentation hardness data for the L-DED Ti55531 alloy containing 0.05 wt% boron. These tests were conducted to clarify how the addition of boron influences the phase-specific strength of the alloy, contributing to the comparative analysis of mechanical performance across the different boron-doped Ti55531 compositions.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the 350 °C tempered sample, revealing a characteristic lath morphology of the grains.
summary: This TEM image displays the microstructure of a sample tempered at 350 °C. The observation confirms a distinct lath morphology of the grains within the material, providing a foundational view of the structural arrangement prior to more detailed analysis of the martensite and austenite phases.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetric (DSC) curve of the PLA-graphene composite, highlighting the glass transition temperature (Tg) at 68.1 °C.
summary: The differential scanning calorimetric analysis of the PLA-graphene composite is presented in panel a. This thermal characterization technique identifies the glass transition temperature of the material at 68.1 °C, providing essential data regarding the thermal properties and phase transition behavior of the composite system under controlled heating conditions.

caption: Paris regime fatigue crack growth data for HSLA steel SENB specimens.
summary: The Paris regime for HSLA steel SENB specimens is depicted in this panel. The data represents the fatigue crack growth behavior of the HSLA steel under the specified experimental conditions, contributing to the overall comparison of material performance across the different specimen types and orientations tested in the study.

caption: Bubble diagram comparing the expression of S. aureus related pathways for 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK versus PEEK, showing statistical significance.
summary: Pfam enrichment analysis reveals significant upregulation of stress protection, adhesion, metabolic regulation, and electron transport-related proteins in S. aureus when exposed to the 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK surface compared to bare PEEK. These changes indicate a distinct bacterial response to the silver-containing composite surface, reflecting the material's antibacterial mechanism.

caption: Selected-Area Electron Diffraction (SAED) pattern of the SAED-1 region, identifying {2 1 1}〈1 1 1〉 type twins within the BCC matrix and revealing additional diffraction spots marked by orange dashed lines.
summary: The SAED pattern obtained from the SAED-1 region confirms the presence of {2 1 1}〈1 1 1〉 type twins within the BCC structure. In addition to the primary matrix and twin diffraction spots, two distinct spots marked by orange dashed lines are observed, indicating the presence of additional phases or structural features.

caption: Representative unit cell geometries for the Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond lattice structures, defining the repeating periodic elements of the designs.
summary: The unit cells for the Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond lattice structures are presented to define the fundamental repeating units of each design. These visualizations clarify the internal topology and connectivity of the lattice architectures, which are essential for understanding the structural characteristics and mechanical behavior of the printed specimens.

caption: Comparison of different HHF loading patterns applied to the mock-ups, including the P2 pattern used to evaluate performance differences between HV Diagonal and HV Chevron designs under varying water flow conditions.
summary: This panel presents the heat loading patterns applied during testing. It highlights the P2 pattern, which revealed distinct performance differences between the HV Diagonal and HV Chevron mock-ups. Specifically, the HV Diagonal design experienced overheating at 20 MW/m2 under WD2 flow, while the HV Chevron design maintained stable performance.

caption: Dilatometric expansion curve for the GJL-316L–316L + TiC composite (sample 6), illustrating the temperature-dependent dimensional change.
summary: This dilatometer test result for sample 6, a GJL-316L–316L + TiC composite, displays the material's thermal expansion behavior. Unlike other samples, the slope of the expansion curve remains upward throughout the test, indicating that the inclusion of TiC hard particles significantly influences the dimensional stability of the composite during thermal cycling.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to the negative control medium.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the negative control group after 72 hours of exposure to extracts. This image serves as the 72-hour baseline, showing the distribution of live (green) and dead (red) cells in the absence of material extracts to compare against the experimental groups at this time point.

caption: Temperature-dependent storage modulus and tan δ curves for CNC-reinforced composites, highlighting viscoelastic behavior.
summary: Storage modulus and tan δ curves are plotted against temperature to characterize the viscoelastic properties of the CNC composites. The dashed lines represent the storage modulus, while the solid lines indicate tan δ. These thermal analysis results provide insight into the material's stiffness and damping characteristics across a range of temperatures.

caption: S-N fatigue curve of GH4169 alloy tested at a stress ratio of R = 0.
summary: This S-N curve illustrates the fatigue behavior of GH4169 alloy under a stress ratio of R = 0. Based on experimental data from four fatigue tests conducted within a stress range of 411–700 MPa, the curve provides a fitted representation of the material's cyclic loading performance and fatigue life characteristics.

caption: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the low CSRO model at 0 T magnetic induction intensity.
summary: Calculated pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the low CSRO system at 0 T are shown here. The system exhibits seven distinct types of chemical order, including Co-Co, Co-Fe, Co-Mn, Cr-Cr, Cr-Mn, Cr-Ni, and Mn-Ni, providing insight into the initial state of chemical ordering before magnetic field application.
