summary: Various zigzag conformal cooling channel designs are presented to demonstrate the range of available geometric configurations. Numerical studies, such as those by Torres-Alba et al., indicate that these zigzag designs are highly suitable for shell parts, providing benefits such as reduced average cooling times and minimized standard form deviations.

caption: Natural logarithm of the ratio of lattice hydrogen concentration to the number of lattice sites plotted against reciprocal temperature to derive the solubility energy of interstitial hydrogen.
summary: Panel (c) presents the natural logarithm of the ratio of lattice hydrogen concentration to the number of lattice sites as a function of reciprocal temperature. This analysis allows for the calculation of the solubility energy of interstitial hydrogen (EL) within the material under the specified cathodic charging conditions.

caption: Fatigue ratcheting and damage strain evolution for the aged specimen with ST surface condition at 123 MPa.
summary: Aged ST specimens tested at 123 MPa exhibit significant initial fatigue ratcheting strain, followed by a plateau around 0.03% after 10^3 cycles. This plateau value is notably lower than that observed in the AB surface condition, demonstrating the influence of surface treatment on the accumulation of fatigue ratcheting strain.

caption: Resistive transition curves for Ta5Mo35W5Re35Ru20C20 HEA measured under varying magnetic fields up to 9 T, showing a gradual suppression of the transition to lower temperatures as the field increases.
summary: Resistive transitions for the Ta5Mo35W5Re35Ru20C20 high-entropy alloy are presented under magnetic fields up to 9 T. The data demonstrates that increasing the magnetic field suppresses the resistive transition to lower temperatures. The midpoint of the resistivity drop is marked by a dashed line, and the arrow indicates the direction of increasing field.

caption: Simulated Time-Temperature-Rupture (TTR) diagram at 700 °C, illustrating the impact of ductility parameters Z = 2%, 4%, 6%, and 8% in comparison to experimental data from this study and reference values from the 2017 ECCC datasheet.
summary: This TTR diagram displays the results of a parameter study investigating the influence of ductility (Z) on rupture behavior at 700 °C. By comparing simulated curves for Z values ranging from 2% to 8% against experimental results and ECCC datasheet benchmarks, the plot quantifies the sensitivity of creep rupture times to ductility variations.

caption: Absorption coefficients of Ga x In 1-x As y Sb 1-y alloys, including endpoint binaries InAs and GaSb, showing direct bandgap behavior across the composition range with an empirical model fit for x Ga = 0.8.
summary: Absorption curves for Ga x In 1-x As y Sb 1-y alloys demonstrate direct bandgap characteristics consistent with theoretical estimations. The plot includes endpoint binaries and an empirical law fit for a Ga content of 0.8, utilizing a specific absorption coefficient parameter to model the material's optical response.

caption: Non-equilibrium Scheil-Gulliver solidification model plotting phase fraction against temperature, indicating the formation of Cr3Si pinning particles during rapid solidification.
summary: The Scheil-Gulliver solidification model demonstrates the non-equilibrium phase evolution during rapid cooling of the CuNi2SiCr powder. Calculations indicate that Cr3Si particles form during the solidification process. These predicted pinning particles are expected to be present in the as-built microstructure, significantly influencing the material's final phase composition and properties.

caption: Arrhenius plot of normalized minimum creep rate versus inverse absolute temperature (1000/RT) at a normalized stress of 2.2 × 10⁻⁴, illustrating the determination of apparent activation energy for upper and lower limit data.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the normalized minimum creep rate against inverse absolute temperature to calculate the apparent activation energy for creep. Testing at 900, 950, and 1000 °C yielded activation energies of 498 kJ/mol for upper limit data and 363 kJ/mol for lower limit data, with a correlation coefficient of 0.97.

caption: Hausdorff distance between predicted and ground truth contour points plotted against varying sequence lengths for both U-Net and Temporal Transformer architectures.
summary: The Hausdorff distance metric is used here to evaluate the spatial discrepancy between predicted and ground truth contour points across different sequence lengths. By assessing this distance, the figure demonstrates the sensitivity of U-Net and Temporal Transformer models to the chosen sub-sequence length when predicting melt pool cross-section geometries.

caption: Rotational rheological analysis of the PD-PEG hydrogel, showing the rapid decline of storage modulus G' from 120 Pa to below 10 Pa during 300 seconds of UV exposure.
summary: This rheological plot displays the mechanical response of the PD-PEG hydrogel under 52 mW cm-2 UV irradiation. The storage modulus G' drops rapidly from 120 Pa to below 10 Pa within 300 seconds. This significant decrease in modulus quantifies the rapid loss of mechanical integrity as the hydrogel network collapses.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis of the coating surface, illustrating the spatial distribution of constituent elements.
summary: The EDS elemental distribution map presented in this panel demonstrates that the constituent elements are uniformly distributed across the coating surface. This analysis confirms the chemical homogeneity of the coating, indicating that the deposition process successfully achieved a consistent elemental composition throughout the analyzed surface area of the material.

caption: Magnetic force microscopy image of the Py square, showing the characteristic perpendicular domain wall alignment observed during the reduction of the applied field from saturation.
summary: This MFM image displays the magnetic domain wall alignment in a 5 μm Py square. The walls are nucleated perpendicular to the applied field. This configuration is part of a broader trend where increased Ar pressure during deposition leads to smaller magnetic domains and more complex end-domain structures within the squares.

caption: Detailed view of the HIP-1 neutron diffraction pattern, highlighting low-intensity reflections that correspond to the tetragonal intermetallic σ-phase.
summary: This focused view of the HIP-1 pattern reveals weak reflections characteristic of the tetragonal intermetallic σ-phase. These findings are consistent with precipitates identified in SEM analysis, confirming the presence of this specific intermetallic phase in the HIP-1 condition, which is not observed in the as-printed state.

caption: Homogenized 2D Voronoi diagram created by redistributing seeds to minimize areal differences between cells.
summary: This panel illustrates a homogenized 2D Voronoi structure achieved by redistributing the initial seeds. By minimizing the areal differences between individual cells, the tessellation achieves a more uniform morphology, which is essential for modeling materials that require a consistent and homogeneous structural representation.

caption: Fracture position of O atom-adsorbed HI γ″-Ni3Al, Ni3Ti, and Ni3Nb structures showing failure at the interfaces.
summary: Oxygen atom adsorption induces a change in the tensile fracture mechanism for HI γ″-Ni3Al, Ni3Ti, and Ni3Nb. The fracture positions are observed to shift from the slabs to the interfaces, demonstrating that the presence of oxygen atoms significantly weakens the interfacial bonding strength during the tensile deformation process.

caption: Hysteresis loops of biomimetic spider silk subjected to cyclic tensile strains ranging from 75% to 450% in 75% increments.
summary: This panel displays hysteresis tests performed on β-sheet-β-crystallite biomimetic spider silk. By applying cyclic tensile strains from 75% up to 450% with 75% intervals, the material's mechanical response is characterized. These stress-strain curves illustrate the energy dissipation behavior of the synthetic silk structure under varying levels of mechanical deformation.

caption: Cu 2p XPS spectra of the Cu 98.5 Ni 1.5 (1 1 1) electrode surface, showing binding energy peaks at 932.6 eV and 952.4 eV for Cu 2p 3/2 and 2p 1/2, respectively, across varying Ar+ sputtering durations from 0 s to 3400 s.
summary: Cu 2p XPS spectra for the Cu 98.5 Ni 1.5 (1 1 1) electrode are presented across different Ar+ sputtering times. The photoemissions for Cu 2p 3/2 and 2p 1/2 appear at 932.6 and 952.4 eV. Depth profiling analysis indicates that the intensity of these Cu emissions increases by 1.75 times after sputtering.

caption: Charpy impact energy as a function of average volumetric oxide spacing for as-printed Ni-Cr-Mo samples.
summary: Illustrating the impact energy relative to the average volumetric oxide spacing, this plot completes the analysis of oxide distribution effects. It shows how the three-dimensional spacing of oxide particles within the Ni-Cr-Mo matrix correlates with the measured Charpy impact energy, providing a comprehensive view of the material's mechanical behavior.

caption: Final state of the transverse domain wall after a 3 ns current pulse with a density of 3.4x10^12 A/m^2, showing displacement along the nanostrip.
summary: After applying a 3 ns current pulse with a density of 3.4x10^12 A/m^2, the transverse domain wall exhibits displacement along the 400 nm wide Au/Py/Ir nanostrip. This observation confirms that current pulses can induce domain wall motion, even when specific transformations of the wall structure are not observed.

caption: Load-displacement curves and indentation distribution patterns observed within planar grains.
summary: Load-displacement curves and indentation distribution patterns observed within planar grains. These mechanical test results characterize the local hardness and elastic modulus of the planar grain structure. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the material's response to nano-indentation, contributing to the overall summary of tested mechanical properties in the study.

caption: Exemplary unit cell geometries developed for the lattice structures in this study.
summary: This panel displays the fundamental unit cell geometries designed for the lattice structures investigated in this research. These geometric configurations serve as the building blocks for the additive manufacturing process, providing the structural basis for subsequent mechanical testing, finite element analysis, and the extrapolation of the design space.

caption: Full diffraction pattern of a LaB6 standard reference material collected at the ID31 beamline of the ESRF.
summary: This panel displays the full diffraction pattern of a LaB6 standard reference material, which was collected at the ID31 beamline of the ESRF. This pattern serves as an instrumental profile example, providing a baseline for characterizing peak shapes and evaluating the performance of the diffraction measurement setup.

caption: Power versus temperature plot for alloy 46 specimen, with the Curie temperature indicated by the average of the transition temperatures.
summary: Fig. 10(b) presents the power versus temperature plot for the alloy 46 specimen. The Curie temperature is identified by taking the average of the two transition temperatures observed in the data, and this value is clearly marked on the plot to represent the magnetic transition of the alloy.

caption: Temperature-dependent electrical conductivity of Bi2-xNixSe3 samples, showing a monotonic increase with Ni content from 101 S/cm to 424 S/cm at 300 K.
summary: Electrical conductivity of Bi2-xNixSe3 samples is plotted against temperature. The data demonstrates a monotonic increase in conductivity as the Ni content rises, specifically increasing from 101 S/cm for x = 0 to 424 S/cm for x = 0.20 at 300 K, indicating enhanced electronic transport properties with Ni doping.

caption: Isothermal section of the Al–O–Ti system at 1500 °C calculated using Thermo-Calc software, illustrating the absence of equilibrium between liquid TiAl and Ti oxides when in contact with alumina.
summary: This isothermal section of the Al–O–Ti system at 1500 °C, calculated via Thermo-Calc, demonstrates the thermodynamic stability of the system. Specifically, it reveals that liquid TiAl in contact with alumina does not reach equilibrium with any Ti oxides, providing a theoretical basis for understanding experimental observations in TiAl-alumina contact studies.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph showing the solidification cell boundaries in the C-HEA sample, characterized by a high density of dislocations.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the microstructure around solidification cells in the C-HEA sample. The cell boundaries are clearly decorated by a significant number of dislocations, indicating localized strain or defect accumulation during the solidification process as the cells grow continuously along the solidification direction.

caption: Temperature-dependent lattice parameters for Ti-Nb alloys containing 12at.% and 14at.% niobium, derived from ADP simulations.
summary: Temperature-dependent lattice parameters for 12at.% and 14at.% Nb alloys are presented, showing the evolution of the α″ structure. The ADP simulation results effectively reproduce the experimentally observed changes in the lattice parameters as temperature varies, validating the model's capability to capture the thermal behavior of these specific Ti-Nb alloy compositions.

caption: Interaction surface plot demonstrating the relationship between scanning speed and laser power regarding residual stress.
summary: The interaction surface between scanning speed and laser power is presented here to highlight their combined influence on residual stress. Analysis indicates that scanning speed exerts a more pronounced effect on the resulting stress than laser power, with the most significant influence observed specifically at a laser power of 320 W.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Cu-Ni system, highlighting the Cu-30Ni composition with a blue arrow.
summary: This binary phase diagram illustrates the complete solid-state solubility of copper and nickel across all compositions. The Cu-30Ni alloy is specifically marked with a blue arrow, indicating that under equilibrium or near-equilibrium cooling conditions, such as casting, no significant precipitation is expected within this solid solution system.

caption: Simulated diffraction pattern for the sigma Fe-Cr phase.
summary: This simulated diffraction pattern represents the sigma Fe-Cr phase. It is included in the comparative analysis to exclude the presence of this specific intermetallic phase, ensuring that the experimental diffraction spots are correctly attributed to the L21 phase rather than other potential secondary phases in the material.

caption: Storage modulus curves as a function of temperature for pure TPU and its bio-composites.
summary: Storage modulus curves illustrate the temperature-dependent stiffness of pure TPU and its bio-composites. This DMTA technique provides crucial information regarding the mechanical response of the materials across a temperature range. The comparative data highlights how the incorporation of bio-fillers influences the stiffness behavior of the TPU matrix.

caption: Luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) of emissions at 1626 and 1436 nm plotted against temperature, featuring the calibration curve, relative thermal sensitivity, and absolute thermal sensitivity.
summary: The LIR of IR emissions at 1626 and 1436 nm is plotted as a function of temperature, showing a high correlation coefficient of 0.998. The calibration curve, relative thermal sensitivity, and absolute thermal sensitivity are displayed, with a maximum relative sensitivity of 2.15 % K-1 observed at 22.8 °C.

caption: Perturbation plot showing the sensitivity of the height model to variations in individual process parameters.
summary: The perturbation plot provides a visual representation of how individual process parameters influence the predicted height. By isolating the effect of each variable, this plot allows for the assessment of model sensitivity and helps identify which specific input factors have the most significant impact on the final height output.

caption: Polarisation curves for drop cast electrode-based microbial fuel cells (MFCs) measured using a load-controlled technique.
summary: Polarisation curves for drop cast electrode-based microbial fuel cells are presented, illustrating the electrochemical performance of the system. These curves were obtained using a load-controlled measurement technique once the MFCs reached a steady open-circuit voltage, providing critical data on the power performance of the internally coated substrate setup.

caption: Feature selection results for Model IV, where 16 elements are selected excluding Na and Pb, achieving a mean CV score of 0.944.
summary: Model IV feature selection results show that excluding Na and Pb results in 16 retained elements with a mean cross-validation score of 0.944. By utilizing the top seven elements identified through SHAP analysis, the model is able to achieve an F1 score of 0.907 for its classification tasks.

caption: Pourbaix diagrams illustrating the formation enthalpies per surface area for various coverages of H, OH, O, and mixed H2O states on the (111) facet of Pd, Pd3Ni, and PdNi catalysts as a function of electrode potential.
summary: Pourbaix diagrams display the thermodynamically stable phases for Pd, Pd3Ni, and PdNi catalysts on the (111) facet. These diagrams, calculated via DFT, show the formation energy of various surface species including H, OH, O, and H2O as a function of electrode potential, identifying the most stable surface states.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of angiogenesis markers α-SMA and CD31 in tissues harvested 8 weeks after transplantation.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining provides visualization of α-SMA and CD31, which serve as critical markers for angiogenesis. Analysis of these tissues eight weeks post-transplantation shows that the expression of these markers is significantly elevated in the PCL/GelMA-Exos group, indicating enhanced vascularization compared to the control group.

caption: Corrosion parameters including corrosion current density and corrosion potential for Zn and Zn-based compositions derived via Tafel extrapolation.
summary: Corrosion current density and corrosion potential are calculated for Zn and Zn-based compositions using the Tafel extrapolation method. These quantitative parameters are critical for characterizing the electrochemical stability and corrosion susceptibility of the materials, providing a direct comparison of the degradation resistance across the different tested compositions.

caption: Full-field longitudinal strain map obtained via DIC for an upright-oriented 3D FFF-printed tensile specimen, showing strain concentration patterns prior to failure.
summary: This DIC strain map illustrates the longitudinal deformation of an upright-oriented 3D FFF-printed tensile specimen. The visualization captures the strain distribution across the sample surface just before the fracture point, demonstrating how the specific build orientation influences the mechanical strain localization and failure behavior of the printed composite.

caption: DMA trace of the cured CCF/epoxy composites, exhibiting a glass transition temperature of 279.24 °C derived from the tan(δ) peak.
summary: The DMA trace for the cured CCF/epoxy composites demonstrates the mechanical response of the material under thermal loading. A significantly high glass transition temperature of 279.24 °C is determined from the peak of the tan(δ) curve, indicating robust thermal performance for the composite system.

caption: Evolution of the L2-norm metric plotted against training iterations for both training and validation datasets.
summary: This plot illustrates the L2-norm progress during the training and validation process. By tracking the L2-norm values across iterations, the graph provides a visual representation of the model's convergence behavior, allowing for a direct comparison between the training performance and the validation performance throughout the machine learning optimization phase.

caption: Pseudo-time trajectory of endoderm lineage cells and UiPSCs showing a single branching point.
summary: This pseudo-time trajectory analysis clarifies the developmental progression of endodermal lineage cells at various differentiation stages. The plot illustrates the lineage relationship between UiPSCs and endoderm cells, highlighting a distinct branching point that serves as the foundation for understanding the subsequent differentiation pathways observed in the study.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction spectrum of a 5 mm rod produced from (Zr50Ti16.6Ni18.3Cu15)97S3 alloy via suction casting, showing a lack of Bragg reflections characteristic of an amorphous structure.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction data for the (Zr50Ti16.6Ni18.3Cu15)97S3 alloy 5 mm rod confirms its amorphous state. The integrated spectrum shows no traces of Bragg reflections, indicating that the suction casting process into water-cooled copper molds successfully produced a fully glassy structure for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Comparative force-displacement curves illustrating the correlation between experimental data and numerical simulation results.
summary: This plot compares the force-displacement curves derived from the experimental testing and the Simsolid numerical simulation. The alignment of these curves demonstrates the correlation between the physical flexural behavior of the lattice element and the predictive capabilities of the numerical model, validating the accuracy of the simulation approach.

caption: Finite element model schematic illustrating the cantilever geometry and the nanoindenter tip position, with dimensions provided in nanometers.
summary: This finite element model represents the cantilever geometry used to interpret load-displacement data within the linear elastic regime. The schematic includes specific dimensions measured from SEM images and indicates the nanoindenter tip position, facilitating the calculation of the oxide layer's Young’s modulus through combined experimental and simulation analysis.

caption: Mean absolute SHAP value summary plot for the GPR model predicting porosity.
summary: This summary plot ranks the importance of features for porosity prediction using GPR. The analysis indicates a distinct hierarchy of influence compared to height prediction, where laser power is the most significant feature, followed by scan speed, and lastly the feeding rate, demonstrating different sensitivities for the porosity model.

caption: Two-photon polymerization (2PP) setup designed for high-resolution microfabrication.
summary: This schematic details the two-photon polymerization setup, which is specifically engineered for high-resolution microfabrication. By utilizing a localized photopolymerization process, this system achieves sub-micron feature sizes, distinguishing it from standard SLA/DLP methods that typically operate at larger resolutions and layer thicknesses for additive manufacturing applications.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation density map of the annealed alloy, emphasizing localized density increases at grain and twin boundaries.
summary: Geometrically necessary dislocation density mapping in the annealed alloy shows that dislocation densities are concentrated near grain and twin boundaries following cryogenic deformation. This distribution pattern confirms that boundaries act as primary sites for dislocation accumulation, while the interior of the grains maintains a relatively low dislocation density.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of Live/Dead stained BMSCs and HUVECs after 3 days of culture, showing high cell survival rates with predominant green fluorescence and minimal red fluorescence across all scaffold groups.
summary: Live/Dead staining analysis of BMSCs and HUVECs cultured for 3 days reveals high cell survival rates across the BHP/G@Met, BHP, and G@Met groups. The images display predominant green fluorescence, indicating viable cells, with minimal red fluorescence, confirming that the scaffolds are non-cytotoxic and support healthy cell populations.

caption: HRTEM image of area C (interface region) showing the transition between phases, with an inset FFT pattern and a corresponding IFFT image.
summary: Area C represents the interface between the α and B2 regions of the AM-HEA. The HRTEM image, along with the FFT and IFFT analysis, visualizes the structural transition at the boundary, providing insight into how the FeCr and NiAl phases interact within the pristine material's microstructure.

caption: Stability curves comparing Ni1Co3@NC and benchmark Pt/C at a high current density of 50 mA/cm2 over time.
summary: The stability of Ni1Co3@NC is compared against the benchmark Pt/C catalyst at a high current density of 50 mA/cm2. This plot demonstrates the long-term durability and performance retention of the Ni1Co3@NC catalyst under sustained operating conditions, confirming its potential for practical electrochemical applications.

caption: Correlation analysis of defect sizes detected via 10 μm and 35 μm voxel size scans, featuring a parity plot with a black line representing perfect correlation and orange lines indicating the log-log correlation with 95% scatter bands and the corresponding Gaussian distribution.
summary: This parity plot compares defect size measurements obtained from 10 μm and 35 μm voxel size scans. The black line denotes perfect agreement, while the orange lines illustrate the log-log correlation with 95% confidence intervals and the Gaussian distribution of the logarithmic defect sizes, providing a statistical assessment of measurement consistency across resolutions.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of precipitates observed in the GH3536 superalloy, highlighting the distribution of Cr, Mo, and Mn.
summary: The EDS mapping analysis identifies the chemical composition of the precipitates present in the GH3536 superalloy samples. The results confirm that these secondary phases are primarily composed of chromium (Cr), molybdenum (Mo), and manganese (Mn), providing insight into the microstructural constituents that influence the fatigue fracture mechanism at 855 °C.

caption: Total energy of Al3Ni as a function of cell volume calculated at 0 K and 0 GPa.
summary: The total energy of Al3Ni is plotted against the corresponding cell volume at 0 K and 0 GPa. This relationship, derived from DFT calculations, provides the fundamental energy-volume data necessary for fitting the Birch-Murnaghan state equation to describe the material's thermodynamic properties at absolute zero.

caption: Mean squared error (MSE) progression over training epochs for scenario 4 of the PEOF-SNF artificial backpropagation network.
summary: This plot depicts the MSE progression for the fourth scenario, illustrating the model's learning efficiency. The small MSE measurements confirm the ANN technique's effectiveness in modeling periodic electroosmotic flow dynamics. The quantity of epochs used here was essential for achieving the observed convergence and ultimate performance of the network.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of a carbon fibre produced at 6.9 bar ethanol partial pressure and 13.4 bar total pressure, exhibiting a morphology comparable to the fibre grown at lower ethanol pressure.
summary: Captured via scanning electron microscopy, this carbon fibre was grown at 6.9 bar ethanol partial pressure and 13.4 bar total pressure. The image reveals a microstructure that is morphologically comparable to the fibre grown at 4.1 bar ethanol pressure, indicating consistent growth characteristics under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Elemental distribution map of Titanium (Ti) within the DED W–Ti–Cr–V alloy microstructure.
summary: This elemental composition map highlights the spatial distribution of Titanium within the DED-synthesized W–Ti–Cr–V alloy. It corresponds directly to the microstructure shown in panel A, allowing for the correlation of specific morphological features with the local chemical concentration of Ti throughout the specimen.

caption: Bode impedance plots illustrating the rapid increase in impedance moduli for DD6, DD6BM, and IC10 alloys as the frequency decreases.
summary: Bode impedance plots for DD6, DD6BM, and IC10 alloys in 10% NaNO3 solution show the frequency-dependent behavior of the impedance modulus. The data indicates that the impedance moduli for all three alloys increase rapidly as the frequency transitions from high to low, reflecting the electrochemical impedance characteristics of the passivation films.

caption: Bode plot representing the impedance magnitude and phase angle as a function of frequency for Alloy 690, measured after 15 hours of immersion in a pH 9.0 borate buffer solution.
summary: This Bode plot provides a frequency-dependent analysis of the impedance magnitude and phase angle for Alloy 690. Measured after 15 hours of immersion in a pH 9.0 borate buffer solution at corrosion potential, the data facilitates the characterization of the electrochemical interface and the determination of the oxide capacitance.

caption: Fourier transform infrared spectrogram of the 1ChCl:2Urea deep eutectic solvent electrolyte.
summary: The Fourier transform infrared spectrogram of the 1ChCl:2Urea electrolyte is presented in this panel. This spectroscopic analysis serves to characterize the chemical structure of the solvent system, providing a baseline for subsequent electrochemical investigations involving the addition of nickel and tungsten salts to the electrolyte mixture.

caption: Diamond unit cell topology used for scaffold construction.
summary: The diamond unit cell is presented as a constitutive topology for the scaffold design. This specific geometric arrangement functions as a fundamental unit cell, contributing to the overall structural properties of the scaffolds as depicted in the topology representation of the constitutive unit cell provided in the research.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 2 fabricated via screen printing.
summary: This panel presents the reflection coefficient of antenna design 2 manufactured through screen printing techniques. Plotted via Origin software, the graph characterizes the signal reflection behavior of the screen-printed antenna, allowing for a direct comparison of its performance against other fabrication methods described in the study.

caption: Current spectrum (CS) map for the valley at 0.24 V, showing the electronic current distribution at this specific bias condition.
summary: This current spectrum map corresponds to the valley at 0.24 V in the RTD device. It provides a visualization of the current distribution alongside the LDOS, with the conductance band minima and average potential energy indicated by white dashed and black dash-dot lines, respectively, to characterize the device's electronic behavior.

caption: Equilibrium molar volume fraction of the BCC_B2 phase in the MoNbTaW equiatomic alloy as a function of temperature.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the equilibrium molar volume fraction of the BCC_B2 phase for the MoNbTaW equiatomic alloy across varying temperatures. The data confirms the formation of a solid solution with a melting temperature of 3158 K (2885 °C), aligning with established literature and phase formation assessments for this quaternary system.

caption: Maximum atomic and electronic temperatures for 50 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFeCr.
summary: Maximum atomic and electronic temperatures for 50 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFeCr are presented for twelve individual events. These findings quantify the peak thermal conditions experienced by the NiFeCr system, reflecting the impact of 50 keV energy deposition on the atomic and electronic temperature profiles during the simulation.

caption: Comparison of hardness values across various material states, illustrating the evolution of mechanical properties.
summary: This figure presents a graphical depiction of the hardness evolution across different material states. The data provides a comparative overview of mechanical performance, highlighting how specific processing conditions or material states influence the resulting hardness values, which serves as a key indicator of the material's mechanical integrity and structural response.

caption: Phase fraction diagram for 0.7 wt% dissolved nitrogen, where the high nitrogen content promotes a γ-first solidification path, with austenite forming at the liquidus and minor transient δ-ferrite appearing at lower temperatures.
summary: Simulated for a 0.7 wt% dissolved nitrogen condition, this diagram confirms a γ-first solidification path. Austenite forms directly at the liquidus, while δ-ferrite emerges only transiently at lower temperatures in minor amounts. This illustrates the significant influence of high nitrogen content on the solidification behavior and secondary phase formation.

caption: Mirror plot displaying the experimental HRMS/MS spectrum of phenylglyoxylic acid leached from Saremco print CROWNTECH specimens into artificial saliva (top) alongside the reference spectrum of an authentic standard (bottom).
summary: This mirror plot provides a comparative analysis of the HRMS/MS spectrum for phenylglyoxylic acid, a major leachable identified in Saremco print CROWNTECH specimens. By aligning the experimental spectrum from artificial saliva incubation with an authentic standard, the identity of the leachable compound is definitively verified through spectral matching.

caption: Dark-field STEM micrograph of the HT-2 sample highlighting the distribution of secondary phase precipitates within the restored martensitic structure.
summary: This dark-field STEM micrograph of the HT-2 sample provides a clear visualization of the secondary phase precipitates formed during the restoration of the martensitic structure. The image complements the HAADF data by consistently depicting the precipitate structure and their spatial distribution relative to the martensitic laths and packets.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram displaying the frequency of powder diameters, with characteristic D10, D50, and D90 values of 28 μm, 41.2 μm, and 60.7 μm, respectively.
summary: Particle size distribution histogram displaying the frequency of powder diameters, with characteristic D10, D50, and D90 values of 28 μm, 41.2 μm, and 60.7 μm, respectively. These values, as shown in Fig. 2 (b), provide a quantitative assessment of the powder feedstock consistency required for uniform layer deposition during printing.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for the Al–Fe binary system, defining the thermodynamic stability regions for the alloy design.
summary: The Al–Fe binary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic framework for the alloy design process. It maps the stability regions of various phases within the Al–Fe system, which is essential for understanding the microstructural evolution and precipitation behavior during the casting process as described in the alloy design concept.

caption: Comparative cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+ in 0.1 M KCl at a fixed scan rate of 25 mV s-1, contrasting the electrochemical response of additively manufactured electrodes printed from AuNP-CO (red), CO (blue), and commercial (black) filaments.
summary: This panel compares the electrochemical activity of three different electrode filaments at a scan rate of 25 mV s-1. The Randles-Ševčík plot inset confirms that the redox process remains diffusion-controlled for all tested electrode types, allowing for a direct performance comparison between the AuNP-CO, CO, and commercial filaments.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the anomaly detection results for the Claude 3.5 Sonnet model when processing G-code data.
summary: The confusion matrix for Claude 3.5 Sonnet demonstrates the model's capability to detect G-code anomalies under a deterministic evaluation framework. By mapping predicted versus actual anomaly labels, this visualization quantifies the model's classification precision and recall, offering insight into its effectiveness for automated G-code analysis and error detection.

caption: Discontinuity magnitude map of the inclusion agglomerate region during the first loading cycle, with red arrows highlighting initial void nucleation sites.
summary: Representing the first loading cycle, this discontinuity magnitude map identifies local regions where void nucleation has occurred due to inclusion decohesion and fracture. Red arrows explicitly mark these nucleation events, providing insight into the early-stage damage mechanisms within the agglomerate region under mechanical stress.

caption: Correlation between yield strength and unstable stacking fault energy (γUSFE) for the investigated MEAs, with blue and yellow trendlines representing random and ordered alloy states, respectively.
summary: Yield strength is plotted against the unstable stacking fault energy to evaluate the validity of their correlation in these MEAs. The results demonstrate that the typically assumed linear relationship between these two parameters does not hold for the investigated alloys, as indicated by the distinct trendlines for random and ordered states.

caption: Friction coefficient profile recorded for the HT-18Ni300 sample.
summary: This panel displays the friction coefficient profile for the heat-treated 18Ni300 sample. By evaluating the COF over the duration of the test, the plot characterizes the wear resistance and frictional stability of the heat-treated material, allowing for a direct comparison with other processing methods used in the study.

caption: Phase stability prediction for the W-CoCrNi system, demonstrating the sensitivity of phase formation to varying tungsten content.
summary: Valence electron concentration analysis reveals that the phase stability of the CoCrNi system with tungsten is highly sensitive to the W content. This sensitivity suggests that precise control over tungsten concentration is required to prevent the formation of undesirable phases at the interface during the alloy design process.

caption: FTIR-ATR spectra comparing PVBC, CMPSF, PVBC-MPy, and the series of AEMs labeled M-1# through M-8#, all analyzed in the Cl- form.
summary: This figure presents the FTIR-ATR spectroscopic analysis of various anion exchange membranes, specifically PVBC, CMPSF, PVBC-MPy, and the M-1# to M-8# series. All membrane samples were prepared and tested in the Cl- form to characterize their chemical composition and structural features through the observed infrared absorption patterns.

caption: Calculated damage profile in displacements per atom (dpa) as a function of proton penetration depth for an amorphous Zr matrix, derived using SRIM with the quick Kinchin-Pease model (Ed = 40 eV) for 2 MeV proton irradiation. The plot highlights specific depths of 0.5 μm (1.5 dpa) for APT needles and 12 μm (2.3 dpa) for TEM foils, alongside the Bragg peak at 29 μm.
summary: This simulation plot illustrates the proton-induced damage profile in an amorphous Zr matrix, showing dpa values versus penetration depth. Key experimental extraction depths are marked: 0.5 μm for APT needles and 12 μm for TEM foils, with the Bragg peak identified at 29 μm, providing context for the irradiation damage analysis.

caption: Full-pattern neutron powder diffractogram of the HIP-3 treated specimen, capturing the diffraction profile after the third stage of hot isostatic pressing.
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction pattern for the HIP-3 condition. As part of the comprehensive analysis of the WAAM material, it contributes to the global assessment of phase evolution, complementing localized microscopy results by providing volume-averaged information on the stability of the austenite and ferrite phases.

caption: Powder number density (p n) distribution at the processing plane for G33 condition, illustrating the influence of varying powder feeding rates (F).
summary: The p n distribution at the processing plane for G33 shows how powder feeding rate affects convergence. Compared to lower feeding rates below 6.7 g/min, the powder stream exhibits increased convergence at higher feeding rates, demonstrating a clear dependency of the spatial distribution on the input powder mass flow.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) maps derived from EBSD scans of COM-2024-T3, COM-2024-SS, and FE-2024 studs, illustrating microstructural variations across different zones including top center (TC), top edge (TE), bottom center (BC), bottom center +6.5 mm (BC+6.5), and flash (FL).
summary: Inverse pole figure maps visualize the microstructural evolution of 2024 aluminum alloy studs following friction surfacing. Scans taken at the tip of the consumed studs, specifically in the BC and BC+6.5 friction zones, reveal significant grain refinement compared to the base material, with additional refinement observed within the flash regions.

caption: Bar chart comparing the elastic modulus (E) and hardness (H) values for SLM, cast, and SPS samples.
summary: Quantitative analysis of the elastic modulus reveals a clear progression among the samples. The SPS-processed material achieves the highest modulus of approximately 200 GPa, which is attributed to its fully dense microstructure and fine equiaxed grains that facilitate efficient stress transfer compared to the SLM and cast counterparts.

caption: Histogram illustrating the distribution of recomputed stress values (Pa) across various tri-layer model configurations, highlighting the similarity in stress levels between partially and fully bonded cases for configurations 2 and 5.
summary: This histogram displays the distribution of recomputed stress values in Pascals for multiple tri-layer model configurations. Analysis indicates that for specific configurations, such as 2 and 5, there is no significant difference in stress values between partially and fully bonded conditions, demonstrating consistent mechanical behavior across these bonding states.

caption: Shear stress amplitude evolution for the primitive TPMS lattice under multiaxial strain-controlled loading.
summary: This graph displays the shear stress amplitude evolution for the primitive TPMS lattice during multiaxial strain-controlled loading. It captures the cyclic shear response, which is essential for understanding the torsional component of the combined loading regime and its influence on the overall mechanical performance of the primitive lattice structure.

caption: Microstructural EPMA point analysis of B4C CoCrFeMnNi HEC, focusing on the chemical composition of cell boundaries and interiors.
summary: Focusing on the B4C CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy, this panel provides EPMA point analysis data to examine the chemical composition of cell boundaries and interiors. These measurements are critical for understanding the partial elemental decomposition of B4C nano-particles, which is a key phenomenon observed during the DED processing of these materials.

caption: Raman spectrum of the cleaned 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode, demonstrating a relative increase in the magnitude of graphitic and polymer-related peaks.
summary: After the cleaning process, the Raman spectrum of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode shows a relative increase in the magnitude of the peaks at 2680 cm-1 and 2928 cm-1. These peaks represent the 2D-band of graphitic structures and C-H stretching vibrations, respectively, indicating successful activation of the electrode surface.

caption: Isothermal magnetization virgin curves of a Pr2Co2.8Si0.2 sample piece, illustrating the magnetic response under varying field conditions.
summary: This plot displays the isothermal magnetization virgin curves for a Pr2Co2.8Si0.2 sample. The data reveals a complex magnetic behavior characterized by a series of distinct jumps in the M(H) curves. These observations indicate significant magnetic transitions occurring within the material as the external magnetic field is applied.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from nano-indentation testing on the 90° sample.
summary: Mechanical response of the 90° sample is characterized by these load-displacement curves. Similar to the 0° sample, the data indicates a significant strain hardening effect below the cut surface, resulting from high dislocation density and associated strain field interactions, as evidenced by the derived nano-hardness measurements.

caption: Comparative micro-Raman analysis of the DLC-based film inside the wear track versus the debris collected along the track edges.
summary: Raman analysis of debris around the wear scar reveals a more pronounced D-band compared to the as-deposited films, which is characteristic of disordered graphite. This indicates that debris graphitization occurred during the wear process, whereas the coating itself inside the wear track remained unaffected by tribochemical changes.

caption: Higher magnification bright field TEM micrograph showing slip dislocations in B2 austenite generated by forward martensitic transformation under 700 MPa stress.
summary: Captured at higher magnification, this bright field TEM micrograph illustrates the high density of slip dislocations within the B2 austenite phase. These defects were generated through the forward martensitic transformation process induced by cooling the 15 ms NiTi #1 wire under a significant stress of 700 MPa.

caption: Tafel curves illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of wrought, uncoated DMLS, NiAl-coated, and NiCr-coated Ti64 specimens in a 3.5% NaCl medium.
summary: Tafel plots demonstrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of wrought, uncoated DMLS, NiAl-coated, and NiCr-coated Ti64 specimens tested in a 3.5% NaCl medium. These curves serve as the primary data source for extrapolating electrochemical corrosion parameters, providing a comparative visual representation of the corrosion resistance across the four distinct specimen conditions.

caption: FTIR absorption spectra of PGTA polymer before and after scCO2 extraction at 140 bars and 40°C for 2 hours, normalized to the C=O peak at 1720 cm-1.
summary: FTIR spectra of PGTA demonstrate that the C=O peak at 1720 cm-1 remains stable after scCO2 extraction. However, the reduction in C=C bond stretching at 1637 cm-1 and C=CH2 at 810 cm-1 indicates post-curing. The absence of -OH groups above 3000 cm-1 confirms the samples are moisture-free.

caption: Fatigue life curves for SLM Co28Cr6Mo samples, contrasting the effects of machining and polishing surface treatments.
summary: SLM Co28Cr6Mo fatigue life is enhanced by surface modification, with machining providing a 60% increase and polishing providing a 40% increase. These improvements correlate with significant reductions in surface roughness, specifically a 30x reduction for machining and a 27x reduction for polishing compared to the as-built state.

caption: Comparison of median fatigue S-N curves for Ti-6Al-4V specimens processed under 800HIP, 920HIP, and 1050+920HIP conditions against historical rotating bending fatigue data from polished literature specimens.
summary: This plot displays median fatigue S-N curves for Ti-6Al-4V under various HIP conditions, benchmarked against historical rotating bending fatigue data. By excluding defect-prone literature samples, the comparison highlights that smaller colony sizes and the absence of continuous grain boundaries contribute to the superior fatigue performance of the 800HIP and 920HIP conditions.

caption: Microhardness measurements of Al–5Cu–1.2Fe and Al–5Cu–1.2Fe–1Ni alloys displayed relative to secondary dendrite arm spacing.
summary: Microhardness data for the Al–5Cu–1.2Fe and Al–5Cu–1.2Fe–1Ni alloys are plotted as a function of secondary dendrite arm spacing. This plot is part of a systematic mechanical property analysis, providing a comparative view of the hardness characteristics of these two alloy compositions based on their microstructural dendrite spacing.

caption: UV–vis transmittance spectra of the 3D-printed glass wafer, with an inset photograph demonstrating the high optical clarity and transparency of the fabricated glass material.
summary: The optical properties of the 3D-printed glass wafer are characterized by UV–vis spectra. The data, complemented by an inset photograph showing the wafer's high clarity, confirms the excellent optical transparency of the printed glass, which is a critical requirement for the intended applications of the glass MMD.

caption: Calculated energy barriers for NH dehydrogenation and N recombination steps across 15 different NiM alloys, categorized by transition metal (d) and main group metal (MG) dopants.
summary: This panel presents DFT-calculated energy barriers for NH dehydrogenation and N recombination steps across 15 NiM alloys, including metals like Sc, Ti, V, and Sn. These calculations provide essential data for evaluating the catalytic activity of various Ni-based alloy surfaces in the specified reaction processes.

caption: Dispersion diagrams illustrating the real and imaginary components of the propagation constant μ = kd for a 1D periodic system.
summary: This dispersion diagram displays the propagation characteristics of a 1D periodic system by plotting the real and imaginary parts of the propagation constant μ, defined as kd. The visualization provides a comprehensive overview of the wave behavior within the periodic structure, highlighting the relationship between the wave vector and the system's dispersion properties.

caption: Tafel curves derived from ORR polarization data, comparing the reaction kinetics of Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocage, nanocube, Co-Ni@NC, and Pt/C.
summary: Tafel analysis demonstrates that the Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocage possesses more rapid reaction kinetics with a lower Tafel slope of 76 mV/dec. This value is significantly lower than those of the Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocube (93 mV/dec), Co-Ni@NC (109 mV/dec), and commercial Pt/C catalysts (88 mV/dec).

caption: Atomic configuration of Alloy III, featuring blue Ni atoms and green Cr atoms.
summary: This panel presents the atomic structure of Alloy III, characterized by the distribution of blue Ni atoms and green Cr atoms. The model serves as a visual reference for the alloy's atomic configuration, facilitating a comparative understanding of the structural characteristics across the different alloy variants studied.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for the first ASA recycling course sample, displaying flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus as functions of temperature.
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for the first ASA recycling course sample are presented, displaying flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus as functions of temperature. These DMA test results characterize the viscoelastic properties of the material, providing essential data on the mechanical response of the recycled polymer across varying thermal conditions.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the impedance characteristics of SLM 316L stainless steel manufactured at a laser scanning speed of 1200 mm/s after 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution.
summary: This Nyquist plot depicts the electrochemical impedance response of SLM 316L stainless steel fabricated at a laser scanning speed of 1200 mm/s. The plot captures the material's electrochemical performance after 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution, highlighting the influence of the 1200 mm/s processing parameter on corrosion resistance.

caption: Current-time measurements corroborating the voltage response patterns for HP, NHP, and ICA@G/NHP scaffolds, highlighting current output stability after 14 days of conditioning.
summary: Current-time measurements corroborate the voltage response patterns, showing that NHP and ICA@G/NHP scaffolds produce significant alternating currents. The ICA@G/NHP scaffold maintains a current output of 10–12 nA after 14 days of physiological conditioning, representing a 60–65% retention of the initial current generation, consistent with the observed voltage stability.

caption: Transmittance values at 405 nm for composite resins containing various concentrations of S-CNCs and A-CNCs, comparing the optical performance of both particle types.
summary: Transmittance at 405 nm is plotted for composite resins with various S-CNC and A-CNC concentrations. The data confirms a significant reduction in the transparency of S-CNC/CTFA compared to A-CNC/CTFA, emphasizing the improved optical performance and dispersibility achieved by using acrylated CNCs within the composite resin formulation.

caption: CAD model of the zig-zag truss-made beam featuring a BCC unit cell architecture.
summary: The CAD model illustrates a zig-zag truss-made beam design based on BCC unit cells. This structure, measuring 80 x 8 x 8 mm, incorporates a 91% overall porosity and a strut thickness of 0.84 mm, establishing the theoretical foundation for the subsequent printing and sintering processes of the lattice beam.

caption: Evolution of FCC and BCC phase volume fractions in FeNiCoCrAl alloy during sequential milling steps.
summary: Sequential milling of FeNiCoCrAl shows significant phase transformation dynamics. Starting from 100% BCC, the addition of Fe and Ni introduces FCC phases, while subsequent Cr addition destabilizes these FCC phases, reducing their volume fraction to 27.72%. This demonstrates the critical role of specific alloying elements in modulating phase stability during processing.

caption: Primary and secondary creep rates plotted against structural non-uniformity, showing an exponential acceleration effect on primary creep.
summary: Primary and secondary creep rates are plotted against structural non-uniformity in H282 microstructures. The results reveal an exponential acceleration effect on primary creep, which is attributed to an increased volume fraction of precipitate-free open regions within the material as structural non-uniformity increases during the phase-field simulation process.

caption: WDS elemental mapping of Cobalt (Co) and Nickel (Ni) distribution within the PS 3 coating cross-section.
summary: The WDS elemental maps for Cobalt and Nickel illustrate their distribution within the PS 3 coating cross-section. Similar to the oxygen mapping, these elements appear to be mixed homogeneously throughout the coating structure. This uniform distribution contrasts with the observed segregation of aluminum, providing a comprehensive view of the coating's chemical composition.

caption: Relationship between k σ s and m σ s parameters for the β-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy at different temperatures.
summary: Depicted here is the correlation between k σ s and m σ s parameters for the β-phase of the Ti6Al4V alloy. The plot demonstrates the temperature-dependent behavior of these parameters within the β-phase, allowing for a comparative analysis of mechanical characteristics between the different phases of the alloy.

caption: Strain-time histories for the tested structures, demonstrating the homogenization of superficial deformations at 15 m/s impact velocity.
summary: Strain-time histories for the meta-skin cladded samples are presented, showing how a threefold increase in projectile velocity homogenizes superficial deformations. These results differ significantly from lower-velocity tests, emphasizing the high sensitivity of the structural mechanics to impact velocity despite maintaining a nearly consistent impact energy across the different sample configurations.

caption: Two-nanometer thick slice of the atom probe tomography 3D reconstruction for the CRSA750 condition, displaying superimposed Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni ion maps.
summary: This 2 nm thick slice of the atom probe 3D reconstruction for the CRSA750 condition reveals the spatial distribution of Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni ions. The superimposed ion map clearly demonstrates the enrichment of Ni and Al elements within the globular L1 2 precipitates dispersed throughout the matrix.

caption: Temperature-dependent Gibbs free energy of formation for Zr2Cu and ZrO2 calculated via FactStage software.
summary: This plot illustrates the standard Gibbs free energy of formation (ΔGf°) for Zr2Cu and ZrO2 across a temperature range of 100 to 2000 K. Calculated using FactStage software, the data reveals that ΔGf° for ZrO2 spans approximately −1101 kJ/mol to −729 kJ/mol throughout this thermal range.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the CALPHAD-based ICME framework designed to predict the yield strength of WAAM Haynes 282 following single-step aging treatments.
summary: This flowchart outlines the integrated computational materials engineering framework used to model the yield strength of WAAM Haynes 282. By incorporating CALPHAD-based data, the framework accounts for intrinsic strengthening, grain boundaries, solid solution effects, and γ′ precipitation, utilizing established physical models like Hall-Petch and Galindo-Nava to quantify these individual strengthening contributions.

caption: Complex structure sample after pyrolysis at 1000 ℃.
summary: This panel shows a photograph of the complex structure sample following pyrolysis at 1000 ℃. The image illustrates the state of the material after the thermal treatment, allowing for a direct visual comparison with the green body to observe any structural changes resulting from the high-temperature processing.

caption: Absorption cross-sections of HF, CO2, H2O, and O2 plotted against wavelength from 1250 to 1350 nm.
summary: Presented here are the absorption cross-sections for HF, CO2, H2O, and O2 in the 1250 to 1350 nm range, based on Hitran database simulations. Concentrations for CO2, H2O, and O2 are scaled by factors of 300, 300, and 210,000, respectively, to visualize their relative spectral contributions.

caption: Raman spectra of FeCoNiMo and CrCoNiMo worn surfaces at 600 °C, featuring experimental data, deconvoluted peaks, and cumulative peaks.
summary: Raman spectra obtained from wear tracks at 600 °C characterize the oxide products formed during sliding. Comparing these results with unworn regions confirms that wear-induced variations in oxidation occur, specifically promoting molybdate formation. This analysis provides insight into the tribo-chemical changes occurring on the alloy surfaces at elevated temperatures.

caption: GND map of the CR10-DA specimen displaying increased dislocation density and emerging stress concentrations compared to the ST-DA condition.
summary: Following a 10% pre-strain treatment, the CR10-DA specimen shows an increase in GND density. The GND map indicates that stress concentrations begin to develop and become more uniform near grain boundaries and within the grains, reflecting the structural response to the applied pre-strain condition.

caption: Atomic resolution HAADF-STEM image of the 920HIP condition, illustrating the phase boundary characteristics.
summary: Atomic resolution HAADF-STEM imaging of the 920HIP condition demonstrates the structural characteristics of the material after this specific processing. Compared to the 800HIP condition, this sample exhibits a lower amount of dislocations, which is attributed to the reduced number of intergranular interfaces present in the 920HIP microstructure.

caption: Structural sample visualization illustrating a failure in automated defect detection, characterized by the presence of purple voxels that require manual labeling alongside pink voxels identified by the automated tool.
summary: This 3D reconstruction shows a structural sample where the automated labeling tool fails to correctly identify all defects. Pink voxels indicate regions detected by the tool, while purple voxels represent areas requiring manual labeling. This highlights the tool's limitation in accurately labeling more complex defective structures compared to simpler ones.

caption: UV–Vis-NIR absorbance spectra comparing TOCN and LPNC-3 evaporators, demonstrating the light absorption characteristics of the materials.
summary: UV–Vis-NIR spectroscopy reveals the light absorption profiles of TOCN and LPNC-3 evaporators. Results indicate that pure TOCN exhibits relatively low light absorbance across a broad wavelength range, whereas the LPNC-3 material shows enhanced optical properties, highlighting the impact of lignin incorporation on the light-harvesting capability of the evaporator.

caption: High-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) pattern acquired from the as-deposited iHEA sample.
summary: This high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern characterizes the structural state of the as-deposited iHEA sample. The diffraction data provides essential information regarding the crystalline nature and phase composition of the material in its initial deposited state, as presented in the experimental analysis of the iHEA specimen.

caption: Comparison of the isotropic 31P NMR peak obtained via the MAS insert experiment at 11 T (black) against the isotropic peak measured using a conventional solid-state MAS stator and probe at 7 T (red).
summary: The isotropic 31P NMR peak from the MAS insert experiment at 11 T is compared to a reference spectrum acquired at 7 T using a standard solid-state MAS NMR setup. This comparison highlights the performance and spectral characteristics of the MAS insert method relative to conventional solid-state NMR hardware.

caption: Overview of the ZORTRAX-M300 Plus 3D printer utilized for the experimental study.
summary: This photograph displays the ZORTRAX-M300 Plus printer, which serves as the primary equipment for the proposed methodology. The device is located at the production and materials laboratory at Yarmouk University in Irbid, Jordan, and is used to facilitate the experimental procedures described in the research study.

caption: Grain reference orientation deviation (GROD) map for the AB + HT alloy, where black lines denote HAGBs and white lines represent low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs).
summary: The GROD map for the AB + HT alloy reveals significant misorientations within many grains, characterized by an inhomogeneous spatial distribution. Black lines represent HAGBs, while white lines highlight LAGBs. This map demonstrates the internal strain and dislocation density present in the alloy's microstructure prior to any applied deformation.

caption: Low-magnification HAADF-STEM micrograph of a cross-sectional TEM lamella extracted from the laser-peened surface, revealing depth-dependent microstructural features.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph provides a low-magnification view of a cross-sectional TEM lamella lifted from the laser-peened surface. It serves to characterize the recast layer and the underlying microstructure, illustrating the depth-dependent nature of the material's structural evolution following the laser-peening process.

caption: Conceptual model of a TiCnm particle shell agglomerate functioning as an insulating wall of thickness dTiC, illustrating the thermal gradient between the laser-heated outer TiCnm surface (TTiC) and the shielded interior AlSi7Mg0.6 particle surface (TAl).
summary: This schematic illustrates the insulating behavior of TiCnm particle shell agglomerates during laser absorption. The outermost TiCnm particles reach high temperatures (TTiC) due to high absorptivity, while the interior AlSi7Mg0.6 surface remains shielded at a lower temperature (TAl), resulting in delayed heat input and slower cooling of the underlying material.

caption: Tafel plots for various austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys measured in [P66614][Tf2N] ionic liquid at 80 °C, illustrating the electrochemical polarization behavior.
summary: This Tafel plot displays the electrochemical polarization behavior of austenitic stainless steels and nickel-based alloys tested in [P66614][Tf2N] ionic liquid at 80 °C. These plots are essential for determining corrosion potentials, as referenced in the study, and demonstrate the current response during anodic and cathodic polarization cycles.

caption: Principal component analysis of spectral reflectance data for MJT specimens, showing a cumulative percentage variance of 90.71% with 95% confidence ellipses.
summary: Principal component analysis of spectral reflectance data for MJT specimens, showing a cumulative percentage variance of 90.71% with 95% confidence ellipses. The PCA results suggest two principal components of PC1 and PC2, which adequately explain the observed behavior in the spectral data for the MJT specimens.

caption: Wear volume and wear rate of Al0.3CrFeCoNi-based coatings evaluated under air conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the wear performance of Al0.3CrFeCoNi-based coatings in air. The Al0.3CrFeCoNi coating exhibits the highest wear volume and wear rate among the tested samples, indicating that the addition of alloying elements like Mo and Nb significantly improves the wear resistance of the base alloy under dry conditions.

caption: Spatial distribution of microhardness values across the cross-section of the deposited layer and the adjacent substrate region.
summary: This microhardness map illustrates the mechanical property distribution across the cross-section of the deposited layer and the adjacent substrate. The visualization provides a clear representation of the hardness variations resulting from the deposition process, allowing for an assessment of the mechanical integrity and transition characteristics between the layer and substrate.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of a Ni electrode in 0.50 M KOH solution containing methanol concentrations ranging from 0.05 M to 1.00 M at a scan rate of 50 mV s−1.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms for a Ni electrode in 0.50 M KOH with varying methanol concentrations (0.05 M to 1.00 M) at 50 mV s−1 are shown. As methanol concentration increases, the Ni(OH)2 oxidation peak gradually disappears, being overtaken by a significant increase in current density associated with the methanol oxidation reaction.

caption: Excitation and fluorescence spectra of doped, UV-cured solid resin disks prepared by the non-hydrolytic pathway, with excitation collected at 380 nm.
summary: This panel shows the photophysical properties of doped, UV-cured solid samples synthesized via the non-hydrolytic route. The excitation spectra, recorded at 380 nm, exhibit a strong signal in the 280-340 nm range, indicating PPO excitation and demonstrating the material's optical performance following the specific curing and doping process.

caption: Atomic configuration of the Al/Al3Ni interface constructed with the LowIndex-2 orientation, featuring a distinct interface termination plane parallel to the repeating unit structure.
summary: Representing the LowIndex-2 orientation, this atomic model illustrates an alternative interface termination plane for the Al/Al3Ni system. By maintaining the same lattice misfit as other models, this configuration allows for a systematic investigation into how varying termination planes affect the overall interfacial energy of the simulated material system.

caption: Dark-field TEM image focusing on the transformed region of the sample sintered at 1300 °C for 1 minute.
summary: This dark-field TEM image highlights the transformed area within the specimen sintered at 1300 °C for 1 minute. By isolating specific diffraction conditions, the image provides a clear visualization of the transformed phases present in the reaction zone, offering insight into the microstructural changes induced by the HPHT sintering process.

caption: Total dissipated energy (Edtot) measured after 3600 cycles of wear testing for samples prepared with various scanning strategies.
summary: The total dissipated energy (Edtot) after 3600 cycles is shown for samples with varying scanning strategies. This metric provides a cumulative measure of energy loss throughout the duration of the wear test, serving as a characteristic value to assess the long-term tribological performance and durability of the different material samples.

caption: Calculated isopleth of the Cu-Ni-Pb ternary system at a constant Cu:Ni ratio of 1.00, showing the liquidus temperature as a function of lead content compared to experimental data from [52] and previous parameter sets [43, 44].
summary: This isopleth diagram illustrates the liquidus temperature for the Cu-Ni-Pb system at a fixed Cu:Ni ratio of 1.00. The solid line represents the current study's calculation, which shows better agreement with experimental data from [52] compared to the lower liquidus predictions derived from previous parameter sets [43, 44].

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the middle region of the slow deposition along the <011> Al zone axis, illustrating a dispersion of needle-like precipitates with diameters of approximately 20 nm.
summary: Observations of the middle region of the slow deposition via bright-field STEM show a distinct dispersion of needle-like precipitates. These features, oriented along the <011> Al zone axis, possess a characteristic diameter of approximately 20 nm, contrasting with the finer features observed in the top region of the deposit.

caption: Oxygen concentration profile measured by EDS along the cross-section of the ODL sample, showing a gradual decrease from the surface toward the substrate.
summary: Oxygen concentration profile measured by EDS along the cross-section of the ODL sample, showing a gradual decrease from the surface toward the substrate. This profile indicates a gradual reduction in oxygen content as the distance from the surface increases, reflecting the distribution of oxygen within the ODL sample cross-section.

caption: Pole figure representing the crystallographic texture of the center region of the HCT sample compressed at 927 °C with a strain rate of 0.01s⁻¹.
summary: Representing the center region of the HCT sample, this pole figure shows the texture development after compression at 927 °C and 0.01s⁻¹. The data reveals specific texture characteristics unique to the center region, which differ from those observed in the top and bottom sections of the deformed specimen.

caption: Actual photographic documentation of the IN718 inserts and thermocouples installed inside the sand mold at the foundry.
summary: The photograph captures the physical implementation of the experimental setup at the foundry. Machined IN718 inserts and thermocouples are shown correctly positioned within the sand mold cavity. This visual record confirms the initial pouring conditions and validates the practical execution of the setup described in the virtual model.

caption: Surviving Ni, Fe, and Cr interstitials in a NiFeCr alloy following a 50 keV classical MD cascade simulation at 80 ps.
summary: This panel displays the surviving interstitial defects in a NiFeCr alloy after a 50 keV classical MD cascade simulation at 80 ps. The visualization highlights the spatial distribution of Ni, Fe, and Cr interstitials, providing a baseline for comparing damage evolution against models incorporating electronic stopping and 2T-MD effects.

caption: Yield strength (Rp0.2) plotted against total elongation (At) for AB-x alloys compared to literature data for Ti-6Al-4V.
summary: Yield strength values are plotted against total elongation to evaluate the mechanical behavior of AB-x alloys. By benchmarking these results against the gray area representing Ti-6Al-4V literature data, the plot illustrates the relative yield performance and ductility of the AB-x material under tensile loading conditions.

caption: HT-CLSM image of K439B alloy dendrite growth at a cooling rate of 50 °C·min⁻¹, with nucleation occurring at 1311.3 °C.
summary: Solidification of K439B alloy at a cooling rate of 50 °C·min⁻¹ is visualized via HT-CLSM, revealing a dendrite nucleation temperature of 1311.3 °C. As the dendrites grow, they reject residual liquid into an interconnected network within the interdendritic regions, which are marked by blue dashed lines to illustrate the partitioning process.

caption: Derivative of magnetization with respect to temperature (dM/dT) plotted against temperature for HT NiMnSn alloys, used to determine the Curie temperature (Tc).
summary: The dM/dT versus temperature plot for HT NiMnSn alloys allows for the precise determination of the Curie temperature (Tc). Analysis of these curves demonstrates that variations in chemical composition and homogeneity among the samples have a minimal effect on the observed Tc values for the investigated alloys.

caption: Representative immunofluorescence images of MCF10A 3D cultures stained for F-actin, β-catenin (polarity marker, cyan), and laminin (basement membrane, yellow) at 10 μm scale.
summary: High-resolution immunofluorescence imaging of MCF10A 3D cultures highlights the structural organization of the acini-like aggregates. Staining for F-actin, the polarity marker β-catenin, and the basement membrane component laminin provides evidence of organized epithelial morphogenesis and the establishment of cell polarity within the ox-ALG-RGD-PVGLIG hydrogel environment.

caption: Three-dimensional rendering of the corner fatigue crack geometry relative to the distribution of solidification gas pores within the hybrid laser welded AA7020-T651 specimen.
summary: A 3D rendering displays the spatial relationship between the nucleated corner fatigue crack and the solidification gas pores in the AA7020-T651 specimen. The visualization confirms that numerous pores become entrained by the crack, which acts as a catalyst for accelerated crack growth as the crack intersects these internal defects.

caption: Comparison of predicted and actual viscosity values, showing consistent trend alignment between the model output and experimental data.
summary: The parity plot for viscosity displays the predicted versus actual values, illustrating that the model effectively captures the underlying variations in the data. The observed trend consistency confirms the model's overall adequacy in predicting viscosity, aligning with the performance observed across the other response variables in the study.

caption: Final stage of the tool cutting into the γ′ phase at 100 m/s, where increased tool displacement leads to local dislocation and stacking fault formation.
summary: Depicting the final stage of the tool cutting into the γ′ phase at 100 m/s, this MD snapshot shows the effect of increased tool displacement. As the tool progresses, a few local dislocations and stacking faults appear, demonstrating the microstructural response to the continued mechanical loading within the γ′ phase.

caption: Scatter plot showing the relationship between the hardness contribution (ΔH) and the measured hardness of the cladding alloy.
summary: The scatter plot displays the correlation between the hardness contribution (ΔH) and the total hardness of the cladding alloy. This visualization helps characterize the influence of specific strengthening mechanisms on the material's hardness, providing a quantitative assessment of how these factors contribute to the overall mechanical hardening of the cladding.

caption: Experimental stress-strain curve for V-specimens subjected to tension, highlighting specific observation points used for Bayesian inference.
summary: This panel displays the experimental stress-strain curve for V-specimens under tension. Observation points are marked with specific color-coded symbols to represent different mechanical stages, including visco-elastic and visco-plastic regimes. These points are utilized for Bayesian inference, with a higher density of observations taken during the visco-plastic stage.

caption: Microstructural overview of Mg–6Zn powders held at 480 °C for 50 min, displaying similar particle morphology to the 440 °C condition with increased Mg powder encapsulation.
summary: Increasing the temperature to 480 °C results in minimal microstructural changes compared to the 440 °C sample. The Mg–6Zn powders retain their general morphology, though observations indicate that a greater proportion of Mg powders undergo encapsulation, as highlighted by the cyan marks representing the melted Zn phase.

caption: Fracture mechanics analysis for F35 composites, showing the ratio of interface to fiber fracture toughness (Γi/Γf) versus the elastic mismatch parameter (α) across varying infiltration cycles and interface-to-matrix toughness ratios (β).
summary: This graph evaluates the fracture behavior of F35 composites by plotting the interface-to-fiber fracture toughness ratio against the elastic mismatch parameter. The boundary curve, derived from Eq. 16, effectively delineates regions of crack deflection from crack penetration, providing insight into the toughening mechanisms influenced by infiltration cycles and interface properties.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded at 50 mV s-1 for 1 mM dopamine in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) using additively manufactured working electrodes printed from AuNP-CO (red), CO (blue), and commercial (black) filaments.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry at 50 mV s-1 evaluates the electrochemical performance of additively manufactured electrodes in 1 mM dopamine solution. The AuNP-CO filament (red) demonstrates superior performance compared to the CO (blue) and commercial (black) filaments, highlighting the enhanced electroanalytical capability provided by the gold nanoparticle-incorporated material in the phosphate-buffered saline environment.

caption: EDS compositional map of the CMT-WAAM sample following API heat treatment, demonstrating a more uniform distribution of Nb, Mo, Fe, and Cr elements and partial dissolution of the dendritic substructure.
summary: This EDS compositional map displays the CMT-WAAM sample microstructure after API heat treatment. Compared to the AMS treatment, this condition results in a more uniform distribution of Nb, Mo, Fe, and Cr throughout the matrix. Additionally, the analysis indicates that the dendritic substructure has undergone partial dissolution during this process.

caption: Inverse prediction parity plot for screw speeds, comparing predicted and actual values across training and test samples with an R² of 0.745.
summary: Inverse prediction of screw speeds for the training and test samples is shown in Fig. 3 (e). The evaluation of the trained model on the test dataset yielded an R² value of 0.745 for the inverse prediction of screw speeds, reflecting the model's performance in determining process parameters from target outputs.

caption: Transformation temperatures (TTs) plotted against stress levels for samples V1 and V5, highlighting the influence of scanning speed on phase transition.
summary: This panel displays the transformation temperatures for samples V1 and V5 across different stress levels. The data shows a consistent trend in how scanning speed affects the thermal transformation characteristics of the material. The anchor point is highlighted in black to facilitate clear interpretation of the thermal data.

caption: Surface morphology of the W-DED Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy under low heat input conditions, showing irregular surface features.
summary: Under low heat input conditions, the surface morphology of the W-DED Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy exhibits significant irregularities.
