This plot evaluates the shielding performance of the materials against gamma radiation, with the linear absorption coefficient serving as the primary metric for comparing the effectiveness of each alloy.

caption: Axial strain evolution plotted against shear strain for Specimen W9, illustrating the accumulation of axial strain during cyclic shear loading.
summary: During cyclic shear loading of Specimen W9 at a constant axial stress of 150 MPa, axial strain gradually accumulates. This observed phenomenon is identified as multiaxial ratchetting, caused by the development of plastic strain along the normal direction of the yield surface as the shear strain amplitude increases.

caption: Normalized magnetic hysteresis loops for the //3Py/3Pt sample, measured by sweeping an external magnetic field along the in-plane easy (y) and hard (x) axes to characterize magnetic anisotropy.
summary: Normalized magnetic hysteresis loops for the //3Py/3Pt sample are shown for both the easy (y) and hard (x) axes. These measurements, obtained via MPMS, demonstrate the magnetic anisotropy of the sample. The loops confirm that even a minimal 50 Oe field is sufficient to initialize the magnetization direction along the axes.

caption: High-magnification HAADF-STEM image of the Al-Zn-Cr specimen, showing the detailed substructure and the region selected for elemental mapping along the <110> zone axis.
summary: High-magnification HAADF-STEM imaging of the Al-Zn-Cr specimen provides a detailed view of the substructure along the <110> zone axis. This region serves as the basis for subsequent elemental mapping, confirming the presence of a cell structure and the specific localization of Zn particles at both cell boundaries and interiors.

caption: Elemental composition analysis of the DL Ni coated etched SS310 substrate after 500 h of immersion, indicating a nickel percentage of approximately 12–15%.
summary: Elemental composition analysis of the DL Ni coated etched SS310 substrate after 500 hours of immersion shows a nickel percentage of approximately 12–15%. This result, consistent with the plain substrate, demonstrates that the nickel coating effectively persists on the etched surface, helping to prevent the out-diffusion of constituent metal ions.

caption: Reliability index of an additively manufactured titanium alloy wheel hub plotted against the number of impact cycles under comprehensive braking conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the fatigue reliability index of an additively manufactured titanium alloy wheel hub subjected to comprehensive braking impacts. The data demonstrates that the reliability index of the component exhibits a gradual decline as the number of impact cycles increases, reflecting the progressive degradation of the wheel hub's structural integrity.

caption: SRIM-simulated energy loss profiles (MeV/μm) plotted against penetration depth for alpha particles with initial energies ranging from 6.5 MeV to 10 MeV.
summary: Energy loss profiles for alpha particles are depicted as a function of depth using SRIM simulation data. The plot demonstrates the characteristic energy deposition behavior for particles within the 6.5 MeV to 10 MeV range, highlighting how energy loss varies as the particles penetrate deeper into the target material medium.

caption: Raman spectrum of monolayer MoS2 displaying characteristic E2g and A1g vibrational modes with a frequency separation of 20.5 cm-1, alongside LO(M) and ZO(M) peaks indicating film polycrystallinity.
summary: This Raman spectrum characterizes the monolayer MoS2 film through its primary vibrational modes, E2g and A1g, which exhibit a frequency difference of 20.5 cm-1. Additionally, the presence of LO(M) and ZO(M) peaks in the spectrum provides evidence of the polycrystalline nature of the synthesized MoS2 film.

caption: Evolution of the HCP phase fraction as a function of true stress for horizontal and vertical samples, derived from sequential Rietveld refinement of 1D HEXRD profiles.
summary: Panel b illustrates the transformation kinetics of the HCP phase during deformation. By performing sequential Rietveld refinement on 1D HEXRD profiles, the HCP phase fraction is plotted against true stress for both sample orientations. This reveals how the phase composition evolves dynamically in response to the applied tensile load.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map of Ta in the as-deposited sample, showing clear segregation between dendrites.
summary: Ta displays significant segregation in the interdendritic regions of the as-deposited sample. This distribution pattern provides a clear outline of the dendrites, as Ta acts as a refractory element that participates in the formation of the eutectic gamma-gamma-prime phase alongside Al and Ti during the late solidification stage.

caption: Thermal strain versus temperature curves illustrating the parallel (αp) and normal (αn) coefficients of thermal expansion for the composite material.
summary: Thermal strain is plotted against temperature to demonstrate the anisotropic expansion characteristics of the glass fiber reinforced PA6,6 cover. The curves represent the parallel and normal coefficients of thermal expansion, αp and αn, which are critical parameters derived from manufacturer datasheets for modeling thermal expansion effects in the material.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph obtained using a superlattice reflection, visualizing spherical L1 2 precipitates with a size scale of approximately 25 nm in the grain interior.
summary: The dark-field TEM micrograph, captured using a superlattice reflection identified in the diffraction pattern, highlights the distribution of spherical L1 2 precipitates. These precipitates, located in the grain interior, exhibit a refined size scale of approximately 25 nm, contributing to the overall precipitation strengthening of the SA750 condition.

caption: Storage and loss modulus curves for pure PLA measured at 185 °C, demonstrating the absence of a G′ and G″ crossover at low frequencies.
summary: Pure PLA modulus curves measured at 185 °C over a frequency range of 0.02–625 rad/s are shown. The results confirm that no crossover between G′ and G″ occurs at low frequencies for this base material, consistent with the behavior observed in the unmodified PLA-PBAT and Lotader-modified blends.

caption: Tabular representation of the specific process parameters applied during the layering deposition of the IN625 material.
summary: This table outlines the precise process parameters employed during the layering deposition of IN625. By documenting these specific settings, the figure provides the necessary technical framework for the deposition procedure, ensuring that the experimental conditions are clearly defined and reproducible for the study of the resulting material properties.

caption: Nozzle and arbitrary sensor configuration relative to the robot trajectory.
summary: This schematic illustrates the physical arrangement of a nozzle and an arbitrary sensor positioned along a robot trajectory. It serves as a foundational representation for defining the end effector coordinate frame, which is essential for tracking the spatial orientation of components during the robotic movement process.

caption: Three-dimensional representation of a multilayered anisotropic system consisting of N rectangular layers with nonlocal thermoelastic properties and imperfect internal interfaces.
summary: This schematic illustrates a three-dimensional multilayered structure composed of N bonded orthotropic, dissimilar, linearly thermoelastic, and rectangular layers. The model incorporates nonlocal effects and accounts for general imperfect conditions at the internal interfaces between the layers, providing a theoretical framework for analyzing complex anisotropic thermoelastic systems.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscope morphology of the top surface of an optimized truncated-pyramid component produced via the IIRI prediction model.
summary: This confocal laser scanning microscope image shows the top surface of a truncated-pyramid component optimized by the IIRI prediction model. Unlike the regular sample, this surface demonstrates high quality, showing no noticeable defects such as spheroidization or voids, which confirms the effectiveness of the IIRI model in improving surface integrity.

caption: Curie temperature characteristics showing saturation magnetization (Ms) versus temperature from 300 K to 1,000 K for the D30 HEA and FeMnZn.
summary: This plot reveals the thermal stability of magnetic properties, where traditional ferrites lose saturation magnetization near 600 K. In contrast, the D30 high-entropy alloy maintains a saturation magnetization of 22.8 emu/g at 1,000 K, demonstrating significantly better performance and suitability for high-temperature electromagnetic shielding applications compared to commercial ferrites.

caption: Normalised peak intensities of {111}, {200}, {220}, and {311} lattice planes at the end of the biaxial loading stage.
summary: The plot depicts the normalised peak intensities at the conclusion of the biaxial stage. Results show a decrease in {111} and {200} intensities at 5° azimuthal angle, suggesting texture weakening, while the {200} reflection increased at 85°, indicating texture strengthening during the final biaxial loading phase.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves comparing NiTi alloy samples across different groups, illustrating the influence of energy density on transformation temperatures.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for group I NiTi alloys demonstrate that transformation temperatures increase with rising energy density when a single independent variable is considered. These DSC results, which allow for the determination of enthalpy changes through area integration, confirm that the phase transformation temperature Af increases with higher laser energy density.

caption: Photoluminescence emission profiles for 0.1 wt% CD-doped HDPE samples at each recycling step under 254 nm excitation, illustrating that the presence of CDs does not alter the characteristic spectral shape.
summary: PL spectra for samples containing 0.1 wt% CDs are displayed for each recycling step. The results reveal that the presence of CDs does not affect the spectral shape of the emission profile. This observation is expected, as the CDs themselves exhibit very weak emission when excited at the 254 nm wavelength.

caption: Simulated TTR diagram for the AM state at 750 °C compared with experimental data.
summary: This panel displays the time to rupture (TTR) diagram for the AM state at 750 °C. It features a comparison between simulated results, represented by solid lines, and experimental data, shown as dashed lines, to validate the accuracy of the simulation model in predicting rupture behavior under these specific conditions.

caption: Optical microscopy image of as-built Ti55511 revealing surface and densification quality.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the surface and densification features of the as-built Ti55511 alloy. The results indicate that the optimized laser parameters achieved relative densities over 99.5%, with a surface roughness of 7.69 ± 0.43 μm, confirming the material's structural integrity following the laser powder bed fusion fabrication process.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulation results comparing interfacial energy trends in systems with and without graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs).
summary: Molecular dynamics simulation results demonstrate the evolution of interfacial energy in systems containing graphene nanoplatelets compared to those without. These computational findings align with the trends observed in experimental shear tests, confirming the significant influence of GNPs on the interfacial energy characteristics within the investigated material systems.

caption: Fourier transform of the Co K-edge EXAFS spectra for Co/ZrO2 and Co1Ni1/ZrO2 catalysts, showing a shoulder feature on the Co-metal scattering path.
summary: Fourier transform Co K-edge EXAFS spectra are shown for Co-based catalysts after 10 h of DRM. The Co catalyst exhibits a distinct shoulder on the left-hand side of the Co-metal scattering path, providing evidence of structural changes or light element interaction compared to the bimetallic Co1Ni1/ZrO2 catalyst.

caption: ANOVA statistical summary table for Pusu river water flow rate at 8.8 L/min.
summary: This table presents the two-factor ANOVA results for the Pusu river at a flow rate of 8.8 L/min. Statistical analysis indicates that the diameter ratio and inclination angle are highly significant factors, as evidenced by P-values of 0.000, confirming their critical influence on the observed water flow performance.

caption: Cr 2p XPS spectrum revealing the presence of metallic Cr(0) and surface chromium oxide (Cr2O3).
summary: The Cr 2p spectral region reveals two chromium species: metallic Cr(0) at approximately 573.4 eV and surface chromium in the form of Cr2O3 at approximately 576.4 eV. This indicates that the chromium on the surface exists in both its elemental metallic state and as a stable oxide.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image showing slip bands traversing cellular boundaries.
summary: This TEM image reveals slip bands passing through cellular boundaries within the grain interior. These boundaries are observed to slow down, but not completely obstruct, the deformation process. This evidence confirms the role of cellular boundaries as barriers that hinder, yet allow for, dislocation motion during material deformation.

caption: Parity plot illustrating the correlation between predicted and actual flexural strength values using the Random Forest + ANN hybrid model.
summary: Flexural strength predictions are visualized in this parity plot to demonstrate the agreement between the Random Forest + ANN model outputs and experimental measurements. This visual assessment complements the numerical evaluation, providing insight into the model's ability to accurately capture the target property across the tested range.

caption: Schematic representation of the hanging drop method for spheroid formation, including the microtiter plate insert setup and a representative optical micrograph of a HT-144 spheroid.
summary: This panel illustrates the experimental workflow for generating HT-144 melanoma spheroids using a hanging drop method. The schematic details the microtiter plate insert configuration, while the accompanying optical micrograph confirms the successful formation of a 3D spheroid structure, providing a baseline for subsequent drug treatment and analysis studies.

caption: Atomic lattice configuration of the Ni foam slab before and after structural compression.
summary: The Ni foam slab lattice structure is shown before and after compression by a water nano-hammer. Prior to damage, the structure comprises FCC, amorphous, and HCP phases with respective proportions of 46.4%, 11.1%, and 42.5%. This visualization helps characterize the structural changes resulting from the nanobubble collapse process.

caption: EDS spectrum acquired at high magnification, demonstrating that the beta-phase is confined to a limited fraction of the observed area.
summary: The EDS spectrum confirms the chemical composition of the observed features at high magnification. The analysis reveals that the beta-phase is confined to a limited fraction of the observed area, providing compositional evidence that supports the microstructural observations of discrete, localized beta-phase precipitation within the Ti64 alloy matrix.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles for Ni–Cu coated electrodes electrodeposited at -1.8 V in Ethaline ionic liquid, tested at current densities of 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, and 1 mA cm⁻².
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for Ni–Cu alloy films electrodeposited at -1.8 V in Ethaline ionic liquid are displayed. The electrodes were subjected to varying current densities ranging from 0.125 mA cm⁻² to 1 mA cm⁻². These results characterize the electrochemical performance and charge storage behavior of the specific alloy film composition.

caption: Current-Voltage (I-V) characteristic curves of the KC 200GT PV module recorded at 25 °C for distinct solar irradiance conditions.
summary: Current-Voltage (I-V) curves illustrate the electrical performance of the KC 200GT PV module at 25 °C under varying solar irradiance. Observations confirm that the current output peaks at 1000 W/m2 and shows a consistent decline corresponding to the reduction in incident insolation levels.

caption: Glass transition temperature (Tg) evolution for TCNF/PLA composite during the ageing process.
summary: The glass transition temperature of TCNF/PLA composites is tracked throughout the ageing period. Determined at the storage modulus onset point, these Tg values reflect the thermal response of the cellulose nanofiber-reinforced polymer. The results illustrate how the reinforcement influences the thermal transition behavior of the PLA matrix during ageing.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus actual yield strength values for the top-performing SVR model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the predictive accuracy of the SVR model for yield strength. By contrasting predicted values against actual experimental data from the test set, the visualization demonstrates the model's satisfactory performance and high prediction accuracy in capturing the mechanical behavior of the examined material dataset.

caption: Creep rupture life comparison of four distinct alloys tested at 765°C / 565 MPa and 982°C / 151 MPa for specimens in the vertical orientation.
summary: This bar chart displays the creep rupture life of four alloys in the vertical orientation under two distinct temperature and stress conditions. The 738_STD alloy exhibits the highest rupture time across all conditions. Error bars indicate low variance between duplicate samples, confirming the reliability of the experimental creep rupture results.

caption: Monkman-Grant plot illustrating the relationship between SPCT and uniaxial creep test data, with m and p parameters estimated according to Eq. (2).
summary: The Monkman-Grant plot presents a comparative analysis of SPCT and uniaxial creep test data. Parameters m and p are estimated using the provided Eq. (2) to characterize the creep behavior. This plot serves to validate the consistency of SPCT results against standard uniaxial creep testing methodologies across the tested conditions.

caption: Nyquist diagram showing the electrochemical impedance response of AA2195 aluminum alloy, TC4 titanium alloy, and AA2195/TC4 composites, characterized by capacitive arcs in the medium-to-low frequency range and an inductive feature.
summary: The Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of AA2195, TC4, and their composite. It reveals distinct capacitive arcs within the medium-to-low frequency region, accompanied by a notable inductive feature, providing insight into the electrochemical characteristics and surface processes occurring on these materials during the impedance spectroscopy measurements.

caption: Isometric view of a cubic porous structural unit measuring 10 mm by 10 mm by 10 mm.
summary: This panel displays a cubic unit cell representing the fundamental geometry of a porous structure. The model is defined by specific dimensions of 10 mm on each side, providing a clear visualization of the structural unit's spatial extent and cubic symmetry before any further computational processing or discretization is applied.

caption: Equilibrium dislocation configuration for a b = a/2 [011] shear loop expanding in a (1-11) plane under an applied tensile stress of 400 MPa.
summary: Representing the dislocation loop configuration at 400 MPa, this simulation snapshot demonstrates the structural response of the shear loop to increased tensile stress. The dislocation maintains its equilibrium state within the misfit stress field, providing insight into how higher applied loads influence the expansion of the loop before cross-slip.

caption: Chronocoulometric Q-t curves and corresponding Q-t^1/2 linear plots for a bare GCE in 0.1 M PBS, showing responses in the absence of analytes (a, a'), with 0.3 μM AC (b, b'), and with 1 μM RT (c, c').
summary: Chronocoulometric analysis of a bare GCE in 0.1 M PBS reveals charge-time behavior and linear Q-t^1/2 relationships. Data is presented for the blank electrolyte and in the presence of 0.3 μM AC or 1 μM RT, demonstrating the electrochemical response characteristics of the bare electrode surface under these specific conditions.

caption: Computer-aided design models displaying length, width, and height annotations for three two-dimensional density gradient (2DDG) honeycombs compared to their uniform density regular (UD) counterparts.
summary: Computer-aided design models are presented for three distinct specimen types, comparing two-dimensional density gradient honeycombs with uniform density regular honeycombs. These models provide precise length, width, and height annotations, serving as the foundational geometry for subsequent structural analysis and performance evaluation of the designed honeycomb specimens in the study.

caption: Internal friction and dynamic modulus spectra for the FMS3 alloy during a complete martensitic transformation cycle, showing a distinct modulus drop at 160 K associated with the paramagnetic to anti-ferromagnetic transition.
summary: The FMS3 sample exhibits internal friction and dynamic modulus curves during cooling and heating cycles. A notable drop in the dynamic modulus at 160 K indicates a paramagnetic to anti-ferromagnetic transition. This sample shows a smaller transformed fraction, likely due to its smaller average grain size compared to other alloys.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the dendrite core in as-cast RR3010, displaying the spatial distribution of Cr, Al, Co, Ni, Re, and Ta atoms.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the dendrite core in as-cast RR3010, displaying the spatial distribution of Cr, Al, Co, Ni, Re, and Ta atoms. This map reveals blocky, irregular γ’ precipitates within the dendrite core, with the γ’ phase demarcated by Al, Ni, and Ta, while the γ matrix is enriched in Cr, Co, and Re.

caption: Comparative load-displacement curves for FeTi and Fe2Ti intermetallic compounds doped with Co, Cr, and Ni alloying elements.
summary: The indentation load-displacement curves for FeTi and Fe2Ti intermetallic compounds doped with Co, Cr, and Ni are shown to evaluate the influence of these alloying elements. The results demonstrate the variation in load response during nanoindentation, which is critical for understanding the impact of alloying on the plastic toughness of IMCs.

caption: Specific cutting energy consumption measured across different thermo-mechanical configurations, highlighting the inverse relationship between cutting temperature and energy requirements during chip formation.
summary: Specific cutting energy is analyzed across diverse thermo-mechanical conditions. Data show a consistent drop in energy consumption when transitioning from low-temperature to high-temperature configurations. This trend is observed in both low-speed and high-speed ranges, with high-speed/high-temperature conditions showing a 28–30% reduction in energy compared to high-speed/low-temperature configurations.

caption: Comparison of absorption peak frequencies between GMSs and AMMs across the first- and second-order interference ranges.
summary: This comparison illustrates that the first-order interference EAP is customizable between 4.22–7.22 GHz, while the second-order EAP is tailored between 12.74–18 GHz. The absorption peak frequencies for AMMs generally cluster near the center of these respective ranges, providing a baseline for evaluating the frequency-tuning capabilities of GMSs.

caption: Frequency distribution histogram of GND values for the LPBF ZGH4142 specimen, illustrating the prevalence of high dislocation density.
summary: This histogram quantifies the GND value distribution for the LPBF ZGH4142 specimen. The data confirms a high dislocation density of 1.1 × 10 14 m −2, reflecting the significant residual stress levels and dislocation formation resulting from the localized thermal-mechanical stresses inherent in the LPBF manufacturing process.

caption: EPMA cross-section elemental distribution map of Bulk B FeCoNiMnCr porous high-entropy alloy oxidized at 900 °C for 8 hours.
summary: Bulk B displays the cross-sectional elemental distribution following 8 hours of oxidation at 900 °C. EPMA analysis confirms the presence of Cr-rich and Mn-rich oxide layers. The color-coded map, ranging from blue to red, illustrates the concentration gradients of elements across the porous high-entropy alloy sample matrix.

caption: Tafel polarization curve illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of Inconel 625 samples.
summary: Tafel polarization curve illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of Inconel 625 samples. This plot provides a quantitative assessment of the corrosion kinetics for the material, serving as a primary diagnostic tool to evaluate the electrochemical stability and degradation characteristics of the Inconel 625 specimens under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of hb-PFAEK-Allyls illustrating the chemical environment of the polymer structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of hb-PFAEK-Allyls is shown to characterize the molecular structure of the material. This spectroscopic analysis provides detailed insights into the proton environments within the polymer backbone and side chains, confirming the successful synthesis and chemical identity of the hb-PFAEK-Allyls sample through distinct resonance signals.

caption: Frequency-dependent induced charge Q ind (ω) on a quantum point contact (QPC) modeled with d = 1 μm, illustrating a significant resonance peak between 10 and 30 GHz and a persistent high-frequency tail exceeding 10⁻³ e near the ballistic band at approximately 125 GHz.
summary: This simulation illustrates the frequency-dependent induced charge on a quantum point contact with a separation of 1 μm. The results reveal a pronounced resonance band between 10 and 30 GHz, while maintaining a high-frequency response tail above 10⁻³ e near the ballistic band at approximately 125 GHz.

caption: EBSD grain distribution map of TC4 alloy Specimen A1, showing the microstructure after deep cryogenic treatment.
summary: Specimen A1 displays the grain distribution following deep cryogenic treatment (DCT). EBSD analysis reveals that DCT drives the migration of low-angle grain boundaries from the grain boundary plane into the grain interior. This process increases the proportion of low-angle boundaries, contributing to the observed microstructural optimization and significant grain refinement.

caption: Combined TGA and derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) curves showing the gradual mass loss of PEEK up to 800 °C, with a peak decomposition rate observed between 550 °C and 600 °C.
summary: The TGA-DTG graph displays the thermal degradation behavior of PEEK up to 800 °C. A gradual mass loss is observed throughout the heating process, with the derivative curve highlighting a distinct peak in the decomposition rate occurring within the 550–600 °C temperature range.

caption: Friction coefficient evolution of Fe0.6Ni0.7CrAl MPEAs recorded throughout the repetitive sliding process.
summary: This plot presents the friction coefficient files of Fe0.6Ni0.7CrAl MPEAs as they evolve throughout the repetitive sliding process. The data illustrates the stability and magnitude of the friction coefficient over time, serving as a key indicator of the material's frictional behavior and wear resistance under the tested sliding conditions.

caption: Hardness evolution for AB and AB + HT samples as a function of equivalent strain extended to a range of 208.
summary: Hardness changes for both AB and AB + HT samples are tracked against equivalent strain up to 208. The data shows an initial increase in hardness to approximately 3330 MPa at a strain of 0.7, followed by a slight decrease to values between 2970 MPa and 3120 MPa at a strain of 1.4.

caption: Live/dead staining micrograph of Saos-2 cells co-cultured with PAMS hydrogel, highlighting predominantly live cell populations.
summary: Following calcein-AM/PI staining, this micrograph reveals the density and health of Saos-2 cells in the presence of the PAMS hydrogel. The imaging results predominantly show live cells, confirming that the hydrogel environment supports cell survival and maintains high biocompatibility compared to the control group under the same conditions.

caption: 3D morphology of SLM-fabricated 316L steel in the as-built room temperature (RT) condition.
summary: This panel displays the 3D morphology of SLM-fabricated 316L steel in the as-built room temperature condition. Analysis of the wear mark reveals significant material accumulation at the edges, which serves as a clear indicator of severe plastic deformation occurring during the dry sliding wear process.

caption: Enthalpy change (ΔHi) plotted against temperature for the Ni50.53Mn33.65In15.82 sample, with an inset highlighting the coexistence interval for pulses B at a higher resolution.
summary: Panel b illustrates the enthalpy change (ΔHi) versus temperature for the Ni50.53Mn33.65In15.82 sample, calculated using the provided equation. An inset is included to enlarge the coexistence interval for pulses B, with the vertical axis scale reduced by a factor of 100 compared to the main plot for clarity.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for Chamaerops humilis (CH) filler, showing mean fiber lengths of approximately 10 μm and widths near 5 μm, with rare larger particles identified.
summary: The particle size distribution for Chamaerops humilis (CH) is displayed, indicating mean fiber lengths around 10 μm and widths close to 5 μm. Although particles approximately 300 μm in length and 450 μm in width were identified, they occur with low statistical significance, as confirmed by the morphometric analysis.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field STEM image of the unmodified AlSi10Mg alloy.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field STEM imaging of the unmodified AlSi10Mg alloy highlights the atomic number contrast within the microstructure. This technique effectively visualizes the intercellular Si-rich eutectic phase and Mg segregation at the solidification cell boundaries, confirming the typical microstructural features present in the unmodified AlSi10Mg alloy samples.

caption: Boxplots and swarm plots illustrating the percentage deviation of Poisson's ratio from the mean, defined as 100(ν - νmean)/νmean, across the sampled simulation patches.
summary: Representing the mechanical consistency of the material, this panel shows the distribution of Poisson's ratio deviations. The combination of boxplots and swarm plots highlights the range and density of the simulated data, providing a clear visualization of how individual patches deviate from the calculated mean Poisson's ratio value.

caption: High-resolution Ti 2p XPS spectrum of the immersed specimen, revealing the coexistence of Ti 3+ and Ti 4+ oxidation states within the surface oxide layer.
summary: High-resolution XPS analysis of the Ti 2p region for the immersed AM TiZrNb-O specimen shows contributions from both Ti 3+ and Ti 4+ oxidation states. This suggests the coexistence of sub-oxide and oxide species, such as Ti2O3 and TiO2, within or beneath the newly formed surface deposit.

caption: Atomic representation of a 4 × 4 × 4 supercell constructed from a Zeolite ID DFT unit cell.
summary: This panel displays the atomic structure of a 4 × 4 × 4 supercell derived from a Zeolite ID DFT unit cell. The modeling procedure utilized VESTA software to convert the single unit cell into this expanded supercell configuration, illustrating the sequential structural modeling process applied to representative zeolite frameworks.

caption: Bode diagram representing the phase angle response for the 1# cathode modified alloy.
summary: The Bode diagram for the 1# cathode modified alloy shows the phase angle as a function of frequency. Similar to the base alloy, this sample exhibits only one distinct plateau peak, confirming that the electrochemical impedance of this modified alloy is governed by a single time constant during testing.

caption: Microhardness evolution of Ni55Ti42(Hf, Zr)3 alloys during 100 h of heat treatment at 400 °C.
summary: This panel displays the microhardness evolution of Ni55Ti42(Hf, Zr)3 alloys during a 100 h heat holding treatment at 400 °C. Experimental results indicate that the hardness values for all tested alloys remained above 670 HV, showing no significant decrease compared to the initial state after solution treatment.

caption: Load-displacement response of 3D-printed notched specimens subjected to single-edge notched beam (SENB) 3-point bending tests.
summary: The load-displacement curves presented here characterize the fracture toughness of 3D-printed samples. By utilizing single-edge notched beam testing under 3-point bending, the plot provides essential data to evaluate the fracture behavior and mechanical integrity of the printed components under localized stress conditions.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the in-situ micro-impacting process occurring during material deposition.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the fundamental mechanism of the in-situ micro-impacting process as it occurs during the deposition phase. The visualization provides a clear conceptual framework for understanding how micro-scale impacts are integrated into the deposition workflow, effectively capturing the dynamic nature of the process described in the research.

caption: Principal component analysis of unit cell architectures (SDF), colored by the L2 relative error for local field predictions.
summary: This visualization shows the principal component analysis of unit cell architectures, with data points colored to reflect the L2 relative error for local field predictions. This analysis helps determine whether the accuracy of local field predictions depends on the underlying geometric features of the unit cell architectures.

caption: Performance comparison between RNN and CNN models, showing the reduction in prediction error over training iterations and the superior efficacy of the RNN architecture.
summary: To explore the efficacy of RNN and CNN as forward prediction models, their performance was analyzed by minimizing prediction errors. The comparative results demonstrate the clear advantage of using an RNN over a CNN, as the RNN achieves lower prediction errors during the training process for the material dataset.

caption: Phase-field profiles and progressive phase fraction evolution during the solidification of a melting pool.
summary: This panel presents phase-field simulation results illustrating the solidification process within a melting pool. Under the coupled effects of thermal radiation and convection, solidification initiates at the top, causing the solid-liquid interface to contract. As solidification progresses, damage propagates in the central region, while circumferential damage forms at the periphery due to heat conduction.

caption: Surface mesh representation of the simulated structure containing a 40% atomic defect concentration.
summary: This panel presents a surface mesh schematic of the simulated material model at a 40% atomic defect concentration. The visualization highlights the structural changes and surface mesh topology associated with this increased level of atomic defects, demonstrating the impact of higher defect density on the simulated surface geometry.

caption: Selected-area electron diffraction pattern of a second carbide-containing area in the HIP sample.
summary: Selected-area electron diffraction pattern of a second carbide-containing area within the HIP sample. By analyzing this diffraction data alongside the bright-field images, researchers can identify and distinguish between the two types of carbides present, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of the phase evolution induced by the HIP treatment.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of the SCI for sample B-2, highlighting the susceptibility profile during terminal solidification.
summary: Sample B-2 presents the SCI profile calculated via Thermo-Calc for the terminal solidification stage. This simulation evaluates the variation in cracking susceptibility within the melt pool region. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the solidification cracking behavior for the nickel-based superalloy under specific LPBF process parameters.

caption: Inverse pole figure map representing the crystallographic orientation distribution of the DP-SLM alloy.
summary: Inverse pole figure map representing the crystallographic orientation distribution of the DP-SLM alloy. This map visualizes the grain orientation relative to the sample coordinate system, providing critical information regarding the texture and grain morphology resulting from the selective laser melting process applied to the HEA material.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the corrosion behavior of SLMed and sintered AlSi10Mg specimens in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for all fabricated AlSi10Mg alloys in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution are presented here. These curves characterize the electrochemical corrosion kinetics of the SLMed and sintered samples, allowing for a comparative analysis of their polarization behavior under saline conditions.

caption: Boxplot comparison of maximum forces for HA-ZrO2-1300-5-1300 and HA-ZrO2-1300-10-1300 specimens, indicating a statistically significant difference (p ≤ 0.001) determined via a two-sided student t-test.
summary: This boxplot illustrates the mean maximal measured forces for HA-ZrO2-1300-5-1300 and HA-ZrO2-1300-10-1300 samples, corresponding to 5% and 10% overlap conditions. The statistical analysis reveals a significant difference between the two groups, with a p-value of 0.001 or less, confirming that the overlap percentage significantly influences the maximum force values.

caption: Validation of the modified Johnson-Cook model against experimental flow stress data for CHT_MS250 at a strain rate of 1700 s-1.
summary: Displayed is the flow stress response of CHT_MS250 at a high strain rate of 1700 s-1. The comparison between experimental results and the modified Johnson-Cook model predictions highlights the model's performance at the highest tested strain rate, confirming its utility for predicting material behavior under extreme loading.

caption: Aperiodic E-type minimal surface derived from the pentagonal prism geometry.
summary: The aperiodic E minimal surface is presented as a product of the Tile(1,1)-based construction method. By incorporating tunnels directed toward the edges of the pentagonal prism, this structure illustrates the versatility of the boundary method in generating diverse, non-periodic minimal surface designs for material applications.

caption: Surface plot illustrating the SR response.
summary: This surface plot visualizes the SR response as indicated in the figure. The representation provides a three-dimensional perspective of the data, allowing for a clear observation of the SR behavior across the defined parameters, as supported by the analysis of the experimental results presented in the study.

caption: Plateau overpotential analysis of Li electroplating for LNPs-CFC and control electrodes.
summary: Plateau overpotential measurements demonstrate that the LNPs-CFC electrode maintains lower voltage hysteresis during the Li plating process compared to control electrodes. This consistent reduction in overpotential across various current densities underscores the improved electrochemical kinetics and stability of the LNPs-CFC interface during prolonged lithium metal cycling.

caption: Training data parity plot at a strain rate of 0.1 s⁻¹, illustrating the correlation between predicted and actual stress values across the specified temperature range.
summary: Representing the training data at the highest strain rate of 0.1 s⁻¹, this parity plot demonstrates the MLP model's predictive accuracy. The color-coded thermal conditions provide insight into how the model accounts for temperature effects on stress, ensuring robust performance across the training set at this specific strain rate.

caption: Unconverged or ill-behaved time series of the wetting angle θ for a simulation at 1337 K and 0.0078 Al concentration, exhibiting oscillations that complicate the determination of a stable equilibrium value.
summary: Representing an unconverged MD simulation run at 1337 K, this panel highlights the challenges of estimating wetting angles when oscillations are present. Such ill-behaved data, potentially caused by capillary waves or lack of convergence, leads to increased uncertainty values when constructing subsequent data-driven models for the system.

caption: Corneal cell viability following 1 hour of exposure to eye drops and a subsequent 10-minute dehydration stress period.
summary: Panel B illustrates the protective activity of commercial eye drops on corneal cells subjected to 10 minutes of dehydration. DayDrop Advanced® demonstrates a significant protective effect, achieving viability levels of 137.72 ± 26.18%, which surpasses the performance of the hydration positive control group at 130.73 ± 25.17%.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC200GT device plotted for various temperature values.
summary: This panel presents the power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC200GT device. By plotting power output against voltage across different temperatures, the graph demonstrates the thermal dependence of the device's power delivery, highlighting the specific performance trends observed under the tested environmental conditions.

caption: Confusion matrices representing the final network performance on the test dataset for various flow rate categories.
summary: This panel presents the confusion matrices of the final network after training, illustrating the classification accuracy of the model for each flow rate category on the test set. The results demonstrate the model's ability to correctly categorize different flow rate parameters within the continuous fiber-reinforced polymer composite 3D-printing dataset.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the homogenized-aged specimen showing lens-shaped (Ni-Cu)4Ti3 precipitates within the B2 matrix.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the homogenized-aged specimen reveals the presence of lens-shaped (Ni-Cu)4Ti3 precipitates distributed within the B2 matrix. These particles, which are less than 500 nm in size, were formed due to aging at 450 ℃ and exhibit a coherent interface with the surrounding matrix structure.

caption: Electron absorbed dose per fluence (D/Φ) plotted against energy for SIL and ICRP 116 phantoms, calculated using MCNPX simulations.
summary: This plot displays the electron absorbed dose per fluence for SIL and ICRP 116 phantoms derived from MCNPX simulations. Both models demonstrate a sharp increase in absorbed dose within the 50 keV to 70 keV energy range, with a maximum discrepancy of approximately 76% occurring at 60 keV.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of a glassy carbon electrode in a Ni-Co/L-Ser electrolyte at a scan rate of 10 mV s-1.
summary: Represented is the cyclic voltammogram for a glassy carbon electrode immersed in a Ni-Co/L-Ser electrolyte. The experiment utilized a graphite rod counter electrode and a Ag wire pseudo-reference at room temperature. The scan rate was maintained at 10 mV s-1 to evaluate the electrochemical performance of the bimetallic system.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing the spatial distribution of carbon and manganese atoms across the austenite/martensite phase boundary.
summary: The APT reconstruction provides an atomic-scale view of the phase boundary between austenite and martensite in the #40HSLA steel. Analysis of the atomic distribution reveals that there is no significant partitioning of manganese or carbon across this FCC/BCC interface, indicating a lack of solute redistribution at the boundary during the solidification process.

caption: Vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) hysteresis loops for samples N1 through N13, which underwent field heat treatment (FHT), compared against sample N14, which was processed without FHT.
summary: The VSM hysteresis loops illustrate the magnetic performance of various samples from Experiment 1. Samples N1 through N13 were subjected to field heat treatment, while sample N14 was not. These curves provide a comparative visualization of the magnetic response and saturation characteristics resulting from the different processing conditions applied to the materials.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) coloring of a single surface grain showing orientation evolution across increasing strain levels.
summary: This panel displays the orientation changes within a specific surface grain as strain increases, visualized through IPF coloring. The grain's structural evolution is tracked across multiple strain states, providing clear evidence of the deformation mechanisms involved, which include both slip and twinning processes during the mechanical loading of the material.

caption: Cell resistances calculated from IR drop measurements for 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 cells, evaluated at the end of lithiation and delithiation steps.
summary: This panel shows the total cell resistance derived from IR drop measurements at the conclusion of lithiation or delithiation steps. The results demonstrate consistency with the sum of individual half-cell resistances, confirming the reliability of the electrochemical characterization for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 calorimetric cells.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification performance for sign language digits “B”, “I”, and “O” using PEDOT:PSS/PEGDA/50 % DES flat electrodes.
summary: This confusion matrix graphically represents the classification accuracy for sign language digits B, I, and O when using PEDOT:PSS/PEGDA/50 % DES flat electrodes. It serves as a performance evaluation metric for the testing set, providing a clear visualization of how effectively the model distinguishes between these specific hand gesture classes.

caption: Mechanical machining process applied to the as-built Al 1060 samples to refine their final geometry.
summary: Mechanical machining is employed as a post-processing step to refine the as-built Al 1060 samples. This stage is essential for transforming the raw, welded structures into precise components, such as the gear wheels, ensuring that the final parts meet the required dimensional accuracy and surface finish specifications.

caption: Crystallographic representation of the O-phase Ti2AlM intermetallic compound projected along the [010] direction.
summary: This panel displays the O-phase Ti2AlM crystal structure viewed along the [010] axis. The visualization highlights the specific atomic configuration and symmetry of the intermetallic compound from this orientation, contributing to the comprehensive structural characterization of the O-phase materials as detailed in the research findings.

caption: Calibration plot comparing measured mechanical properties against values predicted by the GNN model for normal parts, utilizing a 50/50 random split between training and test sets.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the GNN model's predictive accuracy by comparing measured mechanical properties to predicted values for normal parts. The data points are distributed relative to a diagonal dashed line representing perfect prediction, demonstrating the model's performance based on a random 50/50 split between training and test datasets.

caption: Normal probability plot of residuals for the impact strength of as-cast specimens.
summary: Impact strength residuals for as-cast specimens are plotted to assess model accuracy. The points exhibit a linear distribution along the red straight line, confirming that the dispersion is desirable. This alignment indicates that the model effectively captures the response behavior within the expected normal distribution parameters.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the integration of melt-based additive manufacturing, machine learning, and refractory metal alloy development.
summary: This schematic illustrates the intersection of melt-based additive manufacturing, machine learning, and refractory metal alloys. It highlights the research landscape for these three domains, emphasizing the need for further investigation into their combined application as a promising yet underexplored area for advanced materials processing and predictive modeling.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of BMSCs on PT, PTM, and PTMN scaffolds at 14 days, showing RUNX2 (green), actin (red), and nuclei (blue).
summary: Immunofluorescence staining performed at 14 days post-implantation visualizes the distribution of RUNX2, actin, and nuclei in BMSCs cultured on PT, PTM, and PTMN scaffolds. Fluorescence intensity analysis reveals that RUNX2 expression is significantly higher on the PTMN scaffold compared to the PT and PTM scaffolds, indicating improved osteogenic differentiation.

caption: MOKE-measured hysteresis loops for a Py antidot square lattice along the [10] and [11] crystallographic directions, demonstrating magnetic saturation behavior.
summary: MOKE measurements of the Py antidot square lattice reveal distinct hysteresis loops along the [10] and [11] axes. The data indicates that the [11] direction is the magnetic easy axis, as it saturates more readily than the [10] hard axis. Both loops fully close at approximately 500 Oe.

caption: UV-range sonoluminescence spectra of PA under 1000 rpm stirring, with color-coded durations indicating temporal evolution of emission intensity.
summary: This panel displays the UV portion of sonoluminescence spectra for PA under 1000 rpm stirring. The color-coded lines illustrate how emission intensity changes over time. Observations indicate that after switching on the stirrer, the overall intensity initially rises significantly before falling below the levels observed in non-stirring conditions.

caption: Loss evolution comparison for the simple offset method, showing stagnation of IC and total losses.
summary: Panel (a) displays the loss history for the simple offset method, where IC collocation points are shifted by 0.05*hlayer from the interface. The evolution reveals that the IC loss stagnates and remains marginally higher than the baseline, demonstrating limited convergence benefits compared to the pointwise weight method.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the as-cast N1 alloy displaying a uniform distribution of needle-like and granular precipitates inside the grains.
summary: As-cast N1 alloy samples exhibit a microstructure containing needle-like and granular precipitates. These precipitates are uniformly distributed within the grain interior, consistent with the observations for the N0 alloy. The dark-field TEM imaging confirms that the N1 composition maintains this specific precipitate morphology in the as-cast state.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis graph of the pre-heated tung oil-based resin, illustrating two distinct weight loss stages and confirming thermal stability up to approximately 300 °C.
summary: TGA analysis of the pre-heated resin displays two major, distinct weight loss stages. The highly crosslinked nature of the cured resin ensures thermal stability up to approximately 300 °C. This thermal profile is critical for understanding the degradation behavior and structural integrity of the polymer formed after the curing process.

caption: Bode magnitude plot showing the frequency response of PEO-coated series B samples.
summary: This Bode magnitude plot illustrates the frequency-dependent impedance response of PEO-coated series B samples. As part of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) characterization, the plot provides insight into the coating's electrical behavior across a range of frequencies, serving as a representative result for this specific sample category.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the as-printed sample accompanied by elemental distribution maps and a line profile, with SAED patterns acquired from regions I and II.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging combined with elemental mapping demonstrates that the strip-like regions are significantly enriched in copper. Line profile analysis and SAED patterns obtained from specific regions I and II provide detailed structural and compositional insights into the distribution of these phases within the as-printed sample matrix.

caption: Storage modulus (E′) as a function of temperature for 3D-printed and post-cured PI-2-PPC samples.
summary: Temperature dependence of the storage modulus (E′) is shown for the PI-2-PPC sample. The thermomechanical properties of this material composition differ considerably from the PI-1-GS samples previously analyzed, reflecting the influence of the specific PPC composition and post-processing temperature on the mechanical stiffness of the 3D-printed material.

caption: Dependence plot showing the nonlinear relationship between total height deviation and predicted variability.
summary: This dependence plot highlights a nonlinear correlation where moderate total height deviations lead to reduced predicted variability. Conversely, extreme deviations at both the low and high ends of the spectrum result in increased variability, illustrating the complex impact of height consistency on the model's output for printed parts.

caption: Diagram depicting the annihilation of vacancies at the grain boundary of sintering particles, where porosities generated at the neck surface migrate toward the neck center driven by chemical energy reduction.
summary: This diagram details the vacancy annihilation process occurring at the grain boundary during sintering. It shows how porosities formed at the neck surface are transported toward the center of the neck. This migration is driven by the reduction of chemical energy, facilitating the densification of the sintering material.

caption: Surface morphology and height maps of the three MRE samples, revealing that the enhanced MRE sample possesses the smoothest surface finish.
summary: Confocal microscopy images and surface height maps compare the surface morphology of the three MRE samples. The analysis confirms that the enhanced MRE sample exhibits the smoothest surface finish, highlighting the structural improvements achieved through the particle chain enhancement method during the magnetic field-assisted SLA manufacturing process.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectrum of PCN-224, showing an optical band gap energy of 1.38 eV derived from Tauc plot analysis.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectrum of PCN-224 is presented to characterize its optical properties. Tauc plot analysis of this spectral data reveals a band gap energy of 1.38 eV for the material, providing a baseline for understanding its electronic structure and potential for charge transfer processes in composite systems.

caption: GDMS depth-profiling analysis of Ag:TiN/Al samples using the SLM configuration at a discharge pressure of 6.50 mPa.
summary: This panel displays the GDMS depth-profiling analysis for the SLM configuration at 6.50 mPa. The analysis successfully captures the distribution of major and minor elements along the depth direction of the Ag:TiN/Al sample, providing a comprehensive profile of the material composition throughout the sputtered depth.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of GO, rGO, and 3D-rGO, highlighting the π-π* transitions of aromatic C-C bonds between 250 and 280 nm and the n-π* transition of C=O bonds at 300 nm.
summary: UV-Vis spectroscopy of GO, rGO, and 3D-rGO demonstrates the restoration of the extensive conjugated framework of sp2 carbons. Specifically, the absorbance between 250 and 280 nm corresponds to π-π* transitions of aromatic C-C bonds, while a shoulder observed at approximately 300 nm is assigned to the n-π* transition of C=O bonds.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the identified interstitial polyhedra, labeled as T (isosceles trapezoidal trigonal prism), O (octahedron), and L (double lateral dimensional trigonal prisms), highlighting the local coordination environments for potential solute segregation.
summary: The atomic arrangement of the interstitial sites is detailed, categorizing the polyhedra into three specific types: T for isosceles trapezoidal trigonal prism, O for octahedron, and L for double lateral dimensional trigonal prisms. These structural models define the local atomic environments where non-metallic elements may segregate within the grain boundary.

caption: Emergence of capillary waves near the bottom edge of the vibrating plate surface, coinciding with the development of cavitating bubble structures.
summary: As the cavitating bubbles continue to develop within the liquid, capillary waves are observed forming near the bottom edge of the vibrating plate surface. This panel illustrates the direct correlation between the growth of cavitation activity and the initiation of surface wave phenomena in the thick liquid film.

caption: High-resolution C1s XPS spectrum of the CA/3D-MCC sample prior to the adsorption process.
summary: This panel displays the high-resolution C1s XPS spectrum for the CA/3D-MCC material before any adsorption occurs. It serves as a baseline measurement for carbon-based chemical states within the composite structure, providing the initial surface composition data necessary for comparing changes after the material interacts with lead ions.

caption: Common tangent construction applied to the Gibbs free energy curve at 1500 K to determine equilibrium phase compositions.
summary: This panel displays the common tangent construction performed at 1500 K to extract equilibrium composition data. The resulting segment lengths between the tangent points represent the differences in equilibrium composition, which are essential for computing the τ parameter and capturing the temperature-dependent evolution of the Gibbs free energy.

caption: Log-log plot displaying the relationship between feature depth and feature dimension, with diagonal isolines representing constant aspect ratios.
summary: This plot maps the landscape of high aspect ratio structures, using diagonal isolines to define specific aspect ratio values. The purple region identifies a research gap for hollow features smaller than 50 µm with depths of several millimeters, while the green ring demonstrates a successful result achieved via the combined processing approach.

caption: Swarm plot displaying the SHAP values for features influencing yield strength prediction, where dot color represents feature magnitude (pink for low, blue for high) and horizontal position indicates the direction of impact on the predicted outcome.
summary: This swarm plot provides a global perspective on feature contributions to yield strength prediction. By mapping feature values to color and impact direction to the x-axis, it illustrates how specific variables influence the model output. Findings indicate that processing methods like as-built conditions significantly decrease predicted yield strength values.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for water-to-binder ratio (W/B) indicating the sensitivity of compressive strength to ratio variations.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot shows that a water-to-binder ratio (W/B) exceeding 0.20 significantly reduces the compressive strength of the composite. The SHAP value exhibits a drastic drop from +15 to -10, indicating that higher water-to-binder ratios have a strong negative impact on the material's structural performance.

caption: Tan delta behavior of 0HA and 10HA compositions measured over a temperature range of -25 to 180 °C.
summary: Tan delta behavior for 0HA and 10HA compositions is presented over a temperature sweep from -25 to 180 °C. The data indicates that these composites exhibit a broad viscoelastic transition range around physiological temperatures of 37 °C, providing insight into the mechanical property variations observed within these specific material compositions.

caption: Potential energy evolution of Model B during cutting at varying speeds, highlighting energy absorption as the tool transitions from the γ phase into the γ′ phase.
summary: This panel illustrates the potential energy variation in Model B during cutting simulations. As the tool enters the γ′ phase from the γ phase, the interface absorbs energy, resulting in a measurable increase in the system's potential energy. This trend is observed to be dependent on the applied cutting speed.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the target composite architecture featuring B2 and L12 intermetallic phases alongside the desired mechanical and physical properties.
summary: This schematic illustrates the target composite architecture, which integrates B2 and L12 intermetallic phases to achieve specific mechanical and physical properties. The diagram serves as a foundational design guide for the development of the eutectic intermetallic alloy, highlighting the structural goals intended to optimize the material's overall performance.

caption: Model B machined surface structure at a cutting speed of 100 m/s, showing relatively small nano-surface roughness.
summary: In Model B, the workpiece exhibits relatively small nano-surface roughness when machined at a cutting speed of 100 m/s. This result demonstrates the effectiveness of the chosen cutting parameters in maintaining surface integrity and minimizing defect formation within the simulated material structure during the machining operation.

caption: Surface curvature distribution of the enlarged precipitated phase, predominantly showing green coloration to signify a smooth surface morphology.
summary: The surface curvature of the enlarged precipitated phase is visualized, with the majority of the surface appearing green. This distribution indicates that the precipitated phase possesses a smooth surface morphology, consistent with the structural characteristics observed in the interconnected hollow polyhedral network of the alloy.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the middle region of DED-printed G6, illustrating the grain orientation distribution and fine grain structure.
summary: This IPF map captures the middle region of the DED-printed G6 sample, demonstrating the development of a fine microstructure with grain sizes less than 10 μm. The EBSD analysis highlights the crystallographic orientation distribution within this central deposition zone, consistent with the overall microstructural evolution observed across the printed layers.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the polarization data for nanoNi-P electrodes, comparing samples prepared with and without hypophosphite to determine reaction kinetics.
summary: Tafel analysis reveals that nanoNi-P electrodes prepared with hypophosphite exhibit lower Tafel slopes compared to those prepared without it. This indicates that phosphorus incorporation modifies the HER mechanism and enhances reaction kinetics by providing suitable proton-acceptor sites, confirming that phosphorus content is critical for optimizing the overall electrochemical performance.

caption: Dilatometric strain curve for Alloy A showing the determination of the martensite-start temperature.
summary: Dilatometric measurements for Alloy A reveal a martensite-start temperature of 236 °C. The plot displays the thermal strain response, where a dashed line indicates the specific offset used to define the transformation start temperature, following the methodology described in the referenced literature for precise phase transition identification.

caption: Dilatometric analysis curve showing the relative length change (RLC) used to determine the bainitic transformation finish time (Bt).
summary: The dilatometric analysis curve displays the relative length change (RLC) over time to identify the bainitic transformation finish time (Bt). The transformation finish is determined by locating the beginning of the plateau region on the RLC curve, providing a precise metric for the completion of the bainitic transformation process.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image capturing the fine-scale morphology of the κ phases within the wire-arc DED NAB alloy matrix.
summary: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals the fine-scale morphology of the κ phases within the wire-arc DED NAB alloy. This imaging technique allows for the detailed observation of the internal structure, confirming the presence and distribution of these phases at a high magnification level within the alloy matrix.

caption: Thermal imaging camera observation showing the molten titanium pool formed on the Ti sponge after 20 minutes of 17.5 kW electron beam exposure.
summary: Real-time thermal imaging captures the formation of a molten pool on the titanium sponge surface. This observation confirms the successful generation of a liquid metal phase following the 20-minute exposure to the 17.5 kW electron beam, providing visual evidence of the melting process during the experiment.

caption: Classification scheme for the SA2+x samples based on their respective microstructure conditions.
summary: This diagram provides a systematic classification of the individual microstructures for the SA2+x samples. It serves as a reference guide to organize the various aging conditions, including under-aged, peak-aged, and over-aged states, ensuring a clear categorization of the material samples analyzed in the study.

caption: Comparison of estimated load-to-failure values for LPBF-manufactured Ti6Al4V specimens subjected to various mechanical surface treatments followed by HIP, benchmarked against wrought Ti6Al4V material.
summary: This plot evaluates the fatigue performance of LPBF-manufactured Ti6Al4V specimens after undergoing HIP and mechanical surface treatments. By comparing these results to wrought Ti6Al4V, the study justifies the combined processing approach. The data, based on six specimens per group, highlights the effectiveness of these treatments in enhancing mechanical load-to-failure characteristics.

caption: Rate capability behavior of the 3D LFP-GNP electrode tested between C/25 and C/4.
summary: Rate capability behavior of the 3D LFP-GNP electrode is tested between C/25 and C/4. Conducted in a full cell configuration with LTO/LP30, this plot illustrates the specific capacity of the 3D LFP-GNP electrode across the specified C-rate range, demonstrating the material's ability to maintain capacity under varying current loads.

caption: Level 3 hierarchy unit cell displaying cubic symmetry, incorporating all twelve Level 2 unit cells in a tessellating pattern.
summary: Achieving cubic symmetry, this Level 3 metamaterial incorporates all twelve Level 2 unit cells into a tessellating pattern. The resulting macroscale stiffness tensor is defined by three independent elastic constants, demonstrating how complex hierarchical tessellation can produce highly symmetric mechanical behavior from a diverse set of constituent unit cells.

caption: Chemical composition data for MC and M6C carbides across samples with varying melting temperatures (Tm), expressed in mole percentages.
summary: This table presents the chemical composition of MC and M6C carbides in samples subjected to different melting temperatures. The data, measured in mole percentages, provides a quantitative overview of the carbide phases. These results were derived from EPMA analysis, with specific test points illustrated in the corresponding experimental setup figure.

caption: Chemical composition and structural representation of individual laponite nanoclay particles, highlighting their empirical formula Na+0.7[(Si8Mg5.5Li0.3)O20(OH)4]−0.7 and unique charge distribution.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental chemical composition and structural characteristics of laponite nanoclay particles. The empirical formula Na+0.7[(Si8Mg5.5Li0.3)O20(OH)4]−0.7 is provided, alongside a representation of the unique charge distribution inherent to these nanosilicates, which serves as the basis for their application in advanced bioink development and regenerative medicine.

caption: Logarithmic strain rate versus inverse temperature for nanocrystalline Au micropillars, used to calculate the apparent activation energy for the onset of plasticity in both quasistatic and high strain rate regimes.
summary: This Arrhenius-style plot shows the logarithmic strain rate as a function of inverse temperature for nanocrystalline Au micropillars. Following the approach of Wehrs et al., the apparent activation energy for the onset of plasticity is determined from the slopes of the fitted lines for both quasistatic and high strain rate regimes.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves of LPBF NiMnSn annealed for one week, measured near the structural transformation temperature T M.
summary: This panel displays isothermal M-H curves for LPBF NiMnSn samples annealed for one week. Measurements were taken near the structural transformation temperature T M under a decreasing field. The data shows that magnetization increases with rising temperatures as the weak magnetic martensite phase gradually transforms into the strong magnetic austenite phase.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the 316L/IN718 system, where the abscissa represents the mass fraction of IN718 ranging from 0.0 (pure 316L) to 1.0 (pure IN718).
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram for the 316L/IN718 system was generated using Thermo-Calc simulations with a dual-database approach, utilizing TCFE12 for 316L and TCNI12 for IN718. The plot illustrates phase stability across the entire composition range, with the x-axis denoting the mass fraction of IN718 from 0.0 to 1.0.

caption: Confocal imaging of MHC (green), CD31 (red), and DAPI (blue) at day 14, illustrating the formation of aligned myotubes and interconnected endothelial networks.
summary: Confocal microscopy at day 14 reveals the formation of MHC-positive myotubes aligned within the printed constructs. The co-staining with CD31 demonstrates the development of interconnected endothelial networks, confirming that the coculture of satellite cells and HUVECs effectively promotes both myotube formation and endothelial network integration within the differentiation media.

caption: Kubelka-Munk transform, F(R), of the diffuse reflectance for the powder, with the pink region indicating the 1030–1070 nm laser wavelength range.
summary: The Kubelka-Munk transform, F(R), of the diffuse reflectance is plotted to characterize the optical properties of the powder. The pink shaded region highlights the 1030–1070 nm wavelength range corresponding to the laser used in the study. This plot is essential for understanding the light-matter interaction during the laser processing of the powder.

caption: Ti 2p XPS spectrum showing the high-resolution fitting of the titanium signal.
summary: The Ti 2p spectral region displays the high-resolution XPS data for titanium. The fitting of this signal is essential for determining the oxidation state and chemical bonding of titanium on the surface, contributing to the overall understanding of the surface composition of the analyzed material.

caption: Electron beam trajectory and surface electron density at 0.5 A beam current, 35 kV acceleration voltage, and 0.9/0.3 A coil currents.
summary: This panel shows the electron beam trajectory and surface electron density at a beam current of 0.5 A. Increasing the beam current from 0.5 to 2.0 A at a constant 35 kV acceleration voltage enhances the electron density without significantly altering the established beam trajectory path.

caption: Failure morphology of a Ni-based superalloy specimen with a lower volume fraction, exhibiting a less smooth fracture surface due to the rapid growth and coalescence of micro-voids.
summary: Representing the failure morphology of a Ni-based superalloy specimen with a lower volume fraction, this panel highlights a less smooth fracture surface compared to the 60% volume fraction case. The increased surface roughness is attributed to the rapid growth and connection of numerous micro-voids during the tensile deformation process.

caption: Al-based atom distribution map of the bottom sample region, showing the distribution of primary and secondary γ′ phases within the γ matrix.
summary: The bottom region APT reconstruction displays a γ′ phase density of 1.05 × 10^6 /μm^3. This area is characterized by a high number of secondary γ′ phases, illustrating the distinct microstructural evolution and elemental distribution patterns observed in the bottom portion of the BD sample.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the predictive performance of the third model regarding pH level classification.
summary: This confusion matrix offers a detailed view of the classification results for the third model across the different pH level classes. By mapping predicted versus actual pH categories, the matrix allows for an assessment of the model's predictive accuracy and identification of specific classes that are frequently confused during testing.

caption: Transmittance spectrum of sintered C30 SZ glass doped with 0.25 wt% CoO, showing high transparency in the visible spectrum.
summary: This spectrum represents the visible transmittance of C30 SZ glass doped with 0.25 wt% CoO. The sample exhibits remarkable optical properties, achieving a transmittance of 87% at 405 nm. This result confirms that doping with Co salts maintains the exceptional transparency characteristic of the sintered SiO2-ZrO2 glass system.

caption: Velocity distribution cloud diagram of sand particles subjected to a vibration frequency of 400 Hz.
summary: This panel displays the velocity cloud diagram for sand particles under a 400 Hz vibration frequency. The visualization illustrates the spatial distribution of particle velocities, providing insight into the dynamic behavior of the granular material at this specific frequency level as part of the broader frequency study.

caption: Grain boundary sliding map generated via EBSD-DIC algorithm, showing localized sliding around grain G2.
summary: The grain boundary sliding map, derived from the EBSD-DIC algorithm, demonstrates that sliding is highly localized around grain G2. This localized sliding accommodates the rigid-body rotation of G2, which is required to maintain deformation coordination. In contrast, larger grains in the microstructure exhibit minimal grain boundary sliding activity.

caption: Quantitative printability analysis comparing different ink formulations, with the grey area indicating the acceptable printability region (n=15, α=5%).
summary: Quantitative analysis of printability supports the visual findings from the filament drop test. The plot shows the printability metrics for different formulations, with the grey area representing the acceptable printability region. Statistical analysis using one-way ANOVA and Tukey post hoc tests indicates non-significant differences or specific significant variations.

caption: Relaxation volumes of vacancies in Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy structures at 300 K and 2000 K, calculated as a function of the local atomic environment and compared against fcc Ni-Fe reference values.
summary: Relaxation volumes of vacancies in Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy structures at 300 K and 2000 K are calculated as a function of the local atomic environment. These results are compared against values for fcc Ni-Fe, providing insight into how local chemical composition influences the lattice relaxation surrounding a vacancy defect in these alloys.

caption: Creep strain versus time for alloy M0 at 760 °C and 259 MPa, comparing specimens aged at 800 °C for 8, 3000, 5000, and 10,000 h.
summary: Alloy M0 exhibits a significant reduction in creep life following long-term isothermal aging at 800 °C. Creep life decreases from 271 h for the standard 8 h aged condition to 47 h, 38 h, and 23 h after 3000 h, 5000 h, and 10,000 h of exposure, respectively, under 760 °C and 259 MPa testing.

caption: DAPI/F-actin staining of MC3T3-E1 cells at day 7 and hASCs at day 20, highlighting cytoskeletal morphology and network formation on collagen, CHA-7, and CDP-7 scaffolds.
summary: DAPI/F-actin staining shows limited spreading of MC3T3-E1 cells on collagen at day 7, whereas cells on CHA-7 and CDP scaffolds exhibit elongated, aligned cytoskeletons. Furthermore, hASCs cultured for 20 days on CDP-7 scaffolds demonstrate extensive actin-rich networks that successfully span the scaffold pores, indicating improved cell-material interaction.

caption: Bright field STEM image illustrating the fine grain structure formed within the partially γ′ depleted zone during recrystallisation.
summary: Bright field STEM imaging reveals the presence of a very fine grain structure within the partially γ′ depleted zone. This microstructural observation confirms that recrystallisation has occurred in this specific region of the material, resulting in a refined grain morphology compared to the surrounding matrix.

caption: Magnetization versus temperature (M-T) curves for furnace-cooled (#FC) Ni-Co-Mn-Sn powders measured under 50 Oe, 1 T, and 5 T magnetic fields.
summary: The M-T curves for furnace-cooled (#FC) Ni-Co-Mn-Sn powders are presented under varying magnetic fields of 50 Oe, 1 T, and 5 T. These measurements investigate the influence of cooling rates on the magnetic properties of the material, with specific parameters detailed in the accompanying experimental data tables.

caption: Bode representation of EIS spectra for 3D samples after the anodizing process, compared across inflammatory and severe inflammatory conditions.
summary: Bode plots display the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for 3D samples that underwent an anodizing process. Recorded in inflammatory and severe inflammatory conditions, these spectra characterize the surface impedance. The fitting parameters for these specific impedance spectra are detailed in the corresponding tables provided in the study.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the LSFNi sample after reduction at 850 °C for 5 hours, showing the structural state of the material post-treatment.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy of the LSFNi sample after reduction at 850 °C for 5 hours provides a detailed view of the material's structural state. This panel complements the other microscopy results by documenting the physical changes occurring within the LSFNi matrix following the high-temperature exsolution process.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of chitosan (CS) and methacrylated chitosan (CSMA), highlighting new peaks at 5.6 and 6.0 ppm.
summary: Successful methacrylation of chitosan is demonstrated through 1H NMR spectroscopy. The CSMA spectrum displays new peaks at 5.6 ppm and 6.0 ppm, which are absent in the unmodified CS spectrum, confirming the effective chemical modification of the chitosan polymer for use in the bio-ink.

caption: Magnified view of the strain field observed at 1.26% plastic strain, highlighting localized deformation features.
summary: This magnified strain field map provides a detailed look at the localized deformation features present at 1.26% plastic strain.
