By focusing on a specific region of the Alloy 718 specimen, the panel allows for a clearer examination of the sub-grain strain gradients and heterogeneities developed during the tensile loading process.

caption: Color-enhanced high-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of the Al79Ni7Fe7Y7 alloy ribbon, highlighting distinct atomic structural regions.
summary: Presented as a colored HRTEM image, this panel visualizes the Al79Ni7Fe7Y7 alloy ribbon processed at 1200 °C. By applying color enhancement to the high-resolution data, the image facilitates the identification of ordered versus disordered atomic regions, confirming the presence of varied structural domains within the interdendritic areas of the ribbon.

caption: Hardness evolution plotted against aging time at 120 °C for alloys A (black squares), B (red circles), and C (blue triangles), with TEM specimens extracted at the peak-aged condition of 264 h.
summary: This plot illustrates the hardness response of three distinct alloys (A, B, and C) as a function of aging duration at 120 °C. The data highlights the peak-aged condition reached at 264 h, which serves as the reference point for subsequent TEM specimen analysis across the investigated alloy compositions.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image of the precipitates in sample A3, highlighting the internal structure of the second-phase particles.
summary: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy of sample A3 provides a detailed view of the precipitates. This imaging technique allows for the observation of the internal structure of the second-phase particles. The image serves as the basis for further structural characterization, specifically identifying the area used for subsequent diffraction analysis.

caption: Unstacked unit cells featuring a constant wall thickness and varying β-parameter values, illustrating the internal structural hierarchy of the Matryoshka configuration.
summary: Depicting the unstacking of unit cells from a Matryoshka configuration with a β-parameter of 0.8 mm, this panel highlights the structural consistency of the design. Each unit cell maintains an identical wall thickness while varying the β-parameter, demonstrating the modular nature of the porous structure.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of Fe distribution across the NiTi/weld interface, showing the chemical composition variation in the weld zone.
summary: This EDS elemental map illustrates the distribution of iron (Fe) at the NiTi/weld interface. The map provides a detailed view of chemical segregation, which is essential for identifying the formation of specific phases like the γ or B2-(Fe,Ni)Ti phases within the weld region.

caption: Pearson correlation heatmap of geometric morphology features, highlighting strong positive correlations between melt pool area and axial dimensions.
summary: This heatmap displays Pearson correlation coefficients for visible image features. A strong positive correlation is observed between the melt pool area and both the major axis (r = 0.98) and minor axis (r = 0.97), demonstrating that the area metric effectively represents the geometric axial dimensions of the melt pool.

caption: Hyperparameter tuning results for the UTS prediction model, featuring an inset table that details the final optimized hyperparameter values.
summary: Hyperparameter optimization results for the UTS prediction model are presented here, including an inset table that specifies the final tuned values. These results demonstrate the outcome of the optimization process, providing the specific parameters that were determined to be most effective for the UTS prediction model's performance.

caption: Cross-sectional EBSD analysis of the W700 weld joint near the RMEA side, featuring an IPF map, KAM map, and phase composition map.
summary: This panel displays EBSD results for the W700 sample near the RMEA side. The IPF map reveals coarse columnar grains oriented toward the heat source, with an average length of 77.5 μm and width of 24.4 μm. Accompanying KAM and phase maps provide local misorientation and phase distribution data.

caption: Master Sintering Curve (MSC) analysis utilizing time-temperature integration, with an inset showing the minimization process that yields an apparent activation energy of 350 kJ/mol.
summary: The Master Sintering Curve analysis is employed to quantify the thermally activated sintering process. By performing a minimization of the densification data, an apparent activation energy of 350 kJ/mol is determined, which corresponds to the optimal superposition of the densification curves across the tested heating rates.

caption: Comparison of average bending strength for PLA polymer cylinders processed with and without ultrasound-assisted rotary friction welding (UARFW).
summary: This bar chart illustrates the average bending strength of PLA polymer cylinders, comparing specimens processed with and without ultrasound-assisted rotary friction welding (UARFW). The data highlights the impact of this specific welding technique on the mechanical performance of the polymer, providing a clear quantitative assessment of the resulting bending strength values.

caption: Nyquist plots representing the impedance spectra of samples subjected to varying immersion durations in simulated seawater.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the impedance spectra of samples after different immersion periods in simulated seawater. These electrochemical test results indicate that the corrosion resistance in the overlap region is initially lower than that of the substrate, providing critical data for evaluating the degradation behavior of the material over time.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting nanodomains linked to a secondary marked spot in the [1-13] zone axis SAED pattern.
summary: This dark-field image provides further evidence of nanodomains by focusing on a different diffraction spot within the [1-13] zone axis. The presence of these domains, combined with satellites near 1/2 <112> positions, supports the hypothesis of transverse <110> <1-10> displacive waves occurring within the quenched B2 phase structure.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for fiber length (Lf).
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the influence of fiber length (Lf) on the compressive strength of 3DPFRC. It is part of the feature importance analysis used to evaluate how the physical dimensions of the reinforcement fibers affect the mechanical behavior of the printed material.

caption: Relative XRF intensities for the Ni38Co33Cu29 alloy at varying temperatures, demonstrating a slight decline in the Cu peak intensity.
summary: This plot illustrates the relative XRF intensities for the Ni38Co33Cu29 alloy at different temperatures. A slight decrease is observed in the relative Cu XRF intensity, which reflects a subtle change in the trend of thermal expansion previously noted for this specific alloy composition during the experimental analysis.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation snapshot depicting electron trajectories interacting with the printing surface and powder beds, showing the spatial distribution of the backscattering coefficient and powder bed height at 300 μm intervals.
summary: This Monte Carlo simulation snapshot illustrates electron beam trajectories interacting with printing surfaces and powder beds. The backscattering coefficient and powder bed height are recorded at 300 μm intervals along the scan direction. This visualization provides insight into electron behavior and surface interactions during the printing process.

caption: Specific energy loss at 50 Hz for M300 steel plotted against magnetic flux density, comparing performance before and after heat treatment.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific energy loss of M300 steel at a frequency of 50 Hz as a function of magnetic flux density. The data, calculated from hysteresis loops, compares the material's magnetic performance before and after heat treatment, providing a quantitative assessment of the impact of processing on magnetic losses.

caption: High-resolution O1s XPS spectrum of thermally crystallized monoclinic black ZrO2, illustrating oxygen vacancy levels.
summary: This O1s high-resolution spectrum for thermally crystallized black m-ZrO2 allows for the evaluation of oxygen vacancy preservation. The signal intensity is lower than that observed in laser-crystallized samples, confirming that room-temperature laser processing is more effective at preserving oxygen vacancies than conventional thermal crystallization methods.

caption: K–L plots for GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 calculated at different potentials to evaluate the electron transfer pathway.
summary: Based on the Koutecky–Levich equation, the K–L plots for GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 indicate an electron transfer number of approximately 3.97 in the potential range of +0.2 to +0.5 V. This result implies a direct 4e- pathway occurring during the oxygen reduction reaction in 0.1 M KOH electrolyte.

caption: High-resolution Au4f XPS spectrum of the AM-N12 adsorbent following gold(III) adsorption, revealing the presence of various chemical states of gold.
summary: The high-resolution Au4f XPS spectrum of the AM-N12 adsorbent after gold(III) adsorption is presented in panel (a). This analysis reveals the presence of various chemical states of gold on the adsorbent surface, providing insight into the nature of the gold species captured during the adsorption process.

caption: Spatial mapping of the spectral distribution within the incorporation zone, visualizing the local variation of luminescent particle types.
summary: This panel provides a spatial mapping of the spectral distribution within the incorporation zone. It visualizes the local variations in luminescent particle types, allowing for the correlation of specific spectral signatures with the spatial location of the particles within the processed material structure.

caption: High-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectrum of the FeNi@N-CNTs composite.
summary: The high-resolution Fe 2p spectrum provides detailed information regarding the chemical state of iron within the FeNi@N-CNTs hybrid. This analysis is part of the comprehensive XPS characterization used to determine the elemental composition and specific bonding states of the metal species integrated into the nitrogen-doped carbon nanotube structure.

caption: 1H-NMR spectra comparing unmodified pectin, bis(3-aminopropyl)amine (APA) reagent, and the resulting APA-modified pectin product.
summary: The 1H-NMR spectra provide a comparative analysis of the chemical modification process. By examining the signals from the non-modified pectin, the APA reagent, and the final APA-modified pectin, the successful incorporation of the amine into the pectin backbone is confirmed through spectral changes observed across the three samples.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops M(H) measured at various maximum applied magnetic fields, with each loop corresponding to the temperature of maximum hysteresis loss.
summary: Hysteresis loops M(H) are displayed at constant temperatures, illustrating the magnetic behavior of the samples. The area enclosed by these loops allows for the estimation of hysteresis loss (HL), which is shown to be dependent on the maximum applied magnetic field used during the measurement process.

caption: Variation of the Rex12Cfx2 parameter as a function of m and M, illustrating the influence of magnetic field strength on shear stress at the lower plate.
summary: This plot displays the modification of the Rex12Cfx2 parameter relative to variables m and M. It demonstrates that the Hall effect actively reduces shear stress at the lower plate when the magnetic field strength is held constant, highlighting the interplay between electromagnetic forces and mechanical stress distribution in the system.

caption: Conceptual representation of the useable filament length defined as the segment spanning two consecutive out-of-spec diameter values.
summary: This schematic illustrates the methodology for defining useable filament length, specifically identifying the segment between two consecutive out-of-spec diameter values. Such measurements are critical because high cluster frequency often results in short filament segments that are insufficient for completing a print, necessitating a clear definition for quality assessment.

caption: PowerMill simulation environment displaying the initial toolpath start location.
summary: The PowerMill simulation environment is shown at the start of the toolpath. This visualization represents the hardware configuration during the transition to CAM integration, establishing the baseline position for the machine motion analysis and verifying the initial setup parameters for the SDS-10 head assembly.

caption: Evolution of maximum and minimum stress values over the course of the fatigue test, demonstrating the attainment of stabilized cyclic behavior.
summary: The graph illustrates the progression of maximum and minimum stress levels throughout the fatigue test. Observations indicate that cyclic hardening or softening effects become insignificant by the mid-life stage. Consequently, the material reaches a stabilized cyclic behavior, as evidenced by the plateauing of stress values over the test duration.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (Tafel) curves comparing the corrosion behavior of UT, SMAT-ed, UT+GM, and SMAT-ed+GM samples in a 0.9 wt% NaCl electrolyte.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization measurements were conducted on the UT, SMAT-ed, UT+GM, and SMAT-ed+GM samples to assess their electrochemical performance. The resulting Tafel curves demonstrate the corrosion characteristics of each sample, providing a comparative analysis of the polarization behavior across the different surface treatment and coating conditions.

caption: Variation of Si content in Fe-free Al-bearing bridgmanite (Brg) as a function of Al content at 25–27 GPa and 1873–2000 K, comparing experimental data from various sources against theoretical trend lines for coupled substitution (CC) and oxygen vacancy (OV) mechanisms.
summary: This plot illustrates the Si content of Fe-free Al-bearing bridgmanite versus Al content under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. The data, categorized by starting composition stoichiometry (Mg > Si vs. Mg ≤ Si), are compared against theoretical trend lines representing the coupled substitution (CC) and oxygen vacancy (OV) mechanisms.

caption: Thermo-kinetic E-pH diagram for nickel in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 25 °C, showing blue dots for measured OCP values.
summary: Nickel exhibits a wide range of passive behavior at 25 °C in acetate solution, as shown in this E-pH diagram. The blue dots representing measured OCP values indicate that in acidic pH, the electrode potential is notably more positive than the equilibrium redox potential, confirming the formation of a protective layer.

caption: Nyquist plots representing the electrochemical impedance behavior of photopolymer compositions containing 60 wt% of various electrolytes, specifically ethaline, glyceline, [Emim][BF4], and [Omim][BF4].
summary: Nyquist plots are presented for photopolymer compositions containing 60 wt% of different electrolytes, including ethaline, glyceline, [Emim][BF4], and [Omim][BF4]. These plots characterize the electrochemical impedance behavior of the materials, providing insight into the ionic transport properties of the various photopolymer compositions tested in the study.

caption: Alizarin Red S (ARS) staining of MC3T3-E1 cells after three weeks of culture in composite scaffold extracts, revealing significantly enhanced matrix mineralization across all experimental groups, with the highest calcium deposition observed in the DPBM group.
summary: ARS staining performed after three weeks of culture assesses late-stage matrix mineralization in MC3T3-E1 cells. The findings reveal significantly increased calcium deposition in the DPST, BMOG, and DPBM groups relative to the control. The DPBM group shows the highest level of mineralization, confirming its effectiveness in promoting osteogenic differentiation.

caption: EDX elemental mapping of the spherical lattice structure illustrating the localized accumulation of titanium dioxide nanoparticles.
summary: EDX elemental mapping of the spherical lattice structure demonstrates the distribution of titanium dioxide. Complex regions within this lattice exhibit higher nanoparticle accumulation compared to simpler geometries. This quantitative analysis confirms that structural complexity plays a significant role in the migration and final surface concentration of nanoparticles during the printing process.

caption: Chronoamperometric response of the FP-3 experiment performed on Inconel 600 in a LiCl–KCl–5-wt%-FeCl2 molten salt electrolyte.
summary: Representing the third potentiostatic trial, this chronoamperogram details the anodic dissolution of Inconel 600 in the LiCl–KCl–5-wt%-FeCl2 electrolyte. The data collected from this experiment helps elucidate the electrochemical dissolution characteristics of the alloy, serving as a comparative baseline for the broader investigation into its behavior in molten salt environments.

caption: Minor axis length distribution of martensite on XOZ cross-sections for scanning strategies S3 and S4.
summary: Minor axis lengths of martensite on XOZ cross-sections are shown for intermittent scanning strategies S3 and S4. These plots highlight the size distribution of primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite, indicating that intermittent melt pool interference modes lead to larger average martensite sizes compared to continuous modes.

caption: Creep-rupture curves comparing wrought, as-built LPBF, 1100 °C-1 h LPBF, and 1200 °C-4 h LPBF 316H materials tested at 725 °C under a constant stress of 100 MPa.
summary: Creep-rupture curves demonstrate the time-dependent deformation of wrought and various LPBF 316H materials at 725 °C under 100 MPa. This applied stress remains below the 0.2% offset yield point for all tested materials at this temperature, highlighting the complex creep properties inherent to the different processing conditions of the 316H alloy.

caption: Calculated Cr–Ni binary alloy phase diagram generated using Thermo-Calc software, illustrating the equilibrium thermodynamic stability regions for the system.
summary: This panel presents the Cr–Ni binary alloy phase diagram calculated via Thermo-Calc software. It serves as a thermodynamic reference for the system, defining the equilibrium stability regions of various phases, which provides the necessary context for understanding the phase transformations and metastable phase formation discussed in the subsequent schematic.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image and corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental maps of the Ni40Fe40Cr20 alloy, illustrating a homogeneous distribution of nickel, iron, and chromium without evidence of chemical segregation.
summary: The SEM image and EDS maps of the Ni40Fe40Cr20 alloy reveal a uniform elemental distribution. Analysis confirms that the alloy maintains a homogeneous structure with no chemical segregation, consistent with the expected single-phase nature of this composition as observed through the elemental mapping technique.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping displaying the aluminum matrix distribution surrounding the precipitates.
summary: Aluminum elemental distribution is depicted using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping. The map illustrates the aluminum matrix surrounding the S phase precipitates. These precipitates are the main aging strengthening phase in the alloy, playing a vital role in the strong plasticity observed in the Al–4Cu–2Mg–1.1Fe–1.1Ni alloy.

caption: Concentration profiles of vacancy and interstitial defects in Cr as a function of vacancy formation energy under irradiation conditions of 10^-12 dpa.
summary: Panel b displays the concentration of vacancy and interstitial defects in chromium at 10^-12 dpa, evaluated across different vacancy formation energies. The results indicate that the concentration of these defects is sensitive to the chosen formation energy, providing insight into the initial stage of irradiation kinetics in the material.

caption: Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectra of a 50 mg/L phenol solution undergoing degradation by the FeNi porous framework catalyst.
summary: Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectra demonstrate the catalytic degradation of a 50 mg/L phenol solution using the FeNi porous framework. The spectral data tracks the reduction of phenol concentration over time, providing direct evidence of the material's catalytic activity and its effectiveness in breaking down organic pollutants within the aqueous environment.

caption: Under-focus TEM image highlighting the peak damage area, located approximately 150 nm from the surface, in the high-temperature irradiated sample.
summary: This under-focus TEM image captures the peak damage zone, located about 150 nm from the surface, after high-temperature helium implantation. The under-focus technique effectively highlights the defect distribution at this depth, allowing for a detailed examination of how elevated temperatures modify the damage profile within the coating.

caption: In situ monitoring image of Sample 2-1 captured at the 330th layer during the LPBF process.
summary: This in situ monitoring image captures the state of Sample 2-1 at the 330th layer during the LPBF process. It serves as a visual record to monitor the formation processes of deposit loss at the closure, providing a baseline for observing the evolution of the deposit region during layer-wise fabrication.

caption: Load versus time curves for NC Ni and NC Ni–Fe alloy specimens subjected to the CLR indentation test at four different strain rates.
summary: Load-time curves for NC Ni and NC Ni–Fe alloy are shown for four different indentation strain rates during the CLR test. These curves provide the necessary load data to evaluate the mechanical response of the materials, complementing the displacement-time data used to derive the indentation strain rate during loading.

caption: Macroscopic view of a 10 mm diameter by 10 mm height stainless steel specimen after sintering and compression testing, showing plastic deformation and barreling.
summary: Shown is a 10 mm by 10 mm stainless steel specimen subjected to sintering followed by compression testing. The sample displays significant plastic deformation characterized by a barreled shape, suggesting that the sintering process successfully improved metallurgical cohesion and microstructural stabilization compared to the as-sprayed condition.

caption: Orthogonal cross-sections and isometric 3D reconstruction of an upright built LPBF AlSi10Mg specimen, demonstrating the internal density and characteristic linear features along the build orientation axis.
summary: Representing an upright built LPBF AlSi10Mg specimen, this panel includes top, front, and right orthogonal sections and an isometric view. The structure appears similarly dense to the on-edge specimen, though it exhibits more pronounced linear features aligned with the build orientation axis, illustrating the internal density and defect distribution at the specimen scale.

caption: 31P NMR spectrum of potassium pyrophosphate (K4P2O7) acquired at 11 T using a 6 mm spherical rotor spinning at 2.1 kHz within a MAS insert inside a solution-state NMR probe.
summary: This 31P NMR spectrum of potassium pyrophosphate was obtained using a specialized MAS insert configuration within a solution-state NMR probe at 11 T. The sample, consisting of 40 mg of K4P2O7 and 10 mg of KBr for magic angle calibration, demonstrates the feasibility of performing solid-state MAS NMR experiments in a solution-state probe.

caption: Feature importance ranking for the CP-S-P model, incorporating γ′ volume fraction and equivalent diameter as microstructural descriptors alongside composition and processing conditions.
summary: The CP-S-P model feature importance plot demonstrates the impact of integrating microstructural descriptors, specifically γ′ volume fraction and equivalent diameter, into the prediction framework. While these microstructural features contribute to the overall feature set, the analysis indicates they do not overwhelmingly dominate the mechanical property predictions compared to other input variables.

caption: Localized magnification of the TGA curves highlighting the onset of thermal degradation and mass loss transitions for TPU and its composite variants.
summary: Magnified TGA curves provide a detailed view of the initial decomposition phase for TPU and its composite prints. This localized enlargement allows for a precise comparison of the thermal stability and onset temperatures, confirming that the composite materials maintain properties within the acceptable range for typical usage applications.

caption: Bode-phase plots showing the phase angle versus frequency for SLM-manufactured alloys in 0.3, 1.5, and 3.5 wt% NaCl solutions.
summary: Bode-phase plots reveal the electrochemical characteristics of the SLM-manufactured samples in different chloride environments. The maximum phase angles observed in the medium frequency range indicate the formation of a compact corrosion layer on the alloy surface, reflecting the protective nature of the surface film under these specific test conditions.

caption: Incident low power Gaussian beam profile captured on a CCD camera.
summary: This panel displays the incident low power Gaussian beam profile as measured by a CCD camera. The profile serves as the baseline reference for evaluating the beam transformation performance, demonstrating the initial spatial intensity distribution before it interacts with the refractive Fourier transform generator system described in the study.

caption: High-magnification HAADF-STEM image illustrating the boundary region between martensitic laths in the as-built LPBF-NAB sample.
summary: This high-magnification HAADF-STEM image provides a detailed view of the boundary regions between martensitic laths in as-built LPBF-NAB. By resolving the structural features at the junction of martensitic packets, the image confirms the presence of a martensitic phase transformation, which is essential for understanding the material's as-built microstructural state.

caption: Physical measurement workflow representing the experimental data acquisition route.
summary: Physical measurement workflow representing the experimental data acquisition route. This panel serves as the initial component of the general methodology flowchart, outlining the specific steps involved in the physical measurement route as part of the broader experimental framework described in the study's methodology section.

caption: Thermal distribution map of the preheating and liquid cooling specimen at 600 s.
summary: Representing the final stage at 600 s, this heat map displays the thermal profile of the specimen treated with preheating and liquid cooling. It provides a clear view of the sustained thermal control achieved by the cooling process, showing the final temperature distribution across the surface after the full duration.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the TiC-FeCr cermet system, generated using Thermo-Calc 2023b software and the TCFE9 database, illustrating phase stability as a function of carbon content in weight percent.
summary: This CALPHAD-based equilibrium phase diagram for the TiC-FeCr cermet system was computed using the Thermo-Calc 2023b software and TCFE9 database. The diagram maps phase stability across varying carbon concentrations, providing a theoretical framework for understanding the material's thermodynamic behavior and the resulting microstructural evolution within the cermet binder phase.

caption: EBSD map of horizontally built IN939 specimen subjected to TMF-IP loading at 0.4% mechanical strain, showing intergranular crack propagation.
summary: This EBSD map illustrates fatigue damage in horizontally built IN939 under TMF-IP conditions at 0.4% strain. The microstructure reveals winding, intergranular crack paths. Because grain boundaries are oriented perpendicular to the loading axis in this horizontal build, cracks connect easily to the surface, contributing to the observed fatigue failure.

caption: Density distribution map of Standard SLS glass quenched at 50 GPa, visualized at a probe radius of 8.65 Å.
summary: This density distribution map for Standard SLS glass quenched at 50 GPa is shown at a probe radius of 8.65 Å. It highlights the persistence of pentahedral symmetry effects across different probe radii, illustrating the structural transformations driven by the high-pressure quenching process.

caption: Unsupervised learning network architecture illustrating the grouping of input data, represented as orange circles, based on the number of neurons, depicted as octagons.
summary: This panel illustrates an unsupervised learning network used for predicting phase selection in high-entropy alloys. The architecture organizes input data, shown as orange circles, into clusters defined by the number of neurons, represented as octagons. This approach is part of a broader study employing ANN, KNN, and SVM algorithms.

caption: Extended continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for Grade 91 steel, illustrating phase transformation kinetics across a broader range of cooling rates than traditional models.
summary: This extended CCT diagram for Grade 91 steel provides an innovative model for predicting phase transformations. By incorporating cooling rates faster than those typically found in traditional diagrams, the figure offers a more comprehensive understanding of the material's thermal behavior and microstructural evolution during rapid cooling processes.

caption: Statistical distribution of G-code laser distance features comparing desired and undesired clusters.
summary: This box plot illustrates the statistical variations in G-code features between desired and undesired clusters. Specifically, the number of time steps where laser distance is below 1 mm shows significantly higher mean and standard deviation values of 7.15 and 8.44, respectively, within the undesired category compared to the desired category.

caption: Thermal decomposition behavior of the second catalytic sample represented by TGA and DTG curves, highlighting specific weight loss stages and degradation kinetics.
summary: Panel b displays the TGA and DTG curves for the second catalyst sample. By analyzing the weight loss patterns and decomposition rates, this plot offers insights into the thermal stability of the synthesized CNT. These results contribute to the comprehensive assessment of the quality and purity of the catalyst material.

caption: Cooling behavior of the consolidated layer, characterized by a transition to an orange glow immediately prior to the recoating of the subsequent powder layer.
summary: Captured immediately before the next recoating step, this image shows the consolidated layer cooling from its peak temperature to an orange glow. This thermal state reflects the heat accumulation cycle for the 180 µm layer thickness, highlighting the persistent high temperatures maintained throughout the tensile bar fabrication.

caption: Overview of the developed bottom-up projection-based 3D printing system hardware.
summary: This panel illustrates the developed bottom-up projection system hardware. The system was engineered to recoat uniform ultra-thin layers of SiC-polymer suspension with varying volume ratios of SiC particles, ensuring consistent layer thickness throughout the additive manufacturing process.

caption: 3D complex impedance plot of the 300 ℃/2 h annealed sample measured in 0.01 M NaCl, illustrating the evolution of impedance over time.
summary: Representing the 300 ℃/2 h annealed sample, this 3D complex impedance plot tracks instantaneous impedance changes in 0.01 M NaCl. By recording measurements every 5 minutes, the plot facilitates the analysis of dissolution and oxide film formation kinetics, providing a visual representation of the sample's electrochemical stability.

caption: Normalized OPD depth gradient profiles, representing physical property variations such as refractive index changes within the powder bed.
summary: Normalized OPD depth gradient profiles are presented to characterize physical property variations, specifically changes in the refractive index. Derived from the relative OPD changes at different depths, these profiles highlight the spatial evolution of the material's optical properties as the ethanol droplet penetrates the loosely packed powder bed over time.

caption: FTIR-ATR transmittance spectra of as-received and treated aluminium surfaces, normalized to the Al-O vibrational peak located between 600 and 900 cm-1.
summary: This FTIR-ATR spectroscopic analysis compares the surface chemistry of as-received and treated aluminium samples. By focusing on the 600 to 900 cm-1 region, the plot highlights oxide-related vibrational modes. All transmittance data are normalized to the Al-O peak, facilitating a direct comparison of surface oxide characteristics between the different conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the as-cast Al–Cu–Ni–Mn quaternary alloy, highlighting phase identification through specific peak markers.
summary: The XRD pattern of the as-cast Al–Cu–Ni–Mn quaternary alloy reveals the crystalline structure of the material. Based on EDS and XRD analysis, the Al–Cu–Ni rich gray phase is identified by green dots on the peaks, while the Ni-rich white phase is indicated by blue dots, confirming the multiphase composition.

caption: 3D deposition height map of metallic nickel atoms deposited with the electric double layer, showing a slower, more controlled thickness increase.
summary: This 3D reconstruction illustrates the height of nickel deposits formed under the influence of an electric double layer. The data shows that the thickness of the nickel atom layer increases more slowly over time, confirming that the double layer facilitates a more controlled and compact deposition process.

caption: Force-displacement response of sandwich plates subjected to a 50 J low-velocity compression impact.
summary: This plot illustrates the force-displacement behavior of sandwich plates during a 50 J low-velocity compression impact test. The data reveals how core height, wall thickness, and structural topology influence the dynamic crushing response of the lattice structures under this specific energy level, providing insight into the material's initial impact resistance.

caption: Optimized unit cell geometry corresponding to the second design result with the lowest L2 relative error.
summary: This panel displays the second optimized unit cell geometry selected for its low L2 relative error. The design is a result of the inverse diffusion model process, which translates target stress-strain curve requirements into specific structural configurations, demonstrating the model's capability to produce high-fidelity mechanical designs on demand.

caption: Reflectance RL curves demonstrating the collaborative optimization of dual absorption peaks for L5 GMSs.
summary: This panel presents the collaborative optimization results for L5 GMSs, specifically focusing on the dual absorption peaks. The data illustrates the effectiveness of the customized method proposed in the study for tailoring absorption peaks, providing a clear visualization of the optimized electromagnetic response for the L5 configuration.

caption: Density of states calculation for the Al-doped TiNi3–Al2/C interface.
summary: This panel depicts the density of states for the TiNi3–Al2/C interface. Examining this electronic structure helps clarify how Al doping influences the bonding properties and band structure, facilitating a comprehensive comparison of how different dopants modify the electrical conductivity of the TiNi3/C interface.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar module measured under varying insolation levels.
summary: The I-V characteristics of the KC200GT solar module are presented for different irradiation levels, labeled as PEC1. This plot illustrates the electrical response of the module, showing how current varies with voltage under specific insolation conditions, providing essential data for evaluating the performance and efficiency of the photovoltaic device.

caption: Experimental and simulated composition-distance profiles for the C8 diffusion couple at 1373 K, illustrating the agreement between predicted and measured values.
summary: The C8 diffusion couple at 1373 K is analyzed by comparing its experimental composition-distance profile against simulation results. This plot serves to verify the reliability of the simulation framework in predicting diffusion paths for the C8 couple, showing a close correlation between the theoretical model and the observed experimental data.

caption: Dilation derivative and Bi-Gaussian fit results for a cooling rate of 200 C/s, used to define the critical temperatures of the delta to gamma phase transformation.
summary: This panel illustrates the dilatation derivative and Bi-Gaussian fits for the highest cooling rate of 200 C/s. The resulting data points define the (delta to gamma) start, 80%, and finish temperatures, completing the set of measurements used to evaluate the transformation kinetics across the investigated cooling rates.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for ferromagnetic ordering under trilinear coupling QTri, detailing the half-metallic gap and QAFEA mode percentage for the third tuning condition.
summary: Panel c illustrates the partial density of states for the ferromagnetic system under trilinear coupling. By displaying the half-metallic gap of the down-spin channel alongside the QAFEA mode percentage, it confirms that while the magnetic ground state remains unchanged, the electronic structure is systematically modified by the tuning of the QAFEA mode.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry profile of the flexible energy storage device recorded at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry curve at a scan rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ demonstrates the electrochemical performance of the flexible energy storage device. The nearly rectangular shape of the profile confirms the device's consistent capacitive behavior and stable charge storage characteristics across this specific intermediate scan rate range.

caption: (001) pole figure quantifying texture intensities for the SLM-formed IN718 specimen along the horizontal direction.
summary: This pole figure quantifies the texture intensities along the horizontal direction, indicating that grain growth preferentially aligns with the <001> and <011> directions. These findings complement the vertical analysis, confirming the specific crystallographic texture development that characterizes the SLM-formed IN718 microstructure and contributes to its overall anisotropic mechanical performance.

caption: Entropic potential profiles of 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes demonstrating the reversibility between delithiation and lithiation cycles.
summary: Presented here are the entropic potential profiles for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes. The measurements establish that the electrochemical profiles are highly reversible between delithiation and lithiation. This consistency confirms that the tape-casted electrodes maintain stable electrochemical performance, mirroring the reversible behavior observed in the 3D printed counterparts.

caption: Immunofluorescence imaging of wound tissue sections stained with DAPI for nuclei, CD68 for pan-macrophages, and CD206 for M2 phenotype macrophages, showing differential staining patterns across treatment groups.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging of wound tissue sections stained with DAPI for nuclei, CD68 for pan-macrophages, and CD206 for M2 phenotype macrophages, showing differential staining patterns across treatment groups. All three experimental groups exhibited varying levels of positive staining for both M1 (red) and M2 (green) macrophage phenotypes within the wound bed.

caption: Transverse relaxation time (T2) distribution for each HIPPEG group measured via LF-NMR.
summary: The LF-NMR spectrum displays the transverse relaxation time (T2) for each HIPPEG group. This measurement provides critical insights into the molecular mobility and state of water within the gel matrix, serving as a basis for evaluating the internal structure and water-binding dynamics of the different protein-based gel formulations.

caption: Raman-SERS spectra of streptavidin sandwiched between MP-NPs and AuNSts, highlighting the bioorthogonal nitrile peak at 2237 cm⁻¹ as a function of decreasing analyte concentration.
summary: Raman-SERS spectra demonstrate the detection of streptavidin sandwiched between MP-NPs and AuNSts. The bioorthogonal Raman peaks at 1620 cm⁻¹ and 2237 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the aromatic ring and nitrile group of the reporter, remain clearly observable down to 1 ng/mL, with intensity decreasing proportionally to the streptavidin concentration.

caption: Variable focus reconstruction of the fracture surface for the k 67° specimen following tensile testing.
summary: Variable focus reconstruction displays the fracture surface of the k 67° specimen after tensile testing. In contrast to the ± 45° specimen, this surface exhibits a more uniform appearance. Peaks and valleys are distributed evenly across the cross-section, indicating a distinct fracture behavior compared to the other specimen orientation.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the nanoscale reverted austenite films in the 14Ni-CT sample.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging highlights the nanoscale reverted austenite films within the 14Ni-CT sample. This visualization confirms that the residual austenite in this sample is smaller in size than the blocky austenite observed in the 15Ni-CT variant, demonstrating distinct microstructural differences resulting from the varying nickel composition and processing.

caption: L-PBF fabricated scaffold structures labeled CU, CR, HH, and MH.
summary: This panel displays the L-PBF fabricated scaffold structures identified as CU, CR, HH, and MH. The photograph illustrates the physical geometry of these diverse samples, with a scale bar in millimeters included to provide a clear reference for the dimensions of the fabricated scaffolds used in the study.

caption: Scratch coefficient of friction (COF) profile as a function of track length for Ti6Al4V5Cr alloy under varying applied loads.
summary: The scratch COF profile for Ti6Al4V5Cr alloy is plotted against track length, revealing two distinct regions: a running-in zone followed by a steady-state zone. The data demonstrates that the COF increases with higher applied loads, reflecting the interaction between the indenter and the alloy surface during the scratch test.

caption: Bode-phase angle plots illustrating the frequency-dependent phase response of as-built and as-cast Co25Cr5Mo5W alloy specimens.
summary: Bode-phase angle plots are presented for the as-built and as-cast Co25Cr5Mo5W alloy specimens. These results, when analyzed alongside other EIS data, confirm that the as-built alloy develops a dense passive film more rapidly, ultimately displaying superior corrosion resistance and higher pitting potential compared to the as-cast counterpart due to its optimized microstructure.

caption: Experimental data compared against I-V curves generated via TSEC using SDM parameters extracted by the SNF-TSEC approach for the RTC France PV solar cell.
summary: This panel displays the I-V curves generated via the TSEC method for an RTC France PV solar cell. The generated curves, based on SDM physical parameters extracted through the SNF-TSEC approach, demonstrate a close alignment with experimental data across the entire voltage range, validating the accuracy of the parameter extraction technique.

caption: EBSD image quality map overlaid with grain boundaries and a corresponding kernel average misorientation map for the TA7 alloy layer.
summary: The TA7 alloy layer is characterized using EBSD image quality and kernel average misorientation mapping. These visualizations reveal the microstructural state of the recrystallization matrix, highlighting the distribution of grain boundaries and local misorientation gradients, which are indicative of the dislocation density and internal strain within the TA7 material structure.

caption: Isolated austenite matrix phase extracted from the DP-RVE, visualized with an inverse pole figure (IPF) color scheme to represent crystallographic orientation.
summary: The austenite matrix phase is isolated from the dual-phase representative volume element to highlight its individual structural contribution. By applying an inverse pole figure (IPF) coloring scheme, the crystallographic orientation of the 215 matrix grains within the 3D model is clearly distinguished for subsequent crystal plasticity finite element analysis.

caption: Stability testing of the strain sensors conducted through repeated tensile and release cycles at specific strain levels of 30, 60, 90, 120, and 150 με, with 10 cycles performed for each level.
summary: Stability of the alumina thin film strain sensors is evaluated through repeated tensile and release cycle experiments. The sensors were subjected to stability tests at strain levels of 30, 60, 90, 120, and 150 με, with 10 cycles performed per strain level to demonstrate consistent performance across varying mechanical loads.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of Mn nanoparticles-coated Cu foil in 0.1 M KOH at 100 mV/s, comparing the electrochemical response between the first and second cycles.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram illustrates the electrochemical response of Mn nanoparticles-coated copper foil in 0.1 M KOH at a scan rate of 100 mV/s. By comparing the first and second cycles, the plot reveals a distinct electrochemical profile attributed to the presence of the manganese nanoparticles on the copper substrate surface.

caption: Relative density heat map for a specimen printed at a laser power of 100 W, showing powder adhesion due to excess energy radiation.
summary: Relative density heat map for a specimen printed at 100 W laser power reveals the internal quality. Excess energy radiates to surrounding areas, causing partial melting of powder outside the intended processing zone, which then adheres to the specimen. This map illustrates how process parameters significantly influence the overall forming quality.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern confirming the BCC crystal structure of the Mg24(Gd, Y)5 phases.
summary: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) analysis of the micron-sized precipitates near the grain boundaries confirms their identity as Mg24(Gd, Y)5 phases. The diffraction pattern indicates a body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal structure, providing definitive evidence of the phase composition within the GWZ831K layer of the as-deposited material.

caption: Principal component analysis results illustrating the identification of significant Raman ratios used to differentiate between various graphene nanoplatelet concentrations within the printed resin matrix.
summary: This panel displays the results of principal component analysis performed on Raman data. The analysis successfully identified significant Raman ratios that serve as discriminating features for different graphene nanoplatelet concentrations, providing a robust statistical basis for distinguishing the material composition of the 3D-printed specimens based on their spectral signatures.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Cr–Ni system representing the phase stability.
summary: The Cr–Ni binary phase diagram illustrates the phase stability of the system. The diagram confirms that Cr and Ni exhibit complete solid solubility, a property that prevents the formation of brittle intermetallics, thereby ensuring the structural integrity and mechanical reliability of the alloy system in various engineering applications.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the creep fracture surface for the CL specimen, showing a dimpled morphology.
summary: The CL specimen, processed with low current and speed, exhibits a creep fracture surface characterized by dimples. This structural feature is associated with the larger pitch observed in these specimens, providing insight into the ductile failure mechanism occurring under the specified low-current and low-speed creep testing conditions.

caption: Shear stress–displacement curve derived from finite element analysis (FEA) of the sCFRTP specimen.
summary: This panel presents the shear stress–displacement curve obtained through finite element analysis. The data characterizes the mechanical response of the sCFRTP specimen under shear loading, providing the foundational stress values used to evaluate failure criteria and the onset of resin damage near the precrack tip during the simulation.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms showing the glass transition temperatures (Tg) for M-ABS, L-ABS, and H-ABS feedstocks, measured at 91.62, 96.64, and 90.94 °C, respectively.
summary: DSC curves reveal distinct glass transition temperatures for the three ABS feedstocks. The L-ABS feedstock exhibits the highest Tg at 96.64 °C, while M-ABS and H-ABS show lower values of 91.62 °C and 90.94 °C, respectively, indicating differences in the temperature required for softening and chain entanglement during processing.

caption: Magnitude of the Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra for Ni foil and nanoNi-P modified electrodes deposited at varying current densities ranging from -12.5 to -200,000 μA cm⁻².
summary: The magnitude of the Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra reveals the local bonding environment of nickel atoms in Ni foil and nanoNi-P electrodes. By analyzing these spectra across different deposition current densities, the study characterizes the structural evolution and coordination environment of nickel within the modified electrode materials.

caption: Atomic model of the 32-atom γ′-Ni3Al supercell centered on a nickel atom, illustrating the integration of refractory M (Ta or W) atoms into the crystal lattice.
summary: Representing the 32-atom supercell model of γ′-Ni3Al centered on a nickel atom, this panel highlights the structural arrangement of the lattice. Refractory elements like tantalum or tungsten are added to specific substitutional sites. This model serves as a basis for calculations regarding the impact of refractory additions on material behavior.

caption: Spin-wave dispersion spectra showing the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone for the base permalloy-in-cobalt structure with a squeeze ratio of s = 1.0.
summary: This panel displays the spin-wave dispersion spectra for the base permalloy-in-cobalt structure at a squeeze ratio of s = 1.0. It maps the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths within the first Brillouin zone, providing a baseline for understanding the magnetic excitation characteristics of the uncompressed material system.

caption: Simple Cubic unit cell topology representation for the scaffold constitutive unit.
summary: The Simple Cubic unit cell is illustrated as a topology representation for the scaffold's constitutive unit. This basic lattice structure represents the most straightforward geometric arrangement for the scaffold, serving as a reference point for comparing the mechanical and transport properties of more complex, non-orthogonal unit cell designs.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves comparing the corrosion behavior of rolled TA31, SLM TA31-1000, and SLM TA31-900 alloys in simulated seawater.
summary: This figure displays the potentiodynamic polarization curves for rolled TA31, SLM TA31-1000, and SLM TA31-900 alloys tested in simulated seawater. The data reveals distinct corrosion resistance profiles, with rolled TA31 showing moderate resistance (Rf = 1.048 × 10^6 Ω cm^2) and SLM TA31-1000 exhibiting the lowest resistance (Rf = 0.93 × 10^6 Ω cm^2).

caption: Evolution of dimensionless Peclet (Pe) and Marangoni (Ma) numbers as a function of oscillation amplitude in the molten pool.
summary: This line graph illustrates the variation of dimensionless Peclet and Marangoni numbers within the molten pool relative to changes in oscillation amplitude. The calculated Pe and Ma values are presented to characterize the transport phenomena, demonstrating how these dimensionless parameters respond to the specified variations in the oscillation amplitude during processing.

caption: Storage modulus (E′) temperature dependence for MPA-250 samples subjected to varying γ-radiation doses, showing stability at lower doses and a decrease at 10^6 Gy.
summary: Storage modulus (E′) curves for MPA-250 demonstrate that irradiation doses of 10^4 and 10^5 Gy do not significantly alter the material's stiffness. However, a higher dose of 10^6 Gy results in a measurable decrease in the storage modulus, reaching a value of 3530.8 MPa.

caption: Deconvolution of the 29Si MAS NMR spectrum for potassium-activated slag 3 paste with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 1.9.
summary: This 29Si MAS NMR spectrum represents the potassium-activated slag 3 paste with a SiO2/K2O ratio of 1.9. The spectrum appears broader than that of the unactivated slag. Deconvolution reveals peaks compatible with (1Al) and potentially (2Al) configurations, reflecting the increased connectivity of silicon to aluminum in the activated matrix.

caption: Contour plot showing the impact of pitch angle and fibre spacing on the damaged volume of Bouligand-structured polymer composites subjected to impact.
summary: This contour plot maps the damaged volume of Bouligand-structured polymers against pitch angle and fibre spacing. As part of a comparative analysis, it highlights how specific design parameters influence the extent of internal damage, allowing researchers to determine optimal structural geometries that minimize the overall volume of damage under impact loading.

caption: Evolution of magnetic moments for 4a and 4b sites as a function of milling time in the austenitic phase at 300 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of magnetic moments for 4a and 4b sites in the austenitic phase at 300 K. The net magnetic moments of Mn atoms significantly decrease with increasing milling time, confirming the influence of microstructural defects on the magnetism from a microscopic point of view.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to extracts from milled Ti.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy imaging of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 72 hours of exposure to milled Ti extracts is presented. The Live/Dead staining method highlights the live (green) and dead (red) cells, allowing for a detailed evaluation of the biocompatibility of milled titanium after a 72-hour exposure duration.

caption: Photograph of the Panalytical X'pert Pro X-ray diffraction system utilized for phase identification.
summary: This image displays the Panalytical X'pert Pro X-ray diffraction device located at the Physical Science Department of Al-Nahrain University. The equipment is utilized for conducting X-ray investigations to determine the crystalline phases present in the examined materials, as referenced in the study's methodology for phase characterization.

caption: Tensile strength versus elongation to failure for Mo5 alloy and reference materials at 4.2 K.
summary: Tensile strength versus elongation to failure is shown for the Mo5 alloy at 4.2 K. The plot illustrates that the Mo5 alloy retains tensile properties similar to stainless steels, effectively overcoming the strength-ductility trade-off observed in other conventional alloys and HEAs/MEAs at liquid-helium temperatures.

caption: Time-resolved WAXS patterns for the PVDF-HFP/EG composite, highlighting the characteristic (002) reflection of expanded graphite marked by an arrow alongside PVDF polymorph reflection indexes.
summary: Representing a significantly different crystallization behavior compared to the pure polymer, this panel shows the WAXS patterns for the PVDF-HFP/EG composite. The characteristic (002) reflection of expanded graphite is clearly detectable and marked by an arrow, providing insight into the structural evolution of the composite during the printing process.

caption: Surface curvature distribution of the enlarged precipitated phase, predominantly displaying green coloration.
summary: The surface curvature of the enlarged precipitated phase is mapped, with the majority of the surface appearing green. This distribution indicates that the precipitated phase possesses a smooth surface morphology, consistent with the interconnected hollow polyhedral network observed in the enlarged three-dimensional reconstruction.

caption: Columnar grains oriented along the build direction in the as-printed HEA.
summary: This optical micrograph highlights a specific region of the as-printed CuAlFeMnNi HEA dominated by columnar grains. These grains are clearly oriented along the build direction, as indicated by the white arrows, demonstrating the directional solidification characteristics inherent to the printing process of this high-entropy alloy.

caption: Virtual dark-field (VDF) image generated from differential diffuse-scattering signals within the virtual aperture, visualizing the distribution of heterogeneous domains within the MEA matrix.
summary: Generated from differential diffuse-scattering signals, this virtual dark-field image reveals the presence of heterogeneous domains within the solution-treated MEA. The visualization process utilizes the intensity data captured within the virtual aperture to map the spatial distribution of these structural features across the analyzed zone axis.

caption: Distribution of diameters for compressive specimens across various print angles.
summary: This box plot illustrates the diameter distribution of compressive specimens fabricated at different print angles. The data indicates that all printed specimens consistently exhibit diameters slightly smaller than the specified ASTM standard, highlighting a systematic deviation in the geometric dimensions of the samples produced during the printing process.

caption: Original polarization curves of SLMed TC4 alloy samples subjected to PEP and MP surface treatments, measured in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel displays the original polarization curves for SLMed TC4 alloy specimens after undergoing PEP and MP surface treatments. The electrochemical measurements were conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution to evaluate the corrosion behavior of the alloy under these specific processing conditions, providing a baseline for subsequent analysis.

caption: Single shot Time-Of-Flight neutron diffraction pole figures and inverse pole figures for Sample 1, showing overall texture intensity distribution.
summary: Single shot Time-Of-Flight neutron diffraction results for Sample 1 are shown here. The plots capture the overall texture, including intensity distribution and max/min values for specific crystallographic directions. While the overall texture is well-represented, some detailed contours appear blurred compared to the referential EBSD data in panel (a).

caption: Lateral macroscopic view of a gyroid scaffold undergoing a 45-degree shear deformation mode during quasi-static compression testing.
summary: Captured during the testing process, this lateral macroscopic view illustrates the 45-degree shear deformation mode of the gyroid lattice structure. The image corroborates the specific shear-dominated failure mechanism observed in the gyroid scaffold under quasi-static compressive loading conditions, providing visual evidence of the structural response during the deformation evolution.

caption: Histogram of misorientation angles across the ER2205–Inconel 718 interface, showing the frequency distribution of boundary types.
summary: The misorientation angle distribution reveals that approximately 50% of boundaries fall within the 10–25° range. These low to medium-angle boundaries indicate sub-grain formation and partial recovery. The predominance of these boundaries is consistent with rapid cooling and repeated thermal exposure, which favors substructure formation over full recrystallization.

caption: Perturbation plot illustrating the sensitivity of penetration depth to input variables, specifically laser power, scanning speed, and powder feed rate.
summary: This perturbation plot quantifies how individual input variables influence the penetration depth. The analysis reveals distinct trends: laser power exhibits a positive correlation, scanning speed acts as a neutral factor, and powder flow rate shows a negative correlation, providing clear insight into the sensitivity of the process parameters.

caption: Feature importance ranking for the CP-S-P model, incorporating γ′ microstructural descriptors alongside composition and processing conditions to evaluate their contribution to mechanical property predictions.
summary: The CP-S-P model feature importance plot demonstrates the impact of including microstructural descriptors, specifically γ′ volume fraction and equivalent diameter, on mechanical property predictions. While these features contribute to the overall feature set, the analysis indicates they do not overwhelmingly dominate the predictions compared to composition and processing conditions.

caption: Inferred stress component distribution across the cross-section of an SLM-processed sample, derived from neutron diffraction strain measurements.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the spatial distribution of stress components within an SLM-manufactured sample. The data is derived from strain measurements obtained using the KOWARI engineering diffractometer. Markers overlaid on the plot indicate the specific locations where diffraction measurements were performed to calculate the internal stress state across the material cross-section.

caption: XRD diffraction pattern of as-built Hast-X superalloy after oxidation at 1000 °C.
summary: This panel displays the XRD diffraction pattern for the as-built Hast-X superalloy following oxidation at 1000 °C. The data provides structural information regarding the phase composition of the material under these specific thermal conditions, serving as a baseline for evaluating the oxidation resistance of the Hast-X alloy.

caption: Comparative compositional variation of alloying elements Mn and Mo within cementite precipitates before and after the step cooling process.
summary: This panel displays the compositional fluctuations of alloying elements, specifically Mn and Mo, within cementite precipitates. The visualization highlights the changes in elemental distribution occurring before and after the step cooling treatment, providing insight into the stability and partitioning of these elements during the cooling process.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the AlxCo25Fe(50-x)Ni25 system showing phase stability as a function of Al content, with red and blue dashed lines marking 10.5 and 14.5 at. % Al concentrations.
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram illustrates the phase stability of the AlxCo25Fe(50-x)Ni25 system. By varying Al content, the system transitions from a single-phase fcc structure to a dual-phase fcc-B2-NiAl microstructure. The diagram highlights specific compositions at 10.5 and 14.5 at. % Al, which are critical for controlling the solidification mode.

caption: Cells treated with Free-DOX for 2 hours, displaying the distribution of the drug within the cellular environment.
summary: Cells treated with Free-DOX for a duration of 2 hours exhibit the intracellular distribution of the drug. This panel serves as a comparative benchmark for evaluating the drug delivery efficiency of the niosome-based formulations, with internalized nanoparticles observed surrounding the nuclei of the treated cells.

caption: Ragone plot comparing the energy density and power density of the Co-Ni/rGO //3D rGO aerogel supercapacitor against various Ni-Co composite materials reported in literature.
summary: The Ragone plot compares the energy and power density of the assembled supercapacitor with other Ni-Co related composite materials. Notably, the device achieves a high energy density of 39.58 W h kg⁻¹ at a low power density of 200 W kg⁻¹, demonstrating superior performance relative to existing literature benchmarks.

caption: Binary Al-Yb phase diagram computed using Pandat software, indicating the specific compositions utilized for the experimental alloys.
summary: The binary Al-Yb phase diagram, generated via Pandat software, serves as a reference for the alloy compositions investigated in this study. It provides the thermodynamic foundation for understanding the formation of the Al3Yb phase and the eutectic colony structures observed in the experimental alloy samples.

caption: Tensile strength versus elongation to failure for in-situ alloyed Fe–Mn–Al–C LWSs, compared against DED-manufactured stainless (ST), precipitation-hardened (PH), and maraging (MA) steels.
summary: Tensile strength is plotted as a function of elongation to failure to compare the mechanical performance of in-situ alloyed Fe–Mn–Al–C LWSs with other DED-manufactured steels. This comparison includes stainless (ST), precipitation-hardened (PH), and maraging (MA) steels, providing a benchmark for the LWSs' mechanical properties.

caption: Mass spectrum of pristine FPEA-ProGly polymer film serving as a negative control.
summary: The mass spectrum of the pristine FPEA-ProGly polymer film is presented as a negative control. Analysis confirms that this sample shows no evidence of peptide attachment, establishing a baseline for the subsequent coupling experiments. The measurement was conducted over a 500 µm by 500 µm area to ensure consistency.

caption: Logarithmic Frenkel defect count for Cu-10at%Ni alloy subjected to 4 keV PKA energy, plotted against time along the [100] orientation.
summary: This panel displays the Frenkel defect logarithm for Cu-10at%Ni at 4 keV PKA energy. The data shows the characteristic rapid increase to a peak followed by stabilization. Compared to pure Cu, the increased Ni content effectively reduces the maximum number of defects observed during the peak stage.

caption: Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) distribution of the MBT molecule.
summary: The HOMO distribution of the MBT molecule is visualized to assess its electronic properties. Analysis indicates that the contributions of C1 and C3 atoms to the HOMO orbital are comparatively weak, suggesting limited reactivity at these specific sites within the molecular structure during electronic transitions or chemical bonding processes.

caption: Energy barrier evolution for twin fault formation (γutf) in the complex composition γ′ phase as a function of increasing twin thickness, representing a twin growth event.
summary: This panel illustrates the energy barrier for twin fault formation (γutf) in the complex composition γ′ phase. As twin thickness increases, the barrier energy is continuously lowered, facilitating twin growth events. This confirms that the complex composition γ′ phase exhibits a lower energy cost for twin formation compared to Ni3Al.

caption: Molecular dynamics snapshot showing pore distribution at a laser power of 250 eV/ps and scanning speed of 4 Å/ps, highlighting the presence of through-holes.
summary: At a low laser power of 250 eV/ps and a scanning speed of 4 Å/ps, the simulation reveals the formation of through-holes. These structural features are highlighted within the red solid box, though they are not recognized as pores by the OVITO software, resulting in a lower calculated porosity value.

caption: Liquidus projection of the Al-Ce-Ni alloy system, illustrating the phase stability regions and the formation of Al11Ce3 and Al23Ni6Ce4 phases.
summary: This panel displays the liquidus projection of the Al-Ce-Ni ternary system. It identifies the stability regions for phases such as Al11Ce3 and Al23Ni6Ce4. These phases are relevant to the Al-10.5Ce-3.1Ni-1.2Mn alloy, although the specific ternary composition studied may not always produce the phases predicted by this diagram.

caption: Measured fluorescence emission spectrum of a 10 mM fluorescein solution obtained using the fiber-based configuration shown in panel a.
summary: The measured emission spectrum of a 10 mM fluorescein solution is presented, serving as the reference baseline for the study. This fiber-based configuration provides the initial quantification of fluorescence intensity, against which the performance of subsequent grating coupler-based configurations is compared to evaluate signal changes.

caption: Spatial variation of Young's modulus across the Opt1 design solution, calculated using different homogenization approaches.
summary: Young's modulus distribution is mapped across the Opt1 design solution to evaluate the impact of homogenization methods. This visualization highlights how the material stiffness varies spatially within the sphere, providing a comparative view of the mechanical properties derived from classical mixture rules versus advanced homogenization techniques.

caption: Co K-edge EXAFS k2·χ(k) functions for Co/ZrO2 and Co1Ni1/ZrO2 catalysts, highlighting oscillations near k ≈ 4 Å⁻¹ after 10 h of DRM.
summary: Co K-edge EXAFS k2·χ(k) functions for Co-based catalysts are shown after 10 h of DRM. A qualitative assessment reveals a slight modulation of oscillations around k ≈ 4 Å⁻¹ for both catalysts, which is attributed to the presence of a light backscatterer interacting with the Co atoms during the reaction process.

caption: Parity plot displaying the correlation between predicted and experimental values for the response metric σBF as determined by Full Factorial analysis.
summary: Representing the correlation between predicted and experimental values for the response metric σBF, this parity plot is part of the Full Factorial analysis results. It serves to validate the model's performance by comparing calculated outputs against actual experimental data points for this specific mechanical response metric.

caption: Top-down view of an isolated AB RLD 10% strut showing node interference artifacts at the extremities compared to a caliper measurement tool, with surface particle attachment and localized strut thinning highlighted.
summary: This panel displays an isolated AB RLD 10% strut analyzed via micro-CT. Node regions cause inaccuracies in sphere and ray methods, resulting in erroneously lower wall thickness at extremities. In contrast, the caliper tool provides more reliable measurements, while surface particles and localized thinning are clearly identified in the visualization.

caption: Cross-sectional micrograph of the d06 T1 re-extruded composite specimen exhibiting insufficient TPU wrapping.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the cross-section of a d06 T1 re-extruded composite bead. The image highlights a specific structural deficiency where the TPU component shows an insufficient wrap around the core, distinguishing this specimen from other re-extruded beads that otherwise show minimal differences in their internal structure.

caption: Chronopotentiometry curve of the Ru3Ni3NAs catalyst recorded in 0.05 M H2SO4 at a constant current density of 5 mA cm-2.
summary: The chronopotentiometry curve for Ru3Ni3NAs in 0.05 M H2SO4 evaluates the stability of the catalyst at a constant current density of 5 mA cm-2. This test provides essential data regarding the electrochemical robustness and performance retention of the Ru3Ni3NAs catalyst during continuous operation in the specified acidic electrolyte.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ti-W system illustrating the equilibrium relationships between the body-centered cubic (BCC_A2), hexagonal close-packed (HCP_A3), and liquid phases.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the Ti-W system, as reported by Jonsson, delineates the thermodynamic stability regions for three distinct phases. The system is characterized by the presence of body-centered cubic (BCC_A2), hexagonal close-packed (HCP_A3), and liquid phases, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's equilibrium behavior across varying compositions and temperatures.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of tenocytes in phase II culture on MEW wavy scaffolds, highlighting cell distribution and viability.
summary: This fluorescence microscopy image shows tenocytes in phase II culture on MEW wavy scaffolds. The dynamic group exhibited a significantly higher rate of cell viability at 94% compared to the 85% observed in the static group, confirming that dynamic stimulation enhances cell survival and maintenance during the second phase of culture.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of the austenite phase in the T200 specimen.
summary: This panel displays the kernel average misorientation map for the T200 austenite specimen. Quantitative evaluation of the misorientation data reveals a KAM value of 1.28°, which characterizes the local lattice distortion and strain accumulation within the austenite grains following the T200 processing condition.

caption: Contact angle measurements of SilMA hydrogels with varying AA dosages and 0.001 part PEGDMA, assessed after 96 hours of water incubation at room temperature.
summary: This bar chart presents contact angle measurements for SilMA hydrogels with varying AA dosages and constant PEGDMA. Results indicate that the hydrophilicity of the composite hydrogel decreases upon the addition of 0.2 part of AA, evidenced by an increase in the contact angle from 43.2 ± 9.6° to 54.5 ± 3.1°.

caption: Toughness contour map for low contrast and low matrix hardening rate materials, demonstrating the optimal microstructure location.
summary: Representing toughness for low contrast, low hardening rate materials, this plot shows the dependence on volume fraction and grain size. The optimal microstructure is marked by a black diamond. For low contrast materials, the optimal volume fraction shifts from low to high when the hardening rate switches from high to low.

caption: Representative immunofluorescence images showing the distribution of OPN, OCN, and CD31 markers within the defect area at 12 weeks.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging visualizes the spatial distribution of OPN, OCN, and CD31. These images support the quantitative findings, demonstrating the presence of key osteogenic and angiogenic markers within the regenerated bone tissue, confirming the biological activity promoted by the TM/HA/PLCL scaffold at 12 weeks.

caption: Relative strength plotted against relative density for TAOR and Kelvin cells, illustrating the mechanical performance according to the Gibson-Ashby model.
summary: This graph displays the relative strength of TAOR and Kelvin cells in relation to their relative density. Utilizing the Gibson-Ashby model, the interpolated curves characterize the mechanical strength behavior of these cellular architectures, highlighting how variations in density correlate with the overall strength performance of the tested material samples.

caption: Impedance modulus plot of Gr/AlNiTiCrNbx coatings displaying frequency-dependent impedance values.
summary: This impedance modulus plot for the Gr/AlNiTiCrNb0.30 coating demonstrates a nearly linear relationship in the low-frequency region. The data indicates that the impedance value of the coating gradually decreases as the frequency increases, providing insight into the frequency-dependent electrochemical response of the material.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image illustrating the macro-roughness observed on the struts of an additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V lattice structure.
summary: Atomic force microscopy reveals the macro-surface roughness of additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V lattice struts. The analysis identifies homogenous but high roughness values ranging between 460 and 510 μm. These significant surface irregularities are critical features that promote structural failure during cyclic loading conditions, as evidenced by the observed lattice performance.

caption: Photographic sequence of 3D printed PlasCLEAR resin catheters, showing as-printed, post-treated, crimped, stretched, and relaxed states, illustrating limited elastic recovery.
summary: PlasCLEAR resin catheters are displayed through a series of mechanical trials including crimping and stretching. Unlike the KeySplint Soft material, the PlasCLEAR catheter does not achieve elastic elongation, as it fails to return to its original shape after being subjected to tensile stress during the stretching trials.

caption: Fluorescent dye penetrant inspection of a WAAM wall section viewed normal to the build direction (BD), revealing alternating crack-like defects that align with the local welding direction.
summary: Fluorescent dye penetrant inspection of a WAAM wall section viewed normal to the build direction reveals crack-like defects. These defects are parallel to the local welding direction and exhibit an alternating pattern across the wall thickness, providing a clear visualization of internal structural discontinuities within the deposited material.

caption: Indentation strain rate versus time curves for NC Ni and NC Ni–Fe alloy specimens during the CLR test at four different strain rates.
summary: Indentation strain rate-time curves for NC Ni and NC Ni–Fe alloy are presented for four different strain rates during the CLR test. These curves illustrate the temporal evolution of the indentation strain rate, which is calculated using the load-displacement and displacement-time data obtained from the indentation experiments.

caption: Pair distribution function (PDF) profiles derived from SR-X-ray total scattering for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys with x = 0, 0.05, and 0.10, showing the local atomic structure of the BCC phase.
summary: This panel displays the pair distribution function profiles obtained from synchrotron X-ray total scattering for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys. These profiles characterize the local atomic structure of the BCC phase for varying aluminum concentrations of x = 0, 0.05, and 0.10, providing essential data for small-box structural refinements.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of nitrogen solubility in X50CrMoVN15 melt at 0.103 MPa, plotted alongside experimental nitrogen content values for PBF-LB/M samples processed at an exposure time of 80 µs.
summary: This CALPHAD-based thermodynamic calculation estimates nitrogen solubility in X50CrMoVN15 melt at 0.103 MPa. The plot integrates experimental nitrogen content data for PBF-LB/M samples, specifically highlighting the 0.474 mass% nitrogen concentration achieved at an 80 µs exposure time, providing a comparative analysis between theoretical solubility limits and actual processing outcomes.

caption: Projected density of states for Fe atoms within the Fe3Ni(111) bimetallic surface, showing a d-band center shift to −2.00 eV.
summary: The projected density of states for Fe atoms in the Fe3Ni(111) bimetallic surface is shown, with the d-band center shifting to −2.00 eV. This electronic modification, alongside the shift in Ni, demonstrates how the bimetallic interaction optimizes the surface properties to favor enhanced catalytic activity for the Fe3Ni(111) system.

caption: Spatial distribution pattern of discrete laser pulses generated during operation in the PW mode.
