summary: This panel displays the spatial distribution of individual laser pulses resulting from the PW mode operation. It illustrates how the pulsed energy is localized in space, providing a clear visual representation of the discrete nature of the laser track produced under these specific emission conditions.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots showing the inverse square capacitance versus potential for Ni-Cr-based alloy specimens subjected to different scan strategies in a borate buffer solution.
summary: Mott-Schottky analysis of Ni-Cr-based alloys in borate buffer solution reveals the semiconductive nature of the passive layer. The plots demonstrate that different scan strategies influence the defect density within the passive film, with higher dislocation densities in the specimens correlating to lower overall defect densities as calculated from these measurements.

caption: Larger bcc system configuration used for calculating elastic constants, shown with X direction horizontally and Z direction vertically.
summary: This larger bcc system configuration is specifically designed for the calculation of elastic constants. Following energy minimization across 20 bcc systems, this model represents the system with the lowest overall energy. The orientation aligns the X direction horizontally and the Z direction vertically to ensure accurate mechanical property determination.

caption: B-H hysteresis loop measured at 6% strain under an external field.
summary: This panel illustrates the B-H hysteresis loop for the sample at 6% strain. It is used to analyze the evolution of magnetic characteristics under increasing mechanical load, providing data points for the broader investigation into how strain modifies the magnetic behavior of the material under external fields.

caption: High-magnification SEM detail of the 185-S specimen showing compositional inhomogeneity with a non-uniform distribution of fine intragranular (α IG) and grain boundary (α GB) α-precipitates.
summary: This high-magnification SEM image of the 185-S specimen demonstrates significant compositional inhomogeneity. The β-matrix contains a non-uniform distribution of very fine α-precipitates, identified as both intragranular (α IG) and grain boundary (α GB) phases. These features indicate a complex microstructural state resulting from the specific manufacturing process.

caption: Gamma-prime phase composition trends relative to changing bulk Mo content, showing minimal impact on precipitate chemistry.
summary: Increasing the bulk Mo content shows negligible effect on the overall gamma-prime phase composition, with the exception of a slight increase in Co content. The plot displays these trends relative to the RR1000 patent range, which is shaded to denote the standard compositional limits for this alloy.

caption: Longitudinal residual stress distribution on the cross-section of Case B measured via the contour method.
summary: Case B illustrates the longitudinal residual stress distribution on the cross-section, obtained through the contour method. The plot maps the Y-direction stress variations across the sample, allowing for a detailed assessment of the internal stress state and the influence of the specific processing parameters associated with Case B.

caption: Mechanical (X1) M-DfX assessment radar chart for the energy infrastructure case study, illustrating the modified weighting of individual properties within the power transformer component.
summary: This radar chart presents the mechanical (X1) M-DfX assessment specifically tailored for the energy infrastructure case study. It highlights the power transformer component, where the weights assigned to individual mechanical properties have been systematically modified to reflect specific design requirements and performance criteria relevant to the infrastructure's operational environment.

caption: Surface roughness measurements (Sa) taken at ten distinct locations along the length of AlSi10Mg, 316 L SS, and Ti6Al4V specimens, illustrating the trend of improved surface finishing.
summary: Surface roughness measurements (Sa) taken at ten distinct locations along the length of AlSi10Mg, 316 L SS, and Ti6Al4V specimens, illustrating the trend of improved surface finishing. Improvement along the specimen length is evident, though Ti specimens show less improvement and reduced uniformity after polishing compared to the other materials.

caption: HAADF-STEM cross-sectional image of the passive layer, highlighting the protective Pt coating (red arrows) and unoxidized metallic particles (yellow circles) embedded within the oxide layer.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image reveals the cross-sectional structure of a passive oxide layer. Key features include a protective Pt coating, indicated by red arrows, and metallic particles that remain unoxidized, located at cell boundaries and partially embedded in the oxide, as highlighted by yellow circles.

caption: SAED pattern of the fcc A1 phase, marked by a green dot, obtained from the 1000HT sample after 32% strain at 600 °C.
summary: This selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern corresponds to the fcc A1 phase, identified by a green dot, in the 1000HT sample compressed at 600 °C. The diffraction data was used to characterize the phase structure following 32% strain, confirming the identity of the fcc A1 phase.

caption: Binary phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium relationships within the plagioclase mineral series found in lunar regolith.
summary: This panel displays the binary phase diagram for the plagioclase mineral series, which is a key component of lunar regolith. The diagram delineates the equilibrium phase boundaries for the plagioclase solid solution, providing essential thermodynamic data for understanding the crystallization and mineralogical evolution of materials within the lunar environment.

caption: Crack opening stress plotted as a function of dwell time for a stationary crack tip under a loading time of 1 s, ΔK of 25.37 MPa√m, and load ratio R = 0.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between dwell time and crack opening stress at a stationary crack tip. The data is obtained under specific loading conditions, including a 1 s loading time, a stress intensity factor range of 25.37 MPa√m, and a load ratio of zero, with dwell periods superimposed on the peak load.

caption: Yield strength distribution across different heat treatment themes, highlighting outliers and reduced sample sizes.
summary: Yield stress follows a downward trend similar to UTS, with stress-relieving providing the highest values. HIP treatments lower the yield strength, compounded by pore-closure limitations in specimens without contour. The boxplot is based on three values instead of five, marked by a red oval due to fracture stress limitations.

caption: Tensile modulus radar plot comparing multi-material composites with varying face-to-core ratios (f = 0 to 0.8) against the monolithic core baseline.
summary: This radar plot illustrates the tensile modulus performance of multi-material composites across different face-to-core ratios. The gray region denotes the monolithic core performance, while color-coded values highlight percentage variations. These trends reinforce the critical role of the face material in withstanding tensile loads during mechanical testing.

caption: Isolated 3D morphology of the Si phase within the ternary eutectic structure of Alloy B.
summary: This panel focuses on the 3D morphology of the Si phase, isolated from the ternary eutectic network of Alloy B. Using FIB-SEM tomography data, the reconstruction reveals the distinct structural features and spatial configuration of the Si phase, contributing to the overall understanding of the alloy's fine eutectic architecture.

caption: SEM-EDS analysis comparing the chemical composition of the matrix and white particles located at the melt-pool boundaries in AP 6061-0.8Ti.
summary: SEM-EDS analysis of the matrix and white particles reveals the presence of Ti-enriched particles primarily located at the melt-pool boundaries. This compositional mapping confirms the segregation of alloying elements during the solidification of the AP 6061-0.8Ti alloy.

caption: Comprehensive flowchart illustrating the fatigue strength assessment methodology for additive manufactured AISI 316L specimens.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic approach for evaluating the fatigue strength of additive manufactured AISI 316L samples. The methodology integrates experimental fatigue testing data with machine learning techniques to provide a robust assessment framework, serving as the foundational process for the study's analysis of material performance under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Representative uniaxial tensile stress-strain curve for the F30 configuration.
summary: This panel displays the representative uniaxial tensile stress-strain curve for the F30 configuration. The data was obtained through tensile testing of printed bars to evaluate mechanical properties. This plot serves as a baseline for comparing the mechanical performance of support-free specimens printed at a 30 µm layer thickness.

caption: Major axis size of precipitates measured in the direct aged condition.
summary: This bar chart depicts the major axis size of precipitates in the direct aged condition. Data for region A indicates that the size of these coarse gamma-prime-prime precipitates suggests their strengthening contribution is governed by the Orowan mechanism, providing key parameters for calculating the material's mechanical response and strengthening behavior.

caption: Immunofluorescence imaging of osteogenic antibodies (ALP, BMP2, RUNX2, OCN, OPN) in MC3T3-E1 cells on PEEK, 40%HA-PEEK, and 40%HA-2%Ag-PEEK.
summary: Immunofluorescence analysis shows the spatial distribution of osteogenic markers. The fluorescence intensity of ALP, BMP2, and RUNX2 was notably more apparent in cells cultured on 40%HA-PEEK and 40%HA-2%Ag-PEEK compared to those on PEEK, suggesting that these modified surfaces effectively enhance early-stage osteogenic antibody expression.

caption: High-resolution EDX elemental maps illustrating the spatial distribution of Al, Si, and Mg within the AlSi10Mg microstructure.
summary: High-resolution EDX elemental mapping provides a detailed spatial distribution of the primary constituent elements in the unmodified AlSi10Mg alloy. The maps confirm the presence of Si-rich eutectic phases located between solidification cells, alongside distinct Mg segregation at the cell boundaries, consistent with the expected microstructural characteristics of this material.

caption: Vertical deposition orientation utilized in multi-directional WAAM to enable the fabrication of complex overhang structures without requiring additional support systems.
summary: Vertical deposition is a key strategy within positional or multi-directional WAAM, allowing for the fabrication of overhang structures. By utilizing this specific orientation, the process eliminates the need for support structures and external positioners, thereby enhancing manufacturing flexibility and economic efficiency during the production of complex metallic components.

caption: Density of states representation for the Cr-doped TiNi3–Cr1/C interface.
summary: This panel illustrates the density of states for the TiNi3–Cr1/C interface. Analysis of this electronic structure reveals how Cr doping alters the bonding characteristics compared to the clean interface, contributing to the overall understanding of how specific dopants tune the electrical conductivity and band structure of TiNi3/C.

caption: Compressive load and strength values of PEEK dental implants fabricated at varying nozzle temperatures.
summary: This panel displays the mean compressive load and strength values for PEEK dental implants printed at different nozzle temperatures. The data illustrates the mechanical performance of the implants as a function of the printing temperature, providing a quantitative assessment of how thermal processing parameters influence the structural integrity of the final dental components.

caption: Comparative bar chart summarizing the Young's modulus and hardness values derived from nanoindentation testing across the three specified melt pool regions.
summary: This bar chart summarizes the Young's modulus and hardness values derived from nanoindentation testing across the three specified melt pool regions. The data provides a quantitative comparison of the mechanical properties for the transverse sections, melt pool boundary, and longitudinal sections, reflecting the localized variations in material response within the melt pool.

caption: Overview of the electron beam additive manufacturing device, including the vacuum chamber and integrated workbench components.
summary: This photograph displays the electron beam additive manufacturing device, which serves as the primary hardware for the deposition process. The system incorporates a six-axis workbench, an electron gun, and a vacuum chamber, forming the core infrastructure required for the controlled fabrication of TiAl intermetallic components.

caption: Relaxed 125-atom SQS supercell model of the BCC MoNbTaTiV high-entropy alloy, illustrating the atomic arrangement with Mo (puce), Nb (green), Ta (blue), Ti (black), and V (red) atoms.
summary: This panel displays the 125-atom SQS supercell of the BCC MoNbTaTiV alloy following a full structural relaxation. The atomic model highlights the specific distribution of the five constituent elements—Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and V—within the BCC lattice structure, providing a visual representation of the alloy's simulated atomic configuration.

caption: EDS spectrum 4 identifying an α-Al(Mn,Fe)Si dispersoid within the Base+Mn alloy sample in the T6 condition, as shown in panel d.
summary: This EDS spectrum characterizes a specific particle observed in the Base+Mn alloy after T6 treatment. The analysis identifies the particle as an α-Al(Mn,Fe)Si dispersoid, highlighting the influence of manganese addition on the formation of specific intermetallic phases within the alloy microstructure during the T6 treatment.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectrum of the Ti3C2Tx MXene dispersion, featuring distinct peaks at 770 nm and 320 nm, with an inset photograph showing the stable aqueous colloidal solution.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectrum of the Ti3C2Tx MXene dispersion exhibits characteristic peaks at approximately 770 nm and 320 nm, consistent with reported data. A photograph of the dilute aqueous dispersion, shown in the inset, confirms the typical greenish color of the stable colloidal solution.

caption: Tabulated structural parameters for the 1G111–10% BaTiO3 metamaterial structure, summarizing key geometric dimensions and design specifications.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive summary of the structural parameters for the 1G111–10% BaTiO3 metamaterial. It serves as a quantitative reference for the geometric dimensions and design specifications of the printed structure, complementing the qualitative morphological observations provided by the SEM images in the other panels.

caption: Asymptotic escape speed from the Sun plotted against spacecraft wet mass for various launch vehicles, including heritage data and current Interstellar Probe study baselines, with upper limit calculations for Star Ship Superheavy included.
summary: This line graph illustrates the relationship between asymptotic escape speed from the Sun and spacecraft wet mass across multiple launch vehicle configurations. It incorporates heritage planning data, specific study baselines, and recent upper limit calculations for the Star Ship Superheavy, providing a comprehensive overview of performance trends for interstellar mission planning.

caption: Voltage and Faradaic efficiency evolution over time for a Ni-infiltrated cathode SOEC during galvanostatic testing at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻².
summary: This plot illustrates the electrochemical performance of a Ni-infiltrated cathode SOEC under galvanostatic conditions at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻². By tracking voltage and Faradaic efficiency, the data provides insight into the stability of pure Ni infiltration, serving as a comparative reference for the Co-containing and Cu-containing cathode variants.

caption: Loss modulus (E'') of TPU 95A, 82A, and 70A samples plotted against frequency, demonstrating viscous energy dissipation characteristics at temperatures between 30 °C and 120 °C.
summary: Loss modulus behavior for TPU samples is shown during frequency sweeps at temperatures above the glass transition. The data indicates that E'' initially increases slightly with frequency at lower ranges, which highlights enhanced viscous energy dissipation occurring at higher strain rates for the various TPU compositions tested.

caption: Load-displacement (P-h) curve for SLM-316L steel subjected to a nanoindentation creep test at a loading rate of 10 mN/min.
summary: Representing the indentation response at a 10 mN/min loading rate, this curve demonstrates the relationship between applied load and displacement for 316L stainless steel. The plot captures the initial loading phase up to 20 mN and the subsequent holding period, highlighting the creep-induced displacement characteristic of the material's heterostructure.

caption: Reaction network diagram illustrating the six chemical pathways for methyl formate decomposition and related species transformation.
summary: This reaction network diagram depicts the six distinct chemical pathways involved in methyl formate decomposition. Based on established literature, the scheme provides the foundational framework for calculating reaction rates and determining stoichiometric coefficients. It serves as the primary model for understanding the kinetic interactions and chemical transformations within the investigated system.

caption: Field dependence of the temperature-integrated difference between field-cooled (FC) and zero-field-cooled (ZFC) magnetization for Fe-Cr-Ni alloys.
summary: This plot illustrates the field dependence of the temperature-integrated difference between FC and ZFC magnetization. Samples with lower iron content, specifically Fe 45.8 Cr 49 Ni 5.2 and Fe 50.7 Cr 46.7 Ni 2.6, demonstrate significantly reduced magnetic irreversibility across the entire field range compared to the iron-rich Fe 52.5 Cr 45.55 Ni 1.95 alloy.

caption: Principal azimuthal angle map derived from polarization imaging, showing the orientation distribution of the printed sample.
summary: Polarization imaging enables the calculation of this principal azimuthal angle map, which provides insight into the orientation characteristics of the printed sample. By analyzing the polarization state, this map complements the retardance data to offer a comprehensive view of the material's structural anisotropy resulting from the printing process.

caption: Supercell configuration constructed from multiple gamma-TiAl unit cells.
summary: Representing a larger atomic arrangement, this supercell is composed of multiple gamma-TiAl unit cells. This model allows for the simulation of bulk-like properties and the study of alloying element distributions, such as Nb, within the gamma-TiAl phase lattice structure.

caption: Absolute error distribution across the domain comparing ANN-predicted values against numerical solutions.
summary: Panel (b) displays the absolute error distribution resulting from the comparison between the ANN-predicted Nusselt number and the corresponding numerical solutions. This plot quantifies the accuracy of the algorithm across the domain, highlighting the deviation between the machine learning model predictions and the established numerical benchmark data.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of FA, illustrating the mass loss profile during heating.
summary: The thermogravimetric analysis curve of FA displays the mass loss behavior during the heating process. Analysis of the TGA curve reveals that the residual carbon content of the FA sample is 47.75%, providing a quantitative measure of the material's thermal stability and carbon yield after the specified thermal treatment.

caption: Horizontal elemental concentration profile across the dealloyed interface, demonstrating a significant reduction in Ni content from 60 wt% to below 5 wt% within the residual superalloy.
summary: Elemental concentration profiles along the horizontal axis of the dealloyed interface reveal the effectiveness of the process. The data shows that Ni concentration in the residual superalloy drops substantially from 60 wt% to less than 5 wt%, while Ta, Re, and W contents show slight enrichment compared to the original alloy.

caption: Confocal fluorescence imaging of PANC-1 and MIA PaCa-2 cells demonstrating the cellular uptake efficiency of Au-GO@ZC-DOX nanovesicles.
summary: Confocal microscopy images reveal the cellular uptake of Au-GO@ZC-DOX nanovesicles within PANC-1 and MIA PaCa-2 cancer cell lines. These results confirm the successful internalization of the nanovesicles, which is a critical step for their intended application in targeted pancreatic cancer chemotherapy and phototherapy.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) spectra measured at open-circuit voltage (OCV) for STF and STF-Ni electrodes, showing lower ohmic resistance (R ohm) values for the STF-Ni configuration under reducing conditions.
summary: EIS measurements at OCV reveal the ohmic resistance characteristics of the cells. The data indicates that STF-Ni electrodes exhibit smaller R ohm values compared to STF electrodes under reducing conditions, specifically 0.5 Ω cm2 versus 0.55 Ω cm2, highlighting the improved electrochemical interface properties provided by the nickel-containing electrode material.

caption: Phonon dispersion curves and density of states for the α-YbNi intermetallic compound.
summary: Phonon dispersion curves and density of states for α-YbNi are calculated at the theoretical equilibrium volume. These results provide insight into the vibrational properties of the α-YbNi phase. The analysis is part of a broader study characterizing the stability and phonon behavior of various Yb-Ni intermetallic compounds.

caption: Cross-sectional atomic snapshot of the graphene interface after 900 cascades, showing the state of the graphene layer and surrounding amorphous carbon matrix.
summary: After 900 cascades, the cross-sectional snapshot reveals the persistent structural state of the graphene interface. The distribution of Gr-like purple spheres and amorphous grey carbon atoms illustrates the long-term effects of the irradiation cascades, providing insight into the stability and displacement behavior of the graphene within the matrix.

caption: Grain structure evolution during LDED processing modified by the introduction of hot forging.
summary: This panel shows the grain structure evolution during the LDED process when hot forging is introduced. The schematic demonstrates how the application of hot forging alters the solidification behavior compared to the standard LDED process, influencing the resulting grain morphology within the melt pool.

caption: Pressure gradient as a function of superficial velocity for the f 2 ccz 3 lattice structure, showing experimental data points and a second-order polynomial dashed line fit.
summary: Experimental pressure gradient data for the f 2 ccz 3 lattice structure are plotted against superficial velocity. The results are interpolated using a second-order polynomial, represented by a dashed line, which aligns with the Forchheimer equation form used to describe the pressure drop across these specific lattice structures.

caption: Energy variation profile for the Nb-Cu dimer model calculated using DFT and MD simulations with hybrid Lennard-Jones (LJ) and Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials.
summary: Energy variation data for the Nb-Cu dimer model is derived from DFT calculations and MD simulations incorporating hybrid LJ and EAM potentials. These results demonstrate a consistent trend with models using LJ parameters, validating the energetic behavior of the Nb-Cu dimer system within the computational framework provided.

caption: Galvanostatic polarization potential-time curve for the specimen subjected to 30% tensile strain.
summary: This panel illustrates the galvanostatic polarization response of the specimen after undergoing 30% tensile deformation. At this specific strain level, the potential difference between the L-PBF and conventional material curves becomes more pronounced compared to the unstrained state, highlighting the divergence in electrochemical performance under controlled current conditions.

caption: Magnified view of the eutectic point region within the Al-Sc binary phase diagram, highlighting the specific composition and temperature coordinates of the eutectic reaction.
summary: This panel presents a detailed examination of the eutectic point within the Al-Sc binary phase diagram. By focusing on this specific region, the plot clarifies the precise temperature and composition at which the liquid phase transforms into solid phases, offering critical insights into the eutectic solidification characteristics of the alloy.

caption: Oxygen fugacity relative to the IW buffer as a function of sulfur mole fraction in the Fe-Ni-S-C(-O) melt, with contours representing liquid alloy Ni/(Fe+Ni) ratios. Data points are color-coded by the X Mg ol of the coexisting olivine-polymorph, with error bars indicating 2 σ uncertainty.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the oxygen fugacity relative to the IW buffer as a function of the sulfur mole fraction in the Fe-Ni-S-C(-O) melt. The plot is contoured for various Ni/(Fe+Ni) ratios of the liquid alloy, with symbols color-coded by the magnesium mole fraction of the coexisting olivine-polymorph phase.

caption: Nyquist plots for SPS-processed 316L stainless steel, illustrating impedance evolution across 0, 24, 48, and 72 hours of PBS immersion, fitted with an equivalent circuit.
summary: This panel illustrates the electrochemical impedance response of SPS-processed 316L stainless steel during immersion in PBS. Impedance spectra were collected at 0, 24, 48, and 72 hours, and the resulting Nyquist plots, fitted with an equivalent circuit, provide insight into the material's electrochemical stability and surface degradation throughout the immersion period.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) curves for non-inoculated and TiC-inoculated SS CX specimens after 24 hours of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the active-passive corrosion behavior of non-inoculated and TiC-inoculated SS CX specimens in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The results indicate that TiC-inoculated samples exhibit a broader passive potential range compared to the non-inoculated counterpart, following the trend TiC2 > TiC1 > CX, confirming improved corrosion resistance.

caption: Temperature dependence of hysteresis loss (HL) for AQ and ORD samples under a maximum magnetic field of 6 T, compared with literature data from references [43], [44], and [15] at 5 T.
summary: This plot compares the temperature-dependent hysteresis loss of AQ and ORD samples at a 6 T magnetic field. The results demonstrate that ordering the material effectively reduces the hysteresis loss, and the findings are benchmarked against previously reported data from various literature sources measured at 5 T.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the TZ1 region in the TC4-Ti48Al sample.
summary: The IPF map displays the crystallographic orientation of grains within the TZ1 region of the TC4-Ti48Al sample. This map is essential for analyzing the grain texture and orientation relationships in the zone where microcracks were observed, contributing to a comprehensive understanding of the microstructural state of the material.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image along the [011] zone axis highlighting the specific atomic arrangement at the SISF interface.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image, viewed along the [011] zone axis, details the atomic configuration of the SISF. By analyzing the Burgers vectors of the partial dislocations flanking this fault, it is determined that the SISF forms through the dissociation of a/2 < 110 > perfect dislocations, shearing the γ′ particle.

caption: Bode plots of Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL and Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni foams at onset potentials, highlighting the phase angle response in the low-frequency region.
summary: Bode plots at onset potentials illustrate the electrochemical behavior of Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL and Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni foams. A notable decrease in the phase angle within the low-frequency region for the Ni-Zn-Cu/MEL foam indicates an accelerated occurrence of the hydrazine oxidation reaction compared to the Ni-Zn-Cu/Ni foam.

caption: EDS spot analysis conducted at point B to evaluate the chemical constituents of the observed microstructural features.
summary: EDS spot analysis at point B serves to identify the chemical constituents present in the sample's microstructure. By examining this specific location, the analysis aids in correlating the observed morphological features with their underlying elemental composition, which is essential for interpreting the effects of heat treatment on phase formation.

caption: Experimental residual stress distribution in the z-direction for specimen 1 at z ̃ = 0 mm, highlighting the stress concentration near the notch tip.
summary: Experimental residual stress mapping at z ̃ = 0 mm reveals the stress state in specimen 1. Near the notch tip, the highest stress value of 924.24 MPa is observed in the center of the wall. Dashed arcs indicate the spatial stress tendency, showing a transition toward compressive stresses away from the notch.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of directed energy deposition (DED) CoCrNi illustrating the grain orientation distribution on the cross-section perpendicular to the loading direction.
summary: Directed energy deposition processed CoCrNi is characterized by its grain orientation distribution shown in this inverse pole figure map. The analysis is performed on a cross-section perpendicular to the loading direction, providing a clear view of the microstructural state resulting from the additive manufacturing process used for this sample.

caption: Methodological workflow illustrating the sequential research steps undertaken in the study.
summary: This flowchart provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological approach employed throughout the research. It serves as a visual guide to the sequential steps taken, ensuring clarity in the experimental and analytical process. The diagram effectively summarizes the research trajectory, detailing the progression from initial concepts to final results.

caption: Impedance analysis showing Z’ and -Z” versus ω −1/2 for the Li 3 Al 2 phase at room temperature.
summary: The plot illustrates the real and imaginary impedance components for Li 3 Al 2 at room temperature. In accordance with the established electrochemical model, the data show that both components are proportional to the inverse square root of frequency, validating the expected impedance characteristics for this specific lithium-aluminum phase.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the same region as panel a, captured using a specific martensite diffraction spot to highlight the HCP martensite plates in bright contrast against the austenitic matrix.
summary: Captured using a specific martensite diffraction spot from the SAD pattern, this dark-field TEM image confirms the presence of stress-induced HCP martensite plates. The plates appear in bright contrast, clearly distinguishing them from the surrounding austenitic matrix and validating the structural transformation resulting from the extrusion deformation process.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing imidazole, methacrylic acid, and the resulting resin after photopolymerization, highlighting the C=C region.
summary: This figure displays the FTIR spectra of the precursor materials, specifically imidazole and methacrylic acid, alongside the resin formed after photopolymerization. The analysis focuses on the C=C region, as indicated by the spectral peaks. These results demonstrate the chemical changes occurring during the polymerization process of the resin system.

caption: Phase diagram calculation for the Al–7Si–4Cu–1Ni alloy modified with 0.25 wt% Mg and 0.50 wt% Mn.
summary: Featured is the calculated phase diagram for the Al–7Si–4Cu–1Ni alloy with 0.25 wt% Mg and 0.50 wt% Mn. The diagram details the solidification phases and equilibrium conditions, highlighting how the interaction between these specific concentrations of Mg and Mn influences the overall phase stability of the alloy.

caption: Intergranular crack growth rate plotted against 0.2% proof stress for as-received and heat-treated material conditions tested at 650 °C, evaluated across five distinct K max levels ranging from 30 to 50 MPa√m.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between intergranular crack growth rate and yield strength for various microstructures at 650 °C. Experimental data across five K max values from 30 to 50 MPa√m demonstrate that crack growth rates consistently decrease as the continuum yield strength of the material increases.

caption: Spatial differential charge density map of the relaxed diamond/Ti system.
summary: This panel depicts the spatial differential charge density of the relaxed diamond/Ti system. Similar to the graphene analysis, this simulation aims to explore the electron interaction within the crystal cell, characterizing the electronic charge redistribution that occurs when titanium is introduced into the diamond structure at the relaxed state.

caption: In-situ synchrotron GI-XRD pseudo-color plot for the 0Co alloy under identical thermal conditions, highlighting the formation of oxide phases upon reaching the 800 °C isothermal hold.
summary: This pseudo-color plot presents in-situ synchrotron GI-XRD results for the 0Co alloy during fast heating and subsequent 800 °C isothermal oxidation. As the temperature reaches 800 °C, marked by the dashed line, corundum-type and spinel-type oxide reflections appear, confirming the immediate formation of these phases during the oxidation process.

caption: Statistical ANOVA analysis illustrating the influence of paste alloy composition, paste volume, and surface finish on the formation density of Ag3Sn intermetallic particles within SAC solder joints.
summary: This ANOVA analysis demonstrates that paste alloy, paste volume, and surface finish are statistically significant factors influencing the number of Ag3Sn particles formed in SAC solder joints. The box plot provides a quantitative assessment of how these specific processing variables contribute to the resulting intermetallic particle distribution within the solder.

caption: Temporal evolution of the curved part position in the AA cross-section from 0 to 0.32 s.
summary: The AA cross-section provides an XY-direction view of the curved part's movement from 0 to 0.32 s at 0.04 s intervals. The component is divided into four distinct regions labeled R I, R II, R III, and R IV, illustrating the spatial trajectory of the part during the initial simulation phase.

caption: Atomic model of the FCC FeCoNiCr phase represented as a 3x3x3 supercell containing 108 atoms.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configuration of the FCC FeCoNiCr phase, modeled as a 3x3x3 supercell consisting of 108 atoms. This structural model serves as the baseline for investigating the FeCoNiCr1-xAlx high-entropy alloy system, where Cr sites are randomly substituted with Al atoms to simulate alloying effects.

caption: Absorbance spectrum changes for 3-CN-bisPh-B during 30 minutes of water incubation, showing a baseline elevation attributed to the precipitation of less soluble hydrolysis products.
summary: This panel displays the absorbance spectrum of 3-CN-bisPh-B during 30 minutes of incubation with water. A notable elevation of the baseline is observed, which is attributed to the precipitation of hydrolysis products that exhibit lower solubility in the DMSO/H2O mixture, indicating the formation of insoluble species during the reaction.

caption: Optical micrograph of the SLM TA31-900 alloy showing the microstructure after processing.
summary: The optical micrograph of the SLM TA31-900 alloy provides a visual representation of the microstructure resulting from the 900-degree processing condition. This panel serves to document the microstructural state of the alloy, allowing for a comparative analysis with the rolled and SLM TA31-1000 samples presented in the other figure panels.

caption: Solidification map of the CCM alloy constructed based on Hunt’s criterion for the columnar-to-equiaxed transition (CET) as further developed by Gäumann.
summary: This solidification map for the CCM alloy is derived from Hunt’s criterion for the columnar-to-equiaxed transition, as refined by Gäumann. It serves as the foundational framework for evaluating the solidification behavior of the alloy under various processing conditions, providing a theoretical basis for predicting microstructural transitions during the solidification process.

caption: HEXRD patterns for low Fe Inconel 625 in as-deposited and HIP conditions, highlighting the emergence of Z-phase and η-nitride peaks.
summary: Synchrotron diffraction patterns for the low Fe Inconel 625 alloy reveal distinct structural changes between the as-deposited and HIP conditions. The HIP post-processed state exhibits multiple nitride peaks, while increased major peak intensities and the emergence of minor diffraction peaks indicate the growth of Z-phase and η-nitrides within the alloy matrix.

caption: Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) spectra of Si3N4 measured at the spot center following single-pulse and multiple-pulse (2, 4, and 10 pulses) laser irradiation, demonstrating the material's compression behavior.
summary: This panel displays SRS spectra of Si3N4 at the spot center after undergoing single-pulse and multiple-pulse laser irradiation. The data illustrates that Si3N4, characterized by a small coefficient of thermal expansion, is effectively compressed by these laser treatments, as evidenced by the spectral changes observed across the varying pulse counts.

caption: Correlation between predicted and experimental bending strength (BS) values.
summary: This parity plot demonstrates the agreement between experimental bending strength (BS) data and the expected responses calculated from the regression model. By plotting predicted values against experimental observations, the figure facilitates the verification of the model's accuracy and highlights any deviations in predicting the bending strength of the material.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction data collected in-situ during a room temperature tensile test performed after the thermal cycle.
summary: Synchrotron diffraction data is presented for a sample subjected to a thermal cycle followed by mechanical loading. This measurement assesses the influence of the increased ⍵ iso phase proportion on the material's structural response during a tensile test, providing high-resolution diffraction information throughout the deformation process.

caption: Signal convolution and intensity ratios derived from the Raman spectra of the DLC films.
summary: This panel illustrates the signal convolution and calculated intensity ratios obtained from the Raman spectra of the DLC films. These analytical parameters are used to interpret the structural characteristics of the carbon films, offering insights into the bonding states and overall quality of the deposited material samples.

caption: Pseudo-ternary schematic illustrating the 6-component alloy composition space, organized into three distinct material libraries (Matbib-I, II, and III) represented by colored paths, with dashed lines indicating predicted intermixing trajectories.
summary: This pseudo-ternary schematic maps the 6-component alloy system, highlighting three distinct material libraries designed to explore specific composition paths. The diagram incorporates numerical intermixing predictions as dashed lines, facilitating the investigation of base element effects and the synthesis of single-phase regions across the defined alloy composition space.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ single-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 600°C thermal treatment, showing broad defect-related emissions.
summary: Cathodoluminescence spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures treated at 600°C reveal significant defect-related emissions. These broad signals are most pronounced in this first cycle compared to subsequent thermal treatments. The spectra compare Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ dopants at 2.5 mol% and 0.35 mol% concentrations, highlighting the influence of dopant type on luminescence behavior.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves of the HT sample, illustrating the magnetic response across varying temperatures.
summary: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HT sample are presented to characterize its magnetic behavior. The non-zero magnetization observed at temperatures exceeding the Curie temperature (Tc) is attributed to the presence of a residual alpha-Fe(Co,Si) phase within the material structure.

caption: Nucleation boundary plot illustrating the relationship between cooling rate and Sc content (wt.%) for primary Al3(Sc1-x,Zr x) phases.
summary: This diagram maps the nucleation conditions for primary Al3(Sc1-x,Zr x) precipitates as a function of cooling rate and Sc concentration. Results indicate that higher Sc content is necessary for nucleation at increased cooling rates. For LPBF-processed Scalmalloy with 0.7 wt.% Sc, primary precipitates form only at cooling rates below 2·10^-4 K/s.

caption: Comparison of the isotropic 31P NMR peak obtained via the MAS insert method at 11 T (black) against a reference spectrum acquired using a conventional solid-state MAS stator and probe at 7 T (red).
summary: The isotropic 31P NMR peak from the MAS insert experiment at 11 T is compared to a standard solid-state MAS NMR measurement performed at 7 T. This comparison highlights the performance of the MAS insert setup relative to conventional solid-state NMR hardware for characterizing the potassium pyrophosphate sample.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material sample containing Atto465 and Atto495 dyes, measured at a thickness of 0.5 mm.
summary: This panel presents the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed multi-material sample featuring Atto465 and Atto495 dyes. The sample was fabricated with a thickness of 0.5 mm to ensure consistency with other multi-material samples. The spectrum provides a clear representation of the transmission characteristics for this specific dye pair.

caption: Cooling curve, first derivative, and second derivative for the Al–10Ni–1Si alloy, demonstrating the solidification characteristics.
summary: This panel presents the cooling curve and derivative analysis for the Al–10Ni–1Si alloy. By examining these thermal curves, researchers can extract the characteristic temperatures of precipitation reactions and the melting point, which are critical for understanding the solidification kinetics of this specific alloy composition.

caption: TEM-EDS point scanning analysis performed on the Ni5(Gd,Dy) phase.
summary: Point scanning analysis via TEM-EDS is presented for the Ni5(Gd,Dy) phase in the (GdDy)8 alloy. This technique confirms the elemental composition of the precipitate, supporting the identification of the phase as Ni5(Gd,Dy) and providing localized chemical data for the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curve for alloy S2.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curve for alloy S2. This plot illustrates the thermal response of the S2 specimen during the heating process. As part of the broader analysis of the alloys presented in the figure, this curve provides specific data regarding the thermal behavior and phase transition characteristics of the S2 material.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for AWS ER2594 feedstock, generated using JmatPro software to illustrate phase evolution during cooling.
summary: The continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for AWS ER2594 feedstock is presented here, derived from JmatPro software simulations. This diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the phase transformation kinetics and microstructural evolution expected during the cooling process of the specified feedstock material, serving as a critical reference for weld thermal analysis.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern from region d, demonstrating further clarification of diffraction spots as the material moves deeper into the subsurface.
summary: As the distance from the turning surface increases to region d, the diffraction pattern exhibits clearer and more regular spots. This evolution indicates that the plastic deformation degree of the nickel-based single-crystal superalloy is progressively decreasing as the depth into the subsurface region increases.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing iso-concentration surfaces for alloy 6 aged at 510 °C for 16 h, revealing distinct precipitate morphologies.
summary: This panel presents the atom probe tomography reconstruction for alloy 6 aged at 510 °C for 16 h. The iso-concentration surfaces reveal a clear visual difference in precipitate morphology compared to alloys 4 and 5, featuring both spherical NiAl-type precipitates and small disk-shaped Ni3Ti-type precipitates within the matrix.

caption: Optical microscopy images of SSCs Timp2-loaded Gtn-HPA hydrogel solid fibers compared with fluorescent microscopy images of freeze-dried and sectioned samples.
summary: This panel displays optical microscopy images of SSCs Timp2-loaded Gtn-HPA hydrogel fibers, paired with fluorescence microscopy of freeze-dried sections. The images confirm the successful loading and distribution of the biological cargo within the hydrogel matrix, providing visual evidence of the composite material's structural and compositional characteristics after processing.

caption: Critical pitting temperature curves for UNS S30400, UNS S31600, and QN1803 steels, showing the evolution of current density as a function of temperature during controlled heating.
summary: This plot displays the critical pitting temperature (CPT) curves for UNS S30400, UNS S31600, and QN1803 steels, illustrating the relationship between current density and temperature. The CPT values, defined at 100 μA cm⁻², were measured as 8.4 °C, 24.8 °C, and 41.0 °C for the respective alloys, highlighting their varying corrosion resistance.

caption: Magnetization profile within the stripe at t = 500 ns, featuring a fit of Eq. (5) utilizing the αc,2 profile within the ABL to quantify return loss.
summary: This plot displays the magnetization profile of a stripe at t = 500 ns, modeled using Eq. (5) with an αc,2 profile in the ABL. The fit serves as a critical analytical tool to estimate the return loss induced in the line by the integration of the ABL structure.

caption: Magnified SEM image of the wear scar on a 4.5 µm MoS2 composite at 37 °C, showing surface ridges and valleys.
summary: Magnified SEM analysis of the 4.5 µm MoS2 composite wear scar at 37 °C reveals a rough surface topography with ridges and valleys. These features highlight the impact of thermal effects on the wear scar morphology, reflecting the disruption of particle distribution at this elevated testing temperature.

caption: STEM micrograph of the AM state specimen after creep exposure at 750 °C for 901 hours under a 100 MPa load, demonstrating the long-term evolution of the γ’ phase.
summary: Representing the AM state after 901 hours of creep at 750 °C and 100 MPa, this STEM micrograph shows the final observed state of γ’ precipitates. The high activation energy and stress exponents observed are attributed to the resistance these precipitates provide against dislocation glide during in situ creep.

caption: Workflow diagram detailing the design generation process, which integrates a database of stochastically generated geometries, an experimentally validated CFD model, and a diffusion model for predictive geometry generation.
summary: The design process utilizes a diffusion model trained on simplified CFD simulations of randomly generated mixer geometries. Key performance indicators, such as pressure difference, mixing degree, fluid concentration, and channel porosity, are extracted from these simulations to condition the model, enabling the prediction of geometries based on specific user requirements.

caption: Atomic force microscopy images visualizing the surface topography of PLA scaffolds processed under different temperature and time conditions.
summary: Atomic force microscopy images provide a detailed visualization of the surface topography of the PLA scaffolds. These images allow for the assessment of surface features resulting from the different temperature and time treatments applied during the scaffold fabrication process.

caption: Micro hardness measurements for joints fabricated under bonding pressures of 2, 5, and 10 MPa.
summary: Micro hardness values are presented for joints fabricated at bonding pressures of 2, 5, and 10 MPa. Obtained through nanoindentation, these measurements provide insight into the mechanical integrity of the joints and demonstrate how the micro-mechanical properties evolve in response to the changes in the applied bonding pressure.

caption: Three-dimensional perspective of the simulated grain structure after the rescan process, showing the evolution of grains under the same laser parameters.
summary: Representing the grain structure after the rescan, this 3D simulation snapshot illustrates the morphological changes induced by the second laser pass. The model, operating at 130 W and 0.2 m/s, captures the final grain arrangement within the simulation domain following the complete processing sequence.

caption: Compositional distribution map of an MgO inclusion observed on the alloy surface following high-temperature laser confocal microscopy.
summary: This compositional map illustrates the distribution of an MgO inclusion identified on the alloy surface after high-temperature laser confocal experimentation. The visualization highlights the morphology and elemental surface scan of the inclusion, providing insight into its structural characteristics within the alloy matrix under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Morphological evolution of Al3Sc precipitates in an Al-0.2 wt.% Sc alloy, mapped as a function of temperature gradient and cooling rate.
summary: This diagram illustrates the morphological dependence of Al3Sc precipitates on thermal processing parameters for an Al-0.2 wt.% Sc alloy. By varying the temperature gradient and cooling rate, the figure demonstrates how these specific conditions dictate the resulting precipitate structure, as established by previous research on Al-Sc alloy solidification kinetics.

caption: Correlative imaging for P = 450 W and v = 400 mm.s-1, highlighting porosity formation in red within the radiograph alongside the photodiode signal and CWT scaleogram analysis.
summary: Processing at 450 W and 400 mm.s-1 results in the formation of porosity, which is highlighted in red within the radiograph. The corresponding photodiode signal and CWT scaleogram provide a correlative view of the process, allowing for the identification of signal patterns associated with the observed pore formation.

caption: Magnetization M(T) profiles for PBF-LB/M NiMnSn samples comparing as-built (red) and heat-treated (blue) states under 0.05 T and 5 T magnetic fields.
summary: The PBF-LB/M NiMnSn samples exhibit temperature-dependent magnetization curves under 0.05 T and 5 T fields for both as-built and heat-treated conditions. The observed splitting between field cooling and heating curves signifies a partial magneto-structural transition occurring over a broad temperature range below the Curie temperature, consistent with the PBF-EB/M sample behavior.

caption: Wear rate of IN718 and GNPs/IN718 composites as a function of sliding velocity under a constant normal load of 6 N.
summary: Panel (b) displays the wear rate behavior at a 6 N load, showing that wear on the substrate decreases as the slider speed increases. The reinforced composites maintain a lower wear rate compared to the unreinforced matrix, confirming that higher sliding velocities contribute to reduced wear in these materials.

caption: Optical spectrum of the pulse train generated by the 3D-printed femtosecond laser, showing the spectral distribution of the output.
summary: This panel displays the optical spectrum of the pulse train produced by the 3D-printed femtosecond laser. The spectral data provides insight into the frequency distribution and bandwidth characteristics of the generated pulses, confirming the successful operation of the laser system in the femtosecond regime.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the CuO interlayer region.
summary: This histogram illustrates the grain size distribution within the CuO interlayer area. The region is characterized by large columnar crystals ranging from 100 to 300 μm in size. This grain size is notably larger than that observed in the MPZ coarse dendrite area, contributing to the material's overall mechanical properties.

caption: Cycling performance of LSBs with CCC and ZnS@CCC interlayers at 0.2C over 200 cycles, showing capacity decay and retention.
summary: Cycling performance at 0.2C for batteries with ZnS@CCC and CCC interlayers is compared over 200 cycles. The ZnS@CCC battery shows an initial capacity of 884 mAh g-1, decaying to 721 mAh g-1 (81.5% retention), while the CCC battery decays from 832 mAh g-1 to 587 mAh g-1 (70.6% retention).

caption: CAD model of the lattice structure positioned within the additive manufacturing build volume, illustrating the Z-axis build direction and the Y-axis powder recoater path, with beam axes oriented at a 45° tilt to minimize dimensional variation.
summary: This schematic illustrates the CAD model of the lattice structure within the printer's build volume. It highlights the Z-axis build direction and the Y-axis recoater movement. To ensure structural consistency, the beam axes are tilted at 45° relative to the printing direction, minimizing variations in beam dimensions during fabrication.

caption: Crack length (a) versus number of cycles (N) curves for specimens with horizontal (H) and vertical (V) notch orientations tested in a seawater environment at varying loading frequencies of 0.5, 1, and 2.5 Hz.
summary: This plot displays crack growth behavior in seawater for specimens with different notch orientations and loading frequencies. Results indicate that loading frequency significantly influences the crack growth rate. Specifically, the curves track crack propagation for H and V notch orientations across frequencies ranging from 0.5 Hz to 2.5 Hz.

caption: H2-TPR profiles of Ni x Co/NC catalysts showing reduction peaks labeled α, α’, β, γ, and γ’.
summary: H2-TPR profiles for Ni x Co/NC catalysts reveal distinct reduction peaks labeled α, α’, β, γ, and γ’. The reduction temperatures for Ni x Co/NC catalysts between 100 °C and 350 °C are significantly lower than those observed for Co/NC, indicating enhanced reduction behavior due to the presence of nickel.

caption: Pore size frequency histogram for the gyroid-structured sample, generated from micro-CT data.
summary: This histogram depicts the pore size distribution for the gyroid sample, based on micro-CT characterization results. By visualizing the porosity data, the plot clarifies the structural characteristics of the gyroid lattice, contributing to the comprehensive assessment of the sample's internal geometry as presented in the research findings.

caption: Time-temperature transformation diagram of Inconel 718 illustrating the thermal cycling process and the kinetics of γ″-phase precipitation.
summary: The TTT diagram for Inconel 718 highlights the thermal cycling process and the kinetics of phase precipitation. It shows that γ″-phase precipitation is relatively slow. After 2000 and 3000 hours of exposure, a minor γ′-phase peak is detected, reflecting the influence of transformation kinetics on the alloy microstructure.

caption: Nyquist plot for SLMed TC4 alloy S7 after 12 days of immersion in a corrosive environment.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the S7 specimen after 12 days of immersion. The plot characterizes the corrosion resistance of the SLMed TC4 alloy, providing data for equivalent circuit fitting to evaluate the performance of the material under specific process parameters.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of 3Al5Ni alloy irradiated at 500 °C to a dose of 50 dpa, showing the surface boundary with a dashed yellow line.
summary: Displaying the 3Al5Ni alloy microstructure after 50 dpa irradiation at 500 °C, this dark-field TEM image confirms that a high density of nanoparticles persists despite the increased irradiation dose. The dashed yellow line marks the surface, facilitating observation of the material's sustained microstructural integrity under high-dose irradiation.

caption: Hardness profile along the corrosion depth for AlCrFeNi and 316L, showing a smooth transition for AlCrFeNi and abrupt mutations at 6 μm and 10 μm for 316L.
summary: Hardness trends along the corrosion depth demonstrate distinct material behaviors. AlCrFeNi exhibits a smooth, continuous hardness transition from 11.34 GPa to 5.33 GPa. In contrast, 316L displays abrupt hardness mutations at 6 μm and 10 μm, with the latter corresponding to the transition from Cr2O3 to the matrix.

caption: Thermo-kinetic E-pH diagram for copper in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 25 °C, with red dots representing measured OCP values.
summary: This thermo-kinetic diagram for copper at 25 °C in acetate solution shows the immunity region relative to the hydrogen evolution line. Measured OCP values, indicated by red dots, confirm that copper remains in the immunity area above the H+/H2 equilibrium line, demonstrating its stability under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from cyclic voltammograms recorded at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ for four averaged samples, highlighting slopes below 40 mV dec⁻¹ for Fe compositions between 40 and 60 at. %.
summary: Tafel slope analysis, a standard benchmark for electrochemical performance, is presented for various Fe-based alloy compositions. The data, averaged from four measurements, demonstrates that alloys containing between 40 and 60 at. % Fe exhibit Tafel slopes below 40 mV dec⁻¹, indicating favorable kinetics for the electrochemical process under investigation.

caption: Spider graph representing the A2N@95% property values across the tested recycling course levels.
summary: A2N@95% performance metrics are summarized in this spider graph to evaluate the material properties across various ASA recycling courses. The visualization allows for a comparative assessment of how this specific property changes in relation to the first recycling course, highlighting trends observed during the experimental testing of the specimens.

caption: Average cutting force Fy plotted against different AM Ti6Al4V samples with fitted curves illustrating force response across varying microstructural conditions.
summary: This graph presents the average cutting force Fy for AM Ti6Al4V samples, accompanied by fitted curves. The force response is influenced by the sample microstructure, particularly the orientation of columnar beta grains relative to the tool feed direction, which significantly affects the milling process dynamics observed in the experimental data.

caption: Logarithmic scale line graph illustrating the absolute results of surface parameters across varying filter sizes for M and A surfaces.
summary: This line graph displays absolute surface parameter values for M and A surfaces across different filter sizes on a logarithmic scale. SL and SLA surfaces exhibit the largest absolute results. At large cutoff values, the filtering effect diminishes, allowing long-wavelength waviness components to dominate, particularly observed in the A-surface roughness.

caption: Phase stability diagram calculated for the C2 diffusion couple across its composition gradient.
summary: Displayed here is the calculated phase diagram for the C2 diffusion couple. The plot maps the equilibrium phase regions relative to the composition, allowing for the identification of stable phases that form during the diffusion process within this specific material couple configuration.

caption: Line graph depicting the real-time coefficient of friction for A0-3, characterized by three distinct temporal phases labeled P1, P2, and P3.
summary: The real-time coefficient of friction for the A0-3 specimen is plotted against time, revealing a dynamic evolution of frictional behavior. The data is segmented into three specific time phases, identified as P1, P2, and P3, which characterize the progression of the friction coefficient throughout the duration of the tribological test.

caption: UMAP projection of the endoderm lineage and UiPSCs cluster, illustrating the relative expression levels of specific marker genes across different cell types.
summary: This UMAP projection highlights the endoderm lineage and UiPSCs, mapping the relative expression of key marker genes. The visualization confirms that these cells possess the expression characteristics of pancreatic-related genes, providing critical insights into the molecular identity and developmental potential of the endodermal lineage cells within the integrated dataset.

caption: EDS analysis spectrum obtained from the wear track of the SLM IN718 sample.
summary: The EDS analysis spectrum provides compositional information regarding the wear track generated on the SLM IN718 specimen. This spectroscopic data is used to characterize the surface chemistry within the wear scar, supporting the broader surface analysis of the specimen following the dry-sliding wear test.

caption: Inverse pole figure and band contrast map of AM Alloy 718 deformed at 773 K and a strain rate of 1500 s⁻¹.
summary: Microstructural analysis of AM Alloy 718 deformed at 773 K and 1500 s⁻¹ reveals significant grain coarsening and thermal softening. The map illustrates how high-temperature rapid deformation influences the final grain morphology, resulting in a distinct structural state compared to the lower temperature and lower strain rate regimes.

caption: Vickers hardness variation in AFSD-deposited Ti-6Al-4V as a function of layer thickness, evaluated at 0.5 mm, 1.0 mm, and 1.5 mm settings.
summary: Vickers microhardness data for AFSD Ti-6Al-4V builds are presented here to show the effect of layer thickness on mechanical properties. The box plot compares specimens B2 (0.5 mm), B3 (1.0 mm), and B6 (1.5 mm), highlighting the distribution of hardness values across these specific processing parameters for the nine builds.

caption: Comparison of grain size, dislocation density, and hardness values for AM-processed LS1 and LS2 samples alongside the as-cast CoCrFeNi alloy reference.
summary: This table presents a quantitative comparison of key microstructural and mechanical parameters for AM-processed LS1 and LS2 samples and their as-cast counterpart. It specifically details the grain size, dislocation density, and hardness values, providing a baseline characterization of these CoCrFeNi alloys prior to undergoing high-pressure torsion (HPT) deformation processes.

caption: Thermomechanical analysis (TMA) curves illustrating the dimensional change of 0B100 and 1B100 samples during the debinding process.
summary: TMA measurements reveal a slightly higher dimensional change of 0.5% during the debinding of samples containing fibers compared to those without fibers. These results, obtained from printed cylinders tested parallel to the printing direction, highlight the influence of fiber incorporation on the thermomechanical stability of the samples during thermal processing.

caption: Corrosion current densities (icorr) of Ni derived from the polarization curves in (a) plotted against immersion time, with an inset illustrating the Tafel extrapolation method at the corrosion potential (Ecorr).
summary: The corrosion current density (icorr) for the Ni specimen exhibits a significant increase of nearly four orders of magnitude between 0 and 100 hours of immersion in molten ZnCl2 at 593 K. The inset demonstrates the standard Tafel extrapolation technique used to determine icorr from the intersection of anodic and cathodic regions.

caption: Schematic representation of the Joule heating process in a metal wire, illustrating the electrical current flow path through the conductive nozzle.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Joule heating mechanism within a metal wire. It specifically highlights the electrical current flow as it enters the wire through a conductive nozzle. The diagram provides a conceptual model for understanding the thermal energy generation process driven by resistive heating in the metallic conductor.

caption: Comparison of heat transfer rate versus mass flow rate for Test II, illustrating the relationship between experimental measurements and model predictions.
summary: This plot displays the heat transfer rate as a function of mass flow rate for Test II. It serves as a direct comparison between experimental data and theoretical model predictions, allowing for an assessment of the model's accuracy in capturing the thermal performance characteristics observed during the experimental procedure.

caption: Schematic representation of the triangular HMS unit cell subjected to a combined loading mode, featuring normal stress applied along direction-1 (σ1) and a magnetic field oriented along direction-2 (Ba).
summary: This schematic illustrates the triangular HMS unit cell under a combined loading condition. It specifically depicts the application of normal stress along direction-1 (σ1) in conjunction with a magnetic field applied along direction-2 (Ba). This setup is part of a generalized geometrically non-linear HMS beam deformation problem for periodic networks.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetic entropy change for as-built PBF-LB/M samples calculated at various magnetic fields up to 5 T.
summary: The magnetic entropy change (ΔS) is plotted as a function of temperature for as-built PBF-LB/M samples. These values were derived using Maxwell's equation applied to isothermal magnetization data. The plot illustrates how the entropy change evolves under different external magnetic field strengths within the FOMST temperature range for the as-built condition.

caption: Atomic model of the TiO2(100)/Fe(110) interface showing the optimized plane alignment for minimal mismatch.
summary: Shown is the atomic model for the TiO2(100)/Fe(110) interface. This arrangement represents the contacting planes that provide the minimum lattice mismatch between the titanium dioxide substrate and the δ-Fe phase, as confirmed by the calculated results reported in the research.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) dislocation map and grain boundary distribution for NiTi alloy sample 14# viewed in the X–Z plane.
summary: The KAM dislocation map for NiTi alloy sample 14# in the X–Z plane illustrates the grain boundary and dislocation density distribution. As noted in the reference, laser power variations significantly influence the grain size, orientation consistency, and morphological characteristics of the NiTi alloy, as observed in this cross-sectional analysis.

caption: Scree plot illustrating the eigenvalue distribution for principal component analysis, with a red circle highlighting the nine selected principal components (PC1 to PC9) that possess eigenvalues greater than one.
summary: This scree plot serves as a diagnostic tool for determining the optimal number of principal components. By identifying components with eigenvalues exceeding unity, the analysis selects PC1 through PC9 as the most effective independent factors, ensuring that the chosen dimensions capture the most significant variance within the dataset for further modeling.

caption: Immunofluorescence semi-quantitative analysis of CTSK expression, providing additional statistical validation of the inhibitory effect of the 10 wt% scaffold.
summary: This bar chart provides further semi-quantitative analysis of CTSK expression levels. Consistent with other markers, the 10 wt% Ga-MBG/TCP scaffold group exhibits significantly lower expression levels compared to control groups, with statistical significance indicated by p-values, confirming the inhibitory effect of the scaffold on osteoclast differentiation markers.

caption: Chemical composition data for alloy A in the as-atomized powder state, showing the concentration of alloying elements and the absence of detectable nitrogen.
summary: This table presents the chemical composition of alloy A in its as-atomized powder condition. The data highlights the concentration levels of various alloying elements present in the material. Notably, the analysis confirms that no detectable nitrogen is present within the particles of powder A in this initial state.

caption: Fourier transform pattern derived from the corresponding HAADF-STEM image of the CrFeCoNi grain interior, indicating the crystallographic characteristics of the exposed material.
summary: Representing the crystallographic information of the CrFeCoNi grain interior, this Fourier transform pattern is derived directly from the HAADF-STEM image. It serves as a critical analytical tool to characterize the structural arrangement and phase identity of the material after undergoing a 1000-hour thermal treatment at 700 °C.

caption: Dark-field cross-sectional TEM image of the Si/SiO2/Ti/Pt/ZnO/Ti device stack, illustrating the optimized fabrication process with smooth surface roughness at the bottom Pt electrode and top Ti metal layer interfaces.
summary: This dark-field cross-sectional TEM image reveals the layered architecture of the Si/SiO2/Ti/Pt/ZnO/Ti diode. The visualization highlights the successful implementation of optimized fabrication steps, specifically demonstrating the smooth surface morphology achieved at the bottom platinum electrode and the top titanium metal layer interfaces within the device stack.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of RAW 264.7 macrophages cultured on the piezoelectric scaffold, showing F-actin (red), F4/80 (green), and DAPI (blue) nuclei staining.
summary: This panel displays immunofluorescence staining of F-actin and F4/80 in RAW 264.7 murine-derived macrophage cell lines cultured on a piezoelectric scaffold. The visualization highlights the cytoskeleton and mature macrophage markers, providing a structural assessment of cell morphology and distribution on the scaffold surface at a 50 μm scale.

caption: Sonoluminescence emission patterns in 3 M NaCl aqueous solution using Setup B at 36.5 kHz, featuring a whitish-blue emission zone in front of the transducer that shifts to orange under specific stirring conditions.
summary: Setup B at 36.5 kHz produces a whitish-blue sonoluminescence emission in front of the transducer plate. Mechanical stirring significantly alters the phenomenon, causing the emission zone to change both in extension and color, specifically transitioning from blue to orange in the region adjacent to the transducer side.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern acquired from the yellow cycled region indicated in panel (a).
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern was obtained from the yellow cycled area highlighted in the bright-field TEM image of panel (a). This diffraction data provides critical information regarding the crystallographic structure of the phase located within that specific region of the R3 specimen.

caption: Electron probe micro-analysis map illustrating the spatial distribution of Aluminum (Al) across the liquation crack region.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis map illustrating the spatial distribution of Aluminum (Al) across the liquation crack region. This map is part of a comprehensive elemental analysis performed to investigate the composition of the liquation crack, which is associated with the solidification of low melting point compounds in the material.

caption: Nyquist diagram illustrating the electrochemical impedance response of HR224 alloy immersed in ternary chloride molten salt after 1, 3, and 5 hours of exposure.
summary: The Nyquist plots for the HR224 alloy, presented in this figure, characterize the electrochemical impedance behavior during immersion in ternary chloride molten salt. The data captures the evolution of the alloy's surface interface at specific intervals of 1, 3, and 5 hours, providing insight into the corrosion resistance and electrochemical stability.

caption: Continued droplet growth and arc shortening at t = 7 ms.
summary: At t = 7 ms, the leading wire tip continues to be heated and melted by the leading arc. The droplet size increases further, leading to a continued reduction in the arc length. This observation confirms the ongoing droplet growth phase within the periodic welding cycle.

caption: Evolution of the mean γ' precipitate diameter in Mar-M247 alloys as a function of thermal exposure time at 1000 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the change in the mean diameter of γ' precipitates within Mar-M247 alloys subjected to a 1000 °C aging test. The data shows that the equivalence radius of the phase increases as the thermal exposure time varies from 100h to 16000h, indicating significant microstructural coarsening over the duration of the experiment.

caption: Optical micrograph of the WAAM-XY specimen providing a detailed view of the grain structure and orientation features.
summary: This optical micrograph of the WAAM-XY specimen highlights the complex grain structure inherent to the WAAMed SDSS. The image captures the disordered nature of the as-deposited microstructure, which includes various grain boundary types such as GBA, IGA, and WA, contributing to the distinct orientation characteristics of the deposited material.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) strain maps of the BCC-specimen during quasi-static compression, showing deformation stages A through E.
summary: Digital image correlation strain maps illustrate the deformation behavior of the BCC-specimen during quasi-static compression. Stages A through E correspond to specific points on the stress-compression curve. At stage A, the specimen is in an unloaded condition, while stages C and D reveal clear bending loads applied to the struts.

caption: Low-field AC magnetic susceptibility χ´ (T) curves for HT Ni-Mn-Ga samples, plotted against temperature during heating and cooling cycles between 30 and 120 °C, demonstrating the dependence of martensitic transformation on volumetric energy density (VED) and hatch parameters.
summary: This panel displays the low-field AC magnetic susceptibility χ´ (T) for HT Ni-Mn-Ga samples measured during heating and cooling cycles. The data, sorted by VED, illustrates how the martensitic transformation temperature is influenced by varying laser processing parameters, including scanning speeds from 400 to 1000 mm/s and hatch distances.

caption: Room temperature electron carrier concentration plotted against Ni alloying content in Bi2-xNixSe3 samples.
summary: This plot displays the room temperature electron carrier concentration for Bi2-xNixSe3 samples as a function of Ni content. Hall measurements reveal a continuous increase in carrier concentration from 1.24 × 10^18/cm^3 to 7.02 × 10^18/cm^3 as the Ni alloying content is increased within the composite system.

caption: Ni 2p 3/2 XPS spectra of an electropolished specimen after exposure to high-temperature, high-pressure deionized water at 250 ℃ for 1 h, showing the cleaning of the Ni oxide layer.
summary: Electropolished specimen surface analysis via Ni 2p 3/2 XPS spectra demonstrates the sputtering dynamics of the oxide layer. The peak variation indicates that the Ni oxide layer is cleaned after 15 seconds of Ar+ sputtering, which is the fastest cleaning time observed among the tested surface preparation methods.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectra of the molded electrode samples, indicating the chemical functional groups present.
summary: FTIR spectra of the molded samples are presented to identify the chemical functional groups present within the electrode material. This spectroscopic technique provides critical information regarding the chemical bonding and surface chemistry of the samples, which is vital for understanding the material's performance and interaction with the electrolyte.

caption: Inverse prediction parity plot for extrusion temperatures, displaying the relationship between predicted and actual values for training and test samples with an R² of 0.886.
summary: Inverse prediction of extrusion temperatures for the training and test samples is shown in Fig. 3 (f). The evaluation of the trained model on the test dataset yielded an R² value of 0.886 for the inverse prediction of extrusion temperatures, confirming the model's effectiveness in predicting thermal process conditions.

caption: Comparison of experimental quasi-static force–displacement curves with numerical simulation results.
summary: This panel displays force–displacement curves comparing experimental quasi-static test data with numerical simulation results. The black lines represent the experimental measurements, while the colored lines correspond to the numerical simulations. This comparison serves to validate the accuracy of the numerical model against physical testing under quasi-static loading conditions.

caption: Adiabatic temperature change versus temperature plot for the alloy after multiple isothermal forge (MIF) processing, measured across the drawing axis under 0.05 T and 0.2 T fields at 0.3 Hz.
summary: Panel (c) presents the magnetocaloric effect for the alloy after multiple isothermal forge processing, measured across the drawing axis. Similar to the longitudinal measurement, the inverse magnetocaloric effect maximum is observed to shift to lower temperatures by 7 K, indicating consistent structural influence on the magnetic response regardless of orientation.

caption: Classification accuracy trends for the two relation-reasoning heads, demonstrating the network's ability to learn correct classifications over the training duration.
summary: Panel (a) displays the classification accuracy of the two relation-reasoning heads within the self-supervised model. The data provides clear evidence that the network successfully learns to classify inputs correctly across both heads, indicating effective training progress and model convergence throughout the optimization process for the AE signatures.

caption: Force-displacement curves for the standard model configuration, showing experimental data from five specimens compared against FE simulation results.
summary: The force-displacement curves for the standard model demonstrate high consistency across five experimental specimens, as evidenced by their close overlap. These experimental results are plotted alongside FE simulation data to evaluate the mechanical response of the baseline configuration, confirming the reliability of the printing process and material properties.
