caption: Immunohistochemical staining of TNF-α pro-inflammatory cytokine expression at the implantation site after 7 days.
summary: TNF-α staining was utilized to assess the pro-inflammatory cytokine response following the 7-day implantation period. Further immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated that there were no significant differences in signal intensity between the various multichannel conduit groups and the silicon control, indicating a minimal local inflammatory reaction to the implanted materials.

caption: Unit cell dimensions in millimeters for the three Tailored Poisson’s Ratio-reinforcement (TPR) designs.
summary: The unit cell dimensions in millimeters are presented for the three Tailored Poisson’s Ratio-reinforcement (TPR) designs. These geometries, which form the basis for the TPR layouts, were selected to facilitate a comparative analysis of mechanical properties, specifically focusing on variations in theoretical Poisson’s ratio and horizontal cross-sectional area over the height.

caption: Stacked column diagram representing the cumulative importance of mechanical parameters across all eleven lattice shapes, highlighting the Modulus of Elasticity as the most significant overall factor.
summary: The stacked column diagram summarizes the cumulative importance of mechanical parameters derived from the heatmap data. It includes all lattice shapes with an importance value greater than zero. The results demonstrate that the Modulus of Elasticity possesses the highest overall importance among the evaluated mechanical properties for lattice shape classification.

caption: Ultimate strength and elastic modulus plotted as functions of temperature, illustrating the correlation between experimental measurements and the BTD constitutive model.
summary: Ultimate strength and elastic modulus are presented as functions of temperature to evaluate the BTD constitutive model. By comparing these key mechanical properties against experimental data, the plot highlights how the model captures temperature-dependent variations, providing a clear visual validation of the constitutive framework's predictive capabilities across the tested thermal range.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of PDAC cells after 5 days of culture in niches of varying stiffness, stained with calcein-AM (green, live) and PI (red, dead) to assess cell viability.
summary: Live/dead staining images reveal that encapsulated PDAC cells maintain high viability after 5 days of culture across all stiffness conditions. Quantitative assessment confirms there is no significant difference in cell viability between the low, medium, and high stiffness niches, indicating the biocompatibility of the 3D-printed environment.

caption: Al–Mg alloy phase diagram highlighting the processing temperature relative to α-Al and β phase melting points.
summary: The Al–Mg phase diagram in panel e serves as a reference for the thermal analysis. It demonstrates that the rolling temperature of 400 °C lies between the melting points of the α-Al and β phases, providing insight into the microstructural evolution and phase stability of the alloy during the process.

caption: Finite element analysis of a Model 1 unit cell demonstrating anisotropic thermomechanical deformation under a temperature increase from 0 to 200 ͦC.
summary: Finite element analysis of a Model 1 unit cell demonstrates anisotropic thermomechanical deformation under a temperature increase from 0 to 200 ͦC. The simulation reveals positive thermal expansion along the z-axis, while simultaneously showing contraction along the x- and y-axes, confirming the achievement of an anisotropic negative thermal expansion effect.

caption: Placement of the machined test specimen into the mechanical testing apparatus prior to compression.
summary: The image depicts the setup phase where the machined actuator is securely positioned within the mechanical test machine. This step is critical for ensuring consistent alignment and load application, forming an essential part of the standardized experimental procedure applied to all samples to generate the results presented in Table 1.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the base material (BM) showing elongated grains along the extrusion direction.
summary: The inverse pole figure map of the base material (BM) reveals a microstructure characterized by grains significantly elongated in the extrusion direction. Quantitative analysis indicates an average grain size of 12.3 μm for this condition, providing a baseline for comparing the microstructural evolution following subsequent rolling and heat treatment processes.

caption: Steady-state passive current density values for SLMed 316L stainless steel specimens subjected to various solid solution treatments, measured at a constant potential of 0.4 V vs. SCE in a 0.5 mol/L H2SO4 electrolyte at 25 °C.
summary: This panel displays the steady-state passive current density for SLMed 316L stainless steel samples following different solid solution treatments. Measurements were conducted at a potential of 0.4 V vs. SCE in a 0.5 mol/L H2SO4 solution at 25 °C to evaluate the electrochemical stability of the treated materials.

caption: Main effects plot displaying the influence of rotational speed on the x-dimension deformation (Dx) of treated cube upper surfaces.
summary: This plot demonstrates the relationship between rotational speed and x-directed distortion in the upper surfaces of treated cubes. Unlike the dwell time effect, the statistical analysis reveals a relatively irregular relationship between the rotational speed and the resulting deformation, suggesting a more complex or non-linear influence on the surface geometry.

caption: Ni K-edge XANES spectrum of E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 with linear combination fitting.
summary: Linear combination fitting of the Ni K-edge XANES spectrum for the E-Ni 0.15 Fe 0.05 catalyst is performed to quantify the oxidation states and phase composition. This analytical approach provides a detailed breakdown of the nickel species present, supporting the characterization of the catalyst's electronic structure.

caption: Indentation depth plotted against time for [001], [011], and [111] crystallographic orientations under a 0.125 N punch load at 650 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the indentation depth evolution over time during a flat punch creep test at 650 °C. Comparing the [001], [011], and [111] crystallographic orientations reveals that the orientation of the sample surface has only a minimal influence on the resulting indentation depth under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Representative electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data showing the evolution of passive layer formation on the titanium alloy surface over a 7-day immersion period in PBS.
summary: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data tracks the formation and stability of passive layers on the titanium alloy surface. By monitoring the impedance response over a 7-day immersion period in a simulated physiological environment, the study assesses the passivity and long-term electrochemical stability of the material under continuous exposure to the electrolyte.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curves for PLA, PLA-PBAT, PLA-PBAT-Joncryl, and PLA-PBAT-Lotader blends, displaying first heating cycles in black and second heating cycles in red at a 10 °C/min rate.
summary: This figure presents DSC thermograms for PLA and various PLA-PBAT blends, including those modified with Joncryl and Lotader compatibilizers. The data illustrates thermal behavior across two heating cycles, with black curves representing the first heating and red curves representing the second heating, all conducted at a constant rate of 10 °C/min.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of CAMA used to verify the molecular structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of CAMA is presented to further demonstrate and verify the molecular structure of the synthesized compound. Together with the FT-IR data, this analysis confirms the identity of the CAMA material, ensuring the structural integrity and successful synthesis of the compound as reported in the study.

caption: STEM micrograph of the HIP, homogenized, and 24-hour aged sample demonstrating the reformed precipitate structure.
summary: This STEM micrograph captures the microstructure after the final strengthening heat treatment, consisting of 24-hour aging at 130 °C. The process successfully reforms the nanoscale MgZn2 precipitates within the matrix, demonstrating the effectiveness of the aging treatment in restoring fine-scale strengthening phases after the homogenization step.

caption: Line graph illustrating microhardness trends for laminates fabricated with tool T2 at 1200 rpm, highlighting the variation in hardness across measuring points.
summary: This line graph depicts the microhardness profile for laminates produced using tool T2 at 1200 rpm. Consistent with the observed trends, the hardness is higher at the first measuring point than at the second. The data demonstrates how tool-specific processing parameters influence the mechanical properties of the resulting laminate structures.

caption: Fluorescence images of transverse sections displaying new bone as fluorescent green, confirming the spatial distribution patterns observed in the Alizarin red stained transverse sections.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of transverse sections confirms the bone distribution patterns observed in the Alizarin red stained samples. The fluorescent green signal highlights the new bone, mirroring the structural arrangements seen in the transverse histological sections. This confirms the efficacy of the Laponite/BMP-2 coating in promoting specific bone growth architectures.

caption: GROD map of uncharged sample S1 at 9% strain, showing the grain boundary region between grains G2 and G3.
summary: Representing the uncharged sample S1 at 9% strain, this GROD map highlights the grain boundary between grains G2 and G3. Comparison with the H-charged sample S2 at a similar location indicates that the uncharged sample exhibits a lower peak GROD value, reflecting less localized plasticity during tensile deformation.

caption: Training and validation loss curves plotted against epochs, demonstrating model convergence to a low loss value of approximately 10^-3 using optimal hyperparameters.
summary: As depicted in the training and validation loss curves, the model's loss converges to a remarkably low value, nearing 10^-3, with an increasing number of epochs. This indicates that the model with optimal hyperparameters successfully learns the underlying patterns in the data without significant overfitting or underfitting issues.

caption: Confocal micrograph of xylenol orange stained mineralized nodules on P(3HB)/activated carbon aged composite films after 21 days of osteoblast culture.
summary: This confocal micrograph illustrates mineralized nodules on P(3HB)/activated carbon aged composite films after 21 days of culture. Stained with xylenol orange, the image confirms the enhanced mineralization performance of the aged composite, consistent with the broader observation that aged materials promote superior osteoblast differentiation and mineral nodule formation.

caption: Kernel average misorientation (KAM) map for the straight lamellar structure.
summary: This KAM map illustrates the local plastic strain in straight lamellae. The straight regions show lower KAM values compared to the bent lamellae, which exhibit a 1.8-fold increase in KAM. This confirms that the bent lamellae retain substantial residual stresses resulting from the deformation process during fatigue crack growth.

caption: RMS value comparison for the DLP surgical guide group, illustrating dimensional changes following additive manufacturing and steam sterilization.
summary: The DLP group's RMS values are presented to evaluate dimensional deviations after additive manufacturing and steam sterilization. Reference data indicates that DLP guides in vertical orientation achieved an RMS of 0.39 ± 0.15 after manufacturing, highlighting the specific dimensional performance of this group under the tested processing conditions.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the 2H martensite phase.
summary: This bright field TEM image displays the morphology of the 2H martensite phase within the alloy. The micrograph provides structural visualization of the martensitic microstructure, serving as the basis for the corresponding selected area diffraction analysis that confirms the presence of the 2H stacking sequence in the material.

caption: Comparative analysis of Length, Height, and Stability scores for all single-track lines.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive visualization comparing the individual performance metrics of Length, Height, and Stability for all single-track lines. By plotting these three objectives simultaneously, the chart allows for a direct assessment of how each line performs across the different criteria defined within the 3-MMO strategy.

caption: Full-field DIC displacement analysis corresponding to the initiation stage of negative burr formation.
summary: Full-field DIC displacement analysis is presented for the initiation stage of negative burr formation. This map quantifies the material displacement patterns as the cutting process begins, highlighting the localized mechanical response and the onset of deformation that precedes the development of larger intergranular cracks ahead of the tool.

caption: Local viability assessment of HUVECs via live/dead staining, comparing 2D culture (SC group) and 3D culture (SC-Gel group) with a 200 μm scale bar, indicating significant differences in viability (P < 0.05; P < 0.01).
summary: Local cell viability is assessed using live/dead staining to compare HUVEC performance in 2D and 3D culture conditions. High-magnification fluorescence microscopy reveals distinct morphological differences between the SC and SC-Gel groups, with statistical analysis confirming significant variations in cell viability between the two experimental scaffold environments.

caption: Equivalent circuit diagram utilized for fitting the experimental impedance data of the FeCoCrNiMo-based coatings.
summary: The equivalent circuit diagram shown here was employed to fit the experimental impedance data obtained from the FeCoCrNiMo HEA and HEA/CNTs composite coatings. By using ZView software, this circuit model allows for the quantitative analysis of the electrochemical parameters governing the corrosion behavior of the investigated coating systems.

caption: SHAP summary plot evaluating the effect of input variables on the joint shear capacity for the SCG model.
summary: This SHAP summary graph for the SCG model demonstrates how input variables affect the joint shear capacity (Fmax). The visualization helps identify the most significant features influencing the model's predictions, providing a comprehensive overview of the relationship between the input data and the resulting joint shear capacity estimates.

caption: Arrhenius-type representation showing the dependence of ln[sinh( ασ )] on the inverse of absolute temperature (1/ T) at multiple strain rates.
summary: Representing the temperature sensitivity of the flow stress, this Arrhenius plot shows ln[sinh( ασ )] as a function of 1/T for various strain rates. The data is extracted from flow curves at a true strain of 0.8, facilitating the determination of activation energy for the Fe–25Al-1.5Ta alloy deformation.

caption: Temperature-dependent stress relaxation behavior of cured D9G1 samples, highlighting the influence of thermal energy on the relaxation kinetics of this specific resin formulation.
summary: Stress relaxation measurements for cured D9G1 samples are presented to evaluate temperature effects on mechanical performance. The curves show how the material responds to thermal stress, providing insight into the relaxation kinetics of the D9G1 formulation as it undergoes structural changes at different temperature levels during the testing period.

caption: 2D opacity map derived from CT scan data for sample R17.
summary: Sample R17 is represented by a 2D opacity map generated from processed CT scan data. This visualization provides a cross-sectional view of the internal structure, allowing for a direct comparison with simulated structural grids to evaluate the accuracy of the melt pool modeling process for this specific specimen.

caption: Temporal evolution of electronic and atomic temperatures in pure Ni for a 1 ps electron-phonon coupling activation time.
summary: Displayed is the temporal evolution of electronic and atomic temperatures for a representative cascade in pure Ni, modeled with a 1 ps electron-phonon coupling activation time. This simulation tracks the thermal spike dynamics within the center cell of the MD box, initiated by a cascade near the box corner.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental versus predicted hardness values.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the hardness model by comparing experimental measurements against predicted values. The alignment of data points along the diagonal indicates the model's performance in estimating hardness, serving as a primary validation step for the regression analysis conducted in the study.

caption: Microhardness contour map of the HT + LSP specimen, showing the enhanced surface hardness distribution following laser shock peening.
summary: The microhardness contour map of the HT + LSP specimen demonstrates the impact of laser shock peening on surface properties. Following the treatment, the average surface hardness increases to 367 HV, while the maximum surface hardness reaches 442 HV, indicating a significant improvement compared to the untreated HT specimen.

caption: Absolute error comparison of the current output for the KC 200GT SPV module across three distinct analytical methods.
summary: This plot illustrates the performance comparison of absolute error in the current of the KC 200GT SPV module. By evaluating three different methods, the graph provides a quantitative assessment of the error distribution, highlighting the relative accuracy and performance variations observed across the tested analytical approaches for this specific module.

caption: Areal capacitance of 3D-IDCμE/PPy electrodes as a function of the current density used during the 10-minute PPy electrodeposition process.
summary: This plot displays the specific capacitance calculated from GCD measurements for 3D-IDCμE electrodes. The data indicates that increasing the electrodeposition current density from 1 to 4 mA cm⁻² leads to an improvement in specific capacitance, highlighting the influence of deposition parameters on the final electrochemical performance of the 3D-IDCμE/PPy system.

caption: Full-field geometrical eccentricity evaluation for Column B.
summary: This panel presents the full-field geometrical eccentricity evaluation for Column B. Similar to the analysis performed for Column A, this high-fidelity approach captures the spatial distribution of eccentricity, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of the structural characteristics and geometric integrity of the column under the evaluated conditions.

caption: Creep strain versus time curves for Re/Ru-containing alloys subjected to various applied stress levels at a constant temperature of 1170 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep behavior of Re/Ru-containing alloys under different stress conditions at 1170 °C. The curves demonstrate the temporal evolution of creep strain, providing essential data on the material's deformation resistance and mechanical stability when exposed to high-temperature loading environments as specified in the experimental study.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulation results showing the loading and unloading segments for pure Ni, Ni 0.8 Fe 0.2, and Ni 0.5 Fe 0.5, demonstrating qualitative agreement with experimental hardness trends.
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations illustrate the loading and unloading behavior of pure nickel and nickel-iron alloys. These computational results show a qualitative agreement with experimental measurements regarding the hardness differences between samples and the influence of penetration depth, confirming the validity of the simulation approach in predicting material mechanical properties.

caption: Load versus displacement curve for a representative AFRP sample.
summary: Shown is the load versus displacement curve for a representative AFRP sample, selected from the identical tests performed on this group. The graph depicts the mechanical behavior of the aramid fiber reinforced polymer, highlighting the specific load-displacement relationship observed during the testing of this composite material specimen.

caption: EELS spectra of Cr L2,3-edges acquired at the melt-pool boundary, illustrating the local electronic state of Chromium at the specified measurement points.
summary: EELS spectra focusing on the Chromium L2,3-edges were obtained near the melt-pool boundary. These spectroscopic measurements provide detailed information regarding the local electronic environment and oxidation state of Chromium at the specific locations numbered 1 to 5, as identified in the corresponding HAADF-STEM image of the sample.

caption: t-SNE embedding plot illustrating the distribution of melt pool samples based on energy density, demonstrating a clear trend of increasing energy density across the latent space.
summary: This t-SNE plot demonstrates that the latent space representations also capture trends related to the energy density of each melt pool. These results confirm that the model successfully learns generalizable and intuitive representations of the underlying physical mechanisms governing melt pool formation, consistent with the trends observed in the depth-based embedding.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the systematic paper selection process, highlighting the initial identification of 2,806 papers and the subsequent reduction to 202 articles after applying specific filters.
summary: This flowchart visualizes the systematic literature selection process. Starting with an initial search across databases, 2,806 papers were identified, represented by the red trapezium. Following the application of specific filters defined in the study, the pool was refined to 202 articles, as indicated by the yellow trapezium.

caption: Modulated nonlinear emission pattern featuring double focusing points arranged vertically, optimized via the genetic algorithm over 200 generations.
summary: A vertical arrangement of double focusing points is displayed in the emission pattern. Achieving this clear double-focusing configuration required approximately 200 generations of genetic algorithm optimization, which corresponds to an experimental duration of about two hours.

caption: Systematic literature review workflow illustrating the retrieval, relevance screening, and classification process of 257 publications.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic literature review process, detailing the retrieval and analysis of 257 relevant publications. The methodology involves checking literature for relevance, subdividing it into specific categories, and performing quantitative analysis. Of these, 142 publications are classified as pure formwork papers, providing the basis for the assessment.

caption: Large-scale Ni structure generated by McChasy2, showing randomly distributed 3 nm dislocation loops created by merging pristine cells with those containing the ATOMSK-developed defect.
summary: Representing a large-scale Ni structure, this panel illustrates the random distribution of 3 nm dislocation loops. These defects were integrated using the McChasy2 merging procedure, which combines pristine structural cells with those containing the ATOMSK-developed defects to simulate a complex, extended defect distribution within the material lattice.

caption: Ni2p 3/2 XPS spectra for passive films on Cr20, Cr30, Cr40, and Cr50 alloys, showing peaks for Ni metal, NiO, and Ni(OH)2.
summary: The Ni2p 3/2 spectra for the Cr20, Cr30, Cr40, and Cr50 alloys reveal three distinct peaks corresponding to Ni metal at 852.48 eV, NiO at 853.44 eV, and Ni(OH)2 at 856.32 eV. Analysis indicates that Ni exists primarily as metallic Ni, which does not significantly influence the corrosion resistance of the passive films.

caption: XRD pattern of the (111) plane for Ni–W alloy, illustrating the diffraction profile before and after corrosion.
summary: This panel shows the XRD pattern of the (111) plane for the Ni–W model alloy. The data provides insight into the structural integrity of the Ni–W system following corrosion, acting as a comparative baseline for the peak shifts observed in the ternary Ni–Cr–W alloy system.

caption: Quantitative analysis of BSP expression positive areas measured via ImageJ software, highlighting the increased protein expression that validates the efficacy of the combined scaffold treatment.
summary: Quantitative analysis of BSP expression positive areas, measured via ImageJ software, provides further evidence of the superior osteogenic capacity of the combined scaffold approach. The increased expression of this bone-specific protein, as shown in the bar chart, corroborates the immunohistochemical results observed in the experimental groups.

caption: Pole figure (PF) of the HT3 specimen after LCF testing, reflecting changes in crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The pole figure for the HT3 specimen after LCF testing demonstrates a significant reduction in weave strength compared to the initial state. These findings highlight that microstructural heterogeneities directly govern dislocation interactions, thereby dictating the macroscopic mechanical response of the HT3 specimen following the LCF experiments.

caption: Geometric comparison of the Wing 2 model, overlaying the original CAD design in navy against the final fabricated model in gray.
summary: This panel presents a geometric comparison of the Wing 2 model. It highlights the structural alignment between the original CAD design, represented in navy, and the final fabricated model, shown in gray. This visualization allows for a direct assessment of the fidelity between the intended design and the actual physical outcome.

caption: Bimodal size distribution of precipitation statistics for the alloy at 800 °C.
summary: Representing the bimodal size distribution of precipitations at 800 °C, this histogram quantifies the particle size population. It serves as a critical component for analyzing the thermal stability of the precipitation phases and understanding how their distribution evolves at the highest temperature point in the experimental study.

caption: Isoplethal section of the Ti–Zr–Hf–Al–V system calculated for x(Zr) = x(Hf), x(Ti) = 8·x(Hf) at a fixed concentration of 13.2 at.% Al, representing alloy B6 with 4.7 at.% V.
summary: Representing the final alloy in the series, this panel displays the isoplethal section for the Ti–Zr–Hf–Al–V system at 13.2 at.% Al. The diagram illustrates the equilibrium phase stability for alloy B6, which contains 4.7 at.% V, based on the specified atomic ratios of the constituent elements.

caption: Contour map depicting the net cost (green) and coarsening metric (black) as a function of strength (color scale), with converged compositions (white stars) and reduced Ni/Zr compositions (gold stars) indicated.
summary: This plot evaluates the trade-offs between net cost, coarsening metrics, and strength for different Ni and Zr compositions. While the white star indicates a high-strength converged composition, the gold star represents a design modification that maintains benchmark-level performance in cost, strength, and coarsening without significant negative impacts.

caption: Radial residual strain profile along the L3-Bot horizontal scan path at the bottom section of the cylinder.
summary: The radial residual strain profile along the L3-Bot scan path indicates that the strain values remain approximately zero across the bottom region of the cylinder. This measurement confirms the localized nature of the residual stress state in the lower section of the component compared to other scan locations.

caption: Single gyroid unit cell architecture serving as the fundamental building block for the three-dimensional structure.
summary: The gyroid unit cell represents the fundamental geometric building block used to construct the final three-dimensional architecture. This single unit cell is patterned throughout space to form the desired cylindrical shape, which ultimately defines the structural properties of the final sample with a diameter of 19 mm and height of 31 mm.

caption: Spatial distribution map (SDM) of Al-Al ion distances in the xy plane, with annotations indicating the approximate distances to prominent peaks.
summary: The xy spatial distribution map (SDM) of Al-Al distances, generated from the first 20 million ions of the Al 6026 dataset, characterizes the effect of the accelerating mesh on the reconstruction. Annotations within the map highlight the approximate distances to prominent peaks, providing insight into the reconstructed ion distribution.

caption: Predicted applied stress versus rupture life plot generated using a single Larson-Miller Parameter (LMP) fit across the entire experimental dataset.
summary: This panel displays the predicted applied stress plotted against rupture life, derived from a single Larson-Miller Parameter model fit. The experimental data points are overlaid on the model curve to demonstrate the global fit performance across the entire range of stress and rupture life conditions observed in the study.

caption: Transcriptome profiling via RNA-seq comparing global gene expression changes in regenerating uterine tissue at the PLCL scaffold-implanted site versus the EX control site.
summary: Transcriptome profiling via RNA-seq reveals global gene expression changes in the regenerating uterine tissue at the scaffold-implanted site relative to those of the EX control site. This analysis provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular shifts occurring within the tissue environment following the implantation of the PLCL scaffold compared to controls.

caption: Glass transition temperature (Tg) of frontally cured CF tows as a function of the applied compaction force.
summary: This graph displays the glass transition temperature of frontally cured CF tows across different compaction forces. The data indicates the thermal stability of the composite material as it is processed under varying mechanical loads, providing insight into the curing uniformity achieved at different compaction levels.

caption: Contour plot displaying the variation of RLT as a function of PC and DF.
summary: Representing the interaction between PC and DF, this contour plot highlights their combined influence on the RLT. The visualization allows for the identification of trends and optimal parameter ranges for achieving specific RLT values, consistent with the broader investigation into the factors affecting material performance.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining for CK5 and CK18 markers in undifferentiated MSCs, differentiated MSCs, and primary tracheal epithelial cells.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining for CK5 and CK18 markers demonstrates the successful differentiation of MSCs towards an epithelial phenotype. The expression levels in differentiated MSCs are only slightly lower than those observed in primary tracheal epithelial cells, confirming the acquisition of epithelial-specific markers during the differentiation process (P < 0.05).

caption: Raman spectroscopy plot of the shaped glass, demonstrating chemical purity by comparison with commercial fused silica.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is utilized to verify the chemical composition of the shaped glass. By comparing the resulting spectra against commercial fused silica, the analysis confirms that the shaped glass maintains a high level of chemical purity, consistent with the expected characteristics of pure fused silica material.

caption: Average Nusselt number (Nuave) comparison between optimized lattice structures and reference fins.
summary: This bar chart presents the average Nusselt number (Nuave) for optimized lattice structures compared to reference fins. The findings show that the optimized lattice structures, whether featuring voids or not, provide improved thermal performance over the uniform lattice, validating the design improvements achieved through the optimization process.

caption: Load versus displacement curves for Ti 6242 spot weld lap shear specimens processed at a foil vaporizing energy of 8 kJ.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of Ti 6242 alloy workpieces subjected to lap shear testing. The data represents the load-displacement behavior of spot welds produced at a specific foil vaporizing energy of 8 kJ, highlighting the structural integrity and performance characteristics of the welded titanium alloy joints under load.

caption: Overview of the fractured cross-section of the first LPBF-processed L-6 specimen half, highlighting distinct zones including crack initiation, propagation, and fast fracture regions.
summary: This SEM image provides a comprehensive view of the fractured cross-section of the first L-6 specimen half. It clearly delineates the critical zones of failure, specifically identifying the crack initiation site, the subsequent crack propagation region, and the final fast fracture zone, offering a macroscopic perspective of the specimen's failure morphology.

caption: Comparative analysis of cyclic stress intensity factors between mini-bending and standard bending specimens of AlSi10Mg to evaluate transferability.
summary: This panel provides a comparison of cyclic stress intensity factors derived from mini-bending and standard bending specimens of AlSi10Mg. The investigation aims to validate the transferability of defect-based fatigue assessments between these two specimen geometries, ensuring the reliability of the mini-bending approach for characterizing material fatigue behavior.

caption: Extrusion process capturing the formation of the semi-finished biocomposite filament.
summary: Captured during the manufacturing operation, this photograph shows the extrusion of the biocomposite filament. The image provides a visual representation of the material processing stage, confirming the successful integration of the natural yarn within the polymer matrix as it exits the modified nozzle assembly during the fabrication cycle.

caption: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 HT2 (red) and A2 HT2 (green) samples measured at 423 K, illustrating the overall diffraction profiles.
summary: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 HT2 and A2 HT2 samples are presented at 423 K. These profiles demonstrate the structural characteristics of the alloys under identical heat treatment conditions. The data provides a comprehensive overview of the diffraction patterns, serving as the primary basis for comparing the two distinct material compositions.

caption: Mott-Schottky curve illustrating the relationship between electrode potential (E) and passivation film capacitance (C) to determine semiconductor properties.
summary: The Mott-Schottky curve depicts the relationship between electrode potential and the capacitance of the passivation film. This plot is essential for characterizing the semiconductor properties of the film, allowing for the calculation of carrier density, which provides insight into the electronic nature of the passivation layer on the material.

caption: Optical profilometry image displaying the surface roughness profile of the PEO-3 sample.
summary: Optical profilometry is employed to characterize the surface roughness of the PEO-3 sample. This imaging technique provides essential data regarding the surface morphology following PEO treatment, contributing to the comparative study of how different treatment parameters influence the final surface texture and roughness levels across the various specimens.

caption: Mean absolute SHAP values for features in the ST regression model, illustrating the relative importance of descriptors.
summary: This panel displays the mean absolute SHAP values for the ST regression prediction model. It ranks features by their contribution to the model's output, identifying key descriptors like Tm, gamma, and VEC as the most influential factors in predicting ST values, consistent with previous phase structure classification findings.

caption: Grain orientation spread map of P600 pure Cu specimen, illustrating localized deformation and segmentation.
summary: Similar to the P300 condition, the P600 specimen contains many highly deformed zones. A substantial fraction of these grains are non-indexed because of porosity or segmentation, resulting in a per-grain GOS that may appear lower than expected despite the existence of significant local lattice curvature.

caption: Creep behavior comparison between IN718C and TiN/IN718C composite materials tested at 704 °C under a constant stress of 500 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the creep behavior of IN718C and TiN/IN718C composites at 704 °C and 500 MPa. The TiN/IN718C composite exhibits a creep life of 421 hours, which is approximately 1.7 times longer than that of the unreinforced IN718C alloy, demonstrating the effectiveness of TiN reinforcement.

caption: Schematic illustration of the build plate layout featuring horizontally (XY) and vertically (Z) oriented bars, metallography cubes, and the geometry of a machined creep specimen with dimensions provided in millimeters.
summary: This schematic depicts the arrangement of horizontal and vertical bars alongside metallographic cubes on a build plate. It further details the specific machining dimensions for the tensile creep specimens. These components were subsequently removed from the build plate and subjected to solution heat treatment at 1230 °C for one hour.

caption: Surface roughness map for surfaces parallel to the building plane in samples with low layer thickness (tl).
summary: Surface roughness values for surfaces parallel to the building plane are presented as a quantitative map for samples with low layer thickness. This visual representation helps characterize the surface quality trends across the process window, demonstrating the impact of low layer thickness on the final surface finish of the parts.

caption: XRD line profile (intensity vs. 2θ) for the NHT sample, showing experimental data, Rietveld refinement fit, and the difference plot, with black arrows indicating faint bcc peaks.
summary: The XRD line profile for the NHT sample, derived from a 230 μm × 230 μm area, displays the experimental intensity, Rietveld refinement fit, and residual difference. Faint bcc diffraction peaks are highlighted by black arrows. This profile is representative of the LHT100 and LHT300 samples and was used for lattice parameter refinement.

caption: Ti–Al binary alloy phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium relationships between various phases as a function of temperature and composition.
summary: The Ti–Al binary alloy phase diagram provides a comprehensive overview of phase stability across different compositions and temperatures. Analysis of this diagram reveals that decreasing the aluminum content shifts the phase equilibrium point toward the α2 phase region, highlighting the critical influence of composition on the resulting microstructural phase constituents.

caption: Coefficient of friction versus lateral displacement for Al 7075 alloy at different normal applied loads.
summary: The coefficient of friction for Al 7075 is displayed against lateral displacement across various normal applied loads. Compared to the NT Al-Ni alloys, the Al 7075 sample exhibits less stability in its coefficient of friction values throughout the entire range of lateral displacement tested in this study.

caption: Fabrication flowchart illustrating the Binder Jetting (BJ) 3D printing process and the subsequent production of 3D-PRAs.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic fabrication process for Binder Jetting 3D printing and the resulting 3D-PRAs. The process involves a cyclic sequence of material deposition and binding steps that are repeated until the final model is successfully completed, as demonstrated by the fabrication workflow presented in this study.

caption: Temperature dependence of the dynamic magnetic susceptibility for pristine and oxygen plasma-treated Pd-Ni seashell samples.
summary: This plot displays the temperature-dependent dynamic magnetic susceptibility of Pd-Ni seashell samples before and after oxygen plasma treatment. The responses are nearly identical, indicating that the metallic conductivity remains unchanged by the treatment. This suggests that any nickel oxide formed during the process exists only as a thin surface layer.

caption: Fast Fourier transform (FFT) spectra of the β phase performed along the [111] zone axis.
summary: FFT spectra analysis of the β phase, performed along the [111] zone axis, provides the necessary diffraction data to characterize the lath phase. This analysis supports the identification of the body-centered cubic structure within the as-deposited AZT6115 alloy, consistent with the observed lath morphology.

caption: Atomic force microscopy images of the hydrogel dressing surfaces, accompanied by quantitative surface roughness parameters.
summary: Atomic force microscopy images characterize the surface morphology of the hydrogel dressings. These visualizations, paired with calculated surface roughness parameters, provide a detailed assessment of the material's topography. The evaluation confirms that AFM is a primary technique used alongside SEM to analyze the surface characteristics of the prepared dressings.

caption: SRO evolution profile for (Ni,Co)3Al subjected to a single cascade, highlighting the kinetic response of the Co-doped intermetallic system.
summary: This panel displays the SRO evolution for (Ni,Co)3Al during a single cascade. It demonstrates how Co alloying influences the interplay between irradiation-induced disordering and kinetic reordering. The green dashed line indicates the time to reach equilibrium, with shaded regions representing the standard error derived from six independent simulation runs.

caption: Isothermal section at the ternary peritectic reaction temperature (γ + NiMo → Ni3Mo + P), depicting the formation of γ + P + Ni3Mo and P + NiMo + Ni3Mo three-phase regions.
summary: Representing the ternary peritectic reaction occurring above 1073 K, this diagram shows the phase equilibrium where γ + NiMo transforms into Ni3Mo + P. The resulting configuration features the formation of distinct three-phase coexisting regions, specifically γ + P + Ni3Mo and P + NiMo + Ni3Mo, within the Ni-Cr-Mo system.

caption: Calculated time-temperature-transformation (TTT) curves for as-built IN718 alloy, highlighting the kinetics of phase precipitation.
summary: This TTT diagram illustrates the transformation kinetics for as-built IN718 alloy, generated using JMatPro software. The plot identifies the transformation behavior of the delta phase, with the peak transformation temperature estimated at 900 ℃. This data provides critical insight into the thermal stability and phase evolution of the alloy.

caption: Representative 4x4x2 array of Gyroid TPMS unit cells with 10 mm dimensions, forming a 40x40x20 mm3 lattice structure.
summary: This visualization displays a Gyroid TPMS lattice structure composed of a 4x4x2 array of unit cells. Each unit cell maintains a constant 10 mm length along the principal coordinate axes, resulting in an overall sample dimension of 40x40x20 mm3, illustrating the designed geometry and coordinate system for the TPMS samples.

caption: Non-dimensional effective shear modulus G ̄ 12 of a hexagonal HMS beam network with S = -1 plotted against magnetic load ratio r i under anti-clockwise mechanical shear stress.
summary: Panel b displays the non-dimensional effective shear modulus G ̄ 12 for a hexagonal HMS beam network characterized by S = -1. The data shows the variation of the modulus with respect to the magnetic load ratio r i while subjected to anti-clockwise mechanical shear stress and a magnetic field.

caption: Top-down schematic view of the process zone indicating the starting points for Monte Carlo analysis rays, spaced at 1 mm intervals along the axes.
summary: This schematic provides a top-down view of the process zone, marking the specific starting points for the Monte Carlo analysis rays. These rays are arranged at 1 mm intervals along the axes, establishing the spatial grid required to perform the computational simulation of the process zone dynamics.

caption: Combined absorbance and transmittance spectra of 3D-printed discs containing 0.01%, 0.03%, and 0.05% (w/v) RhB-HZ concentrations after 3 hours of soaking in ethanol.
summary: This panel displays the absorbance and transmittance spectra for 3D-printed discs soaked in ethanol for 3 hours at varying RhB-HZ concentrations. The results indicate that these specific samples lack the characteristic visible absorption bands typically associated with RhB-HZ activation, suggesting distinct optical behavior compared to the solution state.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PEB43-i synthesized with two equivalents of BnOH, where the benzyloxide-terminated series [C] becomes the predominant end-group species.
summary: The sample prepared with two equivalents of BnOH, PEB43-i, displays the same mixture of end-groups as the previous sample. However, the benzyloxide-terminated series [C] becomes predominant in this spectrum, clearly highlighting the significant influence of the coinitiator concentration on the final end-group composition of the polymer.

caption: Focused ion beam transmission electron microscopy (FIB-TEM) image of the corrosion oxide scale, highlighting the presence of pore formations and whisker growth within the matrix.
summary: This FIB-TEM micrograph provides a detailed view of the corrosion oxide scale. The imaging reveals distinct morphological features, specifically well-defined pore formations and whisker growth within the oxide matrix, demonstrating the structural complexity of the corrosion layer formed under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of intermolecular forces in CS and HAP-CS films during MD simulation.
summary: This plot displays the time evolution of intermolecular forces within CS and HAP-CS films during MD simulation. The van der Waals interactions are significantly stronger in the HAP-CS film compared to the pure CS film, demonstrating that the incorporation of HAP effectively enhances the overall intermolecular interactions within the material structure.

caption: Mott–Schottky plots (C⁻² vs. potential) for L-PBF 316L stainless steel subjected to various exposure temperatures, illustrating the electronic structure and defect characteristics of the passive films.
summary: Mott–Schottky plots for L-PBF 316L stainless steel reveal the electronic structure and defect characteristics of passive films formed after different thermal treatments. The plots exhibit a broad flat region from approximately −0.2 V to 0.5 V vs. SCE, providing evidence for the stabilization of the passive layer under these specific potentials.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis of the Ni-P layer, revealing a composition of 77 wt% nickel, 15 wt% phosphorus, and 8 wt% other elements including carbon and oxygen.
summary: The EDS analysis provides the elemental composition of the deposited Ni-P layer. Results confirm the presence of 77 wt% nickel and 15 wt% phosphorus, with the remaining 8 wt% attributed to carbon and oxygen impurities. This quantitative breakdown characterizes the chemical makeup of the dense layer formed on the substrate.

caption: Bode impedance and Bode angle plots corresponding to the 1-day immersion condition.
summary: Bode impedance and angle plots for samples immersed for 1 day are presented. These curves provide frequency-dependent electrochemical data that complement the Nyquist plots. By analyzing the impedance magnitude and phase angle, the electrochemical corrosion performance of the DED-produced NAB alloys is quantified for the initial immersion period.

caption: Ashby diagram comparing the density-normalized specific UTS and specific E1 for various SLM metals, FFF polymer composites, and CFRP-AM materials, with PLA-SCF and PLA-SCCF marked by stars.
summary: The Ashby plot benchmarks the specific UTS and specific E1 of PLA-SCF and PLA-SCCF against a wide range of literature-reported SLM metals, FFF polymer composites, and CFRP-AM materials. The stars highlight the relative performance of the study's materials within the broader landscape of additively manufactured structural materials.

caption: Representation of a full atomic structure containing a single vacancy defect at a specific lattice position.
summary: This panel illustrates a pristine atomic lattice structure featuring a localized vacancy defect. It serves as the initial state for the defect identification methodology, providing a clear visual reference for how individual atomic positions are defined within the crystal lattice before applying subsequent computational analysis techniques for defect characterization.

caption: Bode diagrams for CP-Ti specimens showing phase angle versus frequency.
summary: Bode diagrams for CP-Ti specimens exhibit two distinct maxima in the phase-angle inverse Gaussian plot. These features confirm the presence of two time constants, which are associated with the specific electrochemical behaviors of the CP-Ti surface during the impedance measurements in the tested acidic solution.

caption: Equilibrium solidification phase diagram for Fe-based alloys containing 0.2 wt% C with varying Cr content, calculated using Thermo-Calc software.
summary: This CALPHAD-based equilibrium solidification phase diagram illustrates the phase evolution of Fe-based alloys with 0.2 wt% C as a function of Cr content. At a specific Cr concentration of 17 wt%, the simulation identifies the presence of BCC, FCC, M23C6, M2B, M3B2, and LAVES phases within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Schmid factor distribution map for the {111}<110> slip system in the specimen annealed at 900 °C.
summary: This panel presents the Schmid factor distribution map for the {111}<110> slip system after the specimen underwent annealing at 900 °C. As part of the comprehensive quantitative statistics analysis, this map demonstrates the effect of the highest tested annealing temperature on the spatial distribution of slip system activity.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the laminated high-entropy alloy featuring Fe elemental mapping to distinguish between CoCrNi and Fe50Mn30Co10Cr10 layers.
summary: The SEM image displays the laminated high-entropy alloy structure, which consists of alternating CoCrNi and Fe50Mn30Co10Cr10 layers. Fe elemental mapping is utilized to highlight the spatial distribution of iron, effectively enhancing the visual distinction between the two distinct high-entropy alloy components within the laminated material architecture.

caption: Microhardness distribution across the cross-section of the Al–Zn–Mg–Cu alloy build processed at room temperature.
summary: This panel illustrates the microhardness distribution across the entire cross-section of the Al–Zn–Mg–Cu alloy build fabricated at room temperature. The mechanical properties of the deposited component vary with the layer height, reflecting the influence of strengthening mechanisms such as solid solution, dislocation, grain refinement, and second-phase particle strengthening.

caption: Projection of the relaxed L12-type cluster structure along the 〈1000〉hcp direction, illustrating the specific geometric placement of Ni atoms within the octahedral metal framework.
summary: Representing the relaxed L12-type cluster structure, this panel provides a projection along the 〈1000〉hcp direction. The model confirms the lowest enthalpy configuration for the quaternary system, where two Ni atoms are strategically placed at opposite corners of the metal atom octahedron, consistent with the optimized structural model derived from computational analysis.

caption: Schematic representation of the WAAM process defining the reference coordinate system, where the X-axis denotes the welding torch traveling direction, the Y-axis the transverse direction, and the Z-axis the building direction.
summary: This schematic illustrates the WAAM process setup, establishing a standardized reference coordinate system. The X-axis corresponds to the welding torch travel direction, the Y-axis to the transverse direction, and the Z-axis to the building direction, providing a spatial framework for subsequent microstructure characterization and mechanical testing of the deposited alloy.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) trend for the LSP + UNSM-treated sample across sliding cycles.
summary: The LSP + UNSM-treated sample exhibits a COF trend that shows a gradual increase over the sliding cycles. This behavior is likely attributed to surface modifications and changes occurring during the wear test, reflecting the combined effect of the two surface treatment technologies.

caption: Nyquist plot of NAB alloys after 1 h of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, featuring an inset equivalent circuit model.
summary: This Nyquist plot displays the electrochemical impedance characteristics of NAB alloys after 1 h of immersion. The curves exhibit significant overlap, indicating comparable electrochemical behavior across different alloy samples. The inset equivalent circuit model is used to simulate the experimental results, providing a baseline for the initial corrosion resistance assessment.

caption: Bode impedance plots for CP5 samples after 0, 14, and 28 days of immersion, showing the frequency dependence of the impedance magnitude.
summary: Bode impedance plots for CP5 samples display the impedance magnitude as a function of frequency after 0, 14, and 28 days of immersion. Experimental values are compared against fitted data. These plots, alongside phase data, characterize the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy response of the porous surface during the immersion test.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of the blunt bridge microstructure, oriented along the normal direction (ND) with superimposed black lines indicating proposed grain boundaries.
summary: This EBSD inverse pole figure map displays the microstructure of the blunt bridge specimen viewed along the normal direction. Black lines delineate the proposed grain boundaries within the material. The visualization provides a clear representation of the crystallographic orientation distribution and structural boundaries present in the analyzed weld region.

caption: Ternary diagram of the CrFeNi system illustrating the optimized path generated by the RRT*FN algorithm.
summary: The RRT*FN algorithm determines a specific path through the CrFeNi ternary space, which is visualized on a ternary diagram. This path represents a sequence of compositions that can be precisely mapped to the ternary system, providing a clear spatial representation of the alloy design strategy employed in the study.

caption: Energy distribution profile measured outside the focal plane to characterize the curing region.
summary: Energy distribution outside the focal plane is visualized here to support quantitative predictions of the 3D curing region. By analyzing these distributions, researchers can effectively control the cured width and depth in the z-direction, thereby avoiding asymmetric overcuring and maintaining the structural integrity of complex micro-scale components during fabrication.

caption: X-ray slice of the assembly with steel coverings, exhibiting significant metal artifacts and high noise levels that obscure the polymer-background interface.
summary: This panel presents an X-ray slice of the assembly with steel coverings. The high density of the steel induces substantial metal artifacts and elevated noise levels throughout the reconstruction. These conditions create significant difficulties in differentiating between the background and the polymer, complicating the accurate characterization of the specimen's internal geometry.

caption: Chronoamperometric response of SLMed and sintered AlSi10Mg alloys immersed in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel displays the chronoamperometric behavior of additive-manufactured and sintered AlSi10Mg alloys in a 3.5 wt% NaCl environment. The test evaluates passive film stability and pitting corrosion susceptibility. Observations indicate that alloy A1 exhibits superior stability compared to other additive-manufactured samples during the immersion period in the saline solution.

caption: SHAP value summary plot illustrating feature importance for multitask DNN predictions across 1250 test RVE samples, where red and blue dots represent high and low feature values respectively.
summary: This SHAP summary plot quantifies feature importance for multitask DNN predictions using 1250 test RVE samples. Fiber volume fraction emerges as the most significant predictor with a mean absolute SHAP value of 0.314, followed by porosity at 0.221. Color-coded dots indicate the directional impact of high versus low feature values.

caption: Optical micrographs of the Blend 1 (Ar + 50% He) sample at the layer center, showing the microstructure without shielding on the left and with supplementary shielding on the right.
summary: These optical micrographs illustrate the microstructure of the Blend 1 (Ar + 50% He) sample at the layer center. By contrasting the unshielded and shielded conditions, the images reveal how the addition of helium and the use of supplementary shielding affect the grain structure and particle morphology in the layer.

caption: Comparison of experimental and predicted yield strength values for IN718 and IN718-GNP composite materials.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between experimental and predicted yield strengths for IN718 and IN718-GNP composites. The data reveals that the theoretical model consistently overestimates the yield strength compared to the actual experimental results, indicating a discrepancy between the predicted values and the measured mechanical performance of the composite materials.

caption: Measured transmission spectrum of the CuCrZr + 316L composite sample along the build direction, plotted with theoretical spectra for both CuCrZr and 316L.
summary: This panel presents the transmission spectrum for the CuCrZr + 15 wt% 316L composite specimen after FOBI reconstruction. By comparing the measured data with theoretical spectra for both constituent materials, the results indicate that the strong texture observed in the pure CuCrZr alloy is significantly reduced in this mixed sample.

caption: Annular dark-field (ADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy image showing a lamella extracted from a grain boundary region, highlighting the grain boundary alpha (GB alpha) phase.
summary: This ADF-STEM image displays a lamella cut from a region containing two distinct grains. The micrograph specifically highlights the grain boundary alpha phase, providing a structural overview of the interface region before further magnification and detailed analysis of the rectangular-like phase located near the grain boundary.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of rabbit BMSCs cultured on a Coral-hHAp scaffold after 4 days, highlighting enhanced cell attachment and viability.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of BMSCs on the Coral-hHAp scaffold at day 4 confirms high cell viability and proliferation. The results demonstrate that the specific surface morphology of the Coral-hHAp scaffold promotes a healthier cellular environment with fewer dead cells, supporting its potential for effective integration in biological systems.

caption: Electrical resistance evolution of the metamaterial cell recorded across consecutive measurement steps.
summary: This plot tracks the electrical resistance of the metamaterial cell for each consecutive measurement. The resistance change is primarily attributed to the beam-like springs, serving as a viable metric to estimate the average temperature of the metamaterial cell during the experimental testing process.

caption: Non-Eulerian graph example containing more than two nodes connected to an odd number of edges, preventing the existence of a continuous Eulerian path or circuit.
summary: This graph serves as an example of a structure that is neither Eulerian nor semi-Eulerian. It fails to meet the criteria for such paths because it contains more than two nodes connected to an odd number of edges, precluding a continuous traversal of all edges.

caption: Layout of the experimental Air Gap Membrane Distillation (AGMD) rig used for testing the fabricated composite membranes.
summary: The experimental AGMD rig setup is illustrated to show the testing environment for the composite membranes. This apparatus facilitates the evaluation of the three membrane configurations described in the study. By integrating the membranes into this rig, researchers can assess the distillation performance and operational characteristics of the fabricated materials.

caption: Absolute stress-life (S-N) curves comparing as-built, annealed, and aged specimens.
summary: This panel displays absolute S-N curves for as-built, annealed, and aged specimens. The data indicates that both heat-treated conditions exhibit superior fatigue performance compared to the as-built state. Furthermore, within the as-built surface condition, the annealed and aged specimens demonstrate similar fatigue behavior, highlighting the positive impact of heat treatment.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of unmodified gelatin showing the baseline chemical shifts of the protein backbone.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of unmodified gelatin provides a baseline characterization of the protein structure. This spectroscopic analysis serves as a control to compare against methacrylated gelatin, allowing for the identification of chemical modifications introduced to the gelatin backbone through the absence of specific vinylic or methyl group signals.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image highlighting bright spots located at the boundary of an alpha lath.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a high-resolution view of the interface between an alpha lath and the beta phase matrix. Distinct bright spots are visible at the boundary of the alpha lath, indicating localized compositional variations or structural features within the microstructure of the solidified material.

caption: HRTEM image of zone II in modified NiTi, highlighting the exfoliation phenomenon on the surface.
summary: This HRTEM image captures the microstructure of zone II in modified NiTi. Unlike zone I, the surface of this zone exhibits a distinct exfoliation phenomenon. The image provides structural context for the strain analysis performed in this region, which is adjacent to Ti2Ni nanoprecipitates within the B2 matrix.

caption: Initial mosaic cubic model of a Ni-based single crystal superalloy constructed by substituting Ni3Al structural units into a 75x75x75 Ni block.
summary: This panel displays the initial mosaic cubic model of a Ni-based single crystal superalloy. The structure is generated by substituting Ni3Al structural units for Ni units within a 75x75x75 Ni block, maintaining consistent lattice directions to establish the foundational geometry for the superalloy simulation.

caption: Three-dimensional scatter plot illustrating the correlation between inclusion cluster size, average particle distance, and orientation angle for fatigue-tested specimens.
summary: This 3D scatter plot displays the statistical relationship between inclusion cluster size, average particle distance, and orientation. Analysis reveals that inclusion cluster orientations are uniformly distributed between 4° and 70°. Notably, clusters within the higher 35–66° orientation range exhibit a higher propensity for inducing crack initiation during fatigue testing.

caption: Ranking of MEP, T S, and R S control parameters for the ultimate tensile strength (σ B T) and ultimate flexural strength (σ B F) responses.
summary: This panel displays the feature importance rankings for control parameters influencing ultimate tensile strength and ultimate flexural strength. Derived from the second stage of optimization using a Full Factorial design, the plot identifies the relative significance of MEP, T S, and R S parameters in determining these specific mechanical response metrics.

caption: Predicted solid solution strengthening of the gamma-prime phase versus bulk Ta content, with the RR1000 patent range indicated.
summary: The solid solution strengthening of the gamma-prime phase is plotted against varying bulk Ta content. The shaded area represents the RR1000 patent range, allowing for a direct comparison between the simulated strengthening trends and the established industrial specifications for this alloy's composition.

caption: Enthalpy increment of Cr2O3 as a function of temperature, calculated via molecular dynamics simulations using various potentials.
summary: Enthalpy increments for Cr2O3 derived from MD simulations are plotted against temperature. The results demonstrate that all tested potentials yield very similar values, particularly at temperatures below 2000 K. These simulated enthalpy increments show good agreement with established experimental values, validating the consistency of the potentials used in this study.

caption: Mohr-Coulomb failure envelopes representing the shear stress versus normal stress relationship for sand-geocell-GAC interfaces, illustrating the influence of varying geocell pocket sizes on interface shear characteristics.
summary: This plot displays the Mohr-Coulomb failure envelopes for sand-geocell-GAC interface tests. By plotting shear stress against normal stress, the figure demonstrates how different geocell pocket sizes affect the interface shear behavior of the GAC system, providing a visual representation of the failure criteria for these specific geotechnical configurations.

caption: Additional energy dispersive spectroscopy analysis of sample S5, further characterizing the elemental composition within the regions of WC particle agglomeration.
summary: EDS analysis of sample S5 provides further evidence of WC particle agglomeration induced by the applied magnetic field. This clustering of particles is a critical factor in the formation of unfused void defects during the printing process, which ultimately leads to a decrease in the overall mechanical properties of the sample.

caption: Surface morphology of 5Y-PSZ captured via atomic force microscopy after 20h of aging.
summary: Surface morphology of 5Y-PSZ captured via atomic force microscopy after 20h of aging. This visualization illustrates the surface state of the 5Y-PSZ specimen following a 20-hour aging period, allowing for a direct comparison with the unaged sample to assess the impact of aging on the material's surface topography.

caption: Surface topography of F40C60 Y2O3 ceramic sintered at 1700 °C, capturing the roughness features of the 40% additive composition.
summary: Presented here is the surface topography of F40C60 Y2O3 ceramic sintered at 1700 °C. This measurement supports the systematic evaluation of surface roughness evolution in sintered Y2O3 cores, a critical factor for determining the surface finish quality of titanium castings produced using these specific ceramic core materials.

caption: Surface morphology of the SLS sample after 10 minutes of chemical etching, revealing the emergence of slight micro-protrusions.
summary: Following 10 minutes of chemical etching in an H+:H2O2 solution with a 1:0.4 molar ratio, the SLS surface begins to change. Microscopic analysis shows that the previously smooth surface is now covered with slight micro-protrusions, marking the initial stage of surface modification through the etching process.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of the hydrogel contact lenses after immersion in a 0.75 mM gold precursor concentration.
summary: The absorption spectrum for the hydrogel lens treated with a 0.75 mM gold precursor concentration is presented. This measurement is part of a series evaluating the optical response of the lenses as a function of precursor concentration, providing insight into the formation and density of gold nanoparticles within the hydrogel.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for (NdNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattices, highlighting the half-metallic gap and calculated mean magnetic moments for Ni-3d and O-2p states.
summary: Panel e displays the PDOS for the Nd-based superlattice. It includes the half-metallic gap of the down-spin channel and the mean magnetic moments for Ni-3d and O-2p orbitals. This contributes to the broader analysis of how the electronic structure evolves as the lanthanide element changes within the superlattice series.

caption: Phase angle variation across a range of frequencies for 3D-printed coated electrodes.
summary: This panel presents the phase angle response of 3D-printed coated electrodes over a specified frequency range. As part of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis, this plot characterizes the capacitive and resistive contributions of the electrode interface, offering insights into the electrochemical behavior and stability of the printed electrode architecture.

caption: Combined dataset integrating grain-averaged orientations from NF-HEDM and lattice strains from FF-HEDM, prepared as a multi-modal input for the computational framework.
summary: Integrating data from concurrent NF-HEDM and FF-HEDM techniques, this panel presents a multi-modal dataset. By combining grain-averaged orientations and lattice strains, the figure provides a comprehensive structural and mechanical input for the analytical framework, capturing the state of the material within the defined region of interest.

caption: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) table demonstrating that Layer Height significantly influences the response variable with an Adjusted Sum of Squares of 259,118, an F-Value of 1156.61, and a P-Value of 0.000.
summary: The ANOVA table provides statistical confirmation that Layer Height is the dominant factor affecting the roughness of 3D printed results. With a high Adjusted Sum of Squares of 259,118 and a P-Value of 0.000, the analysis demonstrates a highly significant influence of this parameter on the response variable.

caption: Mechanical property trends for Al-Fe alloys presented as a function of alloying content.
summary: This panel summarizes the evolution of mechanical properties for the Al-Fe alloy system as a function of alloying content. The plot illustrates the relationship between the concentration of iron and the resulting mechanical performance, allowing for a direct comparison of how these secondary phases influence the overall mechanical properties of the alloys.

caption: SHAPley values for features in dataset D4 computed over the trained SVM-4 model, showing the distribution of categorical dependent variable influence.
summary: SHAPley values for dataset D4, derived from the trained SVM-4 model, quantify feature impact on performance. Color-coded regimes (red, blue, and green) indicate the influence on categorical dependent variables, demonstrating that all three categories possess equal magnitude and significant importance in the model's predictive decision-making process.

caption: X-ray microtomography scan of an untreated PEI specimen following tensile fracture.
summary: This X-ray microtomography image displays the internal structure of an untreated PEI specimen after undergoing a tensile test. The scan is utilized to evaluate the porosity within the fractured material, providing a visual assessment of the specimen's structural integrity and damage characteristics following mechanical failure.

caption: Macro morphology of a 35-layer thin-walled component fabricated using the CMT + ADV arc mode.
summary: Macro morphology of a 35-layer thin-walled component fabricated using the CMT + ADV arc mode. This photograph captures the macro-scale features of the component, showcasing how the advanced arc mode influences the layer-by-layer build quality and overall morphology of the 35-layer thin-walled structure during the manufacturing process.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulated potential energy curves for BCC (red) and FCC (black) phases as a function of composition in AlxNi0.7-xCo0.132Cr0.064Fe0.104, featuring a blue dotted line representing the common tangent.
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations calculate the potential energy of BCC and FCC structures for the specified alloy composition. The resulting energy-composition curves, shown in red and black, illustrate a thermodynamic driving force for the BCC to FCC transformation in the as-printed state, despite potential kinetic limitations without external disturbances.

caption: Calculated phase stability diagram for the (Ti6Al4V)50(NiCo)50 alloy system, illustrating the thermodynamic regions for B2 and cubic phase formation.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram evaluates the thermodynamic stability of B2 and cubic phases within the (Ti6Al4V)50(NiCo)50 alloy system. Based on this analysis, the specific composition of Ti6Al4V (50 wt%) combined with Ni (42 wt%) and Co (8 wt%) was identified and selected for further experimental investigation and material development.

caption: Reflection magnitude distributions for arbitrary combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 86 GHz and 90 GHz, showing values between 0.67 and 0.98.
summary: Panel d shows the reflection magnitudes for combinations of Cell 1 and Cell 2 at 86 GHz and 90 GHz. The data highlights high reflection efficiency in the higher frequency band, with magnitudes measured between 0.67 and 0.98, validating the consistent performance of the proposed meta-atom across the W-band.

caption: Laser absorptivity spectra of mixed powders measured across the 500–2000 nm wavelength range.
summary: This panel displays the laser absorptivity of mixed powders over a broad wavelength range from 500 to 2000 nm. The data characterizes the optical response of the material system, providing a comprehensive overview of how the mixed powders absorb laser energy across the specified electromagnetic spectrum.

caption: Thermo-kinetic E-pH diagram for Monel 400 in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 85 °C, with black dots indicating measured OCP values.
summary: Monel 400 performance at 85 °C is depicted through this thermo-kinetic diagram. Black dots represent the measured OCP values across the pH range. This visualization allows for the assessment of how elevated temperatures influence the electrochemical state of the alloy in acetate solutions compared to the room temperature baseline.

caption: Tafel slopes for OER activity comparing Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocage, nanocube, Co-Ni@NC, and RuO2.
summary: The Tafel slope analysis for the oxygen evolution reaction shows that the Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocage exhibits a low Tafel slope of 87 mV/dec. This indicates favorable reaction kinetics for the OER process, confirming the nanocage structure as the champion catalyst among the evaluated materials.

caption: Comparison of simulated precipitation kinetics and experimental volume fraction measurements for Cu-1.48Ni-0.5Si-0.52Co alloy aged at 500 °C.
summary: This figure validates a quantitative precipitation simulation for a Cu-1.48Ni-0.5Si-0.52Co alloy aged at 500 °C. It presents the simulated precipitation behavior alongside experimental volume fraction data collected at various aging times, demonstrating the accuracy of the established quantitative relationship in predicting the microstructural evolution of the alloy during thermal treatment.

caption: Volumetric porosity rates of AZ31 magnesium alloy manufactured with and without ultrasonic vibration (UV) assistance.
summary: This bar chart compares the volumetric porosity rates of AZ31 magnesium alloy processed with and without ultrasonic vibration. The application of ultrasound significantly improves material quality by reducing porosity size, facilitating a transition from large-scale lack of fusion defects to smaller, regular pores, and eliminating interlayer chain-like porosities.

caption: 3D surface morphology of the TiC-steel-based cermet worn track at 300 °C under a 10 N load, highlighting extensive debris compaction.
summary: The 3D worn surface at 300 °C exhibits extensive debris compaction and patch formation within the wear track. This structural change is a direct result of thermal softening of the debris material induced by friction heat, which becomes more significant as the operating temperature of the cermet increases.

caption: Side-by-side view of a three-dimensional BCC unit cell with R = 0.35 mm (Vf,3D = 0.457) and the equivalent two-dimensional numerical unit cell with Re = 0.105 mm (Vf,2D = 0.275).
summary: Panel c presents the final configuration of the BCC unit cell with a 3D radius of 0.35 mm and a 2D equivalent radius of 0.105 mm. These geometric parameters are essential for the numerical modeling of three-point bending tests, where simulation results demonstrate a close match to experimental curves in the elastic region.

caption: Pole figure of the {001} crystal plane for the AH-1000–60 specimen.
summary: This pole figure shows the {001} crystal plane orientation for the AH-1000–60 specimen. Similar to other samples treated below 1100 ℃, the maximum intensity is high, and the microstructure preserves the {001} < 100 > rotated cube texture, demonstrating the influence of lower homogenization temperatures on the initial crystallographic state.

caption: Relationship between the LPBF scanning trajectory and the resulting microstructure.
summary: This schematic illustrates the correlation between the LPBF scanning trajectory and the resulting microstructural features. By mapping the laser path, the diagram explains how specific scanning strategies influence grain growth and orientation, providing a clear link between the processing parameters and the final metallurgical state of the material.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the XY-Y specimen at 5% strain, showing unindexed points localized along the MPB.
summary: Deforming the XY-Y specimen to 5% strain results in the observation of unindexed points along the MPB. Similar to the XY-X orientation, these unindexed regions in the inverse pole figure map reflect the impact of mechanical strain on the microstructure and crystallographic indexing within the MPB zone.

caption: Lowest spin-wave band gaps plotted against the squeeze ratio s for the reversed Co/Py 2D MC composition, showing only the second and fourth gaps opening.
summary: The graph illustrates the band gap evolution for the reversed Co/Py material composition relative to the squeeze ratio. In this configuration, only the second and fourth gaps open, and the reference notes that the ability to regulate these band gaps is significantly poorer compared to the Py/Co base structure.

caption: Tabulated dimensions and geometric specifications for the tensile samples used in the study.
summary: Presented are the exact measurements and geometric specifications for the tensile samples illustrated in panel c.
