These dimensions provide the necessary data for calculating mechanical properties during testing, ensuring that all samples conform to the required standards for the L-CPBF material characterization performed in this investigation.

caption: Single cell tracking analysis of C3H10 T1/2 cells treated with TPO, documenting morphological changes and migration behavior.
summary: Single cell tracking analysis for the TPO-treated group documents cell morphology and migration behavior over time. These results are used to compare the biological performance of TPO against C5, showing that TPO results in lower migration capacity and higher cytotoxicity in C3H10 T1/2 cell lines.

caption: Axial, lateral, and shear strain contour plots for hexagonal honeycomb samples under impact loading.
summary: Hexagonal honeycomb structures are analyzed via DIC to visualize strain distribution during dynamic impact testing. The contour plots display the axial, lateral, and shear strain components up to maximum compression. Excessive wall bending in this dynamic scenario reduces observable strain localization, leading to a characteristic smearing effect across the unit cells.

caption: Nyquist plots for printed and cast CORRAX® and 17–4PH samples measured at 70°C, demonstrating reduced charge transfer resistance (Rct) compared to room temperature measurements.
summary: Measurements at 70°C show a reduction in overall impedance and capacitive loop diameters for all materials compared to 25°C. The smaller depressed semicircles indicate lower charge transfer resistance. Notably, 17–4PH exhibits larger semicircle diameters than CORRAX®, confirming its superior electrochemical performance even at these elevated operating temperatures.

caption: Density of states plot for the HfC(001)/Ni(001) interface, highlighting the Fermi level with a black dashed line and the orbital hybrid position with a blue dashed line.
summary: The density of states for the HfC(001)/Ni(001) interface reveals a clear hybrid phenomenon between C p-orbitals and Ni d-orbitals, indicating Ni-C covalent bond formation. The DOS intensity at the interface differs from bulk materials, though the bond strength is limited as indicated by lower DOS at the Fermi level.

caption: Magnetic field intensity variation over time for loaded and unloaded conditions, normalized to the initial mean wire temperature.
summary: Magnetic field intensity variations are depicted as a function of time for both loaded and unloaded experimental conditions. The trends are evaluated relative to the initial mean temperature of the wire, providing a comparative analysis of how the magnetic field intensity evolves during the thermal analysis of the solenoid.

caption: Discharge voltage profile of the nanoporous silver (np-S) electrode, derived from the de-alloying of the Ag-75at.% Al precursor in NaOH.
summary: This panel displays the discharge voltage curve for nanoporous silver (np-S) produced via de-alloying the Ag-75at.% Al precursor in NaOH. Tested in 0.1 M KNO3, the electrochemical capacitance is compared at a 0.20 V datum, highlighting the performance differences resulting from the nanoporous structure compared to the as-deposited alloy.

caption: 3D reconstruction of specimen S7 showing pore distribution within a 20 × 23 × 10 mm³ volume, with pores color-coded by equivalent diameter.
summary: The 3D reconstruction of specimen S7 illustrates the spatial distribution of pores within a 20 × 23 × 10 mm³ volume. Pores are color-coded by their equivalent diameter, revealing a relatively uniform porosity throughout the specimen without the presence of significant interconnected pore networks or extreme pore anomalies.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of tenocytes on MEW wavy scaffolds during phase I culture, where green indicates live cells and red indicates dead cells.
summary: This fluorescence microscopy image displays tenocytes cultured on MEW wavy scaffolds during phase I. Live cells are visualized in green, while dead cells appear in red. Cell viability was well maintained throughout this phase, consistently exceeding the 93% threshold at all observed time points, demonstrating high biocompatibility of the scaffold.

caption: Particle size distribution of the CoCrFeNiMo0.2 HEA feedstock powder represented as a frequency histogram.
summary: This histogram illustrates the particle size distribution of the CoCrFeNiMo0.2 high-entropy alloy feedstock powder. The distribution data is crucial for understanding the physical characteristics of the gas-atomized powder, facilitating a detailed comparison of the feedstock quality across different molybdenum concentrations used in the subsequent deposit fabrication experiments.

caption: Bar chart quantifying the HAGB strength across different heat input conditions, demonstrating the influence of boundary density on mechanical performance.
summary: This plot quantifies HAGB strength, illustrating how these boundaries effectively pin dislocations to enhance both strength and plasticity. By providing more grain boundaries to impede dislocation motion, the fine-grained structure improves deformation resistance, hardness, and overall mechanical performance in samples subjected to varying heat inputs.

caption: Low-magnification secondary electron image of the as-built UNS N07001 specimen showing initial microstructural features.
summary: This low-magnification secondary electron image displays the as-built UNS N07001 specimen. The microstructure exhibits characteristic features of the EB-PBF process, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of subsequent post-processing treatments on the material's internal integrity and grain structure.

caption: Nyquist plot representing the electrochemical impedance behavior of SLM 316L stainless steel processed at a laser scanning speed of 800 mm/s after 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance response of SLM 316L stainless steel fabricated at 100 W and a scan speed of 800 mm/s. The data reflects the material's corrosion behavior after 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution, providing insight into the surface electrochemical properties under these specific processing conditions.

caption: FT-IR spectra comparing the chemical signatures of the pure CuO–ZnO–ZrO2 precursor, clear resin, and the final mixed precursor-loaded ink.
summary: FT-IR spectroscopy was performed on the CuO–ZnO–ZrO2 precursor, clear resin, and the precursor-loaded ink to evaluate the ink preparation process. The spectra confirm whether any chemical changes occurred in the ingredients during the mixing process, ensuring the integrity of the individual components within the final ink formulation.

caption: Average DFT prediction RMSE plotted against the number of factories, comparing Federated Learning (FL) and Independent Learning (IL) approaches.
summary: This plot displays the average DFT prediction RMSE for models trained across varying numbers of factories, ranging from 3 to 45. The data reveals that while RMSE generally trends upward as the number of factories increases, the performance gap between FL and IL highlights the impact of statistical heterogeneity on model accuracy.

caption: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Random_AB specimen showing the distribution of γ’ precipitates and a grain boundary.
summary: This atom probe microscopy reconstruction visualizes the microstructure of the Random_AB specimen. It highlights the spatial arrangement of γ’ precipitates and the presence of a grain boundary. The image demonstrates a clear distinction between coarse primary and fine spherical secondary γ’ phases within the INC738 alloy microstructure.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile for specimen 1, comparing BD (red) and SD (black) conditions.
summary: The neutron diffraction profile for specimen 1 is presented, illustrating the structural characteristics of the material. The plot compares the peak profiles obtained from BD (red) and SD (black) conditions, providing initial insights into the crystalline state of the specimen as part of the broader experimental characterization.

caption: LR regression validation set parity plot for relative density and dimensional change after PCA dimensionality reduction.
summary: The LR validation set parity plot demonstrates compromised predictive performance. Because the model fails to adequately capture primary features and instead learns from noise during training, its ability to generalize to the validation set is significantly hindered, resulting in poor alignment between predicted and actual values.

caption: Temperature distribution within the cross-sectional melt pool during AMMT processing at 179.2 W and 800 mm/s.
summary: This panel illustrates the simulated temperature distribution across the melt pool cross-section for Case B parameters. By utilizing adaptive mesh refinement (AMR), the simulation achieves high accuracy in thermal gradients while bypassing traditional mesh size constraints, providing a detailed view of the thermal field after the laser has passed.

caption: Phase distribution map of SLM TA31-1000 alloy showing HCP α-Ti and BCC β-Ti phases.
summary: The phase distribution map of the SLM TA31-1000 alloy identifies the presence of hexagonal close-packed α-Ti and body-centered cubic β-Ti phases. This mapping confirms the dual-phase nature of the alloy structure as produced by the selective laser melting technique.

caption: Extended continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram constructed from dilatometry results, incorporating predicted transformation temperatures at 500 °C/s represented by open symbols.
summary: The extended CCT diagram provides a comprehensive view of transformation kinetics based on dilatometry measurements. It integrates experimental data with extrapolated transformation temperatures at 500 °C/s, which are highlighted as open symbols. This diagram serves as a critical reference for understanding phase evolution across varying cooling conditions.

caption: Mean wear coefficients of steel ball counter-bodies recorded after tribological testing at 25 °C.
summary: Presented here are the mean wear coefficients for steel ball counter-bodies following tribological testing at 25 °C. These measurements, paired with the plate data, reflect the interaction performance of the MMC system, showing how different MoS2 particle configurations in the plates affect the wear of the counter-body material.

caption: Two-dimensional contour plot illustrating the interaction between the aspect ratio (l/ds) and tilt angle (ω) on the joining strength of Ti/Mg bimetal.
summary: This contour plot displays the interaction between the aspect ratio (l/ds) and tilt angle (ω) regarding the joining strength of Ti/Mg bimetal. The elliptical shape of the contour indicates a significant interaction between these two structural parameters, which is critical for optimizing the bimetal joining process.

caption: Histogram of misorientation angles between neighboring prior-β grains for cases (g-i), highlighting the non-uniform β nucleation characteristics.
summary: This histogram shows the misorientation angle distribution for varying focal offset distances. The observed non-random distribution of angles between neighboring prior-β grains supports the conclusion of non-uniform β nucleation, which is attributed to the cyclic solid-state phase transformation phenomena inherent in the LPBF processing of Ti-6Al-4V.

caption: Cooling DSC thermograms for rPET and PA6-CF 3D printing filaments, highlighting the exothermic recrystallization peaks recorded during the cooling phase.
summary: Cooling DSC curves reveal the recrystallization behavior of rPET and PA6-CF filaments through exothermic peaks. As part of the comprehensive thermal evaluation reported in the study, these results characterize the solidification process of the materials, offering insights into their crystallization kinetics relevant to their performance in 3D printing applications.

caption: CAD model of the Diamond lattice structure viewed from the top.
summary: The CAD model for the Diamond lattice structure is presented from a top-view perspective. This model acts as the design benchmark for the LPBF fabrication process, allowing for a systematic comparison between the intended Diamond lattice geometry and the actual as-fabricated structure to assess manufacturing accuracy.

caption: UV transmittance spectra of RBCs filled with varying contents of HA-SS, demonstrating a reduction in transmittance with increased filler incorporation.
summary: UV transmittance measurements evaluate the optical properties of the RBCs inks as a function of HA-SS filler content. The data indicates that incorporating HA-SS fillers significantly reduces UV transmittance, suggesting that the filler concentration effectively modulates the optical transparency of the resulting material for potential dental applications.

caption: Depth profile of microhardness for unSMATed and SMATed parts, illustrating the hardness gradient induced by the SMAT process.
summary: This panel displays the microhardness depth profile for unSMATed and SMATed specimens. The SMAT process induces a significant hardness gradient, with values plateauing at a depth of approximately 1.2 mm. At this depth, the hardness of the SMATed part decreases to levels comparable to the matrix material.

caption: Photometric absorption at 560 nm measured via Alizarin red assay, quantifying the calcification of SaOs-2 cells on Cr-alloyed Ti samples versus references, with Cr-alloyed samples showing significantly reduced calcification capacity.
summary: Calcification of SaOs-2 cells was measured using an Alizarin red assay at 560 nm. The photometric absorption results indicate that all Cr-alloyed Ti samples exhibit a significantly reduced calcification capacity compared to the reference materials, with statistical significance confirmed by ANOVA and Bonferroni post-hoc testing (p < 0.009).

caption: Fluorescence spectra of SOSG under varying ultrasound (US) treatment durations, showing a progressive increase in intensity.
summary: Fluorescence spectra demonstrate that the intensity of SOSG increases gradually with longer ultrasound stimulation times. This trend confirms the effective generation of reactive species or structural changes within the hydrogel system in response to external US stimuli, facilitating controlled release or therapeutic activation.

caption: Deconvoluted XPS spectra of the pristine powder sample, utilizing the TiO2 2p 3/2 peak at 458.6 eV as a reference binding energy.
summary: Deconvoluted XPS spectra for the pristine powder are shown, employing the TiO2 2p 3/2 peak at 458.6 eV as the reference binding energy. Sequential peak assignments identify primary and secondary peaks as TiO2, while the tertiary peak is attributed to metallic Ti, providing insight into the chemical bonding states.

caption: COHP curves for B-Ni and B-Re atomic pairs, emphasizing the antibonding electronic environment at the Fermi level for boron-segregated grain boundaries.
summary: Boron-segregated and B-Re co-segregated Ni grain boundaries are evaluated through COHP plots. The Fermi levels are observed to fall into the B-Ni antibonding regions, where -COHP is less than zero. This confirms the presence of occupied antibonding states, which are critical for understanding the electronic stability of the segregated grain boundary.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 2.75 μm Co7Ni3 hcp nanorods on glassy carbon at 50 mV s−1, comparing 0.5 M NaOH (dotted) and 0.5 M NaOH + 0.5 M MeOH (continuous) solutions, with an inset showing the current density difference (jox2 - jox1).
summary: Co7Ni3 hcp nanorods exhibit distinct electrochemical responses in alkaline methanol solutions. The cyclic voltammogram at 50 mV s−1 reveals the methanol oxidation peak, which is clarified in the inset by calculating the difference between current densities with and without methanol, effectively isolating the oxidation contribution from the oxygen evolution background.

caption: 3D greyscale reconstruction of the raw WF30-PLA filament illustrating its structural features.
summary: Captured via microtomography at the ESRF BM05 beamline, this 3D greyscale image depicts the raw WF30-PLA filament. The visualization highlights a morphology that is notably more irregular and porous than the GF30-PA6 filament, providing clear evidence of the distinct structural differences between the two raw filament types.

caption: Nyquist plots of NAB alloys after 1 day of immersion, highlighting the formation of larger capacitive loops, particularly for the HT-1 condition.
summary: Following 1 day of immersion in NaCl solution, the Nyquist plots reveal the formation of larger capacitive loops compared to the 1-hour immersion state. This increase in capacitive loop size is more pronounced for the HT-1 specimen, suggesting an evolution in the electrochemical interface and corrosion resistance over time.

caption: Calculated volume fraction of precipitated phases in Ti-12Al-xNb alloys at 700 °C as a function of Nb content.
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated volume fraction of phases in the Ti-12Al-xNb system at 700 °C. Results indicate that the volume fraction of the B2/β phase increases rapidly when Nb content exceeds 48 at%, which negatively impacts the alloy's strengthening effect, suggesting an optimal Nb content below 48 at%.

caption: Number of cycles to fracture (NCF) determined via rotary bending tests for NiTi rotary files heat-treated at 460, 480, and 500 °C for 120 min.
summary: Rotary bending test results illustrate the number of cycles to fracture for NiTi rotary files after heat treatment at varying temperatures. A clear correlation exists between the hardness values and the NCF, supporting the established principle that increasing the hardness and strength of these alloys effectively enhances their overall fatigue properties.

caption: Second cooling DSC thermograms for PEA and FPEA-ProGly recorded at a scanning rate of 10 °C/min.
summary: The second cooling DSC thermograms for PEA and FPEA-ProGly, obtained at a 10 °C/min rate, illustrate the thermal behavior of these materials. Both samples exhibit semi-crystalline characteristics during the cooling cycle, as evidenced by the thermal transitions captured in the DSC analysis presented in the figure.

caption: SR-PXD Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 310 K, with phase indexing for TiNiSi orth., Ni2In hex., and MgZn2.
summary: SR-PXD refinement for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 310 K is presented. The pattern is indexed with tick marks for TiNiSi orth., Ni2In hex., and MgZn2 phases. Joint refinement with PND data enables the determination of Fe occupancies in Mn and Ni sites by overcoming the low contrast between Fe and Ni.

caption: Cr-W-C ternary phase diagram at 1000 °C showing the equilibrium composition for Scenario 1, which aligns with the WC-(Cr,W)3C2 tie-line.
summary: This panel displays the Cr-W-C ternary phase diagram at 1000 °C, calculated via Thermo-Calc. It illustrates the equilibrium composition for Scenario 1, which is positioned on the WC-(Cr,W)3C2 tie-line. This diagram serves as a reference for evaluating the powder and coating compositions under the specified thermodynamic conditions.

caption: Contour plot showing the concentration variation of W, which segregates toward dendrite cores.
summary: W concentration variation is visualized through a contour plot derived from meso-scale simulations. W acts as a γ-forming element that segregates to the dendrite arms. This result completes the observation of elemental partitioning, where γ-forming elements like W, Cr, Co, and Mo consistently segregate to dendrite cores during solidification.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for LPBF-produced 316L steel samples, comparing untreated and LEHCEB-treated surfaces after 30 minutes of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for LPBF-produced 316L steel samples are shown after 30 minutes of immersion in 3.5% NaCl. The data compares untreated and LEHCEB-treated surfaces, revealing a distinct passivation region for all samples tested under these specific electrochemical conditions, indicating the initial corrosion behavior of the materials.

caption: Time-dependent electronic temperature behavior for 50 keV 2T-MD cascades in NiCr.
summary: Represented here is the electronic temperature evolution for a 50 keV 2T-MD cascade in NiCr. The curves depict temperature along the y-dimension of the MD box. The highest temperature regions indicate the cascade development area, while the box edges are maintained at 300 K throughout the simulation.

caption: Hysteresis loops for AM-CM hybrid NdFeB/SmFeN PA12 magnets, illustrating the magnetic response for both random and post-printing aligned conditions at 300 K.
summary: The hysteresis loops for hybrid NdFeB/SmFeN PA12 magnets are shown here, highlighting the difference between random and post-printing aligned particle orientations. The post-alignment magnetic performance is quantified by a remanence of 8.5 kG, a coercivity of 11.05 kOe, and a maximum energy product of 116.18 kJ/m3 at room temperature.

caption: Principal component analysis projection of fingerprints learned by a variational autoencoder compared against artificial fingerprints generated via the Gaussian cloud method, with original data points in grey and artificial points colored by their respective gamma values.
summary: This PCA plot visualizes the distribution of fingerprints learned by a variational autoencoder alongside noise-perturbed fingerprints generated using the Gaussian cloud method. Original fingerprints are represented in grey, while artificial fingerprints are color-coded by gamma values, demonstrating how the model transforms and maps these data points in reduced dimensional space.

caption: Atomic model of the TiNi3 crystal structure, featuring equilibrium lattice constants of a = b = 5.111 Å and c = 8.338 Å.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic unit cell of the TiNi3 intermetallic compound. The crystal structure is characterized by specific equilibrium lattice constants, with a and b dimensions measuring 5.111 Å and the c dimension measuring 8.338 Å. This model depicts the spatial configuration of Ti and Ni atoms.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of the cutting edge using EBM-Al2O3 nanofluid lubrication.
summary: This EDS map displays the cutting edge under EBM-Al2O3 nanofluid lubrication. Notably, this combination resulted in the smallest BUE thickness among all tested cases, demonstrating that while other fluids showed no pronounced differences, the nanofluid significantly influenced the BUE characteristics during the machining process.

caption: Three-dimensional models of L, D, and G type TPMS porous structures designed for DLP fabrication.
summary: These three-dimensional models represent the L, D, and G types of TPMS porous structures. These designs serve as the foundational geometries for specimens fabricated using DLP technology, which subsequently undergo debinding and sintering processes to achieve their final integrated structural forms with varying relative densities.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the 20 mA specimen microstructure showing dislocation tangles.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the 20 mA specimen reveals the presence of dislocation tangles within the microstructure. The analysis indicates that martensitic laths are almost entirely absent in this condition, while a limited number of dislocation tangles and some recrystallized grains are observed, characterizing the specimen's internal defect structure.

caption: Fatigue performance of L-PBF Ti-64 specimens grouped by part location, where central specimens generally exhibit superior performance compared to north and south locations.
summary: Fatigue behavior is analyzed here based on the specific part location within the L-PBF build. The data indicates that central specimens typically demonstrate better fatigue performance than those located in the north or south positions. Grip-failed specimens are highlighted with arrows to ensure accurate interpretation of the fatigue results.

caption: Reflectance RL curves demonstrating the collaborative optimization of dual absorption peaks for L5 GMSs.
summary: This panel presents the collaborative optimization results for L5 GMSs, specifically focusing on the dual absorption peaks. The data illustrates the effectiveness of the customized method proposed in the study for tailoring absorption peaks, providing a clear visualization of the optimized electromagnetic response for the L5 configuration.

caption: Technical drawing of the tensile specimen geometry designed for room temperature mechanical testing.
summary: This panel provides a technical drawing of the tensile specimens used for mechanical characterization at room temperature. The design follows the established experimental parameters for the study, ensuring consistent geometry for evaluating the mechanical properties of the fabricated samples under standard ambient conditions.

caption: Nonlinear surface electric current response of oriented SiC w composites under varying voltage conditions.
summary: Panel c displays the nonlinear surface electric current response of oriented SiC w composites. The data confirms that the electric current increases exponentially with voltage, a characteristic behavior of these oriented composites. This nonlinear conductivity is a key feature of the material's electrical performance as discussed in earlier research.

caption: TOF-SIMS depth profile of an as-grown Cu-Ni alloy film with 1000 nm Cu and 50 nm Ni, representing the elemental counts versus sputtering depth.
summary: This TOF-SIMS depth profile for the 1000 nm Cu/50 nm Ni alloy film shows the elemental counts of Cu, Ni, and C. Carbon atoms diffuse into the alloy during growth, and the Ni- concentration is at its lowest among the samples, consistent with the trend of decreasing Ni- concentration with increasing copper thickness.

caption: Calcein AM staining of MC-3T3-E1 cells cultured on PGCL scaffolds with varying Vancomycin concentrations after 3 and 5 days of growth.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy using Calcein AM staining visualizes the adhesion and growth of MC-3T3-E1 cells on PGCL scaffold surfaces. The images, captured after 3 and 5 days of culture, demonstrate the cellular response to different Vancomycin concentrations, providing a qualitative assessment of cell attachment and distribution across the scaffold architecture.

caption: Ragone plot comparing the specific energy and specific power of the CHBAC device against similar quinone-carbon based symmetrical supercapacitor devices reported in literature (references 45–51).
summary: The Ragone plot evaluates the energy storage performance of the CHBAC device by mapping its specific energy against specific power. By comparing these values with those of similar quinone-carbon based symmetrical supercapacitor devices from existing literature, the plot demonstrates the competitive performance characteristics of the CHBAC system.

caption: Thermal pyrolysis profile of zirconia samples recorded under an argon atmosphere.
summary: Represented here is the pyrolysis curve of zirconia samples under an argon atmosphere. This plot serves as a critical reference for the degreasing process, detailing the thermal behavior of the material in an inert environment to ensure proper sample preparation prior to the subsequent sintering stage.

caption: Main effect plot displaying the sensitivity of bead width (BW) to variations in the primary WAAM process parameters.
summary: The main effect plot for bead width (BW) highlights the relationship between WAAM process parameters and the resulting bead geometry. By analyzing this plot, one can observe how specific adjustments to the manufacturing variables impact the width of the deposited bead, providing essential data for optimizing the WAAM process control.

caption: Nyquist plot representing the electrochemical impedance response of the XY section of Wall 0.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance response for the XY section of Wall 0. Degradation properties are indicated by the reduction of the semicircle diameter over time. Although corrosion phenomena initially occur, the presence of corrosion products appears to decelerate these processes after two days of exposure.

caption: TEM imaging and EDS analysis of ZIF-8 particles, demonstrating the morphology and elemental composition.
summary: TEM imaging and EDS analysis of ZIF-8 particles reveal their morphology and elemental composition. Elemental mapping confirms a homogeneous distribution of Zn and N within the particles, indicating successful synthesis and uniform chemical composition of the ZIF-8 scaffold components.

caption: Thermal expansion strain (dL/L0) versus temperature for the D45 specimen of LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy, with a black dashed line showing the linear extrapolation from 0 ℃ to 300 ℃.
summary: This plot displays the thermal expansion strain of the D45 specimen of LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy. The data includes a black dashed line representing the linear extrapolation of dL/L0 from 0 ℃ to 300 ℃, which helps characterize the thermal expansion characteristics of the D45 specimen.

caption: Calculated martensite start temperature and stacking fault energy (SFE) based on the simulated Scheil microsegregation profile.
summary: Calculated martensite start temperatures and SFE values are derived from the simulated Scheil microsegregation profile. The results demonstrate that solid forming at the beginning of the solidification process will primarily transform into martensite, whereas the terminal solid is predicted to form a fully austenitic microstructure in the #40HSLA steel.

caption: High-power (60 mW) photoluminescence spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample at 77 K, displaying Voigt-profile fits and identifying additional emission peaks E3 and E4.
summary: This high-power 60 mW photoluminescence spectrum at 77 K reveals additional emission features, specifically peaks E3 and E4. These peaks exhibit energy separations of 100 meV and 92 meV from the primary E0 and E1 peaks, respectively, providing further insight into the complex electronic structure of the sample.

caption: Ultimate compressive strength plotted against compressive fracture strain for the AlCr1.3TiNi2 MEA, highlighting its performance relative to other M/HEA systems.
summary: The ultimate compressive strength is evaluated against compressive fracture strain in this Ashby plot. By comparing the AlCr1.3TiNi2 MEA with various Co-free and CoFeNi-based M/HEAs, the plot demonstrates the material's ultimate load-bearing capacity and deformation limits in relation to a broad spectrum of previously reported high-entropy alloy compositions.

caption: MCR-ALS derived component spectra for reduced 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 during DRM at 750 °C and 1 atm with a CH4/CO2 ratio of 1/1.5.
summary: Shown here are the MCR-ALS derived XANES component spectra for the catalyst under DRM conditions with a 1/1.5 CH4/CO2 ratio. The analysis confirms that the derived components are identical to those found in the 1/2 ratio dataset, demonstrating consistent spectral features across these specific reaction conditions during the 30-minute experiment.

caption: Absorbance spectra of TPO, TPO-L, BAPO, and CQ photoinitiators measured across the 350–500 nm wavelength range.
summary: This panel displays the absorbance spectra for TPO, TPO-L, BAPO, and CQ photoinitiators within the 350–500 nm range. These spectral profiles characterize the light-absorption capabilities of each initiator, indicating that CQ would demonstrate superior effectiveness compared to the other tested photoinitiators if the light source operates specifically at a 450 nm wavelength.

caption: Alloy corrosion morphology at 3000 timesteps representing the stabilization period.
summary: Reaching the corrosion stabilization period at 3000 timesteps, the simulation demonstrates that the inner and outer corrosion layers have fully formed on the alloy surface. This stage marks the culmination of the evolutionary flow of the corrosion process, characterized by the established layered structure of the protection products.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots for passive films on annealed Ti–6Al–4V (ATC4) measured after potentiostatic polarization at potentials ranging from 2.6 V to 3.0 V.
summary: Mott-Schottky measurements were conducted on passive films formed on ATC4 samples under potentials between 2.6 V and 3.0 V. These plots allow for the investigation of semiconductive properties, specifically comparing the electronic behavior of the passive films on annealed Ti–6Al–4V alloys against those produced via laser powder bed fusion.

caption: Digital Shore D Durometer utilized for hardness testing in compliance with ASTM D 2240 standards.
summary: Hardness testing is conducted using a Digital Shore D Durometer. The equipment is operated in accordance with the ASTM D 2240 standard to ensure consistent and accurate measurement of the material's surface hardness properties. This setup provides a reliable method for characterizing the mechanical resistance of the tested specimens.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 10 m/min and constant travel speed.
summary: Shown is the current-voltage profile for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 10 m/min. This plot illustrates the electrical behavior of the deposition process at the highest tested feed rate, providing a comparison point for the peak current and duration characteristics observed.

caption: Histogram illustrating the frequency distribution of prediction errors across the entire 18-layer T-shaped wall structure.
summary: This histogram displays the error distribution for the entire 18-layer T-shaped wall structure. It highlights the frequency of prediction errors, showing that approximately 7% of elements exhibit errors exceeding 15%, which confirms the overall efficacy and reliability of the ANN-FE framework in predicting residual stress distributions.

caption: Aperiodic E minimal surface constructed from the pentagonal prism-based unit cell.
summary: The aperiodic E minimal surface is presented as a complex structure formed by the assembly of pentagonal prism-based units with edge-oriented tunnels. This panel illustrates the final result of the Tile(1,1)-based construction method, highlighting the non-periodic nature and structural complexity of the resulting minimal surface design.

caption: Calculated Griffith work difference (ΔWfrac) for interfacial layers at Ni and Ni+Nb positions, representing the energy change when increasing in-plane concentration from 12.5 at.% to 25 at.% by adding a substitute atom.
summary: This plot displays the calculated Griffith work difference (ΔWfrac) for co-existing interfaces at Ni and Ni+Nb positions. It quantifies the energy change occurring when an extra substitute atom is added to a lattice plane, increasing the in-plane concentration from 12.5 at.% to 25 at.%, thereby illustrating the interfacial stability.

caption: Programmed shape-recovery process of a 10 wt% mPLA 4-arm OD triggered by an external magnetic field.
summary: The shape-recovery process of a 10 wt% mPLA 4-arm occlusion device is captured as it responds to an external magnetic field. This demonstration confirms the 4D-printing capability of the device to undergo controlled, stimulus-responsive deformation, which is essential for minimally invasive delivery and subsequent deployment in clinical settings.

caption: Detailed view of the absorption frequency extension achieved by the metastructure in the low-frequency regime of 2–4.5 GHz.
summary: Focusing on the low-frequency range of 2–4.5 GHz, this panel illustrates the absorption frequency extension provided by the multiscale resonant labyrinth metastructure. By strategically combining different cavity dimensions, the design effectively enhances performance in this specific band, showing clear improvements over standard unit configurations as confirmed by comparative analysis.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness values plotted against indentation displacement for as-casted and AM-ed HEA samples, illustrating a general decreasing trend in hardness as penetration depth increases.
summary: This plot displays the nanoindentation hardness as a function of displacement for as-casted and AM-ed HEA specimens. The data reveals a consistent decreasing trend in hardness values as the penetration depth increases, providing a clear comparison of the mechanical response between the two different processing conditions of the material.

caption: Logarithmic Ashby plot comparing stiffness versus yield strength for a variety of common metals and thermoplastics, highlighting the defined physical boundaries for these material categories.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the relationship between stiffness and yield strength for common metals and thermoplastics on a logarithmic scale. By mapping these mechanical properties, the figure defines the physical boundaries of material performance, ensuring that selected values for these categories remain within realistic and physically consistent limits.

caption: Raman spectra comparing fresh and used Ni/ZrO2 and Ni-Zn/ZrO2 catalysts to investigate the nature and extent of coke deposits.
summary: Raman spectroscopy is employed to characterize carbonaceous species on the catalyst surfaces. By comparing fresh and used samples, the spectra reveal the presence and type of coke deposits formed during the 100-hour DRM reaction, providing insight into the deactivation mechanisms of the Ni-based catalysts.

caption: Areal surface roughness (Sa) of the side lattice surface plotted as a function of laser power and scanning speed.
summary: Side surface roughness values are displayed relative to laser power and scanning speed, showing a trend similar to the top surfaces. An exception occurs at 200 W and 200 mm/s, where excessive energy input increases roughness due to larger melt pools and accelerated fluidity, resulting in significant deviations from designed values.

caption: Long-term stability test of the PV-AOR system, tracking the current density and Faradaic efficiency (FE) for nitrite production over a 10-hour duration.
summary: The stability test reveals that the system maintains an average current density of approximately 46 mA cm-2 over 10 hours. The Faradaic efficiency for nitrite production decreases from 77.0% to 40.0% during this period, which is attributed to the progressive depletion of the ammonia reactant in the electrolyte.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of contact lenses following immersion in a 2.25 mM gold precursor concentration.
summary: This plot displays the optical absorption characteristics of the hydrogel contact lens after treatment with a 2.25 mM gold precursor solution. The spectrum provides data on the light absorption properties resulting from the in situ gold reduction process within the hydrogel matrix at this specific concentration.

caption: Proteomics mass spectrometry analysis comparing protein adsorption capacity between Ti-MgPi coated samples and uncoated Ti control samples.
summary: Proteomics mass spectrometry analysis reveals that the Ti-MgPi coated sample exhibits a higher plasma protein adsorption capacity, identifying 97 proteins compared to 76 proteins on the uncoated Ti control substrate. This indicates that the MgPi coating significantly enhances the protein adsorption profile of the titanium surface.

caption: 13C NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer, featuring numbered peaks 1–19 corresponding to various carbon environments.
summary: The 13C NMR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer displays numbered peaks from 1 to 19. These signals confirm the presence of ArCH2N, OCH2N, alkylene chain carbons, as well as aromatic and alkene carbons, all of which are essential components of the BBZ monomer's established molecular structure.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the HT2 90° C263 material variant.
summary: This inverse pole figure map shows the HT2 90° variant, which shares the characteristic eradicated texture and high density of annealing twins found in the HT2 0° sample. These microstructural features are critical for enhancing the material's resistance to crack propagation during superplastic forming operations.

caption: Heating RLC–T curves and derivative plots for steel S2, identifying an operational T A of 1031 °C based on the decay of the derivative peak.
summary: The thermal analysis of steel S2 reveals a clear austenitizing transition during the heating cycle. By monitoring the first derivative of the RLC–T curve, the operational austenitizing temperature T A is determined to be 1031 °C, corresponding to the point where the derivative peak decays and linearity is restored.

caption: Indexed FFT pattern of the grain boundary particle, confirming it belongs to the Fd3̅m cubic space group with a lattice parameter of 2.824 nm.
summary: The indexed FFT pattern of the particle confirms that the precipitate belongs to the Fd3̅m cubic space group. With a measured lattice parameter of 2.824 nm, this structural identification provides definitive evidence of the phase type, supporting the conclusion that these particles are distinct from the aluminum matrix.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph and STEM-EELS elemental mapping of particles sintered in air, demonstrating homogeneous distribution of Co, Ni, and O.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging of air-sintered particles reveals mass-thickness contrast, which is attributed to thickness variations rather than compositional differences. STEM-EELS mapping confirms a homogeneous distribution of Co, Ni, and O throughout the particle, indicating that the observed contrast is purely structural rather than a result of elemental segregation.

caption: Bend-dominated lattice structure featuring a regular hexagonal unit cell topology.
summary: This panel displays a lattice structure characterized by regular hexagonal unit cells, which is classified as a bend-dominated architecture. Three samples of this hexagonal lattice were tested to investigate the mechanical response of this specific topology, highlighting the influence of unit cell geometry on the overall structural performance.

caption: Equilibrium phase fractions calculated at the HIP temperature for the measured Laves phase composition, incorporating all available phases from the thermodynamic database.
summary: This panel displays the equilibrium phase fractions calculated at the HIP temperature using the average measured Laves phase composition as input. By considering all available phases within the thermodynamic database, the plot provides a comprehensive overview of the predicted phase stability for the specified material composition under these conditions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the un-irradiated zone of the 4Al10V sample shown in panel (a).
summary: This SAED map corresponds to the un-irradiated zone of the 4Al10V alloy highlighted in panel (a). It serves as a baseline diffraction pattern to compare against the irradiated zones, confirming the initial crystallographic state of the material before exposure to the ion irradiation process at 500 °C.

caption: Phase angle-frequency Bode plots for SLM and wrought plus annealed samples, highlighting passive film characteristics.
summary: Phase angle-frequency Bode plots demonstrate the electrochemical behavior of the samples. Phase angles approaching -90 degrees from low to medium frequencies indicate the formation and growth of a stable passive film. This behavior confirms the development of a protective surface layer on the SLM as-built and wrought plus annealed specimens.

caption: Contour plot comparing experimental fracture loads against predicted fracture load values.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the relationship between experimental and predicted fracture loads. By mapping these values, the visualization provides a direct comparison to evaluate the accuracy of the predictive model against empirical data, highlighting the correlation between observed mechanical performance and the model's output for the fracture load analysis.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy profile for Mg–5Ni alloy exposed to pure hydrogen gas.
summary: This thermal desorption spectroscopy profile illustrates the hydrogen release behavior of Mg–5Ni alloy under pure hydrogen exposure. The data provides a baseline for analyzing hydrogen desorption peaks, which are critical for understanding the material's hydrogen storage characteristics and the evolution of desorption kinetics across multiple thermal desorption cycles.

caption: Learning curve for Model IV, which identifies deposit types derived from A-type magma.
summary: Model IV shows the learning curve for an XGBoost model developed to identify deposit types originating from A-type magma. The plot illustrates the model's learning progress, highlighting its performance in classifying deposits that are specifically linked to A-type parental magmas.

caption: Catastrophic shattering failure of a 24 mm width HC3DP specimen observed after reaching a maximum force of 45800 N.
summary: This panel depicts the catastrophic failure of a 24 mm width HC3DP specimen. The element shatters completely upon reaching a significantly higher maximum force of 45800 N. This failure mode highlights the distinct mechanical behavior and structural integrity limits of the larger scale HC3DP configuration compared to smaller specimens.

caption: Representative load-displacement diagram obtained from nanoindentation testing, used to determine the strength of the Fe-rich phases.
summary: This load-displacement diagram represents the nanoindentation data collected from the Fe-rich phases in the alloys. By analyzing these curves, the strength of the spherical Fe-rich phases is quantified. These mechanical measurements confirm the positive role these phases play in enhancing the formability and bendability of the homogenized alloys.

caption: Orthogonal view of 3-D ray trajectories for a source located on the x-axis within the x = δ + δ' plane.
summary: This panel displays the orthogonal view of 3-D ray trajectories originating from a source on the x-axis. The simulation illustrates how rays travel from the source inside an aluminum sphere toward the ice medium, providing a geometric representation of the ray path within the specified x = δ + δ' plane.

caption: FFT and IFFT images of zone F, characterizing the dense-row hexagonal structure.
summary: The FFT and IFFT analysis of zone F confirms the presence of a dense-row hexagonal structure. This structural identification complements the amorphous analysis of zone E, providing a comprehensive understanding of the crystalline and non-crystalline phases present within the interfacial region of the 3D-printed TC4 substrate.

caption: Bode impedance and phase angle response of NAB alloys after 3 days of immersion in the electrolyte.
summary: Representing the electrochemical state after 3 days of immersion, these Bode plots characterize the impedance and phase angle of LPBF-deposited NAB alloys. The comparison between as-built and annealed samples highlights how thermal processing influences the long-term electrochemical stability and surface film characteristics during extended electrolyte exposure.

caption: Final grain structure resulting from the DDRX process, showing a refined morphology of 58,617 polyhedral grains evolved from the initial state under a mobility parameter of κ = 0.95.
summary: Representing the final outcome of the DDRX simulation, this panel illustrates a significantly refined microstructure containing 58,617 polyhedral grains. This evolved state was achieved from the initial 3000-grain Voronoi tessellation by applying a grain boundary mobility parameter of κ = 0.95, demonstrating substantial grain multiplication and structural evolution.

caption: Scanning transmission electron microscopy image of a STFN0 powder particle following reduction, highlighting the distribution of exsolved nanoparticles across the oxide surface.
summary: This STEM image displays a STFN0 powder particle after reduction. The visualization reveals the morphology and spatial distribution of exsolved nanoparticles on the surface of the oxide support, providing a clear view of the structural changes occurring during the reduction process under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Reflection phase response for cell 1 across the 60 to 70 GHz frequency range, measured while cell 2 remains constant.
summary: This panel displays the reflection phase delay for cell 1 within the 60-70 GHz lower band. The meta-atom design allows the cell to cover the full 2π phase range during this frequency interval while cell 2 is held constant, demonstrating the effectiveness of the FSS for dual-band reflect array applications.

caption: Scatter plot correlating the number of crack initiation sites observed via fractography with the fatigue life of the specimens.
summary: This plot demonstrates the inverse relationship between the number of crack initiation sites and fatigue life. As the number of initiation sites increases, the fatigue life of the specimen decreases, illustrating the catastrophic impact of pore clusters. This quantitative trend confirms the fractographic observations regarding the detrimental nature of pore interactions.

caption: Magnetic free energy F mag of fcc Co calculated from Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: This panel illustrates the magnetic free energy F mag for fcc cobalt as determined by Monte Carlo simulation. The plot characterizes the magnetic energy landscape of the fcc structure, contributing to the overall assessment of the thermodynamic properties of cobalt as modeled in the study.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry thermograms of neat P(3HB) and composite films, showing second heating cycles as solid lines and second cooling cycles as dashed lines.
summary: DSC thermograms reveal a slight decrease in the melting point for all composite formulations compared to neat P(3HB). Notably, the P(3HB)/Inkjet composite exhibits a double peak, suggesting the formation of two distinct crystalline structures induced by the filler, with the inkjet filler providing the greatest reduction in melting point.

caption: High-magnification scanning transmission electron microscopy image showing the microstructure near the corroded surface of the WAAM-HT sample.
summary: This high-magnification STEM image focuses on the area immediately adjacent to the corroded surface of the WAAM-HT sample. It serves to characterize the local microstructural features and potential phase interactions occurring near the corrosion front, facilitating a better understanding of the material's degradation mechanisms.

caption: Nyquist diagrams representing the impedance response of MP and AR Alloy 690 samples after 24 hours of immersion in simulated PWR primary water at 325 °C and 130 bars.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical impedance spectra for MP and AR Alloy 690 specimens after 24 hours of exposure to simulated primary water at 325 °C. The Nyquist plot illustrates the corrosion behavior of these materials at the corrosion potential under high-pressure conditions, providing insight into the initial surface oxidation characteristics.

caption: Mises stress distribution predicted by CPFE at the end of cycle 3 (4100N) illustrating residual stress patterns.
summary: Cycle 3 CPFE simulation at 4100N displays the Mises stress field. This visualization highlights the residual stress distribution and its inherent heterogeneity around the agglomerate, illustrating how the stress state evolves within the material structure at the unloaded state following the third loading cycle.

caption: Short-circuit current (ISC) versus time curves for a single-branch HETENG subjected to cyclic loading at a rate of 20 mm/s.
summary: This panel displays the short-circuit current output of a single-branch HETENG under cyclic loading at 20 mm/s. The data illustrates the electrical generation performance, showing distinct current peaks during the extending and retracting phases of the mechanical cycle, which are critical for evaluating the device's energy harvesting efficiency.

caption: TGA and DTG thermograms of cured neat adhesive under an air atmosphere.
summary: Thermal stability of cured neat adhesives evaluated under air reveals oxidative degradation processes. All samples exhibit complete combustion of carbonaceous char, resulting in zero residual mass at 800 °C, as demonstrated by the corresponding TGA and DTG curves showing the progression of mass loss during heating.

caption: Energy cost evolution over time for different alpha-Al2O3 bed heights, compared against the thermal limit of air plasma at 965 mbar.
summary: Energy cost is displayed relative to time for various alpha-Al2O3 bed heights. The graph incorporates the thermal limit of air plasma at 965 mbar and a techno-economic target range. It demonstrates how the catalyst bed heating influences energy efficiency, with smaller fill volumes flattening toward plasma-only production levels.

caption: Ge 3d XPS spectrum of the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film anode after 20 cycles.
summary: The Ge 3d XPS spectrum for the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film anode is shown after 20 cycles. This analysis probes the surface chemical information of germanium, allowing researchers to monitor how the chemical environment of the Ge element evolves on the anode surface during the early stages of electrochemical battery cycling.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of the ternary Co–Ni–Mo alloy coating measured at 50 mV s−1 in 1 M KOH across the potential range of −0.08 to −0.58 V vs RHE, characterized by a distinct oxidation peak and cycle-dependent cathodic current density enhancement.
summary: This CV curve for the Co–Ni–Mo alloy coating, measured in 1 M KOH at 50 mV s−1, spans −0.08 to −0.58 V vs RHE. It features an oxidation peak similar to the Co–Mo variant, while the cathodic current density at −0.58 V vs RHE increases with the number of cycles performed.

caption: Thermal analysis curves for Mn1-y Ni1-y Fe2y Si0.95 Al0.05 compositions (y = 0.30, 0.32, and 0.35), highlighting the structural transition behavior observed during thermal cycling.
summary: DSC traces for three Mn1-y Ni1-y Fe2y Si0.95 Al0.05 compositions with y values of 0.30, 0.32, and 0.35 are presented. These curves characterize the structural transition temperatures, which are observed around 273 K for the Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 composition and 303 K for the Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 composition, confirming the structural transition behavior.

caption: Color map visualization of droplet volume (v) and aspect ratio (ra) relative to waveform parameters (u and t) for the last 500 samples.
summary: Representing the last 500 samples, this heatmap shows the relationship between droplet features and waveform parameters. Similar to the first 500 samples, the droplet features here exhibit improved consistency for given waveform parameters, confirming that isolating specific sample segments reduces the observed fluctuations in droplet volume and aspect ratio.

caption: Functional Analysis System Technique (FAST) diagram illustrating the hierarchical relationship between five primary system tasks (T1–T5, yellow boxes) and seven critical system functionalities (K1–K7, orange boxes).
summary: This FAST diagram provides a structured representation of the system requirements by mapping five main tasks, highlighted in yellow, to seven essential functionalities, denoted by orange boxes. The framework, refined from established functional analysis techniques, serves to define and organize the critical operational requirements necessary for the system's overall performance.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves for Ni0.8Cu0.2 layered hydroxides (LHs) and bare Ni(OH)2 in 0.5 M NaOH + 55 mM NH4Cl, showing a sharp increase in ammonia oxidation current above 300 mV.
summary: Linear sweep voltammetry curves compare the ammonia oxidation performance of Ni0.8Cu0.2 layered hydroxides against bare Ni(OH)2 in an alkaline electrolyte. The data demonstrates a sharp increase in the oxidation current for the catalyst at anode potentials exceeding 300 mV, indicating enhanced electrochemical activity for the modified material.

caption: Retardance map for the LCoS-SLM at a gray level (GL) of 150, resulting in a maximum retardance of 605° and a minimum of 560°.
summary: The retardance map for the LCoS-SLM at a gray level of 150 shows a maximum value of 605° and a minimum of 560°. These spatial inhomogeneities are influenced by manufacturing imperfections, boundary conditions, and residual stress within the liquid crystal layer, which are characteristic of the device's performance across different gray levels.

caption: Polar figure of the DAT heat-treated sample illustrating the texture of (001), (111), and (110) planes.
summary: This polar figure displays the crystallographic texture of the DAT heat-treated sample across (001), (111), and (110) planes. The plot highlights the specific grain orientation distribution resulting from the DAT process, with labeled concentrated textures allowing for a clear comparison of the material's structural evolution after heat treatment.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of as-fabricated CM247LC showing small γ′ phases within the dendrite, with an inset SAED pattern showing 010 superlattice reflections.
summary: This panel presents the γ′ phase distribution within the dendrite of as-fabricated CM247LC, marked by blue arrows. The inset selected area electron diffraction image confirms the presence of 010 superlattice reflections. These small γ′ phases, approximately 8 nm in size, result from the precipitation of the matrix γ phase.

caption: Microstructure of the WEBAM-built Udimet 500 sample processed with 600W sonication (US-600W), showing primary γ-grain refinement in the ZOY plane.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the microstructure of the WEBAM-built sample processed with 600W sonication. The effect of primary γ-grain refinement is apparent in the ZOY plane. The sample is characterized by the absence of defects such as voids and cracks, indicating high structural quality throughout the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Elastic modulus curves obtained by fitting the mechanical response data for each specific Gyroid wall thickness.
summary: Elastic modulus curves are plotted to represent the mechanical properties of the Gyroid structures. These curves are derived by fitting the data obtained from the individual wall thicknesses, providing a clear visualization of how the elastic modulus varies across the different structural dimensions tested in the finite element analysis.

caption: Temperature-dependent DC magnetization cooling curve and its derivative for the x = 0.3 composition, showing a two-step transition below the ferromagnetic state at T2 and T1.
summary: The DC magnetization curve for the x = 0.3 composition displays a two-step transition below the ferromagnetic state. Specifically, a transition occurs at T2 followed by a martensitic transition near T1. The temperature derivative of the magnetization curve further highlights these distinct magnetic transitions during the cooling process.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay curve and corresponding fitting for TPU/0.5S composite at 490 nm emission.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime decay and fitting curves for the TPU/0.5S composite are presented at an emission wavelength of 490 nm. Monitored at room temperature with an excitation wavelength of 373 nm, this sample exhibits an average lifespan within the 3–5 ns range, consistent with low SAOED addition levels.

caption: Nanohardness distribution map on the X-Z plane for pure tungsten deposited via SLM at an energy density of 617 J/mm3 (B27).
summary: Displaying the B27 specimen, this nanohardness map characterizes the hardness distribution on the X-Z plane for pure tungsten deposited at 617 J/mm3. The data indicates an uneven hardness profile across the plane, where cracked regions exhibit lower hardness values compared to the surrounding material, reflecting the influence of processing conditions.

caption: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 noHT (black) and A1 HT2 (red) samples measured at 123 K, with green asterisks indicating peaks associated with the Fm-3m austenitic phase.
summary: This figure displays powder neutron diffractograms for A1 noHT and A1 HT2 samples at 123 K. The data compares the structural characteristics of the two samples, highlighting specific peaks identified as the Fm-3m austenitic phase with green asterisks. These measurements provide essential insights into the phase composition at cryogenic temperatures.

caption: Maximum current and power output of the reversible electrochemical cell as a function of NaCl concentration, maintained at a constant pH of 1.0.
summary: This panel demonstrates the impact of salt concentration on fuel cell performance at a constant pH of 1.0. Results indicate that both maximum current and power increase with higher NaCl concentrations, a trend attributed to reduced ohmic losses within the electrolyte, confirming the expected relationship between salt concentration and electrochemical performance.

caption: Four-by-four grid visualization of melting pool imaging clusters, where red integers indicate the count of similar images within each cell.
summary: The four-by-four grid displays clustered melting pool imaging data derived from the SOM analysis. Each cell represents a specific cluster of similar images, with the red numerical values denoting the frequency of occurrences within that category. This visualization effectively organizes high-dimensional melting pool data into a structured, interpretable format.

caption: Yield strength (YS) and ultimate compressive strength (UCS) of LPBF-fabricated Cu–Cr–Zr alloy plotted against varying strain rates, showing error bars derived from four independent tests per condition.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of LPBF-processed Cu–Cr–Zr alloy under dynamic loading. Both yield strength and ultimate compressive strength exhibit a clear increasing trend as strain rates rise, indicating significant strain rate hardening. Statistical reliability is ensured by averaging data from four independent tests, with error bars representing standard deviations.

caption: Top-view fluorescence microscopy image of PEI, P-TCP, and P-T-GDYO scaffolds showing the distribution of live and dead cells.
summary: This top-view fluorescence microscopy image displays the distribution of live and dead cells within PEI, P-TCP, and P-T-GDYO scaffolds. Analysis reveals that green-stained live cells are evenly distributed throughout the scaffold structure, while no red-stained dead cells are observed, indicating high cell viability across all tested scaffold groups.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of HFFs on a printed diamond texture Ti-6Al-4V surface (D1) after 7 days, illustrating ECM protein alignment with surface features and white arrows identifying circular regions of partially melted powders.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of HFFs on a printed diamond texture surface shows ECM proteins aligning with the surface topography. The presence of partially melted powder particles, indicated by white arrows, creates circular regions devoid of fluorescence, illustrating how the printed surface morphology dictates the organization of the extracellular matrix proteins.

caption: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) image displaying the surface morphology of the FSAM AA2195/TC4 joint interface.
summary: This AFM image illustrates the surface morphology of the FSAM AA2195/TC4 joint interface. The visualization provides a detailed view of the topographical features at the junction, which serves as the basis for analyzing the microstructural complexity and the resulting non-uniform potential field observed across the joint interface.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for the Wx(CoCrNi)1-x alloy system, showing the reduction in intermetallic compound fraction with decreasing tungsten content.
summary: Phase-diagram analysis of the Wx(CoCrNi)1-x system shows that the fraction of μ-phase and R-phase intermetallic compounds decreases as the W content is reduced. This relationship provides a strategy for minimizing the presence of brittle intermetallic phases at the W/CoCrNi interface by optimizing the tungsten concentration in the alloy.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto565 dye, highlighting the spectral filtering characteristics of this specific dye formulation.
summary: This panel shows the transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk with Atto565 dye. The data highlights the spectral filtering capabilities of the printed material, allowing for a consistent comparison with other dyes and commercial glasses tested under identical thickness conditions.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of grain G8, highlighting regions of increased orientation gradients and strain accumulation.
summary: The KAM map for grain G8 illustrates regions of increased orientation gradients, which correspond to areas of strain accumulation. These localized zones of higher misorientation highlight the internal deformation response of the grain, providing a clear visualization of the structural heterogeneity developed during the SAT-3 deformation stage.

caption: Melt drop morphology observed at an excitation current of 6A.
summary: At an excitation current of 6A, the molten droplet exhibits an increased rotational amplitude. This peak current condition demonstrates how the interaction between the magnetic field and charged particles in the arc significantly affects the transition behavior and shape of the molten droplets during the process.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (Z) map of Sample 11, processed at a high normalised energy density of 9.55.
summary: Sample 11, subjected to a high normalised energy density of 9.55, is examined using EBSD to evaluate its crystallographic texture. The resulting Inverse Pole Figure (Z) map illustrates the orientation of the grains, contributing to the comparative crystallographic texture data provided for the high energy density specimen in this study.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping showing the spatial distribution of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and gold elements on the adsorbent surface.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping is used to analyze the surface composition of the AM-N12 adsorbent. The maps visualize the spatial distribution of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and gold elements, corroborating the morphological observations and confirming the elemental presence of gold particles on the adsorbent surface after the adsorption process.

caption: Phase distribution map of the as-fabricated M2 HSS sample, identifying the spatial arrangement of α-Fe and other phases.
summary: This phase distribution map for the as-fabricated M2 HSS sample highlights the spatial arrangement of phases. The presence of M2C carbide indicates that eutectic carbides were not fully decomposed during EB-PBF cooling. This map provides a baseline for observing phase evolution across different service temperatures.

caption: Thermodynamic calculation of mixing enthalpy distribution in the HZ25 alloy at room temperature.
summary: Mixing enthalpy distribution for the HZ25 alloy is calculated at room temperature. The data indicates that the Ni-Hf-rich grain interiors exhibit more negative enthalpy values than the Cu-Ti-Zr-rich boundary regions, reflecting better chemical compatibility within the grain interiors compared to the boundary regions.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺:Er³⁺-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after the first thermal cycle at 600°C, showing characteristic Er³⁺ emission peaks and significant defect-related luminescence.
summary: Panel a displays CL spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures treated at 600°C. The data reveals characteristic Er³⁺ transitions alongside pronounced defect-related luminescence, particularly in samples with 7:1 and 1:7 doping ratios. This indicates the presence of amorphous regions and incomplete crystallization following the initial thermal treatment cycle.

caption: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Linear_AB specimen showing γ′ precipitates and a grain boundary.
summary: Atom probe microscopy reconstruction of the Linear_AB specimen reveals the distribution of γ′ precipitates and the presence of a grain boundary. The analysis highlights a clear distinction between coarse primary and fine spherical secondary γ′ phases within the microstructure, providing detailed insight into the spatial arrangement of these features.

caption: Dynamic mechanical response of 50 wt% Al2O3 composite resin during UV curing.
summary: The storage modulus for the 50 wt% Al2O3 composite resin is depicted in this panel. The results show that the storage modulus decreases with increasing concentration at this higher loading, suggesting that the mechanical properties of the cured composite resin are negatively impacted at this specific weight percentage.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of the Fe–Mn–Al–C alloy transverse cross-section processed at a scanning speed of 800 mm/s.
summary: Representing the microstructure of the Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steel, this EBSD inverse pole figure map displays the grain orientation data for the sample fabricated at a scanning speed of 800 mm/s. The map highlights the crystallographic texture developed within the transverse cross-section under these specific L-PBF manufacturing conditions.

caption: Temperature field distribution contour for a 20 μm particle size, showing a narrow, elongated high-temperature region with two distinct peak zones.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the temperature field distribution within a deposit for a 20 μm particle. The thermal profile is characterized by a narrow and long high-temperature region containing two distinct peak temperature zones, reflecting the thermal behavior during the deposition process at this specific particle size.

caption: Size distribution plot comparing CoCrNi and Al2O3 powders, measured via laser scattering particle size analysis in ethanol.
summary: Particle size distributions for CoCrNi and Al2O3 powders are determined using a laser scattering particle size analyzer. The powders were dispersed in ethanol to ensure accurate measurement, with the resulting data presented as a comparative distribution plot to characterize the physical dimensions of the raw materials used.

caption: Exergy destruction distribution across wall thickness and side length parameters for a system velocity of 200 m/s.
summary: This visualization depicts the optimization algorithm output for a system velocity of 200 m/s. By plotting total exergy destruction against wall thickness and side length, the panel highlights the sensitivity of the design space to higher velocity inputs during the iterative optimization process.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of [1-23]-oriented Cr-Co-Ni single crystal deformed to 205% strain, showing end-on deformation twins and an inset SAED pattern with streaks indicating random thin twin formation.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of a [1-23]-oriented Cr-Co-Ni single crystal deformed to 205% strain reveals end-on deformation twins. The inset SAED pattern displays Bragg reflection spots for the matrix and twin, alongside streaks parallel to the (111) primary plane normal, which signifies the presence of randomly formed thin twins.

caption: Temperature-dependent energy storage modulus curves for CP-PLA composites prepared at different PS preparation temperatures.
summary: This panel illustrates the energy storage modulus of CP-PLA composites across a temperature range, highlighting the influence of varying PS preparation temperatures on the material's mechanical response. The curves provide a comparative view of how thermal processing conditions during PS preparation affect the storage modulus behavior of the resulting composite materials.

caption: Pair distribution function G(r) evolution for the GB sample during heating from -175 to 550 °C.
summary: The pair distribution function G(r) for the GB sample is shown across a temperature range of -175 to 550 °C. These results illustrate structural changes occurring during the heating process, providing insights into the atomic ordering and relaxation effects within the GB material as it undergoes thermal treatment.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the chromium carbides observed in the TEM image, confirming the crystallographic nature of the precipitates.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern provides crystallographic confirmation of the chromium carbides observed in the TEM analysis. By analyzing this diffraction pattern, the structural characteristics of the carbides are identified, supporting the microstructural findings regarding the presence and distribution of these precipitates within the Alloy 690TT matrix.

caption: Calculated variations in stable stacking fault energy for the [1 2 ¯ 1] (111) slip system as a function of Cr, Co, Mo, and W solute additions.
summary: Using first-principles calculations, this plot displays the stable stacking fault energy variations for the [1 2 ¯ 1] (111) slip system in Ni3(Al, Ti) when alloyed with Cr, Co, Mo, and W. The results quantify how these specific alloying elements modify the intrinsic stacking fault energy of the base material.

caption: Neutron diffraction spectra comparing undeformed and fractured FCCN alloy specimens at 295 K, highlighting the emergence of a small peak at d = 1.94 Å corresponding to the {0002} planes of ε-martensite.
summary: Neutron diffraction spectra of FCCN alloy specimens are compared before and after tensile fracture at 295 K. While the undeformed specimen shows a single γ phase, the fractured specimen exhibits a small diffraction peak at d = 1.94 Å, indicating the limited formation of ε-martensite within the γ matrix.

caption: Tensile stress-strain curves illustrating the mechanical response of the investigated samples.
summary: Tensile stress-strain curves are presented to characterize the mechanical behavior of the samples. These curves provide a visual representation of the material's response under tensile loading, serving as the primary data for evaluating the strength and ductility of the as-printed and annealed specimens discussed in the study.

caption: APT reconstruction of the specimen after 0.2 h of ageing, highlighting the initial formation of small, globular gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime precipitates.
summary: Following 0.2 hours of ageing, the atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the emergence of small, globular precipitates. These features consist primarily of gamma-double-prime phases with some gamma-prime contributions, marking the onset of precipitation within the nickel-rich matrix as the material begins its transition from the solution-treated state.

caption: (100) pole figure derived from the EBSD map, where B denotes the building direction and S indicates the laser scan direction, characterizing the crystallographic texture.
summary: The (100) pole figure provides a detailed representation of the crystallographic texture within the as-built Inconel 625 sample. By referencing the building direction (B) and laser scan direction (S), this analysis clarifies the orientation distribution of the grains, which is essential for understanding the material's anisotropic properties.

caption: Simplified thermodynamic equilibrium phase diagram of the 316L-Al system generated via Thermocalc, highlighting furnace heat treatment isotherms as black dotted lines and specific Al compositions of the samples as red dashed lines, with B2 NiAl and L12 Ni3Al precipitates predicted in green and blue, respectively.
summary: This Thermocalc-simulated phase diagram for the 316L-Al system illustrates equilibrium phases, including B2 NiAl and L12 Ni3Al precipitates. Furnace heat treatment isotherms and specific sample Al compositions are marked. The diagram provides a theoretical basis for understanding the potential absence of B2 precipitates within the δ-ferrite phase during processing.

caption: Relative abundance of extracted m/e = 18, 12, and 44 ions, representing H2O, CO, and CO2 byproducts released during the heating process.
summary: Mass spectrometry data tracks the off-gassing behavior of 4340 steel during heating. Binder decomposition in as-printed samples generates significant H2O, CO, and CO2. Following binder removal, the detection of an H2O peak confirms the occurrence of deoxidation through H2-based redox reactions at temperatures exceeding 500 °C.

caption: TEM micrograph of the HIP-HT sample cyclically loaded at 0.50% strain amplitude for 689 cycles, viewed along the [011] zone axis.
summary: This TEM image of the HIP-HT sample at 0.50% strain amplitude demonstrates a tangled dislocation configuration. Compared to the HT sample, the HIP-HT variant exhibits significantly higher dislocation density, suggesting more pronounced dislocation interactions and a distinct response to cyclic loading at high strain amplitudes within the GH3536 superalloy.

caption: Laser confocal micrograph of the as-cast 2Y specimen showing the columnar-dendritic α-Al matrix and interdendritic eutectic structure.
summary: This laser confocal micrograph of the as-cast 2Y specimen illustrates the columnar-dendritic α-Al matrix and interdendritic eutectic structure. The observed columnar microstructure is consistent with heterogeneous nucleation on the mold walls. Overall, the microstructural analysis confirms that the 2Y specimen is quite similar to the 1Y specimen in its cast state.

caption: Detailed STEM view of the LCF-tested specimen showing PSBs shearing the matrix and precipitates, alongside the presence of deformation nanotwins.
summary: Detailed STEM imaging reveals that Persistent Slip Bands shear both the matrix and the precipitates within the microstructure. The presence of deformation nanotwins is also observed. Notably, LCF testing at 650 °C does not induce coarsening of the precipitates, maintaining the structural integrity of the material compared to initial states.

caption: Fracture toughness of printed WC-Co coupons, recorded at 11.7 MPa.m1/2, shown in relation to volumetric energy density.
summary: Fracture toughness values for the printed WC-Co coupons are plotted against volumetric energy density. The measured toughness of 11.7 MPa.m1/2 meets the necessary performance criteria for machining titanium alloys, ensuring the tool can withstand the required mechanical stresses during operation.

caption: Spider plot illustrating statistical error metrics for compressive strength predictions.
summary: This spider plot evaluates the predictive performance of developed models regarding compressive strength. It visualizes multiple statistical error metrics, including mean squared error, R-squared, root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and mean absolute error, providing a comprehensive comparison of model accuracy across these specific quantitative performance indicators.
