caption: Baseline experimental configuration featuring a specimen immersed in a solution devoid of elemental sulfur.
summary: This schematic illustrates the baseline experimental condition where the specimen is placed in a solution containing no elemental sulfur. It serves as the control setup for comparing the effects of varying sulfur exposure levels on the specimen during the experimental process described in the study.

caption: Summary of electrochemical corrosion parameters, including corrosion potentials and current densities, derived from Tafel extrapolation of the polarization curves.
summary: This table presents the key electrochemical corrosion parameters obtained through Tafel extrapolation analysis of the polarization curves. By determining the corrosion potentials and corrosion current densities, the data allows for a precise evaluation of the electrochemical corrosion behavior and overall stability of the MoldJet 316L samples.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram illustrating the influence of Si content on phase stability within the selected alloy system.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram, generated via Thermo-Calc, maps phase stability as a function of Si concentration. It highlights the presence of FCC and L12 phases as the primary constituents within the temperature regime of approximately 800 °C for Si concentrations ranging between 6 and 7 at%.

caption: S-N data plot utilizing the TCD-based method with a stress averaging distance of a = 0.1 mm, including a FAT 160 MPa m = 3 reference line.
summary: This S-N data plot demonstrates the application of the TCD-based fatigue strength assessment method using a stress averaging distance of 0.1 mm. The inclusion of a FAT 160 MPa m = 3 reference line indicates that this specific parameter provides good agreement with the experimental fatigue results for the tested specimens.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of carbide precipitation within the inter-dendrite zones of an as-deposited specimen processed at a laser power of 1100 W.
summary: This scanning electron micrograph displays the carbide precipitation morphology observed in the middle region of a thin-wall specimen. The material was prepared using a laser power of 1100 W, revealing the specific distribution of carbides within the inter-dendrite zones characteristic of the as-deposited microstructure under these processing conditions.

caption: Predicted Al composition profiles across the bi-metallic interface after 10, 100, and 1,000 minutes of isothermal heat treatment at 525 °C.
summary: Aluminum composition profiles across the interface are shown for 10, 100, and 1,000 minutes of heat treatment at 525 °C. These profiles demonstrate the concentration gradients of Al as it participates in the formation of intermetallic phases, providing insight into the mass transport occurring within the bi-metallic joint.

caption: Weak-beam dark-field micrograph of NiFe irradiated to 0.4 dpa at 773 K, illustrating the progression of defect density and size.
summary: Irradiation of NiFe to 0.4 dpa at 773 K results in a visible increase in defect density compared to the 0.1 dpa state. This weak-beam dark-field micrograph, obtained with g = (200), demonstrates the progressive evolution of the defect population as the ion dose increases within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Z-axis definition established by calculating the best-fit cylinder from points on the external turned surface.
summary: Defining the Z-coordinate axis is the first step of the CMS measurement process. This is achieved by creating an axis from the best-fit cylinder, which is calculated using data points collected from the cylinder’s external turned region, providing a stable reference frame for all subsequent geometric measurements of the part.

caption: Hardness distribution profile across the graded cemented carbide, correlating mechanical properties with the radial material composition.
summary: This hardness distribution map correlates the mechanical performance of the cemented carbide with its radial composition. By visualizing the hardness values across the graded structure, the figure demonstrates the functional outcome of the material design, showing how the varying Cobalt content directly influences the mechanical properties of the printed component.

caption: Calculated trajectories of particle motion within the granulation chamber, demonstrating the falling regularity of the particles.
summary: Particle motion trajectories within the granulation chamber are obtained by solving governing equations using finite difference methods. This panel illustrates the falling regularity of the particles, showing how individual particles navigate the flow field and pressure environment during the spheroidization process to achieve the desired powder morphology.

caption: Nitrosamine concentrations measured from carbon- and nitrogen-doped TiO2 photocatalysts in chloraminated water (5 mg Cl2 L-1) without the addition of DMA.
summary: This bar chart presents the concentrations of four nitrosamines measured in chloraminated water without DMA. The data indicates that the concentrations of these nitrosamines range from 10.4 to 63.6 ng L-1 under these specific experimental conditions, reflecting the impact of the chloraminated environment on the leaching behavior of the doped TiO2 catalysts.

caption: High-speed photographic sequence showing the third stage of droplet transfer in AWF-CMT-DED mode with an auxiliary wire feed speed of 50 cm/min.
summary: This high-speed image depicts the third stage of droplet transfer during AWF-CMT-DED processing. Maintaining an auxiliary wire feed speed of 50 cm/min, the auxiliary wire tip preserves its contact with the molten pool head, highlighting the stability of the transfer mechanism throughout the deposition process under these specific parameters.

caption: As-received IN100 alloy microstructure showing coarse grains exceeding 200 µm without pre-existing cold working.
summary: The as-received IN100 sample displays a microstructure characterized by coarse grains larger than 200 µm. EBSD analysis confirms that this state is devoid of any pre-existing cold working, providing a baseline for comparing the structural changes induced by subsequent deep cold rolling (DCR) processes in the rolled samples.

caption: T6 heat-treated ACMZ alloy specimen deformed in the horizontal orientation.
summary: Presented is the T6 heat-treated ACMZ alloy specimen after undergoing dynamic impact testing in the horizontal orientation. This orientation is perpendicular to the columnar grain growth direction. The panel serves as part of a quantitative statistical dataset evaluating the anisotropic deformation behavior of ACMZ alloy specimens under various impact rates.

caption: Detailed SEM micrograph and associated EDS elemental maps revealing the presence of Cr-Mn oxides within the Cantor HEA base material.
summary: This panel focuses on the Cantor HEA base material, showcasing the distribution of Cr-Mn oxides. The EDS maps confirm the chemical composition of these oxide features, which are critical for understanding the oxidation behavior and phase stability of the CoCrFeMnNi alloy under the conditions experienced during the welding process.

caption: Power factor of Bi2-xNixSe3 samples plotted against temperature, demonstrating an overall enhancement in performance across the measured range.
summary: The power factor for the Bi2-xNixSe3 samples is presented as a function of temperature. Despite the observed reduction in the Seebeck coefficient, the data indicates an overall enhancement in the power factor, reflecting the combined effects of the modified electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficient on the thermoelectric performance of the material.

caption: Short-circuit charge transfer versus time curves for multi-branch HETENG configurations.
summary: This panel presents the short-circuit charge transfer over time for multi-branch HETENGs. The data provides a clear visualization of the cumulative charge generated by the multi-branch system, confirming the effectiveness of the design in enhancing total charge output through the integration of multiple functional branches.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the electrode in 0.1 M NaOH solution recorded over 10, 20, 30, and 40 consecutive cycles at a scan rate of 20 mV s-1.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammograms in 0.1 M NaOH across 40 cycles. During the positive scan, a wide oxidation peak appears with a maximum near 0.47 V, indicating the electrochemical behavior of the material prior to the oxygen evolution reaction under these specific alkaline conditions.

caption: Longitudinal xz cross-sectional views comparing laser grain angles across two distinct experimental groups with varying laser power levels.
summary: Longitudinal cross-sectional views compare laser grain angles for two experimental groups subjected to different laser powers. The observations demonstrate that laser power has a negligible influence on changing the laser grain angle, suggesting that scanning speed is a more dominant factor in controlling the resulting microstructure and grain orientation.

caption: Low-frequency simulation of fatigue crack propagation representing high cycle fatigue conditions, plotting the rate of area increase (dArea/dN) against the cyclic stress intensity factor range (ΔK).
summary: This panel illustrates a low-frequency simulation model designed to analyze fatigue crack propagation under high cycle fatigue conditions. The plot correlates the rate of crack area growth, denoted as dArea/dN, with the cyclic stress intensity factor range, ΔK, providing a quantitative assessment of crack behavior during standard cyclic loading cycles.

caption: Inter-bead strength of 3D printed PC composites as a function of glass fibre content (0, 2.5, 5, and 10 wt%) for extrusion multipliers of 1 and 1.1, printed in an XY [90°] orientation.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical inter-bead strength of polycarbonate composites reinforced with varying glass fibre concentrations. The data compares performance across different extrusion multipliers of 1 and 1.1 for samples printed in an XY [90°] orientation, providing a comprehensive overview of how fibre content influences the structural integrity of the printed beads.

caption: Contour map showing the sCO2 exit temperature across a range of MS and sCO2 inlet temperatures at constant mass flow rates.
summary: The sCO2 exit temperature is visualized through a contour plot against varying MS and sCO2 inlet temperatures. Observations reveal that the sCO2 exit temperature is significantly more sensitive to changes in the MS inlet temperature than to variations in the sCO2 inlet temperature under the specified baseline mass flow conditions.

caption: UV-vis absorption spectra of the TCP film measured across varying ratios of acetone, illustrating the influence of concentration on optical absorption.
summary: The UV-vis absorption spectra demonstrate how varying ratios of acetone affect the TCP film. The red shifting of the absorption signal when acetone binds with 2D materials, particularly FeCr2O4, is attributed to interactions between acetone molecules and the material surface, reflecting changes in the electronic structure and local environment.

caption: Comparative photoluminescence spectra of BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C and reference SL-InAs/GaAsSb-C samples measured at 77 K under 100 mW excitation.
summary: Comparative photoluminescence spectra for the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C and the single-layer SL-InAs/GaAsSb-C reference samples are displayed at 77 K under 100 mW excitation. The reference sample exhibits a ground state to excited state splitting of approximately 72 meV, which supports the interpretation of the bilayer sample's distinct emission characteristics.

caption: FTIR spectrum of ZnO nanoparticles recorded at room temperature within the 500–4000 cm-1 range to identify functional groups and chemical bonds.
summary: The sample’s functional groups and bonds were identified using FTIR spectroscopy with the range of 500–4000 cm-1 at room temperature. This spectrum allows for the identification of chemical signatures present on the surface of the ZnO nanoparticles, providing essential information regarding the chemical composition and surface bonding environment.

caption: COF-time curve for the C1 textured sample, highlighting the friction behavior under oil lubrication.
summary: The COF-time curve for the C1 textured sample is shown, revealing its friction response during the wear test. Similar to other textured samples, the C1 texture facilitates a shortened running-in period under oil-lubricated conditions, demonstrating the efficacy of this specific energy density in modifying tribological performance.

caption: Mean particle length of γ″ precipitates in Inconel 625 as a function of aging temperature following a 20 h nucleation treatment at 650 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the simulated evolution of mean γ″ particle length in Inconel 625. Following a 20 h nucleation treatment at 650 °C, the data shows that increasing the aging temperature accelerates the growth and coarsening of the γ″ precipitates, reflecting the kinetics of the precipitation process under varying thermal conditions.

caption: Chessboard scan-strategy pattern utilized in the PBF-LB/M process, featuring scanning directions (X', Y') oriented at a 45° offset relative to the rectangular coupon edges (X, Y).
summary: This schematic illustrates the chessboard scan strategy employed during the laser powder bed fusion process. By orienting the scanning directions at a 45-degree offset to the edges of the rectangular test coupons, this specific pattern is designed to minimize the accumulation of residual stresses within the consolidated material.

caption: 3D topography of the wear track on the cold-sprayed CoCrFeNiMo0.5 HEA deposit.
summary: This 3D topography visualization depicts the wear track of the Mo0.5 doped CoCrFeNi HEA deposit. The reduced wear volume observed here is attributed to the higher hardness of the material, confirming that increasing the Mo ratio effectively improves the wear resistance of the cold-sprayed CoCrFeNiMo x HEA deposits.

caption: ANOVA analysis of T Peak values for varying TPU percentages.
summary: Statistical ANOVA analysis of T Peak values demonstrates the significance of TPU content on thermal degradation characteristics. With a calculated P-value of less than 0.05, the results indicate that the addition of TPU is statistically significant in reducing the T Peak temperature observed during the TGA thermal analysis process.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of CGs showing a high density of dispersed, uneven, sub-micron massive secondary phases marked by red arrows.
summary: Within the CGs, a large number of dispersed and uneven massive secondary phases are visible. These features, marked with red arrows, exhibit sub-micron dimensions. This HAADF-STEM image correlates with backscattered electron observations, highlighting the distinct morphology of secondary phases found in the coarse grain regions of the alloy.

caption: Spectrum of carbon migration enthalpy in martensitic Fe-25Ni-2C under longitudinal excitation at 300 K, demonstrating the influence of 25 at.% Ni alloying on the migration energy distribution extracted from AKMC simulations.
summary: The spectrum of carbon migration enthalpy for Fe-25Ni-2C under longitudinal excitation is presented. Extracted from AKMC simulations, this data illustrates how the addition of 25 at.% Ni significantly alters the migration enthalpy landscape compared to binary iron-carbon martensite, reflecting complex interactions between carbon atoms and the nickel-alloyed lattice.

caption: Surface profile map of an air-blast (AR) peened specimen, illustrating the topography used for calculating the Sa surface roughness value.
summary: This surface profile map displays the topography of an air-blast peened specimen. The visualization serves as a primary data source for calculating the Sa surface roughness parameter. By mapping the surface features, this profilometer data provides a quantitative representation of the specimen's texture resulting from the peening process.

caption: Time-of-flight (ToF) energy-converted spectra illustrating the recoil yield of H atoms implanted into tungsten as a function of annealing temperature, measured using 200 keV 22Ne projectiles at a 50° scattering angle.
summary: This plot displays ToF energy-converted spectra of recoiled H atoms from a tungsten substrate. The data demonstrate the evolution of hydrogen recoil yield across various annealing temperatures. Results indicate that hydrogen trapped in the bulk diffuses out at lower temperatures compared to hydrogen trapped at the surface of the tungsten material.

caption: Calculated density of states for the pristine TiNi3/C interface.
summary: This panel displays the density of states for the pristine TiNi3/C interface. The electronic structure and bonding properties of this interface are analyzed to understand the baseline characteristics of the system, providing a reference point for evaluating the impact of various dopants on the material's electronic properties.

caption: Nucleation of MC-carbides, highlighted in red, within the interdendritic liquid regions at a simulation time of 1.6 ms.
summary: At a simulation time of 1.6 ms, this panel highlights the nucleation of MC-carbides within the melt. These carbides, represented in red, appear within the interdendritic liquid channels. This specific cutout demonstrates the early precipitation of secondary phases during the solidification process of the LP state microstructure.

caption: STEM ADF micrograph of the fcc A1 phase in the 1000HT sample compressed at 600 °C, showing a high density of dislocation forests.
summary: This STEM ADF micrograph displays the fcc A1 phase of the 1000HT sample after 32% compression at 600 °C. The image reveals a high dislocation density, indicating that the fcc A1 phase is undergoing severe plastic deformation under these specific testing conditions.

caption: XPS survey spectrum of the Al65Zr20Fe15 ingot surface following electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl solution at 25 °C after a 1 h EOCP duration.
summary: This XPS survey spectrum characterizes the surface composition of the Al65Zr20Fe15 alloy ingot. The measurement was conducted after the specimen underwent electrochemical corrosion testing in a 3.5% NaCl solution at 25 °C, following a 1 h open circuit potential (EOCP) duration to assess surface state and chemical composition.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel across different insolation conditions, illustrating the relationship between output power and voltage as derived from the PEC2 model.
summary: Representing the P-V characteristics of the KC200GT solar panel, this panel highlights the power output behavior under various insolation levels. The data, obtained through the PEC2 model, is compared against measured values to confirm the model's reliability in predicting power generation performance across a range of operational irradiance conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of reinforcement layers showing a distinct inflection point between -0.9 V and -1.1 V.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry curves for the reinforcement layers are presented, highlighting a clear inflection point occurring within the potential range of -0.9 V to -1.1 V. This electrochemical data characterizes the deposition behavior of the reinforcement layers prepared by CAJED under varying composite solution conditions.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from iR-free cell voltage curves for uncoated and gold-coated PTLs in PEMWE cells.
summary: Tafel slope analysis is presented for PEMWE cells utilizing both uncoated and gold-coated PTLs. The gold-coated samples exhibit a lower Tafel slope compared to the uncoated PTLs, indicating improved electrochemical kinetics and reduced activation overpotential for the oxygen evolution reaction within the cell configuration.

caption: Comparative receiver operating characteristic curves showing the performance improvement achieved by utilizing multi-channel signals versus single-channel signals, with AUC values calculated from five experimental runs.
summary: This panel highlights the performance gain achieved by fusing multi-channel signals compared to using single-channel inputs. By presenting ROC curves and AUC values averaged over five experimental runs, the figure confirms that multi-channel signal integration significantly enhances the model's diagnostic accuracy and overall classification capability on the testing set.

caption: Ternary compositional diagram illustrating the volume percentage distribution of ASH-G composite constituents.
summary: This ternary diagram provides a visual representation of the compositional selections for ASH-G composites, expressed in volume percentages. As referenced in the study, this plot serves as a primary guide for the specific material formulations utilized in the experimental investigations, detailing the relative proportions of the constituent phases within the composite system.

caption: Transmittance measurements of acellular bioprinted structures compared to native human cornea and PBS control across the visible light spectrum.
summary: Transmittance of the multi-material bioprinted structures ranges from 74.6% to 87.3% throughout the visible light wavelength range. This quantitative analysis demonstrates that the bioprinted constructs maintain optical properties comparable to native human cornea and PBS, confirming their suitability for corneal tissue engineering applications.

caption: TEM micrograph of Inconel 625 processed via bottom cooling, demonstrating cross-slip mechanisms.
summary: TEM analysis of the CMT Inconel 625 component under bottom cooling conditions shows evidence of cross-slip. This mechanism is one of the various structural features that emerge under bottom cooling, indicating enhanced dislocation activity and reflecting the complex microstructural changes induced by the specific cooling condition applied to the sample.

caption: Contour map illustrating the spatial distribution of Fe concentration (atoms per nm3) within the xy-plane at the z-value marked in panel (a) for the TiFe-based alloy series.
summary: This contour map displays the iron concentration distribution within the xy-plane at the same z-value used for the titanium analysis. It allows for the direct comparison of Fe spatial variations across the TiFe-based alloy series, providing insight into the local atomic arrangement and compositional features within the APT reconstruction.

caption: Smoothed STL file of a freeform beam geometry incorporating structural distortion.
summary: This panel presents a smoothed STL file of a freeform beam geometry that incorporates structural distortion. The visualization highlights the impact of distortion on the freeform design, allowing for a comparative analysis against the undistorted baseline model to understand how geometric deviations manifest in the final beam structure.

caption: Temporal evolution of current density at a constant 1.2 V for the STF SOC, illustrating the degradation profile over 165 hours of operation.
summary: The durability experiment for the STF SOC shows a significant performance decay over 165 hours of operation. The current density drops by 30%, decreasing from an initial value of -250 mA/cm2 to -175 mA/cm2, highlighting the limited stability of the STF material under the tested co-electrolysis conditions.

caption: Galvanostatic step test of Zn nanowires synthesized via varying electrochemical bath compositions, conducted in 30% w/w KOH aqueous solution at room temperature.
summary: This galvanostatic step test evaluates the electrochemical performance of Zn nanowires in 30% w/w KOH. The data, represented as average overpotential per step, reveals a rapid performance degradation. This decline is attributed to the dissolution of the Zn nanowires, which significantly reduces the available electrochemically active surface area during testing.

caption: Statistical distribution of pitting potentials for the investigated Ni-Cr-Fe-Cu alloys, presented as a box and whisker plot with individual experimental data points overlaid.
summary: Statistical analysis of pitting potentials for the Ni-13Cr-10Fe-xCu alloy series is visualized through a box and whisker plot with overlaid data points. This representation highlights the trend that the pitting potential increases with higher copper content, providing a clear comparison of the corrosion resistance across the different alloy compositions.

caption: SKPFM surface potential map of the LPBF dual-phase NiTi sample, where martensitic phases are identified as dark regions indicating lower surface potential.
summary: The SKPFM surface potential mapping provides a visual representation of the electrical potential distribution across the dual-phase NiTi sample. Martensitic phases are distinctly recognized as dark regions, which correspond to areas of lower surface potential, highlighting the heterogeneous electrical nature of the material's microstructure.

caption: Bubble plots illustrating the osteogenic differentiation trends of BMSCs under FAK-MAPK pathway inhibition.
summary: Bubble plots demonstrate the osteogenic differentiation trends of BMSCs when the FAK-MAPK pathway is inhibited. These findings suggest that osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs cultured in stiff hydrogels is effectively blocked upon inhibiting p38 and ERK, confirming the dominant role of the FAK-MAPK pathway in mediating this differentiation process.

caption: Progression of the non-discreteness measure and maximum overfilling constraints, showing a consistent decrease from the initial uniform design toward convergence.
summary: The plot illustrates the convergence behavior of the non-discreteness measure and maximum overfilling constraints. Starting from an initial uniform design, the non-discreteness measure consistently decreases throughout the optimization process, eventually converging to near zero, which confirms the robustness of the CAMP-based framework with respect to the CAMP filter.

caption: Neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain along the z-direction for the cold-machined condition.
summary: Neutron diffraction data for the cold-machined condition illustrates the residual elastic strain distribution along the z-direction. Similar to the hot-machined part, this measurement highlights the development of high tensile strains near the wall edges and spike-like tensile features along the build direction, alongside compressive strains in the center.

caption: 2D synchrotron diffraction patterns for the HZ30 alloy captured during in-situ temperature cycling.
summary: 2D synchrotron diffraction patterns for the HZ30 alloy are presented to visualize the structural state of the material during in-situ temperature cycling. These patterns provide a comprehensive view of the diffraction rings, which are essential for identifying the phase changes occurring within the HZ30 alloy during the transformation process.

caption: Fracture characteristics of the β-crystallite structure evaluated across varying printing temperatures.
summary: The effect of printing temperature on the fracture characteristics of the β-crystallite structure is shown. The optimal printing parameters for the β-crystallite, ensuring peak ultimate stress and tensile strain, are determined to be a pressure of 590 MPa, a speed of 300 mm/min, and a temperature of 100 °C.

caption: COHP analysis for C-Ni and C-Re atomic pairs in Ni grain boundaries, illustrating the alignment of Fermi levels with X-Ni antibonding states.
summary: Carbon-segregated and C-Re co-segregated Ni grain boundaries are analyzed via COHP curves. The Fermi level falls into the noticeable C-Ni antibonding region, defined by -COHP values below zero. This indicates that the occupied antibonding states exist in this energy range, consistent with the overall electronic structure of the segregated boundary.

caption: Feasible set of overshoot-cure duration for a 40 mm glass/epoxy prepreg laminate, comparing conventional curing methods with layer-by-layer (LbL) processing, highlighting the optimized conventional process point A.
summary: This diagram defines the feasible processing window for a 40 mm glass/epoxy prepreg, contrasting conventional curing with LbL techniques. Point A represents the optimized conventional process design with the lowest feasible overshoot. These results validate the cure simulation and confirm the reported process efficiency advantages of the LbL approach.

caption: Temperature dependence of the exchange bias for the top and bottom FM-layers in NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with LNiPy.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent exchange bias behavior for top and bottom ferromagnetic layers in NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with LNiPy. The data shows how thermal variations influence the exchange bias, with the AFM-layer thickness contributing to a more convex curve shape as the temperature changes across the measured range.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus experimental maximum force values.
summary: This parity plot shows the agreement between predicted and experimental maximum force values. The data points exhibit close alignment about the identity line, which indicates that the model achieves satisfactory descriptive power for predicting maximum force performance within the context of the explored design space.

caption: Energy consumption of 3D printed specimens plotted against extrusion parameters, comparing printing temperatures of 40 °C (blue squares) and 80 °C (red triangles).
summary: Energy consumption for 3D printed specimens is displayed as a function of extrusion parameters. The data shows a clear increase in energy consumption at higher extrusion temperatures. Specimens printed at 80 °C, represented by red triangles, are compared against those printed at 40 °C, indicated by blue squares, with error bars reflecting triplicate measurements.

caption: Histogram displaying the distribution of maximum transconductance values, normalized by the geometric factor d*W/L for the various deposition techniques.
summary: This histogram presents the maximum transconductance values (gm,max) for different device sets, normalized by the film thickness (d) and channel dimensions (width W and length L). This normalization accounts for geometric variations, allowing for a direct comparison of the intrinsic electronic performance across the different deposition techniques analyzed in the study.

caption: Relative frequency distribution of the local misorientation angle of the γ phase in the top region of the UHFP-treated TiAl-4822 sample.
summary: The relative frequency plot for the UHFP-treated sample illustrates the distribution of local misorientation angles. The data confirms that the local orientation difference between grains is smaller under this condition, which correlates with the observed decrease in residual stress and improved microstructural uniformity in the top region.

caption: Two-cycle heating program utilized to isolate and quantify the thermal expansion contributions originating from the sample and the tooling assembly.
summary: A two-cycle heating program is depicted to determine the thermal expansion contribution from both the sample and the tools. This calibration step is essential for isolating the true densification displacement from the total ram displacement data, ensuring accurate analysis of the material's behavior during the high-temperature SPS processing.

caption: Ni 2p XPS spectrum of the PTHE PdNi/Ni RDE catalyst, showing the absence of metallic Ni(0) due to electrochemical oxidation.
summary: The Ni 2p spectrum for the PTHE catalyst shows no detectable Ni(0) signal. This absence indicates that the PTHE process exerts a strong oxidative effect on the nickel component, which is distinct from the surface oxidation caused merely by exposure to air during ex-situ handling.

caption: Secondary electron SEM micrograph of high Fe Inconel 625 after 0.5 h of heat treatment at 870 °C, highlighting early-stage MN nitride precipitation.
summary: This secondary electron SEM micrograph displays the microstructure of high Fe Inconel 625 after 0.5 h of heat treatment at 870 °C. MN nitrides, indicated by arrows, are identified as the primary precipitates forming during these early stages of heat treatment due to reduced elemental segregation from HIP processing.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the BM–HP sample showing the presence of nanoscale twins.
summary: This TEM image displays the microstructure of the BM–HP sample, specifically highlighting the presence of nanoscale twins. The distribution of these twins is noted to vary across different regions of the sample, providing evidence of the microstructural characteristics resulting from the ball-milling and hot-pressing processing conditions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarisation curve of the Invar wire feedstock, showing an Ecorr of -0.38 V vs SCE and an Icorr of approximately 2.15 ± 0.62 × 10^-6 A/cm.
summary: The potentiodynamic polarisation curve for the Invar wire feedstock is displayed, characterizing its electrochemical corrosion resistance. Key quantitative findings include an Ecorr value of -0.38 V vs SCE and an Icorr of 2.15 ± 0.62 × 10^-6 A/cm, providing essential baseline data for the feedstock material's electrochemical performance.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve for the GBDT model evaluated on the withheld test dataset, corresponding to a defect diameter of 200 µm.
summary: Representing the detection performance for a 200 µm defect diameter, this ROC curve demonstrates the GBDT model's predictive capability on the withheld test dataset. The results are derived from models trained on the combined builds dataset, providing a baseline for evaluating classification performance at this specific porosity threshold.

caption: Root mean square error (RMSE) of precipitate fraction predictions plotted against the fraction of data retained after filtering out predictions with the highest uncertainty, showing the solid experimental curve alongside theoretical upper and lower bounds.
summary: This plot demonstrates the impact of uncertainty-based filtering on model performance for precipitate fraction predictions. The solid curve shows the RMSE decreasing as high-uncertainty predictions are removed, with distinct steps occurring when significant outliers are filtered out. Theoretical upper and lower bounds provide a reference for the expected error behavior during this process.

caption: UV photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) spectra showing the electron density distribution at the Fermi level for g-C3N4 and modified catalysts.
summary: UPS analysis reveals that modified catalysts exhibit a significant electron density distribution at the Fermi level compared to pristine g-C3N4. This indicates that the introduction of hydroxyacetic acid and phytic acid into the g-C3N4 framework significantly increases the charge density, facilitating improved electronic properties for photocatalytic applications.

caption: YZ-section contour plot representing the net precipitation time calculated by subtracting the dissolution zone duration from the total time spent in the precipitation temperature range.
summary: This YZ-section contour plot illustrates the net precipitation time derived from the precipitation potential model. By assuming the dissolution rate equals the precipitation rate, the time spent in the dissolution temperature range is subtracted from the total time in the precipitation zone, providing a refined estimate of precipitate formation duration.

caption: Transverse membrane residual stress distribution for the third SHS specimen.
summary: Transverse membrane residual stress distribution for the third SHS specimen is presented. The data confirms that the upper half of the tube experiences maximum tensile membrane stresses, a trend attributed to the considerable height of the DED-Arc specimens, which consistently dictates the membrane stress profile across all tested tubes.

caption: Correlation between percentage elongation and maximum valley depth (Rv) for various post-processed and as-built samples.
summary: This graph correlates percentage elongation with the Rv roughness parameter. The results follow a trend where elongation decreases as roughness increases, consistent with other line roughness parameters. Distinct threshold regimes are observed, highlighting the influence of surface morphology on the ductile behavior of the samples under different processing conditions.

caption: Heteronuclear Single Quantum Coherence (HSQC) NMR spectra comparing PS (green) and hydrogenated PS (red) synthesized using Ni-Mo catalysts.
summary: This HSQC NMR spectrum provides evidence for the successful hydrogenation of carbonyl-containing molecules. By comparing the green PS signal with the red hydrogenated PS signal, the figure confirms the chemical transformation. The 1H-13C NMR data serves as a definitive analytical tool for verifying the structural changes occurring during the catalytic hydrogenation process.

caption: True stress-strain curves derived from the tensile testing of as-built and tempered RT Q&P steel, illustrating the evolution of flow stress across different processing conditions.
summary: These true stress-strain curves represent the tensile behavior of as-built and tempered RT Q&P steel. The data indicates that higher tempering temperatures result in a lower work-hardening rate, which influences the ultimate tensile strength achieved by the material during the deformation process.

caption: Cr elemental distribution map highlighting depletion zones near the crack tip and grain boundaries.
summary: This Cr elemental map illustrates the distribution of chromium in the Ni33Cr1Fe alloy. The analysis shows that chromium content decreases from approximately 38% to 30% near the crack tip and grain boundaries, where Cr7C3 carbides precipitate, effectively inducing a pronounced Cr-depleted zone in the surrounding metallic matrix.

caption: Radar diagram comparing the performance metrics of three distinct biphasic structures, including modulus, strength at 0.1% strain, post-impact thickness, thermal conductivity, and backside temperature after 1000 seconds of heating.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of three biphasic structures by evaluating their mechanical and thermal properties. Key performance indicators displayed include modulus, strength at 0.1% strain, residual thickness after impact, thermal conductivity, and backside temperature after 1000 seconds of heating, offering an intuitive visualization of their overall material efficiency.

caption: Wiener filtered HAADF-STEM image of the 205B-T6 sample, highlighting the atomic structure perpendicular to the Ω disk direction.
summary: Applying a Wiener filter to the HAADF-STEM data allows for enhanced elemental analysis of the structure perpendicular to the Ω disk. This processing reveals that Ag atoms preferentially segregate at the Ω phase/matrix interface, creating a solute drag layer that effectively inhibits Cu and Al atom migration and coarsening.

caption: Tanδ temperature-dependent profiles for compression moulded PA specimens under dried and humidified (30%RH, 50%RH, 80%RH) environments.
summary: Compression moulded PA samples are characterized here through DMTA analysis, showing the evolution of tanδ across a temperature range. The curves demonstrate the impact of varying humidity levels—specifically 30%RH, 50%RH, and 80%RH—on the material's damping characteristics compared to the baseline performance observed in the dried state.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the initial copper specimen showing the crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The inverse pole figure map reveals the crystallographic orientation of the initial copper specimen. Analysis of this microstructure indicates that the material possesses elongated grains, which is a characteristic feature of metallic structures following a rolling process. This orientation map provides essential context regarding the initial state of the copper.

caption: Size-dependent property distribution curves for Al2O3 particles, showing the relationship between equivalent particle diameter and both hydrostatic tensile strength and interfacial strength.
summary: This plot illustrates the particle-size-dependent mechanical properties assigned to the Al2O3 particles and the matrix/particle interface. A Python script calculated the equivalent diameter for 225 particles, allowing for the assignment of hydrostatic tensile and interfacial strengths based on size-dependent property curves, represented by blue and red symbolic data points.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of Haynes 214 superalloy deformed to a true strain of 0.11, revealing a high density of dislocations and narrow planar dislocation arrangements.
summary: At a true strain of 0.11, the Haynes 214 superalloy microstructure exhibits highly dense dislocations and narrow planar arrangements. Grain and twin boundaries effectively impede dislocation slip and movement within the matrix, confirming that these structural features play a critical role in restricting dislocation mobility during the early stages of deformation.

caption: Measured UV wavelength pattern captured at and beyond the focal plane.
summary: The UV wavelength pattern is presented here, showing the measured intensity profile at and beyond the focal plane. This data is part of a broader set of results, including blue wavelength measurements and simulations, which collectively validate the accuracy of the optical model and the simulation methodology used.

caption: Tensile stress-strain behavior of 3D-printed PVDF, PVDF/BTO, PVDF/PLA, and PVDF/PLA/BTO composite specimens.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical performance of various 3D-printed PVDF-based tensile specimens. It compares the stress-strain response of pure PVDF against its composites with BTO and PLA. These curves provide essential data on the tensile properties and deformation characteristics of the printed materials under controlled mechanical loading conditions.

caption: EBSD phase map of PBF-LB/M-processed N-alloyed X50CrMoV15_N_mod steel, highlighting the phase composition resulting from nitrogen modification.
summary: The EBSD analysis of the PBF-LB/M-processed N-alloyed X50CrMoV15_N_mod steel illustrates the phases observed in the modified alloy. By comparing this map with the N-free variant, the influence of nitrogen on the resulting microstructure and phase stability can be clearly identified and evaluated within the context of the study.

caption: Ultraviolet absorption cross sections for H2CO (red) and NO2 (blue) plotted against wavelength.
summary: This plot displays the ultraviolet absorption cross sections for H2CO and NO2. The red curve represents the H2CO absorption profile, while the blue curve highlights the NO2 absorption features, which are specifically noted to occur between 320 nm and 360 nm within this spectral range.

caption: Amperometry response of 3D-printed Ultrafuse electrodes measured at a constant potential of 0.7 V.
summary: Amperometry results at 0.7 V demonstrate that current densities for all tested Ultrafuse electrodes are very similar, regardless of thickness. Hydrogen production is negligible across the samples, with the exception of the 3 mm electrode, which exhibits only a very small amount of hydrogen bubble formation during the test.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 2 m/min and constant travel speed.
summary: This panel displays the current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 2 m/min. Analysis of the data indicates that this specific deposition condition results in a relatively higher peak current and a lower peak duration compared to other tested parameters.

caption: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC/MS) analysis of SP 1 and CSP 1 samples, revealing the presence of oxygen-containing components including phenols, alkanols, esters, and alkoxy compounds.
summary: The GC/MS analysis identifies a diverse array of oxygen-containing components in SP 1 and CSP 1, specifically highlighting phenols, alkanols, esters, and alkoxy compounds. Quantitative assessment reveals that phenolic compounds constitute 11.0% of SP 1 and 8.6% of CSP 1, demonstrating distinct chemical compositions between the two materials.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of Cu-9Ni-6Sn alloy samples subjected to various processing conditions.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for Cu-9Ni-6Sn alloy specimens across different experimental states. The data provides structural characterization of the alloy, illustrating how varying conditions influence the crystalline phase composition and peak intensities, which are essential for understanding the material's microstructural evolution during processing.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a potential nucleation site in alloy H, showing an 8 nm depth region with Mg atoms segmented by Gaussian mixture clustering and separated via the maximum separation method.
summary: This panel displays an 8 nm deep atom probe tomography reconstruction of a potential nucleation site in alloy H. Mg atoms are visualized after processing with the maximum separation method and Gaussian mixture clustering to identify distinct atomic clusters, providing insight into the structural features of nucleation sites within the alloy.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing the dislocation structure of the SA specimen after 2 cycles of loading.
summary: Captured after 2 cycles of high-temperature loading, this bright-field TEM image reveals the early-stage dislocation structure in the SA LPBF HX specimen. The image provides insight into the initial microstructural changes as the material begins to undergo cyclic hardening through the development of dislocation networks.

caption: Faradaic efficiency and CO production rates for SOECs tested at 850 °C under current densities of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 A·cm⁻².
summary: This panel illustrates the Faradaic efficiency and CO production rates for SOECs at 850 °C. Short-term galvanostatic testing was conducted at 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 A·cm⁻². Instances of Faradaic efficiency exceeding 100% are noted, which likely stem from errors introduced during GC measurements of the cathode exhaust gas.

caption: Péclet number (Pe) plotted against normalized enthalpy (NE) for 23 distinct laser scan conditions, showing values on the order of 10 with minimal sensitivity to energy input variations.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the Péclet number as a function of normalized enthalpy across 23 scan conditions. The data reveals that Péclet numbers remain consistently on the order of 10, demonstrating a weak dependence on normalized enthalpy, which suggests that thermocapillary flow effects are relatively stable across these specific processing parameters.

caption: Molten pool width plotted against laser power ranging from 20 W to 80 W at a constant scanning velocity of 0.2 m/s, comparing experimental measurements with thermal model predictions.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between laser power and molten pool width at a fixed scanning velocity of 0.2 m/s. The thermal model demonstrates high accuracy at 20 W, while showing systematic underestimation at higher powers, such as 40 W, yet maintains an overall prediction error within 11% across the range.

caption: Polar distribution of parameter ω for the as-received superalloy, showing maximum values along the <011> orientation.
summary: This polar map illustrates the distribution of parameter ω for the as-received superalloy. The data shows that the PR value peaks along the <011> orientation. Notably, the length interval where high PR values gather is significantly smaller than that observed for parameter l, highlighting distinct directional characteristics of the precipitate morphology.

caption: Small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) intensity spectrum plotted against the scattering vector Q for a Ni-20Cr-0.45Y2O3 specimen fabricated via laser powder bed fusion at 140 W and 1.2 m/s.
summary: This SANS spectrum, collected from a Ni-20Cr-0.45Y2O3 specimen printed at 140 W and 1.2 m/s, utilizes a large interaction volume to resolve dispersoids. The spectrum within the Q-range of 0.02–0.6 nm-1 indicates the presence of a nanoscale second phase with diameters ranging between 7 and 100 nm.

caption: Calculated integral enthalpies of mixing for the Yb-Ni liquid system plotted as a function of composition across various temperature conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated integral enthalpies of mixing for the Yb-Ni liquid system at multiple temperatures. The data provides a thermodynamic representation of the mixing behavior within the liquid phase, demonstrating how enthalpy varies with composition and temperature, which is essential for understanding the energetic stability of the Yb-Ni alloy.

caption: Arrhenius-type correlation graph showing the relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of plastic stress and the inverse of temperature, ln ( sinh ( α 1 σ p ) ) versus 1 / T.
summary: Representing the temperature dependence of the flow stress, this Arrhenius plot correlates the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the plastic stress with the inverse of the absolute temperature. It is essential for determining the activation energy associated with the deformation of the β-phase in Ti6Al4V.

caption: View of the resin bath component used in the additive manufacturing process.
summary: This photograph displays the resin bath utilized in the DLP 3D printing setup. The bath contains the photopolymer resin mixture, which is essential for the layer-by-layer solidification process. This component is central to the fabrication of the graphene-reinforced samples, ensuring proper material distribution during the printing phase.

caption: Three-dimensional macroscopic morphology of sample 3 obtained through XCT analysis.
summary: Sample 3 is examined using XCT to reconstruct its 3D macroscopic morphology. This visualization provides insight into the structural configuration of the sample, allowing for a comparative assessment of the morphological features observed in the SLM-Al and SLM-SUS316L interface regions within the experimental framework.

caption: Detailed schematic image of the mechanical fixture utilized for conducting the shear strength test on brazed joints.
summary: This schematic image depicts the mechanical fixture used for the shear test. It serves as a technical reference for the experimental methodology employed to assess the shear strength of brazed joints, ensuring that the testing procedure is accurately represented and consistent with the mechanical evaluation requirements described in the study.

caption: Raman spectra comparing cured resin without filler, Ca-PA and Ca-PA-F fillers, and their respective composites (Ca-PA-c, Ca-PA-F-c).
summary: Raman spectra are presented for the cured resin matrix, the Ca-PA and Ca-PA-F fillers, and the resulting composites. These spectroscopic measurements allow for the identification of chemical signatures across the different material components, providing a baseline for assessing the integration of fillers within the organic resin matrix.

caption: Intensity ratio of D- and G-bands (ID/IG) extracted from Raman spectra of Cu1-xNix@C nanoparticles, plotted as a function of nickel atomic percentage.
summary: The intensity ratio of the D- and G-bands (ID/IG) from Raman spectra is plotted against the atomic percent of nickel in Cu1-xNix@C nanoparticles. This ratio serves as an indicator of carbon structural quality, reflecting how varying nickel content influences the defect density in the graphitic carbon shell formed during synthesis.

caption: Flexural strength of multi-material configurations with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8, highlighting performance improvements over the monolithic core.
summary: Flexural strength of multi-material composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8 is analyzed via radar plot. Enhancements exceed 100% relative to core-only samples in several cases. This data provides a consistent basis for material selection, demonstrating the significant mechanical performance improvements achieved under flexural loading in the studied configurations.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) comparison between Co@NC and NiCo@NC with 50% Ni concentration, highlighting electronic state modifications near the Fermi level.
summary: A comparison of the projected density of states (PDOS) for Co@NC and NiCo@NC with 50% Ni concentration demonstrates the enhancement of localized electronic states close to the Fermi level. This shift is attributed to the alloying effect, which significantly influences the electronic properties relevant to the catalytic performance.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarisation curves for Staballoy® AG17 in 3.5 wt% NaCl, illustrating minimal variation in OCP and corrosion potential after TPN treatment due to its high pre-existing nitrogen content.
summary: The polarization behavior of high-Mn Staballoy AG17 is shown before and after TPN treatment. Unlike the Ni-stabilized alloys, AG17 shows negligible changes in Ecorr and OCP, likely attributed to the high initial nitrogen concentration of approximately 0.5 wt% already present within the alloy matrix prior to the plasma nitriding process.

caption: Isolated Al clusters extracted from atom probe data, demonstrating that these features remain small and contain few atoms across all tested temperatures.
summary: This panel highlights identified Al clusters within the Inconel 718 samples. Analysis of the atom probe reconstructions indicates that Al clusters are consistently small and contain only a few atoms, regardless of the tensile testing temperature applied to the as-built material during the characterization process.

caption: Schematic representation of transect groups illustrating the influence of site-specific attributes on shoreline and waterline variability.
summary: This schematic illustrates the relationship between site-specific attributes and shoreline dynamics. By categorizing transect groups, the diagram highlights how local environmental factors directly influence waterline and shoreline variability. These site-specific features are critical for understanding the underlying mechanisms that shape coastal morphology and long-term shoreline evolution patterns.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of interpass temperature (IT) versus porosity, revealing a clear positive correlation between increased interpass temperature and higher porosity levels in surface pixels.
summary: This SHAP scatter plot displays a clear positive correlation between interpass temperature and porosity. The data indicates that higher interpass temperatures consistently lead to increased porosity in surface pixels, underscoring the critical role of local heating conditions in the formation of keyhole pores during the manufacturing process.

caption: Magnetic field dependence of the maximum magnetic entropy change (ΔSMmax) for the present Ni47Co5Mn40Sn8 alloy compared to representative Gd-, La-, Mn-, and Ni-Mn-based magnetocaloric materials.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic field dependence of the maximum magnetic entropy change (ΔSMmax) for the Ni47Co5Mn40Sn8 alloy. By comparing these values against established Gd-, La-, Mn-, and Ni-Mn-based magnetocaloric materials, the figure evaluates the performance of the present alloy relative to various well-studied systems under varying magnetic field conditions.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy elemental maps showing Al and Ti distribution in the Pt-aluminide coating following 100 h of isothermal exposure at 1100 °C.
summary: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy elemental maps illustrate the Al and Ti distribution within the Pt-aluminide coating after 100 h of isothermal exposure at 1100 °C. These maps help characterize the elemental composition near the surface scale, although identifying specific particle locations within the thermally grown oxide remains challenging due to the complex microstructure.

caption: Magnified view of two co-precipitated particles extracted from the bulk APT reconstruction, illustrating the detailed morphology of the γ′ and γ′′ phases.
summary: A magnified view of two co-precipitated particles is provided to detail the precipitate structure within the bulk material. This panel focuses on the interaction between γ′ and γ′′ phases, confirming that these particles are generally co-precipitated and allowing for a closer inspection of their individual morphologies and structural characteristics.

caption: Storage modulus versus temperature curves for 3D-printed thermosets modified with varying concentrations of CAMA.
summary: This panel illustrates the DMA storage modulus curves for 3D-printed thermosets modified with CAMA. The storage modulus of the original resin and CAMA-modified systems at 25 °C were determined to be 405, 361, 273, and 312 MPa, respectively, demonstrating the effect of CAMA concentration on the thermoset mechanical properties.

caption: Apparent contact angle of methanol measured across grooves as a function of extruder temperature and print speed.
summary: Methanol contact angles are displayed here, showing consistently higher values than ethanol across the tested parameters. This difference reflects the higher surface tension of methanol. The data confirms the lyophilic nature of the printed substrates, with the contact angle trends influenced by the specific extruder temperature and print speed conditions.

caption: XRD diffractogram of the HIPed TiNbCr MPE alloy, indicating an increased volume fraction of the C15 Laves phase to 0.37.
summary: Analysis of the HIPed TiNbCr MPE alloy via XRD reveals the coexistence of BCC and C15 Laves phases. Rietveld refinement using GSAS-II demonstrates that HIP processing increases the volume fraction of the Laves phase to 0.37, significantly higher than the 0.15 fraction observed in the as-cast state.

caption: Higher magnification bright-field TEM image of the NiCrMoAl splat region (area A) characterized by high solute concentration.
summary: This high-magnification bright-field TEM image captures the high solute region within the nickel-rich splat (area A) of the NiCrMoAl alloy coating. By examining this specific area, the image helps characterize the microstructural variations resulting from solute distribution during the rapid solidification process of the thermal spray coating.

caption: Compressive deformation sequence of the MF sample under X-LD, showing the development of a shear band in the middle-upper region.
summary: This panel displays the compressive deformation sequence of the MF sample under X-LD from 0% to 50% strain. Experimental observations reveal that the foam deforms by developing a distinct shear band located in the middle-upper part of the sample, highlighted by the yellow rectangle in the image.

caption: Normalized average camera image frame of the laser-material interaction zone using a triangle beam shape.
summary: This normalized average camera image frame displays the laser-material interaction zone during deposition with a triangle beam shape. The red curve delineates the melt pool boundary, and the arrow indicates the positive x-direction of deposition. The shape of the beam is clearly recognizable within the captured interaction zone.

caption: High-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph showing nearly spherical Si-rich nanoparticles dispersed within the aluminum matrix of the Base+Mn alloy.
summary: This micrograph focuses on the Si-rich nanoparticles found in the Base+Mn alloy matrix. These particles exhibit a nearly spherical morphology with an average diameter of 4.76 ± 1.07 nm and a volume fraction of 0.19%, confirming the distinct nanoparticle dispersion achieved through the addition of manganese to the alloy.

caption: Raman spectrum of LB and HB samples consolidated using PSPS, highlighting carbon evolution.
summary: Raman analysis of LB and HB samples consolidated via PSPS was conducted to check the evolution of carbon in the sintered samples. The resulting spectrum characterizes the carbon content and structural state in samples fabricated with a 0.41 mm nozzle diameter.

caption: Geometric unit cell schematics illustrating the structural configurations for HC, HC-S1, HC-S2, HC-BI1, and HC-BI2 honeycomb-based composite designs.
summary: Unit cell schematics for the HC, HC-S1, HC-S2, HC-BI1, and HC-BI2 designs are displayed to isolate and evaluate their geometric influence. These diagrams illustrate the specific structural frameworks incorporated into the composites, which are essential for understanding the mechanical behavior observed in the corresponding stress-strain and performance analyses.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of Aluminum in as-received HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe, highlighting non-uniform distribution.
summary: Aluminum elemental distribution in the as-received HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe alloy is visualized through this EDS map. The analysis reveals a non-uniform distribution of aluminum throughout the matrix prior to friction stir processing, providing a baseline for assessing the chemical homogeneity of the alloy in its initial as-cast state.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the integration of machine learning with multiscale computational approaches within the Materials Genome Engineering (MGE) paradigm for additive manufacturing (AM) materials research.
summary: This schematic outlines the integration of machine learning with multiscale computational methods within the Materials Genome Engineering framework. It highlights how these combined approaches accelerate materials research and development for additive manufacturing, reflecting the transformative advances in the field enabled by AI-driven methodologies and computational modeling strategies.

caption: Normalized mass change of pure nickel oxidized at 1000 °C for 2 hours.
summary: Normalized mass change for pure nickel oxidized at 1000 °C is shown. Although the order of samples characterized by different surface preparation processes varies during the exposure time, the final mass gain for these samples is nearly identical, confirming that surface preparation does not significantly alter the final oxidation outcome.

caption: Intragranular misorientation map of the microstructure visualized using a voxel-to-voxel grain threshold of 0.5 degrees to highlight localized orientation variations.
summary: This panel presents the IGM distribution within the microstructure using a strict 0.5-degree threshold. By applying this specific threshold, the map emphasizes subtle internal misorientations and localized lattice rotations within the grains, providing a detailed view of the microstructure's state before significant deformation or cyclic loading effects are observed.

caption: Cyclic linear sweep voltammetry comparing silver and gold working electrodes in LiF–NaF at 1173 K, scanned at 100 mV s−1 from open-circuit toward anodic potentials and back, with cathodic polarization intentionally avoided for the gold electrode.
summary: This panel presents an equivalent cyclic voltammogram for gold compared to the silver electrode shown in panel a. The scan rate is 100 mV s−1, sweeping from open-circuit toward anodic potentials and back. Cathodic polarization of the gold electrode was purposely avoided, maintaining highly reproducible curve shapes throughout testing.

caption: Grain boundary map of the CoCrNi alloy in the as-printed state, derived from EBSD data processed via Channel 5 software.
summary: This EBSD grain boundary map illustrates the microstructural state of the CoCrNi alloy in its as-printed condition. The data, processed using Channel 5 software, provides a baseline for evaluating the grain boundary distribution before any subsequent heat treatment processes are applied to the material.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation map of the cryo15 swaged sample illustrating the substructural features resulting from the specific cryogenic processing condition.
summary: The cryo15 swaged sample is characterized using Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) mapping to assess its substructural evolution. This map reveals the spatial distribution of misorientation within the grains, offering insights into the deformation-induced substructure and the effectiveness of the cryogenic swaging treatment on the material's internal crystalline state.

caption: Elastic–plastic transition force (Fe) distribution across reference substrate, as-printed WAAM, and various HIP-treated conditions.
summary: The elastic–plastic transition force (Fe) shows a distinct monotonic decrease as HIP intensity increases. This trend reflects the progressive recovery of dislocations and microstructural relaxation within the initially hardened as-printed WAAM structure. The boxplot displays individual SPT results for each condition, highlighting the shift in yield strength relative to the reference substrate.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a fully heat-treated sample, illustrating the spatial distribution of elements and phases.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction displays the microstructure of a fully heat-treated sample. The analysis provides critical evidence supporting the material's resistance to the deleterious effects typically associated with the formation of the omega-phase, confirming the stability of the secondary phase within the treated alloy's complex atomic architecture.

caption: Hydrogen bubble evolution on a 2 mm thick 3D printed steel electrode at an applied potential of 0.7 V.
summary: This photograph shows the hydrogen bubble evolution on a 2 mm thick 3D printed steel electrode at 0.7 V. The study utilizes these images to compare the bubble behavior across different electrode thicknesses, noting that flat electrodes generally exhibit larger, more persistent bubbles that correlate with lower electrochemical efficiency.

caption: Magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) hysteresis loops for the as-deposited film, illustrating the magnetic response along both the hard and easy axes.
summary: The figure displays the MOKE response of as-deposited films prior to the lift-off process. It specifically presents the magnetic hysteresis behavior of the film, comparing the magnetization characteristics along the hard and easy axes to characterize the magnetic anisotropy of the as-deposited material before further processing steps are performed.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of the Ni-16Cr-9Fe alloy after 300 min of oxidation, illustrating a duplex oxide layer structure characterized by nickel and iron oxides and significant hydration indicated by OH- and OD- signals.
summary: After 300 minutes of oxidation, the ToF-SIMS profile reveals a duplex oxide layer extending to 16 seconds of sputtering. The outer layer is rich in nickel and iron oxides and highly hydrated. Unlike the 1-minute sample, the D- signal persists into the metal substrate, indicating deuterium diffusion.

caption: RMSE curve for the ANN algorithm in the ST prediction model, plotted against the number of descriptors.
summary: This plot shows the RMSE curve for the ANN algorithm applied to the ST model. By tracking the prediction error against the number of descriptors, it highlights the sensitivity of the Artificial Neural Network model to the input feature set size within the ST prediction context.

caption: CO DRIFT spectra of used Ni 0.005 Au/SiO2 nanoparticles, acquired at room temperature following a helium purge to remove gaseous CO.
summary: This CO DRIFT spectrum characterizes the surface state of used Ni 0.005 Au/SiO2 nanoparticles after reaction. The data, collected at room temperature post-He purge, serves to identify structural changes induced by reaction conditions. These spectroscopic results provide insight into the surface oxidation states of the catalyst after use.

caption: Phase distribution map of the as-cast AlCrFe2Ni2 eutectic high-entropy alloy showing the coexistence of FCC and B2 phases.
summary: This phase map displays the as-cast microstructure of the AlCrFe2Ni2 eutectic high-entropy alloy. It highlights the characteristic distribution of the FCC and B2 phases within the material, providing a baseline for understanding the eutectic structure before any subsequent thermomechanical processing or deformation is applied to the alloy.

caption: Experimental device setup and schematic representation of the tribological friction test.
summary: This panel displays a photograph of the experimental device used for tribological testing. It includes a schematic representation of the friction test configuration, providing a clear visual overview of the mechanical setup employed to evaluate the wear characteristics of the material under investigation during the experimental procedure.

caption: Optical microstructure of the WAAM-processed AZ31 specimen viewed along the build direction (BD).
summary: Captured along the build direction, this optical micrograph reveals the grain structure of the WAAM-fabricated AZ31 specimen. The visualization provides insight into the directional solidification and grain growth patterns inherent to the wire arc additive manufacturing process, establishing the structural state of the material prior to post-processing interventions.

caption: Residual strain distribution across the L3-Top horizontal scan path spanning the cylinder walls.
summary: The L3-Top horizontal scan path, which traverses from one wall to the other, shows that the joint region maintains a strain distribution within a range of ±400 με. This profile provides a cross-sectional view of the residual strain state across the component's width at the top section.

caption: Linear relationship between ln(sinh(α1σss)) and ln Z for the α-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary: This plot illustrates the constitutive relationship for the α-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy by mapping the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the stress parameter against the natural logarithm of the Zener-Hollomon parameter. The linear trend demonstrates the dependency of flow stress on deformation conditions within this specific phase.

caption: Electron beam wire-feed additive manufacturing equipment used for the fabrication of NiTi alloy components in a vacuum environment.
summary: This panel displays the electron beam wire-feed additive manufacturing equipment utilized for creating NiTi alloy walls. The system operates under vacuum conditions to facilitate the precise deposition process, serving as the primary hardware setup for the as-built production of the NiTi alloy specimens described in the study.

caption: Model performance assessment based on the inclusion of 100 data points from the enhanced dataset.
summary: This panel presents the model's performance when trained with 100 data points. By comparing this result to smaller datasets, the study highlights the progression of the model's learning efficiency and predictive reliability, illustrating the quantitative benefits of expanding the training set size in the context of the overall research.

caption: Average grain size d plotted against volumetric energy density (VED), highlighting high-density samples 5, 6, 10, and 11.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between average grain size and volumetric energy density (VED). The data highlights specific high-density samples, identified as 5, 6, 10, and 11. Grain size values range from 15 to 31 μm, demonstrating the influence of processing parameters on the resulting microstructural characteristics of the material.

caption: Magnetization curves of FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy heat-treated at 1200 °C, comparing samples processed with and without an applied 6 T magnetic field.
summary: Magnetization curves for FeCoNiCrAl HEA heat-treated at 1200 °C demonstrate the impact of a 6 T magnetic field. Similar to the 950 °C condition, the applied field increases the volume fraction of the ferromagnetic BCC phase, resulting in higher saturation magnetization and reduced coercivity compared to the non-field-treated sample.

caption: Calculated COHP profiles for O-Ni and O-Re atomic pairs, demonstrating the electronic state distribution relative to the Fermi level in segregated grain boundaries.
summary: Oxygen-segregated and O-Re co-segregated Ni grain boundaries show Fermi levels falling into the O-Ni antibonding regions. The analysis of COHP curves reveals that occupied antibonding states exist in the region of -COHP less than zero, characterizing the electronic interaction between the oxygen dopant and the surrounding nickel or rhenium atoms.

caption: F-type stochastic surface RVE with a size ratio of L/l = 2, subjected to mechanical loading.
summary: Stochastic F-type ICMS RVEs are subjected to tensile and shear loads in this simulation. With a size ratio of L/l = 2, the panel illustrates the mechanical response of the smaller RVE. This setup allows for the evaluation of stochastic surface behavior under defined loading conditions.

caption: STEM micrograph of the as-deposited (AD) specimen showing the second carbide analysis spot.
summary: STEM imaging of the as-deposited specimen reveals the second carbide analysis spot used for chemical characterization. By performing STEM-EDS point analysis, the chemical composition of these carbides was determined. These observations confirm the presence of MC-based carbides within the as-deposited microstructure, consistent with the overall material analysis findings.

caption: 3D morphology of the sliding wear trace illustrating surface topography.
summary: The 3D morphology of the sliding wear trace is presented here, highlighting the surface profile resulting from the sliding process. When compared to the fretting wear trace, this surface exhibits lower roughness and isotropy, confirming the different wear mechanisms active during the sliding test at 106 N.

caption: Atomic model of the BCC FeCoNiCr phase represented as a 4x3x4 supercell containing 96 atoms.
summary: The BCC FeCoNiCr phase is illustrated here as a 4x3x4 supercell structure comprising 96 atoms. This computational model provides the framework for the BCC phase analysis, allowing for the subsequent random replacement of Cr lattice sites with Al atoms to study the resulting FeCoNiCr1-xAlx high-entropy alloy properties.

caption: Additional Bode plots for the 316L and 18Ni300 samples, illustrating the frequency response and fitted solid lines for the different heat-treated conditions.
summary: These Bode plots complement the electrochemical analysis by detailing the frequency response of the LPBF-fabricated 316L and 18Ni300 samples. The inclusion of fitted solid lines allows for a precise evaluation of the electrochemical behavior across the various heat-treated conditions examined in the study.

caption: Laser scanning traces observed on the surface of an as-built 18Ni300 sample.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the laser scanning traces on the surface of an as-built 18Ni300 specimen. These traces are distinctly visible, providing insight into the additive manufacturing process characteristics of the sample before any post-processing heat treatment is applied to the material structure.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of secondary phases located at the grain boundary.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image captures the morphology of secondary phases situated at the grain boundary of the as-deposited alloy. The high-angle annular dark-field imaging technique allows for clear visualization of these phases, facilitating further structural and compositional characterization of the grain boundary regions in the material.

caption: Experimental setup for compressive testing showing the MTS Landmark hydraulic test device and a FLIR i7 infrared thermometer for temperature monitoring.
summary: The experimental setup for compressive testing is illustrated, featuring an MTS Landmark hydraulic test device used to load the cellular specimens. A FLIR i7 infrared thermometer is positioned on the right to monitor the temperature of the specimens before the initiation of the compressive testing phase.

caption: Dark field TEM image highlighting the distribution of the α2 phase within the TA37 alloy matrix.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging successfully visualizes the α2 phase within the TA37 alloy after 400 hours of thermal exposure at 600 °C. This technique provides the necessary contrast to clearly identify and map the distribution of the α2 phase, which remained invisible in the corresponding bright field image.

caption: TEM micrograph of DED-Arc processed Invar fatigued at a strain amplitude of ± 0.35%, showing a high density of dislocations and complex substructures.
summary: The TEM analysis of DED-Arc processed Invar fatigued at ± 0.35% strain reveals a qualitatively higher density of dislocations compared to the DED-LB condition. Furthermore, the microstructure exhibits the formation of more complex dislocation substructures, indicating distinct deformation behavior under the same fatigue loading conditions for the arc-processed material.

caption: Mean force-displacement response for the Gyroid topology in SET-B, showing the average trend and standard deviation across three repeated impact tests.
summary: Representing the mechanical performance of the Gyroid topology, this graph shows the average force-displacement curve for SET-B samples. The data is averaged over three repetitions, with standard deviation error bars indicating the spread of the results. Numerical artifacts at the end of the impact duration are noted and ignored.

caption: Scheil calculator simulation showing the evolution of solid phases in equilibrium with the liquid as a function of temperature and solid fraction.
summary: This simulation utilizes the Scheil calculator to model solidification behavior. It illustrates the solid phases in equilibrium with the liquid phase across varying temperatures and solid fractions. The results highlight the expected formation of the three-phase L → β + TiNi eutectic following the initial pre-eutectic formation of TiNi.

caption: Mo K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 12.
summary: Mo K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra for Ni Alloy 59 are measured in total reflection geometry at pH 12. By comparing these results with those obtained at pH 7, the influence of alkaline conditions on the surface electronic structure and oxidation state of Mo in the Ni Alloy 59 can be evaluated.

caption: Stepwise identification flowchart for approach alternative 4c, mapping the logical progression and identification metrics for LSL determination across the 85-home sample set.
summary: This flowchart depicts the identification logic for approach alternative 4c, relying on test excavations to confirm service line materials. The diagram specifies the quantities involved in the process for 85 homes, which serves as the basis for calculating the total estimated costs using the referenced unit cost table.
