summary: This panel presents the Young's modulus depth profile, which exhibits a pattern similar to the hardness profile shown in panel a. The smoothed curve facilitates the observation of elastic property variations across the sample depth, providing insight into the mechanical consistency of the material throughout the build direction.

caption: Summary SHAP plot demonstrating the influence of input features on the detection and classification of gas pores.
summary: This summary plot illustrates the feature impact on the classification of gas pores within the material. It allows for the identification of which input variables are most significant in predicting the presence of gas-related porosity, providing insights into the factors that contribute to this specific defect mechanism.

caption: Pure hexachiral auxetic frame structure featuring a 4x2 cell arrangement with dimensions of 418 mm by 192 mm by 20 mm.
summary: This photograph displays the pure hexachiral auxetic frame, which is composed of four cells along the X-axis and two cells along the Y-axis. The structure measures 418 mm in length, 192 mm in height, and 20 mm in depth, serving as the base geometry for the polymeric composite absorber.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the heat-treated alloy, highlighting dominant crystallographic orientations of [0 0 1] and [1 0 1] within the selected area.
summary: This inverse pole figure map characterizes the crystallographic texture of the heat-treated LPBF-NiTi alloy. Analysis of the selected area indicates that the microstructure is dominated by [0 0 1] and [1 0 1] orientations, providing insight into the grain orientation distribution resulting from the applied solution and annealing heat treatment processes.

caption: Hardness variations across three layers of samples produced at a constant rotational speed of 800 rpm, utilizing varying traverse speeds and feed rates, specifically highlighting a 70/30 ratio.
summary: Hardness across three layers is displayed for samples processed at 800 rpm with varying traverse speeds and feed rates. The 70/30 traverse-to-feed ratio indicates higher deposition speeds compared to the 85/45 ratio. Similar to other samples, the addition of Al2O3 nanoparticles influences these hardness changes during the deposition process.

caption: Confusion matrix showing the predictive performance of the Llama 70B model regarding G-code anomaly identification.
summary: Llama 70B's performance in G-code anomaly detection is summarized through this confusion matrix, generated using a deterministic approach. The matrix serves as a diagnostic tool to evaluate the model's classification accuracy, revealing how effectively the 70B parameter model distinguishes between anomalous and standard G-code instructions during the evaluation process.

caption: Arrhenius plots illustrating the thermodynamic factor Φ for seven distinct compositions of liquid Ni-Al alloys, including comparative data from previous computational studies for the Ni20Al80 alloy represented by open symbols.
summary: This panel displays Arrhenius-like plots of the thermodynamic factor for seven Ni-Al liquid alloy compositions. The data includes empirical calculations and comparative results from previous computational studies for the Ni20Al80 alloy, which are plotted as open symbols to provide a benchmark for the current simulation results.

caption: Elemental distribution mapping of the Inconel 625 coating surface after 1000 h of S–CO2 exposure, highlighting the spatial arrangement of constituent elements within the oxide layer.
summary: This EDS elemental map illustrates the chemical composition of the Inconel 625 coating following 1000 hours of exposure to an S–CO2 environment. The visualization provides a spatial overview of the oxide layer, serving as a basis for identifying elemental enrichment and structural changes at the interface between the substrate and oxide.

caption: Systematic representation of the Taguchi method workflow illustrating the sequential steps involved in the experimental design process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the methodology of the Taguchi method, which comprises several distinct steps as shown in the figure. The diagram provides a structured overview of the experimental design process, serving as a foundational guide for implementing the Taguchi approach in systematic materials science research and optimization tasks.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy layered image of the Ni–Cu coated electrode surface, acquired at a microscopic length scale of 50 μm to visualize elemental distribution.
summary: The EDS layered image, recorded at a 50 μm scale, provides a visual representation of the elemental composition on the Ni–Cu coated electrode surface. This technique allows for the identification and spatial distribution of the nickel and copper elements within the coating layer.

caption: Ellipsometry analysis showing the fit for Zn 0.85 Ni 0.15 Te thin films.
summary: The ellipsometric parameters Psi and Delta for Zn 0.85 Ni 0.15 Te thin films are fitted using the Cauchy and effective medium approximation model. This analysis allows for the precise determination of optical constants and film thickness, demonstrating the effectiveness of the model for the 15% nickel-doped composition.

caption: Schmid factor profile map for basal, prismatic, and pyramidal slip systems in the vertical sample, derived from EBSD data.
summary: This plot displays the Schmid factor profiles for basal, prismatic, and pyramidal {11-22} slip systems within the vertical tensile specimen. Derived from post-deformation EBSD maps, the data illustrates the distribution of slip activity, enabling a direct comparison of deformation mechanisms between the vertical and horizontal build orientations.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the emergy-based environmental impact analysis and improvement methodology for a Selective Laser Melting (SLM) system.
summary: This schematic presents a comprehensive framework for evaluating and enhancing the environmental impact of SLM systems. By integrating boundary definitions with emergy flow analysis and established calculation methods, the diagram provides a structured approach to ecological influence assessment, facilitating systematic improvements in the sustainability of additive manufacturing processes.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the Fe–Ni rich outer-shell of the ɣ-Al2O3 sphere, showing a high number density of bright Fe–Ni nanoparticles.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy reveals the Fe-Ni rich outer shell of the ɣ-Al2O3 sphere. The Fe-Ni nanoparticles appear as bright contrast against the darker alumina support due to their higher atomic number, exhibiting a significantly higher number density compared to the inner core region.

caption: Refractive index of the T(0,1) mode as a function of stub height, determined at x = 20 mm for a design frequency of 34 kHz.
summary: This panel presents the refractive index of the T(0,1) mode as a function of stub height at a design frequency of 34 kHz. By evaluating the relationship at the 20 mm axial location, it establishes the necessary correlation between structural geometry and optical properties for the GRIN-PC lens design.

caption: Thermo-Calc simulated time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram depicting the precipitation kinetics of M23C6 carbides at the grain boundaries of the IN738 superalloy.
summary: Thermo-Calc simulation results are displayed as a time-temperature-transformation diagram specifically for M23C6 carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries of the IN738 superalloy. This diagram serves as a reference for understanding the precipitation behavior, and the experimental results were found to be in good agreement with these simulated predictions.

caption: Full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) values derived from neutron diffraction measurements plotted against the height of the deposits.
summary: The FWHM plot displays nearly constant values along the height of each deposit, with a notable exception near the top. This localized increase in FWHM is attributed to plastic deformation. These diffraction results are consistent with hardness profiles, indicating structural changes occurring at the same depth within the material.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of annealed W625 showing the misorientation distribution after heat treatment.
summary: The Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map for the annealed W625 provides a visualization of the local lattice misorientation distribution following the heat treatment process. This map serves to characterize the internal strain state and dislocation density variations within the moderately textured grains resulting from the annealing of the W625 alloy.

caption: Commercially pure titanium dental implant designed for a monkey maxilla, fabricated via SLM.
summary: This panel illustrates a commercially pure titanium dental implant reconstructed for a monkey maxillary incisor. Liu et al. utilized cone-beam computed tomography for the anatomical reconstruction, followed by SLM fabrication, demonstrating the feasibility of using additive manufacturing for precise dental implant development in animal model research.

caption: Normalised heat flow curves for LC3 mixtures containing varying VMA dosages, illustrating the retardation of hydration kinetics.
summary: This panel displays the normalised heat flow curves for LC3 mixtures with different VMA dosages. The data indicates that incorporating VMA leads to a lower normalised heat flow, with the following peak and slope decreasing, which signifies a clear retardation of the hydration process within the cementitious system.

caption: Average tensile quality metrics including yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation correlated with local composition.
summary: This panel displays the average values of key tensile properties, specifically yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation. These quantitative metrics are correlated with the local composition of the specimens, offering a direct comparison of how material chemistry influences the mechanical performance and tensile qualities across the tested samples.

caption: Dielectric loss (Df) measured at a frequency of 1 MHz.
summary: Dielectric loss performance is illustrated at a test frequency of 1 MHz. The data indicates that the dielectric loss drops from 0.021 to 0.010, demonstrating an improvement in the energy dissipation characteristics of the material following the introduction of the BAG prepolymer.

caption: Convergent beam electron diffraction pattern of the Mo-rich Laves phase taken along the [1 2 ¯ 13] zone axis, showing a 2 mm whole pattern symmetry.
summary: Crystallographic validation of the Mo-rich Laves phase is completed through this convergent beam electron diffraction analysis. By examining the pattern along the [1 2 ¯ 13] zone axis, a 2 mm whole pattern symmetry is identified, consistent with the structural requirements for the Mo-rich Laves phase identified in the research.

caption: Kissinger plot derived from DSC data for peak B, showing the linear relationship between the inverse absolute temperature and the heating rate for samples processed at 10, 20, 30, and 40 °C min⁻¹.
summary: A Kissinger plot is constructed for peak B using DSC data collected at four different heating rates: 10, 20, 30, and 40 °C min⁻¹. The red straight line represents a linear fit to the data, which is typically used to determine the activation energy associated with the thermal process represented by peak B.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot illustrating the linear correlation between ln[sinh(ασp)] and T⁻¹ for the uninoculated alloy, reflecting its thermal sensitivity.
summary: Displaying the thermal activation characteristics, this plot shows the linear relationship between the hyperbolic sine of the peak stress and the inverse of the absolute temperature for the uninoculated alloy. The results demonstrate how the flow stress of the uninoculated material responds to variations in temperature during deformation.

caption: Evolution of compression modulus and plateau stress as a function of polishing time for SP structures.
summary: Compression modulus and plateau stress values are plotted against varying polishing times to evaluate the mechanical performance of the SP structure. These metrics quantify the structural integrity and energy absorption capacity, providing a clear trend of how the polishing process modifies the mechanical properties of the material.

caption: Two-dimensional simulation of γ′ phase morphology in Ni-14Al-3Mo alloy, featuring cubic or rectangular precipitates oriented along [01] and [10] directions.
summary: The simulation panel for the Ni-14Al-3Mo alloy displays the γ′ phase morphology characterized by cubic or rectangular precipitates. These features are aligned along the [01] and [10] directions, consistent with the observed structural evolution patterns in the Ni-Al-Mo alloy system during aging at 1073 K.

caption: Calculated subband energy diagram of the ASFQW system under a 1-V reverse bias voltage, illustrating the spatial alignment of electron and hole states.
summary: This subband structure diagram illustrates the energy levels of the ASFQW system under a 1-V reverse bias. It highlights the spatial separation between electron and hole states, providing the physical basis for negative-order Stark-ladder transitions and the observed Γ-X carrier transfer mechanism between remote quantum wells and barrier states.

caption: Surface profile cartography of the material processed at 60 MPa water pressure and 10 m/min traverse speed.
summary: Surface texture cartography for the specimen processed at 60 MPa and 10 m/min is shown. This condition represents the baseline for the 60 MPa series, where material removal intensity is observed. The color bar indicates the height profile in micrometers, highlighting the surface topography resulting from these specific parameters.

caption: Multiscale homogenisation framework illustrating the sequential steps required to derive orthotropic engineering parameters for numerical modeling.
summary: This schematic outlines the multiscale homogenisation framework employed in the study. It details the sequential steps necessary to derive orthotropic engineering parameters, which serve as essential inputs for the numerical model. The diagram provides a clear visual representation of the methodology used to bridge different scales in the analysis.

caption: High-speed photographic observation of the molten pool flow showing the superimposed impact pressure from multiple droplets.
summary: This image captures the molten pool flow where the impact pressure of multiple droplets is superimposed. This interaction significantly increases the concave amplitude of the molten pool, highlighting the distinct differences in flow behavior compared to conventional GMAW welding processes during the HLAW operation.

caption: Converged time series of the wetting angle θ for a molecular dynamics simulation at 1250 K and 0.042 Al concentration, showing individual time-step ticks, a window-averaged trend line, and independent data draws.
summary: This panel displays a converged MD simulation trajectory for a wetting angle at 1250 K. It illustrates the use of window-averaging and independent data draws to determine the final wetting angle and uncertainty. Only the latter half of the samples, following the vertical line, are utilized for statistical calculation.

caption: S–N fatigue curves comparing 2099 Al alloy strips processed via TR and TRC, showing stress amplitude versus cycles to failure.
summary: The S–N curves for 2099 Al alloy strips demonstrate that the fatigue life of the TRC processed material is significantly lower than that of the TR processed material across all tested stress amplitude levels, indicating a clear performance deficit for the TRC process in this specific alloy.

caption: Electronic dispersion relations for model 1 with relaxed atomic positions, shown in a narrow energy window around the Fermi level before the inclusion of spin–orbit coupling.
summary: This panel displays the electronic dispersion relations for model 1 with relaxed atomic positions, focusing on a narrow window around the Fermi level. The plot illustrates the band structure prior to the inclusion of spin–orbit coupling, providing a baseline for analyzing the effects of symmetry breaking on the system's electronic properties.

caption: Time-resolved 1H NMR spectra of F3–BM at 90 °C, highlighting the evolution of distinctive endo and exo isomer peaks within the 5.0–5.2 ppm chemical shift range.
summary: This panel displays the 1H NMR spectral evolution of F3–BM at 90 °C. The spectra reveal the emergence and progression of characteristic endo and exo isomer peaks, which are specifically identified at a chemical shift of 5.0–5.2 ppm, providing insight into the reaction kinetics and isomer distribution over time.

caption: Overview of the Sisma MYSINT 100 laser powder bed fusion system, modified with an integrated airborne acoustic emission sensor and a photodiode trigger for in-situ process monitoring.
summary: This photograph displays the Sisma MYSINT 100 laser powder bed fusion system, which has been augmented with specialized in-situ monitoring hardware. Specifically, an airborne acoustic emission sensing system and a photodiode trigger are installed within the processing chamber to enable real-time data acquisition during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: High-resolution O 1s XPS spectra for LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi alloys after 1 hour of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution, characterizing the oxygen environment within the surface oxide.
summary: The O 1s XPS signals provide insight into the oxygen bonding environment within the passive layers of the two NiTi alloys. These spectra, collected after 1 hour of exposure to a 3.5% NaCl solution, complement the Ti 2p and Ni 2p data to characterize the surface oxide composition.

caption: Beeswarm distribution of SHAP values for SG and MPT features, demonstrating that higher melt pool area (MPA) values generally contribute to increased porosity, while lower values tend to decrease it.
summary: The beeswarm diagram for SG and MPT features reveals the distribution of SHAP values across core pixels. Higher MPA values are associated with larger SHAP values that increase porosity, whereas lower MPA values contribute to decreasing porosity, illustrating the sensitivity of the model to these specific melt pool conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the sampling position for the bottom region on the cross-section of the WAAM wall.
summary: This schematic illustrates the specific sampling location at the bottom region of the deposited WAAM wall. It serves as a reference for the subsequent EBSD analysis, defining the spatial context for the microstructural characterization of the bottom section of the wall during the experimental investigation.

caption: Survey XPS spectrum of the C3 surface passivation film showing binding energy peaks for C and O.
summary: The survey XPS spectrum of the C3 surface passivation film displays binding energy peaks at 285.23 eV for C and 532.23 eV for O. These values confirm the reliability of the experimental data by aligning with standard binding energies, validating the surface analysis of the passivation film.

caption: Boxplots comparing experimental and numerical temperature distributions across cooling plates for optimal channel scaling configurations at 1 mW pumping power.
summary: Temperature distributions across the upper surface of cooling plates are presented as boxplots for various optimal channel scaling configurations. The boxes represent the first and third quartiles with median center lines, while whiskers indicate the full range of temperatures. Experimental and numerical results show a generally good agreement across all configurations.

caption: Band 8 spectral reflectance map capturing specific surface characteristics through remote sensing imagery.
summary: The Band 8 spectral reflectance map captures specific surface characteristics through remote sensing imagery. As an influential environmental covariate, this spectral data provides unique information regarding surface composition and land cover, contributing to the comprehensive environmental mapping and analysis performed in the study.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map corresponding to panel (a), revealing localized strain accumulation near the intergranular crack.
summary: This KAM map corresponds to the orientation data in panel (a), visualizing the distribution of local strain. The presence of substantial KAM values indicates highly localized strain accumulation adjacent to the cracked grain boundary area, confirming the brittle-like nature of the intergranular cracking observed at 300K.

caption: EDS elemental distribution analysis corresponding to points A and B within the SP NBSC tenon specimen cross-section.
summary: Elemental distribution data is presented for specific points A and B located within the cross-section of the SP NBSC tenon specimen. This spectroscopic analysis provides localized chemical information, facilitating a detailed investigation into the elemental variations present in the material after the surface processing procedure was completed.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the dependence of cluster lifetime on inverse temperature for the A-1%B-1%C alloy, demonstrating how thermal activation influences the stability of vacancy-solute clusters.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the relationship between cluster lifetime and inverse temperature in the A-1%B-1%C alloy. The data reveals that cluster lifetime increases significantly when transitioning from VB to VBC clusters. These findings highlight the temperature-dependent stability of vacancy-solute complexes within the alloy system across the 200 K to 600 K range.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ti–Ni system illustrating the thermodynamic equilibrium states and intermetallic compound formation regions.
summary: The Ti–Ni binary phase diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the thermodynamic equilibrium states within the system. This diagram is essential for understanding the formation of brittle intermetallic compounds during deposition processes, which can lead to interface brittleness and potential crack initiation in Ti–Ni structures.

caption: Chronoamperometry profile demonstrating the electrodeposition of cobalt onto a copper foil substrate.
summary: Chronoamperometry data illustrates the controlled electrodeposition of cobalt onto a copper foil substrate. Analysis of this current-time profile allows for the calculation of the cobalt yield, which is determined to be 1.14 × 10^-4 mol, confirming the efficiency of the deposition process under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectra for the synthesized samples, providing insight into the charge recombination characteristics of the photocatalytic materials.
summary: Photoluminescence spectra are utilized to characterize the electronic properties of the samples. By analyzing the emission profiles, this panel provides essential information regarding the charge recombination dynamics within the materials, which is a critical factor in determining the overall efficiency of the photo-catalytic hydrogen production process observed in the study.

caption: Schematic representation of the sensor elements positioned on the upper layers of a bending beam within the gripper jaw model.
summary: This schematic illustrates the sensor element placement on the upper layers of a bending beam. The model facilitates mechanical calculations to determine effective length changes. By analyzing the measuring grid area of a single sensor element, researchers can derive the strain, noting that the coordinate system renders the strain value negative.

caption: Three-dimensional wear track topography of Gradient 4 material following dry sliding friction testing.
summary: This panel shows the 3D wear track topography of Gradient 4 material after dry sliding friction testing. The reconstruction provides a visual record of the wear scar morphology, which is critical for understanding the material's response to friction and evaluating the effectiveness of the gradient design in mitigating surface wear.

caption: Fluorescent photomicrograph of U-2OS cells on a geometric scaffold, stained with actinRED for cytoplasm and NucBlue for nuclei at 10x magnification.
summary: U-2OS cells seeded on geometric scaffolds are visualized using fluorescence microscopy after 24 hours of incubation. The image displays cytoplasmic and nuclear staining, highlighting cell adhesion patterns on the disc surface at 10x magnification, providing a more detailed view of the cellular distribution and morphology within the scaffold environment.

caption: Mixed morphology of dendrites and Cu-lean spheroids within a Cu-rich matrix in the Cu75 region.
summary: The Cu75 region exhibits a mixed microstructure comprising dendrites and Cu-lean spheroids embedded in a Cu-rich matrix. Similar to the Cu50 region, this morphology results from the metastable miscibility gap between the liquids of the two alloys, which significantly influences the solidification phenomena across the compositional gradient.

caption: Magnified view of the dashed black rectangular region from the APT reconstruction, providing a detailed look at the spatial arrangement of dislocations D1a and D1b where composition profiles were subsequently measured.
summary: Providing a magnified view of the region identified in the APT reconstruction, this panel highlights the specific locations of dislocations D1a and D1b. These features serve as the reference points for the composition profiles measured along the AA' line, facilitating a detailed analysis of elemental segregation at the dislocation sites.

caption: Tribological response represented by the friction coefficient curve for the 1 wt% TiC composite material across multiple load levels.
summary: The friction coefficient curve for the 1 wt% TiC composite is presented, showing its performance during sliding contact with Si3N4. This mechanical test data highlights the specific friction behavior of the 1 wt% TiC reinforced composite under various loads, following the general pattern established for the TiC/Ti6Al4V composite series.

caption: Conceptual workflow for simulation-based microstructure optimization in metal additive manufacturing, illustrating the iterative loop between design generation, macroscale thermal computation, microscale microstructure prediction, and assessment of the final part quality.
summary: This flowchart outlines a systematic optimization workflow for additive manufacturing. It details the integration of an optimization module that generates designs, a macroscale module using ABAQUS for thermal field computation, and a microscale module for microstructure prediction. An assessment module then evaluates the error between the achieved and ideal microstructures.

caption: FT-IR spectrum of CMA showing a prominent stretching vibration peak for -CH2- groups at 2926 cm-1.
summary: The FT-IR spectrum of the synthesized CMA material is presented, highlighting its chemical structure. A significant peak at 2926 cm-1 is observed, which is attributed to the stretching vibrations of -CH2- groups. This spectral feature serves as a key identifier for the successful synthesis and structural characterization of CMA.

caption: Neutron diffraction pattern of the Al71Zr24Fe5 ingot alloy.
summary: The neutron diffraction pattern for the Al71Zr24Fe5 alloy ingot is displayed. This solved diffractogram allows for the identification of the constituent phases within the ingot, providing critical data on the structural characteristics of this specific alloy composition as determined through neutron scattering analysis.

caption: Three-dimensional AFM surface profile illustrating the topography of the PMTA-CNT coating.
summary: Presented here is the 3D surface topography of the PMTA-CNT coating obtained through atomic force microscopy. This imaging analysis allows for the characterization of the surface morphology of the PMTA-CNT material, offering a clear visualization of the topographical profile and structural arrangement of the coating surface.

caption: Comparison of maximum compressive stress (σ max) between experimental data and Gibson-Ashby model predictions for Bccz, Octet-truss, and Rhombic dodecahedron Ti6Al4V lattice cells.
summary: This panel displays the maximum compressive stress results for Bccz, Octet-truss, and Rhombic dodecahedron Ti6Al4V lattice cells. It compares experimental measurements against values derived from the Gibson-Ashby model. The data indicates that the model and experimental results align well across all densities, as Ti6Al4V exhibits minimal density increase.

caption: Small-angle X-ray scattering patterns for PtCu and Pt2Zn nanocrystals, with black lines indicating simulated fits based on the Rayleigh function.
summary: Small-angle X-ray scattering patterns for PtCu and Pt2Zn nanocrystals are presented with simulated fits using the Rayleigh function. Analysis of this data reveals average particle sizes of 6.6 ± 1.2 nm for PtCu and 2.6 ± 0.6 nm for Pt2Zn, providing quantitative insights into the catalyst size distributions.

caption: Excitation and fluorescence spectra of undoped as-synthesized resins prepared via the hydrolytic pathway.
summary: This panel displays the excitation and fluorescence spectra for undoped liquid resins synthesized through a hydrolytic pathway. The plot illustrates the fundamental optical features of the bare resin, providing a baseline for photophysical characterization before the addition of dopants or subsequent UV curing processes.

caption: Multi-arm WAAM configuration employing six robotic arms to perform concurrent additive manufacturing tasks.
summary: Shown is a sophisticated WAAM system architecture that utilizes six robotic arms operating in concert. This multi-arm arrangement demonstrates the scalability of robotic additive manufacturing, allowing for complex, high-throughput production scenarios where multiple arms work simultaneously to build large or intricate metal structures within a unified facility.

caption: Surgical drilling tools utilized for Type B procedures, including a launch drill bit and two twist drill bits of varying diameters and lengths.
summary: This panel displays the surgical drilling tools used for Type B procedures. The set includes a launch drill bit with a 2 mm diameter and 4 mm length, alongside two twist drill bits measuring 2 mm and 3.25 mm in diameter, respectively, both with a 13 mm maximum length.

caption: Residual stress distribution map for a steel plate processed at a travel speed of 10 mm/s and 45 s dwell time with substrate preheating at 150 °C.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the residual stress distribution at a 150 °C preheating temperature. Higher preheating temperatures promote slower cooling rates and more gradual temperature gradients. Consequently, the results indicate a reduction in the magnitude and spatial extent of compressive residual stresses surrounding the crack compared to lower preheating temperatures.

caption: Experimental creep strain versus time data points compared against simulated solid lines for the AM state at 750 °C and 100 MPa, showing two test runs with varying opacity.
summary: Experimental creep strain data for the AM state at 750 °C and 100 MPa is compared with simulated results. The plot demonstrates a stress-based damage evolution model that captures creep strain trends, although it slightly over-predicts material ductility. Two experimental runs are shown to illustrate reproducibility and model alignment.

caption: Experimental configuration for permeability assessment utilizing the falling head method, featuring an air-valve, vacuum pump valve, standpipe, sample holder, Ti–6Al–4V scaffold, and water container.
summary: This schematic illustrates the falling head permeability test setup designed for Ti–6Al–4V scaffolds. The apparatus integrates a vacuum pump valve, air-valve, standpipe, and water container to facilitate controlled fluid flow through the sample holder, providing a structured method for evaluating the permeability characteristics of the porous metallic scaffold.

caption: Intermediate loading stage illustrating increased atomic density in the compressed contact region.
summary: As the loading force increases, the contacted region within the sample is compressed, leading to an increase in its atomic density. This snapshot captures the atomic distribution under higher external pressure, highlighting the localized response of the material structure during the progression of the nanoindentation process.

caption: Ultraviolet–visible absorption spectra of GACu, GANi, and GACu/Ni mixed complex films deposited on SiO2 glass substrates.
summary: The ultraviolet–visible absorption spectra of GACu, GANi, and GACu/Ni mixed complex films on SiO2 glass substrates are presented. The GACu complex film exhibits more intense absorption than the GANi film, suggesting that Cu precipitation is induced by lower thermal energy compared to Ni precipitation in these complex films.

caption: Parallel coordinate diagram visualizing BOHB-based hyperparameter tuning results for Net1–4, where solid lines represent iteration 5 and dashed lines represent iterations 1–4 with decreasing opacity.
summary: Displaying a parallel coordinate diagram, this panel presents the BOHB-based hyperparameter tuning results for the four neural networks across all iterations. The visualization distinguishes between the final iteration 5, shown as a solid line, and previous iterations 1 through 4, represented by dashed lines with decreasing opacity to highlight optimization progress.

caption: Si 2p core-level XPS spectrum of the HS-MP specimen following the wear test.
summary: Si 2p core-level XPS spectrum for the HS-MP specimen is shown for the post-wear condition. This spectroscopic analysis is part of the investigation into the constituent elements of HS-MP, providing essential data on the chemical state of silicon after the material has undergone the wear test.

caption: Subject A wearing the integrated fabric strip with adjustable buckles to ensure firm skin contact.
summary: Subject A is depicted wearing the integrated fabric strip, which is secured using adjustable buckles. This configuration presses the origami sensor firmly against the chest, ensuring the necessary skin contact for high-quality ECG signal recording during both resting and active states.

caption: Raman spectra collected at four distinct locations (A–D) on the counterpart wear scar following a sliding wear test at a 10 N load against the SLM-G-b sample.
summary: Raman spectra obtained at points A-D on the counterpart wear scar after 10 N sliding wear tests show broad D and G peak structures characteristic of an amorphous carbonaceous transfer film. Comparison with the 1 N test results indicates no significant structural changes in the carbon atoms despite the increased load.

caption: Box plot distribution of the phosphate band intensity, representing the mineral phase content across all experimental bone groups.
summary: The phosphate band intensity is presented as a box plot to indicate the mineral phase content across all groups. As the primary indicator of the mineral phase in bone, this measurement provides quantitative insight into the mineralization levels observed in the cortical bone, Rob-12w, and Foam-12w samples.

caption: Reflectivity spectra of the single-layer composite absorber plotted for various material thicknesses.
summary: Reflectivity performance of the single-layer composite absorber is illustrated for different thicknesses. This plot demonstrates how the thickness of the composite layer influences its ability to reflect electromagnetic waves, which is a critical factor in optimizing the material for effective absorption in various metastructure applications.

caption: Elemental mapping of a single powder particle with a diameter smaller than 50 μm, highlighting the spatial distribution of constituent elements and a specific Cr segregation region indicated by a white arrow.
summary: This elemental mapping reveals the distribution of elements within a single powder particle smaller than 50 μm. The visualization highlights the chemical homogeneity of the particle, specifically identifying a region of Cr segregation marked by a white arrow, which provides insight into the internal composition of the powder.

caption: Pseudo-ternary composition diagram showing the distribution of room-temperature (RT) fracture strain for the ZrNbMoHfTa alloy system.
summary: This diagram maps the RT fracture strain for the ZrNbMoHfTa system. Good ductility is achieved within a specific composition range defined by a Mo content of 20 at% or less, Hf and Zr concentrations between 35 and 55 at%, and Nb and Ta concentrations ranging from 35 to 55 at%.

caption: Plot of burst size (Δh) versus displacement for a representative nanoindentation curve at 500 °C.
summary: Representing the mechanical response at 500 °C, this plot illustrates the variation of burst size (Δh) with displacement. The data highlights how dislocation dynamics, including their generation and interaction beneath the indenter tip, manifest as pop-in events during the nanoindentation process at this elevated temperature.

caption: Electronic charge redistribution profile for a helium atom positioned at the int2 interstitial site within a Ni Σ 9(2-21) grain boundary.
summary: This panel illustrates the electronic charge redistribution for a helium atom at the int2 interstitial site in a Ni Σ 9(2-21) grain boundary. The presence of helium at this site weakens the grain boundary binding strength to 3.17, driven by intense charge transfer between He-1s and Ni-3d orbitals.

caption: DSC thermographic record of the TM PAN/CS composite, representing the temperature-dependent heat flow difference between the sample and the reference.
summary: The DSC thermographic record for the TM PAN/CS composite illustrates the thermal response of the material. By measuring the temperature-dependent heat input difference between the reference dish and the dish containing the test sample, the analysis provides a profile of the composite's thermal behavior and characteristic transitions.

caption: Calibration plot for DEXA sodium phosphate measured at a wavelength of 242 nm.
summary: This panel displays the calibration curve used for quantifying dexamethasone sodium phosphate (DEXA) concentrations. The data was obtained via UV-Vis spectroscopy at a characteristic wavelength of 242 nm, providing the necessary baseline for subsequent drug release measurements from various LDH-based nanohybrid samples described in the study.

caption: Formation energies of Cu-Ni alloys plotted as a function of composition, calculated using 4 × 4 × 4 and 6 × 6 × 6 k-point meshes with varying smearing parameters of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 eV.
summary: This panel displays the formation energies of Cu-Ni alloys derived from DFT calculations. The data compares results obtained from different k-point meshes (4 × 4 × 4 and 6 × 6 × 6) and smearing parameters (0.1, 0.2, and 0.4 eV) to evaluate the convergence and accuracy of the energetic predictions.

caption: Relative ice adhesion strength normalized to the average value of the untreated reference surface, highlighting the performance enhancement of the laser-structured samples.
summary: Relative ice adhesion strength is shown as a comparison against the untreated reference surface. By normalizing the data to the reference, this plot effectively demonstrates the efficacy of the laser-made structures in reducing ice adhesion, providing a clear metric for evaluating the performance improvements across different test conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the fatigue-fractured sample tested at 240 MPa and 450 °C, demonstrating the maintained equiaxed grain morphology post-fatigue.
summary: Representing the microstructure of a sample subjected to 240 MPa at 450 °C, this inverse pole figure map illustrates the grain orientation distribution. The fine, equiaxed grain structure remains consistent with the fully recrystallized state established during the hot isostatic pressing process, despite the high-temperature fatigue loading conditions applied.

caption: Pseudobinary section of the Fe–Cr–Ni system at a constant iron concentration, illustrating phase stability regions.
summary: This pseudobinary section of the Fe–Cr–Ni system, maintained at a constant iron concentration, serves as a critical tool for predicting solidification modes and final microstructures in stainless steels. By mapping phase stability, it reflects the relative influence of alloying elements, specifically the chromium and nickel equivalents, on material behavior.

caption: Mean square displacement (MSD) of atoms in a melted prealloyed high-entropy alloy (HEA) sample, calculated using molecular dynamics simulations.
summary: This panel displays the mean square displacement of atoms in a melted prealloyed HEA sample. The MSD exhibits a linear trend over time, which is characteristic of homogeneous samples in molecular dynamics simulations, indicating stable atomic diffusion behavior within the melt structure during the investigation of atomic dynamics.

caption: Magnetization measured at 60 kOe and 300 K plotted against mechanical milling time.
summary: This plot illustrates the influence of mechanical milling duration on the magnetic properties of the material. By tracking the magnetization at a constant field of 60 kOe and temperature of 300 K, the data reveals how the milling process systematically alters the magnetic response of the sample over time.

caption: Bode phase plots for ATI718 Plus, featuring solid lines that indicate the EEC model fitting results applied to the experimental EIS data.
summary: Bode phase plots illustrate the frequency-dependent phase response of the ATI718 Plus alloy. The inclusion of solid lines representing the EEC model fitting results demonstrates the successful application of the equivalent circuit approach to characterize the electrochemical behavior and passive film properties of the material.

caption: Principal component analysis of unit cell architectures (SDF), colored by the L2 relative error for local field prediction.
summary: This panel shows a principal component analysis of unit cell architectures, similar to panel (c), but with data points colored to reflect the L2 relative error for full local field predictions. This analysis investigates the relationship between geometric features of the unit cells and the accuracy of local field modeling.

caption: Simulated intensity distributions for four distinct beam profiles, including a Gaussian profile and three ring-shaped configurations, displayed on a constant intensity scale.
summary: Simulated intensity distributions for four distinct beam profiles, including a Gaussian profile and three ring-shaped configurations, are displayed on a constant intensity scale. The Gaussian profile appears saturated due to the scale, while the ring profiles demonstrate the varied power distributions available on the nLight AFX-1000 laser system.

caption: Arrhenius plot of vacancy diffusion constants (D Va) in pure Ni as a function of inverse temperature (1000/T), illustrating the kinetic validation of the current KMC model against prior computational and experimental benchmarks.
summary: Vacancy diffusion constants (D Va) for pure Ni are plotted on a logarithmic scale versus 1000/T to validate the KMC simulation methodology. The results are compared with previous KMC findings from Goswami, Alfonso, and Schuwalow, as well as experimental data from Bakker and Feller, confirming the reliability of the calculated diffusion kinetics.

caption: Calculated temperature dependence of the Gibbs free energy difference between BCC and FCC phases for the Mo5 alloy.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent Gibbs free energy difference between BCC and FCC phases for the Mo5 alloy. Thermodynamic calculations were performed to quantify the adiabatic heating effect and understand the conjugated relationship between the phase-transformation anomaly and dislocation density evolution within the material during cryogenic testing.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of SaOs-2 cells adhering to Cr-alloyed Ti surfaces and reference materials after 24 hours of incubation, showing nuclei in blue and cytoskeleton in green, with yellow/orange nuclei indicating dead cells.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images illustrate SaOs-2 cell adhesion on Cr-alloyed Ti surfaces compared to reference materials after 24 hours. The staining highlights nuclei in blue and cytoskeleton in green, while dead cells are identified by yellow/orange nuclei. These images demonstrate the cytocompatibility of the tested materials under standard incubation conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPFZ) map of the LPBF sample surface, showing crystallographic orientation gradients and individual cell colonies within grains.
summary: The IPFZ map of the LPBF sample surface illustrates crystallographic orientation distributions. Insets highlight individual cells within larger grains, while gradual color gradients indicate colonies of cells with small misorientations. This map confirms the presence of sub-grain structures that are resolved as subtle orientation variations within the larger grain matrix.

caption: Voltage-time curves for PEO coatings in a P-based electrolyte system with varying hydroxide content, illustrating three distinct growth stages and a decrease in breakdown and final voltages as conductivity increases.
summary: This panel displays voltage-time curves for PEO coatings in a P-based electrolyte system with increasing hydroxide content. The data reveals three distinct growth stages and demonstrates that both breakdown and final voltages decrease as the electrolyte conductivity increases, providing insight into the coating formation process under these specific chemical conditions.

caption: Contour plot representing the theoretically-calculated Stacking Fault Energy (SFE) values as a function of composition within the Cr-Co-Ni ternary system.
summary: This contour plot visualizes the theoretically-calculated SFE values across the Cr-Co-Ni ternary phase diagram. By mapping these values as a function of composition, the figure highlights the variation in stacking fault energy, offering insights into the stability and deformation mechanisms of the alloy system across different chemical compositions.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy analysis confirming that the observed substructures are dislocation cells within the as-built Fe60 sample.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy analysis identifies the previously observed substructures as dislocation cells within the as-built Fe60 sample. This finding confirms the presence of high dislocation densities, which are indicative of the plastic deformation and thermal stresses experienced by the material during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Storage modulus (Eʹ) curves of PLA/hemp hurd composites plotted against temperature, demonstrating the mechanical response across varying numbers of recycling steps.
summary: The storage modulus (Eʹ) curves of the PLA/hemp hurd fibre composites are illustrated in this panel. These curves represent the mechanical performance of the material as it undergoes different numbers of recycling steps, providing insight into how the recycling process influences the stiffness of the composite material over a temperature range.

caption: Comparison of cooling cycles for bottom, middle, and top bins superimposed on a 410 stainless steel CCT diagram, illustrating that thermal cycling remains within the austenite phase field and that austenite-to-martensite transformation is the sole phase change occurring during cooling.
summary: This panel displays cooling cycles for different bin locations plotted against a 410 stainless steel CCT diagram. The visualization confirms that thermal cycling is restricted to the austenite phase field, ensuring that no ferrite or pearlite formation occurs until the final cooling stage, where only austenite-to-martensite transformation takes place.

caption: XPS depth profile of TiFe0.9Ni0.1 highlighting the absence of distinct Ni(II) peaks in the oxide layer and a slight Ni concentration increase just below the Ti-oxide surface.
summary: This XPS depth profile for TiFe0.9Ni0.1 reveals that no distinct Ni(II) peak exists in the oxide layer. Notably, Ni concentration increases slightly 3–5 nm below the Ti-oxide layer, confirming that Ni remains within the metallic matrix rather than participating in the formation of the surface oxide layer.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of AM TiZrNb-O, cast TiZrNb-O, and CP-Ti in SBF, showing potential versus SCE.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for AM TiZrNb-O, cast TiZrNb-O, and CP-Ti in SBF are presented. Both alloys demonstrate comparable corrosion potentials, specifically -0.582 V for the cast sample and -0.574 V for the AM sample versus SCE. These results highlight the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the materials in simulated body fluid.

caption: Feature importance ranking based on the mean SHAP contributions of each feature, summarizing the relative impact of the five processing parameters across all samples.
summary: The feature importance ranking summarizes the overall influence of the five processing parameters by calculating the mean SHAP contributions for each feature across the entire sample set. This plot effectively ranks the variables, highlighting which parameters are most significant in determining the model's final prediction results.

caption: Enlarged view of region A from the C1 sample, accompanied by the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern used for crystallographic identification.
summary: Region A of the C1 sample is magnified to provide a detailed view of the local microstructure. The inclusion of the corresponding SAED pattern allows for the identification of the crystal structure within this specific area, facilitating a correlation between the observed morphology and the underlying crystallographic orientation.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the HT-1 sample showing the tempered martensitic structure.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging of the HT-1 sample reveals that the martensitic structure after tempering remains similar to that of the as-built sample. This observation confirms the stability of the primary martensitic morphology following the heat treatment process applied to the AerMet 100 alloy.

caption: Digital design phase showing the creation of a CAD model representing the intended geometry of the ceramic component.
summary: The second stage of the fabrication process involves the creation of a CAD model. This digital design defines the specific geometry and dimensions of the ceramic part to be produced, providing the necessary geometric data for the subsequent 3D printing program generation and the actual additive manufacturing process.

caption: Tensile stress-strain curves for eight TT samples, illustrating the mechanical response and deformation behavior under uniaxial loading.
summary: The stress-strain curves for eight TT samples were obtained through tensile testing. These curves provide the fundamental mechanical response, allowing for the determination of key tensile properties including elastic modulus, strain until fracture, and ultimate tensile strength, which are essential for characterizing the material's performance under load.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of Hep-DA, demonstrating the successful conjugation of dopamine to heparin.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of Hep-DA is presented to confirm the chemical structure of the synthesized material. By analyzing the spectral data, the successful conjugation of dopamine to heparin is verified, providing essential evidence for the chemical modification process described in the study.

caption: GAM map showing the morphology of Ni5Gd particles in the sample processed at 1050 °C with a strain rate of 10 s⁻¹ and a strain of 0.5.
summary: This GAM map illustrates the characteristic morphology of Ni5Gd particles within the material after deformation at 1050 °C. The sample exhibits a standard structural feature consistent with most observed specimens under these specific thermomechanical conditions, providing a baseline for the particle distribution and phase morphology at this temperature.

caption: Expansion force curve and deformation sequence of the expansion tube during the mechanical test.
summary: The expansion force curve illustrates the mechanical response of the expansion tube, revealing four distinct deformation stages. Due to large-area tearing, the load drops sharply after reaching the peak force, and no force platform is observed, indicating significant structural failure during the expansion process.

caption: Quantitative analysis of product ions derived from DDV, illustrating the specific mass-to-charge signals used for identification.
summary: This panel presents a quantitative analysis of product ions associated with DDV. By examining these specific ionic signals, researchers can accurately identify and quantify the presence of the target compound, providing the necessary foundation for subsequent concentration measurements and ensuring the reliability of the analytical pre-treatment process.

caption: Load–displacement curves for pristine and scCO2-aged 3D-printed PEEK samples under a 10 mN indentation load, illustrating the elastic recovery behavior during the unloading phase.
summary: Load–displacement characteristics for pristine and scCO2-aged 3D-printed PEEK are presented for a 10 mN indentation load. The initial linear region of the unloading curve is depicted, which characterizes the elastic response of the material, where the sample recovers its original shape upon the removal of the applied load.

caption: Magnetic specific heat (Cmag) of hcp Co solid solutions plotted against temperature for various compositions.
summary: This plot displays the magnetic specific heat (Cmag) of hcp Co solid solutions as a function of temperature across different compositions. The data illustrates the thermal response of the magnetic state in these solid solutions, providing insight into the magnetic behavior of the material system as temperature varies.

caption: Distribution histogram of Taylor factors for the as-built IN718 specimen.
summary: This histogram quantifies the Taylor factor distribution for the as-built IN718 specimen. The data confirms that refined grains exhibit higher Taylor factors, which is consistent with the observation that grain boundary refinement increases the average Taylor coefficient, ultimately strengthening the IN718-TiC gradient coatings under tensile loading conditions.

caption: Initial state of the three-point bending test process before loading.
summary: This panel illustrates the initial setup of the three-point bending test process. It captures the specimen's state before the application of any load, providing a baseline for the experimental procedure conducted on the 20 wt% CF/PA6 composite materials to evaluate their mechanical response under bending conditions.

caption: Finite element analysis showing vertical displacement (Uf,z) of the composites under a uniform loading force of 7.5 N.
summary: Finite element analysis results illustrate the vertical displacement of composites subjected to a uniform loading force of 7.5 N. The data indicates that vertical displacement is largest at a suture frequency of 45° and smallest at 11.3°, confirming that bending deformability increases as the suture frequency decreases in the composite design.

caption: Summary collection of various tensile testing indexes derived from the mechanical evaluation of the specimens.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive collection of tensile testing indexes for the as-built and as-cast specimens. By summarizing key mechanical parameters, it facilitates a direct comparison of the material's performance, supporting the broader analysis of how different processing routes influence the overall mechanical properties of the tested samples.

caption: Layout of simplified elbow specimens arranged within the 150x150x300 mm build volume of the FUSE 1 PBF-LB/P printing vat.
summary: This schematic illustrates the spatial arrangement of simplified elbow specimens within the FUSE 1 printing vat, which measures 150x150x300 mm. The positioning is designed to facilitate the experimental fabrication process using PBF-LB/P additive manufacturing, ensuring that all specimens are correctly oriented according to the specified design of experiments.

caption: Cumulative release profile of BMP-2 from MBGNs alone, showing a release of 20.31% by day 10 followed by a sharp increase to 46.31% by day 14.
summary: This line graph illustrates the release kinetics of BMP-2 from MBGNs without the hydrogel matrix. The data shows a relatively slow release rate up to day 10, followed by a marked acceleration in the release percentage, reaching 46.31% by the end of the 14-day observation period.

caption: Detailed geometric dimensions of the tensile specimen used for room temperature mechanical testing.
summary: This schematic illustrates the specific dimensions of the tensile specimen utilized during room temperature tensile testing. The specimen geometry is designed for use with an Instron-3382 electronic universal material testing machine, ensuring standardized mechanical evaluation of the material properties as part of the experimental procedure described in the study.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of DEPGM, highlighting characteristic peak positions used to quantify the extent of methylation.
summary: The chemical structure of DEPGM is characterized using 1H NMR spectroscopy. By analyzing the specific peak positions associated with methylation, the extent of methylation within the DEPGM polymer can be accurately quantified, providing essential information regarding the degree of modification achieved during the synthesis process.

caption: Scenario 5 transition state analysis of the artificial backpropagation network, showing the impact of mu on optimization dynamics.
summary: Scenario 5 shows the transition state of the artificial backpropagation network. The parameter mu quantifies the convergence behavior, offering valuable information about the optimization dynamics. This evaluation is part of the systematic study of mu's regulatory role, gradient evolution, and validation criteria in the PEOF-SNF model.

caption: Computational domain layout for the SLM numerical model, illustrating the defined simulation space and the designated scanning path.
summary: This schematic illustrates the computational domain established for the SLM numerical model. It provides a visual representation of the simulation space and the specific scanning path utilized during the modeling process, serving as the foundational framework for the subsequent numerical analysis of the laser melting procedure.

caption: Electrochemical parameters for rolled specimens, illustrating the distinct changes in corrosion performance before and after heat treatment compared to unrolled counterparts.
summary: Electrochemical parameters for rolled specimens reveal that the change in corrosion performance before and after heat treatment is significantly different from that observed in unrolled specimens. These data points highlight the unique influence of the rolling process on the material's electrochemical stability and corrosion resistance during heat treatment cycles.

caption: Combined residual plot showing the distribution of errors for the ANN model predictions.
summary: This combined residual plot provides a visual representation of the error distribution for the ANN model. By analyzing the residuals, the plot helps evaluate the model's predictive consistency and reliability, reinforcing the finding that the observed performance differences are within reasonable limits and do not suggest overfitting.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of glass samples treated with different metal dopants and laser parameters, illustrating the optical response associated with nanoparticle formation.
summary: UV-Vis measurements of the differently treated glass samples provide quantitative insight into their optical properties. These spectra characterize the light absorption behavior of the glass, confirming the presence and influence of the gold and silver nanoparticles on the material's color and optical performance across different treatment conditions.

caption: Mean fusion zone geometry for the LW-W sample, demonstrating the asymmetric shape resulting from parallel weld bead stacking.
summary: This plot displays the mean fusion zone geometry for the LW-W printing strategy. The asymmetric shape is clearly visible, consistent with the parallel stacking of weld beads along the X-axis. The geometry was extracted using the framework by Palmeira Belotti et al. (2022a) to reiterate the observed structural characteristics.

caption: µ phase crystal structure and its simulated XRD pattern.
summary: Displayed here is the µ phase, featuring its crystal structure and simulated XRD pattern. This entry in the diffraction library provides the necessary structural data to identify the µ phase, ensuring that the thermodynamic simulation results can be effectively correlated with experimental diffraction data.

caption: Virtual representation of the insert placement configuration within the sand mold.
summary: This virtual setup illustrates the planned positioning of machined IN718 inserts and thermocouples within the sand mold prior to the casting process. It serves as a digital model to guide the physical assembly and ensure accurate placement of components before the initial pouring conditions are recorded at the foundry.

caption: Bright-field scanning TEM image of a film deposited at 2 Pa Ar pressure and 0.5% duty cycle.
summary: This bright-field scanning TEM image displays the cross-sectional morphology of a film deposited at 2 Pa Ar pressure and a 0.5% duty cycle. The investigation confirms a less dense morphology, which is identified as the primary reason for the high electrical resistivity observed in these specific thin film samples.

caption: Macroscale force versus mid-displacement plot for the oligocrystal beam, demonstrating progressive strain accumulation and cyclic saturation behavior.
summary: The macroscale force versus mid-displacement curve illustrates the mechanical response of the oligocrystal beam. The data shows that macroscale strain accumulates during loading, with the incremental plastic displacement per cycle diminishing over time until it eventually saturates, resulting in a constant, small plastic increment per cycle.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of the as-built LPBF-NiTi alloy surface perpendicular to the building direction, revealing near-square structural features and small, unevenly distributed spherical and striped white particles.
summary: This SEM image displays the surface perpendicular to the building direction of as-built LPBF-NiTi alloy. The microstructure is characterized by distinct near-square features. Local magnification reveals the presence of small, unevenly distributed spherical and striped white particles that are too small for standard EDS analysis.

caption: Chronoamperometry stability curves for Ni, Ni2Fe1 nanofoams, and RuO2, initiated at a current density of 10 mA/cm2 at specific potentials.
summary: Chronoamperometry curves demonstrate the long-term stability of 3D Ni, Ni2Fe1 nanofoams, and RuO2 catalysts. The tests were performed at designed potentials where the initial current density was 10 mA/cm2, specifically 1.55 V for Ni, 1.42 V for Ni2Fe1, and 1.6 V for RuO2.

caption: Nanohardness and elastic modulus values derived from nanoindentation measurements conducted on the MHR coating cross-section.
summary: Panel (b) presents the nanohardness and elastic modulus values extracted from the nanoindentation testing of the MHR coating. These mechanical properties are critical for characterizing the coating's resistance to deformation and its stiffness, offering a quantitative assessment of the material's performance across the analyzed cross-sectional regions.

caption: FTIR spectra of XG/DD den-NCs with CR 0.4 and 2.5, highlighting the stability of the peak at approximately 2850 cm-1.
summary: FTIR spectra for den-NCs display characteristic peaks at approximately 2850 cm-1, corresponding to O-H, N-H, and C-H stretching vibrations. Despite the complexation of the two polysaccharides, these specific peaks exhibit no observable alternations or shifts, indicating that these functional groups remain unaffected by the interaction process.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of FPEA-ProGly polymer films recorded before and after the click chemistry reaction with MMC in the presence of a photoinitiator.
summary: Presented here are the UV-Vis spectra for FPEA-ProGly polymer films. The plot tracks the spectral changes occurring before and after the click reaction with MMC, facilitated by UV light and a photoinitiator, providing evidence of the successful chemical modification of the FPEA-ProGly film structure.

caption: Obstacle points positioned at the voxel center closest to the centroid of each relevant void region.
summary: Obstacle points are placed within each relevant void region, defined as those meeting specific size and extension criteria. These points are determined by selecting the voxel center closest to the centroid of the void, facilitating the representation of complex void geometries as discrete points within the filtered voxel space.

caption: Lithiation profiles of cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential for 3D printed NMC622 electrodes at a C/10 rate.
summary: This panel illustrates the lithiation behavior of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes. It plots cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential against lithium composition. Notably, the entropic potential surges toward the end of the lithiation process, reflecting the increasing divergence between the cell potential and the open-circuit voltage in this specific electrochemical regime.

caption: Comparison of force-displacement (F-D) curves for parallel combination structures with varying numbers of units (N = 1 to 5) under quasi-static compression.
summary: This panel displays the force-displacement (F-D) curves for parallel combination structures with N ranging from 1 to 5. These curves illustrate the mechanical response of the structures under quasi-static compression, providing a comparative analysis of how the number of units influences the force-displacement behavior during the loading process.

caption: Statistical distribution of NRMSE values across various adaptive sampling designs for an unspecified baseline function.
summary: This panel presents a statistical box plot illustrating the NRMSE deviations for different metamodels. It serves as a comparative assessment of accuracy across various adaptive sampling designs, providing a baseline for evaluating the performance of the metamodeling techniques discussed in the study through statistical visualization of error metrics.

caption: STEM-HAADF BF image of as-built CS-2.9Cu alloy showing a highly homogeneous fine alpha-Ti lath microstructure.
summary: The STEM-HAADF BF image of the as-built CS-2.9Cu alloy reveals a highly homogeneous fine alpha-Ti lath microstructure. This core-shell approach effectively mitigates thermal gradients and solute segregation during solidification, resulting in the refined and uniform microstructure observed in this specimen.

caption: Visualization of the true maximum stress point on Plate A subjected to a traction load.
summary: This panel displays a mechanical analysis of Plate A under traction loading conditions. The visualization highlights the specific location of the true maximum stress point within the material. This identification is critical for understanding the stress distribution and potential failure initiation sites during the mechanical testing of the plate.

caption: Hardness and elastic modulus maps paired with an EBSD inverse pole figure map for the middle cross-sectional specimen, oriented with the outer edge on the left side.
summary: Middle cross-sectional specimen analysis includes hardness and elastic modulus maps, complemented by an EBSD inverse pole figure map along the build direction. The outer edge is positioned on the left side of the maps. Consistent with other regions, these results indicate little variation in hardness and elastic modulus within the build layers.

caption: Ratio of the absorbed dose per fluence between the SIL phantom and each of the six ICRP116 SIG models, illustrating the relative dose deposition variance.
summary: Panel b presents the ratio of absorbed dose per fluence comparing the SIL phantom to each of the six ICRP116 SIG models. This quantitative comparison highlights the differences in dose deposition between the SIL phantom and the standard irradiation geometries, providing insight into the relative performance of the SIL model.

caption: Absorbance spectra of the samples, demonstrating the dye's absorption efficiency across the measured range.
summary: This absorbance spectrum corroborates the findings observed in the transmission data by highlighting the specific absorption efficiency of the dye. The plot provides quantitative evidence of the material's light-absorbing properties, confirming the relationship between the dye's behavior and the experimental conditions applied to the samples.

caption: Correlation between the molybdenum mole fraction in the synthesized Ni–Mo nanopowder catalyst, determined via EDS, and the corresponding molybdenum mole fraction in the precursor solution.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between the molybdenum mole fraction in the precursor solution and the resulting Ni–Mo nanopowder catalyst. EDS measurements reveal that the molybdenum content in the catalyst remains limited, never exceeding a mole fraction of 0.3, regardless of the concentration in the precursor solution.

caption: Surface morphology of a DL Ni coating deposited on a plain SS310 substrate with a second layer deposition duration of 2 min.
summary: Surface morphology of the DL Ni coating on a plain SS310 substrate is captured via SEM after a 2 min second layer deposition. The coating is primarily composed of Ni metal, with no observable metal oxides and only negligible traces of alloy elements due to the increased coating thickness.

caption: Engineering stress-strain behavior of 300 series stainless steel evaluated at room temperature (RT).
summary: This panel displays the mechanical response of 300 series stainless steel under tensile loading at room temperature. The stress-strain curve illustrates the material's characteristic strength and ductility trade-off, providing a baseline for evaluating the mechanical performance of the alloy under standard ambient conditions during tensile testing procedures.

caption: Measured temperature-time profiles for dilatometry experiments conducted at cooling rates ranging from 40 to 500 C/s.
summary: This panel displays the measured time-temperature profiles for dilatometry experiments performed at cooling rates between 40 and 500 C/s. The data illustrates how the cooling rate influences the thermal history of the samples, which is essential for identifying the latent heat changes associated with the martensitic transformation process.

caption: Voltage degradation profile of a co-electrolysis cell operated at a current density of -1000 mA cm-2 in a 20% vol. H2O-CO2 atmosphere at 800 °C, showing a significantly higher degradation rate of 0.72 mVh-1.
summary: This panel illustrates the long-term stability of a co-electrolysis cell subjected to a high current density of -1000 mA cm-2 at 800 °C. The data reveals a more rapid voltage degradation rate of 0.72 mVh-1, highlighting the increased stress on the cell compared to lower current density conditions.

caption: SHAP value distribution for UTS prediction using SVR rbf modelling, identifying the mismatch of valence electron concentration (A5_mis) as the primary influential factor.
summary: The SHAP analysis for UTS prediction reveals the relative impact of various features on model output. The mismatch of valence electron concentration (A5_mis) is identified as the most significant factor influencing the UTS of Al alloys, providing a global explanation of feature importance within the SVR rbf model.

caption: Real-time discharge curves showing anode voltage evolution over time for varying CeO2 content levels.
summary: Real-time discharge curves demonstrate the voltage evolution of anodes with different CeO2 contents. The data indicates that the anode voltage exhibits minimal time lag and maintains relatively stable discharge characteristics within the electrolyte, which signifies sustained high voltage discharge activity occurring at the anode interface during the electrochemical testing process.

caption: First-step process map for S25C steel generated via SVM, illustrating the relationship between laser power and scan speed, with the optimized parameter range highlighted in the upper-left black frame.
summary: This panel displays the initial process map for S25C steel constructed using a Support Vector Machine (SVM). It visualizes the relationship between laser power and scan speed, identifying an optimized parameter range for subsequent L-PBF experiments, which is clearly demarcated by a black frame in the upper-left corner of the plot.

caption: Creep strain-time behavior of EB-PBF Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb samples with varying particle size distributions (PSDs) tested at 250 MPa.
summary: Creep strain-time curves for Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb samples fabricated with three different PSDs are shown at 250 MPa. These samples exhibit the highest consistency in creep properties at this lowest stress limit, demonstrating that the narrowest PSD-A provides stable performance compared to the wider PSD variations under these specific testing conditions.

caption: CAD model representing the ideal geometry of a stent cell with a strut elevation angle of 72.5°.
summary: This panel displays the CAD model representing the ideal geometry of a stent cell with a strut elevation angle of 72.5°. It serves as the baseline reference for comparing the intended design against the actual manufactured geometry obtained from the µCT-scan analysis presented in the subsequent panels of the figure.

caption: Evaluation of the M load for a cracked specimen during cycle 551 at a crack length of 3.6 mm, utilizing secant evaluation on data processed via central moving average filtering.
summary: This panel displays the M load evaluation for a cracked specimen at a crack length of 3.6 mm during cycle 551. The data is processed using a central moving average filter, and a secant evaluation method is applied to determine the load characteristics for the specific fatigue cycle analyzed.

caption: Parallel coordinate diagram visualizing BOHB-based hyperparameter tuning results for four networks, with dashed lines representing iterations 1-4 and a solid line representing iteration 5, where line opacity decreases as iterations progress.
summary: Displaying a parallel coordinate diagram, this panel presents the BOHB-based hyperparameter tuning results for the four neural networks across every iteration. The visualization uses varying line opacities and styles, with dashed lines for iterations 1-4 and a solid line for iteration 5, to track the optimization of network hyperparameters.

caption: Stress-strain hysteresis loops for various loading cycles in a horizontally built specimen subjected to a strain amplitude of εa = 4 × 10⁻³.
summary: This panel presents stress-strain hysteresis loops for a horizontally built specimen at a strain amplitude of 4 × 10⁻³. The loops illustrate the cyclic mechanical response, capturing the material's deformation characteristics and stress evolution over successive loading cycles during the low-cycle fatigue test in the horizontal build direction.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the P91 steel block illustrating the microhardness measurement path (blue line) and the precise location of the tensile specimen (red outline).
summary: The cross-section of the WA-DED printed P91 steel block is shown with superimposed experimental markers. A blue dashed line indicates the path followed for microhardness measurements, while the red outline highlights the specific location and orientation of the tensile specimen extracted for mechanical testing from the printed material.

caption: Two-dimensional surface topography maps illustrating the morphological variations resulting from different post-processing treatments.
summary: These two-dimensional surface topography maps provide a visual confirmation of the effects of various post-processing treatments on surface quality. The images serve as a visual reinforcement of the statistical trends observed in quantitative analyses, demonstrating how specific treatments alter the surface profile and topography of the material samples.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Ta-Al-Co system, illustrating hypothesized phase boundaries via dashed lines and highlighting specific alloy compositions investigated in this study alongside identified phases A, B, D, and E.
summary: This ternary phase diagram for the Ta-Al-Co system, reconstructed from literature, maps hypothesized phase boundaries and specific alloy compositions. It identifies phases A, B, D, and E, with phase E showing structural consistency with a C14 Laves phase, while Ta2Al exhibits higher Co solubility than previously reported in literature.

caption: Surface electric current measurements for oriented SiC whisker composites.
summary: Surface electric current measurements for oriented SiC whisker composites are presented. These composites exhibit anisotropic conductivity, with the electric current increasing exponentially as a function of applied voltage. This nonlinear conductivity behavior is characteristic of the oriented SiC whisker reinforcement within the composite material structure.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to cast Co-Cr alloy extracts.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy analysis of cell viability for the cast Co-Cr alloy group after 24 hours of exposure to extracts. The image visualizes the ratio of live (green) to dead (red) cells, providing insight into the cytotoxic effects of the cast Co-Cr material on Human Gingival Fibroblasts after one day.

caption: Pareto chart showing the significance of process parameters on melt pool height for a 100 μm spot size.
summary: This Pareto chart depicts the significance of process parameters on melt pool height for a 100 μm spot size. The red line represents the threshold of significance. The chart provides a clear visualization of which parameters are statistically significant in determining the height of the melt pool.
