caption: K-means clustering results partitioning the original dataset into eight distinct color-coded classes.
summary: To analyze the structure of the real alloy sample space, the K-means clustering algorithm is employed to partition the data into eight distinct clusters. Each cluster is represented by a different color, providing a clear visualization of the underlying groupings within the original dataset after PCA dimension reduction.

caption: Processing map depicting the maximum height line roughness (Rz) across varying hatch spacing and stripe offset parameters.
summary: This processing map visualizes the maximum height line roughness (Rz) for 316L stainless steel. The data, extracted from experimental measurements, serves to quantitatively evaluate how hatch spacing and stripe offset influence surface morphology, providing a comprehensive view of the line roughness profile under different manufacturing conditions.

caption: Optical micrograph of the W sample displaying equiaxed-dendritic γ-Fe dendrites in the XZ cross-section at 200× magnification.
summary: Captured at 200× magnification, this optical micrograph illustrates the XZ cross-section of the W sample. The microstructure is characterized by equiaxed-dendritic γ-Fe dendrites. Consistent with the W sample series, the image confirms that the equiaxed-dendritic morphology is the primary structural feature observed in these specific processing conditions.

caption: Thermo-kinetic E-pH diagram for copper in 0.1 M NaAc solution at 85 °C, with red dots denoting measured OCP values.
summary: Copper's electrochemical stability at 85 °C in acetate solution is illustrated in this diagram. Similar to the 25 °C condition, the immunity area remains above the hydrogen evolution line. The red dots represent the measured OCP values, confirming the thermodynamic immunity of copper in this high-temperature acetate environment.

caption: Ni K-edge XANES spectra for Ni/ZrO2 and Co1Ni1/ZrO2 catalysts, comparing as-synthesized, reduced at 750 °C, and post-DRM reaction states.
summary: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra for Ni/ZrO2 and Co1Ni1/ZrO2 catalysts are presented across three states: as-synthesized, reduced at 750 °C, and after 10 h of DRM. Analysis indicates no substantial oxidation of Ni atoms or formation of Ni carbide, confirming the stability of the metallic Ni phase throughout the reaction.

caption: Surface roughness profile of an as-built EBM Ti–6Al–4V HCF sample obtained via Alicona profilometry.
summary: This panel displays the surface roughness profile of an as-built EBM Ti–6Al–4V HCF specimen captured using Alicona surface profilometry. The profile represents a worst-case scenario for surface topography, which is directly linked to the observed debit in high-cycle fatigue performance when compared to processed test pieces of equivalent geometry.

caption: Energy absorption per unit volume (W) plotted against true relative density for the tested as-built sample geometries.
summary: Energy absorption per unit volume is plotted against true relative density to quantify the energy dissipation capabilities of the different sample geometries. This panel illustrates the relationship between structural density and the ability of the as-built samples to absorb mechanical energy during quasi-static compression testing.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of dislocation loops in TM 316L stainless steel.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the presence of dislocation loops within the TM 316L stainless steel sample. This micrograph, captured at the peak damage area, serves as a baseline for identifying defect structures under irradiation, confirming the presence of typical dislocation loops without the observation of any voids.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectrum of the Sn 3d region for 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 composites, characterizing the tin bonding environment.
summary: The high-resolution Sn 3d XPS spectrum for the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 composites is shown. This spectrum characterizes the chemical state of tin on the surface of the material, which, in conjunction with the O 1s and Ni 2p spectra, confirms the surface composition of the final composite.

caption: Electrical resistivity, hall mobility, and carrier concentration measurements for pure COC and various COCA coversheets evaluated via the four-probe technique.
summary: This figure presents the electrical characterization of pure COC and COCA coversheets using the four-probe technique. It illustrates the relationship between electrical resistivity, hall mobility, and carrier concentration. The data confirms that the highest hall mobility and carrier concentration values correspond to the lowest electrical resistivity, which is advantageous for reducing resistive losses.

caption: Dilatometry curves showing the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) as a function of temperature for 316L, Al2O3, and 316L-Al2O3 core-shell 3D printed bars.
summary: Dilatometry measurements for 316L, Al2O3, and 316L-Al2O3 core-shell bars are presented, illustrating the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion at specific time intervals identified by slope changes. These curves characterize the thermal behavior of 3D printed structures, where multiple filaments are stacked, resulting in distinct expansion profiles compared to single filament data.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene electrodes measured at different current densities.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene electrodes measured at different current densities. These curves illustrate the charge storage capability and potential stability of the nanohybrid material, providing essential data on the electrochemical performance and rate capability of the printed electrode within the three-electrode testing system.

caption: Calculated phase diagram for the Ti6Al4V-0.5BN composite, highlighting the reduction in solidus temperature and the formation of TiB phases.
summary: This panel presents the phase calculation for the 0.5BN composite. Similar to the 0.25BN variant, the addition of boron and nitrogen leads to a decrease in the solidus temperature. The thermodynamic model confirms the formation of TiB phases, which are critical to the resulting microstructure of the composite material.

caption: Elemental distribution map illustrating the enrichment of niobium in the shell region, co-located with titanium.
summary: This elemental map displays the spatial distribution of niobium. The results show that niobium is concentrated in the shell region surrounding the Al2O3 particle, matching the titanium distribution. This confirms the shell is a complex phase enriched in both titanium and niobium, forming a distinct coating on the alumina.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the S 350 sample highlighting the interface between Ti 2 Ni and B2 NiTi grains.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph focuses on the S 350 sample, specifically illustrating the grain boundaries and structural relationship between Ti 2 Ni and B2 NiTi phases. The image provides clear evidence of the grain characteristics present in the NiTi alloy after the specified aging treatment.

caption: Detailed magnified view focusing on the specific geometry and interaction dynamics within the cutting zone during the machining process.
summary: This enlarged diagram provides a detailed view of the cutting zone, highlighting the specific geometry and interaction dynamics occurring during the machining process. It offers a closer look at the interface between the tool and the FGH96 workpiece, essential for understanding the mechanics of the dry orthogonal cutting experiment.

caption: Relative density versus compressive modulus Ashby chart for the evaluated lattice specimens.
summary: The Ashby chart displays the relative density against the compressive modulus of the lattice structures. Analysis reveals that specimens R 8R and K 8R, characterized by a 0.4 mm wall thickness, 4 mm unit cell size, and 50% overlap area, demonstrate the superior mechanical values among the tested designs.

caption: Principal component analysis of mixture data, with points colour-coded according to their original mixture identity to visualize distribution patterns.
summary: This panel displays a principal component analysis of the mixture data. By colour-coding the points based on their original mixture identity, the plot reveals distinct distribution patterns among the mixtures, highlighting their unique properties and demonstrating that while they share similarities, they also exhibit clear, identifiable differences in the feature space.

caption: Double logarithmic plot of minimum creep rate versus applied stress for the 5C1N alloy, showing the creep rate sensitivity to stress.
summary: This plot presents the double logarithmic relationship between minimum creep rate and applied stress for the 5C1N alloy. Based on experimental creep rupture data, the graph allows for the extraction of the apparent stress exponent, which is essential for understanding the high-temperature mechanical performance of the alloy under investigation.

caption: Al concentration distribution and fluid velocity vectors at a solidification time of 412 s under a temperature gradient G = 1 K/mm and pulling velocity Vp = 50 μm/s.
summary: This panel displays the simulated Al concentration distribution and fluid velocity vectors at 412 s solidification time. Under a temperature gradient of 1 K/mm and a pulling velocity of 50 μm/s, the simulation illustrates the interaction between solute distribution and fluid flow during the solidification process of the material.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing ethylene glycol and the resin at various stages of polymerization and processing to monitor molecular structure changes.
summary: FTIR spectra track the molecular structure of the resin and the curing process, with ethylene glycol and the precursor included for comparison. The disappearance of -C=C- bands confirms the activation of unsaturated bonds in AA and GDD by free radicals generated from TPO-L during the cross-linking and polymerization process.

caption: Temperature-dependent resistivity profiles of Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires after 5k cycles, highlighting the influence of parallel magnetic fields on electronic transport.
summary: Resistivity profiles for Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires after 5k cycles are presented under parallel magnetic fields. The application of these fields leads to a reduction in low-temperature resistivity due to martensite reorientation and suppressed spin electron scattering. These results characterize the material's electronic response following significant mechanical cycling and magnetic field exposure.

caption: Photographic documentation of the physical BMS apparatus components.
summary: The photograph displays the physical components of the Ball-on-Disk Mechanical System (BMS). It highlights the rotor assembly, which includes a radial arm mounted perpendicularly to the shaft. The system is equipped with a downward-pointing pin that features an 8 mm diameter spherical ball at its tip for experimental contact.

caption: Tafel plots derived from electrochemical data in the potential range of -0.8 to -0.6 V.
summary: Tafel plots covering the potential range of -0.85 to -0.6 V are presented to analyze the kinetics of the anodic and cathodic reactions. These plots allow for the determination of exponential coefficients and corrosion current density, providing essential parameters for evaluating the corrosion resistance of the studied steel materials.

caption: Deconvolution of the 5:20 PGM/ALG bead FTIR spectrum in the 1800–1500 cm-1 range, showing experimental data, the fitted profile, and individual peaks at 1730, 1650, 1599, and 1530 cm-1.
summary: Deconvolution of the FTIR spectrum for 5:20 PGM/ALG beads in the 1800–1500 cm-1 region was performed to investigate potential PGM-ALG interactions. The fitted profile and four distinct deconvoluted peaks at 1730, 1650, 1599, and 1530 cm-1 provide detailed insights into the chemical bonding environment within the composite material.

caption: EDS line scan profile illustrating the chemical composition distribution across the cross-section of the IN718 strut.
summary: This panel presents an EDS line scan analysis performed across the cross-section of an IN718 strut. The visualization provides a detailed profile of the chemical composition, allowing for the assessment of elemental distribution within the strut structure as part of the broader characterization of the material's strengthening elements.

caption: Detailed view of the negative thermal expansion region for LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy, highlighting the anomalous behavior observed between -50 and 50 degrees Celsius.
summary: Focusing on the temperature range of -50 to 50 degrees Celsius, this panel illustrates the intriguing negative thermal expansion phenomena observed in LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy. This specific region highlights the anomalous thermal behavior of the material, providing a detailed look at the expansion characteristics within this critical low-temperature interval.

caption: Electrical resistance measurement obtained from an embedded 3D silver structure utilizing a 3-point connection design.
summary: Presented here is the resistance measurement for an embedded 3D silver structure configured with a 3-point connection. The measured resistance is 4.42 MΩ, consistent with the reported maximum resistance value of 4.42 MΩ, highlighting the impact of connection density on the overall electrical resistance of the embedded silver structure.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material sample containing Atto425 and Atto495 dyes.
summary: This panel presents the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed sample featuring Atto425 and Atto495 dyes. Printed at a 0.5 mm thickness, this configuration completes the set of multi-material samples analyzed in the study, demonstrating the transmission behavior of this specific dye combination within the printed material matrix.

caption: Identification of BPA degradation products obtained through UHPLC analysis.
summary: BPA degradation products are identified and characterized using UHPLC analysis. This panel displays the specific chemical species detected following the degradation process, confirming the presence of various intermediates. These results provide empirical evidence supporting the proposed degradation pathway and the effectiveness of the synthesized electrodes in breaking down BPA.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing the Al5Sc2Si phase within the matrix.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the Al5Sc2Si phase embedded in the matrix. Continuous lattice fringes extending seamlessly across the Al5Sc2Si/Al interface indicate a high degree of lattice coherency between the precipitate and the matrix, confirming the structural integrity of the interface between the two phases.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern (SADP) of the as-built Ni-Mn-Ga sample, highlighting paired diffusion streaks.
summary: The selected area diffraction pattern of the as-built Ni-Mn-Ga sample reveals paired diffusion streaks. These features indicate the presence of a multimodulated structure, which arises from a low degree of atomic order and microstrains induced by the LPBF manufacturing process and subsequent rapid cooling rates.

caption: Micro-CT reconstruction highlighting the distribution of new bone formation within the scaffold structure at the eight-week mark.
summary: Focusing on the middle section of the Micro-CT data, this image specifically isolates the new bone formation within the scaffold. Captured eight weeks post-implantation in the rabbit distal femur, this visualization allows for the assessment of osteogenesis and bone ingrowth within the porous architecture of the implanted material.

caption: Spatial distribution of microhardness values across the LDED-processed specimen, showing a localized range between 260 and 280 HV 0.2.
summary: This microhardness map illustrates the spatial distribution of hardness values across the LDED-processed specimen. The data indicates that the material exhibits a relatively uniform hardness range, specifically between 260 and 280 HV 0.2, reflecting the mechanical consistency achieved through the laser directed energy deposition manufacturing process.

caption: Visualization of cell adhesion and proliferation behavior on the surface of the PLA-Hydroxyapatite scaffold architecture.
summary: Cellular interaction with the scaffold is demonstrated through adhesion and proliferation assays. These results confirm the biological compatibility of the SLS-printed PLA-Hydroxyapatite scaffolds, which are highly promising for bone tissue engineering applications, offering effective strategies for bone defect repair and promoting successful bone tissue regeneration in clinical contexts.

caption: Normalized radar chart comparing the compressive strength, flexural strength, and yield stress of LC 3 composites containing different dominant fillers.
summary: This normalized radar chart illustrates the relative performance of LC 3 composites across three mechanical properties. Kaolinite dominates the overall performance metrics, while Montmorillonite exhibits the highest yield stress among all constituents. The visualization provides a comparative overview of how different fillers influence the mechanical behavior of the composite materials.

caption: Small-angle X-ray scattering curves for the three scaffold groups, demonstrating the nano-scale homogeneity of the composite materials.
summary: Small-angle X-ray scattering curves provide insight into the internal structure of the PEEK, 40% HA-PEEK, and 40% HA-2% AgNPs-PEEK scaffolds. The analysis of these scattering profiles demonstrates that the composite materials maintain nano-scale homogeneity across the different groups, confirming the uniform distribution of the incorporated HA and AgNPs.

caption: Coercivity versus temperature for the top and bottom FM-layers in NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with LNiPy.
summary: Coercivity values are plotted against temperature for the top and bottom ferromagnetic layers in NiFe/IrMn(t)/NiFe samples with LNiPy. The results demonstrate that increasing the AFM-layer thickness modifies the coercivity-temperature relationship, resulting in a more convex profile compared to thinner AFM-layer configurations within the studied temperature range.

caption: Particle tracks upstream of the spray gun at Cl = 240 mm and Pl = 10 mm, showing axial movement.
summary: Particle trajectories are depicted for Cl = 240 mm and Pl = 10 mm. The vast majority of particles move along the main axis, consistent with the behavior observed across all Pl = 10 mm cases, where axial flow is maintained despite variations in the Cl distance.

caption: Tafel plots derived from HER polarization curves for Ni-Al alloys, comparing the Tafel slopes of different heat-treated samples to evaluate HER kinetics.
summary: Tafel plots reveal the HER kinetics of various Ni-Al alloy catalysts. The RN30-LR sample exhibits a Tafel slope of 80.6 mV/dec, significantly lower than those of Ni foam, RN15-LR, and RN120-LR. This lower slope indicates that the RN30-LR catalyst possesses the fastest HER kinetics among the tested materials.

caption: Elemental distribution map corresponding to the high-magnification SEM region, illustrating the chemical composition of the surface.
summary: Elemental distribution map corresponding to the high-magnification SEM region illustrates the chemical composition of the surface. The denser structure observed in the coating reduces the penetration of molten salt, resulting in lower ZrO2 phase transformation, as evidenced by the elemental distribution across the analyzed YSZ coating surface.

caption: Extended visualization of the universal control framework applied to diverse additive manufacturing scenarios.
summary: Building on the previous panel, this diagram illustrates the universal application of the control framework. It highlights the feasibility of managing defect dynamics across a wide range of additive manufacturing scenarios, reinforcing the capability to maintain process integrity even when faced with varying and complex operational conditions.

caption: Spectral reflectance profile of the 3DTES-SS material compared against solar flux and a blackbody radiator at 270 °C.
summary: This plot displays the spectral reflectance of 3DTES-SS across the 0.25–25 μm wavelength range. By integrating this reflectivity spectrum, the material demonstrates a solar absorptance of 79%. The data is presented alongside reference curves for solar flux and blackbody emission at 270 °C to characterize its thermal-optical performance.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the IN718 material in the heat-treated, undeformed state, displaying crystallographic orientation relative to the scanning plane with black lines denoting grain boundaries.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the initial microstructure of IN718 following heat treatment. The color-coded orientation map reveals the crystallographic arrangement, while black lines delineate grain boundaries. Notably, the presence of numerous annealing twin boundaries, specifically Σ3 boundaries, characterizes the initial state of the material before any deformation.

caption: Pressure calibration graph for the overpressure range, comparing dimensionless pressure coefficients Cp* derived from the PSP technique against Cp values obtained from reference pressure taps.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the pressure calibration of the PSP system for the overpressure range. It compares the dimensionless pressure coefficient Cp* from the PSP technique with the reference Cp from pressure taps. The measurement points show a good fit to the calibration line, confirming the system's accuracy.

caption: Magnetic torque l(φ) measured at H = 600 Oe after rotating the sample by 90° around the surface normal, showing an identical profile to panel a.
summary: Following a 90° rotation of the sample around the surface normal, the magnetic torque measurement is repeated at 600 Oe. The resulting profile is identical to the initial measurement in panel a, demonstrating that the observed uniaxial anisotropy is an experimental artifact rather than an intrinsic material property.

caption: Pole figure displaying the crystallographic texture distribution of the N-Opt sample.
summary: This pole figure visualizes the texture distribution for the N-Opt sample, with red regions denoting higher maximum uniform density values. By mapping the crystallographic orientation, this plot provides insight into the optimized material structure, which is a key factor influencing the performance of the sample under investigation.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the GH4151 alloy calculated using Thermo-Calc software, illustrating the phase stability regions as a function of temperature.
summary: The equilibrium phase diagram for the GH4151 alloy, generated via Thermo-Calc software, provides a theoretical basis for understanding phase stability. This computational analysis identifies the γ′ dissolution temperature at 1148 °C, serving as a critical reference point for the thermal processing and microstructural evolution of the investigated alloy system.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image displaying the morphology of a nano-scratch groove on the plasma nitrided IN718 AM alloy surface.
summary: This AFM image illustrates the surface morphology of a nano-scratch groove created on a plasma nitrided IN718 AM alloy. The visualization provides a detailed view of the track geometry resulting from a 1 mN peak load applied during the nano-scratch test, highlighting the surface response of the additively manufactured material.

caption: Fluorescence intensity histogram quantifying OCN expression levels in MSCs across different zones of the osteochondral scaffolds, with statistical significance indicated by p < 0.05.
summary: Quantification of OCN fluorescence intensity confirms the low expression of this osteogenic marker in MSCs within the cartilage zone. The statistical data supports the conclusion that TGF-β1 loading successfully directs MSCs toward a chondrogenic lineage, as evidenced by the minimal presence of osteogenic markers like OCN after 14 days.

caption: Final decomposition configuration at 1.74 nm indentation depth, displaying all initial SFTs converted into 1/6<112> extended dislocations and half-PDLs.
summary: At an indentation depth of 1.74 nm, the decomposition of all SFTs formed during the first pop-in event is complete. The final microstructural state consists of 1/6<112> extended dislocations and half-PDLs. This panel confirms the total transformation of the initial SFT structures into these specific dislocation configurations under continued mechanical loading.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics comparing the ADIPSO-VC optimization model against experimental FDM data for the RTC-F SPVM.
summary: This plot displays the I-V characteristics of the RTC-F SPVM, comparing experimental FDM data with results obtained via the ADIPSO-VC method. The comparison demonstrates the effectiveness of the ADIPSO-VC approach in modeling the electrical behavior of the system, highlighting its stability and performance in constraint extraction tasks.

caption: Fluorescence staining of hASC-CSKs on days 1, 7, and 12, highlighting Connexin 43 (red) gap junctions, phalloidin-stained cell morphology (grey), Hoechst-stained nuclei (blue), and ABCG2-stained hPSC-LSCs (green).
summary: Time-course fluorescence imaging of hASC-CSKs reveals the formation of cell-cell connections via Connexin 43 gap junctions. By staining for phalloidin, Hoechst, and ABCG2, the panel illustrates the structural organization and connectivity of the stromal cells alongside the epithelial hPSC-LSCs over the 12-day culture period, confirming the development of cellular networks.

caption: Representative 2D X-ray projection image and quantitative pore morphology metrics for the sample sintered for 5 minutes.
summary: This panel displays the micro-CT analysis of a sample sintered for 5 minutes. It includes a representative 2D X-ray projection image alongside quantitative measurements of pore morphology, specifically the mean Feret diameter and aspect ratio, providing insight into the initial state of porosity and densification in the material.

caption: Selected-area diffraction pattern obtained from the Ni-based alloy and metal carbide hetero-phase interface.
summary: Selected-area diffraction pattern analysis of the Ni-based alloy and M7C3 carbide hetero-phase interface confirms the orientation relationship between the carbide and the f.c.c. Ni-based alloy matrix. This diffraction data complements the high-resolution imaging to characterize the crystallographic alignment of the precipitate within the alloy matrix.

caption: Temperature-dependent low-field AC magnetic susceptibility curves for the unidirectional melting strategy (UMS) sample, measured at scan vector rotation angles of 0°, 45°, and 90°. The inset displays characteristic temperatures T M, T A, and T C, alongside the transformation hysteresis width Δ T hys indicated by green double arrows.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent low-field AC magnetic susceptibility for the UMS sample across three scan vector rotations. The inset highlights critical transformation temperatures and the hysteresis width. The nearly constant Δ T hys values across these measurements suggest a consistent level of chemical homogeneity within the UMS processed material.

caption: Ni 2p3/2 XPS spectrum illustrating the deconvoluted surface chemistry of the FeCoNiMoWCr HEA coating after the corrosion test.
summary: The deconvoluted Ni 2p3/2 XPS spectrum provides insight into the nickel chemical environment within the passive film of the FeCoNiMoWCr HEA coating. By analyzing these surface spectra alongside other elements, the study confirms the development of protective oxide layers that enhance the corrosion resistance of the HEA material.

caption: Viscosity measurements of predicted carbon fiber-reinforced samples categorized by extrusion state, including under, nominal, and over extrusion conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between sample viscosity and extrusion quality for carbon fiber-reinforced materials. Data indicates that lower viscosity values correspond to over-extrusion, while higher viscosity levels are associated with under-extrusion. These findings align with established literature regarding the rheological behavior of extruded fiber-reinforced composites during processing.

caption: Microscopic observation of the neurovascular unit 48 h after cell seeding, showing the progression of cell growth on the hydrogel scaffold.
summary: At 48 h post-seeding, the neurovascular unit demonstrates the progression of cell colonization on the 3D printed hydrogel scaffold. This time point captures the intermediate growth phase, allowing for the assessment of how cells interact with and populate the micro-nano fabricated vascular structure during the early stages of culture.

caption: Twin-specific FTVDF reconstructed image of the blue grain from the 80° tilt dataset, featuring a red line profile corresponding to the 3D profile in (a).
summary: The blue grain is visualized here using a twin-specific FTVDF reconstruction derived from an 80° tilt dataset. A red line profile is overlaid, matching the orientation of the 3D profile shown in panel (a). This image provides a high-resolution view of the grain structure for comparative analysis of reconstruction accuracy.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulation results showing the evolution of shear stress as a function of the impact parameter d, highlighting the asymmetrical pinning strength.
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that the critical shear stress varies significantly with the impact parameter d. The results reveal an asymmetrical pinning effect, where slip planes located at the top or bottom of the void exhibit different critical stress values, confirming that glide plane positioning relative to the void center dictates strength.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of DED-processed Ti-4.0Co alloy in the XY plane, illustrating grain morphology and crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the Ti-4.0Co alloy reveals the grain morphology and crystallographic orientation distribution within the horizontal XY plane. This EBSD analysis confirms that the microstructure consists of α-Ti and Ti2Co phases, with the orientation relationship between these phases highlighted by white circles.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph showing TiC carbides and associated core particles identified as AlTi3 in the US-0W sample.
summary: The bright-field TEM micrograph displays TiC carbides within the US-0W sample, which contain core particles identified as AlTi3. These carbides exhibit specific compositional features, including Mo-enriched edges, and are confirmed through EDS spectrum analysis, SAED patterns, and dark-field imaging to be distinct structural components of the alloy.

caption: Fractal dimension analysis of surface roughness visualized via Avizo software, where red regions indicate areas of higher curvature and purple regions represent areas of lower curvature.
summary: Surface roughness is evaluated using fractal dimension analysis performed in Avizo software. The resulting visualization highlights surface curvature variations, with red areas denoting higher curvature and purple areas representing lower curvature. This analysis provides a detailed spatial assessment of the surface topography of the printed structural model.

caption: DTG curves illustrating the thermal degradation rates of WE and ESE extracts during pyrolysis.
summary: DTG curves were utilized to analyze the thermal degradation profiles of the WE and ESE extracts. These curves serve as a comparative physicochemical fingerprint, highlighting the specific rates of mass loss during pyrolysis, which are essential for understanding the thermal stability and degradation behavior of the materials.

caption: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of Pt-Ni nanocages, exhibiting reduced surface oxidation and a binding energy shift following controlled interior corrosion.
summary: The high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum for the Pt-Ni nanocages shows reduced surface oxidation compared to the alloy. Deconvolution into Ni-Pt and Ni 2+ doublets indicates that only 31.5% of the nickel is in the Ni 2+ state, accompanied by a slight shift in binding energy due to controlled interior corrosion.

caption: Modulus measurements of CoCrFeNiMox HEA deposits showing the variation across different Mo concentrations.
summary: Elastic modulus values for CoCrFeNiMox HEA deposits are shown to decrease slightly with increasing Mo content. Specifically, the modulus drops from 225.88 ± 23.32 GPa for Mo0 to 214.97 ± 27.09 GPa for Mo1.0, reflecting the mechanical response of the deposits during loading-unloading nanoindentation tests.

caption: Schematic representation of the immersion test cell configuration used for evaluating Ni and Ni-20Cr specimens in molten ZnCl2 at 593 K.
summary: This schematic illustrates the immersion test cell setup designed for evaluating Ni and Ni-20Cr specimens. The experimental configuration operates within an Ar-filled glovebox at 593 K, utilizing a quartz cell heated by a custom furnace to maintain controlled thermal conditions for studying material interactions with molten ZnCl2 salt.

caption: Nanoindentation load-displacement curves obtained from the Invar alloy coatings to investigate the mechanical response under localized loading.
summary: Nanoindentation load-displacement curves are displayed to analyze the mechanical behavior of the Invar alloy coatings. These tests were conducted to determine the underlying reasons for the observed increase in hardness, providing detailed insight into the deformation characteristics and mechanical resistance of the material under controlled indentation conditions.

caption: Thermo-magnetisation curves of annealed LPBF-processed NiMnSn alloys measured under a 1 T applied magnetic field.
summary: Thermo-magnetisation curves for annealed LPBF-processed NiMnSn alloys are presented under a 1 T applied magnetic field. These field cooling and field warming curves characterize the magnetic phase transformations. The observed magnetic hysteresis in the M-T curve confirms the presence of a first-order phase transition (FOPT) around the transition temperature.

caption: Atomic configuration of the 8 nm grain size alloy at 0.1 strain, illustrating increased stacking fault density and the emergence of twin structures.
summary: Increasing the strain to 0.1 leads to a higher density of stacking faults within the alloy. Some of these stacking faults extend further into the grain structure to form distinct twin boundaries, indicating that the material is actively developing twin-based deformation mechanisms as the tensile process continues.

caption: Comparison of simulated and measured absorptivity spectra for TE and TM polarizations across varying incident angles (θi = 0°, 30°, 45°, and 60°).
summary: This panel presents a comparison between simulated and measured absorptivity data for the metapyramid. The results are plotted for both TE and TM polarizations at incident angles of 0°, 30°, 45°, and 60°. These measurements validate the electromagnetic behavior of the structure under different illumination conditions and polarization states.

caption: Current density (J geo) versus potential (E) curves for nanoNi-P electrodes synthesized at varying deposition current densities (I dep) ranging from -12.5 to -200,000 μA cm −2.
summary: This polarization curve illustrates the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity of nanoNi-P electrodes. The electrochemical performance is evaluated across different deposition current densities, demonstrating how the synthesis conditions influence the overall current density response relative to the applied potential, which serves as a primary indicator of catalytic activity.

caption: Fatigue crack growth rate versus stress intensity factor range for the beta-annealed condition, illustrating the effect of crack orientation.
summary: Beta-annealed samples exhibit fatigue crack growth rate trends relative to the stress intensity factor range. Similar to other conditions, the data points for different crack orientations closely overlap, confirming that the crack path orientation has a negligible effect on the fatigue crack growth rate for this microstructure.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) plot of proteomic data showing clustering of HCECs across four experimental groups: control (CTR), D609, hyperosmolar stress (Hy), and co-treatment (Hy + D609).
summary: PCA analysis of proteomic data demonstrates high reproducibility within experimental groups through tight replicate clustering. The plot reveals distinct separation between the hyperosmolar stress groups (HP and HDP) and the control/D609 groups along PC1, highlighting the specific proteomic shifts induced by hyperosmolar stress and the subsequent modulation by D609 treatment.

caption: Deconvoluted N1s XPS spectrum for FS electrodes at layer (III) anti-TNFα-Th2CA|AuNPs, confirming nitrogen detection from the antibody layer.
summary: Deconvoluted N1s spectra for the FS electrode at layer (III) demonstrate the presence of nitrogen, which is attributed to the anti-TNFα antibody. This confirms the successful completion of the immunosensor assembly on the FS electrode, mirroring the results obtained for the SS electrode.

caption: Relationship between generated current and coulombic efficiency for EC without irradiation and PhEC processes under different LED light sources.
summary: Panel b displays the currents generated during EC and PhEC processes alongside their respective coulombic efficiencies. The EC process is noted for its high efficiency of 5.88 × 10 −3 Ah mg L −1, despite generating a relatively low current density while removing a minimal amount of 4-NP pollutant.

caption: Visualization of contact angle impact weight factors, showing the sensitivity of this geometric parameter to changes in WFS and TS.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the impact weight factors associated with the contact angle of the weld bead. The red zones represent the process parameter space where WFS and TS have the most pronounced effect on the contact angle, facilitating a better understanding of the geometric control during the welding process.

caption: Ti–Fe binary phase diagram illustrating the eutectic composition range relevant to the brazing seam.
summary: The Ti–Fe binary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic foundation for the brazing process. Analysis of the brazing seam composition indicates that it primarily falls within the eutectic composition range, which is critical for understanding the phase formation and joint characteristics observed during the contact reaction brazing process.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) profile for as-printed IN718 single material cylinders.
summary: This panel displays the measured coefficient of thermal expansion for as-printed Inconel 718 specimens as a function of temperature. These experimental results are essential for informing subsequent thermo-mechanical finite element method simulations, providing the necessary material property data to accurately model the behavior of complex bi-material structures under thermal loading conditions.

caption: Sound absorption coefficient spectra of microperforated sandwich-polyurethane composite structures measured across a frequency range of 160–1700 Hz, demonstrating the impact of varying polyurethane filling thicknesses on peak frequency shifts.
summary: This plot displays the sound absorption coefficient spectra for composite structures with varying polyurethane filling thicknesses between 160 and 1700 Hz. The data indicates that increasing the polyurethane filling thickness causes the sound absorption peak frequency to shift toward the low-frequency direction, specifically observed at 134, 150, 186, and 198 Hz.

caption: Infrared spectrum of NiTi nanoparticles modified with ODPA, focusing on the CH stretching region after rinsing and sonication, showing asymmetric and symmetric CH2 peaks at 2916 cm-1 and 2850 cm-1.
summary: This panel displays the FTIR spectrum for ODPA-modified NiTi nanoparticles. Following rinsing and sonication, the CH stretching region reveals characteristic peaks at 2916 cm-1 and 2850 cm-1, corresponding to the asymmetric and symmetric CH2 vibrations, respectively, confirming the successful surface modification of the nanoparticles with the ODPA ligand.

caption: Reduction in explained variance observed during a permutation feature analysis, demonstrating the sensitivity of the model to specific input features.
summary: To assess the robustness of the PLSR model, a permutation feature analysis is performed. The resulting plot shows a significant decrease in explained variance when specific features are permuted, indicating that the model is highly susceptible to these features and confirming their importance to the overall predictive performance.

caption: Schematic representation of the multi-objective optimisation process guided by an approximate model.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the systematic multi-objective optimisation process employed in the study. Guided by an approximate model, the diagram outlines the sequential steps and decision-making logic required to achieve optimal results, providing a clear visual framework for the computational methodology used to navigate complex design spaces effectively.

caption: Mean squared error (MSE) progression over training epochs for scenario 1 of the PEOF-SNF artificial backpropagation network.
summary: This learning curve illustrates the MSE progression across training epochs for the first paradigm scenario of the PEOF-SNF model. The data confirms the effectiveness of the ANN technique in modeling periodic electroosmotic flow dynamics, as evidenced by the small MSE measurements achieved during the training process.

caption: Force-displacement curves comparing optimized specimens subjected to vacuum-assisted thermal post-processing at 70 °C, 100 °C, and 120 °C.
summary: This plot displays force-displacement curves for optimized specimens under varying vacuum-assisted thermal post-processing temperatures of 70 °C, 100 °C, and 120 °C. Experimental results indicate that while higher post-processing temperatures cause increased mass loss, the structures exhibit improved resistance to deformation, demonstrating the mechanical benefits of the thermal treatment process.

caption: Fluorescence micrographs of encapsulated HDFs stained for live/dead viability, demonstrating high cell survival rates and enhanced spreading in 5 wt% and 7.5 wt% hydrogels compared to the 10 wt% variant.
summary: Live/dead staining of encapsulated HDFs reveals high cell viability within the hydrogel matrices. Observations indicate that cells exhibit more pronounced spreading behavior in 5 wt% and 7.5 wt% cfGel-Hydrogels compared to the 10 wt% formulation, confirming that lower polymer concentrations are more conducive to initial cell morphology and viability.

caption: Comparison of yield strength versus density for the HPDC Al 80 Si 8 Mg 4 Cu 4 Zn 4 alloy against conventional Al alloys, Al-based entropy alloys, and AM Al alloys at 300 °C.
summary: Performance benchmarking at 300 °C compares the yield strength and density of the HPDC Al 80 Si 8 Mg 4 Cu 4 Zn 4 alloy with various classes of aluminum-based materials. This comparison highlights the alloy's relative mechanical efficiency compared to conventional, entropy-based, and additively manufactured aluminum alloys.

caption: Wave velocity versus temperature for as-received Ni–Ti alloy during cooling, showing anomalies at P1′ and P2′.
summary: This plot displays the wave velocity of as-received Ni–Ti alloy during cooling, measured at 10 MHz. An inflection point at 180 K (P1′) indicates structural modification, while a linear regime change near 165 K (P2′) corresponds to a minimum in the elastic modulus before hardening behavior resumes.

caption: VEGF immunofluorescence staining within bone defect sites at 4 and 8 weeks, demonstrating angiogenic factor expression levels.
summary: VEGF immunofluorescence staining within bone defect sites at 4 and 8 weeks demonstrates angiogenic factor expression levels. Immunohistochemical fluorescence analysis confirms that VEGF expression is highest in the 10% PBT group, supporting the conclusion that the scaffold promotes vascular regeneration through the upregulation of key angiogenic signaling proteins.

caption: Performance comparison of four holographic algorithms including Random mask (RM), RS, GS, and GSW.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of four distinct holographic algorithms: Random mask (RM), RS, GS, and GSW. The visualization evaluates the performance metrics of these methods, providing a clear overview of how each algorithm functions within the context of holographic data processing and reconstruction tasks described in the study.

caption: Local strain evolution and DIC strain distribution maps for specimens tested at a nominal strain rate of 100 s⁻¹.
summary: Local strain evolution is plotted at varying global strain levels for specimens tested at 100 s⁻¹. The NHT specimen reaches a local strain maximum of approximately 40% at a global strain level of 20%. DIC images at the bottom illustrate the strain distribution at maximum global strain, highlighting deformation mechanisms.

caption: Expanded view of the superconducting transition region under an applied in-plane magnetic field of 10 mT, tilted at 25 degrees from the longitudinal bridge axis.
summary: This expanded view focuses on the superconducting transition under a 10 mT in-plane magnetic field tilted at 25 degrees. The application of this field causes a noticeable decrease in the transition temperature for both segments, demonstrating the sensitivity of the superconducting state to the orientation of the applied field.

caption: Creep-rupture lifetime data for three heats of CF8C-Plus plotted as a function of applied stress, with distinct symbols and colors representing different test temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep-rupture lifetime of three CF8C-Plus heats across various applied stress levels. Each temperature is denoted by a unique symbol and color, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's creep behavior. Trendlines are included as visual aids to assist in interpreting the relationship between stress and rupture time.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for CrMnFeCoNi-based HEAs with varying WC additions, measured during uniaxial tensile testing at 298 K.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the tensile behavior of CrMnFeCoNi-based HEAs with different WC additions at 298 K. The HEA exhibits an ultimate tensile strength of 652.8 MPa, a yield strength of 532.0 MPa, and a total elongation of 31.2%, demonstrating the material's mechanical response under uniaxial tensile loading conditions.

caption: Normalized apparent strength plotted against the fiber inclination angle for specimens exhibiting slipping rupture, illustrating the determination of the strength reduction factor f'.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between normalized apparent strength and fiber inclination angle for specimens undergoing slipping rupture. The data reveals that apparent fiber strength decreases as the inclination angle increases, as indicated by the black dashed line. This trend is used to determine the strength reduction factor f' for fibers.

caption: Schematic representation of the ensemble learning framework utilized for predicting high-hardness high-entropy alloys (HEAs), incorporating a Stacking model architecture that integrates RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost as base learners.
summary: This schematic illustrates an ensemble learning system designed to identify high-hardness high-entropy alloys. The architecture employs a Stacking model that synthesizes predictions from four distinct base learners: Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost. This integrated approach enhances the predictive accuracy for material hardness within the HEA design space.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the impedance modulus (|Z|) and phase angle distributions for the Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings and the 2Cr13 substrate.
summary: Bode plots showing the impedance modulus (|Z|) and phase angle distributions are provided for the Ti0.1, Ti0.15, and Ti0.2 coatings and the 2Cr13 substrate. These plots characterize the frequency-dependent electrochemical response of the specimens, offering detailed information regarding the passive film properties and charge transfer processes at the interface.

caption: Common Neighbor Analysis (CNA) snapshot of the sample at 300 K and 3% strain, highlighting the structural evolution and dislocation formation.
summary: Representing the structural state at 3% strain, this CNA snapshot reveals the evolution of the material at 300 K. By observing the slice along the X direction, the visualization clearly identifies the formation and distribution of dislocations within the γ′ precipitates phase as the sample undergoes mechanical deformation.

caption: Concentration of graphene in the supernatant measured via UV-spectroscopy as a function of initial graphite and tannin concentrations.
summary: This panel displays the concentration of graphene in the supernatant, determined using the UV-spectrum technique. By analyzing these results alongside mass yield data, it is deduced that optimal graphene concentration values are achieved specifically when the initial graphite concentration is 5 mg·mL⁻¹ and the tannin concentration is 1 mg·mL⁻¹.

caption: Additional energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping of the as-printed 10 wt.% CuSO4 loaded composite, providing further insight into elemental localization.
summary: This energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental map provides further insight into the elemental localization within the as-printed 10 wt.% CuSO4 loaded composite. Captured at a 10 µm scale, the map complements the previous panel by detailing the distribution of specific elements, confirming the chemical composition and uniformity of the printed composite structure.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms at 5 mV s⁻¹ for on-chip μSC using 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H₂SO₄ electrolyte, measured across temperatures from room temperature down to -20 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry profiles for the 5 wt% PEGDA-based electrolyte demonstrate electrochemical performance at low temperatures. Measurements conducted at 5 mV s⁻¹ from room temperature to -20 °C reveal the stability and behavior of the on-chip μSC system, highlighting its superior performance in sub-zero conditions compared to conventional PVA-based gel electrolytes.

caption: Fractured ABS samples with a 0.06 mm layer thickness, displaying stress contours for both coated and uncoated conditions.
summary: This panel illustrates the stress distribution within 3D-printed ABS samples fabricated with a 0.06 mm layer thickness. It provides a comparative visualization of fractured specimens under both coated and uncoated conditions, highlighting the resulting stress contours to evaluate the mechanical response and structural integrity of the printed material.

caption: Comparison of experimental fatigue life values against predicted life values, demonstrating high predictive accuracy within the scatter bands.
summary: This parity plot compares experimental fatigue life against predicted life values. The model demonstrates high accuracy, as nearly all data points fall within the defined scatter bands. Specifically, only one data point lies outside the 1-scatter band, while remaining within the 2-scatter band, confirming the robustness of the predictive model.

caption: Dilatometric curve and its first derivative for the Base alloy with an initial pearlitic microstructure, highlighting the transformation regions and critical temperatures.
summary: The dilatometric analysis for the pearlitic initial microstructure reveals a stronger change in relative change in length compared to the ferritic case. This behavior is attributed to the dissolution of iron carbides in cementite and the formation of ferrite halos around graphite nodules during the transformation to austenite.

caption: Evolution of displaced atoms over time in NiCr alloy during a 50 keV Ni cascade, comparing classical MD, electronic-stopping-only, and 2T-MD model results.
summary: Representing the defect production in NiCr under 50 keV Ni cascades, this panel compares classical MD, electronic-stopping-only, and 2T-MD models. The plot illustrates the time-dependent damage accumulation, allowing for an assessment of how different simulation parameters affect the final number of displaced atoms in this specific binary alloy.

caption: EDS line scan profile quantifying the elemental concentration gradient across the amorphous oxide scale and steel matrix interface.
summary: The EDS line scan profile quantifies the elemental concentration gradients across the interface between the amorphous oxide scale and the steel matrix. This spectroscopic data confirms the presence of specific elements and their distribution, supporting the observation of chemical variations resulting from the LBE exposure conditions at 500 °C.

caption: Tabular summary of the varied experimental parameters and the corresponding measured values obtained from the drag cylinder artifacts.
summary: This table presents the varied parameters and measured values associated with the drag cylinder artifacts. It serves as a comprehensive record of the experimental conditions and the resulting dimensional data, facilitating the analysis of how different parameters influence the geometric characteristics of the measured drag cylinder specimens.

caption: Temperature contour map of the 100th layer at the final increment of the second preheating stage, assuming a neck ratio of 0.15 for partially sintered powder.
summary: This panel displays the temperature at the 100th layer during the final increment prior to melting. The temperature, denoted as θ PH2, serves as a measurable parameter for monitoring pre-heating consistency. The square area above the previously melted region exhibits a slightly lower temperature value compared to the insulated center.

caption: t-SNE visualization of features extracted from the first convolutional layer.
summary: This panel displays the t-SNE visualization of features extracted from the first convolutional layer of the CNN. Analysis of the plot reveals that the signal remains in a disordered state at this initial stage, exhibiting no distinct clustering characteristics or organized patterns within the feature space.

caption: Comparison of experimental fatigue life versus predicted fatigue life using the FS model for in-phase (IP) and out-of-phase (OP) loading conditions across various strain amplitudes.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the FS model by comparing experimental fatigue life data against model predictions. The results encompass both in-phase and out-of-phase loading conditions tested at multiple strain amplitudes, providing a comprehensive assessment of the model's performance in capturing fatigue behavior under diverse cyclic loading scenarios.

caption: Qualitative assessment of printability, needle clogging, and cytotoxicity for GelMA 7.5% hydrogels across different nHA concentrations.
summary: This table summarizes the performance of GelMA 7.5% bioinks with varying nHA concentrations. It highlights that 0.1% and 0.2% nHA concentrations facilitate stable filament extrusion with minimal needle clogging, whereas higher concentrations like 0.5% and 1% lead to frequent clogging and impaired structural coherence during 3D printing.

caption: Radial graph illustrating the comparative performance scores of six distinct samples based on representative evaporative cooling parameters.
summary: This radial graph displays the performance scores of six different samples across several representative parameters. By visualizing these metrics simultaneously, the plot facilitates the identification of the specific channel configuration that provides the highest evaporative cooling effect, serving as a decision-making tool for selecting the optimal material sample for cooling applications.

caption: Evolution of recovery strain and residual strain over 10 compression cycles for the NiTi micropillar from zone I.
summary: This plot quantifies the recovery and residual strain accumulation for the zone I micropillar. The data shows a relatively small residual strain, confirming the material's ability to maintain structural integrity and recover effectively during cyclic loading, which is a key characteristic of zone I.

caption: Detailed technical drawing of the tensile specimen geometry, specifying the dimensions required for uniaxial tensile testing in accordance with ASTM E8 standards.
summary: The technical drawing provides the standardized dimensions for the tensile specimens used in the study. By adhering to ASTM E8 guidelines, the geometry ensures that the uniaxial tensile tests yield reliable and comparable mechanical data, facilitating accurate assessment of the material properties derived from the CW-GMA wall specimens.

caption: Molten pool dimensions, specifically length (L) and width (W), plotted against varying linear energy densities, showing values of 87±3 μm width and 98±4 μm length at 205 J/m, and 95±5 μm width and 109±7 μm length at 270 J/m.
summary: This plot quantifies the geometric evolution of the molten pool by tracking length and width as a function of linear energy density. Specific measurements confirm that increasing the energy input from 205 J/m to 270 J/m results in a measurable expansion of both the width and length dimensions.

caption: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan results across the centre zone on the Ti64 side.
summary: This energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy line scan illustrates the elemental distribution across the centre zone on the Ti64 side. The results demonstrate that the carbon content in the TiC is approximately 10%, which is significantly lower than that observed in traditional bonding methods, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

caption: Neutron diffraction pattern for the IF+ST disc at position P2 showing axial θ0 peak deviation.
summary: Panel (h) displays the neutron diffraction pattern at position P2 of the IF+ST disc. The axial θ0 measurement shows a maximum peak deviation of less than or equal to 0.01°. This result supports the investigation into how microstructural characteristics affect measurement uncertainty across different disc locations.

caption: Crack length as a function of laser energy input for test artifacts produced from dry (black circles) and humidified (red triangles) powders.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between laser energy input and crack length in printed artifacts. Comparing dry and humidified powders reveals that moisture exposure leads to increased crack lengths. This demonstrates the detrimental effect of powder moisture on the crack resistance of the printed material during the manufacturing process.

caption: Phase distribution map of TiAl/TiB2 composite processed at a scan speed corresponding to 80 μm spacing.
summary: Panel (e) displays the phase composition of TiAl/TiB2 composites at a scan spacing of 80 μm. The color-coded map identifies α2 (yellow), γ (blue), B2 (red), and TiB2 (green) phases, illustrating the microstructural state resulting from this specific processing parameter.

caption: Microhardness profile plotted as a function of distance along the deposition direction for the titanium-based coatings.
summary: The microhardness profile along the deposition direction is presented in this plot. By measuring hardness values across the coating thickness, the data illustrates the mechanical property distribution relative to the deposition process, providing insight into the uniformity and strength characteristics of the coatings as they are built up.

caption: Contour plot depicting the influence of laser power and hatch distance on the area fraction of crack defects observed in LPBF-processed specimens.
summary: This plot maps the semi-quantitative area fraction of crack defects relative to laser power and hatch distance. By utilizing these metrics to compare defect trends across different LPBF parameter sets, the visualization highlights the sensitivity of crack formation to specific processing conditions within the experimental design space.

caption: Three-dimensional computer-aided design models illustrating the geometry of thin-walled type A1 and thick-walled type A2 scaffolds, shown in both lateral and frontal orientations.
summary: Three-dimensional models depict the structural design of thin-walled type A1 and thick-walled type A2 scaffolds. These models provide a clear visualization of the scaffold geometry from both lateral and frontal perspectives, serving as the basis for the subsequent 3D-printed physical structures and their internal micro-channel configurations.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves comparing as-printed recipe 1p (red solid line) with 1p after 2 hours of scCO2 extraction at 140 bars and 40 °C (red dotted line), highlighting degradation steps for ECC (green) and PEG400 (purple).
summary: This TGA plot evaluates the effectiveness of scCO2 extraction on recipe 1p. The comparison between as-printed and extracted samples reveals a significant reduction in the ECC degradation step, indicated in green. This confirms that the majority of the ECC content is successfully removed during the initial 2 hours of extraction.

caption: 3D atom probe tomography (APT) reconstruction of Al24.6Co24.6Cr24.6Fe24.6Zr1.5 heat treated at 700 °C (973 K) for 4 hours.
summary: This panel displays the 3D APT reconstruction of Al24.6Co24.6Cr24.6Fe24.6Zr1.5 after heat treatment at 700 °C for 4 hours. The map provides detailed insight into the atomic-scale structure and chemical distribution, which is vital for understanding the thermal stability and hardening mechanisms of the alloy coatings under elevated temperature conditions.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the MoNbTaZr-Ti system, illustrating the miscibility gap of the bcc solid-solution phase with a maximum temperature of 898 K.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram for the MoNbTaZr-Ti system illustrates the miscibility gap of the bcc solid-solution phase. Thermodynamic calculations indicate a maximum miscibility gap temperature of 898 K for the equiatomic TiNbTaZrMo alloy, demonstrating the phase separation behavior within this specific compositional range of the high-entropy alloy system.

caption: Equilibrium solidification diagram of Ti6Al4V5Cr alloy illustrating the temperature-dependent phase fraction changes.
summary: Equilibrium solidification diagram of Ti6Al4V5Cr alloy depicts the temperature-dependent phase fractions. The β-Ti phase begins forming at 1875 K, while the α-Ti phase starts to form at 1145 K. By 500 K, the alloy reaches a 0.88 mol fraction of α-Ti and a 0.04 mol fraction of β-Ti.

caption: Immunohistochemical analysis visualizing CD3+ T cell infiltration and EGFR expression persistence in tumor tissues.
summary: Immunohistochemical analysis was utilized to visualize CD3+ T cell infiltration and EGFR expression levels within tumor tissues. Comparative observations revealed that the EGFR-CAR-T group exhibited higher CD3+ lymphocyte infiltration and significantly reduced EGFR expression in tumor cells compared to the control group, highlighting the therapeutic impact of the treatment.

caption: Evolution of the strain range as a function of the number of load cycles (N), highlighting the progression of cyclic softening in the tested specimens.
summary: The plot illustrates the variation of the strain range versus the number of load cycles. It reveals distinct cyclic softening behaviors, noting that continuous softening occurs in hexagonal lattices, whereas triangular lattices exhibit softening only during the final stages of the high-cycle fatigue test process.

caption: SEM compositional map of the wall top area processed with UHPF current, showing dendritic core and edge regions.
summary: This SEM compositional map illustrates the top area of the wall processed with UHPF current. Point scans performed in the white dendritic core and orange dendritic edge regions demonstrate chemical segregation. The dendritic core contains higher concentrations of Ti and Nb, whereas the dendritic edge shows higher Al and Cr content.

caption: Elongation percentage plotted against yield strength for Al 6061-T6 alloys fabricated via conventional manufacturing and additive manufacturing processes.
summary: This Ashby plot compares the mechanical performance of Al 6061-T6 alloys, specifically plotting elongation against yield strength. It highlights the differences between conventional manufacturing and additive manufacturing techniques. Notably, binder-jetted materials exhibit significantly lower elongation values compared to extruded counterparts, such as the 17% elongation observed in conventional Al6061-T6.

caption: Vickers hardness HV10 values of H11/Cu composite materials plotted as a function of filament feed rate and extrusion temperature.
summary: This panel illustrates the global hardness of H11/Cu composite materials, specifically showing how Vickers hardness HV10 varies according to the printing parameters used for the preform green part. The data highlights the relationship between the extrusion temperature and filament feed rate in determining the final mechanical hardness of the composite.

caption: EDS elemental map of Vanadium (V) distribution within the 10 wt% TiC/Ti6Al4V composite microstructure.
summary: This EDS map illustrates the distribution of Vanadium in the composite sample. By visualizing the V-content, the map helps identify elemental partitioning between the Ti6Al4V matrix and the TiC reinforcement, providing a clear view of how alloying elements are distributed relative to the reinforcing phases.

caption: TEM micrograph of the D region in the HT-1 sample after stress fracture at 760 °C/800 MPa, viewed along the [11-2] zone axis.
summary: This TEM micrograph displays the D region of the HT-1 sample following stress fracture at 760 °C/800 MPa. The image, captured along the [11-2] zone axis, reveals a high density of black stripe-like microstructures, which exhibit contrasts similar to those observed in micro-twins and continuous stacking faults.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) curves comparing hydrogen release behavior between as-built and solution-treated SLM-718 alloy specimens after 24 hours of hydrogen charging.
summary: TDS analyses were conducted on the as-built and solution-treated SLM-718 alloy specimens after 24 hours of hydrogen charging to evaluate the impact of solution treatment on hydrogen trapping behavior. The resulting curves provide a quantitative comparison of hydrogen desorption characteristics across the different microstructural conditions investigated in the study.

caption: QR code representation derived from the pore distance matrix for sample 20.
summary: Sample 20 is encoded into a QR code format based on its unique pore distance matrix. This approach simplifies the management of material identifiers, enabling efficient integration into component documentation and allowing users to quickly scan and access the underlying structural information using standard mobile devices.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the correlation factors for seven geometric parameters affecting the total mass of the support arm.
summary: Presented as a bar plot, this sensitivity analysis highlights the correlation factors of seven geometric parameters relative to the support arm's mass. The visualization effectively quantifies how individual design variables contribute to mass variations, facilitating a deeper understanding of the structural trade-offs identified through the efficient automated simulation process.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of submicron particles, revealing spherical features that suggest the presence of nanometric precipitates formed during material processing.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of submicron particles reveals distinct spherical features. These observations suggest that a small fraction of nanometric precipitates may already form during the processing stage. The image provides structural evidence of these particles, which are further analyzed for their elemental composition in subsequent compositional mapping panels.

caption: Normalized AESEC dissolution profiles and potential evolution for Al-3at.%Mg exposed to 50 mM NaNO3 at 50°C and pH 4.0.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical dissolution behavior of Al-3at.%Mg in a 50 mM NaNO3 solution at 50°C and pH 4.0. The plot tracks the normalized dissolution rates alongside the potential evolution over time, providing insights into the material's stability and corrosion kinetics under these specific environmental conditions.

caption: Energy barrier for the migration of interstitial complexes in Cu–Ni alloys, plotted against composition using split violin plots to differentiate between various migration mechanisms.
summary: This panel depicts the migration energy barriers for interstitial complexes in Cu–Ni alloys. By utilizing split violin plots, the figure effectively distinguishes between different migration mechanisms occurring at intermediate compositions. The mean and standard deviation lines summarize the energetic landscape for interstitial diffusion as the alloy composition is varied.

caption: Three-dimensional CAD model depicting the volumetric structure and critical spatial dimensions of the printed SS and CP samples.
summary: Representing the three-dimensional design, this CAD model details the volumetric configuration of the SS and CP samples. It complements the two-dimensional view by defining the spatial extent and critical dimensions, providing a comprehensive geometric reference for the printed samples utilized throughout the experimental work described in this study.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the LPBFed ALO7.5 sample, illustrating the dense dislocation network within the CoCrNi matrix and the distribution of Al2O3 particles.
summary: This BF-STEM image of the ALO7.5 sample reveals an extensive distribution of dislocations within the CoCrNi matrix. The microstructure analysis highlights the morphology and distribution of internal precipitate particles, which tend to aggregate at the boundaries of the cellular structure, confirming the presence of Al2O3 particles within the matrix.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the corrosion behavior of SLMed Ti–6Al–4V and ODL samples in PBS solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves reveal that the ODL sample exhibits a significantly more positive corrosion potential (Ecorr = 24 ± 12 mV vs. Ag/AgCl) compared to the SLMed Ti–6Al–4V sample (-411 ± 7 mV vs. Ag/AgCl). This shift indicates superior corrosion resistance, likely attributed to the presence of the β phase.

caption: Bright-field TEM cross-sectional image of the Ti0.34Al0.66N coating after 15 hours of oxidation at 700 °C, revealing the overall structural integrity and layer morphology.
summary: This bright-field TEM cross-section displays the Ti0.34Al0.66N coating following a 15-hour oxidation treatment at 700 °C. The image provides a comprehensive view of the coating's structural state during the propagation stage of oxidation, serving as a baseline for identifying the distinct microstructural zones formed within the material.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram for the Ni-H2O-H2 system, mapping the stable phases of nickel in the presence of hydrogen and water vapor.
summary: This phase diagram maps the thermodynamic stability of nickel species within a H2O-H2 system. By evaluating the equilibrium conditions, it provides a visual representation of the stable phases for nickel, serving as a comparative baseline for understanding the corrosion resistance of nickel-based alloys in high-pressure steam environments.

caption: XPS valence state spectrum of the Ce element in Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA, showing a mixture of Ce3+ (50.11%) and Ce4+ (49.89%).
summary: XPS analysis of the Ce element in Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA reveals a surface composition consisting of 50.11% Ce3+ and 49.89% Ce4+. This valence state distribution provides critical insight into the chemical environment of the cerium coating, confirming the successful deposition and oxidation state of the cerium species.

caption: Weibull fracture probability plot of compressive strength for LIS samples sintered in a simulated Martian atmosphere at 1180°C for 3 hours.
summary: Shown is the Weibull fracture probability plot for LIS samples sintered in a simulated Martian atmosphere at 1180°C for 3 hours. By evaluating the characteristic compressive strength, this plot identifies statistically robust trends in the mechanical behavior of LIS ceramics when subjected to the specific Martian atmospheric sintering environment.

caption: R2 score distribution across seven machine learning models, illustrating the explanatory power of each algorithm.
summary: This box plot displays the R2 score distribution for seven machine learning models. It serves as a key metric for evaluating the explanatory power of each model, providing a comparative overview of how well the different algorithms capture the variance within the dataset during the performance evaluation process.

caption: In-phase rotation of oxygen octahedra represented by the Q R + mode with M 2 + irrep symmetry.
summary: This panel illustrates the in-phase rotation of oxygen octahedra, identified as the Q R + mode with M 2 + irrep symmetry. This structural distortion serves as one of the participating modes in the trilinear coupling mechanism that establishes the polar ground state of the material system.

caption: Elemental distribution map (wt%) of the thin inner oxide area shown in panel (c), identifying the presence of Mn-enriched particles.
summary: The elemental map (wt%) for the thin inner oxide region reveals the spatial distribution of elements. Notably, Mn-enriched particles are identified at the same level as the segregation line. This map complements the structural data from panel (c), highlighting the specific chemical features present in the thin inner oxide layer.

caption: Four-microphone impedance tube configuration illustrating the placement of Mic 1, Mic 2, Mic 3, and Mic 4 for energy dissipation analysis.
summary: The four-microphone impedance tube configuration utilizes four sensors to analyze sound wave components. Based on the ASTM E2611 standard and transfer matrix methods, this setup allows for the calculation of energy dissipation, wavenumber, and sound speed within absorptive materials by evaluating incident and reflected wave fractions.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image of the 15-5PH sample microstructure.
summary: This high-resolution TEM image provides a detailed view of the 15-5PH sample microstructure. By capturing atomic-scale features, this visualization allows for the investigation of the martensitic phase and its associated structural characteristics, which are essential for understanding the material's properties following the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Layout illustrating the specific positioning and spatial orientation of the test samples within the WAAM-fabricated structure.
summary: Panel b displays the spatial arrangement and positioning of the test samples extracted from the WAAM-fabricated component. This schematic serves to define the orientation and location of the specimens, ensuring consistency in the experimental procedure and providing a reference for the subsequent mechanical testing of the material.

caption: Relative feature importance estimates for the Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) model trained on Class A micro-droplet dispensers, expressed as a percentage of the total importance.
summary: This panel depicts the feature importance for the GBM model trained on Class A micro-droplet dispensers. The importance values are normalized as a percentage of the whole, allowing for a clear assessment of the relative influence of various features on the GBM algorithm's decision-making process for the dispensers.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the three stainless steel samples, with corrosion potential and current density values derived via Tafel extrapolation.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves demonstrate the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the three 316L-4.5Cu stainless steel samples. Key electrochemical parameters, specifically the free corrosion potential and corrosion current density, were quantitatively determined using the Tafel extrapolation method to assess the relative corrosion performance of the different as-fabricated antibacterial stainless steel specimens.

caption: Overall layout of the self-developed mechanical seal test device, highlighting the integration of the power transmission system, pumping station, experimental bench, sealing chamber, and sensors.
summary: The overall diagram displays the self-developed mechanical seal test device, which integrates a power and transmission system, a pumping station, an experimental bench, a sealing chamber, and various sensors. This comprehensive setup is designed to facilitate rigorous testing of mechanical seals under controlled conditions over a 30-minute loading period.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles at 0.5 mA cm⁻² for three micro-supercapacitors connected in series compared to a single device, illustrating the expanded voltage window.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge testing at 0.5 mA cm⁻² shows the performance of three micro-supercapacitors connected in series versus a single unit. The series connection effectively expands the operating voltage window from 0.8 V for a single device to 2.4 V, demonstrating the scalability of the device architecture.

caption: Peeling testing data showing the typical force-displacement curve and the calculated peeling strength between the cartilage and subchondral layers, demonstrating values comparable to native osteochondral tissue.
summary: Panel c characterizes the interfacial adhesion through peeling testing. It displays the typical peeling curve and reports a peeling strength of 212 N/m, which aligns with the range observed in native osteochondral tissue. Similar to the shear tests, fractures were observed in the cartilage region rather than the interface.

caption: Minimum creep rate comparison for the PBF-LB/M data set, plotting experimental results as solid lines against simulated values derived from elongated Voronoi RVEs as dashed lines.
summary: This panel displays the minimum creep rate for the PBF-LB/M data set, comparing experimental data with simulated predictions using elongated Voronoi RVEs.
