The plot incorporates three combined effects to evaluate the accuracy of the simulation against experimental observations, demonstrating the relationship between the measured and modeled creep behavior.

caption: Dilatometric sintering profiles comparing ceramic VPP samples before (black line) and after (red line) scCO2 extraction, illustrating the thermal expansion and shrinkage behavior used to optimize sintering parameters.
summary: This dilatometry plot displays the sintering behavior of ceramic VPP samples, contrasting the thermal response of untreated (black) and scCO2-extracted (red) specimens. These measurements were essential for determining the appropriate sintering temperature and duration required to achieve the desired material properties during the ceramic processing phase.

caption: Pyrometric image representing the maximum emission signal plotted on a 20.20 µm grid, where changes in mean signal intensity qualitatively correspond to different laser parameter settings.
summary: The pyrometric heatmap displays the maximum emission signal recorded for each laser position on a 20.20 µm grid. Variations in the mean signal intensity across different hatch blocks qualitatively reflect changes in laser parameters. Despite minor aliasing, the data effectively correlates signal changes with the surface defects observed in optical imaging.

caption: Transmittance values measured at 405 nm for A-CNC/CTFA composite resins, showing the evolution of optical clarity with increasing acrylation reaction time.
summary: Transmittance at 405 nm for the A-CNC/CTFA composite resin is plotted against acrylation reaction time. The data indicates that as the acrylation reaction time increases, the transparency of the composite resin progressively improves, reaching values up to 93%, which confirms the positive impact of the reaction on optical clarity.

caption: Formalloy L2 direct energy deposition system utilized for the additive manufacturing of the functionally graded material block.
summary: This panel displays the Formalloy L2 direct energy deposition system used to manufacture the functionally graded material block. The equipment is shown in its operational configuration, highlighting the hardware setup required for the additive manufacturing process employed to create the graded specimen described in the study.

caption: Clamp load versus time plot for homogenous screw trials, illustrating the force retention characteristics during vibration testing.
summary: The graph shows the clamp load decay over time for homogenous screw trials under vibration. By comparing these results to the architected screw trials, the effectiveness of the screw design in maintaining clamp load during mechanical agitation can be directly assessed and quantified.

caption: In-situ FT-IR spectra of CC showing the evolution of functional groups during pyrolysis.
summary: In-situ FT-IR spectra of CC demonstrate the thermal degradation process. The intensity of the –OH vibrational peak at approximately 3430 cm−1 decreases with increasing temperature until it disappears. Furthermore, methyl and methylene bonds undergo significant degradation at temperatures ranging from 250 to 300 °C during the pyrolysis process.

caption: Arc shape of the SCA at an increased ion gas flow rate, resulting in a further decline of both the deflection angle to 4.2 degrees and the SCA width to 4.2 mm.
summary: Panel (e) depicts the arc shape of the SCA under higher ion gas flow conditions. Both the deflection angle and the width of the PMA continue to decline, reaching measured values of 4.2 degrees and 4.2 mm, respectively, highlighting the ongoing impact of increased gas flow rates.

caption: Particle size distribution of the as-received LW 4275 feedstock powder, showing characteristic D10, D50, and D90 values of 12 µm, 24 µm, and 41 µm, respectively.
summary: The particle size distribution of the LW 4275 feedstock powder is presented, highlighting the D10, D50, and D90 values of 12 µm, 24 µm, and 41 µm. These metrics are critical for understanding the starting material characteristics, which significantly influence the final part density, mechanical properties, and surface quality in LPBF processes.

caption: STEM-BF micrograph of the HT700/1 condition along the [001] zone axis, showing more defined cell walls compared to the HT450/4 condition, with some evidence of wall dissolution.
summary: This STEM-BF micrograph of the HT700/1 condition, oriented along the [001] zone axis, displays more defined cell walls than the HT450/4 condition. While the cellular structure remains visible, red arrows indicate areas where some walls appear to have already dissolved, marking a distinct difference in structural sharpness.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine (BBZ) monomer, illustrating characteristic absorbance peaks associated with the successful formation of the oxazine ring structure.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of the synthesized bio-based benzoxazine monomer confirms the successful preparation of the material. The observed absorbance peaks provide critical evidence for the formation of the oxazine ring, validating the chemical synthesis process as previously detailed in established literature regarding BBZ monomer preparation.

caption: Bright field TEM image and corresponding FFT pattern of the region with <1% equivalent strain.
summary: This bright field TEM image and its corresponding FFT pattern illustrate the microstructure in a region with minimal deformation. The precipitates exhibit a relatively homogeneous spatial distribution, similar to the highly deformed region, providing a baseline for comparing the microstructural effects of the cross-die forming process at 180 °C.

caption: Final reference component captured after the completion of the hat-shape forming process.
summary: The reference component is shown following the completion of the forming process. The part exhibits the characteristic hat-shape geometry, which includes a 95-degree angle between the bottom and sidewalls. This final product demonstrates the successful application of the modular forming tool design and the effectiveness of the thermal isolation strategy.

caption: Three-dimensional iso-concentration surfaces highlighting Fe-rich, Cr-rich, and Ni-Mn-Si-rich regions in ferrite after 50 hours of aging at 400 °C.
summary: After 50 hours of aging, this APT reconstruction reveals the progression of spinodal decomposition within the ferrite phase. The visualization clearly distinguishes between Fe-rich and Cr-rich phases, while simultaneously capturing the emergence of distinct clusters enriched with Ni, Mn, and Si, indicating a significant evolution in the material's microstructural composition.

caption: Simulated particle size distribution histogram for 316L stainless steel powder, derived from experimental measurements.
summary: This histogram displays the simulated particle size distribution of 316L stainless steel powder. The distribution is generated based on experimental measurements of the powder, providing a representative model of the particle sizes. This data is presented to characterize the powder morphology used in the study as shown in Fig. 2.

caption: Thermodynamic CCT diagram for Cu5 steel computed via JMatPro, highlighting the specific phase transformation kinetics and boundaries for this alloy composition.
summary: The CCT curve for Cu5 steel is presented here, calculated using JMatPro software to elucidate the thermodynamic phase characteristics. This diagram allows for a detailed analysis of how the specific composition of Cu5 steel influences its phase transformation pathways during cooling compared to other steel variants.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for the ZrO2 powder.
summary: Particle size distribution histogram for the ZrO2 powder. This plot presents the statistical distribution of the ZrO2 microparticles, which possess an average size ranging from 10 to 50 μm. The histogram provides essential quantitative data regarding the particle size variation within the microparticle sample shown in the SEM image.

caption: Marginal P-S-N curves presented on an S-N plot, showing the relationship between stress amplitude and fatigue life alongside experimental data points.
summary: The marginal P-S-N curves are plotted on an S-N diagram to characterize fatigue performance. These curves incorporate experimental data to define the fatigue life behavior. The constant coefficients for these curves were determined using the least square method, providing a statistical representation of the fatigue failure trends observed in the material.

caption: Relative importance of various features utilized for predicting dimensional deviations in the x, y, and z directions, presented from left to right.
summary: This feature importance plot identifies the critical parameters influencing the prediction of dimensional deviations across the x, y, and z axes. By ranking these features, the visualization highlights which variables most significantly impact the accuracy of the S2 printer system's output, providing insight into the primary drivers of dimensional error.

caption: Markforged Sinter-1 furnace interface screen displaying operational parameters.
summary: This panel displays the Markforged Sinter-1 furnace control screen, which is used to manage the sintering process. The interface provides the necessary digital controls and monitoring capabilities required to execute the specific thermal cycles needed for processing metallic components like AISI H13 steel within the sintering environment.

caption: (0001) pole figure showing the crystallographic orientation distribution of grains in region B of the T4 cross-sectional sample.
summary: The (0001) pole figure for region B provides a visual representation of the crystallographic texture in the T4 cross-sectional sample. By analyzing the orientation of the grains, this plot helps characterize the structural properties of the material in region B, supporting the overall assessment of the T4 state.

caption: Schematic representation of the fused deposition modeling (FDM) additive manufacturing process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental workflow of the fused deposition modeling (FDM) additive manufacturing process. It serves as a visual guide to the sequential steps involved in the fabrication technique, providing a clear overview of how materials are processed and deposited to form the final structure during manufacturing.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern confirming the polycrystalline nature of the PtFe alloy.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern demonstrates that the synthesized PtFe alloy is polycrystalline. The diffraction rings correspond to the (110), (100), and (111) planes of the Pt crystal structure, confirming the successful formation of the alloy phase and the retention of the underlying platinum-based crystal lattice.

caption: Transmitted spectral signal of the uncoated AN-PMMA-FOS sensor under maximal point force application.
summary: This plot displays the spectral response of a pure PMMA fiber optic sensor without any coating. The signal represents the maximal spectral intensity recorded before mechanical breakdown. Comparison with coated sensors reveals fundamental differences in spectral shape, highlighting the baseline performance of the uncoated PMMA fiber under mechanical stress.

caption: Three-dimensional surface contour image of the wear track on the A4 sample, illustrating the morphology of the abrasion marks.
summary: Three-dimensional contours of the wear tracks were generated to visualize the surface morphology following friction testing. For the A4 sample, the 3D image provides a detailed representation of the abrasion marks, facilitating the analysis of wear mechanisms and surface damage patterns resulting from the reciprocating friction wear test.

caption: Cross-sectional slice of the ST1 sample highlighting a vertical crack encountering a curved interface and undergoing kinking and trapping.
summary: Captured in this cross-sectional view, the vertical crack propagation within the ST1 sample is shown as it encounters a curved interface. The image demonstrates the crack's behavior as it propagates along the interface, subsequently undergoing kinking and trapping, which illustrates the effectiveness of the architected paths in controlling fracture development.

caption: Property diagram of the Ti1.4Nb0.6Ta0.6Zr1.4Mo0.6 alloy showing the volume fraction of constituent phases as a function of temperature under equilibrium conditions.
summary: This property diagram, generated via Thermo-Calc software, illustrates the equilibrium phase evolution of the Ti1.4Nb0.6Ta0.6Zr1.4Mo0.6 alloy. It displays the volume fraction of constituent phases as a function of temperature, providing a thermodynamic basis for understanding the phase separation behavior observed in the alloy during cooling processes.

caption: In-situ BSE-SEM micrograph of the upper specimen area at a controlled displacement of 595 μm, highlighting initial slip traces within grains marked by yellow lines.
summary: This in-situ BSE-SEM micrograph captures the upper region of the TLM alloy specimen during bending at a 595 μm displacement. The image reveals the early stages of deformation, specifically identifying slip traces that manifest as dark features within the grains, which are highlighted with yellow lines for clarity.

caption: Phase angle response of coated 3D-printed electrodes across a frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 10 kHz, measured in a 1 mol KOH solution.
summary: The phase angle response of the coated 3D-printed electrodes is illustrated across a frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 10 kHz. These electrochemical measurements were conducted in a 1 mol KOH solution to characterize the impedance behavior of the printed material under standard testing conditions.

caption: Implementation roadmap for Digital Shadow (DS), Augmented Reality (AR), and real-time smart dashboards within an intelligent Hybrid Additive Manufacturing (HAM) system.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the strategic implementation roadmap for integrating Digital Shadow, Augmented Reality, and real-time smart dashboards into a HAM system. These components are supported by high-precision sensors, robust database architectures, and advanced interface development tools, which collectively establish the foundation for a seamlessly integrated and intelligent manufacturing environment.

caption: Sequential processing steps for powder preparation including mixing, preloading, spark plasma sintering, hot diffusion, and hot rolling.
summary: This schematic illustrates the sequential experimental processing route applied to the powders. The procedure involves thorough mixing followed by preloading, spark plasma sintering (SPS), hot diffusion, and finally hot rolling to achieve the desired material state before further characterization or specimen preparation for mechanical testing.

caption: Electron probe micro-analysis elemental distribution map highlighting the presence and spatial arrangement of Tungsten (W) within the powder mixture.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis results for Tungsten are presented to illustrate the elemental distribution within the W-3.5TaC powder mixture. This map confirms the spatial arrangement of the primary metallic component, providing critical data on the homogeneity of the mixed powder feedstock used for subsequent laser powder bed fusion fabrication.

caption: Photocurrent response as a function of reverse bias voltage under 1-mW 532-nm laser excitation, with an inset displaying logarithmic-scale I-V curves across varying excitation intensities.
summary: This I-V curve illustrates the photocurrent behavior under 1-mW 532-nm laser excitation. The inset highlights logarithmic-scale responses under different intensities, showing deformations at high excitation levels. Notable increases in photocurrent at 1, 3.5, 8.5, 12.5, and 17 V indicate the emergence of new electron transport paths within the device.

caption: Representative neutron diffraction patterns comparing bulk (solid boxes) and interface (dashed boxes) regions for 3.5 mm (green) and 6 mm (red) spot sizes.
summary: Representative diffraction patterns reveal peak broadening at the interface regions for both 3.5 mm and 6 mm spot size walls, indicating variations in residual strain or microstructure. These patterns, collected from specific extraction locations, allow for a comparative analysis of strain states between the bulk and interleaved interface zones.

caption: Acoustic emission (AE) activity recorded during the fracture toughness test of specimen A2, illustrating the temporal evolution of AE counts and the determination of the crack extension onset.
summary: Acoustic emission activity for specimen A2 is monitored during a fracture toughness test. The data shows a noticeably less intense AE response at the beginning of the test compared to specimen A1. This recording is utilized to determine the specific onset of crack extension during the mechanical loading process.

caption: Magnetization as a function of the applied magnetic field at 2 K, illustrating the magnetic response of the HAA single crystal. Insets provide a visual representation of the HAA single crystal specimen and a magnified view of the low-field magnetization behavior.
summary: Magnetic field-dependent magnetization at 2 K characterizes the HAA single crystal's response to external fields. The main plot displays the M-H behavior, while the included insets offer a physical perspective of the single crystal sample and a detailed examination of the low-field region, highlighting specific magnetic properties of the material.

caption: Schematic representation of the 3D EAC unit cell constructed by stacking five 2D EAC unit cells in a perpendicular arrangement.
summary: The 3D EAC unit cell is depicted as a complex assembly formed by stacking five 2D EAC unit cells arranged perpendicularly. This schematic representation highlights the spatial configuration and connectivity of the unit cell, which is essential for understanding the overall architecture and mechanical behavior of the 3D metastructure.

caption: Delta tan (tan δ) curves plotted against temperature for pure PLA and PLA-sea urchin powder bio-composites, illustrating the loss coefficient behavior of the materials.
summary: The tan δ curves presented in this panel illustrate the loss coefficient behavior of pure PLA and PLA-sea urchin powder bio-composites as a function of temperature. These results, used alongside storage modulus data, characterize the dynamic response of the polymer matrix and the specific influence of the mineral reinforcement on the material.

caption: Higher magnification SEM micrograph of the coarse melt pool (CMP) region, revealing fine particles and elongated needle-like Si precipitates.
summary: At higher magnification, this SEM image of the CMP region reveals two distinct precipitate morphologies: fine particles and elongated needle-like structures. These features suggest a heterogeneous nucleation and growth process influenced by the as-built microstructure, while the underlying Si cellular framework remains preserved following the heat treatment.

caption: Periodic metamaterial architecture and its corresponding representative unit cell.
summary: This panel illustrates the periodic metamaterial structure and the representative unit cell used to characterize its effective material responses. By analyzing this unit cell, researchers can determine the macroscopic behavior of the periodic metamaterial, providing a fundamental basis for understanding the overall mechanical and magnetic properties of the designed system.

caption: Network visualization of keyword density and temporal evolution in reviewed literature, where node color intensity represents the publication year.
summary: This network visualization displays the most frequently used keywords in reviewed papers, with node color indicating temporal trends. Darker nodes represent keywords prevalent around 2010, while lighter nodes highlight recent research topics. The analysis identifies genetic algorithms and optimization as key themes, pointing toward emerging applications in aerospace weight optimization.

caption: Hardness and mechanical strength values of as-built samples plotted against varying layer thickness.
summary: Hardness and mechanical strength of as-built samples are presented in this plot. The data reveals that hardness and relative density exhibit similar variation patterns, characterized by a trend that initially increases and subsequently decreases as the layer thickness of the samples is increased during the fabrication process.

caption: Time-lapse sequence capturing the motion process of the spiral robot at a 5 cm distance and 120 r/min rotational speed.
summary: This panel documents the specific motion process of the spiral robot. Captured at a distance of 5 cm with a rotational speed of 120 r/min, the sequence provides a visual record of the robot's locomotion, demonstrating its operational capability and movement characteristics under defined experimental parameters.

caption: Y3d XPS spectra for GARS processed material, showing experimental data and peak fitting for samples etched at 0 nm and 50 nm depths.
summary: The Y3d XPS spectra for GARS material are presented for etching depths of 0 nm and 50 nm. Experimental data in black is compared against red peak fits. The analysis reveals the presence of yttrium carbonate at 158.7 eV, indicating Y2O3 surface absorption of atmospheric CO2.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) curves comparing the viscoelastic properties of GB and SB samples under heating and dynamic loading, specifically showing storage modulus (E′), loss modulus (E″), and tan δ.
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) curves compare the viscoelastic properties of GB and SB samples under heating and dynamic loading. The SB sample exhibits higher and shifted values in E′ and E″, indicating a delayed glass transition and α-relaxation. Furthermore, the shifted tan δ peak suggests reduced mechanical damping for the SB sample.

caption: Schematic representation of the Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) unit cell architecture.
summary: This panel displays a schematic representation of the Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) unit cell architecture. The illustration provides a fundamental geometric overview of the repeating structural unit that defines the lattice, serving as the basis for the subsequent mechanical assessment of the manufactured TPMS lattice structures.

caption: Quasi-static compressive force-displacement curve for a PLA sample with a 0.6 mm wall thickness.
summary: Illustrated here is the quasi-static compressive force-displacement curve for a re-entrant PLA sample featuring a 0.6 mm wall thickness. This plot captures the mechanical performance of the thicker PLA specimen under compression, serving as a basis for comparing deformation and force response against other sample geometries and material compositions.

caption: Output voltage profile over 1400 cycles demonstrating the long-term durability of the bio-inspired structure S2.
summary: The durability of the bio-inspired structure S2 is evaluated through a 1400-cycle output voltage test. The results demonstrate consistent performance over extended operation, confirming the structural robustness and reliability of the S2 design for long-term energy harvesting applications.

caption: Front top view of the post-treated porous cage after undergoing surface refinement processes.
summary: This image presents the front top view of the post-treated dense cage. The post-treatment process has successfully modified the initial LPBF-prepared structure, resulting in a dense cage configuration that demonstrates the effectiveness of the refinement steps applied to the porous metallic framework.

caption: HRTEM micrograph of a spherical Ti2(Ni, Cu) precipitate, featuring an inset FFT pattern corresponding to a [100]-oriented Ti2(Ni, Cu) matrix.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging of a spherical Ti2(Ni, Cu) precipitate is complemented by an inset FFT pattern. The FFT analysis confirms the [100] orientation of the Ti2(Ni, Cu) matrix. This structural characterization provides essential crystallographic information regarding the precipitate orientation relative to the surrounding matrix phase.

caption: Impedance spectra represented as Nyquist plots for the B10-0.1 wt% La alloy after exposure to a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution for different immersion times.
summary: This panel displays the Nyquist spectra for the B10-0.1 wt% La alloy exposed to a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The plots characterize the electrochemical impedance response of the lanthanum-modified alloy across various immersion durations, providing insight into the stability and corrosion resistance of the surface film over time.

caption: Schematic illustration of the laser exposure strategy applied to the active thermography sample, featuring a 11 x 11 mm rectangular measurement field with unidirectional scanning vectors oriented parallel to the x-axis.
summary: This schematic depicts the laser exposure strategy used for active thermography. The process involves scanning a 11 x 11 mm rectangular area with unidirectional vectors parallel to the x-axis. This specific path configuration facilitates a systematic line-by-line evaluation of pixels on the sensor during the measurement procedure.

caption: Nyquist plot illustrating the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) response for the S5-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion.
summary: This Nyquist plot shows the EIS data for the S5-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion. The analysis is part of a larger investigation into the corrosion resistance of SLMed TC4 alloys, utilizing equivalent circuit fitting to interpret the impedance data and evaluate the electrochemical behavior of the specimen.

caption: Voltage waveforms recorded at the target and substrate, showing a 50 μs HiPIMS discharge pulse and a 250 μs substrate pulse synchronized with a 1 μs delay.
summary: Voltage waveforms for the HiPIMS process are displayed, featuring a 50 μs discharge pulse and a 250 μs substrate pulse. These pulses are synchronized with a 1 μs delay to effectively accelerate ionized sputtered species toward the substrate during both the discharge phase and the subsequent plasma afterglow period.

caption: Magnified view of the XRD patterns focusing on the (111) and (200) diffraction peaks to observe structural variations.
summary: Enlarged XRD patterns specifically highlight the (111) and (200) peaks for the Invar 36 powders and the processed samples. This detailed view allows for a precise comparison of peak positions and intensities, which are essential for evaluating the crystal plane spacings and structural characteristics of the different material states.

caption: High-cycle fatigue SN curves comparing base metals A and B with weld metal at room and elevated temperatures.
summary: This panel displays high-cycle fatigue SN curves for base metals A and B, alongside weld metal tested at room and elevated temperatures. The data demonstrates that the weld metal exhibits significantly reduced fatigue strength compared to the base alloys, with further performance degradation observed at elevated service temperatures.

caption: Dimensional reduction representation of the integrated cell dataset, color-coded to highlight the progression of differentiation stages.
summary: Dimensional reduction via UMAP provides a clear representation of the 21 clusters identified in the sequencing data. By coloring the cells according to their differentiation stage, this plot illustrates the progression of the integrated dataset, facilitating the analysis of cellular transitions from early endoderm to mature pancreatic cell types.

caption: CAD model of the HC_SB lattice topology featuring hollow columns and solid beams at 30% relative density.
summary: Depicting the HC_SB lattice topology, this CAD model features hollow columns and solid beams within a simple cubic unit cell. With a 30% relative density, this design was produced using laser powder bed fusion to enable a comprehensive assessment of how these specific geometric parameters influence lattice structural performance.

caption: Recoverable strain plotted as a function of applied strain for various samples, highlighting that the 850 sample achieves a maximum recoverable strain of 2.5% due to its superior strength-ductility combination.
summary: Quantification of recoverable strain through elastic recovery and residual strain analysis shows the performance of different samples. The 850 sample stands out with a 2.5% recoverable strain, a value comparable to bulk Ni-free beta-type Ti alloys, demonstrating the effectiveness of the alloy's processing in achieving an outstanding strength-ductility combination.

caption: Comparison of strut dimensions for Cell 2 lattice structures fabricated from ZrO2 and HAp, with a reference line at the target design dimension of 160 μm.
summary: This box plot illustrates the distribution of strut dimensions for Cell 2 lattice specimens composed of ZrO2 and HAp. By comparing the measured dimensions against the red reference line representing the designed value of 160 μm, the plot highlights the dimensional accuracy and variability inherent in the fabrication of these specific lattice geometries.

caption: Fatigue strength at 10^6 cycles versus relative density for tensile-tested lattices, evaluated through nominal, effective, and normalized stress metrics.
summary: This plot evaluates fatigue strength at 10^6 cycles against relative density for tensile-tested lattices. HIP treatment is shown to induce a significant increase in fatigue properties compared to as-built, non-stress-relieved conditions. However, these improvements are less pronounced when the data is analyzed using normalized stress metrics.

caption: Multi-rate performance capabilities of three cells utilizing different separator configurations.
summary: Multi-rate performance capabilities of three cells with different separators are presented. During the discharge process, two distinct voltage plateaus are observed between 2.0 V and 2.1 V and between 2.2 V and 2.3 V, reflecting the rate-dependent electrochemical behavior and stability of the different separator systems.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves recorded over 100 cycles for the PEDOT:PSS/TPU/paracetamol:PLGA microparticle composite film.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry was employed to assess the electrical conductivity and electrochemical stability of the composite films. The 100 CV cycles demonstrate the performance of the material under repeated electrochemical stress, confirming the conductive polymer maintains its functional properties within the printed composite architecture.

caption: Load-displacement curves for samples D6 (grey), D7.5 (red), and D9 (blue), demonstrating a characteristic two-stage mechanical response.
summary: The load-displacement curves for samples D6, D7.5, and D9 are plotted to reveal their mechanical behavior. The data clearly exhibits a distinct two-stage trend during the compression test, allowing for a comparative analysis of the mechanical performance and deformation characteristics across the different sample types under investigation.

caption: Current-potential polarization curves for alloy 82 weld samples, including reference HT, cathodically hydrogen-precharged HT+H, and pre-exposed samples, measured in a 1200 ppm boric acid and 2.1 ppm lithium solution at 25 ℃ with a scan rate of 500 mV h−1.
summary: This polarization curve compares the electrochemical behavior of reference, hydrogen-precharged, and pre-exposed alloy 82 weld samples in a simulated PWR primary water environment. The results demonstrate how hydrogen introduction, either through cathodic charging or environmental pre-exposure, influences the corrosion behavior and passive film stability of the alloy 82 weld material.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating ramp thermograms illustrating the distinct thermal histories of the printed samples, highlighting an exothermic crystallization peak at 218°C and an endothermic melting peak at 336°C.
summary: DSC heating ramp profiles reveal the unique thermal histories of the 3D printed samples. The thermogram shows an exothermic crystallization peak at 218°C with an enthalpy of 22.5 J/g, followed by an endothermic melting peak at 336°C, which characterizes the thermal behavior and crystalline state of the polymer material.

caption: Loss versus epoch plot illustrating the training performance of the model.
summary: This plot displays the loss versus epoch analysis, providing a clear visualization of the model's training performance over time. By tracking the loss values across successive epochs, the graph serves as a learning curve to evaluate the convergence and stability of the machine learning model during the training process.

caption: Computed tomography images of the deposited TiAl sample, displaying internal structural features across selected XOY and YOZ cross-sectional planes.
summary: Computed tomography images of the deposited TiAl sample are presented, illustrating the internal structure of the material. Three distinct planes were extracted from both XOY and YOZ cross-sections to facilitate a detailed analysis of the deposited part's integrity and internal morphology.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of polycrystalline Pt electrodes in Ar-saturated 0.1 M HClO4, with Pt 5 Pr currents scaled by a factor of 10 for comparison.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms comparing Pt 5 Pr and polycrystalline Pt electrodes are shown in this panel. The currents for the Pt 5 Pr voltammogram are divided by 10 to facilitate a clearer comparison of the electrochemical features between the two electrode materials within the Ar-saturated 0.1 M HClO4 electrolyte.

caption: Creep strain versus time curves for S1A and S2A materials tested at 760 °C, showing that initial strain in S1A decreases with lower applied stress.
summary: This panel displays creep curves for S1A and S2A materials at 760 °C. The data illustrates the mechanical response of these alloys under varying stress conditions. Specifically, for the S1A material, the initial strain is observed to decrease as the applied stress is reduced during the creep test.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the LPBF-produced Al–Mg–Zr alloy microstructure, highlighting the region selected for elemental mapping.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the representative microstructure of the LPBF-produced Al–Mg–Zr alloy. A dashed rectangle marks the specific area chosen for subsequent EDS elemental mapping, providing a structural context for the distribution of various precipitates and inclusions identified within the alloy matrix during the microstructural analysis.

caption: Raman scattering spectra of prepared membranes displaying characteristic vibrational bands of acrylate- and methacrylate-based polymers.
summary: Raman scattering spectra of the prepared membranes are presented, showing characteristic vibrational bands of acrylate- and methacrylate-based polymers. Distinguishable bands at 1726 cm-1 and 1697 cm-1 are assigned to symmetric stretching of the carbonyl group. Additional bands at 1281, 1243, 1200, 968, 930, and 855 cm-1 correspond to C-O stretching and rocking modes.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) curve for D2 substrate material calculated via JMatPro.
summary: This TTT diagram illustrates the transformation kinetics of the D2 substrate material as a function of time and temperature. Derived using JMatPro thermodynamic software, the curve provides essential data for understanding phase transformation behaviors during heat treatment processes, which is critical for optimizing the material's final microstructure and properties.

caption: Surface topography visualization of the additive manufactured sample showing a regular striped pattern.
summary: This panel displays the surface topography of a material extrusion-based additive manufactured sample. The image reveals a characteristic striped surface pattern, indicating that peaks and valleys repeat regularly across the surface. This visualization serves as a baseline for evaluating the performance of the ResNet18-based prediction model.

caption: Thermal compression diagram for the Ti6Al4V alloy base material.
summary: This panel presents the thermal compression diagram for the Ti6Al4V alloy. It serves as the baseline reference for evaluating the deformation behavior of the material under thermal conditions, providing essential data regarding the alloy's response to compression during processing without the influence of reinforcing phases or additional structural modifications.

caption: Heating and cooling curves for Alloy B, illustrating the linear transformation strain defined by the vertical distance between dashed lines at 450 °C.
summary: Heating and cooling curves for Alloy B provide a measure of total transformation strain when the microstructure fully converts to austenite at specific temperatures. The vertical distance between dashed lines at 450 °C quantifies this strain. Combined with isothermal data, this analysis indicates that approximately 10% austenite forms during tensile testing at 450 °C.

caption: Immunocytofluorescence staining images of AG, AGWOM, and AGWM scaffolds using Calcein-AM and DAPI markers after 1 and 7 days of culture.
summary: Immunocytofluorescence imaging using Calcein-AM and DAPI staining demonstrates the biocompatibility of AG, AGWOM, and AGWM scaffolds. After 1 and 7 days of culture, the constructs show successful cell attachment and proliferation, confirming that all tested scaffold materials are non-cytotoxic and support healthy cell growth throughout the experimental period.

caption: Overlay of isothermal TGA mass measurements and model-simulated oxidation kinetics at 1200 °C.
summary: Isothermal TGA mass measurements are overlaid with model-simulated oxidation kinetics at 1200 °C. This comparison highlights the consistency between the experimental data and the model predictions at the highest tested temperature, confirming the model's applicability across the investigated range of thermal conditions.

caption: Conductance values for different DOE runs, where DOE run 12 achieves the highest conductance of 19.12 μS and DOE run 8 reports the lowest at 2.4 μS.
summary: Conductance measurements across the DOE runs reveal that DOE run 12 attains the highest value of 19.12 μS, followed by DOE run 3 at 16.7 μS. Conversely, DOE run 8 exhibits the lowest conductance at 2.4 μS, demonstrating an inverse relationship with the resistance values observed in the study.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph showing the microstructure of an as-deposited 20 at% Ag PVD sample.
summary: This bright-field STEM micrograph displays the initial microstructure of an as-deposited 20 at% Ag PVD sample. The image provides a baseline for evaluating the structural evolution of the material before undergoing any dealloying processes, serving as a reference for comparison with the post-dealloyed state of the same composition.

caption: Normalized dissipated energy (ψ*) plot, where experimental and FE data are scaled by ρ* to facilitate a comprehensive comparison of joint performance.
summary: Normalized dissipated energy (ψ*) values are plotted to allow for a more comprehensive comparison between experimental and FE data. The results demonstrate that accounting for the weight of the adjoined layers significantly enhances the observed performance improvements, particularly when evaluating the BH sample under these normalized conditions.

caption: Waterfall plot illustrating the feature contributions for the prediction of heat flux, where pink bars denote positive influences and blue bars indicate negative impacts on the target value.
summary: This waterfall plot quantifies the individual influence of features on the heat flux prediction for a specific observation. The target value is shown at the top, with the base value at the bottom. Pink bars represent positive contributions, while blue bars represent negative contributions, ordered by their overall importance to the model.

caption: Grey-boxed data points representing specific parameter settings for PA 12/TPU samples that prevented crack propagation and delamination, even when initial crack lengths were extended beyond 30 mm.
summary: Grey-boxed regions identify parameter configurations that effectively prevent crack propagation and delamination in PA 12/TPU samples. These settings remain robust even when initial crack lengths are increased from 20–25 mm to over 30 mm, demonstrating that these specific processing conditions successfully mitigate the challenge of delamination in the tested materials.

caption: Neat PLA load-displacement curves showing improved repeatability of mechanical response after the cryogenic sample redesign.
summary: Neat PLA load-displacement curves are presented to demonstrate the improved repeatability of mechanical testing results achieved through the Type IV specimen redesign. The data confirms that even in samples avoiding grip-interface failure, there is a clear, consistent shift toward brittle-elastic failure behavior, validating the effectiveness of the updated test procedure.

caption: Interaction effects of scan speed and laser power on the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of the processed material.
summary: This panel illustrates the interaction effects of processing parameters on the ultimate tensile strength. Analysis indicates that both scan speed and laser power exert a significant influence on the UTS, highlighting their critical roles in determining the mechanical performance of the material during the manufacturing process.

caption: Flexural modulus performance of multi-material composites with face-to-core ratios ranging from 0 to 0.8, compared against the monolithic core baseline.
summary: Flexural modulus performance is evaluated for multi-material composites with face-to-core ratios from 0 to 0.8. The radar plot illustrates performance relative to the monolithic core baseline. Enhancements in flexural modulus are significant, with several configurations exceeding 100% performance relative to the core-only samples, providing a consistent basis for material selection.

caption: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherm for membrane M5.
summary: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherm for membrane M5 is shown in this panel. As part of the systematic investigation of membrane materials in Fig. 5, this plot serves to quantify the adsorption capacity of M5, facilitating the analysis of its textural properties and overall porosity.

caption: Polythermal isopleth of the Cu–Ni–S system at a constant molar fraction of S = 0.17, comparing experimental data from this study and literature against FactSage 8.3 thermodynamic calculations.
summary: This polythermal isopleth at a molar fraction of S = 0.17 illustrates phase equilibria in the Cu-Ni-S system. It compares experimental measurements from this study and literature against FactSage 8.3 predictions. The diagram highlights the liquidus of the Cu-Ni fcc alloy, which aligns with previous findings, and shows shifts in matte and alloy compositions.

caption: Strain rate sensitivity map at a higher initial dislocation density of 36 MPa, highlighting a well-defined critical strain at a strain rate of 10 s^-1 and the presence of both normal and inverse critical strain behaviors.
summary: Representing the strain rate sensitivity for a high initial dislocation density, this map reveals a well-defined critical strain at a strain rate of 10 s^-1. The visualization clearly demonstrates both normal and inverse critical strain behaviors, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's sensitivity response under these specific conditions.

caption: Control cells showing baseline conditions without any treatment.
summary: Control cells are shown as the baseline condition for the cellular uptake experiment. These cells were left untreated to provide a reference for comparing the intracellular uptake of the various niosome-based formulations tested in the study, ensuring that the observed effects are specific to the drug delivery systems applied.

caption: Strain map and slip trace analysis for lamella I, located near the initial crack, at applied strains of 0.50% and 4.55%, showing long strain bands spanning the lamella length at 0.50% strain.
summary: This panel displays strain localization and slip trace analysis for an alpha-p lamella situated near an initial crack. At 0.50% strain, long strain bands are clearly observed spanning the length of the lamella. The analysis includes measured and theoretical slip trace angles for basal, prismatic, and pyramidal slip systems.

caption: Comparative plot illustrating the laser absorptivity of pure CuCrZr powder versus the mixed CuCrZr + 15 wt% 316L powder composition.
summary: The plot demonstrates the influence of 316L stainless steel addition on the laser absorptivity of CuCrZr powder. By comparing the pure CuCrZr against the mixed powder, the graph highlights how the inclusion of 15 wt% 316L modifies the optical absorption properties of the material system.

caption: Rate performance evaluation of LNPs-CFC, NCPs-CFC, NPs-CFC, and CFC-based symmetric cells across varying current densities.
summary: Rate capability testing reveals that the LNPs-CFC symmetric cell consistently exhibits steady voltage profile variations at current densities ranging from 1 to 20 mA cm-2. This performance indicates superior electrochemical kinetics and structural integrity of the LNPs-CFC electrode compared to the other tested control configurations under high-rate conditions.

caption: Loss factor (Tan δ) curve for the cured VER-HEMA resin, indicating the glass transition temperature (Tg) at the peak.
summary: Loss factor (Tan δ) measurements for the cured VER-HEMA resin are displayed, with the glass transition temperature (Tg) identified by the peak of the curve. This DMA analysis confirms the thermal transition characteristics of the material, providing a precise metric for the resin's viscoelastic damping properties.

caption: W distribution map of region B, showing significant diffusion toward the NA side.
summary: The W distribution map reveals the elemental concentration of tungsten within region B. Observations indicate that tungsten significantly diffuses toward the NA side of the interface, demonstrating the migration behavior of heavy elements across the WC-Co boundary during the processing of the material.

caption: Atom distribution map of Ti in the middle specimen, highlighting the presence of spherical secondary γ′ particles within the γ matrix.
summary: The atom probe tomography map for the middle specimen reveals the Ti distribution and the γ/γ′ phase morphology. The 10 at% Al + Ti iso-concentration surfaces delineate the phase boundaries, clearly showing the presence of secondary γ′ spherical particles, which are a distinct feature of this specimen's thermal and property gradient.

caption: Numerical data and theoretical power law fits for the critical wavelength plotted against different rigidity ratios of the skin and substrate.
summary: This plot displays the critical wavelength as a function of the skin-to-substrate rigidity ratio. Numerical results from linear buckling analysis are shown alongside theoretical power law curves. The data confirms how the rigidity ratio influences the characteristic wavelength at the onset of the wrinkling instability in the specimen.

caption: S–N fatigue life curves for Ti6Al4V alloy comparing net-shape and Hirtisation® surface conditions at a stress ratio of R = −1, including experimental data points, log-normal regression fits, and 95% scatter bands.
summary: This S–N diagram illustrates the fatigue performance of Ti6Al4V alloy under fully reversed loading conditions (R = −1). The plot compares the fatigue life of net-shape specimens against those treated with Hirtisation®, providing experimental data points, log-normal fits, and 95% scatter bands to quantify the influence of surface processing on fatigue strength.

caption: Resistivity change Δρ as a function of magnetic induction B for Ni75Co25 and Ni40Co60 alloys at 300 K, showing experimental data points fitted with second-order polynomials and compared against nc-Ni foil TMR data.
summary: This plot displays the magnetic-field-induced resistivity change Δρ = ρ(B) – ρ(B=0) for Ni75Co25 and Ni40Co60 alloys at 300 K. Experimental data, represented by symbols, are fitted with second-order polynomials. The results demonstrate qualitatively similar behavior and quantitative differences between the alloys, with magnitudes comparable to previously reported nc-Ni foil TMR data.

caption: Comprehensive overview of the sequential fabrication process for natural fiber composite filaments.
summary: This panel provides a comprehensive overview of the sequential fabrication process for natural fiber composite filaments. It outlines the workflow from material preparation through to the final production stages, as described in the context of using single and twin-screw extruders for creating composite materials for FDM printing.

caption: Mean squared displacement (MSD) of hydrogen atoms within the Fe99H25 alloy lattice at 360 GPa and 5500 K.
summary: This panel displays the mean squared displacement of hydrogen atoms in an Fe99H25 alloy at extreme conditions of 360 GPa and 5500 K. Hydrogen is shown to be highly diffusive within the iron lattice, with calculated diffusion coefficients consistent with previous computational studies, confirming its high mobility under these specific thermodynamic conditions.

caption: Backscattered electron image showing the cross-sectional microstructure of alloy 230 after 92 hours of exposure in a Ni-capsule within purified commercial salt at 800 °C.
summary: This backscattered electron image displays the cross-section of alloy 230 following a 92-hour exposure in a Ni-capsule at 800 °C in purified salt. The specimen exhibits a significantly deeper corrosive attack compared to the sample exposed in a Mo-capsule, highlighting the influence of the capsule material on degradation.

caption: Electronic band structure of the Al-substituted Bi2Te3 sample.
summary: This panel illustrates the electronic band structure of the Al-substituted Bi2Te3 sample. Comparison with the pristine reference system demonstrates that Al substitution results in a slight narrowing of the bandgap from 0.1 eV to 0.04 eV, without introducing noticeable changes in carrier concentration near the Fermi level.

caption: DRIFT spectra of silica powder in the O-H stretching regime, highlighting a sharp band at 3744 cm-1 and a broad feature at 3380 cm-1 attributed to hydrogen-bonded Si-OH groups.
summary: The DRIFT spectra in the O-H stretching regime for silica powder reveal a sharp band at 3744 cm-1 and a broad band at 3380 cm-1. These features are assigned to isolated and hydrogen-bonded Si-OH groups, respectively, providing insight into the surface silanol environment of the silica support under various conditions.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for 17-4 PH stainless steel samples subjected to various heat treatment conditions at room temperature.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the tensile behavior of 17-4 PH stainless steel samples at room temperature. These curves demonstrate the mechanical response of the material under different heat treatment conditions, providing a clear visualization of the tensile properties achieved through the specific processing parameters applied to the samples.

caption: Equilibrium solidification sequence for the 2024Sc alloy, modeled via Scheil simulation to track phase evolution during cooling.
summary: The equilibrium solidification sequence for the 2024Sc alloy is modeled using Scheil simulations with the TTAL7 database. This simulation tracks the phase evolution during the cooling process, providing critical insights into the sequence of phase formation that occurs during the solidification of the alloy system.

caption: Linear EDS elemental distribution profiles for Al, Ti, Co, and W across a scanning line located 100–120 μm below the surface after the first heating and cooling cycle.
summary: Linear EDS analysis reveals the distribution of Al, Ti, Co, and W elements within the composite sample. This profile, taken 100–120 μm below the surface after one thermal cycle, provides baseline data for identifying phase transformations and oxidation processes initiated by directional diffusion from the CaF2 lubricant and Ni matrix interface.

caption: Nesting orientations for Tri-RNLs, detailing the alignment of merged rhombus-based base structures.
summary: This panel showcases the nesting orientations for Tri-RNLs, focusing on the alignment of the merged rhombus-based base structures. By employing TFFAS to produce these configurations, the diagram illustrates how the base structures are integrated to form the final, more complex Tri-RNL lattice geometries.

caption: EXAFS χ(r) spectrum of Co K-edge, revealing a characteristic double-peak structure with distinct peaks identified at approximately 2.0 Å and 2.6 Å after heat treatment.
summary: This panel displays the EXAFS χ(r) spectrum for the Co K-edge. A characteristic double-peak structure is clearly observed, with specific peaks identified at approximately 2.0 Å and 2.6 Å. These features persist following heat treatment, indicating consistent local structural environments around the Co atoms in the analyzed material.

caption: Bode representation of ohmic-resistance-corrected phase angles for Fe–Cr-X alloys, highlighting the capacitive and inductive contributions to the electrochemical interface.
summary: Bode representations of the phase angle, corrected for ohmic resistance, provide detailed insights into the oxide layers of FeCr, FeCrY, and FeCrTi alloys. By analyzing these phase angle shifts across the frequency spectrum, researchers can extract valuable information concerning the electrochemical properties and stability of the passive oxide films.

caption: Projected density of states for the Ni-Nb-W alloy surface slab at 5/15 ML coverage from the Nb attack series, including the Cl curve.
summary: This panel illustrates the projected density of states for the Ni-Nb-W alloy surface slab at 5/15 ML coverage during the Nb attack process. The plot incorporates the Cl curve and utilizes consistent scaling conventions, with d-orbitals and s/p-orbitals represented by colored curves and gray reference curves for comparative analysis.

caption: Deformation strain field of the GSLS sample visualized through digital image correlation.
summary: Deformation strain field of the GSLS sample visualized through digital image correlation. This analysis tracks the strain evolution in the tensile direction throughout the initial yield, intermediate yield, plastic deformation, and fracture stages, contributing to the comparative study of deformation mechanisms across the three distinct material samples examined.

caption: Subdivided particle morphology map color-coded by kernel density, illustrating the distribution of powders based on roundness and sphericity metrics.
summary: This subdivided particle morphology map utilizes kernel density estimation to visualize the distribution of powder shapes. By plotting roundness against sphericity, the map provides a comprehensive overview of the morphological characteristics of the different powder samples, serving as a foundational framework for comparing the shape profiles of TD_8, TD_4, and TD_2.

caption: Individual EDS map showing the spatial distribution of Iron (Fe) in 316H stainless steel after irradiation, exhibiting depletion.
summary: Iron distribution in the irradiated 316H stainless steel is visualized in this EDS map. The results indicate depletion of Fe post-irradiation, which aligns with the observed redistribution of elements within the 316H microstructure, confirming that radiation exposure significantly alters the local composition of the primary alloy matrix.

caption: Vickers hardness (HV 0.1) variation profile measured along the cross-section of the as-sprayed Fe-based AAC specimen at 50 μm intervals, highlighting the transition between the coating zone and the substrate.
summary: This plot illustrates the Vickers hardness (HV 0.1) distribution across the cross-section of as-sprayed Fe-based AACs, measured at 50 μm intervals. The data reveals significant dispersion in hardness values, which is attributed to intrinsic thermal defects such as porosity, microcracks, and unmelted particles within the coating structure.

caption: Creep deformation results for ME3 alloy subjected to testing at various temperatures.
summary: This panel displays creep deformation results for the ME3 alloy, with experimental data obtained from Smith et al. The plot illustrates the creep response of the material when deformed at different temperatures, providing further validation for the model's predictive capabilities across varying thermal conditions in nickel-based superalloys.

caption: Ni–Se binary phase diagram illustrating the formation mechanism of NiSe2 micro-inclusions within the host matrix.
summary: The Ni–Se phase diagram illustrates the formation mechanism of NiSe2 micro-inclusions. At the synthesis temperature of 853 °C, NiSe2 exists as a solid phase dispersed within the liquid Bi–Se host matrix. This analysis elucidates the formation mechanism of in situ NiSe2 and the associated Se vacancies within the material system.

caption: Fe-V-Al ternary phase diagrams at 500 °C and 700 °C, highlighting the measured chemical composition range within the TEM lamella in gray and identifying 2-phase chemical compositions with blue and red crosses.
summary: Fe-V-Al ternary phase diagrams at 500 °C and 700 °C show the measured chemical composition range within the TEM lamella as a gray area. Blue and red crosses denote specific 2-phase chemical compositions found in the lamella, facilitating the identification of phases formed despite low Al concentrations.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plot for the ZNTP-based single cell, with polarization resistance (Rp) values of 1.06, 0.84, and 0.50 Ω cm2 at 700, 750, and 800 °C.
summary: Panel f shows the EIS Nyquist plot for the ZNTP-based single cell. The data indicates polarization resistance (Rp) values of 1.06, 0.84, and 0.50 Ω cm2 at 700, 750, and 800 °C, respectively, confirming the superior electrochemical performance of the ZNTP catalytic layer compared to the other tested samples.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray micro-computed tomography image of a sample processed at 420 °C with a scan speed of 15 mm/s and layer thickness of 0.1 mm, showing minimal porosity of 0.2 ± 0.1%.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray micro-computed tomography reveals the internal structure of a sample processed at 420 °C, 15 mm/s, and 0.1 mm layer thickness. This specific condition results in a high-density material with minimal porosity of 0.2 ± 0.1%, where isolated defects are only discernible through high-resolution synchrotron X-ray CT imaging techniques.

caption: Current-voltage performance of titanium expanded metal PTLs featuring Ti 72 Nb 28 PVD coatings.
summary: Displayed here are the I-V curves for titanium expanded metal PTLs modified with Ti 72 Nb 28 PVD coatings. These measurements characterize the electrochemical response of the expanded metal architecture, which is compared against the titanium felt performance to assess the influence of substrate geometry on the coated PTL performance.

caption: Pole figure of as-built TMC4 sample after heat treatment, showing the resulting crystallographic texture.
summary: This pole figure displays the crystallographic orientation for the TMC4 sample after heat treatment. The results show no preferred orientation, which is consistent with the equiaxed grain morphology observed in the heat-treated samples. This confirms that the thermal processing resulted in a random distribution of grain orientations for TMC4.

caption: Fatigue stress-life (S-N) performance comparison between vertical and horizontal fabrication orientations, highlighting experimental fatigue limits of 95.6 MPa and 83.4 MPa respectively, with black arrows indicating run-out specimens.
summary: This fatigue stress-life curve compares the performance of specimens fabricated in vertical and horizontal orientations. The vertical samples exhibit a higher fatigue limit of 95.6 MPa compared to 83.4 MPa for horizontal samples. Black arrows in the plot denote the run-out specimens, illustrating the distinct fatigue behavior based on build orientation.

caption: Schematic representation of the time-temperature profile illustrating five distinct thermal cycle types occurring during the LPBF process, which induce inherent heat treatment effects in the deposited Ti-alloy.
summary: This schematic illustrates the characteristic cyclic reheating profiles during the LPBF process, which function as an in-situ heat treatment. These rapid heating and cooling cycles force the Ti-alloy into critical temperature ranges below the beta-transus, promoting the diffusion-assisted formation of isothermal omega and equilibrium alpha phases within the material.

caption: Sequential transition showing the arc additive manufacturing robot initiating deposition immediately upon the completion of the FSP stage.
summary: Depicted here is the operational sequence where the arc additive manufacturing robot begins the next deposition phase right after the friction stir processing is finished. This transition highlights the integrated nature of the manufacturing process and sets the stage for how thermal and mechanical inputs affect the material.

caption: Predicted pole figure generated for an alpha angle of 67.5 degrees.
summary: This predicted pole figure for an alpha angle of 67.5 degrees illustrates the theoretical crystallographic texture. The consistency between this simulation and the experimental results from the corresponding EBSD scan underscores the accuracy of the approach in predicting material behavior across different angles.

caption: Confocal maximum Z-projection of NES cells cultured on a 30% PEGDA/0% GelMA pedestal, stained with calcein AM (green) for live cells and SYTOX (red) for dead cells.
summary: This confocal maximum Z-projection displays NES cells cultured on a 30% PEGDA/0% GelMA pedestal. The live/dead staining technique, utilizing calcein AM for live cells and SYTOX for dead cells, allows for the visualization of cell viability and distribution on the printed bioink surface at a 50 μm scale.

caption: Hydrolysis kinetics of methyl ester model compounds at pH 7.4 and 37 °C, measured via 31P NMR spectroscopy, illustrating the correlation between alpha-substituent shielding and reaction rates.
summary: Hydrolysis kinetics of methyl ester model compounds were determined at pH 7.4 and 37 °C using 31P NMR spectroscopy. The results demonstrate that alpha-substituent shielding significantly influences the hydrolysis rate. Specifically, the alanine substituent exhibits an intermediate rate between glycine and valine, confirming that the alpha-carbon substituent effect follows the trend iPr > Me > H.

caption: Current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics of the monolithic perovskite/Si tandem solar cell with a 1 cm2 active area, measured under AM1.5 G illumination in both forward and reverse scan directions.
summary: The J-V characteristic of the monolithic tandem solar cells with a marked active area of 1 cm2 under AM1.5 G illumination is shown. This panel displays the performance of the champion tandem device, comparing forward and reverse scan directions to evaluate the device's photovoltaic response and stability under simulated sunlight conditions.

caption: EDS line scan profile illustrating the elemental distribution of Fe, Mn, Al, Ni, and C across the dark phase and matrix in L-PBF-fabricated Fe–Mn–Al–Ni–C lightweight steel.
summary: This EDS line scan analysis characterizes the chemical composition across the dark region and matrix of L-PBF-fabricated Fe–Mn–Al–Ni–C lightweight steel. The profile demonstrates that the elemental distribution of Fe, Mn, Al, Ni, and C remains uniform, confirming that there is no significant compositional variation between the dark phase and the matrix.

caption: Fractured tensile specimens showing composition region interfaces marked by arrows.
summary: Fractured tensile samples illustrate metallurgical bonding at interfaces. The F25 sample displays a flat fracture surface within the defective composition region, whereas other samples exhibit typical cup-and-cone fracture morphologies at the SS316L terminal alloy region, confirming strong metallurgical bonding across the compositionally graded interfaces of the FGM structures.

caption: FT-IR spectra of LDH and DEXA hybrids at weight ratios of 1:0, 1:1, 1:0.5, and 0:1, highlighting the broad OH vibration peak near 3450 cm⁻¹.
summary: FT-IR spectra are presented for LDH and DEXA mixtures at varying weight ratios of 1:0, 1:1, 1:0.5, and 0:1. The NO3- type LDHs exhibit a characteristic broad peak around 3450 cm⁻¹, which is attributed to OH group vibrations, reflecting a brucite-like structure containing interlayer water molecules.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the μ phase projected along the [1 1 -1 0] zone axis.
summary: Atomic arrangement of the μ phase is displayed along the [1 1 -1 0] zone axis. Different colors are utilized to represent the various crystallographic sites occupied by atoms within the structure. This projection provides a detailed perspective on the atomic packing and symmetry elements inherent to the μ phase unit cell.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the half-cell configuration illustrating the specific cutting plane utilized for visualizing fluid velocity contours.
summary: This schematic illustrates the internal geometry of the half-cell, highlighting the designated cutting plane for velocity contour analysis. Fluid dynamics within this configuration reveal that upon entry, the fluid impacts the internal cell wall, forcing a redistribution of flow that subsequently travels along the surface of the electrode.

caption: Individual HAADF-SEM transmission mode image focusing on the high number density area of type II precipitates within the nitrided sample.
summary: This individual HAADF-SEM image provides a detailed view of the high number density area for type II precipitates in the nitrided sample. It allows for precise observation of precipitate morphology and distribution in regions where these features are most concentrated, complementing the broader stitched images of the same sample.

caption: Comparative evaluation of Fmax prediction accuracy between a linear regression model with interaction terms and a degree 2 polynomial regression model across diverse geometric configurations.
summary: This parity plot compares the predictive performance of linear and polynomial regression models for estimating Fmax values across various geometries. The polynomial model demonstrates superior geometric generalization, particularly for box-shaped APs, while the linear model shows higher accuracy for cylindrical geometries. Overall, the graph illustrates the deviation between model estimations and experimental data.

caption: Magnified dark-field TEM image showing the morphology and distribution of intragranular precipitates within the material matrix.
summary: This magnified dark-field TEM image provides a detailed view of intragranular precipitates located within the material. The visualization highlights the structural morphology of these particles, which are identified as being rich in iron and chromium with minor silicon content, as confirmed by complementary STEM-EDS mapping analysis of the same region.

caption: Temperature-dependent phase-fraction modeling for the V2Nb6 high-entropy alloy, computed through Thermo-Calc software utilizing the TCHEA 3 database.
summary: Representing the V2Nb6 high-entropy alloy, this panel shows the phase-fraction modeling results obtained from Thermo-Calc software and the TCHEA 3 database. The diagram effectively maps the phase structure evolution relative to temperature, facilitating a deeper understanding of the thermodynamic behavior and phase stability of this specific alloy composition.

caption: Longitudinal hardness distribution of the Inconel 625 component plotted against the distance to the interface.
summary: Longitudinal hardness distribution of the Inconel 625 component is plotted against the distance to the interface. This measurement provides insight into the mechanical properties of the component along its longitudinal axis, illustrating how the hardness values vary relative to the interface position within the Inconel 625 sample.

caption: APT reconstruction of the DA sample aged for 19.1 h, illustrating the arrangement of γ“ and γʹ precipitates along dislocations, indicated by red arrows.
summary: This APT reconstruction shows the DA sample after 19.1 h of ageing. The microstructure features γ“ precipitates decorated with γʹ precipitates grown along dislocations, as highlighted by red arrows. This panel confirms that similar precipitate morphologies persist in the DA samples throughout the extended ageing duration of 19.1 hours.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for the as-printed material, displaying measured intensity versus interplanar spacing with Rietveld refinement fit.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for the as-printed material are presented, showing measured intensity versus interplanar spacing alongside a Rietveld refinement fit. These patterns confirm that the material possesses a single body-centered cubic (BCC) martensitic structure, with several specific hkl reflections for the martensite phase clearly identified and labeled.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) profiles for solution annealed, H860, and H1000 metallurgical states, recorded at a constant heating rate of 130 K/min.
summary: TDS spectra obtained at a heating rate of 130 K/min reveal the hydrogen desorption behavior of three distinct metallurgical states. The aged samples, particularly the H1000 state, demonstrate a higher capacity for hydrogen storage compared to the solution annealed material, indicating significant differences in hydrogen trapping characteristics across these states.

caption: Fatigue life characteristics plotted as a Wöhler curve for the G40 gyroid structure.
summary: Depicted here is the Wöhler curve for the G40 gyroid structure, showcasing its fatigue response. This plot is one of several used to evaluate how different porosities influence the mechanical fatigue life of gyroid-based materials, offering a clear visualization of the stress-cycle relationship for the G40 design.

caption: Experimental setup for tensile coupon testing using a 250 kN INSTRON 8820 machine.
summary: This panel displays the experimental setup for tensile coupon testing, utilizing a 250 kN INSTRON 8820 testing machine. The test is conducted under displacement control at a rate of 0.8 mm/min. This configuration allows for precise mechanical characterization of the tensile coupons as specified in the experimental methodology.

caption: Magnetic force microscopy image of a 5 μm Py square prepared at high sputter pressure, indicating the absence of defined domain configurations.
summary: Representing the high-pressure limit of the study, this MFM image shows a 5 μm Py square where no distinct domain configurations are visible. This result confirms that high Ar sputter pressure effectively suppresses the formation of organized magnetic domains, leading to a loss of the characteristic domain patterns observed previously.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF-Z) map of Coating-IN718-A showing randomly oriented grains and unindexed black regions.
summary: The IPF-Z map for Coating-IN718-A displays randomly oriented grains throughout the microstructure. Unindexed black regions appear due to crystalline distortions in inter-splat areas that are smaller than the EBSD detector step size. This indicates that severe plastic deformation has induced grain refinement through mechanical fragmentation and dynamic recrystallisation processes.

caption: Isofield magnetization (M–T) curves for the Ni47Co5Mn40Sn8 alloy after aging at 523 K for 1200 min, showing heating and cooling behavior at 0.05 T, 1.0 T, and 7.0 T.
summary: Following aging at 523 K for 1200 min, the M-T curves reveal that the Curie temperature of the austenite phase (TCA) increases. The transformation temperatures remain field-dependent, shifting to lower values with higher fields, with ΔTB reaching -16.9 K at 7 T, indicating a slight change in magnetic transformation behavior post-aging.

caption: Three-dimensional optical metallographic reconstruction of EBM-fabricated Inconel 625 alloy, highlighting the columnar architecture of γ″-precipitates oriented along the build direction (B) parallel to the Z-axis.
summary: This 3D optical metallographic reconstruction illustrates the columnar architecture of γ″-precipitate disk platelets within EBM-fabricated Inconel 625 alloy. These precipitates are coincident with the fcc-Ni-Cr matrix {1 1 1} planes. The visualization clearly demonstrates the precipitate distribution relative to the build direction, which is aligned with the Z-axis.

caption: Cross-section profiles of worn tracks for the HTD sample across top, middle, and bottom regions, showing nearly overlapping curves.
summary: Cross-section profiles of worn tracks for the HTD sample are shown for the top, middle, and bottom regions. The nearly overlapping curves indicate a declined anisotropy in the HTD sample after the introduction of twins and dislocations, suggesting more uniform wear behavior compared to the AD sample.

caption: Ni-Zn binary phase diagram derived from the thermodynamic model developed by Xiong et al.
summary: This panel presents the Ni-Zn binary phase diagram calculated using the thermodynamic model proposed by Xiong et al. It provides a computational perspective on the phase stability and equilibrium boundaries of the Ni-Zn system, offering a comparison to the experimental assessment shown in the previous panel.

caption: Tabulated mass percentage values for the constituent elements of the HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe alloy.
summary: Tabulated mass percentage values for the constituent elements of the HPDC Al-4Mg-2Fe alloy quantify the chemical composition of the material. This data table complements the EDS analysis, providing precise numerical results for the alloy conditions and facilitating a clear understanding of the material's elemental distribution as reported in the study.

caption: Guanidine hydrochloride (GdnHCl) induced unfolding profiles of CXCL9, HSA-CXCL9(74–103), and HSA, showing the mean fluorescence emission maximum as a function of denaturant concentration.
summary: GdnHCl-induced unfolding profiles demonstrate the structural stability of the fusion protein. CXCL9 and HSA-CXCL9(74–103) exhibit similar chemical unfolding transition points of 2.96 mol/L and 2.83 mol/L GdnHCl, respectively. Fluorescence spectra were recorded from 300 to 400 nm to determine the unfolding transition points for each protein sample.

caption: ANOVA interaction analysis for PLA/TPU 50/50 blend printing parameters.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the ANOVA analysis for printing parameter interactions in the PLA/TPU 50/50 blend. It evaluates six interactions between printing speed, raster angle, layer thickness, and temperature. Lower P-values signify higher statistical significance, offering insights into the most influential parameters for the printing process of this specific blend composition.

caption: Magnified piezoresistive response (-ΔR/Ro vs. strain) showing the electrical behavior of the MWCNT/PA12 HHS during the first three cycles of loading.
summary: Magnified piezoresistive data for the first three cycles provide a detailed look at the electrical resistance changes during initial loading stages. This plot captures the specific -ΔR/Ro response as the MWCNT/PA12 HHS undergoes early cyclic compression, illustrating the sensitivity of the conductive network to the initial mechanical strain cycles.

caption: Two-dimensional chemical structure of the beta-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) ligand, generated via Chem3D 18.2.
summary: The 2D chemical structure of the β-TCP ligand is displayed, as drawn in Chem3D 18.2. This structural model was further processed by retrieving its SMILES code from PubChem and constructing the corresponding 3D geometry in Avogadro to facilitate comprehensive molecular interaction studies with the protein receptor.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image showing the dispersoid/matrix interface, where no evident solute segregation or precipitation is observed.
summary: This high-magnification HAADF-STEM image focuses on the interface between the dispersoid and the aluminum matrix. The observation confirms that there is no evident solute segregation or precipitation at the interface. Furthermore, the image demonstrates the persistence of Mn/Cu enrichment and Ti/Zr/V depletion within the dispersoids after 30 days of aging.

caption: Nyquist plots comparing TPU-LFP TSEs and MSEs before and after 50 stretch cycles, illustrating electrochemical impedance changes.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy was performed to evaluate the electrochemical behavior of 3D printed TPU-LFP TSEs and MSEs. The Nyquist plots reveal the impedance characteristics of these electrodes before and after 50 stretch cycles, providing insight into the stability and performance of the different topological and mesh electrode structures.

caption: Explained variance ratio plotted against the number of principal components for superalloy compositions, comparing the full composition (blue line) with the composition excluding the base element (red line).
summary: Principal component analysis reveals the dimensionality reduction potential for superalloy compositions. The plot demonstrates that low-rank projections of the full composition and the composition excluding the base element provide significant explanatory power. These results facilitate the identification of low-dimensional subspaces for kernel-based modeling, either prior to training or as an optimized hyperparameter.

caption: Cyclic voltammetric curve of AISI 316L stainless steel alloy measured in [EMIM][Tf2N] ionic liquid electrolyte at a scan rate of 5 mV/s.
summary: This cyclic voltammetric curve illustrates the electrochemical behavior of AISI 316L stainless steel alloy when immersed in the [EMIM][Tf2N] ionic liquid. The measurement was conducted at a controlled scan rate of 5 mV/s, providing essential data on the redox characteristics and electrochemical stability of the alloy within this specific electrolyte environment.

caption: Pareto plot showing the six factors that significantly affect fracture toughness.
summary: Fracture toughness is examined in this Pareto plot, which reveals that six distinct factors exert a significant influence on this response. The analysis confirms that all CGP parameters have considerable effects on fracture toughness, reinforcing the comprehensive understanding of how various processing conditions dictate the material's resistance to fracture.
