caption: Representative HPLC chromatogram of SLM spiked in human plasma, demonstrating the method's selectivity within a biological matrix.
summary: A representative chromatogram of the spiked human plasma sample illustrates the analytical method's capability to selectively detect and resolve the SLM peak. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the optimized HPLC procedure in isolating the analyte from the complex biological matrix, ensuring accurate identification despite the presence of interfering components.

caption: Cycling performance of a-SiGe thin-films with varying Ge content over 100 cycles.
summary: Cycling stability tests were performed on a-SiGe thin-film materials with different proportions. Panel a illustrates the cycling performance of these materials over 100 cycles, providing a comparative overview of their electrochemical stability and capacity retention throughout the extended testing period for the four distinct thin-film compositions evaluated in this study.

caption: Tabulated processing parameters utilized during the pre-experimental phase alongside the resulting surface roughness metrics, specifically Sa and Sz, measured along the building direction following the EPP treatment.
summary: This table presents the pre-experimental test results, detailing the specific processing parameters applied during the study. It further quantifies the component surface quality by reporting the Sa and Sz roughness values measured along the building direction after the EPP process, providing a clear correlation between processing conditions and surface topography.

caption: Fatigue life represented as cycles to failure versus applied strain amplitude for HT-AB, HT-M HX, and RT-AB HX specimens.
summary: This fatigue endurance plot compares the failure cycles of HT-AB, HT-M HX, and RT-AB HX samples across different strain amplitudes. The results demonstrate that higher plastic damage at elevated temperatures leads to a shorter fatigue life compared to room temperature conditions for the same applied strain amplitudes.

caption: DIC strain contour map of the H-Gyroid/Diamond hybrid structure under quasi-static loading conditions.
summary: Displaying the strain field of the H-Gyroid/Diamond hybrid structure, this DIC map provides a visual assessment of deformation during quasi-static compression. The 2D-DIC method effectively characterizes the strain distribution, allowing for a detailed observation of how the hybrid architecture responds to compressive loads compared to other TPMS structures.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance behavior of samples immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution for 24 hours.
summary: This Bode plot represents the frequency-dependent impedance response of samples after 24 hours of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The inclusion of a constant phase element in the analysis is essential to accurately model the non-ideal capacitive behavior and achieve an optimal fit for the experimental data.

caption: FBCCZ with X and Y Struts (FBCCXY) lattice structure featuring horizontal X and Y reinforcement struts added to the FBCCZ framework.
summary: The FBCCXY lattice structure is shown, representing an advanced modification of the FBCCZ framework by incorporating additional X and Y horizontal struts. This complex geometry provides multi-directional reinforcement, significantly increasing the structural stability and stiffness of the lattice compared to simpler cubic-based designs in various loading conditions.

caption: Boundary conditions defined for the strut-and-tie model, illustrating the configuration of four loading points and two supports.
summary: This panel displays the boundary conditions used to initiate the strut-and-tie model. By applying four specific loading points and two supports, the setup establishes the structural constraints necessary for subsequent layout optimization and algebraic graphic statics analysis, providing the foundational geometry for the entire printing process design.

caption: In-line transmittance curve of a 4.6 mm thick gradient-doped Yb:YAG laser ceramic, showing a peak transmittance of 82.1% at 1100 nm, with an inset displaying the double-sided polished 17 mm × 17 mm square sample.
summary: The in-line transmittance curve for the 4.6 mm thick gradient-doped Yb:YAG laser ceramic demonstrates high optical quality, reaching 82.1% transmittance at 1100 nm. The inset image confirms the physical state of the sample, which was processed into a 17 mm × 17 mm square shape through double-sided polishing after sintering.

caption: SHAP summary plot illustrating the feature importance and impact on model predictions for the testing dataset.
summary: This SHAP summary plot for the testing dataset provides a visual representation of feature importance and impact on hardness predictions. It serves to validate the model's consistency by demonstrating how the learned feature relationships generalize to unseen data, confirming the reliability of the feature importance identified during the training phase.

caption: Crystal orbital Hamiltonian population (COHP) curves comparing the electronic bonding characteristics of unsegregated Ni Σ3 [110](111) grain boundaries, Re-segregated Ni grain boundaries, and the Ni bulk structure.
summary: This plot displays the crystal orbital Hamiltonian population (COHP) curves for unsegregated and Re-segregated Ni Σ3 [110](111) grain boundaries alongside the Ni bulk structure. These curves illustrate the electronic bonding states, demonstrating that Re segregation maximizes the thermodynamic stability of the Ni grain boundary structure compared to the unsegregated state.

caption: Sequential atomic snapshots of bicrystal NiCoFe from 0.073 to 0.074 dpa, highlighting the absorption of a stair-rod dislocation and vacancy cluster by the grain boundary.
summary: These sequential snapshots illustrate the dynamic absorption of a stair-rod dislocation containing a vacancy cluster at the Σ 5 (210) grain boundary. Atoms are color-coded by element, and black arrows indicate the specific defect absorption events, providing a mechanistic explanation for the reduced defect density observed in the bicrystal simulations.

caption: Load-displacement curves representing the mechanical response of NAB alloy cross-sections after 24 h of corrosion exposure in deionized water.
summary: This panel illustrates the load-displacement behavior of NAB alloy cross-sections subjected to 24 hours of corrosion exposure in deionized water. These curves provide essential data on the mechanical properties and indentation resistance of the alloy surface following exposure to a less aggressive aqueous environment compared to artificial seawater.

caption: PCA-reduced data distribution showing training set (red) and validation set (green) points.
summary: This PCA-reduced plot displays the data distribution of the original dataset, with red dots representing the training set and green dots representing the validation set. The noticeable similarity between these two distributions indicates that the training and validation sets possess similar types of latent alloy composition within the sample space.

caption: Atomic configuration of Alloy IV, featuring blue Ni atoms and green Cr atoms.
summary: This panel shows the atomic structure of Alloy IV, with blue Ni atoms and green Cr atoms clearly identified. The model provides a detailed view of the atomic arrangement, contributing to the comprehensive visual representation of the various alloys investigated throughout the experimental work described in the paper.

caption: Optical transmission profile of a 3D-printed multi-material disk formulated with Atto425, Atto495, and Atto565 dyes, with each section maintained at 0.5 mm thickness.
summary: This panel presents the transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed multi-material disk containing Atto425, Atto495, and Atto565 dyes. With a section thickness of 0.5 mm, this configuration is noted for being closer to the intended spectrum for Pilestone applications compared to other tested dye combinations.

caption: Atom probe tomography ion map showing the distribution of elements in the aged sample after proton irradiation at 400°C to 3 dpa.
summary: Atom probe tomography ion mapping of the aged sample irradiated at 400°C to 3 dpa provides a 3D visualization of the microstructure. The data complements diffraction observations, confirming the formation of Si-rich clusters and Ni3Si precipitates that appear to form homogeneously within the matrix following the irradiation process.

caption: In-situ evolution of the γ 111 peak width (FWHM 111) for IN718 composites reinforced with graphite, GNP, CNTs, MoS2, and WS2 during isochronal and isothermal annealing, showing higher fitting errors for 5 wt% compositions.
summary: This panel displays the FWHM 111 evolution for various SL-reinforced IN718 composites during annealing. Composites with ≤1 wt% SL content show broader peaks at 50 °C compared to the reference. The 5 wt% compositions exhibit higher fitting errors, and nanocarbon reinforcements induce a delay in peak broadening during thermal treatment.

caption: Creep compliance curves of the insert material plotted against time, derived from DMA Creep TTS measurements across a temperature range of 30–110 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the creep compliance behavior of the insert material as determined by DMA Creep TTS testing. The data covers a temperature range from 30 °C to 110 °C, providing a comprehensive view of the material's time-dependent deformation characteristics under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Taylor factor mapping and corresponding pole figure for the LPBF Al–4Ni–2Cu–0.7Fe alloy, characterizing the crystallographic orientation and dislocation activity.
summary: Taylor factor mapping and the pole figure for the 0.7Fe alloy characterize the crystallographic orientation and dislocation activity. Comparison with the 1.4Fe alloy shows that the distribution of activating dislocation orientations is largely similar, indicating that the iron content has a minimal impact on the overall dislocation orientation distribution.

caption: Nyquist plots of as-extruded Mg–Er–Ni alloys in 3 wt% KCl solution, showing an inductive loop at low frequency and two capacitive loops at high and medium frequencies.
summary: Nyquist plots for as-extruded Mg–Er–Ni alloys reveal an inductive loop at low frequencies and two capacitive loops at high and medium frequencies. These features are attributed to charge transfer, the formation of surface corrosion product films, and localized corrosion processes occurring during electrochemical testing in 3 wt% KCl solution.

caption: CD31 immunohistochemistry staining illustrating the density and distribution of neovessels in the vicinity of the constructs.
summary: CD31 immunohistochemistry demonstrates varying degrees of neovascularization around the constructs. The staining reveals limited microvessels in G-Cell, increased frequency in G-sGMS and H-sGMS, and the highest density in H-csFGMS, indicating that the hybrid matrix combined with core–shell microspheres most effectively supports angiogenic remodeling in the surrounding tissue.

caption: Distribution of median Ra surface roughness values (μm) for materials subjected to artificial aging, with outliers marked by circles and asterisks.
summary: This boxplot displays the distribution of median Ra surface roughness values for materials following artificial aging. For specimens treated with process A, median Ra values ranged from 0.17 to 0.21 μm in the unaged state and shifted to a range of 0.10 to 0.27 μm after aging, indicating variable surface topography changes.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map illustrating the initial crystallographic orientation distribution of the Ti-6SS material prior to any mechanical deformation.
summary: This Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map displays the crystallographic orientation of the Ti-6SS material in its initial state before undergoing deformation. It serves as a baseline characterization to understand the starting texture of the alloy, as described in the reference sentences regarding the material's condition prior to mechanical testing.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the 10 wt% TiC/Ti6Al4V composite showing the morphology and distribution of TiC particles.
summary: This bright-field TEM image reveals the morphology and distribution of TiC particles within the 10 wt% TiC/Ti6Al4V composite. The observed TiC particles exhibit characteristics similar to those found in 3 wt% composites, with both chain-distributed and isolated particle morphologies present throughout the microstructure.

caption: Arrhenius curves derived from impedance data to determine the thermal activation energy of sintered Mg-BASE samples.
summary: Arrhenius plots are utilized to analyze the thermal activation process of the sintered Mg-BASE samples. By calculating the slope of these curves, the activation energy of the material is determined, providing insight into the temperature-dependent kinetic processes occurring within the sintered Mg-BASE samples during electrochemical testing.

caption: Interfaces categorized as Others in the HT200-700 condition, showing a mix of flatter boundaries and localized needle-shaped interfaces near the lower corner.
summary: This panel illustrates the 'Others' category of austenite-ferrite interfaces in the HT200-700 condition. While flatter boundaries are characteristic of this group, some needle-shaped interfaces are observed concentrating near the lower corner. The color-coded map provides a detailed view of these non-K-S/N-W interfaces within the intragranular austenite structure.

caption: Strengthening increment (τp) as a function of average precipitate radius in a Ni alloy containing 45% volume fraction of γ’(L12) precipitates with an APB energy of 158 mJ m−2, comparing simulation results for super-edge and super-screw dislocations against analytical model predictions.
summary: This plot illustrates the strengthening increment in a Ni-based alloy with 45% volume fraction of γ’ precipitates. It compares simulation data for super-edge and super-screw dislocations against analytical equations. The results demonstrate how dislocation behavior varies with precipitate radius, providing a quantitative validation of theoretical models for alloy strengthening mechanisms.

caption: Time-dependent H2O2 production curves for the 3D-printed PPY:50 electrode, measured during a 2-hour electrolysis period in an O2-saturated 0.05 M Na2SO4 solution at pH 5 across multiple current settings.
summary: The H2O2 electrogeneration performance of the PPY:50 electrode is shown here. The data reflects the concentration of H2O2 generated over 2 hours in an O2-saturated 0.05 M Na2SO4 solution at pH 5, highlighting the electrochemical response of the 3D-printed material under various tested current conditions.

caption: Extended continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for Grade 91 steel, illustrating phase transformation boundaries across a wide range of cooling rates, including regimes faster than those typically represented in conventional diagrams.
summary: This extended CCT diagram provides a comprehensive overview of phase transformation kinetics for Grade 91 steel. By incorporating cooling rates that exceed traditional experimental limits, the model offers an innovative framework for predicting microstructural evolution, serving as a critical tool for understanding the material's behavior under diverse thermal processing conditions.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves recorded at 10 mV s⁻¹ and 900 rpm in oxygen-saturated 0.1 M KOH, comparing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of NiIIFeIII@NC, NiIIFeII@NC, Fe@NC, and Ni@NC catalysts.
summary: This polarization curve compares the OER activity of various nitrogen-doped carbon-supported catalysts in alkaline media. The LSV data demonstrates that the NiFe@NC catalyst exhibits significantly enhanced OER performance compared to the Fe@NC and Ni@NC control samples, highlighting the synergistic effect of the bimetallic composition on electrochemical activity.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental bond strength values against predictions generated by the proposed regression model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the correlation between experimental bond strengths and values predicted by the proposed regression model. The model demonstrates high predictive accuracy, achieving a coefficient of determination of R2 = 0.93. This indicates that the established mathematical model effectively captures the relationship between the experimental data and predicted outcomes.

caption: Lateral surface morphology of the Kt=1 specimen subjected to corrosion under a 500 MPa stress load.
summary: Surface morphology of the Kt=1 specimen subjected to corrosion at 500 MPa is shown. The average length of cracks increases compared to bare specimens under identical stress. Propagation of transverse and longitudinal cracks leads to spallation of the corrosion layer, exposing the underlying substrate material.

caption: Microwave absorption performance of the multiscale resonant labyrinth metastructure across the 2–18 GHz frequency range.
summary: This plot displays the microwave absorption performance of the multiscale resonant labyrinth metastructure within the 2–18 GHz frequency range. The design incorporates a combination of varying wall thicknesses to optimize the resonant cavity, resulting in significant improvements in absorption performance compared to individual unit configurations as demonstrated in the experimental data.

caption: Maximum force values derived from the test curves for both as-built and heat-treated specimens across different printing orientations.
summary: Maximum force values obtained from the fracture tests are plotted to compare the mechanical performance of as-built and heat-treated specimens. The results indicate that vertical orientation specimens in the as-printed condition withstand higher loads up to failure, demonstrating superior fracture resistance compared to other configurations evaluated in this study.

caption: Temperature programmed desorption profile of structured PEI-MWCNT in argon, displaying the temperature ramp alongside selected mass-to-charge ratio traces monitored by mass spectrometry.
summary: This figure illustrates the thermal decomposition behavior of structured PEI-MWCNT samples under an argon atmosphere. By utilizing temperature programmed desorption coupled with mass spectrometry, the experiment tracks specific mass traces as a function of temperature, providing critical insights into the effluent gas composition and the material's thermal stability characteristics.

caption: Schematic representation indicating the specific extraction locations for tensile and fatigue test specimens within the printed wall geometry.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup by highlighting the precise locations where tensile and fatigue specimens were extracted from the printed wall. It provides a clear visual guide for the sampling strategy used to prepare material for subsequent mechanical testing, ensuring consistency in the specimen extraction process from the printed structure.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of TiC/Ti-alloy composites synthesized via directed energy deposition under varying process parameters.
summary: This panel displays the XRD patterns of TiC/Ti-alloy composites fabricated using directed energy deposition under different process conditions. These diffraction results indicate that variations in process parameters significantly influence the formation of the TiC phase within the composite matrix during the manufacturing process.

caption: Differential pulse voltammograms showing the oxidation of BCM at the SWP10 – 2.5 electrode in 0.12 M BR buffer at pH 4, across a concentration range of 0.2–40 µmol L–1.
summary: Differential pulse voltammograms for BCM oxidation at the SWP10 – 2.5 electrode are presented. The measurements were conducted in a 0.12 M BR buffer solution at pH 4, covering a concentration range of 0.2–40 µmol L–1. These voltammograms demonstrate the electrochemical response of the electrode to varying BCM concentrations.

caption: Temperature contour comparison for IN718 during the first track between the SA and FE models.
summary: This panel displays a comparative temperature contour map for IN718 material during the first track of a manufacturing process. It specifically contrasts the results obtained from the SA model against the FE model, highlighting differences in thermal distribution and the liquidus point marked by a white dashed line.

caption: Temperature-time profiles recorded during dilatometer testing, illustrating various heating rates ranging from 5 °C/s to 200 °C/s followed by a constant cooling rate of 100 °C/s.
summary: This plot displays the temperature history for dilatometer tests conducted at heating rates of 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, and 200 °C/s. All samples were subjected to a consistent cooling rate of 100 °C/s, demonstrating the controlled thermal cycles applied to characterize the material behavior under varying heating conditions.

caption: Calculated precipitation kinetics of the γ' phase in a NiCrAl alloy at 750 °C, illustrating the evolution of average volume fraction and precipitate size over time, with comparisons to experimental SXRD and STEM data for the AM state.
summary: This simulation tracks γ' precipitation kinetics in an fcc NiCrAl matrix at 750 °C. The results show predicted precipitate radius and volume fraction, highlighting nucleation site saturation as plateaus followed by coarsening. These calculated trends are validated against experimental SXRD and STEM measurements obtained from the AM state.

caption: Ternary phase diagram for the W–C–Co system specifically at a 10% cobalt content, indicating the thermodynamic stability regions relevant to sintering temperatures typically exceeding 1200 °C.
summary: The ternary phase diagram for the W–C–Co system with 10% cobalt content maps the thermodynamic landscape of the material. It serves as a reference for sintering, as the sintering temperature of cemented carbides is generally maintained above 1200 °C to ensure proper liquid-phase formation and densification within the stable phase regions.

caption: Detailed schematic of the contact explosion configuration, specifying the relative dimensions and positioning of the TNT charge and the target material.
summary: This schematic details the contact explosion configuration, explicitly defining the geometric relationship between the TNT explosive charge and the target titanium alloy. By specifying the sizes and positioning, the diagram provides essential context for the experimental parameters and the physical interaction between the explosive and the specimen.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for PLA/Mg composites with varying Mg content, illustrating mass loss as a function of temperature.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for PLA/Mg composites with varying Mg content illustrate mass loss as a function of temperature. All samples exhibit an initial mass loss after reaching 70 °C, which is attributed to the evaporation of the solvent, providing insight into the thermal stability of the composite materials.

caption: Cross-sectional morphology of the CG-10 specimen displaying the consolidated material state.
summary: Cross-sectional morphology of the CG-10 specimen displays the consolidated material state. Although some pores and lacks of fusion were detected, the sample maintains excellent metallurgical bonding, characterized by the lack of cracks or obvious boundaries between adjacent layers, confirming the structural integrity of the processed material.

caption: Rate capability profile of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//LiCoO2 full cell, showing specific discharge capacities of 173.1, 160.8, 133.8, 122.5, and 94.2 mAh g-1 at current densities ranging from 0.1C to 5C.
summary: The rate capability of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4//LiCoO2 full cell is evaluated across varying current densities. Specific discharge capacities are recorded as 173.1, 160.8, 133.8, 122.5, and 94.2 mAh g-1 at 0.1C, 0.3C, 0.5C, 1C, and 5C, respectively, demonstrating the device's performance under different discharge rates.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms comparing the thermal behavior of five 3D printed specimens: pure PLA, PLA/PBS blends at 90/10 and 80/20 ratios, and their corresponding DCP-crosslinked counterparts.
summary: This DSC analysis evaluates the thermal properties of five distinct 3D printed samples, including pure PLA, PLA/PBS blends, and DCP-modified variants. The curves illustrate the thermal response of these materials, providing insights into how the addition of PBS and DCP crosslinking agents influences the thermal characteristics of the printed structures.

caption: Training trajectory of the PEK-TD3 algorithm combining pre-training and expert knowledge.
summary: Panel c presents the training curve for the PEK-TD3 algorithm, which integrates both pre-training and expert knowledge. The reference confirms that this combined approach achieves superior and more stable dispatching effects compared to the expert knowledge driven TD3, demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed hybrid training strategy for the system.

caption: Comparison of scaled phonon density of states (DOS) for hcp-structured Fe at various compression points, featuring an analysis of data from Murphy et al. (2011a) on the left and scaling derived from Fei et al. (2016) on the right.
summary: This figure displays the phonon density of states for hcp-Fe, comparing measured data (black with error bars) against scaled theoretical predictions (red). The left panel analyzes Murphy et al. (2011a) data, while the right panel utilizes scaling factors derived from the vibrational properties reported by Fei et al. (2016) at 30 GPa.

caption: Surface strain fields (εxx) for the B-ZZ specimen loaded diagonally, displaying the strain evolution and fractured specimen.
summary: Diagonal loading of the B-ZZ specimen results in the strain fields shown in this panel. The DIC technique maps the εxx component of the Green-Lagrange strain tensor at various engineering strain steps. The panel concludes with the fractured specimen, providing a comprehensive view of the material's deformation and failure.

caption: FTIR spectral analysis of the materials captured at day 0, day 30, and day 45 of the disintegration test.
summary: FTIR spectra are presented for the studied materials at specific intervals of 0, 30, and 45 days. These spectroscopic results reveal chemical changes occurring within the material structure during the disintegration process, allowing for the identification of evolving functional groups and degradation products throughout the experimental testing period.

caption: Load–displacement curves for pristine and scCO2-aged 3D-printed PEEK samples under a 5 mN indentation load, highlighting the initial linear unloading region representing elastic recovery.
summary: This panel displays the load–displacement characteristics of pristine and scCO2-aged 3D-printed PEEK samples under a 5 mN indentation load. The initial linear region of the unloading curve is shown, which represents the elastic response where the material recovers its original shape upon the removal of the applied load.

caption: 3D atom map of the η-γ region in 2.5Hf, displaying an irregularly shaped η phase and Cr- and Co-enriched thin γ channels.
summary: The 3D atom map of the η-γ region in the 2.5Hf alloy highlights an irregularly shaped η phase. Additionally, the map identifies thin γ channels enriched with Cr and Co, which have an estimated thickness of 10 nm, illustrating the complex elemental distribution and phase morphology at the nanoscale.

caption: Relative displacement ΔL/L0 over time t for the X printing direction, showing experimental dilatometry results (top) and the comparison between experimental data, model predictions, and gravity-compensated model calculations (bottom).
summary: This panel displays the relative displacement over time for the X printing direction during dilatometry. It compares experimental dilatometry data with a material model, including a gravity-compensated version. The temperature profile is indicated by dashed and dotted curves, illustrating the thermal expansion behavior during the cooling phase of the experiment.

caption: High-magnification transmission electron microscopy image revealing the morphology of γ′′ monolith precipitates within the Inconel 718 matrix after heat treatment.
summary: High-magnification transmission electron microscopy imaging of heat-treated Inconel 718 reveals the presence of γ′′ monolith precipitates. These observations confirm that specific precipitate morphologies, including γ′′ monoliths, can be successfully formed across various processing routes such as directed energy deposition, providing insight into the microstructural evolution of the alloy.

caption: Shrinkage behavior of four distinct WC-FeNiCoCr alloy compositions plotted as a function of temperature.
summary: This dilatometric plot illustrates the shrinkage behavior of four WC-FeNiCoCr alloy compositions across a range of temperatures. The data confirm that compositions formulated with finer WC powders exhibit significantly higher shrinkage levels during the thermal process, highlighting the influence of initial powder particle size on the densification characteristics of these alloys.

caption: Transversal X-ray µ-CT slice of the CO50/30/20 specimen gauge section displaying cross-sectional morphology.
summary: The transversal X-ray µ-CT slice of the CO50/30/20 specimen displays the cross-sectional morphology after consolidation. This image, part of the comprehensive tomography analysis, shows modifications of the initial cylindrical morphology and allows for the assessment of the internal composite structure and fiber distribution within the gauge section.

caption: Normalized Root Mean Squared Error distribution for the CD,eq-Reeq empirical correlation, showing observed versus modeled settling velocities with standard deviation error bars.
summary: This parity plot displays the NRMSE for the CD,eq-Reeq correlation, comparing observed settling velocities to modeled values. Data points are marked with plus signs, while red error bars indicate the standard deviation of the distribution. This visualization helps assess the predictive accuracy of the empirical model across various particle shapes.

caption: Length change curves of Invar, MnCu, and their bimetallic structure measured from room temperature to 500 °C.
summary: This panel displays the length change curves for Invar, MnCu, and the bimetallic structure as temperature increases from room temperature to 500 °C. The data illustrates the thermal expansion behavior of each material, demonstrating that the expansion of the bimetallic structure consistently falls between that of the two constituent materials.

caption: Assembled orthorhombic TPMS unit cells where the in-plane cell aspect ratio is precisely modulated by the ratio of dimensions a to b.
summary: Assembled orthorhombic TPMS unit cells are shown, emphasizing the control of the in-plane cell aspect ratio through the a/b dimension ratio. This assembly demonstrates the practical application of the investigated topologies, including Schwarz' CLP and Schoen's I-6, I-8, and I-9 surfaces, within a structured, periodic lattice framework.

caption: Volume discretization of the specimen geometry using face mesh functions with a defined element size of 0.12 mm.
summary: Representing the coarsest discretization applied to the specimen, this panel shows the geometry meshed with an element size of 0.12 mm. This approach is employed for the remaining portions of the specimen to minimize computational cost while maintaining the overall structural integrity of the finite element simulation.

caption: Mechanical parameters, including stiffness and maximum nominal stress, for 11 × 11 unit cell OR graded structures.
summary: Mechanical parameters for 11 × 11 OR graded structures are presented. This visualization summarizes the stiffness and maximum nominal stress values, enabling an assessment of how the graded architecture influences the structural integrity and load-bearing capacity of the 11 × 11 unit cell designs.

caption: Spool of PLA-based Tm composite ceramic filaments procured from Wol 3D for additive manufacturing.
summary: This panel displays the spool of filaments utilized in the current project, which were procured from Wol 3D. These materials serve as the base for the study, focusing on the effect of layer thickness, infill density, and printing speed on the mechanical and surface properties of the composite ceramic parts.

caption: Room temperature photoluminescence emission spectra of SCC-1, SCC-2, and SCC-3 samples, showing consistent emission peaks centered at approximately 464.4 nm.
summary: The room temperature photoluminescence spectra for SCC-1, SCC-2, and SCC-3 samples are presented in panel a. These measurements reveal that all three composite samples exhibit similar emission signals, with characteristic peaks consistently located at approximately 464.4 nm, indicating comparable electronic transition properties across the different synthesized materials.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the alloy simulated using JMatPro software.
summary: This panel displays the equilibrium phase diagram for the alloy, which was generated through JMatPro simulation software. The diagram provides a theoretical representation of the stable phases present at various temperatures and compositions under equilibrium conditions, serving as a baseline for understanding the material's thermodynamic behavior.

caption: Normalized Bragg Edge heights for 316L-CuCrZr compositions, showing the transition from pure 316L to pure CuCrZr layers relative to a randomly oriented powder standard.
summary: Normalized Bragg Edge heights illustrate the transition from pure 316L layers through intermediate compositions to pure CuCrZr alloy layers. For the 316L part, the (400) planes exhibit the highest normalized intensity, while (220) and (311) planes show varying intensities, indicating a weak crystallographic texture in the 316L sample regions.

caption: Strain field distribution map at the interfaces of the sigma-II segment, projected along the [001] sigma // [111] gamma' direction.
summary: This strain field map characterizes the interface of the sigma-II segment along the [001] sigma // [111] gamma' direction. By comparing the strain distribution with the sigma-I segment, the figure highlights how different crystallographic orientations and defect quantities influence the local mechanical environment and strain accumulation at the sigma phase interfaces.

caption: Body Centered Cubic (BCC) unit cell topology representation for the scaffold constitutive unit.
summary: The Body Centered Cubic (BCC) unit cell is shown as a topology representation for the scaffold's constitutive unit. This classic lattice arrangement features a central node connected to eight corner nodes, providing a robust structural framework often used in scaffold design to balance stiffness and permeability requirements.

caption: Load-penetration responses for Ps-lattice sandwich structures at varying initial impact velocities, highlighting the structural resistance during penetration.
summary: Load-penetration plots depict the mechanical response of Ps-lattice sandwich structures subjected to three distinct impact velocities. These curves characterize the energy absorption and structural resistance of the core, showing how the load-displacement behavior evolves as the projectile penetrates the lattice structure under different initial kinetic energy conditions.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni-Cr-Mo system at 1173 K, showing the shift of the γ+NiMo+Ni3Mo three-phase region toward the Cr-rich side as Mo is substituted by Cr.
summary: This isothermal section at 1173 K illustrates the phase equilibrium in the Ni-Cr-Mo system. It highlights the expansion of the Ni3Mo phase region and the corresponding shift of the γ+NiMo+Ni3Mo three-phase field toward the Cr-rich composition as molybdenum is increasingly substituted by chromium within the ternary alloy system.

caption: Ray trajectories for a source translated in the y-direction by R'/2.
summary: Depicting the effect of source translation, this panel shows ray trajectories when the source is moved in the y-direction by R'/2. The simulation demonstrates how this shift influences the path of rays radiating from the aluminum sphere into the surrounding ice medium compared to the centered source position.

caption: Linearized Arrhenius plot displaying the natural logarithm of the rate constant (ln k) as a function of the inverse aging temperature (1/T aging) for Ti3Ni4 precipitation in a Ni–Ti alloy.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature dependence of Ti3Ni4 precipitation in a Ni–Ti alloy. By plotting ln(k) against the inverse aging temperature, the slope of the regression line is used to calculate the apparent activation energy, while the y-intercept provides the pre-exponential factor k0, characterizing the precipitation kinetics.

caption: The curve ρ(Q) plotted alongside black dots representing specific points b–g from Fig. 6a, with the corresponding mean albedo over Ωρ+ displayed on the right-hand y-axis and a green star indicating the maximum ρ value.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the ρ(Q) curve and the mean albedo over Ωρ+. Black dots correspond to points b–g from Fig. 6a, while a green star highlights the maximum ρ value. A clear pattern emerges where numerical values of ρ correlate with the mean albedo at these specific points.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the 15-5PH-AT sample, indicating an average grain size of 1.12 μm following austenite-to-martensite transformation.
summary: During the aging treatment, the austenite structure transforms into martensite, a phase transition that facilitates grain refinement and rearrangement. The grain size distribution histogram for the 15-5PH-AT sample confirms this structural evolution, resulting in a refined average grain size of 1.12 μm after the accumulation of transformation-induced changes.

caption: Thermal field distribution calculated at 60 ms following the deposition of the droplet.
summary: The thermal field distribution at 60 ms post-deposition is illustrated, representing the early stage of the solidification process. This panel is part of a sequence showing the evolution of the thermal field after the droplet is deposited, providing insight into the heat dissipation within the remelted zone.

caption: Simulated TTR diagram for the AM state at 750 °C compared with experimental data.
summary: This panel displays the time to rupture (TTR) diagram for the AM state at 750 °C. Solid lines represent the simulated results, while dashed lines indicate experimental measurements. The comparison illustrates the accuracy of the simulation in predicting the rupture behavior of the AM material under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Mass spectrometry profile corresponding to the thermal decomposition products of the printed PEG-0 thermoset during the STA process in air.
summary: Mass spectrometry data is presented here to characterize the gaseous decomposition products released from the printed PEG-0 thermoset during thermal analysis in air. These results, combined with the STA data, provide essential information for establishing the appropriate multi-step thermal treatment process required for the material's post-processing.

caption: Spatial distribution of elements within the CoCrFeNi alloy microstructure.
summary: This panel displays the elemental distribution map of the CoCrFeNi alloy, corresponding to the region shown in panel (a). It provides critical information regarding the actual chemical composition and homogeneity of the alloy, confirming the distribution of constituent elements within the observed microstructure.

caption: Representative 3D geometric model of the Diamond lattice structure used for additive manufacturing analysis.
summary: This panel displays the Diamond lattice structure, which serves as the geometric foundation for the subsequent shell thickness measurements. The structure is characterized by its specific unit cell arrangement, providing the basis for evaluating how various laser power process parameters influence the resulting strut dimensions and shell thickness.

caption: XPS survey spectrum of the corrosion product film on sample A2 after 21 days of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution, characterized by relatively weak peaks for Cu, Ni, Al, Fe, and Mn alongside a pronounced Cl peak.
summary: For sample A2, the XPS survey spectrum displays a pronounced Cl peak, while the signals for Cu, Ni, Al, Fe, and Mn are relatively weak after 21 days of immersion. This indicates a different surface composition compared to A1, with less intense contributions from the alloying elements.

caption: First derivative of the thermogravimetric analysis curves (DTG) for neat P(3HB) and composite films, highlighting the maximum rate of degradation.
summary: Derivative thermogravimetric analysis indicates that the maximum degradation rate occurs at lower temperatures for composites compared to neat P(3HB). The distinct early degradation peak observed in the P(3HB)/inkjet material suggests the presence of two lamellar phases, where thinner lamellae degrade at lower temperatures than the bulk material.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulation results showing the evolution of interfacial energy in systems containing graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs).
summary: Molecular dynamics simulation results demonstrate the evolution of interfacial energy in systems containing graphene nanoplatelets. These computational findings are consistent with the trends observed in experimental shear tests, confirming the influence of GNPs on the interfacial energy characteristics of the material system under investigation.

caption: Relaxed atomic structure of the IN718 brazing model after cooling to 300 K, where Cu atoms are positioned on the surface of the nickel-based superalloy.
summary: Representing the IN718 brazing model, this snapshot displays the relaxed atomic configuration after cooling to 300 K. The model demonstrates the interaction between the copper surface layer and the IN718 substrate, serving as a basis for analyzing the diffusion patterns and vacancy binding energies within the alloy system.

caption: M-T curves for #AC-168WQ Ni-Co-Mn-Sn powders, aged for 168 hours and water-quenched, measured under 50 Oe, 1 T, and 5 T magnetic fields.
summary: Following 168 hours of aging and water quenching, the #AC-168WQ Ni-Co-Mn-Sn powders display M-T curves across 50 Oe, 1 T, and 5 T fields. This panel completes the investigation into the effects of aging time and cooling rates on the magnetic properties of the Ni-Co-Mn-Sn alloy system.

caption: Resistivity curves of 3D-printed PLA-CB composites plotted against varying applied voltage for samples fabricated at temperatures between 230 °C and 280 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the resistivity of 3D-printed PLA-CB samples as a function of applied voltage. Printing temperatures from 230 °C to 260 °C generally improve electrical performance, whereas temperatures exceeding 270 °C result in performance degradation. These results highlight the sensitivity of electrical properties to the thermal processing conditions during fabrication.

caption: Detailed SEM view of the SLA 3D printed alumina micro-channel, revealing sintering domains smaller than 10 µm.
summary: This detailed SEM view of the SLA 3D printed alumina micro-channel highlights the fine microstructure of the material. The image reveals distinct sintering domains with diameters less than 10 µm, which are smaller than the residual metal particles observed on the SLS-produced stainless-steel plates.

caption: Atom probe tomography ion map of Alloy 625 in the solution-treated condition.
summary: This panel displays an atom probe tomography ion map of Alloy 625 following solution treatment. The reconstruction serves as the baseline microstructure for the material before undergoing thermal aging at 650 °C, providing a reference state for comparing the subsequent development of precipitates observed in the aged samples.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image highlighting the interface between TiB particles and the α phase.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) provides detailed visualization of the TiB particles and the α phase within the L-DED Ti55531 + 0.10B alloy. This imaging technique allows for the clear identification of the structural relationship between the TiB precipitates and the surrounding α phase matrix.

caption: Cycling performance comparison of annealed La2MgNi9, La1.9Mg1.1Ni9, and La1.8Mg1.2Ni9 alloy electrodes over 200 cycles at 100 mAh/g and room temperature, with an inset highlighting the initial 10 activation cycles.
summary: This plot illustrates the electrochemical cycling stability of annealed La-Mg-Ni alloy electrodes over 200 cycles at 100% depth of discharge. The data compares three compositions, showing their capacity retention behavior. An inset provides a detailed view of the first 10 activation cycles, characterizing the initial electrochemical performance of these materials.

caption: Corrosion fatigue crack growth rate (da/dN) versus stress intensity factor range (ΔK) for three oil-grade alloy 718 specimens tested in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at room temperature.
summary: Corrosion fatigue crack growth rates for three oil-grade alloy 718 specimens are shown for 3.5 wt.% NaCl at room temperature. Regression analysis indicates that aging treatments in Alloy 718–OSA and Alloy 718–TSA effectively reduce crack growth rates across the ΔK range compared to the Alloy 718–SA specimen.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the classification performance of the CNN algorithm applied to SEM bands without the inclusion of polluted data.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the classification accuracy of the CNN algorithm when processing SEM bands excluding polluted data. It provides the average prediction results and standard deviation for the model performance, serving as a baseline for evaluating the impact of data quality on the deep learning algorithm's predictive capabilities.

caption: Thermomagnetic curve of the uncoated Nd-Fe-B sample reacted for 8 months, showing altered magnetic behavior compared to the starting material.
summary: This panel illustrates the thermomagnetic curve for the uncoated Nd-Fe-B sample following an eight-month reaction period. The data provides a comparative view of how the absence of a coating affects the magnetic response of the material relative to the starting N42 Nd-Fe-B magnet and the coated variant.

caption: CLE values for ATC, DAH, and TLR lattice blocks, showing the comparative performance and the considerable standard deviation associated with each geometry.
summary: CLE values for the three different lattice blocks are illustrated here, revealing significant performance differences between the ATC, DAH, and TLR designs. The plot emphasizes the variability in these values by displaying considerable standard deviations, which underscores the sensitivity of the CLE metric to the specific lattice geometry tested.

caption: Log-log plot of strain rate versus Sinh(ασ), employed to investigate deformation mechanisms within the power law breakdown regime.
summary: This log-log plot of strain rate against Sinh(ασ) is used to investigate deformation mechanisms in the power law breakdown regime. The analysis suggests that dislocation-based deformation occurs in both regimes, specifically involving dislocation climb in the power law region and dislocation glide in the power law breakdown region.

caption: Mean force-time curve and associated standard deviation error bars for the Gyroid topology of SET-B, calculated from three distinct test repetitions.
summary: Gyroid topology specimens of SET-B demonstrate consistent mechanical performance under impact, as evidenced by the average force-time curve and standard deviation error bars. The data, averaged over three repetitions, confirms the repeatability of the results, while end-of-impact deviations caused by varying event durations are considered numerical artifacts and ignored.

caption: Optical micrograph of the SS316L-SLM specimen C-6 in the xz-plane, processed at a VED of 125 J/mm³.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the top region of the MIG sample.
summary: This histogram presents the grain size distribution for the top region of the MIG sample. It offers a statistical representation of the grain dimensions, which is critical for characterizing the microstructural properties of the MIG component as part of the broader material evaluation conducted in the study.

caption: XRD pattern of the Al0.5CrFeNi2.5Si0.25 alloy after annealing at 1023 K for 60 minutes followed by water quenching.
summary: Annealing the Al0.5CrFeNi2.5Si0.25 high-entropy alloy at 1023 K for 60 minutes, followed by water quenching, results in the displayed XRD pattern. This plot illustrates the structural changes and phase stability of the material under these specific thermal processing conditions compared to the as-cast state.

caption: Charge density difference (CDD) maps calculated along the (110) crystallographic plane for Cu6Sn5 and (Cu5.5Ni0.5)6Sn5 crystal structures.
summary: This panel displays the charge density difference (CDD) distribution along the (110) plane for Cu6Sn5 and (Cu5.5Ni0.5)6Sn5 crystal models. These simulation results illustrate the electronic structural changes occurring within the lattice when nickel is substituted into the copper-tin system, providing insight into the bonding characteristics of these intermetallic compounds.

caption: Surface profile image of the end part of the test specimen after 10 minutes of PXMEI-MFC processing, exhibiting an Ra value of 0.009 μm and an Sa value of 0.013 μm.
summary: Laser microscopy imaging of the test specimen end section following 10 minutes of PXMEI-MFC processing confirms consistent surface quality. The measured surface roughness parameters include an Ra value of 0.009 μm and an Sa value of 0.013 μm, highlighting the uniform processing results achieved across the specimen surface.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of the ASC device obtained at different potential windows while maintaining a constant current density of 5 A g⁻¹.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves are presented for the ASC device, tested at various potential windows. By keeping the current density fixed at 5 A g⁻¹, this panel illustrates the charging and discharging characteristics of the device, providing insight into its energy storage performance under different voltage constraints.

caption: Original grayscale cameraman image and the corresponding uncompensated resulting image as projected at the vat platform.
summary: The panel illustrates the projection of a complex grayscale cameraman image onto the vat platform without any compensation. The resulting image shows significant distortion compared to the original input, emphasizing the limitations of the projection system when handling detailed grayscale patterns without corrective image processing algorithms.

caption: Stress–strain curve comparison for the 20th percentile MAPE prediction, illustrating the ANN model performance at a low error threshold.
summary: Representing the 20th percentile MAPE, this panel shows the ANN-predicted stress–strain curve alongside the observed experimental data. This result highlights the model's capability to accurately capture the mechanical behavior of the lattice structures, maintaining a low error margin consistent with the overall performance evaluation of the neural network.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map displaying the spatial distribution of crystal plane orientations within the tensile-tested sample.
summary: This EBSD IPF map visualizes the variation in crystal plane orientation relative to the tensile direction. It serves as a structural characterization tool to understand how local crystallographic textures influence the mechanical response of the polycrystal, providing a basis for the subsequent rheological modeling of the material's deformation behavior.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the interdendrite region obtained using the (100) super-lattice spot, showing the bright ordered BCC matrix and the net-like disordered BCC phase.
summary: This dark-field TEM image, generated using the (100) super-lattice spot, provides structural confirmation of the phase distribution within the interdendrite region. The bright matrix corresponds to the ordered BCC phase, while the surrounding net-like structure is identified as the disordered BCC phase, consistent with the diffraction analysis.

caption: Surviving vacancies resulting from a 50 keV 2T-MD cascade in NiFe, visualized within a 196 Å cubic volume.
summary: Vacancies surviving after a 50 keV 2T-MD cascade in NiFe are shown within a 196 Å cubic volume. The 2T-MD model demonstrates a notable reduction in vacancy clustering compared to the classical MD approach, highlighting the influence of electronic-thermal coupling on the final damage state of the cascade.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns of FCCN alloy specimens at 77 K, showing intensity versus diffraction angle for the undeformed state, intermediate true strain levels, and the fractured state.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns of FCCN alloy specimens at 77 K are presented for various true strain levels, ranging from the undeformed state to fracture. These ex-situ patterns, collected at room temperature, illustrate the structural evolution and phase changes occurring in the material as it undergoes tensile deformation at cryogenic temperatures.

caption: Temporal evolution of current density at 1.2 V for the STF-Ni SOC, demonstrating the long-term stability and performance decay over 162 hours.
summary: The STF-Ni SOC exhibits improved durability compared to the STF cell, showing a 15% decrease in current density from -300 mA/cm2 to -255 mA/cm2 over 162 hours. The cell demonstrates a stabilization trend starting at hour 150, indicating superior long-term performance and robustness in co-electrolysis conditions.

caption: Semi-logarithmic plots of anodic current versus time responses for La2MgNi9, La1.9Mg1.1Ni9, and La1.8Mg1.2Ni9 alloy electrodes measured at 0.6 V, showing two distinct regions separated by a black line.
summary: Semi-logarithmic curves of anodic current versus time responses are shown for the annealed alloy electrodes at 0.6 V. These potentiostatic step-size measurements were used to evaluate the hydrogen diffusion coefficient. The curves exhibit two distinct regions separated by a black line, reflecting the kinetics of the charging/discharging reactions.

caption: STEM micrograph of the as-deposited (AD) specimen highlighting the initial carbide morphology and the location of EDS point analysis spots.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the as-deposited specimen, focusing on the structural characteristics of carbides. EDS point analysis was performed on specific spots within the microstructure to determine the chemical composition of these carbides, providing baseline data for comparing the elemental distribution and phase evolution between the as-deposited and heat-treated conditions.

caption: Nanohardness distribution measured across the interface of sample 4, with specific values in GPa indicated by marked points.
summary: This panel illustrates the nanohardness distribution across the interface of sample 4. By marking specific points with their corresponding values in GPa, the graph provides a clear representation of the mechanical hardness profile, enabling a direct comparison of the interface properties for this particular sample.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plot for the Zr–2.5Nb alloy, illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance response in SBF.
summary: This Bode impedance magnitude plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for the Zr–2.5Nb alloy in SBF. Together with the Nyquist and phase plots, it provides a comprehensive view of the alloy's corrosion behavior under stable OCP conditions, facilitating the subsequent equivalent circuit fitting process.

caption: Micro-CT reconstructions visualizing the extent of tissue repair, with scale bars of 5 mm for the upper rows and 3 mm for the lower rows.
summary: Micro-CT reconstructions provide a visual assessment of tissue repair progress in the bone defect model. The images, captured at varying scales, demonstrate the spatial distribution of newly formed bone. These reconstructions confirm that the PHCZ group exhibits superior trabecular formation and effective osteogenic activity compared to other experimental conditions.

caption: Geometry specifications for the tensile specimen used in uniaxial testing on a universal testing machine.
summary: The geometry of the tensile specimen used for uniaxial testing is detailed in this schematic. These specimens were utilized on a Shimadzu AGS-X universal testing machine with a 10 kN capacity to evaluate the mechanical properties of the fabricated Ti/Al laminates under controlled loading conditions as specified in the study.

caption: Inclined printed truss structure demonstrating support-free fabrication capabilities.
summary: This panel illustrates an inclined printed truss structure. As part of a support-free fabrication method, this printing orientation showcases the versatility of the manufacturing approach. The design is particularly relevant for in-space manufacturing applications, where minimizing support material is critical for efficient and autonomous production of complex structural components.

caption: Property diagram illustrating thermal fatigue resistance performance for terminal alloys and binary gradients, where a dashed isocontour line delineates performance levels and movement toward the lower right indicates enhanced resistance.
summary: This property diagram visualizes thermal fatigue resistance for various terminal alloys and their binary gradients. The plot utilizes a dashed isocontour to represent performance thresholds, where trajectories moving from the upper left to the lower right signify improved thermal fatigue resistance. CGA property trajectories exhibit nonlinear trends with composition-dependent variability.

caption: Neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain ε22 in a hot-machined specimen.
summary: This panel displays the residual elastic strain ε22 measured via neutron diffraction for a hot-machined part. The data reveals stronger compressive strains at the wall edges compared to the cold-machined condition, providing experimental validation for the predictive modeling of residual stresses within the machined cross-section.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map highlighting the spatial concentration of Al across the TLP joint interface.
summary: Al distribution within the TLP joint is visualized through this EPMA map, corresponding to the 1130 °C, 30-minute bonding condition. This analysis is essential for characterizing the element distribution across the joint, contributing to the overall understanding of the chemical composition and structural integrity of the bonded interface.

caption: Gibbs energy evolution as a function of temperature for carbothermal reduction reactions of various oxides within WC-FeNiCoCr powder mixtures, calculated using the Thermocalc SSUB4 database.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the Gibbs energy changes associated with the carbothermal reduction of oxides in WC-FeNiCoCr powder mixtures. The data, derived from the Thermocalc SSUB4 database, indicates that the carbothermal reduction of Cr2O3 into Cr and CO products becomes thermodynamically favorable only at temperatures exceeding 1265 °C.

caption: Arc morphology observed at an excitation current of 0A.
summary: This panel displays the arc morphology during the additive manufacturing process at an excitation current of 0A. The image serves as a baseline for comparing the interaction between charged particles in the arc and the magnetic field, illustrating the arc's shape in the absence of external magnetic influence.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay curve and fitting analysis for TPU/3S composite, measured at 490 nm emission wavelength.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime decay and fitting analysis for the TPU/3S composite are illustrated at an emission wavelength of 490 nm. The data reflects the luminescence characteristics of the material at room temperature, allowing for a comparative assessment of how increased SAOED loading influences the fluorescence decay kinetics of the TPU matrix.

caption: Convergence behavior of global force–displacement curves for the double-notched specimen across varying mesh refinements.
summary: Global force–displacement curves for the double-notched specimen are presented to evaluate mesh sensitivity. The results demonstrate that the curves tend to converge toward a unique, stable solution as the mesh is refined, confirming the consistency of the numerical model across different discretization levels.

caption: Optimized molecular structure of Bisphenol A (BPA) showing the spatial arrangement of oxygen, carbon, and hydrogen atoms.
summary: The optimized structure of BPA is presented, illustrating the atomic configuration of the molecule. Oxygen, carbon, and hydrogen atoms are represented by red, gray, and white colors, respectively. This structural model serves as the baseline for subsequent electronic property calculations and reactivity analysis performed in the study.

caption: Experimental platform designed for electromagnetic coupling treatment, featuring integrated electric and magnetic field generation units alongside a coupling execution unit.
summary: The electromagnetic coupling treatment (EMCT) experiment platform is displayed, highlighting its primary components. It consists of an electric and magnetic field generating unit paired with a coupling execution unit. This setup provides the necessary infrastructure to perform the electromagnetic coupling treatment process as described in the experimental methodology.

caption: Designed 3D model of the 3 × 3 × 3 TO structure array.
summary: The 3D model displays a 3 × 3 × 3 assembly of the topologically optimized unit cells. This configuration represents the macroscopic lattice architecture designed for mechanical evaluation. Following the additive manufacturing process, these structures underwent thermal treatment at 750 °C for 1 hour to relieve residual stresses and stabilize the material phase.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility of CeNiZnH 1.2 measured at a constant field of 0.05 T, showing a notable enhancement in χ(T) below 5 K without evidence of magnetic ordering down to 1.8 K.
summary: The magnetic susceptibility of CeNiZnH 1.2 measured at 0.05 T exhibits an enhancement below 5 K, yet no clear magnetic ordering is observed down to 1.8 K. This temperature-dependent behavior characterizes the material's magnetic response in the low-temperature regime, indicating the absence of a phase transition in this range.

caption: Magnified view of the honeycomb core specimen during the loading process, highlighting the structural response captured by high-speed imaging.
summary: This magnified view shows the honeycomb core specimen undergoing a three-point bending test. The high-speed camera captures the dynamic deformation processes of the honeycomb structure as flexural loads are applied, allowing for detailed observation of the specimen's mechanical response during the experimental procedure.

caption: Parity plot comparing actual versus predicted printing times for five arbitrary groups selected from the dataset to evaluate model performance.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the predictive effectiveness of the model by comparing actual printing times against predicted values. By selecting five arbitrary groups from the dataset, the figure demonstrates the model's accuracy in estimating processing durations, providing a clear visual assessment of the predictive performance across different experimental conditions.

caption: Transmission spectrum of sample 2, showing the optical characteristics post-UV exposure.
summary: Sample 2 exhibits a transmission spectrum that reflects its optical response after UV light exposure. The results demonstrate consistent trends in the transmission profile, confirming that the sample's optical properties remain stable and unchanged when subjected to the UV light degradation test, matching the behavior observed in the other samples.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating action recognition performance for the video dataset at a resolution of 384x384 pixels.
summary: This confusion matrix displays the action recognition performance for the video dataset processed at 384x384 resolution. Diagonal values represent the proportion of correctly classified instances for each of the 11 action classes, while off-diagonal values indicate the proportion of misclassifications, providing a detailed assessment of the model's classification accuracy.

caption: Atomic unit cell model representing the Mg2Cu intermetallic phase.
summary: This panel illustrates the unit cell structure of the Mg2Cu intermetallic phase. As part of the structural analysis of various phases, this model helps define the crystalline nature of the material, with its lattice constants being documented in the accompanying table for reference and further study.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the classification results for the real-time approach implemented with an ANN, yielding a prediction accuracy of 92.7%.
summary: The confusion matrix for the real-time approach using an ANN is shown here, highlighting a prediction accuracy of 92.7%. This panel serves as a key component in the comparative evaluation of machine learning models for real-time classification, providing insight into the model's predictive capabilities and error distribution.

caption: Tabulated summary of selected metallic alloys, detailing their respective operating temperature ranges and the specific manufacturing approaches employed for each material.
summary: This table provides a systematic overview of eleven representative metallic alloys, comprising five additive manufacturing (AM) alloys and six conventionally manufactured alloys. It explicitly correlates each material with its functional operating temperature range and the specific manufacturing process used, facilitating a comparative analysis of material performance across diverse thermal conditions.

caption: Number of surviving displaced atoms as a function of Fe concentration in Ni-xFe alloys, evaluated at irradiation dose levels of 0.003, 0.07, and 0.13 dpa via molecular dynamics simulations.
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations illustrate the number of surviving displaced atoms, defined as those remaining at off-lattice positions, across Ni, Ni-20Fe, Ni-50Fe, and Ni-60Fe alloys. The data tracks these surviving defects as a function of iron concentration under varying irradiation dose levels of 0.003, 0.07, and 0.13 dpa to assess radiation damage resistance.

caption: Predicted versus measured particle number concentration at 850 °C, highlighting the scatter induced by chemical composition tolerances in IN738LC.
summary: Particle number concentration is plotted against time to compare experimental measurements with simulation predictions. The data reveals significant scatter in predicted behavior due to chemical composition variations, which is most pronounced during the transition from a bi-modal to a unimodal particle size distribution within the transient coarsening regime.

caption: Electron charge density profiles calculated through the center of the RTD cross-sections for symmetric barrier thicknesses of 2 nm, 3 nm, and 4 nm.
summary: Electron charge density within the quantum well is shown to be highly dependent on barrier thickness. caption: Comparison of total acceptance rates for undoped and doped systems, categorized by MC move types where moves 1 and 4 represent metallic swaps and moves 2 and 3 represent B or C movement, with an inset showing unweighted atomic motion contributions from the +TiB2 simulation.
summary: This panel contrasts the final acceptance rates for metallic atom moves (1 and 4) against B or C atom moves (2 and 3) in undoped and doped systems. An inset from the +TiB2 simulation provides an unweighted perspective on which specific species contribute most significantly to the overall atomic motion observed.

caption: SR-PXD Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.45Fe0.55NiSi0.95Al0.05 at 310 K.

caption: Beeswarm plot of SHAP values for MSAD regression descriptors, depicting the individual sample contributions for each feature.
summary: The beeswarm plot provides a detailed view of the SHAP values for the MSAD regression model across different samples. By plotting individual SHAP values for each descriptor, this visualization illustrates the range and direction of feature influence, offering insight into how specific variables drive the MSAD regression predictions.

caption: Volumetric XCT model of three sectioned gear teeth.
summary: This panel displays a volumetric XCT model representing three sectioned gear teeth. The visualization provides a comprehensive 3D overview of the gear geometry, serving as the foundational structural representation for subsequent detailed porosity analysis conducted across the sectioned samples using X-ray computed tomography scanning techniques.

caption: Power versus temperature plot for the transition region between alloy 42 and 46, demonstrating the absence of a distinct jump in power.
summary: This panel illustrates the power versus temperature plot for the specimen taken from the transition region between alloy 42 and 46. caption: Comparison of laser absorptivity curves between the first and second layers processed at 390W and 1.2 ms-1, highlighting the temporal evolution of the laser-material interaction starting from 200 μs.
summary: This figure displays the absorptivity curves for the first and second layers during laser processing at 390W and 1.2 ms-1. It illustrates the temporal evolution of the laser-material interaction, noting that the pink point of laser impact becomes visible from 200 μs onwards, providing a comparative analysis of energy absorption.

caption: High-resolution Fe2p XPS spectrum of the surface corrosion product film on specimen A1 after 21 days of immersion.
summary: This panel displays the high-resolution Fe2p XPS spectrum for specimen A1. The data, collected after 21 days of immersion, characterizes the chemical state of iron within the surface corrosion product film, providing essential spectroscopic evidence regarding the surface composition and oxidation states of the corrosion products formed on the material.

caption: Three-dimensional array configuration consisting of a 3 × 3 × 3 arrangement of the unit cells.
summary: Depicted here is a 3 × 3 × 3 array composed of the unit cells shown in panel (a). This assembly demonstrates the periodic arrangement of the metamaterial, illustrating how individual unit cells are organized to form the larger, functional 3D mechanical metamaterial structure for further analysis and testing.

caption: Volta potential map of the cathodically hydrogen-precharged HT+H sample after 200 hours of hydrogen desorption in open air.
summary: Representing the same zone as panel a, this map shows the HT+H sample after 200 hours of hydrogen desorption. A distinct potential contrast emerges after this extended period in open air, suggesting that hydrogen desorption or redistribution processes have significantly altered the surface potential characteristics compared to the initial state.

caption: Relative density Drel map as a function of laser beam power P and scanning speed v, with overlaid contour lines representing line energy El in J/m.
summary: This contour map illustrates the relative density of the material as a function of laser power and scanning speed. The data indicates that relative density is predominantly governed by the line energy, where higher energy inputs facilitate the creation of dense parts, while lower energy inputs result in porous structures.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots of the passive films on Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb, displaying acceptor density (NA) variations that confirm the formation of highly defective films under transpassive conditions compared to protective films formed at 0.6 V.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots of the passive films on Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb display acceptor density variations that confirm the formation of highly defective films under transpassive conditions. The vacancy density of the film formed at 0.9 V is four times higher than that of the protective passive film formed at 0.6 V.

caption: Calculated ternary Ni–Ti–Nb phase diagram at 900 °C, derived from diffusion couple data between Ni–Ti and Ni–Nb alloys.
summary: This ternary phase diagram for the Ni–Ti–Nb system at 900 °C was generated using data from a series of diffusion couples between Ni–Ti and Ni–Nb alloys. The diagram provides a comprehensive representation of phase equilibria at this specific temperature, as calculated by Guanjun and Shiming.

caption: EBSD grain map highlighting equiaxed grains smaller than 30 μm for the 0.06 mm layer thickness condition.
summary: EBSD mapping for the 0.06 mm layer thickness specimen identifies and highlights equiaxed grains smaller than 30 μm. This visualization distinguishes these smaller, randomly oriented grains from the dominant elongated columnar structure, facilitating a quantitative assessment of the grain morphology and distribution within the material's microstructure along the building direction.

caption: Surface appearance and cross-sectional microstructure of the UAM sample processed with 10A current.
summary: Application of 10A current results in a sample surface with relatively uniform texture features. Although the Ti foil remains damaged, a significant reduction in the number of interfacial unbound regions is observed compared to the sample processed without current, suggesting improved bonding at the Ti/Al interface.

caption: Geometric configuration of the lattice specimen for fatigue testing, incorporating a specific setup of X-I struts.
summary: The lattice specimen geometry is presented for fatigue testing applications. Based on the established design concepts, this configuration utilizes a cyclic base lattice that incorporates an X-I strut arrangement. This specific geometry serves as the primary specimen model for evaluating the mechanical performance of the lattice structure.

caption: Normalised permeation current density transients for 4340 steel under varying fabrication conditions in 0.1 M NaOH, showing experimental data as dashed lines and MATLAB-generated mathematical fits as solid lines.
summary: This panel displays normalised permeation current density transients for 4340 steel in 0.1 M NaOH. The high fitting accuracy between experimental data and mathematical curves indicates that hydrogen diffusion is not strongly influenced by traps, highlighting the impact of fabrication processes on the material's hydrogen diffusion behaviour.

caption: High-energy (200 W, 500 mm/s, E L = 0.4 J/mm) melt-view response data for a rectangle geometry, showing signal values for hatch vectors at 0°, 45°, and 90°.
summary: High-energy processing conditions result in a significantly improved fit between the experimental and model data compared to the low-energy case. The relative magnitude of signal noise is substantially reduced, providing a clearer representation of the melt-pool signal values across the various hatch vector orientations within the rectangle geometry.

caption: High-speed camera sequence capturing the dynamic metal transfer process during a single CMT short-circuit cycle.
summary: High-speed camera imaging reveals the dynamic metal transfer process during the CMT mode. The sequence captures the arc morphology and the progression of a single short-circuit cycle, beginning at time T0. This visual record provides a detailed observation of the arc shape and material transfer behavior during the CMT process.

caption: Continuous cooling diagram for Ti–6Al–4V illustrating various cooling curves corresponding to different scanning speeds.
summary: This diagram displays the continuous cooling behavior of Ti–6Al–4V alloy. It presents multiple cooling curves, labeled 1 through 5, which represent different scanning speeds. These curves serve as a reference for understanding how varying thermal processing parameters influence the cooling rates and subsequent phase transformations in the material.

caption: Morphological changes observed in printed grid specimens affixed to a universal testing machine before and after undergoing uniaxial longitudinal stretching.
summary: Printed grid specimens are shown mounted on a universal testing machine to facilitate uniaxial tensile testing. caption: C distribution map of region E, illustrating carbon concentration in the localized microstructure.
summary: This carbon distribution map for region E provides insight into the spatial arrangement of C. The map helps characterize the composition of the various particles and gray regions identified in the microstructure, supporting the overall elemental analysis of the localized features within the sample.

caption: High-speed camera image of the UHFP arc morphology showing the droplet immediately prior to contacting the molten pool.
summary: This high-speed image depicts the arc morphology under UHFP conditions as the droplet approaches the molten pool. caption: Inverse pole figure map illustrating the crystallographic orientation of the sample, where the white circle marks the area chosen for milling a micro-pillar oriented along the [111] direction.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the sample, where the white circle marks the area chosen for milling a micro-pillar oriented along the [111] direction.
