caption: Shape-morphing behavior of a bilayer silane-treated decellularized leaf composite, consisting of GO/nanoclay/PNIPAM hydrogels, showing swelling at 22 °C and deswelling under UV irradiation at approximately 1 W/cm².
summary: The bilayer nanocomposite structure demonstrates excellent shape-morphing capabilities driven by environmental stimuli. The material undergoes swelling at room temperature and rapid deswelling when exposed to UV light. This tunable response highlights the effectiveness of the GO/nanoclay/PNIPAM hydrogel system for responsive soft material applications.

caption: Survey XPS scan of NiMoO and NiMo-400 samples showing the presence of Ni, Mo, and O elements.
summary: The survey XPS scan provides a broad overview of the surface chemical composition for both non-annealed NiMoO and thermally reduced NiMo-400. This analysis confirms the presence of nickel, molybdenum, and oxygen, establishing the elemental foundation for the subsequent high-resolution investigations into the specific valence states of the materials.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the metallic matrix, showing grain orientation distribution relative to the loading axis.
summary: Inverse Pole Figure mapping displays the grain orientation distribution within the metallic matrix relative to the loading axis. caption: Coefficient of friction profile for the 0Y2O3 as-printed sample pin against an alumina disk, showing significant fluctuations during the initial sliding distance before reaching a steady state after the dashed line.
summary: The 0Y2O3 as-printed sample exhibits a coefficient of friction curve characterized by significant fluctuations, which are attributed to plowing effects during the initial sliding distance. caption: Ion map of a 5 nm thick slice from the 3D atom probe reconstruction showing Fe partitioning between the matrix and L12 precipitates in the 60CRA condition.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction displays a 5 nm thick slice of a non-recrystallized region in the 60CRA condition. The ion map highlights the distinct partitioning of Fe ions, represented by dark pink points, between the matrix and the L12 precipitates, confirming the structural distribution within the material.

caption: Comparative analysis of oxygen capacities for CAT-P and SUL-P during the 10th redox cycle, distinguishing between oxidation and reduction phases.
summary: Comparing the oxygen capacities of CAT-P and SUL-P during the 10th redox cycle reveals distinct performance differences. caption: Validation of manufacturing speed parameters relative to build plate transverse location, showing Batch 1 and Batch 2 data with 3-sigma confidence intervals.
summary: This panel displays the validation of manufacturing speed parameters across the build plate's transverse direction. Using Monte-Carlo simulation, the plot illustrates the variation between Batch 1 and Batch 2 samples. The inclusion of 3-sigma confidence intervals highlights the statistical spread of the manufacturing data relative to sample placement.

caption: Log-log plot of strain rate versus applied stress for AlSc 1.1 alloy pre-annealed at 250 °C.
summary: Creep measurements for the AlSc 1.1 alloy pre-annealed at 250 °C are displayed as strain rate versus applied stress. caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells stained with AM/PI after 3 days of culture on scaffolds, showing viable cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells stained with AM/PI after 3 days of culture on scaffolds reveal the distribution of viable and dead cells. caption: Quasi-static nanoindentation curves for Ti41Zr41Ni18 coatings at limit loads ranging from 25 to 41 mN, highlighting the influence of annealing temperature on indentation depth and energy dissipation.
summary: This panel presents the load-displacement curves at higher limit loads of 25–41 mN for the Ti41Zr41Ni18 coatings. It contrasts the as-deposited amorphous sample with the annealed samples. summary: This plot displays the peak value of the p n distribution as a function of the powder feeding rate. The data reveals that the influence of the gas flow rate on the powder stream undergoes a notable change in behavior at a critical feeding rate of approximately 11.8 g/min.

caption: Axial strain-time histories extracted from full-field digital image correlation (DIC) analysis for top-clad and sandwich sample configurations under 13 mm impactor loading.

summary: This panel illustrates the calculated phase diagram for the Al–7Si–4Cu–1Ni alloy containing a combined addition of 0.25 wt% Mg and 0.25 wt% Mn. summary: This panel shows the PDOS for the d-band of a labeled Ni atom on a clean Au-Ni (1 0 0) alloy surface. The data serves as a reference for the electronic state of the Ni atom prior to CO interaction, allowing for a clear assessment of orbital hybridization changes upon adsorption.

summary: Captured at 0.001 seconds after detonation, this high-speed photograph of trial number 5 displays the explosive event. caption: Surface topography of the ground sample annealed at 550 °C, captured via laser confocal microscopy.
summary: Surface topography of the ground sample after 550 °C annealing is presented using laser confocal microscopy. This image illustrates the combined effects of mechanical grinding and thermal oxidation on surface roughness, facilitating an analysis of the material's transformation grade following the specified oxidising procedure at this temperature.

caption: Laser reflectance spectra of gas-atomized AA2017 powder compared to TiC surface-functionalized variants across the 250–950 nm wavelength range.
summary: This plot displays the laser reflectance of gas-atomized and TiC surface-functionalized AA2017 powders. Functionalization with TiC particles and associated changes in surface roughness and chemistry lead to decreased reflectance. Furthermore, the data indicates that reflectance decreases as the size of the TiC particles used for functionalization is refined.

caption: Equivalent electrical circuit model used to simulate the impedance spectra of anodized 3D samples.
summary: This panel shows the equivalent electrical circuit model utilized to simulate the impedance spectra of anodized 3D samples. The circuit parameters are derived from the impedance data, enabling a detailed analysis of the electrochemical behavior and the protective nature of the anodized layer formed on the samples.

caption: Grain boundary misorientation distribution histogram derived from the EBSD data presented in panel (b).
summary: This histogram illustrates the distribution of orientation differences for the Ni–50%Cu alloy at 280 K. As referenced in the study, this distribution provides a quantitative measure of the grain boundary misorientations, complementing the visual orientation data to characterize the alloy's microstructure at this specific undercooling level.

caption: Infrared spectrogram comparing the chemical structure of the polymer before and after ultrasonic treatment.
summary: The infrared spectrogram compares the polymer before and after ultrasound. The reference highlights a reduction in the intensity of the characteristic infrared absorption peak of the double bond at 810 cm-1 in TPGDA, providing strong evidence for the crosslinking of the polymer chains via free radicals during ultrasonic irradiation.

caption: Fatigue performance of L-PBF Ti-64 specimens grouped by part location, where central specimens generally exhibit superior performance compared to north and south locations.
summary: Fatigue behavior is analyzed here based on the specific part location within the L-PBF build. The data indicates that central specimens typically demonstrate better fatigue performance than those located in the north or south positions. Grip-failed specimens are identified by inclined arrows to ensure accurate interpretation of the fatigue trends.

caption: Calculated Al-Ti binary phase diagram illustrating the equilibrium relationships between aluminum and titanium phases.
summary: This Al-Ti binary phase diagram was generated using Pandat software to identify potential intermetallic compounds (IMCs) that may form at joint interfaces. The diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the equilibrium phases present in the Al-Ti system, serving as a critical reference for analyzing material interactions and phase stability during processing.

caption: Progressive grain coarsening observed along the stem of the Ta2 electrode.
summary: Panel e captures the intermediate grain structure along the Ta2 electrode stem. The image highlights the progressive coarsening of grains as the distance from the base increases. This structural change is representative of the overall trend observed in both Ta1 and Ta2 electrodes during the experimental process.

caption: Chronopotentiogram of the NG-2 experiment depicting the electrode potential response during the dissolution process.
summary: This chronopotentiogram illustrates the electrode potential evolution for the NG-2 experiment. Consistent with the overall experimental findings, the potentials remained below the cathode potential, which confirms that no reduction of Cr or Fe took place during the anodic dissolution process, maintaining the stability of the electrochemical environment.

caption: Radar chart displaying the relative frequency of occurrence for significant keywords and keyphrases extracted from the research work.
summary: This radar chart quantifies the relative frequency of significant keywords and keyphrases identified in the research. By mapping these frequencies, the visualization provides a clear overview of the most prevalent topics discussed in the study of strength–ductility aspects in additively manufactured alloys, emphasizing the statistical relevance of the terminology.

caption: Relative length change (ΔL/L0) curve for the E-X structure over a complete thermal cycle, with pointed lines 1, 2, and 3 identifying reproducible kinks observed at specific temperatures.
summary: The relative length change curve for structure E-X is shown across a full thermal cycle. Pointed lines 1, 2, and 3 highlight specific, reproducible kinks in the expansion behavior. These features indicate distinct thermal response events occurring at consistent temperatures throughout the measurement process for this specific unit cell structure.

caption: Frequency-dependent absorption coefficients for the graded, uniform, and linear porosity TPMS structures, illustrating the broadband performance improvements achieved through grading.
summary: This graph presents the absorption coefficients for the three TPMS structure profiles defined in panel (b). It serves as a performance metric, showing how the graded porosity design achieves superior broadband absorption characteristics compared to the uniform and linear-gradient configurations over the analyzed frequency range.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of pBMSCs cultured on 3D-printed β-TCP scaffolds after 7 days, highlighting regions with elongated, oriented cells and abundant ECM synthesis.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of pBMSCs cultured on 3D-printed β-TCP scaffolds after 7 days, highlighting regions with elongated, oriented cells and abundant ECM synthesis. The viability of the cells on the scaffolds was confirmed by fluorescent microscopy observation, demonstrating intensive synthesis of ECM by pBMSCs and pronounced cell metabolic activity.

caption: HRSTEM imaging of the cell wall, including two magnified regions and an FFT pattern highlighting a ring structure with an arrow.
summary: High-resolution STEM imaging of the cell wall provides atomic-scale insight into the microstructure. The inclusion of an FFT pattern with a marked ring structure confirms the presence of specific crystallographic features, which are further analyzed to understand the local orientation and phase distribution within the cell wall.

caption: Evolution of average grain diameter and compression axis grain dimension during deformation at 1070 °C and 1.2 mm/s for initial grain sizes of 860 μm and 1840 μm.
summary: This panel displays simulated grain equivalent diameter and grain dimensions along the compression axis during double-cone deformation at 1070 °C. The results calibrate the evolution of grain size for two distinct initial prior β-grain sizes of 860 μm and 1840 μm, providing critical data for understanding microstructural changes during high-temperature deformation.

caption: Ashby plot comparing density versus specific energy absorption (SEA) for the proposed OIPLs against various state-of-the-art lattice structures.
summary: This Ashby plot benchmarks the specific energy absorption (SEA) of proposed OIPLs against a wide range of existing lattice structures, including truss, shell-strut TPMS, plate, and origami-based designs. The plot effectively demonstrates the performance of the OIPLs relative to current state-of-the-art materials in terms of density and energy efficiency.

caption: Radar plot comparing the multi-metric acoustic performance of bioinspired stochastic minimal-surface metamaterials against traditional acoustic foams.
summary: This radar plot provides a comparative analysis of acoustic performance metrics between bioinspired stochastic minimal-surface metamaterials and traditional acoustic foams. By evaluating multiple functional criteria, the visualization highlights the performance advantages of the metamaterial design, following established methodologies to assess how these structures overcome limitations inherent in conventional acoustic materials.

caption: Experimental and modeled ellipsometric parameters Psi and Delta for ZnTe thin films (x = 0.0).
summary: This panel displays the experimental and modeled ellipsometric parameters Psi and Delta for pure ZnTe thin films. The data fitting utilizes Cauchy and effective medium approximation models to determine the optical constants and film thickness, providing a theoretical basis for characterizing the optical properties of the undoped material.

caption: Neutron diffraction measurement of residual strain in the cold-machined part.
summary: Experimental neutron diffraction data illustrates the residual strain state of the cold-machined part. These measurements are compared against model predictions to assess the fidelity of the 5 mm coarse-mesh simulation, particularly regarding the alternating tensile and compressive strain patterns observed in the center of the specimen.

caption: Variation of TiO2 coating thickness as a function of withdrawal speed, showing a range from 30 to 90 nm for speeds between 5 and 20 cm/min.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between withdrawal speed and TiO2 coating thickness. Ellipsometry measurements indicate that increasing the withdrawal speed from 5 cm/min to 20 cm/min results in a thickness variation ranging from 30 nm to 90 nm, while speeds exceeding 50 cm/min lead to film cracking.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded on a 2D carbon fiber (CF) substrate at a sweep rate of 10 mV/s between -0.4 and -1.4 V (vs. SCE) in three distinct electrolyte solutions containing Ni2+, Sn2+, or a mixture of both.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms on 2D CF substrates reveal the electrodeposition mechanisms of Ni and Sn. The curves demonstrate that Ni reduction is highly sensitive to substrate morphology, while Sn deposition remains relatively stable. These electrochemical measurements provide insight into the deposition behavior of individual and mixed metal ions on planar surfaces.

caption: Reconstructed micro-CT image of the RE-UD specimen at mid-height, revealing pronounced mortar deterioration.
summary: At mid-height, the RE-UD specimen exhibits significant mortar deterioration as captured by micro-CT imaging. This visualization highlights a more pronounced damage state compared to the RE-UR specimen, underscoring the influence of specimen design on the internal failure mechanisms and the extent of mortar degradation under load.

caption: Top surface morphology of a single track in Region C, demonstrating continuous track formation with minimal irregularity.
summary: Panel g shows an optical micrograph of a single track in Region C. The track is continuous with minimal irregularity. This observation is consistent with the classification of Region C tracks, which are characterized by improved stability compared to the discontinuous or severely irregular tracks found in other regions.

caption: Magnetization versus temperature curves measured at 2 T for precursor ribbons and the SPS sample, illustrating the heating and cooling pathways under high-field conditions.
summary: This panel displays the M(T) curves measured at 2 T following zero-field-cooled and field-cooled thermal protocols. The graph illustrates the heating and cooling pathways for both the precursor ribbons and the SPS sample, providing a high-field perspective on the magnetic behavior and thermal hysteresis of the materials.

caption: Schematic representation of bent CCF-PEEK composite rasters printed at various angles ranging from 45 to 150 degrees.
summary: This schematic illustrates the printing geometry for bent CCF-PEEK composite rasters. The study investigates five specific bend angles—45, 60, 90, 135, and 150 degrees—to evaluate their structural integrity. These configurations are part of a broader experimental matrix designed to quantify the performance of printed composite filaments and tapes.

caption: Calculated external quantum efficiency (EQE) spectra for the simulated PSC devices, highlighting the optical impact of the SL-ARC integration.
summary: The simulated EQE spectra demonstrate the influence of SL-ARCs on the optical generation capabilities of the PSC devices. By comparing the spectral response of the coated and uncoated configurations, the plot illustrates how the SL-ARC modification enhances the light-harvesting efficiency of the perovskite solar cells under the defined optimal simulation parameters.

caption: FOBI-retrieved neutron transmission spectra for the individual Fe and Cu layers, demonstrating consistent crystallographic texture trends observed when the neutron beam is aligned along the TD2 direction.
summary: Transmission spectra for the Fe and Cu layers are retrieved using FOBI analysis. These spectra correspond to the regions highlighted in panel (a). The data indicates that the crystallographic texture trends observed in the transmission signal are consistent with those measured when the neutron beam is aligned along the TD2 direction.

caption: Cumulative capacity fading of second-life batteries plotted against Ah-throughput across various C-rates.
summary: This plot illustrates the cumulative capacity fading observed in second-life battery cells as a function of total Ah-throughput. The data highlights the degradation behavior under different C-rate conditions, providing a clear visualization of how cycling intensity influences the long-term capacity retention and usable life of the battery systems.

caption: TGA curve of Ni 80 Co 17 Mo 3 powder mixture milled for 6 h, exhibiting a gradual mass reduction of 0.660 mg.
summary: For the Ni 80 Co 17 Mo 3 powder mixture milled for 6 h, the TGA curve demonstrates a gradual mass reduction of 0.660 mg. This change represents a relatively negligible mass variation of 0.064% throughout the thermal analysis process, indicating different stability characteristics compared to the 2 h milled sample.

caption: Nanoindentation stress-strain curves comparing the mechanical response of TC6 titanium alloy, Coating A, and Coating R.
summary: This plot displays the nanoindentation stress-strain curves for TC6 titanium alloy, Coating A, and Coating R. These curves provide essential data regarding the mechanical behavior of the materials, specifically facilitating the determination of their respective Young's modulus and nanohardness values under localized indentation testing conditions.

caption: Infrared spectra comparing standard ABS resin and a separated ABS filament sample, highlighting specific absorption peaks at approximately 1730 cm⁻¹ and 1160 cm⁻¹.
summary: This FTIR spectrum compares standard ABS resin with a separated ABS filament sample. Analysis reveals distinct differences, specifically the presence of C=O peaks at approximately 1730 cm⁻¹ and 1160 cm⁻¹ in the filament sample that are absent in the main cluster ABS spectra, indicating compositional variations between the two materials.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the expression levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6 in hGF-1 cells after 24 and 48 hours of exposure to various materials including Co-Cr (Ct and SLM), Ti (SLM and M), and PEEK, compared against a control group.
summary: This bar chart quantifies IL-6 pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in hGF-1 cells at 24 and 48 hours. Comparing control, Co-Cr, Ti, and PEEK samples, the data highlights significant inflammatory responses, marked by asterisks for p < 0.05. These results form part of a broader analysis of inflammatory markers in the study.

caption: Summary SHAP plot displaying the impact of various input features on the classification of Lack of Fusion (LoF) defects.
summary: The summary plot for LoF defects visualizes how specific input features contribute to the model's classification of this defect type. By analyzing the distribution of SHAP values, this plot highlights the key variables that drive the prediction of Lack of Fusion, facilitating a clearer interpretation of the underlying physical drivers.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) values plotted against misorientation angles relative to the ideal beta-fiber components, characterizing the local plastic strain variations within the banded structures of the A1050 material.
summary: Variations in KAM values are presented as a function of misorientation angles from the ideal beta-fiber components (Brass, S, and Copper). This plot provides quantitative insight into the local misorientation and plastic strain distribution associated with the specific banded structures identified in the rolled A1050 aluminum alloy sheets.

caption: Rotation field map generated using Heaviside-DIC, demonstrating improved resolution of the rotation field compared to conventional methods.
summary: Heaviside-DIC is employed here to calculate the rotation field for the same 2° rotation and 4-pixel sliding condition. By utilizing internal DIC parameters, this method provides a refined representation of the rotation field, highlighting the specific advantages of the Heaviside-DIC approach in handling discontinuities during image analysis.

caption: Magnified view of the PBF-deposited line showing detailed surface height variations.
summary: Enlarged visualization of the PBF-deposited line highlights specific surface height variations and topographical details. This magnified view allows for a closer inspection of the track morphology, facilitating a more granular analysis of the deposition process and the resulting surface characteristics compared to the broader track height maps.

caption: SHAP interaction plot illustrating the combined influence of MWCNT concentration and sliding speed on the coefficient of friction (CoF).
summary: This SHAP interaction plot visualizes how MWCNT concentration and sliding speed collectively influence the coefficient of friction. The analysis reveals that the interaction effect between these two variables increasingly negatively impacts the SHAP value as sliding speed rises, highlighting the dominant role of these parameters in determining the tribological performance.

caption: Experimentally measured strain rate evolution for CM and two trials of AM states at 100 MPa and 750 °C, highlighting the accelerated grain boundary sliding in the CM state.
summary: Experimental strain rate evolution is shown for CM and two AM state trials at 100 MPa and 750 °C. The accelerated grain boundary sliding observed in the CM state is attributed to the discrete distribution of carbides, which intensifies sliding and promotes the formation of creep voids during testing.

caption: Atomic unit cell configuration of the S20 specimen during the heating process toward 400 K.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic unit cell configuration of the S20 specimen as it undergoes a heating process reaching a target temperature of 400 K. The visualization provides a structural representation of the material's lattice arrangement during this thermal treatment, as described in the heating process study of unit cells.

caption: Phase fraction evolution for 10Cr, 8Cr, and 6Cr alloys under P2 conditions, illustrating the transition from liquid to γ-Fe and the subsequent formation of HP materials during cooling.
summary: This phase-field simulation depicts the phase fraction evolution for 10Cr, 8Cr, and 6Cr alloys under P2 conditions. It highlights the transition from liquid to γ-Fe and the formation of HP materials as temperature decreases. Specifically, for the 6Cr alloy, HP formation is observed to occur at approximately 1250 K.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves of the α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene nanohybrid material measured at different current densities.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves of the α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene nanohybrid material measured at different current densities. These curves demonstrate the electrochemical performance and charge storage characteristics of the negative electrode material, providing essential data on its capacity and potential behavior under varying operational conditions.

caption: Energy Dispersive X-Ray Spectroscopy elemental distribution map of the as-built Haynes 282 cellular-dendritic microstructure.
summary: Energy Dispersive X-Ray Spectroscopy mapping illustrates the elemental distribution across the cellular-dendritic structure of the as-built Haynes 282. This compositional analysis provides critical data on the chemical homogeneity and segregation patterns within the dendritic features, complementing the morphological observations obtained from the SEM micrographs of the same region.

caption: Additional transmission electron microscopy view confirming the distribution of NiCo alloy nanoparticles inside the carbonaceous support.
summary: This transmission electron microscopy image provides further confirmation of the NiCo bimetallic alloy nanoparticles' presence within the nitrogen-doped carbon matrix. The visual data supports the morphological characterization, showing the successful integration of the alloyed nanoparticles into the carbon support structure, consistent with the overall synthesis of the catalyst.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of BMSCs on BG AC3D scaffolds, highlighting live cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of BMSCs on BG AC3D scaffolds shows well-proliferated cells across the surface. The high density of green-stained live cells indicates that the inclusion of nanoceria in the BG AC3D composite provides oxidative resistance and enhances cytocompatibility, effectively supporting the viability of the seeded stromal cells.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy images of BMSCs stained for cytoskeleton (red) and nuclei (blue) to assess cell morphology on scaffold surfaces.
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy reveals the morphology of BMSCs cultured on scaffolds. Ta scaffolds exhibit notably enhanced cellular features, including expanded volumes, improved cytoskeletal organization, and increased nuclear populations compared to Ti scaffolds, suggesting that the Ta surface promotes more favorable cell-material interactions and better overall cellular health.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of PP/B4C nanocomposite containing 4.0 wt% filler at 1000× magnification.
summary: Captured at 1000× magnification, this SEM image shows the PP/B4C nanocomposite with a reduced filler content of 4.0 wt%. The lower concentration of B4C particles compared to the 10.0 wt% sample is evident, reflecting the anticipated decrease in boron concentration within the polymer matrix structure.

caption: Paris regime fatigue crack growth data for HSLA steel specimens.
summary: The Paris regime for HSLA steel specimens is depicted in this panel, summarizing the fatigue crack growth rates obtained from constant fatigue testing. This data contributes to the overall assessment of the HSLA steel performance, allowing for a direct comparison with the AS steel and bi-material specimens.

caption: Raman spectra comparing IOZ samples containing fine and coarse precipitates, identifying the chemical composition of the secondary phases.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of IOZ samples reveals the chemical identity of the observed precipitates. By comparing the spectra of regions containing fine and coarse precipitates, the analysis confirms that both types of precipitates are composed of Cr2O3, demonstrating consistent chemical characteristics regardless of the precipitate size distribution within the material.

caption: Temperature distribution contour for a staggered bundle configuration with longitudinal pitch Sl = 1.5 and transverse pitch St = 1.15 at a heat generation rate of 1.25 W/g.
summary: Represented here is the temperature contour for a staggered bundle with a longitudinal pitch of 1.5 and a transverse pitch of 1.15 at 1.25 W/g heat generation. The thermal pattern indicates increased temperatures in the central zone, resulting in a hot leg above the ingots and cold legs near the walls.

caption: Cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential of 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at a C/10 rate.
summary: This panel illustrates the electrochemical characteristics of 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at a C/10 rate. By plotting cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential against lithium composition, the data reveals very small overpotential and minimal hysteresis, demonstrating consistent electrochemical performance comparable to the 3D printed counterpart.

caption: Overview of the experimental apparatus used for the study.
summary: This panel provides a visual representation of the experimental setup employed throughout the research. It serves as a reference for the physical configuration of the equipment, illustrating the arrangement and components necessary to conduct the experiments described in the study, ensuring clarity regarding the methodology and hardware implementation.

caption: 111 pole figure displaying the representative orientations of banded structures within rolled A1050 sheets, where small symbols denote specific band orientations and large bold symbols represent ideal beta-fiber components including Brass, S, and Copper.
summary: This 111 pole figure illustrates the crystallographic orientations of banded structures in rolled A1050 aluminum sheets. Small symbols mark the representative orientations for each band, while large, bold symbols indicate the ideal beta-fiber components (Brass, S, and Copper) to serve as a reference for the observed texture distribution.

caption: Site-projected density of states for Cr and O species in the O bridge configuration, comparing bulk Cr (left) to surface-adsorbed Cr (right).
summary: The site-projected density of states for the O bridge configuration reveals a strong interaction between Cr and O atoms in the -6 to -4 eV energy range. This interaction becomes prominent as the Cr atom transitions from the bulk environment to the surface position, highlighting significant electronic hybridization between these species.

caption: Ternary phase diagram for the Mn–Cr–O system calculated at 818 °C using FactSage 6.2, featuring an overlaid schematic diffusion path representing the reaction in a dry gas environment.
summary: This ternary phase diagram for the Mn–Cr–O system at 818 °C illustrates the thermodynamic landscape of the reaction. A schematic diffusion path is mapped onto the diagram, demonstrating that the formation of a MnCr2O4 layer over a (Cr2O3 + MnCr2O4) layer is consistent with local equilibrium conditions during dry gas exposure.

caption: Enlarged cyclic polarization segment for the low Fe-content Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb alloy, highlighting a sharp decrease in current density during the downward potential scan from 1.35 V, signifying efficient repassivation.
summary: This enlarged cyclic polarization segment for the low Fe-content Ni-22Cr-9Mo-5Fe-2Nb alloy highlights a sharp decrease in current density during the downward potential scan from 1.35 V. The absence of a considerable hysteresis loop in this region indicates that the alloy undergoes efficient repassivation following the transpassive breakdown.

caption: Hatch distance (HD) parameter validation across the build plate location, comparing Batch 1 and Batch 2 with ±3σ confidence intervals calculated via Monte-Carlo simulation.
summary: Hatch distance parameters are validated against build plate location in this panel, utilizing Monte-Carlo simulations to establish ±3σ confidence intervals. The data highlights how variations in manufacturing parameters, combined with specific sample placement, lead to distinct ultrasound scan results, underscoring the importance of spatial positioning during the manufacturing process.

caption: Measured electrical resistance of an embedded 3D silver structure featuring a 6-point connection configuration.
summary: This panel displays the electrical resistance measurement for a 3D embedded silver structure designed with a 6-point connection. The measured resistance value is 0.759 MΩ, which aligns with the reported maximum resistance of 0.76 MΩ, demonstrating the conductive performance of the complex 3D silver architecture within the embedded system.

caption: Convergence behavior of the anisotropic phase-field fracture parameter optimization process when fixing the parameter.
summary: This panel displays the convergence behavior of the parameter optimization process for anisotropic phase-field fracture. By fixing the parameter, the simulation results successfully converge to the target solution, demonstrating the effectiveness of this specific parameter-fixing strategy within the optimization framework described in the sensitivity analysis.

caption: Ashby plot comparing density versus specific energy absorption (SEA) for the proposed OIPLs against various state-of-the-art lattice structures.
summary: This plot compares the density and specific energy absorption (SEA) of the proposed OIPLs with existing lattice structures, including truss, plate, and origami-based designs. The visualization benchmarks the performance of the OIPLs against state-of-the-art materials, illustrating their relative efficiency in energy absorption applications across different structural architectures.

caption: Box plots comparing the energy distribution within peaks and valleys of the high-frequency acoustic emission band (49.61–50 kHz) across four distinct printing tracks.
summary: This box plot illustrates the energy variance in high-frequency acoustic emission signals during printing. Analysis reveals a significant disparity between signal features, where the median energy for peaks reaches 26.73 dB/Hz, while the median energy for valleys is substantially lower at 2.62 dB/Hz across the four evaluated printing tracks.

caption: Mid-plane mesh discretization of the sample geometry, excluding the grip regions, featuring four-node quadrilateral finite elements and a red cross marking the central Gauss point.
summary: The mid-plane geometry of the sample is discretized using four-node quadrilateral finite elements, excluding the regions held by the testing machine grips. A specific Gauss point located in the central part of the sample is highlighted with a red cross to facilitate localized analysis of the damage variable evolution.

caption: Maximum tensile force plotted against the number of cycles for a tested specimen, highlighting distinct beam failure events.
summary: This plot illustrates the maximum tensile force as a function of the number of cycles for a representative specimen. The data clearly captures the progression of the fatigue test, allowing for the identification of specific beam failure events that occur throughout the cycling process as the material degrades.

caption: Chromium (Cr) elemental distribution map illustrating the Cr content across the dendrite region of the as-deposited-VP sample.
summary: Chromium (Cr) elemental distribution map illustrating the Cr content across the dendrite region of the as-deposited-VP sample. This SEM-EDS elemental mapping test was performed to identify the chemical composition of the dendrite, providing insight into the distribution of Cr within the complex microstructure of the as-deposited material.

caption: Bode diagrams displaying the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi samples after 1 hour of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, including fitted data curves.
summary: Bode plots characterize the frequency-dependent electrochemical impedance of LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi samples after one hour of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These plots, featuring fitted lines, facilitate a comparative analysis of the corrosion resistance and passive film properties of the two distinct NiTi alloy microstructures.

caption: Extinction coefficient (K) values for various nanocomposite specimens at 1 wt% filler concentration, measured at a 405-nm wavelength.
summary: Extinction coefficients for Nano 19, Nano 27, Nano 24, and EOGO nanocomposites are compared at 1 wt% concentration. At 405 nm, the K-values are 0.339, 0.403, 0.448, and 0.449 g/L-cm, respectively. These measurements, obtained via UV-vis spectrophotometry, provide quantitative data on the optical properties of the different filler-matrix systems.

caption: Optical absorption spectrum of commercial CVD correction glasses, including an inset showing the physical glasses.
summary: Absorption spectra for commercial CVD correction glasses are displayed, with an inset showing the physical samples. The data highlights how these commercial products filter light to assist with color vision deficiency, serving as a comparative benchmark for the performance of the 3D-printed Atto dye-based samples.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the crystal structure and phase composition of as-built and heat-treated IN718 superalloy samples.
summary: The X-ray diffraction patterns of IN718 samples are presented to illustrate the structural evolution resulting from different processing conditions. By comparing the as-built and heat-treated states, the data reveals distinct changes in the crystal structure and phase composition, providing insight into the material's microstructural response to thermal treatment.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the local strain-rate distribution along the gauge length for a sample tested at 10^-4 s^-1, overlaid with the engineering stress-time curve in red.
summary: This 3D contour plot displays the temporal evolution of strain-rate distributions along the tensile axis. Data recorded at successive time steps demonstrate that strain localization initiates once a well-defined critical strain is reached. The superimposed red line represents the corresponding engineering stress-time curve, providing context for the mechanical response over time.

caption: Four-point terminal current–voltage characteristics of the copper pillars shown in panels (b) and (c), accompanied by corresponding optical microscopy images.
summary: Current-voltage characteristics for the pillars from panels (b) and (c) are plotted, demonstrating linear and symmetrical behavior. These results, supported by optical microscopy images, confirm that the MetalJet-printed pillars exhibit Ohmic behavior. The four-point probe measurements successfully determine the electrical resistivity of both singular and multiple droplet pillars.

caption: Surface profile of an FDM print showing downward filament sliding caused by higher printing temperatures, which extend the time the material remains above the glass transition temperature.
summary: Higher printing temperatures are shown to extend the duration the material remains above the glass transition temperature, resulting in the tops of the fused filaments sliding downward. This confocal microscopy image illustrates the resulting surface topography, highlighting the impact of thermal processing on the final print geometry.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of as-built Sample No. 4 in the XY direction, revealing the microstructural morphology.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of as-built Sample No. 4 in the XY direction. The imaging technique was utilized to investigate nano-scale segregation and potential TCP phase formation within the material, providing a clear view of the structural characteristics of the as-built HESA lattice sample.

caption: EDXS elemental weight percentage profiles for O, Mo, Al, and Ta plotted against the distance from the oxide scale surface at 800 °C.
summary: The EDXS profiles for O, Mo, Al, and Ta at 800 °C reveal that these elements are present in smaller percentages within the oxide scale. Unlike at 750 °C, the oxygen level remains steady at 800 °C, likely due to oxygen penetration through multiple surface cracks generated under fatigue loading.

caption: Transmission spectrum of sample 1, illustrating the optical response after UV light exposure.
summary: The transmission spectrum for sample 1 is presented to evaluate its optical stability following UV light exposure. Consistent with the other samples in the series, the spectral data indicates stable optical behavior, showing that the material maintains its transmission characteristics despite the applied UV radiation during the degradation assessment test.

caption: EDX elemental composite map of the thin section, displaying kamacite in red, taenite in blue, plessite intergrowths in purple, troilite in yellow, and native copper in green.
summary: The EDX composite map visualizes the distribution of major phases within the chondrite. Kamacite, taenite, plessite, and troilite are color-coded to distinguish their spatial relationships. Native copper is identified in green, demonstrating its entrainment within Fe,Ni metal grains and its specific association with plessitic textures resulting from shock melting.

caption: Thermal desorption spectra of H-charged specimens, plotted as hydrogen desorption rate versus temperature, obtained immediately following electrochemical hydrogen charging during tensile loading at varying constant heating rates.
summary: This thermal desorption spectroscopy plot displays the hydrogen release behavior of H-charged specimens subjected to tensile loading. By measuring spectra at different constant heating rates, the data facilitates the calculation of hydrogen desorption activation energies. Analysis of these spectra reveals three distinct peaks, indicating hydrogen trapping at three unique microstructural sites.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of hBMSCs on pectin scaffolds after 4 weeks of culture, stained with Calcein AM (green, live) and Ethidium homodimer (red, dead).
summary: Live and dead assay results demonstrate high cell viability after 4 weeks, indicated by minimal red-stained cells across all scaffold types. While fibrin-laden constructs support cell viability, hBMSCs on fibrin-free Pect1 and Pect2 scaffolds maintain a rounded morphology and form cell aggregates, confirming the scaffold's ability to support long-term culture.

caption: Mineralogical composition of CUG lunar regolith simulant presented in a tabular format.
summary: This table details the mineralogical composition of the CUG lunar regolith simulant. The material is primarily composed of feldspar minerals, specifically plagioclase and calcium, alongside pyroxene and olivine. Additionally, the analysis identifies minor quantities of hematite and ilmenite, providing a comprehensive overview of the simulant's mineralogical constituents.

caption: Representative creep strain-time curves comparing the deformation response of samples subjected to different heat treatments.
summary: Creep strain-time curves illustrate the deformation characteristics of samples under varying treatment conditions across both directions. Quantitative analysis of the creep data indicates that SA-treated samples demonstrate a creep strain of 52.1%, which is substantially higher than the 11.3% observed for LSA-treated samples, mirroring the trends observed in tensile testing.

caption: φ2 = 45° ODF section for the iHEA-H sample prior to tensile deformation.
summary: The φ2 = 45° ODF section for the iHEA-H sample before deformation reveals specific crystallographic orientations. Analysis indicates that the primary texture components present in this sample are Copper and A, which characterize the initial state of the material before it undergoes any tensile testing or mechanical loading.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-built specimen processed at 105 W laser power, viewed in the loading direction (XY plane) with the Z axis parallel to the build direction.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the crystallographic orientation of the as-built specimen fabricated at 105 W. The data is acquired in the loading direction, with the Z axis aligned to the build direction, providing insight into the grain orientation distribution resulting from the specific laser power processing condition.

caption: Temperature-dependent impedance behavior of HPTH60 and HPE60 materials plotted against reciprocal temperature across a 0–70 °C range during heating and cooling cycles.
summary: Impedance is plotted against reciprocal temperature for HPTH60 and HPE60 materials within the 0–70 °C range. The data includes both heating and cooling regimes, allowing for an assessment of the thermal stability and temperature-dependent electrical characteristics of these i-wi materials in a controlled environmental setting.

caption: Bode split diagram illustrating the frequency-dependent electrochemical impedance behavior of LPBF 316L and R 316L in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Representing the final component of the Bode split diagrams, this plot characterizes the electrochemical impedance of LPBF 316L and R 316L. The results demonstrate how phase angle shifts in the 0.1–100 Hz range indicate the protective quality of the passivation film, with closer approaches to -90° signifying higher corrosion resistance.

caption: Overview of the experimental study design illustrating the systematic approach and methodological framework employed throughout the research.
summary: This schematic provides a comprehensive overview of the study design, outlining the systematic methodological framework and experimental approach adopted in the research. It serves as a foundational visual guide to the workflow, ensuring clarity regarding the procedural steps and logical progression of the investigation as described in the study.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the polarization resistance (Rp) for laser-deposited samples (LDSs) immersed in a 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: This plot illustrates the temporal evolution of the polarization resistance (Rp) for laser-deposited samples (LDSs) during exposure to a 3.5% NaCl corrosive environment. The data, as calculated and presented in the figure, provides a quantitative assessment of the electrochemical stability and corrosion resistance of the LDSs over the testing duration.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the γ-Ni phase within the 250 Hz coating.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern identifies the presence of the γ-Ni phase in the 250 Hz coating. This diffraction analysis serves to confirm the phase composition of the coating, providing crystallographic evidence of the γ-Ni constituent within the material's microstructure as characterized by TEM.

caption: Microhardness profile of cylindrical samples measured as a function of distance from the interface up to 250 μm.
summary: Microhardness results for cylindrical samples are presented, illustrating the mechanical response relative to the interface. The data specifically captures the hardness values within a 250 μm distance from the interface, providing a localized assessment of the material's mechanical properties in this specific geometry following the microhardness testing procedure.

caption: Incident-photo-to-current efficiency (IPCE) spectra measured at 1.23 V vs. RHE for Fe2O3 and Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 photoanodes.
summary: Incident-photo-to-current efficiency (IPCE) measurements were conducted at 1.23 V vs. RHE to evaluate the photo-conversion efficiency of the photoanodes. The improved IPCE observed for the Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 photoanode is consistent with the enhanced photocurrent density results, confirming the beneficial effect of the Ni-Bi modification on the photoelectrochemical performance.

caption: Total structure factor S(q) for Ni75Al25, comparing MD simulation results (solid line) with neutron scattering experimental data (open symbols).
summary: The total structure factor S(q) for Ni75Al25 is presented, showing both MD simulation results and neutron scattering experimental data. The comparison indicates that the MD simulation results are in good qualitative and reasonable quantitative agreement with the experimental measurements for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Discharge curves of annealed La1.9Mg1.1Ni9 alloy electrodes plotted against discharge current densities.
summary: The discharge curves for the annealed La1.9Mg1.1Ni9 alloy electrode are shown here as a function of current density. This alloy demonstrates a maximum discharge capacity near 400 mAh/g and an initial discharge capacity of approximately 346 mAh/g at 0.33 C, showing similar electrochemical behavior to the La2MgNi9 alloy.

caption: Top-down perspective of the sample as captured by the thermal camera, identifying three distinct lines of interest: the center profile (green), the center width profile (red), and the 5 mm offset width profile (blue).
summary: This top-view schematic displays the three lines of interest used to measure temperature distribution on the sample. The green line represents the center profile, while the red and blue lines denote the center width and 5 mm offset width profiles, respectively, facilitating detailed thermal analysis of the heating process.

caption: Rate performance comparison showing areal capacity versus current density for D-3DP and N-3DP electrodes.
summary: The rate capability of the D-3DP electrode is evaluated across increasing current densities from 0.1 to 1 mA cm⁻². The D-3DP electrode achieves high areal capacities of 3.11, 2.98, 2.71, and 2.04 mAh cm⁻², demonstrating superior rate performance compared to the N-3DP counterpart electrode.

caption: Darkfield TEM image obtained using a Cr2O3 reflection, highlighting the presence of nanoscale Cr2O3 platelets within the porous oxidation product at the corrosion front.
summary: Captured using a specific Cr2O3 reflection, this darkfield TEM image provides detailed insight into the composition of the oxidation product at the corrosion front. It confirms that the porous layer consists of nanoscale Cr2O3 platelets, further elucidating the microstructure associated with the IGA oxidation front in the Ni-5Cr alloy.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution after 3600 s of immersion.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization plots for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys are presented after 3600 s of EOCP measurements in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at room temperature. These curves serve as the basis for extracting key corrosion parameters, which are further detailed in the study's supplementary data tables.

caption: Phase distribution map of the solidified model showing the FCC phase throughout the computational domain.
summary: This phase-field simulation displays the solidified model colored by phase. The computational domain confirms the formation of a uniform FCC phase throughout the material following the solidification process, as indicated by the phase distribution map derived from the temperature-time distribution obtained via CtFD simulation.

caption: Atom maps of Cr, Co, Ni, and Mo in a Mo-6 thin film coated on a Si tip, highlighting ROI1 and ROI2 regions.
summary: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the Mo-6 alloy thin film on a Si tip after 360°C annealing. The visualization displays the spatial distribution of Cr, Co, Ni, and Mo. Two regions of interest, ROI1 and ROI2, are identified at the apex and shank for detailed compositional analysis.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis results for as-printed PEKK coupons across multiple recycling rounds, displaying storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor.
summary: This panel presents the dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) results for as-printed PEKK coupons. It illustrates the storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor across various recycling rounds. These curves characterize the viscoelastic properties of the material in its as-printed, amorphous state, providing insight into the mechanical performance of recycled PEKK.

caption: Box plot comparing the distribution range of Taylor factors across different scanning strategies.
summary: This box plot summarizes the Taylor factor ranges for all scanning strategies. By evaluating the {111}<110> slip systems and critical resolved shear stress, it provides a comparative overview of the texture strengthening effect, demonstrating how different processing methods influence the intrinsic strength and mechanical variability of the alloy.

caption: Complex plane representation of EIS spectra for nickel-free steels after 50 hours of primary coolant exposure, displaying experimental data points and best-fit solid lines across varying frequencies.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of nickel-free steels after 50 hours of exposure to primary coolant. The experimental data points are accurately captured by the best-fit solid lines, indicating that all studied steels exhibit very similar electrochemical characteristics under the specified testing conditions.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of silver nanoparticles collected from the FIJR-mCSTR system, monitored at 20 s, 300 s, 600 s, and 24 h post-collection.
summary: UV-Vis absorption spectra of silver nanoparticles produced via the FIJR-mCSTR system were recorded at intervals from 20 seconds to 24 hours. The data demonstrate that the characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak position remains stable, with only minor intensity fluctuations of approximately 5% observed within the first five minutes of collection.

caption: Time-dependent normal strain evolution for the through-thickness line, encompassing points 1 through 5 during in-situ heat treatment at 760 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the in-situ evolution of normal strain fields in Waspaloy during heat treatment at 760 °C. Specifically, it tracks points 1 through 5 along a through-thickness line. The strain profile for points 1 and 3 exhibits a linear decrease, indicating a constant relief of strain over time.

caption: Pareto chart highlighting the key parameters that significantly affect the tensile modulus of elasticity.
summary: This Pareto chart highlights the statistically significant parameters that dictate the tensile modulus of elasticity. It serves as a diagnostic tool to determine which experimental factors have the most substantial impact on the material's stiffness, facilitating a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanical behavior observed during the testing process.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot of g-C3N4 measured under varying alternating current potential frequencies.
summary: This Mott-Schottky plot illustrates the electrochemical behavior of g-C3N4 across different alternating current frequencies. The observed positive slope confirms that g-C3N4 is an n-type semiconductor. This finding is essential for understanding the electronic band structure and charge transport mechanisms within the material for photocatalytic performance.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from the oxidation peaks of the three different modified separator cells.
summary: Tafel slope analysis is performed based on the oxidation peaks of the three modified separator cells. This plot provides insight into the electrochemical kinetics and reaction mechanisms occurring at the electrode-electrolyte interface, allowing for a detailed comparison of the oxidation behavior across the different separator materials tested.

caption: Schematic representation of the measurement spots P1 through P4 defined on the head model for infrared thermal imaging.
summary: This schematic illustrates the four designated measurement spots, labeled P1 through P4, positioned on the head model. These regions of interest correspond to specific head deformities and the varying distances between the head and the cranial remolding orthosis, facilitating systematic infrared thermal imaging from anterior, posterior, medial, and lateral perspectives.

caption: Engineering stress–strain curves for bulk SS-1700 (blue) and SS-850 (red) samples, illustrating the macroscopic mechanical response under tensile loading.
summary: Engineering stress–strain curves for bulk SS-1700 and SS-850 samples are shown. These curves compare the macroscopic mechanical behavior of the two samples, which were fabricated at different scanning speeds, providing a clear view of how processing conditions influence the overall strength and ductility of the 316L stainless steel.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy curves for Ni-based superalloy specimens charged with hydrogen at 290 K, 300 K, and 320 K.
summary: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) curves illustrate the hydrogen desorption behavior of Ni-based superalloy specimens after charging at 290 K, 300 K, and 320 K. These experimental results provide the total hydrogen content measurements for each charging temperature, revealing distinct desorption rate profiles across the tested temperature range.

caption: Load–displacement behavior of QZS samples as a function of the number (N) of beams integrated into the structure.
summary: This plot shows the load–displacement responses of QZS samples with varying numbers of beams N. Analysis indicates that the QZS force (FQZS) increases with the number of beams, while the QZS displacement (WQZS) decreases as N increases, highlighting the structural influence of beam count on the system's mechanical performance.

caption: Convergence history for Joint Model 1, plotting the decrease in average and best objective function values over successive generations.
summary: Panel (c) depicts the convergence history of the identification process for Joint Model 1. The plot tracks the reduction in both average and best objective function values across successive generations. Evaluations were conducted according to Eq. (8), illustrating the optimization progress and the model's refinement over the identification process.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry scans comparing initial and repeat runs for HVOF, Plasma Ar H2, and Plasma Ar He coatings at a 20 °C/min ramp rate, highlighting the first exothermic peak in the HVOF coating starting at 610 °C and peaking at 680 °C.
summary: This DSC analysis compares initial and repeat thermal runs for three distinct coating types: HVOF, Plasma Ar H2, and Plasma Ar He. Conducted at 20 °C/min, the data reveals specific thermal behavior for the HVOF coating, which exhibits an exothermic peak initiating at 610 °C and reaching a maximum at 680 °C.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting the matrix phase of the SA + PT LPBF A709 sample, providing contrast to distinguish the surrounding precipitate structures.
summary: The dark-field TEM image focuses on the matrix phase of the SA + PT LPBF A709 sample. By isolating the matrix signal, this visualization allows for a clearer distinction between the bulk material and the various precipitates that decorate the grain and cell boundaries within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Simulated magnetic reversal curves for varying K edge values in (Nd0.73Dy0.27)2Fe14B shell structures, showing the sensitivity of reversal behavior to anisotropy gradients.
summary: Simulated reversal curves are presented for different K edge values within a (Nd0.73Dy0.27)2Fe14B shell. The analysis demonstrates that under these specific modeling conditions, the coercivity of the magnet cannot be further enhanced, reflecting the limitations of the current core-shell structural configuration in improving magnetic performance.

caption: Vickers microhardness evolution of cast and laser-remelted Al–6Ce–3Ni-0.7Fe alloys during isothermal aging at 400 °C, showing a steady decline in hardness for the laser-remelted specimen over 1050 hours.
summary: This plot illustrates the Vickers microhardness evolution of cast and laser-remelted Al–6Ce–3Ni-0.7Fe alloys during isothermal aging at 400 °C. The laser-remelted alloy exhibits a steady decrease in hardness, reaching approximately 800 MPa after 1050 hours of aging, which correlates with the coarsening of the rapidly solidified microstructure observed during the aging process.

caption: Vickers hardness (HV) values of Ti and Ti–6Al–4V alloys processed by PBF-LB and DED-LB plotted against BN weight percentage, with a dashed vertical line indicating the saturation limit.
summary: This plot compiles Vickers hardness data for Ti and Ti–6Al–4V parts fabricated via PBF-LB and DED-LB as a function of BN content. Hardness increases rapidly with BN addition before tapering off above 5 wt%, with a saturation threshold identified in the 2–3 wt% range, though indentation conditions may influence these values.

caption: Fused filament fabrication printing process illustrating the melting layer stacking technology where filaments are heated to a semi-liquid state and solidified along a preset path at chamber temperature.
summary: This schematic illustrates the fused filament fabrication process, which utilizes melting layer stacking technology. The filament is heated into a semi-liquid state and subsequently solidified along a predefined path at chamber temperature, demonstrating the fundamental mechanism of the 3D printing process used for composite fabrication.

caption: Tafel curve illustrating the electrochemical corrosion response of the material subjected to fretting conditions.
summary: This panel presents the Tafel curve for the material under fretting conditions. The plot demonstrates how mechanical fretting influences the electrochemical corrosion response. By comparing this to the static condition, it highlights the impact of surface degradation and potential oxygen diffusion through cracks on the overall corrosion rate of the matrix.

caption: Local SEM image of the DLC coating scratch track showing no obvious surface delamination despite the presence of pores.
summary: This local SEM observation of the DLC coating surface reveals no clear signs of delamination within the scratch track. Although the surface remains intact, pores are detected at various locations across the sample. This analysis provides a detailed view of the coating's structural integrity following the mechanical scratch test.

caption: Anodic polarization curves of pure nickel in aqueous solutions across varying pH levels, showing active dissolution below 0.2 V (vs. SCE) and a passive zone at 0.1 A/m2 for acidic conditions (pH=0).
summary: Pure nickel exhibits distinct electrochemical behavior in acidic aqueous solutions. At pH=0, the material undergoes wide active dissolution at potentials below 0.2 V (vs. SCE). Upon exceeding this potential, a stable passive zone is established at a current density level of 0.1 A/m2, characterizing the anodic polarization response.

caption: Lithiation profiles of cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes at a C/10 rate.
summary: Shown are the lithiation characteristics for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes, plotting cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential versus lithium composition. Similar to the 3D printed sample, the entropic potential increases significantly near the end of lithiation, driven by the growing difference between the cell potential and the open-circuit voltage.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram for M23C6 and M7C3 carbide precipitation in 420 steel, calculated using JMatPro software.
summary: This CCT diagram, generated with JMatPro, specifically maps the kinetics of M23C6 and M7C3 carbide precipitation in 420 steel. It serves as a critical tool for understanding the thermal conditions required for carbide formation, which is a fundamental aspect of the alloy's phase transformation behavior during cooling.

caption: PCA loading plot identifying the relative contribution and influence of specific mechanical variables, including elastic modulus, maximum stress, and elongation, on the sample distribution.
summary: The PCA loading plot displays the contribution of mechanical variables to the principal components. It highlights which parameters—specifically Young’s modulus, maximum stress, and elongation at maximum force—are most influential in driving the observed differences and clustering patterns among the various experimental groups during the multivariate mechanical analysis.

caption: Low-resolution 3D X-ray computed tomography (XCT) reconstruction of a metallic sample, highlighting the spatial distribution of internal pores rendered in red.
summary: This low-resolution 3D XCT scan provides a volumetric visualization of internal porosity within a material. By rendering the pores in red, the spatial distribution and connectivity of these defects are clearly identified, serving as a diagnostic tool for assessing the structural integrity of additively manufactured components under unoptimized process parameters.

caption: Bode plots showing the phase angle versus frequency for Mo0 and Mo23 alloys, highlighting the maximum phase angle in the medium frequency range.
summary: Bode plots for Mo0 and Mo23 alloys in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution demonstrate that Mo23 achieves a higher maximum phase angle of approximately 79° in the medium frequency region compared to 68° for Mo0. This increased phase angle confirms that the Mo23 alloy possesses significantly better corrosion resistance than the Mo0 alloy.

caption: Engineering stress–strain curves for SS 316L, Type I (straight interface), Type II (zigzag interface), and Nimonic 90 samples.
summary: This panel displays the tensile engineering stress–strain behavior of SS 316L with straight and zigzag interfaces, alongside Nimonic 90 samples. These curves illustrate the mechanical response and deformation characteristics of the different material configurations under tensile loading conditions, providing a comparative overview of their respective strength and ductility profiles.

caption: Histogram quantifying the diameters of the inhibition zones, providing a statistical representation of the antibacterial activity observed in the scaffold.
summary: This histogram quantifies the diameters of the inhibition zones associated with the scaffold. By summarizing the experimental data, it provides a clear statistical comparison of the antibacterial activity, complementing the visual inhibition zone images to demonstrate the efficacy of the scaffold in preventing bacterial proliferation.

caption: XRD pattern of mixed recycled powders collected from various distances, highlighting the presence of Cr2O3, Fe3O4, and FeCr2O4 oxide phases.
summary: Mixed recycled powders from different collection distances were analyzed via XRD to improve the detection of secondary phases. This pattern confirms the emergence of Cr2O3, Fe3O4, and FeCr2O4 oxide phases following DED processing, providing clear evidence of oxidation occurring during the recycling of the 316L SS powder material.

caption: Energy band diagrams showing conduction band (CB), valence band (VB), and Fermi level (EF) for non-graded and 50-nm-thick graded contact structures.
summary: Energy band diagrams for non-graded and 50-nm-thick graded contact structures are presented, detailing the conduction band, valence band, and Fermi level positions. These theoretical calculations, performed in NextNano, demonstrate the electronic band alignment, confirming that carrier transport is concentrated in the p-GaN and p-AlGaN graded layers.

caption: Ternary composition space map illustrating the specific regions occupied by the prepared Cu-Ni-Al, Cu-Al-Sn, and Cu-Ni-Sn diffusion couples within the Cu-rich corner.
summary: This panel maps the compositional regions of various ternary diffusion couples within the Cu-rich corner of the phase space. It demonstrates the experimental scope, including three Cu-Ni-Al couples and two each of Cu-Al-Sn and Cu-Ni-Sn, providing a visual overview of the material systems investigated in the study.

caption: Equilibrium simulation snapshot of the F3 network, illustrating the largest percolated cluster in gray and smaller clusters color-coded by size.
summary: This snapshot depicts the F3 network at equilibrium, featuring the largest percolated cluster in gray. Smaller clusters are color-coded by their bead count, allowing for a visual assessment of the network structure and the extent of cluster formation within the F3 system at the simulated equilibrium state.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of the multimetallic polymeric precursor, Sudan orange G, and TPO-L, highlighting the overlapping absorption range.
summary: The UV-Vis absorption spectra of the multimetallic polymeric precursor, Sudan orange G, and TPO-L are displayed. The gray shaded region indicates the effectively utilized waveband, which covers the overlapping absorption range of the photoinitiator and photon absorber, confirming the suitability of these components for the photopolymerization process.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for scanning strategies S3 and S4.
summary: Major axis lengths for martensite on XOY cross-sections are shown for intermittent melt pool interference modes S3 and S4. These intermittent modes are associated with larger average sizes for primary and secondary martensite compared to continuous modes, as higher cooling rates promote growth along the main axis.

caption: Simulated M-H hysteresis loops for the Cu-Fe-Ti alloy at 0 K, 150 K, and 300 K, generated using VAMPIRE software.
summary: VAMPIRE software simulations illustrate the temperature-dependent hysteretic behavior of the Cu-Fe-Ti alloy. The M-H loops at 0 K, 150 K, and 300 K reveal that at 150 K, the loop maintains magnetic saturation longer than at 300 K, where the loop exhibits a more pronounced curvature.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the built-in feature importance scores derived from a Random Forest model.
summary: This figure presents a bar chart visualizing the built-in feature importance scores calculated by a Random Forest model. The plot provides a quantitative assessment of how different input variables contribute to the model's predictive performance, as referenced in the study to illustrate the significance of specific features within the dataset.

caption: Raman spectrum obtained from the global area of oxidized TMCA, displaying vibrational modes at 141, 302, 486, 676, and 808 cm-1.
summary: The Raman spectrum of oxidized TMCA exhibits several active vibrational modes at 141, 302, 486, 676, and 808 cm-1. These specific peaks are characteristic of Al-O bonds within the material, confirming the chemical composition of the oxidized sample surface as analyzed over the global image area.

caption: Stress-strain curve diagram representing the mechanical response of the tensile specimen.
summary: This panel presents the stress-strain curve diagram for the tensile specimen. It provides a quantitative representation of the mechanical behavior and deformation characteristics of the material under uniaxial loading conditions, serving as the primary data source for evaluating the tensile properties of the tested sample.

caption: Dilatometry curve for specimen D1 tested in a nitrogen atmosphere at 1.1 bar and a flow rate of 4 L/h.
summary: This panel displays the dilatometry curve for specimen D1, which was subjected to a nitrogen atmosphere at a pressure of 1.1 bar and a flow rate of 4 L/h. The data represents the thermal expansion behavior of the material under these specific controlled environmental conditions during the dilatometry test.

caption: Nyquist plot representing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data for the substrate and coated samples.
summary: The Nyquist plot displays the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data obtained for the substrate and coated samples. This plot serves as a primary diagnostic tool for investigating the corrosion behavior of the materials, providing a visual representation of the impedance characteristics across the tested frequency range.

caption: Log-log plot of minimum creep rate versus effective stress for the as-built LPBF 316H sample, demonstrating a linear relationship with a calculated stress exponent of n = 3.0.
summary: The plot displays the minimum creep rate as a function of effective stress for the as-built LPBF 316H sample. Through linear fitting of the data on a log-log scale, a stress exponent of n = 3.0 was determined, characterizing the creep deformation mechanism of the material under the tested conditions.

caption: Linear relationship between ln(sinh(α1σs)) and ln Z for the α-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary: This plot illustrates the constitutive relationship for the α-phase of Ti6Al4V alloy by mapping the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the flow stress parameter against the natural logarithm of the Zener-Hollomon parameter. The linear trend demonstrates the correlation between deformation conditions and flow stress behavior in this phase.

caption: FCC with BCC (FBCC) hybrid lattice structure combining elements of both face-centered and body-centered cubic arrangements.
summary: The FBCC lattice structure is shown as a hybrid configuration that merges the geometric characteristics of both FCC and BCC unit cells. This combination creates a complex repeating unit that leverages the distinct properties of both cubic systems, often used to tailor the mechanical response of lattice materials.

caption: Ternary Ni–Pt–Al phase diagram illustrating the diffusion path of a Ni-13Al alloy coupled with a Pt foil after 15 minutes of annealing at 1100 °C in an argon secondary vacuum.
summary: This ternary Ni–Pt–Al phase diagram displays the experimental diffusion path for a Ni-13Al alloy reacted with a Pt foil at 1100 °C. Crosses represent experimental data points, while continuous and dashed lines indicate known and speculated diffusion paths, respectively, specifically identifying the sequence Pt–α-NiPtAl–γ′-(Ni,Pt)3Al–γ-(Ni,Pt,Al)–Ni-13Al.

caption: Optical micrograph of the weld metal (WM) specimen featuring a lath bainite (LB) dominated microstructure.
summary: This optical micrograph of the weld metal specimen shows a lath bainite dominated microstructure obtained after heat treatment. The image confirms that the intended ferrite morphology was successfully achieved in this zone, simulating the microstructure of the as-received heat-affected zone and indicating the disappearance of prior austenite grain boundaries.

caption: Microstructure of Mg–6Zn powders treated at 560 °C for 50 min, showing persistent particle shapes and ongoing liquid phase formation around Mg powder surfaces.
summary: The microstructure at 560 °C shows little variation from the 480 °C and 520 °C samples. The Mg–6Zn powders continue to exhibit encapsulated Mg surfaces due to the presence of the liquid phase. The optical and SEM images confirm that the overall particle morphology remains stable at this temperature.

caption: Side view of the stub column test assembly, showing the vertical alignment of the specimen and the interface between the end plates and the loading apparatus.
summary: The side view of the stub column test assembly provides a clear perspective on the vertical alignment of the specimen. It demonstrates how the 9 mm thick end plates are positioned at each end to maintain structural stability and ensure an even distribution of the load throughout the test.

caption: Time history of free surface elevation at wave probe WP13 for a 1.0° roll amplitude and 10 mm actuator amplitude at a 4.0 s period, showing slight differences between FDM and CFD predictions.
summary: Representing the time history at wave probe WP13 for a 1.0° roll amplitude and 10 mm actuator amplitude at a 4.0 s period, this graph compares FDM and CFD simulation results. The data indicates that only slight differences are visible between the two approaches at this specific wave probe location.

caption: Actual versus predicted stress values derived from the SVR model at a strain rate of 0.001 s-1 across multiple temperature conditions.
summary: Panel d presents the performance evaluation of the SVR model by plotting actual versus predicted stress values at a strain rate of 0.001 s-1. These results provide a quantitative assessment of the SVR model's ability to capture stress behavior across diverse temperature conditions.

caption: Final phase of the standard DCEP process showing the molten pool state and droplet transition characteristics.
summary: The final phase of the standard DCEP process is shown, focusing on the molten pool state and droplet transition. This high-speed imaging provides essential data on the slag flow mechanism, completing the comparative study between the CMT and standard DCEP processes as illustrated in the figure.

caption: Phonon DOS and vibrational free energy curves for bcc AlCo2, with L-S relationship predictions plotted as black lines and full phonon calculations as red lines.
summary: Displayed are the phonon density of states and vibrational free energy for bcc AlCo2. The plot compares black lines, representing L-S relationship predictions, with red lines obtained from full phonon calculations. These results characterize the vibrational behavior of the bcc AlCo2 phase within the Co-Al system.

caption: Rate performance evaluation of a-Si0.9Ge0.1, a-Si0.8Ge0.2, a-Si0.7Ge0.3, and a-Si0.5Ge0.5 thin-films.
summary: Rate performance tests were conducted on SiGe thin-film materials with different proportions. Panel d displays the rate capability of the four a-SiGe thin-film compositions, illustrating how each material maintains its discharge capacity under varying current densities, which is critical for assessing the high-rate performance of these battery anode materials.

caption: Spectral changes in the UV-Vis absorption of O-14 during continuous 365 nm LED irradiation in an air-saturated acetonitrile solution.
summary: This panel presents the steady-state photolysis of O-14 in acetonitrile. The absorption spectra confirm the molecule's ability to undergo cleavage at 365 nm. Despite having a lower molar extinction coefficient than O-16, O-14 demonstrates a higher photocleavage ability after 240 seconds of irradiation, as evidenced by the spectral consumption data.
