caption: Lap shear load-displacement curves for Ni625 to Ti 6242 VFA spot welds at 8 kJ, showing failure modes through the weld interface.
summary: The lap shear load-displacement curves for Ni625 to Ti 6242 VFA spot welds at 8 kJ are presented. Testing reveals that these samples fail through the weld interface, as shown in the inset. The failure load remains below the 11,500 N threshold required for the parent Ti-Ti spot weld.

caption: Comparison of Vickers hardness values measured in the gauge and grip regions of L-PBF Inconel 718 samples following uniaxial tensile testing at various temperatures and a constant strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
summary: Vickers hardness measurements reveal a 10% increase in the gauge region for samples deformed at 250 and 450 °C compared to those tested at 25 °C, indicating a thermal influence. Furthermore, the hardness trend observed between 450 and 650 °C correlates positively with the yield strength behavior over that same temperature range.

caption: Stress-life behavior of L-PBF Ti-64 specimens after filtering, where marker dimensions and color scales correspond to the √area of critical defects.
summary: Fatigue behavior of L-PBF Ti-64 after filtering is displayed, with marker size and color representing the crack-initiating defect size (√area). Comparison with the before-filter condition indicates that the filter condition has a negligible effect on the fatigue behavior, as the critical defect sizes remain similar.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map illustrating the crystallographic orientation of the vertically printed sample perpendicular to the building direction.
summary: Crystallographic orientation data for the vertically printed sample is presented in this IPF map. Captured perpendicular to the building direction post-experiment, the map reveals the texture and grain orientation distribution, offering insights into the microstructural response of the vertically printed material to the experimental conditions performed in the study.

caption: Young's modulus comparison for 3D-P/G/Si scaffolds with varying pore sizes, including statistical significance.
summary: This bar chart displays the Young's modulus for 3D-P/G/Si scaffolds with different pore sizes. The data indicates that all scaffolds fall within the range of Young's modulus observed in cartilage tissue, demonstrating that the printing parameters effectively maintain the required mechanical properties despite variations in the scaffold architecture.

caption: Laser confocal microscopy images of Al-6061 single tracks deposited via JOD at varying jet spacings and build plate temperatures of 350°C and 450°C.
summary: Laser confocal microscopy images reveal the morphology of Al-6061 single tracks fabricated using JOD printing. The tracks were deposited at a constant stage velocity of 20 mm/s under varying jet spacings and build plate temperatures of 350°C and 450°C, providing a visual assessment of the deposition quality and track continuity.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction of the 1.0Mo2.1W alloy, illustrating the spatial distribution of alloying elements within the tip sample, with the γ/γ′ phase interface delineated by a 9.0 at% Al concentration isosurface.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction visualizes the spatial distribution of alloying elements in the 1.0Mo2.1W alloy. The interface between the γ and γ′ phases is clearly defined by a 9.0 at% Al concentration isosurface, providing a detailed view of the microstructural arrangement and elemental partitioning within the material.

caption: Comparison of I-V curves for a 3x3 mm HPE60 i-wi specimen at rest and under mechanical extension states of 50% and 100%.
summary: The I-V behavior of a 3x3 mm HPE60 i-wi sample is evaluated at rest and under mechanical strain. By comparing the curves at 50% and 100% extension, the panel demonstrates the impact of deformation on the electrical conductivity and current-potential characteristics of the HPE60 material under DC conditions.

caption: Tanδ versus temperature curves for CP-PLA composites with varying CP content additions.
summary: This panel displays the Tanδ behavior of CP-PLA composites as a function of temperature for different CP loading levels. The data indicates that the Tanδ values follow the specific order of Tanδ PLA < Tanδ CP15-PLA, demonstrating the influence of CP concentration on the viscoelastic damping properties of the composite material.

caption: Simulated solidification microstructure at the edge position of the 14th layer in the curved component.
summary: This simulation shows the solidification microstructure at the edge position of the 14th layer, located at the bottom of the component. Efficient heat transfer to the substrate results in a higher cooling rate, producing finer dendrites and weak segregation, characterized by small, discrete, particle-like Laves phases.

caption: Voltage profile recorded across the arc during the duration of one pulsation cycle.
summary: The voltage variation across the arc is plotted over the course of one full pulsation cycle. Recorded alongside the current, this measurement characterizes the electrical behavior of the arc system, with the data acquisition facilitated by high-speed imaging techniques to ensure precise synchronization with the pulsation events.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of #40HSLA steel captured after the completion of tensile testing.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the crystallographic orientation of the #40HSLA steel microstructure following tensile deformation. By comparing this post-test state to the as-built condition, the map helps characterize the microstructural evolution and grain orientation changes that occur as a result of the applied mechanical stress during the tensile test.

caption: Magnetic specific heat C mag of hcp Co determined by Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: This panel shows the magnetic specific heat C mag for hcp cobalt, as modeled through Monte Carlo simulation. The plot characterizes the magnetic thermal response of the hcp phase, which is essential for understanding the phase-dependent magnetic behavior of cobalt within the scope of the simulation study.

caption: Normalized work hardening curves illustrating the deformation behavior of Alloy B samples processed under various conditions, plotted alongside the reference curve for Alloy A at 64.1 J/mm3 VED.
summary: Normalized work hardening curves are shown for various Alloy B samples and the Alloy A reference sample. These curves provide insight into the strain hardening behavior of the materials. The data highlights the differences in work hardening response between the Alloy B variants and the Alloy A control specimen.

caption: Reflectance RL curves showing the simultaneous optimization of multiple absorption peaks for L8 GMSs.
summary: L8 GMSs enable the simultaneous optimization of one to three absorption peaks as shown in this panel. This result further demonstrates the effectiveness of the customized method proposed in this work for absorption peak tailoring, highlighting the capability to manipulate multiple peaks within the L8 gradient structure.

caption: Impact test specimen of the 3D printed PLA/Hemp biocomposite used for evaluating material toughness.
summary: The impact test specimen shown here represents the 3D printed PLA/Hemp biocomposite used to assess material toughness. The experimental results for this specimen demonstrate a significant degree of diversity in impact strength, highlighting the variability inherent in the mechanical response of these bio-based composite materials under high-rate loading conditions.

caption: Numerical FEA ballistic simulation result for the PM9-450 configuration.
summary: This panel presents the numerical FEA ballistic simulation result for the PM9-450 configuration. By comparing this computational output with the experimental data, the study validates the accuracy of the numerical model in predicting the ballistic response and deformation behavior of the material under the specified test conditions.

caption: Comparative deployment architecture illustrating the infrastructure requirements for Small Language Models (SLMs) versus Large Language Models (LLMs).
summary: This schematic contrasts the deployment requirements for SLMs and LLMs. Supporting a large number of users with LLMs creates a significant scalability bottleneck, necessitating a centralized cluster capable of sustaining high throughput during every inference cycle, whereas SLMs offer a more efficient alternative for distributed or resource-constrained deployment environments.

caption: Dislocation network configuration observed at 300 K.
summary: This panel displays a molecular dynamics snapshot of the dislocation network within the material at a temperature of 300 K. The visualization highlights the initial structural arrangement of dislocations, providing a baseline for understanding how these defects evolve and interact as the thermal energy of the system increases.

caption: Defect analysis of the specimen surface performed without applying edge distance filtering.
summary: This panel displays a defect analysis of the specimen surface conducted without edge distance filtering. The visualization highlights an increased number of surface defects identified via CT-scan. These findings are part of a broader investigation into volumetric defects induced by LPBF, distinguishing between actual porosity and surface-related features.

caption: FTIR spectra of WE and ESE extracts showing characteristic functional group absorption bands.
summary: The FTIR spectra of WE and ESE extracts are presented to characterize their constituent functional groups. This spectroscopic analysis provides a chemical fingerprint of the extracts, allowing for the identification of molecular vibrations and the comparison of chemical compositions between the two different extraction samples.

caption: AgNP ink nozzle surface after 8.5 minutes of idle exposure at 25 °C, displaying mild ink spreading around the orifice without clogging.
summary: AgNP ink nozzles exposed to 25 °C for 8.5 minutes exhibit mild ink spreading around the orifice. This spreading occurs because the ink has a lower contact angle, causing it to move beyond the orifice boundary, yet the nozzle remains free of significant clogging or residue accumulation.

caption: Tabulated data summarizing the measured sample contact angle results.
summary: The tabulated data provides a quantitative summary of the measured contact angle results for the samples. This information complements the visual images of the contact angle, allowing for a precise comparison of the surface wettability properties across the different sample groups evaluated in the experimental analysis.

caption: TGA mass loss curves for five CuSn10/biopolymer composite filaments, demonstrating consistent mass reduction trends.
summary: TGA results for five CuSn10/biopolymer composite filaments show mass losses between 6 wt% and 7 wt%. BrzPA5 and BrzPA10 exhibit single-step mass reduction similar to PLA, while BrzPBA5, BrzPBA7.5, and BrzPBA10 show two-step mass loss profiles up to 485 °C, mirroring the thermal behavior of the BVOH polymer component.

caption: Comparison of dry and wet effective thicknesses for polymer brushes (PBs) synthesized in microfluidic stack reactors versus standard reactors, determined via spectroscopic ellipsometry.
summary: Spectroscopic ellipsometry measurements reveal that polymer brushes synthesized in microfluidic stack reactors consistently exhibit greater dry and wet thicknesses compared to those prepared in standard reactors. These results confirm that despite identical polymerization conditions, the reactor architecture significantly influences the final film thickness of the synthesized polymer brushes.

caption: Schematic representation of the corrosion process occurring within the L-PBF 7075 Al alloy cross-section, illustrating the progression of localized degradation.
summary: This diagram illustrates the corrosion process occurring within the L-PBF 7075 Al alloy cross-section. It highlights the mechanism of localized degradation, where MgZn2 precipitates at grain boundaries act as preferential corrosion sites, leading to severe intergranular corrosion as the material interacts with the corrosive environment during the process.

caption: Calculated electronic band structure of CoSi near the Fermi level, determined via GGA-PBE density functional theory without spin-orbit coupling, highlighting a Dirac-like linear dispersion at the Γ point and a multiplet feature at the R point.
summary: This band structure of CoSi, calculated using GGA-PBE without spin-orbit coupling, reveals a Dirac-like band with linear dispersion at the Γ point. The node at the Γ point is positioned near the Fermi level, while a multiplet feature at the R point is located approximately 200 meV below the Fermi level.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for SLM-manufactured Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr-Mn alloys processed at a scanning speed of 1050 mm/s with varying laser power levels.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for SLM-manufactured Al-Mg-Si-Sc-Zr-Mn alloys processed at a scanning speed of 1050 mm/s with varying laser power levels. The samples exhibit a distinct serrated fluctuation characteristic of the Portevin-Le Chatelier effect. Increasing laser power at this constant scanning speed leads to a general decrease in tensile strength, suggesting that excessively high energy density negatively impacts mechanical performance.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of pure HPC, showing the baseline optical response.
summary: This reflectance spectrum characterizes the optical properties of pure HPC. It provides the baseline data for comparing the reflected wavelengths of HPCA samples. The spectrum is part of a set used to analyze how the helical structure and degree of substitution influence the material's light reflection characteristics.

caption: Electrochemical performance evaluation showing open-circuit potential versus time measurements and anodic polarization plots in simulated body fluid (SBF) for uncoated, HA, 2GO/HA, and 5GO/HA coatings.
summary: Electrochemical performance is assessed through open-circuit potential versus time measurements and anodic polarization plots conducted in simulated body fluid. These tests compare the corrosion resistance of uncoated, HA, 2GO/HA, and 5GO/HA coatings, demonstrating the influence of different coating compositions on the electrochemical stability of the Al-MMC materials in physiological environments.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of spatter generation (SG) versus porosity, indicating that low levels of spatter are occasionally associated with increased porosity, potentially linked to undermelting.
summary: This SHAP scatter plot illustrates the relationship between spatter generation and porosity. Observations suggest that low levels of spatter generation can serve as indicators for porosity, which may be attributed to underlying issues related to undermelting during the process. The plot maps these feature values against their contribution to porosity.

caption: Cross-sectional microstructure of CM-H13 specimen subjected to a 9.8 N applied load.
summary: This panel shows the cross-sectional morphology of the CM-H13 material under a 9.8 N applied load. As part of the comparative study, this image provides a baseline for the CM-H13 variant, enabling an assessment of its microstructural response to low-level mechanical loading relative to other processed samples.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength as a function of elongation for Al-Mn-Cr-Zr alloys alongside reference data for PBF-LB AM, wrought, and cast aluminum alloys.
summary: Ultimate tensile strength is displayed against elongation for Al-Mn-Cr-Zr alloys, providing a comparative analysis against conventional cast, wrought, and PBF-LB AM aluminum alloys. By utilizing representative data points for 18 conditions, this plot effectively maps the tensile performance of the studied alloys within the broader context of aluminum metallurgy.

caption: Response surface plot depicting the relationship between pulse-on time (Ton) and pulse-off time (Toff) on material removal rate (MRR).
summary: This visualization highlights the dependency of material removal rate on pulse-on and pulse-off durations. Increasing pulse-on time extends the spark duration per cycle, and increasing pulse-off time facilitates better debris removal, both of which are critical factors for maximizing the material removal rate during the machining operation.

caption: Compact Statix setup integrated within a laboratory tomograph, maintaining a 12 mm sample-to-source distance for high-resolution imaging.
summary: The photograph illustrates the Statix device installed within a laboratory tomograph. Its compact design allows it to fit effectively inside the imaging system, providing a fixed sample-to-source distance of 12 mm, which is essential for performing in situ tension experiments while capturing high-quality tomographic data of the specimen.

caption: Raman spectrum of pure CNT powders, displaying broad vibrational bands characteristic of partially disordered carbon structures.
summary: Raman spectroscopy of pure CNT powders exhibits broad vibrational bands, which are characteristic of partially disordered carbon structures. This spectral data serves as a baseline for comparison with the CNT-copper composite, confirming the structural nature of the carbon nanotubes used in the experimental powder mixtures.

caption: Temperature-dependent DC magnetic susceptibility of the TEM foil measured during cooling (blue) and heating (red) at 4 K/min, highlighting phase transitions and the presence of the NM phase.
summary: This panel displays the DC magnetic susceptibility of a TEM foil as a function of temperature during thermal cycling. The cooling and heating curves, recorded at 4 K/min, reveal structural and magnetic transitions. Notably, the data indicates the presence of an NM phase not typically observed in bulk samples at room temperature.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of an additively manufactured NiTi stent, displaying the characteristic transformation peaks associated with the B2 austenite to R-phase transition during cooling.
summary: This DSC curve characterizes the transformation temperatures of an additively manufactured NiTi stent. The plot reveals broad transformation peaks, indicating the B2 to R-phase transition during cooling. These thermal results provide essential data on the temperature hysteresis and phase stability of the near-equiatomic NiTi material used in the stent.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plot for the B10-0.1 wt% Ce alloy specimen after varying immersion durations in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This Bode impedance magnitude plot characterizes the B10-0.1 wt% Ce alloy during immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl. Consistent with the general trend for these alloys, the low-frequency impedance increases rapidly at the start of the immersion period, exhibits minor fluctuations over time, and ultimately stabilizes as the exposure duration increases.

caption: Comparison of vibrational free energy and phonon DOS for fcc AlCo3, using L-S relationship predictions (black) and full phonon calculations (red).
summary: The vibrational free energy and phonon density of states for fcc AlCo3 are shown in this panel. The plot contrasts the L-S relationship predictions, indicated by black lines, with full phonon calculations, indicated by red lines, to evaluate the reliability of the L-S method for this aluminum-cobalt phase.

caption: Representative raw grinding force data plotted over time, illustrating the force components in the y and z directions resulting from the grinding wheel orbit, alongside the axial x-direction force which remains minimal in the absence of wheel actuation.
summary: This plot displays raw grinding force data, highlighting the force contributions from the grinding wheel orbit in the y and z directions. The axial x-direction force is shown to be minimal, confirming that axial force is effectively suppressed when the grinding wheel actuation is disabled during the machining process.

caption: Fitness curve for scenario 5, displaying error trends across input values ranging from 0 to 5 at 0.5 intervals.
summary: Scenario 5 fitness analysis is presented, showcasing the application of the ANN-BLMA approach. The plot visualizes error trends across input values from 0 to 5 at 0.5 intervals, providing a clear representation of the network's performance and convergence behavior within this specific critical scenario for the artificial backpropagation network.

caption: Force-displacement curves illustrating the mechanical response of five-layer structures under compression.
summary: This plot displays the force-displacement curves for five-layer structures subjected to compression deformation. These curves characterize the mechanical response of the specimens, providing insight into their structural behavior during the loading process. The data complements the compression deformation observations, highlighting the mechanical performance of the five distinct structural configurations.

caption: WDS-derived elemental concentration profiles for the initial diffused Pt coated sample microstructure.
summary: Initial WDS concentration profiles for the diffused Pt coated sample are displayed. These profiles establish the baseline elemental distribution for the Pt-diffused coating, allowing for a comparative analysis of how the concentration gradients of Al, Co, Pt, and Ni evolve under subsequent high-temperature oxidation conditions.

caption: Short staircase sequence performed at 10^7 cycles to determine the fatigue limit of the Ti6Al4V material, representing the intersection point where the sloping fatigue curve transitions to the fatigue limit.
summary: The staircase sequence shown at 10^7 cycles is utilized to experimentally determine the fatigue limit of the Ti6Al4V material. This sequence marks the transition point where the sloping portion of the fatigue curve intersects with the fatigue limit, providing a precise threshold for long-term cyclic loading performance.

caption: Chronopotentiometry profile of the Ni-Fe alloy in 1 M NaOH at a constant current density of -10 mA cm⁻² over a 15-hour duration.
summary: Chronopotentiometry testing at -10 mA cm⁻² reveals the potential evolution of the Ni-Fe alloy over 15 hours. The potential starts at -0.26635 V, reaches a minimum at 31,000 seconds, and eventually recovers to -0.42304 V, demonstrating the material's potential-dependent current behavior during sustained operation in alkaline conditions.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the Cu-Ni-Co-Si-Cr alloy deformation zone, highlighting the distribution of nano-scale precipitates on dislocations, grain boundaries, and the matrix.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph corresponds to the deformation zone shown in panel (d). It provides a clear visualization of nano-scale precipitates distributed across dislocations, grain boundaries, and the matrix, illustrating the spatial relationship between the fine-scale precipitation and the alloy's substructural features following thermal deformation at 800 °C.

caption: Geometric configurations of latticed auxetic unit cells designed with negative Poisson’s ratios ranging from -0.2 to -0.8, solved via a machine learning-driven inverse design framework.
summary: Geometric configurations of the latticed auxetic unit cells are presented, showcasing a range of negative Poisson's ratios from -0.2 to -0.8. These specific patterns were determined using a machine learning-driven inverse design framework and have been validated through experimental testing to ensure their auxetic mechanical properties are accurately represented.

caption: Hierarchical ranking of four surface parameters based on their influence in identifying keyhole mode samples during processing.
summary: This panel displays the hierarchical importance of four distinct surface parameters in the identification of keyhole mode formation. By quantifying the influence of each feature, the plot provides a clear ranking that highlights which surface characteristics are most critical for predicting the occurrence of keyhole mode during material processing.

caption: Stress rupture life performance of the specimen evaluated under high-temperature creep conditions at 950 °C and 235 MPa.
summary: This figure presents the stress rupture life of the specimen tested at 950 °C and 235 MPa. The data illustrates the results of the stress rupture test under these specific high-temperature and high-stress conditions, providing a clear indication of the material's durability and failure behavior during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Skeletonized view of the E-PBF H282 build, emphasizing the internal cube-shaped void architecture within the bulk material.
summary: The skeletonized 3D view reveals the internal cube void structures inherent in the E-PBF H282 build. These internal features are critical components of the fabricated geometry, which also incorporates thin wall struts, providing a comprehensive overview of the complex internal architecture produced by the additive manufacturing process.

caption: NDFI projections comparing stress-relieved (HT-SR) and heat-treated (HT-HIP) pure and TiC-modified IN718, demonstrating the suppression of periodic LOF-related contrast after HIP.
summary: Neutron diffraction projections show the impact of heat treatment on defect distribution. The HT-SR samples exhibit periodic contrast related to lack-of-fusion (LOF) defects. Following the HT-HIP process, this contrast is effectively suppressed, indicating that the hot isostatic pressing successfully mitigates these build-related defects in both pure and TiC-modified IN718.

caption: Original STL input geometry representing the bunny model used as the baseline for the smoothing process.
summary: The bunny model serves as the initial STL input for the proposed smoothing technique. This geometry is discretized directly using octree mesh decomposition to facilitate subsequent processing steps, providing a baseline for evaluating the effectiveness of the smoothing algorithms applied in the following stages of the study.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Al–Ni–V ternary system at 1473 K, incorporating experimental data points from Jia et al. and Prima et al., alongside the deduced E1 invariant at 1453 K reported by Hayes et al.
summary: This isothermal section at 1473 K illustrates the phase equilibria of the Al–Ni–V system. The diagram integrates experimental data from Jia et al. and Prima et al. to validate the calculated phase boundaries, while also highlighting the E1 invariant point at 1453 K as determined by Hayes et al.

caption: Specific capacitance versus scan rate for the supercapacitor under folding conditions, highlighting the reduction in accessible capacitance with increasing mechanical severity.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific capacitance of the supercapacitor as a function of scan rate during folding. The data shows a progressive reduction in accessible capacitance as the severity of the folding increases, reflecting the impact of mechanical stress on the device's electrochemical performance while maintaining its capacitive behavior.

caption: Neuro-fuzzy surface plot illustrating the variation of Tool Wear Rate (TWR) as a function of pulse-on time and the fraction of Al/Cu/Ni.
summary: This neuro-fuzzy surface plot displays the relationship between TWR and the interaction of pulse-on time and the Al/Cu/Ni fraction. The visualization indicates a significant change in TWR as pulse-on time increases, while other process parameters are maintained at their mean positions to isolate the specific impact of these variables.

caption: Energy dispersive spectroscopy mapping photographs of the as-deposited WAAM sample, illustrating the distribution of elements and intergranular segregation.
summary: Energy dispersive spectroscopy mapping photographs reveal the elemental distribution within the as-deposited WAAM sample. As the homogenization process proceeds, intergranular segregation improves continuously. This structural refinement promotes the transformation of coarse columnar grains into equiaxed grains and effectively reduces grain boundary segregation throughout the material matrix.

caption: Low-magnification bright-field TEM image of the as-built Al–Mg–Er–Zr-Sc alloy, illustrating the distinct regions of equiaxed grains and columnar grains within a molten pool.
summary: This low-magnification bright-field TEM image provides an overview of the as-built Al–Mg–Er–Zr-Sc alloy microstructure. It clearly distinguishes between the equiaxed grain region and the columnar grain region within the molten pool, establishing the morphological context for the subsequent detailed analysis of the equiaxed grain structures.

caption: Calculated gravimetric and areal specific capacitance values derived from the charge/discharge profiles of the ASC device.
summary: Calculated gravimetric and areal specific capacitance values derived from the charge/discharge profiles of the ASC device. These results quantify the charge storage capacity of the hybrid system, providing essential data on how the specific capacitance varies as a function of the applied current density during device operation.

caption: Bode phase plot representing the frequency-dependent phase angle response of the electrochemical system.
summary: This Bode phase plot illustrates the frequency-dependent phase angle response of the electrochemical system under investigation. It serves as a fundamental component of the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis, providing insight into the capacitive and resistive characteristics of the material interface as part of the broader characterization of the electrochemical behavior.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image of the substrate revealing a high density of dislocations resulting from plastic deformation.
summary: The bright-field transmission electron microscopy image provides a detailed view of the substrate's internal structure. It reveals a large number of dislocations generated by plastic deformation within the material, illustrating the impact of the processing history on the dislocation density of the GH4169 superalloy.

caption: Non-equilibrium Al-Yb phase diagram focusing on the Al-rich region, highlighting the eutectic coupled zone (ECZ) in green and experimental data points in purple.
summary: This non-equilibrium Al-Yb phase diagram illustrates the Al-rich side, specifically identifying the eutectic coupled zone (ECZ) as a green shaded region. Experimental values, represented by purple points, are determined using a eutectic growth model. These results confirm the reliability of the diagram and facilitate detailed microstructural analysis within the hypoeutectic zone.

caption: Experimental setup of a C CFR 3D printer by Broetje-Automation GmbH during the additive manufacturing of a layered technology demonstrator part.
summary: This photograph illustrates the additive manufacturing process of a layered technology demonstrator part using an experimental C CFR 3D printer developed by Broetje-Automation GmbH. The system utilizes continuous carbon fiber bundles and PPS matrix material, demonstrating a minimum turning radius of 15 mm for reinforced printing applications.

caption: Density of states plot for the HfC(001)/Ni3Al(011) interface, showing the Fermi level as a black dashed line and the orbital hybrid position as a blue dashed line.
summary: This density of states plot for the HfC(001)/Ni3Al(011) interface displays multiple formant peaks between -5 eV and 0 eV. These features signify strong interactions between Ni-C and Al-C bonds, with the interface DOS intensity and position notably varying from internal material values, reflecting significant charge redistribution at the interface.

caption: Optical microscopy image of the Mg–4Zn–1Ca surface after ball burnishing, revealing a refined microstructure with an average grain size of 13 ± 1 μm.
summary: Microstructural analysis of the Mg–4Zn–1Ca surface following the ball burnishing process demonstrates significant grain refinement. The optical microscopy image confirms that the surface region achieves an average grain size of 13 ± 1 μm, highlighting the effectiveness of the mechanical surface treatment in modifying the alloy's near-surface microstructure.

caption: Minimum creep rate versus rupture time for sand-cast Haynes 282 alloy at 704 °C, 760 °C, and 788 °C.
summary: This plot displays the minimum creep rate as a function of rupture time for sand-cast Haynes 282 alloy. The experimental results across all three test temperatures confirm that the minimum creep rate is inversely proportional to the rupture time, following a consistent trend for the material under these conditions.

caption: Surface tension-gated microfluidic transistor logic circuit utilizing DLTMC diodes to activate LED pathways.
summary: This diagram illustrates a selective logic circuit designed using DLTMC diodes. By leveraging differential permeability based on liquid surface tension, specific fluids like aqueous or ethanol solutions activate designated LED pathways, effectively creating a surface tension-gated microfluidic transistor that functions as a programmable logic gate.

caption: Temperature dependence of critical magnetic fields HMs and HAf, along with the calculated equilibrium magnetic field H0, for 0Co, 4Co, and 8Co samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent behavior of critical magnetic fields HMs and HAf for 0Co, 4Co, and 8Co samples. The equilibrium magnetic field H0, defined as the average of HMs and HAf, is shown to increase consistently as the temperature decreases across all tested material compositions.

caption: Electrochemical parameters including corrosion current density (Icorr) and corrosion potential (Ecorr) derived from Tafel extrapolation of the polarization curves.
summary: Electrochemical parameters, specifically corrosion current density (Icorr) and corrosion potential (Ecorr), are derived from the Tafel extrapolation of the polarization curves. These values provide critical insights into the corrosion kinetics of the Mg–Er–Ni alloys under the specified experimental conditions in a 3 wt.% KCl solution.

caption: Tabulated material parameters for AlSi10Mg, including plastic constants (A, B, C, n, p) and fracture parameters (D1 through D5) derived from established constitutive equations.
summary: The table presents the essential material properties for AlSi10Mg used in the simulation. It lists the plastic parameters A, B, C, n, and p, alongside fracture parameters D1 through D5. These values are sourced from literature and are critical for defining the material behavior within the finite element model.

caption: Elemental composition in weight percent measured by EDX on the untreated top surface of the manufactured sample.
summary: EDX analysis of the untreated top surface provides the elemental weight percentages shown in this bar chart. Comparative studies indicate that the chemical composition here differs from other surfaces, with the formation of oxide layers contributing to these variations in the measured elemental content across the manufactured component.

caption: Real-time tracking of CAR-T-mediated cytotoxicity using red fluorescence-labeled LCOs and green fluorescence-labeled Control-T or EGFR-CAR-T cells.
summary: Real-time fluorescence tracking visualizes the interaction between LCOs and T cells. By labeling LCOs with a red tracer and T cells with a green tracer, the experiment allows for the direct observation of CAR-T-mediated cytotoxicity, confirming the targeted destruction of tumor organoids by the engineered EGFR-CAR-T cells.

caption: Cell voltage versus capacity variation for 16P-9N and 9P-16N dimpled metallic bipolar plate configurations at an electrolyte circulation velocity of 4 mm/s and a current density of 100 mA/cm2.
summary: This plot displays the charge-discharge capacity behavior of dimpled metallic bipolar plate cells at a 4 mm/s electrolyte circulation velocity. Comparing the 16P-9N and 9P-16N configurations at a constant current density of 100 mA/cm2, the data illustrates the electrochemical performance characteristics of these specific flow battery cell designs.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectra of various oxime esters measured in acetonitrile solvent.
summary: This plot displays the UV–visible absorption spectra for a series of oxime esters in acetonitrile. The data illustrates distinct light absorption profiles, such as the 355 nm maximum for O-12, which directly correlate with their performance in polymerization reactions when exposed to specific light sources like LED@365 nm or LED@395 nm.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of copper at 600 °C, displaying distinct metal oxidation peaks followed by oxygen evolution.
summary: Copper shows a high current under polarization during the initial cyclic scan at 600 °C. The cyclic voltammogram reveals clear metal oxidation peaks at low polarization, specifically corresponding to Cu to Cu2O and Cu2O to CuO transitions, followed by a discernible oxygen evolution response at higher potentials.

caption: Violin plot of avalanche angles for AlSi10Mg, AM3D7, and AM3D7+BN powders, showing the distribution and median values of flow consistency.
summary: The violin plot displays the distribution of avalanche angles for the tested powders. AM3D7+BN shows a narrow distribution centered at a lower median angle, indicating consistent flow. Conversely, AlSi10Mg exhibits a large standard deviation, reflecting higher inconsistency and sensitivity to physical properties like morphology during the flowability testing.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of the sintered 3D printed PGMs+TiO2+Si composite, highlighting increased surface roughness and sharper features compared to the green state.
summary: Following the sintering process, this atomic force microscopy image illustrates the significant change in surface morphology of the 3D printed PGMs+TiO2+Si composite. The formerly smooth surface has become noticeably rougher and sharper, with surface imperfections clearly visible, indicating the structural evolution of the material after thermal treatment.

caption: Infrared thermal monitoring image of a 1.0 mm diameter wire tip captured immediately after the arc was extinguished, showing a surface temperature of 236.1 °C at the designated measuring spot.
summary: Infrared thermal monitoring of a 1.0 mm wire diameter reveals a surface temperature of 236.1 °C at the wire tip immediately after the arc is switched off. This measurement, taken at the arc-off position, provides critical data on the thermal state of the wire during the WAAM process.

caption: Isoconversional KAS plot of ln(β/Tα^2) versus 1/T for 30 h milled HEA powders, highlighting the reduction behavior.
summary: Representing the reduction kinetics for 30 h milled HEA powders, this plot confirms the reduction of Cr2O3. A conversion fraction of 0.75 is achieved at 881 °C, demonstrating a shift from the expected 0.727 value and indicating enhanced reduction behavior compared to the 5 h milled sample.

caption: Flexural load-displacement curve of the S-I honeycomb structure, highlighting six distinct stages of mechanical response labeled ① through ⑥.
summary: This load-displacement curve characterizes the flexural response of the S-I honeycomb structure. It identifies six critical stages of deformation, providing a quantitative record of the structural behavior under loading. The curve serves as the primary reference for correlating mechanical performance with the observed physical deformation modes during the test.

caption: Confocal fluorescent images of the printed scaffolds showing live cells in green and dead cells in red, with arrows marking the hollow core regions.
summary: Confocal fluorescent imaging was utilized to assess cell viability within the printed scaffolds. The majority of cells appear green, indicating that the co-axial printing process did not induce significant cellular damage. Arrows in the images highlight the hollow core regions, demonstrating that the printing process maintains high cell viability within the scaffold.

caption: Visualization of the arc radius determination process, illustrating the evaluation of a cubic interpolation function within the feasible parameter space.
summary: This plot demonstrates the methodology for determining arc parameters, specifically the arc radius. By evaluating a cubic interpolation function across the defined feasible space, the arc radius is efficiently calculated. This approach provides a rapid and accurate means of parameter estimation as shown in the graphical representation of the function.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy micrograph of the HT-1 sample showing the distribution of the γ'' phase.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy reveals the microstructure of the HT-1 sample. The γ'' phase is present within the material, characterized by an average length of 21.43 nm and an average thickness of 7.08 nm. This imaging provides direct visualization of the phase morphology resulting from the HT-1 heat treatment process.

caption: Three-dimensional topographic map illustrating the surface morphology of a thin-walled cylindrical sample printed in the +Z direction.
summary: This 3D topographic map visualizes the surface characteristics of a thin-walled cylindrical sample fabricated with a +Z gravitational orientation. The reconstruction provides a spatial representation of the sample's geometry, serving as a representative test area to quantify dynamic layer height variations observed during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Thermo-mechanical analysis of spark plasma sintered sample 1 showing displacement (ΔL) versus temperature under bending mode across multiple cycles.
summary: Thermo-mechanical analysis of spark plasma sintered sample 1 showing displacement (ΔL) versus temperature under bending mode across multiple cycles. This plot illustrates the displacement as a function of temperature for multiple cycles, revealing a distinct hysteresis effect during the thermal loading and unloading process of the sintered material.

caption: Statistical distribution of arc sag measurement results, highlighting the positive correlation between arc diameter and sag magnitude.
summary: Presented as a boxplot, the measurement results demonstrate a clear trend where the arc sag increases in proportion to the arc diameter. This statistical representation confirms the consistency of the sag effect across the tested range, showing the variability and central tendency of the measurements for each arc size.

caption: Loading curves representing the mechanical response of BCC POCS structures prepared using the SC2C slurry.
summary: Loading curves illustrate the mechanical behavior of BCC POCS structures fabricated with SC2C slurry. The adhesion tests demonstrate that incorporating Disperal P2 into the slurry significantly improves the adhesion of the catalytic layer, although the overall mechanical stability remains sensitive to the geometry and surface preparation of the structures.

caption: Equivalent circle size distribution for sample 6#.
summary: This histogram illustrates the distribution of grain equivalent circular diameters for sample 6#. It characterizes the grain size frequency resulting from the specific scanning strategy employed, contributing to the comparative analysis of grain morphology across different samples as part of the investigation into material microstructure and processing parameters.

caption: Displacement trajectory of Point-B at the gamma/gamma-prime interface, marked by red circles, illustrating movement from the origin that crosses an SF-like point without reaching the local minimum O'.
summary: Point-B, situated at the gamma/gamma-prime interface, follows a displacement path marked by red circles. It originates at O and crosses an SF-like point, characterized by a non-zero energy barrier due to the interface, but fails to reach the local minimum O' on the GSF energy surface.

caption: Total strain amplitude plotted against the number of cycles to failure for Ti2448 and Ti-6Al-4V porous samples, with arrows indicating samples that did not fail at 10^5 cycles.
summary: This panel displays the strain-controlled low-cycle fatigue properties of Ti2448 samples with RD and TO unit cells compared to Ti-6Al-4V. The total strain amplitude is plotted against the number of cycles to failure, highlighting samples that reached 10^5 cycles without failure, which are marked with arrows.

caption: Secondary electron micrograph of Alloy 2 microstructure on the XZ plane after HT 3 heat treatment, illustrating the final gamma prime precipitate state.
summary: This secondary electron micrograph shows the microstructure of Alloy 2 following HT 3 heat treatment. Observed on the XZ plane, the image highlights the gamma prime precipitates within the grain, serving as a reference for the microstructural state achieved after this specific thermal processing sequence.

caption: Microhardness variation across different regions of the GHEA sample, showing values of 342 HV, 371 HV, and 397 HV for the bottom, middle, and top regions, respectively.
summary: Microhardness measurements across the GHEA sample reveal a distinct gradient in mechanical properties. The hardness values increase from the bottom to the top of the specimen, specifically measuring 342 HV at the bottom, 371 HV in the middle, and reaching a maximum of 397 HV at the top region.

caption: Storage modulus curves as a function of temperature for TPU/CNF composites formulated with different types of CNF reinforcements.
summary: Storage modulus curves illustrate the temperature-dependent stiffness of TPU/CNF composites containing various CNF types. These DMA results, when analyzed alongside the loss factor data, provide a comprehensive overview of the dynamic mechanical properties, reflecting how different reinforcement types influence the viscoelastic behavior and structural integrity of the composite materials.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of 3D-IDCμE/PPy devices with 3–7 stacked OTU layers, recorded at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ in 1 M H₂SO₄.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for 3D-IDCμE/PPy devices with varying numbers of stacked OTU layers (3–7) are presented at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹. These curves illustrate the electrochemical performance and capacitive behavior of the on-chip micro-supercapacitors under identical testing conditions in a 1 M H₂SO₄ electrolyte environment.

caption: Local axial strain distribution map for specimen V1 subjected to uniaxial compression at nominal strain levels of 10%, 20%, and 30%.
summary: Specimen V1 exhibits a relatively homogeneous local axial strain distribution during uniaxial compression. DIC analysis at 10%, 20%, and 30% nominal strain reveals no pronounced strain localization, with higher strain values observed specifically at the z-struts compared to the cross-struts and nodes of the modified f2ccz structure.

caption: Comprehensive morphology and elemental distribution map of SLM-fabricated TC4 surfaces, illustrating the structural and chemical state before and after the anodization process.
summary: This panel provides a comprehensive overview of the morphology and elemental distribution for SLM-fabricated TC4 surfaces. By comparing the state of the material before and after anodization, the map illustrates the successful formation of the TiO2 nanotube layer and the associated changes in the surface elemental composition.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the cluster mobility as a function of inverse temperature, highlighting the kinetic suppression of vacancy-solute clusters in the A-1%B-1%C alloy.
summary: This plot displays the cluster mobility versus inverse temperature for the A-1%B-1%C alloy. The results demonstrate that adding a C solute to a VB cluster significantly decreases mobility by several orders of magnitude. This reduction in mobility effectively suppresses the kinetics of precipitation reactions within the simulated alloy system.

caption: SHAP explainability plot providing a global summary of the feature contributions for the enthalpy (ΔH) model predictions.
summary: This SHAP plot provides a global summary of the feature importance for the enthalpy model. By utilizing SHapely Additive Prediction values, the plot elucidates how specific input features influence the model's output, offering transparency into the decision-making process of the machine learning algorithm regarding thermodynamic enthalpy predictions.

caption: Chronoamperometric current transients for the 1st and 4th acidification cycles, showing the response to +0.4 V applied potential, a 60 s passive monitoring period, and a shortened -0.2 V regeneration step.
summary: Chronoamperometric curves reveal distinct electrochemical behaviors between the first and fourth cycles. The first cycle exhibits a Cottrell-like profile, whereas the fourth cycle shows an initial fast decay followed by a current increase, resulting in a peak. These transients reflect the system's response to the applied potential and regeneration steps.

caption: Computer-aided design model representing the geometric configuration of the BCCZ lattice structure.
summary: This panel displays the CAD model of the BCCZ lattice structure. The design serves as the foundational blueprint for the cubical lattice specimens, which are specified to have 6-mm sides for subsequent compressive testing. This digital representation defines the geometric parameters and architectural arrangement of the unit cell.

caption: Work exerted during the crack propagation phase plotted against the angle φ, with an insert showing the correlation between work and corrected fracture surface roughness.
summary: Work performed after reaching maximum load, representing the crack propagation phase, increases consistently with the angle φ. The insert demonstrates a positive correlation between this propagation work and the local fracture surface roughness, which is corrected to exclude height variations inherent to the specimen geometry itself.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the as-deposited WA-DED VW63K magnesium alloy showing a high density of dislocations and localized precipitates.
summary: The as-deposited WA-DED VW63K magnesium alloy microstructure is characterized by a high density of dislocations and localized precipitates. These features indicate significant residual stress and non-equilibrium solidification occurring during the WA-DED manufacturing process, as observed in the bright-field TEM imaging of the material at room temperature.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction plot for Al0.7CoCrFeNi as a function of temperature, featuring a red dashed line at 1250 °C to denote the specific processing temperature.
summary: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculations for Al0.7CoCrFeNi demonstrate phase fraction variations relative to temperature. The plot highlights the formation of multiple compounds at temperatures below 600 °C, consistent with predicted trends. The red dashed line at 1250 °C serves as a critical marker for understanding the alloy's phase stability before and after heat treatment.

caption: Crack length evolution plotted against the number of cycles for the alloy under varying loading frequencies.
summary: Crack length evolution is plotted against the number of cycles for the alloy under varying loading frequencies. This panel illustrates the progression of fatigue crack growth as a function of cycle count, providing a clear visualization of how different loading frequencies influence the crack propagation behavior in the tested material.

caption: Misorientation angle distribution for the sample annealed at 780 °C.
summary: This histogram illustrates the misorientation angle distribution for the sample after annealing at 780 °C. It allows for the assessment of how higher temperature thermal treatment influences the grain boundary population and overall crystallographic orientation distribution compared to the as-cast and 560 °C annealed conditions.

caption: Elemental distribution map of cracks in HIP + ST LPBF Inconel 625 alloy after tensile testing at 900 °C.
summary: Cracks observed in the HIP + ST LPBF Inconel 625 alloy following tensile testing at 900 °C are visualized via EDS mapping. The results demonstrate that these cracks are enriched with oxygen and silicon, consistent with the high-temperature degradation mechanisms observed across the tested temperature range for this specific alloy.

caption: Dynamic compressive stress-strain response of G1-HPC material evaluated at strain rates spanning 25.1 s⁻¹ to 106.4 s⁻¹.
summary: G1-HPC material shows specific stress-strain behavior when subjected to dynamic compression at strain rates between 25.1 s⁻¹ and 106.4 s⁻¹. The multidirectional confinement inherent in the specimen restricts the propagation of microcracks that initiate within the lattice unit cells, shaping the observed mechanical response in these curves.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of MgZnFe2O4, CoZnFe2O4, and NiZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles, illustrating the structural characteristics of the synthesized materials.
summary: The figure displays XRD patterns for MgZnFe2O4, CoZnFe2O4, and NiZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles. Analysis of these patterns reveals variations in lattice constants, with 'a' values ranging from 7.81 to 8.36 Å and 'c' values from 11.09 to 11.50 Å, confirming the distinct structural parameters for each specific ferrite composition.

caption: DSC traces for 3D printed materials, revealing two distinct thermal events occurring during the heating process.
summary: The DSC thermogram analysis of the 3D printed materials reveals two distinct thermal events. These traces provide insight into the thermal behavior and phase transitions of the printed samples, complementing the thermal stability data obtained from the thermogravimetric analysis of the AAO and LNC-containing composites.

caption: Conceptual workflow illustrating the particle swarm optimization (PSO) based structure generator used to identify optimal structural candidates.
summary: This schematic illustrates the program for seeking optimal structure candidates. The process utilizes a PSO-based structure generator where particles with random scale parameters are initially generated. This systematic approach facilitates the exploration of the structural search space to identify and refine potential candidates for further analysis.

caption: Distribution of part qualification accuracy for bracket, clip, and plug designs in the N=9 factory configuration, illustrating the performance disparity between different manufacturing specializations.
summary: This panel shows the qualification accuracy distribution for each part design at N=9 factories. Bracket factories exhibit the worst qualification performance, followed by clip factories, while plug factories demonstrate the best performance, confirming that the model's accuracy is sensitive to the specific part design being manufactured at each factory.

caption: Ionic conductivity values plotted against different LiOTf concentrations, identifying the specific loading that maximizes electrochemical transport properties.
summary: Ionic conductivity data illustrates the electrochemical behavior of the material across varying LiOTf contents. The specific formulation of 6 wt% PAA and 5 wt% LiOTf achieves an ionic conductivity of 7.48 mS/cm, confirming that this composition provides the best balance of electrochemical and mechanical properties for the electrolyte.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the Type 420 stainless steel deposit and the CF3M stainless steel substrate.
summary: This XRD pattern displays the structural characterization of the Type 420 stainless steel deposit alongside the CF3M stainless steel substrate. The analysis was conducted to identify the constituent phases and determine their relative weight percentages within both the deposited layer and the underlying substrate material through Rietveld refinement.

caption: Full-field Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution across the repaired interface.
summary: This full-field IPF map visualizes the crystallographic orientation across the repaired interface. Analysis reveals that the microstructure in the repaired area is organized into three distinct regions: a central equiaxed grain zone, a columnar grain region, and a surface fine grain region located directly adjacent to the substrate matrix.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance characteristics of the Y-Z section for the Wall 1 sample.
summary: The Y-Z section of the Wall 1 sample is analyzed through this Bode plot to determine its impedance modulus and phase angle. Consistent with the overall electrochemical assessment of Wall 1, the impedance modulus starts near 10⁴ Ω·cm², providing a baseline for evaluating the material's electrochemical performance across this specific orientation.

caption: EDS line scan profile across the AA2195/TC4 interface, highlighting a distinct intermetallic compound (IMC) layer with an interdiffusion zone approximately 1.5 μm thick.
summary: The EDS line scan analysis reveals the chemical transition across the AA2195/TC4 joint interface. A distinct intermetallic compound layer is observed, characterized by an interdiffusion zone that measures approximately 1.5 μm in thickness, indicating significant elemental migration between the aluminum and titanium alloys during the joining process.

caption: TEM micrograph revealing the presence of M2B boride networks located along the dendrite boundary of the V2 sample.
summary: This TEM micrograph highlights the formation of M2B networks situated on the dendrite boundary of the V2 sample. These secondary phase networks are characteristic of the microstructure evolution in the cladding substrate, playing a role in the overall phase distribution and mechanical properties of the material.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of region i at the diffusion couple interface, showing fcc TiAlN oriented along the [001] zone axis.
summary: Region i of the diffusion couple interface is characterized by an fcc TiAlN phase. Electron diffraction analysis confirms this phase exhibits a [001] zone axis orientation. This structural identification is supported by combining XEDS data with diffraction patterns to confirm the presence of the Ti-Al-N reaction product.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis thermograms comparing three distinct resin samples, displaying weight loss as solid lines and derivative weight loss as dashed lines.
summary: This figure presents a comparative thermogravimetric analysis of three different resin materials. The plot illustrates the thermal degradation behavior of each resin by showing weight loss curves as solid lines and their corresponding derivative weight loss curves as dashed lines, providing insight into the thermal stability and decomposition characteristics of the resins.

caption: Adiabatic temperature change dependence on temperature for the initial as-cast alloy state under alternating magnetic fields of 0.05 T and 0.2 T at a frequency of 0.3 Hz.
summary: Panel (a) displays the adiabatic temperature change (ΔTad) as a function of temperature for the initial as-cast alloy state. Measurements were conducted under alternating magnetic fields of 0.05 T and 0.2 T at a frequency of 0.3 Hz, providing baseline magnetocaloric effect data for the material prior to processing.

caption: 2D virtual slice of a rastered wick revealing the internal geometry.
summary: Captured through X-ray microtomography, this 2D virtual slice depicts the internal geometry of the rastered wick. The visualization serves to characterize the specific pore structure and internal arrangement of the rastered design, providing essential data on the material's internal porosity that is otherwise difficult to assess.

caption: Scatter plot illustrating the first versus third principal component scores, highlighting the clear separation of the four distinct cases within the principal component space.
summary: Representing the first versus third principal component scores, this plot provides further evidence of the distinctiveness of each case within the principal component space. The clear separation observed confirms that the PCA approach successfully captures unique features of the SAS patterns across the four different microstructural cases.

caption: Schematic illustration of the remelting phenomenon in L-PBFAM, depicting how slower heating and cooling cycles influence Mn entrapment and spatial variation.
summary: This schematic illustrates the remelting phenomenon occurring during the L-PBFAM process. It highlights how regions such as the heat-affected zone undergo slower heating and cooling cycles, similar to traditional heat treatment, which leads to spatial variations in Mn entrapment and contributes to the overall microstructural heterogeneity of the alloy.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the EIS spectra of heat-treated LPBF AlSi10Mg specimens.
summary: The EIS spectra for heat-treated LPBF AlSi10Mg specimens are shown in this Nyquist plot. The analysis reveals a recognizable time constant at low frequencies. Furthermore, the impedance modulus at lower frequencies is approximately one order of magnitude lower than the corresponding value observed for the MP specimens of this alloy.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the Ti/Al interface displaying a sharp Z-contrast transition.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a clear visualization of the Ti/Al interface, highlighting a sharp Z-contrast transition across the boundary. The lack of a diffuse region in the contrast profile confirms the absence of interdiffusion, supporting the conclusion that the interface remains planar and distinct without any significant intermixing layer.

caption: Load–displacement (P-h) curves recorded during nano-indentation testing of the Fe0.6Ni0.7CrAl MPEA surface.
summary: Nano-indentation testing was performed on the Fe0.6Ni0.7CrAl MPEA surface, with three distinct indents recorded to generate the load–displacement (P-h) curves. These curves illustrate the mechanical response of the alloy under localized loading, capturing the relationship between applied force and penetration depth to characterize the material's nanomechanical behavior.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of N-TTCP nanoparticles and PCL/N-TTCP scaffolds, illustrating the characteristic chemical bonding and functional groups present in the individual nanoparticles and the final composite material.
summary: The FTIR spectra of N-TTCP nanoparticles and PCL/N-TTCP scaffolds are presented to characterize the chemical composition. By comparing the spectra, the panel demonstrates the successful incorporation of N-TTCP into the PCL matrix, providing insight into the molecular interactions and functional groups maintained within the 3D-printed composite scaffold.

caption: Atomistic geometry of the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al interface model, featuring Ni atoms in red and Al atoms in blue, with the γ'-Ni3Al phase positioned as the upper layer and the γ-Ni phase as the lower layer.
summary: This atomistic model illustrates the structural configuration of the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al interface. The γ'-Ni3Al phase serves as the upper layer, while the γ-Ni phase forms the lower layer. Ni atoms are represented by red spheres and Al atoms by blue spheres, providing a clear visualization of the interfacial atomic arrangement.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves comparing as-fabricated L-PBF-AM NiTi alloys with ingot-processed counterparts.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry analysis reveals distinct thermal characteristics for additively manufactured NiTi alloys. Compared to ingot-processed samples, the L-PBF-AM specimens exhibit broader transformation peaks and higher transformation temperatures. These results highlight the significant influence of the additive manufacturing process on the phase transformation behavior and shape memory response of NiTi.

caption: Validation cubes printed at varying extrusion multipliers, demonstrating over-extrusion at 0.65, under-extrusion with pore formation at 0.61, and optimal surface quality at 0.63.
summary: Cuboids printed with 100% infill density were used to assess process stability. The results show that an extrusion multiplier of 0.63 yields an optimal surface without pores, whereas 0.65 leads to over-extrusion and 0.61 results in under-extrusion and pore formation at turning points, confirming the stability of the optimized printing parameters.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification performance of the first model across distinct pH level categories.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed view of the classification results for the first model across different pH level classes. The visualization highlights specific misclassifications, which are attributed to the overlapping colour characteristics inherent to these two pH categories, demonstrating the model's performance limitations in distinguishing between these specific classes.

caption: IWP topology unit cell, periodic lattice, and stochastic TPMS realizations.
summary: IWP topology structures are displayed as a unit cell, a 5x5x5 periodic lattice, and two stochastic TPMS realizations. These 30x30x30 mm samples, featuring a 20% relative density, are generated using optimized control points and unit cell dimensions to represent the structural configuration of the IWP-based cellular material.

caption: Averaged UV-Vis absorbance spectra obtained from sequential separation tests, demonstrating the influence of flow rates (125–250 µL/min) and particle concentrations (10^4 p/mL) on immobilization efficiency.
summary: Averaged UV-Vis spectra illustrate the immobilization efficiency of MP-NPs under different flow rates and concentrations. The highest immobilization efficiency was achieved at a concentration of 10^4 p/mL with a flow rate of 250 μL/min. The absorbance peak remained stable at 125 μL/min but decreased significantly at 250 μL/min after four steps.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of sample S2 illustrating the crystallographic orientation relative to the build direction.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for sample S2 displays the orientation of crystallites relative to the build direction. Analysis reveals that the crystallites lack any preferred orientation and exhibit a relatively equiaxed shape, regardless of the specific E* processing parameter used during the LPBF manufacturing of the Kuamet6B2 material.

caption: Equilibrium composition plot for the Bi-Reforming of Methane (BRM) reaction, modeled via ChemCad with an equimolar feed ratio of CH4/CO2/H2O/N2 = 15 mol/h each across the temperature range.
summary: Representing the BRM reaction equilibrium, this plot demonstrates the thermodynamic outcomes of adding water to the feed stream. Comparison with the DRM plot in panel (a) highlights the distinct advantages of the BRM process, revealing how the inclusion of H2O shifts the equilibrium to improve overall reaction performance.

caption: Tabulated physical parameters of the 3D-printed scaffolds, including pore size, filament diameter, and porosity measurements before and after the leaching process.
summary: Table 2 provides quantitative data on the physical aspects of the 3D-printed scaffolds, specifically pore size, filament distance, and filament diameters. The data indicates that PCL and PP20CS50W scaffolds exhibit the lowest and highest diameters, respectively. Furthermore, the table documents porosity changes resulting from the leaching process.

caption: Comparison of simulated and experimental morphology and phase distribution for CuCrZr and 316L tracks fabricated using a laser power of 375 W.
summary: At a laser power of 375 W, this panel displays the resulting morphology and distribution of CuCrZr and 316L. By contrasting simulated data with experimental findings, the image provides insight into how the material phases are organized within the molten pool at this intermediate power level.

caption: TDS-GU hydrogen desorption spectra of 3.5NiCrMoV steel specimens electrochemically charged in 0.1 M Na2SO4 at various potentials, showing desorption peaks at 160 °C and 210 °C.
summary: This TDS-GU spectrum displays hydrogen desorption behavior for 3.5NiCrMoV steel specimens after electrochemical charging. The data reveals distinct peaks at 160 °C and 210 °C. These peaks are marginally influenced by the charging potential, although the 210 °C peak shows a slight decrease at the most negative charging potential applied.

caption: Full-range XRD patterns of Ti–Mo specimens subjected to hot rolling at varying temperatures.
summary: This panel displays the full-range XRD patterns for Ti–Mo specimens processed via hot rolling at different temperatures. These patterns provide a comprehensive overview of the crystalline phases present in the material, serving as the baseline for identifying phase evolution and structural changes induced by the varying thermal and mechanical processing conditions.

caption: Nanoindentation hardness plotted against temperature for the MPES exemplar, utilizing the Tabor approximation to correlate bulk hardness with uniaxial strength.
summary: This plot displays the temperature-dependent nanoindentation hardness of the MPES exemplar. By applying the Tabor approximation, the data relates bulk hardness to uniaxial strength. Experimental results indicate that the material maintains consistent strength across temperatures up to 1073 K, demonstrating high thermal stability for the two AM builds tested.

caption: Optimization parameter contour plot for SS and Hd settings.
summary: This contour plot displays the optimization parameters for the manufacturing process. Specifically, it illustrates the required settings for scan speed (SS) and hatch distance (Hd) to achieve superior mechanical properties. These parameters are critical for refining the final outcomes of the optimization process as determined by Design Expert software.

caption: Defect detection heatmap generated by the CAE model for sample 16A using a 16 × 8 × 16 configuration and 3 × 3 mm patch size.
summary: This panel displays the defect detection results for sample 16A using a CAE model with a 16 × 8 × 16 configuration and 3 × 3 mm patch size. The model demonstrates high consistency in identifying primary defect regions on the sample surface, as confirmed by the comparative analysis with ground truth data.

caption: Diffuse reflection (DR) spectra of Ni-P coatings plotted as a function of wavelength.
summary: This panel presents the diffuse reflection (DR) spectra for Ni-P coatings across different wavelengths. Diffuse reflection is indicative of surfaces that are rougher or contain a higher density of defects. By comparing these results with total reflection, the optical data helps characterize the surface quality and structural integrity of the coatings.

caption: Field-up and field-down isothermal magnetization M(H) curves of bamboo-grained microwires, highlighting the intersection of curves at low fields within the red dashed ellipse.
summary: Isothermal magnetization curves M(H) for bamboo-grained microwires demonstrate negligible magnetic hysteresis. caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PGA synthesized from GAMes with TSA catalysis at 190 °C for 1 day.
summary: This MALDI-TOF mass spectrum displays the molecular weight distribution of poly(glycolic acid) (PGA) synthesized from GAMes using TSA as a catalyst at 190 °C over a 24-hour period. caption: Experimental and predicted indentation load-depth (P-h) curves for the JG4 cladding specimen under maximum indentation loads of 100 mN, 150 mN, and 200 mN.
summary: This panel displays the comparison between experimental and predicted indentation load-depth curves for the JG4 cladding specimen. caption: Voltage and current profiles over time for a DIW-T50/W142 cathode cell during a charge/discharge cycle at a 0.1C rate.
summary: This panel displays the voltage and current response of a DIW-T50/W142 cathode cell during a charge/discharge cycle at 0.1C. caption: Cole-Cole curve for the Fe50 composite, demonstrating the dielectric relaxation characteristics.
summary: This Cole-Cole curve for the Fe50 composite maps the relationship between ε' and ε". The observed semicircle indicates a dielectric relaxation process occurring between 2 and 18 GHz. caption: Experimental setup for room temperature uniaxial tensile testing of the G91/C22 weld joint, utilizing digital image correlation (DIC) to capture surface strain distribution.
summary: Uniaxial tensile testing of the G91/C22 weld joint is performed at room temperature as shown in this setup. caption: Structural representation of the Rotating Square (RS) auxetic unit cell, characterized by a missing rib mechanism.
summary: Rotating Square (RS) structures represent a distinct class of auxetic models often described in literature as utilizing a missing rib mechanism. caption: Crack growth rate plotted against the stress intensity factor range ΔK for IP-TMF and isothermal fatigue testing at a maximum temperature of 750 °C.
summary: This plot displays the crack growth rate versus the stress intensity factor range ΔK for IP-TMF and isothermal fatigue tests conducted at a maximum temperature of 750 °C. The data indicates a clear influence of hold time on crack growth rates when plotted against the full ΔK range.

caption: Schematic representation of the face-centered cubic unit cell for pure aluminum.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic arrangement within the face-centered cubic unit cell of pure aluminum. caption: SVC model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: SVC model performance is evaluated using a confusion matrix. caption: SHAP dependence plot for laser spot size on residual stress predictions along the scan direction σx, highlighting a sharp transition to positive SHAP values at 6 mm.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot illustrates the effect of laser spot size on residual stress predictions along the scan direction σx. A sharp transition to positive SHAP values is observed when the laser diameter is set to 6 mm, with each dot representing a single prediction.

caption: Total energy evolution as a function of current at 300 K, demonstrating a decrease in energy under forward bias conditions.
summary: Micromagnetic simulations at 300 K show the evolution of total energy as a function of current. caption: Fatigue strength assessment under Large Scale Yielding (LSY) conditions, where maximum nominal stress exceeds the 0.2% proof stress, compared against the PSM design scatter band for structural steels.
summary: This panel displays a fatigue strength assessment for structural steels under LSY conditions, defined by maximum nominal stress exceeding the 0.2% proof stress. caption: Absolute irradiance profile of the Monet laser light curing unit, plotted as a function of wavelength in nm.
summary: The Monet laser light curing unit exhibits a specific absolute irradiance profile measured in mW/cm2/nm. caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized PA12, displaying signals consistent with established polyamide chemical structures to verify successful synthesis.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum provides critical evidence for the successful synthesis of the polyamide. The observed signals align with previously reported data for polyamides, confirming the chemical structure of the synthesized PA12 polymer.

caption: Fracture stress plotted against porosity for specimens oriented at θ = 60°.
summary: This plot depicts the fracture stress versus porosity for specimens with an orientation angle of 60°. By comparing these results with experimental data, the figure demonstrates the mechanical behavior of the material, specifically how porosity levels correlate with fracture stress under this particular orientation condition.

caption: Detailed illustration of a single unit cell representing the repeating architectural element of the HHS structure.
summary: This panel displays a single unit cell, which serves as the fundamental building block for the entire HHS structure. caption: Top view illustrating the OversetO reference frame origin positioned at the geometric center of the extrusion nozzle inlet patch.
summary: This top-view schematic displays the OversetO reference frame origin, which is strategically located at the center of the inlet patch. caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the temperature-dependent activities of Ni, Co, Cr, and Al species in the CMSX-4 alloy, derived from KEMS intensity measurements.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the activity of Ni, Co, Cr, and Al in the CMSX-4 alloy as a function of reciprocal temperature. caption: EPMA elemental distribution map showing the spatial concentration of Chromium (Cr) in the aged sample AG1b.
summary: Chromium distribution across the microstructure of the as-deposited sample AG1b is depicted via EPMA mapping after primary aging. summary: This plot displays the 1-D Generalized Stacking Fault Energy (GSFE) curves for the CrMn binary system. caption: Bamboo-inspired gradient structural unit featuring a hierarchical arrangement.
summary: This schematic illustration depicts a bamboo-inspired structural unit characterized by a gradient design. summary: Presented is the nominal Poisson’s ratio evolution for Lat1 N and Lat1 S configurations at a 15% relative density during quasi-static compression. caption: Model summary table providing the statistical metrics for the regression analysis of 3D printing parameter settings.
summary: This model summary table provides the essential statistical metrics derived from the regression analysis of parameter settings on the roughness of 3D printing results. The simulation indicates that the material solidifies predominantly through a ferritic mode, with phase volume fractions plotted as a function of temperature to characterize the solidification path in the absence of additional nitrogen.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern indexed for the [11−2] δ zone axis of sample B deformed at 960 °C and a strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹.
summary: This selected area diffraction pattern represents the δ phase in sample B, deformed at 960 °C and a strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹. The pattern is indexed for the [11−2] δ zone axis, characterizing the crystallographic orientation of the δ phase within the deformed microstructure of the investigated material.

caption: Load-displacement curves and indentation distribution mapping for equiaxed grain structures.
summary: Load-displacement curves and indentation distribution mapping for equiaxed grain structures. These mechanical test results provide insight into the hardness and elastic modulus of the equiaxed grains. The data is included in the summary of tested nano-indentation hardness and calculated elastic modulus results for the various microstructural features analyzed.

caption: Comparison of fatigue prediction models for Inconel 625 samples built in the Z-orientation and subjected to AB-HIP post-processing, evaluated across stress ratios R = 0.1, 0.5, and -1.
