summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of fatigue prediction models for Inconel 625 specimens manufactured via Z-orientation and processed with AB-HIP. The evaluation covers multiple stress ratios, including R = 0.1, 0.5, and -1. Notably, the model predictions for completely reversed stress conditions demonstrate a high correlation, achieving an R-squared value of 0.87.

caption: Mechanical response of 30 wt% Al2O3 composite resin measured via storage modulus during the UV curing process.
summary: Representing the 30 wt% Al2O3 composite resin, this panel illustrates the storage modulus during UV curing. The data confirms that increasing the Al2O3 concentration up to this level enhances the mechanical properties of the cured composite resin, as evidenced by the rising storage modulus values.

caption: Three-dimensional schematic representation of regions A and B, highlighting the undetermined angular misalignments denoted as α and β between the two-layer lattice structure.
summary: This 3D schematic illustrates the structural configuration of regions A and B, specifically focusing on the undetermined angles α and β. By applying the TEM nano-Moiré inversion method, the Moiré region is identified as a superposition of a two-layer lattice structure, providing a theoretical basis for understanding the observed interfacial geometry.

caption: Single-through resistance measurement configuration for a NiFe-SiO2 nanocomposite featuring a 1 nm single layer thickness.
summary: This panel displays the single-through resistance measurement configuration for a NiFe-SiO2 nanocomposite with a 1 nm single layer thickness. Resistance measurements are critical for characterizing the electrical properties of these nanocomposites, and higher resistance values are generally observed as the total structure thickness increases across different oxidation temperature conditions.

caption: Isosurface representation of the octree cell generated using the standard MATLAB isosurface function without convolution filtering.
summary: MATLAB’s built-in isosurface function is applied to the octree cell to address geometric representation issues. This panel demonstrates the surface output obtained without the use of convolution filtering, serving as a comparison point to highlight the limitations of standard isosurface generation in achieving a smooth boundary for the model.

caption: Pole figure of the CuCrZr sample in the XZ plane, illustrating the orientation distribution of the (100) and (111) crystallographic planes.
summary: The pole figure for the XZ section displays the orientation distribution of the (100) and (111) planes. This data confirms the existence of a preferential crystallographic orientation parallel to the building direction, providing quantitative evidence of the texture evolution resulting from the specific processing conditions of the CuCrZr samples.

caption: Cr 2p region spectrum from the GD-OES crater, featuring overlapping Zn L3M23M45 Auger peaks and deconvoluted contributions from zinc hydroxide and metallic zinc.
summary: This spectrum displays the Cr 2p region alongside Zn L3M23M45 Auger peaks within the GD-OES crater. The decomposition analysis identifies four distinct contributions: two attributed to zinc hydroxide (Zn(II) A1 and A2) and two associated with metallic zinc (Zn(m) A1 and A2), providing detailed insight into the surface composition.

caption: Electron density map of YDy powder with 0 at% Dy content, derived from Rietveld refinement of observed and calculated spectra.
summary: This panel displays the electron density map for pure YDy powder, calculated via Fourier series analysis of Rietveld refinement data. The map illustrates local electron concentration variations in units of e-.Å-3, providing a spatial representation of the crystal structure based on the difference between observed and calculated diffraction spectra.

caption: SHAP analysis result for the alloy composition-median radius of precipitates model, highlighting the impact of alloying elements on precipitate size.
summary: This SHAP analysis plot examines the alloy composition-median radius of precipitates model. The results demonstrate that Cr significantly affects the individual γ′-phase size, consistent with experimental conclusions. As Co content increases, the SHapley values for this model decrease, indicating a negative correlation between Co concentration and precipitate radius.

caption: Elemental distribution map of the interface between the base metal and the heat-affected zone, corresponding to the region highlighted by the yellow box in panel c.
summary: EDS mapping was performed on the region comprising both the base metal and the heat-affected zone to visualize the elemental distribution. This map provides insight into the chemical composition across the interface, complementing the microstructural observations of grain size variation noted in the transition from the base metal.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the marked region in (a), confirming a {112}<111> type twin structure and highlighting periodic extra diffraction spots indicated by red arrows.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponds to the twinned martensite observed in WQT-DZ. It confirms a typical {112}<111> twin structure. Notably, the pattern reveals periodic extra diffraction spots, marked by red arrows, which do not belong to the alpha-prime matrix or the twin, observed from both [110] and [311] zone axes.

caption: Incident light distribution simulation for D10 powder slurry under a 10 V/m electric field.
summary: This simulation result shows the incident light distribution for D10 powder slurry under a 10 V/m electric field. By comparing this to the D5 results, the influence of powder characteristics on light distribution under identical electrical field conditions can be evaluated within the context of the presented study.

caption: Face-Centered Cube (FCC) lattice structure unit cell.
summary: The Face-Centered Cube (FCC) lattice structure is shown as one of the three unit cell configurations utilized as TCEs in this study. This schematic representation highlights the atomic positioning within the FCC lattice, providing a clear visual reference for the structural models employed in the experimental and theoretical analysis.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography image of the binary alloy surface.
summary: Atomic force microscopy topography image of the binary alloy surface. This visualization provides a detailed surface characterization of the binary alloy specimen, serving as a baseline for comparing topographical features against the ternary alloy variant presented in the subsequent panels of the figure.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves for Al2O3/CeO2 and Al2O3/CeO2/Al powder mixtures subjected to two successive heating ramps up to 1500 °C.
summary: DSC measurements were conducted on Al2O3/CeO2 and Al2O3/CeO2/Al powder mixtures to investigate thermal behavior during two successive heating cycles up to 1500 °C. These curves, labeled (1) and (2), track the heat flow characteristics of the mixtures, providing experimental evidence of the thermal events occurring during the formation of the reaction products.

caption: Backscattered electron scanning electron microscopy image of the homogenized AlNbTiV alloy displaying an equiaxed grain structure.
summary: The homogenized AlNbTiV alloy exhibits a uniform equiaxed grain structure as observed through SEM-BSE imaging. This microstructure is a result of the homogenization treatment, which effectively transforms the material's morphology compared to the as-cast state, supporting the retention of a single-phase BCC solid solution.

caption: Logic flow of the feedback control system represented as an activity diagram.
summary: This activity diagram illustrates the operational logic of the feedback control loop. It maps the sequential steps and decision-making processes involved in the system's regulation. By visualizing the control flow, the diagram provides a clear representation of how the feedback mechanism functions to maintain system stability and performance.

caption: {111} pole figure corresponding to position 2 within a dynamically recrystallized (DRX) grain, illustrating the orientation change relative to the parent deformed grain.
summary: Representing the orientation of a DRX grain at position 2, this {111} pole figure provides insight into the recrystallization process. It shows how the new grain orientation relates to the distorted twin structure, maintaining a shared <111> direction with the surrounding deformed grains as observed in the pole figure analysis.

caption: Comparison of XRD patterns between Finemet precursor powder and the L-PBF manufactured component, highlighting variations in phase distribution.
summary: This panel presents a comparative XRD analysis of Finemet precursor powder and L-PBF manufactured samples. The patterns reveal distinct variations in phase distribution between the initial powder and the printed component, illustrating the structural changes induced by the laser processing technique during the fabrication of the L-PBF material.

caption: Superimposed high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns collected across the welded joint, spanning from the NiTi base material to the Ti6Al4V base material.
summary: This figure displays superimposed high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns probing the transition zone of a welded joint between NiTi and Ti6Al4V base materials. Analysis of these diffraction data reveals a distinct evolution in peak intensity, which indicates a progressive austenite to martensite phase transformation occurring near the weld centerline.

caption: Linear shrinkage values measured along the Y-orientation for cuboid and gear samples.
summary: Y-orientation linear shrinkage data for the cuboid and gear samples are displayed. The cuboid sample reached a shrinkage value of 20.6% ± 0.2%, while the gear sample showed a value of 18.0% ± 0.8%, indicating the anisotropic nature of the shrinkage response in the BJ3DP316LSS samples after sintering.

caption: Longitudinal strain contour plot for specimen 4 at frame 290, depicting the final observed stage of strain development during the tensile testing procedure.
summary: This final panel shows the longitudinal strain contour plot for specimen 4 at frame 290. Processed via Ncorr software, the visualization captures the advanced state of strain distribution at the end of the observed tensile testing sequence, completing the documentation of the specimen's mechanical deformation behavior.

caption: Three-dimensional visualization of a 60 μm × 60 μm × 46 μm volume reconstructed via Plasma FIB, featuring backscattered electron contrast and 3D-EDX mappings of Fe, Mo, Ni, and Si segregation at cell boundaries.
summary: Three-dimensional reconstruction using Plasma FIB reveals distinct chemical segregation at the cell boundaries of the 316L steel. Backscattered electron imaging highlights white contrast at these boundaries, while 3D-EDX mapping confirms the specific distribution and segregation of Fe, Mo, Ni, and Si elements within the cellular structure.

caption: Generalized stacking fault energy (GSFE) surfaces for pure Ni and Ni-Mo solid solutions, illustrating the influence of Mo concentration on stacking fault energetics along the Burgers vector b0 = a0/6[11-2].
summary: This figure presents the calculated GSFE surfaces for pure Ni and Ni-Mo solid solutions, highlighting the composition-dependent effects of Mo on unstable stacking fault and unstable twin fault energies. These DFT-based simulations provide critical insights into how alloying elements modify the stacking fault energy landscape in fcc nickel-based systems.

caption: CO stripping voltammogram of Pt1−x−yIrxNiy ternary alloy catalyst measured in 0.1 M HClO4 electrolyte.
summary: This panel displays the CO stripping voltammogram for the Pt1−x−yIrxNiy ternary alloy catalyst, evaluated in a 0.1 M HClO4 solution. The measurement serves to investigate the CO poisoning tolerance of the material, providing electrochemical data essential for assessing the catalytic performance and surface activity of the ternary alloy system.

caption: Force-displacement curves for PLA and carbon fiber reinforced PLA (PLA-CF) filaments with a 1.75 mm diameter, demonstrating the ductile behavior induced by crazing in the reinforced composite.
summary: Tensile testing of PLA and PLA-CF filaments reveals distinct mechanical responses. The force-displacement curves demonstrate that the inclusion of carbon fibers in the PLA matrix promotes crazing, which significantly enhances the ductility of the reinforced filament compared to the neat PLA material during the mechanical loading process.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the 1.4462+1Ni steel composition calculated using JMatPro software, illustrating the temperature-dependent phase stability.
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram, generated via JMatPro for the 1.4462+1Ni steel composition, maps phase stability across varying temperatures. As the Ni-concentration increases in this alloy system, the austenite formation region is notably shifted toward higher temperatures, demonstrating the significant influence of nickel content on the thermodynamic phase transformation behavior.

caption: Stress evolution profiles including minimum, mean, and maximum values for isothermal LCF tests conducted at 730 ∘C.
summary: Stress evolution profiles for isothermal LCF tests at 730 ∘C show a decrease in stress amplitudes compared to the 650 ∘C condition. The data confirms that cyclic softening occurs under these loading conditions, and the evolution trend remains consistent across various mechanical strain amplitudes applied during the test.

caption: Kelvin probe force microscopy surface potential map of the binary alloy, highlighting discrete particles as bright regions.
summary: Kelvin probe force microscopy surface potential map of the binary alloy, highlighting discrete particles as bright regions. KPFM scans revealed that although interdendritic networks were not sharply resolved, discrete particles appeared as bright regions in the maps, providing insight into the local surface potential variations across the binary alloy microstructure.

caption: Schematic representation of various light-curing mechanisms and operational approaches utilized in vat photopolymerization technologies, highlighting the integration of light-emitting diodes (LEDs).
summary: This schematic illustrates the diverse light-curing mechanisms and operational strategies inherent to vat photopolymerization technologies. By incorporating light-emitting diodes (LEDs), the figure delineates the distinct technical approaches used to achieve polymerization, providing a comprehensive overview of the fundamental methods employed within this additive manufacturing process for material fabrication.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing the spatial distribution of Sc (red), Si (green), and Fe (blue) atoms in an Fe-rich alloy containing 0.1 wt% Si after 1 hour of ageing at 350 °C.
summary: This APT reconstruction visualizes the atomic distribution of Sc, Si, and Fe within an Fe-rich alloy sample. Following a heat treatment of 1 hour at 350 °C, the 3D map illustrates the specific spatial arrangement of these elements, providing insight into the microstructural evolution of the material under these ageing conditions.

caption: Regression equation table defining the mathematical relationship between the input parameters and the surface roughness response.
summary: The regression equation table explicitly defines the mathematical model derived from the statistical analysis. It quantifies the relationship between the independent 3D printing parameters and the dependent roughness variable, allowing for the prediction of surface quality based on the specific settings identified in the factor information.

caption: Comparison of predicted versus measured bead profiles for height and width using a low-fidelity model, demonstrating improved accuracy after incorporating six data points.
summary: This parity plot compares predicted and measured bead profiles, illustrating the performance of a low-fidelity model. By incorporating six data points, the model significantly improved its predictive accuracy, reducing the MAPE for height predictions to 3.58% and the absolute percentage error for width predictions to 0.87%.

caption: Pyrometric image generated by plotting the maximum emission signal on a 20.20 µm grid, where variations in mean signal intensity qualitatively indicate changes in laser processing parameters.
summary: The pyrometric heatmap illustrates the maximum emission signal recorded for each laser position on a 20.20 µm grid. Changes in laser parameters are qualitatively identified by shifts in the mean signal intensity across different hatch blocks. Signal changes in this map correspond directly to the surface defects observed in the optical image.

caption: Deposition rate as a function of Ni ion concentration, demonstrating the influence of increasing metal ion content while maintaining a constant 1:1 Ni:Fe ratio.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between Ni ion concentration and the resulting deposition rate. By maintaining a constant 1:1 Ni:Fe ratio while increasing the total metal ion content in the bath, the data shows a clear trend where higher concentrations of Ni and Fe ions lead to an increased deposition rate.

caption: Experimental setup for acoustic characterization of MPP printed samples, showing the sample holder and the frontal view of the mounting on the impedance tube.
summary: This panel displays the experimental setup used for acoustic characterization of MPP printed samples. It includes a general view of the impedance tube equipment and a detailed view of the sample holder. The procedure follows the ISO 10534-2 standard, utilizing the SW470 impedance tube and VAL-Lab2 software for measurements.

caption: Phase-specific orientation distributions showing the crystallographic texture of the oxidized surface.
summary: Orientation distribution analysis reveals the crystallographic texture of the different phases within the oxide layer. The data indicates a pronounced orientation difference between adjacent grains, with a significant proportion of grains exhibiting a 60° misorientation angle. This texture information is vital for understanding the structural evolution of the surface during oxidation.

caption: Force–time response of the Diamond TPMS topology subjected to low-speed impact penetration using a 20 mm hemispherical indenter at 220 J energy.
summary: The Diamond TPMS topology exhibits a specific force-time response during low-speed impact penetration testing. Conducted with a 20 mm hemispherical indenter at an impact energy of 220 J, the smoothened data across three repetitions characterizes the mechanical behavior and energy absorption profile of this specific lattice structure under dynamic loading conditions.

caption: Representative optical image of a printed ring structure without black pigment, demonstrating significant overcuring and the methodology used for measuring feature width.
summary: This optical micrograph shows a printed ring with a nominal width of 2.5 mm produced without any black pigment. The image illustrates the extent of overcuring that occurs in the absence of pigment, providing a visual reference for the measurement approach used to assess the in-plane geometric fidelity of the printed samples.

caption: Bode phase angle diagram revealing the presence of a single phase angle peak for all samples during electrochemical impedance spectroscopy testing.
summary: The Bode phase angle diagram shows that all tested samples exhibit a distinct phase angle peak during electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. This characteristic confirms that the electrochemical reaction system for these samples is governed by a single time constant, consistent with the observations made from the corresponding Nyquist plots.

caption: SEM micrograph of the FCCZ sample fracture site after 50% compressive strain, showing strut damage localized at the intersections of curved and vertical struts.
summary: The FCCZ sample fracture site is shown after 50% compressive strain. SEM analysis indicates that fracture occurs at the intersections between curved and vertical struts, as well as along the curved struts themselves. The sample exhibits a ductile fracture mode, evidenced by dimples and significant plastic deformation of the struts.

caption: STEM-HAADF image of a cast alloy eutectic colony displaying bright Al11Ce3 intermetallic phases and dark Al(Mg) matrix regions.
summary: This STEM-HAADF image of a cast alloy eutectic colony highlights the microstructural contrast between the bright Al11Ce3 intermetallic phase and the dark Al(Mg) matrix. The distinct phase distribution provides a clear visualization of the cast alloy's morphology, confirming the presence of these specific intermetallic and matrix components.

caption: Al-rich corner of the Al-Si-Ni ternary phase diagram, illustrating the equilibrium solidification pathways for hypereutectic Al-Si-Ni alloys, with specific composition points a through e corresponding to Al-22Si-xNi (x = 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 wt.%) alloys.
summary: This ternary phase diagram focuses on the Al-rich corner of the Al-Si-Ni system. It maps the equilibrium solidification behavior of hypereutectic alloys. Composition points a through e represent Al-22Si-xNi alloys with nickel contents ranging from 0 to 20 wt.%, providing a framework to analyze their solidification processes.

caption: Representative fluorescence images of ROS staining in L929 cells following various treatments, showing reduced DCF fluorescence in the PPMP@S hydrogel group compared to controls (scale bar: 100 μm).
summary: This panel displays representative fluorescence images of ROS staining in L929 cells after various treatments. The results show that the PPMP@S hydrogel treatment notably reduced DCF fluorescence in the cells, demonstrating the material's effective ability to suppress intracellular ROS levels compared to the control groups.

caption: Room-temperature VSM hysteresis loops for FeCoNiSi x MEA samples measured under an applied magnetic field ranging from -15,000 Oe to 15,000 Oe.
summary: Room-temperature VSM hysteresis loops for FeCoNiSi x MEA samples are presented, illustrating the magnetic response under an applied field ranging from -15,000 Oe to 15,000 Oe. These measurements characterize the fundamental magnetic properties of the four MEAs, providing the necessary data to evaluate their saturation magnetization and coercivity behavior.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern (SADP) obtained from the region encircled in orange, encompassing the parallel interfaces marked by white dashed lines and the β precipitates indicated by red arrows.
summary: The selected area diffraction pattern (SADP) corresponds to the region containing the parallel martensite interfaces and the associated β precipitates. By focusing on the area encircled in orange, this diffraction analysis provides crystallographic information regarding the interface structure and the precipitates identified by the red arrows in the micrograph.

caption: Compositional EDS maps of the NW H sample showing the distribution of elements across the cell boundaries in LP-DED 316L stainless steel blocks.
summary: Compositional EDS maps of the NW H sample reveal the elemental distribution within LP-DED 316L stainless steel blocks. The analysis demonstrates that cell boundaries are depleted in Fe and Ni while being enriched in ferrite stabilizers, specifically Cr, Mo, and Si, confirming the segregation of these elements at the boundaries.

caption: Radar chart comparing mechanical properties across four distinct cases, highlighting variations in stiffness and ultimate failure energy.
summary: This radar chart compares mechanical properties across four cases, revealing distinct stiffness levels for each. During the elastic phase, the LP case demonstrated superior stiffness, approximately 86% greater than the baseline. Regarding ultimate failure energy, interlayer cases OF and LP showed lower capabilities, while the FP case performed similarly to the drilled case.

caption: Evolution of LRO in (Ni,Co)3(Al,Ti) during a single cascade, illustrating the stabilization of order parameters.
summary: Shown is the LRO evolution profile for (Ni,Co)3(Al,Ti) under single cascade conditions. The green dashed line delineates the equilibrium point at 100 K for irradiation disordering and kinetic reordering. Shaded regions represent the standard error from six independent simulations, manifesting a striking concordance in the profile compared to Ni3(Al,Ti).

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrating the electrochemical corrosion response of LPBF-fabricated specimens tested in 3.5 wt% and 0.1 M NaCl solutions.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves are provided to characterize the electrochemical corrosion behavior of LPBF-fabricated specimens. The data illustrates the response of the AZ91D magnesium alloy and TiC/AZ91D composite samples when subjected to testing in both 3.5 wt% and 0.1 M NaCl solutions to compare their corrosion resistance.

caption: Compositional line profile across the grain boundary of an Al2O3–NiAl3 sample, indicating aluminum excess.
summary: This EELS line profile across the Al2O3–NiAl3 grain boundary reveals an aluminum excess at the interface. Acquired under more reducing conditions compared to the Ni3Al sample, the profile demonstrates the sensitivity of the grain boundary composition to the processing environment, as evidenced by the Al-K and O-K edge measurements.

caption: Glass transition temperature (Tg) of cross-linked models derived from specific volume-temperature linear fitting.
summary: Glass transition temperatures (Tg) were determined by linearly fitting specific volume data obtained at different temperatures. The results demonstrate that the Tg of the cross-linked models decreases as the proportion of 'R' resin increases, a trend attributed to the higher concentration of flexible linkers within the cross-linked system.

caption: Atomic model of the perfect Ni3Al crystal supercell structure used as the baseline for DFT calculations.
summary: This panel displays the atomic model of a perfect Ni3Al supercell. It serves as the foundational structure for subsequent DFT calculations, providing a baseline for comparing the effects of Fe doping and stacking faults on the generalized stacking fault energy of the Ni3Al system.

caption: Ternary diagrams illustrating the distribution of stable phases, Young's modulus (Er), hardness (H), and plastic hardness (Hp) for four samples with varying nominal Cr concentrations after slow cooling from 1120 °C.
summary: These ternary diagrams visualize the phase stability and mechanical properties, including Young's modulus, hardness, and plastic hardness, for four distinct samples with varying nominal Cr content. The data points represent individual measurements collected after the samples underwent a slow cooling process from an initial temperature of 1120 °C.

caption: Band contrast map of Region II at the NiTi/AlSi12 interface, highlighting microstructural features.
summary: Representing the microstructural characteristics of Region II, this band contrast map provides a clear view of the interface features. It complements the phase mapping data by offering a structural perspective on the crack behavior and material integrity within this specific segment of the NiTi/AlSi12 interface.

caption: Calculated photon absorbed dose per fluence (D/Φ) for the SIL phantom compared against six ICRP116 Standard Irradiation Geometry (SIG) models using MCNPX simulation.
summary: This panel displays the photon absorbed dose per fluence (D/Φ) calculated via MCNPX simulations. It compares the SIL phantom results against six Standard Irradiation Geometry (SIG) models defined in the ICRP116 report, which represent the fraction of total body absorbed dose deposited specifically within the skin tissue.

caption: Histograms illustrating the distribution of KAM angles across eight deformation temperatures, with an inset showing the percentage of KAM angles exceeding 1°.
summary: The KAM angle distribution for samples deformed at various temperatures is displayed in this histogram. The inset provides a detailed view of the percentage of KAM angles greater than 1° for each of the eight samples, quantifying the localized strain variations observed under different thermal processing conditions during compression.

caption: Residual force difference between the experimental force and the Burgers model predictions during the holding phase, demonstrating the superior accuracy of the four-parameter model.
summary: This plot quantifies the discrepancy between the experimental force and the model predictions during the holding phase. The four-parameter Burgers model demonstrates superior performance compared to the three-parameter version, primarily by effectively capturing the pronounced short-term relaxation observed at the very beginning of the holding phase.

caption: Shear strength comparison of depth-defined porous samples across varying unit cell sizes (2x2x2, 4x4x4, and 6x6x6 mm3) and porosity levels (65%, 82%, and 90%).
summary: This plot illustrates the adhesive shear strength of depth-defined porous samples, evaluating the optimal depth of a surface porous layer across six different depths and three unit cell sizes. The results demonstrate how varying unit cell dimensions and wall thicknesses influence the resulting porosity, which ranges from 65% to 90%.

caption: Structural characterization of silica species via chemical diagrams of Q2, Q3, and Q4 units alongside solid-state 29Si NMR spectra for printed gels and samples heated to 250 °C under air or vacuum.
summary: Chemical structures of Q2, Q3, and Q4 silicon species are shown alongside 29Si NMR spectra. The spectra compare the condensation states of printed gels before and after heating to 250 °C in air or vacuum, revealing that the vacuum process facilitates improved condensation within the silica network.

caption: Raman spectrum of the carbon fibre showing a prominent D-peak at 1331 cm⁻¹ that overlaps with the diamond peak at 1332 cm⁻¹.
summary: The Raman spectrum of the carbon fibre exhibits a strong D-peak centered at approximately 1331 cm⁻¹, which overlaps with the diamond peak at 1332 cm⁻¹. This spectral signature is characteristic of amorphous hydrogenated carbon (a-C:H), confirming the chemical composition and bonding state of the fibre microstructure.

caption: Comparison of surface roughness (Ra) measurements and total cycle times for hybrid manufacturing strategies involving machining engagement every 20, 10, and 5 layers.
summary: This table presents a comparative analysis of three distinct hybrid manufacturing strategies, categorized by their machining engagement frequency of 20, 10, and 5 layers. The data highlights the resulting surface roughness (Ra) values and total cycle times, providing a quantitative assessment of how varying the machining interval influences manufacturing efficiency and surface quality.

caption: Strain tensor mapping for the LPBF BMG specimen at a high stress level, demonstrating the structural deformation captured by HE-XRD.
summary: Visualizing the strain tensor for the LPBF BMG specimen at a high stress level, this panel utilizes HE-XRD data collected at 2.4 μm intervals. These results are essential for estimating the Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio, providing a comprehensive view of the LPBF material's performance under significant mechanical stress.

caption: Total and projected densities of states for the Mn2FeSn alloy in the Ni3Sn-type crystal structure.
summary: This plot illustrates the electronic structure of the Mn2FeSn alloy, specifically presenting the total density of states (TDOS) alongside the projected density of states (PDOS) for individual atomic constituents. These calculations characterize the electronic distribution within the Ni3Sn-type crystal lattice, providing essential insights into the material's electronic properties.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing pure PLA and GO/PLA filters to determine GO content.
summary: The TGA results provide a quantitative assessment of the GO content within the composite filter. By comparing the thermal degradation profiles of the pure PLA filter and the GO/PLA filter, the analysis indicates a specific GO loading of 2.37 wt%, confirming the successful incorporation of GO into the material.

caption: Nano-hardness variation with applied load for TaN/CrN/ZrN coatings deposited at a substrate temperature of 250 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the nano-hardness response of TaN/CrN/ZrN coatings deposited at 250 °C as a function of the applied load. The data provides insight into the mechanical performance of the functionally graded coating system under varying indentation loads, serving as a baseline for comparison with higher deposition temperatures.

caption: Temperature-dependent solute diffusion coefficients for Re, W, and Ta in a Ni matrix, plotted to illustrate kinetic behavior.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the solute diffusion coefficients for Re, W, and Ta within a Ni matrix as a function of temperature. The data points demonstrate consistent kinetic trends that align with both experimental measurements and simulated values previously reported in the literature, confirming the validity of the presented diffusion parameters.

caption: Fatigue behavior of NiTi strips under varying loading conditions, illustrating transformation patterns with active zones shaded and fatigue failure points marked by arrows.
summary: This panel displays the fatigue behavior of NiTi shape memory alloy strips under different loading conditions. It highlights inhomogeneous deformation characterized by specific transformation patterns and active zones. Fatigue failure points are explicitly indicated, demonstrating preferential failure within these zones as investigated in prior work by Zheng et al.

caption: Sobol sensitivity analysis indices for the INV36-MK500 CGA transition, highlighting the relative contributions of individual elements to property variability.
summary: This Sobol sensitivity analysis illustrates the influence of various elements on the INV36-MK500 CGA transition. The indices demonstrate that iron and aluminum serve as the primary contributors to the observed variability in the material system, providing critical insights into the factors governing the transition behavior of these complex alloys.

caption: Three-dimensional model representation of the optimized cantilever design.
summary: A 3D model of the optimized cantilever is shown, representing the final geometry generated through the optimization process. This model serves as the primary input for the subsequent tool path generation and slicing procedures required to manufacture the component using the identified printing surfaces.

caption: Load-displacement curve measured during nanoindentation of the Cr-rich Ni solid solution phase.
summary: This load-displacement curve characterizes the mechanical response of the Cr-rich Ni solid solution phase during nanoindentation. These tests were conducted to verify the strengthening mechanism of the joints by the introduction of a Mo-Ni skeleton, providing insight into the deformation behavior of this specific phase.

caption: F-actin/DAPI staining images illustrating the morphology and growth status of MFCs on scaffolds after 3 days.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy using Actin-Tracker Green-488 and DAPI staining was employed to observe the growth status and morphological appearance of MFCs on the scaffolds. The assay provides visual evidence of cell morphology and distribution, confirming the successful attachment and growth of cells on the scaffold surfaces after 3 days.

caption: Cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at a C/10 rate.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical performance of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at a C/10 rate. It plots cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential as functions of lithium composition. The cell exhibits minimal overpotential and low hysteresis, indicating efficient electrochemical behavior during the delithiation process.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for MoldJet 316L samples extracted from top, middle, and bottom build heights, tested in PBS at ambient temperature.
summary: Representative potentiodynamic polarization curves demonstrate the passivation behavior of MoldJet 316L samples. By comparing specimens from different build heights—top, middle, and bottom—the plot evaluates the consistency of electrochemical corrosion resistance across the manufactured part, confirming the material's ability to form a stable passive layer in a saline environment.

caption: Tafel curve representing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the material under static conditions.
summary: This panel displays the Tafel curve for the material under static conditions. The plot characterizes the electrochemical corrosion behavior, providing a baseline for comparison with fretting scenarios. It illustrates the passive film formation and corrosion kinetics in the absence of mechanical wear or surface disruption during the electrochemical testing process.

caption: Distribution of tensile sample thickness across various print angles represented as a boxplot.
summary: This boxplot illustrates the thickness distribution of tensile specimens fabricated at different print angles. The visualization provides a statistical overview of the dimensional consistency of the samples, highlighting the range and median thickness values observed across the entire experimental set of print orientations used in the study.

caption: Contour plot displaying the distribution of strains in the second principal direction (ε2) for specimen TS-T2 at 100 kN and ultimate force.
summary: Visualizing the second principal strain ε2, this contour plot provides insight into the strain state of specimen TS-T2 under tensile loading. The map compares the strain distribution at 100 kN and the ultimate force of 277 kN, confirming the mechanical behavior observed via the digital image correlation system.

caption: Gas chromatography analysis of the gaseous products generated during the decomposition of N2H4·H2O over a Ni91Ir9/CeO2 catalyst.
summary: Gas chromatography analysis of the gaseous mixture produced during the decomposition of N2H4·H2O over a Ni91Ir9/CeO2 catalyst confirms the reaction products. This catalytic process achieves complete decomposition of N2H4·H2O into H2 in the presence of 0.5 M NaOH at 50 °C, demonstrating an average reaction rate of 97 h−1.

caption: Tabulated list of candidate ferritic steels, austenitic steels, and Ni-base alloys designated for pipes and tubes within the Chinese A-USC project, including the G115 martensitic 9Cr steel.
summary: This table presents the candidate materials for the A-USC project in China, specifically for pipe and tube applications. It categorizes ferritic steels, austenitic steels, and Ni-base alloys. Notably, it includes G115, a martensitic 9Cr steel developed in China for high-temperature service at 650°C or below.

caption: Full-range X-ray diffraction spectra of the gradient alloy spanning 20–100° 2θ.
summary: This panel displays the full-range X-ray diffraction spectra of the gradient alloy, covering the 20–100° 2θ range. These diffraction patterns provide a comprehensive overview of the phase composition evolution across the gradient alloy, facilitating a comparative assessment of the terminal regions, specifically samples G1 and G5.

caption: Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) lattice design representing a conventional structural configuration.
summary: The Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) lattice is a standard cubic design. While useful, TPMS structures offer significant advantages over such cubic lattice designs due to their more complex internal architectures. This comparison highlights the structural differences between traditional lattices and the more advanced, curvature-based TPMS geometries presented in the study.

caption: Binary Cu–Sn phase diagram used to predict the formation and equilibrium state of the Sn-rich precipitates observed within the α-Cu matrix.
summary: The binary Cu-Sn phase diagram serves as the thermodynamic reference for the Sn-rich precipitates found in the α-Cu matrix. This equilibrium diagram predicts the phase stability and composition of the precipitates, supporting the experimental observations of the Sn-rich features identified during the high-magnification TEM analysis of the copper matrix.

caption: Long-term stability comparison of propane-fueled SOFCs with and without the R-ZNTP catalyst layer, tested at 750 °C and a constant current density of 0.3 A/cm² over 40 hours.
summary: This long-term stability test compares the performance of propane-fueled SOFCs with and without an R-ZNTP catalyst layer. Conducted at 750 °C and 0.3 A/cm² for 40 hours, the data evaluates the durability of the cell and the effectiveness of the R-ZNTP layer in maintaining consistent electrochemical performance over time.

caption: Predicted 1st cycle cold crystallization temperature (Tcc) surface plot as a function of layer height and print head speed.
summary: The surface plot for the 1st cycle cold crystallization temperature indicates a local minimum at 0.12 mm layer height and 20 mm/s printing speed, with a maximum at 0.28 mm and 40 mm/s. Print head speed was selected as a secondary axis due to its significant impact on the model.

caption: Atomic model of a clean-doped Al–Mg–Si alloy, serving as a reference for atomic layer spacing.
summary: This panel shows the atomic model of a clean-doped Al–Mg–Si alloy. It acts as a baseline or control structure for the study, enabling the quantification of how various dopants and co-dopants modify the atomic layer spacing relative to the undoped or clean-doped state of the alloy.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the natural logarithm of the coarsening rate KT as a function of the reciprocal of the absolute aging temperature.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the natural logarithm of the γ′ coarsening rate KT against the reciprocal of the aging temperature. The linear slope derived from this relationship allows for the calculation of the diffusion activation energy, providing critical insight into the temperature dependence of the precipitate coarsening process in the alloys.

caption: Calculated potential-pO2- diagram for Chromium in LiCl-KCl at 450 °C, assuming an activity of 10^-6 for CrClx, with the TiCl2 stability domain overlaid in grey.
summary: This diagram illustrates the potential-pO2- stability domain for Chromium in LiCl-KCl at 450 °C. The presence of TiCl2 reduces the electroactive range, placing Cr partially within its immunity domain. This stability region is critical for understanding the oxidation limits of Cr in the molten salt environment.

caption: Representative dilatometry curve showing dilatation as a function of temperature at a cooling rate of 100 C/s, with critical transformation temperatures marked 1–6.
summary: This dilatometry curve represents the thermal response at a 100 C/s cooling rate. The plot highlights critical transformation temperatures 1–6, determined by slope variations. Observations at this rate indicate consistent transformation behavior, contributing to the broader analysis of how cooling rates influence the martensitic start temperature and overall phase evolution.

caption: Four snapshots of the 316L-CuCr1Zr LPBF fusion process, displaying the material interface and solidified tracks across two distinct time sequences for each layer.
summary: This figure presents four snapshots of the 316L-CuCr1Zr LPBF fusion process, illustrating the material interface and the formation of solidified tracks. These snapshots, captured at two specific time sequences for each layer, provide a detailed visualization of the fusion dynamics and structural evolution during the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Microstructure of PBF-LB/M processed virgin powder showing porous morphology with partially sintered particles.
summary: This SEM micrograph displays the microstructure of PBF-LB/M processed virgin powder. The image reveals a porous microstructure characterized by only partially sintered powder particles. This result highlights the insufficient consolidation achieved when using virgin powder as the feedstock material under the specified process parameters.

caption: Residual image derived from the uncorrected projection, revealing a prominent whitish halo artifact in the central region.
summary: The residual image for the uncorrected projection exhibits a distinct whitish halo in the central part, indicating significant scatter interference. Additionally, the image captures the general shape of the scanned sample, which arises from minor inaccuracies in the mesh estimation process during the reconstruction analysis.

caption: Boxplots showing the distribution of defect roundness for each location after the build, accompanied by individual data points.
summary: These boxplots represent the distribution of defect roundness for each coupon location after the build process. Including all individual data points next to the boxplots allows for a detailed assessment of defect shape consistency across the different locations of the build plate following the completion of the build.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectra comparing PB and PB@QUE, highlighting the disappearance of the characteristic QUE peak at 378 nm.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectra demonstrate the successful loading of QUE onto PB. The characteristic absorption peak of QUE at 378 nm is absent in the PB@QUE spectrum, indicating that QUE was effectively incorporated into the PB structure through specific molecular interactions between the two components.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph and corresponding STEM-EDS elemental distribution maps of the LPBF sample cross-section, highlighting the distribution of elements within the cellular structure.
summary: The HAADF-STEM micrograph and STEM-EDS elemental maps of the LPBF sample cross-section illustrate the internal microstructure. The imaging confirms the presence of round Mn-based oxide nanoparticles within the cross-sectional view. These maps provide a detailed visualization of the elemental distribution, supporting the characterization of the cellular solidification structure.

caption: H’’-R TPMS unit cell geometry with n = 1, displaying the minimal surface faces in contrasting colors and the fundamental patch boundaries.
summary: This H’’-R TPMS unit cell model, with n = 1, illustrates the minimal surface faces and patch boundaries. It is one of several geometries contained within a rectangular prism, providing the necessary framework for calculating the elastic stiffness tensor under periodic boundary conditions in the study.

caption: Coefficient of friction (CoF) profile for the SS316L-SS309 bimetallic WAAM sample during tribological testing.
summary: The CoF profile for the SS316L-SS309 bimetallic WAAM sample illustrates the frictional behavior during sliding contact. Initially, the CoF rises from zero due to asperity interlocking and junction rupture during the running-in period. Subsequently, the transition from static to kinetic friction causes a sudden increase in the measured CoF value.

caption: Ashby map of energy absorption per unit volume versus density for dual-faced structured fabrics, foams, and lattice materials.
summary: Energy absorption capacity of the designed dual-faced structured fabrics is evaluated against various foams, lattice materials, and other structured fabrics. A scaling law, represented by a dotted line, describes the relationship between energy absorption and density, illustrating the competitive energy-absorbing performance of the dual-faced design.

caption: Mn-cluster arrangement on planar objects aligned with the [1 1 1] (red) and [1 -1 1] (blue) crystallographic directions.
summary: Mn-clusters are shown localized on specific planar features within the specimen. These planes correspond to the <1 1 1> dislocation loops, as confirmed by comparative calculations between the field desorption map and the reconstructed image. The clusters are color-coded to highlight their alignment along distinct crystallographic directions.

caption: Microhardness values of composite coatings plotted as a function of varying current densities and Si3N4 particle loadings after a 70-minute deposition process.
summary: This figure displays the microhardness values of composite coatings synthesized under different current densities and Si3N4 loadings for a duration of 70 minutes. The data illustrates the mechanical performance of the coatings, providing a clear comparison of how these specific processing parameters influence the resulting hardness of the composite material.

caption: Pseudo-binary phase diagram calculated using the TTNI8 database, illustrating the relationship between Nb concentration and liquidus temperature, highlighting the promotion of Laves phase formation.
summary: This pseudo-binary phase diagram, generated via the TTNI8 thermodynamic database, demonstrates how increasing the Nb fraction effectively lowers the liquidus temperature. Furthermore, the diagram illustrates that higher Nb concentrations promote the formation of Laves phases during the cooling process, providing critical insights into the solidification behavior of the alloy system.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mappings of aggregated corrosion products, highlighting enrichment in oxygen, phosphorus, and chlorine, with localized calcium around the deposits.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mappings of the aggregated corrosion products are presented. The analysis indicates significant enrichment in oxygen, phosphorus, and chlorine within these deposits. Furthermore, minor amounts of calcium are observed to be localized specifically around the aggregates, providing insight into the chemical composition of the surface corrosion layer.

caption: Minimum creep rate (MCR) versus stress for notched DD6 superalloy specimens on a logarithmic scale.
summary: This panel illustrates the minimum creep rate against stress for notched DD6 superalloy specimens on a double logarithmic scale. Logarithmic linear fitting curves are provided to represent the trend of the MCR data, summarizing the creep performance of the notched specimens under the tested stress conditions.

caption: Current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics of the PMMA/PDMS material, demonstrating the highest performance improvement achieved with the addition of a double-layer anti-reflective coating (DL-ARC) at a 150 nm layer thickness.
summary: The J-V characteristics of the optimized PMMA/PDMS material demonstrate significant performance enhancements following the integration of a DL-ARC. Specifically, the device achieves a short-circuit current density of 29.1 mA/cm2, an open-circuit voltage of 1.19 V, and a fill factor of 87.1% at a 150 nm layer thickness.

caption: Statistical distribution of subgrain sizes observed under different L-PBF scan strategies.
summary: Subgrain size distributions are illustrated using box plots for various scan strategies. The results indicate that subgrain sizes remain consistent across the different processing conditions, with no significant variation observed. These findings suggest that subgrain size plays a limited role in governing the corrosion resistance of the material.

caption: EDS line scan profile across the coating cross-section processed at a TIG current of 90 A, showing a composition of approximately 9 at% Al, 10 at% Cr, 10 at% Co, 11 at% Ni, and 60 at% Fe.
summary: EDS line scan analysis of the coating cross-section produced at 90 A reveals a chemical composition of 9 at% Al, 10 at% Cr, 10 at% Co, 11 at% Ni, and 60 at% Fe. This high iron content suggests the layer does not qualify as a high entropy alloy under these specific processing conditions.

caption: UV–vis to NIR wavelength range absorptance spectra comparing pure Al2O3 samples and high-resolution CuO/Al2O3 ceramic composite 3D structures.
summary: This plot displays the measured absorptance of pure Al2O3 and CuO/Al2O3 ceramic composite 3D structures within the 0.25–20 μm wavelength range. Specifically, panel (a) focuses on the UV–vis to near-infrared region, illustrating the optical performance differences between the pure ceramic and the composite material structures.

caption: Simulated microstructure of NiTi in the YZ-plane (x = 560 μm) for the upper region (2200 μm ≤ z ≤ 3000 μm), colored by IPF relative to the Z-axis.
summary: Simulated microstructure of NiTi in the YZ-plane is shown for the upper region. Stripe-like grains with globally unfavorable orientations, including yellow, purple, and green, propagate along the build direction in the grain matrix. These grains extend over a few layers, illustrating the simulated grain growth behavior in the YZ-plane.

caption: 3D wear track topography of the as-built (AB) sample subjected to a 15 N load.
summary: Displaying the wear track topography of an as-built sample under a 15 N load, this 3D image captures the most severe wear state for the AB condition. The profile reveals the extent of surface degradation, facilitating an analysis of how higher loads impact the wear resistance of the material.

caption: Surface zone temperature profile visualized at a cutting speed of 100 m/min.
summary: Representing the thermal state of the surface zone at 100 m/min, this heatmap shows the temperature distribution during machining. Higher cutting speeds influence the thermal field, which may reach the material's softening point and counteract strain hardening. This panel highlights the thermal evolution as the cutting speed is doubled.

caption: Current–potential HER profiles for AlNi (50 wt.% Ni) alloy particles subjected to high-intensity ultrasound treatment in various media, including ethanol, water, and ethanol–water mixtures.
summary: This panel displays the HER current–potential profiles for AlNi alloy particles modified by high-intensity ultrasound in different sonication media. Observations indicate that using a solution containing as little as 10 vol.% water and 90 vol.% ethanol during the sonication process drastically inhibits the hydrogen evolution reaction performance of the particles.

caption: Thermo-magnetization (M-T) curves of Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires subjected to 1k, 5k, and 10k mechanical training cycles, showing the evolution of magnetic properties under 0.05 T or 0.3 T fields.
summary: Mechanical training cycles of 1k, 5k, and 10k significantly influence the thermo-magnetization behavior of the Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires. The curves reveal the Hopkinson effect via sharp peaks near the Curie temperature, demonstrating how repeated mechanical loading alters the magnetic response during the martensitic and ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic austenite phase transformations.

caption: Schematic representation of the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture utilized for the classification of experimental data.
summary: This panel illustrates the structural framework of the Vision Transformer model applied to the classification task. It serves as the foundational architecture for processing the input data, enabling the subsequent training and evaluation steps described in the following panels of the figure.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay data and fitting curve for TPU/2S composite, evaluated at 490 nm emission wavelength.
summary: The fluorescence lifetime decay data and fitting curve for the TPU/2S composite are shown at an emission wavelength of 490 nm. This measurement provides insight into the material's luminescence kinetics at room temperature, contributing to the broader analysis of average lifespans for varying SAOED concentrations in TPU composites.

caption: Detailed view of the negative thermal expansion region observed in LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy within the temperature range of −50 to 50 °C.
summary: Focusing on the low-temperature regime, this panel highlights the intriguing negative thermal expansion phenomena occurring between −50 and 50 °C for the LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 alloy. This specific region demonstrates anomalous thermal behavior, providing essential data for understanding the material's expansion characteristics under cold thermal load variations.

caption: Three-dimensional topographical reconstruction of the machined surface, highlighting surface texture variations resulting from dry, MQL, and dual-MQL cutting conditions at 150 m/min and 0.2 mm/rev.
summary: Representing the 3D machined surface, this panel visualizes the topographical characteristics of the workpiece under dry, MQL, and dual-MQL conditions. By capturing the surface texture at 150 m/min and 0.2 mm/rev, this reconstruction demonstrates the enhanced precision and superior surface finishes achieved through the novel manufacturing approach.

caption: GD-OES depth profile of A59 alloy illustrating elemental distribution following polarization at 700 mV vs Ag/AgCl, characterized by a layered oxide film where Mo is enriched at the surface and Cr serves as the main constituent.
summary: This GD-OES profile for A59 alloy after 700 mV polarization demonstrates a layered passive film structure. Similar to A625, the results reveal Mo enrichment at the outermost surface, while Cr is located beneath this layer and acts as the major component of the passive film formed in the passive range.

caption: Local mean curvature H S ( p ) distribution mapped onto the surface of a single Reuleaux tetrahedron grain boundary R i , 0 at t = 0, with red lines highlighting points at a distance of 4 from triple junctions.
summary: This panel displays the local mean curvature H S ( p ) for points on a specific grain boundary of a Reuleaux tetrahedron at t = 0. The visualization highlights the spatial distribution of curvature, with red lines specifically marking grain boundary points located at a distance of 4 from the triple junctions.

caption: Lateral perspective comparison of parison geometry dimensions measured using constant die gap opening versus the programmed parison technique.
summary: Lateral view measurements provide a comparative analysis of the parison geometry obtained through constant die gap opening and programmed parison techniques. The data highlights subtle differences in the outer surface shape, confirming that the manufacturing method directly impacts the dimensional consistency and final profile of the parison.

caption: Nyquist plot representing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy response of HEA and LA-HEA coatings after 1 hour of immersion.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy response of HEA and LA-HEA coatings after 1 hour of immersion. As indicated by the experimental data, all samples exhibited Nyquist curves with similar shapes, reflecting the corrosion resistance characteristics of the coatings during the initial stage of the immersion test.

caption: Logarithmic current-voltage characteristics of a printed t-ZnO sensor measured between -10 V and +10 V, comparing dark conditions (black) with UV-irradiated conditions (purple).
summary: Logarithmic current-voltage curves demonstrate the electrical response of printed t-ZnO sensors under dark and UV-illuminated conditions. Measurements taken from -10 V to +10 V reveal that while forward and reverse bias characteristics remain nearly symmetrical, UV irradiation induces a significant increase in current response by over two orders of magnitude.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni-Cr-Mo system at 873 K, showing the final phase equilibrium state at the lowest temperature investigated.
summary: Representing the isothermal section at 873 K, this diagram illustrates the phase equilibrium state of the Ni-Cr-Mo system at the lowest temperature analyzed in the study. It serves as the final point in the reaction pathway sequence, providing insight into the stable phases present at this thermal condition.

caption: Raman spectrum of 85% porous carboHIPEs, providing data on the graphitic structure of the material.
summary: Presented here is the Raman spectrum for 85% porous carboHIPEs. This measurement is part of a broader investigation into the degree of graphitization across various porous carboHIPE samples. The spectrum helps characterize the carbon structure, contributing to the comparative analysis of graphitic quality in materials with different porosity percentages.

caption: Polarization curves normalized by the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) to compare intrinsic catalytic activity.
summary: Polarization curves normalized by the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) are presented to isolate the intrinsic catalytic activity of the materials. This normalization accounts for differences in surface area, enabling a more accurate comparison of the catalytic performance per active site among the various NiCo@NC bimetallic alloy nanoparticles.

caption: Loading cycle evolution for material nodes A1 and A2 during the initial cutting stage.
summary: This plot illustrates the loading cycle behavior of material points A1 and A2 during the first cut. The data provides a baseline for understanding the initial mechanical response of these specific nodes before subsequent processing stages influence the final residual stress distribution within the material.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the polarization curves in 1 M KOH, demonstrating the reaction kinetics of the different Ru-Ni nanoarray catalysts.
summary: Tafel plots for the Ru3Ni3NAs, Ru3Ni2NAs, and Ru3Ni1NAs in 1 M KOH are shown here to evaluate HER kinetics. The calculated Tafel slopes for these materials are 26.9, 29.9, and 30.5 mV dec-1, respectively, indicating efficient charge transfer and favorable reaction mechanisms for the Ru-Ni nanoarray catalysts during the hydrogen evolution process.

caption: Front and top views of the overall G2-GLS-25% model reconstructed from μCT data compared against the original CAD design.
summary: This panel displays a cloud diagram comparing the μCT-reconstructed model of G2-GLS-25% with its CAD design. The visualization provides front and top views of the overall structure, demonstrating that the binder jetting (BJ) fabrication process achieves high precision in reproducing the intended design geometry.

caption: EDS elemental analysis of Zn@dTNT, demonstrating the presence and distribution of constituent elements.
summary: EDS elemental analysis of the Zn@dTNT composite confirms the presence of zinc within the structure. This spectroscopic technique provides critical information regarding the elemental composition, supporting the successful deposition of zinc oxide particles onto the dTNT substrate as part of the material characterization process.

caption: Selected area diffraction patterns acquired along the [110] zone axis, confirming the presence of a single FCC γ-phase with Fm3m space group symmetry across the transition region.
summary: Selected area diffraction patterns acquired along the [110] zone axis confirm the presence of a single FCC γ-phase with Fm3m space group symmetry across the transition region. These patterns provide evidence of the crystal structure consistency throughout the WAAM NiMoCr alloy cladded 316 L stainless steel interface.

caption: Representative load-displacement curve obtained from the nanoindentation of an isotropic material using a Berkovich indenter.
summary: This panel displays a typical load-displacement curve generated during the nanoindentation of an isotropic material with a Berkovich indenter. The curve illustrates the mechanical response of the specimen, serving as the foundational data for extracting characteristic material parameters during the indentation process as described in the study.

caption: Profilometer images of laser treated nickel aluminide alloy A6, detailing the scratch track profile and surface topography under a 15 N load.
summary: Profilometry analysis of nickel aluminide alloy A6 provides a detailed view of the scratch track profile and surface topography after laser treatment. The 3D and cross-sectional images characterize the material's response to a 15 N load, serving as a critical assessment of the surface modification effectiveness.

caption: Comparison of creep stress-time curves at a specific point, evaluating the impact of temperature field optimization on calculation accuracy.
summary: This plot compares creep stress-time curves at the same point in both the original and optimized temperature fields. The analysis verifies that the optimization measures do not significantly affect the accuracy of creep calculations around the holes, confirming the validity of the adjusted temperature field approach.

caption: Heat map illustrating the evolution of precipitate volume fraction over time for the low Fe diffusion couple during in-situ SAXS ageing at 350 °C.
summary: This heatmap displays the temporal evolution of the precipitate volume fraction for the low Fe diffusion couple. Measured via in-situ SAXS at 350 °C, the data provides a quantitative visualization of phase transformation kinetics, assuming the specific precipitate contrast parameters defined in Table C.1 for the low Fe composition.

caption: NMR amplitude signal decay curves for fresh, dried (180 min at 65 °C), and fried (30 s at 210 °C) samples.
summary: Panel A displays NMR amplitude signal decay curves for fresh, dried, and fried samples. These curves characterize water mobility, which influences material properties and moisture diffusion. The fried samples exhibit a decay curve similar to the powder sample, indicating that the frying process effectively drives out moisture and induces oil penetration.

caption: Cooling dilatometry curve for specimen S5, showing the tangent-intersection method used to define the martensite-start temperature of 331 °C.
summary: Specimen S5 exhibits a martensite-start temperature of 331 °C, identified through the tangent-intersection method applied to the cooling dilatometry curve. This thermal analysis confirms the transformation onset following the specified heat treatment, contributing to the overall assessment of how different alloy compositions influence the martensite-start temperature in the studied materials.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting the irregular-shaped twin structure identified in panel (e).
summary: This dark-field TEM image specifically highlights the irregular-shaped twin structure previously observed in the bright-field micrograph. By isolating the diffraction contrast of the twin, this visualization confirms its morphology and spatial extent beneath the fracture facet of the TD-DF specimen.

caption: Inverse pole figure map along the Y-direction showing intergranular austenite grains in the HT200-700 condition.
summary: This EBSD IPF map displays intergranular austenite grains in the HT200-700 condition, projected along the Y-direction. These grains are characterized by their nucleation and growth along prior ferrite-ferrite boundaries. Intergranular austenite represents the most prevalent transformation product among all observed austenite types in the studied material conditions.

caption: Impedance modulus and phase angle distributions for the Ti-based coatings and 2Cr13 substrate.
summary: The impedance modulus (|Z|) and phase angle distributions of the specimens are shown in Fig. 11 c. These Bode plots provide a frequency-dependent analysis of the electrochemical system, revealing the capacitive behavior and resistance characteristics of the passive films formed on the Ti-containing coatings compared to the 2Cr13 substrate.

caption: Scatter diagram of the Zener-Hollomon parameter Z versus the hyperbolic sine of stress.
summary: Panel (e) displays the scatter diagram relating the Zener-Hollomon parameter Z to the hyperbolic sine of the stress. This plot effectively consolidates the effects of strain rate and temperature into a single parameter, providing a comprehensive view of the material's flow stress behavior across the tested experimental range.

caption: Normalized mixture concentration pattern for Case 2, showing the resulting solute segregation profile.
summary: Case 2 presents the normalized mixture concentration pattern after solidification, generated via CAFE simulation. The segregation pattern observed here is similar to those found in other cases. This result provides insight into the solute distribution characteristics under the specific equivalent solutal expansion coefficient defined for this particular simulation case.

caption: Tafel slope comparison for Ni and Ni-alloy nanowire electrodes, including pure Ni (black), Ni-Co (red), Ni-Zn (green), and Ni-W (blue) variants.
summary: This Tafel plot illustrates the electrochemical performance of various Ni-based nanowire electrodes. By comparing the slopes for pure Ni, Ni-Co, Ni-Zn, and Ni-W, the figure highlights the influence of alloying elements on the electrode kinetics. These results represent the optimum Tafel slope values obtained during the electrochemical characterization of the nanowire materials.

caption: Isothermal calorimetry heat flow curves for NS-incorporated Portland cement pastes showing hydration kinetics.
summary: Isothermal calorimetry analysis of NS-incorporated Portland cement pastes reveals that higher NS concentrations promote earlier C-S-H gel formation. The first hydration peak is observed between 5 and 8 hours, confirming that NS accelerates the hydration process and facilitates the rapid development of cementitious products.

caption: Absorption cross-sections of SO2, H2O, and O2 plotted against wavelength from 240 to 325 nm.
summary: This panel displays the absorption cross-sections for SO2, H2O, and O2 within the 240 to 325 nm wavelength range. Data is derived from the MPI-Mainz database, with concentrations scaled by factors of 300 for H2O and 210,000 for O2 to facilitate comparative analysis of spectral features.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram depicting distinct solid–solid phase transformation pathways for the initial layer versus subsequent layers during laser deposition.
summary: This CCT diagram outlines the phase transformation pathways in the Ti–Al–V–Cu quaternary system. It specifically illustrates how the two-phase eutectoid reaction β→α+Ti 2 Cu occurs at higher Cu concentrations. The diagram differentiates the transformation kinetics between the first deposited layer and the successive layers during the laser deposition process.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the structural characteristics of Ni3Al-HT, Ni3Al-HTO, Ni3Al-PM, and Ni3Al-IC catalysts.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for four distinct nickel-aluminum catalyst samples: Ni3Al-HT, Ni3Al-HTO, Ni3Al-PM, and Ni3Al-IC. These patterns serve to illustrate the crystalline structure and phase composition of the as-synthesized and calcined materials, providing a comparative overview of the structural differences between these specific catalyst synthesis methods.

caption: Storage and loss moduli for base and bioactive PLGA formulations, illustrating an upward shift in viscoelastic response.
summary: Moduli for both bioactive PLGA formulations exhibit an upward shift compared to the base material. This observed increase suggests a significant change in the viscoelasticity of the polymer matrix resulting from the incorporation of the bioadditive, indicating enhanced mechanical stiffness and energy storage capacity within the bioactive PLGA composite system.

caption: Overview of the EOS M290 processing chamber, highlighting the shielding gas nozzle configurations.
summary: This photograph displays the internal processing chamber of the EOS M290 system. It features the shielding gas delivery system, including a standard nozzle with multiple holes and a modified slit nozzle design. Additionally, an upper-front square-like nozzle is visible, which functions to suppress powder soaring and fume accumulation.

caption: Variance explanation of principal components for superalloy microstructures exhibiting cubic gamma-prime morphology.
summary: This plot illustrates the variance explanation of principal components for superalloy microstructures with cubic gamma-prime morphology. The first principal component accounts for over 95% of the total variance, indicating that a single component is sufficient to characterize the microstructural features of the cubic gamma-prime/gamma morphology effectively.

caption: Energy Absorption (EA) versus deformation graph for the NDLS-P3 through NDLS-P7 series.
summary: This graph plots the EA against deformation for the NDLS-P3, NDLS-P4, NDLS-P5, NDLS-P6, and NDLS-P7 specimens. It highlights the cumulative energy absorption capacity of each model as it undergoes progressive deformation, serving as a key indicator of the material's efficiency in absorbing mechanical energy during the compression tests.

caption: Force versus displacement relationship observed during the low-speed impact testing of the three structural designs.
summary: This panel illustrates the force versus displacement relationship during the impact event. By plotting these two variables, the graph characterizes the mechanical response and structural integrity of Design A, Design B, and the Baseline, offering insight into how force evolves as the structures undergo deformation during the impact process.

caption: Representative stress–strain curve for an as-built lattice with a relative density of 10.8%, demonstrating the methodology for extracting elastic modulus (E), yield strength (σy), and ultimate strength (σu) via a 1% offset method.
summary: This stress–strain curve illustrates the quasi-static mechanical testing procedure for an as-built lattice with 10.8% relative density. A linear slope fitted to the hysteresis loop defines the elastic modulus, while the yield strength is determined at a 1% offset, providing a clear framework for evaluating the material's mechanical response.

caption: Gibson-Ashby model fitting curve applied to the relative modulus data of SiC lattice structures.
summary: The Gibson-Ashby model fitting curve is applied to the relative modulus data for SiC lattice structures. This analysis demonstrates that the mechanical properties of the GSH lattice are consistent with tensile-dominated deformation modes, as the fitted parameters align with the predicted property ranges for such structural configurations.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure map focusing exclusively on the γ-FCC phase subset within the as-built (AB) sample.
summary: Distribution analysis of austenite grains in the as-built sample shows that neighboring retained austenite regions often share identical crystallographic orientations. This suggests that these grains likely originate from the same parent austenite grain, providing insight into the transformation history and the spatial arrangement of the FCC phase within the microstructure.

caption: APT reconstruction highlighting oxide particles within the Ti-Ta matrix, visualized using 6.5 at% O iso-concentration surfaces.
summary: The 6.5 at% O iso-concentration surfaces in this APT reconstruction reveal the presence of nanometric oxide particles within the Ti-Ta matrix. These findings substantiate the existence of distinct oxide phases that are enriched in Ti and lean in Ta, providing further insight into the material's microstructural features.

caption: Predicted versus experimental values graph for the tensile modulus of elasticity, showing the alignment of model predictions with measured data.
summary: This parity plot displays the correlation between predicted and experimental tensile modulus values. The model shows strong predictive capability across the experimental runs. While most data points exhibit low absolute error, the graph allows for the verification of the model's reliability against the full set of experimental data.

caption: Theoretical build rate response surface for a layer thickness of 180 µm, illustrating the impact of varying laser power and Fourier number.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical build rate for a 180 µm layer thickness. As with other thicknesses, optimal build rates are found at low Fourier numbers and high laser power. The data indicates that increasing the layer thickness improves the overall and maximum achievable build rates within the processing window.

caption: Threshold stress intensity factor values (ΔΚth,LC) as a function of load ratio, derived from CPLR tests and modeled using the Nasgro threshold fitting parameters.
summary: Threshold values ΔΚth,LC obtained from four CPLR tests are plotted against the load ratio. The figure incorporates Nasgro threshold fitting parameters (ΔK1, Cth+, Cth-) to characterize the threshold behavior. This analysis provides essential data for understanding fatigue limits across the three tested load ratios.

caption: Fracture surface morphology of a WAAM specimen following tensile testing with 200°C induction heating applied.
summary: This SEM image reveals the fracture surface morphology of a WAAM specimen subjected to tensile testing under 200°C induction heating. The image demonstrates the fracture characteristics under higher thermal field conditions, allowing for a comparative analysis of how increased induction heating temperatures modify the failure mechanisms and surface features of the specimens.

caption: Polarization curves in linear coordinates for SLM-processed CoCrFeNiMnW alloys.
summary: Polarization curves in linear coordinates illustrate the electrochemical behavior of SLM-processed CoCrFeNiMnW alloys. Analysis reveals that the pitting potential (Epit) increases significantly with tungsten addition, rising from -82 mV for the base alloy to 152 mV and 989 mV for the CoCrFeNiMnW 0.125 and 0.25 alloys, respectively.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from position 3, indicating the presence of an austenitic phase.
summary: Diffraction analysis at position 3 confirms the presence of an austenitic phase. By calibrating the diffraction pattern and combining it with atomic percentage data from point scanning, the co-lattice twin structure at this location is identified, establishing the crystallographic nature of the austenite within the observed matrix.

caption: Time-of-flight (ToF) spectra of H and C recoils and Ne projectiles scattered from a tungsten surface, measured at a 40° scattering angle and 60° incident angle before and after sputter cleaning, with an inset showing the converted energy spectrum of Ne projectiles.
summary: This ToF spectrum, normalized to total Ne projectiles, displays a distinct H recoil peak 145 ns after collision-induced photons, indicating near-surface hydrogen in the tungsten layer. The data, including the Ne projectile energy conversion, allows for the derivation of H content by integrating recoil yields and fitting with powerMEIS code.

caption: Schematic representation of the initial DIW fabrication step for the s-PDMS/PBAT composite substrate.
