summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental procedures used to fabricate the s-PDMS/PBAT structure. It serves as the foundational step in the two-step direct ink writing process, establishing the composite substrate required for subsequent printing of the sensing components in the overall sensor manufacturing workflow.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of the (Zr50Cu30Ni5Al10)99Y1 MGMC coating, illustrating the thermal response during heating.
summary: The DSC curve of the (Zr50Cu30Ni5Al10)99Y1 metallic glass matrix composite coating is shown. This thermal analysis clearly demonstrates the characteristic glass transition and subsequent crystallization events that occur as the coating is subjected to heating, providing insight into the thermal stability and phase transformation behavior of the material.

caption: Spatial distribution of particle velocity along the Y direction at a shock velocity of 1.5 km/s, illustrating the transition from elastic to plastic wave propagation.
summary: Under a shock velocity of 1.5 km/s, the particle velocity profile shows a sharp increase to approximately 1.25 km/s at the elastic wave front. Subsequently, the velocity rises gradually to 1.5 km/s due to the action of the plastic wave, demonstrating the propagation of shock loading in the superalloy.

caption: EBSD orientation map illustrating grain size distribution along the ND-TD section of the Fe78Al10V12 alloy, comparing the hot-rolled state with the post-GG treatment condition.
summary: This EBSD map characterizes the microstructure of the Fe78Al10V12 alloy. It specifically displays the grain size variations along the ND-TD section, providing a visual comparison between the hot-rolled condition and the material state following grain growth (GG) treatment to assess microstructural evolution under these processing parameters.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) strain distribution maps of SiC ceramic lattice structures with varying volume fractions, fabricated via binder jetting and chemical vapor infiltration (CVI).
summary: Digital image correlation strain maps illustrate the deformation behavior of SiC ceramic lattice structures with different volume fractions. These structures, produced through binder jetting and CVI, were subjected to quasi-static compression tests to validate simulation results, providing a visual representation of how varying volume fractions influence the strain distribution during mechanical loading.

caption: Bar chart comparing the Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS), Yield Strength (YS), elongation (δ), and reduction of area (Ψ) for the experimental AT steel samples.
summary: This bar chart displays the tensile properties of the experimental AT steel samples, specifically highlighting the UTS, YS, elongation, and reduction of area values. These metrics provide a comprehensive overview of the material's tensile performance, serving as a primary indicator of the mechanical behavior of the investigated steel alloys.

caption: UV transmittance spectra of RBCs filled with varying contents of HA-SS fillers.
summary: UV transmittance measurements evaluate the optical properties of the RBCs inks as a function of HA-SS filler concentration. The results indicate that incorporating HA-SS fillers significantly reduces UV transmittance, demonstrating the effectiveness of the filler in modifying the optical performance of the composite material.

caption: Overview of the Simpact Engineering Ltd. SPL 6000 pneumatic launcher used for high-velocity impact testing.
summary: This photograph displays the bespoke SPL 6000 pneumatic launcher utilized for experimental impact testing. The equipment serves as the primary apparatus for conducting high-velocity impact experiments, providing the necessary pneumatic force to propel projectiles toward the target samples during the mechanical testing procedure described in the study.

caption: In situ Nyquist plots showing the electrochemical impedance spectra of the battery cell incorporating a ZnS@CCC interlayer, recorded at corresponding voltage intervals.
summary: In situ EIS spectra for the battery cell with a ZnS@CCC interlayer are shown as Nyquist plots. These measurements were taken at the same selected voltages as the CCC cell, facilitating a direct comparison of the impedance behavior and redox kinetics within the ZnS@CCC-modified battery system during operation.

caption: Final viscous parameters of the Burgers model for solid lignin, with gray points denoting specific indentation depths, red points showing depth-averaged values, and a green line indicating the universal lignin parameter average.
summary: Panel d displays the final viscous parameters of the Burgers model for solid lignin. The data includes gray points for specific indentation depths and red points for the average across these depths. The horizontal green line represents the universal viscoelastic properties of solid lignin, obtained by averaging all parameters and depths.

caption: Geometry-optimized atomic structures of Ni (111) surfaces featuring various types of defects.
summary: This panel displays the geometry-optimized structures of Ni (111) surfaces with various defects. These models serve as the foundational configurations for subsequent density functional theory calculations, providing the structural basis for evaluating how different defect types influence the surface properties and catalytic activity of the nickel substrate.

caption: 3D reconstruction of internal damage in a BGS-CFRCs specimen subjected to a 0.2–0.4 frequency.
summary: Representing the internal damage state of a BGS-CFRCs specimen at a 0.2–0.4 frequency, this 3D reconstruction illustrates the influence of varying load positions on crack distribution. The image confirms that changes in frequency induce significant damage redistribution, specifically altering the crack patterns across the width of the composite specimen.

caption: Radar plot displaying the mechanical-performance metrics of Al-based MMCs produced by SLM, EBM, DED, and BJ, highlighting variations in material properties.
summary: Mechanical-performance metrics for Al-based MMCs are evaluated in this radar plot, contrasting the outcomes of SLM, EBM, DED, and BJ fabrication methods. The data illustrates the influence of different AM techniques on the resulting mechanical properties, serving as a key reference for understanding material performance in these composites.

caption: Plot of the strain rate raised to the power of 1/4.3 against applied stress (σ) for the titanium alloy.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between the strain rate, raised to the power of 1/4.3, and the applied stress for a titanium alloy. The x-intercept of this curve is utilized to evaluate the threshold stress, providing a critical parameter for understanding the material's creep deformation behavior under specific conditions.

caption: Sequential process flow diagram illustrating the methodology steps.
summary: This process flow diagram outlines the sequential methodology steps employed in the study. It serves as a high-level overview of the experimental or analytical procedure, with detailed explanations for each individual step provided in the subsequent sections of the paper to ensure clarity and reproducibility of the research findings.

caption: Bright field STEM image showing the microstructure of the cubic specimen at the bottom part.
summary: This bright field STEM image displays the microstructure observed at the bottom section of the cubic specimen. The visualization provides a high-resolution view of the material's internal structure, serving as a foundational characterization of the specimen's state in the bottom region as described in the figure caption.

caption: Nickel elemental distribution map for the as-cast Alloy 3.
summary: Nickel elemental distribution map for the as-cast Alloy 3. This EDX map illustrates the spatial distribution of Ni within the microstructure of the as-cast high entropy alloy. The visualization provides insight into the compositional homogeneity of the material as part of the broader characterization of the three alloys.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Dex-PPy films on porous SLM-Ti substrates, recorded at a scan rate of 100 mV/s, showing peak shifts to -0.05 V and +0.25 V after 20 stimulation cycles.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram characterizes the electrochemical switching performance of the Dex-PPy film on a porous SLM-Ti substrate. After 20 cycles of stimulation in PBS, the reduction and oxidation peaks are observed at -0.05 V and +0.25 V, reflecting the electrochemical response of the drug-loaded polymer.

caption: STEM micrograph of γ’ precipitates after 34,220 h of creep at 700 °C and 165 MPa, accompanied by quantified EDX compositional results.
summary: STEM imaging of γ’ precipitates is presented after 34,220 hours of creep at 700 °C and 165 MPa. The micrograph is supported by quantified EDX results, which were used alongside SAD to characterize the phase composition and structural state of the γ’ precipitates following the long-term creep exposure.

caption: Point cloud representation of part #3 at a key moment during the printing process, corresponding to the maximum value of indicator I1.
summary: This 3D point cloud visualization captures the geometry of part #3 at a specific printing stage. It is associated with the maximum value of indicator I1, providing a spatial snapshot of the part's state during the manufacturing process to monitor structural integrity and layer formation.

caption: Evolution of the maximum relative error for predicted Vickers hardness in LPBF-produced AlSi10Mg as a function of symbolic regression generations, utilizing a population size of 500 and a maximum solution length of 20.
summary: This plot illustrates the convergence behavior of a symbolic regression model applied to LPBF-produced AlSi10Mg. By tracking the maximum relative error across generations, the graph demonstrates how the algorithm optimizes the prediction of Vickers hardness, given a fixed population size of 500 and a maximum candidate solution length of 20.

caption: Complex frequency plane representation of reflection coefficients for the optimally graded porosity TPMS structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the reflection coefficients of the graded porosity TPMS structure in the complex frequency plane. By comparing these results with the uniform case, the plot demonstrates how the optimized graded design modifies reflection behavior, leading to the enhanced broadband absorption performance achieved in the 50 mm thick structure.

caption: Grain boundary plane distribution for the as-built linear scan condition, showing an anisotropic distribution with a peak intensity of approximately 1.5 MRD at the (100) plane.
summary: The as-built linear scan sample exhibits an anisotropic grain boundary plane distribution. Analysis in the crystal reference frame reveals a distinct peak intensity of approximately 1.5 multiples of random distribution (MRD) centered at the (100) plane, characterizing the boundary population for the as-built condition within the linear scan microstructure.

caption: Raman spectrum of a graphite inclusion and hydroxyl (OH) stretching modes in sample B18–1, with reference spectra for graphite and diamond provided for comparison.
summary: Raman analysis of sample B18–1 reveals a graphite inclusion alongside hydroxyl stretching modes in the 3200–3800 cm⁻¹ range. The presence of these OH modes indicates an aqueous fluid-bearing inclusion. High-intensity diamond and graphite bands are observed, consistent with reference data from the RRUFF database.

caption: Cyclic polarization scans for cast and printed 17–4PH and CORRAX® alloys conducted at 25°C, illustrating the electrochemical response before and after reaching the pitting potential.
summary: Cyclic polarization curves for cast and printed 17–4PH and CORRAX samples at 25°C are presented. The solid lines denote the pre-pitting potential region, while dashed lines indicate post-pitting behavior. These curves demonstrate the material's resistance to pit initiation, with quantitative differences in metastable pitting nucleation observed between the various samples.

caption: Quantitative data table summarizing the average GND density values for AB-V specimens at strain rates of 0, 3699, 5650, and 7452 s⁻¹.
summary: This data table provides the quantitative GND density measurements corresponding to the microstructural maps. It documents the increase in average GND density from 0.55 × 10¹⁴/m² in the undeformed state to 2.4, 5.39, and 5.56 × 10¹⁴/m² at the respective strain rates of 3699, 5650, and 7452 s⁻¹, confirming the observed dislocation density trends.

caption: KAM map of the bottom interface region, illustrating localized lattice distortion and deformation within the DED-printed G6 microstructure.
summary: Kernel average misorientation (KAM) analysis of the bottom region provides a map of localized lattice distortion and deformation. This visualization helps characterize the internal strain state of the material at the interface, offering insights into the mechanical history and microstructural development of the DED-printed G6 on the steel plate.

caption: Pareto plot of standardized effects for significant factors influencing extruded line width, identifying the nozzle diameter as the most critical parameter.
summary: Representing the standardized effects of significant process factors, this Pareto plot quantifies the contribution of each variable to the extruded line width. Analysis indicates that nozzle diameter is the most influential factor in determining the formation characteristics of the extruded material, as determined through Minitab software evaluation.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the investigated HEA sample oriented specifically with respect to the casting direction [31].
summary: Depicted here is the inverse pole figure map of the investigated high-entropy alloy, focusing on the crystallographic orientation relative to the casting direction. This map, referenced from previous work [31], characterizes the texture development within the sample, offering insight into the material's structural properties along the casting axis.

caption: Average DIC-resolved axial strain-time histories for sandwich structures, highlighting the foam core deformation and structural stiffness characteristics under impact.
summary: Panel d shows the axial strain-time histories for sandwich structures. The exposed bottom surface of the foam core reduces overall structural stiffness, leading to significant foam deformation. This plot confirms that the sandwich configuration allows the foam to approach its theoretical densification limit under the applied impact conditions.

caption: Pole figure (PF) image representing the crystallographic texture of the as-built sample.
summary: The pole figure (PF) image provides a visual representation of the crystallographic texture within the as-built MEA composite. It complements the IPF data by showing the orientation distribution of the grains, offering further insight into the preferred crystallographic directions present in the material's microstructure.

caption: Compressive stress-strain curves for hybrid materials synthesized from methyl-grafted nanoparticles, illustrating the mechanical response across varying molar ratios of inorganic particles to organosilicon oligomers.
summary: Compressive stress-strain curves demonstrate the mechanical behavior of hybrid materials derived from methyl-grafted nanoparticles. The data reveals that compressive strength initially decreases and subsequently increases as the molar ratio of inorganic particles to organosilicon oligomers rises, indicating a non-monotonic dependence of mechanical performance on the nanoparticle-to-oligomer composition.

caption: Bar chart comparing the total material loss, calculated as the sum of pure mechanical wear and pure corrosion rates, alongside the specific wear and corrosion increments for SLM-ed, LMD-ed, and forged TA15 alloy specimens in PBS solution.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the synergistic material loss for TA15 alloy processed via SLM, LMD, and forging in a PBS environment. It highlights the total material loss, which is essentially the sum of pure mechanical wear and the incremental wear rate caused by corrosion, providing a comprehensive view of the degradation mechanisms.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern characterizing the granular M7C3 carbides identified in panel (a).
summary: This SAED pattern confirms that the granular carbides observed in panel (a) are M7C3-type carbides. Together with the other diffraction results, this analysis completes the identification of the carbide phases present in the H13 steel after 480 minutes of corrosion, demonstrating the specific phase evolution occurring under high-temperature thermal exposure.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOZ cross-sections for scanning strategies S3 and S4.
summary: Major axis lengths of martensite on XOZ cross-sections are displayed for intermittent scanning strategies S3 and S4. These plots demonstrate that intermittent melt pool interference modes result in larger average sizes for primary and secondary martensite, as higher cooling rates facilitate growth along the main axis of the martensite structures.

caption: Schematic illustration of the channel-shaped specimen design used in the characterization process.
summary: This panel presents the channel-shaped specimen design, which is part of the set of printed parts for characterization. The schematic highlights the overall form of the channel component. Detailed dimensions for this specific design, along with the other parts, are provided in the reference material to ensure experimental consistency.

caption: Theoretical reflection loss curve for SiOC ceramics with R = 1.00, plotted across the 2–18 GHz frequency range.
summary: This plot displays the theoretical reflection loss (RL) curve for SiOC ceramics characterized by an R value of 1.00. The data, presented within the 2–18 GHz frequency range, illustrates the electromagnetic wave absorption properties of the material, which are determined by the specific frequency and the thickness of the ceramic sample.

caption: Arrhenius plot of self-diffusion coefficients for Fe-0.8 at.%Ni and Fe-10 at.%Ni alloys, including individual Fe and Ni components, calculated using a vacancy diffusion mechanism for temperatures at or above 800 K.
summary: Arrhenius plots for vacancy-mediated diffusion in Fe-Ni alloys are presented for temperatures of 800 K and above. Data for the 0.8 at.% Ni alloy at 600 K were excluded because Ni atom displacements were insufficient to calculate reliable diffusion coefficients over the 2.8 μs simulation period observed in the study.

caption: Kernel average misorientation (KAM) map of Ti particles in the AA condition.
summary: The KAM map for the AA condition indicates an inhomogeneous strain distribution within the Ti particles, which is attributed to the powder manufacturing process. This map serves as a reference for assessing how subsequent heat treatments reduce internal strain and homogenize the microstructure of the material.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the interlayer bonding area shown in (b), with an average grain size of 73.08 μm.
summary: This histogram presents the grain size distribution for the interlayer bonding area depicted in panel (b). The analysis yields an average grain size of 73.08 μm. This value is 17.1 μm larger than the average grain size observed in the transition area shown in panel (d).

caption: Bar chart displaying the calculated work of separation for the different σ phase models.
summary: The work of separation for the various σ phase models is presented in this plot. These results are derived from first-principles calculations to evaluate the stability of secondary layers with different 8j occupancies, helping to clarify the inducing factors behind the formation of stacking disordering defects in the σ phase.

caption: Tensile testing setup schematic utilizing an Instron 3367 frame to perform lap shear tests at a constant crosshead speed of 2 mm/min.
summary: Lap shear tests are conducted using an Instron 3367 test frame as illustrated in this schematic. The setup maintains a constant crosshead speed of 2 mm/min, enabling standardized tensile testing. This configuration provides a conservative estimate of joint strength compared to the complex geometry of actual busbars.

caption: Forward model flowchart illustrating the thermo-capillary-gravity prediction process.
summary: This flowchart depicts the forward prediction model, which utilizes material properties and process parameters as inputs. The model outputs specific bead geometry characteristics, including layer height, effective wall width, and maximum wall width, providing a comprehensive framework for predicting bead formation based on defined thermo-capillary-gravity physical principles.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the selectivity of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film across various VOCs, highlighting a 3 to 5-fold higher sensing response to 1.32 ppm formaldehyde compared to interfering gases.
summary: This radar chart demonstrates the high selectivity of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film for formaldehyde. Analysis reveals that the composite sensor exhibits a significantly enhanced sensing response, specifically 3 to 5 times higher towards 1.32 ppm formaldehyde than other interfering VOCs, confirming its superior performance in gas detection applications.

caption: Physical configuration of the pendulum impact testing device, utilizing an Impetus system to simulate dental impact scenarios.
summary: The photograph displays the actual pendulum impact testing setup developed using a standard Impetus testing device from 4a engineering-Austria. This equipment is specifically configured to execute dental impact tests, allowing for the systematic evaluation of mouthguard protective performance across a range of controlled impact conditions.

caption: Macrographs of LB-PBF Ti–25Ta bioimplants featuring gyroid, diamond, and Schwarz primitive unit cell architectures designed for orthopedic applications.
summary: This panel displays the geometric design of LB-PBF Ti–25Ta bioimplants. The macrographs illustrate three distinct lattice structures: gyroid, diamond, and Schwarz primitive unit cells. These architectures are critical for tailoring the mechanical and biological performance of the 3D-printed implants in orthopedic applications.

caption: In situ SAXS streaking patterns observed for AM IN625 samples after 1 hour of thermal exposure at 870 °C.
summary: This panel displays the in situ SAXS streaking patterns for AM IN625 samples subjected to a 1-hour heat treatment at 870 °C. These diffraction patterns provide critical insights into the microstructural evolution and phase characteristics of the material under specific thermal conditions as captured during the in situ synchrotron experiment.

caption: Phase map corresponding to the 90CRA condition, highlighting the distribution of discrete L21 grain boundary precipitates.
summary: This phase map, derived from EBSD investigations, identifies the distribution of L21 precipitates within the 90CRA condition. The analysis confirms that these precipitates are discrete and do not form a continuous layer along the grain boundaries, offering critical information on the secondary phase morphology and its spatial arrangement.

caption: Synchrotron XRD patterns comparing the (311) γ matrix reflection peak positions for fine and coarse superalloy powders.
summary: Synchrotron XRD analysis reveals a distinct shift in the (311) γ phase diffraction peak between fine and coarse superalloy powders. The fine powder exhibits a higher d-spacing of 1.0855 Å compared to the 1.0840 Å measured for the coarse powder, indicating differences in the lattice parameters of the γ matrix.

caption: Trajectory path generated on the solid component surface, derived from isothermal surface analysis and corresponding height mapping.
summary: This visualization displays a calculated trajectory path mapped onto a solid component. The path is generated by utilizing isothermal surfaces and their associated height map data. This approach demonstrates a systematic strategy for defining movement or processing paths across the solid part's geometry as described in the research.

caption: Time-of-flight recoil spectra of light contaminants measured from a 50 nm Si membrane following 150 keV 40 Ar projectile transmission along the 100 channelling direction, comparing untreated samples with those subjected to HF-dip and thermal annealing.
summary: Time-of-flight recoil spectra illustrate the presence of light contaminants on a 50 nm Si membrane after 150 keV 40 Ar ion transmission along the 100 channelling direction. The data demonstrate that a combined treatment of HF-dipping and thermal annealing effectively reduces the recoil signal, indicating successful surface cleaning of the membrane.

caption: Geometrical deviation map of the ZigZag trajectory, highlighting surface precision and height variations.
summary: This heatmap visualizes the geometrical deviations of the ZigZag trajectory. The analysis confirms that this trajectory exhibited the highest geometrical precision on the top surface, as evidenced by the minimal height variations shown in the map compared to the other trajectory patterns tested in the study.

caption: Multi-prediction force plot aggregating horizontally aligned individual force plots to represent the collective model behavior across the entire yield strength dataset.
summary: This multi-prediction force plot illustrates the collective behavior of the entire yield strength dataset. By rotating individual force plots 90 degrees and aligning them horizontally, the visualization provides a comprehensive overview of model explanations for every data point, effectively summarizing the influence of features across the complete dataset used in the study.

caption: Nyquist plots for UFM-HEA and 316L stainless steel, showing a single-time constant behavior indicative of charge transfer-dominated degradation, with the HEA exhibiting a significantly larger capacitive arc.
summary: Nyquist plots for both alloys reveal a single-time constant behavior, suggesting that the degradation process is dominated by charge transfer. The significantly larger capacitive arc observed for the HEA indicates a higher charge transfer resistance at the liquid-metal interface, which confirms the superior corrosion resistance of the UFM-HEA compared to 316L.

caption: Dilatometric curve of as-built Dievar steel cooled at a constant rate of 0.5 °C/s, highlighting a distinct thermal event between 694 °C and 767 °C.
summary: This dilatometric curve illustrates the thermal behavior of as-built Dievar steel during cooling at 0.5 °C/s. A notable precipitation process is observed within the temperature range of approximately 694–767 °C, as indicated by the deviation in the curve, providing insight into the phase transformation kinetics of the material under these conditions.

caption: Aluminum (Al) elemental distribution map corresponding to the crack region shown in panel (a).
summary: Aluminum distribution within the crack region is visualized through this EDS map. This spatial analysis of Al helps characterize the local chemical environment near the crack, contributing to a broader understanding of how specific alloying elements are distributed in the vicinity of structural defects.

caption: Bode phase angle plots displaying the phase shift versus frequency for Cu–Ni alloy coatings prepared at five different current densities.
summary: These Bode phase angle plots characterize the electrochemical response of Cu–Ni alloy coatings across five varying current densities. By plotting phase angle against frequency, the data reveals how the capacitive and resistive characteristics of the coating interface evolve, providing insight into the electrochemical stability of the alloy under different deposition conditions.

caption: Elemental distribution map corresponding to the cross-sectional region of the M-Mo-10Si lattice shown in panel l.
summary: Elemental mapping of the M-Mo-10Si lattice cross-section confirms the widespread distribution of silicon throughout the molybdenum matrix. This analysis supports the structural observation that the lattice is predominantly composed of Mo3Si grains, reflecting the high silicon content and the resulting phase transformation within the densified filament structure.

caption: Linear shrinkage percentage plotted against temperature for VBA and MW glass samples during heating.
summary: This panel displays the linear shrinkage behavior of VBA and MW glass pellets as a function of temperature, measured via Hot Stage Microscopy (HSM) on an alumina sample holder. The curve illustrates the thermal contraction characteristics of both glass compositions, providing essential data on their sintering and densification profiles during heating.

caption: Strengthening efficiency of B and N additions to Ti6Al4V, comparing individual and simultaneous alloying strategies.
summary: This plot compares the strengthening efficiencies of B and N added to Ti6Al4V, both individually and in combination. The results demonstrate that the combined use of B and N yields a higher strengthening efficiency per unit of at.% compared to the individual contributions of either element alone.

caption: Bead cross-sectional area process maps for Invar 36, highlighting the geometric response of the deposited bead to changes in WFS, V, and WS parameters.
summary: Bead cross-sectional area is analyzed through these process maps for Invar 36 GMA-AM. By visualizing the effects of wire feed speed, voltage, and welding speed while keeping one parameter fixed, the plots enable a detailed examination of how these process parameters dictate the resulting geometry of the deposited material.

caption: Feature selection results for Model I, showing the iterative removal of elements from eighteen down to one, with 16 elements selected excluding Ba and Mg, achieving a mean CV score of 0.975.
summary: Model I feature selection demonstrates the impact of iteratively removing elements on model performance. By excluding Ba and Mg, the model retains 16 elements to achieve a high mean cross-validation score of 0.975. Using the top seven elements identified by SHAP analysis, the model reaches an F1 score of 0.953.

caption: Three extracted eigenvectors representing the principal components of the grain geometry.
summary: Three distinct eigenvectors are extracted from the grain data pool, as shown in this panel. These vectors serve as the basis for the principal component analysis, enabling the mathematical characterization of the grain's spatial orientation and dimensions within the simulation environment.

caption: Dependence of magnetic properties on varying ageing temperatures for specimens subjected to 95% cold rolling.
summary: This panel displays the relationship between magnetic properties and ageing temperatures specifically for 95% cold-rolled specimens. The data provides a systematic overview of how thermal treatment parameters influence the magnetic behavior of the material, complementing the observations made regarding cold deformation and ageing time in the other panels.

caption: Van't Hoff plot of log P H2 versus 1000/T for the 3# alloy, illustrating the temperature dependence of the equilibrium hydrogen pressure.
summary: The Van't Hoff plot for the 3# alloy displays the relationship between the logarithm of equilibrium hydrogen pressure and the inverse of absolute temperature. This plot facilitates the derivation of thermodynamic properties, providing insight into the stability and performance of the 3# alloy for hydrogen storage applications.

caption: Grain morphology progression for five distinct grains within the Al matrix, where scale bar values of 1.0 represent grain interiors and values below 1.0 indicate grain boundary regions.
summary: Representing the temporal progression of phase evolution in the Al-Cu-Ni system, this panel illustrates the morphological changes of five grains within the Al matrix. The visualization highlights the structural transition of grains over time, with specific scale bar magnitudes distinguishing between the grain interiors and the grain boundary regions.

caption: Log-log plot of strain rate versus applied stress for AlSb 1.2 alloy pre-annealed at 150 °C.
summary: Strain rate as a function of applied stress is plotted for the AlSb 1.2 alloy after pre-annealing at 150 °C. This measurement is part of a broader investigation into the thermal creep properties of various aluminum-based alloys, with results summarized alongside other annealing conditions in the provided data table.

caption: Calculated phase fraction plot as a function of temperature for alloy #3, illustrating the thermodynamic stability of the five constituent phases.
summary: This plot displays the calculated phase fractions for alloy #3 as a function of temperature. It confirms the presence of five total phases, including FCC Al and various Ce-Mn-Ni intermetallics, across the characterized temperature range, providing a thermodynamic basis for the microstructural observations made in the corresponding SEM micrographs.

caption: Idealized high-symmetry P4/mmm unit cell representation of the (LaNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattice, where green, cyan, gray, and red spheres denote La, Ca, Ni, and O atoms, respectively.
summary: This panel displays the idealized P4/mmm crystal structure of the (LaNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattice within a 20-atom unit cell. The atomic arrangement is visualized with specific color-coding for La, Ca, Ni, and O atoms, providing a clear structural model for subsequent analysis of the superlattice properties.

caption: Bubble plot showing GO enrichment analysis results for HUVECs, with an adjusted p-value (q-value) < 0.5, indicating significant biological process enrichment.
summary: GO enrichment analysis of HUVECs cultured on PTMN scaffolds reveals significant biological process enrichment. The bubble plot, generated with an adjusted p-value (q-value) below 0.5, demonstrates that the PTMN group exhibits significantly upregulated genes associated with angiogenesis compared to the PT group, confirming the scaffold's influence on cellular gene expression.

caption: Electronic band structure of single-layer GeN calculated using the HSE06 hybrid functional, with the Fermi level aligned to 0 eV.
summary: The electronic band structure of single-layer GeN is presented, calculated via the HSE06 hybrid functional. The Fermi level is set to 0 eV, providing a clear representation of the electronic states and energy dispersion characteristics of the GeN monolayer, which is essential for understanding its potential semiconductor properties.

caption: Radar map comparing the mechanical properties and corrosion resistance across specimens S1 through S4.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive visual comparison of the mechanical characteristics and corrosion resistance for specimens S1, S2, S3, and S4. By mapping these distinct performance metrics onto a multi-axis plot, the figure facilitates a direct evaluation of how different samples perform relative to one another across multiple criteria.

caption: Shear modulus of TPU85A measured via dynamic mechanical analysis across varying load (1–30 N) and shear angle (0.001°–1°).
summary: The shear modulus of TPU85A is evaluated through dynamic mechanical analysis, demonstrating a strong dependence on both the applied normal force and the shear angle. These results indicate that the material exhibits mechanical properties suitable for robust liners subjected to dynamic stresses during activities like walking or running.

caption: Voltage profile of a cell utilizing an M-6# membrane, tested at a constant current density of 500 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH at 80 °C, with asterisks indicating periodic water replenishment events.
summary: This voltage profile illustrates the durability of an M-6# membrane cell operating at 500 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH at 80 °C. Periodic water supply events are marked by asterisks. The data demonstrates significant electrode degradation over one week, consistent with observed increases in impedance arcs and polarization curve shifts.

caption: Three-dimensional AFM topographic reconstruction of the post-corrosion surface morphology of a near-(1 0 1) grain after 120 hours of immersion in acidic NaCl solution.
summary: Three-dimensional AFM topographic reconstruction provides a detailed view of the post-corrosion surface morphology on a near-(1 0 1) grain after 120 hours of acidic NaCl immersion. The triangular step features exhibit deviations from ideal geometry, reflecting the grain's orientation offset, while maintaining consistent 90-degree top angles across the surface.

caption: Elongation versus ultimate tensile strength (UTS) comparison of the current Fe-based alloy against literature data for various additively manufactured Fe-based alloys.
summary: This Ashby-style plot benchmarks the mechanical performance of the current alloy by comparing its elongation and ultimate tensile strength against a collection of additively manufactured Fe-based alloys reported in literature. The visualization highlights the relative property positioning of the current material within the broader context of existing Fe-based additive manufacturing research.

caption: Comparison of tensile properties, specifically yield strength versus fracture elongation, for 316L stainless steel samples processed via MF and MF+AF assistance (S1 and S2) against literature data including cast, composite-reinforced, heat-treated, HIP-processed, and other MF-assisted LPBF samples.
summary: This Ashby plot compares the tensile properties of 316L stainless steel samples S1 and S2, fabricated with MF and MF+AF assistance, against various literature benchmarks. The data, which can be divided into two regions using a 30% fracture elongation boundary, highlights the performance of these specific processing methods relative to conventional techniques.

caption: Dark-field TEM image generated from the (0 1 1)T diffraction spot circled in red in panel (b), clearly revealing the morphology of the twin structures.
summary: This dark-field TEM image, captured using the (0 1 1)T diffraction spot identified in the SAED pattern, provides a clear visualization of the twin structures. By isolating the specific diffraction signal, the image highlights the spatial distribution and morphology of the twins within the molten pool zone of the LPBF-AB sample.

caption: Nyquist plots of Fe2O3 and Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 photoanodes measured under illumination at 1.5 V vs. RHE, with the inset displaying the equivalent circuit model.
summary: EIS data under illumination reveal two clear semicircles for both photoanodes, indicating the existence of two capacitances. A typical equivalent circuit model, shown in the inset, was used to fit the EIS data, providing further insight into the charge transfer and capacitance behavior of the Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 photoanode system under operating conditions.

caption: Comparison of measured and predicted mean particle radius during isothermal aging at 850 °C for IN738LC, showing sensitivity to chemical composition variations.
summary: This panel displays the mean particle radius evolution during isothermal aging at 850 °C. By repeating simulations 200 times with varying bulk compositions, the results demonstrate that the predicted coarsening rate is highly sensitive to compositional fluctuations, particularly during the transient coarsening regime as the particle size distribution transitions.

caption: Simulated creep strain versus time curves for H282 structures containing uniformly distributed γ′ precipitates at varying volume fractions.
summary: Simulated creep curves for H282 microstructures are presented, illustrating the deformation behavior under varying γ′ volume fractions. These results, obtained through creep test simulations, demonstrate how the distribution and amount of the γ′ phase influence the temporal evolution of creep strain in the H282 alloy structures.

caption: Critical fracture energy release rate Gc plotted as a function of the index p.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the index p and the critical fracture energy release rate Gc. By varying the index p, the figure demonstrates how this parameter influences the fracture behavior of the material, providing a quantitative assessment of the energy release rate under different conditions.

caption: DSC curves illustrating the thermal behavior of PLA/GF composites containing 5 wt% glass fiber content throughout the degradation process.
summary: Thermal analysis via DSC is shown for PLA/GF composites with 5 wt% glass fiber loading. The curves track the material's response to UV-C exposure over several days, allowing for the assessment of how the inclusion of glass fibers influences the thermal stability of the PLA matrix during degradation.

caption: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of EMG signals recorded from the forearm using striped and wavy electrodes, comparing aligned and 90° rotated configurations relative to muscle fibers.
summary: This box plot evaluates the SNR performance of striped and wavy electrodes on the forearm. It compares the signal quality when patterns are aligned with muscle fibers versus a 90° rotated configuration, providing insight into how electrode orientation and geometry affect the acquisition of EMG signals.

caption: Confusion matrix detailing the predictive performance of a hybrid deep learning model focused on analyzing process-build interactions in additive manufacturing.
summary: The confusion matrix illustrates the predictive accuracy of a hybrid deep learning model developed to understand complex process-build interactions. By mapping the model's classification results, this panel demonstrates how hybrid architectures can effectively capture the relationship between manufacturing parameters and build quality, facilitating improved process monitoring and defect detection.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating action recognition performance for the video dataset at a resolution of 384x384 pixels.
summary: This confusion matrix displays the classification accuracy for the video dataset at 384x384 resolution. Diagonal elements represent correctly classified instances across 11 distinct actions, while off-diagonal values highlight specific misclassifications. This configuration is identified as one of the four best-performing models in the study for action recognition tasks.

caption: Cathodic polarization curves (Tafel plots) for the electrodeposition of Cu-Ni alloys in a chloride-pyrophosphoric mixture bath, showing current density versus potential.
summary: Cathodic polarization curves (Tafel plots) for the electrodeposition of Cu-Ni alloys in a chloride-pyrophosphoric mixture bath are presented. The data reveals that Cu deposition initiates near -0.14 V vs. Ag/AgCl, while Ni deposition begins around -1.0 V. Chloride ions act as catalysts, and the deposition potential shifts towards less-noble values as current density increases.

caption: Maximum pit height (Sv) comparison between as-built (AB) and Hirtisation®-treated samples.
summary: Maximum pit height (Sv) increases with RLD in the as-built condition. Conversely, Hirtisation®-treated samples exhibit lower median values of 11.75, 15.17, and 17.04 μm and smaller interquartile ranges, demonstrating the effectiveness of the process in reducing surface pits, except for the RLD 10% condition where the reduction was less pronounced.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the USC 10L catalyst layer, illustrating the complex morphology of the void and solid phases with integrated pore space skeletons.
summary: This panel presents a 3D reconstruction of the USC 10L catalyst layer derived from FIB-SEM tomography data. It provides a detailed view of the void and solid phase distribution, complemented by pore space skeletons. The inset dimensions for the USC CL and MPL are 4090 nm by 3050 nm by 3690 nm and 4185 nm by 2050 nm by 3690 nm, respectively.

caption: EBSD IPF map of heat-treated Ti-27Nb-6Ta processed with parameter set 1 (EA = 1.45 J/mm2), viewed perpendicular to the build direction and oriented along the build direction.
summary: This EBSD map shows the build direction orientation for Ti-27Nb-6Ta processed at 1.45 J/mm2. The microstructure is characterized as fine-grained and near-isotropic. Despite the low energy input, the EBSD analysis indicates a slight increase in pole intensity, which is consistent with the solidification microstructure observed across all orientations for this parameter set.

caption: PDOS analysis for Fe, O, and Zr atoms at the Fe/ZrO2 interface.
summary: Shown are the PDOS plots for Fe atoms, O atoms, and Zr atoms at the interface of the Fe/ZrO2 pre-nucleation model. These electronic density of states profiles detail the electronic structure of the iron and zirconium oxide interface, contributing to the overall analysis of oxide/Fe models.

caption: Schematic illustration of intergranular cracking in the Ni33Cr1Fe alloy.
summary: Shown is the intergranular cracking mechanism for the Ni33Cr1Fe alloy. The addition of 1% Fe to the base Ni33Cr alloy significantly reduces the saturation degree of the ordered phases compared to the Fe-free variant. This modification in phase saturation alters the crack propagation characteristics within the alloy's microstructure.

caption: S-N fatigue diagrams for four LPBF-manufactured aluminum alloys tested in the as-built surface condition according to ASTM E606 standards with a stress ratio of R = 1.
summary: This panel presents S-N fatigue diagrams for four distinct aluminum alloys produced via laser powder bed fusion. The specimens were tested in their as-built surface condition following ASTM E606 protocols at a stress ratio of R = 1, illustrating the fatigue performance characteristics of these additively manufactured metallic materials.

caption: {0001} pole figure of the α2 phase at 1200 mm/s, indicating two dominant crystallographic orientations.
summary: This {0001} pole figure for the α2 phase at a scan velocity of 1200 mm/s confirms the presence of two dominant crystallographic orientations. These orientations correspond to the crystallographic lamellar microstructure observed in the IPF maps, providing evidence of the texture development within the y–z plane.

caption: Optical spectrum of the mode-locked YDFL showing a center wavelength of 1074.90 nm and a 3 dB bandwidth of 6 nm.
summary: The optical spectrum of the mode-locked YDFL is presented at maximum pump power. It exhibits a center wavelength of 1074.90 nm and a 3 dB bandwidth of 6 nm, characterizing the spectral output of the laser system under stable mode-locked operation conditions.

caption: Iterative improvement of the coefficient of determination (R2) for four neural networks predicting n, ρ, b, and A‾, showing performance gains across five training iterations.
summary: This panel illustrates the iterative improvement in prediction performance for four neural networks (n, ρ, b, and A‾). The coefficient of determination (R2) for these models steadily increases with each training iteration, successfully surpassing the defined stopping criterion of 0.98 by the fifth iteration for a dataset containing 340 samples.

caption: Si 2p binding energy region for the Ni80-Cu20 cathode surface, highlighting the presence of silicon impurities.
summary: Si 2p binding energy region for the Ni80-Cu20 cathode surface is shown, revealing the presence of silicon impurities. This spectroscopic peak confirms the detection of Si contaminants on the cathode surface, consistent with the findings reported for both Ni80-Cu20 and Ni80-Fe20 alloy samples in the study.

caption: Digital image correlation analysis showing the distortion of a 3 mm thick sample after it has been cut from the base plate.
summary: Digital image correlation analysis showing the distortion of a 3 mm thick sample after it has been cut from the base plate. The sample is oriented horizontally for the measurement, with the building direction highlighted. This panel demonstrates that the 3 mm sample exhibits less distortion than the thinner 1 mm and 2 mm samples.

caption: Isometric view of the Kagome unit cell geometry used for the parametric scaffold design study.
summary: This isometric view illustrates the Kagome unit cell architecture utilized in a parametric study to identify an optimal bone regeneration scaffold. The design incorporates specific geometric parameters, including the length of the column region, strand diameter, and internal angles, which are critical for determining the feasibility and structural integrity of the scaffold.

caption: Low-field magnetic susceptibility (LFMS) measurements showing magnetization as a function of temperature for the B-400 W sample, with the paramagnetic austenite signal used as the zero-magnetization baseline.
summary: Low-field magnetic susceptibility (LFMS) measurements showing magnetization as a function of temperature for the B-400 W sample, with the paramagnetic austenite signal used as the zero-magnetization baseline. As-deposited samples exhibited significantly lower magnetizations compared to their heat-treated counterparts, highlighting the impact of thermal processing on the magnetic properties of the material.

caption: Local approach strain field distribution for the BVP II specimen.
summary: This panel displays the local approach strain field for the BVP II specimen. The visualization provides a detailed representation of the strain distribution within the material, allowing for an analysis of localized deformation behavior as captured by the experimental strain measurement techniques described in the study.

caption: Carbon contamination levels in NiTi powders processed at 20 kHz and 40 kHz frequencies.
summary: Carbon contamination levels in NiTi powders are measured to assess the impact of processing frequency. Results demonstrate that carbon absorption increases as the process advances, with significantly higher contamination levels detected in powders processed at 40 kHz compared to those processed at 20 kHz, confirming the influence of frequency on impurities.

caption: Relative DFT energies calculated for SS 316 slab models plotted against varying surface chemical compositions.
summary: This panel displays the relative DFT energies for SS 316 slab models as a function of surface chemical profiles. The data illustrates how variations in surface composition influence the energetic stability of the slab, providing a quantitative assessment of the surface state for this specific stainless steel alloy.

caption: Topographic profiles extracted along the lines marked in panel (b), featuring an inset schematic that defines the angle between the triangular pyramid side face and the grain basal surface.
summary: Topographic profiles along the ridges of the triangular pyramid are presented to facilitate the measurement of the angle between the side face and the basal surface. An inset schematic clarifies the geometric relationship, allowing for the calculation of the angle beta, which is subsequently compared against experimental data in Table 3.

caption: Complete synchrotron diffraction patterns for Ti-27Nb-6Ta specimens processed via PBF-LB/M using energy densities of 1.45, 2.05, and 2.78 J/mm².
summary: Synchrotron diffraction patterns for Ti-27Nb-6Ta processed with varying energy densities show consistent peak positions and intensities. These patterns confirm a β+α'' dual-phase microstructure across all as-built conditions. The absence of hcp α-phase peaks indicates that the processing parameters successfully maintain the desired dual-phase constitution without unwanted phase transformations.

caption: Representative field photograph of a drystone masonry retaining wall exhibiting visible bulging deformation.
summary: This photograph illustrates a drystone masonry retaining wall currently undergoing structural deterioration. The visible bulging observed in the masonry units serves as a critical indicator of potential instability, representing the initial stages of collapse for this specific type of earth-retaining structure commonly found in the United States.

caption: Ferrite pole figure for the AB200-700 sample, indicating high texture intensity consistent with the observed <100> fiber texture.
summary: The pole figure for the AB200-700 sample confirms the presence of a strong crystallographic texture in the ferrite phase. The high intensity observed in the pole figure corresponds to the <100> fiber texture along the build direction, reflecting the significant influence of LPBF parameters on the material's microstructure.

caption: Weibull distribution plot representing the three-point bending strength of 5Y-PSZ ceramic samples.
summary: This Weibull plot illustrates the three-point bending strength distribution for 5Y-PSZ ceramic samples. Analysis of the data indicates a characteristic strength of 671.52 MPa for this material, with a calculated Weibull modulus of 9.16, providing insight into the mechanical reliability and strength variability of the 5Y-PSZ ceramic.

caption: H&E and DAPI fluorescence staining of rabbit xiphoid cartilage comparing native and decellularized states.
summary: H&E and DAPI fluorescence staining images demonstrate the efficacy of the decellularization process. Compared to native xiphoid cartilage, these microscopy techniques reveal a significant reduction in cell nuclei post-decellularization, confirming that the protocol effectively removes cellular components while maintaining the structural integrity of the cartilage tissue matrix.

caption: Frequency distribution histogram of carbide size for the HT1 ZGH4142 specimen, displaying an average carbide size of approximately 68 nm along the cellular substructure.
summary: The HT1 ZGH4142 specimen, which lacks high-temperature solution treatment, maintains a fine carbide distribution with an average size of approximately 67.8 nm. Aging at 900 °C does not notably enlarge these carbides, which remain localized along the cellular substructure, contributing to the alloy's specific mechanical plasticity characteristics.

caption: Point analysis results for the precipitates in panel (c), confirming the compositional difference from the Mo matrix.
summary: This point analysis provides quantitative compositional data for the precipitates observed in panel (c). The results confirm a significant enrichment of Ti within the precipitates, which clearly distinguishes their chemical composition from the surrounding Mo matrix and supports the findings from the spectral analysis.

caption: GND density distribution map for the build produced at low temperature.
summary: Displayed is the GND density distribution for the low temperature build, offering a quantitative view of dislocation density. This EBSD data is critical for determining the contribution of dislocation strengthening, as it allows for the integration of the Taylor factor and Burgers vector into the mechanical analysis of the alloy.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern obtained from the Ti2Cu particle shown in panel a, confirming the crystal structure is oriented along the [001] zone axis.
summary: The SAED pattern collected from the Ti2Cu particle identified in the bright-field TEM image confirms its crystalline nature. The diffraction analysis specifically validates that the particle is oriented along the [001] zone axis, providing definitive structural identification of the phase observed within the Ti-4Cu-4Fe alloy microstructure.

caption: Power versus time diagram representing the UHS sintering cycle and steady-state attainment.
summary: The power versus time diagram for the UHS setup is presented, showing the sintering cycle. The process continues until a steady state is reached, which typically occurs in less than one minute, as indicated by the curve behavior in this plot.

caption: Temporal evolution of stress and strain for the thick-hinge rotating-squares structure subjected to an impact strain rate of approximately 200 s-1.
summary: This plot illustrates the temporal variations of DIC-measured strain and stress for the thick-hinge rotating-squares structure under an impact strain rate of approximately 200 s-1. Stress values were obtained directly from impact loads, facilitating a detailed analysis of the structural response of the thick-hinge variant during high-rate deformation.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of U2OS cells infected with various IAV subtypes or NDVs, visualized using H7N9 HA1-specific Nb F4 or broadly reactive IAV NP-specific Nb 204.
summary: U2OS cells infected with different IAV subtypes or NDVs were analyzed via fluorescence microscopy. The results demonstrate that Nb F4 specifically recognizes the H7N9 subtype, while Nb 204 acts as a broad-spectrum probe for IAV NP. This specificity confirms the suitability of these nanobodies for developing targeted viral immunoassays.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the comprehensive WAAM modeling process, incorporating temperature-dependent thermal and mechanical properties, heat transfer mechanisms, phase transformation plasticity (TRIP), and boundary conditions.
summary: This flowchart outlines the WAAM modeling framework, which integrates temperature-dependent thermal and mechanical properties, air or copperplate contact heat transfer, and phase transformation plasticity. By incorporating these factors and specific boundary conditions, the model accurately reproduces the temperature, deformation, and stress response behaviors of materials during the WAAM process.

caption: Acoustic Mismatch Model (AMM) illustrating phonon transmission based on sound velocity differences and acoustic impedance between two solids.
summary: The Acoustic Mismatch Model (AMM) represents a theoretical framework for calculating interface thermal conductance. It accounts for sound velocity variations between solids resulting from significant differences in acoustic impedance. The model assumes that phonon transmission probability can be calculated using equations analogous to those applied for light transmission across interfaces.

caption: Diversity indicator values plotted against 79 iterations for four multi-objective optimization methods.
summary: This panel displays the progression of the Diversity indicator over 79 iterations for four distinct multi-objective optimization methods. The data shows how each method converges toward a Pareto front, with performance rankings indicating that Method 4 (MOGP + EHI) outperforms the other three approaches in achieving diverse solution sets.

caption: XRD spectra comparing untreated 40Al 60Ni wt% samples with laser-alloyed samples ranging from 40Al 60Ni to 10Al 90Ni wt%.
summary: XRD analysis confirms the successful alloying of cold spray deposits through laser treatment. The spectra demonstrate the transition from pure aluminum and nickel phases in the untreated 40Al 60Ni wt% reference sample to the formation of distinct Al-Ni intermetallic phases in the laser-alloyed samples across the specified composition range.

caption: Partial electronic density of states for the first neighboring atoms of the site exhibiting the lowest vacancy formation energy.
summary: This panel illustrates the partial electronic density of states (PDOS) for the first neighboring atoms of the site with the lowest vacancy formation energy. By analyzing these electronic states, the study investigates the orbital distribution changes associated with vacancy formation at this specific, energetically favorable atomic site.

caption: Relative reduction of Ni-Ni bond orders in the Σ11 (110) [113] grain boundary with 1H atom segregation, visualized with a distinct color scale compared to the Σ5 system.
summary: Visualizing the impact of 1H segregation on the Σ11 grain boundary, this panel shows the localized weakening of Ni-Ni bonds. The analysis confirms that hydrogen-induced bond reduction is confined to the immediate vicinity of the H atom, consistent with the observed localized effects of hydrogen on grain boundary cohesion.

caption: Fatigue crack growth (FCG) rates plotted as a function of crack driving force for pure oxygen and mixed oxygen-hydrogen environments, illustrating the influence of varying saturated hydrogen concentrations on crack propagation behavior.
summary: This plot displays fatigue crack growth rates under pure oxygen and mixed oxygen-hydrogen environments. The data demonstrates a clear dependence of the FCG rate on the hydrogen concentration level present at the crack surface, highlighting how hydrogen exposure significantly alters the crack propagation kinetics compared to pure oxygen conditions.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles obtained at a current density of 0.5 mA cm⁻² for micro-supercapacitors with footprint areas of 0.12 cm² and 0.31 cm².
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves at 0.5 mA cm⁻² evaluate the performance of micro-supercapacitors with footprint areas of 0.12 cm² and 0.31 cm². These measurements, alongside the cyclic voltammetry data, confirm the total capacitance values of 37.6 mF and 13.2 mF for the respective device sizes.

caption: Low-magnification bright-field TEM image of 4340 steel tempered at 315 °C, showing the overall microstructure.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the overall microstructure of 4340 steel tempered at 315 °C. The analysis contributes to the study of microstructural mechanisms underlying hydrogen embrittlement resistance, providing a clear view of the bainitic lath morphology after this intermediate-temperature thermal treatment for comparison with other conditions.

caption: EBSD image of the primary stirring region E1 showing grain morphology.
summary: This EBSD image displays the grain structure within the primary stirring region E1. Analysis indicates that equiaxed fine grains are uniformly formed in this zone. The average grain size for this specific region is measured at 5.29 μm, reflecting the microstructural outcome of the primary stirring process.

caption: Regression analysis parity plot for the DNN-BRA model predicting the correlation between anticipated and actual values of the first parameter.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the regression performance of the DNN-BRA model for the first parameter. The high regression coefficient confirms the model's robustness, demonstrating that the transport effects induced by nanoparticles are predicted with minimal error, validating the accuracy of the ANN-BR algorithm under these specific parameter settings.

caption: Double-logarithmic plot of minimum creep strain rate versus applied stress for as-cast Near, Hypo, and Hyper specimens tested at 300 °C, featuring best-fit lines derived from Eq. (1).
summary: This double-logarithmic plot displays the minimum creep strain rate against applied stress for as-cast Near, Hypo, and Hyper alloy specimens tested at 300 °C. Best-fit lines calculated using Eq. (1) are applied to the data, which includes three Near samples and two samples each for the Hypo and Hyper compositions.

caption: Epifluorescence reconstruction of β-catenin (red) and DAPI-stained nuclei (blue) in control versus EGTA-treated Caco-2 cells, highlighting changes in junctional protein localization.
summary: Epifluorescence microscopy images reveal the spatial distribution of β-catenin (red) and DAPI-stained nuclei (blue) in Caco-2 cells. The reconstruction compares control cells with those treated with EGTA, providing visual evidence of how the drug application alters the expression and localization of junctional proteins within the epithelial cell monolayer.

caption: Raman spectra of PSN 2 /TiB 2 /CCP composite films processed at varying laser energy densities, demonstrating intensity fluctuations in the D, G, and 2D peaks at 1350, 1580, and 2700 cm⁻¹.
summary: Raman spectra of PSN 2 /TiB 2 /CCP composite films demonstrate the influence of laser energy density on carbon structure. Variations in the intensity of the D, G, and 2D peaks at 1350, 1580, and 2700 cm⁻¹ indicate that laser energy levels significantly modulate the graphitization degree of the carbonaceous components.

caption: Bar chart showing the percentage of α-SMA positive area in the cranium defect at 4 weeks post-surgery, comparing the efficacy of various BMSC-based treatments.
summary: Bar chart showing the percentage of α-SMA positive area in the cranium defect at 4 weeks post-surgery, comparing the efficacy of various BMSC-based treatments. Quantitative analysis reveals that α-SMA expression is significantly higher in the BMP-2/VEGF/BMSC and VEGF/BMSC groups compared to the other groups, demonstrating a statistically significant difference in vascular maturation.

caption: Log-log plot of crack growth rate versus effective stress intensity range, comparing Paris law fits for specimens tested in water and oil environments.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the effective stress intensity factor range and the measured crack growth rate. Paris-law fits demonstrate that water-lubricated specimens exhibit a significantly higher propagation rate compared to oil-lubricated specimens, a trend attributed to hydraulic pressurization and mixed-lubrication effects occurring during the fatigue crack growth process.

caption: Bee swarm plot illustrating feature importances as mean absolute Shapley values for alloy property predictions.
summary: This SHAP bee swarm plot quantifies the impact of various features on model predictions. The feature E8_mad, representing the mean absolute deviation of electron affinity, emerges as the most significant contributor, influencing predictions by approximately 40 MPa. Less influential features exhibit inconsistent distributions, where low values show negligible impact compared to high values.

caption: EBSD-IPF orientation maps of the AA7075, HSLA, and the Al-Zn eutectic structure at the weld interface.
summary: EBSD-IPF orientation maps reveal the microstructural characteristics of the AA7075, HSLA, and the weld interface. The Al-Zn eutectic region at the interface exhibits a fine, distinctive necklace-like structure, which is critical for achieving strong interfacial bonding and high tensile strength in the USWed joints compared to the base alloys.

caption: Solvent-dependent UV-Vis absorption profiles of RhB-HZ in PEGDA compared to HEMA, PEGDA:HEMA, EtOH, MeOH, and 2-Propanol, highlighting a distinct absorption peak at 562 nm in PEGDA.
summary: RhB-HZ exhibits a unique optical response when incorporated into PEGDA, characterized by a distinct absorption peak at 562 nm. This solvent-dependent behavior is compared across various organic solvents, including HEMA, ethanol, methanol, and isopropanol, demonstrating that the specific absorption feature is unique to the PEGDA environment.

caption: Concentration profiles of Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, and Al at t* = 1000.
summary: At the final stage of t* = 1000, the concentration profiles of Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, and Al illustrate the diffusion and distribution behavior of solute atoms. These profiles are critical to elucidate the formation mechanism of core-shell structure precipitates, confirming the stable distribution of elements in the Fe-7.5%Cu-3.0%Mn-1.5%Ni-1.5%Al alloy.

caption: Grain structure transition map for Ti-6Al-4V plotted as a function of solidification rate (R) and thermal gradient (G), featuring boundary lines that delineate columnar, mixed, and equiaxed zones, alongside experimental data points and a 3D inset showing simulated thermal gradients under specific printing conditions.
summary: This phase diagram quantifies the transition of beta-grain structures in Ti-6Al-4V based on solidification rate and thermal gradient. Boundary lines separate columnar, mixed, and equiaxed regions. An inserted 3D plot demonstrates that increasing preheating temperature and scanning speed reduces the thermal gradient, facilitating the development of equiaxed grain structures during additive manufacturing.

caption: Chronamperometry measurement profile illustrating the corrosion resistance behavior of SUS316-10Cu alloy subjected to the hot isostatic pressing (HIP) process.
summary: Chronamperometry measurement profile illustrating the corrosion resistance behavior of SUS316-10Cu alloy subjected to the hot isostatic pressing (HIP) process. This electrochemical analysis evaluates the material's performance under specific processing conditions, providing critical data on the corrosion resistance of the alloy after undergoing the HIP treatment to enhance its structural integrity.

caption: Internal friction curves of CR15 and CR35 samples plotted against temperature during heating, showing peak temperatures (AIF) for the CR15 sample at 422 K.
summary: Internal friction curves for CR15 and CR35 samples are presented as a function of temperature during heating. The data, obtained via DMA, reveals specific peak temperatures (AIF) for the CR15 sample at 422 K, providing insight into the material's damping behavior and phase transition characteristics during the heating process.

caption: Literature-based C-W-Ni ternary phase diagram representing metallurgical chemical alloying reactions within the molten pool.
summary: This panel displays the C-W-Ni ternary phase diagram sourced from literature references. It illustrates the complex metallurgical chemical alloying reactions occurring within the molten pool composed of WC particles and a liquid Ni matrix, providing a foundational understanding of the phase equilibria in this specific material system.

caption: Raman spectra of the prepared samples, highlighting the D and G bands for structural analysis.
summary: The Raman spectra of the three prepared samples are presented, focusing on the detailed analysis of the D and G bands. This spectroscopic characterization provides insights into the carbonaceous structural features of the materials, serving as a primary method for evaluating the graphitic quality and defect density within the samples.

caption: Schematic representation of the mechanical loading test performed on the β + ω ath material, involving loading to 450 MPa followed by an unloading cycle.
summary: This schematic illustrates the mechanical testing procedure for the β + ω ath material. The specimen is subjected to a loading cycle reaching 450 MPa before being unloaded. This setup is designed to probe the specific mechanical response of the ath-processed material under controlled stress conditions.

caption: Bar chart displaying individual desirability values for each cutting variable and the surface roughness response (Ra), highlighting values near unity.
summary: The bar chart provides a detailed breakdown of the desirability values for each individual cutting variable and the resulting surface roughness (Ra). Each bar demonstrates values close to 1, confirming that the selected optimization parameters successfully meet the desired performance criteria across all evaluated metrics in the study.

caption: 2D fluorescence spectral maps of PLA and PLA/GF surfaces, displaying excitation wavelength on the y-axis and emission wavelength on the x-axis, captured before and after UV-C irradiation.
summary: This panel presents 2D fluorescence spectral maps of PLA and PLA/GF surfaces, plotting excitation versus emission wavelengths. The data illustrates the surface degradation effects of UV-C irradiation, showing that the fluorescence area expands and shifts toward longer wavelengths as degradation time increases, indicating significant changes in the polymer molecular structure.

caption: Geometrically Necessary Dislocation (GND) density map showing the spatial distribution of dislocation density across the deformed microstructure, correlating with the strain localization observed in the KAM map.
summary: The GND density map quantifies the spatial distribution of geometrically necessary dislocations within the deformed columnar structure. This map complements the KAM data by providing a direct measure of dislocation density, which is critical for characterizing the stored energy and deformation mechanisms occurring at the columnar grain boundaries.

caption: Fitness curve for scenario 2, displaying error trends across input values ranging from 0 to 5 at 0.5 intervals.
summary: Scenario 2 fitness analysis is presented, showcasing the application of the ANN-BLMA approach. The plot visualizes error trends across input values from 0 to 5 at 0.5 intervals, providing a clear representation of the network's performance and convergence behavior within this specific critical scenario for the artificial backpropagation network.

caption: Monte Carlo (p=2) optimized design layout alongside the calculated fabrication distortion magnitude.
summary: The design layout shown here was optimized using the Monte Carlo method with p=2, resulting in a clear solid/void solution. The panel includes a visualization of the fabrication-induced distortion magnitude in millimeters. The simulation was performed for a design domain oriented at 90 degrees to the longest dimension.

caption: Adiabatic temperature change as a function of temperature for various structural states under a high-intensity alternating magnetic field of 1.8 T at a frequency of 0.2 Hz.
summary: Panel (d) shows the magnetocaloric effect under a 1.8 T alternating magnetic field at 0.2 Hz. In the region of martensitic transformation, the magnetocaloric effect value reaches 0.8 K across all three structural samples, demonstrating that the high-field response is robust despite the variations in the initial processing states.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot showing the dependence of the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of flow stress (α σ) on the inverse of absolute temperature (T −1) at a strain of 0.7.
summary: This Arrhenius-type plot displays the relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of flow stress and the inverse of absolute temperature. By evaluating the flow stress at a strain of 0.7, the graph characterizes the temperature-dependent deformation behavior of the material within the studied experimental conditions.

caption: Relative error convergence of bulk cohesive energy, stacking fault energy, and solute energies in random alloy configurations as a function of supercell size, compared to average ETN potential values.
summary: This plot illustrates the convergence of bulk cohesive, stacking fault, and solute energies in random alloys toward average ETN potential values. The data demonstrates a consistent Monte Carlo convergence rate of N^-1/2 as supercell size increases, validating the accuracy of the average model implementation across these distinct energy metrics.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves of polyimides (PIs) measured at a constant heating rate of 10 °C/min.
summary: This thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curve illustrates the thermal degradation behavior of polyimide (PI) samples. The experiment was conducted at a controlled heating rate of 10 °C/min to evaluate the mass loss characteristics of the materials as a function of temperature, providing essential data on their thermal stability and decomposition profiles.

caption: {111} pole figure illustrating the spatial relationship and positions of Cube (Grain 1) and Cube-Twin (Grain 2) orientation grains.
summary: This {111} pole figure displays the specific positional relationship between Cube-oriented grains, labeled as Grain 1, and Cube-Twin-oriented grains, labeled as Grain 2. The plot clarifies the crystallographic orientation distribution of these specific components within the material microstructure after undergoing a true strain of 0.51 at a strain rate of 0.01 s-1.

caption: Macroscopic view of the PA6 powder bed surface after spreading at 30 mm/s and 80 °C, showing jagged marks.
summary: Captured at a spreading speed of 30 mm/s and 80 °C, this image reveals the PA6 powder bed surface. Yellow frames highlight jagged marks on a slightly uneven texture, indicating a reduction in surface quality compared to the ambient temperature condition, which is not easily perceivable by direct visual inspection alone.

caption: Comparative radar chart evaluating the performance of HMCM against established acoustic and mechanical metamaterials, including advanced absorbers, micro-lattice structures, and innovative foam materials.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive performance comparison between the HMCM and various established acoustic and mechanical metamaterials. By benchmarking against advanced absorbers, micro-lattices, and foam materials, the chart illustrates that the HMCM excels in meeting high standards across all evaluated criteria, demonstrating its superior performance in the designated ranges.

caption: In-plane rotation field map of the Inconel 718 specimen after 0.32% plastic deformation, calculated using Heaviside-DIC; green arrows highlight grain-scale rotations resulting from structural heterogeneity.
summary: Following 0.32% plastic deformation, this Heaviside-DIC map visualizes the in-plane rotation field of the Inconel 718 specimen. Green arrows identify grain-scale rotations, which are attributed to the inherent heterogeneity of the grain structure, demonstrating the localized mechanical response of the material under monotonic loading conditions.

caption: Magnetic specific heat C mag of bcc Co calculated via Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic specific heat C mag for bcc cobalt as determined through Monte Carlo simulation. The data provides a quantitative representation of the thermal response of the magnetic system in the bcc crystal structure, serving as a fundamental thermodynamic property derived from the computational model.

caption: Manufacturing of the composite specimens using a commercial 3D printer.
summary: The final stage of the fabrication process involves using a commercial 3D printer to manufacture the composite specimens. This step utilizes the previously generated G-code to physically realize the stress-aligned infill patterns, resulting in the testable composite parts required for subsequent mechanical performance evaluation.

caption: Mean squared displacement (MSD) profiles for a single hydrogen interstitial located 2.61 nm from the nickel-graphene interface (NGI) in the NGNC system, evaluated between 500 K and 1200 K.
summary: The MSD profiles for a single hydrogen interstitial positioned 2.61 nm away from the nickel-graphene interface are presented here. These simulation results demonstrate the hydrogen diffusion characteristics within the NGNC system at various temperatures ranging from 500 K to 1200 K over a 5.0 ns interval.

caption: Laser confocal microscopy image of the WP sample surface revealing the loss of the striping pattern and the presence of numerous spotted defects.
summary: The WP sample surface, as captured by laser confocal microscopy, exhibits a significant departure from the uniform fringe morphology seen in the AP sample. Instead of a distinct striping pattern, the surface displays numerous spotted defects, indicating that the polishing process for this specimen resulted in increased surface irregularities.
