summary: Lattice parameter trends for Ti-Nb alloys are shown across a range of temperatures, comparing ADP-calculated values with experimental data. The simulation results confirm that the ADP accurately reproduces the experimentally observed changes in the α″ lattice, demonstrating the model's effectiveness in predicting structural variations under different thermal conditions.

caption: Reflection phase response for cell 2 across the 60 to 70 GHz frequency range, measured while cell 1 remains constant.
summary: This panel illustrates the reflection phase for cell 2 in the 60-70 GHz range. In contrast to the behavior observed for cell 1, the phase response here demonstrates the specific design characteristics required for the dual-band reflect array, where cell 1 is held constant during the measurement.

caption: Electron backscatter diffraction grain boundary map of the as-built LPBF-NiTi alloy surface parallel to the building direction, where thick black lines denote large-angle grain boundaries (>10°) and thin lines denote small-angle boundaries (2-10°).
summary: This EBSD grain boundary map characterizes the microstructure of the as-built LPBF-NiTi alloy parallel to the building direction. The visualization distinguishes between large-angle grain boundaries, represented by thick solid black lines, and small-angle grain boundaries, represented by thin lines. Large misorientation angles are primarily concentrated along the columnar grain boundaries.

caption: First order reversal curve distribution map and horizontal intensity profile for a dense Ni–W alloy film.
summary: The first order reversal curve distribution map and horizontal intensity profile for a dense Ni–W alloy film are shown. This visualization allows for the assessment of magnetic reversal properties in the dense alloyed film, providing a comparative baseline for the porous Ni–W samples presented in subsequent panels.

caption: Strain rate evolution at the specimen centre under target hot stamping conditions, comparing the novel control approach (red) against the conventional method (blue) relative to the target strain rate (dashed black line).
summary: This plot illustrates the strain rate at the specimen centre during thermomechanical testing. It compares the novel control approach, represented by red lines, with the conventional blue-line method against the target strain rate. The data highlights the performance of these control strategies under various hot stamping conditions.

caption: Crystal model of the L12-Ni3Co alloy showing the supercell structure with space group Pm-3m.
summary: The crystal model of the L12-Ni3Co alloy is established with a space group belonging to Pm-3m. This panel illustrates the fundamental unit cell and supercell configuration, providing the structural foundation for subsequent doping calculations and modeling of nonmetallic atom interactions within the alloy lattice.

caption: Atomic model of the nickel-based BCC superlattice featuring molybdenum layers in every fourth (1 1 2) plane, with nickel atoms in red and molybdenum atoms in blue.
summary: A simplified atomic model illustrates the superstructure, where molybdenum layers are arranged in every fourth (1 1 2) plane within a nickel-based BCC structure. The model maintains a lattice parameter identical to the matrix, with nickel atoms represented in red and molybdenum atoms in blue to visualize the periodic ordering.

caption: Strain distribution map of a 40% infill scaffold sample, highlighting full cross-section cracks within the white square region.
summary: This DIC strain map identifies structural failure in a 40% infill scaffold. The white square highlights the region where full cross-section cracks have developed, demonstrating the localized strain accumulation and subsequent material rupture observed during the compression test at the point of fracture.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation curves for the secondary L12 phase within the B2 matrix, illustrating distinct evolution mechanisms: nucleation-coarsening for two-phase alloys (red), nucleation-coarsening-dissolution via Oswald ripening (green), and accelerated transformation under coupled thermal and stress fields (blue).
summary: The TTT diagram illustrates the microstructure evolution of the secondary L12 phase in the B2 matrix. It highlights three distinct processes: standard nucleation-coarsening, Oswald ripening involving dissolution, and accelerated kinetics driven by coupled thermal and stress fields. This model provides a comprehensive framework for understanding phase transformation pathways in these alloys.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the ST specimen showing the presence of the ω phase.
summary: This dark-field TEM image displays the microstructure of the ST specimen. Although the ω phase was not detectable in previous XRD or SEM analyses due to its limited volume fraction, it is clearly visible in this dark-field image and the associated SAED patterns, confirming its presence in the ST alloy.

caption: Cutting force profiles measured during machining experiments in the higher speed range, comparing responses at low and high temperatures.
summary: This panel illustrates the cutting force profiles for experiments conducted at higher speeds. Integrating these results with the speed profiles from panel (a) facilitates the identification of cutting data at specific sites of interest, providing insight into the mechanical force response under high-speed machining conditions at different thermal states.

caption: Main effects plot derived from Taguchi analysis for PEEK, identifying parameter ranks and highlighting optimal levels with red markers for maximum signal-to-noise ratios.
summary: Main effects plot derived from Taguchi analysis for PEEK identifies parameter ranks and highlights optimal levels with red markers for maximum signal-to-noise ratios. Similar parameter levels to those used in Run 1 achieved the greatest signal-to-noise ratios, indicating the most effective processing conditions for optimizing the elastic modulus.

caption: Concentration profiles of Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, and Al at t* = 100.
summary: At t* = 100, the concentration profiles of Fe, Cu, Mn, Ni, and Al illustrate the diffusion and distribution behavior of solute atoms. This stage provides further evidence to elucidate the formation mechanism of core-shell structure precipitates, showing the progression of elemental segregation in the Fe-7.5%Cu-3.0%Mn-1.5%Ni-1.5%Al alloy during the aging process.

caption: Temperature versus the square root of the fraction solid (fs) curve for Alloy 625 derived from Scheil-Gulliver solidification simulations.
summary: This panel displays the temperature versus the square root of the fraction solid curve for Alloy 625. The data is generated from Scheil-Gulliver solidification simulations, providing a fundamental thermal profile that characterizes the solidification behavior of the alloy as it cools from the liquid state.

caption: Top-down perspective showing the radial dimensions and circular geometry of the cyclone reactor assembly.
summary: Representing the top-down view of the cyclone reactor, this schematic highlights the radial dimensions and circular profile of the assembly. Consistent with the vertical orientation of the reactor, this view complements the cross-sectional data to provide a comprehensive understanding of the device's overall physical dimensions and structural design.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of negative ions CrO2-, CrO3H2-, NiO2H2-, and Ni2- for the mechanically ground (M) sample, showing a continuous increase of the Ni2- signal toward its maximum level.
summary: The ToF-SIMS depth profile for the mechanically ground sample displays the intensity evolution of CrO2-, CrO3H2-, NiO2H2-, and Ni2- ions. A key observation is the continuous increase of the Ni2- signal toward its maximum level, while the NiO2H2- signal remains higher than the CrO3H2- signal throughout the depth analysis.

caption: UV–VIS absorbance profiles for H 282 Virgin, H 282 300, H 282 1000, and H 282 1400 powders, illustrating that initial light absorbance at the powder surface increases with higher oxidation states.
summary: UV–VIS spectroscopy was employed to determine the light absorption profiles of H 282 powders with varying oxidation levels. The data reveals that initial light absorbance at the powder surface increases with higher oxidation. This enhanced absorption is expected to increase energy intake, potentially leading to elevated melt pool temperatures.

caption: Plateau force and its remaining percentage for PLA and PETG hexagonal honeycombs evaluated over six programming cycles.
summary: Plateau force analysis demonstrates that the PETG hexagonal honeycomb outperforms the PLA version in maintaining mechanical integrity. The PLA metamaterial shows a 51% decrease in plateau force, dropping from 621 N in the first cycle to 303 N by the sixth cycle, indicating significant material degradation during the process.

caption: Statistical summary of lead concentration metrics for the non-LSL control group, illustrating the range and distribution of fully flushed samples alongside calculated sequential profile sample parameters.
summary: Lead concentration data for the non-LSL control group are presented via box and whisker plots, covering fully flushed samples and sequential profile sample parameters. Concentrations ranged from below the reporting limit to 21.6 µg/L, with an average of 1.5 µg/L and a median concentration of 1 µg/L.

caption: First order reversal curve distribution map and horizontal intensity profile for a porous Ni–W alloy film with 20 nm pore size.
summary: Presented are the first order reversal curve distribution map and horizontal intensity profile for a porous Ni–W alloy film with a 20 nm pore size. The data characterizes the magnetic reversal behavior of the alloyed film, highlighting the effects of the 20 nm porous structure on magnetic properties.

caption: Transition creep rates of matrix alloys measured at 980 °C and 50 MPa plotted against the calculated effective diffusivity D ̃.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between the measured transition creep rates of various matrix alloys and their calculated effective diffusivity D ̃. The data, obtained at 980 °C and 50 MPa, serves as a fundamental component for evaluating the creep behavior of the materials as described in the study.

caption: Higher-magnification secondary electron (SE) micrograph focusing on the interfacial microstructure of the sinter bond.
summary: This higher-magnification SE micrograph provides a detailed view of the sinter bond region. Together with the corresponding EDS elemental maps, this characterization confirms the high quality of the bonding between the D2M alloy shank and the WC/HEA cermet, showing a well-integrated interface at the microstructural level.

caption: Dimensional reduction representation of the integrated dataset, highlighting the distribution of cells according to their specific differentiation stage.
summary: The UMAP dimensional reduction provides a clear representation of the integrated sequencing data, specifically highlighting the progression of cells through different differentiation stages. This visualization, derived from the 21 identified clusters, allows for the observation of cellular transitions and the spatial organization of developmental stages within the manifold.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation map of the sample processed with an 85 μm spot diameter.
summary: Represented here is the Kernel Average Misorientation map for the sample processed using an 85 μm spot diameter. Derived from EBSD data on the X-Y plane, this visualization highlights the local misorientation patterns, allowing for a comparative assessment of how varying spot diameters influence the material's internal strain distribution.

caption: Magnetization loop of NiTiPt alloy homogenized at 925 °C for 72 h, displaying a sigmoidal M/H dependence near zero field and a small developed hysteresis loop.
summary: The magnetization loop of NiTiPt homogenized at 925 °C for 72 h exhibits a sigmoidal M/H dependence near zero field. A small hysteresis loop develops due to the homogenization process, with an enclosed energy density of 2.89 × 10 - 4 J kg - 1, indicating significant changes in magnetic properties.

caption: Von Mises strain contour maps for a thin hinge structure with a thickness of 1 mm, illustrating strain field evolution across various global strain levels with a high-magnification inset of a representative cell.
summary: This panel displays the evolution of equivalent von Mises strain fields within a thin hinge structure (t = 1 mm) subjected to varying global strains. The contour maps, complemented by high-magnification views of a representative cell, characterize the local strain distribution and deformation behavior during the mechanical loading process.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves comparing the precursor powder and LPBF-processed samples fabricated at 750 and 1500 mm/s scan rates, illustrating phase evolution during the first scan and thermal behavior during the second scan.
summary: This DSC measurement displays the thermal response of precursor powder and as-built LPBF samples produced at varying scan rates. The first scan reveals phase evolution characteristics of the as-received material, while the second scan captures the thermal behavior of the same samples immediately following the initial characterization cycle.

caption: Peak stress variation of the Cu-7Ni-7Al-4Fe-2Mn-0.6Cr alloy plotted against varying deformation conditions.
summary: Peak stress values for the Cr-modified alloy are plotted to demonstrate the influence of varying strain conditions on the material's maximum strength. This plot, alongside the base alloy data, qualitatively analyzes the rheological behavior and confirms that the Cr-modified alloy exhibits more obvious dynamic recrystallization characteristics during deformation.

caption: Dark field TEM image illustrating the nanometric distribution of the α" phase within the Ti-9Mo-1Fe alloy.
summary: This dark field TEM image provides a detailed view of the α" phase distribution in the Ti-9Mo-1Fe alloy. The image confirms that the α" phase exists as a nanometric distribution, consistent with the diffraction evidence of the orthorhombic phase identified in the corresponding SAED pattern for this specific alloy composition.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of human gingival fibroblasts exposed to Co-Cr cast extract for 72 hours, showing marked disruption of the actin cytoskeleton.
summary: Confocal microscopy image of human gingival fibroblasts exposed to Co-Cr cast extract for 72 hours, showing marked disruption of the actin cytoskeleton. The visualization highlights significant cellular stress and structural degradation of the cytoskeleton, indicating that the cast Co-Cr extract negatively impacts the integrity of the human gingival fibroblast cells.

caption: Comparison of average microhardness values for LPBF-processed CoCr alloys, specifically contrasting measurements taken at the molten pool boundaries versus those obtained from the interior of the molten pools.
summary: This figure presents the microhardness characteristics of LPBF-processed CoCr alloys, analyzed on planes parallel to the building direction. The data highlights the variation in mechanical properties by comparing hardness values measured at the molten pool boundaries against those recorded within the molten pool regions under various laser processing parameters.

caption: Comparison of numerical and experimental values for the crack initiation regime, demonstrating the fidelity of the linear-elastic model.
summary: Focusing on the crack initiation regime, this parity plot evaluates the fidelity of the linear-elastic model in reproducing material response. For design variations with 6 mm and 10 mm dimensions, no significant differences in the measured parameters are observed, confirming the model's accuracy in predicting these specific mechanical quantities.

caption: Merged fluorescence micrographs of ARPE-19 cells stained with calcein-AM (green, live) and ethidium homodimer-1 (red, dead) at 4× magnification, showing cell morphology and viability distribution across different treatment groups and time points.
summary: Fluorescence imaging provides visual evidence of cell viability, complementing the quantitative data. Micrographs reveal pronounced cytotoxicity in HPT samples, where viability drops significantly from 45% at 2 h to 35% at 24 h. The images display sparse green fluorescence and a predominance of red-stained cells, indicating extensive cell death in these formulations.

caption: Comparison of current densities for the five catalysts at a fixed potential of 1.60 V, highlighting the superior performance of the Ni3FeN sample.
summary: The Ni3FeN sample exhibits a significantly higher current density of 12.7 mA cm–2 at 1.60 V compared to Ni3Fe alloy (9.81 mA cm–2), RuO2 (6.50 mA cm–2), NiFe LDH (6.10 mA cm–2), and NiFeO x (5.21 mA cm–2), demonstrating its enhanced electrocatalytic activity.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of HEMA:PEGDA resin containing Atto dyes.
summary: This panel displays the optical transmission spectrum for Atto dyes dissolved within a liquid HEMA:PEGDA resin matrix. The data illustrates the wavelength-selective filtering properties of these dyes, which are essential for their application in color vision correction materials as described in the study.

caption: Calculated G^3.4/R values for the CoCrNi alloy as a function of varying laser scanning speeds.
summary: This panel illustrates the values of the G^3.4/R ratio for the CoCrNi alloy under different laser scanning speeds. These calculated values, based on the temperature gradient G and solidification rate R, characterize the solidification behavior of the alloy across the range of scanning speeds tested in the study.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of the oxidation scale on DZ445 superalloy after 120 h of cyclic creep (300-200 MPa) at 900 °C, highlighting stress-assisted element redistribution.
summary: This EDS map reveals the elemental distribution in the cross-sectional oxidation scale of the DZ445 superalloy after 120 hours of cyclic creep (300-200 MPa) at 900 °C. It confirms the element redistribution in the outmost layers during stress-assisted oxidation, with the P4 layer composition derived from the dark region A.

caption: 1H NMR characterization of the synthesized PAA-CD-DA polymer, confirming the successful chemical modification of the PAA backbone.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum provides structural confirmation of the PAA-CD-DA polymer. By grafting catechol and cyclodextrin onto the PAA backbone, the researchers successfully created a functionalized carrier designed to improve the therapeutic effect of D609 for the treatment of dry eye disease.

caption: Virtual dark-field (VDF) image constructed from characteristic diffuse-scattering patterns in the [1-12] zone, highlighting bright nanoscale domains.
summary: Constructed from characteristic diffuse-scattering patterns observed in the correlation map, this VDF image reveals the presence of bright nanoscale domains within the solution-treated MEA. These domains represent localized structural features identified through the analysis of diffuse-scattering signals along the [1-12] zone axis.

caption: Orientation distribution function (ODF) sections at φ2 = 0° and 45° for FeSi 6.5 wt% sample TW1.
summary: Sample TW1 of FeSi 6.5 wt% is characterized by its macrotexture, represented through ODF sections at φ2 = 0° and 45°. These orientation distribution functions, derived from scanned areas, provide a detailed visualization of the crystallographic texture present in the material following the specified processing conditions.

caption: Representative live/dead fluorescence staining images of HCECs and HCSCs cultured on SRCP, showing high cell viability with intense green fluorescence and minimal red staining.
summary: Live/dead fluorescence staining images of HCECs and HCSCs demonstrate high biocompatibility of the SRCP material. The cells exhibit intense green fluorescence, indicating high viability, while negligible red fluorescence confirms minimal cytotoxicity. These results confirm that the SRCP scaffold supports the survival of both corneal epithelial and stromal cell types.

caption: Size distribution histogram of Laves phase particles located at the grain boundaries of DAFA26 alloy aged at 800 °C for 240 h, with N representing the count and ± indicating the standard deviation.
summary: This histogram presents the size distribution of Laves phase particles found at the grain boundaries of DAFA26 alloy after 240 h of aging at 800 °C. The plot quantifies the particle size distribution, where N denotes the total number of particles counted and the value indicates the standard deviation.

caption: Linear Tafel extrapolation, Nyquist plot, and Bode plot for titanium alloys in phosphate buffer solution.
summary: Electrochemical corrosion resistance of the titanium alloys is evaluated through polarization curves and EIS plots in a phosphate buffer solution. The panel presents linear Tafel extrapolation, Nyquist plots, and Bode plots, which collectively characterize the corrosion behavior and surface reactivity of the materials under test conditions.

caption: Residual strain measurements in radial, tangential, and axial directions along the L2 scan path on the inner wall of the cylinder.
summary: Measurements along the L2 scan path on the inner wall reveal tensile residual strains reaching up to 1600 με below the joint region. Notably, singular domains exist in the axial stress direction, where the highest tensile and compressive strains are observed at the inner surface of the cylinder bottom section.

caption: Cutting force comparison between LAM and CM processes at a cutting speed of 96 m/min.
summary: Cutting forces for LAM and CM processes are evaluated at a cutting speed of 96 m/min. As established in the experimental results, higher feed rates and depths of cut contribute to increased chip loads and higher cutting forces, providing a comparative analysis of the machining parameters' effects on tool performance.

caption: Spectral changes observed in the absorption profile of O-12 during 365 nm LED-induced photolysis in an acetonitrile solution.
summary: The absorption spectrum of O-12 is shown during steady-state photolysis experiments at 365 nm. These results highlight the molecule's capacity to undergo cleavage. O-12 exhibits the fastest cleavage rate among the tested oxime esters, consistent with its high molar extinction coefficient of 17,800 L mol-1 cm-1 at 365 nm.

caption: Galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles of the Ni-Co electrodes recorded at a current density of 2 mA·cm⁻².
summary: Galvanostatic charge/discharge curves at 2 mA·cm⁻² provide a direct comparison of the electrochemical performance between pristine and soaked Ni-Co electrodes. These profiles illustrate the voltage response over time, highlighting the impact of the soaking process on the charge storage characteristics of the nanowire array electrode structure.

caption: STEM micrograph of the 210 W-1500 mm/s condition, demonstrating the preferential segregation of MC carbide precipitates at the cell boundaries.
summary: In the 210 W-1500 mm/s processed IN738LC alloy, this STEM micrograph reveals the spatial arrangement of MC carbide precipitates. These precipitates are found to be situated at the cell boundaries, which are regions characterized by high dislocation density within the cellular structure of the as-built material.

caption: Fluorescent photomicrograph of U-2OS cells on an alternative geometric scaffold, stained with actinRED for cytoplasm and NucBlue for nuclei at 4x magnification.
summary: U-2OS cells seeded on geometric scaffolds are visualized using fluorescence microscopy after 24 hours of incubation. The image displays cytoplasmic and nuclear staining, highlighting cell adhesion patterns on the disc surface at 4x magnification, providing insight into the cellular distribution and morphology within the scaffold environment.

caption: Current density-voltage (JV) characteristics of GaAs(Sb)(N) devices measured under AM1.5G illumination, comparing experimental data represented by solid lines with calibrated simulation models shown as dashed lines.
summary: This plot displays the JV-curves for GaAs(Sb)(N) devices under AM1.5G conditions, contrasting experimental measurements with calibrated simulation models. The simulations utilize a GaAs material model based on Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination lifetimes, demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in capturing the device performance characteristics observed in the experimental data.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the diverse range of skills acquired by students participating in the VIP class format.
summary: This radar chart visualizes the comprehensive skill set developed by students through the VIP class format. By mapping various competencies, the figure demonstrates the pedagogical effectiveness of this approach in fostering student learning. The data highlights how the VIP structure successfully facilitates the acquisition of new skills in an academic setting.

caption: Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) displacement field map for the sand-geocell interface at 25 kPa normal stress, illustrating the shear deformation pattern.
summary: This PIV displacement field map visualizes the shear deformation behavior of the sand-geocell interface under a 25 kPa normal stress. The plot provides a visual representation of the interaction at the shearing plane, serving as a baseline for comparing the reinforcement efficiency of different geocell-based interface configurations.

caption: Solid-state 13C CPMAS NMR spectrum of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) showing characteristic chemical shifts.
summary: This panel presents the solid-state 13C CPMAS NMR spectrum of CMC. The spectrum serves as a reference for identifying CMC-related signals within complex formulations, complementing HRMAS findings. It provides the baseline chemical shift data necessary to distinguish CMC contributions from other components in the analyzed material mixtures.

caption: Resistance measurement of a NiFe-SiO2 nanocomposite with 2 nm single layer thickness using a double-through configuration.
summary: Resistance characteristics for the 2 nm NiFe and 2 nm SiO2 layered nanocomposite are presented using a double-through measurement configuration. This plot illustrates the electrical response of the material under this specific testing geometry, complementing the single-through data to characterize the nanocomposite's overall electronic behavior and layer-dependent resistance.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the synthesized PA12 polymer, displaying signals consistent with established polyamide chemical structures to verify successful synthesis.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum provides definitive evidence for the successful synthesis of the polyamide. The observed signals align with established literature values for polyamides, confirming the chemical structure of the synthesized PA12 and validating the synthesis process through the identification of characteristic proton environments within the polymer chain.

caption: Current-time transients recorded during potential steps from -0.815 to -0.3 V following a sequential exposure cycle of H2, no H2, and H2.
summary: This panel depicts current-time transients during potential steps to -0.3 V after the material underwent a specific sequence of hydrogen exposure cycles. The data, presented in log(current density) versus reciprocal charge density coordinates, enables the estimation of the cBV parameter, which characterizes the activation energy of ion migration through the oxide film.

caption: DBSCAN clustering results for pelvis elevation maxima derived from PEM data, showing step length in cm versus recording time for participant HP-1.
summary: Clustering of pelvis elevation maxima using PEM data reveals the step length of participant HP-1 across ten distinct walks. The analysis shows very few outliers, and in some instances, no outliers were detected for the participant. Different colors represent individual walks, effectively segmenting the movement data through the DBSCAN algorithm.

caption: Surface SEM morphology of Mg-8Li-4Gd-0Ni alloy after 2 seconds of immersion in 3.0 wt% KCl solution.
summary: Surface SEM morphology of Mg-8Li-4Gd-0Ni alloy after 2 seconds of immersion in 3.0 wt% KCl solution. This initial immersion stage captures the early surface state of the alloy before significant localized corrosion develops, providing a baseline for comparing the corrosion behavior of the nickel-containing alloy variants.

caption: Pole figure for simulation NS3, derived from the steady-state microstructure in panel f, showing the intensity of the fiber texture.
summary: Pole figure generated from the simulated microstructure of NS3 in panel f. This plot illustrates the fiber texture intensity. The reference indicates that the maximum intensity of the fiber texture decreases as the nucleation density increases, as observed by comparing this panel with the pole figure in panel h.

caption: Rate capability comparison of V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1), V 3.5+ - Pd/C, and V 3.5+ - Electrolysis across current densities from 80 to 160 mA cm -2 and back to 80 mA cm -2.
summary: This rate capability plot demonstrates that the V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) electrolyte consistently delivers the highest discharge capacity across current densities ranging from 80 to 160 mA cm -2. The capacity is fully recovered upon returning to 80 mA cm -2, highlighting the electrolyte's strong reversibility and electrochemical stability.

caption: Discretized mesh representation of the system components, including the balloon, plaque, and artery, modeled using C3D8I elements to account for hyperelastic material behavior.
summary: The mesh for the system components, specifically the balloon, plaque, and artery, is shown here. Given the hyperelastic nature of these biological and medical materials, C3D8I elements were selected for the discretization process to ensure the numerical model effectively simulates the non-linear mechanical response of the system under loading.

caption: Atomic model of SL-Si2O stacking mode I, defined by its specific high-symmetry configuration.
summary: Stacking mode I represents one of four high-symmetry configurations derived from the SL-Si2O monolayer. Based on the crystal symmetry, this model illustrates the specific relative orientation of the layers. It serves as the first of four distinct stacking arrangements constructed to explore the structural properties of the vdW system.

caption: Light transmittance measurements for SRCP, NHC, DPC, and RHCP, illustrating the optical clarity of the materials intended for potential use in ocular or tissue-related applications.
summary: This panel assesses the optical properties of SRCP, NHC, DPC, and RHCP by measuring their light transmittance. High transmittance is a critical requirement for materials used in ocular applications, and this comparison helps determine the suitability of SRCP in terms of maintaining visual clarity compared to the other formulations.

caption: Transmittance evolution at 1746 cm−1 for Scenario 1 under hygrothermal aging conditions.
summary: This plot displays the mean transmittance values at 1746 cm−1 for Scenario 1 during hygrothermal aging. The data reveals a linear decreasing trend, characterized by an average reduction of approximately 5% per aging cycle, culminating in a total decrease of 24% due to the accumulation of secondary carbonyl degradation products.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of cells stained with Calcein AM/PI on days 1, 4, and 7, demonstrating the biocompatibility of Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA with a scale bar of 100 μm.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy using Calcein AM/PI staining was employed to evaluate the biocompatibility of Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA over a 7-day period. The images captured on days 1, 4, and 7 reveal that the Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA material supports high cell viability, confirming its suitability for biological applications with a scale bar of 100 μm.

caption: 3D atomic force microscopy topographic reconstruction of the non-activated (NA) 3D-printed electrode surface.
summary: A 3D atomic force microscopy reconstruction visualizes the surface topography of the non-activated (NA) 3D-printed electrode. This three-dimensional representation provides a comprehensive view of the surface features and height variations, supporting the morphological analysis required to correlate surface structure with the electrochemical performance of the printed electrodes.

caption: Comparison of vibration amplitude distributions along the edges of an ultrasonic vibration plate device, contrasting experimental measurement data with finite element method (FEM) simulation results.
summary: This figure illustrates the vibration amplitude distribution across the edges of an ultrasonic vibration plate device. By comparing experimental measurements with finite element method (FEM) simulation results, the study demonstrates a high degree of consistency between the numerical model and the physical device performance, validating the accuracy of the FEM approach.

caption: UV-visible absorption spectra of methyl orange mixed with NaBH4 in the presence of SL-NiNPs.
summary: This panel illustrates the UV-visible absorption spectra of methyl orange and NaBH4 when SL-NiNPs are present. By monitoring the absorbance at 464 nm via a UV-visible spectrometer, the degradation rate of methyl orange is evaluated, demonstrating the catalytic effect of the SL-NiNPs on the reduction process.

caption: Overview of the D30 specimen fracture surface highlighting two distinct crack nucleation sites, labeled 1 and 2.
summary: This SEM micrograph displays the fracture surface of a D30 specimen following cyclic loading. Two primary crack nucleation sites are identified and marked as 1 and 2. The image illustrates the surface morphology where multiple crack nucleations occur, contributing to the overall failure mechanism observed in the analyzed specimen.

caption: Confocal microscopy 3D render of HUVECs within a GelMA scaffold after one week of incubation, showing cell nuclei in blue and actin filaments in red, with dashed lines highlighting early lumen formation along half of the inner cores.
summary: After one week of incubation, HUVECs within the GelMA scaffold exhibit early signs of lumen formation. Confocal microscopy 3D renders reveal the cells lining approximately half of the inner cores, with nuclei stained blue and actin filaments stained red, demonstrating the initial stages of microvessel development within the mm-thick construct.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image illustrating the measurement methodology for flank wear width at three distinct locations on the tool under UAT and LCO2 cooling conditions.
summary: This scanning electron microscopy image demonstrates the measurement of flank wear width on a tool. By analyzing three specific locations, the researchers quantify the wear progression under UAT and LCO2 cooling environments, providing a precise visual basis for evaluating tool degradation during the machining process.

caption: Power density generated by second-type PENGs as a function of composite filler content.
summary: Power density for the second-type PENG is shown. The data indicates that higher voltage outputs significantly increase power densities, with substantial gains achieved through the addition of ZnO and TrGO, highlighting the positive impact of these fillers on the energy harvesting capabilities of the device.

caption: Crack opening displacement (COD) contour map for the T sample tested at 1-90-1-1 loading frequency at 650 °C for 96 h.
summary: Representing the T sample tested at 1-90-1-1 loading frequency, this COD contour map shows the crack opening distribution measured perpendicular to the crack plane. High COD values are concentrated along the crack front lines, providing a detailed visualization of the crack morphology and opening behavior under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Fourier-transformed 79 Br spectrum derived from the free induction decay in panel a, showing the central resonance and associated spinning sidebands marked with asterisks, with a callout highlighting the lower signal-to-noise ratio of the sidebands.
summary: The 79 Br spectrum is obtained via Fourier transformation of the free induction decay signal, resulting from 16,384 scans. The plot identifies the central peak and characteristic spinning sidebands, indicated by asterisks. A specific callout is provided to emphasize the lower signal-to-noise characteristics of these sideband features.

caption: Initial atomic configuration of the MD model at 0% strain, highlighting the starting structure.
summary: This snapshot represents the initial state of the molecular dynamics simulation at zero strain. It serves as the baseline structure for observing the subsequent evolution of stacking faults and twin boundaries, providing a clear view of the atomic arrangement before any external mechanical deformation is applied to the system.

caption: XRD patterns of A-aramid, S-aramid, and aramid fabric showing consistent diffraction peaks at 2θ = 20.5°, 23°, and 28.4°, corresponding to the (110), (200), and (004) crystal planes.
summary: XRD patterns for A-aramid, S-aramid, and the reference aramid fabric are displayed to evaluate crystallinity. All three samples exhibit identical diffraction peaks at 2θ = 20.5°, 23°, and 28.4°, which are indexed to the (110), (200), and (004) planes, indicating that the crystalline structure remains stable throughout the printing process.

caption: Raman spectrum comparing the SiC green body and the sample post-selective laser melting.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis is depicted for both the SiC green body and the sample following selective laser melting. This comparison highlights the chemical and structural changes occurring during the laser processing stage, providing insight into the material's vibrational properties and phase integrity after the selective laser melting fabrication process.

caption: X-ray computed tomography longitudinal view of a carbon fibre filament demonstrating inherent fibre waviness within the polyamide matrix.
summary: X-ray computed tomography imaging reveals that carbon fibres within the printed filament are not perfectly straight but exhibit significant waviness. This structural irregularity, observed after deposition on the FDM build platform, contributes to a notable reduction in the tensile properties of the printed carbon fibre reinforced filament.

caption: Bode plots representing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) response of as-cast B30-x Fe alloys after 0 days of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel displays the initial EIS Bode plot for as-cast B30-x Fe alloys before immersion. It serves as the baseline measurement for evaluating the electrochemical behavior of the alloy in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, providing the starting point for analyzing corrosion resistance changes over the 60-day testing period.

caption: Optical micrograph showing the melt pool dimensions at the top surface of an IN738LC sample fabricated using a 67° hatch rotation and a volumetric energy density of 71.4 J/mm³.
summary: Captured at the top surface of an LPBF-processed IN738LC sample, this micrograph reveals the melt pool dimensions resulting from a 67° hatch rotation. With a volumetric energy density of 71.4 J/mm³, the image provides a clear view of the melt pool width and depth under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Nyquist plots of the DA-SOFC at 650 °C under a 300 mA bias, highlighting the increased polarization resistance associated with lower temperature operation.
summary: Nyquist plots at 650 °C quantify the substantial increase in polarization resistance observed at lower temperatures. The data shows that the cell's electrochemical impedance is highly sensitive to NH3 flow rates under these conditions, reflecting the challenges of ammonia-fueled operation when thermal energy is limited.

caption: BSE-EDS elemental map showing the overall elemental composition and precipitate distribution in heat-treated LPBF HX.
summary: BSE-EDS mapping of heat-treated LPBF HX reveals the formation of molybdenum-rich M6C carbides at grain boundaries. These nanoscale precipitates, measuring roughly 200 nm, are clearly identified through the localized concentration of molybdenum and carbon. The analysis confirms the microstructural changes occurring at the grain boundaries during the heat treatment process.

caption: Calculated density of states for La1.5Mg0.5Ni7 in the hexagonal Ce2Ni7-type structure, highlighting element-resolved contributions.
summary: This panel displays the calculated density of states for the hexagonal La1.5Mg0.5Ni7 phase. It includes element-resolved contributions, demonstrating that the primary valence band characteristics are dominated by Ni 3d bands. These electronic features are essential for understanding the material's bonding and overall electronic structure in the Ce2Ni7-type configuration.

caption: EDS spectra of the BG AC3D biocomposite, identifying the elemental composition of the scaffold.
summary: The EDS spectra of the BG AC3D biocomposite provide a quantitative and qualitative analysis of the elemental composition. This spectroscopic data confirms the presence of the expected elements within the scaffold, validating the chemical makeup of the biocomposite material synthesized for the study.

caption: Extrusion force profiles over time for H_Zn/Alg, H_Ca/Alg, and H_Ba/Alg hydrogels using a 20 G conical needle, highlighting steady-state flow and force peaks for H_Ba/Alg.
summary: Extrusion force profiles for the three hydrogels using a 20 G needle demonstrate a continuous extrusion flow reaching a steady-state condition. Notably, the H_Ba/Alg sample exhibits force peaks exceeding 1 N, which are attributed to hydrogel matrix reconstruction that negatively impacts the continuity of the extrusion flow during the procedure.

caption: In situ DRIFTS spectra for 2Ni-8Fe-13X, indicating the detection of the CH4 vibration signal at 3015 cm-1 at a temperature of 300 °C.
summary: The DRIFTS spectra for 2Ni-8Fe-13X show the CH4 vibration signal at 3015 cm-1 emerging at 300 °C. This temperature is higher than that observed for the 10Ni-13X catalyst, highlighting the influence of iron modification on the catalytic performance and the temperature required for methane production during CO2 methanation.

caption: Hybrid TPMS unit cell lacking cubic symmetry, demonstrating the absence of the orthotropic symmetry planes found in primitive variants.
summary: This hybrid TPMS unit cell structure is shown to lack the cubic symmetry characteristic of primitive TPMS variants, specifically missing the two planes of orthotropic symmetry. Despite this structural difference, the hybrid unit cell retains a 120° rotational symmetry about the [1 1 1] cell body diagonal.

caption: Local density of states (LDOS) map for the valley at 0.24 V, with white dashed lines marking the conductance band minima and black dash-dot lines indicating average potential energy.
summary: Representing the LDOS for the valley at 0.24 V, this panel highlights the electronic state distribution within the device. The white dashed lines delineate the conductance band minima, which are raised by the Al0.3Ga0.7As barriers relative to the GaAs body, while the black dash-dot lines represent the average potential energy.

caption: High-resolution HAADF-STEM micrograph of the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample highlighting microstructural features.
summary: This high-resolution HAADF-STEM micrograph provides a detailed view of the microstructure in the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample. By utilizing high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy, the image reveals fine-scale structural details and phase distributions, which are essential for understanding the material's response to the T6 heat treatment process.

caption: In situ SANS scattering curves for the undeformed IN738LC sample Y43 during a thermal cycle of RT-700-800-900 °C-RT.
summary: In situ SANS measurements for the undeformed IN738LC sample Y43 are presented during a thermal cycle from room temperature to 900 °C and back. The scattering data reveals the formation of 30–40 Å large precipitates specifically at 700 °C, indicating structural evolution during the heating process.

caption: Creep evolution over time for the same randomly selected lattice element.
summary: Creep evolution for a randomly chosen lattice element is plotted to illustrate its deformation behavior during structural analysis. The results demonstrate that early-age creep contributes only a limited amount, roughly 1%, to the total deformation of the element, highlighting the relatively minor role of creep in this specific structural context.

caption: Surface texture profile of the upskin region on a θ = 45° wall specimen.
summary: This panel shows the upskin surface topography for a wall built at a 45° orientation. The surface profile reveals the presence of process defects, including spatter and partially melted powder particles, which are characteristic of the manufacturing process and building orientation applied to these thin wall specimens.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of the specimen fabricated via laser coaxial powder feeding (DED).
summary: This kernel average misorientation map illustrates the local strain distribution within the DED-processed specimen. The visualization provides insight into the microstructural deformation characteristics inherent to the laser coaxial powder feeding process, serving as a comparative baseline for evaluating the local misorientation gradients resulting from different additive manufacturing techniques.

caption: Texture plot derived from EBSD data for the as-deposited LPBF A709 specimen built in the parallel direction.
summary: This texture plot quantifies the crystallographic preferred orientation of the as-deposited LPBF A709 alloy. By analyzing the data from the parallel build direction, the plot highlights the specific texture components developed during the laser powder bed fusion process, providing essential information regarding the material's anisotropic mechanical properties.

caption: Arc morphology observed by high-speed camera for the UHFP condition, illustrating the arc state after the completion of the droplet transfer.
summary: This photograph shows the arc morphology following droplet transfer under UHFP conditions. High-speed imaging confirms that the arc structure remains consistent with the non-UHFP state shown in panel (b). The application of UHFP current does not significantly change the arc morphology during the droplet transfer process.

caption: Bode plot showing phase angle versus frequency, where the SLM-UN sample exhibits a lower phase angle in the low-frequency region and displays only one peak.
summary: The Bode plot for phase angle versus frequency reveals that the SLM-UN sample exhibits a lower phase angle in the low-frequency region. Furthermore, the sample displays only one peak, indicating specific electrochemical characteristics of the nitrided surface compared to the untreated material under the tested experimental conditions.

caption: Visual appearance of the powder bed after filling and blade leveling, demonstrating effective separation of the two powder materials following divider removal.
summary: The photograph shows the powder bed after the filling process and blade leveling. The inclined divider, which is tilted relative to the blade movement, successfully separates the powders into two distinct regions, facilitating the formation of a gradual and continuous transition zone between the materials within the powder platform.

caption: Truncated M-H hysteresis loops for the α-Fe2O3/Ni81Fe19/Pt heterostructure, illustrating the magnetic reversal behavior at 100 K, 185 K, and 300 K.
summary: Truncated hysteresis loops for the α-Fe2O3/Ni81Fe19/Pt sample are presented at 100, 185, and 300 K to highlight the magnetic reversal region. These measurements demonstrate how the reversal behavior changes across the transition temperature, reflecting variations in magnetic coupling within the hematite/Py heterostructure as the temperature shifts through the reversal region.

caption: Ionic conductivity of M-1# to M-8# membranes in the Cl- form plotted as a function of temperature.
summary: The ionic conductivity of M-1# to M-8# membranes in the Cl- form is presented as a function of temperature. These measurements, taken while the membranes were mounted in a conductivity cell, illustrate the temperature-dependent transport properties of the crosslinked materials, highlighting variations in performance across the different membrane samples.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram measurements for three distinct nickel alloy-coated 3D-printed electrodes with a nickel mass deposition of 0.133 g/cm2, performed in a distilled water electrolyte.
summary: This panel displays the cyclic voltammetry results for three nickel alloy-coated 3D-printed electrodes tested in distilled water. Each electrode features a consistent nickel mass deposition of 0.133 g/cm2. These measurements characterize the electrochemical behavior of the alloy-coated surfaces within the aqueous environment, providing baseline data for comparison with alkaline conditions.

caption: Relative density of AlSi10Mg cubes modified with 3 wt% B4C, demonstrating consistent densification performance.
summary: The 3 wt% B4C-modified AlSi10Mg cubes exhibit nearly full densification across various processing conditions. While the material achieves high density, the presence of micron-sized B4C traces is noted, which contributes to premature failure and limits the formation of ridges on the fracture surfaces, thereby impacting the ultimate tensile strength.

caption: Liquidus projection of the Al–Ni–Si ternary system in the Al-rich corner, with red dots indicating the specific alloy compositions investigated in this study.
summary: This liquidus projection of the Al–Ni–Si ternary phase diagram highlights the Al-rich corner, where red dots denote the specific sample compositions analyzed. These compositions are critical for understanding the solidification behavior, such as the primary precipitation of the Al3Ni phase observed during cooling at 756.6 °C.

caption: Nonlinear fluorescence decay profile and corresponding biexponential fit for TPU/1 C composite.
summary: TPU/1 C composite fluorescence decay is illustrated through a nonlinear curve measured at 465 nm. The data is processed using a biexponential fitting model to extract the fluorescence lifetime parameters, providing insight into the emission behavior of the composite at the specified coumarin concentration.

caption: 3D reconstruction image and profile curve of the side surface of the unSMATed part, showing a smooth quality with a measured roughness of 2.88 ± 0.12 μm.
summary: The side surface of the unSMATed part maintains a high quality, as demonstrated by the 3D reconstruction image and corresponding profile curve. Quantitative analysis of this surface indicates a roughness value of 2.88 ± 0.12 μm, reflecting the state of the material prior to the SMAT process.

caption: Exhaust gas composition analysis during CO-TPD, displaying CO 2 and CO signals as a function of temperature.
summary: Exhaust gas analysis during CO-TPD tests detects CO and CO 2 desorption. Peaks in the signal are attributed to the reduction of nickel or cobalt oxides by CO, while higher temperature peaks likely correspond to the Boudouard reaction, where adsorbed CO converts into carbon and CO 2.

caption: White light interferometer (WYKO NT1100, Veeco Metrology) utilized for characterizing the upskin surface roughness of fabricated samples.
summary: This image displays the white light interferometer (WLI) system, specifically the WYKO NT1100 model from Veeco Metrology, used for surface measurements. The instrument is employed to quantify the upskin surface roughness of the fabricated samples, providing essential topographical data for evaluating the quality and finish of the manufactured materials.

caption: Post-heat treatment microstructure of the 0.75 wt% nanocomposite, illustrating the dissolution of reinforcements and alloying elements.
summary: Heat treatment of the 0.75 wt% nanocomposite results in a microstructure where the majority of alloying additions and reinforcements are dissolved within the matrix. This observation confirms that the thermal processing successfully facilitated the integration of the reinforcement particles and alloying elements into the aluminum alloy's solid solution.

caption: Temperature sweeps of storage modulus for PMMA/PVB/PEG/ATBC feedstocks prepared at 60 rpm with smaller PMMA kG7E granulates, highlighting the impact of processing parameters.
summary: Temperature-dependent storage modulus measurements are presented for PMMA/PVB/PEG/ATBC feedstocks compounded at 60 rpm using smaller PMMA granulates. The results reveal that the combination of smaller granulates and higher shear rates during compounding leads to a lower storage modulus, a trend most pronounced in feedstocks containing high levels of ATBC.

caption: Binary Cu–Sn phase diagram used to predict the formation and stability of the Sn-rich precipitates observed in the α-Cu matrix.
summary: The binary Cu-Sn phase diagram serves as the thermodynamic framework for predicting the formation of Sn-rich precipitates within the α-Cu matrix. This equilibrium diagram supports the experimental observations of the precipitate morphology and composition, confirming the phase stability predicted for the copper-tin system.

caption: Optical micrograph of an annealed Ni-30Cr-15Fe alloy sample showing grain boundaries post-electropolishing.
summary: The annealed Ni-30Cr-15Fe alloy microstructure is visualized via optical microscopy after electropolishing. The image shows elongated grains with widths ranging from 0.1 to 0.5 mm. This grain size range is characteristic of the Ni-30Cr alloy series, which consistently exhibits finer grains than the Ni-20Cr alloy group.

caption: Specific load capacity plotted against specific toughness for TPRCC specimens compared to literature data from Barhemat et al. [74].
summary: This Ashby plot compares the specific load capacity and specific toughness of developed TPRCC specimens against literature benchmarks. The data highlights that APCC specimens from Barhemat et al. [74] achieve a superior combination of these mechanical properties, significantly outperforming other materials in the absolute performance space shown in this graph.

caption: Radar plot comparing the multi-metric acoustic performance of bioinspired stochastic minimal-surface metamaterials against traditional acoustic foams.
summary: This radar plot provides a comparative analysis of acoustic performance metrics between bioinspired stochastic minimal-surface metamaterials and traditional acoustic foams. By evaluating multiple functional criteria, the visualization highlights the relative advantages of the metamaterial design, following established methodologies to assess how these structures perform against conventional sound-absorbing materials in various acoustic applications.

caption: Magnetic force microscopy image at 2.4 mT, where the S-state end domains have evolved into a four-domain configuration with a vortex formed near the upper edge.
summary: Magnetic force microscopy image at 2.4 mT, where the S-state end domains have evolved into a four-domain configuration with a vortex formed near the upper edge. At this specific field strength, the magnetic structure transitions into a vortex state, demonstrating the final stage of domain evolution before reaching the remanent state.

caption: Relative permeability plotted against the applied magnetic field for as-built samples.
summary: This panel displays the relative permeability of as-built samples as a function of the applied magnetic field. The data is derived from magnetic induction measurements, illustrating the initial magnetic response of the material in its as-fabricated state before undergoing any subsequent thermal processing or heat treatment procedures.

caption: Coefficient of friction (CoF) plotted against load for Ni-5Ag-10MoS2 coating and reference hot work tool steel during room temperature single-stroke galling tests against Ti6Al4V alloy.
summary: This plot displays the coefficient of friction as a function of load for Ni-5Ag-10MoS2 coating and reference hot work tool steel at room temperature. The results indicate that the coating exhibits similar or slightly higher friction levels compared to the reference steel, as the shear strength of the Ti6Al4V transfer layer dictates behavior.

caption: Immunohistochemical staining of IL-1β inflammatory markers at the implantation site after 7 days.
summary: IL-1β staining was conducted to further characterize the inflammatory response at the implantation site. This analysis demonstrated no significant differences in signal intensity among the various conduit groups and the control, confirming that the multichannel conduits elicit a biocompatible response comparable to the standard silicon control conduit.

caption: Lattice strain evolution as a function of applied load for the Al-5Ce-0.5Zr alloy, calculated within specific angular ranges.
summary: This panel shows the lattice strain as a function of load for the Al-5Ce-0.5Zr alloy, calculated using diffraction data from the 85° to 95° and -5° to 5° ranges. These measurements characterize the load transfer behavior, illustrating how the addition of zirconium affects internal strain partitioning during deformation.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the HT2 specimen cross-sectional fracture surface at 0.8% strain amplitude, showing localized alpha phase refinement.
summary: Representing the HT2 specimen at 0.8% strain, this inverse pole figure map illustrates the alpha phase refinement zones near the fracture surface. The fragmented alpha phase structures are clearly visible. Analysis confirms that these regions lack coherent micro-orientation patterns, reinforcing the conclusion that mechanical property gradients drive the crack deflection process.

caption: Normal atomic structure of the σ phase with inset schematics, where the rectangle outlines a unit cell stacked by four atomic layers (0, 1/4, 1/2, and 3/4) along the [001] σ direction.
summary: The σ phase exhibits a normal stacking sequence along the [001] σ direction, consisting of two primary layers (Z=0 and Z=1/2) and two structurally identical secondary layers (Z=1/4 and Z=3/4). This unit cell arrangement serves as the baseline for identifying the stacking disordering defects observed in the material.

caption: Deformation and stress distribution profiles observed in the tube cross-section following the press-fit process under varying groove geometry conditions.
summary: This panel illustrates the deformation and stress distribution within the tube cross-section after the press-fit process. Finite element simulation results reveal how different groove dimensions influence the final tube shape. Notably, specific conditions result in significant gaps between the mold and the deformed tube, highlighting the impact of groove geometry.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the strength-ductility product against fracture toughness for the LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA relative to various cast HEAs and additively manufactured steel, Ni, Al, and Ti alloys.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the performance landscape of the LPBF-fabricated AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA by benchmarking its strength-ductility product against fracture toughness. By comparing these mechanical properties with a wide range of cast HEAs and additively manufactured steel, Ni, Al, and Ti alloys, the figure highlights the material's unique mechanical property trade-offs.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectrum of commercial graphene quantum dots (GQDs) displaying the characteristic optical response of the nanomaterials.
summary: This UV–visible absorption spectrum characterizes the optical properties of commercial graphene quantum dots. As a key feature of these nanomaterials, the spectroscopic analysis provides insight into their electronic transitions. The data presented in this figure highlights the specific absorption behavior essential for evaluating the potential applications of these graphene-based quantum dots.

caption: J-integral components calculated along the lower boundary (Γ2) or the upper boundary (Γ4).
summary: Numerical values for the J-integral components along the horizontal boundaries Γ2 or Γ4 are shown here. These plots serve as a rigorous verification of the path-independence of the J-integral. The results demonstrate consistent behavior during the stable propagation phase, aligning with classical LEFM predictions for a homogeneous material.

caption: Evolution of cutting forces as a function of removed material for Colmonoy C56.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between cutting forces and the volume of removed material for Colmonoy C56. The data reveals a consistent and constant increase in the measured cutting force as the amount of removed material grows, indicating a progressive change in the machining resistance during the material removal process.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map for sample C90.
summary: Non-uniform color distributions in the KAM map for sample C90 indicate that high KAM values are localized at the grain boundaries. This structural feature highlights the influence of orientation on local strain distribution, demonstrating that C90 shares similar localized deformation characteristics with the C45 sample.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of alloy samples in PBS solution, showing the passive region and current density variations.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves for the alloy samples were obtained in PBS solution following a 1-hour OCP stabilization period. The results demonstrate variations in the passive current density (i pass) as a function of Ga-content. These trends are consistent with observations made within the passive region of the polarization curves, highlighting the electrochemical behavior of the alloys.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the mechanical (X1) M-DfX assessment framework applied to the energy infrastructure case study, specifically highlighting the modified weightings for individual properties within the power transformer component.
summary: This radar chart visualizes the mechanical (X1) M-DfX assessment framework tailored for energy infrastructure. It specifically details the modified weightings assigned to individual mechanical properties within the power transformer component. These adjustments reflect the specific design requirements and performance criteria necessary for evaluating the mechanical integrity of power transformer systems.

caption: SKPFM Volta potential difference map of the CoCrFeNiNb alloy ingot showing subtle contrast between the dendritic (FeCoCr)2Nb phase and the interdendritic FCC phase.
summary: This SKPFM Volta potential map of the CoCrFeNiNb alloy ingot reveals the surface potential distribution. A small difference in potentials is distinguishable between the dendritic (FeCoCr)2Nb phase and the interdendritic FCC phase, highlighting the local electrochemical variations present within the microstructure of this specific alloy composition.

caption: Local magnification of the cell walls from panel (a), highlighting the presence of alumina particles indicated by a blue box.
summary: Magnified view of the cell wall region reveals specific structural features, including the formation of alumina particles highlighted by a blue box. This local analysis confirms that dislocation density at the low-angle grain boundaries is significantly higher than in the gamma phase matrix, with no observed dislocation entanglement.

caption: Nano-hardness profile plotted against depth from the milling surface for DD5 specimens exposed to 900 °C.
summary: Nano-hardness values are measured at varying depths from the milling surface of DD5 superalloy specimens. This panel specifically illustrates the mechanical response of the SRX, CRX, and transition layers following thermal exposure at 900 °C, providing insight into the subsurface hardening behavior under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Inverse fast Fourier transform filtered image derived from the rectangular region in (a), showing the atomic arrangement and misfit dislocations marked by ellipses.
summary: Derived from the rectangular region in the HRTEM image, this inverse fast Fourier transform filtered image highlights the local atomic structure. Ellipses are used to mark the presence of misfit dislocations along the NiTi/Ni4Ti3 interface, illustrating the structural accommodation and strain relief mechanisms occurring at the phase boundary.

caption: ThermoCalc equilibrium phase diagram for the Nimolloy-202 alloy calculated using the TCNi11 database, illustrating the temperature-dependent evolution of phase volume fractions.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram for Nimolloy-202, generated via ThermoCalc with the TCNi11 database, maps phase stability against temperature. It predicts the precipitation of the L12-structured γ' phase at approximately 790 °C, reaching 20% volume fraction at 500 °C, alongside the formation of the D0a-structured Ni3Mo δ phase.

caption: Experimental configuration illustrating the ultrasonic transducer positioned parallel to the printing axis of the step gauge specimen.
summary: This schematic depicts the experimental setup for ultrasonic testing, where the transducer is oriented parallel to the printing axis of the step gauge. The gauge, designed in Solidworks, features a 20 x 20 mm testing surface, allowing for precise alignment during the evaluation of material properties across different thicknesses.

caption: (001), (011), and (111) pole figures derived from the EBSD orientation maps of sets A and B.
summary: These pole figures represent the crystallographic texture of sets A and B, derived from the EBSD maps. The (001), (011), and (111) projections quantify the preferred grain orientations, offering a comprehensive view of the texture evolution that results from the different processing conditions applied to each material set.

caption: LSV measurements for circular electrodes coated with Ni-NiZnFe4O4, illustrating performance variations among different circular geometry configurations.
summary: This panel illustrates the LSV performance of coated circular geometry electrodes. The C3 electrode exhibits superior performance, achieving a current density of -176.01 mA/cm2 at -1.96 V. In contrast, the C2 and C1 electrodes show lower current densities of -130.42 mA/cm2 and -71.04 mA/cm2, respectively, under identical testing conditions.

caption: Experimental setup of the WAAM system featuring a three-axis motion platform integrated with an EWM Tetrix 551 DC TIG welding machine.
summary: This panel displays the physical equipment used for the titanium alloy WAAM process. It highlights the three-axis motion platform and the EWM Tetrix 551 DC TIG welding machine, which are configured to follow a prescribed trajectory for the additive manufacturing process as described in the experimental setup.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram showing the end of the δ-to-γ transformation at 99 vol% γ-austenite, with dashed lines representing LPBF cooling profiles.
summary: The CCT diagram illustrates the completion of the δ-to-γ transformation, marked by the formation of 99 vol% γ-austenite. By comparing these curves against typical LPBF cooling rates (10^5 to 10^7 K/s), the figure provides insight into the final phase composition achieved during rapid solidification processes.

caption: Angular distribution of scattered rays at a monitoring wavelength of 450 nm, showing the deflection angle for four simulated rays across various dome and process parameters.
summary: This Monte Carlo simulation displays the angular distribution of scattered rays at a 450 nm monitoring wavelength. The data accounts for all determined dome and process parameters, revealing a distinct directional dependency of scattering related to the feed direction, which highlights the influence of optical schlieren on coaxial ray deflection.

caption: Relative permeability (μr) plotted as a function of temperature and varying magnetic field strengths.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of relative permeability with respect to temperature and magnetic field strength. The data demonstrates how the magnetic response of the material changes under different thermal and field conditions, providing a comprehensive overview of the permeability behavior across the investigated experimental parameters.

caption: Shrinkage evolution of 316L stainless steel samples plotted against sintering temperature.
summary: This panel illustrates the shrinkage behavior of 316L stainless steel as a function of sintering temperature. The data demonstrates the dimensional changes occurring during the thermal processing stage, confirming the successful application of the fabrication method and co-sintering process for this specific material composition.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of MC3T3-E1 cells on composite scaffolds after 24 hours, stained with Calcein-AM (green, live) and PI (red, dead).
summary: Live/dead cell assay images reveal the distribution and viability of MC3T3-E1 cells on composite scaffolds after 24 hours. Green fluorescence indicates live cells, while red indicates dead cells. Observations show that dead cells are rarely found, and TM/HA/PLCL scaffolds support a larger number of live cells compared to the HA/PLCL control group.

caption: Arrhenius plot representing the temperature dependence of the Ni self-diffusion coefficient in dilute Ni-Al alloys with impurity concentrations ranging from 0 to 1 at.%.
summary: Temperature dependence of the Ni self-diffusion coefficient in Ni-Al alloys is illustrated for concentrations up to 1 at.%. Aluminum exhibits a minor effect on solvent diffusion, similar to silicon, because the resulting vacancy-impurity pairs are difficult to form and lack significant mobility, limiting their impact on the overall diffusion process.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the solution-treated specimen showing a homogeneous distribution of elements within the nickel-rich gamma matrix.
summary: The solution-treated specimen reconstruction reveals a homogeneous distribution of all elements within the gamma-matrix. No indications of precipitation are detected in this state, confirming the effectiveness of the solution treatment in maintaining a solid solution before the subsequent ageing processes are applied to the material.

caption: STEM-BF image of the LoHT SSP + A series surface region displaying a nanocrystalline layer.
summary: Nanocrystalline layer formation is evident in the surface region of the LoHT SSP + A series. This refined microstructure is characteristic of the surface treatment applied to the alloy. The structural features observed here are consistent with the surface modification seen in the LoHT A + SSP series.

caption: Chemical composition table for the FGH4097 superalloy.
summary: Chemical composition data for the FGH4097 superalloy is presented in this table. It provides the quantitative breakdown of the constituent elements, serving as a reference for the elemental mapping results and supporting the overall characterization of the alloy's material properties and phase formation behavior.

caption: Radar plot illustrating the comparative mechanical performance of different lattice structures, specifically highlighting the specific elastic modulus and specific yield strength.
summary: Mechanical properties of the various lattice structures are visualized in this radar plot, which maps key performance metrics including specific elastic modulus and specific yield strength. The plot facilitates a direct comparison between the HBCC design and other structures, emphasizing the geometry-dominated nature of the elastic response relative to plastic deformation.

caption: FTIR spectra of 3D printed 94% alumina samples across various thermal post-processing stages, including groups AP, PC, D6, D11, and S.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy tracks the removal of solvent and the thermal degradation of the photopolymer binder within 3D printed alumina suspensions. The spectra for groups AP, PC, D6, D11, and S demonstrate that the binder is effectively burnt out after debinding at 600 °C, with subsequent spectra showing minimal further chemical changes.

caption: Filament toughness values across various ASA recycling courses alongside a representative photograph of the filament testing procedure.
summary: This panel displays the filament toughness results obtained from multiple ASA recycling courses. It includes a quantitative assessment of the material's toughness performance and provides a visual representation of the experimental setup used during the filament testing process to evaluate the mechanical integrity of the recycled ASA samples.

caption: Deconvoluted Ni 2p XPS spectra for various Bi2-xNixSe3 sample compositions.
summary: Deconvoluted XPS spectra for Ni are shown in Fig. 3(b). These measurements were conducted to further confirm the evolution of surface states at room temperature with increasing Ni content in the Bi2-xNixSe3 samples. The spectra provide detailed information regarding the chemical state of nickel within the material structure.

caption: Microstructural analysis of ETi64 alloy showing the distribution of dark-contrast pores within the metallic matrix.
summary: This optical micrograph provides a detailed view of the ETi64 alloy microstructure, specifically highlighting the presence and spatial distribution of dark-contrast pores. By examining these features, researchers can characterize the porosity within the material, which is essential for understanding the structural integrity and performance of the alloy under various conditions.

caption: Uniaxial and torsional cyclic loading S–N curves displaying experimental data points alongside estimated regression lines bounded by a 95% scatter band T.
summary: This plot illustrates the S–N curves derived from uniaxial and torsional cyclic loading experiments. The regression lines are bounded by a scatter band T (0.95), which successfully encompasses 95% of the experimental data. The estimated fatigue limit and its associated scatter demonstrate strong agreement with experimental points outside the regression line.

caption: SEM-EBSD band contrast image of the hot17.5 sample depicting the underlying microstructure.
summary: SEM-EBSD band contrast imaging of the hot17.5 sample reveals the underlying microstructure. This technique complements secondary electron observations by providing crystallographic information, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of the material's structural state following the hot processing condition, which is essential for understanding the resulting mechanical properties and grain characteristics.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the uncrosslinked composite mixture containing nano-HA, Gel, and CMC components.
summary: This FTIR spectrum characterizes the chemical composition of the composite mixture prior to the crosslinking process. It displays the characteristic peaks associated with nano-HA, Gel, and CMC, providing a baseline for identifying the functional groups present in the 3D-printed bone scaffold material before structural modification occurs.

caption: Interaction surface showing elastic stiffness as a function of curvature and thickness at a constant width of 6 mm.
summary: Elastic stiffness results are presented as an interaction surface where curvature and thickness are varied while width remains constant at 6 mm. The data indicates that stiffness increases strongly with thickness and more moderately with curvature, exhibiting evident surface curvature that is consistent with the significance of quadratic thickness effects.

caption: Boxplot illustrating the measured angle deviation α dev. relative to the nominal angle α nom. across various overhang lengths, angles, and thicknesses.
summary: This boxplot summarizes the measurement results for angle deviation, grouped by strut thickness and nominal angle. The data demonstrates the influence of these parameters on sag, confirming that increasing the nominal angle from the horizontal reference plane leads to a reduction in sag across the tested overhang configurations.

caption: Confocal microscopy imaging of the AB specimen surface, highlighting the captured valley features.
summary: Confocal microscopy is employed here to image the surface of the AB specimen. By selecting the same specific area as the XCT scan, this panel allows for a direct comparison of the efficiency and resolution of confocal microscopy in detecting surface valleys compared to XCT.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) response of the Ni-NiZnFe4O4 coated triangular electrode, detailing its electrochemical behavior.
summary: The electrochemical characteristics of the Ni-NiZnFe4O4 coated triangular electrode are analyzed using cyclic voltammetry. This CV plot provides a detailed view of the electrochemical response, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of the coated triangular electrode's performance and behavior during the hydrogen evolution reaction process.

caption: Close-up STEM view of the crack tip region, further illustrating the parallel slip traces and shear band formation on the left flank of the crack.
summary: This high-magnification STEM view focuses on the crack tip area, emphasizing the parallel slip traces that characterize the left side of the crack. These nanometric shear bands are consistent with the localized deformation observed in the adjacent region, highlighting the specific microstructural response of the material during fracture.

caption: Signal intensity comparison of IRMM-2022 uranium solution isotopes across unnotched and notched filter settings, with a water blank control.
summary: This mass spectrum displays the signal intensity of IRMM-2022 uranium solution isotopes. Applying a notch filter at m/z 241 significantly alters the signal response compared to unnotched conditions. Specifically, the 238U signal drops to approximately 8% of its original value, while the 235U signal decreases to roughly 37% of its initial intensity.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic entropy change profiles for four distinct powder samples measured under a constant applied magnetic field of 1.5 T.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic entropy change as a function of temperature for four different powder samples under an applied field of 1.5 T. The data provides a comparative analysis of the magnetocaloric response across the studied materials, highlighting how the magnetic entropy varies with temperature for each specific powder composition.

caption: Phase diagram calculation for the Al–7Si–4Cu–1Ni alloy modified with 0.50 wt% Mg and 0.25 wt% Mn.
summary: Shown here is the calculated phase diagram for the Al–7Si–4Cu–1Ni alloy with 0.50 wt% Mg and 0.25 wt% Mn.
