This diagram provides insight into the solidification phases and equilibrium conditions established by this specific combination of magnesium and manganese concentrations within the alloy system.

caption: Performance evaluation of the artificial backpropagation network for scenario-3, illustrating the velocity distribution (U) of ternary PGW fluid as influenced by variations in the electroosmotic parameter (Me).
summary: This panel displays the performance outcomes of an artificial backpropagation network applied to scenario-3. It specifically explores how variations in the electroosmotic parameter (Me) influence the velocity distribution (U) of ternary PGW fluid. The results provide a detailed look at the network's predictive capability regarding fluid motion under these specific conditions.

caption: IFFT image of the (10 11 ¯ ) crystal plane for the Ni5(Gd,Dy) phase.
summary: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) analysis of the (10 11 ¯ ) crystal plane for the Ni5(Gd,Dy) phase is shown. This visualization allows for the clear observation of the lattice structure associated with this specific plane, contributing to the comprehensive crystallographic characterization of the Ni5(Gd,Dy) precipitate.

caption: Indentation modulus orientation dependence for various aramid fibers including Kevlar29, Kevlar49, Kevlar119, and Kevlar129, showing experimental results versus VN-calculated predictions.
summary: This panel displays the orientation-dependent indentation modulus for a series of aramid fibers, specifically Kevlar29, Kevlar49, Kevlar119, and Kevlar129. The plot highlights the relationship between fiber orientation and mechanical modulus, contrasting experimental data points with solid lines derived from VN-calculated models to evaluate the performance of different aramid grades.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module, illustrating the relationship between power output and voltage under different environmental conditions as modeled by the PEC2 approach.
summary: Panel b presents the P-V characteristics for the mSi0188 solar module, highlighting the power output variations across different insolation and temperature levels. By comparing rescaled experimental values with the PEC2 model, the plot demonstrates the module's power extraction efficiency and the reliability of the PEC2 model for photovoltaic analysis.

caption: Laser confocal microscopy image illustrating the micro-scale surface waviness of a structure fabricated via a 3D weaving path.
summary: This laser confocal microscopy image provides a detailed visualization of the surface topography of a structure produced using a 3D weaving path. The technique effectively captures the micro-scale waviness inherent in the fabricated geometry, highlighting the structural characteristics resulting from the specific 3D weaving manufacturing process employed.

caption: Atomic models illustrating the three low-index surface structures of TiB2 and the hexagonal close-packed stacking sequences at the (111) Al // (0001) TiB2 interface.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configurations for three low-index surface structures of TiB2. It further highlights the hexagonal close-packed stacking sequences characteristic of the (111) Al // (0001) TiB2 interface. These structural models are essential for understanding the crystallographic matching and nucleation potency of the nucleant particles within the system.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating curve of the AF sample recorded at a heating rate of 20 K/min.
summary: This differential scanning calorimetry heating curve illustrates the thermal behavior of the AF sample when subjected to a heating rate of 20 K/min. The data provided in this plot serves to support the proposed mechanism for the material, offering insight into its thermal transitions and phase characteristics during heating.

caption: Arrhenius plot comparing the transition kinetics parameter k t, derived from nine isothermal experiments, against the model's proposed Arrhenius law.
summary: This plot compares experimental values of the transition kinetics parameter k t with the Arrhenius law proposed in the model. The global evolution of the data points follows the Arrhenius relationship across the entire temperature range studied, validating the model's approach for describing this specific kinetic parameter.

caption: Distribution of scientific articles categorized by 3D molding techniques applied to cellulose, showing the dominance of conventional wet molding.
summary: This pie chart displays the distribution of scientific publications regarding 3D molding techniques for cellulose over the last 20 years. Although only 14% of total cellulose research addresses molding, conventional wet molding accounts for 74% of this specific subset, indicating its prevalence across various application fields in material science.

caption: Neutron powder diffraction patterns of AQ and ORD samples at 400 K, compared alongside full order and full disorder simulation patterns.
summary: Neutron powder diffraction patterns for AQ and ORD samples in the L21 austenite phase are presented at 400 K. The plot includes simulated patterns for full order and full disorder states. Y-axes are scaled to normalize the height of the [222] B2 peak for direct comparison of structural features.

caption: Box plot showing the kurtosis (Sku) of surface height distributions for each contour theme, confirming statistically significant differences.
summary: This box plot represents the kurtosis (Sku) parameter for various contour themes. ANOVA results indicate a p-value less than 0.05, signifying statistically significant differences in the mean values. The wide scatter in measurements for individual themes suggests that multiple factors beyond contour themes affect the final surface roughness.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms illustrating the cathodic current response during negative scanning from the open circuit potential under varying ultrasonic amplitudes.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves demonstrate the electrochemical behavior of the system. Under static conditions, the cathodic current rises sharply during negative scanning from the open circuit potential, which indicates the reduction of Cu2+ ions. The application of varying ultrasonic amplitudes further validates these electrochemical findings during the scanning process.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the deposited metal specimen processed at a travel speed of 150 mm/min.
summary: Cross-sectional observation of the deposited metal specimen processed at a travel speed of 150 mm/min reveals the internal pore structure. As indicated by the reference, increasing the electric arc travel speed leads to a reduction in both the size and volume fraction of pores within the deposited material.

caption: Damping factor variations for 100% infilled coupons after 10 cycles of 72 h aging.
summary: Panel e highlights the damping factor response for 100% infilled coupons subjected to 10 cycles of 72 h cryogenic aging. While overall variations are small, these specific coupons exhibit more pronounced decreases in the damping factor compared to other conditions, reflecting the impact of the extended cryogenic exposure duration.

caption: Dilatometry-derived on-cooling dilatation curves for 410 stainless steel subjected to 0–10 thermal cycles within the austenite phase field, illustrating that the martensite start temperature (Ms) remains unaffected by the cycling process.
summary: Dilatometry experiments were performed to evaluate the impact of thermal cycling on the martensite start temperature. By comparing dilatation curves across zero to ten cycles within the austenite phase field, the results demonstrate that repeated thermal cycling does not cause a reduction in the Ms temperature for this material.

caption: SHAP summary plot displaying the feature influence and correlation direction on the compressive strength (CS) output, highlighting the specific impact of parameters such as water content (W).
summary: This SHAP summary plot illustrates the influence of various features on the compressive strength output. It provides a clear visualization of the correlation direction between input parameters and CS. Notably, the plot reveals the significant impact of water content on the model predictions, confirming its role as a key feature.

caption: Load versus displacement response comparing the elastic-plastic-damage micro-mechanics model and the macro-mechanics model for a cantilever beam composed of NEOV-s with 25% relative density.
summary: This plot illustrates the load-displacement behavior of a 25% relative density NEOV-s cantilever beam. It compares results from micro-mechanics and macro-mechanics models, demonstrating a very good match between the two approaches. The curves characterize the elastic-plastic-damage response of the structure under mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Relative elongation (Δl) plotted as a function of temperature for Alloy 625+TiB2 composites.
summary: This panel displays the dilatation curves for Alloy 625+TiB2 composites, illustrating the relative elongation (Δl) as a function of temperature. These measurements provide essential data on the thermal expansion behavior of the composite materials, serving as the basis for determining the linear coefficient of thermal expansion across the tested temperature range.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve for the GBDT model evaluated on the withheld test dataset, corresponding to a defect diameter of 200 µm.
summary: This ROC curve illustrates the detection performance of the GBDT model on the withheld test dataset. The model was trained and validated on the combined builds dataset, specifically targeting defects with an equivalent spherical diameter of 200 µm to assess classification accuracy at this specific porosity threshold.

caption: Diamond unit cell geometry utilized for the lattice structure.
summary: A diamond unit cell is employed to construct the lattice, providing a consistent inclination of the struts relative to the build plate. This specific unit cell geometry is critical for maintaining manufacturing consistency across the scaffold, ensuring that the structural integrity and density are uniform throughout the produced test specimens.

caption: Raman spectroscopic analysis performed on the post-test SOFC anode to characterize structural changes or carbon deposition.
summary: Raman analysis provides critical insights into the chemical state and potential carbonaceous species present on the SOFC anode surface following the 30-hour electrochemical test. This spectroscopic data complements the electrochemical measurements by identifying the surface composition and structural integrity of the anode material after exposure to methane fuel.

caption: Live/dead fluorescence microscopy images of encapsulated HDFs, demonstrating high cell viability within the hydrogel matrix at a scale of 200 μm.
summary: Live/dead assay images confirm high cell viability for HDFs encapsulated within the cfGel-Hydrogels. These observations substantiate the metabolic activity findings, revealing that the cells remain viable within the 3D environment, with more pronounced spreading behavior observed in the 5 wt% and 7.5 wt% hydrogels compared to the 10 wt% concentration.

caption: Macroscopic deformation evolution of four NiTi porous scaffolds during quasi-static compression, with red arrows indicating the progressive deformation of the first three layers in the cubic unit cell.
summary: This panel displays the macroscopic deformation evolution of four NiTi porous scaffolds under various compressive strains. Red arrows highlight the deformation of the first three layers in the cubic unit cell. Multi-layer overlapping is discernible in gyroid and uniform structures at 22% strain, while longitudinal elongation remains minimal during the compression process.

caption: Radar chart comparing the performance characteristics of various anode materials.
summary: A radar chart is utilized to visualize and compare the multi-faceted performance characteristics of different anode materials. This representation allows for a comprehensive overview of how the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film electrode performs across several key metrics relative to other candidate materials in the study.

caption: Trajectory of spatters under GD-L conditions, where color indicates the velocity of individual particles.
summary: Visualizing spatter trajectories under GD-L, this panel shows particles following near-parabolic or free-fall paths. The color-coded trajectories represent the speed of the spatters, illustrating how the horizontal intercept changes as particles move through the air during the linear energy density process.

caption: Creep rupture time versus stress for notched DD6 superalloy specimens, showing the logarithmic linear fitting curves.
summary: Creep rupture time is plotted against stress for notched DD6 superalloy specimens using a double logarithmic scale. For specimens with a stress concentration factor of Kt = 3, the slope of the creep rupture time in corrosion environments is observed to be slightly greater than that in air.

caption: Rate performance comparison of lithium-sulfur batteries with different interlayers (PP, CCC, and ZnS@CCC) at current densities ranging from 0.1C to 4C.
summary: This plot illustrates the rate performance of lithium-sulfur batteries using different interlayers. By comparing PP, CCC, and ZnS@CCC configurations across a range of 0.1C to 4C, the data demonstrates the modification effect of the ZnS@CCC interlayer on battery performance under varying discharge-charge rates.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Ni and Ni-based alloy nanowire electrodes, including Ni (green), Ni–Co (red), Ni–Zn (blue), and Ni–W (black), measured within a potential range of -0.035 V to 1.265 V vs. RHE.
summary: This figure displays cyclic voltammogram curves comparing pure Ni nanowires with Ni–Co, Ni–Zn, and Ni–W alloy nanowire electrodes. The electrochemical performance is evaluated across a potential window from -0.035 V to 1.265 V vs. RHE, highlighting the distinct electrochemical responses of the different alloy compositions relative to pure Ni.

caption: Load-displacement curves for the directionally solidified (DS) alloy, highlighting phase-specific indentation responses.
summary: Load-depth curves for the directionally solidified alloy reveal unique mechanical behavior compared to other routes. Unlike the SC and NSF samples, heat treatment in the DS alloy leads to a reduction in hardness for the intermetallic phases, with Mg2Si hardness decreasing from 3.10 to 2.08 GPa after the treatment.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of L-PBF-processed CuCrZr + 15 wt% 316L, showing grain orientation along the build direction with a red square highlighting a bimodal region.
summary: The IPF map reveals the microstructure of CuCrZr + 15 wt% 316L, where the addition of 316L induces a finer grain structure compared to pure CuCrZr. A bimodal region, highlighted by a red square, indicates the transformation of elongated grains into a more refined morphology with a weakened <110> texture.

caption: Storage modulus versus temperature for feedstocks containing PMMA and higher PEG content.
summary: This plot illustrates the storage modulus of feedstocks modified with PMMA and increased PEG content. The results demonstrate that these additions significantly increase the storage modulus compared to the PMMA-free variants. This thermal analysis highlights the impact of composition on the mechanical stiffness of the polymer filaments across temperature sweeps.

caption: Pearson correlation heatmap of plasma spectral features, indicating a lack of significant correlation between background spectral mean and elemental peak intensities.
summary: The Pearson correlation heatmap for plasma spectral features shows that the background spectral mean does not correlate significantly with peak intensities of elements like Cr, Fe, Mn, and Ni, nor with their corresponding line spectral FWHM. This suggests that background noise is independent of the primary elemental spectral signatures.

caption: Temporal thermal image sequences of the melt pool captured at 20 μs exposure time for three distinct processing conditions (P=200W/V=0.9m/s, P=350W/V=1.2m/s, and P=250W/V=0.3m/s), processed with a 220 μs moving average window.
summary: Thermal imaging sequences demonstrate the melt pool evolution under varying laser power and velocity parameters. Applying a 220 μs moving average window reveals that the core melt pool structure remains stable over time, while thermal variations are primarily localized to the lower temperature fringes of the surface image.

caption: Co-Ni phase diagram with extrapolation to 60 °C, indicating the two-phase region.
summary: This phase diagram of Co-Ni, extrapolated to 60 °C, indicates that the HCP and FCC phases should coexist only in the range of 26.5 at% to 35 at% Ni. This theoretical framework helps explain the observed differences in morphologies and sizes due to the different growth kinetics of the alloys.

caption: Experimental setup of the Brookfield rheometer featuring a 20 mm by 10 mm vane spindle used for characterizing the rheological properties of freshly mixed geopolymer.
summary: This figure illustrates the experimental configuration of a Brookfield rheometer equipped with a 20 mm by 10 mm vane spindle. This setup is specifically utilized to assess the rheological properties of freshly mixed geopolymer samples, providing a standardized method for evaluating the flow behavior and consistency of the material.

caption: Creep strain evolution for the HT75(2h) specimen throughout the loading and unloading cycles at a holding stress of 10 MPa.
summary: Depicted here is the creep strain profile for the HT75(2h) specimen under a holding stress of 10 MPa. The graph tracks the material's deformation during the loading and unloading phases, highlighting the specific mechanical response of this heat-treated condition compared to other crystallinity levels during the creep test.

caption: TGA mass loss and DTG mass loss rate curves for a hydrated OPC paste, illustrating four distinct temperature-dependent decomposition ranges used for hydration assessment.
summary: This figure displays TGA and DTG curves for a hydrated OPC paste, highlighting four specific temperature regions used for hydration assessment. These curves provide a quantitative basis for calculating mass loss, with the distinct decomposition ranges clearly marked to facilitate the analysis of the OPC-based material's hydration state.

caption: Temperature-programmed reduction (TPR) profiles monitoring the m/z 18 signal for catalysts synthesized via 390 s of electrodeposition, recorded under a 5% H2/Ar atmosphere with a 10 °C/min heating rate.
summary: This TPR profile, obtained under a 5% H2/Ar gas mixture at a heating rate of 10 °C/min, tracks the m/z 18 signal to characterize catalysts prepared by 390 s of electrodeposition. The results provide essential insights into the reduction behavior and surface properties of the electrodeposited catalytic materials.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the SiO2:TiO2-glass, demonstrating an amorphous nature.
summary: The amorphous nature of the SiO2:TiO2-glass was confirmed through XRD analysis. The diffraction pattern shows no sharp crystalline peaks, indicating that the glass maintains an amorphous structure, which is consistent with the desired material properties for the investigated resin system.

caption: Backscattered electron (BSE) image of the Ti48Al alloy in the YZ plane, highlighting the phase morphology.
summary: This BSE image of the Ti48Al alloy in the YZ plane reveals distinct phase contrasts. The gamma phase appears as dark gray regions, while the alpha-2 phase is visible as gray lamellae. These features provide a clear morphological distinction between the constituent phases within the alloy microstructure.

caption: Schematic representation of the wire arc directed energy deposition (DED) system, featuring a custom-built CNC machine integrated with a gas metal arc welding (GMAW) unit.
summary: This panel illustrates the experimental configuration for the wire arc DED process. It highlights the integration of a custom-built CNC machine with a GMAW unit, providing a clear overview of the hardware setup used to conduct the deposition process as described in the experimental methodology.

caption: Tafel polarization curves obtained from potentiometric electrochemical testing for the produced hybrid nanocomposite samples.
summary: Tafel curves derived from potentiometric electrochemical tests are presented for the produced samples. These polarization curves provide the electrochemical foundation for evaluating the corrosion behavior of the hybrid nanocomposites, serving as the primary data source for subsequent analysis of corrosion current density and overall corrosion rates across different processing conditions.

caption: Schematic representation illustrating the classification of additive manufacturing technologies based on the interplay between material type, material form, and the specific activation energy source applied during the fabrication process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the diverse landscape of additive manufacturing technologies. It categorizes these processes by mapping the relationships between material types, their physical forms, and the activation energy required for consolidation. The figure serves as a conceptual framework for understanding how these variables dictate the specific additive manufacturing technology employed.

caption: Ternary plot showing the elastic energy distribution for the Fe-Mn-Co system, where the local maximum elastic energy is observed along the Mn-Co axes at approximately 50 at.% Mn.
summary: Representing the Fe-Mn-Co system, this ternary diagram highlights the elastic energy vicinity at a 50:50 Fe-Mn base. The local maximum elastic energy is identified along the Mn-Co axes at roughly 50 at.% Mn. Co addition demonstrates a relatively small impact on the overall elastic energy of the system.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) results for the PEEK filament, displaying the first and second heating cycles alongside a single cooling cycle.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) results for the PEEK filament are presented, encompassing the first and second heating cycles as well as a single cooling cycle. These thermal profiles provide essential data regarding the phase transition characteristics and thermal history of the PEEK material during the specified heating and cooling processes.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of Live/Dead stained BMSCs and HUVECs after 3 days of culture, showing high cell viability with green-stained live cells and minimal red-stained dead cells.
summary: Live/Dead staining analysis confirms high cell survival rates across the BHP/G@Met, BHP, and G@Met scaffold groups. The fluorescence images reveal a predominance of green fluorescence, indicating viable cells, with minimal red fluorescence, demonstrating that the composite scaffolds support healthy cell growth and maintain high biocompatibility after 3 days.

caption: Mean squared displacement (MSD) profiles for Ni, Al, and Re atomic species in the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al slab during tensile deformation at 1373 K.
summary: The MSD of Ni, Al, and Re atoms is plotted to quantify atomic mobility within the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al slab during tensile testing at 1373 K. These results, which align with trends observed in other modes, demonstrate the relative diffusion rates and dynamic behavior of individual atomic species under applied mechanical strain.

caption: Microtomography cross-sectional images comparing unidirectional (UD) 45° and bidirectional (MD) 45°/135° fiber-reinforced composite samples.
summary: Microtomography images illustrate the internal structural arrangement of unidirectional and bidirectional composite samples. These images provide a comparative view of the fiber orientation and distribution within the PA matrix for UD 45° and MD 45°/135° type specimens, highlighting the distinct architectural differences between the two composite configurations.

caption: Tabular data detailing colony identification numbers and their respective orientations within the MIAM.
summary: This table provides the identification numbers and crystallographic orientations for the 12 nano-colonies present in the MIAM. It serves as a reference for the structural parameters used in the simulation, ensuring that the mechanical analysis accounts for the specific orientation of each colony within the model.

caption: Deformation mechanism and y-displacement fringe patterns for a 5 × 5 × 3 asymmetric cell configuration at global crushing strains of 0.1, 0.3, and 0.6.
summary: Displayed is the deformation mechanism and y-displacement fringe patterns for a 5 × 5 × 3 asymmetric cell configuration. The panel captures the structural response at global crushing strains of 0.1, 0.3, and 0.6, illustrating the mechanical evolution of this thicker asymmetric cell arrangement during the crushing test.

caption: Statistical distribution of Young's modulus deviations from the mean, calculated as 100(E - Emean)/Emean, presented as boxplots with superimposed swarm plots for randomly sampled patches.
summary: This panel displays the statistical spread of Young's modulus values derived from simulated randomly sampled patches. By plotting the percentage deviation from the mean, the graph illustrates the variability in mechanical stiffness. Superimposed swarm plots provide a detailed view of individual data points alongside the aggregate boxplot distribution statistics.

caption: Iron elemental distribution map for Alloy C, showing the Fe distribution within the ferritic matrix.
summary: The iron elemental map for Alloy C illustrates the distribution of Fe within the ferritic matrix. This data is used to assess the chemical homogeneity of the alloy and to identify any depletion zones that may be associated with the formation of carbides during the heat treatment process.

caption: Isothermal transformation (TTT) curve simulation for the Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy system generated via JMatPro software.
summary: The isothermal transformation (TTT) curve simulation provides a predictive model for the phase transformation kinetics of the Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy system. By utilizing JMatPro software, this diagram maps the time-temperature-transformation behavior, which is essential for understanding the precipitation kinetics and optimizing heat treatment processes for this specific aluminum alloy composition.

caption: Detailed geometric dimensions and configuration of the tensile test specimens used for mechanical property evaluation.
summary: The diagram displays the standardized dimensions and geometry of the tensile test specimens. These specifications ensure consistency in mechanical testing, allowing for accurate determination of material properties. The design is directly linked to the sampling strategy shown in panel (a), facilitating a systematic approach to material characterization.

caption: Isofield magnetization (M-T) curves recorded at 0.02 T for as-extracted and bamboo-grained microwires, featuring insets of the first derivative of the magnetization curves and highlighting a sharp peak in the as-extracted sample related to internal stress.
summary: Isofield magnetization curves at 0.02 T demonstrate that bamboo-grained microwires exhibit significantly enhanced magnetic properties compared to as-extracted ones. The first derivative insets reveal fluctuation features during MT transformation, while a sharp peak in the as-extracted curve indicates high internal stress anisotropy resulting from the rapid solidification process.

caption: Line-out profiles of total elastic strain, incompatible distortion, stress, and maximum resolved shear stress across high angle grain boundaries (B-B’), characterizing the mechanical response at these interfaces.
summary: This panel presents the mechanical response across high angle grain boundaries B-B’. By evaluating total elastic strain, incompatible distortion, and stress components, the plot illustrates how these boundaries influence the distribution of resolved shear stress and strain heterogeneity within the microstructure during the macroscopic loading process.

caption: Reduction of area as a function of hydrogen pressure for conventional and hollow specimens, showing an exponential growth trend.
summary: The reduction of area is presented against hydrogen pressure for both conventional and hollow specimens, utilizing an exponential growth function fit. Observations indicate that the hollow specimens tested in air demonstrate a lower reduction of area value compared to the conventional specimens tested under the same atmospheric conditions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of EPCs identified via dual staining with FITC-UEA-l and Dil-ac-LDL.
summary: EPCs were successfully identified through specific immunofluorescence staining techniques. The use of FITC-UEA-l and Dil-ac-LDL markers allowed for the clear visualization and verification of the extracted endothelial progenitor cells, confirming their identity as part of the successful extraction process described in the study.

caption: Elemental distribution map of molybdenum within the DAZ region.
summary: Elemental distribution map of molybdenum within the DAZ region. This map highlights the spatial arrangement of molybdenum atoms, offering a detailed view of its distribution across the microstructure. By comparing this map with the HAADF-STEM image, the specific localization of molybdenum within the DAZ is clearly identified.

caption: Recoverable strain relative to VED for a 200 MPa stress level, illustrating the sensitivity of actuation to laser power, scanning speed, and hatch space.
summary: This plot presents the recoverable strain at a 200 MPa stress level as a function of VED. It highlights how variations in laser power, scanning speed, and hatch space affect the material's transformation behavior. The black anchor point provides a clear reference for the impact of these specific processing parameters.

caption: STEM image of the alloy aged for 50 h, showing γ' precipitates and a central needle-like precipitate imaged along the [001] matrix axis.
summary: STEM imaging of the sample aged for 50 h illustrates the presence of γ' precipitates alongside a needle-like precipitate located in the center of the micrograph. The image is captured along the [001] axis of the matrix, providing detailed structural information regarding the precipitate morphology and distribution.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing hydrogen diffusivity as a function of inverse temperature for a GB-free Fe-Ni-Cr alloy, measured normal to the composition gradient.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays hydrogen diffusivity in a GB-free Fe-Ni-Cr alloy measured normal to the composition gradient. Observations indicate that composition nonuniformity does not significantly affect hydrogen diffusivity in this direction. All plotted data points exhibit a consistent activation energy barrier of approximately 0.64 eV across the temperature range.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF-Z) map of as-printed LPBF copper showing a fine, heterogeneous microstructure with weak overall texture.
summary: The as-printed LPBF copper microstructure is characterized by a fine and heterogeneous grain structure, as visualized through EBSD IPF-Z mapping. The analysis reveals that the material exhibits a weak overall texture and high local misorientation, reflecting the rapid solidification conditions inherent to the laser powder bed fusion manufacturing process.

caption: Performance evaluation of the PEK-TD3 algorithm demonstrating its capability to enforce transmission line constraints during practical application scenarios.
summary: This figure illustrates the effectiveness of the PEK-TD3 algorithm in maintaining transmission line constraints. The results demonstrate that the algorithm successfully enforces these constraints across most practical scenarios, confirming its robustness and reliability when applied in real-world operational environments as shown in the performance evaluation data.

caption: Initial state of GH4169 grains showing comparatively flat grain boundaries before deformation.
summary: This panel displays the initial state of GH4169 grains, highlighting the comparatively flat grain boundaries observed before the application of micro-strain. The visualization focuses on the structural arrangement of unit cells within the material, providing a baseline for analyzing subsequent grain deformation and evolution during the mechanical loading process.

caption: Atomic configuration of the (111) γ' atomic layer, representing the phase interface counterpart.
summary: The (111) γ' atomic layer is shown as the counterpart for the interface analysis. TEM results did not conclusively clarify which of the μ phase layers matched this specific γ' layer, necessitating a comparative analysis based on symmetry and atomic distance to determine the most likely interface configuration.

caption: Binary Fe–Cu phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic miscibility gap that governs the liquid phase separation observed at the interface.
summary: The binary Fe-Cu phase diagram highlights the metastable miscibility gap that thermodynamically governs the liquid phase separation observed in the joint. This diagram provides the theoretical basis for the sharp interface and steep compositional gradient identified in the bright-field TEM analysis of the Fe-Cu junction.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the percentage of cell viability for PLA, PLA/nHA.1, PLA/nHA.2, and PLA/nHA.3 scaffolds, with error bars representing the standard deviation of the measurements.
summary: This bar chart presents the cell viability analysis results for PLA and various PLA/nHA composite scaffolds. The graph displays the percentage of viable cells for each material composition, with error bars indicating the standard deviation. These results provide a comparative assessment of the biocompatibility of the different scaffold formulations tested.

caption: Scattered box-plot representing the distribution of drug w/w% in AI-generated formulations for Models 10–27, showing an API range of 0.57 to 100 w/w% with a mean of 5.79 w/w%.
summary: This scattered box-plot visualizes the API content distribution for AI-generated formulations produced by Models 10–27. The API amounts span from 0.57 to 100 w/w%, with a calculated mean value of 5.79 w/w%. These results demonstrate the evaluation of AI-generated formulations regarding their realism and formulation space.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure map of the 316L stainless steel AB zone, oriented parallel to the build direction.
summary: This Inverse Pole Figure map displays the crystallographic orientation of the 316L stainless steel sample in the as-built (AB) zone, located 6 mm below the top surface. The orientation is mapped parallel to the build direction, providing a baseline for the initial microstructural state before any subsequent thermal treatment or rescanning processes.

caption: Final state of the deposition layer after removal of the laser source.
summary: This panel presents the final state of the SLM simulation after the laser source has been removed. The atoms within the deposition layer have undergone uniform rearrangement, reflecting the completed melting and solidification process. The color-coded atomic heights demonstrate the final morphology of the processed material.

caption: B-H hysteresis loop comparison across different strain levels at a large applied field of 1500 A/m.
summary: Shown are B-H loops at 1500 A/m. Under this large applied field, the maximum magnetic induction of the 14% strain sample drops to 30.1% of the 0% strain sample, highlighting that the impact of strain on the B-H curve is more pronounced at higher external field strengths.

caption: Box plot presenting the bending test data obtained from HAp specimens.
summary: This box plot illustrates the bending test results for HAp specimens, highlighting the variability and range of the mechanical data. As referenced in the study, this plot allows for a direct assessment of the HAp material's performance characteristics under bending conditions compared to the ZrO2 results.

caption: Atomic arrangement at 700 K, displaying partial ordering of the matrix alongside the established B2-ordered regions.
summary: At 700 K, the matrix undergoes partial ordering, as observed in the lower section of the snapshot. This state represents the progression toward a B2 + L21 two-phase field. The Monte Carlo simulation results effectively capture the temperature-dependent evolution of ordering reactions within the Cu-Al-Ni alloy system.

caption: Ti-rich corner of the assumed Ti–Au–Mo ternary phase diagram, constructed by integrating the Au–Ti and Mo–Ti binary phase diagrams, with marked compositions of the fabricated alloy samples.
summary: This ternary phase diagram illustrates the Ti-rich corner of the Ti–Au–Mo system, synthesized from established Au–Ti and Mo–Ti binary phase data. The plot serves as a foundational reference for the study, explicitly mapping the specific chemical compositions of the various alloys fabricated and analyzed throughout the research.

caption: Optical micrograph of the V1 sample showing the molten pool morphology.
summary: Optical micrograph of the V1 sample showing the molten pool morphology. This image provides visual evidence of the solidification interface shape, which serves as a basis for validating finite element analysis results regarding molten pool geometry changes observed during the experimental process.

caption: Polarization curves comparing chemically etched and anodized 3D samples, demonstrating shifts in corrosion potential (Ecorr) and reductions in corrosion current (icorr) and passive current (ipass).
summary: Polarization curves reveal the electrochemical improvements achieved through anodizing compared to chemical etching. The anodized 3D samples exhibit a substantial shift of Ecorr toward more positive values, alongside a reduction in both icorr and ipass. These findings indicate enhanced corrosion resistance for the anodized samples in inflammatory conditions.

caption: Comparison of energy absorption per unit volume and energy absorption efficiency for honeycomb structures designed via LP, DNS, and DFE 2 methods.
summary: This plot evaluates the mechanical performance of three distinct multiscale honeycomb structures. It specifically compares the energy absorption per unit volume and the energy absorption efficiency across designs generated by LP, DNS, and DFE 2 methods, providing a quantitative assessment of their relative effectiveness in energy dissipation applications.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of K4800Co alloy deformed to 0.11% plastic strain at 850 °C, showing a reduced density of stacking faults with g=(1-11) diffraction vector.
summary: Representing the K4800Co alloy at 850 °C and 0.11% plastic strain, this TEM image demonstrates an evident decrease in stacking fault density compared to the 800 °C condition. The observation confirms that higher temperatures suppress the formation of stacking faults in this alloy system during slight plastic deformation.

caption: Western blot analysis of A549 cells transfected with H7N9 HA1-expressing plasmids or infected with diverse IAV subtypes, probed with Nb F4 and Nb 204.
summary: Western blot analysis of A549 cells transfected with H7N9 HA1 plasmids or infected with various IAV subtypes confirms the specific recognition of H7N9 by Nb F4. In contrast to other common subtypes like H3N2, H5N6, H6N6, and H9N2, the nanobodies demonstrate high specificity, validating their potential for diagnostic immunoassay applications.

caption: Maximum atomic temperature distribution per voxel for a 50 keV Ni ion cascade in NiFe alloy.
summary: This panel shows the maximum atomic temperature per voxel for a 50 keV Ni ion cascade in NiFe. The atomic temperature distribution provides insight into the thermal spike dynamics within the alloy, which is later compared to pure Ni to evaluate the impact on defect recombination processes.

caption: Wear rate comparison of TiN-integrated WC-SS316L nanocomposites versus wrought and LPBF-fabricated SS316L, calculated following standardized wear testing.
summary: Wear rate measurements demonstrate the performance of the materials after undergoing wear tests. A pronounced reduction in the wear rate is observed for the composites containing 1 wt% TiN when compared to the wrought and LPBF-fabricated SS316L counterparts, indicating that TiN integration significantly enhances the wear resistance of the nanocomposite.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) distribution histograms comparing as-built LPBF Cu–Cr–Zr samples with those subjected to deformation at varying strain rates.
summary: This histogram displays the Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) distributions for LPBF-processed Cu–Cr–Zr samples. By comparing the as-built state to samples deformed at different strain rates, the plot quantitatively illustrates the extent of lattice rotation within grains, providing evidence for microstructural evolution and internal strain accumulation resulting from the applied deformation conditions.

caption: Oxide layer thickness measured on NiCoCrAlTaY coatings containing varying nano-Al2O3 particle concentrations after 300 oxidation cycles at 1100 °C.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the oxide layer thickness for NiCoCrAlTaY coatings modified with different nano-Al2O3 particle amounts. Following 300 oxidation cycles at 1100 °C, the data highlights variations in layer growth, with statistical significance indicated by asterisks for p < 0.05, reflecting the influence of particle content on oxidation resistance.

caption: Reversal curves for heating (solid red line) and cooling (solid blue line) processes are plotted alongside the full magnetic hysteresis loop (dashed lines) at a 2 T magnetic field.
summary: This plot illustrates the methodology for extracting heating and cooling reversal curves from a modeled magnetic transformation. The solid red and blue lines represent the heating and cooling branches, respectively, while the dashed lines depict the full hysteresis loop. These curves are derived from TFORC distribution analysis at a 2 T magnetic field.

caption: Room temperature tensile stress-strain curve for the WAAM-C Ti–6Al–4V sample, characterized by higher strength resulting from finer grain size and narrower α lamellae.
summary: The WAAM-C Ti–6Al–4V sample demonstrates a superior tensile stress-strain profile at room temperature. This enhanced mechanical strength is directly linked to the finer grain size and narrower α lamellae width observed in the microstructure, distinguishing its performance from the R-series samples.

caption: P 2p XPS core-level spectrum of the nanoNi-P modified electrode prepared at a deposition current density of -200,000 μA cm⁻².
summary: P 2p XPS core-level spectrum for the nanoNi-P modified electrode prepared at -200,000 μA cm⁻² is displayed. This data is used to analyze the phosphorus species present on the electrode surface, contributing to the study of how deposition current density affects the properties of the nanoNi-P modified electrodes.

caption: Raman spectrum of the HEA disc worn surface at 300 °C, showing V2O5 as the dominant oxidation product.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the HEA disc worn surface at 300 °C is presented. The spectrum confirms that V2O5 remains the primary wear-induced oxidation product at this temperature. This finding indicates that the oxidation mechanism at 300 °C is consistent with that observed at room temperature.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curve of CoNi-0.5 catalyst in 0.1 M Na2SO4 electrolyte containing 400 ppm HPAM at a scan rate of 2 mV s-1.
summary: The LSV curve for the CoNi-0.5 sample demonstrates the electrocatalytic performance in a 0.1 M Na2SO4 and 400 ppm HPAM electrolyte. Compared to the baseline, the addition of HPAM results in increased current densities and decreased overpotentials, indicating enhanced electrocatalytic activity for the CoNi-0.5 catalyst during the oxidation process.

caption: EDS line profile data revealing the elemental composition of the outer oxide crystal as 72.5% O, 16% Fe, 10% Cr, and 1.5% Al.
summary: The EDS line profile data provides the quantitative elemental composition of the outer oxide crystal. Analysis indicates a composition of 72.5% oxygen, 16% iron, 10% chromium, and 1.5% aluminum. This spectroscopic data confirms the chemical makeup of the oxide layer formed on the FeCrAl sample surface.

caption: Enlarged view of a stacking fault within the heat-treated TiN/HESMA specimen.
summary: A high-magnification view of the heat-treated TiN/HESMA reveals the morphology of a stacking fault. This enlarged image allows for a detailed assessment of the structural defects remaining in the material after the heat treatment process, contributing to the overall understanding of the microstructural evolution.

caption: Concentration profiles of W, Re, Al, and Ta alloying elements across the microstructure after 5 hours of isothermal holding at 1310 °C, comparing liquid-inclusive and solid-state simulation models.
summary: This graph depicts the concentration profiles of W, Re, Al, and Ta after 5 hours at 1310 °C. The differences in the spatial distribution of the γ′ phase, caused by the initial presence of the liquid phase, lead to variations in the local concentration profiles of these key alloying elements.

caption: Detailed view of the as-cast γ/γ′ eutectic structure at 3 mm/min, highlighting the distribution of coarse and fine γ′ phases.
summary: This detailed view of the as-cast γ/γ′ eutectic structure, obtained at a solidification rate of 3 mm/min, provides a closer look at the phase distribution. The structure is characterized by the presence of both coarse and fine γ′ phases, which are integral to the observed butterfly-shaped eutectic morphology.

caption: S–N fatigue curves for DD6 superalloy thin-walled and rotating bending specimens tested at 760 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the S–N fatigue behavior of DD6 superalloy thin-walled and rotating bending specimens at 760 °C. Similar to the room temperature results, the curves exhibit a continuous, slow decline trend without a distinct plateau in the high-cycle fatigue regime beyond 10^7 cycles, facilitating comparison across different specimen thicknesses.

caption: Absorbance spectra of mixed A92618 and S31603 powder systems, showing the evolution of optical response across varying composition ratios.
summary: This figure displays the absorbance spectra for mixed A92618 and S31603 powder systems. Analysis of the y-axis at a wavelength of 250 nm reveals that the spectra for 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% S31603 concentrations are uniformly distributed, indicating a consistent trend in the optical behavior of the system.

caption: SHAP decision plot illustrating the cumulative decision paths for predicted yield strength across the entire benchmark dataset.
summary: This SHAP decision plot provides a comprehensive overview of how the machine learning model generates yield strength predictions for the full benchmark dataset. By visualizing the collective impact of global SHAP values, the plot offers a straightforward interpretation of model behavior and feature contributions across a large number of observations.

caption: Failure mode observation of a Ti/Mg bimetal joint produced with applying IBS, showing a transition to Ti strut fracture.
summary: This photograph illustrates the failure mode of a Ti/Mg bimetal joint processed with IBS. In contrast to the baseline, the failure mode has shifted to Ti strut fracture. This change in failure location and mechanism demonstrates the significant impact of IBS on the structural performance of the bimetal joint.

caption: Nominal stress–strain responses for SLM-printed RNLs compared with FEA predictions, showing the progression through linear elastic, yielding, post-yield plateau, and densification phases.
summary: The nominal stress–strain responses for SLM-printed RNLs are plotted against FEA results, demonstrating the mechanical progression through linear elastic, yielding, post-yield plateau, and densification phases. This synchronized data confirms the mechanical response stages observed in both experimental testing and finite element simulations for the specified lattice architectures.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of triangular Ni–Cu coated electrodes in alkaline media, depicting the electrochemical response within the -1.2 V to 1.2 V range.
summary: The cyclic voltammogram displays the electrochemical activity of 3D printed triangular Ni–Cu coated electrodes in alkaline media. By utilizing a potential range between -1.2 V and 1.2 V, the scan characterizes the electrochemical behavior of the triangular geometry, providing a comparative metric for the Ni–Cu coated electrode system.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of BCNT-based electrodes at various current densities within a potential range of 0 to 0.5 V, demonstrating symmetric behavior.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for BCNT-based electrodes were collected at various current densities between 0 and 0.5 V. The profiles are almost symmetric, and the rectangular area analysis indicates a maximum specific capacitance of 1,560 F/g, representing the effective charge capacity of the BCNT-based composite electrode.

caption: Live/dead staining images of rMSCs on scaffolds, visualized with a scale bar of 450 μm.
summary: Live/dead staining was employed to assess the proliferation and viability of rMSCs on the scaffolds. This visualization technique allows for the clear identification of live versus dead cells, providing a qualitative assessment of the biocompatibility and cellular health of rMSCs cultured on the various scaffold materials.

caption: Generational progression of the Generational Distance (GD) indicator demonstrating the optimization algorithm's convergence toward the Pareto front.
summary: The GD indicator is plotted against successive generations to illustrate the optimization progress of the NSGA II algorithm. This learning curve confirms the algorithm's successful convergence toward the Pareto front, providing a quantitative measure of how the solution set improves and stabilizes over the course of the optimization process.

caption: Representative CLSM images comparing cellularized and decellularized fibroblast-laden 3D printed RGD-alginate scaffolds, highlighting the removal of DNA (blue) and F-actin (green) while maintaining the extracellular matrix component fibronectin (red).
summary: Confocal laser scanning microscopy images demonstrate the successful decellularization of fibroblast-laden 3D printed RGD-alginate scaffolds. The visualization confirms the effective removal of cellular and nuclear components, evidenced by the absence of DNA and F-actin staining, while simultaneously showing that the structural integrity of the fibronectin extracellular matrix component is preserved.

caption: Weight change kinetics of aluminized alloy 625 during 1000 h of oxidation in wet air at 900 °C and 1000 °C, represented by experimental data points and corresponding power law fits.
summary: This plot illustrates the oxidation behavior of aluminized alloy 625 by tracking weight changes over 1000 hours at 900 °C and 1000 °C in wet air. Experimental data points are fitted with power law functions, providing a quantitative representation of the oxidation kinetics and the growth of the alumina layer.

caption: Bode plots showing phase angle versus frequency for rolled TA31, SLM TA31-1000, and SLM TA31-900 alloys in simulated seawater.
summary: Bode plots for the three TA31 alloys demonstrate phase angles approaching 90° from mid to low frequencies. This behavior indicates the formation of a stable and compact passivation film on all three samples, confirming their electrochemical corrosion resistance characteristics when tested in simulated seawater environments.

caption: Microstructural SEM image of the Ni-11.1Si-3Cr alloy, highlighting the solidification morphology and grain characteristics.
summary: This SEM image captures the microstructural features of the Ni-11.1Si-3Cr alloy. By examining the deposited bead, the image provides insights into the solidification behavior and interfacial interactions occurring during the DED-LB process, which are essential for understanding the resulting microstructural characteristics of this specific alloy composition.

caption: Signal-to-noise ratio main effect diagram derived from the Design of Experiments (DoE) analysis.
summary: This panel displays the signal-to-noise ratio main effects obtained from the DoE analysis. It serves as a diagnostic tool to evaluate the influence of various printing parameters on the process performance, providing the necessary data to identify optimal settings for the subsequent fabrication of the printed sheet samples.

caption: Probability of Detection (PoD) curves for component P1, illustrating the hit/miss analysis at 10 μm and 35 μm voxel sizes and marking the 90/95 defect detection limit.
summary: This panel presents the Probability of Detection (PoD) analysis for component P1. By comparing hit/miss data at 10 μm and 35 μm voxel sizes, the plot demonstrates the impact of resolution on defect detection. The 90/95 defect threshold is clearly indicated to define the reliability of the micro-CT inspection process.

caption: Wilshire predictive stress-rupture curves for Ti-45Al-2Mn-2Nb, showing isothermal data points and the specific 700 °C, 190 MPa experimental result alongside two specimens selected for microstructural characterization.
summary: This plot displays Wilshire predictive stress-rupture curves for Ti-45Al-2Mn-2Nb, illustrating the division into high and low stress regimes separated by a distinct kink. A recently measured creep test at 700 °C and 190 MPa aligns with the predicted curve, while two circled specimens represent distinct stress regimes for further characterization.

caption: Phase-field calculation result for the S33B3 (or S33B1) condition at 50 ms, highlighting the structural evolution under intense grain competition.
summary: Depicting the S33B3 or S33B1 condition at 50 ms, this panel shows the final grain distribution. The microstructure contains many small grains, confirming that grain competition is more intense than in the S0B0 baseline, which leads to the disappearance of more grains during the simulated growth period.

caption: Storage modulus plotted against frequency for samples subjected to varying amplitudes.
summary: This panel displays the storage modulus as a function of frequency for samples tested under varying amplitudes. The data reflects the mechanical response of the materials, with error bars indicating the deviation between three experimental repetitions per sample type, ensuring statistical reliability in the observed viscoelastic behavior across the tested conditions.

caption: Pole figure of the RE-WAAM sample demonstrating a reduction in texture intensity to a MUD value of 5.64, reflecting notable alterations in the crystal structure compared to the WAAM process.
summary: The RE-WAAM process induces significant changes in the crystal structure of the deposited sample. The pole figure analysis reveals a decrease in the MUD value to 5.64, indicating that the addition of RE elements during the WAAM process effectively reduces the intensity of the crystallographic texture.

caption: Stress distribution map highlighting stress localization around the hole edge, where the overall stress magnitude decreases as cycle numbers increase due to stress relaxation.
summary: The stress distribution map for specimen #2 shows significant stress localization around the hole edge. As the number of cycles increases, the magnitude of the stress tends to decrease, which is attributed to stress relaxation phenomena. This behavior is consistent with observations previously documented in low-cycle fatigue testing scenarios.

caption: Experimental configuration for quasi-static three-point bending tests performed on G-TPMS sandwich structures using an MTS 100 kN material testing machine.
summary: This panel illustrates the experimental setup for quasi-static three-point bending tests conducted on G-TPMS sandwich structures. The tests were performed using an MTS 100 kN material testing machine to investigate the bending behavior of the specimens, providing a clear visual representation of the mechanical testing configuration employed in the study.

caption: Raman spectrum of the 47S6 bioglass sample highlighting the vibrational modes related to its structural components.
summary: This Raman spectrum of the 47S6 bioglass sample highlights various vibrational modes that are directly related to the structural components of the material. By analyzing these specific modes, the spectrum provides a detailed insight into the molecular arrangement and structural characteristics inherent to the 47S6 bioglass composition.

caption: Calculated lattice misfit values for the ASC2 alloy and modified compositions lacking Mo and/or W, determined via JMatPro after 16 hours of aging at 800 °C.
summary: JMatPro simulations illustrate the influence of Mo and W on the lattice misfit of the ASC2 alloy after aging at 800 °C for 16 hours. The combined addition of Mo and W results in the lowest lattice misfit of 0.055%, while the misfit decreases significantly from 0.19% as temperature approaches 800 °C.

caption: Grain orientation spread (GOS) coloring maps for samples subjected to hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 1050 °C, 1150 °C, and 1230 °C, illustrating the spatial distribution of grain deformation and recrystallization states.
summary: These GOS coloring maps visualize the microstructural state of samples processed at 1050 °C, 1150 °C, and 1230 °C. By mapping grain orientation spread, the images elucidate the extent of grain deformation and recrystallization occurring under different HIP conditions, providing a spatial representation of the material's internal structural evolution.

caption: Atomic arrangement of the D022 Ni3Nb structure, highlighting the distinct Ni-1, Ni-2, and Nb sublattice sites.
summary: The D022 crystal structure of Ni3Nb is illustrated, emphasizing the specific atomic sublattices present within the unit cell. This configuration includes the Nb site, the Ni-1 site, and the Ni-2 site, which collectively define the structural arrangement of this intermetallic phase as described in the reference literature.

caption: Bright field TEM image showing larger precipitates approximately 200 nm in size distributed along the grain boundaries of the alloy.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging highlights the distribution of larger precipitates within the alloy structure. These particles, measuring approximately 200 nm in size, are observed to be distributed along the grain boundaries. This panel provides the context for the subsequent EDX and SAED analysis performed on region III of the sample.

caption: Cross-sectional profiles of the wear track for mild carbon steel.
summary: This panel illustrates the 2D wear track cross-sectional profiles for mild carbon steel. Compared to the HEA coating, the mild carbon steel exhibits significantly wider and deeper wear tracks across all tested wear temperatures, indicating inferior wear resistance under the specified experimental conditions compared to the HEA coating.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform pattern generated from the blue-highlighted area in panel (c), confirming the presence of Ti2Cu precipitates at the lath boundary.
summary: This Fast Fourier Transform pattern, obtained from the blue-highlighted area in the HRTEM image, confirms the identification of Ti2Cu precipitates. These nano-scaled particles are predominantly confined to the lath boundaries, a structural characteristic that confirms the effectiveness of the core-shell approach in creating a refined, homogeneous alpha-Ti lath microstructure.

caption: One-dimensional composition profile of zirconium across the grain boundary, corresponding to the cylindrical region of interest indicated by arrow #1 in panel (a), with line thickness representing 2σ counting error bars.
summary: This 1D composition profile quantifies the zirconium concentration across the grain boundary identified in the APT reconstruction. By analyzing a cylindrical region of interest, the plot provides precise compositional data, with the line thickness accounting for 2σ counting error bars to ensure statistical reliability of the observed elemental distribution.

caption: SS 253 MA maximum allowable working fluid temperature shown in relation to working pressure and heat flux parameters.
summary: SS 253 MA alloy behavior is represented through this contour plot, showing the maximum allowable working fluid temperature as a function of working pressure and heat flux. The plot effectively demonstrates the relationship between these environmental factors and the thermal constraints of the material within the specified operational range.

caption: UV-Vis spectroscopic analysis of HA-GA determining the second pKa value of 7.61, associated with oxidation-induced crosslinking of the gallic acid derivatives.
summary: This panel presents the UV-Vis analysis used to determine the second pKa value of the gallic acid derivatives conjugated to hyaluronic acid. Based on the spectroscopic observations, the second pKa was calculated to be 7.61, which corresponds to the oxidation-induced crosslinking process of the polymer network.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus reference values for the average magnetic moment ⟨ μ ⟩ of nanoparticles across CatBoost, RF, SVR, and Elastic Net models during the training stage.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the training performance of four machine learning models—CatBoost, RF, SVR, and Elastic Net—in predicting the average magnetic moment ⟨ μ ⟩ of nanoparticles. By comparing predicted values against reference data, the figure demonstrates the accuracy and consistency of these models during the training phase of the study.

caption: Room temperature X-ray diffraction patterns of Ni55Fe17Ga26Co2 as-spun ribbons, comparing the wheel-side and free-side surfaces, including a Le Bail fit for the free side using a P2/m space group.
summary: This figure displays room temperature X-ray diffraction patterns for Ni55Fe17Ga26Co2 as-spun ribbons, contrasting the wheel and free surfaces. The free-side pattern is analyzed via Le Bail fitting based on a P2/m space group, with the difference plot confirming the structural refinement of the 14M martensite modulated phase.

caption: Plane-averaged electron density difference map for the Co-N/C model, with yellow and cyan regions denoting electron accumulation and depletion, respectively, at an isosurface value of 0.003 eÅ⁻³.
summary: This panel presents the plane-averaged electron density difference for the Co-N/C system. Charge redistribution is observed around the cobalt atom, with a slight loss of electrons. The visualization, rendered at an isosurface of 0.003 eÅ⁻³, highlights the spatial distribution of electron accumulation and depletion, characterizing the electronic structure of the material.

caption: Initial stage of the cross-sectional analysis workflow for strut characterization.
summary: Panel a illustrates the first step in the systematic analysis workflow designed for cross-sectional images of struts. This schematic representation serves as the foundational component of the characterization process, providing a structured approach to evaluating the internal geometry and material distribution within the cross-section of the analyzed strut samples.

caption: Optical transmission spectra of Zn1−xNixTe thin films with varying nickel concentrations (x = 0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, and 0.20) measured across the 300–2600 nm wavelength range.
summary: This plot displays the optical transmission spectra for Zn1−xNixTe films with nickel doping levels ranging from 0.0 to 0.20. Data were collected using a UV–vis–NIR spectrophotometer between 300 and 2600 nm to investigate how nickel incorporation influences the optical band gap variation within the semiconductor material system.

caption: Activation energy plot derived from Norton’s creep law for AM and CM states, highlighting the temperature-dependent creep resistance.
summary: Activation energy for the AM and CM states is calculated based on Norton’s creep law. The plot reveals that the observed activation energies are significantly high, reflecting the creep resistance characteristics of the materials at 750 °C and 950 °C as the temperature increases and properties deteriorate.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the classification results for the fifth model across the specified pH level categories.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed view of the classification results for the fifth model across different pH level classes. It offers a comprehensive summary of the model's predictive behavior, enabling a direct comparison of classification accuracy across the various pH levels included in the test dataset.

caption: Pseudobinary phase diagram for the Fe-Cr-Ni system at approximately 70% Fe, showing the solidification mode where δ-ferrite forms as the primary phase from the liquid state.
summary: This pseudobinary phase diagram for the Fe-Cr-Ni system at 70% Fe concentration illustrates the solidification sequence. It demonstrates that the δ-ferrite phase is generated as the primary phase while γ-austenite remains liquid. Furthermore, the diagram is utilized to predict the ferrite mode experienced at temperatures exceeding T8/5.

caption: Cycling performance comparison between 3D-printed and ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrodes at a 1C rate, demonstrating long-term reversibility.
summary: This panel compares the cycle performance of 3D-printed and ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrodes at a 1C rate. The 3D-printed electrode maintains a high discharge capacity of 216.06 mAh g-1 when the current density is reduced to 0.1C, confirming that the material is highly reversible at both low and high current densities.

caption: Proportional breakdown of completion times across different phases of RMfg operations.
summary: This panel highlights the time spent in each phase of the RMfg operations. According to the adopted data, inspection and repair are identified as the two most time-consuming phases, demonstrating the relative duration of each operational stage within the overall manufacturing cycle.

caption: Overview of the microstructural characterization workflow applied to the Haynes 282 alloy samples, including the as-printed state and subsequent stages following solution and aging treatments.
summary: The flowchart summarizes the comprehensive microstructural characterization strategy employed in this study. It tracks the experimental progression from the as-printed state through the various heat treatment stages, providing a structured framework for analyzing the evolutionary pathways of carbides and phase stability within the WAAM-fabricated Haynes 282 alloy samples.

caption: Long-term stability performance of the Ni1Co3@NC catalyst compared to the Pt/C benchmark, measured at a constant current density of 50 mA/cm2.
summary: This stability curve compares the performance of Ni1Co3@NC and the benchmark catalyst Pt/C at a higher current density of 50 mA/cm2. It demonstrates the durability and operational longevity of the optimized bimetallic catalyst under sustained high-current conditions for the hydrogen evolution reaction.

caption: Distribution of SHAP values illustrating the influence of five input features—annealing temperature, laser power, insulation time, scanning speed, and layer thickness—on the model's prediction results.
summary: This SHAP value distribution plot visualizes how five specific processing parameters, including annealing temperature, laser power, insulation time, scanning speed, and layer thickness, impact the model's predictive output. It provides a detailed view of how each feature contributes to the model's decision-making process across the analyzed dataset.

caption: Distribution of the seven numbered grains within the IPF-Z triangle, highlighting their positions along the (0 0 1)-(1 1 1) edge.
summary: The IPF-Z triangle map shows the specific crystallographic orientations of the seven numbered grains. These grains are distributed along the (0 0 1)-(1 1 1) edge, with deviation angles from the (1 1 1) plane decreasing from 50.67° for Grain 13 to 3.92° for Grain 68, correlating with their observed morphological changes.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy image of the surface texture for the pure AISI 420 powder feedstock.
summary: This confocal laser scanning microscopy image displays the surface morphology of the initial AISI 420 powder feedstock without any TiN addition. The visualization provides a baseline characterization of the powder surface texture, which is essential for evaluating the subsequent morphological changes observed in the TiN/AISI 420 powder mixtures.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of BIL at concentrations ranging from 5 to 100 µM in a BRB solution at pH 2.3, compared against a blank control.
summary: This panel displays a series of cyclic voltammograms recorded for increasing concentrations of BIL in an aqueous BRB solution at pH 2.3. The black solid lines represent the BIL-containing samples, while the red dashed line indicates the blank measurement, demonstrating the electrochemical response of the system under these specific acidic conditions.

caption: Final stage of the phase-field variable evolution for two unequal-sized particles.
summary: This panel presents the final state of the phase-field simulation for Test II, involving two particles of unequal size. It illustrates the completed temporal evolution of the particles during sintering, demonstrating the final morphological configuration resulting from the non-conserved phase-field variable dynamics observed throughout the simulation process.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of live-dead stained MC3T3-E1 cells on SLM porous Ta surfaces (65%–90% porosity) after 7, 14, and 21 days, showing viable cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Live/dead viability assessment reveals progressive colonization of the scaffolds by viable cells, indicated by green fluorescence, with negligible red-stained dead cells observed over the 21-day culture duration. The staining confirms that the SLM porous Ta scaffolds support sustained cell viability across all tested porosity levels throughout the experimental period.

caption: Ternary composition map illustrating the distribution of crystal structures across the Fe-Co-Ni alloy library after spark plasma sintering and subsequent annealing.
summary: This ternary diagram displays the crystal structure distribution for the annealed bulk alloy library. Specific compositions, such as Fe2.4Co96.7Ni0.9 and Fe11.1Co87.9Ni1, are identified as maintaining FCC + HCP crystal structures after both the initial spark plasma sintering process and the subsequent annealing treatment.

caption: Phonon dispersion curves for Ni8Mn5Ti3 at 0 K calculated using the phonopy method, showing imaginary frequencies in the austenitic structure.
summary: Calculated at 0 K using the phonopy method, the phonon dispersion curves for Ni8Mn5Ti3 reveal the presence of imaginary phonon frequencies within the Brillouin zone for the austenitic structure. This indicates lattice dynamical instability at low temperatures, contrasting with the stable martensitic structure which exhibits no such imaginary frequencies.

caption: Rate capability performance of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode, illustrating discharge capacity retention across increasing current densities.
summary: The rate capability profile illustrates the discharge capacity of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode as the current density is systematically increased from 0.1C to 10C. This plot highlights the electrode's ability to maintain electrochemical performance and capacity retention under varying operational current loads during charge and discharge cycles.

caption: Nyquist diagram illustrating the impedance spectra for a triangular-pore lattice Pb-deposited electrode, exhibiting a depressed semicircle consistent with charge-transfer dominated kinetics.
summary: Impedance spectra for the triangular-pore lattice Pb-deposited electrode reveal a depressed semicircle, reflecting the electrochemical behavior of the interface. The absence of significant low-frequency diffusion tails confirms that the interfacial charge-transfer processes, coupled with a distributed capacitance, are the primary factors governing the electrochemical response of this architected electrode.

caption: Dilatometric measurement of commercial BaTiO3 powders showing the dimensional change as a function of temperature.
summary: This dilatometry plot illustrates the thermal expansion and sintering behavior of commercial BaTiO3 powders. By measuring dimensional changes across a temperature range, the data provides critical insights into the densification process and thermal stability of the material, serving as a fundamental characterization for processing these specific ceramic powders.

caption: Creep displacement rate versus time for SLM-SS316L specimen B01 at 650 °C.
summary: This panel shows the creep displacement rate plotted against time for specimen B01 at 650 °C. The minimum punch displacement rate was determined by averaging data within the 30–60% range of the total creep rupture time, providing a standardized metric for analyzing the steady-state creep behavior of the material.

caption: Arrott plot for the LPBFed block sample with E = 88.89 J/mm³ near the martensitic transition temperature.
summary: This panel shows the Arrott plot for the 88.89 J/mm³ energy density sample near the martensitic transition temperature. The observed magnetic hysteresis and positive Arrott plot characteristics confirm the presence of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), consistent with the behavior observed in the other samples processed at different energy densities.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry profile obtained from graphite current collectors, illustrating the electrochemical response characteristic of this material.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram demonstrates the electrochemical behavior of graphite current collectors. As a fundamental technique in electrochemistry, this measurement provides critical insights into the redox activity and surface characteristics of the graphite material, serving as a standard diagnostic tool for evaluating the performance and stability of the collectors in electrochemical systems.

caption: Detailed SHAP value distribution plot for the feature θ ⋅ PD, which ranks fifth in importance and exhibits a unique pattern compared to other top-ranked features.
summary: This plot displays the individual SHAP values for the feature θ ⋅ PD, which is ranked fifth in importance. Unlike other top-ranking features, this variable shows a distinctive distribution pattern. This suggests that inward fiber alignment, influenced by twisted angles, significantly impacts the inward deviation of printing paths.

caption: Absorption coefficient spectrum for a 50 mm thick sample with grading optimized for 2700 Hz, comparing experimental and numerical results.
summary: This panel displays the absorption coefficient spectrum for a 50 mm thick sample optimized for 2700 Hz. The red measured lines and black dashed numerical lines show the acoustic performance, validating the design optimization for the specific target frequency in the thicker sample configuration.

caption: Surface topography of the ceramic workpiece after machining test no. 8, executed at a pressure of 12 kPa, velocity of 1.44 m/s, and duration of 120 minutes.
summary: Depicted here is the surface topography of the ceramic workpiece after test no. 8, which utilized a pressure of 12 kPa and a velocity of 1.44 m/s. Confocal microscopy at 20x magnification confirms a clear smoothing of the surface, further validating the geometric structural changes observed across all experimental test conditions.

caption: Continuous Fiber-Reinforced Fabrication (CFFF) trajectories generated by adjusting bar radii.
summary: The second row depicts two CFFF trajectories obtained by modifying the bars’ radii. These trajectories ensure fiber continuity in each layer while successfully retaining the intersecting fiber trajectories within the design, demonstrating the feasibility of maintaining structural integrity through precise control of fiber placement and radius adjustment during the fabrication process.

caption: Dependence plot showing the nonlinear relationship between total height deviation and predicted variability.
summary: This dependence plot illustrates a nonlinear relationship between total height deviation and predicted variability. The data indicates that moderate height deviations tend to reduce predicted variability, whereas extreme deviations—both low and high—significantly increase it, highlighting the complex influence of this specific geometric feature on the model's output.

caption: EBSD map of the aged sample captured normal to the loading direction before tensile testing.
summary: This EBSD map characterizes the aged sample microstructure before tensile testing. While intended to validate diffraction data, the map resolution of 1.5 μm is insufficient to capture fine interphase strains or dislocation pile-ups associated with the 200 nm α-needles, limiting the visibility of aging-induced dislocation density increases.

caption: Phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction under a 10% compressive strain applied in the P to Q configuration.
summary: This panel displays the phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction. The configuration involves a 10% compressive strain applied in the P to Q direction. Red highlights indicate the presence of band gaps within the calculated dispersion relation for the elastic wave propagation in this specific strained state.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength of as-built specimens as a function of volumetric energy density.
summary: Ultimate tensile strength is plotted against the volumetric energy density applied during the manufacturing process. This graph characterizes the relationship between the energy input during fabrication and the resulting peak tensile strength of the as-built material, facilitating an understanding of process-property correlations.

caption: Evolution of the plastic strain range as a function of cycle number for DED-processed Invar alloy subjected to total strain amplitudes of ±0.35%, ±0.5%, and ±0.65%.
summary: This plot illustrates the cyclic plastic strain evolution of DED-processed Invar alloy during total strain amplitude-controlled fatigue testing. It displays the plastic strain range over the number of cycles for three distinct strain amplitudes. The data highlights the relationship between hysteresis loop area and plastic strain range for the investigated DED conditions.

caption: Internal defect distribution in CMT-WAAM aluminum alloy specimen #0 processed with a longitudinal alternating magnetic field.
