caption: Laser confocal microscopy image of the Fe–Mn–Al–C sample surface morphology at a scanning speed of 1400 mm/s, highlighting 2D and 3D structural details.
summary: The surface morphology of the Fe–Mn–Al–C sample, fabricated at a scanning speed of 1400 mm/s, is detailed using laser confocal microscopy. The 2D and 3D views allow for the assessment of surface roughness, completing the analysis of the L-PBF-formed lightweight steel cross-section across the tested range of scanning speeds.

caption: Representative fluorescence micrograph of cells cultured on the BAG/PLGA/SIM scaffold, highlighting blue-stained nuclei and green-stained cytoplasm.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy of the BAG/PLGA/SIM scaffold shows numerous fluorescently labeled live cells adhering to the surface. The staining protocol, with blue nuclei and green cytoplasm, confirms that the scaffold supports cell attachment. These results indicate that the composite scaffold possesses excellent cell adhesion properties.

caption: High-resolution XPS fine spectrum of the Fe 2p3/2 core level obtained from the experimental steel rust layer.
summary: This panel displays the high-resolution XPS fine spectrum for the Fe 2p3/2 core level, characterizing the chemical state of iron within the experimental steel rust layer. The spectral fitting results provide essential data for understanding the composition and oxidation states present in the corrosion products formed on the steel surface.

caption: STEM/EDS cross-sectional characterization of ACCMZ after 168 h of H3BO3 exposure at 50 °C, showing a linear composition profile and selected analysis spots.
summary: Exposing ACCMZ to H3BO3 at 50 °C for 168 hours results in a 33 nm thick surface oxide. Line profiles indicate a subsurface ternary phase containing approximately 62% Al, 23% Cu, and 5% Ce. EDS data from selected spots #1, #2, and #3 further characterize these distinct subsurface phases.

caption: Polished sample surface illustrating the morphology of a lack-of-fusion defect before oxidation.
summary: This SEM micrograph captures the pre-oxidation state of a lack-of-fusion defect on a polished surface. By documenting the defect geometry prior to thermal treatment, this panel serves as a reference point for evaluating how surface preparation and subsequent oxidation processes influence the development of surface features and crystal growth.

caption: Top-view cross-section of a HIP-treated C5 cylinder, showing the structural response to post-processing.
summary: This top-view micro-CT cross-section displays the C5 cylinder after HIP treatment. The panel illustrates the structural response of the material to post-processing, specifically focusing on how HIP mitigates the large irregular pores formed during the initial fabrication. It provides a comparative view of the densification achieved through the HIP process.

caption: Representative neutron diffraction pattern and corresponding fitting results, with the greyscale background indicating normalized neutron beam intensity versus wavelength at the guide exit.
summary: This panel displays a representative diffraction pattern and its associated fitting. The greyscale background represents the normalized neutron beam intensity as a function of wavelength at the POLDI neutron guide exit, where black and white colors denote the maximum intensity and the absence of neutrons, respectively.

caption: Schematic representation of the Ni-base superalloy phase equilibrium near the γ′ dissolution limit within the γ matrix.
summary: This schematic phase diagram illustrates the equilibrium conditions for a typical Ni-base superalloy, specifically focusing on the region near the γ′ dissolution limit in a γ matrix. It provides a conceptual framework for understanding phase stability and the thermodynamic boundaries governing the microstructure of these high-temperature materials.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of the PMTO molecule.
summary: Panel B displays the 1H NMR spectrum of PMTO. This spectroscopic measurement allows for the identification and verification of the proton configuration in the PMTO molecule. By comparing these results with the MTPO spectrum, researchers can confirm the successful synthesis and structural integrity of the PMTO derivative.

caption: ASTM D638 specimen geometry utilized for evaluating warping defects in printed parts.
summary: The ASTM D638 specimen geometry is presented as a standardized form for warping analysis. Its elongated structure makes it particularly susceptible to warping during the printing process, providing a controlled basis for researchers to evaluate how various printing parameters influence the development of this specific geometric defect.

caption: Experimental and numerical force-displacement behavior for spar A.
summary: Spar A exhibits a force-displacement response where experimental data is compared against numerical predictions. A strong correlation between these curves is observed, indicating that the numerical model accurately captures the mechanical behavior of the spar under the tested loading conditions, validating the simulation approach used for this specific component.

caption: Combined Pourbaix diagrams for the W-Cl-H2O and Cu-Cl-H2O systems, illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions of tungsten and copper species in aqueous chloride environments.
summary: This figure presents the combined Pourbaix diagrams for W-Cl-H2O and Cu-Cl-H2O systems. These diagrams are utilized to rationalize the electrochemical corrosion mechanism of W-Cu composites when exposed to neutral NaCl solutions at pH 7, providing a thermodynamic basis for understanding the stability and dissolution behavior of the composite components.

caption: TEM micrograph of the GWZ831K alloy layer post-tensile fracture, visualized using a specific double-beam diffraction condition to identify dislocation characteristics.
summary: This TEM micrograph illustrates the dislocation morphology within the GWZ831K alloy layer after tensile fracture. Employing the twin-beam bright-field technique with a [0] zone axis, the image allows for the investigation of dislocation types in this layered heterogeneous Mg alloy, providing a clear view of the structural response to deformation.

caption: White light interferometry images and corresponding surface roughness measurements for samples 4–9.
summary: White light interferometry is utilized to quantify the surface roughness of samples 4 through 9. These images and measurements provide precise topographical data, allowing for a detailed analysis of how varying processing parameters influence the surface texture and roughness values across the selected set of experimental samples.

caption: Short-circuit current measurements recorded over a seven-day period for the fourth experimental group of SMFCs.
summary: This panel displays the short-circuit current measurements for the fourth experimental group of SMFCs, recorded continuously over a seven-day duration. The data provides insight into the temporal stability and performance characteristics of the specific electrode spatial arrangement tested within this group during the experimental observation period.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectra of samples following complete dissolution in simulated body fluid (SBF), displaying characteristic absorption bands between 400 and 800 nm.
summary: This UV–Vis absorption spectrum illustrates the optical characteristics of samples after complete dissolution in SBF. The data reveals distinct absorption bands within the 400 to 800 nm range, which are identified as characteristic signatures of silver inclusion within the material, confirming the successful incorporation and subsequent release of silver species.

caption: FCC-removed ACNA map of S77 at 4.7% strain, highlighting numerous dislocation nucleation points.
summary: This FCC-removed ACNA map identifies multiple dislocation nucleation points at 4.7% strain. The findings indicate that dislocation walls, which contain both partial and perfect dislocations, serve as the primary sites for ISF nucleation, elucidating the mechanism of HCP phase formation in the S77 material.

caption: Absolute deviations of wall thickness measured across thin-walled geometries.
summary: This box plot illustrates the absolute deviations observed in the wall thickness of thin-walled geometries. The data reflects measurements taken on walls ranging from 0.5 to 3 mm in thickness, providing a quantitative assessment of the dimensional accuracy achieved during the fabrication process for these specific structural features.

caption: TMF life as a function of phase angle across various strain ranges under a 300–700 °C thermal cycle.
summary: This graph displays the relationship between TMF life and phase angle for different strain ranges under 300–700 °C thermal cycling. A clear crossover point between in-phase (IP) and out-of-phase (OP) performance is observed at a strain range of approximately 0.8%, highlighting the sensitivity of fatigue life to phase angle.

caption: Si 2p binding energy region for the Ni80-Fe20 cathode surface, highlighting detected impurities.
summary: This panel shows the Si 2p binding energy region for the Ni80-Fe20 cathode surface. The presence of a Si 2p peak indicates the detection of silicon impurities on the cathode surface, confirming the presence of these contaminants in the Ni80-Fe20 alloy sample.

caption: Bright field image of high-purity aluminum shocked at 730 m/s, revealing extremely fine grains and localized regions of tangled dislocations.
summary: This bright field image provides direct visual evidence of the microstructural refinement in high-purity aluminum subjected to 730 m/s shock loading. The micrograph clearly displays the extremely fine grain structure alongside regions containing tangled dislocations, illustrating the intense plastic deformation and microstructural evolution induced by the high peak shock stress.

caption: Bode diagram displaying the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for DED-produced NAB samples tested in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: The Bode diagram provides the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for DED-produced NAB samples tested in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. This plot, alongside the polarization and Nyquist data, is used to investigate the effect of different microstructures on the corrosion resistance of the NAB alloys before and after heat treatment.

caption: STEM-BF image of Zone 3, exhibiting a dense population of local defects and large clusters of coalesced defect clusters.
summary: Zone 3 is visualized using STEM-BF, revealing a dense population of local defects and large clusters of coalesced defect clusters. This microstructural state represents the distinct radiation response observed in this specific region of the post-irradiated DED TEM lamella, contrasting with the dislocation-dominated structures of the other zones.

caption: Compressive strength at break plotted against porosity for OR uniform, GR5, and GR6 samples, illustrating the influence of varying rib thicknesses and cell numbers on mechanical performance.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between porosity and compressive strength at break for OR uniform, GR5, and GR6 samples. By examining these variables across different rib thicknesses and cell numbers, the figure demonstrates that the observed increase in mechanical properties is not solely attributable to variations in sample porosity.

caption: Averaged SHAP beeswarm plot representing the cumulative feature effects across all pH classes to provide a holistic overview of the XGBoost model's performance.
summary: To provide a holistic view of the trained XGBoost model, SHAP values were averaged over all pH classes. This beeswarm plot summarizes the cumulative effects of features across the entire dataset, offering a comprehensive perspective on the model's overall decision-making criteria beyond individual pH class specificities.

caption: Effective mean free path (λeff) of Haynes282 plotted against tensile deformation for volume fractions (fp) of 11% and 20% at room temperature and 815 °C.
summary: This line graph illustrates the evolution of the effective mean free path (λeff) in Haynes282 under tensile deformation. Data are presented for two distinct volume fractions (11% and 20%) at room temperature and 815 °C. The results indicate that λeff exhibits a stronger dependence on deformation than on temperature variations.

caption: Partial electronic density of states for the first neighboring atoms of the site exhibiting the highest vacancy formation energy.
summary: This panel displays the partial electronic density of states (PDOS) calculated for the first neighboring atoms of the site with the highest vacancy formation energy. The data provides insight into the electron orbital distribution at this specific atomic site, facilitating a comparison of electronic states before and after vacancy formation.

caption: Anode-side ohmic loss recorded over the 1000-h durability test for Ni-GDC and Ni95Co5-GDC anodes, illustrating the stability of ohmic resistance components.
summary: The anode-side ohmic loss was tracked throughout the 1000-hour durability test. Similar to the anodic overvoltage, the ohmic loss shows minor noisy fluctuations in the raw data. These results confirm that the ohmic resistance remains stable and is very similar for both the Ni-GDC and Ni95Co5-GDC anode compositions.

caption: Acetone-driven shape morphing sequence of an artificial worm actuator, showing the film's response to chemical stimuli.
summary: The artificial worm actuator demonstrates the film's responsive capabilities when exposed to acetone. The shape morphing behavior closely mimics the movement of a worm, highlighting the material's ability to undergo complex, biomimetic deformations in response to chemical triggers applied to the actuator surface.

caption: Optical micrograph of a stab-tested sample featuring 0.75 mm fibre spacing and a 45° pitch angle.
summary: Captured via Dino-Lite microscopy, this image shows the damage morphology for a 0.75 mm fibre spacing sample at a 45° pitch angle. The visual evidence highlights the characteristic fracture patterns and footprint size associated with this specific fibre spacing, contributing to the broader analysis of damage localization and crack arrest.

caption: Inverse pole figure map illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution of the CL specimen.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the crystallographic orientation distribution for the CL specimen. As part of the STA specimen series, this map provides a visual representation of the grain orientations, serving as a foundational characterization for analyzing the microstructural texture of the CL material condition.

caption: Dislocation structures in a [1-23]-oriented Cr-Co-Ni single crystal deformed to 3% plastic strain at room temperature.
summary: This TEM image displays the typical dislocation structure observed in a [1-23]-oriented Cr-Co-Ni single crystal after compression to approximately 3% plastic strain at room temperature. The micrograph provides a representative view of the dislocation arrangement developed under these specific deformation conditions, highlighting the material's microstructural response to room-temperature loading.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) distribution map of the T1 alloy following HT-1 heat treatment.
summary: This KAM distribution map illustrates the micro-region dislocation density and plastic deformation state of the T1 alloy after undergoing the HT-1 heat treatment process. The visualization provides a spatial representation of local orientation differences, which are used to assess the microstructural evolution and relaxation of internal stresses.

caption: SHAP feature interaction plot for the twisted angle, highlighting the range of negative contributions to radius error.
summary: This SHAP interaction plot visualizes the influence of the twisted angle on radius error. The data indicates that SHAP values predominantly fall within the negative range when the twisted angle is between 5° and 12°, suggesting a specific range where this parameter effectively mitigates radius errors during the printing process.

caption: Three-dimensional lattice arrangement consisting of a 3 × 3 × 3 grid of topology-optimised unit cells, designed to achieve a 20% relative density structure.
summary: This visualization displays a 3 × 3 × 3 lattice configuration constructed from topology-optimised unit cells. Each unit cell measures 4 × 4 × 4 mm³, and the overall assembly is engineered to maintain a 20% relative density. The arrangement was facilitated using Magics software to create the final lattice structure.

caption: Koutecky–Levich (K–L) plots derived from the LSV data of GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 at different potentials.
summary: Koutecky–Levich plots for GF-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 illustrate the relationship between current density and rotation speed at various potentials. These plots are essential for determining the electron transfer kinetics, confirming the efficiency of the catalyst in facilitating the oxygen reduction reaction process within the specified potential range.

caption: Atomic configuration of the pristine FCC Co10Ni10Cu10Mo10W10 high-entropy alloy supercell modeled using a Special Quasirandom Structure (SQS) approach.
summary: This panel displays the atomic arrangement of a pristine FCC Co10Ni10Cu10Mo10W10 high-entropy alloy supercell. The model is constructed using an SQS approach to represent the random distribution of elements, serving as a baseline for investigating the influence of neighboring atoms on vacancy formation within the complex alloy lattice structure.

caption: Size-angle grain boundary distribution histogram for the 0.25 wt% SiC/TiC/Ti6Al4V region, corresponding to the red block area in panel (a).
summary: Panel (d) shows the grain boundary distribution for the 0.25 wt% SiC/TiC/Ti6Al4V region. By categorizing boundaries into LAGBs (2°–15°) and HAGBs (>15°), this histogram provides a detailed view of the grain orientation differences present in this specific composite region, allowing for comparison with the other zones analyzed in the figure.

caption: Van't Hoff plot displaying the thermodynamic equilibrium characteristics of the TiFe0.7Mn0.2Co0.1 alloy, derived from PCT measurements.
summary: This Van't Hoff plot for the TiFe0.7Mn0.2Co0.1 alloy is constructed from temperature-dependent PCT curves to extract thermodynamic parameters. By analyzing the slope and intercept of the plotted data, the study determines the thermodynamic stability and constants associated with the hydrogen storage performance of this specific alloy composition.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the FeCrMnNi CSA after 4 dpa irradiation and subsequent annealing at 673 K, with an inset showing the corresponding SAED pattern.
summary: Post-irradiation annealing at 673 K results in the preferential growth of helium bubbles at interfaces, as shown in this bright-field TEM micrograph. The inset SAED pattern confirms the retention of an FCC crystal structure, indicating the alloy remains a disordered solid solution without undergoing phase decomposition.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus true values for the parameter t, utilizing only PP and MAT variables as input features for the ANN regression model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the predictive performance of an ANN regression model trained on PP and MAT input features. The model demonstrates acceptable generalization capabilities, as evidenced by a predictive error of 19.8% on the cross-space test2 set, indicating a reliable correlation between predicted and true values for the parameter t.

caption: Phase map derived from scanning precession electron diffraction (SPED) data, illustrating the distribution of the sigma phase precipitate within the surrounding microstructure.
summary: This phase map, generated using scanning precession electron diffraction (SPED) data, visualizes the spatial distribution of sigma phase precipitates within the surrounding microstructure. The technique provides a detailed local view of the phase arrangement, serving as a basis for further crystallographic analysis of the material's local microstructure.

caption: UV-Vis-NIR absorption spectra comparing pure PLA and PLA-HSC composites across the 250–2500 nm wavelength range.
summary: The absorption spectra demonstrate that the incorporation of HSC fillers significantly enhances the light absorption capabilities of the PLA composites across the full solar spectrum. By comparing pure PLA with PLA-HSC, the data confirms that the filler effectively broadens and intensifies the material's ability to capture incident light energy.

caption: FTIR absorption spectrum of virgin PLA pellet, serving as a reference for the polymer matrix functional groups.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of the virgin PLA pellet provides a baseline reference for the polymer matrix. By comparing this spectrum with the composite data, researchers can identify specific PLA-related absorption bands, particularly in the 1000 to 400 cm-1 range, confirming the presence of PLA within the biocomposite material.

caption: Reconstructed APT tip of PBF-LB/M processed Ti-Ta alloy showing rod-like Ti-rich ω-phase particles highlighted by 83 at% Ti iso-concentration surfaces distributed within the β-phase matrix.
summary: This APT reconstruction reveals the 3D microstructure of PBF-LB/M processed Ti-Ta after thermo-mechanical cycling. Multiple rod-like particles, identified by 83 at% Ti iso-concentration surfaces, are uniformly distributed within the bcc β-phase matrix, providing clear evidence of the nanometric ω-phase particles formed during the experimental process.

caption: Microhardness profile across the weld zone, heat-affected zone, and base metal for the Alloy 609 filler metal.
summary: This panel presents the microhardness profile across the weld metal, heat-affected zone, and base metal for the Alloy 609 filler metal. The plot characterizes the mechanical hardness gradient across the welded joint, allowing for a direct comparison of the material's response to the welding process with this filler.

caption: Fluorescence decay curve and biexponential fitting for TPU/0.5 C composite at 465 nm emission.
summary: The fluorescence lifetime of the TPU/0.5 C composite is characterized by a nonlinear decay curve monitored at an emission wavelength of 465 nm. This decay profile is analyzed using a biexponential fitting function to determine the specific fluorescence lifetime characteristics of the material at room temperature.

caption: SAXS curves of DEPGM hydrogels prepared with different grafting ratios, revealing internal nanostructural organization.
summary: SAXS curves for DEPGM with different grafting ratios are presented. These diffraction profiles provide information on the nanostructural organization of the hydrogel network, showing how varying the grafting ratio influences the internal arrangement and scattering characteristics of the DEPGM material.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the polarization data, illustrating the OER kinetics for the various catalysts in 1 M KOH.
summary: Tafel plots were utilized to explore the intrinsic activities and oxygen evolution reaction kinetics of the Ni x Fe y nanofoam catalysts. By analyzing these plots, the electrochemical behavior and reaction mechanisms of the different catalysts were evaluated within the 1 M KOH electrolyte environment.

caption: Photograph capturing the additive manufacturing process of a ZrO2 sample.
summary: The photograph displays the printing process of a ZrO2 sample. The fabrication uses a white zirconia filament (Zetamix, France) at a temperature of 180 °C, a printing speed of 15 mm/s, a nozzle size of 0.4 mm, and a slicing layer height of 0.2 mm to achieve the desired geometry.

caption: Proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR) spectra of GG and GG-sialoglycan conjugates, highlighting chemical shifts indicative of successful conjugation.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra of GG and GG-sialoglycan conjugates are shown to confirm the structural integrity and successful synthesis of the conjugates. By analyzing the proton chemical shifts, researchers can verify the presence of specific molecular components and the chemical environment of the sialoglycan attachment to the GG backbone.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image of the rational approximant cluster monomer viewed along the pseudo-five-fold axis, demonstrating long-range periodic order.
summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging along the pseudo-five-fold axis reveals the long-range periodic order of the rational approximant cluster monomer. This observation confirms translational symmetry within a defect-free lattice, supporting the tile mode arrangement in a three-dimensional framework, which is essential for understanding the structural periodicity of this complex material system.

caption: Wettability assessment of TZ5-0 specimen using a droplet of Hanks' solution at 37 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the wettability of the TZ5-0 specimen. By applying a droplet of Hanks' solution at 37 °C, the surface behavior is observed, allowing for an analysis of how the specific processing condition of the TZ5-0 sample influences its interaction with the physiological-like test solution.

caption: Persistence diagram showing a set of points in the plane derived from the univariate time series, representing topological features.
summary: Represented in this scatter plot is the persistence diagram, which maps topological features extracted from the time series into a 2D plane. Each point corresponds to a specific topological characteristic, providing a visual summary of the data's structure based on the point cloud generated from the initial time series.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of the resin surface containing silver, showing increased surface roughness with an Sq value of 0.874 μm.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image illustrates the surface topology of the resin sample modified with silver. The incorporation of silver results in a significantly rougher surface compared to the unmodified resin, as evidenced by the measured root-mean-square roughness value of 0.874 μm, highlighting the distinct topological differences between the two samples.

caption: Structural model of the O-phase Ti2AlM intermetallic compound observed along the [100] direction, with central labels indicating Wyckoff positions.
summary: The [100] projection of the O-phase Ti2AlM crystal structure is shown, featuring labeled Wyckoff positions in the central representation. This view facilitates the identification of atomic sites within the unit cell, supporting the overall structural investigation of the O-phase intermetallic compounds presented in the paper.

caption: Optical photograph of a green part exhibiting smearing and cracking defects resulting from non-optimized printing parameters.
summary: This photograph displays a green part characterized by smearing and cracking defects. These irregularities, which occur during the printing process, are attributed to suboptimal printing parameters. Such smearing introduces significant structural cracks in the final printed part, highlighting the critical impact of process control on initial part integrity.

caption: Waterfall plot of 1D WAXS scattering profiles obtained from radial integration of complete diffractograms during loading cycles.
summary: This waterfall plot displays 1D WAXS scattering profiles derived from the radial integration of complete diffractograms. It illustrates the structural response of crystals oriented perpendicular to the stretching direction, which remain intact throughout the loading cycles, providing a comprehensive view of the material's scattering behavior during the experimental process.

caption: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) recording the evolution of stress, strain, and temperature over time during shape memory cycle (SMC) testing.
summary: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) data tracks the temporal changes in strain, stress, and temperature throughout the shape memory cycle tests. This measurement provides critical insights into the material's thermomechanical behavior, specifically monitoring the strain at the end of stretching, after force release, and following the recovery step.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry scans of untreated and heat-treated PLA samples evaluated at varying heat treatment durations while maintaining a constant temperature of 90 °C.
summary: DSC scans illustrate the thermal response of PLA samples across different heat treatment durations at a constant 90 °C. Increasing the treatment period results in an increased melting enthalpy slope, which suggests the formation of more perfect lamellae and improved crystal orientation within the polymer matrix during the heat treatment process.

caption: Total energy versus atomic volume plot comparing the BCC MoNbTaTiV alloy against its individual constituent elements, derived from DFT calculations.
summary: The total energy versus atomic volume relationship for the MoNbTaTiV alloy and its pure constituent elements is illustrated here. This plot, derived from DFT simulation results, provides a comparative analysis of the energetic stability and volume characteristics of the high-entropy alloy relative to its individual elemental components.

caption: Thermochemical stability diagram for the Cr-C-O system at 750 °C and 1 atm, illustrating equilibrium phases as a function of carbon activity and oxygen partial pressure.
summary: Calculated using FactSage, this thermochemical diagram for the Cr-C-O system at 750 °C shows equilibrium compounds relative to carbon activity and oxygen partial pressure. The analysis indicates that the equilibrium gas composition is highly oxidizing to chromium, with Cr2O3 serving as the stable phase across a wide range of conditions.

caption: Nyquist diagrams showing the electrochemical impedance response of LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi samples after 1 hour of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, with solid lines representing the corresponding fitting results.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance behavior of LPBF dual-phase and [001]-textured single-phase NiTi alloys following one hour of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. These diagrams, which include fitted solid lines, are used to compare the electrochemical interactions and corrosion resistance of the passive films formed on both samples.

caption: Superimposed 1H–13C HSQC NMR spectra of pure CHES (blue) and F-CHES 1 (red) highlighting the presence of specific signals.
summary: The panel presents a comparison between pure CHES and the F-CHES 1 sample using superimposed HSQC NMR spectra. This visualization substantiates the selective incorporation of CHES, with the spectral data confirming the presence of characteristic signals that distinguish the modified material from the control.

caption: Radar diagram illustrating the relative performance of various Metal Additive Manufacturing (MAM) processes across multiple evaluation criteria.
summary: This radar diagram provides a comparative performance assessment of different MAM processes. By averaging scaled scores for each criterion, the visualization ensures a balanced evaluation. It serves as a foundational guide for SMEs to conduct nuanced assessments of MAM technologies, highlighting the distinct advantages and challenges inherent in each process.

caption: Arrhenius plot of the estimated relaxation times as a function of inverse measuring temperature, yielding an activation enthalpy of 230 kJ/mol.
summary: The estimated relaxation times derived from isothermal heat-treatment measurements are plotted against the inverse measuring temperature. This Arrhenius analysis yields an activation enthalpy of 230 kJ/mol, which is consistent with the activation energy determined for the first exothermic reaction observed in the material's thermal response.

caption: Confocal micrograph of AA F Ti particles exhibiting a characteristic silver luster due to minimal surface oxidation.
summary: Confocal microscopy of the AA F Ti particle reveals a distinct silver luster. This appearance is attributed to the minimal surface oxidation state of the material prior to any compression testing. The image confirms the baseline surface condition for the untreated powder sample before further thermal processing.

caption: Final failure state of the HPC-W1 specimen following complete fracture.
summary: Complete failure of the HPC-W1 specimen is depicted in this final stage of the fracture process. The image shows the ultimate structural breakdown of the material, representing the conclusion of the mechanical testing sequence where the crack has fully compromised the integrity of the sample under the applied load.

caption: Temperature variation profiles over time for Spot1, Spot2, Box1 (shell mean), and Line1 (winding mean) comparing loaded (LC) and unloaded (UC) conditions.
summary: Temperature variations for Spot1, Spot2, Box1, and Line1 are plotted over time to compare loaded and unloaded conditions. The data highlights that the presence of a load contributes to heat dissipation in the solenoid, resulting in a lower temperature increase during LC measurements compared to the UC measurements.

caption: Scratch hardness number and fracture toughness values for Ti6Al4V5Cr and Ti6Al4V alloys plotted against applied load.
summary: This plot demonstrates the mechanical properties of the two alloys, specifically scratch hardness and fracture toughness, across varying applied loads. The data reveals that the Ti6Al4V5Cr alloy maintains higher scratch hardness and fracture toughness values compared to the Ti6Al4V alloy throughout the range of applied loads tested.

caption: V CPD map and corresponding line profile of as-forged Al0.3CoCrFeNi alloy showing a relatively uniform potential distribution across the single A1 phase.
summary: The V CPD map and line profile for as-forged Al0.3CoCrFeNi reveal a uniform potential distribution. This consistency is characteristic of the single A1 phase present in the alloy under this condition, as confirmed by the SKPFM analysis which shows no significant potential gradients across the microstructure.

caption: Cooling dilatometry curve for specimen S4, demonstrating the tangent-intersection method to identify the martensite-start temperature of 310 °C.
summary: Cooling dilatometry for specimen S4 yields a martensite-start temperature of 310 °C, determined by the tangent-intersection of the linear contraction segment. This thermal analysis indicates that Ti microalloying additions do not exert a clear effect on the martensite-start temperature, as observed in the comparative data for this specific specimen.

caption: Microstructural map for the Al-Fe-Si ternary system showing predicted regions and experimental data points where the Columnar-to-Equiaxed Transition (CET) occurs at β = 1.14.
summary: This microstructural map for the Al-Fe-Si ternary system integrates theoretical predictions with experimental findings. It highlights the specific conditions under which the Columnar-to-Equiaxed Transition (CET) is observed, confirming that the transition consistently occurs at a critical growth restriction parameter value of β = 1.14 in this multicomponent system.

caption: Thermal expansion measurement results comparing as-LPBFed Invar 36 and as-LPBFed Invar 36-1.5TiAl specimens.
summary: This plot displays the thermal expansion behavior of as-LPBFed Invar 36 and Invar 36-1.5TiAl specimens. The data illustrates that while the addition of TiAl particles is intended to enhance mechanical properties, it simultaneously results in an increased coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) for the modified Invar 36 alloy.

caption: Bubble diagram illustrating the differential expression of MC3T3-E1 related pathways in 40%HA-PEEK and 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK compared to bare PEEK.
summary: This bubble diagram highlights the significant activation of the mTOR signaling pathway in 40%HA-PEEK compared to PEEK, which promotes cell cycle progression and survival. Furthermore, 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK maintains robust mTOR activity, indicating that the incorporation of HA and AgNPs effectively modulates osteogenic pathways to enhance cellular growth and survival signals.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image of disordered precipitates in the Ag-added alloy aged at 200 °C for 2 h, showing random LDC substructures.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image captures the disordered precipitates in the Ag-added alloy following peak aging at 200 °C for 2 hours. The microstructure is characterized by a prevalence of random LDC substructures, which are highlighted by dashed green circles to distinguish them within the precipitate matrix.

caption: Indenter penetration depth trajectories plotted against time for Bicarbonate samples subjected to varying consolidation stresses.
summary: This plot illustrates the temporal evolution of indenter penetration depth during impact testing of Bicarbonate. The trajectories demonstrate how penetration depth increases over time, with the magnitude of this increase being parametrically dependent on the applied consolidation stresses, highlighting the material's mechanical response under different initial loading conditions.

caption: Statistical distribution of equivalent grain diameters and aspect ratios for the LPBF-processed material, derived from EBSD data.
summary: This histogram displays the grain size distribution of the LPBF material, showing a mean equivalent grain diameter of approximately 32 μm. An inset graph provides the corresponding aspect ratio distribution, which reveals an average aspect ratio of about 4.2, characterizing the grain morphology of the laser-processed sample.

caption: Magnetic induction-dependent total magnetic losses for 3D printed and standard toroids evaluated at a fixed frequency of 1 MHz and a temperature of 25 °C.
summary: Figure 13b displays the evolution of core losses as a function of magnetic induction at a fixed frequency of 1 MHz and a temperature of 25 °C. This comparison highlights the performance differences between 3D printed and standard processed toroids under varying induction levels at high-frequency operating conditions.

caption: Comparison of experimental yield strength derived from hardness measurements against theoretical predictions as a function of ageing time, showing the cumulative contributions of intrinsic, grain boundary, work hardening, solid solution, and precipitate strengthening mechanisms.
summary: This plot compares experimental yield strength values derived from hardness measurements with theoretical model predictions over varying ageing times. The model integrates five distinct strengthening mechanisms, including intrinsic, grain boundary, work hardening, solid solution, and precipitate effects, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's mechanical evolution during the ageing process.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves showing the cathodic reduction of 0.1 M V4+ at a 50 mV·s⁻¹ scan rate, highlighting how varying the catalyst composition influences the vanadium reduction performance.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves showing the cathodic reduction of 0.1 M V4+ at a 50 mV·s⁻¹ scan rate, highlighting how varying the catalyst composition influences the vanadium reduction performance. This showcases the catalytic activity of various materials for the reduction of V4+ to V3.5+, a vital half-cell reaction in vanadium redox flow batteries.

caption: Predicted failure loads derived from FAD versus experimental failure loads for T benchmark specimens.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the accuracy of the FAD approach by comparing predicted failure loads against experimental data for T benchmark specimens. The analysis follows the procedure applied to all specimens, where predicted failures are compared with experimental results to validate the effectiveness of the FAD methodology.

caption: Secondary thermal image recording the flame shock testing process on the Ag/Pt thin film thermocouple array mounted on the blunt body.
summary: Secondary thermal image recording the flame shock testing process on the Ag/Pt thin film thermocouple array mounted on the blunt body. This visual data collection demonstrates the real-time monitoring of the thermocouple array as it is subjected to a 1300 °C flame, providing critical insights into its thermal performance.

caption: Surface roughness prediction results showcasing the model's effectiveness in estimating surface quality metrics.
summary: Surface roughness prediction results are shown to demonstrate the model's high predictive accuracy. These results confirm that the model acts as a reliable proxy for establishing process-structure-performance relationships, thereby facilitating the optimization of process parameters and providing accurate estimations of surface quality metrics for the studied material.

caption: Comparison of absorption spectra between cathodic powders leached for 50 minutes via horn sonication and Co(II) precursors in reline deep eutectic solvent at varying concentrations, with the latter diluted eightfold.
summary: Comparison of the absorption spectra for cathodic powders leached for 50 minutes against Co(II) precursor standards in reline DES highlights the chemical composition. The reference confirms that the horn-sonication-assisted leaching process demonstrates higher selectivity for cobalt compared to nickel, as evidenced by the spectral features observed in this comparison.

caption: EDS elemental map showing the distribution of Nickel (Ni) in the second-phase particles.
summary: The EDS map for Nickel (Ni) shows its distribution within the analyzed region. When compared with other elemental maps, it helps determine the chemical makeup of the second-phase particles and their relationship to the surrounding TGO matrix.

caption: t-SNE projection of bimodal microstructure fingerprints, with a color map indicating the distribution of grain size.
summary: Representing the bimodal fingerprints of the LFTi64BL dataset, this t-SNE plot utilizes two components to map the encoded data. A color map is applied to the plot to denote grain size, facilitating the analysis of how morphological metrics correlate with the learned representations of the bimodal microstructures.

caption: Atomic configuration of the alloy at a strain rate of 10^7 s^-1 in the stable flow stress region, displaying the distribution of HCP structures.
summary: Representing the stable flow stress region at a strain rate of 10^7 s^-1, this atomic configuration shows the distribution of HCP structures. When compared with higher strain rate results, it demonstrates a relatively lower fraction of HCP structures, indicating lower dislocation density under these specific deformation conditions.

caption: Current-potential (I-V) characteristics of HPE60 i-wi samples with varying cross-sectional areas ranging from 1x1 mm to 5x5 mm measured at rest.
summary: This panel displays the I-V curves for HPE60 i-wi materials with cross-sections of 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, and 5x5 mm. The data illustrates the electrical response of these materials under DC conditions at rest, providing a baseline for understanding how cross-sectional geometry influences the current-potential behavior of the i-wi system.

caption: Maximum atomic and electronic temperatures for 30 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in NiFeCr.
summary: This panel depicts the maximum atomic and electronic temperatures for 30 keV Ni 2T-MD cascade simulations in the ternary NiFeCr alloy system. Results are aggregated from twelve separate cascade events, offering a detailed look at the thermal behavior and peak temperature variations within this specific alloy composition during irradiation.

caption: HP4194A impedance analyzer utilized for conducting electrical impedance measurements.
summary: This panel displays the HP4194A impedance analyzer, which serves as the primary instrumentation for performing impedance measurements. The device is essential for capturing the frequency-dependent electrical response of the material samples, providing the raw data necessary for subsequent calculations of effective conductivity and complex capacitance as described in the study.

caption: High-rate discharge (HRD) performance of LaMgNi3.6M0.4 (M = Ni, Co, Mn, Cu, Al) alloy electrodes measured at 303 K across varying discharge current densities.
summary: This plot illustrates the high-rate discharge (HRD) performance of LaMgNi3.6M0.4 alloy electrodes at 303 K. HRD values, which indicate electrochemical kinetics, are calculated based on discharge capacities at current densities ranging from 300 to 1200 mA/g relative to a 60 mA/g baseline, providing a comprehensive assessment of the electrode rate capability.

caption: EBSD phase map of the LPBF-HIP specimen after 1000 h of LBE exposure, indicating negligible FCC-to-BCC phase transformation.
summary: The EBSD phase map provides a detailed look at the phase composition of the LPBF-HIP specimen following 1000 hours of LBE exposure. The data confirms that there is negligible FCC-to-BCC phase transformation within the corroded regions, indicating that the material's primary phase structure remains stable despite the harsh corrosive conditions encountered.

caption: Schematic representation of the laser hot wire additive manufacturing (LHWAM) system, illustrating the integration of a laser heat source and a hot wire power source.
summary: This schematic illustrates the LHWAM experimental equipment, which functions as a hybrid-source additive manufacturing process. By integrating a laser heat source with a hot wire power source, the system is designed to effectively reduce the overall heat input during the manufacturing process, as described in the reference.

caption: Single shot synchrotron X-ray diffraction pole figures and inverse pole figures for Sample 1, illustrating the crystallographic texture.
summary: This panel presents the single shot synchrotron X-ray diffraction results for Sample 1. The pole figures and inverse pole figures provide a high-resolution view of the material's texture, which is subsequently compared against the referential EBSD data to determine the matching quality and accuracy of the synchrotron measurement technique.

caption: Solidification temperature range (STR) across the Fe-Cu-Ni ternary system, illustrating regions of varying thermal stability.
summary: This ternary phase diagram displays the solidification temperature range for the Fe-Cu-Ni system. Calculation results indicate that high STR values are concentrated in regions with low Ni content, reaching a peak of 523 °C at the 90Fe-10Cu-0Ni composition, which helps in qualitatively estimating cracking susceptibility within the alloy system.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of the OQ + AT treated specimen, with yellow dashed lines marking grain boundaries.
summary: The KAM map of the OQ + AT specimen highlights local misorientation gradients, with yellow dashed lines delineating grain boundaries. This visualization provides evidence of the internal stress state and dislocation distribution, which accounts for the high yield and tensile strengths but limited elongation of this specific specimen.

caption: Schematic illustration of the coating process, detailing the initial positioning of the laser nozzle relative to the workpiece edge and the subsequent movement of the workpiece toward the chuck during rotation.
summary: This schematic illustrates the coating process, specifically highlighting the initial laser nozzle positioning 20 to 30 mm from the workpiece edge. It depicts the controlled movement of the workpiece, which travels 10 mm toward the chuck while undergoing rotation, providing a clear visual representation of the operational parameters during coating.

caption: Live/dead staining fluorescence images of BMSCs cultured in the extract solution of manganese-doped strontium-magnesium whitlockite scaffolds.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images reveal the live/dead staining of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) after incubation in the extract solution of manganese-doped strontium-magnesium whitlockite scaffolds. These images provide a visual assessment of cell viability and distribution within the extract environment, confirming the suitability of the scaffold extracts for cell culture.

caption: Optical micrograph of the AM sample showing a coarse, layered structure with a mean grain size of 45 ± 3 µm.
summary: The AM sample displays a coarse, layered microstructure characterized by a mean grain size of 45 ± 3 µm. This morphology is consistent with the alternating thermal cycles inherent in the WAAM process, which promote irregular grain growth and result in a broad grain-size distribution ranging from 20 to 100 µm.

caption: Successive O-Cr-O basal planes illustrating the local atomic environment of octahedral and tetrahedral interstitial sites, where chromium ions are represented as grey spheres and oxygen ions as smaller red spheres.
summary: This atomic model displays successive O-Cr-O basal planes, highlighting the geometry of octahedral and tetrahedral interstitial sites. Chromium ions are depicted as grey spheres and oxygen ions as red spheres. Chromium interstitials preferentially occupy 6b octahedral sites, while oxygen interstitials also favor octahedral sites, specifically displaced along the [0001] axis.

caption: SHAP dependence plot displaying the relationship between specimen state and effective stress ratio.
summary: Analyzing this plot alongside panels (e) and (f) is essential because stress amplitude, mean stress, and stress ratio are highly interrelated. The SHAP values for each state appear on the same vertical line, which may result in overlapping data points due to the categorical nature of the state variable.

caption: Schematic representation of the corrosion-erosion (CE) mechanism in cast nickel-aluminum bronze (NAB) alloy.
summary: This schematic illustrates the corrosion-erosion mechanism for cast NAB alloy. The process involves CE impacts that accelerate material degradation by disrupting protective surface films, thereby exposing fresh metal to the environment. This mechanism highlights the susceptibility of the material to surface damage during exposure to corrosive media.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 0 mA specimen showing martensitic laths containing dislocation tangles and localized dislocation cells.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the typical microstructure of the 0 mA specimen, characterized by martensitic laths. The analysis reveals the presence of dislocation tangles throughout the structure, with a small number of dislocation cells formed in regions where these tangles are densely distributed.

caption: Vickers hardness values comparing as-cast and heat-treated nanocomposite samples.
summary: This figure presents the Vickers hardness values for as-cast and nanocomposite samples. The data demonstrates that the hardness of both the as-cast and the nanocomposite materials markedly improved following heat treatment, indicating that thermal processing is an effective method for enhancing the mechanical properties of these prepared nanocomposite systems.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) response of samples before and after nitriding treatment, highlighting a semicircular capacitive resistance arc in the high-frequency region.
summary: The Nyquist plot displays the EIS response of the material before and after nitriding. A semicircular capacitive resistance arc is observed in the high-frequency region, which indicates a single and dominant electrochemical mechanism associated with charge transfer at the electrode–electrolyte interface, reflecting the surface behavior of the samples.

caption: Plate-twist load–displacement curves for three distinct core designs, where solid lines represent mean responses and shaded bands denote experimental deviation.
summary: Plate-twist load–displacement curves for three core designs demonstrate a consistent mechanical response characterized by an initial linear increase followed by a gradual transition to a plateau without abrupt force drops. Shaded bands illustrate high repeatability across three test replicates, confirming minimal scatter and reliable performance across the tested core configurations.

caption: Ceramic scaffold architecture featuring a gradient pore structure generated via the Voronoi-Tessellation principle to accommodate localized mechanical requirements.
summary: This ceramic scaffold utilizes a Voronoi-Tessellation design to create a gradient pore structure. By varying porosity spatially, the scaffold effectively matches local mechanical demands within the mandibular region. This approach demonstrates a sophisticated method for tailoring the internal geometry of maxillofacial prostheses to optimize structural performance and biological integration.

caption: Bright field TEM image showing the morphology of an MC-type carbide located within the IL area after heat treatment.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging reveals the structural morphology of an MC-type carbide found within the IL area following heat treatment. This observation is part of a broader investigation into the two distinct types of carbides present in the matrix or grain boundaries of the IL area after processing.

caption: Surface height profile of the TD_4 powder bed illustrating increased surface porosity and inhomogeneous packing.
summary: Surface height profiling of the TD_4 powder bed demonstrates a deterioration in packing quality compared to the TD_8 sample. The presence of increased surface pores is attributed to inhomogeneous powder packing, which correlates with the lower theoretical density of the powder used in this specific experimental configuration.

caption: Electronic band structure diagram calculated for the I-WP unit cell architecture at a uniform relative density of 32%.
summary: This panel displays the electronic band structure for an I-WP unit cell characterized by a uniform relative density of 32%. The plot illustrates the dispersion relations of the electronic states within the periodic lattice, providing fundamental insight into the electronic properties of this specific structural configuration at the defined density.

caption: Segregation of Ni atoms and formation of vacancies on the alloy surface.
summary: This panel illustrates the migration paths of nickel atoms on the alloy surface during oxidation. The process involves the segregation of nickel atoms, which results in the creation of vacancies, further demonstrating the dynamic structural changes occurring on the alloy surface during the oxidation simulation.

caption: Isothermal entropy change as a function of temperature for the AQ sample under applied magnetic fields ranging from 1 T to 6 T.
summary: The isothermal entropy change for the AQ sample is plotted against temperature for applied magnetic fields between 1 T and 6 T. These curves demonstrate the magnetic response of the material, and their full width at half maximum is used to estimate the temperature integration range for calculating the refrigeration capacity.

caption: Weak-beam dark-field micrograph of NiCoFeCrMn irradiated to 0.1 dpa at 773 K, imaged using g = (200) reflection.
summary: This weak-beam dark-field micrograph displays the initial defect evolution in the NiCoFeCrMn alloy after ion irradiation to a dose of 0.1 dpa at 773 K. The image, captured under (g, 5g) conditions with a (200) reflection vector, provides a baseline for observing microstructural changes in the four-element alloy system.

caption: Gamma-surface plot for pure nickel with a hydrogen atom positioned directly within the slip plane.
summary: This gamma-surface plot illustrates the energy landscape of pure nickel when a hydrogen atom is placed directly in the slip plane. The simulation reveals significant fluctuations in the surface energy, which are attributed to substantial changes in interatomic distances occurring during the slip process within the crystal lattice.

caption: Time-dependent UV-Vis absorbance spectra illustrating the reduction of 4-NP catalyzed by U-type Pd/C CR.
summary: This panel presents the UV-Vis spectra for the reduction of 4-NP catalyzed by a U-type Pd/C reactor. These spectral measurements allow for the calculation of conversion versus time plots, facilitating a comparative analysis of the catalytic performance between different reactor configurations during the reduction of 4-nitrophenol.

caption: Interlaminar shear failure mode of a 3DP-CFRP bar with 4-mm diameter and 32.6% fiber volume fraction tested at an s/d ratio of 4:1, showing stress concentration and multiple cracks distributed along both sides of the neutral axis.
summary: This photograph displays the interlaminar shear failure mode of a 3DP-CFRP bar tested at an s/d ratio of 4:1. The specimen exhibits significant stress concentration, resulting in multiple interlaminar shear cracks distributed along both sides of the neutral axis, consistent with observed failure patterns in short-beam specimens.

caption: Tensile strength comparison of 3D-printed neat PLA, TCNP-reinforced PLA, and BCNP-reinforced PLA composites under varying crosshead speeds, print orientations, and infill percentages.
summary: This figure illustrates the tensile behavior of 3D-printed neat PLA alongside PLA composites reinforced with Terminalia Chebula nanoparticles (TCNP) and bamboo charcoal particles (BCNP). The analysis evaluates mechanical performance across diverse processing parameters, specifically examining the influence of varying crosshead speeds, print orientations, and infill percentages on the overall tensile strength.

caption: Bode plots showing the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle for the A-DED and LA-DED specimens.
summary: Bode plots are provided to complement the impedance analysis, illustrating the frequency-dependent behavior of the A-DED and LA-DED specimens in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Together with the Nyquist plots, these data facilitate a comprehensive evaluation of the corrosion resistance and electrochemical properties of the two tested specimens.

caption: Hardness evolution measured across the graded layers of the AlN/Mo composite, highlighting the impact of the composition exponent on mechanical properties.
summary: Hardness evolution across the graded layers is presented to show how the composition exponent p influences mechanical properties. When p > 1, the grading between layers becomes notably smoother, which contributes to improved stiffness and mechanical performance, reflecting the successful optimization of the functionally graded AlN/Mo composite structure.

caption: Absorbance-time profile measured via UV-Vis spectroscopy, illustrating a significant decline in absorbance between 5 and 7 minutes.
summary: The absorbance-time curve obtained from UV-Vis measurements reveals a marked decrease in absorbance values occurring between approximately 5 and 7 minutes for all tested compositions. This rapid drop in the spectral data correlates with the sedimentation process, indicating a reduction in the concentration of suspended particles over time.

caption: Normalized mass spectrum and correlation histogram for M23C6 carbides acquired at 100 pJ, exhibiting the absence of Ti and the presence of complex C6 4+ and C12 4+ peaks at 18 and 36 Da.
summary: M23C6 carbides display a distinct mass spectrum lacking titanium signals. Despite the different composition compared to MC, this carbide also exhibits complex peaks at 18 and 36 Da, corresponding to C6 4+ and C12 4+ ions. These features arise from the influence of carbon content on evaporation behavior and ion dissociation.

caption: Surface reconstruction generated from the point cloud data of the representative printed sample.
summary: The surface of the representative printed sample is reconstructed from point cloud data. This 3D representation allows for a direct comparison with the reference model, facilitating the identification of dimensional deviations and surface irregularities that occur during the additive manufacturing process of the printed object.

caption: Power-voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC200GT device evaluated at various temperature values.
summary: This panel presents the power-voltage (P-V) characteristics for the KC200GT device. By plotting power output against voltage at multiple temperatures, the figure demonstrates the thermal dependence of the device's power delivery, consistent with the experimental characterization of the KC200GT module described in the research findings.

caption: Evolution of first principal strain fields in 316L stainless steel specimens during tensile testing, highlighting localized deformation patterns.
summary: This panel displays the evolution of first principal strain fields in 316L specimens during tensile testing. Digital Image Correlation (DIC) results provide a critical examination of the failure mode, revealing localized strain concentrations that contribute to the material's mechanical response and eventual crack initiation observed during the tensile test.

caption: Magnified view of the (101) α/α′ reference peak for the 320 W samples, demonstrating peak broadening and shifts associated with varying scanning speeds.
summary: This panel provides a magnified view of the (101) α/α′ reflection for 320 W samples. The observed peak broadening and systematic shifts indicate significant changes in microstrain and crystallite size. These findings confirm that higher scanning speeds lead to increased peak broadening, reflecting the impact of cooling rates on the microstructure.

caption: First derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves illustrating the rate of mass loss for pure PEEK and CF/PEEK composite powders.
summary: First derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves illustrate the rate of mass loss for pure PEEK and CF/PEEK composite powders. This analysis of the first derivative of the TGA curves was performed to gain further insight into the thermal decomposition behavior and stability characteristics of the tested powder materials.

caption: Partial density of states (pDOS) for Fe, Co, and Ni in the equiatomic FeCoNi base alloy, represented by full lines, dashed lines, and dots, respectively.
summary: This plot displays the element-resolved partial density of states for the equiatomic FeCoNi base alloy. The electronic structure is characterized by distinct curves for Fe, Co, and Ni, illustrating their individual contributions to the total density of states within the alloy system as determined by the electronic structure analysis.

caption: Pole figure of the P60V150 LPBF pure Zn sample indicating a stronger recrystallization texture compared to the P50V150 condition, resulting from fuller grain growth.
summary: Higher laser power of 60 W leads to more abundant heat storage, facilitating a more complete recrystallization and growth process. Consequently, the P60V150 sample exhibits larger grain sizes and a stronger recrystallization texture compared to the P50V150 sample, despite the absence of an obvious preferred orientation overall.

caption: GMAW droplet landing location distribution showing a fixed, concentrated position at the intersection of the welding torch axis and the molten pool.
summary: GMAW droplet transfer landing points are concentrated at the intersection of the welding torch axis and the molten pool. The landing position remains approximately fixed throughout the process, demonstrating a stable and consistent droplet transfer behavior compared to the dynamic variations observed in HLAW processes.

caption: Projection of printed object samples onto the established PCA model, showing a third data cluster that overlaps with both raw filament sample groups.
summary: Projection of the printed samples onto the PCA model resulted in a third group forming. This new cluster overlaps with both the inside and outside sample groups, although it exhibits a higher degree of similarity with the inside filament samples, indicating the impact of the printing process on material properties.

caption: Representative 2D LSCM image of an indent in NC Ni, showing the surface indentation footprint and associated pile-up features.
summary: Displayed is a 2D LSCM image of an indent in NC Ni, capturing the surface footprint after CSM testing. This visualization allows for the assessment of the indentation geometry and pile-up, which are critical parameters for calculating the real contact area during the mechanical characterization of the nanocrystalline material.

caption: Top-down view of indentation imprints and associated surface pileups, with color-coded height mapping representing surface topography post-retraction.
summary: This top-down AFM visualization displays the surface topography of indent pits and their surrounding pileups. The color-coded height map illustrates the deformation profile relative to the original surface after the indenter has been retracted, providing a clear spatial representation of the imprints generated around the specific indent points.

caption: Tauc plot of pure SnO2 nanoparticles showing a calculated optical bandgap of 3.50 eV.
summary: This Tauc plot represents the optical bandgap determination for pure SnO2 nanoparticles. By plotting (αhν)2 against photon energy (hν), the bandgap value is derived as 3.50 eV. This graphical analysis provides a quantitative measure of the electronic transition energy characteristic of the pure SnO2 nanostructured material.

caption: Total structure factor S(q) for Cu75Ag25 derived from MD simulation results, plotted with a 0.5 x-axis shift relative to adjacent curves.
summary: This panel displays the total structure factor S(q) for the Cu75Ag25 alloy obtained from MD simulations. The curve is shifted by 0.5 along the x-axis to facilitate comparison with neighboring data sets, showing a shape characteristic of the Cu-Ag alloy system.

caption: Near-infrared (NIR) emission spectra centered at 1538 nm for the SL:Er,Yb phosphor compared to the CsPbBr1.5I1.5 + SL:Er,Yb composite, recorded under 980 nm excitation.
summary: Near-infrared emission characteristics are presented for the SL:Er,Yb phosphor and its composite with CsPbBr1.5I1.5. The spectra focus on the emission peak at 1538 nm, providing a comparison of the NIR performance between the pure phosphor and the composite material when subjected to 980 nm excitation.

caption: EBSD-IPF map of the LPBF-fabricated SS316L sample tested at room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 in the first orientation.
summary: This EBSD-IPF map illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution of an LPBF-fabricated SS316L sample. The specimen was subjected to tensile testing at room temperature with a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1. This visualization provides essential microstructural data regarding the grain orientation and texture development within the material under these specific loading conditions.

caption: Ti–C binary phase diagram identifying the eutectic point at approximately 1.8 wt% carbon, illustrating the formation of eutectic TiC below this concentration and primary TiC above it.
summary: The Ti–C binary phase diagram defines the solidification behavior of TiC/Ti6Al4V composites. With a eutectic point at 1.8 wt% carbon, the diagram shows that carbon concentration dictates the formation of either eutectic or primary TiC. This phase relationship is critical for controlling the microstructure of peri-eutectic TiC/Ti6Al4V matrix composites.

caption: Potential-composition diagram for Ni74.5Al22Y0.5Nb3 at 750 °C, displaying thermodynamic phase stability.
summary: Calculated at 750 °C for Ni74.5Al22Y0.5Nb3, this diagram reveals structural changes over log[P(O2)]. The computational results align with the oxidized γ' phase. According to these calculations, Nb2O5 eventually becomes thermodynamically unstable, enabling the formation of a pure, continuous Al2O3 layer that impedes further internal oxidation of the alloy.

caption: Relative hardness increase of Hastelloy X and Haynes 230 alloys plotted against ion fluence, demonstrating a more pronounced radiation-induced hardening effect in Hastelloy X compared to Haynes 230.
summary: This plot illustrates the relative hardness increase of Hastelloy X and Haynes 230 as a function of ion fluence. The data reveals that ion irradiation induces a visible radiation hardening effect in both materials, with Hastelloy X exhibiting a significantly more intensive hardening response than Haynes 230 under identical irradiation conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum showing high concentrations of Ti, Al, and O, confirming the presence of a non-metallic oxide-based inclusion.
summary: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy spectrum reveals high concentrations of titanium, aluminum, and oxygen within the crack-initiating inclusion. These findings indicate a non-metallic oxide-based composition. The detection of significant oxygen levels is attributed to the atmospheric conditions maintained during the SLM thermal process, confirming the inclusion's chemical nature.

caption: Isothermal differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) signals for CSP batches measured in an N2/O2 atmosphere, with base signals represented by dotted lines.
summary: Isothermal DSC measurements in an N2/O2 atmosphere provide further evidence of the stabilizing effects of additives. These signals, plotted against base lines, confirm the previous findings from rheological tests, demonstrating how different stabilizers influence the thermal response of the CSP material under constant high-temperature conditions.

caption: Comparative feature importance analysis excluding the spatter region index group, revealing a distribution pattern highly similar to the full-feature model.
summary: Removing the spatter region index group from the input set yields a feature importance plot that closely mirrors the results obtained when all four groups are considered. This indicates that the spatter region index has a minimal impact on the overall predictive performance of the random forest model.

caption: Raman spectra acquired at four distinct locations (A–D) on the counterpart wear scar following a sliding wear test at a 1 N load against the SLM-G-b sample.
summary: Raman spectra collected at points A-D on the counterpart wear scar after 1 N sliding wear tests reveal the presence of a carbonaceous amorphous transfer film. This is evidenced by broad spectral features centered in the D and G peak regions, indicating carbon-based material accumulation on the counterpart surface.

caption: Thermal dilation curve of LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V alloy during heating to 940 ℃, highlighting a minor inflection at 550 ℃ and a pronounced inflection point at 870 ℃ corresponding to the α′→α + β phase transformation.
summary: This thermal dilation curve illustrates the phase transformation behavior of LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V alloy heated to 940 ℃. The data reveals a minor inflection point at 550 ℃, representing the α′→α + β transition, followed by a more significant, pronounced inflection point observed near 870 ℃ during the heating process.

caption: Live/dead staining micrographs of HFE-145 cells co-cultured with F-GelMA scaffolds, displayed at two different magnifications to highlight cell attachment.
summary: Live/dead staining micrographs of HFE-145 cells co-cultured with F-GelMA scaffolds provide visual evidence of cell attachment. The images, captured at two different magnifications, confirm that the scaffold effectively supports the attachment and promotes the proliferation of these normal cells, indicating excellent biocompatibility and suitability for cell culture applications.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the average γ′ phase radius in Ni–20Co–14Al and Ni–20Co–14Al–8Cr alloys at 900 °C, calculated via TC-PRISMA.
summary: This plot illustrates the growth kinetics of the γ′ phase at 900 °C for two alloy compositions. Calculated using the TC-PRISMA module based on classic nucleation theory, the data shows that after 10 seconds, the coarsening rate of the average radius in the Ni–20Co–14Al alloy significantly exceeds that of the Cr-containing variant.

caption: Top-down view of the Al-10.5 at% and Re-4.5 at% iso-surfaces across the entire cross-section of the APT tip.
summary: This top-view reconstruction presents the Al-10.5 at% and Re-4.5 at% iso-surfaces across the full cross-section of the APT tip. By observing the entire cross-section, the spatial distribution and extent of these compositional features are clearly delineated, offering a comprehensive view of the internal structure of the analyzed alloy.

caption: Weak-beam dark-field micrograph of Ni irradiated to 2 dpa at 773 K, featuring an abnormally large loop indicated by an arrowhead.
summary: This weak-beam dark-field micrograph of Ni at 2 dpa and 773 K reveals the largest observed defect loop, which measures 173.6 nm along its major axis. An arrowhead marks this abnormally large loop, illustrating the significant defect growth occurring at this higher ion dose under (g, 5g) imaging conditions.

caption: Inhibition zone assays for S. aureus and E. coli cultivated on the three material groups, showing a distinct clear zone surrounding the 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK samples.
summary: Inhibition zone assays for S. aureus and E. coli cultivated on the three material groups show a distinct clear zone surrounding the 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK samples. While PEEK showed no inhibition, a tiny inhibition ring existed for 40%HA-PEEK, indicating that the silver nanoparticles significantly enhance the antibacterial activity of the material.

caption: Schematic representation of the supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) test loop designed for evaluating heat exchanger (HX) performance.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental sCO2 test loop constructed to characterize heat exchanger performance under supercritical conditions. The diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the system architecture, detailing the flow paths and components necessary to maintain the supercritical state required for accurate thermal performance testing of the heat exchanger.

caption: Total dissipated energy (Etot) plotted against initial stiffness (S0) for the eight selected designs.
summary: Total dissipated energy, Etot, is evaluated against initial stiffness, S0, for the eight selected designs. The results indicate that the introduction of a compliant interlayer consistently increases the total dissipated energy during fracture, a trend attributed to the crack-arresting effect, which remains effective regardless of the specific interlayer geometry.

caption: Stability assessment of the PtFe alloy catalyst performed via cyclic voltammetry measurements at a scan rate of 50 mV/s in 0.1 M KOH.
summary: Stability testing of the PtFe alloy catalyst was conducted using cyclic voltammetry at a scan rate of 50 mV/s in 0.1 M KOH. As stability is a core parameter for oxygen reduction reaction catalysts, these measurements confirm the durability of the PtFe alloy under electrochemical cycling conditions.

caption: UV–vis absorption spectra and digital photographs of RhB dye solution before evaporation and the resulting condensed water after purification.
summary: This panel presents the UV–vis absorption spectra and digital images of RhB dye solution to evaluate purification efficiency. The comparison between the initial dye solution and the condensed water after evaporation demonstrates the successful removal of RhB, confirming the potential of the evaporator for treating industrial wastewater containing organic dyes.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectrum showing the W 4f core level region for the NiW alloy coating after 7 days of immersion.
summary: High-resolution XPS analysis of the W 4f region confirms the presence and chemical state of tungsten on the NiW alloy surface after 7 days of immersion. This tungsten-rich protective layer is essential for the coating's durability, as it facilitates the development of a dense and adherent passivation film.

caption: FIB-prepared cross-sectional SEM image of the wrought Ti6Al4V specimen subsurface, showing increased crack density compared to the LPBF counterpart after tribocorrosion testing at +0.2 V vs. SCE.
summary: This SEM image illustrates the subsurface of wrought Ti6Al4V after tribocorrosion testing at +0.2 V vs. SCE. Compared to the LPBF specimen, this wrought sample exhibits a higher density of visible cracks within the subsurface region, indicating a distinct difference in damage accumulation between the two processing methods.

caption: Mean SHAP value plot illustrating the relative importance of various input parameters in predicting beam shear capacity across all applied machine learning models.
summary: This SHAP mean value plot provides a global explanation of feature importance by quantifying how individual variables contribute to model predictions for beam shear capacity. By aggregating these contributions across the entire dataset, the visualization identifies the relative influence of each input parameter within the applied machine learning models.

caption: Potential energy diagram for CO2 activation on cubic MoC (grey) and Ni/MoC (green) surfaces, showing the transition from physisorbed to chemisorbed bent anionic CO2 states.
summary: This potential energy diagram illustrates CO2 activation mechanisms. On bare MoC, CO2 undergoes physisorption followed by chemisorption into a bent anionic configuration with a 0.36 eV barrier. Conversely, Ni/MoC facilitates a barrierless formation of the anionic CO2 species, demonstrating the enhanced catalytic activation capability of the Ni-decorated surface.

caption: Magnetic flux density (B) versus magnetic field strength (H) curve for 80% nickel permalloy, sourced from the COMSOL nonlinear magnetic material library.
summary: This plot displays the B-H hysteresis curve for 80% nickel permalloy, which is utilized as the magnetic material for the pin in the simulation. The data is derived from the COMSOL nonlinear magnetic material library, providing the necessary magnetic property inputs for accurate computational modeling of the permalloy component.

caption: Time-dependent specific mass gain measurements for the selected alloys during oxidation at 1000 °C.
summary: Oxidation behavior at 1000 °C shows that mass gain increases with temperature and adheres to a parabolic rate law. HESA-1 continues to exhibit the highest oxidation rates among the alloys tested, while HESA-3 and HESA-3A demonstrate significantly lower oxidation rates compared to HESA-1 and IN718 at this temperature.

caption: High-magnification SEM detail of region B, emphasizing the interface between the matrix and carbide phases where pore formation is evident.
summary: High-magnification SEM imaging of region B provides a closer look at the matrix-carbide interfaces within the compressed RHEA. While the carbide and matrix phases remain intact without cracking, this view clearly resolves the presence of pores at the interfaces, confirming the specific microstructural evolution occurring during 1200 °C compression.

caption: SHAP decision plot displaying the individual decision paths for predicted yield strength for a selected subset of 10 data points.
