caption: Dilatometry curve for a cooling rate of 140 °C/s, displaying the transformation behavior and critical temperature markers 1–6 derived from slope analysis.
summary: The dilatometry curve for a 140 °C/s cooling rate is shown here, featuring critical transformation temperatures 1–6. These points, determined by slope changes, reflect the phase transformation characteristics of the sample. This data contributes to the broader analysis of transformation temperatures across different cooling rates in the study.

caption: High-magnification STEM micrograph and corresponding SAED pattern showing coherent gamma prime and gamma double-prime precipitates within the FCC gamma matrix.
summary: This STEM micrograph, accompanied by a selected area electron diffraction pattern, reveals the strengthening precipitates within the FCC gamma matrix of Inconel 718. The image displays near-cuboidal coherent FCC precipitates and ellipsoidal tetragonal precipitates, providing insight into the fine-scale precipitation hardening mechanisms present in the alloy.

caption: Total density of states (DOS) calculated for pure Cu using an 8 × 8 × 8 k-point mesh, illustrating the electronic state profile near the Fermi level.
summary: The total density of states for pure copper is presented using an 8 × 8 × 8 k-point mesh. This visualization allows for the assessment of the DOS shape near the Fermi level, serving as an intermediate step in determining the mesh density required to achieve a flat, converged electronic profile.

caption: Solute B concentration evolution as a function of radiation dose in A-1%B solid-solution alloys, demonstrating the influence of sink plane separation distance (L3).
summary: This panel illustrates the concentration evolution of solute B in A-1%B solid-solution alloys under irradiation. The simulation results highlight how varying the sink plane separation distance (L3) impacts solute behavior. Increased recombination fractions are observed at larger separation distances of 128 and 256 compared to 64, indicating significant kinetic sensitivity.

caption: Nyquist plots of Fe2O3 and Ni-Bi/Fe2O3 photoanodes measured under darkness at 1.5 V vs. RHE, showing the charge transfer resistance.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) in Nyquist plots was obtained under darkness to explore the enhancing mechanism of the Ni-Bi film. The semidiameter of the semicircle indicates the residual double-layer charge transfer resistance, which decreased significantly for Fe2O3 upon Ni-Bi deposition, suggesting improved charge transfer across the electrode/electrolyte interface.

caption: FOB-1 geometry exhibiting approximately 20% hybridisation potential as determined through manual analysis of the structural configuration.
summary: FOB-1 geometry is presented to illustrate its hybridisation potential, which is calculated to be approximately 20%. This value is derived from a manual analysis of the obtained molecular geometries, providing a quantitative assessment of the structural hybridisation characteristics for this specific FOB configuration as part of the broader study.

caption: Time dependence of creep strain for SHNi and nSHNi alloys at 750 °C under an applied stress of 120 MPa.
summary: Creep strain evolution over time is plotted for SHNi and nSHNi alloys at 750 °C under 120 MPa stress. Results indicate that the SHNi alloy exhibits a notably longer creep lifetime compared to the nSHNi alloy, demonstrating superior creep resistance under these specific high-temperature and high-stress conditions.

caption: SEM micrograph of the DD10 microstructure along [001] at 800 °C, highlighting dislocation networks within the γ′ phase that contribute to high flow stress.
summary: This SEM image focuses on the dislocation networks formed within the γ′ phase at 800 °C. These structural features are identified as the intrinsic mechanism responsible for promoting creep resistance and maintaining high flow stress, confirming the critical role of γ′ precipitates in strengthening the alloy at elevated temperatures.

caption: Specific energy absorption (SEA) of SUS821L1 stainless steel plotted against strain, comparing quasi-static and dynamic tensile loading conditions across various temperatures.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific energy absorption (SEA) of SUS821L1 stainless steel as a function of strain. The data captures the material's mechanical response under both quasi-static and dynamic tensile loading conditions. By evaluating these metrics across different temperatures, the figure highlights how strain rates and thermal environments influence energy absorption performance.

caption: Load versus slip response at the loaded end for CFRP-to-steel joints utilizing a brittle adhesive, comparing results from the proposed FDM and FEM models.
summary: This plot illustrates the load-slip behavior at the loaded end for CFRP-to-steel joints with no debonding defects and mechanical anchorage. By employing a brittle adhesive, the graph compares the performance predictions derived from the proposed FDM against standard FEM results, highlighting the influence of mechanical anchorage on bond performance.

caption: Statistical distribution of thermal gradients (G) at different building heights, represented as box plots showing median, quartiles, and range.
summary: Box plots of the thermal gradient (G) demonstrate how this parameter changes with building height. The data indicates that G increases slightly as the build height increases, reflecting the evolving thermal conditions within the PBF-EB process and their subsequent impact on the solidification characteristics of the material.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the dark precipitate region c in panel (b), identifying the particle as a Cr-rich M7C3-type carbide with an orthorhombic structure.
summary: SAED analysis performed on the dark precipitate labeled as region c in panel (b) confirms its crystallographic identity. The diffraction pattern indicates that this particle is a Cr-rich M7C3-type carbide. The analysis further establishes that this specific carbide phase possesses an orthorhombic crystal structure within the 20 mA specimen matrix.

caption: Evolution of Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) plotted against the number of training epochs for neural network models utilizing either Mean Squared Error (MSE) or MAPE as the primary loss function.
summary: This plot illustrates the training efficiency and final accuracy of neural network models by comparing MAPE values across epochs. It highlights how the selection of the loss function, specifically MSE versus MAPE, significantly influences the convergence behavior and overall performance of the model during the training process.

caption: Manual annotation of nine major cell clusters identified within the primary PDAC lesion based on marker gene expression.
summary: Nine distinct cell clusters are displayed and manually annotated in this panel. These clusters were identified based on specific marker gene profiles, providing a detailed breakdown of the cellular composition within the primary PDAC lesion and serving as the foundation for identifying specific cancer stem cell populations.

caption: 2D KDE plots showing the evolution of stress versus incompatibility at maximum macroscopic load across cycles 1, 2, 5, 10, 100, and 1000.
summary: These plots track the stress-incompatibility correlation at maximum load over multiple cycles. The distribution widens significantly during the first few cycles and reaches a saturation point after cycle 5. The contours delineate the density distribution percentiles, highlighting the stabilization of the material's internal stress state as cyclic loading progresses.

caption: Average diffraction pattern captured within the transformation front region, less than 100 nm from the interface at 32°C, showing diffuse streaking characteristics.
summary: Representing the transformation front at 32°C, this diffraction pattern shows diffuse streaking within 100 nm of the interface. Consistent with other regions, the lack of interfacial localization suggests that the observed diffuse streaking originates from long-range effects like phonon softening or thermodynamic phase instability rather than static structural defects.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the shape memory effect (SME) mechanism alongside photographs of 4D printed PEEK-A10 samples undergoing shape transformation.
summary: This panel presents the SME mechanism through a schematic design involving an ACMO polymer network encapsulating PEEK powder. Accompanying photographs demonstrate the practical shape memory performance of 4D printed PEEK-A10 samples, illustrating the transition process enabled by the proposed material design strategy for shape-changing applications.

caption: Surface density of states for the bimetallic NiZn(110) surface, illustrating the electronic shift of the d-band centre relative to the Fermi level.
summary: This panel displays the surface density of states for the bimetallic NiZn(110) surface. The d-band centre, denoted by a continuous red line, shows a shift closer to the Fermi level, represented by a dashed black line, when compared to the respective monometallic Ni and Zn surface counterparts.

caption: S-N curve illustrating plain and fretting fatigue lives at room temperature plotted against maximum axial stress.
summary: This S-N curve displays the fatigue life results for plain and fretting conditions at room temperature as a function of maximum axial stress. Based on ten experimental tests, the data points align perfectly with the generated trend line, demonstrating a consistent relationship between stress levels and fatigue life.

caption: Calculated amount of terminal liquid phase present within the Fe-Cu-Ni ternary system composition space.
summary: The amount of terminal liquid in the Fe-Cu-Ni ternary system is mapped to provide insights into solidification behavior. This diagram serves as a basis for evaluating material properties, specifically contributing to the qualitative estimation of cracking susceptibility when combined with solidification temperature range data across the ternary composition field.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the three-electrode electrochemical testing configuration used for evaluating IN718 samples.
summary: This schematic illustrates the three-electrode electrochemical testing setup employed to analyze IN718 specimens. The samples, prepared from both cast and SLM materials, were cut into 1 cm x 1 cm x 0.2 cm dimensions and ground to a P1200 finish to ensure consistent surface conditions for the electrochemical measurements.

caption: Overview of the integrated optimization framework illustrating the sequential workflow.
summary: This flowchart outlines the comprehensive optimization framework, which integrates geometry generation via MATLAB, finite element analysis performed in Abaqus/Standard, and an iterative optimization process utilizing the CMA-ES algorithm. The diagram provides a clear visual representation of the computational steps required to execute the design optimization process effectively.

caption: Skewness (Ssk) distribution indicating surface topography characteristics before and after Hirtisation®.
summary: Skewness (Ssk) values shift from positive to negative after Hirtisation®, with medians decreasing from 0.33, 0.44, and –0.11 to –0.33, –0.71, and –0.38. This transition indicates a fundamental change in surface topography from peak-dominated to valley-dominated surfaces as a result of the Hirtisation® treatment applied to the struts.

caption: Experimental DIC strain field map of the GSLS sample, illustrating the strain distribution and fracture path.
summary: This DIC strain field map captures the experimental strain distribution of the GSLS sample. By comparing this data with the CPFEM-CDM simulation, the figure confirms the crack propagation and fracture path, validating the simulation's ability to model the mechanical behavior of the Gyroid lattice structure.

caption: Z-LD compressive deformation sequence, highlighting progressive cell deformation near the upper loading device.
summary: Z-LD loading results in a distinct deformation pattern characterized by the progressive collapse of foam cells in the immediate vicinity of the upper loading device. This localized structural response is highlighted by the yellow rectangle in the image, representing the foam's behavior during the 0% to 50% strain test.

caption: Three-dimensional CAD representation of the second auxetic unit cell design.
summary: This panel presents a three-dimensional CAD model of the second auxetic unit cell. As one of five distinct unit cells investigated, it adheres to the standardized global dimensions of 5 mm in length and height and 3 mm in width, ensuring consistency for comparative analysis and scale.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ti-Ni system, highlighting the equilibrium phases and the 600 °C process temperature with a red line.
summary: This Ti-Ni binary phase diagram, produced using the FactSage Education package, maps the equilibrium phases across different temperatures. A red line marks the 600 °C process temperature, where the system is characterized by the presence of several intermediate phases, contrasting with the phase stability observed in the Cr-Ni system.

caption: Solid-state 13C NMR spectra qualitatively confirming the crosslinking process within the continuous phase of the poly-Pickering-HIPE materials.
summary: Solid-state 13C NMR spectroscopy provides qualitative confirmation of the crosslinking process occurring in the continuous phase of the poly-Pickering-HIPE samples. This spectroscopic data aligns with the carbonyl stretching vibrations observed in the FTIR analysis, validating the successful formation of the crosslinked network structure in the PPH-0 and PPH-8 materials.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the distribution and utilization of labeled versus unlabeled data samples across various case studies.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a clear visualization of how labeled and unlabeled samples are allocated within the datasets compiled from the referenced case studies. It serves as a diagnostic tool to illustrate the acquisition and utilization patterns of the data, highlighting the balance between labeled and unlabeled information used in the analysis.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of alloy 5 in the as-quenched condition, displaying the martensitic block structure and the distribution of inter-granular retained austenite grains.
summary: The as-quenched microstructure of alloy 5 is represented by an inverse pole figure, showing the martensitic block morphology. Small grains of retained austenite are identified throughout the structure as white regions. The block size observed here contributes to the material's strength, which is estimated to be 20 MPa higher than alloy 6.

caption: NLP error evolution for the MBB beam with continuous fibers, including an inset focusing on the last 50 iterations.
summary: Evolution of the NLP error for an MBB beam reinforced with continuous fibers is depicted in this plot. The graph illustrates the iterative error reduction throughout the optimization process. An inset is provided to offer a magnified view of the final 50 iterations, allowing for a closer examination of the convergence behavior.

caption: Rietveld refinement of the in situ neutron powder diffraction pattern for alloy B (La1.9Mg1.1Ni9) at 1173 K, highlighting the phase constituents via Bragg peak markers.
summary: Rietveld refinement of the in situ neutron powder diffraction pattern for alloy B (La1.9Mg1.1Ni9) at 1173 K demonstrates excellent agreement between the experimental and calculated patterns. Vertical bars indicate the positions of Bragg peaks for the phase constituents, confirming the structural analysis of the alloy under high-temperature conditions.

caption: STEM micrograph of (Ni43Mn47Sn10)99.5Tb0.5 showing the coexistence of a matrix austenite phase and a distinct secondary phase.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of (Ni43Mn47Sn10)99.5Tb0.5, highlighting the presence of a matrix austenite phase alongside a secondary phase. The image provides a clear visualization of the phase distribution within the alloy, serving as a basis for further elemental analysis of the secondary phase features.

caption: Transition coefficients α' (red) and R' (grey) plotted as a function of nanoparticle size L, with black and red dots indicating simulation conditions corresponding to heterogeneous or homogeneous dislocation nucleation, respectively.
summary: This plot illustrates the size-dependent transition of dislocation nucleation mechanisms in nanoparticles. Homogeneous nucleation occurs in smaller particles (5-20 nm) where α' increases from 0.075 to 0.35, while larger particles exhibit heterogeneous nucleation. The results confirm a size-dependency model, with specific simulations performed for L = 20.0, 22.1, 26.5, and 35 nm.

caption: 3D surface topography of the Ni–Mo–W coating electrodeposited at a current density of 100 mA/cm2.
summary: The 3D surface topography of the Ni–Mo–W coating electrodeposited at the highest current density of 100 mA/cm2 is shown via AFM. This panel completes the series, illustrating the final surface state and morphological features achieved at this specific processing condition within the experimental set.

caption: Carbon uptake (wt. % binder) for 3D printed concrete samples at 7 days, illustrating the impact of CO2-steam integration and PEG-6000 dosage.
summary: Carbon uptake measurements reveal that the CTRL-NP sample exhibits poor thermodynamic stability of precipitated CaCO3. Accounting for moisture retention, the CO2 uptake for PEG-modified samples increased by 106% relative to the control, primarily driven by the formation of well-crystallized carbonate phases within the concrete matrix.

caption: APT reconstruction of the specimen aged for 0.6 h, illustrating a rapid increase in both the size and volume fraction of the gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime precipitates.
summary: After 0.6 hours of ageing, the APT reconstruction shows a significant evolution in the microstructure. The precipitate size and volume fraction increase rapidly compared to the 0.2-hour condition. Turquoise and brown iso-concentration surfaces continue to delineate the gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime phases, respectively, within the nickel-rich gamma-matrix.

caption: Radar chart displaying the stress at the reference point of load (RPL) for both CG and SG structural samples.
summary: Depicted in this radar chart is the stress at the reference point of load (RPL) for CG and SG samples. The results follow a trend similar to the energy absorption data, showing that CG structures generally outperform SG structures, although the variation in stress values is observed to be more gradual.

caption: Isothermal contraction strain measurements over time for Alloy B, demonstrating the kinetics of austenite formation at elevated temperatures.
summary: Isothermal experiments for Alloy B reveal austenite formation through measured contraction strains as a function of time. These contraction measurements, particularly at 450 and 500 °C, indicate significant austenite formation. By comparing these observed contraction strains with total transformation strain data, the extent of microstructural conversion into austenite can be accurately determined.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from region D, representing the NiAl3 phase.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern from region D provides crystallographic data for the NiAl3 phase identified in panel (c). This diffraction analysis confirms the phase identity and structural characteristics of the NiAl3 region, which is observed to contain stacking faults within the Ni/Ni2Al3 composite sheet.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the architecture of the digital shadow framework.
summary: This flowchart delineates the structural framework of the digital shadow, which integrates four primary entities: the User Entity (UE), the Core Entity (CE), the Data Collection Entity (DCE), and the Observable Manufacturing Elements (OME). The diagram maps the functional relationships and data flow between these components within the manufacturing system.

caption: Intense surface strain localization visible on the CHS-H-8.0-45 tension member at the fracture stage.
summary: Intense surface strain localization is visible on the CHS-H-8.0-45 tension member at the fracture stage. This panel captures the localized deformation behavior of the specimen, showing how strain accumulates in a specific zone during the failure process, which is characteristic of the highly localized strain mode observed in this study.

caption: Neutron diffractograms illustrating the structural evolution of the material during deformation at 77 K.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns reveal the structural evolution of the material during deformation at 77 K. The formation of an HCP (10.1) peak hump is observed, which is attributed to the activation of a martensitic transformation mechanism during the deformation process, as evidenced by the diffraction data.

caption: Anchored sample failure mode comparison between laboratory CT scan and numerical simulation.
summary: Anchored sample failure modes are illustrated here, contrasting laboratory CT scan observations with numerical simulation results. This comparison demonstrates how the anchoring mechanism influences the fracture behavior of the material, confirming the accuracy of the simulation in predicting the failure characteristics observed during the experimental laboratory testing process.

caption: Arrhenius-type relationship between the natural logarithm of the strain for 50% recrystallization (ε 0.5) and the inverse of the absolute temperature (1/RT).
summary: This Arrhenius plot depicts the temperature dependence of the strain required for 50% dynamic recrystallization. By plotting ln ε 0.5 against 1/RT, the activation energy for the recrystallization process is determined, demonstrating how thermal energy facilitates the structural evolution of the material during high-temperature deformation.

caption: Dual spot optical configuration demonstrating the split beam intensity profile captured by the beam profiler.
summary: This panel presents the dual spot optical configuration, where the beam is split into two distinct intensity maxima. Captured via the SP928 camera and LBS300 attenuator, this visualization confirms the successful implementation of the dual-beam setup, providing a clear spatial representation of the intensity distribution for further experimental analysis.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for ferromagnetic ordering under trilinear coupling QTri, showing the half-metallic gap and QAFEA mode percentage for a specific tuning condition.
summary: Panel b presents the partial density of states for the ferromagnetic system under trilinear coupling. It provides quantitative data on the half-metallic gap of the down-spin channel and the corresponding QAFEA mode percentage. This visualization demonstrates the sensitivity of the electronic structure to specific tuning parameters within the ferromagnetic ordering.

caption: t-SNE dimension reduction visualization of the testing set embeddings generated by the auto-encoder model.
summary: This panel displays the testing set embeddings produced by an auto-encoder model using the t-SNE dimensionality reduction technique. The visualization serves as a baseline for comparing the feature representation capabilities of the auto-encoder against the Deep SVDD model, illustrating the initial distribution of data points in the reduced feature space.

caption: Final viscous parameters of the Burgers model for porous lignin, showing the distribution of data points across different indentation depths and their corresponding averages.
summary: Representing the final set of viscous parameters for the Burgers model, this plot correlates material properties with porosity in hot-pressed lignin. The inclusion of both specific indentation depth data and averaged red points allows for a comprehensive evaluation of the viscous mechanical response across the tested porous samples.

caption: HSC image of the melt pool at dLBID = 3.0 mm, P = 1300 W, and v = 10 mm/s without powder stream (ρA = 0).
summary: Representing the third row of the 3.0 mm LBID series, this micrograph shows the melt pool without powder. The consistent shape observed here and in panels a and b indicates that the melt pool morphology is stable for this specific LBID diameter under the tested laser parameters.

caption: Point cloud visualization of part #2 at a distinct key moment of the printing process, corresponding to specific indicator values.
summary: This point cloud captures the state of part #2 at a critical moment during the printing process. The visualization is linked to the indicator plots in panel d, allowing for the correlation of specific geometric features or printing impacts with the quantitative data measured throughout the production of the layers.

caption: Dilatometric radial and axial shrinkage curves of a chemically debinded sample processed in an argon atmosphere, featuring an inset plot of the calculated volumetric shrinkage.
summary: Dilatometric analysis of the chemically debinded sample shows radial and axial shrinkage curves during heating in argon. Densification initiates at approximately 1000 °C, with similar shrinkage behavior observed in both directions, despite minor deviations at high temperatures. The inset provides the calculated volumetric shrinkage for the 1-hour debinded specimen.

caption: Crystallographic unit cell representations of the γ-Ni matrix, γ′-Ni3Al, and γ′′-Ni3Nb phases.
summary: This panel displays the fundamental crystallographic unit cells for the γ-Ni matrix, γ′-Ni3Al, and γ′′-Ni3Nb phases. These structures serve as the basis for understanding the phase constituents in nickel-based superalloys, providing a clear visualization of the atomic arrangements characteristic of these specific strengthening phases within the alloy system.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of Cu-Ni 90/10 alloy in 1 mol/dm3 HCl solution containing 1.0 g/L 2BPB inhibitor.
summary: The cyclic voltammogram for the Cu-Ni 90/10 alloy in a 1 mol/dm3 HCl solution with 1.0 g/L 2BPB is presented. This panel completes the series of electrochemical tests, showing the alloy's response to the highest concentration of 2BPB inhibitor tested at 25 °C.

caption: Immunohistochemical staining of IL-1β inflammatory marker expression at the implantation site after 7 days.
summary: IL-1β staining was conducted to further evaluate the inflammatory response at the site of the nerve conduit implantation. The results demonstrated no significant differences in signal intensity among the different conduit groups and the control, confirming that the inflammatory response was consistent across all tested experimental conditions.

caption: Refined scatter plot displaying only the samples within the optimal domain, with color-coding representing the model's prediction uncertainty to highlight regions of high epistemic variance.
summary: Focusing on the optimal domain, this plot filters the generated samples to isolate high-performance candidates. By color-coding these points based on prediction uncertainty, the visualization effectively identifies regions where the model lacks confidence, demonstrating the significant uncertainty inherent in the generative process within this specific design space.

caption: Comparison of elongation versus ultimate tensile strength (UTS) for CSAM Cu-N2 against various reported copper samples fabricated via alternative manufacturing methods.
summary: This plot compares the elongation and ultimate tensile strength of the CSAM Cu-N2 sample against diverse copper processing techniques, including helium-deposited CSAM, as-sprayed, annealed, SMAT, ECAP, electroplating, L-DED, SLM, and SEBM. The CSAM Cu-N2 sample demonstrates a well-optimized synergy of strength and ductility compared to these previously reported manufacturing methods.

caption: Load-displacement curve measured during nanoindentation of the Ni3Si2 intermetallic phase.
summary: This load-displacement curve characterizes the mechanical response of the Ni3Si2 intermetallic phase during nanoindentation. These tests were conducted to verify the strengthening mechanism of the joints by the introduction of a Mo-Ni skeleton, providing insight into the deformation behavior of this specific phase.

caption: Interdendritic regions above the interlayer boundaries containing strings of Nb-rich phases in the API heat-treated IN718 sample.
summary: This panel displays the microstructure of the IN718 sample, specifically focusing on the interdendritic regions found above the interlayer boundaries. Strings of Nb-rich phases are clearly visible in these areas, indicating that the heat treatment parameters were insufficient to fully dissolve these precipitates throughout the entire material volume.

caption: EPMA line scan illustrating elemental distribution within the cellular region of sample B-1 fabricated at 220 W, 750 mm s-1, and 95 μm.
summary: Elemental distributions within the cellular regions of sample B-1 are examined via EPMA line scans. The data reveals pronounced carbon enrichment in the interdendritic regions, alongside peak-like fluctuations of niobium, titanium, and tantalum, confirming that these elements segregate significantly during the solidification process under the specified laser processing conditions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the melt pool boundary region, characterizing the phases present at the MPBs of the Al-2.5Fe-2Cr-0.5Si alloy.
summary: This SAED pattern characterizes the crystalline phases located at the melt pool boundaries of the PBF-LB-manufactured Al-2.5Fe-2Cr-0.5Si alloy. The diffraction analysis supports the identification of local granular phases, such as Al11Cr2, which form at the boundaries during the solidification process of the alloy.

caption: WDS elemental mapping of Fe distribution in sample 0–3 at 5,000x magnification, arranged by vertical height from the substrate.
summary: This WDS map illustrates the Fe distribution within sample 0–3 at 5,000x magnification, organized by vertical distance from the substrate. The results demonstrate a clear trend in Fe concentration from the CI–Cu interface to the center of the third layer, consistent with findings from SEM–EDS and EBSD analyses.

caption: Optical dilatometry shrinkage curves of pristine glass particles plotted against temperature, illustrating the densification behavior used to define the sintering cycle.
summary: Optical dilatometry analysis of pristine glass particles reveals the shrinkage behavior across varying temperatures. The data shows an initial shrinkage event between 450 and 500 °C, associated with the glass transition temperature, and reaches maximum shrinkage near 900 °C, providing the necessary basis for determining the optimal sintering cycle for the material.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for Ti-6Al-4V alloy samples fabricated by CMT-arc and GMA-arc methods, tested in both vertical (z) and horizontal (x) orientations.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the tensile properties of Ti-6Al-4V alloy samples fabricated via CMT-arc and GMA-arc techniques. The data compares performance across vertical and horizontal orientations, highlighting the mechanical response of the alloy. These results characterize the tensile behavior and structural integrity of the components produced by both methods.

caption: Three-dimensional surface plot representing composition-dependent interdiffusivities of fcc Cu–Mn–Ni alloys at 1273 K, where symbols denote experimental data from the Matano-Kirkaldy method and surfaces represent calculated mobilities.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the composition-dependent interdiffusivities for fcc Cu–Mn–Ni alloys at 1273 K. Experimental data points obtained via the Matano-Kirkaldy method are compared against calculated surfaces derived from assessed mobilities. The visualization provides a comprehensive view of the diffusivity matrix behavior across the alloy composition space at this temperature.

caption: Schematic representation of the three-dimensional coordinate system established to model the complex motion and dynamics of the slipper component.
summary: This schematic illustrates the coordinate system framework developed to analyze the slipper's motion. By establishing three distinct coordinate systems, the model provides a structured mathematical approach to capture the complex dynamics of the slipper, enabling a precise description of its movement and orientation within the mechanical system under investigation.

caption: Load-displacement response for a specific lattice configuration subjected to impact energies ranging from 15 J to 90 J.
summary: This panel displays the load-displacement behavior of a selected lattice configuration under varying impact energies between 15 J and 90 J. These curves provide a structured basis for evaluating the mechanical response and energy absorption characteristics of the specimen during high-velocity impact testing.

caption: Capillary wave formation and subsequent droplet detachment observed in a low-surface-tension liquid containing 0.3% SDS at a film thickness ratio of h/hc = 1.5.
summary: This panel displays the dynamic behavior of a low-surface-tension liquid (0.3% SDS) under ultrasonic excitation at 48 kHz and 5 W power. The visualization captures the specific capillary wave patterns and droplet detachment process occurring at a normalized film thickness of 1.5, characterized by a Weber number of 0.19.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern corresponding to the BF-TEM image of the W-Ti-Cr-V alloy.
summary: This selected area diffraction pattern is associated with the bright-field TEM image of the arc-melted W-Ti-Cr-V alloy. It provides crystallographic information at the nanoscale, supporting the structural characterization of the equiaxed grains observed in the corresponding TEM micrograph.

caption: Nusselt number contours at the impingement target surface for varying pedestal height ratios, with fixed jet Reynolds number and spacing parameters.
summary: Nusselt number contours illustrate the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer at the impingement target surface. Reducing the wall spacing increases the maximum Nusselt number at the jet stagnation point and expands the area of elevated heat transfer, demonstrating improved cooling performance for narrower geometric configurations.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy micrograph of the Y2O3 powder.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy is utilized here to characterize the Y2O3 powder. This imaging technique highlights the atomic-scale structural features and density variations within the powder particles, providing essential information regarding the morphology and composition of the Y2O3 starting material used in the study.

caption: High-resolution Cr 2p XPS spectrum of the passive film on Alloy 625+, indicating the presence of chromium oxides.
summary: Chromium 2p XPS data for the Alloy 625+ passive film is presented in this panel. Based on the binding energy positions and peak shapes, the spectrum confirms the presence of chromium oxides, which are essential components of the protective passive film formed on the alloy surface in air.

caption: Validation plot demonstrating the predictive accuracy of the model for the Case 4 numerical specimen.
summary: The final panel presents the validation results for the Case 4 numerical specimen. By comparing the modified predictive model outputs with the numerical data, this plot completes the set of four specimens evaluated in the study, confirming the model's consistency and reliability in predicting material behavior.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for binary Mn-Al alloys featuring varying Mn excesses from 0% to 100%.
summary: This panel displays magnetic hysteresis loops for binary Mn-Al alloys with Mn excess ranging from 0% to 100%. The sample with 100% Mn excess exhibits the highest magnetization. Further increases in Mn content were not pursued because the ferromagnetic τ-MnAl phase is stable only within a narrow compositional window.

caption: Combined EDS surface sweep map representing the overall elemental composition of the powder.
summary: Combined EDS surface sweep map representing the overall elemental composition of the powder. This surface sweep provides a holistic view of the elemental distribution across the selected regions, complementing the individual elemental maps to confirm the successful and uniform mixing of the TC4 and Zr powder constituents.

caption: Comparison of the Modular Transfer Function (MTF) and captured images across transmitted and reflected optical paths to validate system performance.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis of the Modular Transfer Function and resulting images obtained through both transmitted and reflected optical paths. These metrics serve to validate the performance of the infinity-corrected system, ensuring that the optical design effectively maintains image fidelity and resolution across different operational modes.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of nanoNi (i) and nanoNi-Pop (ii) electrodes in 1.0 M KOH, displaying multiple cathodic peaks associated with the coexistence of beta-NiOOH and gamma-NiOOH.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry of nanoNi and nanoNi-Pop in 1.0 M KOH solution reveals the electrochemical behavior of the activated electrodes. The presence of multiple cathodic peaks in the voltammograms indicates that both beta-NiOOH and gamma-NiOOH phases coexist within the oxyhydroxide layers formed on the surfaces of the nanoNi and nanoNi-Pop samples.

caption: Spectral profiles of absorbance, transmittance, and reflectance for CoZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles, recorded from 350 nm to 1150 nm at room temperature.
summary: CoZnFe2O4 quaternary alloy nanoparticles exhibit distinct optical characteristics as shown by their absorbance, transmittance, and reflectance spectra. These measurements were performed at ambient temperature using UV-vis spectroscopy over the 350–1150 nm wavelength range, illustrating the material's optical response and performance within this specific electromagnetic spectrum.

caption: Parity plot comparing model-predicted dot diameters against measured equivalent diameters for lab-grade paper substrates.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the model's predictive accuracy when applied to lab paper samples. The results indicate that the model effectively predicts trends for liquids characterized by medium to high surface tension, specifically including TLC, TL3, and TL4, confirming the model's reliability across these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) plot for Al, Ni, and Cu atoms, derived from DFT simulations of the Al7Cu4Ni structure.
summary: This PDOS plot illustrates the electronic structure of Al, Ni, and Cu atoms within the Al7Cu4Ni precipitate. Derived from DFT simulations, these data provide a detailed view of the partial density of states, which helps characterize the electronic properties and bonding behavior of the precipitate in the Al-Cu-Ni alloy.

caption: Stokes parameters S0, S1, S2, and S3 plotted as a function of gray levels for the LCoS-SLM, showing typical deviations of 0.0267, 0.0385, 0.0872, and 0.0970 respectively.
summary: Stokes parameters for the LCoS-SLM are presented, illustrating how the state of polarization of light varies across different gray levels. The data indicates that these parameters deviate from the expected zero value, with specific typical deviations calculated for each Stokes component, confirming the expected polarization behavior of the device.

caption: Experimental compression deformation snapshot of the D1.9 structure at 1.5 mm displacement.
summary: Experimental compression of the D1.9 bioinspired sandwich structure at 1.5 mm displacement shows the deformation mode. The structural design, featuring inner tubes and joint ribs, promotes a more uniform stress distribution during the compression process, which is consistent with the findings from the finite element analysis results.

caption: Loss curve for the DDA unsupervised domain adaptation method.
summary: DDA displays a loss curve where the loss value decreases slowly over time. This gradual reduction successfully delays the onset of overfitting, as evidenced by the accuracy curves which maintain stability and do not exhibit a clear declining trend until reaching the 80th epoch of the training process.

caption: Energy absorption at 50% strain for X-LD metallic foam plotted against test temperature.
summary: Energy absorption at 50% strain follows a trend similar to the strength properties, characterized by a substantial 90% decrease as the test temperature increases. This reduction in energy absorption capacity mirrors the degradation observed in the material's stress-bearing properties under elevated thermal conditions.

caption: Calculated δ-to-γ phase transformation behavior for EQ2.30 at 190 W, comparing the transformation kinetics at specific locations P1, P2, and P3.
summary: This panel presents the calculated δ-to-γ phase transformation kinetics for the EQ2.30 alloy processed at 190 W. By comparing the transformation behavior at three distinct locations (P1, P2, and P3), the simulation highlights how varying thermal histories across the heat-affected zone influence the resulting microstructural evolution.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the Ti–Nb–Cr–V–Ni alloy, illustrating the grain orientation distribution with an average grain size of 3.66 μm.
summary: This EBSD-based IPF map visualizes the grain orientation and microstructure of the Ti–Nb–Cr–V–Ni alloy. The analysis indicates that the material is composed of BCC A2, BCC B2, and Ti2Ni phases, with a measured average grain size of 3.66 μm across the deposited structure.

caption: Resistivity values obtained from room temperature Hall effect measurements plotted against the thickness of the graded layer for all investigated contact structures.
summary: Resistivity characteristics of the studied contact structures are presented in this panel. By plotting resistivity against the graded layer thickness, the figure illustrates how the electrical resistance of the material system evolves with structural changes, based on room temperature Hall effect data collected for all experimental configurations.

caption: Macrostructural photographs and microscopic surface morphology of Al2O3 samples before and after PDA coating, showing a distinct color shift from white to yellowish-brown.
summary: Macrostructural photographs and microscopic surface morphology of Al2O3 samples before and after PDA coating are presented. The successful coating process is visually confirmed by a distinct color change of the Al2O3 structure from white to yellowish-brown, indicating effective surface modification through the polydopamine-enabled interface engineering approach.

caption: Comparison between experimental XRD-measured residual stress and the reconstructed stress profile in the x-direction.
summary: This plot compares measured residual stress values in the x-direction against the reconstructed profile, incorporating XRD measurement error bars. The reconstruction shows a normalized root mean squared error of 27.7% relative to the experimental data, demonstrating the algorithm's capability to approximate the initial stress states within the IN718 sample.

caption: Relationships between 1000α-T and n-T for PAAM IN718 alloy, showing the temperature dependence of the stress multiplier α and the stress exponent n.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent evolution of the stress multiplier α and the stress exponent n. The relationship between α and temperature is defined by the linear equation α(T) = 8.49 × 10⁻⁷T + 0.42. These parameters are critical for constructing the Arrhenius constitutive equation, with an average n value of 0.0408.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental maps of PLA/HA 20 samples, displaying calcium in red and phosphorus in yellow to confirm the presence of HA particles.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental maps of PLA/HA 20 samples display calcium in red and phosphorus in yellow to confirm the presence of HA particles. These maps demonstrate that the HA particles remain present in the composite material both pre- and post-printing, validating the stability of the composite composition.

caption: Tan δ curves for VeroWhite and FLX9895-DM polymers, showing distinct peaks used to identify their respective glass transition temperatures.
summary: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis tests performed in temperature ramp mode reveal the glass transition temperatures for VeroWhite and FLX9895-DM. These temperatures are determined by identifying the peak values of the Tan δ curves. As VeroWhite approaches this transition temperature at 50 °C, the material exhibits a change in its mechanical failure behavior.

caption: Temperature distribution snapshot at t = 190 ms for a 4 nm/ms scan speed, featuring an inset time-temperature plot for points P, Q, and R, showing a peak temperature of 1900 K at 885 nm from the edge.
summary: At 190 ms, the simulation shows the temperature distribution averaging out to 1900 K beneath the laser source, which has traveled 885 nm. The inset time-temperature plot for points P, Q, and R indicates a total cooling duration of approximately 350 ms to reach ambient temperature post-laser treatment.

caption: Terahertz imaging of the sample upper surface showing spatial distribution of THz signal intensity.
summary: This panel presents a terahertz image of the sample's upper surface. The visualization captures the spatial distribution of THz signal intensity, providing a non-destructive view of the surface characteristics. This imaging technique is essential for analyzing the upper surface morphology and potential defects in the material under investigation.

caption: Detailed investigation of the pitting region for LPBF 316L stainless steel, visualized across XOY, XOZ, and YOZ orthogonal planes.
summary: The pitting region of LPBF 316L stainless steel is analyzed through a 3D investigation. By examining the morphology of pits across the XOY, XOZ, and YOZ planes, this visualization provides a comprehensive view of the localized corrosion damage sustained by the LPBF-processed material during electrochemical testing.

caption: Quantitative elemental composition analysis of six specific points within the BCC/B2 region shown in panel (a1).
summary: Quantitative analysis of six points within the BCC/B2 region reveals a dual-phase structure with markedly different elemental distributions. The Fe and Cr enriched phase contains approximately 53–57 at% Fe and 32–33 at% Cr, while the Al and Ni enriched phase contains approximately 25–30 at% Al and 49–52 at% Ni.

caption: SHAP dependence plot demonstrating the effect of the number of layers on residual stress predictions along the scan direction σx.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the effect of the number of layers on residual stress predictions along the scan direction σx. Each dot represents a single prediction, with the x-axis showing the feature value and the y-axis representing the SHAP value in MPa, colored by the strongest interacting feature.

caption: Cycle stability performance of the alloy electrodes, highlighting the improved capacity retention over repeated charge-discharge cycles following the addition of palladium.
summary: This panel presents the cycle stability of the alloys, which is a crucial aspect of battery performance. A significant enhancement in cycle performance is observed upon the addition of palladium to the alloys, confirming that Pd substitution effectively improves the long-term stability and capacity retention of the electrode materials during cycling.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern of the α-Ti region, characterized by a dominant grain oriented near the [ 1–21 ] α-Ti zone axis.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of AlInN/GaN superlattices with an AlInN fraction of 0.845 grown on a bulk GaN substrate, displaying atomic steps with variable widths.
summary: This AFM image shows AlInN/GaN superlattices with an AlInN fraction of 0.845 grown on a bulk GaN substrate. caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of E. coli and MRSA stained to distinguish between dead (red) and surviving (green) bacteria, confirming the bactericidal efficacy of PPG against both strains.
summary: Fluorescence staining images provide a visual assessment of bacterial survival following PPG treatment. By differentiating between live and dead cells using specific fluorescent markers, the panel confirms that PPG exerts a clear bactericidal effect on both E. coli and MRSA populations.

caption: Hardness versus maximum indentation force for 200 indents on Co-Ni 50/50 alloy, with solid lines representing the maximum hardness of the phase.
summary: This plot maps the hardness against maximum indentation force for 200 indents on the Co-Ni 50/50 alloy. Solid lines denote the maximum hardness of the phase. The data illustrates the mechanical response of the alloy, providing insight into how the composition influences hardness across varying indentation forces.

caption: Radar plot benchmarking the overall performance of the AMed PZT-NC film against other flexible piezoelectric materials.
summary: A radar plot is utilized to benchmark the comprehensive performance of the AMed PZT-NC film against various other flexible piezoelectric materials. This visualization allows for a multi-dimensional comparison, highlighting the superior characteristics of the PZT-NC film in the context of existing flexible piezoelectric technology.

caption: Time-temperature transformation profile for the H13 specimen processed with 20 mA thermal compensation, where the substrate temperature is held at approximately 650 °C with a gradual cooling rate.
summary: At a 20 mA thermal compensation setting, the H13 specimen maintains a substrate temperature of approximately 650 °C throughout the deposition process. This profile demonstrates a less steep temperature decline compared to the 0 mA condition, significantly altering the thermal history and influencing the diffusion-controlled phase transformations during cooling.

caption: Cyclic polarization curves for two Ni-base superalloys in 1 M NaCl solution, recorded at a scan rate of 0.167 mV s−1, illustrating transpassive breakdown at potentials exceeding 0.75 V.
summary: Cyclic polarization curves for two Ni-base superalloys in 1 M NaCl solution, recorded at a scan rate of 0.167 mV s−1, illustrate transpassive breakdown at potentials exceeding 0.75 V. caption: Rietveld refinement of the X-ray diffraction pattern for the annealed La0.75Mg0.25Ni3.05Co0.2Al0.05Mo0.2 alloy, illustrating the fit between experimental data and the calculated structural model.
summary: This figure presents the Rietveld refinement of the XRD pattern for the annealed La0.75Mg0.25Ni3.05Co0.2Al0.05Mo0.2 alloy. The refinement process demonstrates the structural analysis of the material, where the addition of Mo is observed to shift diffraction peaks toward lower angles, indicating a corresponding increase in the lattice parameters of the alloy.

caption: Stress-strain response of samples E and G, illustrating how increased T values significantly improve peak load and plastic ductility.
summary: Stress-strain curves for samples E and G show that a larger T parameter significantly enhances both the peak load and plastic ductility. The observed strain differences between stages confirm that T plays a vital role in the mechanical efficiency and energy absorption capabilities of the samples under compressive loading.

caption: Particle size distribution for SS 316 L feedstock powder, displaying both size-frequency distribution and cumulative sum curves.
summary: This panel illustrates the particle size distribution for SS 316 L feedstock powder. It presents both the size-frequency distribution and the cumulative sum, providing essential data to characterize the powder feedstock. These measurements are critical for determining the factors that control powder flow and powder feed rate during DED processes.

caption: Arithmetical mean height (Sa) comparison across contour themes, where both CL+TH and CL themes demonstrate statistically significant differences relative to contour-first themes.
summary: Arithmetical mean height (Sa) values are evaluated for different contour themes. The CL+TH theme shows a statistically significant difference compared to contour-first themes. Additionally, the CL theme exhibits a statistically significant difference in mean value compared to the contour-first themes, confirming higher roughness for contour-last themes.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of the 3D-printed Navy Blue filter, showing a transmission peak near 450 nm and a distinct dip at approximately 625 nm.
summary: The Navy Blue 3D-printed filter displays a characteristic optical transmission profile. Analysis of the spectrum reveals a transmission peak located near 450 nm, while a significant transmission dip occurs at approximately 625 nm, illustrating the specific filtering properties of this alcohol-based ink formulation within the visible light range.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength data distribution visualized through a violin plot.
summary: Ultimate tensile strength data distribution is visualized through a violin plot. By displaying the spread, central tendency, and outliers, this plot allows for a clear assessment of the ultimate tensile strength performance across all tested samples, highlighting the variability and statistical characteristics of this mechanical property in the study.

caption: Scheil solidification curve for Grade 91 steel, illustrating the evolution of phase fractions during cooling.
summary: The Scheil approach demonstrates that rapid solidification begins with primary delta-ferrite. As the solid fraction reaches approximately 90%, gamma-austenite forms. The solidification process concludes with negligible eutectic constituents, specifically delta-ferrite, gamma-austenite, and Nb(C,N), present within the interdendritic regions of the microstructure.

caption: Capacitance response of 10 wt% YP50F flow electrodes plotted against frequency at the conclusion of testing.
summary: The capacitance of 10 wt% YP50F flow electrodes is shown as a function of frequency following FCDI experimental validation. Consistent with the general behavior of these flow electrodes, the material shows no capacitance at high frequencies, with notable differences in performance observed in the low-frequency regime below 10 mHz.

caption: Experimental setup featuring the 3D printer utilized for the additive manufacturing of ceramic pastes.
summary: This panel displays the 3D printer equipment used for the experimental fabrication process. The setup serves as the primary hardware for conducting the printing tests described in the study, providing the necessary platform for evaluating different paste formulations and their respective printing performance during the additive manufacturing of BaTiO3 materials.

caption: Statistical distribution of small punch creep test (SPCT) results for Inconel 718 alloy at 650 °C, illustrating variations in displacement and creep life.
summary: This statistical analysis presents the small punch creep test results for Inconel 718 alloy at 650 °C. The histogram highlights the distribution of key performance metrics, specifically focusing on displacement and creep life, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's mechanical behavior under these specific high-temperature testing conditions.

caption: Detailed current-voltage characteristics for a thin wall structure deposited at a wire feed rate of 6 m/min, complementing panel (b).
summary: Presented is the detailed current-voltage behavior for a thin wall structure deposited at 6 m/min. The data supports the general observation that this wire feed rate produces a relatively higher peak current and a lower peak duration, characterizing the electrical dynamics of the deposition process.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for 316L powder, indicating D10, D50, and D90 values of 17.6 μm, 31.7 μm, and 54.7 μm, respectively.
summary: The particle size distribution of the 316L powder is presented as a histogram, quantifying the dimensional characteristics of the material. Key statistical metrics derived from the distribution include a D10 of 17.6 μm, a D50 of 31.7 μm, and a D90 of 54.7 μm, defining the overall size range of the powder.

caption: Statistical comparison of pitch and via positional error metrics across seven nominally identical interposer samples.
summary: This plot provides a comparative statistical analysis of pitch and via positional error for seven nominally identical interposers. By aggregating data from multiple samples, the figure demonstrates the consistency and reliability of the fabrication process, allowing for an assessment of the variability in via placement across the produced interposer set.

caption: Specific capacitance values for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors with 5 OTU layers, calculated from galvanostatic charge-discharge data across different liquid electrolytes.
summary: Specific capacitance values for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors with 5 OTU layers are calculated from galvanostatic charge-discharge data to assess performance in various liquid electrolytes. This analysis quantifies the impact of electrolyte selection on the specific capacitance, providing a clear metric for optimizing the energy storage capabilities of the micro-supercapacitor.

caption: Electronic dispersion relations for model 1 with relaxed atomic positions, shown in a narrow energy window around the Fermi level after the inclusion of spin–orbit coupling, demonstrating band splitting.
summary: This panel presents the electronic dispersion relations for model 1 after incorporating spin–orbit coupling. The resulting band splitting, caused by the lack of inversion symmetry in the system, is clearly visible near the Fermi level, highlighting the significant impact of SOC on the electronic structure of the material.

caption: Normalized Ni K-edge Refle-XAFS spectrum at 8331.5 eV, showing characteristic peaks associated with Ni-based surface species.
summary: The normalized Ni K-edge Refle-XAFS spectrum, measured at 8331.5 eV, serves as a reference for identifying surface species. Spectral features, such as the peak at 8353 eV, provide insights into the oxidation states of nickel. Variations in white line intensity at 8346 eV indicate the growth of NiO/Ni(OH)2 on the sample surface.

caption: Average nanoindentation hardness depth profiles for Alloy 625 across three irradiation conditions.
summary: This panel displays the average nanoindentation hardness depth profiles for Alloy 625. Using the Oliver and Pharr method, the hardness values are calculated from load versus displacement data. The profiles illustrate the mechanical response of the alloy under three distinct irradiation conditions, providing a quantitative assessment of hardness variations with depth.

caption: Concentration profile of diffusion couple A1 annealed at 1173 K for 72 h, showing model-predicted values using current atomic mobility parameters (solid line) and ref. [20] parameters (dash-dot line) compared against experimental literature data.
summary: This plot displays the concentration profile for diffusion couple A1 after 72 hours of annealing at 1173 K. It compares model-predicted profiles derived from current atomic mobility parameters and those from ref. [20] against experimental literature data, illustrating the accuracy of the mobility parameters in predicting diffusion behavior.

caption: Voltage-current (V–I) and power density-current (Pd–I) characteristic curves for bulk radial thermoelectric generators.
summary: This panel presents the V–I and Pd–I characteristic curves for bulk radial thermoelectric generators. These plots characterize the electrical output and power density performance of the bulk device configuration, allowing for a direct assessment of how the bulk material architecture influences the thermoelectric generator's voltage and power characteristics.

caption: Calculated stable phase diagram for the Cr-H2O-H2 system, identifying Cr2O3 as the stable corrosion product under specified environmental conditions.
summary: This Pourbaix diagram illustrates the thermodynamic stability of chromium species in a H2O-H2 environment. caption: Experimental partitioning coefficients for elements in the gamma prime phase calculated from atom probe tomography compositional data.
summary: Experimental partitioning coefficients for the gamma prime phase are presented, derived directly from atom probe tomography compositional measurements. caption: Feature visualization of the Tongji dataset using the supervised learning method.
summary: This panel displays the feature distribution for the Tongji dataset as processed by the supervised learning model. It serves as a baseline comparison to evaluate how effectively the supervised approach clusters data points compared to the proposed model, providing insight into the underlying feature extraction capabilities for battery user analysis.

caption: Comparison between an XCT cross-section taken 2 mm from the bottom surface of the polymer interposer and the corresponding slice file utilized during the additive manufacturing process.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis between an XCT cross-section of the polymer interposer, captured 2 mm from the bottom surface, and the original slice file used for printing. This comparison allows for the evaluation of the printed structure against the intended design specifications for the interposer geometry.

summary: This plot illustrates the influence of build orientation angle ϑ on the fatigue life of R90C90 specimens. summary: This confusion matrix displays the action recognition performance for the video dataset processed at 224x224 resolution. summary: The X-ray diffraction pattern of the 3D-HEA specimen is presented to characterize its crystalline structure. summary: STEM imaging of the AM state after creep exposure at 750 °C confirms the formation and distribution of spherical γ' precipitates within the γ matrix. summary: This panel depicts the digital watch powered by the micro-supercapacitor module at -20 °C. caption: Schematic representation of the shear strength test setup used to evaluate the mechanical integrity of the brazed joints.
summary: This schematic depicts the experimental setup for the shear strength test. caption: Imaginary part of the magnetic permeability for D30 high-entropy alloy toroidal samples at different annealing temperatures.

It serves as a diagnostic tool to visualize how specific processing parameters correlate with the prevalence of defects in as-fabricated thin-walled parts, facilitating the selection of parameters that minimize defect formation.

caption: Statistical distribution of the Schmidt Factor (SF) for the RS region.
summary: This histogram provides the statistical distribution of the Schmidt Factor (SF) for the RS region. Analysis of the data reveals that more than 70% of the SF values are greater than 0.44, demonstrating that a significant majority of the grains in this region are oriented for easy slip.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the FeMn alloy displaying elongated Mn-rich regions.
summary: The 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction of the FeMn alloy illustrates the distribution of Mn solute atoms. These Mn-rich areas are interconnected, forming elongated structural regions throughout the specimen volume, which contrasts with the spherical morphology observed in the FeNi alloy system.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for 3D-IDCμE/PPy electrodes tested at 0.5 mA cm⁻², where PPy was electrodeposited at varying current densities for 10 minutes.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements for the 3D-IDCμE/PPy system reveal how the deposition current density affects energy storage. These curves provide the basis for calculating specific capacitance, showing that the performance is sensitive to the current density applied during the 10-minute PPy electrodeposition process, with optimal results observed at intermediate current densities.

caption: High-magnification inverse pole figure map of the region enclosed by the red rectangle, showing low-angle and medium-angle grain boundaries.
summary: Focusing on the region within the red rectangle, this inverse pole figure map identifies low-angle and medium-angle grain boundaries using yellow and white lines, respectively. A black arrow highlights a remaining fragment of the initially statically recrystallized grain, demonstrating the localized nature of the ongoing intragranular recrystallization process at high strain.

caption: Nano-hardness values for as-built and heat-treated specimens.
summary: This figure displays the nano-hardness values for various specimens subjected to different heat treatment conditions. The data provides a comparative overview of the mechanical properties of as-built samples versus those that have undergone specific thermal processing, illustrating the influence of heat treatment on the material's hardness characteristics.

caption: HAADF-STEM image focusing on dislocation interactions at the interface between the T phase and the alpha-Al matrix.
summary: Detailed HAADF-STEM imaging illustrates the interaction between dislocations and the dispersed T phase within the alloy. The observations demonstrate that the T phase exerts a strong blocking effect on dislocation movement, which is a critical mechanism for strengthening the laser cladding alloy under mechanical stress.

caption: Measured drift time spectrum of DT3 displaying signal intensity in nA versus drift time in ms, highlighting preRIP, RIP, five specific ketones, and identified dimers.
summary: This spectrum illustrates the DT3 measurement output, plotting detector current against drift time. Key features identified include the preRIP, RIP, and a series of five ketones (2-hexanone, 4-heptanone, 2-heptanone, 2-octanone, 2-nonanone). Additionally, dimers and overlapping dimers are clearly marked, with all dimer species highlighted by red circles.

caption: Workflow diagram illustrating the μ-CT characterisation process, starting from the acquisition of 2400 16-bit projection images through to the final reconstruction performed using VGstudio MAX 3 software.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic workflow for μ-CT characterisation. It details the transition from raw data acquisition, consisting of 2400 16-bit projection images, to the final volumetric reconstruction. The process utilizes VGstudio MAX 3 software to transform projection data into a comprehensive 3D representation of the material's internal structure.

caption: XPS survey spectra comparing the surface chemical compositions of the four distinct titanium scaffold groups.
summary: XPS survey spectra were utilized to verify the surface chemical compositions of the four titanium scaffold groups. This analysis provides a baseline for understanding the elemental makeup of the scaffold surfaces, confirming the successful preparation of the samples for subsequent comparative studies regarding their surface modifications and functionalization.

caption: Cu K-edge XANES spectra for CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC, illustrating the intrinsic valence state of copper.
summary: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) at the Cu K-edge is utilized to determine the intrinsic valence state of copper in both CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC samples. This spectroscopic data reveals the electronic configuration and oxidation state of the copper atoms within the synthesized catalyst frameworks.

caption: Plastic strain range of the mid-life hysteresis loop as a function of cycles to failure for Nimonic 901, demonstrating consistent trend lines across different test temperatures.
summary: Plastic strain range data for Nimonic 901 is plotted against cycles to failure, revealing that tests conducted at 450 °C and in air at 550 °C align on a similar trend line. This convergence suggests that a common failure mechanism governs the fatigue behavior of the alloy under these conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of Ti–45Al–2Mn–2Nb–1B alloy processed at 1200 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹.
summary: Captured at 1200 °C and a low strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹, this IPF map shows a microstructure consisting of nearly fully developed and uniformly distributed equiaxed grains. The reduction in strain rate facilitates the breakdown of elongated deformed grains, resulting in a more refined and homogeneous equiaxed grain structure.

caption: Surface topography of the as-prepared sample captured via laser confocal microscopy.
summary: This panel displays the surface topography of the as-prepared sample using laser confocal microscopy. The imaging technique allows for the assessment of surface roughness, providing a baseline measurement for the material before any mechanical treatment or thermal oxidation procedures are applied to the specimen surface.

caption: Fatigue performance of SLM Ti6Al4V HIP specimens, plotting maximum applied stress against cycles to failure for varying surface finishes.
summary: This fatigue curve for SLM Ti6Al4V HIP samples demonstrates that surface finish significantly impacts fatigue life. Machining improves fatigue strength from 325 MPa to 875 MPa, a 170% increase, while polishing achieves a fatigue strength of 800 MPa, representing a 150% increase compared to the baseline.

caption: Micro-CT reconstruction of G 0Al M paste showing the internal distribution of trapped air voids within the metakaolin-based matrix.
summary: Micro-CT reconstruction of G 0Al M paste reveals the internal distribution of trapped air voids within the metakaolin-based matrix. These phenomena are linked to stronger capillary forces that bring metakaolin particles closer together, resulting in higher viscosity and increased air entrapment within the paste structure as observed in the tomography.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the elastic modulus for printed specimens, comparing control mixes (M-P) against those modified with 2.5 wt% (M-2.5HM) and 5 wt% (M-5HM) encapsulated NaOH and nano clay over a 10 to 40-minute interval.
summary: This plot illustrates the elastic modulus development of printed specimens over time, specifically comparing control mixes with those containing 2.5 wt% and 5 wt% encapsulated NaOH and nano clay. Measurements taken between 10 and 40 minutes demonstrate how these additives influence the mechanical stiffness of the material following the heating and mixing process.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves for microsupercapacitors at a current density of 1.42 mA cm-2, comparing different ceria nanoparticle loadings.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves at a current density of 1.42 mA cm-2 reveal that electrodes with 3-5 wt% ceria exhibit longer charge/discharge cycles. This trend confirms superior capacitive behavior for these specific compositions compared to other loadings, demonstrating the influence of ceria content on the charge storage characteristics of the devices.

caption: Carbon elemental distribution map highlighting the presence of the fixative resin layer covering the alloy surface.
summary: The carbon elemental mapping specifically identifies the distribution of the fixative resin used during the cross-sectional preparation of the AA2060-T8 alloy. This map confirms the spatial extent of the mounting material relative to the biofilm and the alloy surface after 24 hours of immersion in the bacterial environment.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curves for defect detection in sample C, comparing ultrasonic testing (blue), eddy current testing (green), and fused data (pink) performance.
summary: This plot displays the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves for sample C, evaluating the effectiveness of defect detection methods. It compares the performance of ultrasonic testing (UT), eddy current testing (ECT), and a fused dataset. The results demonstrate the diagnostic capabilities of these individual and combined sensing modalities for material inspection.

caption: Sequence alignment of the loop region for KLac, TmLacS, and a designed TmLacS variant, with the protruding loop segment highlighted in yellow.
summary: Sequence alignment of the loop area for KLac, TmLacS, and a proposed TmLacS version containing a designed loop is presented. The segment highlighted in yellow indicates the protruding loop in KLac. This alignment supports the engineering of a loop insertion in TmLacS to mimic the catalytic-site behavior of KLac.

caption: Statistical strain profile derived from the GPA map, plotting strain magnitude as a function of distance relative to the yellow reference line.
summary: The statistical strain profile quantifies the strain distribution across the twin-matrix interface in the as-deposited alloy. By measuring strain as a function of distance from the reference line, this plot provides a clear numerical assessment of the lattice mismatch and deformation intensity localized at the twin boundary.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of a 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 composite electrode (256 μm thickness) tested at 0.1C within a 1.0–2.5 V voltage window.
summary: The 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 composite electrode exhibits an initial discharge capacity of 215.47 mAh g-1 when tested at 0.1C. These galvanostatic charge-discharge curves demonstrate the electrochemical performance of the thick 3D-printed architecture, which maintains high capacity and stable cycling behavior within the specified 1.0 to 2.5 V voltage range.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve showing the CNN model's classification performance regarding cracking defects.
summary: Displaying the ROC curve for cracking defects, this plot quantifies the CNN model's ability to correctly identify structural cracks. The curve reflects the model's classification robustness, providing a clear visual representation of the true positive rate versus the false positive rate achieved during the defect detection process.

caption: 3D optical profilometry image of the T6 heat-treated sample surface after 10 N loading.
summary: This 3D profilometry image details the worn surface topography of the T6 heat-treated sample. It clearly illustrates pronounced ploughing, edge plunging, and a distinct stick regime, confirming that heat-treated samples undergo more significant wear degradation than as-built samples under 10 N loading.

caption: Force-displacement curves for PLA and carbon fiber reinforced PLA (PLA-CF) filaments with a 1.75 mm diameter, demonstrating the ductile behavior induced by crazing in the reinforced material.
summary: Tensile testing of PLA and PLA-CF filaments reveals distinct mechanical responses. The force-displacement curves demonstrate that carbon fiber reinforcement significantly alters the material behavior. Specifically, the presence of crazing in the PLA-CF filament leads to a much more ductile response compared to the neat PLA filament under tensile loading.

caption: Absorption coefficients plotted against frequency for the graded, uniform, and linear-gradient TPMS structures defined in panel (b).
summary: Absorption coefficients are compared for three different porosity profiles to evaluate their broadband optimization effectiveness. The plot reveals how the graded porosity design influences the absorption characteristics of the TPMS structure, highlighting the performance advantages of the optimal solution over the uniform and linear-gradient configurations.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern for high and low carbon WC-FeNiCo alloys containing 6.5 wt% Cr addition.
summary: This XRD pattern illustrates the phase composition of WC-FeNiCo alloys modified with 6.5 wt% Cr. Consistent with the 5 wt% Cr sample, the diffraction data shows no evidence of Cr-rich carbides, confirming that such phases, if present, exist at concentrations below the 1 vol% detection threshold of the XRD measurement.

caption: Load-displacement curves for Ti41Zr41Ni18 coatings at a 1 mN limit load, comparing the as-deposited state (0) with samples annealed at 470 °C (1) and 570 °C (2).
summary: This panel displays the load-displacement behavior of Ti41Zr41Ni18 coatings under a 1 mN limit load. It compares the as-deposited sample with those annealed at 470 °C and 570 °C. At this low load, the amorphous sample (0) exhibits higher energy dissipation during the loading-unloading cycle compared to the crystalline phases (1 and 2).

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry profiles comparing as-crushed and spheroidized Ni-16.1Si powders, highlighting endothermic peak shifts and additional phase transformation events in the spheroidized sample.
summary: DSC profiles reveal distinct thermal behaviors between the two powder conditions. The as-crushed Ni-16.1Si powder exhibits two endothermic peaks between 1215°C and 1260°C. In contrast, the spheroidized powder displays four endothermic peaks, including additional events at 815–835°C and 1295–1315°C, indicating significant differences in phase stability and transformation characteristics.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of P3HT-PSL copolymer, displaying characteristic resonance peaks associated with the P3HT backbone and the PPI-SL structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of P3HT-PSL reveals that P3HT peaks dominate the signal. These results align with the expected PPI-SL structure, although the P3HT signals appear stronger than anticipated for the PPI-SL components, likely due to the occurrence of space interactions within the copolymer architecture.

caption: Calculated refractive indices of PTFE-filled composite samples derived from MG-EMA modeling across the 0.5 to 2 THz frequency range, with neat photopolymer data included as a baseline reference.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical refractive index values for PTFE-filled composite materials calculated using the MG-EMA model. Spanning a frequency range of 0.5 to 2 THz, the plot provides a comparative baseline by including experimental measurements of the neat photopolymer, illustrating the predicted optical behavior of the composite samples.

caption: Contour map illustrating the concentration of Al in the Ni-19.11 at. % Al binary alloy as a function of aging temperature (200–1400 °C) and aging time (10^-3 to 10^10 s).
summary: This contour plot displays the Al concentration in a Ni-Al binary alloy across a wide range of aging temperatures and times. The concentration decreases with lower temperatures and shorter times, showing an exponential increase as it approaches the equilibrium value, based on calculations across 15,851 data points.

caption: Evolution of matrix microhardness for Al–3.5 wt % Cu alloy as a function of aging time at 190 °C, comparing the unreinforced condition with composites containing 6, 13, and 20 vol % SiC particles.
