summary: This plot illustrates the microhardness evolution of Al–3.5 wt % Cu alloy during aging at 190 °C. It compares the unreinforced matrix against composites reinforced with 6, 13, and 20 vol % SiC particles, demonstrating how the addition of SiC particles influences the matrix hardness over the specified aging duration.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of NiFe LH in 0.5 M NaOH, showing the influence of 55 mM NH4Cl addition on the electrochemical current at 25 mV s-1.
summary: The electrochemical activity of NiFe LH toward the ammonia oxidation reaction is assessed via cyclic voltammetry. The plot illustrates the current response in 0.5 M NaOH electrolyte, both with and without the addition of 55 mM NH4Cl, measured at a scan rate of 25 mV s-1 at room temperature.

caption: Strain distribution map of the notched Ni-SX specimen at 2167 fatigue cycles, where white arrows indicate dislocation cross-slip activity from the (1–11) to the (11-1) planes.
summary: At 2167 cycles, the strain map provides clear evidence of dislocation cross-slip occurring from the (1–11) to the (11-1) planes, as indicated by the white arrows. This observation highlights the complex microstructural deformation mechanisms, including cross-slip, that accommodate the fatigue-induced strain in the notched Ni-SX specimen at 1100 °C.

caption: High-resolution HAADF-STEM image of the μ phase viewed along the [1 1 0] zone axis.
summary: This high-resolution HAADF-STEM image displays the μ phase oriented along the [1 1 0] zone axis. The brightness of the atomic columns in this image is directly proportional to the square of the atomic number Z, allowing for the inference of elemental occupation based on observed intensity variations.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing the mass loss behavior of 316L and 17-4PH metal filaments during heating.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for 316L and 17-4PH filaments are presented to characterize their thermal decomposition behavior. These TGA results were instrumental in establishing the four-stage sintering temperature profile, ensuring that binder removal and carbon residue elimination are effectively managed during the subsequent thermal processing of the metal filaments.

caption: 3D surface topography map of an as-built SS316L specimen fabricated via LPBF at a 50° build angle.
summary: Representing the 50° build angle, this 3D height map illustrates chaotic elevation variations and discontinuous surface features. These topographic characteristics are indicative of poor laser–surface interaction caused by the inclined incidence during the LPBF fabrication process, consistent with observations made at the 40° build angle.

caption: Molten pool surface at 10 ms, showing the early stage of droplet interaction at 110 Hz.
summary: At 10 ms, the molten pool surface is captured during the early stage of droplet interaction at 110 Hz. This image illustrates the progression of the impact event, providing a temporal snapshot of the surface morphology as the droplet begins to influence the molten pool dynamics.

caption: Z-axis cutting force profile during micro milling of LPBF Ti6Al4V at 60,000 rpm and 3 µm/flute with a 45 µm depth of cut.
summary: Displaying the vertical force (Fz) acting normal to the workpiece surface, this plot corresponds to the 45 µm depth of cut condition. The magnitude of this force is influenced by the tool geometry and feed rate, providing critical insight into the micro milling process of LPBF Ti6Al4V material.

caption: Hardness values plotted as a function of varying particle size, illustrating the mechanical response of the material under indentation testing.
summary: This plot displays the experimental results of microhardness testing as a function of particle size. The data illustrates the mechanical behavior of the material, specifically how variations in particle dimensions influence the measured hardness values, providing a clear quantitative relationship between the structural characteristics and the resulting mechanical performance of the specimen.

caption: Photograph of a single-layer UHDMC test block, 360 mm × 280 mm × 13 mm, printed with a 30 mm diameter nozzle and prepared for tensile testing by cutting into four dog-bone specimens.
summary: Depicted is a single-layer test block measuring 360 mm × 280 mm × 13 mm, produced using a 30 mm diameter circular nozzle. The image illustrates the preparation of four dog-bone specimens from this block, which are intended for evaluating the uniaxial tensile performance of the printed UHDMC material.

caption: Confusion matrix showing the classification outcomes for the fourth model across the specified pH level classes.
summary: The confusion matrix for the fourth model provides a detailed view of the classification results across the different pH level classes. It facilitates a quantitative analysis of the model's ability to correctly assign samples to their respective pH categories, highlighting the frequency of correct and incorrect classification instances.

caption: Surface strain distribution at the point of fracture for an as-built coupon oriented at θ = 22.5°.
summary: This panel illustrates the surface strain map of an as-built coupon tested at a 22.5° orientation. The visualization highlights the localized strain patterns observed at the moment of fracture, offering a detailed view of how the material deforms and fails when subjected to this specific angular loading configuration.

caption: Room-temperature tensile stress-strain behavior of as-cast and homogenized V0.5Nb0.5ZrTi alloys, with an inset showing TEM imaging and SAED analysis of the grain boundary region.
summary: This panel displays the tensile stress-strain curves for V0.5Nb0.5ZrTi alloys, which maintain a single-phase BCC structure and achieve approximately 20% ductility at room temperature. The inset TEM image and corresponding SAED map provide structural confirmation of the grain boundary characteristics in these high-ductility refractory high-entropy alloy specimens.

caption: Case 1 configuration of the fuel element featuring a single coolant inlet and outlet following topology optimization.
summary: Case 1 illustrates the geometric configuration of a fuel element optimized through topology optimization. This specific design incorporates a single coolant inlet and outlet, representing the baseline structure derived from the optimization process to determine the most efficient flow path for the fuel element's thermal management system.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the dendritic region in as-cast Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6, showing L12-structured γ' precipitates within a disordered fcc γ matrix, viewed along the [001] zone axis.
summary: This dark-field TEM image reveals the dendritic core microstructure of the as-cast alloy. It displays 63 ± 16 nm sized Al-Ni-Ti rich γ' precipitates embedded in a Co-Cr-Fe rich γ matrix. The inset SAED pattern confirms the L12 structure of the precipitates, with arrows indicating secondary γ' precipitates.

caption: Gas-chromatographic analysis of the condensed outlet liquid collected from the anode chamber during an endurance test with dry ethanol feed.
summary: Gas-chromatographic analysis of the condensed outlet liquid from the anode chamber confirms the absence of carbon deposits during dry ethanol operation. Chromatograms collected at 40 h and 106 h of the endurance test demonstrate the effectiveness of the protective layer in maintaining stable performance without carbonaceous fouling.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Na2SO4-Na2O system, illustrating the liquidus and solidus boundaries with specific solidus points identified at 650 °C and 750 °C.
summary: This binary phase diagram for the Na2SO4-Na2O system illustrates how the addition of Na2O lowers the liquidus and solidus temperatures of Na2SO4. Solidus points are specifically marked at 650 °C and 750 °C, which correspond to Na2O concentrations of 0.28 and 0.13 mol fraction, respectively, facilitating liquid melt formation.

caption: Surface appearance of WAAM-fabricated specimens following fire exposure and air cooling.
summary: This photograph displays the surface color of WAAM specimens after fire exposure and subsequent air cooling. The specimen exhibits a distinct color change resulting from the thermal treatment, which is consistent with the typical oxidation-induced color variations observed in traditional stainless steel materials under similar fire-exposed conditions.

caption: Cycle performance of the ZnS@CCC interlayer battery at a 2C rate, illustrating high-rate cycling stability.
summary: This plot displays the cycle performance of the ZnS@CCC interlayer battery at a 2C rate. The data demonstrates the stability and durability of the battery configuration under high-rate cycling conditions, complementing the performance metrics observed at 0.5C and confirming the effectiveness of the ZnS@CCC interlayer.

caption: Detailed view of the intrasplat fracture surface in an induction-heated cold-sprayed coating, illustrating the modified failure mode.
summary: This scanning electron microscopy image provides a detailed view of the fracture surface in an induction-heated cold-sprayed coating. The visual evidence confirms the prevalence of intrasplat fractures, which are characteristic of the post-processed material. This observation underscores the impact of induction heating on the internal fracture behavior of coatings.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for the distance of the defect center to the surface (L < 200 μm) versus effective area, with dot colors representing the effective area.
summary: This plot focuses on the influence of defect location relative to the surface on fatigue life. By analyzing the distance of the defect center to the surface for L < 200 μm, the plot highlights how subsurface and surface defects, combined with their effective area, contribute to the overall SHAP value for fatigue life.

caption: N-type TPMS unit cell geometry displayed as a conventional cube (top) and as a tetrahedral segment (bottom) following Boolean domain restriction.
summary: N-type TPMS unit cells are illustrated in their standard cubic form alongside the corresponding tetrahedral segments. These segments are generated by restricting the solid material to a central regular tetrahedral domain, facilitating the creation of hierarchical structures through coordinate transformation and reassembly into larger triangulated cube-based frameworks.

caption: Multi-material integrated 3D printing device designed for the additive manufacturing of ceramic and conductive patterns.
summary: The multi-material integrated 3D printing device shown here is employed to fabricate LTCC multilayer devices. This system features two printing units that operate alternately according to a programmed sequence to deposit ceramic structures and conductive patterns, forming the basis of the integrated additive manufacturing process for these electronic components.

caption: Geometric phase analysis map illustrating the normal strain distribution in the y-direction for the as-printed beta-type Ti alloy, showing localized strain variations across the omega and beta phase regions.
summary: Geometric phase analysis reveals the normal strain distribution in the y-direction for the as-printed beta-type Ti alloy. The map demonstrates that the omega phase regions exhibit significantly larger strains compared to the relatively smaller strains observed within the surrounding beta phase, providing insight into the mechanical response of the microstructure.

caption: Average normal stress measurements for W-DED Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy specimens fabricated using low heat input parameters.
summary: This graph displays the average normal stress characteristics of W-DED Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy under low heat input conditions. By analyzing these stress values, the study evaluates the impact of multilayer deposition on the mechanical properties of the alloy, specifically focusing on the normal stress components developed during the fabrication process.

caption: Coulombic efficiency trends for Ni-Co electrodes calculated from discharge and charge capacities across a range of current densities.
summary: Coulombic efficiency, derived from the ratio of discharge to charge capacity, is evaluated for the Ni-Co electrode samples. This plot provides a quantitative measure of the electrochemical reversibility and efficiency of the electrodes as they are subjected to different current densities during the testing process.

caption: Constant wear rate (Kf) for UHMWPE sliding against Ti-6Al-4V, measured at 2.26E-07 mm³/Nm.
summary: Panel e shows the constant wear rate (Kf) for the UHMWPE and Ti-6Al-4V material pair. The data indicates a stable wear response over the extended test period, resulting in a calculated constant wear rate of 2.26E-07 mm³/Nm, reflecting consistent material loss behavior throughout the entire duration of the study.

caption: Sequential photographic capture of the spiral robot's motion process, conducted at a 5 cm distance with a rotational speed of 120 r/min.
summary: This panel documents the specific motion process of the spiral structure robot. The experiment was conducted at a distance of 5 cm with a rotational speed of 120 r/min. These images provide a visual record of the robot's performance under controlled operational parameters, confirming the practical application of the motion principle.

caption: Migration path of a nine-interstitial cluster center within Ni-35Fe alloy at 1200 K during a 20 ns simulation, showing four distinct directional changes.
summary: Represented here is the 20 ns atomistic trajectory of a nine-interstitial cluster center in Ni-35Fe at 1200 K. The simulation data demonstrates that the cluster undergoes four specific directional changes during its migration, providing insight into how increased iron concentration influences the defect mobility and pathway behavior in the nickel-iron system.

caption: Cross-sectional view of a porcelain part fabricated via laser sintering, showing the internal structure perpendicular to the laser tracks.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the cross-sectional morphology of a porcelain component produced through laser sintering. The image highlights the internal structural arrangement of the material when viewed perpendicular to the laser tracks, providing insight into the consolidation characteristics achieved during the laser sintering process for this specific ceramic material.

caption: Micro-CT image of the specimen after SPS treatment at 1150 ℃ (5 mm × 4 mm × 4 mm), demonstrating a significant reduction in pore size and complete elimination of cracks.
summary: Following SPS post-treatment at 1150 ℃, the specimen shows a marked improvement in structural integrity. Micro-CT imaging confirms a significant reduction in pore size, with remaining defects limited to a few micropores around 10 µm, while all cracks present in the as-built state are completely eliminated.

caption: Sequential SXRD patterns captured during isothermal ageing at 350 °C for a duration of 30 minutes.
summary: Sequential SXRD patterns document the structural state of the material during a 30-minute isothermal ageing process at 350 °C. These diffraction data reveal the stability and evolution of the ω phase while the sample is held at a constant elevated temperature.

caption: Pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram of 420 martensitic stainless steel showing the influence of carbon content on phase stability.
summary: This pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram illustrates the phase stability of Fe-0.36Si-0.41Mn-13.7Cr-0.26Ni (wt.%) as a function of carbon weight percent. It highlights key transformations including δ-ferrite formation during solidification, subsequent solid-state δ→γ transformation, carbide precipitation, and austenite decomposition, which collectively define the equilibrium microstructure of the investigated 420 stainless steel alloy.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of CdTe solar modules evaluated under two distinct circuit configurations.
summary: This panel displays the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of CdTe solar modules. The data compares the performance of two different proposed circuit configurations, illustrating the electrical response of the modules under these specific conditions as part of the summarized results presented in the study's performance analysis.

caption: Projection of the input matrix X onto the first and second PLSR components, with data points colored by the target variable.
summary: Input matrix X is projected onto the two-component space defined by the PLSR model. The resulting scatter plot is colored by the target variable, allowing for the visualization of data distribution and clustering within the reduced-dimensional space defined by the primary components of the regression model.

caption: Binary clustering of decomposition and path planning data based on distance-related feature values, showing two distinct groups identified by the K-means algorithm.
summary: This panel displays the binary clustering of decomposition and path planning data using distance-related features. The K-means algorithm was applied to categorize the data into two distinct groups, labeled as desired and undesired. The visualization effectively demonstrates the successful separation of these two clusters based on their underlying feature values.

caption: Adsorption and dissociation pathways of oxygen molecules on the alloy surface.
summary: This panel depicts the atomic migration paths of oxygen molecules as they undergo adsorption and subsequent dissociation on the alloy surface. It provides a visual representation of the trajectory of oxygen species during the initial stages of the oxidation process as modeled in the simulation.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for as-deposited specimens tested in both vertical and horizontal directions, derived from three replicate tensile tests per condition.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for as-deposited specimens are presented for both vertical and horizontal orientations, based on three replicate tensile tests per condition. These results indicate that the longitudinal tensile performance of the LA-DED specimen improves more significantly than its transverse performance when compared to the A-DED specimen.

caption: CPFEM-CDM simulated stress contour map for the GSLS sample.
summary: This panel illustrates the CPFEM-CDM simulated stress contour map for the GSLS sample. The crack initiation area is clearly marked by a red wire frame on the side of the lattice. This simulation highlights how the Gyroid lattice's helical surface influences the stress distribution and subsequent crack initiation during deformation.

caption: Electron backscatter diffraction orientation map of the Alloy 699XA powder, illustrating the internal grain structure and crystallographic orientation distribution within the spherical particles.
summary: Electron backscatter diffraction orientation map of the Alloy 699XA powder, illustrating the internal grain structure and crystallographic orientation distribution within the spherical particles. This EBSD analysis, along with other imaging techniques, demonstrates the powder characteristics of the gas-atomized Alloy 699XA used for LPBF manufacturing processes.

caption: Creep-recovery response of TPU and p-MRE samples (64, 70, and 76 wt%) subjected to a step shear stress of 100 Pa, illustrating the transition from viscous deformation to equilibrium.
summary: Creep-recovery curves for TPU and p-MRE composites under 100 Pa shear stress demonstrate the material's deformation characteristics. The linear segments indicate pure viscous deformation, while the 76 wt% p-MRE sample exhibits fluctuating behavior, suggesting instability and plasticity rather than the expected elastic response as the loading time exceeds the relaxation capacity.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of N-TTCP nanoparticles and PCL/N-TTCP scaffolds, illustrating the chemical bonding characteristics of the materials.
summary: The FTIR spectra displayed in this panel characterize the chemical composition of both the N-TTCP nanoparticles and the PCL/N-TTCP composite scaffolds. By comparing these spectral signatures, the panel provides insight into the molecular interactions and functional groups present within the synthesized nanoparticles and the resulting 3D-printed composite structure.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of E. coli bacteria stained on PEGDA/GMA flat surfaces, highlighting the presence of viable (green) and non-viable (red) colonies.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy of E. coli bacteria on PEGDA/GMA flat surfaces shows the presence of viable colonies. Similar to the S. aureus results, these control surfaces exhibit few to no dead bacteria, establishing a clear reference point for assessing the antimicrobial performance of the functionalized PEGDA/GMA-AG matrices.

caption: Fabricated screw-barrel-nozzle assembly components.
summary: Physical components of the fabricated screw-barrel-nozzle assembly are displayed in this photograph. These parts represent the core hardware of the extrusion system, demonstrating the successful manufacturing of the extruder assembly components required for integration into the broader SEAM experimental setup as detailed in the study.

caption: COF variation versus the number of cycles for as-built and heat-treated samples under a 100 N normal load.
summary: This panel depicts the variation of the coefficient of friction over the number of cycles for as-built and heat-treated samples when subjected to a 100 N load. The plot captures the tribological performance and stability of the different sample conditions under this higher magnitude of normal force.

caption: Maximum intensity distribution images derived from 10,000 frames for G3P500, G5P500, and G7P500 conditions, highlighting the spatial distribution of high-temperature spatters.
summary: Maximum intensity distribution images for 10,000 frames illustrate the impact of gas flow rates on high-temperature spatter formation during LDED line scanning. These images, covering approximately 3.8 mm of scanning, specifically visualize bright, high-temperature spatters, though they do not represent the total quantity of spatters produced during the process.

caption: Geometric parameter definition for case study i, illustrating the hollow transversal section design with variable dimensions including height (H), lattice thickness (t ls), top/down wall thickness (t td), internal wall thickness (t iw), and lateral wall thickness (t lw).
summary: Case study i introduces a hollow transversal section design to optimize the stiffness-to-weight ratio of the nautical gangway. This configuration defines specific geometric parameters, including total height (H) and various wall thicknesses (t ls, t td, t iw, t lw), which were systematically varied across eight different configurations to evaluate structural performance.

caption: Friction coefficient and wear rate of CrCoNiSi films as a function of Si content or sputtering power, where black circles represent the stable friction coefficient and blue squares denote the calculated wear rate.
summary: This plot illustrates the tribological performance of CrCoNiSi films by correlating Si content or sputtering power with the stable friction coefficient and wear rate. The data, derived from friction graphs and wear volume calculations, provides a quantitative assessment of how film composition influences mechanical durability and frictional behavior under testing conditions.

caption: Temporal evolution of Al and Ni compositions across phases ϕ1 (Al2Cu), ϕ2 (Al3Ni), and the Al-rich FCC matrix ϕ3, with Cu concentration treated as a conserved parameter.
summary: This panel displays the simulated temporal progression of composition for Al and Ni within the Al-Cu-Ni system. It tracks the evolution of distinct phases ϕ1, ϕ2, and the Al-rich matrix ϕ3, starting from specific initial concentrations, while accounting for Cu as a conserved parameter throughout the diffusion-driven process.

caption: Wavelength dispersive spectroscopy elemental distribution maps for C, W, Cr, and Mo, corresponding to the cellular microstructure observed in the SEM image.
summary: WDS elemental mapping reveals the spatial distribution of carbon, tungsten, chromium, and molybdenum within the Haynes 230 alloy microstructure. These maps provide insight into the element segregation patterns that occur during the solidification process, confirming the chemical variations associated with the cellular boundaries observed in the corresponding SEM analysis.

caption: Misorientation angle distribution chart for the stir zone region with higher nanoparticle content.
summary: This histogram depicts the misorientation angle distribution in the stir zone region containing a higher concentration of nanoparticles. The data reflects the influence of nanoparticle-induced grain boundary pinning on the crystallographic misorientation characteristics, contrasting with the lower nanoparticle content zone to show the effect of processing on microstructure.

caption: Uniform local strain distribution observed along the digital extensometer for the T specimen.
summary: Following the yield strength (YS) point, the T specimen demonstrates a remarkably consistent and uniform strain distribution along the digital extensometer. This indicates that the tempered condition promotes homogeneous deformation across the gauge length during the tensile test, contrasting with the localized strain peaks observed in the AP specimen.

caption: Three-dimensional digital model representing the PEEK/Na-ALG/Photo-initiator ink design, processed via Prusa Slicer 2.7.1 to generate the G-code and STL file format for additive manufacturing.
summary: This panel displays the 3D digital design model used for the additive manufacturing process. The design is imported into Prusa Slicer 2.7.1 to generate the necessary G-code and STL file format, which serves as the foundational blueprint for printing the PEEK/Na-ALG/Photo-initiator ink blend.

caption: Resistivity curves of 3D-printed PLA-CB composites plotted against applied voltage for samples fabricated at temperatures between 230 °C and 280 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the resistivity of 3D-printed PLA-CB samples as a function of applied voltage across various printing temperatures. Electrical performance generally improves as printing temperatures increase from 230 °C to 260 °C, whereas temperatures exceeding 270 °C result in a degradation of the material's electrical properties.

caption: Bode impedance modulus plot for SLMed TC4 alloys S4–1H, S5–1H, and S6–1H after 1 h of immersion at 200 W scanning power.
summary: This Bode impedance modulus plot depicts the electrochemical performance of TC4 alloys S4–1H, S5–1H, and S6–1H. The data, measured after 1 h of immersion for samples processed at 200 W, provides critical information on the impedance values used to assess the corrosion behavior of the SLMed TC4 alloy specimens.

caption: Bright field TEM image of HIP AM 316L stainless steel captured near the [011] zone using a g 200 diffraction vector.
summary: HIP AM 316L stainless steel is represented by this bright field TEM image, which was taken close to the [011] zone along the g 200 direction. This image documents the pre-irradiation microstructure of the additive manufactured material, allowing for a direct comparison with the wrought 316L stainless steel sample.

caption: Normalized hysteresis curve and magnetization snapshot for a 14 nm thick Ni nanotube at 90° orientation, showing a pseudo-S shape and wave reversal mode.
summary: This panel displays the normalized hysteresis curve and magnetization snapshots for a 100 nm diameter Ni nanotube. The data reveals a pseudo-S shape characteristic of the wave reversal mode, where the magnetic field induces a disturbance in the central magnetic moments that propagates as a wave toward the tube ends.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of M6C carbides, demonstrating the crystallographic relationship with the γ phase along the [200] orientation.
summary: The selected area diffraction pattern confirms that the precipitates are W-rich M6C phases with a complex face-centered cubic structure. The crystallographic relationship between the M6C phase and the γ matrix is identified as M6C ≈ 3aγ along the [200] orientation, consistent with established materials science literature.

caption: Representative Volume Element (RVE) extracted from the top of the simulated microstructure, visualized with Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) color coding along the z-direction.
summary: This panel displays an RVE of size 400x400x400 µm extracted from the top of the simulated microstructure. The visualization utilizes IPF color coding along the z-direction to represent the crystallographic orientation of the material, providing a structural basis for subsequent crystal plasticity finite element (CPFE) simulations.

caption: Turbidimetry measurements of the samples at a concentration of 1 mg mL-1, presented as normalized transmittance data.
summary: Turbidimetry measurements were performed at a concentration of 1 mg mL-1 to examine the thermoresponsive behavior of CS, KC, and 3D printlets of E-5 and E-7. The data, presented as normalized transmittance, reveal variations in cloud point among the reference, upper layer, and lower layer of the examined samples.

caption: In situ Nyquist plots representing the electrochemical impedance spectra of the battery cell utilizing a CCC interlayer, captured at various voltage states during the first cycle.
summary: In situ EIS spectra for the battery cell with a CCC interlayer are presented as Nyquist plots. These measurements were performed at selected voltages based on the first cycle profile, allowing for the monitoring of impedance changes in the CCC-based cell throughout the battery's charging and discharging process.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the ZGH4142 alloy, illustrating thermal events during heating.
summary: The DSC curve for the ZGH4142 alloy reveals a prominent phase transition peak near 900 °C. Analysis indicates melting points of approximately 1120 °C for the γ′ phase and 536.5 °C for M23C6 carbides, with the solidus temperature ranging between 1330–1360 °C. The solution temperature at 1200 °C exceeds the γ′ dissolution temperature.

caption: UV absorbance spectra at 280 nm for trypsin–SL complexes, demonstrating variations in the microenvironment of aromatic amino acid residues as a function of SL/trypsin mass ratio.
summary: UV absorbance at 280 nm was measured for trypsin–SL complexes to monitor changes in the microenvironment of aromatic amino acid residues. The data indicates that the absorbance values shift with the SL/trypsin ratio, suggesting that specific molecular interactions occur between the trypsin and SL components within the complexed system.

caption: Height maps of the fracture surfaces for the specimens shown in panel A, visualizing the local texture and confirming the increase in surface roughness as the angle φ increases.
summary: Height maps of the entire fracture surface are displayed for the samples previously pictured in panel A. These maps provide a visual representation of the fracture surface topography, illustrating that the surface roughness increases with the angle φ, which directly influences the work required during the crack propagation phase.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern and Rietveld refinement results for the as-received Ni–Ti sample, highlighting the coexistence of austenite (B2), martensite (B19′), and Ni4Ti3 phases.
summary: The as-received Ni–Ti sample exhibits a complex XRD pattern confirming the presence of austenite, martensite, and Ni4Ti3 phases. Rietveld refinement reveals a primary diffraction peak at 2θ ∼ 42°, with distinct shoulders at 2θ ∼ 40° and 45° indicating the contribution of multiple crystalline phases within the material structure.

caption: Anodic branches of the potentiodynamic polarization curves for AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys, highlighting the current plateau indicative of passive film formation during polarization.
summary: The anodic branch of the potentiodynamic polarization curve reveals an obvious current plateau for both AP-NAB and HT-NAB alloys. This characteristic feature indicates the successful formation of a passive film on the alloy surfaces during the polarization process, which is critical for understanding the corrosion inhibition mechanisms in the NaCl solution.

caption: Representative ESPI speckle fringe pattern captured under static loading conditions, highlighting the designated region of interest (ROI) for measurement.
summary: This panel displays a representative speckle fringe pattern obtained via ESPI under static loading. The image highlights the specific gauge region of interest, providing the foundational visual data required to evaluate measurement errors and analyze the speckle intensity variations within the experimental setup during the static loading process.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H+1.4% 60 Ni irradiated at approximately 317 °C.
summary: Displayed are the Monte Carlo simulation results for the F82H+1.4% 60 Ni alloy. The irradiation was performed with a target temperature of 300 °C, and SiC thermometry measurements verified that the actual irradiation temperature for this specific isotope-doped specimen was approximately 317 °C.

caption: I–V–P performance graphs for the DA-SOFC at 700 °C, illustrating the impact of NH3 flow rates compared to the H2–N2 reference mixture.
summary: At 700 °C, the DA-SOFC exhibits a more pronounced performance difference between H2–N2 and NH3 fuels compared to higher temperatures. The I–V–P graphs indicate that reduced ammonia conversion efficiency begins to impact the cell performance, leading to a measurable gap between the different fuel flow conditions.

caption: Volume rendering of the high-resolution XCT scan (2 μm voxel size) for a sample manufactured at a build speed of 150 mm/s.
summary: Volume rendering of the high-resolution XCT scan, captured at a 2 μm voxel size, displays the 3D structure of a sample manufactured at a build speed of 150 mm/s. This visualization provides a comprehensive view of the sample's internal architecture, which exhibits a periodic density distribution along the build direction.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation map of the Gd-containing alloy compressed at 1100 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ to a strain of 0.5, showing the distribution of misorientation after extensive deformation.
summary: The Kernel Average Misorientation map at 0.5 strain illustrates the final state of strain distribution within the alloy. By this stage, the recrystallization process is complete within the residual deformed dendrites, reflecting the successful relief of strain concentration and the formation of a more stable, recrystallized microstructural configuration.

caption: Hardness distribution across the columnar zone of H13 ESR ingots processed at 500 A without an axial static magnetic field.
summary: Hardness distribution within the columnar zone of H13 ESR ingots is mapped for samples processed at 500 A without an axial static magnetic field. This baseline measurement reveals the inherent hardness variability present in standard ESR ingots, serving as a reference for assessing the uniformity improvements provided by magnetic field-assisted processing.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the TCP P-phase in the 3Ru degraded sample viewed along the [110] zone axis.
summary: This panel presents the selected area electron diffraction pattern of the TCP P-phase in the 3Ru degraded sample, specifically indexed for the [110] observation direction. Together with the [011] orientation, these diffraction patterns confirm the structural identification of the P-phase, which exhibits lattice parameters of a = 16.57 Å, b = 4.64 Å, and c = 9.65 Å.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from nano-indentation testing on nitrided FeCoCrNi–Al 0.5 HEAs triple-layer system, showing a leftward shift indicative of compressive residual stress in the substrate.
summary: This panel displays the load-depth nano-indentation curves for the nitrided FeCoCrNi–Al 0.5 HEA triple-layer system. The test points are located 50 μm below the HEAs/38CrMoAl interface. The observed leftward shift of the curves relative to the substrate indicates the presence of compressive residual stress within the material system.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the comprehensive mechanical properties of the current copper-base alloys against literature data from previous studies.
summary: This Ashby plot provides a comparative analysis of the comprehensive properties of the copper-base alloys developed in this work against established literature values. By benchmarking these materials against previously studied alloys, the figure illustrates the performance landscape and highlights the relative mechanical characteristics achieved in the current experimental study.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the as-cast GH4151 alloy during the heating process, highlighting five distinct endothermic peaks.
summary: The DSC curve for the as-cast GH4151 alloy reveals five endothermic peaks during the heating process, labeled Peak 1 through Peak 5. These heat absorption peaks correspond to the dissolution process of sediments within the alloy, providing critical thermal data regarding the phase transformation behavior of the material during temperature elevation.

caption: Indentation load plotted against the square of the indent diagonal for Cercom binderless WC under quasi-static and dynamic strain rates.
summary: Cercom binderless WC is evaluated by plotting indentation load versus the square of the indent diagonal. This approach facilitates hardness comparison across quasi-static and dynamic strain regimes, effectively mitigating issues related to indentation size effect variability and dynamic load fluctuations observed during the experimental testing of these tungsten carbide materials.

caption: Off-axis camera image of the PSI + T5 sample showing the melt pool overheating region at the top section.
summary: Representing the top region of the PSI + T5 sample, this image shows the melt pool tailings are consistent with those observed in the bottom and middle sections. This stability in the overheating region indicates a uniform heat distribution during the fabrication of the blade.

caption: Mass change kinetics of Co-30Ni-10Al-6Ta-xCr (x=0, 5, 10) alloys during isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the mass change kinetics of Co-30Ni-10Al-6Ta-xCr alloys during oxidation at 1000 °C. The data demonstrates that the Co-30Ni-10Al-6Ta alloy experiences a significant increase in mass over time, highlighting the oxidation behavior of these specific cobalt-based superalloy compositions as the chromium content varies from 0 to 10 percent.

caption: Atomic configuration of the 0.5% Co structure under 0.063 strain at 300 K, displaying dislocation initiation within the γ matrix.
summary: This MD snapshot depicts the 0.5% Co structure under 0.063 strain at 300 K. Consistent with the other samples, dislocation reactions initiate within the γ matrix. The analysis confirms that the evolution of dislocations and stacking faults is a characteristic response of the material system under the applied strain.

caption: Isothermal magnetization behavior of the HTHed Gyroid sample, illustrating the transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic states.
summary: Isothermal magnetization behavior of the HTHed Gyroid sample is illustrated, capturing the transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic states. By measuring these M(H) curves at various temperatures around the transition point, the magnetic properties and phase change characteristics of the gyroid-structured sample are effectively characterized and analyzed.

caption: Tabulated mechanical property values for LPBF Haynes 188, specifically detailing yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and elongation for different processing conditions.
summary: Mechanical property values, including YS, UTS, and elongation, are presented for the LPBF Haynes 188 alloy. Notably, specimens with insufficient energy input, such as the P 150 v 800 condition, exhibit reduced YS and UTS values of 636 MPa and 864 MPa, respectively, with elongation dropping significantly to 18.2%.

caption: LCSM micrograph of the W45D welded joint fusion zone displaying the ferrite and austenite phase morphology.
summary: High-magnification laser confocal scanning microscopy captures the microstructure of the W45D welded joint fusion zone. This panel illustrates the ferrite and austenite phase morphology, allowing for a detailed examination of the microstructural features present in the fusion zone under this specific orientation.

caption: Comparative analysis of FP percentage in pre-damaged NiFe versus ion impact number, evaluating the influence of thermal conductivity (κ) and electron-phonon coupling (g) parameters derived from NiFe and elemental Ni.
summary: This plot examines the sensitivity of damage recovery in pre-damaged NiFe to simulation parameters. By swapping κ and g values between NiFe and Ni, the results demonstrate that replacing these parameters significantly alters the damage state, highlighting the role of electronic properties in defect evolution during ion irradiation simulations.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectrum of ethyl eosin in water, displaying a prominent absorption maximum at 522 nm and secondary peaks at 340 nm, 303 nm, and 254 nm.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectrum of ethyl eosin in water reveals a strong absorption band in the long-wavelength region, peaking at 522 nm. Additionally, the spectrum exhibits several weaker absorption bands in the short-wavelength region, specifically identified at 340 nm, 303 nm, and 254 nm, characterizing the molecule's optical properties.

caption: Chronoamperometric stability curves for Ni5P4-Co2P/NCF maintained at current densities of 100 and 250 mA cm-2 over a 100-hour duration in 1 M KOH.
summary: The durability of Ni5P4-Co2P/NCF nanowires was evaluated via chronoamperometry at -100 and -250 mA cm-2 for 100 hours. The minimal variations observed in the I-t curves demonstrate the excellent long-term stability of the catalyst, suggesting its potential suitability for industrial-scale water splitting applications.

caption: Equilibrium phase diagram of the Al–Fe binary system illustrating the thermodynamic stability of the Al13Fe4 phase within the Al–4Fe alloy composition.
summary: The Al–Fe binary phase diagram displays the thermodynamic landscape for the Al–4Fe alloy system. Analysis of this diagram indicates that the Al13Fe4 phase is the expected equilibrium constituent for this specific alloy composition, providing a foundational understanding of the phase stability within the binary system.

caption: Histogram of grain size distribution based on equivalent circle grain diameter, showing a range from 7 to 164 μm.
summary: Quantitative EBSD grain size analysis is presented in this histogram, illustrating the distribution of equivalent circle grain diameters. The data reveals a range from 7 μm to 164 μm, with the majority of grains falling within the 10 to 20 μm size interval, characterizing the equiaxed nature of the grains.

caption: Calculated ratio of the anisotropic phase for emulsions i-iii before and after emulsification, with turbidity measurements indicating droplet enrichment in the lower phase.
summary: This panel presents the calculated anisotropic phase ratios for emulsions i-iii, comparing states before and after emulsification. Turbidity measurements of the separated phases confirm that droplets are enriched in the lower phase. The values are derived from the turbidity ratio of the lower and upper phases, quantifying the phase separation behavior.

caption: Three-dimensional visualization of sub-volumes from reconstructed SXCT data and segmented particle assemblies for Sample 1, showing more spherical particle morphologies.
summary: Sample 1 displays reconstructed SXCT sub-volumes and segmented particle assemblies. Analysis indicates that these particles are more spherical in nature, as evidenced by the Maximum Feret Diameter being closer to the Equivalent Spherical Diameter calculated from the particle volume, demonstrating a distinct morphological characteristic compared to the second sample.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map displaying the crystallographic orientation of grains in the A4 alloy after impact fracture.
summary: This IPF map provides the crystallographic orientation of the A4 alloy grains near the impact fracture site. It serves as a basis for identifying specific deformation mechanisms, such as dislocation slip or twinning, within individual grains, facilitating the characterization of grain-level responses to the applied impact stress.

caption: Normalized photoluminescence emission spectra highlighting a secondary peak at 575 nm in the batch-grown crystal, indicative of self-absorption effects.
summary: Normalized photoluminescence emission spectra highlight a distinct secondary peak at 575 nm observed specifically in the batch-grown crystal. This feature is attributed to self-absorption within the perovskite material, contrasting with the flow-reactor crystal and further substantiating the improved optoelectronic quality of the flow-synthesized perovskite crystals.

caption: Complex distribution of residual stresses in longitudinal, transverse, and normal directions across various thicknesses in the TR-AFSD 7075 repair.
summary: This panel illustrates the complex residual stress distribution within the TR-AFSD 7075 repair using neutron diffraction. It highlights the high penetration depth of the technique, which allows for non-destructive measurement of d-spacings in multiple orientations, revealing significant variations in longitudinal and transverse stress magnitudes at different depths below the substrate surface.

caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 450 °C, highlighting the relative intensities of detected elements.
summary: This panel presents the normalised mass spectrum for Inconel 718 samples subjected to 450 °C. Mass spectrum analysis was conducted to evaluate carbon content at this specific temperature. The findings demonstrate that other solutes are present in comparable quantities, despite the inability of atom probe tomography to resolve carbon traces.

caption: Bode impedance plots illustrating the temporal evolution of the supported liquid membrane (SLM) at six distinct time points during the degradation process.
summary: Bode impedance plots are presented for the SLM at six different time points during the EIS test. These plots track the temporal structural changes of the membrane as it undergoes degradation, providing a visual representation of the impedance response over time since the onset of the degradation process.

caption: Optical micrograph of P3 alloy processed with PS-4 parameters, showing the lowest crack density observed in the series.
summary: This optical micrograph features the P3 alloy manufactured with the PS-4 parameter set. As the final step in the transition from PS-1, this condition provides the lowest volumetric energy, resulting in the most significant reduction in crack size and number among the original P3 alloy samples tested.

caption: Comparative Raman spectra of native coaxial electrospun scaffolds, dual-loaded electrospun scaffolds, and dual-loaded scaffolds with adhered liposomes, highlighting an intensity increase between 1160 cm⁻¹ and 1496 cm⁻¹.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals characteristic peaks for PLCL and PVA across all scaffold samples. Following liposomal adhesion, no new peaks emerge, but a distinct increase in Raman intensity is observed within the 1160 cm⁻¹ to 1496 cm⁻¹ range, as indicated by the dotted lines in the spectral plot.

caption: XCT image of as-built GH4061 showing internal porosities, including lack-of-fusion pores and spherical keyholes, highlighted in red.
summary: As-built GH4061 samples exhibit structural defects, specifically lack-of-fusion pores and spherical keyholes, as revealed by XCT imaging. These porosities represent the most significant structural defects in LPBF-fabricated alloys, with a total volume fraction of 0.008% and an equivalent diameter of 11.1 ± 6.4 μm, though no microcracks are observed.

caption: Boxplot displaying the peak load distribution for the 1st, 10th, 20th, 30th, and 40th ranked Voronoi structures with a regularity parameter of δ = 0.4.
summary: This boxplot presents peak load data for Voronoi structures with a regularity of 0.4. Analysis reveals a substantial performance enhancement, with peak loads increasing by 58.6% to reach 1930 N. This value represents the highest peak load observed among all tested regularity levels for the ranked structures.

caption: Statistical distribution of porosity in L-DED deposited 2024 Al bulk samples, plotted as a function of the number of deposited layers.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the layer-by-layer porosity statistics for L-DED processed 2024 Al bulk samples. Statistical analysis reveals that pores are primarily located within columnar dendritic regions at the melt pool solidification front, with approximately 73.2% of the total porosity concentrated specifically along the fusion line between deposited layers.

caption: Simulated solidification microstructure at the corner position of the 11th layer in the curved component.
summary: Depicted is the simulated solidification microstructure at the corner position of the 11th layer. The higher temperature gradient at the corner leads to a faster cooling rate compared to the middle region, despite higher peak temperatures. This simulation highlights the influence of local thermal conditions on the final microstructure.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the 800 mm/s sample, highlighting the smaller, denser distribution of κ-carbide.
summary: This dark-field TEM image illustrates the κ-carbide distribution in the 800 mm/s sample, where bright regions denote the carbide phase. The increased scanning speed impedes the growth of κ-carbide, leading to a smaller size and a denser distribution of these precipitates compared to the slower 650 mm/s processing condition.

caption: Static magnetization curves for M300 alloy before and after heat treatment, measured within a 25 kA/m field intensity range.
summary: Panel a displays the static magnetization curves for the M300 alloy, tested across a 25 kA/m field intensity range. These curves illustrate the magnetic response of the material, providing a baseline for evaluating the impact of heat treatment on the alloy's magnetic properties and overall performance.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the as-built GH4099 alloy grain boundary, highlighting a disc-shaped carbide selected for electron diffraction analysis.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the microstructure of an as-built GH4099 alloy at the grain boundary. A disc-shaped carbide is clearly visible, and the circled region indicates the specific area selected for subsequent electron diffraction analysis to determine the structural characteristics of the grain boundary precipitate.

caption: Custom-built laboratory apparatus designed at the Institute of Materials and Machine Mechanics for the production of large aluminum foam plates.
summary: This photograph displays the specialized laboratory equipment developed at the Institute of Materials and Machine Mechanics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences. The apparatus is specifically engineered for the foaming process of large aluminum foam plates, providing the necessary infrastructure to investigate and manufacture these metallic cellular materials under controlled conditions.

caption: Microhardness profile of the Grad 1 sample measured across the sample height following homogenization at 1200 °C.
summary: The microhardness profile of the Grad 1 sample after homogenization at 1200 °C is presented. Initial hardness values of 600 HV at the bottom decrease rapidly to 330 HV within 1 mm of height, subsequently remaining constant toward the top surface, demonstrating a significant gradient in mechanical properties across the sample.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of the 3D-printed Ruby filter, characterized by increased transmission near 600 nm and a high-transmission plateau in the red region.
summary: The Ruby ink filter exhibits a distinct optical response where transmission increases near 600 nm. This spectral behavior effectively suppresses the blue–green region of the light spectrum, while simultaneously establishing a high-transmission plateau in the red region, confirming the filter's performance as a red-selective optical component.

caption: Pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram for the Ni–19Co-xAl system (0 < x < 50 at.%) calculated using Thermo-Calc, highlighting a eutectic point E1 at 23.7 at.% Al.
summary: This panel displays the pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram for the Ni–19Co-xAl system calculated via Thermo-Calc software. The diagram illustrates phase stability across a range of Al concentrations from 0 to 50 at.%, specifically identifying the eutectic point E1 at 23.7 at.% Al where the γ+β eutectic reaction occurs.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) map corresponding to the region in (b), showing Ag enrichment in the nanoparticles.
summary: This EDS map reveals the chemical composition of the fine nanoparticles (type A1, A2) observed in the ABF-STEM image. The analysis confirms that these particles are significantly enriched with Ag, providing clear evidence of the elemental distribution within the precipitate-dislocation architecture of the PBF-EB sample.

caption: Equilibrium phase fraction diagram calculated for the Al-6Zn-4Ni-2Mg-1Cu-Fe alloy, illustrating the stable phases present across a range of temperatures.
summary: This equilibrium phase fraction diagram provides a thermodynamic overview of the stable phases in the Al-6Zn-4Ni-2Mg-1Cu-Fe alloy. It highlights the formation of primary phases, specifically Al3Ni and Al9Fe2, which remain stable during solution heat treatment and are enriched in heavy elements like Ni, Fe, and Cu.

caption: EPMA compositional map of Co distribution in the as-built condition, highlighting the MP boundary with a black dashed line.
summary: Cobalt distribution in the as-built sample is visualized through this EPMA compositional map. The MP boundary is delineated by a black dashed line to assist in identifying micro-segregation patterns. This map is part of a correlative study investigating the elemental distribution at a finer scale within the material.

caption: Stress-strain profile of PA12 under uniaxial tension, demonstrating a linear elastic response up to a stress threshold of approximately 30 MPa.
summary: The stress-strain profile for PA12 is depicted to confirm the reliability of the mechanical data. As illustrated, PA12 exhibits an initially linear elastic response under uniaxial tension, reaching a stress threshold of approximately 30 MPa. This curve characterizes the material's mechanical behavior during the experimental test.

caption: Experimental setup photograph showing the utilization of two smartphones for imaging the microfluidic chip.
summary: Panel H displays the experimental configuration where two smartphones are employed to capture images of the microfluidic chip. This setup highlights the practical, low-cost approach to data acquisition, utilizing mobile technology for the analysis of the microfluidic device's performance in pathogen detection.

caption: Force response evolution of MEAM structures during a 45° impact test.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of the reaction force during the impact of a hammer against a cantilever-fixed MEAM specimen at a 45° release angle. A sharp drop in the force curve at approximately 7.5 ms indicates the fracture of the ST specimens under the applied impact loading conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental maps of the friction track on the untreated EBM sample, highlighting the distribution of elements within the wear zone.
summary: These EDX maps illustrate the elemental distribution across the friction track of the untreated EBM sample. The mapping correlates with the SEM observations, showing that the petal-like peeling occurs primarily within the dark-appearing oxide layer. This confirms that the friction track profile corresponds to the depth of the outer oxide layer.

caption: Load versus deflection curve obtained from a fracture toughness test conducted at room temperature.
summary: This plot illustrates the load-deflection behavior of the tested samples during a fracture toughness evaluation performed at room temperature. The curve provides essential mechanical data regarding the material's resistance to crack propagation, serving as a primary indicator of fracture toughness performance under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: HAADF-STEM image showing the morphology of W phase and Al3Sc phase precipitates within the aluminum matrix.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a high-contrast visualization of the W intermetallic phase and Al3Sc phase precipitates. The imaging technique was employed to investigate the nucleation mechanisms of the W phase by examining Sc-enriched regions near the grain boundaries within the aluminum matrix, revealing the structural distribution of these intermetallic phases.

caption: Wavelet transform of the EXAFS function measured at the K-Ni edge for the Fe58Ni25B17 alloy following high-pressure torsion (HPT) processing at 77 K.
summary: This wavelet transform plot represents the EXAFS function at the K-Ni edge for an Fe58Ni25B17 alloy subjected to HPT at 77 K. The analysis was performed to refine the composition of the first nearest coordination sphere of nickel, with maxima corresponding to the first peak of the Fourier transform.

caption: Metallographic cross-section of V deposited layer processed at 500 W laser power and 15 mm/s scanning rate, revealing the interface orientation perpendicular to the deposition direction.
summary: This optical micrograph shows the microstructural morphology of a V deposited layer processed at 500 W and 15 mm/s. The interface is oriented perpendicular to the deposition direction. Lower laser power combined with high scanning speeds often results in suboptimal metallurgical quality, characterized by unmelted particles and increased porosity.

caption: Line scan profile showing the Nb element concentration gradient across the η phase interface depicted in panel (c).
summary: This line scan profile quantifies the Nb element concentration gradient across the η phase interface. The data confirms that diffused atoms at the interface fail to rapidly re-form a stable crystal structure, resulting in a solid solution characterized by a measurable concentration gradient within the matrix.

caption: Optimized trajectory for nonlinear quadrotor dynamics performing a 90-degree rotation around the y-axis over a 4-second duration.
summary: This visualization displays the optimized flight path for a quadrotor system executing a precise 90-degree rotation about the y-axis. The trajectory is calculated to avoid constraints and prevent gimbal lock during the 4-second maneuver, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed optimization method in handling complex nonlinear quadrotor dynamics.

caption: Digital image correlation strain map of the CR43%/A500°C-1.5h specimen during the first loading cycle, illustrating localized strain patterns at 6% total strain.
summary: This DIC strain map shows the CR43%/A500°C-1.5h specimen during the first loading cycle at 6% total strain. The image captures the formation of Lüders-like bands in localized high-strain regions, which are transient features that appear during loading and disappear during the unloading process, influenced by the material's specific microstructure.

caption: Cl2p high-resolution XPS spectra of PVBC, PVBC-MPy, CMPSF, and M-2#, M-4#, M-6# membranes, highlighting the absorption peak at 200 eV.
summary: High-resolution Cl2p XPS spectra are presented for the specified membranes. A consistent Cl2p absorption peak at 200 eV is observed across all measured samples. This spectral feature confirms the presence of chlorine in the membrane structures, supporting the chemical characterization and structural analysis of the synthesized materials.

caption: Ragone plot illustrating the relationship between volumetric energy density and power density for the hybrid ASC device.
summary: Ragone plot illustrating the relationship between volumetric energy density and power density for the hybrid ASC device. The device achieves a high volumetric energy density of 6.7 mWh·cm⁻³ at a power density of 11.6 mW·cm⁻³, highlighting its effective energy storage performance for practical applications.

caption: Austenite fraction evolution in the duplex stainless steel cell, comparing MICRESS simulation results with the JMAK-based metamodel predictions.
summary: Austenite fraction evolution is plotted against time, demonstrating the performance of the JMAK-based metamodel relative to the MICRESS phase-field simulation. The graph validates the metamodel's accuracy in capturing the austenite transformation kinetics within the duplex stainless steel cell when subjected to the temperature history defined in panel a.

caption: Raman spectrum of a graphite inclusion, diamond host, and hydrous hydroxyl species in sample B20–1, highlighting the presence of aqueous fluid components.
summary: Raman spectroscopy of sample B20–1 identifies a graphite inclusion and hydroxyl stretching modes, confirming the presence of aqueous fluid-bearing inclusions. The spectrum also displays high-intensity diamond bands. These findings are consistent with the presence of hydrous species within the diamond bulk, as indicated by the 3200–3800 cm⁻¹ region.

caption: FTIR spectrum of synthesized PA12 showing characteristic polyamide absorption bands, including N–H stretching at 3285 cm−1, C–H vibrations at 2920 and 2852 cm−1, amide group stretching at 1631 and 1549 cm−1, C–H bending at 1462 cm−1, and C–N stretching at 1269 cm−1.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of synthesized PA12 confirms its chemical structure through characteristic absorption bands. Key features include hydrogen-bonded N–H stretching at 3285 cm−1, methylene C–H vibrations at 2920 and 2852 cm−1, amide group stretching at 1631 and 1549 cm−1, C–H bending at 1462 cm−1, and strong C–N stretching at 1269 cm−1.

caption: Temperature-dependent calibration of elastic constants demonstrating a significantly higher sensitivity to temperature changes in the FCC (ϕ3) phase compared to the Al2Cu IMC (ϕ1) phase.
summary: Temperature-dependent elastic constants reveal a more pronounced influence of temperature on the FCC (ϕ3) phase than on the Al2Cu IMC (ϕ1) phase. These DFT-computed elastic constants provide critical data for phase field simulations and are compiled to compare values at absolute zero and the specific simulation temperature.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) patterns comparing the solution and stabilization post-deposition heat treatments (PDHTs).
summary: This panel displays the SXRD patterns obtained from the solution and stabilization PDHTs. The diffraction data indicates that both heat treatments result in a final microstructure containing similar secondary phases, as there are no significant differences observed between the patterns collected for the two distinct processing conditions.

caption: Photograph of a 316L-17–4PH multi-material synchronous reluctance rotor manufactured using a dedicated multi-material LPBF system.
summary: Depicted is a 316L-17–4PH synchronous reluctance rotor created with a dedicated multi-material LPBF system. This approach yielded improved spatial accuracy compared to conventional modifications. The material interface zone within this component spans approximately 420 µm, demonstrating the enhanced precision achievable with specialized multi-material additive manufacturing hardware.

caption: Tabulated output parameters for the electron beam melting process, including acceleration voltage, beam current, and exposure duration.
summary: This table outlines the specific electron beam melting parameters utilized during the experiment. The process was conducted at an acceleration voltage of 35 kV and a beam current of 0.5 A, with the beam exposed in a controlled spiral pattern for a total duration of 20 minutes at 17.5 kW.

caption: SHAP summary plot showing the feature contribution analysis for the Random Forest (RF) model regarding joint shear capacity.
summary: The SHAP summary plot for the RF model displays the impact of input variables on the joint shear capacity (Fmax). It effectively communicates which features are most influential in the model's decision-making process, providing a clear visual representation of how input fluctuations correlate with changes in the predicted shear capacity.

caption: Current intensity I represented in relation to the specified process parameters.
summary: Current intensity I is represented in relation to the specified process parameters to demonstrate the electrical response during the manufacturing process. This plot highlights the dependency of current levels on the input variables, serving as a critical metric for understanding the electrical behavior and stability of the system under different conditions.

caption: Radar diagram illustrating the shifts in ranking for critical evaluation parameters (CEPs) following a sensitivity analysis conducted by varying weights.
summary: This radar diagram visualizes the robustness of the model by demonstrating the changes in ranks of critical evaluation parameters (CEPs) after a sensitivity analysis. By varying the weights assigned to these parameters, the figure provides a clear comparison of ranking stability before and after the sensitivity assessment process.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from midpoint 1 at the NiTi-side interface.
summary: Midpoint 1 diffraction results provide crystallographic information for the NiTi-side interface. This SAED pattern is part of a series of diffraction analyses used to identify the distinct phases present at different locations along the interface, contributing to the overall characterization of the weld pool microstructure.

caption: Microhardness distribution profile measured parallel to the substrate for a double-layer CLS with a pitch of 2.0/1.0 mm, processed at alloy/bronze deposition speeds of 100/150 mm/min.
summary: This panel displays the longitudinal microhardness distribution of a double-layer CLS sample. The measurement is taken parallel to the substrate surface at a specific pitch of 2.0/1.0 mm. The deposition speeds for the alloy and bronze layers are set at 100 mm/min and 150 mm/min, respectively, characterizing the mechanical property profile.

caption: Atomic configuration showing the surface adsorption of a single oxygen atom.
summary: This panel displays a top-view atomic configuration resulting from the adsorption of one oxygen atom onto the surface. The representation is derived from DFT calculations, illustrating the specific binding site and local structural arrangement of the oxygen atom relative to the substrate surface atoms at this low coverage level.

caption: Absolute error (AE) assessment for the PEOF-SNFF model in scenario-1.
summary: This panel presents the absolute error (AE) assessment for the PEOF-SNFF model applied to scenario-1. As part of the broader evaluation of the artificial backpropagation networks, this plot quantifies the predictive accuracy of the model, serving as a critical metric for validating the performance of the network in scenario-1.

caption: MAP analysis of the fracture surface for a sample bonded at 1050 °C for 5 minutes, revealing the distribution of phases across the failure interface.
summary: This MAP analysis of the fracture surface for a sample bonded at 1050 °C for 5 minutes reveals that crack propagation occurred through hard eutectic chromium and nickel boride compounds. These structural features indicate low strength and fracture energy, which is consistent with the observed shear test results for this material.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph of 316L stainless steel after exposure to LBE corrosion at 550 °C for 500 hours.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the microstructural characteristics of 316L stainless steel following a 500-hour corrosion test in liquid lead-bismuth eutectic (LBE) at 550 °C. The micrograph serves as the baseline for evaluating the material's surface degradation and microstructural evolution under these specific high-temperature corrosive conditions.

caption: Validation parity plot comparing M2P model predictions against metallographic analysis for oxygen overlap percentages across O_10, O_30, and O_50 conditions.
summary: This parity plot validates the M2P model by comparing its predicted oxygen overlap percentages against actual values derived from metallographic analysis. The results demonstrate the model's performance across three distinct conditions, O_10, O_30, and O_50, providing a quantitative assessment of the model's accuracy in predicting local profile overlaps.

caption: Three-dimensional distribution of L1 2 precipitates in the CRSA750 alloy, visualized using an Al 13.13 at.% iso-concentration surface combined with individual Al ion positions.
summary: The 3D reconstruction of the CRSA750 alloy highlights the morphology and distribution of L1 2 precipitates. By plotting the 13.13 at.% Al iso-concentration surface alongside individual Al ions, the image provides a clear visualization of the precipitate arrangement within the reconstructed volume of the atom probe data.

caption: Rectangular block build at 800 °C after 109.1 seconds of processing.
summary: At 109.1 seconds, the build processed at 800 °C remains highly stable. Unlike the ambient temperature counterpart, this sample shows no evidence of defects or edge distortion, confirming that the elevated temperature environment effectively stabilizes the melt pool and the overall build geometry.

caption: Cross-sectional X-Y view of the simulated dendrite structure at a cooling rate of 400 K/s, highlighting the refined distribution of α-Al and β-Si phases.
summary: At a cooling rate of 400 K/s, this simulation panel depicts the X-Y cross-sectional morphology of the single dendrite. It captures the refined distribution of α-Al and β-Si phases, demonstrating the impact of rapid cooling on the final grain structure during directional growth along the z-axis.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image demonstrating the cellular uptake of DiL-labeled ApoVs by target cells.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images show the uptake of DiL-labeled ApoVs. The visual evidence confirms that the ApoVs are successfully internalized by HUVECs, supporting the functional evaluation of these vesicles in subsequent migration and tube formation assays.

caption: Arrhenius plot of logarithmic shear rate versus inverse absolute temperature, comparing continuous and temperature change experiments at early and later creep stages.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the logarithmic shear rate as a function of inverse temperature. It compares data from continuous and temperature change experiments, with symbols indicating early (0.75% strain) and later (4.25% strain) creep stages, providing insight into the thermal activation of the creep process.

caption: Absorption coefficients of AlxGa1-xAsySb1-y alloys, showing modeled curves alongside experimental data for specific compositions and a red dashed line demarcating two distinct absorption regions.
summary: Absorption coefficients for AlxGa1-xAsySb1-y are presented, illustrating a gradual transition between direct and indirect bandgap behaviors. A red dashed line separates the plot into two regions, with the first region specifically targeting band-edge absorption. Modeled curves are validated against experimental data for selected Al-Ga-As-Sb compositions.

caption: Statistical comparison of the number of HUVECs migrating toward the center of the materials at day 1.
summary: Quantitative analysis of HUVEC migration at day 1 shows that the number of cells in UMS600-treated blood clots is 8.67 ± 2.89, which is significantly higher than the 1.33 ± 0.58 observed in natural blood clots. This indicates that UMS600 treatment facilitates accelerated and deeper cell migration early on.

caption: Vickers hardness values plotted as a function of laser energy density for the Nb–40Ti–20Ta alloy samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between Vickers hardness and laser energy density for the Nb–40Ti–20Ta alloy. The data indicates that the hardness of the alloy is almost positively correlated with the laser energy density, demonstrating that increasing the energy density during fabrication leads to higher hardness values in the samples.

caption: Generated I-V curves for the PhotoWatt-PWP201 PV module, derived from TSEC data (I3,3,1 and I3,4,1) using TDM parameter values extracted via the SNF-TSEC optimization approach.
summary: This panel displays the generated I-V curves for the PhotoWatt-PWP201 PV module. These curves are constructed using TDM physical parameters obtained through the SNF-TSEC optimization approach. The visualization demonstrates the performance characteristics of the module based on the TSEC data points I3,3,1 and I3,4,1.

caption: Schematic illustration of the fusion line evolution under the influence of a magnetic field mechanism, showing the modified interface geometry compared to standard WAAM.
summary: This schematic depicts the fusion line evolution when a magnetic field mechanism is applied during deposition. By comparing this to standard WAAM, the diagram highlights how the magnetic field influences the fusion interface geometry, providing a structural basis for understanding the resulting changes in the deposited layer's fusion line profile.

caption: Conceptual illustration of a biological tongue surface structure.
summary: This panel presents a conceptual illustration of a biological tongue surface structure. As a natural chemical sense, the tongue's surface structure is designed to capture the recognition and uptake of nutrients, serving as the biological inspiration for the development of the composite electrochemical sensor described in the study.

caption: Specific shear strength of joints plotted as a function of bonding time, normalized relative to the performance of the two base materials.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific shear strength of the vacuum diffusion bonded joints in relation to the two base materials. By normalizing the joint strength against the base materials, the graph highlights the relative mechanical performance and efficiency of the bonding process across different bonding time conditions.

caption: EDS line scan profile across an M23C6 carbide and the adjacent matrix in the UT specimen, showing the elemental distribution over a 100 nm range on both sides of the carbide center.
summary: This panel displays an EDS line scan across an M23C6 carbide in the UT specimen. The scan covers a 100 nm region on either side of the carbide center. These results, combined with other data, indicate a reduction of solute atoms, which contributes to an increase in the material's thermal conductivity.

caption: 3D isosurfaces of deformation charge density for Mn-segregated Ni Σ3 [110](111) grain boundaries, with yellow and aquamarine regions representing electron accumulation and depletion, respectively, at an isosurface value of ± 0.008 eV/Å³.
summary: The 3D deformation charge density map for Mn-segregated grain boundaries reveals significant electronic redistribution. Segregation induces electron accumulation around the Mn atom and increases electronic non-uniformity around host Ni atoms, specifically showing increased charge density facing the Mn atom and decreased density in regions backing the solute atom.

caption: Spatial distribution diagram of the Schmid factor for the TA15 alloy.
summary: Panel (a) presents the spatial distribution diagram of the Schmid factor for the TA15 alloy. This visualization provides insight into the orientation-dependent slip activity within the material's microstructure, serving as a baseline for comparing the influence of reinforcement particles on the deformation behavior of the alloy system.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the normalized strength and cost of room-temperature (squares) and high-temperature (circles) aluminum alloys, including three proposed designs relative to wrought Al 7075.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the performance of various aluminum alloys by mapping normalized strength against cost. It highlights room-temperature and high-temperature variants, including three novel designs. The data demonstrates that the proposed alloys achieve superior strength and cost efficiency compared to the benchmark printable alloy, which is comparable to wrought Al 7075.

caption: Overview of the Polymer Impregnation and Pyrolysis (PIP) post-processing sequence for green bodies.
summary: The PIP post-processing sequence is illustrated as a critical step for the densification of green bodies. By infiltrating the porous structure with polymer precursors followed by pyrolysis, this method suppresses internal defects and significantly enhances the final density and mechanical integrity of the manufactured SiC components.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph highlighting dislocation pairs observed in the sample after tensile testing at 400 °C.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging confirms the presence of dislocation pairs in the sample after tensile deformation at 400 °C. These features, characterized by spacings of 10-20 nm, are consistent with the dark-field observations, illustrating the microstructural evolution and dislocation behavior occurring during the tensile process at this specific temperature.

caption: Convergence plot of Bayesian optimization for aerospace bracket lightweighting, showing the optimization progress over 100 iterations.
summary: This plot illustrates the convergence behavior of Bayesian optimization applied to the lightweighting of an aerospace bracket. Utilizing a DNN surrogate trained on 500 GAN-generated RVEs, the process successfully maximizes the stiffness-to-weight ratio under tensile and shear loads of 10 kN, adhering to MIL-HDBK-17 standards over 100 optimization iterations.

caption: CAD models representing four distinct groups of Ti64 lattice architectures, featuring square, octagonal, and round strut cross-sections.
summary: The CAD models displayed here represent four distinct groups of Ti64 lattice architectures designed for the study. These models incorporate varying strut geometries, specifically square, octagonal, and round cross-sections. This design approach ensures consistent anticipated mechanical behavior across the different strut shapes, providing a basis for comparative structural performance analysis.

caption: Laboratory X-ray diffraction pattern showing detectable crystals in the sample printed at the highest ΔH value.
