summary: Laboratory X-ray diffraction analysis of the sample printed at the highest ΔH value confirms the presence of detectable crystals. This diffraction pattern serves as evidence of the crystalline phases formed within the heat-affected zone, correlating with the predicted melt pool geometry and the observed micro-structural distribution.

caption: Pole figure plot for the XY plane of heat-treated PBF-LB 70/30 CuNi, demonstrating the crystallographic texture intensity.
summary: The pole figure for the XY plane of heat-treated PBF-LB 70/30 CuNi provides quantitative evidence of the material's crystallographic texture. It demonstrates a moderate texture intensity with a preferred grain orientation in the <100> direction, confirming the expected microstructural development observed in the XY plane of this alloy.

caption: Close-up view of the test apparatus highlighting the configuration for high-temperature mechanical evaluation of the dot matrix specimens.
summary: The enlarged image provides a detailed view of the test apparatus used for the high-temperature mechanical evaluation of dot matrix specimens. This visual documentation confirms the experimental configuration, which is essential for understanding how the mechanical curves are generated during the testing of these structures at various temperatures.

caption: Transient current-time response curves for SLM-316L stainless steel specimens fabricated in three distinct construction orientations, measured in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at an applied potential of 0.1 V vs. SCE.
summary: This plot illustrates the transient current-time response of SLM-316L stainless steel specimens across three different construction orientations. The measurements were conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution under a constant applied potential of 0.1 V vs. SCE, with j m and t m representing the current density and time at peak values.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of poly(glycolic acid) (PGA) isolated from GACam after 3 hours of reaction at 205 °C, showing the distribution of cyclic and linear chain species.
summary: This MALDI-TOF mass spectrum displays the molecular distribution of PGA isolated from GACam after 3 hours at 205 °C. Analysis reveals that cyclic and linear chain species are present in nearly equal intensities, indicating that both structural forms are formed and maintained under these specific thermal processing conditions.

caption: Dark field TEM micrograph showing thin-film retained austenite (RA) distributed in parallel between the lath bainitic ferrite structures in the LPBF-AB specimen.
summary: The dark field TEM image illustrates the distribution of thin-film retained austenite within the LPBF-AB specimen. The austenite phase is observed to be arranged in a parallel configuration between the lath bainitic ferrite structures, confirming the specific phase arrangement characteristic of this material's microstructure.

caption: High-rate discharge (HRD) performance curves displaying discharge capacities for the three alloys across a current density range of 10–1000 mA g-1.
summary: High-rate discharge performance reflects the electrochemical kinetics of the alloys. The discharge capacities of the La3MgNi14, La2.5Y0.5MgNi14, and La2YMgNi14 alloys are displayed across a current density range of 10–1000 mA g-1, demonstrating how varying Y content influences the rate capability and kinetic performance of the electrodes.

caption: Coefficient of friction values for various materials tested against NiTi at stroke lengths of 50, 150, and 500 µm.
summary: This plot illustrates the tribological performance of selected materials when subjected to sliding contact against NiTi. The experimental results demonstrate that the measured coefficients of friction for these material combinations consistently fall within the range of 0.8 to 1.4 across the tested stroke lengths of 50, 150, and 500 µm.

caption: Time-stamped major strain progression maps for the Al6061/AlSi10Mg multi-material sample during the shear test, generated using GOM software.
summary: Major strain progression maps illustrate the deformation evolution within the Al6061/AlSi10Mg multi-material sample under increasing shear loads. These time-stamped visualizations, processed via GOM software, provide a detailed spatial representation of how strain accumulates across the heterogeneous interface throughout the duration of the mechanical shear test.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the same area as panel (a), generated using the diffraction ring segment indicated in the SAED pattern.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph provides a complementary view of the same area shown in the bright-field image. It was constructed by utilizing the specific diffraction ring segment identified by the black circle in the SAED pattern, allowing for the visualization of specific crystallographic features within the deformed microstructure.

caption: Comparison of tensile properties for the EDPS alloy against various eutectic and near-eutectic HEAs from literature, with dotted lines highlighting specimens characterized by a directional microstructure.
summary: Tensile properties of the EDPS alloy are plotted against a wide range of eutectic and near-eutectic HEAs reported in literature. The EDPS sample exhibits an enhanced strength-ductility synergy compared to most counterparts. Data points within the dotted region specifically represent specimens processed to possess a directional microstructure.

caption: Hall–Petch relationship represented by microhardness (Hv) plotted against the inverse square-root of grain size (D−1/2) for nanocrystalline Ni(Fe) alloys, comparing as-deposited and annealed specimens.
summary: This Hall–Petch plot illustrates the microhardness of nanocrystalline Ni(Fe) alloys as a function of grain size. Black circles represent as-deposited and low-temperature annealed samples, showing a strong linear correlation with a Hall–Petch constant of 23.933 GPa nm1/2. Red circles indicate higher-temperature annealed specimens that deviate from this linear trend.

caption: Weibull fracture probability plot of compressive strength for SC samples sintered in air at 1190°C for 3 hours.
summary: Presented here is the Weibull fracture probability plot for SC samples sintered in air at 1190°C for 3 hours. This analysis allows for the determination of the characteristic compressive strength, facilitating a statistically robust comparison of the mechanical reliability of the SC material processed in an air atmosphere.

caption: Potentiostatic current transients for Ni-Co/L-Ser on a GC electrode, with blue dashed lines marking the (jM, tM) intersection points.
summary: Potentiostatic current transients for the Ni-Co/L-Ser system on a GC electrode are displayed. The plot illustrates the electrochemical response over time, with blue dashed lines indicating the intersection points (jM, tM) that characterize the nucleation and growth kinetics of the Ni-Co alloy deposition process within the DES electrolyte.

caption: High-magnification LSCM image of SLM pure tungsten deposit B13, revealing a low density of pores within the microstructure.
summary: This high-magnification LSCM image of sample B13 demonstrates a relatively low pore density compared to other specimens. The visualization confirms the structural integrity of the pure tungsten deposit. The observed grain boundaries and crack paths are consistent with the overall mechanical properties and residual stress profiles of the material.

caption: Transient current response for the 45° construction direction specimen, evaluated against theoretical progressive and instantaneous nucleation models.
summary: The transient current curve for the 45° construction direction specimen is presented and compared with standard progressive and instantaneous nucleation models. By plotting the experimental data as blue upright triangles against the black and red solid lines, the nucleation mechanism of the passivation film on the 316L stainless steel is characterized.

caption: Shifted liquidus and solidus lines representing the thermodynamic response to high cooling rates typical of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) processing.
summary: This phase diagram illustrates the modification of liquidus and solidus lines under high cooling rate conditions. By incorporating these shifts, the model effectively captures solute trapping behavior, which is a critical characteristic of LPBF processing conditions, providing a more accurate representation of the solidification dynamics in rapid manufacturing environments.

caption: Normalized confusion matrix illustrating class-wise detection accuracy and misclassifications for the crack detection model at the default confidence threshold.
summary: This normalized confusion matrix provides a qualitative assessment of the crack detection model's performance. It visualizes class-wise detection accuracy and identifies specific instances of misclassification at the default confidence threshold. These results complement quantitative metrics, such as precision, recall, and F1-score, to offer a comprehensive evaluation of the model's predictive capabilities.

caption: Camera image focus adjusted to capture the specific region between the torch nozzle and the substrate, enabling the observation of droplet detachment during the WAAM process.
summary: The camera image focus is specifically adjusted to target the gap between the torch nozzle and the substrate. This setup is designed to capture high-resolution images of droplet detachment during the WAAM process, allowing for detailed observation of the material transfer dynamics occurring within the deposition zone.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the UV-Vis absorbance spectrum for 3-OCH3-bisPh-B during a 30-minute incubation period in the presence of water.
summary: The absorbance spectrum of 3-OCH3-bisPh-B is shown over a 30-minute incubation period in the presence of water. This plot tracks the changes in the optical properties of the compound as it undergoes hydrolysis, providing insight into the reaction kinetics and the spectral evolution of the benzoxazinone derivative.

caption: Young’s modulus distribution for the Ni-Cr-Fe-Mo-W composition grid, computed using Voigt-Reuss relations applied to random forest-predicted elastic constants.
summary: Young’s modulus values for the Ni-Cr-Fe-Mo-W alloy system are shown in a box plot format. These properties were evaluated by applying Voigt-Reuss equations to Cij constants predicted by a random forest model. The plot effectively captures the distribution characteristics, including quartiles and outliers, for the specified composition groups.

caption: Vertical section phase diagram of the Ti–25Al-xNb system as determined by Kazantseva et al., showing the evolution of phase boundaries with varying Nb concentration.
summary: The Ti–25Al-xNb vertical section phase diagram illustrates how varying Nb content alters the temperature ranges of specific phase regions in Ti2AlNb-based alloys. This diagram, determined by Kazantseva et al., serves as a comparative reference for understanding the structural evolution and phase stability of these titanium-aluminide alloys as the niobium concentration changes.

caption: High-resolution O 1s XPS spectrum of the passivated H900 sample, indicating the presence of various oxygen-containing species.
summary: Oxygen bonding states on the passivated H900 sample are examined via the high-resolution O 1s XPS spectrum. This analysis identifies the oxygen species associated with oxides and hydroxides, contributing to the comprehensive characterization of the passivated surface as presented in the study's XPS results and supporting tables.

caption: Pole figure of the AC-ST-AFSD sample illustrating the texture evolution under the specified processing conditions.
summary: The AC-ST-AFSD sample exhibits a specific crystallographic texture as shown in the pole figure. Similar to the AC-AFSD variant, this sample demonstrates a pronounced preferred orientation along the (100) and (111) planes, highlighting the consistent shear-texture-related microstructural features induced by the AC-ST-AFSD processing method.

caption: Quantitative elemental composition analysis of Zone 2, marked by a red star in (b), confirming the co-enrichment of Ni and Nb.
summary: Quantitative elemental composition analysis of Zone 2, marked by the red star in the TEM image, confirms the co-enrichment of Ni and Nb. This spectroscopic data supports the identification of the dark-gray regions as distinct Ni-Nb-rich phases within the Nb/Cu interfacial structure.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curves illustrating the performance of a trained Deep SVDD model evaluated on noisy testing datasets across varying signal-to-noise ratios.
summary: This panel displays the ROC curves and corresponding AUC values for a Deep SVDD model tested under different signal-to-noise ratio conditions. The results demonstrate the model's classification performance when subjected to varying levels of noise, providing a quantitative assessment of its robustness in detecting anomalies within noisy signal environments.

caption: STEM-BF micrograph of sample AB subjected to high-pressure torsion (HPT) for 10 turns, showing the microstructure near the disc edge at a strain of approximately 208.
summary: This STEM-BF micrograph displays the microstructure of sample AB after undergoing 10 turns of high-pressure torsion, reaching a strain of about 208 near the disc edge. The image provides a visual representation of the material's state following severe plastic deformation, serving as the basis for subsequent elemental mapping analysis.

caption: Tribological performance represented by the COF curve for Ti–Al–V alloy using an SLA alumina ball.
summary: The coefficient of friction (COF) curve for the Ti–Al–V alloy is shown, illustrating the material's frictional response when subjected to wear testing with an SLA alumina ball. This measurement characterizes the tribological performance of the titanium alloy, highlighting its specific friction profile throughout the duration of the test.

caption: Localized Raman spectra acquired at specific points A and B within the sample microstructure.
summary: Localized Raman spectra at points A and B reveal distinct phase characteristics. The data shows that monoclinic phase peaks are significantly more pronounced near the pore surface, supporting the observation of localized phase distribution and providing evidence for the structural variations occurring in the vicinity of the voids.

caption: Radar comparison model illustrating the performance metrics of various regression models evaluated in the study.
summary: This radar chart provides a comparative visualization of the performance metrics for multiple regression models. By mapping various evaluation criteria, the plot highlights significant differences in predictive capabilities across the models. These insights, alongside learning curves, facilitate a comprehensive assessment of the model development process and overall regression performance.

caption: Parity plot comparing ANN-predicted porosity against experimental porosity values using only the original dataset.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the performance of the ANN model in predicting part density using the original experimental dataset. Observations for both training and testing data are closely distributed around the perfect match line, indicating that the predicted porosities are generally very close to the actual experimental values.

caption: Steady-state cyclic voltammograms comparing Cu(111) and Cu98.5Ni1.5 electrodes in 0.1 M H2SO4 at a 50 mV/s scan rate, with an inset highlighting morphological differences in the potential range of -0.5 to 0 V.
summary: This figure displays steady-state cyclic voltammograms for Cu(111) and Cu98.5Ni1.5 electrodes in 0.1 M H2SO4. The red and blue lines reveal notable electrochemical differences between the materials. An inset provides an enlarged view of the positive-going potential scans from -0.5 to 0 V, highlighting specific morphological variations in the current profiles.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the FeCrAl IR sample, accompanied by a selected area electron diffraction pattern.
summary: This panel presents a HAADF-STEM image of the FeCrAl IR sample alongside its corresponding SAED pattern. The microscopy analysis provides structural insight into the material, while the diffraction data serves to characterize the crystalline nature of the oxide layers formed on the FeCrAl alloy surface.

caption: Computational model of the σ phase featuring secondary layers fully occupied by Mo atoms at the 8j positions.
summary: This computational model represents the σ phase structure where all 8j positions within the secondary layers are occupied by Mo atoms. This configuration serves as the baseline Mo-secondary layer model for first-principles calculations to investigate the inducing factors of occupancy changes and stacking disordering defects in the σ phase.

caption: Traditional reactor configuration mirroring the experimental setup used for chemical reaction validation.
summary: Representing the second geometrical domain, this schematic depicts a traditional reactor configuration that mirrors the experimental setup. It is specifically utilized for validating chemical reactions within the model. This domain provides the necessary framework to simulate and verify the chemical processes under conditions comparable to actual experimental reactor performance.

caption: Equivalent thickness of the VGE as a function of applied voltage, demonstrating a range of 200–490 μm corresponding to voltages between 250 and 400 V in PEP mode.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between applied voltage and the equivalent thickness of the VGE in PEP mode. Experimental data indicates that increasing the voltage from 250 V to 400 V results in a corresponding increase in the equivalent VGE thickness, which spans from 200 μm to 490 μm.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the population fractions of annealing, recrystallization, and deformation twin boundaries, highlighting a significant increase in Σ3 twin types following heat treatment.
summary: This bar chart displays the population fractions of various twin boundaries, specifically annealing, recrystallization, and deformation types. Analysis reveals that the population of Σ3 twins, including Type 1 and Type 3, increases drastically after heat treatment, while Σ9 twins exhibit a slight increase, demonstrating the microstructural evolution induced by the thermal processing.

caption: Isothermal oxidation diagram for the Co-Al-Cr ternary alloy system at 900 °C, constructed by integrating literature data from Co-Al and Co-Cr binary systems with experimental results from various Co-Al-Cr alloys.
summary: This isothermal oxidation diagram for the Co-Al-Cr ternary system at 900 °C provides a comprehensive overview of oxidation behavior. By synthesizing literature data from Co-Al and Co-Cr binary systems with new experimental findings from this study, the diagram maps the oxidation characteristics across the ternary composition space effectively.

caption: Printability map of bulk Fe2VAl0.9Si0.1 samples fabricated at a constant hatch spacing of 50 μm, illustrating the relationship between process parameters and sample quality.
summary: This printability map summarizes the general quality of Fe2VAl0.9Si0.1 samples produced via additive manufacturing at a constant hatch spacing of 50 μm. It serves as a process guide to identify optimal printing conditions and delineate boundaries where defects such as overheating or lack-of-fusion occur during sample fabrication.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for LTT-2 alloy powder, showing a primary size range of 50 μm to 150 μm.
summary: This histogram displays the specific particle size distribution for LTT-2 alloy powder. The analysis shows that the majority of the particles fall within the 50 μm to 150 μm size range, which is consistent with the requirements for the LMD repairing process.

caption: Normalized XAFS spectra at the Mn K-edge for the PEG-3–1500 specimen compared against SrMnO3, MnO2, and Mn2O3 reference materials, including LCF fitting curves.
summary: Normalized XAFS spectra at the Mn K-edge are displayed for the PEG-3–1500 specimen alongside reference materials SrMnO3, MnO2, and Mn2O3. Linear combination fitting (LCF) results are integrated into the plot to characterize the oxidation state of manganese cations within the specimen, providing a comprehensive analysis of the entire spectrum.

caption: Spin-wave dispersion spectra for the squeezed permalloy-in-cobalt structure at a squeeze ratio of s = 0.6, illustrating the shift in the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths.
summary: Representing the compressed state of the permalloy-in-cobalt structure, this panel illustrates the spin-wave dispersion spectra at a squeeze ratio of s = 0.6. The plot tracks the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths, demonstrating how structural compression modifies the magnetic excitation spectrum compared to the base configuration.

caption: Three-dimensional wear surface morphology of the GNPs/IN718 composite tested at a sliding velocity of 300 rpm and a 6 N load.
summary: This panel illustrates the 3D wear surface morphology of the GNPs/IN718 composite under a 6 N load at 300 rpm. The morphology serves as an intermediate state between the high-wear condition at 250 rpm and the smoother, heat-affected surface observed at the higher sliding velocity of 350 rpm.

caption: Deconvoluted micro-photoluminescence emission spectrum of 10 mol% YSZ octet-truss lattices subjected to a 1-hour annealing process at 1050 °C.
summary: Shown is the deconvoluted micro-photoluminescence emission spectrum for 10 mol% YSZ octet-truss lattices annealed at 1050 °C for 1 hour. The results demonstrate that no carbon-related point defect emissions are detectable, reinforcing the finding that these specific spectral emissions are not influenced by the variations in the annealing temperature of the YSZ lattices.

caption: Comparison of experimental and simulated back face sheet residual deflection curves for the solid plate specimen.
summary: Experimental and simulated back face sheet residual deflection curves for the solid plate are compared in this panel. The consistency between the experimental and simulated data validates the numerical approach for the solid plate, providing a baseline for evaluating the performance of the honeycomb sandwich structures.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis graph of solution-treated Inconel X-750 superalloy, highlighting the temperature-dependent dissolution behavior of the γ′ phase.
summary: The thermogravimetric analysis of homogenized Inconel X-750 reveals a significant extremum at 998 °C, marking the onset of γ′ phase dissolution. This thermal data establishes the super-solvus criteria for the alloy, indicating that deformation processes conducted at 1000 °C occur above the dissolution limit of the γ′ precipitates.

caption: Contour projection of the neutron shielding rate data, highlighting the sensitivity of shielding efficiency to variations in Gd content and sample thickness.
summary: Representing a contour projection of the three-dimensional shielding data, this plot visualizes the shielding rate trends across varying Gd contents and thicknesses. The visualization confirms that high neutron shielding rates are attained even at low Gd content, reflecting the significant thermal neutron absorption cross-section inherent to the Gd/316L material system.

caption: Illustration of the MIG additive manufacturing system utilized for the synthesis of Ti–6Al–4V alloy thin-walled components.
summary: This schematic depicts the MIG additive manufacturing system employed to synthesize thin-walled Ti–6Al–4V alloy components. The setup illustrates the primary manufacturing process used to create the initial alloy structures before any subsequent surface treatment, providing a clear overview of the fabrication method for the experimental specimens.

caption: Reflection coefficient (S11) plot for the spherical folded FESA, comparing the wire-only configuration against the wire-with-dielectric-support structure.
summary: This plot displays the reflection coefficient (S11) for a spherical folded FESA, illustrating the impact of a dielectric support structure. A resonant frequency shift of 1.76%, moving from 759 MHz to 745.6 MHz, is observed when comparing the wire-only design to the structure incorporating the dielectric support.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph revealing a low density of dislocation lines in the as-deposited OL-DED Inconel 718.
summary: Microstructural analysis via bright-field TEM reveals a low density of dislocation lines within the as-deposited OL-DED Inconel 718 alloy. This observation characterizes the defect state of the material, indicating that the as-deposited condition maintains a relatively low concentration of dislocations within the alloy's crystalline structure.

caption: Comparison of tensile properties for the current EHEA (star symbols) against literature data for various high-strength HEAs and EHEAs, showing the balance of strength and ductility.
summary: Tensile properties of the current EHEA are compared with literature results for various high-strength HEAs and EHEAs. The plot reveals that the HPT process successfully realizes a high-strength EHEA while retaining significant ductility, as evidenced by the star symbols representing the current work in relation to previously reported materials.

caption: Grayscale and false-colour height maps of the first contour theme specimen, highlighting the global stress region in brown and the local fracture region in purple.
summary: This panel displays grayscale and false-colour height maps for the first contour theme specimen. Global stress regions are marked in brown, while local fracture regions are indicated in purple. These XCT-based maps, processed with tilt correction and filters, facilitate the measurement of surface features like valleys in the material.

caption: Capacitance variation as a function of frequency for the LPBF-718 alloy, highlighting the transition in capacitive response.
summary: Capacitance variation as a function of frequency for the LPBF-718 alloy, highlighting the transition in capacitive response. Analysis of these findings suggests that a frequency of 1 kHz is optimal for isolating space charge capacitance from double layer capacitance, facilitating further Mott-Schottky analysis of the alloy's semiconducting behaviour.

caption: CAD model illustrating the arrangement of spheres within a face-centered cubic (fcc) compact structure.
summary: This CAD model depicts the geometric arrangement of spheres in a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell. As a fundamental compact structure, the fcc configuration serves as a theoretical baseline for evaluating solid volume fractions, where a maximum packing density of 0.74 is achieved when the inter-particle distance is zero.

caption: Superimposed 2D 1H–13C HRMAS NMR HSQC (blue) and HMBC (red) spectra focusing on the hydroxyalkyl region of CHES.
summary: This 2D NMR analysis displays the hydroxyalkyl region of CHES through superimposed HSQC and HMBC spectra. These techniques confirm carbohydrate linkages via proton-carbon correlations, specifically identifying signals between 3–4.3 ppm 1H and 50–85 ppm 13C, including anomeric carbons in the 90–95 ppm range, despite limited aromatic signal detection.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation of the water-to-solid ratio W/S(t) over a representative printing session, highlighting a manual increase in water inflow after two hours.
summary: This Monte Carlo simulation tracks the water-to-solid ratio during a printing session, specifically capturing the manual adjustment of water inflow at the two-hour mark. The plot displays average values per period alongside confidence intervals (σm and 2σm), illustrating the stability and variability of the mixture throughout the printing process.

caption: Isothermal section of the Cu–Ni–S system at 1200 °C, showing the equilibrium phase boundaries determined experimentally and modeled using the FactPS and FTsulf databases.
summary: Representing the Cu–Ni–S system at 1200 °C, this diagram plots experimental equilibrium phases against thermodynamic predictions. The consistency of tie-lines between the two experimental preparation methods validates the model. These results demonstrate that the calculated phase boundaries accurately reflect the experimental findings at this elevated temperature.

caption: Diamond triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) unit cell architecture.
summary: This panel illustrates the unit cell geometry of a Diamond triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structure. Similar to the Gyroid, this Diamond architecture serves as a structural unit for creating materials with tunable relative densities, which are determined by the specific value of the level-set constant c.

caption: Additional Bode plot representation showing the electrochemical response of specimens under varying elemental sulfur conditions, complementing the impedance data analysis.
summary: This Bode plot serves as a secondary representation of the electrochemical impedance data for specimens in sulfur-rich corrosive environments. By analyzing these plots in conjunction with the Nyquist data, the study quantitatively assesses how varying sulfur levels affect the protective nature of the product film formed on the metal matrix.

caption: Fatigue crack growth (FCG) test results comparing the L1-A specimen, which incorporates sintered powder, against plain specimens, demonstrating a life cycle of 81.3 k cycles.
summary: This plot displays the fatigue crack growth performance of the L1-A specimen, featuring sintered powder, relative to plain specimens. The results indicate that the sintered powder design does not significantly accelerate or retard crack growth, yielding a fatigue life of 81.3 k cycles, which is comparable to the average 83.2 k cycles observed in plain specimens.

caption: Anisotropy indices of compressive strength for printed EPS concrete samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the anisotropy indices of compression characteristics across all printed EPS concrete samples. It provides a quantitative assessment of the anisotropic coefficient in compressive strength, highlighting the directional dependence of mechanical performance inherent in the printed material structure as determined through experimental testing of the concrete specimens.

caption: Rate capability profiles of the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 electrode, showing capacity response across varying current densities of 1, 2, 4, and 8 mA cm-2.
summary: Rate capability profiles for the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 electrode illustrate its performance under increasing current densities from 1 to 8 mA cm-2. This assessment evaluates the electrode's ability to maintain capacity at higher discharge rates, providing critical data on its power density and kinetic limitations for lithium storage applications.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves of VPP polymeric resin prints measured from 40 to 600°C at a heating rate of 10°C/min in air (grey) and nitrogen (orange) atmospheres.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrate the thermal degradation behavior of VPP polymeric resin prints. Experiments conducted at a heating rate of 10°C/min between 40 and 600°C reveal distinct mass loss profiles when the samples are exposed to air versus nitrogen atmospheres, highlighting the influence of gas environment on polymer decomposition.

caption: Detection performance of the Exposure network under injected plus-minus fault conditions in network parameters.
summary: The Exposure network exhibits reduced detection accuracy when subjected to injected plus-minus faults in its network parameters. Specifically, Sample No. 6 demonstrates an increased number of missed failures compared to the unaffected condition, with only 8 of 10 failures successfully detected, highlighting the network's vulnerability to parameter-level faults.

caption: Confocal laser scanning microscopy images of L929 fibroblasts cultured on various scaffolds at day 1 and day 3, stained with Calcein AM for live cells (green) and propidium iodide for dead cells (red).
summary: Live/dead cell staining reveals that L929 fibroblasts exhibit excellent biocompatibility on all piezoelectric scaffolds. Cells appear predominantly green, indicating high viability, and demonstrate tight adhesion to the scaffold surfaces at both day 1 and day 3. These results confirm the scaffolds support healthy cell growth and attachment.

caption: Evolution of the β-Ti phase lattice parameter in the alloy powders as a function of increasing milling time.
summary: This line graph illustrates the variation of the β-Ti phase lattice parameter within the alloy powders as milling time progresses. The plot tracks the structural changes occurring in the crystalline lattice of the β-Ti phase, providing quantitative insight into the phase stability and evolution during the mechanical milling process.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map corresponding to the OIM image in (b), illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution along the X direction.
summary: This inverse pole figure (IPF) map, derived from the OIM data in panel (b), characterizes the crystallographic orientation distribution along the X direction. It complements the grain structure analysis by providing a quantitative representation of the texture within the transverse plane of the annealed ingot prior to hot deformation.

caption: 3D profilometry image of the upskin surface at a 60° orientation.
summary: This 3D profilometry image illustrates the upskin surface morphology at a 60° angle. By providing a high-resolution view of the surface, this image supports the extraction of roughness data, which is critical for understanding the influence of build orientation on the final surface finish of upskin regions.

caption: Principal component analysis scatter plot comparing PC1 and PC2 for designed KG-SFA alloys against reference Ni-based self-fluxing alloys.
summary: This scatter plot visualizes the compositional relationships between designed KG-SFA alloys and reference Ni-based self-fluxing alloys using the first two principal components. PC1 and PC2 account for 53.2% and 19.7% of the total variance, respectively, providing a 2D projection of the multi-dimensional compositional space for these alloy systems.

caption: Ternary plot representing the storage modulus G’ of the cured monomer mixtures as a function of the IBOA, HDDA, and ETMPTA monomer shares.
summary: This ternary plot depicts the storage modulus G’ of the material after the curing process. By mapping the mechanical response across the composition space of IBOA, HDDA, and ETMPTA, the figure demonstrates how the specific monomer mixture influences the final stiffness and elastic properties of the cured polymer network.

caption: Initial Nyquist plot showing impedance arcs for LPBF 316L SS planes and R 316L, following the hierarchical order XOZ > XOY > R 316L > YOZ.
summary: This initial electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement displays the impedance arcs for various LPBF 316L stainless steel planes compared to the rolled counterpart. The results establish a clear hierarchical order of impedance magnitude, with the XOZ plane exhibiting the highest impedance and the YOZ plane the lowest among the tested samples.

caption: Middle cross-section of non-impacted BPR 93° specimen acquired via µ-CT-scan.
summary: The µ-CT-scan of the BPR 93° specimen reveals a clear geometrical pattern within the inner cross-section. This distinct arrangement is defined by the specific stacking sequence of the material, providing a well-ordered internal architecture that is clearly visible in the cross-sectional view of the non-impacted sample.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the sub-grains observed in (e), indicating a small misorientation.
summary: The SAED pattern obtained from the sub-grains in the CR40-DA specimen indicates a small misorientation of approximately 2°. This diffraction evidence confirms the sub-grain nature of the observed features, which are formed through the interaction of deformation twins and high-density defects during the high-temperature fracture process at 760 °C.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the impedance characteristics of SiC/NFG/Ni composites under temperature variations.
summary: This Nyquist plot reveals the impedance matching characteristics of SiC/NFG/Ni composites. The presence of multiple semicircles indicates the coexistence of various relaxation processes within the material. Poor impedance matching is identified as a limiting factor for the absorption improvements observed under different temperature conditions during the experimental testing.

caption: Voltage and Faradaic efficiency versus time for a Co-infiltrated cathode SOEC tested galvanostatically at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻².
summary: This panel displays the galvanostatic testing results for a Co-infiltrated cathode SOEC at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻². It specifically tracks the evolution of cell voltage and Faradaic efficiency over the testing duration, providing a baseline for comparing the performance of different infiltrated cathode materials under identical operating conditions.

caption: Raman spectrum of dual-layer Ti–Cu coated diamond powder following SLM processing, showing a sharp, isolated diamond peak at 1331 cm⁻¹ with minimal graphitic signals.
summary: Post-SLM processing Raman analysis of dual-layer Ti–Cu coated diamond powder demonstrates a sharp, isolated diamond peak at 1331 cm⁻¹. The absence of significant graphitic signals confirms that the optimized coating and processing strategies successfully suppressed thermal-induced graphitization, maintaining the structural integrity of the diamond particles during the manufacturing process.

caption: Calcein-AM/PI staining images showing cell viability within 10%, 15%, and 20% GelMA hydrogel concentrations.
summary: Calcein-AM/PI staining was utilized to assess the influence of varying GelMA concentrations on cell viability. The results of these live/dead cell experiments indicated that different concentrations of GelMA did not cause significant damage to the cells, demonstrating the biocompatibility of the hydrogel scaffolds across the tested range.

caption: Bode modulus plot displaying the impedance magnitude as a function of frequency for the bare SUS420 substrate, A02 film, and A04 film.
summary: The Bode modulus plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance performance of the bare SUS420 substrate compared to the A02 and A04 films. Characterized across a low frequency range, these plots provide essential data on the impedance magnitude, highlighting the distinct electrochemical behaviors of the substrate and the applied film coatings.

caption: UMAP embedding of 32,550 integrated cells across endoderm, pancreatic progenitor, and β-like stages, with colors denoting 21 distinct clusters.
summary: This UMAP embedding visualizes 32,550 integrated cells categorized into 21 distinct clusters. The analysis captures the differentiation trajectory from endoderm to pancreatic progenitor and β-like cells. By downscaling the sequencing data, the plot effectively organizes the complex cellular states into identifiable groups based on their transcriptomic profiles.

caption: Coarse-grained model representation of the graphene lattice where each individual bead corresponds to a cluster of four carbon atoms, maintaining the characteristic hexagonal symmetry of the atomic structure.
summary: The coarse-grained model of graphene is illustrated here, where each bead represents four carbon atoms while preserving the hexagonal structure. This mapping strategy involved adjusting the C-C bond length to facilitate the transition from atomistic to coarse-grained scales, as detailed in the supplementary material.

caption: Stacking ensemble model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: Stacking ensemble model performance is visualized through a confusion matrix. By utilizing the same consistent dataset applied across all models, this matrix illustrates the classification outcomes, highlighting the effectiveness of the stacking approach in correctly categorizing the data points compared to individual model architectures.

caption: HAADF-STEM visualization of Alloy C along the [110] Al projection, highlighting the uniform arrangement of small precipitates within the sample.
summary: Alloy C displays a dense, homogeneous distribution of relatively small precipitates, consistent with the observations for the other alloys. The HAADF-STEM image, taken along the [110] Al projection, confirms that the precipitate dispersion is uniform, with the sample thickness being comparable to that of the other inspected alloys.

caption: Strain nephogram of a horizontally printed sample during the first loading cycle under IP conditions.
summary: This panel presents the strain distribution nephogram for a horizontally printed sample during the initial loading cycle under IP conditions. It provides a visual representation of the material's strain response at the start of the test, establishing the reference state for evaluating subsequent strain evolution under cyclic loading.

caption: Zone of interest selected for the digital image correlation analysis of the part.
summary: This panel displays the specific zone of interest defined for the digital image correlation (DIC) analysis. By utilizing the pydic open-source tool, this region is monitored to track transient part deformation during heating and cooling cycles, providing a focused area for subsequent displacement field calculations and qualitative deformation assessment.

caption: Overview of the dual-laser additive-subtractive manufacturing system principle.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental principle of the dual-laser additive-subtractive manufacturing system. It provides a high-level schematic overview of the integrated setup, serving as the primary conceptual framework for understanding how the continuous and ultrafast laser processes are combined within the manufacturing architecture described in the study.

caption: Tafel polarization curves evaluating the corrosion behavior of the Zn anode in different electrolytes.
summary: Tafel polarization curves are utilized to assess the influence of the SL additive on Zn anode corrosion. By analyzing the polarization behavior, the study evaluates how the additive modifies the electrochemical stability and corrosion resistance of the zinc metal anode surface compared to the blank electrolyte.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images showing live (green) and dead (red) MC3T3-E1 cells on SLM porous Ta scaffolds of varying porosities after 7, 14, and 21 days of culture.
summary: Live/dead viability assessment reveals progressive colonization of the scaffolds by viable cells, indicated by green fluorescence, with negligible dead cells shown in red. The images demonstrate that MC3T3-E1 cells successfully colonize the SLM porous Ta surfaces across all porosity levels (65% to 90%) throughout the 21-day culture period.

caption: Orientation map of the matrix at the grip zone projected along the transverse direction (TD).
summary: Represented here is the EBSD orientation map of the matrix at the grip zone, oriented along the transverse direction. This map allows for the evaluation of the material's crystallographic texture and grain alignment in the transverse plane, complementing the rolling direction data to provide a comprehensive orientation analysis.

caption: Photograph of the as-printed SMP-hydrogel stent in its initial, expanded state.
summary: This photograph displays the as-printed SMP-hydrogel stent in its initial, expanded configuration. It serves as a baseline for the device's geometry before it undergoes the programming process to reach its compacted form, illustrating the precision of the 3D printing fabrication method used to create the scaffold.

caption: Density distribution images of accelerated droplets approaching hydrophilic smooth and microstructure surfaces.
summary: Density distribution images illustrate the state of accelerated droplets as they approach hydrophilic smooth and microstructure surfaces. These simulations reveal how the droplet's interaction with the wall influences the fluid layer density, providing insight into the physical mechanisms occurring during the initial stages of impact on different surface geometries.

caption: Resistivity variation as a function of magnetization rotation angle, comparing hard and easy axes measurements obtained via the extended van der Pauw method.
summary: This plot illustrates the anisotropic resistivity behavior of a square-shaped sample measured using an extended van der Pauw method. By rotating the saturated magnetization, the data reveals distinct resistivity profiles along the hard and easy axes, with solid and dashed lines representing the respective average values for each orientation.

caption: Temperature-dependent vacancy diffusion constants (DVa) derived from KMC simulations, illustrating the influence of Re content on diffusion kinetics.
summary: This panel displays vacancy diffusion constants (DVa) calculated via KMC simulations across various temperatures. The data demonstrates that DVa values exhibit a consistent downward trend as the Re content increases within the material, highlighting the significant role of rhenium concentration in modulating vacancy diffusion behavior at different thermal conditions.

caption: Specific modulus values of 3D printed parts compared across different geometric configurations.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the specific modulus of 3D printed parts categorized by their geometric shape. Analysis of the specific modulus highlights minor discrepancies in the relative order of elastic properties between the different geometries, providing a comparative view of the material performance across the various tested part designs.

caption: EDS line scan profile across a grain interior of the 316 L steel, demonstrating a Cr-depleted zone approximately 5.3 µm thick within the exposed grain matrix.
summary: EDS line scan analysis across the grain interior of the 316 L steel substrate reveals a localized Cr-depleted zone extending approximately 5.3 µm into the matrix. This depletion profile provides quantitative evidence of the microstructural changes occurring within the grain matrix as a result of the corrosion process.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental fatigue life values against estimates derived from the Feret-diameter method.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the correlation between experimental fatigue life and values estimated using the Feret-diameter method. The visualization excludes infinite life data points, such as those from Test 2 and Test 5, as the predictive model also yields infinite values for these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength variation plotted against energy density for SLM-fabricated 13Ni-400 maraging steel samples, highlighting the influence of processing energy on material strength.
summary: The plot illustrates the relationship between ultimate tensile strength and energy density for SLM-built 13Ni-400 maraging steel. By mapping strength as a function of varying energy density, the graph demonstrates how specific laser processing parameters directly influence the mechanical properties of the final steel components, serving as a key indicator for process optimization.

caption: Three-dimensional distribution of pores specifically located within the SS phase.
summary: This panel highlights the 3D distribution of pores within the stainless steel phase of the composite. The visualization provides insight into the pore morphology and spatial density within the stainless steel component, facilitating a comparative analysis of porosity distribution between the different phases of the composite.

caption: High-magnification EPMA-WDS elemental mapping of the as-cast TiZrHfCr0.2Mo bio-HEA.
summary: High-magnification EPMA-WDS elemental mapping of the as-cast TiZrHfCr0.2Mo bio-HEA provides a detailed view of the local elemental distribution. Consistent with the low-magnification results, this high-resolution map confirms that chromium enrichment is localized in the inter-dendrite regions, highlighting the microstructural heterogeneity characteristic of this bio-HEA composition.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern acquired from the region labeled 'C' in the bright-field TEM image.
summary: This selected area diffraction pattern was obtained from the specific region marked 'C' in the corresponding bright-field transmission electron microscopy image. It serves to characterize the crystallographic nature of the deformation-induced products observed within the B2 parent phase, facilitating the identification of the phase transformation products.

caption: Synchrotron in-situ X-ray image of the melt pool showing pore distribution at 350 W and 500 mm/min.
summary: This synchrotron in-situ X-ray image illustrates the pore distribution in the melt pool at 350 W and 500 mm/min. At this lower scanning speed, the number of residual bubbles increases dramatically compared to higher speeds, with bubbles concentrated at the front wall and bottom of the melt track.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of L-PBF NiTi processed at 56 J/mm3 (A2) after 30 minutes of immersion in 0.9 wt.% NaCl solution, showing five distinct anodic current peaks across a wide potential range.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry curve for the A2 sample, processed at 56 J/mm3, displays five anodic current peaks within a wide potential range of -1.5 V to 2.0 V SCE. These peaks correspond to specific electrochemical transitions, including the oxidation of Ti to Ti2+, Ti2+ to Ti3+, and Ti3+ to Ti4+.

caption: Gyroid lattice unit cell structure rendered in orange.
summary: The gyroid lattice unit cell is depicted in orange, representing the third architecture evaluated in this work. This lesser-studied structure is compared alongside the Kelvin cell and BCC lattices to assess its specific thermohydraulic performance characteristics within the framework of the POCS structure investigation.

caption: Conceptual architecture illustrating the integration of an optimization framework within a closed-loop decision support workflow.
summary: This schematic presents a conceptual architecture designed to operationalize a decision support workflow. It demonstrates how an optimization framework is embedded into a closed-loop system, facilitating systematic decision-making processes. The diagram serves as a foundational model for integrating computational optimization techniques into practical material science research and development workflows.

caption: Power-Voltage (P-V) characteristics of the KC 200GT PV module measured at an insolation of 1000 W/m2 across a temperature range of 25 °C to 80 °C.
summary: The P-V performance curves illustrate the sensitivity of the KC 200GT PV module to thermal variations. As temperatures increase from 25 °C to 80 °C under a constant insolation of 1000 W/m2, the module exhibits distinct shifts in power output, demonstrating the significant influence of operating temperature on photovoltaic efficiency.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from nano-indentation testing on the 90° sample.
summary: This panel illustrates the load-displacement behavior of the 90° sample. Similar to the 0° sample, the data reveals a significant strain hardening effect beneath the cut surface. This hardening is linked to the accumulation of dislocation density and the resulting interactions within the material's strain field.

caption: Spectral normal emissivity of Inconel 617 measured at 300 °C, comparing the unexposed reference state with samples exposed to 1000 °C helium gas under oxidizing and carburizing environments for 500 hours.
summary: Spectral normal emissivity measurements for Inconel 617 reveal a moderate increase in emissivity following 500-hour exposure to 1000 °C helium gas. The data compares unexposed samples with those subjected to oxidizing and carburizing environments, demonstrating how these specific high-temperature gas chemistries influence the surface radiative properties of the alloy.

caption: Galvanostatic charge/discharge behavior of the 3D LFP-GO electrode across a range of C-rates.
summary: Depicted here are the galvanostatic charge/discharge profiles for the 3D LFP-GO electrode. Evaluated in a full cell configuration using LTO and LP30, the voltage versus specific capacity curves at C-rates from C/25 to C/4 highlight the electrochemical performance and rate capability characteristics of this specific 3D electrode material.

caption: TEM image of a grain boundary in the D060 sample.
summary: This TEM image displays the morphology of a grain boundary within the D060 sample. The observation of such boundaries is essential for understanding the microstructural characteristics and the potential influence of grain interfaces on the overall deformation behavior and defect accumulation within the material's shear region.

caption: Average load–displacement curve for polycrystalline aggregates under adiabatic heating conditions with A = 0.004 N.
summary: Average load–displacement curves for polycrystalline aggregates at A = 0.004 N reveal that the fine-grained aggregate maintains a lower average resulting load compared to the coarse-grained aggregate. This comparison illustrates the distinct mechanical performance trends between different grain size distributions under the specified adiabatic heating conditions.

caption: Quantitative EDS point analysis results showing the chemical composition in mol% for the coarsened intermetallic phases, identifying them as θ-Al13Fe4 based on the measured 22.8 mol% Fe content.
summary: Quantitative EDS point analysis of the coarsened granular intermetallic phases in the annealed Al–2.5%Fe–2%Cu alloy provides precise compositional data. The measured value of approximately 22.8 mol% Fe confirms that these coarsened phases are θ-Al13Fe4, which are characterized by elevated hardness in the processed material.

caption: Fourier transformed EXAFS spectra at the Ni K-edge for Ni2Fe1 before and after the OER stability test.
summary: Fourier transformed EXAFS spectra at the Ni K-edge reveal the local coordination environment of Ni2Fe1. Comparison before and after the OER stability test shows increased amplitudes for Ni-O and Ni-Ni signals, indicating higher coordination numbers and a more ordered metal-oxygen and metal-metal structure following the electrochemical testing process.

caption: Stress–strain diagram for the bcc1 specimen, highlighting critical mechanical transition points including yield, the onset of the plateau region, and the densification strain.
summary: The stress–strain diagram for the bcc1 specimen illustrates the mechanical response under loading. Key transition points, specifically the yield stress, the beginning of the plateau region, and the densification strain, are identified to characterize the material's deformation behavior, consistent with established trends for this type of structural investigation.

caption: Representative SEM-EBSD inverse pole figure for Alloy 625, highlighting grains oriented near the [101] direction in green, which were selected for indentation analysis.
summary: This SEM-EBSD inverse pole figure displays the crystallographic orientation of Alloy 625 grains. Grains oriented near the [101] direction, represented in green, were specifically targeted for indentation testing. The data was processed with a neighboring confidence index of 0.05 and a grain tolerance angle of approximately 3 degrees.

caption: As-printed LPBF region exhibiting a fine microstructure with characteristic small melt pools.
summary: This optical micrograph captures the as-printed LPBF region, which is defined by a fine microstructure. The image reveals the presence of smaller melt pools typical of the LPBF process. This fine-grained structure contrasts with the coarser features observed in the LMD region, demonstrating the influence of the specific manufacturing technique.

caption: STEM ADF micrograph of the bcc A2 phase in the 1000HT sample compressed at 600 °C, displaying the characteristic dislocation network structure.
summary: This STEM ADF micrograph focuses on the bcc A2 phase of the 1000HT sample after 32% compression at 600 °C. The image provides clear evidence of the dislocation network structure developed within the disordered bcc phase during the high-temperature plastic deformation process.

caption: Cross-sectional microstructure of the thin-walled cylindrical part at the +Y (90°) orientation.
summary: Representing the +Y (90°) condition, this optical micrograph illustrates the cross-sectional microstructure of the thin-walled cylindrical part. The visualization highlights the specific microstructural features resulting from this orientation, contributing to the comparative analysis of the three different processing conditions investigated for the thin-walled cylindrical components in this study.

caption: Principal component analysis correlation matrix illustrating the relationships between various laser cladding process parameters and the resulting clad characteristics.
summary: This correlation matrix, generated via principal component analysis, quantifies the interdependencies between laser cladding process parameters and the resulting material characteristics. By applying PCA to the optimization results, the figure provides a statistical overview of how specific input variables influence the final clad properties during the manufacturing process.

caption: Temperature dependence of Cr self-diffusion coefficients in Ni-xCr alloys, comparing simulation results for Ni-5Cr, Ni-10Cr, and Ni-20Cr against experimental data from Joensson and Moulin et al. for Ni-22Cr.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays Cr self-diffusion coefficients in Ni-xCr alloys across varying temperatures. Simulation results for Ni-5Cr, Ni-10Cr, and Ni-20Cr are compared with experimental literature values for Ni-22Cr. The predicted magnitudes are consistent with high-temperature experimental diffusion coefficients for alloys ranging from 7 to 38 at. % Cr.

caption: Photo-DSC thermogram illustrating the polymerization kinetics of ELO-based epoxy formulations containing varying concentrations of H200 filler.
summary: This photo-DSC thermogram displays the polymerization behavior of ELO-based epoxy formulations with different H200 filler loadings. The analysis evaluates how varying the amount of H200 influences the thermal response during the curing process, providing insights into the reaction kinetics and the impact of filler concentration on the material's thermal properties.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF)-EBSD map of an aluminum alloy plane containing the building direction, showing indexed grains and unindexed regions.
summary: This IPF-EBSD map displays the microstructure of an aluminum alloy along the building direction with a 200 nm step size. Approximately 60% of the surface is indexed, revealing micron-sized columnar and coarse equiaxed grains. Unindexed black regions, often found at melt pool boundaries and centers, are attributed to convection flows.

caption: Solid-state specific heat capacity of encapsulated GF_PW composites determined via TGHPT.
summary: Solid-state specific heat capacity values for encapsulated GF_PW composites are presented, derived from TGHPT measurements. The data points represent cumulative heat enthalpy plotted against temperature, with the specific heat capacity calculated as the slope of a linear regression line exhibiting an R-squared value exceeding 0.997 for high accuracy.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of an ordered L12 precipitate in the FNAT alloy, showing the characteristic atomic arrangement of the ordered phase.
summary: Ordered L12 precipitates within the FNAT alloy are shown in this HAADF-STEM image. The Fourier transform diffractogram confirms the ordered structure and the [001] zone axis orientation. This visualization highlights the interface between the precipitate and the matrix, providing critical information on the alloy's microstructural features and phase distribution.

caption: Microstructure of the V7–150 specimen near the fracture surface after hot-isostatic pressing, highlighting the reduced presence of ductile dimples.
summary: The microstructure of the V7–150 specimen near the fracture surface, captured after hot-isostatic pressing, shows a reduced amount of ductile dimples. This observation is consistent with the comparative analysis of the V2, V5, and V7 variants, demonstrating the impact of HIP on the fracture surface morphology.

caption: High-resolution SEM micrograph of region D, highlighting nanoscale or sub-micron equiaxed grains near the molten pool boundaries.
summary: Region D, located near the boundaries of the molten pool, is characterized by the presence of nanoscale or sub-micron equiaxed grains. This fine-grained structure is attributed to the distinct cooling rates encountered at the periphery of the molten pool during the SLM-1000 solidification process.

caption: Lattice structures of the ferroelectric (FE) and paraelectric (PE) phases, demonstrating the transition between two equivalent structures with opposite polarizations via the PE state.
summary: The lattice structures of the ferroelectric (FE) and paraelectric (PE) phases are depicted. Two equivalent structures with opposite polarizations exist, which can convert to one another through a paraelectric phase, identified as state-II. This structural transition highlights the switchable nature of the polarization in these monolayer systems.

caption: Optical micrograph of the Ti–15Mo alloy after heat treatment at 765 °C for 10 minutes, displaying a heterogeneous grain structure.
summary: Following a 10-minute heat treatment at 765 °C, the Ti–15Mo alloy exhibits a mixture of coarse and fine grains. The average grain size increases to 13 μm under these conditions. This micrograph illustrates the progression of grain growth and structural evolution during short-time thermal processing at the β phase transformation temperature.

caption: Statistical summary of nanohardness and elastic modulus values derived from nanoindentation testing for PBF-LB 316L, as-printed Ni-free stainless steel, and heat-treated Ni-free stainless steel.
summary: This figure provides a comparative summary of mechanical properties for three distinct stainless steel conditions. It aggregates nanohardness and elastic modulus data obtained from nanoindentation testing. These results characterize the mechanical performance of PBF-LB 316L alongside as-printed and heat-treated Ni-free stainless steel variants, facilitating a direct assessment of their respective material strengths.

caption: Bar chart illustrating the ranking of feature importance based on mean absolute SHAP values for the outcome variable.
summary: This bar chart displays the ranking of feature importance derived from mean absolute SHAP values. It highlights that features such as Mo, Al, and W exhibit a limited influence on the outcome variable, as their SHAP values are clustered near zero, providing a clear visualization of predictive model feature contributions.

caption: 3D reconstructed micro-CT images showing internal vessel formation within different scaffolds at 2 and 4 weeks post-implantation.
summary: 3D micro-CT reconstructions visualize the internal vascular network development. By 4 weeks, the PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF group displays a substantial increase in mature, continuous blood vessels, whereas the PLA and PLA/GA groups exhibit primarily branch-like new vessels with limited maturity and continuity, demonstrating superior angiogenic potential.

caption: Visual representation of the HFM-100 heat flow meter apparatus employed for experimental thermal testing.
summary: The HFM-100 heat flow meter apparatus is shown here as the primary equipment employed for experimental thermal testing. This device allows for precise thermal conductivity measurements by maintaining a 10°C temperature difference between the hot and cold plates during the testing of various material samples.

caption: UV-visible near-infrared absorption spectrum of CUG lunar regolith simulant plotted against wavelength.
summary: This UV-visible near-infrared absorption spectrum characterizes the laser absorption properties of CUG lunar regolith simulant across a broad wavelength range. Tested using a Shimadzu SolidSpec-3700 spectrophotometer, the data provides essential insights into how varying titanium contents influence the material's thermal properties and laser absorption rates during processing.

caption: Nyquist plots of EIS spectra for uncoated and gold-coated Ti felt samples, including equivalent circuit models in the inset.
summary: EIS spectra presented as Nyquist plots analyze the corrosion resistance of the Ti felt samples. The inset displays the equivalent circuits used to fit the experimental data, providing a quantitative assessment of the electrochemical interface properties for both the uncoated Ti felt and the various gold-coated Ti felt samples.

caption: Time-dependent stress evolution during the 10th cycle at 750 °C, contrasting experimental observations against the viscoelastic–viscoplastic model predictions.
summary: Representing the time-dependent mechanical response, this plot shows the stress versus time behavior for the 10th cycle at 750 °C. By comparing experimental data with the calibrated viscoelastic–viscoplastic model, the panel illustrates the specific time-dependent phenomena occurring within the material during the cyclic testing process.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of RGO-SGFs reinforced PLA composites containing 7 wt% filler.
summary: This TGA curve illustrates the thermal degradation profile of PLA composites reinforced with 7 wt% RGO-SGFs. The analysis provides insight into how the incorporation of these specific nanofillers influences the thermal stability and weight loss characteristics of the PLA matrix compared to the pure polymer counterpart during heating.

caption: Spatial map of time above threshold for the triangular sample layer at 0° rotation, illustrating the qualitative agreement between experimental measurements and superposition predictions.
summary: The spatial map visualizes the time above threshold for a triangular sample layer at a 0° rotation angle. It provides a qualitative comparison between experimental data and superposition simulation predictions. The map demonstrates good spatial agreement, confirming the model's effectiveness in capturing thermal features across the scanned geometry.

caption: Spatial distribution map of the 004 Laue peak width along the short axis (βS) in laser shock peened Ni-based superalloy, with white curves indicating high-angle grain boundaries.
summary: This heatmap displays the spatial distribution of the 004 Laue peak width along the short axis (βS) across the scanned area of a laser shock peened Ni-based superalloy. High-angle grain boundaries, identified by white curves, delineate the microstructural features where peak broadening is measured to assess dislocation density.

caption: Shrinkage rate curves derived from dilatometric experiments for Alloys 2 and 3, highlighting the impact of milling rotation speeds.
summary: Shrinkage rate curves during the heating ramp reveal that specimens milled at 200 rpm exhibit rates approximately one order of magnitude higher than those milled at 100 rpm. This significant increase in shrinkage rate demonstrates the influence of high-energy milling on the thermal processing characteristics of the alloys.

caption: Engineering diagram showing the slot hole geometry and associated dimensions for the 7075-T6 aluminum alloy notched specimen.
summary: This engineering diagram outlines the slot hole geometry and dimensions for the 7075-T6 aluminum alloy specimen. By defining the precise structural features of the notched specimen, this panel facilitates accurate mechanical testing and analysis, ensuring that the experimental setup adheres to the specified dimensions required for the investigation.

caption: Nyquist plots of ATI718 Plus showing incomplete semi-circular arcs of varying diameters, with solid lines representing EEC model fitting results.
summary: The Nyquist plots for ATI718 Plus exhibit incomplete semi-circular arcs of varying diameters, which are indicative of highly capacitive behavior. Solid lines overlaid on the experimental data represent the fitting results obtained from the EEC model, confirming the electrochemical response of the material under the tested conditions.

caption: SHAP value distribution for the FCC+BCC dual-phase prediction, demonstrating the feature sensitivity for this specific phase combination.
summary: This SHAP plot depicts the influence of five features on the prediction of the FCC+BCC dual phase. Analysis reveals that only moderate feature values are favorable for the formation of this dual-phase structure. The horizontal axis represents the SHAP value, indicating the direction and magnitude of feature influence.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of a grain within the stable nano-lamellae region near the (Ti,Al)N/TiN interface in the coating annealed at 1000 °C, oriented along the [101] zone axis.
summary: Located near the (Ti,Al)N/TiN interface, this HAADF-STEM micrograph shows a grain within the stable nano-lamellae region after 1000 °C annealing. The grain is oriented along the [101] zone axis, demonstrating that the nano-lamellar structure remains stable in specific regions of the coating even at this high annealing temperature.

caption: Fluorescence lifetime decay curve and corresponding fitting for TPU/2S composite at 490 nm emission.
summary: Fluorescence lifetime decay and fitting curves for the TPU/2S composite are presented at an emission wavelength of 490 nm. Monitored at room temperature with an excitation wavelength of 373 nm, this sample exhibits an average lifespan within the 3–5 ns range, consistent with low SAOED addition levels.

caption: Overview of the fracture surface morphology for specimen HCF-M.
summary: This panel presents an overview of the fracture surface morphology for specimen HCF-M. The image provides a comprehensive view of the failure characteristics, serving as the primary context for the subsequent detailed magnifications of specific zones observed across the specimen's fractured surface during the analysis.

caption: Relative error distribution for the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) model on the test dataset.
summary: This panel presents the relative error analysis for the RSM model on the test set. These findings support the conclusion that the RSM approach provides a baseline for error evaluation, allowing for a comprehensive comparison of traditional statistical modeling against the advanced machine learning techniques analyzed in this figure.

caption: Voltage variation curve of a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film during the initial charge and discharge process.
summary: The voltage variation curve for the a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-film is displayed during the initial charge and discharge cycle. With an average impedance of 6.1 Ω, this alloyed material demonstrates performance characteristics intermediate between pure a-Si and a-Ge, indicating that germanium incorporation effectively modulates the electrochemical properties of the silicon matrix.

caption: Geometric configuration of the Gyroid unit cell featuring horizontal and inclined sheets oriented at ±45° relative to the horizontal plane.
summary: The Gyroid unit cell geometry is characterized by a specific arrangement of horizontal and inclined sheets. These structural components are oriented at angles of ±45° to the horizontal plane, defining the fundamental geometric shape and symmetry characteristics of the unit cell architecture within the material model.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Pd, Pd3Ni, and PdNi catalysts in 0.5 M methanol and 1 M NaOH solution at a scan rate of 25 mV s-1.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram illustrates the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) performance for Pd, Pd3Ni, and PdNi catalysts. Recorded in a 0.5 M methanol and 1 M NaOH electrolyte at a 25 mV s-1 scan rate, the plot provides a comparative electrochemical assessment of these materials for catalytic methanol oxidation applications.

caption: Surface morphology of Sample 2-3, displaying a prominent structural fracture at the center of the closure.
summary: Sample 2-3 displays a prominent structural fracture at the center of the closure region, consistent with the failure mode observed in other samples processed at similar energy levels. This morphological feature indicates that the laser energy input used for this sample leads to central fracture rather than simple deposit loss.

caption: Box-plot distribution of surface roughness parameters Ra, Rv, and Rz for GBB-UC and GBB-C conditions, showing a decreasing trend in roughness values.
summary: Surface roughness parameters for GBB-UC and GBB-C conditions are presented as a box-plot, indicating a decreasing trend in values including Rv. Despite this reduction in surface roughness, the reference notes that it does not positively impact fatigue life, which instead exhibits a drastic reduction from GBB-UC to GBB-C-24.

caption: Power versus temperature plot for alloy 52 specimen, showing the marked Curie temperature derived from the average of transition temperatures.
summary: The power versus temperature plot for the alloy 52 specimen is displayed here. The Curie temperature is determined by taking the average of two transition temperatures and marking it on the plot, characterizing the magnetic transition properties of this alloy composition within the graded wall structure.

caption: Al-rich portion of the calculated liquidus projection for the Al-Mg-Si system, highlighting the chemical compositions corresponding to the α-Al/Mg2Si two-phase eutectic reaction.
summary: This panel displays the Al-rich region of the liquidus projection for the Al-Mg-Si ternary system, calculated using Pandat software. The liquidus line delineates the boundary between the α-Al and Mg2Si phases, identifying the specific chemical compositions that undergo the α-Al/Mg2Si two-phase eutectic reaction, which is critical for PBF-LB alloy fabrication.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing reverted austenite in the 15Ni-AT sample.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the morphology of reverted austenite in the 15Ni-AT sample. This visualization is part of a broader characterization effort that demonstrates the presence of nanoscale reverted austenite, providing clear evidence of the microstructural features consistent with the 15Ni-AT sample's processing conditions.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of HPC and HPCA samples with varying degrees of substitution (DS) from 0.4 to 1.0, measured in D2O, showing characteristic vinyl proton signals at 5.5–6.5 ppm.
summary: The 1H NMR analysis confirms the successful synthesis of HPCA with varying degrees of substitution. Spectra obtained in D2O for samples with DS values ranging from 0.4 to 1.0 exhibit distinct chemical shifts between 5.5 and 6.5 ppm, which are attributed to the protons present in the -C=C- vinyl groups.

caption: Powder number density (pn) distributions plotted against distance (d) from the nozzle exit plane, comparing G73, G37, and G55 gas flow rate conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of powder number density (pn) as a function of distance from the nozzle exit (d=1 to 15 mm). It compares three distinct gas flow rate configurations: G73, G37, and G55, demonstrating how varying carrier and coaxial gas flow rates influence the spatial distribution of powder particles.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the parabolic oxidation rate constants (kp) for various Ni-base alloys exposed to steam environments across a range of pressures from 1 to 241 bar, incorporating literature data for alloys such as 600, 601, 718, 617, 230, 740, 263, 80A, and PMCr.
summary: This Arrhenius plot compiles parabolic oxidation rate constants for multiple Ni-base alloys in steam environments at pressures between 1 and 241 bar. The data, sourced from various literature studies, demonstrates oxidation behavior across different temperatures. Long-term industrial exposure data for alloys 625 and Waspalloy are included to provide a comprehensive overview of oxidation kinetics.

caption: Volta potential map of alloy M showing the distribution of surface potential across the grain boundaries.
summary: Volta potential map of alloy M showing the distribution of surface potential across the grain boundaries. This map, obtained via SKPFM, illustrates the spatial variation of the Volta potential on the etched surface of alloy M, facilitating a comparison of electrochemical properties between the matrix and the grain boundaries.

caption: Histogram representing the crack volume distribution within the specified region of interest at a compressive strain of 5.0%.
summary: This histogram displays the crack volume distribution for the auxetic lattice reinforced cementitious composites subjected to a compressive strain of 5.0%. The plot characterizes the evolution of crack sizes within the defined 17 mm x 17 mm x 17 mm region of interest as the mechanical loading increases.

caption: Elemental composition and content analysis of the polished specimen surface following PEP and V-PEP treatments.
summary: This table presents the elemental composition and content on the surface of a polished specimen after PEP and V-PEP treatments. Analysis indicates that no significant carbon or oxygen contamination was detected, while the concentrations of other major elements remained consistent with standard composition, showing only minor deviations from expected values.

caption: Pole figures of the {001}, {110}, and {111} planes for Ti–10V–2Fe–3Al alloy processed at a 45 mA electron beam current, showing pronounced anisotropy along the {001} plane.
summary: At a 45 mA electron beam current, the Ti–10V–2Fe–3Al alloy displays significant crystallographic anisotropy. The {001}, {110}, and {111} pole figures reveal a strong preferential orientation along the {001} plane, indicating that the β phase grains exhibit a distinct growth direction under these specific processing parameters.

caption: Raman spectrum of FeNi-CA exhibiting characteristic D and G bands at 1350 cm⁻¹ and 1590 cm⁻¹, respectively, indicating the presence of disordered and graphitic carbon phases.
summary: The Raman spectrum of FeNi-CA is shown in panel (c). The data reveals characteristic D and G bands located at 1350 cm⁻¹ and 1590 cm⁻¹, respectively. These bands correspond to the disordered and graphitic phases of carbon, confirming the structural nature of the carbonaceous component in the sample.

caption: Comparison of compressive strength, yield strength, and elastic modulus values for porous TC4-5Cu alloy samples, showing an increase in elastic modulus from 20.5 to 25.4 GPa as wall thickness increases.
summary: Compressive strength, yield strength, and elastic modulus values are plotted for the porous TC4-5Cu alloy.
