The data demonstrates that the elastic modulus increases from 20.5 to 25.4 GPa as the wall thickness of the porous samples increases, highlighting the influence of structural geometry on the alloy's mechanical stiffness.

caption: Mass loss measurements of 420 martensitic stainless steel hardfacing subjected to dry sand and rubber wheel abrasion testing, comparing as-deposited and tempered conditions.
summary: This panel displays the mass loss results for 420 martensitic stainless steel hardfacing during dry sand and rubber wheel abrasion testing. It specifically compares the wear performance between as-deposited and tempered conditions, providing a quantitative assessment of how heat treatment influences the material's resistance to abrasive wear under low-stress conditions.

caption: Initial assembly of the dry sand-rubber wheel (DSRW) abrasive wear test apparatus designed at the University of Sheffield.
summary: This photograph displays the initial assembly of the in-house designed dry sand-rubber wheel (DSRW) abrasive wear test apparatus. Developed at the University of Sheffield, this specialized equipment is utilized throughout the study to perform controlled abrasive wear testing on materials, providing the necessary mechanical configuration for experimental analysis.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) values measured for the tested specimens in a PBS solution containing 30 mM H2O2 and 170 mM HCl, utilizing an Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
summary: The open circuit potential (OCP) of the tested specimens was evaluated in a corrosive environment consisting of PBS, 30 mM H2O2, and 170 mM HCl. Measurements were conducted against an Ag/AgCl reference electrode to determine the electrochemical stability and corrosion behavior of the materials under these specific physiological-like conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry comparison of 2D- and 3D-IDCμE at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹, following 25 minutes of PPy electrodeposition at 1 mA cm⁻².
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves compare the electrochemical performance of 2D and 3D electrode architectures. At a 25-minute deposition time, the 3D-IDCμE exhibits a substantially larger current response than the 2D-IDCμE, demonstrating superior capacitive energy storage capabilities with a measured capacitance of 86 mF cm⁻² versus 30 mF cm⁻².

caption: Schmid factor distribution across the selected grains, showing values ranging from 0.47 to 0.50.
summary: The Schmid factors for the various selected grains are presented, revealing that they exhibit relatively high values between 0.47 and 0.50 with minimal variation. Grain G189 is specifically identified as having the lowest Schmid factor at 0.47, highlighting the orientation-dependent deformation potential of the analyzed grains.

caption: Cross-sectional BSE-SEM micrograph of an ID.Z. specimen extracted from the interdiffusion zone, revealing the internal microstructure and the presence of embedded grit-blasting particles.
summary: This cross-sectional BSE-SEM image displays an ID.Z. specimen extracted from the interdiffusion zone. The micrograph highlights the internal microstructure and confirms the presence of black grit-blasting particles within the material. This visualization demonstrates the accuracy of the specimen extraction procedure and provides a clear view of the internal cross-sectional morphology.

caption: Time-resolved spin distribution snapshots illustrating the stretch mode propagation in a 400 nm wide nanowire under an applied field of 40 Oe and a bias field of 200 Oe.
summary: This panel displays numerical simulation snapshots of domain wall spin distributions during the stretch mode propagation. Conducted in a 400 nm wide nanowire with an applied field of 40 Oe and a 200 Oe bias, these results visualize the complex spin configurations that characterize high-mobility behavior in magnetic nanowires.

caption: Y-axis cutting force profile during micro milling of LPBF Ti6Al4V at 60,000 rpm and 3 µm/flute with a 30 µm depth of cut.
summary: Y-axis cutting force data is presented here for the 30 µm depth of cut condition at 60,000 rpm and 3 µm/flute. This measurement is part of the experimental comparison used to analyze the effect of depth of cut on the forces generated during the micro milling of LPBF Ti6Al4V.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves of the 3D printed printlet measured in 0.1 M LiCl at 20 mV s-1 and 40 °C to evaluate redox stimulus response.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) was employed to analyze the redox stimulus response of the 3D printed printlet. The measurement was conducted in 0.1 M LiCl at a scan rate of 20 mV s-1 and an elevated temperature of 40 °C to evaluate the electrochemical behavior of the material.

caption: Comparison of cyclic voltammograms for the plating bath 1 on glassy carbon at a fixed cathodic potential limit of -1.50 V, contrasting stationary conditions with nonstationary magnetic stirring.
summary: This panel compares the electrochemical response of the plating bath 1 on glassy carbon at a cathodic limit of -1.50 V. It specifically highlights the effect of mass transport conditions by contrasting stationary electrolyte behavior with the influence of magnetic stirring on the recorded cyclic voltammetry curves.

caption: Polar figures (PF) of the as-built T III alloy, demonstrating relatively weak crystallographic textures and an absence of preferred orientation along the build direction due to the prevalence of equiaxed grains.
summary: The polar figures (PF) illustrate the crystallographic texture of the as-built T III alloy. The results demonstrate a relatively weak texture without a discernible preferred orientation along the build direction, which is attributed to the presence of equiaxed grain structures within the node regions and the struts.

caption: In-situ Vickers hardness measurements of laser-additive-manufactured AZT6115 evaluated from the as-deposited state up to 800 °C.
summary: Vickers hardness values for laser-additive-manufactured AZT6115 are plotted across a temperature range including the as-deposited state and elevated temperatures of 600 °C, 650 °C, 700 °C, 750 °C, and 800 °C. This in-situ analysis provides insight into the hardness evolution of the material as it is subjected to increasing thermal exposure.

caption: Average confusion matrix for Model IV, detailing the classification of deposit types originating from A-type magma.
summary: Model IV classifies deposit types derived from A-type magma, achieving 100% accuracy for Sn–W–Li and epithermal deposits. Conversely, the model exhibits lower performance in discriminating porphyry deposits in the hydrothermal stage, with an accuracy of 0.75. Overall, the model demonstrates robust performance with most identification accuracies exceeding 0.95.

caption: Spectral reflectance of MJT specimens featuring tilted surfaces, demonstrating an increase in reflectance values as the wedge angle (BO) increases.
summary: This panel displays the spectral reflectance of MJT specimens with tilted surfaces. The data indicates that reflectance values increase with higher wedge angles, which corresponds to higher lightness or albedo in the material. This trend highlights the optical response of the specimens as a function of their specific geometric tilt.

caption: Coefficients of friction (COF) measured for as-deposited Inconel 718 and cermet/Inconel 718 coatings, highlighting the superior performance of the 60% cermet variant.
summary: This plot displays the coefficients of friction for as-deposited Inconel 718 and various cermet/Inconel 718 coatings. The results demonstrate that the 60% cermet/Inconel 718 coating maintains the lowest coefficient of friction throughout the duration of the wear test, indicating enhanced tribological properties compared to the other tested compositions.

caption: Calculated subband structure at an applied bias of 3.8 V, highlighting the third highest Γ subband (Γ31) in green, which demonstrates Γ-X mixing with the X11 state.
summary: This figure displays the subband structure of the material at 3.8 V. The green-colored wave function, identified as the Γ31 state, originates from a 10-ML quantum well pair. The plot illustrates significant Γ-X mixing between the Γ31 subband and the X11 state, providing insight into the electronic transport characteristics.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of P3HT-PSL thin films, demonstrating the electrochemical behavior and the significant increase in peak current resulting from the growth of P3HT chains on PPI-SL branches.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry studies were performed on P3HT-PSL thin films to analyze their electrochemical properties. The resulting voltammograms indicate that the growth of P3HT chains on the PPI-SL branches leads to a significant increase in peak current, reflecting enhanced electrochemical activity compared to the base PPI-SL structure.

caption: Boundary conditions and excitation ports defined for the unit cell simulation setup.
summary: Boundary conditions and excitation ports are defined for the unit cell simulation setup. This configuration enables accurate prediction of the array’s performance based on a single unit cell, effectively eliminating the need to model the full array and simplifying the computational requirements for analyzing the MXene-coated frequency selective surface.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heat flow curves for agarose hydrogels with concentrations of 5 wt%, 5.5 wt%, and 6 wt%, highlighting melting temperatures with magenta arrows and gelation temperatures with green markers.
summary: Differential scanning calorimetry heat flow curves for agarose hydrogels with concentrations of 5 wt%, 5.5 wt%, and 6 wt% are presented. The analysis identifies specific thermal transitions, where magenta arrows denote melting temperatures and green markers indicate gelation temperatures, providing a clear comparison of the thermal behavior across different agarose concentrations.

caption: EDS analysis results obtained from point c in the 3003-TRC Al alloy microstructure.
summary: This EDS spectrum corresponds to the analysis performed at point c in the 3003-TRC Al alloy micrograph. The data provides elemental composition information for the specific particle phase identified at the grain boundary, supporting the identification of the Al12Mn3Si phase within the alloy's microstructure.

caption: Gibson-Ashby scaling chart showing yield strength plotted against relative density for cellular materials ranging from 12.4% to 35.6% relative density.
summary: Yield strength is presented as a function of relative density on a log-log scale, utilizing the Gibson-Ashby power law for fitting experimental data. The chart covers a relative density range of 12.4% to 35.6%, comparing the mechanical response of stochastic cellular structures against periodic lattice designs under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the surface laser polishing (SLP) system utilized for the post-processing of PBF-LS specimens.
summary: This schematic illustrates the surface laser polishing (SLP) system configuration. The diagram serves to visualize the experimental setup employed for treating PBF-LS specimens, as referenced in the study. It provides a clear overview of the processing environment and the methodology used to enhance the surface quality of the laser-sintered material.

caption: Secondary electron image of the heat-treated F sample, displaying large spherical porosity and martensitic-like strips within prior Al particle regions.
summary: Secondary electron imaging of the heat-treated F sample highlights the formation of large spherical porosity resulting from the diffusion of Al particles. The microstructure exhibits grains of variable sizes and the partial presence of martensitic-like strips, which are localized within the regions previously occupied by Al particles.

caption: Tafel polarization curve illustrating the electrochemical corrosion behavior of Inconel 625 samples.
summary: This panel displays the Tafel polarization curve for Inconel 625 samples, providing a visual representation of the electrochemical corrosion behavior. The plot serves as a fundamental diagnostic tool for evaluating the corrosion kinetics and current density characteristics of the material under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Sequential progression of the research methodology stages.
summary: This flowchart illustrates the systematic progression of the research methodology. It outlines the sequential stages involved in the study, providing a clear visual representation of the procedural framework adopted to achieve the research objectives and ensure a structured approach throughout the experimental and analytical phases of the investigation.

caption: Grain boundary distribution map of the WD cross-section showing low-angle and high-angle boundaries.
summary: This EBSD map of the WD cross-section highlights a high density of grain boundaries, which constitute 58.5% of the total boundary length. Notably, the analysis confirms the absence of Σ3 boundaries within the microstructure, providing a detailed quantitative assessment of the grain boundary network in the as-deposited sample.

caption: Wavelength shift plot showing the transition of absorption signals from 308 nm to 316 nm upon exposure of the TC film to acetone.
summary: This plot quantifies the red shift of absorption signals from 308 nm to 316 nm when acetone binds to the 2D chromite film. This shift is driven by charge transfer effects, surface plasmon resonance modifications, and structural distortions that lead to a measurable modification of the material's bandgap.

caption: Temperature contour plot representing the cross-sectional melt pool profile during the SLRM process at Point 1.
summary: This contour plot displays the temperature distribution on the cross-section of the melt pool during the SLRM process at Point 1. It serves as the initial observation point for the SLRM method, enabling a direct comparison of thermal profiles between SLM and SLRM processing conditions at this stage.

caption: Energy loss and thermal dissipation metrics for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes, showing individual contributions from Joule heating and enthalpy of mixing.
summary: Presented here are the specific net electrical energy loss and total thermal energy dissipation per unit charge stored for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes. The data, averaged over the last three consecutive charging and discharging cycles, includes predicted contributions from Joule heating and enthalpy of mixing for comparative analysis.

caption: Three-dimensional model generated from the segmented CT image data.
summary: The 3D model reconstruction is generated from the segmented CT images within the Mimics Research 21.0 environment. This digital representation provides the anatomical foundation for the subsequent mandible modeling and surgical planning steps required for the custom implant design workflow.

caption: Star symbol plots of plasma metabolites, including amino acids, organic acids, fatty acids, kynurenine pathway metabolites, and nucleosides, normalized to the Ti group.
summary: Star symbol plots display normalized plasma metabolite levels across Ti, Ti/EB 0.05, and Ti/EB 0.5 groups. Analysis of 37 amino acids revealed that 15 showed opposite metabolic profile changes between the 0.05 and 0.5 groups, while the remaining amino acids were decreased in both treatment groups compared to the Ti control.

caption: Directivity pattern for the spherical FESA support structure.
summary: The directivity pattern of the spherical FESA is shown in this simulation result. Analysis of the support structure indicates that no significant change in directivity occurs for this configuration, establishing a baseline directivity value of 1.76 dBi for the dielectric support design at the specified operating frequency.

caption: Capacity retention trends for the LFP||LNPs-CFC@Li full cell, highlighting the stability maintained across various operational current densities.
summary: Capacity retention data for the LFP||LNPs-CFC@Li full cell across various current densities confirms its robust electrochemical performance. The results indicate that the cell maintains high capacity retention, demonstrating superior stability and efficiency compared to standard LFP-based full cells, as evidenced by the consistent performance across the tested current ranges.

caption: Aperiodic V-type minimal surface derived from the pentagonal prism geometry.
summary: The aperiodic V minimal surface is shown as a result of the Tile(1,1)-based construction process. By utilizing the pentagonal prism with vertex-oriented tunnels, this structure exemplifies the capability to generate non-periodic minimal surfaces, contributing to the broader set of spatial layouts explored in the study.

caption: Schematic representation of Ni-X binary phase diagrams illustrating the criterion for supersaturation at a service temperature of 750 °C.
summary: This panel presents schematic Ni-X binary phase diagrams to define the supersaturation criterion. By ensuring the alloying system remains in a supersaturated state at the service temperature of 750 °C, a thermodynamic driving force is established, facilitating the diffusion of atoms toward empty damage sites during service.

caption: Pareto-ANOVA analysis showing the individual contribution bars and cumulative contribution red dots of design factors impacting the second-law efficiency (η II).
summary: This Pareto-ANOVA plot quantifies the influence of various design factors on the η II target function. Individual contributions are represented by bars, while the cumulative impact is tracked by red dots. This analysis, derived from DoE S/N ratios, effectively ranks the importance of factors to optimize the system performance.

caption: Ashby plot comparing ultimate tensile strength (UTS) versus solid fraction for BCC lattices, including literature data from Ref. [45].
summary: Representing the relationship between plastic/crushing stress and relative density, this Ashby plot characterizes the mechanical performance of the studied lattices. The slope of the lines, defined by the exponent m, indicates the specific loading mode of the lattice structure, providing a comparative analysis against established literature values.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the functional dependence of the thermal parameter θ on variables τ, ξ, and η for niobium (Nb).
summary: This contour plot visualizes the thermal parameter θ as a function of variables τ, ξ, and η for niobium. Higher values of θ correspond to increased thermal energy generation within the system, leading to a rise in temperature. The figure effectively demonstrates the influence of these parameters on the system's thermal behavior.

caption: Raman spectra comparing carbon deposits at the cross-section of Ni/YSZ after 2 h and Cu–Ni/YSZ after 180 h of CH4 exposure at 750 °C, highlighting the D-peak intensities.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals the carbon state at the cross-section of Ni/YSZ and Cu–Ni/YSZ anodes exposed to CH4 at 750 °C. Increased D-peak intensities at 1316 and 1615 cm−1 in the Cu–Ni/YSZ sample after 180 hours indicate the formation of more disordered carbon compared to the Ni/YSZ sample after 2 hours.

caption: Spectral response plot demonstrating the shift in the Bragg wavelength peak of the FBG when subjected to external physical perturbations, highlighting the sensor's sensitivity to environmental changes.
summary: The spectral response of the FBG is depicted here, demonstrating its function as a sensing mechanism. The plot shows how the reflected spectrum changes in response to external perturbations. This perturbation-dependent behavior allows the FBG to act as a sensor, where shifts in the Bragg wavelength indicate changes in the surrounding environment.

caption: Z-direction 10 nm section of the APT specimen located below an Al2Mn precipitate, featuring an iso-concentration surface of 50 at% Mg that delineates the outer boundary of the approximately 5 nm thick homogeneous oxide layer.
summary: A 10 nm Z-section of the APT specimen demonstrates the formation of a homogeneous oxide layer approximately 5 nm thick around the specimen. The 50 at% Mg iso-concentration surface effectively highlights the outer boundary of this oxide structure, specifically in the region situated below an Al2Mn precipitate.

caption: Confocal fluorescent images of printed scaffolds with live cells stained green and dead cells stained red, highlighting the hollow core regions.
summary: Confocal fluorescent imaging was utilized to assess cell viability within the printed scaffolds. The results show that the printing process did not induce significant cellular damage, as the majority of cells appear green. Furthermore, the images clearly indicate the presence of hollow cores, confirming the scaffold's suitability for tissue engineering applications.

caption: Three-directional shrinkage measurements of cube specimens obtained via dilatometry.
summary: Dilatometry tests were performed to evaluate the dimensional stability of cube specimens. The resulting data, presented as three-directional shrinkage curves, quantify the thermal expansion or contraction behavior of the material during the experimental process, providing essential insights into the volumetric changes occurring within the specimens under controlled thermal conditions.

caption: Voltage versus time profiles for CX, CX@Cu, CX@Fe, and CX@Co electrodes under a capacity-limited condition of 1 mAh/cm2 and a constant current density of 0.1 mA/cm2.
summary: This plot displays the charge and discharge voltage profiles for CX, CX@Cu, CX@Fe, and CX@Co electrodes. The experiment maintains a constant current density of 0.1 mA/cm2 with a capacity limitation of 1 mAh/cm2, providing a comparative assessment of the electrochemical performance and cycling behavior for these specific electrode materials.

caption: Schematic illustration of the friction joint configuration, highlighting the specific metallographic observation area located at the edge of the welded rods.
summary: The diagram depicts the friction joint geometry and identifies the precise region selected for metallographic analysis. This area is critical for observing the thermal-mechanical affected zone, as the number of turns during the friction phase significantly influences the heat release and the resulting width of the joint interface.

caption: Atom probe tomography (APT) reconstruction showing the morphology of the precipitated L1 2 phase and the elemental composition of the γ/γ′ phases.
summary: Atom probe tomography (APT) characterization provides a 3D view of the precipitated L1 2 phase morphology. Additionally, this technique allows for the precise determination of the chemical composition of the γ and γ′ phases, offering critical data on the phase chemistry within the alloy.

caption: Detailed 3D microscopic wear profile of the HT2 heat-treated AISI 316L sample.
summary: This panel presents a detailed 3D microscopic wear profile of the AISI 316L sample after the HT2 heat treatment. The visualization reveals the surface wear characteristics of the HT2-treated specimen, which is critical for understanding the impact of this specific heat treatment on the material's overall wear performance.

caption: Belov-Arrott plot of M^2 versus μoH/M for as-quenched Ni0.895Cr0.105MnGe1.05 ribbons, with an inset showing reversible isothermal magnetization curves at 179 K and 175 K.
summary: The Belov-Arrott plot for as-quenched Ni0.895Cr0.105MnGe1.05 ribbons displays positive curve slopes, confirming a second-order ferromagnetic to paramagnetic transition. Inset data demonstrates zero hysteresis loss during field-sweeping cycles up to 5 T, indicating a completely reversible magnetization process at temperatures corresponding to the cold sink for refrigerant capacity calculations.

caption: Tafel curves derived from polarization data for substrate, EAM, and ECM surfaces.
summary: Tafel curves are plotted for substrate, EAM, and ECM surfaces to extract kinetic parameters related to the corrosion process. By analyzing the linear regions of these curves, the electrochemical behavior and reaction mechanisms of the surfaces are elucidated, providing a detailed view of their respective corrosion resistance characteristics.

caption: High-resolution XPS fine scan of the Ni 2p region, identifying the nickel chemical states within the blackened surface layer.
summary: The Ni 2p fine scan identifies the chemical states of nickel within the blackened surface layer. This data, combined with other elemental scans, confirms the presence of NiO as a constituent of the complex oxide mixture, further characterizing the uneven surface oxidation and distinct microstructures of the blackened sample.

caption: Electronic band structure diagram for a hybridized I-WP unit cell configuration combining relative densities of 32% and 22%.
summary: This panel shows the band structure for a hybridized I-WP unit cell design that integrates regions of 32% and 22% relative density. The resulting electronic dispersion reflects the influence of structural hybridization, demonstrating how combining different density components within a single unit cell modifies the overall electronic band characteristics.

caption: Phase map of the H900 sample integrated with EDS oxygen data, showing the distribution of delta-ferrite and spherical particles.
summary: Integrated phase and EDS oxygen mapping of the H900 sample reveals the presence of delta-ferrite and spherical or ellipsoidal particles dispersed within the matrix. These features are critical for understanding the microstructural evolution induced by heat treatment, which influences the material's passive film uniformity and its resistance to localized corrosion.

caption: Detailed shift of diffraction peaks for the (002) and (101) planes across all treated and untreated samples.
summary: Observed shifts of the (002) and (101) diffraction peaks toward lower angles are highlighted in this panel. These shifts are attributed to micro-strain, grain size refinement, and other microstructural factors induced by the various surface treatment processes, indicating significant changes in the crystalline lattice parameters of the samples.

caption: Cross-sectional HAADF-STEM image of the corrosion layer in the S O – C sample, showing the microstructure within the first 4.5 μm from the surface.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the cross-sectional microstructure of the S O – C sample corrosion layer. The analysis focuses on the region extending approximately 4.5 μm from the surface. It serves as the structural baseline for identifying corrosion products and grain boundary features within the alloy after molten salt exposure.

caption: Integrated deuterium retention values derived from thermal release data are presented as a function of reciprocal temperature.
summary: This plot displays the integrated deuterium retention values calculated from the thermal release data shown in Figure 9. By plotting these values against the reciprocal of temperature, the figure illustrates the temperature-dependent behavior of deuterium retention, providing a clear visualization of the release kinetics within the studied material system.

caption: Relaxed microparticle chain at 0.25 kV, demonstrating the return to a shorter chain configuration and substrate equilibrium.
summary: Panel f illustrates the microparticle chain in its shortened state at 0.25 kV. The reduction in voltage results in chain contraction and subsequent substrate relaxation. This reversible and repeatable cycle confirms the precise control over the chain length and force transmission achieved through voltage modulation between 0.25 and 1.0 kV.

caption: Impedance mode and Bode phase angle curves for WAAM and WAAM + UI specimens, where the WAAM + UI specimen exhibits higher peak width and maximum phase angle.
summary: Impedance mode and Bode phase angle diagrams for AZ31 thin walls along the TD direction demonstrate that the WAAM + UI specimen possesses a higher peak width and maximum phase angle. These features indicate greater resistance, lower capacitance, and a lower corrosion rate compared to the standard WAAM specimen.

caption: Immunofluorescence imaging of ZO-1 protein in MCE cells, visualizing the modulation of tight junction integrity and recovery following cL treatment.
summary: Immunofluorescence images of ZO-1 protein provide a visual assessment of tight junction integrity in MCE cells. The images demonstrate the capability of cL to induce tight junction opening and subsequent recovery, illustrating the dynamic impact of the treatment on cellular barrier structures within the corneal epithelium.

caption: Optimized atomic configuration of a methane molecule adsorbed on a Ni4Zn cluster supported by ZrO2.
summary: Depicted is the DFT-optimized structure for methane adsorption on a Ni4Zn–ZrO2 catalyst. The Ni–Zn interface on the ZrO2 support demonstrates a significantly higher methane adsorption energy of −1.11 eV, confirming that the presence of Zn and the ZrO2 support enhances the interaction with methane molecules.

caption: Transmission electron micrograph identifying the presence of oxides within the AM state matrix, resulting from residual oxygen content during the additive manufacturing and powder production processes.
summary: This TEM analysis focuses on the oxide formation within the AM state matrix after creep failure at 950 °C and 25 MPa. The presence of these oxides is attributed to residual oxygen from the additive manufacturing process, which contributes to material embrittlement at high temperatures.

caption: Box plot comparison of the effective Young's modulus (YM) across the three printed zones, demonstrating that regions printed at 100% light intensity exhibit significantly higher stiffness compared to the 50% intensity zone.
summary: The box plot illustrates the effective Young's modulus of the GelMA hydrogel across three distinct zones. Zones printed at 100% light intensity achieved higher mean effective YM values of 22.54 kPa and 20.90 kPa, whereas the 50% intensity zone showed a lower mean effective YM of 12.66 kPa, confirming successful spatial mechanical control.

caption: Hardness values (HV 30) of sintered bodies measured across different sintering temperatures, reaching 1360 ± 16 HV 30.
summary: Hardness values for the sintered bodies are presented relative to the sintering temperature. The results confirm that the optimized binder system and post-processing conditions yield a high hardness of 1360 ± 16 HV 30, reflecting the improved mechanical integrity and densification achieved through the specific thermal treatment applied to the samples.

caption: 3D surface topography of the CX stainless steel sample subjected to a 30 N wear load.
summary: Surface topography of the CX stainless steel sample is shown in 3D after being subjected to a 30 N wear load. This visualization highlights the morphological changes and wear track characteristics on the material surface, demonstrating the progression of wear damage as the applied load increases to 30 N.

caption: Force-displacement response of the third 50% TPU honeycomb specimen subjected to twelve consecutive cold programming cycles.
summary: Displaying the force-displacement response for the third 50% TPU honeycomb specimen, this panel completes the set of individual cyclic tests. The data illustrates the mechanical behavior of the b-FDM printed honeycomb over twelve cold programming cycles, providing essential information for the statistical analysis of the material's cyclic performance.

caption: Statistical distribution of α-colony size across four distinct build heights (P1–P4), representing aggregated data from BD–TD, BD–DD, and DD–TD planes.
summary: This box plot illustrates the variation in α-colony size measured at four specific build heights, labeled P1 through P4. The data represents an average across three different planes: BD–TD, BD–DD, and DD–TD. These measurements characterize the lamellar α/β colony structure that forms within equiaxed prior-β grains during the cooling process.

caption: t-SNE visualization of features extracted from the second convolutional layer.
summary: Represented here is the t-SNE visualization of features learned by the second convolutional layer of the network. This plot serves to illustrate the progression of feature extraction within the CNN architecture, allowing for a comparative analysis of how data organization evolves across successive layers of the model.

caption: Correlation between the single-track width-depth ratio and the applied linear energy density, illustrating the distribution of four distinct track formation stages.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the width-depth ratio and linear energy density for single-track features. It qualitatively categorizes the data into four distinct stages of track formation based on these parameters. The visualization provides a clear correlation, mapping how energy density influences the geometric characteristics of the single-track.

caption: Discharge capacity versus cycle number for rapidly quenched Mg2Ni1-xZnx alloy electrodes over 50 charge/discharge cycles.
summary: This plot illustrates the discharge capacity of rapidly quenched Mg2Ni1-xZnx alloy electrodes across 50 charge/discharge cycles. Each curve exhibits a distinct inflection point, allowing the data to be categorized into an initial rapid decline stage followed by a subsequent slow decline stage, reflecting the electrochemical stability of the alloy electrodes.

caption: Structural column component utilized in the Project Future Tree pavilion.
summary: This photograph displays a structural column component implemented in the Project Future Tree pavilion. As part of a collection of 3D printed formworks, this component demonstrates the application of additive manufacturing to create structural elements with sufficient cross-sectional areas for building construction, highlighting the versatility of modern formwork techniques.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrating the mass loss behavior of pure TPU and various TPU composite prints as a function of temperature.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrate the mass loss behavior of pure TPU and various TPU composite prints as a function of temperature. Pure TPU exhibits an initial decomposition temperature of 291.4 °C and a maximum decomposition temperature of 331.3 °C, with a residual mass of 11.53 % at 600 °C.

caption: Light transmittance curves of CNF suspensions at 0.05 wt% concentration, showing values exceeding 85%.
summary: Light transmittance curves of CNF suspensions at 0.05 wt% concentration, showing values exceeding 85%. According to the light transmittance curves, it is evident that the light transmittance of all CNFs suspensions exceeds 85%, confirming the uniformly distributed cellulose nanofibrils in the suspensions and the high optical clarity of the prepared materials.

caption: Root mean square error (RMSE) plotted against the regularization parameter λ for the physical law-driven physics-informed neural network (PINN) model.
summary: This plot illustrates the performance sensitivity of the physical law-driven PINN model by showing the variation of RMSE values across different λ parameters. The data demonstrates how the model's predictive accuracy on the test set evolves as the physical law constraints are adjusted, providing insight into the optimal regularization configuration.

caption: Stress relaxation response of René 41 at 700 °C, showing experimental data alongside model predictions for initial spring displacements of 6, 8, and 10 mm.
summary: At 700 °C, the stress relaxation response of René 41 is compared against model predictions for different spring displacements. The observed variance in experimental data is notably closer to the model's behavior, with the extreme case suggesting a stress-sensitive model compatibility, despite discrepancies in the overall curve shape.

caption: Particle trajectory simulation upstream of the spray gun with an inlet diameter D i1 of 0.5 mm.
summary: Simulated particle tracks for an inlet diameter of 0.5 mm reveal that the gas vortex induces intense suction and coiling effects. These hydrodynamic forces trigger severe particle backflow and a high probability of wall collisions, which significantly increases the risk of nozzle clogging and reduces overall manufacturing efficiency.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the polarization curves of Ru3Ni3NAs, Ru3Ni2NAs, Ru3Ni1NAs, Ru NAs, and Pt/C in 1 M KOH.
summary: The Tafel plots shown here are derived from the polarization curves in 1 M KOH. These plots provide insight into the reaction kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction for the different Ru-Ni nanoarray catalysts and the commercial Pt/C benchmark, illustrating the efficiency of the electron transfer process.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of hMSC cultured for 28 days on dual-porosity scaffolds, showing immunofluorescence staining for collagen I (red), collagen II (blue), DNA (yellow), and F-actin (green).
summary: Fluorescence microscopy reveals hMSC behavior on dual-porosity scaffolds after 28 days. Staining for collagen I, collagen II, DNA, and F-actin highlights the ECM composition. Collagen II is particularly prevalent in CM-cultured constructs, where it forms a structured, fibrillar ECM, demonstrating enhanced organization compared to other conditions.

caption: Enlarged Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of the sample processed for 7.5 minutes, highlighting the crystallographic orientation distribution of grains.
summary: This enlarged Inverse Pole Figure map displays the crystallographic orientation of grains in the 7.5-minute sample. The visualization provides a detailed view of grain orientations, which, when analyzed alongside other maps, helps confirm that the observed microstructural evolution is driven by recrystallization rather than abnormal grain growth.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectra comparing aqueous suspensions of pure FNF and the FNF@AuNP nanohybrid, highlighting the characteristic Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) band of the gold nanoparticles.
summary: UV–Vis spectroscopy confirms the successful incorporation of AuNPs into the FNF matrix. The spectrum of FNF@AuNP exhibits the characteristic Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) band typical of gold nanoparticles, corroborating findings from similar fibroin-AuNP materials and demonstrating the optical signature of the metallic component within the nanohybrid.

caption: Three-dimensional micro-CT reconstruction of the k 67° specimen, revealing a fragmented and homogeneously oriented porous network.
summary: This micro-CT reconstruction illustrates the 3D void structure within the k 67° specimen. The visualization highlights a fragmented, homogeneously oriented porous network that lacks periodic or stacked voids. This specific architecture reduces overall void interconnection, contrasting with other strategies and influencing the material's fracture behavior under mechanical stress.

caption: Integrated sustainability radar chart combining HPI and TBL metrics to determine the overall performance of each material configuration.
summary: Final sustainability scores are integrated into this radar chart to reflect the overall performance of each material configuration. The data confirms that the V50:R50 blend is the most sustainable configuration, achieving a score of -1.35, while highlighting the inherent challenges of achieving full rPLA substitution in performance-critical applications.

caption: Lidinoid (LSC) TPMS architecture modeled in nTop with 60% porosity.
summary: The Lidinoid (LSC) TPMS architecture is modeled in nTop with a 60% porosity design. This structure is part of a comparative set featuring specific unit cell dimensions, which were selected to ensure comparable volumetric and fluidic properties for evaluating permeability, degradation, and cytocompatibility across different scaffold types.

caption: Dark-field transmission electron microscopy image of the R-phase at −100 °C.
summary: This dark-field image, obtained by selecting the R-phase diffraction spots marked in panel (g), visualizes the R-phase at −100 °C. The image confirms that the high-density R-phase particles remain uniformly distributed throughout the NiTiV alloy matrix, maintaining their structural characteristics at this lower temperature.

caption: Surface electric current response of oriented SiC whisker composites.
summary: Surface electric current response of oriented SiC whisker composites is illustrated. The composites exhibit anisotropic conductivity, where the electric current increases exponentially with voltage. This nonlinear conductivity is a key feature of the oriented SiC whisker composites, consistent with previous discussions regarding their electrical performance and material properties.

caption: Top-down view of the sintered ATZ cube highlighting the geometric precision of the complex printed features.
summary: The top-down view of the sintered ATZ cube confirms the high-fidelity reproduction of complex structures achieved through digital light processing. The successful fabrication of this geometry highlights the effectiveness of the developed slurry composition and processing parameters in producing high-quality, intricate ceramic parts without structural failure.

caption: Intensity-wavelength plots of supercontinuum generation collected via spectrometer while the hexapod stage translates at a constant speed of 100 μm/s under varying pulse energy conditions.
summary: This plot displays the spectral intensity of supercontinuum light as a function of wavelength. The data was captured while a hexapod stage moved at 100 μm/s to ensure continuous excitation. The results demonstrate how varying pulse energies influence the resulting supercontinuum output collected by the spectrometer during the experimental process.

caption: Cycle performance evaluation of printed and tape-casted cells, plotting specific capacity and Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles at a C-rate following rate testing.
summary: Cycle performance is assessed here by tracking specific capacities and Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles at a C-rate. This panel evaluates the long-term stability of the printed LCO cathodes compared to tape-casted versions, confirming the durability of the electrochemical cells after the initial rate capability tests were completed.

caption: Optical micrograph of the stress-relieved sample exhibiting elongated grains within a polygonal structure, despite the absence of significant microstructural alterations.
summary: Optical microscopy of the stress-relieved sample shows that the overall microstructure remains largely unchanged compared to the as-built state. However, closer inspection reveals the presence of particularly elongated grains within a polygonal structure, indicating that the stress relief process does not eliminate the primary molten pool features.

caption: Representative fluorescence microscopy images of hMSCs at day 7, showing live cells stained green and dead cells stained red, alongside DAPI-stained nuclei and phalloidin-stained actin filaments.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy using Live/Dead staining confirms that hMSCs remain viable on THA-Col and THA-Col + CaP matrices throughout the 7-day experiment. In contrast, THA alone shows a reduced number of surviving cells. DAPI and phalloidin staining further illustrate the morphology and attachment of the cells on the composite surfaces.

caption: Statistical distribution of α/α’ lath lengths for Ti-1Fe(S) and Ti-6Al-4V samples, showing the spread and area-averaged values for each specific build condition.
summary: This box plot illustrates the distribution of α/α’ lath lengths across eight experimental conditions. By comparing the spread and the diamond-marked area averages, the plot highlights how different build strategies influence the longitudinal growth of laths in both Ti-1Fe(S) and Ti-6Al-4V, providing insight into the resulting microstructural morphology.

caption: Radar chart comparing the mechanical performance metrics of nacre-inspired composites against solid ceramics, illustrating improvements in strength, stiffness, and toughness.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive overview of the mechanical performance of nacre-inspired composites. By mapping various measured properties, the visualization highlights significant enhancements in strength, stiffness, and toughness compared to traditional solid ceramics, offering a holistic comparison of the material's mechanical behavior and overall structural efficiency.

caption: SHAP dependence plot showing the effective stress ratio on the horizontal axis and specimen state on the vertical axis, with dot colors representing the state.
summary: This visualization examines the dependency of the effective stress ratio on the specimen state. Because stress parameters are interrelated, this plot must be interpreted in conjunction with panels (d) and (f). The SHAP values for specific states may overlap on the vertical axis, reflecting the categorical nature of the state variable.

caption: Accuracy validation plot for sample 10 generated using MATLAB software.
summary: This plot displays the accuracy validation results for sample 10, as processed through MATLAB. The visualization serves as a performance metric to assess the model's predictive capability for this specific sample, providing a quantitative measure of accuracy that confirms the reliability of the computational analysis performed in the study.

caption: Secondary electron micrograph showing the grain morphology within the selected area of Zone 2.
summary: Captured via scanning electron microscopy, this image illustrates the grain morphology within the selected area of Zone 2. It contributes to the overall microstructural assessment of the thermally affected region, highlighting the structural features present in the material before the heat treatment process is initiated.

caption: Live/Dead staining images of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured with scaffold extracts, showing cell viability at 4x magnification.
summary: Live/Dead staining of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured with scaffold extracts demonstrates the biocompatibility of the materials. The PTH(1–34)@PLGA/CS-nHA group exhibits significantly higher cell viability compared to the control groups, confirming that the incorporation of PTH(1–34) synergistically improves the biocompatibility and proliferative activity of the composite scaffolds.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the UA-WAAM sample processed at 50 V and 30 kHz, showing that the columnar grain structure remains largely unrefined at this low ultrasonic frequency.
summary: At a relatively low ultrasonic frequency of 30 kHz and 50 V, the UA-WAAM sample maintains a microstructure similar to the unmodified WAAM sample. The large columnar grains within the deposited layers remain largely unrefined, indicating that this specific ultrasonic setting is insufficient to significantly alter the grain morphology.

caption: R-curve for AS steel specimens showing valid data-pairs as filled markers and repetition tests in grey.
summary: The R-curve for AS steel specimens illustrates fracture toughness behavior, with valid data-pairs for regression highlighted as filled markers. Repetition tests are included in grey to demonstrate data consistency. These curves are essential for identifying specimen-specific differences in the diluted interface layer and are processed using exponential function fitting.

caption: Tanδ temperature-dependent damping curves for compression moulded SFRP samples, compared across dried and humid (30%RH, 50%RH, 80%RH) conditions.
summary: This panel presents the DMTA curves for compression moulded SFRP, showing the variation of tanδ with temperature. The curves illustrate the impact of humidity on the material's damping properties, comparing the dried state against 30%RH, 50%RH, and 80%RH conditions to evaluate the moisture sensitivity of the compression moulded composite.

caption: Tensile strain distribution map for the T specimen at 1.75% elongation, illustrating the strain profile relative to the gauge center.
summary: At 1.75% elongation, the T specimen displays its tensile strain distribution across the gauge length. This measurement, taken between the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength, provides a visual representation of the strain localization behavior within the specimen gauge during the uniform deformation stage of the tensile test.

caption: Statistical distribution of liquid phase channel lengths and grain sizes for SLMed 7050 aluminum alloy and its TiO2-reinforced composites.
summary: This histogram displays the grain size distribution and liquid phase channel lengths for SLMed 7050 aluminum alloy and TiO2-reinforced variants. Specifically, the 7050 alloy exhibits a grain size of 34.95 μm, with solid-liquid channels reaching a maximum length of 31 μm at the grain boundaries, illustrating the microstructural characteristics of these materials.

caption: Backscattered electron image of directional γ′ coarsening at a grain boundary after aging at 800 °C for 1 hour, extending into adjacent grains.
summary: This backscattered electron image highlights the directional coarsening of γ′ precipitates at a grain boundary after 1 hour of aging at 800 °C. The coarsening process is observed even on apparently straight high-angle grain boundary segments, with the coarsened precipitates extending into the grains on both sides of the boundary.

caption: Temperature-dependent resistivity curves of the microwire measured under a 3 T magnetic field applied parallel and perpendicular to the wire axis.
summary: Resistivity-temperature curves are presented for the microwire under 3 T magnetic fields applied both parallel and vertical to the wire length. These measurements characterize the electronic transport properties of the material, illustrating how the orientation of the external magnetic field relative to the microwire axis influences the resistivity behavior.

caption: Strain at peak force measured during cutting tests as a function of porosity, illustrating the brittleness of cookie samples processed via oven baking or air frying.
summary: Strain at peak force is used to evaluate the brittleness of 3D printed cookie samples across varying porosities. Observations indicate that the degree of brittleness remains relatively consistent regardless of structural porosity, although specific variations are noted between different sample types, such as pea samples versus cookie samples printed with 1.0 mm nozzles.

caption: Atomic model of the NiO (001) surface illustrating the antiferromagnetic (AFM) ordering, where solid and dashed lines represent alternating (111) Ni cation layers with opposing spin orientations denoted by black arrows.
summary: This atomic model depicts the NiO (001) surface structure, which is generated by introducing a vacuum gap along the [001] direction. The visualization highlights the antiferromagnetic ordering of the system, specifically showing how alternating (111) Ni cation layers exhibit distinct up or down spin configurations as indicated by black arrows.

caption: Optical transmittance and reflectance spectra of photovoltaic cells encapsulated with pure COC and various COCA coversheets, measured across different incident angles.
summary: This figure illustrates the optical performance of photovoltaic cells protected by pure COC and various COCA coversheets. The spectra display both transmittance and reflectance characteristics, providing insight into the light management properties of these materials when evaluated at different angles to assess their suitability for photovoltaic applications.

caption: Illustration of the auxetic behavior in a re-entrant unit cell, demonstrating transverse expansion upon axial stretching.
summary: This schematic illustrates the counter-intuitive auxetic property of a re-entrant unit cell. When the structure is subjected to axial stretching, indicated by the black arrow, internal mechanisms cause the cell to expand transversely, resulting in a larger volume as shown by the red geometry compared to the original state.

caption: Optical profilometry map of the oxidised sandblasted surface, illustrating the topographical features induced by sandblasting and subsequent oxidation.
summary: Representing the surface topography of the oxidised sandblasted specimen, this optical profilometry map uses a color scale to denote height variations. The image captures the specific surface texture generated by the sandblasting process combined with oxidation, allowing for a comparative analysis of surface roughness parameters in this specific condition.

caption: Averaged UV-Vis absorbance spectra obtained from sequential separation tests, demonstrating the highest immobilization efficiency at a particle concentration of 10^4 p/mL and a flow rate of 250 μL/min.
summary: Averaged UV-Vis spectra illustrate the immobilization efficiency of MP-NPs under different experimental conditions. The data confirms that the highest immobilization efficiency is achieved when fluxing particles at a concentration of 10^4 p/mL with a flow rate set at 250 μL/min, as indicated by the spectral analysis.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded in the BRB buffer/1,2-DCE LLI at pH 4, comparing the absence of BIL (solid red), presence of 150 µM BIL (dashed black), and presence of 150 µM BIL with 50 µM TMACl (dotted black).
summary: Cyclic voltammograms at pH 4 show minimal changes upon introducing BIL into the BRB buffer/1,2-DCE LLI system. The solid red and dashed black curves overlap, indicating that BIL does not significantly alter the electrochemical response in this weakly acidic range. TMACl serves as an internal reference probe for these measurements.

caption: Contour plots illustrating the optimal design parameters (t, l) that minimize the total exergy destruction rate for system velocities of 0 m/s, 25 m/s, 200 m/s, and 1000 m/s.
summary: This figure displays the design space optimization for a unit cell by mapping the total exergy destruction as a function of geometric parameters t and l. By evaluating four distinct velocity scenarios ranging from 0 m/s to 1000 m/s, the plots identify the specific configurations that minimize energy loss within the system.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of reinforcement layers showing an inflection point between -0.9 and -1.1 V.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for reinforcement layers prepared by CAJED are presented. The data reveals a distinct inflection point occurring within the potential range of -0.9 to -1.1 V, characterizing the electrochemical behavior of the reinforcement layers under the specified composite solution conditions during the deposition process.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the phase composition of the as-cast sample before and after corrosion (FRA) testing.
summary: This panel displays the X-ray diffraction patterns for the as-cast sample, specifically highlighting the identified phases present before and after the corrosion (FRA) testing process. These results, as part of the broader analysis in Fig. 14, provide critical insights into the phase stability and structural changes induced by corrosion.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) profiles showing mass loss as a function of temperature for B-PLA composites and pure PLA across a range from 30 °C to approximately 250 °C.
summary: Thermogravimetric profiles for B-PLA composites fabricated at various FDM temperatures are presented alongside neat PLA. The curves demonstrate the thermal degradation behavior of the materials, with a clear observation of mass loss phenomena occurring within the temperature range of 30 °C to approximately 250 °C.

caption: Relative error distribution for the Back Propagation (BP) neural network model on the test dataset.
summary: The relative error analysis for the BP model on the test set is presented in this panel. This visualization supports the finding that the model's predictive performance can be evaluated through its error distribution, providing a quantitative assessment of the BP algorithm's accuracy when applied to the specified test data.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map for Nickel (Ni) in the EDPS alloy.
summary: Nickel distribution in the EDPS alloy is mapped using EDS. The results show that Ni is concentrated in the B2 phase, which is also rich in Al. This confirms the chemical partitioning between the Fcc and B2 phases, consistent with the observed structural refinement in the EDPS alloy.

caption: Calculated chemical diffusion coefficients of Al in Co-7.5Al-(0–20)Cr and Co-32Ni-7.5Al-(0–20)Cr alloys at 900 °C, derived using the PanCo2021-TH + MB atomic mobility database.
summary: This plot illustrates the chemical diffusion coefficients of Al within Co-7.5Al-(0–20)Cr and Co-32Ni-7.5Al-(0–20)Cr alloy systems at a constant temperature of 900 °C. These values were determined through a CALPHAD-based approach utilizing the PanCo2021-TH + MB atomic mobility database, providing essential kinetic data for understanding diffusion behavior in these specific cobalt-based alloy compositions.

caption: Energy absorption profile of DED-Arc built MS250 steel subjected to impact testing at 823 K.
summary: Impact testing of DED-Arc built MS250 at 823 K results in a specific energy absorption value, with a noted 64 MPa difference in flow stress compared to other conditions. This plot, derived from true stress-strain curves, confirms the stabilization of mechanical properties at elevated temperatures for the additively manufactured alloy.

caption: Comparison of prediction errors for machine learning models across varying strain rates at a constant temperature of 270 °C.
summary: This plot displays the prediction error of machine learning models evaluated at 270 °C under different strain rate conditions. The data demonstrates that machine learning models provide accurate and robust predictions when compared to traditional constitutive models, highlighting their superior performance and reliability for material behavior modeling at this specific temperature.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of La1.9Mg1.1Ni9 alloy annealed at 1223 K for 6 hours, showing a predominant two-phase structure of (La,Mg)Ni3 and (La,Mg)2Ni7 with a minor residual LaNi5 phase.
summary: The annealed La1.9Mg1.1Ni9 alloy is characterized by a segregated multi-phase structure with coarse grains. Analysis reveals it consists primarily of (La,Mg)Ni3 and (La,Mg)2Ni7 phases, accompanied by a small residual amount of approximately 2 wt% LaNi5, illustrating the phase composition after 6 hours of annealing at 1223 K.

caption: Surface roughness parameters including Rmax, Rz, Ra, and Pt for the cylinder honed at 500 RPM.
summary: This table presents the quantitative surface roughness results for a cylinder honed at 500 RPM. It specifically lists the Rmax, Rz, Ra, and Pt values, which characterize the surface quality achieved through the honing process. These metrics provide a baseline for evaluating the effectiveness of the machining parameters used.

caption: Thermomechanical analysis (TMA) curves comparing the dimensional stability of PET3 and PETG specimens fabricated via fused granulate fabrication (FGF) using XY-oriented plates.
summary: Thermomechanical analysis curves illustrate the dimensional response of PET3 and PETG specimens produced through fused granulate fabrication. These TMA results facilitate a direct comparison of the coefficient of thermal expansion for these materials, which were identified as the top-performing candidates during mechanical evaluation, highlighting their distinct thermal stability characteristics.

caption: Engineering stress–strain curves for S3 SEBM 316L stainless steel under vertical and horizontal loading, including insets of representative post-fracture morphologies derived from DIC.
summary: Engineering stress–strain curves for S3 SEBM 316L stainless steel under vertical and horizontal loading, including insets of representative post-fracture morphologies derived from DIC. These features are attributed to the elevated processing temperature in SEBM, which promotes dislocation rearrangement akin to annealing, resulting in behavior matching conventionally annealed 316L.

caption: Dynamic pressure response within the CuTi alloy throughout the 200 ps simulation period, driven by the evolving temperature gradient.
summary: This panel illustrates the dynamic pressure response in the CuTi alloy during the 200 ps laser ablation process. The pressure evolution is shown to be directly concomitant with the temperature gradient developed in the material, highlighting the thermodynamic conditions driving the ablation process during the simulation timeframe.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of PCL/IL5% composite before and after chemical recycling via alcoholysis with or without added ionic liquid at 60 °C for 24 hours.
summary: This panel displays the 1H NMR spectra for PCL/IL5% composites, comparing the original material to samples treated with alcoholysis. The analysis investigates the impact of the ionic liquid additive on the chemical recycling efficiency of the PCL matrix when processed at 60 °C for a duration of 24 hours.

caption: Three-dimensional binding site view highlighting the SL molecule surrounded by hydrophobic amino acid residues including Tyr-59 and His-57.
summary: The 3D binding site view illustrates the SL molecule surrounded by numerous hydrophobic residues, specifically Tyr-59, His-57, Ala-56, Leu-99, Ser-96, Thr-98, Asn-97, Gln-175, Trp-215, Ser-214, Ser-195, Gln-192, Gly-219, Gly-216, Ser-190, and Cys-220. This detailed map confirms the involvement of Trp-215 and Tyr-59 in the interaction.

caption: Reverse polarographic diagram of the welded joint, providing a comprehensive overview of the crystallographic orientation distribution across the weldment.
summary: The reverse polarographic diagram summarizes the orientation characteristics of the welded joint. Analysis across the original and repair-welded specimens reveals that while the weld center maintains BCC martensitic and ferritic structures, the texture is significantly influenced by the repair length, specifically through the development of columnar crystal regions.

caption: Normal distribution of first nearest neighbor distances for Ni60Cr40 alloy, showing reduced bond distance and standard deviation compared to the Mo-containing variant.
summary: The normal distribution of first nearest neighbor distances for the Ni60Cr40 alloy is presented here. Comparing this to the Ni60Cr35Mo5 alloy shows that the Ni60Cr40 alloy has smaller average bond distances and lower standard deviations, confirming that the addition of Mo effectively increases lattice distortion due to its larger atomic size.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of unmodified chitosan, highlighting the characteristic signals of the polysaccharide chain.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of unmodified chitosan serves as a reference for the polysaccharide structure. It displays signals arising from the anomeric protons of the polysaccharide chain, typically found between 4.5 and 5.1 ppm, providing a baseline for evaluating subsequent chemical modifications like methacrylation in the chitosan derivative.

caption: Surface construction of the internal channel voids within an as-printed AlSi10Mg sample, highlighting discontinuities as potential obstructions with yellow boundaries.
summary: This panel displays the internal channel voids of an as-printed AlSi10Mg sample using micro-CT imaging. The surface construction reveals structural discontinuities within the channels, which are identified as potential obstructions and highlighted with yellow boundaries to facilitate the analysis of the internal geometry of the printed material.

caption: Atomic configuration following 8 × 10^8 MC/MD swaps at 523 K, illustrating the structural state corresponding to the conditions described in Figure 3.
summary: Representing the atomic structure after 8 × 10^8 MC/MD swaps at 523 K, this snapshot provides insight into the material's configuration post-processing. This state is directly linked to the experimental consistency observed in the study, where MD simulations align with the measured decrease in the dσc/dT value.

caption: Cu–Ni binary alloy phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic equilibrium states for the copper-nickel system.
summary: The Cu–Ni binary phase diagram provides the equilibrium thermodynamic data for the copper-nickel system. As part of the broader analysis of binary systems, this diagram characterizes the solubility and phase stability of the alloy, contributing to the understanding of how these elements behave when combined in metallurgical processes.

caption: Thermal dilation curve of the LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V alloy sample subjected to a heat treatment temperature of 1000 ℃.
summary: This panel displays the thermal dilation curve for an LPBF-ed Ti-6Al-4V alloy sample after heat treatment at 1000 ℃. The curve characterizes the dimensional changes of the material during the thermal dilation test, providing essential data on the phase transformation process occurring at this specific elevated temperature.

caption: Quantitative map of PC1 values derived from M-SVR modeling, illustrating the dependence of microstructural state on service time, stress, and temperature.
summary: This panel displays the M-SVR predicted PC1 values, which exhibit a strong global downward trend as service time and stress increase at a constant temperature. The data allows for the determination of rafting process completion times and provides evidence of the PC1 interval between adjacent service temperatures.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics of titanium felt PTLs coated with Ti 72 Nb 28 via PVD.
summary: This panel illustrates the current-voltage behavior of titanium felt porous transport layers coated with Ti 72 Nb 28 using physical vapor deposition. The I-V curve provides essential electrochemical performance data for the titanium felt substrate, serving as a baseline for evaluating the impact of the PVD coating on overall cell efficiency.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization M(T) of as-quenched ribbons measured under static magnetic fields of 5 mT and 5 T, illustrating the magnetic response across the temperature range.
summary: The temperature-dependent magnetization data, M(T), for as-quenched ribbons is presented for magnetic fields of 5 mT and 5 T. The plot displays the magnetic behavior of the as-quenched material, with ZFC, FC, and FH protocols indicated by arrows to track the magnetization response as a function of temperature.

caption: Volume fraction of the γ′ phase in the Ni-Al binary alloy calculated via phase-field simulation during aging heat treatment.
summary: The volume fraction of the γ′ phase is presented as a function of aging temperature and time. The phase-field module effectively captures the influence of elastic interactions between adjacent precipitates and the replacement of the anti-phase boundary by a thin γ phase, providing an accurate representation of the phase evolution.

caption: Feature importance analysis for architected beams with a slenderness ratio L/h = 8, evaluating the influence of modes [1,10] on mechanical performance.
summary: This feature importance plot identifies the key variables influencing the dynamic mechanical performance of architected beams with a slenderness ratio of L/h = 8. By analyzing modes [1,10], the plot quantifies the relative contribution of different features, offering insights into the structural parameters that most significantly impact the beam's mechanical behavior.

caption: Density of states profile for the V-doped TiNi3–V3/C interface.
summary: The density of states for the TiNi3–V3/C interface is presented. This visualization allows for the assessment of how V doping affects the electronic environment at the interface, providing insights into the resulting changes in band structure and electrical conductivity relative to the undoped TiNi3/C system.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase fraction plot for NA 625 as a function of temperature, generated using Thermo-Calc software and the TCNi11 database.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the equilibrium phase fractions for NA 625 across a range of temperatures. Calculated using the TCNi11 database, the plot serves as a critical reference for selecting appropriate solution annealing temperatures, highlighting the persistence of MC precipitates below 1200°C and the risk of rapid grain growth at higher temperatures.

caption: Representative 3D micro-CT reconstructions of AM and HAM specimens, where internal pores are color-coded based on their surface area.
summary: Representative 3D micro-CT reconstructions illustrate the internal pore characteristics of AM and HAM specimens. Pores are color-coded to represent their surface area, revealing that higher pore densities are observed at both low and high scan speeds for both sample types, providing a clear visualization of internal structural variations.

caption: EBSD pole figure illustrating the crystallographic texture of the TA15 titanium alloy matrix.
summary: This EBSD pole figure displays the crystallographic orientation distribution of the TA15 titanium alloy. It serves as a baseline reference for understanding the texture characteristics of the material before the incorporation of reinforcement phases, providing essential data for analyzing the microstructural evolution of the alloy system.

caption: Laboratory photograph displaying the physical arrangement of the high-speed imaging (HSI) camera and the illumination laser relative to the cladding zone.
summary: The laboratory photograph provides a visual overview of the experimental cladding setup. It specifically highlights the positioning of the HSI camera and the illumination laser, which are essential components for monitoring the process dynamics during the laser metal wire cladding experiments described in the study.

caption: Infrared spectrum of NiTi nanoparticles modified with COOH-PA, highlighting the CH region after rinsing and sonication, with asymmetric and symmetric CH2 peaks observed at 2916 cm-1 and 2847 cm-1.
summary: The FTIR spectrum for COOH-PA modified NiTi nanoparticles is presented here. After the rinsing and sonication process, the CH stretching region exhibits distinct asymmetric and symmetric CH2 peaks at 2916 cm-1 and 2847 cm-1, providing evidence of the chemical attachment of the COOH-PA molecules to the nanoparticle surface.

caption: Vickers surface hardness comparison between CoCr and surface-hardened titanium samples.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of Vickers surface hardness values for CoCr and surface-hardened titanium specimens. The data highlights the final achieved hardness conditions for these materials, providing a clear quantitative assessment of their mechanical surface properties as determined through standard Vickers indentation testing methods.

caption: Thermal expansion coefficient of 3D printed CB-PLA polymer plotted as a function of temperature.
summary: This plot illustrates the thermal expansion coefficient of 3D printed CB-PLA polymer across a range of temperatures. The data, derived from experimental measurements previously reported in the literature, characterizes the material's dimensional response to thermal changes, providing essential information for understanding the thermal stability and performance of the printed polymer structure.

caption: Uniaxial strain versus time curves for compound specimens, comparing experimental creep test data with fitted results derived from inversed material properties.
summary: This plot displays the uniaxial strain versus time behavior for compound specimens subjected to creep testing. The experimental data are compared against fitted curves generated using inversed properties. The results demonstrate that the fitting procedure achieves a reasonably accurate representation of the two creep tests performed on the specimens.

caption: Fourier transforms of the EXAFS oscillations and corresponding structural fits for each sample at the Ni K-edge.
summary: Fourier transforms of the Ni K-edge EXAFS oscillations are presented with their respective structural fits. These results confirm the presence of the β1-NiZn phase, offering detailed insights into the local atomic configuration and coordination of nickel atoms, which is vital for understanding the material's overall phase composition.

caption: Melt pool depth measurements for laser surface glazed Ti-6Al-4V-xB alloys as a function of boron concentration, including a linear regression fit.
summary: The variation of melt pool depths in laser surface glazed Ti-6Al-4V-xB alloys is presented as a function of boron concentration. The graph includes a dotted line representing the best-fit linear expression, which characterizes the relationship between the boron content and the resulting depth of the melt pool during processing.

caption: Tabulated summary of three distinct experimental groups, each defined by unique combinations of printing parameters used to evaluate the knowledge graph's recommendation efficiency.
summary: The table presents three distinct groups of experimental settings, each characterized by varying printing parameters. These groups serve as the basis for evaluating the practical efficiency of the knowledge graph in recommending optimal printing configurations, ensuring that the experimental data is systematically organized for subsequent analysis and knowledge graph updates.

caption: Clustering performance evaluation visualized through the first two principal components of the distance-related features, confirming the separation of the two data clusters.
summary: To evaluate the performance of the clustering process, the first two principal components of the distance-related features are plotted. This visualization confirms the effectiveness of the K-means algorithm in detecting and separating the two distinct clusters, providing a clear representation of the data distribution in the reduced principal component space.

caption: ToF-SIMS secondary ion depth profiles showing the intensity variation of ZnO-, CrO2-, and Ni2- species as a function of sputtering time on a passivated ZnNi alloy surface.
summary: ToF-SIMS secondary ion depth profiles for ZnO-, CrO2-, and Ni2- ions are presented for a passivated ZnNi alloy surface. These profiles illustrate the variation of ion intensity with sputtering time, which directly reflects the in-depth concentration of these specific chemical species within the trivalent chromium conversion coating.

caption: Diffraction rings observed at 2000 μm elongation, representing the final stage of the uniaxial to biaxial discontinuous strain path change.
summary: At 2000 μm elongation, the 2-D XRD intensity data shows the diffraction rings at the final stage of the discontinuous strain path. This observation provides a comprehensive view of the structural evolution in the central thinned regions of the sample after completing the full uniaxial to biaxial loading process.

caption: Specific Energy Absorption (SEA) integrated to 30% strain versus relative density, contrasting hollow-walled TPMS structures with conventional TPMS and other Ti–6Al–4V lattice architectures.
summary: This panel compares the Specific Energy Absorption (SEA) of hollow-walled TPMS lattices against other Ti–6Al–4V metamaterials. The results show a 170% increase in energy absorption for hollow-walled structures compared to conventional TPMS lattices, with values more than twice those of other reported Ti–6Al–4V lattices within the same density range.

caption: Poisson’s ratio as a function of strain, demonstrating the influence of symmetric cell number on the lateral deformation characteristics of the 3D EAC.
summary: The effect of symmetric cell number on the Poisson’s ratio of the 3D EAC is shown as a function of strain. This plot provides insight into how the structural geometry and cell count influence the lateral expansion or contraction behavior of the material during axial loading.

caption: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) trends for HT LW 4275 compared to reference superalloys across a range of elevated temperatures.
summary: The ultimate tensile strength of the LW 4275 alloy is evaluated against Rene 80 and IN 738, showing higher performance at 927 °C. The data indicates a consistent decreasing trend in ultimate tensile strength for all superalloys compared in this temperature-dependent mechanical performance analysis.

caption: Spheroidal morphology of fine γ′ precipitates in the 0.04P GH984G alloy following standard heat treatment.
summary: The 0.04P GH984G alloy maintains a spheroidal morphology of fine γ′ precipitates after standard heat treatment. TEM observations confirm that even at this higher phosphorus doping level, the morphology of the γ′ phase remains unaffected, demonstrating that P doping has no discernible effect on the precipitate shape in GH984G.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) evolution over time for as-built and heat-treated samples tested at a sliding speed of 0.125 m/s.
summary: This plot illustrates the COF progression for both as-built and heat-treated samples during a 0.125 m/s sliding experiment. The COF values for both conditions exhibit similar behavior, rising from 0.3 to 0.5 within the initial 800 seconds of the test before stabilizing at approximately 0.5 for the remainder of the process.

caption: Box plots illustrating the distribution of ellipticity (e) and area (A) of deposited melt spots as functions of laser focus position (ω), laser power (P), and exposure time (Δt).
summary: Box plots display the distribution of ellipticity and area for melt spots across varying laser focus positions, power levels, and exposure times. The whiskers represent the range excluding outliers, while the colored boxes denote the interquartile range, providing a clear visualization of data spread and median values for each processing parameter.

caption: Main effect plot illustrating the relationship between cutting speed and the resultant cutting force.
summary: This plot displays the main effect of cutting speed on the resultant cutting force. Experimental data indicates that increasing the cutting speed leads to a rise in the magnitude of the resultant cutting force. The mean values from three experimental trials were utilized to ensure accuracy and minimize potential errors.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern of the horizontally growing cells, further validating the <100> growth direction.
summary: Selected area electron diffraction pattern acquired from the horizontally growing cells validates the <100> growth orientation. This analysis confirms the crystallographic alignment of the cellular structures within the TiN/0.5/800 alloy, reinforcing the relationship between the observed lateral growth morphology and the specific <100> texture development during the solidification process.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy micrograph of the as-fabricated specimen, highlighting the dislocation density within the cellular structural regions.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the dislocation structures within the cellular regions of the as-fabricated specimen.
