The observed dislocation density is notably higher than that found in the HT02 heat-treated specimen, providing a clear visual representation of the internal lattice defects present in the as-fabricated material state.

caption: Ultimate compressive stress in MPa for NCHA formulations, highlighting superior strength in 40HA, 20HA, and 80HA compared to 100HA and 60HA.
summary: Compressive testing reveals that 40HA exhibits the highest ultimate stress at 0.498 MPa, significantly outperforming 60HA and 100HA. While 20HA also demonstrates high strength, it is not statistically different from 40HA. These findings indicate that specific NCHA formulations provide enhanced mechanical resistance under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Dispersion curves illustrating the phononic crystal pipe behavior at an axial location of x = 20 mm, calculated for an internal diameter of 70.55 mm.
summary: This panel displays the dispersion curves for a phononic crystal pipe with an internal diameter of 70.55 mm. The data is locally calculated at an axial position of 20 mm along the cone axis, providing essential information regarding the wave propagation characteristics within the specified phononic crystal structure.

caption: Rear wall morphological changes featuring large upper bulges that migrate downward, transition to upward movement in the middle, and undergo curling and contraction at the bottom.
summary: Large bulges on the upper part of the rear wall move downward after formation, subsequently shifting to an upward trajectory upon reaching the middle position. The bottom section of the wall exhibits complex behavior, curling backward initially before undergoing a forward contraction, as indicated by the dominant molten metal flow direction.

caption: Fatigue life data for stress-relieved specimens tested at 110 MPa, illustrating the influence of diverse surface processing techniques on cyclic loading resistance.
summary: Fatigue results for stress-relieved specimens are presented here, tested at a constant stress amplitude of 110 MPa. The plot highlights the effectiveness of various surface treatments in enhancing the fatigue durability of the material after the stress-relief process, demonstrating the comparative performance of different surface modification strategies under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Dummy tensile sample manufactured from PLA.
summary: A dummy tensile sample made of PLA is displayed. This component was printed following the resolution of major printing issues through calibration and parameter adjustments, showcasing the system's ability to produce functional test specimens for material characterization.

caption: Procedural workflow detailing the training process for the neural network parameterized HC fracture model.
summary: This panel outlines the procedural workflow detailing the training process for the neural network parameterized HC fracture model. As indicated by the reference, this schematic provides a clear overview of the training steps required to optimize the model, ensuring the neural network effectively captures the fracture behavior within the HC framework.

caption: TGA curve for the feedstock with 62 vol.% solid loading, exhibiting an intermediate mass loss of 6.9% and identifying maximum degradation speeds at 300 °C for PW and 450 °C for HDPE.
summary: Thermal analysis of the 62 vol.% feedstock reveals an intermediate mass loss of 6.9%. The data indicates specific degradation kinetics, with maximum degradation speeds occurring at 300 °C for the paraffin wax (PW) component and 450 °C for the HDPE matrix, guiding the design of subsequent printing cycles.

caption: Initial stage of molten droplet impact on the pool at t = 0.1915 s.
summary: This panel illustrates the initial phase of a molten droplet impacting a molten pool at 0.1915 s. The arc current is 220 A with a substrate rate of 6 mm/s. This image represents the beginning of a complete cycle of droplet impingement and subsequent morphological evolution within the molten pool system.

caption: Vacancy formation energies for the Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy at 300 K, plotted against the number of Ni atoms in the first coordination shell, demonstrating an increasing energy trend with constant Cr content.
summary: Vacancy formation energies for the Fe55Cr15Ni30 alloy at 300 K are plotted against the number of Ni atoms in the first coordination shell. The data reveals that the vacancy formation energy increases as a function of the number of Ni atoms in the first coordination shell when the number of Cr atoms remains constant.

caption: Raman spectra of pure PETG and PETG/RFPG composites with RFPG concentrations ranging from 2.0 wt% to 12.0 wt%.
summary: This panel displays the Raman spectra for pure PETG and various PETG/RFPG composites with filler concentrations between 2.0 wt% and 12.0 wt%. These spectroscopic measurements provide a comprehensive overview of the vibrational characteristics of the composite materials, facilitating the identification of chemical signatures across the different filler loading levels.

caption: BSE image of AS-30 specimen highlighting preferential intermetallic precipitation associated with rounded and finger-like austenite morphologies.
summary: The BSE image of the AS-30 specimen demonstrates preferential intermetallic precipitation occurring at rounded and finger-like austenite morphologies. These sites are associated with incoherent boundaries, reinforcing the observation that specific austenite morphologies act as early precipitation sites for intermetallics in the ferrite/austenite microstructure during the aging process.

caption: Arrhenius plots of total and partial tracer diffusion coefficients for Ni-20 at.%Fe alloy compared against pure Ni and Fe metals as a function of reciprocal temperature.
summary: Arrhenius plots illustrate the temperature dependence of tracer diffusion coefficients for Ni-20 at.%Fe alloy alongside pure Ni and Fe metals. By plotting ln(D*) versus 1/T, the figure provides a comparative analysis of total and partial diffusion rates, facilitating the determination of activation energies for the alloy system.

caption: Lattice strain evolution in the α phase of the DAT sample across different crystallographic planes during the loading process.
summary: This panel displays the lattice strain for various crystallographic planes within the α phase of the DAT sample. caption: Cu–Ni–Si composition profile resulting from the optimization process, highlighting the interface characteristics.
summary: Panel f illustrates the predicted composition profile for the Cu–Ni–Si system. It contributes to the overall assessment of the model's prediction performance. caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve of lime-metakaolin (MK) paste after 28 days of hydration.
summary: This TGA thermogram depicts the thermal decomposition of lime-MK paste at 28 days of hydration. Monitoring CH consumption at this stage allows for a comprehensive assessment of the hydration progress in the control sample.

caption: Differential pulse voltammetry curves for the simultaneous detection of dopamine, uric acid, and nitrite at varying concentrations using a 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode in 0.01 M PBS.
summary: Differential pulse voltammetry demonstrates the simultaneous detection of dopamine, uric acid, and nitrite using a 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode in 0.01 M PBS. caption: Overview of the Toshiba UVM-450C(V2) five-axis machining center used for micro milling experiments, featuring a high-precision resolution of 0.01 μm across the X, Y, and Z axes.
summary: This panel displays the Toshiba UVM-450C(V2) five-axis machining center utilized for the micro milling experimental setup. caption: Correlation plot illustrating the relationship between tensile and shear properties for the investigated samples.
summary: This plot depicts the relationship between tensile and shear properties for the selected samples. caption: Charging profile of a 33 µF capacitor powered by the barium titanate bridge under 500 Hz mechanical stimulation at varying oscillation amplitudes, with an inset showing the rectifier circuit.
summary: This panel shows the charging behavior of a 33 µF capacitor connected to the piezoelectric bridge via a rectifier circuit. The results demonstrate the energy harvesting capability of the device, where the charging rate is dependent on the oscillation amplitude of the mechanical stimulus applied at 500 Hz.

caption: O-K edge EELS spectra acquired at the top, middle, and bottom sections of Ti-rich A1 and Zr-rich A4 variants, showing distinct peak splitting in the A4 variant.
summary: This panel displays O-K edge EELS spectra for Ti-rich A1 and Zr-rich A4 variants at various film depths. caption: True stress-strain curves comparing the AB (blue) and 700-DS (red) samples, highlighting the absence of non-uniform deformation in the 700-DS specimen prior to failure.
summary: This true stress-strain plot compares the mechanical behavior of AB and 700-DS samples. The AB specimen exhibits a region of non-uniform deformation immediately preceding failure, which is notably absent in the 700-DS sample. These curves demonstrate distinct deformation characteristics between the two processing conditions under tensile loading.

summary: Typical friction coefficient fluctuation curves are depicted for pure resin and nanocomposite samples containing 0.5% and 8% alumina nanoparticles. summary: This panel displays the wear progression of the round groove sonotrode tip across three stages of cumulative weld seam length. caption: Photograph of Filament D wound on a bobbin, featuring a diameter of 0.4 mm.
summary: Filament D is shown wound on a bobbin with a diameter of 0.4 mm. caption: Improvement in fatigue life for all treated specimens compared to the as-built (AB) state.
summary: This panel illustrates the improvement in fatigue life for all treated specimens compared to the as-built (AB) state. caption: Partial dependence plots illustrating the relationship between four surface parameters and the predicted probability of keyhole mode formation, with the y-axis representing the mean probability.
summary: Partial dependence plots for four surface parameters are presented, showing their individual effects on the predicted probability of keyhole mode formation. caption: Box plot illustrating the distribution of R-squared values for Model 2 obtained through nested cross-validation on outer test folds, representing the model's predictive performance.
summary: This box plot displays the R-squared performance metrics for Model 2 using nested cross-validation on outer test folds. summary: This inverse pole figure map characterizes the microstructural features of the top area of the thin-wall sample. summary: This schematic illustrates the structural design of the CNN architecture implemented for supervised learning tasks. summary: Lattice parameter a plotted against measured Ag content, comparing experimental electron diffraction data with pure metal values and Vegard's law predictions. The plot illustrates the relationship between composition and lattice structure, showing how the measured values align with the expected behavior of a solid solution in the Cu-Ag system.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results detailing the matrix composition across the substrate, the interface region, and the printed wall layers.
summary: This panel displays energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results for the matrix material. The analysis covers the region from the substrate through the interface up to the fourth layers of the printed wall. These measurements provide a comprehensive chemical profile of the matrix across the different zones of the deposited sample.

caption: Hot processing map for WAAMed NiTi alloy at a true strain of 0.4, highlighting the distribution of flow instability regions.
summary: Representing the hot processing map at a true strain of 0.4, this plot identifies the flow instability region through gray shading. Consistent with the overall analysis, these unstable zones are predominantly located in the high strain rate regions, indicating potential processing challenges for the WAAMed NiTi alloy under these specific conditions.

caption: Hardness contour map overlaid on an SEM image of SLM AlSi10Mg, illustrating the spatial distribution of hardness across the FZ and MPB regions based on 10 nanoindentation indents within a 2 μm displacement.
summary: This hardness contour map, overlaid on an SEM image of SLM AlSi10Mg, visualizes the spatial distribution of mechanical properties across the FZ and MPB. By mapping 10 nanoindentation indents within a 2 μm displacement, the figure highlights local variations in hardness resulting from the underlying solidification microstructure of the material.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparing PEC-NH2 with PEC-genipin mixtures at varying crosslinking durations, specifically t=0, 3 days for the 1:0.6 ratio, and 6 days for the 1:1.5 and 1:3 ratios, highlighting a characteristic intermediate signal at 3.30 ppm.
summary: This figure displays 1H NMR spectra used to investigate the crosslinking mechanism between amino-modified pectin and genipin. By comparing spectra collected at different time intervals for various mixing ratios, the emergence of a specific signal at 3.30 ppm is identified, indicating the formation of reaction intermediates during the crosslinking process.

caption: Major strain distribution at nine points on the rigid physical plate, where upper points (P0–P2) exhibit strains below 0.007% and lower points (P6–P8) range from 0.01% to 0.02%.
summary: This panel illustrates the major strain values measured at nine distinct points on the rigid physical plate after 410 minutes. The results indicate a spatial variation in strain, with the upper section (P0 to P2) showing values below 0.007%, while the lower section (P6 to P8) displays higher values between 0.01% and 0.02%.

caption: Mass gain curves for Fe-25Cr-5Mo-0.99C and Fe-25Cr-21Ni-5Mo-0.91C alloys during oxidation at 800 °C, 900 °C, and 1000 °C, with an inset showing calculated activation energies.
summary: This plot displays the oxidation kinetics of two Fe-based alloys, showing mass gain over time at three temperatures. The curves demonstrate similar parabolic oxidation behavior for both materials. An inset provides the calculated activation energies derived from an Arrhenius-type relation, confirming that oxidation rates are comparable across the tested alloy compositions.

caption: Engineering compressive characteristics of the as-fabricated N-doped titanium samples.
summary: Engineering compressive features of the as-fabricated N-doped titanium are illustrated. These characteristics provide insight into the mechanical response of the material under compressive loading conditions, reflecting the influence of the shielding gas and the resulting microstructural modifications on the overall compressive performance of the N-doped titanium specimens.

caption: Calculated liquidus lines for the Cu-Ni-Pb system at 0, 10, 20, 30, and 38 wt% Pb, plotted as a function of temperature versus nickel composition (wt%).
summary: This plot displays calculated liquidus lines for the Cu-Ni-Pb ternary system across various lead concentrations. It compares results from the current study against parameter sets by Miettinen et al. and Wang et al., while overlaying experimental data from Pelzel to evaluate the accuracy of the thermodynamic models.

caption: Normal spectral reflectance curves for polycrystalline Al2O3, Cr2O3, SiO2, and rutile TiO2 measured at room temperature within the solar spectral region.
summary: This plot displays the normal spectral reflectance curves for polycrystalline Al2O3, Cr2O3, SiO2, and rutile TiO2 at room temperature. These data, extracted from literature, characterize the optical behavior of these oxides in the solar spectral region, highlighting their distinct reflectance profiles relevant to understanding their optical properties in coating applications.

caption: Oxidation cyclic voltammogram of the 3-bisPh-B compound.
summary: This panel presents the oxidation cyclic voltammogram for the 3-bisPh-B compound. By analyzing the current response during the oxidation sweep, the electrochemical characteristics of the material are determined. These results complement the reduction data to define the overall redox potential profile of the derivative as reported in Table 2.

caption: Differential Raman spectra obtained by subtracting the pure PETG signal from the total Raman spectra of PETG/RFPG composites (0.0 wt%–12.0 wt%).
summary: Presented here is the outcome of subtracting the neat PETG spectrum from the total Raman spectra of the PETG/RFPG composites. This differential analysis isolates the spectral contributions of the RFPG filler within the polymer matrix, allowing for a clearer observation of the specific Raman bands associated with the filler material.

caption: Entropic potential profiles of NMC622 coin cells plotted against open-circuit voltage during the lithiation process at a C/10 rate.
summary: This panel illustrates the entropic potential of NMC622 coin cells as a function of open-circuit voltage during lithiation at a C/10 rate. Similar to the delithiation results, the entropic potential profiles for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted electrodes show overlapping behavior with negligible discrepancy during the lithiation process.

caption: SHAP summary plot illustrating the influence of input variables on the joint shear capacity prediction for the GEP model.
summary: The SHAP summary plot for the GEP model visualizes how individual input variables contribute to the predicted joint shear capacity (Fmax). This analysis provides insight into the feature importance and the direction of influence each variable exerts on the model's output, facilitating a better understanding of the underlying predictive mechanism.

caption: HT-CLSM snapshot of the 7 m solutionised high B & C variant at the initial state before significant heating.
summary: This HT-CLSM snapshot displays the initial microstructure of the 7 m solutionised high B & C variant. The observed microstructure remains stable and unchanged at temperatures below 1150 °C, serving as the baseline state for the subsequent in-situ heating experiment conducted at a rate of approximately 80 °C/min.

caption: HR-MAS NMR spectra comparing the chitosan-based hydrogel CS-AD-1 with a physical cross-linked control, featuring 1H spectra for both and a 13C spectrum for the seaweed-crosslinked sample.
summary: High-resolution magic angle spinning NMR spectroscopy confirms covalent bond formation in the CS-AD-1 hydrogel. Panel A displays 1H spectra for the CS-AD-1 hydrogel and a physical cross-linked control, alongside a 13C spectrum for the seaweed-crosslinked hydrogel. A shoulder peak in the 13C spectrum specifically identifies the covalent cross-linking sites.

caption: Self-discharge performance curves for Cu–Ni coated electrodes, showing voltage decay over time for samples electrodeposited at constant voltages between −1.2 V and −1.8 V.
summary: Self-discharge curves for Cu–Ni coated electrodes are presented to evaluate charge retention. The results demonstrate that decreasing the electrodeposition voltage leads to lower self-discharge performance. This indicates that the deposition conditions directly impact the stability and resistance to capacitance leakage in the fabricated Cu–Ni alloy electrode materials.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of Ni5P4-Co2P nanowires synthesized under optimized conditions compared to control samples.
summary: The XRD pattern of the Ni5P4-Co2P nanowires (red line) confirms the successful synthesis of the target phosphide phases. In contrast, the blue line shows that without red phosphorus, only Co3O4 and NiO phases form on the NCF surface, indicating that Co2P acts as the essential nucleation center for nanowire growth.

caption: Advanced build stage at 120 mm height, where continued structural growth drives further elevation of the mass centre.
summary: Representing the cylinder at a 120 mm build height, this panel illustrates the ongoing structural growth. As additional welding layers are deposited following the contour toolpath, the mass centre continues to rise, demonstrating the direct relationship between the evolving geometry of the build and the shifting mass distribution.

caption: High-magnification bright-field STEM micrograph of a 20 at% Ag PVD sample, where red arrows indicate twin boundaries (TBs) and orange arrows indicate grain boundaries.
summary: High-magnification bright-field STEM micrograph of a 20 at% Ag PVD sample, where red arrows indicate twin boundaries (TBs) and orange arrows indicate grain boundaries. This detailed view allows for the identification and quantification of specific internal structural features like TBs and grain boundaries within the dealloyed material.

caption: Comparison of theoretical and experimental RL curves for GMSs, highlighting the first-order interference EAP frequency differences between AO and DO gradient structures.
summary: The first-order interference EAP frequency of the AO gradient structure is observed to be higher than that of the DO gradient structure in both theoretical calculations and experimental measurements. This panel provides a direct comparison of these RL curves to validate the theoretical model against experimental data.

caption: Distribution of the 77 numbered grains plotted within the standard IPF-Z triangle, where each data point represents a specific grain's orientation and its color-coded marker indicates the associated post-corrosion morphology type.
summary: The IPF-Z triangle plot maps the crystallographic orientations of the 77 grains identified in panel (a). Each numbered spot corresponds to a specific grain, with its spatial location representing the orientation and its color indicating the post-corrosion morphology type, thereby establishing a statistical correlation between orientation and corrosion behavior.

caption: Orbegozo Mig 2130 microwave oven with grill, utilized for the thermal post-curing of specimens.
summary: Orbegozo Mig 2130 Microwave with Grill, featuring a 20 L capacity and 700 W power output, is displayed as the apparatus for thermal post-curing. This equipment is essential for the post-processing stage, providing the necessary heat treatment to finalize the curing of the manufactured resin specimens.

caption: Voltage profiles of Li plating/stripping processes for LNPs-CFC and control electrodes using Li as the reference/counter electrode.
summary: Voltage profiles obtained during Li plating and stripping processes reveal that the LNPs-CFC electrode maintains smaller nucleation and plateau overpotentials compared to control electrodes. These results, supported by data across various current densities, indicate more efficient lithium deposition and stripping kinetics facilitated by the LNPs-CFC structural design.

caption: Low-magnification EBSD inverse pole figure and image quality maps of the Ni-based CMSX-4 superalloy, highlighting the [001] growth direction orientation.
summary: This panel presents a low-magnification EBSD inverse pole figure and image quality map for a Ni-based CMSX-4 superalloy. The material is oriented in the [001] growth direction, as indicated by the inset value. These maps provide essential crystallographic orientation data for the single crystal superalloy used in the investigation.

caption: Joint efficiency plotted against the Larson-Miller parameter for A6063/304SS joints processed at a forge pressure of 240 MPa.
summary: This graph displays the joint efficiency versus the Larson-Miller parameter for A6063/304SS joints produced at a higher forge pressure of 240 MPa. Consistent with the observed trend, the joint efficacy undergoes a notable reduction once the Larson-Miller parameter exceeds the established threshold value for this specific forge pressure condition.

caption: Elongation to failure plotted against hydrogen pressure for conventional specimens (CS) and hollow specimens (HS), modeled using an exponential growth function.
summary: This plot illustrates the elongation to failure as a function of hydrogen pressure for both conventional and hollow specimens. The data is fitted with an exponential growth function incorporating a time constant. Notably, the hollow specimens tested in air exhibit lower elongation to failure compared to the conventional specimens.

caption: Normalized H2 capacity as a function of cycle number for the annealed, 2#, and 3# alloys, with values normalized to their respective fully activated capacities.
summary: This plot illustrates the normalized hydrogen capacity versus cycle number for the annealed, 2#, and 3# alloys. By normalizing the data to the fully activated capacity values, the graph provides a direct comparison of the cycling stability and capacity retention characteristics across the different alloy compositions tested.

caption: HAADF-STEM image focusing on a Cr-rich region within the Type-II inclusion, highlighting contrast differences relative to the matrix.
summary: Detailed analysis of a Cr-rich area within the Type-II inclusion is presented using HAADF-STEM. The image reveals distinct contrast differences between the inclusion's Cr-rich region and the surrounding matrix. This specific location was selected to investigate the local microstructural features and chemical composition of the inclusion in greater detail.

caption: Experimental setup of an orthogonal two-wavelength DLP printer featuring two Wintech PRO-6500 light engines, each integrated with a 1080p DMD and configured for 365 nm UV and 460 nm blue light emission.
summary: This photograph displays the laboratory-scale orthogonal two-wavelength DLP printing system. The setup utilizes two commercial Wintech PRO-6500 light engines, each equipped with a 0.65-inch 1080p DMD. These engines are specifically configured to operate at 365 nm UV and 460 nm blue wavelengths to facilitate dual-wavelength additive manufacturing processes.

caption: Detected image reflected from the device with the quarter-wave plate QWP2 set to 30 degrees.
summary: Reflected pattern captured at a QWP2 angle of 30 degrees demonstrates the device's alignment capabilities. Analysis of this image confirms that the reflected pattern coincides with the original calibration image with subpixel accuracy, indicating that the mechanical rotation of the QWP2 does not negatively impact the alignment of acquired images.

caption: SHAP dependence plot illustrating the influence of thickness on residual stress predictions along the step direction σy.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the effect of thickness on residual stress predictions along the step direction σy. Each dot represents a single prediction, with the x-axis showing the feature value and the y-axis representing the SHAP value in MPa, colored by the strongest interacting feature.

caption: Turbidimetry measurements of the sample at a concentration of 1 mg mL-1, presented as normalized transmittance to evaluate the thermoresponsive behavior of CS and KC materials.
summary: Turbidimetry measurements at a concentration of 1 mg mL-1 are used to examine the thermoresponsive behavior of CS and KC materials. The data, presented as normalized transmittance, reveal variations in the cloud point among the reference, upper layer, and lower layer, providing a straightforward method for assessing material response.

caption: Free energy pathway for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), highlighting the energetic preference for water dissociation on the oxidized surface.
summary: The alkaline HER pathway shows that the water dissociation process (H2O to H + OH) is energetically preferred on the partially oxidized Ru-Ni surface. The reaction gains -0.28 eV during bond cleavage, confirming the surface's effectiveness in facilitating the initial steps of the hydrogen evolution reaction.

caption: Time-dependent luminescence intensity profiles comparing LMEI-MFC systems utilizing pure water versus water containing the ionic liquid [BMIM][FeCl4].
summary: This plot illustrates the emission intensity trends observed during the operation of LMEI-MFC trials. By comparing systems using pure water against those incorporating the ionic liquid [BMIM][FeCl4], the data highlights the impact of the electrolyte composition on the luminescence performance throughout the duration of the experimental testing process.

caption: Comparative aspect ratio distributions for micro-defects (peak I: 3.75–6.25 µm) and macro-defects (peak II: 28.75–31.25 µm).
summary: The aspect ratio distributions for the primary and secondary defect peaks are compared to evaluate differences in pore morphology. By isolating defects within the 3.75–6.25 µm and 28.75–31.25 µm ranges, this analysis assesses whether micro-pores and macro-defects exhibit distinct shape characteristics within the processed material.

caption: Propagating rupture front visualized under applied normal stress σap/μ = −0.01 and shear stress τap/μ = 0.1 for a material parameter κ = 0.695.
summary: This simulation snapshot illustrates the propagation of a rupture front under specific normal and shear stress conditions. With κ set to 0.695, the rupture front dynamics are driven by the defined stress parameters, providing insight into the material's response to the applied mechanical loading conditions during the simulation process.

caption: Yield strength as a function of relative density, comparing numerical predictions for stochastic and periodic lattice samples against Gibson-Ashby scaling models.
summary: Yield strength values are plotted against relative density to evaluate the mechanical performance of cellular structures. The graph utilizes numerical data from defect-free lattice simulations, applying Gibson-Ashby power law fits to characterize the scaling behavior of both stochastic and periodic samples, providing a clear comparison of their structural efficiency.

caption: Current density waveforms for the HiPIMS discharge, comparing the magnetron target current density (Jd) and the substrate current density (Js) normalized to the holder surface area.
summary: Current density waveforms illustrate the HiPIMS discharge characteristics, where the target peak current density Jd reaches approximately 1 A/cm2 at a peak target current of 21 A. The substrate current density Js is normalized to the surface area of the holder to represent the ion flux reaching the substrate surface.

caption: Synchrotron XRD intensity profile of the α-AlFeMnSi (013) reference peak during heating at a rate of 0.03 K s⁻¹.
summary: The panel illustrates the synchrotron XRD intensity profile for the α-AlFeMnSi (013) reference peak during a heating experiment at 0.03 K s⁻¹. The data is characterized by significant noise, resulting from the low phase fraction and limited signal intensity observed during the experimental measurement process.

caption: Pseudobinary section of the Fe–Cr–Ni system at a constant iron concentration, illustrating phase stability regions.
summary: This pseudobinary section of the Fe–Cr–Ni system, maintained at a constant iron concentration, serves as a critical tool for predicting solidification modes and final microstructures in stainless steels. By mapping phase stability, it reflects the relative influence of alloying elements, specifically the chromium and nickel equivalents, on material behavior.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the reference hydrated ordinary Portland cement (OPC) paste at 28 days of curing.
summary: This panel displays the XRD pattern for the reference hydrated OPC paste at 28 days. The pattern serves as a baseline for comparing the mineralogical composition of cement pastes modified with calcite-rich stream additions, consistent with the chemical and mineralogical characteristics of hydrated OPC.

caption: Fe 2p XPS spectrum of the passive film formed on FeCrTi alloy after chronoamperometry at 0.100 V for 3600 s in 3.5 wt % NaCl.
summary: The Fe 2p XPS spectrum for the FeCrTi alloy is displayed, characterizing the iron chemical state in the passive film after a 3600 s chronoamperometry test at 0.100 V in 3.5 wt % NaCl. This spectroscopic data helps assess the surface chemistry of the titanium-modified alloy under these electrochemical conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the disk-type tribometer configuration used for friction testing.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the experimental setup of a disk-type tribometer. The figure provides a clear visual representation of the mechanical configuration employed for friction testing, serving as a foundational reference for the tribological evaluation methodology described in the study to assess material performance under controlled contact conditions.

caption: Relationship between density and bulk sound velocity for hcp Fe-Si alloys at 360 GPa and 0 K, where colors indicate silicon concentration levels.
summary: This panel displays the density and bulk sound velocity relationship for hcp Fe-Si alloys at 360 GPa and 0 K. Silicon concentrations are mapped by color, and the solid line shows the trend in the binary system. Silicon is identified as having a significant effect on increasing the bulk sound velocity.

caption: Zeta potential measurements comparing bare carbon cloth and carbon cloth with deposited Ni-Co alloys, illustrating surface charge characteristics.
summary: The zeta potential diagram reveals that at pH 2, the cathode surface becomes positively charged (3.33 mV) due to protonation, creating a repulsive effect against Ni2+ and Co2+ ions. Furthermore, Ni-Co alloy deposition results in a more positive electrode potential, leading to increased rejection of metal ions during electrodeposition.

caption: Distributions and mean values of azimuthal angles φ1 and φ2 relative to build height, derived from Monte-Carlo calculations considering principal stress symmetry.
summary: This plot displays the azimuthal angles φ1 and φ2 associated with in-plane principal stresses σ1 and σ2 across the build height. Monte-Carlo simulations reveal mean values of 91° ± 9° and 0.1° ± 9°, respectively, reflecting scan strategies aligned with the x and y axes of the sample coordinate system.

caption: Elemental distribution maps of SLM-fabricated Zr52.5Ti5Cu17.9Ni14.6Al10 BMGs, highlighting the homogeneity of constituent elements under various scanning parameters.
summary: Elemental mapping demonstrates the distribution of constituent elements within the melt pool of SLM-fabricated BMGs. Results show that scanning strategy III promotes a more homogenous elemental distribution due to increased melt flow, which effectively enhances the formation of amorphous structures compared to other tested scanning strategies.

caption: Composite thermally treated at 280 °C showing the emergence of discrete diffraction spots in SAED, clearer particle boundaries in TEM, and disordered, weak lattice fringes in HRTEM, indicating the onset of partial crystallization.
summary: Thermal treatment at 280 °C initiates partial crystallization in the PEEK composite. The SAED pattern displays discrete diffraction spots, while HRTEM reveals emerging lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.23 nm and 0.31 nm. TEM images show improved particle boundary definition compared to the room temperature state.

caption: Temperature programmed reaction profile of FeNi3@SBA-15 showing methane conversion efficiency across a temperature range.
summary: The temperature programmed reaction profile for FeNi3@SBA-15 illustrates its catalytic performance. Reactivity test results indicate that this material achieves a methane conversion rate of approximately 75% at 600°C, which increases significantly to 98% at 800°C, demonstrating high catalytic activity for the reaction within the tested temperature range.

caption: Thermal desorption spectroscopy (TDS) spectra of the H1000 material state, showing hydrogen release intensity as a function of temperature across varying heating rates from 130 K/min to 230 K/min.
summary: This panel displays TDS spectra for the H1000 material state, illustrating the effect of heating rates ranging from 130 K/min to 230 K/min on hydrogen desorption. These spectra are essential for assessing trapping energies, as the peak shifts observed at different heating rates provide the necessary data for subsequent kinetic analysis.

caption: Overview of the European standardisation framework for steel construction, highlighting the integration of new DED-Arc specific standards and rules within existing product, design, execution, and testing protocols.
summary: This schematic illustrates the European standardisation system for steel construction, encompassing product standards, Eurocodes for structural design, and execution protocols. Proposed additions for DED-Arc components, marked in red, include new product standards, structural design rules for EC3, and specific execution requirements for geometric tolerances and classes, facilitating their industrial adoption.

caption: Performance curves showing I-V and I-P relationships for single cells with diverse anodes, evaluated at 700 °C using methanol as the fuel source.
summary: This panel presents the electrochemical performance of single cells using methanol fuel at 700 °C. The I-V and I-P curves demonstrate the power density and voltage characteristics of the various anode configurations, highlighting their effectiveness in converting methanol fuel into electrical energy under high-temperature operating conditions.

caption: Close-up view of the inverse magnetic susceptibility 1/χ' versus temperature derived from the inset of panel (a), illustrating the linear extrapolation to the x-axis at a Curie temperature of 6.4 K.
summary: This panel provides a detailed view of the inverse magnetic susceptibility data between 25 and 50 K. Graphical extrapolation of the linear section of the 1/χ' versus temperature curve to the x-axis intercept yields a Curie temperature of 6.4 K, consistent with the Curie constant of 0.175 K obtained via fitting.

caption: Comprehensive workflow diagram illustrating the general adaptive sampling process and the three-step optimisation procedure utilized to construct the NURBS-based metamodel.
summary: This flowchart outlines the methodology for generating a NURBS-based metamodel through a three-step optimization process. It incorporates an adaptive sampling technique to iteratively determine the number of Target Points (TPs) within the training dataset, ensuring an efficient and accurate representation of the underlying physical system being modeled.

caption: Temporal evolution of the curved part position in the AA cross-section from 0 to 0.32 s.
summary: The AA cross-section provides an XY-direction view of the curved part from 0 to 0.32 s at 0.04 s intervals. The component is divided into four distinct regions labeled R I, R II, R III, and R IV, illustrating the spatial trajectory of the part during the initial simulation stage.

caption: Quantitative EDS result table summarizing the elemental composition detected within the analyzed zone of the SS-PREP particle.
summary: The quantitative EDS result table provides the final elemental composition derived from the spectral analysis of the SS-PREP Ni-11Mo-8Al-3Ta-2Cr-1Re particle. This data confirms the presence and relative concentrations of the constituent elements within the detected zone, completing the characterization process as reported in the study's findings.

caption: Von Mises stress distribution within the L1 layer atoms, accompanied by a partial enlarged region.
summary: This visualization details the Von Mises stress distribution within the L1 layer. Consistent with the composite-level findings, the maximum stress values are localized at the mismatch of dislocation lines. This stress concentration indicates that dislocations are unstable and may trigger dislocation reactions during shock loading conditions.

caption: Surface topography of the Mg-8Li-4Gd alloy captured via atomic force microscopy.
summary: Atomic force microscopy reveals the surface topography of the Mg-8Li-4Gd alloy. This characterization technique provides a detailed view of the surface morphology, serving as the baseline for subsequent potential distribution analysis of the alloy's constituent phases, specifically the α-Mg and β-Li phases present in the material.

caption: Frequency distribution of holding times employed during the spark plasma sintering process for the fabrication of bulk RHEA components.
summary: The histogram depicts the frequency of holding times used in the SPS consolidation of RHEAs. This data characterizes the temporal parameters typically chosen in powder metallurgy fabrication, reflecting the common processing durations required to successfully consolidate bulk refractory high-entropy alloy parts using spark plasma sintering techniques.

caption: Shrinkage behavior of pristine glass particles measured via optical dilatometry, illustrating the densification process used to establish the sintering cycle.
summary: Optical dilatometry analysis of pristine glass particles reveals the shrinkage behavior during heating. The data indicates an initial shrinkage event between 450 and 500 °C, associated with the glass transition temperature, and a maximum shrinkage observed near 900 °C, providing the necessary basis for determining the optimal sintering cycle for the glass pellets.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the apparent activation energy (Ea) for the glycerol electro-oxidation reaction (GEOR) on PdNi/Ni at potentials near the onset, where values range from 38.1 to 27.8 kJ mol-1 and exhibit a linear decrease as electrode potential increases.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the apparent activation energy for GEOR on PdNi/Ni at potentials near the onset. The data demonstrates a clear trend where Ea values decrease linearly from 38.1 to 27.8 kJ mol-1 as the electrode potential increases, reflecting the electrochemical kinetics in the lower current density region.

caption: Strain concentration map obtained via DIC analysis for the RS-UR specimen.
summary: The RS-UR specimen is analyzed using DIC to visualize strain concentrations before peak load. Colored regions in the map indicate the presence of fine cracks or areas where horizontal strain is concentrated, offering insight into the damage evolution and mechanical performance of this specific TPRCC specimen configuration.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of SLM-fabricated steel showing carbides precipitated between α’-laths.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the SLM-fabricated steel confirms the presence of dispersed nanosized carbides precipitated between the α'-laths of the bainitic matrix. Compared to the wrought sample, this specimen exhibits relatively coarse, sparsely distributed carbides, resulting in the lowest total phase boundary area and dislocation density among the analyzed samples.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph and inset SAED pattern of Ni56Ti41Hf3 alloy aged at 550 °C for 4 h, revealing Ni4Ti3 precipitates, H-phase, and cubic Ni-rich precipitates.
summary: This BF-TEM micrograph and corresponding SAED pattern illustrate the microstructure of Ni56Ti41Hf3 after solution annealing, preaging, and aging. The image displays larger Ni4Ti3 precipitates with reduced strain contrast, alongside densely packed H-phase and cubic Ni-rich precipitates. Diffraction patterns confirm the presence of these distinct phases through specific super-reflections.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of gold nanoparticles derived from TEM measurements.
summary: The particle size distribution histogram illustrates the statistical size range of the gold nanoparticles. Based on TEM measurements, the particles exhibit an average diameter of 16 ± 0.5 nm. This distribution confirms the uniformity of the synthesized nanoparticles, aligning well with established experimental findings for this specific gold nanoparticle preparation.

caption: Magnified segment of the SXRD diffractograms highlighting specific peak regions to facilitate the comparison of phase characteristics across different heat treatment durations and deformation states.
summary: Enlarged segments of the SXRD diffractograms are presented to clarify the complex peak features. These patterns, collected at fracture tips, exhibit low intensity and broad profiles. The overlap of peak positions from multiple phases makes interpretation challenging, necessitating this detailed view to compare the structural evolution of the material.

caption: Low-magnification EPMA-WDS elemental mapping of the as-cast TiZrHfCr0.2Mo bio-HEA.
summary: Low-magnification EPMA-WDS elemental mapping of the as-cast TiZrHfCr0.2Mo bio-HEA reveals the distribution of constituent elements. Analysis of the map indicates that chromium enrichment occurs specifically within the inter-dendrite regions of the alloy microstructure, providing a broad overview of the elemental segregation present in the as-cast state.

caption: Chemical composition comparison of TR-316L and LPBF-316L stainless steel variants expressed in weight percentages.
summary: This table presents the chemical composition of TR-316L and LPBF-316L materials in weight percentages. It provides a direct comparison of the elemental constituents for both processing conditions, serving as the primary reference for the chemical makeup of the specimens investigated in this study.

caption: EPMA line scan profile detailing the elemental distribution of Ni and Cr in the deposited layer following preheating at 500 °C.
summary: Shown is the EPMA line scan profile for the deposited layer after 500 °C preheating. The scan path demonstrates the distribution of Ni and Cr. Results confirm that the Ni- and Cr-depleted zones on the side of the layer close to the substrate further increase in size with this higher preheating temperature.

caption: Pseudo-time analysis of iPSCs and endoderm lineage cells categorized by specific cell types.
summary: This panel categorizes iPSCs and endoderm lineage cells to visualize their specific positions within the pseudo-time framework. The investigation demonstrates that precursor cells located in the apical areas of several branches are responsible for the subsequent formation of alveolar cells and mature endocrine cells during the differentiation process.

caption: Principal component analysis of macroscopic stress-strain curves from the test set, with data points colored by the L2 relative error of the predicted stress-strain curves.
summary: This panel displays a principal component analysis of macroscopic stress-strain curves derived from the test set. The visualization maps the first two principal components, with individual data points color-coded to represent the L2 relative error associated with the predicted stress-strain curves, highlighting the distribution of prediction accuracy across the dataset.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles measured at a current density of 0.5 mA cm⁻² for micro-supercapacitors with footprint areas of 0.12 cm² and 0.31 cm².
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves at 0.5 mA cm⁻² evaluate the energy storage behavior of micro-supercapacitors with footprint areas of 0.12 cm² and 0.31 cm². These measurements provide insight into the discharge characteristics and total capacitance of the devices, confirming the performance metrics associated with the different footprint sizes.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the carbide particle, confirming the M23C6 carbide phase with an FCC structure.
summary: This selected area electron diffraction pattern identifies the crystallographic structure of the carbide particles observed in the C0.1 alloy. The diffraction data confirms that these grain boundary precipitates are M23C6 carbides characterized by an FCC crystal structure, establishing their identity within the alloy's complex microstructural framework.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of short-range order (SRO) in Ni3Al under a single cascade simulation, showing the competition between irradiation-induced disordering and kinetic reordering.
summary: This panel illustrates the SRO evolution in Ni3Al during a single cascade simulation. It captures the dynamic interplay between irradiation-induced disordering and point defect-mediated kinetic reordering. The green dashed line marks the equilibrium point, while shaded regions represent the standard error across six independent simulations, highlighting the atomic-scale structural rearrangements.

caption: In-situ 3D printing of a replacement component within a brick assembly using a clay extrusion end-effector mounted on a 6-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator.
summary: This photograph illustrates the application of extrusion-based mobile 3D concrete printing for on-site repair of building components. A 6-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator, equipped with a clay extrusion end-effector, performs the in-situ printing of a replacement part within a brick assembly, demonstrating the feasibility of automated on-site construction repair processes.

caption: Full width at half maximum (FWHM) values of the (3 1 1) diffraction peak plotted against the position along the welded joint, comparing measurements taken at 0° and 90° azimuthal angles.
summary: This plot illustrates the FWHM variation of the (3 1 1) diffraction peak along the welded joint at 0° and 90° azimuthal angles. These SXRD data provide insight into the effects of grain size and structural defects within the material, serving as a key indicator of the joint's microstructural state.

caption: Vickers microhardness values for as-fabricated and heat-treated NiTi sample S4, calculated from five random test locations.
summary: Mechanical characterization of NiTi sample S4 using Vickers microhardness testing at five random locations highlights the hardening effect of heat treatment. As-fabricated S4 samples show hardness values in the 250 to 300 HV range, while heat-treated samples consistently exhibit higher hardness values, aligning with the overall findings for the NiTi sample series.

caption: Bright field TEM image displaying the distribution of round SiC particles within the as-annealed NiMo DPS alloy matrix.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging reveals the presence of round particles within the as-annealed NiMo DPS alloy. These particles, which measure between 50 and 100 nm in size, are distributed throughout the matrix, contributing to the dispersion strengthening of the NiMo alloy structure as observed in the micrograph.

caption: Binary equilibrium phase diagram of the Ti-Cu system, illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions of various intermetallic compounds and solid solution phases across the composition range.
summary: The Ti-Cu binary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic foundation for understanding the reaction layer formation in titanium alloy joints. Specifically, it identifies the stability of Ti2Cu intermetallic compounds, which are observed as the primary constituents in the reaction layer near the titanium alloy interface during processing.

caption: Schematic representation of the microstructure at a deformation level of 24.1%.
summary: This schematic illustrates the baseline microstructure observed at a 24.1% deformation level. It serves as the reference state for analyzing subsequent morphological changes induced by variations in deformation temperature and strain rate, providing a foundational view of the material's internal organization before further processing steps are applied.

caption: Deconvoluted TDS-GU spectra for 3.5NiCrMoV steel specimens charged in gaseous hydrogen at varying pressures, showing two Gaussian peaks representing diffusible hydrogen trap sites at 114 °C and 160 °C.
summary: This TDS-GU spectrum displays deconvoluted hydrogen trap sites for 3.5NiCrMoV steel after gas-phase charging. Two Gaussian peaks at 114 °C and 160 °C are identified, with the lower-temperature peak increasing in intensity with higher charging pressure, directly correlating to Sieverts’ Law behavior observed in the material's hydrogen uptake characteristics.

caption: Storage modulus curves plotted against temperature to evaluate the viscoelastic properties of TPU/PLA filaments.
summary: Storage modulus curves are plotted against temperature to evaluate the viscoelastic properties of TPU/PLA filaments. This thermal analysis provides insight into the stiffness and energy storage capacity of the composite materials, reflecting how the incorporation of PLA pellets affects the dynamic mechanical behavior of the blended filaments across temperature ranges.

caption: Visual comparison of the unit cell configurations for the proposed architecture and various reference auxetic structures.
summary: This panel presents the unit cell configurations for the structures analyzed in the study. By visualizing these geometries, the panel provides a structural basis for the performance differences observed in the mechanical property plots, allowing for a direct comparison between the proposed architecture and other existing designs.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of RSC-96 cells for NF-200 (red), S100 (green), and DAPI (blue) after culture with various scaffolds.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining of RSC-96 cells for NF-200 (red), S100 (green), and DAPI (blue) after culture with various scaffolds. The staining confirms significantly elevated expression of S100 and NF-200 in the composite scaffold groups relative to the PLA control, highlighting the enhanced neurogenic differentiation potential of the composite materials.

caption: Hardness distribution map across the transverse cross-section of a selective laser melted Ti–40Nb sample processed under single melting conditions.
summary: The hardness distribution map for the single melt Ti–40Nb sample reveals a non-uniform hardness distribution across the transverse cross-section. This spatial variation highlights the limitations of the single melting process in achieving consistent mechanical properties throughout the material structure during selective laser melting.

caption: Calculated NMI content evolution as a function of oxygen injection, predicted using FactSage thermochemical software.
summary: Calculated results of NMI content after oxygen injection are presented. Using FactSage thermochemical computing software with FTstel and FToxid databases, the formation of NMI is modeled. This simulation provides insight into the initial stages of inclusion formation during the oxygen blow process in the Ti-FSS system.

caption: Proposed HR array system incorporating bistable structures, designed to attenuate sound waves at approximately 3 and 5 kHz.
summary: The proposed switchable HR array system is shown, integrating multiple bistable structures to manage sound wave attenuation. The array is specifically engineered to resonate at frequencies of approximately 3 and 5 kHz, effectively attenuating sound waves incident into the penetration hole through the coordinated action of the HR components.

caption: SAXS patterns for the aged CCNZ specimen compared to the as-sintered state, with a green curve representing the difference spectrum that highlights the scattering contribution of a secondary precipitate population.
summary: This panel displays SAXS patterns for as-sintered and aged CCNZ specimens. Subtracting the as-sintered pattern from the aged specimen effectively isolates the scattering signal from large particles, revealing an additional population of precipitates approximately 7 nm in size, which provides critical insight into the microstructural evolution during the aging process.

caption: Business understanding phase of the ML-based IIPQ-AM reproducibility pipeline.
summary: This flowchart segment illustrates the business understanding phase within the ML-based IIPQ-AM reproducibility investigation pipeline. It focuses on analyzing the manufacturing system and defining the specific modeling purpose. The diagram uses standardized shapes to represent hardware, software, inputs, outputs, and process flows to guide the initial project conceptualization.

caption: Live/dead staining fluorescence images at 4x magnification showing cell density and distribution on day 3 for control cells, M-PCL, and M-PCL/TG-BG scaffolds (10, 20, 30% BG), with green indicating live cells.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy was employed to visualize the distribution and density of live cells on the scaffolds at day 3. The images confirm the presence of a dense collection of cells across the different scaffold formulations, demonstrating that the M-PCL and M-PCL/TG-BG materials effectively support cell attachment and viability.

caption: Three-dimensional model corresponding to the 1st-order fractal scaffold pattern.
summary: This 3D model depicts the 1st-order fractal bone scaffold. The structure is defined by 6 concentric rings with an outer diameter of 24 mm and an inner diameter of 8 mm. The model demonstrates the integration of fractal branching within the 16.5 mm height, maintaining a uniform trabecular diameter of 0.5 mm.

caption: Arrhenius plot depicting the temperature dependence of the Ni self-diffusion coefficient in dilute Ni-Si alloys with impurity concentrations ranging from 0 to 1 at.%.
summary: This plot presents the temperature-dependent Ni self-diffusion coefficient in Ni-Si alloys. Unlike P and S, silicon produces a very limited effect on solvent diffusion up to 1 at.%. This minor influence is attributed to the formation of vacancy-impurity pairs that are relatively difficult to form and possess low mobility.

caption: Vertical displacement δy of the hinge on the left side of point P under the third load case.
summary: This panel presents the vertical displacement δy of the hinge on the left side of point P under the third load case. These results characterize the deformation behavior of hinges arranged parallel along the z-axis, contributing to the comprehensive analysis of the hinge system under varying external load conditions.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) profile for the untreated sample plotted against sliding cycles, showing an initial transient phase followed by stabilization at a value of 0.58 with significant fluctuations.
summary: The untreated sample exhibits unstable frictional behavior during the sliding test. After an initial period, the coefficient of friction stabilizes at approximately 0.58. However, the profile is characterized by considerable fluctuations throughout the duration of the test, indicating inconsistent frictional performance compared to the treated samples.

caption: High-magnification STEM micrograph of the CoCr-based MEA revealing a dense forest dislocation structure.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of the fabricated CoCr-based MEA. The image highlights a high density of dislocations, which have organized into a complex forest dislocation network. This dense arrangement of dislocation structures is characteristic of the material's deformed state as observed at this specific magnification level.

caption: Crystal orientation and Kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps for cast and homogenized high-entropy alloy (HEA) specimens.
summary: This panel displays crystal orientation and KAM maps for cast and homogenized HEA samples. EBSD measurements were performed with a 35 nm step size. The maps reveal the local misorientation distribution, providing a baseline for comparing strain accumulation at grain boundaries between the cast material and the AM-produced HEA.

caption: Pressure-time curves recorded during fracture testing of elbows 1 and 4, illustrating the temporal evolution of pressure leading up to the structural failure of the components.
summary: This plot displays the pressure-time curves obtained during fracture tests for elbows 1 and 4. The data captures the dynamic pressure response of the components, specifically highlighting the critical moment of fracture. These curves provide essential insights into the mechanical behavior and failure characteristics of the elbows under test conditions.

caption: Baseline design sub-scale energy absorber manufactured using a 1 mm nozzle 3D printing process.
summary: The baseline design serves as the control specimen among the 3D-printed sub-scale energy absorbers. Fabricated with a 1 mm diameter nozzle, the printing process for this sample took about 2 hours. This panel displays the physical appearance of the baseline geometry used for comparative analysis in the research.

caption: Reverse-engineered computer-aided design model representing a marine communications antenna bracket.
summary: This reverse-engineered CAD model illustrates a marine communications antenna bracket, selected as a representative geometry for this study. The component serves as an example of a field-maintainable part, demonstrating the practical application of rapid and flexible production techniques in manufacturing complex, functional hardware for maritime communication systems.

caption: Magnetization as a function of applied magnetic field for the SPS sample, measured by sweeping the field from 2 T down to zero.
summary: This panel illustrates the isothermal magnetization behavior of the SPS sample, captured by varying the magnetic field from 2 T to zero. These M-H curves provide the necessary experimental input to analyze the magnetostructural transition and quantify the associated magnetic properties of the spark plasma sintered material.

caption: Atomic configurations resulting from 5 MC steps per lattice site at 327, 471, and 575 °C.
summary: Row a displays atomic configurations generated by KMC simulations after 5 MC steps per lattice site. These structures illustrate the early stages of phase transformation across three temperatures. Observations indicate that ordered phases nucleate rapidly at 327 and 471 °C, whereas nucleation is significantly suppressed at the higher temperature of 575 °C.

caption: Three-dimensional model of the cervical spine vertebrae following segmentation, wrapping, and smoothing processes.
summary: This 3D reconstruction illustrates the cervical spine model after undergoing segmentation, wrapping, and smoothing of the original CT data. The resulting CAD model provides a refined geometry optimized for the subsequent build preparation and SLA 3D printing processes required for manufacturing the bone models.

caption: High-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectrum for Sm-based catalysts, showing binding energy peaks indicative of surface iron states.
summary: This high-resolution Fe 2p XPS spectrum for Sm-based catalysts provides detailed information on the surface iron states. The data confirms the presence of iron particles, which is essential for verifying the nature of the in-situ exsolved nanoparticles and understanding the surface chemistry of the reduced materials.

caption: Normalized Bauschinger stress, calculated by dividing the stress by the initial yield strength (β), displayed as a function of forward plastic strain.
summary: Panel b presents the Bauschinger effect normalized by the initial yield strength of the specimen. This normalization allows for a comparative analysis of the Bauschinger effect across different conditions, maintaining the same trend observed in the absolute stress measurements where the effect correlates directly with the forward plastic strain.

caption: Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) results for the MnCr2O4 phase.
summary: These EDS results provide the elemental composition for the MnCr2O4 phase. The data confirms the presence of Cr, Mn, and O, which is consistent with the chromite spinel structure identified through IFFT and SAD analysis in the study.

caption: Force-displacement histories for partially supported top-clad structures subjected to impact from 13 mm and 38 mm hemispherical impactors.
summary: Force-displacement curves for top-clad samples demonstrate distinct impact responses, with peak forces reaching approximately 2 kN and 3 kN for the 13 mm and 38 mm hemispherical impactors, respectively. These results highlight the structural resistance to penetration provided by the rigid bottom skin and the energy-dissipating polyurea foam core.

caption: Effective surface strain map of grain G8, demonstrating concentrated strain accumulation in the middle region of the grain.
summary: The effective surface strain map for grain G8 shows that strain accumulation is concentrated primarily in the middle region of the grain. This distribution correlates with the regions of increased KAM and internal misorientation, reflecting the localized mechanical response of the material under the applied deformation conditions.

caption: Methodological workflow diagram outlining the systematic research approach taken to investigate the influence of printing strategies on the dynamic performance of additive manufactured thin-walled structures.
summary: The research methodology is presented as a structured flow chart. This diagram serves as a roadmap for the study, detailing the systematic steps taken to analyze how different printing strategies affect the microstructural and dynamic properties of the thin-walled Ti6Al4V parts fabricated via selective laser melting.

caption: Wear depth (WD) values measured for the AB, AB + Ni-P, and AB + Ni-P + DLC conditions, illustrating the impact of surface treatments on material loss.
summary: Wear depth measurements demonstrate that the uncoated AB sample suffers from the highest material loss due to low hardness. Deposition of the Ni-P layer reduces WD by over an order of magnitude. The DLC topcoat provides a further decrease in WD, effectively protecting the underlying Ni-P from wear.

caption: Relative transmission spectra of 0.4 mm thick 3D printed PLA samples compared to polystyrene, measured across the 450–950 nm wavelength range, highlighting the highest, lowest, and median performance curves based on varying layer height, print speed, and extruder temperature.
summary: This plot displays the relative optical transmission of 3D printed PLA samples compared to polystyrene across the 450–950 nm range. By adjusting print parameters like layer height, print speed, and extruder temperature, the study identifies optimal conditions for maximizing transparency, with post-print polishing further enhancing transmission values to approximately 100.6% relative to polystyrene.

caption: Sensitivity analysis of the coefficient of determination for yield stress predictions as a function of the number of hidden nodes within the neural network architecture.
summary: This plot examines the relationship between neural network complexity and predictive performance. By varying the number of hidden nodes, the study determines how the coefficient of determination for yield stress fitting evolves, providing insight into the optimal network architecture required for accurate mechanical property modeling during the cross-validation process.

caption: Stress-life fatigue plots for LP-DED A6061-RAM2 specimens, illustrating the raw data distribution and corresponding Basquin fitted lines across various laser types and powder reuse cycles.
summary: This panel displays the raw stress-life fatigue data for LP-DED A6061-RAM2 specimens, featuring Basquin fitted lines for different laser types and powder reuse cycles. The plot highlights significant fatigue scatter inherent in the experimental conditions, providing a baseline for evaluating the fatigue performance of the additively manufactured material.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging of the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample showing atomic-scale contrast.
summary: High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging is employed to visualize the T6-V-5538 s-1 sample. This technique provides Z-contrast imaging, where regions with higher atomic numbers appear brighter. The resulting map highlights the distribution of elements and structural features within the sample, providing critical insights into the local atomic arrangement.

caption: Resistive transition curves for Ta5W35Mo5Re35Ru20C20 HEA under magnetic fields up to 9 T, illustrating the field-dependent suppression of the superconducting transition temperature.
summary: Resistive transitions for the Ta5W35Mo5Re35Ru20C20 high-entropy alloy are displayed under magnetic fields up to 9 T. As the field increases, the resistive transition is systematically suppressed to lower temperatures. The midpoint of the resistivity drop is indicated by a horizontal dashed line, while the arrow denotes the direction of increasing magnetic field.

caption: Three-dimensional atom map reconstruction of the as-printed Al alloy, illustrating the spatial distribution of alloying elements including Mg, Mn, Sc, Zr, Fe, Cu, and Zn within the grain interior.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction provides a comprehensive visualization of the intragranular chemical composition in the as-printed Al alloy. It highlights the spatial arrangement of multiple alloying elements, specifically Mg, Mn, Sc, Zr, Fe, Cu, and Zn, offering insight into the microstructural distribution within the material's grains.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra showing the reduction kinetics of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) catalyzed by Pd/C coaxial reactors (CR) of varying lengths.
summary: This panel displays UV-Vis absorption spectra monitoring the catalytic reduction of 4-nitrophenol using Pd/C coaxial reactors. By measuring the absorbance changes over time, the catalytic performance of the reactor is evaluated across different lengths, providing insight into the reduction efficiency of the 4-NP substrate within the coaxial 3D-printed system.

caption: Deformation process and equivalent stress distribution map of the additively manufactured IN718-P-TPMS structure under compressive loading.
summary: Visualizing the deformation process and equivalent stress distribution, this panel demonstrates how the IN718-P-TPMS structure behaves under load. It highlights that vertical struts bear the maximum load, and their subsequent failure leads to significant structural collapse, which directly correlates with the stress reduction phase observed in the stress–strain curve.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves illustrating the thermal degradation behavior of rPLA-based composites prepared at varying weight percentages.
summary: Derivative thermogravimetric curves characterize the thermal degradation of rPLA-based composites across different weight percentages. Analysis of these curves, alongside TGA data, reveals that neat rPLA exhibits an onset degradation temperature of 315 °C, a maximum decomposition temperature of 365 °C, and a relatively low char residue of 0.5%.

caption: Total density of states (DOS) for pure Ni, showing the spin-polarized (black line) and scaled non-spin-polarized (red line) results for comparison.
summary: This panel displays the total density of states for pure Ni, calculated using 6x6x6 k-point meshes and a 0.2 eV smearing parameter. The comparison between spin-polarized and non-spin-polarized data illustrates how spin effects modify the DOS near the Fermi level, which is critical for determining mechanical properties like shear modulus.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of RA600 alloy grain boundary displaying rod-shaped γ′ precipitates formed by discontinuous precipitation.
summary: At the grain boundary of the RA600 alloy, the dark-field TEM image shows rod-shaped γ′ precipitates. These features are larger than those found in the grain interior and were developed through discontinuous precipitation perpendicular to the grain boundary. The inset diffraction pattern confirms the presence of (100) superlattice spots.

caption: Van't Hoff plot of log P H2 versus 1000/T for the 2# alloy, used to determine thermodynamic parameters of the hydrogen storage reaction.
summary: The Van't Hoff plot for the 2# alloy, represented by log P H2 versus 1000/T, allows for the calculation of enthalpy and entropy changes associated with the hydrogen absorption and desorption processes. This linear relationship is critical for characterizing the thermodynamic stability of the metal hydride phase.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for water (W) content.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot illustrates the relationship between water (W) content and the predicted compressive strength of 3DPFRC. It provides insight into how the absolute water content influences the model output, contributing to the overall understanding of the material's performance drivers.

caption: Comparative summary of average hardness and associated standard deviations across the three tested HEA conditions.
summary: This summary chart presents the average hardness and standard deviation for the CoCrFeNi, CoCrFeNi + 4 at% Ti, and CoCrFeNi + 7 at% Ti samples. These mechanical metrics are essential for understanding the plastic and wear resistance properties of the bulk HEAs under the three distinct experimental conditions.

caption: Zero-field-cooled and field-cooled magnetization versus temperature curves measured at 5 mT for precursor ribbons and the SPS sample, with an inset showing the normalized derivative dM/dT versus normalized temperature T/Tt for the magnetostructural transition.
summary: Magnetization versus temperature curves at 5 mT reveal the magnetostructural transition for precursor ribbons and SPS samples. The inset compares normalized dM/dT curves, highlighting that the temperature full width at half-maximum doubles for the SPS sample compared to ribbons, indicating that the ribbon samples exhibit a more abrupt magnetostructural transition.

caption: Evolution of sample composition over milling duration, showing stabilization after 24 hours of processing.
summary: This line graph illustrates the progression of sample composition as a function of milling time. The data indicates that the composition reaches a stable state after 24 hours of milling. While prolonged milling does not significantly reduce particle size, it leads to increased Fe contamination, as noted in the reference.

caption: Correlation between laser power, melt pool characteristics, and the resulting austenite phase proportion and morphology.
summary: This plot displays the relationship between laser power, melt pool conditions, and the resulting microstructure. It demonstrates that increasing heat input leads to a higher proportion of the austenite phase. The visualization highlights how processing parameters directly influence the morphological development and phase composition of the material.

caption: Close-up view of the thermal orthophoto revealing localized thermal leakage points on the building surface.
summary: This close-up view of the thermal orthophoto highlights specific areas where thermal leakages are visible. By mapping thermal data onto the building façade, the framework effectively visualizes energy loss, providing a clear diagnostic tool for identifying structural or insulation defects that manifest as thermal anomalies.

caption: Saturation magnetization values plotted against varying laser power for Fe-based amorphous samples processed via LPBF.
summary: Saturation magnetization values are plotted against laser power for Fe-based amorphous samples. Increasing laser power up to 130 W improves the saturation magnetization, as higher energy input promotes crystallization. This crystallization reduces the amorphous content, which is critical because higher amorphous content typically lowers the saturation magnetization values in these materials.

caption: Cross-sectional slice of the 3D tomographic image for the R-Octet-30 metamaterial.
summary: Displayed is a tomographic slice of the R-Octet-30 metamaterial, highlighting the internal structural features and defects. The slice provides a clear view of the pores generated by the specific layer-to-layer twist angle, confirming the increased presence of lack-of-fusion defects compared to the standard Octet lattice configuration.

caption: Current density-voltage (JV) characteristics for 3 nm period superlattice (SL) devices featuring varying absorber thicknesses of 250 nm, 500 nm, 800 nm, and 1150 nm, measured under standard AM1.5G illumination conditions.
summary: Experimental JV-curves illustrate the performance of 3 nm period superlattice devices with absorber thicknesses ranging from 250 nm to 1150 nm under AM1.5G conditions. These curves provide critical insights into the electrical behavior of the devices, with corresponding key performance indicators detailed in the associated experimental data table.

caption: Clustree analysis visualization demonstrating the stability and hierarchical relationships of cellular clustering results across varying resolution parameters.
summary: The Clustree analysis provides a systematic visualization of cellular clustering results derived from scRNA-seq data. By evaluating different resolution parameters, this plot illustrates the stability and hierarchical structure of the identified cellular subgroups, facilitating the selection of an optimal clustering resolution for downstream analysis of the single-cell sequencing dataset.

caption: Raman spectra of PLA, PLA-1CaP, PLA-2CaP, and PLA-12CaP scaffolds showing characteristic PLA bands between 2000 and 200 cm-1 and the phosphate symmetric stretching mode near 960 cm-1.
summary: Raman spectroscopy reveals the bonding configuration of PLA and composite scaffolds. PLA scaffolds exhibit characteristic bands at 872, 1769, 1455, 1126, 1043, 398, and 298 cm-1. The inclusion of calcium phosphates in PLA-1CaP, PLA-2CaP, and PLA-12CaP scaffolds introduces a distinct band near 960 cm-1, corresponding to PO4-3 symmetric stretching.

caption: Front view of the LDED-100 specimen after hot forging.
summary: The front view of the LDED-100 specimen demonstrates the macroscopic morphology following hot forging. This image illustrates the impact of the forging process on the overall specimen shape, showing that the material maintains its verticality and structural integrity without evident macroscopic instability or deformation after the applied treatment.

caption: Pie chart illustrating the total distribution of recyclable waste weight percentage across surgical subspecialties, highlighting that arthroplasty surgery generates the highest proportion at 39.04%, followed by oncology at 30.67% and trauma at 30.29%.
summary: This pie chart displays the total recyclable waste weight percentage across different surgical subspecialties. Arthroplasty surgery is identified as the primary contributor to recyclable waste production at 39.04%, while oncology and trauma surgeries account for 30.67% and 30.29% of the total waste, respectively, providing a clear overview of waste distribution.

caption: Conceptual representation of iron oxide MNP-mediated thermal therapy for cancer treatment.
summary: This diagram illustrates the integration of iron oxide nanoparticles into base additive manufacturing components for anticancer thermal therapy. The mechanism relies on the magnetic properties of the nanoparticles to facilitate targeted heating, providing a potential pathway for localized cancer treatment within complex, custom-fabricated medical devices or implants.

caption: 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction of the C-264 alloy, illustrating the distinct elemental distribution between the γ matrix and the TiN precipitate.
summary: This 3D atom probe tomography reconstruction provides a spatial visualization of the C-264 alloy, clearly distinguishing the elemental distribution within the γ matrix and the TiN precipitate.
