The reconstruction facilitates a detailed analysis of the chemical composition across the interface between the two phases.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization M(T) curves for Ni3-xFexAl measured under an applied field of 1000 Oe, demonstrating the onset of ferromagnetic order across the sample series.
summary: The temperature-dependent magnetization curves for Ni3-xFexAl, measured at 1000 Oe, provide clear evidence of ferromagnetic ordering in all samples. These low-temperature magnetization measurements confirm the presence of ferromagnetic phases, serving as a foundational characterization of the magnetic behavior for the investigated alloy system across the studied temperature range.

caption: Cumulative heat release profiles for LC3 mixtures, demonstrating the impact of increasing VMA dosage on total hydration energy.
summary: This panel presents the cumulative heat release for LC3 mixtures as a function of VMA dosage. The results show that the total cumulative heat release decreases as the VMA dosage increases, confirming that the addition of VMA effectively reduces the overall heat generated during the hydration of the mixture.

caption: Three 10 mm diameter endmills fabricated via Metal-X additive manufacturing after a 15 hour and 57 minute build process.
summary: Three endmills with a diameter of 10 mm are shown following their fabrication using the Metal-X printing system. The manufacturing process for these components required approximately 15 hours and 57 minutes to complete, resulting in the printed parts displayed in the photograph.

caption: Magnified TEM image of region C in (a) and its corresponding SAED pattern.
summary: This magnified TEM image of region C in the T0 specimen includes the corresponding SAED pattern. The grain in this region is aligned with a distinct zone axis, demonstrating the crystallographic orientation of the martensite laths and providing structural data for comparison with other regions.

caption: Measured electric field phase and intensity distribution for the metasurface with an OAM topological charge of l = 1, evaluated across the V-band from 60 to 70 GHz.
summary: Experimental measurements of the electric field phase and intensity distribution are presented for the metasurface with an OAM topological charge of l = 1. These results, obtained across the 60 to 70 GHz V-band, validate the performance of the metasurface design through direct observation of the field characteristics.

caption: Confocal micrograph of AO2 F Ti particles oxidized at 500 °C, showing a non-uniform color shift ranging from orange to blue and purple.
summary: Confocal imaging of the AO2 F Ti particle, oxidized at 500 °C, reveals a wide range of colors including orange, blue, and purple. This color variation across the particle surface indicates a non-uniform thickness of the oxide layer resulting from the higher temperature oxidation process.

caption: Overview of the custom-built robotic additive manufacturing platform utilized for the fabrication of complex, irregularly shaped CCFTC components.
summary: This photograph displays the custom-built robotic additive manufacturing platform developed in-house. The system is specifically designed to enable the scalable fabrication of larger, irregularly shaped CCFTC components. This setup serves as the primary experimental apparatus for verifying the effectiveness of optimized manufacturing processes through practical component production and subsequent warpage measurement.

caption: Schematic illustration of the 3D printing and metallization workflow, highlighting the initial addition of metallic salts to the resin followed by a ball-milling dispersion step.
summary: This schematic outlines the 3D printing and metallization process. It specifically depicts the initial incorporation of metallic salts into the resin, followed by a ball-milling procedure designed to ensure uniform dispersion of the additives within the composite material before further processing steps are performed.

caption: Processing state distribution map at a powder feeding rate of 9.3 g/min, showing the influence of laser power and scanning speed on state ranges.
summary: Representing the material states at a powder feeding rate of 9.3 g/min, this plot highlights how laser power and scanning speed modulate the range of the four observed states. The distribution of these states shifts in response to the specific powder feeding rate applied during processing.

caption: Ellipse-packed domain sample, rendered as a 128 × 128 pixel image to represent specific geometric porosity.
summary: Representing a sample of an ellipse-packed domain, this 128 × 128 pixel image is one of the geometries considered in this study. The dataset, which includes this ellipse-packed structure, is utilized to ensure the research covers a broad range of porosities and thermal conductivities.

caption: SAED pattern of bcc grain (7) along the [001]α zone axis.
summary: The SAED pattern for bcc grain (7) is captured along the [001]α zone axis. This diffraction data confirms the body-centered cubic structure of the grain, providing essential crystallographic information that complements the microstructural observations of high dislocation density noted in the corresponding BF-TEM image.

caption: Texture density evolution of V_E-5 specimen at elevated strain, derived from in-situ neutron diffraction peak height measurements.
summary: This panel displays the texture density evolution for the V_E-5 specimen under elevated strain conditions. The data, obtained via in-situ neutron diffraction, demonstrates that texture density changes are directly proportional to the evolution of the corresponding diffraction peak heights, providing insight into the material's polycrystalline deformation behavior during the loading process.

caption: Raman spectra of the prepared catalysts, indicating carbon structural characteristics.
summary: The Raman spectra of the prepared catalysts provide insights into the carbon structural characteristics of the materials. This spectroscopic analysis is used to evaluate the degree of graphitization and the presence of defects within the carbon nanotubes and the overall catalyst framework of the synthesized samples.

caption: Logarithmic plots of storage modulus (G΄), loss modulus (G΄΄), and tan δ for pre-gel solutions with 0 and 1 wt% CNC, monitored over a 20-second UV exposure duration.
summary: The viscoelastic properties of the pre-gel solution, specifically storage modulus, loss modulus, and tan δ, are evaluated during a 20-second UV curing process. Comparing formulations with 0 and 1 wt% CNC, these log-scale plots track the evolution of the material's mechanical response upon exposure to the curing light source.

caption: Resistivity versus temperature plot for a sample annealed at 773 K, illustrating the electrical transport behavior during phase transformation.
summary: This plot displays the resistivity as a function of temperature for a sample annealed at 773 K. The measurement was performed to analyze the material's phase transformation behavior. The resulting curve provides critical data on the electrical transport properties of the sample following the specific thermal treatment process.

caption: Laser microscopy image showing the surface morphology of the alloy, characterized by a uniform distribution of microscale dendrites within the matrix.
summary: Laser microscopy reveals the surface morphology of the alloy, where small and fine dendrites are evenly distributed throughout the matrix. The observed surface area ratio between the dendrites and the matrix is approximately 2:3, indicating a consistent microscale structural arrangement across the examined surface area of the material.

caption: Box-plot distribution of the number of materials per formulation generated by models 1–27, categorized by model performance groups.
summary: This box-plot illustrates the distribution of material counts per formulation across three model groups. Models 1–9 consistently produce single-material formulations due to high learning rates. Models 10–18 generate realistic material counts, while models 19–27 occasionally produce formulations with an excessively large number of materials, demonstrating varying levels of generative realism.

caption: Resistance response profile of the sensor maintained at a stable temperature of approximately 40 °C.
summary: The sensor demonstrates robust performance at 40 °C, maintaining its original resistance response despite the applied thermal load. This stability confirms the device's capability to function reliably under body-relevant temperatures, as evidenced by the consistent resistance measurements recorded during the high-temperature testing phase.

caption: Failure strength plotted against raster angle, demonstrating a decreasing trend in tensile strength as the raster angle increases.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between tensile failure strength and raster angle. The data indicates that failure strength consistently reduces as the raster angle increases. Prediction accuracy for these strengths is notably lower within the 30 to 60 degree range, likely due to the emergence of complex mixed mode failure mechanisms.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the PBMOC2 sample reduced at 900 °C, highlighting exsolved metallic cobalt nanoparticles anchored on the perovskite surface with inset enlargements.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy analysis of the PBMOC2 sample after reduction at 900 °C reveals the presence of metallic spherical nanoparticles anchored on the surface of faceted perovskite crystals. Arrows indicate the exsolved cobalt nanoparticles, with inset enlargements providing detailed views of their morphology and distribution on the perovskite phase.

caption: Seebeck coefficient of Bi2-xNixSe3 samples as a function of temperature, illustrating a decrease with both increasing Ni concentration and rising temperature.
summary: The Seebeck coefficient for Bi2-xNixSe3 samples is shown to decrease as both the Ni content and the temperature increase. This trend is attributed to an increase in carrier concentration, which serves as the dominant factor influencing the Seebeck coefficient, particularly at room temperature, rather than changes in band effective mass.

caption: Comparative Tafel plots for Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples evaluated in a 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte solution.
summary: Tafel curves for Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples are presented for a 0.5 M H2SO4 environment. These plots illustrate the electrochemical corrosion characteristics of the electrodeposited samples, allowing for a direct comparison of the corrosion kinetics between the pure metals and the Ni-Cr alloy in an acidic medium.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for height, displaying the relative importance of input parameters on the predicted melt pool height.
summary: This SHAP beeswarm plot provides an overview of how different input parameters affect the height of the melt pool. By analyzing the distribution of SHAP values, the plot identifies the key drivers influencing height predictions, serving as a diagnostic tool to understand the model's decision-making process for this specific output.

caption: Performance evaluation of the original Exposure network, illustrating the detection outcomes for failure cases.
summary: This figure presents the detection results for the original Exposure network. Analysis of the network's performance reveals that it successfully identified 9 out of 10 failure instances. These findings, which are also detailed in Table 7, demonstrate the effectiveness of the original model in detecting specific failure events during operation.

caption: Darcy permeability values normalized by pore radius, representing the capillary flow capacity of the wick structure while accounting for viscous resistance.
summary: This plot presents normalized wick permeability values, which are directly proportional to the maximum flow rate achievable through capillary action against viscous resistance. By normalizing the Darcy permeability by the pore radius, the figure effectively illustrates the capillary flow capacity of the wick structure under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Experimental deformation and failure mechanism of the Re-Entrant (RE) architecture, highlighting diagonal shear failure via cyan dashed lines.
summary: The Re-Entrant (RE) architecture demonstrates a distinct failure mechanism characterized by diagonal shear. As shown in the experimental observation, this failure mode occurs prior to self-contact of the struts. The cyan dashed lines in the image clearly delineate the shear path, providing a visual representation of the structural collapse.

caption: XCT slice of the sample following the deposition of subsequent layers, where surface asperities begin to manifest more clearly as precursors to defect formation.
summary: Following the initial layer, this XCT slice illustrates the progression of the printing process. As additional layers are deposited, the surface asperities become increasingly pronounced, providing clear evidence of the evolving structural irregularities that eventually lead to the formation of lack-of-fusion pores within the bulk material.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for the pH = 9 class, showing feature importance values ranging from -0.4 to 0.8.
summary: This SHAP plot for the pH = 9 class demonstrates well-distributed values, indicating that the model has successfully learned clear, distinguishable features. The red channel exhibits a consistent negative impact, while the green channels show positive contributions, highlighting significant feature importance differentiation within this specific classification category.

caption: Atomic configurations of Ni-Cr alloy structures, where blue spheres represent nickel atoms and gray spheres represent chromium atoms.
summary: This panel displays the atomic structural models for Ni-Cr alloys. Nickel atoms are depicted in blue, while chromium atoms are shown in gray. These structural representations serve as the basis for the force field development and subsequent energy calculations performed in the study to characterize the alloy system.

caption: Elongation at failure measured as a function of aging time at 800 °C for DAFA26 and DAFA29 specimens.
summary: Elongation at failure is shown as a function of aging time at 800 °C for DAFA26 and DAFA29. DAFA29 exhibits increased elongation as aging progresses from 2.4 h to 240 h, whereas DAFA26 shows an initial increase followed by a slight decrease in elongation over the same aging period.

caption: Calculated phase equilibrium diagram for pristine Ti6Al4V, illustrating the solidification sequence where beta phases form initially.
summary: This panel displays the thermodynamic phase calculation for pristine Ti6Al4V. The diagram indicates that beta phases are the primary constituents formed during the solidification process. These calculations provide a baseline for understanding the microstructure formation mechanisms in the alloy system before the addition of boron or nitrogen elements.

caption: Optical transmission spectra demonstrating material response to tertiary UV exposure intervals.
summary: Optical transmission spectra demonstrate the material response to tertiary UV exposure intervals. By placing samples in a UV chamber at 3.15 mW/cm2, the researchers tracked changes in transmission. The graphs provide the specific exposure time and corresponding UV energy, documenting the ongoing shift in optical properties under sustained UV irradiation.

caption: Experimental propagation of 4-spot square RPVBs with topological charge l=4 and power order n=2, measured at a constant distance d=100 mm across varying propagation distances z.
summary: This panel displays the experimental propagation properties of 4-spot square RPVBs characterized by a topological charge of l=4 and a power order of n=2. The intensity distribution is captured at a constant measuring distance of 100 mm, illustrating the spatial evolution of the beam as the propagation distance z varies.

caption: MTS assay absorbance values for MG-63 cells on uncoated and PDA-coated scaffolds, indicating the biocompatibility of both scaffold types.
summary: MTS assay absorbance values for MG-63 cells on uncoated and PDA-coated scaffolds, indicating the biocompatibility of both scaffold types. The result of cell proliferation by MTS assay presented in this panel confirms the biocompatibility of both uncoated and PDA-coated scaffolds toward MG-63 cells, showing no adverse effects from the coating.

caption: Schematic representation of the magnetic field-assisted laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) system, featuring a 500 mT magnet positioned directly beneath the substrate to generate the required magnetic field during the fabrication process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the magnetic field-assisted LPBF equipment configuration. A 500 mT magnet is strategically placed under the substrate to induce a magnetic field during the sample formation process. This setup provides the necessary magnetic environment for the subsequent experimental measurements of magnetic induction intensity across the substrate surface.

caption: Simulated solidification curve representing the phase transformation behavior of the Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy.
summary: This panel displays the simulated solidification curve for the Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy. It provides a theoretical framework for understanding the solidification behavior of the material, complementing the schematic diagrams of precipitation mechanisms by modeling the phase transformation kinetics that occur during the cooling process of the alloy within the molten pool.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of the starting prealloyed powders, displaying characteristic peaks identified as ferrite or martensite phases, denoted as α.
summary: X-ray diffractograms of the starting prealloyed powders are presented, revealing the presence of ferrite or martensite phases, labeled as α. These patterns confirm the crystalline nature of the starting materials, which exhibit narrow particle size distributions with D10, D50, and D90 values of 17 μm, 40 μm, and 90 μm, respectively.

caption: Grain boundary diagram illustrating the network of boundaries within the internal failure fracture region for the R = -1 condition.
summary: The grain boundary diagram for the R = -1 condition maps the network of boundaries within the internal failure fracture region. This visualization is essential for understanding the microstructural features and grain interactions that influence microcrack growth behavior during VHCF testing at 650 °C.

caption: Synchrotron diffraction plot of the 5 h annealed sample showing the (222) peak region around 2θ = 96°.
summary: Displayed is the synchrotron diffraction profile for the 5 h annealed sample, centered on the (222) peak at approximately 2θ = 96°. This measurement characterizes the diffraction behavior of the material at this specific angular range, contributing to the overall structural analysis of the 5 h annealed specimen.

caption: Crack resistance R-curves plotting J-integral versus crack extension for CS900 and CS1000 samples.
summary: Fracture toughness is evaluated through R-curves, which plot J-integral against crack extension for CS900 and CS1000 samples. The results reveal that the CS1000 deposit exhibits superior fracture toughness compared to the CS900 variant, consistent with quasi-static testing observations and higher K IC values recorded for the CS1000 material.

caption: Fluorescence visualization of MC3T3-E1 cells on an acid-etched NT/TC4 surface after 3 days of culture, with nuclei (blue) and cytoskeletal components (red) clearly defined.
summary: MC3T3-E1 cells cultured on an acid-etched NT/TC4 surface for 3 days are displayed via fluorescence microscopy. The image highlights the distribution of nuclei in blue and the cytoskeletal proteins F-actin and vinculin in red, illustrating the cellular response to the modified NT/TC4 surface topography.

caption: Pentagon diagram illustrating the CPDP parameters for the Al72Cr15Ni13 alloy system after 6 hours of mechano-synthesis, evaluated in a 0.1 mol/L Na2SO4 electrolyte.
summary: This radar chart displays the CPDP parameters for the Al72Cr15Ni13 alloy system synthesized via 6 hours of mechanical alloying. The parameters, including corrosion potential, current density, and various pitting potentials, are visualized within a 0.1 mol/L Na2SO4 electrolyte to assess the electrochemical behavior and corrosion resistance of the material.

caption: Detailed backscattered electron view of fracture features in the PSD-D sample.
summary: This backscattered electron micrograph provides a high-magnification look at the fracture characteristics of the PSD-D sample. Yellow dot-dash lines delineate the melt pool boundaries, while white arrows indicate the presence of microvoids. The panel highlights the structural response and defect formation within the PSD-D material during the fracture process.

caption: Representative photograph showing density assessment cubes and tensile blanks fabricated in the Vz orientation, with cubes measuring 20 × 20 × 20 mm.
summary: This photograph displays physical examples of density assessment cubes and tensile blanks produced using the Vz build orientation. The cubes, which measure 20 × 20 × 20 mm, demonstrate the practical implementation of the Vz orientation in LPBF manufacturing, providing a visual reference for the specimens used in subsequent material characterization.

caption: Voltage profile recorded across the arc during the course of one full pulsation cycle.
summary: Represented here is the voltage evolution over one complete pulsation cycle. Recorded alongside the current, this profile illustrates the electrical behavior of the arc. The measurement was facilitated by high-speed imaging techniques, ensuring precise synchronization with the current data to characterize the arc's electrical performance during the pulsation.

caption: KEGG pathway enrichment analysis showing the top 20 significantly concentrated pathways, including MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and TNF signaling, derived from the identified DEGs in treated RAW264.7 cells.
summary: KEGG pathway enrichment analysis demonstrates that the 2935 differentially expressed genes are significantly concentrated in 20 distinct pathways. Key signaling pathways identified include MAPK, PI3K-Akt, and TNF, providing insight into the intracellular signaling mechanisms affected by the ABOHA@ZnO hydrogel microsphere treatment compared to the untreated control group.

caption: Higher-magnification bright-field TEM image of the Al-Zn-Cr specimen, highlighting Zn precipitates segregated at grain and cell boundaries, alongside nanosized precipitates distributed within the grain interiors.
summary: This higher-magnification bright-field TEM image provides a detailed view of the Al-Zn-Cr specimen's microstructure. It highlights the segregation of pure Zn precipitates at both grain and cell boundaries, as indicated by arrows. Additionally, the image reveals that nanosized precipitates are homogeneously distributed throughout the interiors of the equiaxed grains.

caption: Weibull distribution plot representing the total failure strength of ZrO2 lattice structures under shear testing conditions.
summary: This panel displays the Weibull distribution for the total failure strength of ZrO2 lattices subjected to shear testing. The plot characterizes the statistical reliability and failure probability of the ceramic lattice, providing essential data on the structural integrity and mechanical performance of the ZrO2 material under complete failure conditions.

caption: Confusion matrix representing the classification accuracy of a vision-based melt pool monitoring system for wire-arc additive manufacturing using deep learning.
summary: This confusion matrix displays the classification performance of a deep learning model utilized for monitoring melt pool dynamics in wire-arc additive manufacturing. The visualization serves to validate the vision-based monitoring system's ability to accurately categorize melt pool conditions, which is critical for real-time process control and defect prevention.

caption: EDS elemental mapping illustrating the distribution of Manganese (Mn) around the oxide inclusion and Sigma phase.
summary: Manganese elemental mapping via EDS reveals the chemical environment surrounding the oxide inclusion and Sigma phase. The distribution of manganese is critical for identifying the specific oxide types, such as MnO or MnCr2O4, which serve as nucleation sites for the observed Sigma phase precipitation in the material.

caption: Qualitative thermal history profile of a fixed point A in layer n during the LPBF process, illustrating five consecutive reheating cycles (c1–c5) induced by the deposition of subsequent layers n+1 to n+4.
summary: This qualitative schematic illustrates the thermal history of a fixed point A during the LPBF process, showing five reheating cycles caused by the deposition of subsequent layers. The diagram highlights how cyclic reheating, particularly in cycle 4 below the beta-transus temperature, facilitates the diffusion of V and Cu to grain boundaries, promoting the precipitation of beta-Ti and Ti2Cu phases.

caption: Chromatograms of extractables in ethanol/water for samples post-cured for 14 minutes, showing absorbance at 210 nm.
summary: This panel displays the chromatograms of extractables in an ethanol/water solvent for samples post-cured for 14 minutes. The analysis, measured at an absorbance of 210 nm, reveals that most extractables for the Graphy material are highly polar compounds, as indicated by the presence of mean peaks at short retention times below 10 minutes.

caption: Room-temperature compressive stress-strain curves for d0.01–d0.06 specimens.
summary: Room-temperature compressive stress-strain curves are presented for d0.01–d0.06 specimens. These curves illustrate the mechanical response of the materials under compression, providing the foundational data for evaluating the yield strength, ultimate compressive strength, and total compressive strain across the different hatch spacing conditions investigated in the study.

caption: Size distribution histogram of pores detected in the SLM AlSi10Mg alloy.
summary: This histogram illustrates the size distribution of pores identified in the SLM AlSi10Mg alloy. The data reveals that pore sizes are relatively similar and are primarily concentrated within the range of 0.02 to 0.04 mm, providing a clear quantitative assessment of the defect dimensions detected by micro-CT.

caption: HM-2 configuration illustrating the SP-FDM material placed on the upper side in contact with the indenter, with the LCD material situated on the lower side.
summary: The HM-2 configuration demonstrates an alternative hardness testing setup where the SP-FDM material is placed on the upper side in direct contact with the indenter. In this arrangement, the LCD material is positioned on the lower side, allowing for a comparative analysis of the material stack order during indentation.

caption: (100), (110), and (111) pole figures characterizing the crystallographic texture of the plate-like specimen.
summary: Crystallographic orientation distribution of the plate-like specimen is represented through (100), (110), and (111) pole figures. These diffraction data characterize the initial texture of the material, which contributes to the observed differences in ductility when compared to the rod-like specimens analyzed in the present work.

caption: Schematic representation of the equivalent transformation model, illustrating a layered architecture consisting of three HEA layers (blue) and two graphene layers (white), with defined geometric parameters for length, width, and individual layer thicknesses.
summary: This schematic illustrates the equivalent transformation model for a composite structure. The model features a layered arrangement of three HEA layers and two graphene layers. Geometric parameters, including length, width, and the specific thicknesses of the HEA and graphene layers, are defined to facilitate the subsequent calculation of elastic strain energy.

caption: Phase-field predicted melt pool cross-section for LPBF condition D3 compared to the corresponding experimental melt pool observation.
summary: Condition D3 illustrates the phase-field predicted melt pool cross-section alongside experimental observations. The analysis confirms that single-track responses are dominated by the monotonic influence of laser power and scan velocity, consistent with the broader findings that characterize the LPBF processing conditions evaluated in this experimental series.

caption: SHAP summary plot presenting the feature importance and impact on joint shear capacity for the GBR model.
summary: The SHAP summary plot for the GBR model provides a visual breakdown of how input variables influence the joint shear capacity (Fmax). By mapping the SHAP values, this graph highlights the key drivers of the model's predictions, offering insights into the sensitivity of the joint shear capacity to various input parameters.

caption: Nyquist plot comparing the electrochemical impedance response of LPBF 316L stainless steel against R 316L stainless steel in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: The Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for LPBF 316L and R 316L stainless steel in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. This plot serves as the primary visualization for comparing the corrosion resistance and capacitive behavior of the different steel samples under the specified environmental conditions.

caption: Gas-chromatogram of the anode outlet gas stream collected after the condenser during operation at 0.7 V, revealing the presence of CO2, unreacted CO, H2, and CH4 reaction products.
summary: This gas-chromatogram displays the composition of the gas stream at the anode outlet following the condenser during a 0.7 V test. Analysis confirms the presence of CO2, unreacted CO, and H2, alongside CH4 as a reaction product, providing a clear profile of the gaseous species exiting the system after the liquid trap.

caption: Schematic representation of the atmosphere control and nitrogen gas recirculation system integrated into the slurry laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) machine, highlighting the gas flow path with dashed arrows.
summary: This schematic illustrates the atmosphere control system and nitrogen gas circulation within the slurry LPBF machine. The diagram specifically highlights the gas flow path using dashed arrows to indicate the recirculation process, providing a clear overview of how the machine maintains the necessary atmospheric conditions during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Compactness (Ω) versus sphericity (Ψ) scatter plot derived from μCT data, featuring quadrant divisions at Ω = 0.4 and Ψ = 0.6, accompanied by 3D rendered pore morphologies from an AD-contaminated specimen.
summary: This scatter plot displays the morphological distribution of pores in AD-contaminated specimens based on compactness and sphericity values extracted from μCT data. The data reveals a predominance of spherical pores, characteristic of gas porosity rather than lack-of-fusion defects. Quadrant-specific 3D renderings illustrate the presence of single pores and overlapping clusters.

caption: Support Vector Machine (SVM) model ROC curve evaluated against the unseen test set.
summary: Support Vector Machine model performance is illustrated by an ROC curve on the unseen test set. The figure includes five curves, representing four individual classes and a micro-average, which serve to quantify the classification performance and robustness of the SVM model when tested on unseen data samples.

caption: Main effects plot illustrating the influence of individual factor levels on the average tensile strength, where large vertical distances between mean values indicate significant factor impact.
summary: This main effects plot displays the influence of individual factor levels on average tensile strength. Large vertical distances between factor levels relative to the mean indicate significant impacts. Notably, the center point of individual factors typically yields the highest characteristic values, except for the layer thickness factor regarding tensile strength.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of HSFs stained with DCFH-DA to visualize intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels across different treatment groups.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of HSFs stained with DCFH-DA allow for the visualization of intracellular ROS levels. By comparing fluorescence intensity across different treatment groups, this assay provides insight into the ROS scavenging effects of the hydrogels, which is a critical factor in mitigating oxidative stress in cellular environments.

caption: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy image of the nanoparticle distribution within the TiN/0.5/800 specimen.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image displays the nanoparticle distribution within the TiN/0.5/800 sample. These particles, which underwent melting and precipitation as TiOxNy, are encapsulated by a TiN shell to form a core-shell structure. The image provides direct visualization of the spatial arrangement of these nanostructures within the material matrix.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the greenness assessment of the proposed analytical methodology using the AGREE tool, which yielded a total score of 0.65.
summary: The AGREE tool assessment results are presented in a radar chart, yielding a total score of 0.65. This quantitative evaluation confirms that the proposed analytical methodology qualifies as a green approach, meeting the necessary sustainability criteria established for the assessment process.

caption: Mass transfer coefficient (Koga) values for 3% CO2 concentration at varying liquid loads of 11.73, 18.05, and 25.27 m3/m2h, comparing SpiroPak and commercial packing at 0.2 mol/L NaOH.
summary: Panel A displays the mass transfer coefficient for a 3% CO2 volume fraction. SpiroPak performance is compared against commercial packing across three liquid loads. At a gas flow rate of 600 LPM, SpiroPak values consistently surpass those of the commercial packing by over 40% across all tested liquid load conditions.

caption: Thermal power rating as a function of the total height of the heat exchanger core.
summary: The graph displays the impact of the heat exchanger core height on the thermal power rating. This geometric variable is evaluated as part of the design optimization set to identify the most cost-effective configurations when utilizing various additive manufacturing machines for heat exchanger production.

caption: Dependence plot showing the SHAP value contribution of the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) to the yield strength prediction model.
summary: This dependence plot quantifies the impact of the Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) on the yield strength predictions. By mapping CTE values against their corresponding SHAP contributions, the visualization reveals the sensitivity of the model to thermal expansion properties, which is critical for optimizing autonomous manufacturing processes.

caption: Shear stress versus indentation depth profiles for five rectangular regions (R7–R11) characterized by inclined twin boundaries.
summary: Shear stress profiles for five regions containing inclined twin boundaries are presented here. These curves demonstrate strong agreement during the initial indentation phase up to 4 nm. Beyond this depth, the data points show increased diversity, indicating varied mechanical responses among the inclined twin boundary regions as the indentation process continues.

caption: Three-dimensional scan of the as-printed stiffener structure prior to post-processing, showing a top inner diameter of 170.29 mm and a top outer diameter of 190.83 mm.
summary: This 3D scan provides a detailed geometric assessment of the as-printed stiffener structure. Quantitative measurements reveal a top inner diameter of 170.29 mm and a top outer diameter of 190.83 mm, establishing the baseline dimensions before the application of the salt-bath post-processing technique.

caption: Loading cycle profiles for material nodes B1 and B2 recorded during the first cutting operation.
summary: The loading cycle changes for material points B1 and B2 during the first cut are shown. These curves establish the initial mechanical state of the nodes, serving as a reference to evaluate how subsequent cutting cycles modify the residual stress distribution at these specific locations within the material.

caption: Detailed representation of the βTi/βTi+Ti2Ni phase boundary, derived from experimental data obtained through equilibrated two-phase alloys and diffusion couples.
summary: Focusing on the βTi/βTi+Ti2Ni phase boundary, this panel presents refined data determined from equilibrated two-phase alloys and diffusion couples. This boundary is essential for understanding the phase stability and transformation behavior in Ti-Ni alloys, particularly regarding the diffusion-driven formation of specific phases within the titanium lattice at elevated temperatures.

caption: Atomic supercell model of the η2 phase illustrating potential Cu substitution sites at the interface and within the bulk, marked by numbered white labels, alongside interstitial hydrogen trapping sites highlighted by red circles.
summary: This atomic supercell model represents the η2 phase structure used for DFT calculations. It identifies specific numbered sites for Cu substitution within the bulk and at the interface, while red circles denote interstitial sites designated for evaluating hydrogen trapping energy, providing the geometric foundation for subsequent energetic analysis.

caption: Correlation between laser energy density (179–348 J/mm³) and tungsten specimen density, comparing Archimedes bulk density measurements with optical density (ODD) derived from cross-sectional porosity analysis.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between laser energy density and the densification of LPBF tungsten cubes. Archimedes bulk density and optically determined density (ODD) measurements show a clear positive correlation with increasing energy density. The data indicates that higher energy inputs effectively reduce part porosity, reaching a maximum densification limit of 98%.

caption: Digital Image Correlation (DIC) setup showing the subset used for correlation and the corresponding stress-strain plot derived from averaging axial strains within a 2.5 × 5 mm rectangular region.
summary: Digital Image Correlation (DIC) analysis is performed using a 37-pixel square subset and a 3-pixel step. Axial strains are averaged over a 2.5 × 5 mm rectangular area centered on the most strained zone. This setup enables the generation of accurate stress-strain plots by correlating surface deformation during tensile loading.

caption: ATR-FTIR spectrum of the LOCTITE® EA M−121HP™ epoxy adhesive.
summary: The ATR-FTIR spectrum of the LOCTITE® EA M−121HP™ epoxy adhesive is presented, revealing characteristic signals typical of an epoxy-amine chemical system. These spectral features confirm the chemical composition of the adhesive, which is relevant for analyzing the physical adsorption forces and hydrogen bonding interactions at the interface.

caption: 2D differential charge density map of interface 2 (Al/Cr) at the NiAl/Cr interface.
summary: This panel provides a 2D differential charge density map for interface 2, corresponding to the Al/Cr atomic arrangement. This visualization allows for a more intuitive observation of the charge transfer processes occurring at the NiAl(011)[011]/Cr(011)[011] interface, complementing the structural analysis of the optimized bridge position.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curve of the CM247 LC alloy, illustrating the thermal response during heating to determine phase transition temperatures.
summary: The differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve for the CM247 LC alloy provides critical thermal data regarding its phase transformation behavior. Analysis of this thermal profile reveals that the average liquidus temperature (T γl) for the CM247 LC alloy is approximately 1380 °C, characterizing its high-temperature melting behavior.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map of C in the as-deposited sample, illustrating the spatial distribution of carbon.
summary: The EPMA map of C illustrates its spatial distribution within the as-deposited sample. This elemental map complements the structural analysis by showing how carbon is distributed relative to the dendritic features, providing insight into the chemical composition of the interdendritic and dendritic regions of the alloy.

caption: Surface slab model showing the defined cell boundaries used for the computational representation of the material surface.
summary: The surface slab model is presented with its corresponding cell boundaries clearly displayed. This visualization defines the spatial constraints and periodic dimensions of the slab, establishing the geometric framework necessary for analyzing surface adsorption properties and structural configurations within the computational model of the (110) surface.

caption: BEI transmission spectra obtained from the Fe (316 L) and Cu (CuCrZr) layers of the multilayer specimen oriented in the TD2 direction.
summary: Presented here are the BEI transmission spectra for the Fe and Cu layers of the multilayer sample in the TD2 orientation. These spectra characterize the material layers in this specific orientation, facilitating the comparison of spectral features between different sample directions to support further strain determination.

caption: Compressive elastic modulus plotted against relative density using Ashby’s framework to characterize mechanical performance.
summary: This Ashby diagram illustrates the relationship between compressive elastic modulus and relative density. By applying Ashby’s framework, the plot summarizes the mechanical characteristics of the material, providing a clear visualization of how the elastic modulus scales with changes in relative density within the studied mechanical property space.

caption: Interference fringes observed in a projected image under horizontal alignment conditions.
summary: Horizontal alignment of the PLM and DMD components results in the interference fringes shown here. During the adjustment process, when the offset of these fringes reaches its maximum, the PLM and DMD achieve perfect alignment in the light path, confirming the system is correctly configured for the intended optical measurement.

caption: X-ray CT 2D tomograph slice of the T sample tested at 1-90-1-1, 650 °C for 96 h, revealing a relatively straight crack trajectory within the dendritic regions.
summary: This 2D X-ray CT tomograph slice shows the T sample tested at 650 °C for 96 h. In contrast to the L samples, the crack path is significantly straighter. The crack propagates within and along the main dendritic regions, largely avoiding deflection by the carbides present in the microstructure.

caption: Instantaneous CTE values derived from dilatometry measurements for SB-CoNi-10+ and the reference René N5 superalloy.
summary: Instantaneous CTE values for SB-CoNi-10+ are compared against the René N5 superalloy using push-rod dilatometry data. This plot illustrates the temperature-dependent variation in the instantaneous thermal expansion coefficient, allowing for a precise assessment of the thermal response characteristics of the SB-CoNi-10+ alloy relative to the established industrial standard.

caption: Time-lapse imaging of lung cancer organoid (LCO) development, tracking cell sedimentation at 1 h, cluster aggregation at 8 h, and mature organoid formation by 24 h.
summary: Time-lapse imaging documents the development of lung cancer organoids within the nested wells. The process shows cells sedimenting to the well bottom within 1 hour, followed by cluster aggregation at 8 hours, and culminating in the formation of mature organoids by 24 hours post-seeding.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph and WDS elemental maps of Cu and Mn for the L 67 sample, demonstrating reduced segregation of Cu and Mn at the HAGB compared to higher VED conditions.
summary: The L 67 sample, processed at a lower VED condition, shows a distinct change in elemental distribution. WDS mapping indicates that the segregation of Cu and Mn at the high-angle grain boundaries is notably reduced compared to the higher energy H 133 condition, reflecting the influence of printing parameters on segregation.

caption: Storage modulus curves as a function of temperature for TPU/CNF composites, comparing the dynamic mechanical response across different CNF types.
summary: Storage modulus curves illustrate the temperature-dependent stiffness of TPU/CNF composites. By analyzing these curves alongside the loss factor data, the dynamic mechanical behavior of the composites is fully characterized. These results provide critical insights into how different CNF types influence the viscoelastic properties and thermal stability of the TPU matrix.

caption: EBSD phase map of the recycled 5 wt.% BMD SS316L specimen, depicting the Fe-FCC matrix and alumina inclusions.
summary: Representing the non-metallic population in the recycled 5 wt.% BMD SS316L sample, this EBSD phase map highlights the Fe-FCC matrix and alumina inclusions. The visualization serves to quantify the presence and distribution of these inclusions, completing the comparative analysis of the recycled stainless steel material series.

caption: Nyquist plots of the MGN and MGYN composites after immersion in 3 wt% KCl solution at 25 °C, showing impedance response.
summary: Nyquist plots characterize the electrochemical impedance response of MGN and MGYN alloys immersed in a 3 wt% KCl solution. Analysis of these plots, alongside fitting data, reveals that the MGN alloy exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance and film resistance, correlating with a higher dissolution rate compared to the MGYN alloy.

caption: Peak interface temperature evolution over friction time under process parameters of 400 MPa, 25 Hz, and 2.9 mm amplitude.
summary: This line graph illustrates the peak interface temperature as a function of friction time. A thermal equilibrium plateau is reached at 1 s, while the magnitude shows periodic variations. The cycle time of these temperature oscillations is exactly half the cycle time of the mechanical oscillation applied during the friction process.

caption: Tan delta and elastic modulus curves derived from Dynamic Mechanical Thermal Analysis (DMTA) testing.
summary: This figure displays the viscoelastic properties of the material as determined by DMTA analysis. The plot illustrates the temperature-dependent behavior of the tan delta and elastic modulus, providing critical insights into the material's damping characteristics and stiffness transitions. These collected data points are further detailed in the accompanying Table 6.

caption: Initial stage of the alloy composition design workflow involving the establishment of a comprehensive database.
summary: This panel illustrates the foundational step of the alloy design workflow, which focuses on the establishment of a database. As part of the broader screening process, this initial phase organizes the necessary data required to facilitate subsequent computational or experimental alloy composition design and material selection strategies.

caption: Training and test accuracy curves showing the predictive performance of the supervised learning model.
summary: The training and test accuracy curves provide a clear visualization of the model's predictive capability. By comparing these metrics, it is confirmed that no overfitting issue is observed, as the accuracy levels remain consistent and well-aligned between the training and test datasets throughout the model's learning progression.

caption: Al 11 at.% iso-surface reconstruction showing the spatial arrangement of nanometric ternary γ′ precipitates within the γ-channels of the ODS alloy.
summary: This 11 at.% Al iso-surface reconstruction highlights the presence of nanometric tertiary γ′ precipitates within the γ-channels of the ODS alloy. These tertiary precipitates are typically less than 5 nm in diameter and are observed to be more prominent in wider channels located further away from secondary γ′ precipitates.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the bottom region of the slow deposition along the <011> Al zone axis, illustrating the precipitate distribution at the base of the deposit.
summary: This bright-field STEM image captures the bottom region of the slow deposition along the <011> Al zone axis. It provides a visual record of the precipitate distribution at the base of the deposition, contributing to the overall analysis of precipitation evolution across the height of the slow deposition sample.

caption: Calculated electron absorbed dose per fluence (D/Φ) for SIL and ICRP 116 phantoms using MCNPX simulation, showing a sharp increase in dose between 50 keV and 70 keV.
summary: This panel displays the electron absorbed dose per fluence (D/Φ) for SIL and ICRP 116 phantoms derived from MCNPX simulations. The data reveals a significant increase in absorbed dose within the 50 keV to 70 keV energy range, with a maximum observed difference of approximately 76% occurring at 60 keV.

caption: 3D reconstruction of the fracture zone showing the detachment of subjacent TPU layers at a depth of approximately 100 μm.
summary: The 3D analysis reveals the detachment of subjacent TPU layers within the fracture zone, occurring at an approximate depth of 100 μm, which corresponds to a single layer height. This visualization demonstrates improved bonding and substrate failure, particularly at the downskin regions of the tongue and groove sections.

caption: Time-resolved photographic sequence showing the morphology of liquid metal flow under a constant gas pressure of 3 kPa.
summary: Captured at various time points, these images display the evolving morphology of the liquid metal flow under a 3 kPa gas pressure. The high-speed camera setup allows for detailed observation of the flow state, which serves as the basis for measuring the diameter variations in subsequent analysis.

caption: Rib structure printed on a CF/PA6 composite plate, prepared for quasi-static tensile testing.
summary: This panel shows a rib structure printed on a CF/PA6 composite plate, creating a rib-on-plate geometry. This specific specimen configuration is designed for subsequent quasi-static tensile testing to evaluate the mechanical performance and structural integrity of the printed rib interface on the composite substrate.

caption: Surface roughness parameters Sa and Svk for MEK01 replicates and ripples.
summary: This table presents the surface roughness parameters, specifically Sa and Svk, for MEK01 replicates and ripples. According to the provided data, a replicate of the CF-PEEK AM die exhibits a significantly higher value for both Sa and Svk compared to the ripples, indicating distinct surface topography characteristics for these samples.

caption: Final observed stage at t = 15 ms with continued droplet growth on the trailing wire.
summary: At t = 15 ms, the trailing wire tip continues to be heated and melted by the trailing arc. This results in further growth of the droplet, which makes the arc length become short. This stage completes the observed sequence of the periodic droplet transfer process.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of HEMA:PEGDA resin containing Atto dyes, illustrating the wavelength-selective filtering characteristics of the dissolved dyes.
summary: This panel displays the optical transmission spectrum of HEMA:PEGDA resin infused with Atto dyes. The data demonstrates the selective wavelength filtering properties inherent to these fluorescent dyes when dissolved in the liquid resin matrix, providing a baseline for the optical performance of the 3D-printed materials.

caption: Detailed view of the Dirac surface state crossing in the Rb-doped SnSbBiTe4 sample, highlighting the electronic band modification.
summary: The Dirac surface state clearly emerges in the Rb-doped SnSbBiTe4 sample, as shown by the crossing of the bands. The Dirac point is located at a specific energy relative to the Rashba spin-split surface band, demonstrating the successful tuning of the electronic structure through surface doping.

caption: Comparative impact parameters for various filler configurations, specifically detailing Peak force (F peak), Crushing Force Efficiency (CFE), and Maximum compressive displacement (U max).
summary: This table summarizes key mechanical performance metrics for different filler configurations within the 27-cell structure. It provides quantitative comparisons of peak force, crushing force efficiency, and maximum compressive displacement, allowing for an evaluation of how different fillers influence the energy absorption and structural integrity under impact loading conditions.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectrum of the Ni 2p core level for the original NiTi sample.
summary: This panel displays the high-resolution XPS spectrum focusing on the Ni 2p core level for the original NiTi sample. This characterization is part of the surface chemistry analysis, providing detailed information on the chemical state of nickel present on the surface of the untreated NiTi material.

caption: Transmission spectra of custom-made filter sets compared with normalized temperature-dependent emission spectra of BAM phosphor excited at 365 nm.
summary: This panel displays the transmission spectra of custom-made filter sets alongside the normalized temperature-dependent emission spectra of BAM phosphor under 365 nm excitation. These spectral characteristics are essential for evaluating the system's performance, indicating that the design should provide strong temperature sensitivity within the 75K to 523K range.

caption: Misorientation angle statistical map for the top region of the deposit, characterizing the distribution of grain boundary angles.
summary: The misorientation angle statistical map provides a quantitative overview of the grain boundary characteristics in the top region. By analyzing the distribution of angles, this plot characterizes the microstructural state of the deposit, supporting the observation that the microstructure is uniform and composed of significantly refined grains throughout the sample.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from nanoindentation tests performed at specific locations containing different phase combinations, with the inset indicating the precise indentation positions.
summary: Load-displacement curves are plotted for specific areas of the material to characterize the mechanical response of various phase combinations. The inset provides visual confirmation of the indentation sites, allowing for a localized analysis of how the different nanocrystalline phases influence the material's deformation behavior during the nanoindentation process.

caption: Electron probe microanalysis mapping of the 1TiN as-built Inconel 718 sample, highlighting the distribution of light grey Laves phase precipitates.
summary: Electron probe microanalysis mapping of the 1TiN as-built Inconel 718 sample reveals the distribution of light grey Laves phase precipitates. This analysis demonstrates the initial microstructural state of the material, providing a baseline for observing how the incorporation of TiN influences phase formation and local chemical redistribution within the melt pool.

caption: Categorical ranking of microstructural features observed in low-strength iron-base alloys following irradiation exposure.
summary: Microstructural feature rankings for low-strength iron-base alloys are illustrated in this panel. These features are correlated with IASCC behavior, where alloys exhibiting less severe microstructural changes demonstrate higher resistance to cracking. This analysis highlights the critical relationship between irradiation-induced microstructural evolution and the overall mechanical integrity of the alloys.

caption: WDXRF measurements illustrating the variation in Zn concentration relative to the number of ZnO ALD cycles.
summary: Wavelength-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (WDXRF) is utilized to quantify the Zn concentration in the specimens. The results demonstrate the change in Zn levels as a function of the quantity of ZnO ALD cycles, providing a clear correlation between the processing parameters and the resulting elemental composition of the material.

caption: Side view of the Ti-64-Al-4V thin wall structure after 10 build layers, captured via synchrotron X-ray radiography at 150 W laser power and 50 mms-1 scan speed.
summary: This synchrotron X-ray radiograph displays the side profile of a Ti-64-Al-4V thin wall after 10 layers of laser powder bed fusion. The build was performed at 150 W and 50 mms-1, showing increased powder denudation on the front surface compared to lower energy density builds, indicating significant surface morphology changes.

caption: 3D complex impedance plot of the as-fabricated sample measured in 0.01 M NaCl, showing instantaneous impedance values recorded every 5 minutes.
summary: This 3D complex impedance plot displays the instantaneous impedance of the as-fabricated sample measured in 0.01 M NaCl. The diagram, which captures data points every 5 minutes, allows for the observation of dissolution behavior and oxide film formation as changes in impedance over time.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) strain measurements of the MBLM Zone A, derived from VIC-2D image processing during structural deformation analysis.
summary: Structural deformation of the MBLM Zone A is quantified through DIC strain measurements. By utilizing images captured via VIC-2D and processed with digital image correlation techniques, this panel provides a detailed visualization of the strain distribution, enabling a precise assessment of the material's mechanical response under the applied load.

caption: Creep strain evolution observed in NBSC specimens with diffusive cooling holes under three distinct loading stress levels.
summary: Creep strain curves for NBSC specimens containing diffusive cooling holes are presented under three different loading stress conditions. The results highlight the material's deformation response to varying mechanical loads, showing how the diffusive hole configuration performs under stress and contributing to the overall assessment of creep resistance in the plate specimens.

caption: Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) recording the evolution of stress, strain, and temperature over time during shape memory cycle (SMC) testing.
summary: Dynamic mechanical analysis tracks the thermomechanical behavior of the hybrid resin during shape memory cycles. The plot demonstrates the real-time changes in strain, stress, and temperature, providing essential data to evaluate the material's ability to undergo controlled deformation and recovery under cyclic thermal loading conditions.

caption: Two-way shape-memory performance of X-PCL10-MA under mechanical load, showing strain versus temperature curves at 40% and 50% strain levels with good cycle overlapping.
summary: The two-way shape-memory effect was assessed to determine reversible shape changes under mechanical load. The results demonstrate a good overlapping in the strain versus temperature curves across three thermal cycles, indicating no loss of performance and confirming the stability of the material during repeated two-way shape-memory testing.

caption: Vertical displacement fields obtained via Digital Image Correlation (DIC) overlaid on an in-situ optical micrograph of the workpiece at a cutting speed of 60 m/min.
summary: At a higher cutting speed of 60 m/min, the DIC-analyzed vertical displacement field is overlaid on the optical micrograph. The location of the burr root changes significantly compared to lower speeds. This displacement data serves as a basis for analyzing stress distributions using modified tractional Hertzian contact mechanics.

caption: Refractive index values for the HA-based eye drops, showing compliance with the physiological range of the human cornea.
summary: Refractive index measurements for the four eye drop formulations are displayed here. Each product, including DayDrop Advanced, Hyabak, HyloComod, and Artelac Splash, exhibits values between 1.3348 and 1.3410, which align with the physiological refractive index range of the human cornea, confirming their optical compatibility.

caption: Applied stress plotted against the Larson-Miller (L-M) parameter, featuring two distinct best-fit curves that characterize creep behavior based on stress regimes relative to the proportional limit (σ PL).
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between applied stress and the Larson-Miller parameter, utilizing dual stress regions to optimize model accuracy. The data is represented by two distinct curves, which effectively distinguish creep behavior above and below the threshold of significant plasticity observed at the onset of the mechanical testing.

caption: Real part of the Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS data, presented as open circles with corresponding model fits shown as solid lines for Ni foil and nanoNi-P electrodes prepared at different deposition current densities.
summary: The real part of the Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS data provides detailed structural information through model fitting. By comparing the experimental data points with theoretical fits for Ni foil and various nanoNi-P electrodes, the bonding environment and atomic coordination of nickel are precisely determined and validated.

caption: Temperature and velocity field distribution during the early heating phase at approximately 0.08 ms.
summary: Representing the early heating stage at 0.08 ms, this panel visualizes the evolving temperature contours and velocity vectors. The simulation demonstrates how the molten pool begins to form and expand under the stationary electron beam, establishing the thermal gradients necessary for understanding the subsequent liquid/mushy interface dynamics.

caption: Principal component analysis biplot illustrating the variance in recovery rates for K, Mn, Cu, Fe, Al, and Mg across twelve different lixiviants under both electrokinetic and static leaching treatment conditions.
summary: Principal component analysis was performed to evaluate the differential impact of twelve distinct lixiviants on the recovery of six metals (Al, Cu, Mn, Fe, Mg, and K). The analysis compares recovery rates obtained through electrokinetic and static leaching treatments, providing a multidimensional view of how different chemical agents influence metal extraction efficiency.

caption: Noiseless theoretical redshift drift signal z ̇ ( z ) plotted against redshift z from 0 to 5, showing the true fiducial values as dashed lines and the best-fit model as a solid line.
summary: This panel displays the noiseless theoretical redshift drift signal across a redshift range of 0 to 5. It serves as the baseline for the study, illustrating the true fiducial values represented by dashed lines alongside the best-fit model, providing a clean reference for evaluating subsequent noise-affected cosmological parameter recovery.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the paracetamol-PEG 6000 system established from experimental heating data.
summary: Representing the paracetamol-PEG 6000 system, this diagram displays experimental data points in blue alongside the theoretical liquidus curve derived from the Schroder-van Laar equation in red. The eutectic invariant points are marked by black squares, providing a clear visualization of the phase equilibrium established during the first heating process.

caption: Initial atomic configuration of the Ti6Al4V substrate showing a regular, ordered arrangement of atoms prior to the W-DED deposition process.
summary: This MD snapshot displays the initial state of the Ti6Al4V substrate before the W-DED process begins. The interfacial atoms exhibit a highly regular and ordered arrangement, providing a baseline structure for analyzing the subsequent atomic evolution and interaction with deposited layers during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Deformation stages captured during uniaxial tensile loading of the printed material specimens.
summary: Deformation stages are captured during uniaxial tensile loading of the printed material specimens. These visual records provide insight into the physical changes and failure modes occurring throughout the tensile testing process, complementing the quantitative mechanical data obtained from the stress-strain responses and extracted tensile property measurements.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification diagram of Inconel 718, highlighting the solidification sequence and the potential formation of the δ phase during cooling.
summary: The Scheil-Gulliver solidification model for Inconel 718 outlines the predicted solidification sequence, which is consistent with experimental findings from laser-based DED processes. It specifically indicates that the δ phase can participate in the solidification sequence, providing critical insights into the microstructural development of the alloy during rapid cooling.

caption: Graphical representation of the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, illustrating the relationship between sensitivity and specificity to evaluate binary classification performance.
summary: This plot illustrates the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, which serves as a fundamental tool for assessing binary classification models. The Area Under the Curve (AUC) value, derived from this curve, provides a quantitative performance metric ranging from 0 to 1, reflecting the model's overall diagnostic or predictive accuracy.

caption: Time-transformation-temperature (TTT) diagram generated by JMatPro 13.3, comparing precipitation kinetics between the dendrite core (dotted line) and interdendritic region (continuous line).
summary: JMatPro 13.3 TTT diagram illustrates the distinct precipitation kinetics for γ'', γ', and δ phases in Ni-based superalloy 718. The chemical composition gradient between the dendrite core and interdendritic regions influences these kinetics, though the γ' precipitation rate remains similar across both regions, supporting consistent γ' content across various processing routes.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HTHed Tube sample measured at temperatures near the FM-PM transition.
summary: Isothermal magnetization curves for the HTHed Tube sample are presented, showing the magnetic response measured at various temperatures around the ferromagnetic-paramagnetic transition temperature. These M(H) measurements provide essential data for characterizing the magnetic state transition behavior of the tube-structured sample near its critical transition point.

caption: Shear stress evolution plotted against indentation depth for six distinct rectangular regions (R1–R6) containing horizontal twin boundaries.
summary: This plot displays shear stress as a function of indentation depth for six regions containing horizontal twin boundaries. The curves exhibit high consistency, confirming uniform stress distribution beneath the indenter. Notably, at specific depths of 1.7, 1.9, 2.4, and 3.1 nm, the shear stress exceeds the critical twinning threshold, triggering horizontal twin formation.

caption: Faber-Ziman partial structure factor S_NiNi(q) for liquid Ni25Al75 calculated via MD simulations, compared with experimental neutron scattering data for Ni20Al80 at 1330 K.
summary: This panel displays the partial structure factor S_NiNi(q) for Ni25Al75 derived from MD simulations. It is compared against experimental neutron scattering measurements for Ni20Al80 at 1330 K. The MD results show reasonable qualitative and quantitative agreement with the experimental data for this specific partial structure factor component.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the weld region, where black bold lines delineate the solidification cracks propagating along grain boundaries.
summary: The inverse pole figure map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the weld microstructure. Black bold lines clearly delineate the solidification cracks, which are shown to propagate along multiple sets of solidified grain boundaries. This visualization confirms the relationship between the crack paths and the underlying grain boundary network in the weld.

caption: Compressive load–displacement data for Black material lattices designed with a 3 mm diameter.
summary: Shown is the experimental load–displacement curve for Black material lattices featuring a 3 mm diameter. This mechanical test result illustrates the compressive behavior of the brittle lattice structure, providing insight into how the increased diameter influences the load-displacement characteristics compared to the 2 mm diameter Black material specimens.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile and GP prediction for <111> grains in the axial direction at the sample center (r = 0 mm).
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction peak for <111> grains at the axial center of the sample. The red solid line represents the experimental diffraction data, which is compared against the GP prediction. This analysis is part of a broader study characterizing grain-specific diffraction behavior across the sample diameter.

caption: Evolution of effective stiffness components k ̄ eff,x and k ̄ eff,y during topology optimization, comparing NHT and CNN predictions alongside the final generated structure.
summary: This plot illustrates the iterative evolution of effective stiffness components, specifically k ̄ eff,x and k ̄ eff,y, throughout the topology optimization process. It provides a direct comparison between NHT and CNN predictive models at every step, culminating in the visualization of the final optimized structure derived from these computational methods.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for samples in the green state (green dotted line), after solvent debinding (yellow solid line), and in the brown state (blue dotted line), demonstrating the progressive elimination of binder components.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves verify the success of the debinding process by tracking mass loss across three stages. The green state, solvent-debound, and brown state samples show distinct profiles, confirming the effective elimination of the two-component binder system through the optimized thermal debinding cycle applied to the metal parts.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded at 50 mV s-1 for 1 mM dopamine in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) using additively manufactured electrodes printed from AuNP-CO (red), CO (blue), and commercial (black) filaments.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry tests performed at 50 mV s-1 demonstrate the electrochemical performance of additively manufactured electrodes in a 1 mM dopamine solution. The AuNP-CO filament electrode exhibits superior performance compared to the CO and commercial filament counterparts, highlighting the enhanced electroanalytical capability provided by the gold nanoparticle-incorporated material.

caption: 1H NMR spectra (500 MHz, CDCl3, 500 K) comparing the chemical composition of PC-CF recycling stages R0 (red), R1 (green), and R5 (blue).
summary: This figure displays the 1H NMR spectra for the PC-CF recycling stages R0, R1, and R5, acquired at 500 MHz in CDCl3 at 500 K. The spectra allow for a direct comparison of the chemical composition across these different recycling stages, illustrating the structural integrity of the material throughout the process.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) maps of LPBFed Ti–45Nb specimens, illustrating grain orientation distributions under different annealing conditions.
summary: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) plots visualize the grain orientation distribution of LPBFed Ti–45Nb specimens under various annealing conditions. Analysis indicates that the HT-250 specimen exhibits the largest average grain size with significant fluctuations, suggesting the presence of fine grain areas that contribute to uneven hardness distribution and abnormally high microhardness values.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and solid fraction (fs) curves for the 2.5Hf sample.
summary: The 2.5Hf sample is analyzed through its DSC curve (solid line) and solid fraction curve (dashed line). These thermal analysis results are essential for identifying the oxidation temperature. By comparing these curves, the thermal stability and solidification characteristics of the 2.5Hf alloy can be accurately determined and evaluated.

caption: ΔK evolution profiles for surface cracks in shot-peened (SP) notched specimens, demonstrating the influence of residual stress fields on crack growth behavior at different stress amplitudes.
summary: This plot shows ΔK evolution for SP notched specimens. At a 170 MPa stress amplitude, surface cracks require a minimum length of 190 μm to propagate. When applying a ΔK threshold of 1.5 MPa√m, the calculated crack length for the transition from non-growing to growing cracks is approximately 240 μm.

caption: Vertical specimen deformed at 900 μm crosshead displacement, showing SEM microstructure and DIC strain distribution map with average strain.
summary: Vertical specimen deformed at 900 μm crosshead displacement shows SEM microstructure and DIC strain distribution map. The average strain value quantifies the deformation. Significant strain concentration along the melt-pool boundary is evident, contributing to the enhanced fracture characteristics observed in the vertical specimen during the mechanical loading process.

caption: Maximum principal strain distribution at measurement points along the sampling line for an α = 10° specimen orientation.
summary: This panel illustrates the maximum principal strain profile for an α = 10° specimen orientation. Using DIC-based measurements across 25 points along the flaw periphery sampling lines, the plot captures the variation in strain magnitude, reflecting the mechanical response of the material under this specific geometric configuration.

caption: Specific strength comparison of various high-temperature alloys utilized in turbomachinery applications, adapted from existing literature.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific strength of high-temperature alloys commonly used in turbomachinery. By comparing these materials, it provides a foundational understanding of the mechanical performance requirements for components like rotor blisks, highlighting the material selection criteria necessary for high-stress, high-temperature environments typical of aerospace and power generation systems.

caption: Rate capability comparison for PPy/3D-IDCμE devices utilizing different gel electrolytes, showing capacitance retention as a function of increasing current density.
summary: The rate capability investigation demonstrates the performance of PPy/3D-IDCμE devices with various gel electrolytes. The 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H2SO4, 15 wt% PVA in 1M H2SO4, and 1 wt% agarose in 3M LiCl electrolytes show varying capacitance retention, with the PEGDA-based electrolyte retaining 62% of its initial capacitance under tenfold current density increase.

caption: Force-time plot for a specimen aged for 15 days.
summary: This force-time plot characterizes the mechanical response of the specimen following a 15-day ageing period. The data contributes to the broader experimental analysis of force-time, force-displacement, and energy-time curves, allowing for a detailed assessment of how extended ageing durations influence the material's mechanical characteristics and overall structural integrity.

caption: Simulated load-displacement response for a surface roughness of Sa = 0.07 μm compared against the ideal smooth surface reference.
summary: This panel illustrates the simulated load-displacement curve for a surface with a roughness value of Sa = 0.07 μm during the indentation loading stage. By comparing this result to the ideal smooth surface model, indicated by the red dashed line, the influence of this specific roughness level on mechanical response is highlighted.

caption: TDA-spectrum of CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 1000 bar with a heating rate of 0.125 K/s, featuring the four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit.
summary: Displaying the TDA-spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA samples charged at 1000 bar at a heating rate of 0.125 K/s, this panel completes the series. The four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit function are shown, emphasizing the distinct hydrogen desorption characteristics observed in the 1000 bar charged samples across the tested heating rates.

caption: Detailed view of the thermal spray apparatus components used for bond coat fabrication.
summary: Representing a specific component of the thermal spray system, this photograph illustrates the hardware configuration used to produce NiCrAlY bond coats. The setup is integral to the research, facilitating the thermal spray process required to achieve the desired coating properties for the investigation of plasma and HVOF deposition techniques.

caption: WAXS intensity plots versus 2θ for the alloy in its initial state and after 1000 h of aging at 190 °C, highlighting the diffraction peaks of various precipitate phases.
summary: This panel displays WAXS intensity plots comparing the initial alloy state with a sample aged for 1000 h at 190 °C. The diffraction patterns reveal and index peaks corresponding to various precipitate families present within the alloy, providing a clear overview of the phase evolution during the thermal treatment process.

caption: Nyquist plots representing the electrochemical impedance characteristics of Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocage, nanocube, Co-Ni@NC, and RuO2.
summary: Nyquist plots provide insight into the charge transfer resistance and electrochemical impedance of the catalysts. These plots are used to evaluate the interfacial kinetics of the Fe-Co-Ni@NC nanocage, nanocube, Co-Ni@NC, and RuO2 during the oxygen evolution reaction, supporting the observed differences in catalytic activity.

caption: Calculated total density of states (TDOS) for the C0 specimen, with the dashed line marking the Fermi energy level.
summary: This panel displays the calculated total density of states for the C0 material. The plot illustrates the electronic structure characteristics, specifically highlighting the position of the Fermi energy level with a dashed line, which serves as a reference point for analyzing the electronic properties of the C0 system.

caption: Probability distribution of global warming potential for 30% hemp content mix, showing a reduced environmental impact range with a lower maximum value of 0.667.
summary: At 30% hemp content, the Monte Carlo analysis reveals a further reduction in environmental impact. The distribution exhibits a decreased maximum value of 0.667 compared to mixtures with lower hemp content, confirming that increasing the hemp proportion effectively shifts the global warming potential toward lower values.

caption: Time-resolved sequence showing the drop generation process for CMC-based NMC cathode ink at a single nozzle.
summary: This panel displays the printability test results for CMC-based NMC cathode ink.
