The sequence of images captures the drop generation process at a single nozzle, providing a visual assessment of the ink's behavior during the printing process as part of the broader evaluation of prepared cathode inks.

caption: Three-dimensional surface topography of the A2 sample wear track, showing the characteristic abrasion marks and surface profile.
summary: Three-dimensional contours of the wear tracks were generated to characterize the surface damage. The A2 sample 3D reconstruction provides a detailed visualization of the abrasion marks and surface profile, contributing to the comparative analysis of wear resistance across the different material samples tested under a 150 N load.

caption: CAD model of the Gyroid lattice structure viewed from the top.
summary: The CAD model of the Gyroid lattice structure is shown from a top-view perspective. This model serves as the primary design reference for the LPBF fabrication process, enabling a quantitative comparison between the intended structural parameters and the actual dimensions of the manufactured lattice.

caption: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO model at 5 T magnetic induction intensity.
summary: This panel illustrates the pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO system at 5 T. By examining the seven chemical order types, the results highlight the influence of high magnetic induction on the local atomic ordering within the high CSRO system during the simulation cycles.

caption: Comparison of DIC-measured and FEM-simulated plastic strain values within the weld seam pattern during perpendicular deformation for streamlined and blunt bridge geometries, with dashed light grey lines indicating a ±3% strain deviation threshold.
summary: This plot provides a quantitative comparison between DIC-measured and FEM-simulated plastic strain values near the weld seam during perpendicular deformation. By evaluating both streamlined and blunt bridge configurations, the data highlights the accuracy of the simulation against experimental measurements, with a ±3% strain deviation threshold used to assess performance.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map obtained at the mid-thickness of the first deposited layer L1, near the interface with the SS304 substrate.
summary: This IPF map of the bottom layer L1 shows a microstructure with slightly larger grains compared to the top layer, averaging 18 μm. The region displays a comparatively weaker texture and a higher degree of recrystallization, approximately 72%, which is associated with a high density of high-angle grain boundaries near the interface.

caption: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFT) image of the selected area, illustrating the distribution of dislocations in the distorted regions.
summary: The Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFT) image illustrates the distribution of dislocations in the distorted regions of the Ti-0.4O-3Fe alloy. Consistent with observations in areas of severe distortion, a large number of dislocations were formed, confirming the high-strain state of the as-fabricated L-PBF microstructure.

caption: Specific energy loss measurements plotted as a function of excitation frequency for DED-printed FeSi, reflecting the influence of microstructural features and residual stresses.
summary: Specific losses for the DED-printed FeSi are presented across various excitation frequencies. These measurements demonstrate how the inherent microstructural features and residual stresses resulting from the DED manufacturing process influence the energy dissipation characteristics of the material, offering insight into its performance under different operating conditions.

caption: Vertical cross-section image of sample (a) extracted from segmented SXCT data at a specific density point.
summary: This panel displays a vertical cross-section image of sample (a) derived from segmented SXCT data. The microstructure, characterized by particle and pore distribution, shows highly interconnected porosity, making it difficult to observe major differences in the microstructure compared to other initial samples in the series.

caption: Force–time response of the I-WP TPMS topology subjected to low-speed impact penetration using a 20 mm hemispherical indenter at 220 J energy.
summary: I-WP TPMS topology force-time data is presented for low-speed impact penetration tests conducted at 220 J with a 20 mm hemispherical indenter. The smoothened plots, generated from three separate repetitions, provide a detailed visualization of the force evolution over time, highlighting the mechanical response characteristics of the I-WP lattice structure.

caption: Structural model 2 incorporating the FeAl2 framework with additional Al atoms occupying the Al2 sites.
summary: Model 2 extends the FeAl2 framework by including Al atoms in the Al2 sites. This configuration is used to calculate the overlapped atomic volume during (001) slip, allowing for the assessment of how specific Al site occupancy influences the structural behavior and atomic interactions during shear deformation processes.

caption: Yield strength boxplot distribution, where the red ellipse highlights a reduced sample size of three specimens due to failures outside the gauge section.
summary: Yield strength data is summarized in a boxplot, showing a downward trend similar to UTS. The red oval region indicates a reduced dataset of three specimens instead of five, as fracture stress was used as the UTS value for samples that failed outside the gauge section.

caption: Atomic force microscopy height image of the bulk surface of an AAO sample containing 1 wt% LNC, showing surface morphology and crack propagation direction.
summary: This AFM height image displays the surface morphology of an AAO sample with 1 wt% LNC. The observed surface features indicate the direction of crack propagation during sample fracturing. The morphology highlights the submicron scale structural characteristics of the material following the incorporation of LNCs into the polymer matrix.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of methacrylated gelatin (GelMA) displaying characteristic peaks at 5.3–5.5 ppm for vinylic protons, 2.9 ppm for lysine methylene protons, and 1.8 ppm for methacryloyl methyl groups.
summary: Methacrylated gelatin (GelMA) is characterized by specific 1H NMR signals confirming successful modification. The spectrum exhibits peaks at 5.3–5.5 ppm corresponding to vinylic protons, 2.9 ppm for lysine methylene protons, and 1.8 ppm for methacryloyl methyl groups, demonstrating the effective grafting of methacrylate groups onto the gelatin molecular chains.

caption: XRD patterns (d, e, g) for Ni-Co-W alloy films W-R9, W-R11, and W-R12 produced in bath 2 at a constant temperature with varying W solution concentrations, revealing both Co hexagonal and Ni face-centered cubic (fcc) reflections.
summary: XRD analysis of Ni-Co-W films W-R9, W-R11, and W-R12, produced using bath 2 containing sodium citrate, shows distinct structural characteristics. Unlike bath 1, these films exhibit reflections (1,1,1) and (0,2,2) associated with the Ni face-centered cubic structure, alongside the Co hexagonal reflections, indicating the influence of citrate on the final crystalline phase.

caption: Schematic representation of Sample A, which is initially prepared through furnace recrystallization at 1200 °C for 3 hours prior to in-situ X-ray acquisition.
summary: Sample A represents the furnace-recrystallized condition used for in-situ X-ray acquisition. This specimen undergoes a heat treatment at 1200 °C for 3 hours to achieve a fully recrystallized state before being subjected to the experimental laser-treatment monitoring process, where peak width evolution is tracked over time.

caption: Statistical distribution of deviations from the target 20 mm layer width for blocks B1, B2, and B3.
summary: The box plot provides a comparative analysis of the width distributions for the three blocks relative to the 20 mm target. It quantifies the deviation in layer width, demonstrating the effectiveness of the feedback control system in minimizing variability and maintaining dimensional accuracy across the printed structures B2 and B3.

caption: Constant current discharge curves for four distinct aluminum alloy anodes evaluated across varying current densities.
summary: This plot displays the constant current discharge behavior of four aluminum alloy anodes under different current densities. The data reveals that these alloys exhibit similar discharge profiles. Furthermore, the discharge voltage for all four anode materials consistently decreases as the applied discharge current density increases during the electrochemical testing process.

caption: Digital Image Correlation (DIC) displacement field map of a full-scale assembled bridge structure subjected to the Ultimate Limit State (ULS) design load.
summary: This DIC displacement field map illustrates the structural response of a full-scale bridge under ULS design loading conditions. The visualization reveals a largely symmetrical displacement pattern across the structure, with the most significant downward vertical displacement occurring at the midspan, confirming the expected mechanical behavior of the bridge assembly.

caption: Extent of Stage I deformation plotted against normalized stacking fault energy (SFE/μb) for [1-23]-oriented HEA and MEA single crystals tested in tension at room temperature.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between the extent of Stage I deformation and the normalized stacking fault energy for various HEA and MEA single crystals at room temperature. The data reveals a roughly concave-upward correlation, indicating how SFE influences the initial stage of plastic deformation in these materials.

caption: Larsen-Miller parameter curves comparing SaTNC model predictions (dotted lines) against experimental data (full lines) for six Ni-based single-crystal superalloys, alongside a secondary plot displaying the model-estimated creep activation energy Q and stress index n values.
summary: This panel presents the Larsen-Miller curves for six Ni-based single-crystal superalloys, demonstrating the accuracy of the SaTNC model in predicting creep behavior. The model's performance is validated by comparing predicted curves and parameters, specifically creep activation energy Q and stress index n, against experimental values, confirming the model's predictive reliability.

caption: (110) and (200) pole figures representing the crystallographic texture of the as-built sample.
summary: The (110) and (200) pole figures provide a statistical representation of the crystallographic texture within the as-built microstructure. By plotting the orientation of specific lattice planes, these figures quantify the degree of preferred orientation, offering a clear view of the material's texture intensity and symmetry following the fabrication process.

caption: Violin-box plots displaying the seasonal and yearly distribution of in-situ high water levels (HWL) and low water levels (LWL) at Rosses Point, Sligo, with red and blue shading denoting HWL and LWL distributions respectively.
summary: This violin-box plot illustrates tidal dynamics at Rosses Point, Sligo, over 16 years. Red and blue shaded regions represent HWL and LWL distributions, respectively, with dotted lines indicating mean values. Seasonal analysis reveals higher mean HWL in autumn and winter, while a slight decline in overall water level variability is observed.

caption: Bode modulus plot for the SP2 sample, demonstrating its impedance response characteristics.
summary: This Bode modulus plot displays the impedance magnitude for the SP2 sample. Consistent with the Nyquist plot findings, this data confirms the higher interfacial resistance of SP2 compared to other samples, indicating that the film provides a more effective barrier against corrosive environments.

caption: Toughness increment ΔKIC, calculated as the difference between ZTA and Al2O3 fracture toughness, plotted as a function of relative density.
summary: The toughness increment ΔKIC, defined as the difference between the fracture toughness of ZTA and Al2O3, is plotted against relative density. This graph quantifies the enhancement in fracture resistance achieved by the ZTA composite compared to pure alumina, highlighting the impact of densification on the material's overall mechanical performance.

caption: Distribution of longitudinal residual stress in sample S4 with 100 layers, characterized by synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
summary: The longitudinal residual stress distribution for sample S4 with 100 layers is evaluated using synchrotron X-ray diffraction. This method provides a detailed spatial assessment of the stress state within the thin-wall structure, complementing the hole-drilling data used for samples with fewer layers to characterize the overall stress profile.

caption: Calculated potential-pO2- diagram for Iron in LiCl-KCl at 450 °C, assuming an activity of 10^-6 for FeClx, with the TiCl2 stability domain highlighted in grey.
summary: Representing the potential-pO2- stability for Iron in LiCl-KCl at 450 °C, this panel shows the impact of TiCl2 on the salt's electroactive range. Iron is partially within its immunity domain under these conditions, demonstrating the influence of the amphoteric TiCl2 compound on the electrochemical stability of the system.

caption: Training and validation accuracy curves for the CNN model reproduced using information from the original paper combined with a self-defined hyperparameter search.
summary: This panel presents the training and validation accuracy curves for the CNN model. The reproduction process incorporated both the original paper's information and a self-defined hyperparameter search. These curves demonstrate how the addition of a systematic hyperparameter optimization process influences the model's learning performance and overall accuracy metrics.

caption: Comparison of number-average (Mn) and weight-average (Mw) molecular weights for PLA powder, filament, and scaffold, alongside the PL90 composite filament and scaffold.
summary: This table presents the results of SEC analyses comparing the number-average (Mn) and weight-average (Mw) molecular weights across various PLA and PL90 composite forms. It details the molecular weight characteristics for initial powder, processed filaments, and scaffolds, providing a quantitative overview of the material properties throughout the fabrication process.

caption: EDS mapping of the Ni-11.1Si-3Cr powder illustrating the distribution of nickel, silicon, and chromium.
summary: The EDS mapping of the Ni-11.1Si-3Cr powder visualizes the spatial distribution of the constituent elements. This analysis confirms the impact of chromium on the alloy's phase distribution. Together with SEM images and point analysis, these results highlight the microstructural evolution compared to the base Ni-12Si alloy powder.

caption: Elastic modulus trend along the corrosion depth for AlCrFeNi and 316L, highlighting a sudden change in 316L at 10 μm where the modulus increases from 146.23 GPa to 190.97 GPa.
summary: Elastic modulus profiles along the corrosion depth reveal varying mechanical stability. While AlCrFeNi shows a relatively smooth trend, 316L undergoes a sudden change in elastic modulus at a depth of 10 μm, where the value increases significantly from 146.23 GPa to 190.97 GPa, reflecting the transition to the matrix.

caption: Magnitude of the Fourier transform of k2-weighted χ(k) spectra at Ni and Co K-edges for all samples.
summary: The magnitude of the Fourier transform of k2-weighted χ(k) spectra is shown for both Ni and Co K-edges. These plots represent the best fit for the Ni1Co3@NC sample, providing structural information derived from the EXAFS data to characterize the local coordination environment of the metallic species.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the punch corner region under DD conditions at room temperature.
summary: Focusing on the punch corner region under DD conditions at room temperature, this inverse pole figure map provides insight into the local crystallographic texture. It is instrumental for analyzing the grain orientation shifts that occur during deep drawing, highlighting the structural response of the material at this specific location.

caption: Transmission spectra of Zn1−xNixTe films showing the band gap energy determination.
summary: Transmission spectra are utilized to determine the band gap energy of Zn1−xNixTe thin films. These optical measurements provide the foundational data for assessing how the electronic structure of the material evolves with varying nickel content, consistent with results derived from independent ellipsometry data analysis.

caption: Three-dimensional renderings of defect distributions within the region of interest (ROI) alongside the defined coordinate system and defect parameter definitions.
summary: This figure presents the region of interest and the assigned coordinate system utilized during the micro-CT measurement process. Three-dimensional renderings illustrate the spatial distribution of defects within the samples. Furthermore, the figure establishes the specific definitions for the three defect parameters analyzed for each sample in the study.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the alloy aged at 900 °C for 100 h, showing the long-term distribution of primary γ' precipitates.
summary: After 100 hours of isothermal ageing at 900 °C, the dark-field TEM micrograph captures the microstructure of the Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 alloy. The inset SAED pattern, taken along the [001] zone axis using the (110) reflection of the γ' precipitates, provides insight into the long-term stability and structural characteristics of the primary γ' phase.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the 96MCA-MES integrated with a green PCB adapter for bottom-side electrical contacting, alongside a photograph of the custom-developed frontend interface for individual well unit connectivity.
summary: This panel shows the cross-sectional view of the 96MCA-MES substrate integrated with a PCB frame for rerouting electrode contacts. The accompanying image displays the self-developed frontend hardware used for contacting all single well units, confirming the successful fabrication of the microcavity and patterned microelectrodes in each well.

caption: Dark field TEM image obtained using the (0 ̅1 2) reflection of Ni3Ti, highlighting the distribution of the precipitate phase.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging using the (0 ̅1 2) reflection of Ni3Ti provides a clear visualization of the precipitate phase within the as-built microstructure. The increased intensity observed around the center of the diffraction pattern, combined with blurred spots, suggests the presence of an amorphous or partly crystalline shell.

caption: Raman peak shift (ΔV) of the R2 line measured from the Al2O3 layer on TiAlCr alloys after 100 h of oxidation at 1100 °C, comparing free-doped, 0.4Y-doped, and 0.4Hf-doped samples.
summary: This panel displays the Raman R2 line peak shift (ΔV) for TiAlCr alloys oxidized at 1100 °C for 100 h. The data reveals that the free-doped alloy exhibits the largest shift, followed by the 0.4Y-doped and 0.4Hf-doped variants, indicating that Hf doping results in the lowest residual stress in the Al2O3 layer.

caption: Statistical evaluation of the trabecular number (Tb.N) within the bone tunnel region, measured via Micro-CT analysis to assess bone microarchitecture (n = 4).
summary: The trabecular number (Tb.N) is quantified using micro-CT analysis to evaluate the microarchitecture of the newly formed bone. This bar chart presents the Tb.N values for the different scaffold groups, serving as a key metric alongside BV/TV to support the findings regarding bone formation and integration.

caption: Impact energy comparison of non-FGM specimens (G100, C100, O100) and FGM specimens (P1, P2, P3) at 100% infill density.
summary: This plot illustrates the impact energy performance of various 3D-printed specimens, specifically comparing non-FGM samples (G100, C100, O100) against functionally graded material (FGM) samples (P1, P2, P3). All specimens were fabricated with a 100% infill density to evaluate the influence of different infill patterns on overall impact strength and energy absorption.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module under varying insolation and temperature conditions, modeled using the PEC1 approach.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of the mSi0188 solar module, evaluated under simultaneous variations in temperature and irradiance. By utilizing the PEC1 model, the plot provides a comparison between rescaled theoretical characteristics and experimentally measured values, effectively demonstrating the module's performance under realistic solar operating conditions.

caption: Three-dimensional view of the 316L simulation domain, measuring 2000 × 2000 × 4500 μm³.
summary: This panel presents a 3D visualization of the simulation domain for the 316L sample, which encompasses a volume of 2000 × 2000 × 4500 μm³. This spatial representation serves as the foundation for the subsequent microstructural analysis and melt pool characterization performed within the simulated domain.

caption: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) image highlighting the periodic dislocations at the Fe–TiB2 interface that accommodate lattice mismatch.
summary: The Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) image clearly distinguishes the lattice fringes from both the α-Fe and TiB2 phases. It reveals good interface bonding characterized by periodic dislocations, which effectively accommodate the lattice mismatch between the two phases, ensuring structural stability of the composite.

caption: Cube-frame structure consisting of pre-existing inner and outer frames, captured at a 1 cm scale.
summary: This image presents a cube-frame structure featuring both inner and outer frames as existing components. These frames serve as the base substrate for subsequent additive manufacturing steps, demonstrating the versatility of the levitation 3D printing method in building upon complex, pre-existing geometric configurations.

caption: BF-STEM micrograph of as-received Alloy 625 showing the nanoindent orientation marked by a white triangle and the resulting lobes of extreme strain indicated by red dashed lines.
summary: This BF-STEM micrograph displays the deformation microstructure of as-received Alloy 625 following nanoindentation. The image highlights the specific orientation of the nanoindent, denoted by a white triangle, and clearly delineates the lobes of extreme strain generated beneath the indent using red dashed lines to visualize the localized plastic deformation.

caption: TG-DSC thermal analysis profile of the PA@CCF composite filament.
summary: Thermogravimetric data for the PA@CCF composite filament confirms a CCF mass fraction of 30 wt%, which aligns with the initial feed ratio. This thermal analysis demonstrates the successful incorporation of carbon fibers into the polymer matrix, providing quantitative verification of the composite composition through mass loss observation.

caption: Atomic model of the Cu (100) surface showing a surface atomic monolayer step in magenta atop the blue bulk, with Site A labeled as the active dissolution corner and white arrows indicating potential dissolution directions.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the Cu (100) surface with a surface monolayer step. Site A represents the most active dissolution corner, where charge transfer is most favorable due to weak electrostatic interactions. White arrows indicate the possible directions for atomic dissolution from this specific step edge configuration.

caption: Temperature dependence of thermal expansion (ΔL/L0) for polycrystalline Ni2.15Mn0.70Cr0.15Ga, comparing measurements taken under zero field and a 5 T magnetic field.
summary: This panel displays the thermal expansion behavior of the Ni2.15Mn0.70Cr0.15Ga compound. By plotting ΔL/L0 against temperature, the graph illustrates how the material responds to thermal changes under both zero-field and 5 T magnetic field conditions, providing insight into the thermal expansion characteristics of this specific polycrystalline alloy.

caption: Schematic representation of the one-end-heating configuration where the IR-heater is positioned at a single extremity of the beam.
summary: This schematic illustrates the Case-1 experimental setup, designed to subject the beam to non-uniform thermal loading. The IR-heater is specifically positioned at one end of the beam to induce one-end-heating conditions, allowing for the study of thermal gradients across the specimen under controlled, asymmetric heating parameters.

caption: Elastic modulus of YSZ electrolytes plotted against indenter penetration depth, comparing samples prepared via cold isostatic pressing (CIP) and gel-casting (GC) techniques.
summary: This plot illustrates the elastic modulus of YSZ electrolytes as a function of indenter penetration depth. The data, obtained through nanoindentation, allows for a direct comparison of the mechanical behavior between zirconia ceramics fabricated using cold isostatic pressing and gel-casting methods at a micrometric scale.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for BJ3DP TiC-FeCr cermet sintered at 1400 °C.
summary: This histogram illustrates the particle size distribution of BJ3DP TiC-FeCr cermets sintered at 1400 °C. The data, derived from calculated grain sizes, demonstrates the influence of this specific sintering temperature on the resulting microstructure, providing a quantitative representation of the grain size distribution within the consolidated material.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph of the low B & C variant after cooling at 5 °C/min from 1080 °C.
summary: Presented is a backscattered electron micrograph showing the microstructure of the low B & C variant alloy. The sample underwent a cooling process at a rate of 5 °C/min from 1080 °C. This visualization highlights the distinct microstructural arrangement and phase characteristics resulting from the lower B & C content.

caption: Micro-CT grayscale slice image detailing internal crack morphology for the 0.4–0.4 frequency CL specimen.
summary: This micro-CT slice image captures the internal failure state of the 0.4–0.4 frequency CL specimen. Analysis shows that delamination cracks in the troughs are concentrated in the middle region, while through-layer cracks in the crests appear noticeably shorter, confirming the influence of structural parameters on crack propagation.

caption: Transmittance spectra of A-CNC/CTFA composite resins plotted across the wavelength range for varying acrylation reaction times.
summary: The transmittance spectrum of the A-CNC/CTFA composite resin demonstrates a notable improvement in transparency within the 380–420 nm range as the acrylation reaction time increases. This spectral data confirms that modifying the reaction duration effectively enhances the optical clarity of the composite resin system.

caption: Representative ΔL and CTE curves for the C-T structure, where a kink in the ΔL displacement curve at 20 °C corresponds to a distinct jump in the derivative CTE curve, indicating a switch in bulging direction.
summary: This panel displays the ΔL and CTE curves derived from simulations for the C-T structure. A notable kink appears in the ΔL curve at 20 °C, which signifies a change in the bulging direction. This transition manifests as a sharp jump in the calculated CTE curve, illustrating the thermal expansion behavior.

caption: Custom-designed substrate cooling system comprising a water-cooling machine, a copper water-cooling plate, and a fixed fixture.
summary: This schematic illustrates the custom-designed substrate cooling system integrated into the experimental setup. The assembly includes a water-cooling machine, a copper water-cooling plate, and a fixed fixture, which are essential components for maintaining thermal control during the deposition process as depicted in the figure.

caption: Thermal distribution heatmap of the gear specimen subjected to heat sink cooling at 240 s, marking the end of the coating process.
summary: This heatmap visualizes the thermal profile of the gear specimen at 240 s under heat sink cooling conditions. By capturing the temperature at the end of the coating process, it demonstrates the influence of the heat sink on the initial thermal distribution compared to the untreated baseline.

caption: t-SNE embedding plot visualizing the latent space representation of FLOW-3D melt pool simulations, where samples with the largest depth are clustered in the top-left region.
summary: This t-SNE embedding plot visualizes the latent space learned by a transformer model from FLOW-3D melt pool simulations. Each point represents a compressed read-out token for a specific sample. The visualization reveals intuitive trends, specifically showing that melt pool samples with the largest depth are concentrated in the top-left region of the plot.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping showing the spatial distribution of B, N, Al, Co, Ni, Nb, and W elements across the interface region defined in panel a.
summary: The EDS mapping illustrates the elemental composition and distribution of B, N, Al, Co, Ni, Nb, and W at the cBN/Ni-superalloy interface. This visualization confirms the presence and localization of these specific elements, providing critical chemical context for the reaction layers observed in the corresponding TEM image.

caption: Raman analysis of the reference wear track edges, identifying the presence of amorphous carbon species.
summary: Raman spectroscopy performed on the reference sample wear track provides chemical identification of the surface products. The analysis confirms the presence of amorphous carbon species located along the edges of the wear track, providing insight into the tribochemical reactions occurring during the wear process in the reference scenario.

caption: STEM-EDX elemental map showing the distribution of oxygen (yellow) extracted from the spectrum image dataset, corresponding to the oxidized regions on the fracture surface.
summary: This STEM-EDX elemental map visualizes the distribution of oxygen across the fracture surface. The yellow signal highlights the oxidized regions, providing a clear spatial correlation with the metallic Ni layers and the previously identified oxide phases, confirming the extent of oxidation on the Alloy 690 fracture surface.

caption: CO2 conversion performance for 3D-printed structures with varying fiber sizes, utilizing a consistent 1-1 design configuration.
summary: CO2 conversion is evaluated for structures featuring different fiber sizes while maintaining a 1-1 design. The plot demonstrates how fiber dimensions influence the catalytic activity of the Mo x C/Al 2 O 3 structures. These measurements were conducted at 0.1 MPa with a GHSV of 12,000 h-1 to ensure reliable performance comparisons.

caption: Immunofluorescence micrographs of co-culture μvessels stained for ZO-1 (cyan), γ-H2AX (red), and Phalloidin (green), demonstrating the structural organization and DNA damage markers under different shear stress conditions.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging of co-culture μvessels reveals the spatial distribution of ZO-1, γ-H2AX, and Phalloidin. These micrographs provide visual evidence of cellular responses to mechanical stimuli, specifically highlighting the localization of DNA damage markers and tight junction proteins within the endothelial and smooth muscle cell channels of the μvessel device.

caption: Specific force versus compressive strain for Onyx specimens in Type 1 and Type 2 configurations.
summary: Onyx specimens in Type 1 and Type 2 configurations exhibit specific force-compressive strain curves that demonstrate lower plateau forces and specific energy absorption compared to the neat PA samples. This mechanical testing highlights the performance differences between the base material and the Onyx composite under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Partial instance diagram of the FIM data structure, highlighting functional groups including the spatial structure, BIM component model, and fabrication data.
summary: This schematic illustrates the FIM data structure, which is organized into distinct functional groups. The spatial structure is linked to the IfcProject via aggregation, while the BIM component model serves as the essential core. Additionally, the fabrication data section defines the motion and tool behavior of the AM system.

caption: Reconstructed 3D surface topography of bare PEEK sample without plasma treatment (WOP).
summary: This panel presents the 3D surface topography of a bare PEEK sample without plasma treatment. Profilometry analysis indicates the presence of spots and holes on the surface, which were exposed following the removal of printing structures during the grinding process, characterizing the baseline surface state.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for the steel simulated at a peak temperature of 900 °C with a grain size of 25 μm.
summary: Simulated CCT diagram for steel processed at 900 °C, specifically showing the transformation kinetics for a 25 μm grain size. The simulation utilizes JMatPro to predict microstructural outcomes, incorporating reference cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s to evaluate the impact of grain size on phase formation.

caption: Arrhenius plots representing the temperature dependence of the polarization resistance (Rp) for symmetric cells, with impedance values divided by two.
summary: Arrhenius plots of Rp for the symmetric cells are presented to determine the activation energy (Ea) of the electrochemical processes. The low activation energies observed for the Ni-SSn 10 DC anode contribute to the high catalytic activity and superior performance of the cell in the intermediate temperature range.

caption: Torque evolution curves illustrating the impact of varying PMMA types and blade rotational speeds during the compounding of PMMA/PVB/PEG-based binders at 160 °C.
summary: This plot displays the torque evolution during the compounding of PMMA/PVB/PEG-based binders at 160 °C. It specifically examines how different PMMA types and varying blade rotational speeds influence the compounding behavior, providing insight into the processing dynamics of these feedstock compositions under controlled mechanical shear conditions.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of secondary γ′ precipitates oriented along the [001]γ zone axis, with the inset showing the corresponding SAED pattern highlighting superlattice reflections.
summary: Captured from a FIB lamella lift-out, this HAADF-STEM image shows the cuboidal morphology of secondary γ′ precipitates along the [001]γ zone axis. The inset SAED pattern provides further evidence of the ordered structure through the clear visibility of superlattice spots in the diffraction data.

caption: Comparative length distribution profiles for Fibers A, B, and C, showing the frequency of fiber lengths.
summary: Comparative length distribution profiles for Fibers A, B, and C were generated after 5,000 iterations of image analysis. The data reveals that 84% of Fiber A, 46% of Fiber B, and 45% of Fiber C consist of short carbon fibers measuring 100 µm or less in length.

caption: Bar chart comparing the abrasive wear volume loss in cubic millimeters for Ti64 processed via Method A and ETi64 processed via Method B.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the abrasive wear performance of two titanium variants, Ti64 and ETi64, subjected to different processing methods, A and B respectively. The results, presented as volume loss in cubic millimeters, provide a comparative assessment of material durability under abrasive conditions as tested in a randomized experimental sequence.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of variant B viewed along the [ 2 ‾ 0 1] III zone axis.
summary: Captured from variant B along the [ 2 ‾ 0 1] III zone axis, this SAED pattern contributes to the crystallographic characterization of the variant pair. Analysis of these diffraction patterns at specific tilt angles allows for the classification of orientation relationships between the lamellae within the NM martensitic variant group.

caption: Bar chart comparing the loss moduli (G″) of different hydrogel groups, demonstrating the influence of microgel alignment on viscoelastic behavior.
summary: Loss modulus (G″) measurements reveal significant differences between the hydrogel groups based on their microgel architecture. The viscoelastic properties, characterized using the ElastoSense Bio system, show that structural anisotropy plays a critical role in determining the mechanical performance of the printed hydrogel constructs.

caption: Inverse pole figure map showing the crystallographic texture of the XY plane subjected to 5% strain along the X-direction.
summary: Crystallographic texture evolution is visualized here for the XY plane following a 5% strain applied in the X-direction. The eutectic Si network plays a critical role in this microstructural evolution by restricting plastic deformation and promoting dislocation accumulation at its interfaces, thereby influencing the local dislocation behavior during the deformation process.

caption: Stress-strain curves for 3D filament-based scaffolds, illustrating the mechanical response of PCL, PP20, and PP20CS50 variants before and after the leaching process.
summary: The stress-strain curves for 3D filament-based scaffolds, including PCL, PP20, and PP20CS50, are presented to characterize their mechanical behavior. These curves demonstrate the response of the constructs before and after the leaching process, providing the necessary data to determine the elastic modulus based on the slope in the linear region.

caption: Coarsening curves of M23C6 carbides modeled at 750, 800, and 850 °C, where the interfacial energy is temperature-dependent, ranging from 0.285 J/m2 at 750 °C to 0.245 J/m2 at 850 °C.
summary: The coarsening behavior of M23C6 carbides is modeled here using TC-PRISMA. Unlike the γ′ phase, the interfacial energy for M23C6 is shown to vary significantly with temperature. The simulation utilizes a specific temperature-dependent equation to accurately predict the precipitation and growth kinetics of these carbides within the alloy system.

caption: Comparison of experimental and simulated load-displacement (H-h) curves at a loading rate of 100 mN/min.
summary: This panel shows the H-h curve for a loading rate of 100 mN/min, comparing experimental results against simulation outputs. The consistent agreement between the two datasets confirms that the nanoindentation response is sensitive to low strain rates, further highlighting the significant influence of these rates on the indentation mechanical response.

caption: Comparison of three-body abrasive wear performance for SAW, PTAW, and TIG hardfacings, demonstrating the significant reduction in wear rates achieved through the addition of Cr3C2–Ni particles to the matrix.
summary: This plot compares three-body abrasive wear test results for SAW, PTAW, and TIG hardfacings. The addition of Cr3C2–Ni particles to the Fe or Ni-based matrix significantly improves wear resistance, reducing wear by 1.4 to 1.8 times for SAW, 8.1–8.4 times for PTAW, and 4.1–9.0 times for TIG hardfacings.

caption: Electrical resistivity profiles for Fe26.7Ni26.7Ga15.6Mn20Si11 high entropy thin films as a function of temperature, comparing as-evaporated and 700 K annealed states under zero and 1 T magnetic fields.
summary: Resistivity measurements for Fe26.7Ni26.7Ga15.6Mn20Si11 thin films reveal temperature-dependent behavior between 300 and 550 K. The difference between zero-field and 1 T magnetic field resistivity decreases as temperature increases, suggesting that certain material defects begin to diminish at higher temperatures during the measurement process.

caption: Quantitative data summary of average Geometrically Necessary Dislocation (GND) densities for AB-V specimens at specific strain rates.
summary: This data table provides the quantitative values for average GND density at strain rates of 3699, 5650, and 7452 s⁻¹, recorded as 2.4, 5.39, and 5.56 × 10¹⁴/m², respectively. These figures confirm the trend of increasing dislocation density as the dynamic impact strain rate increases during the compression tests.

caption: Experimental polarization curve of the NAB alloy measured under quiescent conditions.
summary: This panel displays the experimental polarization curve for the NAB alloy under quiescent conditions. It serves as the baseline measurement for evaluating the corrosion process of the alloy, providing a reference point for comparing the electrochemical behavior observed under more complex cavitation erosion-corrosion conditions with or without applied loading stress.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the selectivity of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film across various VOCs, highlighting a 3 to 5-fold higher sensing response to 1.32 ppm formaldehyde compared to interfering gases.
summary: This radar chart demonstrates the superior selectivity of the PCN-224/MoB-MBene composite film for formaldehyde detection. The analysis reveals that the composite sensor exhibits a significantly higher sensing response, specifically 3 to 5 times greater, toward 1.32 ppm formaldehyde when compared to other interfering volatile organic compounds.

caption: White light interferometry profile of a carbon black straight segment showing material distribution.
summary: White light interferometry profile of a carbon black straight segment showing material distribution. This visualization provides a detailed surface topography analysis of the printed raster pattern. The data reveals the structural consistency of the carbon black material, noting that larger spikes observed are attributed to dust particles magnified by the vertical axis.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map of vertically printed SS316L, illustrating elongated columnar grain structures along the vertical axis.
summary: The IPF image reveals distinct grain morphologies within the vertically printed SS316L sample. It shows a columnar structure in the XOZ plane and an equiaxed structure in the XOY plane, clarifying the development of columnar grains along the vertical axis as a result of the LPBF processing conditions.

caption: Backscattered electron image of the L-PBF S2 sample surface, providing a representative view of the post-corrosion microstructure.
summary: This backscattered electron image captures the L-PBF S2 sample surface after potentiodynamic polarisation testing. The microstructure exhibits localized corrosion attack consistent with the other L-PBF samples. The image serves as a representative view of the corrosion morphology observed in the L-PBF fabricated material following the electrochemical testing procedure.

caption: As-built single-track surface morphology and corresponding high-speed camera melt pool image for an extra Ar flow rate of 7.5 l/min.
summary: Displayed is the as-built single-track surface and melt pool image for an extra Ar flow rate of 7.5 l/min. The track exhibits dark oxide film formation concentrated in the middle of the track, indicating that higher Ar flow rates significantly impact the shielding environment and resulting surface oxidation patterns.

caption: Laser microscope image of the GH4169 specimen surface fabricated using the continuous repeated heat input mode.
summary: Surface morphology of the GH4169 specimen produced through the continuous repeated heat input mode is shown here. The measured surface roughness (Sa) for this specimen is 12.33 μm, indicating the specific surface texture and quality achieved under this thermal input mode during the laser powder bed fusion fabrication process.

caption: Storage modulus (E′) as a function of temperature for annealed PEKK/MRS composites printed at a 90° orientation.
summary: Storage modulus (E′) values for annealed PEKK/MRS composites printed at 90° are shown here. This dynamic mechanical analysis curve illustrates the thermomechanical response of the annealed samples, allowing for a direct comparison of how the annealing process influences the stiffness and mechanical integrity of the different composite compositions.

caption: CMWP fitting of the bcc β-phase XRD pattern for the heat-treated (AB + HT) sample, showing the measured data, calculated fit, and residual difference, alongside an inset providing a magnified view of the 200 peak to demonstrate fitting precision.
summary: Representative CMWP fitting results for the heat-treated (AB + HT) sample are presented to characterize the bcc β-phase dislocation density. The XRD pattern demonstrates a precise fit between the experimental and calculated data, with the 200 peak magnification confirming the reliability of the structural analysis performed via the XLPA method.

caption: Equivalent diameter versus sphericity distribution of defects for the P280-V800 sample, providing a quantitative assessment of defect size and shape regularity.
summary: This scatter plot presents the equivalent diameter and sphericity of defects found in the P280-V800 sample. By plotting these parameters, the figure quantifies the defect characteristics, allowing for a comparison of defect types within the specimen. The distribution of data points indicates the prevalence of specific defect morphologies relative to the processing conditions.

caption: Ashby plot illustrating the variation of high cycle fatigue strength (at 10^6 cycles) as a function of relative density (ρ / ρ s) for as-built and hirtised specimens.
summary: This Ashby plot displays the relationship between high cycle fatigue strength and relative density for as-built and hirtised materials. It serves as a baseline to visualize how fatigue performance varies with density across different processing conditions, providing a foundational comparison for the subsequent normalized fatigue strength analysis presented in the study.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the GNP phase identified at the interface, confirming its crystalline nature.
summary: The SAED pattern of the GNP phase at the interface displays sharp diffraction spots, indicating high crystallinity. This confirms the presence of graphene nanoplatelets within the composite structure, which coexist with the Fe matrix and TiC phases at the interface of the Ti3SiC2 particles.

caption: Isometric view of the axisymmetric nozzle geometry.
summary: This isometric representation illustrates the specific geometry of the axisymmetric nozzle (AA). The visualization provides a clear spatial understanding of the nozzle's structural design, which is essential for analyzing its fluid dynamics and performance characteristics within the context of the experimental setup described in the study.

caption: Force-displacement curves comparing experimental and numerical results for sandwich structures with varying face sheet thicknesses.
summary: This panel displays force-displacement curves for sandwich structures with different face sheet thicknesses. By comparing experimental data with numerical results, the plot demonstrates that the numerical simulations agree well with the experimental trends, validating the accuracy of the computational model in predicting the mechanical response of the tested sandwich structures.

caption: Bode plots illustrating the impedance magnitude and phase angle as a function of frequency for ATC4 samples after potentiostatic polarization at potentials between 2.6 V and 3.0 V.
summary: Bode plots for the ATC4 alloy show the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude and phase angle following potentiostatic polarization at potentials from 2.6 V to 3.0 V. These results, when compared with LTC4, indicate that the passive film on ATC4 exhibits lower polarization resistance and protectiveness in the repassivation region.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) response of heat-treated samples immersed in S2 solution, featuring experimental data points overlaid with a yellow line representing the electrical equivalent circuit (EEC) model fit.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance behavior of heat-treated samples in S2 solution. The experimental data, shown as black dots, are modeled using an electrical equivalent circuit represented by a yellow line. Two distinct semicircles are visible in the plot, indicating specific electrochemical features of the material system.

caption: Compositional profiles of Ni and Fe across the void region, derived from EELS mapping along the red rectangle indicated in panel (a), showing localized elemental redistribution.
summary: Elemental concentration profiles for Ni and Fe are presented, extracted from EELS mapping across the void region identified in panel (a). The data clearly demonstrate significant Fe depletion and Ni enrichment in the immediate vicinity of the void, providing evidence of radiation-induced segregation effects within the irradiated Ni50Fe50 alloy.

caption: Energy profile along the diffusion pathway for chromium vacancies in Cr2O3 calculated using the Chartier empirical potential.
summary: This panel displays the energy landscape for chromium vacancy diffusion in Cr2O3 using the Chartier potential. Comparisons with other potentials show good qualitative agreement across the diffusion pathways. The plot illustrates the energy variation as the vacancy migrates, providing insight into the stability and kinetics of chromium defects.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of HA-SH/P(AGE-co-G) constructs after 21 days of chondrogenic differentiation, demonstrating homogeneous ECM distribution throughout the scaffold.
summary: Live/dead staining of HA-SH/P(AGE-co-G) constructs reveals a homogeneous distribution of extracellular matrix components following 21 days of chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs. This result represents a significant improvement over previous studies, which typically achieved only pericellular ECM distribution, confirming the efficacy of the 3% (m/v) formulation for cartilage tissue engineering.

caption: Confocal microscopy image of an Ag target surface fabricated via PBF-LB/M at 400 W, 700 mm/min, and 0.2 mm hatch spacing.
summary: Confocal microscopy illustrates the surface characteristics of an Ag target fabricated via PBF-LB/M at 400 W, 700 mm/min, and 0.2 mm hatch spacing. In contrast to higher energy density parameters, these lower energy density conditions result in a much smoother surface finish for the fabricated Ag target.

caption: Micro-CT imaging of the THA-Col + 30% CaP composite, with a scale bar of 5 mm, showing the distribution of CaP particles (white) within the THA-Col gel matrix (black), alongside a comparative analysis of the top and bottom sections of the printing cartridge.
summary: Micro-CT imaging provides a non-destructive visualization of the internal structure of the THA-Col + 30% CaP composite. The images highlight the spatial distribution of the radiopaque calcium phosphate particles within the radiolucent THA-Col gel, allowing for an assessment of particle homogeneity throughout the printing cartridge.

caption: Co–Al equilibrium binary phase diagram illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions of various phases.
summary: This panel displays the Co–Al equilibrium binary phase diagram, which serves as a foundational reference for identifying phases within the material system. The diagram maps the thermodynamic stability of different phases, providing essential context for understanding the phase evolution and composition of the Co–Al alloy system at equilibrium.

caption: EPMA elemental mapping of a Ni–Mo model alloy cross-section, illustrating the distribution of alloying elements after the corrosion process.
summary: The EPMA analysis of the Ni–Mo model alloy cross-section reveals the elemental distribution following corrosion. This map serves as a baseline for understanding the role of Mo in Ni-based alloys, particularly when compared to the Mo-enriched layers observed in more complex ternary alloy systems like Ni–Cr–Mo.

caption: EBSD map of LPBF Alloy 690 fabricated with a Vz build orientation, displaying the grain structure and boundary distribution.
summary: LPBF Alloy 690 fabricated with a Vz build orientation is analyzed via EBSD mapping. The grain structure and boundary distribution in the XZ plane are compared to the wrought Alloy 690 reference, providing insight into how the Vz build orientation influences the microstructure of the LPBF-processed Alloy 690.

caption: Etched cross-sectional microstructure of the noUA specimen showing the baseline solidification morphology.
summary: This panel displays an etched section of the noUA specimen, providing a baseline view of the microstructure. The image serves as a reference for comparing the solidification morphology against the UA specimens, illustrating the initial state of the material before the application of ultrasonic treatment during the solidification process.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of as-received T92 steel showing the arrangement of dislocations and grain boundary precipitates.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the detailed microstructure for the as-received T92 material. The micrograph displays the presence of dislocations and grain boundary precipitates, which are frequently observed features in this alloy, providing essential information regarding the initial microstructural state of the T92 steel used in the investigation.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of CMA used to verify the molecular structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of CMA is provided to further demonstrate and confirm the molecular structure of the synthesized compound. This spectroscopic technique complements the FT-IR data, providing detailed information about the proton environment within the CMA molecule, thereby ensuring accurate identification of the synthesized material as part of the structural analysis.

caption: Fractography of the vertical tensile specimen (A4) tested underwater.
summary: This SEM micrograph displays the fracture surface of a vertical tensile specimen (A4) tested underwater. The image reveals the specific fractographic features associated with vertical loading in an underwater environment, allowing for a comparative analysis of failure mechanisms between different specimen orientations and testing conditions.

caption: Tensile stress-strain behavior of as-extruded wires measured in the extrusion direction (ED).
summary: Tensile stress-strain diagrams for as-extruded wires are presented, illustrating the mechanical response of the material in the extrusion direction. These curves represent the baseline mechanical behavior of the alloy prior to any environmental degradation, providing a reference for evaluating the impact of subsequent processing or exposure conditions on the material's performance.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image showing the edge of a crumpled reduced graphene oxide (rGO) aggregate.
summary: Atomic force microscopy imaging of the rGO sample highlights the edge of a crumpled aggregate. Due to the challenges in achieving well-dispersed suspensions, single flakes were difficult to isolate. The observed rGO aggregate exhibits an average thickness of approximately 45 nm, reflecting its distinct morphological features compared to GO.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectra comparing the four different scaffold compositions, highlighting the presence of characteristic PEKK peaks.
summary: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy analysis of the four distinct scaffolds confirms the presence of characteristic chemical peaks associated with PEKK. These spectral results verify the chemical integrity of the PEKK component across all scaffold variations, supporting the successful incorporation of the polymer within the composite material structure.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the oxide particle inside the Ti(0.1O)–1Y2O3 alloy powder, demonstrating the crystalline nature of the inclusion.
summary: The diffraction pattern shown here was acquired via FE-TEM from the oxide particle located within the Ti(0.1O)–1Y2O3 alloy powder. This pattern provides critical structural information regarding the crystallinity of the oxide inclusion, serving as a complementary characterization to the high-resolution imaging and compositional analysis performed on the same particle.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) micrograph displaying the morphology of synthesized spherical hydroxyapatite (HA) particles.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy reveals the physical morphology of the synthesized hydroxyapatite particles. The micrograph confirms the formation of spherical HA particles, which are produced via the chemical precipitation process. This structural observation is consistent with the nucleation-aggregation-growth mechanism that governs the formation of these specific apatite precipitates.

caption: Polar distribution of parameter ω for the superalloy pre-serviced at 1050°C/100 h.
summary: The polar distribution of parameter ω for the thermally degraded superalloy at 1050°C/100 h is shown here. This plot tracks the evolution of the PR value distribution under elevated temperature conditions, providing insight into how the precipitate-matrix channel structure changes as the γ' precipitates coarsen and coalesce during the pre-servicing treatment.

caption: Time-dependent state-of-charge (SOC) trajectories for the ESS, contrasting the proposed SL method with the ideal reference.
summary: The state-of-charge (SOC) levels of the energy storage system are plotted over time to evaluate the SL method's efficacy. The graph demonstrates how the ESS is deeply discharged to meet system requirements when load demand is high and renewable energy generation is low, specifically during the 1:00–8:00 h interval.

caption: Second-nearest-neighbor (2NN) short-range order (SRO) parameters between nitrogen and metal atoms in Fe70Ni10Cr20 with 10 at.% N.
summary: Second-nearest-neighbor SRO parameters for nitrogen and metal atoms in the Fe70Ni10Cr20 alloy with 10 at.% nitrogen are presented here. These values characterize the local atomic distribution at the second-neighbor shell, illustrating the specific chemical ordering tendencies present in the simulated alloy system at varying conditions.

caption: Galvanostatic performance data showing voltage and Faradaic efficiency trends for a Ni0.75Co0.25-infiltrated cathode SOEC at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻².
summary: Voltage and Faradaic efficiency measurements are presented for a Ni0.75Co0.25-infiltrated cathode SOEC during galvanostatic operation at 750 °C and 0.2 A·cm⁻². These plots characterize the electrochemical behavior of the Ni-Co alloy infiltration, allowing for an assessment of how varying the Ni-Co ratio influences long-term cell performance and efficiency.

caption: Temporal evolution of current density for the STF SOC subjected to repeated voltage pulses between 1.2 V and 0.85 V over a 96-hour cycling period.
summary: The temporal current density profile for the STF SOC demonstrates its stability and response to voltage cycling. By applying pulses between 1.2 V and 0.85 V over 96 hours, the panel tracks the degradation or performance consistency of the STF electrode material under dynamic electrochemical stress conditions.

caption: Total and partial density of states (DOS) for the MoNbTaVW high-entropy alloy, calculated using the XTANT-3 simulation framework relative to the Fermi level.
summary: This plot displays the total and partial density of states for the MoNbTaVW alloy, computed via the XTANT-3 simulation method. These electronic structure data, alongside numerically determined chemical potentials, serve as the foundational input for calculating specific electronic heat capacities at elevated electronic temperatures for this complex metallic system.

caption: Light absorption spectrum of an aqueous 4 × 10^-4 M Sodium Lauryl Sulphate (NaLS) solution, showing an absorption maximum at approximately 200 nm.
summary: The UV-Vis absorption spectrum of an aqueous 4 × 10^-4 M Sodium Lauryl Sulphate solution is presented, highlighting a distinct absorption maximum at approximately 200 nm. This spectral feature is characteristic of NaLS and distinguishes it from other chemical species like fructose, which exhibit absorption maxima at different wavelengths.

caption: Surface roughness (Ra) trends plotted against grinding feed rate, categorized by different cutting speeds of 8, 11.5, and 15 m/s.
summary: This graph demonstrates the interaction between grinding feed rate and cutting speed on surface quality. Increasing the feed rate at 8 and 11.5 m/s increases Ra values by 2.5 and 1.2 times, respectively, whereas a 15 m/s cutting speed produces a reverse trend, resulting in a two-fold reduction in roughness.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the relative stiffness, strength, and toughness of HC-BI1, HC-BI2, CAM-BI1, and CAM-BI2 composite configurations.
summary: This radar chart compares the mechanical properties of HC-BI1, HC-BI2, CAM-BI1, and CAM-BI2 composites. The CAM-BI2 configuration encloses the largest area, representing the best overall fracture resistance. Furthermore, CAM-BI2 exhibits a 16% improvement in stiffness, strength, and toughness over the HC-BI2 design, while HC-BI1 and HC-BI2 show significant fracture resistance gains over semicircular-edged counterparts.

caption: Evolution of (111), (200), (220), (311), and (420) lattice strains in the spot build cross-member as a function of applied cumulative load, showing both axial (closed symbols) and transverse (open symbols) directions.
summary: This plot illustrates the lattice strain evolution for the spot build configuration under cumulative loading. Axial and transverse strains are tracked across multiple crystallographic orientations. Data points represent the average response from five mapped locations on the cross-member, with error bars indicating the standard deviation of these measurements.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of Al2Gd secondary phases within the GA101K alloy matrix.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging captures the Al2Gd secondary phases in the GA101K alloy. These phases are refined to the 10 nm scale. Observations indicate that the crystallinity of these Al2Gd particles remains relatively low in the GA101K alloy compared to the GA102K variant.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for PEI/Ni-10%vol susceptor samples measured at 25 °C, 100 °C, and 200 °C under a constant field amplitude of 32 kA/m.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis of the magnetic hysteresis loops for PEI/Ni-10%vol susceptor samples. The measurements were conducted at 25 °C, 100 °C, and 200 °C under a fixed applied field amplitude of 32 kA/m, providing insight into the temperature-dependent magnetic behavior of the composite material.

caption: Elemental EDS map showing fine particles within the as-built Dievar microstructure.
summary: Detailed EDS analyses of the as-built Dievar steel revealed the presence of very fine particles. These particles are located in areas with locally increased concentrations of molybdenum, and further investigation shows they contain increased aluminum and oxygen contents, indicating the presence of specific inclusions within the cellular matrix.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing the thermal degradation behavior of neat PE against selected PE/Ni composite filaments.
summary: TGA curves for neat PE and selected PE/Ni composite filaments are presented to evaluate thermal behavior. These results are critical for understanding the thermal stability of the materials during FFF processing. The analysis provides insight into how varying Ni contents influence the degradation profiles of the composite filaments under thermal stress.

caption: Nickel elemental distribution map within the fusion zone of the NiTi/PCB joint, obtained via EDX mapping.
summary: Nickel elemental distribution map within the fusion zone of the NiTi/PCB joint, obtained via EDX mapping. This compositional data, part of a series characterizing the fusion zone, helps reconstruct mass transport phenomena and reactions occurring during laser processing, which lead to chemical heterogeneity and the formation of intermetallic phases.

caption: Near-infrared (NIR) intensity profiles plotted against time for Ti-6Al-4V plates processed at varying energy densities, highlighting the solidification point as the inflection point on the descending curve.
summary: NIR intensity profiles over time for Ti-6Al-4V plates reveal the solidification event as a distinct inflection point on the descending curve. The consistency of these inflection point intensities across various energy densities confirms the reliability of this method for identifying the solidification event during laser melting processes.

caption: Grain size distribution map for the USRP-4 treated sample in region 1, demonstrating significant grain refinement to 4.2 μm.
summary: This EBSD-derived grain size distribution map for the USRP-4 treated sample in region 1 reveals a significant refinement of the microstructure. The analysis confirms that the grain size is reduced to 4.2 μm, demonstrating a more pronounced refinement effect compared to the USRP-1 treatment.

caption: Sixth-order polynomial fit representing the relationship between the material parameter alpha and true strain.
summary: This plot illustrates the sixth-order polynomial fitting curve for the material parameter alpha as a function of true strain. Derived from the strain compensation method, this mathematical relationship is part of a series of equations used to characterize material behavior across varying strain levels as shown in Fig. 7.

caption: Oscillation temperature ramp test plotting tan (delta) and temperature against elapsed time.
summary: This plot tracks the tan (delta) value over time during an oscillation temperature ramp test. The data indicates that the tan (delta) value begins to slow its rate of change after an elapsed time of 0.04 minutes, or 2.4 seconds, providing insight into the temporal evolution of the ink's viscoelastic properties.

caption: Creep strain evolution at 150 MPa for AM and CM states at 800 °C.
summary: Creep strain evolution measured at 150 MPa and 800 °C for both AM and CM states. These tests were conducted to determine the activation energy of the creep process, comparing the deformation behavior of the two alloy states under identical stress and temperature conditions.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the dependence of corrosion current density for 90/10 Cu–Ni on temperature across various hydrostatic pressures, featuring linear fitting curves.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature dependence of the corrosion current density for 90/10 Cu–Ni alloy. Linear fitting curves demonstrate that experimental values align well with the Arrhenius equation across all tested hydrostatic pressures, achieving r-squared values near unity, confirming the validity of the model for these corrosion parameters.

caption: Magnetic entropy change (ΔS) as a function of temperature for HT block samples measured at a 1 T magnetic field, specifically highlighting the behavior around the first-order phase transition (FOPT).
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic entropy change (ΔS) for HT block samples under a 1 T magnetic field. It focuses on the thermal variation of ΔS in the vicinity of the first-order phase transition (FOPT), providing a quantitative assessment of the material's magnetocaloric response during the martensitic transition region.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material sample containing Atto465 and Atto565 dyes.
summary: This panel presents the optical transmission results for a 3D-printed sample composed of Atto465 and Atto565 dyes. Printed at a 0.5 mm thickness, this configuration is part of the set of samples printed with Atto565 combined with an additional dye to evaluate transmission characteristics across the visible spectrum.

caption: Three-dimensional atom probe tomography reconstruction of the CA800 specimen, depicting Co atom distributions within 30 at.% Ni iso-concentration surfaces and the proximity histogram across the γ/γ′ interface.
summary: The CA800 specimen is shown via APT reconstruction, highlighting the Co atom distribution and Ni-rich precipitate boundaries. Consistent with the reference, the γ′ precipitate size and composition in this sample are comparable to those observed in the RA800 specimen, reflecting the convergence of microstructural features at 800 °C.

caption: Phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction under a 10% compressive strain applied in the Q to P configuration.
summary: Shown is the phononic band structure for elastic waves propagating along the z-direction with a 10% compressive strain applied in the Q to P configuration. The structure is pushed from different sides to induce these changes, with the resulting band gaps highlighted in red to illustrate the effect of strain directionality.

caption: Force-time (F-T) curves comparing FEA and experimental results for the unit structure under an impact velocity of 2.0 m/s, highlighting the second stable state reached at 29.92 ms and the resulting large peak force.
summary: Under a higher impact velocity of 2.0 m/s, the unit structure reaches its second stable state at 29.92 ms. The residual kinetic energy generates a large peak force, and the FEA and experimental results demonstrate good agreement, validating the structural response and energy dissipation characteristics observed during the impact.

caption: Ashby plot comparing tensile yield strength versus ductility for DED-processed IN718 and IN718/TiB2 composites against literature data for various AM processes, cast, and wrought materials.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the mechanical performance of DED-processed IN718 and IN718/TiB2 composites by plotting tensile yield strength against ductility. The data includes comparisons with literature values for IN718 processed via DED, L-PBF, EBM, and conventional cast and wrought methods, with all tests performed parallel to the build direction.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis performed on the as-built gyroid strut.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis is presented for the as-built gyroid strut. This technique provides essential compositional information, complementing the morphological data obtained from the SEM analysis. The results confirm the elemental composition of the specimen, supporting the overall characterization of the as-built material structure described in the study.

caption: Support Vector Regressor performance displayed as a parity plot showing the correlation between predicted and validation dataset values.
summary: Support Vector Regressor results are presented via a parity plot, which highlights the relationship between the model's predictions and the actual validation dataset values. This visualization serves as a diagnostic tool to assess the regression efficacy and predictive consistency of the Support Vector Regressor model on the provided validation data.

caption: Cathode droplet shape at a horizontal wire angle of 10-10 degrees, showing the largest droplet size and a clearly visible bottom contour.
summary: At a horizontal wire angle of 10-10 degrees, the cathode droplet reaches its maximum size. This configuration allows for the clear capture of the bottom contour of the droplet, providing a baseline for observing the changes in the SCA shape as the horizontal angle increases.

caption: Yield strength values for GRCop-42 cold spray deposits containing varying amounts of HR-1, evaluated across as-deposited, stress-relieved, and fully heat-treated conditions.
summary: Yield strength measurements are presented for GRCop-42 cold spray deposits with varying HR-1 content. The data compares specimens processed with N2 gas across three distinct metallurgical states: as-deposited, stress-relieved, and fully heat-treated. This plot illustrates how processing conditions and composition influence the material's resistance to plastic deformation during tensile testing.

caption: Beeswarm plot illustrating SHAP feature importance for scan length (SL) and melt pool area (MPA) in core pixels, where shorter scan vectors correlate with higher SHAP values and increased porosity.
summary: This beeswarm plot displays SHAP feature importance for core pixels, highlighting how scan length and melt pool area influence porosity. Shorter scan vectors are shown to cause significant porosity, with data points forming distinct patterns that indicate higher SHAP values, reflecting a more substantial impact on the prediction of keyhole and LOF-porosity.

caption: Polarization curves for flat metallic bipolar plate VRFB cells tested at varying convection velocities while maintaining a constant current density of 75 mA/cm2.
summary: This plot illustrates the influence of electrolyte circulation velocity on the fourth charge-discharge cycle of a flat bipolar plate cell. By varying convection velocities at 75 mA/cm2, the results demonstrate how flow dynamics affect the polarization behavior, providing a comparative basis for assessing the performance benefits of indented plate architectures.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image showing the microstructure of the alloy after thermal exposure at 300 °C for 150 h.
summary: This bright-field transmission electron microscopy image reveals the microstructural state of the alloy following a thermal exposure treatment at 300 °C for 150 hours. The micrograph provides a baseline visualization of the material's internal structure after the specified aging duration, serving as a reference for subsequent compositional and defect-related analyses.

caption: Ashby diagram comparing the specific energy absorption (SEA) of PA 11 FG lattice structures from this study, highlighted in red, against various functionally graded lattice structures reported in existing literature.
summary: This Ashby diagram evaluates the mechanical performance of functionally graded lattice structures by plotting their specific energy absorption. By comparing the PA 11 FG lattices developed in this study against established literature data, the plot demonstrates the relative energy absorption efficiency of the proposed structures within the broader field of lattice materials.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of M327 alloy microstructure featuring secondary phase particles.
summary: Microstructural analysis of the M327 alloy via scanning electron microscopy displays the distribution of secondary phase particles. These particles, ranging from 1–10 μm in size, undergo elongation during the ingot rolling process. This visualization confirms the presence and morphological characteristics of the secondary phase within the M327 material system.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curve of the as-built Al-Fe-Ce alloy, recorded at a heating rate of 10 °C/min.
summary: This DSC curve illustrates the thermal behavior of the as-built Al-Fe-Ce alloy during a heating process at 10 °C/min. The analysis was conducted to evaluate the alloy's thermal stability, specifically assessing its potential for high-temperature applications exceeding 200 °C by identifying phase transitions or thermal events within the material.

caption: Magnified energy spectra highlighting oxygen signal changes, with an inset ternary diagram showing Y-H-O compositions for as-deposited and final films compared to reference photochromic samples.
summary: This panel displays a magnified section of the energy spectra, revealing an uneven increase in the oxygen signal that indicates a composition gradient during oxidation. The inset ternary diagram illustrates the Y-H-O compositions, confirming the transition from the as-deposited state to the final homogeneous distribution of oxygen throughout the layer.

caption: Photograph of the additive-manufactured sample produced via wire and arc additive manufacturing.
summary: The photograph displays the physical sample fabricated through the WAAM process. Heat input and part geometry were precisely optimized by adjusting parameters such as welding current, travel speed, and wire feed rate in the buildup direction to ensure the final component met all specified material dimensional requirements.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing mass loss of unfilled and silica-filled siloxane resin samples heated to 1000°C.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves compare the mass loss of unfilled and silica-filled siloxane resin samples heated to 1000°C. The unfilled printed polymer exhibits approximately 54% mass loss, with significant degradation rates centered at temperatures of 356°C and 418°C, illustrating the thermal stability characteristics of the resin system.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plots for NiCu coatings, highlighting the superior impedance performance of the 1 wt % h-BN modified coating in the low-frequency region.
summary: This Bode plot displays the impedance magnitude as a function of frequency for various NiCu coatings. The coating containing 1 wt % h-BN exhibits the highest impedance values in the low-frequency region, suggesting that this specific concentration significantly enhances the anti-corrosion performance of the NiCu coating compared to other compositions.

caption: Illustration of the n3m1 wave pattern integrated into an I-section stub column, showing the sinusoidal wave distribution across the web and flange elements.
summary: Depicted here is the n3m1 wave pattern applied to an I-section stub column. The web follows the internal plate aspect ratio of 1, while the flange utilizes an aspect ratio of 2. This geometry, verified through selective laser melting, demonstrates superior performance for both internal and external plate elements.

caption: Log-log plot illustrating the scaling relationship between relative elastic modulus and relative density for 3D RATH structures.
summary: This plot displays the scaling relationship between relative elastic modulus and relative density for 3D RATH structures. The data indicates a power-law behavior where the exponent m is 2.15, and the geometric constant of proportionality C1 is 0.12, characterizing the mechanical performance of the RATH architecture relative to its density.

caption: Top-hat rectangular beam profile measuring 500 by 30 micrometers.
summary: The resulting beam shape is a top-hat rectangular line measuring 500 by 30 micrometers. This specific beam geometry is achieved through the spatial light modulator, enabling significantly faster LIPSS fabrication by providing a uniform intensity distribution across the target area compared to standard Gaussian beam profiles.

caption: Nyquist diagram of the MP-treated SLMed TC4 alloy specimen tested in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance response of the MP-treated SLMed TC4 alloy in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The experimental data exhibits strong consistency with the fitted model, providing a reliable assessment of the electrochemical interface properties for the MP-polished surface condition.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the δ-ferrite matrix phase in the Ar P sample.
