caption: Comparative ranking matrix of sixteen geometric shapes evaluated across six integrated weighting-MCDM methods, including PCA-RAPS, PCA-RAMS, PCA-RATMI, CRITIC-RAPS, CRITIC-RAMS, and CRITIC-RATMI.
summary: This heatmap displays the comparative rankings of sixteen distinct geometric shapes derived from six integrated weighting-MCDM methods: PCA-RAPS, PCA-RAMS, PCA-RATMI, CRITIC-RAPS, CRITIC-RAMS, and CRITIC-RATMI. The visualization provides a comprehensive overview of how different weighting strategies influence the final performance ranking of the shapes within the multi-criteria decision-making framework.

caption: Comparison of stress rupture life (bars) and elongation (squares with dashed lines) for two distinct alloys tested at 750 °C.
summary: This figure illustrates the mechanical performance of two investigated alloys under stress rupture conditions at 750 °C. The data presents stress rupture life using bar charts alongside elongation values represented by full squares connected with dashed lines, providing a comparative overview of the materials' durability and ductility at high temperatures.

caption: Power-voltage (P–V) characteristic curves derived from the estimated parameters of the 19 optimization algorithms for the KC200GT panel.
summary: Power-voltage curves are illustrated for the KC200GT solar panel, derived from the parameters estimated by the 19 different optimization algorithms. This plot provides a visual comparison of how effectively each method captures the power output characteristics of the panel when compared to the measured experimental data under the PEC2 model.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing unfunctionalized 3D-printed PCL scaffolds with those subjected to wet-chemical or plasma-assisted surface functionalization.
summary: FTIR analysis confirms the chemical structure of the 3D-printed PCL scaffolds. Representative peaks are identified at 2941 cm-1 and 2862 cm-1 for CH2 stretching, 1721 cm-1 for carbonyl groups, 1162 cm-1 for ester bonds, 1189 cm-1 for hydroxyl groups, and 1045 cm-1 and 1107 cm-1 for C-O vibrations.

caption: Immunofluorescence visualization of rBMSCs within osteochondral scaffold zones, highlighting nuclei (blue), F-actin (green), and G-actin (red) after 14 days of culture with or without growth factor delivery.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging reveals the actin cytoskeleton organization in rBMSCs cultured on osteochondral scaffolds. By staining for F-actin and G-actin, the study visualizes the polymerization state of actin in different scaffold zones. These images provide a qualitative basis for assessing how growth factor delivery influences cellular differentiation and cytoskeletal morphology over 14 days.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy image illustrating the structural transition between 14M and NM phases, where the NM phase appears as a bright region and the 14M phase as a darker region, complemented by inset selected area electron diffraction patterns.
summary: This bright-field transmission electron microscopy image captures the structural transition from the 14M phase to the NM phase. The NM phase is identified by its brighter contrast, while the 14M phase appears darker. Inset selected area electron diffraction patterns provide crystallographic confirmation of the distinct phases present during this transition.

caption: Theoretical and experimental RL curves for optimized complex GMSs with a configuration yielding three absorption peaks.
summary: This panel displays the theoretical and experimental RL curves for the optimized complex GMSs with the configuration (#0) 3 #14#0(#10) 2 #2, which results in three distinct absorption peaks. The data confirms the successful implementation of the design strategy for achieving specific multi-peak absorption characteristics in the GMS material.

caption: LSM image of the PEEK composite worn surface against an aluminum substrate at a 200 N·m/s product value, illustrating increased fiber damage and matrix interaction.
summary: Captured at a higher 200 N·m/s product value, this LSM image shows the PEEK composite worn surface against an aluminum substrate. The visual evidence highlights broken fibers and matrix scratching, reflecting the surface characteristics observed across different metallic substrates during the wear testing of these composite materials.

caption: Elongation-temperature curves for LSF Invar 36 samples fabricated at scanning speeds of 500 mm min-1 and 800 mm min-1, measured from 30 to 500 °C according to ASTM E228-06.
summary: This plot displays the thermal elongation of LSF Invar 36 samples produced at different scanning speeds. The curves show a gradual increase in length as temperature rises from 30 to 500 °C. Notably, the elongation profiles are identical for both scanning speeds, indicating that processing speed has negligible influence on thermal expansion.

caption: Surface topography of a premolar tooth milled at 220 m using scCO2 + MQL coolant.
summary: Confocal microscopy presents the surface topography of a premolar tooth milled at 220 m with scCO2 + MQL coolant. The surface finish is characterized by lower and more stable arithmetical mean height values, confirming that this cooling method provides superior control over the surface topography during the milling process.

caption: Dark-field TEM image illustrating the interfacial region within the interlayer between the matrix and precipitates.
summary: This dark-field TEM image captures the interfacial region within the interlayer. It provides a structural overview of the interface between the matrix and the precipitates, serving as the reference area for subsequent high-resolution imaging and detailed microstructural analysis of the transition layer and dislocation features.

caption: Loss modulus (E″) curves for CP-PLA composites with varying CP additions, showing the influence of filler concentration on viscoelastic response.
summary: This plot displays the loss modulus of CP-PLA composites as a function of different CP additions. The experimental results indicate that the maximum loss modulus follows a specific trend, where the E″ max values are ordered as CP15-PLA > CP10-PLA > CP5-PLA, demonstrating the impact of filler content on material damping.

caption: Frenkel defect accumulation over time in Cu-20at%Ni alloy at 300 K with 4 keV PKA energy, characterized by a maximum defect count in the [110] direction and nearly equal quantities in the [111] and [100] directions.
summary: For the Cu-20at%Ni system, the Frenkel defect count varies with time under 4 keV PKA energy at 300 K. Unlike the lower Ni concentrations, this system produces the highest number of Frenkel defect pairs in the [110] direction, with nearly equal quantities observed in the [111] and [100] directions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction (SAD) pattern of a TCP phase precipitate, indexed to the tetragonal σ phase (space group P4₂/mnm) along the [145] zone axis.
summary: SAD patterns acquired from a precipitate in the NiMoCr alloy cladding are indexed to the topologically close-packed (TCP) σ phase. The diffraction data, viewed along the [145] zone axis, confirms the crystal structure corresponds to space group P4₂/mnm, consistent with the ICSD 188709 reference for this phase.

caption: Structural representation of the S25 unit cell subjected to heating up to 400 K.
summary: Depicted here is the structural representation of the S25 unit cell during the heating process to 400 K. This view allows for the observation of atomic positioning and lattice changes within the unit cell as the material is subjected to the specified thermal conditions during the heating process.

caption: GBDT regression model performance displaying the correspondence between model predictions and experimental measurements.
summary: Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) predictions are plotted against experimental outcomes to assess model accuracy. This comparison chart is essential for evaluating the performance of the GBDT algorithm relative to other machine learning models, providing a clear view of how well the model captures the experimental trends.

caption: Cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes during lithiation at a C/10 rate.
summary: This panel presents the electrochemical response of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes during lithiation at a C/10 rate. The plot shows cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential versus lithium composition. Notably, the entropic potential surges toward the end of lithiation, reflecting the growing difference between cell potential and open-circuit voltage.

caption: Minimum Tafel slope curves for Mo2WS6/NF, MoS2/NF, WS2/NF, and NF.
summary: Minimum Tafel slope curves are presented for Mo2WS6/NF, MoS2/NF, WS2/NF, and NF. These plots allow for a direct comparison of the reaction kinetics between the composite catalyst and the individual components, further validating the enhanced catalytic performance observed in the Mo2WS6/NF system.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot showing the dependence of the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of flow stress (ln[sinh(ασ)]) on the inverse of absolute temperature (T^-1) at a constant strain of 0.7.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the correlation between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of flow stress and the inverse of absolute temperature. By utilizing flow stress data at a strain of 0.7, the graph characterizes the thermal sensitivity of the material's flow behavior during the deformation process.

caption: Failure strain retention percentage for coupons subjected to 240-hour aging cycles.
summary: Failure strain retention is presented for coupons subjected to 240-hour aging cycles. The plot documents the long-term changes in ductility, allowing for an assessment of how extended exposure to aging conditions impacts the failure strain characteristics of the coupons throughout the entire testing period.

caption: Magnified view of the F region from panel (b), displaying the nanostructures at the interfaces between M7C3 carbide, primary α phase, and secondary α phase.
summary: This magnified view of the F region provides a detailed look at the nanostructures present at the interfaces of the M7C3 carbide with both the primary and secondary α phases. These observations are supported by EDS results, which were specifically tested at this region to characterize the chemical composition.

caption: Dilatometric curve representing the thermal expansion and contraction behavior of the deposited metal during cooling at a rate of 20 °C/s.
summary: This dilatometric curve illustrates the thermal expansion and contraction behavior of the deposited metal during a cooling process at 20 °C/s. Such measurements are essential for determining austenite transformation temperatures, specifically identifying the austenite decomposition begin (Ac1) and finish (Ac3) temperatures, which are approximately 750 °C and 840 °C, respectively.

caption: Open-circuit voltage response of the printed device measured under periodic mechanical strain cycles.
summary: Periodic mechanical strain cycles applied to the printed device generate a measurable open-circuit voltage response. This electrical output demonstrates the piezoelectric performance of the tellurium and silver nanowire-based architecture. The data confirms the device's ability to convert mechanical deformation into electrical potential under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of Inconel alloy 625 exposed to nitric acid solutions of varying concentrations.
summary: This figure displays the potentiodynamic polarization curves for Inconel alloy 625 samples immersed in nitric acid media with different concentrations. These electrochemical measurements provide essential data for analyzing the corrosion behavior and kinetics of the alloy when subjected to varying acidic environments, serving as a basis for deriving further electrochemical parameters.

caption: Calculated energy pathway for deformation twinning and martensitic transformation in Ni–Al series Ni-based superalloy.
summary: This panel displays the calculated energy pathway for deformation twinning and FCC-to-HCP martensitic transformation in Ni–Al series Ni-based superalloys. By analyzing these energy pathways, the study elucidates the specific plastic deformation mechanisms active in the superalloy, highlighting how alloying elements influence the transformation energetics compared to pure nano-crystalline Ni.

caption: Focused ternary phase diagram of the Cu-Cr-Zr system featuring non-equivalent axis ranges to emphasize the small composition range of interest.
summary: This focused ternary phase diagram illustrates the Cu-Cr-Zr system with adjusted, non-equivalent axis ranges. By narrowing the composition range, the visualization provides a clearer representation of the phase equilibria within the system, facilitating a more detailed analysis of the specific area of interest for this alloy composition.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization profile of the sample subjected to optimized heat treatment at 1250 °C for 24 h followed by aging at 450 °C for 120 h, measured under an applied magnetic field of 0.01 T.
summary: This M-T curve illustrates the temperature dependence of magnetization for a sample optimized through a 1250 °C heat treatment and subsequent 450 °C aging for 120 h. The measurement was conducted under a constant applied magnetic field of 0.01 T to characterize the magnetic response of the material under these conditions.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph illustrating the phase-specific dislocation distribution, with a higher population of dislocations in the γ channel compared to the γ′ interior.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph demonstrates a significant phase-specific difference in dislocation density within the post-fatigued sample. The imaging reveals a larger population of dislocations localized in the γ channel relative to the γ′ interior, providing insight into the deformation behavior of the material's microstructure under fatigue loading conditions.

caption: Short-circuit current measurements recorded over a seven-day period for the fifth experimental group of SMFCs.
summary: This panel displays the short-circuit current measurements for the fifth experimental group of SMFCs, recorded continuously over a seven-day duration. The data provides insight into the temporal stability and performance characteristics of the specific electrode spatial arrangement tested within this group during the experimental observation period.

caption: Optical spectrum of the mode-locked YDFL showing a center wavelength of 1074.90 nm and a 3 dB bandwidth of 6 nm.
summary: The optical spectrum of the mode-locked YDFL is presented, highlighting a center wavelength of 1074.90 nm. The measurement reveals a 3 dB bandwidth of 6 nm, characterizing the spectral output of the laser system at maximum pump power under stable operating conditions.

caption: Total capacitance evolution over time for samples S1–S6 exposed to PBS + 1M H2O2, with an inset highlighting the initial 4 hours of exposure.
summary: The total capacitance, calculated via ECM fitting, is plotted against exposure time for samples S1–S6. The inset reveals significant variation during the first 4 hours, with responses ranging from no increase in sample S5 to a sharp rise in sample S4, reflecting distinct corrosion onset behaviors across the different specimens.

caption: Completed console fabrication utilizing the integrated reinforcement bars.
summary: This photograph shows the final console fabrication achieved through the SC3DP process. By utilizing the short reinforcing bars previously inserted into the wall element, the console is successfully integrated into the structure, demonstrating the effectiveness of the reinforcement strategy for complex architectural components as described in the research.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loops for the unpinned CFRP specimen measured in both out-of-plane and in-plane orientations.
summary: The out-of-plane and in-plane M-H curves of the unpinned specimen are plotted in Fig. 4 (a). These curves serve as a baseline for comparing the magnetic response of the composite material before the introduction of Z-pin reinforcement, illustrating the inherent magnetic behavior of the unpinned carbon fiber reinforced polymer.

caption: Live/dead staining performance of BMSCs seeded on scaffolds, showing cell viability and distribution.
summary: Live/dead staining performance of BMSCs seeded on scaffolds, showing cell viability and distribution. Fluorescence microscopy observations revealed that BMSCs adhered more densely and displayed a more extensive distribution of the cytoskeleton on the PHCZ scaffolds, indicating good biocompatibility of the material as cells remained viable across the tested groups.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of SPI, Mixture, and Conjugate in aqueous solution, highlighting the characteristic absorption peak near 280 nm associated with the conjugated double bonds of aromatic amino acids in SPI.
summary: The UV-Vis spectra of SPI, Mixture, and Conjugate are presented to analyze their optical properties in aqueous solution. The data reveals that the conjugated double bonds of aromatic amino acids within the SPI structure exhibit a distinct absorption peak near 280 nm, providing insight into the protein's electronic transitions.

caption: Creep strain evolution over time for gamma-alloy single-crystals tested at 1225 °C and 10 MPa.
summary: Creep behavior of gamma-alloy single-crystals is illustrated at 1225 °C under a constant stress of 10 MPa. The curve demonstrates the material's time-dependent deformation characteristics at this specific temperature. The creep rate is shown to be strongly temperature-dependent when compared to curves obtained at other temperatures under identical stress conditions.

caption: Nanoindentation load-displacement (P-h) curves for T4-100, T4-10, T4-1, and T4-0.1 samples subjected to varying cooling rates under identical peak loads.
summary: Nanoindentation load-displacement curves are presented for four distinct samples, labeled T4-100, T4-10, T4-1, and T4-0.1, which were processed at different cooling rates. The experimental results demonstrate that all four P-h curves exhibit a relatively smooth profile when subjected to the same applied load, indicating consistent mechanical response across the tested conditions.

caption: Continuous-cooling transformation (CCT) diagram illustrating the kinetics of phase evolution during cooling.
summary: The CCT diagram maps the transformation kinetics, showing how different cooling paths lead to distinct microstructural phases. It serves as a fundamental guide for predicting the metallurgical SSPT, which encompasses both diffusional and diffusionless transformation mechanisms. This diagram is vital for controlling the final microstructure through precise thermal management.

caption: Tafel slopes derived from the polarization data for nanoporous Cu–Zn–Ni–Co alloys, indicating the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction.
summary: Tafel slopes are presented to characterize the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction for the nanoporous Cu–Zn–Ni–Co alloys. These slopes provide critical insight into the electrocatalytic efficiency of the materials, serving as a key metric for evaluating the performance improvements achieved through the nanoporous structural design.

caption: Scheil-Gulliver solidification curves comparing the solidification behavior of CM247LC and CM247LC-M alloys.
summary: Scheil-Gulliver solidification curves illustrate the solidification behavior of CM247LC and CM247LC-M alloys. The data shows that the solidification interval for CM247LC-M is significantly lower than that of CM247LC, decreasing from 453 °C to 195 °C, which represents a 57% reduction in the solidification range for the modified alloy.

caption: Weight gain versus time curves for three experimental alloys coated with Na2SO4 and exposed to 900 °C, illustrating the kinetics of hot corrosion.
summary: This plot displays the mass change kinetics of three experimental alloys coated with Na2SO4 at 900 °C. The curves reveal distinct oxidation behaviors, where Alloy 2 shows lower initial mass gain due to protective oxide layers, while Re-containing alloys exhibit faster mass gain during the initial 100-hour oxidation-dominated period.

caption: C 1s XPS spectra of CN@γ-Al2O3 and various metal-doped catalysts, showing deconvoluted peaks at 288.3, 286.2, and 284.7 eV corresponding to N-C=N, C-N, and C-C/C=C bonds.
summary: The C 1s XPS spectrum of CN@γ-Al2O3 is deconvoluted into three peaks representing N-C=N, C-N, and C-C/C=C bonds. Metal doping significantly decreases the peak area ratio of N-C=N to C-C/C=C, indicating that the incorporation of metal nanoparticles modifies the skeletal structure of the g-C3N4 support.

caption: Temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) curves for H0, D45, and V90 Invar 36 specimens fabricated via LPBF, measured using dilatometry (DIL) to identify the Curie temperature inflection point.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent coefficient of thermal expansion for LPBF-fabricated Invar 36 specimens, specifically H0, D45, and V90. Dilatometry measurements are utilized to characterize the thermal stability and determine the Curie temperature inflection point, which is critical for assessing the material's shape stability under varying thermal loads.

caption: Impact of abrupt situations on prediction results, showing how the model accounts for periodic fluctuations caused by the 67° scan strategy rotation during the LPBF process.
summary: This panel illustrates the impact of unexpected events on the prediction results. The GRU model effectively captures periodic fluctuations in the sequence information, which are induced by the 67° rotation scan strategy applied to each layer during the LPBF process, ensuring accurate predictions despite these process-related variations.

caption: Main effect plot for flexural strength of PLGA/HA scaffolds, showing the influence of layer thickness, nozzle temperature, printing speed, and fan cooling speed.
summary: Flexural strength of PLGA/HA scaffolds is depicted through main effect plots. Analysis indicates that lower layer thickness (0.12 mm) and moderate nozzle temperature (205 °C) optimize strength. Conversely, higher layer thickness and elevated printing temperatures result in decreased flexural strength, highlighting the sensitivity of mechanical performance to these specific printing parameters.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for the AMZ weld seam at the second oscillation frequency.
summary: Panel b illustrates the grain size distribution for the AMZ weld seam at the second oscillation frequency. As part of the quantitative comparison of AMZ grain sizes, this plot helps characterize how different frequencies influence the grain structure within the AMZ region of the weld seam.

caption: Bottom view of the recoater assembly featuring a modified rubber strip holder designed with a lateral recess to prevent interference with routed cables.
summary: This photograph displays the bottom section of the recoater mechanism, highlighting the redesigned rubber strip holder. The component, essential for uniform powder layer distribution, incorporates a lateral recess to avoid collisions with routed cables. A scale in millimeters is provided to indicate the physical dimensions of the modified assembly.

caption: Average effective fluence variation (Φ av) plotted against oscillation amplitude (A) and linear scan velocity (V) at a constant frequency of 650 Hz, accompanied by representative micrographs demonstrating keyholing or insufficient penetration at extreme parameter values.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between average effective fluence, oscillation amplitude, and scan velocity at 650 Hz. By maintaining a constant frequency, the effective fluence is mapped across the parameter space, allowing for direct correlation with track micrographs that reveal physical defects like keyholing or lack of penetration at extreme settings.

caption: Overview STEM-ADF image of the post-irradiated DED TEM lamella, highlighting three distinct zones characterized by varying microstructural features and chemical compositions.
summary: This STEM-ADF overview of the post-irradiated DED TEM lamella identifies three distinct zones. Zone 1 features a W-Ti-rich region with a Ti-rich boundary, Zone 2 shows high dislocation density, and Zone 3 contains local defects and coalesced clusters. These regions demonstrate the spatial heterogeneity resulting from the radiation response.

caption: Detailed STEM view of the HT specimen highlighting carbide morphology and EDS point analysis spots.
summary: STEM analysis of the heat-treated specimen provides insight into the carbide evolution. EDS point data collected from these spots confirms the presence of distinct carbide types, including M23C6-based carbides which are unique to the heat-treated condition, thereby demonstrating the impact of thermal processing on the material's overall microstructural and chemical composition.

caption: Crystallographic orientation analysis via pole figure for the α-phase in the TiC/Ti-alloy matrix of sample I60–V3.
summary: The pole figure image for sample I60–V3 illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the α-phase in the TiC/Ti-alloy matrix. This visualization is critical for understanding the texture evolution of the composite under the specified process parameters, providing a comprehensive view of the phase's structural alignment.

caption: Zoomed-in neutron diffraction patterns at 293 K in the 1.7–2.2 Å range, plotted on a log-scale to demonstrate the absence of HCP phase formation.
summary: Zoomed-in neutron diffraction patterns at 293 K in the 1.7–2.2 Å range confirm the lack of HCP phase formation. The peaks remain relatively symmetrical until the end of the deformation, indicating that the martensitic transformation observed at 77 K does not occur at this higher temperature.

caption: Structural representation of the HI γ″-Ni3Nb phase showing the optimized atomic geometry.
summary: This panel presents the geometrical atomic model for the HI γ″-Ni3Nb phase. As one of the most stable structures selected for this work, the model highlights the precise atomic arrangement of the Ni3Nb phase. It serves as a key structural reference for understanding interface stability in the material.

caption: Structural alignment showing the [1-1-1] planes of the α-Al lattice in relation to the nanolayered phase, demonstrating parallelism with the b-axis tile features.
summary: This panel demonstrates the structural coherence between the α-Al lattice and the nanolayered phase. Specifically, the [1-1-1] planes of the α-Al lattice are shown to be parallel to the tile features of the nanolayered phase's b-axis, confirming a coherent interface relationship between the matrix and the nanolayered structure.

caption: Faradaic efficiency and CO production rates for SOECs tested at 800 °C under current densities of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 A·cm⁻².
summary: Presented here are the Faradaic efficiency and CO production rates for SOECs at 800 °C. The cells were tested galvanostatically for 20–40 minutes at current densities ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 A·cm⁻². Observed Faradaic efficiency values exceeding 100% are attributed to potential GC measurement errors in the exhaust gas.

caption: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculation for the Co-7.5Al-12Cr alloy at 900 °C, showing the stability of various oxide phases as a function of oxygen activity.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the thermodynamic stability of oxide phases in the Co-7.5Al-12Cr alloy at 900 °C. It highlights the preferential formation of Al2O3 over Cr2O3 or (Co,Ni)O, which is thermodynamically driven, though the actual formation is kinetically limited by the diffusivity of aluminum within the alloy matrix.

caption: Micrograph revealing the internal foamed structure of the MD urethane lattice.
summary: Detailed microscopic examination of the MD urethane lattice reveals its internal foamed architecture. The micrograph provides a clear view of the cellular morphology inherent to the foam structure, confirming the successful formation of the lattice material following the fabrication process using the BVOH mold and V2 geometry.

caption: Nyquist plot detailing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) characteristics of the S9-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion.
summary: The Nyquist plot for the S9-6D specimen illustrates the electrochemical impedance after 6 days of immersion. This data is critical for evaluating the corrosion resistance of SLMed TC4 alloys, and the results are interpreted using equivalent circuit fitting to characterize the electrochemical behavior of the specimen.

caption: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity profile for the CrMnFeCoNiAl alloy film.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent electrical resistivity curve for the CrMnFeCoNiAl alloy film. The data illustrates how the resistivity of this specific Cantor-based alloy composition evolves across a range of temperatures, providing insight into the electronic transport properties of the Al-doped high-entropy alloy film system.

caption: Box plot showing deviations from the z-axis for each group.
summary: This box plot quantifies deviations along the z-axis for the printed specimens. The x- and y-axes exhibit higher deviations relative to the z-axis. These plots help assess the dimensional consistency and accuracy of the printing process across the different groups, identifying the range of variation for each specimen set.

caption: FDTD-calculated absorptivity spectra comparing a planar meta-atom structure (left) with the novel pyramid geometry (right) under TE wave excitation at oblique incidence, demonstrating the performance enhancement of the 3D design.
summary: This panel displays FDTD simulation results comparing the absorptivity of planar and pyramid-based meta-atoms. By evaluating performance under oblique incidence, the data demonstrates the superior broadband absorption capabilities of the metapyramid geometry over the traditional planar structure, which consists of ITO strip arrays on a PET-supported PLA substrate.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni–Cr–Mo system at 1073 K, highlighting the presence of a stable, isolated oP6 single-phase region located at approximately 1 at.% Cr along the 66.6 at.% equinickel concentration line.
summary: At 1073 K, the isothermal section displays a distinct phase stability profile. A stable and isolated oP6 single-phase region is identified within the composition range of approximately 1 at.% Cr, specifically positioned along the equinickel concentration line of 66.6 at.%, demonstrating the phase evolution compared to higher temperatures.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded at 5 mV s−1 for an on-chip μSC utilizing a 5 wt% PEGDA electrolyte in 1M H2SO4 across a temperature range from room temperature down to −20 °C.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms at 5 mV s−1 demonstrate the electrochemical behavior of a 5 wt% PEGDA-based on-chip μSC in 1M H2SO4. The measurements were conducted at temperatures varying from room temperature to −20 °C, highlighting the device's performance stability and electrochemical response in the sub-zero temperature range.

caption: Magnetic moment versus temperature curve for (Fe70Ni28Co2)80Nb4B14Si2 alloy, highlighting the transition temperatures Tc, Tx1, and Tx2.
summary: This M(T) curve illustrates the magnetic moment behavior of the (Fe70Ni28Co2)80Nb4B14Si2 alloy as a function of temperature. Measured at a ramp rate of 1 °C/min, the plot identifies critical transition temperatures, specifically Tc, Tx1, and Tx2, providing a direct observation of magnetic changes during the heating process.

caption: Crystal Orbital Hamilton Population (-COHP) curves for N-H bonds in NH₃ adsorbed on CuNi@BNC, CuNi@NC, and isolated ammonia molecules.
summary: The -COHP curves provide a detailed look at the bonding characteristics of N-H bonds within NH₃ when interacting with CuNi@BNC and CuNi@NC catalysts compared to sole ammonia. This analysis helps quantify the strength and nature of the bonding interactions between the nitrogen-hydrogen bonds and the catalyst surfaces.

caption: Receiver Operating Characteristic curve illustrating the trade-off between True Positive Rate (TPR) on the Y-axis and False Positive Rate (FPR) on the X-axis for a classification algorithm.
summary: This Receiver Operating Characteristic curve visualizes the performance trade-off between sensitivity and specificity at various classification thresholds. The plot displays the True Positive Rate against the False Positive Rate, where a curve approaching the top-left corner signifies a perfect classifier with superior discriminative ability compared to less accurate models.

caption: Electron localization function (ELF) map of the S2/α-Ti interface viewed along the [0001] direction, highlighting an isosurface value of 0.76 in yellow.
summary: This DFT-calculated ELF map of the S2/α-Ti interface supercell characterizes interatomic bonding. The visualization reveals significant electron accumulation between the Si and Ti atoms at the interface, which provides clear evidence of covalent bond formation between the two species when viewed along the [0001] direction of the S2 structure.

caption: Convergence behavior of the objective function corresponding to the optimization results presented in Figure 18.
summary: This plot illustrates the convergence curves of the objective function for the optimization results shown in Figure 18. It tracks the progression of the optimization process, providing a clear visualization of how the objective function values evolve and stabilize over the course of the computational iterations performed for the study.

caption: Superimposition of the layer (2) diffusion path onto a calculated isothermal section at 650 °C, representing temperatures near the AA7075 liquidus.
summary: The diffusion path of layer (2) is mapped onto a calculated isothermal section at 650 °C. This temperature is chosen as it is the lowest investigated value and remains very close to the liquidus temperature of the AA7075 alloy, providing insight into the phase stability at high-temperature processing conditions.

caption: Radar plot comparing the meltpool area, aspect ratio, and irregularity features across the four process regimes.
summary: A radar plot integrates the meltpool area, aspect ratio, and irregularity features to provide a multi-dimensional comparison of the four process regimes. This visualization allows for a comprehensive overview of how each regime is characterized by the combination of these three distinct morphological features in a single view.

caption: CLSM 3D image of live/dead cell staining on Al 1.2, with green fluorescence indicating living cells and red fluorescence indicating dead cells.
summary: The CLSM 3D image of live and dead cells on the Al 1.2 sample is shown, where green fluorescence indicates living cells and red fluorescence indicates dead cells. This visualization provides insight into the bacterial viability and spatial arrangement on the Al 1.2 surface, aiding in the antibacterial assessment.

caption: Comparative X-ray diffraction patterns for the 42CrMo steel substrate, nickel alloy bonding coating, and S3 composite coating, highlighting the dominant γ-Fe phase peaks at 2θ values of 44.7°, 64.9°, and 82.3°.
summary: This panel presents a comparative XRD analysis of the 42CrMo steel substrate, nickel alloy bonding coating, and S3 composite coating. The diffraction patterns identify the dominant phase of the 42CrMo steel substrate as γ-Fe, characterized by distinct peaks at 2θ angles of 44.7°, 64.9°, and 82.3°.

caption: Creep rate evolution of UT and HT90(2h) PLA samples measured at 27 °C under a constant holding stress of 12 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the creep rate characteristics of UT and HT90(2h) PLA samples at 27 °C. The data represents the creep strain behavior under a holding stress of 12 MPa, providing a baseline comparison for the material performance of the untreated versus the heat-treated polymer samples at room temperature.

caption: X-z slice of the HXCT volume prior to the application of the stripes filter.
summary: This panel displays an x-z cross-sectional slice obtained from high-resolution X-ray computed tomography (HXCT) data. The image represents the raw structural state of the specimen before any post-processing filtering techniques were applied to mitigate artifacts, providing a baseline for evaluating the effectiveness of the stripes filter in subsequent image processing.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of NiSn electrocatalysts measured in 0.50 M KOH electrolyte across a potential window of 0 V to 0.70 V vs Hg/HgO, utilizing scan rates from 10 to 100 mV s−1.
summary: NiSn electrodes exhibit cyclic voltammetry behavior in 0.50 M KOH electrolyte, tested in the absence of methanol. The voltammograms cover a potential range of 0 V to 0.70 V vs Hg/HgO, with the scan rates systematically increased from 10 mV s−1 up to 100 mV s−1 to evaluate electrochemical performance.

caption: Detailed view of the creep strain rate curves highlighting the onset of the tertiary creep stage at time t_m immediately following the primary creep stage.
summary: This panel provides a focused view of the creep strain rate curves, specifically highlighting the onset of the tertiary creep stage. The time t_m marks the transition point immediately after the primary creep stage, providing a clear indication of the material's degradation behavior under the specified test conditions.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves of AISI 316L stainless steel in 3.5% NaCl solution at 15 °C under varying hydrostatic pressure conditions.
summary: Shown are the polarization curves for AISI 316L at 15 °C. The data indicates that higher hydrostatic pressure reduces the cathodic polarized current density at a given potential. Additionally, the breakdown potential of the passive film exhibits a shift to more positive values with increasing hydrostatic pressure at this temperature.

caption: Crystal orientation data presented alongside a corresponding pole figure, illustrating the crystallographic orientation of the dendritic region and the specific LAGB identified for APT analysis.
summary: This panel provides the crystallographic context for the analyzed region through a presentation of crystal orientation data and a corresponding pole figure. These data characterize the orientation of the dendrites and the specific LAGB, ensuring a comprehensive structural understanding of the interface selected for the subsequent APT analysis.

caption: Instrumented Charpy impact energy values for Steels A, B, and C, demonstrating a substantial decrease from approximately 350 J to 80 J with increasing Cr and Ni alloying.
summary: This panel displays the low-temperature impact toughness of three test steels. Instrumented Charpy energy measurements show a significant decline from 350 J in Steel A to 100 J in Steel B following Cr addition, further dropping to 80 J in Steel C after combined Cr–Ni alloying, indicating reduced toughness with increased alloying.

caption: TEM image of the K447A region highlighting plastic deformation within carbides located near the main crack.
summary: Focusing on the K447A region near the main crack, this TEM image illustrates the presence of dislocations within carbides. This structural evidence indicates that the carbides underwent plastic deformation during the creep process, contributing to the overall dislocation substructure observed in the uniform deformation zone of the superalloy sample.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of deformed CuCrZr alloy viewed along the building direction.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the microstructure of CuCrZr following compressive loading along the building direction. The visualization reveals significant grain subdivision within the material, demonstrating how the applied compressive stress influences the crystallographic orientation and grain structure of the alloy under these specific deformation conditions.

caption: Shear modulus of TPS30–00 measured via DMA, with load ranging from 1 N to 30 N and shear angles from 0.001° to 1°.
summary: TPS30–00 shows a shear modulus that is highly sensitive to the applied load and shear angle, as presented in the DMA analysis. The material's dynamic mechanical response is well-suited for robust liners, providing the necessary performance to withstand the forces and stresses encountered during active physical movements.

caption: Pole figure map of the LDED-120 specimen, illustrating the crystallographic texture and grain orientation distribution.
summary: This pole figure illustrates the crystallographic texture of the LDED-120 specimen. It serves to characterize the orientation distribution of the grains, providing essential data on how the LDED-120 processing parameters influence the final crystallographic alignment and texture strength of the fabricated material.

caption: Uncorrected enthalpy of formation values derived from OQMD DFT calculations plotted against experimental data.
summary: This panel displays the uncorrected enthalpy of formation values obtained from OQMD DFT calculations compared directly against experimental data. It serves as a baseline to illustrate the performance of the modification scheme, highlighting the initial discrepancies present in the uncorrected OQMD data before the application of the aiOQ correction method.

caption: Overview of the FSP processing equipment used for post-processing the WAAM-fabricated samples.
summary: This image shows the FSP equipment setup employed for material modification. The process utilizes a cylindrical tool with a 12 mm shoulder diameter and a 4.5 mm pin length. This stage is critical for refining the microstructure of the WAAM-produced components through severe plastic deformation and dynamic recrystallization.

caption: Aspect ratio comparison of the α′ phase under different laser power conditions.
summary: Aspect ratio values for the α′ phase are compared across different laser power settings. The results show that the aspect ratio decreases with increasing laser power, which aligns with the observed reduction in length and increase in width, reflecting the overall change in the shape of the α′ phase.

caption: Neural network architecture configured for the inverse design problem, mapping a target swollen shape to the corresponding dimensionless shear modulus distribution along the elastic ring perimeter.
summary: This schematic illustrates the neural network algorithm trained as an inverse design tool. It accepts a target swollen shape as input and outputs the dimensionless shear modulus distribution along the perimeter of an elastic ring, enabling the determination of material properties required to achieve a specific geometric configuration.

caption: R-curve for AS steel specimens showing valid data-pairs as filled markers and repetition tests in grey.
summary: This panel displays the R-curve for AS steel specimens, illustrating the fracture toughness behavior. Valid data-pairs used for exponential regression are represented by filled markers, while repetition tests are indicated in grey. These curves reveal specimen-specific differences in the material, with data processed by fitting an exponential function to the pairs.

caption: Mean square error (MSE) convergence plot showing the optimization process, with a minimum validation performance of 8.7557 × 10^-5 achieved at epoch 47.
summary: The mean square error convergence plot tracks the model's error reduction over training epochs. It highlights the optimization progress, specifically identifying that the best validation performance, reaching a value of 8.7557 × 10^-5, was successfully achieved at the 47th epoch during the training process of the ANN model.

caption: Atomic model of the Al23CuFe4 ((Al, Cu)6Fe) phase, showing the substitution of Al atoms by Cu within the oC28 lattice.
summary: This atomic model represents the Al23CuFe4 phase, where copper atoms replace aluminum atoms at specific sublattice sites within the oC28 structure of the Al6Fe phase. This substitution process is critical for the thermodynamic stabilization of the (Al, Cu)6Fe phase within the aluminum matrix.

caption: Temperature dependence of the magnetic entropy change (ΔSm–T) calculated from the Maxwell relation for field changes from 0.5 to 5.0 T, with the double-sided arrow marking the full-width at half-maximum (δTFWHM) at 5.0 T.
summary: The temperature dependence of the magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) is plotted for magnetic field increments of 0.5 T up to 5.0 T. The peak ΔSm value increases continuously with the magnetic field, indicating incomplete martensite-to-austenite transformation. The δTFWHM at 5.0 T is highlighted to characterize the breadth of the entropy change peak.

caption: R-space Cu EXAFS Fourier transforms for Ni 0.001 Cu NPs, Ni 0.01 Cu NPs, Cu NPs, and Cu foil standard, highlighting the radial distribution of Cu atoms.
summary: R-space Cu EXAFS spectra are displayed for Ni-doped Cu nanoparticles, pure Cu nanoparticles, and a Cu foil standard. These Fourier-transformed spectra corroborate the metallic state of the Cu species observed in the XANES and k-space EXAFS data, providing insight into the radial distribution of Cu atoms after reduction.

caption: Temperature field distribution contour for a 30 μm particle size, characterized by a narrow, elongated high-temperature region with two distinct peak zones.
summary: This contour plot depicts the temperature field distribution for a 30 μm particle size. The thermal field maintains a narrow and long distribution pattern, featuring two distinct peak temperature regions. These characteristics are consistent with the overall thermal behavior observed across different particle sizes during the deposition process.

caption: FTIR-ATR spectra comparing the polymeric material before modification (black) with those functionalized via PS3 (red) and PS4 (blue) protocols.
summary: FTIR-ATR spectra characterize the functionalization of 3DP-F2 formulations. The spectra track the disappearance of epoxy groups at 905 cm-1 from GMA and the emergence of imidazole ring bands at 1560 cm-1 and 625 cm-1, confirming successful modification of the polymer backbone using the PS3 and PS4 synthetic sequences.

caption: Spin-resolved partial density of states for Fe in Ni3-xFe xAl (x = 0.125), comparing (dxy, dxz, dyz) orbitals represented by solid lines against (dx2-y2, dz2) orbitals shown as dash-dot lines relative to the Fermi level.
summary: This plot illustrates the spin-resolved partial density of states for Fe atoms in Ni3-xFe xAl. The data reveals the electronic distribution of specific d-orbitals relative to the Fermi level. Notably, there is no significant lifting of the degeneracy for the eg-states (dxz, dyz), indicating stable electronic configurations within the alloy structure.

caption: Surface morphology of a single-layer NiTiCu deposit on a NiTi substrate processed at a current intensity of 40 A.
summary: This photograph illustrates the surface morphology of a single-layer NiTiCu deposit on a NiTi substrate, fabricated with a current intensity of 40 A. The image reveals the microstretch patterns developed during the printing process, providing a visual representation of the material deposition at this specific energy input level.

caption: Quasibinary NiTi–Nb phase diagram calculated by Piao et al., illustrating the compositional relationships and eutectic behavior within the NiTi–Nb system.
summary: The quasibinary NiTi–Nb phase diagram, calculated by Piao et al., provides a comprehensive overview of the system's phase equilibria. It indicates that the eutectic composition consists of a Ni–45Ti–10Nb at% matrix with Nb–13Ni–13Ti at% lamellae, while also defining the solid solubility limits of Nb in NiTi at the eutectic temperature.

caption: Oxygen elemental distribution map obtained via EDS for the AZ91D alloy wear track at 10 N.
summary: Oxygen elemental distribution within the AZ91D alloy wear track at 10 N highlights the presence of oxide debris. This mapping confirms that MgO forms during the wear process, with a thin oxide layer observed in the vicinity, consistent with the localized oxidation occurring under the applied mechanical load.

caption: Activation volumes measured at room temperature and 77 K for Cr-Co-Ni MEA and Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni HEA single crystals compared to conventional binary FCC solid solutions as a function of yield stress.
summary: Activation volumes for the Cr-Co-Ni MEA at both room temperature and 77 K are plotted against yield stress. These values fall precisely on the master curves defined by conventional binary FCC solid solutions, further supporting the validity of the stress equivalence concept for these complex concentrated alloys.

caption: Comparison of rotating-bending fatigue lives for samples with and without LSPwC treatment.
summary: The rotating-bending fatigue lives of samples without and with LSPwC treatment are compared in this plot. The data illustrates the performance difference between the untreated base metal and the LSPwC-treated samples, highlighting the impact of the surface treatment on the fatigue life of the material under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Standard orthographic CAD projection of the RhD unit cell designed in nTop software.
summary: This panel displays the RhD unit cell in a standard orthographic CAD projection. The unit cell was designed using nTop software to serve as the fundamental building block for the periodically repeated cubic structures, providing a clear geometric representation of the RhD architecture for subsequent structural analysis.

caption: Contour map displaying the iso-residual stress (RS) reduction percentage for the alloy subjected to aging temperatures between 190 °C and 240 °C for durations up to 3 hours.
summary: This iso-RS reduction map quantifies the decrease in residual stress levels as a function of aging temperature and time. Based on XRD analysis, the data demonstrates that specific thermal treatments, such as 244 °C for 180 minutes, correlate with significant reductions in residual stress, consistent with established experimental trends.

caption: UV-DRS reflection spectra of TBPB and TBPB-total protein complexes on paper substrates, illustrating the colorimetric response to total protein concentrations between 1 g/dL and 12 g/dL.
summary: This panel presents UV-DRS reflection spectra recorded from 380 to 750 nm to analyze colorimetric reactions on TBPB-incorporated paper strips. The spectra demonstrate the optical response of TBPB-total protein complexes across a concentration range of 1 g/dL to 12 g/dL, facilitating the study of protein-induced colorimetric changes on the analytical substrate.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) curves for SLM-fabricated and as-cast Ti-64 alloys, showing the evolution of potential over a 3600 s immersion period in various electrolytes.
summary: The OCP curves for SLM-fabricated and as-cast Ti-64 alloys are presented, demonstrating that the potential reaches a stable plateau after 3600 seconds of immersion. This steady-state behavior is attributed to the RedOx reactions occurring at the electrochemical interface within NaOH, SBF, NaCl, and H2SO4 electrolyte environments.

caption: Comparison of power consumption for CT and UAT processes under varying cooling strategies.
summary: This figure illustrates the power consumption characteristics of machine tools during conventional turning (CT) and ultrasonic-assisted turning (UAT). By evaluating different cooling strategies, the data highlights how specific environmental conditions influence energy usage, providing a comparative analysis of power efficiency between the two distinct machining methods under various cooling configurations.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology of the multi-layer multi-bead cladding specimen processed with induction heating at 200°C.
summary: This panel presents the three-dimensional morphology of a multi-layer multi-bead cladding specimen processed under induction heating at 200°C. This visualization demonstrates the impact of higher temperature induction heating on the cladding geometry, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of how varying thermal conditions influence the final morphology of the deposited material.

caption: Coercivity of 72 h milled Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixture plotted against annealing temperature, showing a soft magnetic character at room temperature with a value of 10.87±0.54 Oe.
summary: This plot displays the coercivity of 72 h milled Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixture as a function of annealing temperature. The data confirms the soft magnetic nature of the material at room temperature, characterized by a coercivity of 10.87±0.54 Oe, providing insight into the magnetic stability of the powder mixture after processing.

caption: Representative unit cell geometries generated by varying the incline angle θ from 0° to 180°, showing both top inserts of the parameterized shape and bottom inserts of the mirrored lattice configurations.
summary: This panel displays various unit cell geometries derived from incline angles ranging from 0° to 180°. The structure is parameterized in the top inserts and mirrored across four quadrants in the bottom inserts, resulting in eight distinct configurations selected for simulation, including specific angles like 0°, 33°, 90°, and 165°.

caption: Time-resolved simulation of the melt pool geometry during beam traversal, where colors represent distinct crystal orientations and solidification occurs behind the moving heat source.
summary: This panel displays a time-resolved simulation of the melt pool geometry during beam traversal. The visualization highlights the dynamic nature of the process, showing solidification occurring behind the moving heat source. Colors are utilized to represent distinct crystal orientations, providing insight into the microstructural evolution during the beam passage.

caption: Nyquist plot of Q345 rolled steel immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, showing a depressed arc characteristic of electrochemical impedance behavior.
summary: This Nyquist plot illustrates the electrochemical impedance response of Q345 rolled steel during immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The data reveals a depressed arc within the frequency range of 10^4 Hz to 10 Hz, indicating specific corrosion-related interfacial behavior observed during the exposure period.

caption: Absorbance spectra of SL:Er,Yb phosphor and composite powders (CsPbBr3+SL:Er,Yb, CsPbBr1.5I1.5+SL:Er,Yb, and CsPbBr2.25I0.75+SL:Er,Yb) showing absorption peaks at 268 nm and 358 nm for the phosphor, with broader bands from 280 to 600 nm for iodide-containing composites.
summary: Absorbance spectra for SL:Er,Yb phosphor exhibit peaks at 268 nm and 358 nm. Incorporating iodide into the CsPbBr3 quantum dots results in broader absorption bands extending from 280 to 600 nm. These broadening effects correspond to the main absorption bands of the quantum dots at 510 nm and 553 nm.

caption: Comparative performance evaluation of the fine-tuned model versus baseline models in the option selection task, highlighting superior accuracy despite a reduced model size.
summary: Performance metrics for the option selection task demonstrate that the fine-tuned model achieves superior results compared to larger baseline models. This indicates that the fine-tuning process effectively optimizes the model for G-code generation tasks, allowing for high-accuracy performance while maintaining a reduced model size for improved computational efficiency.

caption: Pole figure of UIT-1 CoCrNi MEA in the XOZ plane, illustrating a significant reduction in texture intensity.
summary: This pole figure displays the crystallographic texture of the UIT-1 CoCrNi MEA in the XOZ plane. In contrast to the other processing conditions, the UIT-1 treatment leads to a significant decrease in texture intensity, suggesting that this specific impact parameter is more effective at reducing the anisotropy of the sample.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the normalized performance scores of produced monoliths across four key indicators: printability, strength, adsorption, and diffusion.
summary: This radar chart provides a comparative visualization of monolith performance by mapping normalized scores for printability, strength, adsorption, and diffusion. Each metric is scaled relative to the best-performing sample in its respective category, offering a comprehensive overview of the material's multi-functional capabilities as detailed in the study's performance evaluation.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the HT0 sample showing grain orientation distribution relative to the build direction.
summary: Inverse pole figure map of the HT0 sample displays the grain orientation distribution relative to the build direction. EBSD analysis over a 1500 μm × 1500 μm area reveals that the HT0 sample exhibits no significant textural differences compared to the as-received AR0 sample, maintaining a consistent grain structure prior to deformation.

caption: Microchannel architecture fabricated within a printed pre-form using sacrificial template techniques.
summary: Microchannels are integrated into the printed pre-form using sacrificial templates. This approach allows for the creation of internal structural features within the extruded material. The process is part of the broader capability to further shape pre-forms using wet or dry methods after the initial direct ink writing extrusion.

caption: Dilatometric curve illustrating the thermal expansion and contraction behavior of the deposited metal during cooling at a rate of 50 °C/s.
summary: Representing the thermal response of the material at a faster cooling rate of 50 °C/s, this dilatometric curve provides critical data for phase transformation analysis. Together with the 20 °C/s data, these results facilitate the construction of CCT diagrams and the estimation of microstructural constituents like bainite content in the deposited wall.

caption: Schematic representation of solute diffusion-dominated solidification at the melt pool boundary, illustrating the formation of Si-rich cellular grains.
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial stage of solidification in the Finemet alloy melt pool. Solute diffusion dominates at the melt pool boundary, leading to the formation of Si-rich cellular grains. These features are highlighted by red arrows, demonstrating the localized microstructural evolution driven by solute-controlled growth mechanisms during the process.

caption: TOF-SIMS depth profile of an as-grown Cu-Ni alloy film with 200 nm Cu and 50 nm Ni, highlighting the elemental counts relative to the sputtering depth into the substrate.
summary: The TOF-SIMS analysis for the 200 nm Cu/50 nm Ni alloy film demonstrates the depth-dependent concentration of Cu, Ni, and C. Carbon atoms are shown to penetrate the alloy film during the 1000 °C growth process, while the Ni- signal intensity is modulated by the specific copper thickness of the sample.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental methane conversion rates against values predicted by the LHHW kinetic model, demonstrating a strong correlation and optimal fit between observed and calculated data.
summary: The parity plot displays the relationship between experimental and predicted reaction rates based on the LHHW kinetic model. The alignment of data points along the parity line confirms an optimal fit, indicating that the model accurately predicts the kinetic behavior of the bimetallic catalysts under the tested conditions.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for dehydrogenated Ti-30V-6Cr-0M-10 (M = Fe, Co, Ni) alloys doped with 4 wt% Zr.
summary: This figure displays the X-ray diffraction patterns of dehydrogenated Ti-30V-6Cr-0M-10 alloys, where M represents Fe, Co, or Ni, all containing 4 wt% Zr. These patterns provide structural characterization of the samples in their dehydrogenated state, allowing for the identification of crystalline phases present in these specific alloy compositions.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of MCF-7 cells (green) within an RGD-functionalized P100 gel (orange/red), with inserts showing the accumulation of RGD peptides around the captured cells.
summary: Fluorescence imaging confirms the efficient incorporation of biotinylated RGD peptides into the P100 hydrogel network. The RGD peptides are observed to accumulate around the captured MCF-7 cells, as highlighted in the inserts, which is consistent with the expected binding interaction between the peptides and cell surface integrins.

caption: Simulated solidification microstructure for the 11th layer at the middle position.
summary: Simulated solidification microstructure for the 11th layer at the middle position. Thermal accumulation in this region slows the cooling rate, impacting the final microstructure. The simulation, which takes 20 hours to compute, captures the solidification morphology for the 11th layer at this specific middle location of the curved component.

caption: Thermophysical parameters of GH3536 alloy utilized in the SLM simulation, compiled from established literature sources [26, 35].
summary: Thermophysical parameters of the GH3536 alloy are presented for use in the SLM simulation model. These values, sourced from established literature references [26, 35], provide the necessary material properties required to accurately model the thermal behavior and physical characteristics of the alloy during the selective laser melting process.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics recorded with a Langmuir wire probe subjected to coil magnetic fields between 0 and 8.5 mT.
summary: Presented here are the I-V characteristics derived from a Langmuir wire probe setup. Similar to the flat probe measurements, these data points were collected while applying coil magnetic fields spanning 0 to 8.5 mT, providing a comparative electronic characterization of the wire probe's performance under varying magnetic field intensities.

caption: Calculated DOS effective mass and band effective mass plotted against Ni alloying content x in Bi2-xNixSe3 samples.
summary: This panel displays the calculated DOS effective mass and band effective mass as a function of Ni alloying content in Bi2-xNixSe3. These electronic parameters are presented to characterize the influence of Ni substitution on the electronic structure of the bismuth selenide system as the composition x varies.

caption: Atomic model of the (Cr, Re)23C6 crystal structure in (001) projection, featuring Rhenium substitution at the Cr2 (8c) site.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the (Cr, Re)23C6 crystal structure with Rhenium substituted at the Cr2 (8c) site. The model is projected along the (001) direction and provides the necessary structural data to simulate the HAADF-STEM image presented in panel (h).

caption: AFM topography of Ni80-Cu20 anode film showing the alloy surface.
summary: Atomic force microscopy of the Ni80-Cu20 anode film illustrates the surface morphology of the alloy. The Ni-Cu electrodes consistently show lower roughness than the Ni80-Fe20 alloy surface, providing insight into how varying the alloying element and concentration influences the structural integrity and surface finish of the electrode films.

caption: Load-displacement responses obtained from compression tests of cross-like structures with a nominal strut diameter of 1 mm, showing post-buckling deformation behavior.
summary: Load-displacement curves for 1 mm diameter cross-like structures demonstrate the mechanical response under compression. The data includes multiple tests per condition to ensure reliability. The observed post-buckling deformation, as evidenced by the collapsed structure image, highlights the structural integrity and failure mode occurring after the peak load is reached.

caption: Areal surface roughness (Sa) of the top lattice surface plotted as a function of laser power and scanning speed.
summary: The top surface roughness of the lattice structures is presented as a function of laser power and scanning speed. Roughness values decrease with higher laser power and lower scanning speed, reaching a minimum of 26.5 µm at 150 W and 200 mm/s, while peaking at 70 µm at 50 W and 1200 mm/s.

caption: Calculated phase fraction of Al2FeSi and BCC intermetallic phases in the bi-metallic joint as a function of time and temperature.
summary: This panel presents DICTRA-computed phase fractions for Al2FeSi and BCC intermetallics within the bi-metallic joint. The calculations evaluate the evolution of these phases across various time-temperature combinations, providing a theoretical basis for understanding the growth kinetics of embrittling intermetallic layers during the isothermal heat treatment process.

caption: Synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) profiles for rambutan and longan starches, highlighting the lamellar architecture of the starch granules.
summary: Synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) profiles for rambutan and longan starches are displayed here. This non-destructive technique probes the lamellar architecture of the starch while preserving its structural integrity, allowing for a detailed analysis of the internal organization of the starch granules across different varieties.

caption: Normalized fatigue S-N diagram and corresponding fitted reference curve for EBM-processed material batches.
summary: This panel displays the normalized fatigue S-N diagram for EBM-processed material batches. It includes the experimental data points alongside the calculated reference curve, illustrating the fatigue performance characteristics of the EBM samples as part of the broader comparative analysis of the considered material batches presented in the study.

caption: BCC unit cells illustrating the effect of the taper factor T.
summary: This panel presents BCC unit cells characterized by a specific taper factor T. This design feature is a critical component of the framework, enabling precise control over strut geometry. By adjusting the taper factor, the structural integrity and load-bearing capacity of the lattice can be systematically modified for specific applications.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph illustrating the transition zone between fine-grained (FG) and coarse-grained (CG) regions in the as-built specimen's bottom section.
summary: This bright-field STEM image captures the microstructural transition between fine-grained and coarse-grained zones within the bottom section of an as-built specimen. The micrograph provides a clear visualization of the grain size variation, serving as a foundational observation for analyzing the spatial distribution of microstructural features in the material.

caption: Individual EDS elemental distribution mappings for the Ti35V35(CrMnFe)30 HEA, showing the spatial distribution of constituent elements.
summary: Individual EDS elemental distribution mappings for the Ti35V35(CrMnFe)30 HEA illustrate the spatial distribution of constituent elements. Consistent with the overlap image, these maps confirm the existence of four distinct phase regions, including areas with varying Ti and V content, following the 900 °C heat treatment process.

caption: Comparison of Young modulus (MPa) and magnetization (emu/g) values for L-MS and H-MS hydrated scaffolds.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the mechanical and magnetic properties of L-MS and H-MS hydrated scaffolds. The Young modulus was determined through unconfined mechanical testing of 20 x 20 mm samples, while magnetization is reported in emu/g. The data provides a comparative overview of the stiffness and magnetic response for both scaffold types.

caption: KAM map of the severely deformed region in sample 718-COL, showing the spatial distribution of local misorientation angles.
summary: The KAM map displays the dislocation accumulation in the severely deformed region of the 718-COL sample. This visualization provides insight into the local misorientation distribution, which serves as a proxy for dislocation density, allowing for a comparative assessment of deformation intensity within the microstructure after tensile testing.

caption: Ohmic resistance characteristics observed during the second electrolysis cycle for cells incorporating cross-linked PVA membranes with different Cs contents alongside a Nafion 117 control.
summary: Ohmic resistance values for the electrochemical cell in electrolysis mode are shown for various crosslinked PVA/Cs membranes and a Nafion 117 membrane. This panel specifically depicts the resistance data collected during the second electrolysis cycle at room temperature under a constant current density of 50 mA/cm2.

caption: Titanium elemental distribution map of the Ti-2.5Al–6Nb–6Cu alloy, demonstrating a homogeneous distribution of the element throughout the microstructure.
summary: The titanium elemental map confirms the successful dissolution of powder particles during processing. The distribution of titanium appears homogeneous across the microstructure, indicating that the alloying elements have been effectively incorporated into the matrix, consistent with the overall goal of achieving a uniform chemical composition in the alloy.

caption: Evolution of the mode I stress intensity factor (SIF) as a function of angular crack extension for a pre-cracked ORL with a fixed crack length of 40 μm, comparing values at the crack center (blue) and crack ends (black).
summary: This plot illustrates the calculated evolution of the mode I stress intensity factor for a pre-cracked ORL with a thickness of 40 μm. By varying the angular crack extension, the graph highlights distinct SIF trends at the center and ends of the crack, providing critical insight into fracture behavior under these conditions.

caption: High-speed photographic capture of the GMAW arc behavior during the fourth stage of the 10 ms observation window.
summary: This high-speed photographic image captures the arc behavior during the fourth phase of the 10 ms observation period in GMAW. The sequence of images, including this one, allows for the detailed observation of arc fluctuations and their direct correlation with the molten pool flow behavior.

caption: Magnetization as a function of applied field for the HTHed Schwarz sample, recorded across the FM-PM transition range.
summary: Magnetization as a function of applied field for the HTHed Schwarz sample is displayed, with data recorded across the ferromagnetic-paramagnetic transition range. These isothermal M(H) curves facilitate the investigation of the magnetic phase transition characteristics inherent to the Schwarz-structured material as it approaches its critical transition temperature.

caption: Pole figure analysis showing the modified crystallographic texture of the meso gear after laser shock peening (LSP) processing.
summary: This pole figure demonstrates the changes in crystallographic texture resulting from laser shock peening. As a surface treatment method, LSP significantly alters the material's orientation distribution, highlighting the potential of this process to improve the endurance and performance characteristics of the processed meso gear components compared to as-built samples.

caption: Three-dimensional phase-field simulation showing the plate-like morphology of a TCP precipitate in Ni–10Al–10Cr–12Mo at 1100 °C after a dimensionless time t* = 10000.
summary: This 3D phase-field simulation illustrates the morphological evolution of a TCP precipitate within a Ni–10Al–10Cr–12Mo alloy at 1100 °C. At a dimensionless time of t* = 10000, the precipitate exhibits a distinct plate-like structure, demonstrating the growth behavior of the TCP phase as time progresses during the simulation process.

caption: Two-dimensional visualization of the overlapped atomic volume projected onto the (001) slip plane.
summary: This panel presents a two-dimensional representation of the overlapped atomic volume on the (001) slip plane. It serves as the foundational geometric model for analyzing dislocation behavior, providing the spatial context necessary for evaluating the atomic interactions and volume overlaps along specific slip directions described in subsequent panels.

caption: UV-shielding rate plotted as a function of wavelength, showing that the UVA shielding efficiency increases with the SL/CNCs ratio, achieving a maximum of 99% for the SL-10/C/P coating.
summary: This plot illustrates the UV-shielding rate of the coatings, where the UVA shielding efficiency increases with the SL/CNCs ratio. The SL-10/C/P coating reaches a maximum shielding rate of 99% in the UVA region and exhibits nearly complete shielding in the UVB region, demonstrating high UV-blocking performance.

caption: Representative fluorescence images of Mito-Tracker Green staining, visualizing mitochondrial morphology in NPs across different groups.
summary: Mito-Tracker Green fluorescence imaging allows for the visualization of mitochondrial health in NPs. The images demonstrate that DEPGM treatment helps maintain mitochondrial integrity under oxidative stress. By reducing ROS generation and protecting mitochondrial structures, the hydrogel effectively inhibits the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway, supporting the overall cytoprotection of the NPs.

caption: Comparative plot of laser reflectivity and Kubelka-Munk (K-M) absorption factors for AlSi10Mg and nano-Nb-modified AlSi10Mg powders.
summary: The laser reflectance and K-M absorption factors of AlSi10Mg and nano-Nb-modified AlSi10Mg powders are shown in Fig. 1 d. This plot provides a comparative analysis of the optical properties of the base alloy versus the modified composite, highlighting how the Nb modification influences laser energy absorption characteristics.

caption: Estimated P-S-N curves for HG geometry, displaying the median, 10-th, and 90-th percentile fatigue life predictions.
summary: The HG geometry fatigue response is characterized by estimated P-S-N curves, including median, 10-th, and 90-th percentile bounds. These curves were derived using the maximum likelihood principle to account for both failure and runout data, showing good agreement with experimental results where approximately 80% of data points fall within the percentile bounds.

caption: Bode modulus plots accompanied by the corresponding equivalent circuit model used for fitting the electrochemical impedance data.
summary: Bode modulus plots are displayed alongside the equivalent circuit model utilized to analyze the electrochemical impedance data of the dissimilar joints. This representation facilitates the interpretation of the corrosion behavior and charge transfer characteristics of the joints prepared with different brazing filler materials under the tested experimental conditions.

caption: High-resolution TEM image of the TiB structure, providing atomic-scale detail of the reinforcement phase.
summary: High-resolution TEM imaging of the TiB structures reveals the atomic arrangement of the reinforcement phase. This visualization, when combined with diffraction analysis, confirms the B27 crystal structure of the TiB phase formed within the titanium matrix during the laser surface glazing treatment.

caption: Off-diagonal thermodynamic factor ΓSiCu displayed against Cu concentration at 973 K, with Si concentration held at 5 at %.
summary: This panel presents the off-diagonal factor ΓSiCu, which represents the thermodynamic coupling between the Si flux and the Cu concentration gradient. As a primary concern for the correction methodology, this term quantifies the effect of Cu on Si diffusion, with the vertical dashed line marking the 2.5 at % average concentration.

caption: SHAP analysis result for the alloy composition-area fraction model, illustrating the influence of various elements on the precipitate area fraction.
summary: This SHAP analysis plot evaluates the alloy composition-area fraction model. Feature importance decreases from top to bottom, with Cr identified as the most significant influence on the area fraction, followed by Co and Ni. The color bar indicates that red represents higher feature values, correlating with the model's output.

caption: 2D wear track depth profiles for untreated, C2T, and C3T samples subjected to 10N wear tests.
summary: This panel displays 2D wear track profiles for samples tested at 10N. The C3T sample shows negligible wear, making the track difficult to identify. Conversely, untreated and C2T samples exhibit deep wear tracks between 25 and 30 μm, characterized by rough surfaces typical of adhesive wear in beta Ti.

caption: Comparison of impedance radii for the XOZ plane of LPBF 316L before and after the passivation process.
summary: The XOZ plane of the LPBF 316L sample exhibits minimal change in its impedance arc radius following the critical pitting initiation and subsequent repassivation. This comparison highlights the specific electrochemical evolution of the XOZ orientation within the broader context of the material's enhanced passivation properties after localized corrosion attack.

caption: Schematic illustration of the additive process for the upper layer, showing how the rotating tool influences grains at the top of the initial layer to promote further fracturing and refinement.
summary: Depicted here is the additive process for the upper layer during the FRAM process. The rotating tool exerts influence on the grains located at the top of the initial layer, leading to further fracturing and refinement of these grains, which demonstrates the mechanism of grain evolution across multiple layers.

caption: First cycle polarization curves for Nafion 117 and cross-linked PVA membranes with varying Cs concentrations in an H2/Cl2 fuel cell.
summary: This panel displays the initial cycle polarization curves for H2/Cl2 fuel cells utilizing Nafion 117 and cross-linked PVA membranes with different Cs concentrations. The test was conducted at room temperature with specific gas flow rates of 50 ml/min for H2 and 30 ml/min for HClO, establishing baseline electrochemical performance.

caption: Control unit featuring a simple 2-axis CNC module and thermocouple interface.
summary: This control unit manages the welding parameters and integrates a thermocouple module for real-time temperature monitoring. It provides the necessary CNC control for the torch holder's movement, ensuring precise execution of the welding process as specified in the experimental methodology for the WAAM manufacturing setup.

caption: Isothermal TTT diagram of X37CrMoV5-1 tool steel specifically derived for the PBF-LB/M processing condition.
summary: This panel presents an isothermal TTT diagram for X37CrMoV5-1 tool steel, specifically tailored to represent the PBF-LB/M processing condition. The diagram illustrates the transformation kinetics and phase stability boundaries relevant to the rapid solidification and thermal history inherent in the laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing process.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology of a truss structure fabricated at a printing speed of 180 mm/s under high-temperature vacuum conditions.
