summary: Shown is the three-dimensional morphology of a truss structure fabricated at a printing speed of 180 mm/s under high-temperature vacuum conditions. This image captures the structural characteristics at the highest tested printing speed, completing the set of morphological data used to evaluate the impact of processing speeds on truss geometry.

caption: Pore volume density map for the intact specimen, where the origin represents the exterior surface and the x-axis denotes the radial distance toward the central axis.
summary: The pore volume density map visualizes the spatial concentration of pores within the intact specimen. The plot uses a radial coordinate system where the origin at zero corresponds to the exterior surface, and the edge distance represents the radial progression from the surface toward the central axis of the sample.

caption: Precision-Recall (PR) curve for the model without missing values, showing trade-offs between precision and recall.
summary: The PR curve visualizes the trade-off between precision and recall, compensating for limitations of individual metrics. The model demonstrates excellent classification ability, achieving AUC values of 0.95, 0.93, and 0.89 for predicting FCC, BCC, and FCC+BCC phases, respectively, confirming its effectiveness in distinguishing between the three distinct phase structures.

caption: Isothermal section of the Fe–Ni–Cr ternary system at 800 °C.
summary: This panel displays the isothermal section of the Fe–Ni–Cr ternary system at 800 °C. According to the provided references, this diagram helps clarify the equilibrium relationships between the FCC, BCC, and σ phases, which are particularly relevant for understanding phase stability at temperatures approaching 1000 °C.

caption: Slip distance versus shear stress for a 4000 Å edge dislocation, calculated from 5 independent PN simulations, with the solid black line representing the average and the shaded region indicating the standard deviation.
summary: This panel presents the slip distance versus shear stress for a 4000 Å edge dislocation based on 5 independent Peierls-Nabarro simulations. The solid black line indicates the average stress across simulations, while the shaded region represents the standard deviation. The horizontal dashed line marks the asymptotic yield stress at large scale.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density distributions for S4, showing a significant reduction from the single track (18.4 ± 10.8 × 10^14 m^-2) to the fine-grained (7.3 ± 4.8 × 10^14 m^-2) and coarse-grained (5.4 ± 2.6 × 10^14 m^-2) regions.
summary: This plot quantifies the GND density across three S4 specimen regions. Results demonstrate a clear reduction in dislocation density, decreasing from 18.4 × 10^14 m^-2 in the single track to 7.3 × 10^14 m^-2 in fine-grained regions and 5.4 × 10^14 m^-2 in coarse-grained regions, indicating varying levels of lattice distortion.

caption: Longitudinal section Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) distribution map of the BM-Ti-25V–15Cr specimen solution-treated at 850 °C.
summary: Representing the longitudinal section of the BM-Ti-25V–15Cr specimen solution-treated at 850 °C, this KAM distribution map highlights the microstructural strain state. Consistent with the cross-sectional data, the specimen exhibits a significant decrease in KAM values after the solution treatment, reflecting effective stress relief within the β-phase.

caption: TG-DSC curves illustrating the thermal decomposition behavior of the feedstock materials.
summary: The TG-DSC curves of the feedstocks are shown in Fig. 3 (a). These curves provide essential data regarding the thermal decomposition behavior of the feedstock materials, characterizing the mass loss and heat flow events that occur during the heating process to inform subsequent processing steps.

caption: Tafel polarization curves for SLM-316L stainless steel specimens fabricated in three distinct construction directions, illustrating the cathodic and anodic polarization processes.
summary: Tafel polarization curves for SLM-316L stainless steel specimens built in three different orientations are displayed. Although the specimens exhibit variations in corrosion potential and current density, they share similar overall trends, consistently demonstrating two primary electrochemical processes: cathodic polarization and anodic polarization across all construction directions.

caption: Reduction ratio of UTS and UFS values for printed specimens presented relative to the increasing number of heating cycles.
summary: Reduction ratios for both ultimate tensile strength and ultimate flexural strength are displayed as a function of the number of heating cycles. This plot quantifies the degradation in mechanical properties of the printed specimens as they undergo repeated thermal processing cycles during the manufacturing sequence.

caption: SAED pattern corresponding to the MC carbides observed in the stir zone of the AM-PWHT specimen.
summary: This SAED pattern is associated with the MC carbides identified in the stir zone of the AM-PWHT specimen. The diffraction pattern serves as a diagnostic tool to confirm the presence and crystallographic nature of the MC carbides, complementing the structural information provided by the HAADF-TEM imaging of the stir zone.

caption: Common neighbor analysis of the initial powder structure showing a uniform FCC phase distribution.
summary: The initial structure of the powder system is visualized using common neighbor analysis, which reveals that the material consists entirely of the FCC phase. This snapshot serves as the baseline state before any equilibration or structural relaxation occurs within the simulated powder assembly.

caption: Chemical structure of the cellulose polymer chain, illustrating the linear arrangement of n anhydroglucose units connected by β1,4 glycosidic linkages.
summary: This panel displays the chemical structure of cellulose, a polysaccharide composed of a linear chain of n anhydroglucose units. These units are linked together through C1 and C4 positions via β1,4 glycosidic bonds, forming the fundamental polymer backbone of the cellulose molecule as described in the structural model.

caption: Transmission spectra of the immersion solution at neutral pH 7, with plots for room temperature (left) and 37 °C (right) demonstrating consistent optical stability.
summary: Testing at a neutral pH of 7 reveals no significant increase or decrease in solution transmission or spectral broadening over time. The transmission spectra remain near 100% at both room temperature and 37 °C, confirming the absence of Au NP leakage from the hydrogel samples into the buffer medium.

caption: Coulombic efficiency performance of the Ti-WO 3 electrode across five reuse cycles during 4-NP degradation.
summary: Panel d presents the coulombic efficiency calculated for each of the five reuse cycles of the Ti-WO 3 electrode. These results, when combined with the energy consumption data, confirm the high stability and effective recyclability of the Ti-WO 3 film for the degradation of 4-nitrophenol in the E3L-PECR reactor.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves showing mass loss under air for 3D printed samples containing 0%, 25%, and 50% wt. titanium acrylate.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrate the thermal decomposition behavior of 3D printed composite structures under air. The data indicates that organic components within the samples, regardless of the titanium acrylate concentration, undergo complete decomposition at temperatures ranging between 500 °C and 600 °C, confirming the thermal stability limits of the printed materials.

caption: Kinetic dose response assay images of C3H10 T1/2 cells treated with C5 photoinitiator, highlighting morphological changes and cell survival.
summary: Kinetic dose response assays for the C5-treated group visualize cell morphology and survival over time. These images demonstrate the biological response of C3H10 T1/2 cells to the C5 photoinitiator, which exhibits enhanced cell viability and migration capacity compared to TPO, as supported by the kinetic measurements.

caption: Overview of the TPCS-based U array dataset generation workflow, illustrating the integration of randomized parameters within 3D trigonometric functions and the implementation of geometric pass/fail criteria to ensure structural manufacturability.
summary: This schematic outlines the TPCS-based U array dataset generation process. It highlights the use of randomized parameters in 3D trigonometric functions to create diverse cellular geometries. Furthermore, the workflow incorporates specific pass/fail geometry tests, ensuring that all generated cells are suitable for fabrication into larger, functional cellular structures.

caption: Isothermal magnetization curves measured at 10 K as a function of the applied magnetic field.
summary: This panel displays isothermal magnetization curves at 10 K. For longer milling times, a higher effect on magnetization is observed at this low temperature. However, when the retained austenite content decreases after 30 minutes of milling, the magnetization at 10 K also decreases noticeably, reflecting the material's magnetic response.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for samples A, B, and C measured at a constant field of 0.05 T, illustrating the thermal evolution of magnetic properties during both heating and cooling cycles.
summary: This figure displays the temperature dependence of magnetization for samples A, B, and C under a 0.05 T magnetic field. Measurements were performed using a Magnetic Property Measurement System on homogenized ingot samples. The data capture both heating and cooling processes, with arrows in the inset highlighting the thermal hysteresis for sample B.

caption: Microhardness distribution map of the LPBFed Ti–45Nb specimen after annealing at 500 °C (HT-500).
summary: Representing the HT-500 annealing condition, this map illustrates the spatial variation of microhardness in the Ti–45Nb specimen. Consistent with the broader findings for the series, the overall distribution of microhardness remains uniform across the analyzed area of the specimen following this specific heat treatment process.

caption: Monte Carlo simulation results for F82H+1.4% 58 Ni irradiated at approximately 317 °C.
summary: Shown are the Monte Carlo simulation results for the F82H+1.4% 58 Ni alloy. While the target irradiation temperature was set to 300 °C, SiC thermometry specimens recorded an actual irradiation temperature of approximately 317 °C for this nickel-doped material during the irradiation experiment.

caption: Image Quality (IQ) map of the void region, demonstrating void coalescence through shear banding and the presence of low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) within the shear band.
summary: The IQ map reveals that voids coalesce with each other through the formation of shear bands. Large numbers of LAGBs are observed within these shear band regions, indicating that the coalescence process is accompanied by significant localized dislocation activity and subgrain formation under the applied 4.8 GPa impact load.

caption: HNMR spectrum of CP displaying chemical shifts at 0.84 ppm (methyl group), 1.81 ppm (methylene group), 3.6 ppm (methoxy group), and 5.3 ppm (double-bond containing material).
summary: The HNMR spectrum of CP identifies specific chemical shifts corresponding to the MMA monomer units and surface features. Signals at 0.84 ppm, 1.81 ppm, and 3.6 ppm are attributed to methyl, methylene, and methoxy groups, respectively, while the 5.3 ppm shift confirms the presence of double-bond containing material on the surface.

caption: Lithiation-phase apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions for 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes, derived from Eq. (1).
summary: This panel presents the apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions during the lithiation phase for 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes. Derived from Eq. (1), the plot characterizes the ion transport properties within the electrode materials, allowing for a direct comparison of diffusion kinetics between the two fabrication methods.

caption: Dark-field TEM image and inserted SAED pattern of the long strip-shaped particle region.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging combined with selected area electron diffraction (SAED) is employed to characterize the long strip-shaped particles. The diffraction pattern provides crystallographic information, confirming the phase identity of these elongated features within the LPBF-850 microstructure, which are distinct from the surrounding matrix grains.

caption: Overview of major industrial applications for Functionally Graded Materials (FGMs) across diverse engineering sectors.
summary: This figure provides a comprehensive classification of the primary industrial applications for Functionally Graded Materials. By illustrating the versatile capabilities of these materials, the diagram highlights their widespread utility across various engineering fields, serving as a foundational reference for understanding the practical deployment and functional scope of FGMs in modern industry.

caption: UV-VIS transmittance curves comparing different samples, illustrating the optical transparency and structural purity of the superlattice materials.
summary: UV-VIS transmittance curves for various samples are displayed to evaluate their optical properties. These measurements confirm the high transparency and structural purity of the superlattice materials, providing further validation of the quality achieved through the hot-wall MOCVD growth process.

caption: Isopleth section of the Ni–Ce–Al ternary phase diagram at a constant 5 wt% Al concentration, showing the predicted presence of FCC-Ni, Ni5Ce, and L12 phases for the Ni–17Ce–5Al composition.
summary: This ternary isopleth section for the Ni–Ce–Al system at 5 wt% Al demonstrates that the addition of aluminum increases the eutectic temperature to approximately 1250 °C. Furthermore, the diagram predicts the formation of the L12 γʹ-phase at lower temperatures, with FCC-Ni, Ni5Ce, and L12 phases expected for the Ni–17Ce–5Al alloy composition.

caption: Ni K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7.
summary: Ni K-edge Refle-XAFS spectra for Ni Alloy 59 are measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7. These spectra characterize the Ni environment at the surface of the alloy, providing insights into the chemical state of Ni under neutral pH conditions as part of the broader X-ray absorption spectroscopy analysis.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification performance of the VGG16 model across five distinct defect categories.
summary: The confusion matrix displays the classification accuracy of the VGG16 model when identifying five specific defect categories. By leveraging its deep convolutional architecture, the model effectively extracts hierarchical thermal features from temperature gradients, demonstrating solid baseline performance and clear class separation in its ability to categorize these defect patterns accurately.

caption: Radar plot evaluating multiple energy absorption metrics for the proposed OIS and OIHS, specifically highlighting the superior performance of the COPH configuration in terms of maximum plateau stress and crush force efficiency.
summary: This radar chart provides a multi-dimensional comparison of energy absorption indicators for the proposed origami structures. It emphasizes that the COPH configuration outperforms non-hybrid and other hybrid structures, specifically achieving the highest values for maximum plateau stress and crush force efficiency, thereby validating its superior mechanical energy absorption capabilities.

caption: TEM morphology of the Cu–Ni–Si alloy strip after stress relaxation at 125 °C, highlighting the coarsened precipitated phase.
summary: This TEM micrograph displays the morphology of the Cu–Ni–Si alloy strip following stress relaxation at 125 °C. The precipitated phase has undergone coarsening compared to its pre-relaxation state, reaching an average size of approximately 200 nm. This increased precipitate size is associated with reduced stress relaxation resistance in the material.

caption: Time-dependent UV-Vis spectra for the reduction of 4-NP using a 2.5 cm long Pd/C CR with a core diameter of 1.8 mm.
summary: UV-Vis spectra are shown for the reduction of 4-nitrophenol using a Pd/C coaxial reactor with a 2.5 cm length and a 1.8 mm core diameter. By tracking these spectra over time, the conversion efficiency of the reactor can be determined, contributing to the broader study of how core diameter affects catalytic performance.

caption: Shifted wavelength design based on design 0 but with the wave shifted by 1.5 mm.
summary: The shifted wavelength design (shift λ/4) is presented as a variation of design 0, incorporating a phase shift of 1.5 mm. This configuration tests the sensitivity of the fracture bending performance to the spatial alignment of the wavy interlayer relative to the loading conditions.

caption: Response surface plot showing the interaction between printing speed and infill density on compressive strength at a 100 % infill level.
summary: Representing the interaction between printing speed and infill density at a 100 % infill level, this plot illustrates the compressive strength of FDM-printed PEEK-carbon fibre composites. The response surface highlights the influence of these parameters on mechanical performance, demonstrating how full infill density affects the overall compressive strength of the specimens.

caption: Linear correlation between predicted incident strain amplitudes and measured values averaged over the plateau region, validating the velocity measurement and initial pulse generation.
summary: This parity plot confirms a strong linear correlation between the predicted incident strain amplitudes and the measured values averaged over the plateau region. This validation step confirms the accuracy of the velocity measurement and the reliability of the initial pulse generation process essential for the SHPB experimental setup.

caption: Friction coefficient curves recorded during tribological testing of the LPBF-fabricated samples under applied loads of 10 N and 20 N.
summary: Friction coefficient curves for the TiC/AZ91D composite under 10 N and 20 N loads are presented, revealing relatively noticeable fluctuations during the testing process. These curves characterize the tribological behavior of the composite material under different loading conditions, highlighting the dynamic nature of the friction coefficient during the wear test.

caption: Representative fluorescence images of hBMSCs stained with an F-actin probe to visualize cytoskeletal morphology after 3 days of culture.
summary: Fluorescence imaging of F-actin stained hBMSCs after 3 days of culture allows for the observation of cytoskeletal morphology. These images provide visual evidence of cell alignment and structural organization within the 3D-printed hydrogel scaffolds, serving as a basis for quantifying actin anisotropy.

caption: XPS survey spectra of Cr20, Cr30, Cr40, and Cr50 alloys after immersion in a 1 M HCl solution.
summary: This figure presents the XPS survey spectra obtained from the passive films of Cr20, Cr30, Cr40, and Cr50 alloys following exposure to a 1 M HCl solution. These spectroscopic results characterize the chemical composition of the passive films formed on the surfaces of samples with varying chromium content.

caption: Camera images illustrating the deformation and crushing progression of the zero-order HC material under compressive loading applied along the x-direction.
summary: Camera images document the structural response of the zero-order HC configuration during crush loading. This panel specifically highlights the deformation trends and the progression from initial loading to densification when the material is subjected to compression along the x-direction, providing visual evidence of the material's mechanical behavior under these conditions.

caption: DSC thermal arrest curve for Ni53Fe21Ga26 AQ ribbons recorded at a scanning rate of 15 K/min, showing a dip that shifts to the right and becomes more accentuated.
summary: This DSC curve illustrates the thermal arrest behavior of Ni53Fe21Ga26 AQ ribbons at a scanning rate of 15 K/min. Observations indicate that the thermal dip shifts slightly to the right and becomes more accentuated compared to other rates, reflecting the alloy's sensitivity to scanning speed.

caption: Digital image correlation strain field map of a 45° printed dog bone specimen at the moment of fracture, including a coordinate system overlay.
summary: This panel presents the DIC strain field for a 45° printed dog bone specimen at fracture, alongside a schematic showing the relationship between global and local coordinates. The data supports the calculation of Young’s modulus E45°, which is expressed as a function of transversely isotropic elastic constants and the printing angle.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization behavior showing the variation of magnetic moment M as a function of temperature.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic response of the material by displaying the variation of magnetization M against temperature. The data provides a clear visualization of the thermal dependence of the magnetic properties, confirming the relationship between the magnetic moment and the temperature range investigated in the study.

caption: 3D μ-XCT reconstruction of the WE43-PEO2 strut highlighting the PEO layer morphology in a region characterized by high segregation of intermetallic precipitates.
summary: This 3D μ-XCT reconstruction displays the WE43-PEO2 strut, focusing on the PEO layer morphology within a highly segregated region. Observations indicate that areas with large Mg-Y or Mg-Nd intermetallic precipitates exhibit a higher density of large indents and increased porosity at the interface between the bulk material and the PEO layer.

caption: Full-range FTIR spectra comparing untreated NBSK and esterified NBSK samples, highlighting chemical changes.
summary: FTIR spectra reveal the chemical transformation of NBSK following esterification. Two characteristic peaks emerge near 1718 cm-1 and 1577 cm-1, which correspond to the C=O and –COO- groups introduced by the maleic acid ester. These spectral changes confirm the successful incorporation of ester groups into the NBSK fiber structure.

caption: In-situ synchrotron HT-XRD patterns of Ni-17Cr-10Al alloy recorded during heating and subsequent isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C in air.
summary: This panel displays in-situ synchrotron high-temperature XRD patterns for the Ni-17Cr-10Al alloy. The data tracks the structural evolution of the material during the heating process and subsequent isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C in an air environment, providing insight into the initial oxidation behavior and phase formation of the alloy.

caption: Frequency-impedance relationship plotted for the electrochemical coatings under in-vitro conditions.
summary: This panel displays the frequency-impedance relationship of the electrochemical coatings tested under in-vitro conditions. As part of the Bode plots, this data provides critical insights into the electrochemical behavior of the material, complementing the Nyquist curves and supporting the overall findings regarding the coating's performance and stability.

caption: Digital 3D models of two distinct brain structures generated from MRI data, with dimensions of x=41.59, y=68.00, z=38.38 for the first brain and x=34.67, y=87.92, z=44.47 for the second brain.
summary: This figure presents digital 3D models of two brains reconstructed from MRI data. The models provide precise spatial dimensions for each specimen, with the first brain measuring x=41.59, y=68.00, z=38.38 and the second brain measuring x=34.67, y=87.92, z=44.47, illustrating the morphological variability captured through the imaging process.

caption: Bode impedance modulus plot for FeCoCrNiMo HEA and HEA/CNTs composite coatings, highlighting the higher impedance modulus of the composite.
summary: This Bode impedance plot illustrates the impedance modulus of the FeCoCrNiMo HEA and HEA/CNTs composite coatings. The HEA/CNTs composite coating exhibits a higher impedance modulus compared to the pure HEA coating, which indicates that the composite provides a stronger barrier effect against the diffusion of electrolyte ions during testing.

caption: Total density of states (TDOS) curves comparing the electronic structure of pure Ti2AlV (110) surfaces against those with adsorbed species.
summary: This figure presents the total density of states (TDOS) curves for Ti2AlV (110) surfaces. It specifically contrasts the electronic characteristics of the pure surface with those of the adsorbed surface, providing a comprehensive view of how adsorption influences the electronic density distribution within the Ti2AlV (110) material system.

caption: Longitudinal profiles derived from X-ray computed tomography (XCT) scans, showing local singularities near the geometrical arches of series AW indicated by red arrows.
summary: Longitudinal profiles obtained from XCT scans provide an overview of the surface topology across all series. In the AW series, specific local singularities are identified near the geometrical arches, as highlighted by red arrows. These profiles allow for a detailed comparison of surface features at a consistent scale.

caption: Pole figure map of the LHAM-HT specimen, highlighting the absence of clear crystallographic anisotropy.
summary: The pole figure map of the LHAM-HT specimen highlights the absence of clear crystallographic anisotropy. Following heat treatment, the material exhibits equiaxed grains with random orientations, indicating that the thermal processing successfully mitigated the directional texture typically observed in the as-manufactured LHAM specimens.

caption: Conventional laminated CFRP specimen demonstrating chip and burr formation characteristics.
summary: Panel C presents the chip and burr formation observed in a conventional laminated CFRP specimen. This serves as a baseline for comparing the material removal behavior and debris characteristics against the AM-CFRP variants, highlighting the differences in structural response and chip morphology during the standard machining process.

caption: UMAP dimensionality reduction plot displaying quartz samples from an I-type system, color-coded by Ti content and delineated by cluster boundaries corresponding to different deposit types.
summary: This UMAP plot visualizes quartz samples from an I-type system, incorporating Ti content data and distinct cluster boundaries. It serves as a machine learning-based approach to classify quartz samples from various geological environments, including IRG, porphyry, and epithermal deposits, providing a clear spatial separation of different deposit types.

caption: EDS elemental mapping of copper (Cu) corresponding to the surface area shown in panel (d), demonstrating the distribution of copper across the laser-activated substrate.
summary: EDS elemental mapping for copper provides a clear visualization of the distribution of Cu species across the laser-activated substrate surface. This map directly corresponds to the SEM image in panel (d), confirming the presence and spatial uniformity of copper within the photopolymer matrix after the laser activation process.

caption: Cross-sectional TEM micrograph of the oxide film formed on A59 alloy following electrochemical polarization at 1100 mV vs Ag/AgCl.
summary: This TEM image illustrates the cross-sectional structure of the oxide film on A59 alloy after electrochemical polarization at 1100 mV vs Ag/AgCl. The micrograph serves as a representative example of the specimen analysis, confirming the accuracy of GD-OES thickness measurements through direct observation of the oxide layer morphology.

caption: Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves for Pt 2.4 Ni/G catalysts at varying rotation rates, with inset Koutecky-Levich (K-L) plots at different voltages.
summary: Detailed reaction mechanism studies were conducted using LSV curves for the Pt 2.4 Ni/G catalyst. The polarization curves at various rotation rates and the corresponding K-L plots provide insight into the ORR kinetics and electron transfer processes occurring on the catalyst surface during the electrochemical reaction.

caption: Galvanostatic Intermittent Titration Technique (GITT) voltage profiles for the Ni-Cu@C/HC cell.
summary: The GITT test curves for the Ni-Cu@C/HC cell are presented to evaluate the electrochemical performance. These curves provide insights into the diffusion kinetics and potential variations during the intermittent titration process, characterizing the electrochemical behavior of the Ni-Cu@C/HC composite material within the cell system.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve illustrating the performance of the discriminator model in identifying anomalous lattice structures.
summary: This receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve evaluates the classification performance of the discriminator model regarding anomalous lattice structures. The plot demonstrates high predictive accuracy, yielding an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.983, which effectively quantifies the model's capability to distinguish between normal and anomalous structural features in the dataset.

caption: Time-resolved stages of the atomization process, highlighting the initial static droplet with pre-existing cavities and subsequent cavitation-driven micro-cloud formation.
summary: Zooming in on the static droplet reveals pre-existing air cavities at t = 0 ms. Upon activation of the plate transducer, these cavities pulsate and cluster into micro-clouds. This interface distortion indicates the incipient growth of capillary waves, demonstrating that ultrasonic atomization is driven by the interplay of cavitation and capillary waves.

caption: Dilatometric analysis of cellulose aerogel showing the relationship between temperature and volume change.
summary: This dilatometric analysis illustrates the thermal response of cellulose aerogel. The plot clearly demonstrates the relationship between temperature and volume change, providing essential data on the material's dimensional stability under thermal influence. These results characterize the aerogel's physical behavior when subjected to varying temperature conditions during the testing process.

caption: Two-dimensional SAXS pattern of the Al-10 wt%Zn/Al-2.5 wt%Mg three-layer composite aged for 60 minutes.
summary: Represented here is the two-dimensional SAXS pattern for the Al-10 wt%Zn/Al-2.5 wt%Mg three-layer composite after 60 minutes of aging. This diffraction data illustrates the evolution of the scattering profile in the composite material as the aging duration increases from 20 to 60 minutes, reflecting changes in the internal microstructure.

caption: Parity plot comparing the heat transfer rates on the air side (q_air) and the sCO2 side (q_co2), calculated using energy balance equations (1) and (2).
summary: This parity plot illustrates the correlation between heat transfer rates on the air and sCO2 sides, derived from energy balance equations. The data highlights discrepancies between theoretical and experimental effectiveness, which are attributed to energy balance differences on the hot and cold sides and minor non-counter flow sections within the pin array.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for the spot build specimen, displaying intensity variations across axial/build and transverse directions.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for the spot build specimen are shown, covering both axial/build and transverse directions. These patterns reveal the dominant presence of {200} orientation, resembling a single crystal. Each run number corresponds to a specific load applied during the in-situ measurement, providing insight into the material's structural response.

caption: Physical appearance of the vacuum chamber assembly utilized for the experimental testing environment.
summary: This photograph displays the physical vacuum chamber setup employed during the experimental process. The image provides a visual reference for the equipment configuration, confirming the physical environment in which the electro-thermomechanical tests were conducted to ensure controlled conditions for the specimen during the heating and loading phases.

caption: Distribution histogram of the circular diameter for water-atomized (WA) powder particles.
summary: Water-atomized (WA) powder particle circular diameter distribution is shown in this histogram. Comparative analysis reveals that the WA powder possesses a finer particle size compared to the gas-atomized counterpart. This quantitative data highlights the influence of the water atomization process on the resulting powder size distribution.

caption: Integrated photoluminescence intensity as a function of excitation power density for sample P033 at 10 K, showing a linear dependence characteristic of pure radiative recombination.
summary: Integrated photoluminescence intensity for sample P033 is plotted against excitation power density at 10 K. The data, fitted with a solid line, demonstrates a linear relationship with an exponent k approximately equal to 1, which indicates that the sample exhibits pure radiative recombination behavior under the tested excitation conditions.

caption: Main effects plot illustrating the influence of layer height, infill percentage, and print speed on the compression strength of additively manufactured polylactic acid.
summary: This main effects plot demonstrates how layer height, infill percentage, and print speed impact the compression strength of polylactic acid parts. Among these parameters, infill percentage exhibits a clear linear relationship with compression strength and exerts the most significant influence on the mechanical performance of the additively manufactured specimens.

caption: Tabulated printing parameters for the PB composite filament using a Creality Ender 3 V3 SE printer, including settings for tensile specimen fabrication with brim adhesion and eight outer layers.
summary: This table outlines the specific printing parameters utilized for the PB composite filament on a Creality Ender 3 V3 SE printer. It highlights critical settings for tensile specimen fabrication, including the implementation of a brim option and eight outer layers to ensure optimal adhesion with the printer bed.

caption: High-magnification detail of the PSD-B creep rate-time curve, specifically isolating the steady-state creep regime at 300 MPa.
summary: This magnified view provides a clear observation of the steady-state creep stage for the PSD-B sample at 300 MPa. By isolating this segment, the researchers accurately measured the duration and boundaries of the steady-state stage, which is critical for understanding the material's long-term deformation behavior under high-temperature stress conditions.

caption: Visualization of C–O chemical bonds formed during the reaction between CO2 and the Ti surface.
summary: This panel illustrates the formation of C–O chemical bonds resulting from the reaction between CO2 and the Ti surface. These bonds are part of the complex reaction products, which primarily include Ti-Cx-Oy, TiC, and free C, as identified during the simulation of the surface carburization process.

caption: Atomic force microscopy topography of an OPS polished and heat-treated CuOF sheet, exhibiting a surface roughness of 4.2 ± 0.7 nm.
summary: Atomic force microscopy topography of an OPS polished and heat-treated CuOF sheet, exhibiting a surface roughness of 4.2 ± 0.7 nm. This measurement serves as a baseline for reflectivity studies, as the sample maintains a low surface roughness of Rq ≤ 4 nm, helping to decouple surface effects from bulk powder properties.

caption: Overview of the steel lifecycle illustrating the material manufacturing flows from raw material extraction to end-of-life processing.
summary: This diagram provides a comprehensive overview of the steel lifecycle, mapping the material manufacturing flows. It tracks the progression from initial raw material extraction through various production stages to the final end-of-life processing, effectively visualizing the industrial journey and environmental considerations associated with steel production and its circular economy.

caption: Comparison of FT-IR spectra for pristine rGO and permalloy/rGO composite materials.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of the FT-IR spectra for pristine rGO and permalloy/rGO. The spectra illustrate the chemical changes occurring upon the deposition of permalloy onto the rGO substrate. These results confirm the successful synthesis of the composite material, which contains Ni, Fe, and Mo elements.

caption: Wear morphology and 3D surface topography of sample S5 (HV = 166.24) on the X–Y plane, demonstrating a wear track largely covered by an oxide layer with localized abrasive damage.
summary: Sample S5, with a hardness of 166.24 HV, exhibits a wear track that is predominantly covered by an oxide layer as observed via laser confocal microscopy. Unlike S6, abrasive features such as furrows and scratches are restricted to locally exposed areas, suggesting a different wear mechanism influenced by surface oxidation.

caption: EPMA concentration profiles of Ni, Cr, Al, and O across the oxide scale of 17Ni-17Cr-10Al alloy after 100 h of oxidation at 1000 °C.
summary: Electron probe micro-analysis (EPMA) concentration profiles reveal the elemental distribution within the thick oxide scale formed on 17Ni-17Cr-10Al after 100 hours of oxidation at 1000 °C. The analysis confirms a layered structure consisting of NiO, Cr2O3, NiCrAl2O4, and Al2O3, demonstrating the complex oxidation behavior of this alloy system.

caption: Summary table defining the specific process parameter sets categorized as low-NEIR and high-NEIR based on the analysis of the process maps in panels (a) and (b).
summary: This summary table categorizes the process parameters into low-NEIR and high-NEIR sets. These definitions are derived from the process maps in panels (a) and (b), providing the necessary framework to apply distinct thermal histories to different sections of the fabricated pins during the PBF-LB/M process.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the corrosion behavior of Ar P and Ar O samples in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the corrosion response of Ar P and Ar O samples within a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The results indicate that both samples exhibit similar polarization behavior when exposed to chloride-containing environments, suggesting comparable corrosion resistance characteristics for the tested materials under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Surface electronic spectrum of the SnSbBiTe4 (111) cleavage surface, where red and blue dots indicate positive and negative in-plane spin projections, and shaded regions represent projected bulk states.
summary: The surface spectrum of the SnSbBiTe4 (111) cleavage surface displays spin-polarized states, with red and blue dots denoting spin projections. On this projection, the conduction band minimum appears at the point of the 2D Brillouin zone, while the valence band maximum occurs at the - direction.

caption: High-magnification 3D reconstruction of the 88.89 J/mm³ sample, focusing on the morphology of keyhole pores.
summary: This high-magnification image provides a detailed view of the round keyhole pores observed in the 88.89 J/mm³ sample. The reconstruction confirms the presence of these specific void types, which are characteristic of high-energy processing conditions that lead to keyhole-mode melting and subsequent gas entrapment within the material.

caption: Comparative mechanical properties including tensile strength, strain at break, and modulus for TPS/PBAT blends compatibilized with maleic anhydride (MA), citric acid (CA), and PBAT-g-MA.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical performance of TPS/PBAT blends, specifically comparing tensile strength, elongation at break, and modulus values. The results demonstrate that these properties vary significantly depending on the specific compatibilizer used, namely maleic anhydride, citric acid, or PBAT-g-MA, highlighting the influence of chemical modification on blend mechanics.

caption: Transmittance spectra of A-CNC/CTFA composite resins plotted over a wavelength range, illustrating the optical response as a function of acrylation reaction time.
summary: The transmittance spectrum of the A-CNC/CTFA composite resin demonstrates a notable improvement in transparency within the 380–420 nm range as the acrylation reaction time increases. This plot illustrates the optical response of the composite resin, highlighting how varying the reaction duration directly influences the light transmission characteristics of the material.

caption: Creep strain rate as a function of time for H230 specimens tested at 800 °C, specifically for the 3.3 mm reduced gage length configuration.
summary: Creep strain rate versus time is plotted for H230 specimens at 800 °C with a 3.3 mm reduced gage length. This graph complements the strain-time data in panel c, illustrating the rate of deformation over time for the smaller gage length specimens under the specified thermal and mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the temperature-dependent activation energy, fitted with a second-order polynomial to capture the non-linear trend observed across the 550 °C to 700 °C range.
summary: This Arrhenius plot demonstrates that the activation energy is not constant, as evidenced by the curved data trend rather than a linear fit. A second-order polynomial regression reveals a significant decrease in apparent activation energy from 286 kJ/mol at 550 °C to 113 kJ/mol at 700 °C, indicating temperature-dependent kinetics.

caption: Performance trajectory of the ANN-GA optimization framework showing the fitness value across generations.
summary: The performance trajectory of the ANN-GA framework is illustrated, highlighting the optimization process aimed at identifying printing parameters for maximal GF. The optimization process demonstrates convergence toward the most favorable configuration by the 40th generation, while simultaneously exhibiting notable diversity within the search space throughout the iterative evolution process.

caption: IRRAS absorbance spectra of pCBMAA homopolymer synthesized over 30 minutes, comparing samples H and J.
summary: Presented here are the IRRAS absorbance spectra for pCBMAA homopolymer samples H and J, which were synthesized over a 30-minute period. The spectra exhibit identical features, verifying that the microfluidic synthesis process successfully maintains the intended chemical composition compared to standard reactor methods, despite variations in the overall mass.

caption: Molybdenum elemental distribution map across the Inconel 625/weld metal interface, showing localized concentration patterns.
summary: Molybdenum distribution across the Inconel 625/weld metal interface is presented. The segregation of alloying elements like molybdenum, along with carbide formation, is linked to the reduced corrosion resistance of the weld metal. This map provides critical evidence of the chemical heterogeneity present at the weld interface.

caption: Vickers hardness distribution measured across the yz-plane of L-PBFed HX specimens.
summary: Vickers hardness measurements in the yz-plane of L-PBFed HX specimens reveal distinct variations across different samples. The hardness values initially increase from the HX1 to the HX2 specimen, followed by a subsequent decline in the HX3 specimen as the volumetric energy density (VED) decreases during the L-PBF fabrication process.

caption: Printing orientation schematic showing the specimen positioned flat on the build platform, with the building direction aligned along the z-axis and outer contour walls surrounding the core.
summary: The schematic depicts the flat printing orientation adopted for the FDM process using a Prusa i3 MK3S printer. By aligning the building direction with the z-axis and incorporating outer contour walls around the core, the design improves the shape retention of the printed parts during the fabrication process.

caption: Ternary phase diagram of the Ni0.5Al0.5-Cr system illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions for the alloy components.
summary: The phase diagram of the Ni0.5Al0.5-Cr system is presented, serving as the foundational reference for understanding the thermodynamic states of the alloy. It identifies critical temperature points, such as A and B, which dictate the transition from a liquidus state to the formation of solid NiAl and subsequent eutectic structures.

caption: Summary table of calculated specimen thicknesses (nm) for the UM, cryo-UM, and FIB preparation methods, derived using Iakoubovskii's equation.
summary: This table presents the calculated thickness values in nanometers for the PLA and PCL specimens shown in panels a, b, and c. The thicknesses were determined using EELS measurements and calculated according to Iakoubovskii's equation, providing a quantitative comparison of the electron transparency achieved by the different specimen preparation techniques.

caption: Bulk texture pole figure for the solution treated-aged WAAM-IN718 specimen, demonstrating a maximum texture intensity of 13 MRD.
summary: The solution treated-aged WAAM-IN718 specimen exhibits a bulk texture intensity of 13 MRD, as determined by neutron diffraction analysis. This value reflects the final state of the material after the full heat treatment cycle, showing a reduction in maximum texture intensity compared to the solution treated condition alone.

caption: Full-range FTIR spectra comparing individual components, binary blends, and ternary blends for both printed and EI samples.
summary: This panel displays the full-range FTIR spectra for individual components, binary, and ternary blends. Characteristic PET peaks at 1712, 1240, 1092, and 719 cm-1 are identified, alongside increased intensity in CH/CH2/CH3 stretching bands at 2960, 2918, 2849, and 698 cm-1, indicating successful compatibilization across the different sample types.

caption: Predictive surrogate surface for the percentage elongation of LPBF AlSi10Mg, showing the variation relative to laser power and scan speed.
summary: This panel shows the predictive surrogate surface for the percentage elongation of LPBF AlSi10Mg. By plotting elongation against laser power and scan speed, the model visualizes how process parameters influence ductility. This map is derived from a ten-variable GPR model, projected onto two dimensions for clear visualization of trends.

caption: Capacitance performance as a function of scan rate, showing a characteristic decrease in capacitance for both capacitors as the scan rate increases.
summary: This plot illustrates the rate capability of the capacitors, where capacitance is measured against varying scan rates. Both devices exhibit a decline in capacitance at higher scan rates, primarily due to the limited time available for K+ ions to diffuse into the KGP matrix for effective surface absorption and desorption.

caption: Structural grain characteristics of WAAMed NiTi alloy after deformation at 800 °C.
summary: This panel presents the structural grain characteristics of WAAMed NiTi alloy after hot compression at 800 °C. By visualizing the deformed and recrystallized grain populations, it complements the comparative analysis of the alloy's microstructural response to varying thermal conditions during the hot compression process.

caption: Experimental determination of the Larson-Miller constant C, derived from the relationship between failure time (tf) and the inverse of absolute temperature (1/T) at a constant stress level of 30 MPa.
summary: The panel displays the experimental determination of the Larson-Miller constant C. By plotting failure time as a function of temperature at a constant stress of 30 MPa, the researchers independently calculated the value of C, providing a validation method for the constant derived from the best-fit analysis.

caption: Relaxed NiCr(1) surface model shown in the absence of any adsorbates.
summary: This panel displays the relaxed NiCr(1) surface structure calculated via DFT in a clean state, serving as the baseline reference for evaluating charge transfer and surface distortion effects induced by subsequent anion adsorption in the following panels of the figure.

caption: Live/dead cell assay images of L929 fibroblasts on P1, F1, DC1, and D1 surfaces, quantifying viability based on 30 cell counts per image with error bars representing standard deviation.
summary: Live/dead cell staining provides a visual assessment of fibroblast viability on the different surface topographies. Quantitative analysis of the images confirms that all surfaces support cell survival with viability rates above 80%. The statistical significance (p < 0.01) highlights the consistent biocompatibility across the diverse surface textures tested.

caption: Tabulated elemental weight percentages derived from EDX analysis for the initial, one-time recycled, and two-time recycled samples.
summary: This table summarizes the quantitative elemental weight percentages detected across the different sample types. By organizing the EDX data into a structured format, it facilitates a direct comparison of the chemical composition changes occurring throughout the recycling stages, providing clear evidence of the material's elemental stability or variation over time.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution of the Ti6Al4V–TiC composite microstructure.
summary: This inverse pole figure map provides a detailed visualization of the crystallographic orientations within the Ti6Al4V–TiC composite sample. Characterized via EBSD, the map reveals the spatial arrangement and grain orientation distribution, serving as a primary microstructural analysis tool to understand the texture and grain morphology of the composite material.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the AM-processed MPES microstructure, highlighting the presence of spherical zirconium oxide dispersoids within the grain structure.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image reveals the complex microstructure of the AM-processed MPES, specifically identifying spherical zirconium oxide dispersoids. These features are likely attributed to the high initial oxygen concentration of approximately 8.5 at.% present in the cryo-ball-milled powder used during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Schematic illustration showing the specific location selected for temperature monitoring during the TW-DED-arc additive manufacturing process.
summary: This schematic diagram identifies the precise spatial coordinate used to record thermal data during the TW-DED-arc additive manufacturing process. By defining this specific record point, the researchers established a consistent reference for tracking thermal history throughout the multi-layer deposition sequence, ensuring accurate comparison between different processing conditions.

caption: Coupon H3.5M20 showing premature fracture behavior compared to other specimens.
summary: Coupon H3.5M20 is highlighted to demonstrate an exception to the general ductile failure observed in other WAAM specimens. Unlike the other coupons that exhibit evident necking, this specimen underwent premature fracture, which is attributed to a lack of fusion within the material structure during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for ER120S-G solid wire under Group D conditions.
summary: Representing the Group D experimental condition, this CCT diagram maps the phase transformation behavior of ER120S-G deposited metal. As part of a broader study on WAAM components, this diagram serves to quantify the relationship between cooling rates, phase fractions, and the development of residual stress during the manufacturing process.

caption: Performance evaluation of the classification task, displaying the confusion matrix that quantifies the accuracy and misclassification rates across different letter categories.
summary: The confusion matrix provides a quantitative evaluation of the classification task performance. By mapping predicted versus actual letter categories, it reveals the model's accuracy and identifies specific misclassification patterns, offering critical insights into the effectiveness of the ResNet-18 and Bidirectional LSTM architecture in recognizing handwritten English letters.

caption: Stress-life (S-N) curves comparing various AlSi10Mg specimen conditions against reference wrought Al 6061 T6+M+P and die-cast AlSi10Mg+P materials.
summary: This stress-life plot evaluates the fatigue performance of AlSi10Mg specimens under diverse surface conditions. By benchmarking these results against wrought Al 6061 T6+M+P and die-cast AlSi10Mg+P reference materials, the analysis demonstrates that surface-post treatments significantly enhance fatigue resistance, achieving performance levels comparable to the established reference alloys.

caption: Ni K-edge XANES spectra of Ni Alloy 59 measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7.
summary: Panel d displays the Ni K-edge XANES spectra for Ni Alloy 59, measured in total reflection geometry at pH 7. The data contributes to the comparative analysis of the alloy's surface absorption characteristics, complementing the transmission mode reference spectra and the measurements taken at different pH levels.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the gamma prime precipitate during the isothermal treatment process.
summary: This APT reconstruction captures the gamma prime precipitate during the isothermal treatment. By visualizing the precipitate in three dimensions, the analysis provides insight into the morphological changes and solute partitioning occurring within the alloy as it undergoes thermal processing, contributing to the understanding of the observed coarsening behavior.

caption: Evolution of stress ranges for as-built (AB) LPBF HX samples during fatigue loading across various strain amplitudes.
summary: This plot illustrates the stress range evolution for as-built LPBF HX specimens under cyclic fatigue loading at different strain amplitudes. The data reveals that these specimens exhibit a cyclic softening response after the initial few cycles, indicating a progressive reduction in stress required to maintain the applied strain amplitude throughout the test.

caption: Stress–displacement curves representing the average shear stress of the adhesive versus displacement for single-lap joints (SLJs) fabricated with various CFRP adherends, as determined through tensile testing.
summary: This plot illustrates the mechanical response of single-lap joints (SLJs) featuring different CFRP adherends. By plotting average adhesive shear stress against displacement, the data characterizes the load-bearing behavior of the joints. These curves, derived from tensile tests, provide a comparative analysis of the mechanical performance across the various SLJ configurations.

caption: Out-of-plane magnetic hysteresis loops of Py films prepared at different Ar pressures, showing a decrease in the saturation field from 1300 mT to 600 mT as the sputter pressure increases, contrasting with the in-plane behavior.
summary: Panel (b) presents out-of-plane magnetic hysteresis loops for Py films across varying Ar pressures. In contrast to the in-plane results, the out-of-plane saturation field decreases from 1300 mT to 600 mT as the sputter pressure increases, illustrating the distinct magnetic response of the films in the out-of-plane orientation.

caption: High-resolution O1s spectrum of the 3DP-C-NF membrane surface.
summary: Panel (e) presents the high-resolution O1s spectrum for the 3DP-C-NF membrane. Deconvolution of this characteristic peak allows for the extraction of detailed chemical information about oxygen-containing functional groups present on the membrane surface, which is essential for characterizing the surface properties of the synthesized nanofibrous material.

caption: Hole mobility dependence on the graded layer thickness, derived from room temperature Hall effect measurements for the studied contact structures.
summary: Hole mobility is shown as a function of the graded layer thickness in this panel. The plot highlights the relationship between the structural gradient and carrier mobility, demonstrating how varying the thickness of the graded layer influences the transport properties of the contact structures at room temperature.

caption: O 1s XPS spectrum of NiTi powder heated at 750 °C, exhibiting characteristic lattice oxygen and surface contaminant peaks.
summary: Heating NiTi powder to 750 °C results in an O 1s XPS spectrum characterized by a dominant lattice oxygen peak at 528.6 eV. The spectrum also contains minor features in the 531–533 eV range, which are associated with the presence of surface hydroxyls and carbonates on the powder particles.

caption: Hysteresis loops for NiFe/IrMn(10 nm)/NiFe samples with LNiPy (red) and HNiPy (black) configurations, measured along the unidirectional anisotropy axis.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic hysteresis loops for NiFe/IrMn/NiFe trilayers with different grain sizes, LNiPy and HNiPy, measured along the unidirectional anisotropy axis. The red curve represents the LNiPy sample, while the black curve corresponds to the HNiPy sample, illustrating distinct magnetization reversal behaviors for the ferromagnetic layers.

caption: FEG-SEM micrographs of wrought NiTi alloy microstructure at 500X and 2500X magnifications, revealing the presence of inclusions within the grains.
summary: Wrought NiTi alloy microstructure is characterized via FEG-SEM at 500X and 2500X magnifications. These images reveal the presence of inclusions distributed within the material grains. This structural analysis provides insight into the baseline microstructural features of the wrought sample prior to any heat treatment or additive manufacturing processing.

caption: Nyquist plot illustrating the EIS spectra of LPBF AlSi10Mg MP specimens.
summary: The EIS spectra for LPBF AlSi10Mg specimens in the MP condition are displayed in this Nyquist plot. This visualization provides critical electrochemical data, allowing for the assessment of impedance characteristics in the MP state, which serves as a reference point for comparison with the heat-treated specimens shown in panel b.

caption: 3D APT reconstruction cube (30 nm side) featuring 16% Cr and 9% Al isoconcentration surfaces, illustrating the morphology of phase separation.
summary: A 30 nm cubic volume of the APT reconstruction displays 16% Cr and 9% Al isoconcentration surfaces. These surfaces illustrate the phase separation characteristic of spinodal decomposition, supporting the conclusion that the formation of γ' precipitates in this material occurs through this mechanism rather than via classic particle precipitation.

caption: Electrical conductivity curves of 3D-printed PLA-CB composites measured at printing temperatures between 230 °C and 280 °C as a function of applied voltage.
summary: This plot illustrates the electrical conductivity of 3D-printed PLA-CB samples across various printing temperatures. Increasing the printing temperature from 230 °C to 260 °C generally enhances electrical performance, whereas further temperature increases beyond 270 °C result in a degradation of the material's conductive properties under varying applied voltage conditions.

caption: Interaction effects of process parameters on Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) showing the relative influence of scan speed and laser power.
summary: This panel illustrates the interaction of various factors influencing the Ultimate Tensile Strength of the material. It highlights that both scan speed and laser power exert a significant effect on the UTS, demonstrating their critical roles in the optimization of the mechanical properties during the manufacturing process.

caption: Surface morphology of Ti foil under a 20A current, demonstrating further reduction in non-contact white areas and improved surface conformity.
summary: Surface morphology of Ti foil under a 20A current, demonstrating further reduction in non-contact white areas and improved surface conformity. The significant decrease in the white area proportion compared to lower currents confirms that increased joule heat effectively enhances the plasticity of the Ti foil during the sonotrode contact process.

caption: Electrical conductivity values of the nanocomposites plotted against increasing graphene nanoplatelet content.
summary: Electrical conductivity measurements demonstrate a clear trend where the conductivity value increases as the graphene nanoplatelet content increases within the nanocomposites. This plot highlights the functional enhancement achieved by incorporating graphene into the DLP polyurea matrix, confirming the successful development of electrically conductive 3D-printed materials.

caption: Cross-sectional X-ray computed tomography view of specimen P3 showing deep, plate-like crack morphology and melt pool characteristics under 111 J/mm³ processing conditions.
summary: This cross-sectional X-ray computed tomography view of specimen P3 illustrates the internal crack distribution and melt pool geometry. The visualization reveals that cracks become deep and exhibit a plate-like morphology, which is observed clearly for this parameter set, despite the low linear energy density and E*.

caption: Isometric camera view of the optimized 3D cantilever beam highlighting internal void channels.
summary: Captured from an isometric perspective, this 3D reconstruction reveals the optimized cantilever beam structure. The image clearly displays the inner void channels that are enveloped by the solid material phases and the design boundary, providing a detailed view of the internal architecture achieved through the structural optimization process.

caption: Surface topography of the Al2O3 sample following the third series of flat lapping using tool no. 1.
summary: Surface topography of the Al2O3 sample is shown after the third series of flat lapping tests performed with tool no. 1. This visualization, alongside selected roughness parameters, illustrates the specific surface finish achieved by this tool, allowing for a direct comparison with the initial state and other machining conditions.

caption: Flexural strength of BJ-printed ZTA ceramics measured after a 2 h sintering holding time across varying temperatures.
summary: Flexural strength of BJ-printed ZTA ceramics is presented for a 2 h sintering holding time. The data demonstrates that flexural strength increases consistently as sintering temperatures are elevated. This trend highlights the significant influence of thermal processing parameters on the mechanical performance of the printed ceramic material.

caption: UV–vis absorbance curves tracking the catalytic conversion of 4-NP by 1 wt% Co-HPMC-C, demonstrating complete conversion within 150 minutes.
summary: The UV–vis spectra show the catalytic reduction of 4-NP using 1 wt% Co-HPMC-C. A comparison with the AP-based catalyst in panel (a) indicates that the HPMC organic binder enhances the catalytic conversion rate, achieving 100% conversion of the 4-NP substrate after a reaction duration of 150 minutes.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) of RNA-seq data from human corneal epithelial cells (HCECs) across four experimental conditions: control (CTR), D609 treatment, hyperosmolar stress (Hy), and combined Hy + D609 treatment.
summary: This PCA plot visualizes the transcriptional variance across four HCEC treatment groups. The analysis demonstrates that cotreatment with D609 effectively suppresses the transcriptional changes induced by hyperosmolar stress, indicating a distinct clustering pattern that highlights the regulatory impact of D609 on the cellular response to osmotic pressure.

caption: Nyquist plots for Al 79 Ni 11 Fe 5 Y 5 alloy samples in ingot, plate, and amorphous melt-spun ribbon forms, measured in 3.5% aqueous NaCl solution at 25°C.
summary: Nyquist plots illustrate the electrochemical impedance characteristics of Al 79 Ni 11 Fe 5 Y 5 alloys in ingot, plate, and ribbon forms. Testing in 3.5% NaCl at 25°C reveals that plate and ribbon samples exhibit a characteristic transition to a 45° inclined straight line in the low-frequency range.

caption: Photographic documentation of the additively-manufactured TPMS-based beam specimens.
summary: Photographic documentation of the additively-manufactured TPMS-based beam specimens is provided to showcase the physical realization of the CAD designs. These images confirm the successful fabrication of the complex architected structures, bridging the gap between theoretical design and experimental testing in the study of beam mechanical performance.

caption: Cross-sectional schematic of the ultrasonic wire feed nozzle integrated into a directed energy deposition (DED) laser tool, highlighting the piezo-actuated mechanism.
summary: This schematic illustrates the ultrasonic wire feed nozzle design mounted on a DED laser tool. The configuration incorporates a piezo-actuator designed to amplify minute strains at a 5:1 ratio, specifically targeting the melt pool region to enhance the precision and control of the wire feeding process during additive manufacturing.

caption: Structural model of the 7-RS-SiOC precursor material.
summary: The structural model of the 7-RS-SiOC precursor is shown to represent the chemical composition prior to ceramic conversion. This model is essential for understanding the material behavior during the additive manufacturing process, where the S-shape manufacturing direction is applied to ensure the integrity of the final R-shaped structures.

caption: Tafel plots illustrating the electrochemical response of Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples within a 0.5 M KOH alkaline solution.
summary: Electrochemical behavior of Ni-Cr, Ni, and Cr samples is shown through Tafel plots measured in a 0.5 M KOH electrolyte. The data provides insight into the corrosion resistance and polarization characteristics of these electrodeposited materials when exposed to an alkaline environment, facilitating comparison between the alloy and pure components.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot representing the relationship between ln t0.5 and the inverse absolute temperature (1/T) for the GH5188 superalloy.
summary: Panel d shows the Arrhenius relationship between the recrystallization time and the inverse temperature (1/T). The slope of this linear plot is utilized to calculate the activation energy QMDRX for the MDRX process, providing a quantitative understanding of the temperature sensitivity of recrystallization in the GH5188 superalloy.

caption: Vicat softening temperature (VST) values for B-PLA composites compared against the neat PLA reference value.
summary: This panel displays the Vicat softening temperature (VST) for various B-PLA composites alongside the neat PLA value. The data, which includes a reference value from the material brochure, illustrates the thermal softening characteristics of the composites, providing a comparative assessment of their thermal stability relative to pure PLA.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for as-built samples tested at room temperature.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the room-temperature tensile behavior of as-built samples. These curves provide a visual representation of the mechanical response under tensile loading, with corresponding property data detailed in Table 1. The data serves as the primary characterization of the material's tensile performance in its as-built state.

caption: Von Mises stress field and crack phase field evolution in a random configuration composite at a displacement of 0.00175 mm.
summary: This panel displays the Von Mises stress field and crack phase field for a random configuration composite during deformation. At a displacement of 0.00175 mm, the simulation reveals a pronounced checkerboard-like stress concentration pattern, which directly facilitates crack initiation within the material structure as the deformation progresses.

caption: STEM micrograph of PH13–8Mo steel in the H1000 condition, revealing the morphology and spatial distribution of nano-scale precipitates within the metallic matrix.
summary: This STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of PH13–8Mo steel subjected to H1000 heat treatment. The image highlights the presence of nano-scale precipitates, which appear to be evenly distributed throughout the matrix, providing critical insight into the material's internal structural features following the specified thermal processing condition.

caption: Immunofluorescence analysis of IL-6 expression in infected bone defects at 1 and 4 weeks post-surgery.
summary: Immunofluorescence imaging reveals the spatial distribution and expression levels of IL-6 within infected bone defects. Observations at 1 and 4 weeks post-surgery indicate that the PGCL@5%Ti3C2 treatment group exhibits lower IL-6 expression levels compared to the control PGCL group, suggesting a reduction in inflammatory response over time.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation map of the central region at stage VII.
summary: The IPF orientation map of the central region at stage VII illustrates the crystallographic grain orientations. This map serves as a basis for identifying specific grains, such as G5, G6, and G7, and facilitates the analysis of how grain-specific orientations influence the development of secondary slip bands.

caption: Digital photograph capturing the practical application of the microtomy device during the slicing of mouse tumor tissue.
summary: This digital image demonstrates the microtomy device in action, slicing mouse tumor tissue. The process involves the microneedle scaffold being lifted by the holder to contact the cover, ensuring precise tissue sectioning as the device moves through the grooves to produce uniform tissue pieces.

caption: Representation of the CAS unit cell showing the fundamental atomic arrangement.
summary: The unit cell of the CAS is illustrated to define the basic structural building block. Detailed parameters for the construction of this unit cell are provided in the paper, serving as the foundational geometry required for the subsequent comprehensive design and modeling of the material system.

caption: Bode modulus plots illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance magnitude for CoCrFeNiMo and CoCrFeNiSi ingots in 5% NaCl solution.
summary: Bode modulus plots are utilized to further characterize the electrochemical impedance of CoCrFeNiMo and CoCrFeNiSi ingots in 5% NaCl solution. The data confirms that the difference in electrochemical performance between the two alloys is pronounced, providing a clear comparison of their impedance magnitudes across the tested frequency range.

caption: Storage modulus curves as a function of temperature for the cTPU/PLLA and MWCNTs-TPU/PLLA scaffolds.
summary: Storage modulus curves derived from DMA testing reveal the viscoelastic stiffness of the scaffolds. The cTPU/PLLA scaffold exhibits a higher storage modulus compared to the 1% MWCNTs-TPU/PLLA scaffold, indicating that the cTPU/PLLA composition provides superior resistance to elastic deformation under dynamic loading conditions.

caption: Microhardness distribution map of the W3 hybrid sample, showing the spatial extent of lower hardness regions (blue) within the deposit where fracture is observed to occur.
summary: The W3 sample displays a 2D microhardness distribution map across the interface. Fracture is observed 2–3 mm above the substrate top surface, aligning with the blue-colored lower microhardness regions. The area of these lower hardness zones increases with substrate thickness, reflecting the mechanical behavior observed across all hybrid samples.

caption: Superimposed EBSD data on a LaserbeamFoam snapshot illustrating the transition from fine to coarse grain microstructures within melt pools where Al3(Sc,Zr) particles have dissolved.
summary: This figure illustrates the solidification process within melt pools, highlighting the direct correlation between particle dissolution and grain morphology. By superimposing EBSD data onto a LaserbeamFoam snapshot, the image demonstrates how the dissolution of Al3(Sc,Zr) leads to a distinct transition from fine-grained to coarse-grained microstructures during the solidification phase.

caption: Al-Ni binary phase diagram illustrating the target compositions for laser alloying marked by a dotted red line.
summary: This binary phase diagram provides the thermodynamic context for the laser alloying process. The dotted red line highlights the specific target compositions investigated in the study, allowing for a direct correlation between the experimental XRD results and the equilibrium phase stability of the Al-Ni system.

caption: Comparison of a 3x3x3 cm DLP 3D printed object using St-Naph-3,5-OMe-PI against smaller objects printed with and without SiO2 nanofiller.
summary: A comparative visual analysis is provided for DLP 3D printed objects using the St-Naph-3,5-OMe-PI initiator. The image contrasts a large 3x3x3 cm object with smaller samples, highlighting the influence of SiO2 nanofiller incorporation on the final print quality and demonstrating the scalability of the cationic vat printing process.

caption: Phase fraction profiles at 1320 °C after 18 s holding time, showing the peak liquid phase concentration of 17.8 vol% between 200 μm and 250 μm, with no detectable γ′ phase.
summary: At a holding time of 18 s during isothermal treatment at 1320 °C, the simulation reveals a maximum liquid phase fraction of 17.8 vol% localized between 200 μm and 250 μm. Notably, the γ′ phase is entirely absent at this stage, representing the initial state of the simulated isothermal resolidification process.

caption: Atomic distribution snapshot at 500 K, showing pronounced M4N-like short-range ordered structures marked by black circles.
summary: At 500 K, the Monte Carlo snapshot displays well-defined M4N-like SRO domains in the Fe70Ni10Cr20-10at.%N alloy. The black circles highlight these ordered regions, confirming that lower temperatures facilitate the formation of these specific structural domains, consistent with the behavior observed in the corresponding SRO parameter analysis.

caption: Overlay of the LEAP 4000 X Si (red) and Invizo 6000 (blue) field evaporation maps, demonstrating the expanded field of view (FoV) provided by the Invizo 6000 system.
summary: This overlay compares the field evaporation maps from the LEAP 4000 X Si (red) and the Invizo 6000 (blue) instruments. By superimposing the two datasets, the visualization clearly illustrates the significantly greater field of view achieved by the Invizo 6000 compared to the LEAP 4000 X Si system.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot for the pH = 7 class, illustrating the distribution of feature importance across RGB channels.
summary: The SHAP beeswarm plot for the pH = 7 class displays a clustering of very small SHAP values across all RGB channels. This concentration of values suggests that the trained neural network model has not learned strong or distinct distinguishing features for this specific class during the classification process.

caption: Micro-hardness profile distribution across all samples, highlighting the characteristic high-low-high hardness variation observed in the as-received material.
summary: This figure displays the micro-hardness profile distribution for all analyzed samples. Specifically, the as-received sample exhibits a distinct high-low-high hardness trend across its profile. This mechanical testing data provides a clear visualization of the hardness variation, characterizing the material's response to indentation across the measured sample regions.

caption: Electronic density of states plot for the O-phase Ti2AlTa intermetallic compound.
summary: The density of states for Ti2AlTa shows that the valence band near the Fermi level is mainly formed by the hybridization of Ti-d and Ta-d states. The s-states of the ternary element are positioned at more than 6 eV below the Fermi level, consistent with the general trend observed.

caption: Binary classification confusion matrix demonstrating an overall classification accuracy of 94.8% for the unsupervised learning model.
summary: This confusion matrix illustrates the performance of an unsupervised learning model applied to binary classification. The model achieves a high classification accuracy of 94.8%, indicating strong predictive capability for distinguishing between the two defined classes within the dataset as presented in the evaluation of the unsupervised learning framework.

caption: Electronic band structure diagram calculated for the I-WP unit cell architecture at a uniform relative density of 22%.
summary: Presented here is the electronic band structure for the I-WP unit cell configuration at a reduced uniform relative density of 22%. The visualization highlights how the energy band dispersion changes when the density of the lattice structure is decreased, reflecting the impact of structural porosity on electronic behavior.

caption: Magnetization versus temperature (M-T) curves and corresponding first-derivative (dM/dT-T) plots for Ni41.0Co5.0Mn43.5Sn10.0Ga0.5 alloy measured under a 0.02 T magnetic field.
summary: The M-T curves and dM/dT-T plots for the Ni41.0Co5.0Mn43.5Sn10.0Ga0.5 alloy under a 0.02 T magnetic field illustrate the thermal magnetic behavior. Cooling and heating cycles are indicated by blue and red arrows, respectively. These derivative plots are essential for determining the martensitic transformation temperatures and the Curie temperature of the alloy.

caption: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) micrographs illustrating the surface topography of pTi, pTi–CZCs, and pTi–CZCs–ZOL samples.
summary: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) micrographs illustrate the surface topography of pTi, pTi–CZCs, and pTi–CZCs–ZOL samples. AFM analysis revealed that untreated pTi exhibited relatively low surface roughness, whereas the pTi-CZCs and pTi-CZCs-ZOL samples displayed significantly higher surface roughness, indicating the successful modification of the titanium surface by the zeolite coating.

caption: High-resolution in situ STM image of the Cu 98.5 Ni 1.5 (1 1 1) electrode at -0.16 V, showing the internal structure of the bisulfate anion adlayer arranged in a moiré pattern.
summary: High-resolution STM imaging at -0.16 V reveals the internal structure of the bisulfate anion adlayer on the Cu 98.5 Ni 1.5 (1 1 1) electrode. The anions are organized into a distinct moiré pattern, allowing for the visualization of the adlayer's internal arrangement on the electrode surface during the in situ measurement.

caption: Microhardness distribution across the vertical plane of Cu-Cr-Zr alloys, highlighting localized variations where hardness increases at regions of small or elongated grains and decreases within larger grains.
summary: Hardness distribution on the vertical plane of Cu-Cr-Zr alloys demonstrates a clear correlation between microstructure and mechanical properties.
