Higher hardness values are observed at the aggregation sites of small or elongated grains, whereas the hardness measured inside larger grains is found to be slightly lower, indicating microstructural influence on local hardness.

caption: Nb3d high-resolution XPS spectra for Ta50, Ti50, and TiTaNb samples after 14 days of immersion in simulated body fluid.
summary: Nb3d high-resolution XPS spectra are shown for Ta50, Ti50, and TiTaNb samples after 14 days of immersion in simulated body fluid. These spectra are integral to the broader analysis of the passive layer composition and the multi-step formation mechanism observed across the different Ti-Ta-Nb alloy series.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of LiCl-KCl molten salt at 450 °C, recorded at a scan rate of 100 mV.s−1 using a tungsten working electrode to determine the electrochemical stability window.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram characterizes the electroactivity range of LiCl-KCl at 450 °C on a tungsten electrode. The plot reveals a broad electrochemical stability domain, defined by cathodic and anodic limits at -2.6 V and 1.1 V, which correspond to the reduction of Li+ to Li0 and the oxidation of Cl- to Cl2(g).

caption: Electron diffraction pattern of the AB sample confirming the formation of hcp-ε phase and the presence of twins.
summary: The electron diffraction pattern clearly indicates the formation of the hcp-ε phase within the AB sample. Additionally, the pattern confirms the presence of twins, providing definitive evidence of these structural features. This analysis complements the bright field TEM images to establish the phase composition and crystalline defects of the material.

caption: TDA-spectrum of CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 200 bar with a heating rate of 0.125 K/s, featuring the four-peak deconvolution and cumulative fit.
summary: This panel shows the TDA-spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA samples charged at 200 bar at a heating rate of 0.125 K/s. The plot demonstrates the four-peak deconvolution scenario and the cumulative fit function, allowing for a detailed comparison of hydrogen desorption kinetics across different heating rates for the 200 bar condition.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram of the powder mixture following 7 hours of ball milling.
summary: This histogram displays the particle size distribution after 7 hours of ball milling. Compared to the 5-hour condition, the increased milling time results in a slight and negligible decrease in particle size, while maintaining the characteristic distribution peaks observed at 20–30 μm and 60–70 μm.

caption: ABF-STEM image and corresponding SAD pattern of the 20Mn8Al alloy, revealing the presence of a tangled dislocation network within the microstructure.
summary: The 20Mn8Al alloy microstructure is characterized by ABF-STEM imaging and SAD analysis. Observations indicate the formation of a tangled dislocation network rather than well-defined dislocation cell structures, which typically arise in additively manufactured materials due to repeated thermal cycling during the in-situ alloying process of Fe–Mn–Al–C LWSs.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the deformed sample surface showing transgranular crack paths and slip trace orientations.
summary: This IPF map illustrates the surface microstructure of a sample subjected to 7% strain and -5 mA/cm2 charging. Most observed cracks are transgranular, with paths following the {111} plane traces. Additionally, the map highlights crack deflections occurring at annealing twin boundaries, providing evidence of their participation in the cracking process.

caption: Conceptual illustration of the deformation mechanisms occurring in the L-DED Nb–2TiC alloy during high-temperature loading at 1000 °C.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the specific deformation mechanisms active in the L-DED Nb–2TiC alloy when subjected to a temperature of 1000 °C. It provides a conceptual framework for understanding how the microstructure of this laser-directed energy deposited material responds to mechanical stress under these high-temperature conditions.

caption: Magnetization curves of as-prepared and 10k-cycle trained microwires measured at 250 K (martensite) and 300 K (austenite), illustrating the relative ease of magnetization between phases.
summary: Magnetization curves at 250 K and 300 K reveal that the martensitic phase is harder to magnetize than the austenitic phase for both as-prepared and 10k-cycle trained microwires. Despite this difference in magnetic hardness, both phases exhibit approximately equal saturation magnetization, illustrating how high fields suppress the magnetic difference.

caption: Dark field TEM imaging highlighting the distribution of ω-phase nanoparticles within the β matrix.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging reveals the presence of ω-phase nanoparticles dispersed within the β matrix of the as-printed alloy. According to the reference, the β matrix is almost completely saturated with these ω-phase precipitates, particularly in regions with lower Mo content, highlighting the phase evolution during the printing process.

caption: Pressure-temperature phase diagram of Fe–11.8Ni–12.7Si showing experimental conditions and phase boundaries compared to previous studies. Symbols denote phase states (hcp, hcp+B2, fcc+B2, liquid), while red stars indicate specific P–T points for electrical resistance measurements at 90, 140, and 150 GPa.
summary: This phase diagram illustrates the stability fields of Fe–11.8Ni–12.7Si under high pressure and temperature. It incorporates synchrotron XRD data and electrical resistance measurements initiated at 90, 140, and 150 GPa. The plot compares current phase boundaries with established literature for Fe, Fe–5Ni–4Si, and Fe–11Ni–5.3Si alloys to contextualize the material's behavior.

caption: NanoSIMS elemental map of 197Au signal, illustrating the spatial distribution of gold markers within the oxide layer of the Ni-30Cr sample.
summary: This 197Au elemental map demonstrates the distribution of gold markers within the oxide layer formed on the Ni-30Cr alloy at 900 °C in a Rhines Pack. The markers are observed to be dispersed throughout the oxide scale, providing insight into the growth mechanism and internal structure of the oxide layer.

caption: High-energy X-ray diffraction patterns comparing initial Ti-Gd1 powder, samples milled at 500 rpm under hydrogen pressure, and an interrupted sample at the end of incubation time, highlighting the complete transformation to TiH2.
summary: High-energy X-ray diffraction patterns reveal a complete phase transformation from Ti to TiH2 in all milled samples, with no detectable oxides or contaminants. The (2 2 0) reflection is modeled as the sum of two distinct peaks, representing the particle interior and the particle surface, confirming structural evolution during the milling process.

caption: Reaction curve highlighting the thermal reactivity of lattice oxygen in the TG reactor.
summary: Panel (e) shows the reaction curve highlighting the thermal reactivity of lattice oxygen. This plot, generated from TG reactor data, helps elucidate the material's oxygen release characteristics, forming a vital part of the reaction curves and lattice oxygen releasing rate analysis presented in the paper's experimental section.

caption: Total density of states (DOS) calculated for β-type Ti-Mo alloys using the SQS method following structural relaxation.
summary: This panel illustrates the total density of states for β-type Ti-Mo alloys obtained via the SQS method after structural relaxation has been applied. Comparing this to the unrelaxed state reveals how the optimized atomic positions influence the electronic DOS characteristics of the Ti-Mo alloy system.

caption: V K-edge XANES spectra for (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloys and hydrides with x=0 and x=0.10, alongside pure V metal reference.
summary: V K-edge XANES spectra for the (TiVZrNbHf)1-xAlx alloy system and its dihydride phases are shown for x=0 and x=0.10. Similar to the Ti K-edge, the absorption edge is identifiable, but the EXAFS region is ill-defined. Pure V metal serves as the reference for comparison.

caption: Entropic potential profiles of 3D printed NMC622 electrodes showing the reversible behavior between delithiation and lithiation cycles.
summary: This panel illustrates the entropic potential profiles for 3D printed NMC622 electrodes. The data confirms that the electrochemical response is highly reversible when comparing delithiation and lithiation cycles. This high degree of reversibility highlights the structural and electrochemical stability of the 3D printed electrode architecture under the tested conditions.

caption: AFM shape image showing the surface topography after 20 minutes of UTPC processing.
summary: Surface topography of the material is captured via AFM after 20 minutes of UTPC processing. This image illustrates the morphological evolution of the sample surface under these specific processing conditions, allowing for a comparative assessment of the structural modifications induced by the UTPC treatment over the specified duration.

caption: Refractive index values obtained from the D-optimal mixture design experiments.
summary: This panel displays the refractive index values measured as part of the D-optimal mixture design study. These experimental results, which are further detailed in Table S2, characterize the optical properties of the material mixtures, providing essential data for evaluating the performance of the formulated samples within the design space.

caption: Nyquist plots derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy at 750 °C with a 300 mA bias, illustrating the total, ohmic, and polarization resistances for different NH3 fuel flow rates.
summary: Impedance analysis at 750 °C and 300 mA bias provides insight into the internal resistances of the DA-SOFC. The Nyquist plots allow for the separation of ohmic and polarization resistance components, facilitating a detailed evaluation of the cell's electrochemical behavior under varying ammonia fuel flow rates.

caption: Tabulated matrix detailing the experimental design, which incorporates three distinct scanning strategies and three heat treatment conditions applied to the as-built SLM samples.
summary: This table outlines the experimental matrix for the 12 prepared samples, which are categorized by three different scanning strategies and three heat treatment conditions. The numerical labels on the sample surfaces correspond to these specific processing parameters, providing a systematic overview of the conditions applied to the as-built material.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plots (|Z| vs. frequency) for SS316L samples printed with different hatch distances, highlighting that sample K exhibits the highest impedance at low frequencies.
summary: Bode impedance magnitude plots display the frequency-dependent impedance response of the 3D-printed SS316L samples. Analysis of the |Z| versus frequency data reveals that sample K, produced with a 0.1 mm hatch distance, demonstrates the highest impedance at low frequencies, indicating superior corrosion resistance compared to the other printed variants.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map corresponding to the Short-vector strategy, illustrating the grain structure and orientation distribution in the XZ plane.
summary: The inverse pole figure map for the Short-vector strategy shows the grain structure in the XZ plane. This map allows for the analysis of grain orientation and distribution, providing insight into how the short-vector printing parameters influence the resulting microstructure compared to other vector strategies.

caption: Digital image correlation (DIC) measurements of vertical displacement values at the burr root for DA Inconel 718 specimens.
summary: This panel presents an overview of the DIC-measured vertical displacement values at the burr root of DA Inconel 718. These experimental measurements provide the foundational data for analyzing the mechanical state at the burr root across various tool-wear conditions and uncut chip thicknesses during the machining process.

caption: Compression properties of PEEK membranes, highlighting superior energy absorption in the P-400 group compared to P-500 under 40 N loading.
summary: Compression testing reveals that the P-400 PEEK membrane exhibits superior energy absorption, achieving 35% lower displacement than the P-500 group under a 40 N load. This finding suggests an optimal balance between pore architecture and structural integrity, making the P-400 configuration particularly effective for energy-absorbing applications.

caption: Reflection (R) spectra of SL-Ti3C2/cotton evaporators, highlighting the surface light-scattering properties of the different composite formulations.
summary: Reflectance spectra for SL-Ti3C2/cotton evaporators with varying concentrations are shown. By measuring the light reflected from the surface of the samples, this data serves as a key component in determining the overall light absorption efficiency of the evaporators, as defined by the relationship A = 1 - T - R.

caption: Low-temperature isothermal time-temperature-transformation diagram illustrating the annealing protocols (1–7) and the rejuvenation protocol (8) for Vit105 beams, where annealing times are set to twice the transition time to avoid crystallization.
summary: This TTT diagram outlines the experimental annealing protocols used to establish specific fictive temperatures in Vit105 samples. Protocols 1 through 7 involve isothermal annealing at temperatures chosen to avoid crystallization, while protocol 8 describes a rejuvenation process involving heating into the supercooled liquid region followed by rapid water quenching.

caption: Magnified view of the XRD pattern highlighting the evolution of peak intensities for FCC and BCC phases as a function of Al content.
summary: This magnified XRD pattern illustrates the structural evolution of the HEA coatings. As the aluminum content increases, the intensity of the (111) FCC diffraction peak decreases, while the intensity of the (110) BCC peak increases, indicating a phase transition or shift in the relative volume fractions of these crystalline structures.

caption: Full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of the G-peak plotted against laser power (LP).
summary: This plot examines the G-peak FWHM linewidths in relation to laser power. The data reveals that low laser powers result in the broadest G-peak FWHM values, which serves as a key indicator of high sp3-content within the carbon fiber structure, highlighting the sensitivity of the material to laser-induced effects.

caption: Reversals to failure plotted against temperature for specimens tested at a strain amplitude of 0.002 mm/mm, with marker size representing the magnitude of cyclic plasticity.
summary: Reversals to failure for specimens tested at a strain amplitude of 0.002 mm/mm are presented across different temperatures. Marker size corresponds to the Δ ε p /2 value. As temperatures increase, dislocation mobility is enhanced and flow stress is reduced, resulting in increased cyclic plasticity as indicated by larger marker sizes.

caption: Graphical representation of the selective laser melting working principle.
summary: This panel illustrates the fundamental working principle of the selective laser melting process. The schematic provides a clear visual overview of how the laser-based additive manufacturing technique operates, serving as a foundational reference for understanding the material fabrication method described in the study's experimental framework.

caption: Experimental fracture toughness values plotted for various specimen configurations.
summary: Experimental fracture toughness values are presented for multiple specimen configurations. These results demonstrate a consistent trend when compared to critical stress intensity factor measurements. Furthermore, surface roughness data was collected for each specimen shown in this plot using a TR100 Surface Roughness Tester to characterize the experimental conditions.

caption: Energy dissipation efficiency factor plotted against peak force recorded during impact.
summary: Panel B displays the energy dissipation efficiency factor relative to the peak force measured during impact. This visualization provides essential design criteria for protective panels, enabling the optimization of energy dissipation and mechanical performance by evaluating how peak force influences the efficiency of the tested architectures under impact conditions.

caption: In-plane and out-of-plane magnetic measurements for NZFO_50 slabs, comparing the magnetic response before Pt deposition (continuous line) and after Pt deposition (empty squares symbol).
summary: Magnetic measurements for NZFO_50 slabs reveal a distinct magnetic anisotropy with an in-plane easy axis. The data compares the magnetic response before and after Pt deposition, showing how the surface modification influences the magnetic behavior of the slabs as measured through in-plane and out-of-plane magnetization curves.

caption: Time-dependent Nyquist plots for HT-AP alloy in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, showing EIS response measured at 5-hour intervals throughout a 60-hour immersion period.
summary: The Nyquist plots for the HT-AP alloy display the AC response as a depressed semi-circle, representing the charge transfer resistance at the alloy/oxide film/solution interfaces. Collected at 5-hour intervals over 60 hours, these spectra characterize the electrochemical impedance and the stability of the corrosion product film on the alloy surface.

caption: Parallelogram unit cell configuration utilizing mode 2 pre-mode settings.
summary: Parallelogram unit cell configuration utilizing mode 2 pre-mode settings. This panel illustrates the impact of pre-mode configuration on the volume fraction of the cellular structure. The results demonstrate the powerful influence of these pre-mode configurations on the volume fraction, elastic anisotropy, Poisson's ratio, and shear-extension coupling of the material.

caption: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) image of the selected region, demonstrating dislocation lines and lattice distortion within the TiB precipitate.
summary: The IFFT analysis of the selected region provides a clear visualization of the internal defects within the TiB precipitate. Observations indicate the presence of distinct dislocation lines and significant lattice distortion, which are key characteristics of the intragranular microstructure in the TA15-0.1B alloy processed with HW.

caption: EBSD phase map of the CoCu 20 FeMnNi high-entropy alloy in its initial state, revealing a microstructure composed of interlayered elongated stripes of two distinct FCC phases.
summary: This EBSD phase map illustrates the initial microstructure of the CoCu 20 FeMnNi high-entropy alloy prior to welding. The analysis reveals a characteristic morphology consisting of interlayered elongated stripes, which correspond to two different FCC phases. These structural features are essential for understanding the material's baseline condition before further processing.

caption: Photograph showing the complex test model equipped with custom-designed end plates.
summary: This photograph displays a complex test model fitted with specialized end plates. These components were specifically designed and 3D printed to ensure that UV light exposure remains strictly perpendicular to the sides of the model during the curing process, thereby improving the precision of the manufacturing setup.

caption: Raman spectrum of the HEA disc worn surface at 800 °C, identifying V2O5 and Fe2O3 as the primary oxidation products.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the HEA disc worn surface at 800 °C is presented. The spectrum confirms that V2O5 and Fe2O3 are the primary oxidation products formed during sliding wear at this high temperature, demonstrating the stability of these specific oxide phases under severe thermal and mechanical wear conditions.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of annealed W625.
summary: This Kernel Average Misorientation map provides a visualization of the local misorientation distribution within the annealed W625 specimen. It serves as a diagnostic tool to assess the internal strain and dislocation density changes that occurred during the annealing process, complementing the grain texture data observed in the IPF map.

caption: Comparison of Vickers macrohardness and stabilized coefficient of friction (COF) values for various metallic samples tested against an SLA alumina ball.
summary: This panel displays the Vickers macrohardness alongside stabilized COF values for metallic samples tested with an SLA alumina ball. The data is presented to correlate the material hardness with friction performance, illustrating the relationship between mechanical properties and tribological behavior observed during the final stage of the testing process.

caption: Absorption coefficient curve for the TPMS structure optimized for a target frequency of 700 Hz.
summary: This plot displays the frequency-dependent absorption coefficient for the 700 Hz optimized TPMS structure. The curve highlights the peak absorption performance achieved at the target frequency, demonstrating the efficacy of the graded porosity design in maximizing acoustic energy capture within the specified low-frequency range.

caption: Initial stage of laser irradiation showing CuSn20 particle melting and diamond particle migration.
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial melting of CuSn20 particles under laser irradiation. The process involves the migration and rotation of diamond particles, driven by gravity and fluid flow. This stage sets the foundation for the subsequent interfacial dynamics observed during the solidification of the composite material system.

caption: Initial SLM system configuration showing the arrangement of Ti nanoparticles, the defined laser heating region, and the underlying substrate layers.
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial simulation configuration for the selective laser melting process of Ti nanoparticles. It highlights the spatial arrangement of the nanoparticles, the defined cylindrical laser heating region with a height of 60 Å and diameter of 50 Å, and the multi-layered Ti substrate structure.

caption: In-depth microhardness variations measured across the five groups of specimens.
summary: This panel presents the in-depth microhardness variations observed in the five groups of specimens. The plot tracks the hardness values as a function of depth, allowing for a direct comparison of the mechanical hardening or softening effects induced by the different processing conditions applied to each specimen group.

caption: Calculated partial density of states (PDOS) curves for the Al(1) atom and its nearest neighbor Ni(2), Ni(3), Ni(4), and Ni(5) atoms within the clean EDC system, focusing on the high-energy electronic region.
summary: This plot displays the calculated partial density of states for the Al(1) atom and its nearest neighbors, Ni(2) through Ni(5), in a clean EDC system. By examining these PDOS curves in the high-energy region, the interaction between the alloying atoms and host atoms is effectively characterized and analyzed.

caption: Storage modulus (E') plotted against temperature for hydrogels fabricated using 390 nm UV light.
summary: Storage modulus (E') measurements as a function of temperature are shown for hydrogels cured at 390 nm. The data illustrates the mechanical stiffness of the crosslinked network. By analyzing the temperature at which E' drops, the reinforcing impact of the network structure is evaluated under dynamic mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of cell viability at 7 days post-encapsulation, confirming the presence of viable cells on both PLA surfaces and within the hydrogel matrix.
summary: Live/dead staining performed 7 days post-encapsulation reveals the viability of cells within the experimental system. The imaging confirms that cells remain viable on both the PLA scaffold surfaces and within the hydrogel matrix, establishing a baseline for cell health before the initiation of the vibration experiments.

caption: Log-log S-N fatigue curves comparing WAAM NAB alloy specimens tested in ambient air and ex-situ corroded conditions, illustrating the stress amplitude versus cycles to failure.
summary: This S-N fatigue plot displays the performance of WAAM NAB alloy under ambient air and ex-situ corroded conditions. Fatigue failure consistently initiates at surface pitting sites, propagating until final fracture. The log-log representation of stress amplitude versus cycles to failure highlights the reduced fatigue life of pre-corroded specimens.

caption: Log-log S-N curve for 90° print orientation specimens, shown with the wrought heat treated IN718 baseline for comparison.
summary: The fatigue life of 90° orientation specimens is characterized by a log-log S-N curve modeled with a power function. By comparing these results to the wrought heat treated IN718 baseline, the figure highlights how print orientation influences the fatigue performance of the material under cyclic loading conditions.

caption: Specific wear rate of austenitic BMS plotted against varying ferrite content.
summary: This plot illustrates the specific wear rate for austenitic BMS. The data demonstrates a clear trend where the wear rate decreases as the ferrite content increases within the material. This relationship highlights the influence of microstructural composition on the tribological performance and durability of the austenitic BMS alloy.

caption: Rate capability plot evaluating the performance of carbon nanotube nanocomposite electrodes across various current densities.
summary: This rate capability plot evaluates the performance of carbon nanotube nanocomposite electrodes under varying current densities. The results demonstrate the material's ability to maintain high capacity and stability, highlighting the effectiveness of carbon nanotube integration for high-performance lithium-ion battery applications in 3D printed systems.

caption: Resistance curve for 3D printed semi-woven non-hybrid laminates with the highest LE material ratio.
summary: The resistance curve shown here represents the fracture behavior of 3D printed semi-woven non-hybrid laminates with the highest LE material ratio. By documenting the crack growth resistance, this plot completes the mechanical assessment of the series, demonstrating the impact of material composition on the toughness of the printed laminates.

caption: Magnified dark-field TEM image (DF2) showing a slip trace shearing a precipitate alongside an unsheared precipitate pinned by a dislocation loop in the strained LPBF sample.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph provides a magnified view of precipitate-dislocation interactions in the strained LPBF sample. It clearly distinguishes between a precipitate sheared by a slip trace and an unsheared precipitate surrounded by a dislocation loop, illustrating the localized plastic deformation mechanisms occurring within the material's microstructure.

caption: Fourier filtered high-resolution HAADF-STEM image of a γ-Al2O3 grain viewed along the [1 1 0] zone axis, showing TBs and SFs along {111} planes with approximately 2 nm spacing; the inset displays the corresponding FFT pattern confirming the γ-Al2O3 phase.
summary: Atomic-scale HAADF-STEM imaging along the [1 1 0] zone axis identifies twin boundaries and stacking faults spaced at approximately 2 nm along {111} planes. The corresponding FFT pattern confirms that the transient oxide phase is primarily γ-Al2O3, with defects aligned parallel to the growth direction of the platelet-like oxide.

caption: Reconstructed topological lattice unit cell model featuring maximum dimensions of 8 mm in length, width, and height.
summary: This panel displays the reconstructed topological lattice unit cell model. The structure is characterized by maximum dimensions of 8 mm in length, width, and height. This unit cell serves as the fundamental building block for the topology-optimized lattice structure components described in the study.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the columnar grain (CG) region in the Al–Mg–Mn-Sc-Zr alloy after heat treatment at 330 °C for 5 hours.
summary: This bright-field TEM image shows the columnar grain region of the Al–Mg–Mn-Sc-Zr alloy after a 330 °C/5 h heat treatment. The strengthening observed in this condition is primarily attributed to the precipitation of numerous nano-sized Al3(Sc, Zr) particles, which effectively pin dislocations and significantly enhance the alloy's mechanical performance.

caption: Scheil solidification simulation for the laser metal deposition (C-LMD) process, showing phase formation versus temperature without considering cooling rate effects.
summary: Representing the laser metal deposition process, this panel utilizes the classical Scheil model to simulate solidification under out-of-equilibrium conditions. By neglecting cooling rate effects and focusing on segregation, the simulation provides a comparative view of phase formation, highlighting lower Ni3Si proportions relative to the equilibrium-based gravity casting model.

caption: Bragg edge ratio of H sample to H powder for (111) and (200) planes in the Fe(316L)/Cu(CuCrZr) bilayer, measured along the TD2 and BD directions.
summary: This panel displays the Bragg edge ratio for (111) and (200) planes in the Fe(316L)/Cu(CuCrZr) bilayer sample. Measurements were taken along the TD2 and BD directions using neutron diffraction. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the crystallographic texture by comparing sample edge intensities to powder standards.

caption: Creep behavior at 950 °C and 270 MPa, showing experimental data in grey and fitted curves in color across three representations: strain versus time, strain rate versus time, and strain rate versus strain.
summary: This panel displays creep test results at 950 °C and 270 MPa. Experimental data are shown in grey, while fitted curves are in color. The three representations include strain versus time, double-logarithmic strain rate versus time, and log-linear strain rate versus strain, illustrating the material's creep response under these specific conditions.

caption: Placement of the filled mold into the compression unit for consolidation.
summary: Following the additive manufacturing phase, the mold is positioned within the compression unit. This step is a critical component of the AMCM foundry system, ensuring the printed composite is correctly aligned and prepared for the application of pressure to achieve the desired material consolidation and final part geometry.

caption: Current-time transients measured at FCDI cells featuring 3D-printed and CNC-milled flow channels, evaluated with a 10 wt% YP50F flow electrode composition in 1.5 g/L NaCl solution.
summary: Current-time transients are presented for FCDI cells equipped with 3D-printed and CNC-milled flow channels. By maintaining a 10 wt% YP50F flow electrode concentration during the desalination of a 1.5 g/L NaCl solution, the plot illustrates the electrochemical current behavior and stability across the different channel architectures tested.

caption: Temperature evolution of the molten pool during L-DED fabrication of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA at an AED of 52.17 J/mm2.
summary: This graph depicts the molten pool temperature change for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA specimens fabricated at an AED of 52.17 J/mm2. Recorded by an infrared thermal camera, the solidification time data is used to define the cooling rate, which characterizes the thermal conditions during the solidification of the deposited layer.

caption: Mean squared error (MSE) progression over training epochs for scenario 2 of the PEOF-SNF artificial backpropagation network.
summary: Representing the second paradigm scenario, this plot tracks the MSE reduction throughout the training epochs. The small MSE values observed indicate successful convergence of the ANN model, demonstrating its capability to accurately capture the dynamics of periodic electroosmotic flow across a stretched surface during the training phase.

caption: Height-based colored surface map of sample O_30, generated from LL system point clouds.
summary: Sample O_30 is represented by a colored surface map illustrating the height of each point relative to the base plate. These data were collected using an LL system and processed via TalyMap software to visualize the layer surface topography, providing a clear representation of the sample's vertical surface profile.

caption: Digital 3D reconstruction of the fracture surface for a standard CFRP specimen, showing the crack deflection path between the first and second plies.
summary: This 3D reconstruction displays the fracture surface of a standard CFRP specimen. The digital model, generated via non-contact optical profilometry, highlights the characteristic crack deflection occurring between the first and second plies of the adherend, a common failure mode observed in the tested specimens.

caption: Thermodynamic phase calculation for the Ti6Al4V-0.25BN composite, showing the influence of boron and nitrogen on phase stability and solidus temperature.
summary: Thermodynamic calculations for the 0.25BN composite reveal the impact of boron and nitrogen additions on the alloy's phase stability. The diagram shows that the solidus temperature decreases with the inclusion of these elements. Additionally, the presence of boron facilitates the formation of TiB phases within the microstructure.

caption: Heel loading test results for Design-3, showing an energy return of 80% and a high stiffness of 121 N/mm.
summary: Design-3 is subjected to a heel loading test, yielding an energy return of 80% and a stiffness of 121 N/mm. Because the energy return falls below the 82% threshold and the stiffness is high, the design is classified as rigid rather than dynamic.

caption: Kinetics of Frenkel defect pair formation in Cu-10at%Ni alloy across multiple PKA energy irradiation scenarios at 300 K.
summary: Shown is the kinetic behavior of Frenkel defect pairs in Cu-10at%Ni alloy under different PKA energy irradiation at 300 K. The graph highlights the temporal changes in defect populations, illustrating the impact of a 10 at% Ni concentration on the radiation-induced defect evolution within the copper matrix.

caption: Exploded view illustrating the design of a single reinforced composite layer composed of distinct solid bodies.
summary: This schematic illustrates the design strategy for a reinforced composite layer, where each layer is constructed as a separate solid body. The exploded view provides a clear visualization of the individual components that constitute the composite structure, serving as the foundational design model for the subsequent fabrication and slicing process.

caption: Maximum intensity projection of fluorescently stained fibroblasts encapsulated in QSGM1 hydrogel, highlighting live cells in green and dead cells in red after two weeks of culture.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy imaging provides a visual confirmation of cell viability within the QSGM1 hydrogel. The maximum intensity projection reveals that most fibroblasts remain alive, indicated by green staining, after two weeks of culture. This result supports the quantitative findings that the hydrogel maintains excellent cytocompatibility for encapsulated cells.

caption: Close-up view of a macroscopic defect extracted from the residual image, accompanied by a line profile demonstrating the variation of residual gray values across the defective region.
summary: This panel displays a close-up of a macroscopic defect identified in the residual image. The accompanying line profile illustrates the variation in residual gray values across the defect, highlighting that scatter-affected projections often exhibit non-zero values even outside the defective zone, which complicates the quantitative evaluation of scatter compensation methods.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves at 0.5 mA cm⁻² for 5 wt% PEGDA in 1M H₂SO₄ at -20 °C, illustrating voltage window optimization.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge results at 0.5 mA cm⁻² confirm the electrochemical stability of the 5 wt% PEGDA electrolyte at -20 °C. The curves exhibit symmetric triangular profiles for voltage windows up to 1.1 V, confirming the device's ability to maintain efficient charge-discharge cycles even in sub-zero temperature environments.

caption: STEM-HAADF image and corresponding fast Fourier transformation (FFT) pattern showing stacking faults and deformation nanotwins with thicknesses of a few nanometers.
summary: The STEM-HAADF image and its corresponding FFT pattern provide atomic-scale evidence of stacking faults and deformation nanotwins. These features, which have thicknesses of only a few nanometers or less, demonstrate that higher densities of stacking faults and nanoscale twins appear as strain increases in the fractured LPBF+HT sample.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the corrosion behavior of wrought, SLM, and SLM + HT Ti-6Al-4V alloy specimens in Ringer's solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrate the corrosion characteristics of Ti-6Al-4V alloy samples. The plot compares the electrochemical response of wrought, SLM, and SLM + HT processed materials in Ringer's solution, providing insight into the influence of manufacturing and heat treatment on the corrosion resistance of the alloy.

caption: Overview of metal additive manufacturing (MAM) processes categorized by energy source according to ASTM standards, including powder bed fusion (PBF), directed energy deposition (DED), binder jetting (BJ), and material extrusion (MEX).
summary: This schematic illustrates the fundamental metal additive manufacturing processes as defined by ASTM standards. It highlights the four primary techniques—PBF, DED, BJ, and MEX—organized by their respective energy sources. The diagram serves as a foundational overview for understanding the diverse technological approaches utilized in modern additive manufacturing workflows.

caption: Bright-field TEM image and corresponding elemental distribution maps of silicide precipitates within the TA37 alloy matrix after 100 hours of thermal exposure at 600 °C.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging reveals the morphological characteristics of silicide precipitates in the TA37 alloy following 100 hours of thermal exposure at 600 °C. Accompanying elemental distribution maps provide spatial confirmation of the chemical composition of these silicides within the alloy microstructure, highlighting their distribution after the specified thermal treatment.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns (4–14°) of Ti0, Ti4, and Ti7 bulk HEAs in as-sprayed, 800 °C/6 h, and 1000 °C/6 h conditions after tensile testing.
summary: Post-tensile synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns (4–14°) are displayed for Ti0, Ti4, and Ti7 bulk high-entropy alloys across as-sprayed, 800 °C/6 h, and 1000 °C/6 h conditions. These high-precision results are used to investigate potential phase changes occurring during the tensile test process for these specific alloy compositions.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) image of sample 2, highlighting uniform orientation within colonies.
summary: EBSD inverse pole figure image of eutectic alloy sample 2 reveals the orientation of the microstructure. The image demonstrates that phases within the same colony share the same crystal orientation, confirming the structural uniformity characteristic of this fully eutectic alloy.

caption: Temperature response and corresponding resistance values of TPU-B25 composites with CB and CB/ZnO fillers under applied voltages ranging from 1 to 24 V.
summary: Temperature and resistance measurements for TPU-B25 composites with CB and CB/ZnO fillers are recorded under applied voltages from 1 to 24 V. This analysis ensures that the relative resistance changes observed during humidity testing are not artifacts caused by Joule heating effects within the composite sensor fibers.

caption: XRD pattern of as-built sample Q, illustrating the FCC-disordered phase and the calculated ratio of <111> to <200> crystallographic orientations.
summary: Sample Q displays an FCC-disordered phase of Fe and Ni atoms. The XRD data highlights the texture of the as-built sample, where the orientation along the hard magnetization axis <200> influences the spin rotation mechanism, thereby impacting the magnetic performance of the material at higher frequencies.

caption: Raman spectra and corresponding multi-peak fitting curves for SL-T char samples, illustrating the structural analysis of carbonaceous materials.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was employed to investigate the degree of graphitization in pyrolysis and co-pyrolysis chars, specifically assessing the impact of SL addition on carbon structure. Panel (a) displays the Raman spectra for all char samples, including detailed fitting curves for the SL-T sample to characterize its structural properties.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry curves for machined wrought NiTi samples at the minimum tool-wear stage, compared against the baseline material state.
summary: This panel displays DSC curves for wrought NiTi samples subjected to machining at the minimum tool-wear stage. By comparing these results to the baseline material state before machining, the thermal response and phase transformation characteristics of the wrought alloy are evaluated under varying cutting speeds to assess the impact of the machining process.

caption: EDS line scan analysis of a corroded WAAM C276 sample, illustrating the spatial correlation between Mo-enriched precipitates and reduced Cr depletion rates.
summary: EDS line scans for WAAM C276 samples demonstrate the impact of microstructure on corrosion behavior. The data shows that precipitate-rich regions, characterized by elevated Mo levels, exhibit delayed Cr depletion. Conversely, precipitate-free zones show rapid Cr depletion, confirming the consistency between experimental observations and the predicted diffusion behavior in the alloy.

caption: Atom probe tomography map highlighting the spatial distribution of Ni atoms in the Ni-60Fe alloy after Ni ion irradiation.
summary: The Ni atom map derived from APT data illustrates the elemental distribution within the Ni-60Fe alloy post-irradiation. Consistent with the pristine state, the Ni distribution remains homogeneous throughout the analyzed volume, confirming that the high-fluence irradiation did not induce any chemical variance or phase separation in the alloy.

caption: Graphical overview of the proposed PGA pipeline architecture.
summary: This diagram provides a comprehensive graphical overview of the proposed PGA pipeline. It illustrates the sequential steps and logical flow inherent in the methodology, serving as a high-level conceptual representation of the entire processing framework as described in the research study's pipeline design.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph and WDS elemental maps of Cu and Mn for the L 117 sample, showing the distribution of elements within the melt pool structure.
summary: For the L 117 sample, backscattered electron micrographs and WDS elemental maps illustrate the spatial distribution of Cu and Mn. The analysis confirms that cracking remains present in the microstructure, consistent with the overall observation that cracking was unavoidable across the various printing parameters employed in this study.

caption: Fracture surface of a variable-angle truncated cone tested at 295K, showing a large smooth tear area with limited dimple formation.
summary: Fracture morphology of the specimen tested at 295K reveals a large smooth tear area with relatively few dimples. This surface appearance is attributed to intense shear deformation occurring during the incremental forming process, indicating a distinct fracture behavior compared to the low-temperature condition.

caption: Five-nanometer-thick slices extracted from the atom probe tomography analysis of DED-LB/w duplex stainless steel aged for 1000 hours at 400 °C.
summary: Five-nanometer-thick slices extracted from the atom probe tomography analysis of DED-LB/w duplex stainless steel aged for 1000 hours at 400 °C. As noted in the reference, APT allows for the selection of very thin layers that closely approximate a genuine 2D elemental map for detailed microstructural characterization.

caption: Axial RBS/C spectra comparing simulated channeling behavior for a single solid nickel structure versus a merged structure composed of multiple boxes, alongside reference spectra for pristine and randomly oriented samples, with an inset highlighting the peak region.
summary: This figure presents simulated axial RBS/C spectra to evaluate the impact of structural interfaces on channeling. By comparing a monolithic nickel structure with a model constructed from multiple boxes, the simulation clarifies how internal boundaries influence the resulting spectra. Reference data for pristine and random orientations provide context for the observed channeling effects.

caption: Energy dispersive spectroscopy mapping of the Al@Ni alloy particle showing the spatial distribution of elements.
summary: Energy dispersive spectroscopy mapping of the Al@Ni alloy particle reveals the spatial distribution of its constituent elements. Analysis of the mapping results indicates that both aluminum and nickel elements are uniformly distributed throughout the alloy particle, confirming a homogeneous elemental composition within the material structure as observed via EDS.

caption: Tabulated physical and chemical properties of the γ-Al2O3 support and supported Ni catalysts, highlighting specific surface area (SBET) values ranging from 231.8 to 268.0 m2/g compared to the support's 299.8 m2/g.
summary: This table presents the physical and chemical properties of the γ-Al2O3 support and various supported Ni catalysts. The data indicates that the specific surface areas (SBET) of the catalysts vary between 231.8 m2/g and 268.0 m2/g, which are notably lower than the 299.8 m2/g measured for the pure γ-Al2O3 support.

caption: XPS spectrum of the Al-10 Ni coating surface after 60 min of MAO processing, exhibiting increased peak intensities compared to shorter durations.
summary: This panel shows the XPS spectrum for the Al-10Ni alloy after 60 minutes of MAO processing. The intensity of the nickel peaks is significantly higher than in the 30-minute sample, indicating that an increasing amount of nickel elements is deposited on the coating surface as the processing time extends.

caption: Nyquist plot of WAAM carbon steel immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, displaying a depressed arc across the measured frequency range.
summary: Representing the electrochemical impedance of WAAM carbon steel, this Nyquist plot highlights the material's response when immersed in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. A depressed arc is clearly visible in the 10^4 Hz to 10 Hz frequency range, reflecting the electrochemical characteristics of the steel under these specific conditions.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the corresponding HER polarization curves for Pt x Ni/C and Pt/C JM catalysts under identical experimental conditions of 0.1 M KOH, 5 mV s-1, 1600 rpm, and 25 °C.
summary: Tafel plots for Pt x Ni/C and Pt/C JM catalysts are shown, derived from the HER polarization curves. These plots characterize the kinetic behavior of the catalysts in N2-saturated 0.1 M KOH at 25 °C, with a scan rate of 5 mV s-1 and a rotation speed of 1600 rpm.

caption: Radar chart comparing the partition coefficients of various elements between γ″ precipitates and the γ matrix for Alloy 625 (blue) and Alloy 625 Plus (red).
summary: This radar chart illustrates the partition coefficients of elements between γ″ precipitates and the γ matrix in Alloy 625 and Alloy 625 Plus. Alloy 625 Plus exhibits larger partition coefficients for Nb and Ti compared to Alloy 625, a compositional difference that potentially contributes to the slower coarsening rate of γ″ precipitates.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph showing the morphology of δ-phase precipitates along the grain boundaries in a DA specimen exposed for 500 hours at 650 °C.
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the morphology of δ-phase precipitates located along the grain boundaries of an Inconel 718 DA specimen after 500 hours of exposure at 650 °C. The δ-phase exhibits a characteristic linearly adjoining feature along the grain boundaries, consistent with its transformation from γ″ phase.

caption: Observation port view of the furnace interior at 1450 °C, demonstrating the invisibility of the ammonia combustion flame to the naked eye.
summary: This photograph captures the interior of the furnace at a temperature of 1450 °C as seen through the observation port. It highlights the specific experimental condition where the ammonia combustion flame remains invisible to the naked eye, providing a visual baseline for the furnace environment during the spectroscopic measurements.

caption: Spectral response curve of a refractometer with a fiber length of 10 mm, a diameter of 50 μm, and a refractive index of 1.43, derived from MPA simulation data.
summary: This plot displays the spectral response of a refractometer, characterized by a fiber length of 10 mm, a diameter of 50 μm, and a refractive index of 1.43. The data presented is extracted from an MPA simulation, illustrating the optical performance metrics relevant to the specified refractometer configuration and material parameters.

caption: Storage and loss modulus plotted against shear strain for formulations containing 0, 0.25, and 1 wt% PVB, measured via oscillatory strain sweep at 20 °C and 10 rad/s.
summary: This panel displays the viscoelastic response of three paste formulations with varying PVB content (0, 0.25, and 1 wt%) as a function of shear strain. The oscillatory strain sweep test, conducted at 20 °C and 10 rad/s, reveals how PVB concentration influences the storage and loss moduli of the material.

caption: Interface energy profile for the HfC(111)/Ni(001) system, highlighting the Bridge2 configuration as the most stable model.
summary: The HfC(111)/Ni(001) interface model demonstrates that the Bridge2 configuration is the most stable, exhibiting the lowest interface energy. Calculated values for this specific interface structure range from 4.349 J/m2 to 4.188 J/m2, indicating a favorable energetic state for this atomic arrangement compared to other potential configurations.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of chondrocytes exposed to 10 µM H2O2, demonstrating high viability with a negligible increase in red-stained dead cells.
summary: Chondrocytes exposed to 10 µM hydrogen peroxide maintain high viability, as evidenced by the live-dead assay. The image shows a majority of green-stained live cells, with only a small number of red-stained dead cells, confirming that the cells remain largely unaffected by this concentration of peroxide.

caption: Temperature-displacement curves for graphite punches during sintering, illustrating thermal deformation behavior between 100°C and 550°C followed by the onset of actual sintering.
summary: Graphite punch displacement is plotted against temperature for four distinct sintering conditions. The curves reveal a slow thermal deformation region characterized by a gradual increase in displacement from 100°C to 550°C. Beyond this threshold, the data indicates the initiation of the actual sintering process for the specimens.

caption: Depth XPS spectra profile of electrodeposited CoNi films on Si/Ti/Au electrodes synthesized at -1.15 V.
summary: XPS depth profiling for the CoNi film prepared at -1.15 V reveals the presence of oxygen within the sample. This spectral evidence indicates that utilizing a more negative potential during electrodeposition leads to the inclusion of oxide or hydroxide content, distinguishing the film's chemical composition from those prepared at lower potentials.

caption: Measured electrical resistance of an embedded 3D silver structure featuring a 6-point connection configuration, yielding a resistance value of 0.759 MΩ.
summary: This panel displays the electrical resistance measurement for an embedded 3D silver structure with a 6-point connection. The measured resistance is 0.759 MΩ, which aligns with the maximum resistance value of 0.76 MΩ reported in the reference, confirming the conductive performance of the 6-point connection design.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves evaluating the thermal stability of HEAEPxPEG solution formulations.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for HEAEPxPEG solutions are shown to provide insight into their thermal stability. This panel serves as a key component in evaluating the degradation behavior and overall thermal performance of the formulations, offering a direct comparison of stability across the different PEG-containing solution compositions.

caption: Light transmittance measurements for SRCP, NHC, DPC, and RHCP, illustrating the optical clarity of the materials.
summary: The light transmittance of SRCP, NHC, DPC, and RHCP is compared in this panel. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the optical properties of these materials, which is a critical factor for applications involving tissue interfaces where visibility or light penetration might be required.

caption: Fatigue crack growth curve for the PSP_2 specimen, displaying a kink at 4.3 mm crack length similar to the thinner variant.
summary: For the PSP_2 specimen, the FCG curve displays a distinct kink when the crack reaches 4.3 mm. This behavior indicates a transition from crack initiation in the PSP material to growth through the full specimen thickness, with data below the lower validity limit excluded from the analysis.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectrum of PLA and transmission spectrum of glass, illustrating the optical interaction between the polymer matrix and the reinforcement material.
summary: This panel displays the typical visible and UV absorption spectrum of PLA alongside the transmission spectrum of glass. These spectral data characterize the relationship between the PLA matrix and the glass fiber reinforcement with respect to UV-C light exposure, providing a baseline for understanding the material's optical properties.

caption: Comparison of corrosion rate versus specific gravity for the current study compared to literature data for Mg-8Li/Mg-9Li and Mg-Gd-Ni alloys, with corrosion rates determined via weight loss or hydrogen evolution in 3.0–3.5 wt% NaCl or KCl solutions.
summary: This plot benchmarks the corrosion performance and specific gravity of the developed alloy against established Mg-Li and Mg-Gd-Ni systems. By utilizing weight loss and hydrogen evolution data from various literature sources in chloride-based solutions, the figure illustrates the relative material efficiency and environmental stability of the current work.

caption: Overlaid 1H NMR spectra of crude and purified AE, LH, and SL fucoidan samples, highlighting structural moieties including α-anomeric protons, β-anomeric protons, O-acetylated and O-sulfated positions, sugar ring protons, acetyl CH3 groups, and fucose CH3 protons, with asterisks denoting mannitol and free acetate impurities.
summary: This 1H NMR spectral analysis compares crude and purified AE, LH, and SL fucoidan samples. The spectra identify key structural moieties such as anomeric protons and various O-substituted sugar ring positions. Impurities like mannitol and free acetate are consistently observed across all purified samples, reflecting the presence of low molecular weight contaminants.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation density map corresponding to the deformed CuCrZr sample shown in panel (a).
summary: Representing the geometrically necessary dislocation density, this map provides insight into the internal strain distribution of the CuCrZr sample after compression. Alongside the IPF map, it confirms that the compressive load applied along the building direction induces grain subdivision, highlighting the resulting dislocation-based microstructural changes within the deformed material.

caption: Friction coefficient as a function of applied load for Cu45.5Zr51Al3.5, Cu44.5Zr51Al3.5Ni1, and Cu43.5Zr51Al3.5Ni2 alloys, with an inset displaying the evolution of the friction coefficient over time.
summary: The friction coefficient is plotted against applied loads ranging from 1 to 15 N for three distinct alloy compositions. The inset reveals a two-stage wear behavior characterized by an initial rapid increase in friction followed by a steady-state phase, indicating the evolution of wear resistance under sliding conditions.

caption: Body-Centered Cube (BCC) lattice structure unit cell.
summary: The Body-Centered Cube (BCC) lattice structure is depicted as one of the three unit cell configurations utilized as TCEs in this study. This schematic representation illustrates the specific atomic arrangement characteristic of the BCC lattice, which is essential for understanding the structural properties investigated throughout the research.

caption: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum of the IC10 superalloy passivation film, showing peak fitting for metallic Ni at 855.48 eV and 872.98 eV, and NiO species at 861.18 eV and 879.08 eV.
summary: The Ni 2p high-resolution XPS spectrum for the IC10 superalloy passivation film reveals the chemical state of nickel. Peak fitting analysis identifies metallic Ni components at binding energies of 855.48 eV and 872.98 eV, alongside NiO oxide species located at 861.18 eV and 879.08 eV within the film.

caption: Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram illustrating the precipitation kinetics and phase stability regions for alloy 625.
summary: This TTT diagram provides a predictive framework for alloy 625, mapping the temporal evolution of phase transformations across varying temperature regimes. By delineating the kinetics of precipitation, the diagram serves as a critical tool for understanding the distribution of alloying elements and the resulting microstructural stability during thermal processing.

caption: Particle tracks upstream of the spray gun at Cl = 140 mm and Pl = 40 mm, showing extensive sidewall collisions.
summary: Particle trajectories are visualized for Cl = 140 mm and Pl = 40 mm. The trajectories occupy the entire region upstream of the spray gun. Collisions with the sidewalls of the convergent section are particularly evident in this configuration, demonstrating the significant impact of increased Pl on particle dispersion.

caption: Nanoindentation load-displacement curves for the 2HEA4mm sample, illustrating the mechanical response at the edge and center positions.
summary: Panel b presents nanoindentation curves for the 2HEA4mm alloy, highlighting the mechanical behavior at the edge and center of the specimen. These curves demonstrate how the mechanical properties, including hardness and indentation depth, vary significantly due to differences in the cooling rate experienced by the 2HEA alloy samples.

caption: Wear rate comparison between the base TC4 alloy and the TaC-reinforced TC4 composite specimens.
summary: Wear rate measurements are presented for TC4 and TaC/TC4 composites to evaluate their tribological performance. This plot provides a quantitative assessment of material loss during testing, serving as a key indicator of the wear resistance improvements achieved through the addition of TaC particles to the TC4 matrix under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Temperature-dependent photoluminescence spectra for sample P033 measured between 10 K and 300 K.
summary: This panel displays an exemplary set of temperature-dependent photoluminescence spectra for the P033 sample. The data, collected across a temperature range of 10 K to 300 K, illustrates the evolution of PL characteristics as a function of thermal conditions, providing a foundational view of the material's optical response.

caption: Areal capacity values of the Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene electrode plotted against varying current densities.
summary: Areal capacity values of the Cu-Ni-O-FPs/MXene electrode plotted against varying current densities. This plot demonstrates the rate capability of the hybrid material, showing how the capacity changes as the discharge current increases, which is critical for assessing the practical electrochemical performance of the printed electrode.

caption: Normalized Co K-edge XANES spectra for all samples, demonstrating the metallic nature of Co in the Ni1Co3@NC catalyst.
summary: Normalized Co K-edge XANES spectra are shown for all samples. The spectrum for Ni1Co3@NC closely matches that of Co foil, confirming that cobalt is in a metallic state. This result aligns with XRD and XPS data, further supporting the metallic nature of the Co species in the synthesized material.

caption: Bode plots comparing the frequency response of CHBAC devices before and after cycling.
summary: Bode plots for the CHBAC device indicate significant post-cycling changes, including a reduction in capacitance and an increase in equivalent series resistance (ESR). Furthermore, the data show shifts in phase angles and alterations in the frequency response, reflecting the impact of cycling on the device's electrochemical properties.

caption: Phonon dispersion curve calculated for the P4/mmm (LaNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattice under ferromagnetic ordering, where negative values on the y-axis signify imaginary frequencies indicating structural instability.
summary: The phonon dispersion curve for the (LaNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattice under ferromagnetic ordering is presented here. Investigation of these dispersion curves reveals dominant structural modes. The presence of negative values on the y-axis indicates imaginary frequencies, which signify that the P4/mmm structure is unstable in this configuration.

caption: FT-IR spectra of the synthesized catalysts showing characteristic vibrational modes.
summary: This panel presents the FT-IR spectra of the catalysts, providing insight into the chemical functional groups present. The spectral data serves to characterize the surface chemistry and molecular bonding environment of the catalyst material, complementing the structural information obtained from other analytical techniques used in the study.

caption: Constitutional undercooling distribution in the melt for a 10 mm chill thickness, featuring superimposed solid fraction contours.
summary: This simulation displays the constitutional undercooling distribution ahead of the solidification front for a 10 mm chill thickness. At 50 seconds, undercooling values range from 1.8 to 3.6 °C. The observed uneven distribution is attributed to solute accumulation in the liquid phase driven by destabilizing natural convection currents.

caption: Three-dimensional morphology reconstruction of the SS/Cu composite, illustrating the spatial arrangement and phase distribution of the constituent materials.
summary: This panel presents the 3D morphology of the SS/Cu composite. The reconstruction provides a detailed visualization of the spatial arrangement and distribution patterns of the Cu and SS phases within the composite structure, as supported by the corresponding 3D morphology analysis and phase distribution data.

caption: SEM image integrated with surface element distribution data, illustrating the transport of coating fragments alongside the forging material.
summary: This SEM image, combined with surface element distribution data, demonstrates the transport of AlTiCrSiN coating fragments. The visualization confirms that these fragments are mixed and transported with the forging material, providing direct evidence of the coating's mechanical degradation and displacement along the punch surface during the forging operation.

caption: Workflow schematic illustrating the machine learning framework developed for phase structure classification in stainless steels.
summary: This schematic outlines the machine learning framework designed for phase structure classification. The workflow incorporates model evaluation metrics such as accuracy, Kappa index, ROC curves, and AUC to assess performance. It serves as the foundational architecture for predicting phase structures, including BCC, FCC, and dual-phase configurations in stainless steel materials.

caption: Cell viability percentage of fibroblasts treated with CS-AL, Bar, Nio-Bar, and Nio-Bar@CS-AL scaffolds across concentrations ranging from 0 to 50 μg/mL, demonstrating that the Nio-Bar@CS-AL scaffold maintains over 90% viability.
summary: Fibroblast cell viability was evaluated across various scaffold treatments and concentrations up to 50 μg/mL. The results demonstrate that all tested scaffold extracts, particularly the Nio-Bar@CS-AL formulation, maintain high cell viability above 90%, confirming the absence of significant cytotoxicity and supporting the biocompatibility of the developed materials for further biological applications.

caption: Deconvoluted micro-photoluminescence emission spectrum of 10 mol% YSZ octet-truss lattices after an extended 2-hour annealing duration at 1050 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the deconvoluted micro-photoluminescence emission spectrum for 10 mol% YSZ octet-truss lattices annealed at 1050 °C for 2 hours. The spectrum confirms the absence of carbon-related point defect emissions, supporting the conclusion that these emissions are not dependent on the annealing temperature or duration applied to the YSZ octet-truss lattice structures.

caption: Simulation snapshot at 355.78 ms showing the laser-induced growth of irregular Ti3Au IMC grains during processing at 150 kW/cm2 and 4 nm/ms scanning speed.
summary: Captured at 355.78 ms, this simulation snapshot demonstrates the dynamic growth of IMC grains during laser treatment. The irregular, distinct shapes of the grains align with experimental observations, confirming the simulation's accuracy in capturing the evolution of the Ti3Au intermetallic phase during the laser processing of the Ti-Au system.

caption: Experimental configuration for acceleration sensing, featuring the CPS connected to a Rigol MSO8104 oscilloscope via two 10:1 passive probes to measure output voltage.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup for acceleration sensing. The CPS device is connected to a Rigol MSO8104 oscilloscope using two 10:1 passive probes. This configuration allows for the precise measurement of the output voltage (Vpp) generated by the CPS during acceleration sensing tests.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot representing the averaged feature effects across all pH classes to provide a holistic overview of the XGBoost model's decision-making process.
summary: To provide a comprehensive understanding of the trained XGBoost model, this panel displays SHAP values averaged over all pH classes. This holistic view summarizes the global feature importance, allowing for an integrated assessment of how different input features influence the model's predictions across the entire dataset.

caption: Evolution of the energy band gap in the Co2TiGe full Heusler alloy as a function of applied uniform strain.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between uniform strain and the energy band gap for the Co2TiGe full Heusler alloy. The data demonstrates how structural deformation influences electronic properties, providing a clear profile of band gap variation across different strain levels as computed for this specific material system.

caption: Isolated internal cross-section extracted from the 3D reconstruction for detailed examination.
summary: The isolated internal cross-section is presented here, having been extracted from the 3D model following the cutting process. This view provides a clear, two-dimensional representation of the specimen's internal geometry, enabling accurate assessment and subsequent quantitative analysis of the structural features.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of Mo2WS6/NF recorded at varying scan rates from 20 to 100 mV s-1 within the potential range of 0.47 V to 0.57 V versus RHE.
summary: Non-Faraday cyclic voltammetry tests were conducted on Mo2WS6/NF at scan rates ranging from 20 to 100 mV s-1. These curves, measured between 0.47 V and 0.57 V versus RHE, demonstrate the electrochemical behavior of the catalyst, providing the necessary data to calculate the double layer capacitance for further surface area analysis.

caption: Open circuit potential (EOCP) evolution for the as-processed (AP) NAB alloy immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution over an extended duration.
summary: The EOCP curve for the AP-NAB alloy demonstrates the electrochemical stability of the material during prolonged exposure to a 3.5 wt% NaCl environment. This trend is consistent with EIS data, confirming the reliability of the electrochemical measurements in characterizing the corrosion behavior of the as-processed alloy.

caption: Total Sobol’ indices representing the combined influence of input parameters, incorporating both individual first-order effects and higher-order interactions between variables at multiple strain levels.
summary: The total Sobol’ indices shown here provide a comprehensive measure of parameter influence by accounting for both first-order effects and higher-order interactions within the machine learning model. These indices reveal how the collective sensitivity of the temperature-dependent crystal plasticity parameters on stress outputs changes as the material undergoes varying strain.

caption: Evolution of creep rupture life for GH984G alloy as a function of phosphorus content, showing an increase from 594 h to 1226 h as P concentration rises from 0 to 0.04 wt.% at 750 °C and 200 MPa.
summary: This panel illustrates the creep rupture life of GH984G alloy tested at 750 °C and 200 MPa. The data demonstrates a significant improvement in performance, with the rupture life increasing from 594 h to 1226 h as the phosphorus content is increased from 0 to 0.04 wt.%.

caption: In-situ DRIFTS spectra of In0.5Ni@SiO2 catalyst recorded in a methane atmosphere at 700 °C.
summary: This panel displays the in-situ DRIFTS spectra for the In0.5Ni@SiO2 catalyst under a methane atmosphere at 700 °C. Observations indicate that strong bands associated with gas-phase methane persist initially after the gas flow is stopped but disappear within one minute, while other spectral regions remain consistent with heating stage patterns.

caption: Structural configurations of HTAM, I-WP, and CFCC lattices modeled at a relative density of 0.50.
summary: Structural configurations for HTAM, I-WP, and CFCC are presented at a relative density of 0.50. These models are utilized in finite element analysis to assess how varying the relative density influences the mechanical properties and structural integrity of the different lattice designs compared to the optimized HTAM.

caption: Y–Z sectional reconstruction of the sintered TPMS structure.
summary: Y–Z sectional reconstruction of the sintered TPMS structure reveals the high density of the sintered ceramic. This cross-sectional analysis confirms that the material maintains structural integrity following the application of the predicted shrinkage adjustment model, demonstrating that the sintered geometry remains consistent with the intended design.

caption: Potential line profile analysis across the Mg-8Li-4Gd alloy surface, highlighting the potential difference between α-Mg and β-Li phases.
summary: Potential line profile analysis performed on the Mg-8Li-4Gd alloy surface quantifies the electrochemical contrast between phases. The data indicates a potential difference of approximately 130 mV between the α-Mg and β-Li phases, providing a precise measurement of the surface potential variation across the selected route.

caption: Magnetization M(T) of annealed ribbons under 5 mT and 5 T fields, featuring an inset showing thermal hysteresis at 245 K and a large magnetization difference of 44 A m2 kg-1 at 5 T.
summary: Annealed ribbons exhibit a distinct phase transition with thermal hysteresis in the M(T) curves at 245 K during heating and cooling cycles, as shown in the inset. At a 5 T magnetic field, a significant magnetization difference of 44 A m2 kg-1 is observed at the transition temperature.

caption: Depth profile of the wear track for the 4WC composite sample.
summary: The depth profile for the 4WC composite is shown here, detailing the vertical extent of the wear track. This measurement is part of the quantitative analysis used to evaluate how WC reinforcement levels affect the depth of abrasive wear tracks across the different composite samples tested in the study.

caption: SEM-EDS line scan analysis across the crack interface in as-built CM247LC, showing elemental intensity profiles.
summary: The SEM-EDS line scan analysis reveals the elemental distribution across the crack interface of the as-built CM247LC alloy. Experimental results indicate that the Hf element is significantly enriched at the crack interface, highlighting the chemical segregation behavior that occurs during the LPBF processing of this specific nickel-based superalloy.

caption: EDS integration spectra of the oxide scale, showing elemental composition peaks including a copper signal attributed to the FIB sample welding process on the copper mesh.
summary: The EDS integration spectrum provides the chemical composition of the oxide scale formed on the aluminide coating. A notable copper peak is present, which is identified as an artifact resulting from the FIB sample preparation process where the specimen was welded onto a copper mesh for analysis.

caption: Hot processing map showing η efficiency contours overlapped with the instability parameter ξ at a strain of 0.2.
summary: Representing the hot processing map at a strain of 0.2, this contour plot displays η efficiency values across deformation conditions. The shadowed regions highlight areas of potential instability where ξ < 0, providing critical guidance for optimizing processing parameters to avoid structural defects during the alloy deformation process.

caption: Elemental point scanning analysis of the interface, illustrating the distribution of chemical constituents across the SS316/V/Ti6Al4V junction.
summary: Elemental point scanning analysis provides insight into the chemical composition across the SS316/V/Ti6Al4V interface. This spectroscopic data confirms the distribution of elements, showing that the V side contains relatively less Fe, while the SS316 side contains more Ti, and the Ti content in the V layer is also higher.

caption: Atomic configuration of a screw dislocation in Fe-20Cr-25Ni alloy post-cascade simulation, displaying black-colored interstitial and vacancy defects determined by Wigner-Seitz analysis after filtering out the fcc lattice atoms.
summary: This MD snapshot reveals the atomic structure of a screw dislocation in Fe-20Cr-25Ni alloy following cascade simulation. The fcc-environment atoms are excluded to emphasize the black-colored interstitial and vacancy defects calculated via Wigner-Seitz analysis. These defects are observed forming loops or migrating into the dislocation, demonstrating the interaction between cascades and dislocations.

caption: Simulated grain structure in the central transverse cross-section of the melt pool at a maximum nucleation density of 10^11 m^-3.
summary: This panel displays the simulated grain structure within the central transverse cross-section of a melt pool, calculated using a maximum nucleation density of 10^11 m^-3. The simulation illustrates the initial grain morphology, providing a baseline for comparing how increasing nucleation density influences the resulting grain distribution and columnar-to-equiaxed transition.

caption: Load-displacement curves obtained from nanoindentation tests on LPBF-fabricated Nd-Fe-B magnets, illustrating the mechanical response across various laser scanning strategies.
summary: The load-displacement curves characterize the mechanical response of LPBF-built Nd-Fe-B magnets subjected to nanoindentation. These curves demonstrate the material's deformation behavior under localized loading, providing essential data to evaluate the mechanical integrity and performance of the magnets produced through different laser scanning strategies during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Fluorescence image of a 3D-printed denture resin base composite containing 15% microcapsules, demonstrating homogeneous spreading of the healing agent across the fracture surface.
summary: The fracture surface of the 15% microcapsule-loaded composite shows a significant improvement in healing agent distribution. The rhodamine B-labeled TEGDMA is clearly detected covering the entire fractured surface homogeneously, confirming that increasing the microcapsule content to 15% leads to a more pronounced and effective release of the healing agent.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the triple melted (TM) Ti–40Nb sample, showing an altered microstructure with elongated and coarse needle-shaped phases.
summary: The HAADF-STEM image of the triple melted (TM) Ti–40Nb sample demonstrates a distinct change in morphology compared to the SM condition. The microstructure is characterized by elongated and coarse needle-shaped phases. This observation is consistent with SEM data, confirming the impact of triple melting on the phase morphology of the alloy.

caption: Nucleation boundary plot illustrating the relationship between cooling rate and Sc content (wt.%) for primary Al3(Sc1-x,Zrx) phase formation.
summary: This diagram maps the nucleation boundary for primary Al3(Sc1-x,Zrx) precipitates as a function of cooling rate and Sc concentration. Results indicate that higher Sc content is required for nucleation at increased cooling rates. For LPBF-processed Scalmalloy with 0.7 wt.% Sc, primary precipitates form only at cooling rates below 2·10^-4 K/s.

caption: Comparison of strut dimensions for Cell 5R lattice specimens fabricated from ZrO2 and HAp, with a reference line at the design target of 260 μm.
summary: This box plot illustrates the distribution of strut dimensions for Cell 5R lattice structures composed of ZrO2 and HAp materials. The visualization highlights the variance in manufactured dimensions relative to the intended design specification of 260 μm, represented by the red line, allowing for a direct comparison between the two material types.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the L-DED processed specimen in the Y-orientation.
summary: This XRD pattern characterizes the phase composition of the L-DED processed build in the Y-orientation. Analysis of the diffraction data indicates that the phase composition remains consistent throughout the L-DED process, confirming that the manufacturing method does not induce detectable changes in the material's phase structure.

caption: Compositional path calibration for Ti60-Ti2AlNb dual alloys, illustrating transition zone widths of 12 mm (solid line) and 4 mm (dashed line) within the 700 °C isothermal section.
summary: This panel displays the isothermal cross section of the Ti-Al-Nb ternary phase diagram at 700 °C, calculated via Thermo-Calc. It specifically highlights compositional distributions for Ti60-Ti2AlNb dual alloys, comparing transition zone widths of 12 mm and 4 mm to calibrate the compositional path between the two alloy systems.
