caption: Micro-CT reconstructions of rabbit femoral defects at 6 and 12 weeks post-implantation, showing varying degrees of bone regeneration across the control, BHP, G@Met, and BHP/G@Met groups.
summary: Micro-CT imaging of rabbit femoral defects at 6 and 12 weeks reveals the extent of bone regeneration. The BHP/G@Met group demonstrates enhanced new bone formation compared to the control, BHP, and G@Met groups, confirming the superior regenerative capacity of the combined scaffold system in this specific animal model.

caption: SHAP beeswarm plot representing the averaged feature effects calculated over all classes for the neural network model.
summary: The averaged SHAP beeswarm plot provides a comprehensive overview of the neural network model's feature effects across all classes. By aggregating the contributions from each class, this visualization summarizes the overall influence of the input RGB channel features on the model's decision-making process during the classification task.

caption: Nanoindentation depth profile for the H240 composite coating sample containing 40% WC.
summary: The H240 composite coating, featuring 40% WC, is analyzed via this nanoindentation depth profile. The graph maps indentation locations relative to depth, with a dashed line indicating the transition from the coating to the substrate, providing a clear view of the mechanical indentation depth distribution for this specific sample.

caption: Young's modulus measurements displayed for the complete range of sample compositions.
summary: Young's modulus values are displayed for the complete range of sample compositions. This visualization highlights the stiffness trends observed across the different materials, allowing for a direct comparison of elastic properties as derived from the experimental testing and documented in the study's comprehensive data tables.

caption: Atomic configurations resulting from 10 MC steps per lattice site at 327, 471, and 575 °C.
summary: Row b presents the simulated atomic structures after 10 MC steps per lattice site. These snapshots demonstrate the progression of phase ordering at 327, 471, and 575 °C. The results confirm that nucleation kinetics vary significantly with temperature, showing advanced ordering at lower temperatures compared to the delayed nucleation observed at 575 °C.

caption: Bar chart displaying the length fraction of Coincident Site Lattice (CSL) boundaries with Σ values ranging from 3 to 19 for both as-received (AR) and heat-treated (HT) specimens.
summary: This bar chart quantifies the length fraction of special Coincident Site Lattice (CSL) boundaries, specifically those with Σ values between 3 and 19. The data provides a comparative analysis of these special boundary fractions for both as-received (AR) and heat-treated (HT) material specimens to evaluate microstructural evolution.

caption: Opening load ratio U as a function of normalized crack length a/W for WAAM specimen S4T, featuring crack growth oriented transversely to the deposition direction.
summary: Specimen S4T displays the relationship between the opening load ratio U and the normalized crack length a/W across Paris and near-threshold regimes. Near-threshold crack growth data is specifically highlighted, demonstrating that the opening load ratio variations track the load stepping behavior observed during the mechanical fatigue testing of the material.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map of AlSi9Cu3 alloy after T6 heat treatment, depicting the spatial arrangement of Si and Cu.
summary: The EDS map of the T6-treated AlSi9Cu3 alloy provides a visual representation of the elemental distribution of Si and Cu. This map confirms the significant microstructural modifications induced by the T6 heat treatment, showing how the distribution of these elements changes under higher temperature processing conditions.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of Au-NSps, M-NPs, and MP-NPs, highlighting the emergence and growth of the plasmonic peak.
summary: The UV-Vis spectra demonstrate the optical response of the nanoparticles. A distinct plasmonic peak appears at 534 nm following the first gold decoration step. Subsequent growth steps lead to increased absorption intensity within the 534–539 nm range, confirming the successful plasmonic tuning of the multicore MP-NPs.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of RR1000 superalloy cooled at 360 K min⁻¹, displaying the fine-scale γ′ precipitate microstructure.
summary: Representing the fastest cooling rate of 360 K min⁻¹, this dark-field TEM image reveals the resulting γ′ precipitate microstructure. Compositional analysis indicates that these fast-cooled samples exhibit much smaller compositional variations across the precipitates, consistent with the behavior observed at the 100 K min⁻¹ cooling rate.

caption: Pole figure map of the as-printed LPBF IN738LC superalloy showing the initial crystallographic texture.
summary: The pole figure map displays the crystallographic texture of the as-printed LPBF IN738LC superalloy. This visualization allows for the observation of texture changes in the material, serving as a reference point to evaluate how the grain orientation evolves during the creep process at 850 ℃/280 MPa.

caption: Interference fringes visualized when the system lacks vertical alignment.
summary: Lack of vertical alignment between the PLM and DMD pixels leads to the misaligned interference fringes shown in this projected image. This pattern illustrates the impact of pixel-level spatial errors on the resulting light field, confirming that the system is not currently optimized for perfect light path alignment.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the evaluation criteria applied to generated design variants, with weighting factors manually adjusted via Fusion 360's recommendation system.
summary: This radar chart visualizes the multi-criteria evaluation process used to assess various design variants. By manually adjusting the weighting of specific criteria within the Fusion 360 recommendation system, the researchers optimized the selection of the final design, ensuring that the chosen configuration aligns with the specific requirements of the application.

caption: Measured material density values plotted as a function of layer thickness, illustrating the influence of processing parameters on porosity.
summary: This plot displays material density as a function of layer thickness, evaluated using Archimedean density measurements across various energy inputs. The data highlights how layer thickness impacts porosity, while the included standard deviation bars demonstrate that process parameter optimization can effectively mitigate these effects to maintain high-quality lattice structures.

caption: Box plots illustrating the distribution of ellipticity (e) and area (A) of deposited melt spots as a function of laser focus position (ω), laser power (P), and exposure time (Δt).
summary: Box plots display the statistical distribution of melt spot ellipticity and area across varying laser processing parameters including focus position, power, and exposure time. The whiskers represent the range of data excluding outliers, while the colored boxes delineate the interquartile range, highlighting the median values for each experimental condition.

caption: Tabulated initial critical resolved shear stress values for various slip systems in Ti-6Al-4V and Zircaloy 4 alloys.
summary: Tabulated data presents the initial critical resolved shear stress values for specific slip systems in Ti-6Al-4V and Zircaloy 4. These values, sourced from Semiatin and Bieler (2001) and Gong et al. (2015), provide essential mechanical parameters for understanding the deformation resistance of these specific alloy systems under stress.

caption: Processed fluorescent image demonstrating background removal and droplet enhancement performed via Python and the OpenCV library.
summary: Processed fluorescent imaging is displayed, where background noise has been removed and droplet features have been enhanced for improved clarity. This computational refinement, performed using the Python OpenCV library, facilitates more accurate identification and subsequent analysis of the droplets within the dPCR experimental setup.

caption: Thermo-magnetization curves measured at an applied field of 0.01 T for HTHed specimens fabricated with an energy density of 238.1 J/mm3.
summary: Thermo-magnetization behavior of HTHed samples, processed with 80 W laser power, 550 mm/s scanning speed, and 0.02 mm hatch distance, is illustrated under a 0.01 T applied field. These curves characterize the magnetic response of the specimens as a function of temperature, providing the foundational data for identifying magnetic phase transitions.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra tracking the reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) over time using an L-type Pd/C catalytic reactor.
summary: This panel displays the UV-Vis spectra for the reduction of 4-NP catalyzed by an L-type Pd/C reactor. These spectral data points serve as the basis for determining the conversion versus time kinetics through linear fitting, illustrating the catalytic performance of the L-type reactor configuration during the reduction process.

caption: Structural interface matching for (110) Cu stimulated grains on a (001) Ni substrate.
summary: This atomic model illustrates the interface matching between (110) Cu stimulated grains and a (001) Ni substrate. Green balls represent Ni atoms in the stimulated grains, and blue balls represent Cu atoms in the substrate, demonstrating the crystalline plane alignment modeled for this specific Cu-Ni interface configuration.

caption: Comparative analysis of surface metrics and weight retention for substrates treated with different etchant types, contrasting PLA precursor solutions with NaOH.
summary: Comparing different etchant types, this plot illustrates how substrate weight and surface roughness are affected. Unlike NaOH, which causes significant weight loss, the PLA precursor solution preserves the surface morphology and maintains sample weight, as evidenced by the comparative statistical analysis of Ra and kurtosis values.

caption: Overview of the XYLON FF85 X-ray detection system utilized for non-destructive inspection and characterization of the printed samples.
summary: The XYLON FF85 X-ray detection system is shown as the equipment used for the inspection of the printed ceramic samples. This system enables the non-destructive analysis required to generate the three-dimensional reconstructions necessary for verifying the geometric accuracy of the sintered TPMS structures against the design model.

caption: FTIR spectrum of pure sodium carbonate displaying characteristic molecular vibrational absorption bands and a broad O–H stretching peak at 3360 cm⁻¹.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of sodium carbonate in panel a reveals characteristic absorption bands corresponding to its molecular structure. A notable broad peak at 3360 cm⁻¹ is identified, which is attributed to O–H stretching vibrations, confirming the presence of hydroxyl groups within the sodium carbonate sample structure.

caption: Durability test of the F-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 catalyst in 1.0 M KOH aqueous solution at a potential of 0.55 V.
summary: A durability test is conducted for the F-CNT@Fe2-Ni3 catalyst in a 1.0 M KOH aqueous solution at a constant potential of 0.55 V. This measurement provides critical information regarding the long-term stability and operational lifespan of the catalyst under sustained electrochemical conditions.

caption: Evolution of average helium cavity size as a function of annealing time for 3D-HEA, Arc-HEA, and 304 SS, compared against an empirical model from Ref. [26].
summary: This line graph illustrates the growth kinetics of helium cavities in 3D-HEA, Arc-HEA, and 304 SS during in-situ annealing. Starting from an initial size of approximately 1–2 nm after room temperature irradiation, the data tracks cavity size progression over time, with an empirical formula from Ref. [26] provided as a reference.

caption: Concentration of solute B as a function of radiation dose for binary and ternary A-B-C alloys with varying B-C binding energies.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of solute B concentration versus radiation dose. Comparing binary alloys to ternary alloys with different B-C binding energies, the data shows that increasing the B-C binding energy significantly improves the retention of B atoms within the simulation cell compared to the binary A-B system.

caption: Representative electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data showing the evolution of passive layer formation on the titanium alloy surface over a 7-day immersion period in PBS.
summary: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data tracks the formation and stability of passive layers on the titanium alloy surface. By monitoring the impedance response over a 7-day period in a simulated physiological environment, the study assesses the long-term electrochemical stability and passivity of the material under continuous immersion conditions.

caption: Raman spectra of ZTA samples sintered at various temperatures with a 2 h holding time.
summary: Raman spectra of ZTA samples sintered at different temperatures under a holding time of 2 h are presented. These patterns provide insight into the phase composition of the material after the specified thermal processing duration, serving as a baseline for comparison with samples subjected to longer sintering times.

caption: Ratio of D-peak to G-peak intensities plotted as a function of pressure and laser power (LP) for carbon fibres, representing a Raman spectral phase diagram.
summary: This panel displays a Raman spectral phase diagram generated by calculating the ratio of D-peak to G-peak intensities for individual carbon fibres. The plot illustrates the structural evolution of the fibres across varying pressure and laser power conditions, providing a quantitative metric for characterizing the material's phase state.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the intermetallic reinforcement phase showing the Heusler phase with an overlaid selected area aperture.
summary: This bright-field TEM micrograph displays the intermetallic reinforcement phase within the CCA72 alloy. The image features an overlaid selected area aperture used to isolate the Heusler phase for further structural analysis, confirming the presence of this secondary phase after homogenization at 1343 K for 5 hours.

caption: Additive Manufacturing Suitability (AMS) radar chart comparing performance metrics for pure Mo and alloyed Mo8Re powders.
summary: Panel b displays a radar graph that visualizes the various rheological properties used to calculate the Additive Manufacturing Suitability (AMS) value for pure Mo and alloyed Mo8Re powders. This chart synthesizes multiple performance metrics, allowing for a direct comparison of the suitability of these two powders for additive manufacturing processes.

caption: t-SNE visualization of the ResPFSN-type2 model feature space showing a tight distribution of sample points with exceptional class separation and minimal overlap.
summary: The ResPFSN-type2 model t-SNE plot exhibits a tight distribution of sample points with exceptional separation between classes. With minimal overlap observed, this model exemplifies superior performance in distinguishing defect classes compared to all other models tested, confirming its effectiveness in high-dimensional feature representation and classification tasks.

caption: Comparison of Young's modulus and strength for Bouligand structures against reported values for composites, aerogels, and porous ceramics, demonstrating the enhanced mechanical performance of the Bouligand design.
summary: This plot compares the mechanical properties, specifically Young's modulus and strength, of the Bouligand structure against various reported porous ceramics, aerogels, and composite materials. The comparison reveals that the Bouligand structure exhibits a more pronounced advantage in mechanical performance, confirming its superior strength and stiffness relative to existing material benchmarks.

caption: Current density versus potential curves for ZCIS quantum dots modified with MPA, TGA, and DDT surface ligands.
summary: This panel displays the current density versus potential curves for ZCIS quantum dots. The measurements compare the performance of devices prepared with different surface ligands, specifically MPA, TGA, and DDT. These curves illustrate the electrical response of the ZCIS-based solar cells under the specified ligand exchange conditions.

caption: EBSD IPF map of heat-treated Ti-27Nb-6Ta processed with parameter set 8 (EA = 2.78 J/mm2), viewed perpendicular to the build direction and oriented along the transverse direction.
summary: This EBSD map illustrates the transverse direction view of Ti-27Nb-6Ta processed at 2.78 J/mm2. The high energy input promotes a sharp texture and epitaxial growth. These results, supported by X-ray diffraction, confirm the significant impact of processing parameters on the final grain orientation and the development of a strong crystallographic texture.

caption: Time-lapse fluorescent and optical microscopic images showing the migration and distribution of GFP-HUVECs over a 12-day period following the transfer of the coated microgel onto a GelMA surface.
summary: Fluorescent and optical microscopic images track the behavior of GFP-HUVECs for 12 days after transferring the microgel to a GelMA surface. The cells were observed not only around the microgel but also in surrounding areas lacking microgel, indicating that the skin layer had become vascularized during the culture period.

caption: Representative dilatometry curve showing dilatation as a function of temperature at a cooling rate of 40 C/s, with critical transformation temperatures marked 1–6.
summary: Dilatometry curve for a 40 C/s cooling rate demonstrates the material's dimensional response during thermal cycling. Critical transformation temperatures, labeled 1 through 6, are identified based on slope changes in the curve. These points provide the necessary data to characterize the martensitic transformation and construct the extended CCT diagram.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot of the inverse absolute temperature versus the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of stress, enabling the determination of activation energy Q.
summary: Panel d illustrates the relationship between T −1 and ln[sinh( ασ )]. The activation energy Q is calculated from the mean slope of these plots by substituting related experimental data, which is essential for characterizing the temperature-dependent deformation mechanisms observed during the mechanical testing of the material.

caption: Nyquist plots comparing BAC and CHBAC devices, with an inset highlighting high-frequency impedance spectra.
summary: Nyquist plots for BAC and CHBAC devices reveal that the CHBAC device exhibits a more prominent semicircle at high to mid frequencies. The inset shows that the CHBAC device has a smaller intercept compared to the BAC device, indicating superior electrical conductivity for the CHBAC configuration.

caption: Pseudobinary section of the Fe–Cr–Ni ternary system illustrating phase stability regions.
summary: This panel displays the pseudobinary section of the Fe–Cr–Ni ternary diagram. It serves as a foundational reference for understanding the phase stability and equilibrium conditions relevant to the alloy system investigated in the study, providing a basis for interpreting the solidification behavior of the welds.

caption: Pareto plot of standardized effects for CGP-processed Al 3105 sheets, specifically illustrating the influence of lubrication conditions on material toughness.
summary: This Pareto plot displays the standardized effects of CGP variables on the toughness of Al 3105 sheets. The analysis reveals that lubrication has a negligible influence on toughness. Consequently, researchers suggest that omitting die lubrication during the CGP process could effectively increase production rates and reduce overall manufacturing costs.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to the region shown in panel (a), confirming the [110] FCC twin orientation.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the region shown in panel (a) confirms the crystallographic orientation of the FCC twins. By analyzing this diffraction data along the [110] FCC zone axis, the presence and structural characteristics of the deformation twins are verified at the nanoscale.

caption: Short-term OCP behavior of Ni-Cu-P during the first 30 seconds of the conversion treatment.
summary: The OCP curve for Ni-Cu-P is displayed for the first 30 seconds of the conversion treatment. Similar to the Ni-Fe-P sample, this material does not show the initial potential drop linked to oxide film dissolution, indicating that the surface characteristics differ from those observed in the MP sample.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the as-built Ni-Mn-Ga “O” alloy showing a high density of dislocations.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the as-built Ni-Mn-Ga “O” alloy reveals a significant presence of dislocations within the microstructure. These structural defects, highlighted by white arrows in the micrograph, are characteristic of the as-built state, providing clear evidence of the material's internal deformation and microstructural state following the fabrication process.

caption: UV/vis absorbance spectra and corresponding photographic evidence of DPPH solution degradation after 120 minutes.
summary: UV/vis spectroscopy tracks the reduction in DPPH concentration, indicated by changes in absorbance spectra following 120 minutes of treatment. The inset photograph provides visual confirmation of the color change in the DPPH solution, directly correlating the optical data with the successful degradation of the radical species.

caption: Ashby plot comparing tensile yield strength versus ductility for DED-processed IN718 and IN718/TiB2 composites against literature data for various AM processes, cast, and wrought materials.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the mechanical performance of DED-processed IN718 and IN718/TiB2 composites by plotting tensile yield strength against ductility. The data includes comparisons with literature values for IN718 processed via DED, L-PBF, EBM, and conventional cast/wrought methods, with all tests conducted parallel to the build direction.

caption: Geometric phase analysis (GPA) map illustrating the εxx strain distribution across the atomic structure of the deformation twins.
summary: Geometric phase analysis (GPA) mapping of the εxx strain distribution reveals the localized stress concentration within the deformation twins and the surrounding gamma matrix. The data indicates that DTs effectively hinder dislocation motion, as evidenced by the specific strain patterns observed at the twin boundaries in the CR40-DA specimen.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) heat flow curves for the as-built GH4099 Ni-based superalloy during heating and cooling cycles.
summary: This DSC analysis characterizes the thermal behavior of the as-built GH4099 Ni-based superalloy. The plot displays heat flow as a function of temperature, capturing the thermal response during both heating and cooling processes. These measurements provide essential data regarding phase transformations and thermal stability prior to any subsequent heat treatment.

caption: Pure aluminum (Al) elastic property distribution showing homogeneous 2D and 3D characteristics.
summary: Pure aluminum exhibits moderate anisotropy with an index of 0.1435 and high ductility, characterized by a B/G ratio of 2.32. These mechanical properties are visualized through homogeneous 2D and 3D distributions, confirming the material's intrinsic structural stability and uniform elastic behavior under the studied conditions.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for the line build specimen, highlighting intensity variations across axial/build and transverse directions.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for the line build specimen are presented, covering both axial/build and transverse directions. The line build exhibits a relatively stronger presence of (311) planes compared to the spot build. These patterns reveal the dominant presence of {200} orientation, resembling a single crystal, with each run representing different loads.

caption: ERR values measured from G15 DCB samples, where solid and dashed horizontal lines denote the mean ERR and mean peak ERR, respectively, amidst the extrinsic bridging data points.
summary: G15 DCB samples show distinct ERR values, with mean ERR and mean peak ERR values marked by solid and dashed lines. The data points, reflecting extrinsic bridging, confirm the mechanical toughness characteristics of the G15 samples, consistent with the observed correlations between peak ERR and extrinsic OC bridging.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns (λ = 1.28 Å) of the deuteride phases, confirming the adoption of an FCC lattice structure consistent with the hydride phases observed in SR-XRD.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns obtained at a wavelength of 1.28 Å for the deuterated samples provide further evidence that the formed hydride phases adopt an FCC lattice. These results corroborate the structural findings obtained from synchrotron X-ray diffraction on the corresponding hydrogenated alloy phases.

caption: Comparison of photoluminescence spectra for neat HDPE polymer across multiple recycling cycles, acquired under 254 nm excitation to evaluate the impact of thermal oxidation and chain breakage on optical properties.
summary: Spectra comparing neat HDPE polymer samples across all recycling cycles are displayed. Thermal oxidation during the recycling process induces chain breakage, which significantly alters the molecular structure and mechanical properties of the polymer, as evidenced by the variations in the photoluminescence emission profiles observed under 254 nm excitation.

caption: Comparison of average microhardness values across different regions and testing directions within the y-z plane specimen.
summary: This panel compares the average microhardness distribution across various regions and directions in the y-z plane. The results indicate a uniform state with no significant variations in hardness values. Measurements consistently fluctuate between 200 and 215 HV 0.1, demonstrating structural homogeneity across the tested regions and directions of the specimen.

caption: Full XPS survey spectrum of the composite ceramic sample pyrolyzed at 1000 ℃, showing the presence of Si, O, C, N, and B elements.
summary: The full XPS survey spectrum of the composite ceramic sample pyrolyzed at 1000 ℃ is presented. The analysis confirms the presence of five distinct elements within the material: silicon, oxygen, carbon, nitrogen, and boron. These elements were subsequently analyzed individually to determine their specific chemical bonding states within the ceramic matrix.

caption: Dark-field TEM image obtained using the (−110)β // (002)α″ diffraction spot, which selectively highlights the β-phase matrix and a specific variant of the α″ martensite.
summary: This dark-field TEM image, acquired at higher magnification using the (−110)β // (002)α″ diffraction spot, provides selective contrast. It effectively highlights both the β-phase matrix and the specific variant of the α″ martensite indexed in the diffraction pattern, while keeping other α″ variants in dark contrast.

caption: Atom probe tomography ion maps for Fe and Nb, highlighting γ′ precipitates and the δ/η phase, with 5 at. % Nb isoconcentration surfaces defining the phase boundaries.
summary: Atom probe tomography ion maps for Fe and Nb visualize the spatial distribution of γ′ precipitates and the δ/η phase within the bimodal sample. The inclusion of 5 at. % Nb isoconcentration surfaces effectively delineates the phase boundaries, providing a 3D perspective of the chemical architecture of the material's microstructure.

caption: Peak-to-peak stress values measured during cyclic loading for reference specimens and ACCCs fabricated from SHCC mixtures.
summary: Peak-to-peak stress during cyclic loading is plotted for three replicates of each mixture. The reference specimen demonstrates a lower peak-to-peak stress of 0.0124 ± 0.0004 MPa compared to ACCCs produced from SHCC mixtures. Error bars represent the standard deviation across the tested replicates, confirming the observed performance differences between the materials.

caption: Comparison of experimental composition profiles with NI (solid line) and MK (dashed line) model-simulated diffusion paths for diffusion couples annealed at 1023 K.
summary: Experimental composition profiles for diffusion couples annealed at 1023 K are compared against model-simulated diffusion paths. The NI method results are represented by solid lines, while the MK method results are shown as dashed lines. These simulations demonstrate the diffusion behavior of Ag and Ni in solid solutions.

caption: Convergence rate of the OAA optimization process plotted against the number of iterations.
summary: The convergence rate of the OAA optimization process is plotted against the number of iterations. The algorithm demonstrates rapid convergence, achieving stability within the first 10 iterations of the drone design parameter optimization. This rapid performance indicates an efficient search process for the specified design parameters.

caption: Mo 3d XPS spectrum showing Mo(0) at 227.1 eV and oxidized Mo species at 232.0 eV.
summary: The Mo 3d XPS spectrum indicates the presence of molybdenum in two states. Metallic Mo(0) is detected at 227.1 eV, while oxidized molybdenum species, corresponding to oxidation states IV, V, or VI, are identified at 232.0 eV for the Mo 3d(5/2) region.

caption: CCT diagram simulation for a steel specimen with a 50 μm grain size at a 900 °C peak temperature.
summary: This CCT diagram simulation illustrates the predicted phase transformation behavior for a steel specimen with a 50 μm grain size at a 900 °C peak temperature. Numerical modeling using JMatPro software incorporates specific grain size inputs to predict microstructural evolution, with red arrows marking reference cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s.

caption: High-speed camera capture of the molding process, highlighting sputtering and fume generation at the laser irradiation point.
summary: Captured during the fabrication process, this high-speed image reveals the dynamic behavior at the laser irradiation point. The visual data clearly shows the presence of sputtering and fumes, providing critical insight into the physical phenomena occurring during the rod-leading molding method as the laser interacts with the material.

caption: Three-dimensional Vickers hardness map correlating local mechanical properties with microstructural evolution in the Ti-alloy sample.
summary: This three-dimensional Vickers hardness map provides a spatial correlation between mechanical hardness values and the underlying microstructural evolution of the material. By highlighting distinct regions of high and low E 0 * values, the map effectively visualizes how microstructural variations influence the mechanical performance across the analyzed sample volume.

caption: Atomic configuration of a single HEA crystal subjected to a heat and quench simulation using the Cantor interatomic potential.
summary: This panel displays the atomic configuration of a single HEA crystal following a heat and quench simulation using the Cantor interatomic potential. Calculations of the glassy state's average potential energy reveal an excess energy of 30 meV relative to the crystalline reference, which is significantly lower than DFT-predicted values.

caption: Predicted evolution of mean diameter and number density for 1 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles in Sample 4 under linear cooling to 1690 K.
summary: This plot illustrates the simulated growth kinetics of 1 wt% Y2O3 nanoparticles within an alloy matrix. Under a linear cooling profile reaching the melting point of 1690 K, the model tracks the simultaneous changes in particle mean diameter and number density, providing insight into the nanoparticle evolution during solidification processing.

caption: Hydrostatic residual stress magnitudes along the edge and centre scan paths as a function of build height.
summary: Hydrostatic residual stress distributions are presented for both edge and centre scan paths. The data indicates an increasingly compressive behavior as the build height increases. These findings, derived from neutron diffraction, provide a comprehensive view of the internal stress state across the build geometry in relation to the scan paths.

caption: Latent space representation of virtual raster melt experiments for printed cubes with widths ranging from 15 to 23 mm, illustrating thermal response variability induced by random data augmentation.
summary: This latent space visualization maps the thermal response of printed cubes varying in width from 15 to 23 mm. The distribution highlights the impact of random data augmentation on the model's latent representation, incorporating all training data to demonstrate how geometric variations influence the simulated thermal behavior of the printed structures.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image of the LPBF 316L steel interface after exposure to LBE at 500 °C for 3393 h.
summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging reveals the interfacial structure of LPBF 316L steel following long-term exposure to LBE at 500 °C. This high-magnification micrograph provides a clear view of the atomic arrangement at the interface, serving as a baseline for analyzing the structural integrity and potential segregation phenomena within the material.

caption: Microhardness distribution profile of the Ti–Nb–Cr–V–Ni alloy deposit, illustrating the variation in hardness values across the deposited height.
summary: The microhardness distribution of the Ti–Nb–Cr–V–Ni deposit is presented, highlighting the mechanical properties across the deposited structure. Measurements indicate that the intermediate layer at a height of 0 mm exhibits a hardness of 517 Hv, characterized by significant variability and a high error range due to molten pool formation.

caption: Immunofluorescence imaging of CD31 (PECAM-1) expression in HUVECs, with relative fluorescence intensity quantified across OS, OS+β-TCP, and OS conditions.
summary: Immunofluorescence microscopy highlights the network formation and proliferation of HUVECs through CD31 expression. The results demonstrate that network development is most prominent in samples containing only OS spheroids, whereas the presence of β-TCP particles correlates with the least pronounced network development and proliferation of endothelial cells after five days.

caption: Surface density of states for the bimetallic NiZn(100) surface, highlighting the d-band centre position relative to the Fermi level.
summary: The surface density of states for the bimetallic NiZn(100) surface is depicted with the d-band centre marked by a red line. Consistent with other NiZn surfaces, the d-band centre of Ni and Zn atoms has shifted closer to the Fermi level, shown as a dashed black line, versus monometallic surfaces.

caption: Atomic model of a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell representing the primitive unit cell of the Cr30Fe2.5Ni alloy.
summary: The atomic structure of the Cr30Fe2.5Ni alloy is illustrated using a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell of its primitive unit cell. This structural model is utilized in DFT calculations to analyze the role of increased chromium content on the lattice parameters and mechanical moduli of the alloy.

caption: PND Rietveld refinement profile for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 310 K, displaying the experimental fit and difference plot.
summary: PND refinement for Mn0.68Ni0.68Fe0.64Si0.95Al0.05 at 310 K is depicted. The experimental data are shown as black dots, while the red line represents calculated intensities and blue lines show the difference. This measurement, combined with SR-PXD, circumvents low contrast issues between Fe and Ni to determine site occupancies.

caption: In situ SANS scattering curves for sample VB81, previously fatigue-cycled at 800 °C, during a thermal cycle of RT-700-800 °C-RT.
summary: Sample VB81 was fatigue-cycled at 800 °C for approximately 6 hours and subsequently subjected to in situ SANS heating at 700 and 800 °C. The scattering curves demonstrate that no new precipitate formation occurs at these temperatures, contrasting with the behavior observed in the undeformed and 900 °C cycled samples.

caption: Voltage output comparison of T-TENG devices featuring four distinct 3D-printed surface patterns (gyroid, zig-zag, grid, and lines) of PP on conductive fabric tested against EcoFlex.
summary: This panel compares the voltage output of T-TENG devices fabricated with varying 3D-printed surface patterns, including gyroid, zig-zag, grid, and lines. The data demonstrates that these surface geometries significantly influence the electrical output, with the line pattern providing more consistent contact compared to the more complex gyroid and grid designs.

caption: Temperature versus incubation time plot for competing phases in Ti-37 at% Al alloy, showing crossing points at Tβ-α and Tα-γ.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between temperature and incubation time for competing phases in Ti-37 at% Al alloy. Two crossing points at Tβ-α and Tα-γ indicate that the β phase is primary above Tβ-α, the α phase is primary between Tβ-α and Tα-γ, and the γ phase is primary below Tα-γ.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plot for the four samples, where the ST and ST + AT samples achieve impedance values reaching 10^5 Ω cm^2 in the low-frequency range.
summary: The Bode impedance magnitude plot reveals that the ST and ST + AT samples reach impedance values of 10^5 Ω cm^2 in the low-frequency range. These high impedance values indicate that these specific samples successfully form a dense and stable passivation film characterized by high capacitance properties.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the as-received Al 7075 sample, highlighting the high-density distribution of precipitates within the alloy microstructure.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image provides a high-contrast view of the as-received Al 7075 sample. It confirms the presence of a high density of precipitates, consistent with the bright-field TEM observations, showing their distribution throughout the alloy microstructure.

caption: Dilatometric cooling curves from 1100 °C for SPS-sintered AFMAR-10-10, AFMAR-10-13, and AFMAR-12-14 alloys without carbon additions.
summary: This dilatometry plot displays the cooling behavior of three SPS-sintered alloys from 1100 °C. AFMAR-10-10 exhibits both Ms and Mf transformation temperatures. AFMAR-10-13 displays only an Ms temperature, while AFMAR-12-14 shows no evidence of martensitic transformation, highlighting distinct phase transformation characteristics among the three alloy compositions during cooling.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph highlighting austenite particles with rod and block morphologies dispersed within the lath martensite phase.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph reveals the presence of austenite particles within the lath martensite matrix of the AD_MS250 specimen. These particles exhibit distinct morphologies, appearing as both rods and blocks. The dark-field imaging technique effectively isolates the austenite phase, allowing for the clear visualization of these specific structural features.

caption: Temperature-dependent self-diffusion coefficients of Pd40Cu30Ni10P20 metallic glass, comparing NEP-calculated values derived from viscosity coefficients against experimental data from literature.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the self-diffusion coefficients of Pd40Cu30Ni10P20 alloys across a temperature range of 1200 K to 900 K. It highlights the agreement between calculated diffusion values derived from NEP-based viscosity coefficients and previously measured experimental data, demonstrating the reliability of the computational approach in predicting transport properties in this alloy system.

caption: Loss modulus (E″) curves for CP-PLA composites with varying CP additions, showing the influence of filler content on viscoelastic behavior.
summary: This panel displays the loss modulus curves for CP-PLA composites with different CP additions. The experimental results indicate that the maximum loss modulus follows the specific order of CP15-PLA > CP10-PLA > CP5-PLA, demonstrating that increasing the CP filler content significantly enhances the viscoelastic energy dissipation properties of the composite material.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PEB106-i synthesized with one equivalent of BnOH, revealing a mixture of end-chain groups including species [A], benzyloxide residues [C], and ethylene glycol units [D].
summary: In the presence of one equivalent of BnOH, the MALDI-TOF spectrum for PEB106-i reveals a complex mixture of end-chain groups. The identified species include structure [A], benzyloxide residues [C], and a minor fraction terminated by an ethylene glycol unit [D], which indicates that transesterification occurred during the polymerization process.

caption: TEM image of 2Ni steel at 5% engineering strain, highlighting the emergence of (1-11) slip bands.
summary: At 5% engineering strain, the microstructure of 2Ni steel is characterized by the initial formation of slip bands. Specifically, panel a displays the appearance of (1-11) slip bands, marking the onset of deformation-induced substructural evolution within the material as it undergoes mechanical loading.

caption: Comparison of relative density for as-printed and post-processed IN738LC samples, showing an increase from 98.86% to 99.86% following the LIH treatment.
summary: This bar chart compares the relative density of the IN738LC superalloy before and after LIH post-processing. The data shows a measurable improvement in density, increasing from 98.86% to 99.86%, which serves as quantitative evidence of the crack-healing effect achieved through the applied post-processing treatment.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of pre-osteoblast cells cultured on 3D-printed nanocomposites (PLACTIVE, SN, Mg, and SM) over 7 days, showing live cells in green and dead cells in red.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of pre-osteoblast cells cultured on 3D-printed nanocomposites (PLACTIVE, SN, Mg, and SM) over 7 days, showing live cells in green and dead cells in red. This cytotoxicity assay demonstrates that the nanocomposite materials support cell viability, as no significant cell toxicity was observed throughout the seven-day experimental period.

caption: Minimal surface geometry enclosed within a pentagonal prism featuring tunnels directed toward its edges (E).
summary: This minimal surface is constrained within a pentagonal prism, with tunnels oriented toward the edges (E) of the prism. This specific geometric arrangement demonstrates the boundary method's capability to produce varied tunnel configurations, which are essential for the subsequent construction of the aperiodic E minimal surface.

caption: Energy filtered elemental map of Al distribution in the Al83.5Ni8.0Sm6.5Pb2.0 alloy ribbon.
summary: The energy filtered elemental map for Aluminum shows its distribution across the microstructure of the melt-spun ribbon. Observations indicate that the central nanocrystal, identified as a Pb-rich phase, also contains some Aluminum, confirming the presence of Al within the nanocrystalline region of the alloy.

caption: Full solar spectrum transmission curves comparing halogen lamp-SI detector measurements against full solar spectrum integration, demonstrating a 6% overestimation of τe when using τv.
summary: Full solar spectrum transmission curves are compared using halogen lamp-SI detector measurements and full solar spectrum integration. The analysis reveals that spectral averaging based on measured visible transmission results in a 6% overestimation of solar transmission, highlighting the importance of using the full solar spectrum for accurate material characterization.

caption: Low-magnification cross-sectional view of a PLA-CF filament following a tensile test, revealing internal structural voids.
summary: This low-magnification optical micrograph displays the cross-section of a PLA-CF filament after undergoing a tensile test. The image highlights the presence of several internal voids within the filament structure, which are known to act as sites for stress concentration and potential brittle failure during mechanical loading.

caption: Wang-Raj (WR) method plot based on the logarithmic derivative of the densification rate, providing an independent linear fit estimate of the activation energy at 357 kJ/mol.
summary: The Wang-Raj approach provides an independent method for estimating the activation energy of the sintering process. Through linear fitting of the logarithmic derivative of the densification rate, the analysis yields an activation energy of 357 kJ/mol, which complements the results obtained from the Master Sintering Curve analysis.

caption: Transition of the capillary bridge from Type I to Type II as the particle detaches from the meniscus, facilitating the formation and stabilization of a growing particle chain.
summary: As the particle detaches from the meniscus, the initial Type I capillary bridge elongates and transforms into a Type II interparticle bridge. This transition allows the bridge to stretch and stabilize the growing chain, effectively enabling the continuous formation of particle chains through the controlled overcoming of the capillary barrier.

caption: Polar plot comparing root mean square error (RMSE) values for PEC1, PEC2, and 18 literature-based optimization methods applied to the PHOTOWATT-PWP 201 solar module, where radial distance represents RMSE magnitude and each axis corresponds to a specific method.
summary: This polar plot evaluates the estimation accuracy of PEC1 and PEC2 models against 18 literature methods for the PHOTOWATT-PWP 201 solar module. PEC1 and PEC2 are represented by solid magenta and dashed black lines, respectively. The results demonstrate that the proposed models achieve superior accuracy compared to all other literature approaches.

caption: Near-threshold fatigue crack growth rate plotted against effective stress intensity factor range for WAAM specimens S3L and S4T at a stress ratio of R = 0.1.
summary: This plot displays the near-threshold fatigue crack growth behavior for WAAM specimens S3L and S4T tested at a stress ratio of R = 0.1. The data represents closure-corrected results, providing a baseline for comparing crack growth rates in longitudinal and transverse orientations relative to the WAAM deposition direction.

caption: Dark field TEM image of the F25 specimen captured under a two-beam diffraction condition, with the g-vector indicated by an arrow.
summary: Complementary dark field TEM imaging was employed to characterize the nature of the stacking faults observed in the F25 alloy. This specific dark field micrograph was acquired under a two-beam diffraction condition, with the g-vector orientation marked by an arrow to facilitate detailed analysis of the fault structures.

caption: Pareto chart illustrating the standardised effects of process parameters on the layer width (wL) at a significance level of α = 0.05.
summary: This Pareto chart displays the standardised effects of various process parameters on the layer width (wL) with a significance threshold of α = 0.05. Regression analysis indicates that spraying distance significantly influences layer width, as larger distances increase material dispersion prior to impact, thereby broadening the resulting layer dimensions.

caption: Global Warming Potential (GWO) values for 1 m³ of 3D-printed concrete across various mixture designs.
summary: This bar chart presents the Global Warming Potential (GWO) for 1 m³ of 3D-printed concrete, analyzed using OpenLCA software. The data provides a comparative view of environmental impacts across different mixture designs, with trends in these indicators remaining consistent with the other environmental metrics presented in the figure.

caption: Phase-field simulation mapping the distribution of the β-Si phase near the melt pool boundary.
summary: This panel displays a phase-field simulation result focusing on the β-Si phase distribution within the melt pool boundary region. The visualization provides a computational representation of the sub-grain microstructure, serving as a baseline for comparing experimental observations and evaluating the accuracy of the predictive modeling approach used in the study.

caption: Polarization scans of as-built and mechanically polished side surfaces from the SLM280 machine, operated at a different site than the SLM280(b) unit.
summary: Data from the SLM280 machine, which shares the same model as the SLM280(b) but operates at a different site, are shown for as-built and mechanically polished side surfaces. These results confirm that surface finishing, regardless of the machine or build orientation, consistently improves corrosion performance and eliminates metastable pitting events in the potentiodynamic scans.

caption: Second arc shape configuration of the SCA observed during CV power supply operation.
summary: The second arc shape of the SCA is shown under CV power supply conditions. Consistent with the hybrid state behavior, the IWA and PMA remain closely coupled, illustrating the consistent arc morphology maintained throughout the operational sequence as the system transitions through different arc states.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curve illustrating the total metal loading of the G/Pt 54–Ni 46 electrocatalyst.
summary: The total metal loading of the prepared G/Pt–Ni electrocatalyst is determined through thermogravimetric analysis. This TGA curve provides a quantitative assessment of the catalyst composition, serving as a primary method to evaluate the thermal stability and metal content of the G/Pt 54–Ni 46 material synthesized for electrochemical applications.

caption: Dark-field micrograph of precipitate-strengthened 725 Ni-base alloy after 150 dpa dual ion irradiation, displaying faulted dislocation loops.
summary: Precipitate-strengthened 725 Ni-base alloy subjected to 150 dpa dual ion irradiation shows faulted dislocation loops in this dark-field rel-rod micrograph. The inverted intensity highlights these defects, which were observed in all alloys following irradiation. This structural feature is characteristic of the radiation damage sustained by the material.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of in-situ alloyed 20Mn12Al with an inserted FFT pattern highlighting distinct B2 and L21 ordered structures.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the 20Mn12Al alloy reveals the microstructure of the material. The inserted Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) pattern provides critical crystallographic information, identifying the presence of distinct B2 (blue) and L21 (orange) ordered phases within the ferrite matrix, confirming the alloy's complex structural composition.

caption: Representative unit cell geometry utilized for the mesh generation of the burner.
summary: This panel illustrates the specific unit cell geometry utilized for the mesh generation of the 3D printed burner. The burner design, which incorporates this unit cell, features a porous area of 50 by 50 mm and a thickness of 25 mm, defining the fundamental repeating structural element.

caption: False colour representation derived from the initial AOLP image, highlighting spatial variations in fibre orientation.
summary: A false colour image is generated from the raw AOLP data to visualize fibre orientation patterns. This processing step transforms the polarisation information into a clear, interpretable map, facilitating the identification of structural features and orientation distributions across the observed fibre sample.

caption: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO model at 2 T magnetic induction intensity.
summary: Pairwise multicomponent short-range order parameters for the high CSRO system are depicted at 2 T. The analysis focuses on the seven chemical order types, demonstrating the structural stability and evolution of the high CSRO configuration when exposed to a moderate magnetic field during the Monte Carlo simulation process.

caption: Line EDX analysis profile across the bcc precipitates, with the corresponding SEM image showing the scan path overlaid at the bottom.
summary: Line EDX profile analysis was performed across the bcc precipitates to determine their chemical composition. The results reveal that these precipitates are significantly enriched with Ta and Nb elements. The scan path is clearly indicated by the overlay on the accompanying SEM image of the 60-minute sample.

caption: Bright-field STEM micrograph of an as-deposited 20 at% Ag EHD-RP sample.
summary: Presented here is a bright-field STEM micrograph of an as-deposited 20 at% Ag EHD-RP sample. This visualization documents the initial structural characteristics of the EHD-RP processed material, providing essential data for comparing the effects of different deposition techniques on the final microstructure after subsequent dealloying procedures.

caption: Temperature-dependent low-field AC magnetic susceptibility curves for the unidirectional melting strategy (UMS) sample, measured at scan vector rotations of 0°, 45°, and 90°, with an inset highlighting characteristic temperatures T M, T A, T C, and the transformation hysteresis width Δ T hys.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent AC magnetic susceptibility for the UMS sample across three scan vector rotations. The inset provides critical transformation temperatures and the hysteresis width. The constant Δ T hys across these conditions suggests a uniform level of chemical homogeneity within the unidirectionally melted material structure.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing the electrochemical corrosion behavior of 304ss and HEA coatings.
summary: This panel displays the potentiodynamic polarization curves for 304ss and HEA coatings. These curves are used to evaluate the electrochemical corrosion resistance of the materials, providing a direct comparison of their performance under corrosive conditions to determine which coating offers superior protection against degradation in the tested environment.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrating the electrochemical corrosion response of LPBF-fabricated specimens when tested in 3.5 wt% and 0.1 M NaCl solutions.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves are presented for the LPBF-fabricated specimens to characterize their corrosion resistance. The data, obtained from testing in 3.5 wt% and 0.1 M NaCl solutions, provides insight into the electrochemical behavior and degradation kinetics of the fabricated materials when exposed to these distinct saline environments.

caption: Cell scatter plot showing UMAP dimensional reduction by lineage, with a specific focus on the endoderm lineage and UiPSCs on the right.
summary: This scatter plot utilizes UMAP dimensional reduction to categorize cells by lineage. By isolating the endoderm lineage and UiPSCs, the visualization allows for a targeted analysis of these specific cell types. These results confirm that the identified endodermal lineage cells exhibit distinct expression characteristics relevant to pancreatic development.

caption: Axial evolution of the refractive index distribution for the T(0,1) mode, maintained at a design frequency of 34 kHz.
summary: The plot shows the variation in the refractive index distribution of the T(0,1) mode along the entire axis of the cone at a design frequency of 34 kHz. This visualization confirms the spatial gradient of the refractive index, which is fundamental to the functionality of the GRIN-PC lens.

caption: Calibration plots derived from differential pulse voltammetry for the detection of dopamine in the 5–100 μM concentration range, comparing electrodes printed from AuNP-CO (red), CO (blue), and commercial (black) filaments.
summary: Calibration plots for dopamine detection in the 5–100 μM range are presented for electrodes printed from AuNP-CO, CO, and commercial filaments. These plots demonstrate the practical electroanalytical application of the additively manufactured electrodes, with the AuNP-CO filament showing distinct performance characteristics during the differential pulse voltammetry determination of dopamine concentrations.

caption: Proposed reaction mechanism illustrating the activity enhancement of Ni-based hydrotalcite-derived materials during the removal of COS and CH4S.
summary: This schematic diagram outlines the proposed mechanism for the enhanced catalytic activity of Ni-based hydrotalcite-derived materials in the removal of COS and CH4S. It provides a visual representation of the reaction pathways and structural interactions that contribute to the improved performance of these materials in sulfur-containing gas purification processes.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the water-based EDM sample captured via backscattered electron SEM imaging.
summary: Captured via backscattered electron SEM imaging, this panel illustrates the cross-sectional view of the water-based EDM sample. This visualization is essential for examining the surface features of the EDMed material, providing critical data for the broader investigation into the corrosion characteristics of these specific machined surfaces.

caption: Reflected spectra of the FP micro-object showing the experimental curve recorded at room temperature in black and the corresponding theoretical fit in pink, derived from the reflection intensity equation for the interferometer.
summary: Measured reflected spectra for the FP micro-object are displayed in the 1170 nm–1620 nm range. The experimental data, shown as a black curve, demonstrates close agreement with the theoretical model plotted in pink, which accounts for reflection coefficients, transmission parameters, and the refractive index of the glass material.

caption: Dark field TEM image displaying the approximately square morphology of γ′ particles in the sample with a Ti/Al ratio of 1.80 after a stress-rupture test at 700 °C and 200 MPa for 13480 hours.
summary: Dark field TEM analysis of the sample with a Ti/Al ratio of 1.80 after a 13480-hour stress-rupture test at 700 °C and 200 MPa shows that most γ′ particles exhibit an approximately square shape with varied sizes, reflecting the microstructural evolution under these specific high-temperature and long-duration test conditions.

caption: Ultimate compressive strength (UCS) values for TXU1010 samples across various heat treatment temperatures, with statistical significance marked relative to the 225 °C condition.
summary: This bar chart compares the ultimate compressive strength of TXU1010 samples across different heat treatment temperatures. Results indicate that varying these temperatures has a minimal effect on UCS values. However, samples without DAS show lower UCS values compared to those treated with DAS, emphasizing the importance of the fabrication process.

caption: Thermal distribution heatmap of the gear specimen without heat treatment at 420 s after the start of the process.
summary: Representing the thermal state at 420 s, this heatmap illustrates the temperature profile of the gear specimen without heat treatment. The data captures the cooling or thermal evolution of the component following the initial coating stage, providing insight into the heat dissipation characteristics of the untreated material.

caption: CNA visualization of Fe-bulk Ni (Model H) at 1 K under 0.055 strain, illustrating the effect of bulk Ni addition.
summary: CNA results for the Fe-bulk Ni (Model H) system at 1 K under a strain of 0.055. This model demonstrates how bulk Ni addition influences the microstructure during the high-stress state, specifically enhancing plastic deformation compared to the pure iron baseline model.

caption: GDMS depth-profiling analysis of Ag:TiN/Al samples using the SLM configuration at a discharge pressure of 6.50 mPa.
summary: This panel displays the GDMS depth-profiling analysis for the SLM configuration at 6.50 mPa. The analysis successfully captures the distribution of major and minor elements along the depth direction of the Ag:TiN/Al sample, providing a comprehensive profile of the elemental composition throughout the material's thickness.

caption: Final scorecard summarizing the calculated effectiveness of various polymers evaluated for the energy infrastructure case study.
summary: This table presents the final effectiveness scores for a range of polymers assessed within the context of an energy infrastructure case study. These calculated values provide a comparative overview of material performance, enabling the identification of the most suitable polymers for specific infrastructure applications based on their quantified effectiveness metrics.

caption: Confocal microscopy images of cells cultured on scaffolds for 3 days, with cytoskeleton stained by rhodamine-phalloidin (red) and nuclei stained by DAPI (blue).
summary: Confocal microscopy images reveal the cell adhesion and morphology of cells cultured on scaffolds for 3 days. By staining the cytoskeleton with rhodamine-phalloidin and the nuclei with DAPI, the images provide detailed structural information regarding how cells interact with and attach to the scaffold surfaces during the culture period.

caption: Optimized structural model of the twin Ni (111) surface.
summary: The optimized structural model for the twin Ni (111) surface is presented here. Computational analysis reveals that the introduction of a twin boundary shifts the Ni d-band center to -1.66 eV, demonstrating a distinct electronic modification compared to the perfect Ni (111) surface configuration.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the Fe21.5 EHEA composition, highlighting phase evolution as a function of temperature.
summary: This CALPHAD-derived equilibrium phase diagram for the Fe21.5 EHEA composition maps the phase stability regions. It provides essential thermodynamic data for understanding how varying the Fe content influences the phase constituents and the resulting microstructure of the Ni-Al-(FeCoCr) alloy system at elevated temperatures.

caption: Bode impedance magnitude plots for the coatings, showing high-frequency impedance values representing solution resistance between 4 and 5 Ω cm 2.
summary: Bode impedance magnitude plots for the coatings reveal high-frequency impedance values (|Z|) ranging from 4 to 5 Ω cm 2, which represent the solution impedance. The low-frequency region impedance ranking is C3 > C2 > C1 > C4 > Substrate, confirming the superior corrosion resistance of the C3 coating.

caption: Bipolar resistive switching behavior observed in a TiO2-based device, characterized by current-voltage characteristics where switching occurs at different voltage polarities.
summary: This panel displays the bipolar resistive switching characteristics of a TiO2-based device. The I-V curve illustrates the device's ability to switch states depending on the applied voltage polarity. This switching behavior is determined by the specific coupling between the TiO2 active core material and the applied electrical bias.

caption: Representative EdU staining images (a) and corresponding cell proliferation percentages (b) for HGFs on specimens after 24 hours, comparing conditions with and without the glycolysis inhibitor 2-DG.
summary: EdU staining images and quantitative analysis reveal that HGF proliferation is significantly influenced by SFMG coatings. The addition of the glycolysis inhibitor 2-DG diminishes the proliferative effects induced by the SFMG specimens, confirming that glucose metabolism is essential for the observed cell growth enhancement on these materials.

caption: UV–visible transmittance spectra of SilMA pre-gel solutions containing varying AA dosages, measured across the 300–700 nm wavelength range with a specific focus on the 405 nm mark.
summary: This panel displays the UV–visible transmittance spectra of SilMA pre-gel solutions with different AA dosages between 300 and 700 nm. The data indicates that light transmittance across this spectral range increases consistently as the dosage of AA is increased, with the 405 nm wavelength highlighted for specific reference.

caption: Logarithmic current density versus inverse charge density plot for PM-HIP1, demonstrating the high-field re-passivation model validity.
summary: This plot displays the log(i) versus Q^-1 relationship for PM-HIP1, serving as a test for the high-field re-passivation model. The re-passivation rates derived from these plots exhibit values closely similar to those observed for PM-HIP3, confirming consistent re-passivation behavior across the tested step-potentials for this powder metallurgy sample.

caption: Thermal response curves obtained from DSC measurements for PLA/GF composites with 10 wt% glass fiber content over the course of UV-C degradation.
summary: DSC curves for PLA/GF composites with 10 wt% glass fiber content are displayed to monitor thermal changes during UV-C irradiation. These results, obtained from cross-sectional samples, help characterize the degradation behavior of the composite material and determine if the increased fiber content affects the thermal properties over time.

caption: Parity plot illustrating the iBNN framework predictions for polymer toughness within the validation domain.
summary: Focusing on the validation domain, this parity plot depicts the iBNN model's accuracy in predicting polymer toughness. The results confirm the model's robustness and ability to generalize to unseen polymer properties. Consistent with other panels, the scatter plot shows clean color gradients, indicating minimal interaction between the input data features.

caption: Minimum MAPE prediction result at the 0th percentile, showing the observed versus predicted stress–strain curve generated by the CNN model.
summary: This panel displays the 0th percentile prediction result, representing the minimum mean absolute percentage error for the CNN model. The observed versus predicted stress–strain curve demonstrates high accuracy, effectively capturing the elastic, plastic, and densification stages of the material's mechanical response using polygon input data.

caption: Initial three galvanostatic charge-discharge voltage profiles for the Ni0.9Sn electrode measured at a current density of 0.2 A g-1.
summary: The initial electrochemical behavior of the Ni0.9Sn electrode is characterized by the first three galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles. These curves, obtained at a current density of 0.2 A g-1, provide insight into the early-stage lithiation and delithiation processes and the associated voltage plateaus for this specific nickel-tin alloy composition.

caption: Schematic representation of the tensile test configuration used for evaluating mechanical properties.
summary: This panel illustrates the experimental setup for tensile testing. The schematic provides a clear visual representation of the mechanical test configuration, which is essential for assessing the material's response under uniaxial tension. This setup serves as a foundational component for characterizing the mechanical behavior of the specimens under investigation.

caption: Unit cell configuration after the first thermomechanical cycle.
summary: This panel illustrates the unit cell configuration following the first thermomechanical cycle. During this initial stage, the unit cell angle for the S20 specimen increases from 60° to 60.08°. The cycling plots indicate that recovery is relatively low during these initial cycles for structures characterized by a high angle.

caption: Range analysis results illustrating the relative influence of various process parameters on the compressive elastic modulus of porous TPE structures.
summary: Range analysis results reveal the degree of influence of each parameter on the compressive elastic modulus. Layer thickness exhibits the largest range, directly determining interlayer adhesion and exerting the most significant effect on the overall stiffness of porous TPE structures, thus it is regarded as the primary parameter in FDM.

caption: Thermal response profile obtained via differential scanning calorimetry for microwave sintered Sn–Cu–Ni, highlighting phase transition temperatures.
summary: Representing the microwave sintered Sn–Cu–Ni variant, this DSC curve tracks heat flow during heating and cooling at 10 °C/min. The analysis determines the liquidus temperature, freezing range, and undercooling for the microwave-processed material, allowing for a direct comparison of thermal properties against the conventionally sintered counterpart.

caption: Tan δ curves representing the glass transition temperature (Tg) of the polybutadiene (PB) phase for pristine ABS (solid lines) and FDM-processed ABS-F (dashed lines).
summary: This panel displays the tan δ curves for the PB phase in pristine ABS and FDM-processed ABS-F samples. The data reveals that while pristine resins exhibit similar Tg values, FDM processing induces variable shifts: ABS-F1 and ABS-F2 show decreased Tg, ABS-F3 and ABS-F4 remain stable, and ABS-F5 shows a significant increase.

caption: Reflected phase characteristic curve of the base unit, illustrating the electromagnetic response across the 10–18 GHz frequency band.
summary: This plot displays the reflected phase characteristic curve of the base unit. The data indicates that the electromagnetic attenuation performance of the unit effectively supports RCS reduction within the 10–18 GHz frequency range, demonstrating the unit's capability to integrate effective bandwidth for electromagnetic wave management applications.

caption: Cross-sectional view of a single deposited bead showing its characteristic geometry.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the cross-section of a single deposited bead. The structural analysis reveals that the bead dimensions are approximately 150 μm in height and 570 μm in width. These specific geometric parameters characterize the deposited material profile as observed in the cross-sectional view provided in the figure.

caption: Raman spectrum of an isolated breyite inclusion in sample B6–1, showing characteristic peaks at 663, 990, and 1050 cm⁻¹ compared against reference data.
summary: This Raman spectrum identifies an isolated breyite inclusion within diamond sample B6–1. The observed peaks at 663, 990, and 1050 cm⁻¹ confirm the presence of breyite, formerly known as CaSiO3-walstromite. The data is compared against established reference spectra to validate the mineralogical composition of the inclusion.

caption: Schematic illustration of the build plate configuration, highlighting the definition of vertical (90°) and horizontal (0°) build orientations for LPBF-manufactured cylinders.
summary: This schematic defines the build plate design and orientation parameters for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) manufacturing. It illustrates the distinction between vertical (90°) and horizontal (0°) orientations, which were utilized to produce ten cylinders in total, with five specimens manufactured in each of these two specific build orientations.

caption: Comparison of FTIR spectra for the initial polyS2MA mixture (blue) and the final UV-cured material (purple).
summary: FTIR spectra of the initial polyS2MA formulation and the final material after UV curing are presented to confirm the completion of the polymerization reaction. The comparison between the blue initial mixture spectrum and the purple final material spectrum demonstrates the chemical transformation and successful curing of the polymer system.

caption: Quasi-3D finite element model representing the S1 submodel, constructed using real microstructural data derived from EBSD measurements.
summary: The finite element model for the S1 submodel is established as a quasi-3D representation based on actual microstructural data obtained from EBSD measurements. This computational model serves as a basis for finite element simulations to evaluate the effects of grain characteristics on the alloy's macroscopic mechanical performance.

caption: Comparison of tensile strength versus elongation to failure for in-situ alloyed Fe–Mn–Al–C LWSs against DED-manufactured stainless, precipitation-hardened, and maraging steels.
summary: Tensile strength is plotted against elongation to failure to benchmark the mechanical performance of in-situ alloyed Fe–Mn–Al–C LWSs. This comparison against DED-manufactured stainless, precipitation-hardened, and maraging steels demonstrates the competitive mechanical properties of the LWSs, with 20Mn8Al specifically showing a favorable combination of high tensile strength and good uniform elongation.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the ST + AT-treated SLM-fabricated HX alloy, showing a diffuse distribution of two representative precipitate types with sizes around 700 nm.
summary: The combined solution and aging treatment (ST + AT) of the SLM-fabricated HX alloy results in a microstructure containing a large number of two distinct types of precipitates. These features are diffusely distributed throughout the matrix and reach sizes of approximately 700 nm, indicating significant microstructural evolution during this treatment.

caption: Discharge curves for annealed La1.9Mg1.1Ni9 alloy electrodes plotted as a function of discharge current density.
summary: This panel presents the discharge curves for the annealed La1.9Mg1.1Ni9 alloy electrode across different discharge current densities. The results demonstrate the electrochemical response of this specific composition. Similar to the La2MgNi9 alloy, this material shows a maximum discharge capacity of approximately 400 mA g-1 under the tested conditions.

caption: Tensile performance of 3D printed parts at varying distances between the nozzle and substrate.
summary: Tensile performance of three-dimensional formed parts is evaluated at varying distances between the nozzle and substrate. This plot provides a quantitative assessment of the mechanical strength, demonstrating how the nozzle-to-substrate gap distance directly impacts the load-bearing capacity and tensile properties of the final printed components.

caption: True stress-strain curves of the EN AW-7108 T6 aluminum alloy illustrating the influence of varying strain rates on plastic material behavior.
summary: This figure presents the true stress-strain curves for the EN AW-7108 T6 aluminum alloy, highlighting the material's plastic response under different strain rate conditions. These curves demonstrate how the mechanical behavior of the alloy evolves as a function of strain rate, providing essential data for characterizing its deformation properties.

caption: Simple cubic unit cell oriented with [111] parallel to the loading direction (LD), highlighting the relationship between the x'y'z' and xyz coordinate systems.
summary: Representing the [111] orientation, this unit cell is aligned with the loading direction parallel to the build direction. The illustration includes both the original x'y'z' coordinate system and the new xyz coordinate system, facilitating the analysis of the unit cell structure and its orientation relative to the applied load.

caption: Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model performance represented as a confusion matrix.
summary: GBDT model performance is illustrated through a confusion matrix. Utilizing the same dataset as other models, this matrix provides a quantitative view of the GBDT's classification performance, enabling a direct comparison of its predictive accuracy and error patterns against the other machine learning models presented in the study.

caption: Logarithmic current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of a printed t-ZnO sensor measured between -10 V and +10 V under dark (black) and UV-illuminated (purple) conditions.
summary: Logarithmic I-V curves demonstrate the electrical response of printed t-ZnO sensors at room temperature. Measurements taken from -10 V to +10 V reveal that forward and reverse bias characteristics are nearly symmetrical, with UV illumination inducing a significant increase in current by two orders of magnitude compared to dark conditions.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni–Cr–Mo ternary system providing insight into the formation process of the weld microstructure.
summary: The isothermal section of the Ni–Cr–Mo ternary system is shown to explain the specific formation process of the weld microstructure. This diagram provides the necessary thermodynamic context to understand the phase stability and transformation pathways that occur during the solidification of the alloy system under investigation.

caption: Superimposed high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns collected across the welded joint, illustrating the spatial evolution of phase composition.
summary: This panel displays a superimposition of high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns obtained across the welded joint. It serves as a comprehensive overview of the structural variations and phase evolution occurring from the base metal through the heat-affected zones and into the fusion zone of the weldment.

caption: Current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics of dye-sensitized solar cells (DSCs) utilizing Pt3Ni/CNs and Cr-Pt3Ni/CNs composites as counter electrodes.
summary: The J-V curves illustrate the photovoltaic performance of DSCs fabricated with Pt3Ni/CNs and Cr-Pt3Ni/CNs counter electrodes. These measurements, alongside the data in Table 1, demonstrate the impact of the Cr-doping on the current density and voltage output of the solar cells, providing a direct comparison of the electrochemical efficiency between the two composite materials.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of rabbit BMSCs on a 3D-printed porous scaffold at day 4, highlighting the spatial distribution of viable cells across the scaffold surface.
summary: Visualizing rabbit BMSCs on the 3D-printed scaffold via live/dead staining at day 4 provides evidence of cellular health. The results indicate that the Coral-hHAp scaffold promotes superior cell proliferation and reduced cell death, underscoring the positive influence of the scaffold's micro-nanosized surface features on BMSC viability and overall biocompatibility.

caption: Scanning transmission electron microscopy micrograph displaying nitrides and surrounding precipitates within the NiTi-N 2 matrix.
summary: This STEM micrograph captures the microstructure of the NiTi-N 2 sample, focusing on nitrides and associated precipitates. Observations confirm that the nitrides generated during the SLM process remained stable and did not undergo significant morphological changes compared to the as-printed state, maintaining the structural integrity of the material after aging.

caption: Stress-free reference lattice profiles of the {311} plane along the height of the as-deposited wall specimen.
summary: This panel displays the stress-free reference lattice profiles for the {311} plane in the as-deposited wall.
