The data highlights the inherent challenges in establishing a representative d0 reference for neutron diffraction measurements, particularly in materials characterized by significant texture and coarse grain structures, as evidenced by the observed profile inconsistencies.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the Fe–Mn–Al–C alloy sample fabricated at a laser scanning speed of 800 mm/s.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging of the Fe–Mn–Al–C alloy processed at 800 mm/s allows for the observation of microstructural features and precipitate characteristics. The increased dislocation density observed in this sample compared to the 650 mm/s condition highlights the impact of laser scanning speed on the material's deformation behavior and structural integrity.

caption: Poisson’s ratio plotted against strain for 3D EAC structures, illustrating the mechanical response variations across different alpha values.
summary: This plot displays the Poisson’s ratio–strain curves for 3D EAC structures, highlighting how different alpha values influence the mechanical behavior under strain. The data provides a clear visualization of the structural response, demonstrating the sensitivity of the Poisson's ratio to the specific alpha parameters defined for the 3D EAC material.

caption: Fluorescence images acquired at sequential time intervals, confirming the colocalization of green signals from MP-NPs and blue signals from cells, indicating successful accumulation at the channel sidewalls.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images acquired at different time intervals confirm the successful magnetic labeling of cells. The colocalization of green signals from MP-NPs and blue signals from the cells provides clear evidence of the magnetically induced accumulation of cells at the channel sidewalls.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of negative ions CrO2-, CrO3H2-, NiO2H2-, and Ni2- for the H2 annealed (MH) sample after 4 h of potentiostatic passivation at 0.25 V vs. SCE in 0.5 M H2SO4.
summary: The ToF-SIMS depth profile for the H2 annealed sample shows a less homogeneously thick inner layer, evidenced by a large Ni2- plateau between 10 and 30 seconds. The CrO3H2-/NiO2H2- intensity ratio is 1.6, reflecting a different distribution of hydroxide species compared to the mechanically ground sample after electrochemical passivation.

caption: Simulated columnar dendrite morphologies generated under extended solidification conditions, with the diagonal arrangement representing the specific solidification parameters along the solid/liquid interface of the molten pool.
summary: This simulation illustrates the steady-state morphologies of columnar dendrites formed under extended solidification conditions. The diagonal arrangement of the dendrites corresponds directly to the solidification parameters observed along the solid/liquid interface of the molten pool, providing a visual representation of the microstructural evolution during the solidification process.

caption: Small-angle XRD patterns (2°–30° range) for PBMA/rGO composites and pure PBMA, highlighting an order-of-magnitude increase in scattering intensity for the filled polymer at length scales below 50 nm.
summary: Small-angle XRD patterns in the 2°–30° range demonstrate an order-of-magnitude increase in scattering intensity for the filled polymer compared to the pristine material at length scales below 50 nm. The 10 nm spacing coincides with the 2θ = 6.9° maximum, providing precise insight into the spatial arrangement of macromolecular chain fragments.

caption: Interface matching schematic for (111) Cu stimulated grains on a (001) Ni substrate.
summary: This schematic illustrates the interface matching between (111) Cu stimulated grains and a (001) Ni substrate. Green balls represent Ni atoms in the stimulated grains, while blue balls represent Cu atoms in the substrate, visualizing the atomic arrangement and crystalline plane matching modeled for this specific heterostructure interface.

caption: Neutron diffraction peak profile for the <220> grain family measured in the axial direction at a radial position of 12 mm, compared against GP model predictions.
summary: This panel displays the neutron diffraction peak for the <220> grain orientation at a radial distance of 12 mm from the sample center. The experimental data, represented by a red solid line, is plotted alongside GP model predictions to evaluate the accuracy of the theoretical framework in capturing axial diffraction behavior.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) diagram showing local plastic strain distribution near the fracture site.
summary: The Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) diagram maps the local plastic strain distribution within the fractured TA11 sample. This EBSD analysis highlights regions of high dislocation density, which are critical for understanding the crack propagation and hindrance mechanisms observed in the material.

caption: Dilatometric strain curve recorded during continuous cooling at a rate of 50 °C/s.
summary: This dilatometric curve captures the thermal expansion and phase transformation characteristics of the material subjected to a faster cooling rate of 50 °C/s. These experimental results, combined with other data, were used to determine critical transformation temperatures and support the analysis of the resulting bainitic microstructure in the deposited wall.

caption: Vickers hardness of Ti–15Mo specimens plotted against average grain size, showing a decrease from 359 to 288 HV as grain size increases from 4 to 13 μm, with an inset highlighting mechanical twinning near indentations in larger-grained samples.
summary: This plot illustrates the inverse relationship between Vickers hardness and grain size in Ti–15Mo materials, where hardness drops from 359 to 288 HV as grain size grows from 4 to 13 μm. The inset reveals that mechanical twinning near indentations contributes to the observed hardness behavior in larger-grained specimens.

caption: Fe 2p3/2 fine spectrum of SLM-316L Fe fabricated at a 0° construction direction.
summary: The Fe 2p3/2 fine spectrum for SLM-316L Fe at a 0° construction direction displays four distinct component peaks. These peaks correspond to metallic iron at 705.70 eV, Fe3O4 at 706.98 eV, Fe2O3 at 708.94 eV, and FeOOH at 710.24 eV, characterizing the surface chemical state of the sample.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of ternary Co–Ni–Mo alloy coating measured at 50 mV s−1 in 1 M KOH, illustrating the electrochemical profile within the 1.0 to −0.58 V vs RHE window.
summary: The cyclic voltammogram for the ternary Co–Ni–Mo alloy coating, recorded at 50 mV s−1 in 1 M KOH, characterizes the electrochemical performance between 1.0 and −0.58 V vs RHE. This profile provides insight into the redox behavior of the ternary alloy system compared to the binary counterparts.

caption: High-magnification HAADF-STEM image of the MgZn2 precipitate in the OA1 specimen, highlighting the fully coherent interface.
summary: High-magnification HAADF-STEM imaging of the OA1 specimen reveals the atomic-scale structure of the MgZn2 precipitate. The interface is identified as fully coherent, providing a clear structural reference for the initial state of the precipitate before the development of semicoherency observed in more advanced aging conditions.

caption: Transmission spectrum of sample 2, showing the optical characteristics post-UV exposure.
summary: Sample 2's transmission spectrum is shown to assess its optical behavior after UV light exposure. The results indicate that the transmission characteristics remain consistent with the expected trends, confirming that the sample maintains its structural and optical properties without degradation when exposed to the specified UV light conditions.

caption: Stress-free reference lattice profiles of the {311} plane along the height of the as-deposited wall following SQA treatment.
summary: This panel shows the stress-free reference lattice profiles for the {311} plane in the as-deposited wall after undergoing SQA treatment. The inconsistency in the data underscores the persistent difficulties in identifying a representative d0 reference for neutron diffraction analysis in materials with coarse grains and strong crystallographic textures.

caption: Dilatometric measurement of sample S1(5 °C/min) showing elongation (ΔL) as a function of temperature during three consecutive heating cycles from 20 °C to 1000 °C at a constant rate of 5 °C/min.
summary: This dilatogram illustrates the thermal expansion behavior of sample S1(5 °C/min) across three repeated heating runs. The data demonstrates that elongation occurs consistently in the sample as the temperature increases from 20 °C to 1000 °C, confirming that thermal expansion is independent of the specific heating cycle performed.

caption: Low-magnification inverse pole figure map of SDSS CW-GMA walls processed at an interpass temperature of 75 °C.
summary: This low-magnification inverse pole figure map displays the grain orientation of SDSS CW-GMA walls processed at 75 °C. Acquired in the cross-sectional plane, the map covers multiple layers over a 5 mm by 3 mm area with a 0.5 μm step size to characterize the initial microstructure.

caption: Raman spectra of FeCoNiMo and CrCoNiMo worn surfaces at 800 °C, illustrating experimental data, deconvoluted peaks, and cumulative peaks.
summary: Raman spectroscopy at 800 °C identifies the oxide products within the wear tracks. The data shows distinct peaks representing the tribo-film composition. By comparing these spectra to those of unworn regions, the study confirms that wear-induced processes significantly promote the formation of molybdates on the sliding surfaces of the alloys.

caption: Atom probe tomography ion map of Alloy 625 after thermal aging at 650 °C for 25 hours, illustrating elemental partitioning.
summary: After 25 hours of aging at 650 °C, the atom probe tomography map demonstrates significant elemental partitioning. Nickel, niobium, and titanium are shown to concentrate within the γ″ precipitates, while chromium and iron partition into the γ matrix, highlighting the continued growth and chemical evolution of the precipitates.

caption: Two-dimensional spatial distribution map illustrating the calculated surface acoustic wave (SAW) velocities across the sample surface detection regions.
summary: This two-dimensional spatial distribution map visualizes the calculated surface acoustic wave (SAW) velocities across the sample surface. The data was derived by determining the center frequency at each scanning point on the sample surface and applying specific velocity calculation equations to generate this comprehensive representation of the measured area.

caption: Maximum wear depth (WD) values for Ni-P coated disks under different heat treatment conditions, showing that WD is consistently lower than the total coating thickness.
summary: Maximum wear depth values for the Ni-P coated disks are shown to be significantly lower than the total coating thickness, ranging between 20% and 50%. The T6R_1 condition exhibits the lowest wear depth, correlating with the superior micro-hardness achieved through the specific heat treatment cycle applied to the coating.

caption: Three-dimensional graph illustrating the particle flow trajectories and positions at different moments for the wire material.
summary: This 3D plot displays the particle flow trajectories for the wire material. Compared to the strip, wire particles exhibit greater horizontal displacement, which leads to increased deposition heights. The flow patterns at the wire's center are shown to be similar to those observed at corresponding positions on the strip.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Cr-Ni system showing the equilibrium phases, with a red line indicating the 600 °C process temperature.
summary: The Cr-Ni binary phase diagram, generated via FactSage, illustrates the equilibrium phases present across varying temperatures. At the specific process temperature of 600 °C, highlighted by a red line, the system exhibits no stable intermetallic compounds, providing critical information regarding the phase stability of the Cr-Ni system under these conditions.

caption: Inverse pole figure map showing the vertical orientation of the 60 μm layer thickness Al–Mn–Mg–Sc–Zr specimen.
summary: Displaying the vertical cross-section of the 60 μm layer thickness specimen, this map reveals large columnar grains within the melt pool and fine equiaxed grains at the boundaries. The larger grain size observed here, compared to thinner layers, is associated with the reduced microhardness values measured in this specific specimen condition.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT device measured across a range of operating temperatures.
summary: This panel displays the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of the KC200GT device. The data illustrates how the electrical response of the material varies under different temperature conditions, providing insight into the device's performance and stability across the tested thermal range as referenced in the study's experimental analysis.

caption: Geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density map of the HX-M sample.
summary: The GND density map for the HX-M sample illustrates the distribution of geometrically necessary dislocations following high-temperature processing. This visualization helps characterize the dislocation density associated with the reduced residual stress state observed in the HX-M sample, providing a spatial representation of the material's internal defect structure.

caption: Nyquist plots showing single capacitive arcs for LPBF DSS 2205 and WC/W2C reinforced composites in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: The Nyquist plots for LPBF DSS 2205 and WC/W2C reinforced composites exhibit single capacitive arcs, which are indicative of passive behavior in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. Larger arc diameters in these plots suggest a more stable passive film and higher corrosion resistance for the tested LPBF specimens.

caption: TEM and STEM morphology of Cu2 steel highlighting the presence of Cu-rich precipitates.
summary: The TEM and STEM morphology of Cu2 steel displays the local microstructure with Cu-rich precipitates marked by yellow arrows. Similar to Cu1, Cu in this steel is mainly in a solid solution state, which inhibits the anode reaction and leads to a decrease in the corrosion current density of the material.

caption: Glass transition temperature evolution for the second cryogenic aging protocol.
summary: Glass transition temperature data for the second cryogenic aging protocol are shown. The results demonstrate minimal fluctuations, with changes consistently lower than 0.5%. These findings suggest that the material maintains stable viscoelastic properties despite the applied cryogenic cyclic aging, confirming a lack of statistically significant impact.

caption: Minimum creep rate plotted against varying stress levels from 20 MPa to 50 MPa at a constant temperature of 250 °C for the studied alloys.
summary: This plot illustrates the minimum creep rate of the studied alloys as a function of applied stress, ranging from 20 MPa to 50 MPa, while maintaining a constant temperature of 250 °C. The data provides insight into the mechanical response and creep resistance of the materials under these specific loading conditions.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of the FeCoCrNiMn-(N,Si) high-entropy alloy near the fracture surface after tensile deformation at 773 K.
summary: Captured near the fracture surface, this EBSD inverse pole figure map illustrates the grain orientation of the FeCoCrNiMn-(N,Si) alloy after tensile deformation at 773 K. The alloy maintains a fully recrystallized grain structure, demonstrating that the grain size remains stable within the temperature range of 573 K to 873 K.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of S. aureus bacteria stained with a live/dead kit on composite scaffold systems, with a scale bar of 50 μm.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of S. aureus bacteria stained with a live/dead kit on composite scaffold systems, with a scale bar of 50 μm. By utilizing a live/dead bacterial staining kit and fluorescence microscopy, we were able to detect the number of dead and live bacteria on the scaffold surfaces.

caption: Parity plot displaying predicted porosity values versus the corresponding measured experimental data.
summary: This parity plot demonstrates the correlation between predicted and measured porosity values. The alignment of the data points along the parity line signifies that the model successfully captures the experimental porosity trends, showing good agreement between the predicted values and the actual measured data obtained from the samples.

caption: Split P TPMS unit cell oriented along the x, y, and z axes.
summary: This panel illustrates the Split P TPMS unit cell. Following the software's UVW orientation convention, the structure is aligned along the x, y, and z axes. This visualization highlights the specific topological features of the Split P geometry within the defined coordinate framework used for the study's unit cell modeling.

caption: Confocal micrograph of the 2Y specimen displaying columnar grains and solidification cracking (indicated by arrows) along the grain boundaries, etched with Keller’s Reagent.
summary: Confocal imaging of the 2Y specimen shows columnar alpha-Al grains spanning adjacent melt pools, similar to the 1Y specimen. However, this specimen exhibits pervasive solidification cracking, particularly along the columnar grain boundaries, which is highlighted by arrows to indicate the susceptibility of the 2Y composition to cracking.

caption: Normalized mass spectrum and correlation histogram for MC carbides acquired at 100 pJ, showing a profile dominated by complex peaks including C6 4+ and C12 4+ at 18 and 36 Da.
summary: The MC carbide mass spectrum is characterized by a high density of complex peaks. Specifically, the data reveals significant signals for C6 4+ and C12 4+ ions at 18 and 36 Da, respectively. These complex ions are promoted by high carbon content and specific evaporation mechanisms like paired field evaporation and dissociation.

caption: Statistical R-squared values derived from fitting various mathematical models to the drug release kinetics of the thermosensitive printlets.
summary: This table presents the R-squared values obtained from fitting experimental drug release data to various kinetic models. These statistical metrics were used to evaluate the release behavior of the prepared thermosensitive printlets, providing a quantitative basis for understanding the underlying drug release mechanisms and model suitability.

caption: Fluorescence micrograph of HFFs on a polished Ti-6Al-4V surface (P1) showing collagen type I (green), fibronectin (red), and nuclei (blue) after 7 days, with ECM proteins oriented parallel to the cell long axis.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy reveals the distribution of collagen type I and fibronectin by HFFs on a polished Ti-6Al-4V surface after 7 days of culture. The ECM proteins exhibit a distinct orientation parallel to the long axis of the cells, demonstrating the influence of the polished surface topography on protein organization.

caption: Optical behavior of PE polymer powder as a function of layer thickness during exposure to a 10.6 μm CO2 laser.
summary: This panel displays the optical characteristics of polyethylene (PE) powder under 10.6 μm CO2 laser irradiation. Comparative analysis shows that PE possesses lower absorbance than PA12, which limits its effectiveness in selective laser sintering processes due to reduced energy coupling efficiency during the powder bed fusion manufacturing cycle.

caption: Volume fraction of γ″ precipitates in Inconel 625 aged at 600 °C, demonstrating a monotonic increase during the early stages of aging.
summary: This graph illustrates the volume fraction evolution of γ″ precipitates in Inconel 625 during aging at 600 °C. The simulation results show a monotonic increase in the volume fraction during the early aging stages, consistent with the expected precipitation kinetics driven by the phase-field model parameters.

caption: Temperature ramp DMA profile displaying the tan delta curve and storage modulus as a function of temperature to identify the glass transition temperature.
summary: This DMA temperature ramp test characterizes the viscoelastic behavior of the material. By analyzing the storage modulus profile and the tan delta curve, the glass transition temperature is determined to be approximately 65°C. This measurement provides critical insight into the thermal stability and mechanical response of the specimen under heating.

caption: Single-layer dielectric coupon featuring 300 μm through-holes, fabricated via DLP printing with 20 μm layer thickness, 1 s exposure, 18 mW/cm2 irradiance, and 0.33 mm/s lift speed.
summary: This panel displays a single-layer dielectric coupon successfully fabricated with 300 μm through-holes. The printing process utilized a 20 μm layer thickness, 1 s exposure, 18 mW/cm2 irradiance, and 0.33 mm/s lift speed. This demonstration confirms the capability of the designed photocurable resin to achieve precise through-hole geometries for interlayer metallization.

caption: MC3T3-E1 cell viability measured via CCK-8 assay after 3 and 7 days of exposure to 3 mg/L and 6 mg/L zinc ion concentrations.
summary: Panel C presents the MC3T3-E1 cell viability results from the CCK-8 assay at 3 and 7 days. The data shows that zinc ion concentrations influence cell viability, with the 0.3 mg/L concentration demonstrating the highest cell viability on day 7, confirming the biosafety of the zinc-releasing scaffold.

caption: Top-view snapshot of the CtFD simulation of laser-beam irradiation at 2.72 ms, with temperature represented by a color gradient.
summary: This top-view snapshot from the CtFD simulation illustrates the laser-beam irradiation process at 2.72 ms. The temperature distribution across the surface is visualized using a color scale, providing insight into the thermal state of the material during the laser interaction at this specific time point.

caption: UMAP projection of congruent TPMS flow regime features, revealing three distinct clusters identified by dashed lines.
summary: This UMAP projection visualizes the feature space of the congruent TPMS flow regime. The analysis identifies three distinct clusters, which are demarcated by dashed lines. As noted in the reference, these projections lack physical axis labels, and the individual interpretation of these cluster groups remains complex for the flow regime.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for as-fabricated specimens subjected to varying scanning strategies, highlighting the influence of interlayer rotation on mechanical response.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves illustrate the mechanical behavior of as-fabricated specimens produced via different scanning strategies. Analysis of these curves reveals that interlayer rotation induces an approximate yield strength difference of 35 MPa, demonstrating the significant impact of processing parameters on the tensile deformation characteristics of the material at room temperature.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for three AM compositions: Stellite6 0.25/17-4PH 0.75, Stellite6 0.5/17-4PH 0.5, and Stellite6 0.75/17-4PH 0.25.
summary: This figure displays the XRD patterns for three distinct additive manufacturing compositions of Stellite6 and 17-4PH. Analysis of the diffraction data reveals that the primary peaks observed at 43°, 50°, 74°, 90°, and 95° correspond to the Ni–Cr–Co–Mo phase, as confirmed by the reference pattern 00-035-1489.

caption: Conceptual framework illustrating the four core phases of the Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment (LCSA) process.
summary: This schematic outlines the four fundamental phases of the LCSA framework, which serves as an integrated methodology for evaluating product sustainability. By supporting triple bottom line thinking, this process assists in informed decision-making, identifies critical trade-offs, and highlights potential opportunities for improvement throughout the entire life cycle of a product.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of 316 L-2 stainless steel soaked at 1100 °C for 60 s, displaying grain orientation distribution and BCC phase distribution relative to the sheet normal direction.
summary: Representing the microstructure of 316 L-2 stainless steel after soaking at 1100 °C for 60 seconds, this EBSD inverse pole figure map displays grain orientations aligned with the sheet normal direction. White-colored pixels indicate the distribution of the BCC phase, providing a clear visualization of the material's structural state.

caption: Environmental (X6) M-DfX assessment scorecard for the aeronautics case study, evaluating energy efficiency indicators across various high-performance materials.
summary: This radar chart presents the environmental (X6) M-DfX assessment scorecard for the aeronautics case study. It highlights energy efficiency indicators for several high-performance materials, including PPSU, PSU, PEI+CF, PEI+CF (AERO), PEI+GF30, ULTEM 1010, and ULTEM 9085, which demonstrate considerably high performance within the evaluated environmental property framework.

caption: Current density-voltage (I-V) and power density-current (I-P) characteristics of single cells featuring various anodes, measured at 700 °C under dry hydrogen fuel conditions.
summary: This panel displays the electrochemical performance of single cells with different anode compositions. By measuring I-V and I-P curves at 700 °C with dry hydrogen, the plot illustrates the power output and voltage behavior, providing a baseline for evaluating the catalytic activity of the various anode materials tested.

caption: SEM micrograph of an alumina ball counterface after sliding against an as-printed Ni 49.8 at.% alloy, revealing the presence of adhesive transfer films.
summary: Presented is the SEM image of the alumina counterface following a wear test against the Ni 49.8 at.% alloy. The surface shows clear evidence of adhesive transfer films. The absence of significant oxide accumulation suggests that metallic interactions, rather than tribo-oxidation, govern the wear process for this material.

caption: Binary phase diagram for the Fe-Cr system illustrating the equilibrium phases as a function of temperature and chromium content.
summary: This Fe-Cr binary phase diagram maps the equilibrium phase boundaries for the iron-chromium system. It highlights the temperature-dependent stability of various phases, which is critical for predicting the microstructural evolution and phase transformations that occur during the heat treatment and service of iron-chromium based alloys.

caption: Experimental deformation sequence of 3D printed BF/L-PA honeycomb specimens under compression loading, illustrating five distinct stages: linear elastic, elastic buckling, collapse, plateau, and densification.
summary: This panel displays the experimental deformation sequence of 3D printed BF/L-PA honeycomb specimens during compression. The structure undergoes five distinct stages, including linear elastic, elastic buckling, collapse, plateau, and densification. Lateral bulging and localized folding lobes at the bottom end of the cells are clearly observed during the compression process.

caption: Contoured pole figure of the reconstructed beta phase for the parallel WAAM build type, characterized by a strong beta//ND partial fibre texture.
summary: The reconstructed beta phase for the parallel build is shown here, confirming a strong beta//ND partial fibre texture. This alignment, common in WAAM-built Ti64, indicates that columnar beta grains are oriented parallel to the vertical loading direction, with rotation occurring primarily around this specific axis during the build process.

caption: Histogram representing the frequency distribution of melt pool areas, showing a concentration of data points around 0.5 mm2.
summary: The histogram depicts the distribution of melt pool areas within the dataset. It demonstrates that a diverse range of melt pool sizes was acquired for training the machine learning model, with the majority of the measured melt pool areas clustered around a value of 0.5 mm2.

caption: Comparison of ultimate tensile strength (UTS), yield strength (YS), and percent elongation (El%) for specimens processed under argon (Ar) and nitrogen (N2) atmospheres.
summary: This table presents the mechanical properties of specimens fabricated under Ar and N2 atmospheres, specifically comparing UTS, YS, and El%. The data indicates that mechanical properties remain comparable between the two processing environments, demonstrating that N2 treatment does not degrade the material's performance while effectively preventing interfacial cracking.

caption: Force–displacement curves comparing the mechanical response of edge-notch lattice structures subjected to different heat treatment conditions.
summary: This panel displays the force–displacement relationship for edge-notch lattice structures under varying heat treatment conditions. The data indicates that heat treatment in the notch region significantly enhances the mechanical performance of the structure, as evidenced by the improved elongation and energy absorption capacity observed during the mechanical testing process.

caption: Wear rate of TiC/Ti6Al4V composites as a function of applied load for different TiC addition levels.
summary: The graph displays the relationship between wear loss and applied load for various TiC addition levels in Ti6Al4V composites. Observations indicate that the wear loss increases in an almost linear fashion as the applied load is increased, maintaining this trend consistently across the different TiC content levels tested.

caption: Short-range order (SRO) parameter α(100) for atomic pairs in the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al slab during tensile testing at 1373 K.
summary: This plot displays the SRO parameter α(100) for atomic pairs, reflecting the local chemical ordering within the γ-Ni/γ'-Ni3Al slab during tensile deformation at 1373 K. Consistent with broader observations, the evolution of this parameter provides insight into the structural changes and atomic arrangement stability under high-temperature tensile stress.

caption: Energy-volume curve for pure Pd calculated using DFT and NEP methods.
summary: This panel displays the energy-volume relationship for pure Pd. The data demonstrates that the neural network potential (NEP) model provides a high degree of accuracy when compared against standard DFT calculations, confirming the reliability of the computational approach for determining equilibrium lattice constants in this metallic system.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image showing Bi atoms adsorbed at the steel surface or incorporated into the FCC Fe lattice.
summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging demonstrates that Bi atoms either adsorb onto the steel surface or appear to be incorporated into the FCC Fe lattice. This observation, supported by the 2D projection, indicates a coherent interfacial phase with an effective chemical width of approximately 1 nm, potentially containing 3D structural steps.

caption: Measured porosity and strut diameter values for the simple cubic wick geometry.
summary: Simple cubic wick geometry data is presented, detailing the measured porosity and strut diameter. These metrics are derived from helium pycnometry and SEM analysis. The strut diameter is maintained at approximately 325 μm, consistent with as-built wick specifications, providing a baseline for evaluating the structural characteristics of this specific lattice configuration.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing dry-fresh, dry-aged, and water-submerged specimens after 90 days of exposure.
summary: FTIR spectra reveal the chemical composition and contaminant presence in specimens under various conditions. Comparison between dry-fresh and dry-aged samples shows no significant spectral differences after 90 days. A persistent absorption peak at 2360 cm-1 across all conditions confirms the presence of carbon dioxide gas, which exhibits strong infrared absorption characteristics.

caption: Charge density difference map for Ni106TaVa visualized at an isovalue of ± 0.0675 e/Å³, highlighting the spatial distribution of charge accumulation (yellow) and depletion (cyan) near the vacancy site.
summary: Visualizing the charge density difference for Ni106TaVa demonstrates how the Ta solute modifies the electronic environment near the vacancy. The resulting spherical charge distribution, caused by the solute's close integration with surrounding Ni atoms, generates a repulsive interaction that is associated with a high diffusion barrier for the solute.

caption: Interfacial strengthening energies for the β-NiAl(110)/α-Al2O3(0001) interface co-doped with alloy elements and sulfur, showing lower Estr values compared to chlorine-doped systems.
summary: This panel illustrates the Rice-Wang interfacial strengthening energies for the β-NiAl(110)/α-Al2O3(0001) interface co-doped with alloy elements and sulfur. The resulting Estr values are significantly lower than those observed with chlorine doping, with the overall trend aligning with the results obtained from first-principles tensile tests for this specific interface.

caption: Summary of key laser processing parameters, specifically a powder layer thickness of 60 μm and a hatch spacing of 90 μm.
summary: Laser parameters applied during the LPBF process are detailed here, highlighting critical manufacturing settings. Specifically, the powder layer thickness is maintained at 60 μm, while the hatch spacing is set to 90 μm, ensuring controlled energy input and layer-by-layer consolidation during the fabrication of the test specimens.

caption: Experimental and simulated minimum creep curves for the PBF-LB/M dataset, showing the temporal evolution of strain.
summary: This panel displays the minimum creep curves for the PBF-LB/M dataset, comparing experimental data represented by solid lines with simulated results using elongated Voronoi RVEs shown as dashed lines. The plot provides a linear scale evaluation of the creep behavior, illustrating the alignment between the experimental measurements and the simulation approach.

caption: Proposed methodological workflow for identifying critical locations and estimating fatigue life using average strain energy density (ASED) criteria.
summary: This flowchart outlines the systematic procedure for fatigue life estimation. It integrates finite element simulations to identify critical locations within the geometry by calculating the maximum von Mises stresses. This workflow serves as the foundational framework for the subsequent numerical analysis and structural integrity assessment of the lattice specimens.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of NCS and NCS-MA, highlighting characteristic proton peaks for starch glucosides, water absorption, and methyl groups.
summary: Proton NMR spectroscopy of NCS and NCS-MA reveals specific chemical environments. Peaks at 3.59 and 3.66 ppm correspond to starch glucoside protons, while NCS-MA exhibits a water absorption peak at 3.35 ppm and a distinctive methyl group peak at 1.9 ppm, confirming the successful chemical modification of the starch.

caption: Comparison of laminar burning velocities for ethanol-ethyl acetate/air mixtures derived from Eq. (3) and Cantera software using the Dayma et al. (2012) kinetic mechanism, including RMSE and R2 values across the specified range of equivalence ratios and ethanol concentrations.
summary: This parity plot displays the agreement between Eq. (3) and Cantera-calculated burning velocities using the Dayma et al. (2012) mechanism. By analyzing diverse equivalence ratios and fuel mixtures, the results support the conclusion that flame temperature is the primary driver of laminar burning velocity in these ethanol-ethyl acetate mixtures.

caption: Retained strength of monolithic samples A0, A10, and A20 plotted against temperature difference.
summary: This plot displays the retained strength of monolithic samples A0, A10, and A20 as a function of temperature difference. At a temperature difference of approximately 200 °C, the strength values for all three monoliths remain consistent with their non-shocked reference samples, indicating no thermal shock-induced degradation occurred.

caption: Operational demonstration of the multilayer circuit placed on the wireless charging coil, resulting in the LED being illuminated.
summary: The multilayer circuit is shown placed on the wireless charging coil, successfully lighting up the LED. This in-situ photograph demonstrates the functional capability of the wireless sensing system, confirming that the integrated circuit design effectively receives power from the charging coil to operate the LED device.

caption: Optical micrograph of the 11000 structure cross-section containing 0.05 wt% MWCNTs, highlighting interface boundaries characterized by elevated filler content.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the cross-section of the 11000 structure composite with 0.05 wt% MWCNTs. The image vividly depicts interface boundaries within the material, showcasing a region with elevated MWCNTs content, which provides insight into the internal structural distribution of the filler within the composite matrix.

caption: Computational domain representation for the 4C heterostructure specimen.
summary: This panel depicts the finite element method computational domain for the 4C heterostructure. By incorporating work-hardening behavior into the numerical simulations, the study captures strengthening effects and provides realistic predictions of tensile behavior for this specific heterostructure, which is modeled as a plate-shaped specimen for testing.

caption: Grayscale image-replicating result of the irregular particle shown in panel (c) within a 40 × 40 μm zone.
summary: This grayscale image-replicating result corresponds to the 40 × 40 μm zone of the irregular particle shown in panel (c). While the technique is effective for this visualization, the results for the irregular particle are noted to be less clear than those obtained for spherical particles.

caption: High-resolution peak-fitted W 4f XPS spectra for both 3D W meshes, illustrating the chemical states of tungsten.
summary: Panel b displays the high-resolution, peak-fitted W 4f XPS spectra obtained from the 3D W meshes. These spectra provide detailed information regarding the chemical states of tungsten present in the WO3 layers, allowing for the identification and characterization of specific tungsten species on the mesh surfaces.

caption: Spectral responsivity curves measured for COCA1, COCA2, COCA3, and COCA4 modified photovoltaic devices.
summary: Spectral responsivity measurements for COCA1 through COCA4 modified cells are presented in this panel. The results highlight a substantial enhancement in responsivity across the 300 nm to 1100 nm spectral range, confirming that the COCA modifications effectively improve the light-harvesting capabilities of the photovoltaic devices throughout the visible and near-infrared spectrum.

caption: Cycling performance curves comparing the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 and 3D-MP Ni3Sn2 electrodes, evaluated at a constant current density of 1 mA cm-2.
summary: Cycling performance curves for the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 and 3D-MP Ni3Sn2 electrodes, tested at 1 mA cm-2, demonstrate the long-term stability and capacity retention of the materials. These galvanostatic charge-discharge results highlight the superior electrochemical performance of the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 composite compared to the 3D-MP Ni3Sn2 counterpart.

caption: Mean SHAP value distribution plot illustrating the relative contribution of individual features to the model's predictive output.
summary: This SHAP value distribution plot quantifies the contribution of each morphological feature to the model's predictions. By calculating the mean SHapely Additive exPlanations for various instances, the graph effectively illustrates how specific martensite characteristics influence the final classification results generated by the XGBoost model.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curve of Cu foil in 1 M KOH at 40 °C, displaying oxidation peaks at 0.75, 1.0, and 1.16 V/RHE.
summary: The cyclic voltammetry curve for Cu foil in 1 M KOH at 40 °C reveals distinct oxidation peaks at 0.75 V/RHE, 1.0 V/RHE, and 1.16 V/RHE. These results indicate that the oxidation potential range for copper extends from 0.65 to 1.2 V/RHE, consistent with established electrochemical behavior.

caption: Maximum tensile force plotted against the number of cycles for a tested specimen, highlighting distinct beam failure events.
summary: This plot illustrates the maximum tensile force as a function of the number of cycles for a representative specimen. The data clearly captures the progression of the fatigue test, allowing for the identification of specific beam failure events that occur throughout the cycling process as the material degrades.

caption: Surface-based gyroid unit cell model generated using an implicit mathematical equation.
summary: The surface-based gyroid unit cell is modeled in MATLAB using an implicit equation. This mathematical approach allows for precise control over the unit cell size and the scaling parameter, which dictates the surface geometry and the resulting enclosed volume of the porous NiTi scaffold structure.

caption: Layout of the four thermocouples (TC1–TC4) used for temperature monitoring on the Start Plate and Heat Shield.
summary: This schematic illustrates the locations of the four thermocouples, labeled TC1 through TC4, used for temperature monitoring. TC1 and TC2 are positioned on the Start Plate, while TC3 and TC4 are located on the inner Heat Shield walls, specifically on Face A and Face B, respectively, for the build cycle.

caption: Comparative analysis of ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elongation for 17-4 PH stainless steel, including aging treatments at 550 °C and 620 °C for 4 hours, benchmarked against literature data.
summary: This plot summarizes the ultimate tensile strength and elongation of 17-4 PH stainless steel across various heat-treatment conditions, specifically aging at 550 °C and 620 °C for 4 hours. The results are compared with established literature values to evaluate the performance of the heat-treated samples against previous research findings.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) map of HA heat-treated LPBF Alloy 718 in the XY plane, illustrating the spatial distribution of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs).
summary: The KAM map for the XY plane of HA heat-treated LPBF Alloy 718 visualizes the distribution of geometrically necessary dislocations. This map provides insight into the local strain and dislocation density within the microstructure, which retains most of the original AM characteristics after the standard heat treatment.

caption: EPMA map illustrating the spatial distribution of Cobalt (cCo) within the indented region of Sample C.
summary: The EPMA map reveals the spatial distribution of Cobalt within the indented region of Sample C. As indicated by the reference data, the concentration of Cobalt increases with increasing distance d, providing insight into the compositional variations present in the material's microstructure following the mechanical indentation process.

caption: Snapshot of the segmented keyhole shape at 400 W laser power, derived from high-speed video analysis.
summary: This panel shows a segmented snapshot of the keyhole shape at 400 W laser power. The image provides a direct visual correlation to the plateau observed in the keyhole length evolution data. It captures the physical geometry of the keyhole during the laser-matter interaction on the Ti-6Al-4V substrate.

caption: Raman spectra of the graphitized sample, highlighting the characteristic G band at approximately 1575 cm-1 associated with sp2-bonded carbon vibrations.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the carbon structure derived from polyacrylonitrile shows the characteristic G band at approximately 1575 cm-1. This peak corresponds to the in-plane vibrations of sp2-bonded carbon, confirming the graphitic nature of the material in both the stabilized and carbonized samples analyzed in this study.

caption: Predicted labels generated by the K-means model following the application of a dimension reduction technique.
summary: This panel illustrates the predicted labels resulting from the K-means model after the dimensional reduction process. By comparing these predicted clusters to the true labels shown in panel (a), the effectiveness of the model in capturing the underlying data structure within the reduced dimensional space can be assessed.

caption: K–L plots for GF-CNT@Fe0.5-Ni3 derived from LSV measurements at different potentials.
summary: The K–L plots for GF-CNT@Fe0.5-Ni3 are used to analyze the reaction kinetics at different potentials. By evaluating the slope and intercept of these plots, the electron transfer mechanism during the oxygen reduction reaction can be determined, reflecting the catalytic performance of the Fe0.5-Ni3 composition.

caption: Raman analysis of the reference sample wear track, identifying amorphous carbon species located along the track edges.
summary: Raman spectroscopy performed on the reference sample wear track identifies the presence of amorphous carbon species. These signals are specifically detected along the edges of the wear track. This analysis confirms the chemical nature of the reaction products formed during the tribo-testing process in the absence of MXene lubrication.

caption: Correlation between elastic moduli and calculated Mo-equivalent ([Mo]eq) values for the investigated alloy series.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between the elastic moduli and the calculated Mo-equivalent ([Mo]eq) values for the studied alloys. The data demonstrates a strong correlation between these two parameters, indicating that the elastic properties of the materials are significantly influenced by their specific Mo-equivalent composition.

caption: Fatigue S-N curve for WAAM steel derived from curvature-based local stress analysis.
summary: Depicted here is the fatigue S-N curve for WAAM steel, where local stresses are determined using curvature-based analytical models. This visualization complements the bending-based analysis, offering an alternative perspective on the fatigue life behavior of the material under cyclic loading conditions to ensure accurate structural fatigue life predictions.

caption: Differential scanning calorimetry heating thermogram of an expanded PLA-LW sample, illustrating the thermal response during the first heating cycle.
summary: This DSC heating thermogram characterizes the thermal behavior of an expanded PLA-LW sample. The presence of an enthalpy relaxation phenomenon suggests thermal aging of the material. Furthermore, the data indicates that the 3D printed samples may not have achieved their maximum degree of crystallinity during the printing process.

caption: Voltage charging history of the capacitor during the operation of the IoT node.
summary: This panel displays the voltage charging history of the capacitor during the operation of the IoT node. The data illustrates the energy storage behavior and voltage fluctuations as the capacitor powers the device, providing insight into the performance of the SMFC-powered system during its active duty cycle.

caption: Conceptual representation of the Phase-Field (PF) model, illustrating the continuous field approach used for predicting microstructural evolution.
summary: This panel presents the Phase-Field model, a computational approach used for predicting microstructural evolution. By utilizing continuous field variables, the model provides a framework for simulating complex morphological changes, serving as a complementary predictive tool to the discrete CA model for analyzing material phase transformations and growth phenomena.

caption: Regression coefficients for PLA/TPU 50/50 blend specimens.
summary: Shown are the regression coefficients for the PLA/TPU 50/50 blend, which characterize the influence of printing parameters on the tensile modulus. These values complete the dataset for all compositions, enabling a comprehensive analysis of how printing parameters affect the mechanical properties across the entire range of PLA/TPU blends.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of an AlInN/GaN superlattice featuring an AlInN fraction of 0.964.
summary: This atomic force microscopy image shows the surface morphology of an AlInN/GaN superlattice with an AlInN fraction of 0.964. The observed surface structure remains consistent with the bulk AlInN reference, demonstrating that the superlattice maintains its morphological integrity at this specific AlInN fraction.

caption: Mole fraction of constituent phases as a function of temperature for an alloy containing 0.25 wt% Zr.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the temperature-dependent molar fraction of constituent phases in an alloy with 0.25 wt% Zr. The plot highlights the thermodynamic stability of phases, noting that primary Al3Zr formation is minimal, as the Zr remains largely dissolved within the aluminum matrix during the solidification process.

caption: 3D surface topography of the CX stainless steel sample subjected to a 10 N wear load.
summary: The 3D surface topography of the CX stainless steel sample is visualized after undergoing a wear test at a 10 N load. This reconstruction provides a detailed view of the post-wear morphology, allowing for the assessment of surface degradation and material removal characteristics resulting from the applied mechanical stress.

caption: Deformation behavior represented by the stress-strain plot for the L-6 specimen processed via LPBF.
summary: Displaying the mechanical characteristics of the L-6 specimen, this stress-strain plot provides a clear visualization of the material's response to stress. As part of the comprehensive evaluation of LPBF-processed Ti6-4 specimens, this data point helps characterize the mechanical performance and ductility variations inherent in the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Projected image of interference fringes when a rotation angle is present.
summary: Presence of a rotation angle between the PLM and DMD pixels leads to the misaligned interference fringes shown in this projected image. This visual result demonstrates how rotational errors affect the light field, necessitating careful calibration to eliminate the rotation and ensure accurate alignment of the optical system components.

caption: Redundancy analysis (RDA) triplot displaying CMYK specimen scores and explanatory vectors for luminance Y, with red points indicating specular and near-to-specular scores and blue points representing remaining scores.
summary: This RDA triplot visualizes the relationship between CMYK specimen scores and luminance Y variables. Red points denote specular and near-to-specular data, while blue points represent the remaining scores. The plot incorporates vectors for observed variables θi and θr, providing a comprehensive overview of the specimen distribution and luminance characteristics.

caption: Magnified view of the disordered γ matrix region extracted from the HRSTEM image in panel A, illustrating the atomic arrangement of the matrix phase.
summary: Focusing on the disordered γ matrix, this magnified HRSTEM image allows for a detailed examination of the matrix structure. By isolating this region from the broader interface shown in panel A, the image confirms the presence and structural characteristics of the γ matrix phase in the as-built sample.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto495 dye.
summary: Transmission spectrum for a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto495 dye is displayed. The data characterizes the specific wavelength filtering profile of this dye within the 3D-printed resin, contributing to the comparative analysis of various Atto dyes for potential use in color vision correction devices.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping showing the spatial distribution of carbon within the PA/WS2/AM nanocomposite powder.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping showing the spatial distribution of carbon within the PA/WS2/AM nanocomposite powder. This elemental map confirms the presence and distribution of the polymer matrix component within the composite structure, supporting the structural verification of the advanced mixing preparation method used for the powder.

caption: High magnification field image focusing on the morphology and thickness of the oxide layer formed on the sample surface.
summary: High magnification imaging captures the detailed morphology of the oxide layer formed on the sample surface. These layers are subject to significant stress under high-load conditions, eventually deteriorating and flaking off due to shear forces, which directly contributes to the observed increase in the coefficient of friction during wear.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of irradiated material displaying Fe and Cr enriched regions as blue iso-concentration surfaces, viewed edge-on to highlight the rod-like morphology of the precipitates.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction visualizes Fe and Cr enriched regions within an irradiated sample using iso-concentration surfaces. By displaying the precipitates edge-on, the image demonstrates the characteristic rod-like morphology of the irradiation-induced features, confirming that all rods within the analyzed grain are oriented in a common direction.

caption: Creep strain evolution of the UT sample measured at 27 °C, 37 °C, and 47 °C under a constant holding stress of 8 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the creep response of the UT sample subjected to a constant holding stress of 8 MPa across three distinct temperatures: 27 °C, 37 °C, and 47 °C. The data illustrates the time-dependent deformation behavior of the material under these specific thermal and mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Rheological plot showing the storage modulus (G′), loss modulus (G″), and tan δ of the SilMA/AA/PEGDMA hydrogel as a function of UV exposure time, identifying the 2 s gel point.
summary: This rheological plot presents the storage modulus, loss modulus, and tan δ of the SilMA/AA/PEGDMA hydrogel during 20 s of UV exposure. The data identifies a 2 s gel point, confirming that this duration is the minimum UV exposure required to successfully transition the pre-gel solution into a solid gel.

caption: HAADF-STEM image of the polygonal nanoprecipitates, emphasizing the core-shell structure with sharp interfaces.
summary: HAADF-STEM imaging provides a detailed view of the polygonal nanoprecipitates in the (CrCoNi)94(TiAl)6 MEA. The image highlights the core-shell structure characterized by sharp interfaces, which is a distinct morphological feature of these precipitates. This visualization supports the investigation into the strengthening mechanisms of the additively manufactured material.

caption: Reflectance RL curves demonstrating the collaborative optimization of dual absorption peaks for L5 GMSs.
summary: This panel presents the collaborative optimization results for L5 GMSs, specifically focusing on the dual absorption peaks. The data illustrates the effectiveness of the customized method proposed in the study for tailoring absorption peaks, providing a clear visualization of the optimized electromagnetic response for the L5 configuration.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of the PtFe alloy catalyst in 0.1 M KOH electrolyte under nitrogen- and oxygen-saturated conditions without electrode rotation.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry curves for the PtFe alloy in 0.1 M KOH demonstrate its ORR catalytic activity. In nitrogen-saturated electrolyte, the curve exhibits no obvious reduction peaks but shows an anodic peak at approximately 0.3 V, which is attributed to hydrogen evolution, contrasting with the oxygen-saturated condition.

caption: Yield strength comparison of Diamond and Gyroid structures measured at 400 °C.
summary: This panel shows the yield strength of Diamond and Gyroid structures at 400 °C. The findings indicate that the yield strength of Gyroid structures is significantly improved at this elevated temperature compared to room temperature, reflecting the robust mechanical response of the lattice architecture under thermal loading conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode recorded at scan rates from 15 to 150 mV s−1 in 1 mM [Fe(CN)6]4−, featuring the Randles–Ševčík plot inset.
summary: Electrochemical performance evaluation of the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode using the inner-sphere redox probe [Fe(CN)6]4− at varying scan rates (15–150 mV s−1). The resulting cyclic voltammograms and the Randles–Ševčík plot provide further evidence of the electrode's consistent electrochemical behavior and suitability for diverse redox probe applications.

caption: Apparent crystallite size parallel to the c-axis (ACS∥c) for the Ti-Sr-O miniscrew, mapped across a range of 11.5–28.6 nm.
summary: This map displays the apparent crystallite size parallel to the c-axis for the Ti-Sr-O miniscrew, utilizing a color scale covering 11.5 to 28.6 nm. The data illustrates the spatial distribution of crystallite dimensions parallel to the c-axis, facilitating comparison with the standard Ti miniscrew sample.

caption: Heatmap illustrating the test accuracy of the DADDA model across a comprehensive range of trade-off factor combinations.
summary: This heatmap displays the test accuracy of the DADDA model across a wide range of trade-off factor combinations. Accuracy values exceeding 0.76 are highlighted with black font, while those below this threshold are marked in white, providing a clear visualization of model performance sensitivity to parameter variations.

caption: Deformed geometry of the D-DG lattice structure derived from finite element analysis.
summary: Deformed geometry of the D-DG lattice structure derived from finite element analysis. This visualization provides a detailed view of the structural deformation for the D-DG lattice, showcasing the computational results that describe how this specific geometry behaves under the simulated mechanical conditions applied in the study.

caption: Variable focus reconstruction of the ± 45° specimen fracture surface following tensile testing.
summary: Variable focus reconstruction reveals the fracture surface of the ± 45° specimen after tensile testing. The surface is oriented preferentially at 45° relative to the loading direction. This morphology demonstrates a strong dependency on the underlying 3D porous network, which dictates the specific fracture path observed in the reconstructed image.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the CR750 condition showing an Al 7.8 at.% iso-concentration surface, highlighting the interface between an FCC recrystallized grain and a coarser B2 precipitate.
summary: This APT reconstruction displays the 3D atomic distribution within the CR750 sample. By utilizing an Al 7.8 at.% iso-concentration surface, the visualization captures the structural relationship between a recrystallized FCC matrix grain and an adjacent coarser B2 precipitate, providing site-specific insight into the microstructural features of the recrystallized region.

caption: Zr3d core level XPS spectrum acquired from the Al65Zr20Fe15 ingot after 1 hour of electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl.
summary: This Zr3d core level XPS spectrum details the chemical state of zirconium on the Al65Zr20Fe15 ingot surface after electrochemical corrosion in a 3.5% NaCl environment. The data reflects the surface composition and potential oxide formation on the alloy following the specified one-hour open circuit potential duration.

caption: Defect pair population dynamics in Cu-5at%Ni alloy as a function of irradiation time and PKA energy at 300 K.
summary: The graph displays the temporal evolution of Frenkel defect pairs in Cu-5at%Ni alloy at 300 K across different PKA energies. It highlights how the introduction of 5at% Ni influences the defect production and recovery processes compared to pure copper, as observed through the simulated irradiation time-dependent defect population.

caption: Inverse magnetic susceptibility plotted against temperature for various Fe-Cr-Ni alloys measured in the field-cooled (FC) mode under a 500 Oe DC field, featuring Curie-Weiss law fits (dashed lines) and Eq. (1) fits (solid lines).
summary: This plot displays the inverse magnetic susceptibility of Fe-Cr-Ni alloys measured in FC mode at 500 Oe. Curie-Weiss analysis was performed to characterize long-range magnetic ordering below the Curie temperature. Dashed lines represent Curie-Weiss law fits for high-temperature regions, while solid lines indicate fits to Eq. (1) for the data.

caption: Neutron diffraction patterns for the spot build specimen, illustrating intensity profiles across axial/build and transverse directions.
summary: Neutron diffraction patterns for the spot build specimen are presented, covering both axial/build and transverse directions. These patterns reveal the dominant presence of {200} orientation, resembling a single crystal. Each run number corresponds to a specific load applied during the in-situ measurement, providing insight into the material's structural response.

caption: Conceptual overview of the primary research challenges and prospective future directions associated with the Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) process.
summary: This diagram illustrates the critical research challenges and future development pathways for the WAAM process. It serves as a high-level conceptual framework, identifying the key technical hurdles that currently define the research landscape and outlining the strategic directions necessary for advancing the maturity and application of WAAM technology in manufacturing.

caption: In-plane strain contours for 20 wt % GμB reinforced Schwarz diamond structures, showing the distribution of strain components as a function of increasing global strain.
summary: Reinforced 20 wt % GμB Schwarz diamond structures display strain localization patterns similar to neat samples under compression. DIC mapping highlights the concentration of lateral compressive strains and vertical tensile strains within the struts. These observed strain fields are attributed to the nonuniform topology and shape anisotropy of the TPMS structures.

caption: EPMA elemental distribution map of Ni in the as-deposited sample, demonstrating uniform distribution within the gamma matrix.
summary: The EPMA map of Ni shows a uniform distribution throughout the as-deposited sample. This homogeneity indicates that Ni is primarily involved in the formation of the gamma matrix, maintaining a consistent concentration profile that aligns with the structural uniformity observed in the corresponding SEM micrograph of the dendritic structure.

caption: HAADF-STEM micrograph showing heterogeneous bright spots at the intercellular boundaries, indicating the presence of particles.
summary: This HAADF-STEM micrograph provides a high-contrast view of the intercellular boundaries in as-printed IN718. The image reveals heterogeneous bright spots, which indicate the existence of discrete particles segregated at these boundaries. These particles are distinct from the surrounding matrix and are associated with local elemental enrichment.

caption: EELS elemental intensity profiles showing the chemical composition across the interface, highlighting high concentrations of Nb and Al in the precipitates and a sharp increase in C intensity at the phase boundary.
summary: These EELS profiles quantify the elemental composition across the precipitate/matrix interface. The data reveals that the precipitates are enriched in Nb and Al while depleted in Cr and Fe. Furthermore, the sharp increase in C intensity at the interface confirms the strong enrichment of carbon in the phase.

caption: Detailed breakdown of the pseudocapacitive contribution within the CV profile at a scan rate of 1 mVs-1.
summary: The CV profile at a scan rate of 1 mVs-1 is analyzed to show the specific pseudocapacitive contribution. This detailed visualization highlights the portion of the current response attributed to surface-controlled processes, providing a clear representation of the capacitive storage component within the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode system.

caption: Rate capability performance for the 3D LFP-GO electrode ranging from C/25 to C/4.
summary: Rate capability performance for the 3D LFP-GO electrode is shown ranging from C/25 to C/4. Measured in a full cell configuration with LTO/LP30, this plot depicts the specific capacity of the 3D LFP-GO electrode, illustrating its electrochemical rate capability and performance consistency across the tested range of C-rates.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for (LuNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattices, indicating the half-metallic gap and mean magnetic moments for Ni-3d and O-2p states.
summary: Panel i presents the PDOS for the Lu-based superlattice. It reports the half-metallic gap of the down-spin channel and the mean magnetic moments for Ni-3d and O-2p states. This final panel in the series confirms the decreasing trend in the half-metallic gap observed from La to Lu superlattices.

caption: Non-local analysis of fatigue strength under pure shear loading for gas pores, resulting in a decreased anisotropy factor of λ = 1.10.
summary: Non-local spherical plot analysis for gas pores indicates a 15% reduction in the anisotropy factor, dropping from 1.29 in the local analysis to 1.10. This trend mirrors the behavior observed in LoF defects, confirming that non-local modeling consistently reduces the calculated anisotropy for different types of fatigue-inducing defects.

caption: Time-resolved evolution of discharge current and discharge voltage during the pulse on-time, evaluated at an argon pressure of 2 Pa for varying pulse frequencies and two distinct duty cycles.
summary: This plot illustrates the temporal behavior of discharge current and voltage during pulse on-time cycles at 2 Pa argon pressure. By varying pulse frequencies and duty cycles, the data demonstrates how reduced pulse off-times, resulting from increased frequency, directly influence the discharge characteristics and current pulse profiles observed during operation.

caption: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM image of deformation twins and HCP layers in [1-23]-oriented Cr-Co-Ni single crystals deformed in tension slightly beyond the inflection point.
summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM imaging reveals deformation twins and thin HCP layers in [1-23]-oriented Cr-Co-Ni single crystals deformed in tension beyond the inflection point. These thin HCP layers are clearly resolved with <110>-type incidence, and isolated thick HCP layers are occasionally observed without association with twins, as shown in panel a2.

caption: Cooling DSC curves for SOL-condition samples aged at 450 °C for 1, 6, and 12 hours, displaying a consistent two-step formation process.
summary: Cooling DSC curves for SOL-condition samples aged at 450 °C for 1, 6, and 12 hours consistently yield a two-step formation process. This behavior is characterized by the presence of the intermediate R phase, which remains a stable feature in the cooling cycle regardless of the specific aging duration.

caption: OCN immunofluorescence staining (green) of bone regeneration sites at 4 and 12 weeks, visualizing osteocalcin expression as a marker for osteogenic activity.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining for OCN demonstrates varying levels of osteogenic activity across experimental groups at 4 and 12 weeks. Both BMP-2/VEGF/BMSC and BMP-2/BMSC groups exhibit stronger OCN signals than controls, with the BMP-2/VEGF/BMSC group showing the most potent osteogenic capacity, confirming enhanced bone formation through these specific therapeutic combinations.

caption: Optimized molecular structure of MBT showing the spatial arrangement of nitrogen, sulfur, carbon, and hydrogen atoms.
summary: The optimized atomic structure of MBT is presented, illustrating the specific configuration of nitrogen, sulfur, carbon, and hydrogen atoms. This structural model serves as the foundational geometry for subsequent electronic property calculations, including Fukui indices and orbital analysis, to determine the molecule's reactivity and susceptibility to various chemical attacks.

caption: Fracture of dendritic arms resulting from the composite field action, leading to the formation of fragments.
summary: Depicted here is the fracture of dendritic arms, which follows the initial remelting phase. These resulting dendrite fragments are subsequently transferred from the interface into the high-temperature liquid region, where they undergo further remelting. This mechanism is central to the grain refinement process promoted by the ultrasonic-magnetic composite field treatment.

caption: Raman spectra acquired from particles located on the surface of the monoliths, showing characteristic vibrational bands.
summary: Raman spectra obtained from particles on the monolith surface are presented in panel a. These spectra reveal distinct Raman bands that correspond to the spinel Co3O4 phase. This analysis confirms the presence and chemical state of the cobalt-based particles distributed across the surface of the sintered monolith materials.

caption: Absorbance values of h-BN/PVSA slurries with varying h-BN mass fractions from 0 to 10 wt%.
summary: The absorbance values of the slurries are plotted for h-BN mass fractions ranging from 0 wt% to 10 wt%. The data demonstrates a clear positive correlation, where the absorbance value of the slurries increases consistently as the h-BN content increases, reaching 3.12 at 10 wt% loading.

caption: In-plane displacement gradient tensor component Hxy in grain G2 at a tensile strain of 0.046.
summary: Component Hxy of the in-plane displacement gradient tensor is presented for grain G2 at 0.046 strain. The map illustrates the shear-direction displacement gradients resulting from non-uniform deformation. Slip bands are identified by dashed red arrows, reflecting the localized strain concentrations that develop across the grain during the tensile process.

caption: Flowchart illustrating the iterative density updating procedure for additive manufacturing optimization, highlighting the distinction between individual optimization steps and the broader SIMP iterative process.
summary: This flowchart depicts the density updating procedure for additive manufacturing optimization. It illustrates how elements outside the target density range are fixed after each optimization process. The diagram distinguishes between individual steps within the coarse problem loop and the broader iterative process required for each SIMP application, ensuring systematic structural refinement.

caption: UMAP dimensionality reduction projection of 100 initial morphologies, where data points are colored according to their measured locomotion speeds.
summary: This UMAP projection visualizes the 225-dimensional binary encodings of 100 initial morphologies generated via Latin-hypercube sampling. The plot illustrates the distribution of these morphologies in a reduced parameter space, with individual points color-coded by their corresponding locomotion speeds to highlight baseline morphology-performance relationships and ensure broad coverage for design exploration.

caption: SHAP scatter diagram of heat intensity (HI) versus porosity, displaying two opposing trends where increasing HI values can either promote or inhibit pore formation, suggesting complex competing physical effects.
summary: Heat intensity exhibits two opposing trends in its influence on surface porosity, as shown in this SHAP scatter plot. Higher heat intensity values generally correspond to greater absolute SHAP values, reflecting the complex, dual nature of energy density in both causing keyhole pores and potentially healing lack-of-fusion porosity.

caption: Comparative creep curves for HT samples tested at 980 °C and 250 MPa, contrasting specimens prepared without and with a 0.06 T alternating magnetic field (AMF).
summary: Creep curves for HT samples at 980 °C and 250 MPa reveal a significant improvement in creep life when using a 0.06 T AMF. Specifically, the creep life of the alloy increased from 62 hours for the 0 T sample to 102 hours for the sample treated with a 0.06 T AMF.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the NAB alloy substrate, showing random grain orientation in the cross-section perpendicular to the build direction.
summary: The inverse pole figure map of the NAB alloy substrate reveals a random grain orientation distribution. This analysis, performed on the cross-section perpendicular to the build direction, confirms that the substrate microstructure is characterized by randomly oriented grains, consistent with the observed structural features of the wire-arc DED processed material.

caption: WDS elemental mapping of Cobalt and Nickel distribution in the HVOF 1 coating cross-section.
summary: Wavelength-dispersive spectroscopy elemental mapping of Cobalt and Nickel provides a detailed view of the metallic matrix composition within the HVOF 1 coating. These maps complement the Aluminum and Oxygen data, illustrating the distribution of the primary alloying elements throughout the cross-section of the thermally sprayed material.

caption: Time-temperature transformation profile for the H13 specimen processed with 40 mA thermal compensation.
summary: The 40 mA specimen profile reveals that the substrate temperature is sustained above the austenite transformation temperature (A1). This condition ensures a prolonged period of austenitization before cooling commences, which is a key factor in the thermal history that dictates the final microstructure and carbide precipitation behavior.

caption: CALPHAD phase stability diagram for the 48% Ni-41.5% Fe-8.1% Ti-1.55% Cr alloy composition at point 5, located at the weld center.
summary: Thermodynamic calculations for the 48% Ni-41.5% Fe-8.1% Ti-1.55% Cr composition at point 5 confirm that the gamma phase is the stable primary phase at the weld center. This result aligns with the observed microstructural characteristics of the central weld region during the thermodynamic analysis of the specimen.

caption: Infrared spectra of 3D-printed geopolymer samples aged for 4 hours under varying microwave heating conditions.
summary: Infrared spectra of 3D-printed geopolymers aged for 4 hours under various microwave heating conditions are presented. The 998 cm-1 peak corresponds to Si-O-Si (Al) asymmetric stretching, while the 452 cm-1 peak represents Si-O-Si in-plane bending, both indicating the formation of C-A-S-H gel and the progress of geopolymerization.

caption: Atomic model of crystalline CrOOH showing the stacking of atomic planes.
summary: This atomic model of crystalline CrOOH illustrates the stacking of atomic planes. Red spheres represent oxygen, white spheres represent hydrogen, and colored spheres represent metal atoms. The gray arrow indicates the crystallographic stacking direction, providing a structural reference for interpreting the experimentally determined thickness of the hydroxide layer.

caption: Atomic model of the MWCNTs/Al–Mg–Sc–Zr composite represented as a cuboid with dimensions of 56 × 56 × 56 lattice parameters, where red spheres denote Al atoms and blue spheres denote C atoms.
summary: The atomic model for the MWCNTs/Al–Mg–Sc–Zr composite is depicted as a cuboid structure measuring 56 × 56 × 56 lattice parameters, with a lattice parameter of 4.05 Å. Red spheres represent aluminum atoms, while blue spheres represent carbon atoms, providing a detailed visualization of the composite's structural arrangement for computational analysis.

caption: Total failure energy and critical stress intensity factor (Kc) of the USWed joints plotted against welding energy.
summary: Total failure energy, defined as the area under the load-displacement curve up to the maximum load, is plotted alongside the critical stress intensity factor (Kc) for the USWed AA7075-HSLA joints. These metrics are presented as a function of welding energy to characterize the fracture behavior and toughness of the joints.

caption: BF-TEM image illustrating the presence of nano-phases within the Cu-4.84Ni-1.04Si-0.5Ti alloy matrix.
summary: This BF-TEM image captures the nanoscale precipitates distributed throughout the Cu-4.84Ni-1.04Si-0.5Ti alloy. The visualization confirms the existence of these nano-phases, which are critical to the alloy's mechanical properties, and serves as the basis for subsequent compositional mapping and detailed structural analysis of the precipitates.

caption: Atomic configuration showing partial dislocation nucleation from the corner of a perfectly shaped Ni3Al nanocrystal using the DWY potential.
summary: This MD snapshot illustrates the heterogeneous nucleation of 1/6 < 112 >{111} partial dislocations from the corner of a perfectly cubic Ni3Al nanocrystal. Using the DWY potential, the simulation confirms that nanocrystal corners act as preferential nucleation sites for plastic deformation under [001] compression conditions.

caption: Total deformation profile of the specimen processed using the CSD strategy.
summary: The total deformation profile of the specimen processed using the CSD strategy is illustrated. By comparing this to the HSD strategy, the impact of deposition methods on thermal management is highlighted. The CSD strategy demonstrates the resulting deformation patterns when progressive heat buildup is not mitigated by hybrid deposition techniques.

caption: Ascorbic acid content values for gels formulated with acerola pulp, native maize starch, DHT-modified maize starch, and pea protein.
summary: This table presents the quantitative ascorbic acid content measured in various gel formulations. The samples incorporate acerola pulp combined with different starch types, specifically native and DHT-modified maize starch, alongside pea protein. These measurements provide essential data regarding the nutritional composition and antioxidant potential of the developed food-grade gel materials.

caption: ATR-FTIR absorbance spectra of CFRP, illustrating progressive chemical modifications resulting from UV-induced oxidation and polymer matrix rearrangement.
summary: CFRP samples exhibit progressive chemical changes when subjected to UV exposure, as evidenced by the normalized ATR-FTIR spectra. These spectral shifts indicate that UV radiation drives significant oxidation and rearrangement within the polymer matrix, highlighting the susceptibility of the CFRP composite to chemical degradation over the duration of the experiment.

caption: Polarization curves comparing the electrochemical performance of three tubular cells against a reference planar cell, designated Pl-2-07.
summary: This panel displays polarization curves used to evaluate the electrochemical performance and reproducibility of three tubular cells in comparison to a planar cell, Pl-2-07. These curves provide a direct assessment of the cell behavior under operating conditions, serving as a baseline for analyzing the consistency across different cell geometries.
