caption: Atomic configuration and charge transfer for an O adatom adsorbed at the hollow site of the NiCr(1) surface.
summary: This panel illustrates the atomic configuration of an O adatom at the hollow site of the NiCr(1) surface. It highlights the charge transfer between the surface Cr atom and the O adatom, demonstrating the surface distortion characteristic of this specific hollow site configuration.

caption: Liquid bridge formation under 1 g gravity directed at +Z (180°) with 150 W laser power and 120 mm/min wire feeding and movement speeds.
summary: The transient metal wire melting process is shown during a single deposition. With 1 g gravity oriented at +Z (180°), the liquid bridge is observed under 150 W laser power and 120 mm/min wire feeding and movement speeds, demonstrating the influence of gravity direction on the melting behavior.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the Fe60 alloy central lamella, highlighting similarly oriented grains with low-angle boundaries within the matrix FCC (cF4) phase.
summary: The dark-field TEM image illustrates the central lamella of the Fe60 alloy, focusing on the matrix FCC (cF4) phase. It reveals several separated grains that share similar orientations and are separated by low-angle boundaries, confirming the presence of a refined, oriented grain structure within the annealed and USSP-treated sample.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves for TPMS samples, providing the rate of mass loss to complement the TG degradation data.
summary: DTG curves for TPMS samples are presented to complement the TG analysis. These curves provide the rate of mass loss during the thermal degradation process, confirming the single-step degradation behavior observed in the TG curves within the 280 to 380 degrees Celsius temperature range.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loop of flash annealed (Fe70Ni30)85Nb0.5B14.5 ribbons treated at 450 °C for 5 s, exhibiting low coercivity and soft magnetic properties.
summary: Flash annealed (Fe70Ni30)85Nb0.5B14.5 ribbons treated at 450 °C for 5 s exhibit low coercivity and optimal soft magnetic properties. This improved magnetic performance is directly attributed to the refined nanocrystalline microstructure achieved through the flash annealing process, contrasting with the coarser structures found in conventionally annealed samples.

caption: Simulated IN625 microstructure cross-section at a build plane depth of 150 μm, highlighting grain morphology at the center of the scan path.
summary: Representing the simulated IN625 microstructure at a build plane depth of 150 μm, this panel focuses on the grain morphology observed at the center of the scan path. The grains are colored based on their crystal orientation, providing insight into the simulated material structure under the specified processing conditions.

caption: Confocal microscopy images of the complex tissue captured at three distinct focal depths, revealing the spatial distribution of GFP-HUVECs on the microgel surface and the red-stained fibroblasts within the skin layer.
summary: Confocal microscopy imaging at three different focal lengths confirms the successful integration of the tissue components. Both the GFP-HUVECs coated onto the microgel surface and the fibroblasts stained with Cell Tracker CM-Dil in the skin layer are clearly observed, demonstrating the structural organization of the complex tissue at varying depths.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of an aluminum nanoparticle showing a slightly increased surface roughness compared to the smooth baseline.
summary: Representing the second stage in the progression of surface roughness, this transmission electron microscopy image captures an aluminum nanoparticle with a slightly textured surface. The image illustrates the transition from a smooth morphology toward a rougher state within the synthesized nanoparticle population.

caption: Tabulated chemical composition of five baseline alloy variants expressed in weight percentage (wt%) of Si and Mg.
summary: This table presents the specific chemical composition for five distinct variants of a baseline alloy, detailing the weight percentage of silicon and magnesium. These values serve as the foundational input parameters for subsequent precipitation modeling and are used to define the compositional window for the alloy variants.

caption: Fracture toughness (KIC) values for PETG-based fiber-reinforced specimens under mode I loading conditions.
summary: This panel displays the fracture toughness results for PETG-based materials under mode I loading conditions. The plot highlights how fiber reinforcement affects the fracture toughness of the PETG matrix, offering a clear comparison of the mechanical performance and crack resistance characteristics observed during the mode I fracture testing experiments.

caption: Magnetic entropy change of fabricated nanowires plotted against temperature, showing a peak value of approximately 2.5 J.kg-1.K-1 at 350 K under a 2 T applied magnetic field.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic entropy change of fabricated nanowires as a function of temperature. A distinct peak in entropy change, reaching approximately 2.5 J.kg-1.K-1, is observed at 350 K under a 2 T magnetic field. The data indicates that the peak begins to emerge at 330 K.

caption: Grain Orientation Spread (GOS) map of coarse and secondary recrystallized grains, illustrating internal misorientation differences.
summary: This GOS map highlights the internal misorientation within coarse and secondary recrystallized grains. The data shows that while the misorientation angle within primary recrystallized grains remains below 1.5°, it increases significantly at the boundaries of secondary recrystallized grains, reflecting distinct structural differences between these grain populations.

caption: Liquid-phase projection of the Ti–B–C ternary phase diagram focused on the titanium-rich corner, highlighting the solidification path of composite powders as a red dot.
summary: This panel presents the liquid-phase projection of the Ti–B–C ternary phase diagram within the titanium-rich corner. It specifically identifies the solidification path of the composite powder samples, marked by a red dot, which serves as a reference point for understanding the phase evolution during the melting process.

caption: Spin-resolved total density of states (DOS) for Ni3Al (dark green), Ni3Al0.875Fe0.125 (blue), and Ni2.875Fe0.125Al (red) calculated via DFT methods.
summary: This plot displays the spin-resolved total density of states for three distinct nickel-aluminum alloy configurations. The data compares pure Ni3Al with iron-doped variants, specifically Ni3Al0.875Fe0.125 and Ni2.875Fe0.125Al, each at a concentration of 0.125. These calculations provide insight into the electronic structure modifications resulting from iron substitution in the Ni3Al lattice.

caption: Dark-field TEM image obtained using the ̅100α reflection, highlighting specific precipitate features within the ferrite matrix.
summary: Captured using the ̅100α reflection, this dark-field TEM image highlights specific precipitate features within the ferrite matrix. By isolating this reflection, the micrograph reveals the spatial distribution and morphology of the hardening phases that contribute to the diffuse spots observed in the diffraction analysis of the hardened material.

caption: Representative stress–strain behavior of cellular materials under compression, illustrating the characteristic deformation stages observed in cellular solids.
summary: This plot displays the characteristic stress–strain behavior of cellular materials during compression. The curve exhibits typical mechanical responses for cellular solids, which are essential for determining material toughness. Toughness is calculated by integrating the area under this stress–strain curve up to the densification point, providing a measure of energy absorption.

caption: X–Z plane Inverse Pole Figure of NiTi alloy sample 9# fabricated at 1000 W laser power.
summary: This Inverse Pole Figure shows the X–Z plane grain orientation for the NiTi alloy sample 9# processed at 1000 W. The visualization provides a detailed view of the crystallographic texture along the cross-section, illustrating how the 1000 W laser power setting affects the grain structure during the SLM fabrication process.

caption: Spider graph showing the percentage of voids measured in specimens throughout the recycling process.
summary: Void percentage results are presented in this spider graph to characterize the structural integrity of specimens across different ASA recycling course levels. The plot provides a summary of how internal porosity evolves during the recycling process, highlighting differences in material quality relative to the first course of the M-H system.

caption: Additional selected area electron diffraction pattern acquired at 50 mA to confirm phase presence.
summary: Representing a secondary SAED pattern at 50 mA, this panel confirms the structural findings for the Ti–10V–2Fe–3Al alloy. The diffraction data consistently shows that the omega phase remains present in the alloy at higher electron beam currents, validating the stability of the phase distribution under these conditions.

caption: Ti-2p core level X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectrum and corresponding peak fitting results for the aged Ni55Ti40Hf5 alloy.
summary: This panel displays the Ti-2p core level XPS spectrum for the aged Ni55Ti40Hf5 alloy. The data includes the measured spectral intensity plotted against binding energy, accompanied by detailed peak fitting results. These results characterize the chemical state of titanium within the aged alloy matrix, providing essential information on its electronic environment.

caption: Bode magnitude plots displaying impedance values across a frequency range for SS316L samples, highlighting higher impedance in the low-frequency region for samples produced at lower scanning speeds (800–900 mm/s).
summary: Bode magnitude plots reveal the impedance characteristics of the SS316L samples. Samples fabricated at lower scanning speeds, specifically in the 800–900 mm/s range, exhibit higher impedance values, particularly within the low-frequency region, suggesting improved corrosion resistance compared to samples produced at higher scanning speeds.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image of the worn surface of the Fe-Cr-V-B-C sample following abrasive wear testing, revealing the surface morphology and wear mechanisms.
summary: Surface morphology of the Fe-Cr-V-B-C sample after abrasive wear testing is visualized using scanning electron microscopy. This phenomenological investigation aims to reveal the underlying wear mechanisms responsible for the material's performance, providing insight into the surface degradation characteristics observed after the pin-on-disc wear test.

caption: Wavelength-dependent absorbance spectra comparing alumina-based LTCC powders to pure Al2O3.
summary: The absorbance spectra demonstrate that the LTCC powder absorbs 405 nm light approximately eight times more strongly than pure Al2O3. This increased absorption, attributed to the presence of an amorphous glassy phase, presents a significant challenge for the photocuring process during additive manufacturing of these ceramic materials.

caption: Static FEA simulation of deformation concentration in the G slab bicycle helmet liner under front loading.
summary: This simulation result visualizes the deformation concentration within the G slab bicycle helmet liner during front loading. The model provides a computational representation of how the helmet structure deforms under frontal compression, serving as a comparative baseline for evaluating the performance of the embedded capacitor sensor array.

caption: Experimental current-voltage (I-V) data compared against simulated curves generated via TSEC (I4,3,1 and I4,4,1) for an RTC France PV solar cell, utilizing FDM parameters extracted through the SNF-TSEC approach.
summary: This panel displays the I-V characteristics of an RTC France PV solar cell. It compares experimental data with simulated curves generated by the TSEC method using FDM parameters from the SNF-TSEC approach. The results demonstrate a strong agreement between the generated I-V curves and the actual experimental measurements.

caption: DC four-probe conductivity measurements for PCL/BT composites with varying BaTiO₃ concentrations.
summary: DC four-probe data for PCL/BT composites reveal a numerical decrease in resistivity and a corresponding numerical increase in electrical conductivity as the BaTiO₃ content increases. These results indicate that the addition of BaTiO₃ filler effectively modulates the electronic transport properties of the PCL matrix.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-built sample showing an acicular α' martensitic microstructure.
summary: The as-built sample exhibits an acicular α' martensitic microstructure, as visualized through the inverse pole figure map. This EBSD analysis highlights the initial grain structure prior to any heat treatment, providing a baseline for comparing the microstructural evolution and phase composition changes observed in the subsequent HT-1050 processed sample.

caption: Electron intensity map across an 80 mm diameter circular area, illustrating the TiB2 piece placement within the vacuum chamber.
summary: The electron intensity map provides a spatial overview of an 80 mm diameter circular region within the vacuum chamber. It effectively demonstrates the precise positioning of the TiB2 piece relative to the chamber environment prior to the initiation of the spot exposure testing procedure.

caption: Elemental distribution maps and AFM topography of the NCCG-PNC wear track, detailing the surface composition and structural features.
summary: EDS mapping and AFM topography provide insights into the NCCG-PNC wear track surface. These maps visualize the distribution of C, O, N, S, and Ni elements. Combined with tribological data, these results help characterize the wear behavior and surface composition of the NCCG-PNC composite after sliding tests.

caption: Magnetic entropy change (-ΔSM) curves of Er20Gd20Dy20Co20Al20 microwires plotted against temperature under varying magnetic field strengths.
summary: The magnetic entropy change (-ΔSM) curves for Er20Gd20Dy20Co20Al20 microwires are presented across different magnetic fields. These values exhibit a temperature-dependent behavior, where they initially increase with rising temperature and reach distinct peaks in the vicinity of the Curie temperature (TC), characterizing the magnetocaloric response of the material.

caption: Cr2O3 oxide phase crystal structure and its simulated XRD pattern.
summary: This panel illustrates the Cr2O3 oxide phase, featuring its crystal structure and simulated XRD pattern. It is part of the system-specific diffraction library, providing the necessary data to identify this prospective oxide phase and differentiate it from other phases in the system.

caption: Comparison of exchange current densities (j0) for LNPs-CFC and control electrodes, highlighting the maximum value of 5.64 mA cm-2 achieved by the LNPs-CFC sample.
summary: Exchange current densities are compared between LNPs-CFC and control electrodes to evaluate interfacial kinetics. The LNPs-CFC electrode achieves a maximum exchange current density of 5.64 mA cm-2, demonstrating significantly rapid Li-ion transfer kinetics at the electrode/electrolyte interface compared to the control samples.

caption: Enlarged EBSD inverse pole figure map focusing on the fracture surface, revealing the presence of randomly oriented equiaxed grains alongside cavities.
summary: This enlarged EBSD inverse pole figure map provides a detailed view of the fracture surface in the crept DS CM247LC sample. It clearly shows the presence of randomly oriented equiaxed grains and cavities, offering insight into the localized microstructural changes and grain evolution that occur during the high-temperature creep failure process.

caption: Statistical distribution of α-colony size across four distinct build heights (P1–P4), representing aggregated data from BD–TD, BD–DD, and DD–TD planes.
summary: This box plot illustrates the variation in α-colony size measured at four different build heights, labeled P1 through P4. The statistics are derived from data averaged across the BD–TD, BD–DD, and DD–TD planes, providing a comprehensive overview of the structural morphology resulting from the recrystallized β-rich state during cooling.

caption: Load-displacement curves comparing MEX D2 HT and Wrought D2 HT specimens.
summary: Load-displacement curves for MEX D2 HT and Wrought D2 HT are presented. The data reveals that MEX D2 HT exhibits a steeper slope and a higher maximum load compared to the Wrought D2 HT specimen, which indicates a stronger matrix response for the MEX processed material under nano-indentation testing conditions.

caption: Overlapping projection of UV and blue light patterns captured by a CMOS camera, highlighting the alignment of the two wavelengths.
summary: The overlapping regions and gaps between the UV and blue light patterns are captured by a CMOS camera. By analyzing the pixel values within this combined image, the alignment precision between the two wavelengths is assessed, revealing how the projected patterns interact and overlap in the experimental setup.

caption: Force-displacement (Fr-Δ2) curve derived from Monte Carlo simulations using connection model 1, with a dashed red line indicating the service limit state (SLS) at a node displacement of l/250.
summary: This panel displays the Fr-Δ2 curve obtained from Monte Carlo simulations for connection model 1. The curve represents the resisting force at a node under monotonic loading conditions. A vertical dashed red line marks the service limit state, defined as a node displacement of l/250, providing a critical design threshold.

caption: Loss factor (tanδ) of VeroWhite specimens as a function of different absorbed doses.
summary: The loss factor, or tanδ, is presented for VeroWhite specimens across a range of absorbed doses. This plot characterizes the damping properties and energy dissipation behavior of the material, highlighting how radiation-induced changes influence the viscoelastic response of the specimens during the dynamic mechanical testing process.

caption: Open circuit potential (OCP) curves of the Ti–Mg composite measured after immersion in 0.9 wt% NaCl solution for 3, 7, and 14 days.
summary: The open circuit potential curves illustrate the electrochemical stability of the Ti–Mg composite over a two-week immersion period in a 0.9 wt% NaCl solution. These measurements, taken at 3, 7, and 14 days, provide insight into the surface potential evolution and corrosion behavior of the composite material in saline environments.

caption: Radar plot illustrating the quantified atomic percentage of elements present in particles categorized by boundary type.
summary: The radar plot visualizes the quantified atomic percentages of elements within particles across various boundary categories. It highlights concentration variations that align with the trends observed in the mean chemical spectra, confirming consistent elemental distribution patterns across the different boundary types analyzed in the study.

caption: Secondary electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS 2) Bode phase plot demonstrating the electrochemical response of LPBF planes after passivation, characterized by increased phase angles and shifts toward higher frequencies.
summary: The secondary EIS 2 Bode phase plot illustrates the electrochemical behavior of LPBF planes following passivation. The observed increase in phase angles and the shift toward higher frequencies indicate the formation of a more stable and protective passive film, confirming the effectiveness of the passivation treatment on the material surface.

caption: Microhardness measurements plotted against build height for low and high Fe content samples in both as-deposited and HIP conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the microhardness values as a function of build height for low and high Fe content builds. Comparing as-deposited and HIP conditions, the results demonstrate that microhardness values remain consistent across different locations, showing no significant dependence on build height for either Fe content level.

caption: Principal component analysis of the dataset, where individual data points are colour-coded to represent the formed clusters identified through the elbow method.
summary: This principal component analysis plot visualizes the data after clustering, with points colour-coded by their assigned cluster. This representation complements the initial PCA by showing how the data points are grouped based on the optimal cluster number, further revealing the distinct distribution patterns and unique properties of the mixture data.

caption: GD-OES depth profile of A59 alloy showing elemental mass concentration after polarization at 1100 mV vs Ag/AgCl.
summary: This GD-OES depth profile for A59 alloy at 1100 mV illustrates the elemental distribution within the oxide film under transpassive conditions. The profile highlights the oxide thickness and significant shifts in elemental composition compared to the passive range, reflecting the impact of increased anodic polarization on the film's chemical structure.

caption: Detailed geometry of the sonotrode pattern, featuring pyramidal-shaped knurls with a 1 mm spacing between adjacent tips to prevent sheet slippage during the welding process.
summary: The sonotrode geometry is depicted, highlighting the pyramidal-shaped knurl pattern used in the welding process. The distance between adjacent knurl tips is set to 1 mm to effectively prevent sheet slippage. This configuration, along with the four microweld rows, influences the force distribution observed during subsequent mechanical testing.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves of G/Pt-Ni catalysts in N2-saturated 1 M KOH at 50 mV/s, with current normalized to total metal loading and an inset showing graphene behavior.
summary: Panel b presents cyclic voltammetry curves for G/Pt-Ni catalysts in a N2-saturated 1 M KOH solution. The data, collected at a 50 mV/s scan rate between -1 V and 0.5 V, features current normalized to total metal loading, with an inset providing the cyclic voltammogram of pure graphene for comparison.

caption: DMA performance metrics, specifically flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus, for the sixth ASA recycling course sample as a function of temperature.
summary: The sixth ASA recycling course is analyzed via DMA, with graphs showing flexural modulus, storage modulus, tan(δ), and loss modulus plotted against temperature. These results complete the set of six recycling courses, offering a detailed view of the material's mechanical evolution throughout the entire experimental sequence.

caption: Interior perspective of the spectroscopy chamber, highlighting the internal configuration and environment where the irradiation experiments are conducted.
summary: The interior view of the spectroscopy chamber provides a visual representation of the experimental environment. This setup is designed to house the samples during irradiation tests, ensuring that the conditions within the chamber are controlled and optimized for accurate spectroscopic analysis of the materials under investigation.

caption: High-temperature yield strength comparison of K4800, K4800W, and K4800Co alloys, illustrating the temperature-dependent degradation behavior.
summary: This plot compares the yield strength of K4800, K4800W, and K4800Co alloys at elevated temperatures. While W and Co additions slightly reduce the strength of K4800 at 800 °C, they effectively delay the strength degradation of the base alloy at temperatures exceeding 800 °C, demonstrating improved high-temperature mechanical stability.

caption: Optical transmission spectra of the sample after initial UV exposure, showing the spectral response to a 3.15 mW/cm2 intensity source.
summary: This panel displays the optical transmission spectra of the sample following initial UV exposure. The measurements were conducted in a UV chamber with an intensity of 3.15 mW/cm2. These spectra illustrate the baseline change in transmission characteristics as the material interacts with the ultraviolet light source over time.

caption: Regions of interest defined for stereo digital image correlation (DIC) analysis, specifically isolating internal cell wall surfaces and external strut surfaces to resolve strain states within the Schwarz diamond meta-structures during loading.
summary: Digital image correlation is utilized to quantify strain development within the 3D printed meta-structures. By defining specific regions of interest on internal cell walls and external struts, the stereo DIC setup resolves strain states as a function of loading history and reinforcing weight ratios, enabling detailed mechanical characterization of the geometry.

caption: Detailed view of the (4 2 0) diffraction peak for the A1 noHT, A1 HT1, and A1 HT2 samples at 423 K.
summary: A detailed view of the (4 2 0) diffraction peak is provided for the A1 noHT, A1 HT1, and A1 HT2 samples at 423 K. By inspecting these diffractogram peaks corresponding to the cubic austenite phase, the presence of internal stresses can be deduced for the different material processing conditions.

caption: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) curves comparing the viscoelastic response of neat and CNT-loaded 3D-printed resin samples.
summary: DMA curves reveal the influence of CNT incorporation on the mechanical properties of the 3D-printed resin. The results confirm that adding CNTs increases the elastic modulus of the material without significantly altering the glass transition temperature, which remains consistently observed at approximately 7–8 °C for both sample types.

caption: Carbon elemental distribution map corresponding to the STEM region in panel (a).
summary: The carbon elemental distribution map, derived from EDXS analysis of the cell boundary region, highlights the spatial arrangement of carbon within the as-built Fe-Cr-V-B-C microstructure. This map, alongside other elemental distributions, helps identify the chemical composition of the phases present in the cell wall.

caption: Interface between the CuAlFeNiMn HEA deposit and the substrate, showing a dense and continuous fusion zone.
summary: This SEM image displays the interface between the as-printed CuAlFeNiMn HEA and the substrate. A dense and continuous fusion zone is clearly visible, indicating strong metallurgical bonding between the deposit and the substrate. This interfacial integrity is essential for structural applications requiring high adhesion and durability under mechanical loads.

caption: Schematic design of a simple cubic (SC) unit cell, representing one of the constituent symmetries of the plate-based lattice.
summary: The simple cubic (SC) unit cell is illustrated as a fundamental building block for the plate-based lattice structure. This geometry is combined with FCC symmetry to construct the final SCFCC lattice configuration analyzed in the study.

caption: Projected density of states for Ni atoms within the Fe3Ni(111) bimetallic surface, where the d-band center shifts to −2.05 eV.
summary: This panel illustrates the projected density of states for Ni atoms in the Fe3Ni(111) bimetallic surface. The d-band center shifts to −2.05 eV compared to the pure Ni(111) surface. This shift in the electronic structure is a key factor contributing to the optimized catalytic performance observed in the bimetallic system.

caption: Coefficient of friction (COF) evolution plotted against the number of cycles for as-printed NiTi alloy specimens.
summary: This plot illustrates the frictional behavior of as-printed NiTi alloys by tracking the coefficient of friction (COF) as a function of the number of cycles. The data provides a dynamic view of the wear performance, showing how the frictional resistance changes throughout the duration of the tribological testing process.

caption: Training performance of the conventional TD3 algorithm showing convergence difficulties.
summary: Panel a illustrates the training curve for the conventional TD3 algorithm. The reference indicates that this specific approach faces significant challenges in achieving convergence, resulting in poor dispatching performance. This plot serves as a baseline to demonstrate the limitations of standard TD3 in the context of the dispatching task.

caption: Visual documentation of the physical experimental apparatus, showing the fiber optic connections and the data transmission pathway via ethernet cable to a computer for subsequent analysis.
summary: The photograph displays the physical experimental setup used for the finger tapping test. It captures the arrangement of the optical fiber connections and the data transmission interface. Ethernet cables are utilized to transfer the recorded data to a laptop, where it is stored as an Excel file for further analysis.

caption: EDS line scan profile for the S2 sample, showing the distribution of Ti, Cu, and Fe elements across the build interface.
summary: S2 sample EDS line scan data indicates a gradual change in elemental composition within the gradient zone. Unlike S1, the S2 powder was mixed prior to laser building, resulting in broader elemental diffusion. The scan confirms that diffusion distances vary significantly depending on the build direction relative to the composition.

caption: Fracture surface morphology of WAAM-NbZr1 specimen subjected to the second stress level.
summary: Displayed here is the fracture surface of the WAAM-NbZr1 specimen at the second stress level. Fracture surface analysis was conducted to provide further insight into the failure characteristics of the WAAM-NbZr1 material, revealing the specific surface morphology developed during the fracture process at this intermediate stress level.

caption: Experimental setup at D&T Hydraulics utilized for applying EHLA claddings onto a cylindrical bar substrate.
summary: This photograph displays the commercial EHLA system configuration at D&T Hydraulics used for cladding operations. The setup is specifically oriented to facilitate the application of coatings onto a cylindrical bar substrate, demonstrating the industrial equipment arrangement employed for the experimental processing of the materials described in the study.

caption: PCA scores plot illustrating the distribution of samples taken from the inside and outside of eight raw PLA filaments.
summary: PCA scores plot illustrating the distribution of samples taken from the inside and outside of eight raw PLA filaments. Analysis of these scores reveals clear separation along PC1 and PC2, which supports the findings of the homogeneity study regarding the chemical consistency of the filament material across different sampling locations.

caption: Inverse pole figure map showing the grain structure of Fe-36%Ni alloy following 1 turn of HPT at 250 °C.
summary: Representing the microstructure of Fe-36%Ni alloy after 1 turn of HPT processing at 250 °C, this inverse pole figure map highlights the crystallographic orientation relative to the rotation axis. The image demonstrates the ongoing grain refinement process induced by the severe plastic deformation under the specified thermal condition.

caption: Spatial distribution of total distortions in cube 1.2 in the partially cooled state, highlighting uneven top surface topography.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the total distortion distribution across cube 1.2 in its as-built, partially cooled state. The visualization highlights significant structural irregularities, specifically identifying uneven top surface profiles resulting from the cooling process. These distortions provide critical insight into the geometric stability of the cube under the specified thermal conditions.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the USGP6 sample at a sectional depth of 100 μm, showing a microstructure dominated by twins.
summary: At a sectional depth of 100 μm, the bright-field TEM image of the USGP6 sample illustrates a landscape dominated by twins. These structural features indicate significant plastic deformation and twinning activity occurring within the material as the depth from the treated surface decreases.

caption: Temperature-time-transformation diagram for the R725-Ta alloy, showing predicted phase transformation kinetics for exposure times at temperatures between 600 °C and 800 °C.
summary: Representing the R725-Ta alloy, this TTT diagram outlines the kinetic phase transformation behavior observed during exposure at temperatures from 600 °C to 800 °C. The plot serves as a predictive tool for understanding how the addition of tantalum influences the temporal evolution of phases within the specified thermal range.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF-X) map of the 0.3B-LPBF specimen, showing the crystallographic orientation distribution in the plane parallel to the build direction.
summary: This IPF-X map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the 0.3B-LPBF specimen in the plane parallel to the build direction. The analysis reveals a homogeneous and refined grain structure within the material, consistent with the overall characterization of boron-modified specimens produced via laser powder bed fusion processes.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of P1, P2, and P3 tips for the FSA2 alloy, visualized using 43.5 at.% Fe and 1.2 at.% Cu isoconcentration surfaces to delineate phase boundaries.
summary: Three-dimensional reconstructions of P1, P2, and P3 tips are presented for the FSA2 alloy. By applying isoconcentration surfaces at 43.5 at.% Fe and 1.2 at.% Cu, the structural morphology and phase distribution are clearly delineated, providing insight into the microstructure after the specified heat treatment and aging process.

caption: False negative error instance demonstrating a missed detection in the predictive model.
summary: This panel illustrates a false negative error, representing a specific failure mode where the model fails to identify a target feature. Such errors are critical for evaluating predictive performance, and their impacts are systematically categorized alongside other failure types to improve overall model reliability and accuracy in subsequent analysis.

caption: Atomic structure and interaction energy profile for the second stacking sequence of the (001) interface, featuring Ni atoms as blue spheres and Al atoms as pink spheres.
summary: Panel (b) illustrates the atomic structure and interaction energy for the second stacking sequence of the (001) interface. Similar to the first sequence, the interaction energy between the Ru atom and the dislocation core strengthens at closer proximity, reaching a minimum value of -0.81 eV at the second (001) plane.

caption: Processing map of alloy ChS57 at a true strain of 0.693, featuring distinct high and low efficiency zones, with the high zone further subdivided into four specific domains (I-IV).
summary: This processing map for alloy ChS57 at a true strain of 0.693 is divided into high and low power dissipation zones. The high zone is further categorized into four distinct sub-domains, labeled I through IV, providing a detailed analysis of the material's deformation behavior and stability under these conditions.

caption: Average absorbed energy measured via Charpy impact testing at room temperature for conditions A through D of two distinct alloys.
summary: This bar chart displays the average absorbed energy during Charpy impact tests at room temperature for four specific conditions (A-D) across two alloys. Condition A serves as the reference, while conditions C and D represent post-oxidation states. These results provide a baseline for evaluating the impact resistance of the materials.

caption: Pole figure of the FSP nugget core demonstrating the crystallographic orientation distribution.
summary: The pole figure of the FSP nugget core illustrates the crystallographic orientation distribution of the sub-micron grains. Together with the inverse pole figure map, this data reveals a randomly oriented arrangement of grains separated by large-angle grain boundaries, characteristic of the microstructure formed under hybrid DED/FSP conditions.

caption: Surface plot of normalised nonlinear buckling resistances for SHS stub columns with longitudinal wave number m=2, illustrating the relationship between slenderness, wave amplitude, and structural failure load.
summary: Displaying the buckling resistance for SHS stub columns with a longitudinal wave number of m=2, this plot relates failure load to plate slenderness and wave amplitude. The data demonstrates how increasing the longitudinal wave number generally decreases nonlinear resistance, providing a comparative view of structural performance under varying geometric parameters.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectra of the Fe 2p region for the FeNi porous framework, comparing valence states before and after the degradation process.
summary: High-resolution XPS spectra for the Fe 2p region are presented to illustrate the valence state changes of the Fe element in the FeNi porous framework. These spectra provide a detailed view of the surface chemical state modifications that occur as a result of the material degradation process.

caption: Schematic representation of butt joint specimens illustrating two distinct build orientations, labeled A and B, relative to the printing process.
summary: This schematic illustrates butt joint specimens in two different build orientations, A and B. Orientation A is recommended to position the zone of adhesion perpendicular to the build direction, while Orientation B increases the risk of discontinuities and misalignments within the adhesion zone, demonstrating the critical influence of printing orientation on structural integrity.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of Macf1 protein expression in SD rat calvarial defect models at 2 weeks post-implantation, showing scaffold-dependent enrichment at the bone-scaffold interface.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining at 2 weeks post-implantation reveals the spatiotemporal expression of Macf1 in rat calvarial defect models. The imaging confirms significant Macf1 enrichment at the scaffold-bone interfaces for PLA-196 scaffolds, while PLA-N and PLA4 groups exhibit intermediate expression levels, demonstrating a scaffold-dependent gradient change in protein accumulation during bone regeneration.

caption: Primitive sheet network unit cell geometry highlighting the orthogonal connectivity of the primitive minimal surface sheets.
summary: As part of the six-geometry study, the primitive sheet network unit cell demonstrates the relationship between wall thickness and porosity. The research confirms a strong linear correlation between porosity and pore size, with the primitive sheet network maintaining consistent mechanical strength properties across the various unit cell sizes investigated.

caption: Reflection coefficient profile for the antenna design 2 fabricated via Aerosol Jet Printing (AJP).
summary: This panel displays the reflection coefficient of antenna design 2 produced using the AJP fabrication method. The data, plotted using Origin software, illustrates the electromagnetic performance characteristics of the printed antenna structure, providing a baseline for evaluating the effectiveness of the aerosol jet printing process in antenna manufacturing.

caption: Reconstructed 3D-volume and defect distribution of Invar processed via DED-Arc.
summary: Reconstructed 3D-volume and defect distribution of Invar processed via DED-Arc. X-ray CT investigations reveal a higher amount of process-induced defects in the DED-Arc condition compared to DED-LB. These relatively larger defects are observed throughout the volume, though they do not correlate with the superior fatigue performance of the DED-Arc material.

caption: Minor axis length distribution of martensite on XOZ cross-sections for scanning strategies S1-S5.
summary: Minor axis length statistics for martensite on XOZ cross-sections are provided for the five scanning strategies. The data indicates that intermittent melt pool interference modes (S3-S5) lead to larger average primary and secondary martensite sizes than continuous modes (S1, S2), as higher cooling rates promote growth along the main axis.

caption: Support Vector Machine (SVM) model performance shown via a parity plot of predicted versus true values.
summary: The SVM model's predictive capability is evaluated in this parity plot, which contrasts predicted values with true values. By plotting these data points, the figure provides a visual representation of the model's regression performance, facilitating a comparison with the other machine learning models included in the study.

caption: Strain-dependent reflection spectra of the CSP4 opal film, highlighting the material's mechanochromic response.
summary: Strain-dependent reflection spectra of the CSP4 opal film are shown to demonstrate its mechanochromic behavior. This indicates that the optical reflection properties of the polymer compound are sensitive to mechanical deformation, allowing the material to change color in response to applied strain as measured in the opal film.

caption: Loss modulus (E'') profiles for PPcoPE and TPU binders with 60 vol% Mg, illustrating energy dissipation behavior at frequencies of 1, 5, and 10 Hz.
summary: Loss modulus (E'') profiles for PPcoPE and TPU binders with 60 vol% Mg, illustrating energy dissipation behavior at frequencies of 1, 5, and 10 Hz. This panel reveals distinct differences in the viscous and energy-dissipating characteristics of the two composite materials, highlighting how their internal structures respond to dynamic mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern of the as-cast Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi alloy, showing a monolithic face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure.
summary: The synchrotron X-ray diffraction pattern for the as-cast Al0.5CoCrCuFeNi sample confirms the presence of a monolithic fcc phase. This observation aligns with previous reports indicating that the as-cast material maintains a single-phase structure prior to undergoing any mechanical compression tests at elevated temperatures.

caption: Nyquist plot of Ni20Cr (H) bond coating with top coatings, showing impedance behavior in 20 vol% H2SO4 solution.
summary: Ni20Cr (H) bond coating with an HVOF top coating exhibits a reduced corrosion rate, attributed to a homogeneous microstructure. The Nyquist plot, obtained in 20 vol% H2SO4 at room temperature, reflects this improved electrochemical stability, highlighting the effectiveness of the HVOF processing method for this specific bond coating.

caption: External view of the component showing water leakage following the pressure test.
summary: This photograph captures the external surface of the component after a pressure test, clearly demonstrating a water leak. The leakage serves as the primary indicator of structural failure, which was subsequently investigated to determine the root cause of the design flaw at the leg-to-shell attachment point.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern of the rosettes, showing matched interplanar spacing and orientation relationships between Al3Ti and Al9(Fe,Co,Ni)2.
summary: The SAED pattern of the rosettes demonstrates the orientation relationships between the two intermetallic types. It confirms that the orientation relationships remain consistent with the as-printed sample, characterized by matched interplanar spacing. This diffraction data is crucial for identifying the crystallographic alignment between the Al3Ti and Al9(Fe,Co,Ni)2 phases.

caption: Schematic representation of the Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) rejection strategy, illustrating the iterative process where shear modulus values are sampled from a prior distribution and processed through an ANN surrogate model to predict swollen shapes, which are then compared against target data using an error function and tolerance threshold.
summary: This flowchart details the ABC rejection algorithm used for parameter inference. It depicts the workflow from sampling shear modulus values to the ANN surrogate tool's stochastic calculations. The process concludes by comparing the generated pseudo-data against target shapes, accepting only those results that fall within a specified error tolerance threshold.

caption: Correlation between interfacial bonding strength and bonding mode across varying sintering temperatures, demonstrating how [Ti, Nb]C reinforcement optimizes strength-ductility through improved load transfer efficiency.
summary: This plot quantifies the relationship between interfacial bonding strength and the bonding mode at different sintering temperatures. The [Ti, Nb]C reinforcement is shown to enhance interfacial load transfer efficiency, which enables the simultaneous optimization of strength and ductility in the FGH96 alloy system during the powder metallurgy fabrication process.

caption: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis of the Ta x NiTiCrNb coating surface following the passivation process.
summary: XPS analysis of the passive films formed on the Ta x NiTiCrNb coating surface reveals the chemical state of the material after passivation. The intensities of the spectra indicate that the passive films created by each coating exhibit comparable trends, providing insight into the surface chemistry and composition of the films.

caption: Current density response for electrolyte E-c3, maintained at pH 2.8 with a modified Ni2+/Fe2+ ratio of 7:1.
summary: Panel c presents the current density loops for electrolyte E-c3, which uses a Ni2+/Fe2+ ratio of 7:1 at pH 2.8. The total current density is shown as a solid green curve, while partial current densities for Fe-Ni deposition are represented by dashed lines, reflecting the specific deposition conditions studied.

caption: Dilatometric curve (black) and isochronal ageing curve (red) of IN718 alloy, illustrating phase transformation peaks.
summary: This figure displays the dilatometric curve of as-built IN718 alloy alongside its isochronal ageing curve. The dilatometric data reveals specific phase transformations, with peak I attributed to γ' precipitation and peak II to γ'' precipitation. These peaks correlate with the strengthening phases identified in the isochronal ageing curve.

caption: Electrochemical activity of Pt-based catalysts evaluated via cyclic voltammetry in 1 M KOH containing 1 M ethanol, using a sweep rate of 50 mV s−1 within a potential range of −0.9 V to +0.3 V vs. SCE.
summary: Electrochemical performance of various Pt-based catalysts is assessed in an alkaline ethanol solution. By measuring the cyclic voltammograms at a sweep rate of 50 mV s−1 between −0.9 V and +0.3 V vs. SCE, the panel highlights the catalytic activity of these materials toward ethanol oxidation in a fuel cell environment.

caption: Ratios of measured normalized unit width Y2,m to predicted normalized unit width Y2,p plotted against Wa,n, featuring a ±7% reference band.
summary: This plot illustrates the ratio of measured to predicted normalized unit width Y2,m/Y2,p versus Wa,n. The data points fall within a range of 0.9734–1.0546, indicating a maximum error of 5.5%. All points are contained within the ±7% reference band, confirming the reliability of the predictive model.

caption: Al-rich portion of the calculated liquidus projection for the Al-Mg-Si ternary system, highlighting the chemical compositions corresponding to the α-Al/Mg2Si two-phase eutectic reaction.
summary: This panel displays the Al-rich portion of the liquidus projection for the Al-Mg-Si ternary system, calculated using Pandat software. The liquidus line between the α-Al and Mg2Si phases identifies the specific chemical compositions that facilitate the α-Al/Mg2Si two-phase eutectic reaction, which is a critical pathway for PBF-LB alloy fabrication.

caption: 3D surface topography map of sample L1.69, demonstrating surface characteristics similar to the initial L0 state.
summary: Sample L1.69, processed at an energy density of 1.69 J/mm², retains surface characteristics comparable to the initial L0 sample. The topography map reveals that the laser energy applied at this level is insufficient to eliminate the large surface fluctuations present in the as-printed material.

caption: Parity plot comparing predicted versus experimental stability values, showing data points tightly clustered around the diagonal line.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the RSM-BBD model's predictive accuracy for stability. The visualization demonstrates a high degree of correlation between predicted and experimental values, as evidenced by the data points being tightly clustered along the diagonal line, indicating that the model effectively captures the stability performance metric.

caption: Initial light spot distribution observed on the screen via DMD reflection prior to the pre-treatment experiment.
summary: This panel displays the initial light spot distribution captured on a screen through the reflection of a Digital Micromirror Device (DMD). This baseline image represents the optical state of the system before the pre-treatment experiment was conducted, providing a reference for evaluating subsequent changes in the light spot pattern.

caption: Experimental setup featuring the UNITRONIC machine equipped with an extended loading plate designed to accommodate horizontal movement during cyclic testing of ACCCs.
summary: The experimental setup for testing ACCCs utilizes a UNITRONIC machine. An extended loading plate is integrated into the system to facilitate and accommodate horizontal movement throughout the cyclic testing process, ensuring proper alignment and mechanical response during the compression and release cycles performed on the specimen.

caption: Metal grid layout illustrating the structural arrangement of simulated particles.
summary: Metal grid panel provides a view of the simulated material surface, where different particles are denoted by unique colors or symbols. This methodology ensures that the simulated surface exhibits varied and realistic complexity, which is critical for ensuring that the simulation results are representative of actual material surface conditions.

caption: Defect structure process map for LPBF-manufactured Ti–6Al–4V, illustrating the systematic variation of defect morphology across a power-velocity (P–V) parameter space.
summary: This process map characterizes defect morphology in LPBF-manufactured Ti–6Al–4V across varying laser power and scan speed parameters. It specifically highlights that keyhole defects are concentrated in the high-power and low-scan-speed region of the P–V space, demonstrating a systematic relationship between processing conditions and the resulting material defect structure.

caption: Aluminum elemental distribution map of the HTD specimen cross-section.
summary: Aluminum elemental distribution map of the HTD specimen cross-section. This map illustrates the aluminum distribution across the worn track, helping to characterize the material's chemical response to the wear test and providing a basis for comparing the structural and compositional changes between the HTD and AD specimens.

caption: Three-dimensional X-ray microscopy (XRM) reconstruction of the fractured Alloy B sample.
summary: This panel presents a three-dimensional XRM reconstruction of the fractured Alloy B sample. The visualization provides a comprehensive view of the failed specimen, serving as a post-mortem analysis tool to investigate the overall morphology and structural integrity of the material following the failure event.

caption: Displacement versus time curves for NC Ni and NC Ni–Fe alloy recorded during the CSR test at three different strain rates.
summary: Panel (c) illustrates the displacement versus time curves for both NC Ni and NC Ni–Fe alloy specimens. These curves were obtained during CSR testing at three different strain rates, providing the temporal evolution of indentation depth necessary for analyzing the mechanical response of the materials under varying loading conditions.

caption: Diffraction patterns of the SMAT-Fe sample illustrating phase distribution at different depths after 800 °C sintering, highlighting the influence of the nanocrystalline layer.
summary: Presented here are the XRD patterns for the SMAT-Fe sample, which reveal the phase distribution within the Fe–Ni alloying coating at various depths. The nanocrystalline layer formed by SMAT pretreatment contributes to an increased thickness of the high-hardness alloy layer, as confirmed by these diffraction results following 800 °C sintering.

caption: HAADF HRSTEM image of the σ phase showing stacking disordering defects on the (110) σ plane, with an inset displaying the corresponding FFT pattern.
summary: High-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (HRSTEM) imaging reveals the presence of stacking disordering defects within the σ phase. The HAADF image, captured along the (110) σ direction, provides a clear visualization of the defect configuration, while the inset FFT pattern confirms the structural characteristics of the observed phase.

caption: Special boundary map of the matrix at high temperature, showing a high density of <1–210>85° twinning boundaries.
summary: High temperature machining results in a distinct population of <1–210>85° twin boundaries within the matrix. The map illustrates these features in relation to the SiC fibre boundaries, demonstrating that the specific twinning mechanism is temperature-dependent and influenced by the mechanical interaction between the matrix and the reinforcing fibres.

caption: EPMA elemental mapping of key elements in the as-deposited Alloy2.
summary: EPMA elemental mapping of the as-deposited Alloy2 provides a comprehensive visualization of the distribution of key alloying elements. These maps confirm the microstructural observations regarding dendritic growth and phase precipitation, validating the chemical homogeneity and elemental segregation patterns present within the as-deposited material structure.

caption: Confocal-style fluorescence image of HFFs on a printed diamond crystal texture Ti-6Al-4V surface (DC1) after 48 hours, demonstrating cell adaptation to the textured geometry.
summary: HFFs were seeded on a printed diamond crystal texture surface (DC1) for 48 hours. Immunofluorescence staining shows that fibroblasts attach to the powder particles and spread along the curvature, adapting to the complex geometry of the diamond crystal texture. This demonstrates the influence of surface topography on cell morphology.

caption: Saturation magnetization and remanence values for CoNi alloy thin films deposited on various substrates, illustrating the magnetic response characteristics.
summary: This plot displays the variation of saturation magnetization and remanence for CoNi alloy thin films deposited on various substrates. The data highlights how different substrate choices influence the magnetic properties of the alloy films, providing insight into the relationship between film composition and magnetic performance in these specific thin-film systems.

caption: Calculated chemical composition variations of the A2 phase in AlxNi(40-x)Fe40Cr20 alloys at 800 °C, where Fe content peaks at x = 20 and Cr content exhibits an inverse trend relative to Al concentration.
summary: The A2 phase composition in AlxNi(40-x)Fe40Cr20 alloys at 800 °C is presented here. As aluminum content increases, the iron concentration initially rises, reaching a maximum at x = 20 before decreasing. Conversely, the chromium content displays an opposite trend, demonstrating the complex phase stability and compositional shifts occurring within the A2 phase.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the H282 alloy dataset acquired using a LEAP 3000 Si instrument, containing approximately 80 million atoms.
summary: This panel displays an atom probe tomography reconstruction of the H282 alloy sample, captured using a LEAP 3000 Si system. The dataset comprises 80 million atoms, with blue dots representing Al ion positions and orange surfaces denoting (Al, Ti) 10 at.% isoconcentration surfaces, illustrating the typical volume analyzed by this instrument.

caption: Absolute irradiance output of the Elipar S10 single-peak LED light curing unit, displayed as a function of wavelength.
summary: The Elipar S10 single-peak LED light curing unit demonstrates a characteristic absolute irradiance profile measured in mW/cm2/nm. By mapping the intensity across its emission wavelength range, this plot allows for a direct comparison of the spectral output of the S10 system against the laser and quad-wave curing technologies.

caption: Bode magnitude plot displaying the relationship between impedance modulus |Z| and frequency for as-built and HIP-processed 316L samples, characterized by a slope near -1.
summary: Bode magnitude plots for both as-built and HIP-processed 316L samples exhibit a linear relationship between the impedance modulus |Z| and the frequency range. The observed slope near -1 across the frequency spectrum indicates consistent electrochemical behavior and the development of a stable passive layer on the surfaces of both sample states.

caption: Ternary composition diagram illustrating the band gap distribution of MgO–NiO–ZnO thin films, where experimental data points (black squares) derived from UV–vis Tauc plots are interpolated and smoothed to create a color-coded map of band gap values across the entire composition range.
summary: This ternary diagram maps the band gap values of MgO–NiO–ZnO thin films across the composition space. Experimental data points, obtained from UV–vis Tauc plots, are interpolated to visualize the band gap variation. The transition from blue to red regions highlights that increasing MgO content significantly elevates the band gap from 5.4 to 5.8 eV.

caption: Calculated isothermal section of the Al–Ni–V ternary system at 1073 K, incorporating experimental data points from Zapolsky et al. to validate the phase boundaries.
summary: This isothermal section of the Al–Ni–V system at 1073 K provides a calculated representation of phase equilibria. By integrating experimental data from Zapolsky et al., the diagram serves as a reliable reference for phase stability at this specific temperature, which is identified as an appropriate condition for the system analysis.

caption: Evolution of the Bauschinger stress at 1% reverse plastic strain offset as a function of forward plastic strain for various ageing conditions.
summary: This plot illustrates the Bauschinger stress (σB 1%) as a function of forward plastic strain. The stress remains negligible before generalized plastic deformation but increases sharply as strain approaches 1%. Notably, σB 1% decreases with increased ageing time, indicating a reduction in the magnitude of long-range back-stress within the material.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from 11 distinct points across the joint interface during nanoindentation testing.
summary: Load-depth curves are presented for 11 distinct points across the joint interface during nanoindentation testing. These curves illustrate the mechanical response of the material at various locations, providing the raw data necessary to derive localized mechanical properties such as Young's modulus and microhardness across the joint region.

caption: Immunofluorescent staining of iNOS protein in RAW 264.7 cells cultured with DA-CDs, visualized at 20 μm scale to assess inflammatory marker suppression.
summary: Immunofluorescent staining provides visual evidence of iNOS protein expression in RAW 264.7 cells treated with DA-CDs. This technique allows for the observation of inflammatory marker distribution and intensity at a cellular level, supporting the findings that DA-CDs modulate the inflammatory state of the cells.

caption: Net section tension failure mode observed in the bolted connection specimen.
summary: The net section tension failure mode is depicted here, representing one of the primary failure mechanisms for the bolted connection. According to the reference, the ultimate capacity for this specific failure mode can be calculated using Eq. (1a), based on the geometric features defined in the initial specimen configuration.

caption: High-speed photographic sequence capturing the MDPP detachment mode, illustrating the formation and subsequent release of multiple droplets within a single electrical pulse cycle.
summary: This high-speed photographic sequence illustrates the MDPP detachment mode, specifically detailing the dynamic process of formation and detachment of multiple drops occurring within a single pulse. The visual data provides a clear observation of the droplet evolution, confirming the complex nature of the detachment mechanism during the pulse cycle.

caption: Calculated compositional path for the Ti60 to Ti2AlNb transition, incorporating an intermediate layer of Ti-17.4Al-33Nb (at%) to optimize the overall transition path.
summary: The panel illustrates the designed transition path for the Ti60 to Ti2AlNb system at 700 °C. By introducing an intermediate layer with a calculated composition of Ti-17.4Al-33Nb (at%), the transition path is refined within the ternary phase diagram to ensure accurate phase equilibrium relations during the alloy design process.

caption: Tensile properties, specifically Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) and Yield Strength (YS), of LPBF-fabricated 24CrNiMo steel after quenching at different temperatures.
summary: Tensile properties including UTS and YS for LPBF-fabricated 24CrNiMo steel are shown following quenching treatments. Strength values rise significantly after quenching at 800 °C, remain relatively stable between 800 °C and 900 °C, and eventually decrease as the quenching temperature is further increased to 1000 °C, demonstrating optimal processing windows.

caption: High current density deposition morphology characterized by pronounced edge effects on the nickel deposit.
summary: Under the highest current density condition, the simulation reveals significant morphological changes in the nickel deposit. The atomic arrangement exhibits clear edge effects, demonstrating how elevated current densities influence the growth patterns and structural distribution of nickel atoms on the substrate during the simulated electrodeposition process.

caption: Systematic flowchart illustrating the architecture and data processing steps of the alpha lath width prediction model.
summary: This flowchart provides a comprehensive overview of the alpha lath width prediction model's architecture. It outlines the sequential data processing steps and logical framework employed to estimate lath dimensions. The diagram serves as a visual guide to understanding the computational workflow and methodology utilized for predicting microstructural features in materials.

caption: Plactron vase model produced via additive manufacturing using recycled polycarbonate.
summary: The Plactron vase is one of several models fabricated to assess the mechanical and practical viability of recycled polycarbonate. By successfully printing this complex geometry, the study confirms that rPC maintains sufficient structural integrity and printability for use in various decorative and functional objects after multiple recycling steps.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the S region of the carbide hardening layer.
summary: The SAED pattern acquired from the S region provides crystallographic information regarding the carbide hardening layer. This diffraction data is essential for identifying the phase composition and structural characteristics of the material at the specific location S within the cross-sectional foil.

caption: UV-Vis absorbance spectra of FNF@AuNP and enzyme solution demonstrating optical responses to levodopa concentrations ranging from 6 to 500 μM.
summary: The UV-Vis absorbance spectra reveal the optical response of the FNF@AuNP and enzyme system to varying levodopa concentrations. Significant changes in absorbance at 525 nm are detectable at concentrations as low as 6 μM, confirming the sensitivity of the sensor across the tested range of 6 to 500 μM.

caption: Weak-beam TEM image of the HIPed, STA, and aged sample, showing stacking faults within the secondary γ′ precipitates.
summary: Weak-beam TEM imaging of the HIPed, STA, and aged sample reveals stacking faults within the secondary γ′ precipitates. These features are identified as loops, confirming the presence of internal defects that accommodate strain during room temperature tensile testing, consistent with the findings across the various heat-treated sample conditions.

caption: Schematic representation of the initial loading conditions applied to crane hooks.
summary: This schematic illustrates the initial loading conditions applied to crane hooks. As specified in the reference, these components are subjected to specific load configurations during operation. The diagram serves to visualize the mechanical environment and force application points relevant to the structural analysis of the crane hook assembly.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy elemental mapping images corresponding to the region shown in the HAADF micrograph.
summary: These EDS mapping images illustrate the spatial distribution of elements within the AT 1 alloy microstructure. By correlating these maps with the HAADF image, it is observed that the precipitates are enriched in specific elements, including C, Cr, Mo, Co, and W, indicating a complex chemical composition.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the CoCrNi MEA sample after short-time annealing (S-AT), highlighting the initial stages of recrystallization.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the CoCrNi MEA microstructure following short-time annealing. Compared to the as-printed state, this condition initiates recrystallization processes. The map serves as a baseline for evaluating the evolution of grain morphology and nucleation density as annealing duration increases toward the 2-hour mark.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk containing Atto465 dye, which exhibits a balanced filtering profile in the target region.
summary: This panel presents the transmission spectrum for a 0.5 mm thick 3D-printed disk with Atto465 dye. The dye is noted for its balanced filtering performance in the required spectral region, demonstrating the effectiveness of the 3D-printing process for creating wavelength-selective optical components.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and corresponding EDS mapping of the HT02 specimen, illustrating the elemental distribution between γ and γ′ phases.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image combined with EDS mapping reveals the elemental distribution within the HT02 specimen. The analysis clearly shows that the γ′ phases are deficient in Co and Cr, while being significantly enriched in Al, Ta, and Ti, confirming the distinct chemical partitioning between the γ and γ′ phases.

caption: Friction coefficient profile for the 3 wt% TiC composite sample, demonstrating sliding performance under diverse load parameters.
summary: Displayed is the friction coefficient curve for the 3 wt% TiC composite sliding against Si3N4. This plot captures the material's tribological response under different loads, consistent with the general friction patterns observed in TiC/Ti6Al4V composites, providing insight into the influence of TiC content on the friction coefficient over time.

caption: Bright field TEM image showing a U phase grain and its interface with the surrounding Ni-matrix.
summary: A bright field TEM micrograph reveals the internal structure of a U phase grain and its spatial relationship with the adjacent Ni-matrix. This image provides the necessary context for the selected-area diffraction analysis performed on the U phase grain, highlighting the grain boundaries and local microstructural features.

caption: Evolution of long-range order (LRO) parameters for various intermetallic alloys plotted against irradiation dose, featuring exponential decay fits derived from molecular dynamics cascade simulations.
summary: This plot illustrates the LRO evolution for intermetallic alloys during irradiation disordering, generated through 500–1000 iterative cascade simulations. Exponential fitting reveals disordering rates between 9 and 15 dpa-1, which align closely with experimental ion irradiation data for these materials, confirming the validity of the simulated disordering process.

caption: Contour plot detailing the adhesion strength distribution across the experimental parameter range for LPCS.
summary: This contour plot provides a detailed view of how adhesion strength is distributed across the tested LPCS parameters. It supports the finding that gas temperature is the most significant factor influencing adhesion strength, with clear trends showing improved performance as temperature increases and spray distance is optimized to 10 mm.

caption: Tafel slope curves calculated for the Mo2WS6/NF-x electrocatalysts to determine reaction kinetics.
summary: Calculated Tafel slope curves for the Mo2WS6/NF-x electrocatalysts are shown to characterize the reaction kinetics. These plots are essential for understanding the HER mechanism, indicating that the process follows the Volmer-Heyrovsky mechanism, with the Volmer step identified as the rate-determining step of the electrocatalytic process.

caption: Ni-Ti binary phase diagram illustrating the solidification transformation of liquid NiTi into solid NiTi and a Ti-rich liquid phase.
summary: The Ni-Ti phase diagram is shown to explain the solidification process of the alloy. According to this diagram, when the NiTi alloy transforms into the liquid phase, the solidification process begins with the transformation of liquid NiTi into solid NiTi and a Ti-rich liquid phase, influencing the final microstructure.

caption: Atomic resolution HAADF-STEM image of the cubic Ni-rich phase within the B2 matrix along the [001] zone axis, with an inset FFT pattern confirming the characteristic cubic structure and grid-like atomic arrangement.
summary: Atomic resolution HAADF-STEM imaging along the [001] B2 zone axis provides detailed insight into the structure of the new cubic Ni-rich phase. The repeating grid-like arrangement of high Z-contrast atoms is clearly visible, while the inset FFT pattern confirms the characteristic structure of the cubic Ni-rich precipitate within the B2 matrix.

caption: Principal component analysis (PCA) score distribution of the four thermal treatment histories, showing distinct clustering of samples based on their processing conditions.
summary: The PCA plot demonstrates the effectiveness of dimensionality reduction in representing complex thermal histories. By utilizing three principal component scores, the distinct processing conditions are mapped into a low-dimensional space where samples with similar thermal profiles cluster together, providing a consistent representation for subsequent machine learning model analysis.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles of the Ni-Co/rGO cathode obtained at varying current densities.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge curves are depicted for the Ni-Co/rGO electrode at various current densities. These profiles illustrate the voltage response of the cathode during cycling, serving as a fundamental assessment of the material's ability to store and release charge under different operational current loads.

caption: Calculated density of states for bulk Ni3Al, illustrating the electronic structure.
summary: The density of states for bulk Ni3Al is presented here to characterize its electronic structure. This plot provides a baseline for understanding the electronic properties of the material before and during deformation, serving as a comparison point for the more complex γ′ phase shown in subsequent panels of the figure.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve illustrating the CNN model classification capability regarding stringing defects.
summary: The ROC curve presented here demonstrates the effectiveness of the CNN model in detecting stringing defects. This plot serves as a key metric for evaluating the model's ability to distinguish between stringing and non-stringing instances, reflecting the overall predictive reliability of the machine learning approach for this specific defect.

caption: Uniaxial monodomain director pattern on a rectangular domain with director orientation B aligned along the short side.
summary: Representing a uniaxial monodomain pattern on a rectangular domain, this panel illustrates the director field oriented along the short side. The visualization confirms that the algorithm achieves perfect filling of the domain, maintaining consistent quality and coverage for this specific director orientation within the rectangular boundary.

caption: Wear rate comparison of WC-reinforced and TiN-integrated WC-reinforced nanocomposites against wrought and LPBF-fabricated SS440C.
summary: Wear rates calculated after tribological testing demonstrate the performance of the developed nanocomposites relative to wrought and LPBF-fabricated SS440C. The reference indicates that the wear rates for the wrought and LPBF samples were lower than those of the nanocomposites developed in this study, reflecting distinct material resistance characteristics.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the 425 °C tempered specimen, revealing significantly coarsened carbides compared to lower tempering temperatures.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the specimen tempered at 425 °C reveals a notable increase in carbide size. The carbides are approximately three to five times larger than those in the as-fabricated state, growing from roughly 10 nm to 50 nm, indicating significant coarsening at this higher tempering temperature.

caption: UV-visible near-infrared absorption spectrum of CUG lunar regolith simulant plotted against wavelength.
summary: This UV-visible near-infrared absorption spectrum characterizes the laser absorption properties of CUG lunar regolith simulant across a broad wavelength range. Measured using a Shimadzu SolidSpec-3700 spectrophotometer, the data provides essential insights into how varying titanium contents influence the material's thermal properties and laser absorption rates during processing.

caption: Thermal elongation ΔL/L as a function of temperature T, illustrating a distinct plateau between 750 °C and 850 °C.
summary: Thermal elongation is plotted against temperature based on the EN 1993-1-2 standard. The curve features a characteristic plateau occurring between 750 °C and 850 °C, which corresponds to the phase transformation of the steel, reflecting the material's structural changes during heating within this specific temperature range.

caption: Comparison of LB-PBF AlSi10Mg microstructure in as-built (AB) and T6 heat-treated states across transverse (XY) and longitudinal (XZ, YZ) planes.
summary: This panel displays optical micrographs comparing the overall microstructure of LB-PBF AlSi10Mg in the as-built and T6 heat-treated conditions. Observations are provided across the transverse (XY) plane, perpendicular to the build direction, and the longitudinal (XZ and YZ) planes, which are parallel to the build direction, highlighting microstructural differences.

caption: Multi-track simulation snapshot illustrating the in-situ alloying process during PBF, where blue particles represent CP-Ti powder and red particles represent SS 316L powder.
summary: This multi-track simulation provides critical insights into the in-situ alloying process during PBF. By visualizing the distribution of CP-Ti (blue) and SS 316L (red) powders, the simulation reveals a non-uniform elemental distribution. This heterogeneity leads to local SS 316L enrichment and the subsequent formation of a heterostructured martensite phase.

caption: Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra recorded at the Zr absorption edge for as-deposited and annealed Ni-Zr films, showing experimental data points as open circles and theoretical model fits as solid lines.
summary: This figure displays the Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra at the Zr absorption edge for as-deposited and annealed Ni-Zr films. The data points are represented by open circles, while solid lines indicate theoretical model fits. Notably, the emergence of peaks near 3 Å confirms the presence of the Ni7Zr2 phase in these samples.

caption: Training and validation loss curves plotted against epoch count, demonstrating the convergence behavior of the invertible neural network using 70 training samples.
summary: The training and validation loss curves are shown in Fig. 3 (a), which visualizes the training process using 70 training samples. This plot tracks the loss values across different epochs, providing a clear indication of the model's convergence and stability during the training phase for the invertible neural network architecture.

caption: Atomic configuration showing partial dislocation nucleation from the corner of a perfectly shaped Ni3Al nanocrystal using the AMB potential.
summary: This MD snapshot illustrates the heterogeneous nucleation of 1/6 < 112 >{111} partial dislocations from the corner of a perfectly cubic Ni3Al nanocrystal. Using the AMB potential, the simulation confirms that nanocrystal corners act as preferential nucleation sites for plastic deformation under [001] compression conditions.

caption: Bacterial colony formation of S. aureus on the surface of control 316L stainless steel.
summary: This panel shows the bacterial colony formation of S. aureus on the surface of the control 316L stainless steel. By providing a reference for standard bacterial growth, this image allows for a direct assessment of the antibacterial reduction achieved by the 316L-4.5Cu alloy when exposed to S. aureus strains.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of alloy samples under various experimental conditions, featuring an inset highlighting the 37–40° 2θ angular range.
summary: X-ray diffraction patterns of alloy samples under various experimental conditions, featuring an inset highlighting the 37–40° 2θ angular range. These XRD scans demonstrate that a primarily α’’ phase formation occurs in all cases, confirming the structural consistency across the different conditions tested in the study.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves showing mass loss as a function of temperature for bleached enset and sisal fibers, pure PLA, and their 3 wt% fiber-reinforced composites.
summary: TGA curves illustrate the thermal degradation behavior of bleached fibers, pure PLA, and 3 wt% fiber-reinforced PLA composites. Bleached fibers exhibit initial weight loss near 40 °C due to moisture evaporation. Pure PLA and its composites remain thermally stable until approximately 273 °C, followed by sharp mass loss from backbone degradation.

caption: Grain deformation map of the as-built sample fractured at 450 °C.
summary: Illustrating the grain deformation characteristics of the as-built sample after fatigue fracture at 450 °C, this map highlights the structural changes occurring under elevated temperature conditions.
