caption: Comparative loading-unloading curves for both the Al side and Ti side of the powder-powder configuration, spanning from the Ti6Al4V region to the LPBFed AlSi12 substrate.
summary: Loading-unloading curves are shown for both the aluminum and titanium sides of the powder-powder configuration. These measurements, spanning from the Ti6Al4V region to the LPBFed AlSi12 substrate, characterize the mechanical response across the multi-material interface, providing data on the residual stress states present in both materials.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing as-received α-alumina powder, green specimen, and sintered specimen, highlighting the presence of α-alumina phases across all samples and the detection of Pluronic F-127 in the green specimen.
summary: This XRD analysis displays absolute intensity versus diffraction angle for as-received α-alumina powder, green specimens, and sintered specimens. The diffraction patterns confirm the presence of the α-alumina phase in all three conditions, while the green specimen uniquely exhibits peaks corresponding to the organic binder Pluronic F-127, indicating its presence before sintering.

caption: Kissinger plot showing the linear dependency of ln(β/T^2) versus 1/T for the Zr40Al20Ni5Co15Cu20 alloy, where β represents the heating rate and T_P denotes the peak temperature.
summary: This Kissinger plot displays the linear dependency of ln(β/T^2) versus 1/T for the Zr40Al20Ni5Co15Cu20 alloy, where β represents the heating rate and T_P denotes the peak temperature. This graphical representation allows for the calculation of the activation energy of the observed reaction using the Kissinger method and the universal gas constant.

caption: Crystal orbital Hamilton population (COHP) curves for atomic pairs in interstitial-doped systems, plotted against energy relative to the Fermi level.
summary: This plot displays the calculated COHP for various atomic pairs within interstitial-doped systems. The data illustrates the bonding and antibonding interactions as a function of energy, with the Fermi level set at zero. These curves provide insight into the electronic stability and chemical bonding characteristics of the doped materials.

caption: Capacitive currents of NiMo@NF versus scan rate, evaluating the impact of CV cycling as an accelerated degradation test compared to fresh 1 M KOH conditions.
summary: This panel shows capacitive currents versus scan rate for NiMo@NF, highlighting the effects of CV cycling. The data indicates an approximate 16% increase in double-layer capacitance following the cycling process, demonstrating how electrochemical degradation protocols influence the surface charge storage characteristics of the NiMo@NF catalyst in alkaline media.

caption: Comparative line graph displaying the thermal propagation profiles across different polymeric materials used in the workpiece.
summary: This plot compares the thermal propagation characteristics of various polymeric materials. By evaluating these different materials, the simulation aims to verify the physical correctness of the heat propagation formula. However, the actual thermal behaviour observed in real-world conditions is more complex than the assumptions made in this 2D simulation.

caption: Micro-CT cross-sectional view of the oxide layer joint keyhole processed with a spherical pin tool.
summary: This micro-CT image illustrates the oxide distribution at the keyhole of a joint produced using a spherical pin tool. In contrast to the flat pin, this configuration shows a higher oxide density at the bottom of the tool compared to the retreating and advancing sides, representing a significant improvement in material distribution.

caption: Constrained-surface SLA system design showing the interaction between the build platform and the resin vat.
summary: The constrained-surface SLA system is depicted here, highlighting the mechanical arrangement where the build surface is restricted during the photopolymerization process. This configuration is a key variation of SLA technology, facilitating the localized curing of resin layers to build complex three-dimensional structures through controlled light-induced solidification.

caption: Aggregated ecosystem impact contributions for OPC and LC3 cement models in QC and FR contexts, with striped sections indicating categories where LC3 impacts exceed those of OPC.
summary: This bar chart displays the midpoint contributions to aggregated ecosystem impacts for OPC and LC3 cement models across QC and FR geographical contexts. Striped sections highlight categories where LC3 impacts are higher than OPC. The data illustrates a minor contribution of marine indicators, explaining the overall decreased ecosystem score for LC3.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot illustrating the dependence of ln[sinh(ασ)] on the inverse absolute temperature (1/T) for the β phase.
summary: Panel d presents the Arrhenius relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of the flow stress and the inverse absolute temperature for the β phase. The slope of this linear plot allows for the calculation of the activation energy, which is found to be 569.22312 kJ mol⁻¹ for the β phase.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the CFRP laminate illustrating varying degrees of bending and warping across different plies.
summary: Bending behavior of the CFRP laminate is examined to assess structural deformation. The analysis reveals that the extent of warping varies significantly across the thickness of the sheet, with outer plies exhibiting more pronounced warping compared to the inner plies, indicating non-uniform mechanical response under elevated temperature conditions.

caption: Surface morphology of nickel atoms deposited on a substrate at 1000 ps under high-frequency pulse conditions, showing minimal atomic stacking.
summary: This MD snapshot illustrates the surface morphology of nickel atoms deposited on a substrate after 1000 ps of electrodeposition using a high-frequency pulse. The visualization demonstrates that high-frequency pulsing results in a notably smooth surface with almost no stacking of nickel atoms on the substrate surface, indicating a highly uniform deposition process.

caption: Band contrast EBSD image of conventional IN625 (sample D) cross-section, illustrating an equiaxed grain morphology with twinning boundaries marked in red.
summary: Conventional IN625, designated as sample D, exhibits a distinct microstructure compared to the PBF-LB samples. The EBSD band contrast image reveals an equiaxed grain structure characterized by a significant density of twinning boundaries, which are highlighted in red throughout the cross-sectional view.

caption: Magnified atomic force microscopy view of a pyramidal slip trace bundle, where the black arrow denotes the specific location of the height profile measurement.
summary: Higher magnification observations reveal that the slip traces identified in the previous topography image are actually composed of multiple slip traces arranged in distinct bundles. The black arrow indicates the precise path used for the subsequent height profile measurement, allowing for a detailed analysis of individual slip step dimensions.

caption: Mass magnetization versus applied magnetic field for pure Ni particles at 25 °C, showing the characteristic magnetic hysteresis loop.
summary: This panel displays the magnetic hysteresis loop for pure Ni particles measured at 25 °C using VSM. The mass magnetization is calculated by normalizing the measured magnetic moment by the total mass of the Ni particles. Minor loops at different amplitudes are clearly visible within the plotted data.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data represented as a Nyquist plot, with an inset highlighting the high-frequency region for detailed analysis.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results are displayed in this Nyquist plot, providing insight into the internal resistance and charge transfer kinetics of the microsupercapacitor. The inclusion of an inset focusing on the high-frequency region allows for a more detailed examination of the device's impedance characteristics and interfacial electrochemical processes.

caption: Experimental time-response thermograms for solid IN625 specimens measured across various temperatures, representing the average of three distinct experimental trials.
summary: This panel displays experimental time-response thermograms for solid IN625 specimens at various temperatures. These curves, derived from the average of three separate measurements, serve as baseline data for a multivariate inverse method. This optimization algorithm utilizes these experimental results to calibrate simulation models and extract thermal conductivity properties.

caption: Calibration mean squared error (MSE) plotted against varying neural network architectures, defined by hidden layers and node counts, for Ecoflex and DM datasets.
summary: Calibration MSE values for various PANN architectures are displayed for Ecoflex and DM datasets. The results indicate that while increasing nodes beyond eight can reduce loss values, this improvement is of no practical relevance, suggesting that smaller architectures are sufficient for the intended application of the constitutive models.

caption: In-situ FT-IR spectra of SL displaying the thermal decomposition of C=O bonds.
summary: In-situ FT-IR spectra of SL illustrate the thermal decomposition of the material. It is observed that the thermal decomposition of the C=O bonds leads to a distinct decrease in the peak intensity as the temperature increases, confirming the chemical breakdown of carbonyl groups during the in-situ pyrolysis experiment.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulation results showing the evolution of shear stress as a function of the impact parameter d, highlighting the asymmetrical pinning strength.
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations reveal the shear stress evolution during dislocation-void interaction for varying impact parameters. The results demonstrate that critical shear stress values are dependent on the glide plane position relative to the void center. Notably, the pinning strength is asymmetrical, even for identical absolute values of the impact parameter.

caption: Representative tetragonal unit cell structure of the double perovskite Sr2NiMoO6.
summary: This panel displays the representative tetragonal crystal structure of the double perovskite material Sr2NiMoO6. The visualization highlights the atomic arrangement within the unit cell, providing a clear structural model that characterizes the symmetry and spatial configuration of the constituent strontium, nickel, molybdenum, and oxygen atoms in the lattice.

caption: Major axis length distribution of martensite on XOY cross-sections for scanning strategies S1-S5.
summary: This panel displays the major axis length distribution of primary, secondary, and tertiary martensite on XOY cross-sections using a combined violin and box plot. Data indicates that intermittent melt pool interference modes (S3-S5) generally promote larger average martensite sizes compared to continuous modes (S1, S2) due to higher cooling rates.

caption: Overview of the cyclic nano-indentation testing procedure showing multiple loading and unloading segments.
summary: This panel provides a summary of the cyclic nano-indentation tests performed on the material. It illustrates the experimental methodology by displaying the load-displacement response across multiple cycles, which serves as the foundational data for evaluating the mechanical behavior and determining the residual Young's modulus throughout the indentation process.

caption: Strain rate versus plastic strain for C-264 at 900 °C, highlighting the creep minimum and the 5% plastic strain threshold.
summary: Depicted here is the strain rate versus plastic strain for C-264 at 900 °C, which displays a similar shape to the C-263 alloy, including a sharp creep minimum. The 5% plastic strain threshold, indicated by a vertical dashed line, serves as the reference point for calculating the material's Norton exponent.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the chromia scale formed on CM IN625 after 1000 h of air exposure at 900 °C, providing a comprehensive overview of the oxide microstructure.
summary: This APT reconstruction displays the chromia scale grown on CM IN625 after 1000 h of air exposure at 900 °C. The visualization provides a full overview of the oxide microstructure, serving as the basis for further compositional analysis of grain boundaries within the chromia layer.

caption: Neutron diffraction pattern for the IF+ST disc at position P3 showing axial θ0 peak deviation.
summary: Panel (i) illustrates the neutron diffraction pattern at position P3 of the IF+ST disc. The axial θ0 measurement demonstrates a maximum peak deviation of less than or equal to 0.01°. This finding is consistent with other positions, helping to quantify the impact of microstructure on measurement uncertainty.

caption: Grain boundary map of the fusion zone (FZ) in the EBWed specimen, highlighting low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) in green and high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) in black.
summary: This EBSD map displays the grain boundary structure of the fusion zone in the EBWed specimen. LAGBs are represented in green and HAGBs in black. Observations indicate that LAGBs are more frequently present in the EBWed fusion zone compared to the fusion zones of MA and BA processed samples.

caption: Stress intensity factor as a function of temperature for ice, including a fitted expression and experimental data points with 10% error bars.
summary: This panel displays the temperature-dependent stress intensity factor for ice. The plot incorporates experimental data points, marked with 10% error bars, alongside a fitted mathematical expression. This representation allows for the analysis of fracture toughness trends in ice across varying thermal conditions as reported in the referenced literature.

caption: Top view of the test plate featuring various channel diameters ranging from 2 mm to 12 mm, confirming that all channels remain clear after infiltration.
summary: This top-view photograph confirms that all investigated cooling channel diameters, ranging from 2 mm to 12 mm, remain clear after the stilt infiltration process. These results validate stilt infiltration as a reliable and promising technique for preventing unwanted copper infiltration in additively manufactured tool inserts with complex cooling geometries.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental and RF-predicted cycles to failure for long carbon fiber composites, using stress as the input measure for the baseline dataset.
summary: This parity plot presents the baseline performance of the Random Forest model using stress as the input measure without additional data production. It serves as a reference to evaluate the predictive accuracy of the model on unseen data when compared against the enhanced dataset results.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry profiles comparing an ideal capacitor to a non-ideal capacitor exhibiting resistive behavior.
summary: This panel displays four cyclic voltammetry graphs illustrating the electrochemical response of supercapacitors. The comparison highlights the difference between an ideal capacitor and a real-world capacitor affected by internal resistance. These curves serve as fundamental examples for evaluating capacitive performance and identifying deviations from ideal electrochemical behavior in energy storage systems.

caption: Temperature-composition (ϑ, x, y) diagram for a binary propane and n-butane mixture, highlighting equilibrium condensation (A), local total condensation (B), and an intermediate condensation case (C) for a vapor mixture with an initial propane amount fraction of 0.5.
summary: This temperature-composition diagram illustrates the phase behavior of a zeotropic propane and n-butane mixture. It identifies three distinct theoretical condensation pathways: equilibrium condensation, local total condensation, and an intermediate case. These cases are demonstrated for a vapor mixture starting with an initial propane amount fraction of 0.5.

caption: Time-dependent current response of HPTH60, HPG60, HPE60, and HPO60 i-wi materials (3x3 mm cross-section) held at a constant 1 V potential while undergoing cyclic 100% extension.
summary: Current versus time curves are presented for four different i-wi materials (HPTH60, HPG60, HPE60, and HPO60) under a constant 1 V potential. The measurements compare the electrical stability of these materials at rest and during cyclic 100% extension, characterizing their performance consistency under dynamic mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Spider graph illustrating the tensile strength performance across various ASA recycling course levels.
summary: This radar chart summarizes the tensile strength of specimens subjected to different ASA recycling course levels. The data indicates that most recycling levels show an increase in tensile strength relative to the first course, with specific variations observed across the third and sixth levels for the M-H material system.

caption: Detailed evolution of the (1 1 0) Bragg reflection peak, illustrating a systematic shift toward higher 2θ angles as nickel content increases.
summary: The (1 1 0) Bragg reflection peak shifts toward higher 2θ angles as nickel content increases in the (Fe0.7Al0.3)100-xNix powders. This shift is attributed to the substitution of Fe and Al atoms by smaller Ni atoms within the bcc-Fe crystal lattice, reflecting the influence of atomic radii on lattice parameters.

caption: Bright-field STEM image of the specimen deformed at 300 °C and 10^-5 s^-1, showing a low density of dislocations.
summary: Captured in the specimen deformed at 300 °C and 10^-5 s^-1, this bright-field STEM micrograph reveals a sparse distribution of dislocations. Observations across both the FZ and CZ regions confirm that only a few dislocations are present, contrasting significantly with the higher density observed at lower temperature and higher strain rates.

caption: Macroscopic morphology of a thin-walled specimen fabricated without SOAM assistance, exhibiting uneven deposition collapse at the start and end points of the arc.
summary: This photograph displays the macroscopic morphology of a thin-walled specimen produced without the swinging alternating magnetic field (SOAM). The specimen exhibits significant uneven deposition collapse at both the start and end points of the arc, indicating poor geometric control during the additive manufacturing process without magnetic field assistance.

caption: Pole figure of sample L 67 in the {100} build direction plane, illustrating a weakening of texture as the volumetric energy density decreases.
summary: Analysis of the L 67 sample pole figure reveals a reduction in crystallographic texture compared to higher energy density samples. This weakening of the orientation distribution across all directions indicates that decreasing the volumetric energy density leads to more limited preferential grain alignment within the build direction plane.

caption: Experimental demagnetization curves measured for homogeneous, c-plane GBD, and SAGBD treated Nd-Fe-B magnets, validating the simulated performance trends.
summary: This panel presents actual experimental demagnetization curves for homogeneous, c-plane GBD, and SAGBD treated magnets. These measurements provide empirical validation for the micromagnetic simulation results, confirming that the SAGBD treatment effectively enhances the coercivity of the magnet by suppressing the nucleation and propagation of reversed domains during demagnetization.

caption: Rendered 3D computer-aided design models of the gyroid structure, displaying a top-down view on the left and two distinct perspective angles on the right to illustrate the complex geometry.
summary: This panel presents the 3D computer-aided design model of a gyroid structure, which serves as the target geometry for mSLAb printing. The rendered views, including a top-down perspective and two angled projections, illustrate the complex architecture used as a reference for evaluating print fidelity across various experimental conditions.

caption: Comparison of I-V curves for a 3x3 mm HPE60 i-wi specimen at rest versus states of 50% and 100% mechanical extension.
summary: The I-V behavior of a 3x3 mm HPE60 i-wi sample is evaluated at rest and under mechanical strain of 50% and 100% extension. This comparison demonstrates the sensitivity of the electrical current-potential relationship to physical deformation, highlighting the material's performance as a strain-responsive electrical conductor under DC conditions.

caption: Flexural strength, sintered density, and Weibull modulus comparison between 15 h scCO2 + 67 h debinding samples and commercial Admatec A130 prints.
summary: This panel displays the flexural strength, sintered density, and Weibull modulus for the experimental 15 h scCO2 extraction and 67 h debinding samples compared to commercial Admatec A130 prints. Outliers were removed from the analysis, and horizontal lines indicate average values, demonstrating that the experimental samples are comparable to commercial standards.

caption: EBSD phase map of the LPBF-HIP specimen after 1000 h LBE exposure, showing negligible FCC-to-BCC phase transformation.
summary: The EBSD phase map provides insight into the phase stability of the LPBF-HIP specimen after 1000 h of LBE exposure. The results demonstrate that there is negligible FCC-to-BCC phase transformation within the corroded regions, confirming that the material maintains its primary phase composition despite the harsh liquid metal environment.

caption: Monte Carlo snapshot of CrN nitride at 1500 K, displaying Cr and N atoms with magnetic states indicated by color (gray for spin-down, purple for no-spin, and pink for spin-up).
summary: This Monte Carlo snapshot at 1500 K illustrates the chemical and magnetic configuration of CrN nitride. Cr and N atoms are shown, while Fe and Ni are hidden. The magnetic states of Cr atoms are color-coded, revealing nearly equal numbers of spin-up and spin-down atoms, which facilitates the formation of CrN-rich domains.

caption: Monte Carlo snapshot at 500 K for the pseudo-ferrimagnetic (FiM) simulation, showing the distribution of Fe (red), Ni (green), Cr (blue), and N (dark blue) atoms.
summary: This Monte Carlo snapshot at 500 K represents the atomic configuration of the FiM state. Fe, Ni, Cr, and N atoms are color-coded to visualize their spatial distribution. The FiM state is shown to favor Fe-Cr ordering and effectively suppresses the formation of B1-type CrN-like domains compared to the NM state.

caption: Live/dead staining visualization of BMSCs seeded on scaffolds, illustrating cell viability and distribution patterns.
summary: Live/dead staining images reveal the viability and spatial distribution of BMSCs seeded on the scaffolds. These observations provide a qualitative assessment of the biocompatibility of the materials, showing how cells interact with the scaffold surface and maintain their viability under the experimental conditions tested in this study.

caption: Confusion matrix illustrating the classification accuracy of the stethoscope-CNN model on the test abnormality dataset.
summary: Stethoscope-CNN classification performance is evaluated via this confusion matrix using the test abnormality dataset. The results confirm the high classification accuracy of the stethoscope sensor-based model, which aligns with the robust anomaly detection performance observed in the s-CAE model, effectively distinguishing between normal powder flow and various abnormality types.

caption: Dynamic interaction of dislocations within the subsurface region of the nickel-based superalloy, highlighting their continuous motion post-formation.
summary: This panel displays the dynamic behavior of dislocations within the subsurface of the nickel-based superalloy. Following their initial formation due to machining-induced plastic deformation, these dislocations remain in constant motion, leading to complex interactions within the subsurface microstructure as they propagate through the crystal lattice of the material.

caption: Atom probe tomography elemental composition profile of WP4 highlighting the distribution of Mo and Fe within the matrix phase.
summary: The atom probe tomography profile for the WP4 alloy demonstrates the specific distribution of Mo and Fe within the matrix. Quantitative analysis indicates that Mo is present at approximately 3 at.% and Fe at 0.4 at.%, confirming their preferential localization within the matrix phase of the material's microstructure.

caption: Void denuded zone width measurements for Fe-10Cr alloy, highlighting observed deviations between 0.1 and 10 appm He/dpa irradiation conditions at temperatures exceeding 500 °C.
summary: Fe-10Cr alloy void denuded zone widths are plotted against inverse temperature using average distance and slope variation methods. A key finding is the divergence in denuded zone width between 0.1 and 10 appm He/dpa irradiated samples at temperatures above 500 °C, indicating sensitivity to helium concentration at higher thermal regimes.

caption: Schematic representation of the experimental chamber assembly, illustrating its mounting configuration between two stainless steel flanges.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental setup, featuring a chamber mounted between two stainless steel flanges. The system is designed to hold 200 mL of distilled water, as indicated in the experimental procedure. The diagram provides a clear visual overview of the physical arrangement used for the described testing conditions.

caption: ALP staining results of BMSCs after 7 days of culture, comparing matrix scaffold extracts against negative (C-) and positive (C+) controls.
summary: ALP staining was conducted after 7 days to evaluate the osteoinductive activity of the matrix scaffolds. The positive control group (C+) showed strong ALP positivity, whereas the matrix scaffold groups showed no significant difference compared to the negative control (C-), indicating that osteoinductive activity was successfully removed from the scaffolds.

caption: IDMAP projection of the top-12 color features for the phantom experiment, showing distinct clustering of levodopa concentrations at 100, 200, and 300 μM alongside blank tests.
summary: The IDMAP plot for the phantom experiment illustrates the effectiveness of the 12 selected color features in discriminating between different levodopa concentrations. The visualization reveals well-separated clusters corresponding to 100, 200, and 300 μM levodopa levels, as well as the blank control tests, demonstrating clear sample differentiation.

caption: Arrhenius-like plot displaying the temperature dependence of critical (σc), peak (σp), and steady-state (σss) stresses for WAAM Al-4043 deformed at a strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹ across the 200–400 °C range.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the temperature sensitivity of WAAM Al-4043 under a strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹. The critical, peak, and steady-state stresses decrease monotonically with increasing temperature. These metrics remain closely spaced, indicating rapid work hardening saturation and a steady flow behavior dominated by dynamic recovery processes.

caption: Isometric 3D view of the wavy surface topology for sample 3 prior to laser shock processing.
summary: This panel displays the 3D isometric view of the wavy surface topology for sample 3 before the laser shock processing. It establishes the baseline surface condition for the third sample, documenting the initial wavy morphology prior to the application of the LSPwC processing technique.

caption: Comparison of a three-dimensional BCC unit cell with radius R = 0.25 mm (Vf,3D = 0.264) against its two-dimensional equivalent with radius Re = 0.070 mm (Vf,2D = 0.188).
summary: This panel illustrates the geometric comparison between a 3D BCC unit cell and its 2D numerical equivalent. With a length of 2 mm and a radius of 0.25 mm, the 3D structure is modeled against a 2D counterpart with a radius of 0.070 mm to maintain structural equivalence for TPB testing.

caption: SKPFM surface potential difference map of the DED-LB Ti–6Al–4V sample.
summary: Scanning Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (SKPFM) provides a map of the surface potential difference for the DED-LB Ti–6Al–4V sample. This technique is integrated with SEM and AFM to correlate compositional variations with surface potential, offering a comprehensive understanding of the electrochemical properties across the additively manufactured sample's surface.

caption: Calculated Zn-Fe binary phase diagram generated using the TCFE12 database.
summary: This panel displays the equilibrium Zn-Fe phase diagram calculated via the TCFE12 database using Thermo-Calc software. It serves as the baseline reference for comparing the effects of alloying elements on phase formation within the 600–900 °C temperature range and the full 0–100% Zn composition spectrum.

caption: Isothermal M-H curves for the Gd20Dy20Er20Al20Fe20 high-entropy amorphous alloy.
summary: The isothermal M-H curve for the Gd20Dy20Er20Al20Fe20 high-entropy amorphous alloy is displayed to investigate magnetic transition features. The curve exhibits higher slopes under low magnetic fields when T < TC, followed by a gradual flattening, which is characteristic of ferromagnetic state behavior in this amorphous material.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation (CCT) diagram for ER110S-G steel, featuring a shaded region representing the cooling rate range observed in the 15th layer of thin-wall structures, bounded by the highest (S1) and lowest (S6) heat input conditions.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation behavior of ER110S-G steel under varying cooling rates. The shaded region highlights the experimental cooling range for thin-wall structures. Sample S1, corresponding to the upper bound of this range, is expected to exhibit a predominantly ferritic microstructure with low martensite fractions.

caption: Laser microscope image of the GH4169 specimen surface fabricated using the strip-based linear heat input mode, resulting in a surface roughness of 14.89 μm.
summary: Laser microscopy illustrates the surface morphology of the GH4169 specimen fabricated through strip-based linear heat input. The measured surface roughness is 14.89 μm. This value is statistically similar to the roughness observed in specimens produced using the sub-area distributed heat input mode, indicating comparable surface quality between these two methods.

caption: Dilatometric expansion curves representing the bainitic transformation kinetics during isothermal holding for steels processed under varying intercritical annealing conditions.
summary: This dilatometric plot illustrates the linear expansion behavior of steels during isothermal holding. Reducing the isothermal holding temperature from 300 to 200 °C significantly slows the bainitic transformation kinetics. Higher holding temperatures promote faster transformation rates, resulting in increased bainite fractions and lower retained austenite levels, which directly influence the final material hardness.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction displaying 0.5% of the total Ti atoms, with a dark green iso-composition surface highlighting regions where Ti content exceeds 20 at. % to delineate the fine Laves phase.
summary: This APT reconstruction provides a 3D visualization of the fine Laves phase particles within the alloy. By plotting 0.5% of the Ti atoms and using a dark green iso-composition surface for regions with Ti content greater than 20 at. %, the morphology and distribution of the Laves phase are clearly resolved.

caption: Magnified view of grain E showing a larger structural unit with a c-axis deviation of 37°.
summary: High-magnification SEM analysis of grain E displays a larger structural unit compared to grain D. This grain demonstrates a moderate c-axis deviation of 37° from the normal direction, illustrating the range of crystallographic orientations present within the shell's fibrous laminate architecture during the growth process.

caption: IPF-X map of the S1-S specimen, where white arrows indicate grains oriented close to the [111] direction.
summary: The IPF-X map reveals the crystallographic orientation of grains in the S1-S specimen. Analysis shows that the majority of grains encountered by the crack during steps (i) and (iii) are aligned near the [111] direction, as highlighted by the white arrows, indicating a preferred orientation along the crack path.

caption: Raman spectrum comparing the SiC green body and the sample following selective laser melting processing.
summary: Raman analysis is depicted for both the SiC green body and the sample post-selective laser melting. This spectroscopic data provides insight into the chemical and structural changes occurring during the laser processing stage, complementing the diffraction results obtained from the various PIP cycle samples.

caption: Electronic band structure diagram for a hybridized I-WP unit cell configuration combining relative densities of 32% and 22%.
summary: This panel shows the electronic band structure for a hybridized I-WP unit cell design that integrates regions of 32% and 22% relative density. The plot demonstrates the resulting electronic dispersion characteristics of the combined architecture, illustrating how hybridization of different density components influences the overall band structure properties.

caption: Calculated Mo concentration profiles across half a dendrite in low Fe Inconel® 625 at 1160 °C, showing temporal evolution from Scheil-calculated initial conditions.
summary: This panel displays the simulated Mo concentration profiles for low Fe Inconel® 625 during a 1160 °C heat treatment. Starting from Scheil solidification profiles, the data illustrates the diffusion-driven homogenization of Mo, which is identified as the alloying element with the lowest diffusivity (9.5 × 10⁻¹⁵ m²/s) in this alloy system.

caption: Continuous cooling experiments performed from the supercooled liquid region at 713 K using various cooling rates, with fictive temperatures determined via the Moynihan method to correlate cooling rates with equivalent enthalpic states.
summary: Continuous cooling experiments starting from 713 K are depicted to characterize the thermal history of the material. By applying the Moynihan method to calorimetric measurements, these experiments allow for the assignment of specific cooling rates to various fictive temperatures, providing a direct link between processing conditions and the resulting enthalpic state.

caption: Average coefficient of friction (COF) values for Alloy 800HT plotted against temperature, including standard deviation bars to represent the variability observed during sliding tests in helium at 0.04 m/s and 5 N.
summary: Average COF values for Alloy 800HT are presented as a function of temperature in a helium environment. The inclusion of standard deviation values confirms the trend observed in the in situ data, where the magnitude of COF fluctuations varies significantly across the tested temperature range from 500 °C to 750 °C.

caption: Polar plot quantifying cell alignment for 18% porosity constructs across 0, 50, and 250 mW·cm⁻² ultrasound conditions using a three-degree accumulation range.
summary: Polar plots quantify cell alignment for 18% porosity scaffolds under varying ultrasound intensities. Utilizing a three-degree accumulation range ensures accuracy in the quantitative assessment of cell orientation. These plots confirm the positive influence of ultrasound on cell alignment, supporting the qualitative findings observed in the corresponding confocal imaging panels.

caption: Transmittance spectra of SL/C/P coatings compared to the SL-0/C/P control, illustrating the superior UVA and UVB-blocking performance of the modified coatings.
summary: The transmittance spectra reveal that all SL/C/P coatings exhibit excellent UVA and UVB-blocking properties compared to the SL-0/C/P control. This panel highlights the optical performance of the coatings, confirming their ability to effectively attenuate UV radiation across the relevant spectral regions.

caption: 3D surface topographic map of the unimodal coarse green sample.
summary: This panel displays the 3D surface topographic map of the unimodal coarse green sample. The visualization provides a detailed representation of the surface morphology and roughness characteristics of the material in its green state, serving as a baseline for comparing the surface features of the various processed samples.

caption: Dielectric constant (Dk) values measured at a frequency of 1 MHz.
summary: Dielectric constant (Dk) measurements are shown in panel (b). The introduction of the BAG prepolymer results in a slight increase in the dielectric constant, with values rising from 3.19 to 4.10 when tested at a frequency of 1 MHz, indicating a measurable change in the material's electronic polarization properties.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data for PNCs, including (i) Nyquist curves, (ii) impedance magnitude (|Z|) versus frequency plots, and (iii) Bode phase plots.
summary: Electrochemical mechanisms of all PNCs were investigated using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The resulting data, presented as Nyquist curves, impedance magnitude versus frequency plots, and Bode plots, provide a comprehensive analysis of the interfacial electrochemical processes and the impedance characteristics of the different PNC materials under study.

caption: Average stress intensity factors (SIFs) as a function of crack length for both the PSP and Alloy 247DS materials, derived from FEA calculations.
summary: This graph illustrates the relationship between average SIFs and crack length for the PSP and Alloy 247DS materials. The data, obtained through FEA calculations, provides a comparative overview of the fracture behavior for these two materials as the crack propagates through the tested specimen configurations.

caption: Schematic representation of the EMP preparation procedure involving demethylation, ethanol precipitation, and vacuum lyophilization at −50 °C.
summary: This panel illustrates the preparation process for EMP, which includes a demethylation step followed by precipitation with 95% ethanol. The material is then subjected to vacuum lyophilization at −50 °C for 48 hours and stored in a desiccator at 25 °C to ensure stability for subsequent experimental use.

caption: Isolated 3D morphology of the Q phase within the as-cast HPDC aluminum alloy matrix.
summary: The Q phase morphology is isolated from the bulk 3D reconstruction of the as-cast HPDC Al-8Si-4Mg-4Cu-4Zn alloy. This view highlights the specific spatial distribution and interconnected structure of the Q phase, which is a critical intermetallic component within the complex microstructure of the investigated aluminum alloy.

caption: Deconvolution of the 29Si MAS NMR spectrum for slag 3, showing a primary resonance peak at -74 ppm.
summary: The 29Si MAS NMR spectrum for slag 3 exhibits a main resonance peak at -74 ppm. Peak deconvolution indicates that silicon predominantly exists in a single configuration. Given the low silicon content in slag 3, the structure likely includes silicon atoms with two connections to aluminum, specifically (1Al) and potentially (2Al) environments.

caption: Hydrogen permeation transients for Alloy 625 samples, comparing specimens with the largest (center) and smallest (edge) grain sizes under a cathodic current density of -20 mA/cm² at 60 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the hydrogen permeation transients for Alloy 625 samples with varying grain sizes, specifically comparing center and edge specimens. Tested at 60 °C under a cathodic current density of -20 mA/cm², the data allows for the calculation of hydrogen transport parameters using time-lag and time-breakthrough analytical methods.

caption: Backscattered electron SEM image of the Orthoflex material post-cured for 14 minutes, shown after aging at 100x magnification.
summary: This SEM image illustrates the Orthoflex material, post-cured for 14 minutes, after it has been subjected to aging. Observed at 100x magnification, the image provides a clear overview of the microstructure, enabling the assessment of how the specific post-curing duration influences the material's morphological response to the aging process.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectrum of SL:Er,Yb phosphor under 380 nm UV excitation, featuring an inset schematic illustrating the energy transfer mechanism from the phosphor to the perovskite quantum dots.
summary: This panel displays the photoluminescence emission spectrum of the SL:Er,Yb upconversion phosphor when excited at 380 nm. An inset diagram is included to visually represent the energy transfer process occurring from the SL:Er,Yb phosphor to the perovskite quantum dots, providing a mechanistic understanding of the observed optical behavior.

caption: Minimum energy path for the fourth NbTaV sample realization, showing the energy landscape E(x1) and an inset of the dislocation line configuration at the local minimum energy position derived from atomistic NEB and PN modeling.
summary: This panel presents the energy landscape for the fourth NbTaV sample realization, comparing NEB and PN model results for dislocation glide. The inset highlights the dislocation line configuration at the local minimum energy position, offering a visual representation of the atomic structure obtained from the simulation methods used.

caption: Radar chart comparing the energy absorption (EA) up to the reference point of load (RPL) for coarse-grained (CG) and small-grained (SG) structural configurations.
summary: This radar chart illustrates the energy absorption (EA) up to the reference point of load (RPL) for various CG and SG structural configurations. The data reveals that CG samples consistently exhibit nearly twice the EA capacity of SG samples across almost all configurations, despite only a 45% increase in specimen mass.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the HT-NNS-HIP NAB alloy after annealing at 700 °C for 2 h, displaying the resulting grain orientation.
summary: The HT-NNS-HIP NAB alloy, subjected to annealing at 700 °C for 2 h, is characterized by this inverse pole figure map. The EBSD results reveal a generally random grain orientation across the sample, indicating that the near-net-shape hot isostatic pressing process maintains a uniform crystallographic structure following the thermal treatment.

caption: Persistence diagram (PD 1) of Standard SLS glass illustrating loop size distribution, with highlighted representative atomic structures showing Si (blue), O (red), Na (green), and Ca (yellow) atoms.
summary: This persistence diagram displays the distribution of loops of various sizes for Standard SLS glass based on birth and death times. Loops near the diagonal represent subloops, while those within the red circle indicate intra-tetrahedral SiO 2 loops and four- and five-membered loops containing modifiers. Larger loops concentrate in the blue square.

caption: Experimental test matrix outlining the organization of four biological replicates (B1-B4), each derived from a distinct colony inoculated into media for initial overnight culture.
summary: The experimental test matrix defines the structure of the study, utilizing four biological replicates labeled B1 through B4. Each replicate originates from a single colony that underwent an initial overnight culture in media, ensuring consistency across the two separate experiments conducted for the CFU counting analysis.

caption: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results for Al-10 wt%RE binary alloys, highlighting the superior corrosion resistance of the Al-Y alloy through its highest impedance value.
summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results for the Al-10 wt%RE binary alloys align with observed corrosion trends. The Al-Y alloy exhibits the highest impedance among the tested samples, which directly reflects its superior corrosion resistance compared to the other binary alloys when exposed to the natural seawater environment.

caption: Nb-Ti-Zr ternary phase diagram illustrating the explored compositional space, with yellow dashed lines delineating the design criteria for single BCC phase formation.
summary: The ternary phase diagram summarizes the single-phase design guidelines for the Nb-Ti-Zr system. Yellow dashed lines highlight the specific region of the diagram where single BCC phase formation is expected. This design space is narrowed down to approximately 10% of the total ternary diagram, providing clear compositional guidelines for alloy development.

caption: FTIR spectra of MBGNPs, ESPWOM, and ESPWM particles at day 0, showing characteristic chemical bonding information.
summary: FTIR spectra for MBGNPs, ESPWOM, and ESPWM particles at day 0 are presented to identify the chemical composition and functional groups present in the samples. This spectroscopic analysis establishes the baseline chemical signature of the materials before they are subjected to the 28-day immersion in SBF solution.

caption: FT-IR spectra acquired from the surface of a porous titanium cube, illustrating chemical changes across sequential modification stages.
summary: This panel displays FT-IR spectra characterizing the surface of a porous titanium cube at various modification stages. These spectroscopic measurements, conducted on an edge fragment of the cube, reveal distinct chemical signatures corresponding to the different surface topographies and modification steps applied to the material during the experimental process.

caption: Phase angle versus frequency plots for the 625+ alloy before, during, and after cathodic polarization in 0.5 M H2SO4, showing a broad time constant near -90° at low frequencies.
summary: This Bode plot displays the phase angle response across a frequency range for the 625+ alloy. Before cathodic polarization, the data exhibits a broad time constant between 10 and 0.1 Hz, indicating a highly capacitive, homogeneous, and compact interface. The response remains consistent across different polarization conditions.

caption: Rietveld refinement of the in situ neutron powder diffraction pattern for alloy C (La1.8Mg1.2Ni9) at 1173 K, with vertical bars denoting the Bragg peak positions of the constituent phases.
summary: Rietveld refinement of the in situ neutron powder diffraction pattern for alloy C (La1.8Mg1.2Ni9) at 1173 K demonstrates excellent agreement between the experimental and calculated patterns. Vertical bars indicate the positions of Bragg peaks for the phase constituents, confirming the structural analysis of the alloy under high-temperature conditions.

caption: Room temperature M-H magnetic hysteresis loops for as-prepared Ni-Fe alloy powders with varying compositions, measured using a vibrating sample magnetometer with an applied field range of 0 to 7 kOe.
summary: This figure displays the magnetic hysteresis behavior of Ni-Fe alloy powders at room temperature. The M-H curves were obtained using a vibrating sample magnetometer with an applied magnetic field ranging from 0 to 7 kOe, illustrating the magnetic response characteristics of the alloy particles across various compositions.

caption: Hemispherical conductivity domain representation encapsulating solid features within the three-dimensional design space, where grayscale intensity denotes the influence of neighboring elements on local conductivity.
summary: This panel illustrates the three-dimensional conductivity domain as a hemisphere surrounding the solid features of the design. The grayscale shading serves as a visual indicator of element influence, where darker regions signify a higher degree of influence from neighboring elements on the local conductivity within the computational domain.

caption: Hardness versus indentation depth (H-h) curves comparing hard and soft columnar grains in Alloy B.
summary: The H-h curves demonstrate a clear divergence in the indentation size effect (ISE) regions between hard and soft columnar grains. For the hard columnar region, the ISE region is shifted upwards, indicating a reduced dislocation storage volume caused by the saturation effect of pre-existing GNDs around densely packed quasi-crystalline particles.

caption: Visualization of the first four principal component bases, ϕi, which serve as fundamental patterns for reconstructing SAS data.
summary: Depicting the first four basis PC bases, ϕi, this panel illustrates the fundamental components used to reconstruct any SAS pattern. Eight principal components are required to account for 95% of the explained variance in the dataset, providing a robust mathematical framework for representing the complex 2D SAS patterns observed.

caption: High-resolution SEM-BSE image corresponding to the magnified IPF map in panel (g), revealing the local grain features along the build direction.
summary: This high-resolution SEM-BSE image corresponds to the magnified IPF map in panel (g). It provides a detailed visual representation of the local microstructure along the build direction, enabling a direct comparison between the physical grain features and the crystallographic orientation data presented in the corresponding IPF map.

caption: High-resolution Co 2p XPS spectrum displaying peaks at 793.45, 784.79, 781.23, and 778.42 eV, corresponding to Co 0 2p 1/2, unknown species, Co 2+ 2p 3/2, and Co 3+ 2p 3/2.
summary: The Co 2p XPS spectrum exhibits multiple peaks at 793.45, 784.79, 781.23, and 778.42 eV. These signals are assigned to Co 0 2p 1/2, an unknown peak, Co 2+ 2p 3/2, and Co 3+ 2p 3/2, respectively, illustrating the complex chemical environment of cobalt in the passive layer.

caption: Bar chart displaying average yield strength (YS) and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) values for vertical and horizontal tensile specimens.
summary: Average yield strength and ultimate tensile strength values are compared across vertical and horizontal orientations. This plot serves as evidence for the mechanical property variations observed between the two specimen directions, highlighting the specific strength metrics derived from the tensile test results.

caption: Unified Modeling Language use case diagram illustrating the primary interactions and functional requirements of the mobile application.
summary: This panel presents a UML use case diagram that defines the functional scope and user interactions within the mobile application. It serves as a foundational architectural model, outlining the primary system requirements and user-driven activities that guide the application's workflow during the initial user engagement phase.

caption: Averaged load–displacement curves for anodic Al2O3 samples subjected to 0, 4, 12, and 20 hours of hot water sealing (HWS), with shaded regions representing measurement uncertainty.
summary: Averaged load–displacement curves for the unsealed sample and three different HWS times are displayed. The data shows that increasing the HWS duration leads to a reduction in the maximum load sustained during constant displacement of the nanoindenter tip, indicating a change in mechanical response due to the sealing process.

caption: Galvanostatic electrolysis performance of PdNi catalyst during glycerol electro-oxidation reaction (GEOR) conducted at 100 mA cm-2 g eom, 80 °C, and 500 RPM in 2 M NaOH and 1 M glycerol, featuring periodic reactivation at -0.6 V vs. Hg/HgO and electrolyte refreshment every 2 hours.
summary: This plot displays the galvanostatic electrolysis performance of a PdNi catalyst during the glycerol electro-oxidation reaction over a 10-hour duration. The test conditions include a current density of 100 mA cm-2 g eom at 80 °C. Periodic reactivation and electrolyte refreshing every two hours were implemented to maintain catalytic stability.

caption: Primary surface topography of the 3D printed sample measured post-production.
summary: The primary surface topography of the 3D printed sample is visualized here. This measurement was obtained by scanning the surface slowly post-production to ensure high resolution. The resulting 3D reconstruction provides a baseline representation of the sample's surface state before the application of specific filtering processes to isolate waviness and roughness.

caption: Experimental measurement of the powder angle of repose, calculated as the inverse tangent of the height-to-radius ratio, yielding a value of 53°.
summary: This panel displays the angle of repose for the utilized powder, which is determined to be 53° by calculating the inverse tangent of the height-to-radius ratio. This measurement provides a quantitative assessment of the powder's flowability and internal friction characteristics, which are critical for understanding its behavior during processing.

caption: High-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy image capturing the atomic-scale structure of the twin boundaries within the austenite phase.
summary: High-resolution STEM imaging is employed here to resolve the atomic structure of the twin boundaries. By visualizing these interfaces at the atomic scale, the image confirms the presence of twins within the austenite grains, supporting the hierarchical twin structure model observed across the different scales of the deformed material.

caption: UV–VIS absorbance profiles for H 282 Virgin, H 282 300, H 282 1000, and H 282 1400 powders, illustrating that initial light absorbance at the powder surface increases with higher oxidation states.
summary: UV–VIS spectroscopy reveals the light absorption profiles of H 282 powders subjected to varying oxidation levels. The data demonstrates that initial surface absorbance increases with higher oxidation, which presumably leads to greater energy intake and elevated temperatures within the melt pool during the laser-based powder bed fusion process.

caption: μ-Raman spectra of KSER samples oxidized in a muffle furnace at 1373 K, showing spectral evolution across varying oxidation durations.
summary: This panel displays μ-Raman spectra for KSER samples oxidized in a muffle furnace at 1373 K. By analyzing these spectra, researchers identify various phases, including silica, alumina, silicon, and molybdenum disilicide, based on literature data. The results reveal how the material's phase composition evolves over different oxidation duration times.

caption: In situ FTIR spectra of CeNi BA@Al2O3 at 750 °C, showing enhanced CO2 characteristic peak intensities.
summary: In situ FTIR spectra for the CeNi BA@Al2O3 catalyst at 750 °C exhibit superior intensity changes in the 2160–2465 cm-1 range compared to the unmodified Ni@Al2O3. This indicates that the cerium-modified catalyst possesses enhanced performance in facilitating the conversion of CO2 during the reaction.

caption: Transformation temperatures (TTs) as a function of stress level for samples H1 and H5, illustrating the effect of hatch spacing on thermal transformation characteristics.
summary: Transformation temperatures are displayed as a function of stress level for samples H1 and H5, which represent changes in hatch spacing. A consistent trend is visualized for these TTs, with the anchor point highlighted in black, providing data on the material's thermal transformation behavior under varying hatch spacing.

caption: Differential thermal analysis (DTA) heating curves illustrating the solidification behavior of alloys with varying Hf content.
summary: Differential thermal analysis (DTA) heating curves are presented to characterize the solidification behavior of alloys with different Hf content. These curves provide essential thermal data, allowing for the systematic comparison of phase transformation temperatures and solidification characteristics across the various alloy compositions investigated in this study.

caption: Overview of the physical fixturing setup employed to secure the substrate during the laser mesh deposition process.
summary: The panel provides a photograph of the fixturing setup used to hold the substrate in place during the laser mesh deposition. This physical arrangement ensures stability and precision during the process, supporting the implementation of the various scan trajectories and mesh geometries described in the experimental methodology.

caption: Ferrite pole figure for the AB100-300 sample, showing lower texture intensities compared to the AB200-700 sample.
summary: The ferrite pole figure for the AB100-300 sample shows significantly lower texture intensities than those observed in the AB200-700 sample. This confirms the absence of a sharp ferrite texture along the build direction, highlighting how variations in LPBF processing parameters substantially alter the crystallographic texture of the as-built ferrite.

caption: Classification results from the cut class algorithm, highlighting the detection of various cut states and the successful identification of grid disturbances during the process.
summary: The classification results demonstrate the algorithm's capability to categorize cut classes in real-time. Notably, the plot confirms the correct detection of grid disturbances, indicating that the system effectively distinguishes between normal cutting conditions and external process interruptions during the experimental run described in the study.

caption: Final solidified state of the Inconel 713 lattice structure obtained via the top-gated casting method.
summary: This panel illustrates the solidified Inconel 713 lattice structure following the top-gated casting procedure. The successful infiltration of the 3 mm struts is confirmed, demonstrating the effectiveness of the top-gated system when operating at a pouring temperature of 1550 °C and a mold preheating temperature of 900 °C.

caption: Predicted evolution of the volume fraction of η-precipitates, highlighting the differences in precipitation kinetics resulting from distinct plunge time parameters.
summary: This plot shows the calculated volume fraction evolution of η-precipitates as a function of time for both fast and slow plunging speeds. The simulation results indicate how the chosen plunge parameters significantly alter the precipitation kinetics, allowing for a quantitative comparison of the phase evolution under different processing conditions.

caption: Latent component Z1 extracted from stress-strain curves across various deformation parameters.
summary: This panel displays the first latent component, Z1, extracted from stress-strain curves. The component represents a specific feature of the deformation data captured through the latent space analysis, providing insight into the underlying variables governing the mechanical behavior of the material under the tested deformation conditions.

caption: Pairwise scatter plot matrix illustrating the initial training database distribution for Q t 0 using a Leja knots sampling strategy with N = 3 samples.
summary: This pairwise plot visualizes the initial training database, which consists of N = 3 samples. The distribution of these samples is generated using a Leja knots distribution method. This matrix provides a comprehensive overview of the initial data points, serving as the foundational dataset for subsequent modeling and analysis tasks.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the laser mesh deposition using mesh 16, illustrating the resulting geometry and material distribution.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the cross-sectional profile of a laser mesh deposition produced with mesh 16. The image highlights the specific geometry achieved under these processing conditions. Analysis indicates that this configuration results in a total measured surface area of 5.62 mm2 for the deposited mesh structure.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the SLM-fabricated steel, showing carbides precipitated between α’-laths.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging of the SLM-fabricated steel shows carbides precipitated between α'-laths. This specimen, consisting predominantly of upper bainite with relatively coarse, sparsely distributed carbides, exhibits the lowest total phase boundary area and dislocation density compared to the wrought sample, reflecting its distinct microstructural characteristics and lower hydrogen trapping capacity.

caption: XRD pattern of MPC1 produced by EBM-PDME, showing a single-phase BCC Im-3m crystal lattice, attributed to the high cooling rate inherent to the process.
summary: This XRD pattern demonstrates that MPC1 synthesized by EBM-PDME maintains a single-phase BCC Im-3m crystal lattice. The structural integrity and phase purity are attributed to the high cooling rate characteristic of the EBM-PDME processing technique, distinguishing it from the arc-melted counterpart.

caption: Strengthened heterogeneous FCC unit cell.
summary: This panel shows a strengthened heterogeneous FCC unit cell. By applying optimization methods to the heterogeneous FCC base, the design achieves increased strength, illustrating the effectiveness of structural reinforcement techniques in enhancing the mechanical performance of complex lattice architectures.

caption: Finite element model of the re-entrant honeycomb structure subjected to compression along the X-direction, positioned between two rigid loading plates.
summary: This finite element model illustrates the re-entrant honeycomb structure during X-direction compression. The structure is positioned between two rigid plates to simulate loading conditions. This numerical simulation provides insight into the mechanical response of the honeycomb geometry when subjected to uniaxial compressive forces along the specified axis.

caption: Brightfield TEM image of the DED-fabricated W–Ti–Cr–V alloy after dual-beam ion irradiation at 900 °C to a dose of 12 dpa at focus.
summary: Documenting the microstructural state at 12 dpa, this brightfield TEM image captures the DED-fabricated W–Ti–Cr–V alloy during dual-beam ion irradiation at 900 °C. The image provides evidence of the ongoing defect accumulation and structural response of the BCC tungsten matrix as the irradiation dose continues to increase significantly.

caption: Radar chart illustrating the multi-criteria assessment results for various filament materials evaluated in the study.
summary: This radar chart provides a comprehensive visual summary of the multi-criteria evaluation performed on different filament materials. By mapping multiple performance metrics onto a single plot, the figure facilitates a direct comparison of material properties, allowing for an efficient assessment of the overall suitability of each filament for specific applications.

caption: Magnetic hysteresis loop of a LPBF processed 45–2000-5 sample subjected to conventional heat treatment, measured at 300 K with a maximum applied field of 2 T.
summary: This magnetic hysteresis loop characterizes a LPBF processed 45–2000-5 sample after conventional heat treatment. Measured at 300 K with a 2 T field, the material exhibits a coercive field of approximately 2.7 (10^3 /4π) A/m and a saturation magnetization of about 160 A.m^2/kg, indicating its soft magnetic behavior.

caption: Pore diameter distribution histogram for the anode foil processed with 12.5 vol% PSM content.
summary: Pore diameter distribution for the anode foil with 12.5 vol% PSM content is presented here. This histogram is part of the systematic evaluation of the top powder surface, illustrating how the pore size distribution evolves as the PSM concentration increases, which directly influences the morphology of the anodized anode foils.

caption: Thresholded T1-weighted MRI-reconstructions of three resin-printed phantoms, demonstrating the structural integrity of the casts following the molding process.
summary: Thresholded T1-weighted MRI-reconstructions of three resin-printed phantoms are presented to confirm the structural integrity of the casts after the molding process. Although minor inhomogeneities such as air pockets and TiO2 clusters were detected within the tissue-mimicking material, these features were sufficiently sparse to avoid impacting the subsequent acoustic results.

caption: Thermodynamic activity of Ni as influenced by Sc content in the Ni–20Co–20Cr–2Al–1Si-xSc alloy system, computed using FactSage 8.0.
summary: FactSage 8.0 thermodynamic software was utilized to calculate the activity of Ni in the Ni–20Co–20Cr–2Al–1Si-xSc alloy system as a function of Sc concentration. The resulting plot demonstrates the influence of Sc on the primary matrix element, providing fundamental data for understanding the thermodynamic landscape and alloying effects in this specific system.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of a γ-γ grain boundary in an alloy, visualized using 8.9% Mo isosurfaces to delineate the boundary structure and identify the region for 1D compositional analysis.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction highlights a randomly selected γ-γ grain boundary within the alloy. The boundary is clearly delineated using 8.9% Mo isosurfaces. A cylindrical analysis volume is superimposed on the structure, defining the specific path for extracting a 1D elemental concentration profile across the grain boundary interface.

caption: Color-coded X-ray micro-tomography micrograph of the central area, where open porosities are highlighted in green, closed porosities in blue, and the metallic Fe–Ni alloy matrix appears in white.
summary: This micro-tomography micrograph illustrates the porosity distribution within the heat-treated LPBF 45–2000-5 sample. Open pores are identified in green, while closed pores are represented in blue. The surrounding metallic Fe–Ni alloy matrix is clearly distinguished in white, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of the internal void structure.

caption: High-magnification view of the rectangular region in panel (a), revealing Ti(C,N) precipitates remaining on the surface after melting.
summary: High-magnification view of the rectangular region in panel (a), revealing Ti(C,N) precipitates remaining on the surface after melting. These precipitates were observed on the upper surface following the laser treatment and were subsequently confirmed through EDS analysis, providing insight into the microstructural evolution of the material under these specific processing conditions.

caption: Hexagonal y precipitate arrangement defined by a point-symmetry center, representing an alternative structural configuration to the hexagonal x arrangement.
summary: Panel d illustrates the hexagonal y precipitate arrangement, which is distinguished by its own point-symmetry center. Similar to the hexagonal x arrangement, this structure is generated through point-symmetric operations relative to the domain boundaries. It serves as a comparative structural model for analyzing precipitate distribution within the simulation framework.

caption: In-situ thermal monitoring of the M-MT-10L sample during the ninth-layer deposition, emphasizing a distinct defect feature within the track.
summary: This image displays the in-situ thermal monitoring of the M-MT-10L sample during the ninth-layer deposition. It focuses on a distinct defect feature, providing a clear visual representation of the thermal conditions surrounding the irregularity as the deposition process continues toward the tenth layer on the M-plate.

caption: Strain distribution along a sample featuring decaying amplitude reinforcement geometry, plotted against position at three distinct stress levels during uniaxial tension.
summary: Strain distribution along a sample featuring decaying amplitude reinforcement geometry, plotted against position at three distinct stress levels during uniaxial tension. Experimental strain values are compared with theoretical model predictions, demonstrating that the predictions closely follow the experimental data and support the initial hypothesis regarding the reinforcement geometry's effect.

caption: FTIR spectra of synthesized TP compared to pectin, measured across the 4000 to 700 cm-1 range.
summary: FTIR spectra of synthesized TP compared to pectin are shown, covering the range from 4000 to 700 cm-1. This spectroscopic comparison allows for the identification of characteristic functional groups and structural changes resulting from the synthesis process, providing evidence of the chemical modifications made to the pectin backbone.

caption: DTA baseline and reduced baseline diagrams for a 90% cold-rolled, recrystallization-annealed IN907 alloy sample heated to 1200 °C.
summary: This panel displays the DTA baseline and reduced baseline diagrams for a 90% cold-rolled, recrystallization-annealed IN907 superalloy sample. The data represents the thermal response of the material during heating up to 1200 °C, providing a foundational reference for identifying thermal events within the alloy's microstructure during the STA process.

caption: Pie chart illustrating the proportional distribution of direct energy consumption during the printing process for experimental conditions Exp 4 and Exp 7.
summary: This pie chart visualizes the energy consumption breakdown during the printing process for Exp 4 and Exp 7. The data reveals that the heated bed is the primary contributor to total energy usage, highlighting its dominant role in the overall power requirements during the fabrication of these specific experimental samples.

caption: Tabulated chemical composition of the regenerated passive film on the ATI718 Plus surface.
summary: This table summarizes the chemical composition of the regenerated passive film formed on the ATI718 Plus surface. It integrates the quantitative findings from the high-resolution XPS spectra of various metallic elements, providing a clear overview of the oxide and hydroxide proportions present in the surface passivation layer.

caption: STEM-BF image of M23C6 precipitates interacting with dislocations, including a magnified HAADF image, EDS mapping of the dislocation region, and a schematic diagram illustrating dislocations as diffusion channels.
summary: The STEM-BF image displays M23C6 precipitates that capture dislocations, acting as obstacles to their movement. A magnified HAADF image and EDS mapping characterize the local dislocation region. The accompanying schematic diagram illustrates how these dislocations serve as transfer channels for element diffusion within the material during the creep process.

caption: Low-field magnetic susceptibility (LFMS) magnetization versus temperature plots for the B-400 W sample, showing the evolution of magnetic properties before and after heat treatment.
summary: Low-field magnetic susceptibility magnetization versus temperature plots for the B-400 W sample, showing the evolution of magnetic properties before and after heat treatment. The magnetization of paramagnetic austenite serves as the zero-magnetization baseline. As-deposited samples exhibit significantly lower magnetization compared to their heat-treated counterparts, indicating a clear change in magnetic behavior.

caption: Polarization curve for the CO2 electroreduction cell tested at 750 °C, providing a secondary view of the electrochemical response.
summary: This polarization curve for the CO2 electroreduction cell at 750 °C displays a non-linear region at low current densities, transitioning into a linear relationship between voltage and current density. The data reflects the electrochemical behavior of the infiltrated catalyst oxide particles within the scaffold structure under these specific test conditions.

caption: Velocity distribution in the x-z section of the molten pool for Case 14 at 885μs, featuring liquid phase temperature contour lines.
summary: Representing the x-z section for Case 14 at 885μs, this simulation shows the velocity distribution within the molten pool. Liquid phase temperature contours are marked by white solid lines. Similar to other cases, the melt velocity is significantly elevated at the pool bottom and keyhole wall protrusions.

caption: Comparison of BCC lattice specimen with 0.17 relative density at 0.07 strain, showing solid FEM results left of the red line and beam-based simulation with optimal penalty parameters on the right.
summary: This panel displays a comparative analysis of a BCC lattice specimen with a relative density of 0.17 at a strain of 0.07. It contrasts solid FEM modeling on the left with beam-based simulation using optimal penalty parameters on the right, illustrating the global correlation between experimental testing and numerical predictions.

caption: Continuous cooling experiments performed at varying cooling rates to determine the relationship between cooling history and enthalpic state.
summary: Continuous cooling experiments conducted at different rates are presented to characterize the material's response to thermal processing. By mapping these cooling rates, researchers can assign specific fictive temperatures to each annealing state. This approach enables the identification of equivalent enthalpic states that are not directly accessible through isothermal experiments alone.

caption: Galvanostatic electrolysis performance of PdNi catalyst at 300 mA cm-2 in 2 M NaOH and 1 M glycerol at 80 °C, comparing continuous operation (red curve) against periodic reactivation at -0.6 V vs. Hg/HgO (blue, orange, and green curves).
summary: This plot illustrates the galvanostatic electrolysis of PdNi at 300 mA cm-2, demonstrating that periodic reactivation at -0.6 V vs. Hg/HgO effectively mitigates potential decay. While the non-reactivated electrode shows significant degradation, reactivated samples maintain potentials within 80 mV of the initial value, highlighting a strategy to sustain high-current glycerol electro-oxidation.

caption: Storage modulus (E') of TPU 95A, 82A, and 70A samples as a function of frequency, measured across a temperature range of 30 °C to 120 °C.
summary: Storage modulus trends for TPU specimens are presented across a frequency sweep at temperatures from 30 °C to 120 °C. Analysis reveals that E' increases with frequency while diminishing as the test temperature rises. These measurements were conducted above the glass transition temperatures for all tested TPU compositions.

caption: Electron probe X-ray microanalyzer maps of two melt pools in the Ti–Mo–Zr alloy, comparing elemental distribution under strong Marangoni motion (left) and weak Marangoni motion (right).
summary: These EPMA maps illustrate two distinct melt pools within the alloy cross-section. The left panel shows significant Ti enrichment at the swirl center with barren streaks of Zr and Mo. The right panel displays a swirl with minimal elemental enrichment, featuring only localized Zr concentration at the molten pool bottom.

caption: Calculated electronic densities of states (DOS) for La1.5Mg0.5Ni7−yCuy (y = 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) phases, illustrating the shift of the van Hove singularity toward the Fermi level with increasing copper concentration.
summary: This plot displays the electronic density of states for La1.5Mg0.5Ni7−yCuy compounds calculated using the scalar-relativistic PBE FPLO scheme. The results demonstrate that increasing copper concentration shifts the van Hove singularity to the Fermi level, qualitatively confirming the theoretical explanation proposed by Tazuke et al. regarding the electronic structure near the Fermi level.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves comparing 15 h scCO2 extraction followed by 101 h debinding in air (black) versus nitrogen (red dotted) atmospheres.
summary: This panel displays TGA curves for samples subjected to 15 hours of scCO2 extraction and 101 hours of thermal debinding. Comparing air and nitrogen atmospheres reveals that while air debinding effectively degrades organic content, nitrogen-debinded samples retain a higher residual organic content of approximately 1.2 to 2.0 wt.%.

caption: Geometric representation and design parameters of the lattice structure.
summary: This panel illustrates the geometric design and structural modeling of the lattice architecture. It provides a clear visualization of the lattice unit cell and its spatial arrangement, serving as the foundational design reference for the subsequent fabrication process described in the study's structural analysis.

caption: High-magnification STEM ADF image of the Chess strategy, showing the reduced dislocation density and entanglement characteristic of this scan strategy.
summary: High-magnification STEM ADF imaging of the Chess strategy confirms a lower dislocation density and improved strain distribution. This finding is supported by TEM analysis and FE-SEM backscattered images, which demonstrate that the Chess strategy results in a significant reduction in LAGB fraction, leading to enhanced material properties.

caption: XRD pattern and microstructure of the sintered Ti skeleton showing monophasic equiaxed grains.
summary: The XRD pattern and microstructure of the sintered Ti skeleton confirm the presence of monophasic equiaxed grains of hexagonal close-packed alpha-Ti. This diffraction data provides evidence of the crystalline composition, supporting the structural characterization of the Ti skeleton as a high-purity metallic component.

caption: IDMAP visualization of the 12 most relevant color features extracted from drop experiment samples.
summary: This IDMAP visualization displays the 12 most relevant color features derived from the drop experiment samples. By projecting these high-dimensional features into a lower-dimensional space, the plot illustrates the distribution and clustering of the experimental data, providing a clear representation of the top-ranked features identified for the drop experiment analysis.

caption: Load-penetration depth curves obtained from nanoindentation tests on GH4169 specimens processed via varying thermal input modes.
summary: Nanoindentation load-penetration depth curves are presented for GH4169 specimens fabricated using different thermal input modes. These curves characterize the mechanical response at the nanoscale, serving as the primary data source for evaluating the intrinsic mechanical properties of the gamma matrix across the various processing conditions investigated in this study.

caption: Photoluminescence emission profiles of 0.1 wt% CD-doped HDPE composites at each recycling step under 254 nm excitation, demonstrating that the presence of carbon dots does not alter the fundamental spectral shape.
summary: Photoluminescence spectra for samples containing 0.1 wt% CDs are shown for each recycling step. The results reveal that the presence of CDs does not affect the spectral shape of the emission profile. This observation is consistent with the CDs exhibiting very weak emission when excited at the same 254 nm wavelength.

caption: FT-IR spectral analysis of the BAG prepolymer synthesis.
summary: This figure displays the FT-IR spectrum obtained during the synthesis of the BAG prepolymer. The spectral data serves as a critical analytical tool to monitor the chemical reaction progress, providing confirmation of successful synthesis through the identification of characteristic molecular vibrations and functional group transformations within the material structure.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image displaying the surface morphology of the powder particles.
summary: This panel presents the morphology of the powder particles used in the study.
