The image provides a visual representation of the powder characteristics, which is essential for understanding the initial state of the material before the LPBF fabrication process, as described in the provided reference sentences.

caption: HSQC spectrum of DHPMA showing two unexpected proton signals coupled with additional carbon signals at 61 and 75 ppm.
summary: The HSQC spectrum provides detailed structural confirmation of DHPMA by mapping proton-carbon couplings. Analysis reveals two unexpected proton signals that correlate with additional carbon resonances at 61 and 75 ppm, further validating the chemical structure of the synthesized monomer beyond the initial 1H NMR observations.

caption: Electronic band structure and projected local density of states for a 2 × 2 supercell of single-layer GeN under 4% in-plane biaxial tensile strain, modeled with the PBE functional.
summary: Representing the electronic band structure and projected local density of states for a 2 × 2 supercell of single-layer GeN, this panel illustrates the material's response to 4% in-plane biaxial tensile strain. The results, modeled with the PBE functional, contribute to understanding the half-metallic properties emerging in single-layer GeN.

caption: Hadamard Mask (HM) pattern featuring an 8x8 grid configuration with 64 total apertures.
summary: This panel presents a Hadamard Mask (HM) structured as an 8x8 grid with 64 apertures. Like other HM panels, this configuration is linked to the centroids provided in the Supplemental Document, illustrating the progression of aperture density within the Hadamard-based mask design.

caption: Higher magnification STEM ADF view of the No pattern 180 strategy, focusing on the specific regions of dislocation entanglement highlighted by the blue arrow.
summary: Higher magnification STEM ADF imaging of the No pattern 180 strategy provides a detailed view of dislocation entanglement. High-resolution TEM analysis confirms that this strategy leads to higher dislocation densities. These structural characteristics are linked to the formation of more stable passive layers, as evidenced by lower electrochemical current densities.

caption: Fluorescence intensity at 590 nm for three samples: unconjugated MP-NPs without probe (1), unconjugated MP-NPs with free AlexaFluor568-streptavidin (2), and biofunctionalized MP-NPs with assembled AlexaFluor568-streptavidin (3).
summary: Fluorescence intensity at 590 nm is compared across three samples. The molecular assembly of the fluorescent probe on biotinylated MP-NPs (sample 3) yields a significant 10-fold increase in signal intensity compared to the control samples (1 and 2), confirming the effective binding of the probe to the biofunctionalized nanoparticles.

caption: Two-phase flow in a serpentine anode channel with baffles at a vertical–vertical orientation, showing slug-dominated flow at t = 10 s.
summary: Depicted here is the two-phase flow in a serpentine anode channel equipped with baffles at a vertical–vertical orientation. At t = 10 s, the flow is dominated by slugs. Interpreting the specific flow characteristics in this geometry remains challenging due to the prevalence of these slugs within the channel structure.

caption: Number distribution of spatters categorized by pixel area under GD-W conditions.
summary: Depicting the distribution of the number of spatters in each pixel region under GD-W, this line graph analyzes the frequency of spatter sizes. This distribution analysis helps characterize the spatter population behavior and size variations observed during the laser processing under the GD-W condition.

caption: Relative EDX elemental distribution map of AlCoCu0.6FeNi alloy after annealing at 1050 °C and slow cooling.
summary: This EDX mapping illustrates the elemental distribution within the AlCoCu0.6FeNi alloy following a 1050 °C annealing treatment and slow cooling. The analysis reveals a mixed microstructure characterized by distinct Cu-rich and Fe–Co-rich phases, providing insight into the phase separation behavior of the alloy under these specific thermal processing conditions.

caption: Digital image correlation displacement field map at the onset of burr formation, illustrating the emergence of a negative shear zone.
summary: At the onset of burr formation, this displacement map illustrates the formation of a negative shear zone. Subsequent deformation is localized along this specific plane, which is characteristic of the transition from steady-state chip formation to burr formation when using sharp tools during the machining process.

caption: Bright field TEM micrograph of LPBF-processed Ti-6Al-4V, revealing high dislocation density and the presence of alpha-prime martensite laths.
summary: This bright field TEM image captures the microstructure of LPBF-processed Ti-6Al-4V alloy. Key features identified include a high dislocation density caused by thermal strain and the presence of alpha-prime martensite laths, which are significant microstructural characteristics resulting from the rapid cooling rates inherent to the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Logarithmic intensity plot of the WPPM fit for the S-3000 specimen, showing the experimental neutron diffraction data, the superimposed fitted curve, and the residual plot.
summary: The S-3000 specimen is analyzed using neutron diffraction and the WPPM procedure. The experimental data is shown as black dots, with the fitted profile overlaid in color. The fit residual is reported above the pattern, and the intensity is presented on a logarithmic scale to aid in microstructural characterization.

caption: Macroscopic nominal stress-strain curves comparing experimental data against results derived from various simulation techniques.
summary: Macroscopic nominal stress-strain curves are plotted to evaluate the mechanical response of the material. By comparing experimental results with those obtained from different simulation techniques, this panel illustrates the predictive capability of the models in capturing the deformation behavior of the polycrystalline aggregate under applied mechanical loading conditions.

caption: EIS data for Ti6Al4V samples exposed to hydroxyapatite dissolution in SBF at pH 7.4 and 37.5 °C, reflecting the corrosion resistance in simulated physiological conditions.
summary: Nyquist plots display the EIS data for Ti6Al4V samples in hydroxyapatite dissolution within SBF at 37.5 °C and pH 7.4. These results, validated by equivalent circuit modeling with low chi-squared values, enable the analysis of corrosion mechanisms. The data track specific changes in the equivalent circuit for individual samples over time.

caption: Summary table outlining the primary advantages, potential disadvantages, and specific biomedical applications of Zn alloys produced via LPBF.
summary: This summary table provides a comprehensive overview of Zn alloys fabricated by LPBF. It categorizes the material's performance by detailing its advantages, limitations, and practical applications in the biomedical field, serving as a concise reference for the material's suitability in various clinical and structural medical scenarios.

caption: Comparison of minimum heat-treatment temperatures for binder-free silica systems versus literature-reported SLA-based transparent glass printing methods, distinguishing between binder-free (hollow circles) and organic/hybrid binder (solid circles) approaches.
summary: This scatter plot benchmarks the minimum heat-treatment temperature of the current binder-free silica system against existing SLA-based glass printing methods. By differentiating between binder-free and binder-containing approaches, the plot highlights the thermal processing efficiency of the developed method relative to established techniques in the field of transparent glass printing.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the natural logarithm of the relaxation time beta as a function of the reciprocal absolute temperature, derived from Avrami-type fitting of resistivity data.
summary: The Arrhenius plot displays the natural logarithm of the relaxation time beta against the reciprocal of absolute temperature. By calculating the slope of these data points, the activation energy for short-range order formation is determined to be 167 ± 24 kJ/mol, characterizing the kinetics of the structural evolution process.

caption: Detailed visualization of a second macroscopic defect with a corresponding line profile, illustrating the desired contrast where high gray values correlate with the defect and zero values indicate its absence.
summary: This panel provides a detailed view of a second macroscopic defect. The line profile shows the distribution of residual gray values, confirming the desired performance where high values are localized to the defective area and zero values represent the absence of defects, contrasting with the non-zero scatter-affected projection values.

caption: Magnified view of the 35–60 μm grain size range for the DCT-0 sample, focusing on the distribution of larger grains.
summary: Focusing on the 35–60 μm size range, this panel provides a magnified view of the larger grain population in the DCT-0 sample. It is part of the statistical analysis of grain refinement, establishing the baseline frequency of larger grains prior to the application of the DCT 36 h treatment.

caption: SAED pattern of the yellow-marked region in (d), viewed along the [100] α’ zone axis, confirming the presence of transition-iron-ε' carbide and cementite.
summary: The SAED pattern from the yellow-marked area in panel (d) identifies the carbides as transition-iron-ε' carbide and cementite. Viewed along the [100] α’ zone axis, the diffraction results confirm that these phases maintain a well-established orientation relationship with the ferrite, consistent with the lower bainite structure observed in the 1200 mm/s sample.

caption: Visual inspection of internal channel connectivity using a torch light source.
summary: The openness and continuity of the internal channels were evaluated by passing light from a torch through the sectioned heat exchanger. This visual verification method confirms that the channels are unobstructed and properly formed, demonstrating the success of the printing and depowdering procedures in creating functional internal pathways.

caption: Tafel plots derived from the polarization curves of Ni–B-1/BC, Ni–B-2/BC, and Ni–P/BC electrodes in 1 M PBS.
summary: Tafel plots derived from the polarization curves of Ni–B-1/BC, Ni–B-2/BC, and Ni–P/BC electrodes in 1 M PBS are presented. Ni–P/BC exhibits a lower Tafel slope than both Ni–B-1/BC and Ni–B-2/BC, which reveals that the Ni–P/BC catalyst possesses faster hydrogen evolution reaction kinetics.

caption: Particle size distribution histograms comparing 316L powder and ODS-316L mixed powder, highlighting the D50 values of 34.98 μm and 34.50 μm, respectively.
summary: This histogram displays the particle size distribution for 316L and ODS-316L powders. The D50 values of 34.98 μm for 316L and 34.50 μm for ODS-316L are nearly identical. These results demonstrate that the ball milling process used to create the ODS-316L mixture did not cause significant damage to the 316L matrix particles.

caption: Calculated solubility products of TiAl3, TiB2, and AlB2 phases in Al melts, demonstrating the thermodynamic stability of TiB2.
summary: The calculated solubility products reveal that the TiB2 phase possesses significantly lower solubility in Al melt compared to TiAl3 and AlB2 phases. This thermodynamic favorability is critical for the in-situ refinement strategy, as it ensures the stability and persistence of TiB2 particles within the molten aluminum matrix during processing.

caption: Backscattered electron (BSE) micrograph of the as-built Ti-27Nb-6Ta alloy processed at an energy density of 2.78 J/mm², revealing the microstructure with gas entrapment pores highlighted by a white circle.
summary: This BSE micrograph displays the microstructure of as-built Ti-27Nb-6Ta processed via PBF-LB/M at 2.78 J/mm². The image reveals the presence of tiny pores, which are highlighted by a white circle and attributed to gas entrapment originating from the initial powder feedstock material used during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Fluorescence imaging of rBMSCs on porous alloy scaffolds after 3 days of coculture, showing effective cell spreading and proliferation.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy using live/dead staining reveals that rBMSCs effectively spread and proliferated on all four types of porous alloy scaffolds after 3 days of coculture. The images confirm that the scaffold architecture supports initial cell attachment and growth, with scale bars provided at 500 μm for reference.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulated potential energy curves for BCC (red) and FCC (black) phases of AlxNi0.7-xCo0.132Cr0.064Fe0.104, featuring a blue dotted line representing the common tangent.
summary: This plot displays molecular dynamics simulated potential energy curves for BCC and FCC phases in the AlxNi0.7-xCo0.132Cr0.064Fe0.104 system. The common tangent indicates a thermodynamic driving force for the BCC to FCC transformation in the as-printed state, suggesting that while the transformation is energetically favorable, kinetic limitations may prevent it without external disturbances.

caption: Final sustainability score radar chart integrating HPI and TBL metrics to evaluate overall material configuration performance.
summary: Integrating HPI and TBL scores, this radar chart reflects the overall sustainability performance of each material configuration. The results confirm that the V50:R50 blend is the most sustainable configuration, achieving a score of -1.35, while highlighting the inherent challenges of achieving full rPLA substitution in performance-critical applications.

caption: Voltage–current density characteristics of the Cu–Ni/YSZ anode measured at 750 °C under flowing He/H2 and He/CH4 atmospheres.
summary: Voltage–current curves for the Cu–Ni/YSZ anode are presented at 750 °C. The performance is evaluated under two distinct gas environments: He/H2 (100 sccm, 50 vol% H2) and He/CH4 (100 sccm, 50 vol% CH4). These curves illustrate the electrochemical response of the anode material during operation in different fuel compositions.

caption: Apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions in 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during the delithiation process, calculated using Eq. (1).
summary: This panel displays the apparent diffusion coefficient of lithium ions for both 3D printed and 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation. Calculated via Eq. (1), these data points illustrate the kinetic behavior of lithium ions within the working electrodes, providing insight into the diffusion characteristics during the extraction process.

caption: Comparative analysis of the elastic modulus design range for Sine structures versus human cancellous bone tissue across different orientations.
summary: Comparing calculated mechanical ranges to human bone properties, this panel shows that the elastic modulus of Sine structures in 0° and 45° directions aligns well with cancellous bone requirements. This indicates the suitability of the Sine structure for orthopedic implants by matching the mechanical characteristics of natural bone.

caption: FTIR spectra of AFRP samples measured at 25 °C, 120 °C, and 200 °C, illustrating the chemical stability of the Onyx matrix.
summary: FTIR spectra of AFRP samples are presented at temperatures of 25 °C, 120 °C, and 200 °C. Because the surface consists solely of the Onyx matrix, these spectra exhibit peaks highly similar to those observed in CFRP, confirming consistent functional group assignments across the tested thermal conditions for the AFRP material.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation (CCT) diagram for the matrix of 420 steel, illustrating the martensitic transformation kinetics.
summary: Illustrating the CCT behavior for the matrix of AISI 420 steel, this diagram highlights the martensitic transformation process. Since the decomposition of austenite is highly dependent on the cooling rate, this plot provides the necessary data to predict the resulting microstructural constituents based on specific thermal cooling profiles.

caption: Optical micrograph of the LbL laminate showing dark domains corresponding to a modifier-rich phase.
summary: Optical microscopy of the LbL laminate reveals distinct dark domains within the material structure. These dark regions correspond to a modifier-rich phase, providing insight into the distribution of additives within the LbL-processed composite compared to conventional materials produced in a press.

caption: Electronic density of states for FeTi displaying a semimetallic profile with a pseudogap at the Fermi level and a band structure inset.
summary: FeTi displays a semimetallic electronic density of states with a significant pseudogap at the Fermi level. The inset sketch of the band structure reveals a slight overlap of valence and conduction bands, which occurs at different Brillouin zone locations and involves different orbitals compared to the Fe2VAl compound.

caption: Time-dependent mean square displacement of atoms in a melted stack of five elemental layers, simulated using the Farkas interatomic potential.
summary: Panel b illustrates the atomic dynamics in a stacked system of five elemental layers using the Farkas interatomic potential. Unlike the homogeneous prealloyed sample, the MSD in this stacked configuration shows time-varying diffusivities, reflecting the complex intermixing processes occurring within the structure during the MD simulation.

caption: Continuous cooling transformation diagram for the steel simulated at a peak temperature of 900 °C with a grain size of 100 μm.
summary: CCT diagram representing the simulated phase transformation behavior of steel at 900 °C with a 100 μm grain size. The JMatPro simulation provides insight into microstructural development, with red arrows marking cooling rates of 100 °C/s and 10 °C/s to facilitate analysis of the cooling process and resulting phase constituents.

caption: Live/dead fluorescence staining of rBMSCs after 24 hours of exposure to scaffold extracts, with live cells appearing green and dead cells red.
summary: Live/dead staining of rBMSCs after 24 hours of culture demonstrates the cytocompatibility of the scaffolds. The visualization shows that the majority of cells survived, indicated by the prevalence of green-stained live cells, confirming that the scaffold extracts do not induce significant cytotoxicity under the tested conditions.

caption: Resistivity versus temperature plot for the CrMnFeCoNiZr alloy film.
summary: The temperature-dependent resistivity curve for the CrMnFeCoNiZr alloy film is shown in this panel. This measurement tracks the electronic resistivity of the Zr-doped Cantor alloy across varying temperatures, completing the set of data used to evaluate the impact of different alloying elements on the electrical properties of these films.

caption: Voltage-current (VI) characteristics of patterned (thick lines) and un-patterned (thin lines) segments measured at 8 K under transverse magnetic fields of 3, 10, and 23 mT.
summary: This plot displays VI curves for patterned and un-patterned segments at 8 K under varying transverse magnetic fields. Patterned segments exhibit a distinct second kink with a significantly steeper slope compared to un-patterned sections. This behavior at high currents suggests accelerated vortex motion along the TIs and potential heating effects.

caption: Diffusion trajectory of a single H atom near the NGI at 1200 K over a 5.0 ns duration.
summary: The 1200 K trajectory of the H atom near the NGI is mapped by connecting 10.0 ps displacement vectors. This visualization captures the atomic-scale dynamics, showing that even at elevated temperatures, the NGI interface significantly influences the H atom's diffusion through trapping and potential sp3 C–H bond formation.

caption: Ni K-edge Fourier transformed EXAFS spectrum of freshly prepared Ni NFs, displaying metallic and oxidized features with limited long-range order.
summary: Freshly prepared Ni NFs exhibit Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra characterized by both metallic Ni-Ni and oxidized metal features. The absence of outer shell signals for Ni-Ni metallic bonds indicates a disordered atomic structure, distinguishing the material from the long-range order typically observed in standard nickel foil reference samples.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns for four distinct specimen groups, illustrating the crystalline phase characteristics of the materials.
summary: This figure presents the X-ray diffraction patterns for four distinct specimen groups. These patterns provide essential data regarding the crystalline structure and phase composition of the materials under investigation. The results serve as a primary characterization tool to evaluate the structural integrity and phase purity of the tested specimens.

caption: Comparative thermogravimetric analysis of ceramic VPP prints, showing mass loss profiles for samples before (black) and after (red) scCO2 extraction processes.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves for ceramic VPP prints are presented to evaluate the impact of scCO2 extraction on thermal stability. The plot compares the mass loss behavior of the ceramic material in its initial state (black) against the post-extraction state (red), providing insight into the effectiveness and chemical changes induced by the extraction process.

caption: Ti–Nb binary alloy phase diagram showing the region of infinite solid solubility where Nb forms a BCC-structured (β-Ti, Nb) solid solution.
summary: This Ti–Nb binary phase diagram demonstrates the thermodynamic stability of the system. Nb exhibits infinite solid solubility in β-Ti, facilitating the formation of a body-centered cubic (BCC) structured (β-Ti, Nb) solid solution, which is a critical feature for understanding the metallurgical compatibility of these elements in alloy design.

caption: Comparison of TGA thermograms for not aged and aged samples in PBS for 15 days, specifically in the 40–250°C range, with weight loss in green and derivative weight loss in blue.
summary: TGA thermograms compare not aged and aged samples in PBS over a 40–250°C range. A mass loss of 1–1.5% is observed between 50 and 160°C for all three resins. The maximum peak temperature occurs between 100 and 120°C, which is consistent with the evaporation of water from the samples.

caption: Dilatometric measurement of cellulose aerogel showing the correlation between temperature and volumetric expansion.
summary: This dilatometric analysis illustrates the thermal response of cellulose aerogel. The plot clearly demonstrates the relationship between temperature and volume change, providing essential data on the material's expansion characteristics. These results confirm the structural behavior of the aerogel when subjected to varying thermal conditions during the testing process.

caption: Localized TUNA current-voltage curve for needle-like primary Al13Fe4, showing a measured current of 0.20 nA.
summary: Localized TUNA current-voltage measurements for the needle-like primary Al13Fe4 phase demonstrate a current value of 0.20 nA. This significantly lower current confirms that Al13Fe4 possesses inferior electric conduction properties relative to Al3Ni, providing quantitative evidence of the varying conductivity across different secondary phase geometries.

caption: TEM micrograph of balled NiO-5 displaying the structural characteristics of the refined particles.
summary: TEM analysis of the balled NiO-5 sample reveals the structural characteristics of the refined particles. The imaging confirms that the sample consists of particles ranging in size from tens to hundreds of nanometers, demonstrating the effectiveness of the ball milling process in achieving structural refinement.

caption: Comparison of the simulated fraction of β-Si as a function of solid fraction between 3D Cellular Automata (CA) simulations and the Scheil model at cooling rates of 20, 200, and 400 K/s.
summary: This plot evaluates the accuracy of 3D Cellular Automata simulations by comparing the predicted fraction of β-Si against the theoretical Scheil model. Data is presented across three distinct cooling rates—20, 200, and 400 K/s—to demonstrate how solidification kinetics and phase evolution deviate from equilibrium predictions under varying thermal conditions.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM FcMeOH recorded before and after incubation with faecal pellet supernatant from 12-month-old mice, exhibiting a minor decrease in current.
summary: Electrochemical analysis using 1 mM FcMeOH was conducted on faecal pellet supernatant from 12-month-old mice. The resulting cyclic voltammograms showed a slight reduction in signal intensity, consistent with the observations from 3-month-old samples, suggesting relatively low TNFα concentrations in these middle-aged murine faecal samples.

caption: Ni–Se binary phase diagram illustrating the formation mechanism of NiSe2 micro-inclusions, where NiSe2 exists as a solid phase dispersed within the liquid Bi–Se host matrix at the synthesis temperature of 853 °C.
summary: The Ni–Se binary phase diagram illustrates the formation mechanism of NiSe2 micro-inclusions. At the synthesis temperature of 853 °C, NiSe2 exists as a solid phase dispersed within the liquid Bi–Se host matrix. This phase behavior is critical for understanding the in situ formation of NiSe2 within the composite system.

caption: Nyquist plots of Cu-7Ni-3Al-1Fe-1Mn alloy samples after 21 days of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution, showing single capacitive arcs and an equivalent circuit model used for electrochemical interface simulation.
summary: Nyquist plots for Cu-7Ni-3Al-1Fe-1Mn alloys immersed in 3.5% NaCl for 21 days reveal single capacitive arcs across all samples. An equivalent circuit model was utilized to simulate electrochemical interfaces. Sample A2 demonstrates the largest impedance arc radius, indicating superior charge-transfer resistance and enhanced corrosion resistance compared to other deformation levels.

caption: Thermal distribution map of the WAAM sample 3 seconds after arc extinction, showing the temperature profile of the hammer and the 21st deposited layer.
summary: This thermal distribution map displays the temperature profile of the WAAM sample 3 seconds after the 21st layer deposition. The hammer's movement in this configuration inhibits effective convective cooling, resulting in a distinct thermal signature compared to stationary hammer setups, which influences the subsequent cooling rates and final microstructure.

caption: Small-angle scattering image of the bottom section of the coating annealed at 950 °C, showing the evolution of the diffraction pattern.
summary: The bottom part of the coating annealed at 950 °C displays a distinct small-angle scattering pattern. This image captures the structural state of the material at this specific depth, reflecting the influence of high-temperature annealing on the epitaxial nano-lamellae and the overall texture of the coating.

caption: SAED pattern of the triple melted Ti–40Nb sample corresponding to the body-centered cubic (bcc) crystal structure.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction pattern for the triple melted Ti–40Nb sample confirms the presence of a body-centered cubic crystal structure. This result demonstrates that the bcc phase is maintained in the triple melted condition, providing insight into the stability of the crystal lattice under repeated laser melting cycles.

caption: FTIR spectrum of Si-doped BCP treated at 1100 °C, displaying the range of 450-4000 cm⁻¹.
summary: FTIR spectra for Si-doped BCP samples treated at 1100 °C demonstrate that characteristic infrared peaks associated with A-type and B-type carbonates become significantly less pronounced or disappear entirely. This observation indicates the successful decomposition of carbonate groups within the powder following the higher temperature heat treatment process.

caption: SEM morphology and elemental distribution map of the WC coating.
summary: This panel displays the SEM morphology and elemental distribution of the WC coating. Analysis reveals that the constituent elements within the coating are uniformly distributed throughout the structure. Importantly, there is no evidence of element segregation, indicating a homogeneous composition across the observed region of the coating material.

caption: Deformation mode schematic for SRA structures with specific t2 values.
summary: This schematic illustrates the deformation behavior of SRA structures characterized by specific t2 values. The visualization highlights the structural response under load, demonstrating that these SRA configurations exhibit a significant auxetic effect, which is a key mechanical characteristic observed during the deformation process of these specific material architectures.

caption: Linear sweep voltammograms comparing the electrochemical behavior of the investigated steels.
summary: This panel displays linear sweep voltammograms for the studied materials, providing a comparative overview of their electrochemical response. The data serves as a fundamental characterization of the corrosion behavior of the investigated steels under the specified experimental conditions, facilitating the subsequent analysis of their anodic and cathodic reaction kinetics.

caption: Al 2p core level XPS spectra recorded after different sputtering durations to evaluate the aluminum chemical state within the oxide film.
summary: Aluminum 2p core level XPS spectra are provided for the oxide film across various sputtering times. These spectroscopic findings contribute to the overall XPS results, which establish that the products from the two pre-oxidation treatments are different, detailing the aluminum chemical state within the oxide film structure.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectrum acquired from the amorphous solid region identified on the YSZ coating surface.
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectrum acquired from the amorphous solid region identified on the YSZ coating surface is shown. Residual Na2SO4 is detected on the surface by EDS, indicating that the amorphous material corresponds to the molten salt residue resulting from the hot corrosion process on the YSZ coating.

caption: Pole figures for the {001}, {101}, and {111} planes of specimen S5, showing a maximum intensity of 1.821, which suggests a near-random orientation distribution.
summary: Pole figures for the {001}, {101}, and {111} planes of specimen S5 demonstrate minimal texture development. With a maximum intensity of 1.821, the orientation distribution is shown to be nearly random, confirming the lack of significant preferred grain orientation within the specimen's microstructure.

caption: Relationship between tensile dwell time and rupture time for directionally-solidified Ni-based superalloy DZ445 tested at 900 °C under a total strain range of 1.6%.
summary: This line graph illustrates the correlation between tensile dwell time and rupture time for the Ni-based superalloy DZ445 at 900 °C with a 1.6% total strain range. The data clearly demonstrates an increasing trend of rupture time as the dwell time increases, highlighting the material's specific creep-fatigue behavior under these conditions.

caption: Friction coefficient evolution over the number of cycles for Stellite 6, C-GC, and C-LMD alloys at 25 °C.
summary: The friction coefficient for all three alloys is shown as a function of cycle count at 25 °C. Results indicate an equivalent performance across the materials, characterized by a significant increase in the friction coefficient up to 50,000 cycles, followed by a subsequent stabilization or slight increase in values.

caption: EBSD orientation maps and corresponding inverse pole figures (IPF) relative to the build direction (BD) for the S400 scanning speed condition, showing the crystallographic orientation of γR, PAG, and α′ phases.
summary: This panel displays EBSD orientation maps and corresponding IPFs for the S400 scanning speed. The crystallographic investigation reveals a preferred grain orientation along the <100> direction. PAGs and γR grains in the same area exhibit identical orientations, indicating that these grains form from dendrites with the same initial orientation.

caption: Load-deflection response of the F35–1X composite specimen during in-situ three-point flexural testing, highlighting the ultimate load point followed by a gradual load drop attributed to frictional work during fiber fracture and matrix crack propagation.
summary: The load-deflection curve for the F35–1X composite during in-situ three-point flexural testing reveals the mechanical behavior under stress. The plot captures the ultimate load point where fiber fracture initiates, followed by a gradual load drop caused by frictional work as matrix cracks propagate through the bulk of the sample.

caption: Fitted response plot comparing experimental data points, represented by red markers, against the predicted values derived from the regression model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the performance of the regression model by comparing experimental data, as listed in Table 2, against the model's fitted response. The red markers indicate the alignment between observed experimental results and the predicted values, providing a visual assessment of the model's accuracy and predictive capability.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of the as-built specimen showing γ' phase precipitates with sizes ranging from 100 to 200 nm.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph, captured using the <100> superlattice reflection, reveals the distribution of γ' phase precipitates within the as-built specimen. The image demonstrates that these precipitates exhibit a particle size distribution between 100 and 200 nm, confirming the presence of the γ' phase within the grains of the material.

caption: Experimental Co–Al phase diagram compared with a calculated version incorporating both configurational and vibrational entropic contributions.
summary: This panel displays the experimental Co–Al phase diagram alongside a calculated version that accounts for configurational and vibrational entropy. The comparison highlights the influence of vibrational entropy on phase stability. Reference sentences confirm that this plot represents the whole phase diagram and indicates that vibrational entropy effects are significant.

caption: Three-dimensional atom map of the M1 sample matrix showing the grain boundary (GB) region and the plate-like morphology of the F phase.
summary: The 3D atom map of the M1 sample matrix reveals the grain boundary structure obtained via atom probe tomography. The F phase exhibits a plate-like morphology that deflects the grain boundary path, consistent with SEM observations. This zig-zag morphology of F-phase-decorated grain boundaries serves as a favorable site for cracking.

caption: Modified Thompson tetrahedron representation adapted for the gamma phase to describe dislocation movement and interaction behaviors within the non-equivalence structure.
summary: Dislocation movement and interaction behavior within the non-equivalence structure of the gamma phase are described using this modified Thompson tetrahedron. Originally developed for FCC structures, this geometric model is applied here to analyze the complex dislocation dynamics and interactions occurring within the TiAl-4822 alloy microstructure.

caption: Maximum force required to compress bulk material to a 10 mm target layer height, plotted for 48 parameter combinations ordered by water content.
summary: This plot illustrates the maximum applied force required for compressing each of the four layers of the test specimens. Data indicate that increasing the water content leads to a reduction in the required compression force and decreases the scattering of values, while force values generally increase with higher compression ratios.

caption: Pareto chart quantifying the standardized effects of 3D printing parameters on the plateau stress of bone scaffolds.
summary: Quantifying the standardized effects of 3D printing parameters on plateau stress, this Pareto chart illustrates the significance and correlation of these variables. The visualization helps determine which printing parameters are most influential in defining the plateau stress characteristics of the bone scaffolds during mechanical testing and structural evaluation.

caption: Dilatometric curve and its first derivative for the Base alloy with an initial ferritic microstructure, showing the relative change in length (RCL) during continuous heating.
summary: This dilatometric curve for the Base alloy with an initial ferritic microstructure illustrates the continuous increase in relative change in length during austenite formation. The vertical dashed lines denote the start and finish temperatures, determined by slope changes in the first derivative, reflecting the atomic volume increase during the ferrite-to-austenite transformation.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for nanoscale nickel electrodeposited at 2.0 A/dm² for 4 hours.
summary: Depicting the grain size distribution for nickel electrodeposited at 2.0 A/dm² for 4 hours, this plot allows for the assessment of deposition time effects. Results indicate that increasing the electrodeposition time results in a relatively small range of variation in the grain size compared to current density changes.

caption: TDA desorption rate spectrum for CoCrFeMnNi-HEA charged at 200 bar.
summary: Presented is the TDA spectrum for the CoCrFeMnNi-HEA alloy following hydrogen charging at 200 bar. The resulting ion current shows a decreased desorption rate relative to the 1000 bar charging pressure. This curve contributes to the overall assessment of material-specific hydrogen absorption and release characteristics in the high-entropy alloy.

caption: High-resolution HAADF-STEM image demonstrating high coherence at the interface between phase 3 and phase 4, with a measured misorientation of less than 2°.
summary: This high-resolution HAADF-STEM image provides evidence of high coherence at the interphase boundaries between phase 3 and phase 4. The structural analysis confirms a low misorientation angle of less than 2°, indicating a highly ordered interface between these two specific phases within the MPES microstructure.

caption: Atomic model illustrating single Re and Mo solute atoms substituting sites within the local atomic environment (LAE) of a Ni lattice, highlighted in orange.
summary: This panel displays an atomic model showing single Re and Mo atoms substituting seven inequivalent sites within the local atomic environment of a Ni lattice. DFT calculations indicate that these specific substitutions enhance Ni self-diffusion barriers, with the tuned barrier values varying by approximately 20% compared to the pure Ni system.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the temperature dependence of interdiffusion coefficients for various nickel-based alloys, including pure austenitic binary Ni-Cr alloys represented by filled symbols.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the interdiffusion coefficients of nickel-based alloys as a function of temperature. Filled symbols denote data for pure austenitic binary Ni-Cr alloys, while a dashed line represents a fit with a pre-exponential factor of 0.1 cm2 s-1 and an activation energy of 240 kJ mol-1, incorporating comparative data from literature.

caption: Experimental creep curve (thin red line) plotted with the predicted counterpart (thick dashed red line) at 950 °C and 300 MPa.
summary: The creep curve measured at 950 °C and 300 MPa is shown as a thin red line, with the predicted curve overlaid as a thick dashed red line. This comparison highlights the quantitative fit of the model, with the reference noting that the predicted strain for this condition is quite accurate.

caption: Open porosity and bulk density measurements of scaffolds with varying WF content.
summary: Quantitative analysis of scaffold physical properties reveals that increasing WF content leads to a significant rise in open porosity from 37.8% to 49.2%. Concurrently, the bulk density decreases from 2.8 to 2.3, demonstrating the inverse relationship between these structural parameters as the composition of the scaffold is modified.

caption: EBSD characterization of the interlayer region in the middle of the multilayer specimen processed under a magnetic field with an orientation angle of θ = 30°.
summary: EBSD characterization was performed on the interlayer region of the middle of the multilayer deposited specimen. This panel demonstrates the microstructural characteristics observed when the external magnetic field is applied at an orientation angle of θ = 30°, allowing for an assessment of how this field angle modifies the interlayer microstructure.

caption: Calcium deposition levels, quantified via ARS absorbance, for hADSCs on PCL, G, and GO scaffolds at 14 and 21 days of osteogenic differentiation.
summary: Calcium deposition, measured by ARS absorbance, is shown for hADSCs on PCL, G, and GO scaffolds at 14 and 21 days. The data demonstrates an increasing trend in calcium deposition over time, confirming that all scaffold types are capable of supporting the osteogenic differentiation process of the seeded hADSCs.

caption: Compressive yield strength represented as a function of relative density within an Ashby diagram.
summary: Displaying compressive yield strength versus relative density, this Ashby diagram serves as a summary of the material's mechanical behavior. Utilizing the established Ashby framework, the plot effectively maps the yield strength characteristics, allowing for a comparative analysis of mechanical performance relative to the material's density.

caption: Methodological flowchart illustrating the systematic workflow and procedural steps involved in the research study.
summary: This schematic diagram presents a comprehensive methodology flowchart, outlining the sequential steps and logical progression of the research process. It serves as a visual guide to the experimental or analytical framework employed, ensuring clarity regarding the systematic approach taken to achieve the study's objectives and overall scientific workflow.

caption: Dilatometry curves displaying relative length change (dL) as a function of temperature for specimens austenized at 1040 °C for 3 minutes and cooled at 10 °C/s.
summary: Dilatometry measurements illustrate the longitudinal expansion behavior of specimens austenized at 1040 °C and cooled at 10 °C/s. These curves are used to determine the martensite start (Ms) temperature, with the 17–4 PH alloy exhibiting a phase transformation from FCC to BCC at approximately 132 °C.

caption: Comparison of long crack fatigue thresholds (ΔKth,LC) across varying load ratios, benchmarking the experimental results against established literature values for metallic alloys.
summary: This plot illustrates the fatigue crack growth threshold ΔKth,LC for the material across different load ratios. By benchmarking these values against existing literature, the figure provides a comprehensive assessment of the fatigue crack growth resistance of the AM Al2618 + TiB2 composite compared to standard alloy data.

caption: Atomic force microscopy image of the Ti–6Al–4V alloy surface at 900 °C, revealing the formation of ridges up to 700 nm high resulting from the orogenesis of coarsening α lamellae.
summary: Atomic force microscopy analysis of the Ti–6Al–4V alloy surface at 900 °C reveals the formation of ridges reaching up to 700 nm in height. This surface topography is attributed to the orogenesis of coarsening α lamellae, which occurs to accommodate the intensified stress during the heating process.

caption: Lattice strain evolution in the loading direction (LD) and transverse direction (RD) as a function of elevated applied stress.
summary: Lattice strain evolutions in both the loading direction and the transverse direction are plotted against elevated applied stress. These measurements, derived from neutron diffraction, allow for the evaluation of elastic constants for specific crystallographic planes, including <111>, <200>, <220>, and <311>, under various loading conditions at 700 °C.

caption: Reflection phase response of Cell 2 across the 79 to 90 GHz frequency range while Cell 1 remains constant.
summary: Represented is the reflection phase for Cell 2 within the 79-90 GHz frequency band. The data confirms that the phase response is contrary to that of Cell 1, validating the dual-band reflect array design's ability to manipulate phase independently across different frequency regimes for the respective meta-atom cells.

caption: Maximum-intensity projection of the z-stack showing the cubical epithelial cells at the front and spindle-like HGFs at the back of the OMC membrane.
summary: A maximum-intensity projection of the z-stack provides a comprehensive view of the OMC membrane, highlighting the distinct morphologies of the two cell populations. Cubical epithelial cells are visible at the front, while spindle-like HGFs are located at the back, demonstrating the successful spatial organization of the oral mucosa components.

caption: Optimisation framework architecture utilizing a genetic algorithm integrated with a neural network (NN-3) to identify quasi-global optima for scaffold design schemes.
summary: This panel illustrates the optimisation framework designed for scaffold development. It employs a combination of a genetic algorithm and a neural network, specifically NN-3, to search for quasi-global optima across various optimisation schemes. This systematic approach ensures efficient evaluation of objective and constraint functions within the scaffold design process.

caption: Electrode potential profiles recorded during a constant current experiment conducted at a current density of 4 mA cm-2.
summary: Electrode potentials of a typical Li-NRR experiment are shown in this panel. The data represents the potential response of the cell during a constant current experiment performed at 4 mA cm-2. This measurement provides insight into the electrochemical stability and behavior of the electrode system under the specified operating conditions.

caption: Cumulative (Q3) and differential (q3) particle size distribution curves for IN718 powder, determined via optical image analysis.
summary: The particle size distribution of IN718 powder is presented through cumulative (Q3) and differential (q3) curves. These measurements were obtained using optical image analysis in accordance with the ISO13322–2 standard, utilizing a Camsizer X2 particle analyzer to characterize the powder morphology and size characteristics effectively.

caption: Adjusted Bode phase angle plot for Q345 rolled steel, showing shifts toward lower degrees at frequencies between 10^3 and 10^2 Hz as exposure time increases.
summary: Adjusted Bode phase data for Q345 rolled steel reveals significant trends after discarding solution resistance. As exposure time increases, the phase angle shifts toward lower degrees in the 10^3 to 10^2 Hz frequency range, indicating the gradual formation of surface defects during the corrosion process.

caption: Friction coefficient versus time curve for the C1 textured TC4 sample under dry sliding conditions.
summary: The friction coefficient evolution for the C1 textured sample is illustrated under dry sliding conditions. This plot contributes to the comparative analysis of different energy density textures, showing how the specific surface modification of the C1 texture influences the friction behavior compared to other textured and base samples.

caption: Gaussian Process Regression model for Young’s modulus of 3D printed cellular structures, plotting experimental data as black crosses against blue predictive lines with shaded confidence intervals as a function of relative density.
summary: Gaussian Process Regression models the Young’s modulus of 3D printed cellular structures relative to density. Experimental data points are compared against blue predictive lines, with shaded confidence intervals illustrating the model's robustness. This approach extends predictive capabilities beyond measured regions, allowing for accurate forecasting of mechanical properties for untested densities.

caption: Schematic illustration of the crack propagation obstruction effect, demonstrating the transition of the failure model from intergranular to intragranular fracture in the Al-Cu-Ni alloy.
summary: This schematic illustrates the crack propagation obstruction effect within the Al-Cu-Ni alloy microstructure. It highlights the mechanism by which the failure model transforms from intergranular to intragranular fracture. This transition is a critical component of the alloy's fracture performance, as the microstructure features actively impede crack growth during mechanical loading.

caption: Thermal degradation behavior of DMA45-P denture base resin represented by weight loss percentage versus aging status.
summary: Thermal degradation behavior of DMA45-P denture base resin is represented by weight loss percentage across different aging statuses, including no aging, TC, TBA, HCl, and NaOCl. TGA analysis confirms that weight loss occurs in this material, highlighting the thermal response of the resin following exposure to these aging media.

caption: Nyquist plot for the S7-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion in the electrolyte.
summary: This panel presents the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy results for the S7-6D specimen after 6 days of immersion. Part of the S7-6D to S9-6D group, this data supports the evaluation of corrosion resistance for SLMed TC4 alloys, contributing to the overall assessment of material performance over medium-term immersion.

caption: Statistical microhardness profile of NiV7 alloy following 96.6% cold-rolling reduction.
summary: This panel shows the microhardness distribution for the NiV7 alloy at the maximum reduction of 96.6%. The statistical data provides insight into the material's mechanical properties at this extreme deformation level, completing the comparative analysis of hardness values across the different cold-rolling reductions investigated.

caption: Comparative FTIR absorption spectra of oxygen vacancy-rich red-ZrO2 powder and conventional vacancy-free white-ZrO2 powder.
summary: This panel presents a comparative FTIR analysis of red-ZrO2 powder, which is rich in oxygen vacancies, against conventional white-ZrO2 powder. The spectra are utilized to probe the formation of the Zr(OBu)4-acac complex and characterize the nature of the acac-Zr chemical bonds within the synthesized material.

caption: Intermediate stage of grain growth showing newly formed grains and orientations over the substrate, with unassigned regions in black.
summary: Representing an intermediate snapshot of the microstructural evolution, this panel displays the newly created grains and their orientations. The colored domains indicate individual grains, while black areas represent regions where no new grains have been assigned, illustrating the progression of the solidification front across the substrate.

caption: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 noHT (black) and A1 HT2 (red) samples measured at 123 K, with green asterisks indicating peaks associated with the Fm-3m austenitic phase.
summary: Powder neutron diffractograms for A1 noHT and A1 HT2 samples were measured at 123 K. The comparison between the black (noHT) and red (HT2) traces highlights structural differences, with green asterisks specifically marking the peaks corresponding to the Fm-3m austenitic phase present in the analyzed materials.

caption: Optical transmission measurements taken at five distinct locations (A through E) across a U-shaped nanocomposite sample to assess Au nanoparticle distribution.
summary: Optical transmission measurements were utilized to assess the spatial distribution of Au nanoparticles within the hydrogel samples. By determining the transmission at different sites, denoted as A through E across a U-shaped sample, the uniformity of the nanoparticle dispersion throughout the material was effectively characterized and evaluated.

caption: Extended dislocation nodes containing stacking faults in single-crystal CrCoNi alloy, exhibiting non-equilibrium features such as asymmetric node sizes and abrupt cusps on partial dislocation lines.
summary: Extended dislocation nodes in single-crystal CrCoNi alloy are observed via TEM. These features display non-equilibrium characteristics, including significant asymmetry and abrupt cusps along partial dislocation lines. Attempts to quantify the stacking fault energy from these nodes suggest a minimum cutoff value of 27 mJ m-2, despite inherent structural irregularities.

caption: Calculated binary Ti-N phase diagram showing the equilibrium relationship between titanium and nitrogen, including the high solid solubility of nitrogen in alpha-Ti and a maximum nitrogen solubility of approximately 30 at% in liquid titanium.
summary: The binary Ti-N phase diagram, calculated using Thermo-Calc software and the TCHEA3 database, illustrates the thermodynamic equilibrium of the system. It highlights that nitrogen exhibits high solid solubility in alpha-Ti, contributing to interstitial hardening, and reaches a maximum solubility of approximately 30 at% within the liquid titanium phase.

caption: Battery temperature profile over four cycles without BCP, showing a peak temperature of 48 °C at the end of discharge followed by cooling during CC-CV charging.
summary: This plot illustrates the battery temperature variation during four discharge-charge cycles at a 2.9C discharge rate without BCP. The temperature reaches 48 °C at the end of the discharge process and gradually decreases to ambient conditions during the subsequent CC-CV charging phase, providing a baseline for thermal performance.

caption: Compressive stress-strain curves for Schwarz P structures with relative densities of 0.28, 0.32, and 0.43.
summary: Compressive stress-strain curves for Schwarz P TPMS structures are shown for relative densities of 0.28, 0.32, and 0.43. The plot illustrates the mechanical response of the Schwarz P topology, highlighting the relationship between relative density and the resulting stress-strain behavior under compressive loading conditions.

caption: Load–displacement curves for relative density graded Nylon lattices showing multiple force peaks.
summary: This panel displays the load–displacement behavior of relative density graded Nylon lattices. The curves exhibit multiple peaks in force profiles, which indicate specific failure mechanisms that contribute to the overall crashworthiness of the structure. The moderately graded configuration is highlighted as reaching the highest load values among the tested Nylon specimens.

caption: Refractive index values of SL samples as a function of AlInN fraction, ranging from 0 (bulk GaN) to 1 (bulk AlInN), measured via spectroscopic ellipsometry at 401, 501, and 601 nm.
summary: Spectroscopic ellipsometry data illustrates the refractive index of SL samples across varying AlInN fractions from 0 to 1. Measurements were performed at specific wavelengths of 401, 501, and 601 nm. The resulting plot demonstrates the dependence of the refractive index on the AlInN composition within the studied material system.

caption: Surface roughness profile of sample 1 before laser shock peening (LSP) treatment, with long-wavelength form and waviness components filtered out.
summary: This panel displays the surface roughness of sample 1 prior to laser shock peening. By applying wave analysis to filter out long-frequency form and waviness, the underlying surface topography is revealed, providing a baseline for assessing the structural changes induced by the subsequent laser shock peening process.

caption: EBSD-based phase identification map highlighting the distribution of Ni3Nb, Cr2Nb, and Fe2Nb intermetallic compounds within the fine-grained regions at the interface.
summary: This EBSD phase map identifies the fine-grained regions as primarily Ni3Nb, with minor Cr2Nb and Fe2Nb phases. These findings suggest that Fe and Cr elements from the GH4169 alloy interact with Nb521 during welding, leading to intermetallic formation that contributes to increased microhardness at the interface.

caption: Conceptual illustration of heat convection patterns occurring within the molten pool during laser processing.
summary: This schematic illustrates the heat convection dynamics within the melt pool during laser processing. It serves as the foundational mechanism for understanding how thermal gradients are established, which subsequently influence the development of internal stresses and the initiation of crack formation within the material during the manufacturing process.

caption: GD-OES depth profile of A625 alloy after transpassive polarization at 1100 mV vs Ag/AgCl, displaying significant increases in Mo and Nb content alongside a reduction in Cr concentration below base material levels.
summary: At an increased anodic potential of 1100 mV, the A625 oxide film undergoes significant characteristic changes. The GD-OES profile shows that Mo and Nb contents increase substantially within the film, while the Cr content decreases to levels below that of the base material, indicating a shift in film composition.

caption: Quantitative analysis of rBMSC viability on scaffolds, showing percentages exceeding 95% at day 1 and day 3.
summary: Quantitative analysis of the fluorescence images confirms high cell viability, with values consistently exceeding 95% for all groups at both day 1 and day 3. Statistical evaluation indicates no significant difference between these time points, demonstrating that the scaffolds support robust cell survival throughout the observed culture period.

caption: SHAP dependence plot for curing age (CA) demonstrating the effect of time on compressive strength development.
summary: The SHAP dependence plot for curing age illustrates the influence of time on the compressive strength of 3DPFRC. Results indicate that a curing age of 28 days significantly enhances the compressive strength compared to shorter curing durations, highlighting the importance of age in the material's strength development.

caption: Reflection coefficients of the spherical FESA plotted against frequency for varying relative dielectric constants (εr).
summary: This plot illustrates the reflection coefficients of a spherical FESA as a function of frequency under varying relative dielectric constants. Increasing the dielectric constant causes the resonance frequency to shift toward lower frequencies, with the data indicating a maximum frequency deviation of approximately 5 MHz across the tested range.

caption: STEM-EDS elemental mapping of the HIP and homogenized sample showing the redistribution of alloying elements.
summary: STEM-EDS analysis of the homogenized sample confirms the successful solutionization of magnesium and zinc. The mapping shows that the elements previously concentrated in large intergranular MgZn2 precipitates have been redistributed back into the matrix, reflecting the chemical homogenization achieved through the post-HIP heat treatment process.

caption: Linear fitting of true stress–strain curves derived from the Hollomon equation to determine plastic deformation parameters.
summary: Linear fitting of true stress–strain curves is performed based on the Hollomon equation to characterize material behavior. The slope of the curve during the plastic deformation stage is utilized to extract specific mechanical values, providing insight into the strain-hardening characteristics of the H13 steel under investigation.

caption: Flexural strength plotted against elastic modulus for various DIW-printed samples compared to trabecular bone regions.
summary: Flexural strength versus elastic modulus data shows that most samples fall within the range of trabecular bone. D-DIW samples are identified as exceptionally strong and stiff, potentially leading to stress shielding. The plot confirms that mechanical properties can be systematically varied by adjusting print nozzle diameter and filament spacing parameters.

caption: Comparison of creep rupture prediction accuracy for CMSX-4 at 950 °C, demonstrating the lack of significant improvement in the model.
summary: Panel b illustrates the results of an attempt to improve the creep rupture prediction model for CMSX-4 at 950 °C. According to the study, this specific approach did not yield any significant improvement in the accuracy of the rupture time predictions compared to the baseline LMP method shown in panel a.

caption: DSC/TG thermal response of the LSM filament after partial debinding in coke grit, showing a carbon removal peak between 350 °C and 450 °C.
summary: Following partial debinding in coke grit, the LSM filament exhibits a distinct DSC signal characterized by a sharp carbon removal peak. This peak occurs within a temperature range of 350 °C to 450 °C, reflecting the thermal decomposition and mass loss behavior specific to this pre-debinding procedure.

caption: Spatial heatmap visualizing the relative error between input and measured pixel grayscale values for the uncompensated image input.
summary: This spatial heatmap maps the relative error across the projection area for the uncompensated input. It highlights the non-uniformity of the projected light, providing a visual representation of how aberrations affect the intensity accuracy across different regions of the pattern before the implementation of corrective compensation measures.

caption: Chemical structures of the mesogen RM257, chain extender EDDET, and BDB used for LCE ink synthesis.
summary: This panel displays the chemical structures of the primary components used to synthesize the LCE ink. The mesogen RM257, chain extender EDDET, and BDB are combined via a thiol-acrylate Michael addition reaction, catalyzed by dipropylamine, to form the liquid crystal oligomers necessary for the printing process.

caption: High-resolution Ni 2p XPS spectrum for reduced samples, with a peak at approximately 707 eV attributed to metallic iron (Fe 0).
summary: This Ni 2p XPS spectrum for the reduced samples includes a peak at a binding energy of approximately 707 eV. This feature is attributed to metallic iron (Fe 0), confirming the formation of bimetallic Fe-Ni alloys and providing evidence of the surface chemistry of the reduced catalysts.

caption: Raman spectrum acquired from the wear track of the Inconel 718 superalloy.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was utilized to characterize the oxide species formed at the interface of the Inconel 718 sample. The spectrum collected from the wear track serves to identify the nature of the oxides developed during the testing, contributing to a broader understanding of the interface chemistry.

caption: Quasi-binary phase diagram of AlSi9Cu3 alloy illustrating phase stability as a function of varying copper compositions.
summary: This quasi-binary phase diagram displays the phase stability of the AlSi9Cu3 alloy system. By varying the copper composition, the plot maps the equilibrium phase boundaries, providing a comprehensive overview of the material's thermodynamic behavior and phase transitions across different chemical concentrations relevant to the alloy's solidification characteristics.

caption: Ridge Regression (RR) testing response evaluating the model's predictive performance on the testing dataset.
summary: Ridge Regression (RR) testing response is presented to evaluate the model's predictive performance on the testing dataset. This parity plot serves as a diagnostic tool to visualize the accuracy of the Ridge Regression model when predicting experimental values, highlighting its effectiveness on data not used during training.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profiles of specific oxide anions including 18O-, Cr2-, Ni2-, OH-, and O2- measured from the inner extreme surface of alloy 690 steam generator tubes after transient corrosion testing up to 170°C.
summary: This panel displays ToF-SIMS depth profiles for various oxide anions, specifically 18O-, Cr2-, Ni2-, OH-, and O2-, within the inner surface of alloy 690 steam generator tubes. These measurements were taken following transient corrosion testing in the BOREAL loop up to 170°C, providing insight into the surface oxide composition.

caption: Pearson correlation analysis illustrating the relationship between process parameters and the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of samples processed via pulsed-wave (PW) laser.
summary: This panel presents a Pearson correlation analysis focused on the ultimate tensile strength of samples subjected to pulsed-wave laser processing. By evaluating the statistical correlations between various process parameters and the resulting UTS, the analysis identifies key factors influencing the mechanical performance of the laser-processed materials.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of the Al5Si5–800 alloy after tensile fracture, highlighting the morphology of the B2 phase precipitates.
summary: This dark-field TEM image displays the B2 phase precipitates within the Al5Si5–800 alloy following tensile fracture. The observation reveals that the precipitation phase morphology includes both spherical and rod-like shapes, which deviate from the expected homogeneous spherical distribution typically found in such alloy systems after processing.

caption: Three-dimensional CAD representation of the third auxetic unit cell design.
summary: This panel illustrates a three-dimensional CAD model of the third auxetic unit cell. It is designed with the same global dimensions as the other four unit cells in the set, measuring 5 mm in length and height and 3 mm in width, which are essential for the study's characterization.

caption: Thermogravimetric (TG) analysis curve illustrating the mass loss profile of pectin hydrogels as a function of temperature.
summary: The TG curve displays the thermal degradation behavior of pectin hydrogels. Analysis of this curve, alongside the DTG data, reveals that all tested hydrogel samples undergo three distinct stages of mass loss during the heating process, providing a comprehensive overview of their thermal stability and decomposition characteristics.

caption: Comparative analysis of Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) and elongation values for the current study against established literature data.
summary: This scatter plot provides a comparative analysis of Ultimate Tensile Strength and elongation values for the current study against established literature data. By benchmarking these results alongside various previous studies, the figure contextualizes the mechanical performance of the as-built and HIP-treated samples within the broader field of materials research.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing rPLA pellets coated with polydopamine (rPLA-PDA) and rPLA-PDA reinforced with kenaf fibers.
summary: This figure displays the FTIR spectra of rPLA-based composites, specifically comparing rPLA pellets coated with polydopamine against those reinforced with kenaf fibers. The spectral data provides chemical characterization of the dopamine coating on the rPLA-based composite materials, highlighting the structural differences between the two distinct composite formulations presented in the study.

caption: Mott-Schottky plots displaying the inverse square of capacitance versus potential for LPBF-consolidated NAB alloys in as-built and two distinct annealed conditions.
summary: Mott-Schottky plots for LPBF-consolidated NAB alloys illustrate the relationship between space-charge capacitance and potential across three sample conditions. These curves reveal both positive and negative slopes, indicating complex semiconducting behavior. The donor and acceptor densities, labeled N1, N2, and N3, are derived from these specific regions of the plots.

caption: Phalloidin staining of MSCs revealing a heterogeneous size distribution and irregular morphology.
summary: Phalloidin staining of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) highlights their distinct structural features. In contrast to EPCs, these cells exhibit a heterogeneous size distribution and irregular morphology, characterized by larger cytoskeletal structures and a more loosely organized cellular arrangement within the culture environment.

caption: Overview of the QX800-II spinning machine used for the experimental procedure.
summary: The QX800-II spinning machine is presented as the primary apparatus for the experimental setup. This equipment is utilized to perform the spinning process, serving as the central experimental platform for the study. The image provides a clear visual representation of the machine configuration used throughout the conducted experiments.

caption: FTIR spectra of scaffolds after 28 days of immersion in PBS, highlighting changes in molecular composition due to degradation.
summary: FTIR spectroscopy was employed to investigate structural alterations during the degradation of the scaffolds. The spectra capture distinctive changes in molecular composition after 28 days of immersion in PBS, complementing the findings from the FE-SEM analysis and degradation kinetics, thereby elucidating the chemical evolution of the degrading polymer matrix.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetization measured at a low applied magnetic field of 100 Oe for milled samples.
summary: This M-T curve illustrates the temperature-dependent magnetization of milled samples under a 100 Oe field. A distinct magnetization jump, indicating a ferro-paramagnetic transition, is observed near 360 K for most samples. Notably, this transition is absent in the sample subjected to 90 minutes of milling, highlighting microstructural influence on magnetic behavior.

caption: Calculated spin-wave frequencies for Co dots embedded in a Py matrix at the FBZ centre (k = 0) as a function of external magnetic field, with line colours representing the in-Co concentration factor.
summary: This plot displays the ten lowest spin-wave modes for Co dots in a Py matrix, calculated at the FBZ centre. As the external magnetic field decreases from 300 to 50 mT, the frequencies exhibit nonlinear softening. Line colours indicate the specific in-Co concentration factor, illustrating the magnetic response of the system.

caption: Laser confocal micrograph of the as-cast 2Zr alloy microstructure, etched with Keller’s Reagent, illustrating the equiaxed α-Al matrix.
summary: This laser confocal micrograph captures the as-cast microstructure of the 2Zr alloy after etching with Keller’s Reagent. The image clearly illustrates the equiaxed α-Al matrix, providing high-resolution confirmation of the microstructural morphology. These findings are consistent with the broader observations of the as-cast samples within the experimental study.

caption: Shrinkage and shrinkage rate curves for WC-Co alloys, illustrating the densification behavior as influenced by carbon content.
summary: This panel displays shrinkage and shrinkage rate curves for WC-Co alloys. The data highlights how carbon content significantly influences the densification behavior of these alloys during sintering. These dilatometric measurements provide critical insights into the material's structural evolution and densification kinetics under controlled thermal conditions.

caption: Chondrite-normalized rare earth element (REE) patterns for various Hongge ore types, including GH oxide, OPH oxide, and massive oxide ores.
summary: This plot displays chondrite-normalized REE patterns for Hongge ore types. GH oxide ores exhibit higher total REE contents (302 ppm) compared to OPH and massive oxide ores, attributed to varying apatite and silicate mineral abundances. Despite these differences in total concentration, all oxide ore types maintain similar normalized REE distribution patterns.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the classification accuracy and error distribution for the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model.
summary: This confusion matrix provides a detailed breakdown of the Support Vector Machine model's predictive accuracy. It illustrates the various instances in which the classifier is confused when making predictions, allowing for a clear assessment of how the SVM model performs across different classes compared to the other tested algorithms.

caption: Graphical representation of the Kissinger method applied to thick samples, plotting ln(Φ/Tmax^2) versus 1000/Tmax to extract hydrogen diffusion activation energy.
summary: This plot illustrates the application of Kissinger's approach to thick samples by relating ln(Φ/Tmax^2) to 1000/Tmax. The resulting linear relationship is used to derive the hydrogen diffusion activation energy, offering critical insights into the energetic barriers associated with hydrogen migration in the studied thick material samples.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map showing Fe segregation at the middle region of the PSI + T5 processed titanium alloy.
summary: This EDS map illustrates the iron distribution at the middle of the PSI + T5 processed titanium alloy. The analysis confirms that the Ti3662 alloy achieves a uniform iron distribution across this specific location, highlighting the effectiveness of the homogenization process in maintaining chemical homogeneity within the material structure.

caption: Transverse relaxation time (T2) distribution curves for fresh, dried, and fried samples, showing distinct peaks corresponding to different water and oil environments.
summary: Panel B illustrates the T2 distribution curves for the same samples. Protons in different chemical environments exhibit varying transverse relaxation times, resulting in distinct peaks that correspond to specific water environments. The T2 spectra allow for the clear differentiation of proton signals between water and oil within the samples.

caption: Cathodoluminescence spectra of Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ single-doped ZrO₂ microarchitectures after 750°C thermal treatment, displaying stable defect-related emission profiles.
summary: Cathodoluminescence spectra for ZrO₂ microarchitectures subjected to a 750°C thermal cycle demonstrate that defect-related emissions remain similar to those observed in the initial 600°C cycle. The analysis includes Yb³⁺ and Er³⁺ dopants at 2.5 mol% and 0.35 mol%, showing consistent luminescence characteristics despite the increase in the annealing temperature.

caption: Dependency graph illustrating the logical inter-dependencies and structural connections between the decomposed hexagonal mesh chunks.
summary: The dependency graph provides a systematic overview of the inter-dependencies between the hexagonal mesh chunks shown in panel (a). By mapping these connections, the diagram clarifies the sequence and structural requirements necessary for the printing process, ensuring that all dependencies are accounted for during the fabrication workflow.

caption: Ac magnetic susceptibility curves for NiMn0.82Cr0.18Ge at various pressures, featuring an inset that highlights the transition between helicoidal antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic ordering.
summary: The plot shows the temperature-dependent ac magnetic susceptibility for NiMn0.82Cr0.18Ge under hydrostatic pressure. The inset specifically details the magnetic order-order phase transition from helicoidal antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic states. Additionally, at pressures of 1 kbar or higher, a first-order magnetic order-disorder transition is observed with associated thermal hysteresis.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph of Ti−13.5Mo+5Sn revealing the distribution of ω phase particles.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph displays the ω phase within the Ti−13.5Mo+5Sn alloy. Analysis indicates that the addition of 5.0 wt% Sn to the base alloy significantly reduces the ω particle size, resulting in a mean Feret’s diameter of 2.9 nm, which remains well below the critical size range.

caption: Calibration curve for Na+ in human saliva (9.0 mM–100.0 mM) using the 3D-printed Na+ ISE, with green data points indicating spiked Na+ concentrations in fresh saliva samples.
summary: The 3D-printed Na+ ISE calibration curve in human saliva demonstrates a Nernstian response of 59.1 mV/decade. Spiked Na+ concentrations, represented by green data points, confirm the sensor's accuracy and linearity within the 9.0 mM to 100.0 mM range, validating its potential for practical, point-of-care physiological sodium monitoring applications.

caption: High-resolution HAADF-STEM image focusing on a specific α-β-α interface region.
summary: Detailed HAADF-STEM imaging reveals the atomic-scale arrangement at the α-β-α interface. This panel provides a focused view of the boundary between the alpha and beta phases, serving as the basis for further chemical and crystallographic characterization of the interface structure within the 1050 RQ condition.

caption: Confocal microscopy images of MC3T3-E1 cells at days 1 and 3, and hASCs at day 10 on collagen and CDP-7 scaffolds, showing green viable and red dead cells.
summary: Confocal microscopy of MC3T3-E1 cells at days 1 and 3 reveals high initial viability across all scaffolds with minimal cell death. At day 10, hASCs cultured on CDP-7 scaffolds exhibit denser, predominantly viable cell coverage compared to collagen, confirming sustained cytocompatibility and enhanced cell presence on the DDM-p-reinforced scaffold.

caption: Bi-directional scanning vectors X1 and X2 represented within the horizontal build plane (HD-SD).
summary: This schematic illustrates the bi-directional scanning strategy employed during selective laser melting. Vectors X1 and X2 are defined within the horizontal build plane, serving as the foundational parameters for determining the subsequent heat flow directions and the resulting dendritic growth patterns observed in the processed material.

caption: {001} and {111} pole figures illustrating the crystallographic texture of the large grain identified as domain 1 in the orientation map.
summary: These pole figures characterize the crystallographic texture of the large grain labeled as domain 1 in the orientation map. By presenting the {001} and {111} orientations, the figure provides a detailed representation of the grain's specific texture, which is essential for understanding the structural modifications induced by the HCPEB treatment.

caption: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity of hcp-Fe-1.8Si alloy at 106(3) GPa up to 2690(67) K, compared against previous experimental results for hcp-Fe at similar pressures.
summary: Resistivity measurements for hcp-Fe-1.8Si alloy at 106(3) GPa are shown up to 2690(67) K. The data follows a quasi-linear trend consistent with the Bloch-Grüneisen formula. Comparisons are provided with previous experimental results for hcp-Fe at 105 GPa and 106 GPa, illustrating the pressure-dependent behavior of the alloy's electrical properties.

caption: Pole figure of the {001} crystal plane for the AH-1100–60 specimen.
summary: For the AH-1100–60 specimen, the pole figure shows that the pole clusters along the BD direction move downward as the temperature reaches 1100 ℃. The maximum pole figure value is reduced to less than 10 MRD, indicating a modification of the texture compared to samples processed at lower temperatures.
