caption: Spin-wave spectrum showing the ten lowest-frequency modes for permalloy dots embedded within a cobalt matrix, calculated along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone.
summary: This panel presents the spin-wave spectrum for permalloy inclusions in a cobalt matrix, focusing on the ten lowest-frequency modes along high-symmetry paths in the first Brillouin zone. The line colors indicate the in-cobalt concentration factor, allowing for a comparative analysis of magnetic excitation modes between the two distinct matrix-inclusion material systems.

caption: Creep rupture life measurements for three heat-treated alloys evaluated at 982 °C/248 MPa and 1040 °C/145 MPa.
summary: This panel displays the creep rupture life of three heat-treated alloys under specific temperature and stress conditions. Results indicate that increasing the Mo:W ratio slightly reduces rupture life at 982 °C/248 MPa, while conversely improving performance at 1040 °C/145 MPa, demonstrating the sensitivity of creep life to alloy composition.

caption: Fracture energy of the weakest planes (Γ0) plotted against varying raster angles for 18 CT and 18 CTS samples subjected to a 15° loading angle, with the red dashed line denoting the mean and the gray shaded region representing the standard deviation.
summary: This plot illustrates the critical fracture energy of CT and CTS samples as a function of raster angle. By testing 36 total specimens at a 15° loading angle, the data reveals the average fracture energy and associated standard deviation, providing a quantitative assessment of the material's weakest plane performance under mechanical loading.

caption: Arrhenius plot of bulk resistance (R bulk) for Pt/8YSZ/Pt cells measured between 250–600 °C under air, comparing UHS and conventional heat treatments.
summary: Arrhenius plot displaying the temperature dependence of bulk resistance (R bulk) for Pt/8YSZ/Pt cells across the 250–600 °C range. Data collected under air for both UHS and conventional heat treatments reveal the thermal activation behavior of the bulk resistance, providing insight into the impact of sintering methods on the electrolyte's electrical properties.

caption: EDS elemental map for the ST 1125 microstructure showing the distribution of Cr.
summary: Chromium distribution within the ST 1125 microstructure is visualized through EDS mapping. The map confirms that chromium is a primary constituent of the oxides segregated at grain boundaries. This spatial data supports the identification of (Cr, Mn)-rich oxides as the specific particles present in the ST 1125 condition.

caption: IFFT image of the (2 11 ¯ 0) crystal plane for the Ni5(Gd,Dy) phase.
summary: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) processing of the (2 11 ¯ 0) crystal plane for the Ni5(Gd,Dy) phase is displayed. This filtered image highlights the lattice periodicity and structural integrity of the specified crystal plane, facilitating a detailed analysis of the precipitate's internal atomic arrangement.

caption: Schmid factor (SF) distribution map for various dislocation slip systems within the deformation twin and matrix regions of the annealed alloy.
summary: Visualizing the Schmid factor distribution for individual slip systems in the annealed alloy, this map characterizes the twin concentration region. It demonstrates how the annealing process influences the slip system orientation and potential activity, serving as a baseline for comparing deformation behavior against the as-deposited state.

caption: Chromatographic profiles of various resins acquired at a 210 nm detection wavelength, highlighting the presence of multiple components and minor products within the concentrated samples.
summary: The chromatographic profiles of the resins, detected at 210 nm, reveal that these materials are composed of several distinct components. These components vary significantly between different resin samples. The resins were prepared at sufficiently high concentrations to ensure that minor products could be successfully detected and analyzed.

caption: Diffuse reflectance spectra comparing LMS-1 loose powder and pure olivine mineral, with a vertical red line marking the 1070 ± 10 nm laser wavelength.
summary: Diffuse reflectance spectra comparing LMS-1 loose powder and pure olivine mineral, with a vertical red line marking the 1070 ± 10 nm laser wavelength. This spectral analysis provides a comparison between the powder and the pure mineral, identifying optical characteristics relevant to the specified laser wavelength used in subsequent processing.

caption: EDS spectrum of the worn-out surface of the as-processed (AP) sample tested under room and elevated temperature conditions.
summary: This EDS spectrum characterizes the worn-out surface of the as-processed (AP) sample. The analysis, conducted under both room and elevated temperature conditions, serves as a qualitative indicator of surface composition. Consistent detector settings and sample orientation were maintained to minimize topography-related artifacts during the acquisition of these spectral data.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of BMSCs on PT, PTM, and PTMN scaffolds at 14 days, visualizing RUNX2 (green), actin (red), and nuclei (blue).
summary: Immunofluorescence staining performed at 14 days post-implantation reveals the spatial distribution of RUNX2 in BMSCs cultured on PT, PTM, and PTMN scaffolds. The staining utilizes green for RUNX2, red for actin (phalloidin), and blue for nuclei (DAPI), showing higher fluorescence intensities of RUNX2 on the PTMN scaffold compared to the others.

caption: Three-dimensional rose diagram visualizing the angular orientation distribution of force chains within the analyzed network.
summary: A three-dimensional rose diagram is utilized to visualize the orientation of the force chains. This plot effectively maps the directional distribution of the force chain network, providing a clear statistical representation of how these chains are oriented within the material structure under the studied conditions.

caption: Lingual profile deviation analysis of the incisor tooth, illustrating surface accuracy through color-coded mapping.
summary: This panel displays the lingual profile deviation analysis of an incisor tooth. The visualization utilizes a color-coded heatmap to represent surface accuracy, where blue regions indicate deviations within -0.0392 mm and yellow regions indicate deviations within 0.0515 mm, providing a quantitative assessment of the manufactured dental profile's dimensional precision.

caption: Temperature dependence of the derivative of magnetization (dM/dT) used to identify Curie temperatures (Tc) for Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond HTHed samples.
summary: Plotting the temperature dependence of dM/dT allows for the precise determination of Curie temperatures for various HTHed geometries. The analysis reveals distinct Tc values of 267 K, 240 K, 250 K, and 239 K for the Tube, Schwarz, Gyroid, and Diamond samples, respectively, highlighting the influence of structural design on magnetic phase transitions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of site 2 in panel (e), indicating the presence of multiple TiO2 grains and potentially superimposed structures.
summary: The diffraction pattern of site 2 reveals the presence of multiple TiO2 grains. The complexity of the pattern suggests that other structures may be superimposed, indicating a more disordered or multi-phase region compared to site 1, which is characteristic of the oxide film's polycrystalline nature.

caption: Ti-rich clusters extracted from the atom probe data, showing a prevalence of large, atom-dense features (indicated by red arrows) specifically in samples tested at 250 °C and 450 °C.
summary: Ti-rich clusters in Inconel 718 samples exhibit significant growth at elevated temperatures. Large clusters containing numerous Ti atoms become the dominant feature in samples tested at 250 °C and 450 °C, as highlighted by red arrows, suggesting temperature-dependent evolution of Ti-based precipitates during the tensile deformation process.

caption: Band Contrast (BC) map of the bonding interface processed at a deformation temperature of 1040 °C.
summary: This Band Contrast map visualizes the bonding interface microstructure at a deformation temperature of 1040 °C. The BC map provides essential structural information regarding the quality of the interface, serving as a foundational EBSD characterization for analyzing the bonding characteristics of the material under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Flexural strength (FS) testing configuration using a GTM2500 machine following ISO 527 standards.
summary: The GTM2500 testing machine is depicted here during the flexural strength (FS) testing of the polymer samples. By following ISO 527 standards, this experimental setup allows for the precise determination of the material's response to bending forces, complementing the tensile test data obtained in the previous step.

caption: Probability of Detection (POD) curve as a function of porosity percentage for the optimal GBDT model, featuring a 0.05% porosity classification threshold, a 95% confidence interval, and the 90/95 porosity level.
summary: This plot illustrates the performance of the optimal GBDT model by displaying the POD curve against porosity percentage. It highlights the 0.05% porosity threshold for classification, the 95% confidence interval, and the 90/95 porosity level. Green data points represent model signals, providing a clear visualization of the model's detection capabilities.

caption: Ten representative load-displacement curves obtained from nanoindentation of zone I, which consists of B2 austenite and Ni4Ti3 precipitates.
summary: Zone I, characterized by a B2 austenite matrix containing Ni4Ti3 precipitates, exhibits ten representative load-displacement curves that are relatively stable and dense. These mechanical responses indicate consistent indentation behavior within this specific microstructural region, reflecting the influence of the Ni4Ti3 phase on the local mechanical properties of the modified NiTi material.

caption: Photograph of the PDMS-glass chip demonstrating effective, leak-free sealing, despite the presence of a faint waving texture at the channel edges resulting from the SLA-layering process.
summary: The PDMS-glass chip is shown to have achieved effective, leak-free sealing. Although a faint waving texture is visible at the channel edges due to the SLA-layering process used to fabricate the negative molds, this structural feature did not compromise the device integrity, as no leakage phenomena occurred during operation.

caption: Snapshot at t = 5720 ps, marking the point where the density of Hirth locks reaches its maximum value.
summary: This MD snapshot at t = 5720 ps identifies the critical point in the synthesis process where the Hirth lock density reaches its maximum. The structural state at this time represents the peak of dislocation interaction and locking, serving as a reference for the subsequent decomposition phase observed under continued loading.

caption: HAADF-STEM image and corresponding EDS elemental mappings of the as-built 5Al 3 Zr sample, illustrating the spatial distribution of alloying elements.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image and EDS elemental mapping of the as-built 5Al 3 Zr sample reveal the distribution of alloying elements. The EDS mappings show phases enriched with Zn, Mg, and Cu within the alpha-Al grains and at grain boundaries, which are identified as eta-Mg(Zn, Cu)2 precipitates.

caption: Infrared luminescence spectra of the temperature sensor immersed in water, recorded between 21.0 and 49.4 °C under 700 nm excitation, featuring a magnified inset of the 831 nm emission peak.
summary: This panel displays the infrared luminescence spectra of a temperature sensor in water from 21.0 to 49.4 °C under 700 nm excitation. As temperature increases, the emission intensity at 1626 nm rises, while the emission at 831 nm decreases, as highlighted by the magnified inset of the 831 nm peak.

caption: Laser power-dependent SERS spectra of control group samples measured using the 3D superstructure platform.
summary: Representative laser power-dependent SERS spectra were acquired for the control group by placing actual AH samples within the 3D superstructure. These spectra demonstrate the spectroscopic response of the control samples under varying laser power conditions, confirming the utility of the 3D superstructure for sensitive metabolite detection.

caption: 2D fluorescence spectral maps of PLA and PLA/GF specimens before and after UV-C irradiation, displaying emission wavelength on the x-axis and excitation wavelength on the y-axis.
summary: Fluorescence spectroscopy evaluates surface degradation in PLA and PLA/GF specimens following UV-C irradiation. The 2D spectral maps reveal that as degradation time increases, the fluorescence area expands and shifts toward longer wavelengths. These spectral changes indicate molecular chain scission within the PLA resin, confirming the impact of UV-C exposure.

caption: EDS elemental distribution map corresponding to the as-deposited sample, highlighting the spatial arrangement of alloying elements at the grain boundaries.
summary: The EDS map illustrates the elemental distribution within the as-deposited Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy. Analysis confirms that alloying elements, specifically Zn, Mg, and Cu, are primarily concentrated at the grain boundary positions. This spatial arrangement correlates with the discontinuous reticulation of grain boundary phases observed in the corresponding SEM morphology.

caption: Histogram illustrating the distribution of powder particles, with the maximum percentage observed within the 80 to 200 mesh size range.
summary: Histogram illustrating the distribution of powder particles, with the maximum percentage observed within the 80 to 200 mesh size range. This plot quantifies the particle size distribution, demonstrating that the majority of the self-shielded flux powder falls within the specified mesh size interval, confirming the material's consistency and size characteristics.

caption: Atomic projection model of the crystal structure on the (1 1 0) atomic plane viewed along the [1 1 0] axis.
summary: This atomic projection model on the (1 1 0) plane viewed along the [1 1 0] axis provides a detailed view of the atomic arrangement, which is critical for visualizing the coherent orientation relationships and the structural compatibility between the γ matrix and the γ′ phase.

caption: Cyclic stability of CO2 adsorption capacity for geopolymer specimens over multiple adsorption-desorption cycles at 0 °C.
summary: This plot tracks the CO2 adsorption capacity of geopolymer specimens across repeated adsorption-desorption cycles at 0 °C. The data reveals a slight reduction in capacity as the number of cycles increases, demonstrating the long-term stability and performance degradation characteristics of the geopolymer monoliths under these specific testing conditions.

caption: FTIR spectra of Orthoflex material subjected to varying post-curing times, illustrating the evolution of polymerization-related bands.
summary: Orthoflex material spectra are shown for different post-curing durations to evaluate polymerization progress. The spectra track the evolution of bands associated with the aromatic structure and the growing polymerization peak. This comparison demonstrates how extended post-curing times influence the chemical composition and the intensity of characteristic acrylate absorption bands.

caption: Scatter plot of calculated DFT conversion voltages versus composition index, highlighting the initial random dataset, the equimolar baseline, and optimized compositions identified through Bayesian optimization.
summary: This plot displays DFT-calculated conversion voltages for various fluoride alloy compositions. It identifies the equimolar baseline at 2.21 V, the initial random dataset with a mean of 2.39 V, and optimized compositions found via Bayesian optimization, including high-voltage candidates like HEF-88211, which achieved a voltage of 2.81 V.

caption: Principal component analysis of mixture data, where individual points are colour-coded according to their original mixture categories to visualize distribution patterns.
summary: Principal component analysis of the mixture data is presented, with data points colour-coded by their original mixture categories. This visualization reveals that while the mixtures share certain similarities, they also exhibit distinct distribution patterns, which highlights the unique properties inherent to each of the different mixtures analyzed.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the EIS spectra for passivated WAAM 316L stainless steel specimens tested in a 0.9 wt% NaCl electrolyte environment.
summary: The EIS spectra for as-fabricated WAAM 316L stainless steel specimens are presented in this Nyquist plot. Consistent with the wrought samples, these results are effectively modeled by an equivalent electrical circuit featuring a single-time constant, with fitted values for the impedance spectra summarized in the study's data table.

caption: Tafel polarization curve for AISI 304 stainless steel after 8 hours of immersion in chloride molten salt at 720 °C, showing the electrochemical fit used for corrosion rate assessment.
summary: This Tafel plot illustrates the electrochemical behavior of AISI 304 stainless steel following an 8-hour immersion in chloride molten salt at 720 °C. The curve includes a fitted analysis, which is essential for determining the electrochemical parameters required to accurately assess the corrosion rate of the material under these specific conditions.

caption: Stage IV of the LC crystal growth process showing amorphous phase transformation.
summary: Stage IV of the LC crystal growth process shows the remaining melt transforming into an amorphous phase. This occurs if the cooling rate exceeds the critical cooling rate, resulting in a composition close to Zr-based amorphous powder, marking the final stage of the solidification process in laser cladding.

caption: 1H NMR spectra comparing unmodified gelatin and synthesized GelMA, highlighting the emergence of new peaks at approximately δ = 5.5 ppm corresponding to vinyl methacrylate protons.
summary: 1H NMR spectroscopy was utilized to confirm the successful synthesis of GelMA by comparing its spectrum to that of pure gelatin. The appearance of two distinct peaks at δ = 5.5 ppm in the GelMA spectrum confirms the successful grafting of vinyl methacrylate protons onto the gelatin backbone.

caption: Normalised mass spectrum of Inconel 718 tested at 250 °C, illustrating the solute composition at this elevated temperature.
summary: Representing the mass spectrum of Inconel 718 at 250 °C, this panel highlights the solute profile of the alloy. Consistent with the broader study, carbon detection was specifically targeted via mass spectrometry. The results confirm that other solutes are present in amounts comparable to those observed at other test temperatures.

caption: Bright-field TEM image showing the morphology of blocky Al6(Mn,Fe) precipitates located at the grain boundaries of the S0 sample.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging focuses on the blocky precipitates found within the S0 sample. These particles, measuring approximately 250 nm in size, are situated at the grain boundaries, indicating their role as primary precipitates that form during the aging process at 350 °C for 300 minutes.

caption: Overview of the DED-arc additive manufacturing system, featuring a six-axis Fanuc M-10iD12 robot, a Fronius TPS500i CMT welding power source, and a two-axis translocator platform.
summary: The DED-arc system hardware is displayed, comprising a six-axis Fanuc M-10iD12 robot with its control cabinet and a welding gun. The setup integrates a wire feeding system and a Fronius TPS500i CMT welding power source, all mounted on a two-axis translocator platform used for block deposition experiments.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of contact lenses following immersion in a 1.5 mM gold precursor concentration.
summary: This plot displays the optical absorption characteristics of the hydrogel contact lens after treatment with a 1.5 mM gold precursor solution. The spectrum provides data on the light absorption properties resulting from the in situ gold reduction process within the hydrogel matrix at this specific concentration.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms recorded on a 3D nickel-plated carbon (NPC) substrate at a sweep rate of 10 mV/s between -0.4 and -1.4 V (vs. SCE) in three distinct electrolyte solutions containing Ni2+, Sn2+, or a mixture of both.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms on 3D NPC substrates illustrate the electrodeposition behavior of Ni and Sn. Comparison with 2D CF results shows that Ni reduction is significantly influenced by the 3D microstructure, whereas Sn deposition is less sensitive to surface morphology, resulting in comparable loading masses on both substrate types.

caption: Emission spectra for argon and krypton sparged solutions, comparing conditions without stirring and with stirring at 1500 rpm, with tentative annotations for CN and C2 species.
summary: Spectra reveal that stirring intensifies emissions for both argon and krypton. Despite significant UV absorption by the PMMA container and liquid, clear emissions are identified, including the OH radical at 310 nm. The emission shapes remain consistent with non-luminol cases, though stirring enhances the overall intensity of the observed spectral features.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the as-cast sample deformed at 1100 °C and 0.001 s⁻¹.
summary: This inverse pole figure map displays the microstructure of an as-cast sample deformed at 1100 °C and a strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹. The map reveals that dynamically recrystallized grains exhibit a slight elongation perpendicular to the loading direction, with black and white lines indicating high-angle grain boundaries.

caption: Hardness values plotted against strain rate for the Nb-graded specimen, illustrating the mechanical response under microscratch testing conditions.
summary: This plot displays the hardness of the Nb-graded specimen as a function of strain rate derived from microscratch experiments. The data provides insight into the mechanical behavior of the AM-processed alloy, serving as a basis for evaluating the material's response to varying deformation rates during the testing process.

caption: Principal component analysis of spatter ejection direction data, with samples colored to represent variations in ejection orientation.
summary: PCA analysis of spatter ejection direction reveals distinct clustering patterns. The data indicates that larger ejection angles are correlated with higher scanning speeds, which corresponds to lower input energy conditions. This visualization confirms that the first two principal components successfully account for more than 95% of the dataset variance.

caption: Current density response over time during the potential pulse testing sequence, illustrating the electrochemical behavior of the specimen under the applied potential pulses.
summary: The current density response over time is depicted for the potential pulse testing sequence. This plot captures the electrochemical behavior of the specimen as it undergoes the defined potential pulses, providing essential data on the current density fluctuations associated with the formation and stability of the passive film.

caption: Stress amplitude versus fatigue life (S–N) curve for HSLA-100 steel specimens repaired via laser additive manufacturing, illustrating the fatigue performance under high-cycle fatigue (HCF) testing conditions.
summary: This S–N curve characterizes the fatigue behavior of laser additive manufactured HSLA-100 repair samples. By plotting stress amplitude against the number of cycles to failure, the graph provides essential data on the high-cycle fatigue performance of the repaired material, serving as a baseline for future fractographic analysis of crack initiation.

caption: Isosurface 3D rendering of the β-TCP bone implant showing the low-resolution scan in transparency and the specific cutout region selected for high-resolution analysis.
summary: This 3D isosurface rendering illustrates the complete β-TCP sample S10 scanned at a 10 μm voxel resolution. It highlights the specific cutout region manually prepared for subsequent high-resolution imaging, demonstrating the spatial relationship between the bulk sample overview and the localized area of interest for detailed structural investigation.

caption: Current efficiency of electrodeposited Cu-Ni alloy thick films plotted as a function of applied current density.
summary: This plot illustrates the current efficiency of electrodeposited Cu-Ni alloy thick films across varying current densities. The observed efficiency trends are attributed to hydrogen evolution occurring as a side reaction during the electrodeposition process, which acts as the rate-limiting step for the mass transfer of the alloy components.

caption: Secondary electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS 2) Bode phase plot demonstrating the shift in phase angles toward higher frequencies following the passivation process.
summary: The secondary EIS 2 Bode phase plot illustrates the electrochemical response after passivation. The observed increase in phase angles and their shift toward higher frequencies indicate the formation of a more stable and protective passive film on the LPBF planes, confirming the effectiveness of the surface passivation treatment.

caption: Temperature profile of the Ni slab/nanobubble/water system during the nanobubble collapse process, showing heat concentration at the leading edge of the water nano-hammer.
summary: This panel displays the temperature profile of a Ni slab/nanobubble/water system during the nanobubble collapse process. The simulation reveals that transferred heat is predominantly concentrated at the leading edge of the water nano-hammer, providing insight into the thermal dynamics occurring during the rapid shrinkage and collapse of the nanobubble.

caption: Wavelet transforms of Cu K-edge EXAFS signals comparing Cu foil and CuNi@BNC.
summary: Wavelet transform analysis of the Cu K-edge EXAFS signals is performed for both Cu foil and the CuNi@BNC sample. This technique provides a two-dimensional representation of the EXAFS data in both R-space and k-space, allowing for a detailed comparison of the local atomic environment of copper.

caption: Top-down projection of the horizontal layer showing the spatial arrangement of nodes and cables.
summary: Top-down visualization of the horizontal layer reveals the geometric layout of the module. Connectivity at the interfaces between adjacent modules is ensured through shared nodes or cables, preserving the local connectivity of the module during periodic translational replication to form the metamaterial array investigated in this study.

caption: Model B crystal defect distribution at a cutting speed of 50 m/s.
summary: Model B is examined at a cutting speed of 50 m/s to assess the influence of an internal interface. The presence of this interface alters the structural response within the workpiece as the tool passes through, resulting in a reduced fluctuation of the total dislocation fraction compared to Model A.

caption: Grain boundary habit planes for Ni nanograins colored by boundary normal, where the dominant blue color indicates the presence of numerous {111} twin planes.
summary: Grain boundary habit planes are visualized for the Ni nanograins, with colors representing the boundary normal. The prevalence of blue indicates numerous {111} twin planes within the material. Some grains are composed of two components and enclose multiple twin systems, such as the system marked as number 1.

caption: Down-skin roughness comparison between single and double exposure specimens.
summary: This bar chart compares down-skin roughness values for specimens fabricated using single and double exposure strategies. The data indicates that the double exposure strategy effectively optimizes surface roughness, with Specimen No. 12 showing a 14.92% improvement over Specimen No. 2 and a 17.55% improvement over Specimen No. 5.

caption: Logarithmic plot of relative modulus versus relative density for DCC lattices compared against BCC, FCC, and Octet literature benchmarks.
summary: This logarithmic plot displays the relative modulus as a function of relative density for DCC lattice samples. By comparing these results with literature-reported data for BCC, FCC, and Octet structures, it is observed that the DCC lattice consistently falls within the predicted range for bending-dominated mechanical behavior.

caption: Size distribution profiles for micro/sub-micron and nano/sub-micron TiB2 particles across different experimental samples.
summary: The histogram displays the size distribution of TiB2 particles, categorized into micro/sub-micron and nano/sub-micron ranges. By comparing these distributions across different samples, the figure highlights the variability in particle size control achieved during processing, which is essential for understanding the resulting microstructure and particle-matrix interactions.

caption: CHNS/O elemental analysis quantifying residual carbon weight percentage in dried silica gels, comparing samples with and without ethanol rinsing.
summary: This bar chart displays the residual carbon content in dried silica gels as measured by CHNS/O elemental analysis. The data compares the carbon weight percentage between samples that underwent ethanol rinsing and those that did not, providing a quantitative assessment of organic content removal from the printed silica structures.

caption: Small 3D printed mullite monoliths with a diameter of 0.7 cm and height of 1.5 cm, featuring a gyroid design in both blank white and blue HKUST-1 functionalized versions.
summary: Small-scale 3D printed mullite monoliths with a 0.7 cm diameter and 1.5 cm height are shown here. The samples feature a gyroid architecture and are presented in both their blank white state and after functionalization with HKUST-1, which imparts a distinct blue coloration to the ceramic structure.

caption: HAADF-STEM image showing the precipitation of Fe and Ni-rich nanocrystals within unoxidized zones of the material.
summary: This HAADF-STEM image captures the precipitation of Fe and Ni-rich nanocrystals within unoxidized zones of the material. The presence of these nanocrystals indicates that the local chemical environment and structural evolution significantly influence the corrosion behavior of the alloy, providing insight into the microstructural changes occurring during the process.

caption: Optimization convergence profile for the CWaOA algorithm shown in a 3D plot.
summary: CWaOA algorithm convergence is visualized through a 3D curve, mapping the progression of the optimization process. This representation allows for the assessment of the algorithm's stability and speed in reaching an optimal solution, contributing to the comprehensive evaluation of all tested algorithms within the reported convergence characteristics.

caption: Atomic model of the γ′-Ni3Al phase supercell viewed along the b-direction, with the alloying atom M doped at the slip plane.
summary: This panel displays the supercell model for the γ′-Ni3Al phase, viewed along the b-direction. The atomic arrangement features an alloying atom M doped at the slip plane, which serves as a critical input for calculating the generalized stacking fault energy of the γ′-Ni3Al phase slip system.

caption: Cycling performance of a-Si, a-Ge, and a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-films over 100 cycles, showing discharge capacity evolution.
summary: Cycling performance of a-Si, a-Ge, and a-Si0.8Ge0.2 thin-films over 100 cycles is presented. The maximum discharge capacities are 1588.4 mAh g-1 for a-Si, 1544.3 mAh g-1 for a-Ge, and 1685.7 mAh g-1 for a-Si0.8Ge0.2, demonstrating the superior initial capacity of the alloyed thin-film.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra showing the reduction kinetics of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) catalyzed by Pd/C coaxial reactors (CR) of varying lengths.
summary: This panel displays UV-Vis absorption spectra used to evaluate the catalytic performance of Pd/C coaxial reactors. By monitoring the reduction of 4-nitrophenol over time, the graph illustrates how varying the length of the Pd/C CR influences the catalytic reduction process, providing essential data for assessing the reactor's overall efficiency.

caption: Kernel Average Misalignment (KAM) map of the vertical specimen, showing localized deformation near crack paths with an average KAM value of 0.70°.
summary: The KAM map for the vertical specimen reveals only a small amount of deformation localized near the crack propagation paths. With an average KAM value of approximately 0.70°, this result demonstrates that the vertical specimen underwent significantly less plastic deformation compared to the horizontal specimen during fracture.

caption: Contour map representing the aspect ratio of the melt pool as a function of laser power and scan speed.
summary: The aspect ratio of the melt pool is visualized through this contour map, which plots the geometric relationship between track dimensions against laser power and scan speed. This map serves as part of the comprehensive analysis of melt pool characteristics developed from the processing window investigated in the study.

caption: Evolution of average ϵ xx plastic strain across the graded specimen gauge length plotted against applied macroscopic stress, with color-coded segments representing distinct compositional ratios.
summary: This plot illustrates the progression of average ϵ xx plastic strain along the gauge length of a functionally graded material specimen. By correlating strain values with applied macroscopic stresses and specific compositional ratios, the data reveals how varying material compositions influence local plastic deformation behavior under increasing mechanical loading conditions.

caption: Receiver operating characteristic curve evaluating the performance of the proposed real-time classification approach.
summary: This panel displays the receiver operating characteristic curve for the proposed real-time classification approach. The ROC curve plots true positive rates against false positive rates across various discrimination thresholds. A higher area under the curve value indicates superior classification performance for identifying positive data points within the real-time system.

caption: Annular bright-field (ABF) STEM image of the PBF-EB sample top, illustrating the precipitate-dislocation architecture.
summary: This ABF-STEM image captures the precipitate-dislocation architecture at the top of the PBF-EB sample. The observed structure is noted to be similar to that previously reported in PBF-EB-built Cu-Cu2O alloys, providing a visual representation of the microstructural arrangement within the material.

caption: Surface potential distribution map of the Colmonoy 56 surface obtained via Scanning Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (SKFM) in ambient air.
summary: The SKFM potential mapping of the sintered Colmonoy 56 surface reveals the distribution of surface potentials. Comparison with the AFM topography shows that secondary phases exhibit potentials several millivolts higher than the [Ni] matrix. These potentials, representing a mix of work function and corrosion potential, indicate the high stability of secondary phases.

caption: Temporal temperature variation curves recorded at monitoring point 9 under varying laser power levels.
summary: This line graph illustrates the temporal temperature variation curves at monitoring point 9 across different laser power levels. The data provides a clear representation of how the temperature profile evolves over time in response to changes in laser power during the thermal process, serving as a baseline for thermal characterization.

caption: Computer-aided design model of the thrust chamber assembly, illustrating the segmented structure and integrated cooling circuits.
summary: This CAD model displays the thrust chamber assembly used for testing. The design features distinct segments, labeled A, D, and R, which utilize specific cooling circuits. Segments A and D are water-cooled, while segment R employs gaseous nitrogen cooling to optimize the measurement-over-error ratio during experimental activities.

caption: Raman spectra of spent catalysts, characterizing the structural nature and graphitization degree of carbon species formed, with analysis indicating improved crystallinity and reduced defect density in the graphitic domains.
summary: Raman spectroscopy of the spent catalysts evaluates the nature and quality of the carbon species formed during the reaction. The results demonstrate that the graphitic domains produced across all catalysts exhibit improved crystallinity and a lower defect density, as quantified by the structural parameters summarized in the study.

caption: EBSD inverse pole figure map of the T2 Ti-6Al-4V sample, displaying the reconstructed prior-β grain orientation and boundary network.
summary: This panel presents the EBSD inverse pole figure map for the T2 sample, visualizing the reconstructed prior-β grain structure. The map, superimposed with grain boundaries defined by misorientation angles above 10°, provides a detailed view of the grain orientation distribution resulting from the specific processing conditions applied to this specimen.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the Ti–22Al–25Nb powder, the as-built sample, and the heat-treated sample, highlighting the primary presence of the β phase alongside minor B2 and O phase constituents.
summary: XRD analysis of the Ti–22Al–25Nb alloy reveals the phase composition across different processing stages. The as-built component is primarily composed of the β phase, with smaller amounts of B2 and O phases present. These patterns provide a comparative view of the structural evolution from powder to heat-treated states.

caption: Time-resolved FTIR spectra of the acrylate benchmark blend containing O-16 sensitized by ITX, showing the emergence of a specific CO₂ peak at approximately 2350 cm⁻¹ during exposure.
summary: FTIR spectra demonstrate that the addition of ITX to the O-16 system facilitates decarboxylation during photopolymerization. The detection of a specific CO₂ peak at approximately 2350 cm⁻¹ confirms that ITX effectively sensitizes O-16, leading to chemical changes that are absent when the oxime ester is used without the sensitizer.

caption: Co-occurrence network map of author keywords derived from raw data using VOSviewer, where circle size indicates occurrence frequency and colors denote thematic clusters.
summary: This co-occurrence network map visualizes the relationships between author keywords extracted from raw research data. Generated via VOSviewer, the map uses circle size to represent the frequency of keyword occurrences, while distinct colors identify thematic clusters. Wires connecting the circles illustrate the links between various research topics within the dataset.

caption: Total heat generation rate, calculated heat components, cell potential, and open-circuit voltage as functions of lithium composition for 2D tape-casted NMC622 during lithiation at 1C.
summary: Panel d shows the thermal and electrical parameters for 2D tape-casted NMC622 during lithiation at 1C. The plot includes the total heat generation rate, calculated heat components, cell potential, and open-circuit voltage versus lithium composition, allowing for an assessment of the electrode's behavior and resistance during the lithiation phase of cycling.

caption: Remanent magnetization (Mr) of the 72 h milled Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixture shown as a function of annealing temperature.
summary: This panel illustrates the remanent magnetization (Mr) of the 72 h milled Ni80Co17Mo3 powder mixture as it changes with annealing temperature. The data provides a clear view of how the remanent magnetic state of the material is influenced by the thermal annealing process applied to the milled powder mixture.

caption: Evolution of elastic modulus and nanohardness values as a function of distance from the worn subsurface in SLMed IN718 alloy.
summary: Elastic modulus and nanohardness values are plotted against the distance from the worn subsurface for the SLMed IN718 alloy. The results demonstrate a clear increase in both mechanical properties when measured closer to the worn subsurface compared to the bulk region, indicating localized strengthening due to the contact sliding process.

caption: Fluorescence micrographs showing the angiogenic potential of EPCs cultured in GelMA hydrogels with concentrations ranging from 4% to 14%.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images illustrate the angiogenic potential of endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) encapsulated within GelMA hydrogels. The study evaluates these cells across a concentration gradient of 4%, 6%, 8%, 10%, 12%, and 14% GelMA to determine the optimal hydrogel environment for supporting angiogenic activity and cellular development.

caption: Contour plot of the average rate of curvature change at T p - H p level (0,0), showing dense contour lines at low print layer heights and low printing temperatures.
summary: This contour plot illustrates the interaction between printing temperature and layer height at level (0,0). The data reveals a higher density of contour lines at lower printing temperatures and layer heights. Notably, the response variable remains largely stable at opposite positions, with printing temperature showing negligible influence between 0.12 and 0.15 mm.

caption: APT reconstruction of the DA sample aged for 0.6 h, displaying the distribution of γ“ and γʹ precipitates along dislocations as marked by red arrows.
summary: Representing the DA sample aged for 0.6 h, this APT reconstruction illustrates the continued growth of γ“ precipitates decorated with γʹ precipitates along dislocations. The red arrows point to these specific structural arrangements, which are consistent with the morphologies observed across the various ageing times in the DA sample series.

caption: SHAP dependence plot showing the impact of NPD on residual stress predictions along the scan direction σx.
summary: This SHAP dependence plot displays the effect of NPD on residual stress predictions along the scan direction σx. Each dot represents a single prediction, with the x-axis showing the feature value and the y-axis representing the SHAP value in MPa, colored by the strongest interacting feature.

caption: Schematic representation of the strain gauge circuits bonded to the outer surface of the tubular specimen gauge section.
summary: Vishay 120 Ω strain gauges were strategically bonded to the middle of the outer gauge section of the thin-walled tubular specimens. This configuration allows for the precise measurement and control of axial, shear, and hoop strain components during mechanical loading, ensuring accurate data acquisition for the yield surface experiments.

caption: Deconvoluted nano-hardness distribution of an HEC-cermet derived from 350 nanoindentations performed at a 20 mN load, presented as a histogram with 1 GPa bin sizes.
summary: This histogram displays the deconvoluted nano-hardness distribution of an HEC-cermet based on 350 nanoindentations at 20 mN. The data reveals a tri-modal distribution, which corresponds to distinct microstructural features including carbide/binder interfaces, (Ta,Nb,V)C rich carbide cores, and (Ti,W)C rich rim areas, reflecting the material's high measurement standard deviation.

caption: Perspective view of the interconnected porous network observed across all 3D-printed composite printing conditions.
summary: Displaying the porous network architecture, this panel utilizes X-ray micro-tomography to illustrate the internal structure of all 3D-printed composites. The rendering highlights the spatial arrangement and connectivity of pores resulting from various printing conditions, offering a comprehensive view of the material's internal morphology after the fabrication process.

caption: Measured bending stiffness S plotted against the number of load cycles N for a cantilever specimen, with red arrows indicating specific data points corresponding to separate load and displacement measurements.
summary: This panel displays the experimental fatigue behavior of a cantilever specimen by plotting bending stiffness S against the number of load cycles N. The curve illustrates the degradation of stiffness over time, with specific points highlighted by red arrows to correlate the stiffness data with independent load and displacement measurements.

caption: Quasi-static B-H hysteresis loop comparing the magnetic behavior of as-fabricated (AF) and heat-treated (HTed) samples, illustrating the reduction in coercivity (Hc) and changes in magnetic softness.
summary: This quasi-static B-H hysteresis loop displays the magnetization characteristics of AF and HTed samples. The heat-treated samples exhibit significantly softer magnetic behavior compared to the as-fabricated samples, evidenced by a halving of the coercivity (Hc) despite the absence of grain growth or texture evolution during the heat treatment process.

caption: 1H NMR spectrum of PUA, showing proton signals between 5.8 and 6.5 ppm corresponding to the double bond (–CH=CH2) characteristic of an acrylate-terminated polymer.
summary: The 1H NMR spectrum of PUA is presented to confirm its chemical structure. Proton signals observed in the 5.8 to 6.5 ppm range are identified as characteristic peaks of the double bond (–CH=CH2), providing evidence that PUA is successfully synthesized as an acrylate-terminated polymer.

caption: Line scan profile across the corrosion region of plain Ni-coated Ha230 alloy after 500 h of immersion in PAC salt.
summary: This line scan spectrum displays the elemental composition of the corrosion region on a plain Ni-coated Ha230 alloy after 500 h of immersion. The data indicates the formation of a thick layer of magnesium oxide, with no other significant oxide phases detected on the surface.

caption: Low-power (1 mW) photoluminescence spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample measured at 77 K, featuring Voigt-profile fits to resolve individual emission peaks.
summary: The 77 K photoluminescence spectrum of the BL-InAs/GaAsSb-C sample under 1 mW excitation is presented. Voigt-profile fitting is applied to the emission features to resolve individual peaks. This low-power measurement serves as a baseline for identifying the primary emission characteristics of the quantum dot layers.

caption: Second-nearest-neighbor (2NN) SRO parameters for nitrogen-metal pairs in Fe70Ni10Cr20 with 1 at.% N, demonstrating persistent negative values below 1000 K.
summary: The 2NN N–Cr SRO parameter is plotted against temperature for the 1 at.% N alloy. The results show that the parameter remains negative at temperatures below 1000 K, which serves as a clear indicator of order–disorder transition behavior within the nitrogen-metal atomic configuration of the alloy system.

caption: Comparison of the coefficient of friction (COF) and wear rate for the material tested under a 10 N load at 750 °C in a helium environment with a sliding velocity of 0.04 m/s.
summary: This plot illustrates the tribological performance of the material under high-temperature helium conditions. The average COF is determined by analyzing the final 30% of the experimental duration, ensuring the values represent a stabilized state. These metrics provide a quantitative assessment of the wear resistance and frictional behavior under specified parameters.

caption: Comparison of experimental I-V data for the RTC France PV solar cell against curves generated via TSEC using DDM parameters extracted by the SNF-TSEC approach.
summary: This panel displays the I-V curves generated using the SNF-TSEC approach for the RTC France PV solar cell. The generated curves demonstrate a close match with the experimental data, confirming the accuracy of the DDM physical parameters extracted through the SNF-TSEC optimization technique for this specific photovoltaic device.

caption: Electronic states projected onto Fe, O, and Ca atoms at the Fe/CaO interface.
summary: Displayed are the projected density of states for Fe, O, and Ca atoms at the Fe/CaO interface. These plots describe the electronic structure of the pre-nucleation model, offering insights into the interaction between Fe atoms and the CaO surface through the analysis of their respective electronic density of states.

caption: Experimental setup featuring a quartz sample rack holding specimens prepared for CO2 exposure within a horizontal tube furnace.
summary: This photograph displays the experimental configuration used for CO2 exposure testing. It highlights the quartz sample rack and the arrangement of specimens prior to their insertion into a horizontal tube furnace. The setup is designed to facilitate controlled environmental exposure of the materials during the high-temperature treatment process.

caption: Line graph illustrating the variation of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) as a function of the parameter λ for the weak boundary effects-based Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model.
summary: This line graph displays the relationship between the RMSE and the parameter λ for a weak boundary effects-based PINN model. The plot serves to evaluate the model's predictive performance on the test set, illustrating how varying λ influences the error metrics within the physics-informed machine learning framework.

caption: Average nominal stress–strain curves obtained from uniaxial tension tests for S4 and S5 samples.
summary: This plot displays the average nominal stress–strain behavior of S4 and S5 samples under uniaxial tension. These specific samples were selected for comparison because they exhibit superior mechanical properties and fewer structural defects compared to the S1 through S3 variants, highlighting their enhanced performance during tensile testing.

caption: Bubble diagram comparing S. aureus related pathway expression between 40%HA-2%Ag-PEEK and bare PEEK, highlighting statistically significant changes.
summary: Pfam enrichment analysis reveals that 40%HA-2%AgNPs-PEEK induces the up-regulation of stress protection, adhesion, metabolic regulation, and electron transport-related proteins in S. aureus. These changes in the bacterial pathway expression profile demonstrate the antibacterial efficacy of the composite surface compared to the bare PEEK control, likely through autophagy-mediated pathogen clearance.

caption: Optical micrograph of ODS-316L alloy processed via LPBF at a laser energy density of 170.1 J/mm³.
summary: This optical micrograph reveals the macroscopic structure of an ODS-316L alloy manufactured through LPBF at an energy density of 170.1 J/mm³. The image serves as a key data point in evaluating the structural evolution of the alloy across varying laser energy densities during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Evolution of x-direction displacement values along the AB path of the NBSC superalloy specimen, demonstrating the capability of the SMM technique to resolve hundred-nanometer scale displacements using a 6 μm grid pitch.
summary: This graph displays the x-direction displacement evolution along the AB path of the notched NBSC superalloy specimen. At 618 MPa, the curve shows maximum and minimum displacement values of 0.285 and -0.249, respectively, confirming the SMM technique's high sensitivity in capturing sub-micron scale deformations during the specimen's mechanical loading process.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the frequency-dependent impedance response for the Y-Z section of the Wall 0 sample.
summary: Electrochemical impedance data for the Y-Z section of Wall 0 is presented in this Bode plot. Consistent with the overall sample behavior, the initial low-frequency impedance modulus starts at 10⁴ Ω·cm². A subsequent decline in this modulus by one order of magnitude after 14 days indicates reduced barrier performance over time.

caption: Absolute mean SHAP plot illustrating the relative significance of input features for the model output.
summary: This absolute mean SHAP plot quantifies the significance of various input features in the model. Water content and silica fume exhibit the highest mean SHAP values, followed by sand. While the plot effectively ranks feature importance, it does not indicate the direction of correlation between these features and the output.

caption: Comparison of experimental and predicted creep-fatigue life for DD6 superalloy at 760 °C based on the Manson-Coffin empirical model.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the predictive capability of the Manson-Coffin model for uniaxial creep-fatigue life in DD6 superalloy at 760 °C. By comparing predicted values against experimental data, the plot demonstrates that most data points reside within a factor of ±2, serving as a baseline for evaluating life prediction methods.

caption: TDS thermal release profiles for AM and sintered tungsten exposed to D plasma at 1000 K with a fluence of 10^26 m^-2, confirming the persistent high-energy trap states in AM tungsten.
summary: Exposure at 1000 K results in further reduction of total D release for both materials. However, the AM tungsten continues to exhibit an unexpected desorption peak, confirming that D trapping in AM tungsten consistently involves higher energy trap states compared to the sintered tungsten variety across these high temperatures.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction of the build-H specimen, displaying a uniform distribution of γ' (turquoise) and γ" (brown) precipitates delineated by iso-surfaces of 10.0 at% (Al + Ti) and 13.5 at% (Nb), respectively.
summary: This APT reconstruction of the build-H specimen reveals a uniform distribution of γ' and γ" precipitates. The turquoise interfaces represent γ' precipitates, while the brown interfaces represent γ" precipitates. These features are delineated by specific concentration iso-surfaces, highlighting the structural arrangement of the nano-precipitates within the material's grain structure.

caption: Twin network structure formed by twin variants with dimensions smaller than 200 nm.
summary: The formation of various twin variants results in a complex twin network structure. This network is characterized by dimensions smaller than 200 nm, which significantly constrains dislocation motion. The structure is particularly effective at pinning dislocations at the junctions where different twin variants meet, influencing the overall mechanical behavior.

caption: {001} pole figure for AlSi10Mg with 3 wt% B4C, indicating a weakened <001> fiber texture with a maximum MUD of 1.24.
summary: Consistent with the grain refinement observed in the IPF maps, the pole figure for the 3 wt% B4C condition shows a substantial weakening of the <001> fiber texture. The maximum MUD value of 1.24 indicates a narrow range of texture intensity, confirming the effectiveness of B4C in disrupting preferred grain growth.

caption: Current efficiency (CE) plotted as a function of applied current density during the electrodeposition process.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between electrodeposition current efficiency and applied current density. It demonstrates how the efficiency of the deposition process varies as the current density is adjusted, providing critical insight into the electrochemical performance and optimization of the deposition parameters for the material under investigation.

caption: Scanning electron microscopy image and corresponding EDS elemental distribution map for Sample A, highlighting the spatial arrangement of Ni, Ti, and Al at the aluminum core interface.
summary: Sample A is characterized using SEM and EDS to visualize the elemental distribution of Ni, Ti, and Al. The imaging focuses on the aluminum core region, providing a visual representation of how these elements are alloyed and distributed within the sample structure at the specified location.

caption: Wavelength-dependent reflectivity and absorptivity curves comparing AlFeCrSi and commercial AlSi10Mg powders, with a vertical line marking the 1070 nm laser wavelength.
summary: This plot compares the optical properties of AlFeCrSi and AlSi10Mg powders across a range of wavelengths. At the 1070 nm laser wavelength used in the L-PBF machine, the AlFeCrSi powder exhibits a reflectivity of approximately 35% and a corresponding absorptivity of approximately 65%, which is critical for laser-material interaction.

caption: Reaction curve showing the progression of lattice oxygen reactivity under controlled TG reactor conditions.
summary: Panel (c) depicts the reaction curve representing the progression of lattice oxygen reactivity. By utilizing the TG reactor, this plot captures the material's response during the oxygen release process, contributing to the comprehensive evaluation of reaction curves and lattice oxygen releasing rates described in the research.

caption: Calculated chemical potential difference of Al between the Ni–50Al–9Pt coating and Ni–16Al-(0–10) Cr or Ni–16Al-(0–10) Mo substrates as a function of Cr or Mo content, derived using the TCNI10 database.
summary: This plot illustrates the chemical potential difference of Al between the Ni–50Al–9Pt coating and various superalloy substrates containing 0–10 at. % Cr or Mo. Calculated using the TCNI10 database, the data highlights how varying alloying element concentrations influence the thermodynamic driving force for Al diffusion across the coating-substrate interface.

caption: Projected density of states for surface Ni atoms on the Ni(111) crystal surface, exhibiting a d-band center of −1.49 eV.
summary: The projected density of states for surface Ni atoms on the Ni(111) surface is presented here. The d-band center is determined to be at −1.49 eV. This electronic characteristic provides a reference point for understanding how alloying with Fe influences the d-band position and subsequent catalytic performance of the material.

caption: Coarse-grained model representation of the PLA polymer, illustrating the mapping of atomistic structures into simplified beads.
summary: The coarse-grained model of PLA is depicted here, showing how the atomistic structure is reduced to a simplified bead representation. This approach effectively lowers the degrees of freedom compared to full atomistic models, which facilitates the efficient simulation of larger material volumes while maintaining essential physical characteristics.

caption: FTIR spectra comparing CNC, PLA/LNR blend, and PLA/LNR/CNC bionanocomposite, highlighting CH stretching peaks at 2999, 2946, and 2847 cm-1.
summary: FTIR analysis of CNC, PLA/LNR, and PLA/LNR/CNC reveals characteristic CH stretching absorption peaks at 2999, 2946, and 2847 cm-1 for the PLA/LNR blend. The observed reduction in absorbance peak intensity in the bionanocomposite provides evidence for the formation of hydrogen bonds between the CNC and the polymer matrix.

caption: Assembled 3 × 3 × 3 multi-cell structure illustrating the scalability of the modular assembly technique.
summary: This panel displays the 3 × 3 × 3 structure following the assembly of individual planar elements. By using FFF-printed components without supports, the assembly process successfully creates a 3D geometry where layers are aligned parallel to the xz and yz rings, highlighting the scalability of this modular construction method.

caption: Wear volume loss of the matrix and AM-IPC materials plotted against varying applied loads.
summary: This plot illustrates the quantitative wear volume loss for both the matrix and AM-IPC materials under different normal applied loads. As the load increases from 5 N to 15 N, the wear volume of the AM-IPC composite rises, yet it consistently demonstrates superior wear resistance compared to the matrix material.

caption: Cross-sectional Micro-CT image of Ti–Mg composites after 8 weeks of implantation.
summary: This cross-sectional Micro-CT image displays the Ti–Mg composite specimen following an 8-week implantation period. The visualization provides a detailed view of the internal structural integrity and material distribution within the composite, serving as a key diagnostic tool to evaluate the performance and bioactivity of the material in vivo.

caption: Spatial distribution of microhardness values across the YOZ cross-section of the Al-6.0Zn-2.5Mg-1.5Cu alloy component.
summary: This visualization displays the microhardness distribution across the YOZ section of the fabricated Al-6.0Zn-2.5Mg-1.5Cu alloy. The map provides a detailed spatial representation of the mechanical properties, allowing for the assessment of hardness uniformity and potential variations within the alloy component as calculated and plotted for the specified cross-sectional area.

caption: Confusion matrix detailing the classification accuracy and error distribution of the process state classifier during the testing phase.
summary: This confusion matrix displays the performance of the hierarchical classification tree when applied to the testing dataset. By comparing predicted process states against actual outcomes, this visualization allows for a quantitative assessment of the model's generalization ability and overall reliability in classifying process states outside the training set.

caption: Spatial distribution of the low-frequency cap mode magnetization in the elliptical sample subjected to a 900 Oe magnetic field oriented along the y-axis.
summary: Shown here is the magnetization pattern of the low-frequency cap mode at a magnetic field of 900 Oe applied along the y-axis. This mode is distinctly localized near the edges of the elliptical sample, contrasting with the uniform distribution observed in the higher frequency Kittel-like mode.

caption: Contour plot representing the selectivity of caprylic acid (C8) over acetic acid (C2) after 4 hours of extraction, mapped against normalized closed pore area (Acl/Atot) and normalized membrane liquid span (dcl/l) at a mass transfer coefficient of 3.0 × 10^-5 m s^-1.
summary: Selectivity of caprylic acid over acetic acid is visualized here as a function of SLM degradation parameters. The plot uses the Acl/Atot and dcl/l domain to map performance, with translucent circles tracing the experimental degradation trajectory. Red-highlighted points denote the specific membrane states tested in the associated batch experiments.

caption: Recovery phase of the melt pool surface at 5.6 ms.
summary: Recorded at 5.6 ms, this frame shows the melt pool surface undergoing a rapid recovery after the initial rupture caused by high-momentum particle impacts. This dynamic behavior is characteristic of the L-DED deposition process for 2024 Al, highlighting the fluid nature of the surface film during the deposition.

caption: Comparison of predicted and experimental ultimate tensile strength (UTS) values, with performance bounds highlighted by ±5% and ±10% grey error regions.
summary: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) predictions from the AE4PSP model are plotted against experimental results. The inclusion of ±5% and ±10% grey shaded margins provides a visual metric for model reliability, demonstrating the degree of deviation between the machine learning output and the actual measured UTS values for the materials.

caption: 3D scatter plot of the first three principal components for a representative 0.1% GNP specimen, displaying overlapping data points from three different regions to demonstrate local material homogeneity.
summary: To evaluate local material homogeneity, a 3D scatter plot of the first three principal components is shown for a representative specimen containing 0.1% GNP. Raman spectra collected from three different regions of the sample overlap significantly, providing evidence of a homogeneous distribution of graphene nanoplatelets within the printed material.

caption: Pseudo-ternary diagram mapping feed ratios against phase information and micro-Vickers hardness, illustrating the composition-structure-property relationships.
summary: This pseudo-ternary diagram integrates feed ratios, phase information, and micro-Vickers hardness data to map composition-structure-property linkages. The visualization highlights two primary trends across a wide compositional range of FeCoCrNiMo FeMEAs, effectively summarizing the results of characterization and mechanical testing to demonstrate how alloy composition dictates structural and mechanical outcomes.

caption: Final stage of the ballistic impact test where a fragment penetrates the witness plate, resulting in the formation of a large hole.
summary: In the third phase of the ballistic test, the high-speed camera captures the terminal effect of the impact. A fragment from the 200A1 plate successfully penetrates the witness plate, creating a large hole. This sequence confirms the failure of the monolithic aluminum alloy to sufficiently resist the kinetic energy projectile.

caption: Schematic representation of the pull-off test specimen geometry and dimensions.
summary: This panel illustrates the shape and dimensions of samples used for pull-off testing. The 3D MJF printed samples measure 180 by 60 mm with a 5 mm thickness, featuring laser-textured areas of 15 by 15 mm. This setup defines the specific method for evaluating adhesive joints through a pull-off mechanism.

caption: Cathodic cyclic voltammograms for 1.6 M V 3.5+ electrolytes using PdNi/NrGO (1:1), Pd/C, and electrolysis, highlighting the V 3+ /V 2+ redox couple activity.
summary: This cathodic cyclic voltammogram illustrates the V 3+ /V 2+ redox couple activity. The V 3.5+ - PdNi/NrGO (1:1) electrolyte demonstrates the highest cathodic peak current density of –27.37 mA cm -2 , significantly outperforming the electrolysis-derived sample at –24.35 mA cm -2 and the Pd/C-based electrolyte at –14.44 mA cm -2 .

caption: Second mode-oriented parallelogram unit cell with specific geometric modifications.
summary: The second-mode oriented parallelogram unit cell is presented as part of the six distinct configurations analyzed. Like the other variants, it utilizes controlled arc-based strut curvature to investigate the effects of geometric changes on mechanical performance, maintaining consistent node locations and connection angles to isolate the impact of the strut shape.

caption: Martensitic transformation start temperature (Ms) plotted as a function of the applied magnetic field for Ni50−xMn37Sn13Cox (x = 1, 2, 3) alloy ribbons.
summary: This panel illustrates the dependence of the martensitic transformation start temperature (Ms) on the applied magnetic field for Ni50−xMn37Sn13Cox alloy ribbons with varying cobalt concentrations (x = 1, 2, 3). The data demonstrates how external magnetic fields influence the thermal stability of the martensitic phase transition in these specific alloy compositions.

caption: GP + NSGA-II multi-objective optimization results displaying 3D Pareto fronts with decision variables mapped by surface roughness (i) and response processing rate (ii).
summary: Utilizing the GP + NSGA-II approach, this panel presents 3D Pareto fronts that visualize the multi-objective optimization of surface roughness, relative density, and processing rate. The plots map decision variables to highlight the distribution of optimal solutions, demonstrating how the GP model navigates the trade-offs between these competing material processing parameters.

caption: Current-voltage (I-V) characteristic curve comparing the experimental data of the RTC-F SPVM FDM with the results obtained via the ADIPSO-VC optimization method.
summary: This I-V characteristic curve demonstrates the performance of the ADIPSO-VC optimization method by comparing its predicted output against experimental data from the RTC-F SPVM FDM. The plot validates the accuracy of the ADIPSO-VC approach in modeling the electrical behavior of the system, highlighting its potential for reliable constraint extraction.

caption: Thermal expansion coefficient profile for a ceramic shell composed of silica sol, zircon powder, and mullite sand.
summary: Thermal expansion characteristics of a ceramic shell fabricated from a silica sol, zircon powder, and mullite sand system are shown. The results indicate that the resin's thermal expansion coefficient is approximately 27 times higher than this ceramic shell material within the temperature range of room temperature to 180 °C.

caption: Representative indentation load-displacement curves demonstrating the mechanical response of the material layers during penetration.
summary: Representative indentation load-displacement curves are presented to characterize the mechanical response of the material. These curves correspond to the nano-hardness measurements of 9.3 ± 0.4 GPa for the major layer and 10.4 ± 0.8 GPa for the minor layer, reflecting the behavior observed at different penetration depths during testing.

caption: Vacancy formation energies calculated for all atomic sites within the Ti-15Zr-5Mo-3Al supercell, where cross symbols represent the average energy values for each constituent element both before and after structural relaxation.
summary: This plot displays the vacancy formation energies for all sites in a Ti-15Zr-5Mo-3Al supercell. By comparing the energy values across different atomic sites, the figure illustrates the energetic landscape of vacancy formation. Cross symbols indicate the average energy values for each element, providing insight into the effects of structural relaxation.

caption: Inverse pole figure and grain boundary distribution maps for HT1 condition specimens subjected to concentric and linear scanning strategies.
summary: Inverse pole figure and grain boundary distribution maps for HT1 condition specimens subjected to concentric and linear scanning strategies. Microstructures in the HT1 condition, annealed at 1000 °C for 2 h, appear similar to as-built counterparts, indicating that residual stresses and stored energy provided insufficient driving force to trigger significant recrystallization.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the quasi-binary Fe-0.21C/xMn system, showing phase stability across a manganese concentration range of 0 to 15 wt%.
summary: This equilibrium phase diagram for the quasi-binary Fe-0.21C/xMn system was calculated using Thermo-Calc software with TCFE11 and MOBFE5 databases. It illustrates phase stability for manganese concentrations between 0 and 15 wt%. The diagram highlights the primary austenitic solidification region and identifies various bcc phases present at lower temperature regimes.

caption: Summary table detailing the microstructure characteristics of T1 alloy resulting from different heat treatment regimes.
summary: This panel provides a structured summary of the microstructural characteristics observed in T1 alloy after various heat treatments. It serves as a reference for correlating specific processing conditions with the resulting material microstructure, which influences the observed mechanical properties such as yield strength, tensile strength, and overall alloy plasticity.

caption: Bright-field TEM image and SAED pattern of the Ni51.2 matrix, identifying it as the B2 austenite phase.
summary: Panel C illustrates the microstructure of the Ni 51.2 matrix. A bright-field TEM image provides visual evidence of the matrix structure, while the corresponding SAED pattern confirms that the matrix consists of the B2 austenite phase, as demonstrated by the diffraction analysis of the deposited sample.

caption: Melt pool monitoring intensity map for a PBF-LB sample processed with a 0.5 mm stripe width.
summary: Displayed is the melt pool monitoring intensity for a sample built with a 0.5 mm stripe width. The color-coded intensity values represent the relative energy input into the material, which is a critical parameter for understanding the melt pool behavior and thermal history during the laser powder bed fusion process.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern corresponding to a different interfacial area than that analyzed in panel (b).
summary: This SAED pattern is conducted to further confirm the phase of the interfacial region between the Cr–C modified C/C substrate and the Cu filler. By analyzing diffraction patterns from various areas, the study systematically identifies the phases formed at the joint interface of the DD3 alloy and composite.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the 450-10 specimen showing the crystallographic orientation.
summary: The 450-10 specimen is characterized by an IPF map to visualize its crystallographic orientation distribution. This map serves as a structural representation of the sample, allowing for the assessment of grain morphology and orientation patterns resulting from the 450-10 heat treatment process applied to the martensitic steel.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns of HP, HPD, and HPDM scaffolds, identifying consistent characteristic peaks and specific regions of differential peak intensity and width.
summary: XRD analysis compares the crystal structures of the HP, HPD, and HPDM scaffolds. The diffraction patterns remain largely consistent across all samples, with minor variations in peak intensity and width. These subtle differences are attributed to the surface modification processes involving polydopamine and Mg 2+ ions on the scaffold surfaces.

caption: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the scaffold surface at the nanoscale obtained via Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM).
summary: Three-dimensional reconstruction of the scaffold surface at the nanoscale is performed using AFM. This analysis enables the evaluation of topographic changes at the nano-level, providing a detailed 3D view of the surface features to further characterize the structural modifications across the different scaffold groups.

caption: Output characteristics of the electronic device measured at a gate voltage of Vgs = -0.2 V.
summary: The output characteristics of the electronic device are presented for a gate voltage of Vgs = -0.2 V. These measurements were conducted across four different scan rates for three sets of devices to evaluate the electrical performance and stability of the fabricated components under controlled testing conditions.

caption: Log-log plot of relative elastic modulus (E*/Es) versus relative density (ρ*/ρs) for AlSi10Mg TPLs, CO, TO, and RCO topologies, benchmarked against reported metal SSLs.
summary: Relative elastic moduli for the AlSi10Mg TPLs are plotted against relative density to evaluate structural performance against established metal SSLs. The results indicate that the TPLs exhibit mechanical properties consistent with reported and experimental SSLs but fall short of exceeding the performance capabilities of conventional strut-based lattice structures.

caption: Detailed Ni2p 3/2 XPS peak deconvolution results for the passive film formed on the SLM-fabricated HX alloy.
summary: Detailed peak deconvolution of the Ni2p 3/2 XPS spectrum provides information on the nickel chemical states within the passive film. This analysis, performed after potentiostatic polarisation at 0.6 V in NaNO3 solution, helps elucidate the surface chemistry of the SLM-fabricated HX material.

caption: Charge-discharge polarization curves for flat and indented metallic bipolar plate VRFB cells operating at a higher current density of 125 mA/cm2 and a convection velocity of 8 mm/s.
summary: Operating at 125 mA/cm2, this panel shows the polarization curves for both cell configurations. Comparing this to the 75 mA/cm2 results reveals that the flat bipolar plate experiences a significant 31% loss in discharge capacity, whereas the indented configuration demonstrates superior stability with only a 12% capacity reduction.

caption: Model-predicted absorbed energy values showing the subtle variations captured by the computational model.
summary: This panel presents the model-predicted values for absorbed energy. It highlights the subtle variations observed in the model's output, demonstrating the sensitivity and precision of the predictive framework in capturing nuanced energy absorption behaviors within the analyzed dataset.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves comparing the thermal degradation profiles of virgin TPU against 35, 40, and 45 wt% CB/TPU filaments.
summary: TGA curves compare the thermal degradation of virgin TPU with 35, 40, and 45 wt% CB/TPU filaments. The analysis reveals no significant change in the onset of degradation temperature, indicating that the incorporation of carbon black does not destabilize the polymer matrix during the thermal decomposition process.

caption: Mott–Schottky plots of C⁻² versus potential for L-PBF 316L stainless steel, illustrating the electronic structure and defect characteristics of passive films formed under varying thermal treatment conditions.
summary: Mott–Schottky plots for L-PBF 316L stainless steel reveal the electronic structure and defect characteristics of passive films formed after different thermal treatments. These plots exhibit a broad flat region from approximately −0.2 V to 0.5 V vs. SCE, providing evidence for the stabilization of the passive layer under these specific potentials.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) distribution map at the 50-50 | IN718 interface, highlighting local plastic strain and crystal defects.
summary: This KAM map visualizes the distribution of crystal defects and local misorientations at the 50-50 | IN718 interface. The results demonstrate a lower density of crystal defects in the 50-50 composition region compared to the SS316L region, consistent with the observed evolution of the grain structure during additive manufacturing.

caption: Confusion matrix for the combined CNN1+CNN2 quality monitoring model, highlighting the classification performance on the testing set.
summary: This confusion matrix evaluates the combined CNN1+CNN2 model on the testing set. By comparing actual labels on the y-axis to predicted labels on the x-axis, the matrix demonstrates the classification accuracy achieved by integrating these two specific models for the quality monitoring task described in the study.

caption: Nyquist plots showing the electrochemical impedance response of TS and DC samples, featuring a capacitive loop at high frequencies and an inductive loop at low frequencies.
summary: Nyquist plots for the examined AA5182 samples exhibit a characteristic capacitive loop at high frequencies followed by an inductive loop at low frequencies. These plots, modeled using an equivalent electrical circuit, characterize the heterogeneous interface and charge transfer resistance, demonstrating the distinct electrochemical behavior of the TS and DC cast samples.

caption: Rate capacity profiles of the 3D-HP Sn-Ni electrode evaluated at varying current densities of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 mA cm-2.
summary: Rate capacity profiles for the 3D-HP Sn-Ni electrode were measured across a range of current densities, specifically 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 mA cm-2. These measurements characterize the electrode's ability to maintain capacity under increasing current loads, demonstrating its performance capabilities under different operational conditions.
