caption: Experimental and simulated stress-strain curves for bio-inspired chiral aperiodic monotile composites and benchmark designs, where solid lines represent experimental data and dashed lines denote simulation results.
summary: Stress-strain behavior of various chiral aperiodic monotile composites is characterized through both experimental testing and numerical simulation. The plot displays the mechanical response of these materials, with solid lines indicating experimental measurements and dashed lines representing simulated results, providing a direct comparison of performance across different design architectures.

caption: High-magnification bright-field STEM image focusing on the morphology of individual nanoprecipitates in the BCC(B2) phase.
summary: High-magnification bright-field STEM imaging provides a detailed view of the nanoprecipitates embedded in the BCC(B2) phase. This panel serves as the basis for subsequent elemental mapping, allowing for a precise characterization of the structural and compositional nature of the precipitates observed within the material matrix.

caption: Smart industry framework illustrating the macro-level interconnection of multiple FSW factories via a centralized digital twin application.
summary: The smart industry framework depicts the macro-level architecture of an FSW Smart Industry. It demonstrates how multiple FSW factories are interconnected through a centralized digital twin application, enabling an autonomous, self-optimizing process that detects anomalies, adjusts parameters adaptively, predicts maintenance requirements, and improves quality through continuous learning within the Industry 4.0 vision.

caption: Schematic representation of the LPBF manufacturing setup featuring a permanent NdFeB magnet positioned beneath the Ti6Al4V alloy substrate to generate a static magnetic field during the fabrication process.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental configuration for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) of a Ti6Al4V alloy. A permanent NdFeB magnet is integrated at the base of the build platform to apply a static magnetic field throughout the fabrication process, providing a controlled environment for studying magnetic field effects on material growth.

caption: Compressive stress-strain curves for Ti55 alloy subjected to various thermomechanical treatments, illustrating the deformation behavior and yield strength characteristics.
summary: Compressive stress-strain curves for the Ti55 alloy are presented across different thermomechanical treatments. These curves provide insight into the material's deformation characteristics and yield strength, allowing for a direct comparison with tensile test data. The results summarize the mechanical response of the alloy under compressive loading conditions.

caption: In situ XANES data comparison for np-Ni 0.001 Cu, Ni 0.001 Cu, and Ni 0.01 Cu nanoparticles after reduction, including a linear combination fitting for the Ni 0.01 Cu sample and Ni foil reference.
summary: In situ XANES spectra highlight the structural differences between various NiCu nanoparticle compositions after reduction. The panel includes a linear combination fitting for the Ni 0.01 Cu nanoparticles to characterize their oxidation state, providing a direct comparison against Ni foil and other nanoparticle variants to elucidate the influence of copper content on nickel electronic structure.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map of the LDED-100 specimen, displaying the columnar grain morphology and crystallographic orientation characteristic of this specific processing condition.
summary: The LDED-100 specimen exhibits a columnar grain structure with preferential growth along the deposition direction, as shown in this inverse pole figure. This visualization confirms that the specific processing parameters used for the LDED-100 condition maintain the characteristic grain morphology observed in the base LDED process.

caption: Temperature versus deflection graph for snap-through buckling, illustrating the determination of buckling temperature via the double tangent method.
summary: This panel displays the temperature versus deflection graph for snap-through buckling. The buckling temperature is identified using the double tangent method. Following initial heating, viscoelastic force regain causes the sample to return toward its original position, while further heating eventually deflects the sample in the opposite direction.

caption: Diamond lattice structure showing the characteristic tetrahedral bonding arrangement of atoms.
summary: The Diamond lattice structure is presented, illustrating the classic tetrahedral bonding arrangement where each atom is connected to four neighbors. This highly stable and rigid structure is fundamental to the properties of diamond and silicon, serving as a key reference for understanding complex, non-cubic lattice architectures.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of a 3D-printed multi-material sample containing Atto425 and Atto465 dyes.
summary: This panel shows the optical transmission spectrum for a 3D-printed sample containing a mixture of Atto425 and Atto465 dyes. This sample is part of the multi-material group excluding Atto565, printed at a 0.5 mm thickness to allow for consistent analysis of transmission properties across different dye combinations.

caption: Definition of the design domain, including specified boundary conditions, applied loads, and structural supports.
summary: The initial phase of the layout optimization process involves defining the design domain boundary and establishing the specific loading conditions and supports. This foundational step sets the geometric and mechanical constraints required for subsequent discretization and structural analysis, as illustrated in the provided schematic representation of the design space.

caption: Fourier-transform infrared spectra of bentonite, kaolinite, and the composite membrane, showing characteristic absorption bands for PA12 including N-H and amide carbonyl vibrations.
summary: FTIR spectra characterize the starting materials and the composite membrane. The PA12 component exhibits distinct N-H absorption bands near 3300 cm-1, along with amide I carbonyl bands between 1630–1660 cm-1 and amide II bands at 1540–1550 cm-1, consistent with established literature data for polyamide structures.

caption: 3D rendering of the GB sample modeled using AVIZO software.
summary: This 3D rendering of the GB sample, modeled using AVIZO software, provides a volumetric visualization of the initial porous structure. By integrating phase-contrast micro-CT data, this reconstruction allows for a detailed spatial understanding of the loosely bound SiC particles within the PR binder matrix.

caption: Ashby plot comparing thermal conductivity versus density for the hybrid aerogel against various existing aerogel materials reported in literature.
summary: This plot compares the thermal conductivity and density of the hybrid aerogel against existing materials from literature. The data indicates that the hybrid aerogels achieve one of the lowest thermal conductivities, particularly when accounting for material density, highlighting their superior performance compared to previously reported aerogel insulators.

caption: Open circuit potential (EOCP) evolution for the heat-treated (HT-NAB) alloy during extended immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: The EOCP curve for the HT-NAB alloy demonstrates the electrochemical response during prolonged exposure to a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. This trend aligns well with the EIS results, providing a consistent evaluation of the alloy's corrosion resistance and electrochemical performance throughout the duration of the immersion test.

caption: Dark-field transmission electron micrograph of the γ matrix, utilizing the 002 diffraction reflection to demonstrate the coherent interface with the M3B2 boride.
summary: Using the 002 diffraction reflection of the γ matrix, this dark-field micrograph provides visual evidence of the coherency between the M3B2 boride and the γ matrix. The imaging confirms that the boride is coherent with the lower side of the matrix, supporting the mechanism of intergranular boride nucleation.

caption: Cu-Ni binary phase diagram at elevated temperatures showing a continuous solid solution without phase separation.
summary: The Cu-Ni phase diagram at elevated temperatures is presented, illustrating the thermodynamic stability of the system in the solid state. As indicated by the reference, this temperature regime does not exhibit any phase separation, confirming the formation of a continuous solid solution across the entire composition range.

caption: As-built strut surface visualization at a relative density of 18.3%, demonstrating the surface topography captured via micro-CT for roughness analysis.
summary: Representing an as-built lattice strut at a relative density of 18.3%, this 3D micro-CT image provides a detailed view of the surface topography. The data allows for the extraction of surface plots, enabling the identification of key roughness contributors like weld lines and semi-fused particles at the pixel scale.

caption: Water contact angle measurements for 3D-printed PCL and composite scaffolds, showing individual data points (purple crosses) and statistical significance (n = 3, *P < 0.05).
summary: Water contact angle measurements were performed to evaluate the hydrophilicity of 3D-printed PCL and composite scaffolds, addressing the inherent hydrophobicity of PCL. The bar chart displays the measured contact angle values, incorporating individual measurement points and statistical significance markers to compare the performance of the different scaffold compositions effectively.

caption: Average molecular structure of the cardanol-based epoxy resin NC-514.
summary: The average structure of the cardanol-based epoxy resin NC-514 is depicted in panel (b). This material is synthesized by curing cardanol-derived epoxy with isophorone diamine and Jeffamine D400 using stoichiometric epoxy–amine equivalence, resulting in a crosslinked polymer network structure suitable for various industrial applications.

caption: EDAX spectrum of the wear scar on the MoS2 composite plate after tribological testing at 25 °C.
summary: The EDAX spectrum provides elemental analysis of the wear scar on the MoS2 composite plate after tribological testing at 25 °C. This spectroscopic data characterizes the chemical composition of the worn surface, supporting the identification of MoS2 particles and potential oxidation products present within the wear track.

caption: 3D areal surface topography map of the C-I sample, illustrating the surface profile characteristics.
summary: 3D areal surface topography map of the C-I sample, illustrating the surface profile characteristics. This 3D representation demonstrates the influence of high VED on the melt pool and surface roughness, revealing how the manufacturing process parameters impact the final surface topography and potential crack formation in the printed sample.

caption: Mirror plot displaying the experimental HRMS/MS spectrum of phenylglyoxylic acid leached from Saremco print CROWNTECH specimens into artificial saliva (top) alongside the reference spectrum of an authentic standard (bottom).
summary: This mirror plot provides a comparative analysis of the HRMS/MS spectrum for phenylglyoxylic acid, a major leachable identified in Saremco print CROWNTECH specimens. By aligning the experimental spectrum from artificial saliva incubation with an authentic standard, the identity of the leachable compound is definitively verified through spectral matching.

caption: Low-magnification Magnetic Force Microscopy image of a Co/Py-thick magnetic antidot array with a 240 nm lattice constant, acquired at a 30 nm lift height.
summary: This low-magnification Magnetic Force Microscopy image reveals the magnetic nanostructure of a Co/Py-thick hexagonal magnetic antidot array with a 240 nm lattice constant. The imaging, performed at a 30 nm lift height, demonstrates how magnetic moments homogeneously depend on the array symmetry due to the pinning effect of the holes.

caption: Mobile amorphous fraction (MAF) as a function of EBA-GMA content.
summary: The mobile amorphous phase fraction is plotted against the EBA-GMA content. The data shows that the MAF quasi-linearly decreased as the function of EBA-GMA content. This panel is part of the comprehensive DSC test results summarizing the thermal properties of the filaments and 3D-printed specimens.

caption: Bead width fitting curve generated by the KNN algorithm at a welding speed of 4.0 m/min.
summary: This panel presents the KNN-fitted bead width at a welding speed of 4.0 m/min. The results indicate that bead width values are maintained near 2 mm at low power levels below 2500 W, followed by a sharp increase in the measured width as power levels rise beyond 3000 W.

caption: Trailing wire tip melting at t = 12 ms, showing droplet growth and arc shortening.
summary: At t = 12 ms, the trailing wire tip is heated and melted by the trailing arc. This heating results in the growth of the droplet, which causes the arc length to become short. This stage mirrors the earlier leading wire behavior, demonstrating the periodicity of the welding process.

caption: Indentation load-depth curves for composites subjected to varying He ion irradiation doses.
summary: Indentation load-depth curves illustrate the mechanical response of composite specimens under different He ion irradiation conditions. These curves provide the fundamental data required to calculate nano-hardness based on the applied load and the resulting indentation area, serving as the primary input for subsequent mechanical property analysis across the irradiated samples.

caption: Magnified bright-field TEM image of the α-Al/Mg2Si microstructure, highlighting nanoscale particles interacting with dislocations within the α-Al phase.
summary: Magnified TEM analysis of the α-Al/Mg2Si eutectic microstructure shows nanoscale particles interacting with dislocations within the α-Al phase. These features, observed within a region approximately 200 nm wide, provide insight into the fine-scale interactions occurring within the melt-pool microstructure during the solidification process of the PBF-LB sample.

caption: Representative load-depth nanoindentation curves comparing the mechanical response of coarse NbC particles and the surrounding γ matrix.
summary: Nanoindentation load-depth curves illustrate the localized plastic deformation resistance of the material. By comparing the response of coarse NbC particles against the γ matrix, these curves provide a quantitative assessment of hardness, highlighting the distinct mechanical behavior of the reinforcing phase relative to the metallic matrix in the alloy.

caption: Mott-Schottky curves comparing the passive film properties of LPBF 316L stainless steel and annealed LPBF 316L stainless steel measured in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This figure displays the Mott-Schottky curves for LPBF 316L stainless steel and its annealed counterpart. The measurements were conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution to evaluate the electrochemical characteristics of the passive films formed on these materials, providing insight into their semiconducting behavior and corrosion resistance properties.

caption: FTIR spectrum of the 3D printed PEEK–HA–Mg2SiO4 composite, illustrating the retention of characteristic functional groups.
summary: The FTIR spectrum of the 3D printed PEEK–HA–Mg2SiO4 composite confirms the retention of characteristic functional groups from both the PEEK matrix and the ceramic fillers. This analysis demonstrates that stable chemical interactions were maintained throughout the thermal processing of the composite material, supporting the structural integrity of the printed samples.

caption: EDS compositional analysis of the as-extruded E1Gd alloy showing the atomic distribution of alloying elements.
summary: Compositional analysis via EDS for the as-extruded E1Gd alloy indicates atomic ratios of approximately 4.01–4.54 at % for Er + Gd and 2.55–2.66 at % for Ni. These results quantify the elemental distribution within the matrix and secondary phases following the extrusion process.

caption: CTE curves for structure E-X measured across different days, where the kinks identified in panel (b) manifest as distinct jumps in the black CTE curve, while the purple curve represents a cycle lacking these jumps.
summary: CTE curves for the E-X structure are compared across different measurement days. The black curve exhibits jumps corresponding to the kinks identified in the ΔL/L0 data, marked by arrows 1, 2, and 3. In contrast, the purple curve, representing a different cycle, does not display these same jumps.

caption: Optical transmission spectrum of commercial CVD correction glasses, showing the filtering performance of EnChroma and Pilestone products.
summary: Transmission spectra for commercial CVD correction glasses, specifically EnChroma and Pilestone brands, are shown in this panel. These measurements provide a comparative benchmark for the wavelength-filtering capabilities of the commercial products against the experimental 3D-printed samples developed in the study.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of 1 mM FcMeOH recorded before and after incubation with faecal pellet supernatant from 18-month-old mice, demonstrating a substantial reduction in current.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry of 1 mM FcMeOH was utilized to detect TNFα in 18-month-old mouse faecal pellets. A substantial reduction in current was observed after incubation with the supernatant, indicating a significantly higher concentration of TNFα compared to the younger age groups previously analyzed in the study.

caption: Impedance modulus (|Z|) plotted against frequency for various scan strategies in borate buffer solution, featuring an inset showing the equivalent electrical circuit used for data fitting.
summary: This Bode plot displays the impedance modulus across different frequency regions for various scan strategies in a borate buffer solution. The data, fitted with an equivalent electrical circuit shown in the inset, provides insights into the electrochemical response and passive layer properties of the system under investigation.

caption: Room temperature tensile stress-strain curves for TC4 titanium alloy samples subjected to various heat treatment regimes following casting and additive manufacturing processes.
summary: This plot illustrates the room temperature tensile stress-strain behavior of TC4 titanium alloy specimens. The data compares different heat treatment systems applied to samples produced via casting and additive manufacturing. These curves provide a comprehensive overview of the mechanical response and performance variations resulting from the distinct thermal processing conditions employed.

caption: ODF map of the middle layer processed at low temperature, illustrating the crystallographic texture distribution within the build.
summary: The ODF map for the middle layer produced at low temperature provides a visualization of the grain orientation distribution. This map is part of the comparative analysis between room temperature and low temperature builds, identifying the specific texture components present in the middle section of the low temperature processed specimen.

caption: Vickers microhardness measurements of LPBFed CoCrMo samples corresponding to variations in layer thickness.
summary: Microhardness values for the LPBFed CoCrMo samples are plotted against layer thickness variations. The results demonstrate a distinct dependence of hardness on the layer thickness, with optimized samples exhibiting Vickers hardness values ranging between 330 and 375 ± 10 HV 0.5, confirming the influence of processing parameters on mechanical properties.

caption: Grain Orientation Spread (GOS) map highlighting the distribution of recrystallized grains within the microstructure.
summary: GOS mapping is utilized to identify and distinguish recrystallized grains from the surrounding deformed matrix. By quantifying the internal orientation spread, this map effectively isolates recrystallized regions, providing critical insight into the microstructural evolution and the extent of recrystallization occurring within the material during processing.

caption: Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) curves for HT1 and HT2 samples measured across the temperature range of -100 °C to 300 °C.
summary: The CTE curves for HT1 and HT2 samples are presented over the temperature range of -100 °C to 300 °C. These curves characterize the thermal expansion properties of the materials, providing a detailed view of how the CTE evolves as the samples are subjected to varying thermal conditions within this specified interval.

caption: Dried spinel crucible fabricated via binder jetting using the Sp_CMg_95_5_S30 composition.
summary: This photograph displays a spinel crucible composed of Sp_CMg_95_5_S30 in its dried state. The specimen was produced using binder jetting technology, representing the initial stage of the manufacturing process before the material undergoes thermal consolidation through sintering to achieve its final refractory properties.

caption: Scatter plot illustrating the relationship between geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density and the percentage of recrystallisation for LB-PBF SS316L samples processed under HT 2 conditions across various wall thicknesses.
summary: This scatter plot demonstrates the correlation between GND density and recrystallisation percentage in LB-PBF SS316L samples subjected to HT 2 conditions. The data indicates that higher GND density does not necessarily promote recrystallisation, as evidenced by the 1.8 mm thick sample, which exhibits high GND density but limited recrystallisation.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of SF cells subjected to a scratch assay, comparing control samples, WD without extract, and WD containing 0.5 wt% PM or PL extracts at 0 and 18 hours, with live cells stained green and dead cells stained red.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images visualize the scratch assay on SF cells, comparing control conditions, WD without extract, and WD with 0.5 wt% PM or PL extracts. Cells are stained with a Live/Dead kit to distinguish between living (green) and dead (red) cells, demonstrating the clear effect of the WD on cell behavior.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation diagram corresponding to a 5% transformed fraction, comparing the thermal stability of cast and LPBF-processed Zr-based bulk metallic glasses.
summary: The TTT diagram, derived from isothermal annealing measurements, characterizes the transformation kinetics of the bulk metallic glasses. The data provides evidence that the laser additive manufacturing process results in lower thermal stability for the Zr-based bulk metallic glass compared to the as-cast material, as indicated by the transformation curves.

caption: Nanoparticle size distribution histogram for the Fe3Ni/CB catalyst determined using ImageJ software.
summary: The nanoparticle size distribution for the Fe3Ni/CB catalyst, determined via ImageJ software, shows a narrow size distribution. This quantitative analysis is consistent with P-XRD results and the STEM-HAADF imaging, confirming that the as-prepared alloy catalysts possess a uniform and narrow particle size range across the sample.

caption: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image focusing on the atomic-scale twin interfaces within the C4 specimen.
summary: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy imaging reveals the detailed atomic structure of the twin interfaces in the C4 material. This panel provides a close-up view of the nanotwins, allowing for the characterization of the interface geometry and confirming the structural integrity of the twin boundaries observed in the sample.

caption: Nano-beam selected-area diffraction pattern obtained from the external NiO particles, confirming their crystalline structure.
summary: Nano-beam selected-area diffraction analysis of the external NiO particles confirms their crystalline nature. By obtaining this diffraction pattern, the study verifies the phase identity of the particles observed in the dark-field TEM images, establishing the presence of NiO within the corrosion product layer formed at 565 °C.

caption: Orientation distribution function maps displaying the crystallographic texture of B2-IMC and austenite phases within the conventional LWS alloy.
summary: Orientation distribution function maps for the conventional LWS alloy demonstrate the crystallographic texture of the B2-IMC and austenite (FCC) phases. These results serve as a comparative baseline to the L-PBF fabricated alloy, showing how conventional laser welding solidification influences the resulting phase orientations and overall microstructural texture of the material.

caption: Gel-melting process represented by the temperature-dependent changes in G' and G" for 0 and 0.9 mM Ca-EMP.
summary: The gel-melting behavior is characterized by the relationship between G' and G". Throughout the process, G" remains higher than G', confirming the weak gel nature of the material. This behavior, combined with spectroscopic data, supports the conclusion that the structure is maintained by limited cross-linking interactions.

caption: Pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram for the Ni–19Co-xAl-8Cr system (0 < x < 50 at.%) calculated via Thermo-Calc, showing a eutectic point E2 at 21.7 at.% Al.
summary: Calculated using Thermo-Calc, this pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram represents the Ni–19Co-xAl-8Cr system with aluminum content varying from 0 to 50 at.%. The addition of 8 at.% Cr shifts the system characteristics, resulting in a defined eutectic point E2 located at 21.7 at.% Al within the specified composition range.

caption: Backscattered electron micrograph and WDS elemental maps of Cu and Mn for sample L 48, revealing weak but visible segregation patterns that were not previously apparent, alongside representative line profiles extracted from the indicated regions.
summary: Sample L 48 displays weak but detectable Cu and Mn segregation, as evidenced by high-resolution WDS mapping. These maps complement previous findings by identifying subtle elemental enrichment at grain boundaries. Quantitative line profiles extracted from the indicated regions further characterize the segregation behavior observed under these specific printing conditions.

caption: Chronoamperometric response curves for FCDI stacks featuring 3D-printed and CNC-milled flow channels, tested with a 15 wt% YP50F electrode concentration during the desalination of 1.5 g/L NaCl solution.
summary: Depicted here are the chronoamperometric curves for FCDI stacks using a 15 wt% YP50F flow electrode concentration. The graph compares the current output across 3D-printed non-conductive, 3D-printed conductive, and CNC-milled graphite flow channels, providing insight into the electrochemical desalination performance of these distinct channel architectures at higher electrode loadings.

caption: XPS spectrum of the Ti 2p region for the Ti felt after corrosion testing, showing the dominance of Ti4+ oxide peaks.
summary: Following corrosion testing, the Ti 2p XPS spectrum reveals that the metallic Ti0 peaks at 459.7 eV and 453.7 eV have significantly diminished. Instead, the spectrum is dominated by Ti4+ oxide peaks at 465.1 eV and 459.2 eV, indicating substantial surface oxidation of the titanium felt during the testing process.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot illustrating the electrochemical response of the Ni-doped Fe-based alloy passive film across various formation potentials.
summary: The Mott-Schottky plot for the Ni-doped Fe-based alloy passive film is displayed for formation potentials of 0, 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 V SCE. These electrochemical measurements allow for the calculation of donor density values from the linear slope, providing insight into the semiconductor characteristics of the film.

caption: Boxplot showing the diameter deviation from nominal values for the top and bottom of the drag cylinders, highlighting that top diameter deviations increase with cylinder size and thickness, while bottom diameters maintain a constant positive deviation.
summary: This boxplot compares diameter deviations from nominal values for the top and bottom of drag cylinders. Results indicate that top diameter deviations scale with increasing diameter and thickness, whereas bottom diameters consistently exhibit a positive deviation, demonstrating distinct geometric behaviors based on the specific section of the cylinder.

caption: Misorientation angle histogram for the 55 mA sample, detailing the distribution of grain boundary misorientation angles.
summary: The misorientation histogram for the 55 mA sample illustrates the distribution of grain boundary misorientation angles in the Ti–10V–2Fe–3Al alloy. This quantitative data is vital for assessing the impact of the 55 mA electron beam current on the grain boundary network and the overall crystallographic texture of the material.

caption: Von Mises stress distributions computed for the N2 fractal lattice with seven layers.
summary: Von Mises stress distributions are visualized for the seven-layer N2 fractal lattice structure. This simulation highlights the stress distribution characteristics that enable the seven-layer design to outperform the five-layer structure, providing a clear view of how the increased layer count influences the internal stress state and mechanical robustness.

caption: Top-view minimum intensity projection of defects for the second sample, highlighting the spatial distribution of irregular blue and rounded brown pores.
summary: Representing the second sample, this top-view minimum intensity projection illustrates the internal defect structure segmented from XCT data. The visualization distinguishes between irregular blue defects and rounded brown defects against the grey solid material, allowing for a comparative analysis of pore morphology and distribution under this specific printing recipe.

caption: Paste light transmittance measurements comparing the clarity of different starch samples.
summary: Paste light transmittance measurements are displayed to evaluate the optical clarity of starch pastes. The results indicate that MSS and MRS samples exhibit lower paste clarity values compared to CRS and WCS, reflecting distinct differences in the light-scattering properties of the starch pastes during the gelatinization process.

caption: Z-axis vertical cutting force profile, acting normal to the workpiece surface, at 65,000 rpm, 3 µm/flute, and 20 µm depth.
summary: The z-axis vertical force, which acts normal to the workpiece surface, is shown for the 65,000 rpm, 3 µm/flute, and 20 µm depth condition. This force magnitude is influenced by tool geometry and material properties, providing critical insight into the mechanical interactions during the LPBF Ti6Al4V micro milling process.

caption: Contour mapping of ELO intensities for the first experiment, captured at layer 359 after powder application and preheating, with isolines representing powder bed heights at 35, 60, 75, and 85 µm.
summary: This contour plot displays ELO intensity mappings for the first experiment at layer 359. By utilizing isolines at 35, 60, 75, and 85 µm, the visualization characterizes the powder bed height distribution across the specimen surface immediately following the powder application and preheating stages of the additive manufacturing process.

caption: Phase-field simulation of Cu-rich phase precipitation in Fe-15at.%Cu-1at.%Mn-1at.%Ni alloy aged at 823 K with magnetic energy contribution (Gm ≠ 0).
summary: This panel displays the phase-field simulation of precipitation in the Fe-Cu-Mn-Ni alloy aged at 823 K, incorporating the magnetic energy term. The blue regions correspond to the matrix, and red regions represent the Cu-rich phase, demonstrating the morphological impact of coupling magnetic energy to the Gibbs free energy during aging.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of CB-OH and CB-Ring, with numbered proton assignments corresponding to specific chemical environments to validate the molecular structure.
summary: The 1H NMR spectra provide detailed structural verification of the synthesized CB-OH and its conversion to CB-Ring. By assigning specific proton types to chemical shifts, the analysis confirms the molecular integrity and successful synthesis of the zwitterionic and cationic forms.

caption: Secondary elemental mapping providing further resolution of the chemical heterogeneity within the stepwise dealloyed precursor structure.
summary: This elemental map provides additional resolution of the chemical heterogeneity within the dealloyed precursor. It supports the identification of the two distinct dealloying stages, illustrating how the composition varies across the reaction zones formed during the 30-second immersion at 973 K in the Mg melt.

caption: Raman spectra comparing GNS, TiC-TC4, and GNS-TC4 composites, showing a reduction in graphene characteristic peak intensity following laser forming.
summary: Raman spectroscopy results for GNS, TiC-TC4, and GNS-TC4 composites reveal that the intensity of graphene characteristic peaks decreases after the laser forming process. This reduction indicates that the content of graphene with a complete structure exhibits a decreasing trend following the thermal processing of the metal matrix composites.

caption: Parity plot comparing experimental creep stress values against predicted results from an S–P model excluding principal component (PC) features.
summary: This parity plot illustrates the predictive performance of an S–P model for SX superalloy creep stress when physical features are used without PC1 and PC2. Compared to models incorporating PCs, the results shown here are notably more scattered, highlighting the reduced accuracy when these statistical features are omitted from the input.

caption: Energy dispersive spectroscopy map illustrating the spatial distribution of Titanium within the 0.25 wt% SiC/Ti6Al4V composite powder.
summary: The energy dispersive spectroscopy map highlights the spatial distribution of Titanium in the 0.25 wt% SiC/Ti6Al4V composite powder. This elemental mapping, conducted after 10 hours of homogenization, confirms the presence and relative uniformity of the primary matrix element within the blended powder particles used for additive manufacturing.

caption: Comparison of experimental and simulated Bragg-edge profiles, with normalized neutron beam intensity shown as a function of wavelength.
summary: Experimental and simulated Bragg-edge profiles are compared to characterize the material's diffraction behavior. The grey scale indicates normalized neutron beam intensity relative to wavelength at the POLDI guide exit, where black and white represent the maximum intensity and the absence of neutrons, respectively, validating the experimental diffraction data against simulations.

caption: Surface structure comparison of TmLacS (6SD0) and KLac (30B8) highlighting the D6 domain in gray and the KLac-specific protruding loop in orange.
summary: This panel illustrates the general surface structure comparison between TmLacS and KLac. The TmLacS structure features an extra D6 domain colored in gray, while the KLac structure displays a distinct protruding loop colored in orange. This structural difference, involving a long loop in KLac spanning residues 425–446, is absent in TmLacS.

caption: Line graph illustrating the correlation between the volume fraction of the beta phase, represented by white lamellae, and the corresponding annealing temperatures.
summary: This line graph displays the relationship between the volume fraction of the beta phase, identified as white lamellae, and the applied annealing temperatures. The data provides a quantitative assessment of how thermal processing conditions influence the microstructural evolution of the beta phase within the material system under investigation.

caption: Tafel slope analysis derived from the LSV polarization curves, illustrating the electrocatalytic kinetics of the different catalyst samples.
summary: Tafel slope values calculated from the LSV curves provide insight into the electrocatalytic kinetics of the synthesized materials. The analysis confirms the superior reaction kinetics of the Ni5P4-Co2P/NCF catalyst compared to the other tested samples, indicating a more efficient pathway for the hydrogen evolution reaction.

caption: Kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps illustrating the local deformation state for as-built (AB), DR1, and DR2 samples, highlighting higher deformation grades in deep-rolled specimens with isolated areas of elevated misorientation in DR1.
summary: Kernel average misorientation maps visualize the local deformation state across as-built, DR1, and DR2 samples. These maps demonstrate that deep rolling significantly increases the grade of deformation compared to the as-built state. Specifically, DR1 exhibits a heterogeneous distribution with isolated regions of higher misorientation above the bounding zone.

caption: Electron charge density profiles calculated through the center of the RTD cross-sections, comparing the baseline 3 nm second barrier thickness with 2 nm and 4 nm variations.
summary: Electron charge density distributions through the center of the RTD cross-sections are presented for different second barrier thicknesses. The simulation results highlight how varying the second barrier width from 2 nm to 4 nm, while keeping the first barrier at 3 nm, influences the internal charge density profile of the device.

caption: Optical microscopy image at 20× magnification showing melt pool boundaries and porosity in a sample subjected to 50% power remelting.
summary: Optical microscopy at 20× magnification reveals the melt pool boundaries and porosity in a sample processed with 50% power remelting. Melt pool boundaries are indicated by double yellow arrows, while porosity is highlighted using dotted white circles and rectangles to characterize the structural features resulting from this specific remelting condition.

caption: Full-range FTIR spectra comparing SMP-10, SMS-992, and the resulting SMP-10/SMS-992 crosslinked hybrid network, highlighting the Si-H stretching vibration at 2130 cm-1.
summary: This panel displays the FTIR spectra of SMP-10, SMS-992, and their crosslinked hybrid network. The presence of the Si-H stretching peak at 2130 cm-1 in both the SMP-10 precursor and the final hybrid system confirms the successful integration of the polycarbosilane component within the crosslinked network structure.

caption: Leo C2C displacement map illustrating the spatial distribution of surface deformation on the curved wall specimen.
summary: The Leo C2C displacement map visualizes the surface deformation of the curved wall specimen. This 3D imaging method successfully detects the displacement of the targeted bulge region, demonstrating the capability of the technique to capture structural changes with specific precision in the analyzed area of the curved wall.

caption: ANOM mean response plot for the material characteristic Cε.
summary: This panel illustrates the ANOM mean response for the material characteristic Cε. By plotting the means across different levels of Cε, the simulation highlights the sensitivity of the thermoelastic response of the Ti6Al4V alloy to this specific parameter, maintaining constant loading conditions and experimental noise levels throughout the analysis.

caption: Raman spectra obtained from the surface of recycled and virgin monolith filaments, showing comparable band widths that indicate similar structural characteristics of the cobalt spinel particles.
summary: Raman spectroscopy was utilized to analyze the surface of recycled and virgin monolith filaments. The resulting spectra reveal that the width of the Raman bands is similar for both sample types, which demonstrates that the cobalt spinel particles possess a comparable structure regardless of whether the monoliths are recycled or virgin.

caption: Reflectance wavelength variation plot for 3D-printed HPCA objects across the tested temperature range.
summary: This plot illustrates the variation in reflected wavelength for 3D-printed HPCA objects as temperature increases. The data confirms the material's stability, showing that while the measured reflectance wavelength decreases slightly, the total variation remains within a 10 nm range, supporting the observed robustness of the printed structure under thermal stress.

caption: Pole figure representation of the random-textured microstructure generated via MATLAB-calculated Euler angles for the polycrystal model.
summary: The pole figure illustrates the random-textured microstructure of the polycrystal model. By utilizing a set of random Euler angles generated in MATLAB, the model achieves a representative texture, ensuring that the simulated polycrystal microstructure accurately reflects the intended random orientation distribution for the subsequent finite element analysis.

caption: Ternary compositional diagram illustrating the weight percentage distribution of ASH-G composite constituents.
summary: This ternary diagram provides a visual representation of the compositional selections for ASH-G composites, expressed in weight percentages. As referenced in the study, this plot serves as a primary guide for understanding the specific material formulations used in the experimental analysis of these composite systems.

caption: Ashby-type performance comparison plot positioning the Silafont®-36 alloy in its three heat-treated conditions against a range of commercial Al-Si alloys.
summary: This Ashby-type plot benchmarks the Silafont®-36 alloy in as-cast, T4, and T7 conditions against various commercial Al-Si alloys. The visualization facilitates a comparative analysis of mechanical properties, highlighting the relative performance of the studied alloy conditions within the broader context of established industrial aluminum-silicon material standards.

caption: Conceptual layout of the short-wave infrared (SWIR) hyperspectral imaging (HSI) system.
summary: This schematic diagram illustrates the configuration of the SWIR hyperspectral imaging system. The setup is designed to enable the capture of reflectance emission from materials within the short-wave infrared range, providing the foundational architecture for the experimental hyperspectral analysis of the composite films described in the study.

caption: Laser microscope image displaying the cross-sectional profile of coupon #4.
summary: This laser microscope image provides a detailed view of the cross-sectional surface morphology for coupon #4. The visualization technique allows for precise examination of the coupon's internal structure and surface integrity, serving as a primary diagnostic tool for evaluating the physical condition of the specimen after processing.

caption: Phase angle plot of Gr/AlNiTiCrNbx coatings as a function of frequency.
summary: The phase angle plot for the Gr/AlNiTiCrNbx coatings illustrates the relationship between the phase shift and frequency. This plot, alongside the Nyquist and modulus plots, characterizes the electrochemical impedance performance of the coatings, providing a comprehensive view of the system's capacitive and resistive behavior.

caption: Density of various metallic materials as a function of temperature, calculated using JMatPro software.
summary: Density values for typical metallic materials are plotted against temperature up to 3000 °C, with aluminum alloys specifically limited to 2000 °C due to their lower melting point. These thermophysical properties were calculated using JMatPro software to illustrate the temperature-dependent behavior of the materials across the specified thermal range.

caption: Bode-phase plots displaying the phase angle response of cladded coatings, where the low-frequency impedance is observed to decrease as the heat treatment temperature increases.
summary: Bode-phase plots characterize the electrochemical response of cladded coatings in a 3.5% NaCl solution. The data indicates that the low-frequency impedance values decrease as the heat treatment temperature of the coatings is increased, highlighting the influence of thermal processing on the electrochemical stability and performance of the cladded material.

caption: Thermodynamic property diagram for the 1 wt.% TiC-reinforced Al–Mg–Li alloy, highlighting the altered solidification sequence where Al3Ti precipitates prior to Al crystallization.
summary: This diagram displays the thermodynamic properties of the 1 wt.% TiC-reinforced Al–Mg–Li alloy. Thermodynamic calculations indicate that the inclusion of TiC particles modifies the solidification sequence, specifically enabling the precipitation of the Al3Ti phase before the crystallization of the primary Al phase occurs during the cooling process.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the HT-1 powder viewed along the [011]β zone axis, revealing diffraction spots corresponding to the ωath phase within the β-Ti matrix.
summary: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the HT-1 powder is captured along the [011]β zone axis. This diffraction analysis confirms the presence of the ωath phase within the β-Ti matrix, providing crystallographic evidence of the phase distribution resulting from the single-step heat treatment process.

caption: Scan rate dependence (5–500 mV s-1) of 1 mM [Ru(NH3)6]3+ in 0.1 M KCl using a 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode, with the corresponding Randles–Ševčík plot shown in the inset.
summary: Benchmarking the 40 wt% CB/TPU electrode via scan rate studies with the outer-sphere redox probe [Ru(NH3)6]3+ allows for the determination of the heterogeneous electron transfer rate constant. The cyclic voltammograms across a wide range of scan rates (5–500 mV s-1) and the linear Randles–Ševčík plot confirm the electrode's electrochemical reliability.

caption: Viscoelastic relaxation profile of the hydrogel over a 100-second interval, showing the experimental data (blue) and the corresponding 2-term exponential decay fit (red) as it transitions from 2.8 × 10^-5 MPa to a long-term value of 2.1 × 10^-5 MPa.
summary: The viscoelastic behavior of the hydrogels was characterized by measuring stress relaxation over a 100-second period. The resulting data was modeled using a 2-term exponential decay function, demonstrating a decrease in stress from an initial 2.8 × 10^-5 MPa to a long-term equilibrium value of approximately 2.1 × 10^-5 MPa.

caption: Evolution of the full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of the 311 diffraction peak as a function of gauge volume position during the additive manufacturing process, with varying gauge volume sizes along the building direction (GV BD) indicated.
summary: Neutron diffraction measurements reveal a gradual decrease in the FWHM of the 311 peak as the number of rescans increases during the build. This reduction in peak broadening, which is indicative of dislocation recovery, highlights the bulk mechanical behavior of the FCC Fe-based alloy throughout the manufacturing process.

caption: Tensile strength-to-cost ratio comparison across different specimen configurations, with dashed lines representing the mean value.
summary: This bar chart displays the tensile strength-to-cost ratio for various specimen configurations. According to the reference, minor differences are observed between the configurations for the Young’s modulus/cost ratio, and the data indicates that the ratios of material properties to costs relate to the respective relative fiber content of the specimens.

caption: Calculated n and k parameters plotted against electronic temperature ranging from 0 to 30,000 K for crystalline alloys at a laser wavelength of 800 nm.
summary: The refractive index and extinction coefficient parameters are presented for crystalline alloys at a laser wavelength of 800 nm. The investigation explores how these optical properties evolve under electronic excitation, providing a detailed view of the material response across the specified electronic temperature range of 0 to 30,000 K.

caption: 1H NMR spectra of QS (bottom) and QSGM1 (top) acquired in D2O, demonstrating the structural changes following the modification of QS with GM.
summary: 1H NMR spectroscopy was utilized to further investigate the synthesis of QSGM. The spectra for both QS and QSGM1 are presented, with the bottom row showing the QS precursor and the top row showing the modified QSGM1. These results provide evidence of the successful chemical modification of the QS structure.

caption: Layer-wise progression of pearlite volume fraction in the 800 W laser-processed sample, showing a monotonic increase from the bottom to the top layers.
summary: This line graph illustrates the layer-wise evolution of pearlite volume fraction in an 800 W laser-processed sample. The data demonstrates a clear, monotonic increase in pearlite content from the bottom to the top layers, which correlates with a decreasing critical cooling rate as the build progresses from Layer 3 to Layer 10.

caption: Orientation Distribution Function (ODF) map of the bottom layer processed at low temperature.
summary: Displaying the bottom layer produced at low temperature, this ODF map completes the analysis of the low-temperature build. It allows for the evaluation of texture consistency across the vertical profile of the sample, highlighting how thermal environment influences the final grain orientation and overall material texture.

caption: X-ray diffraction patterns comparing the NiTi base material, which exhibits B2 austenite phase, and the Ti6Al4V base material, which displays a mixture of α-Ti and β-Ti phases.
summary: X-ray diffraction patterns reveal the phase composition of the base materials. The NiTi base material is characterized by the B2 austenite phase, while the Ti6Al4V base material, in its rolled and annealed state, contains both α-Ti and β-Ti phases, providing a baseline for the subsequent resistance spot welding analysis.

caption: IWP topology shown as a unit cell, a 5 × 5 × 5 periodic lattice, and two stochastic TPMS structural realizations.
summary: IWP topology is depicted as a unit cell, a 5 × 5 × 5 periodic lattice, and two stochastic TPMS realizations. Designed with a 20% relative density in 30 × 30 × 30 mm samples, these structures utilize optimized control points to define the geometry of the periodic and stochastic cellular materials.

caption: Ternary composition plot displaying calculated solidification temperature ranges, with the composition limits identified in panel (a) superimposed to show the relationship between phase fractions and thermal behavior.
summary: Calculated solidification temperature ranges are presented in this ternary plot, which incorporates the composition limits defined in panel (a). This integration allows for the assessment of thermal properties across the composition matrix, facilitating the identification of finer regions for further experimental investigation and high-throughput characterization.

caption: Phase map of the welded joint identifying the distribution of gamma-FCC and epsilon-HCP phases.
summary: Phase mapping across the welded joint confirms a microstructure composed of both gamma-FCC and epsilon-HCP phases. The HAZ and base metal exhibit a higher concentration of the epsilon-HCP phase, indicating that the HAZ underwent no significant chemical changes during welding, consistent with prior light optical microscopy observations of the material.

caption: Live/Dead staining fluorescence images of bioprinted constructs evaluated at 24 hours post-printing.
summary: Live/Dead staining images acquired 24 hours after bioprinting demonstrate that the majority of cells remained viable. This indicates that the entire bioprinting process, including pre-printing crosslinking, extrusion, and post-printing crosslinking, did not negatively impact cell viability, confirming the suitability of the dECM biomaterial ink for 3D cell culture.

caption: Logarithmic plots of relative modulus and relative strength versus relative density, comparing experimental data with the Gibson-Ashby model and other 3D printing technologies.
summary: Logarithmic plots of relative modulus and relative strength versus relative density compare experimental data with the Gibson-Ashby model and other 3D printing technologies. This analysis evaluates the performance of Ti-6Al-4V porous materials prepared via DLP against EBM, SLM, and DIW methods, establishing relationships between density and mechanical properties.

caption: Cell adhesion and morphology on electrodeposited Fe-Cr-Ni samples.
summary: Cell adhesion and morphology on electrodeposited Fe-Cr-Ni samples are visualized to assess biocompatibility. Comparison with stainless steel standards reveals comparable cell adhesion and no visible morphological differences, indicating that the electrodeposited material supports cell growth similarly to conventional AISI 304 and AISI 316L stainless steels used in medical applications.

caption: Optical spectrum of the BOSL device under SLM operation, showing a central wavelength of 1564 nm and an SMSR of 33 dB.
summary: This spectrum illustrates the SLM operation achieved by pumping both the MLL and TISE waveguides. The device demonstrates a central emission wavelength of 1564 nm and a side-mode suppression ratio of 33 dB, confirming the effectiveness of the electrical control mechanism in switching the device state from MLM to SLM.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profile of polycrystalline Alloy 600 oxidized at 350℃ for 15 minutes, showing elemental distribution changes after intermediate exposure.
summary: ToF-SIMS depth profiling of polycrystalline Alloy 600 oxidized at 350℃ for 15 minutes illustrates the progression of oxidation kinetics. This measurement captures the elemental distribution within the alloy surface after an intermediate duration, contributing to the overall understanding of the material's oxidation behavior under these specific thermal conditions.

caption: Simple hatching strategy illustrating the recoater and gas flow directions, with a 60-degree scanning angle and a 67-degree rotation applied between sequential layers.
summary: Simple hatching strategy is depicted for cubic specimens, which were oriented at a 45-degree angle relative to the recoater. The process utilizes a 60-degree scanning angle, with the orientation rotated by 67 degrees for each sequential layer to ensure uniform build-up during the additive manufacturing process.

caption: HE-XRD strain map of the εxy shear component, highlighting localized regions of high shear strain marked by circles within the metallic glass.
summary: The εxy shear strain map shows a relatively uniform distribution across the metallic glass, contrasting with the normal strain components. However, specific areas of high shear strain are identified and marked by circles, which are located in the vicinity of the largest normal strain concentrations observed in the material.

caption: Spatial distribution of iron losses across the specimen cross-section under magnetization aligned with the growth direction.
summary: This heatmap illustrates the iron losses distribution within the material when magnetized along the growth direction. The observed losses are attributed to mechanical separation at the lower face baseline plate and unwanted melting phenomena occurring at the upper face, highlighting the impact of processing conditions on magnetic performance.

caption: Logarithmic plot of minimum creep rate versus applied stress for Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb samples fabricated with three different powder size distributions (PSDs), where the slope of each linear fit represents the stress exponent (n).
summary: This plot illustrates the creep behavior of Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb samples using the power law equation. The stress exponent (n) is derived from the slope of the ln(creep rate) versus ln(stress) curves. Calculated values for n are 5.58 for PSD-A, 7.03 for PSD-B, and 8.55 for PSD-C, indicating varying stress sensitivity.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern of the Ni60 deposited layer, illustrating the crystalline phases present in the material.
summary: The X-ray diffraction pattern of the Ni60 deposited layer is presented to characterize its crystalline structure. This analysis provides essential information regarding the phase composition of the deposited material, confirming the successful formation of the Ni60 layer through the identification of specific diffraction peaks corresponding to its constituent phases.

caption: First-nearest-neighbor (1NN) short-range order (SRO) parameters for nitrogen-metal pairs in Fe70Ni10Cr20 with 1 at.% N, showing a transition from negative to positive values near 800 K.
summary: This plot displays the 1NN N–Cr SRO parameter as a function of temperature for a 1 at.% N Fe70Ni10Cr20 alloy. The data reveals a significant transition from negative to positive SRO values at approximately 800 K, indicating a change in the local atomic ordering behavior of nitrogen and chromium atoms.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves recorded at 50 mV s-1 on a glassy carbon electrode in plating bath 4, demonstrating the effect of 8 and 15 s potential holds on the oxidation peak intensity and width.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry of plating bath 4 on glassy carbon at 50 mV s-1 reveals that holding the potential at the oxidation peak onset for 8 or 15 s causes a progressive decrease in peak intensity, a shift in peak potential, and a reduction in the overall peak width.

caption: STEM micrograph of the heat-treated (HT) specimen, focusing on the morphology of γ′ precipitates located in the dendrite core and interdendritic regions.
summary: The STEM micrograph of the heat-treated specimen illustrates the refined microstructure of γ′ precipitates. By examining both the dendrite core and the interdendritic regions, this panel provides a clear visualization of the precipitate characteristics resulting from the heat treatment process, serving as a comparative baseline for the HT condition.

caption: Isothermal section of the Al–O–Ti system at 1300 °C, showing the phase stability regions.
summary: Representing the Al–O–Ti system at 1300 °C, this isothermal section highlights the phase relationships during cooling. It specifically identifies the three-phase equilibrium region involving Ti3Al(O), TiAl(O), and Al2O3, which correlates with experimental microstructural observations of these phases in TiAl-based systems exposed to alumina environments.

caption: Fluorescent micrograph of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts cultured on Ti6Al4V-15 for 12 hours, showing stained cytoskeletons and nuclei.
summary: Fluorescent imaging of MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts on Ti6Al4V-15 after 12 hours of incubation reveals cell morphology with cytoskeletons and nuclei highlighted in green and blue, respectively. This visualization serves as part of the initial cytocompatibility assessment for 3D-printed fusion cages, illustrating the successful attachment of pre-osteoblast cells on the material surface.

caption: Validation of Ti6Al4V deposition profiles against experimental data.
summary: This panel provides further validation of the numerical deposition profiles for Ti6Al4V. By comparing these results with experimental data, the figure illustrates the effectiveness of the predictive model in replicating the deposition behavior of this specific alloy, contributing to the overall assessment of the numerical simulation framework.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for WA-DED samples subjected to T6 heat treatment and tested at high temperatures.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for WA-DED samples subjected to T6 heat treatment and tested at high temperatures are shown. This plot characterizes the mechanical behavior of the heat-treated material under elevated thermal conditions, highlighting the influence of the T6 process on the tensile performance of the WA-DED samples.

caption: Calculated orientation distribution for martensite variants with positive interaction work (IW) values, displaying poles at [705]M, [12-11 1]M, and [881]M relative to the Y-axis, with color-coded IW values in MPa.
summary: This panel illustrates the calculated orientation distribution of martensite variants with positive interaction work values. Three specific poles, [705]M, [12-11 1]M, and [881]M, are identified relative to the Y-axis. The color-coded spots represent varying interaction work values in MPa, providing a visual representation of the orientation-dependent mechanical response of the martensite.

caption: Time-resolved inductive signals obtained via PIMM at room temperature, featuring a damped sinusoid fit (solid black line) and its corresponding envelope (dotted black line) to determine the damping parameter, with the vertical dotted line marking the initiation of the fit to ensure a small angle of deflection.
summary: This panel displays time-resolved inductive signals measured using PIMM at room temperature. A damped sinusoid fit and its envelope are applied to the grey signal line to extract the damping parameter, frequency, and relaxation time. The fit begins after the signal start to ensure a small angle of deflection.

caption: FT-IR spectra comparison of 3D printed, solvent debound, and thermally debound samples, illustrating the progressive removal of binder components.
summary: FT-IR spectra are compared for as-printed, solvent-debound, and thermally-debound samples. The results demonstrate that solvent debinding effectively removes binder components. Subsequent thermal treatment leads to the complete removal of the binder, as evidenced by the absence of characteristic peaks in the thermally debound sample's spectrum.

caption: Capacity retention of the SC device over 5000 charge-discharge cycles under various mechanical deformation states, including undeformed, 180° twisted, 90° bent, folded, and washed conditions.
summary: This capacity retention plot illustrates the long-term cycling stability of the SC device across 5000 cycles. The data demonstrates consistent performance under diverse mechanical stresses, such as twisting, bending, and folding, as well as after washing, confirming the robust durability and structural integrity of the SC under various operational conditions.

caption: 3D-printed template fabricated using a co-polyester transparent filament via an Ultimaker S3 printer.
summary: The 3D-printed template is shown here, produced using an Ultimaker S3 printer with a co-polyester transparent filament. This material was selected specifically for its high resolution and capability to accurately reproduce the fine structural details required for the monolith's internal channel geometry.

caption: Additional uniaxial tension stress-strain curves for homogeneous materials, representing the mechanical performance of the tested specimens.
summary: Uniaxial tension tests were conducted on standard samples of all materials to determine their mechanical properties. Panel (b) presents the stress-strain curves for these homogeneous materials, complementing the data in panel (a) to characterize the tensile response and mechanical performance of the materials under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: CCK-8 proliferation assay results for cells cultured for 3, 5, and 7 days.
summary: CCK-8 proliferation assay data demonstrates the proliferative activity of cells across three groups over 3, 5, and 7 days. All groups show enhanced proliferative activities as the culture time extends, indicating successful cell growth and viability on the sample surfaces throughout the experimental duration.

caption: Stress-free reference lattice profiles of the {311} plane along the height of the inter-pass rolled wall following SQA treatment.
summary: This panel depicts the stress-free reference lattice profiles for the {311} plane in the inter-pass rolled wall after SQA treatment. The observed data variations illustrate the fundamental challenges associated with determining a representative d0 reference for neutron diffraction in textured, coarse-grained materials, even after post-processing heat treatments.

caption: ODF section at ϕ2 = 45° for recrystallised fcc grains annealed at 725 °C, segmented by grain average misorientation > 0.5°.
summary: The recrystallised fcc micro-texture at 725 °C is shown in this ODF section at ϕ2 = 45°. The orientation distribution is similar to the reverted fcc grains, demonstrating the crystallographic characteristics of the recrystallised fraction after the specified thermal processing and segmentation based on misorientation thresholds.

caption: DSC heating profiles for CMSX-10K alloy specimens subjected to solution heat treatment and primary aging, recorded at 5, 10, and 20 K/min to track the γ′ solvus transition.
summary: Thermal analysis of CMSX-10K alloy samples via DSC heating curves at 5, 10, and 20 K/min demonstrates the phase transformation behavior. The data highlights the transition from the two-phase γ+γ′ region into the γ phase, with the γ′ solvus temperature identified as a reaction occurring before the melting process.

caption: Dislocation glide path at 240 MPa stress with ω = 32, showing dislocation pairs forming super dislocation cores after interface crossing.
summary: At an applied stress of 240 MPa and ω = 32, dislocations move in pairs after crossing the interface to form super dislocation cores. The red arrow marks the emission point, while the external driving force dominates the slip behavior, allowing dislocations to cut into the phase and assemble into superdislocations.

caption: Fluorescence spectra of DEPGM solutions prepared with varying grafting ratios.
summary: Fluorescence spectra are presented for DEPGM at different grafting ratios in aqueous solution. This optical characterization reveals how the chemical modification density affects the emission properties of the polymer, serving as a diagnostic tool to evaluate the consistency and optical behavior of the synthesized DEPGM bioink.

caption: UV-VIS-NIR absorbance spectrum of a PEDOT:PSS solid thin film measured across the 250 to 3000 nm wavelength range.
summary: This panel displays the optical absorbance spectrum of a PEDOT:PSS thin film, captured using a UV-VIS-NIR spectrometer. The data covers a broad spectral range from 250 to 3000 nm, providing a comprehensive characterization of the material's light absorption properties in the ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared regions.

caption: Micro-CT cross-sections of hPLA/PLA interfaces showing (i) PLA printed onto hPLA and (ii) hPLA printed onto PLA, demonstrating consistent layering without significant defects.
summary: Micro-CT cross-sections of the hPLA/PLA interfaces reveal that the materials layered directly onto each other in both printing configurations. The absence of significant imperfections or gaping at the interface indicates good material compatibility, confirming that the two polymers bonded effectively during the additive manufacturing process for both printing sequences.

caption: TGA curves comparing the thermal degradation profiles of printed A-aramid, S-aramid, and aramid fabric in a nitrogen environment.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis was conducted on printed all-aramid materials and aramid fabric under a nitrogen atmosphere. The resulting TGA curves in this panel allow for a direct comparison of the thermal stability and degradation characteristics between the printed samples and the reference aramid fabric material.

caption: Minimal surface geometry enclosed within a pentagonal prism featuring tunnels directed toward its faces (F).
summary: The minimal surface shown is constrained within a pentagonal prism boundary, with tunnels oriented toward the faces of the prism. This configuration demonstrates the boundary method for constructing minimal surfaces, providing a specific geometric arrangement that serves as a building block for the aperiodic F minimal surface.

caption: YQ32-500 T three-beam four-column die closing press used for multi-directional composite loading hydraulic calibration experiments.
summary: The YQ32-500 T three-beam four-column die closing press is shown as the primary experimental equipment. This apparatus is specifically utilized for conducting multi-directional composite loading hydraulic calibration experiments on thin-walled tubes, serving as the foundational machine for the experimental setup described in the study.

caption: Tabulated summary of microstructure characteristics observed in T1 alloy under various heat treatment regimes.
summary: This panel provides a structured summary of the microstructural characteristics resulting from different heat treatment regimes applied to the T1 alloy. It serves as a reference for correlating the observed mechanical property improvements with the specific microstructural changes induced by the various thermal processing conditions described in the study.

caption: 2D scattering intensity I(q) patterns for the five cases, plotted in arbitrary units with the scattering vector defined in the plane.
summary: 2D scattering intensity patterns demonstrate the effect of morphology on SAS signatures. Case 2 displays isotropic concentric rings, while Cases 1, 3, and 4 exhibit anisotropic fourfold symmetry. These scattering features corroborate the symmetry observed in the corresponding 2-point autocorrelation functions, confirming the relationship between microstructure and scattering behavior.

caption: Cracking site in configuration 3, iteration IV, marked by an arrow.
summary: This image highlights the cracking site in a configuration 3 sample during iteration IV testing. The arrow points to the location of the fracture. This result supports the finding that iteration IV exhibits an invariant initial fracture position across configurations 1, 2, and 3 during tensile testing.

caption: Measured reflection coefficient (S11) plotted against frequency for the spherical form FESA.
summary: This panel displays the measured reflection coefficient (S11) for the spherical form FESA. The data represents the electromagnetic performance of the fabricated antenna structure. By comparing these measured results with simulated values, the effectiveness of the spherical design in achieving specific reflection characteristics is clearly demonstrated and evaluated.

caption: Height map visualization of short-beam shear samples, illustrating the resulting waviness pattern across varying sinusoidal wavelengths.
summary: This height map displays the surface topography of short-beam shear samples printed with different sinusoidal wavelengths. The visualization confirms the successful implementation of the waviness pattern, which is generated by the specific motion of the 3D printer, providing a clear view of the structural variations achieved across the printed samples.

caption: Sensitivity analysis of precision metrics regarding Pmax, EPS, and MinP parameters, illustrating the impact of individual factor perturbations on model performance.
summary: This sensitivity analysis evaluates how perturbations in Pmax, EPS, and MinP parameters influence precision metrics. By systematically varying these key factors, the study provides insights into their individual effects on model performance, helping to identify which parameters most significantly impact precision across various detection scenarios within the evaluated system.

caption: Derivative thermogravimetric (DTG) curves showing the rate of mass loss, highlighting the single-stage degradation of LWP and the high-intensity decomposition peaks of PBAT near 400 ºC.
summary: Derivative thermograms reveal distinct degradation stages for the materials. LWP exhibits a single-stage degradation process. In contrast, the PBAT component shows significant decomposition after 325 ºC, characterized by high-intensity peaks near 400 ºC, which correspond to the breakdown of functional groups present within the polymer matrix.

caption: XPS surface analysis of Ti, Ti/EB 0.05, and Ti/EB 0.5 implants.
summary: X-ray photon spectroscopy results identify the chemical composition of the implant surfaces. The peaks were successfully assigned to oxygen (O), phosphorus (P), calcium (Ca), and titanium (Ti). The relative ratios of these elements are presented, providing insight into the surface chemistry of the Ti and EB-modified titanium implants.

caption: Cubic lattice unit cell geometry designed with a relative density of 0.3 and dimensions of 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm.
summary: The cubic lattice unit cell is presented as a fundamental building block for the investigated samples. It features a designed relative density of 0.3 and specific dimensions of 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm, serving as a monolithic structural component in the study of additive manufactured lattice geometries.

caption: Magneto-transport measurement of a CuNi(50)/Py(25) multilayer at 185 K, showing two sharp peaks associated with the coercive field of the Py layer.
summary: At 185 K, which exceeds the 150 K Curie temperature of the CuNi layer, the MTEP measurement for the CuNi(50)/Py(25) multilayer film reveals two distinct central sharp peaks. These peaks correspond specifically to the coercive field of the Py layer, indicating that the CuNi layer remains in a paramagnetic state.

caption: Capacitance variation of the LPBF-718 alloy as a function of frequency, derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data.
summary: Capacitance variation of the LPBF-718 alloy as a function of frequency, derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data. Analysis of these findings suggests that a frequency of 1 kHz is optimal for isolating space charge capacitance from double layer capacitance, facilitating further Mott-Schottky analysis of the alloy's semiconducting properties.

caption: Front view of the LDED specimen showing the initial macroscopic morphology.
summary: This panel displays the front view of a specimen fabricated by laser directed energy deposition (LDED). The image serves as a baseline for comparing the macroscopic morphology of the specimen before any hot-forging treatments are applied, illustrating the initial state of the material surface and overall structural geometry.

caption: Kernel average misorientation map of the subsurface region processed at 3 W laser power, showing an increased thickness of the near-surface softening layer.
summary: At a laser power of 3 W, the kernel average misorientation map illustrates the microstructural state of the subsurface. The observation indicates that increased laser power contributes to a measurable increase in the thickness of the near-surface softening layer compared to lower power conditions, as quantified by local grain misorientation data.

caption: Projected density of states (PDOS) calculated for the Sm0.75Y0.25Ni2 compound.
summary: The projected density of states for the Sm0.75Y0.25Ni2 compound is presented in panel (a). This calculation provides insight into the electronic structure of the material, serving as a baseline for comparing the electronic properties of the substituted alloy system described in the study.

caption: Non-equilibrium solidification simulation of AA2024 waDED material based on the Scheil model.
summary: This non-equilibrium thermodynamic simulation utilizes the Scheil model to predict solidification behavior in AA2024 waDED material, assuming no diffusion in the solid phase or at the solid-liquid interface. The lack of diffusion results in the enrichment of alloying elements within the remaining melt, leading to the formation of Cu-rich segregations.

caption: Dependence plot illustrating the influence of heat treatment parameters on the SHAP values for yield strength predictions.
summary: Representing the influence of heat treatment, this dependence plot demonstrates how specific thermal processing conditions affect the yield strength prediction model. The visualization clarifies the relationship between heat treatment variables and model output, providing insights into how these parameters drive the self-optimization of the additive manufacturing system.

caption: Comprehensive schematic diagram illustrating the experimental apparatus, detailing the integration of gas supply systems, pressure regulation, thermal control, and vacuum components.
summary: This schematic provides a detailed overview of the experimental setup used in the study. It highlights critical components including compressed air and hydrogen cylinders, pressure valves, check valves, a K-type thermocouple reader, a furnace tube, a vacuum pump, and heating control systems, ensuring precise environmental control during the experimental process.

caption: Local magnification of the Nyquist plot highlighting the impedance arc differences between LPBF 316L and R 316L stainless steel specimens.
summary: This magnified view of the Nyquist plot provides a detailed look at the impedance arcs for LPBF 316L and R 316L stainless steel. The data reveals that the XOZ and XOY planes of LPBF 316L exhibit larger capacitive arc radii, indicating higher electrochemical impedance compared to R 316L and YOZ planes.

caption: Model fit results for control, FG-modified, and RG-modified pastes, highlighting the rates of structural build-up observed during the initial 30-minute testing period.
summary: Model fit results for the control, FG-modified, and RG-modified pastes are presented. The analysis indicates that the rates of structural build-up for FG-0.02 and RG-0.02 pastes are considerably higher than those of the control paste, which affirms the enhanced buildability heights achieved through these specific graphene-based modifications.

caption: Time evolution of the critical ice-forming temperature functions Ta (blue) and Tr (red) in degrees Celsius.
summary: The time-dependent functions Ta and Tr are plotted to show the critical ice-forming temperatures in degrees Celsius. By comparing these functions, one can observe how the advancing and retreating temperature thresholds evolve, which directly dictates the oscillation dynamics observed in the corresponding phase plane trajectories.

caption: Ternary oxidation diagram for Ni-Cr-Al alloys showing the superimposed compositions of the tested alloys alongside representative SEM images of the resulting oxide scales.
summary: This ternary oxidation diagram illustrates the oxidation behavior of Ni-Cr-Al alloys as defined by Giggins and Pettit. By superimposing the compositions of the tested alloys, the figure demonstrates that sufficient aluminum content leads to the formation of an external alumina scale, corresponding to the regime III oxidation behavior.

caption: Zoomed-in view of the nanoindentation matrix performed on a powder particle, highlighting specific indentation sites within the matrix.
summary: This panel displays a zoomed-in view of a nanoindentation matrix containing 25 indentations performed on a powder particle. The matrix allows for localized mechanical assessment, with specific areas of interest identified for further analysis regarding the relationship between local microstructure and hardness values within the particle.

caption: Error rate analysis of the SLS-PCCNN-MAGRes-UNet method.
summary: This figure presents an error rate analysis for the SLS-PCCNN-MAGRes-UNet method.
