The visualization illustrates the performance metrics of the proposed simulation approach, providing a quantitative assessment of the model's accuracy and error distribution during the computational process as described in the study's simulation results.

caption: Biexponentially fitted fluorescence decay curve for TPU/3 C composite monitored at 465 nm.
summary: The TPU/3 C composite displays a nonlinear fluorescence decay curve at 465 nm emission. By applying a biexponential fitting function, the fluorescence lifetime is determined, allowing for a detailed assessment of the emission dynamics within the TPU matrix containing 3% coumarin concentration.

caption: Infrared temperature field distribution observed during the machining process.
summary: Represented as an infrared temperature field, this panel visualizes the thermal distribution generated during the cutting experiment. The heatmap highlights the localized temperature gradients across the workpiece and tool interface, offering critical insights into the thermal behavior and heat dissipation characteristics occurring during the CNC machining process.

caption: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the PDAC liver metastasis lesion (GSE197177) showing the distribution of identified cell clusters.
summary: This panel displays a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of a PDAC liver metastasis lesion, sourced from the GSE197177 dataset. The visualization maps the cellular landscape of the metastatic site, providing the necessary spatial and transcriptomic data to compare cell populations with those found in the primary tumor lesion.

caption: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) visualization of NiTi micro-segregation within the alloy matrix.
summary: Scanning transmission electron microscopy provides high-resolution insight into the micro-segregation of Ni and Ti within the WMoTaNbNiTi RHEA. This technique confirms the localized concentration of these elements, which is essential for characterizing the microstructural features that influence the mechanical and thermal performance of the additively manufactured material.

caption: EDS line scan profile across the crack region identified in panel (a), confirming a local concentration of approximately 15 wt% copper.
summary: The EDS line scan provides quantitative compositional data across the crack path observed in the BSE image. The results confirm a local copper concentration of approximately 15 wt%, which aligns with the simulation findings regarding the peak susceptibility to solidification cracking in the IN625-CuCrZr alloy system.

caption: Polarized optical microscopy image of the thermo-mechanically affected zone (TMAZ) in the WAAM+2NFSP sample, showing evidence of multiple pores.
summary: This polarized optical microscopy image focuses on the thermo-mechanically affected zone (TMAZ) of the WAAM+2NFSP processed material. The observation confirms the existence of multiple pores within the TMAZ, consistent with the microstructural characteristics observed in the HAZ, highlighting the localized impact of the processing parameters on material porosity.

caption: Irradiation-induced Frenkel defect pair formation in Cu-10at%Ni alloy, plotted against time for various PKA energies at 300 K.
summary: This plot shows the temporal evolution of Frenkel defect pairs in Cu-10at%Ni alloy under different PKA energy irradiation at 300 K. The results demonstrate the defect density changes over time, reflecting the impact of a 10at% Ni concentration on the radiation response and defect stability within the copper matrix.

caption: STEM image revealing nano-oxide particles within the as-fractured SLM316LSS specimen, characterized by an absence of Mn segregation.
summary: STEM imaging of the as-fractured SLM316LSS specimen reveals the presence of nano-oxide particles. Notably, these particles are observed without associated Mn segregation. This structural feature provides critical information regarding the distribution and chemical nature of oxide inclusions within the laser-melted stainless steel matrix following the fracture event.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of gold nanoparticles with an inset photograph of the cherry red solution.
summary: UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy of the gold nanoparticles shows a maximum absorption peak at 400 nm, which corresponds to their characteristic surface plasmon resonance bands. The inset photograph displays the solution's distinct cherry red color, providing visual confirmation of the successful formation of gold nanoparticles in the colloidal suspension.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of human osteoblasts cultured for 14 days on TCP emulsion (E-DIW) scaffolds, showing cell nuclei, F-actin, and collagen type I.
summary: Human osteoblasts cultured on E-DIW scaffolds for 14 days exhibit cell nuclei, F-actin cytoskeletons, and collagen type I staining. Confocal microscopy reveals that these scaffolds appear to support fewer cells compared to CS-DIW and D-DIW variants, consistent with quantitative findings regarding cell density on these specific printed architectures.

caption: Electron density map of YDy powder with 0.5 at% Dy content, showing the spatial distribution of electron density.
summary: This panel presents the electron density map for YDy powder containing 0.5 at% Dy. By utilizing Fourier series analysis of Rietveld refinement spectra, the map depicts the local electron concentration in e-.Å-3, offering insight into how the crystal structure accommodates the specific Dy dopant concentration within the lattice.

caption: Complete cyclic voltammograms for the CB:30 electrode comparing non-activated and 3-minute activated states in O2-saturated solution, alongside a control scan in N2-saturated solution to identify the hydrogen evolution reaction onset near –1.10 V vs. RHE.
summary: This panel shows complete cyclic voltammograms for the CB:30 electrode in O2-saturated and N2-saturated media. Comparing non-activated and 3-minute activated electrodes reveals performance improvements. The N2-saturated scan highlights the hydrogen evolution reaction occurring at approximately –1.10 V vs. RHE, which is a critical side reaction affecting overall Faradaic efficiency.

caption: Mean fluorescence intensity quantification derived from Calcein AM/PI live/dead staining images at days 1, 3, and 5.
summary: Mean fluorescence intensity measurements from live/dead staining provide a quantitative assessment of cell viability on the scaffold. Consistent with the CCK-8 data, these results show no significant differences in cell viability between the groups at days 1, 3, and 5, further validating the biocompatibility of the scaffold structure.

caption: Full-pattern neutron diffractogram of the as-printed WAAM specimen, showing indexed reflections for the FCC γ-austenite matrix and BCC δ-ferrite phase.
summary: The as-printed WAAM specimen exhibits distinct diffraction reflections corresponding to the FCC γ-austenite matrix and the BCC δ-ferrite secondary phase. Full-pattern Rietveld analysis of this diffractogram estimates the δ-ferrite volume fraction at approximately 6.3%, providing a global microstructural measurement that complements localized microscopy observations of the as-printed material state.

caption: Combined EDX elemental composition map of the ZrB2-20 surface, illustrating the distribution of intergranular phases surrounding the grains.
summary: The combined EDX elemental map corroborates the SEM observations by highlighting the distribution of intergranular phases surrounding the ZrB2 grains. These phases, formed through the solidification of a liquid phase during sintering, are essential for achieving the high density observed in the ZrB2-20 composite microstructure.

caption: Inverse pole figure (IPF) map representing the crystallographic orientation distribution of the as-deposited HNS at the top layer.
summary: This inverse pole figure map illustrates the crystallographic orientation of the as-deposited HNS at the top layer. Obtained via EBSD, the map provides a detailed visualization of the grain structure and texture development within the top region of the material, serving as a baseline for comparing microstructural evolution across different layers.

caption: Bee swarm plot illustrating the distribution of Shapley values for all alloy samples, highlighting the influence of individual alloying elements on predicted yield strength.
summary: This bee swarm plot displays the distribution of Shapley values for all samples, providing a visual representation of feature importance. The analysis reveals that higher concentrations of Si, Mg, and Mn generally correlate with a decrease in the predicted yield strength of the alloy, demonstrating the model's sensitivity to these specific elements.

caption: Pseudo-ternary composition diagram showing the MSAD value distribution for Co-Ni-Cr-Mo MPEAs with 30 at.% Co, within the solvus temperature range of 650–850 °C.
summary: Mapping the MSAD values for Co-Ni-Cr-Mo MPEAs with 30 at.% Co, this diagram illustrates the effect of Co content on lattice distortion within a 650–850 °C solvus temperature range. It completes the series showing the evolution of MSAD values in FCC single-phase MPEAs as the Co concentration is systematically varied.

caption: High-magnification TEM image of nano-precipitates within the L sample.
summary: Detailed TEM imaging of the L sample at higher magnification reveals the specific morphology and spatial arrangement of the nanoscale precipitates. This observation is critical for assessing the precipitate volume fraction and distribution, which are key factors in the material's overall precipitation hardening and strengthening mechanisms.

caption: Glass transition temperature of frontally cured CF tows as a function of compaction force, indicating the thermal stability of the cured resin matrix.
summary: This graph illustrates the glass transition temperature of frontally cured CF tows across various compaction forces. The data provides insight into the thermal properties of the cured resin matrix, showing how the compaction process influences the final thermal performance of the unidirectional CF tows under the specified processing conditions.

caption: Volumetric particle size distribution of ultrasonically atomized 99.9% pure aluminum powders produced at a constant frequency of 60 kHz, comparing results for input power amplitudes of 60%, 75%, and 100%.
summary: This plot displays the volumetric particle size distribution for aluminum powders manufactured via ultrasonic atomization at 60 kHz. By varying the input power amplitudes between 60%, 75%, and 100%, the figure illustrates how processing parameters influence the resulting powder size characteristics, demonstrating the effectiveness of ultrasonic atomization for aluminum powder production.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph and diffraction pattern for Al88Sm4Ni7Cu1 alloy ribbons after reaching the end of the second DSC reaction.
summary: Al88Sm4Ni7Cu1 alloy ribbons, heat-treated to the end of the second DSC reaction, show a microstructure examined through dark-field TEM and diffraction. This structure remains similar to that seen after the first DSC reaction, and XRD patterns indicate that only α-Al nanocrystals are identifiable after isothermal treatment.

caption: TGA results illustrating the weight gain kinetics of the alloys during isothermal exposure at 1100 °C.
summary: At 1100 °C, the isothermal oxidation kinetic curves show a rapid initial increase in weight gain that gradually decreases over time. This temperature highlights the superior performance of JL-1 and JL-2 alloys in high-temperature environments, as they demonstrate lower weight change trends compared to other alloys tested under identical conditions.

caption: Partial electronic density of states for the first neighboring atoms of the site exhibiting the highest vacancy formation energy.
summary: This panel displays the partial electronic density of states (PDOS) calculated for the first neighboring atoms of the site with the highest vacancy formation energy. The data provides insight into the electron orbital distribution at this specific atomic site, facilitating a comparison of electronic states before and after vacancy formation.

caption: Superimposed 1H–13C HSQC NMR spectra of pure CHES (blue) and F-CHES 1 (red) highlighting the chemical signature of the incorporated species.
summary: Panel B presents a comparison between pure CHES and the F-CHES 1 sample using superimposed HSQC NMR spectra. This visualization substantiates the selective incorporation of CHES into the material. The spectral alignment confirms the presence of characteristic CHES signals within the F-CHES 1 structure, validating the synthesis process.

caption: Atomic configuration and charge transfer for a Cl adatom adsorbed at the top site of the NiCr(1) surface.
summary: Depicted is the atomic configuration of a Cl adatom positioned at the top site of the NiCr(1) surface. The visualization highlights the relative charge transfer between the surface Cr atom and the Cl adatom, alongside the resulting surface distortion compared to the clean reference surface.

caption: UV–visible absorption spectra of O-14 and ITX in acetonitrile, highlighting the lower molar extinction coefficient of O-14 (270 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹) compared to ITX (3030 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹) at 395 nm.
summary: The UV-visible absorption spectra in acetonitrile compare the light-harvesting capabilities of O-14 and ITX. The data reveals that O-14 exhibits significantly lower absorption at 395 nm compared to ITX, with molar extinction coefficients of 270 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹ and 3030 L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹, respectively, influencing their performance as photoinitiators.

caption: Raman spectrum of the HEA disc worn surface at 700 °C, revealing V2O5 and Fe2O3 as the main oxidation products.
summary: Raman spectroscopy analysis of the HEA disc worn surface at 700 °C is presented. The spectrum confirms that the main oxidation products formed during sliding wear at this temperature are V2O5 and Fe2O3 oxides, indicating a shift in the oxidation products compared to lower temperature wear conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping of the AMed Al alloy surface, comparing the surface morphology and chemical distribution before and after electron beam (EB) polishing.
summary: This figure presents EDX mapping images of an additively manufactured (AMed) aluminum alloy surface. The visualization compares the elemental distribution and surface characteristics of the alloy in its as-manufactured state versus the state following electron beam (EB) polishing, highlighting the impact of the polishing process on surface composition.

caption: Two-dimensional PCA scatterplot illustrating the clustering of CDF-feature data into four distinct vertical bands along the PC1 axis.
summary: The PCA scatterplot visualizes the CDF-feature data, where k-means clustering effectively partitions the data cloud into four roughly equal vertical bands along the PC1 axis. This representation confirms that the clustering method successfully identifies four distinct groups within the feature space, providing a clear structural overview of the data distribution.

caption: Synchrotron XRD pattern of the fully melted zone in a laser weld with a nickel dilution (D Ni) of 55.3%, showing diffraction peaks associated with the MC carbide phase.
summary: The XRD pattern for the 55.3% nickel dilution fully melted zone demonstrates the structural characteristics of the alloy at higher dilution levels. Consistent with the 30.2% threshold, this pattern confirms the presence of MC carbide phases, illustrating the phase stability and composition changes resulting from the laser welding process.

caption: Impedance magnitude |Z| and angular phase response θ Bode plots for SLM 316L stainless steel samples fabricated at a laser scanning speed of 1000 mm/s following a 15-day immersion period in Locke's solution.
summary: Represented here are the Bode plots for SLM 316L stainless steel processed at 1000 mm/s. The data shows the magnitude of impedance and angular phase response across the tested frequency range, providing insight into the electrochemical stability of the material after 15 days of immersion in Locke's solution.

caption: Mean surface tension values for SFs modified with G, Ti3C2Tx, and G-Ti3C2Tx at concentrations of 0.5, 2, and 10 mg/mL.
summary: Surface tension measurements across the specified concentrations are presented to reveal distinctive alterations in intermolecular forces at the liquid-air interface. The bar chart displays the mean values and standard deviations for SFs with different additives, highlighting how varying concentrations of G, Ti3C2Tx, and G-Ti3C2Tx influence the liquid's interfacial properties.

caption: Arrhenius-type plot showing the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of stress ln[sinh( ασ )] against the inverse absolute temperature 1000/T for calculating the activation energy Q.
summary: This Arrhenius plot depicts the relationship between the natural logarithm of the hyperbolic sine of stress and the inverse absolute temperature. By substituting the slope of this linear fitting curve into the constitutive equation, the activation energy Q is determined to be 981.158 kJ mol −1 for the material.

caption: Bode plot illustrating the impedance response of the 3D printed rectangular Ni electrode measured across a frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 10 kHz.
summary: The Bode plot for the 3D printed rectangular Ni electrode displays the impedance response over a frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 10 kHz. This electrochemical measurement provides insight into the impedance characteristics of the Ni electrode, serving as a baseline for comparison with the Ni-Cu coated electrode.

caption: Comparative S-N fatigue performance plot illustrating the relationship between maximum applied stress and the number of cycles to failure for 3D-printed interfaces across various stress types and surface textures.
summary: This S-N plot evaluates and compares the tension and shear fatigue performance of 3D-printed interfaces. By presenting data for all configurations on a single graph, the figure allows for a direct assessment of how different surface textures influence the fatigue life and stress-bearing capacity of the printed components.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the S0 sample aged at 350 °C for 300 min, revealing the presence of primary Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the S0 sample aged at 350 °C for 300 minutes reveals the morphology of primary precipitates. These structures are identified as Al3(Sc,Zr) phases, which are part of the three main precipitate types observed at the peak-aging condition within the aluminum matrix.

caption: Immunofluorescence staining of host macrophages in 400, 600, and 800 μm scaffolds at 2 weeks post-implantation, showing DAPI-stained nuclei, INOS-positive M1 macrophages, and ARG1-positive M2 macrophages.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining reveals the host macrophage response to scaffolds of varying pore sizes two weeks after implantation. By visualizing DAPI, INOS, and ARG1, the images demonstrate that the scaffolds effectively recruit and induce macrophage differentiation, thereby influencing the immune microenvironment under complex in vivo conditions.

caption: Atomic representation of a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell constructed from a Zeolite ID 9590293 unit cell.
summary: This panel presents the atomic structure of a 3 × 3 × 3 supercell generated from a Zeolite ID 9590293 unit cell. The conversion process was performed using VESTA software, demonstrating the systematic approach to building larger zeolite supercell models from specific unit cell precursors as part of the modeling framework.

caption: Ortho view of the standard Octet lattice model.
summary: The ortho view of the standard Octet lattice model provides a baseline for comparing the structural geometry of the bio-inspired R-Octet metamaterials. This model serves as the reference point for evaluating the effects of introducing rotational degrees of freedom into the lattice architecture.

caption: Immunofluorescent staining of CD31 and VEGF markers in femoral slices at 21 days post-implantation.
summary: Immunofluorescence staining of CD31 and VEGF in femoral slices at 4 weeks confirms enhanced angiogenic activity. The PLA/GA/MgCu-MOF group shows substantially higher expression of these angiogenic markers compared to control groups, consistent with the observed improvements in vessel maturity and density within the implanted scaffolds.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis curves used to quantify the inorganic component mass fractions within the various piezoelectric scaffolds.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis is employed to quantify the inorganic component amounts within the various piezoelectric scaffolds. This thermal characterization provides essential data on the composition and stability of the materials, allowing for the precise determination of the inorganic mass fractions present in the final scaffold structures.

caption: Visual representation of the fracture morphology observed in the tensile specimen post-failure.
summary: Fracture characteristics of the tensile specimen are illustrated to provide insight into the failure mechanism. Analyzing these fracture surfaces is essential when evaluating mechanical properties, as they offer direct evidence of the material's integrity and response to stress when correlated with the corresponding stress-strain and strength data.

caption: Velocity field distribution corresponding to the thermal parameter λT.
summary: This panel illustrates the velocity field distribution influenced by the thermal parameter λT. The visualization highlights how variations in this specific parameter impact the overall velocity profile within the system, providing a clear representation of the thermal effects on fluid or material flow dynamics as described in the study.

caption: Approximation of a sharp crack into a diffusive region of width lc, where the phase field damage variable Φ represents the transition from intact to damaged material.
summary: The panel demonstrates the regularization of a sharp crack into a diffusive region of width lc using a phase field damage variable Φ. This approach allows for the mathematical representation of crack evolution within the system's total energy formulation, effectively approximating discrete fracture behavior through a continuous damage field.

caption: Brightfield STEM micrograph of EBM-processed material subjected to ER cycling at a mechanical strain amplitude of 0.8% until failure at 186 cycles.
summary: This brightfield STEM micrograph displays the microstructure of EBM-processed material following ER cycling at a mechanical strain amplitude of 0.8%. The specimen reached failure at 186 cycles. This imaging technique was utilized to investigate the microstructural state of the material under these specific thermomechanical fatigue loading conditions.

caption: Force-time histories for monocoque and sandwich structures with 3D-printed carbon fiber skins and polyurea foam cores under 15 m/s impact.
summary: Force-time histories for monocoque and sandwich structures with 3D-printed carbon fiber skins and polyurea foam cores are shown under 15 m/s impact. The curves exhibit a brief linear onset, a plateau phase, a rapid peak force increase, and a final descent, highlighting the dominant elastomeric behavior of the polyurea foam cores.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry curves for the bracelet prototype sensor across ketamine concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 5 μg/ml.
summary: Cyclic voltammetry analysis of the 3D printed wearable bracelet prototype demonstrates the sensor's response to varying ketamine concentrations from 0.01 to 5 μg/ml. A direct relationship is observed between the peak current values and the logarithm of the ketamine concentration, confirming the sensor's sensitivity to the target analyte.

caption: Pie chart displaying the proportional contribution of strengthening mechanisms to the yield strength of the IN718-0.5GNP composite.
summary: This pie chart presents the strengthening mechanism contributions for the IN718-0.5GNP composite, which exhibits a solid-solution strengthening increase of 270 MPa. It completes the series by showing the distribution of strengthening factors at the highest GNP concentration, facilitating an analysis of how reinforcement loading affects the overall mechanical strengthening profile.

caption: DIC strain distribution map of the vertical as-built specimen deformed at 600 μm crosshead displacement.
summary: The DIC strain map for the vertical as-built specimen at 600 μm displacement reveals high strains exceeding 10% locally at the melt-pool boundaries. This strain localization was more pronounced in the vertical specimen compared to the horizontal orientation, contributing to the preferential fracture observed along these specific melt-pool boundary regions.

caption: Nyquist plot showing the impedance spectra of TC4 titanium alloy after heat treatment, characterized by an increased arc radius of the bulk reactance.
summary: Following heat treatment, the Nyquist plot displays an increased arc radius of the bulk reactance compared to the sedimentary state. This change indicates improved corrosion resistance and enhanced uniformity of the overall tissue composition across different regions of the TC4 titanium alloy sample, as evidenced by the reduced impedance variations.

caption: Current transients of Fe-Ni co-deposition under ultrasonic conditions at step potentials ranging from -0.8 V to -1.7 V.
summary: These current-time transients illustrate Fe-Ni electrodeposition under ultrasonic conditions. Unlike static conditions, the current decay is minimal and remains stable at identical step potentials. This stability suggests that ultrasonic agitation significantly influences the deposition process, preventing the rapid current decay observed in the absence of external mechanical stimulation.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern obtained from area Q of the interface.
summary: Selected area diffraction pattern obtained from area Q of the interface. This diffraction data, in conjunction with STEM-EDS mappings, confirms that the thin layer at the interface is primarily composed of the FeAl phase with a B2 crystal structure, providing critical evidence for the phase identification within the analyzed region.

caption: Creep strain evolution for AA2195-T3 alloy plotted against applied stress, with yellow and blue regions indicating linear elastic and nonlinear stress-strain regimes, respectively, and dashed lines representing strain ratios relative to the rolling direction.
summary: AA2195-T3 alloy exhibits creep strain evolution under applied stresses of 120, 160, and 200 MPa. These values fall entirely within the linear elastic stress-strain range. The plot highlights anisotropic deformation behavior through creep strain ratios for 45° and 90° orientations relative to the rolling direction, showing monotonic trends in elastic regions.

caption: Process window for 180 µm layer thickness showing the most restricted manufacturability range.
summary: Depicting the highest tested layer thickness of 180 µm, this plot reveals a significantly restricted process window. Successful manufacturing is only achieved at very high laser powers and low scan speeds. This highlights the extreme parameter constraints required to maintain structural integrity when processing thicker layers in this additive manufacturing setup.

caption: Time-dependent absorption spectra of O-14 recorded during photolysis experiments using a 365 nm LED light source.
summary: This panel illustrates the absorption spectral evolution of O-14 during photolysis. Despite having a lower molar extinction coefficient at 365 nm compared to O-16, O-14 demonstrates a higher photocleavage ability after 240 seconds of irradiation, confirming its efficient performance as a photoinitiator under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Separation force required to detach the cured ceramic slurry layer from the PDMS membrane, plotted against different solids content levels.
summary: Separation forces required to detach the cured ceramic slurry layer from the PDMS separation membrane are shown for different solids contents. This mechanical test quantifies the adhesion strength between the slurry and the membrane, providing critical data for optimizing the slurry formulation in the manufacturing process.

caption: Superimposed isothermal ternary phase diagram of the primary elements in IN625 alloy at 600 °C, highlighting distinct corrosion product regions.
summary: This isothermal ternary phase diagram at 600 °C maps the corrosion product regions for IN625 alloys. Region I corresponds to Cr2O3 and nickel-rich sulfide formation in as-built and HT-I alloys, while Area II represents the mixture of NiO, Cr2O3, CrS, and NbS1.6 observed in HT-II and forged specimens.

caption: STEM-BF-S micrograph and corresponding EDS elemental maps of the as-built material, demonstrating the detection and distribution of in-situ formed TiB2 particles.
summary: STEM analysis confirms the presence of in-situ formed TiB2 particles within the as-built material. The micrograph, combined with STEM-EDS elemental mapping, provides a detailed visualization of the highlighted area, allowing for the identification and spatial distribution analysis of these specific reinforcement particles within the aluminum matrix.

caption: Number average molecular weight (Mn) of PCL scaffolds as a function of immersion time in PBS at 47 °C, reflecting the degradation kinetics of the polymer chains.
summary: Number average molecular weight (Mn) evolution is tracked over 18 weeks of immersion in PBS at 47 °C. The data confirms that the hydrolytic bulk degradation mechanism of PCL is successfully replicated, leading to a consistent reduction in molecular weight while maintaining the overall shape of the polymeric fibers.

caption: Electron localization function (ELF) distribution map for the β-Ti (110) surface.
summary: ELF distributions for β-Ti (110) are constructed based on crystal structure information via first-principles calculations. In contrast to α-Ti, the valence electrons in β-Ti are more localized. This electronic configuration reflects a less active electron state, which is associated with stronger metallic bonding characteristics in the β-Ti phase.

caption: Plastic energy dissipation (PED) at perforation for the lattice core, skin, and sandwich structures, evaluated against core cell size.
summary: Plastic energy dissipation (PED) at the point of perforation is compared for the lattice core, skin, and sandwich structures as a function of core cell size. This bar chart highlights the variations in plastic energy absorption, providing insight into how structural geometry affects the dissipation mechanisms during high-velocity impact.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of the third Ni-based nanocomposite coating, highlighting grain growth patterns.
summary: This inverse pole figure map characterizes the grain growth patterns in the third Ni-based nanocomposite coating. Consistent with the other coatings, the grain types are nearly identical, demonstrating that the layered structure does not significantly alter the fundamental grain orientation characteristics of the Ni-based nanocomposite material.

caption: Time evolution of argon species concentrations under low-pressure plasma conditions at 200 W and 1 slm flow rate.
summary: This plot illustrates the time-dependent concentration of argon species in a low-pressure plasma environment. Under these conditions, microwave energy excites argon into higher energy states, specifically Ar* and Ar+. Analysis reveals that Ar+ becomes the dominant species, followed by neutral Ar and excited Ar* states throughout the evolution process.

caption: Polarization curves illustrating the electrochemical response of substrate, EAM, and ECM surfaces.
summary: Polarization curves are displayed for substrate, EAM, and ECM surfaces to characterize their corrosion behavior. These curves illustrate the relationship between current density and potential, providing essential insights into the anodic and cathodic kinetics of the materials under test conditions, which is critical for assessing their overall electrochemical performance.

caption: Dissipated energy of HPC specimens calculated from the area under the load-displacement curve during compression testing up to approximately 10% strain.
summary: This plot illustrates the energy dissipation characteristics of lattice reinforced concrete specimens under compressive loading. By calculating the area under the load-displacement curve, the total energy dissipated by both the concrete matrix and the reinforcement is quantified, providing a comprehensive view of the material's performance until reaching a strain of 10%.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram of triangular Ni electrodes, evaluating electrochemical performance in alkaline media within a -1.2 V to 1.2 V range.
summary: Triangular Ni electrodes were evaluated for electrochemical activity in alkaline media using cyclic voltammetry. The T3 geometry configuration achieved a current density of -10.11 mA/cm2 at -1.2 V, showing performance characteristics consistent with other geometries tested under the same potential range of -1.2 V to 1.2 V.

caption: X-ray diffraction pattern obtained from the fracture surface of the specimen.
summary: This X-ray diffraction pattern provides a detailed analysis of the phase composition present on the fracture surface of the material. By examining the diffraction peaks, the study characterizes the crystalline phases existing at the fracture site, offering insights into the material's structural integrity and phase distribution following mechanical failure.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy image of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to extracts from milled Ti.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy imaging of Human Gingival Fibroblasts after 24 hours of exposure to milled Ti extracts is presented. Utilizing Live/Dead staining, the image displays the ratio of live (green) to dead (red) cells, providing insight into the biocompatibility of the milled titanium material under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) image of the 0° sample at 25% strain, where color gradients from blue to red indicate increasing residual plastic strain.
summary: Representing the local plastic strain distribution, this KAM image reveals that the 0° sample undergoes severe plastic deformation throughout the entire observed region after 25% tensile strain. Blue regions signify minimum residual strain, while red regions highlight areas of maximum strain accumulation resulting from the deformation process.

caption: Charge-discharge curves of a-Ge thin-film at various current rates, illustrating electrochemical response at high densities.
summary: Charge-discharge curves for a-Ge thin-film are displayed at different rates. When the current density increases to 10 A g-1 and 20 A g-1, the capacity of the a-Ge thin-film is 1233 mAh g-1 and 1013 mAh g-1, respectively, demonstrating better rate stability than pure a-Si.

caption: UV–Vis absorption spectrum of the AuNP-modified castor oil, featuring a characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak centered at 535 nm.
summary: The UV–Vis absorption spectrum for the AuNP-modified castor oil solution is presented, revealing a distinct absorption peak centered at 535 nm. This peak is characteristic of gold nanoparticles and shows good agreement with established literature, confirming the presence and successful synthesis of the colloidal gold nanoparticles within the oil.

caption: Two-dimensional PCA scatterplot illustrating the clustering of CDF-feature data into four distinct vertical bands along the PC1 axis.
summary: The PCA scatterplot visualizes the clustering of CDF-feature data, revealing that k-means effectively partitions the data cloud into four roughly equal vertical bands along the PC1 axis. This representation confirms the successful identification of four distinct clusters within the dataset through the applied machine learning methodology.

caption: EPMA elemental map illustrating the spatial distribution of Zirconium (Zr) within the cross-section of the coated specimen.
summary: Zirconium distribution is captured in this EPMA elemental map, revealing a uniform presence of Zr within both the outer and inner layers of the coating. This consistent distribution suggests that Zirconium participates significantly in the formation of the observed boride phases throughout the treated alloy cross-section.

caption: Schematic representation of the ultrasonic-assisted TW-DED-arc system used for fabricating the TiAl-4822 alloy, illustrating the integration of the TW-DED-arc unit and the UHFP current system.
summary: This schematic illustrates the experimental configuration for the ultrasonic-assisted TW-DED-arc fabrication process of TiAl-4822 alloy. The system architecture integrates two primary functional components: the TW-DED-arc system and the UHFP current system, which work in tandem to facilitate the current-assisted additive manufacturing process for this specific intermetallic material system.

caption: EPMA elemental maps of Fe, Cr, Ni, Mn, Si, S, P, and O for recycled 316L stainless steel powder.
summary: Recycled 316L stainless steel powder displays pronounced elemental segregation within the particle interior compared to the virgin state. EPMA mapping confirms a noticeably higher oxygen concentration, which is present both at the particle surface and throughout the interior, highlighting significant chemical changes resulting from the recycling process.

caption: Initial and healed fracture toughness values represented as means ± SD for all 3D printed groups.
summary: Initial and healed fracture toughness values are shown as means ± SD for all 3D printed groups. This comparison highlights the material's ability to recover mechanical properties after a fracture event, providing insight into the healing efficiency of the tested composites.

caption: Molecular structure of PEGMA monomer.
summary: This panel depicts the chemical structure of the PEGMA monomer. The representation provides the molecular configuration necessary for understanding the chemical composition of the material system used in the study, serving as a fundamental building block for the polymer synthesis described in the research context.

caption: Precipitate mean length distribution of Al3Sc in Al-Sc alloy calculated via PRISMA® simulation.
summary: This panel displays the precipitate mean length distribution for Al3Sc in an Al-Sc alloy, derived from PRISMA® simulation. The data illustrates how heat-treatment temperatures influence precipitate size, with higher temperatures expected to yield a greater dispersion of precipitates, reflecting the coarsening behavior observed during the simulation process.

caption: Cross-sectional morphology and elemental distribution map of the oxide scale on a ground HVOF NiCrAlY coating after 100 h of isothermal oxidation at 1050 °C, showing a uniform mono-layer structure.
summary: Ground HVOF NiCrAlY coatings develop a distinct, uniform mono-layer structured oxide scale after 100 hours of oxidation at 1050 °C. This contrasts with other surface treatments, as the ground surface promotes the formation of small, uniform grains rather than the complex multi-layered oxide scales observed in the other coating conditions.

caption: Live/dead staining images of hBMSCs cultured on 3D-printed hydrogel strands after 24 hours of incubation.
summary: Live/dead staining images reveal that hBMSCs adhere effectively to the 3D-printed hydrogel strands after 24 hours of incubation. The cells exhibit a flattened morphology, indicating good biocompatibility and successful cell attachment on the hydrogel surface within the specified culture period.

caption: Aggregated confusion matrix illustrating the performance of a k-nearest neighbor classifier at k=5 for droplet type prediction.
summary: This aggregated confusion matrix evaluates the k-nearest neighbor classifier at k=5 for droplet type prediction. The model demonstrates perfect classification of no-droplet types and achieves a 99% accuracy rate for normal droplets, representing a notable improvement over the 98% accuracy previously observed with the k=3 classifier configuration.

caption: Chemical composition comparison of TR-316L and LPBF-316L stainless steel alloys expressed in weight percentages.
summary: This table presents the chemical composition of TR-316L and LPBF-316L stainless steel alloys, detailing the weight percentages of their constituent elements. The data provides a direct comparison of the elemental makeup between the two processing conditions, serving as a foundational reference for the material properties investigated in this study.

caption: STEM micrograph displaying the fine rosette microstructures within the as-printed alloy, accompanied by elemental distribution maps for the region highlighted by the yellow square.
summary: STEM imaging reveals the presence of fine rosette microstructures in the as-printed alloy. These subtle features are further characterized by elemental distribution maps within the specified region. The micrograph provides a clear visualization of the alloy's morphology, serving as a basis for understanding the intermetallic distribution within the printed material.

caption: Lasso regression chart illustrating the relative influence of various FE model parameters on the resulting melt pool profile.
summary: Lasso regression analysis identifies the sensitivity of the melt pool profile to specific model parameters. The results demonstrate that efficiency and mass flow rate exert the dominant influence on the melt pool geometry, providing a quantitative basis for prioritizing these variables during the subsequent model calibration and refinement stages.

caption: Molecular weight distribution profile for Sinovial® solution, 10x diluted in PBS and filtered through a 0.2 µm membrane, with an orange marker denoting the 1 MDa threshold.
summary: Sinovial® molecular weight distribution is presented as a histogram for a 10x diluted, 0.2 µm filtered solution. SEC-SLS chromatography was utilized to determine molecular weight moments and polydispersity. The distribution is scaled specifically for this substance to highlight size variations, with an orange indicator marking the 1 MDa reference point.

caption: Bode plot detailing the impedance modulus and phase angle measurements for the X-Y section of the Wall 1 sample.
summary: Depicted here is the Bode plot for the X-Y section of the Wall 1 sample. The impedance modulus begins at approximately 10⁴ Ω·cm², aligning with the general electrochemical behavior of the Wall 1 specimen. This measurement contributes to the comprehensive analysis of the sample's impedance across different spatial orientations.

caption: H2-TPR profiles of SRM catalysts, illustrating the reduction behavior of HEA/GDC compared to Ni/YSZ and Ni/GDC.
summary: H2-TPR analysis evaluates the chemical interaction between metal and support in SRM catalysts. The profiles reveal that the HEA/GDC catalyst requires a higher reduction temperature than Ni/YSZ and Ni/GDC, indicating distinct chemical interactions between the metal and the support material during the reduction process.

caption: Spin-polarized density of states for the La1.25Gd0.25Mg0.5Ni7 phase, showing distinct contributions from two spin channels.
summary: Spin-polarized density of states for the La1.25Gd0.25Mg0.5Ni7 phase are shown with red and blue lines representing two distinct spin channels. The electronic structure exhibits the characteristic two main maxima at -1 eV and -2.5 eV, which are primarily associated with the Ni 3d orbitals in this complex composition.

caption: Comparison of experimental creep strain data for the SR-2-R1 IN617 specimen at 780 °C and 200 MPa against physics-based model simulations with varying grain boundary viscosity parameters.
summary: This plot compares experimental creep strain data, derived from SR-2-R1 stress relaxation tests, with physics-based model simulations for IN617 at 780 °C and 200 MPa. The results demonstrate that the model reasonably predicts primary creep behavior, while highlighting the sensitivity of initial creep rates and saturation to grain boundary viscosity assumptions.

caption: Distribution of minor axis radii for LPBF-fabricated Ti-xFe alloys, determined via ellipse fitting of EBSD grain data.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the minor axis radii of grains in LPBF-fabricated Ti-xFe alloys, derived from EBSD ellipse fitting. A significant reduction in grain size is observed with the addition of 0.1 wt% Fe, demonstrating that minor axis dimensions decrease markedly compared to the base alloy composition.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the AB sample showing high-density entangled dislocations within the cellular structure.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the as-built (AB) sample reveals high-density entangled dislocations distributed both inside and along cellular boundaries. These features result from significant thermal residual stress generated during the fabrication process, with a higher concentration of dislocations observed specifically at the cellular boundaries.

caption: Equilibrium phase mole fractions for the base HEA calculated across a temperature range of 750 °C to 1400 °C.
summary: This CALPHAD diagram illustrates the equilibrium phase evolution for the base HEA between 750 °C and 1400 °C. The analysis identifies specific transition points, noting that the γ solidus temperature is 1263 °C and the γ′ solvus temperature is 1116 °C for the Ni30Co30Fe13Cr15Al6Ti6 alloy composition.

caption: Nanobeam diffraction pattern of the Al2Gd phase in GA102K, demonstrating high periodicity and elevated crystallinity.
summary: Nanobeam diffraction analysis of the GA102K alloy confirms the high crystallinity of the Al2Gd secondary phases. The resulting pattern is highly periodic, which directly supports the observation of improved structural order within the precipitates compared to the GA101K alloy under the same processing conditions.

caption: Fracture morphology of specimen #1, showing the surface state under initial ultrasonic power conditions.
summary: Specimen #1 displays the fracture surface morphology resulting from the application of ultrasonic power. Similar to the baseline specimen #0, this panel provides a visual assessment of the fracture surface, contributing to the comparative analysis of how varying ultrasonic power levels influence the presence of large-sized pores within the deposited material.

caption: MALDI-TOF mass spectrum of PEB236 synthesized without a coinitiator, showing a series of peaks corresponding to the composition {(C15H26O4)n + Na}+ from n = 3 to n = 14.
summary: The MALDI-TOF spectrum for PEB236, synthesized without a coinitiator, displays a series of peaks representing the polymer composition {(C15H26O4)n + Na}+. These peaks range from n = 3 at m/z 833 g/mol to n = 14 at m/z 3807 g/mol, confirming the polymer structure and end-group composition.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of dislocation loops in SLM 316L stainless steel.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the SLM 316L stainless steel sample shows dislocation loops formed under irradiation. Compared to the TM sample, the SLM 316L stainless steel exhibits a lower overall defect density at the peak damage area, with no voids observed in the analyzed TEM micrographs.

caption: Cycling stability data for compositions #0, #4, #16, and #17 over 50 cycles.
summary: Cycling stability data for compositions #0, #4, #16, and #17 demonstrate the long-term performance of the cathode materials. Specifically, compositions #16 and #17 show robust performance, retaining capacities of approximately 124 mAh/g and 156 mAh/g, respectively, after 50 cycles, highlighting their potential for stable electrochemical energy storage applications.

caption: Long-term cycling stability of Zn||MnO2 full cells at a constant current density of 0.5 A g−1.
summary: Long-term cycling performance of the Zn||MnO2 full battery is tested at 0.5 A g−1. The cell with 1% SL electrolyte exhibits superior capacity compared to the additive-free battery, successfully delivering approximately 120 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles, demonstrating improved stability and capacity retention over the extended cycling period.

caption: XPS spectra of the ACBF/APTMS/Co0/Ni0 composite following the absorption of Co2+/Ni2+ ions and subsequent in-situ reduction to metallic states.
summary: Panel (c) presents the XPS spectra of the material after the absorption of Co2+ and Ni2+ ions followed by an in-situ reduction process. This data characterizes the final chemical state of the Co0/Ni0 species on the ACBF/APTMS substrate, confirming the successful reduction of the chelated metallic ions.

caption: Hardness profile of the CDFW specimen featuring a schematic overlay of distinct microstructural zones.
summary: Hardness testing results for the CDFW specimen are presented alongside a schematic classification of its microstructural zones. This visualization maps the mechanical response across the material, providing a clear correlation between the identified microstructural regions and the corresponding hardness values measured during the testing process for this specific specimen.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the IC31H dislocation network within the gamma channels near the fracture surface, captured under a two-beam condition with g = [-20-2].
summary: This bright-field TEM image displays the dislocation substructure within the gamma channels of IC31H after creep at 1200 °C/80 MPa. Captured under a two-beam condition with g = [-20-2], it reveals a dense, irregular network of interfacial dislocations, including cuboidal and hexagonal meshes, used to determine the Burgers vectors.

caption: Remanence Br values for synthetic microstructures with and without GB-phases versus SEM-digitized microstructures.
summary: Remanence Br is shown to be affected by the microstructural configuration. The data compares synthetic microstructures, both with and without GB-phases, against those digitized from SEM-photomicrographs. This plot highlights how the inclusion of specific microstructural features, such as the GB-phase, directly impacts the remanence values of the magnetic material.

caption: Top-down view of the as-built C5 cylinder specimen showing the internal pore distribution.
summary: This panel displays a top-down micro-CT view of the as-built C5 cylinder. The visualization highlights the internal pore distribution within the sample, providing a baseline for assessing the effectiveness of subsequent hot isostatic pressing treatments on the material's structural integrity and overall porosity levels.

caption: Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) profiles of flexible supercapacitors measured at current densities of 20 mA g-1 and 18 mA g-1 under various twisting angles.
summary: Galvanostatic charge-discharge profiles illustrate the electrochemical performance of flexible supercapacitors. Analysis was conducted at current densities of 20 mA g-1 and 18 mA g-1 to evaluate the impact of different twisting angles on the device behavior, highlighting the stability and response of the electrode-electrolyte system under mechanical deformation.

caption: Calculated continuous cooling transformation (CCT) plot for 316L stainless steel, derived using JMAT Pro 7.0 based on specific chemical composition ranges for C, Cr, Ni, Mo, Si, and Mn.
summary: This CCT plot provides a theoretical estimation of phase transformations during the cooling of 316L stainless steel. By utilizing JMAT Pro 7.0 software and the specified chemical composition, the diagram serves as a predictive tool to understand phase evolution and stability during the thermal processing of the material.

caption: Orientation difference distribution histogram for the 304 stainless steel base metal.
summary: This histogram presents the orientation difference distribution for the 304 base metal. Included in the broader assessment of base metals and weld metal, this plot quantifies the crystallographic orientation relationships present in the 304 alloy, facilitating a detailed comparison of microstructural features across the different zones of the welded joint.

caption: Inverse Pole Figure (IPF) map relative to the Z-direction for a sample dynamically deformed at a strain rate of 2150 s⁻¹.
summary: This IPF(Z) map shows the grain orientations for the highest strain rate condition of 2150 s⁻¹. It exhibits the most significant degree of plastic deformation and grain fragmentation among the tested samples. Consistent with the other maps, this microstructure shows no signs of adiabatic shear band formation despite the high strain rate.

caption: Comparison of XRD patterns for 18Ni300 samples aged at 380 °C and 480 °C, revealing no significant differences in the diffraction profiles between these two aging temperatures.
summary: This panel compares the XRD patterns of 18Ni300 samples aged at 380 °C and 480 °C. The results indicate that there is no significant difference in the diffraction profiles between these two aging temperatures, suggesting that the phase composition remains stable within this specific range of heat treatment conditions.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves illustrating the thermal degradation behavior of rPLA-based composites across varying weight percentages.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis curves illustrate the thermal degradation behavior of rPLA-based composites across varying weight percentages. Analysis of these curves, alongside DTG data, reveals that neat rPLA exhibits an onset degradation temperature of 325 °C, a maximum decomposition temperature of 365 °C, and a relatively low char residue of 0.5%.

caption: Isothermal section of the Ni–Cr–Mo system at 1573 K, illustrating the equilibrium between the γ phase, liquid (L), and P phase, with evidence of phase separation (L → L1 + L2) occurring above this temperature.
summary: The isothermal section at 1573 K reveals the equilibrium relationships between the γ phase, liquid, and P phase. Experimental findings indicate that the γ + P two-phase region is situated between the γ + L1 and γ + L2 regions, suggesting that liquid phase separation occurs at temperatures exceeding 1573 K.

caption: Grain size distribution histogram for HT-18Ni300 steel, indicating an average grain size of 2.6 μm.
summary: This histogram depicts the grain size distribution for the HT-18Ni300 steel, which exhibits an average grain size of 2.6 μm. The data indicates a slight increase in average grain size compared to the SLM-18Ni300 condition, reflecting the microstructural changes induced by the applied heat treatment process.

caption: Comparison of density fluctuation profiles along the building direction between the simulation model (black line) and experimental SXCT data.
summary: The plot compares the density fluctuation evolution along the building direction of the sample during sintering. The model results, represented by a black line, are compared against experimental data. The comparison indicates that the model effectively replicates the density increases and the evolution of fluctuations observed during the sintering process.

caption: Ni K-edge XANES spectra for Ni/SiO2-CS and Ni/CeOx-CS catalysts after reduction at 300 °C.
summary: The Ni K-edge XANES spectra illustrate the oxidation state of nickel catalysts during in-situ reduction at 300 °C. Comparing Ni/SiO2-CS and Ni/CeOx-CS reveals distinct spectral features corresponding to different reduction behaviors, providing insight into the chemical environment and metallic fraction of the nickel species supported on these specific substrates.

caption: Alignment visualization generated by CloudCompare, overlaying a reference 15 mm cube with the STL file derived from the optical scan of the printed geometry.
summary: This panel illustrates the alignment process performed using CloudCompare software. A reference 15 mm cube is superimposed onto the STL geometry obtained from the optical scan. This comparison serves as the basis for evaluating the dimensional accuracy and geometric deviations of the printed sample relative to the intended design.

caption: Tan δ (damping factor) curves for pure PLA, PLA + EtLa, and PLA-based nanocomposites containing cCNC, illustrating the effect of surface chemistry on interfacial interactions.
summary: The tan δ (damping factor) curves are plotted against temperature to evaluate the influence of surface chemistry on the interaction between the PLA matrix and cCNC fillers. Examining the tan δ peak provides insight into the interfacial dynamics and damping characteristics of the various PLA-based nanocomposite formulations.

caption: Macroscopic cross-sectional view of the U960 sample showing the distribution of the δ phase.
summary: This macroscopic cross-sectional view of the U960 sample illustrates the distribution of the δ phase. High-density precipitates are observed forming on the surface, with a measured precipitation depth of approximately 230 μm, providing a clear visual representation of the phase distribution within the UR sample cross-section.

caption: Magnetization versus magnetic field (M-H) curves for the 0Co sample, recorded under pulsed magnetic fields across a temperature range of 4.2 to 280 K.
summary: The 0Co sample exhibits temperature-dependent magnetization behavior under pulsed magnetic fields between 4.2 and 280 K. These M-H curves characterize the magnetic response of the material, and the area enclosed by these loops is utilized to calculate the energy dissipation (E dis) for the sample across the measured temperature range.

caption: Monte Carlo uncertainty distribution for the Global Warming Potential (GWP) of rapid investment casting (RIC) calculated from 1000 simulation runs.
summary: This Monte Carlo uncertainty distribution for rapid investment casting (RIC) is based on 1000 simulation runs. In contrast to the other processes, the RIC distribution is comparatively narrow and near-symmetric, indicating a more stable and predictable GWP outcome under the evaluated input uncertainties.

caption: Contour plot displaying the contact width response surface for a layer height of 2.5 mm, varying with deposition speed and extruder rotation.
summary: Representing the contact width at a 2.5 mm layer height, this contour plot highlights the relationship between deposition speed and extruder rotation. It serves as a tool to analyze response surfaces under specific input parameter combinations, helping to identify optimal process conditions and understand the sensitivity of the contact width to these variables.

caption: EBSD recrystallization map of the T1 alloy following HT-1 heat treatment, illustrating the resulting grain morphology transformation.
summary: Following the HT-1 heat treatment, the T1 alloy exhibits a modified grain morphology. The EBSD map highlights the degree of recrystallization, with blue indicating recrystallized grains, yellow denoting incomplete sub-structures, and red marking original tissue. This distribution reflects the structural evolution induced by the specific HT-1 thermal processing conditions.

caption: STEM micrograph of the as-built AlSi10Mg alloy sample after tensile deformation, showing extensive dislocation density near the cell wall boundaries.
summary: Captured after tensile deformation, this STEM image illustrates the significant accumulation of dislocations within the as-built AlSi10Mg microstructure. The high density of GNDs concentrated around the cell walls is a key feature, facilitating the kinematic hardening effect observed in the alloy during mechanical loading.

caption: Absorption coefficients of the graded, uniform, and linear-gradient TPMS structures, illustrating the broadband performance improvement achieved by the optimal design.
summary: Absorption coefficients are plotted for the three TPMS structure profiles to evaluate their broadband performance. The data shows that the optimally graded structure achieves superior absorption compared to the uniform and linear-gradient profiles, confirming the effectiveness of the optimized porosity design for the 30 mm thick material.

caption: XRD traces for isothermally oxidized diffused Pt coatings at 1100 °C, where superlattice reflections indicate high γ′-Ni3Al volume fractions.
summary: Diffused Pt coatings subjected to isothermal oxidation at 1100 °C exhibit high γ′-Ni3Al volume fractions. XRD patterns show distinct superlattice reflections, confirming the prevalence of the γ′ phase. This structural state is established prior to oxidation, as Pt segregates preferentially to the γ′ phase, influencing the overall phase composition of the coating.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves comparing bare NiTi and O2-treated samples (O2-0.4-300, O2-0.8-300, and O2-1.2-300) in SBF solution at 37 °C, highlighting the anodic branch behavior.
summary: This plot displays the potentiodynamic polarization behavior of bare NiTi and various O2-treated samples in SBF solution at 37 °C. The anodic branch of the bare NiTi curve reveals the formation and subsequent breakage of a passive layer occurring at a potential of 606 mV vs. Ag/AgCl.

caption: B-scan image of a specimen with a 1 mm subsurface defect, acquired by detection laser (1), featuring a polarity reversal at the right edge.
summary: Acquired using detection laser (1), this B-scan shows a 1 mm subsurface defect. Dashed lines delineate the defect edges, while a red arrow indicates a polarity reversal occurring specifically at the right edge of the defect, demonstrating the sensitivity of the ultrasonic signal to localized subsurface structural discontinuities.

caption: Core-loss EELS spectra of the Fe L2,3-edges obtained from points 1 to 7, showing complete overlap of the spectral features across the boundary region.
summary: Core-loss EELS spectra for the Fe L2,3-edges were collected from the same seven points used for the Cr analysis. The resulting spectra exhibit complete overlap with each other, indicating that the electronic environment of iron remains consistent across the measured points despite the observed changes in elemental concentration.

caption: SCC growth behavior comparison for AM SS 316L in uncrystallized (650 °C), partially recrystallized (955 °C), and fully recrystallized (HIP + SA) states, tested in X-Z orientation.
summary: SCC growth behavior is evaluated across different microstructural states of LPBF SS 316L, including uncrystallized, partially recrystallized, and fully recrystallized conditions. The fully recrystallized HIP + SA samples exhibited the best performance, highlighting the significant influence of heat treatment and recrystallization on the stress corrosion cracking resistance of the material.

caption: Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) patterns of Zn alloy surfaces following a 16-day immersion period in simulated body fluid (SBF) at 37 °C.
summary: Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) patterns characterize the thin corrosion films formed on Zn alloy surfaces after 16 days of immersion in SBF at 37 °C. This technique effectively detects surface corrosion layers that are too thin for conventional XRD, confirming the presence and formation of specific phosphate corrosion products.

caption: Relevant section of the Ni-Sn binary phase diagram, highlighting the master alloy composition and the homogenization temperature set at 700 °C.
summary: This panel displays the relevant portion of the Ni-Sn binary phase diagram. It specifically marks the master alloy composition and the homogenization temperature of 700 °C, providing the thermodynamic context for the thermal processing of the sample as described in the study's experimental methodology.

caption: Anisotropy index of elongation for Ti6Al4V alloys, illustrating the effect of B and N additions on mitigating directional mechanical property variations.
summary: Assessing the tensile strength increment and elongation anisotropy, this panel evaluates the relative strength normalized to pristine Ti6Al4V alongside the anisotropy index. The data demonstrates how B and N additions effectively mitigate elongation anisotropy, providing a quantitative measure of the mechanical improvements achieved through these specific alloying modifications in Ti6Al4V.

caption: Mean Squared Error (MSE) performance metric for height deviation prediction using a model trained with three input features.
summary: This panel displays the Mean Squared Error (MSE) performance metric for height deviation prediction models. The evaluation utilizes a model architecture configured with three input features to assess predictive accuracy. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the model in minimizing error for height variations as shown in Fig. 11.

caption: Band gap energy plot derived from optical measurements of the Ti-WO3 film.
summary: The band gap energy of the Ti-WO3 film is determined through optical analysis. This measurement is a critical component of the optical property characterization, providing insight into the electronic structure and light-harvesting potential of the deposited film as investigated in the study of its material properties.

caption: Comparison of transmittance spectra for 10 mm thick CD-16 glass samples before and after the 3D printing process, with Fresnel losses included in the measurements.
summary: This plot compares the transmittance of casted CD-16 glass against the 3D printed element for 10 mm thick samples. The results demonstrate that the 3D printed glass exhibits lower transmittance compared to the initial casted glass, indicating a reduction in optical performance following the printing process.

caption: Envelope-processed EMG signal waveform recorded during the book-holding action.
summary: The envelope-processed EMG signal waveform for the book-holding action is displayed, representing the refined data used to evaluate the device's performance. This processed signal allows for a clear assessment of the muscle activity involved in maintaining the hold, providing a basis for comparing signal quality across different methods.

caption: Thermographic temperature distribution map of the sample top surface at 6000 s.
summary: Thermographic imaging captures the temperature distribution on the sample top surface at 6000 s. This measurement is part of a series monitoring the process, where temperatures recorded just before laser scanning were observed to be nearly consistent with the target thermal conditions throughout the experimental duration.

caption: WDS elemental mapping of Aluminum (Al) distribution within the PS 3 coating cross-section, highlighting distinct segregation patterns.
summary: The WDS elemental map for Aluminum reveals clear signs of segregation within the PS 3 coating. This distribution pattern is linked to the formation of Al2O3, as confirmed by analyzing SEM micrographs and elemental mappings. The mapping effectively captures the localized concentration of Al, which is not restricted to splat interfaces.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetization curves for Fe52.5Cr45.55Ni1.95 under a 100 Oe field, comparing Zero-Field-Cooled (blue rectangles) and Field-Cooled (red circles) protocols, with the green line indicating their difference and the black line showing the first derivative of the FC data.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic response of the Fe52.5Cr45.55Ni1.95 alloy by comparing ZFC and FC magnetization curves measured at 100 Oe. The data highlights the thermal evolution of magnetization, while the calculated difference between curves and the first derivative of the FC data provide further insight into the magnetic transition behavior.

caption: Steady-state dislocation configuration characterized by significant pile-up at the grain boundaries.
summary: In this stage of the simulation, the dislocations reach a steady-state condition. The atomic model clearly displays the pile-up of these dislocations at the grain boundaries, demonstrating the tendency of the polycrystalline material to accommodate structural defects at these interfaces throughout the fatigue deformation process.

caption: Inverse pole figure map illustrating the crystallographic orientation distribution of the WAAM specimen.
summary: The inverse pole figure (IPF) map for the WAAM specimen is displayed, providing a visualization of the crystallographic orientation distribution within the material. This map serves as a primary characterization tool to analyze the grain structure and texture development resulting from the wire arc additive manufacturing process.

caption: Storage modulus and tan δ curves of a printed dense A-aramid sample, showing a modulus drop to 3.35 GPa at 330 °C.
summary: The DMA analysis of the dense A-aramid sample reveals a storage modulus that decreases to 3.35 GPa at 330 °C, representing half of its initial value at 30 °C. Notably, the material exhibits stable mechanical performance within the temperature range of 360 to 420 °C, demonstrating its thermal resilience.

caption: ζ-potential analysis comparing 0 and 0.9 mM Ca-EMP samples to evaluate surface charge density changes.
summary: This bar chart illustrates the ζ-potential analysis used to evaluate changes in the surface charge density of EMP samples. By comparing 0 and 0.9 mM Ca-EMP, the data highlights how calcium concentration influences surface charge, with significant differences indicated by lowercase letters (p < 0.05) across the tested conditions.

caption: UV-Vis absorption spectra of the gold nanoparticle solutions used for reference.
summary: The absorption spectra for the gold nanoparticle solutions are provided as a baseline for comparison. These reference measurements allow for the characterization of the gold nanoparticles independent of the hydrogel matrix, facilitating a clearer understanding of the spectral features observed in the gold-loaded contact lenses.

caption: Maximum bending force plotted against the A core /A tot ratio for 316L-Al2O3 filaments sintered at 1350 °C, including average values for pure alumina and steel reference filaments.
summary: This scatter plot illustrates the peak force achieved during bending tests as a function of the core-to-total area ratio. It compares individual 316L-Al2O3 composite filaments against average values for monolithic alumina and steel filaments. The data demonstrates how the metal core ratio influences the mechanical load-bearing capacity of the sintered filaments.

caption: Inverse pole figure map of Ti-12Mo deformed at 860 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹.
summary: This panel shows the deformed microstructure of Ti-12Mo alloy at 860 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹. Compared to higher strain rates, this condition resulted in larger subgrains. The vertical orientation indicates the compression axis, providing insight into the grain evolution and size distribution under these specific high-temperature deformation parameters.

caption: Bode plots showing the impedance magnitude as a function of frequency for PEO coatings after 24 hours of immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: The Bode plot illustrates the impedance magnitude response of PEO coatings after 24 hours of exposure to a 3.5% NaCl solution. This frequency-dependent data provides insight into the electrochemical behavior of the oxide layer, serving as a key component in the analysis of the coating's corrosion resistance properties.

caption: Surface optical micrograph of the untreated 6 h mechano-synthesized Al72Cr15Ni13 specimen following the CPDP corrosion test in 3.5% NaCl electrolyte.
summary: This optical micrograph displays the surface morphology of an untreated 6 h mechano-synthesized Al72Cr15Ni13 specimen after undergoing a CPDP corrosion test in a 3.5% NaCl electrolyte. The image reveals the distribution of corrosion pits resulting from the electrochemical exposure, highlighting the material's susceptibility to localized anodic degradation in saline environments.

caption: Hardness squared (H^2) plotted against the inverse of indentation depth (1/h) for Al-doped Ti3SiC2 specimens.
summary: This plot presents the relationship between the square of the nanohardness (H^2) and the inverse of the indentation depth (1/h, in 1000/nm). This representation is used to analyze the indentation size effect and mechanical properties of the Al-doped Ti3SiC2 specimens, providing insight into the material's deformation characteristics.

caption: Apparent Poisson's ratio as a function of axial strain for thin and thick-hinge structures at a slow strain rate of 5 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹.
summary: Apparent Poisson's ratios measured at a slow strain rate of 5 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ indicate highly negative values at small strains, confirming the auxetic nature of the samples. The near-zero initial elastic Poisson's ratios identified in quasi-static conditions highlight the unique mechanical response of these structures under the specified loading rate.

caption: Electrochemical profiles including cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential for 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation at a C/10 rate.
summary: Depicted here are the electrochemical characteristics of 2D tape-casted NMC622 electrodes during delithiation. The plot tracks cell potential, open-circuit voltage, and entropic potential as functions of lithium composition. Consistent with the 3D printed counterpart, this cell shows very small overpotential and hysteresis, indicating reliable performance for the tape-casted electrode configuration.

caption: ANOVA analysis of glass transition temperature (Tg) values across varying TPU percentages in PLA blends.
summary: This panel presents an ANOVA analysis evaluating the statistical significance of TPU content on the glass transition temperature (Tg) of PLA-based materials. The box plot illustrates the distribution and variance of Tg results, providing a clear visual assessment of how different TPU concentrations influence this specific thermal property.

caption: Reflectance spectrum of HPCA at DS = 1.0, showing the longest reflected wavelength.
summary: This reflectance spectrum for HPCA at DS = 1.0 displays the optical response at the highest degree of substitution. The wavelength increases significantly, reaching up to 775 nm, which correlates with the near-invisible structural color observed in the corresponding photograph.

caption: Molecular dynamics simulation of the heat and quench process for aluminum using the Farkas interatomic potential, highlighting the material's tendency toward amorphization.
summary: This molecular dynamics simulation illustrates the heat and quench process applied to aluminum using the Farkas interatomic potential. The visualization focuses on the material's tendency toward amorphization during the cooling cycle. Although amorphous states are generally metastable, this specific potential is utilized to investigate structural evolution under rapid thermal processing conditions.

caption: Lateral cervical radiographs showing the successful implantation of cages between the C3/4 and C4/5 vertebrae at 0, 3, 6, and 12 weeks postoperatively, with no observed migration or dislocation in the Ti and Ta groups.
summary: Lateral cervical radiographs demonstrate the successful surgical implantation of cages between the C3/4 and C4/5 vertebrae. Observations at 0, 3, 6, and 12 weeks postoperatively confirm that the implants remained stable, with no instances of migration or dislocation detected in either the Ti or Ta experimental groups.

caption: Pseudo-binary section calculated for the AlCrFeNi system, derived from experimental chemical compositions of BCC and B2 phases to predict phase stability.
summary: The pseudo-binary section provides a theoretical framework for understanding the phase evolution in the AlCrFeNi alloy. It was calculated using experimental chemical compositions of the BCC and B2 phases. This diagram successfully predicts the presence of a eutectic structure observed in the grain boundary regions of the as-cast alloy.

caption: Elemental distribution map showing the spatial arrangement of Cu.
summary: Elemental distribution mapping of Cu illustrates its spatial localization within the material. As shown by STEM/EDS analysis, this map helps identify the presence of specific phases, such as the θ (Al2Cu) precipitate, by correlating the copper distribution with the structural features observed in the corresponding TEM images.

caption: Tabulated design parameters for the AST configuration, specifically detailing the geometric specifications for diameter ratios of 0.36, 0.4, and 0.44.
summary: This table presents the comprehensive design parameters utilized for the AST experimental test. It specifically outlines the geometric configurations corresponding to diameter ratios of 0.36, 0.4, and 0.44. These parameters serve as the foundational specifications for the experimental setup, ensuring consistent testing conditions across the varying diameter ratio configurations.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the coefficient of friction for LPBF and wrought Ti6Al4V alloys under a cathodic potential of -1 V vs. SCE.
summary: This plot illustrates the coefficient of friction evolution over time for both LPBF and wrought Ti6Al4V alloys during sliding tests conducted at a cathodic potential of -1 V vs. SCE. The data provides a comparative view of the frictional behavior of these two distinct alloy processing conditions under electrochemical influence.

caption: Compositional distribution of Ni versus Mn content for nominal, ribbon, powder, and as-built N and O samples, overlaid on established stability regions for 10M, 14M, and NM martensite crystal structures at room temperature.
summary: This plot illustrates the Ni and Mn content for various Ni-Mn-based samples, including nominal, ribbon, powder, and 3D-printed N and O specimens. By comparing experimental SEM/EDS data against established stability ranges for 10M, 14M, and NM martensite phases, the graph identifies the structural phase characteristics of each material condition.

caption: Force–time response of the Gyroid TPMS topology subjected to low-speed impact penetration using a 20 mm hemispherical indenter at 220 J.
summary: Gyroid TPMS topology performance is illustrated through force-time curves obtained from three repetitions of low-speed impact penetration tests. Utilizing a 20 mm hemispherical indenter at 220 J, the data captures the dynamic mechanical behavior and force evolution of the Gyroid structure during the impact event in the SET-A series.

caption: Average microhardness values measured at the top, middle, and bottom sections of Non-IPM, IPM200, IPM300, and IPM400 thin-walled parts.
summary: This figure presents the average microhardness values across three distinct vertical positions—top, middle, and bottom—for four different thin-walled part configurations: Non-IPM, IPM200, IPM300, and IPM400. These measurements characterize the mechanical consistency and hardness distribution within the thin-walled structures, providing a comparative analysis of the different processing conditions.

caption: Wind rose pattern recorded during the testing period from 15:10 to 16:30, indicating the prevailing wind direction.
