caption: Optical micrograph of the Ti6242 alloy cross-section processed via DED at the B scan speed condition.
summary: Optical micrograph of the Ti6242 alloy cross-section processed via DED at the B scan speed condition. Similar to the A scan speed condition, this region shows no visible defects like lack of fusion, strain-age cracks, or microcracks, indicating consistent material quality across the tested processing conditions.

caption: AA cross-section view during the reverse rotation stage of the BPR from 0.8 s to 1.6 s.
summary: This panel illustrates the rotations of ω 1 and ω 2 during the BPR movement from 0.8 to 1.6 s. By t=1.6 s, solid dielectrics of various colors, representing different layers, are shown gradually depositing onto the AA plane of the gray layer, highlighting the final stage of the simulation.

caption: EDS elemental mapping corresponding to the middle layer microstructure, revealing the chemical signature of the T and η phases.
summary: This EDS map provides chemical characterization of the middle layer, supporting the identification of T and η phases. The mapping confirms that these phases precipitate in the matrix after thermal cycling, with the E-phase dispersoids serving as nucleation sites for the T phase within the grain structure of the material.

caption: Displacement trajectories of nickel atoms within the interfacial region, showing predominantly in-plane motion along the xy-plane.
summary: Representing the movement of nickel atoms, this trajectory plot illustrates that metal atom migration occurs primarily within the interfacial region. Similar to the graphene behavior, the nickel atoms exhibit significant in-plane motion along the xy-plane, with the inset highlighting specific areas of notable atomic displacement during the relaxation process.

caption: Long-term cycling stability comparison of 3D-printed and ink-cast Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrodes at a high 5C rate over 450 cycles.
summary: This panel presents the long-term cycling performance at 5C, where the 3D-printed electrode exhibits a stable discharge capacity of 71.63 mAh g-1 and nearly 100% coulombic efficiency after 450 cycles. In contrast, the ink-cast electrode shows lower initial specific capacities and poor cycling stability under the same high-rate conditions.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images showing dose screening of SV, AMPs, and combined drug groups on MC3T3-E1 cells, with a scale bar of 100 μm.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images illustrate the dose screening process for SV, AMPs, and combined drug groups applied to MC3T3-E1 cells. The final concentrations were determined to be 0.8 μM for SV and 150 μg/ml for AMPs, matching the release concentrations observed in the bionic scaffolds, with a scale bar of 100 μm.

caption: XRD diffraction patterns of neat PLA and PLA/Hemp biocomposites showing characteristic peaks at 16° and 22°.
summary: The XRD patterns for neat PLA and PLA/Hemp biocomposites are presented in panel a. The presence of distinct diffraction peaks at approximately 16° and 22° indicates that the PLA/Hemp biocomposites possess a crystalline nature, confirming the structural influence of the hemp reinforcement within the semi-crystalline PLA matrix.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of Ni, Co, and Co–Ni alloy nanoarrays deposited on AAO substrates, recorded at the 1st, 500th, and 1000th cycles with a sweep rate of 50 mV/s.
summary: This panel displays cyclic voltammograms for electrodeposited Co, Ni, and Co–Ni alloy samples on AAO templates. The curves illustrate the electrochemical stability and performance of these nanoarrays over 1000 cycles at a sweep rate of 50 mV/s, providing insight into the degradation or retention of electrochemical activity over time.

caption: Crack growth rates at 650 °C under constant static load for various material conditions, featuring an inset composite micrograph of the HIP + S + DA Z-X crack path showing deflection and bifurcation.
summary: This plot displays crack growth rates at 650 °C under constant static load. ASTM-valid rates were obtained for wrought and HIP + S + DA conditions, while S + DA samples only show initiation values. The inset micrograph highlights crack deflection and bifurcation, which caused some data to violate ASTM E1457 standards.

caption: Time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram for Inconel 718 calculated using JMatPro software to characterize δ phase dimensions.
summary: Calculated via JMatPro, this TTT diagram provides a framework for understanding the δ phase evolution in Inconel 718. It serves as a critical tool for analyzing how the interplay between cooling rates and intermediate solution temperatures dictates the final dimensions and formation kinetics of the δ phase.

caption: Scheil–Gulliver solidification simulation of M326 showing phase fractions as a function of temperature, highlighting the primary formation of the FCC nickel austenite matrix.
summary: This panel displays the phase fraction evolution of M326 during solidification based on Scheil–Gulliver cooling calculations. The simulation demonstrates that the nickel austenite matrix forms an FCC structure as the primary phase during the solidification process, providing insight into the initial solidification behavior of the alloy.

caption: Transmission electron micrograph identifying the formation of oxides within the AM state microstructure, attributed to residual oxygen from the additive manufacturing process and powder production.
summary: TEM analysis of the AM state alloy after creep failure at 950 °C and 25 MPa reveals the formation of oxides. These oxides originate from residual oxygen present during the AM process and powder production, contributing to grain-boundary enrichment and subsequent material embrittlement observed at high temperatures.

caption: EBSD-IPF map of the wrought sample.
summary: This EBSD-IPF map illustrates the microstructural orientation and grain distribution of the wrought sample. The visualization provides insight into the crystallographic texture and grain morphology resulting from the wrought processing route, serving as a comparative baseline for the other processed conditions presented in the figure.

caption: Cell migration rate derived from the transwell assay, comparing the migratory efficiency of HUVECs across different experimental groups.
summary: Quantitative assessment of the transwell migration assay confirms that Zn@dTNT/Ce-TA promotes a significantly higher number of cells traversing the invasive chamber at 24 hours compared to the Zn@dTNT and control groups, reflecting an enhanced migratory response induced by the treatment.

caption: Comparison of DMA storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor for neat PHB and PHB plasticized with 5 wt% of GT, DINCH, and ATBC.
summary: This panel compares the viscoelastic response of neat PHB against PHB plasticized with 5 wt% of three different additives: GT, DINCH, and ATBC. The DMA data, including storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor, illustrate the distinct effects of these specific plasticizers on the thermal and mechanical behavior of the PHB matrix.

caption: Unit cell configuration after the fourth thermomechanical cycle.
summary: Presented is the unit cell structure after the fourth thermomechanical cycle. At this point, the shape memory effect (SME) for the S20 specimen begins to stabilize. The cycling plots confirm that the recovery process is evolving, transitioning from the low-recovery behavior observed during the initial cycles of the experiment.

caption: Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram showing the distribution of simulated rays at a 200 mm coaxial distance from the process zone for Point 0,0 at 450 nm wavelength, utilizing stable dome parameters for probe 1.
summary: This Monte Carlo frequency scatter diagram illustrates the ray distribution at a 200 mm coaxial distance for Point 0,0 at 450 nm. Using stable dome parameters from probe 1, the analysis beams exhibit minimal deflection, hitting the detector center with a 99.78% probability, confirming high process stability.

caption: Load-displacement response of three distinct stent geometries subjected to three-point bending tests until structural fracture occurs.
summary: This panel illustrates the mechanical failure behavior of three processed stent geometries under three-point bending conditions. The plot tracks the load-displacement relationship until the point of fracture, providing critical data on the structural integrity and ultimate load-bearing capacity of the different stent designs during destructive mechanical testing.

caption: Stress-strain response of TAOR lattice specimens characterized by a 10% relative density.
summary: This panel displays the stress-strain curve for TAOR lattice specimens with a 10% relative density. The data highlights the mechanical behavior of these specific structures, reflecting the wide range of stresses obtained during testing, which is essential for understanding the material's performance under load at this specific density level.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms of the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 electrode recorded over the first three cycles within a potential range of 0.01 to 1.5 V vs. Li/Li+ at a scan rate of 0.1 mV s-1.
summary: The cyclic voltammograms of the 3D-HP SnOx@Ni3Sn2 electrode for the first three cycles, measured between 0.01 and 1.5 V at 0.1 mV s-1, reveal the electrochemical Li storage mechanism. These curves provide insight into the redox behavior and stability of the electrode material during initial lithiation and delithiation processes.

caption: High-magnification HAADF-STEM image of the 1.5Y2O3 sample, showing numerous agglomerated nanoparticles larger than 200 nm, with a white box indicating the region selected for HRTEM analysis.
summary: High-magnification HAADF-STEM imaging reveals the presence of numerous agglomerated nanoparticles within the 1.5Y2O3 sample, many exceeding 200 nm in size. The white box highlights a specific region chosen for further HRTEM investigation. This observation confirms that the 1.5Y2O3 sample contains larger nanoparticles compared to the 0.6Y2O3 sample.

caption: Charge and discharge voltage profiles of the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode measured at varying current rates from 0.1C to 10C.
summary: This panel displays the charge and discharge voltage profiles for the 3D-printed Li4Ti5O12-Li4SiO4 electrode across a range of current densities from 0.1C to 10C. The electrode maintains a high discharge capacity of 52.41 mAh g-1 at 10C, demonstrating excellent electrochemical performance and stability at high current rates.

caption: In situ Fe K-edge QXANES spectra of reduced 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst during DRM at 750 °C and 1 atm with a CH4/CO2 ratio of 1/2.
summary: This panel displays in situ Fe K-edge QXANES spectra for a reduced 8Ni5Fe/MgAl2O4 catalyst during dry reforming of methane at 750 °C. The experimental data, shown as solid lines, are compared against reference spectra (dashed lines), with bold arrows indicating the spectral evolution observed over the 30-minute reaction period.

caption: Pole figure analysis of grains G1 and G2 marked in panel (e), showing specific crystallographic texture.
summary: Pole figure analysis of the selected grains G1 and G2, which were identified in the XZ plane, quantifies their specific crystallographic orientations. This data confirms the presence of preferred grain alignment within the SLM-processed microstructure, providing insight into the solidification texture of the IN625 superalloy.

caption: Orthographic projections of porous defect distributions in conduction (C1, C2), transition (T1, T2), and keyhole (K1, K2) mode cylinders, viewed along the XY build plate plane.
summary: This orthographic projection displays the spatial distribution of porous defects within conduction, transition, and keyhole mode cylinders derived from XCT data. These projections illustrate the defect morphology across different printing modes, providing a visual comparison of porosity characteristics alongside previously reported density values for these specific cylinder replicates.

caption: Tan delta (G″/G′) temperature sweep for PMMA-free feedstocks, representing the ratio of viscous to storage modulus.
summary: Viscous behavior of the filaments is examined through the tan delta plot, defined as the ratio of the viscous modulus to the storage modulus. This panel provides insight into the damping properties and viscoelastic nature of the PMMA-free feedstock, characterizing how the material dissipates energy across varying temperatures.

caption: Overview of the machine learning pipeline illustrating the integration of computer vision-based features into supervised and unsupervised classification algorithms to categorize welding regimes.
summary: This schematic depicts the machine learning pipeline utilized for classifying welding processes. Computer vision-derived features serve as inputs for both supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms. The system is designed to distinguish between four distinct operational regimes: dripping, incomplete melting, stubbing, and stable, providing a structured approach to process monitoring.

caption: Radar plot comparing mesh and scan data across six parameters: alignment, 3D comparison, front silhouette, lateral silhouette, hole silhouette, and teeth silhouette, with metrics including mean error, RMS error, and standard deviation in millimetres.
summary: This radar chart provides a quantitative comparison between mesh and scan data by evaluating six fundamental parameters: alignment, 3D comparison, front silhouette, lateral silhouette, hole silhouette, and teeth silhouette. The visualization incorporates mean error, root mean square error, and standard deviation values, all measured in millimetres to assess data accuracy.

caption: Effect of the magnetic parameter (Mf) on the fluid motion (U) distribution within the PEOF-SNF model for scenario-4.
summary: This panel illustrates the influence of the magnetic parameter (Mf) on the fluid motion (U) distribution within the PEOF-SNF model for scenario-4. The artificial backpropagation network results demonstrate how variations in the magnetic parameter impact the fluid motion properties of the ternary PGW fluid, providing insights into the system's behavior.

caption: 3D minimum curvature map of the gyroid surface, corresponding to the same area as the roughness map, with magnifying windows detailing down-skin and up-skin regions (rcurv = 50 µm and λS = 0.05 mm).
summary: This 3D map visualizes the minimum curvature across the same surface area analyzed in the roughness map. By applying a curvature radius of 50 µm and a short-wavelength filter, the panel highlights localized geometric variations in the down-skin and up-skin regions, offering insight into the surface morphology of the gyroid.

caption: Hall flow meter apparatus used to evaluate the flowability of plasma spheroidized Ni-32.4Si powders.
summary: The Hall flow meter is utilized to assess the flowability of plasma spheroidized Ni-32.4Si powders, a critical parameter for additive manufacturing. Experimental results indicate that powders processed at higher pressures or lower feeding rates exhibit improved flow properties due to enhanced sphericity, reduced surface roughness, and more complete particle melting.

caption: Surface shape image of the sample subjected to EI-MFC processing for 30 minutes, captured through KFM analysis.
summary: Surface morphology of the sample processed by EI-MFC for 30 minutes is captured using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy. This shape image illustrates the physical surface characteristics resulting from the EI-MFC treatment, allowing for a direct comparison of surface features with the UTPC-processed sample under identical processing durations.

caption: Surface profile z(x,y) of the untreated (UT) specimen showing a planar surface characterized by discontinuous ridges.
summary: The surface profile of the untreated (UT) specimen is characterized by a planar morphology featuring discontinuous ridges. This relatively high surface roughness and associated superficial porosity contribute to the observed drops in the open circuit potential (OCP) during electrochemical testing compared to the modified specimens.

caption: Three-dimensional magnetic field distribution for the M-0 configuration.
summary: This panel displays a COMSOL simulation of the three-dimensional magnetic field distribution for the M-0 configuration. The visualization illustrates the spatial arrangement of magnetic flux lines, providing a baseline for comparing the magnetic field characteristics across different magnet arrangements used in the study.

caption: EDS elemental map showing the distribution of oxygen within the analyzed region.
summary: This EDS elemental map displays the spatial distribution of oxygen within the analyzed region. By correlating this map with the HAADF-STEM image, the presence and localization of oxygen are visualized, assisting in the characterization of the chemical composition of the particles found in the 2Zr-1Y LRM sample.

caption: Fracture stress plotted against porosity for specimens oriented at θ = 45°.
summary: This graph shows the fracture stress variation relative to porosity for specimens oriented at 45°. The relationship is evaluated against experimental data to characterize the mechanical properties, providing insight into how porosity influences the fracture stress of the material when subjected to this specific orientation angle.

caption: Schematic illustration of the beta-annealing thermal cycle, depicting the heating process above the beta-transus temperature followed by either air cooling or furnace cooling paths.
summary: This schematic illustrates the beta-annealing heat treatment process. The material is heated above the beta-transus temperature, as specified in the reference, before undergoing controlled cooling. The diagram highlights two distinct cooling pathways, air cooling and furnace cooling, which are critical for determining the final microstructure of the processed material.

caption: Capillary (Ca) and Ohnesorge (Oh) numbers plotted against normalized enthalpy (NE), both showing a decrease as energy input increases.
summary: Both the capillary and Ohnesorge numbers decrease with increasing normalized enthalpy. This reduction implies that viscous damping becomes less significant relative to inertia and capillarity at higher energy levels, contributing to the observed deterioration in surface quality and the emergence of unstable keyhole dynamics and spatter generation.

caption: Temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility for CeNiZn and CeNiZnH 1.2 measured at 3 T, with an inset showing the inverse magnetic susceptibility of the hydride and its corresponding Curie-Weiss fit.
summary: This plot displays the temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility of CeNiZn and CeNiZnH 1.2 under a 3 T field. The hydride exhibits significantly higher susceptibility values compared to the parent compound. The inset confirms that the hydride follows a Curie-Weiss behavior at temperatures exceeding 30 K, as indicated by the linear fit.

caption: Bright-field TEM micrograph showing the morphology of a grain boundary in the FG LSHR variant after testing at 725 °C, specifically highlighting a region devoid of bulged oxide formations.
summary: This TEM micrograph displays the grain boundary morphology of the FG LSHR alloy variant following exposure to 725 °C. The image focuses on a region characterized by the absence of bulged oxides, providing a baseline structural observation for comparing grain boundary degradation mechanisms in the tested superalloy material.

caption: Kernel average misorientation (KAM) profile of the slightly deformed 4# specimen.
summary: The KAM profile of the slightly deformed 4# specimen illustrates the local misorientation distribution. This map provides insight into the strain accumulation and microstructural response of the 4# specimen under deformation conditions, allowing for comparison with other specimen compositions.

caption: Kernel misorientation map (KAM) of the as-built sample, representing the baseline local lattice strain distribution.
summary: The as-built sample's kernel misorientation map (KAM) provides a baseline for local lattice strain. This map is used to compare the degree of deformation and lattice distortion introduced by varying laser shock peening intensities in the subsequent samples, highlighting the initial state of the WAAM material before processing.

caption: Relative density and defect area fraction as a function of laser power, illustrating the influence of processing parameters on specimen integrity.
summary: Laser power is plotted against relative density and defect area fraction to evaluate the impact of PBF-LB/M processing conditions. While high energy density samples exhibit consistent values between the two metrics, lower power settings lead to observable deviations, highlighting the sensitivity of defect formation to the specific laser power applied during fabrication.

caption: Confusion matrix displaying the LCNN model's detection results for pore status in Test-2, highlighting the model's ability to correctly identify samples despite varying brightness levels.
summary: Representing the LCNN model's performance for Test-2, this confusion matrix quantifies the correct and wrong detection samples. The results confirm the model's robust capability to maintain accurate pore status identification, reinforcing the finding that the architecture effectively resists interference caused by brightness variations in the verification set.

caption: O 1s XPS spectra ranging from 528 to 540 eV for polished Cu-plates and Cu-powders in virgin and oxidized (300 °C) conditions, highlighting characteristic peaks at 529.9 eV, 530.4 eV, and 532 eV.
summary: The O 1s XPS spectra for Cu-plates and Cu-powders are analyzed across the 528 to 540 eV range. Three distinct peaks at 529.9 eV, 530.4 eV, and 532 eV are identified, providing insight into the surface oxidation states of the samples in both virgin and 300 °C oxidized conditions.

caption: Magnetization curves plotted as a function of magnetic field strength for samples subjected to a 1200 °C heat treatment, measured across varying frequencies.
summary: This plot displays magnetization curves for materials heat-treated at 1200 °C, illustrating magnetic behavior across different frequencies. Data acquisition was performed using LabVIEW software integrated with a National Instruments data acquisition card. The curves characterize the magnetic response of the processed specimens under the specified experimental conditions.

caption: Diagram of an acoustic emission (AE) sensor setup designed for detecting elastic waves generated by material deformation or cracking during manufacturing.
summary: Acoustic emission spectroscopy is depicted as an in-line monitoring technique for powder bed fusion. This method captures transient elastic waves produced by internal material changes, providing a non-destructive means to detect defects or structural evolution in real-time during the fabrication process.

caption: Full width at half maximum (FWHM) values derived from diffraction peaks for both L-PBF-fabricated and conventionally annealed light weight steel specimens.
summary: The bar chart presents a quantitative comparison of the full width at half maximum (FWHM) values for diffraction peaks observed in the L-PBF-fabricated and conventionally annealed light weight steel samples. These measurements serve as an indicator of microstructural characteristics, such as crystallite size and lattice strain, resulting from the different fabrication methods.

caption: Arrhenius plot illustrating the temperature-dependent diffusivity of various solute elements within the titanium beta phase.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the calculated diffusivities of alloying elements in the beta phase of titanium across the investigated temperature range. By plotting these values, the figure provides a comparative overview of solute mobility, facilitating a systematic analysis of diffusion kinetics as summarized from the study's experimental data.

caption: Dark-field TEM image of as-fabricated CM247LC-M showing small γ′ phases within the dendrite, with an inset SAED pattern showing 010 superlattice reflections.
summary: This panel displays the γ′ phase distribution within the dendrite of CM247LC-M, indicated by blue arrows. The inset SAED pattern confirms the superlattice structure. Observations indicate that the number density and nucleation rate of these small γ′ phases are significantly reduced in the CM247LC-M variant due to lower Al and Hf concentrations.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) pattern derived from the austenite HRTEM image, exhibiting a standard diffraction pattern devoid of satellite reflections.
summary: The FFT pattern corresponding to the austenite HRTEM image confirms the absence of lattice modulation. The lack of satellite reflections in this diffraction data is consistent with the uniform lattice structure observed in the austenite phase, indicating no periodic structural distortions or shuffling within the analyzed region.

caption: 3D topography and cross-sectional profile of the wear scar on the LN17 surface, viewed parallel to the microgroove.
summary: This panel illustrates the 3D topography and cross-sectional profile of the wear scar on the LN17 surface, viewed parallel to the microgroove. Similar to the LN21 surface, the LN17 specimen exhibits minimal wear areas under oil-lubricated conditions, highlighting its effective performance in reducing wear damage.

caption: Comparison of maximum load crack tip opening displacement (CTODm) values across base metal (BM), weld positional (WP), and specific microstructure (SM) specimens tested in air at 27 °C and –90 °C, and in a sour environment at 27 °C.
summary: This fracture toughness plot compares CTODm values for BM, WP, and SM specimens under varying environmental and thermal conditions. Results indicate that fracture toughness decreases from the base metal, characterized by ferrite with dispersed carbides, to the specific microstructure of the CGHAZ, which consists of martensite and coalesced bainite.

caption: Pentagon diagram representing the CPDP parameters of the 6-hour mechano-synthesized Al72Cr15Ni13 alloy system when tested in a 3.5% NaCl solution.
summary: Represented as a pentagon diagram, this plot characterizes the CPDP parameters for the Al72Cr15Ni13 alloy system following 6 hours of mechanical synthesis. The electrochemical performance is evaluated in a 3.5% NaCl electrolyte, providing a comparative view of corrosion-related metrics such as pitting potential and current density for this specific alloy.

caption: Cyclic voltammogram measurements for three distinct nickel alloy-coated 3D-printed electrodes with a nickel mass deposition of 0.133 g/cm2, performed in a 1 mol KOH solution.
summary: Presented here are the cyclic voltammogram measurements for three nickel alloy-coated 3D-printed electrodes, maintaining a consistent nickel mass deposition of 0.133 g/cm2. These electrochemical tests were conducted in a 1 mol KOH solution to characterize the performance of the alloy-coated electrodes in an alkaline electrolyte.

caption: Optical micrograph of sintered Cu-Ni alloy reinforced with 1.5 wt.% carbon nanotubes (CNT).
summary: Depicted is the microstructure of the sintered copper-nickel alloy composite with 1.5 wt.% CNT. The image reveals the morphological characteristics of the composite, highlighting how the increased concentration of carbon nanotubes integrates into the copper-nickel matrix following the sintering procedure.

caption: Variations of the coefficient of friction (CoF) during sliding wear tests, highlighting a reduction from 0.333 to 0.214 for laser-modified specimens.
summary: Variations in the coefficient of friction during sliding wear tests are presented for both as-built and laser surface-modified specimens. The results demonstrate a significant 36% decrease in the mean CoF value, dropping from 0.333 to 0.214, which indicates improved tribological efficiency following the laser surface modification treatment.

caption: Strain nephogram of a horizontally printed sample during the 50th loading cycle under IP conditions.
summary: Displaying the strain distribution after 50 loading cycles under IP conditions, this nephogram illustrates the internal strain state of the horizontally printed sample. It allows for the assessment of how cyclic loading influences the strain localization and distribution patterns within the material structure over the course of the fatigue test.

caption: Corresponding agent performance metrics for the third phase of reward shaping under the specified extrusion error conditions.
summary: Complementing panel (e), this visualization shows the agent's performance during the third phase of reward shaping. It confirms the agent's learning outcomes under the 232% flow rate at 190 °C, demonstrating the final state of the agent's performance after completing the structured reward shaping training phases.

caption: SHAP dependence plot showing the interaction between effective stress ratio and specimen state.
summary: This plot visualizes the SHAP values for the effective stress ratio across different specimen states. Because stress ratio is interrelated with other mechanical parameters, this plot is analyzed in conjunction with panels (d) and (f). Note that data points for specific states may overlap on the vertical axis.

caption: Atomic structure model of twin boundaries (TBs) within γ-Al2O3, illustrating the arrangement of Al3+ (red) and O2- (blue) ions, with parent crystals and twins distinguished by light and dark yellow coloring.
summary: This atomic model depicts the structural configuration of twin boundaries in γ-Al2O3. Al3+ and O2- ions are represented by red and blue circles, respectively. The visualization highlights the geometric relationship between parent crystals and twins, which are color-coded in light and dark yellow to facilitate structural analysis of the oxide scale.

caption: Photoluminescence emission spectra of GCN and GCN@CD-A, displaying a strong emission peak near 460 nm related to charge carrier recombination.
summary: PL spectroscopy was employed to investigate the recombination behavior of photogenerated electron-hole pairs. Both GCN and GCN@CD-A display a strong emission peak centered around 460 nm, attributed to the direct recombination of photoexcited charge carriers and n to pi* transitions associated with lone electron pairs on nitrogen atoms.

caption: Statistical distribution of lengths for Cr-Ni-CNF and Ti-Ni-CNF samples measured across different growth durations.
summary: This box plot displays the length distribution of CNF samples with a sample size of 20. Observations indicate that 5 min and 10 min Cr-Ni-CNFs are significantly shorter than their Ti-Ni counterparts, although both sample types achieve comparable lengths after a 30 min growth duration.

caption: Transmission spectrum of the Ruby ink filter, demonstrating increased transmission near 600 nm with a suppressed blue–green region and a high-transmission plateau in the red region.
summary: Ruby ink filters display a transmission spectrum where the blue–green region is suppressed. Transmission increases significantly near 600 nm, resulting in a high-transmission plateau across the red region of the spectrum, which defines the optical filtering characteristics of this specific 3D-printed material.

caption: Overlayed fluorescence microscopy image of FDA/PI dual staining, where green indicates live cells and red indicates dead cells.
summary: Live/Dead staining using FDA/PI dual fluorescence imaging confirms high cell viability rates within the 3D printed constructs. The overlayed image shows a predominance of green-stained live cells, validating the metabolic findings. This viability was confirmed at both 7 and 14 days post-printing, demonstrating long-term survival of the embedded chondrocytes.

caption: Top-view atomic relaxation pattern demonstrating oxygen atom relocation toward Ta, Nb, and Ti dopant sites.
summary: This panel illustrates the post-relaxation atomic configuration for the γ' phase surface doped with Ta, Nb, and Ti. In contrast to the Cr and Si doping cases, the oxygen atoms are observed to relocate toward the dopant atoms, highlighting the significant influence of dopant identity on oxygen adsorption behavior.

caption: SEM-BF image and corresponding EDS elemental mapping showing the chemical distribution of Co, Cr, Fe, Al, and Ni across the FCC and BCC phases.
summary: SEM bright-field imaging combined with EDS mapping illustrates the chemical partitioning between phases. The FCC phase is enriched with Co, Cr, and Fe elements, while the BCC phase shows significant enrichment of Al and Ni, demonstrating the distinct elemental composition of the dual-phase microstructure.

caption: Representative curves showing the evolution of the coefficient of friction (COF) values for the studied alloys during sliding tests in PBS solution.
summary: The evolution of the coefficient of friction (COF) during sliding in a PBS solution is presented for the studied alloys. These representative curves provide insight into the tribological performance and frictional behavior of the different titanium-based samples under sliding conditions, complementing the electrochemical data recorded during the tribocorrosion analysis.

caption: Proposed reaction pathways for the hydrogenation of CO2 into CO, CH4, and C2H6 over Ni-based and Ni-Fe-based catalysts, specifically 10Ni-13X, 8Ni-2Fe-13X, 5Ni-5Fe-13X, and 2Ni-8Fe-13X, highlighting the initial hydrogenation of CO2 to HCOO* mediated by Ni-domain species.
summary: This schematic illustrates the catalytic conversion pathways of CO2 to CO, CH4, and C2H6 over various Ni and Ni-Fe catalysts. It highlights the initial hydrogenation step where CO2 is converted to HCOO* on Ni-domain species, integrating experimental findings with established literature to explain the reaction mechanism across different catalyst compositions.

caption: Representative DSC thermogram of annealed PEKK specimens, displaying bimodal melting behavior characterized by secondary crystal melting between 210–240 °C and primary crystal melting from 270–330 °C.
summary: The DSC thermogram provides a representative analysis of annealed PEKK specimens to quantify crystallinity. The curve reveals a distinct bimodal melting behavior, identifying secondary crystals that melt in the 210–240 °C range and primary crystals that undergo melting at higher temperatures between 270 °C and 330 °C.

caption: Optical photograph showing the as-built NiTi alloy samples following the additive manufacturing process.
summary: This photograph displays the as-built NiTi samples produced via the additive manufacturing process. The image provides a visual record of the physical state of the components immediately after the build, prior to the removal of the rectangular-tapered sections and subsequent post-processing steps.

caption: Cyclic voltammograms at 25 mV s-1 scan rate for activated (top) and as-printed (bottom) electrodes fabricated from AuNP-CO, CO, and commercial filaments in 1 mM [Fe(CN)6]4- solution.
summary: Cyclic voltammograms compare the electrochemical performance of AuNP-CO, CO, and commercial electrodes in both activated and as-printed states. The AuNP-CO electrodes exhibit distinct peak responses, suggesting mixed material kinetics. These plots demonstrate the influence of electrode composition and activation state on the redox behavior of the [Fe(CN)6]4- probe.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry profile of the flexible energy storage device recorded at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹.
summary: This cyclic voltammetry profile at 5 mV s⁻¹ shows a nearly rectangular shape, yielding a specific capacitance of 20.39 F g⁻¹ under no-load conditions. The data highlights the device's storage capability, although mechanical deformation such as 180° twisting can reduce the specific capacitance to 12.05 F g⁻¹.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing the spatial distribution of Ni atoms in blue and (Al, Ti) precipitates in orange-brown, representing a total volume of 59.6 million ions.
summary: This atom probe tomography reconstruction visualizes the non-uniform distribution of (Al, Ti) precipitates within a nickel matrix, forming distinct ring-shaped patterns. Comprising 59.6 million ions, the data allows for the calculation of precipitate number density based on the identified features within the reconstructed volume of the analyzed tip.

caption: Elemental distribution mapping and AFM topography of the NCG-PNC wear track, showing the spatial arrangement of C, O, N, S, and Ni.
summary: EDS mapping of the NCG-PNC wear track shows that Ni, C, O, N, and S are evenly distributed across the surface. The low content of Ni detected suggests that this element actively participates in the wear process during tribological testing, providing insight into the material's degradation mechanism.

caption: Selected area diffraction pattern confirming the crystallographic nature of the alpha-double-prime martensite observed in the planar traces.
summary: The selected area diffraction pattern provides crystallographic confirmation of the alpha-double-prime martensite phase. This diffraction data, combined with the observed planar traces in TEM images, validates the occurrence of a deformation-induced BCC to orthorhombic martensitic transformation near the beta-Ti matrix and unmelted Nb particle interfacial regions.

caption: Chronoamperometric current profiles recorded for FCDI stacks utilizing 3D-printed non-conductive, 3D-printed conductive, and CNC-milled graphite flow channels with a 5 wt% YP50F electrode concentration during 1.5 g/L NaCl desalination.
summary: This panel displays the chronoamperometric current response of FCDI cells during desalination of a 1.5 g/L NaCl solution. The data compares three different flow channel materials—3D-printed non-conductive, 3D-printed conductive, and CNC-milled graphite—using a 5 wt% YP50F flow electrode, illustrating the electrochemical performance variations under these specific experimental conditions.

caption: Electron probe microanalysis mapping of the 2TiN as-built Inconel 718 sample, showing an increased density of Laves phase precipitates compared to the 1TiN condition.
summary: Electron probe microanalysis mapping of the 2TiN as-built Inconel 718 sample shows an increased density of light grey Laves phase precipitates. This increase, relative to the 1TiN sample, is attributed to the redistribution of Nb and Mo in the melt pool, which is promoted by altered local chemistry from TiN decomposition.

caption: Simulated demagnetization curves at 300 K for modeled magnets featuring a ferromagnetic grain boundary phase, demonstrating the magnetic response under varying core-shell configurations.
summary: Simulated demagnetization curves at 300 K are shown for magnets with a ferromagnetic grain boundary phase. Research indicates that the formation of a non-magnetic grain boundary phase, rather than a ferromagnetic one, is more effective for achieving significant coercivity enhancement in these nanocrystalline Nd-Fe-B magnet structures.

caption: Fatigue crack growth (FCG) rate diagram comparing L2-S specimens against plain control samples, highlighting specific acceleration and retardation events caused by crack path deviation.
summary: This FCG diagram illustrates the crack growth behavior of L2-S specimens in comparison to plain samples. The plot highlights distinct regions of crack growth acceleration and retardation, which are attributed to the deviation of the crack from its intended path, providing insight into the fatigue performance of the L2-S material configuration.

caption: Atomic model of the 32-atom γ′-Ni3Al supercell centered on an aluminum atom, with refractory elements M (Ta or W) substituted into the lattice.
summary: This panel displays a 32-atom supercell model of the γ′-Ni3Al phase centered on an aluminum atom. The structure incorporates refractory elements, specifically tantalum or tungsten, at substitutional sites. This atomic configuration is utilized for computational modeling to investigate the influence of these alloying elements on the phase properties.

caption: Isolated Ni-Mn-Si 20% iso-concentration surfaces after 10 hours of aging, demonstrating the absence of significant clustering for these elements.
summary: Focusing on the Ni-Mn-Si-rich regions, this panel displays the 20% iso-concentration surfaces after 10 hours of aging. The analysis confirms that no noticeable clustering of Ni, Mn, and Si atoms has occurred at this stage, as the concentrations have not yet reached the threshold required for significant structural display.

caption: Hydrogen desorption rate curve for a 168 h H-charged specimen measured at a heating rate of 200 °C/h, featuring a dual-Gaussian fit to characterize desorption kinetics.
summary: The hydrogen desorption rate curve for a 168 h H-charged specimen is shown at a heating rate of 200 °C/h. The data is fitted with two Gaussian curves to analyze the desorption behavior. These peaks correspond to specific temperature ranges, providing insight into the hydrogen trapping characteristics of the material.

caption: Fourth Vickers microhardness indentation within the ferrite phase of the 2209 DED-LB/w DSS cylinder after 200-hour aging at 400 °C.
summary: Shown is a Vickers microhardness indentation in the ferrite phase of a 2209 DED-LB/w DSS cylinder after 200 hours of aging at 400 °C. The indentation is positioned to exclude the austenite phase, ensuring that the hardness measurement is specific to the ferrite phase of the cylinder.

caption: Hall coefficient RH as a function of temperature for sample S0 ASD, exhibiting positive values throughout the entire measurement range.
summary: This plot displays the Hall coefficient RH for sample S0 ASD across its temperature range. Unlike the Seebeck coefficient, the Hall coefficient remains positive for all measured temperatures. This observation provides critical insight into the electronic transport properties and the dominant carrier type within the investigated material sample.

caption: Ashby plot comparing the Shore A durometer versus elongation to failure for FFF-printed elastomers and traditional castable elastomeric resins.
summary: This Ashby plot illustrates the performance landscape of elastomeric materials, contrasting the limited range of properties achievable through FFF 3D printing against the broader spectrum of chemistries and mechanical characteristics available via traditional castable resins. The data highlights the current constraints in material selection for additive manufacturing of flexible components.

caption: Load-displacement response of neat and GNP-reinforced Onyx bulk samples during quasi-static tensile testing, demonstrating ductile deformation modes.
summary: Tensile load-displacement curves for neat and GNP-reinforced Onyx bulk samples illustrate the material's response to quasi-static loading. Neat Onyx exhibits a typical ductile deformation mode with significant plastic strain before rupture, providing a baseline for evaluating the influence of GNP incorporation on the tensile properties of the 3D-printed composites.

caption: Grain boundary distribution map of as-built IN718, illustrating the initial microstructural state prior to heat treatment.
summary: This panel displays the grain boundary distribution map for as-built IN718. It serves as a baseline for evaluating the microstructural characteristics of the material before undergoing high-temperature treatment, providing a reference for comparing grain boundary evolution and distribution patterns across the different processing conditions investigated in the study.

caption: Model predictions for average recrystallised grain size and corresponding volume fraction variation in IN 625 superalloy across various temperatures.
summary: This panel displays model predictions for the average recrystallised grain size and volume fraction in IN 625 superalloy. By plotting these variables across different temperatures, the figure provides a comprehensive view of the microstructural evolution, demonstrating the model's effectiveness in predicting grain growth and recrystallisation kinetics for this specific alloy.

caption: FFT micrograph showing the masking treatment applied to all reflections encircled by dashed yellow circles.
summary: This FFT micrograph illustrates the specific masking procedure used to isolate structural information. By treating all reflections within the dashed yellow circles, the analysis effectively filters the signal to highlight specific crystallographic features, facilitating the identification of distinct phases within the petal regions of the material.

caption: Continuous Cooling Transformation diagram for the IN718 base alloy overlaid with cooling rate curves corresponding to various distances within the dissimilar AL6XN-IN718 welded joint.
summary: This CCT diagram illustrates the phase transformation kinetics for the IN718 base alloy. By superimposing cooling rate curves from different locations in the AL6XN-IN718 weld, the figure highlights how thermal gradients influence microstructural evolution, specifically the formation of delta phase precipitates and the development of soft zones in the heat-affected zone.

caption: Color-coded elemental distribution maps for the β-Mg2Si particle, highlighting the spatial segregation of Mg (red) and Si (dark blue).
summary: Spatial distribution of alloying elements within the β-Mg2Si precipitate is visualized through color-coded EDS maps. The maps highlight the segregation of Mg in red and Si in dark blue, confirming the chemical homogeneity and phase identity of the angular particles observed in the AA6082 alloy microstructure.

caption: Localized TUNA current-voltage curve for eutectic Al13Fe4, showing a measured current of 0.58 nA.
summary: Localized TUNA current-voltage measurements for eutectic Al13Fe4 yield a current value of 0.58 nA. This result indicates that the eutectic Al13Fe4 phase exhibits inferior electrical conduction properties compared to the Al3Ni phase, contributing to the overall understanding of the material's microscopic electrical behavior.

caption: Bar charts illustrating the relative weights of laser power and powder density as input variables for predicting three distinct mechanical properties in single-output models.
summary: This panel displays the interpretability of machine learning models by visualizing the weights assigned to laser power and density for predicting mechanical properties. These weights quantify the contribution of each input variable, providing insight into how specific processing parameters influence the model's output for different mechanical performance metrics.

caption: STEM bright field image and corresponding EDX elemental maps showing oxide distribution ahead of an interrupted crack in a FC testpiece.
summary: This panel displays a STEM bright field image alongside EDX elemental maps for a FC testpiece. It highlights the oxide intrusion located approximately a few microns ahead of the crack tip. The color-coded EDX maps indicate relative concentration levels, revealing the specific oxide constituents present in the crack tip region.

caption: High-resolution Ni2p XPS spectra of the evaporator zone, showing measured signals and fitted peak models for NiO and Ni(OH)2.
summary: High-resolution Ni2p XPS spectra of the evaporator zone are presented, featuring measured signals alongside fitted peak models. Analysis of these spectra confirms the presence of NiO and Ni(OH)2, which are associated with a distinctive green coloration observed in the material after the experimental process.

caption: Local von Mises equivalent strain distribution across the PBF-EB/M manufactured steel X5CrMnNi16-6-6 lattice structure at 20% engineering strain.
summary: Digital Image Correlation analysis reveals the local strain field within the lattice structure under compressive loading. The map displays the von Mises equivalent strain distribution at an engineering strain of 20%, highlighting the deformation behavior of the struts and nodes within the PBF-EB/M manufactured steel X5CrMnNi16-6-6 specimen.

caption: Feature dependence plot of the ANN regression model for Tmax, visualized using SHAP values to illustrate the influence of individual input features.
summary: The SHAP-based feature dependence plot reveals the relative influence of input variables on the ANN model's Tmax predictions. This analysis provides interpretability for the regression model, identifying key features that drive the temperature output and aligning with established physical relationships regarding material deformation and flow behavior.

caption: Grain orientation distribution of the sample prior to friction stir processing.
summary: Panel (a) illustrates the grain orientation distribution of the sample before friction stir processing. The material exhibits randomly oriented equiaxed grains. This baseline measurement provides a reference for evaluating the microstructural changes induced by the subsequent processing technique, confirming the initial state of the sample's grain structure.

caption: Derivative melting curves between 60 and 95 °C for the second cycle (left) alongside schematic representations of the specific melting events associated with each observed peak (right).
summary: Derivative melting curves between 60 and 95 °C isolate specific thermal transitions for the hydrogel samples. The accompanying schematics correlate these derivative peaks to distinct melting events, providing a mechanistic interpretation of the structural changes occurring within the DNA hydrogel networks as they transition through the specified temperature range.

caption: Nanoindentation load-depth curves for as-spun (Co0.75Cr0.125Mo0.125)100-xB x glassy alloys with boron concentrations ranging from 25 to 31 at%.
summary: Nanoindentation load-depth curves are presented for as-spun (Co0.75Cr0.125Mo0.125)100-xB x glassy alloys. The data covers a boron content range of 25 to 31 at%, providing a fundamental mechanical characterization of the indentation response for these specific metallic glass compositions as they vary in boron concentration.

caption: Particle size distribution (PSD) analysis of on-bed powder derived from the HAM process.
summary: This histogram displays the particle size distribution of powder collected from the HAM process. The data provides a quantitative assessment of the powder characteristics, which, when compared to the AM process results, helps explain the observed differences in the amount of unsieved powder collected during the manufacturing cycle.

caption: Maxima of the magnetic entropy change (ΔSm,max) plotted against the applied magnetic field for all studied alloy samples.
summary: This panel displays the maxima of the magnetic entropy change as a function of the applied magnetic field for all investigated alloys. The data indicates that the magnetic entropy change values consistently increase with the applied magnetic field, providing a quantitative assessment of the magnetic response across the different sample compositions.

caption: Temperature-time profiles for dilatometer tests conducted at varying heating rates of 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, and 200 °C/s, with a constant cooling rate of 100 °C/s.
summary: This plot illustrates the temperature history for dilatometer tests across a range of heating rates from 5 °C/s to 200 °C/s. All samples were subjected to a uniform cooling rate of 100 °C/s. These profiles provide the thermal input parameters necessary for analyzing the material's response during controlled dilatometry experiments.

caption: Comparison of microhardness values for various HEA products fabricated through additive manufacturing and conventional manufacturing processes.
summary: This panel presents a comparative analysis of microhardness values for high-entropy alloys produced via additive manufacturing and conventional techniques. These additively manufactured HEAs demonstrate significant potential for creating geometrically complex components with tailored performance characteristics, which has led to their increasing adoption across a wide range of industrial applications.

caption: True compressive stress-strain response of HST alloy measured across a range of strain rates.
summary: This panel presents the true compressive stress-strain curves for the HST alloy. By plotting these curves at different strain rates, the figure characterizes the mechanical performance and strain-rate sensitivity of the HST material, highlighting how the alloy responds to varying levels of compressive impact during the mechanical testing.

caption: Cyclic voltammetry response of NiTi materials with and without hydrogen modification in PBS at a scan rate of 0.1 V/s, showing a higher current peak of 0.04 mA for the hydrogen-enriched sample.
summary: This cyclic voltammogram compares the electrochemical response of NiTi materials in PBS solution. The hydrogen-modified NiTi electrode exhibits a higher peak current of 0.04 mA compared to the unmodified NiTi sample, indicating that hydrogen enrichment significantly influences the electrochemical behavior of the material at a scan rate of 0.1 V/s.

caption: Over-focused bright-field TEM micrograph of MoTaTiV CSA irradiated with 1 × 10^16 cm^-2 He ions, showing initial bubble formation.
summary: This over-focused bright-field TEM micrograph displays the MoTaTiV CSA microstructure following He-irradiation at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 cm^-2. At this initial implantation stage, the columnar microstructure of the alloy facilitates bubble nucleation, which is primarily observed at the column boundaries, acting as preferential sites for bubble development.

caption: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for O-14 in acetonitrile, illustrating the spectral features and the crossing point for S1 energy determination.
summary: Normalized UV-visible absorption and fluorescence spectra for O-14 in acetonitrile are shown. The intersection of these two spectral curves allows for the experimental calculation of the singlet excited state energy level (S1), which is essential for characterizing the electronic structure and optical behavior of the O-14 molecule.

caption: Time-dependent FWHM evolution for peaks categorized as type (ii), showing a distinct change in slope occurring between 9 and 12 seconds.
summary: Category (ii) peaks demonstrate a notable change in their FWHM evolution slope between 9 and 12 seconds. This transition in the narrowing rate suggests a shift in the underlying microstructural kinetics, distinguishing these peaks from those with constant slopes during the heat treatment process.

caption: t-SNE visualization of features extracted from the fourth convolutional layer.
summary: Displayed is the t-SNE visualization of features extracted from the fourth convolutional layer of the CNN. This plot completes the sequence of layer-wise analysis, enabling the evaluation of how deep convolutional layers refine the signal representation compared to the disordered state observed in the initial layers of the network.

caption: LDH activity levels normalized to the cp-Ti control group following 24 hours of direct contact with cp-Ti, STQ, or AG640 surfaces.
summary: LDH activity, normalized to the cp-Ti control, serves as a measure of cytotoxicity after 24 hours of contact. The AG640 group demonstrated an 80% decrease in LDH release compared to the cp-Ti control, indicating superior cytocompatibility for the AG640 material compared to the other tested surfaces.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the control specimen gauge section showing baseline structural characteristics.
summary: The control specimen's gauge section is displayed in this cross-sectional optical micrograph. It provides the baseline structural state of the material prior to any treatment. This image allows for a direct visual comparison with the treated condition to identify changes in morphology or integrity resulting from the experimental process.

caption: Force-displacement behavior of Ti64 specimen EV212 at 293 K, featuring optical micrographs that illustrate crack propagation along lamellar boundaries without arrest.
summary: Testing of Ti64 specimen EV212 at 293 K yields a force-displacement curve characteristic of the impact conditions. Optical micrographs indicate that the crack propagates continuously along the lamellar boundaries, demonstrating that the crack is not arrested during the impact event for this specific specimen condition.

caption: TEM-DF micrograph of the R725-Nb alloy showing intragranular gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime co-precipitates, with an inset displaying a high-resolution image of the interface.
summary: The TEM-DF micrograph of the R725-Nb alloy, taken along the [100] gamma zone axis, illustrates the intragranular gamma-prime and gamma-double-prime co-precipitates. An inset provides a high-resolution view of the co-precipitate interface, offering detailed structural information about the phase boundaries within the Nb-modified alloy matrix.

caption: Fluorescence intensity measurements of three PDMS types and glass across four excitation wavelengths: 405 nm, 488 nm, 594 nm, and 647 nm.
summary: Fluorescence intensity was measured for three PDMS types and glass at four excitation wavelengths. The results indicate that the fluorescence intensity of the three PDMS types remains nearly identical across all tested wavelengths, while the glass substrate exhibits a slight decrease in fluorescence intensity compared to the PDMS samples.

caption: Linear extrapolation of (α(E)E)^2 versus photon energy E for GaP1-xNx layers, demonstrating the determination of the direct bandgap energy from the horizontal intercept.
summary: This plot displays the linear fitting of (α(E)E)^2 against photon energy E for GaP1-xNx layers near the absorption edge. By performing a linear extrapolation to the horizontal axis, the direct bandgap energy Eg is determined. The data illustrates that the direct bandgap energy decreases as the nitrogen content increases.

caption: Three-dimensional models of L, D, and G type TPMS porous structures.
summary: This panel displays the three-dimensional geometric models for L, D, and G type Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) porous structures. These models serve as the foundational designs for the subsequent fabrication of green bodies using DLP technology, which are then processed through debinding and sintering at 1300 °C for 2 hours.

caption: Benchmarking of Sine structure mechanical properties against existing literature data for bone implant materials.
summary: This comparative plot positions the mechanical properties of Sine structures against existing studies. The analysis highlights the specific advantage of the Sine structure, which is its suitability for ultralow-modulus bone implants, demonstrating superior performance in meeting the design requirements for modern orthopedic medical devices.

caption: Atom probe tomography reconstruction showing solute clusters within a 10 × 20 × 20 nm³ volume at a depth of 710 nm under single-energy ion irradiation.
summary: Visualizing the microstructure at 710 nm depth under single-energy irradiation, this reconstruction demonstrates a clear reduction in cluster number density and size. These findings suggest that the nucleation and growth of MnNiSi clusters are significantly suppressed at this greater depth, likely influenced by the specific irradiation conditions and implanted ion content.

caption: Measured drift time spectrum of DT3 displaying signal intensity in nA versus drift time in ms, highlighting preRIP, RIP, five specific ketones, and red-circled dimer species.
summary: This spectrum, measured using the DT3 instrument, illustrates the signal intensity as a function of drift time. The plot identifies various chemical components, including preRIP, RIP, and five distinct ketones (2-hexanone, 4-heptanone, 2-heptanone, 2-octanone, and 2-nonanone). Additionally, dimer species and overlapping dimers are clearly marked with red circles.

caption: Bending toughness dependence on annealing temperature for Fe84-xCoxSi2B13P1 metallic glasses, highlighting the mechanical response to thermal processing.
summary: Bending toughness values for Fe84-xCoxSi2B13P1 metallic glasses are presented relative to annealing temperature. The results demonstrate a correlation between thermal treatment and mechanical integrity, specifically noting that increasing the temperature to 585 K leads to crack formation along localized shear bands in Fe78Co6, corresponding to a reduction in bending toughness.

caption: PDOS distribution for Fe, O, and Al atoms at the Fe/Al2O3 interface.
summary: Displayed are the PDOS plots for Fe atoms, O atoms, and Al atoms at the interface of the Fe/Al2O3 pre-nucleation model. These electronic density of states results highlight the specific contributions of iron, oxygen, and aluminum atoms to the electronic structure at the oxide/Fe interface.

caption: Grain size distribution map of the central region of the T-CMT-DED stainless steel sample, illustrating the spatial arrangement and scale of the grains.
summary: This grain size figure, derived from the central region of the T-CMT-DED component, provides a detailed visualization of the microstructural characteristics. By employing EBSD technology, the map illustrates the grain size distribution, which serves as a critical indicator of the microstructural development within the T-CMT-DED stainless steel sample.

caption: Graphical representation of the effective toughness (Γ) calculated for the DCB joints.
summary: This plot displays the effective toughness (Γ) values derived for the DCB joints. It serves as a key metric for evaluating the fracture resistance of the joints, providing a clear visualization of the toughness characteristics as determined through the established experimental and numerical analysis procedures.

caption: Pearson correlation coefficients for Al-Ni-Er-Zr-Y-Yb alloy properties modeled via equilibrium and Scheil calculations, with parameters color-coded by their relevance to high-temperature strength (magenta), room-temperature strength (maroon), or both (cyan).
summary: This heatmap displays Pearson correlation coefficients for Al-Ni-Er-Zr-Y-Yb alloy properties derived from equilibrium and Scheil modeling. Parameters are categorized by their influence on high-temperature and room-temperature strength using specific color coding. Notably, Er shows a strong correlation with high L1 2 phase percentages, highlighting its critical role in alloy performance.

caption: Bacterial colony formation of E. coli on the surface of control casting 316L stainless steel.
summary: Shown here are the bacterial colonies of E. coli formed on the surface of the control casting 316L stainless steel. This panel serves as a baseline for comparison, illustrating the extent of bacterial colonization on standard stainless steel without the addition of copper, which is essential for evaluating the antibacterial efficacy of the 316L-4.5Cu alloy.

caption: Octavoid (OV) tessellation unit cell featuring eight-cornered voids.
summary: This panel presents the Octavoid (OV) tessellation, formed by interlocking each peak of the main origami cell with eight surrounding cells. The resulting structure features eight-cornered voids, illustrating a complex, highly interconnected tessellation pattern derived from the primary origami tube design through systematic geometric arrangement.

caption: Full discharge profiles of the CX@Fe cathode at 0.1 mA/cm2, showing the initial discharge (solid line) and a subsequent discharge (dashed line) after electrode washing.
summary: The discharge profile of the CX@Fe cathode is presented at a current density of 0.1 mA/cm2. The solid line represents the initial full discharge until 2 V cut-off, indicating complete surface passivation. A subsequent discharge, shown as a dashed line, confirms the electrochemical behavior under identical testing conditions.

caption: Normalized XRD diffractograms comparing templates, green body, untextured, and textured KNN samples fabricated via VPP.
summary: Normalized XRD diffractograms are presented for templates, green body, and sintered samples fabricated using VPP. The comparison includes both untextured and textured 10 wt% templated KNN samples. These patterns illustrate the structural evolution and phase characteristics of the materials across different processing stages and textures, with intensities normalized by the highest peak.

caption: Phase map of the interface region, where blank areas represent unidentified phases.
summary: The phase map identifies the distribution of different phases at the bonding interface, with blank regions indicating unknown phases. This analysis is essential for characterizing the oxide film area and the nanograined zone, where TiO2 grains are observed to persist within the shear zone of the interface.

caption: Logarithmic creep rate plotted against accumulated strain for as-cast ERBO/1, ERBO/15, and derivative alloys under 1323 K and 160 MPa conditions.
summary: Representing the creep behavior as the logarithm of the strain rate versus strain, this panel highlights the deformation kinetics of the as-cast materials. The results confirm that all four alloys undergo primary creep, with global creep rate minima occurring at accumulated strains of less than 2% during testing.

caption: Engineering stress-strain curves for horizontally built (XY plane) Haynes 188 specimens fabricated via LPBF, demonstrating the influence of varying laser energy densities on tensile performance.
summary: Engineering stress-strain curves for horizontally built Haynes 188 specimens fabricated via LPBF illustrate the critical role of laser energy density in tailoring mechanical properties. These curves demonstrate how varying processing parameters directly impact the tensile behavior of the alloy under ambient-temperature testing conditions, highlighting the sensitivity of the material to energy input.

caption: Statistical orientation distribution of stimulated grains across three distinct material substrates.
summary: This figure displays the quantitative statistical results regarding the orientation distribution of stimulated grains observed in three different material samples. The histogram provides a comparative analysis of how grain orientations are distributed across these specific substrates, offering insights into the microstructural characteristics resulting from the stimulation process across the tested materials.

caption: Probabilities of distinct atomic swap types plotted as a function of inverse temperature β and atomic coupling constant J, normalized by the total number of pair occurrences observed during the Monte Carlo simulation.
summary: This plot illustrates the probabilities of various atomic swap types as a function of inverse temperature β and atomic coupling constant J. These probabilities, normalized by the total number of pair occurrences during the simulation, were used to estimate base probabilities by fitting a 13-degree polynomial to the observed curves.

caption: Illustration of two distinct HEA/UHEA design strategies, contrasting a key-element-centric approach with an equal-weighting strategy based on pairwise cosine similarities.
summary: Two primary design strategies for HEAs and UHEAs are illustrated: one approach prioritizes a key element and its most similar neighbors, while the other treats all elements equally by averaging pairwise cosine similarities. This comparison evaluates candidate potency and informs how elemental selection influences overall material performance and stability.

caption: Normalized stress–strain response of pentamode lattices, where stress is adjusted by sample weight to evaluate specific mechanical performance, highlighting the 3% relative density lattice as the most efficient design.
summary: Normalized stress–strain response with respect to weight reveals the specific performance of the pentamode lattices. The 3% relative density lattice exhibits the highest specific performance, maintaining a relatively high stress for its mass throughout the compression process compared to other tested densities.

caption: Specific heat capacity as a function of electronic temperature for pure Ni (grey dashed line) and equiatomic NiFe (blue solid line), calculated using the coherent potential approximation (CPA).
summary: This plot illustrates the specific heat capacity for Ni and NiFe systems across a range of electronic temperatures. The data, derived from coherent potential approximation (CPA) calculations, demonstrates the comparative thermal response of pure Ni and the equiatomic NiFe alloy, highlighting the influence of electronic temperature on these materials.

caption: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) image corresponding to the nano-twin and stacking fault layer shown in panel (i).
summary: The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis of the high-resolution TEM image in panel (i) validates the presence of deformation twins. This diffraction pattern confirms the structural identity of the twin boundaries, providing evidence for the thermally activated twin-mediated plasticity mechanism occurring in the alloy at 800 °C.

caption: Partial density of states (PDOS) for (TmNiO3)1/(CaNiO3)1 superlattices, detailing the half-metallic gap and mean magnetic moments for Ni-3d and O-2p states.
summary: Panel h displays the PDOS for the Tm-based superlattice. It includes the half-metallic gap of the down-spin channel and the mean magnetic moments for Ni-3d and O-2p states. This panel is essential for tracking the electronic structure evolution as the lanthanide element changes toward the end of the series.

caption: Bright field TEM image of the 1080S specimen showing stacking faults within the gamma channels, indicated by yellow triangles.
summary: Bright field TEM imaging of the 1080S alloy reveals the presence of stacking faults located within the gamma channels. These structural defects are highlighted by yellow triangles, confirming the existence of gamma stacking faults as observed through transmission electron microscopy analysis of the material's microstructure.

caption: Low-magnification STEM image of as-built IN738LC showing the grain structure.
summary: This low-magnification STEM image displays the as-built microstructure of IN738LC. The analysis reveals two distinct grains separated by a boundary. The matrix consists of a continuous gamma-phase structure, providing an overview of the grain morphology and the distribution of internal features within the as-built material state.

caption: Thermodynamic equilibrium concentration of N2O species during DA-SOFC operation across various fuel utilization conditions and temperatures.
summary: Thermodynamic equilibrium composition calculations for N2O emissions are shown across different fuel utilization conditions and temperatures. These results suggest that NOx emissions, including N2O, are a negligible concern during DA-SOFC operation, indicating that the system maintains favorable environmental characteristics under the evaluated thermodynamic equilibrium conditions.

caption: Comparison of specific energy absorption (SEA) values for various lattice structures across different matrix materials and configurations, highlighting performance variations relative to existing literature.
summary: This plot evaluates the specific energy absorption of lattice structures by comparing current experimental results against data from related studies. It encompasses a diverse range of matrix materials and structural configurations, providing a comprehensive benchmark to assess the mechanical efficiency and performance stability of the lattices developed in this research.

caption: Contour plot illustrating the functional dependence of the thermal parameter θ on the variables τ, ξ, and η for niobium (Nb).
summary: This contour plot visualizes the thermal parameter θ as a function of τ, ξ, and η for niobium. Higher values of θ correspond to increased thermal energy generation within the system, leading to a rise in temperature. The figure effectively demonstrates the influence of these variables on the thermal state of Nb.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profiles confirming the chemical purity of the Al particle (point 1) and the Ti particle (point 2).
summary: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy analysis was performed to verify the chemical composition of the feedstock particles. The resulting spectra confirm that the particles analyzed at points 1 and 2 consist of pure aluminum and pure titanium, respectively, validating the material purity of the feedstock.

caption: Evolution of the C11 component of the damaged stiffness matrix for fibers oriented at 90 degrees, indicating no reduction due to detachment damage.
summary: This panel shows the C11 stiffness component evolution for 90-degree fiber orientation. Unlike the 0-degree case, there is no reduction in this component because it is only affected by detachment damage. The trend follows the C22 component, as both are regulated by the same damage variable.

caption: Ce 3d XPS core-level spectrum of the spent CeNi BA@Al2O3 catalyst, revealing the oxidation states of cerium.
summary: The Ce 3d XPS spectrum of the spent CeNi BA@Al2O3 catalyst shows the presence of Ce 3+ and Ce 4+ species. The substantial increase in Ce 3+ content post-reaction promotes reversible charge transfer between cerium oxidation states, which is directly accompanied by the generation of additional oxygen vacancies in the catalyst.

caption: Relative feature importance scores identifying the influence of input variables on the predicted wear rate.
summary: This feature importance plot ranks the influence of input variables on the wear rate prediction. Analysis reveals that Al content is the most significant factor, followed by the H3/E2 ratio, wear form, and VHT temperature, providing critical insights into the primary drivers of the material's wear behavior.

caption: Magnetization versus temperature curves measured at a constant 50mT field for various positions along a DS rod, highlighting the martensitic and austenitic transition temperatures (Ms, Mf, As, Af) and the premartensitic transformation (Mp).
summary: This plot displays magnetization versus temperature curves for different positions of a DS rod under a 50mT magnetic field. Key phase transition temperatures, including Ms, Mf, As, and Af, are determined via linear extrapolation. Additionally, the curves reveal an abrupt magnetization decrease corresponding to the premartensitic transformation, denoted as Mp.

caption: Time-temperature-deformation diagram illustrating the thermomechanical processing (TMP) routes, including water quenching (WQ) and compression direction (CD), with key strain and stress values (εp and σp) for dynamic recrystallization initiation.
summary: This time-temperature-deformation diagram outlines the various thermomechanical processing routes applied to the samples using a Gleeble 3500 simulator. It compiles critical strain and stress values, specifically εp and σp, which are essential for determining the initiation of dynamic recrystallization during the processing of the alloy compositions.

caption: Transmission spectra of synthesized Au nanoparticles suspended in water, showing the characteristic optical response as the solution transitions to a wine-red color.
summary: The transmission spectra of synthesized Au nanoparticles suspended in water are presented. The solution exhibits a distinct wine-red color over time, which signifies the successful development of the nanoparticles. This optical transition is captured in the transmission data, reflecting the characteristic behavior of the Au NP solution during synthesis.

caption: Schematic representation of the sampling location at the bottom of the fin section.
summary: This diagram highlights the extraction point for a 10 mm by 20 mm specimen taken from the bottom of the fin. By isolating this region, researchers can perform detailed cross-sectional analysis of the welding direction, providing critical insights into the structural integrity and microstructural characteristics at the base of the fin.

caption: False colour representation derived from the AOLP image, highlighting the spatial distribution of fibre orientations.
summary: Derived from the raw AOLP data, this false colour image provides a visual mapping of fibre orientations. By converting polarisation information into a colour-coded format, the image facilitates the identification of structural patterns and orientation variations across the specimen, as supported by the reference documentation.

caption: Correlation plot between the first principal component of the stress-strain curves and the maximum macroscopic stress observed during testing.
summary: This plot illustrates the relationship between the first principal component of the macroscopic stress-strain curves and the maximum macroscopic stress. A strong positive correlation is observed, indicating that the first principal component effectively captures the variation in maximum stress values across the analyzed mechanical test data.

caption: Summary table of histological evaluation scores based on UNE-EN ISO 10,993–6:2017 standards, detailing inflammatory response, new blood vessel formation, fibrosis, and fatty infiltrate levels.
summary: This table presents the semi-quantitative histological assessment of local tissue effects following implantation. Scores ranging from 0 to 4 are assigned to parameters including inflammatory response, angiogenesis, fibrosis, and fatty infiltration. These metrics, derived from Lévai-Laczkó stained slides, provide a standardized evaluation of biocompatibility according to UNE-EN ISO 10,993–6:2017 protocols.

caption: Oxygen reduction detection using a rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) system at 1600 rpm, with the ring biased at 0.2 V vs. RHE, demonstrating negligible oxygen reduction current for CuNi@BNC, confirming the suppression of OER and dominance of AOR.
summary: Oxygen reduction detection via RRDE at 1600 rpm reveals that CuNi@BNC produces nearly negligible oxygen reduction current at the ring electrode. This result confirms the effective suppression of the oxygen evolution reaction and the dominance of the ammonia oxidation reaction under the specified experimental conditions for the CuNi@BNC catalyst.

caption: Temperature-dependent magnetic moment of a 110-nm-thick alpha-Fe2O3 film, normalized to the 300 K value, measured during a 50 to 300 K sweep under a 50 Oe field following field annealing.
summary: This panel displays the in-plane magnetic moment of a 110-nm-thick hematite film as a function of temperature. The measurement, conducted from 50 to 300 K in a 50 Oe field, reveals the Morin transition, where the magnetic moment begins to increase rapidly with rising temperature, as indicated by the sweep direction.

caption: Thermal expansion curves showing the change in length as a function of temperature for S1 and S2 alloys.
summary: Figure 10a displays the thermal expansion behavior of S1 and S2 alloys by plotting the change in sample length against temperature.
