summary: The modification efficiency of the ENs was assessed using FITC-labeled streptavidin. Fluorescence microscopy images display green fluorescence on the vesicles, providing clear evidence that biotin was successfully modified onto the surface of the ENs, confirming the efficacy of the biotinylation process.

caption: Nyquist plots showing the electrochemical impedance response of as-built WAAM SDSS and Hot-rolled SDSS samples in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 °C, where all specimens exhibit typical capacitive arc characteristics.
summary: Nyquist plots for as-built WAAM SDSS and Hot-rolled SDSS samples tested in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 °C are presented. These plots demonstrate that all tested samples exhibit typical capacitive arc characteristics, indicating the electrochemical impedance behavior of the passive films formed on the different material surfaces.

caption: Geometric configuration of the Gyroid unit cell featuring horizontal and inclined sheets oriented at ±45° relative to the horizontal plane.
summary: The Gyroid unit cell architecture is defined by its specific geometric arrangement, characterized by horizontal and inclined sheets. These structural elements are oriented at angles of ±45° to the horizontal plane, establishing the fundamental geometric shape and symmetry characteristics of the unit cell design within the material structure.

caption: Correlation between the Z-parameter and peak stress values observed in the HIP-1230 alloy.
summary: The relationship between the Z-parameter and peak stress for the HIP-1230 alloy is presented here. Utilizing the calculated deformation activation energy, linear regression is performed on the data to extract the material constants A and n, which are essential for characterizing the flow stress behavior of the alloy under deformation.

caption: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns showing the evolution of γ’ and M23C6 carbide phases in the as-manufactured state aged at 750 °C for durations ranging from 0.5 h to 901 h, with an inset highlighting the superlattice reflections.
summary: Synchrotron X-ray diffraction patterns track the precipitation kinetics of γ’ and M23C6 carbides in the as-manufactured alloy aged at 750 °C. Comparison between the solution heat-treated condition and various aging durations allows for phase identification, as evidenced by the superlattice reflections shown in the inset of the diffraction data.

caption: SHAP summary plot illustrating the influence of printing parameters on radius error, with features ranked by descending impact.
summary: This SHAP summary plot ranks printing parameters by their influence on radius error in CCFRP 3D printing. The setting radius exhibits the greatest impact, followed by the twisted angle and print width, demonstrating that yarn twist plays a more significant role in reducing radius errors than the small yarn diameter.

caption: Bright-field TEM image of the annealed alloy corresponding to the red dashed box in panel (d).
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging of the annealed alloy, focused on the region indicated in panel (d), provides a clear view of the structural features present after heat treatment. This imaging technique complements the HAADF-STEM data, offering further evidence of the phase distribution and stability within the annealed material.

caption: Adhesion strength measurements plotted as a function of varying surface roughness levels.
summary: Adhesion strength measurements are plotted as a function of varying surface roughness levels. This mechanical test data illustrates how surface topography influences the adhesive performance of the material. The results, as detailed in Fig. 9, provide a quantitative assessment of the relationship between roughness and the resulting adhesion strength values.

caption: Tabulated test matrix detailing the 48 individual parameter combinations used for the parametric study of the production process, ordered by water content.
summary: This table presents the systematic test matrix comprising 48 unique parameter combinations designed to evaluate the production process. By varying key factors such as moisture content, heating time, pressing time, and compression ratio, the matrix provides a structured framework for defining future bulk material qualities and establishing viable production boundary conditions.

caption: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy profile confirming the elemental composition of the stir zone nanocomposite.
summary: The EDS spectrum analysis provides quantitative confirmation of the elemental constituents present within the stir zone. By identifying the characteristic peaks of the elements, this spectroscopic data validates the composition of the aluminum-based nanocomposite, supporting the microstructural observations of the processed material after three friction stir processing passes.

caption: Schematic representation of the in vitro enzymatic biodegradation mechanism, illustrating the sequential steps of enzymatic fluid penetration, scaffold swelling, and polymer chain cleavage into oligomers and monomers.
summary: The enzymatic biodegradation process is illustrated as a multi-step mechanism. It begins with the penetration of the enzymatic simulated body fluid into the scaffold pores, followed by scaffold swelling. Finally, the polymeric chains undergo cleavage, resulting in the formation of oligomers and monomers as the primary biodegradation products of the composite material.

caption: XGBoost (XGB) model ROC curve performance metrics on the unseen test set.
summary: XGBoost model performance is depicted via an ROC curve on the unseen test set. The plot features five curves, including four for individual classes and one for the micro-average, providing a comprehensive assessment of the XGB model's ability to correctly classify instances within the unseen test dataset.

caption: Ternary scatter plot illustrating the zero-shear viscosity distribution across the ethanol-glycerol-water composition space.
summary: This ternary scatter plot maps the zero-shear viscosity across the ethanol-glycerol-water composition space. The visualization helps investigate the relationship between solution ratios and their resulting viscosities. High viscosity peaks are observed in the middle region of the ternary plot, specifically where ethanol exceeds 20% and alginate concentration is above 2% w/v.

caption: Longitudinal inverse pole figure map of the Al-Mg-Sc-Ti alloy, illustrating the grain orientation and morphology characteristic of the titanium-modified microstructure.
summary: The longitudinal inverse pole figure map of the Al-Mg-Sc-Ti alloy provides insight into the grain morphology and orientation relationship of this specific LPBF-manufactured composition. EBSD analysis reveals the structural features resulting from the titanium inoculation, contributing to the overall comparison of grain characteristics across the four alloys.

caption: Hydrogen desorption spectrum measured at a heating rate of 300 °C/h, featuring experimental data points overlaid with a Gaussian-fitted curve.
summary: This panel displays the hydrogen desorption spectrum for a material heated at 300 °C/h. The experimental data is deconvoluted using a Gaussian peak function to identify specific trap sites. This analysis, combined with other heating rates, allows for the quantification of hydrogen release from distinct microstructural trapping sites.

caption: Coarse-level converged solution for the narrowest relative density interval, resulting in a nearly solid-and-void material distribution.
summary: This coarse-level solution utilizes the narrowest density interval, leading to an almost solid-and-void material distribution. It highlights the extreme case of the threshold study, where only a limited number of cells undergo optimization at the fine level, demonstrating the sensitivity of the distribution to narrow density constraints.

caption: High-resolution XPS spectrum of the Cu 2p region for the Cu6-MAO coating, showing peak fitting results.
summary: High-resolution XPS spectra and corresponding peak fitting results for the Cu 2p region of the Cu6-MAO coating are shown. This detailed analysis identifies the oxidation states of copper within the coating, providing critical information regarding the chemical composition and surface characteristics resulting from the micro-arc oxidation treatment.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern obtained from the red marked region in (a), showing the diffraction characteristics of the bainite block area.
summary: The SAED pattern from the red marked region in the TEM micrograph characterizes the bainite block area. Comparison with the thin-film region indicates that the diffraction patterns are almost identical, suggesting that the thin-film structure shares the same phase features as the adjacent α' matrix without detectable γ phase.

caption: Fluorescence emission spectra of 1a (2.98 × 10⁻⁵ M) in acetonitrile solution, showing progressive quenching upon the incremental addition of EDB quencher under 400 nm excitation.
summary: Fluorescence quenching experiments were conducted on 1a in acetonitrile to investigate interactions with the additive EDB. The spectra demonstrate a clear reduction in fluorescence intensity as the concentration of EDB increases, confirming the quenching effect of the additive on the BODIPY dye 1a under 400 nm excitation.

caption: Hardness versus indentation depth curves for ODS Fe-Cr steel before and after 6 MeV Au+ ion irradiation, showing reduced hardening increments of 16.2%, 66.0%, and 70.6% at 20, 40, and 80 dpa.
summary: These curves illustrate the mechanical response of ODS Fe-Cr steel subjected to varying levels of ion irradiation. Compared to the Fe-Cr counterpart, the ODS steel exhibits markedly lower hardening increments under identical irradiation conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of Y-Ti-O nanoprecipitates in mitigating irradiation-induced hardening across all tested damage levels.

caption: Pourbaix diagram for the Mn/S/H2O system at 288 °C, highlighting the stability regions of SO4 2− and Mn2O3 under NWC conditions.
summary: This Pourbaix diagram for the Mn/S/H2O system at 288 °C illustrates the thermodynamic stability of species in aqueous environments. The blue square marks NWC conditions, where MnS dissolves to form SO4 2− and Mn2O3. The addition of trace H2SO4 for conductivity control is noted to have negligible effects on pH.

caption: Flank wear progression during machining with the application of coolant.
summary: Machining performance using coolant is displayed in panel b. The data indicates that this specific condition results in the shortest tool life attained across the entire test series. The plot quantifies the flank wear evolution, highlighting the reduced durability of the tool when subjected to these cooling parameters.

caption: Mapping of cells at different differentiation stages onto the established developmental trajectory.
summary: Cells at various stages of differentiation are mapped onto the trajectory, revealing a gradual transition toward the pancreatic progenitor stage. The analysis indicates that β-like cells primarily emerge during the late stages of development, demonstrating the temporal progression of cell identity along the established pseudo-time path.

caption: Diffusion path plotted on the Ni-Cr-Al phase diagram, identifying the Kirkendall plane, characteristic features 1-4, interdiffusion zone boundaries, and end-member compositions.
summary: This diffusion path on the Ni-Cr-Al phase diagram exhibits a zig-zag morphology similar to previous literature, though it lacks a concentration jump at the interphase boundary. An outward-horn-like structure near the 2L composition is noted, though it may be an artifact of EDS measurement errors rather than a physical feature.

caption: Thermogravimetric analysis comparing the weight loss of resin substrates and PEEK inks after high-temperature treatment.
summary: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) curves compare the thermal stability of resin substrates and PEEK inks following high-temperature treatment. The data reveals that PEEK exhibits significantly lower weight loss than the resin, even when accounting for PEEK percentage variations, demonstrating that PEEK incorporation effectively improves the overall thermal stability of the material.

caption: 2.5D deviation height map of the horizontal SPY 4 mm channel, illustrating the distribution of dross defects that increase steadily toward the ceiling center.
summary: This 2.5D height map visualizes the surface deviations of the horizontal SPY 4 mm channel. Dross defects are observed to appear at a steadily increasing pace toward the ceiling center of the channel, providing a clear representation of the surface profile and defect distribution within this specific geometry.

caption: Time-dependent evolution of the diffraction 2θ angle in the normal direction for through-thickness points 1–5 during in-situ heat treatment.
summary: This plot illustrates the evolution of the diffraction 2θ angle during in-situ heat treatment of Waspaloy across the thickness (points 1–5). The data reflects changes in the normal direction, providing insight into the material's structural response and residual strain behavior as the temperature changes during the thermal processing cycle.

caption: Cross-sectional surface profile of the wear zone for sample B27, processed at an energy density of 617 J/mm3.
summary: Sample B27, fabricated at an energy density of 617 J/mm3, displays this surface profile measured at the center of the wear track. This measurement is part of a comparative analysis intended to quantify the wear behavior of the samples, illustrating the impact of varying energy densities on wear track geometry.

caption: Global root mean square error of cross-validation (RMSECV) plotted against the number of components for the AS system regression model.
summary: This plot illustrates the global RMSECV for the AS system regression model. Analysis of the curve indicates that the optimal number of components is two, as this value corresponds to the first local minimum point observed in the validation process, ensuring an efficient and accurate model configuration.

caption: Grain boundary map of the LPBF ZGH4142 specimen, illustrating the distribution of high-angle and low-angle grain boundaries.
summary: The LPBF ZGH4142 specimen grain boundary map displays the distribution of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) and low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs). This structural characterization serves as a baseline, as the grain boundaries in subsequent HT1 and HT2 heat-treated specimens remain similar to this printed state.

caption: High-resolution three-dimensional surface topography of the composite obtained by atomic force microscopy over a 2 × 2 μm scan area.
summary: Detailed surface topography of the composite is shown using atomic force microscopy at a smaller 2 × 2 μm scan area. This high-resolution visualization allows for a precise assessment of surface roughness parameters, which are known to be dependent on the specific dimensions of the area being analyzed.

caption: Deconvoluted O 1s XPS spectrum of the α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene nanohybrid, detailing the oxygen bonding environments.
summary: The O 1s XPS spectrum provides a detailed analysis of the oxygen bonding environments present in the α-Fe-O-FPs/MXene nanohybrid. By deconvoluting the spectrum, the various oxygen species associated with the iron-based components and the MXene substrate are identified, offering insight into the surface chemistry and oxidation states of the material.

caption: LSV curve of the monolithic perovskite/Si/Ni foil/NiFe photoanode integrated with a Ni nanowire cathode for unassisted overall water splitting.
summary: The integrated overall water splitting system, consisting of the perovskite/Si/Ni foil/NiFe photoanode and Ni nanowire cathode, is evaluated under continuous illumination. The system achieves a current density of 12.3 mA cm-2 at 0 V, demonstrating effective unassisted water splitting performance in a 1.0 M KOH electrolyte.

caption: Flatwise compression test result for the sandwich structure sample without a face layer, showing honeycomb core buckling.
summary: This photograph displays the flatwise compression test result for a sandwich structure lacking a face layer. The specimen exhibits a distinct deformation mechanism characterized by the buckling of the honeycomb core. This structural failure mode is consistent across all tested sandwich configurations, highlighting the core's role in energy absorption.

caption: Temperature increase (ΔT) versus exposure time to a 268 kHz, 200 Oe alternating magnetic field for FeCaP1–40 powders in non-calcined (NC) state and after calcination at 700 °C and 1000 °C.
summary: This plot illustrates the magnetic hyperthermia performance of FeCaP1–40 powders under an alternating magnetic field. Non-calcined samples show minimal heating, with a ΔT of approximately 3.5 °C after 5 minutes. Calcination at 700 °C and 1000 °C significantly enhances the temperature increase, reflecting improved ferromagnetic behavior in the treated materials.

caption: Flashforge Guider IIs FDM 3D printer utilized for the manufacturing of experimental specimens.
summary: The Flashforge Guider IIs FDM 3D printer is presented as the primary equipment used for specimen manufacturing. This system provides precise control over various printing parameters, which is essential for ensuring high levels of reproducibility and dimensional accuracy in the fabricated parts throughout the experimental process.

caption: Geometric parameters defining the metamaterial unit cell architecture, specifically the triangle angle θ, strut thickness t, and base-to-side offset o.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometric design parameters used to create varied unit cell architectures in CAD software. Key features include the triangle angle θ, the thickness t of the struts in the XY-plane, and the offset o between the triangle base and its sides, which collectively define the metamaterial structure.

caption: Dark-field TEM image highlighting the distribution of residual austenite in the 15Ni-CT sample.
summary: Dark-field TEM imaging provides a focused view of the residual austenite phase within the 15Ni-CT sample. By isolating the diffraction signal from the austenite, this panel confirms the blocky morphology and spatial distribution of the phase, complementing the bright-field observations to characterize the microstructure of the 15Ni-CT material.

caption: Architecture of the feature generator MNet, which utilizes a U-Net-inspired structure with parallel kernels of varying sizes to predict initial stress fields from composite configuration data.
summary: The feature generator is an MNet model designed to imitate a U-Net architecture. By employing parallel kernels of various sizes, it enhances extrapolation capabilities to accurately predict initial stress fields based on input configuration data of the grid composite, serving as the first component of the hierarchical DNN model.

caption: Room temperature electron carrier concentration plotted against Ni alloying content in Bi2-xNixSe3 samples, showing a continuous increase from 1.24 × 10^18/cm^3 to 7.02 × 10^18/cm^3.
summary: This plot displays the room temperature electron carrier concentration for Bi2-xNixSe3 samples as a function of Ni content. Hall measurements reveal that the carrier concentration increases monotonically from 1.24 × 10^18/cm^3 to 7.02 × 10^18/cm^3 as the Ni alloying content rises, indicating a significant modification of the electronic properties.

caption: SAED pattern obtained from a large cuboidal γ′ precipitate along the [011]γ zone axis, displaying intense superlattice spots characteristic of the ordered precipitate structure.
summary: This SAED pattern corresponds to a large cuboidal γ′ precipitate viewed along the [011]γ zone axis. The presence of intense superlattice spots, observed when the diffraction pattern is collected solely from the precipitate, confirms the ordered nature of the γ′ phase within the AA-HTA specimen.

caption: Atomic configuration snapshot representing the second layer of the Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 alloy during the W-DED process as modeled by molecular dynamics.
summary: This panel displays an MD simulation snapshot of the atomic arrangement for the second layer of Ti6Al4V-NbZr1 during the W-DED process. The visualization provides insight into the structural evolution at the early stage of the additive manufacturing simulation, illustrating the specific atomic configuration achieved at this layer.

caption: Resistivity versus temperature curves for Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires subjected to 1k fatigue cycles, measured under different parallel magnetic field strengths.
summary: Resistivity measurements for Ni46Mn23Ga22Co5Cu4 microwires after 1k fatigue cycles are shown under varying parallel magnetic fields. The data demonstrates that magnetic field application consistently reduces low-temperature resistivity across the tested conditions, consistent with the suppression of spin electron scattering and martensite reorientation mechanisms observed in the as-prepared state.

caption: Binary phase diagram of the Ti-Cu system illustrating the thermodynamic stability regions and the formation of various intermetallic compounds.
summary: This figure presents the binary phase diagram of the Ti-Cu system, detailing the thermodynamic equilibrium states across varying compositions and temperatures. It highlights the stable intermetallic compounds formed within this binary system, providing a comprehensive overview of the phase relationships and structural transitions characteristic of Ti-Cu alloys under equilibrium conditions.

caption: High-resolution O 1s XPS spectra of MEX printed samples subjected to Fe beam irradiation at doses ranging from 0 to 80 Gy.
summary: High-resolution O 1s XPS spectra are presented for MEX printed samples exposed to Fe beam irradiation at doses of 0.2, 2, 8, and 80 Gy compared to pristine samples. The spectra reveal distinct peaks at 531.5 eV and 533.5 eV, corresponding to C=O and C-O bonds, respectively, indicating surface chemical composition.

caption: Scanning electron micrograph of grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V powder particles, highlighting the high degree of sphericity and the presence of satellite particles indicated by red arrows.
summary: This SEM image displays grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V powder, which exhibits a high degree of sphericity characteristic of plasma-atomized production. The micrograph reveals the morphology of the feedstock, specifically identifying satellite particles attached to the primary spherical powder surfaces, which are marked with red arrows for clear visualization.

caption: Longitudinal X-ray µ-CT slice of the CO50/40/10 specimen gauge section highlighting internal structure.
summary: This longitudinal X-ray µ-CT slice of the CO50/40/10 specimen provides a detailed view of the internal composite structure after consolidation. The image highlights the quality of yarn positioning within the gauge section, contributing to the comparative analysis of the four different sample types examined in the study.

caption: Fluorescence microscopy images of LC-SPI25 and LC-SPI25GLY scaffolds at 1, 3, and 7 days of culture, displaying live cells in green and dead cells in red with a 200 μm scale bar.
summary: Fluorescence microscopy images of LC-SPI25 and LC-SPI25GLY scaffolds at 1, 3, and 7 days of culture, displaying live cells in green and dead cells in red with a 200 μm scale bar. These scaffolds demonstrate high cell confluence and a typical fibroblastic phenotype throughout the entire studied culture period.

caption: Overview of the stereo-digital image correlation (DIC) experimental configuration utilized for monitoring gauge displacements during tensile testing.
summary: This photograph illustrates the experimental setup employed for measuring sample gauge displacements during tensile testing. The configuration utilizes a stereo-DIC technique to capture deformation data. Specific parameters regarding the stereo-DIC setup and the subsequent image correlation process are detailed in the accompanying technical data provided in Table 5.

caption: Transmission spectra of the immersion solution at pH 10, displaying results for room temperature (left) and 37 °C (right) to evaluate stability in an alkaline environment.
summary: In an alkaline environment of pH 10, the buffer transmission spectra exhibit insignificant changes over time at both room temperature and 37 °C. The consistent transmission near 100% across all periods confirms that the Au NPs remain stable within the 3D printed nanocomposite hydrogel without significant leakage.

caption: Microstructure of the sample following a 16-hour secondary aging treatment.
summary: Captured after 16 hours of secondary aging, this panel reveals the final microstructural state. The grain size distribution has become more concentrated compared to earlier stages, demonstrating the long-term effects of the aging process on the material's internal morphology and the stabilization of the γ′ phase distribution.

caption: Transformation enthalpies upon heating and cooling for NiTi powder and LBPFed samples, highlighting the impact of PW versus CW laser emission modes.
summary: This plot shows transformation enthalpies for NiTi samples, revealing that LBPFed specimens exhibit increased values up to 20-21 J/g. Furthermore, the data demonstrates that pulsed wave (PW) laser emission induces higher enthalpy values (20-22 J/g) compared to continuous wave (CW) mode (16-20 J/g), indicating significant processing-dependent thermal behavior.

caption: Specific areal capacitance values for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors as a function of the number of stacked OTU layers, derived from galvanostatic charge-discharge measurements.
summary: Specific areal capacitance values for 3D-IDCμE/PPy micro-supercapacitors are plotted against the number of stacked OTU layers. These values, calculated from galvanostatic charge-discharge curves, quantify the energy storage performance improvements achieved by increasing the number of stacked layers, with an areal mass loading of PPy measured at 18 ± 3 mg/cm².

caption: DMA trace of the cured CCF/epoxy composites, indicating a glass transition temperature of 279.24 °C.
summary: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA) trace of the cured CCF/epoxy composites demonstrates the material's viscoelastic response. The results indicate a significantly high glass transition temperature (Tg) of 279.24 °C, which is determined by the peak of the tan(δ) curve, reflecting the robust thermal performance of the composite system.

caption: Optimization iterations versus P1 frequency output error, demonstrating a convergence to an error below 1 GHz after 2500 iterations.
summary: This panel illustrates the correlation between the number of optimization iterations and the P1 frequency output error for the FNN architecture. The results reveal that the error reduction drops below 1 GHz after 2500 iterations, confirming the effectiveness of the optimization algorithm in refining the frequency prediction performance.

caption: Multiple arrest events recorded for Ni55Fe18Nd2Ga25 ribbons following a thermal treatment process of 1 hour at 400 °C.
summary: This panel presents the magnetic thermal memory behavior of Ni55Fe18Nd2Ga25 ribbons after undergoing a specific thermal treatment of 1 hour at 400 °C. The data demonstrates that the material retains multiple arrest characteristics even after this heat treatment, confirming the persistence of the observed magnetic properties.

caption: Atomic force microscopy analysis of surface roughness for HP, HPD, and HPDM scaffolds, highlighting the increased height variation in the HPDM variant.
summary: AFM analysis characterizes the surface roughness of the three porous scaffolds. Results indicate that dopamine modification significantly increases surface roughness, with the HPDM scaffold exhibiting the greatest height variation. This enhanced surface topography is specifically noted to be more conducive to promoting effective cell adhesion on the scaffold.

caption: Current spectrum (CS) map for the resonant peak at 0.22 V, illustrating the spatial distribution of current flow through the quantum well structure.
summary: This current spectrum map for the resonant peak at 0.22 V reveals a strong band of current flowing through the ground quantum well. Additionally, a smaller current channel is visible through the first excited quantum well eigenvalue, demonstrating the electronic transport characteristics within the 55 nm long RTD device structure.

caption: Tabulated range of laser welding parameters utilized for the Ti6Al4V/Ni80Cr20 dissimilar material joining process.
summary: This panel presents a summary table detailing the specific range of laser welding parameters applied to the Ti6Al4V/Ni80Cr20 material system. These parameters serve as the foundational inputs for calculating the laser fluence values used throughout the welding process, establishing the experimental boundaries for the study of the joint characteristics.

caption: Dark field TEM image obtained using the 501 reflection of Ni4Ti3, specifically visualizing the distribution of Ni4Ti3 particles within the matrix.
summary: Dark field TEM imaging using the 501 reflection of the Ni4Ti3 phase allows for the selective visualization of Ni4Ti3 particles. These particles are observed at martensite lath boundaries and inside grains, where they often grow on coarser globular Ni3Ti particles, demonstrating the complex precipitation behavior within the tempered martensite.

caption: Force-displacement (Fr-Δ2) curve generated via Monte Carlo simulations for connection model 2, highlighting the service limit state (SLS) at a node displacement of l/250 with a vertical red line.
summary: Shown here is the Fr-Δ2 curve for connection model 2, generated through Monte Carlo simulations based on a global truss model. The plot illustrates the resisting force behavior under monotonic loading. The service limit state is clearly identified by a vertical red line at a node displacement of l/250.

caption: Bode and phase angle plots for LPBF-718 alloy measured in a borate buffer solution at open circuit potential (OCP) relative to a saturated calomel electrode (SCE).
summary: Bode and phase angle plots for LPBF-718 alloy measured in a borate buffer solution at open circuit potential (OCP) relative to a saturated calomel electrode (SCE). These plots demonstrate that the electrochemical system exhibits dominant capacitive behaviour across the medium to low frequency ranges during the EIS measurements.

caption: Protein expression levels for the seven successfully generated glycine/serine-altered mutants, visualized via gel electrophoresis to confirm successful production.
summary: Protein expression analysis for the glycine and serine-altered mutants is shown here. Out of the eight initial mutations attempted, seven were successfully expressed. This panel serves as a quality control step to verify that the mutant proteins were produced before proceeding to the subsequent activity testing phase.

caption: Thermal strain of SRM 738 specimen plotted against temperature, comparing raw measured displacements with corrected data obtained by subtracting the distortion offset, alongside NIST standard reference values.
summary: This plot displays the thermal strain of an SRM 738 specimen as a function of temperature. It compares raw experimental data against a corrected dataset, which accounts for a measured distortion offset. The results are benchmarked against NIST standard data to validate the accuracy of the thermal displacement measurements.

caption: Bode plot showing the impedance modulus and phase angle measurements for the X-Y section of the Wall 0 sample.
summary: The X-Y section of the Wall 0 sample is characterized by this Bode plot. At the start of the immersion stage, the impedance modulus is measured at approximately 10⁴ Ω·cm² at low frequencies. The observed decrease of one order of magnitude after 14 days confirms a decline in the sample's barrier properties.

caption: Secondary elemental distribution map illustrating the localized concentration of alloying components across the powder surface.
summary: This secondary elemental map further clarifies the distribution of alloying elements within the Dievar powder. By visualizing these specific chemical variations, the panel assists in identifying localized concentrations, providing essential data to correlate the powder's chemical composition with its observed morphological characteristics and structural integrity during the analysis.

caption: EIS spectra represented as Nyquist plots for PEO-coated samples after 1 day of immersion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: This panel displays the EIS spectra of PEO-coated samples after 1 day of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution. The oxide coating formed during the PEO process exhibits three distinct time constants in the EIS data, indicating the electrochemical behavior of the coating under these specific environmental conditions.

caption: Etched cross-section of the 500 °C preheated specimen, showing the fine microstructure and localized regions of incomplete boron homogenization.
summary: Etched cross-sections of the 500 °C preheated specimen reveal a finely structured Mo-3.5 at.% B alloy. The image displays isolated vortex structures indicative of local insufficient B-homogenization, which serve to visualize the convective dynamics within the LPBF melt pool during the solidification process of the material.

caption: Raman spectra of abraded DLC, DLC-Si, and DLC-W coating surfaces across various sliding conditions, highlighting shifts in D and G peak intensities and broadening of FWHM values.
summary: Raman spectroscopy of abraded DLC surfaces reveals increased intensity of D and G peaks, accompanied by shifts to higher frequencies and broader FWHM values. DLC-Si demonstrates superior structural stability compared to pure DLC and DLC-W, which exhibit more intense and shifted peaks, indicating greater susceptibility to structural transformation during sliding.

caption: Generalized stacking fault energy (GSFE) profiles for Ni-M systems where alloying elements M are positioned on the third atomic layer relative to the slip plane.
summary: This panel presents the GSFE profiles for Ni-M systems with alloying atoms M situated on the third atomic plane from the slip plane. These DFT results demonstrate that even at this distance, alloying elements exert a non-negligible influence on the GSFE, significantly altering the energy landscape compared to pure Ni.

caption: EBSD-IPF map of the top region of the slow deposition, characterized by fine equiaxed grains.
summary: The top region of the slow deposition sample exhibits a refined microstructure consisting of fine equiaxed grains. This observation highlights the significant grain refinement achieved during the AFSD process compared to the feedstock material. The specific thermal and deformation history of the slow deposition contributes to this distinct grain morphology.

caption: Schematic representation of the inclined thin-walled geometry used for surface roughness sampling.
summary: This schematic illustrates the geometry of the inclined thin-walled parts utilized for the surface roughness sampling test. The setup is designed to facilitate the evaluation of surface characteristics across different deposition angles, providing a foundational framework for the subsequent measurement of roughness values relative to the building direction of the DED samples.

caption: Tabulated chemical composition in atomic percentage for points D through L, confirming the presence of a (β-Ti, Nb) BCC solid solution within the identified mixed zone.
summary: The chemical composition data for points D through L, presented in atomic percentage, confirms the formation of a (β-Ti, Nb) BCC solid solution in the mixed zone. This table provides quantitative evidence of the elemental distribution within the transition region identified in the microstructural analysis of the bimetal interface.

caption: Transmission electron microscopy image of the heat-treated TO structure, featuring an inset electron diffraction pattern that indicates stabilization of the beta phase.
summary: Transmission electron microscopy of the heat-treated TO structure shows the continued presence of the beta phase. The inset electron diffraction pattern supports the observation of slight stabilization of the beta phase following the thermal treatment, consistent with the refined and more uniform grain structure observed in the EBSD analysis.

caption: High-speed imaging frame and corresponding schematic illustration of the melt pool during laser processing with the powder side facing upward (Experiment No. 8, 3 kW, 2.4 m/min).
summary: This high-speed imaging frame shows the melt pool behavior when the powder side is oriented upward. At 3 kW and 2.4 m/min, the melt pool is significantly larger than in the binder-side-up case. The process induces both solid spatter and powder agglomeration spatter, characteristic of the MAPS process.

caption: TEM micrograph representing a region with intermediate dislocation density.
summary: Representing an intermediate state of deformation, this TEM image displays a moderate dislocation density. The visualization allows for the identification of dislocation structures that are less crowded than in strongly deformed zones, providing a balanced view of the material's microstructure for quantitative density measurements.

caption: Stress evolution during fatigue–creep testing at 650 ∘C incorporating a compressive strain dwell.
summary: Compressive strain dwell fatigue–creep tests at 650 ∘C reveal the cyclic stress behavior of the specimen. Consistent with other loading conditions, the material undergoes cyclic softening. The evolution trend remains stable regardless of the applied strain amplitude, providing insight into the material's mechanical stability under compressive dwell conditions.

caption: Normalized photoluminescence spectra of rare-earth doped germanosilicate glasses after heat treatment at 1100 °C, with Eu- and Tb-doped samples excited at 260 nm.
summary: Normalized photoluminescence spectra characterize the optical properties of rare-earth doped germanosilicate glasses following a heat treatment process at 1100 °C. The data, which includes specific excitation at 260 nm for Eu- and Tb-doped samples, provides a comparative view of the emission characteristics for the different rare-earth dopants incorporated into the glass matrix.

caption: Schematic representation of the WA-DED manufacturing system, illustrating the integration of a three-axis CNC machine, TIG welding torch, wire-feeding unit, and control system.
summary: This schematic illustrates the WA-DED equipment configuration, which is assembled using a three-axis CNC machine tool, a TIG welding torch, a welding machine, a wire-feeding device, and a control system. The setup provides the necessary framework for the additive manufacturing process used to fabricate the Al-Ce-Mg alloy components.

caption: Time-dependent coefficient of friction (COF) profiles for SBF lubrication with and without Ti3C2Tx and Mo2TiC2Tx MXene additives.
summary: This plot displays the representative coefficient of friction (COF) over time for SBF lubrication, comparing pure SBF against samples modified with Ti3C2Tx and Mo2TiC2Tx MXenes. The data shows that the COF stabilizes around 0.18 after the running-in period, while exhibiting pronounced fluctuations throughout the sliding duration for the tested conditions.

caption: Intensity-wavelength plots of supercontinuum emission generated under varying pulse energy conditions, collected via spectrometer during continuous hexapod movement at 100 μm/s.
summary: This plot displays the intensity-wavelength characteristics of supercontinuum emission generated under different pulse energy conditions. The data was collected using a spectrometer while the sample was moved by a hexapod at a constant speed of 100 μm/s, demonstrating the spectral response of the supercontinuum generation process under varying excitation parameters.

caption: UMAP dimensionality reduction visualization illustrating the clustering of proteomic data derived from rat BMSCs on GC, G365, G270, and GU implants.
summary: The UMAP plot provides a visual representation of the proteomic data distribution for rat BMSCs grown on GC, G365, G270, and GU implants. This dimensionality reduction technique effectively clusters the protein expression profiles, revealing distinct biological responses of the cells to the different 3D-printed implant surface topographies and compositions.

caption: Arrhenius plot showing the temperature dependence of relaxation times for both polyS2MA and polyMES, used to derive activation energies.
summary: Arrhenius analysis of relaxation times versus inverse temperature is presented for both polyS2MA and polyMES. This plot enables the calculation of the activation energy for the exchange reactions occurring within the materials. These findings, supported by DMTA data, provide critical insights into the thermomechanical properties of the polymers.

caption: Elemental point scanning analysis conducted at five characteristic locations across the coating, bonding interface, and substrate.
summary: Five characteristic points were selected at different locations across the coating, bonding area, and substrate to investigate the element distribution near the interface. This point scanning approach provides localized compositional data, allowing for a detailed comparison of elemental concentrations across the transition zone between the coating and the substrate.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for Al2O3 fillers.
summary: The particle size distribution of Al2O3 fillers is shown as a histogram. Data from a laser particle size analyzer reveal that the grain diameter varies between 1 and 60 μm, with an average diameter of approximately 12 μm, providing the necessary filler specifications for the subsequent casting process.

caption: Arrhenius plot displaying the measured steady-state creep rates as a function of inverse temperature for various aluminum alloy specimens.
summary: This Arrhenius plot illustrates the measured creep rates versus inverse temperature for multiple aluminum alloy specimens. The data reveals that creep rates across the different alloys vary by a factor of approximately 20, providing a comprehensive summary of the creep behavior observed during the experimental testing of these thin film materials.

caption: Contour surface showing the dependency of the initial crushing stress (σs) on the dimension parameters D and T.
summary: The BBD response surface for initial crushing stress (σs) demonstrates how varying the dimension parameters D and T affects the onset of compressive failure. This visualization allows for the identification of optimal geometric configurations that satisfy specific initial stress requirements during the compression testing process.

caption: Intermediate lattice beam intersection positions extracted from the reconstructed tomography data.
summary: This panel displays intermediate lattice beam intersection positions extracted from the reconstructed tomography. These points represent the structural nodes of the lattice, which are essential for the subsequent comparison with the as-designed model to compute the camera parameters through a nonlinear least-squares optimization algorithm.

caption: Average maximum slip amplitude per crystallographic grain as a function of average slip trace spacing for precipitation-hardened (sample #4) and solid-solution (sample #3) Alloy 718.
summary: This graph displays the relationship between the average maximum slip amplitude per grain and the average slip trace spacing for both precipitation-hardened and solid-solution Alloy 718 samples. The analysis quantifies the correlation between slip localization and trace spacing, revealing differences in the slip characteristics between the two metallurgical states of the alloy.

caption: Kernel average misorientation density distribution map for the HT1 specimen, showing an initial KAM value of 0.34°.
summary: The KAM density distribution map for the HT1 specimen quantifies the initial internal stress state. With a measured KAM value of 0.34°, this map provides a baseline for evaluating the effectiveness of subsequent heat treatments in relieving internal stresses within the material before mechanical testing.

caption: Line roughness measurement results, displaying parameters such as arithmetic average roughness (Ra) and maximum height roughness (Rz) to characterize surface undulations.
summary: Line roughness measurement results are presented, focusing on parameters like arithmetic average roughness (Ra) and maximum height roughness (Rz). These metrics provide a quantitative assessment of surface undulations, where Rc values intermediate between Ra and Rz reflect the averaged intensity of the surface profile features.

caption: Overview of key automation integration areas within additive manufacturing processes.
summary: This schematic illustrates the primary domains where automation is integrated into additive manufacturing workflows. By highlighting these specific areas, the diagram provides a structured overview of current trends and applications in the field, serving as a conceptual framework for understanding how automated systems enhance various stages of the additive manufacturing process.

caption: WDS-derived elemental concentration profiles for the diffused Pt coated sample after 100 h of isothermal oxidation at 1100 °C.
summary: Following 100 hours of isothermal oxidation at 1100 °C, the diffused Pt coating shows altered elemental concentration profiles. These WDS measurements illustrate the redistribution of Al, Co, Pt, and Ni, providing insight into the diffusion kinetics and phase stability of the coating system under prolonged thermal exposure.

caption: Flat tensile specimen following failure during mechanical testing.
summary: This photograph displays a flat tensile specimen fabricated via fuse deposition modeling with a 0.3 mm layer depth. The component exhibits clear signs of brittle failure after undergoing tensile testing. The visual evidence confirms the structural integrity loss characteristic of the brittle fracture behavior observed in the tested component.

caption: Compact tension force-displacement curves for Nylon-PVA combinations, showing moderate variability between the three printed samples.
summary: Compact tension force-displacement curves for Nylon-PVA combinations are shown for three tested samples. The results exhibit deviations between the three printed samples, although to a lesser degree than observed in the uniaxial test, reflecting the mechanical response of the material combination under compact tension loading.

caption: Magnified STEM-HAADF view of the L12/matrix interface at the corner position of the cuboidal precipitate.
summary: Magnified STEM-HAADF imaging of the precipitate corner highlights distinct interfacial characteristics compared to the edge. This region is critical for understanding how the material accommodates lattice mismatch, as the interfacial coherency at the corner differs significantly from the edge regions.

caption: Particle size distribution histogram for the 2024Al powder, illustrating the frequency of different particle diameters within the sample.
summary: The particle size distribution of the 2024Al powder is presented as a histogram. This plot quantifies the frequency of various particle diameters, offering a statistical representation of the powder's size characteristics, which is essential for understanding the consistency and quality of the material used in the experimental process.

caption: Temperature-dependent crack-growth rate measurements for Ni-5Cr alloy plotted against inverse test temperature in hydrogenated water and N2 gas environments.
summary: This Arrhenius plot displays the crack-growth rate response for the Ni-5Cr alloy as a function of inverse test temperature. The results demonstrate a significant difference in crack-growth behavior compared to the pure Ni and Ni-Fe/Cu alloys, highlighting the distinct influence of chromium alloying on the material's environmental degradation response.

caption: SEM micrograph of a coaxial A_18GNP strut cross-section.
summary: The SEM image of the A_18GNP coaxial strut demonstrates the structural differentiation between the core and shell. By observing the specific fracture modes characteristic of each material, the interface between the A and 18GNP components is clearly discernible within the coaxial geometry.

caption: XRD pattern of the fresh Co catalyst supported on γ-Al₂O₃.
summary: The XRD pattern for the fresh Co catalyst on γ-Al₂O₃ is presented here. This profile provides the initial structural state of the cobalt-based catalyst, allowing for comparison with the used sample to evaluate changes in crystallinity or phase composition following the catalytic reaction.

caption: Laser scanning confocal microscopy images of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured in Zn porous scaffold extracts for 3 days, with live cells stained green, damaged cells red, actin cytoskeleton green, and nuclei blue.
summary: Confocal microscopy images of MC3T3-E1 cells cultured in Zn scaffold extracts for 3 days reveal healthy cell morphology. Staining results for live/dead cells and actin/nuclei confirm that the Zn scaffold extracts do not exert negative effects on cell viability or morphology during the initial 3-day culture period.

caption: Atomic model illustrating the structural interface between the γ- and γ″-phases.
summary: This atomic model provides a theoretical representation of the interface between the γ- and γ″-phases. It serves to illustrate the structural transition and atomic-scale characteristics observed in the high-resolution TEM imaging of the phase boundary.

caption: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculation using the CALPHAD method, illustrating phase stability and transformation temperatures for X40CrMoV5-1 steel.
summary: Thermodynamic equilibrium calculations performed via the CALPHAD method are presented to compare against non-equilibrium models. The diagram indicates that the DED-Arc/M process occurs within the stable austenite region, with the gamma to alpha transformation occurring below approximately 850 °C, confirming that the microstructure forms primarily during the cooling phase.

caption: ToF-SIMS depth profiles illustrating the signal intensity of complex oxide and hydroxide anions, specifically AlO2-, TiO-, CrO-, FeOH-, NiO-, NiOH-, TiO2-, CrO2-, and CrO3H-, for the initial surface state of the alloy 690 steam generator tube.
summary: ToF-SIMS analysis was performed to estimate the thickness and chemical composition of the native oxide on the alloy 690 steam generator tube. Panel b shows the depth profiles for various complex anions, including AlO2-, TiO-, CrO-, FeOH-, NiO-, NiOH-, TiO2-, CrO2-, and CrO3H-, characterizing the initial surface state.

caption: Dual powder feeder configuration integrated into the DED system to facilitate the production of the graded material block.
summary: The image illustrates the two powder feeders employed within the direct energy deposition system. These components are essential for controlling the material composition during the additive manufacturing process, enabling the precise production of the functionally graded block by managing the powder ratios throughout the deposition cycle.

caption: High-speed photographic frame showing the globular transfer mode during the welding cycle.
summary: This high-speed photographic frame shows the globular transfer mode during the welding cycle. The metal transfer is a hybrid mode of globular and projected transfer. The droplet transferring period is short, and the droplet diameter is small, occurring under the peak arc voltage during the HLAW welding process.

caption: Qualitative contact angle measurements demonstrating the surface wettability characteristics of the different scaffolds.
summary: Surface wettability of the various scaffolds is evaluated through qualitative contact angle measurements. This panel provides a visual assessment of how different scaffold surfaces interact with liquids, serving as a primary indicator of the surface energy and hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity of the materials tested in this study.

caption: Comparison of H–h curves between simulation and theoretical model under the first loading condition.
summary: This panel shows the H–h curve comparison between simulation and theoretical results under the first loading condition. The obtained P–h curve is substituted into Eq. (24) to verify the proposed theoretical model, demonstrating the effectiveness of the model in predicting hardness variations relative to indentation depth under displacement control.

caption: Flank wear progression curve for the PCD(C) tool grade as a function of increasing cutting time.
summary: Flank wear progression for the PCD(C) tool grade is shown as a function of increasing cutting time. This plot characterizes the wear rate evolution for the grade, offering insight into the tool's degradation behavior during the machining process compared to the other tested PCD grades under similar experimental conditions.

caption: Precipitation-temperature-time (PTT) plot illustrating the kinetics of precipitate formation in Inconel 718 superalloy.
summary: This PTT diagram serves as a foundational guide for designing heat treatment processes for Inconel 718 superalloy. By mapping the precipitation kinetics across temperature and time, it enables the optimization of solution treatment parameters, such as the specific temperatures and durations used for the four experimental alloy groups.

caption: FOBI-retrieved neutron transmission spectra for the Fe and Cu sides, calculated by averaging data from the regions marked in panel (a).
summary: The FOBI-retrieved neutron transmission spectra for the TD2 direction are presented for both the Fe and Cu sides. These spectra were derived by averaging the transmission data over the large areas defined by the blue and red dashed rectangles shown in the sample photograph, providing distinct spectral signatures for each material.

caption: Scratch track height profile for N sample under a 20 N normal load.
summary: This panel displays the scratch track height profile for the N sample, obtained through tribological testing. The measurement was conducted under a constant normal load of 20 N to characterize the surface deformation and wear behavior of the material during the scratch test process.

caption: Bode phase angle plot representing the phase shift versus frequency for series A PEO-coated samples.
summary: Representing the phase angle component of the EIS results, this Bode plot characterizes the frequency-dependent phase shift for series A PEO-coated samples. The data serves as a representative measurement for this sample category, highlighting the electrochemical response and capacitive characteristics of the coating under the tested conditions.

caption: Time-resolved XRD patterns illustrating the microstructural evolution during the melting and mixing stage, highlighting periodic intermetallic phase formation and β-Ti peak shifts.
summary: This panel displays a sequence of XRD patterns capturing the microstructural evolution during the mixing stage. Red superimposed boxes indicate slight shifts in β-Ti peaks, reflecting heating during re-melting. At approximately 223 ms, intense peaks emerge, marked by a green arrow, signifying the solid phase formation of intermetallic compounds.

caption: Micro-hardness distribution graph illustrating the mechanical consistency achieved in FSAM components.
summary: The micro-hardness graph demonstrates the mechanical performance of the FSAM technology. Compared to standard approaches, this method significantly improves the uniformity of microhardness and ultimate tensile strength across the building direction, confirming that the cooling strategies effectively enhance the structural integrity and mechanical reliability of the fabricated material samples.

caption: Comparison of ultimate crack stresses between specimens subjected to constant uniaxial forces and those under hypergravitational forces at identical temperatures.
summary: This plot compares the ultimate crack stresses observed in materials under constant uniaxial forces versus hypergravitational forces at the same temperature. The comparison highlights how different force environments influence the threshold at which cracking occurs, providing insight into the material's fracture resistance under varying external loading conditions.

caption: Technical drawing illustrating the geometry and dimensions of the tensile specimen used for mechanical testing.
summary: This schematic provides a detailed representation of the tensile specimen geometry. It serves as a reference for the physical dimensions of the samples utilized during mechanical testing procedures. The diagram clearly defines the specimen shape and size, ensuring consistency and reproducibility in the experimental evaluation of material properties.

caption: Impact strength measurements for horizontal printing FDM parts (ABS-FH) across varying PB content levels.
summary: Impact strength of horizontal printing FDM parts (ABS-FH) is shown to assess mechanical behavior. This data, when compared with vertical printing results, demonstrates the existence of dual thresholds for PB content in achieving optimal FDM performance, indicating that printing orientation significantly impacts the mechanical properties of the FDM parts.

caption: Elastic modulus in flexure for printed PLA patterns, comparing 0.1 mm and 0.2 mm layer thicknesses.
summary: This panel illustrates the flexural modulus of the printed PLA samples. The findings regarding the flexural modulus are similar to those observed in the flexural strength tests, confirming that thicker layers result in reduced mechanical stiffness during bending deformation for all tested concentric, rectilinear, and honeycomb pattern configurations.

caption: Comparison of simulated dislocation density values derived from the current model against the established Gourdet and Montheillet (GM) model.
summary: This figure presents a comparative analysis of dislocation density predictions. It evaluates the performance of the current dislocation model by benchmarking its simulated results against the established Gourdet and Montheillet (GM) model. The plot highlights the relationship and consistency between these two distinct modeling approaches for predicting material dislocation behavior.

caption: Ratio of energy absorption to maximum compressive strength, calculated using the average values obtained from the GSLS specimens.
summary: The ratio of energy absorption to maximum compressive strength is calculated using average values from the GSLS specimens. This metric provides a normalized assessment of the structural efficiency, with GSLS-II maintaining the highest energy absorption performance among the tested configurations, as supported by the comparative analysis of the different lattice structures.

caption: Dilatometric results for AS1 alloy during heating at 0.167 °C/s up to 400 °C, showing dilation values and their corresponding derivative.
summary: Dilatometric measurements of the AS1 alloy during heating at 0.167 °C/s up to 400 °C provide dilation values and their derivatives. These results, analyzed alongside HEXRD data, confirm that precipitation begins near 250 °C and that significant precipitate growth occurs at temperatures above 300 °C, as evidenced by the derivative analysis.

caption: Hydrogen bond parameters, including average length and density, for cross-linked models.
summary: Hydrogen bond parameters for the cross-linked models are presented, detailing the average H-bond length and the number of H-bonds per unit volume. These values were calibrated using the Calculate Hydrogen Bonds module and a custom script program to characterize the bonding environment within the simulated cross-linked polymer network.

caption: Cross-sectional view of the simulated melt pool for S200 alloy, modeled without considering the effects of Mn evaporation during deposition.
summary: Representing the S200 melt pool without Mn evaporation, this simulation provides a baseline for comparison. The molten region is depicted in yellow, while surrounding zones are shown in turquoise and dark blue. The results demonstrate that excluding evaporation leads to a shallower melt pool depth compared to the evaporation-inclusive model.

caption: 3D and cross-sectional profilometer view of the scratch track on alloy B3, processed at 50 W and 2000 mm/s in an argon atmosphere.
summary: Alloy B3, processed at 50 W laser power and 2000 mm/s scanning speed in argon, shows a scratch track width of 98 μm and a depth of 7.47 μm. Increasing the laser power while maintaining high scanning speed leads to a reduction in both track width and depth.

caption: Stability assessment of the 3D-printed cassette-based aptasensor for dengue antigen detection over 30 days, measured via CV method with n = 5 replicates.
summary: Stability of the 3D-printed aptasensor was evaluated by storing it at 4 °C and performing CV measurements on the 1st, 7th, 15th, and 30th days. The sensor remained stable up to the 21st day, producing findings nearly identical to the initial Apt/GO-ZnO-NC/3DP-PAC performance, confirming its reliability for long-term antigen recognition.

caption: Normal map calculated from a different powder bed condition.
summary: This panel presents a normal map computed from a distinct powder bed condition. Similar to the primary map, the pixel colors represent surface normal orientations, where the R, G, and B channel intensities correspond to the magnitudes of the normal vector components along the x-, y-, and z-axes.

caption: Conceptual overview of the Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) approach, illustrating the iterative process of sampling parameter points from a prior distribution, simulating corresponding datasets, and applying a tolerance threshold to accept or discard parameters based on their proximity to target data.
summary: This schematic illustrates the likelihood-free Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) method used to estimate parameters. The process involves sampling from a prior distribution, generating simulated datasets, and comparing them against target data. Parameters are accepted only if the simulation satisfies a predefined tolerance threshold, providing a robust statistical estimation framework.

caption: Comparison of compressive yield strength versus relative density for MEX-produced SUS316L foams against literature data for SUS316L porous materials manufactured via alternative processing routes.
summary: This Ashby plot evaluates the mechanical performance of MEX-produced SUS316L foams by benchmarking their compressive yield strength against relative density. By comparing these results with established literature values for SUS316L porous materials fabricated through various other manufacturing processes, the graph effectively highlights the relative mechanical efficiency of the MEX-produced samples.

caption: UMAP visualization illustrating the contraction of the parameter space across 30 optimization rounds, with color intensity representing the progression from round 0 to 30.
summary: Parameter space evolution is visualized using UMAP, showing how the search space contracts over 30 rounds of optimization. The color intensity indicates the progression of rounds, revealing a three-phase strategy. Specifically, the exploration phase from rounds 0 to 10 demonstrates broad coverage of the parameter space.

caption: Band structure and density of states representation for the Ti2AlTa O-phase compound.
summary: The band structure and density of states for the Ti2AlTa O-phase compound are illustrated here. The material demonstrates a small indirect band gap, consistent with the electronic behavior observed in other Ti2AlM compounds. These findings contribute to understanding the stability and elastic properties of the O-phase system.

caption: Evolution of the α-AlFeMnSi (022) reference peak during cooling at a rate of 3 K s⁻¹.
summary: This panel depicts the synchrotron diffraction signal for the α-AlFeMnSi (022) reference peak during cooling at 3 K s⁻¹. The signal is affected by substantial noise, which is linked to the low phase fraction and the low count intensity of the HEXRD measurement performed during the cooling cycle.

caption: Mott-Schottky plot representing the scale film formed on Inconel 625 in 0.1 mol/L phosphoric acid.
summary: This Mott-Schottky plot characterizes the electronic properties of the scale film formed on Inconel 625 when exposed to a 0.1 mol/L phosphoric acid solution. The curve provides essential data regarding the semiconductor behavior of the passive film developed on the alloy surface under these specific acidic conditions.

caption: Selected area electron diffraction pattern verifying the hexagonal crystallographic structure of the acicular Fe2Mo phase found within the grain.
summary: Selected area electron diffraction analysis confirms the presence of the Fe2Mo phase within the grain interior. The diffraction spots verify that these acicular-shaped precipitates possess a hexagonal crystallographic structure, providing structural validation for the phase identification within the SLM-fabricated HX alloy following the ST + AT heat treatment.

caption: Half-section volume rendering of a cold plate microchannel showing obstructed regions at different threshold levels (T L, T Iso50, and T U).
summary: This half-section volume rendering illustrates the obstructed region of a cold plate microchannel. The channel appears impassable at T L and T Iso50, while T U appears more porous. T Iso50 is identified as the most accurate representation, as it correctly reflects the channel's failure in the flush test.

caption: Tukey simultaneous 95% confidence intervals for pairwise differences in mean grain aspect ratio across four distinct scanning strategies (ST1–ST4).
summary: This plot displays Tukey simultaneous 95% confidence intervals comparing mean grain aspect ratios for four scanning strategies. Analysis reveals that ST1 and ST2 exhibit similar aspect ratio behaviors, whereas ST3 and ST4 are grouped together, demonstrating significantly higher aspect ratio values compared to the first two strategies.

caption: Raman spectrum of dual-layer Ti–Cu coated diamond powder following SLM processing, showing a sharp, isolated diamond peak at 1331 cm⁻¹ with minimal graphitic signals.
summary: Post-SLM processing Raman analysis of dual-layer Ti–Cu coated diamond powder demonstrates a sharp, isolated diamond peak at 1331 cm⁻¹. The absence of significant graphitic signals confirms that the optimized coating and processing strategies successfully suppressed thermal-induced graphitization, maintaining the structural integrity of the diamond particles during the laser manufacturing process.

caption: Correlation plot between the first principal component of the stress-strain curves and the maximum macroscopic stress, demonstrating a strong positive relationship.
summary: This plot illustrates the correlation between the first principal component of the macroscopic stress-strain curves and the maximum macroscopic stress. The data reveals a strong positive correlation, suggesting that lower values of the first principal component are generally associated with higher prediction errors in the stress-strain curve modeling.

caption: Standard optical configuration showing the focused beam spot profile captured by the SP928 camera.
summary: This panel displays the standard beam spot configuration as observed by an Ophir optronics beam profiler. Utilizing an LBS300 attenuator and an SP928 camera, the image provides a baseline measurement of the focused beam intensity distribution, serving as a reference for comparing different optical configurations within the experimental setup.

caption: Von Mises stress distribution across the compound specimen composed of material 1 and material 2.
summary: This panel displays the von Mises stress distribution within a two-material compound specimen obtained through finite element analysis. The results indicate that stress levels in both materials closely approximate a uniaxial state throughout the majority of the uniform section, demonstrating the mechanical behavior under the assumed material properties.

caption: Summary table outlining the comparative advantages, potential limitations, and diverse biomedical applications of Zn alloys processed through LPBF.
summary: This table provides a comprehensive overview of Zn alloys fabricated by LPBF, summarizing their key advantages and disadvantages. It serves as a reference for understanding the practical utility of these materials in various biomedical applications, balancing their mechanical performance with their degradation characteristics in physiological environments.

caption: STEM micrograph illustrating the altered morphology and dimensions of γ′ and γ′′ phase precipitates following fatigue–creep testing with a tensile dwell.
summary: This STEM micrograph reveals the microstructural evolution of γ′ and γ′′ phase precipitates in a specimen subjected to fatigue–creep testing with a tensile dwell. A common feature observed in these tests is a distinct change in the shape and size of these precipitates, regardless of the specific dwell orientation.

caption: Lattice strain map in the loading direction resolved via FF-HEDM at the initial state, revealing slight bending loads present before plastic deformation.
summary: FF-HEDM characterization at the initial state resolves the grain-averaged full elastic strain tensor within a 100 µm tall volume. The map highlights a slight bending load induced by the gripping process, which is subsequently reduced as the sample undergoes plastic deformation during the mechanical loading sequence.

caption: Potentiodynamic polarization curves illustrating the corrosion behavior of the substrate and Ni–Mo–W coatings electrodeposited at varying current densities in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
summary: Potentiodynamic polarization curves are presented to evaluate the corrosion resistance of the substrate compared to Ni–Mo–W coatings produced at different current densities. These tests, conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, provide essential data on the electrochemical corrosion behavior of the materials, with specific corrosion parameters detailed in Table 4.

caption: Summary table of key electrochemical parameters, including electrochemical active surface area (EASA), standard rate constant (k 0 ), anodic current density (jₐ), and peak potential separation (ΔEₚ).
summary: This table summarizes critical electrochemical performance metrics, specifically the electrochemical active surface area (EASA), standard rate constant (k 0 ), anodic current density (jₐ), and peak potential separation (ΔEₚ). These parameters collectively quantify the electron transfer kinetics and surface activity of the electrodes, facilitating a direct comparison of their electrochemical efficiency.

caption: Dark-field TEM micrograph identifying the specific locations of regions A and B, which exhibit differing crystallographic orientations within the fine grain structure.
summary: This dark-field TEM micrograph highlights the specific regions A and B within the fine grain structure. These regions are separated by a low-angle grain boundary, as confirmed by the corresponding CBED patterns. The image demonstrates that these areas possess distinct crystallographic orientations within the sub-micron grain.

caption: First-principles calculated generalized stacking fault energy curve for the equiatomic Fe20Co20Cr20Ni20Mn20 alloy composition.
summary: This panel illustrates the generalized stacking fault energy curve for the equiatomic Fe20Co20Cr20Ni20Mn20 alloy, obtained through first-principles calculations. The results confirm that varying Fe and Mn contents significantly influence the maximum and minimum points of the energy curve, demonstrating the compositional dependence of stacking fault energy in these complex alloy systems.

caption: Calculated equilibrium phase diagram for the 316L/IN718 system, illustrating phase stability as a function of IN718 mass fraction.
summary: This binary equilibrium phase diagram for 316L/IN718 functionally graded materials was generated using Thermo-Calc simulations. It employs a dual-database approach, utilizing TCFE12 for the 316L side and TCNI12 for the IN718 side. The abscissa represents the mass fraction of IN718, ranging from 0.0 for pure 316L to 1.0 for pure IN718.

caption: Wear track cross-section profile extracted from 3D surface data for the 1B Invar alloy coating.
summary: Representing the 1B Invar alloy coating, this cross-sectional profile is extracted from 3D surface data to characterize the wear track. The profile highlights the material's response to wear, with raised edges on both sides indicating that plastic deformation occurred during the wear process, consistent with the observed residual wear debris.

caption: Release rates of Met from G@Met and BHP/G@Met scaffolds with and without ultrasound (US) stimulation, alongside PBS absorbance measurements at 233 nm.
summary: This panel displays the release kinetics of Met from G@Met and BHP/G@Met scaffolds, highlighting the influence of ultrasound stimulation on drug release. Additionally, the absorbance of PBS soaked in BHP and GelMA is measured at 233 nm to quantify the release behavior and verify the controllable drug delivery performance.

caption: Bright-field transmission electron microscopy micrograph and corresponding selected area electron diffraction pattern for the [011] zone axis, demonstrating the absence of γ′ and γ′′ superlattice reflections.
summary: Bright-field TEM imaging and SAED analysis for the [011] zone axis confirm the microstructure consists solely of the δ phase. The absence of γ′ and γ′′ superlattice reflections in the diffraction pattern and the lack of nano-size precipitates in the micrograph verify the complete dissolution of these phases.

caption: Experimental setup utilizing a blue light 3D scanner to capture the surface geometry of the printed component.
summary: The 3D scanning process is illustrated using a blue light 3D scanner, specifically the GOM ATOS Q system, which features an absolute accuracy of 0.0125 mm. This setup captures the complex surface geometry of the printed component, facilitating the generation of high-fidelity digital data for further dimensional analysis.

caption: Neutron diffraction strain measurements obtained from the 6 mm spot size wall deposited in the presence of coolant.
summary: Experimental strain values measured via neutron diffraction are presented for the 6 mm spot size wall deposited with coolant. These measurements show good agreement with the thermo-mechanical model predictions, specifically capturing the alternating compressive and tensile regions above the fillet area, confirming the model's overall predictive accuracy.

caption: Two-dimensional reflection loss (RL) projection for the 30% SCC-2/PEEK composite.
summary: The 2D RL plot for the 30% SCC-2/PEEK composite maps the reflection loss performance across frequency and thickness. This visualization helps in identifying the specific operational parameters where the material exhibits its most significant electromagnetic wave absorption, reflecting the impact of the 30% filler concentration.

caption: Time-dependent core center positions of the second dislocation under varying magnitudes of applied external stress.
summary: The core center positions of the second dislocation are plotted over time to demonstrate the influence of different applied stress magnitudes. By tracking these positions, the panel reveals how external stress levels dictate the evolution and velocity of the dislocation core as it interacts with the material interface during simulation.

caption: Transformation-time-temperature (TTT) diagram generated by JMatPro, comparing precipitation kinetics between dendritic core (solid line) and interdendritic (dotted line) regions.
summary: This TTT diagram, calculated using JMatPro based on the chemical composition distribution from the Scheil-Gulliver model, demonstrates the distinct dissolution and precipitation kinetics of the dendritic core versus the interdendritic regions. The results corroborate the influence of microsegregation on phase stability and kinetics in Inconel 625.

caption: Three-dimensional surface plot depicting the relationship between process parameters and interfacial porosity, generated via a 3rd-degree polynomial regression.
summary: Interfacial porosity is analyzed here through a 3D surface plot, demonstrating its dependency on specific process parameters. By employing a 3rd-degree polynomial function to fit the data, the plot highlights the trends and variations in porosity levels observed across the range of processing conditions tested in the research.

caption: Parity plot of simulated versus experimental shrinkage for the BJ-printed ZTA parts, validating the model's predictive capability regarding dimensional changes during the sintering process.
summary: This parity plot evaluates the predictive accuracy of the SOVS-based FE sintering model by comparing simulated shrinkage against experimental measurements. It serves as a validation step to ensure that the model effectively captures the dimensional changes occurring in the BJ-printed ZTA parts during the sintering process.

caption: Atomic composition table for the Cr0.31Fe0.69 alloy at a normalized depth of approximately 0.09, derived from Scofield sensitivity factor-scaled XPS peak areas.
summary: This table provides the quantified atomic composition of the Cr0.31Fe0.69 alloy at a normalized depth of 0.09. The values are calculated by scaling fitted XPS peak areas with Scofield sensitivity factors, while bulk atomic percentages are determined through interpolation of EDX atomic concentration maps for comparison.

caption: Tafel plots derived from linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves at 1600 rpm in 0.1 M HClO4, showing a Tafel slope of 62 mV per decade for the PtFe alloy.
summary: Tafel plots for the PtFe alloy were generated from LSV curves at 1600 rpm in 0.1 M HClO4. The observed Tafel slope of 62 mV per decade indicates that the first electron transfer is the rate-determining step for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) at room temperature.

caption: Deviation chart derived from CT measurement data, mapping the spatial distribution of dimensional errors across the ZrO2 part surface.
summary: A deviation chart provides a spatial representation of dimensional errors for a ZrO2 part printed with a curing energy of 105 mJ/cm2. Derived from computer tomography data, this visualization quantifies the geometric discrepancies between the printed ceramic part and the target design, identifying specific areas of dimensional inaccuracy.

caption: Current-voltage characteristics for the PhotoWatt-PWP201 PV module generated using TSEC parameters derived from the SNF-TSEC approach.
summary: This panel displays the I-V curves for the PhotoWatt-PWP201 PV module. The data is generated via the TSEC method, utilizing FDM physical parameters extracted through the SNF-TSEC approach. These curves illustrate the electrical performance characteristics of the solar module under the specified experimental conditions described in the study.

caption: TGA and DTG profiles for untreated and flame retardant-treated rayon rovings, recorded in a nitrogen environment with a heating rate of 20 K/min.
summary: Rayon rovings are analyzed using TGA and DTG curves to determine their thermal decomposition characteristics. By testing both untreated and flame retardant-treated specimens under nitrogen at 20 K/min, the figure illustrates the influence of flame retardant additives on the pyrolytic degradation kinetics of the rayon material.

caption: Simulated XRD pattern for the Sm0.38Y0.10Mg0.52Ni1.93Co0.03Al0.05 alloy where Mg atoms occupy both 4a and 4c sites simultaneously.
summary: This simulated XRD pattern corresponds to the Sm0.38Y0.10Mg0.52Ni1.93Co0.03Al0.05 alloy with Mg occupying both 4a and 4c sites simultaneously. Unlike the single-site occupation models, this simulation produces results that are completely different from the experimental data, indicating this structural configuration is not representative of the actual alloy.

caption: Absorption coefficient spectra of GaP 1-x N x layers plotted against photon energy, demonstrating a progressive red-shift of the absorption edge relative to the GaP reference sample.
summary: This plot displays the absorption coefficient spectra for GaP 1-x N x layers as a function of photon energy near the absorption edge. The data reveals a strong absorption coefficient characteristic of a direct bandgap, with a clear red-shift in the absorption edge as nitrogen content increases compared to the GaP reference.

caption: Load-depth curves obtained from nanoindentation testing of a TiZrTa0.7NbMo RHEA powder cross-section, performed at a 0.65 mN/s loading rate with a 10 mN peak load, featuring an inset showing the triangle indentation geometry.
summary: The load-depth curves illustrate the mechanical response of the TiZrTa0.7NbMo RHEA powder cross-section during nanoindentation at a 0.65 mN/s loading rate and 10 mN peak load. An inset within the plot provides a visual representation of the triangle indentation geometry used to characterize the material's local mechanical behavior.

caption: O1s XPS spectra for passive films on Cr20, Cr30, Cr40, and Cr50 alloys, displaying peaks for O2-, OH-, and bound water.
summary: O1s spectra for the Cr20, Cr30, Cr40, and Cr50 alloys consist of three peaks attributed to O2- at 529.72 eV, OH- at 531.72 eV, and bound water H2O at 533.64 eV. The Cr30 sample exhibits the highest relative content of bound water, which correlates with its enhanced corrosion resistance performance.
